_childDocuments_.review: You can explore, construct, and interact with people in a post-apocalyptic desert village in the endearing and captivating life simulation game My Time At Sandrock. _childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of loot & gather as well as resource management, this game is just amazing. The game does an excellent job at introducing new elements without overwhelming the players' options, but also offers plenty of casual events that seem to never end. This game is constantly interacting with the player in a truly immersive sense while keeping them busy with things to do, without making it difficult for the player to keep up. The game has a way of rewarding the player for going out of their way, and shows how the player impacts the small town of Sandrock. They've done an excellent job of organizing the game in a way where, even if you hadn't played it in some time, you're not absolutely lost and forget where to get resources.The few cons to the game, in terms of dynamics;This is certainly a casual game. Hardcore gamers who enjoy tons of stimulation may find this game a bit slow or tedious. There is a fair amount of passive gameplay involved, and so far, the combat is fun but rather linear. It also takes some playtime before all avenues of the game are introduced, some of which I haven't come across even 36 hours in. For perspective, time passes in the game. In 36 real-time hours, only three seasons have passed in-game.In short:This is a casual game that rewards a fair amount of patience. To truly enjoy this game, you're in it for the long-haul. If you're okay with that, you will love every minute of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This game is excellent; buy without hesitation imo.Long version! I've rarely seen a developer take such good strides on their second iteration of a game. Portia was already fun and they've improved on the mechanics, characters, story, everything.Inventory management has been the easiest I've seen - if it's in a chest on your property, you can use it basically anywhere except for gift giving or donating to the museum. Throw it in a chest and forget about it.At first blush, the townsfolk seem like straight stereotypes. The Science Guy. The Conservative Rancher. The Boring Guy. The Grandma. But the writers lean in to each type, giving breadth and life to each one in a way I've rarely gotten to enjoy. This is the most I've cared about characters in this kind of game since I wanted to help Shane with his alcoholism.Let's take Science Guy. I went from rolling my eyes to being lured in by his delicate voice acting and giggling as they put in some of the funnier bits of nerdom to finally asking him to marry me and now he greets me each morning with wishing me a well-rested brain. Thanks, babe!The story is long and has twists. Twists! The wiki is good about hiding spoilers but be wary of looking up quest titles, etc.Combat is mostly point-and-click easy with a few notable exceptions. If you bring enough healing supplies, you can negate any difficulty. If you dislike combat, bring a bunch of healing items and you can slam your way through it just fine.I also like that there's no in-game reason to hurry through things or a deadline to face, so even if I feel I didn't get much done in a day, it's fine because I'm not up against a timeline of grandfather's spirit judging, etc.If I had any complaints, it might be the story went on longer than I wanted it to. It took me two and a half in game years to finish it up. And that there were two fights I had trouble with, which would have been fine if I'd brought more supplies than I had, but I'd gone in cocky because combat had been too easy before those points.I spent over two hundred hours on a single run through and thoroughly enjoyed it. I hope you do too.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy open world crafting/building/farming style of games. Like Portia, Sandrock has a little bit of everything. There's also plenty of main storyline and character based quests to keep you busy as well as commissions to help you stockpile those hard earned gols!  Those are great ways to boost your relationship score with those characters as well as the characters they are also close with such as their friends and family.  The interface for building and crafting is much improved over the original one in Portia since you can access your building materials directly from storage or inventory without having to have them in your characters hands to use them for building.  The storyline itself is immediately captivating and it gives you an enjoyable feel for what a struggle their lives would be like in a harsh and unforgiving climate like that.This game is definitely worth your time and investment.  You will get loads of gameplay out of it without ceasing to be entertained.  I love coming home from work and unwinding by playing a little Sandrock before time to get ready for bed!

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely love this game. I went into it mostly blind and it has been one of the most fun experiences so far since I started gaming again. The most I read about it was that it was an improvement on My Time at Portia (MTaP) in nearly every way (which I hadn't played yet) and it was long. I only just started playing MTaP after finishing the main story in Sandrock. and I would have to agree Sandrock is such a step up. It seems like the devs actually listened to what the players wanted. The graphics, art style. and UI are better. There are QOL changes that were wonderful. There can be a bit of a learning curve, but once you have it down and know where to source things it's not too difficult, but can still be challenging.The NPCs are some of my favorites I've ever come across in a game like this. Everyone has their own personality and the marriage candidates are solid. There are some that are clearly older or younger than each other, so you don't have to feel weird being an almost 30 year old adult dating someone who is like, 18. Or an 18 year old stuck dating someone in their 30s or 40s. There are even romance mechanics I didn't know about until it was too late that made it so much fun and unpredictable. All I'll say is maybe don't flirt with everyone if you don't want them to act on it because some will. Only complaint is that imo the male characters seem like they have a bit more depth, which is pretty common for games like these.The original game isn't in English, but the English translation and voice acting is incredible. There may be a small typos here and there in some written texts, but nothing major. The game is surprisingly funny at times, too. There are even self aware moments that add to the humor. I would say it is long, especially if you take your time instead of plowing through the main story quests. For me, that's a good thing since the pacing seemed great and there was always something going on. There are some quests with time limits that can affect a lot, so make sure to pay attention to when they are due. The map feels really big and fast travel is unlocked pretty early on.Some aspects of the story are directly related to the events of MTaP, but you dont need to know everything that happened. There are a few references, but it isn't reliant on the story of the first game, just interconnected. There are some small pieces of dialogue that could be considered "spoilers," and some NPCs from Portia are mentioned or show up in Sandrock at some point, but nothing that I've found too crazy or like Portia wasn't worth playing. Rather than being a sequel that happens after the events in Portia, I believe they are (mostly) concurrent games. The events at Sandrock may actually happen a little before some of the ones in Portia, but I'm not entirely sure.It's not a perfect game, no game ever will be, but it is a fantastic one if these types of games are something you're into.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - 5 out of 5 StarsThis is now one of my favorite games of all time. I was part of the kickstarter for this game after having played My Time at Portia, and I now know it was a very worthwhile investment. I waited until the game had been out for awhile to play and over the past few weeks, I have invested over 200 hours, something that is a miracle for my ADHD-addled brain.The characters, the setting, the gameplay - it's amazing. I haven't had as much fun playing a game in a long time. It got to the point where I didn't want to do ANYTHING but play this game. Thankfully, my friends and family are patient people.I didn't expect the plot to be so complex and interesting, or to fall in love with the town the way I did. I also didn't expect to like  so much, especially not so much that I ended up marrying them. But the characters are so endearing and well-written, and there are little Easter eggs sprinkled throughout the game, both for the previous Portia game and for pop-culture. Overtime, the town changes thanks to your work and it's very satisfying to see. The mechanics - fighting, collecting resources, completing commissions, building up your workshop - they are all really fun and not too tedious. And the plot! The plot shocked me - I wasn't expecting some of the twists and turns that happened. I'm normally really good at picking up on what's going to happen, but they really surprised me.There are a few things I didn't like - just like in Portia, the mechanic of having children is just awful. I plan on playing the game over again in the future and my character will NOT have kids - they aren't cute, your Spouse doesn't watch them while you work (in fact, throughout my pregnancy, my Spouse went on and on about needing to be there for me and the baby and the SECOND I gave birth, they took off running as fast as they could to the middle of the desert. I think they were having some sort of parental crisis), they have random needs throughout the day but you have to be home and near the kid to know and you still have tons and tons of work to do outside of the house. And then if you miss the time window in the evening where they need fed (which is random) and your SPOUSE feeds them, they will have an upset stomach in the morning and you lose favor points with your Spouse and the baby. And overall, that's really the only thing I didn't like, and it can be easily avoided in the future. And the fact that I am already planning a second playthrough once my brain forgets some of the story should tell you how good this game is. If you like games like Stardew Valley, Coral Island, Graveyard Keeper and you're good with wholesome, I cannot recommend this game enough. I can't wait to play again.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I never totally clicked with My Time at Portia, it gave me kind of a creepy feeling, which I think the character models had something to do with. In Sandrock the gameplay loop is fun and can be relaxing, there is lots of QoL features like saving anywhere anytime and pulling items out of chests for crafting or fulfilling requests -  but what I really really enjoy about this game is the writing and the social aspect. I feel like a lot of indie farming/cozy sims do not focus a lot on the characters and dialogue, but every NPC in Sandrock feels alive and it just gives me a different cozy feeling no other sim game has before. The voice acting is really good for the most part, they comment on a new hairstyle you have, they comment on you not going to bed early enough, sometimes characters talk to each other and you can listen in. I am sure the very long story has a lot to do with it too, which I have not finished yet, but is way more involved and in depth than other games of this kind (from what I know).Personally I have had no bugs on PC in the full release, but I do know that there are things to be fixed, which the developers are very quick to address, from what I have seen. I am really glad I picked this up, and I am sure it will be one of my favourites in this genre for a long time!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is silly and story wise you shouldnt take it too serious. it has it's own charms but it might be too overwhelming for people who havent played my time at portia before. im close to end game and im having tons of fun, definitely 8.5/10 or even more in my standards. it's pretty much up there for a relaxing life sim games and this game is unique on it's premise.Anyways there is some things that needs to be solved still- one year in and the game is still buggy as hell in quests, everything just feels a bit rough around the edges- cutscenes are sometimes weird especially when using my own costumes.- cutscenes are still buggy as hell. fps drops, my character being stuck and i have to alt+f4 and various weird stuff- please have an option to abandon/restart missions. one example i had was during one of the festivals in the same day as a main mission. the npc then made me insta lose during the event because he had to tp somewhere else.- horseriding/mounts (although better than during the beta) still have some weird clipping problems at times- im pretty sure theres a memory leak or something, playing the game for more than 1 hour would make my game run in 30fps rather than 60+ in some areas

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game I've played in a long time and I'm so glad that I decided to take the chance on early access. The gameplay loop is really fun and there's always something for me to do. It's so addictive that it's hard for me to not just keep playing and starting another day even when I say I'm done and this is the last one. I'm sure my husband's sick of that. I did play my time in Portia and though I liked it, this game improved it in many ways. My favorite improvement is the fact that I can sprint without using endurance and it's one of the reasons why I can't go back to playing Portia after this. I also love that the mining no longer feels like a tacked-on mechanic. It's so addictive that half the time, I return to my house too late and end up with ghastly dark circles the next day. : There is so much to do! This game has everything: farming, building, mining,  simple but fun combat, relationship building, engaging writing, a fun plot, and a frankly addictive gameplay loop. The skill tree system is unique in that the types of skills are in their own categories, and you only earn skills in things you're doing a lot of.: Building stuff in the workshop is incredibly fun, even though there are timers to manage. I like that as you upgrade your equipment, the less you need to manage, and unlocking perks drive me to keep at it to reap the rewards.Farming is not the main part of the gameplay, but the farming system is still fun and rewarding enough to invest time in. I think that it ties in well with cooking and gives you another way to make money.: The combat is really fun even though it's incredibly simple and I'm just mashing a button all day, but the animations and the combos make it feel less monotonous and look very impressive. I like that. It's easy enough for people that are playing it for the life sim rather than for the combat aspect. You don't have to be good at video games, so it doesn't detract from the relaxing vibe of the game. Playing through the Breach and the Shipyard Ruins feels like a completely different game and I welcome the change of pace.Adjustable Pacing: I love that you can adjust the pace of the day and I always set it to 0.6x but I would love it if I could set it down even lower. The pace is pretty perfect right now but even slower would be nice. Regardless, this is a great QoL option I wish more farming sims would implement.: The characters are also lovable and the NPCs make me want to go out of my way to talk to them every single day. I love that I can build relationships with everyone even if they are not romanceable, and they're all very different. Some of them took time to grow on me, and that speaks to how well the characters are written.: I love how cute and wholesome everything is even when it should be dire, and the humor is on point. I love the desert setting and the way the narrative tackles the challenges and explores solutions to revert the desertification and economic crisis. As someone who is very depressed about climate change, this is like a soothing balm for my soul.: The economy in this game feels very balanced, which many games seem to fail at. Certain story events make certain items cost more until they're resolved, and the game rewards you for building relationships with shop owners via them giving you friendship discounts. It feels like the interactions matter, and not just through the conversation.: There's a bug that I kept running into throughout the game where key cards glitch and it's happened in two dungeons already.  It doesn't always happen, but when it does, I can't progress. I can get around it by making a save right before I enter the key card so it's not completely game-breaking, but I lost a lot of progress before I started doing that.: The game should not be giving me commissions that I can't complete at that point. This has happened to me several times where I have failed commissions because I didn't research ahead of time to see if I have access to materials or machines that would enable me to complete them. If they could just not make them available or even just let me know that I'm unable to do them with my current equipment or being at this point in the story, that would be a huge improvement. This just adds stress to a game that should be relaxing and I hate that I have commissions that have failed due to a lack of details. Additionally, the details for materials from monster drops should be more specific and helpful. Instead of an item being described as "from monsters", it should specify which monster so I can know where to hunt them.Another issue with commissions is when I don't have access to a character to turn commissions in because they're asleep and I end up failing it overnight. I want the option to turn in commissions straight to the board when a character is unavailable due to the story or because it's after 19:00. It would still make sense but it would make the game a lot less stressful.: I would like the option to turn off sandstorm days. They can be such a drag and sometimes I want to sleep early to skip them because I don't feel like doing anything when the visibility is so bad. Let me adjust the intensity of the sandstorm or give me an incentive to not skip them by going to bed early like certain monsters are higher level/have better drop rates during them.The fog inside the Moisture Farm also makes my game lag like crazy. Even playing on a nicer setup that should be able to handle it just fine, this game seems like it could be optimized better. Being able to turn off the fog would be great.: I don't like how the clothes look in this game and I wish there were more girly dresses and just clothing options, in general, to play around with. I end up just going for what has the best specs and my character looks like a hot mess most of the time. There are clothes in Vivi's shop that looks cute, but they're not available to buy. I would like more furniture as well because most of them look terrible and they don't match and I'm hoping there will be more matching furniture sets in the future. Some of the wooden furniture you can paint, but others you can't, and that makes no sense.: Building my workshop through Construction Junction is the opposite of fun. The mechanic is tedious and unintuitive and I hate that NOTHING IS CENTERED. This is probably my biggest gripe along with how things need so much clearance space for no reason, so I can't put beds flush up against the wall or centered with the windows This is so stupid and it takes up so much space and it doesn't look good. I would like to be able to place stuff more easily because the locking mechanism is very clunky right now. I notice how there are certain things you can place with Ctrl, but I don't understand why it doesn't work across the board with placing everything.Currently, it's so hard to build your house from scratch that I'm just saving up for one of the presets.Inventory: I don't like the fact that sometimes I need the stuff in my bag for certain things, whereas the rest of the time, the game automatically pulls from my storage. It's so tedious to go through my chest to find the pieces of relics to bring to the museum when quests and commissions don't require the same. It's just inconsistent.

_childDocuments_.review: I must say, I am enjoying Sandrock much more than I thought I would. For example, when you kick a cactus and you get a thorn stuck in your shoe. I find it amusing and it also adds realism. _childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but as it is now, I don't think it's up to par. I can definately see where they've improved from my time at Portia in terms of game mechanic and there's a very real attempt at world building, but it's still very much an unfinished product. For me, the game is also very laggy and I get stuck in cutscenes often enough for me to notice, and there are clearly some characters who are more flashed out than others in terms of their dialogues, schedules and impact on overall storylines (I've had 2 characters get stuck on my front porch already). There are no multiple interwoven storylines for every / every group of characters, only 1 linear main story and lots of side quests that have no impact on the main story. I think this is a missed opportunity and great shame.The stories have good ideas behind them but with this kind of games, the devil is in the details. Good story, depth and execution is what makes this kind of games from grindy to relaxing. Like, I want to smile at the dialogues and feel like me slaving away in the mines to make a certain character something is impactful to the game's overall storyline!  But as it is now,there are alot of characters that I just don't care for and alot of 'side quests' that don't develop into anything so it feels grindy at times. Of the characters I've met so far, I really like Justice. Probably because I have a soft spot for his kind of personality/ vibe, The sleazy commerce guild 'president' made me chuckle a couple of times too. Absolutely hate Qi's condesending attitude (I hope the character gets more diamension soon), and the Pottery lady and her brother kept making me run errands for them. She apologised in the end but never talked to me again... wtf you think everything's ok just cus you said "opps sry~" !?? >:( They're lucky they're good looking.  You could tell the game production is split into sections during the production process, developed by different teams then stitched together. Perhaps this is why they couldn't do the multiple storylines or go very indepth with character development. I know a lot of games are produced like this, but if it's so obvious that even the player notices, I think you have a problem. During character creation, we got to select our character's voice. I initially was really excited because I thought we were gonna get some player character voiced lines, but the selection was only for grunts when chopping wood and stuff. It was so uncanny how silent the player character is throughout the different conversations in the cutscenes. Makes me think that they wanted to give the player lines at first but the publisher probably asked the developers to release the beta before they even had the whole script done so they couldn't record the player character's voice lines. I really hope the player is voiced during the game's actual release. Also side note, there is a very strong sense that this game was either made with a PRC Chinese crew at some point or made specially with a China release in mind. I'm not saying this is a good thing or a bad thing, it's just a thing that I felt while playing. There is just a very mainland/ taiwanese Chinese game design vibe to this game that I can't quite describe. Maybe it's the asethetic choices, maybe it's the food assets or something. I love the representation, though it's slightly east asian leaning imo. It's not a good or nor bad thing, and doesn't really affect my gameplay, it just made me do a double take because I don't recall My time in Portia was made by a chinese developer but this game felt like it was made at least in part by a chinese developer team hahaha My favourite character is still the the black dude Justice and the Cat captain tho! Still haven't met Logan, can't wait to meet Logan and Haru!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved MTaP so I couldn't wait for this to be released, I was a little hesitant on playing right away since it's in early access but for an early access game I have been thoroughly enjoying it! Like I said, I loved MTaP but this just feels so much better but it still retains the charm of the previous game. (ngl the cloth and hair physics made me so excited for some reason lol). Honestly, I've been trying to space out my time playing this game because I'm afraid I'll run out of content in the early access but I can't stop playing it. If you haven't played My Time at Portia yet, I would recommend playing that first before this just so you could come back and play Sandrock when it has been developed a little further it's always nice to see small bits of MTaP showing up in Sandrock. Still, this game does explain the world clearly enough for new players to grasp the story.There are some places that feel empty and some characters have weird habits (I didn't know who Krystal was until about 20 hours in the game because she never leaves their house and Grace is sometimes in the Graveyard shack?) that I don't know if it's intentional. The dialogue does get repetitive and so do the NPC's requests -- Arvio has asked me for water more times than I could count so my relationship with him is much higher than the others and on the flip side, as much as I want to increase  my relationship with Fang, I could only do so in small increments per day and on top of that he doesn't even accept gifts (but that might be his unique character quirk???). Anyways, the game is in early access so these don't bother me as much since the gameplay loop has me hooked for now. Overall, I really like it so far but please make Logan a romance candidate. pls and thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Portia so I've been very excited for Sandrock. So far I've absolutely enjoyed it. Graphics seem on par with what I expected, and any bug issues have experiences have been minimum or usually bug-fixed out quickly (at least in my experience).The characters that live in town, while yes still feel a little early access, still seem like they are going to be just as fun once they have a little more content added to them. I like the fact that the developers included how much content is available so far as it set pretty decent expectations.Skill Trees are a nice touch, and I cant wait to see where they end up, once more traits get released. The sorting feature of the House expansion while more hands on, can get a little clunky, especially if you want a second floor as there aren't a lot of stair options yet, but once you spend some time on it and get the hang of it works ok, you just gotta be careful with how much you edit with items inside as then your mailbox will be full. I feel once more options are available it'll be alot more fun/easier.Overall if you liked Portia you are more than likely going to like Sandrock, I'm excited to see where the story goes and if the stores you see 'Closed' end up reopening down the line as the town becomes more successful. If you are new to the 'My Time' games I recommend you get it, as its a fun crafting experience that can suck you in, just go in realizing that it IS Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, relaxing, quirky game that scratches all the right itches of this type of genre, while at the same time being unrefined, not at all challenging, and laughably cheesy. H O W E V E R - Seriously yall, some of the bugs, mistakes, glitches and quirks in this game are just so bad and look like really easy fixes. - Tree art has meshes that don't line up where it would appear "chopped" at the trunk. - The voice acting is either fantastic, or fantastically bad. If the actors have really thick native accents, don't tell them to sound country! It doesn't work! Just have them speak in their native accent, it sounds fine and doesn't break immersion in a post calamity fantasy world. - Do one more quality pass over your writing and dialogue, possibly with a native English speaker. There's some easy mistakes in the text/speech that can cause a lot of confusion. - Fix the pop-in of assets! Even if you have to force another second of load time for the player. I've gotten stuck in things that haven't appeared yet - especially on holidays. - Don't automatically have the player start chopping a tree that they shouldn't be chopping! I don't want to be punished in game for doing something that I didn't mean to do in the first place. - Allow calendar reminders for NPC Birthdays. - MORE SANDSTORMS! They should damage shops and buildings, allowing for the builder to take on special commissions to repair them for temporary discounts. - Warn players further in advance that quests are going to expire... - Not everyone should get along. Perhaps consider in the future that becoming friends with some people, means making enemies of others. Make the relationship meters less linear. Put more hints into the game to help the player know what gifts NPC's love. I don't want to have to google this stuff! - More quests for the animals! -Whoever comes up with your monsters (honey pot ant, rocket rooster, etc) deserves a raise.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played their fair share of life simulation games, with the variety of Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and Palia to be some of the main ones, this game comes very close to beating them all. I was thrilled to find out that this game was going to have multiplayer in it, seeing as My Time at Portia does not have multiplayer, which heavily influenced my choice to buy it or not.      This game can be buggy at times and while I only have a 980 gpu, I can run this game at medium settings and it still looks pretty decent. I did not play the early access, only full release, and I can say that there seems to be quite a bit of content to this game. This game is very multifaceted with social/town, farming, combat, mining, building, animal, and pet aspects, with that just being what I have discovered with 19 hours of playing. I play with 2 other people and the game runs fairly well. I have only encountered a few lag/server sync issues between other players, a few UI glitch errors, and 1 wonky combat fight with an elite. But beyond those few things I haven't seen much to stop me from wanting to play this game as much as possible. - Lots of Content (19 hours in and it feels like I have so much more to do)- Decent price (I was gifted the game but seeing the price for how fun this game is seems fair)- Fun with friends- Multiplayer actual works- Leveling up feels important and good- Missions feel good and not like leg work (You can visually see the work you put into the town)- Tons of townspeople- Combat feels good and fun- Character Customization (You can super customize your character with sliders)- Gear (Weapons and clothes have stats that can help you with gathering and fighting)- Weather (The weather events in this game are really great. So far I have seen rain, sandstorm, and summer    heat. I am waiting to see snow in this game as of yet.)- Server Stays Up (No matter who owns the town, I am able to play on my friends server even after the    person who made it has left. This is a big game changer for me seeing as you don't have to stop playing on    one server because the host has left or crashed.)- Desync/stutter issues (I have only had this happen 2-3 times playing so far and it is fixed by a simple return   to lobby and rejoin.)- UI machine icons disappear (I have only seen this once and it was fixed by rejoining the lobby)- Forced Personal Chests (I mention this because it was a pain to have only so much room in the ONE    community chest you get at the start of the game. You can upgrade it, but I would like to have the option    to share my personal chest contents if I choose to. And not have to run back to home every time someone    needed something.- Combat (could use a little work on hit registration and how your character can go through the enemies    while swinging your weapon)- Accidental Playable Character Requests (In the game there is an option to talk to real people and play a    mini-game called Critters. It feels a bit annoying at times when you are trying to interact with machines or    doors and other playable characters get the input over the item/machine/door. Could be quite annoying if    playing with a lot of people in one area but not too bad overall.)Overall this game feels pretty fun to play and in just 2 days my friends and I have put in almost 20 hours each.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it took me 80+ hours to finish "Early Access" content. And I rushed it, lol.This game has just so much to give even though it's created by a modest developer team.The new NPCs have a far stronger character than the people of Portia, even though the Early Access version contains little content related to their individual stories. Mining got more interesting with the new style of abandoned ruins, but the hazardous ruins got really insignificant.The new house building mechanic is really nice, though I'd prefer a smaller staircase option to have place for more furniture... and also more furniture options.Centering the construction economy around recyclers is a nice new touch, also, the higher machine efficiency (had half as many machines compared to Portia, and it was just fine) is a good step to balance things. Water acquisition on the other hand is bothersome in the early game, and annoying in the late part.The game is overall really really fun, only in the late first year (or later if the player isn't rushing things) does it start to show that it's missing planned content.Presently transitioning to the last resource set is bothersome due to the missing late-game content, but it's still great fun. My only concern is that I'm not sure people unfamiliar with Portia could get into the game with the simplistic tutorials it offers.

_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I have been waiting a very long time for. I was a huge fan of My Time at Portia and I have put hundreds of hours into that game, so when the announcement for My Time at Sandrock happened I got very excited. Even though this game is still in early access at the time of writing this review, I am absolutely blown away by how well the small dev team did. This sequel feels way more polished than the first, and it isn't even finished yet! I highly recommend buying this game at the discounted early access price.This is a game that you can kick back and relax while playing, you play at your own pace! It has everything you could want such as crafting, farming, building, combat, exploration, a story, interesting characters, etc. If you like games such as Animal Crossing, then you'll love My Time at Sandrock. But keep in mind the game isn't complete and there is still much more content on the way! I will update this review when it is officially released and out of early access.You don't need a high end rig to run this game, it looks beautiful with its unique art style. The lighting and coloring is a massive improvement compared to My Time at Portia. The character models are also a massive improvement. Character customization is much more in depth with plenty of sliders to make your character unique. You can also change your hairstyle, color, and makeup any time once you're in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This Review is still on Early Access:While many Players might be afraid to purchase Early Access Games, the Developers are active!!They Release new content regular, keep active/respond in Discort and Forum, so you can see the Progress.For Players who already played my Time at Portia and loved it:i strongly recomment Sandrock. They added so many quality of life upgrades.You are not in a beautiful green place, but a desert.So they overworked a few aspects of the game (like recource gains etc) but kept alot of the known game mechanics (Museum, Dungeon, Mine etc), so you will feel right at home.For Players who not know the My Time at - Serie.This is a nice farm and crafting game, the strong point of this Game is def. the Crafting.Like in most such game you have a different variety of Fighting, Gathering, Farming/Planting and Fishing to keep you occupied.I think the strong point of the Game is the Story, while you progress you contiue to unlock more things to farm and craft so it never feels like a grind, wich sadly other games tend to feel like.The Game gets more complex as your progress, but you learn all there is though tutorial Quests so it is not a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting over 130+ hours into the story I finally feel comfortable enough to leave a review. It's a fantastic game with a story that is way better then it should be. When the game play loop starts to get stale they add new areas and tasks that keep the game fresh. Is there a grind at times, sure. But the characters and the story keep you coming back for more. The new pet update has been an fresh and interesting addition to the game and has added a new twist to the combat. The combat isn't the greatest, but it doesn't need to be in a game like this where it is more about the journey and characters you meet along the way. Overall, it is a game that is bigger the Portia. Has a ton of amazing characters and content. And can be played at a speed runners pace or taken slow over hundreds of hours. This was one of my favorite games I have ever played and I implore others to experience this game to its fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Every time I play,  I love this game more. More and more and more. I feel like other farming/crafting type games have no more excuses. There's ALWAYS something to do. So many quests, immersive festivals, mini games, dungeons, combat, etc. etc. I really feel like, for the amount of content there is, the price of this game is a steal. I'm going to have hundred of hours, I can tell. Plus, the desert/Western aesthetic is such a fun aesthetic. Just an endlessly good time. As I get deeper and discover more about the lore, I realize just how much the dev's love this game they've made. It really shows.I have 4 hours in this on PC and 11 on Switch. Switch version is rough, and I still was obsessed with it. Enough so that I had to buy it on PC to have the best experience and it was so worth it. In my opinion, the game on PC is worth more than the asking price. It's big, beautiful, diverse, and really brings a new perspective to the "farming game." I did not play My Time at Portia, but I've heard this is an improvement. I cannot say enough great things, as someone who is new to this series. I just want to keep going. I love the story and worldbuilding and the fact that this takes place in a post-apocalyptic community. Extra kudos to the mining which is definitely my favorite mining system in a "cozy" game so far. It feels so dynamic AND you get a jetpack. Overall, a game I can't wait to sink hundred of hours into (because I will).

_childDocuments_.review: You have ominous phrases like "bringing telesis to Sandrock" and that we are living life after the "Day of Calamity", but then you end up in a world that is more like something created by a suburban housewife.I just really wish whoever writes/designs these games would be more tasteful and ambitious across the board. I started playing this, and the bad vibes of immature writing from Portia came back right away, and I just don't want to experience that again. In both games, it always feels like someone says you are living in a post-apocalyptic world with ancient ruins, but then in reality you end up in conversations with people that are like "I lost my glasses" and "gee whiz, I love burgers". Starting off, you have this animal card game you can play against people, and the animal card game is, I'm sorry, really slow and infantile, barely disguised rock paper scissors. This is a sequel to a successful game and I really want to see some kind of improvement on the drawbacks of Portia in terms of world-building and immaturity (where it felt so suburban and major themes in the writing weren't really developed at all), but I don't see any hope here. I played a lot of Portia and I am just not on board for this again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is well done and very addicting especially once you find your rhythm of crafting and gathering. Probably the best feature of the game is how they handle inventory and storage. You can craft at any worktable/machine from items that are in any chests and you can turn in quests anywhere on the map with items that are in your chests at home. You can also push a button to store and sort items from your inventory into matching items that are in any of your chests. This is the best QOL feature of the game imo since inventory management in other games is a pain so I'm glad Sandrock is doing it right.

_childDocuments_.review: As an Early Access game, My Time at Sandrock is looking good. Drawing from previous titles from Pathea such as Planet Explorers and My Time at Portia (which this is a sequel of), MTAS is their most polished and solid project yet.Although there is still some time until its done, the game already features enough content to draw a good picture that this is a great sequel to MTAP. The game looks, sounds and behaves much better than previous games, and Pathea is clearly serious about making good Crafting/Gathering/Life Sim games - very similar to Stardew Valley, but expanded upon.My biggest gripe with Portia (the previous game) was its prototype-looking, console-intended UI. Here, it was completely replaced by a sleeker UI. Actually, the whole game engine was replaced.Some simple QoL features such as the game automatically selecting the quantity of items to be crafted based on the amount required for a mission or a larger Assembly project is just neat. Many ideas or suggestions from the community clearly have been incorporated or taken into account.Gameplay-wise, it feels like a 'harder' (in terms of economy) but smoother MTAP, where the townsfolk are nice and looking forward to a bright future. In the previous game, I had a hard time relating or caring about most (if not all) characters, as most of them presented some weird attitude at some point or another. Here, folks are generally glad you're around and most know you're just trying to fit in and support their sand-filled boring hole of a town, so it feels like a chillier and cozier experience than before.I do have to mention that although all the positives from a Pathea game appears here, all the negatives also do. Sucks to say it, but most of their games feel "rough around the edges" and feature a certain amount of jank. Although clear work has been put into making Sandrock smoother and polished, there is still some janky animations here and there (usually on combat), clunky enemy behavior, and some other minor issues.Although this is to be expected from Early Access, I've seen on two projects I've followed from them that such things may end up left behind. Portia had a lot of janky animations, cutscenes, missing sounds and weirdness that was left unaddressed - hopefully they will take these on seriously, as MTAS has the potential to be much bigger than Portia.A crucial positive point to bring up is: Multiplayer is being tested, It Just Works, and it's a different "game" than Singleplayer. Not only is it another client, Multiplayer features a separate story with separate features intended for Co-Op play only. I'm unsure whether it will be like this in the future, but I love the fact that the Co-Op story happens some years before the Singleplayer story. Although its not really built upon at the moment, playing Singleplayer and Multiplayer paints a larger picture of the town and its story, and I really like to see it all working so well. Even during the current playtest (which isn't even the actual Multiplayer Early Access release yet), Multiplayer has worked flawlessly.Of course, it lacks the amount of content and features available on SP, but already allows us to see that it will be an amazing multiplayer game - its greatness only limited by how much time and effort the devs are spent on it.Here's hoping no stupid microtransactions will appear (such as lootboxes, benefits, extra-exp packs... DON'T do a Fallout 76 here if you don't want to utterly destroy your goodwill), but paid DLCs and additional Singleplayer and Multiplayer content would be easily applied and welcomed here.Other than that, I'm excited again over the universe of this "My Time series" (as the devs call it). I'm also looking forward to Planet Explorers 2 for probably over a decade, and the good work they do here will directly reflect on PE2.I wish them good luck on yet another big endeavor, and would say it's definitely worth trying. For those who like both Singleplayer and Co-Op crafting games, you're nearly getting 2 games for the price of one.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend, this game rivals my all time favorite Stardew Valley. Similar mechanics and foundation to My Time at Portia, but vastly improved graphics and play-ability. I have found all the characters interesting and fun to talk to, missions engaging and thoughtful, and gameplay smooth and cohesive.I've had this game since Christmas last year (so most of my hours were in early access) and the game has only been improved with full release. When I came across a game breaking bug in the afternoon, it was fixed by the next morning. Pathea has outdone themselves. I have something like 280 hours played (230 hours on my main file) and am close to completing the main story, but not quite there yet.I love time sink games like this and the only con I can think of is that sometimes it takes a while to load a new area (exiting the house, going into a dungeon, etc). _childDocuments_.review: It took me 114hrs to finish the (early-access) main story line AND to get the doctor to go on a date with me. Our first date was during a sandstorm. Is that relevant to this review? No. But we still managed to make it romantic, and that's what matters to me.I've followed Pathea from My Time at Portia to My Time at Sandrock. There were many issues with Portia that I was willing to overlook because I loved the story, but while this isn't a review of Portia, I think it's important to have played both games to judge Sandrock on its own merit. It's hard to forget how Portia updates were so quickly forgotten the second this game was announced.Sandrock has a lot of promise, and I'm excited to see it finish. The characters are very well fleshed out, the progression isn't overly-grindy for the sort of genre it falls into, and it's easy to just tell yourself "one more day" just like you did when you first played Stardew Valley.I'm excited to see where this game goes, and I'm cautiously optimistic that they're going to stick to their guns and see this project through to the end instead of abandoning like they did to My Time at Portia. I want to know how it ends, I want to have a more meaningful relationship with my new love interest, and I *really* want to punch whoever has been trying to run Sandrock into the ground.Temporary 9/10 for the current progress. I was tempted to add points for certain cameos from Portia just out of nostalgia, but we have to be fair here.Please keep up the good work and don't disappoint us. That's really all I'm asking.Well, that. And to let me marry Fang.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, runs smooth, story's about as good as a Chinese company can make and then half-bake into English. Gameplay loop is satisfying as well, with either farming and gathering or combat, crafting, building. The world is... Well, about as nice as a desert can be, and you can make it a bit less... desert-y by decorating, at least your plot of land, your house, your farms. Character customization is..... Decent. Base models are expandable enough, plus you can swap out clothes pretty easily, if not a little... grindy, and there's a pretty decent variety as far as things go, nothing groundbreaking but at least nice enough.However.We all knew the price was going to hike up a bit on full release, but in addition to that, they waited until after release to drop all the DLC, a very disappointing half-step that the players definitely should have known better about before the game released. If I'd known there was gonna be DLC aafter release, I would have thought twice about even getting it. However, honestly it's still a really solid package, and some dinky cosmetics aren't going to really make or break your gameplay in most cases.The game is probably a 7/10, it would have been an 8, however I'm not one to take this game's early-access transition DLC hat-trick lightly.If you like farming and gathering, decorating and just general life-simmery, I would recommend you get it at a discount, It's 40 USD on release but I would get it for 30 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is the follow up game to My Time at Portia although you do not need to play Portia first in order to have fun with Sandrock since it is its own story within the same world. In both Portia and Sandrock you play as new builder in town and the main mechanic of the game is building items to complete commissions. My advice to new players is to change the day length to long when first starting and to take your time completing missions that do not have a time limit. Don't rush the story and take time to get to know the residents, fish, relic hunt, and gather materials. The game can easily overwhelm new players if they trying to rush to complete too much and there is always something to do in this game so just take it easy and enjoy!10/10 I wholeheartedly recommend this game to everyone and anyone!

_childDocuments_.review: It's sort of halfway between a sequel and an expansion. The graphics have been much improved, and it's got a new setting, but the gameplay is almost untouched.That said, they have smoothed off a lot of the rough edges on Portia. Mining in the abandoned ruins notably got an upgrade, it feels more like an adventure now. And they've added the card game "critters" as a way of building relationships(It plays as a cross between scissors-paper-rock and poker).Somethings actually got smaller. The town is smaller and there are fewer NPCs. BUT this generally keeps confusion to a minimum, as none of the NPCs seem like filler and the town is easier to navigate.All that said, the game isn't finished. The story line feels roughly 40%. It also has CPU bound performance issues(maybe single-threaded?), so if you play now, expect the fps to bounce between 45 and 90 fps even on high-end systems. (variable refresh monitors help a lot)

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is a very fun and relaxing farming sim and is the sequel to My Time at Portia. The game is in early access, so there are some bugs in the game. However, the devs are constantly working on the game which makes the game enjoyable.I enjoy the crafting aspect of the game and progressing the story. However, there is farming and combat in the game. The combat is pretty solid and the farming is a little tedious but once you get use to it, it can become fun as well. One of the cool features about My Time at Sandrock is that there is a lot of voice over so if your streaming the game, you don't have to do a ton of reading and I really appreciate that. Overall, if you are into farming sims, then I highly recommend picking up My Time at Sandrock.

Relationship system is good too (I personally like how you can choose what kind of relationship you have with the romanceable characters based on choices, so if there is a character you want to be just friend with, you totally can).Oh and also for those who like decorating, the house in My Time at Sandrock has a lot more freedom for decorating, where you choose how many rooms ti has, how big they are, windows,doors and so on, so you can build just a simple house or a 4 floors mansion if you so like. (for those who aren't good at decorating, there is a book with a list of pre-amde houses made by other players you can buy in game which let to build them with the only requirement of having enough space and money).

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like My Time at Portia? If so you'll find a lot to like here.Unlike Portia I've been impressed so far with how the game runs. Obviously there will be bugs given it is in early access, but overall it is a more polished experience than its predecessor and through 30 or so hours the game only crashed on me once. If you played My Time at Portia you know how significant an improvement that is!My gripes to this point mainly involve the pacing and innovation. It took a bit too long to get through the beginning stages of the game to the point where I almost bounced off it between the 5-10 hour range. There is a lot to discover but in the early going the game can get a bit too dull and grindy.As far as innovation is concerned...Sandrock certainly differentiates itself from Portia as a location and there are a bunch of new characters to meet, but the gameplay itself is EXTREMELY similar to Portia. I wasn't necessarily expecting them to reinvent the wheel with the sequel, but there is honestly not a lot you will do on a day-to-day basis in this game that plays all that different from My Time at Portia. That could be why the beginning stages of the game have a bit too much of that "been there, done that" feel.Building Mode also needs a TON of work, and the UI could do with some serious simplification. It took a couple hours until I was comfortable just moving items around my inventory.I know these are quite a few complaints but since the game just released in EA I'm willing to give the devs some time to flesh out the experience and make it stand out compared to Portia. I'll still give this a thumbs up as I am definitely enjoying it, but it there is no question that Sandrock still needs quite a bit of TLC before it elevates itself properly from its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early on at just under 10 hours. I know this game is very long! I've heard there are three acts and it will take over 100 easily to complete them all.This game manages to stand apart from other sort of 'chore' games like Stardew Valley, Rune Factory, and so on. This game focuses on crafting machines rather than farming, although farming does exist. The crafting is fairly complex, and there are lots of different machines that you can create that will help you make more and more parts to create even more things. The complexity is staggering even 10 hours in. I have 5 more 6 machines and have barely scratched the surface of the book of craft-able things. Furthermore, my machines have upgrade paths. The more you unlock, the more flexibility you have in crafting more things. You can craft multiple tiers of weapons that you can use to fight enemies or craft new clothes, furniture, etc. There are an endless number of requests to craft things for money, reputation and items.As for other chores you will be doing? There are arcade mini games that can help you get items, there are dungeons to explore and ruins to mine out for ore and data discs. Data Discs are used at the research lab to help research new blueprints for more machines.Now, townspeople and relationships. This game has a LOT of NPCs. Everyone has voiced dialog which is impressive. The game also inundates you with tons of events in the main story and outside the main story as well. Anyone can date anyone regardless of gender, so pick who you like. I think there's an absurd amount of romanceable options, like 21.  From what I've seen the townspeople are fun, and there's a lot of different personality types. Some people come off very distant, but I'm certain will warm up to you if you raise their affection. I haven't even touched the social aspects of the game, but if you like creating gifts and raising affection, you are going to be very busy. There are machines for cooking meals, and you can farm or raise animals for other unique items.Did I mention that as you gain experience doing various tasks, you'll be getting skill points to invest in a variety of different skill trees? There is a skill tree for gathering, there's one for social relationships, one for crafting and even more I can't even remember off the top of my head.If you like collecting, there's also things you can dig up in the ruins and offer up to the museum.One last notable thing to mention is the story. Well, the main story is very long and you will always have a main task to work on if you want to advance. The premise of the game is that you are in a small desert town built on the ruins of an ancient, advanced civilization. One of the dungeons you can explore is like a giant skyscraper that was buried in the sand and no one knows how tall it is, because they haven't dug to the bottom floor yet. That's our job. There's also a sidestory with a bandit gang involving a person who used to be a member of the town but went 'crazy'.Anyway, it's a HIGHLY ambitious game that you can really sink your teeth into. It's got so many layered systems that I never know exactly what I'm going to be doing day-to-day. It's a long road - perhaps one might call it a tremendous grind!- but it's a satisfying one.

_childDocuments_.review: The #1 issue with this game is bloat. According to the devs, the story is 3.29 times longer than My Time at Portia – already a pretty long game, mind you. I know “more game” is supposed to be good, but Sandrock overstays its welcome and makes you wonder when it finally ends. Imagine watching a movie, and after an epic showdown with the main villain, when you’re ready for the credits to roll - another movie begins instead. It means you need many hours of your life to complete the story in one sitting and not lose track of it. There are more than twice side quests than Portia, too - and most of them are on a timer. I ended up so overwhelmed by quests that I began refusing them at some point, which in turn led to a frustrating feeling of missing out on content. There is more of everything else as well. There are hundreds of items - scrap alone comes in like 15 varieties - making inventory management an ever-present annoying part of the gameplay. If a developer from Pathea is reading this - I would like you to grab a sheet of paper, write “Less is More” on it, then hang it somewhere in the office where everyone can see it every day. I have no need for 20 romantic interests in the game, if the majority of them will lack character, quests, unique items, voice acting... Give me just 3 but make them really fleshed out and rich with content. Case in point: Nia - she got so much backstory, relevance to the plot, unique events and ties to the main character that she makes every other romance look like an unnecessary waste of development resources.Sandrock is a heavily narrative-driven game. For 100-150 hours you will be listening to dialogue with multiple people, constantly referencing your character. For some reason, even though your character is not a “blank slate” and has a backstory, parents, childhood friend etc. you are free to name him/her whatever you want. This creates a huge problem for voice actors. You see, expecting them to voice dozens of custom names like Codsworth or Vasco would be unrealistic, so they only had two options - either skip the player character’s name entirely, or to use generic “the Builder”. As a result, dialogue constantly loses meaning and feels jarring. For example, “Me, Harris and you will go to the cave” turns into “Me and you will go to the cave”; “S.S. Harris” (ship name) turns into “S.S.” (???), and even though you can be a best friend to people and marry them, they will still refer to you as “the Builder” (even if there are other builders present in the same scene). What exacerbates this issue is the silent protagonist. Which on its own perhaps wouldn’t be that bad - if Mi-an didn’t exist. Mi-an is also a Builder, and so in most scenes she effectively speaks for both of you and ends up praised for things you did. All leading to a feeling of the player character being a sidekick to Mi-an. While I realize voicing the whole 250.000 words main story is unrealistic, this just leads back to my point - why did they write a huge story like that?Sandrock feels awfully derivative - it just grabs about every single gameplay element and design decision from Portia and carefully copy/pastes them into a new game. The only meaningful difference here is the new desert setting, and frankly - it’s terrible and doesn’t work for a game like this. You will struggle to tell the seasons apart - it’s always just sand, with the (very) subtle coat of white in Winter and green in Spring. Outside of an occasional sandstorm the weather is also static for the most part – you will not see any snow and I only witnessed rain 1 (one!) time after 100+ hours into the game. Of course, there are setting-based complications: like you need water (rare and expensive) to cool your machines; sand accumulates on them over time so you need to clean it; you are not allowed to chop trees near the city etc. However, ultimately all of it feels like busywork, aimed at making your early game more painful and tedious than it needs to be.Narratively, it’s just a mix of every Wild West cliché. Your will hear “Howdy!” from about every character, even the newcomers. There are sheriffs, bandits, cowb... I mean, Yakboys. Which I could probably live with, but the huge appeal of a My Time game is to be able to improve your community and see a meaningful impact of your actions over time. I still remember building a fast travel system in Portia and how much of an achievement it felt. Here the main theme is greenification of the desert however, which essentially makes you feel like a sidekick to botanist characters and a glorified gardener, as the Builder stuff takes a backstage to planting trees. Furthermore, the first half of the exceedingly long story just has you doing barely meaningful stuff, with the common theme being “bandits broke our bench/water tower/farm/statue - please repair it!”. Yes, there are guns now - but they feel like a gimmick, requiring entering an “aiming” mode, and are so ammo-hungry that using them is just not sustainable, unless you enjoy grinding mines to make more bullets. You do get the ability to join Civil Corps as a Deputy this time round, but ultimately this only serves to further distract you into becoming a “jack of all trades”.Sandrock tries to be more of an RPG, with everything from your chair to your horse coming in multiple tiers of quality. You can also “refine” an item to increase its level and quality by throwing rare gems you first have to grind at it. At first I thought this to be a very cool system, as I imagined it would be possible to upgrade any piece of clothing indefinitely and make it competitive in the late game - but you’re only able to upgrade anything up to 10 levels above its “required level”, making the system pointless. Furthermore, this system only made matters worse as for the first half of the game I had to actively avoid the “blue” quality commissions - because I simply did not have the required gems at the time to make such quality items.Also, while there are levels and skill points – you will easily unlock everything provided you play long enough, so there are no builds or anything like that. The perks are subtle buffs rather than something that has great impact over the gameplay. As such, the main form of progression comes in the form of gear - and is fully tied to the main story, which unlocks more areas and resources. While you unlock Bronze and Iron relatively early on and at a steady pace, it is unfortunately followed by a very long and stale midgame where you don’t unlock anything until late game, where you get Chromium and Aluminum almost back to back.Sandrock is filled to the brim with memes and popular culture references, and every quest title is an attempt at a witty pun. It all looks quaint and fun at first, but quickly grows exhausting, especially as the writers make NPC go more and more out of character just to throw in another “Mic drop!”. The writing feels too concerned with the “current day” agenda for a game that’s supposed to take place in a post apocalyptic setting. For example, a woman I offered my help said she does not accept “free help” from strangers, and almost reported me for sexual harassment. And after that a homosexual man made advances on my male character without my consent, or ever speaking to that particular character to begin with. Some characters are so obnoxious I found it really hard to co-exist with them in the same game.My time at Sandrock was almost 200 hours full of adventure and emotions. Just like Portia, this game has quite a few enjoyable things. Pretty graphics, some quality of life additions, even the optimization is finally half-decent! Unfortunately, all the diamonds are buried deeply under the sand of a game that is too ambitious for its own good.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: We were having a lot of fun with Portia, and Sandrock is even more of that. Gameplay is really improved and managing resources is less of a chore and more of a system you learn. Characters are nicely fleshed out for the most part, though you can see who the dev favourites are. And there's enough to do that you have to manage your tasks, but rarely drown in them, and still have some days when you can catch up.The story is a cosy-cartoonish one, but still has a solid and interesting core of important issues and problems in it. And the environmental message as a theme is really interesting, especially since Portia didn't have much of that. Social dynamics and things to do for and with NPCs are fun to experience, and the romancing system is a lot better than in Portia, with the NPCs in question interacting with your character on their own, not just waiting to be interacted with. There are some issues with controls, especially on PC, but nothing gamebreaking. Some characters and story elements are shaky and not very fun to interact with, but they're few and far between. We were very happy with the game before it got a ton of touchups, and even pre-launch, and now it's way more fun and a great leisure time-waster. _childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a farming sim type game because of Stardew Valley and came across this one. I had never played 'My Time in Portia' tho I know this is the 2nd in the series. So, I'm going to do my best not to spoil it for anyone.Its got fabulous graphics, fun battle effects and fulfills all my garden, base building, farming, cooking, and crafting check boxes. There are romance-able characters in this game just like Stardew. You can even challenge people in town to duels for fun. You can do dungeons that pay out in different currency for unique gear. They have sand fishing for those that aren't into farming and it is a much more accessible form of fishing because I straight up sucked at fishing in Stardew.The characters you come across in Sandrock are very engaging and have unique personalities. The MSQ I have completed so far is also great and feels pretty well paced. They have cool seasonal events, one in particular I wish was available year round. Even better, pets have now become available :DCrafting in this game is pretty awesome, they have some quality of life features I hope will be adopted by other games. One really big plus when base building, is that you can get a full refund when you destroy something like doors, windows, accessories that aren't part of the original house and size. Complete refund. So nice! So if you add something to your house you don't like later on and remove it, instant refund. Not to be confused with furniture--just housing decor and base expansion.If I did have a gripe about this game? Um maybe more wall decor options? Maybe the ability to dye gear? Maybe a pet stand for Coco? They don't have any pet furniture for birds yet.All in all, can't wait for the next content update! Looks like a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 Review update:After nearly 2 years of allowing for Pathea to address issues I and others brought forward, I decided to revisit the game and see what's changed. Not much. I do appreciate that a representative addressed my last review, but unfortunately, many of the issues I had previously stated involving day length, resource gathering, stamina and general gameplay remain even today.- Voice acting is terrible, at least in English. Cut outs, obnoxious variations in speech volume during spoken conversation parts, random failures for interactions to engage properly and speaking styles mismatched with their character counterparts make the game really hard to stay immersed in.- Machine translations are terrible, stop using them in the final product. At the very least, pay native writers with at least a 5th grade understanding of their native language to re-translate and correct mispronunciations. - Continuity. The game has none. Players not using mods may feel this less, but alas, after 20 hours of banging my head against the wall playing vanilla, trying to get enough resources to complete the easiest quests, and being time, level, progression, and gohl gated to hell and beyond, I gave in. With mods the progression stoppages are much more present, leading to days where, if the story doesn't progress upon awakening, you may as well just go back to bed.- Movement. The base game movement speed is atrocious. Stuck either walking slow enough that dead snails are passing you like you're standing still, or jogging at a slightly faster rate, early game takes forever to get anywhere. In a game where even the slowest time settings cause the in game day to pass far too quickly, I was really hoping this issue would be addressed and fixed.- Gathering. Base game gathering is just as frustrating and unenjoyable as it was in 2022. With no base stamina restoration, taking six to eight swings to break a rock or shrub for the two or three units of RNG'd  resources you get from them feels more like punitive labor than recreational gameplay. This is better with mods, but you have to be careful, else you wind up bloated with mats you won't be able to use fast enough and gameplay becomes boring for completely different reasons. Early game machines are still over complicated for the stage of game, still require heavily RNG'd resources to create, and still require ridiculous amounts of time to process materials. I don't have a side by side comparison, but I doubt anything was done to address this. As well, the best "quality" machines don't do much more than the base level per set, even upgraded to their max versions. Pathea did this and resource gathering much better in Portia, I truly do not understand why they chose to Duvos this release as badly as they did. I thought that was an April Fool's joke. Relationships. Seriously, Pathea? Either the NPCs are throwing themselves at the player, or refusing every advance. Half the romanceable characters are locked behind end game content, leave or are otherwise unavailable for most of the game. This was bad enough with the I think three? in Portia, but you went whole hog this time.Factory and greenhouse are pointless. As little as they do, and as late in the game as you obtain them, and with their extremely limited functionality, there is no reason to have them. At all.Combat mechanics could be better. I get really tired of facing an enemy right in front of me, hitting the attack button, and watching my character attack the air behind him.The freestyle build function is a fun idea, but poorly implemented, with nothing in the way of a tutorial on how to use it, leaving players to stumble through the process. I find the roofing portion to be especially aggravating, for too many reasons to list here.The story directly contradicts lore established in Portia, particularly concerning the end of the old world and Duvos.Character/NPC sizing. I have a 5 year old niece that would be taller than many of the adults in this game. Seriously, even midgets are taller. While we're on the subject, body customizations. Come on, even cheesy F2P (word that rhymes with corn) games have this. TL;DR: With mods, the game can be very enjoyable. I'm sure some find it just as enjoyable without them. The same ones that got a kick out of eating Tide Pods. Personally, I play games to feel rewarded and escape reality, not to recreate reality in a fantasy setting. Base game is much more chore list and less fantasy adventure than any game should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Ridiculously good. It's "3D Stardew Valley" but with a workshop instead of a farm. The amount of content (without DLC!) is absurd. Around 80 or 90 hours I remember thinking 'Well, I finished that <big plot point>,' I guess I'm about done with the game except for a little bit of cleaning up. Nope. It keeps going. And going. And going. And going. You get more than your money's worth of content.There's one other reason I particularly like this (and Portia, get Portia first!) and that's because it offers direction, unlike Stardew Valley. I love SDV! Who doesn't? But I tend to find that my own initiative usually isn't enough to play forever. I rarely even finish the community center. I just get bored with no direction. Portia and Sandrock have an actual story. You can still go at your own pace (a few side quests have time limits, I think, but I don't think the main quests do) and take as long as you want to build up your workshop and house and everything else, but if you're like me and need someone to say 'Okay, now do this thing next' then having a story is great.The game is also surprisingly funny and well written. The plot is a little generic, but there were a handful of twists I didn't see coming - and again, it lasts forever. The universe itself is fairly interesting and there's a good bit of story to it aside from just Sandrock itself - there's clearly a lot of thought put into the world in which your character lives.I really don't have a lot of negatives. Ran into maybe a handful of bugs over 112 hours. Who cares, nothing that destroyed the game and a reload inevitably fixed it. AAA games are worse than that. A handful of quests aren't voice acted, but so what? Most are.It also runs fine on a steam deck (had to turn the graphics down a bit to keep the frame rate up). Played start to finish on mine. Absolutely worth buying if you like this kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a 'not sure' recommendation but...The game is generally good, the story works well and flows okay for the most part, mechanics make sense, though some aspects will require a look at the in-game help as the first descriptions may not give all the information you need...With 200 hours at the time of writing, I have 'completed' the game and enjoyed my time in Sandrock...But it's the cosmetic DLCs, available on, or shortly after, release, that total more than one and a half times the price of the base game...  Some of the DLCs come in three parts - each one giving a costume for four of the characters (And three addition recolours of the same costume.)  Why does it take THREE DLCs just to give the main NPCs a beach outfit each?It's not enough to turn my opinion negative, but certainly has made it less of a positive one...Tl;DR - Good base game, don't bother with the DLCs unless you have that money to spare and don't mind considering it a donation to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved My Time and Portia and so far, Sandrock has taken the concept of Portia and upped the gun on it.Why I love this game series isn't because of the gameplay or design, though those are major perks, but it is the atmosphere. You are told pretty early in both games you're in a post-apocalyptic scenario, where a dark age of corruption and technology destroyed the world. Instead of the hopeless and despair you've seen in other games, though there is elements of it in the 'My Times At' series, there is a hopeful atmosphere and instead of giving into that despair or likely anger from all that has happened, you see people trying to rebuild one step at a time.I love that because it is such a refreshing take on the genre and the story is captivating, the more we learn about the Age of Corruption and the time before Peach, the more I want to discover and find out! Plus the fact you're told in both games that it is NOT all sunshine and rainbows (the issue with Duvos and Lucien for example) there is a resilience where those that have faced hardship are working to make something better, which captures the spirit of being a Builder so perfectly. So, thanks Devs- thanks for making this world and I cannot wait to see what else you do!

_childDocuments_.review: I spent probably a hundred hours on My Time at Portia, and I loved every minute of it. Unfortunately, after playing My Time at Sandrock, I probably won't be able to go back. Sandrock takes the good things about Portia and makes it better, and the quality of life changes fix many of the things that were frustrating about Portia. In Sandrock, customizing your house and yard are much easier, farming is more interesting, resource management is more rewarding, the NPCs are more interesting and diverse. Additionally, even though I've clocked over thirty hours of playtime, I have not reached the end of the Early Access content yet. I look forward to seeing how Sandrock develops as it moves through Early Access (because there is certainly content missing (e.g., romance quests, marriage, children, etc.)), but the game is absolutely worth buying and playing now. It's quickly becoming one of my favorites.
