_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed with the state Coral Island had been released in, so I asked people on the subreddit if there were other games I should play instead. A few people suggested Sandrock - and now over 100 hours later I wish I could meet each of them in person to thank them for pointing me in the direction of this game.I tried Portia once, didn’t like it, and assumed I wouldn’t like this. Especially because I’m not usually a fan of desert/cowboy aesthetics. But the heart and uniqueness the world and characters have is so endearing and well-realized that I fell in love pretty quickly. The gameplay loop itself is very satisfying, very much its own thing (you could never call this another Stardew ripoff like most other games in this genre). I personally changed the time setting to 0.8 because I like a more chill experience and this worked amazingly well for me. Tons to do, tons to work toward, but never felt stressed or overwhelmed. The story and town progression are surprisingly long. It takes a lot of cool twists and turns and I still haven’t gotten to the end at over 100 hours!Every character is worth maxing out and getting to know because the writing is so good, genuinely funny, and at times surprisingly deep and emotional. Good luck picking a romance candidate because they’re all awesome (I ended up going with Mi-An, but it was a hard choice). Is it a technically perfect game? No. There are definitely bugs here and there. I suggest saving often, however updates and fixes are always being rolled out. Point is, I have rarely played a game where the dev’s passion, heart and love ooze out of every frame. This game has helped me with my anxiety and put me in a good mood more times than I can count. I will now be following everything this studio does and cannot wait for Evershine. If you’re disillusioned by all the Stardew clones, or even if you just want to play a great game, just get it!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Early access is early access, but this is looking like, when it's finished, it's going to be an improvement over Portia in pretty much every way.PROS- Kept everything that made Portia great- Improved graphics- Improved combat- Slightly more crafting depth- Interesting new challenges to do with being in a desert, like managing your water supply- Main rival is someone who's friendly this time, rather than antagonistic (wasn't bad before, but I prefer this)- Although I don't fully know how it'll pan out because the story isn't done yet, the main villain seems to be more interesting so far in Sandrock than the one in Portia wasCONS- Story and non-starting zones not finished yet (totally reasonable for an early-access game that came out only a week ago)- Some wonky stuff with activating items/doors/etc when not _directly_ facing them or when multiple options are very close together- Which lines are voiced and which aren't isn't super straightforward, but I assume this has something to do with not all the lines being recorded yet (same deal as the story not being fully implemented)

_childDocuments_.review: I missed out on playing My Time at Portia, so I cannot compare it to that.  Instead, I can compare this game to others in this genre such as Harvest Moon, Rune Factory and Stardew Valley.  This game is fantastic, even in early access stages.  The characters have depth, making it fun and rewarding to engage with them and develop friendships.  There are lots of missions and tasks for those who like to have goals (vs freestyle Animal Crossing type of play).  I love the combat system, especially being able to craft weapons, improve fighting skills and get comfortable with my weapons of choice.  The music is good, the graphics and game environment are wonderful.  I love the seasonal events- they are interactive and actually fun.  Most of all, I enjoy the characters.  Some of them are so hilarious.  IMO, I have not enjoyed characters this well developed in this game genre in years.  This game is well worth the money.  I highly recommend it, even in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: If you had fun with My Time at Portia then you will enjoy this even more. New place and new people and with still some links to Portia, I found the pace much more relaxed.With the building aspect easier to manage, once the money starts coming in the water ration part becomes easier as well to the point I almost forgot about it. They also made quite a few changes from the beta side to 1.0 and it's been a nice surprise to find these little extras as I play through the main story line. They made sure that you are never truly stuck in your progress as if you can't reach the new mine area yet, check the junkyard and recycle the scrapes. You will soon be getting the last materials needed for the current main quest project. As to the ever present sandstorms, well they improved on that as well but I wouldn't spoil on how as it's nice to found out in the game, just a side note the enraged beasts do level with your character so they will still present a challenge.With the other changes to house building to now have a bigger line of style options, I'm sure more then a few people have posted their in game homes, so take a look to see what may inspire you in your own home set-up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything and more of its predecessor, my time at Portia, the conservation of water fits the theme of being in a desert and feels natural. The characters all are kind and lively and makes you feel as if you really are part of a community. The story is engaging and makes you want to see it through to the end, though because it is still in development the story is not yet finished but worth it all the same. The crafting and combat are fun and easy to get used to, and the dungeons and enemies are interesting as well. I have yet to try the multiplayer and i'm not sure if i will get the chance to try it until later but the concept is something i can agree will make this game even more fun. if you enjoy simulation and crafting games with the option of meeting characters and befriending or romancing them i highly recommend this game and its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I tried to spend enough time playing to get a good comparison against My Time at Portia for those that were interested and wanted to know how it fared against the predecessor or prequel or whatever else you'd like to call that installment in this franchise.Graphics, Models, Textures:My first impression when opening the game for the very first time was "Wow". It sound stupid but it was easy to tell this was already pretty polished for an early access game when you compared it to Portia. Portia was a great game but the features I always found lacking at times were the graphics and character models. Some other minor stuff felt very grindy and repetitive but overall I loved the game. In this game, which of course this is still in development, the graphics are already substantially better. Even the cut-scenes feel more polished and less choppy to watch than they were in Portia (and even then they were perfectly fine in my opinion). The landscaping and plants feel more detailed and have better modeling though I don't think it's a major difference. The character models are a noticeable improvement. While Portia had a nice style and the quirkier designs felt appropiate for the game, these take a step towards more proportional features and realism that still stay in the same style. The voice acting while not completely implemented for all the characters or all dialogue is considerably higher quality and the lip syncing to their character's mouth movements lines up pretty well. In Portia this wasn't the case, the character's mouths usually stopped talking before the audio finished playing. The textures in this game like the modelling are a noticeable improvement but not in a major way. All things considered, it's an all around improvement even when in Early Access.Soundtrack:The soundtrack is... amazing. I like it a lot. I'm from the south in America so hearing the soundtrack reminds me of home and represents the aesthetic of Sandrock pretty well. I don't have a lot else to say but the audio quality is good and I don't find it annoying. I think it fits the theme pretty well.Gameplay, Mechanics, Etc:The gameplay is overall pretty much the same as Portia so if you liked Portia and were worried this would be a lot different then fear not, you'll like this just as much if not more. The crafting still feels a bit grindy to me but I'm also still learning how to craft everything and all the locations for items needed. I think in this kind of game though, it's always going to have that "grinding" aspect if you're trying to rush the storyline or complete a lot of commissions at once. The combat system is roughly the same but it feels less like a hack and slash. You still hack and slash and dodge their attacks but the weapon variety is larger and it incorporates a few more 'RPG' aspects like guard meters where you can break their defense for a better window or blocking to reduce damage. The happiest change I can notice is sprinting doesn't consume stamina. Feels like such a minor thing to say that but it was a relief not having to worry about stamina in that regard. Right now, the world is still pretty limited for me but given that I'm still early in the story (I assume) and that only the first part of the story is complete, that was to be expected. Regardless, it's still a pretty big area to explore and the space doesn't feel wasted. In Portia, I felt like some things were *too* far apart. This is scaled in a better way that feels more realistic and not wasting an unnecessary amount of time.At the time I'm writing this, I'm one or two days away in the game from unlocking farming so I'll be editing that into this review later to let you know my thoughts on it.Character Customization:Like I said, the character models are better and so is the customization. It's not a huge overwhelming improvement in my personal opinion but I actually enjoy the way my avatar looks without a severe amount of tweaking. It has a lot more adjusters and sliders or it feels that way compared to Portia so I think it's an improvement that deserves some credit. If I had to complain about it, I'd like more hairstyles and especially more facial hair options but honestly it's still good regardless. I'd imagine there's a possibility they could incorporate more like that in the future.Final Thoughts & Summarized:If you're still unsure if you want to play this game because you never played Portia, then just buy Portia. It's cheaper than this (or it's on sale while I'm writing this review at least). It's a complete game and it's roughly the same. If you enjoy it a lot and want more, then get this. I think if you know that you want this game eventually but you're afraid of committing until you see a review on the final product then you'll have to decide whether or not this is right for you. I think all things considered, the gameplay I have available to me right now for the $25.00 price mark is approaching being worth it. Even more so knowing that when the game is completed I already own it from Early Access. There's been a few minor bugs like I've noticed maybe ... 2? Nothing game breaking, happened so fast I almost didn't realize it. Overall, if you're a returning fan then grab a copy. If you're not, maybe try their first game if the review wasn't enough to convince you.PS: For what it's worth, if you've played Stardew Valley and loved it and that's what drew you to this game, odds are you'll like it. Similiar aspects in different ways with a bigger world and more things to do I feel like.

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND if you are a fan of Stardew Valley, Sims, and Animal Crossing!My Time at Sandrock gives you all of those games combine and so much more!After playing the game for 4 hours, My Time at Sandrock makes me want to play even more. There is so much to do in the game. From having combat encounters and having to time when you are going to dodge or hit an enemy; to being able to customize your workshop (inside and out), along with your character; to just the concept of gathering things to create new objects, are just the few things that make this game amazing. The NPC interaction is astounding as well and actually gives you a connection to each one. Some minor compliants would be that the loading time is very slow and the games audio bugs out every now and then (not as frequent). But for a game that is in Early Access, it still receieves a 9.5/10 in my book!!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the My Time games! I played this before any of the big updates, loved it and wished for more content. Waited a while for the more recent update to come out and the wait was worth it - I love the new additions even more! The characters are unique and the romance options are fantastic! There is a lot of content, where I know I'm not even halfway though the main storyline at about 100 hours for this current playthrough. It's a very slow paced game, but can ramp up when events in the town occur, the slow-downs are a nice chance top catch up on commissions and talk with villagers. Very relaxing and pretty stress-free. It does have some bugs still, and a few issues with cutscenes, but overall it's well done. This game is still in beta, so I'm very excited for the full-release version!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the first game in this series, you will love this. On top of what was already a graphically beautiful game, with lots of device characters and a big land of exploration, comes a lot of quality of life changes that I was happy to see added into this new chapter. Gathering new materials felt a lot more smooth and free flowing, while still grindy of course, it felt like you got a lot more out of each day than you did in the previous game. Which is something I can appreciate, it must be difficult to try and balance out making the game have some amount of longevity to it, while not making it feeling like a complete slog. Each new character in this chapter of the series have their own distinct personalities and quirks. I love how much more cats and dogs there are roaming around! If you do enjoy games with building, story progression and interacting with interesting characters, all the while being able to just have a chill time. Then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of fun in the beginning, but ultimately repetitive. The main quest is time-consuming; after 84 hours, I'm only 60% through. As a builder, there are numerous activities like interacting with NPCs, completing tasks, and making money, but progress toward the main quest feels slow. Crafting, farming, mining, and the open world didn't meet my expectations.While the game has potential, it falls short of being a "Harvest Moon" equivalent. It becomes monotonous; even with things I have, and stuffs, there's little to do. Mining for copper ores and revisiting old dungeons for parts feels like a grind, sand fishing becomes so boring, interaction with NPC is meh. It feels like the game's progression so sluggish.HOWEVER, I still like the game, but I just feel like it isn't worth it to waste another hours to follow the storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to the amazing My Time at Portia. And it is just as amazing. If you didn't play Portia, this game would fall under the "Farm Life Sim" genre like Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon. However, instead of running a farm, you are running a workshop. So instead of growing crops, you are building machines to refine materials like ores you mine up and monster drops. You do this to make gear, more machines, and commisions to prove you are the best builder. It honestly makes it feel very different from those under games but a lot of things make it feel very familiar. Things like eating food to refill your limited energy bar, giving gifts to townsfolk to raise your relationship with them, and eventually marrying someone (Thou marriage is not currently in the game as of the writing of this review.)Definitly a game people who like those other Farm Life Sims should play.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, Sandrock improves on nearly every aspect of Portia. I can't think of anything that was streamlined or made more intuitive. If you liked the last game, you'll like this.I have two gripes: One is that the game keeps you VERY busy in the early to mid game with side quests, but drops off almost entirely by the last act, and the second is experience gain slows down DRASTICALLY in the last act.To elaborate on the first point, there's very little to do between the last 5-10 main story missions. You'll find yourself grinding materials and experience just to kill time. By the time the last mission rolled around, I was only lacking some early-game materials that I had to go into a lower level mine to grind. It was very underwhelming that the last task of the game was mining somewhere I'd been 100 times before. By the end, I was dragging myself to finish merely because I was so close. I just wanted it to be over. That said, you'll enjoy 95% of the game. I did. But the final few hours are important in any game and left a lasting impression on me. It kind of killed my desire to replay. Maybe I will come back after a few more updates and DLCs, or just wait for a sequel.On the second point, the opportunities to gain experience drop off and the threshold to level up rises throughout the game, but the gap becomes particularly acute in the final act. There are three end-game challenges left for me to complete, but to even stand a chance in the next one, I estimate I'd need to do nothing but grind for another hour at least. Right now, the best way to grind is mining. I have no need for mining materials. While going through each mine is fun the first time -- the mines are not randomly generated this time and lower levels feature puzzles and obstacles, a great improvement over Portia -- it becomes mind numbing tedium after the 10th. The story is fun, exciting, goofy at times and heartfelt. I don't want to say much about it because it's better to experience it. I greatly enjoyed it. Some characters are better-written than others. The ones that have a lot of involvement in the main story are generally fleshed out. I can't speak to other love interests, but my choice, Elsie, was very involved in a few major plot points. I do wish there had been more acknowledgement of the romance there.As per usual, the costume DLCs aren't really worth the money unless you have some specific interest in them. They don't add anything beyond aesthetics. Each character has an alternate color scheme for their basic outfits in vanilla, and a few have story-related outfits you can unlock. I imagine the monster-taming DLC (blanking on the name right now) would be a lot of fun if you have it from the beginning. I got it right near the end, but it was fun having a few of the creatures whose designs I liked following me around. They have a basic level and quality system, unlock new attacks and can be given assignment (not workshop or farming related tasks, unfortunately).In summary, I very much enjoyed this game aside from a few relatively minor complaints out of a 600-plus hour playtime and I look forward to the next game in this series.

_childDocuments_.review: With only a "yes/no" recommend option, I'll start this by saying that it's actually neutral. Not bad, but not great. It is a nifty little game, equally as fun as the first My Time at Portia game. I just picked it up earlier today and I'm having fun with it, and I have a bunch of hours in Portia, too. The combat is basic but serviceable, the characters are mildly interesting, and the views and scenery are fun. There are some minor gripes which include poorly balanced voice lines (one line is too loud, and the next line in the same conversation is too low) and glitchy little bugs all over the place (your feet do crazy things when swinging the axe, doors to crazy things when entering/exiting, the mini map does crazy things when moving, targeting anything is a crap shoot, etc). These don't feel game breaking though. I did completely turn off the voice volume, though.The big problem for me is that I do *NOT* understand the insistence on the terrible stamina usage system. 16 hours in a day that I can spend doing things, and your stamina is spent in the first hour. And you need stamina for EVERYTHING. You can only do 1 commission a day to start with, so after that the rest of your time is spent.... twiddling your thumbs? Or going to bed at 11 am because there's nothing left to do. Yes, you can eat food that costs a stupid amount of money per stamina, or you can sit in a chair and regain approximately 5-10 stamina an hour. But on the flip side of the argument, if this game is anything like Portia, by the end of the game you won't even come close to using all of your stamina, even if you're trying to. And that makes the entire system feel half-baked and irrelevant.Overall, it has lots of potential, but currently lots of bugs and balance issues. Maybe I'll let this one simmer for a year or so and try again.Oh, edit to say: the game has been in 1.0 for only a month now, and there are about a dozen purchasable cosmetics. I find that... distastefully EA-ish.

I see the blue circles on the map that begins SQ's. I try to avoid those areas. But then I'm into the game and I forget. If I yearn for fighting, I'll play a fighting game that is actually made for fighting.. not just jumping around and blindly hitting stuff-Or these stupid "jumpy" sections (the goat mission - bleh) where vertigo is setting in and one cannot move on. - The story goes on and on and drags along... way too many side mission that do not add to the story at all (Catory world.. why??). _childDocuments_.review: Sandrock is absolutely addicting. The simplest comparison many hear is to Stardew, which is true but kind of different. Your main activity boils down to crafting and exploring the world instead of farming (though farming IS in the game, along with animals, pets, mounts~) and single player is a fairly story heavy based mode with a LOT of quests and subquests. romances in this are far superior to the likes of Stardew in my opinion, where you can actually take the romance options on various dates and activities. Tons of mini-games and festivals, combat dungeons to go through, you name it. For those who, like me, enjoyed the idea of Portia but couldn't really get into it, Sandrock as a *vast* amount of polish that puts it leads above Portia. Between the vast amount of varied content and activities, watching the town and characters grow and develop, and an actually entertaining (if a bit too silly at times personally) story, you'll be hard pressed not to get completely sucked in and obsessed with Sandrock.The biggest elephant in the room for people is how separate the singleplayer and multiplayer modes are, and I'll probably be the rare voice in that I actually *enjoy* this distinction. despite having played through the story (mostly, there is a LOT of dang content here seriously) I'm not any more bored for it playing multiplayer with my friends because of how fresh and different it feels. I'd akin singleplayer toward rune factory whereas multiplayer is more stardew, while single player follows a narrative heavy story, where many things are locked behind narrative events; multiplayer is a free form mode where you do whatever you want and choose the direction you want to go. The multiplayer town starts in a VERY barebones state (no general store, no train, passageways blocked off, etc)  so even having played the story it was a completely new experience building the town practically from the ground up with friends and dungeons being in different states. Many people complain they can't experience the singleplayer story in multiplayer but honestly...that type of gameplay just would NOT translate well into multiplayer like people seem to think it would. with how many story conversations and cutscenes there constantly are any multiplayer session would pretty much be everyone constantly being ripped away from whatever they're trying to do to be pulled into watching the story progress..... or miss half the story because they don't get to see the cutcenes, there's just no way it would go well. You can't have seperate story progression in the same session either because the town itself is affected by the story. I honestly feel the way they went about it was the best way, and honestly gave us all the more content for it as a bonus. If i were to scrounge up some negative points off the top of my head, my first priority would be the multiplayer save system. I love that like grounded everyone shares the file and can log on without the "host" at any time, but we seriously need to be able to join other people's towns without losing all our progress in the original town. people with more then a 3 friend circle or want to jump in some rando's world or help someone else out would have to sacrifice virtually all their progress to do so. The cutscenes could use just a bit of touch up at the end, they can end a bit too abruptly and awkwardly.The combat could use some more depth for sure. It's not *bad* but it's not anything to write home about either. A few of the romance options basically make you wait til you finish dang near the whole story before you can finally engage in that side of the game. Narratively I get it for some cases but it doesn't make it any less frustrating for a  story that takes many, *many* hours to get through. Last but not least... sand sledding.... I want to love it but dear god.... Somebody fix the handling please, there's nothing fun about something thats as unresponsive as a boulder.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game so far. I have played and fell in love with "My Time at Portia" . If you  have played that game then there are many improvements that I think you will like, plus a bunch of things that make this game unique. _childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play cozy farm sim games, but decided to try this one out for a change and I was pleasantly and incredibly surprised.I liked the idea of building a home at Sandrock and developing relationships with the town. The story is engaging and I would say overall it is a "Feel good" story. The relationships you build with the NPCs felt organic and the conclusion of the main story felt earned and satisfying.Romance: If you decide to romance a NPC, the romance  system, while wholesome and cutesy, is one of the best in any game to have "romance" that I've played. You can form relationships, break up , marry, divorce, seek forgiveness to start a relationship up again, which was something I hadn't seen. In other games with a "romance" option, you would eventually have to lock in with a particular NPC for the entire play through and if you decided to break it off, you would be locked out from pursuing any other relationships, but not this game, as far as I have seen anyway. You can even date multiple people at once however there are ramifications if you get caught. (But why would you want to to do that?).  Also...the hand holding in this game is so darn cute, that I would often just run around with my chosen partner in the game to watch them hold hands. Such a simple thing to be overjoyed about, but it would always make me smile.The overall experience in designing my workshop and farm was satisfying. I thought the amount of personalization options were well balanced - not too many to feel overwhelmed, but not too little to feel like you couldn't put a personal touch to your workshop/homestead.Voice acting overall was well done (for English VA anyway).There is a ton to do in this game, and even after finishing the lengthy main story quest line, I'm still finding new side quests. It seems like you could endlessly play one play through for however long you wanted.  I loved this one so much, I became a backer for the Kickstarter campaign for their next game, My Time at Evershine.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time in Sandrock is just as great as its predecessor my Time in Portia. The artstyle is amazing, game's world is immersive and the music makes it a very relaxing game. I've been waiting for about two years for it to be released and am extreamly excited to try it out. The character customisation has gotten even better in this installment so you can really make a character that fits your imagination. If you like farming and building sims this is the game for you. The story is set in a post apocalyptic world where people had to live underground for generations because a robot had destroyed the world. Now that it is safe on the surface again people shun the technologies of the past. You are a builder arriving at your new job in a dessert town called Sandrock where you have to build up and old work shop to complete commissions and quests, while diving for resources in old ruins and sourcing from the world around you while also balancing usage of water and fuel to keep production running. Make friends in this new town or even romance the locals its up to you..

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock's character creator takes pretty much all of what was available in My Time at Portia and makes it just a little bit better. While the character creator only allows for what is essentially human male and female it still allows quite a lot within those confines. You get to customise skin colour, face shape, hair and facial hair, the entire face and make-up, and then some tattoos along with all of that. Unfortunately for male characters there are only two different facial hair styles which kinda sucks. The colour selection system in Sandrock is also full RGB and allows for some pretty silly looking characters, if that's your thing. My highlight of the character creation system is definitely the modular hair system that allows you to mix and match different hairstyles, bangs, and ponytails to create whatever your heart desires. There is room for improvement and I am almost certain that more will be added over time, much like was done with Portia.All of that said, though, the character creator is quite refined and the characters you can make with it look great, very Pixar. _childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock (MTAS) is an amazing game in the cozy game genre. Despite its farming sim tag, I would not classify it as that. In My Time at Sandrock you are a builder, not a farmer. Your goal is to complete quests and build tools and machines to improve the quality of life for the citizens at Sandrock. MTAS has a great storyline that sometimes feels like it can drag but the pace stays rather steady throughout. I did rush to complete some story content but the full game and all it has to offer is easily 100+ hours of content. As far as games in the cozy game genre go I think this one has one of the better stories and characters. Some characters may be frustrating but give them time. I think you'll grow to love most of them. MTAS does have combat but as someone who plays a lot of games the combat feels pretty lackluster and not challenging. If you are not used to combat in games it may be a bit challenging but I personally think it's very easy. It doesn't bother me that it isn't a challenge because I'm interested in the story and characters.MTAS is improved from Portia with excellent quality-of-life updates. For example, when completing board requests the items in storage now count. You no longer have to be carrying those which is soooo nice. Makes it a lot easier. I also think the character models have improved which is a nice touch. If you are planning to purchase MTAS for multiplayer it is important to know that you can't do the main story with multiplayer. Instead, you will have quests from the townsfolk and things like that. The only con I have for MTAS besides a few bugs I encountered is the mis-proportionate romance quests. Depending on who you romance, some characters have more content than others. While the dev team has been adding new content and working to improve this it's pretty obvious which characters are the favorites based on their content.There is also one particular side quest that I needed to do to advance the main quest. It may have changed in the last year but if not then just know that it is important to do all side quests with Elsie early on. I had to search online when the main quest was not advancing and discovered it was because I hadn't advanced her side quests forward.I completely recommend MTAS. It was one of my favorite games last year. I enjoyed it so much and can't wait for the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I have become obsessed with this game! The story is rich and engaging making the progression rewarding. The only bummer is that the customization of your home and character are very limiting. So many acquired objects that come with the game progression, but the game doesn't let you display them adequately. The female character body and clothing leaves much to be desired. Even being able to change clothing colors would have helped. At first you're tricked thinking you have all these ways to make your home your own, but then get stuck by the baffling limitations. Somehow, I find ways to overlook those dead ends. Hopefully Evershine goes beyond the bare minimum to enrich the player experience as much as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game is amazing. If you played My Time at Portia, you will love this as they are pretty similar in game style. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: So... I reaaaaly like this game. Gameplay is fun, NPCs and their little stories engaging, main story gives satisfaction of  "job well done" when you see how far can you develop Sandrock and surrounding areas. Changes to My time at Portia are not really significant, which can be good, as I liked it as well, or bad, as you can have the feeling that you are fer same dish as before, just on nicer plate. One of new mechanic, sand getting into your machines and slowing them down was toned so much between early acces and full release, that it is basically not there anymore. Machines needing water to work is just another meter to look at and is not really groundbreaking, but fits setting and narrative quite nicely (but in the end, you never really run out of water, so is there a point?). There are many minor flaws and game is still buggy as hell even after full release. Pacing of main story is too slow. Maybe it is because I replayed it few times since early access, but most of main story quests that demands me building anything ends the same day I receive diagram since I have enough material at hand to cover almost any request. And then I have to wait for story to develop, sometimes for few days, so I gather more resources and it goes on.Some romance options are locked behind main story, so you have to progress in game to start dating them, but for some it is super late game so you will probably see end credits before marriage option is on the table (you can play after that too, but is there still enough game to play at this point?).Bugs, bugs are still everywhere. Pathing issues, memory leaks, not being able to start interactions with npc/items causing soft locks during quests (ie you cannot talk to npc to leave quest area). I spent a lot of time reloading or even turning game off to combat them, good that autosave and quicksave features work flawlessy and I never lost more than few minutes of progress.So as I said at the beginning, I enjoyed My time at Sandrock. I hope that few futures patches will adress bugs and devs will hammer out flaws in next part of the series (I thibk they hinted strongly about setting in final story mission).
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I have a really good computer and internet connection, not top of the line mind you, i'm not rich by any means. But the game in its current state is very glitchy, it loads very slowly and it shouldn't (takes my computer less than a minute to completely boot itself or restart any other MMO or game I have including the newest on the market if I can afford them or want to play them), or it completely crashes altogether. These problems should not arise at all. I LOVE this game, don't get me wrong, I have played through before it was finished, and look forward to TRYING to finish the completed version of it. The characters are great and so is the crafting and game play, if you can get past the rest of it. Personally it REALLY gets on my nerves at times. So my suggestion is wait for at least a half price SALE or better, it is a little steep at its current price tag for the problems that still exist. Including the pathways of the baddies in some of the ruins is wonkie at times.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I know, it's a strong statement, especially among the cozy game community, but I haven't found myself so invested in a cozy game's plot as I have in Sandrock. You can tell that the developers really poured their heart into this game. The writing is unexpectedly witty and constantly breaks the fourth wall in increasingly clever ways. Each main NPC is a round character, with unforgettable traits, and really you could fall in love with any one of them. The art style is gorgeous, which is amplified by the 3D design that most games of this style tend to shy away from. The game-play loop only got stale towards the end, almost 200 hours deep, and by this time, I was well enough invested in the story, that I very much wanted to see it all the way through. Sandrock is a 10/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I love games like these with characters you can get to know and romance. Sadly, most of the games I've played in the past fall short in this department and I honestly wasn't expecting this one to be much different. But I was wrong!Instead of talking to townies once a day and getting a dull line of conversation(I mean...it does do that too)there are a bunch of story related quests you can do for/with them with a lot of cut scenes and dialogue that really bring the characters to life. You get to know them and their personalities(yes they actually have those) and there were some characters who I didn't like in the beginning but after a certain point in their story I was like...darn, they're growing on me. I think I like them now. Let's face it, usually in these types of games what you see is what you get when it comes to romanceable characters. They don't tend to change much or have much in the way of interesting dialogue. Also, I was beyond excited when I found out you can have children and they're more than decorative objects although I haven't gotten that far yet. The story itself is so far highly entertaining. There were so many moments that made me laugh and that never happens in these types of games for me usually. The dialogue in my opinion is very well written for this type of game. I love that the story is long(I'm still not entirely finished)but I'm so glad they got rid of the timed main missions like in Portia. So you can go at your own pace and not feel rushed. They improved upon the house building mechanics which I like although I will admit they dropped the ball on furniture for your house and sadly most of what's available is behind paid DLC. Although it's not very expensive, but still. All in all I would 10/10 recommend if you're looking for a good story, well written dialogue, fleshed out characters and lots of humorous moments.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. I am running it on a pretty new gaming laptop and have had some minor issues with loading times and starting conversations, but besides a few hiccups I haven't had any issues framerate wise even in the sandstorm. The love interest pool is wide and deep and delicious and I love almost all of them I'm going to need many saves for this one. Mi-An is super cute, but Owen is also fantastic, and I could probably go on for quite a while about the characters. This dev is excellent at making characters deep and I was worried the "southern" motif would cheapen the characters, but it's been worked in well.Graphics are gorgeous even through they're stylized and I really enjoy the detail that went into making the MC look like they're actually interacting with scenes as opposed to just stuck on top (an issue I had with Portia).I don't know if there are more quests but it certainly feels like it, you do not go very long before a new quest pops up. I haven't played enough to get through even a bit of the content, but I'm trying to go slow so I can play with the updates. For early release the content feels well fleshed out and there's no teasing of things that aren't in the game yet except perhaps multiplayer, but I'm not interested in that aspect of the game. If you've played Portia this is a well made sequel that I am pleased has come to fruition. I have great faith that it can only go up from here.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Here’s a positive review you can use for My Time at Sandrock:My Time at Sandrock is an absolute gem! From the moment I stepped into the world of Sandrock, I was completely immersed in its vibrant, post-apocalyptic environment filled with charm, creativity, and endless opportunities. The game's unique blend of farming, crafting, and exploring makes every moment enjoyable, and the attention to detail in both the storyline and character development is impressive.The characters feel alive, each with their own personalities and stories, which makes interacting with them incredibly rewarding. The crafting system is deep and intuitive, allowing for endless possibilities to build and improve your workshop. There’s always something to do, whether it’s gathering resources, completing quests, or exploring the beautifully designed desert landscape.One of the standout features is the balance between relaxation and excitement. The game provides plenty of laid-back moments, but it also includes a sense of adventure with its combat mechanics and intriguing mysteries. It’s a perfect blend of cozy and challenging gameplay that keeps me hooked.The developers have clearly put a lot of love into creating this world, and it shows in the seamless mechanics, stunning visuals, and the overall smooth experience. I can’t recommend My Time at Sandrock enough for anyone who enjoys simulation games, crafting, and open-world exploration. It’s a must-play, and I can’t wait to see where the story goes next!
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed My Time at Portia and assumed Sandrock couldn't top it- absolutely wrong.Every mechanic that originated in Portia has been smoothed out in Sandrock, from acquiring new diagrams to mining to combat to actually building. The characters feel a lot livelier and the writing is incredibly charming; I have startled my partner with my cackling at some of the dialogue. It's not a perfect game, the pacing is a little awkward and the climax of the story was in the second act, but I ultimately love it. If you like the farming/life sim genre and want something unique, My Time at Sandrock is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I feel a little let down by the game. My time at Portia was so charming with its unique artstyle and what I really enjoyed about it was that there were so many "game modes" within one game (different style dungeons, mini games, etc.) that I couldnt stop marvelling at it. In my entire time playnig Portia, I had only encountered one bug which was more than negligible. Because of all this, I decided to buy Sandrock and boy, is it a bit of a letdown.The different game modes feel messy at best. Things are confusing. There's hardly any reason to go into the hazardous ruins now. The combat is somehow worse than in Portia.What annoys me the most is that in Portia, you slowly unlocked areas bit by bit through bridges or lifts that were being built over time. Here, we have the desert. And invisible walls. The desert (yes, i know its a desert, what do I expect?) is empty. There is absolutely nothing in it. You can walk for five minutes in one direction and encounter nothing. No monsters, no loot. Until you hit an invisible wall. It feels like such a lazy solution to a problem. Couldve placed buildings there... or something to mark that this is where the map ends. It's also buggy. One of the bugs that annoy me the most is that once I bought my camel, people would despawn and then spawn somewhere else whenever I got close. I had it once that I got close to an NPC to drop off a comission on my camel, only for that NPC to despawn right in front of me. The minimap indicated that they were basically on the other side of town, so i made my way there. Only for them to disappear and reappear in the original location again. I had to get off the camel and approach them slowly to drop off the damn comission. Also the camel is so damn difficult to manouver that sometimes I just get off because the damn thing just keeps running into walls.I play this game because I still enjoy the story. I enjoy the characters. I want to see where things go. But I am frustrated on an hourly basis, because of the bugs and the lazy way that a lot of things were done. It feels unfinished. Bare bones. I am not certain if I will get the next installment of the games that has been announced on Kickstarter. The artstyle has been completely changed to mainstream games like Final Fantasy or Monster Hunter and I just don't vibe with that... And given how this game feels like an absolute disappointment, I am not sure I am willing to spend any money on another one.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game so far. Early access has already exceeded my expectations. I LOVE My Time At Portia, and this feels like it took all the best things from that game and improved on them.Highlights:-Massively increased customizability for your character-Reworked inventory/quick bar features (i.e., you no longer have to be holding an item in your quick bar to add it to a project on the assembly platform; hotkey to switch things from quick bar to inventory and back)-Fun, animated characters-Good story line so far-Perfect difficulty level for acquiring materials and progressing through building-Very few bugs encountered so far and NO crashesIf you liked MTAP, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: After one of the major story line quests (only about 10% of people have got this far) the game won't stop stuttering in town. Seen it's a common problem on the discussions, and running a 4090 so not exactly a lack of power. Game outstays it's welcome and feels overly long and repetitive. They tout it's X time longer than Portia, and for me, it feels it. I enjoyed Portia, but this feels like work, and is very repetitive. The combat is terrible too. Mobs are so big on screen you can't always see health bars and you can't zoom out, and your character doesn't seem to turn to face the mob very quickly which can get frustrating. Very average. Get on sale for a long game and a lot of value for money if you want a repetitive, bland game
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely in love with this game. It's downright addicting - one more commission, one more day just to mine or fish; I haven't played Portia and I've heard fishing is better in that one, but honestly with an upgraded sandtrap and the right kind of bait, it's pretty fun. It's super exciting that the devs are actively working on improving this game. There are def some bugs, none are gamebreaking tho and it's easy enough to give feedback. One of the biggest issues is this game eats up nearly all 16gb of RAM when turning up the graphics to the highest setting. Even RDR2, NMS, and other big games don't put nearly as much strain on my pc as this game lol.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played so far, for the most part the game is great. The only real issue I ran into was after resizing my house, I lost my door and didn't realize it until it was too late to go back and change it. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I'm VERY impressed with the multiplayer. This game has achieved what I've been hoping for since forever really. Your world that you share with friends is accessible to others even when you're offline,. Simply amazing. This is the new standard for coop games imo.The game itself seems fun from whatever little i've played so far.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game even though it has a few weaknesses. The camera could be a bit smoother and a way to spend skillpoints on the skill tree after you have unlocked everything (or not getting skillpoints for that skill tree) would be nice. But overall it became a really good game. Especially if you follow the story.Also I would have liked easier access for modding the game. Especially adding your own models and textures would give this game such a nice boost. Really something you should consider for the future @devs.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, but the "Early Release" process is too slow to keep anyone's attention that isn't just a straight up fanboy or fangirl.  Basically if you buy now, you'll play for a week or two, then there will be nothing left to do.  You will put the game down for a month or two, and they will release some major new content that takes about 2 days to play through, then you're stuck waiting months again for new content. ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE business concept.  So basically you're paying full retail price to beta test the game for the company for free.  When the game is fully released, people will be paying the same price for a finished game as you paid to test the game for them.  No perks besides random garbage items you will get in your in-game mail every once in a while. This is the EXACT same thing they did with My Time at Portia.  Kept promising and promising, and if you go back to that game today, it still isn't finished.  Great devs, great game, horrible marketing team.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: A fun cozy slice of life adventure/gathering game. Controls very well, and the town is pretty. All the characters you meet, and interact with are unique with their own personality. It gives a good day to day grind while the power creep settles in nicely as well. Great for coop, and building with friends too!
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing ride.The plot, the characters, the cozy village vibes! Way more polished than My time at Portia. This is for me a 10/10 game. It just makes you never want to leave Sandrock. This games deserves even more love and popularity. It surpasses in my opinion all the other popular farming sim games (even tough this game is more about building stuff).Almost 120 hours and i didnt even finish the game! And im not tired of it! Thank you Devs for your amazing work.I will patiently await for your next game. And we need more outfits for npcs! Please!Edit: finished 100% (with achievments). Loved every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: After a long day at work, Sandrock is now my go to game to unwind. I've played Portia before which was what led me to purchase Sandrock asap eventho it's still in Early Access. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Portia and this game really delivered on improving many things that made Portia a bit hard to like. Building up a failing town is a lot ore interesting than turning an already nice town into a tourist attraction. There are a lot of the same issues I had with Portia though, which is a bit disappointing. Targeting with the pickhammer/axe is kind of wonky, there are a lot of visual glitches that are kind of funny to see but also super immersion breaking. You'll be talking to someone in a sandstorm and their protective gear will bounce up and down on their head or you'll be walking around town and a row of bushes will fly up into the air and gently bounce while still suspended above you. It's not enough to make me stop playing but it does get frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game runs pretty janky. Its pretty. I loved My Time At Portia. I think one of my biggest complaints so far is how janky interacting with some things feel. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I played the prequel Portia on my switch and while I liked that game, I absolutely love My Time at Sandrock. The plot is much more well written and the characters have more depth into them than in Portia. In my opinion. I am in my final main quests in this game and I am already planning to start this game again because I really enjoyed it!Suuure, the game also has few bugs but what game doesn't?? _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Just for now - I would not recommend purchasing this product, though, I give it 90% to be worth it in the future. So, if you really have nowhere else to put the 20Eur - go for it now. If not - wait a little bit longer.I played it literally 2min after leaving My Time in Portia, so, if you have not played that game - you might not have the same issues I had, but:1. The interaction with various things seems more clunky (buggy?) than in Portia - I had multiple occasions where I had to readjust my character's position just to be able to gather a scrap pile or talk to an NPC.2. The new scrapyard system seems like a downgrade from the Ruin system in Portia. They should have kept basically the same system, just adding the Scrap system on top, imo.3. The game looks pretty, but some things annoyed me, like having no decent facial hair options or other customization stuff (unless I made myself look like a complete clown, it was pretty much the default character). 4. The beginning of the game seems super slow and you more or less just run. This is also somewhat due to the slightly different system of obtaining early materials, when comparing to Portia.Overall - it seems like everything is going in the right direction, the game just needs a bit more feedback from the playerbase and some tweaks from the developer's side.I myself will return for sure, hopefully, without a refund next time, as it was suuuuper close for me already.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I've wanted from a game in this genre. I ended up loving all the stories and that many characters make you challenge your initial thoughts and impressions. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started this game, I did not like it and actually put it down for a few months before trying again. Then it happened, the plot and gameplay made me fall in love. There are so many twists and turns and so much interactive, blush-worthly dialogue. While there are still a few frustrating bugs, the dev team is awesome and is quick to fix them! If you love cozy games where you can forget all of your real life worries and worry about saving Sandrock, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely "farm" sim game with blessed small farming requirements. I love farm sims but find the actual farming in them tedious and often the weakest aspect, so this was a nice change of pace! There is plenty to do, and in fact much better things to do other than farm to progress the game/make money and that was a huge draw for me.I never played My Time at Portia but I'm told there have been a few great QoL updates from its predecessor, so if you are on the fence due to gameplay gripes of Portia, I'd suggest seeing if your biggest ones have been fixed.World is interesting, characters are charming, writing is funny. Fair warning, though, as of now the fan wiki is still very outdated and under-maintained so it can be hard to find info if you're coming from a very robust game community like Stardew. There is a discord but I have not joined it. There are also still bugs getting worked out so be patient. I missed out on romancing my first pick because a specific quest overlapped with a story quest and I was never able to take it, for instance.Luckily I'm still quite happy with my silver medal. 😎

_childDocuments_.review: I played My time in Portia and loved it, so when I saw this I had try it too. _childDocuments_.review: Very cautious recommend.My Time at Portia is notorious for being half-finished before the developer abandoned it to make this game.  My Time at Sandrock is certainly broader than MTaP--more characters, more quests, etc, more mechanics--but it's not yet apparent whether they're going to flesh out the game's depth--finish scripting/voicing the characters, fixing the multitude of bugs, and so on.  Nevertheless, it's a mostly relaxing time.If I hear any funny business about them not paying their voice actors like what happened with Portia, though, then Pathea's going on my ****list.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Portia, you'll like this.  It is clearly the sequel with tweaks to crafting, combat, management, and saving (not just when sleeping! FINALLY!) But it clearly shows promise.Short version, if you like sandbox crafting games with some social aspects, get this and look forward to updates!

_childDocuments_.review: Today I decided to change my analysis because I wasn't feeling there was honesty anymore. I guess My Time at Sandrock had their problems since the start. I still don't think their update reports are the best, but it have been improved. Besides that, the game have a lot of bugs. Some of then are really anoying (Like piles of plastic in random places, or the mount's bug, or when my char get stuck after a cutcene and I had to reload a past save).  Even then, the game have such a nice atmosphere that you can easyly bypass thouse problems. I guess the highest point of My Time of Sandrock is the history. The characters are so alive that you can even forget they're npcs for a time. The history it's so envolving, that you get atched to the role play. Ofcourse, there is still some silly archs, but even then, I belive anyone in any age can come to like it. Every character have their own history, and it's deep histories that mold who they are. _childDocuments_.review: If this game is Skooma, then I'm a Khajiit junkie... totally and utterly addicted. _childDocuments_.review: This is how a sequel should be made: take the previous game, and make it better, reminds me of going from Ratchet and Clank 1 to 2 to 3, each game was better than the last.The game does so much right but my most favourite thing was learning about the villains ambitions and motives, having conversations with them and learning why this character now regrets what they did, or one villain who is so remorseless that beating them doesn't really feel like a win.the developers put a lot of love in this game, there are some issues but they are minimal and are overshadowed by the amount of good this game has.each character is so unique and have their own quirks, motives, stories (not enough character stories in my opinion and there are a lot!) and past. Cooper is the best comic relief, Unsuur is the weirdest, nicest character i have met in a game in a long time, Vivi is the grandma we all deserve, Yan is the perfect 'boss you hate', Rian is the laziest carpenter with the most loving wife Dan-bi, Burgess is an oblivious sweetheart, the list goes on.if you love life sims game then this game is for you10/10
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. Previously my favourite farming game was Portia, now it's Sandrock. It's such an amazing game that its existence makes me happy.Let me explain: I play a lot of farming games and I love the genre. Many of them share a number of common flaws however, such as shallow characters, weak non-farming mechanics, quest design that feels like chore. Not in Sandrock (or Portia, for that matter)! The characters interact with each other in believable and lively ways. It's no longer that the player is the only thing that exists to them. Everyone comes together to build a town and the player is only one small part of it. This makes the quests so much more believable.What really impressed me was the way it differs from/improves upon Portia. Portia did a lot of things very well, but Sandrock didn't just take those mechanics unchanged. Instead, Sandrock improved upon every little thing in Portia that bothered me (e.g. the guns were a bit weak in Portia; they're totally viable in Sandrock) and also refreshed other aspects (e.g. I liked the fishing mini game in Portia; Sandrock changed the mini game but it's equally entertaining) so that series fans like me aren't bored.The way the multiplayer is implemented is also quite good.Overall, I just love the thought and care the devs have put in this game. It's incredibly rare nowadays to see a game in a popular genre where the devs didn't settle for easy formulas and past success, but continue to improve. Love everything about this game!
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is a wonderful sequel to My Time at Portia.  As a beta tester I have seen the many stages of seeing this game come from a jittery start to the polished game you now see at early access.  There are already tons of things to do and explore.  Think Portia but with sand instead of water.  Lots to check out!  Sandrock actually happens at the same time as Portia so you will have many of the same machines, types of quests and interactions with NPCs as you did in the previous game.  The difference is that the developers had time to create a game that was much more polished out of the gate.I would definitely recommend this game.  I have well over 300 hours already and I know there is much more to do.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Never having played My Time at Portia, I recently took a gamble on My Time at Sandrock, after repeatedly hearing it described as Stardew Valley with better graphics. While that is a fair description, I think it undersells the fact that Sandrock has several unique qualities that make it stand out even in the genre, and which led to me getting hooked for dozens and dozens of hours. One thing that is immediately obvious is that the game oozes atmosphere, with plenty of memorable characters, and the writers/localization team did a great job consistently coming up with entertaining, funny, and witty situations and lines. Just about everything has a Saturday morning cartoon vibe to it, in a good way, which makes it suitable for younger audiences, while also containing many references that adults will enjoy. As far as the overarching narrative is concerned, I feel like they played things  straight at times, leading to predictability, but perhaps not subverting expectations is itself subversive at this point. The voice acting is generally good, but notably uneven in quality, where it is easy to tell that experienced VAs were paired with less experienced ones. This can be jarring to hear on occasion, but perhaps it can be seen as a positive that they were willing to give unknown actors a chance. Mechanically and in terms of design as well, there is much to admire about Sandrock. It is very good at keeping you invested by steadily drip-feeding the happy chemicals as you complete quests, finish projects, improve your relationships with NPCs, expand your lot, and so on. When you are tasked with improving infrastructure around town, for example, those upgrades will be permanently visible, and sometimes have a practical effect as well, making the player feel as if their actions have consequences. There are many quality-of-life features that were much appreciated, such as different types of storage all being linked to each other, so that your entire storage can be accessed all at once. After a certain point, you can also start hiring NPCs to start gathering resources for you, reducing tedium in that regard. There are many more examples that all show that much thought was put into the design, including the UI.As with any game, there are unfortunately also negatives to point out. While the story and characters are entertaining and well-done overall, I feel that the game suffers from serious pacing issues. You will be stuck at certain stages of machine/character development for much longer than others, and the narrative climax occurs when the main story is about two-thirds done, after which it continues meandering for another 40 hours or so. Many players will never finish the main story at all, because it takes such a long time to do so, and it feels like the stakes are no longer there after a certain point.Sandrock was overall stable for me, and I experienced almost no game-breaking bugs or glitches, but NPC pathfinding on the whole is very wonky, and you will often see them behave in unintended, occasionally bizarre ways. There is also still a bug with the feather duster where sometimes you will not be able to get the 'sand-clogged' icon to go away from a machine unless you pick it up and put it back down. Apparently this has been in the game ever since release, which is an unacceptably long time for such a basic issue to be fixed. I also strongly suspect that some of the NPC relationship boosts are not working correctly, particularly the +5 Stamina boosts that you are supposed to get from reaching a certain tier with characters such as Burgess and Venti. There are also still numerous typos sprinkled throughout the text, despite the fact that the game has been out for more than eight months. I can understand that it is not a priority to fix these, but it does create a slightly amateur impression.Finally, even though the game is generally well-designed, I have to subtract marks for the way player inventory is handled specifically. They decided to have things like relic pieces and quest items count towards your overall inventory limit, meaning that you will be forced to engage in tedious inventory management throughout the entire game, no matter how many extra inventory slots you buy. This is highly questionable for a game released in 2023, and had a significant negative impact on my enjoyment at times.Overall, if I had to summarize Sandrock in a single sentence, I would say that it is exactly what you're probably expecting, but better. As a game, at every turn it shows that it has plenty of heart, and it is generally well-designed in a way that effortlessly strings along the player from milestone to milestone. Even though I listed a number of complaints, most of these are not deal breakers, and many will likely be addressed through future patches and hotfixes (perhaps with the exception of the atrocious inventory management). I can therefore easily recommend it to anyone the slightest bit interested in the life sim genre.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock certainly doesn’t skimp on the content, with players able to expect at least a hundred hours before they hit the credits. It uses those hours well enough, with an absorbing gameplay loop that always gives players the feeling that they are progressing in one manner or another. Despite a weaker presentation (after patch) and not great technical state than contemporary titles, the game is a pleasing experience and one that those with even just a passing interest in the life and crafting sim genre are likely to enjoy their time with.PROS:✓ Imparts strong sense of progression✓ Likeable cast of characters (for the most part)✓ Plenty of things to do✓ Pacy main storyline✓ The visuals are actually quite nice (were better before the downgrade patch)✓ Focus on crafting over farming is still a nice change✓ Interesting world to explore✓ Some references to My Time at Portia✓ Rich standalone co-op mode✓ Loads of content and quality-of-life features✓ RPG mechanics help to spice up the gameCONS:- Game support of this game does not help at all (after a few months of e-mail correspondence with them, I finally discovered myself the reason why the game was crashing to the desktop after a few minutes of playing, in my case I had to update the motherboard bios)- Major technical problems and bugs- Clunky, unsatisfying combat (especially melee)- Instead of fixing the game, they prefer to focus on paid DLC- Horrible downgrade in graphics after patch (supposedly work is underway to improve this)- You have to wait longer for patches because the creators want all new updates to be released at the same time on all platforms

_childDocuments_.review: After loving My Time At Portia (was my lockdown game), backing Sandrock was a no brainer. I've seen this game shape up from the early demos to the Early Access release all the way to the latest patch now in a time where My Time at Evershine is at the horizon, and after finally beating the main story yesterday I can truly say what a great ride it has been. This is a farming/crafting sim with an absolutely staggering amount of content, and I can't believe how much of it is fully voice acted. I truly found the characters engaging (my end summary showed I befriended everyone), loved all their little arcs they had, and beyond that in general just love Pathea's endearing weirdness to just pick a direction they think is cool and fully commit to it, sometimes you're rebuilding a thing that got broken, sometimes you make a tiny hat for a cat, sometimes you become involved in uncovering a conspiracy while working with the FBI. I truly mean it when I say the game  took many surprising turns but never felt anything other than genuine in its execution. This is a quality shared with Portia and I'm sure Evershine will have it too, but which way they want to take the story is only something Pathea knows and the tendency to deviate from the norms makes these games one of a kind. Overall, to summarize, I loved My Time At Sandrock, and wherever Pathea goes next with My Time At Evershine, I can truly say I can't wait to see what adventure they send us off to next.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always a bit reflecting when playing a second opus as to "Should I play it completely as a new game or should I assume it will build on the previous opus?", and same goes for a "critic" (if that self indulgent term can be applied there).So yes, I've played Portia, and to be honest, I waited for more in this opus.I was never that much into the characters of this game, but to be fair, they are pretty much all "new" from the previous opus, so...The story to me is honestly a bit "meh". It's actually even worse than Portia, because the story of Portia was really meh, but at least it didn't offer a picture of considering that seriously its story as a selling point. There Sandrock never really knows whether to be serious or just fun and light, won't be too spoilery there but where Portia was pretty much what was advertised, Sandrock leans on giving more grit to its world, but if feels at time a bit cringy and ... too long. Honestly the main story is really long, especially when the game mechanics behind it revolves around crafting and combat : 1. CraftingThe crafting is exactly the same as the previous one. There was maybe some small addition, but all in all, it's the same concept. Some general ideas were a bit abandoned like the tentative full automative system of the first opus. It leans a bit more on gardening, and fishing which for me is not a good idea (there are a lot of gardening & fishing games out there already).2. CombatCombat has improved... yes. But it's still "not good". It does "a" job, rather than the job, and it's pretty much as complicated as using a pickaxe to mine ore. The whole dodging/combo break adds really nothing to it all.3. MissionsThe missions have exactly the same issue than the first opus, which is to always pick missions from a limited pool of items. And it's even more funny when you put this aside the fact that there are a loooooot of items in this game (again, too much really, it's just hollow content that just adds to more inventory management than anything).4. The restTo me all the systems never get too deep, and there are "too many" stuff. Fishing, cooking, crafting, fighting, romancing, missions, side missions, etc, a lot of the system are too clicky-clicky and the gameplay as a whole is pretty much just ticking boxes over and over with little sense of achievement.It was good for a first game, but for the second, I hoped for system to be improved and give a bit more challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Most negative reviews are regarding significantly less story driven experience in multiplayer. I don’t play multiplayer so can’t comment but if like me you’re predominantly or only looking to single player then this game is a gem and storytelling is great for indie/even AA & AAA level.Another common complaint is game performance, bugs, pacing and Sandrock not deemed to have received proper post v1.0 release support like no major content DLCs or fixed all bugs. First the game has some janky bugs like events/side quests not properly triggered if you are not at the exact right location at the exact hour on the dot, other issues include your mount would sometimes get stuck trying to walk onto a porch (minor issue resolved by just walk away few paces to respawn) or menu/inventory can take few seconds to tens of seconds to load in at times. The loading issue affects SSDs.But this game imo is still overall optimised from low end to high end PCs & the bugs that are still in-game are minor UI/glitches that doesn’t impact overall gameplay except for maybe losing out on some extra in-game items/progression points etc. due to faulty event triggers etc. I would rate this game as more optimised than most games released these days especially in the open world/sandbox genre.The game is a treat to play. A huge variety of mini games, systems within systems & excellent world design and content pacing. The onboarding experience was not overwhelming despite this game containing a lot of inter-connected systems like skills/equipment/base progressions tied into quests/gameplay mechanics/social interactions etc. You can play this game in short bursts even 15mins sessions here and there or go for hours at a time. The game has intuitive UI/UX considering sheer amount of information, stats, mechanics, upgrades, NPC relationships, resources, quests and more. I did not encounter anything frustrating to be noteworthy.This game at current ver Oct 2024 is robust and performant on variety of hardware from the Steam Deck (LCD model - originally installed on a SD card & migrated game file to stock SSD due to SD card too slow), to the Rog Ally (2TB SSD 30W mode) & ultimately looks awesome on higher rigs/displays like my 4090/13900 paired with QHD OLED. can easily play at 60FPS on low settings 800p or mix of medium - high settings locked 40FPS. Rarely does game underperform & dip below 40FPS.: With AMD AFMF I’m getting generally 70~120FPS on high settings. 25W turbo mode on battery works just as well. : Most games that play well and look ok on PC handhelds etc. generally won’t scale as nicely on higher hardware as the assets etc. were likely designed & optimised for lower end PC. This game looks good on higher end hardware and is arguably where I’d recommend the most immersive experience is. However, there is a low GPU/CPU utilisation issue where the game (and only this game) only uses 30~40% of my GPU and 10~20& of my CPU. So I should in theory get 144FPS (max FPS of this game) but I'm generally around 80~120FPS at maxed settings due to this low GPU/CPU utilisation issue which doesn't seem to have any updated responses from devs since 2022/23. This of course is not game breaking issue and vs. other comparable sandbox games that barely work (looking at you Craftopia) this might be a luxury problem for most Sandrock players.

Lastly the Dev. team is super responsive and provides updates when new content is coming or if deadlines are being moved, their commitment to putting out a quality game is amazing! _childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel to "My Time at Portia", which I really enjoyed. So buying this was a no-brainer! The mechanics are basically the same. There have been some quality of life improvements, such as being able to choose the next research rather than get a random item, and not having to carry things around with you all the time (you can make deliveries from your storage).For those new to the series, it's a building and fighting game. You build stuff, you get orders, you upgrade your equipment, and then you slay some monsters too. Early game is a grind, but that really makes you appreciate the automation which comes along later!It is set in a small sleepy town, and there is some social interaction too. You can talk to people and make friends (although the dialogue is very limited).Unfortunately, as with Portia, the voice acting is far from complete. Some entire scenes have ten or twenty lines of subtitled dialogue while the characters just grunt or say "uh-huh". Eventually I just turned off voices because it was so annoying.But I enjoyed the game and at 300 hours for a single playthrough, that's value for money! I would like to do some videos on it, but I think I will take a break for a while. The late game is as grindy as the early game but it's clicking through seemingly endless dialogue and sitting through endless cutscenes as a grind. It was more a relief than satisfying to finally see the credits roll and it did feel like a chore these last few (real life) days. But overrall, yeah, a good game even if incomplete.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderfully adorable game that only builds upon the wonderful ideas that My Time at Portia started.  I still love the whole "ruined technological world" aesthetic and enjoyed all the references to your hard-working builder in Portia.I found the story even more interesting than the Portia story and really enjoyed having a more friendly nature with your "rival" builder, unlike in Portia.  I felt very invested in Sandrock and really like how invested I got into the well-being of the town.I have thoroughly loved every minute of this game, but I do feel that the end game becomes a little tedious.  Once you get past the climax of the story and are only left with the city development stuff, story events start getting spread out and since most of your building is pretty self-sufficient due to the stockpiled resources, days can become quite empty and unfulfilling.  Additionally, while I like some romances being unavailable until later in the game (same as in Portia), some of the options only appear SUPER late, making it a slog to make friends with or romance the last few people.While I think these are valid criticisms, I still wholeheartedly love this game and look forward to putting many more hours into it.
