_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god how f*cking good is this game please? I've never had the urge to thank the developers for this game as much as I do here. I'm a fan of the genre, but what's on offer here is unique. I feel right at home in Sandrock now and would like to stay there all the time. No other game in the genre has ever managed to make me grow so fond of the inhabitants and their various character traits in such a pleasant and unobtrusive way. No other genre-typical game manages to make me so excited about the story and holy sh*t ... the story goes on and on and on and on and doesn't get boring, quite the opposite... I'm now looking at around 100 hours of gameplay, I haven't finished the main story yet but I'm getting the depressing thought that I'll soon reach the end. The game captures me so emotionally. The town and character development feels so alive, characters come and go, it's all just so good. I love this game so much, it has easily become one of my top 3 all-time favourite games.I've also played its predecessor My Time at Portia and had a good time there too, but Sandrock is 10x better for me on almost every level. _childDocuments_.review: I never played the predecessor because I somehow thought it was more of a game for kids. I regret that very much by now. Because My Time at Sandrock was a lot of fun and really captivated me.The story is kid-friendly, but I actually consider that a big plus. I’ll be happy to play the game together with my nephew in the near future. Parents don’t need to be afraid here, the game is absolutely family-friendly, and the predecessor was approved in Germany for 6 years and up. If the multiplayer is ready soon, this could be really fun for joint family gaming sessions.Sandrock is enormously complex, and at times still lacks a bit of beginner’s help. In parts, the story progress is a bit too tied to the crafting of a particular item. And then, it can take longer to progress, better get a candy bar.I don’t have much to complain about otherwise. The game is not perfect, there are a few small corners in the inventory system, so far some tooltips, book texts, or dialogues are not 100% well translated, and some are not even included yet.There is also by far not all game content in the game that the developers have planned. And the balancing is possibly also improvable. But overall, My Time at Sandrock already offers a lot more in-game content and fun at the Early Access release than many full-price AAA titles. My Time at Sandrock is a sandbox RPG diamond in the desert sand.After more than 25 hours of testing, I don’t feel like I’ve played through the game anytime soon. So here I assume easily 40-50 hours of playtime as a minimum, with upcoming expansions even more.Is My Time at Sandrock better than My Time at Portia? It is an evolution of the well-known and popular system. It offers a completely new story and new locations, as well as all sorts of improvements in gameplay, and completely new features are in the pipeline, such as multiplayer mode. In my opinion, fans of My Time at Portia can’t go wrong here, there’s more of what you loved. It’s the proven concept, expanded, enhanced with a new world and storyline, and all sorts of new stuff to play with as well.For the price of $24.99 or €24.99 (20,99 with release discount), My Time at Sandrock already offers a nearly complete game at Early Access release that combines many different elements of RPG, sandbox, survival, and life sim games.For the great concept, the extensive features, and the story and world that are suitable for children, but still appealing to adults, I would like to give a base score of 90 %. Minimal gaps in translation result in a 3 % deduction. This brings me to a current final rating on the My Time at Sandrock Early Access Release Date of 87 %.Since Pathea still has a large amount of additional content planned and the game should thus receive some major updates in the coming months, I expect that this rating could still rise above 90 %.EN DE

_childDocuments_.review: ✅ Interesting Story with Plot-Twists.✅ Lots of Content.✅ Great Artstyle.✅ Dungeons/Ruins hugely improved compared to Portia. ✅ Lots of different NPCs with great Storylines and Character-development. ✅ Most Voice Acting is pretty good (Burgi-boy especially).❌ Games is way too easy. Except the final Dungeon which I beat at Level63 (75 Enemies) I never died or even had to use Healing.❌ Lots of Side-Quests aren't voice-acted. Seems kinda random which Quests are voiced and which aren't. ❌ The Game teases you with your Childhood Friend very early on, but it literally takes until the Final Quest of the Game before you can romance her. I regret waiting the whole Game for her. ❌ The Pacing isn't perfect. Early on you get flooded with Quests and late in the Game you often times have nothing to do anymore. Spreading the Quests out a bit more would be nice.❌ I felt the Museum was kinda disappointing. In Portia I had more drive to donate stuff. After you donate 100 Items, which is pretty easy there is no reason to do anything anymore. Also the Museum lacks more Slots.❌ Decorating your House is clunky and annoying. You can't put Carpets near you bed because they somehow block the Bed?❌ The Perks are mostly completely useless. Its lots of x% change to get 1 Favor or something. Its completely pointless. ❌ There are some bugs. I had a Quest-Marker stuck on my Map for 100hrs. The Quest was completed but the Quest-Marker never went away. Overall, this is a huge improvement over Portia, but I'd recommend EVERYONE to play Portia first, because the Game kinda expects you to have played Portia. Without knowing all the Portia NPCs and most of the Story you'd miss out on a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time in Sandrock is the Sequel to My Time in Portia, a game that I found by chance and thankfully, found very entertaining. So entertaining in fact, that I purchased the next game in Early Access. And I'm happy I did. It's made jumps and leaps since My Time in Portia, not only graphically but also storywise, socially and in many other fields. The NPCs seem more fleshed out, lots of variety and the love interests are well written and have backgrounds that are interesting. (Except you Yan. F*** you Yan.) What I also love is that you can't rapid fire a relationship with someone, it really takes some time and effort, but there are multiple ways to garner affection with your targeted partner. Romance is a social gameplay mechanic that allows the player to date and eventually marry any eligible marriage candidate, regardless of gender.  The festivals are fun and so are the mini games that come along with some of them. The Building and Farming is tailored to the environment. You live in a desert so to find wood, you'd normally cut down trees right? WRONG! Well...I mean you can but everyone will hate you for it. Since you're based in the harsh desert, Water is a priority and anything that would disturb the delicate co system is forbidden. A nice tid-bit in game design.Combat and Dungeon exploring might not be the main focus of the game but it's still quite fun, which is good since it's integral to getting certain materials.All in all, it's a good game that will tie you up for QUITE a long time, Visually it's great, Character customisation is nicely done and while of course there are some small bugs here and there, for something not coming from a triple A studio, it's a really REALLY good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is awesome! Just like My Time at Portia, it has a good story line. I love the dungeons, challenges, and all the quests. But once we report these glitches, the developers are quick to get it fixed. In my mind, this game is cozy to play with and the crafting aspect of it is wonderful. I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: The multiplayer, however, feels really half-baked and rushed out the door just so they can have it as a checked-off feature. Me and my girlfriend looked into it before she bought it me, as many games have disappointed with multiplayer implementation as of late, and found that the story is not included when you play multiplayer, as well as characters get removed from your town if you don't log in after 2 months (What is this even doing in a relaxing farming game??). This almost stopped my girlfriend from getting the game for me, as we felt it would be just building for the sake of building with no real goals and logging in just to keep our save going rather than wanting to play. After looking up some gameplay and watching her play some single-player, I felt like "eh, let's just give it a try, the town planner seems like it will at least give us things to do..." but it got even worse as we booted into the character creator to realize the actually decent system is also strangely lacking content in multiplayer. For some reason, the devs have only implemented three faces for multiplayer even though there are eight in singleplayer?? It's such a weird design choice that I can't even figure out why this is a thing. For people who love creating characters like me and my partner, this was the moment we both looked at each other, said "Really?!" and then closed the game disappointed.We will probably come back and give this a try once stuff is added back in for multiplayer, but it's basically a separate game from the single-player and not one that I would recommend purchasing.Apparently systems like kids, the green house and the factory aren't going to be added in for multiplayer. They recently ported over some tools over to the multiplayer but again, there's even less content in the multiplayer than I was led to believe, even after research. I will be playing the single-player just so we can get our money's worth and the single-player is actually a game that feels fleshed out, so that's why my hours are going up despite being disappointed with the original thing we bought the game for. - No story in multiplayer.- After 2 months of not playing, your character is removed from the town.- Fewer face options in character creation, which for us was a big part of the game.- Some systems and tools are not in multiplayer, something I didn't even know about until their latest dev letter.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the My Time series. I purchased Sandrock over a year when it was in Early Access. I enjoyed it and looked forward to the full release. Now that the full release is out, the game has become essentially unplayable on my system, which is quite hardy. I'm not sure what they did in the last 6 months or whatever, but the load times are  awful and the game stops for 10 seconds at a time whenever there's story dialogue. The main loading screen comes up with this message saying "long load times are detected," and I should "check that my hard drive has space." I have 500 gb free. It's clearly some serious problem they created for themselves, because I played the game without issue less than a year ago, and it was nearly in a completed state.(Update Feb 7, 2024)In response to the developer's response: I AM using a SSD. It's in fact the exact same pc that ran the game fine in Early Access. It's also the same pc that runs every other game I've purchased without issue. My review was 3 months ago. I attempted to run the game today on a brand new save file, and encountered the same errors that made it unplayable. Ironically, the developers made a post about "addressing concerns," and they're still talking about people having issues with performance.It's unfortunate because I purchased My Time at Portia for both the PC and Switch because I was such a huge fan. Now, I've just sent a request to Steam for a refund (which they'll probably deny), for a game that I loved in Early Access. The developers have lost a fan, for whatever that's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: (Early Access review-- may change with future updates!)As a fan of the previous game, Portia, My Time At Sandrock has some excellent improvements that --so far-- have made it a pleasure to play. There's some incredibly useful things like being able to craft from your storage instead of needing the items in your inventory, and same for using the Assembly Station. That automatically puts it much higher.There's been some overhaul of the skill trees and character equipment, which is nice, and allows for a little more specialisation depending on what you want to prioritise.From the story chunk I've played so far (up to the end of available quests), things seem to be progressing in an interesting direction; we have a bit of a mystery and character dynamics to explore. Once more of the character based stories unlock and grow, I'm looking forward to seeing them develop. The mining section has been upgraded, and now suits thematically to Sandrock as well. I also appreciated the characters looking more in proportion, and the voice acting has matched the characters nicely. Since this is early access, I'll offer my thoughts on options and concepts I'd enjoy seeing implemented too:-I'd like to see more improvements to the town in terms of story and Building-- so far, there hasn't been much that has  the town, only fixed what was broken. Minus one story quest. Are we able to upgrade buildings or renovate or encourage new people to return? What about helping the townsfolk upgrade their buildings? Something along those lines to show the town is growing again.-The trash littering the ground. These reset daily to give the player scrap materials, except that it constantly makes the town look like a dump. What if instead of daily, the new sandstorms blow trash around? That would give the player plenty of clean days, while providing a storyline-setting related excuse to blow rubbish around.-Possibly adding more greenery to the town? There's a quest that lets you plant things. What if players, after reaching certain goals, could add more plants in locations around shops and houses and on roofs? There's plenty of roofs where one could easily put a garden bed and start planting things!-Another game or two for the Game Center. The original ones in Portia were quick and fun, whereas Sandrock's minigames aren't quite as fun or easy to grind tokens for prizes. They might add one more (there's a blank minigame there), but for now it's a struggle to play.-The ability to pin recipes. This would help when I need to find multiple items to make things and don't want to keep opening my handbook or run between the upgrade building to my storage to figure out what I need to craft.Since the devs are aware of the super-long loadtimes and are working to fix it, I'll state that on my end I haven't really found any gamebreaking bugs or issues. (There's a couple of weird collision spots around Mort's shack and in one level of the ruins but that's it for me.)*Update: I've had two game crashes now. There seemed to be no trigger; I'd go to move and everything freezes. Not bad in 60 hours.Overall, Sandrock is shaping up to be a fine successor to Portia; keeping the same core concepts and enhancing them with some much needed quality of life upgrades. I'm looking forward to seeing how the story unfolds, and in the meantime I'll work towards the rest of the achievements I can get currently.Well worth it if you enjoy mixed farming/crafting sims or you were a fan of the original!
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying My Time at Sandrock. It is similar to Portia, but with some differences. I like that I can craft items at the machines/workshop and assembly station without having to have them in my hot bar, it takes items from chest inventories. I like that running doesn't drain stamina as in Portia. I like most of the characters, and can't wait for them to all be fully voiced, but as this is early access, only some parts are voiced. I like that the gathering is different than in Portia and the new machines for scrap are a nice addition. Having a friendly building to work with is much better than the mean rival in Portia.Some of the things I do not like is the fact that the gardening does not work like the machines, so you have to go get all your gardening stuff to do your gardening actions before you start and have them in your inventory. I also do not like that if you are not in bed by midnight, then you wake up with "Panda Eyes" and are exhausted and tired. The game lets you stay up later, but you are not fully rested if you do not sleep by midnight. I would like to stay out till the game forces me to go to bed, and not have ill effects from it. I do not remember Portia having this effect on you if you collapsed while mining. I wanna say it might have used to, but they got rid of that in an update. I also am not too fond of that fact that it seems every day or so some new calamity makes all the prices increase for everything you purchase. There are some characters that I don't like, but that is expected as you can't like everyone, and I know some are made to be antagonistic such as the head of the builders guild. In my opinion though, there are fewer bachelors/bachelorettes than in Portia, but that could be because it is still in early access, and that was one of the wishlist goals that was reached but not implemented yet. Overall it is a fun game to play and I would recommend to anyone that likes Portia, or any other farming/building sim type games.

_childDocuments_.review: was a real surprise for me when I first played it. I'm pretty sure I got it in a bundle. It looked like someone had repurposed the assets of a Korean MMO from 2010. But it turned out to be an unexpectedly feature rich game with an interesting post-apocalyptic worldbuilding, gameplay with genuinely novel ideas in combining the day-to-day work cycle and socializing of  with softer factory game mechanics and combat, and just a good amount of content that was fun despite the jank. takes all the good ideas of its predecessor which felt accidentally good at many times, and elevates them so you can make no mistake that Pathea are actually a really talented and hardworking company that knows what they're doing. Is it free of jank? No, not really. But it's so chockful of good things that even the jank becomes charming. It has a great, interesting story full of characters with vibrant personalities and not the paper-thin cutouts you get in . The world of the setting is so fully realized despite the series' cartoony nature and you feel excited to explore and learn about it. It is genuinely laugh out loud funny at many points, and genuinely emotional at others. I have to give it up for the VAs who don't seem like professionals but are still giving their best. The building gameplay while its core loop is the same, sees a lot of QOL improvements. The combat is more dynamic and offers a bit of challenge though it's still on the casual side. There's so many small charming details too, like when you go on dates in-game, they put in an animation where your significant other holds your hand. They didn't have to do that. It has no mechanical value. It's just cute and it makes you feel good.Stuff like that is why I think most of all, what the game nails is that it makes it good to be in Sandrock, and to see Sandrock grow. Everyone who plays games for long enough understands the feeling where a place in a game becomes like a real place we have visited and been in, and we feel a sort of nostalgia seeing it. I think Sandrock will feel that way to many people playing the game, it's such a wonderfully crafted setting, and it really fulfills the promise of the genre of "Life Sim" where you can take a break from reality and live somewhere else for a little while. I'm not even done with the main story. I restarted with 1.0 to experience it as intended since in Beta lots of the quests squished together in buggy ways as they were implemented, but I feel glad to have done that. This is gonna be a game I will have good memories of and consider a favorite years from now.P.S. Just to be clear, I'm only really reviewing the single-player experience. I have not tried and am not that fussed about multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: A true spiritual successor to My Time at Portia. It plays smoother, better, and yet the core gameplay is still the same. So if you enjoyed the way you build your way through the main story and side quests in Portia, you will find it here too, but better.Some of my favorite improvements are:- The cutscenes are A LOT more polished- Inventory management is a lot better. For example, now you don't have to have an item in your inventory to give it to an NPC for a commision.- The characters and their backstories, lore and interactions are a lot more organic- The festivals and events are better made, tooBasically, if you like games like Stardew Valley and My time at portia, you'll love this one, too!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked My Time at Portia you'll be happy with the follow up! I wasn't crazy about the change in UI when I first started playing it since it's so different from Portia, but once I got used to it I have to say it is better overall. There are other features that have been changed from the first game and mostly they are positive. Some negatives however is the house designing, I'd prefer there to be preset houses you can build as the current building system is a bit wonky and I can't make something that I actually like. Combat offers more options in terms of weapon selection, but it's still very brainless, spam the attack button til everything is dead, dodging is very optional unless you decide to tackle mobs much higher in level than you are (but honestly that's a bad idea regardless as you do so little damage if you are under leveled that fights take forever). There is a nice variation of dungeons to explore and gather loot, however to get the best score you only need to worry about time, so you can blow thru every level killing almost nothing (except the few enemies in certain spots you have to kill to move forward) and get the best score vs if you fight and kill everything you will get a worst score because you took too long. It would be better if it was a combo of time/enemies killed. The new ruin/mining system is much better than the first game and more changes have been promised so it can only get even better! The story that is currently available is nice and intriguing, my only complaint is I want more, but that is the issue starting an early access game. Overall very worth it, give me more content please!

_childDocuments_.review: Quantity over quality. While we're seeing a massive increase in harvest moon type games after the success of Stardew Valley, we're now in a time period where the demand for these types of games is bigger than when Harvest Moon was still kicking. And so with demand and supply at an all time high, we're seeing a lot of takes on the farming sim genre. Most other farming sims try to replicate what Stardew Valley did, while adding a different setting. A lot of the newer farming sims try to set themselves apart from the competition by doing something unique, so what does My Time at Sandrock do?My time at Sandrock, and Portia as well to be fair, are games where the developers add half baked features inspired by other farming sims into the game that they will never completely finish. Combat exists but every single enemy encounter is dealt with in the exact same way. There is no strategy beyond button mashing and rolling. The main story is servicable, super forgettable.NPC's have improved since Portia but are incredibly forgettable and tropey. By reaching a certain friendship level you get a little cutscene/quest with the character, but these aren't anything to write home about. What makes Stardew Valley great is the different characters and their stories. Whereas these characters don't develop beyond what you learn about them in the main storyI didnt mind doing daily tasks in Portia as it was a fairly new spin to the Farming Sim Genre, but it got very exhausting near the end of the game and felt like it was only there to keep you busy. Sandrock has done nothing to improve this system except make it even more grindy than it was before. Would recommend this game if you've played all the other Farming Sims on the market and still need more.Give Runefactory 4 a shot, maybe replay Stardew Valley, try replaying some of the older Harvest Moon games (not remakes). Just make sure to come back to me once you've experienced what a rewarding gameplay loop and interesting characters are like.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of My Time at Portia, but I prefer multiplayer games in general - so when Sandrock came out, of course I was super excited. While let down that multiplayer isn't out yet (at the time of my review) I tried the game anyway. My biggest issue is that the game itself seems to run very hard on my computer, which it really shouldn't. I've turned down every setting as low as possible... installed the game onto my SSD... like, the game lags bad in certain aspects for me, yet in the multiplayer testing - it is just fine. I'm not entirely sure why. That said, that doesn't make me not recommend this game though. I still play it and I still REALLY enjoy it when I can get the game to stable and not lag. The characters are interesting, world is immersive - game is every bit as fun as MTAP was; the only thing I wish they'd change is adding back rock paper scissors. idk why I miss that, buuut I do. The critter game just isn't as fun to me and seems WAY more of a gamble, lol but maybe i'll change my mind about it once I figure it out more.In general, if you like crafting/farming sims, you'll probably like MTAS.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played My Time at Portia about a year or so ago after finding it on sale for the Switch. After completing the main story missions, I found out about Sandrock after checking out some things online and very impatiently waited for the early access version... and I'm obsessed. When Disney Dreamlight Valley came out, I put this one on the backburner, but I picked it back up recently and really got the hang of it and I am obsessed and again, impatiently waiting for the next update. _childDocuments_.review: I was already in love with Portia. Sandrock adds an additional layer of depth to the world and to the previous game while sticking to what it's good at.It's a laid back experience (especially on lower speeds), with well crafted characters and lovingly created story moments which draw you in even further. A refreshing take on the whole genre that tried something different with their previous game and improved upon their predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: If you love games like Stardew Valley or Coral Island I think you'll love this game. It's similar in the game style, but instead of a farmer you're a builder. The storyline is amazing, with plot twists, and the game is definitely grindy. You'll get to points where you can't progress without upgrading your machines, and then it's a mad dash to get everything needed. There's also reference to My Time at Portia since the stories take place at the same time, PLUS multiplayer mode now, which I haven't gotten to explore yet, but look forward to!
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing and addicting game loop. I initially played this because of MT Portia but this is way better. The qol changes were a welcome addition and the actual story is longer. At times it did feel a bit slow and the house building mechanics is not intuitive. Its not hard but it can be improved upon. There are game mechanics that I didnt care for but overall I liked about 90% of them. The fights got pretty monotnous and it showed no challenge up to a certain point and the skill tree is only useful in the early stages. Wish that the new game Evershine will have a better load out for the skill tree.The best thing about the game has to be the NPC and their stories. Going into this game I didnt know that the old yakboy rancher would be one of my favorites. The story itself is really fun and there is a plethora of references to pop culture that I really adore. It is a very charming game and I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND it. If you enjoy a slower paced game then you will love this one. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game right around its release through early access and watching this game grow and develop was a really cool experience. After playing many hours in My Time At Portia, this game is truly the sequel I was looking for! Relaxing and fun gameplay all the way through, many ways to build relationships and gain experience, and just a whole new vibe compared to Portia. The devs are awesome at fixing bugs and taking the players opinions into consideration. One of my favorite games and can't wait to see where else this game goes. <3
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: What a MASSIVE improvement from My Time in Portia, which was already an incredible game! Many many improvements overall. Most notably the graphics, improved character models, visuals & aesthetics of the game! The biggest and greatest change for me. Is the storage. Yes correct, storage and inventory management is a thing of the past with this new system! You can now auto-store all stacks of items across all your stashes at once! Thus allowing you to keep unique items on you, but stack up all your inventory junk instantaneously. Not only that. But your stashes act as a sort of backpack now. Anything in your stashes count as being on your person for the sake of crafting, handing in commissions etc.. This is a GAME CHANGER as the most tedious park of Portia that burnt me out and prevented me from completing it. Was the CONSTANT inventory management. In Sandrock you can now auto-store all stacks then continue the focus on having fun! And boy is it fun! there is 2-4x the content than in Portia, and with inventory management to the wayside. You can really dive in and just get lost in the experience!I can't really find any faults with the game. For the price you are paying this is def a 10/10 product imo.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I loved My Time at Portia, so when they announced they were working on a new game that related to it, I was ecstatic and immediately looked into it. Thankfully, I was gifted it as a late valentine's day gift of sorts, and I immediately set about playing it. So far it is still in Early Release, but is amazing thus far. I'm a little bummed that I've already caught up to the story content thus far, and that you can't really romance anyone and get married as of yet, but it's not even fully released yet, so it's not too surprising. I eagerly await for more content to come out and will likely update my review as it goes along.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game just over 24 hours before posting this review and already have spent a lot of time playing it. One of the things I really like is that I can save my progress at any point - I don't have to make my character go to sleep just to save. I like that getting blueprints for the machines and the materials needed for crafting takes a bit of time as well - this game is not a quick play-through, which is the type of game I prefer.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed My Time At Portia, you will enjoy this - it's similar yet different enough to have the same fun experience but new. That said, there are definitely some clunky things about this one. The story flow feels really intrusive; you're trying to get familiar with the mechanics but keep getting bombarded with cutscenes and story that you're not ready to take in - additionally the somewhat different mechanics feel obstructive and at times frustrating; it takes forever to level things up or get anywhere, in some ways. Just upgrading your worktable the first time is a giant ordeal.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a truly beautiful sequel and stand alone game that deserves all the praise in the world. As early access it had plenty of quirks but with the full release there has been a huge amount of change and smoothness added. Overall a visually stunning, funny, fun, addictive game for anyone looking to meet and befriend cute quirky characters, scrap, build, cook, and play a new world of a post-apocalyptic jewel.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: like the first game in the series (My time at portia), Sandrock is a charming take on the Slice of life genre.It has all the trappings of a "farming sim" other than having much to do with farming.  You meet interesting townsfolk, and maybe romance someone.  despite being the newest member of an established community you somehow have to become the core of the community *and* the savior in a year or two.  You build a small "honest" business from nothing to spectacular in a similar time frame (in this case it's a workshop that makes furniture/machines)Almost every change from portia is a positive one.  Kept everything that made the first game work, and did some new stuff that really makes it better
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

It has crafting, gathering, minigames, combat, exploration and so much more! I have not yet played single player, and have exclusively played multiplayer at this point, but we are having a great time and look forward to where the devs take the game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you come across randomly, then you are 100 hours into the game. I got this game when it was early access and I can confirm that it delivered what it promised. _childDocuments_.review: If you played my time at portia and enjoyed it, there's no question that you MUST get this game. It's very true to the spirit of the first game, but with changes that make it feel much improved. For example, there are new mechanics to keep it interesting, some quality of life changes (you can pretty much access everything in your chest from anywhere, even if you are going to turn in a commission), and obviously the visuals are much improved! _childDocuments_.review: In the last week I've played this game for 80 hours. So I like it. Just a a little.My sister bought me this since she'd played the beta. Normally I'm not the most excited to play life sims with farming in it because the market is oversaturated with samey, boring games that wish they could be like Stardew Valley.Instead, I got a game where I don't have to farm if I don't want to (except for some quests but. No daily watering anyway, so that's dope). The story itself has been super enjoyable, and fun. I didn't think it'd ramp up like it did, but serious, emotional moments would pop up out of nowhere, and it felt like such a treat. I can do basically anything, and at my own pace. There's very little the game stopped me from doing that wasn't story related. It's fun to have all the options in the world, and have none of them be a bad on.Sandrock has easily become one of my favorite games, and I hope there's more like it and Portia in the future.

Between the two Games i like this one better. For me i got 32 Hours gameplay out of the content that is implemented so far and a few side quests that came up later when i had a better reletionship with the characters. What i really like is that the developers learned how plants are grown in the desert and Implement this into the game and that we have to converse water. A re-load of the last save game or save at that moment and re-load that helps to get right of that bug. For the gardening i would love if we have the plant menu open that we didn't have to have all the things in the inventory to use it, but that we could use them right out from the chests instead.Otherwise i have enjoyed the Early Access Gameplay so far and i'm looking forward to the future updates that are to come.

_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: So far this feels like a downgrade to Portia.- Even though it is essentially the same game, loading times entering/exiting buildings are way too long, even on m.2 SSD with high end hardware. Runs like crap in general, 50-75 FPS around my house in a an empty area with nothing in it with RTX 3080 and 5900X. My PC fans are pretty loud too. It is weird hitting the same temperatures in a cartoon game as in Cyberpunk.- The skill tree is dull. Every category, every direction is like...10% XP to whatever the activity is. Not very exciting is it.- Energy management feels absolutely terrible. Within 1 hour of waking up, I'm out of energy. I sit in a chair for 5 minutes and browse online, switch back, break 2 rocks, I'm out of energy. Can't get anything done, have yet to take a single commission because I have no energy to get even basic materials.- The game floods you with pointless items from the very beginning. I filled up my 30 slot inventory on day 1. I bought 15 more inventory slots, filled them up on the next day. Inventory management is incredibly painful.- Machines also feel like they work slower, running non-stop and processing very few resources. They now don't just need fuel (which you have no energy to mine up), but also water, which is a separate resource you have to get too.- Character dialogues are way too repetitive. I get that this is early access, I get that not everything will be voiced, but if the NPCs repeat the same sentence at me 3 days in a row, something is wrong. It's been months since the beta. Adding a 2nd sentence shouldn't be very hard.So yea if you enjoy AFK simulators waiting for timers and energy to recover, go for it. I'll give it a bit more time, but so far I'm really disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is the most polished and streamlined game in it's genre. When you go to use a machine, the first tab that opens shows you exactly the materials you need for commissions, assemblies and side tasks. Not only that, it automatically selects the quantity you'll need to complete those things. You don't need to dismount before entering a building. All available missions are conveniently displayed to you on your map and in your mission log. All inventory chests can be accessed from any chest, effectively making one massive storage split apart into smaller compartments. There's a sort all button that will automatically take your inventory items and slot them into their respective chest, assuming a copy of that item is already stored. It's amazing. The game massively reduces the amount of time spent in game menus and gets you back into the parts of the game you want to spend more time in. It will be very difficult to go back to other village life sims after having been spoiled by Sandrock.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: What a game....If you're like me, you probably got roped into this game after finishing Stardew Valley. Probably itching for the same type of chill, farming and building type of vibes.Instead, what I received was a compelling storyline, great voice acting, and extremely likeable and all around unique characters, as well as an ending that left me wanting for more. Not going to spoil anything, but the twists in this game keep you hooked for what's to come after every main quest.Beyond that, MTAS is one of the few games where you look back at what you've done and felt like you've made an impact. Pieces of your work are sprinkled in full view all over the town, and your relationship with NPCs reflect that as well. You'll get that sensation that your Builder has truly grown into someone remarkable, worthy of their title by the game's end.Sure, the game might have a tad few bugs lying around, even after release, but honestly the fact that the story was good enough to push me through does spell out something for the writing in this game.I had a bittersweet ending to My Time at Sandrock. To know that such an amazing journey will come to an end leaves an empty feeling in my heart, and yet, I look forward to the next entry.Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes what was already a great experience in My Time at Portia and makes it even better. The crafting, delivery, and building systems are all more streamlined and smoother. The story is more engaging and the stakes are higher, which makes caring about the different projects more effortless. The variety of characters is wider while also maintaining the charm and familiarity of the characters from the original game. Even just the small but very vital change of making the autosave more forgiving, and allowing manual saves at any time, is a huge improvement and changes the game completely. I loved Portia, I put hundreds of hours into it, and this game surpasses that experience in every way. Mining, building, and fighting make for engaging and addictive gameplay, as they did in the first game, only it's all easier, smoother, and less frustrating. If you liked Portia, you'll love this game! And if you enjoy games like Minecraft, Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, etc, you should check this one out too.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited on the 4.0 patch (still not full release).Sandrock feels like it's taken two steps forward and one step back compared to Portia. It's not to say that I hate the game, I've definitely been having fun. It's just not what I was expecting. Some of the mechanics are similar, some have been improved but there's also random filler put into parts of the game that is just annoying or strange.The combat feels just as clunky as Portia. There is different attack combos on different weapon types that feel stiff and forced. Monsters now also have barriers that you can break to get some extra damage and daze them. It's just so awkward that combat quickly became incredibly monotonous. Oh and you can shoot guns now.The early game is fetching piles of scrap that give you everything you need and more for most jobs and commissions. It drains your stamina incredibly quickly so that you have to order ridiculous amounts of food at the Inn or sit on a bench for a measly amount of stamina regeneration. The game even prompts you in the loading screen to order huge amounts of food. The only thing that really speeds things up is tool upgrades that unlock based on story progress. In Portia you could raise your attack stat to break things quicker but in Sandrock most gathering is locked behind "tool strength" with few ways to increase it, which I thought was a missed opportunity for gear and accessories.Some of the townsfolk are frustrating. I'm sorry but I rolled my eyes at the stereotypes and unoriginal characters. You remember that overly camp secretary from Portia called Antione? Yep. There's someone called Pablo who looks incredibly similar, is very camp and this time LOVES FASHION AND GOSSIP. There's also the typical old lady tailor and a character that is basically Annie from League of Legends (bear and all) to name some others.The social grind is now actually manageable. The story and game length are long enough that you will most likely befriend at least a few people before "finishing" the game.Each of them give a bonus at different stages in the friendship like they did in Portia. However, when you get around to earning those perks, you probably won't need them because you are so far into the game already. It was the same issue in Portia. I'm half a year into the game and just unlocked a +100 hp bonus when I already have about 4.5k.There's now a quality system with crafting that adds some depth to the workshop side of the game but it didn't actually feel relevant for most of the game, outside of wanting the most from your equipment or the occasional high quality commission. Tools, weapons, gear accessories all have randomised stats on it so you'd better pray for a good roll if you're hunting for some good items early on, or enjoy re-rolling them over and over until you get the one you want.P.S The game doesn't tell you what random affixes/stats are even available on each item so you'll have to work it out yourself, enjoy re-rolling!Tooltips are misleading, some completely wrong and a lot still have poor English. There's a luck stat. What does it do? Who knows because the game doesn't tell you.There's trash everywhere in town. I cleaned up everything I saw and 2 days later it was worse than before. Let me build some darn bins so I can teach these townsfolk how to put their rubbish in it.The environment is cool, albeit a little monotonous at times. There are also parts of the map that are just completely ugly. The desert has rocks that look okay from a distance but when you are next to them, they are a completely different style to the rest of the game. They literally look like big blobs of cheese.The map is enormous for no apparent reason and not in a good way. There's so much nothingness in some areas. I had to set my time scale all the way down because traversing the desert to explore it took an entire day.There's weird invisible barriers where it looks like there shouldn't be. The map doesn't match up with the world in some areas. There's gaps, seams and holes in some areas of the map. The research in this game can still be frustrating. I'd been churning out research for new machines every day but because you can only research one thing at a time and it takes days to complete I got locked for a week in game on story content because I wanted to research the cooking stations. You can't queue research either, so you have to run over to the building every time you want to start a new research.House decorating is an absolute shemozzle. You have very limited decoration options, most things don't match, adding multiple stories means multiple staircases which by default seem to take up 1/4 of a room. Moving buildings can send huge amounts of items from your machines/chests/house to your mailbox. Picking machines or chests up is incredibly annoying. Your cursor will auto default to the middle option most times which is "retrieve". Guess what happens if you accidentally click it? More items to your mailbox.There's no pathing options.Storage and inventory management is a mess. I wish luck to anyone who isn't a compulsive sorter by nature. You can quick dump items but guess what happens if you use up all of that item? You gotta find the box it goes in when you get another. There are HUNDREDS of items.What's worse is that the bigger chests have pages, so opening a chest means you have to flick through different pages sometimes.It seems like they didn't realise quite how big the game was going to get and just slapped on extra pages to your inventory and chests to compensate.The museum is incredibly dull in this game. They should have literally kept it the same as Portia but open straight off the bat like it is in Sandrock. Apart from a luck necklace reward (which again, is not explained what it actually does) and a few social points with one person, I saw no point to donating things. I barely saw anyone in it and the only time I'd actually get social points from them admiring items, they were relics that I'd put on my house or in my workshop, not actually in the museum.Load times can still be long at times and you'll have to enter a lot of houses and buildings because there are so many things indoors (restaurant/commission board/research/people/shops, etc). I can see this still being an issue for people with lower-middle range computers.Despite all of this, Sandrock just has that juicy gameloop which they have really nailed. It feels rewarding to play and you always have something to do or work towards. You are constantly fixing or upgrading things around town. You are always earning Gols or earning hearts with the townsfolk. It's just solid.There's also a story that is a little bit more cohesive than Portia. It's still got it's clunky moments but it tells it through cut scenes and is sprinkled in better portions. I will say that most smaller side quests weren't voiced, which is fine... but reading the dialogue with just the background music is deafeningly quiet compared to the main story quests. Please add some  "hmm/ahh/okay" or at least the text noises that the rest of the game's dialogue has.The UI is pleasant and readable most of the time. The talent/knowledge page has an awful description layout but it seemed fine other than that.The ruin diving was a huge improvement. The dungeons are more visually interesting. Good enemy variety.Farming is cool. Sand fishing is cool. I like both of them being styled a bit different to most farming sims.If you are happy to wait I would recommend letting the game get a few rounds of polish but if you buy it now I'm sure you will still enjoy it. There's A LOT of game and you will absolutely get bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: This followup to My Time at Portia contains a similar charm to it's predecessor. The story is very engaging, and there's a lot to do beyond a regular farming sim. I think there were a lot of aspects the game has improved on. For example, having the location set in a desert and having water as a limited resource was a unique and interesting mechanic. Being able to take on multiple commission tasks a day with diverse options (building/fishing/hunting) allows more flexibility in gameplay and progression speed. The voice acting is also a significant improvement from Portia as previously it was quite hit and miss with some characters. There are some gameplay changes from Portia that are not as well implemented, or just doesn't feel as fun - the notable areas would be fishing (quite boring), farming (extremely laborious), and home design (confusing/frustrating). Didn't even really try dating as my character was proposed to very early?? Despite these drawbacks, I still really enjoyed playing through the story and hope Pathea will continue the series. There are several good sequel opportunities with the story and world they've built.

_childDocuments_.review: Not until late game, but planting with the mech is broken and not in a good way. No matter the size of the grid, it doesn't plant correctly. I plant a 4x4 on a 4x4 plot, during planting the trees for a green wall, and it plants one tree in the middle of the grid. This leads to whole sections either taking forever (using 1x1 only) or trees being all over the or even running out of spots to put all the trees. Something like this, for a story mission, should not exist at this stage of the game.Aside from that, the DLC, while cosmetic, is really too much and adds nothing to the actual game. The monsters are not really worth it and only serve to collect things that you can do on your own. The romance DLC is also not worth it, for just a few extra romance quests for people that I at least know I am not interested in.After a point, I found myself sleeping before noon, with little to do.Game is Ok and I would suggest it on a deep discount (with out getting any DLC), but overall I can't recommend the game due to the issues and business model for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has brought me a lot of joy in the almost 300 hours I have played it, however I cannot recommend it to others as there are currently two critical/showstopper bugs that have not been fixed since release:1. In single player, the game looks much worse than the trailers and screenshots on Steam. Regardless of your hardware or graphics settings, the shaders are busted leaving all the models looking flat and the colors washed out.2. For many people in single player, the game has crippling loading issues. Doesn't matter if you run the game off SSD and/or lower graphics settings, many are having severe loading issues constantly during gameplay.I will gladly change this review once those core and near game-breaking bugs are fixed. It really is a charming game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:  180 hrs in (a few playthroughs):  This is exactly how early access is supposed to work.  They released the first couple of chapters with a good bit of polish, steadily released new content and patches and ACTUALLY FINISHED DEVELOPMENT.   The final product is an awesome game.  If you liked Portia or really any kind of crafting/life sim kind of game, this is one you don't want to miss. Two days out from early access launch, the game is still rough around the edges and incomplete, but it is already quite fun.  While following the spirit of My Time at Poria, it is different enough to make it interesting and new.  Definately recommend and can't wait to see the complete version.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy, quality sequel. “My Time at Portia” was a decent game, but “My Time at Sandrock” takes nearly all the ideas to the next level, making it hard to go back to the previous game.The game does a good job of combining lore and gameplay elements, which is quite unusual and pleasant for the genre. Thanks to the fact that the player has a goal from the very beginning, and the set of actions is mostly based on how the world is structured, the game feels cohesive. For example, the ability to plant crops is not just given because it’s necessary, but due to certain plot events, and it’s given by an NPC. The process of growing plants, although a bit tedious and requires excessive micromanagement, is still justified by the game world: water is scarce, the soil isn’t the best, so you have to put in the effort.There’s a lot of content in the game, it unfolds quite slowly, but that’s not a downside, because there’s always something for the player to do. Both the main quest and all the side quests may not be Tarantino-level in terms of execution, but they’re adequately composed, always capable of keeping the game interesting.The game has a few downsides:Overall, My Time at Sandrock is a worthy representative of the sandbox genre. The gameplay, except for the combat component, is decent, the plot is also decent, the graphics are decent, albeit with a specific stylization. Against the backdrop of glitchy, unfinished games, this one looks pretty good.

I bought it knowing full well it wasn't going to be finished right out of the box, and had a couple of crashes, thankfully those have since been fixed. I will however say, Add cosmetic "armor" slots or allow players to refine armors. That way we can wear what we like best without sacrificing defence or other perks to the armor.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally find Mtas alot more interesting and addictive than Mtap. Having played both for well over 100 hours (on mobile and console for Mtap), Mtas just feels more put together and offers more fun mechanics. The mining aspect is still a bit grindy, but also significantly more fun than it was in the previous game. I also really enjoyed the new house building mechanic as it gives alot more freedom and allows for more personal designs. However, I do wish they didn't make such large gaps between furniture placements and allowed us a little more freedom with furniture placements like allowing diagonal placements or placing more decorative objects on surfaces. The romance options are abundant and each one comes with at least 1 romance quest and special item that you can only get through romancing, although we all know who you'll end up marrying in the end...  The new monster hunter update is very cute. It makes it alot easier to farm resources from very early on, especially water if you don't want to spend money on water at the tower. There are also a few bugs the occasionally occur, but nothing detrimental to the story or even just casual play.

The audio distortion followed by crashes was an issue they claimed to have fixed in the June 7th, 2022 patch notes, but several people complained they still had the issue and it was never mentioned by the devs again.This is the second time Pathea has released a game that I literally cannot play because of all the constant crashing even out of early access.EDIT: After returning to the game I no longer have issues as long as I do not touch the multiplayer mode, playing the multiplayer mode will result in crashes within minutes of playing. _childDocuments_.review: So, I'm kinda old.  When I say "My first game was Pong."  I mean it.  I've played and beaten a LOT of games.  The first game I beat was "Raiders of the Lost Ark" for the 2600.  I've been playing for a while.Why do I bring this up?  I'm SO happy you asked.I can't just sit and have marathon game sessions anymore.  Neck/back/hand pain, and, /sigh responsibilities...But, because circumstances (and the help of various remedies) i was able to finally put a few uninterrupted hours into this.   Fast forward almost 12 hours.  This game is a great "Just one more day/turn/scenario/event.", and it hooked me in even further than I had already been invested.  Now I'm sore and writing this dumbass review.There are few games that can get and most importantly keep my attention anymore.  This is one of them.  Interesting characters, quests that keep you advancing as well as keeping you interested, lots of customization.Oh, OK.  Old ass, what's the downside?Well, super simplistic combat, not any real consequence for dialog choices (other than making things more difficult for yourself), some mini-games controls are a bit meh, repetitive/grindy game play (hunt/gather) .Bottom line, if you like life sim/building/planting/mining games, you will probably like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. Is there some jank? Sure. Did some of the voice acting performances make the STRANGEST choices imaginable? Yes. Is it an extremely addictive and rewarding game to engross yourself in? Most Definitely. Honestly this game has excellent gameplay loops, incredible level design, and a surprisingly well written story (there have been multiple times when something didn't add up that was revealed to have been untrue, many decisions that characters have made that just make sense narratively, and many ideas that were set up and then totally brought to fruition later instead of being forgotten about and abandoned later). I can't recommend it enough. I feel like I'm coming to the end of my single player campaign, but there is still multiplayer to enjoy and other characters to romance... I'm sure I'll be visiting Sandrock again!

_childDocuments_.review: Though I haven't gotten very far, I have to say, I am having so much fun with this game! _childDocuments_.review: If you want to make stacks of money and grow a capitalist empire... go play Stardew Valley. As for My Time at Sandrock, here we enjoy exploring, talking to NPCs, playing mini games as well as getting some materials along the way.You don't have to rush through the game. You have time to get your resources and enjoy all there is around the town as well. Yes, for a few in-game days I felt like I couldn't make any money and the game was really difficult... and then I kept playing. Ya know... for more than three hour ;) and I was doing just fine balancing out material gathering/socializing/etc. I actually find it much more entertaining so far in this game to balance out the aspects of my characters life. This leads me to another thing: I actually feel like my character/the townspeople/the town itself and even the landscape are a lot more ALIVE in this game. They have put a lot of love and detail into the energy this game breathes... and trying to rush through that hard work does not seem to be the intend play style for this game.In my opinion, this game is delivering everything and more that I was missing from My Time at Portia. It is also an EARLY ACCESS release, so the developers deserve more time and patience from all of us. Thank you for creating a lifesim that reminds me not to let my character pass out somewhere... this is what we need after being taught to go go go. Slow down a bit, and come to Sandrock!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game took me by surprise. I did not play My Time at Portia, but I thoroughly enjoy playing this one. The overall artstyle, the mixed desert/western and ruined civilization theme, and the general gameplay loop make My Time at Sandrock a solid purchase. There is quite a bit to do and the game seems to have enough varied content to appeal to several types of people. This game holds my interest far greater than other social sims/RPGs like it. It's insanely satisfying to take on the role of a builder and aid the town through economic turmoil by taking on commissions and helping out individuals. Using water as a scarce, critical resource is a fantastic idea (while admittedly not original) for this type of game and setting. Many of the characters are interesting enough to want to build up your relationship stat with them day-to-day. Mi-an, the fellow builder who also recently moved into Sandrock, is a great character and her addition really helps remind you of your role through good will and some friendly rivalry. It's easy to become invested in this world.The game is very clearly Early Access, however. Performance is an issue and crashing is inevitable. You can tell some features haven't been fully implemented. The characters aren't all consistently fully voice-acted and will repeat the same 3 lines of dialogue for day-to-day interaction. The skill tree needs more than 10% changes to abilities. The devs seem to know what they are aiming for in the finished product, however, and I only wish I waited to play this at full release.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up, but keep in mind a lot of stuff's still missing and likely will be for a long while. It's the beginning of early access, not all the story's in yet (about 30 hours worth before you hit the current end point), and it's obvious that things are not implemented yet (perks locked, friendship missions mostly limited to a few characters while several others have little to none, no marriage yet and some romance options not yet implemented, etc.). However, especially if you're a fan of My Time at Portia, this is pretty dang good. I do like the general feel and flow of the game and so far it's been better than MTAP in my opinion. Unfortunately some stuff that wasn't so great in MTAP is here as well--awkward friendship/romance mechanics, anyone?--but overall considering this just went into early access and therefore has a lot of patches and content additions ahead of it the overall result is quite decent. If you're someone who hasn't played MTAP before I would recommend playing that one first, at least at this point--it's not necessary for playing this game, it's just that this one is still a bit too incomplete and clunky for those not familiar with the previous game, imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Previously, I had a bad review for this game because of certain things that I thought were missing, such as the homey feel that Portia had. However, the devs blew up all the complaints I had up. Of course, there were things I preferred that were different but ultimately didn't matter in the review.  Firstly, the characters are simply amazing and will have you laughing. Unsuur is so funny to me, I can't describe it. You'll have to buy the game yourself to understand it. The residents of Sandrock really shine through the side quests and the main storyline. I can only imagine how great this game will be once it's fully finished. Secondly, the graphics are lovely. Riding on your horse around this dry paradise will have your soul warmer than the sun. It's a different feeling, I tell you! During events if the best place to take pictures, especially during the last winter event. Definitely improved from the previous game. Screenshots alone aren't enough to truly experience the graphics of the game. Although, the graphics do make my pc turn into an airport. Just a thing to keep in mind. Thirdly, the story is great. It makes sense and really builds upon the world-building. Like the character, the story got lots of giggles out of me from the sheer surprise of some of the parts. I'll be so sad when the main storyline ends, but also glad I got to play through it. Finally, the gameplay is interesting to me. I like how you can either make a small hut for a house or a huge castle to show off your dominance. At first, I didn't like some of the mechanics such as needing water and fuel for your machines, but I got into it and it didn't really matter anymore. It just adds an extra challenge to the game. Also, the fact you have such cool weapons to pick from with different animations just sits right with me. My personal favorite is the daggers. (P.S. Thank goodness the devs fixed the stamina.)If any of these factors sound appealing to you, I'd suggest you give this game a try. I don't regret it, and I bet you won't, too.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the wait!! I held off until most of the game was ready because I loved Portia and I wanted to experience Sandrock in full. With over 300hrs played, it's one the best games I've played in YEARS!! Everything they wanted to fix from Portia, they did. _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock is a fun game! Sure, it's Early Access, but the amount they have already created is amazing! The character art is an upgrade from their last title, I'm happy that the characters are voiced. I guess I'm writing this review because I've played a lot of farming games, and I mean A LOT, and MTaS has found a way of making the experience refreshing. There are some minor improvements I would make so far like having more of the romantic dialogue being voiced, your SO doesnt really call you by your name, so there's not really a reason to not have them voiced. I feel it would make the game more immersive. I would like more date options when it comes to locations and romantic festival holidays.As far as the game mechanics, It would be really awesome if we got reminders for the blue quests, some have deadlines, others do not and I forgot some of them because the game didnt remind me, and i couldnt differentiate without going into the laggy menu to check all the time. Inventory and storage system is great, i just wish that commissions detected my items in my storage as well as my bag. Why am I making things that I already have??Last complaint: maybe make the horse rent cheaper by 50% since everything in this game costs money? either that or make the fast travel free. (oh and also it would be nice if the horse rent would renew itself until cancelled, or would pop up with a "your horse rent is almost over, would you like to renew?" having to run over there every week is annoying.)Tbh though, those are nitpicks. It's early access, it's really good. There is a finite place that you can take the game to at this point in time. I have already become the #1 workshop, I already have a boyfriend, and have completed all main quests, I've just decided that i'll keep playing to get my animals and structures ready to go.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: I started out playing My Time at Portia, and have been so excited to play the not-quite-sequel, My Time at Sandrock. It's early days yet, but I can tell you that the quality of life improvements alone have made the game worth the wait. Well done there, devs! Sandrock is much heavier on the resource management aspect than Portia was, so it's a nice step up in difficulty. There are also more characters for you to love to hate. Higgins is downright lovable next to Yan and Pen! Grrr!Newbies: If you like games like Stardew Valley and Minecraft, you will love Sandrock. It's very light on combat, so if you're the kind of person who stays away from bigger games because of complicated combat mechanics, you have nothing to worry about here! You have a huge impact on the world: the townspeople rely on you to build the improvements they need to make the town successful. Your builder is no smallfry!In the box: time management, resource management, building, crafting, farming (plants and animals), socializing with characters/ dating and marriage.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: Massive improvement to their previous work, my time at portia. The residents have their own little quirk and personalities where each and every single one of them contributes to the theme and atmosphere of Sandrock. Personally while I like the more social side of the game the actual gameplay loop is fun and rewarding. No need to remember what item is for which person as item requirements for all types of missions are global and as long as they're stored in a chest back at base or on your person you're good to go. I would like to think I've been playing pretty optimally as in finishing most quests, main and side, on the same day but it feels I'm only halfway through the game as of now. So lots of casual content to keep you busy! Definitely worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a positive rating but I don't like this game. I rate it as positive because for the right demographic this game has enough going for it.Be careful what you start, especially if you feel compelled to complete something, as this game has so many time gates that it will drag on and on. I wouldn't liken this to a grind, but more a marathon that is on an unpleasant incline without shade. I was exhausted with what this game had to offer at around the 70 hour mark, but it took me over 190 hours to get to the end. You may get a bit more value out of this game if you play as a female character, and can enjoy the journey, without striving for the end credits.I'm going to look around the game a bit more, but I'm very glad that it's over with. I don't feel that this game respected the time I invested.The problems for me were:Finite StaminaFinite Character Storage exacerbated by clunky external storage (TIP: put the cursor on the external storage and hold down right thumb stick to auto-fill from your inventory, but you have to do it on every external container you have)Events that required specific datesEvents that required a certain amount of time to passUnclear direction as to how to progress (TIP: look to the map and head towards the blue circles in town)Despite 200 hours, I'm at level 49 and there are weapons and armour I can't use because they're locked to level 50 or 55.No fast travel back to your base (TIP: don't bother going home to bed, just pass out. It's not worth the effort.)

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played and liked My Time at Portia (MTaP) then you'll probably enjoy this game too. More questing, unlocking new areas, ruin diving, relationship developing etc.However, I don't recommend this game because it's buggy. It's still fun for sure, but the number of quests that glitch, the number of times I've had to reload the day to reset the game, the number of times I've had to skip a particular action or cut-scene to prevent a game-breaking bug is simply too many for a $40 game. It's unfinished - much like MTaP was for months and months. There are numerous characters with missing voice lines. There are vast empty spaces in the world with literally nothing in them. There are main-story quests that bug out and make you reload to progress (looking at you Showdown at High Noon) and there are bugs that mean you have to reload because you chose to speak to a character when the game wanted you to do something else.It's frustrating and it spoils my enjoyment of the series. Now, (again) we have DLC content for an incomplete game. Releasing DLC before addressing bugs in the main quest-line for me is unforgivable. I'm disappointed in Pathea and disappointed in myself.Them for milking the cash cow and myself for allowing to be milked.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game and it's a bit sad that I can't find something similar.  NOTHING CAN COMPARE!! My search history is now full of "games like my time at Sandrock/Portia" but other games just can't seem to hit the same spots. EDIT: The children concept still bother me and the lack of interactions with them especially with adopted children like Andy and Alo. I hate that they don't treat you like a parent. They don't even call you mom/dad even when there's an option to do so (Andy, don't know about Alo). Also when you go on a date with your spouse, you take your child with you (if they're past the crawling stage and if you have one) and they're just there. They just follow you around and not join in.  Let's not forget the running back and forth whenever your baby needs something or else they'll get bored/sick. The family thing is still majorly lacking (like portia with the doll babies) All in all, it's still great. The My Time series is truly one of a kind (believe me I've looked). _childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

_childDocuments_.review: About 71 hours in and i am completely hooked.I'm nowhere near close to finishing the story, but what i love so far is that everyday there is PLENTY to do.The main gimmick is building and crafting items, which i adore in every game. This is all weaved into a pretty massive story, and comes naturally as you play.There are clear goals to work towards, raking in the gols with commissions so you can upgrade your workshop is fun. Combat is pretty basic, but it stays fun because there are different fightingstyles to choose from and again, not the main focus of the game.There is also (sand)fishing, gathering items, farming and ofcourse all the lifesim stuff.All characters feel very well written and the main story itself is also just really good!Even all sidequests are fun because i feel like i learn something new about the world and characters.Another thing that i really appreciate is that the more you progress the story, the more you see the town blossom.  In the start there is just you and the NPC's that live there, but eventually you will see tourists coming in, the town getting prettier, etc etc. It feels very rewarding.All in all, this is for me a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: *Early Access Review*If you enjoyed my time at Portia definitely worth giving this one a chance. Its allot of fun I'm a big fan of this style of sequel, interacting in the same world but from a different perspective(In this case an entirely different town).The adventuring, crafting, mining and fighting is allot of fun. But I don't find myself enjoying the farming/animal raising... Its a little tedious for me. But you get a good amount from each of the crops so its not something you have to do all the time thankfully. As for the animals it seams like so far I can get anything they would give me from fighting animals so I haven't had an issue with just getting rid of them and playing the parts of the game I enjoy.Obviously the game is incomplete so I'm going to hold off judgement on some of my technical issues. Just know that it is a little glitch  at times not so much as to completely break your game, but you're likely to run into one or two odd graphics glitches, and possibly get soft locked if you walk into the wrong corners. So if that kind of thing frustrates you I would suggest waiting till it is out of early access to get into the game.Personally I don't mind, and it's nice to get a look into what the story and game play will be, and for me that is allot of fun. I've played a little over 70h and I still enjoy playing even with the limited story that's out.

The combat is a real treat, especially when you get more combos. The time limits being removed for story missions is such a massive improvement over Portia. Anything else I could complain about are known bugs being worked on.I really see myself playing this even more than Portia, and I think I sunk like 300 hours into that game lol. Just a great time, highly recommend.
