_childDocuments_.review:
My Time at Sandrock-Just like My Time at Portia, takes place in a wholesome post-apocalyptic world around 300 years after the Day of Calamity.

You'll take a job offer in the city-state of Sandrock, assume the role of a fledgling Builder being sent to a wild and rugged townscape. It's up to you and your trusty toolset to gather resources, build machines, and fix up your workshop into a well-oiled production machine, and save the town from the jaws of economic ruin, as well as a few other unexpected complications.

Key Features:

CUSTOMIZE AND BUILD YOUR WORKSHOP: You'll have an intricate set of machines that all work together to produce parts of huge structures for the town that you assemble piece by piece, or head to your worktable to craft hundreds of unique items that can help out individual townspeople or be placed throughout your own homestead.

EXPLORE THE OPEN WORLD: You'll explore the vast deserts surrounding Sandrock, diving into ruins to find ancient relics from the Old World, facing the dangers of dungeons and their denizens, then return to your homestead with encumbering bags of treasure in tow. 

MORE ELABORATE STORY AND DEEPER CHARACTERS: a vastly enriched storyline, hundreds of side-quests boasting over 30 completely new characters, each getting more attention than before with their own story to discover, as well as the return of a few familiar faces for fans of the series. 

NEW COMBAT: a revamped combat system that allows the player to quickly shift between melee combat and 3rd person shooting mechanics.

SKILL UP: Level up your character with a variety of skills to aid you in your adventures. Decide on whether to boost your crafting, combat or social skills depending on your play style.

AND THERE'S MORE: You'll take your profits and convert the empty prairie lands around you into farmable land for a more leisurely lifestyle, then sell your crops, or transform them into delicious dishes. There is an original soundtrack with dynamic in-game music that reflects where the player is and what they're doing. 

You will find everything you enjoyed about My Time at Portia and more, and you will feel right at home in the delightful life-sim RPG that is My Time at Sandrock.
_childDocuments_.name: My Time at Sandrock

name: Chicken Police - Paint it RED!
detailed_description: Buzz About the Game Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is a narrative-driven noir adventure with a complex interrogation system and mystery-solving detective gameplay. KEY FEATURES: A thrilling, rich storyline with a classic film-noir twist Professional voiceover with more than 8 hours of spoken dialogue! A carefully crafted, unique and 'colorful' world A complex interrogation system 30 fully voiced characters A cinematic film-noir experience with more than 20 cutscenes! Lots of clues, information, and collectibles to find And a beautiful original soundtrack A mysterious Dame... A strange case... and the wildest cops of the Wilderness! MEET THE CHICKEN POLICE Sonny Featherland and Marty MacChicken were once a legendary detective-duo, the Chicken Police. But that was almost a decade ago, and time had passed them by... Now, Sonny is just a semi-alcoholic wreck of a bird on his paid leave, while Marty still hides behind the facade of a star-detective. During their last case, they nearly killed each other, and they haven't spoken ever since... Now Sonny and Marty are forced to work together on a case that's weirder and wilder than anything they've ever encountered before! NARRATIVE-DRIVEN, DETECTIVE GAMEPLAY Chicken Police is a story-rich, dialogue-heavy adventure, combining elements of the visual novels and classic adventure games. The game has more than 30 characters to talk to, with some having to be seriously interrogated. Collect tons of clues, evidence, and highly sensitive personal information from the shady characters of Clawville to use ruthlessly against them! EXPLORE THE CITY OF CLAWVILLE (again, and again...) There are more than 30 places to visit and some of them will change several times during the story. You can return to previous locations on several occasions to find hidden secrets, meet new characters, or gather information about the world and its inhabitants. But the dream remained just a dream while Clawville slowly became the darkest corner of all the Wilderness. short_description: A wild tale of love, death, chickens, and redemption! Chicken Police is a buddy-cop noir adventure with a carefully crafted world, a gritty story, and absurd humor. The game mixes classic adventure games with visual novel-style storytelling, presented in a beak-droppingly unique art style.

_childDocuments_.review: Chicken Police proved to be an outstanding, witty noir detective game and is much more meritorious than its title may suggest.  Featuring exemplary voice acting, a prominent and purposefully cliche story, an original soundtrack and bountiful animal puns, its masterful cinematic experience is a true stand out in 2020 and deserves a place in your Steam library.+ Professional, captivating voice acting amongst the entire cast.+ Witty and wacky humour, teeming with animal puns throughout.+ Astonishing photo-realistic art.+ Strong narrative with classic noir tropes.+ Mixes visual novel elements with classic adventure games and minigames.+ Original & elegant soundtrack that perfectly fits the setting.+ Interesting interrogation scenes.+ Ample dialogue with over 8hrs of voiceovers.+ A multitude of references to classic noir films, detectives and more.+ Credit message bringing awareness to the alarming rate of animal extinction.+ Collectables.- Cannot replay interrogations to achieve a better score.Chicken Police is truly, a wild adventure. Playing as Sonny Featherland, a seasoned detective and chicken who stumbles across an intriguing case. Despite being only a few months from retirement, Sonny takes it up and is forced to reunite the 'Chicken Police', rekindling with his old partner and fellow fowl, Marty MacChicken. The two have extremely cliche, opposing personalities but it works well and if you're into this type of humour, it will definitely cause a few chuckles along the way.  Players explore Clawville, the civilised town, home to many different species of animals. It is split into tiers, much like our own society. The townsfolk still fall victim to their old ways and prejudice regarding 'interspecies' relationships (predatory and prey species), of course imitating that of interracial relationships. Insects are also at the bottom of the food chain and are commonly disregarded and discriminated against. The foundation and lore behind each character is rather fascinating and expertly crafted, with many diary entries for each individual, allowing players to become truly immersed in the fable.The story focuses on one case, involving threats to the well sought-after dame, Natasha Catzenko (yes, it's a cat). As it always is, the case is much more complex than our protagonist first imagines, taking a sinister turn, bringing many of the characters true personalities to light. The famous chicken duo must question and investigate everyone if they are to unveil the truth behind Clawville and the source of the threats.Whilst it is a point and click title, Chicken Police does make a conscious effort to branch out and include other gameplay elements, including some minigames of shooting practice and even car chases. The map is used to easily navigate between each area, clearly marked with pivotal story locations and some extras places to explore. Each location has an abundance of objects to interact with, that will instigate fully voiced narration. Even clicking the same object 2-3 times would commonly cause new dialogue, it was never the same bland description. This was extremely effective in quickly establishing the personalities of the main characters, Sonny and Marty and removed any insipidity that frequently plagues the genre. With each character, there are 4 options, look, speak, ask and sometimes, interrogate. I never felt any sense of repetitively through my 7.5hr playthrough, despite constant conversations and dialogue, the game flows terrifically well and kept me enthralled from beginning to end. Interrogations are also done well, whilst it is not anything ground-breaking, it is still complex and engaging and players must tailor their line of questioning to the personality of the character they're speaking with. A handful of options are presented to us and we must choose which to say, some will sway from the topic at hand and cause a reduction in 'points' and some may just simply not match the character, angering them. Upon the conclusion of each interrogation scene, a ranking out of 5 stars will be displayed, demonstrating how effective the line of questioning was. However, it was slightly disappointing that these specific scenes could not be replayed to achieve a better score.It is clear after playing and important to state that Chicken Police is much more like a visual novel than a typical adventure game. The focus is evidently on the exceptional quality of the dialogue and whilst the investigative elements are present, majority of the game is divided into searching areas and speaking with others. This is by no means a critique and I wouldn't wish it to change, however for potential buyers who do not enjoy reading/VN's, I recommend watching some gameplay before proceeding with the purchase.I definitely agree with the store page description, the best way to describe this visual style is 'weirdly-stunning'. Utilising real photos and photo-realistic 3D backgrounds, involving research into animals at zoos and days spent photographing the many creatures to create an incredibly realistic cast is astonishing. Combining this with the noir aesthetic, it ultimately crafts a striking, theatrical authenticity that I have not seen replicated before and left me taking screenshots of every scene. Inspired by  and classic film-noir movies, Chicken Police expertly manages to make a name for itself and standout above other, more well-known anthropomorphic titles such as Although the style is definitely eccentric and unconventional, it is undeniably clear that the graphics and art included in this title is one of a kind. This expert craftmanship also oozes into the audio and the noir aura is further complimented through the voice acting and original soundtrack. Instantly, it is evident that the voice actors are professionals, and each character is a joy to listen to, with very defined personalities. This comes as no surprise, given that the actors are from the same studio involved in I experienced no issues, and it ran smoothly.Simply stated, I cannot really fault this game. I am a lover of Indie titles and Chicken Police did not come across as amateur in any way, shape or form and I am almost in disbelief of its Indie tag. Everything from the cinematics to dialogue to the audio was masterfully designed and implemented from start to finish. I highly recommend this to everyone, especially those who enjoy noir aesthetic and witty dialogue. It is a standout title of the genre and undoubtedly deserves many more accolades than it has currently received. I eagerly await further releases from the developers and wish all the success on their future endeavours.This review copy was provided to the Devils in the Detail curator.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of visual novels and have a soft spot for aging detectives, then I would definitely recommend the Chicken Police. It is well written with black/white visuals and a sound track that are true to the film noir style. The story is engaging and plays out in great detail with a wide variety of animal characters in classic roles (the sidekick, the sexy damsel in distress, the mob boss, the madam, the police chief, etc.). I classify it as a 'visual novel' because 95% of your time will be spent clicking through dialog and clicking on hot spots to find out more about them.  You point and click on a map to travel between locations and you continue clicking and listening for almost all of the 8+ hours it may take you to get through this title.I love detective games and favor a balance between participation and observation (for example - the Darkside Detective, The Silk Rose Murders, the Tex Murphy games).  For me, the sheer volume of dialog in the Chicken Police grew tiresome and I found myself speed reading and clicking rather than listening. There are about a half dozen 'active' moments and some cut scenes to watch. But, overall, it is a very passive game. As an achievement junkie, I clicked everything multiple times, spoke to every character again and again, and visited every location multiple times but still missed items. Since there is no 'chapter' revisit, the only way to collect the missing achievements is to repeat the whole game and hope for the best.  This is not something that I am inclined to do.The game autosaves so there is no chance to backtrack to a prior scene and some locations disappear once the story moves forward.  I realize that this is the approach in many current games but I still don't like it. I became a bit frustrated with the lack of control instructions on the investigation and activity screens. When presented with these, you have to figure out what is required. I wasn't looking for solutions... just instructions on how to fire/reload a gun or what you were supposed to do on the investigation summaries. There is a 'hint' on these screens which gives a clever comment but no true assistance.For the most part, the story moves at it's own pace and locations become available as the plot progresses. However, on multiple occasions, I found myself stuck because I had not clicked items in a particular sequence or initiated an additional conversation required to activate the map. This resulted in time spent clicking and clicking, trying to figure out what was expected (after I thought I had exhausted all options). At such moments, the Steam discussion forum was most helpful as other players had found the same sticking points.To summarize, I'm glad I played and I enjoyed the story.  Kudos to the development team for a job well done and making this title work with chickens, dogs, rats, cats, etc.  If you are a gamer like me who prefers to keep moving during an adventure (rather than sitting still), you may want to consider your own tolerance for visual novels prior to investing in this title.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected nothing more than a funny satire and couldn't have been more wrong. The game is a full-fledged detective noir game, with really cool and charismatic characters, stunning black-and-white environments, with rare bits of color that pop up very nicely, reminiscing of Sin City. Great fully-voiced dialogues, superb soundtrack, and a detailed, around 8-10 hours long, very immersive story. Achievement completion is a little tedious but nothing too bad if you're willing to do it. All in all, this was a cluckin' awesome detective-noir game well above my expectations and I'd recommend it to any fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: 10.2h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (22 achievements, all are missables). No. is a visual novel disguised as an adventure game about... chicken police. It sets in a world where animals with human bodies rule the world. You will investigate a case, interrogate people, and perform deductions. Before you ask, no, it's not a murder mystery game.- Smooth animation and beautiful-looking visuals- Lively dialogues - No manual save and no saving indication in autosaves- Unable to scroll lengthy dialogues Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650To be honest, I couldn't tell whether the characters use real-life models or not. Characters look so similar to how it looks in real life, whether it is the animal or human part. If you don't notice already, all animals in  has an animal head and human body, and the neck merges seamlessly. I also like the little details like the animal skins or furs that reach their arms sometimes. Moreover, the animation when they are talking is also done flawlessly. You will see their mouth stopping after each sentence, their eyes blinking, and minimal movements as they talk - they all felt real.Dialogues are golden. Characters talk like people do in real life, fooling around with their sarcasm and jokes. They never seem to run out of jokes either - Marty, one of the main characters, seems to have a talent to lighten the situations, even when he is almost dead. There is never a moment when the game feels dull with these two going around and doing their remarks.The cinematics in the cutscenes is also brilliant though. Although characters hardly move, the camera and effects help to make them look cooler. Sadly, dialogues can be hard to read. Some dialogues will be longer than the dialogue box's size, and instead of moving the rest of the dialogue in the new dialogue box, the text will be appended to the existing one, removing the text above you. However, the game won't allow you to scroll through the dialogue box to read the whole text. As someone who rather read all texts once they show up, I had a hard time catching up on what people said whenever the dialogues are presented in this manner.Although I mentioned the game as a visual novel, you won't be sitting around reading dialogues all the time. The game also borrows some mechanics in point and click game, allowing you to interact with some objects and talk with people. Some objects will also be available to pick up, adding more conversation topics for some people. You don't have to worry about missing some objects though - the game always states whenever you have to get an item. The only thing that you will miss is the collectibles, which are not needed to finish the game.Talking to everyone is not necessary to finish the game, but is needed for collectibles and trivia. The more that you talk and interact with objects, the more that you will know about them. However, some collectibles can be hard to find since they will not show up if you use the eye button, which is used to show all objects that you can interact with within the area. As police officers, you will be able to conduct some interrogations. You will know more about the person that you interrogate this way, allowing you to change your approach in your questioning. Some questions will give you negative points, some will give you positives. It's not hard to get enough points to complete the interrogations, although you might need to retry it several times to get the perfect score.Although you will be conducting interrogations, don't expect the game to be a murder mystery. The best that you will get is doing a deduction through a minigame, which will help to let you know what happens to the story. However, it can be hard to understand what the game wants sometimes, although luckily, they can be brute-forced. The case will be solved on its own - you don't have to guess which one is the culprit. Moreover, it wasn't hard to guess the culprit, especially since all clues will point to one solution. Some puzzles are available in the game, but hints can be cryptic. I was lucky enough to clear them, although it took me a hard time to clear the first one. The thing is, I know the solution, but I needed an in-game reference which wasn't available in the area. Since you can get locked out from existing areas if you progress the game, I was afraid to move to the area that has this reference - I thought that I won't be able to return to the area to solve the puzzle if I did that.I finished the game in 9.8h. The rest of my playtime was spent obtaining the rest of the achievements. You won't be able to return to some areas once you progress the game, and there are a lot of collectibles that can be missed as a result. As for the difficulty, you won't have any difficulties in finishing this game.The game has no manual save. It will save as you progress the game, but there is no saving indicator at all.Honestly, I didn't expect  to be this good. The dialogues are one of the better ones that you can get from these kinds of games. The main characters are not the ones that you usually see either. You won't be seeing an overly serious main character that is solving cases brilliantly - you'll see an old man complaining about being old and a gun maniac that names all of his guns. I always enjoyed reading what the main characters are talking about.The visuals help to set up the atmosphere. Characters look gorgeous with their realistic look, and even though you will be looking at animals, you still can see how beautiful the women are. Don't let your children play it though. Some pictures might not be... appropriate. If you enjoy playing games with lively dialogues, especially with 2 chickens joking around, I would recommend playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔹After getting sucked into visual novels a few weeks ago by  which you can find my review of it , I was thoroughly impressed and hungry for more, when I stumbled upon this game.  is an alluringly mad love song to film noir. It strikes into the mind that in the enormous cloud of unpolished AAAs, there are indies that stand out superbly.🔹Sonny Featherland is a weary detective counting days until his retirement and also the first half of the legendary chicken police duo. He is dragged into one last case that only leads to a bitter truth. He and his partner, Marty McChicken, follow clues through the city of Clawville to unravel a mysterious case of blackmail and murder that goes all the way up to the big-shots of the city. is more of a visual novel than a detective game and it will appeal to the fans of the former much more. Nonetheless, its take on point-and-click elements as well as puzzles and mini-games is discernibly evident. It is set in a world of anthropomorphic animals that mirrors the 30s-40s America and its penchant for organized crime. Clawville is depicted in a thorough manner, that its origins and rich history lie in a country that has had economic downturns, war, and interracial tensions.You don't usually get a chance to see Roosters conducting investigations, Kittens singing, Raccoons with tattoos talking in an American-Italian accent, and many more archetypes straight out of a noir movie merged into a fabled and plausible world of a video game. These certain archetypes are based on the characters' animalistic traits that perfectly match their appearances and occupations in . They have compelling and heavy backstories but they aren't shoved into your mouth. The plot doesn't focus on those things since their interactions play out in such a natural way through optional dialogues and entries written down in Sonny's journal.The gameplay mostly relies on talking to characters and questioning them in a multiple-choice format. Sonny will chronicle significant and insignificant details as he comes across Clawville and its townsfolk which can be accessed at any time. Interrogations, however, play a bigger role in the story's progression. He makes notes of his impressions of the characters during interrogations, to further aid the player in getting the right answers out of them. Sadly, whether it's a relevant answer or not, they have no impact on the narrative as it carries on to one conclusion.Each location has plenty of investigative elements. This consists of searching for clues to be stored in your inventory which can be used in conversation as a new line of inquiry and possibly even reveal new locations. Between these moments, you find yourself solving simple yet effective puzzles while minigames such as a shooting gallery or a car chase break up the norm. At the end of every chapter, another type of minigame kicks in. Sonny can piece together the clues to draw conclusions on what to do next. It's a nice visual representation of detective work, but due to the linear narrative, you can't progress without plugging in the proper pieces.The look of  is quite astonishing with an unmatched cinematic presentation. Each location and character is sumptuously brought to life in a striking black-and-white style. Although almost static, the rain-swept Clawville is pictured with stunning effects and realistic backgrounds that make you feel you've instantly been dropped into a classic like . The use of animal heads on human bodies is enchanting and bizarre at times, but the fusion is weirdly seamless that you get used to it.The eccentric collection of characters wouldn't be as vivid if it weren't for the prominent voice actors. Fully voiced characters by professionals like Kerry Shale, Jules de Jongh, Shai Matheson, and others from big titles like The Witcher, Mass Effect, Mirror’s Edge and etc. Another aspect of  that is carried out precisely is its original soundtrack. A jazz-tinged score that is full of wailing trumpets and grand pianos that you would expect from a game inspired by noir movies.🔹🔹The game runs with all settings maxed out, using about 60% of VRAM at 1680x1050 60 FPS.🔹🔹🔹 is a one-of-a-kind experience that manages to carve a deep world with its remarkable characters and voice-acting, through an unconventional yet striking presentation. It's a unique take on detective works that stands out among other titles like  or .🔹I can say the story is rather short if you only aim to close the murder case asap, but Clawville is enriched with details and characters you could interact with for hours. Needless to say, a secret ending and many achievements are missable if you're not looking around carefully which adds to the replayability. The price tag is justified for the effort that's been put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best games i played this year so far, and even though i was already hooked just from store page alone, the game still managed to surpass my relatively high expectations for it!The story was pretty good for the most part, nothing too groundbreaking but still entertaining enough to keep me hooked all the way to the end, what can i say? i really can't say no to a good buddy-cop noir adventure! :PAs for the characters, they're some of my favorite in recent memory, i simply love the premise of this game and the human-animal hybrid designs, not only did they manage to make me memorize every single one of them but they also made them all actually interesting!Each character looks pretty distinct not only in their appearance but also in their accents & personalities, this was a breath of fresh air compared to other games where all the generic side characters start to blend into each other after a while.The voice acting was pretty good as well, especially for the 2 main characters, i really enjoyed the constant banter between them, but i also have to admit that i was hesitant at first after hearing Sonny Featherland's first monologue (the way he breaths after each sentence), but he either stopped doing that later on or i simply got used to it that i completely forgot about it lolCouple that with some great dialogue and you're in for a treat! the only other game that was able to make me chuckle this much (probably more but still :P) is Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, which is some real high praise for this one.Hmm, what else? i also simply adore the black & white aesthetic the game has, and i found the world to be interesting enough & worth exploring (multiple times), i also wish there were more cutscenes but the ones already there are still well made. (i also love the little easter eggs sprinkled through out the game, the blind lawyer bat Murdock and his partner anyone? *wink wink*)All in all, this was a very good point & click noire detective game, definitely something unique, at least characters-wise, definitely worth a try if you're into this kind of games. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. It plays out its absurdist premise with resolute straight-faced humor, every single character is a joy to speak with, and the choice of animals to convey personality quirks and character tropes puts Bojack Horseman to shame.This game completely nails the black-and-white aesthetic, the classical whiskey-drenched, hard-boiled narrative, and a cast that is at once familiar and memorable. Chicken Police also enjoys the tremendous benefits of absolute top-tier voice acting (especially from the two leads), and a really masterfully crafted mystery that gradually unfurls into an immensely satisfying final act. I played through this with a friend, enjoyed every minute of it, and laughed until I wheezed. A great experience and an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Chicken Police is one of my favorite games, and the fact that I willingly typed those words in that order is both amusing to me and a testament to how good I think it is.Many of the game's characters have unique personalities and outlooks, well developed personal histories, and many of them seem to have had some form of lengthy relationships with each other prior to the start of the story. This gives each of them, and therefore the world overall, some nice depth. The history, culture, and politics of the world are also intriguing and make the world feel more lived in.The writing seamlessly weaves humor and dark themes throughout. Sometimes I'd be cackling at some banter between characters, other times I'd be floored by the seriousness of a topic being discussed. Often, I'd find myself laughing at the way drama itself is used a comedic tool, Sonny delivering a line that, while perhaps a serious thought on his part, is phrased in a way that is so poetic and overly dramatic that becomes absurd and funny again. Put another way, the game finds a way to really embrace the noir genre and have fun with it.And all of this wonderful writing is of course delivered by stellar voice acting, which I think is likely the game's strongest aspect.The soundtrack is incredible and really sets the vibe in every scene.The art style is unique, this odd mixture of hyper realistic animal heads on human bodies... in 2D... in black and white (with the occasional pops of color). Off the top of my head I can't really think of anything else I've seen that looked quite like it and I think it deserves points just for that haha.There are a couple of features I really appreciate. Being able to toggle auto-play on the dialogue is great and being able to back up a bit in the dialogue is wonderful for those of us who sometimes get distracted haha. I also appreciate that if one somehow messes up an interrogation (or just wishes to do it better) they are given the option to restart it at the end of each one.In terms of gameplay, the few puzzles there are aren't particularly difficult, nor are the other couple mechanics you see along the way. You aren't even given much room to flex your own Sherlock muscles and show off for Watson, as Sonny, as part of his inner monologue, tends to guide you on how best to direct your questions during interrogations. Challenge does not seem to have been a goal in the design of this game. That's not really an insult or criticism, as I don't think the game is suffering from the lack of challenge. I just think it's useful to note what the game is trying to accomplish and what it isn't.Overall, I think the game nails everything it was trying to do and if you don't give it a shot at some point, I think you're really clucking yourself over ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don’t play visual novels, but Chicken Police made me interested and curious immediately when I saw it on Steam for the first time. I decided to buy it because of its distinctive art style and the fact that I love crime/detective games like L.A. Noire, The Wolf Among Us, Sherlock Holmes: Crimes and Punishments, Grim Fandango and many others.Chicken Police has a very special noir look combined with very sharp colors when the game wants you to really NOTICE something, for example a text painted RED or stunning GREEN eyes on one of the characters. I absolutely love the contrast. The idea of having human bodies and animal heads is amazing! Also it gave the game a great opportunity to make good animal related jokes.The play with words in Chicken Police and its humor (even the dark one) make you want to click around on everything you can and even more than once! I kept returning to some optional locations after every main story progress just to get them talking/commenting on things more! I didn’t want to miss any cheeky lines or funny jokes. It’s extraordinary that this game can make clicking around on objects, which is normally a bit boring in most games, quite interesting. We should prize the wonderful voice acting for it. That makes me think back to the first visual novel I played - Doki Doki Literature Club with no voice acting and how I expected the same from Chicken Police. What I got was much better. Let’s say that my own voice acting would be a bit limited and much less professional. ;)Chicken Police is a point and click game with hidden objects. Clicking on an object will make your character comment on it or discuss it with your partner. Most of the time two clicks are enough to get all the unique reactions. You can find the clickable objects yourself or you can let the game show them to you. Very useful option which enabled double checking when I was done with it myself and just wanted to make sure that I didn’t miss anything. Clicking on other characters gives you more options if they are part of the story. You can look at them, talk to them, sometimes ask questions and on special occasions interrogate them. As mentioned before it is a visual novel so most of the time you sit back, relax and enjoy the game’s story. Then once in a while you get to interrogate someone which makes you think about choosing the right questions at the right time to get witnesses/suspects talking and revealing important clues. It is not very hard to score an average interrogation rank 3-4*. 5* can be quite challenging the first time around. If you don’t like the result or fail it completely you can redo it right after. Another part of the gameplay involves connecting people, clues and items on the board which helps you work towards solving the case. There are few pressing challenges with timers in the game. I found them fun. At least there was a bit of the thrill once in a while!The story of the game is very interesting. It starts very strong. Big mystery, a lot of interesting clues and characters and it’s almost impossible to make any guesses what’s behind it all. But that breaks towards the ending. The game has 4 chapters and what I learned in chapter 3 gave away the whole mystery too early because the plot became too predictable. Don’t get me wrong. It is still really fun to play the last chapter. But the mystery had been blown up too soon in my opinion. Part of me was hoping that I was wrong and misled and something shocking would still happen, but it didn’t. That’s the only downside for me. That little bit is missing for the game being a true masterpiece. I definitely recommend Chicken Police to everyone who likes atmospheric indie games with good humor, who wants to chill with a cinematic game with not too much gameplay and who wants to experience something very different and unique. I can only hope now that The Wild Gentlemen will decide to make more special games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: "It was New Year's Eve, and I was driving, half-drunk, risking my whole life's work, but still...it didn't feel any different. Every day was the same. And the hundred and twenty-one days I had left till my retirement seemed like an eternity." is a point-and-click adventure game developed by The Wild Gentlemen and published by HandyGames.Game takes place in Clawville, a city populated by anthropomorphic animals.You play as Santino "Sonny" Featherland, a burnt-out cop who used to be a part of legendary Chicken Police, together with his partner Marty MacChicken. Nowadays Sonny prefers to drink and count days until his official retirement, but a case that quickly turns into a personal one will force him to teamup with his old partner once again.Chicken Police combines point and click gameplay with detective elements and few minigames. Main goal is to investigate locations and scenes in order to push the story further and unlock next area.Point and click points out you can play this game with only your mouse, as for the most part you will drag your cursor across specific elements and click to investigate them, collect, or to hear a comment. Game has an option to highlight all items you can interract with (besides collectibles) if you feel lazy.Sonny can also chat, ask or even start an interrogation with characters encountered throughout Clawville.Additionally game features few minigames you encounter on your journey to break the constant dialogue wall you get thrown into, and puzzles!In his trusty journal, Sonny writes all the clues, information about people, places and contains a codex filled with data about Chicken Police world. It also has a page featuring statistics, for interested.You also have an option to check your inventory, and a map that lets you travel between locations, those are seperated onto major ones that push story further, and time limited secondary locations.It took me 8 hours to complete a case, however I did visit all areas and interacted with pretty much everything, didn't skip any dialogue, so your playtime can be way, way shorter depending on your approach. Game can be beat in less than 4 hours if you will focus on main part of it only.Collecting specific items will unlock a secret ending, and if you rushed your first playthrough, you have another reason to give it a go too!Chicken Police does a great job at being a buddy cop noir game, as game is styled after classic noir films from 1940's, filled with jazz soundtrack, stylistic monochrome and enviroment reasembling said time period.Synergy between two main characters is fantastic, and hearing all snarky comments they give each other across the game made interracting with everything around me worth it even more.  While "old burnt out cop and young cocky gun" is not the most original duo, it works really well in the game! As a cherry on top voice actors do a great work to narrate the journey, with Kerry Shale being a bright star, doing a wonderful work in voicing Sonny.Unfortunately game lacks a bit of interraction between Sonny and Marty in main bits of the game, as most of the talk to NPC's and entire interrogations are done by Sonny only, leaving a feeling that Marty's presence is not always needed. Strong secondary characters you encounter make revisiting locations as enganging as when you visited them for the first time.Gameplay plays second fiddles here but occasional minigames and puzzles make up for a decent break away from chatting.The element I found simply odd was character design. Majority of characters is depicted as humans with animal heads, with occasional additions of tails or scutes. While some characters look decent, quite often game leaves an impression characters you talk to are humans simply wearing a piece of some Halloween costume on a head. It just looks silly and takes a moment to get used to.Game could use a bigger amount of locations considering Clawville is not a little village and revisiting same area for fourth or fifth time does get boring sooner or later. As I was approaching the end of the game I did get a little burned out on it due to constant revisits of same areas and talking to same NPC's for gods which time, but as I stated before I did go for a completionist run so I might have done more dialogue than usual player on his first playthrough would.Game features a demo available on the store page if you want to try out the game before buying it!Chicken Police is a buddy cop title that combines great noir setting, solid writing and good cast of main and side characters into one fantastic detective adventure. Check out  for more reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I expected a lot from the noir game "Chicken Police", the promotional materials were too attractive, but it did not live up to my expectations. She simply smashed them into dust, lifting my emotions to some unprecedented height, because it turned out to be a real shining pearl, of which there are few. Stunningly stylish, dynamic, never losing its charm, the game takes all the good that the genre of noir has to offer and creates an incredible story out of it. And there is everything that your heart desires - a sullen old cop and his impudent partner, femme fatale, pursuits, salvation from death, the dirty underside of the city, the acrid cigarette smoke that is breathed in this city instead of air. And all this with anthropomorphic animals as all the characters, which made it possible to expand the range of used humor in general to incredible proportions. The writers skillfully keep the red thread of the narrative taut, making you constantly feel yourself in the Hitchcock maelstrom of passions.Considering that, for the most part, the game is dialogues, interrogations and logical conclusions (puzzles and mini-games are here, but there are not so many of them to make it a classic adventure), then the elaboration of the characters, their storylines, becomes the cornerstone for success. And the creators handled it brilliantly. Not a single passing character, everyone has a story, everyone is connected to this dirty city with their own ties, everyone brings their colors to the palette of this black and white world. And this voice acting of the characters, my God, it is phenomenal ... I enjoyed every second of the dialogues, so the actors get used not even just into the role, but into the character of the animal they play. Bizarre absurd animations fit this crazy world like a glove, more than once caught myself thinking that this game could easily turn into a full-length animated film, changing almost nothing.This game can be praised for everything without ceasing, it now definitely occupies an important place in my heart. And if you are even a bit fond of noir in games and movies, be sure to give it a try, this fantastic work is simply worth seeing. And a sequel. And she and we deserve a sequel, or Bloody New Year's Eve prequel to start with.

_childDocuments_.review: Ha. What a game. . At home they must sure love me quoting this game constantly. . :')You play as Sonny, an alcoholic cop with a gunshot hole in his comb. He was planning to just drink until retirement, which is only a few months from now. Of course some dame comes in with a mysterious case that you cannot possibly turn down, as it becomes rather . Oh yea, and you're a ©ock.This game has amazing voice-acting (for every single line!), I really enjoy and appreciate the voice-acting, its exactly how I would imagine the characters to sound. Top notch! The game has clever dialogue- its funny and, as you'd expect, full of animal jokes. The dialogue shines with the two main characters. I thought they were a hilarious duo. Holy chicken Jesus, these two can't stop teasing each other. So much chicken banter.It think its fair to mention the game tries to sell itself as a new genre which seems a bit far fetched to me. While it is definitely unique and funny, it is a visual novel, not a detective game, not an adventure game. The 'complex interrogation system' can be explained as a scoring system; pick the best answer out of 1 to 3 questions. Each answer will give you points. At the end of an interrogation (which usually is 9 questions), you get a score. Don't like the score of your interrogation? Rewind the dialogue, , and try again until you get the score you like. Not so complex, eh? I'm not trying to down-talk the game, but I think it's important to realize this isn't an adventure game or a game with elaborate interrogation mechanics, else it might get disappointing. It's a great detective story that reads itself out loud to you.Finally also worth to mention: A few of the scene transitions felt slightly rushed to me. Leaving me wonder, hey what just happened to those other guys, or how the hell did we go from here to there?! _childDocuments_.review: 1. Fantastic aesthetic that's heavily influenced by classic film noir.2. Beautiful moody music.3. Intriguing murder mystery with a great buildup.4. Wide range of characters to talk to and places to explore.5. A lot of passion from a talented Hungarian team.1. No manual save. It's inexcusable that a VN, in the Year of our Lord 2022, doesn't have this option. When the story ends, the game doesn't even allow you to go back to your last save and just promptly deletes it.2. No dialogue history. No way to re-read dialogue beyond reloading the last checkpoint.3. Hammy writing. A lot of tired clichés in both story and dialogue. A bad guy literally says "We're not so different, you and I" lol. And no, it wasn't an attempt to be ironic, self-aware or humorous.4. Abrupt ending. The game, while having an intriguing start, is very short and ends before it really got going IMO. A lot of the characters and their relationships felt pretty half baked in hindsight.5. I think having animals in the main role is a really interesting artistic choice and I commend the devs for their great love of nature. But the game suffers from what I dub the "Lion King remake effect". Animals are just not very expressive and feel pretty stiff when it comes to their faces and expressions. Also, I think it would have been better if they just played it straight and went with the "yeah they're humans with animal heads, so what?" route rather than trying to enrich the world with lore about why things are the way they are as the lore just doesn't make a lot of sense.I think this is worth playing for VN fans or fans of the film noir aesthetic but it's by no means a masterpiece or a hidden gem. At least not from a story perspective. I'm happy to give Chicken Police a halfhearted thumbs up because I really do believe it's an interesting, beautiful game and I'm sure the devs have what it takes to make a real classic somewhere down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is rather niche, but one that fits the niche well. It randomly popped up on the front page for me, and decided to give it a try. I must say, I deeply enjoyed this lil' game. Much more than I expected.The sad thing is, with this game being a point and click, not many people are going to be willing to give it a shot, and that is a darn shame as everything about this game oozes charm and heart and I want it to do really well, so giving it the praise it deserves as well as encouraging other folks to give it a try after playing it through once myself.Presentation is key for something like this, and it completely blew me away. I hadn't seen any trailers or news on Chicken Police, so I didn't know what I was getting into. That being said, I want to give who ever was behind sound design and voice management a platinum medal or something, because every delivery of the dialog and every note on those jazzy brass instruments went above and beyond for something involving the pulp fiction era. The use of a monochromatic color pallet save for those few important scenes help add to the atmosphere of a pulp noir detective story, and the use of animals for characters helped make for some rather interesting quips from the cast portrayed as well as help the story develop in a rather interesting way. Gameplay itself is simple, your standard point and click affair involving clicking dialog boxes and finding items to progress, with with key elements involving logic and trying to figure out what questions to ask in order to get key information out of characters involved in the plot, and I must say it is kinda nice, and does require a bit of brain power if you want all the details.It's a bit short, but its something that left me hungry for more. I wanna see more of the Chicken Police, and the moment a sequel is announced I'm throwing money at it.Point and click adventures aren't for everyone, mind you. But for anyone who likes them, or the pulp noir of the past, or anyone who wants a nice mystery to wet the whistle, this is a perfect pick up.And here's hoping to another game involving Sonny and Marty, and may they introduce Mr. Sinclair and Bertha the Second to the clucking criminal underbelly of Clawville again in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A noir visual novel set in a crime-ridden city with anthropomorphic animals instead of people. The two main characters that our story follows are Sonny Featherland and Marty MacChicken, also known around the city as Chicken Police. Despite their reputation, their glory days are over and the last time they saw each other ended badly. However, now they need to get back together to solve a new case.While solving the case, we visit various places in the City of Clawville and get to learn a lot about its history and inhabitants. The game does an excellent job at bringing this setting alive and making it seem like a real place. The plot might seem a bit predictable in places, but it also has some nice twists and turns and is generally fun to follow because the characters are all very interesting and well-developed, especially the main duo. Every dialogue and banter between them is just great.The story is pretty linear though and there is no branching narrative. I think having some choices and consequences with multiple outcomes would've made it even better, but not having it is not a big flaw.The game is mainly a visual novel, so most of the gameplay involves talking to NPCs, travelling from one area to another, and interacting with objects in the environments to progress the case. In some instances we need to interrogate the NPCs, and during that we have to choose from different dialogue options in order to build trust with the character and have them reveal information to us. We can make some mistakes. We only fail that interrogation if we do too many mistakes and lose the character's trust entirely. There are some puzzles and mini-games present too, but most of them are pretty easy to solve and fit the casual experience very nicely.The film noir visual style with characters having human bodies and animal heads is pretty great and very unique. I thoroughly enjoyed it. The voice acting for each character is superb and really helps to bring each of them to life. Music is also fitting and some pieces stand out especially.Overall, a good visual novel with casual gameplay elements taking place in a very well-crafted setting and with interesting characters. _childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere on show here is fantastic. A friend saw the demo of this and grabbed it and was streaming it on Discord - we all assumed based on the name and premise it was going to some kind of parody.And, lets be clear, in many ways it is - a pile of cliches the story smashes through from beginning to end. But is is very, very well done and whilst funny it also has some depth to the story and keeps you wanting to find whats next. The various people you talk to all seem to have character and attitude and you can fell that coming through - unlike a lot of indie, and bigger, games i've played the voice acting was superb.One thing to be aware of is this very much in my experience a visual novel rather than a game - I never got close to failing an investigation and other than, very cool and fun it must be said, conversations to flesh the world out there isn't any reason to go anywhere other than where it tells you the plot is.All told though I highly recommend it and really hope this is the first of multiple games they do and set in this world.

_childDocuments_.review: An interactive novel with a unique aesthetic and outstanding voice acting that is let down by its paper thin but still somehow frustrating gameplay mechanics and convoluted writing. The story that is at the centre of the experience simply falls apart from the mid-point once you begin unravelling the mystery. To give you a better idea if this review is relevant for you I am someone who doesn’t often play point and click games but was attracted to the title based on the visual style and the innovative setting. I really want to give this game a positive review because it is clear that a lot of care and toil has been put in by the developers but my experience became increasingly frustrating as the game progressed and left a bad taste in my mouth by the time I reached the credits. As the cliché plot twist involving a (minor spoiler) a twin became clear in the final act I audibly groaned and lost any sort of investment in the story. This is first and foremost an interactive novel with very, very light gameplay elements meaning your enjoyment will be dependent on how much you care about the plot. Sadly that element begins to unravel at the seams as it progresses and the whole thing becomes incredibly contrived. For example in one instance you are knocked out and taken to a different part of the city leaving your car behind. Thankfully the writers managed to solve this headache by including an off mark remark that a character you haven’t met up to that point and who has no reason to be at the establishment where you were captured found your car there, decided that something was afoot, FOUGHT your assailants to take it and delivered it to the place where you just now happen to be after escaping. The main gameplay elements are interrogations where you question various characters by choosing the right dialogue option based on the subject’s traits and the line of questioning the main detective advises you to take. The relationship between these parameters and the options offered to you are at most tangential and often you’ll find yourself feeling like you’re guessing rather than taking a thought out line of questioning. There is no mechanic of collecting and using evidence or including items you have found in this process. If you think you can bring in information you have learned from dialogue previously think again. Naturally you are also often shown only the first line of the dialogue you pick and whether subsequent lines are in the spirit of what you picked feels random. This game is also one of those that are a nightmare for people who are thorough with their playthroughs and talk to everyone but who do not wish to undertake multiple playthroughs to collect all details about the setting. I almost missed out on the end credits because the game has decided that I need to exhaust all dialogue options on the final two screens while hiding one character (who had no reason to be there of course) behind another with no indication. There was also at least two instances where I was forced to leave a room before thoroughly examining it because I examined things in the wrong order. If you decide to purchase and play this make sure you’re not a completionist. The game unexpectedly touches issues of race in what I would argue is a rather clumsy fashion and features sex work in what I felt was a regressive way. I was also disappointed that it falls into the tired old trope of featuring people with mental illness in a role of a violent villain. This final complaint here is what swayed me into giving it a negative review. There is a lot to like here, voice acting in particular being excellent but overall I was left clucked off at the squandered opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Chicken Police - Paint It Red is a brilliant mix of point & click and puzzle solving.- The dialog and characters are well written, the story is intriguing from the start, full of twists & turns, and it kept me hooked until the end.- Investigation sections are decent, with them requiring a bit of brain power to figure out (I only got stuck at a section once, because of my own stupidity).- Finally, the interrogation sections are well made with the dialog choices actually mattering as they can send you down alternative paths in the interrogation and the hints the protagonist gives the player at the start of each of these are helpful, but subtle enough not to feel like hand-holding.Overall, I'd highly recommend the game for people that like their film-noir style plot & setting with well made characters and written dialog that has made me laugh out loud quite a few times.P.s For those concerned, this isn't a furry game, the only animal parts are the heads and the animals chosen are supposed to relate to a character's archetype.

_childDocuments_.review: It is really impressive what you can do with a few talented voice actors, brilliant writing, black and white noir lightning, two chickens, a cat, a rabbit, and a few other animals, and there you have it, the finished product, a treasure: The Chicken Police.From the start, the UI is easy, smooth, and fitting, you know for sure that can enjoy clicking wherever you want to click and then you are greeted with that gritty son-of-a-bird, Sonny, Mr. Featherland, the broken rusty rooster whose days as a prime, world-class detective are long gone, dwelling on his misery, alone, on a new year's eve, in his rather clouded apartment with memories, sorrow, and blood. And before you know it, and before he knows it, everything is about change!The world of Chicken Police is amusing, brutally honest, and realistic, albeit, no humans in it but it depicts us in its new exclusive inhabitants, the animals, in their lives, faces, emotions, pain, jobs, and dreams, the animals who are just like us, there are the wise and kind, the fool and evil, their world has real problems, problems our world has, racism, discrimination, corruption, murder, organized crime, hate... hate and love.Their society is plagued with issues and they are just like us, simple individuals trying to get by, trying to survive. ain't no heroes here, no superanimals, just survivors and white, black and a hundred shade of grey.This aspect of the game, in my opinion, was outstanding but what really stole the spotlight was the clucking magnificent voice acting, I didn't expect such quality from an indie visual novel, and I am very glad that I was wrong about it.The best way to put it probably is a voice that fits the face. You can probably try to guess what kind of character you are talking to without knowing how they look or what they do just through their voice, that was very well done.Combined with a sense of humor that tries to face a thrilling, dark, and rainy night, that is bounded by fate to be painted red, Chicken Police was the best new year's eve I have ever had.recommended

_childDocuments_.review: "Chicken Police" is a good point & clicker with a setting that mixes noir hardboiled detective stories with a world populated by anthropomorphic animals. As you might suspect, it doesn't take itself too seriously - so don't expect Animal Farm-levels of subtext - but it still wants to tell a story of murder and mystery, vice and deceit. And it does a decent job in this regard. However, the plot does have a few logic errors and probably goes on for a bit too long. The game needed a couple more iterations of tightening and eliminating plot holes IMO - then it would have been outstanding.On the plus side: The developers absolutely nailed the atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: I went into  with zero expectations. I had been in a bit of a slump lately where nothing in my Steam library appealed to me much at the moment when the thumbnail for this game caught my eye while browsing Steam's Store page. I watched the trailers, liked what the developers were doing with the art style and overall "feel" of the game and decided to give the available demo a shot (why more games don't offer demos nowadays as in the past, I'll never know). Once I was finished with the demo I knew I needed to see this through to the end. I purchased the game and spent the next week or so going through the story and was wholeheartedly surprised with the quality of the experience.The narrative places you in the shoes (claws...talons?) of Santino "Sonny" Featherland and his partner Martin "Marty" MacChicken: two rooster-headed detectives on a gritty, noir-style adventure that takes you through a rich world full of its own lore, twists, turns, and other great surprises. The gameplay consists of a blend of point-and-click adventure as well as visual novel elements that create an experience that I haven't had the pleasure of enjoying for quite some time. Admittedly I haven't been drawn to games of this nature in the past, but the trailers and premise of a buddy cop story with this premise and art style are major boons that  has going very strongly for it.The entire game is also enriched with very high quality voice acting as well as original music that further sets the right tone throughout your playtime. I would like to give major kudos to the voice actors who clearly put their heart and soul into these characters as you very much connect with their personalities and various hardships as the story progresses. There's a very strong world here, and I was very happy to have gotten to experience it through my playthrough. Honestly, it left me wanting more by the end. I think that's a sign of good storytelling, all things considered.If you are looking for a tale that will draw you in with its characters, setting, and above all narrative, do yourself a favor and pick  up and enjoy the ride. You (probably) will come out at the end very happy you did. -George Orwell

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. Brilliant game. Absolutely frustrating achievements. Short but definitely worth it.-Story: The story is great. Unfortunately it might be quite easy to predict where the story is heading but with all the conversations you can delve into, it is very immersive. I was surprised how well the characters are written, the humour and the fidelity of Noir 70's gangster movie. Most other games have dreadful writting or obvious inserted modern day terms or some sort of political slant. This game does it excellently and really goes hard on animal stereotypes which really pops out the humour. -Animals: At first I had no interest in a game called "Chicken Police" and play with weird zoomorphic characters. It reminded me of "Animal Farm". Once giving it a try, I realised that it is definitely worth the playthrough. The humour and racism between animals is hilarious. Very much akin to how the Irish, Italians, Greeks and other ethnicities in New York City will bash each other in a stereotypical way. It works super well. The utilisation of animal stereotypes to create characters is also fantastic. A very smart usage of anthropomorphism in story telling.-Humour: It is so subtle and yet in your face. Some of the jokes might miss you but, the writing is spot on and excellent. Whoever wrote this game is a genius in my opinion.-Graphics: Surprisingly good. I do not know if it is all drawn or a mismatch of pictures and FMV, it works perfectly. It enhances the Noir gangster theme so heavily and beautifully. Really helps you understand the story and keep you on track with that is going on. Via the animations, different animals and voice acting, it is super easy to understand what is going on.-Voice Acting: 10/10. None of this Californian accent or some stupid modern american accent that most games are doing. This is the real deal. The voices really feel they belong in this time period and, you can hear their personalities and emotions when going through the dialogues. The immersion is excellent and the voice acting is responsible for how amazing this game is.-Short: It is a short game. Probably 4 hours or less yet it does the whole point and click genre very well. I do not really play point and clicks but, this is the best I have played ever.-Gameplay: Not really much there other than conversing with certain characters and objects, with the occasional on rails shooting parts. There is not that much of point and click either, so I can safely say there is not much gameplay. I would have been a better game if there were more shooting involved in the game. There were several places throughout the game that could have been a more grandeur scene or spectacle with some sort of shootout since we are dealing with gangsters. There is even an emphasis in referring to guns several times during the story, making you believe you will use them. Unfortunately it does not happen.The detective mechanics are pretty cool in my opinion. Obviously there is only one correct answer to be able to progress which makes the game a bit dull, as you must pick the correct answer to progress. Unlike other games of the same genre, you will naturally pick up all the clues and hints because the game basically forces you and will not let you progress without them. Very linear but it means minimal backtracking.The interrogation mechanic is also pretty neat because here you can make mistakes and progress. Unfortunately, it is mostly for show because they are inconsequential to how you progress. It is mostly a gimmick but a damn good one as you immerse yourself as a detective very well.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs took every single detective noir trope they could think of and threw them into this game.  You're the grizzled aging detective, a loose cannon cop suspended from the force, weeks from retirement, taking a request from a mysterious woman.  The devs then thought this would be too formulaic, so they made him a chicken. (I can see the planning meeting in my head now..."Get it, cause he's hard boiled!")The art style of this game where everyone is a realistic animal head grafted onto human bodies never stops being hilarious, especially because the game always takes everything so seriously.For the game itself, it's more of a visual novel, with very light gameplay mechanics.  The bulk is taken up by characters conversing with each other or you examining the environment.  There's a few puzzles and some multiple choice questioning segments, but there's not actually that much gameplay overall.  Most of the content in the game is actually worldbuilding side content with inspecting background elements (multiple times) and talking to characters not strictly necessary for plot progression.  If you purely followed the main story thread the game would be very, very short, and even with everything it's not very long.  Definitely get this on sale if you want value.The game is hard carried by the excellent voice acting.  Great job to everyone involved.  The lack of meaningful gameplay drags down the decent story, but overall the game tilts towards the positive side.

_childDocuments_.review: I received a key for this from the developer and although visual novel/point-and-click stuff isn't really my thing I decided to give it a whirl because the premise of chickens as police is pretty interesting to me.I wasn't planning to play much but I did get a bit sucked into the story and ended up going through the first chapter which took about four hours. The game feels quite polished mostly because of the art and voice acting (which is almost always great) but I also didn't really encounter any bugs, except one time I did things out of order and the characters talked about visiting a place they had already been (maybe they were trying to block out the body they had just found).The questioning/interrogating of characters is probably my favourite bit (choosing the right dialogue options based on your updating knowledge of their personality) especially because I'm not sure what happens if you completely screw it up and getting the "True Detective" stamp at the end is a super satisfying relief after previous anxiety.The game is mostly about visiting locations, talking to characters, and trying to learn who you can trust while unraveling the mystery. _childDocuments_.review: I don’t know why animal detective games have become a thing in recent years, but there seems to be a trend that they disappoint me. Voice acting for the main character is outstanding and generally good for the others (I say generally; I can do without ever hearing Quetzal again), and graphics are reasonable. The former…not so much. The story is centred around a hackneyed “twist”; the only saving grace of which is that it is not drawn out, but is rapidly solved by the main character. _childDocuments_.review: I honestly expected this to be more of a meme but once you get used to the whole anthropomorphic animal society setting, it turns out to be somewhat of a hidden, little gem. When it comes to design, it's clearly a homage to film noir and that not only visually. The city where the game takes place has some heavy 40-60s USA vibes, you encounter your fair share of cynicism & pessimism, which were also trademarks of film noir so on. The developers seem to have had a pretty clear idea about what kind of game they want to make, how it should feel for the audience etc., which you can clearly see in all those little details like the well written characters, the unique setting/style but what really stood out to me was the great voice acting. For a game in this price range, it's probably among the best I've ever experienced and could easily have been from a game double that price tag. The only little letdown was the ending or rather the last chapter, where the story took a really clichéd plus rather foreseeable turn. It also felt kinda abrupt compared to the long, mysterious build up...maybe they ran out of time or budget. The mess-up between schizophrenia & personality disorder plus the overgeneralized portrayal of mentally ill people might also be an indicator for it. Nevertheless, I would consider this game as a little gem and can suggest it wholeheartedly during sales, if you search for something outside of the mainstream.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the furry exterior, there is a lot to admire here. The art style is strange, but works surprisingly well with the noir theme. There is a lot of background world-building here that I really enjoyed, snippets about gods and wars between predator and prey. Having these jarring-looking creatures act like people really added to the campy absurdity I admire in noir. I've just never seen a game that looks like this before, and I really admire that they took a chance here and did something so different.The voice acting is excellent, for the most part. Sonny sounds spot on as a beleaguered detective, and I have no real complaints. One character is quite irritating, but you'll know who I mean if you do end up playing this game. I spotted two or three typos over the course of the game but none of these were especially disruptive. Gameplay is a mix of visual novel 'click on stuff' gameplay, and some mini games. The mini games are simplistic and mainly involve shooting things. Personally I would have preferred a straight visual novel instead, but I get what they were going for here.So why the negative review? What I don't love here is the story. I was compelled enough to reach the ending, and I now regret putting so much time into this game. Think of a cheesy procedural crime show twist. There you go, you have the ending.End game spoilers below.SPOILERS:Overall, I'm disappointed. This is the 2nd review I've ever felt compelled to write because I was so frustrated by this game. There were the bones of a great visual novel here. And it was squandered away by poor, cliche storytelling. What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 3rd, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.What the heck is this? Chicken Police is a noir detective story, with references to Philip Marlowe early on it’s clear that the creators love the format, and do imitate it almost flawlessly. The writing is on point, there’s a great deal of mystery coming from multiple angles and there’s even a game where you interrogate people. It’s an intriguing game. Oh right, it also has the strangest character models of all time. Every character has a human body, including this woman, and yet the head of an animal and both parts have a ridiculous amount of detail. Oh and oddly good lip syncing.  Why is there cleavage? Serious question. Why? Outside of a few puns about the genre or the characters' names, the game is played pretty straight and the writing does a great job with it. Pick this up if you like a Detective story…. Or if you are a furry. I like this game, and in the first hour, I’m hooked. I want to know more, there are multiple different threads the game is teasing me with, and I am curious where the story will take the player. But I’m also really curious about the characters because every character is equally odd and unique. It’s an art style that I doubt I will ever forget. _childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised by this game. It's got a goofy name, lots of text, and anthropomorphic furry animals to boot - three things that made me apprehensive.So, I'm pleased to say that it was a thoroughly engaging experience - although the story beats are cookie-cutter for a detective noir, it was adult, well-written and funny throughout, with a high level of visual and audio polish, and enough minigames to break up the monotony that typically plagues games with a heavy emphasis on narratives.The developers also bothered to add in a bit of a living world feel, as you can sometimes revisit locations throughout the story for no real functional reason, and the characters will react to recent events - a kind of non-linearity that's appreciated.I did ultimately guess 'whodunnit' with time to spare, but the game is less focused on the answer and more what you do with it.I'm looking forward to a sequel set in the same universe, especially if they flesh out the racial politics - it's like Zootopia after dark.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant game ... I had no idea what to expect really other than, well, Chicken Police ... Im gonna keep this one short as the game sells itself really ... This is a brilliant written, brilliantly made, and brilliantly voiced/acted. The story had me gripped and guessing the whole time and I was hooked from the first time I played it.The visual style was unique, original and very well done, i thought the whole black and white set up was going to get old but it doesn't and it even serves a part of the story.The voice acting is second to none, each character is very well done and they all add a part to the story. Each possible thing you can click on and each person you interact with have many and varying dialogue options. Even repetitive clicks on the same thing results in differing dialogues, this leaves you happily going forward and back checking to see if new dialogues were available based on new evidence ... Ya know, like the real chick ... erm ... detectives.The story could easily be a film. Well written, full of cliff hangers, suspension builders, clues and some very well planned foreshadowing. I was guessing and wondering the entire time right up until the end. The setting of the game is also original and unique but i wont go into too much detail there.All in all, highly recommended, 9/10. I cant wait for the next installation.

_childDocuments_.review: How i found this game:So, I actually was looking for some goof-off games. I randomly searched a key word "chicken" and this was at the middle of the list of results. My thoughts:I read about it before getting it...I was like "this looks like a ♥♥♥♥-post meme noir..." but then I actually got to playing and it was AWESOME. It's actually a super rich story, with really grabbing cliff hangers and events. It keeps you on the edge of your seat through the whole game! I was honestly shocked...like really shocked. I showed it to my friends, playing through it with their help. They went from laughing at it to being fully invested in it. I rarely get my hopes up anymore for games, this day and age is mostly highly polished ♥♥♥♥, remasters, or even the SAME DAMN GAME with a new price tag... so to find something that was different...and also very fun...was...refreshing, to say the least. I would honestly put this game up there as one of my favorites. Considering my intense love for mystery related games. Like seriously. Not to mention all the references to early pop culture! Holy moley! SOOO much thought was put into this game, like seriously.The Characters:I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love them. I love them all. The good ones. The bad ones. They're all complex personalities, with very organic dialog. The voice actors are actually top notch! They sounded natural, not forced, with real emotions. I was really really impressed. Not to mention they all sound so...so...COOL. Classic grime filled, brooding deep voices...luxuriously sensual, smooth, alluring ones.honestly perfect for a playable novel, especially a noir themed one.Sonny is...probably my favorite besides Marty, or even Bosco! Gah it's hard to pick a favorite...they're all so complex and interesting! (this is the longest review i've ever written...)Over all view, what you should know:Over all, top tier to me. If you like noir themed games, simple single player, point and click, this is a good game. Some may find the imagery silly...but, honestly, I found it charming. Give it a chance, you will see what i mean.10/10 I do highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't play detectives much before, and picked this one out of my library mostly because of «funny people with animal faces». I don't see «Comedy» tag for this game on Steam, but actually humour is one of the best parts of the events in the game: while topics and story are quite dark (as it should be for noir media), the jokes of a main duo bring a life-affirming outline to the grim animal-criminal-inhabited city. Also, the voiceover makes the story even more great: it catches and combines both mannerisms of the characters and of the animals, and brings much better immersion than simple text would. The gameplay is pretty simple, but the story is key to this game either way, so no reason to complain at all. Mini games are sparse and simple, but fun. Also, I might be a terrible detective myself because questioning sequences required serious thinking and I still could not exceed 90%.

_childDocuments_.review: The style is very unique and the shares many similarities with LA Noire... on the surface. However, the dialogues/gameplay is very trial and error based. For example, for the first case, the game tells you to be gentle at first, so you'd think asking about things like star signs to establish rapport/friendliness with small talks, or ask how the lady is feeling... but those are all wrong choices. In fact, all the correct choices are blunt and straight to the point. So, what that tells me is that we are just supposed to do trial and error until we got things right, but how the dialogue plays out is seemingly arbitrary. Considering that's the core gameplay loop, I can't recoomend this game for anyone. The upside is that you can keep redoing the choices until you are satisfied, so that's good, but I'd rather the game gives us the proper hints so there'd be cost to our actions.
