_childDocuments_.review: The Chicken Police offers not only a well balanced game but also a reincarnation of the hardboiled detective genre into the world of video games. This game is not only a well made contribution to the genre, it is a great amalgam of the detective elements and mixes general elements with originality. I believe it is safe for me to say that this game has quickly been granted a place among my favorite Noir fictions and maybe my favorite gamesReasons to play this game are:1) Gameplay: Due to the quantity of text, I had an inkling that this game might be a visual novel. The gamer has, however, more freedom than your typical visual novel and can greatly interact with the characters and the world (to the point where I am now doubting whether I really should call this a visual novel).2) Story: The clear Noir theme can already reveal the fact that the makers are experiencing with the hardboiled detective genre regarding plot and its elements. As a result of the large number of dialogues, the story has a deep and complex meaning disguised by hilarious humor and the rough mentality of hardboiled detectives. The antropomorphism is simply amazing which reminds us of the great Blacksad franchise in the sense that it offers a new view of society with a wider range of different races and once again proves that Noir and antropomorphism are quite compatible with each other.3) Characters: Chester Himes introduced in the detective world the famous Harlem duo Grave Digger Jones and Coffin Ed Johnson. The duo of this game, Sonny Featherland and Marty McChicken, are very similar to Himes' Harlem detectives but the Chicken Police are more iconic, in my opinion, due to their personality balance, their humor and simply their presence that offers enjoyment to a wide range of tastes. Furthermore we encounter typical Noir characters such as the powerful mob boss, the aggressive police or the mysterious and alluring femme fatale.4) Art: the art is more focused on photoshopping than drawing, which is innovating to the noir genre and antropomorphism. It definitely is intriguing and is most pleasing. It is normal to see noir and white colours with this kind of genre but the few appearing colours offer a more dramatic importance of certain details that can subtly appeal to the soul.5) Music: the music might not be the most important point but I wish to point out that  it suits the Noir genre terribly well and really adds a convincing touch that allows one to really plunge into the darkest of detective stories.

_childDocuments_.review: This is well worth picking up for fans of games that are more about the story and atmosphere than the game play. The story is very well told and the plot is straight out of a classic detective novel, making it slightly predicable but also entertaining. The most winning part is the characters and the world in general. Everything is tongue in cheek, producing a nice blend of sombre detective story and hilarious interactions between the characters. The voice acting is also brilliant. When you put it all together the game is surprisingly immersive and makes you totally forget how ridiculous it is that you're playing an old chicken detective, interrogating various members of the animal kingdom. Everything just fits and works.The game play is fine, it mostly lies in the interrogations which are really only made slightly challenging by having the available questions be obscure and in some cases be variations of the same thing even though only one will turn out to be correct. The short phrase you select is also not usually indicative of how the conversation will end up going so it's not always obvious why you would pick a specific option until you've actually picked it. In this case it feels like just a way to pad game time since you'll find yourself looking to retry a conversation at least once to try get a better score.This can all be forgiven though seeing as the journey is still well worth it.If adventures are your thing and you're looking for a noir thriller, this is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Marty MacChicken (Young, trigger happy, gun nut) and Sonny Featherland (old, grumpy, alone) are the Chicken Police. The legendary detective duo clearly has seen better days when they are approached by the mysterious Natasha Catzenko who is being threatened.With only 121 days left until Sonny's pension what could go wrong ?Chicken Police is a detective game set in the city of Clawville which is populated by various animal characters and humans are considered mythical creatures. The game is presented in as a film noir inspired visual novel in grainy black&white 2,5D style and a nice smooth jazz soundtrack in the background. I particularly liked the character design with the animal heads on top of human bodies in the dialogues. In combination with the superb voice acting all characters felt very deep and relatetable. There is a lot of inter-species banter and witty wordplays in the dialogs which makes it worth visiting all the optional locations and exhaust all dialog options. The game itself relies on the typical mechanics: canvas the scene, talk to everyone or perform an interrogation to gain clues which can be combined in a mini-game. I found the story quite entertaining and it made some interesting turns which kept me in the dark for some time. It would have been interesting to get more immersed in the overall world since the Devs put some effort in carving out an animal society with a own history, politics and its own struggles. (A lot is hinted at in dialogues which enable more detailed "codex" entries which can be accessed in your notebook but I found that a little bit tedious ). The length of the game was ok for me - I think I did most of the dialogues and visited all locations with next to no dialog skipping in 11h.  Overall, I enjoyed the game very much and can wholeheartedly recommend it.

Sometimes i knew exactly what to say and sometimes it felt like flipping a coin and waiting on the completed dialogue to inform me if my guess was right. _childDocuments_.review: Mild spoilers, nothing plot-critical, nothing blatant. I finished the game in /one go,/ and it took me 7-8 hours.  The story's nothing revolutionary, but it is incredibly well done and pulls off things that usually would be considered a cop-out.  Like a good detective game (in my opinion), there is nothing that the characters figure out that you can't yourself with the evidence provided.There's a rather unique system for recapping parts of the case that sums it up particularly well and doesn't punish you if you get the details wrong (it'll hold your hand), and the interrogation system seems to scale difficulty with how difficult it actually would be to interrogate that person;  People eager to inform you are a breeze, while somebody who's rather deceitful will provide a decent challenge.You've already seen the unconventional art style, so it's your call on whether or not that's worth it for you.  The music is on-point, the characters are well written (seems like a pattern).My single biggest issue with the game was that once I finished a shooting scene it was the most abrupt transition to afterward I'd ever experienced (I thought I skipped a cutscene, but apparently not), and at the 2nd to last cutscene my game stuttered and I missed a rather impactful moment.9.7/10I'd also recommend for the developers to make some plot-critical achievements hidden ones as well. Somebody can easily get some shocks ruined for them if they check achievements before playing.Also, if you like this, check out Backbone.  Similar concept, different art style and execution.  It's coming out ~Q1 of 2021.

name: Old Gods Rising
detailed_description: Thomas Winston, Professor of Ancient History and recently fired host of the popular TV show “Finding Britain,” has been in hiding for weeks. Publicly embarrassed by the revelation that his latest book was largely based on fraudulent evidence, he decides to accept an invitation from maverick film director, Maz Kayfer, to act as a consultant on his new film: “Old Gods Rising.” Ashgate University, where the filming will take place, seems to be an ideal location, but when Tom arrives, things get very strange, very quickly.  Has he become the unwitting star of Kayfer’s latest film?  Or, has he stumbled into something far more sinister? Old Gods Rising is a first-person adventure mystery that puts you in the role of disgraced History Professor, Thomas Winston, as you explore Ashgate University and try to uncover the truth behind the strange events that seem to be unfolding. Examine architecture and artifacts to find clues about the university's ancient origins, and use your expertise to decipher long-forgotten languages and cryptic carvings. Solve the puzzles that block your progress and uncover hidden areas that could help you decide what is real and what is not. As you search for answers, use the phone numbers you have collected and navigate conversations to build a more complete picture of what is actually happening and why. Are the Old Gods rising? It's up to you to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning I was quite hooked. The world is beautifully crafted and the general setup (I don't know whether what I experience is real or not) is very interesting. Also there is quite a bit to look at - notes that shed some light on what is happening, hidden rooms (similar in spirit to what Portal has done) and curious artworks full of geeky references. But overall, even though it is beautiful and interesting, the levels conjured up the feeling of an artificial stage and not a world that is being lived in. I think this is mostly because you find everything, without fail, at just the right moment and have no room to miss much of anything. There is no superfluous information or corridor. Any doors you should not walk through are locked. There are virtually no dead ends and nearly all information you find is relevant for the plot. All of this is at odds with the premise that wants you to keep wondering whether the experience is real, or not.Nonetheless, I had fun playing the game up until the last 15 minutes which rushed in an ending that was very unsurprising and simply felt unfulfilling since it does not really conclude or answer anything.Minor notes:- The game was very buggy for a release in 2020. I have fallen through the floor several times, had issues with disappearing levels and so on. This is a no go for a fully linear game of three hours length.- The story has no clear conclusion and ends very abruptly. Another hour or so would have done wonders, I'd wager. I'd recommend to buy the game for a few Euros, not the full price, if you don't mind the negative points above.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this would have been better with a less restrictive approach. As it is, this game is a bit of a walking simulator that occasionally throws "puzzles" at you. However, the level design is amazing. There is some really cool scenery in this game, as well as some interesting lore accompanied by a scattering of unique points of interest and tons of gated off areas that would have had a lot of potential for use in a larger, more in depth game.The story, while short, is pretty good. It's very predictable, but still a commendable addition to the Cthulhu Mythos.  My only real complaint is that there are a couple lines of comedic dialogue near the end of the game that are very out of place and kind of disrupt the atmosphere.I hope we can see some more titles like this from Bad Blood in the future with more open world and interactive aspects, but for now I'll just say that I think most people who appreciate Lovecraftian works will find this to be worth the 20 bucks.Also, supporting people who expand the mythos is always a worthy cause.

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring a closed university as adviser for a film director ... and finding not only weirdly fascinating statues but a lot more! You are alone, but have regular communication with your assistant and the film director, who asks you to explore areas within the university and the outside facilities.  You listen to your own steps, expect to meet somebody behind every corner, but you will not for a long time.  And when you meet people, it will be for the big task, you had to fulfill, without knowing it.  Loved the atmosphere, the story as well as the great voice acting, that made characters visible. It is a more silently creepy feeling not blunt horror, that is presented.  Would love to see more of that.Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Old Gods Rising ~~~~~~~~~~~~~Old Gods Rising, an adventure first-person game that focuses on Lovecraftian genre. Named after American author H. P. Lovecraft, Lovecraftian brings a great sub-genre of horror to the table. Lovecraftian focuses on comic horror characteristics of the unknown, gore or other elements of shock. The game Old Gods Rising got the Lovecraftian genre just right. It’s all smooth sailing in a peaceful first-person adventure game, until things start to get complicated and mysterious. Our main protagonist is Professor Tom Winston, an expert in the field of Ancient History. Tom’s recent success on his TV show, ‘Finding Britain’, attracts the attention of maverick film director, Maz Kayfer. Maz Kayfer invites Tom to be his consultant for the new film: Old Gods Rising. Convinced that Kayfer’s project needs a consultant on Ancient History, Tom arrives at the Ashgate University. The moment Tom set his foot in the university parking area, he knows something is wrong; the University seems empty.Tom goes in search of the director, and instead finds a wireless where Kayfer alerts Tom about his little situation. Kayfer requests that Tom look into some Ancient landmarks and Store structures. Heading out alone in an empty and ominous university campus, Tom finds both local and foreign stone structures; some are dated BC and others are AD. Surprised to find this many ancient stone structures in one university ground, and not knowing Kayfer’s intensions, Tom alerts Kayfer about every event and discovery. At first, you don’t expect anything out of the ordinary. Ashgate University seems like an ideal place for Kayfer’s project. But as you go through one discovery to another, the truth starts to unfold. You start to question Kayfer’s intentions, so you use a payphone to call your better half, Lex, who starts to research Kayfer’s past misdeeds. Now aware of Kayfer’s ill intensions, Tom investigates the university grounds while keeping Kayfer in the loop with minor details. Kayfer alerts Tom that he has film crews in the university area, but you can’t seem to find anyone at all until you hear a loud call for help. You look behind you and realise that it’s coming from the sewer. Responding to the cries for help, you hear the voice of a girl, a member of Kayfer’s crew. The sewer is dark and narrow; by the time you come back with a light, the poor girl’s call for help is gone. Tom is greeted by an ominous silence, followed by a loud, terrifying roar. Upset with the events that are taking place, Tom sets off on a journey of intense investigation to find answers and try to uncover Kayfer’s misdeeds and ill intentions. As you move forward, you start to realize that Kayfer is trying to raise the old Gods, and you find yourself in a struggle to stop Kayfer’s plan.Let me start by staying Old Gods Rising is bringing a unique genre of storytelling to the table, creating a really strong, well-detailed, and very well scripted game. I must say, I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing this game, if only because of its impressive voice acting and dialogue. The voice acting for the main protagonist and antagonist was very strong and well-executed. The character progression of Tom Winston was slow and subtle. Sound effects were well executed, too; at times the game was outright terrifying because of its well-placed and effective sound effects. The Monster sounds in the dark caves and alleyways were horrifying. Although the game presents a unique player experience with its incredible story, strong characters, and voice acting, it has its fair share of shortcomings.Conversations between Tom and Lex were annoying and repetitive due to the audio levels dropping so low at times that I could not figure out what Lex was saying, which in turn lead to a lot of confusion.Although I have a lot of good things to say about this game, good performance isn’t one of them. Among the many issues, the most noticeable were: random frame drops, stutter, lag, 20 – 30 frames dropped consistently while walking on the footpath in the parking, and the map/playable area loads very slowly.I had to wait outside rooms and alleyways for the game to finish loading the next section of the map.I must say the game brings some originality to the table when it comes to puzzles; they were unique and fairly easy to complete. By far the best part about this game is its attention to detail; though nowhere near perfect, for an indie creator to bring this level of detailing to a game is very impressive. There were multiple structures in place which were very well detailed, including large rooms and alleyways, caves, and ancient sites. Although well detailed for a university of this size and caliber, the world/map seemed empty.Positives: + Short yet rich story+ Attention to detail + Great voice acting + Great sound effects + Large playable area+ Decent puzzles + Unique example of the Lovecraftian genre of horror + Implementation of the investigating, discovering, and going through the mysteries were done wellNegatives: - Minor graphic issues - Audio issues while in conversation with Lex - Frame drops- Lags and Sutter - Poor lighting in some areas- The map/world loads very slowlyA great, story-rich Lovecraftian horror experience with decent gameplay, if you can overlook some performance issues. 7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing Old Gods Rising. It is a first person exploratory adventure seen through the eyes of Professor Winston. At the request of a movie director, he visits Ashcraft University to research it for a movie location. The university is empty (film crew nowhere to be found) and the story is told through phone calls made by Tom and his radio conversations with the director.The sound track and voice overs are well done. You will need to listen to them, as you can't click through dialog or leave a scene during many of the conversations or narrations. The university is vast and has been created with great details. It was very authentic, with many buildings, corridors, rooms, gardens, artwork, etc. Tom soon begins to find some oddities in the artifacts he is examining (which he describes in great detail) and suspects that all is not as it appears. To tell more would be to enter spoiler territory so I will leave it at that. The game is really a huge hidden object exercise. The story leads you down a basic path but there are several sets of items to find if you are achievement oriented. The university is maze-like and you will need to explore every doorway, room, and corridor that you can access. There are 'you are here' maps posted which are helpful if you get lost. There are a handful of easy puzzles to access certain gates. Otherwise, it is just explore at your own pace, getting through objectives as they are presented, and trying to find as many of the 'objects of interest' that you are inclined to search for.Towards the end, there is a 'point of no return.' I stumbled through this doorway prior to finding everything I was looking for. After seeing the end, I replayed from the beginning. Although you have to repeat some conversations and puzzles, your achievement progress is saved so you only have to find items missed on previous games.Although none were game breaking, there were some minor bugs. Doorways that led to 'blue sky' nothingness and an occasional game freeze. Both required reloading from the last save point. I soon learned to avoid 'blue sky' openings, as they would self-correct if you left the area and returned. The game auto-saves so often that you don't lose progress if you stop playing (either by choice or due to a glitch). I also had some issues with achievements on my second time through - the counts seemed to get out of synch but all corrected in the end and I reached the 100% I was targeting.I thought Old Gods Rising was an interesting story that held my interest and I took pleasure in wandering the halls of a virtual university. I recommend it to those who enjoy a slower paced game with much to see.An added note - there is a bonus chapter available if you load your saved game after completion. It did not make a lot of sense to me, as it added some action elements without explanation so I walked away, feeling quite satisfied with completing just the core game.

_childDocuments_.review: "When does mildly meta become aggressively meta?", the game asks itself without a hint of irony.Once again, there should be a more nuanced way to review games besides fully negative or fully positive - because this game deserves your time and money, but it doesn't deserve your respect.The game is riddled to the core with referential humor, to it's own detriment. It's obsessed with undercutting any possible tension with a joke - like playing D&D with someone can't go for more than a few seconds without cracking wise. Even with it's last gasp, the game refuses to take itself seriously.To a point, this works in the games favor. It will make you question if this really a horror game, or some sort of comedy like "Hot Fuzz". But it doesn't ever turn the silliness off and let you be afraid.The sculptures littered across the campus are one of the best examples of this. Some of them are moderately clever puns, which have several layers to them. Others are so garishly out of place they feel like they should be Easter eggs, hidden behind something.The setting is wonderful. The plot is nicely set up. The game-play itself is solid with a few rough edges where you can see the game's seams. The puzzle system is under-utilized and needed more puzzles. The mythological research in the game is spot on and made me think that once the game got to the "third act" it be serious for the big reveal. It was not. It stopped just short of having something jump out at you wearing a giant purple hat that looks like a strangled Muppet. I encourage you to try the game and form your own opinions. It's not wholly un-enjoyable. I had a midly fun three hours.I hope the dev goes on to do more games that are either more serious or more comedic - because they can do both, but not both at once.

_childDocuments_.review: A great premise, and strong ideas - but simply not a professional final product in any respect.I really wanted to love Old Gods Rising.  The idea is great, and at first it feels like an entire game made out of the "behind the walls" portions of Portal or the Stanley Parable, with a horror twist.But then the problems start.  The interface feels incomplete.  Achievements fail to pop.  There are frequent typos in the subtitles.  The visual design looks more like something from the late 90s even when it's working - but on top of that, textures are misaligned or fail to load, geometry is janky, and on two separate occasions I fell through the world entirely and had to reload from an earlier save.  In a game where it's supposed to feel significant when something looks a bit "off", it's crippling when there are so many things *unintentionally* broken.  On top of that, the story simply doesn't know where it's going.  The ending reveals both too much and too little.  The tone seems to deliberately aim for the intersection of comedy and horror (as implied by the final postscript) but rather than achieving an effective blend, it just makes it hard to care much about what's happening by the time you approach the end.  I can't recommend this game, certainly not at its current price ($29 AUD).  It's possible a patch may fix some or all of its many, many bugs - but no patch is going to fix the art design, or the story.  At best, a version of this game with no bugs may be worth your time if its price falls below $6 AUD.

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts interestingly, but it descends below mediocrity very fast. The writing that's supposed to hold this game together falls flat and with it the entire rest of the game. I straight up solved some of the puzzles accidentally. The graphics are nice, but the technical state of the game is precarious. By the end of the story there was no mystery and the ending was just bad. The game tries to set up ambiguity while it's constantly undercutting one of the two possibilities and then it still expects you to take seriously the undercut possibility. Other than the arguably quite nice graphics the game has nothing to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a hard game to review, because despite its variety of flaws it was still fairly fun and engaging. If you enjoy walking simulator games, this may be for you. If you enjoy only slightly spooky games it could be for you. If you want to spend a couple hours noodling around in the game for the hell of it, it's not terrible. But I have trouble recommending it for $20, which is what it's currently priced at. The voice work is good enough, the game design and story leave something to be desired, though. I fell through the floor a few times, and there are a couple major story areas that you need to emphatically suspend your disbelief in order to see past. I think $5 would be a good price for this game. I remember when firewatch came out, I played it through in one sitting, which took somewhere between 5 and 7 hours. This game took me less than 3, and I wouldn't say that I was looking in every corner, I took my time. It's just not quite worth it in my opinion. With that said, though, I still enjoyed it. I don't know how many people worked on it, or how long it took them, or anything about what it took to make the game, I'm just looking at it compared to a similar game, with a comparable price. If you get it, I hope you enjoy it! Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR/Summary:  I highly recommend this game to anyone, especially those who like narrative driven mystery/adventure concepts, Great atmosphere, Graphics, Lore, Voice acting, wit,  and more.         I didnt have much of an idea how entertaining this game would be... but 4 hours in and I am itching to pick it back up as soon as possible to beat. So far its well worth the purchase, and I feel like there's a lot more in store too...     The game does have some minor bugs that happen here and there (as to be expected from any  $20 indie game i've ever played),  but it is only an issue because they can briefly break the excellent- captivating immersion that the game creates in the first place! The only other gripe,  is that it can be a little dry at the beginning, especially for those that as of recent, have been used to playing  $80+ games like DOOM (and not fire watch or Long dark etc.), but the ~$20 game quickly takes mysterious and intriguing turns, that really make it a great mystery, and better than a book of the same genre.  As i said earlier it is  Very immersive due to its great graphics (especially the textures) which you can tell have been worked on meticulously, and has a lovely atmosphere, with its attention to detail, clever lore, witty easter eggs,  and great voice acting, even the sound is hyper dimensional/dynamic (which help to cause a few frights).  I highly recommend this game to anyone, especially those who like narrative driven mystery/adventure concepts with unique wit and Sci fi horror themes blended in.

_childDocuments_.review: is yet another game that surprised me more than expected. It has some rough edges and is very clearly indie, but it still managed to be an interesting experience.The voice acting and art style is pretty good. You're quite simply exploring a regular-looking college campus for most of the game, but you feel like something bigger is at play here, and weird things are happening while you look for a film crew (your character's job is to help work for a new film).This game is really one hard to explain but the best way to put it is that it examines paranoia and conspiracy theories.I'm not sure I could say it's worth $10 because it is probably only about 2 hours in length, assuming you're not exploring every piece of the campus. You can find some hidden optional areas or Easter eggs that point at the plot early on. It can be a couple of hours longer depending upon your pacing and if you go for all of the achievements.At the same time, I don't think the game needed to be longer. However, it could've handled its ending a little better, as it was too abrupt.One thing to note is that they added an extra chapter onto the game, but I thought it made little sense and played pretty poorly. If they had rounded out the main game and fixed up issues, that would've been much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. It's sort of like a Lovecraftian Stanley Parable type game with lots of references to pop culture and nerd humour as well as general humour. This is a walking simulator that has lots to look at and explore as well as a captivating story which keeps you intrigued the whole way through as you try to work out what is going on. You can get the gist of what is actually happening but there is something about the way that is executed that leaves you unsure of yourself the whole way through. The ambient music is superb and so are the sound effects and it really adds depth and immersion to the game along side the fantastic visuals.Some problems I have however include the lack of options in the pause menu; no real saving structure (as I couldn't achieve 100% in one playthrough because the "Empty Graves" achievement seems to have bugged, I found the last grave which is story related and the achievement never unlocked and I am unable to reload a save from that point in order to retry). Ordinarily I would replay the whole game again just to achieve it, but I feel as though one playthrough is enough and doing so would be too tedious, as the final grave is at the end of the story. All in all, I really do recommend "Old Gods Rising", it's a great time-killer!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game after reading an article about it in Game Informer. This game comes from Bad Blood studio which is a one man operation. I implore people to read the article to get a bit of insight into the development and the man behind the scene.Gameplay	The game at its core is close to a walking simulator with some puzzle elements thrown into the mix. I never felt like the puzzles were overly hard or too easy. Felt just right. You walk or run place to place and piece together what’s going on at the university. You have run, jump, and crawl at your disposal. You won’t use jump a whole lot but glad it’s there as it would’ve been hard to get over some obstacles in the game. Crawl I believe is only used about four times or so. There’s various clipboards and books scattered throughout the game for the player to read that will shed a bit of light on the story. If you’re looking for explosions every five seconds or so then this isn’t the game for you. Go watch a Michael Bay film or play Call of Duty.Story	The game starts out in the protagonist, Tom’s, office. After a brief conversation you’ll head to the university where the story begins. The story is a slow burn. You get snippets here and there but just enough to keep you going. The story is different and that’s what I liked about it. I wouldn’t say it’s a story that’s never been told but just enough to keep me intrigued. You’ll definitely get the Lovecraftian vibes from the get-go. The story, honestly, gets kinda weird but in a good way. I hope there’s a sequel.SpecsYou won’t need a NASA computer to run it. I’m running on an older FX series AMD CPU with a 1660Ti and it ran just fine. You do get the option to pick your graphics quality but not fine tune to your needs. You got low, medium, and high.BugsI did have some problems with areas not loading as I approached them. Basically I walked into a vast gray area. Then the environment loaded. On the flip side though it may be my hard drive. It’s not exactly a top tier one either. There’s one grave that Tom makes a comment on but no subtitles pop up. Other than that I didn’t encounter anything else that was game breaking. OverallI’m satisfied with my purchase. I didn’t feel like $20 was too much. Theaters charge $15 a person and give you less entertainment. For $20 I got three and half hours of entertainment and if I want to do achievement hunting I could get another two hours or so out of it. I look forward to what this studio does in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I NEVER finish a game in one go -- even games I enjoy I tend to only play an hour at a time.  However, I played this game from start to finish in one session, so it's safe to say I enjoyed it.  I can't say it's too short, as if it had been too much longer it might have felt like padding.  My only real gripes are the weird way it loads areas, as several times the area nextdoor would load at the last possible second, or once didn't load at all and I fell into the abyss.  That and the weird tone shift at the end was kind of a bummer.I will for sure be keeping an eye on this developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Whats in a classification? I wouldn't necessarily call this a "game" as much as an interactive experience. If you're looking for something with head scratching puzzles this won't hit your mark, but there's a lot of love in other places. If you enjoy the VR Story adventures this will fit better. I Picked up the game to stream something Chill and support the Canadian indie scene and Old Gods definitely hit the chill vibes, with the odd neck hair standing on end creeping in here and there. The story is well done, the art is great overall, the audio is nice, the cheeky nods with the sculptures are great - especially the "Pinball One" if you know it you'll know it :). I spent about 4 hours total playing through, enjoyed just vibing out, game set a mood and I kept going. If you just go straight through I feel you'll take maybe a couple hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine, I guess. Writing and voice acting are both good. But it has some technical issues. Feels very amateur. I still had some fun with a story but I'm not sure the story alone is good enough to justify the recommendation. So only try it if you really want some short mystery adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: 'Old Gods Rising' is a cheeky and mysterious adventure game set in an English university. The main story line for our character, Professor Thomas Winston, is to investigate Ashgate University’s ancient artifacts for movie director, Maz Kayfer. Although reluctant at first, our character heads off to explore the university upon encouragement from his partner, Lex.Throughout the game, the player is pushed in various directions leading to the player suspecting a few contrasting conclusions (I don’t wish to spoil things). This is realized through great voice acting (especially by the voice acting behind Lex, Tom’s partner) and a ton of satirical and amusing artwork. The artwork was my favorite part of the game and I made efforts to painstakingly explore every corner of the university in search of it – I was not disappointed. This is most evident through my discoveries of a plethora of Easter eggs subtlety hidden throughout the university, waiting for the player to discover.The world consists mainly of the university, which is brilliantly modeled (you can tell this is the developer’s forte). Even though the university is designed to be empty, it still manages to feel alive; birds chirping, crickets in the bushes and don’t forget those pesky CCTV cameras. The entire setting feels sarcastic and hyperbolic in nature – a grand, stone university at first glance that actually turns out to be a bit of joke of an institution.The main characters are all voice-acted incredibly well and is one of the game’s strengths! Tom’s partner Lex easily instills an impression of calmness and sensibility that keeps Tom grounded. The main character, Thomas Winston and movie director, Maz Kayfer, are both written and voice-acted in a manner that depicts themselves as exaggerations (like the University), which I found highly amusing and thought-provoking!If you are a fan of Lovecraftian elements, enjoy games with a hint of humor (especially English humour!) and/or you like uncovering mysteries…this one is for you!P.S. Played about 10 hours with non-Steam version of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I weep for humanity and the future of its entertainment to see so many reviews say this is "ok". It's not ok for $12.99. This game is 3-4 hours long. The missing crew (and missing people in the entire experience) eventually are proven to be a convenient excuse to not render any people, either due to technical inability or a lack of motivation. Game would avoid a negative rating if it was $4.99 and bought on sale for $1.99.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: On the technical side, playing this game with anything but a QWERTY keyboard layout is huge pain, as the only way to move in the game is by using the WASD keys. No way to remap it, no way to even use arrows or a pad controller.Apart from this, the game has some nice or funny moments but the writing is not memorable. It has some plot holes and inconsistency that damage the story by the end.Nevertheless, it's not a game for everyone, but if you fancy a light game with some twist on pulpy cosmic horror tropes, it is short enough to be enjoyable despite its flaws.My biggest regret is the bonus chapter after the ending. It changes the gameplay to something much more action oriented and it is not very good at it. Beside, it cheapens the ending of the story and the voiceover during the credits.Not a memorable game, and I would not recommend it to most of the people, but could be worth for the curiosity.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: great game, especially for the low price point, i havent finished it yet but i already like the setting and the story so far. its a nice little gem of a game especially for those who are looking for games which reference archeological related stuff and are down for uncovering a mystery.  though some ppl might find this game to be simple, and not challenging enough, i actually like how much hand holding the game does for you, so instead of getting a frustrating ui or confusing map, the gameplay experience of walking trough the various places of ashgate university was a smooth experience and made for a quick and easy game to enjoy. the game art is also good, i was worried that it would look uncanny but the game art actually looks very well done and i liked looking at the various statues in the game. overall its an interesting idea, definitely something that i would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good graphics and art direction- Quality voice acting- Fun story- Achievements are reasonable- Not too longCons:- Some visual glitches- Movement can be kind of janky when stepping up ledges- Save system is auto-save only- No dialog skip featureOld Gods Rising is a well-made walking simulator that I enjoyed my time with. If you played other cosmic horror-themed games like Moons of Madness or Call of Cthulhu then you will likely enjoy this. Despite the subject matter, I'd say OGR is more comedy than horror. The humor is a bit reference-heavy for my taste, but isn't overbearing.The achievements in this game are not absurd and instead act as a guide for you to experience all the game has to offer, which is how it should be. This prompts comment on the biggest problem this game has...the save system.I had to replay the game as it prevents you from backtracking at a certain undisclosed point and you'll almost certainly be missing a good amount of optional content when you cross that line. Unfortunately, replaying the game is a bit of a chore as there is much dialog and no way to skip it. I recommend playing the game once and then coming back through while listening to a podcast to mop up. Also, check out the last game news update for instructions on starting the post-game mode...I had a good time with it even though the dessert gameplay is very different from the main course.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

It's bizarre how this isn't better known or championed.  Very much recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I really liked this game xD. At first, I was feeling it was just ok; I couldn't help myself but to compare it to other great walking simulators, like Firewatch and Conarium. I kept feeling that it was sub-par when compared to those, which is fine, those are incredible, I wasn't expecting something like that, but I kept asking myself what was it that those did so well, and that this one failed to. But the ending was really great, and I think a lot of stuff falls into place afterwards. It's its own thing, it definitely didn't try to be actual lovecraftian horror like Conarium, or a realistic and serious game like Firewatch, it tried to be a bit lovecraftian, with a bit of comedy, and a lot of exploration. And for what it tried to do, I think it totally succeeded. I think fans of exploration games will probably have a great time with this. It could have used more puzzles, but it wasn't its goal, and I'm fine with that. It was also pretty well optimized, I didn't encounter any relevant bugs while I played it (maybe some textures took a while to load here and there, and I got stuck once on terrain, but there's an autosave feature that's very well implemented, it saves really really often, and you can even choose when to do it by crossing doors and stuff, so it wasn't a problem at all). It has very good voice acting too, and the comedic elements got me to laugh many many times (especially the dialog). It doesn't have the atmosphere of a lovecraftian game, but it's fine, it is its own thing, and I praise it for that. Gameplay was ok, one of the most annoying things a walking sim like this can do is having your character be as slow as a granny when walking, and as fast as an average walking person when running; luckily, this wasn't the case here, you walk and run at normal speeds, and that's a relief. If you explore thoroughly, you can get all the achievements in one playthrough (I did) without any walkthroughs or guides, and if you don't, a quick second playthrough should get you to find what you missed fairly quickly (and you don't need to find everything again, just the stuff you missed). There are other little details implemented to ensure you have a smooth ride, and don't need to backtrack a lot or anything like that (the only nitpick I have on this is that a portable map, like a brochure, would have been really helpful for those of us who like to explore a lot). On top of it all, there's even an after-credits minigame, kind of like an fps, and if you complete it, you'll get an extra piece of dialog that can help you piece everything together, if you weren't sure what to make of the ending (which is a bit ambiguous, but in a good, totally intentional way).TL,DR: it's pretty good, especially the ending, and everyone who enjoys exploration games, especially walking sims, should have a fun time with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: In general I enjoyed my short time with this game. Short, easily digestable walking simulaters like these are totally my jam. Gameplay-wise you just walk around and explore, which is fine by me, and you check stuff out. As geek trash I sometimes chuckled at some of the references. The Reservoir Dogs one was my favourite. The University was in general a treat to explore. A sort of quest log would've been nice, since at one point I received 3 seperate sets of instructions and I tend to quickly forget things like locations etc etcThe three main voice actors do a pretty good job , the sound design is on point, the sparse music set the scene.In short, I enjoyed my short time with this game, but the ending kind of soured it. I wasn't the biggest fan of the shooter chapter after the credits, but if this experiment is any indication of them maybe creating a lovecraftian themed shooter, consider me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying this game except for the last part. I'll avoid spoilers.When working with the team, the puzzle was too easy. It's like my hand was held the whole way.The post-credits portion turned into a first person shooter with no guidance or even a health meter. And if you died, you had to go back to the beginning. Other issues: If/when you're asked to meet people at places, it would be useful to have those added to your objective list. It was a little too hand-holding for some objectives to appear and others not to.I'd love for there to be a button to change the dialogue choices so that I could play with my trackpad rather than having to deal with my mouse scroll wheel.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "could have been great games....could have been". However, it is buggier than a Motel 6, have to wait for location renders or you fall through the floor on an ongoing basis.Some puzzles are stupidly easy and are VERY hard to believe NO ONE at the university discovered the stuff you are finding out? Plus the game doesn't even give you a chance to figure it out, it is like playing a puzzle game with that one annoying kid that has already played it trying to show off by spoiling the answers for you. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game had me hooked from the start. Pretty short little game but I loved it. If I remember correctly from the reddit post that first introduced me to it, it was a one man team (?) and you can see the love put into it in every scene, it really is very well done and pretty to look at.Story wise, totally my thing too. All the little extra tidbits, random numbers that you can call but don't have to, the snarky posters riddled throughout. This guy didn't just make a story, he put stuff in there for the people who poke in all those nooks and crannies. The story was great too, had me second guessing and then second guessing my second guesses up until the end.I hope this guy keeps going and if so I can't wait to see what he has up his sleeve next. Just looked ad his website, keep it up Hayden, I loved it!!!Performance wise there was some streaming issues that lead to me falling through the map if I got impatient and walked into them, but I think that's since improved.As a fan of the What Remains of Edith Finch type game, this was perfect for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and intriguing game. The graphics are great and the story was really interesting, at risk of showing my age, it had similar vibes to Myst. While it's a little on the short side, the price is reflective of this and it's worth the cost. I would have liked the story to have been a bit deeper in places, and it felt like it started to sprint toward the end whereas I would have been happier for it to go on a little longer and maybe be a bit more fleshed out. _childDocuments_.review: The game is decent and looks pretty pro, the problem is that because of those points the game is naturally held to higher standards.  I kept expecting more, because the game looked like it was going to give more, but really, it didn't need to.  Well, actually it would have been nice if there was a bit more depth to the story.  This game is pretty much Scratches DX, but with less story material and waaay more physical ground to cover.  I mean, right down to the main character being an author, having an extremely similar voice and accent, and being instructed by phone calls.  They just forgot to have novels worth of story in loose paper scattered around.I'm pretty convinced that this game was based on Scratches, but updated with a larger set, and a much grander supernatural element.  Or maybe its structure is just more common than I realize.  Unfortunately the writers missed out on how Scratches had you actually think for yourself sometimes, learn about the history of the setting as its own character, the history of several actual characters, intertwining them with a threatening supernatural element (which we also learned the history of) that our player is now facing, and the mystery of how it ties to a potential physical threat that is evolving around us.OGR has a cool setting.  The lack of other humans kind of breaks immersion, but most of the time it helps the atmosphere.  Especially when someone new speaks to you from in a tunnel, or runs away from you at a distance.  The graphics make my computer scream so they're probably good, and the story is decent enough.  It just lacks a few layers.  There were lots of neat little things that I kept hoping were going to be developed along side the plot as their own thing, but they just kind of popped in and popped out as reminders to the main mystery, as if we might have forgotten what the game was about.I'd say buy it when it's on sale, but apparently it's already had a permanent price drop since I bought it, so maybe just do it; if you want a light, short, walking simulator to chill with.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- it's very pretty and atmospheric- the university is fun to explore- lots of great (virtual) artwork and sculptures to look at- most of the voice acting is well done- it's essentially a walking simulator (and I like those and maybe you do too)Cons:- the story is not deep nor very interactive, so if that's what you're looking for you might be disappointed- it's short-ish, took me around 4 hours- with apologies to the dev, it seems a bit overpriced at $20 so try to catch it on sale- one of the voice actors is a little over-the-top and irritating- it's essentially a walking simulator (and I like those but maybe you don't)Sounds like some folks had technical difficulties, but my experience was fine. In 4 hours of play over multiple sessions I had one instance where the environment didn't render properly until I was right on top of an area, and elsewhere I ran into one place with a small missing texture, but beyond that I didn't have any problems. The game could use some more exposed config points, especially to increase mouse sensitivity or to adjust FOV, but while I found the inability to adjust those things kind of offputting initially, I stopped noticing after a while. The dev seems responsive on the forums and is continuing to make updates so maybe these points will be addressed in a future patch.Lots of fun details to be found all over, particularly the nods to other games and media in the sculptures. There's not as much game here as I had hoped, but It's easy to see the care and craft put into what is here. All told it's a promising first release from this dev; I'll be looking forward to the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It's interesting to start with. However, a lot really needs to be fixed. A lot of the time I've spent in the game has been sent waiting for the next area to load. Until, I'm stuck staring at an empty area that, if I try to walk in, will have me falling endlessly while the rest of the map disappears above me. There'll be sudden moments where the game just pauses for a few seconds. Trying to walk in certain places is difficult unless you approach it from the right angle. All of this detracts from the atmosphere of the game and pulls me out of it. If these things can be fixed, I'm sure I would enjoy it more. As it is now, I can't recommend this game.Nevermind. The ending was stupid and the new chapter is lousy.

The few puzzles in the game are rudimentary and not remotely challenging. It is worth checking out if it is on sale and you like supporting the little guys, but I don't think I could recommend it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Old Gods Rising. If you liked similar games like Gone Home or Firewatch then you know what to expect here. A gorgeous game to wander through as you unlock the story as you progress. The art is great and the story and writing is good and I didn't experience any bugs. The voice acting is particularly good. The developer also seems active in the forums and in patching and updating the game so that's a good thing.I'd recommend this to anyone that likes narrative based games with very light puzzles and just wants to walk around for a few hours and unwind a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game, played with partner in one sitting. game looked great on top settings with just a few glitches on the way that caused us to restart however the frequent auto-saves helped us there. overall, good story with some good humour in parts, just wished we'd taken more time to explore the area as we completed the story in a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy the game, there were a couple of things that bugged me. First, having to stand around while I wait for the next area to load was a little annoying. Second, the ending was rather abrupt and felt a bit rushed. Other than that the voice acting was good and, the puzzles were interesting, and the models were fairly well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of these narrative based exploration games and this one was by far the most intriguing. The narrative is well paced with lots of additional story hooks and moments if you dig deep. The art is consistently impressive and pleasure to experience. Every new set piece out does the last and really pulls you into the story. I typically view these sorts of games as short stories and temper my expectations around that.If you are looking for something a little different that is thought provoking and beautiful to look at don't hesitate to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game this morning and I really enjoyed it.  I'm sure there were a handful of things I missed catching, but overall I was pretty locked into the game the entire time.  The only complaint I have (which may be my fault for playing games in this genre so much) is that if you're paying attention and try to piece things together, you can probably figure the ending out on your own about 75% through.  It is a little on the short end for $20, even though it is a gorgeous game.  And I had a handful of graphics related glitches for a little while, but nothing game breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful graphically, It has an interesting start, and it is of a subject matter I adore. However the game is lacking in very big areas. It is rushed, buggy, and it has a unfulfilling end. I had sections of the game where you could see sky trough a glitch in the wall. I also had whole sections of a level disappear. The story is okay. it has a strong opening that is very plausible, but the late game dialogue and the ending are trash. The ending pops up out of nowhere and the final dialogue is disjointed and feels like a pre-teen wrote it. I can understand if the game was trying to be campy, but I don't get that vibe from the game. This was a game that could of been a lot better if the developer paid a little more attention to the story. The ending  is too contrived and in the end makes no sense at all. If they were going for a Lovecraftian feel to the game they started out strong with the realism then the supernatural and finished extremely weak.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Its well done but is a short game. _childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The story is cleverly done with lots of optional secrets you can find which give you a different perspective about what might be happening. The visuals are definitely the strongest part of the game with the story and voice acting following. If you're looking for a good story based game then give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review:
Thomas Winston, Professor of Ancient History and recently fired host of the popular TV show "Finding Britain," has been in hiding for weeks.

Publicly embarrassed by the revelation that his latest book was largely based on fraudulent evidence, he decides to accept an invitation from maverick film director, Maz Kayfer, to act as a consultant on his new film: "Old Gods Rising."

Ashgate University, where the filming will take place, seems to be an ideal location, but when Tom arrives, things get very strange, very quickly. Has he become the unwitting star of Kayfer's latest film? Or, has he stumbled into something far more sinister?

Old Gods Rising is a first-person adventure mystery that puts you in the role of disgraced History Professor, Thomas Winston, as you explore Ashgate University and try to uncover the truth behind the strange events that seem to be unfolding.

Are the Old Gods rising? It's up to you to decide.
_childDocuments_.name: Old Gods Rising

name: Figment 2: Creed Valley
detailed_description: Piano bridges, dancing plants and musical showdowns, ready to dive into The Mind? Figment 2: Creed Valley is an action-adventure game set in the human mind. Nightmares are spreading chaos and have overrun once-peaceful lands. Join Dusty, The Mind’s courage, as you make your way through puzzles, musical boss fights and unique environments. Face your fears head-on. Nightmares have shattered the Moral Compass, making The Mind unable to function properly. Dusty and his ever-optimistic sidekick, Piper, must travel to Creed Valley, where The Mind’s ideals are formed to restore peace. A journey filled with musical showdowns and mind-bending puzzles awaits. Nightmares have their own theme songs, shining light on why they have appeared. Dodge and weave as they taunt you. Chat with The Mind's ever-changing opinions and tune in to the world's rhythm. Explore The Mind’s two fundamental states: Open-minded and Closed-minded. Switch between states and adapt to the shifting environment to move forward. Prove your mental and physical strength through mind-bending puzzles and fights timed to the soundtrack. We should never have to face our fears alone. Piper is now a controllable character for local co-op. Controller required. Joy, sadness and everything in between. Figment 2: Creed Valley draws from emotional experiences that affect us all. Face stress, anxiety and the fear of the dark in a musical and surreal universe. Grab your sword and restore the light that once was. Figment 2: Creed Valley is the standalone sequel to Figment.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played Figment 1 prior to this. The faults are still fresh on my mind. They were: -Stiff controls & fight mechanics with no depth -Problems with animation on high FPS -BacktrackingPretty much all those problems got taken care of. The controls are far more responsive and feel better. It’s still not deep and is mostly swinging your sword and dodging. The charge attack is gone but you get one small combo in return. You also don’t level up by collecting grey orbs anymore (the XP in Figment 1). This means your health won’t increase. Instead of making the battle system deeper, the dev went with making the fights more challenging and needing to figure out enemy patterns or how to deal with multiple enemies. You also have less health scattered around or you need them more at least. This makes the fights more engaging even though they’re still simple. So thumbs up! Piper had weird animation on high FPS and there were still some weird instances on 60fps. It’s pretty much a none issue with 2. Maybe there are some very minor rare instances but you have to look really hard to spot them. I was very happy playing on 165fps. As for backtracking, instead of having to go through multiple areas to reach your destination, there’s now a list you can select where you want to go. That’s just perfect.So are there some flaws? Yes, one real flaw and the second one depends on whether you like this big change or not. Figment 2 is quite buggy. Nothing really game breaking but it does affect immersion when the game is so magical and you want to get lost in its world. I have 3 distinct ones. Sometimes the green health orb doesn’t heal your last health but it follows you around instead. This fixes itself after loading a new area. Second one is reaching one place where if you walk too soon while a dialogue is going, the camera doesn’t move where you’re supposed to go, blocking you from progressing. You can reload the last checkpoint (which is seconds away), be a bit more patient and done! Third one is weird. I loaded my save the next day and the characters were suddenly talking and you keep running until you can’t anymore. For this you need to delete the save of that level and start that level from the beginning. It’s not a long one, so it’s not as bad as it sounds. There are some other minor visual bugs and that’s about it. I hope they’ll get fixed to give an amazing first experience but you don’t need to wait for a fix to play the game. It’s just for extra polish and immersion. I’ll update this if a patch releases.So the big change, I’m talking about the game’s focus. Figment 1 was far more about puzzles and less about fights. This has been reversed with 2. There are still some puzzles, but they’re easier and they don’t keep you long in one area. However, the ethics maze level is very focused on puzzles. So it’s an outlier for the fans of 1. Collecting the remembranes also required some creativity before, kind of like mini puzzles to get them. Now you just need a sharp eye to spot them.There is also one big improvement. The cutscenes are better compared to 1. The remembranes now also have voice acting and you can view them whenever you feel like it from the menu instead of backtracking to one town.In terms of length, it’s a bit complicated. The game is shorter but there is no backtracking that extended the play time like with 1. Figment 1 took me 8 hours to do everything except for a few silly achievements. Figment 2 took me less than 5 hours and I came back to 100% the rest in 6.5 hours. Well kind of, I missed some remembranes in one area even after my proper second run. I’m planning on doing this a third time but that’s on me. If you’re very skilled with spotting things, then you might get everything done the first time. The achievements are also easier to get and some are just plain cute. I’m only missing the last one which is collecting everything. I prefer spending less hours on a game instead of backtracking and given the illusion the game is longer. So I’m happy with this. I did get the game on sale though. At €15 or less, I’d say the game is definitely worth it. At €25, it might be a hard sell with the amount of hours you get. But if you’re rich and don’t care, then just get it.Figment 2 is special. You can tell it’s made with care and love. The devs truly gave it their all. It’s evident that it looks dreamy and sounds fantastic. Whether it’s the songs or the distinct voice acting. The areas are also more varied in terms of assets compared to 1. While 1 might be ‘longer’, it also re-used its assets more often. There is also some unexpected variety with the gameplay. I’m not going to spoil too much on that. The game is definitely worth experiencing. If the bugs get patched, then almost nothing stands in its way!I really enjoyed my time with Figment 1. It made me love the world that it created but there were also some frustrating moments near the end. I’m not sure if those moments were frustrating for not being skilled enough or they could have been designed better. You don’t have that with 2. It just puts a smile on my face the entire time. It also continues on building more of that world. I absolutely love Jester, the new character. I hope we’ll get Figment 3 one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2: Creed Valley is an action-adventure title with musical segments and puzzles. It is a stand-alone sequel to the popular original, and although it has a slightly different tune to its predecessor, it is just as entertaining and memorable.Once again, Figment 2’s universe is set within the boundaries of the human psyche. Players control Dusty, a cantankerous character, known as the minds courage. Dusty’s role, alongside his sidekick Piper, is to protect the mind and ensure stability is maintained. Things begin to go awry when nightmares start taking hold of different regions of The Mind and spreading chaos. These nightmares have offset the Moral Compass and The Mind is unable to formulate ideas, leading it astray.  Dusty and Piper must once more restore peace to the troubled mind, brightening the path to clarity and enlightenment.The narrative is similar to the first game, but Figment has managed to create such a wondrous, unique universe that I am glad that the setting and lore has barely changed. Instead, this sequel allowed developers to focus more on character development and smooth out gameplay kinks. The narrative nuances are still heavy, but focuses on more common problems including poor time management and decision-making, work-life balance and more. I enjoyed the snippets of memories into the human’s thought process and despite this altering the tone dramatically, I found this to be a good change. Overall, Figment 2 manages to convey its humorous and light-hearted approach, whilst still showcasing the complexity of the mind. Its heavier undertones are explained metaphorically and through brief memories, allowing the fantastical world to capture players’ focus just enough to ensure the emotional moments are as especially poignant. Figment 2’s action-adventure gameplay compliments the first game and shares many similarities. Dusty traverses areas of The Mind to fix its moral compass to ensure stability and rational thinking. In this sequel, majority of the gameplay is centred on only one nightmare, but it is still spread into many different chapters and areas of The Mind. The main elements of the game are combat and puzzles, with various musical sections being incorporated into boss battles. Fortunately, my biggest complaint with the first Figment is no longer an issue here. Figment had very clunky movement controls, often having issues walking onto floating platforms and becoming stuck in the middle of the ground. Developers seemed to have lessened the amount of these platforms and luckily, movement is now completely smooth and I encountered no issues with traversal. Figment 2 also introduces a co-op mode where Piper can be controlled locally as well, although I did not test this in my playthrough.Combat is very simple and accompanied by Dusty’s enormously large health bar, dying is sure to be a rare occurrence. There are enemies to fight scattered in every chapter, mostly consisting of enemies connected to The Jester (the main nightmare). Dusty still has his trusty sword and can simply mash the attack button, or roll and attack to cause damage. Enemies have their health bars displayed on top of them and Dusty does immense damage to take care of each enemy type fairly quickly. The enemies and their attacks are varied, including canons,  spinning tops or even column-smashing clowns. I found the puzzles to be easier than in the first Figment, but they were just as engaging and interesting. Many of the puzzles are symbolic, encouraging player reflection on what this might mean when the appropriate context is considered. Dusty can also switch between The Mind’s two fundamental states, open-minded and closed-minded. Switching these states will alter the environment, often opening up previously sealed areas and changing attitudes of other Opinions nearby. Traverse areas of moving blocks to get to batteries or levers, face the ethics maze and complete all wisdom trials and more.Despite focusing on the one antagonist, there are still plenty of boss battles to be had. Mostly involving dodging incoming projectiles and waiting for a safe opportunity to attack. These fights are typically combined with musical elements and feature extremely catchy fast-paced tunes.Yet again, Figment 2’s creative art style shines through every chapter. The stunning universe created in the first game is difficult to beat. Figment 2 is still visually beautiful, filled with symbolic detail and colours. I found it to be almost an exact replica of its predecessor and although this is gorgeous, I was looking forward to some more major design changes, but they never came. Perhaps artistically, Figment had already reached its peak in the original.All characters are fully voiced, including the Opinions (characters) scattered around The Mind. Voice-acting is great, with Piper being as high-pitched and child-like as originally. The musical segments are fantastic and sprinkled in well and the lyrics are hilarious (particularly the Rejected Opinion Choir) None encountered Approximately 5 hours for completion. 7 hours for 100% achievements. Player choice.  None, only for achievement hunting and there is a useful chapter select to aid this (unfortunately some dialogue and all cutscenes cannot be skipped).Figment 2: Creed Valley is a wonderful addition to the Figment series. It can be played as a standalone title, but has improved many elements and issues seen in the original. Its eccentric story-telling, enhanced gameplay and quirky, detailed art are what makes Figment 2 so memorable. Its charming characters and vibrant environments provide a fantastic foundation for its metaphorical and trenchant narrative, demonstrating the complexity of the human psyche, and reminding us to follow what matters most in our lives.

_childDocuments_.review: You want to play something with your significant other?Journey through the troubled mind of a husband and father, who only wants the best for his family but might have set his priorities wrong on how to achieve this. You play Dusty, his never hesitating mind’s courage, to clean up the mess inside his brain. Fight large nightmares, open mind blocks, talk with different opinions and free his mind from negative thoughts. Find the Creed Valley and restore the missing cardinal stones (justice, wisdom, integrity, compassion) of the moral compass in the center of the world to restore peace to your mind.You do this by traversing the isometric world together with your bird friend and sidekick Piper, who comments on your actions and prevents you from having to talk to yourself while explaining what is going on in the game. The game is an action-adventure. You have to navigate through the creative levels, remove toxic clouds with light, navigate little puzzles of moving machines, switch levers from open-minded to close-minded, find and use items at the required spots. Then there are fights - destroy venom spitting plants or cannons with your sword, fight large nightmares (bosses) by evading their attacks timed with the music, weakening and killing them in the right moment. The difficulty starts rather low, finding the way after a bit of searching around can be done by everyone but the most unoriented players, defeating the bosses in the first or second try is no big task (as long as you know how to hold a gamepad and recognize simple boss attack patterns). There are healing plants, often even in the areas where combat takes place so you can heal yourself during a fight. Later fights are more difficult, but mostly because you have to fight off more enemies in a locked area. There is no large variety of enemies or their attack patterns, fights do get a bit repetitive. You also can’t do much but whack your foes with your wooden sword, send some projectiles back by hitting them at the right moment, rolling out of danger and evading moving fog clouds.I am normally not a guy who notices the music in a game, but you simply cannot ignore the music in this one. During the bossfights and sometimes during normal gameplay as well some characters sing - which is quite a delight - the music is good and the text is funny. Game works fine with gamepad. A second (local) player can join and fly around with Piper, but this is just for your kid to be occupied because the annoying bird cannot attack or do anything but fly around and collect healing orbs without receiving damage. Polished, not too long and not too hard action-adventure that simply continues the gameplay mechanics of the first part. Also, a really nice game to play in co-op with your younger kid.

_childDocuments_.review: So far just as good as the original- if even a little better. It still maintains a charming storyline, though Dusty is a lot more prepared and ready for his roll given his successes in Figment 1. While it does still feel a little short, with some areas ending far sooner than I would like (so far), I do find that what is here presents a greater variety of gameplay. Musically, and let's be honest that is likely the best element of these games, it is improved too. While some of the songs are mildly less distinct than something like the plague, they are actually better songs. That "discard opinions song" specifically is particularly catchy even if the lyrics mean you likely shouldn't be singing along with it much. Interesting and new to the series is a greater focus on the outside world. While there are still memories which give you insight (though, they seem glitched at the moment); there is also an ongoing storyline about another struggle our character is going through. This is also reflected in the gameplay mechanics which match very well with the ways in which this game is focused. One primary change that surprised and delighted me is that instead of knocking on a house door, hearing a thought and moving on; now there are opinions who live in the houses. They come out and can actually HELP you (or hinder you) during the puzzles.Overall this is a charming new game in what I hope continues to be a series. I can suggest checking it out as it is clearly made with love and passion, and a hell of a musical touch.I have now finished it and I still stand by what I wrote in this review. It is a lovely little game.

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2 is an AMAZING game and even better than the 1st one!Highly underrated and not enough people have tried this one! The "Song of Discarded Opinions" is still freaking genius! My JAW dropped like "No way they did that!"I love how we further explore the depths of the human psyche and internal workings of the mind.In the 1st game we had the 2 sides of the brain, creativity and logical thinking.This time we tackle pros and cons of open-mindedness and closed-mindedness.Courage and Optimism are once again on a journey to help Opinions by retrieving Compassion, Integrity, Justice and Wisdom to fix the Moral Compass.
