_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Pros:+	Memorable music from the very beginning+	A visual masterpiece, delivering brilliant use of colours+	A meaningful story which saw me reflecting on my personal life+	For the achievement hunters out there, Figment 2 is easy enough to obtain a 100% completion rate in a single run🟥 Cons:-	Relatively short, clocking in at just over 3 hours to complete-	The puzzles were too easy for my tastes, however, this is a subjective topic (you may love them)-	While initially fun, the combat became repetitive due to limited enemy times (and limited tactics)Straight away, I was captured by the music. Not only is it one of the main mediums by which the story is delivered, but it also brings with it some outstanding boss battles. Immediately, I was thrown into battle, facing a big ol’ hog with an attitude problem.Rock music blaring, with nothing but a wooden sword in hand, I knew what I had to do. Dodging attacks to the beat of drums, running away to the sound of shredding guitars and a brilliant ballad sung by the swine… This nightmare was less horror, and more of a rock show!Eventually I removed the hogs gloom and put the little piggy into his place. As Piper eloquently put it, “Black hog down”. A cheesy take on ‘Black Hawk Down’, but the line mustered a laugh out of me nonetheless. I was only a few minutes in, but Figment 2 had me engaged, hook, line and sinker!Dusty and Piper are back at it again, protecting the human mind. The moral compass is in pieces, and it’s up to you to fix it! Is the jester behind this mess, or is there a deeper issue at hand? As you fix the compass at the centre of the mind, fragments of the story are unlocked, delivered through beautifully painted scenes which tell the tale of a family in the process of purchasing a house. The message delivered made me take a moment to reflect on life once I completed the game, as I found the story very relatable.The duo compliments each other and prove that opposites really do attract. Dusty is a brave, yet stubborn hero, who’s closed minded nature gets them in more trouble than he cares to admit. Piper is an enthusiastic, yet fearful sidekick, who’s timid nature holds her back from reaching her full potential. Listening to them converse (argue) reminds me of an old married couple, in particular, a conversation regarding if it’s better to be open or closed minded.Ethics, opinions, rational thought, all these traits and more are explored in Figment 2!As mentioned earlier, the story is delivered via beautiful hand painted scenes. The visible brushstrokes ooze a charm which many other titles lack, while the colours express the mood of each scene perfectly. Figment 2 looks like a storybook, and I loved every bit of it!Playing the game, my joy was only furthered as I explored the world. Backgrounds are animated, objects in the foreground are animated, footsteps are visible, and a variety of special effects are on display. Even the animations were fluid, honestly, no area of the game was lacking in the visual department.Figment 2 is easy, both to complete and to 100% (for all you achievement hunters out there). Dodge and swing your way to victory against the handful of creatures trying to stop you in your quest to fix the mind. While the hack and slash gameplay starts off satisfying, it quickly becomes a slog.A small variety of creatures to battle against and simple mechanics saw me rushing through combat wherever I could. A few whacks to their robotic heads was more than enough to defeat most challenges I encountered. The words tiresome and tedious come to mind when I look back at most of the battles in the game, especially those in smaller areas (which is common).Boss battles on the other hand are outstanding and cannot be faulted. The visuals are on point, in all their vibrant glory, with a banging soundtrack to match. They were quite the spectacle. I felt like I had a front row seat at the theatres.In the case of puzzles, a majority involved inserting coloured light bulbs into their correct socket - Simple, really. Outside of this, other puzzles involved flipping switches, or matching pairs. While none saw me ripping my hair out from frustration, none offered more than surface level difficulty. Unfortunately, I was left wanting more.Figment 2 is a brilliant example of a video game done right. My eyes, ears, and mind all engaged with the game right from the get go, which is no easy feat for any medium. I may have faulted the combat and puzzles, however it may be the case that Figment 2 targets younger audiences, in which case they fit the scope of the game perfectly. Do yourself a favour and give it a try, you won’t regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Figment 2: Creed Valley is an isometric adventure game where the story takes place inside the mind of a person and concepts like courage and fear are materialized as characters and areas of consciousness are transformed in physical places you can explore. The main character that you control has to explore these places, solve puzzles and defeat the enemies with his sword.The story and characters are well written and you can clearly see the different personality traits of each one, and even the more deranged one makes some good points. The voice acting is excellent just like the soundtrack, which features very made and catchy songs that will stay in your ear, you can check it out .The graphics look very unique, with a vibrant color scheme and a style that resembles hand drawn illustrations with a few quirks visible on how the houses and the characters are represented, similar to a children’s book or cartoon show.The gameplay and its elements like combat and puzzle solving are very easy for experienced players but on the other hand it’s very accessible to younger ones, who will also be able to complete the game easily. Technically the game also has local co-op, but it’s more like Sonic and Tails, and the second player has a secondary role and can only help the main character.  19 Achievements. Around 5 hours Easy, the puzzles and combat encounters are easy to complete.  Easy, a few are missable but you can use the chapter select to replay any chapter. If you pay attention while exploring the levels you will be able to collect all the shards, which is the hardest achievement. Figment 2 is a very enjoyable game with an interesting story, likable characters, magnificent voice acting and an outstanding soundtrack, filled with catchy melodies and great lyrics, but the puzzle and combat are too easy most of the time and won’t be a challenge.   .

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 6th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Inside Out the game. Figment is a series set in a human brain. Players take on the role of Dusty, a character who has to fight his way through the mind. On his trip, he’ll fight the fears of the man whose mind he’s inhabiting as he’s dealing with buying a house or work/life balance. However, the focus is on the innovative ideas at play as the character explores the mind. These can be anything from opening and closing the character’s mind to progress and talk to various creatures, to fighting the embodiment of a fear of the dark. There are a lot of clever concepts in here, and the fact that each boss encounter has a unique song is good.Still, Figment 2 had a nasty habit of taking two steps forward and one back often. The first boss and song were excellent, as was the second. However, the Mayor’s song just felt more annoying and tedious. Many puzzles are good but every once in a while, a puzzle has a lot of backtracking. The experience is mostly good, but mostly, not always. Also, there’s a lack of variety in bosses, and the whole game is only about five hours long. The only actual negative thing I’ll say is the game just tosses you in the middle of the story. Perhaps the game is assuming you played the first title, or maybe this just doesn’t have the best opening but it’s not a huge criticism, you get the idea of what’s going on quickly.Pick this up if you want a novel or interesting world to explore with some clever ideas but are also willing to put up with a weaker package, to get at those moments of inspiration the developers had. I liked this game quite a bit, but I can also say it still didn’t fire on all cylinders like it should have. Also, just a quick mention there is a Disney character named Figment, who was a purple dragon on the ride Journey into the Imagination. I have a pin of him on my shelf.  Last month, it was announced that Journey into Imagination is being replaced by Inside Out.   RIP Figment. Not a big thing about the game, just some interesting coincidences. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2: Creed Valley - A Fun Romp Through the Mind (with a Familiar Feel)!Just wandered out of the wonderful weirdness of Figment 2: Creed Valley! It felt like a delightful reunion with some old friends, with a few new surprises thrown in. Here's the lowdown:What Makes it Shine:•	Welcome Back to the Mindscape! Figment 2 brings back the awesome exploration of the human brain we loved from the first game. This time, we're tackling worries in Creed Valley, and it's a hilarious mix of humor and clever psychology puns.•	Sing Along with Your Subconscious! The music is still top-notch! Catchy boss battle themes and whimsical background tunes set the perfect mood for this quirky adventure.•	Smoother Sailing: Figment 2 feels a bit more polished than the original. The puzzles are more streamlined, and the combat, while still on the simpler side, is a touch more engaging.A Few Familiar Echoes:•	Shades of Figment 1: While Creed Valley is a cool new location, the overall experience felt a bit similar to the first game. Some extra innovation in level design or story might have made it stand out even more.•	Short & Sweet Adventure: Figment 2 is a shorter ride than its predecessor. The price matches the playtime, but some folks might crave a little more time exploring this wacky world.The Final Verdict:Figment 2: Creed Valley is a fun follow-up that captures the spirit of the original. It's a quirky adventure with loveable characters, catchy music, and a lighthearted look at mental health. If you enjoyed Figment 1, you'll definitely have a blast here. For newcomers, starting with the first game might give you a deeper appreciation for the world and characters.So, how was your trip to Creed Valley? Did the new mental landscape tickle your fancy, or did you wish for a bit more exploration time in the brainwaves?

As far as bugs go, I only encountered 1 or 2 minor visual bugs and one that let me skip part of a small platforming section, so the game in my opinion is reasonably polished as far as that goes. As far as everything else...The lack of enemy variety really hurt in my opinion. Even in a short game, there was like.... the alarm o bots, the cannons, the guy that looks like the pringle's mascot, and the spinning tops, so about 5 enemies and 2 unique bosses (both with escape sequences). Almost impossible to die to any of those (unless if you're a novice to games i suppose) and it got monotonous after awhile.I guess I'm in the minority here, but for the most part, the singing didn't do it for me. To be fair, i LOVED the discarded opinions choir, had me cracking up, but that was about it. Glad most others enjoyed it, but to put it kindly, we were a tad disappointed. The puzzles were fine, but while I can't seem to put my finger on it, the first game seemed more... fleshed out? The story didn't land for us either. Granted I didn't get all the memories so there's context I reckon I'm missing, but it felt very lackluster. I get the main boss fight is meant to be untraditional, but in my opinion the jester should've had some "corruption" or a bad manipulator that had to be fought; call me old fashioned, but someone who parties by throwing rockets and explosions around isn't someone I typically get along with - just a cultural thing, I don't like nursing burn wounds. Definitely also feels overpriced, I'd highly recommend waiting for a sale before purchasing. Game was definitely way shorter than expected, figment 1 (also without me 100%ing it) also took double the time of this game. Dusty didn't really seem to move differently or build off of the first game's mechanics (outside of the dodge attack).Bottom line is, if you enjoyed figment 1 you will probably also like this game, but as I saw no critical reviews here that had any real substance or fairness to this, figured I'd add my 2 cents.

_childDocuments_.review: 5h 2/10 1 Yes,  and  No No, there is chapter selection No No No No No No difficulty option NoI was already blown away by , which I played just before this one, but this one is a sequel in almost every way. It can be played without playing the first one, but if you have plans on playing the first one as well, I would highly recommend playing that first, as this second title in the series feels easier to control and has chapter selection and other improvements like that. Figment 2 made me wonder if they came up first with the songs or first with the gameplay, as the gameplay fits so well with the songs! There were moments when I stood still to enjoy a song a little bit more than I would by keeping going. (Especially that song of the discarded thoughts, that was so funny). You play as Dusty and have to fight a nightmare that is running havoc in the brain of the human you live inside of. His support and friend Piper is also joining you at this party. The first title felt like it had more puzzles than combat, here it feels quite 50/50 but with fewer boss fights.  I had so much fun playing through Figment 2. It was just wonderful and I enjoyed it so much more than the first one, which I did enjoy already so much. Bedtime Digital Games did such a great job in both games with the songs and voiceovers. What I like so much next to the story of this one is that it has a chapter selection. No worries anymore about missable achievements, as you just can go back to a chapter to still get that missing achievement. None of the achievements are particularly hard, and most of them you'll already get by just playing through the game without looking at a guide. I would try to keep an eye out for those memory stones so you get 100% on those in the levels where they can be found. If you missed something, you can go back with the chapter selection option but you start from the start of that chapter, so avoiding that would decrease the time needed to 100%. However, even with the chapters resetting in chapter selection, I would highly recommend playing the game first without any guide, as it is just so much fun to figure things out yourself. I know some games with awesome music and some games where music is the main focus of the game, but this... this is of another caliber than most of those! The songs are so well done, it is just like you play an interactive musical. It is just a treat to play through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first. Yes, the game is actually good. But it's really disappointing.My main point is that, if this had been Figment 1. It would be good, and even then, Figment 1 lacked quite a bit of things as an independent game. But, that was fine, it was the first one. However, the fact that this is the second game makes it sad. It's better than the the first game is some ways, but worse in others and in the end I find it a bit insulting that a second game in a franchise would be as good as the first one. Generally, all second games are better! Not here, and it's bit embarrassing.Graphics: Figment 1 graphics were somewhat goodish, but certainly nothing to write home about. They were helped a lot by the interesting Art Design. Graphics improved for Figment 2, but it's not always noticeable and yet it's quite noticeable at other moments. So it's a good improvement, although a bit wonky. I'm not too sure how to rate that one. I had to go back to videos of Figment 1 to really appreciate the changes so I wouldn't say this is a striking graphic overhaul either. Still good.I guess one thing good to say is that since the NPCs are outside their houses for the most part this time around, they actually have desings.As such, it's a bit better here, but not much, since the NPCs are all Opinions, so basically all the same. And there are less Nightmares and less common enemies, so not much more character designs in the end.Sound: It's basically the same level than Figment 1. Except that since there is more NPCs this time, there are more voices, so it's better on that part.And there are things that are worse. Notably, there is less songs than in Figment 1! Piper's intermission this time has actually the same melody than Figment's main theme, instead of having an original one like in Figment 1, and there are less Nightmares/Bosses, so less songs for them! This is one of the main selling point of the franchise, it's the second game, and there are LESS NIGHTMARES!!! "New nightmares" promised the trailer! Yeah! Two! Even though there were three in the previous games. I was hoping for I don't know, let's be crazy! 5 nightmares in this game! But no: 2. Which means as much songs as in Figment 1. This should have be called "Figment 1: but differently". Cause I don't see the upgradeThe voices are good, some are greats, LIKE IN FIGMENT 1. A bit more NPCs, so a bit more voices I guess. But LIKE IN FIGMENT 1, the NPCs don't have much dialogue.Gameplay: There are more puzzles, and they're a bit more diverse than in Figment 1 and that's good. But that's it. I'm not even sure that puzzles here are that much diverse, and they're super simple, so they are not very fun.  I even managed to succeed one of the puzzles unwillingly... They barely even pad up time.And while there might be a bit more puzzles, at the opposite of the spectrum we have ... less fights... which are less enjoyable and diverse! Whohooo! Less bosses (2 instead of 3 like in Figment 1). And the two bosses are too spread out as well, you beat the first boss (which was more intended as a tutorial and introduction to the game, I guess) in the first hour of game. And then you meet the second boss in four occasions, which are relatively short. Except the final fight which is quite good. The bosses are good, but they're only 2, LESS THAN FIGMENT 1. And they're presence is completely stretched out. First boss in the first dozen of minutes of the game, second (and last) boss for the rest of the game... And also, less bosses implies less different enemies since the enemies are based on their "leaders".  FIGMENT 1 HAS MORE BOSSES AND MORE ENEMIES THAN FIGMENT 2! With that, I feel ridiculous with my expection of double bosses and double enemies... 100% the game is also much less interesting than for Figment 1. You still have to find Memories as your only sidequest, and it's even less interesting than before.Trailers also promised a revamp fighting mechanic. Nada. Same numbers of move (THREE!), barely different.Fights against common enemies where already very repetitive in Figment 1, but since in Figment 2 there is basically only one boss for the whole game, all enemies are themed after him and as such, it feels even more repetitive.To finish it off, I would like to speak about the main NEW THING of the game. The one that was supposed to be the big PLUS to the gameplay: The Open/Close minded mechanic. It's not bad but it's not much used and it's not even always present. It's feels more like several different puzzles that are not original enough to use a different mechanic. Rather than one big rich mechanic that is used to interact with a lot of little mechanics (like how the portals are used in Portal 2), it's a little, very simple mechanic that triggers a few more other little effect to finish simple tasks and puzzles. Disappointing.Length: I think I did Figment 1 in 7 hours and I did Figment 2 in 6. And I finished Figment 2 fiding all memories without making an effort... This is sad for a second game in a franchise...Story: Finally! Now I can say good things. More NPCs, so more dialogues. Sadly, we don't explore much more of the mind since we essentially stay in Creed Valley, which is repetitive. However, the main story is much more interesting than in Figment 1. And we have an actual story with the "owner" of the mind and his family, so the interaction between what's happening in the mind and what's happening in the life of the owner of the mind makes more sense and is quite richer.The story of what's happening in the mind is more interesting as well, and our two protagonists have more exchanges together and actually change and grow themselves, which is interesting. And there is an interesting twist in the story. Sadly, the twist becomes EXTREMELY previsible from a certain point in the story... It's not right at the beginning of the game, but still... I had guessed the story at like... 25% of my playthrough, which is quite disappointing. And it went pretty much like I expected to from there... And we have Piper's intermission just like in Game 1... So it still follows a substantial amount of the structure of Figment 1's scenario... except that there are less Nightmares, so the scenario actually feels... shorter due to the fact that there are less obstacles, ordeals and plot. The whole game is about just the Jester. And truly, more about finding the stones of the Moral Compass. You don't do much in the end nor do you meet much people or visit much places. It's mainly the same place, Creed Valley, the same enemy, The Jester, and the same NPCs, the Opinions.That's more NPCs, but less places and less Bosses/Opponents/Antagonists. So, the story, if better as it's much more profound and interesting (well it's not incredible eithers) still lacks a lot. It's less substantial because it has less parts, less chapters, so it feels even shorter than it really is. The bosses/nightmares were really important (along the change of scenery) because they gave a big sense of conclusion to each part of the game. Instead, it feels like the game is structured as :Intro/Tutorial: The Black HogChapter 1: The JesterChapter 2?: "What are you speaking about, Player? The game is already finished!" (there is no chapter 2)Conclusion: This is the second volume of the franchise. It should have been substantially better than the first game which was already lacking quite a bit on some department... It is not. This is a good "other" Figment 1. It should have been a good Figment 2...

_childDocuments_.review: and it was a wonderful game to play at a very difficult time.Fast-forward ten months.  Times remain difficult, so some more Figment would be nice.This sequel definitely didn't affect me as positively as the first game did.  Maybe that's because my own mindstate has degraded so heavily since June 2023.  Or, maybe the game's designers just couldn't recapture the magic again.Somehow, Figment 2 feels less charming.  It's more plodding and mechanistic.  That''s not surprising, since depicting the inner-workings of a man's mind and his sense of morality as a system of magical boollshizz psuedo-machines is literally soulless.It was actually kind of draining to play Figment 2.  The chaotic dialogues full of nonsense.  Piper's wonderful characterization in the first game is changed from being loving & supportive to being sassy, know-it-all, and occasionally dismissive or condescending.  The inappropriate elevation of the developers' stock-standard authority-derived opinions over what their players may believe.I assume there will be trilogy of Figment games.  But it might take until the end of the 2020s, judging by the 5+ years gap between the first and second games.  Let us all hope and pray that I will have my own mindstate improved by time I sit down to play Figment 3.  My own mind's versions of Dusty and Piper have their work cut out for them!

_childDocuments_.review: Review after just the tutorial zone, focusing on the thing I was curious about and didn't see mentioned in any other reviews: the two-player couch co-op.Short version: it's not very good.I thought from a brief interaction with it that it might be a good one to play with my wife because she's not generally great at game dexterity, and it does have *that* aspect covered, in that the second player is an invincible sidekick. The problem is there's very little the second player can actually do - they can peck the minor bad-guys for a small amount of damage, and help collect health, which is okay, but 90% of the time neither of those things are needed so the second player has nothing to do and is bored. It seems like this role is targeted at the "4 year old brother" demographic, but even there it would be a failure, partly because of the nothing-meaningful-to-do time, but worse, every time there's a cutscene (even when it's still "in game") both players lose all control over their characters (which is extra frustrating when you're a player who has no control over when this happens, and I think would frustrate the hypothetical four year old into doubting they're controlling anything at all!) This is weird because in the original Figment after knocking on a door, for example, you could move around while they respond, but this time it seems you're stuck waiting for the duration of the response, as is the sidekick.During the boss battle, especially, it's quite a long duration and there is nothing the sidekick can do with any impact at all.Still selecting yes to recommend, because it seems like it's more of the same as the original Figment, but if you were eyeing it specifically as a co-op game, would not recommend. Also it seems *slightly worse* than the original Figment in that it locks you out of controlling anything more - cutscenes in the original were shorter and much of the dialogue played while you were playing rather than freezing.Edit additional after finishing the game: it's also shorter than the first one, with more cutscenes (that aren't as good), more bugs, and less interesting puzzles. It's still a decent game so I'm going to leave the recommend as a yes, and I wouldn't say it's *disappointing* after the first one, but it's not as good as the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like it, I liked the first one. But in here it was mostly frustrating and boring, with a ton of small annoying problems. Which is a shame because it had potential and I can see a lot of people worked hard on it. But after 15 minutes it is much more of a repetitive chore.Pros:+ music is goodCons:- no option to skip cutscenes, even in chapter select after beating the game- chapter select resets all the shards for that level. Meaning that if you miss even one in normal playthrough, you need to replay the whole level again. Annoying especially with the cutscenes being unskippable- the Jester isn't a good antagonist, not really able to carry the whole narrative. there's no real incentive to fight them, the only reason you do it is because the game tells you you should- fighting is boring, enemies are annoying, and there's way too much of it, with waves after waves in some places, without a clear indication of how many waves are left- the puzzles aren't really puzzles. When the clue is "sometimes you need to take one step forward and two steps back" and the solution is literally going one tile forward and two steps back, you can't call this a puzzle- all the levels are basically the same. In the first game it was much more diverse. The perspective switch mechanism is nice, but it basically changes the colour pallette of every level in the same way so it's not really enough- the plot doesn't really exist and feels forced and uninspired

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2 takes a promising premise and squanders it with repetitive gameplay and a shallow experience. The puzzles start out intriguing but quickly devolve into a monotonous loop, failing to provide the kind of challenge you'd expect. Backtracking through the same areas feels like a chore designed to pad out the playtime, which is shockingly brief for the game's price tag.While the concept of musical boss battles is interesting, the execution falls flat. The combat mechanics feel clunky and unresponsive, a particular letdown considering you're playing on PC. The voice acting, especially the singing in these boss fights, is cheesy and undermines the atmosphere. It feels like a port of a Nintendo Switch or console game, failing to leverage the power of a PC.Figment 2's charming world can't salvage the repetitive gameplay and lack of depth. If you're looking for a puzzle game with clever challenges or a rich narrative, this one misses the mark completely. It might hold some appeal for those seeking a lighthearted romp, but the high price tag and underwhelming experience make it a hard sell. You're better off checking out other games that can offer a more fulfilling adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2: Creed Valley by Bedtime Digital Games is a captivating action-adventure game that transports players into a whimsical and musical journey within the human mind. It combines a rich narrative with unique gameplay mechanics, making it a delightful experience for fans of imaginative adventures.Pros:- Stunning Visuals and World Design: The game's art style is vibrant and painterly, creating a visually stunning world. Each area is meticulously designed with imaginative details, such as bridges made from piano keys and singing trees, which enhance the overall immersion​. - Engaging Musical Elements: Music plays a central role in the game, with boss fights often set to dynamic and genre-spanning musical numbers. This not only adds an auditory delight but also integrates seamlessly with the gameplay, making battles more engaging and memorable​​.- Creative Puzzles and Gameplay Variety: Figment 2 offers a variety of puzzles that are both challenging and creatively designed. The incorporation of musical elements into puzzles and the diverse enemy types keep the gameplay fresh and interesting throughout the adventure​​.Cons:- Short Game Length: One of the main criticisms is the game's short length. And with such a lovely world it might leave players wanting more​.- Repetitive Combat: While the combat is smooth, it can become repetitive over time. The game lacks depth in combat mechanics, with limited attack combinations and no significant upgrades, which might make battles feel monotonous after a while.- Lack of Character Progression: There is a noticeable absence of character progression. Dusty, the protagonist, does not visibly grow stronger or gain new abilities as the game progresses, which can make the gameplay feel static and less rewarding​​.Conclusion:Figment 2: Creed Valley is a beautifully crafted game that excels in its artistic design and musical integration. Despite its short length and repetitive combat, the game offers a memorable and emotionally engaging experience. If you're looking for a unique adventure that blends puzzles with a whimsical narrative, this game is worth picking up. I’d give it a "musically magnificent" Rating: I give it 4/5 musical notes.

_childDocuments_.review: Watch Full Review: Story:The story is cleverly told in this game, opting for a more subtle approach than an in-your-face one. You'll get your cutscenes that show bits of the story, but most of it comes from the way the game operates on an open-minded and close-minded state. Through these states you'll see the opinions (rather, the adorable little creatures that are around the world) change their text lines, the puzzles change, and even the main character and his feathery friend will drop some one-liners that have you contemplating their deeper meaning. This game has a fluffy surface with a darker undertone and yes, a few cringey characters. I did find the story overall enjoyable though as it does a great job of portraying itself through the gameplay. The end is climactic enough to support the first parts of the game, and the game does a great job leading up to the end where you don't sit there going "huh?" like some games do. Gameplay:The gameplay isn't particularly hard, more just mentally engaging as you'll have to consider the puzzles from both perspective game states (open-minded/closed-minded) which I honestly found made the puzzles a lot more enjoyable. It was a lot of "do one task in a close-minded state then adjust it back to open-minded in order to proceed", or vice versa. There are enough puzzles, as well as variety in them, to keep you entertained from start to finish. I will say the game is short. We nearly 100% it in just over 3 hours. The levels are replayable but unless you missed something, I'm not sure why you would go back. Audio:The soundtrack is great on this one, absolutely enjoyed that part, but the voice acting is a bit over-enthusiastic and a tiny bit cringy, but it's effective. We actually just turned dialogue down a bit and it definitely helped not having their enthusiasm be so *loud*. The most humorous part of this game is the giant Nightmare Pig singing metal lololCombat:It's pretty easy, not going to lie. It's your normal, dodge all the stuff and wait for your turn to attack, smack them a few times, then repeat, until the boss is finished off. The final boss was a decent challenge, but every interaction prior to that was no challenge. The little mini-fights throughout the world are equally no challenge. We found a lot more enjoyment in the puzzle and story aspects than in any of the fighting. Ultimately, this game isn't really about combat but I feel it could be improved vastly if they explored some more interesting fight sequences... at least for the bosses. Multiplayer: We don't consider this multiplayer. You're a glorified cheerleader who can peck a few enemies in the face and interact with a couple of the puzzles, plus one part you actually take the spotlight on towards the end of the game, but honestly, you don't need a second player at all to get through it with ease so having one just felt like an afterthought. Definitely feels more like a, "parent plays the main character, kid plays the bird to feel like they're doing something", sort of multiplayer. All-in-all:I think it would be great to play with your pre-teen kids honestly. Maybe not young ones due to the theme of the story and some of the freaky characters (giant nightmare pig screaming in heavy metal to die, or giant clown singing dance like an idiot), but definitely pre-teen kids. If our kids were a bit older, I could absolutely see us paying for this game and enjoying it with them, especially because the bird Piper is very kid-like and optimistic so it would be a fun dynamic to experience with your kids. While my partner and I enjoyed talking through the story and points that the game was exploring, I don't know how much I'd recommend it for an adult wanting to experience it. Maybe if you're a big fan of the genre or a puzzle enthusiast, I'd say it's great, but if you're looking for something with a decent bit of content and strong gameplay, this might not be the title for you. It's engaging at parts, and lacking in others so, we encourage you to consider your preferred games and what you look for in them prior to making a purchasing decision.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅The discarded opinion song✅Good music➖Constant controller vibration with no option to turn off➖Some parts go on for way too long➖FPS drops➖Game-breaking bug➖No real improvements over Figment 1You can find my review for Figment 1 here: This review is going to assume you are familiar with Figment 1 (F1), so I’m going to focus on the changes for the sequel. Game World: Figment 2’s (F2) game world is very similar to F1. Both take place inside the same “body” and focus on the same characters with the same gameplay. The big difference here is simply that in F2 you visit new areas with different puzzle mechanics. Narrative: For 75% of F2 is mostly a similar but worse story than F1. The final 25% of the story in F2 is where it really starts to take off and be different. I wish it kept that same creativity throughout. I was getting frustrated with the story at the start, how one-dimensional and backwards the characters have grown since F1, but I was delightfully proven wrong with the final fourth. I would say my favorite part of the story, that isn’t even part of the main plot, has to do with all the creativity around the opinions and discarded opinions. Length: I finished F2 in a little over 4 hours. Mechanics: I was disappointed with the mechanics in F2. While there are some new puzzle types, there feels like much less puzzles overall and instead more padded content. I’ll start and end by saying the combat is almost exactly the same from F1, with the charge slash replaced by the dodge slash. Combat really needs an added element like Bastion has upgrades or multiple weapons. There were some new puzzle elements like the close/open minded swap, but I feel like that wasn’t really a big enough feature versus something like goo in Portal 2. The moral compass pieces just drag on for about 40% of the game alone. The maze part I felt was way too excessive. Overall, I expected more after the somewhat barebones mechanics of the first one. F2 fails to impress here. Difficulty: I would say that the difficulty is around on par with F1, with one caveat - very often healing spheres seem bugged when trying to heal before combat. For some reason I absorbed the healing orbs, but didn’t heal. Made a few parts very testy. Overall, I think I only died maybe once or twice. Quality: F2 looks pretty much the same as F1. No real improvements or changes here. Performance: There were some slight issues I experienced with performance. I was able to keep a constant 240 FPS fully maxed. There were many times when the game slowed to a stutter, sometimes dropping ~150 frames in an instant. I played with my XB360 controller over KBM - no issues other than some wonky binding choices. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: No change from F1. Only standout point seems to be some better/more voice acting. Music: I mentioned that one of the best parts of F1 was the music and boss songs. Unfortunately with F2, there is really only 2 (!) boss fights, so the best part of the first game was cut significantly here. There are some other various songs, but none of them hit as hard as the boss music. Overall, I consider audio a step backwards from F1. Same as F1 - not a great reason to replay this other than for achievements. If the entire game was as good as the ending, then F2 would be a better game than F1. Instead, you’re met with a sequel without any improvements, without addressing many of my cons with F1, and in some cases, adding in new negative aspects. These combined makes it hard to recommend. I would say only pick this up if you absolutely loved F1, because F2 feels like it could pretty much be a DLC for F1 at best. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: Whole 6 years after the release of Figment, the second game delivers more of basically the same experience.Figment 2 is a top down adventure game mixed with slasher combat, you control with WASD, space to dodge, e to use, q to cycle inventory items and lmb to attack. The game feels very similar, but it does have some design choice tweaks, one is the lack of charged attack, instead you have the same charge attack animation as a combo finisher, another big difference is lack of pickable elevator platforms, that most of the puzzles relied on in Figment 1, instead of those, you get world switch totems. where each area has 2 states you can swap between by hitting said totems, you've probably seen a similar system in other puzzle games.Something in the design that is not immediately obvious is the way this game balances puzzles and combat, compared to 1, puzzles are now even easier it felt like, I called them simple in the first game, so this would make them elementary, there is nothing like the sokoban sequences for example, most of it felt like flipping switches in correct order to create a bridgeway to the next area. In turn, the combat was spiced up significantly, in Figment it was extremely barebones, until you reached a puzzle boss, here you actually have light-bullet hell moments, and a lot more enemies on screen at a time, instead of being a waiting game, it was more of an action game requiring a bit of reflexes, another good adition for these small hordes is friendly fire, which works especially well with rocket turret enemies, whose projectiles you can deflect and redirect not only at the turret itself, but other enemies too.Overall, it is a very similar game, with even easier puzzles, way more action oriented combat, but still a surprisingly good flow throughout the experience.Audio and visuals are almost exactly the same quality as before, it has the exact same artstyle and music style, not to say that there aren't improvements - it is technically more impressive, there is more animated background elements, there are actual animated NPCs now besides the mayor, there is even more vocal tracks, more visual effects and a lot more enemies rendered at once. It's not an overwhelming change, but it's probably for the best, as it helps maintain the exact style og had going for it.Lastly the story and characters, it is now a different turmoil for the character whose mind you play in, you could say it's a different trope, this time more tied to work stress etc.. The protagonist, sidekick and mayor are back, but instead of 3 villains, you now have 2, given its presence on the cover art, you might guess who the game revolves around. The memories now also work a bit differently, instead of 25 of them throughout the character's life, you get like 6, which in some ways tie to the main conflict. It's a more focused game for sure, but I felt like it was a bit less varied and dreamlike, compared to Figment 1, also some of the lines in this one have ties to modern western political discourse, nothing malicious, but I did still roll my eyes that a game reminds me of what year it might've been made in.Overall, it's a good time, I prefer Figment 1 personally, but if you wanted more out of that game's combat, then you might prefer this one instead. Since they share so many similarities you really can't go wrong with playing both, as long as you like one of them, a solid sequel in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything the first did, this one does better. The rough edges were almost all polished and that leaves a pleasant experience to play.The combat got a big glow up, feeling less clunky and more strategical along with a bigger prevalence in the adventure. The catchy tunes got developed as well, with longer and varied lyrics. The chapter selection structure was useful.A sad note would be that the level structure was more linear and the bonus objective were in the form of a collectathon instead of the previously side branch puzzles, making finding each one less interesting. In terms of gameplay it was decently varied and tried fun new ideas, and the writing had a lot of witty hidden meanings that were nice to find.The main plot was also a very important message many need to hear.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming whimsical game with a surprising emotional side. I had lots of fun playing. It has a great variety of puzzles, the story is pretty well-written and the music is really (really) good! They did it! They made a game that's also a musical, and it works great!I had really enjoyed the first game, had found it quite inspiring visually and audio-wise, and this 2nd game did an even greater job!The new mecanics are so well thought and fit so well with the game's themes and story/core. Lots of rhymes and puns, and the humour is pretty great too! I was really caught me off-guard.Some say the game is  but in my humble opinion I think it works better/safer that way, otherwise it'd become difficult to keep the story and gameplay engaging without it becoming too repetitive or dragged out.It's perhaps a bit annoying that you can't skip cutscenes/dialogues when replaying a chapter (say, to find missing "memory shards", the in-game form of collectibles).All in all, I definitely recommend the 1st game and this one to any fans of surreal visuals, puzzles, musicals, puns and endearing characters. And if the price is a problem to you, knowing the game is about 5-6hrs long, maybe just add them to your wishlist and get them on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and charming game with a lot of love put into it.Excellent writing and themes, adorable soundtrack and musical numbers.Gameplay is simple but engaging, and the puzzles are creative.The voice acting and sound design is... mixed... sadly... I had to force myself to get used to it before I could start enjoying the excellent writing.The musical numbers are solid tho, mostly delivered by the stronger voice actors anyway.The game wants to be a lot of things and is surprisingly adept at all of them. I know cheap virtual instruments when I hear them but that doesn't mean they don't make the most of what they've got
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2 continues where the last one left us of. You play as the hero "Dusty" who resembles the courage of the mind. He goes on a quest to protect the mind from the evil jester by means of whacking and puzzling  his way through various sections of the mind A fair bit spicier than the last game. Though the collectibles are a lot easier to find.Overall still pretty easy and will add only an hour or two to your play time if done right.-Amazing soundtrack-Charming art style-Good puzzle design-Felt a bit padded with the amount of combat-Enemies are fairly spongy making them rather tedious-Collectibles require replaying the entire level (unlike the first game)I overall loved this game. Whilst I would say the first was better, this one was still great fun and had a lot of very clever dialogue. There is a considerably heavier emphasis on combat, and whilst better in that regard than the first, the sheer amount of fights became a bit tedious toward the end. The game is also quite short (~6hrs) and thus that makes this game feel incredibly short. The puzzles were a nice change from the first and were a lot faster paced in contrast though.Overall I'd say this is a good sequel.Short, but good. Whilst I vouch against the full price as it's quite expensive for the amount of playtime, I recommend buying it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: And once again, I did not regret buying this game!This time around, Dusty is not too rusty anymore, and actually has a new attack that is completely overpowered for something you can just get I-frames and punish the enemy for attacking; but still, the game is not focused on complex combat, it's just there to give a little challenge. In both games, the real deal is the music and the story, and Bedtime did not disappoint!I can't talk too much about the game without spoiling it, but I must say: throughout the entire game I have waited, listened to every dialogue and did every puzzle (which were a bit easier than the last game, except in Ethics Maze), even happened to find myself listening to the Discarded Opinions' song about three times (and enjoying it), but finally, right at the end, the Gem I was waiting for: Dance-Off, Part 2, the song in the Trailer. It's just so good!In conclusion, the game is a worthy sequel to such a great game. I really cannot recommend the game enough!Now, for the achievements:All can be done in a single run if you pay attention to them. 2 about the easy collectibles, a bunch story-related and unskipable, some made just for the curious ones that like interacting and beating everything with a sword, 3 for the keen-minded.

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the first game, it caught me by surprise the overall theme of the story. I truly started playing without knowing what to expect, nor expecting anything from the game. The art style was cute, well defined and simple enough.At first I thought that the game was based on a children book due to the way the story was being told. Cute, simple, and with jokes that probably make a kid laugh. Not to demerit the developers nor the game itself, but certainly the humor of the game was simple enough as to be shown to a kid. Good times overall.Most of the story was told in a simple way. The characters were being described enough and you knew some basic stuff: Dusty was the courage, Piper was a supporting character. All good.It wasn't until the end that the reality check was received: Your mind was in distress because your kid was in the hospital. Basically, you as a kid, had PTSD due to the traumatic experience and Dusty was basically trying to keep you alive. When you first get this (when walking through the map with the car pieces and start noticing the theme) hits you hard. Really hard.When I finished the game, I truly cried a little. Not because the story was a masterpiece. It isn't. But it was told in a very interesting way and the plot twist was unexpected and heartwarming. I loved it. I would 100% recommend the game to other people and ask them to play without investigating the topic of the story, trying to make them feel that plot twist.Now, in Figment 2, I came with a lot more expectations. Since I was playing with the same Dusty, I was expecting to be the same child. "Now what? What could top off the PTSD of an accident and having your dad almost die?"The story is told in the same way. I can certainly notice both the improvements on the game graphics and animations, but also some extra bugs. Rushed game or just not enough manpower to fix them in time? Hard to tell. I can relate, and certainly none issue was a dealbreaker, but certainly these were more visible than in the first game.The story itself is told in an even simpler way, and now the actual plot is being told via memories. I honestly didn't unlock all of them in the first game, and I suppose that most people also didn't, because now in the second game its quite easier to do.The memories are the elements that carry most of the story. The game itself is more casual about the underlying story.Yes, by the end, the game tells you that the Jester is not evil. It tells you that the Jester was actually something like the happiness of our human, and that growing up with responsibilities has buried his home. In the end, you help cleaning his home, which translates in the real world as your human allowing itself to be more happy without worrying too much about responsibilities.The story itself is good, and something I can personally relate to. The biggest hit was learning (through memories, not gameplay) about your human relationship with his wife and the difficulties he was having. Something that resonated with myself, certainly.Overall, I would say that the game is good, but not as good nor deep as the first one. I can't say the proper way the devs should have told the story, but probably relying more in the memories to let the player know what was happening wasn't the best choice. Probably that, after defeating the Jester he tells you his side of the story? Probably that, after defeating the Jester, your human had some kind of mental break that you had to solve by bringing back/freeing the Jester? I'm not sure. But I'm sure that the game, even when being shorter than the first one, feels that it is stretching too much the story of the Jester.As I say, probably defeating him and then, at that moment, learning the actual situation of your human, and having to help the Jester come back to try to save your human from suicide? I know, its a kids game, but... I think it could have been told in a darker and more meaningful way.So, my review? Good game. Interesting. I can recommend it, but definitely can't recommend it to everyone, nor as much as the first one.Maybe the devs can make a Figment 3 when you are old?

_childDocuments_.review: The first figment game walked so this one could run. Holy moly. The first game already had a special place in my heart as a psychology and neuroscience major. _childDocuments_.review: During Steam sales I like to pick up bundles that have a couple of indie titles in them for pretty cheap. (Search for the term "bundle" in the store.) This is how I found Figment 1. Fell in love immediately, and everything I liked about it is done just as well, if not better, in the sequel. The puzzles still aren't hard but they've definitely increased the difficulty a step from F1 and shifted the focus to the combat. F1 felt more geared to "all ages" while F2 has grown up and definitely skews older while still being casual enough for all players. The most important thing for me in this game is that you can tell that people LOVED making it. In a world of games, music, and movies being churned out by big studios, it's a breath of fresh air to find a piece of media that has love baked into it. Like Grandma's cookies. This game has big Grandma cookies energy.//Also if they made a whole game out of musical boss battles I'd buy it in a heartbeat. The final boss fight was insanely fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2 is a delight. A musical action-adventure, where you are the personification of the minds courage on a quest. _childDocuments_.review: Starting to overthink a few things? Well, maybe its time to take a journey into Figment 2 with the help of Dusty and his talkative friend, Piper. You'll need all the help you can get, friend! And off we go, into The Mind once more! o0oGAME-PLAY: 10/10The realm of Figment 2 is just so darn satisfying from its game-play as it handles itself from the perspective above your main character, Dusty. Dusty is your main key to this game and he handles ideal for anybody who has done a hack/slash before. Along with a trusty roll to accompany you, there's a marvelous balance between action, strategy and even some thought puzzles! Along with the action, great level of story and plenty of interactions with different character and aspects of The Mind to keep things fresh and always moving. Figment 2 never lets up, in the best way possible.GRAPHICS : 10/10Given the already impressive unique design of the world of The Mind you play in Figment 1, prepare yourself for even more delight coming into Figment 2. As with the game-play this aspect never lets up! Thus, you'll find the beauty everywhere you go thanks to this game's design of its visuals. From its gorgeous landscapes, oddball/fun design to even the far-off (and wild) scenery. Along with the characters, everything just sings with personality!The wild visuals feel colorful, inviting and there are too many times where you really are stopped by how lavishing some of the levels and creativity went into the game. You won't find Figment 2 lacking anywhere in its graphics (or remarkable art design).CONTROLS : 10/10As simple as the game moves and plays, big respects to how ideal the controls of Figment 2. Dusty moves at a good smooth pace and the element of the roll feels nicely controlled and rewarding when its done right. You won't find any part where the game "fights you." Another feather in the cap for this game!SOUND/MUSIC : 100/10HEY, DID YOU KNOW GAMES CAN'T BE MUSICALS?! There is not enough words I can type or shout to praise this game's music. EVERYWHERE you walk, talk and interact is done with the the element of music, charm and something you'd only see in the highest quality animated features.I really HAD to break the score rating on this part. The slight nods the game gives to its earlier Figment 1 tunes, the magnificent feeling of the characters and music as it goes along with you as you play. It really is a feeling that gets you lost in the wonder that Figment 2 has to offer. By the way, the Voice Actors/Actresses really give it their all. Be prepared. ^-^Lastly , I really believe the composer of this game deserves an actual award for their musical efforts/creativity. And not spoil anything else, but Dance Like An Idiot. <3DIFFICULTY : 10/10While Figment 2 can be considered "Easy," the game has a fantastic mix of hack/slash that might challenge you and some very hefty puzzles to ponder on. I think this game works marvelously for the Teens/Adults, but I think later aspects might really challenge a youth.HOWEVER, thanks to a very forgiving Checkpoint system setup for players. It's good enough mix to keep you engaged and determined at what comes next. Good luck! *winks*STORY : 10/10Sort of like with some "kiddy" games out there, I really have to respect the ideas that are being played with here. Alot of push towards the mental aspects of people and their Moral Compass balancing between two worlds, you might say! <3But the story started off simple enough and as you go along you do feel into this adventure with Dusty. Along with the chatty Piper, the game keeps its story flowing smoothly. All thanks to its characters, world and it refined dialogue. Its fun, charming and never overstays itself to keep you bored not even for a moment.AUDIENCE : KIDS/TEEN/ADULTSVery happy to say this game fits all crowds. Simple good fun humor for the kids to leave with a good chuckle and maybe a lesson or two. Everyone else I think would get a huge delight for playing Figment 2. I really do mean it. ^-^COST : 10/10For the price of a movie ticket, why not just take part in your own game movie instead? For what you get by the end of this game (if you've had the wonderful chance to play Figment 1) and its artwork, music, visual design and the story itself, its all worth it. If your like me, you'll even want to buy the game's soundtrack once you've finished it! ^o^TLDR : 10/10 - If you enjoyed any bit of Figment 1, you really have to pick up this sequel. Its everything and more with music, charm and design that makes it such a gem.Overall Score :10/10 - There is so much more to Figment 2 I didn't mention and you need to find out for yourself! Along with its bountiful world of beautiful ideas, wondrous music to sing you along its adventure and such endearing characters, its a true experience in itself. Perhaps this final score was a bit obvious by this point, but this game truly connects on such a great level. Even if not that, its just a plain romp through The Mind with the courageous Dusty and his chatty Piper. Simple enough! ^o^So hold on, prepare yourself for a journey into a wild and yet familiar place. You might say, it's just another day at the office. *tips hat*

_childDocuments_.review: As a lot of the other reviewers have said, this game is more of a DLC to the first game than a second installment. Combat has been streamlined since the first game but is still pretty clunky; some fights are absolutely frustrating due to an abundance of enemies and new mechanics that make me question if combat actually did improve between games. Missing achievements is much less forgiving than he first game too. Having to re-do entire chapters with no ability to skip cut scenes just to do one missed activity is tedious, and memory fragment progress resets if you start a level and don't finish it, which also sucks. I actually spent more time on this game than the first simply due to how progress would reset when replaying a level. Overall alright, but I honestly liked the first one better.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute joy of a game from beginning to end. I loved the first game and was so keen for this to come out and it did not disappoint. The artwork and music continue as they left off in the first, immediately drawing you in and creating a bright and vivid world to enjoy. The music, which is as you expect full of good humour and energy, made me smile throughout with hints of Tim Minchin to one song in particular (when you find it you'll know!). Aside from looking great the game really made me reflect on myself, my work life balance and the other things the character in the game is going through. Add in to the mix the disconnect at times between Dusty and Piper it really lent itself to underlining what our character is going through. Mental health can be a minefield of a topic to navigate in any medium, let alone a game, but like Psychonauts I think Figment 2 handles things very well, with a dash of humour that if anything enhances their message rather than diluting the seriousness of the  topics we face. My only complaint - I'd have loved more of it! Not a long game, but what they pack in is amazing and I haven't had a game leave me smiling like this for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Similar premise as the 1st game. but there are a lot of core changes:- Illustrated cut scenes that flat-out explains what the mind (you) is going through.- Less challenging / (sometimes) frustrating puzzles.* Less puzzles in general.* Much more combat-oriented gameplay. You can see that in the dodge-attack mechanic.* Lots of fights compared to the 1st game.* Dusty / general graphic is more refined but less variety of "biomes". (probably bc of the open/close mind mechanic)All in all fun game, it's more focused on telling a story and combat and less on challenging puzzles. This game got few highlights/Drawbacks I want to mention.+ The Jester is great character, love his aesthetics and idea behind him.+ The Opinion characters are brilliant addition that enrich the environment and worth to listen to!+ The opinion choir is amazing and funny af.+ No insanely complex / tedious puzzles compared to some puzzles in the 1st game.+ Combat feels fluid.- Cringe ending solution, trust me. (although the final fight was very fun)- The game feels like it doesn't know what it wants to do. It wants fights/action, puzzles, storytelling, everything. It feels less coherent than the 1st game puzzle-oriented gameplay and story to support it.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: A nice puzzle adventure. I didn't care about the story though but it plays great, looks great and more importantly, it is fun to play.It's not that hard. Actually, it's pretty easy which may be a downside to some.Personally i am not a hard core gameplayer anymore and do not want to spend many hours playing a game. Figment 2 lasted a 4 hour. While the first Figment lasted about 5 hours. I didn't pay the full price and got a discount since i allready had Figment, the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: For those who didn't play the first one, Figment 2 is a good game and if you're wanting to try it then take the plunge. The music is good, the graphics are good, the gameplay is good, the story is good. It is on the short side (3-4 hours) so that may be concerning for people not willing to pay full price.For those returning from Fig. 1, 2 should be viewed as basically a DLC. When comparing it to the first game, the story is smaller in scope and more streamlined. There's only  bosses. They removed the remembrance puzzles so now there's no reason to explore. The only way to re-visit a map is basically to play through the level again. This is slightly disappointing because a sequel should expand on what came before it, or at the very least not reduce the scope. But the saving grace is that 2 is discounted for owners of 1 so you can treat it as a standalone dlc but I wouldn't fault you if that was still too rich for your blood.
_childDocuments_.name: Figment 2: Creed Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Wake-up Dusty!!!Gah, I have no words for the Figment games really. In short: The first Figment was already amazing, and Creed Valley just follows in the same footsteps. Fun puzzles (not too hard), awesome bossfights, great puns and the songs brought a tear to my eye. THIS is how you tell a story, folks!I play a lot of puzzle games, or games with boss battle, so I'm used to quite a lot of that, but it was refreshing that the puzzles and fights in Creed Valley weren't so tough that you would get stuck, but they weren't so easy either so clearing an area still felt like a fun accomplishment. It allowed the game to have a nice chill flow, that's more about the story and experience, in my book.Figment 3: Greed Rally next year, anyone!?

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style and the music in this game. The story is great; better than the one in the original game, in my opinion. Overall I enjoyed the game and would recommend it. It's certainly a work of art; the choir song in particular is pure gold.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game! The music is consistently good (and adds a rhythm game element to pretty much every combat), the combat is smoother and frankly more fun, the art matches the first game while adding new details. The heavy Aztec vibe of the new area is a little weird, though, and doesn't mesh with the first game all that much. Mechanically, much of the game is on a level with the endgame of Figment. It's a bit of an odd choice given how the story seems  kid-oriented? The vocals are much better - I'll miss the accents, but given the increased amount of voice work, it works out.Speaking of increased voice work, Piper and Dusty have a lot more banter. (Their VAs appear to be the same, so it's not jarring, which is nice.) On one hand, the devs took the opportunity to flesh them out more, which I can appreciate. On the other hand, it's just... not a very long game, and takes place in a more constrained environment than the first one. On top of this, it's impossible to skip a lot of the cutscenes and dialogues (many of which also take control from the player; it makes sense to prevent scene-skipping, but it feels very blatant after being able to run around in convos in Figment). This all adds up to an experience where it feels like every character is talking a lot, constantly. They've added a Closed-vs-Open Mind mechanic, and Dusty and Piper Have Very Opinions on this. It gets real old, real fast - it feels like they have to talk about it virtually every time it comes up. They also decided Piper is a bookworm, which isn't a bad choice, but it feels weird for her to have never mentioned it in the first game and now to bring it up every other sentence. Dusty's rowdy brawn era is emphasized as well, though it's not quite out of place for him.Mechanically, I like how memories work in this game, and they've added a chapter select, which is really nice after trying to comb areas for Remembranes in the first game. I also really like how combat works, even if some of the later bullet-hell combs get a little out of hand. Roll+Attack now does a jump attack, and Spin Attack comes from combos rather than holding (this can sometimes be a problem). There's fewer puzzles, and a lot of them have combat elements to them now, but they're pretty fun still. A few old elements come back, but there's new things too.It's a good game with a catchy soundtrack, decent story, and good voicework. If you liked Figment, you'll probably like this. The base price seems a little much for what a short and short-seeming game it is (I have more hours on it, but the game taking place almost entirely in one area that you can't really leave of your own volition makes it a bit more monotonous).

_childDocuments_.review: Figment 2: Creed Valley is an action-adventure game set in the human mind. Nightmares are spreading chaos and enemies have overrun once-peaceful lands. Join Dusty, the Mind’s courage, as you make your way through puzzles, musical boss fights and unique environments. Face your fears head-on. Nightmares have shattered the Moral Compass, making The Mind unable to function properly. Dusty and his ever-optimistic sidekick, Piper, must travel to Creed Valley, where The Mind’s ideals are formed to restore peace. A journey filled with musical showdowns and mind-bending puzzles awaits.

name: Baldur's Gate 3
detailed_description: Gather your party and return to the Forgotten Realms in a tale of fellowship and betrayal, sacrifice and survival, and the lure of absolute power. Mysterious abilities are awakening inside you, drawn from a mind flayer parasite planted in your brain. Resist, and turn darkness against itself. Or embrace corruption, and become ultimate evil. From the creators of Divinity: Original Sin 2 comes a next-generation RPG, set in the world of Dungeons & Dragons. Choose from 12 classes and 11 races from the D&D Player's Handbook and create your own identity, or play as an Origin hero with a hand-crafted background. Or tangle with your inner corruption as the Dark Urge, a fully customisable Origin hero with its own unique mechanics and story. Whoever you choose to be, adventure, loot, battle and romance your way across the Forgotten Realms and beyond. Gather your party. Take the adventure online as a party of up to four. Abducted, infected, lost. You are turning into a monster, but as the corruption inside you grows, so does your power. That power may help you to survive, but there will be a price to pay, and more than any ability, the bonds of trust that you build within your party could be your greatest strength. Caught in a conflict between devils, deities, and sinister otherworldly forces, you will determine the fate of the Forgotten Realms together. Forged with the new Divinity 4.0 engine, Baldur’s Gate 3 gives you unprecedented freedom to explore, experiment, and interact with a thriving world filled with characters, dangers, and deceit. A grand, cinematic narrative brings you closer to your characters than ever before. From shadow-cursed forests, to the magical caverns of the Underdark, to the sprawling city of Baldur’s Gate itself, your actions define the adventure, but your choices define your legacy. You will be remembered. The Forgotten Realms are a vast, detailed, and diverse world, and there are secrets to be discovered all around you – verticality is a vital part of exploration. Sneak, dip, shove, climb, and jump as you journey from the depths of the Underdark to the glittering rooftops of Baldur’s Gate. Every choice you make drives your story forward, each decision leaving your mark on the world. Define your legacy, nurture relationships and create enemies, and solve problems your way. No two playthroughs will ever be the same. allows you to combine your forces in combat and simultaneously attack enemies, or split your party to each follow your own quests and agendas. Concoct the perfect plan together… or introduce an element of chaos when your friends least expect it. Relationships are complicated. Especially when you’ve got a parasite in your brain. 7 unique Origin heroes offer a hand-crafted experience, each with their own unique traits, agenda, and outlook on the world. Their stories intersect with the overarching narrative, and your choices will determine whether those stories end in redemption, salvation, domination, or one of many other outcomes. Play as an Origin and enjoy their stories, or recruit them to fight alongside you. based on the D&D 5e ruleset. Team-based initiative, advantage and disadvantage, and roll modifiers join an advanced AI, expanded environmental interactions, and a new fluidity in combat that rewards strategy and foresight. Three difficulty settings allow you to customise the challenge of combat. Enable weighted dice to help sway the battle, or play on Tactician mode for a hardcore experience. featuring 31 subraces on top of the 11 races (Human, Githyanki, Half-Orc, Dwarf, Elf, Drow, Tiefling, Halfling, Half Elf, Gnome, Dragonborn), with 46 subclasses branching out of the 12 classes. Over 600 spells and actions offer near-limitless freedom of interactivity in a hand-crafted world where exploration is rewarded, and player agency defines the journey. Our unique Character Creator features unprecedented depth of character, with reactivity that ensures whomever you are, you will leave a unique legacy behind you, all the way up to Level 12. Over 174 hours of cinematics ensure that no matter the choices you make, the cinematic experience follows your journey – every playthrough, a new cinematic journey. With the looming threat of war heading to Baldur’s Gate, and a mind flayer invasion on the horizon, friendships – though not necessary – are bound to be forged on your journey. What becomes of them is up to you, as you enter real, vibrant relationships with those you meet along the way. Each companion has their own moral compass and will react to the choices you make throughout your journey. At what cost will you stick to your ideals? Will you allow love to shape your actions? The relationships made on the road to Baldur’s Gate act as moments of respite at camp as much as they add weight to the many decisions you make on your adventure. so that when you hit ‘go live’, your stream isn’t interrupted by a bear, swear, or lack of underwear. Baldur’s Gate 3 has 3 different levels of streamer-friendly customisation. You can disable nudity and explicit content separately (or together), and you can enable Twitch integration to interact directly with your audience, just as we do at our Panel From Hell showcases! You’ll be able to stream Baldur’s Gate 3 without any problems, regardless of how you play, thanks to these options.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rolling 1d20s with Shadowheart's 1d4 guidance in my dream. 10/10This game is just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. _childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Divinity Original Sin and its sequel, I have acquired a love-hate relationship with Larian studios. When I heard that they would be taking Baldur's Gate 3, I had mixed feelings. There are a lot of positives about their projects, but there is an unfortunate amount of jank built into their fundamental design and the story-telling of their previous projects was rather unimaginative.Though there is some jank in BG3, the game's use of 5e D&D has clearly helped the studio to avoid some of the more persistent issues that beset Divinity. With a wealth of lore and a full setting to draw on, the game has tightened its narrative elements considerably. Sure, there's still some mechanical jank but hopefully these issues will be mostly ironed out by the time of full release and, I'm happy to report, this jank is considerably less impactful on my experience than it was in their previous titles.Even though it is still in early access, there is plenty of content to explore, and quite a few character options to play around with. I do, however, await the introduction of certain character options with baited breath (in particular the addition of the three (I believe it's just three) classes yet to feature, these being the bard, paladin, and monk, as well as several subclass options (having pact of the chain as the only available subclass for warlocks was a let down!)). I'm having a good time playing around with the options and look forward to the final product!
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap. This game exceed my expectations. Yes, there are still some kinks, but the active development seems to be an unstoppable force. Everything you see online isn't even overly-hyping the game, it genuinely is everything everyone is saying.I've seen a lot of companies saying "don't set this as the bar". This was the bar before loot boxes and paid cosmetics. It's a welcome sight having that bar back to such an extraordinary quality. Well done Larian Studios!The DLC content is well worth it btw, the art book is a game developer's wet dream, and the character sheets are so well designed. And having Div2 inspired items is such a great addition.______________________________________________________________________PRE-RELEASESuper glitchyConstantly stuck in cutscenes and dialogAnimations constantly breakCouldn't save, went back to character creation when having to restart the gameDon't buy this until full release.Suggestion for devs: add an option to invert mouse camera movement to swap left and right around.Edit: Changed my recommendation to 'yes'.The latest update fixed all the game-breaking problems we were having. The only problem is visual glitches. I still can't suggest you buy this till full release as it is very likely that your character and save will be deleted. There is also the fact that not everything has been implemented, like the bigger features of character creation.So far...Character Creation: 6/10 - needs to be finished and needs more voice optionsGraphics: 5/10 - so many visual bugsStory: 7/10 - This is purely because we haven't been following the story as we are just messing around since our characters will probably be deleted. What we do know of the story is quite interesting though.Controls: 7/10 - The camera breaks sometimes, hard to explain. I also still wish I could invert the left to right movement when moving the camera.Not sure if this is a bug or whatever but we seem to have lost Us. We got him on the ship but since landing on the island, we never saw it again. Are we meant to still have it as an available companion?

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I'm not going to deny that I'm a huge sl*t for a certain pale elf, but that's definitely not the only reason to play this game. I have not been able to do anything irl since I started playing and I can honestly say it's one of the best games I have ever encountered. 100/10, would recommend devoting your life to this for several hundred hours. (Displayed play time is inaccurate btw lol)
