_childDocuments_.review: I personally loved Larian's work with D:OS2 so I thought this game was worth the shot. After a few hours, I can say that its awesome- but it's still a huge work in progress. Lots of weird movements and multiplayer issues. Get this game if:1. You loved Divinity Original Sin 22. Are looking to get into DnD/Are a fan of DnD and DnD-style gamesI'm really looking forward to what Larian produces over the next year in the form of content updates, bugfixes and QoL changes :)
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: After immersing myself in the captivating world of Baldur's Gate 3 for over 5 hours, I can confidently recommend this game to any RPG enthusiast. Larian Studios has undoubtedly crafted a landmark event in the gaming industry, setting new standards for what a true and classic RPG can be.The game stays true to the essence of role-playing, where your decisions, choices, and actions truly shape the story, making numerical values merely tools to convey your role in the narrative. Visually stunning with beautifully staged cutscenes and deep role-playing mechanics, Baldur's Gate 3 offers a rich and immersive experience that draws you into its world.However, it's not all smooth sailing in this epic RPG adventure, as the game suffers from some technical problems, including sudden crashes, which can disrupt the flow of gameplay and cause frustration. Nonetheless, I remain hopeful that the developers will swiftly address and fix these issues, as the game's potential to become a true classic in the RPG genre is undeniable.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Very loyal to the D&D experience. Multiplayer is finicky but well done overall. The decisions you make really do matter on a personal level, even if you're doing the same quests and exploring the same maps. I've already played over 35 hours in the past week. I may have a problem. :DEDIT: Read it wrong - I've played 48 hours......EDIT: 475 hours in. My friends haven't seen me in weeks. My children have forgotten what I look like. My desk is a jungle of Monster cans and Cheetos dust. Do not send help.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: The game improved much more thanks to the Early Access. Felt scummy at the time charging full price for EA, but i think Larian nailed it. So i give them a pass.Overall, experience is wildly different playing solo and multiplayer. Multiplayer feels off at times with dialogue bugs, animations and cutscenes. Solo though, it is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the game and completed every companion quest. And oh boy was it a ride. 10/10 time to do it again.My only negative point is, that i wish there were more merchants with actual good stuff. Most buyable items are not as good as the loot you find while adventuring, so all that gold felt kinda useless in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is what you get when you have a group of passionate experts and let them do their job freely: A jewel. (Yes, I'm looking at you Homeworld3 and Kerbal2)The amount of dedication and attention to detail in this title is simply overwhelming. Every NPC has a line to say, some of them even have complete dialogs, even when they aren't relevant to the story. I can figure a lot of DMs working on the different stories giving them life and some kind of purpose. The graphics in this kind of games are not very relevant, but I must say that the scenery is beautiful and very well done.The soundtrack is a thing from another level. Whenever I play role-playing games on my PC, I usually put music in the background, and I mute the game's music volume. Well, not with this jewel. The soundtrack is superb with special tracks for some boss battles. And last but not least, the playability is very intuitive. You need to think your tactics and sometimes you REALLY need to use your potions and scrolls. Remember those days when you never had to drink a potion of fire resistance because without it, you can easily win? Ok, those days are over. You'll need them. Use them wisely.This game is a jewel created with passion and dedication. You may not agree with the devs with some of the decisions they made, but you can also say that those decisions were made consciously.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very good: areas were beautiful, story was interesting, and the soundtrack is great. There are some bugs at the time of writing that got me annoyed, like certain weapons not having their unique weapon actions that I wanted to use, along with certain armor effects just not working or getting disabled if you load the game. Besides that and some performance issues, I never really experienced anything game breaking. Back in early access my game crashed an innumerable amount of times when playing multiplayer. I have not played much of multiplayer so I cannot say if those issues have been fixed or not. The class variety is significant, just like in actual DnD, allowing u to multiclass and grab feats to use weapons that class would not normally use. There is even an achievement for multiclassing into every class in one playthrough, which is pretty funny since you have to pretty much screw up your entire first two acts of the game just for it. Overall, the game is great, and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys RPG's, DnD, or games with moral choices and consequences, since this game has many.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 has exceeded all my expectations and more. From its stunning visuals to its deep and immersive storytelling, this game truly transports you to Faerûn. The character customization options are not bad, and the choices you make have a real impact on the unfolding narrative. Whether you're a fan of classic RPGs or a newcomer to the genre, Baldur's Gate 3 is an absolute must-play.I won't give a thumbs up for a technical bug-fest though. Maybe after they've fixed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this game deserves all the high praise. Every main characters are likable, the gameplay is complex in many ways to deal with the problem or an enemy, many dialog options with different consequences, and the story is surprisingly engaging. It is sad we will not see a DLC, but at least the future mods will spice this game up a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Baldur's Gate 3

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Divinity Original Sin 2 you'll like this. If you didn't like that game because it was a bit silly complicated well they've streamlined it so you'll probably like this. If you like the D&D setting you may like this. Be aware that although they added A LOT of mechanics and tried to be as true to the rules as possible there are some effects that are not 100% translated into the game. Which makes sense, some things won't work well when put from the table into a video game. Also I get to make a dwarf daddy who's into other dwarf daddies. What's not to love?Unless it's Temple of Elemental Evil. That game was the closest we will ever get to rules as written from table to video game.

DO NOT Freaking hesitate, take it, love it, and do it again! This is a masterpiece, a game made by RPG lovers, for RPG lovers!STOP READING THIS, SCROLL UP, BUY IT, and FxCKING PLAY IT DUDE!

_childDocuments_.review: The first part of this review will be  for most of the negative reviews that seem to never have played an rpg before.The game is pretty much an alpha. To all who complain that it " Looks too much like Divinity"It doesn't. It's literally going for the real rules of Dnd5e as much as it can while streamlining it.I have played most Divinity games. I play Dungeons and Dragons.This has a large amount of things  done differently than Divinity.What, because there are terrain interactions "ITS DIVINITY!!!!" No. And there are *less* terrain interactions than I remember from Divinity OS2.Because The line you have when you use a ranged weapon "ITS DIVINITY!!!!" No. You want a weird  Squiggly line to show you where you're shooting?No. It is not.To the ones saying the story is bad and characters have no real reason to join you:Having a brainworm in your head isn't enough to join forces to find a healer quicker? You would just go " Lol no I want to struggle alone byyyye."?And once again for Dnd, what is most of DM's starting point? "You start in a tavern with your companions." You think that's better, maybe?The battle is better than the very, very, outdated Baldur's gate 1 and 2 games. From what I remember, It was ten pixels hitting other pixels, with barely any other interaction in the game, *even though it was real-time with pause.*Here, It is  closer to what DND is, a turn-by-turn game, but still with people acting at the same time if they have initative- so you still do have to act quickly if an enemy has the same initiative as you do.The story is great, poking at various things from DnD Lore. And This is barely the beginning of it.The bugs, the glitches, the corrupted saves?It's an alpha, and knowing Larian, They will fix all of that for sure. _childDocuments_.review: If there existed a “correct” way of making a roleplaying game, Baldur’s Gate III is probably it. It tells a remarkable story, featuring characters of depth in a world replete with fantasy tropes that avoid presenting as hackneyed and stale—despite the continued fan proliferation of the world in which it’s set. The combat system is robust; choices made before and after spilling blood are always compelling and occasionally moving. Indeed, the extent to which things are made possible and open to experimentation is what sets Baldur’s Gate III apart from, not nearly, but all of its contemporaries. If player immersion is found in freedom, then based on its roleplaying scope alone, Baldur’s Gate III is one of the best games ever made. Baldur’s Gate III uses Dungeons and Dragons’ 5th edition ruleset. As such, the game comes stock with (mostly) set character progression for all classes. It’s important to note that this limitation is necessary, as Baldur’s Gate remains a Dungeons and Dragons intellectual property. However, character progression still provides you agency over selecting the new skills you want to learn, the feats you’d like to choose, and how you allocate acquired ability points for characters. Even then, nothing is entirely set in stone, as you can re-spec or multiclass as you desire. Maybe you want to be a bard? Maybe a bard who’s also a ranger? Maybe even a bard who’s also a ranger who becomes a barbarian? And so on. The multiclassing choices are only limited by the amount of levels you can gain—this number currently rests at 12. And there are also 12 character classes…do with that what you will. Like developer Larian’s Divinity: Original Sin series, Baldur’s Gate III uses turn-based combat. This is a departure from the original games, but as it is Larian’s expertise, it is welcomed. Order of combat is usually secured by a character’s initiative rating. Assuming you start combat to begin with (stealthier folks may sneak attack a room to death without entering turn-based mode), you’ll choose spells via a radial menu that’s replenished every time the character fully rests at camp. And you’ll want to rest often because many of the story’s characters are developed at the campsite. Battles progress like you would expect, with each class bringing something useful for winning—some support, some attack, and some throw spells. Balancing your party to account for all scenarios possible is recommended, especially on harder difficulties (three difficulty options), as combat can be punishing. Particularly in a battle’s opening, you can get swarmed quickly.Aside from traditional turn-based combat, the game within the game is really about rolling dice. Without tangentially explaining how Dungeons and Dragons operates, at a base level, game progression hinges on succeeding or failing dice rolls. The die numbers read 1-20; the difficulty of the situation (self-evidently determined [e.g., a bank vault will naturally be harder to break into than a lockbox]) sets the difficulty number. The player must roll a die at or over that number to pass the check; if they roll below the number required, they fail. And it’s not all bank vaults. Dice rolls extend to nearly every playstyle lane—shooting arrows, throwing magic, playing music, intimidating gnomes, seducing half-elfs, and saving companions. The RNG component of this will no doubt frustrate you at times, but some of the finer moments are born from failure. My advice: embrace that failure. The dice can be loaded too. Depending on how you progress your characters, numbers will automatically be added to your die based on your characters’ proficiencies and expertise. As an example, if I need to intimidate a troll, I could get lucky and pass the roll check. Or, if I have added points to my charisma rating, I’ll naturally get a boost to my roll on this check. If I roll 11 and I need 14, but I received +6 based on my skills, I still succeed on the roll despite rolling 11 (17>14). The above makes Baldur’s Gate III a meta-game within the actual game. There is always more going on than can be accounted for. And because of that, there’s no way to play the same way twice without saving thousands of times and reloading. Everything feels new and living.Baldur’s Gate III opens by having you create a character—our first introduction to Larian’s gift of nearly absolute autonomy. Aside from customization of the standard fare (brown hair/blonde, beard/no beard, etc.), you’ll have the option of choosing one of 11 different races owning 31 subraces. Furthermore, the player will also select one of 12 unique character classes that combined contain an additional 46 subclasses, all of which feel viable. You may skip customization and opt to play as any of the seven origin characters that, if not selected, can potentially be recruited later. I have never encountered an RPG that graced me with this many different playstyles.Set 120 years after the events of Baldur’s Gate II, the game functions as something akin to a soft reboot. Lore, locations, and some characters may return, and previous knowledge may enrich your gratification. Still, there is no requirement of having played the series’ progenitors to enjoy the content held within. The story opens with the protagonist attempting to wrest control of a crashing alien ship. Your character, along with future party members, have been taken captive by Mind Flayers—a version of Lovecraftian, eldritch horrors. The ship rips through multiple realms before eventually crashing into the land of Faerûn, where the player escapes. All is not well, however, as the Mind Flayers have infected your brain with a parasite, the removal of which serves the role of the plot’s MacGuffin. And thus, your tale begins.And, oh, what a tale it is...Your introduction to Faerûn is swiftly placed in contrast to most video games. There is very little hand-holding or guidance. That’s simply not Larian’s intent. You’re given the tools to progress, to interact with the world, to try things out, succeed, or fail. As an example, if an encountered wall is too high, stack boxes and climb over it. Or pick the lock at the gate. Or knock the gate down. Or teleport over it. Or simply ignore it altogether. Given the sheer amount of tools at your disposal, it’s hard to account for how one might deal with that wall. Or that chest. Or that boss. Or that…lover. You get what I’m saying here, right?In the past, RPGs’ freedom in progression has typically been measured in the macro. And Baldur’s Gate III cares a lot about that too. But it also cares about how you get over that wall. Baldur’s Gate III is one of the greatest video games of recent years; moreover, it will rank among the truly elite for perhaps decades to come. Even for fans who aren’t typically attracted to the genre, there’s still so much contained within that it’s difficult to imagine there not being  for . The story is immense, the characters are excellent, the progression is satisfying, and the options feel boundless. It’s one of the first games I’ve encountered where I felt that only my imagination was limiting me. And that’s a magnificent feeling.And Baldur’s Gate III is a magnificent game.Note: While players have reported bugs, particularly in Act III, this was not my experience. I suffered only one crash and one levitating helmet.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having an amazing time with Baldur's Gate 3. The turn-based combat is incredibly fun and rewarding, and I love how my choices actually matter and shape the story in meaningful ways. The characters are so varied and likable, and the voice acting is top-notch. It really brings them to life. The graphics are stunning, and the story has me hooked from start to finish. Plus, the way the game reacts to the things I try is just so organic; it makes the world feel alive.That said, I did notice a few things that could be better. Some of the changes to D&D mechanics lead to weird balance issues, and I ran into a few bugs (nothing major, though). The multiplayer-first design can be a pain when playing solo, as I've missed cutscenes or been forced into combat because I couldn't pause. Also, planning character builds is tricky without guides since the game doesn't show high-level perks.Still, despite these hiccups, I can't get enough of this game. It is easily one of the best RPGs I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite series of RPG games is  and , after completing them I of course understood that the story was completed and there was unlikely to be a continuation, but still I hoped and waited... and it's finally happening! Since I have not played other Larian Studios projects, it was very unusual to play.The mechanics of the game, the turn-based combat, everything has changed so much that I simply did not see in Baldur's Gate 3 the game that I loved so much earlier, of course this is not surprising, since the game was made by a completely different studio, with a completely different vision. And 20+ years have passed, so they added a bunch of new features to the game. This is not a continuation of the story, but a completely new story that took place in the same city and its environs more than 100 years after the first two parts of the game., well-developed characters, everything is at the highest level. I especially liked playing as The Dark Urge, it was very unexpected for me (I won’t spoil it :)). Of course, there are bugs, but they are all so insignificant in comparison with the scale of the entire game that I see no reason to find fault with them. Moreover, patches are released regularly.Of course, the feeling that this is not exactly the game that I loved so much 20+ years ago never completely went away, but I was very pleased while playing.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of turn-based combat, stories that deviate vastly from how you experienced them in previous play-throughs, impeccable voice acting, and or theory crafting and party composition then this is going to be a safe bet for you.It is currently in early access and I will update my review upon full release, but even now this game is fun beyond expectations. The graphics are beautiful and the ambient music throughout is entrancing. Larian Studios has done it again. Divinity: Original Sin 2 is probably one of my top 3 games of all time and Baldur's Gate 3 may just get there too.EDIT:Now that the game has been finally released, I can say without a shadow of a doubt that this may be the greatest RPG of all time. While that sounds hyperbolic, I am 100% confident in the statement.Never have I seen such a finely craft world complete with TRUE MEANINGFUL choice-consequence decisions that directly and drastically impact your game all the while never making you feel like you made "the wrong choice". There are no "wrong choices" in this game, just like tabletop D&D (assuming your DM is cool).The combat is thrilling and can absolutely provide a tactical challenge. The characters all have impeccable, world-class voice acting and motion capture; each one showcasing the unrivaled and unparralleled skill and heart of the writers behind them. The storyline seemed farfetched to me at first, being a D&D lore nerd, but holy nine HELLS, did Larian tie it all together in an explosive and incredible way. I was floored. Even the character arcs for your party members are rich, deep, and so enthralling that I caught myself feeling emotional when things started to look dire or when I made a choice that negatively impacted a character that I like.Even if you haven't played D&D, even if you don't love turn-based combat, even if you have no idea what you're in for, I highly encourage you to give Baldur's Gate 3 a try.In a world of modern gaming largely comprised of a micro-transaction laden, greed-driven miasma of disappointment, Larian has delivered a sterling, gleaming example of what video games (and RPGs specifically) can and SHOULD be. THIS IS WORTH EVERY F***ING PENNY

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO AMAZING. The amount of detail and content is breathtaking. I love anything related to fantasy, especially beautifully fleshed out, immersive, lore heavy worlds, like Elder Scrolls. I love how you can really choose your adventure to a T. Be bad, be good, be chaotic, anything. All of your choices matter and customize your playthrough to you specially. I was worried about the combat at first, since I'm not a fan of turn-based top-down stuff, but I quickly learned to love how strategically fun it was, especially turning into an Owlbear and destroying everyone.  Pay attention to everything or you'll miss something and want to restart 40 hours later! That's how expansive and detailed this game is. This game has it all: fun combat, beautiful, fleshed out worlds and environments and communities, an amazing, gripping story that pulls you right in, and of course, a sassy, charismatic, chaotic, devilishly handsome vampire elf boyfriend. I've had this game for less than 2 weeks and have sunk over 70 hours into it, unapologetically.  It's seriously amazing and has quickly climbed up to one of my favorite games EVER. Such a masterpiece, honestly. I can't get enough of it, and when I've finally finished the story, I'm sure I'll restart immediately just to re-experience everything and redo everything I missed (I'm sorry Owlbear cub).If you're thinking of getting it, do yourself a favor and GET IT. And be prepared to give hours of your life to it.

Often cutscenes cause desync in audio with the characters.  Cutscenes wont actually have the characters mouths moving, which is shame because when they work properly they are really well done.  Often textures of the game world will unload and reload during cutscene transitions causing a less than happy graphical experience.  Characters will load in "T" posing sometimes.  Honestly the game is worth it.  Larian did right by the fans and supporters with DOS 2 and I genuinely believe they will again.  Worth the buy even in EA.

_childDocuments_.review: Why are you reading steam reviews about this game ? Buy it, play it, the chances are you're going to love it. The hype and reviews surrounding it are not wrong. I went into this game with no expectations - if anything I was expecting it to be over hyped. Wrong ! Great game. Great production. Excellent all round - gets a little janky the further you get into it ( a few bugs and issues ), but really, you can overlook this. Even if you're not a big fan of this kind of game, you should play it, up there with some of the best production values in a game ever. Plays great either solo or multiplayer, truly, each giving a potentially different game.Only one real flaw with this game is that it ends. It would have been *lovely* to see this game engine opened up to allow people to create their own scenarios and maps, a la Neverwinter Nights. Shame !

_childDocuments_.review: After completing my first run of the game, I have to say this comes with one of my biggest recommendations for a game ever. This is a masterpiece of a game and something that will hopefully set a trend for future RPGs. If there is a will, there is a way with this game. You want to tackle something in your own unique style, then have at it and the game will let you. The choices are almost endless.Gameplay is great, be warned it is turn-based combat for those of you that aren't aware, world traversal however is in real time and you have the option to enter turn-based if you wish (to pick those locks and not be seen!)The story is highly compelling and one of the best I've played, driving you to want to succeed or... dominate and rule... But I won't be putting any more spoilers here.The voice acting is superb, everyone from party character to NPC to animal (yes, you can speak to animals) did an excellent job. Some of the best in the industry. My solo run through took me around 80+hrs and I can't wait to go back in as I know I have missed some side quests here and there! And another awesome feature is that if you have 1 - 3 friends that own the game you can all play together in one of the best co-op games of the year. And even this late after the release the devs are still adding more to the game! If you've been on the fence about this game and are reading this review, I'd highly recommend picking it up. It is well worth the asking price. Get in to BG3 now and you'll never want to leave. This is easily my game of 2023 and I cannot wait to start my next story.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically only ever leave reviews when a game makes a strong impression on me, as a way to support or, on the contrary, show my discontentment towards the product. In this instance, no words of praise would ever do justice to the sheer effort and love that went into creating this masterpiece.Every once in a while, burned out from playing multiplayer competitive games and the like, I tend to forget why I even like games to begin with. Then, I get completely blown away by gems such as this one. Games that leave me changed, a feeling somewhat similar to when you walk out of the theater after having watched a spectacular movie and think you're never gonna be the same person ever again.The last time a game had me feeling that way was when I got into Mass Effect. The thing about Baldur's Gate is, despite being high fantasy, it does such an incredible job at immersing you into the story, at making the whole thing feel alive through a sense of detail that is sometimes astonishing. Nearly every possibility, every alternative choice is accounted for in a way that's felt even accross different acts of the story. The visual atmosphere is breathtaking. Newcomers to DnD will find a great medium to get accustomed to the setting, while long standing fans of the franchise and Baldur's Gate will find plenty of nods to past iterations to enjoy.The characters are fleshed out and interesting to a point where after spending 100 hours with them at your side, saying goodbye as the credits roll by almost feels like leaving long lost friends.To be fully honest, I came very late to the party. That game was a tad outside my comfort zone, turn by turn combat, point and click, sort of not made for 3rd person. And yet despite all those elements I'm not too fond of, it's still managed to lodge itself amongst my favourites just by the sheer strength of its narrative.This game will make you laugh, it'll make you cry, it'll make you panic, it'll make you nostalgic. it'll make you feel every emotion a good story's meant to bring out, something lots of games nowadays tend to lose sight of.I mean if you want a TL;DR, there's a very good reason this game had other publishers quaking in their boots going "Baldu's gate shouldn't be the standard other games should be held to" on twitter lmfao.

_childDocuments_.review: I definetly will replay game with other classess. My first was obviously favorite - barbarian. And I love how fun it is to play that kind of fierce warrior. All kind of class checks are totally hilarious (ripping out the doors from the hinges to reach goal is just the example ;))) )EDIT - After finishing the gameAs a long time fan of Baldur's Gate series I can clearly confirm that Larian Studios succesed at the trial of reviving BG legacy. Third instalment is very good game, having great mechanics, story and characters. I had a lot fun trying diffrent things while combat, but also grow to like side characters. Last couple of years games rarely got me hooked to even bother to finish them. BG3 is diffrent. It brought the magic of old RPG's to the new era.  Companions stories and secrets are really good - and that always was very important part of RPG for me. My favorite is Shadowheart, and this is the one I choose to romance. And the romances are propably the only thing I can complain about. Shadowhearts romance was great, the characters tend to know each other with time and grow a bond. My immersion was broken tho by other character from both genders - who constatly behave like anime harem characters - hinting they want me all the time. Doesnt matter that I didnt flirt with them, and just was nice for them in conversations. In the future it will be nice, if characters will flirt with you - when you flirt with them. It just feels forced as hell when everyone behaves like that. Still this is just one complain, and over all I just ignored that and proceed with creating better bond with Shadowbae. I really, really recommend playing BG3. It's great adventure. I will surely come back to relive it again. You should try too.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 is definitely an achievement for Larian that will likely catapult them to new heights, but for as much as the game tries to tie itself to the legacy of Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II, it doesn't have the spirit of those games. It's its own thing, closer, by all accounts, to Larian's well-regarded Divinity series than to the titans that have spawned numerous spiritual successors over the last 10 years or so in particularIn another world, where those two games weren't foundational to the gamer I am today, I might be able to look at this game with the fresh eyes I know so many others are seeing it with, but that's not the world I'm in. If you're looking specifically for a Baldur's Gate 3 because you loved the tone, writing, and gameplay of the originals, you probably won't find any of those hereIf Larian truly meant to make a worthy successor to Baldur's Gate I and II, they would have done well to properly study what made those games, as well as their many spiritual successors, so great—instead, we have a game that has the surface trappings of Baldur's Gate, but none of its soulIf you don't have the history that I do with the original games, or you're a fan of Larian's other isometric offerings, you might find plenty to love here, and if so, I'd recommend checking out the many other positive reviews, because I do think there's a lot to celebrate here. I'm just not the one to celebrate it

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the Baldur's Gate legacy, and perhaps the greatest CRPG of the past decade or more. No RPG has ever captured the spirit of tabletop gaming quite like Baldur's Gate 3, from the classic "Gold Box" adventures of the 1980s, to the Infinity Engine games of the 1990s and early 2000s. Character creation, story, NPC interactions, and in-game concept is all perfect. Larian takes the solid base of the Divinity games and adds D&D and the Forgotten Realms to make something truly great. Other studios and publishers—especially in the increasingly degenerating "AAA" space—should look to Baldur's Gate 3 to see how games should be properly made. EA's zombie version of Bioware has never produced a game this good, and it's most recent titles—Anthem and Mass Effect: Andromeda—are pale shadows in comparison to what an indie studio, Larian, has achieved. No other game combines choice, content, and mechanics so masterfully.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Story is quite thrilling. You are abducted by mindflyers, which are highly intelligent, mind dominating creatures, scheming to conquer the world. You have been planted with one of their tadpoles into your brain. With fear you can transform into one of the tentacle thralls any moment, you are pushing forward to find answers as soon as possible. Story progresses with feel of urgency and it is full of unexpected twists and important decisions. Through 3 Acts you will visit wilderness, underdark, shadow-cursed lands and revisit the great city of Baldur´s Gate from original game.Gameplay: Surprisingly true to D&D tabletop rules. Almost every aspect is implemented. Most notably there is roll for each skill check with 20-sided dice using your primary stats and proficiencies. This dice become without doubt most recognisable feature of this instalment. This time around your party is restricted to only 4 characters, which I am not fan of. This results in constant changing of your party composition. In original Baldur´s Gate I was using 5 characters most of the time and 6th spot was reserved for guest companion tied to some side quest. I really appreciate I could choose side and go semi-evil path, which i took without hesitation. This is improvement from previous games, where evil options were present, but fairly limited to few minor quests.Character creation: Pretty basic, but sufficient. There is good amount of customisation and races to choose from. There is no rolling for stats, but you simply assign extra points to attributes you will use the most according to your class. When level up, you have really nice look on your characters. Every couple of levels, you can choose special ability or attribute improvement. I find special ability choices with few exceptions quite marginal and I almost always took main attribute improvement. If I compare it to previous rulesets, i think levelling up in Baldur´s Gate 3 is better than Baldur´s Gate 2, but worse than Icewind Dale 2.Graphics: Graphic side is simply amazing. I have made literally thousands of screenshots. Locations are beautifully done with attention to detail. Underground areas are especially immersive. Lights and shadows create spectacular projections. I really appreciate return to isometric view, which is true to original games, but with ability to pan and zoom. What will not please is lack of dynamic weather or day and night cycle. Cutscenes: This is where game shines. It is clearly an area where most money went and it is visible. Hours and hours cutscenes. Certainly, it deserves awards for best story, cinematics, atmosphere, immersion and voice acting. Especially voice acting is mind blowing. Every character is voiced by different actor and voice acting is really there. It is not just soulless reading. Almost every character with few exceptions has its own unique face. Their face mimics and voice syncing are breathtaking. Music: Ranging from OK to good. There is no track overly bad, but no memorable either. Soundtrack does good job overall. I mostly like music and ambience from dungeons, rather than music from outdoor or city. In no stretch it can compare to excellent soundtracks from Baldur´s Gate 1+2 or Icewind Dale 1+2 by Jeremy Soul, which i keep dear in memory to this day.Combat system: Not a fan in the slightest. Combat itself is easily the worst part of the game for me. Main reason is turn-based combat. In original Baldur´s Gate, there is dynamic real time combat with option to pause anytime. Turns were used merely for effect duration and how often you can cast spells or make your next attack. Tactical pause was a such distinctive feature in the series and game feels less authentic without it. Main action and bonus action system is step in right direction. Fact that everyone can jump around during combat across the battlefield is straightforward bad design, your formation means nothing. Combat in this game is few and far between. This is not necessarily bad thing, because you can role play and talk out from most encounters, if that is your preferred game style.Magic system: Nothing to write home about. Feels like placeholder. Spells don´t have enough information on them. You can´t even say if it is area of effect spell, touch or missile. You can´t see duration of effect. I would much rather have spell book from original game, where i could inspect all effects, spell pre-requisitions and detailed description. Option of using higher tier spell slot for lower tier spell is nice, but it makes chaos in spell tabs. I can´t properly see what is naturally tier 3 spell and what is boosted low level spell. I have been using it by selecting tier I spell and then chose which tier i want to use, never other way around.Inventory: Terrible experience with inventory. Loads of junk and garbage. Lot of items you will never need. Mostly uninteresting magic items, which i could barely remember i have in inventory. I think it would be better to have fewer items in the game but more useful. Lack of dedicated potion bags, scroll bags and arrow quivers. Yes, there are plenty of bags and such, but no way to differentiate them one from another. Also, you can´t sell stuff stashed in bags. You need to manually remove them from bag and then sell it. Short and neglected item descriptions. In Baldur´s Gate 1 and 2, Items had their page with detailed monochrome hand drawn picture, history and description. Hundreds of different potions with not enough opportunities to use them. You can´t see duration of a potions and in lot of cases you can´t use multiple potions together, because they nullify previous effect. I was using lot of poison coatings though. UI: Could be much better. You have hundred icons for basic attacks, movements and abilities. Not sure what led developers to implement this MMO style layout. It is hard to organize. When you do reorganize it, each new item will insert new icons into empty slot and makes mess again. There is an option to switch between different tabs though, like main action, bonus action, special ability and such, which i have been actively using.Final Verdict: 8/10. Story and immersion carrying this game sky high, but it is dragged down by bad quality of life features. There is room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: Succeeding a masterpiece like Baldurs Gate 2 (BG2) is a challenging task. Larian has accepted this challenge and delivered an overall decent game. However, it feels more like Divinity Origin Sin 3 with a little bit of Baldurs Gate and DnD flair. If you want a real spiritual successor of BG2 get the excellent "Pathfinder: Kingmaker". In the following I summarize my critique on this game. - Excellent writing. It does not require a lot of words to express much and this game really satisfies in this regard- Solid gameplay. The battles are solid, and there are no annoyances like limited resting or no fast travel.- Nice graphic & nice voices. The game really has a dark and gripping atmosphere.- Detailed and smart Level Design- Challenging and fun encounters. Nearly all fights are challenging, but not unfair and overall doable.- Probably related to EA: many cut sequences have a buggy animation- Jumping: it's a nice game mechanic for D:OS 2 but seems out of place here. Too much jumping.- Level Progressing Menus seem to be a bit empty. In Pathfinder: Kingmaker leveling is much more complex (and fun).- Party is limited to 4. Yeah, would be fun with more!- Many have complained about to much element interaction on grounds. There is no lack of it, but it wasn't that annoying.- There are too few merchants. And nearly all of them get killed by you eventually (I killed around 4 of 6). And they do not even have a good inventory. It needs some rework!- EA: The Price. 60 € is just too much for an EA game. But a BG2 veteran could not resist in this case.- EA: Level Cap. Only 4 Levels is too less :(- EA: Unfinished Quests: Yeah, there is often no indication that you can not complete the quest right now.Overall, it is obvious that this will be a great game. It has not the genius touch you can notice in BG2. It doesn't even feel much like BG. But it is a decent and fun game. I'm looking forward for the release. Act I was quite promising and took me around 35 hours, which were are lot of fun. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This is indeed one of the best RPGs for me in the last seven years. Everything in this game is superb. The graphics and landscapes are beautiful, the music is enchanting, the voice actors are well-chosen, and the memorable companions add depth. There's freedom of choice (although it's somewhat conditional in the finale), and quests can be completed in various ways. Personally, I've always preferred turn-based combat over real-time with pause. And if desired, countless other advantages could be listed. But why bother? Larian has once again proven that they make fantastic RPGs. The game is rightfully recognized as the game of the year.P.S. And it was also very pleasant for me to return to the world of Baldur's Gate and meet the old characters again.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most polished release I've seen in my life, watching other people play and have different progressions makes me believe the replayability is quite high. There are a lot of features you'd only expect from a game on its 2nd expansion, like you can filter/search all characters' inventories and its very functional, wow the technology, imagine that in Diablo 4..Content is massive, I'm still on Act 1 and there seems to be multiple ways to resolve every quest from what I can tell so far.Playing a Bard,  I can totally feel that I am indeed a bard, there's so many unique dialogue options and also you can do stuff like just taking out your lute and start performing and everyone around will gather to applause and even throw a coin or two(while your rogue sneaks around pickpocketing them of course) and also other bards(if any) around will join in with their own instrument.Also you can slip out of many hard situations with the power of fr- i mean deception.Gameplay is basically DOS in a very broad sense but less environmental damage focused(still possible to barrel-explode an entire room with some effort) and D&D rules apply so the especially defense system is very different. It's a slow game with a slow combat so folks assuming this is something like Diablo might be disappointed but at the same time if you're gonna try this genre, might as well start with this one as it's leagues beyond it's predecessors.There's a ton of customization and classes and races thanks to D&D and honestly it's so much that all the D&D stuff can be a little overwhelming and to be fair my biggest critism would be that the game doesn't really convey information about class progression/multiclassing very well, hell I doubt they even attempted honestly it felt like they added multiclassing just for the sake of D&D veterans but you're really gonna be in the dark if you don't use a 3rd party website to check out what benefits you can actually get at each level and plan out a build. Though you can still be perfectly fine if you completely ignore multiclassing on first playthrough I'd say.Playing on a 3440x1440 monitor I didn't need to do anything to adjust UI for once, even though folks are right to complain about the lack of scaling(though you can scale the texts), I'm glad to say this game is very ultrawide friendly unlike some games still being released in 2023.Performance is also quite good so far, had 1 crash on Vulkan and none on DX11 so far. Shouldn't be hard to play with 60 FPS on ultra with many rigs and the graphics are quite good honestly for a game of this genre.I can see why all the other companies are pissed at this release because it's a massive AAA game that had an almost flawless launch and has no microtransaction or battlepass or day 1 DLCs, of course they will be afraid that the customers will start comparing them and see that you can still make money off of developing games without sucking the players dry through dirty practices and mind manipulating techniques. Overall this is an easy recommend for me and without having finished it yet I can already say it's a must play for anyone into RPG genre in general as long as the niche combat system isn't a HUGE turnoff to you.Edit after ending: So the ending was actually a let down, idk why but it looks like the main plot has less variatians that are relevant enough to count than subplots in Act 1 and Act 2. Act 3 is basically a lot of random side content but lacking in terms of main content. I hope they get around changing how the main plot concludes on their enhanced edition/goty edition whatever, it's gonna be bad for the replayability of the game if the mainplot isn't on par with the side quests.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy RPGs and Tactical Combats, old school BioWare or tabletop D&D, then this game absolutely lives up to the hype and I cannot recommend enough. The good outshines the bad so spectacularly, as long as you aren't daunted by a looooong game (100-200hrs), don't hesitate.I went into this game with high expectations, and I was still blown away. I've played a lot of Larian's old games, but skipped DOS2 after losing steam in Divinity Original Sin, simply because games of this type are more difficult to get through as I get older and have less time. But this game flowed so well it was easy to stick with. To say they've upped the ante is not an overstatement. If they keep using this engine to make games in other settings like "Curse of Strahd"  I would pre-order on day one------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The good:The Game faithfully recreates 5th edition D&D, there are some differences  that work great with a digital DM that can keep track of it all (better items w/ complex modifiers, minor rules on things a nice DM might bend anyway, and some power-gamer stuff is allowed that wouldn't be like 2-spells in a turn while hasted and stacking of stat boosts). The game enables a level of power-creep beyond what you find in a typical D&D game, and presents challenges that take that into account. The main issue I've had with 5e: over-simplified choices upon leveling up, works well in a game where you get to level up your entire crew of 8+ characters.The story was riveting, flowed well, the accompanying characters were interesting and contributed greatly to the game. I honestly sat staring at my screen gobsmacked by some of the scenes, there are a lot of twists and escalations in the story that feel well laid out (and not cheap gotcha-twists), and it feels like the characters and advisors are grappling with situations with no perfect solution and sometimes unintended consequences.The combat flows well, it's very tactical, wizards are fun, melee is fun, the terrain often plays a factor in how you approach a fight, fighting in bosses lair employs special rules that require you to overcome the home field advantage they have, and there are a lot of important fights where you have special factors and objectives to accomplish.The game is very long, however there were not many sections that really dragged on, the pacing is fantastic for the scale of it all. The fast travel points are well placed to be convenient never felt like I was trudging back and forth. None of the quests feel pointless or like a chore, they're almost all involved in the story or a well-laid sub-plot. You can easily respec your character and companions with no penalties, which makes it easier to explore all the options.Your choices matter in ways most games ignore, some lead you to bad or problematic outcomes, there are branches and options I had late in the game because of the things I had done earlier, a few characters give advice and plans that don't pan out. It's crazy to think about going back and replaying a 170hr game, but I'm  excited to see the paths I didn't take, because they seem like they'll lead to more than just a few dialog swaps in the finale.The graphics are just plain beautiful, I don't worry too much about them in games anymore, but they clearly put a lot of effort in, and it helps the game immensely.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The bad:There are a few bugs, nowhere near Skyrim levels and nothing game-breaking, but sometimes they're noteworthy or annoying enough that you might want to reload. Performance was pretty good but you can tell the "AI" sometimes struggles making prompt decisions by the end of game, but Larian seems to keep working hard on this. The camera during "split up" battles can be pretty annoying, as the camera jumps between different the areas too much for what's happening. It would be good if you could "look ahead" and plan character choices. This would be a difficult thing to do, I don't blame them for not having it in the game, but it's hard to see where your level-up choices will lead. The game should auto-save a bit more. My auto-saves were sometimes hours apart, and there were a few times I wasted a decent amount of time due to being a save-scummer without a save.

_childDocuments_.review: For background, I've played:- 75 hours in multiplayer with 4 players coop in tactician mode.- 5 hours in single-player tactician mode.Overall, I've enjoyed both multiplayer and single-player modes. Each has its highs and lows. Before diving into a detailed list, BIG SHOUTOUT to developer for delivering different vibes and fun in multiplayer and single-player.    - Lots of fun and laughter with friends (obviously).    - Plenty of exploits in this mode.    - Reap what you sow moments: My friend (Astarion) always steals from other party members, .    - My party enjoys zero-cost resurrections .    - "Should we kill this person for XP?" - when meeting high level character    - Tactician mode feels more rewarding and balanced compared to DOS 2.    - The dialogue seems truncated or forcefully being cut down. I think because all characters are controlled by me and my friends instead of being NPC.    - 'Bug'dur's Gate 3': A ton of bugs in multiplayer, such as can't join the non-private dialogues, unresponsive enemies requiring game reloads, mismatch version issues after patch #4 in the WEEKEND, and the worst part is missing voice acting in the beginning.    - Tactician mode doesn't seem well-adjusted for multiplayer    - Dialogue feels more complete compared to multiplayer where choices matter (party members' approvals and disapprovals).    - Fewer bugs in single-player.    - Tactician mode is significantly more challenging, alot better compared to DOS 2 and BG3 multiplayer mode.    - Flexible companion system,     - (I don’t recall any major issues during my single-player run).- I like the overall story, but it's not in my top 10 for masterpiece storytelling, especially the multiplayer ending. i got the spoiler for single-player ending and it's entirely different (will give a shot later on).- Larian Studios definitely improved on the voice acting from DOS2, a big plus for me since too much text and relaxing music can make me sleepy. However, the voice acting often feels flat and somewhat dull.- Camera angles are tricky to manage, both in default and combat modes.- The long rest and short rest concept is more challenging than unlimited bed rolls.- Me: Playing as Shadowheart. use Guidance in every single conversation.- Me: Playing as Shadowheart. Wondering if Sacred Flame can harm the enemy.It seems the developers focused more on single-player. I recommend playing in single-player mode for those craving story, challenging gameplay, and richer game aspects. However, multiplayer is still worth it for sheer fun and exploiting various game mechanics with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons: - The main story has a very strong and intriguing beginning but it falls flat by the end of it. - The writing of the game is quite sub-par at some points, especially when it comes to the main storyline.- The Emperor was a way less interesting take on illithid infection then the Dream-lover was.- Despite the game being about the dead three, only Myrkul makes an appearance. The other two are barely present. I expected to see more of these guys. - The three main villains are mostly a disappointment, they are barely involved in the bulk of the story. Ketheric was the most well-done of all of them and we kill him at the end of Act 2. - In many regards, the Early Access was a more polished, nuanced and higher quality game then the full version.- The game peaked in Act 1. Act 2 and Act 3 both fall desperately short of the quality of Act 1 both in terms of content and writing quality. - The Cleric class in particular feels like it got shafted hard in terms of roleplay. Not only did the deity options got cut by a lot (in early access you had access to a lot more deities), but deity reactivity is incredibly shallow and mostly meaningless, I also consider this to be a writing issue, so it's another vote for the game having bad writing.- All in all the game needs higher quality writing and a better, more intriguing conclusion.Pro:- The game had such a gripping introduction and the first Act is so incredibly well done and so polished that it's worth playing the entire game just for Act 1. - I absolutely love the combat system in this game. It's the best turn based game I ever played. - The graphics and the music are both fantastic, and the game has an absolutely wonderful ambience.- I'm SO giving you bonus points for the Underdark section of Act 1. The Underdark was superbly done and accomplished beyond anything I've seen before. I kinda wished Act 2 could have taken place there because it is so amazing, you could have totally made that work.- Multiclassing works and it's fun!- Jumping and shoving make approaching combat a lot more fun.- You can solve problems and encounters in various clever ways and the game will not break, in fact it's rewarding to think your way out of situations. - Companions can be respecced completely, and respeccing is easily available from the beginning. All in all I think this is a great game, I would give an 8/10.The -2 points are for the really bad writing quality in some crucial areas. Otherwise it's a perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: A few different qualms I have- First, the game's rules are frustratingly close to RAW DnD 5e, but different enough where I get different-than-expected results in BG3 and it just feels bad. Some of the changes make sense for the purposes of being rules-as-fun for a video game, but the super closeness is making me forget what's a BG3 rule and what's a 5e rule. This goes extra for character creation being restricted to "PHB content".The auto-save feature feels so erratic that it is nearly useless. I've had enough crashes where I need to quicksave before I take any turn.The inventory system needs a lot of work regarding useful ways to sort or sell items across the party.The loading screens of all things spoil key tidbits about companions.However, I do have to give it props for both feeling like a true video game adaptation of DnD and being a wonderful game to look at. The negatives, though, reinforce my distaste for Early Access. I definitely want to revisit when full release is out.Review update since launch- Aside from adding a few different options for character creation, they've reinforced each of my issues with the game. They opened up the action economy, which very much impedes your 4-character party versus many more NPCs. Autosave is worse than useless, it kicks in only before a big fight or RP scene, giving it away. And the spoiled character backstory has now been introduced inside of the character creator while still pretending it's a secret in the game

_childDocuments_.review: “No, there are no in-game purchases in our game. We believe in providing a complete and immersive gaming experience without the need for additional purchases. Enjoy the game to its fullest without any additional costs or micro transactions.”Baldur's Gate 3 is a game that has been living rent free in my head for the past 3 weeks since its release. If you had the choice to spend $80 on a video game (depending on your region), Baldur's gate 3 would be one of the few games that are currently worth your money, time, and attention. The value you would get from purchasing this game can rarely be compared to what you would commonly find in other games out in the market. The game focuses on looting, exploration, and offering multiple ways for players to approach a situation while rewarding them for their different play styles. I spent 3 hours on one encounter resulting in a fight whereas I had one friend spend 3 minutes talking his way out of the same encounter to progress (I was livid). I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys a mix of real-time turn-based combat, puzzles, problem solving, and coming up with creative ways to resolve encounters as it features a top-down style of game play. This style of game play may not be appealing to everyone however, you will find an experience that is worth your time if you are willing to give it a chance. The game is divided into 3 acts that are packed with content waiting for you to explore. At some points it can even be overwhelming for the player to explore everything as you will likely get side tracked and deviate from what objective you were originally planning to resolve. Factors such as your class and race also influence game play as unique dialogue options may show up when talking to NPCs or access to certain areas are blocked off depending on your race.The story starts off slow but transitions into a grander scheme that unveils as you progress further in the acts and the choices that you make throughout your journey will impact the outcome of how that story unfolds which can lead to some tense moments where you need to take a few minutes to pick your choices carefully. The story of your companions are also affected by your choices as well which can determine whether they will stay with you on your adventure or go their own separate ways. Dialogue is voiced acted and certain performances prove to be very convincing both in and out of main story quests. The music is work of art that is choreographed extremely well to fit the worlds environments in relation to what is taking place in the moment. Some notable pieces include “Down by the river” and “Song of Balduran”. If there was anything negative to say about the game, it would mostly be centred around some bug related issues with the quest system causing a save to be reloaded or the performance issues in certain areas. It would also be appreciated if there was a transmog system put in place or the ability to preview dyes on clothing or the clothing itself.Baldur's Gate 3 is a game that has other game developers worried about its success and deserves any praise that it gets given the amount of value you are getting from a single purchase without requiring any additional purchases that many other game developers have adopted. The game is a work of art and you will not be able to seeing everything in one play through as you are bound to miss some content given how expansive it is. Something like this doesn’t come around too often in this day and age and games like this can prove that you do not need to adopt a micro transaction monetization model to offer a sound and complete product that consumers would buy.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: My do not recommend review here echoes the problems everyone else who has reviewed this as a do not recommend is saying. After 60 hours, I just cannot deal with the issues anymore. It's gotten so buggy and frustrating that I just cannot finish it which is upsetting because I REALLY WANT TO! I had fun in the beginning. I want to fully enjoy this game, but the longer it went on, the worse the game became. The only thing worse than a bad game is a good game that became worse after you were already invested.This game has OVERWHELMINGLY positive reviews, and I fully understand why. The beginning handful of hours (5-15) have minor issues but are really good. This game has 3 acts and the first is almost flawless - I assume this is why this game got so many 10/10s and adoring praises on the reviews within the first few days of its release. Great graphics, good companions to choose from, good challenges that can be easy or frustrating depending on how you play. But the game as a whole has so many awful, gameplay breaking bugs or quality of life issues and Act 3 is so dreadfully incomplete and sloppy, I just cannot recommend it right now. I'm sure Larian will fix it in the future and add the content (there's a lot of promised content that wasn't included), but this is just very poor form to release/advertise a completed game when it's not done properly. The poor performance has really killed this game for me and made me feel I wasted dozens of hours with no payoff because the game is just running/acting so poorly at the end.  I don't think it really needs a PROS list - if you're interested in this game, you know what it entails. It's D&D but in game form - pretty similar to Divinity Original Sin 2 with some different nuances for spells and rolls. When it comes down to it, there's two central issues - an insane, unforgivable amount of bugs that break/ruin the game and just completely missing BASIC quality of life features that are missing and have no excuse to not be here in a game like this. CONS:1. The Bugs. Absolutely unreal and frustrating. The patch fix addressed over 1000 bugs that needed to be addressed but it did not fix the most annoying ones. I played co-op with my partner and these are the bugs we ran into in a COMPLETED GAME. Unacceptable. -The spectral weapon summon broke the game for us about ten times. It simply would on occasion not let us do anything with it during its turn (end it, unsummon it, skip it, attack, etc,.) and restarting wouldn't fix it. We had to reload an older save to fix it. This didn't happen to any other summon, only the spectral weapon.-enemies or allies not entering combat and still being able to attack/take actions outside of it, unbound by turn based system. -multiple times, the turn order decided to skip turns of the main characters. They weren't hit or affected by anything that should skip their turns, it just decided to happen.-When the game reloaded, half the time I unlearned all my alchemy knowledge I had. The only fix to this was transferring my alchemy bag from one character to another and then I have to one by one see my entire list of potions/elixirs I can craft pop up one after another with NO OPTION to skip through them/make the dialogue box go away-we had one big backstory cutscene for one of the companions that got interrupted/ended abruptly for no reason and none of the characters have anything to say about this big fight/revelation we just had.-Enemy turns can take OVER A MINUTE for one character where they do nothing. Not sure if this is a big or just poor oversight. When you're in a long fight with a ton of characters, some enemies would snap to their turn and just refuse to act OR they'd do an act and stand there or spin around like deciding and do nothing. -visual cutscene bugs where models/assets did not load right. In the second two acts, there were multiple times in cutscenes where parts of the companion characters did not fully load.-there were multiple times where things just didn't work right. A skill can hit one moment at a target and other times when you go to attack again, it says it's blocked/out of range. Sometimes spells or attacks said they'd connect but they wouldn't - you didn't miss it, the game just didn't process you targetted.2. Poor quality of life features-You cannot move items anywhere with a button or click. You cannot move multiple items at once. You literally have to drag your items one at a time to chests, inventories, traders, etc. In a game that has a TON of loot, it's insanely time consuming and annoying to do this.-once you sell/move items, your items DO NOT autofill blank spots. So your inventory is full of empty random slots where previous items were. Super messy and frustrating to try to manage the inventory. -the camera clipping/following is terrible. Trying to go up or down floors and angle the camera proper is more frustrating than half the battles. This happens both in battles and while trying to explore. It can be a challenge to get the game to look at something and the screen not go crazy-ADDITIONALLY, in combat it will yank to whoever character is acting. There is NO OPTION TO TURN THIS OFF. This is present in divinity 2, why the hell isn't it in this game. This game has turns where multiple people can act at the same time, so when you're trying to do something IF other characters are also acting, it yanks you away to them and often messes up your spells/movement/actions. Again, there is ZERO way to turn this clipping to the person acting off. -You cannot run/dash outside of battle. Your character is slow outside when exploring/backpedaling to old areas-the pathing is awful. For NO reason, your character or your companions or summons will decide they can't go somewhere they just went. They get stuck, they refuse to go somewhere that there's no obstacles in the way of. Your character/companions try to avoid things that hurt them (traps, bad terrain, etc), but they sometimes choose to go through anyway leading to damage/status effects. -The rolls can be frustrating. I get this is a luck-based system with rolling in some aspects, but some story beats you CANNOT complete or explore if your characters roll poorly. Sometimes you just get unlucky and now the game expects you will just not get to do/explore a significant part of the story/sidequest OR you have to savescum because it feels there's no way to alternatively progress along the path you want to. -Act 3 just gives up on cut scenes, dialogue trees, and companion interaction. Act 3 feels horrible and unfinished. We ended up fighting one of the big bads after huge preparations. We got into their area, cleared out a bunch of smaller battles and got to the big bad. there was no cut scene, no dialogue, no acknowledgement. This happened to another major side quest that a companion's entire big background as well.-The level cap is only 12...why. We didn't even explore half of two of the main maps and we're not done with the game and already at the level cap. So now we have nothing more to explore with skills, levels, or multiclassing (which we didn't know you could do and the game never specifies - we only found out after when reading some articles on the game)

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding achievement. _childDocuments_.review: So, this game was gifted to me and I was excited to play it and..........I was not disappointed. No matter how many times I play it, it's a different game every time. The turn based style is amazing and honestly I don't have a single bad thing to say about this game.Each origin character has their own story, and the fact that your decisions at the beginning of the game affect the end game is something they did extremely well. I wish more games were like Balder's Gate. I have played through it so many times, I can't even really keep track anymore. _childDocuments_.review: This game has lots of potential. Combat mechanics are fun, and there is some great voice acting and interesting stories. It's just too short right now though, the 'Early Access' means you can't progress past the first 'chapter' in the story line yet. The combat encounters feel very unbalanced, and skewed to be a little too difficult. It ends up forcing you to save and reload often trying to exploit terrain and items to squeak by with a victory. Dialog options are random, and it feels unfair. You can just spend extra time reloading saves to get the outcome you want, but it feels cheap. In some encounters a 'failed' dialog option means death, forcing you to reload anyways.When they release Chapter 2, and do some balancing on the combat encounters, this game will be awesome, it's just not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Critically succeeded in headbutting a friend. I'm playing D&D!***Edit: I'm having fun. The game is close enough to D&D rules that you get the familiarity, and it's cool to see passive checks and dice rolls translated into the game. Its going to upset people because it's 5e, and it's upset people because of...reasons.I like playing video games and I like D&D. This is a pretty cool way to feel like I'm doing bits of both. _childDocuments_.review: My experience was pretty rough, I played with some fools like myself, so I missed a lot of the plot points. However, I still had a lot of fun and excitement.  And it's inspired by the D&D  universe and mechanics. The influence of D&D can be found in every aspect of the game, from gameplay mechanics to lore, stories, characters, and beyond. Winning dice rolls usually gets you what you want, but losing can lead to another unique situation. The chances of winning depend on various skills, traits, items, , effects on the character, etc. It's a fairly complex mechanic that has a big impact on the gameplay, and every mechanic in the game is so complex,   No, I don't want to describe this whole piece of cheese here, but I can say that it is quite large (66.5 hours, according to some fools on the Internet), complex and interesting.  You gather various companions with their own stories related to the main plot, and at the end you fight (or you join) some b1tches who want to conquer the world. It's a simple yet effective structure. It's quite interesting to watch the heroes develop as they move towards their goal.   The skills in this game are a whole topic on their own. You can freeze, burn, enlarge, shrink, poison, throw, summon a black hole, 4ucking strike with lightning, turn into gas, transform into another character, finally deliver F-16s to Ukraine, summon elementals, summon a goblin, explode, blow up someone else, teleport, fly, throw a fireball, summon a fireball, suck, explode, summon a goblin, blow up someone else, teleport, fly, throw a fireball, summon a fireball and much more.  You can bypass many difficult battles with yo charisma. And not only in battles, but also in quests, your charisma can be invaluable. Choosing the right dialogue options can earn you more gold or provide hints. Different choices can also influence the story and outcomes of quests. The game offers great diversity in this aspect .

_childDocuments_.review: Early access review. This will be rather short as almost everyone has said everything 1000 times already.Almost everything has been said elsewhere, maybe everything even. I bought this and didn't play it for quite awhile as I wanted to wait on the full release. Watching a few streamer friends play it I decided to give it a try. This is what I've found in 45 hours so far, getting ready to play another 6 or so tonight and probably 4-10 daily for the foreseeable future.Starting with the cons as I usually do.Negatives to me -#1 The most sinful con is no stat rolling will be introduced even after release. This is BG3, the first 2 rewarding those that stayed up rolling all night was an epic part of the game. It should at least be optional, like Solasta (that's right I said it). Solasta kicks your arse on this one aspect. Whenever I meet people involved with the development of this game, which I'm sure that I will, I will bring up this topic, not the gazillion positives. Not having the option to stat roll is TOTAL BS in a BALDUR's GATE title. Most people involved probably never played 1 & 2 (or Icewind Dale, Planescape Toprment, etc. or pretty much anything D&D related ever) or maybe weren't even born yet. Whatever, BS, moving on.#2 There are some bugs and glitches still which I do not think will be ironed out as they could've easily patched act one again, even this close to release, if they had been worked out. Characters holding weapons incorrectly, ears through helmets, I saw the camera move in a characters head and you were looking at the back of his eyeballs for part of a dialogue, I jumped all of my characters to an area and they couldn't jump back due to a tiny fraction of a millimeter height difference and I had to reload a save an hour earlier (no biggie but sucked and shouldn't happen), some how I bugged some inventory and had 2 of some items - again it was a nice bonus selling but it wasn't as intended and they were unique items so this isn't a case of me being mistaken. etc. etc. Fine tuning is going to be going on for a long time and the worrisome part is that I'm sure they are drooling over all of the gazillion DLC's planned so they may never fine tune the little things further..3) NPC's talk to whoever is closest to them. That's ridiculous because maybe a persuasion chance comes up and your fighter has to do it just because he was standing close to somebody that started blabbing. I understand if you're controlling the wrong character and you talk to someone but this is different and happens often enough to be a gripe. NPC starts their rant and the wrong person is standing next to them for whatever kind of check is going to be needed. How about assuming the party is smart enough to have the best person for the job do whatever it is that comes up? Like several other games....4) Maybe this is a non issue at release but there needs to be a ton of voices to chose from for the PLAYER CHARACTER and any custom characters made. All of this time into all of the cinematics and stuff with every origin character and so far there's like 2 male voices and 2 female voices (that's right I said male and female) and funny that they took the time to make sure that the guys can pick female voices and the girls can pick guy voices but only showed 2 of each... Again maybe that'll be resolved in 7-8 days and we'll have 50 male and 50 female voices to chose from. It's just not good when everyone talks the same regardless of gender or race.5) That's about it for the negatives. A lot could be explained better but maybe it will be a bit and it seems like they want people to learn by trying, trial be fire.POSITIVES -I'm not going to use a list here as I'll just do a little paragraph instead. The game is huge, as huge as they all say. My 45 hours I've seen probably I'd guess about 80% of Act 1, that's seeing it from only the perspective of my choices + races + classes etc.. This game is epic in size. They say that Act 3 is the biggest so I expect non speedrun  games should take at least 150+ hours and considering acts 2-3 haven't even been seen yet possibly much much longer. So many options with how to handle anything and everything that it'd be almost impossible to see every single thing in the game. I'd be surprised if anyone at Larian has seen it all. Literally anything could give you several different options based on some optional thing you did 20 hours before which the choices were based on something 5 hours before etc. etc. It makes my brain hurt to think of how much thought they put into all of the different paths to do things. A+ on that and other game devs are going to have a very hard time keeping up with that. Voice acting is great, the best that I've seen and it's all the time everywhere. They must have spent more on voice acting than competing games spent on their whole budget. A+ on that. Cut scenes, everyone knows from watching trailers even, they are stunning. A+ on that. Art/sound/ everything else A++To sum it up this will be the greatest game of it's type released to date. ZERO competition on that. I'm very confident with that. It'll set the bar for future RPG's so high that it will require very smart and very dedicated people to come close to it in the future. That's awesome for all gamers even if you don't care for this for some ridiculous reason. Studios need to strive to produce awesome work instead of rolling out cash grabs every chance they get. I'm no fanboy, I listed my negatives first. I didn't log in and just fall instantly in love. It's a process. If you play it like an RPG should be played, think about your choices, give meaning to your play through, then you'll love this game. If you want to play it like a murder hobo then you may still like it but there's probably better games for you out there.If you're considering buying it I would and did. You'll get the free upgrade after release and save $20 or so because of that. It's a deal at this price. I don't want to say what I would've paid for this but if they did the early release as a free weekend or something, I would've paid much more. If you read my whole review, which turned out longer than I planned, then thank you for your time even if you don't like it or don't agree.  Comments are on for praise or flames. I'm off to play it so take what you will out of this one. There's only a couple of games that I've felt this good about and I still love and play them so I know this will be a long term love for me, even without the f'ing stat rolls that should be an option.Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 has set a new standard for not only RPG's, but video games in general. It seems all too common nowadays that game developer push out slop games, and expect people to pay $60-$70 for said slop. No creativity, no passion, no pride in what they create, Baldur's Gate 3 could not possibly be a better example of what games SHOULD be. Immersive storytelling, beautiful scenery, variations in game-play , the list goes on. I can confidently say that Baldur's Gate 3 is by far the best video game that I have ever played, and quite possibly the best video game to ever grace this Earth. I know this review seems dramatic, but Baldur's Gate 3 is truly is a masterpiece that deserves every ounce of recognition and praise that it has received.
