_childDocuments_.review: Do i think this a bad game? absolutely not.Do i think its different from the Original Baldur's gate games? very much so.If you want the short version of how I feel about this game its simply that its not a bad game, it just feels like a different game from the original 2 two Baldur's gate games, much like how people feel about the two divinity original sin games of both one and two (same series, drastic differences).Three things this game does well:1. Most quests in this game do not have a singular path to completing an objective. there are plenty of routes and choices to take/make when completing an object, giving the exploration a lot more depth.2. The immersion of the game just by how you make a character can get really good. between the time i played as a drow and dwarf they each had different/special dialog and dialog choices just for being different races. the same also applies to the class you pick.3. The combat can be challenging. going into a fight blindly can be a big mistake. sometimes it might be better to prepare an ambush, sometimes its better to be in one place for a character than somewhere else, and there are plenty of times where enemies can out number you making it better to fight smarter, not harder.Three things the game could do better:1, to put it shortly, minus the sub classes, the amount of classes right now are limited at 6 which isn't terribly many compared to some games in the CRPG category. the races, again minus the sub races, are also limited to only 7 and aside from that about half of them are based around Elfs. more classes and races would be nice, and more varied races beyond Elfs based ones would be even better2, despite the combat being good, I feel I should mention the jump command, in combat, is very easy to exploit as it makes it far too easy to avoid getting a free attack applied to someone that is very clearly threatened. I feel some adjustments should be made to this so that players have a harder time when confronted by what is suppose to be a dilemma during combat,3. Pick pocketing from others can feel too forgiving. you can do it a lot and either bribe them or even make a skill check for them to not exercise punishments should you get caught with no additional punishment afterwards. i feel at the very least if you get caught, they should be at least be more aware of you doing it and make the skill checks become increasingly harder for the npc in question, if only slightly over time.its a great game and there are really just a few small things here and there that could be better.

_childDocuments_.review: [Updated after three full different complete games.]This is the mother of all CRPGs. I am absolutely blown away. I played three different characters through the entire game. 70, 80, and 90 hours. Each game felt wildly different, with amazing twist and revelations that I didn't see in other attempts.I knew that I was going to enjoy this game - and I knew that it was going to be my fave of the BG series. But, I did not expect it to over take Disco Elysium as my favourite CRPG. How this game reacts to your character and their choices is unequalled. I can not think of another game that allows this much freedom and choice. This game makes me feel selfish and greedy, for any changes or modifications I would want, because it already does so much. I played a Heroic Elf Scoundrel, whose maintaining the moral high ground caused many issues.I played a Dark Urge Half-Orc who wallowed in his depravity. And I played as Astarian, redone as a Monk, and played as an anti-hero. It really felt like they were three different games that happened to hit some of the same beats and scenes. If you are big in to RPGS and freedom of choice in them, give in to your own Dark Urges and grab this game. [EA thoughts]7 hours in so far and I am pleased as punch. This is a long laundry list of everything I ever wanted Baldur's gate to be. While the old games will always have a warm place in my heart, BG3 captures the tabletop RPG experience of D&D unlike any game I have played in sometime. Wonderful graphics, many choices, and obvious replay value, this is a classic in the making. The only thing this needs is a DM mode, a world building toolkit, and the ability to host persistent servers - and we will finally be able to put poor NWN out of its misery.

_childDocuments_.review: I kicked a goblin into the abyss while he was peeing.Game of the Year.100 hours in.Still creating my character.I genuinely don't know how human beings made this game. It's like the video game version of the pyramids. It’s better than the hype. It's the best money you will spend this year.As someone who played Dragon Age Origins so many times as a teen, playing this game felt like meeting a long lost friend and it made me so happy. To me Baldur's Gate 3 felt like a fully realized version of DAO.After the first 20 hours, I was simply stunned. They managed to take everything that I've loved about D&D, and distilled it into a video game. To say it’s been worth my time is an understatement. This is like showing up to play D&D and your DM has every battle map, mini, a binder of world lore ready to tie into your own backstory, voices every character perfectly, lets you pickpocket the boss because it’s fun, and tells you they got nowhere to be so you can play for the next four days.I literally cannot get the game out of my head. The combat. The lore. The story. The sheer audacity they thought they could this and they did. I love it very, very much - pretty much everything is of such an outstanding quality. The voice-acting, the plot, the visuals, the cinematic qualities, the soundtrack (ohh, the soundtrack) It's intense and beautiful, hauntingly sad. It's about deeply flawed people, about redemption and love and forgiveness. There is a vast amount of quests, often compellingly written. You get attached to characters, you take your time reading notes because not only do they tell you more about the lore, they help you understand what is happening and make decisions upon it. This game is 123GB and they're all used for something that matters.I think the complexity of the game is its selling point.  The world is so dense with content, filled with characters who directly influence the story and are directly influenced by it.  Even a random NPC that you chat with in Act 1 could end up playing a major role in the story by Act 3... or no role at all if they die instead.  You can see the layers within the decision making, which gives weight to everything you do.  Who you save, kill, team up with, etc. all end up telling a different story, making the game really feel like it's YOUR story being told. Then they did that thing that separates good writers from average: make absolutely memorable characters, make you invest yourself emotionally in them and then put them into impossible situations where they can’t possibly win.The fact you can play 100+ hours on your first playthrough and come back for round 2 to have a literal UNRECOGNIZABLY DIFFERENT STORY play out is part of the magic. There will be "did you know in Baldur s Gate 3" videos for years to come as people find more and more. It’s actually so amazing, my wife’s boyfriend is doing his own play through and then doing one with me and he's getting a completely different experience and dialogue. I have three saves right now & each one feels so dramatically different from the others. From timing changing world events, to origin companion dialogue, to choices you make as you're playing - there're so many aspects that change completely. It’s so interesting and shows your actions really do change the story. This game rewards creativity in an almost infinite number of ways. The choices presented to the player during the course of the story are staggering in number and a lot of them are impactful. Few games will reach this level of excellence. Well done Larian.I also really can't get over how every little piece of extra attention you give to an item or an area is rewarding. You can go from stumbling onto a regular book or chest in a random area to having a 3 hour quest you'd otherwise have totally missed. There's probably 50+ hours of content minimum that the game doesn't steer you towards at all. Like there's entire areas you can only find by hovering your cursor over a small hitbox that some players may never discover. All my friends who played had vastly different playthroughs from one another.The voice acting alone makes this game perfect. It just feels like you are part of a big adventure and there is so many things to do and so many ways to do it that it begs playing it over and over again. Even letting the dice fall as they do vs save scumming is a strategy. The characters take me back to caring like I did back in Mass Effect. And it's true turn-based which I have grown to love as I've fallen out of FPS's and moved to a primarily single player game player.The rule set, which is the hardest thing to comprehend for non D&D people, is pretty accessible and the tutorials work well.  It does require some planning, but you can watch a video or two and get a gist. There's also no Ironman mode or anything, so you can literally mess up an infinite amount of times with no repercussions. If you get it, make sure to save frequently! The game saves at odd times and isn't very consistent. There's no rolling "save every 15 mins" or anything.On top of that, the tactics of the combat is immensely satisfying.  It can be obtuse at times because there are LOADS of status effects, environment effects, spells, items, and conditions that can overwhelm you if you're not paying attention.  But to those who WANT to pay attention, there is nothing more fun than examining an enemy, determining their weaknesses, seeing they have a weak WIS and using a spell with a WIS save to completely neuter them. In that way, fights have a way to be incredibly difficult if you're not paying attention to the details or an absolute breeze if you know how to use every tool at your disposal.Yes, this really is a once in a decade kind of game. Crazy it is also a $60 no strings attached no shops, no passes, no DLC, just one huge and complete game. Truly has permanently raised Larian into RPG developer godhood among the likes of those like Square and Bioware. I'm convinced this masterpiece will be studied by many game developers for years to come. It’s a game that will be referenced for decades. As far is the specific genre goes and arguably gaming in general it just set a high bar. Much to the displeasure of dogsh*t publishers and devs everywhere.BG3 is not a perfect game but man the experience, replay value, freedom is unparalel to anything I have ever seen. You can just feel that every person involved with this game has put all their efforts and devotion to this. It's made with so much love. It's a game that stays with you.If you like Dragon Age Origins, I guarantee you'll like the game. It's a CRPG but also a successor to BioWare games like DA, Kotor, and Mass Effect (and obviously the original Baldurs Gate games if you're old like me). I highly recommend it.10/10

We spent well over an hour trying to figure it out, even stating a new game to see if that would work and doing what the company suggested by switching to the other game type. None of these work, so for that reason i can not recommend this game as it is. Combat was not the only thing that was bugged either, there were many times that the game would just black screen and never render again. Hopefully at that time i can change this review to show it in more of a positive light.Edit: While the game has improved and me and my friends have made it reliably through combat there are still massive issues. The conversations will skip to differing parts leaving you confused and lost in the story. It also show player locked in a conversation that is only fixable via long rest. This makes saving difficult resulting in sometimes massive losses of progress. Edit: After multiple updates the game has become much better, many of the issues that were previously mentioned have been fixed. There are still some issues with parts still heavily bugged or wonky for groups to play in. I can say though that I am very happy with the progress they are making. I still can not recommend the game to buy for its current state if you are planning on playing with a full party of friends. _childDocuments_.review: If you are/were a D&D tabletop gamer, and considering this game, this review is for you.  As a kid, teen & young adult, I played Dungeons & Dragons. I played 2nd & 3rd Edition.  As life does, I got busier as I got older.  As an adult, full-time worker, husband & father, my priorities changed and I struggled to find the chance to get back into it because tabletop gaming is cumbersome -- it is difficult to find other like-minded players, coordinate times to play, get all the necessary supplies, get organized, find someone else to take care of my responsibilities while I play a game, etc...  However, the progress of video games over the years gave rise to the hope that one day, the tabletop game could be re-created in the same image as a video game, with the same feel & ability to play simultaneously with friends and family regardless of how close they lived.That day has arrived.  Baldur's Gate 3 is it.  Finally.  I have put more hours into this game since the August release than I have put into all games not named 'Minecraft' in the last 5 years combined.  This game is so much like the tabletop game, but with conveniences to save the player time that it compels you to play.  I haven't played fully through the game yet, but I will...and I already know the replay value is off the charts. This game also gives me the ability to share my passion for D&D with my kids, as we can be members of the same party and adventure together.

_childDocuments_.review: You buy this game, download it, boot up, and see a peaceful city on the ocean, a cool breeze fluttering the foliage. You press the left mouse button. The camera pans down to a mysterious crypt, and you see four adventurers walk through a door, torches in hand. The music kicks in - and it's straight up earbliss. That's the only way to describe this song. So you sit there, entranced, and listen to the main menu theme in its entirety. Silence ensues - then, remarkably, another song plays. Main Menu OST #2. Equally as epic as the first song, you can't believe that the main menu has music this good, let alone the fact that there isn't one, but TWO tracks. But then - unbelievably - after the calm begins again, after the earbliss ends, after you think it can't get any better - a third song starts to play. And my god, is it just the most epic song you've ever heard. Not one, not two, but three songs - at the main menu alone - that single-handedly trounce any song from any other game, period. That is Baldur's Gate 3 in a nutshell.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good AAA developers are crying about how bad it makes them look. The massive amount of cut-content is one thing, but the game is just a buggy broken mess. NPCs just vanish, including party members. Quest triggers fire off, or don't, at random. Items and loot that are unreachable because they are 2cm to the right of an item on a shelf. Etc.The cut content is very noticeable also. That they've already started patching it back in is rather telling.And it's rather worrying that said patches are further breaking more quest triggers and story-beats.It's still the best RPG released since larian's last game, but the frustration is massive. I specifically avoided buying the game in early access, and reading/watching anything about it as I wanted to fully experience it on the first play through. Now I am left waiting for patches to fix things, wondering what I've missed, and what will be added back in through upcoming patches. The point of releasing out of early access is that you are saying the game is done. Not "Well, we finished Act 1. And we got 95% of act 2 done... Act three is playable!"I'm sure it will be fixed eventually, it's just incredibly frustrating.Still leaving it a thumbs up, because it's still so much better than other devs games that it made them cry. Just sad that it wasn't the 10/10 it could have been had they actually finished it before release.

_childDocuments_.review: Post-completion update: This is 2023's GOTY for me. Absolutely Recommended. A Massive Landmark RPG. Acts 1 and 2 are probably some of the best acts in narrative RPGs. Act 3 falters a tad bit due to the weight of the game, but not to the extent that it detracts significantly from the rest of the game. Looking forward to more updates in the future!(Multiplayer is also fun and chaotic lmao)Before a more in-depth list of features, a list of what this game is and isn't♠ This game is NOT   Divinity Original Sin 3, a 1:1 port of D&D 5e to video game, the perfect video game, a bug-free experience, a game that will satisfy every single person's wants or preferences♠ This game IS   A highly reactive and deep RPG, a great synthesis of some of the best elements of CRPGs updated to modern standards, a beautifully cinematic game, the closest thing to playing an actual session of D&D in video game form at the moment, one of the best games to come out in 2023, Larian's best effort to date imo-----Features and Observations:♣ Character creation gives you analysis paralysis♣ Game adapts the best parts of D&D 5e into video game form, while revising aspects that don't work well with video games with a Larian/Divinity flair♣ A lot of Quality of Life improvements over DOS2, namely search bar for the inventory and freeform movement♣ Companions AND NPCs remember things you did/said to them♣ Companions banter with each other ala Dragon Age♣ Character facial and body animations are astounding during cutscenes♣ Multiple paths to solve puzzles and quests exist♣ Dialogue options and ability checks are sometimes dependent on your class and race, making it so it feels like the world actually reacts to who you are and makes both relevant for roleplaying purposes♣ Nested tooltips!!!♣ Bugs so far are mostly of the Skyrim variety- either minor ones or funny ahh bugs♣ Most importantly, trust the dice. Having bad rolls doesn't mean the end of the game, it's just a new path in the journey

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far I had only played the pre-release of the first chapter. On old gaming laptop that barely was able to run this game on minimum settings, and only on single player mode. As that it blew my expectations. Expands on the very entertaining and re-playable Divinity 2 combat system, while bringing on the Advanced Dungeons and Dragons rules. Quality of action is excellent, the stories and characters are the inspiring and surprising Larian level, which means very high indeed. Difference to Divinity series is that this game brings the story in player's face as well with the acted close up dialogues. No prior knowledge of either, Dungeons and Dragons or the Divinity series is needed, those are like under the hood technical details which the player does not need to know, but may come to appreciate. Over all impression from that early stage testing was like playing particularly well made very entertaining and carefully detailed old school tabletop roleplaying game, with great sense of immersion in the story and the world. Except all the details are visible, detailed and made into virtual models to interact with, which is a mind staggering amount of details to interact with. But, as with Divinity the real highest quality fun starts when playing together with friends, solving and at times blundering, stories, battles and all sorts of interactions. And now I am about to start the actual ready and released Baldur's Gate III, which will probably blow my mind, then restructure my mind and then blow it again. Then I will become annoyance as I cajole and coerce my friends to come play it with me.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved and adored this game from start to near-finish. It's a great journey, with plenty of challenging combat, plenty of ways to adapt your story to how you wish to play it, and a true DND campaign come to life on your computer screen. Aside from a few bugs that'll be patched out over the course of time, there's something to love for everyone who enjoys a good story, some hearty combat and a few moral dilemma. TLDR: Definitely would recommend this to everyone, but I would suggest to anyone picking it up soon after release, take your time so that maybe some of the problems I encountered are patched out by the time you experience it. Happy adventuring!((UPDATE ON PARAGRAPH BELOW: FIXED))Spoilers ahead, stop reading here:The only complaint would be the ending. I went through a lot of effort to save most of my companions and gain the good ending with their favour, and decided to romance Astarion. Helped him kill his master, but did not let him usurp the ritual for himself. He stayed a vampire spawn, and felt better for it. We were very close and had max intimacy. After the final fight, he simply starts burning and runs, and is implied to not be seen again. After all I went through to persuade him to stay, after his promises to stay with me and to want to be by my side, he simply runs and is not seen again. No epilogue to say goodbye, not even a word of goodbye, just dashing off into the horizon. I hope this issue will be patched out, and a proper epilogue will be added, with your actions summarised and a chance to interact with your party one last time, and some important NPCs, much like the ending of act 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* There's a huge amount of content, including lots of witty animals saying amusing things, lots of quests, a huge city to explore. Lots of dialogues. Many maps with lots of fine detail.* A nice combat system almost, but not quite, reproducing dnd5e combat.Cons:* Feeling crippled by not being able to point the camera upwards - much of the maps have very high places, and you cannot look at them from below.* The bad way in which the divinity/divinity 2 engine were configured are still the same: NPCs still reacting stupidly to 'stealing' red marked items. NPCs still running around like idiots if they see your summons/animal form druids etc. It makes the game feel aged and broken.* Badly made transition from 'real time' to 'turn based' combat, where many creatures of the world still move around in real time while you are 'frozen' in turn based combat, thus people can wander into the combat zone if you take too long to decide what to do on your turn.* The token 'reactivity' (important NPCs acknowledging your choices), while impressive for a second, is incredibly shallow. Many rational dialogue options are missing. * Some of the main villain NPCs don't have rational motivations of their own, they just really want to ask the player to express themselves giving them choices to make, and responding to them with 'interesting, very well - we shall make the game go your route!'. This kind of bad writing exists in much of the genre (i.e. Baldur Gate's 1 and 2, Torment etc)* Lazy bad writing - i.e. you see a door, and 'feel' that it wants to hear a cypher - the narrator just appears and tells you how things are instead of these things being revealed organically via things that happen in the world.* Shoving enemies into instant death chasms and being shoved into them is too big of a deal - i.e. push distance is configured to be 2-3 times longer than I'd realistically expect, and for some silly reason shove is a bonus action rather than an action.Overall I really enjoyed most of the game, in spite of the bugs and quirks. If you like the genre I heartily recommend it. It's just that I had greater expectation after such a long gestation period. In particular for some of the ancient maladies of the Divinity engine to be removed.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited for this for over 18 years.Big disappointment. Nothing to do with Early Access really. It just feels so much like Original Sin 2. If you liked that game, you'll like this one as well. If you liked the old BG games, it does not mean you feel anything when playing this.Few positives. Graphically it looks just fine. Music is nice. Voice acting not bad, and there is plenty of it. Although they often have nothing interesting to say. Liked the dice roll events somewhat. Inventory management is rather confusing and split into three different views, out of which none really completely serve the purpose.All the maps are just like Original Sin. A lot of height differences, which does not help with the camera controls at all. Areas consist of somewhat confusing paths which feel constrictive and it feels that it constantly funnels you forward towards the next mandatory event. I found absolutely no sense of grand adventure, just running the gauntlet from one event to the next. I actually liked the small campsite encounters more than the game itself. I could not help thinking of Dragon Age 2 when playing this game. I mean it's not bad... just mediocre, lukewarm and void of passion. I wanted to think that this might just be the start of Act 1, but then remembered thinking the same with Original Sin 2, and I dont think Larian can create anything different.And I know Larian and their games are highly liked. I've never understood why, I got precious little out of them. But many people do, and I'm sure they will like this one as well.After 8 hours I found that I was forcing myself to play this game. Decided to refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit on 2023/11/15: Still not done playing this game, this is it.Spoilers for Dragon Age Origins and Baldur's Gate 3 below.I remember when I was 14 years old I played a game called Dragon Age Origins, an RPG set in a fantasy world with magic and the like, where you could form a party with other characters from the world.There was this one time where I was in a tower full of mages that was being attacked by monsters, or something like that, my party found a group of mages who had taken shelter in one of the rooms inside the tower and my evil witch companion suggested killing them all for being cowards. Being an edgy teenager and roleplaying as an evil edgy half-elf wizard, I obviously agreed, so we got to doing a little magicicide and kept going our way, cleared the tower, finished the game a long while after, and that was that.I enjoyed the game so much I started a new playthrough, got to the mage's tower and found this group again, but this time I decided to help them instead of giving them a ticket to the afterlife and, to my surprise, it turned out one of the mages, an old woman, could become one of your companions. She had tons of dialogue, a personal quest, a personal story to tell,  My decision of being an edgelord and slaughtering a bunch of mages caused me to miss a possible companion, and the game was full of situations when your actions would impact your character and the world around you. One of my companions left my party near the end of the game because I spared a guy he hated. In one playthrough, I'd ally myself with a group werewolves and kill a settlement elves so I could have them in my army for the final fight, in the other I'd help the elves cleanse the werewolves of their curse, losing them as allies but befriending the elves. You could help people in distress or make matters worse, and the world would continue on, and this was true for the whole game.I searched a long time for a game that could give me that same feeling, of being in a world that doesn't give you the "right" or "wrong" path, but simply choices and consequences, but none would do it. Not the other Dragon Age games, nor Mass Effect, nor The Witcher, nor thePathfinder games, and I eventually gave up, thinking that I was seeing DAO through rose-tinted glasses, the special feeling I had being no more than nostalgia.Ten years or so from that, I played Baldur's Gate 3, and I finally felt I was playing DAO for the first time all over again.This game accounts for everything, and I mean . Every single conflict can be solved in a multitude of ways. Whether you play the hero or the villain, the ways in which you can act can vary depending on how you got to the place, your character`s class, your race, your past actions, your companions, your character skills. And it doesn't matter what you decide to do, the game keeps going, the world changes to fit the consequences of your actions, the biggest example of this being that Being in early access, I can't talk much about the story, but what we have so far is really promising. Each companion is wonderfully voiced acted, and they all have interesting backstories and quests that you may only get to see if they approve of you enough.Combat feels amazing even though it can be a little slow at times, being turn-based and lacking RTWP as an option. Every hit carries a lot of weight, and most of the spells look and sound incredible. Larian's done a pretty good job at adapting the D&D 5e rules to a video game format. Also, the music is fantastic overall.Right now, the full game is two months from being released, and I'm hoping the finished product has the same level of quality the early access has shown. For in that case, this could truly end up becoming an unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As a slightly late adopter of BG3 due to an unending backlog of games all I can say is wow! The game is a masterfully crafted role-playing game that seamlessly blends a captivating narrative with deep, strategic gameplay. As a fan of D&D, RPGs and the previous games in the series, diving into the world of BG3 felt like a nostalgic journey with a fresh and modern twist.The standout features of the game is its attention to detail in world-building. The Realm come to life with stunning visuals, intricate character designs, and atmospheric soundscapes that create an immersive experience. The level of detail in the environments, from bustling cities to eerie dungeons, is nothing short of impressive. And not that I've delved into the extended capabilities of modding I've been reassured by friends this can be extended ten-fold should I want it to be.Another strong point is the story they've gone through and your constant changing path through that narrative, weaving a complex and engaging story that keeps players hooked from start to finish. The game allows for meaningful choices (assuming you don't save/reset each one), each impacting the story you experience and the character relationships you develop along your journey, fostering a sense of agency that is integral to any great D&D style experience. The well-written dialogue and voice acting further enhance the storytelling, making each character feel unique and memorable, not to mention the wild ways you can 'have at' each of those characters as well!Also the amount of stuff they have littered around that you can collect sets off my inner magpie at an alarming rate, where is the bag of holding to offset the amount of shinnies I need to gather. Or a side quest that propels me off to another area when I've yet to finish the current one. It's great to see that with it being as open world as it is there is still alot to do and see and collect (even if my camp storage chest would be bigger than an amazon distribution hub) to that my only complaint would be a better mechanic for sorting / auto sorting storage to combine up items that already exist in containers so I can spend less time chronically sorting and get out and adventure more (though that might also be more of a damning look at my OCD than a missed in-game opportunity).Furthermore, the game is continually evolving through updates and patches, demonstrating the developers' commitment to refining and expanding the player experience through the studios' engagement with the community, actively seeking feedback and implementing changes, shows a dedication to creating a game that fans can truly enjoy. I just wish some of the other larger studios did this too! I can't wait for any additional content drops / expansions in the futur!If you'd not already guessed from the brain waffle above, I would 100% recommend this game to anyone, even more so if you have a former love of D&D / RPGs or those wishing to get transported to a fantasy realm or even as a starter to D&D/TTRPGs to get a loose grip on the rules before heading out to find a gaming group!UPDATE | Played this again recently after all the work they've been doing to add bits here and there as well as a continued drive to fix things that are broken and all I can say is wow! The games as good as ever and should my partner get some time free I'd love to start a joint dark campaign to see where that leads!

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 is a magnificent journey that immerses players in a world of magic, mystery, and mayhem. From the very beginning, the game captures your attention with its stunning visuals, engaging storytelling, and intricate character development. Larian Studios has truly outdone themselves in creating an experience that pays homage to the beloved Baldur's Gate series while introducing fresh and innovative gameplay mechanics.The first two acts of the game are nothing short of brilliant. The attention to detail in the environments, the diverse array of characters, and the complex narrative choices make for a truly unforgettable experience. The combat system is both strategic and dynamic, offering a perfect blend of classic RPG elements and modern gameplay.The character creation and progression system in Baldur's Gate 3 are exceptional, allowing players to mold their characters into unique personalities with their own strengths, weaknesses, and backstories. The companions you encounter throughout your journey are well-written and add depth to the overall narrative, with each having their own quirks and motivations.However, where Baldur's Gate 3 falters is in its final act. The journey to the climax is nothing short of spectacular, but as the story reaches its pinnacle, the experience becomes marred by a noticeable lack of polish. Quests become less refined, and the overall level of detail in both the narrative and the environment seems to take a hit.While the final act still manages to deliver a satisfying conclusion to the overarching story, the lack of polish is undeniable. Some plotlines feel rushed, and there are instances where the game's performance dips, breaking the otherwise immersive experience. It's disappointing to see such a fantastic journey conclude with a slightly tarnished finale.Despite these shortcomings, Baldur's Gate 3 remains a must-play for any RPG enthusiast. The majority of the game is a testament to Larian Studios' dedication to quality, and the final act, although unpolished, doesn't diminish the overall enjoyment of the game. With the promise of updates and improvements, there's hope that the developers will address these issues, ensuring that Baldur's Gate 3 stands as a shining example of modern RPG excellence.

There are endless possibilities and it truly feels like I'm playing a "choose your own adventure" book. I really cannot recommend this game enough.When I first purchased this game, I did it solely on principle to support Larian's vision of games today. I knew nothing about the game itself.  I'm so tired of AAA studios pumping out half-assed games then drowning us with micro-transactions, battle passes, and pay-to-win crap. I had never even played a cRPG or a game with this type of turn-based combat.  When I first played, I was confused-- gotta be honest. I sucked at combat and thought I might not end up playing it much. Eventually I got the hang of it, and I'm so glad I stuck with it.  The story is rich, the environment is gorgeous, the soundtrack is incredible, and I actually care about the characters. Seriously, I think about them when I go to sleep at night. I cannot remember the last time a game haunted my dreams like this. I can't remember the last time I played a game and actually genuinely cared about the characters like they're real people (...am I okay?). How can an NPC make me feel guilty about my choices IN A GAME? I love it.I'm on my 3rd and 4th play-through (another Dark Urge and another "normal" character) and I'm still finding things I missed before. Hidden objectives, caves, quests, interactions. I'm going to be playing this game for a LONG time. There are just so many things I want to try out. Different builds, different relationships, different choices.Larian Studios is amazing. They listen to us. They care. Seeing the voice actors getting involved with the community and even joining us in playing is so wholesome.If you're on the fence about buying this game, GET IT! You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 is what I would call an amazing game. Even though I've only had the chance to play the first chapter (Early Access and all) I'm already in love. This game takes the brilliant genre the original Baldur's Gate games revolutionized and drags it into the modern era. When I found out that it was Larian Studios that was making it I was even more enthused. Larian Studios' Divinity Original Sin 2 was a masterpiece. And now they are making something even more ambitious. Wizards of the Coast apparently turned down several developers who approached them about Baldur's Gate games, they even turned down Larian Studios! But after making DOS2, WotC finally gave in and let Larian Studios work.So far the gameplay is amazing, sure it has bugs, but it's EA for a reason, it's not finished. It takes the combat style of DOS2 and mixes Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition rules into it. It's fun, difficult at times, and makes you think. An excellent feature of Baldur's Gate 3 is being able to interact with the environment around you during combat. You can set flamable things on fire, causing massive explosions before or during combat to give you an edge, poisons, water, and oil litter the battlefield, giving you different effects based off of what hits you. And once you find a fight pattern that works for you the game goes to work making you feel badass and skilled.The story is just as strong as it's gameplay. You expore the world of D&D with characters who have strong personalities (A little to strong sometimes I would add) and deep backstories that you dive into as you get to know them. The npcs are fun as well, they all give BG3 a sense that you are in a living breathing world and it isn't just waiting for you to solve it's issues. Avoiding spoilers, the premise of the story is intriguing and unique. You'll be spellbound from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Decision fatigue and no soul.I really wanted to like this game. But it has a really ♥♥♥♥ up content/quest progression. And this is a systemic problem with Larian games. So I really wanted to share this feedback.For the context, this is coming from a person who played both Baldur's Gates, Icewind Dales and thinks that Planescale Torment is the best RPG ever.This game suffers from exactly the same problem as Divinity 2 (that I also dropped around the hour 7-10). In both cases you start fine, you have 2-3 quests, surrounding location is comprehensible and you have 1-2 heroes with fairly clear skills. 5 hours later and you end up being hell knows where with 20 quests, hundreds of items in your backpack, 10 spells/actions for each hero and loosing any sense of where you are in the storyline.This would be bad even for the endgame. For the early game it's pure nonsense. Example:, I have to find some druid guy. Going there, entering a town full of goblins (!) where I meet a bunch of random characters that I now have to deal with, in addition to 5 more side-quests. And all of that not giving me any sense of why this is happening, who are these goblins and why should I care. Because of that (and also generally uninspiring storyline, as with DOS2) I don't have any connection with the game and it completely looses any charm.I'm writing this review not to bash the game. I'm writing it as a feedback piece to game developers from a game developer (had been making games for 15 years). Folks, get your game designer in a room and ask to freaking fix the quest tree and make it MUCH more narrow. Also, focus more on the storyline, not adding more and more stuff, but really having some discipline to have LESS.This could have been a good game. But unfortunately it is not. Who knew that you can have too much of everything! Individually all elements kinda make sense. If you'd just have much less of this vast openness without any clear narrative vector. Don't make Elder Scrolls from Baldur's Gate. It was always much more linear and story driven and that was the beauty of it.

_childDocuments_.review: You will not see another game like this in a long -LONG- while, if ever again. From the very beginning the dialogue, characters, voice acting, the writing, everything will pull you in and make you actually feel something towards the end. The game is choke full of content. There's just so much stuff for you to see and do and you're free to go through the whole, entire game any way you'd like. No one set path, evil options are evil because of actual reasons and not just because of "Ho ho! I'm such a twit!" although you can play like that too if you want.There are surprises around every corner and each of the three acts of the game will leave you reeling because of how the plot gets thicker and thicker and new revelations are brought out into the open. It made me grip my seat more than in one occasion for sure.I have nothing but praise for Baldur's Gate 3. It seriously over delivered and exceeded all my expectations when it comes to what a good, oldfashioned roleplaying game should be like. It is actually very difficult to find anything bad to say about this roller coaster of an experience and the 150 hours I spent playing my character through the story never felt like I was just doing stuff because I had to.It even had an ending that was exactly what I wanted from the very first hour when I started playing. It is absolutely insane to think the game actually had an ending that did the exact thing I was planning on doing from the very beginning! Truly marvelous stuff!If there's something I could criticize the game about. I don't think the character creation is particularly strong. I don't meant the classes you pick, but the visual aspect of your character. I was wishing for more face options, more horn styles for the dragonborn, more normal looking hair instead of these endless frilly barber-cuts and many other things like that.While there's plenty to change when it comes to colour options and the like, and we even got those buff body types everybody was asking at one point, but even after then I still think there were too little choices to be made.Naturally the game also has a lorry-load of bugs and odd things that most likely will cause issues along the way, but nothing truly game breaking ever came my way. Patches will fix these with time.Now that I've finally gotten through this... spectacle of a game, I can put it aside for a while, wait for those patches and then dive in again on another character and see what a goody-two-shoes playthrough brings with it in contrast to my first playthrough.TL;DR: The game deserves all the praise it gets. Truly a once in a life time experience with nothing like it on the market. Gripping story, amazing writing, stellar cast! Worth the money, the wait and most certainly worth the time commitment.I can't say it better than: I LOVE THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: Only 8 hours in and I'm loving it.BG3 fans, beware though, if you're expecting a remastered BG1/2 you will be sorely disappointed. This is Larian's version of Baldur's Gate and it is therefore very similar to Divinity. If you like DnD5e you will LOVE this game.If you like any Divinity game you will LOVE this game.If you like BG1/2 you MIGHT love this game.Edit after 490 hours more:As much as the game is not entirely like the original Baldur's Gates, the amount of easter eggs and similarities (most of which because they're all part of the same canon continuity of the Forgotten Realm) make this game thoroughly enjoyable for OG fans of D&D, FR series and Baldur's Gate alike. So I would change the "MIGHT" for a "MOST LIKELY". The replayability is top tier. There is so much content to be explored that on my most recent run I still found at least 3-4 entirely new cutscenes and interactions. The playability is also top tier. While it might be hard to get into for people not used to D&D or Turn-Based RPGs, the combat is simple enough as long as you're willing to read spells or simply click stuff and see what happens. In explore difficulty this is specially true since combat is a lot more forgiving and you can get away with the most basic spells without having to play optimally or tactically even and simply enjoy the adventure.The story is so well developed that it got me really into Forgotten Realms just to learn more about this universe that I hadn't truly explored before. I purchased Evermeet: Island of Elves and I plan on reading the series in chronological order, I'm excited about that.All-in-all this game deserved the GOTY award hands-down.Thank you Larian for making this fantastic game!

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate as a series has stood as the quintessential CRPG: you assume the role of a character as part of a larger story, the story shifts and adjusts for the choices you make, the core gameplay is based around pitting your carefully-built party against the myriad encounters and set pieces, and by the end of the experience, you've formed a deep connection with the world for one reason or another. Baldur's Gate 3 stands as a testament to not just this, but to the developer team who brought this project to life through multiple hurdles and challenges during its life cycle. To see this game released in the current climate of games-as-a-service and incomplete packages with predatory monetization practices is monumental. The core gameplay is based around managing your party using an engine based around Dungeons and Dragon's 5th edition rules - you have stats six stats that govern your ability to interface with the world (strength, dexterity, constitution, wisdom, intelligence, and charisma), certain classes favor the use of some stats over others (e.g. Barbarians favoring strength and constitution while Wizards favoring intelligence above all), and your ability to progress from levels 1-12 is based on how well you can build a party to cover individual shortfalls in order to overcome the world's challenges. Experience to level up is based on the enemies you defeat, exploration, and completing quests, though you may be left wondering why the level cap wasn't higher with the way you can hit the experience cap midway through Act 3 of the game's 4 act structure especially when 5th edition has a level cap of 20. The story is very self-contained: while there are references to (and even characters from) previous games, you do not need knowledge of the previous Baldur's Gate entries to enjoy what's put in front of you. There is a minimum level of buy-in required: you are in a medieval fantasy world where magic is prevalent, gods are real and can interface with mortals, and different planes of existence can be traveled to using magical means, but even so, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone. From those who have no idea what a "role playing game" is to fellow forever dungeon masters well-versed in the lore of the Sword Coast, everyone will find something to enjoy in a 75-100 hr epic.Having played Divinity: Original Sin 1 and 2, I am eagerly looking forward to the next project Larian Studios has to offer, whether it is a campaign editor like DOS2, DLC for BG3, or a new game entirely. At the time of writing this, I've earned 30 of the 53 achievements on a single playthrough, but after running through over 100 hours on one character alone, I feel as though I will need to take some time before I start another character to pursue a second playthrough by myself especially if I am not playing with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Dungeons and Dragons since I was ten, introduced to the game by my old fashioned geek father. I've played quite a few other TTRPGS through my life-- Pathfinder, Lancer, World of Darkness, and some others. I've also played a whole hecking lot of video game adaptions of TTRPGs. This one is hands down the only one that actually feels like playing real in-person DND as well as the only one that manages to truly convey the curiosity and excitement of a tabletop game. PROS: -The story line is truly one of the most creative and cool I've ever seen, hands down. The opening cinematic blew me away. -This was made by people who are genuinely passionate about every inch of the game and the setting. It shows.-One of the deepest games I've ever seen. There is so much content that can be found by a little bit of creativity and non-linear thinking. Often when playing a game you can safely assume that most things aren't implemented even if they would be cool. This game? Go ahead. Talk to that corpse. Talk to the squirrels. Turn into a cat and sneak around. Throw a health potion. Throw your friend! Why not, it will probably work! I'm continuously shocked by how far the mechanics go and how much freedom the game gives you. Creativity in this game is real. -The companions are very interesting and the voice acting is A+. I love how real they are and how they react so uniquely. These are not easy companions-- they will challenge you and do require some thinking. -The love for player characters! Everyone gets to make their own character and even PCs can even talk to each other. Very lovely-Overall just wonderful attention to detail and visual polish. -Every update and every class added makes the game's quality and fun increase exponentially. I would have been happy with the base game classes, but I'm so glad they added more. This game continuously challenges me to raise my expectations. -The character creation is simple but very good! I love all of the new content that has been added over time and look forward on what's to come. Suggestions for improvement for the devs/CONS:-Oh god, the bugs and the lag. The most frequent bugs are visual during cutscenes, but especially during online play some players get stuck on black screens or lag forces us all to reboot. Some builds as the beta has gone have been more stable than others. The current one is pretty shaky.-WHY oh WHY do all of the loading screens spoil so much of the story?! Please remove those or have them unlockable only after getting the character to spill their secret. The spoilers are one of the strangest choices I've ever seen, especially how long you have to stare at those spoilers during the long load times.-During the optional conversations between player characters, please add in a cutscene that makes it clear which character is speaking. Often it is me and my sister yelling "PAY ATTENTION! CHOOSE PLEASE!" Not knowing who is speaking makes those very confusing and also detracts from the character moment. -bring back the impact noise when you hit Astarion. I adore him, he's easily my favorite character... but elbowing him in the nose with some oomph brings me true joy. -I am personally not a fan of Gayle's "upkeep" requirements.... but I am willing to hear the game out on it.The highest compliment I can pay to this game is to tell everyone that my family and I crashed or had such bad lag that we restarted seven times (some of that may have been due to my own internet lagging issues, not even the game's fault). This is a compliment because we loved playing it so much and didn't want to stop SO BADLY that we kept trying over and over until the game and my internet started cooperating.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of high-fantasy but this game really is that good. Great writing, awesome voice-acting, Motion-capped cutscenes and the new persuasion system (deception, intimidation, persuasion) make it so I want to pay attention despite the high-fantasy setting not really being my thing (western-post apocalyptic, gothic-lovecraftian and cyberpunk are my go-to's).Obviously I haven't played the full game yet but so far the last time I played a CRPG with this much depth was Fallout New Vegas. I have also played some turn-based games before (not a ton, but enough to comment) and this blows them all out of the water.One thing that really makes the combat stand out in this game is the way it combines typical stat-based gameplay with Immersive-sim elements. If you want to win a fight the normal way, then you absolutely can, as long as your stats and skills are up to par. But if they're not up to par, there is almost always a way to work the fight into your favor, if you are creative enough (environmental-interactivity is insane).And if you enjoy playing a rogue like me, stealth in this game is far more consistently viable than it was in Divinity. That's partially because the stealth mechanics are more in-depth now, but its also partly because now everyone has less hit-points, so it is (usually) possible to one-hit an enemy from behind.  Last improvement I noticed in combat was that it moves much faster now when playing with other people. Due to the new ruleset (I assume) it is often possible for multiple players to move at once.

_childDocuments_.review: Baldur's Gate 3 is being touted as game of the year for 2023 and those claims are completely justified. It is a typical RPG adventure quest fighting game set in a high fantasy medieval setting. It's not an unchartered genre, but the way Baldur's Gate tells its story is entertaining and memorable. The story line of the game entices you right from the start and holds your attention throughout the progression of the game. There's a lot to praise Larian for because the graphic design, the plot, the combat design, the diverse character builds, the origin character story lines, the music score, the absence of micro-transactions, the freedom of choice, the modding capabilities and the ability to play co-op with friends are all aspects of the game I enjoy. Not to mention how receptive the developers over at Larian have been towards constructive criticism, Many of the patches take note of player feedback and promptly address player concerns, wants and needs. If other game companies ran their games the way Larian runs theirs, there might be competition for Game of the Year but right now nearly every person who buys the game have nothing but praise for how well made it is.That being said, it isn't all perfect though. Baldur's Gate 3 is a turn based combat game, so action junkie players may find it to be too "slow and boring" for their tastes. There is also the problem with the camera jankiness; sometimes the camera can go where you don't want it to go or it can get "stuck" at times. Generally double clicking a character's portrait fixes this but it is my biggest gripe about the game. And the other major complaint I have is that the end game isn't nearly as polished as the beginning stages. So in the end game you will see character models clipping through clothing, less variability in dialogue choices, and the occasional bug here and there but as mentioned earlier Larian has been prompt at fixes any bugs players report. As a game it starts off very strong and it isn't until the very end where it starts to falter ever so slightly. But compared to all the other modern games coming out right now that is a very slight fault. It isn't perfect but it is damn near close to being perfect and should you enjoy these types of games or you're on the fence about it, it is a game that you will most likely enjoy and get plenty of hours of enjoyment from.I highly recommend this game and hope it wins game of the year because it deserves the recognition.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that was "The Forever DM" in my real life plays of Dungeons & Dragons I have to say this is so faithful to the 5th Edition of D&D. Characters feel fleshed out and like real life everyone has their own problems and struggles. You can absolutely derail from the main story for the most part and while there is the big overarching story you aren't forced to do it. (Unless you progressed too far into the next act and want to go back but that might be because I'm playing on tactitian not sure.) Overall I'd describe Baldur's Gate 3 as "D&D without needing friends but you can absolutely play with them!"  As far as things I will be critical about are two things. First is while this is a turn based game for larger battles (20+ mobs) AI tends to grind to a halt where the game is pretty much staring at a single mob make up its mind for up to 2 minutes at a time just for it to walk 15 meters and attack with their weapon just to watch the other 12 do relatively the same thing. This does negatively effect my review on this but perhaps a hotfix will optimize large battles better. Maybe they can add an autopass button that will just make everything go until you can do an action or reaction.  Second thing I'd bring up is while the game is amazing on all fronts character creation seems lacking. As a trans person while I was surprised at the genitals options I would rather have better faces and perhaps body sliders. This is more minor than the first issue I had with the game though.8/10 Because large fights really slog for no reason but I look forward to Larion Studios giving bigger companies a reason to shape up.Larion Studios with 400 people on BG3 > BLizz with 9k people on D4.

Like many others, I was pulled in by the romance aspect of the game, and wasn't disappointed. I will note that at least for me, this game had a steep learning curve. I put a lot of time into figuring out what I was doing wrong, what spells/cantrips were most useful, etc. It took a bit to figure out, so I don't think I can say I recommend this game for beginners.  Something extremely important that I neglected to considered before diving in was: Can my computer even process this game? Answer: Barely. I have to run on the lowest graphics and my computer still struggles. I work through it, but I'm sure there's others who haven't been so lucky. _childDocuments_.review: The game has lots of promise but as of late January 2021, has marginally more problems than it has fun.  Incompletable quests, crashes, corrupted save files, bad auto-save feature, and although I love easter eggs in games, it seems many important items are very easy to miss/ignore.  Character pathing is terrible (e.g., walking through fire when there is a clear wide path around it) and the map visualization / zoom is problematic.  I'd recommend waiting until this is a polished game to spend $60US on it.Update post druid release (3-19-21):As another user pointed out, I have certainly played this game "a lot" considering my no recommendation.  I love this genre and style of game, and in this case I'd already spent the $60 AAA title price on it, so I forged ahead.  There is a lot to like in this game and it has a ton of potential to be very fun and highly rated.  My "no" recommendation is (still) based on the fact that there are many game breaking core mechanics that, combined with a bad auto-save feature means you will find yourself getting stuck trying to disarm a trap/pick a lock and then force quit/reload to notice your last save was three and a half hours ago.The introduction of druid is cool.  The combat bear form is very nice, tanky, and makes some encounters that were difficult in my prior playthrough a lot easier, especially with the AOE taunt feature (and increased knowledge of the encounters, to be sure).  I haven't experimented with the other druid variant extensively and while it may be powerful at later levels, with the current level cap still at 4 it's just my conjecture.Provided the development team polishes this game and achieve their vision, this would be a strong "yes/buy" recommendation but at $60, I'd still wait.  I am concerned that some things that worked fine before now break the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So BG3 is universally celebrated and for good reason. The amount of love that everyone involved in this game has put into it during and after its making and release is incredible, and hard to come across anymore in videogames. Hats off to Larian. You can play dress-up, explore the hot singles in your area, and do just about anything you want in the world around you without (many) consequences (there will be consequences, oh god there are consequences). There's no micro-transactions, no ads, no walled-off sections of the game that shake their fingers at you and say "Only if you buy our expansion!" And its replayability is almost incomparable to any modern game.I joined the bandwagon late, but absolutely fell in love with BG3's quirkiness. Yeah, the skin that stretched into infinity and the awfully incorrect rigging (owlbear Halsin talks with his eyes?) is fun. You laugh at that stuff if you're not too stuck up about a game being polished to perfection. Larian is active in its fixes of these issues, anyway. What I had a scare with in my time with BG3 is a bug concerning save files. My game froze one day in Act 2- I was in the builder's guild(?) basement's hallway. I couldn't do anything, my entire PC was frozen. I had to shut it down by the power button, nothing else worked. When I got the game back up, the cloud was giving me trouble. And after I got the game to load, my entire save game was gone and the game treated me like I've just started to play for the first time. This was just a month, maybe two, ago- long past the early access difficulties I wound up reading through when searching for a solution. I did eventually find a way to grab my game files and move them, but it was an intimidating bug to encounter at 1am nevertheless. After the fix for the rest of that playthrough, every time I started it for the day, I got a new camp chest and helpful tips all over again- Collecting four chests on a solo playthrough being pretty good for my organized packrat mentality at least.I still 100% recommend the game to any who have been on the fence. I also strongly urge some caution in your time playing the game if it comes to larger bugs such as the one I experienced. Larian is a great studio, deserving of its praise, and they work hard to ensure the community has a good time with their pride and joy. I feel like I'm going to easily sink another 300 hours into this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 8/10. The first two acts are stellar but the quality takes a nosedive (in the Larian tradition) in the final Act of the game. The story conclusion is poorly written and you are severely railroaded - all your prior decisions throughout the entire game are effectively made to be irrelevant. It will almost certainly be reworked a year or two from now when Larian releases the finished version of the game under a Definitive/Enhanced Edition (given to people who own the game for free, should history repeat). The combat is enjoyable, but not all that challenging even on Tactician game mode. Many of the features advertised are only superficially or partially implemented, and some of the very big ones are not there at all (eg. Upper City and most of the Lower City of Baldur's Gate is not a playable area, which is not what was advertised). The final Act quests, including the Main Story Quest, are extremely buggy and frequently break inexplicably. The final bosses are, for the most part, inferior to the final boss fight of Act 2. There is one stand-out (optional) boss of Act 3 which is probably the best content that the game has to offer, but that aside the rest of the Act is vastly inferior to the preceding content.The companion relationships are mostly superficial. They either don't really want to talk to or connect to the PC, or they wanna ♥♥♥♥ 'em. There's no in between, which is not what was advertised. They do not have their own lives, they don't go out into the world in Act 3 where you can "run into them", or anything like that - again, not what was advertised. They are also extremely buggy, and will spoil things from future events in their dialogue, refer to things that never happened, or sometimes even still be alive after they die in a cutscene, with everyone else thinking they're dead. Their relationship progression flags regularly break which can in turn brick your entire party from that point onwards, making it so that they will have nothing to say to you for the rest of the playthrough.The failure to deliver on advertised features is not something I attribute to malicious behaviours, rather constraints imposed by timelines of production and competition with other big games coming out (eg. Starfield). This game needs another 6-12 months of production on it to be truly complete in the way that they sold it to us. Once the outstanding issues with companions are fixed, and once Act 3 is made release-ready, and the story ending is rewritten, this game will be a 9.5/10. In the meantime, if people want to sink a hundred hours or more into 2-3 playthroughs of a generally fun game, they should pick it up. The game deserves praise for at least the attempt being made and the commercial model on which it operates.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by saying that I love Larian as a developer, and continue to do so. I still eagerly await news of whatever project they tackle next. I'm not happy to downvote this game, but I must judge it based on my personal enjoyment and whether I would recommend it to others because of that. I'll try and explain why my decision is what it is.I'll start with what I like: I think in terms of graphics and overall presentation, the game is a home run. It's beautiful to look at and is, by all accounts, a massive leap forward from DOS2. The more dynamic camera during dialogue also brings the conversations much more to life than in the previous games. I would kill for DOS2 to get this kind of facelift.And that's kind of it, sadly. I don't want to say that the story or the writing is bad, because it isn't. But I struggle to care for it, and that's no surprise either. I don't like Faerun, and I knew going in that I wouldn't really be interested in whatever story Faerun has to tell. That's fine. I don't really care about Rivellon either. I'm here because DOS1 and 2 provided such a fantastic coop CRPG experience in terms of gameplay that I just cannot get elsewhere. The story just kind of happens and I am largely indifferent to it. I'm perfectly fine with that.So here's my beef with the game: First, the dialogue system feels especially bad in this one, mechanically. I really hate that only the initiating character is relevant for the vast majority of them because it would often make sense to include other party members at specific junctures (often for skill checks, but maybe because their character would have something compelling to add, like a unique class option). The more dialogues I went through, the more it bothered me. It's even worse in coop, where you don't even see the other players' characters be physically present during the dialogue, let alone give your fellow players an opportunity to chime in. It's clunky and unsatisfying, and makes me feel like I am missing out on options every time. It also fails to create any sense of being, you know, a party - something I thought was core to the D&D experience.The game also has some quality of life issues that, while easily forgivable in a more enjoyable game, do provide regular minor problems. The inventory isn't the most fun to operate (although I appreciate the search function even if it's very basic). I have trouble realizing when someone else is in a dialogue so I can listen in - I always felt like it was more notable in DOS1 and 2, never struggled so much with that before. Characters sometimes do really stupid stuff or path in unexpected ways. None of this is game breaking but it's worth pointing out.I actually cannot speak too much about bugs (game breaking or otherwise). I've seen them, of course, but none of them were too bad or enough to deter me from playing or even really hinder me from having fun (aside from my last session where a Disarm move actually DELETED my rare and powerful weapon from the game). I think much of that can be attributed to the fact that I never saw Act 3. I heard it gets much worse in the final act, so that's unfortunate. I, however, gave up partway through Act 2 out of sheer frustration.Which leads me to the principal source of said frustration, and the reason why BG3, ultimately, gets my downvote: D&D. I'll be frank here and say that I genuinely believe D&D 5e is a terrible system, both on the table and even more so in a video game. I knew this going in, but I wanted to give Larian the benefit of the doubt. I have immense trust in them and figured, devs who made such amazing games before would surely find ways to make a game based on D&D fun and playable. I was wrong.Here's what gets me:1) Restrictive Action SystemI just don't see the point behind an arbitrary and limited main action / bonus action system. We already had a perfectly granular and working system in action points from the previous games. I know that this is how it works in D&D - my point is, it's not good. I also understand that action points would be a mess to track on a table (probably), but this isn't a tabletop. It's a video game. And it's not a good video game mechanic.2) ConcentrationIt really limits the utility of a lot of spells because characters cannot have more than one concentration spell active at a time, leading to less choice during turns and a higher likelihood of just casting the same instant attack abilities repeatedly. Concentration breaking / not breaking is also a very unfulfilling, random and thus frustrating experience both when trying to break an enemy, or having your own broken. More on pass / fail mechanics later.3) Vancian MagicI don't know how else to put it: I hate Vancian magic (or whatever variant thereof 5e uses, I've been told this isn't "true" Vancian magic anymore). Rationing limited spell slots is reductive and boring. A good combat system should encourage you to use all the fun tools you have, not make you dread having to use them and make you feel bad afterwards for having done so because it means going back to do a long rest. Coming from the Original Sin games where varied ability usage and pumping your most enjoyable spells every fight is the norm, this feels incredibly oppressive and boring. I am of the belief that powerful abilities should be limited in their use through build-up mechanics (i.e. some kind of system that makes you have to build up to unleashing your strongest spells) as opposed to tear-down mechanics (such as here, where you have all your power available, but using them loses them).4) Limited BuildsWith a mere 12 levels and rather strict level-up bonuses on every class, the possibilities for builds feel quite limited. I don't want to rag too harshly on this because, in my limited playtime and exposure to 5e, I felt that there was "enough" freedom to do a bit of building, but I can easily see how I'd have exhausted the system once I played each class once. Multiclassing is often a harsh tradeoff that's only worth it in specific circumstances I find. For the most part, you'd be well served just monoclassing and picking whatever flavor of subclass serves your fantasy. I've seen much better class systems in other games (for example classless like in the Original Sin games, or the much more freeform class mixing like in Xenoblade Chronicles 3).5) Binary Success / Fail Mechanics (ergo everything involving a D20)I hate these mechanics in any game, any system. Failing a skill check and just NOT doing the thing you wanted to do, is frustrating and boring. Wasting an action on NOT doing anything to the enemy and effectively skipping your own turn is frustrating and boring. Hitting an enemy only for them to save against the debuff is frustrating and boring. D&D is full of pass / fail nonsense and I have zero tolerance or patience for it. I hate hit chances in any game (looking at you XCOM). BG3 is filled to the brim with them and it only gets worse with every D20 I roll. I have nothing but disdain for that die because it singlehandedly ruins BG3 for me.And those are my feelings on BG3. It genuinely makes me sad because, as said, I really like Larian, and I think that there's a really fun campaign in here. Unfortunately, a problematic dialogue system and, above all else, D&D drags it down and makes it an absolute pain to play. If only it were possible to rip out the entire engine and insert the gameplay of DOS2 into this, I wouldn't be writing this - I'd be busy playing. Alas, that's just not something I can have. I'll keep my eyes peeled on any overhaul mods that might come out in a year or so, see how much they can salvage, if anything.I'm happy for the success Larian is enjoying and I pray that they take their profits and go back to doing what they're good at, unburdened by the yoke of a terrible TTRPG system.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been such a long time since a game has completely captured my heart and imagination.  Not since the original Baldur's Gate (1 and 2) series, and more recently the Mass Effect Trilogy, have I become so invested in the lives and stories of my character and companions.   I admit, I was a bit doubtful when I first heard that they would be making a third Baldur's Gate, and it wasn't going to be done by BioWare/Black Isle.   Larian has demolished all my expectations and provided me and countless others with the most epic, most endearing, most enjoyable RPG since the early 2000s.   I laughed, I cried, I fell hopelessly in love...and I saved the world in the most epic fashion!  There is seriously nothing else like this currently on the market as far as quality voice acting, quality writing, quality story-telling, character development... Larian continues to crank out additional content:  not just bugfixes, but they are actually enhancing the gameplay, as well as expanding on the already magnificent story to give players "closure" and satisfying story arcs to truly flesh out their characters and their companions.  I could go on and on about what a masterpiece this game truly is, or you could just go ahead and experience it for yourself.  I promise you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Outrageously good. Take it with a grain of salt since I’m not even close to the end and I didn’t play early access, but the game seems to keep expanding in ways that leave me wondering how huge it must be, both in terms of what you see in a single playthrough and the possibilities for alternate playthroughs. The level of reactance to player decisions is second only in CRPGs to Disco Elysium, a game with a single developer-designed player character in a much smaller setting. (Absolutely no shade to DE either, it and BG3 represent the peak of what you can do with RPGs in this era, perfect apples and oranges.)A few minor graphical bugs and camera hitches don’t stop BG3 from being the obvious game of the year. If it finishes as well as it’s gone, it should be an easy addition to the canon of all time great games.Plus it’s only ♥♥♥♥♥♥’ 60 bucks with no obnoxious DLC or roadmap, and the developer is also the publisher. Go mow your grandma’s lawn a few times if you can’t afford that. It’s worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a great rendition of 5e D&D, but if you go in expecting it to play like the tabletop version, you'll be sorely disappointed.As an Early Access, there are bugs to be found. I've seen at least 1 T-pose during animation transitions, at least 1 enemy spaghettify while dying, and mouths not move during first lines of dialogue.That being said, I think the game is looking great, music sounds awesome, and the combat, while not a direct mirror of all the rules in D&D (e.g. Mirror Image gives + 3 AC per image up, Fire Bolt's damage is 1d6, can do bonus action and action leveled spell), is faithful to the system as it can be, given the confines of the game. A lot of "old-time BG fans" will likely complain about the game not being RTwP combat, but to be honest, turn based feels pretty good. Honestly, take off your nostalgia glasses and look at the game for what it is: Larian's interpretation and vision of Baldur's Gate in the 5e ruleset, and you'll see a jewel that looks beautiful, even before its final cut and polish.

_childDocuments_.review: The inclusive and diverse nature of this game provides a fully imaginative story, world building, and game play. You have more than enough options to live your fantasy life within this expansive world. The biggest downside so far was the character creation. Don't get me wrong, they're diverse and inclusive in those areas too but I wish they gave more facial, body, and hair presets. I am very heavy on character creation and I can make do but I have been browsing nexus to fully live *my* fantasy. - Don't take my full word on this either, I am a huge hater on presets either way. Overall, love this game!Edit: I finally finished the game after all of the patches and updates that I have been waiting for. I've put countless hours into this game and I gotta say...it was worth every penny. There's a lot of controversy over the ending but I think with all of the decisions I made with my last playthrough, the ending was amazing. This game made me smile countless times and even made me cry a few times. I loved the story so much. Can't wait to see any DLC released and/or any new projects to come. 10/10 one of my top favorite games.
