_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is definitely a mixed a bag, I enjoyed it as much as I found it infuriating at times, as an artist myself I appreciate the work that went into the world, props, character design but not so much in the gameplay department, level designs were too simple at times and hence it gets repetitive later on, don't get me wrong I did enjoy my short time with it but wouldn't recommend it outside of the really pretty world building (bonus points for a pretty good UI design), I got it at a discount so I won't complain much.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a third-person , story driven, action-adventure title that tells the story of Rani and Becks, best friends and partners who scavenge the galaxy in a old spaceship called the Dust Bunny. You land on a planet that is covered in gunk and through exploring as Rani you come to discover how the planet came to ruin and what happened to its peoples. Game play has some light combat, puzzle solving and exploration. The game is done in a linear style with environments broken up into different areas. The artwork is beautiful and I had no real problems with the game play itself. I had no crashes, no real game breaking bugs or issues and it ran well on a ultra widescreen display. I would suggest getting this game on sale. I knew I would enjoy it as I previously played it on Xbox when it hit gamepass. However the whole game is only about 5-6 hours of play time on average. Maybe up to 8 hours depending on the player. I am 3 hours in and at the end area at this point. Maybe another hour or two at most to finish it. There is no dlc and it is a complete game. It is a fun, friendship filled game that at its heart shows the consequences of continuing to harm the planet. I do recommend it but on sale.  💖🌎

_childDocuments_.review: An ascetically beautiful game with a great story. It's not as adventures in the sense that you won't battle a bunch of gunk-monsters, but that's fine for the type of game it is.I was here for what the narrative conveyed, as it was a heartfelt and endearing experience which you can see with each character dialogue exchange. There was a lot of humor to bring some levity to the situation and a lot of truth bubbled up on a meta level.I also appreciate how much real science was implemented to heighten the sci-fi of it all, which underlying environmental message hit perfectly for what the story was displaying and it wasn't too overbearing or preachy. Everything said with the lore in-game to the real world elements that we can ascribe in our own world was excellent and landed flawlessly.I loved the design of the gear and characters, despite the humans having 4 fingers which caught me off guard, it all still worked well for me. CuRT having a little tie and baseball hat was fun. The fact that one of Rani's pieces of gear looked like a repurposed Gameboy really worked well for the nostalgia feels. Becks design fit perfectly for who she was in this universe.I think if the right people play the game they'll enjoy it and have fun with it. It's not very hard to beat or anything, and there are a few bugs, but it doesn't break the game or the experience in any way. I loved it for what it is, and I hope those who give it a try have fun while playing and exploring in the world of Gunk.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).The Gunk is a third person adventure game set in space where you play the role of a bankrupt team of adventurers in search of riches on an alien planet. The gameplay mixes exploration, resource collections, platforming, simple combat and puzzle solving.The story revolves around finding out why there is this weird “gunk” material all over the planet and what’s causing it. Along the way new things about the planet are discovered and the friendship between the main characters is tested.The alien planets and the different game zones look very good and mostly distinct from one another. You’ll search and explore jungles, caves, ruins and “factories” and each of these areas look different and have different plants, features and challenges. The characters have a unique look similar to fantasy dwarves and interesting details on their clothing and equipment. The light and particle effects also look good, as well as the weapon effects and the animations that make the “gunk” seem alive.The enemies are completely different from each other in looks and the way they attack you, but unfortunately there are only three different types of enemies.The game also offers very competent voice acting, but there are very few characters and NPCs in the game. The OST is also very good, especially the main theme, that you can listen to .The gameplay is accessible for all players, neither the combat nor the puzzle or exploration is too hard to figure out. The types of puzzles are limited and they only get slightly more challenging on the last levels and the combat is never too hard as the enemies are easy to kill and it gets even easier as you unlock upgrades for your gear. To unlock these upgrades you need to explore and scan elements from the planet like minerals, plants and fungus, and fill an experience bar that will unlock the next upgrade. Another important part of the game is getting resources, and if you want to 100% the game you need to be through, since you’ll need a lot of them to unlock every upgrade. I ran short of stone and had to go back to a previous game zone and get some I left behind.Something that can get tiresome is removing gunk as in some zones that is a lot of it, so I suggest getting the upgrades for your “vacuum cleaner” as soon as possible to make it faster. Exploring can also be faster if you get the running upgrade right at the beginning of the game.  17 Achievements. 6 hours on my own, without a guide. Easy. Medium. The achievements related to the monsters are missable, but you can make manual saves and return to the required levels and replay them, which is necessary because the monsters don’t respawn. The Take Charge it's easier to get on the . As mentioned you also need to be thorough with the exploration to get the “All in” and “Space Archaeologist”, but you also can go back to  previous levels.  The Gunk is a great third person adventure game with accessible puzzles and combat, set in a vibrant alien world that is fun to explore and great to look at, and the voice narration and music is also great. On the negative side, removing gunk can get tiresome and the variety of enemies and types of puzzles is very limited.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely pretty to look at, but at the end of the day, there just wasn't enough game. I don't mean in terms of time it will take you to beat it, a metric I mostly find useless at best, but in terms of its own mechanical evolution. Within its general genre, oftentimes a game will expand upon itself with regard to the complexity and difficulty of the tasks you're asked to complete. This really isn't the case here, or if it is, the lede was deeply buried as I reached no real mechanical growth in about 4 hours. It feels like an ASMR experience tied to some very high quality art, and billed as an adventure game. The story as far as I got was pretty thin, predictable and tired; the characters shockingly poorly-voiced and unlikable. Unfortunately not worth the investment of time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in a bundle and was decently surprised. Took around 5 hours to beat and get most achievements. Feels like the right amount of time to play and did not overstay its welcome The game is basically a "cleaning" game with a mix of platforming and light combat. For majority of the game, it was pretty zen because there is no enemies or danger. However, you later meet some enemies then get access to a pulse gun and lure bomb. Story is basically that the two protagonists are stranded on an unknown planet and discover "gunk" related to a civilization that was there before them - nothing really mindblowing+ The best part of this game: the GORGEOUS ENVIRONMENT! Was genuinely surprised with the amount of times I had to take a pause (and screenshot) of the surroundings.+ Exploration is rewarded by materials you can use to upgrade your equipment which means that there are no "collectibles". If you wish to blaze through the game, you are not really punished by missing out on hidden collectibles.+ Pretty simple gameplay and can be relaxing for the most part+ One of the characters is wearing crocs!- Encountered a few bugs (forever falling off an edge, invisible elevator, etc) ~ nothing too bad- The bickering of the two protagonist is pretty annoying- story is pretty forgettable, cutscene animation can be jankyAll in all, a welcome surprise and a good hidden gem. _childDocuments_.review: Developed by , who previously presented us with the popular  series, finally release The Gunk on Steam. A title already available on Microsoft's Game Pass, that surely deserves our attention. An untamed and colorful journey to find the truth about a lost alien civilization.Rani and Beck are two space scavengers living by whatever job they can pull off while traversing the vast space. We play as Rani, a natural born explorer who always seeks to understand the truth, and is clearly fascinated by history. On the other hand, Beck does her best to keep the ship flying on a low and tight budget. Their lives change forever after arriving at an unknown planet completely off the grid. Originally, they wanted to harvest the planet's energy, but as the game progresses, it's obvious there is something else at play here. Seems this long forgotten place has a rich architecture, and there's where the game really shines. You'll uncover the planet's long lost history and understand the dilemma of its civilization. The story is far from complex or extremely intense, but suits quite well within the main narrative, and tests the friendship of the protagonists as new events arise. A simple, but at the same time emotional light journey, surrounded with beautiful exotic locations. Interaction between Rani and Beck through the radio are smartly done, usually with bits of humor and elegantly put together. This delivers some insight on their individual past, while we learn more about their history together. delivers an exploring third person adventure where players will scan the environment with Rani's powerful arm tool, as well as clean up the gunk to reveal beautiful green sceneries, filled with vibrant vegetation and alien resources that once harvested, will allow you to install new upgrades. These consist of a powerful laser gun mod, running speed, increased health, and plenty more useful mods.Gameplay wise, it's very simple but pleasant. Explore and complete minimalistic puzzles to unlock passage ways to proceed, while always gathering materials. Level design receives an easy A+ grade from me, with impressive geometry placement and really high fun value. There's even some really smart shortcuts to unlock. The game is not open world, but delivers some connected hub areas. There is a teleport system to quickly travel to the desired location, which is handy.Traversing each area feels really good and some mechanics like using plants as bridges or stairs, are nice to see. Expect some little hidden secret paths and a few less seen areas with some neat loot as well. Overall the level design matches the colorful atmosphere, that blends particularly well in the whole Alien theme.If by any chance you played  on Game Pass, you'll be happy to know this version seems to be updated. Motion Blur can now be removed through in-game option, and already scanned objects will display a red symbol, while not-scanned ones will appear green. This will help those aiming at full completion.Unfortunately, some extra options are not available, such as Field of View, Chromatic Aberration, and others, that can only be activated or removed through config files. Check  for extra help.Which is a shame because the performance looks very solid, with constant 60fps with an RX 580, at 1080p. DX12 mode seems extremely well optimized, and that's always great news for AMD users.Easily a game between 5 to 10 hours, if you're like Rani, a seeker of truth. Less if you aim only at the main goal. Regardless,  is an absolute blast, with impressive exotic visuals, an entertaining campaign and a smooth casual adventure. A relaxing take on the genre, with satisfyingly gameplay and plot.

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: ~6h (probably 4-8 for most people)Graphics are nice, design is consistent. _childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is an extremely forgiving 3D Action Platformer that I could easily see being adapted into a movie. You play as Rani, who, with her “roommate?” Becks, end up nearly stranded on an alien planet. This planet has an intense source of energy that they are hoping to sell to their corporate overlords to settle their debts. With Rani as scout, you quickly discover that the surface is covered in Gunk, some pulsating reddish-black, semi-sentient substance that is attracted to pools of some light bluish-green substance; Gunk drains the area of most life in the process. The removal of the Gunk (by vacuum hand) causes the local flora to spring to life once again. Will Rani be able to track down the source of the energy? Why does Gunk also seem attracted to the energy? The story itself is relatively simple with a moral that is some variation of “environmental exploitation is bad”, with allusions to either oil drilling/refining or industrialization. You have some alien deer as a stand in for nature in the first half of the game that the Gunk impedes or harms. Earth has apparently been ruined by similar events in the game's story (this is brought up at least 3 times). The main antagonist of the game brings up this fact as well in response to your meddling. However, there is no real nuance here, both the antagonist and the tech used to drain the planet of its resources are Obviously Evil (TM) that they must be taken down. The game is short, and setting up anything deeper would require more time.The general loop of the game is “Vacuum Gunk → Vacuum Crafting Materials → Platform to new area → Repeat until Fast Travel point is unlocked to upgrade back at the base.” Any climbable areas are marked with yellow slime or scratches. Backtracking is limited if you are meticulous in your exploration, and the only obligatory backtracking segment plays differently the second time so it is okay. Any jumps over death pits respawn you at a relatively close safe point to try again after a quick fade to black. The only time you can really Game Over is taking damage in a Gunk infested area, and everything that can deal damage has a telegraphed attack or regular attack pattern. You would think that this game was made for young children given its lack of difficulty, but the main characters (Becks especially) curse often. I think there were two F-Bombs during the playthrough (one of which can be clearly heard). Removing Gunk is satisfying the first few times, but overstays its welcome IMO (reinforced in the fact that the game provides 2 upgrades that speed up removal). If the game was longer or its platforming more punishing (non-plaforming terrain is slippery, and some of the jumps are hard to judge; I would have liked the ability to grab any ledge), I'd probably have some more feelings. It is okay for its short runtime. My big criticism is that the game is short for $25. I think I played through it relatively slowly (backtracking through a whole area once to grab some crafting materials I missed), and my play time came out to about 5 ½ hours. The thing is, I don't think the game's systems would hold up if the game was longer. Adding more Gunk removal sections or harder platforming sections would just make the game feel tedious or frustrating. I am interested in a bit more of the lore but adding a new section devoted to it would drag down the story's pacing. The only thing that I would really do is increase the material drops in the third act such that you will more easily have a fully upgraded character by the game's end. As it stands though, this is an alright game to pick up for a sale, as a palate cleanser between more involved/lengthy games. There are however, a few issues that I think need to be addressed:

The controls are intuitive and responsive, ensuring smooth movement and precise interactions.The Gunk introduces players to a captivating and mysterious narrative that gradually unfolds as you progress. The well-developed characters and emotional depth add authenticity, making the quest to save the world more than just an ordinary one.The game offers an exceptional audio experience with meticulously designed sound effects. _childDocuments_.review: While the “The Gunk” is certainly not an old game, it gives off a vibe as though it were from the era of the PS3/X360 — around the 2010 mark. I personally see this as a good thing.Being reductive, the game combines elements of Super Mario Sunshine, a bit of Slime Rancher with a pinch of Wallace and Gromit. Using more traditional terms, this game is a 3D platfomer that utilizes a suction gun for both puzzles and exploration, a variably small amount of resource collection with a unique art style that will stand the test of time.Playing as Rani, her and her partner Becks will land on a planet searching for things to sell, as they are a team of scavengers. Through exploration, Rani will discover there is more to the planet than meets the eye and despite Becks protest, adventure awaits.Played from a third person perspective, Rani will use her suction gun (which she refers to as Pumpkin) to clean up a substance found on the planet referred to as 'Gunk'. As you progress, the Gunk becomes more difficult to suction for various reasons and enemies will appear — what's interesting is that while there are not many enemy types, they all have a unique way of being dealt with. The platforming is not overly challenging, checkpoints are forgiving, and upgrades can be earned through resource collection.It's a shorter game, something I had sought after failing to 'get into' larger titles on a tighter schedule in my 'real life'. It's relatively linear aside from a few branching paths for extra resources. The story is decent, if not traditional. The characters are likable, their banter is humorous. I think it's a fun romp and worth your time. It feels older, as I mentioned, but it's a pseudo-nostalgic sort of old feeling that I can really appreciate. I originally intended to play this on my PC where I have an RTX 3070, so as to see the game's unique visuals in their best representation. But I ended up playing it almost entirely on my Steam Deck. Despite it only running at 30FPS (sometimes lower) at 800p on high, using 22W of the allotted 25W the Steam Deck offers. I found (much like my experience with the Zelda games on Switch) that resolution and frame rate just don't matter to truly enjoy something. While they can certainly offer an arguably “richer” experience, both in visual fidelity and responsiveness — they just aren't something that really affects your overall experience — something I think gaming industry has forgotten and is getting too caught up in.I thought it looked and played great on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really charming adventure game that quickly captures the attention of players with its aesthetically pleasing graphics. _childDocuments_.review: It's a relatively short action-adventure game set on an alien world with a few quirky characters and a lot of black gunk all over the place. Yep, it's an action-adventure with power washer simulator elements, except instead of blowing you suck. Quite literally, actually. I have no idea where our heroine stuffs all that away. Her right hand is magic.Ok, ok, enough with innuendos. There's nothing in the game that deserves those, and the game itself is actually quite fun despite being somewhat short. Don't look at my time; I forgot to close the game, and it was running overnight. There's a lot of jumping over rocky terrain, climbing, and overall exploration, with occasional cleanup episodes whenever you stumble upon yet another pile of black goo with a slow introduction of enemies into the mix. There aren't many, though. There are just two variants, but while working well, combat isn't the main focus of the game, so that's not a big deal. It's more about exploration, cleaning up the mess, and watching alien nature flourish.The exploration part is actually quite decent, but I don't recommend going through the content of later chapters again if you forget to collect some resources in the middle of the chapter since you may end up in a situation where you neither can go forward since one-time thingamajig isn't there nor go back since our heroine is terrible at actually climbing actual rocks without little help from nature. Your only hope will be that there's an auto-save before the point of no return. Thankfully, the game keeps up three of those, so there's likely at least one good.Oh, and since I mentioned collectible resources, there are upgrades for your magic glove to unlock and install. Most of them are completely optional, but they provide very nice QoL features. Especially fast recharge and stun for shooting mode. It might be a bit confusing, but upgrades are unlocked with overall scanning progress instead of scanning specific things, though. So, if you wish to unlock them all, scan everything you can along the way. And if you wish to actually get them all, collect as many resources as you can.Overall, I'd give it a 6.5/10. It isn't anything great, but it's fun, and while there isn't much variety, the game is short enough to end before it gets boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Rani and her crewmate Becks stumble upon an unusual energy spike on a dead planet. Curiosity getting the best of them, Rani heads down to investigate, only to find life on its last legs and something strange, something that looks like it’s smothering anything that tries to grow; Rani calls it what it is – The Gunk. Follow the energy readings and clean up The Gunk to allow life to flourish once again, and hopefully get rich while doing it too! 5-7+ hours to complete, The Gunk is a linear action-adventure nature restoration game with super simple mechanics, easy puzzles and gameplay, and unchallenging enemies. Graphics are beautiful, and for a while I was having a pretty fun time! Rani is very optimistic, while Becks is a pessimist, which made for some interesting back-and-forth dialogue as you explore an alien planet and go on an adventure. However, becks gets more negative as the game goes on and at one point she just straight up becomes hostile and extraordinarily annoying. Despite the angst and the various areas you can softlock yourself into, I was still planning on rating The Gunk positive! However, the ending was abrupt, disappointing and nonsensical. With no spoilers, it made me feel like the entire game I just tried to enjoy was pointless.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a really well-placed adventure about landing on and exploring an unknown planet. You can play it start to finish in 4-5 hours with no guide, but along the way it will get you exploring, hunting, and trying to piece together the world's history.The two main characters are fairly basic, but also decent company.The gameplay is mostly exploring; light puzzling (I can turn this platform to reach this switch); and "cleaning things up". There are a handful of enemy types in the cleaning phases, but in general it's low stress and low difficulty: you're here for the adventure.It was well worth 5 hours of my time, and I recommend it as an adventure you can crack through in an evening or two, having a good time along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: 7h 2/10 1 There is a good achievement guide on  but it says this game has no missable achievements and that isn't the case.  No Yes, "Space Archaeologist " has one missable item. And for "All In" you need to find almost all the resources and I'm not sure if none of those are missable. No No No No No No NoThis review for The Gunk is hard to write. At this moment I feel quite devastated. I did start this game with the idea that none of the achievements are missable, as the guides which I saw before starting said so. So I didn't check out much of the achievements, but I knew I needed a lot of resources and scan a lot of objects, so I paid special attention to those 2 things. And to learn at the end that one item for the achievements where you have to scan everything is missable and just that one I'm missing (the others I managed to mop up) just sucks. I'm also missing resources but couldn't find them while mopping up the other scannable items, so I gave up on that one. But let us go back to how this journey on an unknown planet started for me: I was really hyped for The gunk from the moment I heard about it. It first was Xbox exclusive but I'm glad it now also is available on Steam.  I wasn't disappointed, the game is amazing. I love cleaning up in games and combine that with a Metroidvania and you get a good game in my book. Sometimes the game felt a bit boring, mostly around the "tower" area where there is soo much Gunk, and you don't need to clean it all, but you need to clean a lot to be able to pass through it. For me, this area felt like the least fun area in the game. I enjoyed the look of this game a lot, especially a beautiful animal you meet around the beginning of your journey. the faces of the human characters felt a bit weird though. I can't figure out what felt weird about them, but they just do.  Another negative point is that if you go backtrack in this game, there is one area you can get stuck because you jump in an area where you can't leave and the elevator is at the top where you left it the last time, so no way to get out of that area except for loading an old save file. Gladly the game has multiple autosave files, but I would highly recommend also making a bunch of manual saves on different slots, just in case. Even with those negative points, as a game that doesn't care about achievements I would highly recommend it, it is a fun experience that isn't too long, with a nice story. As an achievement hunter, I would be a bit more reserved for this game, as you need to scan 58 different objects and one of them (Gunk Dripper) is missable. Backtracking to the others is still no fun, especially since this game doesn't have a map or any way to see where you have scannable objects left, or where you have resources left. And those resources are also very tide, you need to almost find them all. what I have read from others is that there are like 2 more metal resources in the game than you need for all the upgrades. If you want to get all the achievements, the best thing might be to play with a video guide next to it that points out all the scannable objects and resources, but that takes a lot of the fun away than just being able to play the game and figure it out yourself without risking it to miss out on achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a meh rating if I could.It's a pretty game and the characters are fun but the game boils down to just another generic platform puzzler. You can upgrade stuff but your upgrade options are drip fed to you so slowly that your choices don't really matter. You've often got the choice between a few upgrades where one is the clear winner in terms of it doing more of the stuff you need and the others are just little tweaks to gameplay that you could take or leave. A bunch of the game is spent collecting collectables which are the currency for these upgrades which means that the act of collecting them feels boring too because the upgrades themselves are boring.If you want a chill, mindless game to run around and do what you're told and not have to make choices with some very light kinda clunky combat then this is your game. _childDocuments_.review: A genuinely beautiful game and one of the nicest looking games I've played in a while. The game play is simple action platforming with puzzle elements - though nothing complicated. The vacuum mechanic is fun and slurping up gunk to beautify the world is satisfying. It also gives key areas two versions of the room, firstly doing combat and clean up in the dirty version, then puzzle platforming in the clean version. The platforming also feels SO smooth and movement is really good, reminiscent of Ratchet and Clank but less floaty.The game has few downsides but they are sizeable. The game is super short and I completed it twice in one day just to 100% the achievements. There's almost no challenge either since it was a cake walk from start to finish. Also the story is a bit wonky, both from the characters maybegay relationship to the overarching story itself, as you can feel the moment where the studio realised they needed to ship the game and took a sharp turn towards tying everything off.Without spoiling, it felt like just as the game was about to open up by hinting at a much larger sprawling world with more to do, it suddenly skips to the end level. That's the most disappointing part of the game - there's so much potential that goes unexplored. I was hoping for more areas, biomes, puzzles, challenge, ways to use the vacuum, gunk towers, ways to interact with enemies... Sadly you experience most of the game in the first 20 minutes and it doesn't evolve far beyond that.There's a lot of unrealised potential here and that's a shame but you do get a short sweet adventure game that's worth a play if only to encourage a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a very well made, technically proficient game with excellent controls and short loading times, etc. The story is a fitting allegory for our current environmental crisis that is on the verge of spiraling out of control if it hasn't already. The two main characters, both women, have a nice chemistry and their dialogue provides just the right amount of humor, insight and tension. The Gunk is more about exploration and puzzles than it is about combat, which is exactly what some of us are looking for in a game. I've said this before in my reviews but every gamer is different and not all of us are looking for combat on the level of "Souls," or whatever. Personally, after about 8 or 10 deaths in the course of a single boss fight, I'm getting ready to hang it up, lol. Unless I'm extremely invested in and interested in the story and it's characters...I'm thinking of something like "Hellblade," I guess...I don't care for dying 65 times just in order to advance the game to the next epic battle which is, of course, right around the very next corner. But it all depends on your given personality  and hand eye coordination, etc. So if you don't mind a more laid back experience, "The Gunk," might be a perfect game for you. I wouldn't call the story great but it definitely qualifies as good and we would all do well to heed the moral of the story. The world building/environments are all fascinating and make you look forward to seeing what's in the next area of the game. The one complaint, as many others have pointed out, is the price tag is a bit on the high side. But if you can hold out for a sale price of, say,  $20, I think you can't go wrong here. (As long as you're more of the type of gamer that I described above.)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like giving negative reviews to games, specially to the developers of a series/universe I like so much, that is SteamWorld, but damn, how am I glad I finished this already. In no way I can recommend it. Halfway through, it felt like playing an internet argument.The game models and environments are beautiful and that's the only good thing about it.It's a linear, 'adventure-platformer' mix, in the likes of Uncharted, except it has no action or puzzles, whatsoever.Although the OST fits the atmosphere, it has no identity and it's pretty forgetful. Not something I would hear outside of the game.Gameplay is repetitive and linear: You follow a single road (even when it bifurcates, you need to go through both roads to progress) and very so often needs to clear the gunk to proceed. Also, it holds your hand all the way through, either through yellow paint or through dialogue.There's a scan system, which is similar to Metroid Prime's, yet it adds absolutely nothing of useful to the gameplay or the lore. Many of the "comments" of the analysis are disposable, pretty much like those open-world games which you can gather documents, books and etc.. But, unlike these games, The Gunk unlocks upgrades based on the number of scans you have... I don't mind that, but at least the analysis should've been somewhat useful...It has combat, but it's ridiculously bad. You basically absorb small enemies with the glove and throw them back at one another (or at the ground/wall so they get squished). There are a total of 3 enemies (4, if you count the gunk, which is basically an environmental hazard you need to absorb): a small flea-like one that gets close and jumps at you, a turret-like one that occasionally spits a rock of some sorts at you and that you need to either pull it off the ground or throw a bomb-like plant onto it (bombs in the fighting area happens 2 or 3 times), and a big one that only charges at you (you only fight 3 or 4 of it throughout the whole game) and you have to lead it to a wall so it's gets stunned so you can then absorb the core on its back...Speaking of dialogue, my god, how awful it is. It's badly written and cliched, not to mention halfway through the "we're an inseparable team" couple starts to argue out of nowhere bc protag dives head-first into saving the world. And the antagonist? Well. It's an alien known as "the Gardener" that dislikes wilderness and also hates humans bc they destroyed their home planet, yet, he's doing exactly the same thing... Needless to say, characters are very forgettable (gladly) and annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Gunk

_childDocuments_.review: A four hour runtime for nearly 100% completion is not the best look for most video games. For Image & Form Games' The Gunk, however, it was just enough time. I don't mean that as harsh criticism, nor do I want to impress that the game was masterfully crafted. The Gunk sits somewhere in the middle: it is visually splendid with clunky controls and an obvious but fun plot that lasts just long enough to feel worthwhile before getting boring or tedious.The Gunk is an action platformer, set in the far future where humans are trawling through space. What exactly humanity's future society is like is left mostly up to your own imagination. What we see are two humans and their robot on a leased ship searching for materials to sell and make ends meet. They land on a planet they assume to be uninhabitable and quickly learn that it both contains life, and has a massive pollution problem. Cue plot as plucky do-gooder scavenger protagonist Rani decides to cleanse the planet of "the gunk" with her vacuum arm prosthetic. Basic setup, clear from the get-go what the overarching plot is going to be.The gameplay is very basic. You run, you jump, you vacuum up resources with your robot-arm (which Rani lovingly calls "Pumpkin" due it is size and color). When you clean up all of the gunk in an area, the landscape blooms beautifully as plant and insect life returns to the world in an explosion of what feels like sci-fi nature magic. There are a handful of combat sequences, but really its the same as the rest of the game: vacuum things up and platform around. By the end of the game the simple and few game mechanics start to get stale, but by that point the game is basically over so you may as well keep going. It's a feel-good romp through an alien world, though a tightly linear one with little room for exploration.Not that there is a lot to explore. The game has roughly 8 different zones that all lead one into the other. This game is by no means a Banjo-Kazooie, Jak and Daxter, Gex, what have you. There are no collectibles to uncover, secrets or puzzles to find, and essentially no backtracking to be done. Once you've ran through a zone once, you really have no reason to go back unless you happened to miss a resource for an upgrade to your arm (which I will get into in the next paragraph). The game is short and sweet, and it doesn't want to waste any of your time with frivolties other games litter themselves with to pad gametime. That sounds meaner than I intend it, but let's be real, as fun as running around grabbing collectibles can be, it's still just padding.Now about those upgrades. There's almost no point. The game initially gives you the impression that you'd be finding resources for a variety of upgrades to help you on your path or unlock secret areas. But again, there's basically no secrets, no backtracking, so the upgrades aren't for that. Honestly the upgrades felt pointless. For the story you are required to get at least one or two upgrades, but all the rest didn't feel like they added anything. One of them added the ability to sprint, but it is by far one of the worst sprint mechanics in any game I've played. It doesn't even keep momentum when you jump, which is part of the whole reason to include sprinting as a mechanic. The other upgrades are basic, like a shorter charge time for the arm's electric shot, or the ability to revive if you get downed. Which could be helpful, but the game is also incredibly easiy and the AI of the few enemies you encounter are so pitiful that getting downed would have to be a mercy on a strangely sympathetic player's part. The whole upgrade system could have just been scrapped, but I guess they had to maybe shoehorn it in so that, while cleaning up gunk, you can also gather resources and lend a little more credence to this whole "we need resources to sell for money to pay off our ship loan" bit that the game mentions every so often.The aesthetics of the game might be its main selling point. The art style is a mix of cartoony and realistic, with highly detailed and interesting plant life, architecture, and more. The character design is fun, and I never found myself getting bored of the visuals or the sound design for that matter. Not that the music or audio is particularly memorable, but it all fit, blended together to create an enjoyable sensory experience. The story and characters, which I will avoid spoiling at all, was what kept me going. I enjoyed the back-and-forth between protagonists Rani and Becks, their discussions are honestly what I played the game for. I thought they were cute, their interactions charming and funny at times, tense and serious at others, and if this were a longer game with a more fleshed out world with a wider scope of game mechanics I would have loved to spend more time with these characters. But, this is all we get, so it'll have to do. That said, one thing I only realized after starting to write this is that Rani and Becks are never explicitly stated to be a couple. They sure as heck feel like it though! I think I'd be hard pressed to find anyone who didn't think they were a couple, the way they more or less flirt and take care of each other. It all feels implied, but that's it, and that is super unfortunate to me because it feels like "queerbaiting", where they want the "praise" or "recognition" of having a lesbian cast but never actually committing to it. In that way it feels less unfortunate and more disingenous, but I will reserve immediate judgement. Could be the developers wanted to and the publishers nixed it, or could be literally anything else. We have no idea, so why speculate? I only hope that if the team ever returns to this worldspace, and I hope that they do, that they just lean into it. I mean, hell, if Daxter the weasel is allowed a love interest, why can't these two be a couple?That aside, The Gunk is an interesting sci-fi game with fun but simple mechanics and a short plot and endearing characters, all set on a beautiful world rank with pollution. If you're looking for something really expansive with lots of meat, then maybe look elsewhere. But, if you are looking for a game that is short, easy, and cute, then pick up The Gunk and have some fun for a few hours!

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 7/10Plot/Story: Simplistic story of two friends with fairly opposite personalities working together. Kinda cute but predictable. The game definitely has a not-subtle message about the danger industrialization and luxury has to the environment, and how living in harmony with nature is better than soft/escapist living. The voice acting is mostly good (especially for an indie game). The dialogue is also mostly good, though occasionally some of the phrases felt off or cringy.Art/Graphics: The game has a unique aesthetic, using vibrant colors and natural shapes for the plentiful vegetation and fungi in the game. The gunk does a great job of standing out with a black & white color palette wherever it appears with a sinister red around the edges. The animations all felt pretty natural. I would say the graphics lean closer to stylized cartoon over anything particularly realistic.Gameplay: Cleaning gunk is the star of the show; restoring an area to it's natural state is very satisfying as well as getting rid of all the slime. Collecting resources to install upgrades was a well-done way to encourage a bit of exploration. Scanning stuff to unlock upgrades to install was less interesting (there wasn't much to scan). Platforming is solid but very basic. There's a bit of puzzle solving but they 'puzzles' are super simplistic. The game is not doing anything you haven't seen if you've played any platformers in the last 2 decades.Performance: The game ran really smoothly everywhere...except one elevator section late game you have to play through twice. Both times, my 4090 struggled to keep even single frames multiple times. Maybe the game is more CPU-bound? It's fortunately a small section, but it was a surprise to see in an otherwise well-performing experience.Random thoughts: Beyond the gunk vacuum mechanic, nothing about this game is novel or done in an especially impressive way. It's a nice little title to give you a change of pace from more serious stuff, and it's short enough that it doesn't overstay its welcome. I'd suggest getting it on sale if you are interested. If you want a more dynamic platformer with better puzzles, get Ratchet and Clank.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Gunk," it's like this third-person 3D puzzle thing with a splash of shooter vibes. Perfect for the ankle-biters and chill enough for us grown-ups to kick back with. I blasted through this gem in just three evenings, mate.Now, the story, it's short and sweet, only about five to seven hours long, but it's got this graceful flow to it. Controls? Piece of cake. You dive in and start having a blast right off the bat.But let's talk about the visuals, yeah? They've crafted this world with some real finesse, showing off this epic battle between the beauty of nature and this invasive gunk. It's not just eye candy, though. It's like a call to arms, urging you to clean up nature's backyard as you play.Overall, it's a neat little adventure, perfect for winding down after a hard day's graft. _childDocuments_.review: Like how I assume other people may feel, I really wanted to like this game but it's just too simplistic and brief to be truly good. I would say it's just slightly below average. Essentially, it's a watered-down Mario Sunshine (Pun not intended), but Mario Sunshine came out about 20 years ago, and it somehow manages to be more simplistic than that. This is a platforming game where you clean up "gunk." What is gunk? Well, supposedly it's alien waste (Making the main character a space janitor at least the second space janitor in gaming behind Ed from Tonic Trouble way back on the N64). So, when I think of Gunk, and especially with how the game is marketed and the font it uses, I think of 70s and 80s horror films like "The Blob" and "The Stuff." Or at least the pink ooze that Vigo the Carpathian uses in Ghostbusters 2. But it's not that, really it just sort of sits there, waiting for the player to suck it up. Some times it rotates around in a circle like a snake for no apparent reason, even after watching all of the cutscenes I'm not really sure what it is, but only that it's bad and it needs to be gotten rid of. Basically, you play as a one armed girl with an arm cannon that she talks to called "Pumpkin" (Appropriate enough since it's orange and hexagonal). You move around, explore collect resources, clean up gunk, destroy one of three extremely simple enemy designs, and defeat the final boss. I wish there was more to it. The reason I really wanted to like this game is that the production is fantastic. The music is top notch, and reminds me of simplified versions of indie instrumental artists or even jazzy alternative musicians like Gigi Masin. The graphics are also very nice, although they really so heavily on Unreal engine resources that they don't feel very unique. Alien worlds are hard to design because they have to look foreign without being unrecognizable. Whenever you suck up all the gunk in an area, the place flourishes with light and dead plants suddenly come alive. I think of the first level of Mickey Mania on the SNES as being a game that did this before, but actually tons of games have copied this style, so it's nothing new.Basically the game is graphically trying to feel like a Pixar film, which I suppose is appropriate since the environmental plotline is torn straight out of WALL-E. Except that the characters are very grating, and most of the dialogue is just them arguing constantly, to the point that I eventually just turned the voice work off because it was giving me a headache. I find it hard to believe that these two main characters travel around the galaxy collecting resources when they bicker like a husband and wife that are planning on getting a divorce. So, while the presentation is fantastic, this is a great example of a game that probably had a ton of wonderful concept art but no knowledgeable way to  integrate it into a fully complete game. As such, since the game just consists of sucking up gunk and moving from one area to another, you wonder where the challenge is. The gunk, I believed, would be a threat, as in it would fill up the room, but most of the time of the time it just sits there, like moldy jello. It looks nice, with bubbles popping in and out, but why doesn't it chase after you, or grow claws or do something that makes it feel like a challenge? I think of Heart of Darkness on the PS1 as a very similar game thematically, but the difference there was that Heart of Darkness was challenging, and there was a sense that there was something sinister underlying the seemingly childish gameplay. This game appears to be made for children, but that can't be the case since one of the characters uses an expletive in the first fifteen minutes. If it is designed for adults, then it's just way too easy. Mario 64 and Mario Sunshine aren't particularly hard games, but it takes time to master the controls. If the developers would've at least added a double jump or a hover function and made the platforming harder it would've made a world of difference. The combat is extremely minimal, despite the fact that you have tons of upgrades. The "puzzles" consist of collecting a piece of fruit and throwing it into a green pool, or picking up an explosive piece of fruit and using it to blow up some scrap. It's okay I guess, but it never gets more challenging. Imagine if they made this game extremely hard, like Demon's Souls-level hard. Even games like Spyro the Dragon, while fundamentally very easy, still present a devilish challenge and some point. But because the game is so short, combined with the fact that there's no challenge, it often doesn't even feel like a game. Even if you die, you just immediately respawn. If you miss a jump, then you appear right next to the ledge you fell from. The achievements add a little bit of extra replay value, but not much. If you really want to take the extra time to scan some chairs and rusted metal to get all the achievements, it doesn't feel like much of an achievement. Even the final boss is a total joke. At best, this is an OK exploration game, but as an adventure game it doesn't really gel (Not sure if that's a pun since I don't know if "The Gunk" is considered gel.) It's not really bad, it's just mediocre. It feels like an early Xbox-era platformer with shiny graphics and dull characters.

_childDocuments_.review: feels like a promising prototype with a cool gameplay concept, but poor writing and underwhelming level design made it fall flat for me. i intend to finish the game to satisfy my completionist tendencies, but that's mostly because i know it's pretty short.  also, this is VERY subjective, but it's a pet peeve of mine when stories ostensibly about discovering alien worlds have the characters immediately intuit the meaning and purpose of everything they encounter (including having a perfect translation of an undiscovered language in what seems to be about one ingame day).  while i get the allegorical purpose of having aliens be improbably human, taking it this far makes me wonder if the story they wanted to tell wouldn't be better suited to a different setting and/or genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game to people who want a game with environmental focus, who can connect with the main characters, and are good with a 5 hour linear adventure. That's too limited of a recommendation for me to give this game a thumbs up here, even at a $5-$10 sale price.Here's what you need to know, spoiler free:+Nice looking and sounding game, with great performance on Ultra 1440p 144 Hz with only some hitching when going up the biggest elevator.+Solid voice acting for the main 2 characters.+The choice of portraying these characters as a certain socioeconomic status and a certain race was done respectfully and seemed authentic.?Subtitles only for certain alien speech after language translation is complete seems kinda silly.+Unlocking upgrades when scanning more things is cool. Upgrades were reasonable.-Getting rid of gunk gets tiring in certain places in the mid and late game. Most areas can be cleared to bring back life, but some you are only meant to clear a path through.-The "save the planet" trope is a bit thin for the story, though it can be argued that the story is just as much or more about the two main characters.?The game isn't so long that the game world or core gameplay overstays its welcome.?The gameplay is usually like a simple 3D platformer, with the exception of a handful of non-gunk enemy types you deal with.?It is only a "family friendly" game, like Steam tags suggest, if your family occasionally uses the cuss words "sh!t". It would be rated T for Teen by ESRB if it had a rating.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pleasant 8 hrs, but it's not a must-play.    The game will entice you with its story and it's sense of discovery, but the devs didn't stay focussed on this towards the end.  They must have ran out of money because (no spoilers) instead of a cinematic ending they had a bare bones slideshow of silent storyboards.  No lie.  And the sense of discovery means that you get to scan lots of new plants and wildlife at the start, but then this form of discovery tapers out before the half-way point.  This means that the 2 things that grabbed you at the start are never fully delivered at the end, and I was left feeling a little cheated.  It's a peasant time though, so it gets a Yes, but with a few caveats.  It feels like Jak & Daxter's level designs fused with the art style of a grungy stop-motion version of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.  It could do with a little more time in the Charm oven, but overall it is aesthetically appealing.   The relationship seemed like it was heading somewhere between the two leads, but hearing them bicker like they were in a dysfunctional marriage was quite a turn off, and was handled poorly.  A missed opportunity.  The gunk itself was always fun to scoop up and felt rewarding to get rid of completely, every time.  I'm glad I played it, but now that I have, I'll uninstall it.  I'm disappointed by the fact that the end cinematic was storyboards.  I feel a little cheated, but not enough to take away my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where the only people how knew what they were doing were the artistsThe Gunk is beautiful the art direction is very good and the environments stay mostly fresh during its short duration, unfortunately that is the only 100% positive thing I can say about this game.First let's talk about the level design, it sucks who ever was involved with it, I hope this was their first game, it has been a while since I have experience such an artificial feeling when playing a game. There is no need to bother with exploration or looking around for the path to take the levels are strictly linear with maybe some minuscule detours leading to dead ends with some resources, extreme use of yellow paint to a point there is no need to look at anything else, you will find obstacles twice your size with yellow paint that you easily climb and others that are barely bigger than you that are impossible to surpass this game feels like somebody saw the yellow line of Stanley Parable and completely missed the point. Because of that linearity, the world itself feels completely artificial. You will clean the gunk and nature will bend itself to your will to create a single perfect linear path for you to traverse.The story is pretty meh nothing special or new but omg the main character is an insufferable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ which keeps getting enabled and being self-righteous with impunity most of the time and what is even worse the other characters are the ones apologizing for not having the patience to deal with her ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The gameplay is solid but boring most of the time you are just cleaning gunk and solving "puzzles" to traverse the environment that because of the nature of the levels the puzzles require zero thinking and the small instances of combat are more annoying than anything else.Finally, I want to talk about the scanner, why does it exist if you are not going to put any work to it? You can't scan anything besides small plants, see that cool weird tree? Cant scan it sorry, see this energy puddle thing that we are trying to find the source? Cant scan it sorry, see The Gunk? Wonder what it is? Cant scan it sorry, there isn't even like an error it just refuses to scan and the things that you can scan have the most boring, uninspiring descriptions that just make me wonder WHAT IS THE POINT if you aren't going to put any amount of work, though or creativity in it just remove it. Even worse, the amount of things you scan is what unlocks your upgrades, which leads to situations like me scanning the cooking pot on our base camp and unlocking better lasers.Overall I'm not giving a negative review because this game is bad but because it doesn't even try to be good or different from anything else, I can't recommend this game when there are dozens of games that are exactly the same but either with a better story, better gameplay or better characters and with all of those around there is zero reason to play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Embarking on a journey through the visually stunning and emotionally resonant world of "The Gunk" has been a truly remarkable experience. This action-adventure game, developed by Image & Form Games, not only captivates with its breathtaking visuals but also surprises with its engaging gameplay and a narrative that pulls you in from the very start.The first thing that strikes you about The Gunk is its gorgeous, otherworldly environment. The attention to detail in creating the alien planet, filled with vibrant flora and mysterious landscapes, is simply awe-inspiring. Every step feels like a discovery, and the developers have successfully crafted a world that begs to be explored. The visual design is complemented by a dynamic day-night cycle and weather effects, adding an extra layer of immersion to the experience.The heart of The Gunk lies in its gameplay, seamlessly blending exploration, puzzle-solving, and action elements. As you navigate through the diverse environments, clearing away the mysterious substance known as "The Gunk," you'll find yourself engrossed in clever puzzles and challenges that keep the gameplay both entertaining and mentally stimulating. The intuitive controls and well-designed mechanics contribute to a smooth gaming experience, making it accessible to players of all skill levels.What truly sets The Gunk apart, however, is its narrative. The game manages to convey a touching story without relying on extensive dialogue, allowing the player to interpret and emotionally connect with the unfolding events. The protagonist's journey is not just about cleaning up the alien planet but discovering the secrets it holds and the impact it has on both the environment and the characters involved.The musical score deserves special mention, perfectly complementing the atmosphere of each location and heightening the emotional impact of key moments. The sound design, from the ambient sounds of nature to the subtle cues during gameplay, enhances the overall audio-visual experience and adds another layer of depth to the game.In conclusion, The Gunk is a testament to the creativity and craftsmanship of its developers. It successfully blends a visually stunning world with engaging gameplay and a narrative that resonates on a deeper level. This is more than just a game; it's an immersive journey that stays with you long after the credits roll. Whether you're a fan of exploration, puzzle-solving, or emotional storytelling, The Gunk delivers a satisfying and memorable gaming experience that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up on Humble, then played this game on the steamdeck, and I honestly think it's a good fit to be played that way. It's not a difficult game, and whether you enjoy it or not will probably come down to how patient you feel re: vacuuming up the eponymous Gunk. As a Power Wash Simulator enjoyer, that didn't bother me at all -- it's not as wholly absorbing and meditative as that, of course, but it's still sort of satisfying to clear the gunk out of the environment, anyway. It's essentially a lightweight puzzle-platforming experience with an eco-narrative you'll find familiar. The voice acting is great, and I thought the personalities of the characters really gave the emerging story a lot of its charm.It's not a very long game, either, but I think the amount of time you spend with it is about right. It follows a nice story arc to a comfortable conclusion, and doesn't try to pad itself out.If I had any quibble with it, I would say it's that most of the upgrades you can get feel a bit tacked-on and not especially necessary, but since you can unlock everything by the end without grinding (and in fact grinding would be impossible, as resource nodes don't appear to respawn), it hardly matters.

_childDocuments_.review: From the developers of the SteamWorld series, including the fantastic SteamWorld Dig 2, The Gunk is an altogether different sort of game. Like an intergalactic Luigi’s Mansion, but starring a one-armed space lesbian instead of a nervy Italian plumber, the setting is an uncharted planet ready to be pillaged with the assistance of a rather satisfying to use proton pack.This back-mounted vacuum cleaner can be used to scan your environment, which also fills an experience bar that unlocks upgrades, suck in resources to build said upgrades and clean up the titular gunk that’s polluting the otherwise beautifully rendered world. The proton pack can also be upgraded later on to help vanquish the world’s hostile lifeforms, most notably by sucking the innards out of the arseholes of the larger four-legged creatures.The Gunk is at its absolute best in the first two-thirds of its approximately six hour running time. The unnamed planet you get to explore is resplendent with vivid colours, and accompanied by a pleasingly unpressured musical score. Things take a turn for the final third, as the tediously on-the-nose eco plotting has you infiltrating a miserably dark and gloomy base in which the sense of wonder is replaced with too many of the annoying but unchallenging enemies and a sense of the plot spinning its wheels to add an extra hour to the total.Something that unfortunately plagues the entirety of the game is the unutterably awful writing and some of the worst voice acting ever to befall our ears. This starts out bad and rapidly descends to ear-rapingly horrendous, thanks in no small part to the two protagonists falling out and throwing the most pettily juvenile hissy fit in the history of gaming.The bugs, by comparison, are easier to forgive. This is, after all, an indie game, so occasionally getting stuck on the scenery and entire textures spontaneously disappearing are easy enough to tolerate.It never gives us pleasure to stick the knife into an indie title, but the fact The Gunk is so enjoyable until that final schizophrenic third makes it difficult to maintain a charitable outlook. It almost feels like a potentially great game has died at the altar of a hamfisted ecological tale, eschewing what could have been an unequivocally pleasing entry into the increasing bastion of titles that are both satisfying and relaxing.Pros:Gorgeous visual environment designSucking up resources and the gunk is enormously satisfyingFirst four hours make for a gloriously relaxing and enjoyable timeCons:Some of the worst writing and voice acting we’ve ever heard in gamingSomewhat glitchyLast third is a gloomy messHorrendously annoying and unrelatable protagonists69% // Fair

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk : By Triple F"The Gunk" is not your typical action-adventure. It's a captivating experience that blends environmental puzzle-solving, platforming, and a touch of narrative intrigue into a surprisingly compelling package. Developed by Image & Form, the creators of the beloved "Munch on Lunch" series, The Gunk delivers a unique blend of mechanics and a visually stunning world that, while short, leaves a lasting impression.The heart of "The Gunk" lies in its core gameplay loop: gunk-sucking and exploration. You take control of Rani, a scavenger who crash-lands on a vibrant alien planet covered in a black, gooey substance called, unsurprisingly, "gunk." Armed with her trusty "Power Glove" – a powerful vacuum attachment – Rani sets out to clean the gunk and uncover the secrets of the planet.The act of sucking up gunk is surprisingly satisfying. The sound effects are delightfully squelchy, and watching the vibrant flora reclaim its former glory as the gunk is removed is genuinely rewarding. This core mechanic is further enhanced by a light platforming system that allows Rani to navigate the diverse landscapes. While not overly complex, the platforming sections offer a nice break from the gunk-sucking and introduce clever environmental puzzles that require manipulating platforms and strategically using your gunk-sucking power.The alien world itself is a visual treat. Lush jungles teeming with bioluminescent flora stand in stark contrast to the barren wastelands choked by gunk. The developers have masterfully crafted a world that feels both alien and strangely inviting. The vibrant color palette and detailed environments create a sense of awe and wonder, making exploration a joy.While the core gameplay loop is undeniably fun, "The Gunk" isn't just about cleaning up gunk. As Rani delves deeper, she uncovers a narrative about a lost civilization, its connection to the gunk, and the potential consequences of Rani's actions. The story unfolds gradually through environmental storytelling and conversations with Rani's sardonic yet loyal companion, Beck. While not the game's strongest aspect, the narrative adds a layer of intrigue and keeps you invested in uncovering the mysteries of the planet."The Gunk" throws in a few encounters with gunk-infused creatures for some light combat variety. However, the combat system is quite basic, relying solely on your gunk-sucking and a weak projectile attack. While it doesn't detract significantly from the experience, it doesn't add much depth either.The biggest shortcoming of "The Gunk" is its length. The entire campaign can be completed in roughly 5-6 hours, leaving some players yearning for more. While the game offers some replay-ability in the form of optional collectibles and secrets, it might feel a bit short for those looking for a lengthy adventure.Despite its brevity, "The Gunk" offers a charming and satisfying experience. The core gameplay loop of gunk-sucking is surprisingly addictive, and the vibrant alien world is a joy to explore. While the story and combat might not be the game's strongest points, they do enough to keep you engaged throughout your journey. If you're looking for a unique and visually stunning game, with a focus on environmental restoration and a touch of lighthearted exploration, "The Gunk" is definitely worth checking out. Just be prepared for a relatively short but memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: At a glance, The Gunk looks like a simple adventure game. It's got vibrant areas to explore, a nasty big bad gunk everywhere, and a fun and for the most part engaging game play loop. If you're into playing games and beating them, this game is really good. A short five hour experience with a fulfilling story, simple but fun puzzles, and shallow yet rewarding combat. If you're like me and you go for 100% completion it's an entirely different experience. The only real gripe I've got with this game is the amount of attention and thoroughness you need to collect enough materials for upgrades. My last two hours in the game were spent scouring the game again from start to finish just to find eight (8) of one specific material to make the final upgrade and claim my achievement. In conclusion, highly recommend The Gunk for a short fun experience. I also recommend using a guide if you're gunning for the 100%

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely underrated. I had real fun with this one. I remember it getting a lot of hate when it first released, but I dont remember why. I think its because It wasnt clear on what kind of game it was and we all had different expectations. 3D world of goo? Atmospheric horror type? Something like viscera cleanup detail perhaps?Well, what it is is a collect-a-thon platformer. It reminds me most of slime rancher, for some reason.. only without the ranching. And outer worlds too, only less combat.There is a nice little story in here, the level design is very good, with much variation and verticality and nice unlockable shortcuts, though they are more for allowing you a qyicker way back up if you were to fall down than massive level-cuts. The graphics and world were really quite beautiful, but there is room for improvement on a lot of the factors here. I feel like it just falls short of an 8/10 because things could have been done a lot better. Like, there were nice upgrades but no real incentive to use them and by the time you got some of the later ones most of the combat was over. The game lacked difficulty in puzzles or combat until the latter third, which was a nice challenge. Overall though I would recommend this to most people who would enjoy a quick (2-3 long sessions) refresher from other, longer games.7.75/10

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this one. I'm a big fan of adventure exploration games, and the graphics in this are both technically impressive and stylistically beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: Get it on sale cheap, but it is oddly fun cleaning the GUNK.You and your sister land on a lifeless planet looking for energy sources. You have a robotic hand that allows you to scan and gather most anything you wish. You find the planet overrun in GUNK: a dark blob of stuff that is choking out everything on the planet. You impose yourself to change this.The game play is a simple platformer with grade school puzzles. You can "upgrade" your robot arm which you call "Pumkin" with the resources you gather by finding nodes through the level. They are not hard to find or rare.The story is "We have destroyed Earth so we must save this one." a very overdone story but it is what it is. The banter between the sisters, (your character and the only other human) is stereotypical and also overdone but... meh. It is a moving character to make do things.This is actually aimed at a younger crowd- I'd say 9-10 to early teens in order to push the message "people are bad, mm-k. Don't destroy the planet, mm-k."It took 7 hours to play and I think I searched the maps really good. Get it cheap and don't expect much.-Mr.GrAnD

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a fantastic game that immerses you in a beautiful, mysterious, and dangerous alien world. The game's story is captivating, and the characters are engaging, drawing you into their struggle to survive and save the planet from the gunk. The gameplay is a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat, with a satisfying sense of progression as you upgrade your abilities and equipment. The visuals and sound design are top-notch, creating a haunting and atmospheric setting that draws you in from the start. However, the game is a little bit short, but the low price more than makes up for it. Overall, The Gunk is a must-play for anyone who loves exploration-based games, sci-fi adventures, or just great storytelling. Don't miss out on this gem of a game!

_childDocuments_.review: Other than the environment design, nothing is good. - The dialogue and/or voice acting feels off. The draw of the character banter fails completely when this is the case- Your friend, for the first solid hour of the game (15% or so of the story length) is just complaining over the radio doing nothing while your character is working hard. Doesn't come off cute or endearing banter or whatever, just annoying. This follows afterwards where she complains less but is definitely not carrying her half while ordering your character around- The dialogue compares the civilization they found to the pyramids to make some intrigue due to not seeing any machinery to ajd in construction. Oh man, how'd the pyramids get built? I don't know how these things got built so oooooh, mystery. But this is barely seeing the civilization at all and obviously you wouldnt see that stuff yet if it existed. - I also did not care for the alien civilization. The writers took the way of pursuing both mysteries together but if I don't care about the alien portion, then I don't care about half the dialogue.- The main antagonist "gunk" feels awful. There is no hitbox for it so everything goes through it without interaction. You would think from the visual design it's Jello-y or something but that makes it act more like a gas. Where there is still no interaction when passing through like a proper gas. Also the damage it i flicts by running through it seems negligible, especially the feedback you get from the character. Later your character says the gunk is more aggressive here but the gunk is just... moving in a pattern pretty slowly. Not a threat at all.- Busy work central with tacked on upgrade system. The only reason to explore is to find upgrade materials but these are the worst upgrades. Some are mandatory, which basically makes the material hunting replace getting a key item at a specific story beat like kther games, while some are optional. You get the great ability to.... guess what. Run! Wow! And then you can upgrade your vacuum ability to suck the passive and not at all threatening gunk better! Wow! If an upgrade system serves no actual gameplay benefit other than saving time for the player, generally it's a bad upgrade. There's some "combat" upgrades but with no difficulty option or any difficulty to speak of, it feels tacked on to pad the short 5 hour game. - After exploring the entire first stretch until the first fast travel point, I was able to get the mandatory item upgrade and faster gunk sucking. That stretch feels like a solid half hour and to get so little for the busy work feels awful.- The puzzles seem dead simple so far. But I'm not too far to be fair. Not sure I intend on playing further.5 hour games are fine, just not with the poor offering this game is giving me.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a fantastic game that deserves more attention. If you love games like Subnautica, Slime Rancher, and Journey to the Savage Planet, you'll like this!The game shows it has a ton of heart and tries to do a lot with what it has. The environments are fantastical and beautiful (after clearing out some gunk), and the photo mode is a great touch to go along with it!You get a little of everything. A bit of light platforming, light RPG, light puzzling, and a lot of adventure. There's nice value in learning new skills, collecting resources, and clearing out the gunk to have nature flourish again.The VO is good and it's enjoyable to listen to characters go back and forth with one another. The characters have personalities, which makes the time put into the adventure even more enjoyable.The environmental animations were good while the character animations were OK to a little rough. Overall, the game has a lot of heart, a good story, and was a fun experience that didn't overstay its' welcome.Overall: ➡️Beautiful environment design➡️Fun platforming sections ➡️Simple puzzles that didn't detract from the story➡️Fun exploration➡️Can bug out your character in the environment if not careful➡️ Good VO➡️ Good music 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Who knew that after gaming for decades, having Steam for an eternity with over 700 games and thousands of hours into a good handful of them, that this would be my very first review!I struggle to complete games (adhd!) but this one was so relaxing, so beautiful, encompassing and honestly, just therapeutic that I was looking forward to coming back to it every day.I knew from the get go from other reviews and looking at the playtime of those that had completed it that, sadly, it was going to be a relatively short (5-6 hours) playthrough. However, those 5-6 hours are possibly some of the best that I have had in a game in a long time. It's not trying to be a massive AAA title, but that is a plus in this case and definitely not a flaw as what we end up with is a heartwarming and lovely gem that everyone should have in their library. "Short but sweet" is definitely how I would describe it.With it being on the shorter side, I had to force myself to *not* play it religiously every day, although I found myself dearly wishing to dip back into it's cute narrative (even though at one point your partner becomes almost equal to a nagging mother, but one that just wants the best!) which was well voice-acted. I really *wanted* to dive back into just siphoning up the gunk! With the companies use of colour contrasts, making these dark, dingy and angry looking landscapes into beautiful, lush and sparkling places was wonderfully addictive as well as just wanting to cleanse what was obviously a lovely planet back to it's original beautiful form.My only question now is Gunk 2 when? Gunk 3? 4... 5? I'd play them all! It is a shame that they could not perhaps get a bigger team onboard to create the same experience but on a much grander (and longer) scale.Now to the meat of gameplay, this is not a walking sim BUT, it is linear... HOWEVER, it takes me back to the good old days of gameplay where a game didn't HAVE to be an open world sandbox to still be enjoyable.The game pleasantly guides you through what you have to do and where you have to go whilst still providing enjoyable (albeit exceptionally easy) little puzzles and "fights" which still make you feel that you have accomplished something as they always end with a lovely flourish of colour. I found myself not wanting any more than this. I never found myself wandering around aimlessly wondering where to go either or needing a map.The "skills" you get when using mats to upgrade is really, in my opinion, "there for show", but the fact they thought of it is nice. I don't begrudge it and I am not here to slam it or compare it to any other games that have huge progression trees etc. The skills are there to aid with platforming/opening up new areas, no more and no less.I believe this game is extremely enjoyable playing as an adult but would be equally enjoyable then passing it on to your kids/being played by kids (because, of course, you will want to play it first!!) ;)I am extremely thankful for the relaxing time I had with this game, seeing end credits roll is unusual for me but I knew this was one that I would complete.Don't hesitate, pick this up, *unless* you are in the mood for/looking for a shooter/looter/open world lootfest or roguelike.Sit back, relax and enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Ehhh... hmm. It's fine. It's both too short and yet, for what gameplay is there, feels too long - the platforming is rare, the puzzles are simple, the combat might as well not exist, and vacuuming up gunk can only stay enjoyable for so long. The game tags itself as exploration but the journey is completely linear, you go down one path until it ends, then a second path (twice) and then the game ends. The story is... okay, but the game fails to make Becks' pushy, hostile behavior justified, she ends up coming off as obnoxious not just to Rani but to the player. The crafting mechanic is nice at first but when you realize the only thing the game can reward you with is more crafting materials (or upgrades for scans, the vast majority of which will be unlocked in the first hour of gameplay) and like, half the upgrades are geared towards the barely-existent combat system... not very exciting.I do lie the visuals, the presentation in general, and the core mechanics, at least to start with, are pretty fun, and the overall story has its moments, the game's atmosphere is pretty great, it's not very difficult but not completely free either, I did get some enjoyment out of it, and if you can get it on sale then, sure... and it doesn't do anything really, horribly wrong either, but, I dunno, between the cost and the general shallowness of the gameplay it's hard to fully recommend either. Meh.
