_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a cute indie game with surprisingly good voice acting. I'd even say that the voice acting is perhaps one of the better parts of the video game. I was pleasantly surprised to discover that the lady who voiced the main protagonist here, Rani, is Fiona Nova, formerly of Rooster Teeth. She does pretty well to express Rani's change in emotion as she explores an alien planet that she and her associate(?), another woman who goes by Becks, landed on in their mission to locate materials or resources that can be sold for cash.Except they land somewhere that is full of a mysterious substance that they label as the "gunk," but fortunately, Rani is equipped with some sort of vacuum that allows her to suck up the gunk in addition to useful resources like metal and fiber that you can use to upgrade your equipment. You have the option to scan fauna and flora as you progress through the rather linear areas and the more you scan, the more options you acquire for unlocking.There are puzzles scattered about that you have to complete in order to progress, but the puzzles are not at all challenging. Mostly, you pull from a vine a spherical object and toss it into a puddle and it instantly sprouts into leaves that you jump onto in order to cross gaps or achieve verticality. The objective is always the same with each puzzle: just locate this spherical object. The fun here is really in the alien planet and watching it transform from a dying wasteland into a sprawling, colorful ecosystem as you remove the invasive gunk that is slowly sucking the energy from everything around it, but there are a lot of reused resources throughout the game so the beauty of it becomes rather stale. Each area that you transform starts to look identical.Fortunately, the game is rather short and this does it far more justice than the developers having tried every idea they could think of to prolong the game time. It would have become very repetitive if it took more than ten hours of playtime. You can easily beat it on just one Saturday evening or whenever you have the time to play.Now, for the most important questions: Not really. At most, the video game has two main characters who are female. The playable character happens to be a woman of color, and while women, and people of color, are generally the very first ingredient to wokeness, it doesn't necessarily mean that it will result in a woke product.Their relationship status is not even defined by this video game. Other than that their relationship had started around five years ago as of the event's in the video game, it is not explicitly stated or even implied that these two ladies are in a same-sex relationship. To me, they just seemed like good friends and business partners who cared about one another because they needed each other. One was the pilot and the other was the one collecting the resources. They're just a team of spacers trying to pay off their debts, and I can respect that.There isn't any blatant or obnoxious "female empowerment" tropes. While there's only four male characters that we see, one of which is their friendly robot, and the main villain is an  or something, the ladies don't really act superior or morally correct nor do the male characters exist to service the intelligence of the female characters while they are made to be dumb.At first, I was concerned that it would have some sort of underlying message about climate change but I don't really think messaging exists here either. No, it's just a fun little adventure game that does its characters properly. It was a nice, short video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like vacuuming? Do you really really like vacuuming? Cause you'll be doing that for the better part of this game vacuuming up a mysterious byproduct called the gunk in this game.The Gunk starts out as an intriguing and interesting adventure that appeals to you sense of curiousity, but in my opinion, quickly degrades into a boring chore as you listen to Rani, Becks and  go on an on about things that I actually couldn't care less about nor contributes to the story of the game. Things can go from wonder and awe to doom and gloom then everything's okay again within a minute or so. The game makes an attempt at telling a story that could've been good, but the way it is experienced by the player makes it fall flat. Character arcs are minimal and the story and dialogue do not do anything to draw me into caring about the characters or their plight at all. The premise for the game is weak too.  As such, when the game attempts to stir feelings of loss and reunion between the characters I found myself rolling my eyes half the time cause honestly, I couldn't care any less.I often found that things were super linear and mundane. When things went awry in the story, something convenient would pop up and save the day. Stuck in a room? Oh wait! Look! A convenient hole to get out of it is right there. Sealed door? Not to worry,   I often found myself thinking that the puzzles offered no challenge and I was just going through the motions to be able to progress to the next level. More often than not, getting to the next level was mundane and more of the same. A couple of times, after the level loaded, I was psyching myself up for some "combat", but as I walk forward, the screen suddenly fades to black and a new level loads. Boss battles are meh and can be successfully completed by a new player if they started playing at the boss battle. Two or three times I had to reload the game because Rani would suddenly be stuck in a falling position above some rocks or because an enemy that needs to be killed spawned halfway into or below the ground. Rani's glove is up-gradable, but I found that I didn't really care or need any upgrades after the first three because I wasn't really feeling challenged by the game in order to progress. In fact, I only discovered that I had missed out on a lot of upgrades towards the end of the game and googled how to get upgrades, which in my opinion, didn't really do much to improve the enjoyability of the game. Half way through, I found myself trudging onwards just to finish it.Despite all this, never-the-less, the graphics are decent, the world building is okay and the melancholic and beautiful soundtrack helps to keep things palatable. Get this game when on sale. The experience it provides and the time it takes not worth more than $5 in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 2nd, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Creating a lush beautiful world out of slime pools. The Gunk has a beautiful moment where the player removes the last of the Gunk in an area and the player flashes a green sphere and the world’s flora comes back into view.  That moment plays again and again about every five minutes or so, and each one feels uplifting.  The beauty being restored is never really lost on the player as they explore the massive world that surrounds them even if it’s a guided path.   While there is combat, this is almost a casual game, with a great story and interesting locations to discover. At the same time, there’s just enough combat to make this more active than most casual games, as well as some platforming.  Only a few moments have a real challenge, but it’s in a weird position.  The idea of cleaning up a world while investigating what caused the calamity might not appeal to everyone, but this is a unique title in that respect. Pick this up if you like what you’re seeing.  This is just an odd game to gauge but I enjoyed myself and fully played through this title on Game Pass.  It took me 6 hours and while 5 of them were great, the last hour dragged just a bit, but it still has an interesting tale, and I will applaud there’s a lot said in the story without being shoved in the player's faceIf you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscious recommend this game. Though the price may reflect a different kind of quality than a full $60 release, the game is incredibly basic and not challenging. This is the kind of game you give to a child to play and though I had some interest in the concept of cleaning up "The Gunk" sadly the game play loop is horribly lacking. There are a total of three enemies in the game and the puzzles are limited to two kinds: throwing an object and blowing a device to rotate platforms. This game is simply lacking in game play. The world and environments are beautiful and many times I did catch myself simply looking at the sky because of how stunning it looked. It's simply a shame the rest of the time couldn't have gone further towards any better animations on the characters. Speaking of characters... You and your partner exploring this planet are just not likable. There are times when you are forced to do something that I as a the player have no desire to do without reason such as willingly ignoring my partners request to return to base. As well, your partner is horribly negative to you and the alien you rescue. I feel like due to the games short length I feel what the writers were attempting to create between the two of them, but ultimately it's too short to really make me care about the game. I finished this game in 5 hours and missed one unlock, which was for an ability I never needed to use maybe the final fight but you can literally sleep on it and win, and apparently I missed one object to scan even though I have unlocked all upgrades. Final verdict: this game is perfect for someone who isn't a gamer or who is a small child but there are so many better options out there and this game will ultimately blend into the sea of games nobody will remember. I can never see myself wanting to ever play this game again even for the easy achievements I missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale for $18 bundled with Wave Tale and a couple small 2D games, it was worth it IMO. This is a beautiful-looking adventure game with very light combat, puzzle solving, and a bit of platforming. I think the art style is cute, it remind me of stop-motion animation like Wallace and Gromit or Chicken Run, with the same look to the character models. It’s very charming and cute. The premise is that you are a miner in space, you and your pilot are low on resources and you detect some kind of signal on a strange alien world, so you land on the planet to investigate and find that it has been overtaken by this “gunk” that kind of looks like evil grape jelly/jam. The main character has a robotic arm that doubles as a futuristic vacuum cleaner, which you use to vacuum up all of the evil gunk. This changes the environment back to normal and restores the ecological balance to the planet’s environment. As you proceed to do this, you discover ruins  of an ancient civilization (as well as resources to upgrade your vacuum arm). It’s somewhat reminiscent of Luigi’s Mansion in terms of the game play mechanics. You can use your robotic vacuum arm in combat as well. I enjoyed this game and think it’s a cute little indie title with some beautiful visuals. This is for people who enjoy exploring and a simple story with more or less easy, laidback gameplay with some slight puzzle solving. This is not for people who want lots of combat or challenging gameplay. Keep your expectations in check and you will enjoy it. I think most people could finish this in 6 hours or so, while seeing the vast majority of what is here and finishing the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: It didn’t even take me four hours to finish, but boy am I glad it’s over. The only redeeming quality is the sometimes beautiful environment. Seriously, that’s it.About 80% of the gameplay consists of running around with a vacuum in your fist, sucking up the so-called gunk, while the other 20% involves some of the most pathetic attempts at “puzzles” and combat I’ve ever seen in a video game. Aside from a single boss at the very end, you’ll face three enemy types, all of which are just annoying to fight. Because guess what... It’s not enough to spend the bulk of your time vacuuming gunk out of the environment; no, you have to suck off *pause* these sad excuses for enemies as well. The boss fight has to be one of the worst in any video game. Throughout your time playing you'll have a much harder time fighting the urge to quit and uninstall this piece of s...oftware.The enemies are no challenge at all and seem to exist solely to extend gameplay by another half-hour so you’re not eligible for a refund.The puzzles, and I'm really stretching it by calling them that; feel like they’re aimed at an audience of literal lobotomites and offer no sense of satisfaction when solved. "This isn't a puzzle game!", I hear you cry out. Sure buddy, but what is the point of incorporating a gameplay mechanic, which takes up a significant part of the playtime, if you're not making sure that it is somewhat challenging and/or rewarding to play? Level design is fine most of the time, but veers into mind-numbingly poor and unintuitive territory on occasion, probably to again waste more of your time. It's a shame really because some of the environments are really beautiful to look at, only for them to be ruined by poor layout choices, resulting in some paths being obstructed from the camera until you backtrack and find the right angle.So, what about the story, characters, and dialogue? Surely there must be something compelling there, right? Think again.The story is okay at best. it's fine for kids I guess, although your standard episode of Spongebob has more depth. The antagonist is built up like this powerful and genius scientist, his reasoning for doing things he does though is so unbelievably idiotic and riddled with contradictions. Again, fine for kids, anyone over the age of 14 though will be having a tough time not laughing their a** off at how stupid this is.The characters look fit this zeitgeist of inclusivity and "diversity", which is fine if that’s your thing, but if you’re somewhat tired of the overly familiar formula of the past years, expect your eyes to roll with each cutscene. Speaking of cutscenes, it's a generous term for something you'll quickly start skipping. They don't convey any critical nor mildly interesting information, while failing to be cinematic in any shape of form. You can easily follow the mediocre plot without sitting through a singular cutscene. The lip-syncing, if you can even call it that, is laughably nonexistent, as if they hired a puppeteer with a reaction time of two to three business days for the mouth animations. They’d really have been better off not animating the mouths at all.But the worst part? The dialogue between the protagonist and her girlfriend(?). It’s some of the most cringeworthy, unfunny, and annoying dialogue I’ve ever endured, period. I'm struggling to find a singular instance of when I've been so utterly annoyed by any piece of dialogue in any form of media. While the dialogue as a whole has no redeeming quality, I think it's important that whoever wrote the girlfriend’s lines (I can’t even remember her name) might want to consult a team of very expensive therapists. While being bland and unfunny in the first hour of the game, she suddenly becomes completely irrational and frankly bipolar.Please whoever wrote that her character/dialogue, seek help.Performance wise, it ran OK on the Steam Deck on high settings. One part at the very end, even ran very poorly on medium settings. It was playable 95% of the time and it's an often good looking game though so I'll allow it.

_childDocuments_.review: As the first fully 3D game from Image & Form, creators of the excellent Steamworld games, I had a lot of high hopes going into this game. The Gunk isn't a total wash but it has some serious issues. Everything you've learned to do in the first 30 minutes is the entire game play pattern for the meager 4 hour runtime of the whole game (and that was completing 100% of achievements as well). The environments are mostly pretty but there is some serious frame rate issues here and there, especially in a certain elevator ride near the end, while running on a 3080 Ti GPU and Ryzen 3950X CPU. The story has no real twists or turns. No surprises; what the protagonists think The Gunk is at the start is 100% dead on accurate: it's just pollution. By no means an awful experience but I'd highly recommend if you are interested in playing it do not pay full price. Wait for a sale or if you can go play it on Xbox GamePass.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just preface this really quick.The game is a 6.5/10 at most. Don't listen to people stating it's a trainwreck, or that it's a 9/10 almost masterpiece. The game isn't even that good. It's just fine.The reasoning is simple, in a vacuum, the game would be a 7/10. It's 3 hours long and has no replayability.The gameplay is simple and it works. It doesn't feel like it flows supremely well, but it gets the job done. I like the uniqueness of the combat, but that's not enough to overcome the game's weaknesses.I love when games don't overstay their welcome, it's a huge pet peeve to me when games go on and on for no reason, it leaves me fatigued.However...I despise it even more when games are much shorter than what they should be and are missing story, lore and gameplay mechanics because of the excuse that it's an indie title.If the game were 2 hours longer, had better mechanics and much more flushed out lore and story. Then I'd say the game is worth it at $25-30. The concept is interesting, but not entirely original (not starting a philosophy debate here, shove it). I do like the idea, but it was barely brushed upon before the ending stage. I didn't feel like I was exploring a planet that was on the cusp of dying, I felt like I was being guided along rails to scooch me along the story.The characters are flat, but have a lot of potential. Which makes me even more disappointed because I actually think they could've done this far better with the buildup and climax of the relationship between Rani and Beck if they just had a bit more time and better writing.Instead the drama comes off super artificial and kneejerkish just to attempt to get you to feel something.Anyways, if you see the game at $10, pick it up if you want a small platformer that at the end you'll forget about and never play again. You'll enjoy yourself for a bit, get a small bit invested in what's happening, then everything ends and you're like "Huh... So....... That's it?"6/10, "You just got served"

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda hate this whole binary rating system, because I feel like I'm just giving everything a positive rating unless it's really bad. I think this will be an exception. The game is like 6/10. Nothing terrible. It's very pretty, it has an interesting world and the characters are ok. Unfortunately the puzzles are not super inventive and almost none of them actually require any critical thinking, just looking around to find that one mcguffin you need to advance to the next part of the map. I can't say I had a ton of fun playing the game, it was just ok. I'm fine with either good gameplay or good story/characters. Both of those were mediocre in this game.I would have probably left the review at positive, but what put me over the edge was the technical side. I didn't have any issues with overall performance, but I did have some stuttering a few times, then I had an elevator completely disappear once, so I was running around trying to figure out what to do only to discover that I needed to reload to see an elevator that can take me upstairs. I also got stuck twice while crawling through a narrow passage, so another two reloads. The game has black bars in cutscenes in ultrawide, which is just completely pointless since there is a utility that removes those bars and nothing looked weird with them gone even in super-ultrawide with increased FOV, so there's no reason to have them in the first place. Devs really need to start at least giving us the option to disable them. The Last of Us has this option and just warns you that some things might not look ideal or might be framed awkwardly. Give us that option. Also, ALWAYS add a proper FOV slider that has correct scaling for UW monitors. So yeah, the technical part just barely pushes me into the negative territory. At least it was short, and I do like short and sweet games, but when being short works to a game's benefit, it's probably not an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little game! The gameplay loop is pretty straightforward and what you see at the start is what you have until the end. While the gameplay IS stagnant throughout, the game features a pretty consistent supply of pretty nice puzzles, platforming, and exploration that doesn't overstay its welcome so it never feels repetitive or old.This game managed to squeeze its way into my favorites. It beautiful, it's optimistic and hopeful, it's cutely-written, and it's the perfect size for what it is. It's a FANTASTIC game to play between bigger games. A welcome reprieve. My biggest gripe about the game is the protagonists. They're not bad! They're actually good! The problem is that partway through, their relationship VERY suddenly changes. It feels less like a disagreement and more vitriolic. It's touched on shortly after but the whiplash was enough to make me want the characters to just not interact for a good chunk of the final act. It felt unwarranted, even when explained afterwards, and severely out of character going off the chemistry they had until that point. ALSO THE QUEERBAITING NEEDS TO STOP.Loved this game. Loved the opportunity to play it and show it to the world. And I'd love to see more games like this overall. If the game ever receives some sort of major update (idk what you could even add, but y'know), please consider having Rani and Becks kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: Should be called The Clunk.The only positive: art direction. Looks great. This is what hooked me: I love this stylized look.But this game suffers from doing everything "OK" and not having a hook other than: you suck stuff up. That is not a hook. That's like one mechanic.This is a weird game and I don't know what audience this would vibe with. It is not action enough to be an action game. It is not big enough to appeal to the No Man's Sky crowd but has elements of scanning and harvesting from that game. The story and dialogue is boring / annoying and won't appeal to story gamers. So it's going to be too boring for action people, not big enough to explore for the exploration / environment people, not interesting enough for story people.It also has terrible level design that lacks clear focus on where to go / what to do. I was immediately frustrated within 2 minutes of playing by running the wrong way into a dead end, then turning around with no obvious way to go. This is the first few minutes of gameplay...there is no excuse for a dead end here. You need a straight line like 1) here is the direction to go and 2) these are your controls.Left shift to run is an UNLOCKABLE UPGRADE. You will plod around the level (slowly) sucking up goo (slowly). This makes the poor level design even worse, because when you go the wrong way...it feels so much worse because of how slow you move.So overall, it's not fun which is really sad because the look of the game is great. But if I'm like "I'm so bored, I just want to get off this planet" and then I'm like "how do I get back to my ship" and then I'm like "how do I get out of this game" within the first 30 minutes, that's a big problem.But really, at the end of the day what drove me to leave a negative review is...solder is pronounced "sah-der" not "sole-der" which this dialogue says repeatedly and drove me absolutely bonkers.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer at the top, I did receive a code for this game from the developer, but as you'll see in my review, it most definitely does not ever do anything to change what I say about this (or any) game. A few months ago I did my first real steam review on a game called Expedition Zero, which was a dumpster fire of a game that cost way too much, was essentially an alpha version of a game marketed as a full release and cost about 15$ more than it should have.This is not that game, but I am not recommending it for the same reason. I streamed this game, and even with taking time to talk to my chat and detour and just sit and talk for awhile, I ended with 4.4 hours in this game, only missing 5 of 17 achievements, that if I paid more attention to while I was playing, I would have gotten. This game does not have nearly enough content to justify the price tag. With what is here, I would say don't pay more than 10 bucks for it. The only time I can justify a game as short as this being as expensive as it is, is when its something like Gris where those few hours are some of the most gorgeous and polished you will ever experience in a game. This is not the case with The Gunk, but it's also not a bad game by any stretch of the imagination.The visuals here are actually really great, although both I and my chat agreed that the character models were really disappointing for an otherwise gorgeous looking game. The story, while very barebones and nothing special, is interesting enough to keep me going. The gameplay is extremely simple, and I think that honestly if the few swears the MC drops during the game were cut from it, this would make a really good game for kids entering their teens. Hopefully, this game gets a sequel, and I say that not because I was so in love with what IS here, but the potential for what is here to be something absolutely worth 25$ and more is astronomical. Add some more spice to the gameplay. You gave me a fist that I cant punch with. Expand the enemy variety and let me smash some stuff. Or, maybe you expand the puzzles and the ways in which you interact with the  environment. How the team decides to iterate doesn't particularly matter as long as they DO iterate on this. For a first attempt at a 3D game from this developer, this is a solid take, and hopefully round 2 shows a lot of improvement. If you made it this far I would really appreciate it if you could follow my steam store curator page in the link at the top, it helps me out a ton. Thanks for reading, and let me know what your experience was if you played the game too.

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed cleaning up the yucky gunk, especially in places where there is a ton of it.A big part of the satisfaction is due to the physical and visual effects of the vacuuming itself.Another reason is the transition from a dark, sad landscape to a vibrant one.Cool models of the lifeforms, somewhere between clay and plastic toys.Fully voiced characters.The game is an old-school linear adventure, with light puzzles and light combat, which makes it suitable for pretty much anyone.The way back is always blocked, therefore you can only revisit an area after you reach a fast travel point.This can cause you to end up softlocked, when revisiting a place where activated lifts or switches do not reset.However, the abundance of prior auto-saves makes it highly unlikely that you would lose much. Do cycle on manual save slots all the same, it's never a bad idea.The one negative aspect of the game is excessive darkness, down to near-zero visibility in several locations.I'm not a big fan of directional flashlights, of their weak power and insufficient cone of illumination; even less so here, as the light keeps turning on way too late. I would have really appreciated a manual switch.It's a simple game and an enjoyable one.Technically and artistically well done.Admittedly, I'm a sucker, not only of gunk, but for wandering on alien worlds as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played and enjoyed all of Image & Form's other games, which was especially impressive to me because they've made games in genres that generally I don't enjoy much (platformers, sort of Metroidvanias, deck building, turn based strategy, none of which I usually have any interest in).  All their prior games had interesting and original enough gameplay along with great characters and writing to make fun games in  genres that I probably wouldn't have liked much from almost any other developer.So it was a real disappointment that The Gunk falls so flat on its face in both those elements, original and interesting implementation of a particular genre of game and good writing.  The gameplay isn't terrible; it's just kind of uninteresting most of the time and almost walking simulator like in its simplicity.  There's never any challenge of any significance in either combat or puzzles or exploration, and it seems kind of silly that the game even bothers to have a bunch of upgrades to your weapons you can craft when the combat never presents enough of a challenge to need any upgrades at all.  Still, the gameplay isn't at all terrible, just not all that engaging a lot of the time.  It's the writing that really ends up being pretty abysmal, especially in the last few chapters, which is something I never would have expected from Image & Form.  The characters in this game just become intolerable to the point that when they started whining and complaining back and forth to each other over the radio incessantly towards the end I just started hitting the mute button on my speakers every time they started talking until they shut up while I trudged through the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game borrows a lot from the Metroid Prime series, down to an arm beam weapon, and a scanner.  It actually could have made a decent Metroid.  The environments are really nice, and clearing The Gunk to beautify the planet is satisfying.  This could have been much more of a Metroidvainia if the upgrade system was better utilized and the enemy variety was better (it's practically non-existent).  Many of the upgrades seem pretty pointless, especially due to the general lack of difficulty.  There are environmental puzzles to solve, but they lack much variety and most are obvious.  I had lots of audio glitches, some of which would temporarily keep the game from loading certain sections.  With ray tracing off, the game ran generally well at 4k (3070 TI Laptop on a 4k VRR display), until the end section which suffered from bad slow-downs. The story is so-so.  The older sister type character is annoying.  The character models of the two mains are ugly, but it doesn't really take away much from the game.  The game seems like it should be for all ages, with the exception of the odd choice to include cursing for no apparent reason.  The ending is underwhelming, and doesn't even really fulfill the main story objective.  Fortunately, the creative and beautiful environments mostly make up for these flaws. It's a good game, that probably could have been great, but it doesn't overstay its welcome, and is worth a play-through if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Premise:The gunk is a single player adventure and exploration 3d platformer set on an alien planet. Our protagonist lands on this planet after detecting an energy source and encounters the mysterious gunk that seems to be suffocating the local plant and animal life. They start clearing the gunk away and they begin the explore. Then they discover alien ruins...Game play:Although this sounds like a prelude to a horror game, it is not a horror game. It is a very relaxing, very forgiving 3d platformer with beautiful visuals and soothing music. The world is large and progression is linear. The pacing and reveals are also well scripted and rewarding. There are some resource gathering and crafting elements, but there is no grinding involved. It might even be child friendly in terms of content and game play, although there are certain comments that mention swearing in game (have not encountered so far)System requirement & compatibility:In terms of graphics and compatibility, I am able to run this game on high graphics settings (not Ultra) very smoothly on a rig with a ryzen 5 5600G, GTX1650 super (4GB vRAM) and 16 GB of RAM running Linux with proton. No issues or stutters what so ever. Controller support for dual shock works with steam inputConclusion:If you want a relaxing time with a narrative based game and are not looking for a challenge or climbing skill trees, then pick this game up. You will not regret it . 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a nice, short adventure story. It's heavily narative-based and not very difficult. It plays fine and I did not experience any bugs.Combat is nothing to write home about. You have little critters that are annoying, static artillery that you need to find a way to and chargers that are cheating annoying beasts with too much hp that you have never seen before in any game ever (tm, don't steal). Combat is not the focus and I feel as if the game itself would be better if they did away with it entirely and found a few more ways to make puzzles in the world.Graphics are nice to look at, character design is a bit weird, but not uncanny-valley weird.The music is good. Not especially grandiose, but very suited for the job. It was never annoying and supported the somber ambience of a planet on the brink of death very well.The sound effects are spot on. The Gunk is just a simple mass of stuff sitting there and not doing anything much, but the sound scape manages to make it unsettling.The story itself is not especially great but it was okay for the 4,5 hours the game took.Where The Gunk really shines is in the delivery of the story. The two main characters are talking to each other frequently and we know enough about them that the turns the story takes can be inferred before they become relevant. They are telegraphed, but in a way that worked for me.Hero-Girl and Captain Responsible do the heavy lifting, and apart from a few scenes where I felt they could have used a bit more emotion in their delivery they did a really good job. I also love how undefined their relationship is, so you can interpret whatever you are comfortable with into it. Are they good friends? Girlfriends? Sisters? The game doesn't care, but if you do they can be whatever.You also have Not-Groot, a charming robot that is inconsequential to everything but still has a lot of character for a machine that only ever says one sentence and Exposition Person, whose job is to deliver exposition. I whish they did that in a different way, but it's fine.All in all I really enjoyed my time with The Gunk. It's short, it's on point and it doesn't waste your time. The exploration could have been stronger, but I'd rather have a linear and short experience than hunt for 1000 collectibles that are somewhere on a map that is only huge to hide those collectibles somewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Gunk" is a game served in the right dosage: less of it could have made it feel unsatisfying, and more of it could have ruined it. Its mechanics may not be groundbreaking, but it's a fun game that doesn't overstay its welcome: you go in, do your business and get out. I guess there are completionists out there who would be interested to 100% a game like this, to get all the achievements and what not. But by its very nature, it's a semi-casual adventure puzzle game that is not meant for very large gameplays. The first thing I want to point out on this game is the visuals. "The Gunk" is visually superb: the kind of game that makes you stop to appreciate your surroundings. It uses the Unreal Engine, and instead of going for photo-realistic scenarios and models, it goes for more cartoony visuals - complete, with characters having four fingers instead of five. Still, the visuals are drop-dead amazing, really selling me of the idea of being in a densely forested alien planet, with fungi-looking flora and striking colours.Now, the game requires players to clean out the titular gunk. Your main device for that is a vacuum glove that you aim with M2 and activate with M1 - pretty basic stuff. Whenever you get in a place full of gunk, you need to clear it in order for paths to open up - or for key items to appear, so you'll open up paths. At first, there's something incredibly satisfying about cleaning places: your drab surroundings will explode with colours and vegetation, and I felt like Marie Kondo just tidying everything up. However, cleaning the gunk can eventually feel like a bore, but this is when the game starts to variate: it brings in new puzzles with different mechanics, such as machines, bridges and enemies. And when the game showed everything it had to show, it ended.You also gather resources to improve your gear at you home base, but I'll warm you from now: it's nothing to write home about. Don't expect this to be something like "Don't Starve"; once again, it's more casual than that. Some resources are right at your sight, but other resources are a little bit more hidden, in side paths that may require some extra work to be accessed. Curiously, there's no sprint at first, and I imagined the game didn't have a sprint prompt. But I was wrong: you have to get the perk to run faster, which is weird and completely unnecessary. There's also an upgrade that makes the vacuum stronger, sucking in the gunk faster, which is incredibly helpful, in that there will be environments very crowded with the stuff.Also curiously, perks can only be avaible to be activated by researching the environment around you. Some things have a green marker over them, indicating they can be investigated, and hitting them with Q will include such things - organic or mechanic - into your encyclopedia. With enough inclusions, only then a perk will be ready to be traded with your collected resources. The game is also very linear: you can activate some fast travel points, but there's not a lot of need for backtracking, and the game would naturally bring me to the base camp so I could upgrade my stats with all the resources I gathered.Combat is perhaps the worst aspect of the game. You gain at a certain point of the game a plasma cannon, but it serves much more to activate certain buttons to open doors. The most bothersome foe is a sentinel that fires flame balls at you, and when there are several, they can chain hits. Enemies require the vacuum to be defeated, and many of them are directly related to the gunk: the place will not clear up until you get close to the bastards and pluck them out. There are ticks that can easily be disposed, and the bulls are tricky but nothing hard: just get out of their way. There will be a moment when you'll see floating gunk, and some of them may even come at you.The game has a lot of platforming to be done, and movement is intuitive and precise - which is all I ask from platformers. Some ledges can be grabbed - they'll be marked with a yellow tone. And should you fall, the game is incredibly kind, immediately bringing you back to try again. But sometimes, falling from a higher altitude will make your character lose her balance and hit the ground - and I feel that was totally unnecessary.The story is also nothing great, and it feels a bit intrusive sometimes, with unnecessary drama tossed in close to its final act. But hey, I bet it could make for a terrific "Love, Death and Robots" episode.Overall, I really enjoyed my short time with this game - little less than five hours (and I detoured a lot). Even through I've played better puzzle games, this one grabbed my attention from beginning to end, by its visuals and engaging puzzles. You can see it was a very dedicated output from Image & Form Games. And should they follow it with a more focused, straightforward game - one that wouldn't try so much to be perk-oriented - I think the concept of this game could truly come into its own.

Though through that the game feel is pretty smooth, and I'd rather have smooth game feel than top tier animations that constantly lock out controls.It has some  performance issues in some very few, very specific spots - that 10fps elevator ride sure is something.I find the writing, especially the constant quips to be a touch corny and overwritten - sometimes less is more.the voice-acting is kinda B-tier at times as well. _childDocuments_.review: As with all the games I play, the playtime is not representative of my time playing it, actual play time for this game is about 5 hours.First impression was it's very pretty, has resource gathering but isn't annoying, fairly easy game.Unfortunately this was about all it had going for it the more I played.  It's a pretty game yes, but it's got lots of bugs, some being game breaking that required me to load save files that I luckily manually made ahead of time (others on the steam discussions were not so lucky).The game goes in several directions, it has a more childish look to it, and childish drama, but has a fair amount of swearing in it.  It has checkpoints and fast travel points like an open world game but you often cant travel backwards from where you are.  You have a scanner that makes you think you can scan most things in the game, but probably less than half of the things are able to be scanned, even if they're unique and out of place, screaming "scan me, add me to your logs!!".  You cannot close the scan result window without scanning nothing or waiting a long time for it to go away which is annoying too.  The story at the beginning of the game is almost forgotten and changed to a different one half way through, which is fine but it feels messy how it was done and I wish they focused a bit more on the original story of why they landed in the first place.As for bugs and technical things, the character often remarked on things you couldn't see yet, either through thick fog, or behind closed doors that hadn't opened yet, or out of order.  My character said they found what they were looking for, and then about a minute later said they need to find something for this.  There's a few times I had to reload saves because either I fell through the floor, or enemies I needed to kill to progress fell through the floor (mostly on elevators).  There's also a couple times floors disappeared completely but were still there.  Twice also I found game breaking bugs that I did everything needed to progress but either nothing happened, or the thing i need to interact with I couldn't.There's a line near the end of the game where my character says "I'm getting sick of this stuff", and I felt the exact same.  There's a lot of the same in this game.  Some of the "graphical prettiness" started to get annoying and made no sense too the more I played.Either way, this game is probably a recommend if you're just looking for a casual pretty game, but don't expect a lot from it.  I cannot recommend it myself.------------------------------Control Scheme I Used:Keyboard and Mouse default controls.Menus are clearly meant for gamepad, which is common, but certain things like upgrading abilities is strange because you can't hover over the item to see what the upgrade is before accepting to upgrade it, unless you use the keyboard arrows.------------------------------Worth the current price (CDN$ 28.99)?  Absolutely not.What I actually paid: approx $2.24 with Humble Monthly------------------------------Completionist Review:DLC Achievements: No DLC.Rating:  Hit or miss... depends on if you miss stuff your first play.Can be completed in one run:  Yes.Chapter Select: There is no chapter select, there are warp points, but if you've missed something, you cant go back to get it, you have to start a new playthrough.Did I need/use a guide?  Yes for the 2nd playthrough, although I probably didn't need it.This was brutal for me, although the game was only about 5 hours, I almost didn't want to complete it.  I had to run through the game a 2nd time to grab some things i missed on the first run, because you just can't get them if you've already picked everything up (you have to scan everything before you pick them up and things don't respawn ever).  I had to do a mixture of both playthroughs in the end to get the final 2 achievements.... somehow i didn't have enough resources on the 2nd run even though i'm pretty sure i did everything the exact same, but obviously not.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; A solid 3rd person action platformer that falls well short of its potentials. Worth checking out at a discount.Thumbs up here, but a VERY qualified one. My final opinion on The Gunk is mostly one of disappointment. There’s a lot of good to this game and it shows love and dedication from the team that made it… and it shows how little time it got, which is in stark contrast to the obvious passion of the creators. Visually, the game is stunning. Super high fidelity characters and environments with a unique and strong sense of style.Mechanically, the game is rock-solid. Your character controls exactly as one would hope and expect from the 3rd person action-platformer camera perspective.Writing-wise, the game is passable. “Down-on-your-luck space prospector” is a fun setup for exploring an alien planet and it does the job.Despite these positives, The Gunk does not even approach the potential of these pieces. The game is short, has very few enemies, fails to explore its movement and combat mechanics, and has a shallow, predictable story.This feels like a game that, a year away from completion, the team was told: “Ok, this looks great. We ship in a week.” There is the backbone for something special here and it’s really a shame that it doesn’t get to reach its potential. Still worth experiencing (at a discount), but a little bit tragic to be made to think about what it could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved my short & sweet time with this game. Whilst not the most deep game with the intense gameplay, this adventure does provide just enough light platforming, mild puzzling and sparse combat (all of which ramp up over the course of the game) to string you along the path of what is it's biggest appeal - the overall  of the thing.This game is absolutely STUNNING. It's not exceptionally detailed or anything, and doesn't look especially realistic, but it has a stylised presentation that is well polished on all fronts. The colours, lighting and effects are all a visual feast, and the environments are masterfully composed in such a way that there's almost always some jaw-dropping scenery to be looking at. The music is also just incredible; the soundtrack from Ratvader is so perfectly fitting to most every situation and scenario, it really helps to tie the experience together cohesively. Just the right emotive inflections or atmospheric swells, exactly where they need to be. I generally don't care much for game OSTs, but even I could honestly just listen to this one leisurely.The one area I guess I probably have an issue would be on the narrative front. I actually like the STORY - the overall plot, and the beats it hits. I just think the script is a bit ridiculous and trite, and the characters a little annoying. Neither of them do much to endear themselves to you, with your partner's tiresomely perpetual bad attitude and the player character's  need to narrate the adventure with pretty inane, naive whimsy gets very old by the end of it. The whole thing does at least come around to a satisfying end, but once I finished the story and went back to clean out the last achievements I honestly turned the dialogue volume to zero.Speaking of achievements, the game is pretty short - most people say a few hours, but it took me around six hours to finish a VERY leisurely playthrough, where I was exploring every nook and cranny and was constantly stopping to open the photo mode for screenshots (honestly, the game looks THAT good, I couldn't help myself). I then spent a couple hours backtracking just to clean out the last four achievements I'd missed. It's pretty difficult to get a 100% completion on a single consecutive playthrough unless you have a guide from the start, so to make it easier if you want to go back I would recommend manual saving OFTEN to give yourself plenty of story bookmarks to return back to.Overall, I find it very easy to recommend The Gunk. I got it from Humble Choice so I'm obviously pretty stoked, but even if you've had your eye on I feel like it's a worthwhile purchase -  on sale, but maybe even full price if the idea of just immersing yourself in a piece of interactive art is appealing enough.★★★★✰

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of the Gunk is simple: You're a black, midget space lesbian of the working class. Thanks to modern technology, missing arms can now be converted to high-powered vacuum cleaners capable of mining, harvesting plants, moving large pieces of trash and picking flowers. It's you and your lesbian lovers job to save this world the folly of it's inhabitants flagrant disregard for the environment. Stupid aliens, don't you realise you need the environment to live?Beck and Rani are partners (both in business and in bed). Beck, the ships pilot and the foil to Rani is a stick-in-the-mud / straight up B I T C H. Rani, the fun loving diversity-check box and adventurous one is a reckless idiot, so naturally it's your job to get out there as Rani and slurp up all the goo you can find because that stuck up ♥♥♥♥♥ Beck sure isn't going to help.It's Rani's job to guzzle down all the greasy goo in the game with her Glizzy-Glop-9000 vacuum cleaner. By sucking up the goo, you're saving the environment, allowing plant life to flourish and your character to progress puzzles or through the environment. The level design is linear, but the environments are open enough that it's easy to get turned around in the nooks and crannies where resources are hidden, but you'll never get properly lost and it's easy to get back on the main path.The controls are tight, Rani never felt 'out of control' in the platforming sections, but she's also not a particularly mobile character in this genre. Combat is limited and progression is really more about exploring the environment and creating paths ahead while removing the corruption. While I never hit that high of "having fun" with "The Gunk", I was never bored either and the time I spent playing it went by in a blur.I have a few complaints.1: The brevity of the game made me wonder why more of the game play elements weren't available to the player sooner.  The Gunk really comes in it's late-game acts with level design, and all the disparate elements of the game you've learned up to this point being thrown at you. Because the core of the gameplay *IS* so simple, it left me wishing that more of the early levels were this well designed, and the early mechanics explained more concisely. Decisions like depriving the player of the ability to shoot enemies until the late game seem strange. It's not as if the enemies are easier to deal with by doing so. A problem with most of the combat encounters is the game play loop is identical to cleaning the environment - in fact, you're often doing both at the same time so you can just *ignore* the enemies and sweep them up while you clean everything else. In fact, there's times where you don't even realise hostiles are there until one of them gets caught in your hand and you need to throw it away to resume clean up duties. By the time being able to shoot comes into the game play loop, there's maybe all of 10 enemies left in the game, and it really broke up the monotony of just vacuuming everything instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is pretty boring to be honest. The store description honestly feels very misleading. They say it's an action-adventure. The action is so minimal it shouldn't even be considered an action game at all, just an adventure. The environment is pretty but the whole game is running through very linear areas, collecting materials, and cleaning gunk. That's it. That's what the whole game feels like.I admittedly stopped after an hour and a half or so out of boredom and don't have much interest in returning to it. The store description also says, "duo of gritty space haulers" but they don't feel gritty at all. The dialogue between the two comes up often, probably to fill the dead space in the game as you run down a mostly empty path, but they sound the furthest thing from gritty. The main character that you play as just seems to enjoy nature and wants to explore it and look at stuff. The other girl is on the radio constantly complaining about how hungry she is. You also can't rebind the movement keys. They let you rebind all the other keys but not the movement keys for some reason. It's very strange. It won't affect many players but there are some of us that don't use WASD and we're stuck either using WASD or a controller.If you want a basic adventure game, you may like this. But that's strictly who this is for. I've seen such minimal action I wouldn't call it an action game at all. I haven't seen any puzzles yet. It's strictly just an adventure game with a standard story in a pretty world. There are plenty of other games with pretty worlds with more to offer. I'd suggest playing one of those.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really sucksThe Gunk is a game wherein you travel around an alien world, exploring and uncovering what occurred to its denizens. Following an energy source you run into the titular gunk which is killing the planet. You suck up the gunk which causes the area to spring back to life. It's pretty straightforward overall. Throw in some gunk enemies and some average platforming and light puzzle solving and you've got The Gunk.In terms of the gameplay, The Gunk really is quite simple but it controls well. You have a suck action which is used to suck up gunk, grab objects and enemies and to gather materials. You can launch held objects. You can jump and later down the line you can get some upgrades to aid in navigation and combat. All in all I think the gameplay is lacking. It feels good to play but I really wish there were more done with the mechanics and abilities. A double jump, a force push, pulling vines and swinging on them, hovering over obstacles with a blow etc etc. It really feels like wasted potential to me. The story, characters and writing are generally serviceable. The plot is pretty by the numbers and doesn't really have any twists though I did like the initial mystery of what has occurred and what the gunk is. The dialog is largely between the protagonist and the other person from the ship. I feel sometimes the dialog sounds clunky, possibly due to the performances or writing. Overall it's fine. The strongest part of the game lay in its aesthetics. I think the games visuals are fantastic overall. There are lots of moments with great looking areas and set pieces. Seeing areas come back to life is done really well too as are most of the effects, elements and plant life in the game. Additionally on the sound side of things, the soundtrack is engaging and adventurous and fits the beats of the story perfectly. All of the sfx are also done really well and are satisfying. All in all I feel a lot more love went into these parts of the game rather than the gameplay. All in all, this game reminds me of those random titles that would come out back in the PS2 era. You'd pick it up preowned because the box looked interesting and you have a decent time with it but it's nothing groundbreaking. All in all I had a decent time but it could have been a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a serviceable 3D platformer. I had thought about buying it more than once, but then I received it in my Humble Bundle monthly subscription and was excited to give it a whirl.The Good:The controls are precise. The sound design is decent. The puzzles are fairly simple but satisfying. The environments are pretty enough, but could use some additional biomes and variability.Slurping up gunk feels right.The Bad:I've read a lot of game reviews over the years where people complain about the voice acting and most of the time I thought it was overblown and petty, but YE GODS was the voice acting in this TERRIBLE. They can't even pronounce basic words like solder correctly. They pronounced it as "SOL-DER" instead of "sodder" and it's incredibly jarring and took me right out of the experience early on and it didn't get any better every time they said it.It also doesn't help that the dialogue feels like it was written by a 5th grader. I'm seriously not joking on that part. The back and forth banter is incredibly childish, and the drama between the two protagonists that comes in the second act comes completely out of nowhere and they are literally huffing at each other over absolutely nothing. They do not come across as a seasoned team of mining adventurers who've been together through years and made incredible sacrifices for each other, but rather a pair of emotionally stunted 12 year olds who met a few days ago and decided to be best friends without knowing anything about each other and then sparking off into a major fight after their first disagreement.The lore is equally brain dead. At one point you scan a chair and the lore states that it would be impossible for an alien species to come up with a CHAIR without first having contact with humans. Seriously!? A freaking CHAIR is something only humans could come up with? I worry for the mental health of the writers at this point. The story is your basic people abused nature too much and now you have to fix it that these kinds of games love to ham handedly shove down your throat as an allegory of human waste and pollution. The big bad even chides the humans (which he is somehow aware of despite there being no record of contact before) for destroying their own planet, seemingly completely unaware that he has been doing the very same thing for hundreds of years, so you'll forgive me if I'm not moved by his tongue lashing. The main gameplay loop has you go around slurping up "the gunk" which allows the area to return to life and open up new areas. Rinse repeat ad nauseum. Very similar to the mechanics of Okami, No Place Like Home, and Kena Bridge of Spirits. Unfortunately this game doesn't live up to the same potential as those games (which I also highly recommend), but it's not terrible overall.Enemies are almost non existent and trivially dealt with when they do appear. However, I did encounter a bug several times wherein one of the tiny enemies would yeet himself off a cliff but fail to hit the death plane and soft lock my game. Very annoying but only happened a couple of times and checkpoints are generous so not a lot of lost time for having to reload.The art design for the environments is pretty good. I especially liked the creativity of the "fowl tongue" designed to look like a goose tongue that unfurls into a makeshift bridge. I just wish that they had a bit more variance as once you've been through the first area you've really seen all the flora and fauna the game has to offer, so it gets repetitive fast.The character design is...awful...just awful. Good god Rani the main character looks like she was beaten with an ugly stick so hard that they probably should have cast the stick in the role instead. Probably would have been a better voice actor too. Second is a personal pet peeve of mine, but the "humans" only have 4 fingers. They weren't stylized enough to make this even somewhat ok in my book (ie the Simpsons). They look roughly like normal (ugly) humans, but they have these goblin hands that make you reel back when you first notice them. Finally the aliens look like they came directly out of a stock library of aliens, as I swear I've seen this very same design in several other games. Nothing terrible about the design, but it is incredibly generic for a game that is designed around presenting a pretty and intriguing aesthetic.Conclusion:Despite the terrible writing, story and ugly characters, the gameplay was decent enough and I had a good time. Thankfully the game is pretty short, any longer and the characters might have pushed me to set it down and step away, but it knew when to end it. If you're looking for a short 3D platformer with some interesting visuals then there are much better fare out there, but if you're intrigued by the art design, then by all means give this one a shot...but only if it's on sale.

However there was one part near the end where your traveling up an elevator and I was getting frequent significant frame-drops down to 15fps.- Good voice acting- Pleasant soundtrack.- Really nice game-play; vacuum up gunk, scan flora, vacuum resources, unlock upgrades both passive and some extra abilities and just explore the surface and caves of a mysterious planet. No way to turn of the chromatic aberration for example or adjust shadow dept individually.- The mouse isn't often supported for confirming things on the UI, you use the space button instead,- Lots of plants look like they can be scanned but can't- Can start to feel a bit repetitive.- Arguably the planet side can be too bright while the caves can be too dark. There is a brightness slider in the game but it obviously it effects both environments.Overall just a really chill experience to explore a planet with really nice visuals and calming soundtrack. _childDocuments_.review: "The Gunk" is not a bad game. It has decent graphics, a good art style, and interesting gameplay mechanics (cleaning the gunk and solving some small puzzles). Sucking in the gunk is satisfying, but gets a bit tedious until you have some speed upgrades.However, there are some negative parts that I must mention. Firstly, the game has platformer elements, but the jumping and climbing feels extremely janky. This is partly due to pretty terrible hitboxes (imo). If you hit something you are not supposed to hit, you just slide off. That is a possible solution to limit player movement but it is quite intrusive.Furthermore, the game's story is rather bland, it may have a few good moments. But overall it's just bland. The story feels like it's only there because it has to be.However, the worst offender, and this is just my opinion, are the characters. Not only are they as bland as the story, but Rani is one of the most annoying protagonists I've had the honor of playing. It's especially annoying when she talks while you're enjoying the scenery. This really annoyed me during the "Wasteland" part of the game. Fortunately, you can mute the voice dialog, which I did. I understand that the developers wanted to convey this as a moment of character development. But a character can grow throughout the game, not just 10–20 minutes of constant babbling. There were 4.x hours where the character had multiple opportunities to grow.I am most likely not the target audience as this is not a shooter, not a RPG and not an open world game. But I enjoyed the game somewhat and it was long enough. One positive point, not for the game, was that I got this through humble choice. I think €25 is a bit too much, but the price during the current sale feels fine.

_childDocuments_.review: - The visual design was unexpectedly good. For a dev that I knew exclusively from the Steamworld franchise, I was pleasantly surprised by the often very scenic 3D environments- The lighting effects are also quite good, which is very apparent given the huge variation in terms of light to dark environments- I'm a little less positive when it comes to the character designs. There's not many characters in the game, but they're all very cartoony. That's not inherently negative. It just feels inconsistent with the numerous serious narrative moments- The music is passable but maybe not memorable. The voice acting is pretty good all around, though. Both leads are able to make all the melodrama pretty convincing- And man, is there quite a bit of melodrama. As another entry into the pantheon of lesbian sci-fi romances (of which Steam has many), it's more on the serious side. It's not that there aren't comedic attempts, but the humor misses more often than it hits. The space/soap opera drama lands a bit better- As far as plot points go, you play as a down-on-your-luck spacefarer with a robot arm who lands on a mysterious planet that is being ravaged by the titular "gunk". Your romantic partner pilots the ship around while you handle the exploration and resource gathering- Eventually, you learn a bit more about the relationship of the gunk to the planet as well as its origins. However, your character's obsession with the mystery begins to cause friction with your partner and her more pragmatic financial concerns. The narrative conflict you're up against is twofold--you find your goals of saving the planet and saving your relationship at odds- The gameplay is fairly standard 3D platforming fare with the occasional dash of Powerwash Simulator thrown in- As you traverse the game's colorful environments, keep an eye out for upgrade materials that can be located with your scanner. With these resources, you'll be able to enhance standard things like the movement speed, health, and damage as well as more mechanically specific skills like the efficiency with which your arm vacuums up gunk- There are some platforming puzzles, but nothing that'll surprise or excite you if you've so much as sniffed a puzzle platformer in the past- The platforming is also pretty quotidian. Run. Jump. Grab a ledge. Maybe swing from a branch. I feel like the main character's robot arm is really underutilized in the context of movement and navigation- Combat is mostly fine. It's satisfying to vacuum up an enemy and blast his buddy with it. Your MegaMan blaster doesn't offer much beyond a stun setting, unfortunately. Like the platforming, I felt like combat could have used a little more variety. The robot arm is certainly used in combat, but the lack of melee really makes it feel like they could have gotten more mileage out of it. I get that it's a design choice. It's just one that makes little sense- The level design is actually pretty good. In addition to distinct visual designs, many of the areas (especially the architecture of the alien structures you explore) are really imaginative and a pleasure to navigate- I missed some achievements, upgrades, and collectibles in the course of beating the game, but I'm not feeling a replay is on the horizon. It's a fine game, but there aren't any branching paths or alternate endings to draw me back- I was pleased by the optimization and performance. My setup is only mid-tier, but this game ran extremely well with minimal tweaking.- Not much to report as far as bugs go. I experienced some "spaghettification" when graphics and collision physics disagreed about what I should be looking at, but that's not all that remarkable and certainly not game-breaking- In retrospect, I realize you could paint my critiques about movement and combat as a pointless wish that the game were more like one of the 3D Metroids (which is valid). I'm just saying that if you give a character a multitool robot arm that shoots lasers, there may be some preconceived notions- . It's a nice little dramatic story with cool that you can experience in 5-8 hours. The level design, lighting, and overall setting were pretty good too. Just wish the gameplay had a touch more to offer; both platforming and combat manage to feel stale despite how compact the game is. Feels like the existing pieces could have been explored a little further without adding fluff

_childDocuments_.review: No idea how I came across this game, but it was well worth the sell price. Took around 6hrs or so to fully complete. I probably spent more time than necessary trying to 100% it and find the remaining scannables. You can probably beat the game under 5hr 30min.That said, a pretty basic, yet addictive platformer. You control a vacuum arm basically and light laser blaster. The majority of the time however you'll be vacuuming up all kinds of things. Materials, switches, some blobs that you toss to activate doors and obviously the gunk. The gunk itself is rather unique to look at. It moves and flows and when you vacuum it up, it has a satisfying animation of being pulled apart. Eventually, when you clean enough of it up in a given area, you basically free it to allow the area to come back to life again.Visually, it looks outstanding. Like a quality little animated cartoon. The planet looks incredible and gives you plenty of awe struck moments as you traverse all around. This accompanied by the incredible soundtrack, gives the place a sense of wonder. Some of the animation on the main character however could have used a little more time, but you get over it quick (such as the walking/running animations). I also don't think the facial movements during conversations are all that great, but again, they get the job done.So yeah, I would recommend it for anyone that wants a short platformer that looks amazing (runs incredible despite the visuals) and gives you the sense of wonder. Just don't go in expecting a brilliant story or dialogue for that matter. They're not the greatest, but for the short time I had with the game, it didn't bother me as much as others may have complained. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: In the life of space haulers many owe their ships and their very souls to the companies that they work for. These companies are only interested in one thing and that is valuable resources on unexplored planets, some of these planets might end up killing a hauler, or they might even be simply the haulers’ final resting place, but there are those unknown planets out there that are brimming with resources that when all the stars aline a hauler cannot only make their quota but actually get ahead of what is demanded of them. In The Gunk you will be taking on the role of Rani, a hauler whose curiosity is more than likely to get them in trouble, and who is willing to risk life and limb to satiate that curiosity. The game starts with you landing on an unknown planet that is causing your sensors to go bonkers. If the sensors are right, the resources on this planet could be the “gold mine” that haulers dream of, but something isn’t completely right with this planet. Rani’s partner starts to get a bit antsy about what this planet might hide, but Rani can’t wait to get to the bottom of this mysterious planet. Of course this planet turns out to be more than Rani can chew, but that won’t stop them from digging deeper into the mysteries that keep popping up.Most of this game will be focused on puzzle solving and exploration, but don’t be fooled there are still plenty of battles that you’ll have to face, and plenty of different enemies that will try their best to defeat you. One of the game mechanics, which is optional, but I’m the type of gamer who has to take full advantage of it, is the research mechanic. As you progress through the game there’s going to be plants, enemies, structures, and more that you can scan with your glove. When you scan enough things you can level up which of course in turn will allow you to power up Rani. There are also items/ingredients to collect in the game that will allow you to upgrade your equipment (for example: make the suction power stronger).This was definitely a departure from the games that this developer has created, but I have to say that I enjoyed it from start to finish. Sure there were a couple of times where I got a little lost and so my progress slowed to a crawl, and there was also one specific enemy that made my number and I had to face off against it several times in order to win, but overall I really did enjoy this game. There was a part of me that wished the game lasted a little longer, but after putting in just under 4 hours I still feel like I got my money’s worth.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a new project from Image & Form Games, a studio best known for the SteamWorld series and also their first fully 3D title. And it’s pretty good.The game plays like a third person action adventure with platforming and slight focus on exploration and puzzle solving. And it’s hard to not see the influence of SteamWorld Dig in its design. As you explore an alien planet you landed on to find something good you could sell, you will be gathering resources for upgrades, just like you would in Dig. And even the titular “gunk” substance is reminiscent of mining in the Dig games. We even get a “huge robotic hand” again, though this time it’s used for shooting and sucking things in.That said, the overall experience of The Gunk is more streamlined and similar to a linear action adventure. There are occasional optional dead ends with resources, some of which require solving additional puzzles. Scanning different things unlocks further upgrades and this process is also mostly optional. But unlike Dig, you move forward down a specific path most of the time, solving problems that prevent you from doing just that along the way. There’s also a slightly bigger emphasis on the story (although the story did play a big part in Dig games too) and you can’t change the path through the locations like you could in Dig, but that is to be expected from a modern 3D title (I see you snickering in the corner, Red Faction).And while the game looks nice, the music is wonderfully fitting, the characters are cute and the story is intriguing, I couldn’t help but think that this is more of cool idea done well, not a title that is truly exceptional or super fun to play. It feels more like Dig 1, which was then expanded into the stellar Dig 2. So I could only hope that the next 3D title from the studio will only get better, now that they’ve got their feet wet.I liked The Gunk, even though it’s not amazing. It’s a good game that also lasts a nice 5-6 hours, so it gets to a satisfying conclusion before it starts getting boring. But I do hope that the next game will be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: It's quirky at times. Generally, you expect a puzzle-platform game to expose all of the basic movement tools early on, to let players learn and make levels more interesting to explore, but they only add the 'hanging backjump' kind of thing very late in the game (it's always there, but it serves basically no purpose). The 'running' shouldn't be an upgrade. Just give that to people right off the bat. The gunk-destruction is... quite slow at times, especially before getting the necessary upgrades, and because all materials are carefully given to you in small increments (even those you get from alien life, thanks to the limited respawning), you end up in a situation where not having an upgrade that they expected you to have leads to a very untenable situation.I give all this criticism because I genuinely like the game, though. It's fun, entertaining, and the levels are just long enough to let you enjoy the world while being short enough to let you relax and take it at your own pace. The plot line, while predictable, is enjoyable. And I genuinely think that this takes place in the Steamworld universe, especially with the references to earth.Anyhow. Good game. If you like Image and Form's method of storytelling (where things are hidden and implied and you have to learn things from a characters attitude more than their words), you'll have a good time. If you puzzle platformers or exploration games, grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunk is a game about two friends who run a small scavenging outfit together, and who travel from one space rock to another in search for resources they can harvest and sell. One day they land on a planet that looks dead from a distance, turns out to be unlike any other they’ve set foot on. A slimy parasite­ — or gunk — covers vast areas and seems to corrupt the otherwise vibrant nature and wildlife. It’s clear that they must fight this gunk to understand what’s happened and to save the dying planet. But this also creates a rift between them; on one hand, the planet will die if we don’t rid the planet of the gunk. On the other, we’ve got problems of our own and surely this isn’t our fight to begin with. So, who cares… right? Do we have to? [Thunderful Group]

detailed_description: Experience the third chapter of the Kazuma Kiryu saga with restored content in 1080p and 60fps. A year after the Kanto-Kansai all-out war, Kazuma Kiryu and Haruka Sawamura have left the unforgiving streets of Kamurocho for the island of Okinawa to run the Morning Glory Orphanage. Despite his efforts, shadows of Kiryu's past threaten to entangle the Morning Glory Orphanage in a deadly power struggle involving the Tojo Clan and political world. Thus begins a dramatic tale set in the ''sleepless city'' of Kamurocho in Tokyo and the tropical lands of Okinawa. Can Kiryu rescue the children of the orphanage from the looming threats emerging from the depths of the underworld and state power? Complete The Dragon of Dojima’s journey.

_childDocuments_.review: This game did a really good job at expanding the Kiryu lore and other aspects of his life and the Tojo Clan.The soundtrack was great, the story was amazing, and the new characters (or recurring characters) were really well-done as well.The one caveat I have is the battle system. Like most Yakuza/LAD games, the battle system can be really hit or miss. Y3's is pretty much all miss. By the end of the game, I found myself convincing myself that it "wasn't that bad", but then I remember every other part of the game and think: "oh yeah... that wasn't good".The reason a lot of fans of the franchise call Y3 "Blockuza" is because of the garbage mechanic which is that for every attack/combo/finisher that you do, the enemy will block 99.99% of those hits. And the other 0.001% of the time is the enemy counter-attacking you, forcing you to block (hence the given name).Battle system aside, I would really recommend this game (even if it was just a port of a PS3 title). 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and highly underappreciated in the Yakuza commuinity. Its got some of my favourite characters and possibly the best story of any Yakuza game. Fortunately we play on PC and can fix this issue with a single file that's less than 1MB, go look on the community page and find this fix before playing, there's also a mod that switches in-game models with highrez cutscene counterparts, recommend this too. Once you have these installed the game is very enjoyable.

The story was engaging and I enjoyed the new scenery of Okinawa. Kiryu in his tropical fresh tee is a great change of pace. Watching him fulfill his dream of owning an orphanage and how his old life catches up to him is a good story to experience.The music was decent, I cannot recall any particular pieces that were outstanding, but most were alright and fit Yakuza pretty well.Overall, if you are going through all the Yakuza games after playing 0 like I am, I'd recommend getting this without a doubt.
