_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to go on a little rant here. Yakuza 3 was a wierd one thats for sure. There were pros and cons and for most of the game, the cons were overwhelming the pros. The only thing that made me continue the game from around the halfway point was the thought of not playing all of them. I pulled through and got rewarded at around the last 3-4 chapters. The combat and the encounter rate were just straight up so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad. I'm not even joking when I say playing on hard was the biggest mistake I made while playing the yakuza series. I highly recommend playing it on medium or easy. I did not know why the game was also called blockuza 3 but now I understand completely. The combat system felt rushed. The skill point gain for pretty bad to say the least. The enemies you encounter on the street had around 1,5 - 2 health bars in around chapter 6. Money was always tight and getting money for taxis, heals, etc, was painful. The enemies and allies had little to no voice lines and repeated the same ones over and over. I remember when Rikia called me Aniki 8 times in 10 seconds, or when a thug on the street did HYAAAH 9 times in a row. It was bad, but I pushed forward and reward I got was the best story I ever seen, heard, read. Just the writing of the characters was so good. The cutscenes were full of life and everytime I entered one I was so happy. The deaths made sense, none were meaningless and could have been avoided. The story had depth, and made sense. In the end it was hard to decide if I like the game or hate it. After thinking it over I realized that I kinda liked it tbh. And honestly? I think if they decide to do yakuza kiwami 3 I'd buy it in a heartbeat. I think this game is worth the pricetag IF it's on sale. TLDR: I think its good ig.

_childDocuments_.review: After 0 and Kiwami 1 + 2, was expecting a huge drop in quality given that this game is now the most dated in the main series + this entry is often regarded as worst in the series.   I found it to be surprisingly excellent. Story:  The main story does have kind of a slow burn early on, but it adds to the plot in a deliberate and meaningful way that allows the story to build on itself and have events carry more weight.  If you enjoyed the other Yakuza game stories, there is a high chance you will appreciate this one.  It fits in well as continuation from Kiwami 2.  If its your first Yakuza game, it works well as a self contained story, and it provides recaps on the main points of past events.  Graphics:  At 4k max settings 60 fps this game actually looks amazing for a 2009 Ps3 title.  It is close to par w/ yakuza 0 and Kiwami 1.   Also, there is the added visual variety from having a new major location (Okinawa) in additional to Kamarocho .  Sound:  Top tier soundtrack that compliments the experience well.  Gameplay:  The overall game structure is actually really similar to Yakuza 0 to Kiwami 2.   If you liked the gameplay in those, there's a high chance you'll appreciate it here.  Enemies do seem to block more than in other entries; however, this entry allows you to acquire extremely powerful moves pretty easily and early on (like the Komaki Parry + Tiger Drop + most of the tech abilities).  The combat might be also a little stiff compared to other entries, but it did not feel like a jarring change at all.  It actually felt like it made sense, because at this point in the story, Kiryu is almost 40 years old.  Last, mods improve the experience even more.  Here is the list of mods i used:-Silent Patch-Yakuza 3 Licensed Music Video and Uncensor Restoration Patch-High resolution character textures (for nearly all characters) mod-Quickstep Restoration-Removal of the loud ambient audio in Downtown Ryukyu to better match the PS3 and PS4 versions.

_childDocuments_.review: The least technically impressive of the series, as it is sans a Kiwami full remake and is instead a 2009-ass game with a new coat of paint. Still, it is very playable, one might even say enjoyable, and while not perfect, even the developers themselves acknowledged and learned from their missteps in this entry to create better stories moving forward. This can eb seen in a small substory in K2, where a stand in NPC for the director of Yakuza 3 is sad that his game was so poorly received, even though he had the best intentions and thought his story was good. The substory ends with the director of the first two Yakuza games saying he enjoyed the new installment, despite its faults, and the new director vows to improve his craft and agrees to make the fourth installment. All that is to say, lampshading a problem doesn't make it go away, but leaning from it can lessen the blow. Given that I still have at least five more games after this one until I am caught up with the narrative, I can rest assured they have improved their craft and taken the failings of Yakuza 3 to heart. That being said, Yakuza 3 is by no means a complete failure. The cabaret system is a joke compared to the earlier-set but later-made instalments that I played previously, but it is clear that they served as inspiration for those minigames that I so enjoyed. This was also the first game to introduce Karaoke, now a staple of the series, and the setting of Okinawa is a lovely piece of serenity to enjoy after the Mission Impossible levels of stress Kiryu has endured for the last 20 years. Taking into account Yakuza 0 an the added minigames of the Kiwamis, which at the time, weren't canon to this game, Kiryu has been a real estate magnate, gone to prison for a decade, lost several loved ones and friends, fought his way to the top of the Yakuza, the Korean Mafia AND the triads multiple times and lost two true loves in the space of a year (imagine making Kaoru so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hot to do nothing ubstantial with her, wtf RGG). Man needs a break, and his adopted daughter Haruka and the other orphans he takes under his wing bring him that closure of raising those in a similar position to himself at a young age to be better than he had to become. The pacing of this game can, at times, feel a little...epileptic in how it jumps from world-altering spy thriller to homely orphan child's play, but honestly, having now finished the game, and without spoiling why, although the execution was FAR from perfect, the amount of time spent with the children and the orphanage, and the time spent with Mikio, Rikiya and Nakahara and their interactions with the children was, dare I say NECESSARY for the final act of the game to actually function at all. I understand why for many, this one point alone is enough to make this game feel like a "side quest" or not very interesting, but seeing Kiryu relaxed at first, just enjoying his life with these kids, only for that illusion of peace to be shattered over and over until he finally snaps wouldn't have hit as hard if the often tedious children sections had been cut for time. A necessary evil, that I wouldn't want to repeat, but I respect and understand. The combat was one thing I was warned about going into this, and was told in no uncertain terms that anything above "easy" difficulty would border on rage-inducing. This was very good advice, perhaps too good, as now the one who told me that looks a little insane to me, simply because the combat was genuinely quite fun. Having the difficulty that low meant enemies were quite fair and the damage I could sneak in around their infamous "hold block forever" mentality was far more rewarding that it would have been on normal or hard. Still, relatively speaking this was the weakest combat system that I have played with, and I didn't engage with enough side content to actually progress it very far, though this wasn't all that concerning given my difficulty level (I reached 12% completion overall). The main story was patchy in terms of quality, falling somewhere between K1's simplicity and 0's convoluted web of lies and political backstabbing that you needed a mindmap to unravel. The final 4 hours were very good though, and the death of a certain character genuinely made me quite sad, again because of HOW MUCH TIME was spent establishing their rapport with Kiryu and the kids. The main villain was a very cool fight, but had a pretty shoddy motivation after all that buildup, and a melodramatic drawn-out death, but still, dragging the American secondary boss off a building as he screams in English gets bonus points for originality for a mainly Japanese audience game at the time. Yakuza 3 is a flawed, yet well-intentioned attempt to follow up VERY good original games, but now unfortunately has the unenviable task of following up far superior remakes of said originals, and the graphical drop from K2's Dragon engine to the PS3-ass polygons is ROUGH. Still, the love and care is commendable, the effort clear from the word 'go', and while certainly nowhere near the quality of the rest of the series, should definitely not be skipped (though maybe play on easy).6.5/10 - wouldn't play again, but doesn't deserve to be skippedEdit: I should also mention that Majima plays a large role in the narrative and has some genuinely funny and wholesome moments. Can't play as him, or team up with him in combat but damn is it good to see him with such a large impact on the plot. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2009,  was a huge step forward for the  game series in terms of gameplay and graphics. It’s the first main series game to feature a controllable game camera for the adventure portion, and to introduce more elaborate side content that would become synonymous with  games. Visually, the power of the PlayStation 3 allowed major characters to be depicted with greater detail and realism, cementing their iconic designs. These advancements laid the technical and stylistic foundation for future  titles in the main and spin-off series.The technical and stylistic similarities between  and future  games meant it didn’t require the major overhaul that  and  needed in bringing it over to modern platforms. It’s therefore understandable that developers at Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio decided to remaster  than to remake it, especially when they were also working on  and , as well as remastering  and  around the same time.Sadly,  is not a great remaster, in part because of the uneven remastering workmanship. The flaws of , on the heels of the superb  and the excellent  and , were also amplified in comparison and with time. What we ended up with is a game that showed us that  should have been remade – that is given the  treatment – instead of remastered. is a decent looking game on modern platforms. While it’s obvious that the character models have fewer polygons than those in more recent games, they look good enough even when upscaled to 1080p from the original 720p resolution. However, some textures, such as those for male hands, still appear low-res. In-game cinematic sequences also look decent, but pre-rendered cutscenes were simply resized from 720p without any additional image sharpening or colour adjustments done. The contrast between in-game and pre-rendered visuals is quite jarring, making  look unpolished.The visual inconsistencies could be forgiven if the gameplay is solid. Unfortunately,  is a bit of mess under the hood. Although the PC version can run at framerates higher than 60 fps, it’s not fully optimized for it. A few minigames (e.g., fishing, massage parlour) are actually harder to play if they’re run at above the original 30 fps cap. I suppose you can play  at 30 fps at the expense of smoothness in graphics, but that would defeat the point of playing a game that was specifically and supposedly refurbished for modern systems.The inherent framerate issue also affects combat, which is the core of  games. For some reason, basic quickstepping doesn’t put adequate distance between you and your enemy, making the technique rather useless until you’ve upgraded it. Quickstepping behind your enemies so you can strike them from behind is also difficult to pull off at above 30 fps. These are flaws that should have been detected and fixed during the remaster, and not doing so only made  feel like an unfinished product.Yet, two of the biggest problems with combat in  (reportedly carried over from ) are enemies blocking attacks too often and swarming you in all directions at the same time. I guess these are meant to add a touch of realism to the game, but they don’t make it fun. These become a major problem when you try to build up Heat for special moves and takedowns. You can’t build up Heat when enemies are blocking, and Heat also depletes if you get hit or if you’re idle. Downing a couple of Tauriner or Staminan drinks is a quick workaround, but even with sufficient Heat, timing your Heat Action execution can be tricky – again, possibly due to framerate issues. It’s often frustrating, and I did finish the game at normal difficulty by learning to circumvent this semi-broken combat system. But, it shouldn’t have been this way. was originally the third part of Kiryu’s story, with him now running an orphanage in Okinawa. On the surface, it’s a tale of Kiryu going up against the yakuza who wants to seize the land on which the orphanage sits. At its core, it’s about vulnerable and abandoned people looking for love, support and acceptance. In fact, the first third of  focuses on Kiryu being father figure to the orphans he is looking after. It’s actually a refreshing change of pace in line with Kiryu’s post-yakuza life. It’s not until Chapter 5 of 12 that he returns to Kamurocho to take care of business.Unfortunately, outlandish plot devices and set pieces muddle the otherwise awesome story of one man versus the yakuza to protect the children he cares about. Although  and  are bizarre and incredible in their own ways,  dials the absurdity up to eleven, so much so that it’s more like a story dreamed up by prepubescent boys, with story beats clearly taken from prominent films, including a couple by Francis Ford Coppola.The story’s pacing is also very uneven, necessitating in dedicating a whole chapter three-quarters into the game for exposition by a single character to explain the convoluted plot. Instead of revealing the main antagonist’s motivation bit by bit throughout the game, it has him describe it in full prior to the final showdown. The ending feels like a quick fix for a major plot hole, and any tension and significance it might have had is then quickly resolved with a post-credit scene. It’s such a mess that I feel ,  and  form a better, more complete story arc for Kiryu than ,  and . might have been good back in the day, but in the decade that followed, many innovations and refinements have been made to this game franchise’s gameplay and graphics. Remastering  without fixing flaws that negatively affect the original gameplay, and without doing a thorough job in upscaling the graphics is simply inadequate for a title that follows the ,  and . No wonder  feels dated, unpolished and incomplete.Considering  was a pivotal title for the game series, it deserved better. But, I get why RGG Studio and SEGA didn’t give  the  treatment: it made no sense for them to spend time and money on recreating assets that won’t be used in future titles. After all,  games are lower-budget titles made to look like AAA games. But as a result,  is now seen as the worst game in the series for the wrong reasons.A properly made remaster could have salvaged ’s reputation, even with the absurd plot elements that didn’t age well. At the end of the day,  completionists would buy this game – likely as part of the  – regardless of its quality. I may give it a thumbs down in this review, but I think at the very least it’s worth playing the first few chapters to see Kiryu’s gentler, loving side that contrasts his Dragon of Dojima persona. It’s really too bad that the rest of the game couldn’t be as straightforward as Kiryu’s life in Okinawa, but instead become more unnecessarily complicated, much like his time in Kamurocho.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is playing the Yakuza series for the first time, in chronological order, this game is just okay.TLDR; gameplay and story is weak compared to 0, K1 and K2 but still worth trying.Since it's only a remaster, unlike Kiwami 1+2, and 0, which is a comparatively newer game, the expectations to meet fall short for Y3R.The controls just don't feel as nice, and if you're playing this game just to get the full story of the series, I would suggest either playing on easy or just skipping it all together.Usually, the story makes up for lulls in the gameplay, but the characters felt like they were just lacking oomph, especially compared to Kiwami 2 which arguably has my favourite characters. Without spoiling, the characters just didn't really feel like they meant business, or just that by this point in the Yakuza story much bigger fish have been fried.This in conjunction with the combat really doesn't bode well. It's like everybody has titanium forearms, and can just block anything. Of course, if you're good at the game, this isn't a problem, but it's really annoying when you just wanna beat the crap out of your enemies. What makes this even worse is the bosses.The bosses are, in large part, not fun. I only recall two good boss fights in the entire game. The reason behind this is, again, the excessive blocking. To add on top of this, the bosses just take waaay too long. It's either because your attacks just don't do much damage compared to other games, or the bosses just have way more health than what they need. It feels so so bloated.Having said that, it still has it's memorable Yakuza charm - the silly substories, the exciting cinematics, the awesome music, it retains all the charm I've seen from "previous" entries. It's enough to make me want to sit through the aged combat system and progress the story, which is still pretty good.In conclusion, I would still recommend playing this game, just definitely not for the gameplay. I've just started Yakuza 4 Remastered, and it plays a lot lot better. Though, if janky controls from the early PS3/late PS2 era don't fit the bill, the game isn't strong or significant enough to the overarching story to be considered an essential play in my opinion, so don't feel discouraged if you feel like skipping it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even really know what to say to be honest, I'm writing this review after just completing the main story line and I don't really know what else to say but wow. I won't lie, I was a bit worried that as I progressed through the Yakuza saga that the quality in these games would begin to fade, but I couldn't say how wrong I am so far. This game was no disappointment, and continues the pretty amazing theme of the yakuza games, as well as being able to evoke emotions just as well as the previous installments. As I stated before, the story of Yakuza 3 is great. I feel like it did an amazing job of allowing the player to create solid bonds and attachments to the other characters, especially that parental connection between Kiryu and the kids at his orphanage, and that brotherly bond with Rikiya. I thought at this point in the Yakuza series I would have experienced so many emotions through Kiryu, like his genuine happiness, sadness, or anger, that I would grow numb to it. Again, I was dead wrong, and Yakuza 3 accomplished all three of those for me once again. One thing I would like to especially address is the combat system for Yakuza 3. One of the main complaints I have seen for Yakuza 3 is that its combat system is lacking compared to its predecessors, or that people just straight up can't put up with it. I personally think it is too easy to just compare Yakuza 3's combat to 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2 just because they are so great, but on its own Yakuza 3's combat system was bearable to me, and honestly wasn't bad at all. To be absolutely fair, yes I do prefer and more enjoyed 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2's combat gameplay, but I also appreciated Yakuza 3's combat system in its own way. I truly hope that the combat system alone isn't what turns people away from this game, because those who do skip Yakuza 3 are missing out on a pretty amazing continuation of Kiryu's story. TLDR: I absolutely do recommend for the story alone, and once again I look forward to the next chapter, Yakuza 4 Remastered.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, Yakuza 3 suffers from some at times abysmally bad pacing, enemies block too much ESPECIALLY in the remastered version, and there are some DUMB pulls in the plot.That said, it's in my top 3 favorites of the whole franchise, as much as I think they should be optional the stuff with Kiryu's kids is adorable and provides a really fun alternate perspective to watch him through, and Ryukyu is one of the absolute comfiest video game towns I've ever explored, bar none.So, most of my problems with this game specifically lie with this specific port. Optimization is awful, load times take way longer than they SHOULD for how small these maps are, and... the Big One, because the game's framerate was increased from 30 to 60 FPS, Kiryu's quickstep is pitifully useless. The first two can't be easily solved, but you can find a patch on Yakuza 3's nexusmods page to (mostly) restore his quickstep to its original PS3 form.You'll probably find yourself tempted to skip cutscenes from time to time, and you'll probably end up screaming at the screen for Kiryu to stop wasting time with his kids, but Yakuza 3 is a really, really good game, even in this compromised port. Pick it up, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: So yet another Yakuza game under my belt. It's remastered, but it hasn't been revamped like the kiwamis so it looks a little rough sometimes. I hear a lot of people complaining about combat. It's not debilitating but it definitely does not have the polish I'm used to. Yakuza is inevitably a lot of button mashing... IDK this felt like a WHOLE lot more button mashing with not as many combos to break up the monotony. I think my favorites as far as ANYTHING goes were Kiwami 2 and Yakuza 0.The story was a bit complicated... more so than usual in my opinion, and I found myself getting a bit bored. If it tells you anything... I was falling asleep during the last chapter. Like... I remember why I fell in love with this franchise, they usually do a great job of amping you up. There's this tension that gets built beautifully and then you unleash. I didn't get this here... not really at least. Anyway, It got interesting again when the cut scenes picked up at the very end though. Also... the map is not the best. I remember driving myself crazy trying to get to a location marked on the map only to realize that there were stairs somewhere and what I wanted was on the second floor. Also to see a street name, you have to zoom in on the map. You'll see. The map is not terrible but if you've played earlier yakuzas you will realize you've been spoiled.The inventory system seemed a lot slimmer than usual... so that was annoying. Also at restaurants, you could not have Kiryu try multiple items at once. So it takes a lot more time to complete the menus on restaurants.So spoilers here. I've noticed that anytime there So yeah the writers keep reusing the same tropes. Also, the end Okay so what DID I like? I liked that this game does not just HAND things to you. Like for example with substories, they'll tell you the name of something sometimes not even marked on the map and you just gotta get there. There are better examples but you'll see what I mean. There is also this new system of unlocking moves through zany little cut scenes. Kiryu and Mack call them revelations. They all go on Kiryu's nifty little blog.  As usual, I liked the substories (did not like the interface in keeping track of them) - those were always fun.The host club mini game was a lot different and perhaps not as fun but I liked that they changed it up! Also the characters that it presents are generally very lovable or interesting and you wanna know more. Like in the beginning, they did a good job of connecting you to each of the children, Date is back as with the boys from Stardust. We get new characters like Rikya, who are really great to get to know. For Kiryu,  Despite all my complaints I can give this an 7/10. I would say that it is a must-play if you are going to continue in the series. and please remember that it is remastered. It's not going to be as clean as 0 or the Kiwamis. So with all that said. Decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard a lot about Yakuza 3. Some people have said it was the worst in the series, some people said they liked it or had mixed feelings, and some people just couldn't get into the graphics. Having fought my way through three games prior, I finally got to play this little gem wanting to find out for myself. I honestly believe this series is very well structured and a blast to play, and I have nothing but great things to say about it so the only logical game to review, if any, would be this one.Although it didn't have a lot going for it graphically I would go as far as to say Yakuza 3 had some of my favorite combat mechanics out of all four games thus far. It's a lot more methodical and the abilities you learn feel much more rewarding. It was less about smashing square and triangle and more about countering the enemy or finding unique ways to use your heat. It struck me as everything a game should be. Having consistently played Yakuza on hard mode, I expect the need to utilize every tool at my disposal. If I have to do that then it's a pass. Of course, the game got easier, but that's what being rewarded for putting in the time is all about. Every point spent and skill chosen creates more possibilities and better improves Kiryu from faster attack speed to much-needed heat moves, and those heat executions are wild. Most importantly, you  the strength as you gain skills and new methods become accessible. 3 begins very slowly, but the ramp feels smooth and fun.I think the story is strong. It has shoddy parts but all of the themes that it presents definitely circle back around and the symbolism is on point. The kids are symbolic, and you get to know the family as Kiryu's struggle continues. Some of it is too on the nose though, like but I did like the antagonist(s) and thought some of them were comical. The heavy themes in this one are pretty brilliant.It's very weak in the mini-game department for me. That's about all I have to say about that. I found myself spending hardly any time on mini-games this go around.It's a shame that this didn't get the Kiwami treatment because I think it could have been incredible if it did. Either way, Yakuza 3 brings something a little more old-fashioned to the table and fits comfortably in the series with its own unique and classic style.I appreciated this and look forward to the next.As always, thanks for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a bit tricky to rate. One the one hand it has an amazing story with one of the most brutal moments in the series. On the other - gameplay with a combat that didn't age very well.The story starts slow with showcasing what Kiryu did after Yakuza 2. He opened an orphanage in Okinawa and with Haruka takes care of a large group of children. Okinawa is really beautiful and chill city, it's a nice change of atmosphere after previous games. Then Kiryu again gets caught in some crap (he just can't find peace in this world) and we get a classic yakuza crime story with a well done combination of funny goofiness and brutal moments.And then there's a combat that makes me wish Yakuza 3 was a remake like Kiwami instead of remaster. It's too clunky and notorious for it's tedious fights where enemies block, dodge and make you stunned way too much - doesn't matter if you fight a skilled fighter or some random street thug. Skills take too much time to learn compared to how long it takes to finish the main story. There's also master Komaki in this game, but I never found him.I still highly recommend playing this game just for the story, it's so good that you won't mind the gameplay flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, especially after so many hours of gameplay, but I just can't. People say it is the worst of the series, and they are right. Fanboys huff my balls.Despite a somewhat decent storyline, pacing is really sloppy in certain areas (ie. being prompted by the game to go to the Okinawa airport, only to be pulled back to the orphanage twice for extremely mundane plot filler, and THEN FINALLY being able to go to Kamurocho)Fights are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare, even streetfights in late game when you have more skills. Heat action prompts only show up half the time despite fulfilling requirements, and even then, they do next to no damage. Parry doesn't work at all (R1 then B; I never got the prompt in the 100+ hours of playing) and blocking is useless because even street thugs immediately break through it and beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of you before you can even raise your arms again. Blocking doesn't even raise your heat like it does in other games, so what is the point in having the block if it never works? Weapon attacks are more useless than trying to use your fists to break through the enemy's guard (even weapons with high attack do next to no damage), so there's hardly any point in buying/modding weapons, or using them at all. Grabs only work a quarter of the time (even street thugs just push you off and stun you) and do hardly any damage when they do. So the only way you can do any damage AT ALL is to spam ♥♥♥♥♥♥ heat actions until you can use Hell's Gauntlet (the only attack worthy of being called a 'finisher'). There's no way to be creative or actually have fun with this fighting engine, except with some of the earlier hitman missions. If you don't fill your inventory with Tauriner ++, you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥. ♥♥♥♥ THE CHASE ENGINE♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ guys I never experienced a gamer moment until I had to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chase Mac S I X TIMES on N O R M A L. The opportunities to tackle are so few and far between and dashing is completely useless because they just speed up when you do, and slow back down when you don't dash. And, because of course it is, it is EVERYWHERE in this game. Yes, I know you can train chasing with Mac, but the only course that is actually doable is the first one, which extends the amount of time you can dash for. At least the chase engine gets cleaned up a bit in Yakuza 4 (check out my lengthy review for that one too).Let's talk minigames:♥♥♥♥ pool and its entire life. This game clearly hates hot girls with iron deficiencies like me, where you have to keep the trigger COMPLETELY straight in order to make a proper shot. I can't believe how sensitive they made the curve for pool. I've poured hours into the pool minigame alone and can only beat the beginner pool challenger half the time because of the stupid curve. My ego is in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ground because of how many fouls this baby can fit in it (I do not get nearly as many fouls in other Yakuza pools, excluding 4)Baseball and its accompanying substory is easy enough, it's not nearly as much of a grind as Kiwami, but unfortunately there isn't a prompt to hit the ball at the right time like there is in Y5 and 6 (and probably others), so it is more of a headache for some. ♥♥♥♥ the bowling pin physics, guys. Why they so heavy and also not move like pins. It's so whack and I can't believe I got the turkey achievement. It only took me 2000 tries to bowl over a 200 and now I am procrastinating the substory that comes with that burden.Darts is fine. I've never raged so hard at a claw machine teddy bear beforeDon't @ me about any of the gambling mini games or shogi/mahjong. Who the ♥♥♥♥ knows how to play Mahjong. The hostess club mini game is,,, Once you accrue enough items to actually be able to dress up the hostess, it's okay. Though, for how expensive some of the items are, your hostess really doesn't make enough money. I'm almost done training my 4th hostess and I barely have 400,000 saved... how the hell am I supposed to be able to buy things that actually boost stats if, after that much gameplay, I have that little and a flower ring is 32,000,000. How do you make money? Am I missing something?At least street fights, though way too frequent, often give you decent money to ball a little bit (I was able to start hitting up hostess clubs and buy luxury healing items very early game)Visiting hostess clubs is fine. It's easy enough without a guide for some of them, but a couple of the hostesses were so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insufferable and nonsensical that I didn't want to finish them (But I did) (It was Saya and Yui; especially Yui's substory ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what a self-entitled brat)Apprehending all the hitmen is easy enough. It is certainly a grind, but these fights actually have different styles, and a good amount of them don't require just heat actions to be able to do. Anyways, I think the only redeemable part of this game is the substories. Some people may hate how many there are and want to focus on main story, but I like side quests, and a lot of them give you money, so sue me for being a bourgeoisie ♥♥♥♥.Putting so many hours into completing this godforsaken game just shows my dedication to this series. Anyways, Majima game when?

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, after more than 10 years as a Playstation exclusive, the third canonical entry to the Yakuza series arrives on the PC. Here in its remastered version. Set chronologically 3 years after the previous entry, legendary yakuza Kiryu Kazuma has left behind organized crime and the dark alleys of Kamurocho for sunny Okinawa and a peaceful life as an orphanage manager, along with his beloved adoptive daughter Haruka. Unfortunately, a proposed resort deal to be built on the grounds of his orphanage comes to disturb his peace and pull him back to a world he thought he had escaped.The initial setup of the game is very well crafted. Okinawa is a beautiful new location to explore. The local "friendly-neighborhood" yakuza family that Kiryu befriends introduces some pretty likeable characters. The orphanage itself is also very pleasant and all children have a memorable moment or two. Kiryu's philosophy on childrearing fits more with the late 80s and early 90s rather than the late 00s, but that is certainly part of his character and following his firm but extremely caring parenting can be quite heartwarming. Kiryu in general shines in this game, perhaps more so than usual, being a parent suits him. This beautiful atmosphere obviously helps heighten the stakes as the orphanage and the children within find themselves under threat. The plot, by its very nature, is also very high stakes. As Kiryu tries to unravel the mystery behind the resort deal he is thrown in the middle of a conflict that doesn't just include various yakuza factions, but top-level politicians, international crime syndicates and the very CIA itself. All that while a mysterious man that bears an uncanny resemblance to Kiryu's long-dead stepfather, Kazama Shintaro, is implicated in the elimination of Kiryu's allies. Unfortunately, the way the mystery is resolved and the finale itself are not as compelling or satisfying as the setup. Let's just say that trying to excuse a heinous villain with a lame sob story was already not serviceable in the 80s, much less today.The game's main gameplay loop, street fighting, handles quite well. A return to form after Kiwami 2's rather lackluster combat system. Kiryu is an absolute beast. The skill progression present does mean you won't unlock many of the most entertaining moves until pretty late in the game. But even the basic moveset is more than adequate and the game did keep me looking for mooks to floor well into the post-game. Speaking of random encounters, I should note that aside from entertaining, they can also annoy at times. They are too frequent. That's fine when roaming, not so much when they constantly interrupt you while on your way to somewhere. And I really do have to ask, what kind of braindead two-bit thug sees a monstrously ripped dude, surrounded by a flaming aura and says "that's the guy I wanna jump"?Aside from the main plot and combat, the game treats the player to the usual buffet of quirky substories and minigames. There are several memorable substories, including one where Kiryu is investigating a murder all Hercule Poirot style, gathering all suspects for the grand reveal scene in the end included. The various leisurely mini-games can also offer hours of entertainment. I don't think I've ever enjoyed golf before as much as I did in this game. But bowling or pool is also lots of fun. Then there is the hostess management minigame. Coming from Kiwami 2 and its excellent version of that minigame doesn't help, but the version found here is disappointingly subpar anyway. Likewise, there is a rather poor chase minigame that for whatever reason was also included in the main story. Thankfully only briefly.All in all, this game is fairly typical Yakuza-fare. That's a good thing. It is not the best Yakuza game out there but it is absolutely a good game. Fans of the series will find a lot to like here. Of course, if you are a newcomer to the series I would recommend starting with the exceptional Yakuza 0 instead. Besides, I believe the games should be played in order. Either way, this is a thumbs up. Bought in a package with 4 and 5, it is excellent value for money too.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is dated. It'll hit you more so if you come from Kiwami 1 and Kiwami 2.That much is a given, as opposed to making Kiwami/Extreme versions, they opted to Remaster and port them.Playing on Hard Difficulty, the game experience is very difficult to just hop straight into.For the story, The story itself attempts to split itself between Kiryu's life at the orphanage as well as the main ongoing plot -- as expected, there will be times that these two blend together but it will not be to a heavy degree. The former is used as a way to break the tension between the plot.While it is understandable that the story after all is just point A to point B, you cannot help but feel as if what you're doing is a waste of time during these moment to moment things.That feeling is an indicator that a game is losing your interest. I got this feeling multiple times during these Morning Glory segments. Definitely apparent at the beginning of the game (it does not try to grab your attention, it quickly attempts to build the new world that you're in, as Kiryu is no longer in Kamurocho.)It is not to say that these segments are all bad.I think the amount of perspective that these children give and how they act is pretty natural and insightful -- not counting a very specific one relating to money issues, that truly was a comic relief plot. The gameplay is not worth the attention, but the story and their corresponding cutscenes is worth your watch.Now I usually focus on the gameplay and that is where it is  to play.As an action RPG, it can be granted that you will not start off at your best.Combat will feel very stiff but this stiffness will last a  with Yakuza 3.Like the moniker, Blockuza 3, enemies block A LOT in this game. However, if this was all there was to it, then it wouldn't make much of a difference. To me, enemies and bosses feel ,  making it frustrating on your part.It's not just blocks that can frustrate you.- I've seen most people say it's just grab-grab, but then you run into enemies who resist or outright nullify grabs.- Enemy attacks have an INSANE amount of tracking to their moves. Simple explanation, some attacks have enemies home in on you so hard that even if you stand behind them, they will autocorrect themselves to perfectly turn around and hit you.- Enemies are also sometimes much faster and also recover from your attacks faster. This means that some moves you will not do since they act faster than you -- usually a simple punch or two, but a full-fledged combo from bosses.- Also have noticed that some also are input reading(?) or rather move reading? Some moves are immediately countered each time, save for attacks that you are doing in the middle of them getting up from the floor. Bonus points if the move has super armor.The result is that enemies feel like they are playing an  game than you and not in a good way. So back to yourself, how does it feel controlling Kiryu?The game has  chapters total. I did not feel much in control until Chapter 10.Some skills -- like resisting stronger attacks, second follow-up to your combos,  the Komaki line of techniques (THE MOST IMPORTANT, DO NOT SKIP IF YOU CAN), and specific heat actions (there's one multi-enemy heat action that will save you WONDERS) are not a suggestion but a necessity to elevate the experience.However, they are not there in natural progression -- you can miss them if you zoom too fast through the story.  Either from ignoring side content or from lack of EXP.Despite these, you will still feel clunky to an extent controlling Kiryu. This is primarily because a GREAT deal of your attacks are very committal. If you start a basic combo, you damn sure are gonna finish it.You will lean in heavily to your defensive options, however enemy AI at times default to "Don't attack, wait to block/evade Kiryu's attack(s) before retaliating", forcing you to act first and sealing your defensive options.Since you must commit to your attacks, you cannot block/evade as quickly. If I could compare, it's as if you are always on Y0 Beast Style while every enemy can use Rush Style (or sometimes Brawler) I would say the amount that I played, I did get used to Y3's combat -- you do figure out enemy quirks but you'll quickly understand that getting hit is definitely going to be inevitable. I could only believe that the combat would be even more enjoyable if I had grinded out more skills. Funny is by the time I completed the game, I was one level away from gaining an enhancement to Kiryu's Quickstep (not barring that it's broken on this port).Despite my criticism, I'm still gonna recommend a play if you're going through the Yakuza games. Bringing price point into the mix, sale or not -- I say that you are still getting bang for your buck in part of it being a Yakuza game.  At the very least, in terms of similar feeling games in franchises, I would take this over Devil May Cry 2 -- which actually put me to sleep mid-combat several times (To an extent I still enjoyed DMC2 still though).Try to wait for a sale solely because this game, or rather the remastered collection, ends up on sale frequently to the point that you are just wasting money buying it full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 unlike the earlier titles on steam uses an older engine thus has some quality of life changes missing from the other games. The biggest gripe people have with it is combat because of how much enemies block you. _childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3: A Promising Yet Flawed Entry in the SeriesRating: 3/5 starsYakuza 3, the third installment in the beloved Yakuza series, brings players back into the seedy underbelly of Kamurocho with its trademark mix of crime drama, intense combat, and immersive open-world exploration. While it retains many of the elements that made its predecessors so engaging, Yakuza 3 falls short in several key areas, leaving fans feeling somewhat disappointed.One of the biggest letdowns in Yakuza 3 is its pacing. The game starts off slowly, taking a considerable amount of time to build up the main plotline. While this deliberate approach can be appreciated, the excessive amount of filler content, including repetitive mini-games and side quests, bogs down the experience. These distractions often feel disconnected from the main story and lack the depth and variety that fans have come to expect from the series.Additionally, the localization of Yakuza 3 suffers from some questionable decisions. The English translation fails to capture the nuances of the original Japanese dialogue, resulting in moments of awkward dialogue and a loss of emotional impact. This issue is particularly evident during crucial story moments, hindering the player's ability to fully invest in the narrative and connect with the characters.Another major drawback is the combat system. While it retains the satisfying brawling mechanics from previous entries, Yakuza 3 feels somewhat clunky and outdated compared to more recent installments. The lack of fluidity in combat, combined with limited move sets and repetitive enemy encounters, makes the combat segments feel monotonous and uninspired.Despite these shortcomings, Yakuza 3 does have its merits. The game's setting, Kamurocho, is meticulously detailed and beautifully recreated, offering a visually stunning and atmospheric backdrop for players to explore. The main story, once it picks up, still manages to deliver engaging moments of suspense and drama, showcasing the series' signature storytelling prowess.Additionally, Yakuza 3 introduces a new focus on the protagonist's personal relationships and explores deeper character development, which adds emotional depth to the narrative. The side quests, although excessive, do provide some humorous and heartfelt moments that further flesh out the world and its inhabitants.In conclusion, Yakuza 3 is a mixed bag. While it retains the series' charm and strengths, it falls short in crucial aspects that hinder the overall experience. The pacing issues, localization problems, and outdated combat mechanics prevent it from reaching the heights set by its predecessors. However, fans of the Yakuza series may still find enjoyment in the game's story and exploration elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of each of the Yakuza games I've played, Yakuza 3 has been a rather strange one, but it is very much like the other Yakuza games with their serious and emotional main story with the various strange to comedic side stories existing throughout the game. However, out of each of the yakuza games, 3 has been my least favorite so far for two reasons. One being there are a few segments that feel like they were implemented simply to drag out the game time, even if they do invoke some of the same emotions as the rest of the story. The second is the combat itself, which the game unfortunately makes most of the combos and abilities you can get useless in most cases, and it took me the same amount of time to learn this game's combat as it did when I first started with Yakuza 0. Despite the flaws Yakuza 3 has, it's still a fun and brilliant game that I recommend anyone who's interested in playing the Yakuza series to play, even if you just play through it once. It's story is memorable, emotional, and entertaining, even during the more drawn out parts, the combat is still fun once you learn how to use it, all while the substories and the rest the game has to offer still lives up to that of a Yakuza game.

_childDocuments_.review: My journey into the Yakuza franchise continues, and having completed Yakuza 3, I can firmly say...That this game definitely isn't the strongest of the bunch I've played thus far.HOWEVER, that is not grounds to say this game is "bad." It's just not nearly as exceptional, and considering the fact that Yakuza 3 is older than 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2, that makes perfect sense.Let's just go ahead and start with the bad and get it out of the way.The beginning of the game is a bit of a boring slog. The whole dad thing in the title of this review was put there for a reason: Kiryu basically does "dad things" in this game, and most of it happens in the beginning. I'm not entirely opposed to this. I'm more so opposed to how slow it all feels. At least 5 chapters worth of this game is spent mostly being a "dad" instead of doing what the Yakuza franchise is mostly known for: over the top action, violence, some more violence, more violence, and uh yeah that one goofy side quest where you pimp out women, not teaching children the importance of valuing another's hard work or selflessness. It works wonders for the story, by further developing Kiryu's character and showing how much he has changed as a man, but it doesn't make for "fun" gameplay, running around Okinawa, looking for a ball to give to a dog. Not in this sense at least.Combat in Yakuza 3 is...not nearly as bad as everyone makes it out to be. However, it's still not as good as the previous games that most people would be coming from (such as 0 and Kiwami, which have the best combat in the series from what I have played). See, Yakuza 3's problem with the combat is that enemies are ANNOYING. I played the whole thing on Hard mode and only died once (second majima fight. Lost cause I didn't heal). Enemies simply block way too much, they don't respect combos (this whole, enemies blocking mid-combo is pretty annoying), Kiryu gets knocked down too easily and all the fights that you would need the upgrades to stop being thrown around so much don't appear till late game, throwing is overpowered unless it's a boss or the enemy is large (but at that point, dodging and parries do the trick), and there's no downside for taking your meds, so the game is really only as difficult as how much crap you have in your pocket.However, "gitting gud" at the combat mitigates some of those problems, not all, some, and the komaki parry has never been more useful to me than now. The combat is in the "bad" section because it came off more annoying than cathartic, and that's the problem, especially when it's the core gameplay. You don't want your core gameplay to be "annoying" you want it to be fun but also challenging. This is just annoying.And the last thing I'm gonna complain about here is the "chase" sequences. Why does this game have Sonic 06 mach speed sections? This is ridiculous. I had a harder time with these than the actual combat, and the combat is what everybody and their grandmother complains about. This "mechanic" is only ever used like two times in the main story, and I played a decent portion of the side-quests and never had to deal with it, so why is it even here? It's not very good, it was barely even used, and every section that they have you chase somebody down you could have had another combat sequence.Yakuza 3 follows the trend of having a fairly solid story that's captivating. I enjoyed it. It gets a little needlessly complicated in some areas, the beginning is quite a slow burn (and a little disjointed when it comes to the time frame, so it was a little confusing), and some story bits are downright laughable considering how cheesy they are (but I come to expect this and actually welcome it; they give this series charm).The whole "revelation" thing is fairly interesting. I don't like how you can fail it by picking the wrong response, because you just end up having to do it again. It'd be better if you just kept your eye out, found something interesting, and then it would happen and you'd get your new heat action, instead of having to retry again trial and error style to figure out what the correct thing to say is so that you could get it. That's the bad part about the revelation system. The good part about the revelation system is that it's dumb, silly, comedic crap that I thoroughly enjoyed and would like to see more of. A lot more of. I'd take these over stupid fetch quests any day.Yakuza 3 has more or less the same kind of side content I've come to expect from the series. So you've got your bowling, kareoke, etc. The cabaret club is also here, but it's VERY different from 0's and Kiwami 2's. Granted, Yakuza 3 is older than those games, and I totally see where and why the evolution took place. I didn't play it much, so this being in the good section is solely because you have the option to partake in it, not because I legitimately thought it was good. I haven't played it enough to make a proper opinion on that.There's also golfing. Legit golfing. Fantastic.One of the things that I found quite interesting was the level of detail that happens to an enemy both while you're clobbering them and after. No other Yakuza game I have played has had that level of detail given to your enemies. It actually looks like you beat them up, and that they actually probably need to see a doctor, whereas in the other games they don't even so much as have a bloody nose. This also extends to Kiryu, who actually gets a bloody face, and bloody fists, arms, and even legs, which is again something that I didn't really see in the other games beyond story specific events and cutscenes.This game reeks of Playstation 2 era gameplay/world design backed by Playstation 3 graphics. Like I've been saying, and will continue to repeat, Yakuza 3 is old. It was released in 2009 after-all. The game does not look nearly as graphically impressive as the other games I've played, to be expected, but I came away rather impressed with how good the game actually looked sometimes, but then again, that might've been because it's a remaster.That being said, they sure didn't give the FMV's any updates. They are grainy as all hell, and look poor on an HD monitor, and the texture up-rez isn't all that up to snuff. It looks more "uncompressed" than it does "remastered."Character animations range from solidly animated to very stiff and robotic. Kiryu in specific has a really stiff way of moving around. The way he walks, jogs, attacks his enemies. He's like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robot. This extends to enemies and allies as well. Certain animations are fine, but those are likely done with mo-cap, and cutscenes were absolutely mo-capped as well.I don't see myself replaying Yakuza 3 any time soon. The other games offer more content and better, refined core combat. It's not Yakuza 3's fault though. If anything, Yakuza 3 paved the way for 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2, so if anything, the fans of the franchise should be thankful. The Yakuza series has certainly come a long way, and being able to jump from the modern outings to one of the older ones certainly puts things into perspective.If you're looking to play Yakuza 3 because you played 0, Kiwami, or Kiwami 2, then go ahead. I enjoyed my time with it, I just simply won't be coming back to it. This is one of those "experience it and be done" kind of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Its the black sheep of the series. Yakuza 3 crawled so Yakuza 4 could run.Yakuza 3, for all intensive purposes is not an unplayable game by any means. However it's gameplay is a far cry from the high points of the franchise as many of the games aspects were the first iterations, thus they're very hard to stomach if you're playing this after the newer entries, or didn't grow up / live with games that came out between 2000-2012.For the guys reading this that are considering getting this game for the story and aren't sure if they want to go through the hoops themselves or watch a longplay online, I won't sugar coat it.If all you want is story, just play it on easy mode.If you're feeling brave and want to know hurt similar to your loved ones being the reason you're feels like its ending, play on normal to get the emotions out.Why has this one in particular aged poorly exactly?Gameplay, and solely gameplay. Don't be fooled by criticism over the writing as most qualms for better or for worse have smoothed over as the series went on rather than take strides to retcon this out of the canon.tldr, if it was still 2010 and the series future was up in the air, you'd be right to be cautious. but, thats not the case.like previously stated, many of the aspects of this game are now staples of the franchise, however this was the game many were introduced and as a result are clunky or obtuse to figure out.Hostess maker / cabaret club manager is the biggest example of this as far as minigames go...Combat is especially jarring. Yakuza 3 doesn't reward the more aggressive or rush down play styles some my be accustomed to, which requires taking time to learn its more...Reserved combat that relies more of waiting and punishing enemies through use of countering, parrying, or learning the weapons system, which are essential if you intend to brave Hard or legendary difficulty.Things most will be aware of right out the gate:-enemies will attack you from off screen-the heat meter drains quickly, more so if you happen to get grabbed-QTE's are everywhere-enemies will often spam sidestepping to avoid attacks which ultimately makes them invulnerable-enemy guard can't REASONABLY be broken with normal attacks.-when enemy guard is broken, they will put back up again immediately.-And last but not least, due to the games pacing, it takes upwards of 6-10 hours before you're able to really get into the meat of the combat.Progression is earned through EXP similarly to yakuza 1 & 4. you have one resource to divvy up between 4 skills trees in a fixed order. Getting through the skill trees isn't hard of course unless you're b-lining it through the story and skipping everything else. The problem is, even if you fulfill it, you still won't have your full tool set to fight with. Certain tools that are more or less necessities aren't able to be unlock through exp.Perhaps one of my biggest nitpicks is how additional moves can be earned. through out the game kiryu meets different characters who for the most part are upfront saying "I have something to teach you. come back when you have time." sometimes you can earn health or heat upgrades, other times kiryu can handle certain weaponry better (his or his enemies), however my least favorite is Mack.You meet Mack early on, he tells you to find interesting moments in the overworld and make a not twitter post, and as a result, kiryu learns a new move. The problem is, when you've unlocked the ability to do these, all you're given is a vague clue as to what or where you need to look. you must then go into a first person mode and zoom in on the moment of interest, do a small series of QTE's, then make a timed decision on what to caption the event with (only one out of three being the right response). If you fail, you have to leave, and come back.As much fun as hidden unlockables can be... In an beat em up, the last thing I want is my tool set being locked behind obtuse puzzles.Theres also a chase "minigame" lets call it.the premise is simple, chase someone through crowds and tights spaces and tackle them. do it enough times before you run out of stamina.you have to play it on a couple occasions in the main story, but fortunately for completionist out there and handful of these moments were cut from the remaster (if you don't know why, don't worry. neither gameplay or related side quest story was worth it.)Its cluncky, its mandatory to play, its unforgiving at first, its not fun. plain and simple.final verdict: 6/10TLDR:if you're gonna play it just for story, play easy mode.This ones rough, we need a Kiwami 3 to happen

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is the third installment of the Yakuza franchise, this being a remaster of the original PS3 game.Being a remaster, it has its ups and downs, but I'll get to that later.It's a big graphical upgrade from Y2 to Y3 using the technology the PS3 had back then, as it's also a way bigger game overall compared to both PS2 games.Funny thing aside it's not the first Yakuza game on PS3, that goes to Yakuza Kenzan a spin-off samurai game which also introduced the beloved mini-game of the Yakuza games, Karaoke.Still being a beat em up, the way they made the story was quite a refreshing take and I absolutely loved the story this game has. I also just love this Kiryu design, giving so much expression compared to the Stoic and cold lookin classic Kiryu.You'll notice that he smiles like a lot, but man, this Kiryu can also be quite emotional...()We see a beautiful blue sea and a beach, we see Haruka waving to Kiryu as he comes out of the sea having caught a big fish and his hair ain't even wet lol,he tells Haruka to make dinner ready and hopes to not let anyone waiting, as we are wondering who does Kiryu mean with everyone? It's dinner time, and we see a lot of children playing ball, and Haruka is calling everyone to sit on the table,one of the children notices a person coming that they all know, all the children go to him, altho the man doesn't really seem so happy, it's like he's here to tell something to Kiryu.Kiryu asks if something happened, and the man responds by telling that their boss got shot, a quick fade to black, and we see Daigo Dojima again in a car, and it looks like he became the next chairman of the Tojo clan, his assistant gets a call telling them about a deal of some sort.Daigo keeps telling them that he ain't interested in it and that his answer is final. As he discusses with his assistant to stop speaking about considering he ain't interested, his assistant tells him if it has to do because of the fourth chairman, as Daigo tells his driver to take him back to Tojo HQ and cancel the banquet.Daigo arrives back at HQ as he is tolled by someone that a mysterious person is here to speak with Daigo, as Daigo didn't believe when he said to Daigo who wants to see him. Daigo enters the room and meets the mysterious person, they talk about letting Daigo have the deed instead Daigo kept refusing and to Daigo's eyes it looks like the mysterious man goes for his gun, so he picks his gun trying to shoot him....Back at Okinawa, we see Kiryu and the man that tolled him about his shot boss run to the operation room, as he confronts a little girl and she lets Kiryu see how the man looked drawn in her sketchbook.()Now before anyone goes at it saying stuff like blockuza 3, you're wrong and just bad at the game. (just kidding)Yes there is a lot of controversy with the gameplay of Yakuza 3 for the amounts of blocking the enemies do in this game, the sad thing about it isit was totally normal in the original PS3 version of Yakuza 3, in the remastered version however enemies block almost the entire fight, what's more frustrating is that when you try to dodge to the back of the enemy or boss, kiryu makes a whole spin which is so dumb beyond belief,this was also not an issue in the original PS3 version of Yakuza 3. Let's just say the beginning of the game might be a lot of doing the same moves but trust me when having komaki moves asap like the  and  the game gets fun as ♥♥♥♥ with its combat system and trust me you're going to use Komaki Parry a lot! Imo the combat is way better than the DE DOD combat (sue me). The combat is so technical you have no idea the possibilities of doing combos, like mf WALL COMBOS, that ♥♥♥♥ broken af and very useful against bosses.Progression is again with XP in this game, you go to the  when click on  and upgrade your move set from there. A new thing that is added in this game are , strong deadly heat moves and  moves against bosses that are very useful and cool af not so late in the game do you get to learn about it. Another new thing that is added to the game are , where you go and chase enemies or normal people as they are running away from you.Overall combat is the same as the OG Y1 and Y2, but more refined.()Most of the beloved substories return from the OG PS3 Yakuza 3 in Yakuza 3 Remastered, as some substories are completely removed as they were against modern times.As always, you can come across them randomly, and they are fun as always. One of my favorites being one where Kiryu goes full detective mode in a murder case that happened in Café Alps.Most of the minigames return as well, with Karaoke and Fishing being a first for the Yakuza title and let me tell you fishing in this game oh man, be ready to put some hours into catching that darn tuna.Pool and Bowling return in this game, but man does bowling suck in Y3, on the other hand pool feels fine and playable. The Purgatory returns as well with a new mode having TAG-BATTLES and like I said you can still learn moves from Komaki but not a lot this time.A small part of side content is back that went missing in Yakuza Kiwami 2 and that is the Cabaret Club, you meet a woman on the streets ask them if they'd like a job as a cabaret hostess and complete the side activity by having the hostess rank to S, it can be annoying in the beginning but when you find a perfect look for the hostess it's going to be fine.()In Yakuza 3 we have a new location called Okinawa, it's also a lot smaller compared to Kamurocho, but it's still a nice location never the less.In both Kamurocho and Okinawa you can come across enemies, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do they appear very fast when you're just walking in each location, and the annoying thing is they are everywhere and not even have a unique design that it's an enemy, they look like basic residents.Enemy variety is also less in this game, just Angry Guys, Yakuza and Punks, yeah not a lot, The Story does have lots of enemy variety on the other hand.I also like how some groups in the story you fight against have their own theme and not everyone has the exact theme, altho you do hear one theme almost every time when fighting groups of enemies.Another thing added is the HLA, an organization that tries to hunt killers, as you get bounties to hunt each killer and take them back to the HLA. The final boss in that is a nostalgic character from Y1/Kiwami.As for bosses there are really some enjoyable bosses in this game especially in the final act as Y3 is also technically the first Yakuza game having a Dynamic boss intro, and some bosses have also a great boss theme.()The Yakuza 3 OST is louder, hardcore, rocked, metal, techno, beat, mixed into one. Also being one of my favorite ost's in the franchise,it's definitely quite a change compared to Y1 and Y2 (just wait till Yakuza 4 hehe), Battle music also has variety again depending on who you fightMy personal favorite being Crush & Strike, such a great ost to fight enemies with it. Yakuza 3's soundtrack is really great in every way, and like I said, it's something that RGG Studios does for every Yakuza game of theirs.Having an absolute banger of a soundtrack.That concludes my review of Yakuza 3 RemasteredThe game can be janky at sometimes, but I still enjoy playing it with it's great story, the combat is good minus the weird issue that enemies block almost everything, which again wasn't an issue in the og PS3 title.And also what a nice refreshing take to a Yakuza story and especially for Kiryu.(9.4)

_childDocuments_.review: If you're here reading this, chances are you're probably on the journey of playing through this series in chronological order. There's not really any other point in playing through this. If that is you and have started with Zero, well, this is not that. As others have pointed out, the combat is slow and can be very frustrating. Finding Komaki and his training is not optional - it's fundamental. With that, it gets a little more enjoyable, but you'll likley need to put in some hours until I got used to it. Bosses can be challenging. Random encounters are one of the most tiresome and annoying parts of the game, since they're inescapable, they take a long time and you can also just spot the guy waiting to kick you on the street, so most times it felt like I was just running away from them, hoping they wouldn't see or catch me. I have mixed feelings here. You're probably used to it by now, but Yakuza continues its tradition of being overly cryptic and complex and introducing way too many characters than it has time to explore. That said, I found the story to be better than that of 2. Yes, that's right. It starts slowly at first, but then it just goes all over the place and by the end it feels like you're not actually justified in doing anything else apart from the story missions due to how urgent they feel. I'd say it was worth it though.Aside from Kamurocho, you also get to experience Okinawa which was really chill and enjoyable and had the distinct feeling of being a different place. Way too many. A lot of fat that gets in the way. There are some notable highlights that are really good and/or explore main characters. There is also one that's a murder mystery and feels like the prototype for what would later be Judgement. I recommend those but the problem is that you have to dig through some very boring ones to find them. And the hostesses, once again, get in the way of completing everything. Idk, I just didn't enjoy them at all. Yea nah. Overly difficult. Don't even get me started on the cabaret minigame here - even with a guide I just couldn't get anything to work. Some people may enjoy them, but I've always found minigames to be unnecessarily challenging and grindy.There's also an odd reliance on modding weapons and finding or purchasing catalogues and items to combine and enhance weapons. I didn't get it, personally - and I didn't find it useful in any way. It's hard to play this in the current era of gaming where there's better out there, but if you're here to experience Kiryu's third chapter, then I'd recommend it for the story if nothing else. If it gets too tedious, try Easy difficulty and don't worry too much about the side content.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I am not a native english speaker so mistakes are bound to happen, not just that, but I'm lazy and I got the ADHD thingy so yeah, I sometimes don't care enough to correct my mistakes. That being said, let's get started: Pros:-Continuation of a great series-I like HarukaCons:-Ugly graphics-badly aged gameplay-tedious mission design-not so well written storySoo, After I've played Yakuza 0, and Kiwami 1 & 2 I've expected a lot, and there was the first mistake, you can clearly tell, that this game 12/10 would've benefitted a lot from the Kiwami-treatment. This game, when it comes to gameplay is a joke in comparison to the modernized remakes and I wish I would've had that. Apparently this game is known for splitting the playerbase from those, who stopped after this to those who continued to play it.Now the reason I bit and stuck with it was one of my besties and me being stubborn to not wanting to quit, and see where this adventure ends. But I have to admit, I could not beat the endboss with the mechanics so I've used cheats to finish the game. Just a heads-up, everyone should enjoy the games the way they want, I only would ever condemn cheating if you ruined someone else's fun (e.g. multiplayer) but It was better and funnier for me that way when I had to beat mine.So, the story starts interesting and strong, mind you, Ive completed Yakuza 0 so it was really interesting to see, what 1 substory told us about the future, about having all these children. The Setting really started strong but the story lost track soo quickly, became stale and boring, it forced me to do stupid ♥♥♥♥ like watching for a bunch of children, which was really unfun, probably so you care more for them and what happens in the story, but it was really more a bummer than anything. The Ending is pretty okay tho, it gives decent closure tho I am not a big fan of stupid redemption-arc's but I'll let it slide.Visually speaking the game is not too bad, you can tell, some textures have been redone, some have not. The variety of NPC's is for a PS2 game pretty good, fedality not too bad and some animations were okay, BUT a lot of things felt and looked so stupid, prime example is Haruka's normal walk cycle or anything that is Smaller than our 2 Meter (6.75 feet for those who don't know what a kilometer is) behemoth, and it was quite weird. Also while I'm at it, the sound design was all over the place, you sometimes have really good immersive atmospheric sounds, and the music is quite decent aswell, but then you step on wood and it sounds like Kiryu is a damn horse, or some sounds being recycled and sounding just bad.Back to music, overall it was a 7/10, not every track really a banger but overall pretty decent. I'd love to admit but 0 and 1 thus far were killa when it came to music and I liked the Joji Theme and Mine's boss fight too, just some parts, when it came to these atrocious chases with people, yikes, just no. Bad music, bad gameplay.Because of the terrible mission design I really skipped the side content, not like in Kiwami 1 or 2 where I did plenty, or 0 where I did everything (with cheesing), I hated the engine soo much, that I wanted to get this game over with as soon as possible. My Mistake was to play at Hard difficulty, not knowing what I was getting myself into, and that may have ruined my experience since I've had to cheese a lot of fights (you see, I am really not a beat-em-up guy, more strategy games, but the story overall's just enjoyable) and therefore my experience may have been harder than necessary BUT even my best friend who LOVES THIS SERIES and is really atteched to it, told me this could've been a better game as a remake rather than remaster. So where does that lead us? Besides the story, the gameplayloop felt tedious and was unenjoyable, I was happy when I finished the main story, and apparently I only played 7% of the game. Technically speaking, I'll better avoid this game as a second playthrough.Time for Story, that really struggled on some ends, why do we have Kazama back (the way they brought him back was just stupid), why would the CIA ever entangle in japans inner affairs, what are men in black, why do we have a dog now??? I cannot answer these questions. I feel like there were a bunch of ideas in a bowl and they just grabbed 4 main plots and knotted them together into a game. I really tought in the beginning the action's going to be great but meeeh. Merely the end, as mentioned before, gave some closure and even that was random as hell.Now I think I've made my point clear that everything I've played up until now was superior, and I'd like to state that I had some fun with this game, but not enough to justify the times I've suffered from bad game design, I've hated the mechanics soo much, and yeah, I will probably never attempt to finish this game to 100%. I hope there may be a Kiwami remake at some point but until then, may this game rest forever in my library. I really hope Yakuza 4 gives me a better treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I really enjoyed playing this game. However, I will be talking about all this game has to offer, and from there, you'll understand why I have so much criticism for this game.If you know anything about this game, is that the combat is not nearly as fun to play as Yakuza 0, Kiwami or Kiwami 2. This is true. It's a downgrade, and you should avoid playing on Hard difficulty. I recommend Normal difficulty and learning moves at the Dojo. I only died twice in this game and that was becaause of some early game cheese bosses. The combat is not bad, it's just not nearly as good as the games you are more familiar with. You just get used to a pattern fairly quickly. Grab, throw, grab, combo. This will be your go to combination for most of this game. Apart from that, learning the Tiger drop makes bosses much easier, though don't expect it to be much help when fighting street thugs. That being said, the heat actions are probably my favorite throughout the series, and the method of unlocking them is a load of fun as well.This is one of my favorite stories in the Yakuza series so far. It is my second favorite from 0, 1, 2 & 3, and has my favorite villain in the series. It's amazing how much you can go from thinking 'Oh this guys kind of cool' to 'Screw this guy' to 'Please, I don't want this man to die, I am begging you.' A lot of the characters in this game are fantastic. They are all interesting in their own ways and you really build a connection to them over the story. That being said, the game has a slow start.Kazama Kiryu has tried to retire for the nth time, and he's running an Orphanage by the beach in Okinawa. While I didn't have a problem with this at first, it becomes a bit of a drag when dealing with non-Yakuza related plot points that simply aren't as interesting. When this game is focusing on Yakuza related content, it thrives. When it is focuses on the kids Kazama is looking after, it's boring. Another slight criticism I have is that Majima isn't in this one as much as the previous 3, but I am biased on this because he is one of my favorite characters.The music is also stellar. While I'm not a fan of the battle music of this game, The track that takes place in the hospital and the roof's hospital has made it become one of my favorite moments in the series.Outside of combat, there is a total of 119 side stories. Instead of Sotenbori, you get explore Ryukyu in Okinawa. The map is much smaller, but still has plenty to do. The sub-stories aren't much different to the standard ones seeing in the previous games. Mostly fun & whacky adventures. However, there are a few character heavy side-stories with cutscenes that are definitely worth playing because they add both character development to these characters and you get more attached to them as well.This game is filled with minigames, with most being awful. Fishing is fun once you understand how to play. Massage mode is low quality in terms of gameplay. Golf & Baseball are not fun to play. Darts is one of the most frustrating minigames to play and Pool is one of the hardest minigames I have ever played in a game. The CPUs for these two games are some of the strongest & most broken CPUs I have ever played against, and what makes it worse is the absolute abysmal aiming system for these 2 minigames! Karaoke, while the tracks are not as good as the previous games, is fun in the same way the previous games are. There's a fun enough shooting game in the Arcade I enjoyed playing (even if it was simple). The Claw Machine Bowling's physics are stupid & broken, the variations of Poker play like any other, I never got a good grasp of cee-lo, cho-han, koi-koi, oicho-kabu, and Mahjong. I do enjoy Shogi and I had fun playing that.The Colliseum is another big side event, made a lot easier by spamming Tiger Drop. It's a grind certainly, but it's not nearly as hard as the Ultimate Match mode, which have varying levels of combat related challenges. The hostess stuff is not nearly as interesting as the Cabaret clubs as well.While most of these minigames are very bad, they are not mandatory and can be ignored. However, as someone going for 100%, this is an awful experience.The game is filled with a brilliant story with lukewarm combat. I enjoyed a lot of the substories but hated the large majority of the Minigames. It really is gutting that this game didn't get the Kiwami treatment, because it really would have made it shine. It definitely wouldn't be considered the worst in the franchise. The majority of my time hasn't been completing all the minigames yet as I still have to finish every substory and I enjoy that.However, then there are achievements like 'Break Ace' which is to pot the nine ball on the first shot that literally took hours to complete.If you are a fan of this series, I really recommend playing through the main story. Easy might be the best experience so you don't suffer through 'Blockuza', but for the love of all things holy, do not try and 100% this game! Anyone that does or is trying is absolutely crazy.
