_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 sits  above the borderline that splits this game between "recommended" and "not recommended".Although it released just about three years after the launch of the PlayStation 3, this was still early enough in that console's life cycle where it was evident developers were still trying to get a hang of the PS3's infamous system architecture. While Yakuza 3 isn't necessarily buggy, it is quite unrefined and . It's especially disappointing to see this when you've just come out of Yakuza Kiwami 2, which was running on that absolutely  Dragon Engine.It's been a while since I last played so I'll try to recall what stuck out to me:First off, Kiryu shouldn't be able to  when roaming the overworld. Basically, nothing feels like it has weight: heat Moves lack a sense of impact. Hitting with objects doesn't feel satisfying. Things just move at a brisk pace in an unsatisfying manner.In fact, this also extends to the game's golf minigame: the ball moves as though there is intense gravity, with no attempt at some sense of realistic physics. Which leads me to...Assuming you've played the Yakuza games in a chronological order to this point, then you'll surely have played the variety of minigames playable in each. Here, unfortunately, things just feel sloppy and rushed: karaoke doesn't seem to respond to your input appropriately, the unique Boxcelios arcade game is too simple to be enjoyable, and even standbys like baseball, bowling, and pool were frustrating.It goes without saying the iteration of cabaret club featured here and in Yakuza 4 is the absolute worst. Thankfully they figured out how to make it fun but unfortunately, this is where it started. Ignore it.Look, I don't have any issue with the inclusion of the orphans and having the creators wanting to focus on them but  whole chapters were dedicated to them, one of which was right before the game's finale. It should have all been relegated way back earlier in the game while not taking anywhere near as long. Yes, we're supposed to know Kiryu is a responsible caretaker but don't drag it out.This is the bitter truth of the matter: regardless of the game's litany of technical and design issues, we have to let it all slide. Again, this was made early on for a console that was difficult to work with. The jump from PS2 to PS3 was also a big technological leap so the devs were likely trying to find footing and figure out what to do with the series at this point, which is what I think why the game turned out the way it ultimately did.Making this review comes at an interesting point of time: it was just over two weeks ago that the series director made the curious comment that a Kiwami 3 seems likely to happen in the future. That would be  just for all the quality of life improvements it would come with.Should you wait for this potential remake or even outright skip Yakuza 3? While Yakuza 3 does build upon what happened in prior games, anything of major consequence that occurred in 3 isn't followed up in Yakuza 4.Yakuza 4 is a soft reboot of sorts: some lesser events/details from the series are touched upon but overall, Y4 starts off with something new, storywise. I think you could just skip 3 but if you're willing to rush through the main story and sidestories, then get Y3 on sale.Yakuza 3 isn't unplayable, it's just got problems and not as enjoyable to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is a very interesting game, from its tone to its gameplay. For the time, its visuals are stunning, and even now its art style and settings differ completely from the other entries in the series. It purposefully depicts the two sides of our main character's life as being entirely different, with the dirty backstreets of Kamuroucho being their own world away from the sunny beaches of Ryukyu. You get to play the role of a father figure to a group of orphans, much like Kiryu himself once was, and see how he continues to struggle with the aftermath of the first two games. It has one of the saddest and heartfelt stories in the series, let down a bit by pacing that has a hard time slowing down. Seishu Hase was not present for this game's story, and his oversight over the first two games' plots were most certainly missed a bit here, but the strong direction without his presence really does lend itself to a bold new direction, coinciding with Kiryu's new lease on life. I would recommend Yakuza 3 remastered as long as you grab the quickstep mod and restore the original soundtrack, as Eikichi Yazawa's opener is an absolute killer.

_childDocuments_.review: What? You don't like the combat because "the enemies block too much"?Sounds like a skill issue, the game gives you a wide variety of moves for a reason. I don't want to sound like one of those people but it really is just a case of getting good.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this after playing 0 and the two Kiwami games on PC within the last 2 years or so is a total trip.  Its kinda like playing a £200 epiphone after you’ve been playing a Les Paul Custom – sure, its still kinda cool but its weird after you’ve gotten accustomed to that much higher quality.  Oh, and some of the enemies are a real bag of mouldy cheese - there's just so many who constantly block, some ridiculous hit boxes (ie dodge behind a chump and still get hit by them) or sometimes your hits don't connect because your opponent is in the middle of a combo and your fists magically wiff through them.  It does get a lot better if you do a certain side mission that brings back a certain someone who teaches you a few parry moves, but these moves are pretty much mandatory to enjoy the combat and should not have been side mission content imho as dodging and enemy attack tracking is straight up broken.I wish Sega had ponied up and made this a remake rather than a remaster, or at least re-balanced the combat.  On the plus side, while 3 does seem to have a reputation as being the worst in the franchise, I actually think there's something a wee bit special going on.  Sure, the story isn't the best in the series and the last fight is very anti-climactic , but the parts where you mince around sunny Okinawa are a nice contrast to the series usual hangouts, and sections were Kiryu goes full dad with his orphans are very touching.  And there's a certain boss fight in a love motel which is straight up hilarious and worth the price of admission alone!  Go in with realistic expectations (and perhaps on normal instead of hard mode) and you'll be grand.  And whatever you do, make sure you look for side missions in the streets near West Park so you can unlock the parry and tiger drop!

_childDocuments_.review: As Date-san once said "In for a penny, in for a pound." If you have played 0, (maybe) 1, and 2; might as well keep going for the story. Graphics-wise this remaster looks okay on 1080p, not sure about higher resolutions. The main story was good but near the end had some small issues. Most of the substories were decent. Now for my grievances... Not going to say anything new here but the combat really sucks the fun out of the game. Just really love the constant blocking that gives bosses almost full immunity. Also appreciate how easy it is to get knocked down / stunned and then repeatedly stunned. The street thugs were a nuisance, yes they were in the previous games as well but in this game they love to run up and engage in a dialogue with you, wasting time. Plus, in past games you could sweep them in 3 button presses by using a bike or whatever object laying around, in this game these objects felt almost completely useless. The host club was a snoozer, might as well have been a capsule hotel mini-game since I was falling asleep in my chair trying to play it. Finally, don't waste your time like me collecting the locker keys past whatever the first achievement is (I think collecting 5 or so) since there's no achievement for opening all the lockers. Just really loved the gimmicky first-person camera mechanic for finding the keys. Overall... I give this remaster a 5/10, don't think I'll ever be replaying it. Sayonara aniki.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is a product of its time. I can't say that I 100% enjoyed this game as it had a lot of awful aspects and these made the experience sometimes unbearable. You can really feel the age of the game in the gameplay and controls. The visuals are good for the most part, sometimes they even feel nostalgic for that early PS3 gaming era which I absolutely love. The soundtrack is fire. The story is good in the first half, but later on it just feels like a generic american action movie for me. Perhaps my favorite aspect of this Yakuza entry is Kiryu itself. I've been playing the saga in chronological order, and so far this was the best rendition of our hero. He's very expressive, caring and considerate and yet he retains that serious and menacing aura we all love. After all those flaws I pointed out, I still can't not recommend this title, since it is pretty much essential for Kiryu's development and some of its plot points are important for the next entry, Yakuza 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Players coming to Yakuza 3 after running through 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2 will get a bit of whiplash from how dated Yakuza 3 feels. The combat feels plain and frustrating as enemies frequently block attacks, an annoyance that only really exists in this game and none of the others. And while Kiryu's turn as an orphanage caretaker is a great new arc for the legendary Dragon of Dojima, it also means a lot of Yakuza 3--particularly the beginning--can drag a bit as you deal with the children in your care. I still recommend it for anyone planning on going through the whole series, but with the caveat that as soon as you start to lose interest you should bail out and watch a cutscene compilation or story recap on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite how much i like Yakuza 3, i think this game's biggest fault was the time period it was developed in. An awkward transitional phase to newer hardware and a more modern take on the formula (at the time) -- the results are more positive than negative, this is one of the most concise Yakuza games out there even if the pacing at the start of it is a little rough. Either way, it's definitively an entry that has been done no favors by the passage of time and introduced stuff that would be greatly improved in Yakuza 4 and 5.Its an essential part of Kiryu's story, even if some parts of it are a little bit of a slog, i think they're worth going through. Yakuza truly started with the 4th entry, in my opinion, but this one is really solid. For a "black sheep", it's better than most games out there anyway. So hey, thats somethin'.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 aged better than people claim it has. It's without a doubt the weakest link regarding to the combat system and while the graphics aren't the Dragon Engine they still please you. There's one combat style similar to Kiwami 2 if you're playing this after that title. Seeing Kiryu outside of his Yakuza life and just being a chill dad was a nice occurrence, and Okinawa was a good change of scenery. It also seems to find every possible opportunity to send you on a search quest for some person or item. But even after all of the hell it puts you through I genuinely think the story was well-written and I felt emotional at parts. A lot of the new characters you meet are easily favorites and final boss is one of the best in the series. Majima was *this* close to being put on trial for at least 30 counts of vehicular manslaughter and that's not an exaggeration. Overall I'd say it's still worth a play and after everything it still has a place in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is my personal favorite entry in the entire Yakuza mainline franchise. It is definitely NOT THE BEST ONE but the atmosphere, the characters and all the "new" elements it got after the original 2nd game really makes this game a MILESTONE. When people say "I love Yakuza!" this is basically what they mean. The karaoke, revelations, hostess management, the new and creative heat actions, very weird and sometimes wholesome side quests, multiple world maps, long battles with EXTREMELY GOOD music, DYNAMIC INTROS, positive masculinity (like this is the gayest Yakuza game and I mean that in a good way), Kiryu being a positive father figure and its meaningful themes about family, loyalty and friendship for everyone.Also this game is arguably an okay point to start the franchise. Yakuza 0 felt really complicated to me as my first Yakuza game (yes even worse than 4 in terms of complication) but 3 is right in the middle of being a soft reboot and a sequel to the second game. It also explains the other important characters from 1 and 2 right in the beginning so you're not really left out. And if you like this one you can always go back and play the first 3 after you finish it. All in all a really good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this after Kiwami 2 was... Rough. It's a good game, it's great for a 15 year old PS3 game, but the presentation, engine and mechanics really feel like a massive downgrade if coming from Kiwami 2. I also feel like the combat in this game is the worst yet, I even decided to play on Easy and just breeze through it to not get stuck playing a combat that not only I really dislike but also is hard. Enemies block like crazy here, more than in past games, even on easy. Your combos feel awfully repetitive, it's always a combination of pressing X 1 to 4 times and then Y twice, or grabbing. Heat actions feel a lot less crunchy, are harder to do, and are less diverse. Random encounters have 2 lines of dialogue before and after battle, which slogs the game down a ton. The minigames are not bad, but some feel very undercooked (like the cabaret hostess training one).However, despite all this, I really liked everything else in the game. The setup is very different to earlier Yakuza games, it begins with Kiryu having a brief moment of peace in his life, and the game lets you sink into that feeling a lot. It then grows into a Yakuza plotline like we're used to, but those first few hours of "slice of life" make you care a lot about the new characters, and that half of the game being set in Okinawa is a treat. The main villain is one of the best I've seen in this series yet, maybe tied with Ryuji from the previous game, but it (and the other villains) could benefit from a bit more screen time and development, it feels like they do one specific thing in the story and stop existing.Enjoyable overall despite everything, I hope it's uphill from this point on :D

_childDocuments_.review: Clicking the thumbs down is because I just want to prepare you for disappointment. If you're like me and you've been belatedly working through this series, starting with Yakuza 0 and on through Kiwami and Kiwami 2, what you are going to find here is the first game that doesn't have a newer touch on its game mechanics, and it shows. Everything is clunkier! Combat is not as fun. Street encounters are less dynamic and harder to avoid when you reach the point in the game where you just want to run away from guys. New mechanics, like chases, are annoying. Kamurocho is less alive outside of cutscenes. Heat actions are very undertuned against bosses. Even the progression mechanic isn't particularly satisfying, with little feeling that Kiryu gets much stronger from the beginning to the end of the game. I was disappointed that the story made the decision to just write out Sayama from Kiwami 2 rather than carry over a potential love interest for Kiryu. The new location of Okinawa is not as cool of a secondary location as Sotenbori has been in prior games.Looking over all of those flaws, I did like experiencing the story of this game, when it was there. Kiryu acting as the father figure to a house full of orphans, including Haruka, is sweet to see, how he tries to have a normal existence for them even when some of the craziness of his old life starts to catch up. I wish there was a bit more of this mixed in with the plot, which ends up being several chapters in a row in Okinawa that awkwardly try to catch up the story from where Kiwami 2 left off to when the main plot of 3 is set, several more chapters in Kamurocho, and not much back and forth until the very end. The cast is always committed to every cutscene and the plot is full of dramatic turns as you'd expect from this series. I'll be continuing the series, but I sure hope that 4 and 5 (which are the other games that were made before the 0 prequel, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2 came along) represent an improvement over this.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I recommend this game, but this has been probably the worst of the Yakuza games I've played so far. Gameplay in this one is worse too, with the combat being the most to suffer. I read other reviews calling this game "Blockuza" and they weren't kidding. The block in this game is widely used and so strong that any boss fights feel like a nightmare to get through due to the size of their health bars and frequency in blocking. My immediate thought on hearing about that was "well, just grab them and throw them around" and while that strategy works wonders for the random encounters and most of the unimportant fights, tougher enemies just won't allow you to grab them seemingly at all. It's still Yakuza, so the minigames and side content is still a strong point for the game, but feels like a much worse entry overall than every other game in the series I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: So it turns out I was told a bunch of lies about Yakuza 3. I was expecting a whiplash from the drop in quality and archaic engine, but I have to say I much preferred it to Yakuza Kiwami 2. People on the internet said the story wasn't as good, but I found it quite compelling, showing the audience Kiryu as a father, rather than focusing on the same old yakuza politics from the previous games. People said the combat wasn't as good, but even if the controls were clunkier, there is actual progression to Kiryu's moveset here, unlike in Kiwami 2. I found this much more satisfying. I myself was expecting the game to look like crap, but the clear directorial vision made seeing Kamurocho again one more year into the future refreshing as always. The crowds were a surprising touch too, filled with many varied NPCs that really brought a sense of life to the world. If I had to pick one grievance with the game, it would either be the lackluster bossfights or the return of Feel The Heat, but the former didn't exactly bother me and the latter was vastly improved upon from its Kiwami 2 iteration. Overall, I give Yakuza 3 an 8/10 - though if you've played far enough into the series to care, you'd probably have played it no matter what I said.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 Remastered it's a game, the third entry in the Yakuza/Ryu Ga Gotoku series and fourth entry chronologically speaking, on that I think everybody can agree pretty much. Me, personally, have to say that this game is "an experience". It's really hard to say if it is a really bad good game or a really good bad game, it sits in between which is also kind of ironic since it's also the "in-between" point in the franchise were it evolved from the ambitious games from the PS2 era to the style the franchise is most known for. On that fact alone, Yakuza 3 does deserve certain recognition for being sort of a testing ground of ideas that would work better later, kinda like Shenmue but not dry and lame and f-cking boring.Having mentioned the good stuff, this game is one of the weirdest things you can ever play in a "bad good" way. It's not a train-wreck or anything (don't expect Sonic 2006), but the whole thing is so jarring and theres such a huge disconnect between main plot, the B-plots, the story progression and the gameplay that it just keeps you wondering and wondering what the f-ck were the writer/s doing. The plot basically could be summed up in "Villain wants a lot in Okinawa where Kiryu has his orphanage", yet there's so much unnecesary stuff around it: there's a whole political subplot around two politicians clashing about building a resort vs building a military base in Okinawa, a doppleganger of Kiryu's step dad that starts shooting people, a weapons dealer infiltrated in the CIA even though the CIA is after him so they should know his face but whatever, a main villain whose motivation is not really clear even after it is explained (he wants to make money but doesn't care about money because who cares, we need a bad guy), and in between all that they shoe-horn stuff from the previous games because this was after all the third entry in the series.I say play it and have fun wondering at the end of every chapter why the hell did they story progressed the way it progressed when it does not make any f-cking sense.

_childDocuments_.review: The black sheep of the Kiryu saga in regards to a number of growings pains the series took coming off of Yakuza 2.Due to this being the first mainline entry not written by the guy who did Yakuza 1 & 2's plots, the narrative follows an unusual flow for the series (with 4-onward returning more to following the progression of story beats like Yakuza 2 had). As a result, this game has a much more "chill" vibe in parts of the main plot than you may be accustomed to. This direction seems to be a "love it or hate it" type of deal.This was also the first mainline game (introduced in "Ryu Ga Gotoku Kenzan!") to adopt the format and style to be used and expanded on by all subsequent entries. As a result, due bare that in mind in regards to how basic this will feel if coming off-of Kiwami 2.There are also a number of quirks in the game I would classify "tech demo stuff", as it just comes off as the developers flexing with the superior hardware(at the time) the game was designed for.Also as a heads-up: Bosses like to block.....a lot.As a Remaster, this mostly refers to the comprehensive overhaul the localization recieved, bringing its quality to be consistent with Yakuza 0 and beyond. They also restored nearly all cut content from the original PS3 localization, which was removed due to time and budget constraints.The PC is interesting in that you can apparently use the superior assets generally reserved for cutscenes during normal gameplay (something the PS4 should be able to handle, but just doesnt). However, 60 frames per second appears to be the upper limit on fps (whereas all non-Remastered Collection releases sport uncapped).For $20 or even cheaper, this game is absolutely worth playing if you are going through the series. Just trying to enjoy it for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note, I’ve only played 0, Kiwami, and Kiwami 2. I haven’t experienced the game on PS3 or PS4, and sadly have not played the PS2 games. RIP to Mark Hamill Majima.)(Edit: Doesn't help this game has aged very poorly compared to Y4 and Y5. Combat is clunky in this game compared to 4 and 5, especially 5, and moves feel rigid.)TL;DR — This game has issues and is my least favorite Yakuza, but is still a damn good game you should play. Yakuza 3 is like the red-headed stepchild of the Yakuza games: about 70% is what you expect coming from games like 0, Kiwami/1, and Kiwami 2/2. A crime thriller exploring the dark secrets of the yakuza, with complex characters and goals. The other 30% of this game is the legendary Dragon of Dojima finally taking a long needed break since 1, and running the Okinawan orphanage Morning Glory, helping solve minor issues that aren’t as large scale as “beat up your former sworn brother or have the Tojo Clan war with itself” or “beat up this Kansai guy or have the entire country’s yakuza war with itself.” The entire thing is nice and sweet, where Kiryu embarks on more substory like missions, like helping Mitsuo ask out one of the other orphans to a date, or helping Shiro not get bullied by playing golf with a government bigwig. You end up caring a lot for the kids, and by the end I was devastated along with them. Both sides of the story are ultimately interesting in their own ways. What I don’t like about this separation is that it feels somewhat awkward switching between both styles of storytelling. The sudden shift in Chapter 9-10 when returning to Okinawa is a bit jarring. I won’t go into depth but going from political events to chasing around one of the kids is really weird. Not exactly a dealbreaker but it’s a major issue I have with the game.Gameplay wise, if you’re coming from 0/Kiwami, it won’t feel jarring playing 3. Kiwami 2’s dreamy Dragon Engine is not present in this game (hold out for Y6) but combat is still fun and engaging. I was playing on Normal and never felt like I needed to change the difficulty. The bosses do get very block-happy, and their AI can get into some shenanigans (Majima was dodging everywhere trying to evade my attacks while I was standing completely still) but this isn’t a major issue as much as it is a minor inconvenience. Slight adjustments need to be made to your gameplay, where you should focus on dodging the bosses’ attacks and following up with a counterattack. Leveling up is based on four different trees, Soul for buffs to Heat and the meter, Body for HP and throws, Tech for combo speed and new moves, and Heat (little confusing, but eh) for new Heat actions and adding a red Heat bar (previously known as Climax Heat.) I’m fine with these trees, nothing special about them, nothing bad. New to this game (and present in 4 and 5 as far as I’m aware) is the Revelations system, where you can look at an event in the world and create a new move that you don’t need to spend EXP on. I’m torn on this system: while the cutscenes are fun and the moves themselves are usually pretty good (shoutouts to that tissue paper ninja, that move was insane in the final long battle) the whole thing is basically just a QTE with a checkbox at the end with a chance of needing to redo the cutscene. It’s like watching a Bill Nye video in the 6th grade and needing to fill out questions.A returning feature from 2 is the “Feel the Heat” sections, where you are basically whooping the a** of the boss so hard you can get a neat little cutscene to finish the fight. In 3, you do a chunk of damage instead of just getting a “you win” card at the end. You can choose between 3 actions (1 unlocked from default and the other 2 from Revelations) and I don’t really like them in this game. I don’t know, I know I missed out on getting Komeki lessons and I probably missed out on leveling up my Heat tree or something, but I just always felt like they never did enough damage. The only one I ended up liking was Hell’s Gauntlet, unlocked at Chapter 10. This one you would just do a quick QTE for and end up doing... an absurd amount of health. Actually felt like this one was too much damage, but I’m nitpicking. And here are two issues I felt like I had personally, and you probably won’t have these issues. Number 1: Lack of damage. I’m somewhat glad that there are no flat “damage up” or “weapon damage up” skills, otherwise there would be some issues, but I felt like Heat moves did too little damage as well, This is remedied, however, with the help of the Soul tree’s skill which gives some Heat moves an extra button prompt. The other issue I have (and this is definitely 100% preference,) but I didn’t feel like doing substories in this game. Might be spoilt by 0 and K2’s substories just being downright absurd and stupid, but I just wanted to get through this game fassstt. I didn’t really like exploring Okinawa in the beginning since it was different than the other games, then when I got to Kamurocho I felt like I just wanted to do the main story, and same with the return to Okinawa. Again, 100% preference.I’ve just been nitpicking about this game, but let me stress something. This is a good game. A bad Yakuza game is still a good game. Combat is fun. The world is diverse. The story is engaging. I had fun. This is nowhere near a mediocre, 6/10 game. This might not even be a bad Yakuza game to some people. That is okay. This is my least favorite Yakuza, but still a damn good game. You should not skip out on this game. I would not start with this (my ideal order is still: 0, K1, K2, 3, 4, 5, 6) but I would not judge you for starting with this. This was also where SEGA got its footing for Yakuza on the PS3, so there are issues. That said, I still wholeheartedly recommend this game. Play it. Do not go straight to 4 or 5.Also the music’s really good but that’s inherent to a Yakuza game. Fly is one of my favorite opening themes.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly underrated and its negativity is blown out of the water, please try out the game before making judgments, I've completed every game in the series (Excluding spin-offs and Judgement) and I can confidently say this is STILL in my top 3. I found most of the characters to have enough reasons to care for them and it really counted in a story that was risky but somehow against all odds made it all feel pretty dang entertaining and heart wrenching, which is a hard feat to pull off (Despite some mishaps which is a given with a series full of them). But of course, the common criticism is the combat, I can't argue that the combat is the best, but I can argue how much it taught me in the way of a dragon, as in there is no denying that this is THE hardest Yakuza experience by far but if I was looking for a piss easy game I wouldn't have felt as accomplished figuring out this combat in and out allowing me to get creative and see what made things tick as in the end it actually made me interested in the combat part again, a system I was starting to grow tired of as the games went on. It still has many oversights but in my opinion it gives the games combat CHARACTER, and if this game has anything going for it, that's it, overwhelming personality and identity.Overall can I say this is an experience YOU will enjoy with absolute certainty? No, this series has an entry for all kinds of people and there were a vocal few that didn't like this game and WILL LET YOU KNOW, but are they wrong in feeling that way? Of course not, it's their opinion, but they could stand to be a bit less blindly negative.It's a game that has many positives but it's far from a perfect game, you don't have to like it but at least give it a chance, you might just love what you see like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: After fully completing this game from my previous review (Which was about 6 Hours) I'm finally ready to give my full thoughts on Yakuza 3: The most controversial game in the franchise.Starting off the story is my 2nd favorite in the franchise (barring Like A Dragon), with a lot of wholesome moments for Kiryu to be himself instead of just "Cool Guy McGee", helping out in the orphanage helps you get attached to Kiryu's kids, including Kiryu himself, you see a sensitive side to the Ex-Yakuza that most games before (and after with 0) haven't shown. and by the time the real story begins, you fall in live with every character in the game, especially the Ryudo Family, which gives a hard gut-punch in the last few chapters, especially if you really like Rikiya  (we'll get to him soon). The weakest part for the story would have to be it's pacing, it feels too short, it feels about the length of a DLC Story mode, let alone an entire game, but the short pace still gives one of the best Yakuza stories to date. The voice work is great, especially the somewhat corny English voice acting, but Kiryu's VA absolutely gives what I believe is his best performance so far/since, with  , the guy you see as being the coolest sunuvabitch, gives one of the most emotional and heart-wrenching performances of all time, this time, Kiryu doesn't feel like a cool guy to insert yourself in, but an actual character.Now to get back to the game and not the story, time to tackle the most controversial parts of the game: The Combat, and I'll be honest, it's not the best combat in the series, but I do think that it's not as bad as people say. Yes the blocking is a problem, but there are multiple solutions to stop it, to me the worst part was all the bosses who stun-lock you, and the gun users in the later parts of the game,  are the worst part of the game, not the blocking. Other than that, the combat is solid, and given that this is my first time experiencing Kiryu's Dragon Style for the rest of the series, it does a good job at getting me used to a moveset I'm sure I'll get antiquated with for the rest of the series. Honestly, the only part of the game that I really hate is how wonky the camera controls are, but given that this is a remaster rather than a remake, I'm willing to give it a pass.I'm going to avoid giving reviews to the substories and the extra content because A. They aren't as important as the main story, but are solid, and B. I didn't do most of the minigames.And so, this game isn't as horrible as people say it is, but it isn't some hidden gem of the Yakuza series that people are overlooking, it's a solid game, that most people have trouble with. 8/10, would recommend, but wouldn't play again.

_childDocuments_.review: [SPOLIER FREE]As a fan of the Yakuza series this game sucks. So far it's the only one I didn't like by the end of it. - Combat: 3/10Negatives: It's clunky, shallow, and the enemy AI is abysmal. They block constantly meaning that fights are just an annoying mess. The bosses are hard purely from a mechanic standpoint which makes them no fun to fight, and the random encounter system is just annoying. I hate that I can't see them coming most of the time and it wastes so much time.Positives: I guess you can learn new moves through some fun mini-games and side things, but they shouldn't be almost essential if you want to stand a chance, like they are in this game.- Story: 5/10Negative: I expected at least a good 7/10 story going off of what the other games gave me but nope. It felt like they rewrote it halfway through. It gets needlessly complicated, way too many characters are introduced, there are some cheesy and predictable tropes early on, and random moves later on that don't make any sense plot wise.Positive: There are a few well written characters and lots of activities to do with those few characters before they disappear from the story.- Gameplay: 8/10Positive: Outside of combat the game holds it's own well. There are plenty of interesting submissions and characters to interact with. The mini-games are fun and most of them can be enjoyed for hours depending on your tastes. Negative: Kiryu feels a lot less fluid than the KIWAMI games if that's what you're used to but it's very minor. The only real downsides in gameplay is the day/night mechanic and the map. The game often doesn't tell you anything about where to go, and I found myself wandering the map several times frustrated cause I couldn't find where it wanted me to go. The day/night mechanic is just that some submission can only be completed at day or night and you need to progress in the story to change the time of day. I had to wait several chapters for nightime in order to finish a submission at one point.- Soundtrack & SFX: 7/10A bit dated as expected and the game is almost silent a lot of the time but it's nothing too bad, just it's age showing through I think.Overall: 4.5/10If you love your submissions you may enjoy this game more than I did, but the combat, one-sided villains, and various plot holes really drag this game down for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have decided to give this a negative as I ultimately did not find it that fun. After finishing Kiwami 2, I realised I had to wait until the summer sale to get the other Yakuza games on sale. During that time I played Fire Emblem Awakening and absolutely loved it. Then I played Yakuza 3 Remastered...Yakuza 3 is easy to hate and hard to love. It is easily the most dated of the Yakuza games, and any pretence about it being modern makes it about as modern as a BlackBerry nowadays. This game's not some diamond in the rough, it's just rough overall. Granted, this was the first mainline game to ever hit the PS3 back in the day, but even then, I have to wonder how good the reception must have been, or how low the standards must have been back in the day for some reviewers to give it scores in the 9s. Though I guess the jump from 2 to 3 must have been a sight to behold to warrant such high scores. In any case, the game is severely dated nowadays.Most people complain about the orphanage as one of the main issues of 3's story, but my grievances go far beyond just that simple matter. I didn't mind the orphanage much, despite breaking the pacing at times, though I suppose that's what having kids must be like. The main hook for the entire crime aspect is so underwhelming when you find out why in general, that I think that's a good way to describe the entire story. Good concepts, executed terribly. I mean, how could you make the inclusion of the CIA and Americans into the story boring? There is even a literal 30 minute exposition dump in a chapter literally called, "The Plot", leaving little to the mystery side of things and just explaining there because the game did such a horrible job with it. The main villain also seems like he's trying way too hard, but can you blame him? All the secondary antagonists are forgettable and bland. All this would have been fine but they even decided to reuse a cardinal Yakuza cliche, leading to an undeserved and lazy death, the only upside being that Kiryu's VA delivers one of his most emotional moments in the series overall.You've probably heard everything there is to hear about the game's combat. All the systems are there to make it a regular Yakuza beat em' up fare, but the problem lies in the fundamental design of the AI to block all of your attacks to high heaven. Yes, Komaki makes the combat bearable, but is at best a band-aid solution to a gaping bullet hole wound. Everybody mentions the blocking, but nobody mentions the other terrible AI design to be dodge heavy too, anyone who's gotten to the end of the Hitman missions will know what I mean. Even the Heat actions don't feel like they have any heft to them. They look like they hurt, sure, but it doesn't sound like it. It's not that Kiryu is weak, it's just that everybody else makes it seem that way by blocking at least 90% of attacks. There are minor solutions to make it better, but by no means is there a way to be a true master of combat in this game. Please try to get all the Heat Actions done so you can get a War God Amulet if you are able, because this baby will let you execute Heat Actions without needing any Heat at all.Oh boy, the minigames....as if everything else about playing this game doesn't make you appreciate the other games more, the minigames really solidifies this to a tee. Ever wonder if Cabaret Club wasn't Diner Dash and was boring and tedious? If the UFO Catcher and bowling had wonky physics to them? If the gambling was the most rigged it's ever been? If trying to get a tuna could give you mild anger issues? If golf was a thing? Then play this game, and you will immediately appreciate all the polish the other games have, because for a lack of better terms, there isn't one single minigame in this that I would consider fun in any way. The Chase minigame is masked by how short the sections are, but it really isn't quite good, anybody that's done the Ultimate Match where you have to chase Mack in under a minute can attest to that.Ultimate Matches here are pretty annoying and tedious to do, some of them are quite hard, but the majority are painful to get through. S ranking these will give the War God Talisman, this has the same function as the Talisman except you are always in Red Heat, from what I've heard, I didn't bother trying to do these more than I needed to.The completion for this is rough because I wouldn't recommend anyone start on Hard to even try to have fun with this game, so you will have to bust through Hard and then Legend because Legend only unlocks after Hard mode is beaten. The gambling is rigged the most here, so that will be rough to get through, and the tuna and Boxcelios and pool are tough to get through. Golf can also be a minor annoyance too, but if you manage to best those, then you're set. This is definitely the hardest so far to get through just because of the fundamental design flaws this game has. Only do what the game wants you to in terms of achievements for the completion list because other than the Heat Actions ones, the rewards aren't really worth it.My verdict for this is that even after all this, is to go in expecting the worst. If you somehow come out of it better, then good for you. If you can put up with the overall dated quality this game has, then perhaps you may even love it. Just note that even if they do a Kiwami 3, the orphanage and its connected stories as mandatory was a creative decision. So even if Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio decides to give this game the Kiwami treatment, that aspect wouldn't really go away. If there's anything positive to be said about this, is that you really will appreciate the other games once you've played this one...it's certainly an experience. This is definitely the weakest by far though. Hopefully 4's better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's story is a great continuation of the series' 8-title spanning narrative, albeit with some hiccups along the way. The plot starts slow, with Kiryu beginning a new step in his life by starting an orphanage in the game's new location, Ryukyu. This makes the first few hours a bit arduous, but with some great moments. Once the plot begins to gain momentum, it's standard Yakuza fare with excellent dialogue, plotting, and directing. In particular, new characters Mine, Rikiya, and Nakahara are standouts. The plot conveniently ties up one loose-end in the final moments of the game, which felt pretty rushed and maybe unfinished.The gameplay in Yakuza 3 is its weakest point. The first section of the game is filled with glorified fetch quests for the kids in Kiryu's orphanage. These do result in satisfying character building moments, but the gameplay accompanying them is lackluster. The pacing does improve, however. The other half of my gameplay gripes come from the combat. The boss fights always start so hype, but lose all their steam when you realize they block almost every attack from the front and the only tactic you have is to get behind the enemy and finish one full combo then reset and wait for them to attack again so you can get behind them. This makes these boss battles way longer than they should be and so boring. Even regular encounters on the street suffer from the fact that enemies block every single move you do. Overall, the combat is a major detractor for the game.That being said, if you want to see a satisfying continuation of the Yakuza series' epic grand narrative, the game comes highly recommended, flaws and all.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Yakuza Kiwami (9/10) and Yakuza Kiwami 2 (10/10) before I played this. I should play Yakuza 0 but I'll do that after I beat the Yakuza 3-6. Now onto the actual review. Mild spoilers. This time around Kiryu leaves Tokyo for a quite life in a tropical island off of mainland Japan to run an orphanage. As expected, situations come up and it is back to beating people to near death for the rest of the game. Combat was decent, Kiwami 1 and 2 were essentially remakes of the original games so I can understand why the brawling wouldn't feel as good in this one. But it wasn't bad or boring either. There were a few bossfights where enemies used guns or throwing knives and those were the only fights that got annoying. The rest of the combat was enjoyable. The story was good. I didn't like it as much as the previous 2 but seeing Kiryu attempt to leave the Yakuza life behind and start a looking after the kids in the orphanage was wholesome and good development in his character. Haruka was the favorite child but I actually didn't dislike any of the kids in his orphanage. Some of the quests around the kids were annoying but the overall story was good enough to keep myself paying attention. As far as the rest of the story goes, it felt like it just pulled aspects from the previous games and downgraded them. A lot of the plot twists and surprise scenes were easily predictable down to each individual word in their lines. However, there were still moments in the game that had that classic Yakuza charm like a woman flying through the air on her bike while looking at a poster or Majima driving a truck trough a bunch of guys to help you. While I'm on the topic of Majima he doesn't have enough scenes in this game so automatic -1 point. Overall this game wasn't as good as Kiwami 1 and 2 but it was still worth playing. The story continuation was good enough to keep me around and I didn't find myself taking more than a 2 day break between putting the game down. It's a 7/10 for me but it was totally worth the play.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me start by saying this game is my guilty pleasure, and I might have some bias, I went in fully expecting jank, an outdated story, atrocious minigame controls, and bad gameplay, heck, the fighting gameplay was so bad I had to download a couple rebalancing mods for me to enjoy the game from the get-go, it took me around 10 minutes to beat Rikiya in the beginning of the game without anything installed. To clarify, the fighting gameplay loop is very very fun in this game, but mechanically the heat gauge is near impossible to fill up, enemies don't take much damage, and they block a ton. The graphics don't really hold up either, it's jarring seeing these PS3 renders after playing Kiwami and Dragon engine games back to back.The game's pacing is extremely slow, you spend around 6ish chapters mostly doing mundane orphanage errands and missions that aren't that innovative nor interesting, outside of a couple orphanage related stories, It felt really difficult to care much about the children, getting through this part of the game took a lot out of me. Unlike the previous games in the series, the minigames in Yakuza 3 are beyond atrocious, their controls are sloppy, outdated, an actual nightmare to play and enjoy, and the minigames in Yakuza are partly why I love these games so much, but in this game none of them were good, even the hostess club minigame isn't the same as 0 nor K2, it's just walking around your club then dressing up the hostess in conjunction with the customer's preferences, don't make me get started on the golf minigame that you are coerced into doing before progressing through the main story in the beginning.Now, why am I giving this game a thumbs up despite it's glaring issues? I mentioned how the pacing was very slow, and the first 6 chapters felt like an orphanage simulator. This game has 13 chapters, and after Kiryu is finally in Kamurocho, the game picks up, really fast, and IMO it easily has the best action sequences in the series so far after playing 0, K1, K2. Kiryu's character development in this game is incredible, Yakuza 3 fleshes Kiryu out as a character more than the other entries before it, and it wouldn't be farfetched to claim that Kiryu has had the most development out of all the other previous entries combined. This game doesn't have many great characters as 0, but the ones in Y3 stand out a lot; most notably Rikiya and Mine, I've grown to love these two characters to an unimaginable degree, Nakahara is an amazing character too. Albeit this game has cheap and silly tropes such as  The OST of this game is amazing, Fly is personally my favorite track of all time currently. Lyricism without Tears, Clay Doll on the Cradle, Independence for Violence, honestly, I would list all of them because this game's OST is timeless.Kiryu than any other game is much more emotional and human, there's so much focus on him, it's incredible. Yoshitaka Mine carries this game so hard and makes it top tier, and Y3 truly deserves a KIWAMI remake with the dragon engine, I can't wait for this game to be remade so everyone can actually play it and enjoy it, the second half of Y3 is personally my favorite Yakuza so far, and It feels difficult to imagine it'll ever be topped, this game made me go through so much emotion, I grew attached to the major characters, especially Mine and Rikiya, I love them, I hope they get more spotlight in the KIWAMI remake. If you love Yakuza, if you love Kiryu, play this game, it's the most important game for him as a character, just please ignore the uninspired boring sidestories and minigames, and just focus on beating the game as quick as you can. Make sure to download rebalancing mods.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the one Yakuza game (so far) that I would say to skip out on. Not because of one issue per se but a myriad of them. The combat is enemies being bullet sponges in terms of health and on top of that they block basically anything, can break out of your hits to woop you on your ass for no reason whenever they feel like it AND the story is not exactly riveting either.It includes entertaining topics like real estate legal struggles and children's issues at school or with their dogs. That is basically 80% of the game. Then you have some of the most jarring ass-pulls of the Yakuza franchise, for no real good reason (it isn't even really that entertaining either, just pointless and generic) and it only picks up in the last stretch. Honestly, even if you want to be a Yakuza fan, you don't need to push yourself through this game unless you really need the whole story. At no point was it really fun, I pushed through it for the sake of playing through them all and I don't feel particularily great about it.

_childDocuments_.review: The remastered collection's port is  bad. I've been getting constant slowdowns and crashes during my playthrough. I've managed to reduce the slowdowns by going into task manager and changing the game's priority setting to high, but the game still crashes after awhile. Besides the technical issues, I think Yakuza 3 has to be the worst Yakuza entry in the franchise so far. The combat is very barebones and the AI is frustrating. I'm playing normal difficulty, but enemies will prioritize blocking over fighting. There isn't a guard break to stun the enemy and the enemy's guard is up for most of the the time in combat. In my opinion, a brawler  is not fun if I'm constantly trying to break the enemy's guard. It slows down the pacing of the game and drags on a boring fight. Another issue I have is the execution of the story. The story introduces several different subplots and tries to combine them all together to create one cohesive story. But the execution is a tangled mess as the main focus of the story constantly shifts. At one point in the game, they dedicate an entire chapter just to clarify the story and all the varying subplots. If a game has to dedicate an entire section of the game for clarification and exposition on how the story is progressing-- they've done a poor job on telling the story through gameplay.The game is clunky and outdated. Kiryu is as wide as a tank and moves like a tank. Walking and fighting animations for every character is very stiff. I don't understand why everyone walking has to swing their arms like they're on an invisible elliptical. Honestly, I think Yakuza 3 should have been given the Kiwami treatment like its predecessors, not a re-master. It's outdated and I found myself rushing through the game so I can get started with Yakuza 4. TLDR; Go ahead and play this game if you're a Yakuza fan, but it's an outdated game with a poor port. I would not recommend this game for someone trying to get into the series.Edit: I played through Yakuza 0-6. This is definitely the worst game in the series. They patched out the technical issues though.

_childDocuments_.review: Before starting this review I'd like to state that I don't want to take either 0 or the Kiwami versions into consideration. Since, to be fair and straight off the bat absolutely ruin your expectation of Y3 from the very beginning. I'm taking this game into the same consideration of what a remaster would have been at the time. Meaning  Y3 PS2 to Y3R PS3.The story/main campaign alone does not do the "Like A Dragon" storyline any favors, it does however flesh out our main character as a multi dimensional protagonist. Ex-con, father, protector etc etc. If the game itself was simply just that? It'd be perfect since every single other aspect of the gameplay that holds it back would just be a minor oversight. You can call Y3 the "beach episode" of the series since you don't have to play it but it does give some context to our main character and toss them into a story that serves no real purpose to the series, besides making it just so much more complicated than it needs to be.The orphanage portions are the highlights of the game, making every visit charming and memorable, but being shoehorned into a slow and otherwise boring campaign- you wind up feeling like a forced and obligated parent.Combat in this game is... not good. You are more than capable of beating any enemy or boss- it just takes an absurd amount of time. There are no real moments where you feel like you interact with your enemies besides the rare Heat moments which deplete while not attacking, after having been attacked and pretty much just breathing. Weapons are a bit overtuned and under modified making them useful when used correctly and useless because they break so quickly.Nearing the end of the game, the each mission stops pointing you in the direction you need to go- forcing you to run around or just look up online what to do next. Hitting the pause menu opens up a general hint about what to do next but at times it comes off vague and unhelpful. Like find "So and so" and there's literally no clue as to where they are, you spent minutes if not hours just trying to figure out tiny things that advance the story about two and half steps before you're stuck doing another chore filled side mission? Or just a mission inbetween your usual Campaign progression?Anyways, if you want the achievements- if you want the full experience; buy it. But if you're just interested in seeing what happens. Just watch a video on the story you'll pretty much get the basics of what's going on and you can move on with your life and Kiryu's.

_childDocuments_.review: This was without a doubt the weakest in the series so far for me, but that isn't saying much considering the quality of 0, 1 and 2. The story was the strongest part of the game by far, only lacking in its pacing. By the end I was well invested and stopped pissing in order to see what happens next, but at the start I was dead ass thinking of doing biology revision instead due to it suffering from this little issue: It was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring as ♥♥♥♥. The villain and supporting cast in this game were spot on with Rikiya, Nakahara and Mine being the highlights among some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ characters like Richardson.However, The part in which this game suffered the most was in the combat and world. The combat felt less satisfying than shoving porridge up my ass, and was easy to button mash or repeat the same x x x y y combo over and over in my experience (then again that is partially my fault for being a boring ass guy and not spicing things up, although the game never really encouraged that all too often). Next, the world was nice and big yes, but I felt as though it was quite lifeless in comparison to prior games. I was never all too eager to explore and when I did it felt like a chore to engage in any of the activities or side quests I stumbled upon, which removes half the fun of a Yakuza game. So I often spent my time rushing through and trying to get to the next main story quest a lot more than in the others which kind of blows hard. Some of the main story quests were tedious as ♥♥♥♥ as well e.g. Finding any of the annoying ♥♥♥♥♥ in chapter 10 (this was the game's lowest point and was frustrating as paper stuck in your ass when you go for a ♥♥♥♥).Overall the game was pleasant compared to most, however, it lacked something present in the other games that led to me disliking a lot of the time I spent in between main story quests and especially the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ start of the game. Also the karaoke sucked in my opinion (at least in comparison to 0 and kiwami 1 + 2).7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, Yakuza 3. One of the most controversial Yakuza in 2024. What should we start?I'm writing this right after finishing the game.Gameplay.- Yes, it feels like a 2009 game. I can't deny, the "blockuza 3" meme is true here. Everything feels outdated.- If you're from Kiwami 2, it'll be as night and day. Might be a hot take but I still prefer Dragon Engine over this one.- Random encounter is way too annoying. Enemy approaching you so fast that if you got locked, you can't outrun them like 90% of the time.- A ridiculous achievement is to get the encounter while you're in the FPS mode. Holy Jesus.- Probably the only game I rushed to finish it. I did once with Pass.Story- Probably the only redeemable part of the whole game but still kinda weak. Like they tried to make it so complicate but just solved by simply dumping on one thing as a reason. Sounds nice but not really.- Many colorful characters. I mean, how good it has to be that even 15 years later people still remember most of the character from this games. I mean, if you ask the same thing with Yakuza 4 or 5 you probably won't remember any side characters at all.Graphics- It's not as bad as when it was launched, I can vouch for that as I tried the early version. Now it runs so fantastic.- If you're on 1080p display, put the scaling around 150% should make the environment crisp enough.- You can't do anything about the "un-remasterable" things like facial animations or some cutscenes.Overall... I don't know, honestly. The story isn't that bad, especially compared to other remastered series, but it shows its age here and there. Some redundant and unnecessary side stories. The first iterations of cabaret club (which I'm so glad how it evolved in later series), hostesses, many mini-games.Sadly, this is the starting point of the "grinding" series. 4th is the worst one.Recommended?Only if you can live with early PS3 gameplay.Blockuza is real and I don't care which kind of copium you're smoking it's the worst gameplay in the series (that's why people asked for Kiwami 3 despite it sounds nonconstructive to ask a studio to constantly remake stuff).I feel like it's probably the only game in the series that you should just watch a "full movie" stuff on YT instead of playing. I bought and played it just because I love this series and leaving one is not sitting right with me, despite how bad it is.The simplest explanation for PS3 era games of this series is "you trade the gameplay for the story". 5 has the best game play (of PS3 era) but the worst storywriting ever, while 3 is the vice versa.And now you know why it costs $2 for a Y4..Should you wait for Sales?Absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Yakuza game I've ever played. I have mix feeling towards yakuza 3, but I think I understand why people like and hate it. The game only has 12 chapters, so that leaves me 6 of the main story chapters that were actually a bit more interesting and enjoyable to proceed with. _childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is probably the weakest entry in the series. If you're playing in chronological order, it definitely feels like a step backwards in everything; graphics, game design, gameplay, etc., because it's literally a PS3 game that came out in 2009, albiet slightly touched up. It's by no means a bad game, it just suffers in the shadow of previous games. This shouldn't be a huge issue because the real 'point' of playing this is the story, but if for whatever ungodly reason you don't care about that and only want good gameplay, don't bother with this. Gameplay seems to suffer slightly from the old engine and their ♥♥♥♥ job with this port. And if you're really bothered by it feeling dated and just want to experience the story, watch the cutscenes on YouTube. If you do like the series for its story and gameplay formula, it's probably safe to assume you'd at least enjoy this one, but there are a number of things worth noting, ESPECIALLY if you're playing in story order (0-6) so as to temper your expectations, otherwise you're more likely to be disappointed.Despite being a remastered port released in 2021, there are some things that are screwed up that they never bothered fixing, that YOU need to either get mods to fix, change the FPS, or deal with. I really have no patience for this kind of ♥♥♥♥ these days and cannot stand relying on modders for quality of life features and especially to fix broken mechanics. These are primarily related to the 60fps upgrade that breaks some physics and mechanics. Most of the minigames (bowling, golf, pool) are much harder because their physics are tied to the framerate, but it doesn't seem like there are any mods to fix this. If you're going to attempt 100%ing this game, for the love of God lock the game to 30fps. I have no interest in the minigames outside of karaoke (which doesn't seem to be negatively affected) so if you're like me you're probably OK with leaving it at 60fps, HOWEVER...Get the "Quickstep Restoration" mod, ESPECIALLY if you're playing on hard. Because of issues with the framerate upgrade, they halved the distance of Kiryu's quickstep/dodge. You could probably live without this fix for most of the game on normal, unless you want to try and beat the harder bosses like Amon, but if you're on hard you NEED it. Enemies will block way too much compared to the previous games on this difficulty. Without the original quickstep distance, you are forced into a more time consuming fighting style that feels tedious compared to 0/K1/K2, relying on the cheese of your Komaki moves that unlock in chapter 5 or 6. I didn't know about the quickstep nerf and simply restarted on normal because I could just easily envision this ♥♥♥♥ getting untenable late game. Quickstep is integral to how you'll be successful in this game THE way to efficiently counter hard difficulty's blockspam.You also need the "Yakuza 3 Restoration Patch" too. There was a bunch of licensed music they cut that this restores, but most importantly, the cutscenes in the PC version are much lower quality than the remastered PS3 version and look horrific. This mod restores them and the difference is ridiculous, almost comical that the developers didn't do this themselves. And there's also a really stupid bug where the Ryukyu street noise is much louder than other parts of the game so you should probably get "Fix for the loud ambient car sound in Downtown Ryukyu". All of these issues are laid out on the PCGamingWiki, but who would've thought you'd need to check there for a so-called remastered version released in 2021?Gameplay is the typical Yakuza format of watching cutscenes, running around the city, beating up enemies, doing side stories, and fighting a boss or two, then doing the same in the next chapter. This game is much shorter, between 16 and 30 hours depending on how much side content and minigames you distract yourself with. As for that side content, I found myself taken out of the 'main quest' more than other games. They felt more tedious, boring, repetitive, less interesting, consequently less complementary to the game's storytelling, and more vehicles for leveling up and getting items. Some are missable unless you know how to initiate them by checking walkthroughs. They're technically not 'completely' missable as you can go back in Premium Adventure (free-roam after the story) to finish them up, but to me that's kinda pointless; the 'point' is to level up and to give you things to do between major story events. They've always been diversions, but it's way more noticeable that they are in 3.You only have one fighting style and enemies are drop dead stupid, even on hard. Hard is less of an actual 'hard' difficulty and more an exercise in tedium; it only seems to turn up enemies' block frequency, health, and damage output, NOT intelligence and stuff that matters like attack frequency, combos, etc. Besides boss fights, combat is pretty boring, and since you do a LOT of it, most of the game can feel pretty boring. But like I said from the beginning, you're here for the story. I personally think it's strong enough to warrant playing through and dealing with everything mentioned previously, but it's not free from critique.The story is definitely weaker compared to previous games. It's not bad, but again, just not as good. Kiryu leaves Kamurocho for Okinawa and sets up an orphanage with Haruka, but it's existence is threatened by a land development deal involving people in the Tojo clan, the Japanese government, and spoilers but not really: , who all have converging interests in setting up a resort, casino, and military base. The characters are all fine, obvious standouts being Kiryu, Rikiya, Date, and of course Majima. None of the few antagonists are as compelling as those in previous entries. All of the Tojo leadership are lame and the main bad guy who is revealed later in the game is really uninteresting. The whole plot is a little predictable, but there are a couple effective deaths. The orphanage thread was a fun change of pace, but it seems somewhat out of place. Sure, there are glimpses of this kind of Kiryu in 0/K1/K2, it just gets a little too goofy and feels slow. Like I'm here for a crime drama full of intrigue and doing Yakuza things, not raising kids and being a great dad. Also I wish there were more fully voiced cutscenes. This wasn't as noticeable in previous games but it feels like there were more of the static in-engine "press X to read more dialogue" stuff. Again, probably due to it being a remaster, but I would much prefer all of the story segments as full cutscenes to not break the flow and interfere with tone.Despite everything I've said up to this point, it's still fun and I enjoyed my time with it. To sum things up, Yakuza 3 is just an older, dated game that suffers in comparison to 0/K1/K2. This game is rooted in the context of it being the third entry of a young series that was still finding its footing for storytelling and character development. It's significantly shorter than 0/K1/K2 and despite my playtime, not a 77 hour investment, I just really enjoy taking everything in and seeing as much of this game as possible (minus some of the minigames, I'm not that masochistic). A better estimate is 20 hours if you're focusing on the story and somewhere between 30 and 100 if you the more substories, minigames, crafting, collecting, etc. you want to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with a negative: this game's combat feels *awful*. It's not for no reason; this game was adapted from Ryu ga Gotoku Kenzan!, a swordfighting game with guard breaks -- and this game is missing all of them. As a result, be prepared for a lot of blocking from the AI that you can't do anything about -- do *not* play this game on Hard if you value your time (I did, and I wish I hadn't).All that aside, though, this game is still a fantastic follow-up to Yakuza 2 (not Kiwami 2), and it's not hard to get invested in the ever-present power struggles within the Tojo Clan once again. In Yakuza 3, our main hero Kiryu Kazuma has retired from the yakuza life and now runs an orphanage with his surrogate daughter, Haruka, on the sunny shores of Okinawa Island, Japan -- but it's not long until the rug is pulled from underneath him once again and he is pulled back into the fold to solve yet another problem in the Tojo Clan.Naturally, Kiryu doesn't really have time for politicking, and solves his problems by punching them in the face.Really, really hard. Feels good, though, when you're not having to battle through the bullet-sponge difficulty style.8/10, brought down from a 10/10 by the laborious combat. Absolutely essential to play if you're invested in the Yakuza story.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is a flawed game but not to the point where I'd skip it, it's still worth it if you care about Kiryu, his story, and exploring new places. As someone who decided to play Yakuza 2 on PS2 instead of Kiwami 2 (I don't like how it's basically a completely different game that tells Y2's story) I appreciated the way it advanced the series more than others I think.The story, unfortunately, feels a bit rushed and gives the impression of something that was originally going to be way bigger. You can kinda tell with how  and the infamous giant exposition scene. If you're someone that not the type to do every substory, you're gonna be annoyed with all the mandatory orphanage stories, but as someone who does do all of them I really like seeing Kiryu's new life and how happy he is as a dad. The story does otherwise have some fun moments and an enjoyable finale though.Game was played on hard, I don't know if anything significant changes in Normal or Legend.On one hand, Kiryu's kit has improved a lot since Yakuza 2, with improved controls, getting tiger drop and parry pretty early, and powerful heat moves like Essence of Rolling. However, as you probably know, the problem with this game's combat is the enemies. Their problem isn't just that they block all the time, it's combined with some other factors. So, if they block, why not go behind them since they can't block from behind? That does work on occasion, but depending on the moveset the enemies can have attacks where they turn 180 as they do it. Grabs can work, but they're not that strong and even then there are enemies which just can't be grabbed, which sucks. There's also the way the ai works: enemies will mostly only attack when they know you're vulnerable, such as when you're attacking someone else. Later games' enemies do a downplayed version of this ai but combined with the blocking this can make early game group fights really annoying. Even later on this makes standard enemy fights longer on average than most others in the series. Now, at least it can be easy to tiger drop enemies on one-on-one fights, right? It would be if they actually attacked you. Biggest example of this is  who as far as I remember just didn't attack for the longest time and waited for you to mess up, this is the same for the Coliseum enemies where if you wanted to counter them, you need to try bait their ai into attacking by facing away from them or with blockstrings, which even then doesn't always work (works pretty well on Majima though). Probably the worst offender is Komaki who I swear wasn't play-tested. There are a couple of alternate ways to whittle enemies' health down but it's not exactly efficient or consistent. Funny thing though, Amon and the final bosses actually attack you constantly, making them the funnest bosses in the game since you can actually counter/get behind them!Anecdotes from my experience:-Komaki Parry only works for punches and most weapons, but you can do it the moment the enemy enters the attacking animation compared to tiger drop where it's just before they attack, so get used to using that on enemies with punching movesets. Enemies may take forever to attack, but they'll do it eventually! I think enemies with weapons are slightly more aggressive too.-Get some swords for annoying group fights, they can't block them bare-handed.-Get used to heat actions that are initiated by grabbing and essence of rolling since that's basically free damage.New to the series is Ryukyu, which is pretty comfy if I do say so myself. In a series that's so far focused on city life, it's nice to explore a place a bit more rural, with a good amount of substories focusing on its culture and how life is like there. While failable substories can be a bit annoying, There being one where you play hide and seek with Kiryu's kids is very cute.Kamurocho has some enjoyable stuff as well, the first time you can explore it at a good run speed (compared to ps2) with a free camera and some nice substories. Following up what happened way back in Yakuza 1's intro in 95 was a pleasant surprise and the journalist is pretty enjoyable for one that's sub-story only. Rikiya's substories helped the character a lot too.Chase missions are fine when you figure out you can quickly stop pressing run for tight turns then start running again.Accessing the item box from pay phones started here and it's super welcome. Having to go all the way back to a hideout to sort the box with your 9 item inventory in ps2 honestly demotivated me from playing a bit.Weapon modding came here and it's fine here too, but I'd always rather try to just continue the game than gather materials for things I don't really need. I just come here to repair my swords.Locker keys' sparkly spots aren't as obscured as the ps2 but now require looking in places you'd never otherwise. I do wonder how many have gotten them all without a guide 'cause I certainly don't have the patience.Hostesses are back and as a carryover from the past game you need to complete all 9 to face Amon. I don't know why so many of these games have so many, they're never that interesting.IF7 lets you fight past enemies and they get you a few new abilities, mostly not that useful but I'd still get the 'guard against swords bare-handed' upgrade if you're planning to face Amon.Of course there's Karaoke which debuts in this game. They didn't go too far with it yet with Kiryu only having one song but at least the hostess songs are enjoyable enough and Kiryu has cute cheers.Pool and Darts are new, and the batting cages now require you to aim the bat as well as time it. Quick tip, Pool and Batting is way easier with the mouse & keyboard if you're into completion. Darts is easier depending on the yakuza game you're in or maybe you'll have better luck than me in 3. I found it extremely brutal on controller though, same with Pool. With batting, just remember to time it with Kiryu's hands becoming steady rather than the ball. I'm pretty sure cee-lo, koi-koi and oichu-kabu debuted here too. Koi-koi you'll eventually get by remembering the hands, what cards are high-value and how they combine by playing. I'd recommend turning cherry blossom viewing off.Fishing I actually found pretty fun, didn't even have that much trouble with the tuna though I played post-patch. It does take ages with the tougher fish though, especially in Y4.Golf I also found actually pretty fun despite the complaints I heard about it. It's harsher than, say, Mario Golf but a bit of practice should get the golfing substory done. Just remember the wind, the way the ball rolls and the downhill spots when putting. Getting -5 for completion is however pretty dang tough.Boxcelios is a nice little arcade game where you pay attention to glowy weak points and laser them. Just remember you're way faster when not firing.There's also hostess maker which is really boring and returns in 4 for some reason.Soundtrack's cool, favourite tracks are Sounds Storm and Receive and Stab You. Best Karaoke song is Saturday Night Lover. In the context of 'English speaking people that were seemingly just in Japan at the time and were probably given no direction', Donald Glover did a pretty alright job compared to the 'VAs' for the Mega Man ps1 games. Revelations are fun too but unfortunately don't get much better apart from the moves you getThat's all I can cover within character limit. While Yakuza 3 definitely has issues, it also added a ton for the series in terms of controls, exploration and minigames. If you're fine dealing with annoying enemies and exposition I think there's a lot to like here.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game.I don’t enjoy leaving negative reviews. I prefer to sing praises instead of criticizing, since I know any piece of media might float some people’s boats, but I cannot for the hell of me give this any praise. The shock of coming to this from such an amazing game as Kiwami 2 is insane, and I think Yakuza 3 would really benefit from getting Kiwami’d.Once upon a time, the Yakuza Series was at stake of not being localized due to low performance on the western market. It was laid in the shoulders of Yakuza 3’s success for a decision to be made about the localization of future Yakuza games. Now WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking in laying such a responsibility on THIS GAME, out of all of them?This is a brawler game where 90% of your hits do not connect. Enemies are either blocking everything or in a state of invincibility. You are given absolutely no tools of fighting back, at least until you level up. Enemies can block while you’re in the middle of your attack string and you CAN’T DO THE SAME for theirs until you level up. I have spent most of my game time looking at Kiryu dizzied or laying on the ground, waiting for him to get up only to get downed again by some boss with the most annoying barks I’ve ever heard.Kiryu hits as hard as a child here. In the beginning, heat actions do not cause enough damage to be worth the hassle. Regular attacks do chip damage. Your grabs are useless on a ton of enemies.Your enemies, meanwhile, hit like a truck.I have let myself get killed in a boss battle (Yes, it was ) so the easy mode prompt triggered and I wouldn’t want to pull my hair out with the same fight again. I missed a QTE and lost what, about 25% of my health? ♥♥♥♥ that.The chase minigame is dumb and I dreaded every time the POSSIBILITY of a chase or an escape sequence arose.The story Is silly and I enjoyed it. I liked some of the new characters, Haruka is great here and the kids from the orphanage are annoying but not to the point of pissing me off. I played this game solely for this, and I’d STRONGLY recommend to just play it on easy from the get go, if you want to experience the story for yourself. As a story? I enjoyed my time with it. As a game? I hated every single second.I have never rushed a Yakuza game so far, until deciding to skip all side content on this game because I couldn’t stand it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people in the fanbase dislike this game, but they're crazy, it's a good game. This is a Remaster of a 2009 game, this is a sequel to the original 2, and going from PS2 to PS3 was a huge improvement at the time.The story gets me really emotional, and it's a really deep look in the most human part of this legendary man. It's one of my favourite stories in the franchise.Music slaps as always.Gameplay starts a little slow, so be prepared for that.
