_childDocuments_.review: Before I played this game, i heard it was the worst in the series. So maybe it's just because I had low expectations, but I'm actually enjoying it a lot!It's definitely kind of a shock to go back to the very old-fashioned 3D brawler controls. When I used Kiryu's classic style in Yakuza 0 and Kiwami, it was unbearably slow and stiff, But in a game that's designed around it, it feels a lot better to use. All the RPG systems are obviously more primitive, but it's not as big of a downgrade as I feared.I've noticed that weapons seem to be a lot more useful in this one. For the other games, it was more of a gimmick to bring out from time to time, but for this one it's something that's very useful for boss fights, and there's a whole system for upgrading them using crafting materials, not unlike Yakuza: Like a Dragon.The new area of Okinawa is very well-realized. Be forewarned that this game starts off with a LOT of Kiryu hanging out with a bunch of adorable kids. I didn't mind it, but if you're waiting for the plot to really kick into gear, I can see it being very frustrating. The substories are not like Kiwami, but more along the lines of the goofy, fun things you see in 0 and Kiwami 2.I find a lot of value in seeing the origin of running gags and characters, so I think it's very worth playing through this one. Connecting the dots from the old PS2 brawlers to the sprawling RPGs they eventually become.I haven't finished it yet, but from what I've played so far, it's another good Yakuza game!

As much as it's repeated, Yakuza 3 is the weakest game in the franchise, however I think it's still worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the worst PC ports I've ever played. The game has some kind of weird CPU usage problem that'll drive the vast majority of CPU's to 100% usage. Playing for just a few minutes drives my temps right up to 90+--numbers I've literally never seen, even when multitasking CPU intensive applications. It's no exaggeration to say that this game can permanently damage your hardware.Changing the volume sliders in-game at all causes crazy audio stuttering, certain minigames like fishing are broken as certain timers and values appear to be tied to CPU clock speed... The game is an absolute mess and never should have been released in this state.Moreover the game itself hasn't aged well at all. The combat is extremely stale and infuriating--as none of your combos actually cause enough hitstun to combo and enemies will turtle up indefinitely whenever you attack, and gang up on you in group fights with no limit to the frequency of attacks or number of enemies attacking at once, limiting your options significantly and guaranteeing stunlock hell situations.Can't recommend. Even if you just want to suffer through it for the story to get to 4, wait until the CPU usage issues are resolved (if they're ever resolved).

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending this with hesitance. Many features of this game are average at best, with others faring worse because of its age. Also, for players jumping over from Y0-K2, the experience will feel jarring and it takes time getting used to. That being said, the game isn't terrible, and is definitely worth the playthrough.The plot is decent, albeit with pacing issues. You'll be doing virtually nothing relevant to the main story during certain chapters, only to be slapped with a huge info dump in the next. Most of the newly introduced characters didn't really stand out for me as the story unfolded, save for one which I will not mention to avoid spoilers. The intense portions of the plot weren't mindblowing, but they got the job done at moving the story forward.The combat is a mixed bag for me as well. The enemies are tougher than those from Y0-YK2, but it does encourage better positioning and timing. That being said, your foes will block ALOT, and this does get frustrating especially during certain boss battles, where it becomes a challenge to land your combos unless you perform specific techniques.The minigames are just downright broken. Frame perfection is required for fishing, the hostess minigame is downright terrible, and the physics for many others is just janky and appalling to experience firsthand. It might be because of the change to 60FPS, but jesus, they were horrific.The substories. This was one of the more disappointing aspects of the game for me. Many of the substories from Y0-YK2 were enthralling, comedic, sometimes even depressing. I looked forward to searching for substories from those games. In Y3, this wasn't the case at all. An overwhelming majority of the substories that I experienced felt like cookie-cutter fillers, like mundane sidequests from AAA games that were designed to be stuffed in there for the sake of content. Some were funny, admittedly, but they didn't grip my attention as much as the ones from the older games.Now, it might seem as though I'm trashing this game, but ultimately, I did still enjoy it somewhat. I never felt like I wanted to put this game down and cast it aside during my playthrough. The character development for the recurring main cast is great, more Kiryu and Majima is great, and more Yakuza is always great. It might not be the best Yakuza game; hell, it might not even be an average one, but as a fan of the Yakuza franchise, I still recommend giving it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the third game in the series, released back in the year of our lord 2009 for the PS3. If you're this far into the series you've probably played the previous games so I don't need to give you a summary of what these games are like. If you're new just stop reading this and go play Zero.Everything you've heard about this game's combat. It's true. But it's not even my main gripe with this game. I'll get into the other stuff later, because somehow .Yes, it's slow and stiff.Yes, you deal literal single-digit pixels of damage with every attack. No damage upgrades ever.Yes, bosses have added resistance to weapons and heat actions, just to waste your time.Yes, enemies block everything you throw at them from the front. Two thirds of the enemy types (there's a grand total of three) either resist or counter your grabs.Yes,  is not even remotely a thing with this game's pathetic-ass dash that moves one millimeter.Yes, you need to grind your ass off to even make Kiryu remotely playable by the time you're 2/3 done with the game. Your combos aren't even true combos until you have every "combo speed" upgrade at your disposal so you can keep a single chain going without an enemy casually walking out of it.Hitboxes are the most inconsistent in the whole series.Grabs go through enemies if there's even the slightest height difference (inclines, stairways), grabs also go through enemies if they're in any kind of attack state.Heat action requirements are INCREDIBLY picky, and generally require enemies to be at a complete standstill, giving you only a frame or two to trigger them before that enemy's AI decides to do whatever else it feels like doing (usually dashing out of your way or otherwise moving out of range to be defensive and waste your time, because they HATE being aggressive in any way, so you're never even in any danger of dying, outside of dying of boredom).You've heard all of this before if you've seen anyone talk about this game, it's nothing new. We know.I would like to talk about this game's STORY though, because it is genuinely insane to me that any deranged person can go out and pretend that it's anything close to good, let alone "one of the best in the series".Needless to say I was mentally tuning out by the end from boredom.Immediately forgot most of the character names as soon as they were unceremoniously removed from the plot, too. That's how unmemorable everyone in this game is.The music's nothing to write home about, either. JUST finishing the game, I remember... two or three songs at most. Anything that isn't generic ambience is just generic Yakuza "rock" themes that are like four notes in total and have no memorable melodies to them.Easily one of the quickest ALT+F4+Uninstalls I've done, soon as I was done 100%ing to avoid the blemish in my series 100% journey. Minigames and side content were the most bloated and miserable in the entire series BTW. 119 bland substories, censored/removed content notwithstanding.I was THIS close to waiting for a Kiwami 3 after seeing the bad reputation this game had. But caved in and bought the remaster pack. This game does NOT deserve a remake. It does NOT deserve a Kiwami 3.And if I had waited for something like that to happen, I would have simply never got around to playing the rest of the series.Ripping the bandaid off now so I can play the games after and actually have anything  a good time was the best choice here.Fans of this game are actual insane toxic gatekeepers too. Stay away from them.

_childDocuments_.review: A severe downgrade that still hits the mark.If you are like me and never played the Yakuza games on console, but in the order they came out on PC, this iteration of the series might be disappointing. Since this is not a remake but just a remaster there are several game mechanics that are not as refined and at times even incredibly frustrating to someone who started the series with Yakuza 0 or the Kiwami games.- The minigames are mostly boring as hell (especially the cabaret club) and the acompanying stories have not an ounce of the charm that the later games have.- The chase mechanic where you have to run after people in certain story missions is poorly executed and rage-inducing.- Combat is a lot less fluid and the enemies in the later stages of the game block so much that you basically have to default to counter moves, as offensive actions are mostly useless.- The weapons are either underpowered or break so easily and are so expensive to repair that you might as well not bother with them at all.- The inventory system is one of the most infuriatingly stupid systems I've ever encountered in any game. You have to constantly get to a save point to swap stuff because there's no room for anything.- Tracking of side missions (or substories as they are called) is abysmal and without the help of online game guides, you'll miss half the content the game has to offer.- Saving and fast travel locations are so sparse that you don't bother using them most of the time, which leads to a lot of running around.Of course one has to take into account that this game is now more than 10 years old and they fixed a lot of this in later games. Although that makes it even less palatable, knowing that there are better ways to almost every mechanic the game employs.All that being said, if you're a fan of the series and want to experience the whole story of Kazuma Kiryu, it is worth playing for that alone. And you can get used to a lot of the flaws of the game over time. It's still very much enjoyable, introduces a lot of characters that become important later on and has a lot of heart.Just don't make the same mistake as me and play it back to back with an almost perfect Yakuza game like Kiwami 2 or "Like a Dragon".

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this make me wish there was a middle ground on the review page. Yakuza 3 is the first game to come out on new hardware, the Playstation 3. Unlike the PS2 games, it did not get a remake on a modern engine. It got an update to its graphical capabilities, like higher resolution and framerate.Being the oldest, 'current' game of the series, it lacks the fighting styles of 0 and Kiwami, nor does it have the buttery smooth physics of Kiwami 2. Despite that it holds up fine, mechanically. The fighting isn't the issue I had with this game. The problem is the story is dreadfully boring.Without summarizing the whole game, Kiryu opened an orphanage to distance himself from the yakuza lifestyle. A big part of the game is spent bonding with the children there, which ends up being going through loads of texts boxes, walking somewhere, then a ton more text. This isn't new for the series, but there's something fascinating about reading dialogue about the conspiracies and plots of criminals and scumbags.The game could have offset the story with some more interesting game mechanics, but being the oldest of the modern games it can't hold up very well. It's a shame, because there are a few bosses and cutscenes I enjoy in this game. You should only consider getting this if you're a diehard fan of the series and are interested in what happens between the 2nd and 4th game, other than that you'll be fine skipping this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 3 is another example which proves that a game being bad doesn't stop it from being good. Imagine it like this. Yakuza is like your favourite TV show (let's say Breaking Bad), and you know that the show is legendary overall. But it has some quirks to it. Each game is like a season and the chapters within it are like episodes. Does every episode have to be good for the season to be enjoyable overall? Do you have to like every character or story decision? The answer to both of these questions is a big "NO". Play this game and you will understand exactly what I mean. You will at times really hate this game and you really won't want to play it. But at other times, you will feel like this is the only game that exists. The story seems to be a big substory for the most part. As if our hero forgot who he is and decided to do something completely unrelated to what we're used to. Many times you will be presented with an interesting plot point which will immediately be followed by something incredibly mundane and uninteresting in comparison. But to be honest, it's a welcome break from the frustrations of the last two games. A big problem however is that immediately at the start of the game, a plot-line which is at the crux of Kiwami 2 will be shut down like it was all for nothing. This will instantly piss you off. Be ready!Not constantly being in Kamurocho for once is really nice. It's a great change of pace that gets you to remember that Japan is much bigger than just Tokyo itself. It shows that the concerns of ordinary people matter, and that being a Yakuza is more than just being a money hungry thug. Speaking of money hungry thugs, these are your villains: Tsuyoshi Kanda the meat-head coomer, Yoshitaka Mine the smug rich prick, Goh Hamazaki the torturer, Andre Richardson the dumb American, and Heihachi Mishima (he apparently calls himself "Tetsuo Tamashiro" for some reason) the child abuser. The good guys are all goofs. Majima the insane friend who doesn't care what anyone says as always, Mikio the fat ♥♥♥♥, Nakahara the Hungarian grandpa, and Rikiya the "Aniki!" spammer. The story is all over the place, the pace slows down and speeds up in a strange way. Ultimately, it seems that the majority of the events of this game don't really matter outside of its own context. For now, I don't see how what happened here will impact the following titles. I will say that despite this, everything felt important. So pay attention!Okay, the combat is probably the worst in all of Yakuza. If you play this game on hard difficulty (as you should all Yakuza games), the enemies will forever guard your attacks. You will be forced to find ways around this as you play the game, because fights are quite common as always.Enemies will appear out of nowhere and you will be forced to fight them when you really don't want to. Grab spamming is a viable strategy throughout the entire game against most enemy types, except for fatsos and boss fights. Using weapons and items is a must, due to a certain exploit existing. If you hit an enemy with an item, they get stunned and you can keep repeating the same attack until the item breaks, after which you can hit them with a combo. There is a certain string you can unlock which will break through the guards of enemies, but even that they will block a lot, meaning you will often land only the first hit and the last hit a lot of the time. Heat helps alleviate this issue.You will deal next to no damage to the enemies, while the enemies will do way too much damage to you. You will get knocked down frequently, and will have to wait a long time before you can get up again. Many of the enemies' attacks will home in on you, some of those will break your guard and knock you down. This can get very frustrating, very quickly. Especially because of how aggressive all of the enemies are. Do yourself a favour and finish Komaki's training in order to Tiger Drop and parry everybody. It'll make your life easier.On a side note, the side content in this game is decent, though flawed. The hitman missions are entertaining and surprisingly interesting. Although, they get quite frustrating at times. The revelations are quite fun and give you useful abilities, but Mack is annoying. The substories are funny as always, the acting story stands out. The cabaret clubs are under-developed and I don't recommend them unless you really like playing dress up. Fishing in this game is like watching a documentary about rocks whilst cooking a meal with lots of onion in it. It's a slow and painful process where for every step you take, you take 300 steps back. Why? Because the game has drawn arbitrary lines on what causes your line to snap and what causes the fish to ♥♥♥♥ off the hook. Either way, you're screwed. Catching a tuna in that one substory is not worth it. Just pay the man. -300,000 yen :(The upside of all of these issues is that the game has it's own unique charm. It's hilarious, both intentionally and unintentionally. The best voice lines are heard here. Tamashiro's "wooa ah aaaaaahhhhhhhhhh", guy with gun's "koya ora" and fat guy's "dure dure oyaeaaa". The substories are kinda funny and are better than a lot of Kiwami 2's substories. This is a great old game, where its faults compliment its strengths. You will get used to it pretty quickly and grow to love it for what it is. It's worth all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The music is awesome too! The main theme, Fly might as well be the theme of the whole series. Lyricism Without Tears might the most beautiful song of all the games. End Point is far more epic than expected. Ogre Has Returned is really cool. FM-Sound's Storm is catchy as hell. That's really the main strength of this game. Its aesthetics. The locations feel real and the vibe is chilled out. It fits the narrative perfectly. The game has aged really well, actually.I give this game "Aniki!" out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve just finished Yakuza 3 after playing through its remakes/prequels, and up to this point, this definitely seems to be weakest entry in the series so far. Sure, comparing Yakuza 3 to latter entries is a bit unfair, but that is the context that I have, so be it. Kiwami 1 and 2 is a Remake of Yakuza 1 and 2 plus Yakuza 0 came also after. If you're a newcomer to the yakuza franchise - don't start here - play Yakuza 0, Kiwami 1 and 2 first:Someone else once stated that Yakuza 3 is more like a "gaiden" (side-story) version of the Kiryu saga, and I have to agree. Everything is a bit slower-paced compared to the prequels; from a slower-pace Okinawa beach and smaller-city setting taking a large chunk of the gameplay. It's fine for what it is, but does feel a bit off compared to the other sagas.Presentation is appropriate for an early PS3-era game, so if you keep your expectations in it's fine, but it didn't quite teleport me back to kabuki-cho/dotonbori like its prequels but thats completely fine because its just a REMASTER of the Original and not a REMAKE with new Engine. If you expect Yakuza 0, Kiwami 1-2 type of quality then its obviously your fault.The fight gameplay is fairly average - it just doesn’t have the bone-crunching effect of the earlier entries mentioned, and the moves and the play seems a bit… plain and kind of "boring" since it doesn't have the variety-palette of yakuza 0. Mostly button-mashing with a few dodges thrown in here and there for the tougher fights, but nothing that will make you sweat for an extended period of time.The main story is absolutely decent and better than what I expected from the Reviews here. Your typical crime-drama storyline here with some melodramatic plot points (with you running an orphanage and all). I can’t say the storyline was exceptional like that of part 0, but there’s nothing wrong here. I absolutely enjoyed every second of it!The side-story missions are okay, but I feel the formula is starting to wear thin. I found myself just wanting to move on with the main story as I didn't find the side plots particularly compelling nor all the mini games interesting.All in all, Yakuza 3 is up to par or above average in most aspects. Some will complain about the lengthy cut-scenes, but I think this is a bit overblown. The game always gives you an opportunity to save before showing you a long cut-scene, plus the scenes themselves are skip-able, and you can also re-watch them from the menu. So there's a good deal of flexibility there. Even without the removed content, Yakuza 3 has upwards of 50 hours of content to enjoy. If you're only interested in finishing the story, this takes about 20 hours.Some Reviewers also mention to just skip this: DON'T! This Game is absolutely worth it and no one should skip this. People who say "SKIP!" are definitely trash at video games becuase there is nothing wrong here!★★★★★ Story★★★★☆ Visuals/Graphics★★★★☆ World Design (Universe, Lore and Artwork)★★★★☆ Level Design (Environment and Space)★★★★☆ Exploration Factor★★★☆☆ Combat, Equipment and Enemies (Mostly button mashing and some bosses just block everything. Bosses aren't the strongest part of the game)★★★☆☆ Side Quests (Some are cool like the movie set sidequest and some are straight boring)★★☆☆☆ Certain Movement Mechanics (The variety isn't really high - you can level up etc but get like 10-15 abilitys max and movement pattern of your attacks mostly stays like that throughout the game)★★★★☆ Certain Characters and Dialogue★★★☆☆ Quest Rewards*RECOMMENDED*

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most problematic and conflicted recommended I'll ever give. Maybe. Exaggeration for effect but I do believe it somewhat. The Combat... is not unplayable. As a matter of fact, I'm pretty sure if you were to play it on easy you can have a relatively fun time with it. This is the precedent to all the Yakuza games you play today so a lot of things here are very identifiable. The heat moves, the variations of weapon attacks, hell there's even ragdoll physics. I didn't play it on easy though.And neither should you have to which remains to be the biggest elephant in the room. See, Yakuza 3 Remastered combat has a big problem, it's AI. Most enemies you encounter, on hard difficulty, block all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time. What's worse is that you can't break it. There's no stamina system here so that ultimate blocking makes sense, no, it's free real estate. So, whenever you try to hit someone head on they can just block and other than one very specific double heavy attack combo it remains unbreakable. That does not make for a fun experience at all. And then I hear this deflection all the time how you should just play it on easy and ‘learn’ to have fun. Look, I’m sure as a fan of Yakuza 3 it doesn’t feel good to have so many people just straight up clowning on the game, I do understand the feeling and to an extent those people are correct but at the same time you cannot ignore the flaws blatantly in your face. This game’s AI is some of Alien ♥♥♥♥, I swear to god. The second boss fight and the first fight as Dad Kiryu, you’ll find yourself standing against an enemy that does not know how to walk. Or run. During this fight, this man will DASH towards you the entire time. He has ultimate dashes while you are left with just one. This is also another big problem with the combat. Exactly like blocking, most enemies somehow can dash continuously towards you and away from you. Sometimes they just dash back and forth. This isn’t well programmed AI is what I’m trying to say here. It’s very sloppy. Also, apparently, they messed up the dodge like whoever was in-charge of porting it, QLOC I guess. Which explains a lot because let me tell you the dodge is extremely inconsistent here. Often times even after you dodge the enemy, the attack somehow will still hit you. Even if you end up behind them chances are the enemy will end up hitting you through either a janky hitbox or straight up land the attack by turning around through some sick matrix ♥♥♥♥. ‘It’s not that bad, you just need to strategize. Use grabs.’ Okay, then what? I threw an enemy then they got up and I threw them again. This is another defense that I hear. In order for me to enjoy this game, I need to play this very specific way which happens to be throw spamming. Keep in mind there are enemies you can’t grab, many enemies who have infinite dashes so the chances to actually grab them are second to none and finally the grab which itself is a very straining move to do so it’s not feasible to do it around heaps of enemies as they’ll attack you during cooldown. After all of that, this what the combat will actually look like for an average player until chapter 5. Attack: Enemy BlocksGrab & ThrowGrab another and heat move onto the downed enemy.Repeat.Post chapter 5, you can get two moves that will somewhat ease the pain but won’t make the combat any better. It’s just by this point you’ll be so used to this game’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI that either you’d have stopped playing or you’ll probably be numb to it. Hopefully the former.  Calling it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ would be a bit harsh but at the same time calling it the best Yakuza has to offer would be a joke. It’s uneven. Exactly like the game it’s working with.So, there’re two points to this. The actual crux, the main meat of the story, there’s a traitor in the Tojo Clan. While the other side being a Dad as Kiryu juggles his responsibilities managing an orphanage. Orphanage stuff is actually pretty decent. It’s wacky, it’s got the same charm of Yakuza that so many fell in love with in the Kiwami games and it does that with a lot of heart. There are stereotypes like for some reason every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kid other than the orphans turns out to be really mean or a bully which is weird. It almost seems like a lazy attempt to create conflict rather than creatively coming up with something that seems natural. However, it’s not really that noticeable considering the kids are all charming and humane enough for you to care for them. The short stories involving them is probably the only the time when the game shines, at least for me.On the other hand, the main story remains to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I’m not trying to be harsh here just for the sake of it, it’s just not that good. Look, storytelling in Yakuza has never really been that good considering they more or less always tell the same story. There’s a traitor in the Tojo Clan, Internal Conflict, External Conflict etc. The strength in Yakuza stories has always been its characters. Colorful characters who make you believe in them, laugh with them, cry with them and just overall make you care for them. That isn’t something that I felt in Yakuza 3. Most characters get barely any development in this game so they end up being one dimensional which simply makes me not care for them. There’s also a distinct lack of good secondary villains in this game that leaves a lot to be desired.Substories are fine. Typical Yakuza stuff, if you had fun doing substories in any other Yakuza game then you’ll have fun here.Minigames are also more or less the same and fun to do except the cabaret, ♥♥♥♥ the cabaret.So, after all of that, would I still recommend this game? No, not really. Should you skip it? I wouldn’t advise you to. What I would tell you is this. Give it a chance. You’ll most likely be buying the Remastered collection and if you do maybe spend a few hours messing around and see if you like the vibe. Why the ♥♥♥♥ did I write a 1000+ word long review if at the end I knew I’ll only be giving you a 50/50 answer? Idk depression and a lot of free time prolly.

_childDocuments_.review: I began with Yakuza 0 and ran a marathon, all the way here with Yakuza 3 Remaster. For all 4 Yakuza games I've played so far, Yakuza 3 is the one mostly unlike a Yakuza game, rather, a single parent sim that teaches how to educate 8 young kids. Honestly Yakuza 3 is very confusing, half of the gameplay - around 6 hours I've been dealing with endless minor missions with kids, including chasing runaways downtown, looking into stolen pocket money, dealing with school bullying, taking care of the trauma and sick kid etc... all those a parent may face when raising up a kid but in Yakuza 3 you have 8 to take care of. It's not about whether those missions are good or bad, it is about as a YAKUZA game yet I am stuck with 8 kids' everyday life not knowing when the "real" game begins. It's okay if RGG studio introduces a new orphanage founded by Kiryu but it's too much, I bought Yakuza games excepting Yakuza stories.And for the real part of the Yakuza story - it sucks. The script feels like it was written by a bunch of amateur who are not even working together, without a main line nor a main villain with personality but little broken stories here and there. It involves politics but barely scratches anything. Fighting the Chinese Gang is a joke, the Korean Jingweon Mafia in Kiwami 2 is worth fighting as it is a threat, but making Kiryu do an entry-level job sucks. Majima quit in the middle of the game, and what is that again everyone lets the guard down not checking on weapons near a defeated bad guy? Then the backfire / taking a bullet for someone else is to be expected, and I can't feel anything when Kiryu sheds tears because it is not emotional at all, not even close to what happens to Tachibana in Yakuza 0. The ending is plain like the entire game, unreal as too many convenient coincidences happen. The entire game is awkwardly unreal - with Kaoru Sayama bidding goodbye to Kiryu just one day before leaving the country, but only death would part them in Kiwami 2. Kazama Family chairman Kashiwagi looks like a sitting duck at the french sash on an unusual power outbreak, not moving before a chopper. Joji Kazama is clearly a hint for RGG Studio ran out of ideas, and on top of everything, what is that Kiryu doing facing Goh Hamazaki at the end? I can only assume he stays with k-8 kids too long that he forgot how to act and think like a yakuza.Yakuza 3 Remaster tells an awkward and broken story. Removing the first half of the story at Morning Glory (Why the name???) Orphanage into a DLC might help a little bit. I'm disappointed that I wish I hadn't played this game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from Kiwami 2, there are a lot of downgrades in graphics and quality of life that you will have to swallow. While it certainly improves thing over the original localisation, this is not a remake. You will get used to the downgrade. On the other hand, I felt very indifferent about the main story in Kiwami 2, but this one was awesome. People might find the start of it slow, but I considered it all good character building and necessary to show in order to have the emotional resonance with what Kiryu cares about. After you leave Okinawa the story really picks up fast anyway, as this game has only 12 chapters instead of the usual 16. Though I really like Okinawa, a very needed change of scenery. The combat is much more challenging then the Kiwamis and 0, because enemies really like to block (though they block less on harder difficulties). So I hope you learned how to quickstep behind enemies by now. While more cheap at times with the stun locking, I did enjoy the challenge in the combat more. Though heat actions do not have the same weight to them and combat feels more arcade-like-clunky then how fluid they did in Kiwami 2. But it still felt alright and I still had fun punching things.    I would consider the side stories in this game to be on the weaker side overall, though I did like the change that you can now fail them so that made them stand out enough for me. Minigame wise, what's new (if you come from Kiwami 2) is an arcade shmup, outside golf, fishing (more fun then Yakuza 0) and the massage parlor. This used to also be the game that introduced karaoke, but if you played the Kiwamis and 0, you take that for granted (goes to show it's important to place a game in perspective). There's also a sidegame where you train a single hostess, but figuring it out it incredibly frustrating. The other minigames that were in the Kiwamis are of course, not as polished. So I don't know why you would want to play those. Then there's some other side content, like Hitman missions, revelations and IF7, those were alright, not really worth getting into here.

_childDocuments_.review: While Yakuza 3 isn't a bad instalment in the series, of the first four games in the series (the fourth being Yakuza 0), Yakuza 3 is the lesser of the batch played so far. Although the gameplay is mostly as solid and enjoyable as the previous instalments, despite the combat feeling more rigid in areas, it's the plot and overall story that holds back Yakuza 3. Although the tone of the series has often been inconsistent by splicing in sickly sweet humour into its very serious and  hard boiled crime story, the juxtaposition of the story telling style is more apparent and distracting in Yakuza 3. Despite the first half of the game making for an interesting setup concerning a proposed legislation with potential for American investment, the overall reveal of the promising plot is severely hampered by the mastermind's motivation and, frankly, loud out loud hilarious antics and voice acting of a certain English speaking character. Where the previous Yakuza games masterfully mapped out the power struggles within the Tojo Clan, along with the ramifications for what construes an "honourable" Yakuza member, the story to Yakuza 3 doesn't explore these themes in anywhere near as much detail and is sidetracked by its superficial political story.  There are also substantial sections of the game which feature unavoidable side-stories that do little to add to the story, mainly the side-quests that are focused on the orphanage and making it feel like a parent simulator. These sections are fairly long and substantially shift from the story in such a way that the main plot points can feel abandoned. Out of any game in the Yakuza series, the story feels shortchanged. Therefore, story is Yakuza 3's greatest weakness - a shame as this has always been one of the major strengths of the series (Yakuza 0, in particular). The skill system, additionally, also feels unfulfilled compared to previous titles in the series where upgrades are limited to basic fight moves, health or heat (a super charge mode to unleash extreme combat moves). But, this isn't to say Yakuza 3 is a bad game. It's still fun and whenever the story offers mystery, it is engrossing. But, none of it is done to the standard of the previous games, while being very respectful to the spirit and overall style of what to expect from a Yakuza game. At best, Yakuza 3 is a solid  entry into the series while, at worst, it's mediocre. By gaming standards, Yakuza 3 is a great game while, by Yakuza standards, it is something of a disappointment. 3 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: B E A U T I F U L E Y E SLike most people playing this game, I came from 0 through Kiwami 2, so the step back in time to the oldest non-remade game in the series is jarring to say the least.Most people fall into the trap of playing this on hard, because they feel like they're veterans of the series at this point and the previous games are a bit more generous in ways. Hard is beyond frustrating in this game, and it's designed to be beaten only with grinding new moves and doing a lot of cheese, especially in boss fights. Some people enjoy that aspect of it, others (myself included) find it tedious and miserable. You'll be doing a whole lot of light light light heavy heavy, or just spamming tiger drop. Don't get me started on the chase sequences... which are *truly* miserable on hard difficulty.The story is paced a little weird and feels kind of rushed at some times, yet the downtime exploring Kiryu's life at the orphanage drags on. It almost feels like the devs realized how fast the player would breeze through the main story and had to pad out the length with a ton of orphanage side content. It's cute at first but drags on by the end.This is still an enjoyable Yakuza game. My recommendation is to not play it on hard, perhaps try hard or legendary for NG+ if you really want to. Also, do not play it immediately after finishing Kiwami 2. Give the series some room and come back to it later, so your expectations aren't as high. The game has an enjoyable story, really great characters, a decent soundtrack, and Okinawa is a fun setting, as small as it is. I've been to Naha before and they absolutely nail the location.The ending to this game is incredibly silly and should probably be experienced by everyone at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: i think y3 needed to be kiwamified even more than the first 2 games. the blocks would've been fine if kiryu actually managed to deal any damage to anyone. it is kinda funny to see how the man who used to take down guys with chainsaws and rocket launchers now struggles to pacify petty goons in ugly sweaters. wasn't the most pleasant experience but, well, signature yakuza experience nonetheless. bonus points for the yandere antagonist

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than I feared it might be. I slept on the yakuza series for a long time, only getting into it relatively recently. After 0 and the kiwami games I was thinking of giving 3 a miss because of its relative age and the game play videos giving me flashbacks to the horrors of controlling early 3d games. Yakuza 3 thankfully came out a good deal after the worst of those issues had been sorted out. The control is fluid the camera is never a problem, in some ways it feels better than the kiwamis because Y3 does not care about smooth realistic animation. The graphics are of course a huge downgrade and there is quite a bit of jank in some of the minigames but there are good guides available so if you are going for all the achievements it can be done, I really did not find achievement hunting in this any worse than the kiwamis. If you are just playing through the story that is basically flawless, some small quality of life problems that later games fixed but overall still surprisingly good.So if you, like me were on the fence about giving the remasters a shot I would say wait for the inevitable sale and buy the remaster bundle, imo it is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Yakuza games are all excellent, however this one in particular resonated with me the most despite the numerous flaws it might have. Yakuza 3 was the third mainline title and second PS3 title, this is important to note if you're coming from 0 and the Kiwamis, this will feel like a noticeable bump in the road if you've gotten accustomed to the modern Yakuza titles and remakes, as a result I implore you to check out the original PS2 titles before immediately jumping into this one to set your expectations.If you're only interested in Yakuza's gameplay and never grew attached to the story nor characters, I would probably skip this one - where Yakuza 3 excels is in it's story, atmosphere and characters. Without getting into too much detail, the game definitely takes a bit to get going, and it will pull you into mandatory slice of life character interactions that won't be to everyone's taste, if you're able to set aside a few hours and really get yourself invested I think it really pays off.As for the gameplay, I'm going to give a few recommendations now: when you get EXP, focus on upgrading your tech and body at first up until you meet Komaki (who at a specific point in the story will send a letter pointing to where he is) and relearn his moves. Coming from Kiwami 2's lack of a parry and especially K1's overpowered Tiger Drop, you might be conditioned to using the Tiger Drop as your counter of choice, however the Komaki Parry is far more effective as you'll have a wider window to hit it, it'll counter more attacks and allows you to accumulate more damage while they're stunned. The Daruma Tumbler also alleviates many of the problems with your quickstep introduced in the buggy "Remastered" port, at this point I'd focus on bringing heat and soul up.So, with that in mind, I highly recommend this game if you don't mind some light grinding to sand down some of the rough edges, and you value the story, atmosphere and characters above all else. If you don't have the time nor particularly care to get super invested in the more slice of life aspect to the story and additionally want faster paced fights, I'd skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all before buying this game you need to know that the fighting is not the best when it comes to boss fights all they do is block and you get two or three punches in which was annoying but the story was good and the world was good their are a few funny jokes i enjoyed so overall ill give this game a 7.5/10 just because of the fact that the fighting was trash.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza 3 Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: A great entry into the Yakuza series, continuing Kiryu's storyline and introducing new characters. The story was a lot of fun and very interesting, especially exploring the new locales.This remaster is very pretty given the age of the original game and holds up well with the current series, the framerate and gameplay runs smoothly.The only downside i experienced was the combat, the AI is programmed to block infinitely. This paired with the fact that they have no break limit results in all fights (Including no name npcs) taking a very long time where you do little to no damage and they block non stop. The only way to get around this is to learn a couple of special moves and spam them, which is very boring, or alternatively spam guns.If the combat was updated or the ai programmed to not infinitely block, i think it would have helped the game out alot.To date i've played: 0, Kiwami 1 and Kiwami 2. Yakuza 3 is the worst out of the lot solely because of the combat and i couldn't wait to rush to the finish line.I'd recommend to pick it up to continue Kiryu's story, but be prepared for the awful combat.

But trouble shadows Kiryu and the Morning Glory Orphanage is soon entangled in a deadly power struggle.

name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy
detailed_description: Reviews & Accolades “Embraces the true spirit of the Guardians” Game Informer – 8.5/10 “A serious contender for game of the year” CBR “Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy excels in its storytelling” GamesRadar+ – 4/5 “Never stopped being fun” IGN – 8/10 “Absolutely worth playing” Windows Central – 4.5/5 “Guardians of the Galaxy is a jam-packed package for single player and story fans” Gamestar_de – 85/100 “Has more heart than a cardiologist” USA Today’s For The Win “A thrilling adventure” JV Jeuxvideo_com - 16/20 “Its soundtrack easily figures among the best of the generation” Voxel “A True Super Hero Experience” Feber - 9/10 About the Game Fire up a wild ride across the cosmos with a fresh take on Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy. In this third-person action-adventure game, you are Star-Lord, and thanks to your bold yet questionable leadership, you have persuaded an oddball crew of unlikely heroes to join you. Some jerk (surely not you) has set off a chain of catastrophic events, and only you can hold the unpredictable Guardians together long enough to fight off total interplanetary meltdown. Use Element Blasters, tag-team beat downs, jet boot-powered dropkicks, nothing’s off-limits. If you think it’s all going to plan, you’re in for a world of surprises, with the consequences of your actions guaranteed to keep the Guardians on their toes. In this original Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy story, you’ll cross paths with powerful new beings and unique takes on iconic characters, all caught in a struggle for the galaxy’s fate. It’s time to show the universe what you’re made of. You got this. Probably. LEAD THE GUARDIANS OF THE GALAXY You play as Star-Lord, so nothing’s off-limits with your bold combat style, from Element Blasters and jet boot-powered dropkicks to tag-team beat-downs. With the Guardians fighting at your side, call the shots and overwhelm your opponents with signature attacks. Meanwhile, the consequences of your decisions will range from light-hearted to downright unexpected as your journey unfolds. ALL-NEW STORY Your newly-formed band of legendary misfits is set to save the universe in this fresh but faithful take on the Guardians of the Galaxy. Somehow, you set off a chain of catastrophic events, leading to a wild ride through mind-blowing worlds inhabited by iconic and original Marvel characters. Turn up the all-star ‘80s mixtape and get ready to kick it. FROM MISFITS TO SUPER HEROES You’re the only thing holding the unpredictable Guardians together, so you’ll have to get better at this leadership thing fast. With this offbeat approximation of a family at your side, there will be tears and laughter as you set about tearing into the cosmos together. Whatever’s waiting around the next corner, you know it’s going to be a blast. DIGITAL DOWNLOAD BONUS Buying the digital version of the game will unlock the Social-Lord Outfit for Star-Lord.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the guardians in the movies, comics, and shows you will love this game. It is its own story and has nothing to do with them. Its the classic F*** up guardians doing what they do best. The banter between the team alone, is worth playing through. It is ~ 15 - 20 hours long and also has New game + (A feature no single player game should ship without). You only directly play as Star Lord, but you directly control the other Guardians as well. Highly recommend you play with a controller as well, keyboard will have you playing Twister with your fingers.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Usually don't write but I like this game. And I was bored ;p (No Spoilers) Story/Characters: Good dialog, good character development, and you can relate to who you are playing with.Pro- Major props to the voice acting, it's actually funny at times and makes the game way smoother. Story made sense and was easy to follow along. The connection to the teams stories made the experience way more interesting. Ending actually has some emotion and climax worth all the playing, so keep going and prepare tissues. Con- Only issue I had was the pacing of the game. Some chapters seem filler-ish and unnecessary long in the middle, but they all do add to the story and the characters.  8/10Game-play: Little wonky at first but you can get the hang of it eventually, and thats when combat gets really fun.Pro- It was wise to have all 4 characters have their own skill tree, then as you progress unlocking them along with the story. Felt like I earned the moves instead of them being given to me, and when I use them has more meaning then just pressing a ability. It was different and it had a lot of options and ways to play.Con(ish)- Towards the end its a lot to choose from in terms of combat, you have to toggle between a lot of skills, choose/remember the right weaknesses, and make sure no one dies in the process. Which I liked, but it can cause a headache at some point with a lot happening on screen so take breaks. 8.5/10Environment: It looks pretty, big, but glitchy.Pro- The interactions with the different beast and characters in tons of diverse worlds is a nice touch, keeps the game fresh but also like you are apart of a movie. Being able to use teammates perks and using your own for different types puzzles on the map made it really fun. Con(ish)- Very few times things just didn't work, so I had to reset the chapter. That wasn't so much a problem, its a big game. It was the constant being stuck or a part of the map wasn't working the way it should. Good thing they have a anti-glitch reset mechanic in game, where it takes you back to the closest main area. 7.5/10Overall made me feel something in a game I haven't in a while. Highly Recommend. Overall 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I have more hours into the game and just started NG+ I wanted to do a more in depth review but my score still remains high because the game is just awesome!The good:-Amazing characters with excellent development, you start off as a fresly built team and nobody likes each other too much but by the end of the game you will have a dream team!-Voice acting is just top tier on every character all throughout the game!-Character animations especially the facial animations are great-Captivating story arc that will suck you in so fast and you just can't stop playing it cause you wanna see what's next!-Drax-By far the best and most interesting rendition of Mantis right here-Every costume is unlockable by playing the game there's nothing behind paywall.-The style of the game is more akin to the MCU Guardians of the Galaxy but the whole story and characters are straight up of comic books which is awesome.-The perfect soundtrack! Both the licensed and the original soundtrack is just out of this world!-Graphics aren't usually the thing I'm looking for in a game but still really stands out from all the games that released on PC this year.-No Crisp Rat Star LordThe Bad:-The gameplay is average at best, it's not bad but it's nothing stand out either with no depth what so ever. You only play as Star Lord who has like 3 skills but you won't use them most of the time and the other team members are just extra skills for you. At some point you run out of perks to buy but you still get currency to buy stuff you just can't spend it on anything at all.-There's 4 weapon elements you unlock through the game but the last 2 unlocks too late and you barely use it in the game for exploration or puzzles.-Bugs, lots and lots of bugs and some of them are game breaking to a certain degree. A lot has been patched out and by the time you might get this game there won't be many in the game.-Performance isn't too great and the game had many issues for a lot of people and it also has DENUVO which is a huge problem for many, for a weekend some Denuvo servers went down and you couldn't even play the game...That's about it there might be more positives for sure and the negatives aren't that much of a dealbreaker for me and I still highly recommend the game, it's one of the GOTY contenders for me and I'm a huge Capcom/Resident Evil shill but Village can't even touch this game for me. I was smiling all throughout the game it was that good of an experience!Storm Lord/10

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game was the most fun I've had playing video game for a long while.  (That might be my fault for trying to play BF2042!).  I found myself laughing out loud a the humour and the quips from Rocket and the teams interactions with each other and the choices you had to make.  The game play is super smooth, involving, you genuinely feel like you are managing the team and need to make the right choices to nail the battles, which can sometimes very challenging whilst you work out the best approach.  Spliced in between all this is fantastic voice acting, stunning graphics and a sound track that will have you grinning from ear to ear! Being in the midst of mass brawl whilst Relax - Frankie Goes to Hollywood is playing... wonderful!  The game isn't a rehash of the movie, Star Lord isn't the Peter Quill presented by Chris Pratt.  I actually related more to this Star Lord, his upbringing, the era, etc.  The rest of the team are familiar, but varied enough to feel new with a bit more depth to them compared to the big screen adaptation.  The narrative is excellent and it builds nicely through the game.  The game is 'on rails', but if you are coming here to play this type of game its about the story and not levelling up your wood cutting skills in the middle of nowhere on a giant map in Skyrim!Pros:Fun! It will make you laughExcellent graphicsExcellent voice actingEngaging and new narrativeUnreal music!Cons:Very minor gripe is some of the later levels lost some variationMinor bugs - I got stuck in the scenery twice and I had to restart two missions as they didn't complete after killing the last bad dude, which added maybe an extra 1hrs game playMy scores (out of 10)Gameplay - 9Story - 10Graphics - 9Sound - 10Overall - 9

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine someone would write a solid book about the Guardians, with beautiful, believable, immersive dialogues and all the little bickering involved to make it seem plausible. Now imagine someone made an actual game out of that. With 2022 graphics, a perfect surround sound (all speaker angles can be set separately! glorious) and a heckload of fun involved. Damn, then think about the current state of the industry.NFT madness, releasing broken-alpha stage games, "live-service" BS that will only lead to money grabbing, low-effort cash-grabs through ridiculously priced cosmetics, blaming the community for rejecting broken garbage... AND IN THAT MOMENT! Comes this game. A game well made. Well crafted. No major bugs. Simply... a beautiful one. Showing everyone what all gamers with a brain already knew for decades... the best games are good single-player games. But then... the industry doesn't like that. They tried to convince us that live-action, multi-player games are the true pinnacle... and they lied. The reason? It's simple. Good single player games take a hell lot of effort. It's hard. It's difficult. It's no low-effort cashgrab. It's not a league of legends or fortnite, where a couple devs can pump 2 skins out a quarter and call it progress (whilst still the billions come flowing). Or a Fifa where EA recycled the same engine and the same game without meaningful new features for more than a decade, and still the billions come flowing. So they fear this. They do not want to invest money and risk low sales because the end result sucks.Of course the problem starts lower, it's not the devs fault that people are mindless and buy cr*p, they just want to earn money with the least amount of effort involved. It's the easy choice. The fast way. Making money off people that do not have any standards or dignity. That like to buy the same thing, over and over again, even though nothing ever changes.Then comes this game... Let it be known, good single-player games are the greatest, IF done right. And this one does it. This one proves, again and again, that franchises like the Witcher, Mass Effect, Hitman, Divinity: Original Sin 2... command authority amongst the gaming community without one braincell wasted on microtransactions, live-action, DLCs or anything like that.Buy this game. Support the devs. This is the way.

_childDocuments_.review: A ballad to sing in battle.Square Enix messed up with Avengers, and I'm so sad Guardians of the Galaxy has to suffer because of it. This game has all the heart and soul its predecessor lacked, and then some. I'm not well versed, or versed at all, in comic book lore, so I can't say whether or not Eidos Montreal weave a particularly original story with this cast of characters, but I can say that it's exceptionally well told, with plenty of emotional weight. This game suffers from some of the worst marketing I've ever seen. Its reveal trailer gave off the impression that this is another grindfest with a superhero skin, while that couldn't be further from the truth. Guardians' focus, from beginning to end, is its story and cast. That may rub you the wrong way, depending on your taste. The combat never grows beyond average, and if you're looking for a particularly deep or challenging gameplay sandbox, you won't find it here. If, on the other hand, you want a sci-fi blockbuster that manages to be equal parts witty and sweet, you won't find many better than this one.I can't give this game enough praise, or a higher recommendation. It's one of the best releases the western video game industry has produced in recent memory, and stands as my absolute favorite superhero game I've ever played.Beyond fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Amazing Music, Solid Story, Lot of minor annoying bugs.Very close to being as good as mass effect for comic fans. Pros:-1.) Vibe - Absolutely nailed the Guardian's of the Galaxy team vibe(which means a bunch of clueless idiots with moderately decent morals coming together and somehow saving the day).2.) Dialogue and Characters - Perfect lines and delivery for all the guardian's crew. Each has their own distinct way of speaking, bs-ing and outlook. 3.) Music - Check out the playlist for this game on spotify. Bunch of classics. Absolute 10/10 good time.4.) Plot - Decent enough. An adventure where everyone faces and overcomes their own personal battles before unifying to take down the bigger evil. Classic plot, very well executed.5.) Combat mechanics - Surprisingly deep. Was not expecting that after the fiasco with the other Avenger's game. But they pulled out a lot of interesting team based combat mechanics. Super fun.6.) Characters- This is not a first meet/coming together story, but even with the team already together at the start of the story, they focused a lot on each individual guardian's story.7.) Visuals are pretty good too.8.) Strong linear storytelling. Doesn't overstay its welcome. Good length. Around 16-17 hours.Cons:-1.) Save system - Absolute trashcan manual save system. The manual saves get overwritten by the auto save if that is the last used save slot. If you die after a lot of exploration, it will spawnyou at the beginning of the checkpoint, so you have to go through all the cinematics and enemies, but all the loot will already be in your inventory. Extremely irritating but a minor inconvenience.2.) Interface - Sometimes you will interact with an object and the interaction buttons will not disappear even after you have stopped interacting with the item. Sometimes, button presses don't registerunless you are at a specific angle which highlights the interact button. 3.) Lot of minor bugs - They needed to polish the way button inputs work. My controller never worked with this game for some inexplicable reason(controller works fine with all other games). There is a lot of delay between button press and it registering in the game. This is the one thing they needed to polish in the game. Rating - 8.5/10 Very very very fun experience with amazing music, story and fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: 8 out of 10. The game has problems and flaws, but it evokes a lot of emotions. This game is not about shooting, this is not grinding, this game is about the power of friendship and teamwork. At the beginning, the team is not very friendly and fights all the time, but little by little it becomes more friendly and united, not without your help. Of course, this is all accompanied by a bunch of jokes and a huge number of dialogues. Your teammates never shut up, constantly joke, tease each other. If you've watched the movie and liked the characters, then forget it. These characters are worked out much deeper. Drax, for example, turns out to be not a stupid goon, but a brainy warrior who simply does not know the metaphors, but tries to fix it) Gamora collects dolls, Rocket is afraid of water, and Groot is Groot. Finally, I would like to note that the game has cool graphics, the level design, the variety of levels is also amazing. And of course the soundtrack here is awesome. What could be better than fighting the boss to the music, Don't worry Be happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: The group's dynamic took me by surprise to be sure. Chatter between members of the team are truly hilarious!The graphics are really nice, the art style is great specially on latter missions and the original soundtrack goes along the setting splendidly.The only things I would change/ fix are the crazy amount of stuttering due to shader compilation I would guess, and the kinda lackluster animations when engaging in one to one dialogs with the crew. I mean, it ain't no Horizon Forbidden West in that regard, that's for sure, but it still gets the job done.Guardians of the Galaxy is actually impressive considering it came out of nowhere practically unannounced and with poor marketing, and obviously considering Square Enix disastrous handling of the Avengers game. All in all, I would easily give this game an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is exactly what Marvel's Avengers should have been last year. More inline with the wonderful Spider-Man games from Insomniac. GotG is a tight story-driven single player experience with excellent dialog, awesome graphics, and fun gameplay but focuses more on the adventure then action which some people might not like but I absolutely love it. Gives me slight Mass Effect 1 vibes but way funnier. I can whole heartily recommend Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, do not let this game slip passed you if you are a fan of the MCU or comic book games. I am Groot!

_childDocuments_.review: Biggest surprise of the year. I am a massive Marvel fanboy, but this game was not really on my radar, because of how terrible The Avengers game was. However I did get it for free with a gaming laptop, so I jumped in day one, because I saw a lot of positive reviews and I gotta say, if it wasn't for It Takes Two, this would have been my GOTY. What an amazing game world. It took me 25 hours to finish the game just because of how often I would aimlessly wander around to just sit back and soak up the scenery. Normal playtime is not longer than 15-20 hours, which in my opinion is the sweet spot for story heavy singleplayer games.The only thing that holds it back is the slightly basic combat especially the clunky keyboard controls when controlling other Guardians during combat and the absolutely pointless lock-on auto-aim. Just give me more damage and let me directly affect my accuracy with my skill. Tiny change, which would make this into a much more fun experience. Maybe add it as an option later? The difficulty settings are pretty granular, so why turning off lock-on is not there? But honestly it's not a complete deal-breaker, the combat is still fun enough and it's not the main focus of this game. The story is. And boy what a blast that story is.This is my favorite incarnation of these characters, I love their chemistry. I love how much of their own thing they are compared to the MCU knock-off Avengers from last year. Groot is more expressive and can grunt and laugh, Quill is smarter and more relatable than Chris Pratt's rendition, Drax is given way more space and backstory than Bautista's version and Rocket is crazier and more entertaining than the one Gunn has penned. I also love the many great secondary characters, especially the much more interesting Mantis and the best boy Cosmo.I'm a big fan of the presentation in this game. Everything is gorgeous. This is one of the most colorful games I've ever played. The art team went absolutely bonkers on the environments and they deserve all the praise. And it's all complemented with a very solid technical side as well. I've personally had very few bugs and only had to reload past save twice, because I jumped somewhere where I got stuck and once because I couldn't find the last enemy, which was preventing me to progress to the next part.If this is what the future of the Marvel Universe in gaming is, I'm very hyped for the future. Just please, no more multiplayer grindfests, we want more great stories like this one. When this game drops under 30€, it will be an absolute must-have for any real Marvel fan.boring technical stuff:I've tried it on a desktop rtx3080 in 5120x1440 and a mobile rtx3070 in 1920x1080 and both experiences were absolutely flawless (apart from a minor HEX edit to remove cutscene black bars in 32:9, which is normal for most cinematic games). I didn't even really need DLSS to stay above 60FPS. I did end up using the DLSS quality preset to have a flawless 80-100 FPS experience. I just lowered raytracing reflections from ultra to high, which is barely noticeable when you don't directly look for it, but it adds loads of extra performance. Other than that, every other setting was the highest possible and I've noticed no noticeable frame drops in the entire game. And I know, these are very high-end cards, but this game looks better than Cyberpunk and runs literally three times as fast on ultra settings, so don't worry if you have a 1070 or something. You'll be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: The short: Amazing game. Great visuals, soundtrack, and interesting story (which has consequences throughout the story and not just the end).If you are at a point where a decent story is needed to hold your interest in games, look no further. This is a space adventure and with adventure comes story. There is a clear goal that surfaces, but you must travel to several locations and make decisions that could aid or hamper your progress.The combat is engaging enough when you start unlocking the talents for you and your crew. Your mileage may very. I couldn't remember the button layout till towards the end. However when it does start to click, there are plenty of those "I am unstoppable!" moments :)Basic RPG elements. Collect basic and advance resources then pick from a list of 15 enhancements. Things such as charged shot, faster shield regen, slow time down when doing a perfect dodge.Difficulty has MANY options. You can pretty much tweak anything you want. My 1st play through I set it to normal but turned the slow down when selecting an attack to .9. This way you get to know the button layout w/o completely killing the tension. A setting of 1 pauses action completely. My 2nd play through on new game plus was Hard with default settings. This was fairly easy.The look of the characters can be a bit off putting at first if you are a fan of the movies. They quickly grow on you and I personally love their design. Also worth noting, you can unlock their outfits from the movies. It pays to explore nooks and crannies.There are a lot of cut scenes. Many of them are interactive requiring you to make a decision on what to do or say. Some interesting enough to warrant a 2nd play through. It feels like watching a long Guardians movie. I found myself laughing at many of the conversations that go on between everyone in and out of cut scenes.I only ran into one type of bug that did not happen often. Three times in total. A teammate might get held up on something and not be able to advance. Normally this is fine as the game will teleport them to you. On the rare occasion you might get to a section that requires that person to keep going and you haven't walked far enough for them to be teleported. Reloading last check point fixes this and require no rehashing of what you have already done.In a world of bug loaded launches, lazy remakes, and cookie cutter sequels, this game grabbed my attention for 2 full plays back to back. I can not remember the last game that did that for me.I hope you find escapism and joy like I did in this wonderful title.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't care less about the marvel or guardians of the galaxy brand names. this game is the space adventure I've always wanted and it manages to actually immerse you in the role of the leader of a group of superpowered aliens. the real amazement is with the amount of dynamic conversation these 5 characters have. remmember how bad escort missions used to be? with the robotic AI destroying all hope of immersion and staring at you with dead eyes as they repeat dialouges? and then came Bioshock infinite with Elizabeth who interacted with her environment and proved helpfull without blocking your progress or being in the way. to the point that player said me and -Elizabeth- fought these guys?now there are four of them, all with their own style, powers, dialouges, ideals and character arcs.the gameplay and the narrative are combined marvelously with each other and with immersing you as the leader of this group. with several smart breaking of the mechanics for narrative or character purposes.the combat, IE the core gameplay might be a little too innovative but I loved it. I can deffinetly understand not liking it though. it's chaoric and quick paced. but it is balanced and varied and demands skill and attention to get right. and chaotic, dynamic gameplay is so much better at immersing this space adventure than the endless cover based shooters everywhere.this game is genuinelya must play game for me. for immersing me in a space adventure of my dreams.

_childDocuments_.review: People might be keeping an eye on this game because the recent release on theaters of the third movie featuring these characters. Gameplay is repetitively funny, engaging from the start, even tho some chapters of the game lack it, This game is hugely story oriented, with decision making, paths, alternate story arcs, and deep character development both individual and as a team. This characters are now associated(and apparently required) with some One-Hit Wonders of a decade, and this time is no exception. With an 80s and 90s soundtrack of around 2 and a half hours, these songs not only play during some cinematic sequences or cutscenes, it is also implemented in the combat as a "super friendly team boost" that the player can trigger during a combat section to, not only boost the party of guardians, giving buffs and deleting cooldowns of their abilities, but you do it with style at the sound of a One-hit wonder! _childDocuments_.review: It's nothing like that one AVENGERS game (as I originally thought) but more like a JEDI: FALLEN ORDER / SURVIVOR style game set in the MARVEL universe with typical Square Enix style combat.I honestly forgot this game even existed until I saw it in my friend's library when I keyword searched for "MARVEL" and it is absolutely one of the coolest things I've ever played. I vaguely remember this game being announced a while ago but I never saw any gameplay or anyone talk about this game AT ALL and I don't get why not. The needle-drops give me chills. The facial animations are some of the most lifelike and endearingly expressive I've ever seen. The textures are so tangibly realistic I feel like I can mentally reach through the screen and touch the surfaces of these environments; from the cold slick spaceship interiors to the wet and rubbery vines that drape across the first planet you visit. Everything is done so unbelievably well.I am writing this review very early into the game, but I already I feel an attachment to the rest of the team members and I genuinely like every one of them. Even though they *do* talk constantly talk over each other, I still enjoy listening to whatever they're yapping about. Plus, the Telltale style branching narrative story "Groot will remember that" mechanics keep you engaged in the conversations because you have to make dialogue choices that bend the narrative in unique ways. It also helps that the writing is consistently laugh-out-loud hilarious.I can't wait to beat this and then immediately play through it again.

Which is great, it feels different, but good.Now the combat is not the greatest ever, but it's good enough to have kept me going, without too much frustration and no boredom.Technically the game is sound, i have not encountered any major bugs, some small clipping issues here and there, but nothing egregious.The soundtrack is just awesome. _childDocuments_.review: In the era of gaming where big companies mostly sell shallow open-world games, focusing on quantity over quality, this game just doesn't belong to it. It's an old-school adventure game. It's just going through the story and having fun, with minimum exploring and looting. Maybe not everyone likes games like this, but I really enjoy games that get straight to the point.You play as a Star Lord, captain of the Guardians of the Galaxy. And who are they? They are a bunch of ex-criminals, who somehow got together and now are acting as paid guns, doing all sorts of different favors, etc. Other than Star Lord, who was born on Earth, we also have Drax the Destroyer, who killed mad titan Thanos in this timeline (not a spoiler, you find out about it soon); then we have Gamora, the daughter of Thanos, Groot who keeps saying "I am Groot", and Rocket, who is a raccoon, completely chaotic, yet loving. At the very beginning, the game will let you know that you can expect tons and tons of explosions, sliding, and awesome music, which Star Lord plays on his walkman. Later a bit, the story gets kinda confusing, and while it wasn't anything special, it was a decent superhero story, however, characters are amazing, and I really got attached to them. Dialogues are awesome, Guardians are talking all the time and not just rubbish, but so much different stuff. Every so often you will get the option to choose some dialogue options, and even make some choices, but most of the time it won't matter much. Yes there are some choices where helping some allies will make them help you later, and some chapters will play differently, but that's pretty much it about choices. There is just one ending.Gameplay is amazing and really fun. At the very beginning, first 20-30 minutes I thought that the gameplay was kinda bad, you don't have any powers, you just have guns, and jumping feels off as you can double jump up, but you can't double jump forward. However, you can jump and dodge, so that's kinda similar. You play as Star Lord the whole game, you can't switch between characters, but you control their powers all the time. Each of the Guardians has 3 powers that can be upgraded with ability points, and also one more that they get while playing through the story. Star Lord can use his guns, Rocket has tons of guns, a rocket launcher, and so on, Groot can attack with his branches, Gamora will slash opponents with her sword, and Drax is just really strong and can throw around stuff. Combos are insane, and it's extremely fun to play this, once you get used to it. The game is not really hard, I played on the hard difficulty, and it wasn't a challenge at all, but it wasn't super easy either. Just enough challenge to enjoy the story. Aside from combat, there is a lot of sliding down, which is really fun at first, later gets a bit old, but it always looks cool. You can collect some components, which let you install some upgrades, and there are 15 of them. As for other stuff, music is amazing like I said, rock and metal music. Performance is okay I guess, some drops here and there which I didn't mind, mostly while loading areas, but the game mostly runs well and looks beautiful. Took me 24h to beat it, while leaving it idle occasionally, but I would say it's around 22-23 h to beat. - Amazing gameplay- Amazing characters- Amazing dialogues- Looks great- Amazing music- Story is decent, but nothing special- Performance are okay but could be better As someone who rarely enjoys superhero movies, I really enjoyed this game. Guardians are awesome here, I dare to say even better than in the movies. I would recommend this game even if you don't enjoy superhero themes much, because it's a genuinely really good and wholesome adventure game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Marvel's Avengers for about 2 hours and giving up entirely thanks to the weird characters, horrible controls and bugs, terrible voice acting and cringy main character, I hardly had high hopes for Guardians of the Galaxy. I bought it because it was nominated for game of the year, and so I thought I'd give it a shot. But sure enough I was met with the same familiar modeling style, same art, same visual feel to the characters in the game as the Avengers at first glance, and I felt my heart sink after paying 50 dollars for the game.Then I actually got around to the meat of the game itself, which happened really quickly mind you, and any and all doubts I had were immediately erased. This game defied all expectations I had, and even fixed several issues that I'd had with the previous games. The writers and dialogue captures exactly what the Guardians of the Galaxy are; a group of ragtag "heroes" that basically hate each others' guts and aren't afraid to show it. The story narrative was great, choices felt meaningful in the context of the larger story, and each character had a charm to them that is hard to build in a game where every character needs to be meaningful to complement choices. Peter Quill was a fantastic main character, and though his blasters feel underpowered at the start, it falls into place after you realise that the true combat is making your teammates do the damage and not you.More notably, there were plenty of technical changes that were really welcome in this game. Though the characters don't feel particularly physics heavy, this was a vast improvement over the Avengers. For example, in the Avengers, characters didn't feel like they had any weight at all, and made movements such as turning with the characters feel weirdly sudden and inhuman. This was not the case with Guardians, though it's definitely not physics heavy of a game. Peter Quill felt like a human being, not just a character model, and his movements were punchy and satisfying. Watching Drax wail on an enemy or throw something across the room was immensely impactful and memorably, unlike watching Hulk smash something in the Avengers which felt really more like breaking cardboard than smashing through metal or otherwise. Controls in this game are much smoother feeling, no weird hitches like I had in the Avengers, and interacting with objects in Guardians was thankfully not a weird game of guessing the correct distance to be from an object for the interact button to show up (seriously Avengers, why).Aside from slightly repetitive combat, as well as some really difficult situations, the game was overall a real bag of enjoyment, and I highly recommend it for a nice linear story where some choices matter, and others are just there for the ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles.
