_childDocuments_.review: + Amazing soundtrack+ Stunning graphics+ Fun combat+ Good story-pacing+ Entertaining yet meaningful story+ Great voiceacting [EN]+ Easy completion+ A lot of gameplay/accessibility customization options+ Photomode/Probably managed to kick my former GOTY 2021 off the throne and replaced it. It's been a while since I had so much fun with a linear story game. Probably one of the best releases in 2021.The game took me about 20 hours to play through but I'll likely go for a NG+ run to get the remaining achievements, which aren't many, you can very likely get them all in the first playthrough, beware that they might contain spoilers however if you wanna play with a guide, which is why I usually don't read any before playing a story game like this one. Talking about the technical aspects the game is pretty much flawless, I played with RTX on and it didn't stutter or drop frames even once. In the last 2 or 3 hours of the game I experienced two random crashes but due to the pretty good autosave feature I didn't loose much progress overall and could just hop into the action again (the menu also shows you the time passed since the last save aswell, props for that feature, never knew I needed that until now).The story overall is first and foremost very entertaining due to the group dynamic of the Guardians. They go through quite some character development, which in the end leads them to grow together as a team after some hardships at the beginning. Seeing them grow closer with time was really nice, the story-pacing in this aspect and overall was really good aswell, there were no parts where I felt like I just wanted it to be over. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring the world aswell and looking for trivia bits or collectibles like outfits. The underlying tone below the humorous first impression is quite the contrast, however a quite fitting one, which captures the essence of what the Guardians of the Galaxy are quite well. I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who is interested in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but this time I'll make an exception.To be honest, I hardly heard about Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy before the release, and even if I've heard something, I simply ignored it for a few reasons:a) I am not a big fan of Marvelb) another game in the Marvel universe was released about a month ago (from the same publisher) and it has collected all the worst of modern games.Therefore, I did not pay attention to the game, until I saw a review somewhere that immediately persuaded me to give it a chance. And I don't regret buying it for a minute. For me, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy has become GOTY and possibly one of the best games of the last few years. Why? Because it has no boring open-world, no unnecessary side quests, no meaningless DLC's and microtransactions, only a concentrated 20-hour adventure.The story here is perhaps the strongest side, I would say that it's even slightly better than the movie. All characters are well written, and each has its own strengths and weaknesses. The dialogues are brilliant, guardians are constantly discussing their problems and making jokes about each other, and this is not just empty chatter, almost every line makes some nice additions to the story.Some other reviews say about boring combat - indeed, the first hour or two, the set of combos is very limited. But then, when more abilities of the guards are revealed, the combat becomes very fun and does not get boring almost until the very end of the game.Of course, Guardians of the Galaxy is not a perfect game, especially when talking about technical aspects. Once the game rebooted my computer, several times I got stuck in textures, and sometimes there were massive FPS drops during cutscenes. But despite this, I cannot call the state of the game bad, I completed the game and did not come across a single game-breaking bug.10/10 for me, I hope publisher will make correct conclusions, and we will see more games like this in the future

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr This is possibly my favorite iteration of the Guardians group, and the movies will need to play catch up with them in the future. 9/10, near perfect game. Play this game if you like the characters or liked Mass Effect. This game is cool, it's more story than game however, so don't come to this game for complex mechanics or strategy outside of "shoot this guy, then have team member shoot other guy", so if you aren't compelled by the story, don't bother.The story follows the Guardians as they try to make decent pay for once, and end up inadverdently causing a galaxy wide conflict to occur, typical Guardians antics. In terms of dialogue, the game focuses heavily on getting you to like this characters and have their conversations feel natural, and I feel it does that fairly well (outside of the occasional battle dialogue happening twice in the same fight).Outside of dialogue, think Mass Effect in terms of you get a limited number of dialogue options, and those can affect your relationship with the team, and to an extent, your ending of the game. Now, I only payed one playthrough, but I also went out of my way to explore the various areas for extra costumes, money (used for upgrading yourself) etc. So if you didn't want to find EVERY pile of money, or every costume, you're probably looking at a 10-15hr story experience, not bad.If I were to give this game a short description, it would be; "Player friendly game, encourages but never forces, you sail your own ship (to an extent)". As in you get various dialogue options, and these can change how the story goes to an extent (such as having help in some areas or not having help, but in the end you're gonna go through the same areas.) Of which I cant really say much on without spoilers, theres just a decent amount of areas that become easier or harder depending on your succesfull or un-successfull dialogue options.I can't really think of much else to say, but heres answers to some questions I believe people would have.- No, you cannot bang Gamora, this isn't the movies.- Groot probably gets the least development out of the characters, followed closely be Gamora- Starlord and Drax get the most  character development- Starlord and Rocket get the coolest costumes, Drax gets the lamest (with a few exceptions)- Soundtrack is forgettable besides certain boss themes and the metal soundtrack (honestly, the star lord album is good enough on its own)- You don't need to collect ALL the money to get ALL the upgrades, you get a decent safety blanket to where that isn't necessary. - Shooting feels fine, not groundbreaking, not crap.If Square or any other Dev sees this interview, here are the things I would want to see improved in possible DLC or Sequel games:- More Groot development- More Starlord upgrades, really, only 15 in the whole game? And some of them are useless!- The team costume combo I had at the end of the game was "War Lord", Katathian Funeral, Casual Attire, Golden Rocket, Golden Groot- Perhaps moments in the game where you can either play as or see in the eyes of the other team members, maybe not for a sequel but I really wouldn't mind a DLC story for each character, where you play as them (maybe a 3 hour mini campaign for each Guardian, where you play as Rocket, Drax, Gamora, etc each with their own play style?) I get Starlord is the STAR of the show, but switching it up in the DLC wouldn't hurt, but maybe keep it just Starlord in a possible GotG 2.- More team upgrades, seriously I fully maxed them out about 3/4ths of the way through on standard.- Maybe new game modes, unlocked after certain requirements? Maybe a boss rush, or mini games, etc.- Maybe new game settings, custom submitted by the community. Like, maybe a melee only game mode where you cant use your blasters in a fight, team assists are disabled, etc (Or, for dialogue, you could have a "Groot Game Plus" where all dialogue is replaced with "I am Groot" if you really wanted to screw with players)

_childDocuments_.review: A great way to end the year, this was a fantastic single player game. The graphics are stand out (facial animation is some of the best I've seen) and the voice acting is brilliant for the whole cast - not a Nolan North or Troy Baker in the whole bunch of them, which was a refreshing change. The soundtrack is magnificent and to be fighting a horde of Chitauri whilst Rick Astley booms out or [slight spoiler] fighting a huge space battle alongside Fin Fang Foom with 'Don't fear the reaper' playing are some of the most memorable encounters I've had in gaming this year.The game is strictly linear with some branches to pick up costumes, crafting mats, etc and the Milano serves as a hub between levels to chat to the team. Gameplay-wise this came across to me as a mix of Uncharted's spectacle, Mass Effect's decision making system (some pretty large story points can hinge off making the right call) and a battle system similar to Final Fantasy 15. The battles seemed overly simplistic when I started and I wasn't that impressed, but when the skills start opening up it can lead to some great (and suprisingly hard, for me anyway) battles where choosing the right Guardian skill is crucial to victory.Also of major note is the story which is easily on a par with the MCU movies (and probably better than Guardians 2) with proper arcs, and actual emotional content (in a video game!) and also loads of Marvel Easter eggs for us nerds. The Star Lord of this game is very much one based off the comics, and not the MCU, which might put some people off, although the other 4 are very much more like their cinematic cousins. Can't recommend this enough, me old mucker.EDIT: Must mention that I had 5 or six game blocking issues during the 28 or so hours, that necessitated restarting from the last checkpoint - a couple of fall through the floors and 3 times when, after a long fight, the game didn't register all enemies as defeated so wouldn't unlock the next section, seems they were either outside of the map or stuck in scenery somewhere - these issues ran contrary to the experience of the rest of the game so stood out a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: :  is a Marvel-inspired third-person action-adventure game created by Eidos-Montréal, the studio behind ,  and  Reboots. You play as Star-lord, the leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy, and you are on an epic quest to kill powerful monsters, score quick cash, defeat a religious empire and ultimately save the universe. I am not a big Marvel fan, not even into comics, but the game definitely exceeded my expectations and Eidos-Montréal delivered a captivating storyline with a lot of memorable moments. ✔️ Well told story, with a very likable cast of characters.✔️ Excellent writing, plenty of funny jokes and banter between the characters✔️ Simple gameplay that never gets boring.✔️ Amazing visuals, with top-notch facial animations and voice acting.✔️ Fantastic soundtrack. ✔️ Well-optimized, no FPS drops or crashes. ❌ Ran into multiple bugs and glitches.❌ Decisions that lead to unnoticeable narrative differences.You play as Peter Quill, (Star-Lord), the charismatic leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy. The other members are; Rocket, a cute but trigger-happy talking raccoon; Drax the Destroyer, the strongest guardian with zero understanding for symbolism and metaphors; Gamora, a vicious assassin and the daughter of Thanos; and Groot, a talking tree and Rocket’s life long friend. The game starts with you and your team trying to capture a monster on a forbidden planet to earn some money, and everything just falls apart after Peter coincidently finds and picks up a glowing yellow gem, better known as the Soul Stone (one of six powerful infinity stones). Thankfully, you don't need to know the comics to understand the story, as it is a fresh take on the Guardians (completely optional, but if you have the time, I recommend watching at least the first Guardians of the Galaxy movie, just to know basic information). Even though some awkward jokes don’t quite land, I was hooked from start to finish; I just love the random conversations and banter between the guardians, and there are many hilarious and heartwarming moments scattered around from beginning to end, thanks to the top-notch facial animations and voice acting. As for the choices, they were somewhat disappointing; the majority of them don't have any real consequences or change in the narrative, so it is basically a linear game with only one ending.Unfortunately, you can only control Star-Lord with his dual laser pistols (which have special ammo types that you will unlock as you progress). That being said, your team will fight beside you, and you can order them to use their powers in combat or during puzzles. Each character, yourself included, has four abilities that match their combat style(Rocket can use his rockets, Drax has a slam attack, Groot can grapple multiple enemies in place, Star-Lord can fly using his rocket boots, and so on). You can upgrade your dual pistols using components scattered around the levels, and you have to use a workbench to do so, located on your ship, the Milano (that you go back to every now and then), and at least one in every level. As for abilities and powers, you can unlock them through the menu using points that you earn from defeating enemies.I’ve set the game on the highest difficulty option, yet didn’t find it that hard, so there are custom difficulty options that you can play with to make the game more difficult/easier (I set the “damage received” option to its highest for example). You will fight different types of enemies and monsters, and the banter between the characters in combat makes it more enjoyable, even though they sometimes repeat the same phrases and jokes.When things get rough, you can use the “Huddle Up” ability where all of them gather around you for a pep talk, and depending on the response you choose, either a temporary damage buff will be granted for everyone or to yourself only. You can use your visor to scan your surroundings, highlight important objects, help solve puzzles (which aren’t very common) and to find hidden resources and collectibles. Finding collectibles in levels will unlock optional dialogue options that mainly focus on the backstories of the Guardians, as well as outfits and skins. There are a few quick-time events (QTEs) during gameplay, which you can disable in the menu. After you beat the game, you can either replay the chapters or continue to New Game Plus where your unlocked abilities will carry over (except the ammo types of your dual pistols for story reasons). The game is absolutely stunning; you will spend your time visiting very rich worlds, exploring the Milano and battling weird-looking aliens and monsters in fighting arenas. In addition, the characters' facial expressions and lip-syncing are detailed and look amazing, even the raccoon. The game worked well and ran beautifully, with buttery smooth 60 FPS. However, I ran into a few bugs and visual glitches, such as blurry or bushy textures, characters standing idle when enemies are nearby, and not being able to scan objects with my visor. Fortunately, nothing game-breaking.  The game’s soundtrack mainly consists of nostalgic 1980s pop and rock songs from multiple famous artists, such as Europe's The Final Countdown and Take on Me by a-ha. There are two original songs included, called “Zero to Hero” and “Space Riders with No Names”, and I think they are okay. All in all, it’s a solid soundtrack.  The game is about 17 chapters long and it took me almost 20 hours to finish. Overall, it’s a great game; a gripping storyline, likable characters, fun gameplay, great visuals and a solid soundtrack. Even if you are not a comic book fan, I highly recommend giving this game a shot, you won't "flarking" regret it

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever do reviews, but I felt this one deserves it.While the shooty bits, while not bad, aren't mind blowing, everything else about the game is an incredible act of love.  To give some game comparisons, it feels like a weird love child of Mass Effect and Uncharted.  It's got lots of story telling bits, fun set pieces that have you hitting a good number of environments navigating and fighting your way through, party combos that you can set up once you get more abilities. Aside from all that, the story is wonderfully mature. It's got the funny comedic bits that help break up the tension (and it did get quite a few chuckles from me just from the amazing camera work or silly thing that would happen), but the story wrapping as a whole is a very mature take on learning to cope, moving forward, forgiveness, and bonding with family and friends.  I highly recommend this game for the amazing swashbuckling space drama story heavy game that it is, it was probably the most satisfied I've been with a game purchase in some time.

_childDocuments_.review: After the awful mess that the Avengers game was, i had no intention of playing this game as i thought it would be similar in quality, but then i saw the amount of praise it was getting so i decided to give it a shot. I also found out that Eidos-Montreal, the Deus Ex developers made this game. Even though i would have preferred a sequel to Mankind Divided, this game turned out to be great and i enjoyed it quite a bit. This is a straightforward, linear story driven game with no bulls*it monetisation added. The characters are entertaining to interact with and they've done a great job of recreating the guardians we know from the movies and comics but they are different enough to be their own version of these characters. The amount of optional dialogue for certain situations is crazy and you can tell a lot of effort has gone behind these interactions and making them feel seamless and natural in conversation. I loved the visual variety and all the different locations you explore it kept the game from getting stale and it is a very good looking game too, i took a lot of screenshots. The story is engaging and well written but i felt the momentum slowed down a bit in the second half. The gameplay is solid and can be quite a bit of fun but it's also nothing special and it can feel repetitive at times. Also have to give a shoutout to that licensed soundtrack it has so many classic bangers and made so many moments in the game that much better. This was one of the best games of the year and definitely worth playing.8/10 (Great)

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is an action-adventure game with a fantastic original narrative. Incredibly impressive and unfortunately underrated, I believe it is one of Marvel's best video games to date. It adapts the feel of the MCU, but does not copy it. In fact, it excels in many ways.+ An original story that shines in all aspects. At first, it may seem like a standard story of saving the Galaxy, but once you are a few hours in you begin to see some of the more nuanced scenes that provide depth to the whole narrative. All main characters undergo change and each have their own deeply personal moments, perfectly presented in a way that feels natural to the whole plot and larger theme of the game.+ Our iconic Marvel characters finally in a video game. Eidos-Montréal managed to keep them true to their comic book and MCU personalities, but also added a great layer of original traits that keep the game fresh and distinct.+ Fantastically written banter between characters. The humour here resembles that of MCU movies, however, it is a little bit more on the mature side, which is a nice change in my opinion.+ Stellar soundtrack consisting of many licensed 80s songs. Iconic and essential part of this specific group of superheroes. It was awesome to see the game also take music seriously, just like the Guardians of the Galaxy movies and comic books.+ Combat (Part I) - "Part I" of the combat system is definitely a positive part, meaning the whole "team effort" mechanic. Passing combat encounters relies heavily on team effort, you have to command your fellow guardians to execute specific moves in order to aid you in battle. Just relying on Star-Lord's guns to win will only get you so far, further into the levels you will need to make sure you use your companions as much as possible.+ Outfits that, unlike Marvel's Avengers, can be obtained through exploration in the world. A lot of licensed and original outfit designs if you want to tweak your team. No microtransactions required unlike elsewhere.- Combat (Part II) - "Part II" of the combat system, meaning pretty much everything apart from the "team effort" thing is unfortunately one of the few negative points I have. Apart from Quill's abilities, the only thing you use in combat are his Element Guns. All you do is shoot at enemies with them until they drop dead, which gets repetitive so that alone is reason enough to use abilities as much as possible. I believe that combat is nicely spaced between platforming sessions, however, and it shouldn't really bother anyone too much at all. It was really not a "negative" point for me and didn't make me enjoy the game any less, but I still feel it should be mentioned here, as it could have been done better.- Collectibles are not saved separately and can't really be obtained via "Chapter Select", mostly considers people who want to go for all achievements though.Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy represents what a good superhero game with original narrative can be. Loads of fun, thanks to its great banter, characters and design. At the same time coated with a nuanced, but equally as fun, story. It is a shame that sale expectations were not met. I had no expectations of my own going into this game, but I must say that I was so pleased, I now call it one of the best Marvel games I have ever played. I have to give it a  and I strongly recommend everyone who is a fan of Marvel to pick it up, disappointment is not an option!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a mostly great story backed up by a mostly average game. In an era where everything is either a metroidvania, open world, or Destiny clone, Guardians of the Galaxy feels like a throwback to the kind of action games they made 10 years ago. This is the kind of theme park ride style 'interactive experience' we used to see all the time back in those days, only this time with a modern AAA budget to back it up. The meat and potatoes of this game is the story as well as the experience of leading the Guardians of the Galaxy as Star Lord. Unlike other ensemble games, you only control a single character, with everyone else relegated to AI controlled support. This narrows the gameplay down a bit, but really helps with the immersion, as you're always right there following along through Peter's perspective. This game seems to take place in it's own version of the Guardians canon, borrowing elements from both the movies and comic universes. We start out with the team already assembled, but still early enough in their careers to experience many of the same growing pains they went through in the films. A lot of the character beats will be familiar to anyone who's seen the movies, but they're very well executed for the most part. Outside of the core cast, it does feel like a conscious effort was made to steer clear of retreading the same plot as the films, instead bringing in a new supporting cast as well as a unique threat that ends up challenging the team on a very personal level. My only gripe here is that the central antagonist behind everything isn't all that compelling, and the secondary antagonists are pretty thinly developed. The game tries to make you feel motivated to settle the score with them, but I felt more invested in seeing the characters through the end of their journey rather than finally besting the mostly uninteresting antagonists.Gameplay wise, this is an extremely linear game with only a small smattering of collectibles to find. There are upgrades for Star Lord and the rest of the team to earn, but you'll likely be able to max out everything well before the final act. Combat has the player control Star Lord directly, while frequently ordering the rest of the Guardians to use their abilities to either support the team or do damage directly to enemies. One of my biggest issues with this game is that playing as Star Lord is a pretty mediocre experience. His twin guns are about as effective as super soakers and it's pretty clear the devs deliberately nerfed him in order to force you more into a quarterback roll for the team, calling on the rest of your party to do the real damage. Most enemies outside of the basic cannon fodder have tons of health, and you'll frequently find yourself waiting for the other guardians to work through their cooldowns so you can fire off the next big damage ability. Due to having four team members with you at all times and the large quantity of enemies, things can also become extremely chaotic and it is very easy to loose track of what's going on around you. When the system works you really do feel like a team, but when it falls apart you'll often find yourself overwhelmed by the chaos around you, plinking away with pea shooters that constantly overheat. This game also has some serious pacing issues. I understand the need to provide value given the $60 asking price, but honestly this game feels way too padded at it's current length. Completing the same handful of navigational puzzles or slogging through a seemingly endless stream of repetitive combat encounters against damage sponge enemies really begins to grate after a while. The game does have some stellar moments which I won't spoil that help break up the action a bit, but this game can feel very monotonous at times.I do need to mention that this game was also fairly buggy and unstable. Prior to the most recent patch the game was constantly crashing for me with ray tracing on. There are often lip syncing errors, weird lighting issues, and pathfinding goofiness from your allies as well. Nothing too catastrophic overall and the game is absolutely gorgeous when everything works properly, but it definitely could use a bit more polish.Overall I enjoyed this one, but probably won't ever feel the need to replay it. It just feels like a good 'one and done' kind of game to me. Definitely grab this one if you can find it on sale, just set your expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly captures the rowdy camraderie of the Guardians of the Galaxy. Story, gameplay, graphics, music, even facial animations are of the highest order. Narrative choices matter, too! Some technical glitches mar the experience, and sometimes the squad-mates talk a little too much. But otherwise a blast from start to finish. 9/10Total size on my ssd: 75.6 GB++ Characters are true to the comics. ++ Story has got great stakes and gravitas.+ Choices matter. Want the final fight to be easier? Treat other characters right and you  get some help.+ Takes a bit to get the flow of combat down and properly stacking moves, but once figured out it becomes easy to do a lot of damage in a short time.+ Exploration is rewarding, but never takes you too far afield+ Visually GotG looks good, with lots of detail in the environments, excellent lighting and crisp textures. Facial animations are great too. + Great selection of classic tunes (which can be disabled in the settings if you want to live stream the game)+ Catchy orchestral score by Richard Jacques perfectly captures the Guardians’ spirit of adventure.+/- There is a LOT of talking in GotG. Many conversations are optional, but there is a lot of ambient conversation that is constantly occurring. I liked it – I’d even argue it wouldn’t be the same game without it – but some might find it annoying.+/- Requires hardware asynchonous compute. While Guardians of the Galaxy can run on some fairly dated hardware, Nvidia GTX 900-series (which emulates asynchronous compute in the driver) chugs along at 15 fps. GTX 1000-series (1060, 1070 etc) and newer has hardware async and should run GotG fine. On Radeon, my R9 290 (which also has hardware async) ran it without issues at 1080p low settings.- While the graphics are good, mirrors look bad, even with ray-tracing enabled. - Lack of enemy variety. It’s the same basic group of enemies, re-skinned for different factions. As a result…- Combat encounters generally play out the same (not bosses, thankfully). Gets boring near the end.- Quick-time events in a modern game? Seriously?- Technical issues. Had to restart from a checkpoint three times in 20 hours because the battle didn’t end even though I had eliminated all the enemies. Audio skips and stutters were also an issue. Visual stuttering was also an issue; seemed tied to frame-pacing, but no matter how much I played with vsync settings (in-game and in the Nvidia control panel) the stutter improved but never quite went away. At least the game never crashed on me.If you’re a fan of comic book games, like the Batman Arkham series or the Spiderman games, or just enjoy good old-fashioned adventure games, absolutely get Guardians of the Galaxy. It’s right up there with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy completely surpassed my expectations. This isn’t just a good game; its an awesome game and I would absolutely recommend it. In a world where so many games are open world for no reason, it really is a breath of fresh air to play such a high quality, linear, single player, game. There are no large open areas to explore, there aren’t hundreds of collectables you should be searching for (There were a few, but I found most of them and I wasn’t looking particularly hard), and there aren’t many alternative paths you could be taking. Everyone who plays this game will have an almost identical experience, and that is great. It means they can really focus on making that experience the best it can be, and it really is an amazing experience.The first thing I noticed upon starting this game is how good it looks. Its one of the best-looking games I’ve played to date, and it runs great, other than one level that had some performance issues for me. While graphics don’t make a bad game good, they can improve an already good game. This game really shines in its characters. They all felt really well written and constantly had funny and interesting lines. There was almost never a quiet moment. The story felt a little out there, especially towards the end, but that’s sort of what I expected from a Marvel game. It was still a pretty good story that I found interesting, and I think I liked it better than most of Marvel’s movies. The story takes you to several planets and locations that feel quite varied and alien, which is perfect for a space game.The game has a great balance between story segments, combat sections, and puzzles. The combat wasn’t anything that hasn’t been done before and none of the puzzles were hard, but it was all fun, which is what matters. Towards the end some of the enemies felt a little bullet spongey, but there is an option to increase the damage you deal, so that should help alleviate that problem if it bothers you enough.Something that did bother me was the movement. There is no momentum in your movement. This like trying to jump across a game feel off because even if you have a running start, you still jump almost straight up. You can still cross gaps, you just need to use your boosters. There were also a few quick time events that feel super awkward when using KBM, and one section that felt impossible to do with a mouse as it was not reading mouse inputs properly.The game also had a few bugs. The worst bug I experienced was when quitting the game. Twice in my playthrough, upon quitting the game, my entire system would freeze, and I’d be forced to reboot it through the reset button on my case. There were also a handful of times that I fell through the floor, and a few more times where the game randomly teleported me across the room. There was one are where I could see crafting resources but could not get to them as the ledge I was supposed to cross was bugged out and as soon as I finished the ledge walking animation, it would take me back to the side I started on. It was not a big deal since the game gives you way more materials than you need to get every upgrade. Overall, nothing major, but stuff I feel is worth noting.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... 18h of pure condensed fun !The story is rich and engaging and the gameplay is fun enough to make you chew through this game like a warm cookie. Too bad I can't play it a second time for the first time...

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy felt pretty much felt like a 20-hour movie that you get to play. I experienced a few minor bugs during jumping and combat. Also, sometimes the  dialogue gets cut abruptly, which is a shame, because the writing and voice acting are top-notch. The character interactions, the witty one-liners, the drama - it all feels like it was pulled straight from a Marvel movie.The combat, while not groundbreaking, is fun enough to keep you engaged. It has its highs and lows, and the upgrade system is a nice touch that adds a layer of strategy to the mix. It's not the best part of the game, but it certainly doesn't drag it down either.What really took me by surprise were the choices. They matter. It's not just a gimmick, the choices you make have tangible effects on the game, making every decision feel weighty and important. It adds an extra layer of depth that I didn't expect to find.Despite its flaws, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy delivers an experience that I can easily recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Family. Fam fam fam fami family.' - Furries 9.If you've seen the Guardians of the Galaxy movies, this hits very similar notes and goes through some of the same story beats. The dialogue is really enjoyable if you like snarky sarcastic comments rapid fire. More than anything, it has really good setup and payoff. There's some technical issues but a quick reload usually fixes what broke. It's a great game for the story and fun dialogue and for everything else, there's a pretty robust level of choice in difficulty (skipping stupid QTE's? Hells ya) making the game enjoyable as bawls to go through. Worth the full price and every damn second. It was roughly 18-20ish hours on my playthrough.First and foremost, good on this game for having the best option for the basic standards of a story focused game. Quick time events, optional, pausable in cutscenes and everywhere else in a single player game (thank you you beautiful bastards), subtitles color coded for who's speaking, controller/keyboard instant swapping along with prompts, individual difficulty sliders for cooldowns, enemy damage, player damage, cc durations, frequent checkpoints. All of these adds up to the most accessible and unique customizability that should be the new standard for games.As for my only complaint, the combat. It's a really good base but does not have enough progression to keep things fresh through the whole game. It kind of runs on empty near the midpoint of the game where the player already has all they want to deal with the encounters which all feel very samey. There's a bunch of trash mobs, a few big bois, and some environmentals. Gravity/pull everything into environmentals, blow them up. If no envornmentals, combo AoE's. Big bois are an act of dodging until cooldowns come up to burst them down. The formula is just too shallow to feel interesting through the game. It begins to feel more tedious than fun. Targeting is also a bit iffy but serviceable. Oh right, load times are also a bit on the long side if you have to reload a save/checkpoint.The best part of the game is the flarkin dialogue. The story is alright, something something family and stuff but the dialogue is like an extended take on the Guardians of the Galaxy movies hitting the same notes/humor but also being its own thing. What this does better than the movie is the setup and payoff. What seems to be a one off joke comes back in a different light and hits different a second time. This is what the game's all about and it does it so well.The story is alright. It's more of a vehicle for the dialogue than the main driver. There's some great moments but the overall message and journey rings much louder than the story itself.Graphically, eveyrthing is animated really well, at points a bit uncanny valley but barely not quite. Faces are not tired and express a lot of emotion. This is also a very colorful game and at times can be a little visually loud but it oozes style everywhere.Audio is a bit of a mixed bag. Voice overs are flarkin great, directionals are a little iffy and it's sometimes hard to pinpoint where something is coming from. The combat sounds seem to be deliberately toned down for the snark to have it's time in the light but this leads to the impacts lacking a bit of oomph. Again, since dialogue is the star of the game, this is more an observation than a complaint.There's some great tracks in the game and it's utilized well in only a handful of places. It most others, these fantastic tracks feel wasted as background noise rather than emphasizing a moment.I enjoyed the hell out of Guardians of the Galaxy, it doesn't waste your time, is packed full of fun moments (to the point I really wanted to finish it in one sitting) and is just a fun game. Definitely recommend it even at its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have always revered the Spiderman series for being the only game that every actually felt like "playing a comic book come to life." I still think the Spiderman series is better than this game but Square really nailed the Guardians' vibe from the comics and the MCU combined. I liked that they weren't affraid to throw in the more esoteric details and characters from the comics that movies often shy away from because "normied wouldn't get it". That in itself earns this game it's recommendation. The gameplay is a little clunky sometimes do to the controls being just a little off. I can't explain it but I feel like there needs to be a better control scheme for the game. It also would have been nice to have more control over the rest of the team rather only ever controlling Peter Quill. That being said the story is very fun and enjoyable with real "laugh out loud" moments throughout. Particularly Drax and Mantis are the standout characters here. I very much like what was done with Mantis in this story compared to the MCU version. It's one of those games where I could not walk away from it until credits rolled.  Absolutely recommend this purchase at full price. If you love comics and video games this is a no brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: Guardians of the Galaxy is a straight forward action adventure game developed by Eidos-Montréal the makers of the Deus Ex squeals. While most super hero titles in the gaming space aren't great (with a couple of exceptions), Edios really kept true to what made the Guardians movies great. Guardians offers a basic yet enjoyable experience with great moments, well written characters, a solid 20+ hour campaign, and a fantastic visual fidelity. Guardians does have a couple of issues, mainly with the Gameplay dragging by the end of the experience, and a couple of instances of mouse and keyboard controls not working well. Mainly in the flying portions of the campaign having bad controls, and the combat lacking enough interesting combinations of abilities. Mainly this leads to a simple combat system that doesn't have a tone of depth. Overall I do recommend Guardians of the Galaxy, and is definitely worth picking up on sale, if possible. I'll give Guardians a solid 7/10!

_childDocuments_.review: +Great cast of characters with pretty distinctive personalities that leads into some funny interactions and interesting world building. _childDocuments_.review: GOTG makes me feel nostalgic as a complete new game. It reminds me of the times in which games were suppose to be fun without hitting you with heavy depressive stuff right from the get go. It makes you laugh & enjoy your time, rewards you for exploring the world around you while you listen to the hilarious banter of your crew. I am more of a DC comic type of person, so I haven't read many Marvel comics, let alone a single GOTG comic. But I've seen the movies. The game makes the crew members more likeable than the movies, because it explores their stories more & shows more of their actual characters, instead of using them solely for comic reliefs.The gameplay itself reminds me a little bit of Lego games. You can only play as Star Lord, but you can make awesome battle combos with your team. Every team member has its unique strengths on the battlefield. It also allows you to individually adjust the difficulty settings, for casual gamers who want to relax to hardcore gamers who love the challenge.I also saw some people finishing the game in under 15 hours, while I'm 22 hours in & just reached the middle of the game. So yes, you can rush it if that's what you like, but if you take your time to explore the world, go out of your way to find hidden details or dialogues, then you will spend more than 30 hours on your first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best single-player rides I've had in a long time. Great characters, tunes, and a focused story is a refreshing pace from all the open world games that came out recently. There are still some glitches along the way, but nothing detracting.It took me 45 hours to finish this game due to taking so many photos, so I'm definitely coming back for a pure gameplay run on New Game+My only complaint is that the combat can feel a bit awkward and too hectic. I'll definitely use a controller on my next run. I resorted to managing the rotation of all the character's skills as the main way of playing. Although some skills are quite underwhelming, some, like the Groot 1->1 + Rocket 4->4 are great at clearing tight groups, with Gamora and Drax's single target damage to be great at distant targets or sponges. when you get more skills, it opens up more options for combos. I felt that the main character played a more supporting role than the rest. Thanks to a special sponsor for providing a key and the chance to screenshot this awesome adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: + Excellent character development and depth+ Captures the goofy spirit of the GotG movies, but with surprisingly heartfelt and emotional moments+ Great voice acting+ Photo mode has tons of customisations+ Collectibles actually have a point; they provide bonus dialogue and insight into the backstories of the Guardians- A number of bugs, but most of them to do with achievements- Locked FOV; might be a problem if you are prone to motion sickness- Long loading screen times- Early chapters can be underwhelming- Combat is rather simplistic; overall pretty fun, but can get a little boring towards the end of the gameMost games that take inspiration from TV and movies tend to be mediocre because they're made to simply ride on the respective hype and cash out on it. Amazingly, GotG, while sharing the same goofy nature of the movies, actually puts in a lot more effort into giving depth to its characters, with Drax in particular being incredibly well written and voiced. While his movie counterpart is kind of a clownish, occasionally dimwitted man-child, this game actually manages to turn him into a serious, yet emotional character while still having his fair share of hilarious dialogue; "most unexpected", as he might say.As the story progresses, you grow to like and care for the characters, and they too as well go from begrudging allies to a close-knit family. And this IMO, is what truly makes the game great.If you find yourself a little underwhelmed by the game, try and at least give it until chapter 4 because that's when (IMO) the game starts to pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: I was honestly torn about picking up this game on release, but I'm glad I did.  Basically, you're getting a good single player story-driven 3rd person shooter / beat 'em up with a Marvel GotG flavor.  The story is excellent with great writing and good story beats that really delivers.  The combat is actually quite a bit more fun than I expected after watching some reviews--though it's no DMC, it's active and involved and I felt like it was just the right level of challenging (I played on normal).  It has a TON of configuration options for display, audio AND difficulty that I'm really pleased with.  I ran into a couple of bugs, but none of them totally game breaking.  I had to restart one checkpoint when an enemy became invincible, I got some weird display glitches in a couple of places (pretty sure those were memory-leak issues...restarting cleared everything up) and when using my Xbox Elite V2 controller in BT wireless mode it was showing me Switch control prompts.  Other than that, it ran great on my fairly well built gaming PC.  Bottom Line:  If you like GotG, Single Player Story driven, and you're not adverse to DMC-Lite gameplay you'll probably like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Short Version:This game is probably a prime example of not judging a book by its cover (regardless of how pretty the cover looks). Guardians of the Galaxy took me by surprise. It is a title that excels in all of its core areas and delivers a fantastic, memorable experience.Whether you’re a fan of the comic books, the films, or have never experienced anything related to it whatsoever, the game will send you on a captivating ride that’s brilliant from start to finish. One of the best single player games I’ve played in a while.Pros:Cons:-Gorgeous visuals-Great story-Fantastically well-written characters-Engaging combat-Brilliant soundtrack-Very well optimised	-Ship combat is poor-A few bugsMy Rating:9.5/10 - MasterpieceFrom Misfits to Super Heroes!Guardians of the Galaxy (GotG) is a third-person, action-adventure game based on the iconic Marvel comic book series of the same name. It follows a group of deviants aptly named the ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’, as they are thrown into a dire situation of galactic proportions.Despite the story revolving around the gang as a whole, you’ll only be playing as Star Lord, the cocky and mostly capable leader of the group, originally born on Earth but taken away from his home planet at a young age.The world of GotG is full of sentient alien life, with a vast number of species colonising the cosmos. There are many factions, groups and civilisations spread throughout, each with their own traits and agendas.The ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ themselves are diverse. As well as Star Lord, there is Rocket: a tech-savvy raccoon with a knack for weapons. Alongside him is Groot: a tree-like creature whose roots can offer great assistance in traversal and combat. There’s Drax: a powerful warrior who definitely doesn’t let sarcasm go over his head. Last, but certainly not least, is Gamora: an assassin who’s stride and determination are unmatched. There’s also a llama, and he’s amazing.These characters are what made the story so memorable for me. They’re just so likeable and well-written. The banter between them during missions is amusing, and makes the game feel even more enjoyable than it already was. They never feel tacked onto the narrative either, since each one has their own personal stake in the conflict.They all go through some kind of development. The relationships between them are tested multiple times, which helps set them apart. A Screenshot of Marvel's Guardians of the GalaxyAs for the actual story itself, it’s great. I haven’t read the comics, but I really enjoyed watching the films, and the game takes the same charm, excitement and variation that those movies had and makes something really gripping and entertaining out of it. In essence, it felt like playing through a twenty hour GotG film, and I mean that in the best possible way. If anything, I enjoyed this more than the films.I’m not going to go over the premise or any other specifics of the narrative, as I think it’s best to go in blind. What I will say is this: if you’re looking for a game with a linear, compelling story followed by a captivating cast of characters and a good sense of humour, then here it is.It’s a Beautiful Galaxy…A quick look at some of the screenshots will tell you that GotG is a treat for the eyes, and the visuals showcased there are very much representative of what the final game looks like. In truth, during my first play session, I was in awe.Remember when I said that playing this game feels like a really long GotG film? Here’s another example where this is very apparent. The set pieces are absolutely stunning, possibly some of the best I have ever seen.Everything from the colors, to the details is executed in such a spectacular way that I walked through most levels, taking it all in. The locations you travel to are incredibly diverse and unique. They may follow a singular path, but there are dozens of small detours that can reward you with crafting materials, collectables, and dialogue between characters, all making exploration worthwhile. They also pose their own challenges, which helped set them apart and basically eliminated any risk of repetitiveness.Another area in the visual department that has to be talked about is the fantastic character designs. Like the environments, the level of attention to detail is nuts, and this is especially noticeable with characters who have fur, such as Rocket. It’s amazing how realistic it looks. The rest of the gang look just as good though, and their outfits and appearances look great.Then there’s the animations, which, in some cutscenes, are astonishingly well-done, with some of the best uses of motion capture I’ve ever seen in a game. The smaller conversations don’t have the same impact as these, but they’re still satisfactory.All of this, and the game is still really well optimised. I had occasional brief frame stutters when interacting with certain things, but the performance during intense cutscenes and escalating gameplay sequences rarely ever had an issue. I was able to keep well over 60 frames per second from start to finish, which is worth high praise.A Team Like No Other…GotG is quite an action-packed experience, with most levels containing dozens of combat areas. Since you play as Star Lord, you are equipped with two blasters and a pair of jet boots. That may sound rather mundane, and to begin with it is; but the more you progress, the more varied the fighting becomes.At the end of a combat encounter, you are awarded experience based on how well you fought. Once that reaches a certain threshold, you are given an ability point to be spent on yourself or on other characters. Each character has four abilities to unlock, with the fourth being an ultimate ability that’s given to them once they’ve reached a certain narrative point.On top of having unique combat advantages, each member has a hand in progressing through the levels, making you actually feel like a team. A Screenshot of Marvel's Guardians of the GalaxyBy: NarukoopaSince you’re the head of the group, you get to command your squad, making them target specific enemies with an ability. It takes some getting used to since you’ll be moving around a lot during combat, but once you get into the flow of it, it becomes really engaging and fun to play. The initial staleness of Star Lord’s gameplay becomes a lot more fulfilling when you can fly around the area and unleash havoc on your enemies.Then there’s the ‘huddle’ mechanic, which is nothing short of iconic. This is something you build up towards during confrontations. Once activated, the group huddles together, with Star Lord giving a riveting speech, ending with him turning on his tape recorder which plays a random classic 80s song. Do you want to play a game where you can fly around, shooting things and blowing stuff up, with ‘Never Gonna Give You Up’ playing in the background? GotG lets you do that, and it’s here where the combat is at its best.The only area that’s a bit of a let down is the aerial combat. You travel around the galaxy in the ‘Milano’, a small but spacious ship that’s lived in by the gang, and acts as the game’s hub. There are a few sequences in the story that have you flying it, and they’re not great. The aiming is off, and the actual flying of the vehicle feels sluggish.It's also worth mentioning that GotG still has a few bugs, most of which are minor and have little impact… others can be game-breaking, though the latter of which I only experienced twice, with characters failing to respond to certain commands, stopping me from progressing. A simple save and reload fixes this, however, so as a whole, these didn’t bother me too much, and they certainly didn’t stop me from having a blast of a time.

_childDocuments_.review: ***** No spoilers **** Let me start by saying that even if you're mot a marvel fan or a gaurdians fan in particular this game still hits the spot. From the amazing graphics, to the world building, and especially the team dynamic/family building. They hit every spot perfectly. The characters interactions always felt fluent and relatable. There's many lines of dialogue that are specific to the places you're in and the choices you make, so hearing the same thing almost never happens unless in combat maybe. Unlike it's predecessor Marvels Avengers the games combat is not only great it's barely repetitive and you don't have to hit a target common target like 30 times to kill them. I barely notice the repetitiveness in it too because the games sets the mood very well, to the music blastin in the backround, to the new enemies/bosses almost every chapter, and especially to the skill tree upgrades that allows you to test out new combos it's amazing. At first I was doubtful I'd appreciate playing as only Star Lord ( Peter Quill ) and having to control a team, but in reality it's one of the most enjoyable combat systems I've ever had to play with. It always feels good executing combos quickly when you remember them aswell as it feels rewarding. I won't go into detail but the mechanics and tools the game gives you to work with are also just so nice, they feel just right and don't hinder you at all. At the start of this game I barely listened to rock and metal, but after I found myself loving it and I can credit the game with that for tying memories to those songs that I enjoyed so much. The game has many moments for breathers and just flat times where everyone is joking and having fun with you, It feels amazing. The game also has a lot of comic related material. along with a lot of nods to characters from the comics and easter eggs. The characters also have costumes you can find, it's very fun to see rocket in a tuxedo and shades blasting whatever he sees into oblivion.  The choices in the game DO matter as it leads to many different dialogue options and in some cases story altering changes, so a second play through is worth it. I'm stuck with putting this as my favorite game of all time or at least my top 3 guaranteed. This game was worth every penny, but especially every second I played it for. I hope a sequel comes out because there is room for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game all the way through! a straight forward action game that is fun and engaging. This game is great if your an avid comic reader, a big fan of the MCU, or a gamer looking for a fun Sci-Fi adventure game!

_childDocuments_.review: James Gunn is dead and These Guardians ANNIHILATED HIM.What an amazing Story and wonderful characters. This game is nothing like the movie, but that is an amazing thing. You still have the guardians, you still have the action, but less funny jokes every minute and more serious discussions between the team. Drax is an actual living being, not a brainless meat sack with arms. Gamora has more motivation than Daddy issues, Rocket and Groot have backstory (Granted through Dialogue but, more than we've gotten from Gunn). So many small references that made me smile and also think "Hey, this would be good for non comic fans, because it doesn't shove references everywhere" I feel you could label this game as it's own and it would be believable. _childDocuments_.review: As good as peoples say it is (aka: Very). Easily recommended.The characters are just straight up better than their movie counterpart and are more in-line with their comic versions. They are funnier, more relatable, less cliché, and well written. Even their design is just much better (Gamora especially)The story is bonker, and it's quite fun how it doesn't hold back about being a comic book story.The vista the story will lead you through are also worth stopping and looking at.The combat is decent, with enemies having weakness and such, but nothing completely out there. Though i do like the Guardians having their special moves and how you can fight while some old school music are playing. Which obviously improve it all and make it more unique.But the best part is probably all the dialogues and interactions you have with the other Guardians and between each others. And some of your decisions matter in the short or long run.The only issue i'd have would be the lack of polish. Characters popping out just on the edge of your screen during cutscenes, characters being stuck after using a lift, or their dialogue not playing out (once).Reloading fix the issues, but that still break the flow of the game.Basically: Very good game, even more if you like story and characters interactions.If they ever make a sequel, i only hope they are given time to fix any issues and improve the combat, and it'll be perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I have had in a game this year. From the gameplay, to the graphics, to the incredibly well written dialog and the amazing soundtrack, everything about this game oozes quality.The expression gets bandied about a lot these days, but for this game it is obvious that the developers had a love for and knowledge of the source material. _childDocuments_.review: I thought I could have a decent time with it, given I love the Guardians and Marvel games can mostly be just okay enough to be tolerable but holy hell did this game just take all those expectations and just blow right past them. Right off the bat, it takes the title of my favorite Marvel game, and firmly plants itself just generally as a top tier experience in the Action-Adventure genre. A few things I'd like to highlight: First gotta just say, how AMAZING it is to play a Marvel game by Devs who ACTUALLY GET the heroes of the game they're making. You know whether it's the recent games or even the recent Marvel movies, it just feels like they don't GET the characters they're working on? This game completely voids that concern. This whole game felt like a passion project & love letter to the GoTG characters & fans. I honestly think this game exceeds even the GoTG movies, and I love that trilogy. If you're a GoTG fan at all, you won't regret buying this. The characters are all fleshed out and have had a lot of attention paid to them, EACH of them. (Seriously, this game's Drax is fantastic compared to MCU Drax who was reduced to pure goofball material.) The Group Dynamic and banter is top tier & they masterfully balance the tightrope of comedy in this that feels enjoyable, but never overly cringey or trying too hard like the MCU movies have gotten. The writing & chemistry is handled to perfection. Have to give a MAJOR shoutout to the Environment & Level Design Teams, they totally knocked it out of the park. So many of the planets & environments are just stunning and really capture your attention. These guys get the "Game Ball" for me, just everywhere you go the game is total eye candy.  The Performance was excellent. I played on Maxed out, 1440p  Graphics on a 3080 and I was a constant 144 fps nearly the entire game. No hiccups, no glitches no crashes nothing. Silky smooth and gorgeous visuals all game long. The action feels very hectic at first but quickly as you familiarize yourself with the combat system, I found it a ton of fun. You control Quill, but also can order the others to use a collection of unlockable abilities as the battle continues real-time. Quick paced, smooth and engaging  from a tactical standpoint. (It's also worth noting here that the Difficulty settings are highly customizable and you can change how a lot of the game works. I played on the Default normal settings.) As can be expected from anything Guardians of the Galaxy, the Soundtrack lives up to the hype and is filled to the brim with 70s, 80s, 90s greatness. Wouldn't be GoTG without the music and they deliver here.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: This latest stream of games that are practically interactive movies based on only source material has been a breath of fresh air and in my opinion, a step in the right direction for video games based on comic book super heroes. Especially when they're handled as a game and not a movie tie in.The gameplay is smooth, the story is fun and engaging, it has a decent amount of content without getting too competitive and even if you aren't too into finding secrets, you can easily unlock every perk before finishing the game.I remember as a child playing games based on TV shows and Movies but being disappointed that it was just a shameless way to generate more cash on the side. Playing Spider Man on the PS4 and then Guardians of the Galaxy, having their own contained storylines with characters that are only vaguely talked about among fans brings a whole new feeling to these games that make it feel like you're watching a whole movie. Only it's much much longer.I think I may start New Game Plus and try to finish every achievement in an attempt to squeeze a few more hours out of this marvelous game.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer is get this game if you're even on the fence.I remember seeing this game get announced at one of those game shows E3 or VGA can't remember which exactly. All I can remember is seeing it and thinking it looked weak, corny, uninspiring, and boring. I could not have been further from the truth.First off the performance is top notch. Yes I am fortunate enough to have a 3070 but I also pushed the game to its max with RTX on while playing at 3440x1440. Never went below 70fps. This is the only game I have played that actually did RTX correctly. Any other game I have played with RTX I lose close to 30fps. Not even sure I lost any fps in GOTG.Gameplay was so fun and engaging. I chose not the normal difficulty but the next highest and it was just right for me. You're always shooting and firing off abilities. It's beyond enjoyable. I was always looking forward to the next combat moment. Also the pacing as a whole from combat to exploration to adventure moments was spot on. It was all so fluid. Story and dialogue I personally loved. The banter was hilarious and not annoying. Story flowed very nicely and often times while I may have guessed what was going to happen I never guessed to what scale it would happen or exactly how. I should point out I am always figuring out stories in anything I watch/play/read, its just who I am so take that how you will. I get my enjoyment in stories by the smaller surprises like this story in how it presented its story on such cool scale and style.I could go on about this game being great and how it just took me by surprise but I will leave this here. Love this game and so ready for the second. I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun, engaging, light-hearted, adventure game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I have ever written for a game, and that should say something. This game singlehandedly made me reconsider how muhc content I demand for a $60 game. On paper, it isn't advertising much. It's a linear story campaign with various lore and collectible items and outfits to pick up throughout the levels. I would say it's not unlike uncharted in terms of traversal, environments, and puzzling. That said, it is so, so much more than what's on the tin. If you like the MCU Guardians, you will forget about the, by the time you're finished with this version of them. This game has so much love and heart poured into every aspect of it, and it shows. From the consistently evolving gameplay, to the pretty much constant new dialogue between characters, to the gorgeously detailed horizons, to the intimate, shockingly emotionally intelligent moments between characters, this game takes the best aspects of the Guardians of the Galaxy and gives you nothing else for about 20-25 hours worth of story. I went into it with relatively low expectations, and I came out of it with my new favorite superhero game.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an entertaining game, with a fair amount of unique game play mechanics. The graphics are also outstanding, with immense attention to detail nearly everywhere you look. The game is very well optimized - I was quite surprised at that considering the level of graphical fidelity. The combat is fun at times, but gets repetitive after a while.The game has the feel of the first Guardians of the Galaxy movie, down to the ambient hues, colors, and glowing internal lighting on everything that we saw in the film. It also has a ton of the same humor as well as the awesome music. The characters in the game are all vaguely rendered to the cast from the 2014 movie, with Rocket and Groot being the only ones that are near exact, and you can find the 2014 movie costumes to apply to the whole crew to make them look similar to the first movie.I did run into a few bugs, and crash to desktop issues occasionally, but overall I was able to work past them. I also found a small number of the fights to be kind of lame, and overly difficult for no reason, mainly due to not having enough feedback on what needed to be done to stop the infinite loops of enemies being spawned.The game has a lot of the clunkyness from Tomb Raider, or Assassins creed due to the engine being used, and there are a lot of quick-time events that are a little annoying at times, but I got passed it all. If you liked the movies, you'll like the game as it is very much another story out of that series.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not expected to get a guardians of the galaxy game that gives me the same feeling as watching the 2 mcu movies. I absolutley adore these movies for how lighthearted but emotionally rich they are.Filled with colorful and creative designs, interesting deep characters and a fun story to go on a ride with. And thats exactly what you get here but in a freaking game!I have almost zero connection to the comics and got introduced to the guardians via the mcu where i instantly fell in love with them.When i first saw the trailer for this game i was a bit dissapointed for the characters not having the likenesses of the actors of their mcu counterparts. To be completley honest this was a big downer for me. So big even that i was considering not buying the game at all at first.But Im very happy to say that this really didnt matter. What makes the guardians so great is their relationship to each other and their character development throughout their journey. They often fight but in the end realize that they are family and will be there for each other.The voiceactors are only intensifying this by doing a very good job with carrying emotion. Often i found myself sobbing or laughing out loud because it was just so believeable and well written dialog. All this is underlined with great music fromt he 80's. are beautiful. I have cranked up all settings to the maximum and its just gorgeous to look at.The colorful and creative looking world really shines in those graphics. The levels you visit on different worlds are so well designed you feel like you are really exploring otherworldy planets and regions. Nowhere was one of my highlights personally. is very good. The only times i somtimes encountered microstutters was when tranistioning between scenes which happend maybe 4-5 times in 20 hours. All in all a very well optimized game. is good. It very much feels like a guardians story for all i can say. The journey makes the story great even. There was one moment where i was utterly stunned by the massive balls the devs had to pull this up. You will get to that point and you will feel the same way as i did.Especially in todays gaminglandscape where most bigger Developerstudios like to go save and dont expect too much from you this really suprised me. I appreciate that a lot! are fun.At first i was thinking its a shame that you only control Peter directly and that there is no coop even. But with that compromise you will soon see the benefits and how it is designed to work that way.You will have to command your teammates to help you out with for example cracked walls for drax to break down or too far to jump pits for Groot to make a wooden bridge over to uncover secret paths that lead you to journal entries and outfits for the guardians.The same goes for the combat. You unlock 1-4 abilites throughout the game which look and feel awesome. Steam achievements are very fun to do because of that.Im so sad my journey with this game is over. I loved every second of it. I hope so ever dearly that there will be a second guardians of the galaxy game.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game completely blind. My entire knowledge of Guardians of the Galaxy was that there's a talking tree and some weird raccoon thing. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best and source faithful comic book games that I have played. Absolutely fantastic and highly recommended.The graphics are fantastic.The story is brilliant. The script, voice acting and personalities are all superb.My only complaint is the game becomes buggy the further along towards the end. I twice had to restart the game due to getting stuck inside of terrain. Fortunately, saving and restarting/loading from the save puts the character in a safe location, so nothing is really lost. I have had only one crash to the desktop, but multiple sound bugs in the later part of the game. The game was bug free until nearing the 75 percent complete mark. At such point, I even had some graphical lighting issues, in which the final part of the game went pitch black and I lost the fight. Losing has no real impact fortunately, so it was not much of a frustration. The lighting was fine in the second attempt. The soundtrack is excellent, as is the world interactions and interactions to those interactions. There are a lot of layers of awesome throughout this game. Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a mostly trouble free and highly recommended gaming experience, that stays true to the comic books and is highly enjoyable. I will be playing another run through and enjoying 100 percenting the achievements of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great linear action game. So much fun. It really reminds me of games of old that we don't really get anymore, linear action games that didn't take themselves so seriously with a banging soundtrack and fun stories. I never thought the GotG IP would be used so well in a game, and I thought the best we’d ever get is the Telltale game. I was wrong.The story, characters, dialogue, locations and cutscenes are all much better than I expected. I was hooked from start to finish. The game is paced really well, no section overstays its welcome and the game constantly keeps things fresh in terms of story and locations.Performance and PC port wise impressions overall are positive. The game runs well with smooth framerate and frametimes outside one or two small moments, and has no major issues outside a couple moments where I had to reload the last checkpoint as progression was blocked due to game bugs. However, the game does suffer from some shader cache compilation stutter. It’s obvious the stutter is related to shader cache as if a chapter is replayed, the stutter is completely gone. A shame because with a linear game like this, I’m not going to be replaying chapters. Luckily the stutter is not too bad or constant, i’ve seen much worse in other games, but it’s there.The game visually is stunning and on a 2080 Super at max settings, no ray tracing, and native 1440p, I quickly noticed I could not maintain 60fps at all times. This doesn’t mean poor optimisation in this case though. It makes sense, the game is one of the better looking games available today, even without ray tracing. But there is a solution, DLSS. The DLSS in this game is the best implementation I have seen so far. It’s almost impossible to tell the difference between native 1440p and DLSS Quality. In other games with DLSS, there are issues, such as ghosting, trails, or losing too much detail/quality, to the point where I can’t use it, but not in this game. I played with DLSS on for practically the entire game which allowed me to maintain 60fps. I have to seriously praise the developers for how much obvious care was placed into the DLSS implementation here.It’s sad that this game apparently didn’t sell well. I really hope the devs get a chance at a sequel. One where they get to build a better and deeper combat system, as that’s the only real thing that needs improving with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being named after the team, you spend the entirety of this roughly 18-hour campaign playing as Peter Quill, AKA Star-Lord. That was a surprising choice to me, but it’s one that ends up working very well for the story that’s being told. The main plot is basically exactly what you’d expect: a cosmic comic book adventure about the Guardians trying to get out of debt, learning to work together, and maybe saving the galaxy along the way – but it’s framed by events that are much more personal to Peter. The result is an engaging story that balances its constant barrage of spectacle and banter with some genuinely heartfelt moments, for both Peter and the rest of the crew: Gamora, Drax, Rocket, and Groot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is mediocre. If you are a fan of the franchise, then you will likely enjoy this game and its story. However, * The battles tend to be tedious.* The puzzles are sometimes confusing at first, but in the end straight forward.* The NIS are unskippable, even though you may have seen them before. This makes any death hugely time consuming and frustrating* this brings you to the additional issue when you die, the load time can be quite long too.* there is a tendency to have multiple game play systems at different times - although this isn't necessarily a 'no-no', it doesn't help solidify what the game is trying to be. Is it a dog-fight flight sim? FPS? TPS? Puzzle? Dialog selection? Team game?* playing with keyboard and mouse is not great (I prefer this to controllers generally)- it is clearly implemented for a controller first. e.g. I found flying or dog fighting with a mouse almost impossible, but the controller was simple - that should not be the case. And so I had to switch to the controller for a couple of game sequences. So what was good about the game?* the voice acting was well done* the models, faces and expressions were excellent* the music was fun* the rendering (RTX especially) great* the environments were very detailed and alive feeling.* the story was somewhat interesting (I didn't expect much of one)So did I have fun? Yes. If I could rate it more finely, probably 3/5. I only would play it once out of vague curiosity. Is it worth it? No.
