_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion  offers the best version of the guardians to date.  During the story you get to know each guardian, while learning about their past trauma. The themes of "Healing" and "Hope" play a huge part in the narrative. The humor you would expect from a Guardians of the Galaxy-experience is also smashed into the cooking pot, really well!  Eidos Montréal nailed the balance between all of those ingredients, that contribute to a story that you feel invested in! You also get to choose between dialogue options, which will trigger some "Telltale-like" pop-ups informing you, that the choices you made, will have some impact later in the game. Some characters may like or dislike you during the game here and there, depending on the choices you made! Being able to talk to your crew on the Milano (your ship) adds to the feeling that this is a journey, that you take a part in, releasing some "Mass Effect Lite"-vibes (which is agood thing!).While playing the game you can feel care and love to detail the team put into this game! You just feel happy and emotionally invested for the whole duration. The game is like a very long, well-paced, playable Marvel movie with all the spectacle you would expect: You meet many (new interpretations) of Marvel characters. Each actor does a great performance. The facial-mocap quality and emotional range the cast delivers are of the highest standard!The visuals looks absolutely stunning, you visit many unique and very beautiful planets and places. All the environments add a lot of variety to the experience. For example, you start your journey in the Quarantine zone, A place that contains the remains of the galactic war. The broken shipwrecks are held together by some beautiful looking pink "popcorn-goo" during another mission you travel to a cyberpunk-like city. There are lots of planets and each one is rich. full of details and little side areas to explore! ...What I am trying to say: If you like bright colors, fancy landscapes and visual variety and are in general a graphics fetishist, you will get aroused for sure.The game is well paced: Switching between exploration, light puzzles and combat-sections. Sadly you only play as Starlord during this game, while being able to use unlockable abilities of your allies to attack the different weaknesses of your enemies (basically a bit like Mass Effect again). The combat is definetly the weakest part of the game, but still very enjoyable. If you are a fan of spectecular boss-fights, this game will deliver you that! The light puzzle elements, exploration and also some space battles are a true joy! I got never bored playing the game.Sound and music make up half of the experience of a game, in my opinion. Most of us associate Peter Quill with his walkman and his love for music form the 80s. That is exactly what you get! The selection of licensed music is huge! You got all the bangers you expect to be there. The sound effects during the gameplay are also well implemented and believable. All underlined by a great soundtrack which delivers a theme that will be stuck in your head! A perfect audio-mix!

_childDocuments_.review: The story is great, way more fun than the MCU movies, imo. Doesn't follow the MCU plotline at all, it's more an amalgam of comic book plots.The combat is fun mostly. Enemies tend to be bullet sponges, which means you're relying entirely on the guardian combos and special abilities to clear out enemies(including Star Lord's own specials). Combat can be really hectic so it isn't uncommon to miss combo or finisher prompts simply by trying not to die.I'm uncertain about the Huddle mechanic. It's actually a nice break from combat when you're being overwhelmed, giving you a chance to breath, but it can break your own flow. Having to make a choice during this isn't difficult, just adds a little bit of annoyance to it. However, I absolutely love that it huddles switch from regular combat music to one of Peter's tracks. There's just something amazing about slaughtering hordes of enemies to Rick Astley's Never Gonna Give You Up or other similar songs. Just try and picture that. You're surrounded by a horde of enemies, feeling overwhelmed, so you huddle up. Guardians get together, break, and you hear that familiar intro... "We're no strangers to love..." as you order Rocket to set off an explosion.If you have no interest in the comic books or don't have the patience for the combat, this game is not going to be fun for you. But if you do have that patience, you'll enjoy every moment of the game. I just wish it were longer. On the bright side, it does have a New Game+ option.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's got it all. If you're looking for what it delivers then you will love it. So what does it deliver? A really good, mostly linear, story with amazing characters. A good but not amazing combat system that really emphasizes teamwork. and spectacular visuals (cannot emphasize this enough). The plot itself isn't breathtaking or anything but it is good. But all the characters (mainly talking about the guardians themselves, but there are some other standouts as well) are incredibly well-written and well-acted. They each have a fulfilling arc that also interweaves with the arc of the team as a whole. Aside from that, the team members feel very true to their source material. if you know the guardians from the films, you will feel very familiar with their characterization. But their stories differ from the movies. So it doesn't feel like a rehash. The world is also very realized, and a lot more comic-book whacky than what you might be familiar with. The game does not apologize at all for its comic book roots. There's a lot of world-building. But its often in the background so it doesn't get in the way.Aside from the story, it is a visually stunning game. The environments in particular are truly some of the best ♥♥♥♥ in any game ever. I struggle to come up with examples on the same levels. Maybe you could say it's on par with Elden Ring, but honestly I think this is better.As for the general gameplay. It's probably the weakest part of the package. Not to say it's bad, it's actually really enjoyable. The gameplay comprises two main modes. One where you explore, find upgrade materials, talk with your teammates, and solve puzzles using your team's various abilities. There are also unlockable costumes that you can find. These sections are fairly linear, with some secrets here and there. The second mode is combat. The combat is very team-oriented. The player (star-lord) really isn't very formidable by himself. Your main source of power are the other guardians. You will spend most of combat ordering them to activate abilities that combo in different ways. That's not to say that you can't do anything. You can do a lot of crowd-control and can deal with grunts fairly effectively.In conclusion. I believe that you should play this game if you enjoy kinda whacky sci fi storytelling with really good characterization and truly best-in-class presentation, and good combat that really emphasizes teamwork.

_childDocuments_.review: After that huge flarkin' mess called "Marvel's Avengers", Eidos-Montréal/Square Enix finally redeemed themselves and extracted the best of Marvel's IP forging this masterpiece. Mark my words, in a few years people will BEG for a sequel, here's the breakdown:- Great mix alternating all  members during combat & puzzles;- Above the average good looking graphics and level design;- Certified comedy gold, not pushing every time to be fun but naturally dropping fun-bombs along the storyline dialogs;- Campaign length is neither too short nor too long (~20 hours);- Very creative and such steady-flow out-of-fillers narrative;...and the icing on the cake: SOUNDTRACKHoly s♥♥t, I FLARKIN' loved this game's soundtrack, not only because the 80's licensed good stuff but in fact they recorded/wrote an 80's heavy metal album for this game and it's not those average game-type albums you listen once in a while, I'm flarkin' revisiting this album each day after beating the game because the music is just too good. _childDocuments_.review: A really pleasant surprise. I picked this up for half off on the SE publisher sale after reading some reviews. Very well written story. Remarkably funny. I can't remember the last game I audibly laughed at multiple times.Charming cast of characters.Excellent character animations and voice work. Beautiful graphics and solid performance.The only real thing that holds it back is combat being kinda "eh." It's not bad, but it certainly doesn't stand on its own. The squad powers are cool but once I had them all unlocked the best strategy was generally to just smash all the biggest AOE buttons on cooldown, occasionally having Gamora or Drax use their single target abilities on a sturdier guy. I'm fine with it though, it moved along fairly quickly and was fun enough that I never dreaded combat or just wanted a combat section to be over.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like an extremely polished release, nothing like Marvel's Avengers got. This is the real deal here, no need to wait for months until things get fixed. Just jump right in and you'll get your money's worth. No co-op of course, it's a singleplayer game.Edit: Seems my optimism was way premature, the game does have difficulty running with GPU's of recommended spec & lower. I recommend you have at least GTX 1080 or newer for the game, preferably something newer. My RX6800 runs it just fine when I have the proper drivers for it.Also since a lot of people are struggling with the QTE's in the game, these can just be switched off entirely in the accessibility options of the game. I did that for myself too since I'm a bit impaired and not good with these things.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for September 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 1st, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.This is how to do a Marvel game. Guardians of the Galaxy was a movie I thought would be Marvel’s first flop. I was wrong. The thing is the Guardians of the Galaxy Marvel chose are likable, interesting characters, with a lot of great dynamics between the characters that allow them to have interesting stories. Rather than going for the same actors in the movies, this is a different tale, a unique take, and a new look, but it all works. The story is enjoyable; the characters banter pretty effectively, there’s a couple of fresh mechanics like the Huddle up, and the pacing is just right. I even love how the boss is dealt with at the end of the first chapter. Still, I think if you’re not already a Guardians of the Galaxy fan, this might not change your mind. The movie isn’t required viewing but does help set up the dynamics of the group faster, though it is well told here. The gameplay is solid, but also it’s probably not going to be the deepest experience. Honestly, the biggest problem is Square said this wasn’t a great seller after everyone went crazy about it, so this is it. Also, for some reason, sometimes the button prompts were the Playstation version and sometimes they were the Xbox version, very strange, though I am using an 8bitdo Ultimate, so maybe that’s confusing it.Pick this up if you like Marvel Movies, superheroes, sci-fi, humor, or interesting environments. This won’t be for everyone, but if you’re even slightly interested, I would recommend this one. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Guardians of the Galaxy is an absolutely phenomenal game. It's so much better than the movies, funny, genuine, and heartfelt, with some of the most jaw-droppingly beautiful art design and visuals I've ever seen in a game, with more than enough alternative outfits and the like to offer an incentive to explore the linear levels. I loved practically every second of this game, I felt with the characters and their excellently executed arcs, I felt with them and their struggles and redemptions, it was all so well done, with heart and soul poured into the story and world, making it an easy Game of the Year contender in my book. I strongly recommend this game if you care at all about storytelling and breathtaking worlds, whether you're a fan of Marvel or not, hell I'm not either, but this game was still a joy to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game. The first part (first story?) was a bit boring but once the game moved on to the main story it suddenly started getting good. I agree with a lot of people commenting that the fighting in this game was a bit lame. It felt like the same combat each time but with different skins for the enemies. Where this game shines is with the banter between the main characters. I would often just stop moving so I could just listen to the talk, laugh or insulting each other and didn't want to accidentally cut it short as I was enjoying them so much. The comedy on this game was very well done and found myself laughing out loud and sharing the jokes with my brother later on. You get choices here and there that mildly changes parts of the game an example being you can get a key card to avoid doing a handful of puzzles later on. I completed the game in 24.5 Hours and just Googled the other options which only took an hour to watch the videos. Some people might want to replay but I just have a big bad log of games id rather get through instead. Over all 92/100!! Must get!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is what happens when big publishers back off, and let artists ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cook.I'm going to list the flaws below, but just know that they are tiny specks of sand, in an otherwise glorious cake.Cons:• No manual saves and save slots. This is actually very relivant, because while the autosave and checkpoint system both do a good job, there are times you can accidentally advance the story too fast, or miss content because you stumbled into the wrong path.• Mandatory Cutscenes. As in, moments of the game where you are pseudo in control but are essentially just cut-scenes. They're semi-rare, about one every two "Chapters" but they can't be skipped, so they make replaying the game a chore.• Quick time events. Seriously, we're still doing this? Random QTE's spoil a lot of moments, and are blatently inserted to hammer home a theme that you would have to be blind to have missed (Peter Quill is not a super anything, and is dependant on his team, so he constantly almost dies to keep up with them, but he's the dad/soul of the team. That's it that's the entire reason there are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ QTE's in the game).• Adam Warlock is in the gamePros:• Solid, if simple, combat. It pretends to be a DMC style game but very easy, it's really not. The combat is not taxing, it's just about status and cooldown management, but it's still engaging, and it's quick, so you won't begrudge it.• Amazing writing. Now I don't mean story plot writing, I mean character writing. All the actual characters of the story are multi-layered and fun to experience, even if only briefly for the cameos (except ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Adam Warlock, who the game mocks for the atrocious Gary Stu he is).• Good score. The music is pretty fun, not all the licensed classics fit, but none of them are bad. It was a bad choice of what can end up playing in combat, because while the MCU films do work scores you wouldn't expect in fluidly, the game can't replicate that my just tossing them into combat. Still, they're good tracks.• Decent, honest, and respectable practices. No micro-transactions for skins, they're all in the world for you to find, along with bonus dialogue. It's so refreshing to go back to a time of game content actually being in the game, without paying extra. For nothing else, the game needs bonus points, for having been made by artists, that understood what a game needs.• ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heart, actual characterisation that isn't cramming itself down your throat, or full of dated memes. This isn't the MCU guardian's, it's a blend of what's worked over all forms of the characters, and it deals with its themes in an adult way. Quickly, and a little messily, but still giving the arcs of every character respect, and not ending everything with a maguffin or the power of freindship. I mean, well, the power of friendship is a thing, but in a real sense, of friends helping one another, and being better together. No combined friendship laser beams here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off slow but it keeps coming and does a really great job after the first chapter or so. _childDocuments_.review: Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy is a game that some people surely will miss this year, probably thinking it’s just another bad or poor Marvel game adaptation riddled with MTX or skins to buy, but that is not the case here in GOTG.This is a game from , creators of Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, and this game is in fact a pure single player experience, with none of the micro-transaction crap and nonsense. It uses, in fact, the same Dawn Engine we saw in Mankind Divided or, at least, It is based on it.The PC port has been done in collaboration with d3t, which recently also did the Alan Wake Remaster, and I think they have done a decent job, considering this is not a very common engine to see out there.There are different  in the game, but you have to , by playing the game of course. Yeah, you know, single player games? They exist, and many are in fact, good games, like GOTG here.Let’s now talk PC port and some tech numbers and specs: on my  and  this game performs quite well, way over 60 FPS even at 1620 DSR resolution. My native resolution is 1080p but, at that resolution, the game is quite CPU bound and, if you want to get over 100 FPS, you’re going to need a very fast CPU. For most people with CPUs similar to mine, increasing the resolution and, if supported, enabling Raytraced Reflections, will be a much better option to keep that GPU working as it should.In my case, 1620p DSR Downsampling, Ultra Settings and with RT set to Ultra (including Transparent Raytraced Reflections), the frame-rates are usually above 70, sometimes even 80-90’ish, depending on the area.The game does make good use of  to provide excellent temporal stabilization to the image and, even if you prefer gaming at lower resolutions, I suggest enabling DLSS at Quality mode at least, because it sure does look better than Temporal Anti-Aliasing in this game. Of course, at higher resolutions, DLSS is an invaluable tool to keep 60 FPS or more, and a nice looking image, without compromising much on Graphics Settings.Due to being quite CPU limited unless we play at high resolutions and with Raytracing, lowering graphics settings quite often does not provide enough scaling to gain big performance chunks on the FPS, so it’s best to choose the highest possible resolution and Settings that provide us with at least 60 FPS.Moving on, to the actual game, and its : I think it’s great, it has quite a few surprises and twists, and the characters are so fun in this game, I mean...they’re the Gardeners of the Galaxy! Wait…yeah, they are : )If you only know the Guardians from the MCU movies…you’ll find something familiar in this game, but if you also know them from the comics and other media, yeah, there’s a lot here to enjoy as well. I think the actors did such a good job, so congratulations to all of them, I had a lot of fun with their banter and dialogue choices and all the craziness (I played in English). is pretty straightforward, it feels a bit familiar if you’ve played Mass Effect games, in a way, but not quite, and to me the  itself is the weakest aspect of the game, it’s not bad but also not the best I’ve seen in an action / adventure game; it can be fun, but I often felt it could’ve been a bit more.The  in this game is top notch, the different worlds and locations we visit feel pretty unique and indeed something I’d expect to see in anything related to the Guardians, and I often had to stop and activate the handy Photo Mode and take lots of pictures, sometimes even in combat.The  in this game is great, of course it’s full with some of the greatest hits of the 80’s and therefore, it’s copyrighted, but the game has a “Streamer Mode” that disables all those tracks and instead uses the, also amazing, regular game soundtrack.But of course, when you play the game with the full soundtrack it feels truly epic, like it couldn’t be otherwise.I really liked this game, and it left me wanting more, there’s potential for more, for sure. It’s not really a short game, just an average length, I probably played around 25-30 hours, but I spent a lot of time in Photo Mode and testing / doing benchmarks too, but if you take your time and look for all the collectibles and stuff, yeah, expect around 15-20 hours for sure.I hope we get more single player games like this, and more people give this game a chance, I think it deserves it. Seriously, play this game, it's really fun and well done.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and great Marvel adventure. Expect a great "Uncharted like" adventure and a lot of flarcking jokes!To be honest, I prefer this to the movie 2014 version. The best part of this game is that people at Eidos-Montréal NAILED character interaction and humor. I should not forget to mention AMAZING visual direction, great animation quality (facial animations in cutscenes are great!), and that you can control some of the outcomes via the dialogs. This game also features a lot of accessibility features.The downsides are acceptable combat system (compared to the rest of the game, this feels like the weakest part of it), minor rendering issues (the game looks good, but can be buggy), and poor UI resolution on high-resolution screens (I played at 2K screen and the UI was blurry), also, gameplay bugs, be ready to restart from the checkpoints multiple times.Also, I'd like to note the Star-Lord Band - a virtual group that was "created" just for this game, it has a Metallica vibe and is very 80s. It has more tracks than SAMURAI from Cyberpunk 2077. Check it out on Spotify!It feels like this game was made by people who love what they do and care about their characters. Thank you Eidos-Montréal for this amazing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are gorgeous and you often just stop to admire the surroundings. Even though the path before you is linear you can search around and find collectibles or completely different path toward your goal. The fights are hectic, crazy and you can lose your head easily, but they are also great fun and fill you with a lot of adrenaline. You are pretty safe on your travels thanks to frequent checkpoints. Falling over the edge won't kill you, just immediately respawn on the spot - even during a battle! The soundtrack is excellent and when the songs from the '80s start you wish for the fights to never end. :D Happy to hear some of my favorites on the tape. <3All of the characters are greatly written and I loved the chemistry between the Guardians. I am familiar only with the movies but I quite liked their in-game portrayal (they say it’s closer to the comics). I find this Drax far better than in the movies actually (loved his war choral and the fact that he then sang it at every opportunity he got, priceless). The voice actors do a perfect job and bring all of the characters to life. It's a joy to listen to their bickering. xDThe atmosphere changes rapidly with the story progression. In one moment it can be funny, relaxed, friendly and in the next moment, it becomes serious, heavy, dark… you name it. The pace of the game is quick, so are these changes and you are kept in a sweet tension of what’s coming next. Some moments were rather emotional.The game isn't perfect of course.▶ I stumbled upon a few bugs - I got stuck and had to reload a checkpoint (which was rare, you usually get respawned), my crew disappeared although the talks continued (had to reload), and it crashed on me once (I think it was caused by my especially frantic clicking during a heated battle).▶ The fights are very hectic and one can become lost in what is the goal. Also, sometimes you can activate the Huddle ('80s songs) just before the fight ends thus not enjoying the music enough.▶ The talks can be interrupted in the middle by anything you do and you can't pretty much prevent it - you stop to listen, maybe it would be a good idea to survey the surroundings with your visor, bump!, they start commenting on that… it can be anything. Not really a problem, I just don't like it when it works this way (my OCD kicking in).▶ When you read in your journal there is no music, just silence - in my opinion the biggest oversight when we consider the excellent soundtrack we have at our disposal.▶ The game is linear so we can't visit or re-visit points of interest on our own.▶ Sometimes I got a little lost in the lore.But all of this is unimportant in the light of great characters, captivating story, beautiful visuals, and legendary music! You don't need to be a fan of the  franchise to enjoy the game (but if you already are you will enjoy it even more for sure), so I can safely recommend it to everyone! Just beware that they really don't shut their mouths. xDI wouldn't mind getting on another adventure with these rascals. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Guardians of the Galaxy took me by a surprise, initially I was not even planning to play the game as its reveal during E3 looked rather bland and when combined with the fact it was being made by the same studio partially responsible for the GAAS abomination that is the Avengers it certainly didn't inspire much of confidence that it would be any better. However after the release I read a lot of positive impressions and in general the word of mouth seemed to point to that this was indeed a game worth trying - so I did and I'm very glad that I did.In many ways GotG feels like the developers took some inspiration from Mass Effect and Uncharted games, then mixed in some new ideas to create an ability focused linear action game. One that has a surprisingly heavy focus on story, characters and dialogue, especially the latter comes very apparent in the massive amount of unique party banter - in fact there is so much talk between party members that sometimes it feels like it never really pauses. Fortunately the dialogue is well written and voice cast performance is excellent across the board with a couple particularly stand out performances.During the course of the story you also get to make some choices, some of which resolve instantly while others pay off (or come back to haunt you) several hours later. Which I found to be a fun little extra that allows you to have a small degree of control of over how Star-Lord acts as a character as well as having some influence over how certain things play out during the narrative,At a very basic level, the gameplay structure can be roughly summed up in to visiting a location, followed by an intermission section on your ship where you have some optional dialogue with your team and then repeat. Locations themselves have an impressive amount of environmental variety, even if for the most part the levels are linear with occasional dead ends and looping paths you can "explore" to collect some additional costumes as well as currency you use to unlock perks.So what about the parts that aren't good then?Combat is a mixed bag, not only it lacks polish in terms of how responsive it feels and how the animations sync up but it also lacks the potential for any complexity as the system is built around spectacle and ability usage. While this gives you a flashy combat that sells the illusion of working as a team and as the leader of the team, it comes with a trade-off where the combat itself is very basic.Star-Lord at a core is a ranged combat character, you have one button melee attack/combo that changes based on enemy you fight but you spend majority of your time using your guns and abilities. In addition to that you also command the ability usage of your team members, along with some contextual team member actions - for some reason the combat made me think of playing extremely streamlined version of Mass Effect combat where the cover system and ability synergy has been replaced with spectacle.Another negative aspect is the lack of polish, while I did not experience anything game breaking there were a plethora of small bugs and glitches. These range from annoying things like enemies not removing their cutscene/spawn immortality properly, button prompts not registering during some sequences, dialogue cutting off to smaller things like npcs standing on tables, huge amount of clipping, people walking through doors, rough scene transitions, animations not syncing up quite right. Combine that with things like poor pacing of dialogue where walking at a normal speed (and sometimes even taking time to explore) can result in you hitting the trigger for next dialogue/cutscene before the ongoing one ends - it gave me an impression that the game could have used a tiny bit more time to iron at least the most noticeable of these issues.That being said, what I expected was a game with fun combat along with a mediocre to poor story, what I got instead is a game that has fairly mediocre combat with some fun encounters but is largely carried by its compelling characters, very enjoyable story and a great soundtrack that combines some original tracks along with licensed hits from the 80s. If you're a fan of linear/cinematic action games, I'd absolutely recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely hate super hero movies and the Marvel brand in general but was strongly recommended this game and am extremely glad I gave it a shot. Guardians of the Galaxy is easily one of the most entertaining single player games I have played in a long time full of moments you will remember and laugh at. On top of that, there's plenty of  licensed songs that will leave you pretty surprised hearing legally in a video game. _childDocuments_.review: - It's good.- Fairly well optimized. Was able to run this at 1440p on ultra everything including raytracing. Capped my frames at 72 to remove stutter (there is some of that here) and it was smooth sailing from there. My 1% was in the high 40s with averages at the cap. Rig is a RTX 2080s / Ryzen 9 3900x / 32gb 3200 Ram / Win 10- Graphically this is a really nice early show piece for this generation. One of the best lookers on the market so far, and the facial animations are excellent, though there are some rough moments during side stuff. I'm assuming it was done by outsourced teams, and if I'm correct, it shows.- The writing is next level, and the amount of it is mind boggling.- Combat is fairly simple and even on the hardest difficulty isn't much of a challenge. The upgrade system is basic and if removed nothing would be lost. I didn't play through this twice for it's combat or even mechanics. The spectacle and writing kept me coming back. In a way, it's peak walking simulator, and I mean that in the best possible way.- 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: ---Marvel's Guardians of the Narcolepsy!... or SERIOUSLY?! "OVERWHELMINGLY POSITIVE"?!?!?! WTF IS WRONG WITH YOUR BRAINS?!?!?!---Trouble sleeping? Play this game. "Play" being loosely used here - more like, "passively walk around for 80% of the game wondering why all the characters look and sound like Chinese knock-offs of the originals... interspersed with the incredibly gripping ducking or squeezing through tight spaces simulator sections (which are HILARIOUSLY frequent, another 10%)... and finally, slip into unconsciousness with some of the most tedious combat I've ever seen for the final 10%".It's not even got a charming level of jank... it's just an annoyingly beautiful yet boring slog of a game - I only had the energy left to write this review because I COULDN'T BELIEVE it was rated as "Overwhelmingly positive"?!?!.... Could one of you please send me some of whatever you've all been smoking, as whatever it is, clearly has the power to break spacetime and reality itself!THE GOOD- Graphics are beautiful. A truly fantastic looking game. A turd rolled in the finest of glitter!- A Destiny-like smoothness to the mind-numbingly boring combat and walking simulator sections.- Voice acting is pretty good for some of the characters. Others again, feeling like a strange rip-off of the originals.- 3 out of 785 jokes are chuckle out-loud.- Nice interior details to some of the areas that you'll be fighti- oh sorry... walking* through.THE BAD- Combat is puddle-deep at best. Mastering the quick reload is about it. Other than that, just endlessly holding the pea-shooter RT button, whilst spamming your other party members' attacks make up EVERY SINGLE FIGHT.- You ONLY get to play as Star Lord. A Star Lord that is apparently made of lead and can't fly using his rocket boots; only managing to jump 3ft in the air whilst looking like you've just sh*t yourself. No playing as Groot?! WTF?!?!- 782 out of 785 jokes are so middle-of-the-road and predictable, that it becomes an extremely light form of torture.- Some of the cut scenes and story events are completely moronic. There's one bit when Quill gets stuck with everyone in a kind of quicksand... He needs to save Rocket from being the first to drown, and for some ridiculous reason... his "stress" (or something?!)... forces his two pistols to magically turn into into a freeze ray gun(?!?!?!?!).... so he can freeze the quick sand and free Rocket. Sound r*tarded? Yeah, it was.- Puzzles that someone in a comatose state would find "a bit too easy".- Upgrades so dull, I found myself dreading my next level up. A weird feeling I haven't felt before. Well... not "levelling up", but reaching the next hilariously and randomly placed human workbenches in the middle of a goo planet or something, I guess.- Auto-aim is a necessary evil for damage; so you don't even have to bother with AIMING your ONE weapon in the whole game.  - The INCESSANT banter. F*ck me, do they never shut up! I don't know why, but the way Rocket says "Quill" started really annoying me - giving me a weird instinctual huff and grinding of the teeth eventually, every time he said it. - QTEs that clothes line the pacing in parts, but are admittedly very funny because of their baffling timing and subsequent death scenes from not being ready (funniest bits).FAVOURITE MOMENT OF MEDIOCRITY Very near the start, there was a hilariously "on-rails" feeling I got; a section where you "fly" your ship through an asteroid field. It's completely impossible to die. You can literally never touch your controller, and you'll be fine. This is the moment when I realised, I was in for some serious hand-holding tedium. CONCLUSIONIf you can't get any meds for your insomnia, seriously give this a go. My faith in any Steam review score has now been shaken to the core, after seeing this as "Overwhelmingly Positive" (22 Oct 2024). "Overwhelmingly DULL" more-like... Jesus.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is an enjoyable single player adventure, filled with funny banter throughout. The game is certainly inspired from the MCU films, and that's definitely not a bad thing. The story itself spans multiple worlds, as well as flashbacks that allow the characters to grow on us. There are some feels and wholesome parts and realisations that all teams (and families) have their dysfunctions and quirks but have the potential to come together when they're needed most. However, I did find Rocket was quite annoying throughout the middle of the story but luckily he gets more tolerable towards the end. The action sequences are spaced between various cinematic and dialogue pieces. I was a bit surprised about the amount of cinematics, but they are well done and the visuals really shine. The gameplay itself is fairly simple, but responsive enough and does a good job of incorporating the entire team during battles. There are various character costumes to find throughout the game, with some throwbacks to the the films and comic books, allowing a nice but limited level of customisation. I had an enjoyable 20+ hour ride with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy the game because of it's association with the atrocious Marvel's Avengers game, I thought it would be similar in game play and in it's monetization but no, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is an amazing game. The game play is fantastic if a little bit on the easier side, I played on the hard difficulty and most common enemies stood no chance if I was properly using my teams abilities but zipping around the battlefield with the rocket boots and blasting enemies with the element blasters feels fantastic. The way you command the other guardians to use their abilities is a little bit jarring at first because it takes a second to open the menu, look for the ability you want to use and then tell them to use it, all while having to stop combat for yourself (no shooting while in the menu); this does get better as you memorize where each ability is in each menu, just takes some time to get used to. The only sore point on game play for me is the Milano. It feels awful on mouse and keyboard, but it might be better on controller, plus you only manually fly the Milano 3 or 4 times.There are a number of weird bugs that may require a restart from check point or a reboot from time to time. At one point Drax got stuck T posing on a barrel I told him to throw, nothing I did could get him out of it and for some reason the elevator we needed to use wouldn't move because of it. At one point you can go to a museum and read about a bunch of legendary in-universe artifacts, but one of the text boxes got stuck on my screen so whenever I tried to read something it would pop up instead.The star of the game is the voice acting and writing for sure. I honestly believe that this incarnation of the Guardians of the Galaxy is miles better than the movie; The characters are witty but believable. At one point I needed to step away from my computer before a mission so the crew was just hanging out in the hangar on the Milano and for almost 15 minutes the crew was just organically talking to each other about the previous mission and the next and none of the dialogue repeated; it was incredible. The dialogue is so amazing that one of my complaints is that it is too easy to interrupt and cancel conversations and dialogue accidentally and it's so unfortunate.I would give Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy a solid 8/10 with the only loss of points being the bugs.This game is an amazing adventure and I would love a sequel by the same team.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for the game for several reasons. I had high expectations for character banter among the group and the music selection. After completing the first chapter, I am NOT disappointed. Game will not be for everyone, its basically a cinematic action movie. The combat controls will be smoother using a game pad than a M&K. Will need to plug mine in next time.-- Edit --Finished 1st play through at 22 hrs or so. Dialogue and banter between the team was one of the things I enjoyed and was excited for and it continued thru the whole game. It changed as the game progressed and characters developed. I ensured to talk to everyone on the team whenever possible and hung around sections to hear everything before continuing which led to higher time played for 1st completion.I GREATLY enjoyed the game and would recommend it to anyone looking for a single player experience who is a fan of GOTG. Though would caution those who dislike a ton of cutscenes and timed dialogue choices. There is QTE's but have ability to turn em off in menu and just have them always succeed(?).I enjoyed the story. There were times I thought I was nearing the end only to realize I was nowhere close to the end.Controls are definitely better with a controller. I did play through with M&K as controller was broken. Just rebound a few keys.Performance was decent while having graphics at high/very high with RTX/Nvidia features on.There were a few spots where performance dropped heavily. One was bad enough a game restart was needed to get out of 1 FPS slide show. Booted back in to normal performance.Occasionally dropped to 40 FPS in other sections but went back to normal upon leaving that level. Assuming it is the environment that was causing it.There are bugs. Appears some invisible walls are in certain areas they shouldn't be. I have only experienced it once but didn't impede my progress, just some bonus tech for upgrades which is plentiful. I finished with nearly 2.8k in supply mats of the 1st type at the end

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie; I had zero interest in this game due to a combination of disappointment at Eidos Montreal moving over to an Marvel game from Deus Ex (I was really hoping we'd get a new one), and general Marvel / MCU burnout. Guardians of the Galaxy are one of the few Marvel / superhero IPs I can usually enjoy, but even so the total saturation of super hero ~stuff~ in film and video games made the idea of jumping into yet another linear story based super hero game about as appealing as chewing glass.Fast forward to now and I'm pleasantly surprised, and happy to eat crow. I do feel the combat and pacing isn't quite there, like the combat systems and encounter design went through several iterations before they settled on what we got. It's not bad, and becomes a lot more enjoyable as you unlock new companion powers, but it does also feel it needs a couple more balance and polish passes to get it ~just right~.But really, it's the location variety, story, cast, and tone that elevate the whole experience. Some of the best writing in the medium in a long while, that manages to be genuinely laugh-out-loud funny without compromising character identities or regressing their entire personalities to punch-lines. Instead the entire cast, central and secondary, are fully formed and rich with distinct personalities, each taken on an earnest journey of growth and companionship. The banter is clever and witty, the relationships feel authentic, and the development of the crew emotionally earned through the scenarios and conflicts they find themselves in. Outstanding voice acting, too.I think as a whole it's a notch away from being a true gem, but what's in there is markedly better than I could have ever expected. Gorgeous, funny, and at its worst at least servicable in play, but more often than not still very fun in its own right. If you've been hungry for a linear, single player, story focused action adventure game, one built on a high budget with excellent production values, I think this is gonna scratch the itch. It's not my favourite game of the year (that's probably a tie between Pyschonauts 2 and Metroid Dread), but I can see why Guardians of the Galaxy is for some. It managed to both surprise and delight me, and make me quickly forget about my superhero burnout. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: So, here's the thing. This is a pretty solid Mass Effect knockoff, in a lot of ways. -Writing and story veer from B+ to A. Really enjoyed a lot of it, and the way it broke completely from movie canon was very welcome. The actors were good and really carried the story. -Combat is very uneven. This is where it most resembles Mass Effect, but also where it has no reasonable sense of scaling or pacing. This game, on easy, should be much easier, because it should be normal by now to have a "Story mode" for these games. Instead, it's kind of a pain in the ass, because you have to match the shield type to the attack and fall off a ledge a few times before any fight is over. The checkpoints are very forgiving, so you won't exactly throw your controller, but it just drags down the game. -Level design is also very uneven. You'll spend a lot of time in samey hallways playing "find the relatively inconsequential pickup" and it feels like filler. I don't really mind the guardian power puzzles, but it says something that the game improves quite a bit when basic puzzles get automated later on. -Mostly, the problem is incentives. The character/RPG development stuff is very flat, so you're never really pushed to think of combat or anything else as something that will give you options or make your characters develop in any meaningful way. So it's really just the story pushing you forward, and the rest of the mechanics getting in the way, even when it comes to telling the story (the timed dialog versus untimed dialog is a jarring disconnect, pick one and ideally leave an accessibility option for untimed because it's not my fault I spaced out during the cutscene). Anyway, the game is fine. We played it to completion, mostly because my kid wanted to see the rest of the story. But it's definitely padded with nonsense and filled with bad design choices, and it's a tribute to the writing and acting that it survives those things.

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa, this game came out of *Knowhere* and, as a massive Marvel fan, I was really excited to play it. Shout out to brother Jordan for gifting me this game. The strongest point of this game is the narrative. It feels like a Guardians comic, or film, either way it's dope. You've got appearances from many different loved, deadly, and iconic Marvel characters- some of which were completely unexpected. Additionally, the cinematography is dope, there are some shots which are completely unforgettable, partially because of the awesome soundtrack. Seriously, they did better with the music in this game than was done in the actual Guardians movies.The combat is interesting, and it took some time for it to grow on me. You play as Peter while your allies control themselves, however, you can command them to use 4 combat abilities, and while you do so the game goes into slo-mo. It's pretty challenging to choose the correct target, select the guardian you want to attack with, and then select the ability you want them to use, all by pressing the 1-4 keys in different orders. While doing this you can still be hit and need to be dodging incoming attacks. Overall, the combat is really easy and I died in combat once the entire game (playing on second hardest difficulty, not hardest), however, I did often find myself using abilities I didn't intend to use, or attacking with the wrong ally because I was rushing to give out orders without being attacked. Additionally, early on in the game there isn't a smooth transition from exploration into combat; it feels more like a JRPG encounter where you'll have an animation or cutscene, followed by a fight, then a rewards screen before heading back into exploration mode. I didn't like how this felt when I first started playing, but as the game goes on combat encounters start to feel more natural, which I really appreciated.The story took me about 15 hours to beat, and I found most of the hidden outfits, info, and objects during my playthrough, then was able to use chapter select and new game plus to quickly grab up what I had missed for the 100%. My biggest issue with the game was all the bugs I experienced. I had the game crash on me on three occasions, encountered a few bugs which required me to reload from the last checkpoint, a bug which had my cursor on the screen while playing, and a few other glitches. While they weren't super impactful because the game auto-saves so often, they were still frustrating and led to me taking a few breaks. Regardless, I had a great time with this game, and I'm sure anyone who enjoys the Guardians will- the developers really did the franchise well, and the voice actors had wonderful performances all around. It's certainly worth the price, but it would be a lot easier to endorse without the bugs in it.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews , but I feel like I had to. There is one major reason why I can't recommend this game: It's way too expensive for what it is. This should have never been a full priced game, not in the current state of it. It's not horrible, but it's not good neither.The GOOD: The game's humor, narration and overall character chemistry is on point. It really sucks you into the character, the jokes are great and the tone is spot on. Really, when it comes to mood and character - the game really nails it. BUTThe BAD: First off and most importantly: The battle mechanics suck. The action is extremely lackluster - your basic Run & Gun feel like an early 2000's action game, definitely not a 2021 post-God of War game. The enemies are ALL bullet sponges, even the most basic ones, to the point I went down from Hard to Normal difficulty not because I had trouble getting through the sequences - they were mostly braindead easy, but because the took WAAY too long, and it was just incredibly boring. It does get better as you unlock abilities, but these are so bland and straight-forward, there is never a real dilemma of - Which ability I could have used in this or that scenario, no real rock-paper-scissor elemets, it's all just either AOE or Single Target, and it's always really obvious which you should use. The problem is that while getting these abilities, especially at the first half of the game, it's just bad. The basic mechanics are just very poorly designed, and paying a triple A price for this level of gameplay was really a bummer and constantly irritated me (not because of the price mind you - because it just wasn't fun most of the time).This severe lack of emphasis on the basic gameplay loop makes this game a one-ride only kind of game, and it's not a long, satisfying experience which would make that OK. I don't know if I'll ever have the time to revisit God of War again, but I would definitely love to. Experience new builds, challenge myself to the highest difficulty, and generally just getting better at the game because it allows you this kind of growth and challenge.The story is nice, nothing too amazing but it keeps you interested. The problem here is that the game constantly presents you with choices you have to make - but you never feel their impact. You never feel like "damn, I should never have picked that choice earlier in the game because it screws me over". It was always either completely negligible or it was extremely obvious which option is the only sensible one to choose. Unimaginative and sad honestly, I don't mind a game just taking me on a thrill-ride with no say besides the experience, but this has no thrill, and I do have a say, it just really doesn't make any difference.The game is also quite buggy, not the game breaking kind, but definitely the immersion shattering one as these bugs repeat themselves over and over - and considering the absolute lack of replayability this game has - this is a major issue as I won't be revisiting the game once they solve bugs like characters instantly teleporting down a ledge instead of falling down, getting stuck in a little hole or just random enemies clipping and doing stupid stuff altogether.And the final nail in the coffin for me and for my roommate who watched the whole thing with me, was the really lame loot and general design of things that you can get. The skins are almost all either really cringe or just extremely boring, the loot & upgrade system is basic and really barely feel like it gives you anything interesting. I'm a looter, I always look for all the secrets and rewards that you can get, I always go back to win every challenge etc... This game has all this on paper, but it's never satisfying or gratifying, you never say "WOW check out the new skin!". No, it's all stupid basic and it's really disappointing at times. Also all of your important abilities are things you'll get anyway as you progress, there's no skill tree or decisions you need to make of "I'll invest in this type of ability and not another because I like it more"... No, by the end of the game you'll easily have unlocked everything the game has to offer, and it still feels like you barely got anything.Bottom line - for me this game had a lot more wasted potential than it had actual good gameplay. It's decently fun, don't get me wrong, and quite funny - I would definitely recommend it if it was a 20-30$ game. But this is not a AAA level action game, I'm sorry, and it's not about the money, I don't care about the 'wasted' extra 30$ I feel I paid, but I do care about expecting a high level solid action game for that price, and that wasn't even close to my expectations...

_childDocuments_.review: Words alone can't express how packed this game is with fun content, and that's without any multiplayer support and pesky in-game micro transactions (let's be honest, it's the the worst offender of all. I mean... when was the last time you played a AAA title that actually encouraged exploration for unlocking perks and outfits lol).This is exactly what Marvel's Avengers should have been. A single-player experience that focuses on not only engaging gameplay but also organized storytelling, one that meaningfully rewards (or punishes) the choices you make throughout the game, one that always fills you up with strong emotions. and one that leaves you with a great level of satisfaction by the end.And how can I not talk about how freaking awesome the soundtrack and the '80s music playlist is! I am shocked how well it goes with the overall theme of the game. Also, I can sleep well at night knowing I gotta be honest... when I saw the first trailer for this game, I couldn't help myself but ignore it altogether, induced by the sour taste of Marvel's Avengers that was still lingering in my mouth. But when I saw how overwhelmingly positive the critics were about this game, I decided to put aside my early misjudgement and snag a copy on Steam Winter Sale — and OH BOY was it worth EVERY SINGLE PENNY.While I can't be bothered explaining my rating system right now,  because why not. It gracefully managed to exceed my somewhat meagre expectations and encouraged me to write this review, something which I rarely care about. I hope you would feel the same too.And finally, kudos to the folks over at  for bringing this wonderful experience to life. Hope Square Enix and your fellow studios learn a thing or two from you guys. I can't wait for what you guys do next!

_childDocuments_.review: Most positive reviews are going to say something like "this is what Avengers should have been" which is fair, but misleading. This game is nothing like Avengers.First off, it's a single player campaign. It'd be like comparing Call of Duty multiplayer to the campaign which are two different things entirely. There is a lot of story, dialogue, lore, relationship dynamics, voice acting (not just cheeky one-liners), and a focus on the team/family that is the GotG. This game is primarily about Peter Jason Quill and his origin story. You literally start the game as a 13 year old Quill on his birthday and you're introduced to his relationship with his mom. It's hearfelt, occasionally moving, and the tone fluctuations between mildly dark themes and dry humor.Each character is developed quite a bit, even though I'm only 13 hours in. Rocket is a snarky, feisty, arrogant genius that constantly bickers with Quill and criticizes his leadership. Gamora is a level-headed ninja with a chip on her shoulder who has a soft spot for the team. Drax is an aloof meathead that holds honor and murder above all else. I'll stop there, because you already know all of this, right? Well, you will if you didn't already, because the game focuses more on the team than it does getting out of sticky situations GotG are notorious for getting into. Again, hardly a punch fest starring the green roid rager and bendy girl.The graphics are exceptional, assuming you apply an AMD/Nvidia sharpening filter given that there is forced TAA (which is great if you're totally used to blurry textures and ghosting). Otherwise, environments, character models, animations, and attention to detail is impressive. Sound design is chunky, impactful, and it doesn't hurt that the game features a handful of licensed retro hits even the younger generation will recognize.The game is also RPG-lite; you earn XP, level up your abilities, and collect components along the way that contribute to more passive skills like additional health. There's also no tiered loot system, which is again what practically defines the rewards in Avengers. I say lite because none of these systems feel particularly in depth, non-linear, or give the player difficult choices.Combat is probably one of the more highlighted components and it's for good reason. I would describe it as a squad-based button mash beat-em up. While you'll occasionally left-trigger-right-trigger and pew pew everything, you'll spend most of your time telling your squad via an intuitive control scheme to execute certain attacks. After a while, I stopped attacking altogether and just dodged attacks while my team killed everything. Honestly, they didn't make me feel powerful as Quill himself, but more like a leader barking orders at subordinates with considerably stronger and more effective attacks.  This may not sit well with some, but as a "pet-class" type player, it felt great.Beyond that, there are minor mini-games, optional content, and dialogue choices that impact outcomes, and you'll often be presented with a choice on who to side with in a conflict. Also, when I say "often" I mean like most of the time. Someone will be arguing with someone else and you'll play the mediator. There is definitely some influence from the Telltale series here as well i.e. "Rocket will remember that."I'd absolutely recommend this game as an independent, squad-based beat-em up with minor RPG elements and a rich story. It reminds me a lot of the movies, and I think that's kind of the point. Light-hearted, focused on comedy, a few dark themes here and there, with a focus on the crew and their ongoing (and occasionally annoying) differences. Speaking of which, one of the complaints I've seen is the somewhat generic intrepretation of their appearances versus the movie, and while I agree it's jarring, I'd argue that the movie was also an interpretation of the comics. Chris Pratt is not Star Lord, that's what the casting director decided. In the comic books, it's not Chris Pratt's face. Just something to think about before judging the faces. The voice acting is excellent and I appreciate that they kind of own their own identities without being holywood celebs.Pick it up and have a good time. That's all this game can promise. It's not incredibly deep, sophisticated, or complex. It's also not simple, stupid, and broken. I'm looking at you, Avengers.

_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: First, a disclaimer. Think of this more of an interactive movie sprinkled with a bit of dialog choices, a bit of exploration and some serviceable combat.With that out of the way, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is surprisingly quite, quite good! The story is fun, the banter (which, believe me, there's tons of) between the Guardians is very faithful to the characters. Constantly funny! At at times laugh-out-loud hilarious!On the technical side, it's linear, so don't go in expecting an open-world. You can only control Peter Quill, but it's understandable if you play the game and realize what they have done with the other characters and how they tie to the combat. All the places our heroes visit are incredibly detailed and colorful, as are the secondary characters we meet. As I said in the beginning, the combat is just okay. It gets the job done. At this point I'm playing it more for the story and characters than for the combat.It's also a fairly well optimized product. It's running fine on my rig (i7 7700K, RTX 2080, 16 gigs RAM), maximum settings minus Ray-tracing and DLSS at "balanced". I encountered a few bugs here and there, but none game-breaking for me and, I think, quite fixable.This is also, as far as I'm aware, a complete package, as in, there won't be DLC in the future. I think making an actual finished product at launch has value and needs to be recognized considering how the majority of AAA games never do that nowadays.All in all, I bought this thinking that "it's just to hold me up until Forza Horizon 5", but while in terms of playtime that maybe so, the story and characters are so appealing that I think I'll be revisiting this again.So yeah, recommended!EDIT: just to say I finished the game with a playtime of 22,6 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun story, Very good dialogue, Voice actors really brought these character to live. You really buy that these characters are the ones your familiar with from the movies, (even though this is based on the comics not the movies).Game looks BeautifulThere were some cheese cutscenes which i though was goofy (the collectable convos and huddle up)There was some bugs with caused me to reload checkpoints.Definitely Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I gave this game a chance.You can tell the developers are huge comic nerds and have put the utmost care and effort to deliver an amazing, wholesome yet a hilarious experience.This game is to GoTG the way Arkham Asylum is to Batman.The characters start off as juvenile pricks, but slowly develop into their better, yet cool headed selves overtime unlike James Gunn's take where they become unbearable and cringy as seen in GoTG Vol 2. I thought this would be an 8-10 hour game at best, but I certainly didn't expect a ~20 ish hour campaign which is rare for a linear, story centric game in 2021.The combat felt really lackluster and wasn't as impactful, until the last few chapters where you have most of your skills and combos unlocked, I hope they improve it in a sequel.But the best part about this game is the phenomenal soundtrack featuring multiple classic hits as well as original music by the in-game band, Star-Lord which also serves as an inspiration for Peter Quill's alias.Overall, this game is well worth your time and money, and it certainly won't let you down as long as you expect a decent, but not perfect experience.8.5/10, Chef's kiss.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: How can it be that there is a game released in 2021 which is a complete, purely linear single-player experience, without any DLC, without seasons pass, without microtransactions, and without any shoehorned in online component? Was Square Enix' corporate asleep when they greenlit this project?And how can it be that this game is probably the best narrative gaming experience I had in years? With excellent voice-acting throughout, good writing with fleshed-out characters as well as both actually funny and truly heartfelt moments? And with marvelous (pun somewhat intended), original art design?On the gameplay side, I had some grievances, as the combat lacks proper flow, many enemies are awful bullet sponges, and there are a few of pretty bad QTEs, but that didn't spoil the experience for me.The game could have also used another round of bug-fixes and optimisation, as there's a lot of texture and geometry pop-in, and some stuttering when new assets are loaded. No complaints regarding the performance, as I got solid 70ish fps on "Very High" settings including raytracing at 1080p (on an RTX 2070).Last game I played in 2021, best game I played in 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: A 3rd person action-adventure, linear, single player title, bereft of DLC/Microtransactions/Games-as-Service corruption.  Developed by the same team at Eidos-Montreal who produced the fantastic  reboots, the production values are absolutely aces.  All the care and attention to detail applied to their immersive sims have been brilliantly translated to a narrative-heavy experience.  The writing is some of the strongest I've experienced in a video game.The best way I could describe it is a pulpy, sci-fi mashup of , , and (the good)  games.  Dialog and cutscenes are heavily featured, and are the focal point of the experience.  Set designs feel extravagant and never wasted.  Combat is a little dull, but serviceable.  If one is only interested in gameplay and would skip all the cutscenes, this isn't for you.  But if a story with a lot of heart, fantastic alien worlds, and a rocking 70/80s soundtrack sounds appealing, please check this out.  The industry is really shifting away from linear, curated single player games that are complete packages, so gamers speaking with their wallets will hopefully push production houses to greenlight more games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: One playthrough - 20.5 hrs - Normal difficulty9/10 overallAbsolute effing blast. Caveats being you need to like the 3rd Person Action/RPG genre, but if you do you're getting a prime example of it here. The gameplay does get a little repetitive, but I've yet to come across an example of this type of game where that isn't the case. The combat is satisfying, but it's not the primary draw here. What makes "Guardians of the Galaxy" so excellent is its combination of top notch graphics, fun gameplay, outstanding writing, and a truly exceptional comic book story. Seriously, the voice work and writing in each and every one of the key story beats were as good as in any game I've played in recent memory. What a pleasant surprise. I'd read the reviews on here, but I was still surprised. Great stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommended. It's so sad to think the failure of Marvel's Avengers caused this one to fly under the radar for so many people including myself. Guardians of the Galaxy tells an incredible story and is one of the best-looking games I've played in some time. If you have any interest in these characters at all, this is a must-buy. I also think if you're only familiar with the Guardians because of the MCU, you may be surprised to find you like the characters in this game better actually! The balancing between comedy and emotional dramatic moments is handled much more gracefully and allows the contrast between a laugh or cry moment to hit harder.Unfortunately it's plagued by a lack of polish in the technical department; I encountered lots of frequent small bugs and crashes during my playtime. Most of the crashes went away when I disabled raytracing but it was so disappointing to have to do that because it really does look amazing. The bugs were always really small things, like animations bugging out or getting stuck in map geometry (the game detects when this happens and relocates you so not a big deal) but they really do detract from the immersion when they happen.The gameplay is serviceable, especially knowing that it is a narrative-focused game first and foremost. Combat is pretty fun, though not very deep, and encounters don't stick around too long to get boring. Exploration is a vehicle to take in the sights and hear conversations between the Guardians that flesh their personalities and rich histories out, with some collectible hunting elements that requires the player to toggle Starlord's helmet to find secrets in the environment. It's fun to collect different outfits (and trinkets that unlock new conversations) for each Guardian, but it's a shame that the visor vision is so needed to collect them. You spend most of the game using it and seeing the visuals of these beautiful environments completely washed away with the heavy visual filters applied by the helmet.Don't let the nitpicking above deter you from playing the game however. This is a genuine hidden gem that I think more people should check out. It was a financial failure for Eidos Montreal but it's a real labor of love and it's so clear that the writers understood what makes a fantastic sci-fi adventure with a ragtag group of lovable characters growing closer together.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is flarking awesome, one of the most cinematic, polished, fun experiences in gaming. Its a better journey than the second movie. Graphics, history and voice acting are top notch. Not once while playing i wished the characters looked or sounded more like the movie actors. Its impressive the amount of dialogue they made in order to feel the constant banter between the characters. I waited to build my new pc in order to play it and it was totally worth it, it looks awesome in ultra settings with ray tracing, it also supports DLSS.  It's sad to know it was not a commercial success while pay to win crap and micro transaction sh*tty games are making millions. This is what gaming is supposed to be about, and incredible crafted piece of entertainment made by people who understands the material they are working with.  I would personally love to play a sequel where you could change the character you fight with, but i wont hold my breath, i just hope more people buy and experience the game and the developers get the credit they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 13 hours in, still haven't finished the game, this is my review so far:*looks amazing - very detailed environments, interesting looking character design *runs smoothly - though I'm using a 2080 so your experience may vary, but runs smooth af and everything is cranked to the max including ray tracing and DLSS on quality.*gameplay is fun enough - you basically have a few systems: you control Peter exclusively but you have skills for your other guardians that you can use whenever(they have a cooldown) which you can combo together, either with themselves or with the environment.  peter has some of his own skills and elemental weapons that you HAVE to use in order to kill some mobs - basically the combat mechanic isn't really that complex and deep but it's hella fun and pretty fluid...unless it's the ship battle...that was clunky and unfun for me.*story, lore, dialogue and interactions with the world and between the guardians of the galaxy is *chefs kiss* - the story itself is pretty fun, not the best ever but it's fun, I personally enjoyed so far.  there's tons of text logs scattered around the maps that give some lore about what's happening right now or in the past - really recommend reading all of them, they're not that long. and now the creme de la creme - the dialogues - easily the best part of the game for me, characters are deep, true to their sources, feels like you actually playing as the guardians of the galaxy, I won't expend too much on it, you gotta experience it yourself ;)I would rate this game 8.5\10 -almost everything is 10/10 in this game, the combat started to get boring a little after a couple of fights and there was a bug that kept repeating itself at random time that despawns bosses which made me restart the game. for me personally it's not a deal breaker because the rest of the game was really polished.

_childDocuments_.review: I found it hard to put the game down. The writing of the characters and story is fantastic, the worlds are colorful and interesting, the voice work is top notch and maintains quality and quantity throughout. I would recommend this game to anyone. I wouldn't say it left me wanting more, but the game doesn't overstay itself and I can easily see myself playing through the game again in the future.While the game itself is great, it is not 100% completion friendly. While outfits can be grabbed for a permanent unlock, compendium lore items cannot be saved but by chapter skipping so if you want them, you'll have to do full playthroughs. You can't skip cutscenes, only individual lines of dialogue. Also many of the collectables have conversations with team members tied to them the usually explore some emotional backstory for one of the characters, but doing a new game plus keeps the items collected but doesn't allow you to revisit these scenes. I also encountered a few bugs that soft-locked me, but most were fixed by reloading the last checkpoint. The game auto-saves often and I never lost much progress.Don't let the poor decisions of the Avengers dissuade you from this game. I was pleasantly surprised. It is a lot of fun and has lot of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: A great comparison from movie to game.Our band of misfits start on a mission promising glory and riches, yet does the opposite by releasing a monster, angering all the wrong people and having all plans complicated by religious fanatics. Lady Luck is not on your side.On your mission to fix everything, possibly loot everything as well, you will be acting as Star Lord shooting your way out of all the problem. The game is designed to you acting as the leader yelling out orders to the other members. It's up to you to decide what skills to use based on the situation. Groot does well with holding down enemies, Gamora is a strong single target damage dealer, Drax is a middleground aiming to add a lot of "stagger" and Rocket is your AOE damage guy. Starlord is a bit of everything, but main purpose is to stay alive and make use of Elemental Shots.The world, story, music and direction is great. Everything just fits in nicely and the 90's music soundtrack is similar to how you remember it from the movies, with Star Lord listening to his old cassette player (ah those days!). One other thing is that the game has a ton of dialogue in the same sense from the movie. The different members talk a lot, but it's not boring and so much has been added to each mission. Members constantly roasting each other is also great.The situation is most dire, but you're "The flarking Guardians of the Galaxy!"

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  Pricey for the length, but it frequently goes on sale for an excellent price.  The game is gorgeous, both technically and artistically.  The soundtrack is mostly great.  The battles are fun once you get used to the controls.  There's good enemy variety.  The voice acting and writing are excellent!There are QTEs but don't panic!  You can turn them off in the options if you don't like them.  Except for a weird one that I had to screenshot to figure out what it wanted me to do, the QTEs are quite easy, so I would suggest leaving them on, but the option is there under accessibility.The game does have a few bothersome bugs lying around.  The two worst ones I ran into were solved simply by going back to the main menu and reloading the game.  It also crashed on me a few times.  Convincing your crew to attack the enemy you want when there are lots of enemies all running around can be pure frustration, too.Saves are done by FREQUENT checkpoints.  There are three save slots and you can save anytime.  It will revert to the previous checkpoint, but they are so frequent that you shouldn't lose more than a few minutes.Replayability is pretty weak.  There are a few choices that matter, but they don't matter enough to be worth replaying, in my opinion.  Your characters each get 4 skills each and it isn't too hard to get all of them by the end of the game.P.S.  If anyone could please let me play this game about 20 years back when game designers were putting as much brown as possible into their games, I would really appreciate it.

The music is great.During the gameplay I encountered some minor bugs and performance drops, even important in some game areas, but between my hardware not at the top and the fact that I played it on day one I hope that all the defects have been fixed in the updates. In summary I enjoyed it, maybe the ending was not as great as the rest, but it was a long time since I liked a video game that much.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what AAA gaming should look like. Fantastic voice acting, graphics, story, combat and all the systems that hold everything together. Yes, there are a few bugs that caused me to have to reload the last checkpoint but it didn't really take me out of the game much at all and they were few and far between.The biggest thing I have to praise though is the voice acting. Especially a few scenes where the main ones involved were Gamora and Nikki. You could feel the emotions and how real it all was. I really hope we get some sort of sequel or just more Marvel games like this in general. THIS is how a Marvel game should be now and into the future. Continue to improve upon this and it can only continue to get better and better. Time it took me to finish the game is 18 hours.Performance was VERY good. I am running an i9 9900k @ 5ghz and an RTX 2080 Super and I was able to easily do maxed out graphics including Raytracing. Also had DLSS turned on to Quality. I held 100fps for the majority of the playthrough, with it lowering to 85fps for a very light heavy fight later in the game. It all ran extremely smooth and no crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful step back to what feels like a simpler time. Guardians plays like a game from the 360 era with a heavy focus on characters and level design.A singleplayer affair from the get go seems like a odd choice for a game with such a team but it works out really well with you able to "control" your allies in a few simple ways while influencing the battlefield.You play as Star Lord himself and he controls pretty well with responsive dodging and able to keep on target easily with his weapons and melee combos.The visuals are fantastic, exactly what you'd expect from a big marvel property with crazy layouts, sky boxes and unique alien designs (though sometimes a alien is just...blue and thats it).The character design has that same feel the Avengers game has where everyone is a familiar face but different at the same time.The story so far has been interesting with it taking place i guess after the Infinity war, you can respond to conversations mid game in a way similar to the Tell Tale series (with several options but always the option to stay silent) how much these choices impact your game down the line vary.Sound design is possibly the only area i find lacking in this game and i hope they improve it. Sound sources seem to bounce alot between my speakers to the point where it can be jarring sometimes.You can very easily skip segments of dialogue by just moving forward too fast and causing the character to jump to the next set of lines something thats always plagued dialogue heavy action games.Lastly Starlord's lines seem to vary heavily with their inflection and emotion sometimes, he'll sometimes respond to another guardian and his tone won't match and feels stilted.Music is fantastic with 80's classic hits littering the game and a entire tape's worth of new recordings designed to emulate their feel.Still overall a small set of issues that hopefully will get addressed as time goes on. This is the first time in a long time i've seen a big commercial property get treated well and it's highly enjoyable.
