_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! GOTG is a linear choice-based action adventure game. I enjoyed most aspects, but the clear allure of the game is the dialogue and banter between the guardians. There is so much spoken dialogue, that you probably will not hear all of it on your first playthrough. Even standing around will earn you a lot of back and forth between all the characters. You can also find collectibles that add dialogue from each character. The lines are funny, engaging, and you can tell everyone had a lot of fun with it. The story is also a wild ride.  Just like a movie, the stakes seem low but as the chapters go on, it becomes very high. The game is so much fun that I never questioned the narrative, I was just along for the ride! There is also a nice moral message in the game that helps balance out the craziness. It's just fun to watch a horribly dysfunctional and flawed group come together and grow as you play. The gameplay is disliked by most players I would say. I personally really enjoyed the gameplay, but I can see how it can get boring very fast. It's still not bad though and unlocking different abilities and combining them when fighting is really neat. I especially enjoyed the huddle feature. The huddle brings out the soundtrack which comprises of 70's and 80's music. If you play I highly recommend turning your dialogue and sound effects volume down to around 80 percent. Then turning your music volume up to 100. As long as you can clearly hear the dialogue, blasting the soundtrack heavily improves the game! The only complaint I have with GOTG is the bugs. My first playthrough had a lot of bugs which was very distracting. Dialogue cutting off, cutscenes cutting a second to early/late and making it feel awkward. Lag for no reason, or when a boss fight wouldn't move on to phase 2, so I thought I was doing something wrong. Turns out I just had to restart the fight. I'm playing through the chapters to get all the collectibles and outfits I missed, and I am getting fewer bugs, but it's still very noticeable. Overall I highly recommend this game. I think you'll enjoy it if you are new to GOTG and you will really enjoy it if you are already a fan of the source material. Whether it be the movies or comics. I actually enjoyed this game more than the movie as far as characters and narrative went. If only they would fix the bugs, it would be a near perfect game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Guardians of the Galaxy is a 3rd person action adventure game developed by Eidos Montreal and produced by square enix in the year 2021. The game puts you in the shoes of Care free and comical Star Lord whose goal apparently is to lead a group of misfits assembled from different parts of the universe to fame and glamour. This so called group is guardians of the Galaxy which comprises of Drax the Destroyer, Rocket the walking science experiment (who is not a raccoon), the deadliest woman in the galaxy Gamora and the lone surviving flora colossi Groot.Tension is evident  among the guardians right from the beginning of the game where everyone is trying to figure out their fellow members motives. Following Star Lord’s less than reliable sources for completing their next job they head out to the bubble gumish garbage bin of space quarantine zone which serves as a sad reminder of long fought war and the unfolding of events here has further dented the team’s fortunes. From these lows how the guardians pick themselves up trusting each member with life to become the best team/family is game’s offering which the player will be experiencing.As stated above  game allows the player to play as Star Lord and he issues certain commands to the other guardians as a combat mechanic and for puzzle solving during exploration. Progressing through the story successfully awards with xp points which are used for unlocking more powerful attacks in combat. The game offers two items that can collected in game for unlocking different perks useful for both combat and exploration. And lastly the whole game has choice based dialogue where most are for immersion and getting the feel of the team’s dynamic and some that are designed to change the course of the playthrough. •	The story and character build up is excellent, all characters get enough time in the sun to shine through along with some very human elements. •	The soundtrack is phenomenal. It gels so well with the combat sequences.•	Graphics are very pleasing to the eye with a good number of varied locations to explore. •	An all around easy to complete game with no filler content.•	The Milano is tough to control and breaks the fun feeling almost instantly•	Combat is straightforward after a certain level, so it can be boring.To conclude my review I will say that this game is a really fresh surprise after the disappointed of Marvel’s Avengers. Expectations were low with this title but it shines brightly to go well above and beyond them. Highly recommended, one of the best games this year.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing GotG, I watched the credits roll; the 80’s music lulling me to simpler times. I had so many things I wanted to say about the game, like how perfectly the score and soundtrack set the mood throughout the story. How wonderfully paced the story was and how I appreciated that there was time given for the surprisingly emotional parts of each character’s backstory and how each of the Guardians dealt with their grief and pain. It is rare while playing a game that I think about how good the writing is and how perfect the voice actors are performing, but I did with this game. The writing is tight, relatable, and emotional. The acting is perfect and believable. I felt every bit of Drax’s hurt for the loss of his family; I felt the pain Peter felt in every scene with his mother; Gamora’s guilt for her sister; Rocket’s anguish around water. Every, “I am Groot,” hit me a little differently each time. Aside from the tragic backstories, the comedy is gold. The banter between all the Guardians made me laugh on many occasions. I loved being with all these characters, and then Mantis showed up and became a standout character for me. The actor playing her did an amazing job. Each world visited in the game was stunning. Knowhere, Quarantine Zone, The Rock, Lamentis, Seknarf Nine, and Sacrosanct are worlds packed with details and, though linear, enjoyable to explore. The battles fought were fast paced and exciting and the boss battles felt unique and worthy of being boss battles. They were challenging, but not aggravating. It’s been a long time since a game has so fully drawn me in so fully. I am so very surprised to say this, but I would put GotG’s story up there with RDR2, and Bioshock Infinite. I’m not saying it’s better, but I am saying the quality of storytelling is on par with the best stories I have played.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardian of the Galaxy is proof that eidos montreal as a developer is still one of the best at delivering linear stories with engaging characters when free of corporate interference.The story of Guardians of the Galaxy is the main reason I would recommend this game to anyone. If you are familiar with the the comic book, the game follows a similar structure where our Guardians start of with a job that eventually unravels into a Galaxy saving plot. I will not go any further into the plot so as to avoid spoilers on who the big bad is eventually revealed to be. Apart from the main story, another defining feature will be the character writing in this game. Every character in the game is written amazingly, sticking very closely with the comic book, Character banter made mundane walks between combat and story moments entertaining and was something i looked forward to every time.Now on to the only sub-par part of the game and unfortunately seems to be an issue with eidos games, is the combat. Initially it can be satisfying to combo each guardians abilities to deal massive damage, but after the half way point, it soon boils down to shooting with star-lords blasters and changing elements as required to deal with specific enemy types and waiting for your other guardians abilities to cooldown. I played this on hard and your mileage will vary, but some enemy types felt very spongy. Apart from regular combat, there are moments of dog fighting in the milano, with my only gripe being how twitchy it felt with the mouse and keyboard, but once you understand how it controls it doesn't become an issue. While I am still a fan of their deus ex franchise and am still hopeful for a sequel, I can confidently say that I am also hopeful for a sequel to Guardians of the Galaxy as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many of you, I didn’t know what to expect with this game at all after the disappointment that was The Avenger’s game so, at first, I didn’t really care about it but slowly the community began to share their impressions and to my surprise, they were good and positive so I jumped in and yes, I can safely say that Guardians of the Galaxy is one of those games that fly under your radar and end up surprising you in a very positive way once you notice them. Great story and really well developed characters are the main reasons to enjoy this adventure so, after this unusually positive introduction for one of my reviews, Is Guardians of the Galaxy a game you will enjoy? Well, let’s find out.The Story begins in what appears to be a normal job for this team in the Quarantine zone, at some point something happens in this mission an unknown entity is liberated although they team runs and doesn’t look back, after getting arrested by the Nova corps and keep doing their low profile jobs, things are gradually starting getting weird as a mysterious church starts gaining power at a very alarming rate and the destiny of the galaxy is in the hands of this crazy but surprisingly competent team, it is time for the Guardians of the Galaxy to prove themselves worthy to carry that name or we will all be flackerd!Eidos did a really great job with the writing of this story. I'm not only talking about the situations or pace but also how the characters interact and develop through the entire story from start to finish, that being said, that doesn’t mean the story is bad, on the contrary, the story is legit good.The story is completely original for this game, while it will use a lot of already existing elements from both comics and the movies, what we will find here is a story that goes from low profile space pirates to big space opera epic adventure and that’s really cool because, we will notice how gradually the story changes and expands to become something memorable. While there’s a big focus on the main narrative, as you could expect from this team, there are tons of dialogs and documents that expand the narrative at a more ground level, additionally there are certain moments in which we will be able to interact as Quill in 2 types of conversations, the first type will make a difference in your potential final outcome in this story, the other will make bounds of the crew stronger and let you learn from characters, totally worth checking them.What really shines in here though is how the team behind the game represented all the characters.I would say the way they represent this peculiar team is superb, there’s a lot of time for all of them to develop and interact with other characters creating very cool dynamics in the dialogs, there are also situations in which you can interact face to face with some of them and oh dear, some of those are particularly well done, in fact I would say some of those moments are the best writing of the game. If you like the MCU versions I think you will enjoy them even more here as they have an absurd amount of time to really expand their backgrounds and personalities. The relation between characters is a very important part of this game and when I say important I mean the relation between them is key, from motivations to their own interactions when facing some situations. An important element I would like to introduce for this part is the Milano, our ship, because if you explored well enough each level you might find objects that once in the ship will unlock special conversations with specific characters, they are completely optional but if you want to get some more depth about them, I totally recommend to not only find all those special hidden objects but also to listen those dialogs once you are in the Milano.Now that we have talked about the story, the narrative and the characters I think it’s a good moment to straight jump into the visuals because, let me tell you this, Guardians of the Galaxy sure is a looker.Let’s start by saying that this game is graphically impressive, in general it has a similar level as games like Deus Ex and is more cohesive than Avengers. Effects, environments and set pieces, it’s the type of game in which you will likely stop every few seconds to take some pictures because what you see amazes you.If there’s something great about this adventure is that we will visit quite a lot of places, from the Quarantine Zone to Seknarf-9, all this places have their unique style and distinctive visual language, artistically speaking this game is top notch and you can really see how varied and cool this universe is, while it’s not the only game that will make us visit very different places but as this is the open space, they can go crazy with the designs and they sure went crazy, when it comes to the art aspect, it’s jaw dropping.If visuals are good I don’t think I have to say that music ROCKS!Let’s start with what I think it’s a really cool addition to the game. The team decided to create a fictional rock band and let me tell you, original tracks for this game are really good.But of course the licensed stuff is what steals the show, a lot of beloved artists in here such as Iron Maiden or Blondie, yeah, this is an absolutely amazing 80’s festival that you will be able to enjoy in the Milano whenever you want to enjoy the music.Surprisingly there’s something potentially divisive in this game, gameplay.Look, I liked it and I enjoyed it, quite a lot in fact but I know for sure it is not everyone’s cup of tea.Game has a very familiar gameplay loop at first, it  is a third person adventure game with shooting mechanics, this time with 4 characters even though only Quill is playable, however, it quickly introduces the command system which is the cherry top of this game’s gameplay loop. At first it might look like it’s tedious, difficult to master and in general chaotic to command 4 independent characters in the battlefield, however, in my own experience, this was not the case and once I got used to it the results were quite amazing and dynamic.Let’s face it, every single combat is the same from start to finish in this adventure which might end up being repetitive but I can’t say I got tired of it, I tried new combos, I “mastered” the system and experimented with the upgraded characters and at the end of the day I ended up enjoying this fighting elements, I seriously hope you do too because I found it to be very entertaining.Let’s also not forget about the huddle up motivational boost that happens from time to time, if you answer correctly to this piece of changing dialog you will get a really cool unlimited boost for abilities for a period of time.Speaking of upgradable characters, your characters will be upgradable but in different ways, to upgrade your set of movements for the command system you will have to level up in combat by getting better scores for as long as possible, that way the game will grant you with level points that you can trade in the menu for new special movements but when it comes to Quill, in addition to his special movements there are the benchbanks in which you will have to find energy bars and spheres to exchange with Rocket for upgrades like shield, health and boots upgrades, do not forget to explore all places in order to find those hidden objects that will come in handy and do not worry if you end up with more than you need, I’m not the only one that finished the game with more elements than required for all upgrades.That’s about it, as you can see I thought this game was not only amazing but also one of the best adventures of this year, sadly it didn’t get the recognition I think it deserved but things are getting better for the game slowly but steady thanks to the community, I really hope this review helps you deciding if you want to jump in or not and hope that, if you end up playing it, enjoy it as much as I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: Guardians of the Galaxy is surprisingly a great game. GotG is about a dysfunctional team of superheroes trying to make a name for themselves across...well...the galaxy. You start off trying to hunt a monster for a queen and end up accidentally unleashing something far more sinister. I can't really go into too much more detail other than that the story is a hell of a ride. It isn't quite as typical as other superhero stories which makes it even better.This game is absolutely gorgeous from start to finish. There were a few times my jaw dropped. The colors are very vibrant and the attention to all the details are very good. One of the best looking games I've ever played. I think it's important to note that you will not be playing any other hero other than Star Lord a.k.a. Peter Quill. The gameplay is fun but can feel clunky at times. Especially the initial jump. The animation feels very quickly and lazily done. You don't even really jump. You just...teleport up a bit. The jet boost jump afterwards looks very fluid which is very odd and until you get used to it it's irritating. Star Lord uses his trusty special Quad Blasters and jet boots to keep distance between him and his foes or transform them to get in close with CQC. Over time you'll learn new ways on how to use them and exploit enemy weaknesses. As the leader, you'll be issuing orders and taking advantage of each Guardian's unique abilities. You'll also get an 'ultimate' ability where you rally your teammates and depending on your answer you'll either boost the whole team or hilariously fail and only boost yourself for a time. It's a lot of fun combining different abilities to maximize crowd control and damage enemies. Overall, GotG is a mix of Spider-Man (PS4/PS5) mechanics, Final Fantasy VII Remake mechanics and a choice system similar to Telltale games. There were some FPS drops in certain scenes areas in my playthrough and a few times I had to reload my save because all the enemies didn't spawn. Nothing game breaking but definitely annoying. I've also seen (early access stream on Twitch) that the controls won't align with the controller you're using and depending on your setup you may experience more FPS drops. I was lucky I guess. It needs some patching. There's also some replayability with New Game + and the fact that you can't access everything in your first playthrough because you lack the abilities. So if you like collecting and discovering every nook and cranny, you got incentive for that NG+ and I thought that was a cool idea. Can't wait to dive back in and do exactly that myself.Coming from someone who wasn't a huge a fan of GotG this is a must buy for any superhero and/or Marvel fans. The story and dialogues hit all the emotions and capture each character really really well. I was even introduced to villains and heroes I never even heard of before and loved all of them. I was skeptical with the footage prior to release and I'm glad I decided to purchase and try it. It is an absolute blast from start to finish and I really hope they come out with a GotG 2. This is definitely one of my favorite superhero games and while not the best, definitely one of the better games to come out this year. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic single player action-adventure with some light RPG elements. The story and characters are surprisingly well written, with backstories, personalities, and unique quirks that are infinitely more fleshed out than anyone in an MCU movie. In fact, this is not set in the MCU as far as I can tell, and that's fantastic. There are dark themes dealing with war crimes, ethnic cleansing, addiction, PTSD -- I was pleasantly surprised by how much more human, both in the ugliest sense and the most wonderful sense of the word, this story felt. As for the gameplay.... it's nothing to write home home about. The battle system is satisfying in that you feel like a badass, but even on hard mode, the combat mechanics themselves lack any real depth and practically zero skill.The worldbuilding and lore, of course, are fantastic. Together with DLSS 2.3 and RTX reflections, the game is gorgeous at 4k/60fps and runs easily on a 3080 in HDR. Overall, 9/10. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time GotG comic nerd, I gotta say that this is everything I could have ever asked for.- Eidos doesn’t try to recreate the team from the movies or from any run of comics. They take every version of the characters and blend it together then add their own spin on the characters. I’m not a huge fan with a few of the characters but I appreciate all of them.- Just like the characters the setting is also unique. It takes events from the comics and some of the more noticeable characters from the movies and does its own twist to make a new but recognizable galaxy. - The writing is incredible from beginning to end. Eidos knocks it out the park at every turn. On top of the writing being amazing the way the game plays make it even better. As you make your way through the levels the team will talk about all kind of things and will even comment on what the player is up to. I hope to see more like this from other studios in the future.- The combat is really enjoyable as well as different from similar games. The gameplay makes you feel like you’re one part of a real team. In a lot of games your teammates are just walking guns, but in GotG it feels like everyone is just as important as the player is.All in all, this game is a masterpiece, as a massive Guardians nerd and as a video game nerd I love everything about this game. Eidos deserves a ton of praise and other studios should take notes from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with GotG, would definitely recommend for anyone who enjoys witty humor, character rich stories, and rock music! The soundtrack was incredible, the use of songs at key moments pushed the energy through the roof and felt extremely satisfying. The overall script and hilarious banter between the characters is definitely one of the biggest draws that keeps you immersed in every moment. I found myself pacing through the game slower than average because I enjoyed listening to the characters back and forth banter not wanting to miss a thing they said.There are huge parallels with it and something like Mass Effect in subject and genre, but completely deviate in execution. Where Mass Effect(ME) is at times broody and serious, GotG keeps it humorous and lighthearted even when the stakes of the universe are at hand. Where ME has you second guessing every decision for the perfect ending, GotG gives you choice but never makes you feel as though your missing anything huge. Removing that gravitas allows you play more freely and enjoy the ride.Speaking on the actual combat, I think this is where the game feels the weakest. The combat loop gets pretty repetitive after a while, I believe this is due to two things: limited enemy variety, and limited character customization. Unlike ME, GotG doesn't offer character trees where you can choose to power up a specific play types. You'll have exactly 15 equipment upgrades for Starlord, and 4 ability upgrades for each character. You'll quickly realize the best play pattern (Spam AoE abilities) and stick to that for the rest of the run. You'll have the occasional, hit this enemy with electric attack, situations but the combat really doesn't go very deep so that's where I'd say this game is at it's weakest.Overall though I had a great time with it and glad I spent about 40 hours on it. The worlds are vibrant, the characters are interesting, and the music is top tier. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a great game. If you enjoyed the GotG movies, this game feels very much like playing through one. It has the same blend of serious story and wacky humor that made the movies so great, and the storyline moves along at a good pace while not being bogged down by endless combat encounters. Honestly, it's just a really good time. Cannot recommend this one highly enough.A full playthrough was 17 hours, which is pretty much perfect for a story-focused game for me. It's long enough to tell the story it wants to tell and doesn't pad it out with extraneous BS. I appreciate that.If you aren't a fan of the MCU GotG franchise, this might not be for you, but if you are, you absolutely owe it to yourself to give this one a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with a compelling story. The music is a nice touch and there is a streaming mode you can turn on if you're worried about copyright issues. You can see the choices you make impact the dialogue throughout the entire game. Only complaint is that the combat voice lines can feel repetitive at times but otherwise worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Yea its linear, yea its singleplayer only.. no open world and not very much impact of your dialogue choices BUT its one of the most entertaining games i've played this year. The Story, the characters and the presentation of this game are 10/10.. i really recommend it if you want a game witch is like some of the older action rpgs/ spectacle fighters... you dont need to be a fan of Marvel comics to enjoy ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, really recommended!! - The story is amazing and keeps you entertained. It's also a story of it's own, not inspired by any movies or comic books (as far as my knowledge goes), which really works here!- The dynamic between characters feels great. - Has loads of humour, but also many action-packed sequences.- THE VISUALS!? ♥♥♥♥ they're good.The earnable outfits are also really good looking! Ranging from the MCU-outfits, to comic accurate outfits and even their own designs (no microtransactions, big W).
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: how did i not see this sooner? Honestly i dont like many super hero games but this gem is so entertaining! Somehow even manage to get on sale for my steam deck. 60 fps no prob. looks and plays great. voice acting an banter during play will hook you. just finished first chapter and hard to put down! i scored this for $15 on sale and id pay $50 all day for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: Fantastic visuals and graphics, Good combat and abilities (Arkham-style combat), and the best tunes. The Huddle ability makes combat even more fun.The Bad:Has some bugs, performance issue (frame drops, memory leaks, unoptimized hardware usage) and some things don't load in so you have to go back to the last checkpoint to fix. Doesn't happen often to be game-breaking but can get annoying if it does.The Decent:Story is decent with some nice twists and subpar pacing, nothing to write home about. Characters skins are really nice, and they're all free (no microtransactions) and hidden around the map(s). Dialogue options are nice and creative.Game takes about 15-25 hours to beat, varies based on skill and time spent exploring.If you get it on sale, it'll be worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Only recommending on sale unless you're a Marvel Fan, it's really a situational game. As someone not particularly crazy about Marvel, but open minded to it I gave this a try. Graphics are great, gameplay is not. The combat is extremely repetitive and the constant humor begins to get really stale line after line. The world immersion is very good, the music is like listening to a set of oldies from a playlist which some find very appealing. The puzzles, if you can call them that are often more an annoyance that puts the game on stop where you're ready to continue forward. It's a great casual game to turn your brain off to, but I'd never pay full price for it. The gameplay itself I find extremely one dimensional. I was burned out with the group huddle to motivate the team very fast. Graphics and universe are what sell me on this game. Everything else was so so.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've placed so far. I'm a noob at gaming so it's hard for me to fully immerse myself in games that are new (but I want to because of the better graphics) bc theyre usually very complex with multiple things like items, skill sets, map locations, etc. This game has barely any of that, but has good graphics and cut scenes with hilarious dialogue. I usually don't have patience for watching all the scenes, but I have barely skipped any of it with this game. Yes the combat can get dull, but again, I'm a noob and it's refreshing to have than every other game with gore or scary/gross monsters/zombies. I love all the background stories for the characters; so you don't have to have watched the movies to play this game. My bf and I also think the huddle times are hilarious and cheesy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything the Avengers game should've been, a great story with awesome gameplay (just instead of having teammates do specials at your call you could seamlessly switch between them in the battlefield) and superb character building. This feels like the good old days where the game you buy comes with everything packaged at launch, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ live service or no microtransactions or no ♥♥♥♥♥♥ season pass or extra paid story content. Plus the branching choices gives it alot of replay value and also also this comes with a new game plus at launch, what more would you want. As for performance you can check my profile for my rig and its running butter smooth with everything cranked to max, just have experienced some minor low framerates where there is huge draw distance and the game is loading the section and unloading the previous section, other than that its perfect, have only seen one glitch so far that when i was talking to gamora for just a sec the toothbrush just misplaced and got placed back again, the rest is just plain and perfect. Get this if you can you really will not regret it, at first i was not planning on buying this I wanted to buy RDR2 as it went for a pretty low cost this is a bit higher but this is on sale too so no harm there and finally decided to get and BRUH, was i not surprised..... THIS GAME IS WHAT ALL KINDS OF MARVEL GAMES SHOULD BE!!! STORY DRIVEN WITH AMAZING NARRATIVE AND CHARACTER PLUS WORLD BUILDING WITH SATISFYING GAMEPLAY AND LOADS OF EXPLORATION WHICH REWARDS FANS WITH ALOT OF FANSERVICE.... and trust me there is a lot of fanservice in this. All in all, its a no brainer just BUY IT!!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an easy game even on hard difficulty but the combat is fun.  The story is VERY good, it is very linear but it had me playing for hours to see where it was going.  If you are a Marvel fan you will enjoy this game, it brings the crew you know and throws them into a new adventure for you to control and make decisions.  While these decisions aren't very impactful, they do affect how you approach certain situations and how characters view you.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: - Rocket, seriously? "The Gardners of the Galaxy"?!- What? I let Groot fill in the form.- I am Groot.That summarizes this game, it's a fun, humorous space adventure with themes of heroism, teamwork, overcoming the impossible, friendship, and family. The combat can be braindead, it's probably better to play on the hardest difficulty to make it somewhat challenging at least but you play this game not for the combat but for the characters, story, and dialogues.I thoroughly had fun playing it and I already miss listening to those 5 argue with each other. This is what American action movies would be if they were good and funny.

_childDocuments_.review: After the debacle that was the Avengers game this was surprisingly a fun joy ride through and through.9/10I initially did not want to play this but after all the good reviews I picked it up on black Friday for cheep and spent the following two days glued to my TV.  GoodGreat Graphics - Have a new 3070 TI and was able to jack everything to max at 4K and it looked great.Great Music - As with anything Guardians Of The Galaxy it had great music but if I could change it I would have more of that great music during combat.Great Story - Its is a straightforward not to convoluted story (Except the last fight) and a joy to play.  It also is not to short or to long and ends on a good note.Voice Acting - The best part of the game is the acting and scrip.  You will laugh, may even cry but you will love it.  The banter between the cast cracked me up a lot but at times you can tell they did not record their lines with each other or even knew that one line was going to come after another. Not so goodControls - I started playing with mouse and keyboard and it felt weird and cumbersome but kept with it.  After about a quarter way through I tried my Xbox controller and it made it much easier to play but still not great.Combat - It was fun combat but both M/K and controller felt weird and clumsy.  The other characters do very little damage unless you manage them like crazy.  Also don't get the Knockdown Dash perk till the end or you will be dashing yourself off platforms like crazy.BadQuicktime crap - Yes there is quicktime events in this.  There are some that are a pain in the ass and others that are not bad.  I will say after 35% of the way through the game the pain ones dry up and you get used to the not so bad ones.Hills - There are parts where a drop off pop up while sliding and it will piss you off. So yea pick this up if you was a fun game that does not have a crap ton of glitches or micro transactions.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: It's the flarkin' Guardians of the Galaxy! What's not to love about that lovable bunch of a-holes?! The characters are all amazing, fun and true to themselves (well, Rocket starts out pretty cranky but gets better). There are plenty of times they had me chuckle and/or snort. The humor is certainly spot on and the voice acting was also great! The whole game feels more like an interactive movie, really. Very entertaining! The story is interesting and keeps you wanting to play to find out more. The worlds and environments are breathtaking! The music is also top notch and adds to the whole experience - to huddle up and then have Wake Me Up Before You Go Go blaring while you're taking out bad guys has been a special little treat! Quality content right there. The Bad: But sadly, there is... also plenty of bad. The awesomeness of the characters notwithstanding, there is often times SO much banter.. that it's really TOO MUCH banter. It gets repetitive, too. In general the audio kinda blips in and out or overlaps - both in combat and I've noticed it on the Milano (the ship) as well. Speaking of combat, that would be the next cringe factor to me - it's messy. Now, it might be a LOT better with a controller, but I am just not a big fan of them. I like to play the piano - aka mouse and keyboard. But it's really nothing but hectic chaos.. Until the very end I never quite felt like I was really in control - or knew totally what I was doing. Maybe it's intended to be that way? I do not know but did not enjoy it a whole lot. It had its epic moments (WHAM!) but on the whole.. meh. Now, the biggie... the bugs. And there are a lot of them. Very.. VERY annoying bugs... From combat that continued past defeating all the enemies, to Peter freezing in mid-fight until he got beat to death - one time he also just simply fell... and continued to fall... and fall... and fall - and Fing Fang Foom must have stepped on an especially painful Lego piece as he continued to shoot fire into the air, with one hit-point left and I had to reload yet another boss fight because nothing else would happen. THAT really took the fun out of it more times than not. Also, I never did quite get the oh-so-hyped-up Ray Tracing to work, I mean, it worked until it did not - and crashed. It would run alright for an hour or two, then bam (not Wham!). On top of all the other bugs, I simply turned it off, at least that stopped the crashes. The Ugly: There's really nothing ugly. Heck, the game is GORGEOUS! Even without ray tracing the graphics are absolutely superb and seriously delicious eye candy! Rating: So, all things considered, I am giving it a Thumbs Up because it is a cool game. I had fun. I also cussed a lot, screamed a bit, not sure I will be replaying it anytime soon, but it was certainly an adventure! 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: This game really bested my expectations. Combat was super fluid, graphics were beautiful, and the story had me hooked from beginning to end. I also couldn't get over the improvised banter between all the characters! The voice actors really didn't need to record as many lines as they did, but I'm so grateful for their efforts - it really helped me believe in the world of GOTG and had me deeply invested in the motivations and backstories of all the amazing characters you meet along the way. If you love Marvel, GOTG, or just great narrative-driven buddy comedies, this is your game! Can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember the 2013 Deadpool game? It had great dialogue, and somewhat repetitive, swarm-based combat. That is Guardians of the Galaxy. The story, dialogue, and camaraderie between the team? Excellent. The combat? It is repetitive, and swarm-based...as in, just tons of bullet sponges and enemies thrown at you. But if you are a Guardians of the Galaxy fan, it will be forgivable because they nail the comic-team dynamic, second to none.

_childDocuments_.review: If laughter is the best medicine, then Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is the intergalactic pharmacy you've been looking for!If you're like me and have always dreamt of being a superhero, but your only real superpower is being able to find the TV remote in the couch cushions, fear not! With this game, you can be the legendary leader of the galaxy's goofiest group of misfits, the Guardians of the Galaxy.First off, let's talk about Star-Lord, aka Peter Quill, the guy who looks like he raided a lost-and-found box from the '80s. With his hilarious one-liners and penchant for making pop culture references that only your dad would appreciate, he's the perfect mix of hero and goofball. Seriously, who else could pull off saving the galaxy while rocking a Walkman and a killer mixtape?Then there's Gamora, the deadliest woman in the galaxy. Sure, she may have a sword that could slice through a spaceship, but deep down, she's just a big softie... or at least as soft as someone who grew up with Thanos as a dad can be. Watching her deadpan reactions to the rest of the team's shenanigans is worth the price of admission alone.And let's not forget about Drax the Destroyer, whose idea of subtlety is about as subtle as a rocket launcher to the face. His complete lack of understanding of metaphors leads to some of the game's most side-splitting moments. Plus, watching him try to pet a space llama is a sight to behold.Rocket and Groot round out the team with their dynamic duo act. Rocket may be small, but he's got a big attitude... and an even bigger gun. And Groot? Well, he may only say three words, but he's got more heart than most of the characters in the Marvel universe combined. Plus, who doesn't love a talking tree that's basically a walking, talking houseplant?But it's not just the characters that make this game a laugh riot. The writing is sharp, the dialogue is witty, and the action is as fast-paced as Quicksilver on a caffeine bender. From battling cosmic baddies to navigating the complexities of team dynamics, there's never a dull moment in this game.So, if you're in the mood for a hilarious, action-packed adventure that's guaranteed to leave you in stitches, grab your controller and join the Guardians of the Galaxy on their quest to save the universe. Just don't forget to pack your sense of humor... and maybe a spare pair of underwear for when you laugh yourself silly!
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up the game due to the overwhelming positive reviews and because it seemed interesting. However, I do not think it is a good game. There doesn't seem to be any skill based content, so all players will effectively have the same experience, which is fine, but will tie into the rest of the review. It is slow-paced and story-driven, and the gameplay/combat feels more like an intermission between roaming and narrative than the actual content of the game. Supposedly your decisions matter, which is where I guess the gaming experience will deviate between players. Ultimately, for me, if the game is not fun to play and the redeeming quality is the narrative aspect of the story, I think this game could be enjoyed by watching someone else play. They are going to have the same combat, same content, and it will not deviate. You can just play a game that is actually fun or do something productive around the house while you stream the content. It would be the same experience, minus the chore of holding the controller/keyboard and mouse.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is more like it!  After the disaster that was Avengers, I was worried that everything coming from the “new era” of Marvel's digital entertainment division was going to be a soulless cash grab.  Luckily, Guardians of the Galaxy is the furthest thing from, and is a blast from start to finish.GotG is about as old school as a Triple A title gets these days.  Completely linear, single player, no online components, no currency, no battle passes, etc and it is a better game for it.  You can just focus on enjoying the game and the interplay between the characters and the amazing environments.  You control Peter Quill (Star Lord) only, but almost always have your trusty squad with you, Rocket, Groot, Drax, and Gamora, with some other guests along the way.  Combat is brisk and enjoyable, you mostly use your blasters with a little melee mixed in, you have strong dodge move, and you can command your buddies to do special moves, with additional moves unlocking as you work through the game.  At times it reminded me of a more modern, single player take on Marvel Ultimate Alliance and games like that.  The combat is not brutally difficult, but it is not mindless, if you do not pay attention you will be wiped out.  Basically, it seems like fun was prioritized over everything, when the combat engine was designed, and its a big win for the developers, as it fits this game like a glove.  The visuals in Guardians of the Galaxy are absolutely stunning.  Jaw droppingly detailed and incredibly imaginative alien landscapes and technology are constantly being thrown at you as you and your motley crew travel from system to system trying to save your own ass, and maybe the galaxy as well along the way.  The engine leverages all the modern bells and whistles including ray tracing, and was quite the workout for my 3060ti @ 1440/75.  The last thing I want to talk about, and by far the biggest reason the game is so enjoyable, is the writing, which is ⅔ fantastic and ⅓ normal pretty bad video game dialog.  The dialog between yourself and the other Guardians is so important to the game, and is its best feature.  It is wildly entertaining, laugh out loud funny, and bonds you much more to the team, making you care so much more about their fates.  It is an order of magnitude better than most video game scripts.  Well, let me expand on this a little because its so odd.  There are three main times in the game when there is dialog.  During cutscenes, when you are walking around and/or fighting during missions, and when you are on your ship between missions.  The cutscene dialog is excellent.  Natural, funny, well performed, the whole deal.  The in mission dialog is incredible, some of the best ever in a game.  The team banters while you walk around, the banter has to do with things actual plot points and things in the environment, sometimes you will even be given choices on what you want Quill to reply with, and everything is legitimately laugh out loud funny at times.  Amazingly, when you find a little secret side path the team will actually react as you explore it “Quill, where the hell are you going, thats the wrong way!” type of stuff.  Its really great.  In between missions when you are on your ship, there are a lot of optional conversations.  Both regular chats, where you can walk up to the other teams members and initiate a conversation and longer talks, where you discuss the hidden characters items that you can find during the missions.  Compared to the other writing in the game, these interactions are horrible.  Boring, rote, exposition dumps, with littler personality or excitement.  To be fair, its not much worse than most video game exposition, but with the rest of the writing being so stellar, it sticks out like a sore thumb.  Still, overall, the writing and dialog and performances are huge plus to the game, not a negative.In trying to crystalize my thoughts for this review and come up with a score, the game I kept ending up coming back to when evaluating Guardians of the Galaxy is Ryse Son of Rome!  I know that sounds bizarre but both games push many of the same buttons.  Pure linear games that give you the illusion of choice at times but nothing you do really affects much.  A leveling system that doesn’t really give you access to anything important and side paths that always lead to a reward of some kind and then put you right back on the main path.  Stunning, gorgeous graphics paired with B-movie-esque stories that are very enjoyable.  GotG gets an edge because of the great dialog discussed above.  Much like Ryse, GotG is greater than the sum of its parts, a cohesive, fun experience that I enjoyed very much.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Simple action game 3rd person shooter game - but it has some cool twists being able to command your fellow guardians to use special abilities. The combat is pretty fun overall, and there is some coordination on using the right gun types (shock, freeze, etc.) on the correct enemies to break down shields and stuff faster.Story is pretty great - fits right into the ridiculous ways the guardians will save the galaxy. The game is beautiful - scenes are amazingly well done and across several planets with alot of variety. Dialog, sound, everything about the game assets is stunning. My one complaint is maybe the fighting gets a little repetitive - it's a mix of story-based game and action (your dialog actually has story changing consequences) so I was happy overall in the amount of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Square Enix has disappointed me by not disappointing me.After Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy was announced sometime earlier this year, I was adamant in my belief that this would not be a good game. Square Enix's attempts at making a game out of Marvel's Avengers was still bitter in my tongue, and their continued dedication to making Avengers worse was not changing my mind. Up until about a day or two prior to this game's release, I was sure — Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy would suck.I'm writing this review five days post-launch and man, was I wrong.This game is dripping with character from every pore. The Guardians are all incredibly well-written, true to character, and funny. The gameplay is engaging, though the combat is simple, and every level varies things up and keeps the atmosphere of adventure going. Through it all, your eyes are constantly treated to a feast of lovingly rendered, gorgeous settings. The story is new, though there are familiar beats to it that both comic readers and moviegoers will recognize, and utilizes characters you might be familiar with in new and exciting ways. The soundtrack of select 80's music plus the new original songs written for the game are all on point.On top of all that, the game is also incredibly well-optimized, even with RTX on and all the other bells and whistles. That was another concern of mine when I first heard the download size would be 150 gigs before the optimized it and reduced it to around 80, but ooof. They did some good optimization work here. With every graphical setting at it's highest, my 2070 can maintain a stable 60 fps throughout, except in combat when there are some drops.Whoever made this game (Eidos-Montréal, I assume) has a true passion for video games, the Guardians of the Galaxy, and the larger Marvel universe and it is clear throughout the game.Other than the fact that the combat is simple, I literally have nothing negative to say about this game.As a Marvel fan who has been waiting for a good game, I am more than pleased, and I hope there is a sequel to this someday. And who knows, maybe if we're lucky enough, this team will tackle the Avengers next!

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? Wow! What a game. Easily one of my favorites this year. Speaking as a player who has completed 100% of the achievements in the game, it's a solid 9/10 for me. Really hope to see a sequel or some simple DLC (time trial challenges?) for this game.The character designs are all fantastic. The original designs for this game are great. The additional costumes you can unlock for the Guardians while playing are killer. They picked very well for the additional fashion and grabbed some of the best costumes I've seen the Guardians in. The environmental design is absurdly good. The different planets you visit throughout the game are just jaw-dropping. Absolutely gorgeous work on the set design too. You can see a lot of passion from the artists put into making these areas feel ALIVE, which is something a lot of studios criminally underestimate the impact of. The voice actors in this game all deliver their lines with PASSION. There are some truly emotional and gut-wrenching moments in this game and those would've been a lot less impactful if they were delivered by someone who just wanted their paycheck. Gamora and Drax both had some very heavy scenes and their voice actors were particularly phenomenal. You can really feel the pain of these characters in these moments. The jokes all landed very well. I went in thinking that they would go for cheesy, poorly-timed jokes with decent frequency. Instead, I found myself genuinely laughing along with the characters. The story of the game is great. There's a lot of 'hidden' lore that shows up in the form of communication logs, Guardian Collectibles,  the in-game compendium, and more. You can really get a feel for the world in this game and the developers really put work into making it feel fleshed-out, even for the characters you don't meet and the places you don't visit in a playthrough. The conclusion of the game was great. You get to make certain choices that impact the ending of the game in a few different ways. I won't say anything to spoil the moments, but rest assured that there is actually a great deal that changes because of what you choose. It's not a flat-out linear adventure where what you pick doesn't matter, thankfully.Photo mode is awesome. You get a lot of variety when it comes to posing, framing, lighting, etc. It's nothing as comprehensive as the Spider-Man Photo Mode, but you do get a lot of stuff to play around with. I am a huge fan of the photography options and just sitting around playing with the settings is a ton of fun. You can pull off some really satisfying shots. I've posted a few publicly, so check those out if you want some examples. There are a lot of appearances by noteworthy characters related to the Guardians of the Galaxy as a group. There are also some callbacks to others. I won't say anything here to spoil who shows up as a cameo and what guest characters play a huge role in the story, but rest assured that fans of the comics will be treated to a great lineup!!This game is phenomenal. My only complaint is that I wish there was more of it. You can 100% the game in a single playthrough, which is really neat. Eagerly anticipating the next release from the studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of my better RPG experiences in recent years. Is it an expansive open world romp? No. But it doesn't sell itself as such. It's a well told story with well written tight dialogue and some RPG elements from combat builds to relationship development. I believe its more contained plot and story elements gave developers more control in directing the player experience; which shows in spades in the jokes I actually laughed at and the characterizations and character development I actually cared about. If there is to be a sequel, It'll be a day-1 buy for me. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, one of the best games i had the pleasure to experience this year!It's simply beautiful and full of different cool looking planets & landscapes to explore, i also appreciate the game being linear instead of forcing it to be yet another hollow open world borefest. It also ran great for me aside from a few minor bugs.The characters are amazing, i loved each and every single one of the guardians, the voice actors did an amazing job with them! i also loved the constant banter between them, something that i've never experienced in other games before, not like this anyways, and i was genuinely surprised by the amount of unique dialogue they had, and how fun it was to listen to, it all felt true to the characters & helped immerse me even further & highly elevate the experience for me.Kudos to the devs for not only managing to make it not annoying having to listen to your crew talk almost all the time, but also fun and enjoyable!The game also has some very cool looking costumes for you to collect, and thankfully even though they're pretty hidden, i was still able to get all of them without having to rely on any external guides, the game also has some other collectibles that will triggers unique dialogues with your crew mates on the ship, which add some lore and backstory and help flesh out the characters even further, those seem to be even harder to find so you'll probably need a guide for them. (they're worth getting though, IMO anyways)The gameplay is also very fun & intuitive, you basically play as Star Lord, but also get to issue special commands to the other guardians to make them perform certain actions & moves, every character has a skill tree to unlock (including 3 skills you can get by spending points & a 4th final one you auto unlock by the final few levels as you advance in the story)all skills are fun to use, and i especially love Rocket's Five Barrel Barrage!(the Huddle system was also a cool surprise, but you'll have to find out about it yourself :P)I can't say i'm a comics guy, but i was exposed to a lot of marvel's characters & lore through other mediums including the movies and other games including Marvel Snap in particular, so i was able to recognize many of the Easter Eggs & hidden stuff & even some of the obscure characters included (the Rocket's move i spoke about earlier was one of the things i recognized, which made me super excited to finally acquire it & see how they would possibly animate it, it did not disappoint xD), the game is simply full of stuff like this, and you can tell the team behind this game had so much passion and love for it.I also really enjoyed the story, and consider it to be one of the better ones i experienced this year, i also constantly found myself genuinely laughing out loud thanks to the excellent dialogue, and the choices you make throughout the game seem to actually pay off by the end, so that was cool. oh, and you can also craft upgrades on different workbenches you'll stumble upon in each level, but there are only 15 upgrades in total which is a shame as i was hoping for more.All in all, this game was amazing for me, i simply could not get enough of it, and would totally buy the sequel if they ever make one (they totally should!), highly recommended! 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game but mainly because the story is a lot of fun. Specifically, the dialog and voice acting is great. The game has nearly non-stop banter between the various Guardians, and it's really well done and fun to listen to. The story is engaging and the cut scenes are very good (though there are too many). So I really enjoyed playing through the story. Unfortunately, the gameplay itself is mediocre. It's a linear 3rd person shooter in which most battles happen in small arenas - you basically move from one arena battle to another, interspersed by travel requiring some puzzle solving (mostly simple puzzles requiring you to use your team's abilities to get past obstacles). You only play as Starlord but in battle you manage your team's special combat abilities. This requires memorizing a lot of combinations of keys (press shift, select number for character then select number for skill). That was ok but you have to do this in the heat of battle and so I regularly was selecting the wrong key. All of that so far is fine, though I didn't find it more than ok. The two things I disliked most bout the gameplay were forced target lock and quick time events. - Quick time events happen throughout the story and I failed basically every one the first time it popped up (and I often failed many times), causing a death and reload. This was especially annoying because most autosaves are before unskippable cutscenes (why do games do this?) and most quick time events are after cutscenes. - The game has target lock (which apparently cannot be disabled) which interferes with your ability to control your character's facing/aiming. Having your character constantly turn away from where you are trying to look is immensely frustrating. This really undermined combat; I often just could not do what I was trying to do because I had target lock on some enemy and couldn't get it switched to the enemy I wanted (the one I was trying to aim at!). This was so frustrating that I almost gave up on the game multiple times. (Marvel Avengers did not do this, so why in this game?) There are also many times when the story/dialogue unnecessarily takes control of your character away from you, though that was just mildly annoying and didn't directly affect combat. Lastly, the game runs poorly on my PC. I don't generally have problems running any modern games but I had frequent periods where the frame rate dropped low enough that it impacted gameplay (including every scene that takes place in the Milano). I did not have any problems running Marvel Avengers. So, overall I enjoyed this experience, but that was because the story, dialogue and voice acting kept me wanting to see what happened next. The gameplay experience was marred by a few significant flaws that prevent me from rating this game anything better than "ok". Comparing to Marvel Avengers, also partly by the same studio - I much preferred the gameplay in Marvel Avengers, but that game suffered from being repetitive and having weak story and dialog.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game all-around, one of the best first-person games I've played in a while.  It's been out for a few years now, so I'm not going to rehash the great graphics, gameplay, etc.  I'm just focusing on the "little things" that impressed me.1) On normal difficulty, it's challenging without being frustrating.  Yes, there are several sections that I had to play more than once due to getting myself killed.  However, so far I haven't encountered any sections that I've had to replay more than four or five times, at a maximum.  Meanwhile, I'm watching my son repeatedly fail to kill the Rancor in Jedi: Survivor.  That doesn't look fun.2) Great dialogue, and use of dialogue to help the game.  If you run down a tunnel the wrong way, you can count on Rocket to shout insults.  Nice immersion.  The dialogue is both clever, funny, and non-repetitious.3) You can pause during cutscenes!  I'm gonna say it again: You can PAUSE during CUTSCENES!  Most game developers have no idea how important this is during single player games.4) I hate quicktime events.  I know, others like them, but when I'm calmly exploring, I don't want to be ready to perform a high-speed button-mash to prevent Quill from falling off a cliff.  And the game settings allow me to simply turn them off so they play as a cutscene.  Thank you.5) While it's a feature I would never use, the game gives players the option to switch the awesome 70s / 80s soundtrack with standard in-game music so streamers don't have to worry about music copyright violations.  The fact that the developers considered this means a lot.In short, the developers put some serious thought into ways to make the game fun for everyone, and it shows.  I don't know if the developer are working on a sequel, but if they are, I'll seriously consider buying it at full price, given my experience with the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:-------------The story is great, genuinely felt touched at some points and the humour mostly lands. I was surprised by how long the story was (I put in 16 hours for one playthrough). The gameplay has some cheesy moments but actually has some great moments of emmergent gameplay and a real sense of progression. The characters feel very inspired by the movies in a good way for the most part.I could not imagine a better soundtrack; there is a mix of both songs and a more formal orchestral OST - similar to the movies. Felt curated and matched the tone of the game really well. Also did not feel limited at all - I don't think I repeated a song more than twice in 16 hours. The Bad:----------Not in any way bad enough to outweigh the positives but the game is not perfect, biggest gripes are the bugs- I had to reset the protagonist about 8 times in the playthrough each time setting me back about 30 seconds to 3 minutes in cutscenes and gameplay. The animations can feel smushed together and discontinuous.  The story had a little bit of pacing issues in my opinion- without getting into spoilers, there were a few moments where I felt a lack of urgency on the Guardian's side. The movie comparisons - the game sits in a different universe or timeline or something from the movies and, whilst is a pretty easy recommendation whether you watched them or not, it kind of hurts it in 2 main ways - firstly the group seems freshly formed but seems to lack a large shared experience as to why they are together or why these selfish solo acts would be family or sacrifice for each other. I suspect this is like a hurried version of the first movie but I wish they had a large heist fail or jail escape or something to bind them better - or if there was, for it to be made more clear to the player somehow. Secondly I think it hurts the voice actors - whilst most of the cast in the GotG squad work well, Peter and Rockets' VAs are given the impossible task of immitating very unique famous movie stars, Chris Pratt and Bradley Cooper and I felt like it could be very jarring at some points when they got it slightly wrong - uncanny valley stuff - if you didn't watch the movie you should be fine. TLDR:---------Highly recommend this game at a sale: $15 is a great price for this experience. Pros far outweigh cons. PS: game experience is far better at a Normal Difficulty setting, higher difficulty will expose some of the underlying simple game mechanics and take you out of the game. Also leave hints on slow.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a fantastic ride that captures everything fans love about the Guardians, while delivering a compelling story and engaging gameplay.The character writing is excellent, each Guardian feels like they’ve stepped straight out of the comics and movies, and their interactions with one another are filled with humour, wit, and heart. The voice acting is also great, and I found myself genuinely caring about the story, especially as it delves into the characters' backstories and relationships.The combat is fun and dynamic, with the ability to control all the Guardians in battle while focusing on Star-Lord's abilities. It feels fresh, and there’s a lot of depth to how you approach each encounter. The environments are gorgeous, and there’s a nice mix of exploration and puzzle-solving to break up the action.What really stands out though is the emotional depth. I didn’t expect to feel so connected to the characters, but by the end of the game, I felt like I’d gone on a personal journey with them. The soundtrack is awesome too, bringing some great 80s tunes that fit perfectly with the vibe of the game.Whether you're a fan of Marvel or just looking for an awesome action-adventure game, Guardians of the Galaxy delivers on every level!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, one of the best I've played this year. GotG took me by a massive surprise, and it seems that SE has learned some sort of lesson coming from the dumpster fire that was the Avengers. The writing, voice acting, music and chemistry between everyone is 10/10. It really feels like a new movie, with extremely fun gameplay. Combat is great, the animations are fluid and smooth. It's extremely satisfying using all of the Guardian's abilities in unison with your own. This is a gem, and deserving of the utmost praise. If you're at all a fan of the movies, this is a must own.

_childDocuments_.review: I am here to assure you that yes - this is indeed not another Avengers. I genuinely enjoyed this game from start to finish. The story is very compelling and I found myself very invested in not only the main stories, but all of the side stories and anecdotes  you learn about all of the guardians along the way. There are a plethora of appearances from across the Marvel universe - both expected and not expected. Honestly this is just one of my top games of the year and I think it is well worth your time to play.Gameplay wise the combat is nothing special in my opinion. It is fun controlling all the guardians but you will find yourself doing the same repetitive combos after a while and most of the damage done will be done by your team and not Star-lord. What really kept me going was the Telltale like decisions and the ever expanding story. I couldn't help but feeling this game stole some of the magic from Mass Effect as well. You grow closer with your crew as the game progresses until you feel like a real team at the end. I will say that I have only completed the game once, however, so how much your decisions actually matter I am not sure.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've picked up a game and the gameplay struck me as fun. too often are things dragged out with xp requirements and grinding turning a fun 10 hour experience into a grueling 30+ hour slog through unimpressive dialogue and gameplay mechanics lacking in innovation. This is a fun 15 hour game that doesn't wear out its welcome, its a shame that it can't shake the stigma of the Square Enix Avengers game that suffered from aforementioned issues.What we have here is a game that wears its heart on its sleeve, an action adventure game with decision making that affects relationships between characters. definitely worth a try if you enjoyed what video games were prior to the whole games as a service idea.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for The Guardians of the Galaxy game.I bought it the first day I could.I had uneasiness buying this game. I had heard all about micro-transactions killing The Avengers game before this, and I didn't know quite what I was getting into. To my Joy, there Is no micro-transactions in the game!This game is so much fun and so easy to learn I got right into the action, and played for 3 hours straight. I Laughed and Loved the banter of the crew or their comments. This game is Not the movie, but has a few differences. When I was in game it didn't matter. The game is short for such a Lavishly appointed game. 15 to 20 hours and its not really open world even though, it Feels like it. Its a linear plot. All characters even the ones that have nothing to do with you are unique and seem alive, or just unconcerned with you. It Feels real, and alive. Its a cool feeling to check out the sights and look at All the beauty.Game play is great with an intuitive game system. It will take learning the signs to make a better Combo. Combo attacks make this game work. The team aspect of winning is amazing because the Leader of your group, The Star Lord, makes all decisions for the others in his group. It might seem weird but watch a few You tube videos of the game play and find the things you'll need to know before starting. It helped me.The game leaves me with the desire to play it More, and That's a mark of a great game. Its not Borderlands 3 deep but it is so beautiful an d colorful you'll be distracted with that.Play this game and then, play it again. I have seen so many people who do.I know I am going to.9-10 A must add to your game library. The game is too much fun to miss !

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is one the best games of this year.It's a blend of Uncharted, Mass Effect and FF7 Remake.The story is the highlight with story choices that do end up paying off or hurting you in the duration of the campaign. The characters are expressive and carry a lot of heart. The story hits some very high emotional moments.Gameplay is linear with focus on exploration while combat heavily derives from FF7 Remake where you give commands to your team mates while you build up combos. The combat I found really fun.The game is gorgeous. The facial animations are some of the best I've ever seen! Rivaling games like The Last of Us and God Of War.Soundtrack is fantastic. The random 80's hits that plays on the ship or after you pump up your Guardians during combat never gets old.Don't go in expecting anything MCU. It's a team of different Guardians with a very different and crazy story.Play this game if any of this speaks to you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're someone like me and likes to scroll through the negatives of a game before buying them then this review is for you !First and foremost, you gotta understand what this game is and what it isnt:In short, this game is for someone who would enjoy some humour, narrative and rich lore, character development and just pair well with some popcorn because I definitely felt like enjoying a 30 hours Guardian of the Galaxy movie session. You do have some role play fun as Star lord by picking some dialog choices ( which bring minor changes to the story ). There's not so much depth to the combat system and boss fight but its still interesting and fun. Don't expect lots of customizations, high skill ceiling or crazy build out of this game's mechanic and combat. In the end, the third person action combat is secondary and the narrative, role playing, character development and humour is primary.I highly recommend that you play this game with that in mind and you will get the most out of your experienceIn my personal opinion, this game did a much better job of building the relationship between the guardians than the MCU movie due to the length time you get the explore and connect with each guardian. If you felt like both MCU movies are a bit rushed, this might be the version of the Guardians that you will actually enjoy. I rarely leave a review for a game but this one certainly deserves its praise and I hope Eidos-Montréal will learn from its success to make better games

_childDocuments_.review: Hard recommend, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy was definitely an unexpected surprise after seeing the announcement. The trailers didn't sell me on it at all and frankly, I was sad to see Eidos-Montreal making this. I'm a huge Deus Ex fan and my first thoughts were along the lines of "Why this? and not the sequel Mankind Divided rightfully deserved?" But I was happily proved oh so wrong.Despite what Eidos-Montreal has made in the past, this game is quite linear. I would compare it more to something like Uncharted or the newer Tomb Raider games. Puzzles, combat, and navigating alien worlds is most of what you'll be doing. However, it has a slew of dialogue choices and direct choices that affect the outcome of the story. Main theme of the whole thing is teamwork makes the dream work. All puzzles and combat situations are a team effort and as the Leader of the Guardians, you'll be giving orders and trying to keep them from killing each other.Pro's: A great story with a surprising amount of emotional highs and lows and thank the lord, an actual ending. The combat is fun, fast, and satisfyingly unique. The soundtrack has a treasure trove of classics, and a whole album made by a fictional band to tie in to the story. (that is also very good) Lots of great Marvel cameos and some big names that play a big role in the story. There's stuff in there for the MCU fans but quite a bit more for the comic buffs. Decision making that has some actual impact on the way characters see the Guardians and how they act towards the end. P.S. the huddle mechanic is pretty hypeCons: Bugs. Not a ton but a couple of animation bugs that effect some cool moments. One ♥♥♥♥♥♥ one that kept me on a ledge forever, but nothing that kills the whole thing. Dialogue can be a bit hammy if you're not a fan of the MCU style banter, and some that is hammy even so. Not a fan of the voice actor picked for Quill.In conclusion, a full recommend from me. Support Eidos-Montreal!P.P.S there's some fun little nods to Deus Ex for the fans out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I've yet to finish the game but I want to share how much stupid-good fun I am having with GotG.I definitely underestimated it after the reception of SE's disastrous Marvel Avengers, but there's something incredibly unique and special to be experienced here. Sure it's not the most perfect or mind-blowing game out there, but the overall direction of the game is incredibly entertaining.The game is graphically beautiful, with strong character modelling, environment sets and solid animation work -- the magic I feel is in how all these elements combine together contextually with the amazing writing and voice acting. I feel deeply for these characters and know I will be a life-long fan of this game and its iteration of GotG.The combat is somewhat clunky, although jetting around and commanding the other Guardians to execute a move or two is fun and fast-paced. You can tell it is not the focus of the game, although it improves as you buy upgrades.There are also visual/environmental glitches, but I can easily overlook these as they don't break the game, and for me, it's an amazing achievement from SE altogether.Overall, it's a great time with its stellar narrative providing a hugely entertaining and slapdash adventure in space.

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everyone.This is kind of difficult but I would rather say yes than no, but for the first time I really wish there was an option of neutral review. It is difficult to recommend this game since it is unexpected in many ways and more than once you would not be sure whether it is good or bad. First of all the combat is unusual to say the least. You play as Peter and run around arena and shot your blasters. But you also issue commands to your teammates. Each guardian will obtain up to 4 skills which are great but they will not use them until you say so, there is stagger mechanic which works as a stun and there are finishers it all requires some getting used to. You will also have to dodge constantly, since most of the time you are the target, break enemy shields with specific elements, since you are the only one who can, and also disarm long-range enemies. It all feels like you try to write a code while running a marathon. Well not exactly like this, but it is a bit frustrating more so if you play on the higher difficulty. About this as well, there is absolutely no point in playing on higher difficulty, enemies apart from rare cases specific mecahincs are mostly just sponges. If you put your damage ouput to lower levels, you would be just running and deal miserable damage all the time and rely only on skills which also do underwhelming damage until you get better options. Also there is this strange huddle up mechanic that makes no sense.What I liked is the story and interactions. It is a bit cheesy and even cringy sometimes, but it is a great Marvel story with a lot of characters each with their own quirks. You have some choice making options which have minor impact on gameplay but it is fun to listen to banter among Guardians or their mocking of some enemies. Characters are great and I like them more than their movie counterparts mostly. At the end of the day I enjoyed how the story concluded.The other stuff to notice is that:- Game run poorly on steam deck, that green mark is a lie. I had to change some compatibility to even run some levels and even then it was bearable at best- I had some crashes both on deck and pc. But it is AAA game so I will give it a pass- Some achievements are buggy, so keep that in mind.OSTs are great but those in the movie were much better.
