_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardian of the Galaxy is a genuinely delightful surprise especially considering at the time Marvel’s Avengers was our latest introduction to the universe in the gaming format.Released 1 year after the absolutely awful Avengers game, this had everything going against it and I am so happy that I managed to give it a go and see it through to the end.About the game;You take control of Peter Quill and his band of a recently formed Guardians of the Galaxy. You go toe to toe against some impossible odds and learn so much about these characters and understand why their bond is so strong. All characters and their performances are delivered so well and the actors behind them deserve praise.Firstly, I like these characters much more than the movies. The reason why this game worked and avengers did not work is simply down to how they were introduced to us. This is a new team and they are learning to trust each other throughout their journey whereas in avengers we’re meant to assume we know or care about them which we don’t.I am beyond elated that Peter Quill in this game is not Chris Pratt. He’s not the best leader and based on some of the dialog options you select, won’t make the best decisions either but he’s someone the team can rely on (I think, maybe. probably not).Drax the destroyer, much like his character portrayed in the movies is such a pleasure to be around. His extremely literal understanding of words to his neutral delivery of his sad back story telling makes him my favourite character in this story. Also, mad titan killer (allegedly). I love this design of Gamora and her realistic rational and logical demeanour. She’s one of my favourite strong female characters ever made.If you’ve ever seen the movies then you already know what Rocket is like. He’s short tempered, self-centred and quick to make dumb decisions but always has a plan to get out of a jam.I love Groot.Not using the likeness of the movies at first seemed like a bad idea. We got a taste of what it was like when Avengers came out and it was rough. In this game, however, it’s one of its biggest strengths and I look forward to playing future games with these characters.There’s a nice mix of story and gameplay here with the latter being repetitive in the later chapter. You take the role of Peter Quill and can’t switch or change between all the characters which might seem boring but you can command your team and combo abilities into each other for some satisfying effects. The synergy between characters is really fun and makes combining together abilities such as Groot’s CC and then Gamora’s high damage pop so nicely.The visuals for this game are so impressive. Every location is new, fresh and visually striking. Even though it’s a linear game there was still a bunch of little side tracks to explore and find hidden items. No location apart from revisits are the same and with the amount of content in this game, it really made me want to see what comes up next.The music is just fantastic. There’s a feature to have a banging soundtrack or have a ‘streamer mode’ which does not play any copyrighted music. I did not select that option but it’s nice to know it exist given how popular the songs are and how quickly they would be picked up for DMCA strikes if you streamed.The technical performance of this game is good. I’d like to mention that I played about 20% of this game on my PC and the rest on my steam deck. On the PC, it ran really good on my 3080 with no issues from what I remember. This game runs steady at 40fps with some FSR options on the steam deck which is fine for the small screen.Things I don’t like;-	The combat really starts to drag on once you have unlocked all the abilities. It feels rewarding to unlock more and more but once I finished, I just wanted to finish the story.-	Sometimes when travelling through the maps, you’ll come across forks in the road. Some will take you to a dead end with an item hidden or one will progress you further down your mission and you won’t be able to back track.Overall I think this game would appeal to anyone looking for a fun and deep story, after all, it did win best narrative from the game awards for its writing. If you enjoyed the movies as well then this is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: For the £25 sale price, this was a very well put together and enjoyable action-adventure game, though I can't say the original £50 was an appropriate tier. The narrative and pace of the game is generally well executed with plenty of interesting set pieces, well written/voiced plot and biome variety. The combat is... passable, if a bit repetitive, without much character development, where you should expect just a few linear perk/ability unlocks and not any builds or variation.You definitely  buy this game if you're looking for a competent third-person shooter, a deep RPG or a serious team tactics game. This game has a pretty focused scope and, whilst it dips in to a lot of other areas, it is an action-adventure through and through.I would say that, along with seemingly a fair few people, I'm kind of burnt out on Marvel properties at this point but I did enjoy it thoroughly and I'd give it a try despite that. Especially if it's at the far more reasonable half price.

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated Gem - One of the Best Superhero GamesThis game blew me away! I am honestly really sad that it did poorly financially because that means we probably will never get a sequel.Here are the positives:- The graphics are truly next-gen. The game looks incredible.- The story is super fun with lots of twists and turns. It is incredibly well paced. Expect 15-20 hours.- Great achievement design. You can get them all in one play through if you are intentional with collectibles (which are not excessive).- The combat is very fun. You play as Star Lord but command the whole team with special abilities and group combos. It is very satisfying and fun. Ability progression is perfectly balanced throughout the game. Love the combat!- Movement feels great.- The villain is awesome and very comic book accurate!- The cast is easily the best part. You will love this version of the guardians. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: 8/10Story was much more engaging than I expected. Voice acting was top-notch. Visual style was excellent - really vibrant with a huge variety between different locations.However, the game frequently crashed during cinematic scenes. Thanks to auto-save, this never set me back too far, but it was annoying and drained the moments of dramatic tension. Happened about 10 times total. Also had a few moments where I was confused by the interface or by the level design and ended up just feeling annoyed until I finally figured out what the game wanted me to do.Last complaint is that the combat is so chaotic that I often didn't know what was happening and sometimes lost track of the objective completely. I adapted to this by focusing on the button shortcuts for a few companion moves and spamming those, but I feel like I didn't get much use out of about half the special moves. Despite this, I would still definitely recommend the game as an action adventure with a fun and far-reaching story. And there is NG+ if you really want more time to test out the combat.Took just under 20 hours to complete with all upgrades done and about half of the unlockable outfits found. I thought the alternate outfits were all terrible, but that's okay because I liked the default ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game so it gets a thumbs up, but with some pretty significant caveats. $15-$20 felt like a very good price point and the game is frequently on sale so I recommend waiting for one.In short the story and characters were great and the combat was pretty good, but the level design was bland and repetitive and the game doesn't have a lot of depth to it.Let's start with the characters. These are much more faithful to the marvel comics than the MCU, which for me was a plus. While Rocket and Groot aren't much different, I liked the version of Star Lord better, and pretty much every other character is a significant improvement - Gamora, Drax, and Mantis especially. The characters that were original for the game (or obscure enough that I didn't recognize them) were also very well done for the most part. Without spoilers the story is fairly simple but manages to go through the satisfying emotional triggers of tugging on the heartstrings and producing laughs at the antics of the cast. It very much stays in its lane as far as what a comic book based game is expected to deliver, and I think that's a good thing.The combat is pretty fun, and the gimmick of having your guardian buddies as basically power moves you can drop on the enemy worked for me and it did make you feel like the team leader calling the shots. But the fights got repetitive. There's a decided element of - beat five of these guys, now beat five more with a few powered up ones thrown in, now beat ten, that gets a bit tiresome. The combat engine feels like it could have done more. There really is no exploration or choices that matter much (some do to a minor degree) and the hidden objects system of finding stuff that unlocks new conversations with your buddies or costumes for them felt very skippable. I found really cool costumes for Gamora (Black Vortex, hell yeah) and Rocket (business suit!) in Chapter 13, but never really found anything for the other guardians that I liked better than their base outfits. There's a decent amount of lore dumps in the codex/journal system that the game never reminds you exists and you can safely ignore. None of the 'hidden' objects are really that hidden. You pretty much have a linear path through the story with obvious sidepaths where all the hidden things are. I stopped bothering at a certain point as none of them really did much.The worst part is the level design. While you go to all sorts of amazing cosmic places it seems that no matter where you end up you will be sliding down the same sorts of ramps, walking sideways through the same tight spaces, and crawling through the same sorts of tunnels. It gets old far faster than the spectacular locations should. Also, I don't know who QTEs are for but it sure isn't me.Technically the game was very good. No crashes, and only one major bug which forced a reset where I was somehow out of combat and couldn't get hurt or hurt anything but the frequent autosaves meant I didn't really lose any time. Load times are a bit longer than you would think, but hardly to the point of annoyance.If you see a sale and you're a fan of the characters, this is a definite recommend. If you don't care or know who the Guardians of the Galaxy are, I doubt the game can really hold its own enough to keep your interest.

Exploring different planets, uncovering secret costumes scattered around in hidden areas is made more fun by the hilarious banter between the team and I mean it when i say its hilarious like its laugh-out-loud level of hilarious and this also makes it quite clear that the writing and voice-acting is phenomenal. The story was fine with some uncharted-like big set pieces and awesome moments scattered in-between. I cant help it but feel like it overstayed its welcome, that's my only complaint with this game.pog/10

_childDocuments_.review: + The game is astoundingly beautiful to look at.+ It is unapologetically Guardians of the Galaxy. The near-constant banter alone is fantastic.+ The story is great and takes you to a myriad of different locales with tons of Marvel characters and references.+ The time and effort put into the gradual examination of each character provide far more entertainment and artistic value than the constraints of the film medium allow.+ No microtransactions (looking at you, Avengers).- Controls (M&K) are unresponsive and sluggish. The game has trouble recognizing mouse and keyboard input so it'll take a couple of presses for virtually any command you want to give to go through. It is so infuriating, like trying to run in a dream.- 'Slide' controls are even worse, one second a press of a button barely moves you, the next you're on the other side of the screen with the camera having trouble following you.- The UI occasionally just vanishes, so you have less of an idea what's happening. Also, often when you pick up a collectible, the UI stays in collectible mode, so you can't do anything else without reloading your save.- The game has an option for 144fps yet it caps mine to 60? A simple google search indicates this is a common issue.(It seems that the different RTX settings cap the framerate at different intervals although tbh I can't see any improvement beyond the lightest setting)- The team's dynamic is very flavourful, but story beats always interrupt conversations. Terrible tempo there.- Whoever designed the spaceship segments should not be allowed to design or play another video game ever again.- I got stuck in objects more often than should be expected in a game of such renown.- Most collectibles are practically invisible.- Somewhat confusing and non-responsive quicktime events.- Uninspired skill tree.- Unskippable cutscenes. Also, the way you can skip bits of dialogue is horribly done.- Helmet vision. Thank ♥♥♥♥ it's not like Arkham Asylum detective vision, you don't need to have it on all the time.- Occasional freezes and crashes.? Drax has jiggle physics on his pecs, lats, and triceps? Why?I give this a thumbs up for the astounding graphics, exhilarating story, and faithful representation of the characters. But just barely.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a lot better than I had anticipated and a sorely needed recuperation for the Marvel franchise in particular after their previous Avenger's game. Guardians of the Galaxy is more reminiscent of the source material from the comics and not the cinematic universe which is both refreshing and pleasant. The dialogue, while sometimes falling flat, does an excellent job of making the team feel alive and idiosyncratic. Some moments are genuinely really funny and add personality to the team's dynamic. I am not 100% sure how much in-game choices affect the overall story arc, but the moments you make a choice seem like they impact at least the following moments to a significant degree. The combat is fun, albeit slightly clunky to work with especially if you are playing without a controller. Controller support is great, even changing input graphics to match the type of controller (Xbox, PS4, etc...) which is a nice QOL benefit. At the time of writing this, there are few bugs that I found a bit annoying such as audio sometimes not showing up, your mouse still being on the in-game screen after using the menu, weapons being in a characters hand during a cutscene when it's obvious the shouldn't be, and sometimes dialogue choices bug out if you choose too late. Overall I am enjoying this game, but there are a few bugs that require ironing out. Otherwise - my only other frustration is that in the games admittedly valiant and appreciated attempt to make dialogue more dynamic and prompted by your decisions, actions, and movements as a character, sometimes separate dialogues can intercept with each other, and while nothing ever plays simultaneously, it can be difficult to keep track of conversation that overlap each other by accident.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks great, controls are tight (I recommend a controller), gameplay is hectic and fun, funny and endearing dialogue between the whole team, and a compelling story to boot.  If you've been looking for a Marvel game that's actually fun - look no further.The banter among the team is awesome and very intuitive, and supplemented by great voice acting talent.  They also waste no time introducing the team.  If you've watched any of the recent GotG films, you'll feel right at home with this cast.  Sometimes I forget Rocket isn't actually voiced by Bradley Cooper.  Game is about 15-20 hours if you rush through.  Gameplay is similar to Marvel's Avengers, albeit more refined and less mtx-oriented.  You are presented with various different timed decisions, which can affect the method of getting from point A to point B, but typically doesn't change the overall outcome.  Still, it's enough to make another playthrough interesting enough to try the other possible paths.All in all, this should be the standard for Marvel games in the future.  A nice self-contained story that helps develop the heroes, and having a good time while doing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game with zero to none expectations, but oh boy oh I was so wrong.This game somehow managed to bring a smile to my face and made me giggle lots of times which I am extremely grateful about. The dynamics of the team is very well written and every dialogue option you choose seems to have an effect of some kind. Which also applies to other little choices you do throughout the game. Even though you think that actions means so little or has no meaning it actually builds up later and affects the game in some sort. The combat felt fun for most of the time, but some enemies were just bullet sponges and were a partykiller. I guess thats just the side effect of me playing in the hardest difficulty. But after getting some hefty upgrades and unlocking new skills they did not bore me. Being the leader and directing the team really felt amazing along with the dialogue options.I really don't want to spoil the game for those who want to play it, it was an amazing experience for me story felt good and never made me feel bored, on contrast I was wondering what would happen on the next chapter. It made me feel like I was watching a really good film serie and I wanted more in every chapter. If they ever make a second game I think they should add side missions and non-story related gigs/jobs for us to do as GARDENERS OF THE GALAXYAnd I want to finish this review with those magical and meaningful words which rebel our most pompous, esteemed and prestigious poets.I am Groot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game on the adventure/banter/characters side is absolutely stellar, it made me laugh several times and it's just downright enjoyable. Fights are.. well, itself the model is fun, you control Peter Quill directly and the other Guardians by giving them orders, but it gets a bit repetitive and some fights are a tad annoying. I've heard it didn't have too much success and they won't make a sequel, it's a shame because I'd definitely play it. There are many choices but most of them make the story "deviate" a bit but mostly lead in the same direction, sometimes granting/ not granting you help from some secondary character; collectibles and costumes are quite easy to find, if you're so inclined, and often offer additional lore to the game. Overall recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the galaxy is my game of the year so far, with no microtransactions or garbage multiplayer insight. The outcome is a visually stunning game with a killer soundtrack and beefy story. The relationships and banter between the characters keep the game fresh throughout and add some generally heartfelt moments to tug on the old strings. There're always choices to make or voice dialogues to choose from, which adds some surprising twists to your playthrough and gives the game that replayability once it's all said and done, which is a nice touch. Sure it doesn't change things massively, but it does just enough to tease you into a new game plus to see what might happen. The combat is simple but fun. Although I feel it could, have been improved slightly. Each character has unique abilities, "4 in total." Which can create some deadly combinations, once combined, and some fun gameplay moments visually. I almost slept on this game, which would have been a mistake. Solid, 8.5 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It was such a good game that felt like I was watching a new GOTG movie. The visuals, graphics, dialogues, facial expression, story and MUSIC all those are gonna make you feel like you're watching a movie. The only problem was this game has an optimization issue. _childDocuments_.review: The game is GREAT! The amount of love, care and passion put onto this game is astounding! The story is compelling, all the characters are unique with interesting personalities, every single Guardian of the Galaxy gets their shine in the spotlight. Gameplay is satisfying, though more melee combos and abilities would have been nice. Costumes are nice, but could be better (Rockets „The Stinger" is THE BEST ONE HANDS DOWN). Quick time events are cool. BUT MAN, this game needed a few more months in the oven due to bugs (texture bugs where an invisible object will act like a wall and you can not proceed to your objective, or just blocking the view of an entire cutscene, but they don't happen often, so it's not really a biggie and a few crashes), but that could just be me with my outdated pc :) And I see the devs putting bug fixes, which is really nice to see. OVERALL, 9/10 (Since I'm a huge superhero fan). It's a must play for any action adventure enjoyer and marvel fan, with references that will put a smile on your face :)I hope we see a GOTG 2, with MORE boss fights, improved combat, more frequent use of the Milano (make it upgradable, more weapons, skins), MORE WORLDS TO EXPLORE! Holy scut can't wait to see waht the future holds!

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie i wasnt expecting a quality game as i know almost every game based on movies (especially so if its a superhero one) are literally trash that been made just to service and satisfy its fans. BUT.. This game is different. Its not short, i completed it in about 18 hours, has some quailty mechanics and although its not the best it still has a good story. The combat is not that great and doesnt feel special but i cant say its so bad that it affects the experience. Actually i understand why they made the combat so simple. Imo the reason is that you can pretty much control the whole team not just yourself. They probably just thought that if they make a complicated fight mechanics over the team management it will tire and bore the player. Anyway none of these matters as this games dialogues are just EPIC. They're just too beautifully designed and placed that you cant really focus on the other things at all. Im literally in love with the conversation the characters have with other team members and the way they make fun of each other. _childDocuments_.review: An underrated gem of a game. The story, the characters, the cinematic set-pieces, the graphics, the locations you go to, and the amazing implementation of classic 80's rock and pop music. All of those make this game a worthwhile 20-25 hour banger experience. Playing through this and listening to all of the characters banter, their stories, their grievances, their regrets, and their love for each other on the team, makes me want to spend more time with them. Unfortunately, because of Square Enix's bad decisions causing their recent "western" titles to "underperform," it hurt the potential interest in this game and made this game "underperform" like Square Enix's other Marvel child. Ultimately, this led to Square Enix selling off some of their studios, including Eidos Montreal. Sad to say that we probably won't see a GotG2 anytime soon.Only problems I had with the game were the gameplay being repetitive and some performance hiccups. The gameplay is simplified to pretty much holding left trigger/right trigger (or M1/M2) then occasionally commanding your squad to do various attacks that you unlock throughout the game. The enemies are very bullet-spongy at least on normal difficulty, so you'll spend a lot of time shooting tanky enemies. It's not terribly bad, it's just serviceable to the story which is phenomenal enough to go through. In the 25 or so hours I spent in the game I haven't crashed once, but I did have a few stuttering issues throughout the levels. I imagine this is from the game loading in new areas as you go through the levels, so I would probably recommend putting the game on an SSD at least. There was one section of the game where you're placed on a planet with a ton of fog and I was constantly stuttering playing through about the first half of the level. I restarted the game and it fixed the stuttering, so if you do experience stuttering issues on certain levels, try to restart the game.TL;DR 9/10 worthwhile 20-25 hour experience with amazing set-pieces, characters and story. Gameplay is serviceable but a little repetitive with performance hiccups, but it could depend on hardware. Definitely buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: 11 hours in, and really mixed feelings.I'll start with the Pros:The interpersonal banter is fun.  Even though the voices are all wrong, or awful in Groot's case, I got used to them, and found myself mostly enjoying their banter and interactions, which were pretty true to form.  Except Rocket.The environments, and especially the locations like Quill's(Rocket's) ship, and Nowhere, are just really interesting places to explore.  I spent over an hour just looking around in Nowhere.  Lots of personality in this game, and much more than expected from bit characters around Nowhere.  It felt expansive and alive! Honestly, it was more fun than most of the combat.Cons:But that's because the combat isn't very good.  Having to shoot everyone dozens, often hundreds of times, while hopping around in what is effectively a cage, isn't fun.  A lot of the enemies are little more than geometric shapes. (I'm not kidding!)  The controls only work when they want to, and just toggling the visor often takes 3 tries, let alone the regular fail-jumps to my death.  Unresponsive controls are unacceptable.  And then there are those DDR moments where you hit one key out of timing and die, and have to watch a whole cinematic over.....and over, and over.......  after a 20 second load time on a black screen!Finally, In the movies, Rocket Raccoon is my favorite Guardian, but (so far)this game seems to have taken away his heart.  He's getting hard for even me to like.  Rather than a reluctant hero, he just seems to be a terrible person with no loyalty or compassion at all.  I hope the story can salvage him.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the previous Marvel game tarnish this one reputation; Guardian of the Galaxy is a solid game. The good third parties games that we used to have during the seventh generation of consoles (Xbox 360, PS3, Wii).Cons: - Technical bugs creating softlock; usually you can simply reload a previous checkpoint which are very abundant; - If you move around too fast, dialogues will fight for your attention, meaning that you'll often hear the beginning but not the end of some discussions. If you really want to hear everything, you kind of have to stay still and wait for it to finish; - You can't manually save, so if you like to save scum and see what happens depending on your choices, you'll have to replay specific chapters again or try new stuff in the new game plus; - Not all guardians are created equal; some of your team members have more time fleshing them out than others. Without saying too much, some get a chapter for them, and others only get a cutscene.Pros: - Personally, I found the writing great. It's an origin story; therefore, the guardians are a dysfunctional family, and their banter is solid and consistent. It might be bothering for some since you rarely get a moment of silence; - You can only play Star-Lord, which could be a deal-breaker, but honestly, the fact that you're controlling your team during the fighting sequence is satisfying when you nail the combos; - Additionally, as mentioned prior, some choices impact how the story flows; there is even prompts telling you which decision resulted in that outcome; - You probably won't like the soundtrack if you don't like 80s music. They did create their own fictitious 80s hair metal band named Star-Lord, and honestly, they are worth a listen; - Sad that it's a selling point, but there is no microtransaction or loot boxes; there are cosmetics, but you have to find them while playing, which is nostalgic; - A playthrough lasts around 15 to 25 hours, and most of it doesn't feel like it's there to add tedious filler content for the sake of longevity; it's well-paced and knows when to stop.All around, I highly recommend Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy if you're a fan of narrative-driven single-player games and you're not fed up with the Marvel Universe.

_childDocuments_.review: This should be a thumbs down. The performance is terrible (I've had to lock in at 30 on an RTX3080), the combat is a mess and levels either have too much or not enough of it, dialogue gets cut off frequently as sequences aren't timed to fit it all in, flying sections are confusing and infrequent enough that you forget the controls, and overall it just feels lacking in refinement.But... God is it fun, the writing is peak Marvel but that's exactly what you want from a Guardians of The Galaxy game, the plot is genuinely interesting, it's funny and heartfelt and genuine. And it looks gorgeous - when it's not lagging or dropping frames.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game. Just a solid, fun action adventure game with tons of humour, heart, and character. If you want a relatively short (20 hr), lighthearted space sci-fi romp with some emotional moments, this is it.- Great humour and writing. The witty banter never got grating or obnoxious. Dialogue was well-written and very funny, acting was great, and the characters really stood out. - Each character felt unique, and I came to love them all. They all had touching backstories that I came to learn about during cutscenes and gameplay, and it never felt like overt exposition or trying to make me sympathise with a character.- Weird sci-fi. The worlds of GotG isn't grounded in reality, and really goes wild with the imagination when it comes to strange alien worlds/planets.- Using each guardian's special moves was fun, and combining their powers was quite satisfying.- Gorgeous graphics and stable performance.- Combat gets somewhat repetitive over time. By the last 1/3rd of the game, you've kind of seen everything there is in terms of progression.- Odd graphical glitches. When a cutscene cuts to a new shot, the frame sometimes takes a second to smoothly render, causing a stutter. - Overstays its welcome by a couple of hours. By the end, it wasn't doing too many new things gameplay-wise to keep me hooked. I still enjoyed it, but the story was far better than the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun setting brought to life by vibrant graphics and enjoyable combat, but made quite exhausting by sheer amount of dialogue. I cannot stress how badly this game handles dialogue pacing -- not only is there never a lull in conversation, characters seemingly fall over themselves to comment on the environment, the story, something you're doing or should be doing, and these voicelines constantly overlap or interrupt each other. Taking five steps forward is enough to interrupt dialogue for a mundane "Look up there!" voiceline and this became very frustrating very quickly. It is worse during the already chaotic combat where now all the party banter is shouted, alongside callouts for what enemy to focus on and teammates signalling they're ready for a special attack -- there's always someone speaking, all the time.Which is a shame because the characters come more to life than in any of the movies, and the typical quippy Marvel banter that I've grown to hate in the movies, is pretty enjoyable and the humour is fine if never laugh-out-loud funny. All in all, I don't regret playing it and I would recommend it to Marvel fans but anyone who isn't already invested in the MCU can safely give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: You're in for a hell of a good time.Easiest (and shortest) way i can sum this game up is that, in ways, it's like The Witcher in space, but split amongst your team of 5 with splashes of Mass Effect and the like.  The game play is varied greatly, and the emphasis on team work is enforced very well - it's never at all forced or feels over baring to a point where battles become a pain in the ass.  Above all, the game-play is fair.  There is hand to hand combat as well and classic run and gun approaches to fighting, and the unlock-able moves for each of the Guardian's feels both rewarding and satisfying when you unlock them.I've seen loads of folks moan about the appearance of the Guardians, but for the love of god just remember its NOT  a movie based game, its a series based one from the comics - so take what you will from the design, I for one really like the redesign.  The story is rich and immersive, with a 'choices matter' element thrown in, and it works really well.  Actually, the story is great, and when i play, I'm always wondering whats happening next as the game's take on the characters has made me fall in love with each of them all over again. One of my favourite things about the characters and story is how much it immerses the player in with the narrative and the crew.  Every interaction you'll have throughout the game comes across as genuine, and the characters really pop to life and feel very believable - deff something that more studios should aim to create these days.  The graphics are gorgeous - running on a ryzen r9 5900x, 32gb, rtx 3070'oc GPU,  Ive only encountered frame drops once so far, and this was with DLSS running on quality mode with every setting at max/ultra.Overall, I'm very surprised at just how well Guardians of the Galaxy turned out, and it is for sure a game i will be recommending to people and replay again once completed.  The humour is spot on, the soundtrack is fantastic, dialogue is well and responsibly written - and above all, the game play is FUN and the story is FUN.If, like me, you wanted to take a break or slow down from FPS games and online games, this is for you.  The game oozes charm and charisma, and as a fan of the comic books and science fiction in general, i couldn't be happier.  Well done devs.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the best games on the market for fiction fanatics. This piece of art from Square Enix takes the player on a wild roller coaster filled with twists and turns. Let's break it down and discuss the key elements:My experience with gaming has so far been only improved with Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy. _childDocuments_.review: When people said this game was amazing, I had no idea what they meant. The characters come to life, the writing is fantastic, the story is immersive, and the world-building is beautiful and astounding. If i could sum it up easily, it's like Mass Effect for Marvel fans, but with much more comical writing and banter. You don't change your weapons as in ME, but the interactions between characters and finding things are very similar. Also you can't deploy things to planets to mine. It's a pretty linear story, but it's a good one at that. I, for one, am sick of the open world gimmick. No one has been doing it right. Open world doesn't mean freedom. It's an illusion. Get this game, ESPECIALLY on sale. There are some bugs, but you can find workarounds that are not laborious. I am not a Marvel nerd, but I am a fan. I grew up on Deadpool/Wolverine/X-men, etc. Comics, cartoons et al. One thing I never really liked was the "universe" aspect of crossing over multiple character stories. I liked following one hero. Watching an underdog, etc. It wasn't until the Avengers franchise took over and made much larger stakes. But considering I am more into space and sci-fi with the quick quips of clever personas, GotG is among my favorites now and this game has definitely reinforced that. A must play!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most misunderstood game premise's of all time if the reactions to the trailers of this game are anything to go by. Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a action team leadership simulator and it is surprisingly fun in how it plays. All of the Guardians have four abilities by the end with each functioning uniquely both from a member to member basis as well as for the individual members. Drax is the brute so he can bulldoze through enemies, Gamora's abilities do high damage to individual targets which can be helpful with tougher mobs and boss fights, Groot is all about Crowd Control and Support which includes the only healing ability in the game because you heal relatively quickly in battle as well as after every encounter, and Rocket is AoE damage to the nth degree which suits him and his explosives perfectly. Your gameplay as Star Lord is to mostly guide them effectively through battle while taking out any shields with elemental damage shots and making sure the situation never becomes unmanageable, which along with all of the couching gameplay actually makes this game extremely fun. The Huddle when I saw it in trailers was something I thought was just going to be a gimmick, but you have no idea how much I spammed that ability throughout this game for the pure endorphins I got from spamming everyone's abilities, shooting everything in sight and listening to a random 80s song from one of the best curated playlists that I've found in any game ever. You have no idea how much my heart jumped when Rick Astley started playing as my soundtrack to ass kicking the Dweller in Darkness.However, the one aspect of this game that I absolutely have to credit for nailing tremendously is the story, characters and lore. Each of the Characters are each a healthy mix between the original comic characters and their James Gunn movie counterparts. Peter Quill's backstory is much more in line with the comics with his father being the king of Spartox with a much more serious leadership mindset throughout the story, but they somehow adjusted the comic backstory just enough to retain the boyish charm and slight goofiness he had as a boy who was never allowed to grow up quite properly. Gamora is much more standoffish and socially awkward compared to both other iterations, but that surprisingly makes this Gamora feel much more well-rounded as a character compared to both the comics and the Gunn movies. Groot is more or less just comic book Groot, which is just a more sure and confident version of Groot from the first Gunn film. Rocket is pretty much just Rocket from the Gunn films, but that's great because the Gunn films nailed Rocket anyway. Drax is actually a massive improvement (though not to say I don't adore Bautista's Drax) due to his personality including his stoicism and brutality being much more in line with his comic book counterpart to actually justify his title. Mantis actually had her comic book backstory and powers in this game, though she still retained the bubbly and offkilter energy that made the Gunn-version so fun to follow. Cosmo is best boy. Adam Warlock is actually Adam Warlock through-and-through, literally the most faithful adaptation of that character I think anyone will ever do. This led to some of the most realised, fun and emotional dialogue I've ever heard in any comic book games before. The lore of each location is also much more fleshed out and full that it was portrayed in the Gunn films, like just comparing Knowhere in this game to Knowhere in the films and this game managed to not only provide different areas and districts of the Head, but also to nail the scale of the Celestial Head with much more accuracy than the films and this accuracy and depth can be seen from ever location that you traverse in the game which shows the tremendous amount of love and care this team had for the Cosmic Side of the Marvel Universe. Finally, the story is just as fun and just as emotionally vulnerable as the rest of the story. For a story that allows Gamora to hoard dolls from online vendors as a hobby and allows Peter Quill's inspiration speeches and 80s references to feel just as cringey and funny as they need to be, it's also a story that explores grief, a history of violence, PTSD and many other more specific linked themes with just as much depth and care as they deserve to be felt. I haven't felt nearly as heartbroken as I have while watching some of these cutscenes than I have for years since probably the end of Insomniac's first Spider-Man game, but even then I'd say that this game does miles better than even that as it's not reliant on moment-to-moment storytelling like the Insomniac Spidey games... it's just a well written ensemble character journey from start to finish. This is a game I wholeheartedly recommend if you want to not only experience the definitive versions of each of these Guardians characters, but also if you want to add another game to the list of quintessential Marvel Comic-adaption games that aren't Spider-Man like the Nolan North-Deadpool game and the X-Men Origins: Wolverine tie-in game that was way better than it had any credit being. Like those two games, there is no comparison and no need for one because there will never be a better game that could encapsulate the energy, characters and dynamics of the Guardians of the Galaxy quite like this game that everyone believed was gonna be bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this if you buy it on a sale. It can be buggy in parts and a lot of the game feels like a grind. I thought there would be a big more exploration, but it's very much a Square Enix game -- all hallways and enemies. I put in about 18 hours of the game. The parts that I absolutely did not enjoy were the flight sims for the Milano. I quit at the start of Chapter 13 with that whole flight sim as the guardians are crashing onto a planet. I have no idea what is the expectation with those controls for landing that crashing ship. I died about three times and decided that I was done with the game. I really want to play other games. GoTG takes up a lot of time because it's very story heavy (which is a definitely plus!) and it's a LOT of grinding. Some of the QTE's don't make sense, either. And if you fail them, much like any typical Square Enix game, they make you sit through a big unskippable cut scene over and over and over. As much as I am criticizing the game, it is definitely fun. It has amazing music. And if you are a GoTG fan, then this game is definitely for you. It felt more like I was playing through an interactive GoTG film than anything else. It takes away some of the magic when your dramatic scene turns into a slideshow.This game is focused on team work and banter between the guardians. _childDocuments_.review: I imagine most people reading this review will have some idea of what Guardians of The Galaxy is, and likely have a positive view of the film(s).  If you aren’t aware of the film, in brief it’s a team of very whacky misfits including a sentient tree and a rocket loving racoon set in a Marvel Universe. They’re not typical good guys, having a lot of hang up’s and occasionally committing crime, though it’s more bank robber/smuggler type level. The other characters are even more whacky if possible.The game is pretty faithful to the film in tone and style albeit with some different actors (I’m guessing Hollywood star actors don’t give away image rights for free) and a universe that isn’t quite the MCU. It’s hard to explain more spoiler-free but the universe has deviated with where the MCU went. The music is very 80’s with a ship based stereo available with 80’s hits and in moments of high drama when you execute a team huddle a random 80’s track blasts out. This isn’t always a great thing as there are a lot of different types of 80’s music and I got Rick rolled more than once.But what of the game itself. Well, it just does enough for me to recommend it. You play Peter Quill, the Star Lord and are assisted by 4 of the team. It reminds me a bit of Mass Effect in that you control a main character and have companions which can use a special ability occasionally. However lacking a weapon choice and no skill tree/class for your main character it’s slow at the start. Combat is at its weakest in the beginning when you and your team only have 1 normal ability, and no special ability. Eventually you will get all 4 special abilities and ultimate for each character, your character will get different elemental ammo types and it becomes much more fun. There’s still no skill tree and you can’t choose your companions but honestly, they’ve nailed the guardians dialogue and comic book type OTT special attacks well. The adaption of all the characters is well done, though they are different looking in the case of the humanoid ones, likely because of before mentioned imaging rights, they act and sound like I imagine the team to be.The plot does get better and Peter Quill becomes less of the goofy verbal punching bag, and more of a realised character with a fairly moving story arc. And the team as might be expected go through the break up/get back together, but its done well and by the end I was cheering for them.The best bits of the game are for me when you are just hanging out with the crew and listening to them interact,There are decisions and dialogue options which normally don’t have much of an effect though there are ones which will affect the story/ what help you might get from the games other characters. It’s not quite Mass Effect with hugely important decisions and a reputation system. The game its closest to me is Mass Effect. Guardians is beautiful and the locations if pretty linear are great to explore. By the end of the game I was invested in the plot and team and looked forward to ‘beating’ the enemy. I’d started not liking the combat and feeling a bit sorry for Peter Quill who just seemed to be there in uniting the team in their disdain for him. But I ended thinking the combat was okay, after enjoying it more in the middle of the game when I didn’t quite have access to everything and wasn’t dreading Never gonna give you up blaring out again in the middle of a tense combat.  It may not be quite Mass Effect in its depth and scope. But you know what that’s okay. It’s a decent Marvel adaption, and there aren’t micro-transactions. This is a decent single player game and it’s very Guardians of the Galaxy and that’s good enough for me. Guardians Guardians of the galaxyMCU Marvel cinematic universeRick rolled – the art of minding your own business then suddenly being hit by a bit of Rick Astley’s never gonna give you up

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I had no idea about this game till a month or two after it's release, I remember watching a launch trailer by accident and thought "that doesn't look that great" so the marketing was well... bad.But my god have I enjoyed and loved this game, the effort and care is always in your face.I may have not played avengers but if they do this with other superheroes games, I honestly can't see anything going wrong (just learn from the avengers failure).Pros:-The sound and audio in this game is fantastic, from the awesome 80's songs to the 'Star Lord' band (which honestly have no bad songs at all, they did not need to go that hard for a completely fictional band) every piece of audio I see no faults anywhere.-Voice acting is great, when it comes to the emotional sections the actors hit it on point and never makes it feel off.-The combat I did enjoy, while it can be kinda basic and not have a lot of depth, I liked the whole manage the team while looking after yourself quite fun, I didn't find one character weaker than the rest they all have a purpose and I love it.-The dialogue and writing is very, very good i'm so glad this wasn't a copy paste of the films or comics (tho it does heavily take character stories from the comics but with a few twists so it's still fresh) my biggest gripes with the films is that it really was just star lord, gamora and rocket doing the heavy lifting while drax is just comic relief and groot was just "look cute big tree look at him!!!!!!"Star Lord clearly has a power struggle, Gamora is just full of regret and embarrassment, Rocket is like a child who always wants his way, Groot is the bigger brother to rocket but is prone to being silly with him and Drax is still having personal issues causing difficulties when he is supposed to work with the team.So there are a lot of arcs in the story and they are satisfyingly done really well by the end of the game and the team dynamic works really well, at the start of the game when you walk around and you hear drax, rocket, groot and gamora talking about their adventures and stories it makes you feel like they've done this for a while but still ain't quite comfortable with each other to work as a team 100% of the time.Cons:Some face models are off, when you see a very famous marvel character near the mid part of the game and he starts laughing like a cliche villain, I had mass effect andromeda flashbacks or the final boss starts laughing and it's just a open mouth it really just doesn't look right when you have the guardians with their spot on expressions and body language.The combat can be quite boring at times and you kinda just wanna rush into the huddle mechanic to listen to some music to get really going.Peter's father is kinda just mentioned a few times and that's it but answers no important questions like is his father still alive? Did he know of Peter's capture/mother's fate? Later on they do mention why they can't go to his father's homeworld but it would be nice to know what happened to him.The dialogue is great, the atmosphere is amazing but the dialogue gets cut off so much because there is either:A- too much of it and you skip a whole 10 minute conversationB- you tell a character to do something so it stops the talk just to go "hey can you do this" So you either have to wait every 5-10 minutes or just risk losing important dialogue and then go "wait I don't understand what is going on" So overall it's a fantastic game and I hope it gets a sequel because this was so much better than the movies (I am biased since i'm not a huge fan of the mcu) and i'm glad they learned from their mistakes, money well spent.(Took about 19 hours to complete)

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Pros:+ Great story+ Very funny (the banter is top-notch)+ Good character development+ Wacky and faithful to the comics+ Tons of easter eggs+ Fun combat+ Amazing soundtrack+ Terrific voice actingCons:- Buggy- A few blurry textures"Long" version:After the debacle that was , I, like many others, was apprehensive about a game featuring the Guardians of the Galaxy. The gameplay looked a bit chaotic in the trailers and a game revolving around a team screamed online features and maybe even microtransactions. Thankfully,  is a single-player, third-person, action-adventure experience that feels like everything I wanted  to be.It takes some inspiration from the MCU, mainly the team’s line-up, but everything else relies heavily on the comics – which is much appreciated! I am a big silver-age comic-book nerd!You play as Peter Quill, AKA Star-Lord, as he tries to make a name for himself and his team and also getting out of debt after some shenanigans happen (no spoilers).The story is really good – even if you are not into some of the crazier aspects from the comics, I believe you will still find it enjoyable. If you are in any way, shape or form familiar with the source material, I feel like this is an easy recommendation and a must-play for Marvel fans.While some might be worried you should be able to control the whole team, focusing on Star-Lord was the correct choice in my book. He is flawed but very likeable and he slowly learns what it takes to be a leader. You will be able to make choices that change the experience you get quite significantly. The other members are not as fleshed out, in comparison, but they certainly get a lot of screentime and character development.The game also features countless easter eggs that were just a treat to experience. From obvious references to other Marvel characters from Earth to mind-blowing cameos from lesser known… individuals.It is also quite hilarious. While a few jokes did not land for me, those were few and far between; the game is so light-hearted that you cannot help but chuckle at most of the dialogue. When things get emotional, it also works, for the most part. Characters are not one dimensional. They interact and have clear goals, relationships and interactions. Really great stuff.When it comes to gameplay, I also enjoyed it.The platforming is very forgiving but you get to experience one of the best aspects of the game while you are at it – the banter – which I will talk about later down in the review. If you fall off of maps you will lose a bit of your HP and get teleported back. Even on the hardest difficulty, the amount of HP you lose is inconsequential. You can also command your team members to interact with objects and solve a few puzzles which are very easy but are, nonetheless, a nice change of pace.Combat is simple, yet strangely satisfying.When you first start out, Peter can do nothing but shoot his elemental guns which overheat rather quickly but you soon unlock more abilities that allow you to strategize and use different tactics. It took me about 3 or 4 hours to really get the hang of it, but once you do, it is very satisfying. You dodge, you complete a “QTE” to perform a quick reload, you keep shooting, your teammates have abilities to help you out and everything keeps getting more complex but still very approachable.As stated, your teammates can be commanded to use certain abilities to help you in battle. I loved this. There is strategy behind every ability and you can clean a room full of bad guys if you combo them smartly. From stuns to AoE damage, there is a little bit of everything and all characters have 4 distinct abilities that serve different purposes.There is more to the combat than I mentioned but I feel like explaining other mechanics is not useful, as the game slowly introduces them and does a good job.Moving onto the visuals. I feel like the game is gorgeous. It is colorful, the character models have a distinct look to them and the environments are outstandingly detailed.There is an aspect regarding character’s hair that I ought to mention – while not game-breaking, characters like Rocket and Gamora have weird hair textures sometimes. I was not sure at first, so I just got used to it, but after uploading my screenshots a lot of things looked blurry and pixelated. I ran this on max setting but tried changing a lot of things in the options but nothing seemed to work. A friend of mine had other glitches like textures stretching that required him to reload checkpoint somewhat regularly. As for the hair thing, it was distracting at first but I started ignoring it and enjoyed the ride.Voice acting is great.While all the Guardians deserve praise for their performances, Jon McLaren is clearly the standout. I loved him as Star-Lord. I think this was his first video-game gig ever but I sure hope they make a sequel and he comes back. What a likeable voice!Everyone else is very talented too, they hit the right notes and nail the drama and the comedy perfectly.The quality of the sound effects is good but I would like to point out how great the soundtrack is. While this was not a character trait in the comics before the movies came out, Peter Quill is a music fan in this game, just like in the movies. We get to listen to a wide array of songs and there are several which will please everyone for sure. They even went out of their way to create a brand-new band with a full album of awesome songs! Peter’s Walkman also play a part in the story and in combat but I will not spoil it!You can finish  in about 18-24 hours if you stop to smell the roses. I think it is worth it. I loved every single moment with this game, even when I had to restart because I got stuck in the geometry (around 5 times during a playthrough).The game has been patched to fix some of the issues and I feel like restarting once or twice will not be that annoying as the game is not particularly hard, but I cannot just stand here and ignore the issues, no matter how much I liked it.I am certainly biased - as I said before I am a big Marvel fan - but wholeheartedly feel like this game is enjoyable and most people will like it. It is entertaining to play, hilarious and, most importantly, it is not soulless, like many, many AAA games coming out nowadays (*cough*  *cough*).Easily the best game I played in a while. Got it for 40€ and I do not regret it!Now, where is my sequel? Where is my Fantastic Four game? 😉Final score: 9 out of 10.If you enjoyed this review, please consider joining my  and following my  on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I am Groot! I am Groot. I...am Groot. I am Groot? I....am....Groot! I AM GROOT!Edit: I just recently finished the game and it was a fantastic experience the whole way through! This game was not on my radar whatsoever after the result of the Avengers game and I don't believe that much marketing for the game was done due to the lack of advertisements I saw or discussion of the game in general. This is a fantastic narrative driven single-player experience! The combat can get repetitive towards the end of the game but the story holds up through its entirety. The game separates itself from the MCU and does its own thing and is apparent pretty early on. It does use the same characters we are familiar with, but that is about where the similarities end. Character designs are fantastic! I will definitely be going back through to find the collectibles I missed and 100% the title as the game does feature a New Game+ mode and collectibles unlock additional dialogue options with   that really help flesh out the characters and add depth to the universe they are set in. For me, finding a game I can thoroughly enjoy all the way through for 20 hours is rare and well worth the full price tag, versus a game I will shut my brain off for half the time to grind through. I would highly suggest and recommend this game to any Marvel fan or anyone that enjoys well crafted single-player driven experiences!

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for the journey among the stars. It will be adventures, fights, plots and a lot of fun.By the gameplay this is an action game. We play as Starlord, using a pair of guns to shoot the enemies, avoiding their attacks using dodge. There is no cover system - we always fight in the open. The entire team participates in combat, however we do not have direct control over the other characters. Instead we can order the particular squad member to perform a special ability against the selected enemy. Some of these abilities affect a group of enemies, others deal a heavy damage to the single target and so on. Issuing the correct orders depending on the current combat situation is a key to the victory.Starlord also has his own set of abilities and special elemental ammo, which adds different effects during the shooting.Unfortunately, the controls are unhandy. Picking the exact ability of the particular team member is tricky. Too often it ends up in selecting the wrong character or wrong ability or gun mode instead.Jumping also behaves weird.There is a decent variety of enemies. They use different tactics and have different resistance and vulnerabilities. We have to utilize the team's special abilities during the exploration too. For example: Rocket can crawl into the small hatches and hack the consoles, Drax can move heavy objects and so on. We need to use teamwork in order to traverse the terrain.The party gains an experience, which allows them to unlock the new abilities. There are also gear upgrades, but for Starlord only.The story is very interesting and worthy of Hollywood. It has twists and unexpected turns. We visit the different worlds, meet the charismatic characters and, of course, save the galaxy.You’ll have to be familiar with the original franchise (at least see a movie) before playing. Otherwise too many things will be unintelligible for you. The game does provide some lore, but not enough to create a whole picture from the scratch.The game is very lively. There are constant conversations between characters in our team. They have different opinions on current events, arguing and joking with each other. Complemented by the proper cinematics, it creates a feeling of reality, like all these characters are alive. Unfortunately the backside of this are numerous glitches in the cutscenes, when the game does not progress to the next stage because some dialogue has not happened or the character is stuck at the door. I have to reload the checkpoint and even fight some bosses twice due to these problems.The game is linear. One chapter comes strictly after another. There are no side quests or any other activity. However during the events we will have to make several choices, which will affect the story later. These are not very significant, but satisfying. It is quite interesting to replay the game and see how it may change due to a particular choice.During the missions we can find certain items, which may be interesting to the particular crew member. It unlocks additional conversations on the ship. But there is no actual relationship building: no affection, extra perks or anything. Graphics is quite impressive. It is vivid and colorful, picturing the bright galaxy and crowded space stations. Some landscapes and views are really stunning. The characters have also been designed with care. In particular, there is a nice job of rendering fur for Rocket.The optimization is good. The game maintains high quality graphics over the high speed gameplay without any lags or glitches.As expected, much effort was spent on music. The game utilizes various famous songs from the 80's and 90's as background music. I wonder: how did all this get licensed? Anyway the matching between a particular game event and music creates an astonishing atmosphere. Well done.Total Rating 8/10.The game is almost perfect. But the problems with the controls and cutscenes do not allow it to score the max points.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, where to begin. The story is fine--typical comic book "end is nigh and you have to stop it" story. It was good enough for me. The voice acting was my favorite part. I thought it was very well done and really enjoyed the banter during battle or walking to the next section of the game. It made me want to hear more of busting each other's cajones. Gameplay is average beat 'em up with shooting involved. Some puzzles are needed to be solved, but nothing too difficult. There are choices to be made during the game that may or may not affect parts later on in the game. This gives it a little bit of replayability to see how it plays out differently. It has a "new game plus" mode that allows you to replay it with all the hidden outfits and perks that were purchased, in case you want to find outfits or secrets that were missed. The music is a collection of 80s music that most will know and love (or hate to love). If you don't want that nostalgia hit, there's a completely brand new 80s hair metal band soundtrack that plays instead, which is also well done.I would recommend this game. Maybe not at the 60 dollar price tag, but if you snag it on sale, it'll be worth it. At least 16 hours worth for your first playthrough, with more if you search for all the secrets or different choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks and plays great on the Steam Deck OLED. As I understand, this title used to be "playable" and is now "verified" for the Deck. Settings-wise, the game runs smooth capped at 45 FPS with no TDP limit (although I suppose capping the TDP to 10w will work) with in game graphics set to defaults (a mix of low, medium and high settings for details, shadow and textures with blooms, reflections etc. toggled on). The game performs very well on these medium-high settings on the latest Proton (v8) and Proton Experimental, but switching to an older v7 forces the in-game settings to be "low" throughout for some reason. Surprisingly, although I am on the OLED Deck, the in-game HDR setting under the Display option does not seem to work -- colors look washed out when I toggle it on. Another oddity is regardless of the settings (even setting everything to "low") there is mild stutter in the first half of the very first chapter of the game where the Guardians are exploring the exterior of a space ship / station / robot thingy and installing "thumpers" to bait out some kind of monster. This goes away soon after this initial external section is completed, and the game starts running at smooth 45 FPS without any issues. This game could be more optimized to run even better on the Deck, but I don't suppose Eidos Montreal has the incentive to do so. Overall, a solid action adventure title.

The production values are quite high. Superb Voice acting and script writing are on par with the movies. Awesome Graphics and art direction. A little downside is the lack of replay value since the levels are all linear. Even with that said the levels are for the most part very beautiful and are a joy to traverse. You will be shooting with your pistols a lot. To break a bit of monotony there are elemental attacks and summoning powerful allies abilities. The action loop is fun, but it will not take precedence over the story. Come for the action and stay for the story as I say. The enemy variety is decent, but gets old near the end of the game. The playtime is about 20 hours which is quite long for an action game. Think of it as Mass Effect without the slow parts. What a fun experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my goodness.  I bought this on a deep sale discount and finally decided to sit down for a little bit and try it out, because I had a half hour free or so before I wanted to take care of some errands.Over four hours later, I had to painfully tear myself away from the computer.This game is glorious!  I can't believe I hadn't seen it or played it before.The primary source of enjoyment is the characters and the story.  The banter between the guardians is absolutely phenomenal, and kudos to whomever the writers are because this is truly a love letter to Guardians of the Galaxy.  It's kind of a hybrid between what you see in the films and the 2013 GOTG comic series.  Honestly, this is my favorite "feeling" for Guardians for sure, especially this take on Gamora.Do note, there is a lot of dialogue here, and much of it is banter that occurs while you are moving through the mission levels.  The combat is decent, but it's not earth shattering.  I find it fun, but honestly it's a side note to the main story and simply playing through and seeing what happens to the crew.  Not that it's bad, it really does flow quite well and has a whole momentum mechanic that encourages you to use different moves and establish a kind of "combat flow."  But again, the true enjoyment here is the story and the dialogue.I am enjoying the hell out of this story and after dinner here, I'm diving right back in.Ok AND I'm back... after almost 23 hours I finished the game.So first... I very rarely ever finish games.  The fact that I finished this one says more than my words ever really can.I have not had this much fun playing a game in a long time.  A very long time.  This is really the first time I'm actually considering New Game+.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game was first announced, I was hesitant about how good it could possibly be. Especially after Avengers from Square recently. But then a few days before release, I saw all the glowing reviews not only from a bunch of review sites but also YouTubers I trust like SkillUp and ACG. So I bought it at launch.I do think most of the comments SkillUp made in his video are pretty accurate. I just didn't realize how much some of the negatives would bother me. First off, there are a few bugs I've encounters that, if fixed, could drastically improve my feelings about this game. The two big ones are a lot of texture pop in and input issues. The input issues are what I want to focus on here. I play all my PC games besides FPS games and anything better with a mouse (e.g. strategy games) with an Xbox Elite Controller V2. It works flawlessly on every other game I've used it with that has controller support (both on Steam and other platforms). But here, the controller *works* fine but the game randomly decides it's a different controller constantly. Sometimes it will correctly be an Xbox controller. Other times it will be a DualShock/DualSense. And other times still, it will be recognized as a Switch Pro controller. This changes the in-game button glyphs which makes things like QTEs and other combo button prompts difficult to accomplish since all three of those controllers have the X button in different places, for example. Beyond those bugs (which I hope get patched soon), the game isn't awful. The story, writing, voice acting, facial animations, and detail in every environment you visit are incredible. The reflections are great - especially with ray tracing on. And the game isn't super demanding. I was able to run it at 1440p on my 2080 (latest Nvidia drivers) on nearly all High settings with ray tracing on High and DLSS on Quality getting 70-80 fps on average.That said, the combat kind of sucks. You can't control any of the Guardians besides Starlord - which would be fine except Star Lord's guns do almost no damage. They feel like pea shooters. You can issue commands to do special attacks by your teammates but those are on cool downs after you use them once. The combat is serviceable but it's pretty boring. I was always looking forward to the next story bit or even just exploring the map of each mission looking for hidden chests and resources more than I was looking forward to combat. And the set pieces (usually accompanied by QTEs) are awful. Get the QTEs right or die and start at a checkpoint right before that QTE. Sometimes the areas you have to jump off or to before the QTE kicks in aren't clearly defined and if you get it off by enough you just die.Ultimately, if this game's story, acting, and writing weren't so good, I'd have quit playing hours ago. And for now, I might shelve it until there's a patch addressing the input issue and pop in I've seen. The game is not a disaster, but I'd recommend waiting for a patch or two and/or a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this; Guardians of The Galaxy is a wonderful experience and is personally my Game of The Year thus far.I finished this title a couple of days ago and honestly was impressed and immersed in the experience from beginning to end. GoTG does a fantastic job of telling an engaging story and populating it with well written characters and scenarios throughout it's lengthy run time.How lengthy you ask? Well speaking anecdotally of my own playthru it took me 21 hours until I rolled credits. This was a thorough playthru, I unlocked 48 of the 59 achievements, and unlocked 35 of the 40 alternate outfits. Meaning I did explore environments quite thoroughly and enjoyed just listening to the banter of the Guardians. The game is also absolutely STUNNING graphically and I quite often would stop to just look at the incredible visuals on display.The game is an almost entirely linear story affair that sees you jumping all over the galaxy to various exotic locales on your adventure. The linearity is a positive here, as it means the talented folks at Eidos Montreal have been able to craft a well paced and emotionally resonate story without having player agency affect the pacing. The title is also not devoid of exploration, or player choice with the regards to certain dialogue options (of which there are many throughout the story) which can have some quite impactful changes to how further scenarios will play out.Combat in the game is actually a very fun affair, but does take awhile to hit it's stride. I personally didn't mind this as it made the progression of skills acquired thru playing feel rewarding. However, I can see why others may have wanted these abilities earlier to spice up earlier combat encounters. This was a bit of a double edged sword for Eidos Montreal and I think they chose the right path. I also feel like they chose wisely in limiting the player to playing only as Peter (Star Lord) as this makes you feel more like it is YOU developing these relationships further with the other members of the team. That is what everything is ultimately in service to here; the story. Combat (though quite good) is not the star, the story and characters are. It says something that at the end of the title, despite feeling like it was a really lengthy and satisfying adventure, I was sad to be parting ways with this rendition of the Guardians. I'd really got to like hanging out with them, and as someone that was not a die-hard fan of the movies (not that I disliked them either) that's a huge accomplishment. I hands-down can say this was my favourite and now benchmark rendition of these characters.Graphically speaking, this is currently one of the best looking games out there. No question. I am lucky enough to have played the title on a powerful PC, where I was able to set all settings to 1440p/Ultra and enable Ray Tracing with DLSS at Quality and I averaged 100fps according to the in-built benchmark. The game just routinely had my jaw dropping to the floor. The implementation of ray tracing is one of the best I've seen yet, the colour palette of the game really pops, the character models are excellent and the environments are gorgeous. The fact the game jumps all over the galaxy to different locations made me always excited to see what I'd be experiencing next. Musically, the game has an outstanding collection of (doubtless) expensive to licence 80's classic tracks that can play during combat and also be selected in the ship when in between missions.A special mention must also go to the Milano, the Guardians spaceship. It is a beautifully realised hub space in the game which has been lovingly crafted, with a tonne of little touches that happen between missions etc for those paying attention.I could go on for ages about why this game so thoroughly impressed me, but the bottom line is this; If you like narrative focused titles that tell a compelling story with engaging characters, this is a must buy. Also, if the idea of hanging out with a space-faring crew like the Guardians (or maybe Han Solo and Chewie if Star Wars is more your jam) is appealing, then this definitely can scratch that itch.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand how a game this great exists in current year.A 15-20 hour linear story, without an over-bloated open world, instead featuring tight action, great pacing, amazing banter, and unlockable cosmetics in lieu of DLC? What year is it?!I loved every minute of this game, which is largely carried by the banter and dialogue between the main cast and a few interesting side characters. I know that the witty dialogue that is all too common in comic book movies today can get a bit grating, but I feel that it is written and preformed with enough restraint here that it comes off as earnest and real. Our heroes laugh in the face of danger, but never diminish it to the point of a farce. Even if you tire of (or even hate) modern comic book movies, I'd still recommend you give this story a chance. It's honestly more Star Wars (the original one) than superhero flick.As for the gameplay, this is definitely the game's weakest link, although it really only suffers at the beginning when you don't have any abilities unlocked. Star Lord's blasters feel a bit like nerf guns and the enemies are a bit too bullet-spongey. Once you unlock most of the abilities and alternate fire modes for the blasters, the combat gets more interesting and a lot faster, although it still could be better.Fortunately, the game offers custom difficulty settings. I haven't tried messing with them yet, but just looking at them I'd recommend setting the damage you deal and receive to maximum. That might speed things up a bit while still keeping the danger.Still, I don't need every game to be Dark Souls, sometimes I just want a fun and engaging story that entertains me and even pulls out a few emotions from my cold, dead heart. I whole heartedly recommend Guardians of the Galaxy, unless you hate fun.A note: I'd recommend getting this game soon (as in, within a year or two), as it is chock-full of (great) licensed music and those tend to expire, putting these games in legal limbo. Remember the Deadpool game?
