_childDocuments_.review: This game really could have been something great if it weren't infected with Denuvo DRM which ruins performance on even the best hardware and sometimes makes the game completely unplayable for the naive people who actually trusted SQUARE ENIX with their money. Even when running "properly" this insidious DRM reduces performance by a huge amount while increasing the workload on your computer.Because of how Denuvo puts strain on your computer, there is is also a real chance that just running it will reduce the lifespan of your hardware since as anyone familiar with computers knows, working them harder reduces their lifespan. This game is already protected by Steam DRM so adding Denuvo to the version that that people already paid for on Steam is both unnecessary and evil. Punishing people who trust you by STEALING the game from them after they paid you for it is just as vile as Pay-to-Win, lootboxes, or any other sleazy scheme. What's worse, the strain Denuvo puts on your hardware puts this product in the same category as a bitcoin miner IMHO. Do NOT buy this game until such time as Square Enix removes Denuvo (Namco-Bandai already did that with Ace Combat 7 so it is definitely possible.) In its present state, the game shouldn't even be available for sale.No microtransactions... single-player... this game could have been a contender for game of the year. Unfortunately it's now just another stuttering mess containing an insidious piece of bloatware.Below are items which wouldn't have prevented me from recommending the game but are still annoying.I've played through and even recommended games like Resident Evil 5 so I am no stranger to Quick Time Events.HOWEVER, this game has the worst quick-time-events of any game I can remember. This is the first game where I can fail the QTEs over and over again simply because I am not sure what I am supposed to do and when I am supposed to do it even after seeing a fail state.I'm used to missing a QTE the first time and getting it on the second or third. I am NOT used to watching the same thing over and over again trying to figure out what it is that the devs want me to do. What makes matters worse is that you have to sit through a long loading screen each time you want to retry... even with the game installed on an internal SSD.I'm not the only one who finds that the badly implemented QTEs ruin this game as you can see below.Go to the Main Menu or the Pause Menu and select Settings. Press the Accessibility option in Settings. There is an option to turn on "Auto-Win Quick Time Events" in accessibility.(From the article below)The soundtrack for the actual game contains some licensed music... but you still have to listen to the terrible, made-up "Starlord" band because the studio decided they needed something to put in the "Digital Deluxe Edition" and if they didn't use their terrible studio musicians in the game, they couldn't sell their sub-par work as a "soundtrack".I am glad that the devs didn't put weapons and abilities that would ruin the base game in the "Deluxe Edition" but this game would have been better if it didn't have a deluxe edition at all. This is just disgusting. There is apparently some rule at Square Enix that while they WILL pay EXTREMELY expensive incensing fees for franchises, music etc., they hate actors and will never pay even the tiniest fees to use their likenesses. I very much doubt that Chris Pratt would have demanded much money for use of his likeness considering that he is literally starring in Amazon b-movies now but rather than pay a pittance to use his charismatic likeness, we get stuck with a gormless doofus who seems to have been created NOT to look good but rather, to look legally distinct from Chris Pratt. Considering that this is literally the ONLY playable character, this is a problem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. It's exactly what I wanted to play this period. The gameplay is fantastic. While exploring you can interact with the other characters as if you were Peter Quill. You can remain silent or choose what to say, and depending on what you choose it may affect what they think of you. It's like "Life is Strange" but in a more interactive way.Haven't finished it yet, but the story so far is great. It's exactly what a fan should expect of the Guardians. Crazy stuff that somehow connect perfectly with each other. As for the characters' arc, there are some same with the movies and some not. It's a different version of Guardians with similar backstory. If you have seen the movies you'll definitely understand the details of the characters' backstory. Now if you haven't seen the movies, you'll still understand the main story, but not some details for the characters. Also you'll see some easter eggs or refrences for other disney movies (Mostly Marvel movies).The soundtrack is great, especially if you love old school rock as I do. It has many licensed songs that everyone loves. If you want to stream you have an option to replace the licensed songs with alternative ones. Although, I don't think the deluxe edition is worth the extra money cause the soundtrack included are just 10 songs, and only 3 of them from the band "Star Lord", while in-game there are at least 10 songs from this band which you can choose to hear when you're in the ship.And last but definitely not least, the combat is much better than I expected. We all have heard how great the combat is, but once you play the game you have a different feeling. Once the combat starts, you don't want it to stop. And I love how many things you can do at once. And when you gather your team to get the boost, is just great.To conclude, we finally have a great Marvel game on PC. I know there are the PS exclusive Spider-Man games which are great, but I'm talking about non-exclusive games. It's difficult to find a great super-heroes game these days, and thankfully Guardians are better than what anyone expected. And thankfully it kept Guardians as we've always knew them, but a lot more improved.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't sure about this MULTIVERSE version of the Guardians of the Galaxy. It's a bit of a slow burn from the start, and for fans of the OG team it feels a little unfamiliar. In fact, both the Guardians and the majority of characters we meet throughout the game have not only had their models AND voices changed, but their backstories too. It's not the Guardians of the Galaxy fans are used to and as that's not explicitly stated anywhere, so we're left a little confused from the start, having to guess as we go. The opening gameplay largely consists of long platforming sections between combat arenas. In fact, that's mainly the case for the whole game, with some flashbacks and scenarios to explore along the way. (Oh, and some short, tanky flying sections that require some patience.) The platforming sections DO contain a lot of banter between the characters however, fleshing out their backstories and personalities, and filling the player in along the way. Which IS a nice way to do things, albeit a little slow, and too frequently presents the opportunity to miss dialogue if one isn't paying attention or progresses too quickly. "Put your game face on Drax" - "I only possess one face, Peter Quill"In fact the game is MOSTLY platforming around the - somehow - progressively more gorgeous environments. The graphics really shine in this title and the environments truly come to life, and despite the odd texture flicker or stutter during a transition or screenshot are extremely immersive. That is of course when you're not using Peter's visor to scan for the collectables, or the upgrade materials necessary for the player weapons...In fact Quill's main two handhelds start as powerful pea-shooters, and the bulk of the damage throughout the game comes from his own and the squad's own special abilities which are purchased through upgrades. Actually, they mainly stay as pea-shooters outside of on-use abilities with cooldowns, which is a little frustrating.Like the visuals though, the combat improves over time. Significantly. With upgrades to the party's characters via abilities, and additionally upgrades to the player character, the fights evolve from drudgery to a genuine want to master the mechanics and bring the fight to the enemy. It's quite satisfying to perfect the use of the situational talents and environmental objects, picking up those coveted achievements along the way. In fact, at the end of the upgrade cycle the frenetic fights are so colourful, so satisfying - they pack a punch and you can really feel it. Add to that the "huddle" performance booster, which speeds up cooldowns, increases damage and adds an "Awesome Mix" track to kick ass to!(I will add that the tracks are seemingly random, though. Kicking ass to Rick Astley feels a little silly, Marvel.) Wait - are you Rick Rolling me?The story is the final thread to mention, which whilst in set in a different universe is a very "Guardians" narrative. It has all of the expected themes of a Guardians game - taking serious issues and adding a layer of candor, whilst the overarching theme being one of unity / family. I did find that repeatedly referencing backgrounds of characters made for a darker backstory though, and that I questioned some of their actions going forward, especially through the lens of those redeemed. I thought you were the good guys now, guys? I suppose it's one of those things we'll have to overlook, especially considering the galaxy saving narrative(s). You lovable rogues, you...Overall I strongly feel the game is worth hanging on for, if a little confusing and a little slow in the beginning. It offers a whopping ~20 hours on the first playthrough and with New Game + a lot of replayability at a reasonable price. Definitely worth picking up on sale if you have the time to commit to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Never seen a Guardians of the Galaxy movie, got no idea whatsoever about them and is unlikely I'll see the movies after finishing the game.However, this game is seriously a gem. The dialogues between the characters are hilarious and their chemistry become stronger as you progress. Everything is focused on delivering a fun game experience and even tho the game can be unforgiving at certain points, I won't call it difficult. After playing this game I was surprised how It wasn't nominated for GOTY 2021, this one seriously deserved to be there.If you are in search of an old school action packed game, you need to give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommend this game to whoever got tired of mindless MCU titles. While this game does have certain similarities with MCU's Guardians of the Galaxy, it can proudly stand on its own, characters backstories are deep and engaging, and by the end of the game you become deeply immersed with the whole aestethics of the game and your teammates. Man, Drax's personal story is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing and MCU's movie does not make any justice in this regard.Gameplay wise the game does not offer much, it's a shame you cannot directly control your teammates as you play Starlord, but the way it is handles here is alright, giving commands to your teammates becomes natural and each encounter serves as a waymark to highlight your teamwork. All in all, great game, had my share of fun with it, hope there will be a sequel with more great stories to tell and more refined gameplay, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely stellar ride from start to finish. Just a seriously fun video game! Graphics are lush and colourful, fight mechanics are fun, narrative is super solid, as are the voice performances.There were a couple of graphical glitches early on, and at times the traversal - particularly jumping from platform to platform - felt a little clumsy. Once I lost the entire crew during an elevator ride, and they weren't available for the next fight (could have reloaded the checkpoint but wanted to see what would happen if I didn't). But these are nitpicks at best, and glitches were so sporadic that the ones that did happen stood out - most of the time it was a flawless experience.On the flipside I really like how they handled ultrawide monitor support (cutscenes smoothly transition to a pillarbox before expanding back to fill the screen when they're done) and the graphics really pop with all the settings dialled up to ultra. And the narrative is an award-winner for a reason. Not gonna lie, got a little misty-eyed at times.The crew banter is one of the best features, but to get the most out of it you need to modify the way you play. There's scripted lines that happen at checkpoints or when you perform actions, then there's random banter as you're moving through a level or your ship. If you hit a checkpoint in the middle of random banter, it'll get cut off to play the scripted lines. This'll happen frequently unless you slow down or just stop moving and listen. I'd recommend the stop-and-listen approach. The banter is good enough that it's worth the extra time it takes to hear as much of it as possible. You'll still accidentally cut off some lines, though, so I'd recommend turning the subtitles on. Sometimes you'll still get to read a line before it gets cut off.Overall this was just a super fun experience with a great story. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the absolute best story driven action adventure games I have plaid in my entire life! 10 x 10 rating from me for this masterpiece! One of a kind, & should become the standard for story telling, & character building! In this game Universe you have the ability really cause eventful changes from the choices you make, or chose not to make. Cause to effect really comes into play here big time. The music is superb 80's classic rock themed which I love so much! The ability to control your team easily, & extremely fun in battles, missions, & exploring the different worlds, and environments is amazing too! I've not had this much fun playing a game in ages. I enjoy many games, but nothing will come close to this beauty of a game for a long time I feel. It will take a lot to top this epic saga tale! Hats off to every single person that made this game possible, you did a masterful job of story telling, & made every character in the game universe matter, and feel real.. Even the side aliens on the streets of "NO WHERE" seemed alive with their own stories unfolding too. I felt seriously immersed in this game universe, something not just any game can accomplish. This was a true joy to experience, & I hope there is some D.L.C. content to come, & or a sequel as well. Here's to hoping for both! I highly recommend this game anyone! No matter if a Marvel fan, superhero fan in general, fan of science fiction space battles, and exploration, drama, action, suspense, the works! This has it all, so get your copy today! Normally I would say buy a game always on discount if able, but this amazing gem is well worth the full price of admission so buy it even not on sale to show the makers of this game some love to support more content like this in the future! _childDocuments_.review: its pretty good. especially if youre into story driven action games. the voice acting , story, graphics are really good so far. the gameplay has a surprising amount of depth to it . its fun. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, So I grabbed this game *mostly* because some reviewers claimed it to be the greatest game of it's kind since Red Dead 2, Arkham or Spiderman. Well... Let me tell you.It's not.It's nothing like those games at all. This is a story driven platformer. Full stop. There is no exploration, there is no free roaming sandbox style gameplay. It's punch and shoot your way from start to finish.Things I disliked about this game. Combat felt very samey, I was playing on hard the whole way through, and whelp. There was no challenge until the final *cough* boss. That was when I first felt I had to use the distance mechanic to really get the most out of my guns. Speaking of guns, they are pew pew pew... That's it. Sure you have the elements in them, but, I never really had to use them, and even then a lot of the fights were over not long before they started. New game plus might give me more challenge.... but we will see!The level design was pretty basic too... run down corridor, come to big open room, fight, rinse, repeat. Not much else to see or do.Things I liked.The story was pretty cool, and the dialogue. Genuine laugh out loud moments as the Guardians banter back and forth. The aesthetic of the game was nice too, the graphics are good, and the art style was very good. There were some decisions to be made throughout the story line, but really hard to tell how they impact the overall story. The length of the game was also decent enough.All in all, this game is for fans. If you are looking for something with substance. This isn't it, though it is better than a lot of the other marvel games at the moment.Buy it on special, but only if you are looking for a pleasantly written distraction.

_childDocuments_.review: Never read a marvel comics in my life and I guess never will, nevertheless I've really enjoyed this game for its humor.- big parts of the game are movie/story driven but the humor kept me going- short, took me around 20h to finish the main storyBought it in discount for 13EUR and for sure recommend it for the price

_childDocuments_.review: Really funny, interesting characters, decent story, fun if 'safe' type gameplay. It has that same sort of Uncharted, God of War cinematic thing going on. I'd say it's about on par with God of War for how fun and enjoyable the gameplay itself is, rather than Uncharted which is just... bog standard 3rd person. Amazing visuals, in all regards. Looks fantastic maxed out with ray tracing, and even without ray tracing it's still stunning. Enjoyable exploration in the missions too, some clever stuff. Fun puzzles throughout the entire game that don't overstay their welcome. Overall, if you enjoy story rich cinematic adventure games, and want to experience that with a hilarious and charming humour element injected in, with GOTG no less? Then buy this. 8/10 -- Brilliant, well worth buying at full price or on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly fun  space romp with great characters, fun banter and detailed environments. _childDocuments_.review: First few hours are a bit slow, and combat is rare, but in the second third of the game, boy there are a lot of fights, just warm up for them. After a few fights, some challenging enemies will appear. Frustrating at first, but this is actually because the game is teaching the player. Teaches teamwork above all, and also how to counter enemy weaknesses, rely on team instead of Star-Lord gun going pew-pew.There is a consistently good (but not great imho) story, there are good characters, the environments are great. Wroth going off the path, to find components for upgrades, or outfits.Individual elements of the difficulty settings can be changed, 'Normal' with a little bit of extra mmph (auto-huddle, bit stronger guns for Quill) provides a fun, but still challenging experience for me. Probably most players should start at 'Normal' and see if it is too easy, too difficult or just about right.There are _some_ bugs here and there, but the game is mostly alright. There was serious work put in the story, the visuals, dialogues, etc. I definitely recommend this game, even at full price.Playtime: 16 hours in, I am at about 66%, so the final playtime should be at about ~25 hrs.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when quick time events were all the rage in the early 2000's, but then games got rid of them because everybody hated them. Well, "Guardians of the Galaxy" thinks it's the early 2000's again and throws so many boring and pointless quick time events in your face and if you manage to fail them you get to enjoy the same unskippable animation time and time again. The game itself is simplistic and buggy crap. Just to name a few you can get stuck on objects and glitch through floors and sometimes you can't even progress unless you load the last checkpoint because your team mate doesn't want to break to wall only he can break. The combat is boring and lackluster and mostly you just spam your team mate's abilities or shoot your extremely weak water guns that barely do any damage and you have to keep reloading them all the time. Most of the time you are just walking forward listening to boring and unfunny banter until you reach the next arena where you get to enjoy the poor combat and then you repeat the same thing time and time again.

_childDocuments_.review: After finaly finishing the game , i gotta say , i loved every minutes of it! While because of avenger its a game people will ignore , it is incredibly good! The story , the lore i loved everything about it! And this game is absolutly gorgeous! I would recommend for any marvel fans reallly! It has a few bug , but reload checkpoint and it'll fix it! _childDocuments_.review: Nice game ! Marvel Studios output in the movie genre is awesome and this feels like a genuine extension of the MCU. Visuals are really good and the story and characters are spot on . The fight mechanics for me can be a bit overwhelming especially late game, the AI spawns lots of enemies and they mostly target you . Quill is a bit squishy and his damage output is low at the best of times so you must use the team mechanic to stand any chance of survival. That said once you understand this style of game play it gets a bit easier but the game throws up different enemies that require different solutions so in my case i die a lot before i figure it out. Have not finished the game yet so a lot more dying to do! Overall 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: So much better than Avengers. This is a step in the right direction in terms of Marvel games. One of the best stories ever mixed with smooth gameplay. The visuals are insane and some of the best ever for modern art. Reminded me a lot of Mass Effect and Destiny at times. Also has that Ratchet and Clank style humor and shooting / puzzle mechanics. This is also very comic accurate which is nice and the length is decent at 30+ hours. Love the soundtrack as well with a mix of original songs and classics. Got this as a gift so I'm not supporting China / Epic directly.Gamora is def in the top 5 Video game assets.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: It might be pretty far-fetched to call Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy a spiritual spin-off of the movies but it manages to ace that and blow it out of the water.However, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy does fall flat on one department, being extremely linear.Thru the entire game, players will be taken through a long series of various events and combat segments in a linear fashion but boy does it do a damm good job at immersing the players in the shoes of Star-Lord and his crew.Never would i have expected a game to come this close to nailing down the accuracy of the movies and so much more!Anyone who enjoyed the movies but is left wanting more should definitely give this a gander.TL;DR Great Story, Banging Soundtrack. Now go grab some popcorn and enjoy the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game came out of nowhere, I suppose Square Enix chose not to market it so heavily in fear it would flop like Avengers did, but the internet never expected such quality after that fiasco, GoTG has great writing, sweet pacing and a kinda fresh new look at already familiar characters, they don't look a lot like in the movies but I believe they wanted a more comic-like appearance and personalities, I really prefer this Drax to the one in the movies where he's written as the butt of all jokes.Regarding the game itself, the gameplay can get a bit repetitive at times, but there's a few options to mix and match, the leader abilities are pretty cool and while your team's abilities are not yours per se you can use them for amazing combos and absolute damage.It also has many cool and unique mechanics that I enjoyed a lot, like the huddle. The soundtrack of course is amazing, several great songs and a few rickrolls here and there, overall a great experience without much filler and perfect length. Totally recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true masterpiece and my game of the year 2021. In times of vast open worlds with endless filler content it is really refreshing to play a linear story driven game without side quests.The story is very well written and told over 16 playable and engaging chapters which took overall 19 hours to complete. One standout feature is the constant chatting between the characters which makes them believable and very likeable. It is like you are really there with them.Another highlight is the soundtrack. To fight while listening to "Never gonna give you up" is truly amazing. And last but not least the visuals are great, too.On the other hand the game has its minor flaws: the combat is confusing from time to time and jumping sequences may end in sudden death because the game fails to register that the character is in the right position to grab the ledge. But overall these are minor problems because the combat is still very fun and checkpoints are set very fair.During my playthrough I had one major crash to desktop and no performance issues so all in all the game seems to be very fleshed out.To sum things up: Lovely characters, excellent story, awesome soundtrack, great visuals and good overall performance! Highly recommended!tl/dr: I am Groot!

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat this might be the best super hero game I have ever played. Most super hero games have very unique parts that make them special so comparisons are difficult, but this one is firing on all cylinders! I have played through the game twice, once casually and once for achievement cleanup. I had a lot of fun both times but going for collectibles does put a slight damper on things. Now what makes this game special in my eyes is the the fact that its story forward. In most games of this genre the story is perfectly serviceable but in Guardians of the Galaxy its something to boast about! There was many moments that I actually laughed out loud which I cant say about most games. You also are allowed to choose dialogue options throughout the various cut scenes and even when exploring. This aids in immersing you and deepening your bond with the characters. I cant thing of a super hero game that does a better job of making you care for your team. The feeling of comradery increases with the gameplay itself. While you only control one character directly (Star Lord) you also get to give orders to your team in both combat and exploration. You companions never feels like dead weight and the team leader role is fully imagined! Through the game you will gain access to a fair amount of passives for your self and active skills for the entire team. While I was invested in the narrative combat and exploration was always fun aswell. On to sound, yet another area in which the game excels! What we have here is one of the best licenced soundtracks to ever be heard. Its honestly great and the way its used in cutscenes and combat is perfect, you truly feel like your playing out scenes from a movie! The voice acting is also top notch and the delivery aids to the emotional value. General sounds like blasters, creatures and ship thrusters also sound just fine. The last thing I will touch on are the visuals. All of the environments and eye popping and varied! I really enjoyed the game's color pallet and was always excited to see the next planet or ship I would visit. In addition to that the character and enemies had very memorable looks too. A nice thing to mention is the fact that there are a ton of outfits to find for you and your crew through the game. Unlike many games out now you don't have to pay for these just take your time while exploring to find them all! If you would like a narrative driven adventure game or like the Guardians of the Galaxy movies then this is a must buy!

_childDocuments_.review: A MUST buy for fans of Guardians of the Galaxy, especially if you miss the comic-accurate characters.THE Guardians of the Galaxy game we want; great music selection, solid teamwork feel during combat, and great dialogue between the members of the team, and everyone feels accurate to the comics and not the MCU versions. The banter between everyone is great, whether you're on the Milano, exploring the map, or in battle. It really helps them feel like a group that is coming together, learning about each other and growing as a team and not just static, one-sided characters with only a single trope to them.Combat can start to feel repetitive towards the end and so far there's no real incentive for NG+ besides experiencing the story all over again--which in my opinion is great. And you carry over all your unlocked perks and skills. And some of the songs that end up playing after using the Huddle--while amusing, don't really make for hype battle music, like having Never Gonna Give You Up playing while you shoot down a big baddie.If you aren't a content creator, play with Streamer Mode off so you can get the full intended feel of the game and appreciate the song choices in the game. The songs will really help solidify the action and feelings of cutscenes, as certain scenes will play certain songs that will have some sort of lyrical relevance to the situation, you just need to pay attention.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really tested my patience and by its end I didn't want to have anything to do with it.This game is a one trick pony that keeps repeating the same trick expecting treats and adulation every single time.Admittedly the writing in this game is somewhat funny and the characters do transfer rather well (mostly copying what the mcu GOTG did with the presentation of the characters.) but this writing can not save the game, specially when mid battles you realise the characters keep repeating 1 dialogue sequence over and over again. This is a new meaning to one trick pony. The team at Eidos Montreal didn't even bother to write more than one dialogue sequence for each battle sequence and sometimes the lines are reused in more than one.This becomes extra annoying because the game insists on having the character constantly yap on in every single situation.Pause and pacing and taking your time are concepts that this game is completely a stranger to.But you can still forgive some of these issues if it wasn't for the fact that this linear A to B paint by number game is still to this day plagued by bugs and glitches everywhere.And the further you play more bugs and glitches appear.From audio glitches, to visual glitches to complete game breaking glitches.The number of times I was stuck in the geometry and had to reload or the times the game would bug out to the point of restarting the game is ridiculous.This game has so many glitches and bugs you would think it is some Elder Scrolls game or something but as I mentioned it is not.So it makes no sense for these issues after so long to exist in a single player linear game.Other issue is the padding, there are too many slow sequences that fulfill no other function except padding the "game length" and give you the illusion of variety in gameplay.Chief of them all are these sequences where you are put in "control" of the spaceship crashing, or something similar and you are supposed to steer the ship but because it is an extreme on rail sequence you can not control anything really and are forced to sit there wondering "why isn't this a cutscene?".There are a couple of on rail space ship flight sequences that don't really do much, but are ok.And the biggest missed opportunity in the entire game is the soundtrack of this game.Imagine licencing a bunch of cool 80s song and barely using them in favor of muddied and dull and muffled orchestral pieces that are drowned in all the quips and pew pew sounds.The only time you can listen to these songs are on the spaceship where you are treated to many many dialogue sequences with a few that are actually interesting or funny.And even in there the music is played in the background and as soon as you take two steps away from it it gets very low.In the battle sequences you can hear 1 song if you have a charged ability meter that will call the team in a huddle form where you are supposed to deliver a speech from 2 vague dialogue choices and after you deliver that the game will play 1 random song out of the playlist.If this is not stupid I do not know what is.All in all this game is full of missed opportunities and bad decisions and I didn't care for it at all.But if you want to play it you definitely should not pay more than 20dollars.It just isn't worth it imho

_childDocuments_.review: Some jank in combat and traversal but it is still one of the best comic-book stories I've ever had the pleaseure of watching/playing through. The team is still hilarious and there are elements that translate well from the movies, like the music and pop culture references. The game however stays faithful to the canon of the comic books. You get to bond with each character as the story develops and as you find mementos strewn throughout the galaxy. You legitimately feel for each one and by the end you really  do feel like part of the team. The team's bickering is hilarious some choices made me burst out laughing.  The game has an amazing sense of scale and you truly feel small in this galaxy despite it's "on rails" approach to game play. And that "on-rails" approach is not a bad thing when a game is quite simply a roller coaster ride. Honestly the best thing I've played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game! What a ride! What a rush. Not sure exactly how long it took to finish it completely, one time through, but Steam's counter seemed to stop around the 13 hour mark, and I was on Chapter 10. There was a total of 16 Chapters, so it was closer to around 20 hours total, although I tend to play a bit slower than the average player, as I fully explore sections and take my time with them.This game is a non-stop thrill ride, complete with the cutting banter and companion quips that made the first GotG movie such a huge success. Even though the change of characters from their on-screen counterparts was quite noticeable at first, it didn't take long before I felt like I was adventuring with some old pals. I liked Rocket's, Mantis's, and Drax's voice actors the best, but Peter, Gamora, and Groot's did oustanding as well.The 80s rock music lent a nice touch to the whole experience, and the space visuals were nothing short of extraordinary, and it brought back so many good memories of what a great space exploration sim should be.  I won't bore you with a bunch of nitpicky details, but the graphics are seriously out-of-this-world stunning.I can only hope they do more games like this in the series, as they captured the magic and essence of the first movie and made it into an epic space adventure. I saw many, many complaints about the game being "too short", but I felt like it was just right, with no filler, and only epic goodness that stayed just as long as it needed to. I'd be Team Guardians' wingman any day. Rock on!!

_childDocuments_.review: It is kinda funny how one of the most interesting and compelling videogames of this whole year will not get an attention it deserves. But rest assured, it is definitely worth your time and money. First of all, it is the best version of Guardians of the Galaxy to date. I love both MCU movies directed by James Gunn, but characters here are so much more fleshed out, especially Drax, who is not just a comedic relief (sometimes still is tho), but deep, flawed warrior who cannot get over the loss of his family. And believe me, I can continue talking in the same way about Gamora, Quill, Rocket, even Groot (and he is just a tree dammit!) but this is something that you should experience yourself. What really surprised me it's the plot in general. Well, to be honest, I did not know what to expect from it at all, even from watching the trailers, and, in my opinion, it captured the very essense of GotG - this story and personal and grand in scale at the same time, which is totally mind-blowing, so I guess we all should thank writers at Eidos Montreal for this, these are the same guys who worked on Deus Ex after all.Presentation is top-notch across the board - environments are rich with detail and variety of places which we can visit during 20-hour campaign is impressive. And the soundtrack, man, the soundtrack. When I first launched the game the very first song that I heard was "Never Gonna Give You Up", so GotG rickrolled me and got my attention for the get go, the rest of OST is brilliant to and listen to "Final Countdown" by Europe during the battle it is just whole another level, as if we are inside Quill's head when he listens to his Walkman during the battle (or whatever cassette player he has).Speaking of battles the combat itself is... fun. It is not flawless that's for sure, but it has a certain depth to it, which is enough to not leave you bored in the middle of the mission. All Guardians have a set of special abilities which we can combine into simple but effective combos. What I can say for sure - it can be a little jarring at the start of the game but I suggest to give the game some time, buy a couple of abilities for each member of the team and you will not be disappointed, it will be at least fun, just like I said at the start of this paragraph :)If you are still hesitating about buying this game - don't. It is a well-crafted, solid experience that has something that most of the games do not have nowadays - beating and passionate heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a fantastic game that captures the spirit and humor of the comics and movies. You play as Star-Lord, the leader of a ragtag group of misfits who have to save the galaxy from a cosmic threat. The game is full of action, adventure, and witty dialogue that will make you laugh out loud. The graphics are stunning, the soundtrack is awesome, and the gameplay is smooth and varied. You can switch between different weapons and abilities, such as pistols, rifles, grenades, and elemental blasts. You can also use your jetpack to fly around, dodge attacks, and reach new areas. You can command your teammates to unleash their skills, such as Rocket's bombs, Gamora's sword slashes, Drax's brute force, and Groot's vines. The game also features choices and consequences that affect the story and your relationships with your crew. You can choose how to respond to different situations, such as whether to be a hero or a jerk, whether to sell out or stick together, and whether to follow or break the rules. Your choices will have an impact on how your teammates react to you, how the galaxy views you, and how the story unfolds. For example, in one mission, you have to decide whether to give a valuable artifact to a shady collector or keep it for yourself. Depending on your choice, you will either get a lot of money or a powerful upgrade, but you will also anger one of your teammates who wanted the opposite. This will affect their loyalty and their performance in combat. The game is a blast to play from start to finish, and I highly recommend it to anyone who loves Marvel or sci-fi games.The game has about 17½ hours of main story content, but if you want to explore everything and complete all the side missions and collectables, you can expect to spend around 25½ hours . The game also has some replay value, as you can try different choices and see how they affect the outcome. However, if you are looking for a multiplayer or co-op mode in this game, you will be disappointed. The game is **strictly a single-player affair. There’s no multiplayer or co-op features here whatsoever . It may seem strange – after all, a game about a group of heroes seems like the perfect base for a co-op game. But you can only ever play as Star-Lord, and the other Guardians are controlled by AI. This may be a deal-breaker for some players who want to share the experience with their friends or play as their favourite Guardian.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is a visually stunning game that offers an immersive gameplay experience. Although the launch was initially problematic, the developers quickly fixed the performance issues with several patches, making the game run smoothly. The game's combat system is one of its most outstanding features, where as Starlord, you can give commands to your team, each with its own unique set of abilities, allowing for a more strategic approach to fights.The story is well written, and each character is meticulously crafted, allowing you to form an emotional connection with them. Your choices will influence the story's direction, adding a layer of depth to the game. The enemies are diverse, and to defeat them, you need to understand their weaknesses, which adds another element of strategy to the game.While the game is not open-world, it still provides ample opportunities for exploration, and discovering hidden chests and other rewards is rewarding. The game's progression system is well designed, with no microtransactions, and everything is unlocked by either exploring or progressing through the story.Finally, the game offers a new game plus mode that allows you to enjoy the game even more, especially if you want to experience different aspects of the story or improve your combat skills. Overall, Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy is an exciting and enjoyable game, offering a perfect mix of strategy, exploration, and action.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game not on my radar in the slightest, I was completely blown away by my experience. I am not even much of a Marvel fan and by all accounts this game should have not have been anywhere near as good as it was following the heels of Avengers. The story, characters, dialogue, music, environments, art style and overall experience was superb. The one aspect lacking was the combat, it starts pretty bland and becomes better as the game progresses and more abilities are unlocked, then starts to sag again towards the end. It is best to describe it as a beat 'em up with special abilities, which means lots of spamming, which may turn away some folks. There is also a under-baked huddle mechanic where you can pump up the team in the middle of a fight. It was fun at first, but felt like it may have been able to be incorporated into more meaningful moments rather than having it be a gauge activated by the player.Otherwise, every other aspect of the game was amazing. I was thoroughly engaged with the story and actually saw it through to the end, which is a rarer feat these days. Major respect for each of the voice actors whose performances were shockingly good. I can confidently say I like game Guardians way more than I liked the movie Guardians, they felt closer aligned to the comics and felt more real. Easily one of the best non-indie games I played all year.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game a recommendation but with the reveal of the DLC characters my opinion was swayed negative. Don't get me wrong if you're a fan of One Piece and Warrior titles this game is fun. But they've done pretty much the same amount of negative changes as they did things right. The DLC characters however are the final nail for me because we already have 4 Germa 66 Characters and now we get another one. We already have a good amount of Charlotte Pirates but now get two more. Why aren't previously playable character no longer playable like : Caesar Clown, Perona, Gecko Moria, Magellan, Kuma, Enel and probably more. Why aren't characters like Mr 3/1 and many more avaible as Enemies but not playable? I really feel like they wasted some slots, especially 4 G66 characters, for Characters that deserved it more and also would've been more fun to play.But let's get to the most annoying changes, because a Roster is always hard to select when you've got over 20 years to choose from.Characters are now split into Power, Speed, Technik and Sky types.This has turned some of my previous favorite characters into my least played characters. Because the new Full burst mode you can activate means you'll be hanging in the sky only using Aerial Combos and Attacks that all feel alot less powerful and effective than being on the ground.To be fair however they've improved alot of the characters to be able to change somethings however, even though you only really feel this for Luffy and Sanjii. Luffy for example can activate gear 2/4/snakeman to change his moveset also changing his Type. I've always hated gear 4 and this makes gear 2 Luffy a viable option. However it feels like only a few characters received this overhaul. Chopper and Franky in my opinion really needed an Overhaul like that but didn't get it. Both of these Characters could've been great if you could just change their modes to get different skillsets...The Special attack changes are mostly great.You've now got 4 different special attacks you can choose from, however one of them should always be the Full burst mode whch is the new equivalent to Haki/Kizuna Rush from the old games. However as mentioned this turns Sky types into always flying characters that can't use ground moves. However choosing what ultimate attacks to use really allows some customization that feels great.The new leveling system are essentially skilltrees which are a nice touch to level up characters the only thing I don't like is that it doesn't tell you where to find the coins you need to unlock special attacks. Which means you'll be scrolling through that mission list looking for things related to that character to find them.Lastly are of course the actual roster and I've already mentioned that I'm missing some characters here. Logia users are no longer as much fun to play as they used to and I'm really missing Magellan here. It's a shame that Luffy, Sanjii and Zorro get 5-8 outfits while Nami only gets two playable outfits and Franky, Chopper, Brook and Robin all get no alternative outfits despite having alternative models in the game.The game does have an great if not too large representation of the Big Mom storyline with atleast 10 and a few Worst Generation characters such as Kid, Bege, Hawkins making their debut, especially Kid play interesting while Bege is a summon type character that usually would be my favorite but this might be the worst version I've seen and I really liked this type in other Dynasty Warrior games. The Roster seems ok overall even though I'm really missing a few. Personally I would've cut atleast half of the new character to bring back Magellan, Enel, Perona and Kuma atleast if not a few never before playable characters from either CP9 or the Alabasta Saga. But that's just personal preference.Anyway as I've said I'm really conflicted wether to give this a recommendation or not so it's a buy at discount  since it's good but it's not better than PW3

_childDocuments_.review: Saying it's worse than Pirate Warriors 3 is like saying a banana split with chocolate syrup on it is worse than a banana split with butterscotch syrup on it. You're still getting a banana split, it's still delicious, and it's really all down to personal taste.This game slaps, but I'm a butterscotch kinda guy. One thing I really don't like about it, though it's not a game breaker, is how much looser the combat feels compared to its predecessors -- you really feel like, especially with speed and sky-type characters, you're just zooming around almost to the point of being out of control. I haven't played as all of the characters yet, so I can't really say I've settled into one I enjoy deeply, but as a result I'm finding myself playing as a wider variety of characters compared to earlier titles *because* I haven't settled into a main. The characters I usually play as have been changed dramatically (Sanji) or gutted to an unfortunate degree (Tashigi), so finding a new one is a bit of an ongoing effort, I'd say.The campaign mode is fine, it's about as good as any of the PW games' campaigns are, though I really do miss PW1's more linear, mission-type layouts with obstacles to overcome and problems to solve compared to later games' more traditional musou play. I didn't realize how much I missed that kind of musou game until I played P5 Strikers, actually. PW4 being a more traditional musou game like PW3 but without the *impact* you feel with your attacks and without some real army-clearing attacks like the Kizuna follow-ups makes it feel a lot less dynamic as a result. The fact that there's not much free-play or mission mode like PW3's is also a point against it.But, where the game falters is also where it really kicks up something new and interesting by comparison. If you're a grindfest kinda guy like I am, the new character upgrade maps are a treat and make you feel like you're really advancing a character unlike PW3's coin system. The giant enemies are fun as heck to take down even on harder difficulties, where you'd expect them to just be HP sponges, and they add a layer of strategy to the greater map design that I really enjoyed. Overall, I would say the feeling of taking down a giant and capturing territories in this game is about as fun and high-pressure as getting Kizuna score was in PW3, and I'm a lot more thankful of how much less stressful S-Ranking a map is in this one.Game's solid, definitely a recommend.But man, they really did my boy Sanji dirty. Though, if you were playing Sanji in Pirate Warriors games to begin with, you're already a special kind of masochist, I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and straightforward musou game with a good amount of playable characters. Graphics are very nice for conveying the anime artstyle, nothing like the abomination that is Jump Force. The game has three primary game modes and I haven't even gone through the first one yet which is the main story. The game's just so fun that I felt I had to drop a review already. But it's only really worth it if you're a fan of One Piece. This game does go through the storyline events but in an extremely condensed manner. It skips over entire arcs like East Blue, Skypiea, Thriller Bark, Impel Down, Fishman Island and Punk Hazard on top of only showing the bare minimum of what happened during the arcs that it does cover. So unless you've read the manga or seen the anime, you'll have no idea what is happening and who the characters are. Cutscenes are also in 30fps so they look hideously out of place and choppy. A lot of the story content that has you going through dialogue boxes just looks very flat and emotionless. Personal score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Been a One Piece fan for years now, I love the story, the characters, the humor, everything. As a long time fan this game has been just one MASSIVE disappointment. The "Dramatic Log" being the main story, skipped over a disgusting amount of the source material. After glossing over all of the East Blue Saga (the beginning adventures of One Piece, where much of the world and it's rules are explained) you abruptly start halfway through the Alabasta Arc. This game is very obviously targeting long time fans, they expect you to know 90% of this stuff going in, but they continue on at a break-neck pace to the point where the game condenses whole chunks of story into miniature cut scenes. Typically, though momentarily, touching upon the more memorable scenes from the source material. Honestly the last Pirate Warriors game did a much better job going through the story.Aside from the bungling of a main story, there's the "Treasure Log" game mode, specifically there to run you through hypothetical battles and situations in order to give character specific coins that'll allow you to get specific upgrades to certain characters. Honestly the game play isn't half bad, (aside from the occasional frame drop) it runs great, looks pretty good too and I'd say it's exactly what you expect from a "Dynasty Warriors" type game, just a cathartic action game, smashing through hoards of enemies and using coins and berries to level up the various characters to make it easier to smash through hoards of enemies. If that's your jam, more power to you, it's a pretty decent game if that's all you care about. Me personally being a long time fan, I'll still play it but I am thoroughly upset at how the story was portrayed. I was hoping to get my friends into One Piece through this game and unfortunately that seems highly unlikely.Story 2/10Gameplay 7/10Graphics 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth having as a One Piece fan and it`s a pretty decent musou game in general though it`s not without its flaws.Pros- Much better roster than Pirate Warriors 3, and the characters feel quite distinct. Additions like Kid, Hawkins, Reiju, and  Carrot are lots of fun to play.- Kaido's Dragon Form (and the Yonko in general) are insanely powerful and fun to play- Better controller support than Pirate Warriors 3 but still requires some tweaking- Pretty good quality cutscenes and animationsCons- Abridged story is hard to follow for beginners. Lots of important characters and side-plots are glossed over entirely. This   is definitely not how you want to get introduced to One Piece's story.- The game content feels more sparse than Pirate Warriors 3. I should have 100% achievements and gotten S class finishes    on all missions (Story and Treasure Log) by about 35hrs in. Learning to use the entire roster will obviously add more time   but I can't really see myself playing this for more than 70hrs in total if that.- Camera is very slightly improved over Pirate Warriors but still pretty bad in general.- The HUD gets cluttered very quickly and the minimap gets lit up like a Christmas tree which can make navigation a real    pain. Overall, I'd still recommend owning this game but don't buy it at full price. Wait for at least a 20-30% discount, and that's only if you're a One Piece fan. If you're new to the series or just like musou games, wait for something more steep like half off.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% it in 2 days. This is the best pirate warriors to date. ===================================================================The Good Stuff:+++ The Y / Triangle string has been removed and has been replaced with each character's unique action. It has the best move-set for all characters due to the new Jump action, harder characters like Marco plays better in this than in Pirate Warriors 3. Extremely powerful characters like Kizaru from Pirate Warriors 3 is completely balanced in this, that being said, he is still incredibly op.++ There is a new stamina system where you cannot spam attacks using dash and constantly stun-lock your enemy anymore. Some SKY characters like Kizaru have the ability to dash across the map, flying over buildings and enemy while using up his stamina.+ There is destructible environment in this game. This greatly help the game to look like One Piece when every fight has a building destroyed.+ It is also easier to 100% this game since the crew level system is greatly improved. It takes a few battles to level them up to MAX which is so much better as you need the coins from them to upgrade your characters and unlock new moves. In Pirate Warriors 3, you had to really grind the crew level system to get certain skills or a better version of an already unlocked skills. ===================================================================The Not So Good Stuff:-- However there is a lack of content? Some characters from Pirate Warriors 2/3 are not here, costumes and outfits from previous are also not included. Smaller arcs like Romance Dawn and Arlong Park are completely omitted.- Bosses like Drake are incredibly frustrating to fight when using taller characters like Katakuri, basically Drake's hitbox causes you to go up in the air when you are attacking him which switches your X / Square attacks to be Air attacks.===================================================================Overall 10/10, Charlotte Katakuri is way too over-powered like Hello? If there is any missions I could not get rank S in. I just swap to Katakuri.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Warriors game. If you don't want a mindless beat-em-up/hack-n-slash, you will likely not enjoy this game. If you are not a One Piece fan, you will likely not enjoy this game. Combat changes are super but not all characters fit it particularly well. About half the characters are a blast to blaze through while the other half feel either incomplete or like they were ripped straight from the previous game with little care. Compare Luffy, Katakuri, and Ace who got lovingly crafted and versatile movesets to Tashigi and Ivankov who feel like NPCs made playable with little adjustment. Bartolomeo in particular feels like a WIP. Your favorite character's effectiveness will do a lot to determine your enjoyment of this game. Story attempting to be more in-depth on a few arcs is also super but after Alabasta falls flat with the lack of map variety and glossing over of important events and characters even in the drastically reduced scope of the story. Enies Lobby and Onigashima are particularly awful maps. Online is terrible! No way to mute or kick bothersome players nor can you create private rooms so playing with friends is a crapshoot. A notable chunk of story missions are also single player only which hinders the point of playing cooperatively. Tons of costumes were removed from the previous games, even costumes that literally appear in cutscenes don't make the cut. Barely any new costumes were added. Dressrosa is one of the arcs in this game. Luffy is the only Strawhat with his Dressrosa outfit. Even among those who had their Dressrosa outfits in PW3. Leveling up characters is a drag. You have to upgrade every single individual stat point by hand. There is no way to speed up the process of leveling characters. If you like to swap characters often, expect to be spending minutes before every stage slowly bringing your characters up to level. Every other Warriors game I've played has an easily accessible quick level system. On the brightside, the PC port is MUCH better this time around. Actual options and controller support! For those having trouble setting up their controllers, go to settings > controller > general controller settings and enable configuration support for your controller of choice. I enjoyed my time with this game but I do not think this is a quality and worthwhile experience for anyone who wants something beyond watching their favorite One Piece character do their Warriors thing.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece is one of my top favourite animes. I would of loved to play the east blue arc, as well as skypea and all the other ones. But they did include really good arcs too, even the original wano arc made up by them. One problem I have with the game is, that there isn't a big selection of costumes. The pre time skip nami, chopper, robin, and franky characters aren't playable, just the post time skip. Those aren't really a big problem, but still something I always think about. The rest of the game feels really nice, and is very much playable. In the first 2 days, I have spent 20 hrs on this game, which is quite something, cause not many games can grab my attention right away. I love all the characters, and their abilities are just like in the anime. Which makes me happy. Some more characters could of been added though. For example, to just name a few. Garp, Sengoku, Kawamatsu, Sandersonia, Marigold, Dogstorm, Cat Viper, Pedro, Enel, Caesar, and probably many more. But I am very content with the current characters. Overall I would say that, if you really like one piece, and you want to play the major characters and feel like you are them. Then you should get this game. It's worth every penny, and I will guarantee that any one piece fan would love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm the kinda guy that starts from 0 being bad, but I'd give it a 7/10! This is a very fun game. If you've played Pirate Warriors titles in the past or even Dynasty Warriors games then you're in luck! The gameplay is a standout for this game and gives you hours of content just trying to figure out the optimal way to play for each character. Graphics are pretty decent and the writing is good. My only complaints are the lack of relevant and wanted costumes for characters that appear in story missions (such as Nami in the Big Mom arc) and the inability to do much against characters that have too much poise or logia fruits when using an inferior character. This game would really benefit from the addition of resource grinding maps, a way to hit logia users (perhaps a skill), more costumes for other characters, Perona (please), or extra missions that weren't just a listed menu. Pirate Warriors 3 did all of these well and if the controller support on steam was any good I'd say to play that instead. However, I loved almost every bit of gameplay so far and would definitely recommend to those searching for some One Piece content.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game A LOT, I can say it's great. I'll run it down more detailed, but tldr: controller support is there (just needs to be enabled in properties>and controller settings), and I play on an XOne mini and it functions perfectly, the game looks good, the combo system is fun and there's a lot to sink time into. Now let's get more into it. The story: the story covers from  to  ,although it's apart from the very beginning a game original. It does briefly cover them but gameplay-wise skips over  ,  ,  ,  and  . Playing coop (Ill cover it too) we finished the story in 20 hours. The maps are also really well done to represent the actual layout used in the anime/manga this time around.The gameplay: classic musou style combat, aerial combos add more depth from previous titles. Musou/special attacks are a grid now, where you "build a loadout" of 4 different ones, ranging from traditional cutscene-y musous to transformations to heals/buffs to basic empowered versions of special attacks. Overall, very fun combat.Other notable stuff: Coop works well and you can experience all story/treasure log maps in 2p coop, as well as a few dozen treasure log maps that can be played with up to 4 players (empty slots are filled with AI). The progression has been made interesting and instead of just levelling up you use coins and berries to progress the abilities of your characters.Negatives: In coop the timing for invites is awkward, and sometimes I'd end up with a random player joining me before my friend could join. Also there are multiple major characters missing that were included in previous games, and while there are 9 upcoming dlc chars, missing chars they already had movesets for is kinda sad.Overall, the game is really good and I can easily recommend it to any warriors/one piece fan

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I can finally recommend this game on Steam Deck since a user posted the definitive fix for the missing cutscenes in the forums. So let me explain: if you play this game right out of the box on Steam Deck, it won't show the cutscenes. Forcing compatibility with Proton GE (8-25 in my case) will show them with music only but no voices. So you still need to add a launch command which you can easily find if you search for "Steam Deck fix for Pirate Warriors 4".Now, that being said, the game is awesome. I'm not a long time OP fan, but this game is fun and has way better graphics than PW3 (I love that one too for other reasons). You won't find much of a challenge here, just mind numbing button mashing, but it's great to deploy that big amount of power over hundreds of enemies. You can also enjoy this as a two player couch or online co-op (a note on this: I like it better how the 2p mode is handled in PW3, here you can't compete for points in story mode).Conclusion: you can play this on Steam Deck, it runs pretty well, and I highly recommend doing all the configuration thing explained above to enjoy the full experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is one of the best One Piece games available right now. However, be warned if you want this game for the story of One Piece prepare for a severe cut in content compared to Pirate Warriors 3 and If you want to buy the game for this I do not recommend it for you. Buy pw3 instead.I personally did not look forward to and purchase the game for the number of story arcs included but for the new characters, new gameplay mechanics, updated maps, online game modes and future characters. For the most part it delivered on these expectations.The new mechanics work great for a lot of characters however, some characters do not have any aerial combos.Any character you choose has a decent moveset of combos and special attacks which only expand once you upgrade that character with higher input combos, new special attacks with some characters gaining a form change which completely changes their moveset and attacks dependant on the character you choose.The character roster overall is an improvement compared to pw3, however certain character's were cut for more questionable choices such as all of Sanji's siblings which all have similar gameplay. Otherwise there are more characters to choose compared to pw3 and they is far more variety between characters in pw4. Each is so unique in how you can play with them.The maps are overall a nice visual enhancement, however, they are more confusing at times in tight spaces with the larger characters and take some time to learn to navigate. The online mode works ok, but doesn't have great compatibility with each player as you will have to join each other's game every time you want to start a new mission rather than make a party and be able to stay in it like every other online game has. With the gamemodes they are ok, however, Bandai has gone pretty basic with their approach to it. The boss battles are fun only if you have the difficulty maxed out on extreme diffifculty (which is only available after you complete the story) and on the higher levels, when enemy's have higher amounts of health and attack more often.The problem I had the most with pw3 is that it takes soo long to get access to the higher level combos and abilites of characters no matter how great or trival they are between characters. pw4 solves this for the most part, however, gameplay is different in a good or bad way for some. Main enemies now have an armour you have to break before you can actually start damaging the enemy. In the early game this is fairly annoying and the animations of massive white circles forming gets in the way for seeing the enemy which makes it harder to fight them rather than easier which was the developer's intentions. They did not think this through well, the sounds everytime you hit would have been more than enough. Now in the later sections of the game when your characters are a lot stronger this does benefit this gameplay as fights last longer than in pw3 and you actually feel like you are battling the character's in the world on the higher difficulites compared to pirate warriors 3 which I felt was too short with the 1v1 battles at times. However, this can get more overwhelming to deal with compared to 3 if you are not good enough on the higher difficilities. Pretty good changes overall though for the gameplay and obtaining new abilites for you characters. Be warned Bandai has left some characters wanting with the new mechanics like air combos and form changes especially were left out for a lot of characters such as Chopper and Carrot which would have benfitted immensely from a form change.Overall if you are looking for a good One Piece beat em up game and a different kind of Pirate Warriors game, I recommend this game with a new roster it keeps things interesting for many hours and more characters for the future will be in the character pass even if it is likely way overpriced for what we will get like Cracker, Smoothie, Judge so far and potentially the Beast Pirates like X-Drake if the scans I have seen are correct.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PIECE: PIRATE WARRIORS 4

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must have for everyone who ever enjoyed One Piece in their lives, possibly even to people who had no prior experience with the series. It's better than Pirate Warriors 3, which was already incredible, in basically every aspect, Smoother gameplay, better graphics, more interesting character progression, destructible terrain...all that good stuff. All the canonical techniques from One Piece are here, characters, locations, which also includes all the newer stuff like Big Mom, Kaido, etc.The only possible downside I can find is the story. It seems they wanted to fit the whole of One Piece in this game for some reason, which results in like 75% of it being cut out, or told to us by narrator through cutscenes. If you know the story from the manga or the anime this won't be an issue, but people who hope to follow the plot through the game will probably not be able to do that here. I wish they'd just started from a later part of the story and followed it more closely instead.

_childDocuments_.review: For fans and newcomers of OP, this game is probably my favorite Warriors off-series game on Steam. As a hack 'n' slash genre contender, OPPW4 has powerful and fun characters with cool combos and VFX, beautiful stages and interesting matchups. The game loosely follows the plot of the manga/anime (loosely = skipping the filler and abridging most of the important events) and adds "what if" scenarios to the mix via another game mode.Leveling characters can be a bit tedious, because the game's coin system makes you grind more than just a few battles to get the rarest of coins. Money won't be as big of a problem. As a musician, I really appreciate the soundtrack. There are nice rock beats, a hint of metal and exceeding amounts of funky flavor in it. It really packs a punch and just makes you listen to it. I've sometimes just stopped fighting to listen to the BGM, it's really good!Absolutely worth the price! :)

_childDocuments_.review: (TL;DR) If you liked Pirate Warriors 3, you'll love this.Where PW3's story log covered the majority of One Piece from the start to the Dressrosa Arc, this installment gives a brief overview of early events with the earliest level taking place at the end of the Alabasta Arc. After getting caught up to where the previous game left off and properly finishing Dressrosa, the story goes through Whole Cake Island, skipping Zou for the most part, and finally (to a certain point) the Wano Arc. It should be mentioned that at this point the game continues with its own original story, as the Wano Arc is still in progress at the time of this game's release.Gameplay-wise it's more of the same from PW3 but with more polish and a different roster of characters. Also the absurd grinding needed to get certain coins has been done away with and made MUCH more streamline while also making leveling individual characters less of chore.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PIECE: PIRATE WARRIORS 4

_childDocuments_.review: These are just my personal thought about the game.Likes:- They upgrading (or reworking?) aerial battle works much better than i thought, especially for Speed and Sky type character. It makes the combat much faster, feels like a dbz fight when you juggle and move the enemy around with those aerial combos. And the aerial fight actually suits the character like Sanji, Marco, Vinsmokes brother, Crocodile, etc- Giant unit are hella fun. They felt so strong and can clear those higher difficulty mission easier. The destructible environment also helps in making them feels more powerful- The new upgrade and skill system also feels nice. Help yourself by not watching the moveset from Youtube. It is part of the fun to wonder what kind of move you can unlock from the skill map.- The cutscene looks clean, you can feel the upgrade from Pirate Warrior 3Dislikes:- Half of the new unit are locked behind DLC. You can get vinsmoke brothers and sisters, kaido, bigmom, katakuri, carrot, kidd with the basegame. But other supernovas, sweet commanders, wano characters are locked behind dlcs (which i don't really mind buying when discount)- No costume for wholecake island nami, despite her being a big contributor in the arc. And in general, the costume just seems lacking- Wholecake island is supposed to be the new big arc that they can implement fully following the anime since Pirate Warrior 3, but the execution seems a bit lackluster. No Crackers fight, no Smoothies, no Djinn dude. I'm not demanding them to be playable, but they definitely need to shows at least as enemies- The campaign starts from pre-timeskip as far as Arabasta arc, which i think won't be needed anymore. Yes Arabasta and Ennies Lobby arc is really cool, but we have saved vivi and robin in the previous game (which also more fleshed out). There's no point in doing that again, and should just focused on making new world stuff better.Final verdict:- The progress for character feels fun, the new mechanic (aerial combos and giant unit) are hella fun, and makes it different from previous game. Definitely worth buying it.- Don't pirate it since it unlocks everything iirc, which takes half of the fun away- The issue mentioned in "Dislike" is quite annoying. So for best value, just buy it when discount (but when it's in discount, go buy the DLC. I think the DLC characters are fun and the price is actually justified)

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Among the better games in the Warriors series.+Beautiful art and animation. Nami truly is pleasing to the eye ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)+Runs smoothly, minor choppiness during cutscenes+++Combo system is really great and allows more options than any other game in the series I have played so far+Destructible environment. Throwing enemies into buildings damages both enemies and the buildings, falling rubble causes damage to enemies. +Very fluid movement. Very few invisible walls (practically none)+thousands of enemies to fight even in early maps, aside for 1v1 duels+visits parts of the story not seen in previous games--no remote play together support during the time of writing. Hoping for this to be fixed soon.-certain maps do not allow coop at all, some allow only online coop for whatever reason.-early on fighting some bosses feels dull, since you do so little damage to both their HP and shields. This does get fixed over time as your characters grow stronger.-1v1 duels are generally dull because no hordes of peons flying around in the background-some story points from older games are skipped altogether

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a frigging blast!I've played the Dynasty Warriors titles from 1 to 5 with great pleasure until 6 disappointed. Picked up PW 3 last year and had tons of fun. This 4th part however blows it out of the water.Pros:- The gameplay is much smoother and the combos feel great. Aerial combat is just nuts.- You can use and choose more special moves(musou). They all charge individually.- The coin system seems less grindy so far.- You have a lot more freedom on the maps. There're less invisible walls which gives a better feeling while traveling/fighting and you can destroy most buildings etc. Always wanted to use Whitebeards quake powers to destroy a bunch of buildings? Well here is your chance!- Best thing of all is you can finally play the story via online coop, though it isn't perfect. You have to invite your friend for every map and don't stay together after finishing one.Cons:- The multiplayer might disconnect sometimes which they'll hopefully fix. It doesn't happen to often but still sucks since the person who disconnects doesn't get the points for that round.- Some people seem to have lost their save file after the game crashed, though mine didn't crash once I wouldn't want that to happen. Needs to be fixed asap.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of Dynasty Warriors for years and recently finished the manga up until the Wano arc of one piece. This game is a great Mosuo and One Piece game. The game in general is loads of fun and I find it to be a great stress relief to be able to slay thousands on a battlefield. It also does a really good job of recapping the story considering the amount it has to go over. TLDR: Definitely worth the buy if you love Mosuo games or the show!

_childDocuments_.review: The good:+ Gameplay and new movesets for many characters feel more fluent and devastating than PW3.+ New giant type enemies are fun to fight.+ The biggest roster of playable characters with 43 in the base game and 9 DLC.+ New, bigger maps with the new building-destruction mechanic really help sell the power fantasy.+ Better visual and effect when compared to PW3.+ Great music.The bad:- Lock-on camera is god awful at times- Many playable story arcs like Arlong, Thriller park, Fishman island in PW3, are either removed or reduced into recap cutscenes in PW4.- With the revamped gameplay, the kizuna rush mechanic is gone, I can't say if this is for the better or worse in term of gameplay but without it, a somewhat unique aspect of characters' interactions is gone.- Less alternate outfits for many characters.- Dream logs' interface is severely downgraded from an interactive map to a simple selection menu.- No more treasure events, legend diary or anything that would encourage you to replay story missions except for getting S grade.- Some maps can be quite annoying to navigate.- The new buildings-destruction system feel somewhat underused, like i was hoping to be able to create new routes on some maps and not just dealing extra damage to enemies.Overall:- Is this a good musou game? Yes.- Is this game a good sequel to PW3? Absolutely not, if anything this is more PW3.5 than a full sequel.- Should you try this out knowing nothing about One piece? Maybe not, many of the main story arcs are greatly abridged or glossed over.- Should you try this out as a One Piece fan? Yes, but i highly recommend getting this on sale.

Another plus is that controllers work fine, all with button prompts. For those who played Pirate Warriors 3 you know how much this was a problem then.
