_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - Not a perfect One Piece tribute, but Musou games have never been better. Full review below.= Intro =Love 'Musou' games, love One Piece. Recently started playing Berserk again, really looked forward to this after the letdown of DOOM: Eternal.= Gameplay = It's a Musou. You play an absurdly powerful hero and beat up literally thousands of enemies with a variety of splashy attacks and combos, while conquering territory to spawn thousands of your own troops.PW3 was a lot of fun, but felt floaty, repetitive and bland at times. Fortunately PW4 fixes a whole lot of that - combat is meatier, the new specials system is a fantastic improvement, boss fights are now fully realized and have some interesting mechanics (although Pica in particular reveals one of the game's biggest remaining flaws) and you even have a rudimentary skill tree - although not quite as good as Berserk's loot/crafting system. Story mode is solid, with a few caveats - and the Treasure Log (similar to the Dream/Nightmare log of the previous game) is a huge improvement, with some genuinely creative and fun mission goals.Characters are well designed and varied, with each one having a unique mechanic or two. Honestly, gameplay wise there isn't much to complain about here. As a Musou, this feels like the genre is heading towards some point where it's going to explode into the mainstream.Everything feels like an upgrade - maps are bigger, enemies are more plentiful, tons of little refinements and improvements all over the place. As a game, it's really good.That said, there are some issues. I don't like having to play through the story to unlock the majority of characters - in the previous game you could earn them gradually through the Log mode. I don't like how much content the game skips over (more below) and the difficulty settings feel out of whack. Hard is great - if you don't mind a bit of grinding and a *huge* difficulty spike midway through, Normal is 'my first Musou game' and Easy is 'my drunk cat's first Musou game'. = Graphics & Audio =While it's not going to knock your socks off, it's a much prettier game (and a great PC port) - with stuff like tesselation adding a lot of visual oomph. The game does look slightly washed out, but pumping up the vibrancy with something like Reshade works well.However, the camera - a common problem in Musous is really bad here. The inclusion of gigantic enemies makes it worse, when the camera zooms out and starts clipping into the boss, the scenery etc. It's been a problem for a while in the genre, and the general excellence of the game makes it more obvious over time.Music is solid, but I turned it off after a while. = Style =This is where PW4 comes a bit short. As a game, on it's own merits, it's great. As a One Piece tribute, it's...complicated. Rather than focusing on the *entire* story of OP, PW4 instead cuts things down and focuses more on depth within each arc. However, this feels a little odd sometimes - so many really great bits of the story are cut here. No Skypeia, no Thriller Bark, no Impel Down, no Zou, no Fishman Island. And yes, this means that most of the characters from these arcs are cut too - no Enel, Moria, Magellan etc.The real shame though is that the later arcs that PW3 didn't get to also feel a bit thin. Whole Cake island is done decently, but Dressrosa is ridiculously cut down - the only Doflamingo Family characters are Diamante and Pica (neither are playable). No Trebol, no Baby 5, no Gladius and you never get to play Greenbit, the underground docks etc. Meh.If they wanted to cut redundant content and focus on newer stuff, why not cut Alabasta and give us a more fully realized version of Dressrosa?Beyond this, there are a few fully realized characters in the game that are not playable - evidently being kept back for DLC. I despise DLC in a AAA priced game like this.= Value =There is a *lot* of game here. 36 main story missions (although it's more like 30, as quite a few of these are just boss fights. Beyond this, you've got the excellent new Treasure Log to play, online features etc. Definitely good value even at a AAA price - although, again, I dislike how much was cut and the evident DLC shenanigans going on here.I do wish skill trees were a bit more fleshed out, but with a cast of 40+ characters, that may be a bit ambitious.= Overall =+ The best Musou game to date.+ Insanely fun.+ Plenty of content.+ Lots of improvements and added features.+ I'm already stoked for #5- A huge amount of the OP story is missing here.- Giant characters are not implemented well.- Horrible camera.At the end of the day, this game just...rocks. It's not a perfect One Piece game, but it's fairly close to a perfect Musou. Highly recommended, but if you are in it purely as a OP tribute, you may be let down.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros+ Dash Cancels, Air Combos and Big Damage to the Environment+ Great Character Models+ Mega-Church of Katakuri Approved+ Co-op is Solid+ Big Mom and Kaido are BIG!!!+ It has that Lego Star Wars vibe of defeating a boss, and then getting to Free Play as them.+ BIG MONKE LUFFY VS GIANT LIZARD KAIDO is a good final battle for this game.Cons- This game skips a few arcs (Skypiea, Fishman Island, pretty much all of East Blue.) It does recap events that aren't playable, and focuses more on the major battles within the series.- This game is also really quick to beat your first time through, and there isn't much replay value outside of mastering different characters and - The Boss Armor is ANNOYING! It only pads out the fight, and can easily break the flow of combat when it recharges. Not as big of an issue in the late game, but by that point it's a grind to surpass.- Invisible Walls where you think you should be able to jump, and the maps tend to be bigger than needed - especially when a mission-important ally needs help from the other side of the battlefield.- I miss the Crew Attacks from 3... being able to have the crew line up and unleash a Combination Finisher on the Bosses really hyped-up the fights.OVERALLGameplay - B (Only repetitive if you don't do combos on the plot important enemies. There is a lot of impact with the Supers, but you do have to grind in order to start One Punch styling on enemies. Controls feel good, Camera never fights, but the boss battle armor can get annoying if you aren't learning air combo tech.)Story - EH (Watch/Read One Piece, this game doesn't flesh out all the characters)Music - SSS (I highly enjoyed the remix of the returning OST in this game series.)Graphics - Anime +BOTTOM LINEIf you are already a fan of One Piece, and enjoy the Warrior-style gameplay... then I recommend giving this installment a try. I still recommend 3 as the starting point of the Pirate Wars series, since 1 and 2 were just full-priced Betas back in the day. For a PROPER One Piece game experience, I still want a game where you sail around and can fully explore islands - needs more inspiration from Black Flag and the Caribbean in KH3, or even P5S!

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play this game once I found out it'd be coming out this year.Gameplay and fighting is way smoother than PW3 was. Animations and characters are done very well.But some things bug me a lot:- AI allied NPC's seem to love kicking your target away whenever you try launching a skill on it.- A lot of content / Arc's have been skipped, such as ALL Arcs before Alabasta, All Arcs after Alabasta up to Water 7, Thriller Bark, Amazon Lilly, Impel Down, Fish-Man Island, Punk Hazard, Zou, Levely- The Wano Kuni Arc is some filler-like stupid fan-made looking crap and not actual manga/anime based- Lots of Characters are not playable, although they're in the game; - have animations & skills but only work as "Support Units" (hopefully added later into the game)- Playable characters are not as many as I hoped, I assume there will be more, but as (overpriced) DLC's- Deluxe Edition Content is nowhere near to be called worth it (do not waste your money for it)- Character Upgrade System is not very good, you'll have to farm lots of the same missions in order to progress your favorite characters. Spare Coins are converted into Berry, but you cannot buy coins with the loads of Berry you obtain.- Just like in every PW Game, the characters have insanely OP ones and really garbage characters. At least 50% of the playable characters are below average and nowhere close to be useful/fun.Apart from that, the game is very fun, and I'm kind of addicted to it. If you can live with the negative stuff I listed above, the game will offer you lots of fun.I will keep on updating this review if the game changes or balancing/updates happen.Edit: After about 30 hours, you have seen the whole Game, trust me. I spend more time listening the characters in the scripted talking with each other, than fighting. After doing the whole story on S Rank & S Rank on ALL Missions on ALL the 3 Logs (East Blue, Grandline & New World) + EVERY crew you can currently obtain to crew level 5, then you're about to end your life. The game gets stretched for more wasted time in every other mission. I usually spend about 1–2 minutes waiting for the characters to finally finish their chitchat to get my mission completed and get the next one...Edit 2: After over 6 months, the game has not received a single patch or content update. A solid cash grab in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Pirate warriors four is a great step up from pirate warriors 3 with completely overhauled graphics as it is designed for the ps4 and new voicelines. The game hosts a wide range of new and returning characters and goes more into depth within the covered story arcs. The game implements the ability to swap special attacks, and skills as well as four types of character, Power, Speed, Sky and Technique. Power is strong, speed is really fast, sky forces you into the air and boosts air attacks and Technique requires setup for "powerful blows". Sadly the game has removed characters such as; Perona, Moria, Kuma, Caesar, Magellan, etc. and locked garp behind a DLC. The game is also lacking in costumes after the extreme number that a 100% completion will get you in OPPW3, this also made bandai decide it was somehow a good idea to remove pre-ts Nami, Chopper, Robin, Franky and Brook, Not just their movesets but the costumes as well!!! The DLC is quite expensive however it offers a new level cap from 18 to 30. Way more more skills, 3 special modes, and 18 new characters as well as some costumes. The game only covers the arc's of Alabasta, Water 7/Enies Lobby, Sabaody/Marineford, Dressrosa, Whole cake and a very bad game original wano. Sadly this cuts the east blue, skypiea, thriller bark and fishman island content from OPPW3 however has a very good PC port unlike the last. If your on a budget get OPPW3 if you can afford the latest one piece musou experience i believe OPPW4 is worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want to have a dopamine rush, smash buttons wildly. do funny numbers to thousands of npcs and juggle an innocent marine as a 30ft Whitebeard. There's no other better game. It looks good, it plays good, the combat is surprising varied for how easy and for how many characters there are. There's enough progression that lasts long enough to give you something tangible to go for.The biggest issue I have is the map design. It is so dumbfounding how they designed most of the maps. Most objectives don't have markers, you have to use your mini map. When you have hundreds of guys to fight, particle effects everywhere covering up a mini map that is already chalk full little icons it can be frustrating trying to figure out where to go. It doesn't show you different levels it just highlights what level your on. I don't need to see which level I'm on I need to find the stair case that takes me to that different level. Being such a fast paced game where their are literal thousands of enemies spawning every second you'd think they want you quickly go between objectives and keep up a combo streak. No they don't. That put objectives on complete opposite sides of maps they design it in such a way where you to go around everything to get to it. You can't jump over environments, invisible walls block pretty much every thing. If an objective is 5m away but there's a railing in the way, you can't just jump over it you have to walk all the way around the map to go the one spot the devs want you to go. For how fast paced the game is it not uncommon to go minutes of game play in total of you just walking around with nothing to do. It is also not uncommon for this hack and slash game to have levels go on for 15/20 minutes which can drag on. There is also a lot of small technical issues. The menus are just god awful to navigate. Do you have a mouse and keyboard? Well good luck, there is no mouse support in the menus, you have arrow key to every tab. You can't just click things like a normal game. The lock on is awful it's so slow it actually handicaps you, the camera can't keep up with how quickly you can juggle enemies and throw them across maps so your stuck in a situation where you can't see in front of you but you also can't move the camera. Anytime you use can attack that has a long wind up you can't aim it anywhere, you're stuck in direction you aimed it before. With hundreds of effects, sounds, thousands of npcs, text on screen, it is very easy to miss something and you can't correct your mistake. One could cancel the animation but that just means you dropped your combo and wasted your skill. Combos timers still decay during wind ups and in animations which is a questionable choice.

_childDocuments_.review: "A downgrade from One Piece Pirate Warriors 3"- Maps are bigger but enemies are scattered (not concentrated as it should be in a mosou game).- There are more characters but they are extremely unbalanced. Some are awesome to play with, some are boring as fk because they were made in a rush. Some animations are pretty good, others are bugged, and others are annoying to use because they don't behave as they should.- They removed secondary objectives in story mode, which they used to reward unique things when you completed them (also gave the game more depth and content).- They removed the level system, so you can't level up your characters any more.- The previous game (one piece pirate warriors 3) had a lot of extra content besides story mode, this one doesn't, it has a mode that can be completed in 10-20 hours and that's it. 10 hours story mode, 20 hours secondary mode.- They removed the "poster" system, in which you had to complete certain objectives with each character in the rooster, which then encouraged you to play with other characters.- They removed the Kizuna system, which allowed you to perform "final" attacks alongside your NPC companions.A lazy version of One Piece Pirate Warriors 3. That's all this is, really.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, wanted to wait for platinum, but that's gonna take some grinding, so here's a quick review.It's pretty much the same old formula and it works here, too. There are quite a few changes to the core gameplay, but they all pretty much work together well and soon you'll be jumping, transforming and dabbling with different supers all over the place.Supers are so much better in this one, since you just go from 1 to 4 supers, that you can also swap around, if you like a different kind of super more.The roster is big, quickly unlocked and has lotsa different characters, that all play at least somewhat differently. Seeing the super clear the screen or wipe like 3 commanders is still immensely satisfying.The "leveling" system is weird at first and pretty intuitive after looking at it a bit. You get one general "tree" for passive skills, that affects all characters. Then you get 2 separate trees for each character, the second one being unlocked after working with that char for a bit, either by having them exist in quests or just by playing them. Just make sure you actually switch over to the character sheet in the first few hours, because that's where you unlock actual combos and supers, which makes fights a lot easier (and more fun).One negative regarding the leveling is that it's not quite transparent and needlessly complicated menuing. First off, it seems to be built around slow progression. There's no way to dump your resources and just buy all the upgrades in one node. You have to go to the node, click upgrade, navigate to "yes" in the pop-up, confirm and then you need to do the same thing again for all skill points.And the later you get in the game, the more frustrating this gets, with you suddenly having WAY more resources and maybe wanting to switch to a different character, but then spending 5 minutes in the menu constantly pressing the same buttons.You also can't easily check which quests you get coins from (that are shown in your tree). There's no "complete xyz to unlock" or anything. And then you also get the hidden nodes, that literally force you to guess what the ability is and how to unlock it. The "coin unlock guide" doesn't give you much relevant info. It's also really badly placed, because you'd basically need to write down the coin you wanna check, then completely go out of the character select, exit mission select, go to the main menu, select gallery, select the coin guide, flick through every coin and compare to the coin you wrote down.Sounds long and complicated? Yeah, try doing that like 10 times for different skills and you quickly kinda stop caring. I'm currently looking for a coin that unlocks, what I presume to be a super for Whitebeard and it's just "oh is it this quest? No? Cool, time to waste another 5 minutes".It's forced stretching of gameplay and it's too obvious and annoying to be interesting. You wanna do the treasure log with your favorite character and all their cool stuff? Ok, screw you, try guessing which of the hardest quests will get you that move you maybe want and grind for it.And that brings us to difficulty. I played on normal, but there's a hard option right from the start and an "ultra hard" option that unlocks after the story. I found the difficulty to be quite ok. It's surprisingly much harder than the previous OP musou, but that doesn't mean it's difficult per se. It's just a little bit tougher than "mash buttons = win". You'll actually need to dodge some of the stronger attacks later on and be on top of your leveling. S rank can be a bit tough to achieve on your first run through the log, considering some of the objectives have you guess what's the fastest way to complete. It's often the time that was the issue for me; kills are usually easier to get, but vary wildly from 1k to 2.5k or more.What can also kill your S ranks, are the weirdly useless sub-missions. Do not go for any submissions. All you get for completing them is a tiny bit of money at the end and very rarely a small bonus to aid you on the battlefield (like preventing reinforcements). Sub-missions will usually get you around 1/10th of the berry prize at the end, while attaining S rank will literally get you double the reward money.And as ok as the difficulty is, the "new world" logs are gonna pretty much kill you, even if your character is maxed, in around 5-6 hits, depending on the enemy. You also get swarmed with tons of named characters that can all interrupt you, meaning you sometimes can't even get away, especially if you locked on and are now flying in a circle on accident. Buuut, if you now equip a self-buff and the "heal while self-buffed" skill, you suddenly have no issue with dying anymore, because the heal is so substantial.Last point, if you like that stuff: TrophiesThey are some of the easiest trophies to get in any game I've ever played. You will get more than half just from playing story stuff, more than 3/4 if you go for a bit of grinding and I'm 2 away from full trophies; literally just need to amass money now.That's in part due to the fact that there are no trophies for different difficulty levels. There's no trophy for completely s-ranking the story (which I stupidly didn't look up) and also no trophy for completely s-ranking the treasure log or maxing out all characters, maxing out the trees of one character, even.Tl;dr: It's an improvement of OPW3, controller issues seem mostly resolved (although my game switches my keyboard input to a different layout every time) and it's still the good old "get big numbers; do the cool move" gameplay that you play dynasty warrior games for.If you like this kinda gameplay and OP, this is a pretty neat game to pick up. If not, the gameplay's gonna feel a little shallow and you'll wonder who different characters are and why they're capable of weird stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Musou title!It might take a little while to get used to the new, fast and unapologetic (sometimes confusing) gameplay if you're immediately coming after playing Pirate Warriors 3, but once you do, you'll really appreciate the changes.What I like about this, is that it adds a different twist to the almost perfect Pirate Warriors 3 formula, so both 3 and 4 are highly valued for different things.If I had to put it simply, I would rank them like this:- Warriors 3: Slower gameplay and flashy team moves. - Warriors 4: Improved graphics, faster gameplay, no special team moves but more exciting, breakable buildings and bigger scale (giant enemies).All in all, this is an excellent game, maybe the best One Piece game so far.Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Pirate Warriors 3 before this one you'll constantly be aware of how much stuff is missing. Most notably are the majority of story arcs both pre and post timeskip (and even in the ones that are included, some plot points are skipped over or changed slightly to help the musou gameplay fit in, so I wouldn't recommend this to someone wanting to catch up to the series with this), but also specific characters (most of the strawhat crew pre-timeskip are unplayable, and their respective costumes aren't available either), and extra content (the gallery shop and Dream Log from 3 have both been removed, with the latter replaced with specific 'what if?' style battles instead). Reading this, you may wonder why I'm recommending it.The fact is, Omega Force seem to have focused on the depth of what's in the game rather than a wide spread of things to do. Combat is much more developed than in 3, and most characters really feel like a unique, authentic experience to play as. The upgrade tree is now split up into 3 parts, with the first conferring stat upgrades to all of the characters rather than just one specifically, meaning you don't have to grind to enjoy playing as a character you just spent hours trying to unlock. It isn't an extravagant feast of content, but what is here is a lot of fun.Side note, the background music in this one is honestly really good! I don't have the anime music DLC but with songs like this I don't think it's really needed at all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an action game developed by Omega Force and published by Bandai Namco, based on Eiichiro Oda's popular manga and anime *One Piece*. The game belongs to the "musou" (hack and slash) genre, where players face hordes of enemies and defeat powerful bosses in large-scale battles. It is the fourth installment in the *Pirate Warriors* series, which combines the *One Piece* universe with the gameplay style typical of *Dynasty Warriors* games.GameplayThe gameplay  focuses heavily on fast-paced action. Players can choose from over 40 playable characters, each with unique abilities and different fighting styles. Each character can perform special attacks and devastating moves to take down hundreds of enemies at once. The game introduces some new features compared to previous entries, such as "air combos," which allow for spectacular aerial combos, increasing the fluidity and variety of combat.The mission structure follows the main story arcs of *One Piece*, up to the Wano arc, including some original episodes not found in the manga. The story is presented through animated cutscenes and dialogues between characters, retracing the key moments of the series. However, some parts of the story have been shortened or altered, which may not satisfy fans looking for a faithful reproduction of the original work.Graphics and SoundThe graphics have improved compared to previous titles, with more detailed environments and refined character models. The visual effects of special abilities and attacks are spectacular and effectively convey the power of the protagonists. However, there are still some moments where the quality of the textures and animations is less polished, especially in secondary characters and common enemies.The sound design is solid, with energetic music that complements the action well and the original voices of the Japanese anime voice actors, which help create an authentic atmosphere. The sound effects of attacks and explosions are also well-executed, adding impact to the battles.Game ModesIn addition to the story mode, the game offers a "Free Log" mode, where players can replay missions with any available character, and the "Treasure Log" mode, which features extra missions and additional challenges with increasing difficulty. The multiplayer mode allows for cooperative play both locally and online, enhancing the gameplay's longevity and variety.Strengths1. **Large character roster**: With over 40 playable characters, each with distinct fighting styles, there is plenty of variety for players.2. **Spectacular battles**: Combos and special attacks are visually engaging and capture the essence of the *One Piece* universe.3. **Multiplayer mode**: The ability to play cooperatively, both online and offline, adds a social element that enriches the experience.Weaknesses1. **Repetitiveness typical of musou games**: Despite the new mechanics, battles can become monotonous after many hours of gameplay, with objectives often being similar.2. **Abbreviated storytelling**: Some important story arcs have been condensed, and the complexity of the original story is not always fully represented.3. **Technical issues**: There are occasional frame rate drops and some graphical limitations in the environments and enemy models.Conclusion"One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4" is a game that manages to entertain and satisfy fans of the series thanks to its faithful representation of the characters and the ability to relive iconic story arcs. Although the repetitiveness of the gameplay and some narrative simplifications may limit its appeal, the game is a good example of adapting an anime into a musou-style action title. It is recommended especially for *One Piece* enthusiasts and those looking for a fast-paced, spectacular combat experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, I'd be happy to provide a review for One Piece Pirate Warriors 4.Released in March 2020 for multiple platforms, including PS4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is the fourth entry in the One Piece Pirate Warriors series. The game is a hack-and-slash action game that follows the story of the popular anime and manga, One Piece.One of the standout features of One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is the vast roster of playable characters. The game features over 40 characters from the One Piece universe, each with their own unique move set and abilities. Fans of the series will enjoy being able to play as their favorite characters.The gameplay in One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is fast-paced and exciting. Players control various characters from the One Piece universe and fight their way through hordes of enemies. The combat is easy to pick up and play, with simple combos and special moves that can be executed with ease.The game's story mode follows the events of the anime and manga, allowing players to experience the main story arcs of the series in a condensed format. The game also includes a variety of side missions and challenges, giving players plenty of content to keep them entertained.The graphics and visual effects in One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 are also noteworthy. The game features vibrant, cartoonish graphics that capture the look and feel of the anime. The animations are smooth and fluid, and the game is filled with over-the-top special effects that add to the spectacle of combat.Overall, One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is a fun and enjoyable game that fans of the One Piece series will appreciate. The vast roster of playable characters, fast-paced combat, and vibrant graphics make it a worthy addition to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Went in knowing absolutely nothing about one piece apart from that it was bonkers. This was confirmed, but the game also went to the effort to plot out the events of the manga fairly well and didnt leave me floundering.Gameplay wise, as a someone who has played the vast majority of warriors games, this is a solid entry with familiar mechanics mixed with some unique and thematic ones. Giant characters and hugely destructible environments abound, as well as every character feeling unique in play style and move set, with an attribute and skill tree system for all characters as well as passives that once unlocked can be used by all characters.The art style is that of an anime, so lends itself to a timeless aspect that will likely look good 20 to 30 years from now still. My own pc I played on is an old man in terms of hardware, running a 1080TI and very VERY rarely did I have any noticable frame drops, the few noticable occasions being when several giant enemies were attacking me at once alongside other powers and abilities being used. This however only occurs late game in both the story and the treasure mode, so I wouldnt count it as much of a big deal. Solidly optimised.In terms of things that struck me as irksome, some people may find it tedious to grind out currency or other items needed to unlock skill tree progression, whilst others may be disappointed that certain characters arent as powerful as portrayed in the show? But that is the most that I can think of. For a Warriors game enjoyer, I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and entertaining game. Played a lot of musou game over multiple consoles, this one easily on top 3.Below are the pros and cons for this game, in comparison with previous game, Pirate Warriors 3.Pros:- Better graphics.- Better gameplay.- More playable characters. Previous game has 37, this one 43 + 9 from DLC.- Characters are more diversed, gameplay wise. The addition of "character type", "character size", and "airborne attack" really change the feels and perspective of a musou game.- Each maps are more unique. No more "square area" scattered all over the map.- Customizable list of special moves.Cons:- The game includes new arc and expands arc from previous title, but they also remove some arcs, like Skypiea and Thriller Bark.- Seven of playable characters were cut (Enel, Moria, Perona, Kuma, Garp, Caesar, and Magellan). They haven't however reveal the 9 characters for DLC. So, some of them might return as additional paid content.- Pre-Time Skip of Nami, Chopper, Brook, Robin, and Franky also not playable. But this one is not that big of a deal since the post-TS version of characters that have playable pre-TS easily overshadow their pre-TS version.- No more Dream Log. While I don't like Dream Log from previous game, they can do something to improve the mode instead of replacing it with a new mode that's basically just a long list of missions.Overall, I'll give this game 8.5/10.

But if you don't get any DLC, you can wait until you unlock Luffy (with fourth gear) Whitebeard or Ichiji-- they are fairly powerful. - I totally recommend anybody to play this game on Hard difficulty. Normal is way too easy. The boss is literally standing in front of you, walking around waiting for your attacks if you play on Normal. - Playing with a controller is highly recommended, seriously, playing on a keyboard will give you carpal tunnel. - The One Piece is real.

_childDocuments_.review: Humble Pre-orderrough issues at launch related to controller issues and the trashy steam community declarig that anyone with said issues was idiot did not help.. Issues since have been resolved, though not sure why. Game sometimes crashes, but this appears to be related to a driver update for AMD that causes problems with dual monitors. Very impressed with actual game play now that i've gotten some time to put into it. The way the story is approached is actually excellent. Still don't think the game has full controller support (it loads "official config" when launching, requiring a config isn't full controller support. Not sure why companies don't understand this and it needs to be changed to "partial controller" support so people know what they are getting into. However, despite how I feel about this, it's no longer as much of a gamebreaker as it was at launch and as far as i'm concerned the game runs great, looks great and plays great. There are some minor changes to the combat system which at first were hard to get used to and seemed a bit off. I miss Kizuna drive, and don't feel these static ai partners are the same.  some creative changes made during pw3 have been carried over (bellamy always in his new world appearence in older cutscenes,  absence of most cp9 members ) however this one takes the time to flush out the story. Instead of just attempting to tell everything, giving one mission for each story arc/saga, it focuses on the more popular ones (alabasta, enies lobby, marineford, new world, whole cake island, wano). While this means no visiting sky island and no early east blue adventures, these parts of the story are told through nice cutscenes. It's possible they may add more missions for story mode in dlc. Characters no longer have levels. There is still a crew level, but this is no longer tied to skills and the gallery. Instead you unlock things (still with coins, which seem easier to acquire for rarer ones) on the growth map. Each character has a specific growth map, with a crew growth map for everyone and some other crew map I haven't unlocked yet. I think this may be tied to the treasure log. Treasure log replaces dream log in this iteration, but it's basically the same thing. They got rid of the 2.5d map (fortunately, this was annoying to navigate in pw3) and instead missions are selected via a menu. When you complete key missions you unlock more missions in that category. There are 3 logs in treasure log each representing a major story arc or central location. Cutscenes are mostly rendered in FMV, though there are still image cutscenes still. Characters no longer remain motionless during cutscenes, or when using powers. This is beneficial as they will often walk into range as you trigger a special or as a cutscene plays and it makes the game feel seemless. Much more care was taken to translating the game. Phrases such as "okama" now are in the game instead of being censored, the sexuality of some of the characters is also more apparent versus it's heavily censored predecssor. Kenpou is no longer translated as "karate". Zolo actually uses his different sword styles instead of always being depicted using itoryou. some of the more emotional scense (ussopp leaving the crew , robin being rescued) play out a bit differently. Felt that ussopp v luffy was  a bit better played in pw3, but robin was done way better in this version.All that said, it's a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is an musou game through and through, letting you satisfyingly steamroll hundreds of thousands of enemies single handedly as powerful hero (or villain) characters. But it comes with most of the typical baggage that goes along with that distinction, it’s not the prettiest looking game in the world, there are lots of reused assets from prior games, and outside of a few select boss fights, its hoards of baddies offer very little resistance.It has the unusual honor of being both one of the best anime-based games and best Warriors games I've ever played. It has its flaws, including the tiresome return of Giant foes and the usual Warriors repetitiveness, but it's a great example of how to reinvigorate something that seems like a tired formula. If you're a One Piece fan or a fan of the Warriors franchise, PW4 is absolutely worth a go. Once you've taken a bite of gum-gum, you won't be able to resist more.

But like most, this game also has its light and dark sides.But first let me give you a rough overview.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~===[]=== ☐ Kids☑ Everyone☑☑  Anime Lovers☑  Casual players☐ Pro players===[]=== ☐ Potato☐ Really bad☐ Bad☐ OK☑ Good ☐ Beautiful ☐ Masterpiece===[]=== ☐ Full price☑ Wait for sale☐ Average☐ Refund it if you can☐ Don't do it===[]=== ☐ 90' PC☐ Minimum☐ Medium ☑ Fast☐ High end ☐ NASA computer===[]=== ☐ You just need 2 arms ☑ Ez☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master ☐ Hard (first few hours)☐ Dark Souls===[]=== ☐ Really short ( 0 - 2 hours)☐ Short ( 2 - 8 hours)☐ Few hours ( 8 - 12 hours)☑ Long ( 12+ hours)☐ Endless===[] === ☐ It doesn't have☐ Still better than Twilight☑ Average☐ Good☐ Fantastic===[]=== ☐ Game itself is one big BUG☐ Bugs destroying the game☐ Lot of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☑ Haven't seen one===[]=== ☑ Multiplayer☑ Couch-Coop☑ Singleplayer8,5/10 Even though i am a huge fan of One Piece, there are still one or two problems. For example, you can fight against some opponents that you are not allowed to play yourself. Like Garp, Pazifista, Sentomaru, Mr.1, Mr.2, Mr.3, Corby, Sengoku, Vista, Jozu, Kuma, Rayleigh, Diamante, Pica, Bellamy, Burgess, Perospero, Jack and probably many more. Which means these polygons and attack's are already present for these characters but you are not allowed to play them yourself, which i find pretty silly.But what i find pretty positive is the quick combat system. I have to admitthat i am a big Dynasty fan and that i already have gained some experience, but i only played the first title of Pirate Warriors. For me it was much to slow paced and sluggisch. Fortunately however, they learned from it. Pirate Warriors 4 is much faster and literally puts you in some kind of trance. You always want to test the next character and see what he/she can do cause the combat system is so quick and enjoyable. Most of my missions were 10-12 minutes long but they always seems like 3-4 minutes for me. In conclusion, i can say that i really like One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4, which you can see from my current 30 hours of game time. But i think a total of 52 characters is way to less. Just imagine that you fight against way over 10 characters more that are already in the game. But to ignore characters that are already in Pirate Warriors games before the fourth? Like Perona, Enel, Kuma, Garp, Magellan, Gekko Moria and many more? Its just a shame...But as negativ as my "judgement" may sounds, i loved to play the game for many hours without even notice the time flew by me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is so far the best addition to the Pirate Warriors series, I've played it almost non-stop since it's release. If you're a fan of the IP and any of the previous Pirate Warriors games you should get it. But don't go in it expecting too much, it's fun it really is, but there's of room for improvement. I'm going to list some of my peeves,If you share my mindset of enjoying investing time and thought in learning the ins and outs of a game, you might get a bit frustrated with this one. Alot of the aspects regarding gameplay go unexplained, there's basically no data available to you as a player, for example something simple as a characters damage output.There's no interaction between haki and devil fruit powers, sometimes an enemy character might completely ignore the damage from a special attack, and you're left not knowing why. Was my placement bad? Did the enemy move out of range? Does the particular attack not effect characters in a Logia form?Some characters have unique attack modifications that affect enemies hit by you or that are within a certain range in a different way depending on the characters. What does these attack modifications actually do? Well, the game doesn't tell you. You can sometimes guess what they do, but in most cases, you can't or at least i can't.The matchmaking system is just a mess, you can either host a game yourself (recruit) or join another. Joining another players game is a chore... There's no list showing you players that are recruiting, you are given a menu where you can specify 1 of 3 Logs, which character you are going to play and a specific Log mission or just "any". The latter is your only choice basically, even then most of the time you get the result "Unable to find a session". Your first try you receive this message instantly, the second time, and every time there's suddenly a delay before you receive the same message again. If you manage to find a host session, you'll find at max 3 different sessions (on a good day), and you better join quickly before you lose that spot. Oh and if you're struggling on a mission in the Story Log, yes i want join you and give you a helping hand, but i'll never be able to find your game.Long story short, it's a fun and visually pleasing game, it has the potential to become a great game with the right attention from the developers and i really hope it gets that much needed attention. Especially with the revenue they receive from the dlc character pass.

The leveling up system/power system is really cool, all characters share a map where everyone gets upgrades but if you want to upgrade a character to there full potential and unlock more moves you can put points into a specific character map which only boosts that character.In this game there are skills/special buffs where you can only have a select amount of them so its interesting to think of what you'll need for each character.There are 4 character types( I think) Power, Runner/Flying, Defense and Technique. Each character type has different pros and cons. Power characters tend to do more damage and runners are really fast.Transformations:There are 3 transformations in the game for luffy.Gears 2, 4 bounceman, 4 snakemanGear 2 is only available for pre timeskip because after that gear 2 moves are incorporated into normal fighting.Gear 3 is only an attack but there are many gear 3 attacks. These attacks do more damage but they take a long time to charge up. Pre timeskip luffy also shrinks after using this attack but this effect is removed after timeskip.Bounce man and snake man both change Luffy's class to runner.IMPORTANT:Some really annoying things about this game are that they skip short or unimportant arcs.but they do have cut scenes explaining the blanks.They skip:The whole east blueSkypieaThriller barkFishman islandpunk hazardZouThis game is still really really goodoverall its a 7/10 game for a non one piece fanbut a 9/10 for any one piece fan

The controls are very simple, allowing you to unleash powerful combos mainly through button mashing against numerous foes.Furthermore, the game includes some RPG elements, such as a leveling system and skill trees, allowing you to make these powerful characters even stronger.On a side note, the icons for the achievements look very poorly made.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my favorite thing about PW4 is that it doesn't eliminate PW3 and make it a dead game in your library. Now of course this will vary from person to person and what they enjoy about these games as a whole, but personally I love to see what different aspects and systems a musou focuses on and how they're implemented.PW4 is different enough from PW3 that it felt like a fresh experience, even when the story was retreading old waters. Personally I was a fan of the focus on later stages of the story, as these games tend to draw in a particular crowd that probably doesn't need to fight Don Kreig for the 20th year in a row.The Gameplay is a whole different beast from PW3. The trait button for characters is gone, those moves instead being placed into their kit in a more streamlined fashion. There's a high emphasis on expanding aerial combat, most likely due to the existence of giant type enemies and bosses. This doesn't detract from the flow of combat however, and the high speed of the Pirate Warriors games is still there, if a bit gimped by a stamina meter stopping you from dash cancelling 100 times in a row.Overall, its a great experience. The optional grind is still there as always, though lacking a bit in character as optional missions become a list rather than islands you explore between. Hopefully updates to the game will bring with them more character and life, but even as it is now the game rests on equal footing with its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it so far, the game handles itself fairly well on the Steam Deck. I might have to go through settings to troubleshoot the controls, because using an external keyboard with my deck seems to make whatever character I'm playing as run in whatever direction they're facing for no obvious reason, making it impossible to navigate stages properly. I enjoy the graphics, but sometimes the cutscenes won't load until part way through them, showing a TV off-air type screen until it loads, even as the subtitles show up. The combat is fluid and performs well, and the steam deck controls handle well.This isn't wildly different from the handful of other musou games I've played so far, but the characters and attacks feel different enough from each other to keep things interesting. It is definitely worth getting, though I'd personally wait for a sale.If you're here, you're probably also a One Piece fan, and if that's the case you know enough to fill in the little gaps in the story, so you'll enjoy this-- that said if you haven't read/watched it, I wouldn't recommend this as an introduction to the narrative. This game does the best it can at condensing entire arcs to a few levels, but it inevitably has to cut parts for time. Some plot points are left as 1-2 sentence summaries, which is fine for someone who understands what's going on before but could be confusing to someone who's completely new. For example one of the more emotional parts of Water 7 (arc, not saga for existing fans, it's the duel and what leads up to it) definitely doesn't have the gravity it does in the full story. Considering it would take more than three weeks straight to watch the anime, it's not really possible for a game to go into that much depth, especially at the steal of the price it costs on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: OP is available in many formats: the open world World Seeker, the turn based Odyssey, even the adventure style of Unlimited World, but I keep coming back to Pirate Warriors.  I first played Pirate Warriors 3, which ran up to Dressrosa, had a killer jazz-fusion soundtrack, and preferred 3 over 4 for a long time.  But then content kept coming out for Pirate Warriors 4 long after release: more characters, the treasure mode that added smaller episodes, and the story arc DLC's with Roger and Koby.  I highly recommend Pirate Warriors 3 for those that want to dive deep into the events that took place prior to the events in The New World, but damn if Pirate Warriors 4 didn't solidify for me just how at home One Piece feels in a Warriors style game.  I can only hope that one day, Koei Tecmo sees the value of capturing the entire story of one piece in one game.

_childDocuments_.review: So let's see, I'm a big fan of the Pirate warriors games, now I hold pirate warriors 3 up on a pedestal as the greatest warriors style game out there, nice amount of characters, they were balanced, the levels were also balanced for K.O and time and the like, it played well, it was just all around great but what about 4 dood?So 4 is super fun and has some great ideas, sadly those ideas in a weird way ended up being a step backwards, especially for the hardest stuff, okay so for starters the balance has been broken once again, some characters are just too good to use while others not so much, even with the new special attack system where you can press R1 and one of the space buttons for a special attack there are some moves that are just poor, especially with how the new system works for battle, you see all "enemies" have super armour now, it can be broken but until it does they are free to interrupt your attacks at their leisure, this becomes a major issue on harder fights in the treasure log and can even be a hassle normally as the damage at times even when decently levelled up is rather high and health drops are extremely low, this can be mitigated...at the cost of attack as there are skills that allow you to heal over time that you can equip but they take two whole slots, it's a give and take situation where your time score if that's important to you is going to suffer, the old system had some invulnerability going on for characters who powered up but that was at least temporary and only happened once, here it can happen multiple times not only allowing for them to recover their meter but gaining an insane defence boost making for some fights to be more of a chore than fun dood.next is power up types, there are more than a few which are honestly poor, so here we'll cover the four base types, Power, speed, Sky and purple...because I can't remember what it was actually called XD still power, speed and purple are great, they all have their perks, boosted speed, seemingly a damage boost too but sky? sky is a cool concept but suffers because it makes it harder to hit...well anyone, especially boss types, it even has the flaw of the fact that it takes you a while to fall because you can be pretty high up, it also took away from Sanji's original fighting style that was pretty awesome in 3 that allowed you to basically jump to the opponents you hit with an R2 I believe it was near instantly and then there are forms, Luffy get's a certain power up form that you see on the very first stage you'll play for reasons and it's a massive degrade, besides the fact it's sky it doesn't get the speed boost and if there is a damage boost it's hampered by the attacks being frankly poor dood.The game world is vast, the levels are nice and long and generally varied and interesting, certainly fun to play in, the soundtrack has some classics from older games, some music from the anime and some new tracks of it's own which are all real, it's fun to play in but it also makes some maps hard to read and traverse dood.So what do I think? I think it's a stellar game even if it isn't as good as it's predecessor, it has it's annoyances but nothing bad enough that you will regret buying the game by any means, rank doesn't really matter as far as I know either outside of showing off to...I guess your friends IRL? so you can feel free to take your time playing how you want really, the fighting styles are all varied and interesting as is typical of one piece and it's just a fun time, thanks for reading and if you buy it I hope you enjoy dood ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: After playing a decent amount, I actually really enjoy this game. All of the characters are pretty faithful to the actual story, as well as having a lot of different environments and unlockable moves. The game is pretty grindy, so it can get really easy to burnout, which is what happened to me. But I can't deny that for the most part it's really fun to just go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with some of the more broken/destructive characters. Big Mom and Kaido actually feel like complete powerhouses, without being so broken that it starts to become boring and braindead to play them. Although I wish some characters were a lot better like Usopp and Chopper. Usopp is my favorite Straw Hat in the story, but he is by far my least favorite character to play in this game due to how weak he is. Another negative that I have is that I wish that there was a lot more stuff that could've been added in. Because of the fact they put every single Vinsmoke brother in the game, I feel like they could've at least added in some other fan favorites, with some of them already being in the game as different AI. I will have a list of all the stuff I wish was in the game, but overall I think this is a great game for both One Piece fans as well as Dyansty Warriors fans, due to the fact that anime powers can make everything feel way more fun and chaotic. Stuff I wish that were playable in the game:-Bon Clay-Rayleigh-Moria-Magellan-Nekomushi and Dog Viper-Yamato-Kuma -Garp-Perona-Enel-Caesar Clown-Bellamy-Hody Jones-Literally any costumes for Chopper, Robin, Franky, Brook (Seriously where are they?)-Costumes and Characters from Pirate Warriors 3

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, its a much better improvement compared to Pirate Warriors 3. Way more comboes, and a easy flashy super move you can do with the crazy combo attacks is very fun overall! Its only fun like this, but sadly you have to grind individually for each character in order to unlock all their combos and moves, which is ridiculous cause of how long the grind is. But if you manage to level them all up, and play them normally, it becomes a really fun game to pull out whenever I wanna kill an hour or 2 for time. Graphics are an improvement, and has quite a bit of options to tweak to compared to pirate warriros 3. And whats even better, the port of this game is good! Your able to actually play the episodes and not having to worry about crashing or being randomly kicked out. The only thing I didn't like was that if u left the game for any reason, you cant save and go right back into action like PW 3 had (tho it wasnt auto save, so i had to manually save to do this) but still better then not being able to save at all. If u play an episode, better hope to god u can finish it before you get called up and have to leave the game. Not only is the grind and progression really slow, the only way to lvl up your characters is to actually load up a game, I found this to be pretty annoying. Much less episodes compared to PW3, PW3 covers mostly all the arcs, and is pretty accurate. PW4 decides to skip some arcs which is sad cuz skypiea was one of my underated favorite arcs, but sad to see its not in the game. Choosing to start at alabasta arc instead of replaying the episodes to get your crew was a smart decision (every arc before alabasta besides arlong was pretty boring im not gonna try to cap) IN conclusion, its a good game. one of the few games where instead of unistalling after finishing the story, I wanna complete the treasure logs in order to unlock the rest of the characters. (cant wait to see how shanks, and black beard plays.) The only other con I would say about this game is some characters are pretty boring to play. Mostly the Technique fighters like robin, and kuzan who by the way u would expect to have cool moves and combos, but his attacks r so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sloww! Speed, power, and sky are the only actual fun characters.

Also, you get to hear the silly otomat laughs of the pirates in their classic Japanese, what's not to like there?Get the game on sale if fictional pirates that stretch or set fire to things or literally sunder reality by willing it sounds a bit over the top, but this is def a great game. _childDocuments_.review: Verdict: A pretty good musou game that fixed the majority of my issues with Pirate Warriors 3. Recommended for any fan of OP or Dynasty Warriors. +Steam achievements (40, a playthrough of the campaign and the majority of the dream log is enough)43 characters in base game + 9 in DLCs5 Story arcs (Alabasta to Whole Cake Island) + non-canon version of Land of Wano Arc 35 missions The game doesn't force you to replay the campaign 3-5 times this timeAbility to play coop (2 in campaign, 4 special missions in treasure log)4 new multiplayer modes - Giant Boss Battle, Total Bounty Battle, Timed Defense Battle, and Territory Battle Free log to play the finished campaign missions as anyone you wish A treasure log is a great end-game activity (random maps, enemies and allies, 103 missions in total)Quite a lot of abilities for every characterGallery where you can see encyclopedia, glossary, cinematics, music, coin and crew guides5 save slots Pretty solid options menu - basically everything you may want 4 different colourblind supports I haven't encountered any bugs and the game never crashed on me -No steam trading cards (they were in PW3, so no clue why they are missing here)3 out of 9 DLC characters were already in the game which seems pretty shady (2 even had complete movement sets)There are quite a few unplayable characters that were usable in PW3 Levelling your characters is a lot and a lot of clicking on "select, move, confirm and repeat") Costumes are more often than not really underwhelming The highest difficulty is locked behind finishing the game once Difficulties are not explained at all Camera is still terrible, especially if you fight one of the giant bosses

_childDocuments_.review: So One Piece:Pirate Warriors 4 isn't the worst game ever, but it's not as good as its predecessor in a lot of ways. At its root it's still a Warriors title, which means you can have mindless fun bashing millions of enemies around, and in this series do it as popular one piece characters.That said, the game suffers from what feels like rushed dev time. There's not a lot of polish and there IS a lot of DLC. There are fewer playable characters, fewer costumes, the maps feel less varied, everything feels like a step down from OPPW3 and considering this game's price and the amount of DLC you're better off going back and just playing 3 instead.Most annoying, is that the story campaign is both not canon(because it came out before the end of the Wano arc of the manga), you also cannot do it completely co-op until you've beaten the campaign once.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game. Perfect for all One Piece fans who want to play as their favourite characters from the series. Aight lemme start with the positives: The story in general is honestly pretty decent it takes you through  parts in each arc of one piece from the east blue to the grand line (Alabasta --> Wano Country) are accompanied with great missions which reflect the story. The music slaps, every one of the tracks fits the theme at hand. The movesets and abilities are unique for each playable character. There is Co-op missions so playing with friends makes missions a lot more fun. So, now we move on to some negatives: For the games price i would recommend if you enjoy the One Piece story and its characters the game would be a perfect fit in your steam library but if you know nothing about the story and just looking for another musou game this accomplishes that too but i would recommend getting it on a steam sale either way. Second point, your favourite character could have a weak unreliable playstyle or moveset, most of the main characters in the game such as Luffy, Zoro and Sanji have great movesets which are fun when playing but people like Chopper, Franky, Urouge and surprisingly Crocodile i have found to have very gimmicky underpowering movesets. The camera when using gear 4 Luffy or really fast sky type characters can be faulty at times.All in all a great musou One Piece game I would rate it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a HUGE Dynasty Warriors fan, and HUGE One Piece fan, and I'm sad to say this game could've been way, way better. It doesn't feel like they put their heart and soul into this like they do for their Dynasty series,In Dynasty warriors, ALL weapons and playstyles can kick butt and be incredibly fun, flashy, unique. In Pirate Warriors it's not the same at all. You have the play as the big well-known fighters or go home, Chopper for instance has 0 effort put into his mechanics. Despite being THE transformation character of the show, he doesn't hold ANY OF HIS TRANSFORMATIONS and has NO UNIQUE MOVESETS based off his forms, but yet Luffy does. Why? Idfk, makes no sense.A LOT of characters suffer this, Usopp, Crocodile, many others suffer this lack of ambitious builds. And it's not just me not liking a playstyle, I loved ALL weapons in ALL dynasty warriors because they were all unique, and effective. Chopper is NOT effective AT ALL. I did my absolute best on 1 mission and it took 2 and a half hours. Then I went in it again with a character I didn't try yet, Frankie, and I beat it in 5 minutes. THAT'S ABSURD. What makes it worse, is these characters on back burner all mechanically work closely the same. They're slow, low damage, no arial potential, and only hit 1 small area once in a great while, and have slow combos. Another issue is awesome abilities have to be equipped and make you leave behind other abilities. This should be canned and instead introduce complex input systems so all characters can bring in all moves. This alone would make the trash characters more baerable.Now for online. Online is so badly done, there's a ton of Desync and it makes it that you might as well be playing alone because of this. And it's not flukes or a glitch, it's 100% constantly desynced intentionally. You will NOT fight the same enemy at the same time. Instead you should Parsec and splitscreen this, but that's lame that you have to do this.Another issue it lacks is lack of character specific campaigns. Dynasty Warriors let you pick any character, stick with them from their perspective, build up, get stronger, and help whatever cause, it was an RPG game. Pirate Warriors has none of this. I get its trying to be true to the story, but they could easily have another gamemode for this. It's a Video Game trying to be like Dynasty Warriors, so where are the golden, tried and true Dynasty Warrior mechanics? They could have AT LEAST a non-cannon alternate mode.I won't say don't try the game or avoid it, it can be fun with friends, and if your favorite characters are characters like Luffy and anyone who almost beat Luffy then you'll have a great time. But I still give a negative review for how little effort they put in so many loved characters. You either play Emporers, Warlords, or don't play at all because picking Chopper will mean you spend up to 4 hours on a short mission.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets worse and worse the more you realize how few features and content it has.While Pirate Warriors 3 was a great musou game with a coat of One Piece on it, Pirate Warriors 4 is a OP fandom jerk off with a mediocre musou game attached. The same OP fans that will celebrate not having lesser characters in the game but will suck Oda's balls after expending three whole chapters in some tertiary character's flashback.First problem is the garbage story mode it has. PW4 has chapters focusing on an arc with several levels dedicated to it, it sounds good on paper but the levels are pitifully short (In the Alabasta arc two of those levels were 1v1 with Crocodile), lack unlockables, side challenges, etc.PW3 had one major arena level condensing an arc; they were big, challenging and with a lot of side stuff in them. Not to mention PW3 had one of those arena levels for every arc (up to date). PW4 doesn't even acknowledges East Blue, Skypea and many other things.Just to put it into perspective Alabasta was 5% of the content in PW3 and 20% of PW4 story mode.Character models and graphics don't look that much better than PW3 and while the level assets look better they are reused a lot more as well.Some levels drag on and on making you do the same thing over and over. The Shabondy level for example consists of dozens of minutes of fighting pacifistas over and over. It also features an optional fight with Kizaru; wich in PW3 was challenging and unlocked special items when beaten, here it just gives you a message saying "Kizaru has recovered, please run away".Lastly, they ignored huge chunks of the actual series and instead put a lot of effort into that garbage fanfiction at the end. Wich of course has to include every character ever conceived by the series and turns out it has all been some Kurohige's plot, just like PW3's Dressrosa (except there it was only 5% of the whole story mode). Nobody cares about that, go to deviant art if you're so eager to write trash; your fanfictions suck. I can't stress enough how cringe inducing this fanfiction is. It's cute that they think they can write because they add little cutscenes every five minutes as if this garbage has any value. Tea party from hell! has to be the worst designed level in history, i'm convinced nobody tested it properly. You have to constantly deal with Katakuri wich can basically kill you in two hits (more proof this whole thing is just to jerk off OP fans) and it shows how bad the targeting system is; "oh, did you want to lock on the hyper powerful gary stu that's murdering you? not the generic soldier next to it?" The only way i found to beat it was using Brook's broken healing skill (i'm playing on hard though, so maybe it's not ♥♥♥♥ in lesser difficulties?).Levels are horribly designed in general with a lot of cliffs and ramps where half of the time you can jump/drop from and half the time have force walls. It's specially annoying since enemies are blown away after every combo team rocket style completely breaking the pace of the combat, you can chain it a bit but the game has some stupid stamina mechanic for that as well; I guess for the desperate souls that want some online balance in this dumpster fire?Another issue are the stupid npcs. A lot of missions require certain npcs to reach an area but they just get stuck watching the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scenery while you have to fight extremely powerful enemies that revive after a minute! And keep in mind that is the only real different objective other than beat X and is not even properly working?You can notice how much they cared about fanservice during the Katakuri fight. Instead of simply giving you a new tool (Snakeman) and letting you figure the boss, they interrupt the fight with power ups and cutscenes to make it accurate to the series! Who the ♥♥♥♥ cares! You do understand that people buying this already watched the series right? That fight is ♥♥♥♥ from the start, Katakuri does so much damage that it's ridiculous and the power ups seem to show whenever they want. Maybe they are expecting you to dodge as if you were playing Dark Souls or something but instead of understandable patterns you have to deal with random ♥♥♥ shots from the floor and attacks that can hit you from the other side of the map at bullet speed.Next issue are the ginormous characters. Sure they are more accurate to the size they have in the series (wich in itself tends to be quite inconsistent) but for ♥♥♥♥ sake there's a reason why PW3 kept them around the same scale! You end up so away from the action that becomes really dull, everything you fight is just a miniature figurine with no characteristics. Jesus christ create a fun game instead of pandering to OP fans!When fighting against giant characters your biggest enemy is the camera (ironically), it has no clue what to do. It doesn't keep your character in frame, gets stucked against walls and that's when your character isn't stuck inside the giant enemy model. At this point i'm just wondering why couldn't they just use the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game as before and improve a lot of stuff (unless they did, in wich case kudos on how much effort you required to ♥♥♥♥ it up).And you think characters will behave different when fighting a giant character or a miniature one? Of course not, giant character will swing their weapons in the air and the small playmobile enemies will get hit anyway, all giant characters are is a bag with more hit points and a bigger hit box.Another thing is the character types. In paper sounds good, assign each character a different type (power, speed, sky, etc) but what ends up happening is that characters of a similar type end up feeling similar. In PW3 each character was unique and the lack of customization forced you to adapt to that character (wich made them more varied and fun to experiment with) while here since you can customize everything, characters become really bland and samey to play as (in a game that's already quite repetitive).Sky characters are specially stupid since they hover above everyone when powered up wich makes your skills and attacks miss enemies half the time (and you're crazy if you think enemies won't be able to hit you during that time).Let me tell you about the special skills, they are as everything else ♥♥♥♥♥♥. There's some sort of classification for them i guess; well there's different types of icons at least but they don't mean anything as far as i could tell. Half of the time they can't kill even the simplest enemies. Worst, since even the most basic elite has a shield and they can stagger you, most of the time your skill gets canceled and can't even repel the enemies a bit.The shield mechanic is pure garbage, nothing more to add to that. There's too much character moments from the series inserted as cutscenes instead of just giving the story basics, wich makes no sense. Think about it, if you're a OP fan you wouldn't care about the story bits (you've probably already read the manga, watch the anime, seen youtube shorts, etc) but how the story is adapted to this type of game. Meanwhile if you're a musou fan you couldn't follow the story because it's completely disjointed!Let me tell you, the cutscenes in this game are so stupid and cringe inducing, it's One Piece as interpreted by the head injury ward patients. Why they waste so much time and money in those is ridiculous.Here's a gripe i have with both entries. If you already have a lot of characters modeled, voiced and mechanically sound enough to be fighting against, why not go the extra mile and make them playable!? There has to be around 100+ characters in the game and only around half of them playable, it's dumb.In conclusion if you want a good musou go and play Pirate Warriors 3, otherwise go and play Senran Kagura for a mediocre musou with more fanservice (considering the state of One Piece is around the same level).

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so i've completed the story and i've finished the treasure log plus all achievements. These are my thoughts on the game.The visuals are a huge stepup from oppw3, the game looks amazing in terms of gameplay. However the cutscenes are just really awkward looking. One piece just does not transfer well into 3d. Atleast the animators don't put enough effort into the cutscenes in order for them to look somewhat good. The combat is cool, characters now have the ability to do aerial combos, expanding everyone's moveset from oppw3. However actually performing combos on any major enemy is a nightmare. You'd think that when you successfully stun an enemy you'd be able to perform a combo on them right? No, they produce a red aoe that stuns you wether they're midair or being hit. Then they go into their full force burst and if you're fighting any type of logia then have fun because they're going to be impervious to all damage despite you being in full force burst yourself or not. Additionally you can't continue your combo after dashing like you could in oppw3, in this game dash has a hitbox which is just awkward when you try to combo. It was nicer before when you could do half your combo, dash, then do the rest after the dash.If you bought this game looking forward to playing as characters like Kaido then don't. Kaido is extremely linear when it comes to his standard form moveset. Due to the wano arc being like 4-5 episodes in when they made this game they didn't have any clue what to do with Kaido since he has only used about 2 moves in the anime at the time. In the game Kaido launches rocks, yells and belly flops. His dragon form is cool but it's EXTREMELY awkward trying to combo anyone with it due to how big he is. However Whitebeard was well done in this game. Way more fun to play than in oppw3 and he's even bigger this time around.The story is a huge letdown from oppw3, while oppw3 was made before dressrosa finished they had to improvise on how to end the arc. They went with the "power of friendship" path in that game which was cringe. In this game it's the exact same, the later half of wano is a huge letdown since they just bring back all previous characters into wano for no reason at all because they have no reason what to do with the story. They don't even feature important characters like Tama in the story which is one of Luffy's main driving forces to actually fight Kaido. In my opinion they should've released the game after wano is finished or just not include an unfinished arc in the story. Speaking of arcs, They skipped the entire East Blue storyline and the first mission starts directly in Alabasta, they skip a bunch of arcs for no apparent reason making the story feel very clunked up together. If you want to play this for the co-op then I don't recommend it. The online might as well not exist. When i bought this game i got it because one of my friends also bought it so i wanted to play together with him. I expected us to be able to do combos together and use teamwork to our advantage, turns out that online  is extremely desynced when it comes to fighting any enemy that isn't a minion. In conclusion this game was a letdown for me, takes like 30 hours of gameplay to complete the story and about another 30 to complete the treasure log stories, which is just more improvised cringy storylines. Not worth 50 euros

_childDocuments_.review: I rather wish I could recommend this game... I'm a long-time fan of the entire 'Warriors' style of games, and a somewhat-lapsed One Piece fan, so it's right up my alley. I played and enjoyed the first three games in the series, too. And... well, there's the rub. Frankly, to me, this sequel just doesn't feel like it's managing to justify its own existence.Let me explain. Putting aside the first game - which was understandably quite experimental - the second title provided an engaging and original Warriors-style plot featuring all your favorite characters from One Piece. A perfect game for someone who just wants a fun and feisty hack-and-slash game featuring superpowered pirates instead of ancient Chinese heroes. The THIRD title provided a thorough exploration of the entire One Piece plot by way of hack-and-slash gameplay, clear from Luffy's first meeting with Zorro in East Blue and up to the confrontation with Doflamingo on Dressrosa, which was where the Anime was at the time. A perfect game for a One Piece fan who wants to play their way through somewhat exaggerated versions of all the major fights of the series.This one, though... it's got a story mode, sure enough, following the plot of One Piece, but it's EXTREMELY abbreviated. ALL of East Blue is skipped along with the start of Grand Line, leaving you to start with the Alabasta Arc. Skypeia? Skipped. Thriller Bark? Skipped. Impel Down? Skipped. Fishman Island? Skipped. Punk Hazzard? Skipped. All the unique characters found in those places, who were playable in previous games? Gone. The interesting battlegrounds and armies found there? Gone. Dressrosa has been somewhat expanded, conversely, and Whole Cake Island has been added along with a game-original 'Wano Arc' tagged on at the end. So a lot less than what was dropped.Enough new playable characters have been added to bring the total playable number up above what it was in the third game... though I'm honestly not sure HOW, since I keep noticing characters that are missing outright or have been demoted to non-playable. Also, some of the missing characters are being sold back to you as part of the extremely pricey Character Pass, which... just feels WRONG. I don't usually blame Bandai-Namco for their expensive DLC, since it's simply their way to deal with the rising price of AAA development, but selling you characters who were ALREADY PLAYABLE in the previous game just feels like cheating. And it still doesn't address the lack of variety in terms of battlefields...Adding to my annoyance, there are a LOT of cutscenes. LONG cutscenes, cutscenes that try to bridge the huge gaps between chapters while still leaving out important details and defusing any emotional weight, cutscenes that appear in the middle of stages to interrupt the action, LOADS AND LOADS of very NICE cutscenes... but WHY?! There's an ANIME out there if you just want to WATCH One Piece. Why the heck didn't they spend all that time, money, effort and resources making more ACTUAL GAMEPLAY? More characters, more stages, more generic armies, maybe even more game-modes... I mean, yes, the story-mode obviously requires SOME cutscenes to be accessible, but you really don't need to be spoon-fed the ENTIRE plot when you can just GO WATCH THE ANIME if you want to.So yeah. Why does this game need to exist? Between the second game, the third game, and the actual ANIME, everything it does has already been done better. The basic campaign is vastly inferior to the one from 3, the original Wano Arc is vastly inferior to the original plot from 2, and all it's really got going for it is a handful of new characters and transformations, and some halfway decent destructible environments. It doesn't even look noticeably better than the last two games. Just play them instead.TL;DR: To quote one of my favorite reviewers, "I miss the days where sequels having MORE stuff was taken as read..."
