I would recommend waiting until they announce the DLC characters and then picking up whoever you like. However, personally, I got the season pass because I want to have all the characters regardless.The combat is incredible. I've played many Musou games in my life, (including but not limited to: Dynasty Warriors 1 through 7, the previous Pirate Warriors games, and the Berserk Musou game), and I have to say this game is one of the best demonstrations of how fun and engaging the Musou battle system is. I feel a rush of adrenaline every time I finish a combo and topple a hundred enemies in one go.On the completion side of things, this game is in the middle of the spectrum. There are only 3 main quest logs: The Dramatic Log which is the story mode where you play as a select set of characters each quest, the Free Log which allows you to replay Dramatic Log missions with any character you want, and the ratings you get for each quest is shared between the two logs, and finally, the Treasure Log, where you'll probably spend most of your time because it has a whole lot of quests that when completed will reward you with golden coins that you need to level up your characters skills or stats.Speaking of which, the Growth Maps offer a decent method of progressing your characters through buffing their main stats or unlocking new abilities for them. You can choose up to 4 abilities for these characters to use during each battle but the number of abilities you can unlock makes it so you have options in case you wish to change up your play style whenever you want. The only thing that bothers me is that you have to select a mission first before you can access the Growth Map, which isn't much of a problem since you can still navigate between different characters' maps, it's just a tedious process is all. I'm hoping that in a future patch the devs will add a Growth Map option to the main menu just to make it easier to access.Oh, right, I almost forgot. The graphics of the game are pretty good. They're not incredible or realistic to any measure, but they do the job of representing a CGI anime game. The action cutscenes are definitely incredible though. It feels like a trip down memory lane but also a whole new experience at the same time. All in all, I give this game a good ol' 9/10. It's incredibly fun and can get addicting if you're not careful. I mean, look at me, I played 12 hours of this on launch day alone. That's dangerous, but it's a damn good time. Anyway, that's all I got for you. If you read all that, thank you first of all, and I genuinely hope you give this game a try. As a One Piece and Musou game fan, this brings me so much joy. Can't wait for the DLC characters!

_childDocuments_.review: Steamdeck users.This game says its verified for steamdeck. It is not. The cutscenes do not work right out of the box. But I have been able to get them to work. At first I was using the latest version a proton GE. That got me video for the cutscenes. But no audio. After some experimenting, I was able to get both the video and audio for cutscenes by doing the following.I went into settings -> Compatability and switched to Proton Experimental. Then in settings -> General, I entered the following into the Launch Options: GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK=protonaudioconverterbin:NONE %command%This fixed cutscenes for me. Hopefully it works on others devices.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4 has made a big leap from its predecessor ( One Piece: Pirate Warriors 3 ). One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is a fan's dream game, as it takes the iconic battles and moments of eight major story arcs and puts you right in the action like never before. Combat is fun and flashy while still managing to be surprisingly thoughtful, and although a few characters aren't a joy to control, a majority of the cast is an absolute delight to play as.  The combat system works well . Each character’s unique fighting style is represented so they all feel different to play , also there's a ton here to enjoy. The prospect of getting hands-on as Big Mom, Kaido, and Katakuri then smashing through armies of Samurai on Wano is wonderful. The characters play fantastically, each distinct and diverse, with fantastic realisations of their moves and abilities.The biggest issue ( for me ) with One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is the camera, which is at best unreliable, and at worst unusable. When facing multiple of the weak opponents it’s not really an issue, but when you lock onto one of the tougher opponents it’s awful. The camera follows the enemy far slower than the action, and sometimes just unlocks for no reason. It’s a really unfortunate blemish on an otherwise fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Already finished 80% of the main story after 9 hours, figured i'd add a quick review of my time so far.The game follows the classic one piece story, starting off from the Alabasta arc and finishing at a 'game only' re-imagined ending in Wano, however many of the islands / arcs have been cut, these include:-East blue saga-Anything pre Alabasta (Drum, little garden, whisky peak)-Sky Island-Thriller Bark-Impel Down / Amazon Lily-Fishman Island-Zou arcSo a large portion of the actual series / manga has been cut, with many of my personal favourite moments missing, personally this made the game less enjoyable, especially since it means i'm going to finish the game within about 10 hours. On top of this certain scenes have been edited for the cutscenes, the iconic moment where luffy rescues ace for example, or just certain characters being completely removed. The gameplay is a slightly more polished version of PW3, with some moves copied but mostly an entirely new moveset established, and an added "burst mode" which temporarily strengthens your character or adds new moves / features such as flight, as well as some characters having an awakening mode (Luffy's gear second and 4th mainly that changes their appearance and moveset). Also your Special moves are now selectable, so you can pick and choose whatever suits your playstyle more.You level your characters in a similar way to the prequel, using medals / badges collected throughout the game as well as 'Beli' to add specific stats that increase their stamina, health and damge, as well as unlocking upgrades for moves and new skills / specials, however to max out these skills a lot of grinding is needed. Graphics seem slightly sharper than that of it's predecessor, however the colour palette after sabaody seems to get very washed out and bland, i'm assuming in set up for the whole cake arc which suddenly looked very vibrant again.Performance wise i'm having no issue on a gtx 1060, 16gb of ram and a ryzen 3600, running the game at max settings on a 1440p monitor, and any issues people seem to be facing aren't ridiculously common, the main being either the game not launching (which a fix hasn't really been found for), or it not recognising a controller, which as many others have said is a simple fix, Overall it's more of the same, if you enjoy the warriors games and are a fan of One piece, then you'll enjoy this, just don't expect anything amazingly new or groundbreaking, and expect a lot of cut content, probably not worth the £40 price tag but fun nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun but gets very repetitive later on. There are a lot of improvements but there are a few problems I have with the game. The game reuse a lot of the models and animation during cutscenes, not movie cutscenes. Second problem is they removed like about 7 playable characters from the previous, Enel, Kuma, Garp, Perona, Magellan, Moria, and Caeser. While the roster of playable characters in this game is bigger, yes, even with the DLC characters, it is a downgrade by removing (or in this case replacing) previous playable characters. Third problem is they removed Kizuna Rush and replaced it with Full Force Burst but without the APC characters appearing at the end of your combo strings and combination cinematic attack. Some people dislike them and some people like me like them. I enjoy looking at the different combination attacks cinematics and having APC attack with you at the end of a combo string makes them feel alive. In this game, allies APC are useless and boring. Fourth problem is the DLCs. I didn't buy the DLCs mostly because they're pointless, in my opinion. They should had added additional maps and Arcs for the DLC. But instead we get more playable characters which doesn't add any replayability to me after finishing the game. If the characters DLC were like 5 or 6 USD I guess they're worth it. The new improvements they added are as follow. You can jump, customize your character's Skills and Special Skills loadout, and they removed the Treasure Events. This is a musou type game with a One Piece skin slapped on it. You either like One Piece and/or Musou games or you don't. I like both but eventually it starts to feel very repetitive like I said earlier. Not worth full price. At least 20 to 30 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Pirate Worries 4 is based on the hit anime  and is the predecessors of the three other games in the series. Combat is played the same, however, it is tweaked and is more smooth and air combat is much better as well. The game is sure to keep fans of , both casual and hardcore invested with its wonderful gameplay and retelling of the story.  + A great retelling of the  story.+ Fun gameplay that can sometimes even be addictive+ Both casual and hardcore  fans can find enjoyment in this game+ Over 43 different characters to play as, plus a season pass with some more.+ Four different subtypes to play as.- Gameplay may get stale for some people. - Some fan-favorite arks did not make it into the game.- Some of the characters that were playable in OPW3 are not playable in this game. The game’s story follows the anime’s story and plays it through arks with a few levels in each and every word. The story of One Piece is great and the game tells it very well with the arks that we have been giving, the story has the One Piece charm and that is something that all fans can enjoy. However, not all arks made it into the game and fan favorites were removed as well. The entire  was cut, the game starts at , so no ,  was removed, , , , and  were also removed. This is disappointing, mainly because a lot of  fans loved some of these arks.  and  were not even shown in the story or mentioned, however,  was shown once in the story when the game was talking about . Gameplay in the game is very fun and can be addictive at times as well, there are many characters for you to select sometimes depending on the mission you are giving. Each character has its own moves and has one of the four subtypes, Power, Speed, Technique, and Sky. Some characters can be a certain subtype in the Pre-time skip but have different moves in the Post-time Skip due to certain transformations, for example, Sanji is a speed type in the Pre-time skip but at the Post-time skip, he will be a Sky type due to some of his moves been modified.  Every character has three special moves and a mode where they can be powered up and do extra damage. Most of these special moves will take out most enemies and will do a large chunk of damage to bosses. At some point, characters will enter a  mode, when this mode is activated they will get a special benefit depending on their subtype. Power Types are centered around the fact that they can deal large amounts of damage and take out enemies very quickly. When a power type character is hit by an enemy, a wall, or the floor, a shock wave is sent out and will damage any enemies that are near it. When power types are in , they will get more attack damage and their smash attacks are more powerful.  Speed types are more focused on combat as they have combo potential, and they can move around very fast, their stamina usage is also reduced in a power dash. When Speed types are in , their stamina usage is greatly reduced in a power dash. Technique types are the most interesting as they have special moves that affect gameplay, like putting enemies to sleep, using oil, and lighting it up to make fire, and there is so much more. Technique types can also perform an attack while charging that will push enemies towards them. When a Technique type enters  their special traits of that character are powered up.  Sky types are a bit weird at first but they focus on air combat and have the most characteristics out of all the types. They are immune to all damage during a power dash, their power dash counties until all the stamina is used up, enemies that are not on the ground can get caught up in their power dash, and they can use stamina to start an attack when falling from an aerial attack. When a Sky type goes , they will have the ability to float constantly and their stamina usage is decreased during a power dash.  Combat is like other  games and the main objective for every single mission is to beat up a bunch of enemies, beat up leaders to take over territories to get more minions to help you fight. At some point, you will fight a mini-boss or a boss, when bosses come out they will have an  if you remove all of the  they will be stunned and put into a state called , in which they will take more damage.Depending on who you fight, that characters  may come into play as well if the character has one of course.  and  don’t really have any gimmicks when it comes to attacking them other than the fact that their devil fruit is their move set mostly. However, if a Logia activates their ability, their appearance can change and normal attacks will not harm them. To harm someone with a Logia they will need to be put in their armor break state and all attacks will harm them when they are in this state.Sometimes a  may take place during the level at a certain location or if you do certain requirements, these  can be things like normal missions as well when the time comes for them. If you are able to complete these missions, then you will get rewarded barries which is the currency for the game.   is a mode that lets you play a bunch of missions, in this mode, you can get barries that help you level up your characters.  has you do the same missions as what the story mode provides but it’s mostly just you fighting a bunch of enemies, you will have different characters that will team up with you. You can play as any character in this mode if you have them unlocked, some character can only be unlocked in  after completing certain missions. The gameplay is fun but it can get stale sometimes, especially after you are done completing the story.  is a nice feature but you are doing the same thing over and over again and there is really no motive to continue playing. I was able to play the game in high settings, I used a NIVIDA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, 16 GB of RAM storage on a 2560:1440 [16:9] monitor. The game runs really smooth and I had no issues what so ever while playing, the game may look like you need a good computer, but if you have a decent computer, you should be able to run the game in low settings.One Piece Pirate Worries 4 is a great addition to the series and is a wonderfully made game, I have been an avid player of the previous game and this one proves once again why this series is great. Fans of the series can look forward to more of what they’ve come to love and expect.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Koei cannot do stable online play.I absolutely loved Pirate Warriors 2 and had a lot of fun on the Playstation version of it. Sure, having to beat a level before being able to play with a friend sucked but I had a lot of fun regardless.In the years since playing Pirate Warriors 2, barely any progress has been made with regards to online functionality and stability and, with the kindest regards, the multiplayer aspect of Pirate Warriors on the PC, as well as many Warriors titles, is some of the shoddiest and downright abysmal implementation of online I've seen in years.The visuals are wonderful and the presentation of each chapter is a treat for old and new fans, but the main draw is enjoying the series with my friends and playing through the wonderful arcs of One Piece together as our favorite characters. With so many random disconnects half-way through a level, I can only be reminded of how atrocious Dynasty Warriors 8 on the PS4 was for almost a year after launch. It's worth noting that Dynasty Warriors 8 on PC STILL doesn't have an online component, despite console versions having said capability.I can't in good faith recommend this to anyone who wants to play multiplayer. I can, however, recommend this to anyone disappointed with Pirate Warriors 3 and looking for a more relaxing style of play without timeskip "characters" being a thing. It's definitely more akin to Pirate Warriors 2 (though unfortunately still not a new Oda inspired story like 2 was) but it still leaves a lot to be desired.To say that this is the 4th installment in a series is downright depressing. I love this series but it's just such a disappointment to try to play with friends. Alone, it's still got the content you're here for, but it's hardly moved since the earlier titles in terms of growth.It's a great game, it's just a shambles of the same old errors, disconnects, and disappointment that Koei have seemingly instilled in every Warriors game in the past 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphically, the game is probably the best looking musou game on the market right now. It's colorful and vibrant, however the environment textures are still relatively low-rez. This, however, is made up by the fact that this game displays more enemies than any other musou before it; in some cases you can literally see hundreds of enemies at the same time, especially given the now more open level-design, another plus imo.Musically, the game sounds good, with the addition of the anime soundtrack a bit nostalgic and perfectly fitting for this game.The story follows the manga/anime, but it only covers a few, big arcs such as ,  or the  arc. Everything else is covered in cutscenes featuring scenes from PW3, which somewhat feels lazy, but really isn't a problem. Of course, the main part of the game is it's post-game, which, just like in PW3, is amazing.The gameplay is almost exactly the same as PW3, but with a few added mechanics to makes combos more fluent and thus more fun. Overall, it is incredibly satisfying and is now also customizable, giving every character the chance to equip any 4 moves you have unlocked, thus providing more variety. This, in turn, leads to the gamplay not becoming repetetive as quickly as other games in the genre.Overall, if you liked PW3 and you want an enhanced version of it, this is it. If you've never played a Pirate Warriros game before or seen the anime, I recommend playing PW3 before this, to get an idea of the story and the gameplay basics. However, this game is amazing and I very much recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enjoyable hack and slash action game in the vein of Dynasty Warriors - Your hero will take on massive crowds of enemies and tackle thematic objectives around a map, often with wildly changing objectives throughout a particular mission. The One Piece series is represented well here. The characters look and sound incredible. Their move sets are hilarious and true to their presentation in the anime more or less. In this game you will play through the following arcs: Arabasta, Enies Lobby, Marineford (just the battle, not the prison breakout), Dressrosa (Really just the birdcage, the colosseum is minimized, and a missed opportunity), Whole Cake Island, and Wano Country. Arcs inbetween and around those played through are covered in a voice over montage between Islands. There are a wide array of characters and costumes for the characters to spice up your visuals and play styles. The advancement for the characters and their abilities is rewarding and fun, I can see it being a bit grindy towards the end. The music in the game is... 'fine'. With so much amazing music from the show, there are just a lot of missed opportunities to incorporate it here. The additional music pack that they are selling for $17-$20 USD is absurd, and it should be included. I read some reviews where that music had some issues as well, but they appear to have been resolved (the music didn't loop, it does now)So, I recommend this game with a caveat: You really need enjoy the game play of the Dynasty Warriors games and One Piece to get value here.  It captures the madcap and wild adventures of the One Piece crew, and the massive crowd battles really seem to fit - The "Deluxe" edition simply includes all of the character DLC packs, so if your interest in those characters is low, you can likely skip it for the base game, and be perfectly happy.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is by far the best anime adapted game I've ever played, and my favorite Musou title of all time.There's so much things this game did right, and so much was improved from the previous installment.Let's start with the roster. You get to play as your favorite characters from One Piece. From the basic Straw Hat Crew to Katakuri to Law, all favourites were included in the game. I always dream of letting me experience as the characters in One Piece, using different techniques to defeat enemies. Now you can, using different combos to defeat hordes of minions. It's so satisfying to launch a Red Hawk and wipe out over 50 enemies in an instant, or create a ROOM and see all minions turn into bombs, or use Gear 4th Bounce Man to just jump around.Speaking of techniques, the combat is so good. The last installment isn't bad, using a combination of Triangles and Squares (or X and Y Buttons) to launch different combos, and usually 2 specials  and 1 awakening for each character. This time it's just a straight improvement from the last one. More combos and specials included, and 4 specials/awakenings can be used at once. Now you can be awakened, Bounce Man and Snake Man at the same time. Or use all Zoro's New World Techniques at the same time. Now that's dope.The introduction of animation cancel is also really fun and makes the game more fast paced, comfortable and make the skill ceiling higher. You feel so much more powerful using different cancels, usually attack-dash combos, and it feels so much less clunky compared to OPPW3.Air Combos are fun as hell. Using Sky characters to use air combos continuously is hella fun. Sanji with Sky Walk awakening and keep jingling Katakuri non-stop is both hilarious and insanely fun. And most importantly, all characters feel fun and unique to play. OPPW3 is fun, but once you realised the strongest characters and start spamming them with their broken moves like Fujitora throughout the Treasure Log, the game just gets stale real quick. Now it feels like every character has their own niche to try out and have fun with. Usopp's explosive combos are fun as hell, so is Hancock's immobilizing moves and Law's Room moves.There's so much good things about the combat and characters, I haven't even touch on the story mode. Unlike the previous title where it goes through all islands from Shells Town to Dressrosa, this time they include the most memorable moments only, so starting from the Alabasta, Water 7/Enies Lobby, Sabaody/Marineford, Dressrosa, Whole Cake Island and Finally Wano. And most importantly, the Game Original story of Wano is so good. Compared to OPPW3, where the Dressrosa original story is an absolute mess, OPPW4's Wano original story is actually interesting and fun to watch. Seeing how Katakuri, Kid and Luffy work together is incredible, or having Bartolomeo & Cavendish come to Wano after listening to Luffy's news is really heartwarming. The final clash is real cool and intense, and the animation against Kaido is well done. It's a really unforgettable experience.Overall a very solid beat'em up game. This review is finished by the time I've finished the main story missions, and I can't wait to jump into Treasure mode and experience more new characters.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: As far as One Piece Pirate Warriors installments go, this game is the A1-Steak Sauce Tier game of the century. DELICIOUS! I've played Pirate Warriors 3, and for some reason, Pirate Warriors 4 actually runs more smoothly on my computer, whereas Pirate Warriors 3 had a lot of bugs and often wouldn't play the cutscenes. I've also played through a lot of World Seeker, and this game is a lot more complete than World Seeker was. They got the original voice actors, everything is fleshed out, and this game is super complete from a music, voice and graphics standpoint (except for maybe some flat facial expressions). The combat system is pretty awesome, and the aerial combat system is an awesome addition to the game. If you are a One Piece fan, especially those who are huge fans like me, you'll be drawn into the game immediately. Other than the fact that they put a ton of emphasis on Marineford (as most games in the series do), the parts of the storyline they pick are awesome! The game doesn't really have any East Blue or Skypiea stages, but they do manage to touch a lot of the main plot in the first half of the game. 10/10 Would recommend to anyone who likes One Piece. If you've been following One Piece for the past 12 years like I have, the game will totally make your weekend awesome! :)

I've completed 4 stories worth about 10 stages each and I'm basically at the last story. It took me way longer to get this far in OPW3.The character progression feels more involved in this game, with us now being able to unlock, upgrade and swap out character skills to build a cooler feeling experience and allowing a difference in playing which OPW3 didn't have (which made combat feel samey). Let's get into the important bit.I am not anywhere near done so IDK the full list of characters compared to OPW3, I am hoping it's added rather than taken away but I would say I feel that removing the amount of storyline they did for the sake of adding a plethora of characters which most people won't ever touch, whilst also robbing us of the opportunity to see explored arcs post-Dressrosa feels... _childDocuments_.review: After multiple adaptations from the best-selling manga ever created by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece finally turns into a proper JRPG (perhaps for the first time in its history) and let me anticipate that is going to be one of the best to date. The plot of Odyssey can be considered like a sort of spin-off, meaning it has nothing to do with the events happening in the main series. While sailing across the New World, Luffy and his crew are shipwrecked on Waford, a legendary island surrounded by raging storms and populated by mysterious golems. Here the Straw Hat pirates are stripped of all their powers by two new interesting characters, Adio and Lim, who somehow have developed a deep hatred towards pirates. Lim has the special ability to make people forget about their powers and she uses it on the Straw Hat crew, thinking they are just like all other evil pirates. With their powers lost and the ship heavily damaged, Luffy and his friends are unable to leave the island, thus they accept Lim and Adio’s help to recover their powers by visiting “Memoria”, a dreamlike dimension in which our protagonists can relive their past adventures and remember how they gained those skills.Obviously, the story is just an expedient to make you relive the Straw Hat journey, starting from the Arabasta arc and moving forward, with Adio and Lim stories that are unfortunately overshadowed by the most memorable episodes of Luffy and his crew. Fans of the series who have already read or watched those might feel tired of re-living them again, just like in Pirate Warriors 4 before, although Bandai Namco was smart enough to include many new secondary events for each chapter. Those who are new to One Piece should know that there is a lot of fan service, such as references to other characters and events connected to the series, that newcomers wouldn’t be able to catch. Thankfully, each story arc has short recaps that give plenty of info on what happened in the canon storyline, so there isn’t any risk of being confused.Speaking about the gameplay, I’m not exaggerating when I say that Odyssey pretty much resembles Dragon Quest XI (the developer ILCA collaborated with Square Enix during its development). Not just the graphics, which are really great and perfectly in line with the anime art style, but also the narration, with its countless dialogues, the funny monsters’ design and the focus on exploration, gave me plenty of DQ vibes. Plus, it is possible to swap characters and use their abilities while exploring. For example, Luffy can use Gum-Gum Rocket to grab items or reach distant areas by stretching out his arms, Sanji can sense rare ingredients, Chopper can explore small tunnels, Nami can find hidden money and so on. This encourages swapping characters on the go and helps to diversify the gameplay during exploration.Each story arc accessed from the Memoria dimension can be freely explored through multiple maps that offer a great amount of secondary content, such as side quests, bounties and time-space fractures that will transport some of your characters into a new space called Hysteria, a corrupted memory that needs to be fixed to allow them to go back safely, increasing their bond level and unlocking powerful group attacks. There are also some greatly appreciated quality of life options, such as the ability to fast travel from any position (towards predefined locations), the option to increase the combat speed and even an auto-battle mode controlled by the AI, which can be helpful when facing low-level enemies that only need a few attacks to be defeated.Combat is turn-based, meaning you will have a party of four members taking turns to fight against small groups of enemies. Each character is initially positioned in a different area of the battlefield and must defeat all enemies on its front before moving to another area. All characters can be replaced at any time with the reserve crew, even if they have been knocked out (but one must still be alive). Replacing the team is recommended, as each one has a different type of attack based on a simple rock, paper, scissors scheme that defines strengths and weaknesses. Luffi, Sanji and Chopper belong to the Strength category, meaning they are more effective when facing enemies in the Speed category (such as Nami and Usop), who are more advantaged against enemies that use attacks based on Technique (like Zoro and Nico Robin), the latter being best suited when dealing with enemies of the Strength category. Other weaknesses and resistances are represented by Burn, Freeze and Lightning elements, so you always need to keep an eye on the enemies’ stats to understand how to deal heavy damage by exploiting their weak points. All members can also use special skills by spending tension points (TP), which can be accumulated with standard attacks. During the fight it is also possible to incur in “dramatic scenes”, which activate specific conditions such as “defeat the enemy before it unleashes a powerful attack” that grant additional experience if completed.While combat is satisfying enough, it can often be too simple and easy, perhaps to not scare off those One Piece fans who are new to RPG games. It makes sense, but on the other hand, veterans of the genre could be somewhat disappointed by the lack of challenge and customization (though camping and crafting accessories are also present).

_childDocuments_.review: So far I like the game a lot, this is the second time I have purchased the game, the first being on the switch. After I realized that the game had severely cut back graphic features like no grass, I needed to get it on PC. I have only finished alabastas arc, but so far I can pin point things I miss about the PW3. I miss the little dodge mechanic purely for angling your character in the middle of an attack chain, that really helped combos in that game. I also miss having more of an option to choose which character you play as during the story, because I don’t ever want to play as usopp. I don’t think anyone wants to play as usopp. I am enjoying the game but so far the combos for pre time skip zoro and Sanji feel kind of stiff. Then again I have not mastered that games new fighting mechanic nor have I gotten all the skills the game for them. I have high hopes for the game and if you are a fan of pirates, one piece, anime, or dynasty warrior games I recommend this game.EDIT: After having plenty of time with the game, and having gotten 100% of the achievements with it I can say that I fully recommend this game. One of my previous grips with the game was that the combat was kinda clunky, but after learning how to play with the new mechanics I find it even better than in PW3. Some characters are clearly better than others, like kaido, big mom, and whitebeard completely destroy everything in this game, all of them have 4 equivalent of kizuna rushes (except kaido, but his xxyyy combo is insane). I find my favorite characters in this game are crocodile, doffy, katakuri (I don't really like his combo chains, but my god he is immortal. Also his mochi foot stun prevents logia users into transforming into their forms which is super helpful). whitebeard, kaido, big mom, blackbeard (not as op in this game or fun to play as, but still powerful with his special attacks. Wish his basic attack chains were better and used more of his devil fruits) Characters I was disappointed in, in this game were Aokiji, and Kizaru. I wish the move sets were just better, Aokiji hits like a wet noodle, and his powerful specials don't do enough damage, or just plain miss the enemies. Kizaru is like sonic, but doesn't do enough damage as well. I hope the DLC roster includes Burgess ( snowballs chance in hell, I know) X Drake, Jack, and perospero.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the better warriors games, but I wish there were more move slots, skill slots, & that you would do more damage by endgame (Was really hoping I could one shot with Katakuri's mochi anemone or White Beard's super for example by end game with all damage passives equipped, w/ maxed out damage coins) I personally was just a little disappointed by the lack of oomf in supers in general.Also I was pretty disappointed by how some characters were either shortchanged with skills & transformations (Such as Carrot Frankie & debatably Chopper not getting transformations; but Big Mom, Kaido, & Luffy did get transformations), lack of costumes, or straight up being worse than in OPPW3 (I personally found Tashigi & the Fujitora to be a lot more enjoyable in OPPW3), or just outright terrible (I'm like never going to play as Boa Hancock, she legitimately has the worst moveset in the game imo). Oh & they removed a few characters from the previous game such as Perona, RIP Perona.Apart from all of that I still feel like out of all the Warriors games I've played, I still feel like Fire Emblem Warriors, Hyrule Warriors, DW7EL, & DW PsVita probably all handled enemy captains better; I was never particularly thrilled to run into any captains, & never felt challenged in any recent warriors game, pretty much it boiled down to just needing better stats in this OPPW4 or the other OPPW3, or just running off to find a medkit (meat/food), or just playing as a factually better character (Like Big Mom, or Katakuri who can heal themselves & deal great damage).If anything the combat encouraged playing as the "OP" characters, since you want to deal with the regenerating "health bar" quickly & having a self heal makes things significantly easier, it just felt like if you wanted to have any fun you had to give up a few skill slots to damage boosting so you could tear through the armored health bar thing faster so you could beat a stage in a reasonable amount of time. And I am still very annoyed by the "victory conditions have changed" thing where every stage is just constantly dragged out, does it really hurt to let us know how much time we will be spending on a stage, like come on, sometimes I just want to get my upgrades or money & move on instead of having to randomly commit to a long mission.As for the new types I personally didn't like it, it really didn't make a whole lotta sense: For instance Luffy's Snake Man is a Speed type, but his Bound Man is a sky type, yet the Sky type moves faster & can hold the dash button to fly across the map, but Snake Man has to spam the dash button (And snake man has a problem doing damage or connecting hits so he isn't that great either really). This same issue is sorta across the board as Kizaru & Big mom both in sky type forms can dash infinitely, but speed type characters seemingly cannot. Then when it comes to movesets it feels like Technique types are always Clunky, & Strength types are always robbed of any aerial moves, so sky types tend to be both faster & more versatile than everyone else.I will say I really liked the addition of being able to equip moves onto characters, but I wish we were able to equip another 4 to the other trigger, I just find it odd that we have so many unused buttons, & that captain fights have not gotten more intelligent, it pretty much boils down to spamming attacks & having better stats & running off to heal when necessary still.All in all, I feel this warriors game is worth your time, it has the groundwork to be a great game, but falls just short of being great by taking a few steps forward from past titles (selectable moves, better graphics, larger characters & enemies, destructible environments) & a few steps back (Armored health bars, clunkier movesets, less costumes, not everyone gets aerial combos, not everyone can hold dash, not everyone gets transformations, cut characters & stories, difficulty largely based on stats rather than skill).

_childDocuments_.review: **Title: A Swashbuckling Adventure Worth Every Doubloon!**If you're looking for a game that combines the thrill of high-seas adventure with the heart-pounding action of a warrior's tale, look no further than "One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4." As a longtime fan of both the "One Piece" manga/anime series and the Warriors-style games, I can confidently say that this latest installment hits the mark and then some.**Graphics & Animation (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐):**The visuals in Pirate Warriors 4 are nothing short of stunning. From the vibrant, cel-shaded art style that perfectly captures the essence of Eiichiro Oda's iconic characters to the fluid, dynamic animations during combat, every frame is a testament to the craftsmanship of the developers. Whether you're unleashing devastating special attacks or engaging in epic boss battles, the attention to detail is impeccable.**Gameplay & Combat (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐):**The gameplay is where Pirate Warriors 4 truly shines. As a musou-style game, it delivers non-stop action with a roster of beloved characters from the One Piece universe. Each character feels distinct and true to their manga counterparts, with unique abilities and playstyles that keep the combat fresh and exciting. Whether you're mowing down hordes of enemies with Luffy's Gum-Gum techniques or unleashing Zoro's powerful swordsmanship, the combat mechanics are intuitive yet deep enough to satisfy both newcomers and veterans alike.**Story & Content (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐):**Fans of One Piece will be delighted by the faithful retelling of key arcs from the series, from the East Blue saga to the Wano Country arc. The game does an excellent job of blending storytelling with gameplay, offering both newcomers and longtime fans a chance to experience the epic journey of the Straw Hat Pirates. With multiple game modes, including a compelling Dramatic Log mode and an engaging Treasure Log mode for replayability, there's no shortage of content to explore.**Sound & Music (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐):**The soundtrack of Pirate Warriors 4 perfectly complements the action-packed gameplay, with memorable tunes that evoke the spirit of adventure and camaraderie found in One Piece. From stirring battle themes to emotional character moments, the music enhances the overall experience and immerses you deeper into the world of pirates and warriors.**Overall Experience (⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐):**"One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4" is a must-have for fans of the series and action game enthusiasts alike. With its captivating visuals, exhilarating gameplay, faithful storytelling, and superb sound design, it stands as a testament to what a licensed game can achieve when done right. Whether you're reliving your favorite moments from the manga/anime or experiencing them for the first time, this game delivers an unforgettable adventure that will have you hoisting the Jolly Roger and setting sail for excitement!Set course for adventure and join the Straw Hat Pirates in their quest for the ultimate treasure—your enjoyment awaits in "One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4." Aye, this game be worthy of all five stars and then some!

_childDocuments_.review: As a One Piece fan, who really enjoyed OPPW3, this game was really enjoyable.+ Very different Characters. If you get bored by one, you can always play with another - the feeling is guaranteed to be different.+ Even the characters, who are of the same type (Power, Sky, Technique and Speed) are very different from each other. Yes, they have similar traits, but you always know that you are playing Luffy and not just a Power Type Character, for example.+ Maps are gorgeous, even though they are pretty similar to each other (which can be Considered a -). The destructible terrain makes it more realistic and makes you feel even more powerful.+ Music is awesome. I personally like the OPPW3 tunes more, but these are not bad as well and the fact you can choose your favorites whenever you want is cool.+ Cinematics are very well made - they make the stories much more enjoyable (at least during the first play through :D)- The Story is most likely not gonna be able to grab the casual player, if they are not a One Piece fan and haven't watched the anime or read the manga. A lot of arcs were skipped, which they tried to fill with cutscenes between the in-game arcs, but I, personally, think it's pretty difficult to follow the story still.- The game is pretty repetitive after you complete the Story and might get boring for some. DLC's are coming, which will likely fix that, but if you're not a fan of repetitive gameplay, you'll likely quit the game very fast.Overall, I think the game does what it aims to do - provide a fun experience for the One Piece and Musou fans with a lot of the most-loved and popular Characters from the anime. If you're a One Piece fan, I definitely recommend it, you're gonna have a blast. I know I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Massive One Piece fan, and a big fan of both Pirate Warriors - and Warriors games in general. This game has a lot going for it, but just as much working against it. I haven't played it a lot on Steam, but have Platinumed them all on Playstation.Pros: Nice graphics, destructible environments, decent roster, great new additions to the roster, jumping (?), Nami., great core gameplay as always, online is pretty fun, Gear 4thCons: Lack of costumes, a LOT of cut story content/maps, plenty of classic characters cut from the roster this time around.This game tries to do a lot of new things with the Warriors formula - and I can appreciate the vision, but the execution is rather lacking. The jumping and addition of "sky" combat seems great, until you realize that it interferes with a lot of character's movesets and I cannot stress enough that not all air combos were created equal. Unless you're playing a Sky type or Luffy, you're ♥♥♥♥ outta luck. I'm not a fan of the added dash/stamina system either. The new skill select is okay, I can see why people may not like it as it does interfere with established movesets once again. Personally I'd go with PW3 for the definitive "Pirate Warriors" experience.Still, if you're a fan of One Piece, pick it up on sale. It does have a lot of the newer characters and forms working for it over PW3, so if that's more your cup of tea then I'd say its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: "One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4" sets sail with high expectations but ultimately capsizes under the weight of its own shortcomings, failing to live up to the standards set by its predecessors.First and foremost, the gameplay feels like a step backward. While the series has always been known for its fast-paced, hack-and-slash action, "Pirate Warriors 4" fails to innovate on the formula, instead relying on tired mechanics and repetitive combat. The controls are clunky and unresponsive, making executing combos and special moves a frustrating exercise in trial and error. Battles quickly devolve into mindless button-mashing, with little in the way of strategy or depth to keep players engaged.The story mode, which should be a highlight of any anime-based game, is similarly disappointing. While it attempts to follow the events of the One Piece storyline, it does so in a disjointed and rushed manner. Important plot points are glossed over or omitted entirely, and character development is virtually nonexistent. As a result, the narrative feels shallow and unsatisfying, leaving fans feeling shortchanged.Graphically, the game is a mixed bag. While the character models are well-rendered and faithful to their anime counterparts, the environments are bland and uninspired, lacking the vibrant energy and personality of the One Piece universe. Animations are stiff and awkward, with characters moving in a way that feels unnatural and janky.Even the online multiplayer, which should be a major draw for fans of the series, is plagued by issues. Matchmaking is slow and unreliable, and laggy matches are all too common, leading to a frustrating and unenjoyable experience.In the end, "One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4" is a disappointing addition to the One Piece video game series that fails to capture the excitement and energy of the anime. Its clunky gameplay, lackluster story, and uninspired design make it a hard game to recommend to anyone other than the most die-hard One Piece fans.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4 takes the series to new heights with revamped combat and progression mechanics. In addition to these new mechanics comes new story missions including a canon ending to the Dressrosa, Whole Cake Island, and Wano Country. On top of all this, stunning new soundtracks, visuals, and playable characters help make this game feel like a worthy purchase. My only gripes with the game are how much of the story is glossed-over, with only a handful of crucial arcs left in a playable state. This is especially a bummer considering how much of the story was covered in the previous games. Still, this game set out what it wanted to do, which is deliver us new content from previously untouched arcs in the manga and anime. It is an addicting game and one that I can see myself playing for months on end. If you're a fan of either One Piece or other Musou (Warrior) games, this one is a must-play!

_childDocuments_.review: Edited 2023 a ton of Pro's and - important - constructive criticism regarding the hud for future console versions and pc updates + some ideas for a sequel.Pro's - a very long listA+ in general, fantastic game. Got it also for switch. The most fantastic One Piece game, I should say. Full recommendation. Please don't change anything - except the few aspects about the hud mentioned in constructive criticism. The amount of details which have been put into the combos for each character is just insanely good. This is one of the things that I love about a beatem up game. The amount of detail in general (it sounds vague, I know - but they clearly just put their souls into their work to create that detailed gigantic playground and the phenomenal characters that you can see and hear ingame. Never seen such a beauty of a game that has been created with an anime series as a model.)Fluid gameplay, colourful map design with love for the details - e. g. cup cakes and trees on Whole Cake Island, which laugh or make faces. Or the big, branched territory on Enies Lobby. Magnificent coulourful and fun - just the right mood for a One Piece video game title.Constructive criticism reg. the layout About the layout: the messages (e.g. "Sabo appeared!" or "*xyz location* could fall") appearing in the middle of the screen while fighting. I partly understand why you chose to put them in the middle of the screen, but please hear me out. The messages are important, because they determine how the players reacts to certain eventy which determine - in some cases - victory or defeat. You put them in the middle of the screen to let the player know as clearly as possible about what is going on. I appreciate that and I acknowledge that the messages are important. The problem with them appearing in the middle screen is obviously, that the messages are popping up very frequently. If we would be dealing with a message at the start and a message at the end - no problemo. You could easily put the messages on the top of the screen - when you play for hours you start to get better picking them up automatically, so it's fine - you could also let the player rule their visibility via a general hud option, although I'd prefer the first option in case of the messages. I am not sure, but I also assume this decision you made was kind of a safe call for handheld console versions - simply to make sure that there wouldn't be any issues with the messages being too tiny or unnoticable or sth. Here is the thing: if that seemingly little but important issue was fixed, this title would be the best One Piece game ever created and I can almost assure you that it would stay at the top for decades. So I politely ask you to fix this with an update or at least in the next console version - the messages really disturb the playing experience at times, since the textblocks are blocking the sight - and you could easily fix it. A good idea would also be to add a hud setting to change the visibility of the yellow/red marks on the characters and the yellow lines to be able to make them less- or even invisible. If it wasn't possible to remove the messages in the middle, as I mentioned earlier this would be an alternative option. The green, circled stamina bar can be added underneath the life bar. All these marks help when you are a beginner, but within a certain period of time you know precisely how the game works and it then would very nice to make the game look better to enhance the playing experience. Another thing that has come to my attention are some invisible barriers around some buildings - e. g. the higher houses in Wa no Kuni. I get that barriers are important to limit the possibility of bugs and ram capacity - if there was anything you would invest time in when making a future ultimate version, I would add this to the list. The hud regarding issues are way more important though. + some ideas for a free mode and dlc characters:Pica (standard appearance: normal size without using the fruits ability - bigger size while power boost "stone giant" (could change Picas appeareance to a stone giant in size of almost as big as Kaidos and Big Moms) and maybe equally big or even bigger while performing special attacks)Free Mode- 10-20 possible scenarios- getting to choose your team mates- getting to choose the enemies- getting to choose the locationThat's it. That would be perfect.  So in conclusion - besides the hud aspect - One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is a fantastic game I never dreamed of being created. Played it for hours and hours already. I mean it - good job and thank you very much!Yours sincerely, Jerôme

_childDocuments_.review: For those looking to see if the game works or if it's a good port or just wanting to know what's different about this title, I'll be giving a quick review of features and functionality, not so much content.I'm reading a lot of other reviews talk about controllers not working, but I've not had any of this. I use a PS4 controller, no extra software installed. Worked up front with no additional issues. I cannot vouch for others, but this is my experience.While the game comes with a lot of graphical options for fine-tuning your experience, it looks as you'd expect. Graphics are not spectacular, but they are what they are. Even pushed to max, it's not a visually impressive game.As far as I can personally speak, the game runs very smoothly (60fps) with no hitches or anything as long as you hardware can push that. I can't imagine you'd need much, but it seems to be one of the better Warriors ports that we've seen. There are more options in the menus than I've ever seen before, so it seems they've finally modernized a little bit.Now, when it comes to gameplay, there are some very big changes for Musou fans. Firstly, the game still plays like you'd expect. Normal attacks mixed with Charge attacks to make unique combos. There are MANY more combos in this game than before, and now jumping in the middle of a combo will launch enemies into the air so you can continue fighting in the air. Because of this, there seems to be a lot more input options and ways to chain combos together.  Instead, there is now a skill palette system. You hold down RB/R1 to pull up 4 skills on the face buttons and you can use those whenever they are charged. They charge up by damaging enemies. Every character has their own skill tree that can unlock new combos and new skills that you can then slot into your character's skill palette. You can only have 4 active skills equipped at a time, so there are more skills than you'll need, offering for a lot of variation in what you can do between players. Each character also has an archetype now. Depending on that, your boost mode (called Full Force Burst) will provide different bonuses, such as faster traversal on the map or increased damage. Overall, it adds an attack speed boost to all characters. Each character has a skill tree, as I mentioned before, and there you can also find passive upgrades to damage, defense, stamina, and life. There's also one big skill tree that affects ALL characters, so you can choose to level up everyone or focus on a few. These trees are separate, so you can do both.These are all of the major changes I've encountered in the first two hours of play; I'm sure there are more. As you can imagine, the game does feel a little different from the typical Warriors experience (to me, anyway). It feels more like a brawler with a few Musou elements. I'm a little sad Musou attacks are gone, but the overall combat does feel a little bit more varied and deeper now because of the changes. It's also possible that greater attacks will be unlocked later that can make up for that lack of "musou attack" gravitas.So far, it's a recommend for One Piece fans, though it's probably not enough to bring in outside fans not already familiar, as the story also picks up in the middle of the One Piece story, so there's very little build up or background for any of the characters. Playing Pirate Warriors 3 before this one would be a better introduction to the game, and PW3 is also much more similar to the Dynasty Warriors formula.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay...I know, my game time and my review really don't match up. I'll concur. It was an easy game to get all achievements with so I just gave in. Another big appeal is cloud saves. One big reason why I cared to play it over the third again was because of that. For whatever reason it doesn't have remote play together despite it asking to press F2 on some pages for multiplayers. Bummer.I played on Steam Deck. The major problem it seems to have is that cutscenes from the main campaign have a memory leak type of effect on it. Watching too many cutscenes in a play session will freeze or hang your device in a way that renders the experience impossible unless you quit or reset the device. Playing missions in free mode alleviates the issue by a lot. As for the version of proton used. Proton experimental is the way to go. I think the main draw I have on the game is that I can't help but feel like the special attack changes have made the game feel more like meter management than actually doing attacks. dashing in between combos to skip attacks in the string doesn't happen, so doing strong finishers in combos requires you to follow through the combo the old fashioned way. And because both parameters for S ranking missions are on the lines of, kill fast, kill quick, there is less room for fancy combos and more incentive to plow the field as efficiently as possible. And in my opinion, it makes a lot of characters and moves lose appeal. Powerful attacks and power states are things I ended up favoring more than the combo extension moves that were free to use in Pirate Warriors 3.Basic combo structure feels more natural is something I can admit. Jumping in the middle of a combo to do a launcher is something I wouldn't mind having adapted to the regular series at all. A stamina bar being allowed to be chained and depleted completely is another thing I'm okay with. And the first tree being usable for every character does alleviate a lot of the neglect a lot of characters typically get if you prefer others. So in my opinion, these changes are good. I won't lie to you, One Piece Grand adventure was my first One Piece game, and it does bother me when so many characters in this series are seen but not playable. I had a hope in my stomach to play as Eneru and shock the entire battlefield with lightning ravens and pummeling everything to dust with Amal. I feel like after watching games like Warriors Orochi exist as well as Dynasty Warriors 9 that they could really add a lot of these characters easily, but may not want to because of a small amount of significance. Treasure mode honestly was more of a drag than it needed to be. And it wasn't because it was bad, but because it was only three scenarios, and each of them were extended by playing key missions in them. it felt more like a chore when the area you sought to complete expanded by 8 missions sometimes, as the differences between each are distinct, but on seemingly random stages. Nothing is wrong with this, but I really don't know why there was much of a need to only make 3  areas if it was pretty much only separated by difficulty. I feel other versions of this I have tried did a lot better. All in all it's an alright game. But I don't feel like the changes are worth losing a lot of the mechanics and appeal the game before it had. And the criteria for getting the best clear time leads to bad habits, like combing over peons, missing sub quests, ignoring strong foes and etc. So it kind of steps on its own toes when it comes to content, and the playstyle they encourage. I ended up favoring Ace and blazing through the game because his attacks were fast and deliberate, and his dash was very effective at rushing everywhere I needed to be. Get it if you must, but if you don't need the latest, there are better titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Please note, I have not played any previous Pirate Warriors titles, but have greatly enjoyed Dynasty Warriors since PS2.With that said, One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is a far cry from being a decent Warriors game and I am increasingly disappointed that I didn't refund when I had the chance. This game is definitely more for fans of One Piece then Warriors.The greatest sin of this game is the most vile any piece of entertainment can commit, and that is being boring. The game play relies entirely on repeatedly pommeling the same clone enemies over and over. But that isn't atypical of a warriors title. The real problem is with officer fights. They are absolutely terribly done and expectantly numerous, some levels only consisting of the player fighting an officer. Not only is EVERY SINGLE officer an absolutely tank that does basically nothing while you pummel them for several minutes straight but, to add to this tedium, EVERY SINGLE officer has magic shields that make them invincible until you bring them down, with, of course, more pummeling. Even then, you do so little damage that you're just constantly spamming the same attacks for minutes on end. Then, TO TOP IT ALL OFF, invincibility shields regenerate, causing the player to have to continue their ceaseless pummeling to bring them down once more to chip off another embarrassingly small bit of the enemies actual health bar.This might sound like a small gripe to the uninitiated, but know that every map requires the defeat of numerous officers, sometimes over a dozen and each and every one requires the same exact treatment. It never changes. It was exceptionally lazy on the part of the developers and this constant throughout the game has completely killed what interest I had in the series.While not terribly familiar with the One Piece story, I get the feeling that a GREAT deal is skipped over during the 'story mode' leading to confusion and a disinterest in that as well. Further, the character selection remains very limited, despite other characters being present and playable in other modes, which I found not only stifling but baffling.Overall, a very disappointing experience and complete waste of time and money in my opinion. Even on a significant sale, I would not recommend this to anyone I respect.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game for One Piece fans, but I'd give it a mixed review.It is a good game, but I think there's nothing really that stands out.I bought this game out of hype for One Piece Odyssey and because it was really cheap. I had fun paying it, but I felt like I didn't enjoy it as much as intended due to not really being into One Piece in a very long time.Gameplay is smooth and fast. It's the classic Musou formula mixed with the One Piece aesthetic and characters.You can choose between a few selection of characters, but I felt like most of the missions were restricted to the same characters. Each of them plays differently and have different set of skills that can be customized, giving the game an extra layer of replayability.The combat felt a bit repetitive and lacks depth. Almost everything from the enemy types, objectives and maps looked very similar and the camera is terrible, especially when it's locked to an enemy. In Free Mode and Treasure Mode, it's possible to play as any character you've unlocked and keep farming coins/money to get stronger.The story was weird and I don't think it was interesting enough. The game is definitely for One Piece fans who already know all the characters and have already watched the anime episodes since the game basically skips almost everything related to the story and covers them incredibly quickly in some narrated cutscenes.I like One Piece but I don't consider myself a big fan of the anime and I haven't watched the anime completely, so I felt I didn't have as much fun as intended playing the campaign.It takes about 14 hours to beat the main campaign mode.The DLC characters from the Deluxe Edition were wasted in my opinion. They are added basically just for the grind in Free Mode. There is no additional story content or new missions for them, so if you're planning on getting the DLC, it's not really worth it. Get the Deluxe Edition only if the difference in price from the standard edition is minimal.About the PC Port, it runs really well at 1440p 60fps Max on a RTX 2060 Super. Very smooth frame rate without any drops or stutters. Zero issues during my entire playthrough.If you're a big One Piece fan, this game is quite fun and recommended. The bad aspects can be easily overlooked since you'll be having a lot of fun playing with your favorite characters in 3D action.But, if you like One Piece, but don't consider yourself that much of a big fan of the series, you might have to think before buying this game because it's pretty average. The combat is not as good as other Musou titles, and the story mode is not that good. On sale, yes, it's worth a try. Get it for Nami and Robin big plot.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Musou game, this is a pretty good one. It's in the modern Musou style, where special moves aren't tied to your combo string but have dedicated buttons, though the combos themselves can also be pretty flashy. The gameplay is pretty fun in general. The may story feels shorter than the Pirate Warriors 3 and the retelling of the One Piece story is severely abridged - the missions start at Alabasta, skip from it to Water 7/Enies Lobby from there to Sabaodi/Marineford and after time skip it skips the Fishman Island, Punk Hazard and Zoa, you only get little text summaries of what happened. So if you wanted to feel nostalgic about the Romance Dawn and such, Pirate Warriors 3 is a better option. It also has a funny "game original" take on the Wano Arc because the game came out when it was just getting going, so they made up their own version of how it could go which is kinda fun in its own way, but - no King, no Queen, Yamato is DLC.The shortness of the main story mode (the "Dramatic Log") is somewhat covered for by the extra stages of the "Treasure Log". There are a lot of them and they are fun to constantly switch characters, but that runs into one notable issue I have with the game.If you're going to play missions with the higher recommended level while constantly switching characters, you'll quickly run into the need to grind. Money is easy to grind, tokes are harder, but once the recommended level goes above 10-12, leveling characters you didn't use before starts being harder. And when to get to the highest level missions, they aren't any harder by design, but the enemy stats get jacked. The Treasure Logs are still fine to clear, though you may need to focus on a few good characters rather than everyone. You can totally pull it off with having stats a point or two below the recommended level. But the two hardest levels of the Roger DLC are different. Fully maxed out Roger maps will get you stat levels of 22-23, and with recommended levels of 29 and 31 respectively it means a couple of big hits will kill you. Maybe if you grind for Souls you can get your stats higher, but that's the line for me - gridning for souls would change the grind from soemthing I don't always like to an actual issue with the game. So I just cheesed those levels with Roger's long range Y attack.But all in all, the game is fun. If you like One Piece and/or Musou, check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until I had completed the game's final mission (in its free-play mode) before writing a review, and I can now say without any doubt that this is by far my favourite Pirate Warriors game (and I was extremely fond of the earlier ones).To get the cons out of the way, it misses out a handful of characters from the earlier games because it does not cover their arcs in the main story mode. Actually, that's the only con I can think of...Oh, actually, the game's final arc, in Wano is fun because it's pretty wacky, but it's not a particularly good story.But as for pros, it makes up for those missing characters with some 15 or more different ones, which can be SO much fun to play as! It's so satisfying playing as each of Big Mom's Sweet Three, or each of Sanji's brothers (whose play-styles are varied in the game - I may not remember which name belongs to who, but I certainly remember their different moves!) Also, Katukiri is a boss. And each of the Worst Generation. Secondly, and SUPER random, but I thoroughly enjoy the new "jumping" mechanic, and it really does make it feel much more like the One Piece of the manga/anime.Also, the giants really do FEEL like giants, and they are absolute power-houses in the game: Kaido, Big Mom, Jack, Sengoku and Whitebeard all feel physically imposing when you come up against them in a random match, and their strength corresponds with that, you have to employ a lot more skill when dealing with them.A lot of people complain about the game not being very "long", but they only seem to be addressing the main storyline. At nearly fifty hours I still haven't even played all of the missions (the main story took me around 18 hours). What is also fun in the main story is that you get to pick very different characters (so not merely the straw hats, but others who were involved in the events, like playing as Ace or Whitebeard at the battle of Marineford), which is a heap of fun. Of course, you get the chance to go back and play every level with anyone you want, but these were especially touching.With so many characters and such good gameplay, I would strongly recommend the game, whether you like One Piece (or Koei games) or not.9/10. Only because there isn't a whole lot more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the newest in the series and many gameplay improvements compared to the last game. Having been following the series from the first game I gotta say this edition has the most 'immerson' in terms of story battles, in that there are multiple maps (typically 5~7) per arc. Progressing through the Onepiece storyline is more akin to the manga/anime experience and in-depth with the major highlights of each arc. Combat is slightly different with 4 assigned skills with the shift key and combos that are either longer and activated mid-air for some aerial characters. I do have to make the point that quite a few character has lost a bit of mobility compared to OPPW3, so AOE and large swiping attacks are less prevalent in this game. Also, characters with special forms like luffy will have a complete different set of skills and combo when activated. Gameplay for the campaign is roughly 15 hours as many said, and the 'dream log' end game content in this game is a similarly progressive form of individual levels, with increasing character stat requirements. This, I comment, feels less diverse and exploratory than OPPW3, the missions are more or less random and some players may lose interest.Having said all that I still believe it is worthwhile to invest IF you are a hardcore One Piece fan and is willing to support the developer's OP related franchise. However, if you are new to the anime/manga or this type of BN musou game in general I'd recommend the wait for a sale. This game does contain major spoilers and a custom Wano arc ending.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4 is an action-packed musou game with a huge roster of characters from the One Piece universe to play as. The game's colorful and vibrant visuals capture the essence of the One Piece anime and manga, making it a treat for fans of the series.The game's combat mechanics are easy to pick up and play, offering exciting and satisfying gameplay. The cooperative multiplayer mode also allows players to team up and take on challenges together.However, the game can feel repetitive after extended play sessions, with some players finding the camera angles and movement to be disorienting and difficult to control. The story mode can also be short and lack depth compared to other musou games, leaving players wanting more.Furthermore, some players may find the lack of challenge in the game to be disappointing, with the game feeling too easy. The music and sound design can also feel repetitive and lacking in variety, detracting from the overall experience. The game's story mode is also not fully voice acted, which can be a drawback for players looking for a fully immersive experience.Despite these drawbacks, One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4 is a great choice for fans of the One Piece series, offering great fan service and faithfully recreating many iconic moments and locations. However, for players looking for innovation and new features compared to previous Pirate Warriors games, the game may feel lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: A few years ago, I mostly enjoyed playing through the predecessor of One Piece: Pirate Warriors 4 (PW4). However, the Steam port had some bugs which crashed the game. It was possible to get around them, but I'd admit that it tarnished an experience I otherwise enjoyed. Having played a few of the Dynasty Warriors games since then, I'm curious whether this is the best Warriors game.   My primary focus is on the unique mechanics of PW4 instead of the ones consistent to the Warriors style games. First of all, leveling up is very different from most games. Using character coins and money, you purchase upgrades from skill trees. They're presented as connected islands, but its merely a cosmetic choice. There's one that applies to every character, which is a good way to raise your bare minimum. Since every character has two skill trees, full of skills, attack combos, and stat increases, it will be a grind to level them up, even though its in an unorthodox way. If you buy the character DLC, the overall expense for maxing everyone out would be egregious. Combat was another area that had some interesting changes. Each character is categorized into one of four types: power, technique, speed, and sky. Power characters are as direct as you'd expect, smashing into opponents. Usopp is a good example for technique, as he makes use of tools and gadgets to fight. Speed and sky seem similar to me, although with how sky characters remain in the air so long, I found them more interesting than the grounded version. Rocking the four motif, replacing a single powered-up attack, each character can equip four to use in battle, and can also unlock more from their island. Even if you don't love some of their original options, you'll likely find a good combination after earning more of them.  When first booting up PW4 it didn't recognize my controller. However, after right clicking on the game from my library and going to Properties, I was able to configure my Steam settings. Making it recognize my Xbox controller fixed things up immediately, and may also reduce problems I've had with other new titles. After this was taken care of, I didn't have any further issues with the controls, as they handled like other games from the series.  Due to how many characters and arcs the series has, instead of going through many of the smaller sections like the previous entry, it touches on only some of the more involved arcs. For instance, none of the enemies prior to Crocodile are covered at the start of Dramatic Log, so they've skipped several chapters from the onset. Since the Treasure Log starts off in the East Blue, I thought it might skim over situations from earlier in the anime, but they're completely random nonsense. As an example, settling a fight between Zoro and Sanji. Even though it'd have been redundant to cover everything from the beginning like the previous entry, I find this abridged version a less than thrilling replacement.  Something that diminishes some of the issue KT games has had in its visuals is the anime aesthetic. Instead of trying to recreate more realistic or true-to-life forms and expressions, the characters and people in PW4 are able to lean into simpler designs. I'm not trying to diss One Piece, but there's a substantial difference trying to draw still-life images compared to an anime character. Regardless, although some characters' facial expressions can look a little off, they're much better than the outright ugly faces I saw in Dynasty Warriors 8. Another example where this helped was character scaling, as it doesn't seem so significant if enemies don't look quite right when much smaller or larger than you.  Listening to the music during the gameplay, none of them sounded like songs from the anime. A few of them were at least reminiscent, but only ones that'd play during unimportant moments of navigating the game, like the title screen. Otherwise, I'm pretty sure they were just generic tracks. I don't know all the issues surrounding licensing, yet it seems like a waste to not make use of the entire IP if you're going to pay for the rights anyways. Apparently, there's a song pack DLC that includes some of those songs, but it's insultingly overpriced for what you pay for. 🌟 Even though the gameplay isn't a drastic departure from the series, new mechanics give it a bit of vibrancy. 🌟 Some characters change substantially as you upgrade them. ❌ Because so much of the story is skipped over, I didn't find it worthwhile to watch all the cutscenes. Why watch a diluted, altered version? Plus, they drug story events out across several stages. I can only rescue Ace from the marines so many times. ❌ There's a significant amount of stages in the Treasure Log. However, they're not that engaging with how short and random they are. 🔍 Several characters have an equipable skill that can be unlocked on their first treasure map. They're represented by a sun icon, and are worth investing into. I found Sabo's, Nami's, and Bartolomeo's to be especially valuable for grinding. 🔍 If your health gets low, dart away and look for a treasure chest. They often have large healing items inside, and are best saved for emergencies. On harder stages, you may want to equip a skill that heals you.🔍 Your special moves fill up rapidly, so don't be stingy with them.  Having earned all the achievements, I haven't found much reason in playing as many of the characters, particularly the underwhelming or weak ones. In some ways, I found many of them lackluster, as their combos weren't very good. Once you clear the main story mode, all that's left are a plethora of gimmicky stages, IE the Treasure Logs. Beating them is necessary to earn special coins to unlock character skills, which is how you'll strengthen your characters. However, as you grind and level them up, what would you do with them at that point? Keep clearing side levels without a more robust or engaging mode to hold your interest, primarily because you need so many coins to pay for level-ups? Maybe I've just gotten a bit burned out on these games, but lately I've not been seeing the appeal in playing them for dozens, let alone hundreds, of hours. Frankly, I found the previous entry had a more compelling reason for playing it so long, even if new mechanics make this one a bit novel. PW3 was recently on sale for around $3 on Fanatical, which is a great price for its potential playtime. Considering I'd rather play the game that occasionally crashed, I can't recommend getting PW4. Instead, I stand behind the 3rd one.

_childDocuments_.review: A super fun game for One Piece fans. The gameplay is easy to understand and you don't have to memorize long combos. It's really satisfying to beat up hundreds of enemies, and see your favorite characters in action. In the Dramatic Log, there's a chapter for most important arcs. I'm a little bummed that there isn't Punk Hazard though lol. There's also the Treasure Log, which is fun to collect berries and coins from. Characters feel unique from one another, so if one character doesn't fit your play style you can always play from the many other characters that might.There are some things that make the game frustrating, like the map designs. It's really easy to get lost, and sometimes I find myself running back and forth trying to find where I'm supposed to go. With how spread out your allies can be sometimes, it's hard to run and help them if they're struggling. There's a lot going on at once, which can be hard to manage. Split-screen co-op is really hard to focus on and can be easy to miss sub-missions. You can pause the game to view things like your missions and allies in more detail, but it's really annoying to keep having to pause the game to see what's going on. The pause menu is easy to navigate though, so it's not a huge pain.Overall though, I would recommend this game to other One Piece fans. It's certainly enjoyable!
