_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time playing a musou game. I came in with low expectations thinking I would just be mashing buttons and enjoying the One Piece aesthetic and this is the exact experience that I received, but the gameplay is a bit above what I expected. Unlocking characters, learning their quirks, and leveling them up to take to high level logs is a decent enough gameplay loop to keep you invested for at least a few dozen hours. If you like One Piece, beating the ever-loving **** out of stuff, and doing cool flashy combos, then there's quite a bit here for you. My only complaints are the price, some slightly awkward mechanics (like red burst being seemingly random at times and flying not having any vertical movement options outside of a locked-on dash), and the lack of a few key characters that have no excuse not being in the game (where's Kuma, come on!) Even with these flaws, at sale price, there's enough fun in this game that's worth looking into for all caught-up One Piece fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I’ve played for a little more than three hours so here are some of my honest first impressions of Pirate Warriors 4:The combat is A LOT faster than PW3. It takes some getting used to in the beginning but once you get it it’s really satisfying. The combat animations are all really good and the different skills and classes for each character make them all feel unique. Lots of stage destruction and character voices. All your allies talk a lot during combat which makes the whole thing feel alive (For example Sanji names all his attacks which is really cool). Ariel combat is a nice touch too and extending combos into them is easy. I played on hard mode and I gotta say it’s far more challenging than PW3. If you’re up for the challenge I recommend it.Like I said the combat is fast paced so that meant that the camera was super fast too. Imo the camera was way too sensitive but luckily there’s options to tone it down. The environments are very detailed and beautiful and the graphics in general are a huge improvement over the last game. Not to mention the roster is completely revamped and everyone has a different fresh moveset than before. The music is amazing as well.Now for the negatives: The camera itself is not the best. When running from place to place it always forces you to slightly look downwards for some reason which is annoying at times but you get used to it. When you lock the camera onto a target, I’ll be frank, it’s not good. Due to the far field of view, when you get up close to your enemy, 80% of the time the camera won’t be focusing on them. The animations during dialogue scenes are not good. Sometimes the mouth movements don’t fit the tone or expressions of the characters at all. Also, the crew from what I’ve experience in the Alabasta arc are all stuck in there East Blue costumes. Although there are small iterations like the bandaged arms and Mr. Prince but it would’ve been far more appropriate to have their proper attires. Some cutscenes are also plainly copy pasted from the previous game. Though, the new rendered animations they made are really good.These are my thoughts for now. I still think the gameplay is the core element of the game and I just love playing as One Piece characters in general so I’m still having a blast playing. If you’d ask me, I’d recommend it but that might just be my One Piece biased talking so I tried to be as honest as possible. Whether you decide to buy it or not is up to you but I hope you enjoy it if you do. PS: I don’t know if this mini review came off as more negative than positive but let me say that the positives are far more impactful than the negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually really fun, if you like Warrior style games where you beat up crowds of enemies. It does a somewhat decent job at telling the story of One Piece, even though it glosses over a lot of major arcs like Arlong Park arc, Thriller Bark arc, etc with recaps instead. But I honestly liked the stage design, such as Whole Cake Island, which became a favorite with it's aesthetic. But if you want a full One Piece experience, I don't recommend this game, watch the really long anime or read the manga! Especially because it does it's own take on the Wano arc and this game came out in 2020, the anime is still tackling the Wano arc right now and it's closer to the end of it, then it was in 2020.But the only negative thing I can think of is the lack of costumes. Like half of the Straw Hats that aren't Luffy, Zoro, Usopp, and Sanji don't have their pre-timeskip designs, a good example is Robin, who appears in the story as Ms All Sunday and then appears in her Enies Lobby outfit after the arc, she didn't become playable until you reach the timeskip portion of the game, so her pre-timeskip outfits are locked to NPC only, which sucks, but you can also view said outfits in Glossary, which makes me scratch my head at that choice to not make them playable. But the game needs more costumes for characters in general, because Luffy just got all of them and bunch of characters like the costume-less Straw Hats deserve the love. Otherwise, the game is fun and It's a good experience for me at least! I do recommend if you like both franchises and you just want to dip your toes into them.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 so far has been an amazing sequel in the series with very minimal flaws.  To start off as with the track record of previous PW games, the roster got beefed up, and while there were a few characters from PW3 who were cut, the games base roster is bigger than any previous installments and has a character pass which will be adding 9 more characters total to the roster.  As far as character variety goes, this game has it.Campaign Review:  The main campaign of the game is one of the things I see that is most upsetting to people, and understandably so.  In PW4, a few arcs have been cut, which means you aren't getting the entire experience of One Piece, however the fact that each arc has a few missions instead of each arc BEING a mission or 2, makes them more worthwhile to take home.  As far as length of the campaign, it still is something to sink time in to and feels very rewarding.Treasure Log:  The Treasure Log is PW4's post game option which consists of multiple, non canon scenarios that add interesting team ups and rivalries.  Treasure Log is where you will be spending most of the time in the game for it's load of missions as well as character grinding purposes, missions also get progressively harder as you go through the three tiers (East Blue, Grand Line and New World).  It is a very fulfilling and good time killing post game to sink into .Overall:  An absolutely BEAUTIFUL game, with amazing graphics, fluent combo structures with the addition of air combat and being able to replace skills and form changes, I feel Pirate Warriors 4 takes the cake on being the best game in the series.  Absolutely would recommend, Pirate Warriors 4 is worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: PW4 is a fun musou game crippled by a couple bizarre design flaws. It has engaging combat and does a good job at making its diverse cast feel very distinct from one another, but lacks long term replayability because there is no incentive to grind, or mechanism to track grinding.Due to how grades are set permanently at the first stage clear, there's no incentive to re-do stages on different characters and difficulties to grind for the S. And due to how character progression works, you can power a character up all the way without having played them at all. These design flaws make the content in the game feel even more limited, and work against its strength of character diversity. It's unfortunate that Bandai neglected to at least give us a statistics page where we could see our kills etc by character; that alone would go a long way towards making it feel like you're accomplishing something when clearing stages you've already completed. As it is, it feels like the game wants me to stop playing after I've finished all the content once. DLC characters seem cool but don't address this issue or add any replayability. Still, it's at least 40 hours of solid fun and the combat really is well done. It could have been great, but it's still good. Highly recommended for One Piece fans.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PIECE: PIRATE WARRIORS 4

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Pirate Warriors 4 is an excellent game for fans of One Piece, and I count myself among that fanbase, but let's set that aside. As a Warriors game, it's pretty good and probably one of the best looking and most streamlined ones I've played. I'll admit, I haven't played a Warriors game in so long, with my personal favorite being Dynasty Warriors 4 with the Extreme Legends expansion pack on the PlayStation 2. But it's good to see this particular genre extending to various franchises, such as One Piece and even Legend of Zelda.If you're expecting dynamic gameplay, you're looking at the wrong game. However, the monotonous action is GREATLY alleviated by the massive roster of characters! Each one plays completely different than the last, and all have varied combos that keep the combat fresh despite the repetitious fighting. These characters are split into four types: Power, Speed, Technique, and Sky. Power is straightforward, focusing on outward brawling and jumping into the fray with powerful combos. Speed's definitely about dashing about using the "power dash", unleashing quick combos. Technique is quite hard for me to get used to, focusing a lot on abilities that lay traps or inflict status effects, with normal attacks not being as effective as the combos and abilities ( which allow you to bring groups of enemies closer to you ). Sky does what it says on the box, it's all about air combos and flying from enemy to enemy unleashing attacks, with much less focus on ground combos. It's really fun collecting characters, leveling up their strength, and mastering their capabilities. This is a One Piece fan's dream come true, because anyone who's anyone is here! From my personal favorite Trafalgar Law, to complete badass powerhouses such as Whitebeard, you can't go wrong with the roster.Like any other Warriors game, the gameplay is exactly as you expect. Missions pit different forces against each other in fairly diverse locales, and different events happen to throw variety into the mix. It's repetitive, but cozy and relaxing, with some tense moments. Unlike the Warriors games I'm used to, you can't just defeat every "officer" and suddenly win. There is some level of strategy at play, and it's up to you to choose whether an optional objective is more important or to go rescue an allied officer in trouble. Allied officers can actually win fights, and don't always need babysitting, depending on what mission you play and on what difficulty. This is probably one of the few Warriors games where it feels like you absolutely need everyone in order to win, and you aren't just a powerhouse who can win the entire battle on your own, especially on hard mode where you need every ally you can get. It's a legit challenge, and I'm pleased that it ditched the stupid systems of the past. Dynasty Warriors 4 was so good, but it often felt too easy to win once you closed every reinforcement gate and defeated every single optional officer to lower enemy morale. There is no morale system in Pirate Warriors 4, meaning that victory is about achieving objectives or striking specific targets rather than blowing away every enemy officer.I'm very impressed with the amount of love and content put into this game. You can tell that the developers love One Piece, including all of the most iconic moments in the "Dramatic Log" story mode which acts as your campaign. I'm often left wondering "WHO THE HELL ARE THESE PEOPLE?!" when I look at these generic pirate armies allied with Luffy and his comrades, but the story does a fantastic job recapping the anime for you without you needing to even watch ( or rewatch ) the dauntingly huge anime. Well, for the most part. Other modes including "Treasure Log", which is a fantastic mode featuring all sorts of fun missions. These missions act as alternate reality "What if THIS happened..." scenarios. They are an excellent way to earn coins ( a fun currency featuring little images on them ) and Berries ( in game currency ) to level up your characters outside of the main Dramatic Log. "Free Log" on the other hand allows you to play any mission with whoever you like, from what I can tell. Dramatic Log is very restrictive with who you can play as per mission, after all.The amount of content will keep you coming back for more, and wanting to collect everything, including leveling up the quite enjoyable "Growth Map" progression system for each character. There's a Growth Map that powers all characters up, and then there's personal unique Growth Maps for individual characters. This system is fun because each stat, ability, or skill is represented by tiny little islands upon an ocean. I found this a really cute and thematic progression system, with some abilities being more meaningful rather than straight power increases. Such as upgrades that grant new combos, and entirely new skills. I mean, I enjoy straight power increases, but it's sometimes hard to tell when I'm playing on Hard mode! Believe me, that difficulty mode will kick your ass! You're going to need every point of health and attack power you can get!What else is there to say? Well, I like the music sometimes and it sounds very One Piece, and other times it sounds like royalty free tunes. The voice acting is good if set to Japanese with English subtitles, which is what the game appears to be at by default anyway. Is it me, or is EVERYONE here? And I mean every Japanese voice actor for One Piece? Other than sounds, I wish the combat was more satisfying and chunky, when I slash at my enemies with Zoro it doesn't really sound enough like I'm really CUTTING into some fools. This problem persists for many characters, but luckily it helps that buildings or objects get destroyed in satisfying ways as you rampage around. I'd still say that Dynasty Warriors 4 has the most satisfying combat, with meaty metallic weapon sounds as they land on your enemies. It's a trivial thing, yes, but it often feels like the hits aren't as satisfying as they could be ( in Pirate Warriors 4 ). Maybe it's because they are often overpowered by other sounds, and even the music? As for the visuals, they are pretty good looking for a genre that is often ugly as sin and low fidelity. Unfortunately, you do get plenty of muddy textures, and low polygon details sometimes. But the characters themselves look straight out of the anime, for the most part. I'm not going to complain when the Warriors franchise doesn't deliver good visuals most of the time, I welcome these colorful and decent graphics!Well, that's all I have to say. If you're a One Piece fan, this game is an absolute must!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun button-mashy musou beat-em-up. I'm a big One Piece fan, have played a ton of the previous 3 games, and while I'm not sure after 25ish hours where I'd rate PW4 across the "Warriors" franchise, it's still a solid (yet unremarkable) entry.---POSITIVES: The world of One Piece is best suited for these types of games considering the wide range of abilities and powers, and this entry does an excellent job of highlighting just how unique each character is. The added jumping, character sizes (giants), environment destruction, and aerial types are all wonderful new additions to the gameplay, and the cast itself is large and varied. In particular, the new / DLC characters (still waiting on the final pack) are all a LOT of fun - highlights for me would be Smoothie (DLC), Cracker (DLC), Kid, Killer (DLC), Hawkins, Drake (DLC), and Carrot...+ there are many others I haven't had the time to try just yet, and a lot of tweaks for the recurring characters. Besides the cast, certain story arcs do a good job of capturing moments and characters that previous entries have skipped over, and similar to the other games we have what are basically Story, Free, and Mission modes all present and accounted for.NEGATIVES: Even with the large cast, it's a shame that some of the previously playable characters were excluded (Garp, Enel, Perona, Magellan, Gecko Moria, and Caesar). However, considering the Skypiea, Thriller Bark, Impel Dawn, and Punk Hazard arcs are all missing, it makes sense. Speaking of which...unfortunate that those and so many other arcs are gone! In PW4 you'll find Alabasta, Enies Lobby, "Summit War" (few missions each for Sabaody & Marineford), Dressrosa, Whole Cake, and an original take on Wano. Problem is that a lot of the level-designs are reused throughout each arc, and aren't entirely interesting to begin with.Beyond that, I really wish Koei Tecmo would standardize a few quality of life things across their games, mainly...(1) warp points throughout stages, (2) the ability to switch between characters during missions, and (3) leveling-up / expanded RPG-light systems - any one of these would have made a HUGE difference.Character progression for this entry is based entirely on upgrading "maps" (think skill trees), using coins you find during missions to enhance stats and skills. What's frustrating is the balance between coins, and constantly finding you lack a specific one that just about every single upgrade requires in abundance. This leads to a few choice characters you typically focus investing in being ridiculously overpowered, while the other 30+ are completely underleveled compared to where you might be in the game. To be fair, these games ARE all about grinding...but, this one damn coin has stopped me from testing out and having fun with other characters, and in-turn I generally end up defaulting to a certain handful while slowly trying to push the rest up bit by bit.Unlockables and customization...? Eek. You'll have ~80% of the cast by the time you get through the main story, and the rest within a few more hours. Sadly, most of them don't have additional costumes or even color swaps. Luffy gets a costume for each arc, the rest of the Straw Hats MAYBE have a New World and Wano set (some don't), while the other 30+ stay in their basic garb. No equipment or levels either, as mentioned above it's really just the coins for improving your base stats. There is a Gallery with general story bits, a character viewer, music player, and cutscene library, but everything there is about as standard as you can get.Localization unfortunately feels very dull, lifeless, and "off", which, considering the source material and work for the english anime / manga is a huge shame. I imagine most people picking this up are doing so solely for the gameplay, but still would have been nice to see a bit more time and focus on these aspects. Music as well, I honestly couldn't tell you if this one had any unique tracks from the other games - it's complete background noise, ready your podcasts.Finally, with the DLC / Season Pass, you're only getting the characters. There's no themed levels or new stages that give them a chance to shine, they're basically just another row on the character select screen added from the get-go. Don't hold-off on using them thinking you may unlock extra content or special locations, there isn't anything that's added to the main modes.---All in all...if you've played a previous Pirate Warriors game, you should know what you're in for. If you haven't but enjoy other Warriors / Musou-style games, you'll most likely have a blast (all the better if you're familiar with the One Piece world), and if you flat-out don't like the "genre" there's nothing here that will change your mind - it plays things extremely safe.Fingers-crossed Koei Tecmo and Bandai Namco will take their time with the inevitable PW5 and go all-out, I'm still enjoying these overall but wondering if I should've skipped this entry after playing a lot of PW3 during its release. PW4 doesn't feel as fresh as I would have liked, but it's still some good mindless fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to One Piece fans, as it has that sensation; you fight the masses, you fight the bosses, you have the moves, you talk the talk and you walk the walk. The graphics style is niche; clay-realism with black anime-esque outlines. Gorgeous!But if we turn our eyes away from Nami's chest area, I would not recommend this game in general because:- While they updated skill mechanics and unlockables via the really creative islands, the game is just a pure downgrade of PW3.- Graphics are nicer than the first PC PW3 game but I miss that comic-style cutscene direction. I really thought they knew they had something good there and would build upon it.- Returning to the cut argument, while you have a lot of playable characters with a lot of specific things to do to unlock it all, PW3's content of characters and maps was just far more magical.- They know fully well they could sell the One Piece story to us a thousand times over yet they decided to release a high priced game to us that is basically just a technical preview of what the previous version could have been if they tried.- One Piece Pirate Warriors 5 needs to learn from these mistakes, because the Musou genre is perfect for the world. You need to feel OP against the masses and only bosses should be a challenge, it digs that, it just needs balance. It also needs far more depth, JRPG depth, food, training mechanics, fishing, exploration, Straw Hat Fleet mechanics, I could come up with more and more and it would all still fall into place with this story-telling Warriors-like game.All in all... If you want a PC re-sensation of One Piece, play Pirate Warriors 3 rather. It has issues in regards to high fps, resolution and controler support but they can be fixed. It's giant in comparison to this 4th entry, sadly or rather in the perspective of that game, luckily, you'll have the awesome Arlong moments and Fishman Island story, more Sanji and Zoro, the important parts! ... a ton more of the very important story details in short. Games will always flop if the next entry isn't an expansion, developers please, try to finally understand this fact. We've had enough paint thrown over our eyes. Something as big as One Piece deserves respect from all of us. Never cut; only expand! Take the good you had going, remove the bad and tedious, come up with new streamlined ideas. Make it a 250gb game, I'll happily download it. Just gimme the perfect One Piece Video Game experience in the next entry, please, this genre is *made* for this; all it truly needs is clever balance and more of everything.

_childDocuments_.review: It's another musou game.If you're into that genre, then this is a Good One, and you should check it out. If you're interested in One Piece, you should also check it out!Honestly, this one plays a lot better than past entries in the series. They have really nailed the feeling of being in a sort of action shonen series fight. Boosting after enemies or to avoid attacks feels great, it's easy to use different special attacks and abilities, all the characters feel totally unique, it's just great all around. The RPG systems are interesting, you have like a whole bunch of skill trees to fill out. One for ALL characters, so new unlocks don't start out weak, and then multiple for each character. And they're not just giving 3% increased damage or whatever, they give whole new combat abilities and skills that really change the way the character plays. It's great.I only have two quibbles with this game:- It doesn't cover as much of the story of One Piece as the last one. But, this feels totally fair, as One Piece is an absolutely absurd amount of story to cover.- They replaced the island-hopping mode from OPPW3 with just a list of maps to go through, which doesn't feel as fun, even though it's more convenient overall.That's it! Otherwise, it's real good.

_childDocuments_.review: (Edit: I highly suggest you read the WHOLE review before judging off of recommended.)great game, dialogue scenes look kinda ugly but gameplay is really nice, fun and addicting.Edit after another 20 hours: The game is really good if you only consider the gameplay. I assume only one piece fans will consider this but I want to highlight that you should ONLY consider purchasing if you have watched/read One Piece. Originally I said the dialogue scenes look kinda ugly, this is still true but they are also executed worse as you progress through the game. Iconic quotes are changed, 5 minute scenes are rushed into 2 seconds, characters no longer exist (resulting in scenes being changed like Flampe's needle being shot by a chess guard or the scene not existing at all - King Riku is not in this game, so looking back Dressrosa has a very vague ending.)To contrast from this, considering the gameplay itself I've really enjoyed this. This is potentially my favourite Hack & Slash game.Edit after finishing Wano arc: It had a nice start but goes downhill. It was really interesting to play through the arc at the start due to it being non canon and not knowing what will happen, and the start does bring some hype with returning characters. However it feels rushed, short and doesn't feel that much thought has been put into it. This arc is joint shortest levels of any arc along with Alabasta for 5 levels, with the remaining few arcs having 6 (Enies, Marineford, Saboady) and WCI having 7. Mid arc feels repetitive and confusing, the levels end up just being fight the same Kaido/Big Mam pirates over and over until the final boss fight (which was a walk in the park, he didn't really attack you at all.) This leaves an unsatisfying ending, where Wano is free but no luxurious celebration occurs, just a normal, generic banquet outdoors. Alongside this, the ending does not feel amazing as the only Kozuki present are Momonuske and Kinemon.I currently have this remaining at reccomended as throughout the game, majorly the gameplay has been amazing and given me the most joy out of a Hack and Slash game. However, this recommendation depends on if you are willing to only judge the game through its gameplay and if the game is on a large sale (I picked this up for about £15.99, no more should be payed.)

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this is my first pirate warriors game, but not my first warriors game.As a one piece fan, I love this game and its portrayal of these beloved characters. The abilities are a great way to encapsulate one piece attacks and transformations flow smoothly into combat with great effect. But, this game is lacking in one way compared to the warriors games I remember from my childhood. A campaign map where I can conquer territory while fighting other commanders throughout the land. Game modes like this were the reason i got so hooked on games like samurai warriors back in the day. Unfortunately, due to the absence of this mode, the game lacks incentive to play the next level. Because I don't have that sense of progressing a campaign to eventually control this land, playing the next level inevitably begins to feel like a grind. Additionally, without this incentive, the low mission variety begins to tax even more, since most missions boil down to beat up the enemies, literally in terms of mission objective. If you enjoy slaughtering hordes of foes this is alleviated, but still an issue none the less. Despite all this, I would still recommend this game, at least to certain people. I would say that, in general, one piece fans will enjoy this game, and warriors fans may like it for the new abilities mechanics. Honestly, a conquest type mode would make this game perfect and I would pay for dlc to add that. Regardless, this game will still be my go to for a quick one piece fix. If you read this far, thanks for hearing me out and lets hope bandai adds more than just chars.

_childDocuments_.review: Online could be better, it's Abit Lacking, Could do with a Lobby system and perhaps letting folks just continue through with Friends as you would other games, but overall the Fighting system has a nice upgrade compared to the third game, the Verticality of movement is a great change and the Amount of customizable moves is a neat addition. The Story is a bit lack luster though, with cutting out major plot points, and some characters don't even have that many Voice lines or Available movement options. I can understand cutting back on things for time and not having the material to work with, but it was a better opportunity to just re due the third game, with this engine and landscapes, and Play the same story, with the Full New world arc up to [SPOILERS] instead of rushing through 'SOME' of the main plot points. Cutting out Sky Island and Thriller bark makes Robin and Brook's segments Seem really rushed and out of place when your supposed to care for them.If the game was supposed to be an introduction to the series it fails hard with how the story is told, and adding some Characters that are towards the end of the Games story in as early as The First mission/Thing you do is a REALLY bad move story wise...Not to mention cutting out Half the character roster of the main characters just cause they didn't want to fix/finish their Previous game incarnations? Franky, Robin, Chopper, and Brook aren't playable till half way through the game and most of them are with the crew at the first level. They use their moves from the third game, they have their costumes also, but they aren't selectable unless you're playing Free log and are restricted to 'ONLY' playing their New World versions. A terrible move for the sake of Fast forwarding to.... Basically a Black hole where they lost the main story and made up alot of interactions.

_childDocuments_.review: A middle of the road musou game. I've played worse, but a lot better too. There's a lot of cool stuff here, but there's also a lot of annoyances and tedium too. Positives1. This game is frequently on sale for dirt cheap. If you want to try this game, for the love of god wait for a sale. It is almost always less than $10 dollars for the basic edition, which more than justifies it's asking price. 2. The cast of playable characters is extremely varied and well put together. A lot of musou games cut corners by having lots of clone characters or a shared weapon system for the cast. While there are a handful of sort-of-clones here, the overwhelming majority of characters all have unique basic and special attacks that often make them play completely differently from anyone else. While this does result in the roster being very unbalanced, with some characters being absurdly more powerful than others, almost all the characters are at least interesting to play.3. The game scales well for a variety of machines. This developer is notorious for poor optimization on PC, but I was able to get satisfactory performance and visuals on both desktop and the ROG Ally with everything still looking great. I had a little initial trouble getting my xbox controller to work, but this was easily sorted in the steam settings. Overall this game looks great and runs at 60 fps even on middle of the road machines. 4. The combat is flashy and impactful. The basic musou weak-strong attack combo system has been further expanded to include air combos and a customizable palette of special moves that can all be linked together fluidly. As an added bonus, environmental destruction is a prominent feature here, with entire buildings crumbling to rubble form your errant attacks. These features all ramp up the power fantasy aspect of these games to new levels, making you feel like an unstoppable juggernaut who can reduce entire cities to dust. Negatives1. The story presentation is atrocious. Of course this was going to be a cliff notes summary of the One Piece saga at best, I expected that, but what really surprised me was how slapped together the story segments actually feel. Still images, pre-rendered scenes, and footage that seems to be lifted straight from previous games are often mashed together in overly lengthy lore-dump sequence. It just feels like a lot of corners were cut here, and the most laughable example was the refusal to give Iceburg an in-game character model for the Water 7 sequences. All of his dialogue just comes from somewhere off-screen while the characters stand around staring at nothing. It's bizarre and unintentionally hilarious at the same time. Also, once again, there is no English voice acting in this game. For most Japanese games this isn't a problem, but it is almost impossible to follow the dialogue for half a dozen characters quickly barking orders at you in the middle of combat.2. Named characters are very annoying to fight. By default all enemy officers have a super-armor meter you have to first deplete in order for them to stagger and take increased damage. The problem is that as soon as you do this, without fail, most named characters will activate their full-burst ability, buffing their attack and allowing them to repeatedly ragdoll your character. A few of the characters, such as Crocodile and Kizaru, are also invincible while in this state and will force you to deplete their super-armor a second time to stop it, all while they constantly blast you away with massive AOE attacks. The game overall isn't particularly difficult, but for me the fun fell off a cliff every time I had to deal with one of these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 3. Progression is pretty mediocre. You don't gain experience or level up in this game, but instead have to spend collectible coins and money to purchase raw stat boosts and abilities for each character. This system was fine overall, but I was a bit disappointed that the power ceiling felt relatively low for a Musou game. Once you're 10 hours in or so it doesn't take much effort to max out a character, and once you've filled out their ability map that's pretty much it. A dlc was recently rolled out that introduced a new progression system where you collect and spend souls for infinitesimally small stat boosts, but the currency for this is an extremely rare drop unless you own a particular dlc pack that lets you earn them more easily. Considering that a lot of other Musou games let you become ridiculously overpowered with levels in the hundreds, late game progression here just felt tame and underwhelming in comparison. Overall, pretty cool game, get it on sale if you are a musou or One Piece fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I like the game quite alot, though it has some flaws. The combat system is quite fluid, while it limits you to a ground and a air combat chain, it allows you to extend combos with the dash and change into the air combat chain whenever you want with a launch attack. Also the characters play quite different and usually have access to their iconic moves. Sadly some characters from the previous game arent in this anymore (especially as playable characters) like Kuma or Hannyabal. And here we come to a quite troublesome choice in terms of the games desing: The Story Missions. While the story arc usually get a good batch of missions to represent them, all with a certain ammount of maps of various sizes (usually cut into pieces for missions rarely left in One Piece ;) ) the game focuses in contrast to PW3 only on a hand full of arcs jumping from one to another (Arcs that actually made it in the game: Alabasta, Water 7/ Enis Lobby, Sabody Archipelago (befor time skip), Marine Fort, Sabody Archipelago (post time skip), Dressarosa, Whole Cake Island Arc and the Wano Arc (with a custom end like they did in PW 3 with Dressarosa). Also having alot of non playable characters in there that only function as enemies (usually most of the underlings in dressarosa and Wano, also drake) while some didnt make it in the game at all (just saying Biscuit isnt a thing in this game.). The lack of different scenes kinda hurts the treasure log due to it playing on allways the same maps, which are usually quite well desinged and big but at some point it kinda hurts the game. A good point are the transformations that actually change the gameplay of the character a bit though only a vew characters have access to it (sadly Chopper and Franky dont belong to those chosen vew). So I can only hope that they ll add missing arcs as dlc, though as far as I know Bandai Namco most of the stuff will be costumes...

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game with an actual good story then look away. One piece is really popular but I seriously fail to see how it is with this story telling.The GoodThe graphics are good.There are tons of 3d animated cutscenes.The menu is easy to navigate through.I loved upgrading the stats and skills of my characters.The game is really fun to play. The change in fighting mechanics compared to pirate warriors 3 is so much better. It’s the reason why I played it for so long after I beat the game.With the gameplay being so good, there was a mode called” treasure log” that you can play to waste time in. You have to trust me that this mode is nothing more than a time waster. If you have a steam deck, I would say that this mode would be a perfect game to play while taking a sht.The BadThe story is crap. No one ever dies. There were only two people who died and it was somewhere close to the beginning in one of the arcs. They weren’t even part of Luffy’s crew so why should we give sht? The other person just stands still at one point and then dies and I was left confused. It was stupid.Like, no one ever dies. When Luffy’s crew fights the big bads and they are down, they don’t actually kill them. They just let them rest and carry on. It’s so stupid. And the same thing with the bad guys. You’d expect truly bad terrible enemies to kill their opponents when they have them beat but no, they also let their opponents rest to fight another day. It’s the most idiotic story telling. How am I supposed to believe that a bad guy is really bad when every single one of them just lets people live? The last boss of this game who was supposed to be this all-powerful dude, but then says that he doesn’t want to kill them now because it wouldn’t be fun... That’s not bad guys, that’s like playground pretend enemies. It's sht writing and sht story telling.Another thing about how bad this writing is, is that everyone always escapes or teleports. This is how you know that this is sht writing. Any time there is a story where the big bad guys teleport instead of finishing a fight to kill each other is sht tier storytelling. To me, this franchise is a failure and just a tool to print money. And the thing is, it has always been this way. This will be the last time I give anything “one piece” my time.The game rehashes arcs that we’ve already played from PW3. We don’t need to play them again… Some are skipped but it’s so odd for such an important arc to be skipped over. Like really? Skipping over Luffy having to team up with villains to break out of prison?The game isn’t dubbed.Didn’t really get to use all the other characters in the game during the story. Why would I when spreading out your upgrades to other characters doesn’t help you in the long run when playing the story mode?The story arc with the girl in a skimpy attire who was adopted by a toy soldier was so weird. I fail to see how that is acceptable other than giving boys who read the manga, something to jrk to. If you are going to try and attempt to make an emotional sub plot, do better.The perv Sanji didn’t want to bring his bride on his journey or even settle down. He just wants to sail the seas and find treasure with his captain and make food for his crew. Like, he didn’t even bring up the topic of her coming with him when talking to her. It’s pathetic for what the viewer is supposed to believe, is an emotional scene at the end of that fiasco, during their last conversation. Oh and how could I forget, when Sanji didn’t want to come back because of family dues, Luffy just sat and starved himself and waited till Sanji finally fed him, even though Luffy has made countless promises to other people on how he would be there for them and other crap, but we just have to believe that no one is waiting for Luffy to come back to the ship and continue their quest. It’s so stupid.And Luffy still at the end of the day wants to be king of the pirates. Like, who gives a sht at this point? Just help people in need at this point. ConclusionI had fun playing the game because of it’s good gameplay and its brain-dead story. I wanted to see if one piece was really as good as people claim it to be and going from arc to arc, watching, and reading those long cutscenes, only proved to me that this story is just not up to par with what I want in a story. Even as a kid, I watched better shows and played games with a better story. It’s sad.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED: After a few comments in this review, I will add a few points that I didn’t mention before, making it more complete (I will also correct a few grammar mistakes that I made).Is this a good game? Yes!Is it better than One Piece Pirate Warriors 3?? Absolutely no!Is it worth it? Even if you are a One Piece fan, I have my doubtsPirate Warriors 4 has a few positive aspects over PW3. Better graphics, new characters, the possibility to choose from several skills/moves and a few more (and new) missions. But that's it. Nothing more!There are ONLY SIX arcs ().  Bandai had just ONE job: explore the Yonko saga. They didn't even manage to do it properly. There is no Zou Arc. There is no Reverie Arc. The lack of the old arcs and the poorly explored Yonko Saga disappointed me. The only thing new in here is the Whole Cake Island Arc and a poorly made Wano Country Arc.They separated those 6 arcs in different missions. 5 of those missions are an easy 1x1 fight. Bandai should've put them inside a long mission, e.g. a final boss battle, like they did in PW3. Bandai chose to have more cutscenes (explaining 2/3 of the anime that weren't in the game) and less gameplay. Bandai randomly chose a few arcs to make them playable and the rest (the most part of the anime) to be cutscenes.It took me a long time to get along with the combat camera. I just didn't like it. There are a few situations where you will experience a few bugs (Usopp's barrels don't stay in stairs, ally stuck inside a destroyed building for a long time, ranged characters have trouble to attack enemies that are on different heights, one of Luffy’s air attack send you flying above buildings, missing everything, etc.). There is also a bug where an enemy stay stuck above you (when you are close to the wall or the edge of the map) with a “falling animation”, even if you aren’t doing anything. You can attack it for free for a long time.THERE IS NO DREAM LOG!! PW3 story mode was incredible. It was very exciting to remember the whole anime. But after getting an S on all missions, you could still have a lot of fun in Dream Log. Too bad, no dream log in here.Besides that, there is not a single reason for getting an S-rank on all missions (and to complete the gallery) in PW4. You don’t get any reward, any achievement, nothing! The new mission rank system is completely useless."New characters". Nice, right? F* no!!!! Why will I want to play with all Sanji's brothers?? Where is Moria? Perona? Eneru? Garp? Kuma?!? ().Don’t get me wrong. It was funny playing with some new characters. The thing I hated the most was the lack of characters that you could play with in PW3. There are a lot of characters that you see their development and growing in the anime and you don't even have a chance to play in PW4 because more than 2/3 of the anime are just cutscenes.I won’t say anything about the online system, because I played the whole game solo. But you can read a few reviews saying that it is bugged and poorly implemented.Bandai don't want you to struggle to get S ranks on all missions (as I said, it’s useless). They've made an easy and short game where you'll play only once the story mode, and if you want to have all the achievements, just play a few more missions of the Treasure Log. What about Free log? Pointless.There isn’t any struggling point in PW4. Despite replaying a few missions, I completed the story mode in a few hours.I've spent 130 hours on PW3 getting 100% of it. It took me just 29 hours on PW4, and I think I'll never touch it again.I can't recommend a game that explores less than 1/3 of the anime.It would be better if Whole Cake Island arc and Wano arc were launched for PW3 as a DLC.They could have included ALL arcs on PW4. Too bad :(It just seems like an unfinished game.

name: Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 3
detailed_description: The only Official Monster Energy AMA Supercross Championship videogame is back! Everything is official, from real teams to the training compound, Monster Energy Supercross 3 is the exact replica of the Supercross world! OFFICIAL 2019 SEASON Relive the 2019 AMA Monster Energy Supercross season with 100 riders of both 450SX and 250SX categories, 15 official stadiums and tracks and - for the very first time - race with the official Supercross teams of the 2019 Championship in the career mode. CO-OP MODE IN THE NEW COMPOUND Get ready to enjoy an amazing Co-op experience with your friends in the brand new compound inspired by the Supercross test tracks used by the official teams, where you can train, race or roam freely in an even bigger area! DEDICATED SERVERS The addition of dedicated servers has made playing online more fun than ever! Challenge your friends in different modes: Race Director: choose the starting grid, give penalties and direct the race! Public Lobby: create a fully customisable lobby (race mode, race type, weather, etc.) or scroll through the list of lobbies available and pick the one you like the most. Private Lobby: create a custom event and challenge your friends. TRACK EDITOR Create, share and download an infinite number of tracks with the limitless track editor. Unleash your creativity to create the track of your dreams or vote and download the one you like the most. THE STRENGTH OF A WOMAN Show the world how strong a woman can be. Choose to play as a female rider to become the next Supercross champion! ENJOY AN IMPROVED GAMEPLAY New ground and in-air physics, new rider models and new animations will give you a more immersive experience to enjoy the Supercross world at its best!

_childDocuments_.review: Every year I tell myself that I'm not going to buy it. I buy it every year. I'm part of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ problem and I realize it. Guess what, I'll probably buy it next year. Don't be like me. Don't be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Go play literally any game other than this. It's not good. I'll break it down though.The Good:You can be on a factory team. That's neat. Only 3 games too late.You can kind of free style whip.....but it doesn't really work. It's like they tried to copy MX vs ATV all out, but it's still tied to the stupid push the sticks in opposite directions to trigger it. Maybe I'm just not getting it.I totally did a backflip on the wall at A2. That was cool. That being said, I landed flat from at least 75 foot up and rode it out.It's pretty. Like really pretty. It runs great. 1440 UW on full ultra runs a crisp 120 with no dips on my 2080.The compound is neat. Especially since you can take your friends into it.You can be a girl I guess. The Bad:The physics are awful. The bikes feel bad. They only kind of do what you want them to do some of the time. In fact, there's a few spots where you can do the same thing and the outcome is entirely different. You can rewind half a second and instead of crash, you ride it out. You can literally case every jump, and in some cases, it's faster. Is there a particular rhythm section you're struggling with? Just lean back and skim it like whoops.Speaking of whoops, just lean back and wheelie through them like Tomac at Daytona. I'm like 90% sure that the ruts that form during the race are purely visual. I've tried to hook ruts that look like they're up to the foot pegs and just blow right through them.LOL SOUND. Bikes sound mediocre at best. I'm also pretty sure I've heard the area announcer say "Kenny is going to force the issue" every 3rd lap on every race.Customization is bad. You know how the "bE LiKe Us" pros have their names and numbers massive across their back? You won't. You're stuck with 4 bad fonts that are all tiny. It looks hilarious. It seems like there is less gear to chose from this year than last year, which is funny because last year's game wasn't anything to write home about.I may be in the minority, but I thought the practice sessions and the "pre race" week calendar from last year was neat....It's not there anymore. I could go on and on for this, but I'd just avoid it for now. I've not messed with the track builder, but from what I've read, it's the same thing as last year, only with new and improved bugs. I'll still probably put a boat load of hours into it because I'm an idiot.

_childDocuments_.review: Most likely the best motorbike Milestone has put out so far. MXGP 2020 might take the crown soon. GET IN ON SALE ONLY.Here goes some MASS of opinions.Pros:++ First person view experience is great.+ Lots of customization and official gear.+ Free Roam map.+ Nicely crafted courses.+ Official content from AMA SX Series.+ Fun to ride and push hard+ AI is better than previous++ Graphics are pretty neatCons:-Milestone usual quirks as it feels like they take the worse from AAA titles.:--- No option to launch from stationary during qualifying. Being forced to watch the auto pilot until the player has control.-- Lack of camera adjustments on options.---- Missing set default camera in options menu for those who enjoy more first person view or one of the other 3 camera options other than the default 3rd person.-- Loads of cutscenes at the beginning of each racing session (Heat 1/2, LCQ, Main Events). _childDocuments_.review: The new monster energy supercross game brings many new things with it compared to the previous version from 2019.The first thing you'll have to do in the game is to create your driver and to choose your bike. You can adjust your driver & bike to the deepest details for a personal most wanted customization.There are several single player events you can go through from a career to single races and challenges to an official training compound. The game also includes a multiplayer mode with a few mini gamemodes next to the normal races.Choose from 100 drivers from different categories and race over many tracks on 15 stadiums. There are also a lot of custom tracks wich are made by other users. You can create your own tracks in the track editor wich is included in the game and share them with other users.The graphics look really good and you can really enjoying watching the fireworks.The physics are well done, you can anticipate the grip through the dirt very good. You can also adjust that grip if you put other tires on your bike.there are a lot of available tires to choose from, and each is unique in how they respond on the dirt or while making turns or other manouvers, it's up to you to find out what suits best for your driving style.The blocks at the sides of the route aren't a huge problem like in the previous version, in the 2019th version it made you fall from your bike faster then it does now. still when you end up next of the track you get a few seconds to get back on the track without respawning. If you respawn you will loose a couple extra seconds as well. Doing jumps and airstunts are also very good to controll, if you made one mistake on a jump the first time then it's not so hard to correct that jump the next time you'll have to do it. You can also enable 'flow aid' wich is some kind of help for you in order to do your jumps better. But you can also disable this function via the race options. You can also adjust your bike with new parts wich will improve your jumping and landing.In order to upgrade your bike you'll have to score points. In order to score points you'll have to perform clean manouvers or stunts. You can also use these points to change the appearance of your driver and you have several different slots so you can choose different styles that you like. this will prevent that the points you spend are not lost if, for example, you want another outfit without losing the first one.Once you saved enough points to customize your driver and bike, you'll probaly need to grab a coffee with you, the bike customization has so many options from different parts and brands, to different colors of each part to even the chain. Same goes for driver customization wich also gives you a lot of options. All this will ensure your look to be unique from all the rest in online multiplayer mode.You can change the difficulty level of the AI in the game but you aren't able to do this when you race against other people online. When you join an online game, you might have to wait a moment untill the current race has finnished. But this give you a chance to explore the spectator camera views and to learn techniques from other humans. As a spectator you'll have more camera views then in a normal race, but if you want to look at your performance in from these camera angle's then you should watch the replays of the races you done.Playing online is not only normal races, there are mini gamemodes as well wich are also fun and challenging to do. You can do checkpoints, where the racers will have to race from checkpoint to checkpoint and who has the highest score at the end wins the race.Knockout mode is an elimination mode, here a timer will count down and when this timers ends then the racer with the least points is eliminated from the race. At the end the racer with the most points will be the winner.In treasure hunter all players will start from different locations on the map and they'll have to race to a highlighted area on the map, inside this area you'll have to search for 'the treasure' Via sounds and vibrations on your gamepad you will have to locate the treasure inside this area.Singleplayer mode also comes with a championchip and also a career mode where you can also compete for the first time for the official Supercross teams of the 2019 championship.There is time attack where you'll have to do time challenges and an official training compound where you can enjoy freestyle fun or train your style. The compound also supports a co-op mode.the last singleplayer mode are the challenges, each challenge has a a large amount of levels, the higher the level, the more difficult the challenge of that level will be. I'll show you a couple of these challengesIn 'go with the flow', you'll have to perform jumps and follow the 'flow aid' in order to complete the challenge. The green color means that you are doing it good, the red means that you can do it better.In mind the gates you'll have to ride through the most gates you can before the time runs out. According from the color of the gates you can score more points.Holeshot hunt is all about speed and timing, the challenge is to beat your opponent on short parts on the tracks, whoever finnish first wins the challenge.There are a few other challenges wich i leave for you to explore. The game is in general very good, i really like to playing it as i like to do with all milestone releases. Each year they make huge improovements in the motorcycle racing genre. The game also runs great on a steam deck:

_childDocuments_.review: Best game ever released by Milestone by a lot, really. And I see from noobs like me to the pros, everyone generally agreeing on that. Supercross 1 and 2, which were good games, are closer to 'Big Rigs: Over The Road Racing' than to this title.Physics are great, the bike now has inertia and there is actually freedom in the air. Fully separated bike and rider dynamics create a very fun challenge. The tracks feel better when it comes to dimensions than Supercross 2. Also the dirt in SX2 looked like a cat either puked or took a crap all over the stadium, depending on the soil. The default setup is also very good unless you're an alien wanting to extract every tenth of a second. You have to be careful on the wheelie and general inputs, unlike the first two SX games. Just a recommendation though: start playing right away with the advanced physics, the normal physics are clunky like the first two games.Crash physics are better and now landing on the head of an opponent can cause problems. The inexplicable crashes from the previous game are not present here as well.The AI, although still easy for the pros, gives a very good challenge for the normal people. It's also one of the most consistent AIs from Milestone since its difficulty is a bit more balanced from track to track than other titles and it doesn't try insane maneuvers. Of course, Milestone's AI being its Achilles' heel, there is still a long way to the top if you wanna rock and roll.When it comes to career, the game lost the tests from SX2, which were mostly annoying anyway, and gained factory teams, which adds immensely to the immersion. Independently of the race duration, you get the ten minutes classification to practice. Even if you're not the fastest, you can win the championship through consistency, since unlike the previous iterations, the AI has good and bad days — without seeming random. It feels more realistic. For the more controversial sides, it shall be said that Ricky Johnson's 2-stroke bike riding there with you can be a huge immersion killer for some, and it is not the case with me though. Another flaw that it brings to the table is: if the AI can ride a two-stroke bike, why can't the player ride a customized one on the many game modes? Still, nothing that ruins the experience by any means.Also, it can run on most of modern machines with high graphics and very good framerate. I am not an expert, but the recommended settings seem slightly overdimensioned.The weakest point of the game, and which prevents it from being an all-time classic though, is the lack of meaningful terrain deformation. There is some visual deformation, but it's not functional and it's still lightyears behind MX vs. ATV Reflex, a title released over a decade ago.This review is targeted mostly towards the average Joe, but some of the features this game brings will please even the most afictionado motocross/supercross fan. Milestone was really inspired when developing this. I give it 8/10 and will definitely be watching the sequences with great interest.

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the fact that we have a official license Monster Energy Supercross game, but the game needs to be seriously focused beyond the graphics. The graphics are good. Lets instead focus on the fact how nobody should be encouraged to treat every rhythm section like a whoop section. There needs to be more of a benefit for hitting rhythms clean and instances where doubling and singling in our out of a section is encouraged. People want ruts, but I believe that flat corners can help encourage throttle management. I dont like the idea that now im stuck with old school James Stewart, Davi, Ricky Johnson, Grant Langston, and Tim Ferry in my career mode now. It should've been an option when setting up an individual race/career mode. It goes without saying that the AI needs to have a tougher setting and maybe even a slider setting like the F1 games and all official tracks need to have all problems ironed out. The AI shouldn't be singling doubles (Anaheim 2 i think). They shouldn't constantly be endoing in one set of whoops at a particular track (glendale) while you cruise through just fine. Or the finish line jump that nobody can jump at daytona. This stuff shouldn't have been release this way and it should've been in a patch ages ago. Why am I stuck to two random factory teams/sponsors when given an opportunity to sign? In the older games there would be a reputation bar. It should be based on current form, a privateer shouldn't have to win 10 races before signing with a team.its frustrating being a fan... still giving a thumbs up

_childDocuments_.review: Just don't. Seriously. I'm a huge fan of moto games, all the way back from ATV Offroad Fury. The trend of "Make every moto game as realistic as possible instead of as fun as possible" began with Mx Vs ATV Reflex, and Milestone took it 50 steps farther than that game. This game is the horrible cesspool of a combination of all those efforts.The good:> The graphics of course.>Also the bike sounds are pretty ok.>The built-in tracks are all pretty good, no major stinkers this year except for Daytona.The meh: >The track creator is literally hardly any different. No improvements to speak of except for sweeping turns and more sand options. But it's actually worse than last year's track creator because they limit how many jumps you can turn around. Why can't we turn the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ table tops around anymore?! That was a fun idea!The bad: >The AI. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI is borderline psychotic in this game! On any custom track, they will single or double instead of triple or quad, and them braking will make you crash into them, EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. It feels like when they created the AI, Milestone's goal was to make them take you out, to try and make the game more challenging. Yeah, screw you if that was your intention guys. That makes me not want to play the game at all our of protest.Also, the career mode is just...meh. I don't think it really improved from last year and still feels like an unnecessary grind.>I wanted to like the compound tracks, but i think Milestone got a little too happy with their terrain deformation tool. IT'S INSANE. In real life, those track are located in California, and the companies that own them (Honda, Suzuki, Husqvarna and others), really take care of and maintain those tracks. They're not that eroded. So why are they so painfully eroded in this game?! It's ridiculous. I'd much more enjoy them if they were clean and well-maintained!>The free-whipping system. It's so...half-assed. You can kind of free whip, yet it still feels like the game controls what you're doing. It's not fun like it was in Reflex. I don't get why a true free-whipping system is so hard to do. Major letdown there.Overall, i feel like Milestone tried to make this game different from the last game, but halfway through they got tired and said "Screw it, give us your 60$ now". It's not improved upon, it's not fun. If you buy it, don't EVER play career or single event. The AI will make you want to delete the game.Overall, i give it a 4/10. I'm gonna go back to M.E. 1 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- Handling seems more realistic (I can't move in the air anymore)- You face a larger penalty if you screw up in rhythm sections- 9 total compound tracks- Sand in Track Editor- Online is goodCons:- The AI are slightly better, but still wildly inconsistent and unrealistic- The game crashes intermittently.- Lag spikes when turning or changing camera.- Many bugs throughout the game    * In qualifying, how do the other riders have twice as many laps as me? That doesn't make sense    * AI qualifying times are not based on the actual lap times of the riders    * When looking at race info, "LCQ" shows results from a previous races LCQ. This also happens with the heats.    * AI riders are not forced to driver slower when they exit the course    * AI riders gain momentum out of nowhere when they mess up in a rhythm section. Come on.   * Lap riders appear ahead of you at the end of the race, but this doesn't carry over to final results which is good.- After a race, I can only see every riders best lap time? Really? Why not their time behind the leader?- The Track editor menu is not user friendly. I shouldn't have to go back to the first page to switch from whoops to a corner.WANTS:- Why am I limited to three choices of race length? Why can't I set it to any amount of time I want? Maybe I want to do a 60 minute race.- Why can't I pick which riders are in my "championship", or even in a single event race?- The 17 official tracks all have different dirt textures, why is there only one texture within track editor?- A more immersive season mode. Riders retiring, moving up to the 450's, injuries (maybe exclude that).- Better historical records of season statistics. "Oh I finished 5th at Nashville last year, wow".I DO NOT recommend this game for $50. Sure its a lot of content, but there are so many small issues that it just feels like the game was rushed or made lazily. I may be wrong, but this is just my opinion. Get it on sale, but only then.

_childDocuments_.review: The inconsistencies in bike handling, overly aggressive AI, and lack of proper tutorials really hurt this game.I've been playing many other racing games for years (rFactor, GTR2, Automobilista, Assetto Corsa, Project Cars, MotoGP, F1 games, Dirt Rally, etc, with all aids off & manual gears) but the handling in this game makes no sense to me. I can never understand why I'm crashing (one lap I can land from a jump just fine but the next lap I crash for no apparent reason), or why the bike slows down miserably whenever I go through a jump section. If I make a flat track with no jumps in the track editor I can play the game just fine, it's the jumping sections that make no sense to me and where I lose a ton of time against the AI.AI is overly aggressive, they don't seem to be aware of my presence and hit me all the time, collisions usually result in me crashing while the AI keeps going normally like nothing happened.The tutorial in the game is pretty useless, it simply throws you into a race, shows the controls on the screen, and doesn't explain anything, doesn't tell how to do jumps properly, how to scrub, how to setup the bike, weight transfer, no useful information on how to control the bike in the tutorial.It might be a good game for players with lots of experience in Supercross games but for people with no previous experience in Supercross games the inconsistent handling and lack of information makes this game very frustrating to play even for players like me who have a lot of experience in other racing sims.

_childDocuments_.review: The best looking and smoothest controlled of the first 3 games in this series, and IMO even looks better and more realistic (in rider movement) than what I've seen of the 4th and 5th games. I don't know why many are claiming the AI is too hard in this game, because once you learn effective techniques, they are quite manageable. For me it was a simple matter of applying a weight back acceleration boost on jump takeoffs and landings, which improved my result so much I had to give the AI a head start even on Realistic. Which brings me to my only nit pick, the AI on Realistic need to be more capable. Once you master the game, I found they need to be either 2 sec vs 1 sec faster per lap than Hard mode, or more consistent at how well they handle rhythm sections.I'm hoping Supercross 4 will feel as smooth and look as realistic in rider movement once all the skills are upgraded, but the venues look the best in this game IMO, even IF the dirt color is a bit less realistic. I know in reality many of the actual real world venues have a more greyish color, construction fill looking dirt, but I find it looks very dingy.

_childDocuments_.review: MESX3 is definitely an improvement on both Milestone's SX franchise and their MXGP franchise. The graphics are beautiful, the animations are smooth, and  the whip mechanics are dependant on rider input instead of being a canned animation. Unfortunately this game still has issues in regards to physics and momentum, and it may be a deal breaker for those that are unable to get a grasp on how this game  you to ride.I say "expects" because the rhythm line in MESX3 isn't there as a mere suggestion or an aide, it's the only "fast" line you can realistically take if you want to win. Why? Because all the bikes in this game feel painfully anemic at the best of times. If you case a jump or land a little flat abandon any hope of recovering, you won't be able to chain together a new rhythm until you're back following the rhythm line. Obviously this isn't always the case, but it's common enough that there's no reason to even attempt new lines, and for a SX game that's very disappointing.Overall I still recommend this game for MX fans, but only on a sale. I feel like Milestone is slowly getting to where they need to be but they still have much to learn. I genuinely hope that when MXGP 2020 comes around all of these problems will be addressed, because it would be a shame to see so much potential squandered for another flagship MX title.

_childDocuments_.review: RECOMMENDED for Supercross fans ONLY (YEARS of the Same In-Game Problems). NEW Features + Improvements to Ground & Air Physics don't offer enough improvement to stop Rage Quitting after a few hours.”I felt that Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 2 was darned near perfection (with LOTS of issues). So I had extremely HIGH HOPES for Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 3.Guess what?  Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 3 is Darned near perfection (with LOTS of issues).MES3 has made some excellent additions to the game, but ignored feedback & made some absolute Rookie mistakes.o This looks amazing!o Most realistic Supercross Game ever released.o LOTS of new features & content (Tutorial, Challenges, Career mode + MORE).o Bike modelling, track creation is ALL top notch.o Whip, flow and ride training is much better (not perfect).o FULLY LICENSED & OFFICIAL (with the exception of...?).o CO-OP on the NEW COMPOUND is going to be cool.o The off TRACK 5 second reset is SH*T!!  I hate it + after 3 seconds it will RESET YOU ANYWAY!!!!!o AUDIO is shocking.  I cannot hear my bike at all & with no HUD that makes gear management impossible.o Physics - whilst some is really good we still have this bouncey weightlessness issue.o AI -> You've played this before right?o UI So MANY Rookie mistakes, why have 1 button click when you can have 20 o UI FLOW Management -> You want to try again?  Then let's take a quick scenic detour via the menu shall we WTAF???o You cannot change your view when on the start line.o You can cheat and get off the start WAY before anyone else.o The Challenges are BRILLIANT but stupidly implemented;  - FLOW = Stay on the line, even if your FLOW is TERRIBLE for max points????? <- what?  - WHIP = Perform the action marker.  --- BUT :  HOW?? + What does each one mean + can't even see it.  - GATES = Now forget EVERYTHING you have learnt & weave about all over the place????? <- what the hell?This game is incredible but ruined by really poor decisions made by someone who doesn't understand the difference between GOOD/BAD UI, AI or physics.The AI still just slam into you, slide you across the track and destroy you without any attempt to stay clear.  The AI difficulty is a strange thing, as they don't so much race better as cheat (supersonic acceleration).  The real & only opponent against you is the game itself (and those bloody soft barriers which take me out all of the time).What simply OUTRAGES me is how the game auto resets you in 2 seconds if you go even slightly off track (more annoying when bounced off by the AI).  I DO NOT WANT THIS FEATURE IN THIS GAME!  FFS, you don't see auto resets on Assetto, PC2 or ANY Racing simulator.  This is something games in the 80's and 90's used because of limitations at the time, FIX THIS.  If I go off track, having to get back on track is my punishment because it will lose me time.Moments in this game are AMAZING, and that shows how good this game could be.  These moments are hidden behind layers and layers of poorly implemented decisions.  Give me 1 month and the freedom to make 20 changes to the game and it would be transformed into the BEST Supercross Simulation (with Arcade Fun in-place) which the community have been craving for!If I had paid £40 for this game (& I didn't) I would be refunding it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get it. The first person view when turning the bike is so completely wrong. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game similar to MX vs ATV, this isn't it, it's a satisfying rhythm based MX racing game, with more sim-like mechanics while remaining arcade-y enough to enjoy and not be punished at every little mistake. It's difficult, with an emphasis on map memorization and knowing when to slow down / maintain speed. The graphics are very nice, tire tracks remain in the dirt, realistic wind effects on clothing, amazing replay features, it's an all around pleasant game to play. There are rewinds available in single player to add forgiveness to the game, and a jump-boost mechanic to allow you to make jumps you might've been too slow during the approach for. Very surprising to find a MX game this good that's been out since 2019, thanks Cody for recommending it. (:

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my mind, I like the game now. I don't know if it was that I got used to it or the update tweaked the physics a little or a combination of both, but I'm liking the feel of it now. I'll leave my original review untouched below for the lol's....============================================Gameplay sucks, let me explain. Ever ride a bike in Grand Theft Auto V and be like this is basic arcade handling with not much sophistication? Well you'll get not much more sophistication in handling and physics in this game. Case anything with no penalty, rip whoop sections without having to do any body leaning, endless traction with no need for throttle control, and bounce into the air like a pogo stick off every jump like some auto preload - boing.. boing.. boing.. weeeeeeeee. There, you have the gameplay wrapped up in a nutshell.More bad: The damned audio is still just as bad as previous titles. Now take into account I'm running a $16,000 audio system consisting of Bowers & Wilkens flagship 800 series speakers, a 2800 watt Sunfire Subwoofer, and all room tuned with Audyssey MultEQ XT32 and in surround your bike sound is very faint and still sounds like a hoover vacuum cleaner when you can hear it. Actually, a vacuum cleaner sounds less cheesy. To hear my own bike I have to either select stereo or multi channel stereo on my surround processor/pre amp. Since I mentioned Grand Theft Auto V, the surround sound is so good in that game on my system that I have in fact mistaken police being outside my house for the actual in game sound coming from my system! Milestone, maybe you should consider getting a real surround system and calibrating it properly! I'm thinking that you guys are only using headphones in stereo in development. The bike(s) should freaking roar and rumble on a $16,000 properly calibrated surround system!Is there any good? Any? Yup, It runs very well. Playing it with maxed out graphics on a 75" 4k HDR display in 4k I'm not noticing any performance dips and it runs liquid smooth without having to turn down any option (albeit I'm running a 12GB 2080 Ti OC but much older games like Gold Club 2 that came out many moons ago can give my card a bit of a performance drop maxed out at 4k from bad optimizations so no problem here with performance).That's the game in a nutshell.1. Grand Theft Auto V arcade vehicle physics. (MXGP 2019 is much better)2. Same old poor sound with no updates from the previous titles3. Not much of a graphical advancement, same old same old repackaged with new tracks4. Runs great at max graphic settingSeriously, as someone whose pretty much owned nearly every MX game in existence starting back from Excitebike on the NES and being a huge fan of the sport, I'm seriously just done buying these games from here on out. They come out every year with minimal improvements or none at all and fail to really advance, and sometimes even go backwards. I think the gameplay in MXGP 2019 is much better than this.
