_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I give this a 7 out of 10. The game is pretty good, with a few minor issues.The good,-Lots of content, from riders to tracks, a fair bit of content to keep you occupied.-Good Graphics.-60 FPS on modest hardware. (4 core 3.5 ghz) Low end graphics.-Fun side modes and a training compound, which is basically a big pit.-Licensed stuff, and official riders.-Mostly good physics. The racing physics are very good and realistic, with a few exceptions.-Pretty Fun base gameplay.-Track Editor XD. I love these kinds of features. The bad-Some of the specs are way out from real life. The CRF450R in the game is underpowered on the low and mid range compared to a real life. The CRF450R in real life is a insane bike, but the game doesnt quite map your intent 1:1 to the bike, which can be annoying.The automatic player weight distribution will mess you up sometimes, and i recommend turning this off. The bikes have odd disimilarities, like, they all seem to have traction control and you have to fight to wheelie them. Which is unrealistic, because a real life 450R will power wheelie through 4th gear. The other game made on this same tech, shares a similar problem, the bikes do not perform correctly compared to real life. The gear ratios are incorrect too.-The most annoying thing about this game is that the physics model, although excellent for racing, cannot handle stunts. Doing even simple wheelies, which is way harder in this game then in real life, pretty much always ends in a flip or a crash. Why? The game isnt expecting you to wheelie I guess. Which can be annoying, and limits the techniques you can use in racing. Without wheelies, the physics are on point, and handle well. This kind of kills alot of the fun for me.-The freerange map is a little too small, but its a very good idea thats a ton of fun.-Minor annoyance, but the sounds arent correct. They are using street versions of engine sounds which top out at 10K RPM. Race bikes, go very high, and sound cool.-The customization is limited. You cant pick custom sprokets for example, or do tuning. You cant replace engine components to add or shift power. This is kind of annoying. Its kind of amazing to build OP bikes and sink money into them like grand turismo. ThoughtsThis game has tons of potential, and is a decent supercross game, that is much more on the realism side, as opposed to arcady racers. Some of the stuff isnt right, and the stunt physics are broken, (wheelies kill you half way to balance point) but overall for the racing experience, this is probably one of the better racing games I have played. What this game needs in the future.-All racing games need much more in depth tuning and car building. Engine swaps, gear swaps, custom cams, timings, intakes, headers, valve sizes, oil thickness, etc. Needs an in depth carrer mode where you have to buy used bikes and build engines to race with. Maybe invest in your shop and dealership to earn passive income, hire other riders, train them.Would be nice if you could build some custom bikes. GSXR1000 dirtbike. (Look on youtube)Should add drag races, grudge racing, enduro rides on big randomly generated maps. City stunt supermoto challenges. Dog fighting/team deathmace multiplayer. Hill climbs. Smuggling while being chased by fourwheelers or something, (with custom high perf bikes netting you higher rewards from harder missions.OVerall I would recommend this if you are into dirtbikes. Its a solid and polished product with a fair bit of content.

_childDocuments_.review: One of two games I've ever returned.jI wanted to like this game, I wanted to play this game. I own and play almost all motocross games to exhaustion. I'm just tired of these games where if you get out of a main rhythm on a track, it becomes a pain to get back into the rhythm. Why is there only one 'fast way' to get around the track? I miss the days of old MX vs ATV where you could design a track with multiple rhythms. For example: if you roll the first jump out of a corner and then hammer the gas, you should be able to clear the following gap. That's how it works in real life - it happens literally all the time and is how other lines are discovered. In this game, if you try that, you'll just case the jump and have to being the process of leaning back, throttle wide open and trying to get back into the 'fast line'. It's stupid.The game plays pretty nicely, the bikes handle okay (not great). The graphics look very nice which is cool. But I myself just can't get over the lack of options when racing. The last two Milestone games where the same way. There was like one fast line, you hit it appropriately or suffered with lackluster speed and lots of cased jumps. In real life the bikes are powerful enough to create different lines and put different jump combinations together in unique ways -but not in this game. Once again, stuck with just one line boredom.I wanted to like this one, I played and hoped. I just couldn't get over the fact that I could see faster lines... the bike (in real life) would have easily been capable of hitting those lines... but because of the game mechanics I could not perform those lines. And it's not like they were difficult lines... just stringing together small rhythms together in different ways. So very, very frustrating.I'm pretty sure I'm done with the Milestone games at this point. This is the second game I've ever returned in decades of game play. That says something.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: STEAM CLOUD FUNCTIONALITY IS MISSING! I filed a ticket with Milestone support about it on July 10th 2020 and never received a response. The ticket is  open.PC was never a priority when you left us out of the opportunity to pre-order and play early as you otherwise afforded to console players. This is precisely why I purchased a pre-order from cdkeys for half price, because you don't deserve full price for this game. Some genius middle-manager at Milestone has come up with the brilliant idea of the starting gate being transformed into this half-concussed, COD-like crescendo into consciousness while you wait for the gate to drop and now you can no longer hear your bike or any of the other bikes rev anymore. It's horrendous.The nickname font on the rider, even when customized to the largest size possible is still TINY. How can you miss a bug like this?You simply cannot fall off the bike anymore when casing. At all. That skill-gap is gone. Cornering no longer has any weight and continuous, forward momentum. Instead of sliding out while exiting a corner, as was the case in the slide/drift-fest that was MESX2 & MXGP2019, now you're more likely to 180 into a corner as they have loosened the bike and, subsequently, its weight far, far too much. The right stick does nothing. Don't even bother with it, especially while cornering. It does absolutely nothing while cornering. They've gimped it. Riding simply feels slow and unengaging. I remember YellowS2K stating that you cannot move the bike around in the air to change its trajectory, while true, even hitting the smallest jump i am able to lay the bike flat and immediately crash. I'm trying to lean and Milestone's IK rig wants to literally lay the bike flat for me. One of the most egregious UX fails of this game, as if this UI isn't bad enough, is the obfuscation of the exit to main menu. It's hidden within a sub-menu that gives no indication it's hiding there. I literally thought the feature was removed from the game until I was able to find it in the sub-menu (it's hidden under results).As has become a long-standing Milestone tradition, it's nigh-impossible to get a podium qualifying lap-time against realistic difficulty AI, but as soon as you hit the main event you'll blast ahead of them.For all those who moaned about being able to blast their way over the whoops, well, you got your wish. You now crawl over the whoops and it's boring as f$%K. Congrats.Rider model can't seem to keep his feet on the pegs..can't keep his right leg tucked in either, odd. This was present in the earliest alpha builds and still hasn't been fixed. #justmilestonethingsThis is all I have to write about 1.5 hours in. I will continue to update, but I feel everyone should know this before purchasing. [I'm also researching to determine whether the animators/modellers responsible for the excellent rider & bike IK rig in MESX1, 2 and MXGP2019 were 86sixed and outsourced to Rainbow post THQ Nordic merge because the abysmally-bad and down-right embarrassing rider posture and movement is simply too reminiscent of Rainbow studios horrendous work to be just a coincidence]Update after reading the credits: the "Lead Animator" hasn't changed since MXGP2019, the "Animator" position added a second Animator while retaining the last person and "Junior Animator" is the same case as "Animator" — same person retained, another "Junior Animator" added. I have no idea if these people are responsible for only animating IK rigs previously created for them or they created the IK. They do not list "Riggers" in their credits.

_childDocuments_.review: Feminism: First of all, i'm male and i support feminism, i'm a proud feminist at heart. I've just gotta say that Milestone failed miserably to support feminism. I mean sure it's awesome to tell people to show how strong a woman can be, but at least make the AI female riders too and not everyone else be male only. Comparison of all games:I've played both MES1 and MES2, they seem a lot more fluid in riding and control then MES3 does. I feel like this game felt more unprofessionally made than the last two games are. The camera doesn't really have an FOV which makes the game feel very non-immersive. The rider seems to always be sitting on the very front end of the bike which looks uncomfortable. Multiplayer:The multiplayer doesn't really exist since there are no lobbies available.  Graphics:The color of the world looks very dried out and dead, graphics are basically the same as the other games. The character model structuring could use some more work since both females and males don't look that good. The screenshots of the game make it look way better than it really is. To me I would give this game a 2/10 and only play it because it has good graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of MESX 2 and MESX 4 this one is the better one  Cant speak for mesx 1 or mesx5 But I would say its a good place to start if you want to try the franchiseGood stuff- Bike sounds, (much better than mesx 4 actually audible) very good sounds -Graphics, Slight improvement over 2 and still much better than 4 ( 4 was a severe downgrade)-Physics, although arcady which is to be expected it is still fun and somewhat realistic -Riding, lighter in the air maybe abit too light compared to 2 and 4 but still fun player movement is good leaning helps in the air and turning and general control, Whips and scrubs are kind of free but dont expect mx bikes-Career, Fun again pretty simple, 15 tracks to race at 450,250 east and west good customisation female and male riders :) compounds are alright I think 2 had the best compound but its not bad by any means-AI, Actually not bad still sometimes ride into you like you dont exist but less infuriating than 4 I found can have some good battles and at some tracks they can be strung out apart so its okBad stuff-Slighty too floaty get in the air easily and for too long but its okay-Recycles voice lines from 2 and used again in 4 cutscenes are repetitive-music is not great but maybe just not my taste-you can get holeshot pretty much every time the ai are really slow on gate drop-first person camera is not as good as mesx 4 Conclusion- More fun than mesx 4 and more realistic than 2 My preffered mesx title as of now and for the price you will get your moneys worth of enjoyment-

_childDocuments_.review: For me there is WAY too much ping-pong from side to side that is allowed and the super powered launches with no speed... However, your can ride the rhythm section like whoops if you lean back a bit which, is the only time body position really mater all that much.Fun, but  incredibly frustrating. Maybe with another mess of hours I will have every bit of every track memorized so these are actually rideable without the benefit of the big bikes or Ricky Johnson's CR250R.I would recommend this at a deep discount because it can be fun as a video game, but not what I'm after in a dirtbike game.

_childDocuments_.review: Best MX game since MX UnleashedAfter looking desperately for good MX games for pc that contained the perfect blend of arcade and simulation handling, I ran into no luck. MX vs ATV All out had terrible controls, MXGP had terrible controls, MX vs ATV reflex was "okay" but the controls were still terrible and required too much right stick handling to correctly steer your bike against tough turns... They were all bad.. But then I ran into this game. This game has that perfect blend of the old PS2 ATV Offroad Fury and MX Unleashed games many old school MX players were looking for, as well as adding their own twist and formula to the mix. This game is phenomenal. Pros:+Beautiful graphics and phenomenal environments +Excellent sound design and steering+Great customization options for your rider+Free roam compound maps which add to the enjoyment+Gameplay is flawless+Great physicsCons:-Terrible garbage soundtrack that does not match the game. -Could use more free roam optionsVerdict:9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a thumb sideways because if you find a great sale feel free to give it a try, but be aware that MXGP3 is so much better (in my opinion). If you  want a supercross game, grab the first MESX (if you already have it don't upgrade). It will be cheaper too. MESX3 CAN be fun, but it is very frustrating. If you get this one, just be ready to put in some time before getting comfortable with it.Here are some of the problems I have had with this game, specifically with the 250s in career mode (450s are much less frustrating but not enough of an improvement to justify the purchase at full price). The tracks seem very tight. Maybe it is more realistic, but the bike is so much more unpredictable and the NPCs can bounce you across the track so easily that the tight tracks are just super frustrating. Also the physics are very bad. I constantly hit invisible walls, landing jumps can some times slow you down for no reason, changing AI difficulty doesn't really make a big difference, bike setup is arbitrary and pointless, I sometimes loop out for no reason (even in muddy races where it is supposedly slick), you feel light compared to the NPCs (for example they will mow you down when passing you and you can bounce from NPC to NPC like a pinball, but if you hit them it hardly affects them), the NPCs are almost on rails and you can match their speed and line yet they will get invisible boosts in order to hit jumps (especially in the mud). I could probably keep going, but I don't want to rag on the game. I love motorcycle games and want to see more investment into them, but this one was just not for me. MX vs ATV Reflex set the bar high for me. Milestone has great graphics and I would love to see them make a game that makes me forget about reflex. I really wish they would add AMA Motocross to one of their franchises. It would make a lot of sense to combine supercross and motocross, but would probably be easier to just add some US tracks and riders to MXGP. Honestly, I think they should combine all three into one game and start spending 3 years on making the game. I know they won't do that, but this yearly stuff is going to make games like this go away for good. Sorry for the rant. Don't buy THIS game, put your money on MXGP3 and the first MESX.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great graphical improvement compared to the previous one, but the downside is they removed the dynamic track so there are pretty much no ruts at all.  The only ruts in the game are the ones created into the game.They also added a stupid audio queue to the gate drop so you can time the drop better, and get better launch which is not very realistic.physics feel like they got worse.  You can land on another racers head and they wont crash but I promise you will either bounce another 10 feet in the air like a trampoline or you will crash.Like the previous one as well if you land on the rectangle boxes you pretty much ice skate across them and will probably crash.The announcers are really annoying too, expect the same comments made every race and qualifier every other lap you take.If you have a bad section you can ride the tops of the jumps like whoops, speaking of which dont expect to get good rythm in jump sections you will more than likely undershoot it or over shoot by a mile.  During this time the AI with no speed will cruise right past you and get a 10 second lead on you pretty much making you lose the race.If you crash at all expect to lose at least 5 spots in the race and never catch up.But the main reason why I down-voted is because the game practically has 1 difficulty and that's realism.  While the game has "Very Easy," "Easy" "Hard," and "Realism" if you play on very easy don't expect to have it be easy, you are pretty much never going come in first unless its raining or the track has mud on it.  The AI will more than likely beat you by at least 5-10 seconds and even qualifying expect to have the perfect line where you will more than likely make the fastest lap by .1 seconds.  I really wish I didn't play for so long so I could refund it but sadly I left the game up by accident.  Save yourself the time and money and don't buy this crap until they decide to fix some issues--Update 11/29So since this update they seemed to have adjusted the difficulty where very easy is a bit easier now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid motocross game player on console. I love them. MX vs. ATV Reflex being my all time favorite still. THIS GAME IS FUN, BUT THE JUMP MECHANICS NEED WORK. It's really annoying when you're flying past the AI in Career and then launch off a jump and you go straight up and case the landing 85% of the time while the AI lands perfectly on the face of the landing or at the bottom of it. IF YOU PRELOAD YOU GO UP AND BACK DOWN, it doesn't really help much with the distance. The bike setup is nice but they all virtually do the same thing(make bike more stable or precise). WHEN YOU DO LAND PERFECTLY, YOU SLOW DOWN to the point it almost impossible to hit the next jump, unless you preload and just send yourself flying straight up, losing time either way. If the Jump mechanics were tweaked just a tad bit to add distance to the preload distance instead of height this game would be excellent, BUT seeing as in you case the landings 50% of the race it makes this game really frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the East and West seasons, now a decent way into the 450 class. The rider physics in this game have the potential to be really good if the devs stick to them and look to improve them for future SX titles. The game Looks really good visually, the compound is pretty awesome. The biggest issue for me personally are the physics like casing and some of the whoop sections, I don't think they feel as good as other games. For example there are jumps that if you are going to case you can use the scrub mechanic to not only avoid yourself from bouncing but you can also keep a decent amount of speed. I still feel like there is too much sliding/drifting happening.To put it simply, I feel like you need to delete what you know from the previous MES games and come into this game with an open mind and appreciate what potential these physics have.There are some fun lines you can experiment with, for the most part I think the tracks are pretty fun. Most tracks are unique and that is a good thing. The only thing I don't like is sand and wet tracks probably should be less slow and slidey, and more of that boggy feelingOnto the stuff outside of the racing short and sweet. the only issue I kinda have is the number and names on the back of jerseys, they really do not look clean IMO. other than that it is pretty decent.The reason I recommend this game, is because I feel like these current physics could be awesome in future titles if they choose to continue to work of this games version. The game play relatively well how it is, if your into SX games give it whirl. but if your planning to not play often, I would recommend an older title.

_childDocuments_.review: While I did find some things about the game fun, I felt there hasn't been enough development behind one of the features I most look forward to in any type of racing game: Driver/Rider Customization. Even with the addition of female riders into this game, the baseline set by the first game of the franchise has not expanded upon only 12 or so different "heads", with the only changes available being hair and eye colors, and even those are limited. You have dozens of different suits, helmets, goggles, boots, etc... But you can't change the color pallet of the designs, thus if you want to find a particular color scheme, you're likely SOL.As they use similar (if not the same) game engine, let's compare this game to NASCAR Heat 4 by 704 Games.... Heat 4 has expanded on the customization of most things (though the custom car paint booth was a few steps back), and one of those things is fine-tuning of what your custom driver looks like. You can even change things like the particular colors and design of your driver suit, as well as even add logos from a (albeit limited) list.Even Codemasters has been able to add in custom helmets, and even custom schemes for the F1 games!On top of way-too-limited options, the physics are a bit wonky, and can sometimes glitch out (my bike would randomly change direction as if it was hit from the side by an invisible object). Plus, every time that I tried to "scrub", my rider would just preform physics-defying rotations and land headfirst into the ground. There's also another couple of glitches that were a turn-off for me.....THAT ALL SAID....... I would still recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of AMA Supercross. While I'm more into 4-wheels than 2-wheels in regards to motorsports, I did enjoy the first MESX game, and the gameplay I've had for MESX3 was more good than bad, despite any bugs or glitches I encountered. If Milestone can find a way to open up the customization options just a little bit more, as well as touch up on the physics, then they would have a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a giant improvement upon 2, but a pretty good game. If you are used to fast paced "hold down the gas and win" games this will be super annoying to play. Because of this focus on rhythm, if you aren't good at the game it will be no fun at all with you bouncing off every jump.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! It adds a lot of changes to the ground and air physics that are awesome! Honestly, I didn't even realize I wanted some of the changes they added. One example is the change that caused the bike to continue traveling in the direction it was when it left the lip of a jump. Another example, you can now lean back AND pull back on the handlebars! People have been referring to this as "three pre-load options". I thing that it's much more than that. For example, I can now (crisply) wheelie over bumps.I love the game so far, however- there are a few gripes... Please accept my apologies if this sounds whiny- I don't know how else to complain :)Let's get the bad stuff out of the way... Your rider still looks like he is sponsored by the local screen-printing company. The hideous fonts on the rider and bike are terrible. They are the same crappy ones that I never liked in the other games. @Milestone: Please give us access to the same fonts that you used to create the official riders' gear and bikes... Yes, this does matter to me because- wallpapers. Secondly, the clutch doesn't work properly. The clutch mechanic in MXGP Pro was spot on, but here- the clutch just cuts the throttle. This is annoying, especially indoors. Finally, the career lets you join an official team, but does not let you use the team's helmet. I have never understood why Milestone misses the mark every time with this stuff... Some of us would love it if we could make our rider look EXACTLY like our teammates- head-to-toe. Again- wallpapers.With all of that out of the way, let me just say- buy this game. It is awesome and really fun. I have played MX games for years and this one is def top 3 of all time. Sure, there are a few things that I wish that Milestone would change- but they're clearly putting a ton of effort into making this series better. Now, I only have to wait for better fonts and a clutch like MXGP Pro... Then the game will be perfrect lol

name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus
detailed_description: Coming Up Legendary Edition About the Game Granblue Fantasy has soared into the hearts of millions since its release as a browser game for smartphones in 2014, and will celebrate its sixth birthday in March 2020. Featuring Cygames' high-quality art, captivating sound design, and an ever-expanding game system, Granblue Fantasy has continued to charm its fans throughout the years. Now Cygames has partnered with Arc System Works, known for such popular fighting franchises as GUILTY GEAR and BlazBlue, to bring Granblue Fantasy to the world of fighting games, complete with top-notch game design and one-of-a-kind 3D graphics. Overview A new game in the Granblue Fantasy universe, available on Steam! This fantasy game blends fighting game action and RPG-style adventure. The gorgeous graphics and sound you expect from Granblue Fantasy, with an intuitive game system easy for both console and smart phone gamers to pick up. Throw yourself into matches or enjoy powering up your characters! *This content does not include digital purchase bonuses for the original smartphone/browser game Granblue Fantasy. RPG Mode: The GBVS RPG mode features a brand-new tale set in the world of Granblue Fantasy, fully voiced in both English and Japanese! Play through the story and upgrade your characters and weapons! Versus Mode: GBVS features an intuitive yet extensive battle system, with skills that can be activated with the touch of a button, a unique skill cooldown system, and super skybound arts that can dramatically turn the tables on your opponent! Players new to fighting games will enjoy the ease of controlling their favorite characters, while fighting game veterans will be able to experience the thrill of intense, tactical battles!

_childDocuments_.review: Build a fighting game with a focus on fundamentals and slower playstyles, making it fun and approachable for both beginners and veterans. Mix in a fantastic artstyle and soundtrack, a solid tutorial, and a load of single-player content.Steam sales? Don't need 'em. DLC fighters at $7 each? Yes please - and definitely don't offer a discount for buying multi-packs, either. Paid battle pass? Sure, toss it in there. Make sure everyone is spending a bare minimum of $100 to experience the full game. Nobody should be able to convince their friends to try it out.NEVER update the netcode, even if the game's life depends on it. Try not to reach out to new players or advertise the game in any way. Crossplay is absolutely off the table. Sit back and watch the player base drop to double digits. If done correctly, this should happen less than a year after launch.---Seriously, though, this game is a ton of fun... but I can only recommend it to people with money to burn and a high tolerance for the typical ArcSys netplay shenanigans. I hesitate to say GBFVS is a dead game, but it's close. It's probably worth trying if you're a huge Granblue fan, but I don't know much about the IP.

Oh, and it still has gacha elements if you're into it by the way!Overall good game that you might want to give a chance to; too bad it's competetive potential was so harshly held back by the COVID pandemic as we all now that fighting games blossom at offline events.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a big fan of Arcsys games, so I was excited to try out GBFVS and it did not disappoint.  The simple inputs allow for easy access to specials when the execution isn't quite there, and gives players a chance to further optimize as they play.  I like the slightly slower speed of GBFVS, when compared to GG or BB, allowing for more what I think is more consistent feeling neutral.  The visuals are flashy and the characters all have unique feels, without being so off the wall different that you can't readily hop in and play them (like some of the GG characters feel to me).  Overall, a great fighting game for competitive minded people.  And even RPG mode isn't all that bad; gives you something to feel out the game with as you unlock all the colors/weapon skins!

_childDocuments_.review: If you are interested in fighting games and don't have much experience with them, this is the game for you.A great place to start to learn basics and apply them to other fighting games. Highly suggest doing all of the tutorials in regards to game play and then the character that you will want to use before playing online. Once online you will lose a bunch but keep going back to what you practiced in the tutorials. Also if you are stuck against a certain character use the character specific missions for defending against them. Most of it is very useful in helping you get better so refer to it often in the early stages to help you remember some core things that will help you learn.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a whole lot of fun, and it has fantastic game play. It's a solid game with really gorgeous visuals and good voice acting all around. The music and sound design is really killer and it's a fun game. Online is decent enough and you're able to get in matches at a fair enough pace. The gameplay is fast, but a bit clunky; and it's something you can really get used to. It's great for beginners and great for veterans of fighting games as well.Those are the pros though. The cons are that the game can get a little stale after a bit if you don't play online too often and the game's base roster is laughable and it doesn't give you many options in terms of characters, with there only being about 8 or so characters available to play as from the get-go, compared to all of Arcsys' other games like Dragon Ball Fighterz, Guilty Gear, or Blaz Blue where they all have sizable rosters. The thing that sucks is that so many  of the new characters look like they should've been in the game to begin with. One of them (Beezlebub) should've been in the game to begin with since he is the Arcade mode final boss and one of the big bosses in the game.Overall, Granblue Fantasy: Versus is a solid game but I would tell you to get it on sale instead of getting it for a whopping 60 bucks with little content. This should've been a $40 game at MOST. However, it is still a 7/10. It's not great, but it's a little above your average fighting game. Wait for a sale of 40% or more before getting this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A very expensive game that has very little content and a very mediocre online experince, but has solid gameplay. So it's like Street Fighter 5 at launch - will satisfy your fighting urges but you aren't getting bang for buck no matter how you look at it. Granblue is a game that seems to epitomize the things that are wrong with japanese fighting games. It runs well, the game can be fun, looks great and plays pretty damn well, but everything in the mp section is garbage-tier. The franchise doesn't mean anything to me, so I can only judge the game based on its technical and gameplay merits. The cast has most of the main archetypes represented so if you feel like going for a slow grapler or a fast mixup-character, this game has you covered. We even get the classic dual shoto setup with one being more defensive and all-roundy and the other one being more in-your-face (think Ryu and Ken).The game also simplifies fighting games by removing the physically technical side of the game if you really want to use single button specials - called skills in this game. You have all your special attacks bound to a button+direction input to make using them more consistent and easy, thus making the game super accessible to most people. We also get a heavily scaling auto-combo of three-or-so attacks on all characters and a universal overhead attack to boot, so each character has an answer to crouch-turtling.The combo system in this game is similar to Street Fighter where you input frame-precise attacks to keep an enemy comboed up, and you usually start with an attack cancel. Featured also are two kinds of supers in the vein of SF4 with one being tied to your hp pool and being available as a catch-up mechanic. The supers are very well animated and satisfying to use and not dominating the game flow like Fatal Blow does in MK11. Sure you need to be concious of their existence, but they aren't a get-out-of-jail-free card like some games seem to have. The pacing of the game is on the slower side, and features a block button that has cross-up protection enabled, so defense is very strong. You can also use an invicible forward dash or spot-dodge to parry or evade pressuring attacks and close up on zoning, so matches can easily come down to a good slog.However, the PC port feels overpriced and rushed because of the following issues that pervade the multiplayer side of the game, and I don't expect them to fix most of these things. Steam doesn't show you recently played players, because why not.In-game money is useless I guess? Sure lobby avatars, stickers and stuff like that is cool I guess.No changing keybinds when queuing for ranked.No gacha codes on pc (don't really care about this tbh)Super small roster with paid DLC from the get-go. So consider the game to actually cost around 80€ and there isn't that much material here to justify this price. Like 7 stages by default?No crossplay even if Sony seems to be pretty kosher with it.Small and divided playerbase - so just go to discord. Can't friend ranked players.To be fair, a human being in this game is harder than it should be.Can't rematch in ranked beyond two sets.Lobbies are half-dead (north eu)Rooms are half-dead (north eu)Netcode is what is is - delay beased and unable to tell you your actual input delay. So have fun punishing ♥♥♥♥.No actual frame data available, just some indicators in practise mode. Watch it being added as paid DLC (cough tekken cough).

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 13 DECEMBER 2021:-They still haven't fixed the netcode, but the game is finally available at a reasonable price - $50 for the game with all current DLC included, or $20 for the base game, compared to a $60 game with two $35 DLC passes before.PROS:-I've enjoyed my time with this game enough to double-dip (also have it on PS4). It's one of the few titles that did the "simple to pick up and learn" thing properly; it's a completely new IP, so it's not clashing with any expectations, and the input shortcuts, mission mode, and relatively simple combo structure make it a good first fighting game to pick up and/or a good teaching tool. (The simple inputs are well executed, too - DP still requires a forward input so you can't mash it while blocking, except on the charge character, for example, and simple versions of special moves do less damage and/or have more cooldown.)-There's a lot of love put into the game for actual fans of the Granblue universe; every character pairing has a unique intro, the stage backgrounds are recognizable as battle backgrounds from the mobile game, characters' movelists are based on their mobile game skills, etc.-Single player story is pretty generic throughout the middle (good intro/decent ending) and relies on some investment in the GBF universe, but the RPG Mode's actual gameplay sets a good example for other fighters to follow, and has co-op availability!-Everything looks pretty. As expected of something ArcSys helped out with.DEPENDS ON YOUR PREFERENCE:-Despite the anime aesthetic, this game plays closer to a KOF (if it was 1v1) or "classic 2D" style fighter like Street Fighter. That may make you like it more or less. There are some anime-game-like aspects though; you can air block but there are air unblockable moves, and damage is insane in the corner.-Specials being on cooldown like they're RPG skills is weird, but it's an interesting way to implement EX moves, since the cooldown is negligible for L/M specials, meaning that using your EX fireball to extend pressure may take it away from you as a corner combo extension if that pressure leads to a hit; it's something genuinely unique about the game.-There's a block button. You've got Lancelot and Narmaya wanting to do nasty crossups, but there's a block button. Roll and dodge are tied to this button, which is not shared with other functions, and that enables some silly option selects like being able to dodge and tech a throw at the same time, to avoid getting throw baited by the universal hopping overhead attack.CONS:-The netcode lol. It's not as bad as, say, MK9, MvC3, Tekken 6, or BBCS, but... it's really not great. The ArcSys game I played the most was Persona 4 Arena (and Ultimax) - most of the bad matches (look if you're playing on WiFi with another country that's your fault) aren't nearly as bad as the worst connections I experienced in that game, but the mediocre (East to West coast of the US, or even a few states away really) matches are worse; I've had games where I started predicting the overhead instead of reacting to it and was still getting hit. You don't have the weird "pause and catch up" like T6 or the weird stuttering when it gets bad like P4A or BB, but instead you just feel like you're behind the game. //Now that the DLC no longer feels like extortion pricing, this is easily my biggest complaint with the game.//-Your local FGC members will try to force you to play SFV or Strive instead.

_childDocuments_.review: My thumb remains down until net code rollback. Buying this game on sale is a gamble, maybe they will do a rollback later, lets hope. - Update 1/25/23: I gambled and lost, apparently they are going to add roll back net code, but it's going to be in the next game, presumably it will be on steam soon. -Having played Blazbue for 7 years, I really wanted a fighting game with less bull***t to deal with. No instant cross up over heads that start a combo that can do 4k damage, instant cross ups while stuck in the corner, instant overhead attacks, or an overdrive that completely changes the mechanics of your character, as if having 35 characters to know the match up isn't bad enough. Stupid top tiers, why can Arakune curse me off of a combo he started with a air jab?!?This game is pretty fun but it some ways it's a little too simplistic, you can't start a combo off of an overhead(unless you counter hit with one), so there is little to fear from one. extremely simplistic combos.Tactical moves aren't too impressive, but hey at least they are there, and at least they are still updating the game even if it's minor balance changes. Most characters have a small move set, perhaps a little too low, Blazblue got that right imo.But on the upside, the game has a good pace, you still have all the fundamentals of a fighting game, while the game has an overdrive, it's a lot more tame and doesn't completely change the mechanics of your character. You do more damage, have faster overheads, and you can cancel it for a ultimate attack.Character intros and interactions are good, English voice acting is overall good, with some bad examples. I think someone forgot to give Percival's VA the context for all of his lines, and at least 2 characters sound like country bumpkins.Overall I like this game, and if you can get into an online game with someone who has good connection quality, the input delay is barely noticeable, but that's kind of rare. The player base will fall off fast after the sale, mainly due to the lack of rollback.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently got into the FGC community and started with Tekken 7 as my main fighting game(I played tekken 3-5 but never really got into the competitive online scene). That game literally was like asking a baby to feed itself due to its lack of tutorials and enormous learning curve, and although I have spent hundreds of hours into the game both on ps4 and pc, I still suck and sometimes even lower rank opponents raped me just by mashing buttons. I must admit, it will probably take me until the release of Tekken 8 to be even decent at that game. I have a love and hate relationship with that game. No game has enraged me so badly before while at the same time satisfied my ego to the fullest until I played Tekken 7. Recently I got demoted 3 times in a row in that game and just needed a break before I punch my screen. I bought Grandblue Fantasy Versus as I wanted to experience 2D fighting game for the first time and also, the characters in the series piqued my interest as they have great artwork and design. I must say, what a breath of fresh air this game is. Easy to pickup, GREAT tutorials especially for people like me who has never touched 2D fighting games before, each characters are unique and has certain niche but they all feel fair. Community(So far) has been very friendly and respectful, as compared to the Tekken community which can be really toxic at times(Ki charging, hate messages, Tekken youtuber beefs, degenerate Leroy and Xiaoyu players).  If you are using pad like I do dont be discouraged because this game is not too execution heavy. Online is great, not too laggy and gotta love that online room, it really feels like a place where GBVS players get together as a community and just enjoy and learn the game, while being respectful to each other. Single player RPG mode is very good!! I havent got into it much but it is definitely pretty engaging and well-designed. The mechanics of this game are simple, easy to learn and get into, but of course takes time to master. The price tag of this game is rather demanding but it is damned worth it. All in all, support this game. If you want to get into fighting games that doesnt require crazy learning curve and skill gap between players, and experience a good FGC community(Respect, learning together, and generally enjoy the game) pickup this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say something up top: my opinion on this game largely comes down to how I enjoy it on an aesthetic level. Seeing as I play Granblue Fantasy (the mobile game) basically all the time and fighting games almost never, what you have is somebody that is biased toward the IP and poorly versed in the actual genre I'm reviewing. Everything I'm saying here should be taken with a grain of salt. Multiple grains of salt, even.PROS:- Visually, this game is gorgeous. Visual effects are punchy, character models are that 2D-3D thing which ArcSys has down pat. - Music is a godsend. All the different remixes to character themes and the original game's OST are CANDY. Yasunori Nishiki (the composer for Octopath Traveler) being involved makes this unsurprising, and if I'm being honest, that alone was enough to make me want the game outside of my love for Granblue Fantasy.- English voice work is largely excellent. I know most people switch it to Japanese, but the English cast has some voice actors that I follow almost religiously.- I'm sure this is something that is typically a given (or at least required) with fighting games, but all the characters are super unique. I also just love how expressive they are. Some are similar, but none of them feel like copies. Some of my faves that I play are characters I suck at, but their design and personality sells me on them so hard that I'm willing to struggle.- Teaching tools and the training exercises are super helpful to learn the bare basics of combos and countering, but the more complicated stuff falls to you.CONS:- DLC is pricey, no doubt. Also, character packs that don't include the stages? Yike.- I'm going to defer to the people who know more about fighting games than me for the rest of this. As I said, fighting games are something I almost never play and you don't need me to tell you that it's one of the toughest genres to learn. I also almost never play online, so I can't speak to that experience. My online rank is F5, the lowest possible rank. Any negative feedback I'd have to offer comes from the fact that my brain absorbs fighting game tech about as well as a sponge absorbs a block of solid steel. Things like footsies, neutral, resets etc. take YEARS to bake in, and I simply don't have the time available to reach a point of even being COMPETENT.But considering that even though I'm hot garbage at the game and still found it enjoyable, I'd say it's worth giving it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: So as a fighting game fan, I had my own level of expectations for Granblue Fantasy Verses. What I got was something that most fighting game fans may or may not have been asking for. A fighting game where we (or at least I can) just relax. Granblue Fantasy Verses is the most lay back fighting game I have played in a long time, and that is not a bad thing. Granblue Fantasy Verses or GBFV, is an extremely easy to pick up and play. People who I can see picking this game up are Smash Bros players who are used to the way they play that game with pressing B and look at direction or down. That is not to say that the normal why most fight are played are not present in this game, you still have your quarter and half circles etc.Story (spoiler free): Now for people who do not get these characters and story, let me explain one thing. Granblue Fantasy story has been going on for a long time. Basic this is fan service to Granblue fans (which even I am new to this series) but if you want a little more background of the of the characters. You can go play the web/mobile game which you have to get though some ungodly downloads or watch 2 seasons of the anime to just get the jest. I did both and watch the anime to the end and the main oh boy its long. Back to my review of this story, if do not do what I said. The games story is still fun. The cast of colorful characters are nice to talk and team up with. The downfall with this story is its story mode game play, mix an RPG and fighting sounds really cool. But it has gameplay more like a beat em up. With boss fight breaking up the normal story game play which can be really fun and tuff in the end game.Normal gameplay: well it a fighting game, has normal fighting gameplay, two people throw down and beat the ever-loving crap out of each other with flashy moves and combos. Not much more than that.Soundtrack/ art style: both are really nice, as soon as I saw this art style, I fell in love with it. It’s just so IT is the best way I could put it. The soundtrack sounds epic, some of my favorites are kind of spoiler so not going to say.Online: this is the one thing that is not great which is a real shame. With how bad it could get makes it unplayable. This need to get fix but if DBZ Fighters is still bad, I’m not holding out hope.Overall, I give GBFV an 8.5 out of 10. It has much more room to grow and I think if this is your first fighting game, I would give this a shot, go for it. And for hard core player there is a lot of fun stuff for people that doing instance combos. Honestly just try if you want to relax in a good fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: But that doesn't just go for the character design and graphics. The UI is clean and easy to read. And that goes for the rest of the game as well. By design, it does a fantastic job to give information across. Characters don't blend into the background, hitboxes make sense, and the readability in general is just very good. The core gameplay mechanics of the game aren't too convoluted for beginners. And it has plenty of features that help with ease of access. Whether that be a Skill button to bypass motion inputs, or Auto Combos on close up hits that add leeway to special cancels etc. Make no mistake, despite it being easier to get into, it wouldn't be a fighting game without things to master. The reward for learning motion inputs, optimal combos that usually forgo auto combos, and other hallmarks of fighting games are all here and encourage players to get better at the game.  The game might not have the numbers of bigger and longer-running fighting game franchises out there, but that has its upsides too. It’s sincere and down to earth, with players from all skill levels interacting and helping each other improve at the game. Trying to recommend this game before was a lot harder, as it was very expensive especially if you wanted all the DLC. But with the recent permanent price drop, you can buy the base game for 20€, and the Legendary Edition (which includes all current DLC characters) for 50€. If you’re serious about picking up the game, I highly recommend buying the Legendary Edition since buying DLC separately will still cost you more.  You can’t really go around this aspect when discussing fighting games in 2022. Unfortunately, GBVS did not feature rollback when it came out, and it doesn’t seem likely that it will ever get it. Though, it must be said that the delay-based netcode found in the game is one of the best. Claiming that the online is unplayable would be a lie. After all, on a good connection you are usually playing with 2 frames of delay, which isn’t all too different than playing the game locally on a PS4. On worse connections it isn’t ideal, though. Rollback does allow for more leniency, after all. Where playing on worse connections can be endured more, which will always expand the number of players one can play with no doubt. Hence why this needs to be brought up.  If you’re the type of person who only wants to play through Ranked Matches and in Lobbies without ever seeking out Community Discords, you will have a harder time with GBVS. The recent price drop has made ranked and lobbies a bit more active for a bit, but aside from Wednesday Lobby Nights in the UK1 Lobby for EU, expect Lobbies to generally be dead (At least in the EU). It is not a long-running series where the number of casual players online allow you to play someone else all the time. It is a Discord Fighter, and you will have to interact with a community to get quick games and the most out of the game in general. All that being said, I have roughly 400 hours in the game as of writing this review, and most if not all of that time has been spend playing the game online. It has been a good time and I doubt I will be stopping any time soon. I can highly recommend trying out the game if you’re interested and join one of the community Discord Servers if you do as it will be the best way to get started, find people to play with, and talk about the game with others.

_childDocuments_.review: I was never a big fan of fighting games, I'm still not, I kind of hate playing them. BUT this game captured my heart with its cast, artstyle, beautiful graphics, music, style and most of all: *ACCESSIBILITY* ACCESSIBILITY is the name of the game. From the simple movesets that are easy to grasp but hard to master, to the fact that you can forego technical inputs and choose to use single button prompts for all your specials/supers if you're not as skilled at inputting/memorizing long command strings (like me), the fact the game doesn't just let the opponent combo you forever and lets slower methodical playstyles shine as much as rushdown ones and the fact that there is a bigger emphasis on resource management and cooldowns (Which I love as an RPG fanatic) that allow me, someone with weak mechanics, to focus on the fights and interactions/metagame themselves rather than fighting against the buttons and my fingers, the fact that there's legitimately good tutorials (something very rare in fighting games) for your characters but to counter OTHER characters and the tools you might struggle with is so welcome. OH, and let's not forget: A FULL FLEDGED SINGLE PLAYER CAMPAIGN?! Oh my stars!It blows me away that other fighting games, popular as they may be, are *light years* behind this one in terms of allowing new players to be eased into the game and the competitive aspect and properly teaching/rewarding them, this is not only the first FG I've been interested in, but the first one I've adored this much and play consistently with friends and even in random lobbies. Heck, it even got me to download the mobile game AND watch some tournaments. Which is crazy to me. I'd give this game a 10/10 but now that Versus Rising is fast approaching, I'd be remiss to not see that one as the definitive edition, so please pick it up when it releases! I promise you'll find something in it for you. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Never heard of it til I saw it on sale, saw it was an Arc Systems game and figured at that price, how can I not? Best $2 I ever spent. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. It's basically a beat 'em up disguised as a fighting game which are both styles I love. It's using the superior Arc Systems cel-shading, and surprisingly the single player RPG mode is just freakin' great, They are so generous with the animations so even when they're portraits talking at each other, it still watches like an actual show. The writing is interesting enough and I'm already getting into the story, and the voice-actors for ♥♥♥ are great and ENG are quite good. Above all else though, the fighting mechanics are extremely fun and the most generous I've ever seen to new players without dumbing the game down. Allowing a simple execution method that has a long delay is genius, especially in that both new players and veterans can swap between them to suite their style or even needs. For example, using the technical (manual) input can get exhausting after long play sessions, or even over-complicates execution of certain attacks during combat against vets. So even though there's a shorter delay, if you have no intent of spamming that skill again anyway, why not use the simple execution method for that skill? Genius, it truly is. I know it can't ever balances pros against newbs but it really goes a long way to help. I'm only 4 hours in, played mostly RPG, beat Arcade, and a match of Versus as well as a lot of training. Oh, and the tutorials are 10/10 excellent. If you want to learn this game, you easily can using the glossary. In fact, reading this game's glossary would even help you understand other fighting games if this were your first ever.I feel like I stole this. Thanks a ton to Arc and to the people to made the IP because apparently I'm a Granblue fan now?

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite fighting game!  I’ve been interested in fighting games since Street Fighter II, and I have to say that Granblue Fantasy Versus reaches a new high water mark for me!  Why?  Well, the character, level, and special effects art is the most gorgeous I have ever seen.  The characters and their scenarios are extremely likeable as well.  Their move sets are also very interesting.  I can watch the intros and outros again and again.  It’s really like a beautiful anime come to life.  (And I have a GTX 1070 - not the top of the line by 2021 standards - and I can play this game in stunning 4K!)  There are training modes and even a simple yet fun RPG mode.  This is also the type of fighting game that I personally love.  Not tag teams with helper characters on the screen all the time and a mess of combos that you can barely follow, much less pull off yourself.  It’s more of a traditional “footsies” one-on-one battle game.  If you like the classics, you’ll love this!And on top of all that, the number one reason I like playing it is that while it is complex enough for fighting game veterans, it can also be simplified enough for those who have trouble pulling off all of the moves and combos at will.  Let me put it like this.  You know Zangief’s 360/720 degree throws and Guile’s SSFII Turbo charging super?  In Granblue Fantasy Versus, there is a simplified input method.  There is a “special move” button, and to pull off different special moves, you simply press the button while holding one of various directions or no direction at all.  And the “supers” (Skybound Arts) are generally a quarter circle forward and the special button.  You can pull off moves with technical inputs and get some minor benefits, so those who are perfect at inputting them are at a slight advantage, but this dual-input situation still levels the playing field to an extraordinary extent.  Fighting games should ALL be about strategies and thinking about which moves to use in which contexts.  They shouldn’t be about actually managing to pull off a move.  Now, every character’s moves can be pulled off by anybody, and characters that you may never have used now become approachable.  (I would rarely use Zangief, and even Guile because of the supers that I had trouble getting to come out the majority of the time.)  Some high level fighting game players may think this is not important, but it is for many who would normally not attempt online matches or only play with one preferred character when they do.)The negatives that I have read about have been the delay-based netcode (rather than roll-back), the lack of players online, and the price.  And they are all warranted.  However, I’ve generally been able to have matches that play pretty well.  Also, I’m off some weekdays, and I was able to find some matches in lobbies (primarily the NY one) during the day when most are at work.  There are few people, and I wish there were a ton more, but I would not let this be the deciding factor.  And then, there’s the price.  I got this for 50% off (Character Pass Set with first season DLC characters and extra outfits for $40), and at that price, it’s a steal.  I’ll get more DLC content when it goes on sale as well.  Here is my recommendation.  For ANY fighting game fans, this is a MUST-BUY.  If you’re really into fighting games, you’re not late on rent, and you’re looking for something new to play soon, even the $80 would be worth it.  If not, and you’re able to wait a few months, add it to your favorites on Steam and get notified when the price drops.  If the $79.99 version goes on sale for $50 or less, JUMP ON IT!  And if you’re not really into fighting games but are interested in dipping your toe into this world, then this is really the best you can do.  I just have to reiterate that this has become my favorite fighting game, and again, I have been into fighting games since the early 1990s.  Check this out, and I doubt you’ll regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: (Review from a European player) It's a mechanically solid game that is relatively enjoyable with a group of friends or at offline tournaments and other gatherings. But the online is out right terrible and a gigantic step back from both Dragon Ball FighterZ and Guilty Gear Xrd -Revelator- 2. - World Lobby -On a surface level, the game's main way of matchmaking uses ASW's traditional world lobbies, but thanks to some changes it is an abysmal way of playing the game.First off, they decided that it was a great idea to remove connection indicators. This means that you have no idea whether or not you will have a good connection with people before you play with them. Because of that I've run into countless players who have had terrible connections most likely due to playing on Wi-Fi or because they were from another region entirely. Secondly, they've replaced the usual color rankings with a weird star system that nobody was quite able to decipher just yet. Basically, if the game deems another player to be at your level, then there will be a star displayed next to their name. This system, however, is almost always incorrect. The stars are extremely inaccurate. Color rankings were a much better way of judging relative skill. - Ranked matchmaking - Ranked mode uses a queue based matchmaking system that lets you use training mode while waiting. That in of itself is very solid. However, this method of playing also comes with a bunch of problems; the point system is terrible, the mode is too unpopulated to be played regularly, and the connection requirement setting does not work. I constantly get 0-1 bars despite setting the limit to "highest". Sometimes it will show you a 5 bar connection, but the connection during the match will be horrible anyway.- Player rooms - The player rooms look very identical to Guilty Gear Xrd to the point where it is deceiving. They lack a lot of the functions the Xrd rooms had, such as: automatic queuing, access to training mode, and join/leave notifications on screen. It's a terrible way of playing with a group because its such a hassle to do rotation manually and if someone decides to join without prior notice then the players who are already playing will have no way of knowing, meaning that it's utterly pointless to join player rooms that have more than 1 person in them. This is the definitive way to play 1v1 though, as there is infinite rematch.So all in all, it is very annoying to play this game online. Especially if you don't already have a group of players at hand.

_childDocuments_.review: Rated from a scrub with a background in fighting games, but never cracked into a top 8.- Beautiful art style.- Epic Soundtrack.- Easy to play. Plenty of depth to master.- Varied, charismatic base roster.- Stunning animations.- Helpful, specific tutorial tools in the Mission Mode.- Little touches like stage transitions, alternate outros and match-up based voice lines.- Online is dead.- All online features locked away until you play 2 ranked matches (which is tricky due to the above point).- When you do get online, delay based netcode dampens experience.- Anemic single player offerings.- DLC over priced relative to other fighting games and rarely goes on sale.- Fighting game fans with access to couch co-op or a friend on a nearby network.- Anyone looking for SoundCloud content.-  - Gorgeous visually, audibly and mechanically. Every pro on my list plus solid network play and a community that's still present. Not quite as easy to onboard with though.-  - Super streamlined and approachable for beginners, but also a dead community. Free to try at least.-  - A lateral recommendation. You could take this review and more or less apply it to DBFZ, although their online community is more vibrant and it'll be getting Rollback Netcode soon. More complex than any of the other games here due to the need to master 3 characters that are somehow mechanically distinct despite all being Goku.I intend to keep playing Granblue as I'm one of the lucky few with local friends who are also playing it, but if you're not so fortunate, consider my alternatives. If ever rollback is announced, purchase the base game immediately and consider a DLC character only if they really speak to you, as the core roster scratches a lot of thematic and mechanical itches. _childDocuments_.review: So many things about this game are great. The lobby system's great. The character roster's great. As much as it looks like an anime fighter, there's no dashing or double jumps; the mechanics are approachable without feeling shallow. It still demands good fundamentals over just spamming skill moves (which are even on a cooldown) such that you can be challenged without just, y'know, getting launched once and losing 80% of your health to a single combo (lookin' at you, Tekken 7... and that's not just salt talking. It's BS when it happens to me, and it's exceptionally BS when I do it). Each character has two types of supers that are all insanely hype and insanely creative, and, joyously, aren't activated by a single button press (lookin' at you again, Tekken 7, and especially you, SoulCalibur 6). It's got a decent training mode with small challenges to help you learn its basic mechanics, as well as a glossary that has descriptions for every character, weapon, stage, AND the game's mechanics and systems. Its stages are all wonderfully vibrant and varied, and its music does something that even some of my most favorite fighting games haven't been doing in the past several years: it has CHARACTER themes rather than stage themes. That's one thing I loved most about a lot of old school fighting games like Tekken 3 and the original Marvel vs Capcom. I haven't played a lot of ArcSys' fighting games, so maybe this is the standard for them and I can look forward to it for when I finally get Guilty Gear Strive, either way, I love it. The music helps to build up the character you're fighting, or the one you're fighting as if you choose your pick's theme. It's great. It's something I sorely missed from my favorites in this genre.But I'm sure just from the way I'm trying to sell all the good aspects of this game, you can tell there's something sorely lacking with it.Yup. The online. No rollback. I've come to understand from both SC6 and now this game why it's such a huge sticking point, because I can stand as much as 6-10 frames of delay, but 19? 19 frames HURTS, bro. If you're from Asia, it's not the end of the world. I can't speak for the three other regions, but in Asia, you'll find populated lobbies mostly in Japan and China, especially at night, and you're bound to find some people with tolerable connections. But that doesn't change the fact that if you've played games with rollback, this can and will be suffering.Of course, this game is so wonderfully polished that I honestly think its offline offerings are still worth it. If you've got friends nearby to play with online or locally, even better. It's a fantastic game that got me hooked on a world and characters I once avoided like the plague because there's no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way I'm touching another gacha game (for those who don't already know, Granblue Fantasy, the IP this fighting game sprang out from, is a browser/mobile RPG with, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it, WAIFU GAMBLING... ain't nobody got time for that).I wish ArcSys would go back to this game and implement rollback. They still have a sizeable playerbase of different skill levels. Yes, actually, it's not just diehards who'll stomp on you every single time, but there IS a lotta them too. They even have updates and community tournaments. This game's nowhere near either being deserted by its players or abandoned by its developers, but it could be so much better.Will they put it in though? Probably not, and that's turned and will continue to turn many, many people away who'd otherwise stick around for this game's fantastic presentation and gameplay.Will that stop me from playing? Absolutely not. Game's too good. Djeeta's too cute. Ladiva's too fabulous and wholesome. And it's certainly not gonna stop me from being one of the many people who still enjoy this game and are huffing the copium and hounding ArcSys to finally improve this game's online.ARCSYS PLS. ROLLBACK DOKO?UPDATE: I played this game a bit more after this review... like over a 150 hours more... and I can safely say that I still love it. Despite the miserable experience I've had with its ranked and lobby system, everything else it has to offer turned out to be far more worth my time. I've gone through the RPG Mode. The boss fights are insanely fun, with their own theme music that I wish was selectable in Versus mode. I enjoy the game's OST even when I'm not playing. I've unlocked all the Gallery artwork. I enjoyed its story. It somehow got to do a merging of different dimensions in a way that's compelling despite being very anime about it. Yes, like MK11, but without the time travel. It has so many interesting locations and characters and factions that get hinted at from the larger RPG lore that it makes me want to learn more about the world. Insane amounts of lore and worldbuilding... in a FIGHTING GAME. It's to a point where I almost WANT to play the mobile game (I tried, sadly the app's not available in my region). Granblue Fantasy Versus is honestly my favorite fighting game right now. Maybe for a long while. I want more of it. I still wish its online wasn't utter suffering, but there's enough in here that I don't regret the purchase.By the way, for folks complaining about the DLC for weapon skins, I agree with you on the way they price things, but just play the RPG Mode. You can unlock so many skins and colors from there without spending any money. There's some you unlock via the game's Draw mechanic which is like a gacha except you don't ever spend any real money for it. I don't even think you can at all in this, thankfully. You just get draw tickets from playing the game and completing bonus missions. There's others you unlock by gaining the weapon from completing challenges in certain chapters. And there's some that's random loot drops from mobs and bosses. A little sneaky that that's never mentioned to folks who might want skins but are only interested in the online, but hey, I personally consider those weapon skin DLCs as just grind skips for something that's entirely cosmetic, and the game's fun enough that I'm not tempted at all to take them just because I want more and different weapons for Vira to shank people with.UPDATE (2): RPG Mode tracks are selectable in VS matches now! Also, yes, Rising's coming out, but when this game gets as cheap as it often does, I'd still say it's worth getting if you want it for the RPG Mode, because Rising is a sequel with a new story, unlike how some reviews are painting it (i.e. as a cash-grab update, despite the fact that it's gonna get visual improvements, crossplay, rollback, an entirely overhauled lobby system, new moves for the whole roster, and a new story... sure, it's a "simple" update they can "just put in this game"🙄). It's good to grab the base game on sale even just as a way to prep for Rising's release if you wanna get a feel for its systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Update July 2021: A year later, and I unfortunately still do not recommend this game. The reasons I listed in my original review still hold true, although the community is even smaller now, averaging less than 100 people online at any given time, let alone in lobbies. In addition, the game is severely overpriced, more so considering there are now several additional DLC characters to purchase on top of the base game which still sits at $60.  As others have mentioned, the publisher doesn't seem interested in offering any discounts, and releasing new characters at $7 each when the roster was already small to begin with on top of battle passes and other paid additions just seems like gouging. I should add on a positive note that I discovered the game's mission training mode, and have found it to be a great way to learn new characters, see which normals are effective and chain or cancel into specials, and in general better figure out how the character plays. I wish other games would include such effective learning modes. Even considering the positives, with other newer fighting games apparently knocking it out of the park, the bar has been raised well beyond where this game currently stands. I don't see any reason to throw good money after bad and buy into a game that costs too much, uses outdated systems, and has a vanishing player base. This is disappointing, because I really wanted to get into this game, but it lacks the creativity and innovation to survive long-term.Original July 2020 review follows:Two things drew me to this game: the art style, and recommendations from the community that it was a friendly game for people who were new to fighting games. After spending several hours with the game, my frustrations with it are such that I cannot recommend it. The main reason I cannot recommend it is that just a few months after release there are not enough active players to justify a purchase, particularly if you are a beginner like me. After finishing my certifying matches for online play (more on that below), I tried to find a lobby for casual play. On a weekend afternoon in late July 2020 which should have been prime time, there were only fourteen (14) people online in just one North American lobby. The rest of the lobbies were completely empty. Every one of the other players was at least A rank, and many were S rank or higher. As a C-rank beginner, this made it impossible to find a match at or near my skill level. With such a tiny community I cannot recommend it for anyone, regardless of skill level.Here's what else I found frustrating: the controls are not sufficiently customizable for a release on the PC platform. You can adjust the inputs for battle controls thankfully, but nothing else. The game maps page left and right to the 'O' and 'P' keys respectively, and 'U' for opening a menu. Except that sometimes you use 'tab' to open a menu, and 'backspace' to return, but sometimes you don't and you use 'enter' instead. In other words, the interface lacks consistency. The game also lacks important prompts. After my first certifying match a character dialog box appeared with a prompt that looked like you should press 'enter' to proceed. Except when I did nothing happened, and there was no indicator of what else I should be doing to the point where I thought the game had frozen. I restarted my computer and after checking my drivers and attempting the certifying matches again the same thing happened: the game appeared to freeze after my first match. It was only through random keyboard mashing that I figured out I needed to press the 'U' key to bring up a contextual menu to proceed to the next match. The start screen also gives no indication of how to quit the game. NB - you press 'backspace,' which brings up an option to quit the game.The concept of RPG mode is interesting; the implementation, not so much. The storytelling is lackluster, consisting of talking head dialogue and exposition. The main reason to play RPG mode is to collect weapon skins to use in other modes. RPG mode's battle system is conceptually interesting, but confusing in practice. Interesting because your character is not locked into facing your enemy as you would be in a match, similar to the beat em up genre. This should open up lots of possibilities. It ends up confusing, however, because the game still uses facing-dependent technical inputs. Without being locked into a facing, several character moves become difficult to use. RPG mode gameplay is otherwise not particularly challenging. It mostly consists of mowing down waves of trash mobs until you reach a raid boss. Fighting a raid boss changes the control scheme again, and has you face the opponent rather than free move. The raid bosses are not particularly difficult, though the fights were enjoyable. RPG mode overall tended to feel like a chore I needed to do to unlock the full main game rather than a welcome addition. And for that reason, I would call it a missed opportunity.Now for what's good: The art style is gorgeous, and as fighting games go it is competent. If you have the option for local play with friends or family I'd say give it a go. If you're looking for a broader community, however, skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun.Backgound on the review: I'm not a Granblue Fantasy fan, I haven't played the mobile RPG at all. I am however a huge fan of Arc System Works. I'm a novice FG player, so not exactly the most experienced out there, but I do know the genre relatively well.The game is accessible. Everyone can pick up and play it without ever having played a fighting game, thanks to the simplified moves, that come with drawbacks but are waaaay easier to perform. Intermediate or experienced players will probably not use these and will be rewarded with faster move cooldowns for their more complex inputs.The cooldown system is fun. It still forces the player to manage their resources, but frees up the meter so they can use it for their supers, making them viable and strong tools without compromising other aspects.It's also one of the slower paced anime fighters out there. Combos are shorter, but deal hefty damage, there are no airdashes, and a lot of footsies are played in neutral. It feels like an in-between of Guilty Gear and Street Fighter and that fills a niche that doesn't really have anything else.Finally, the graphics are gorgeous. ArcSys has been doing it again and again with their 3D fighters, they consistently have beautiful graphics and are hands down the best looking FGs using 3D models out there. GBFV is no exception, a lot of care went into every single animation, and even the lip sync, which was admitedly not amazing in campaign cutsenes in previous titles, is now solid.
