_childDocuments_.review: Granblue Fantasy: Versus is an amazing fighting game with tons of content & simple yet brilliant & deep mechanics.It surely doesn't deserve the mixed ratings it currently has & I can't stand many fool's negative reviews even after it's recent changes , especially those who scream "trash netcode" & such, so here's my 2 cents in hopes to balance those out. To those unaware, game price was reduced from 60$ to 20$ for base game , while you can get Legendary Edition which includes all chars (Season Pass 1&2&Vira/Avatar Belial) + extra stuff for 50$.  This happened almost after a year of it's release, where game is still considered new & fresh , so Cygames apparently listened to it's playerbase. The only downside I see is that there is no special discount/bundle edition for complete edition to owners of the game & DLCs standalone are still expensive compared to base game's price but I hope that this will be fixed. To add more into this , Cygames are doing a survey regarding game's future which can be found here  (until 26th December 2021) 2nd & most importantly. Netcode. Asking for rollback is one thing but giving this game negative reviews just for that aspect alone is absurb. As a Day-1 Owner, only issues i ever had with the netcode was either with players from other continents & probably Wifi Users. I've played with almost perfect ping with even the other side of Europe. Hell, I've even played against some American players when EU lobbies were empty and half of those were playable too. Crying about the netcode while you have unstable internet/play on wifi or just copying the new trend about demanding all FG's to have rollback cause you ve read it much online is really sickening.  Those aside, to talk about the game itself. Game's visuals & soundtrack are actually superb & a joy to behold, as expected from ArcSystem. Characters are unique and with great variety on their playstyle, inputs & combos are easy to grasp & perform while remaining footsie lenient (you have dodge/roll but no air dashes & double jumps, neither FADC mechanics) playing a bit like old school fighters such as Street fighter 2. Offline content might be huge for some , since Story mode alone will take you 8-15 hours to complete & can be played in co-op other locally on online! To make it even better, it has an almost endless tower mode in which you farm for materials & weapon skins (that can be used of course in Versus & Online modes) All that plays like a 2D side scrolling dungeon crawler , with hordes of enemies and Bosses with unique attacks & patterns. If you into this , you can spend hundreds of hours alone on it. I bought the game Day-1 and Season passes separately and yet ,I have zero regrets, even if in most cases online used to be a ghost town. Of course, on each character's release day it was always populated for small periods. But all that might change from now on for the better.For the price drop and with all that content , the game's is a steal @20 bucks and is surely worth your time if you re remotely interested in Fighting games, Dungeon crawlers or GB's universe.  Hope to see the playerbase numbers rise as I also hope for it to get rollback at some point. But as it is right now , it still gets an 8.5/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: So I think this might be my first ever Steam review? But anyways, I play a lot of fighting games, and played the hell out of this on PS4 before it came to PC too so my hours might not reflect my actual gameplay time.But I think this is deserving of a talk about as unlike most fighting games, this game is designed for both longtime fighting game players and new/casual players coming into it.PROS:- Simple to play, hard to master: Granblues specials are not like other fg's where you have to always use things like dragon punch inputs, fireball inputs, charge motions etc to access them, they offer simple inputs as well as manual inputs. This is good for newer players who may struggle with these inputs while still encouraging to learn the manual inputs as the penalty for it is a slightly longer cooldown on the skill for using the easy inputs. Supers can also be done with simple inputs. But yeah, by far this is the biggest reason I love this game, I love the accessibility of it and yet how hard it can be to beat someone better than you in this game. It's very simple to see where you are going wrong, and it's a great game to improve yourself in, that's what I love about this game the most.- The skill system: This is probably my favourite feature of this game, the unique thing about GBVS is the skill system. Instead of a meter system where you use powered up versions of specials in exchange for meter, you can always access these ex moves in GBVS but in exchange your entire skill will go on a cooldown and you will be unable to access that move for a set amount of time. The only thing meter is used for in this game is for supers, one you can access at any time when you reach 100, and a 'desperation' super when you go below 30%. This may discourage some people, as it is a very very simple system, but for me I find it refreshing. The game focuses a lot on basic classic 2D fighter style such as a more balanced version of SF2.- Single player content is fun and good: RPG mode was actually kind of refreshing for me. FG's are not exactly known for having amazing single player content and that's not really the focus for me either. I want to just get on and play people and improve - but I went back and tried out the RPG mode and I was surprised to find it wasn't just beating up mindless AI opponents (though an arcade mode does exist for that with character endings and all that you can unlock), but more a Streets of Rage'esque mode where it's more of a beat 'em up style. It's obviously not as great as an actual beat 'em up game but it was refreshing and a new experience. The side scroller levels get very tedious and repetitive I won't pretend, but the boss fights are legitimately great and have mechanics to avoid and all that, so that is very fun. The customisation is based on the gacha game of Granblue where you collect and upgrade weapons onto a grid with different elements opposing each other, with a skill based system too. It has multiplayer too though I doubt you'll find randoms in the queue for that, so would probably need a friend.CONS:Activity: This isn't a con on the game itself but more the accessibility of the game. There's obviously no crossplay between this version and the PS4 version and the game can be kind of dead online. Ranked especially, you will mostly find people in the open lobbies of the game. And while the avatars and art are all great in ASW fashion as they are known for, the amount of actual people in the lobbies can be.....very low, you will have to go on in prime hours to get many games. Don't get me wrong, for me at least, I can still find games every single day on the open lobbies, but there are also a lot of times where I'm just sitting on an arcade cabinet with my avatar and just.....waiting....hoping someone will show up (who is also not going to be laggy/a lot worse than me who will leave after one game). However, the discord community for this game is huge and places exist where you can just ask people to play, so if that's for you, you can do that too - and most people in fact prefer the PC version as it has a better netcode, though that's not saying much, which raises me to the next point.Netcode - The netcode for this game is.....to not mince words....not great. It's delay based, and it's not a great delay based netcode either. It's definitely playable and not as bad as other fg's atm such as UNICLR and Samurai Shodown or whatever, but it's still not passable in my opinion.Prices - I have no idea why this game is still so expensive, and the pass you get from steam does not even give you all of the character colour DLC and the two stages, it's just a character pass. PSN made slightly more sense as they came with gacha codes for the gacha games, but the prices are the exact same on the PC version, and they're way too expensive for the content you get.Final thoughts: I highly recommend this game for anyone who might be considering getting into a fighting game but don't know what to learn. This is a great first fighting game. I also recommend this to any fighting game fan who might be looking for a simple game to outfootsie people in but not be too boring, a bit of anime sprinkled in here and there, which this game has plentiful of. Not much else to say sorry if I rambled, reviews are not normally my thing I just kinda felt like leaving one as this game is pretty unique to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue Fantasy: Versus is a great fighting game, I highly recommend it to beginners in the genre or people looking to get into fighting games, it's a really nice entry-point to the genre. That said, this doesn't mean it has no depth or that you'll find it easy to defeat other people, as it is an easy to play, hard to master game... I think I'll die without ever getting to know how to play Eustace or defeat Seox, though I'm still working on that second thing!The characters are all really nice and they have a lot of personality to them, this steems from the fact that GFV is based on the wildly popular Granblue Fantasy mobile/browser game, a JRPG with gacha mechanics (pretty generous ones as well) that's been running for quite some time now, and boasts a massive playerbase (though this might actually be the total registered accounts) of a staggering 32 millions souls. To put this in perspective, if the whole GBF community were to band up and invade Bolivia, the bolivians would have to fight off like 3 GBF players each on average. And I'm not quite sure they'd be able to win.When it comes to gameplay, it features an interesting mechanic which I think they were the first to implement it. You see, most characters here have like 4 special moves, 2 supers and a handful of normals, kinda similar to STRIVE in this sense. By inputting R1 + a direction, your character will use a special move.Now, you might think that's some casual ♥♥♥♥. But nope, by using this shorthand command, you can get some really interesting plays, like using a charge attack while on the offensive, a reversal DP without having to fear a miss-input, or a command grab without doing a 360. This does have a few disadvantages as well, to reward players who use the technical inputs: DPs usually do a bit less damage and so do command grabs, and the specials enter a longer cooldown period.Yes, specials have cooldowns. Every time you cast a special, it enters a brief cooldown preventing you from using it until it has refreshed. By using the technical input, you can pretty much spam specials like in any other fighting game (unless you use the EX version, which will always have a bigger cooldown, yet will also be shorter if you use technical inputs). Cooldowns add a layer of complexity to the game, as you'll have to decide when to use your DP or big damage move, and your opponent can try and make you pay for it.Supers, however, have no R1 input, and they can be cast using a QCF + X/A, being this the easy input, which also has disadvantages in some cases (like reducing the damage a bit, or making it so it has less range)There are also supers that are available on low health only, they do more damage than the regular ones, and have flashy animations.Making it so the supers must be used with a QCF is a nice "+1" exercise to eventually get the players to give the technical commands a spin.Other than that, it has a pretty massive single-player experience built in, complete with your staples like a great training mode, arcade mode, and (something unique to this game) an RPG-mode that re-tells the story of the original game (I think it mostly adapts the first part and Paradise Lost) via VN-like cutscenes and a sidescroller beat'em up that features various missions in which you can also learn to use the characters (they have a little tutorial for each of them, complete with explanations on what do the moves do) and if that doesn't seal the deal, it even includes a "mission mode" that teaches you all the mechanics of the game, inputs for every character, basic combos and even countermeasures for most matchups.One of the biggest issues it has is  the lack of the so-called Rollback Netcode. I'm sure a lot of people would appreciate it being implemented soon. Delay-based netcode is not the devil, however, it does work, take my word as a Tekken 7 player that's been playing since Season 2. But well, nowadays rollback netcode and full crossplay should be the standard for fighting games.Overall I'd give it a Free Draw Ticket over whatever today's SSR rate is in the gacha. Awesome game, if I had more money I'd buy it again, so with my taxes the argentinian government can buy one for themselves as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game all around, great for beginners. Has a number of unique mechanics that veterans may find interesting and refreshing.I want to make clear that I have never seriously played a fighting game before, this is my first. This review is from the perspective of someone new to fighting games.What's great about this game is that anybody can load it up and do a basic combo pretty much immediately using the game's auto-combo system. Hit 3 buttons, do a special, and there you go, babby's first combo. Of course these very basic combos are not optimal, but as a new fighting game player it makes a big difference to be able to do SOMETHING when I go into a match. The game has several mechanics that will work in your favor if you are a new player, making it exceptionally easy to pick up and play. If you can press 4 buttons, you can do a combo. No hours sitting in training mode required. Yes, you will get destroyed online, there's no way to avoid that no matter what game you are playing. But once you start getting matched with players of your own skill level you will have a lot of fun. If you can play with friends, even better. Playing against a new character for the first time is an exciting experience because all you can do is improve.The art and music are fantastic, exactly as you would expect from Arcsys.Not going to whine about the netcode because I don't care that much. I am able to play games with my friends overseas with only 4 frames of lag, so take that how you will.RPG mode is a ridiculous grind, but you have to do it if you want cool weapon skins. Acts as pretty good execution practice if you're a new player, but otherwise don't expect to be impressed.Definitely give this game a shot if you are new to fighting games and have been looking for an excuse to get into the scene.

_childDocuments_.review: Slower Paced - great fundamental system. As a Guilty Gear and BlazBlue Player, having a game like this is sobering. I never got into Street Fighter, but this is a game that could be an "Anime Street Fighter". Granblue's system does not feature airdashing, commits its fighters to every dash and jump, and tries its best to look as good as it can. It can be a new challenge for anyone, but an approachable one.And it looks good. Every one of these Unreal Engine fighters from ArcSys are very good - the question is if Cygames will be good stewards of their own game.The game is expensive - there's no two ways about it. A full priced game, with no more features than its predecessors in DBZ, Xrd Revelator, and Xrd SIGN, has a lot of DLC that is also premium priced. The core gamer in me has gotten their money's worth out of the game, but the casual gamer in me still looks sideways at the actual full price of being IN this game.I recommend this game for anyone that loves Granblue and likes fighters, but I'm giving ArcSys and Cygames a disapproving glare at its product management.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently one of the best anime fighters available right now in terms of how the game actually plays, so many basic systems were introduced into this game that makes it feel so tense and brought back memories of how SF2 feels where any character could comeback at any moment if they had super.  The introduction of a block button did worry me abit but after playing it for 100s of hours on the PS4 version I've found it's completely optional and actually helps make it easier for other fighting game players to enjoy the game (Smash, MK, Soulcalibur ect).Was abit skeptical about the cooldown system with special moves but it ended up being such an amazing but simple mechanic that drastically changes how matchups are played during a match (Gran has no ex dp? go ham on him)  Game also runs fantastic I can run this at 4k 60fps at max settings with absolutely no issues on an RTX 2060 setup.Only huge downside is the delay based netcode arcsys has been using since the early days of Guilty Gear Xrd, I'm hoping that moving forward with future instalments of this series and others that rollback is a feature that is standard across any fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, I know nothing about the Granblue franchise but love Guilty Gear.  The problem with Rev for me is my fighting game days of fast reflexes and chaining together 1-2 frame FRC combos are long behind me.  Guilty Gear is an incredibly technical fighter with an insane amount of mechanics that is pretty inaccessible from the wider community.  It has its place in the EVO community and the franchise is amazing, but us slow people need something else.  Granblue fills that void so perfectly and without being shallow (for technical depth just look up Narmaya's guides - and holy____ is that character loved.  I think her fanbase might be larger than the entire GBVS fighting community).Going to Granblue, I not only found this game to be accessible but you can tell that an immense amount of love was poured into this game by the devs.  To speak to the volumes of this game, during my sons party we had a bunch of kids over from 9-15, about 12 of them.  I popped this on with 2 Xbox controllers and it pretty much dominated the house for the next 10 hours.  Everyone, including the adults in the room were absolutely mesmerized by this game.  The kids and teens had no problem picking this up with the young kids standing a fighting chance against the older ones thanks to easy inputs.  Smash players adapted almost instantly and loved GBVS.  The whole room pretty much stopped what they were doing when someone got Super Skybound Art'ed.I think this is a truly easy to learn hard to master game.  There is a huge amount of depth here and I think this is the perfect in-between for Street Fighter and Guilty Gear.  Also the english voices (despite what the hardcore weebs say) are pretty good.  Also, I was told RPG mode was pretty boring but I found it fun.  There are some pretty well done boss fights that are truly action-RPG like with AoE avoidance, patterns, and attack windows.One thing I also like about this game is it just has this generally "positive energy" about it.  Many of the characters are friends with funny dialogues (Lowain is amazing).  Many of the fighters have good attitudes and messages.  It's nice to see that now days.Additionally one thing that is overlooked is just how painstakingly each character moveset is designed to match the personality of their fighter.  Gran's attacks are filled with imbalanced strikes and junior level swordsmanship but he seems to pull through fights through sheer willpower.  Katalina is much more measured, like her personality, and fights very defensively with strategic pokes.  There isn't a single moveset where their personality does seethe through their moveset with every attack.Everything is beautifully animated, with all of the animated cutscenes, supers, intros/exits looking like a AAA miyazaki movie in 4k.  There is alot of quality here and to me this is well worth the entry price.  I hope for many new seasons of fighters (I'll buy them all) and a strong community to support the game.For anyone who is looking for a first fighting game, or veterans that are looking for something different that isn't based on 100 airdashes and 50 hit juggle combos without losing the depth of what makes a fighting game good -Granblue is it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is super easy to pick up and understand and fun as all hell. Nice change of pace from the bombastic action of BBCF and Melty Blood for me. Character designs are immaculate and gameplay systems are engaging. There are plenty of matchmaking Discords to find matches on as well so you don't have to worry about matches. And now at a greatly reduced price, I can recommend it to anyone who is thinking about picking it up. I do hope in the future that we get the JP only announcer DLC and prices reduced in general because for anyone who bought before the reduction, it is rather pricey.My one gripe with the game is, obviously, the netcode. Delay based netcode is less than ideal for a game of this type. However, the director of both the original game and GBVS stated in May of 2020 that he sees rollback as a must-have and wants to add it. And considering ArcSys has said previously that retrofitting for games such as GBVS is possible, but up to the publishers of those IPs, I think it's likely that we'll get rollback implementation with the new battle system in Summer. Only time will tell.

I got this so I have a not-dead fighting game to practice basic fighting game skills here and there, and it's basically perfect for that. It's also a relatively simple and easy game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot better than I was expecting. The roster is on the smaller side, but I feel that's been mitigated by each character feeling vastly unique compared to one another. The gameplay is very solid as well, compared to other arcsys games I've played that's very focused on solid rushdown gameplay and air dashing across the screen, this game is more focused on playing footsies with a traditional neutral style similar to street fighter. My main gripe with this game right now is with the online and the netcode. The netcode itself isn't as bad as I was expecting from arcsys, half of my matches usually run with 3 frames of delay and feel playable for the most part, while the other half may run around 6 frames of delay which can occasionally mess with my inputs, but the online is still playable and enjoyable. Ranked matches always display ping before you decide to get into a match which is good for avoiding laggy fights, but for some reason the same thing isn't done in online lobbies. When you join a lobby, ping isn't displayed for other players so whether or not you get a match with solid connection is kind of a coin flip. Most matches I've played felt good for the most part though, but It's probably worth noting I play in NA which seems to have the most populated lobbies right now, so it's possible finding good matches if you play in another country may be difficult. Besides that, this is a great fighter for both newcomers and vets, with a solid tutorial and even a game mode dedicated towards teaching players matchup knowledge. I feel all this game needs is some quality of life changes for online play, and adding rollback netcode could definitely improve the stability of matches, but overall this game is a 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I have been playing 2D fighters since SF had only two pressure sensitive buttons.  I have watched the trends go from sprites, to polygons, and now we have anime cells on rendered backgrounds.  This game addresses many of the missteps brought about by both Capcom and SNK.  And everybody knows I love SNK to pieces but I have to speak truth to power.  Capcom went all-in on 3D models and I have to say that they look unnatural in an SF game.  Samurai Spirits did the same thing and again it is unnatural, albeit better than everybody else's attempts at the same.  That in itself is a boon to the great corp that is SNK (fanning a little bit; okay I hear you....).GG is a pretty game with some of the same producers as this title but it pales in comparison.  The heavy amount of mechanics in GG makes the game nearly unapproachable.  The strange hit boxes never really gelled for me.  That combined with the advanced combos and the volume of derived play styles is daunting and I'm a serious vet of the genre.  I remember cleaning out many 'o pocket full of quarters in a good ol fashioned Sega arcade.Anyways, GBFV (GranBlue Fantasy Versus) is an answer to a prayer that many expats from Capcom (umm, nobody ever leaves SNK!) have embraced.  Sure, it's light heart themes with the music and characters when they are posing or standing still BUT........   there is a visceral and gratifying crunch to all the animations in this game.  Oh wow, there is even a track on the BGM that features a voice.  Few games execute braver.Bravo Devs!  Instant Classic.  So good was the job that I bought the full package at 80 shellbacks, noticed that all the characters weren't even available yet, and didn't wrinkle not one cm of my forehead.  I just went through and enjoyed.  She provides full aggro transfer with the animations and voice acting is 10/10.  Awesome job voice talents!!!!!!!   Now if only we could get more HAND DRAWN ANIME and not all this unnatural 3D characters.  Even if the hits that SFV chars deliver are hard with all the glorious particle effects, when the models are silly looking so is the overall impact XDGranblue Fantasy Versus.... nuff said; buy with confidence.  See you in the lobby.... in like 2 months lol.PS: Narmya is like the best char ever.  Super well polished.

_childDocuments_.review: After lurking on Team Spooky and a number of other streamer's channels I decided to take the plunge and buy this game. It was worth every penny. Seriously, I haven't had this much fun with a fighting game since Soul Calibur 2. The artwork, animation, and music are all out of this world and the system itself is very easy to learn. As an old timer I've appreciated the easy inputs far more than I thought I would, because they allow me to focus on improving my mental game (footsies, spacing, punishing etc.) without having to worry about whether or not I can execute a dragon punch or double fireball motion in the clutch. The RPG mode was a nice surprise too - there's more to do here than just online matches. TL;DR Granblue Fantasy Versus has rekindled my love for fighting games and for that I have to give it a thumbs up.I do need to acknowledge that the delay-based netcode is not great. Most local lobby matches are 4 frames or less which feels fine, but I've had ranked games that were 12+ frames and it just straight up felt like I was underwater. The netcode was obviously built with countries like Japan and Korea in mind, where the physical distance between players is small.

_childDocuments_.review: positive things:-ArcSys did another amazing job with this game. Visuals and soundtrack are great, the characters are cool and the gameplay is very fluid.-Its very beginner friendly and easy to get into without being too casual. There are tutorials for almost everything. -All the characters are the same input wise. They all come with their own unique moveset and skills of course. Its similar to DBfighterZ in a way.-I feel this game is more counterhit based. There are a few big combos but dont expect another Guilty Gear or DBFZ here. -The Story /RPG mode gives me slight SoulCalibur vibes because u can unlock different weapons with different attributes for each character. You can even use them as weapon skins in battle against other players. Another nice feature is that missions in story mode can be played coop. So if there is a hard quest, then just get ur friends to help u out.-Online feels pretty good too. No lag issues on my end.negative:-some people could complain about the lack of character because at the time of this rewiew there are only 12. not a big deal tho so u can ignore this one.-there is alot of lore to this franchise, so its a bit hard to understand what is going on at times. I didnt know that there was an anime and a RPG game of this.-the game doesnt have a V-Sync option but it definetly needs one. There is a way to force V-Sync on the game by adding a command in the Engine.ini file via text editor.-there are some major balancing issues wich need to be fixed. for example: if Vaseraga (big heavy guy) fights Metera (archer) its pretty damn hard to get even close to her, even tho Vaseraga has hyper armor and stuff. I got perfected 4 times in a row due to projectile spamming. Usually i am able to deal with stuff like that in other games like Mortal Kombat or Street Fighter, but here it felt impossible to me. Maybe there is a way around that i havent tried yet. Im still new to this game.-the price tag of 60 bucks is bit much in my opinion. i know that its new on Steam, but the PS4 version has been out for a while, so if u consider to get this game then u should wait for a price drop. 30 bucks or less are perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, easy to play and hard to master as they say.I might be a bit biased as a Granblue Fantasy mobile player but I think the game captures the essence of GBF very well and plays smoothly as a passable fighting game. Not as fast paced as BlazBlue or Guilty Gear, not quite as technical and  as Street Fighter, I have to admit there's absolutely no balance regarding the moveset of the characters but the game hits the sweet spot overall as a 2.5D fighting game.There's the classic arcade and versus modes, an RPG mode where you get to play it like a beat em up kind of game and collect stuff for your "weapon grid", an online mode that I haven't touched, plenty of decent tutorials and 'missions' you can go through. The concept art is straight from the GBF mobile game and it's as gorgeous as it was over there, music is beautiful and I believe most of it is from the mobile game as well, UI is sleek and responsive, plenty of PC options unlike most console ports. Everything feels high quality.As for the downsides, I don't have a lot of bad things to say about the game, as far as fighting games go I love asymmetrical game design and fluid easy-to-perform combos. If I had to complain about one thing it'd be how long it takes to start up the game with the "Connecting to Server" pop up just staying there for a while, but that's a nitpick.To conclude, the game is pretty damn expensive, even moreso with the added DLCs and character packs. Honestly I don't know if it's worth the full price, but definitely worth a buy with a bit of discount (%30~%50), especially the character packs. Beautiful game, interesting characters, good quality production.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid game for learning the Fundamentals of 2d Fighting games. Also a fun title for fighting game veterans who want a simpler title to play on the side. If you've played Street Fighter II or V this plays kind of like those but you have a few extra defensive options like a block/dodge button (still can hold back to block but you do better against crossups with the button), the option for (weakened) 1 button specials, and auto combos off of very close normals to help one confirm into combos. I'd say more but this review isn't meant to be long. Just know this game is a good starting place to play 2d fighters while still staying fun for long time players of 2d fighting games. The only thing it really lacks is complex techniques and gimmicks to mess with that other 2d fighters from Arc System Works library tends to offer.Edit: Just pick up the sequel instead. I can't really recommend this anymore but don't want to change the old review cause.

_childDocuments_.review: A beginner-friendly fighting game with very attractive sprites. Special moves are easy to execute. Really fun game!It's a pain and a half trying to find another person to co-op with in the RPG mode. The game was released to NA a few months ago and it's already difficult finding someone. Very unfortunate for those who enjoy co-op related things. There's also no cpu vs cpu in versus mode, which I feel should be a thing in fighting games. _childDocuments_.review: While I'm giving this a "no" recommendation over all, if you already know people who are good at this game you might enjoy it. I know a few people who wanna play this game, so I'm probably going to play it enough to lab then play with just them. I doubt this will become my "main" fighter though. First off this game is a fighting game where it has gacha mechanics. This is automatically a huge deal breaker for most people I'm sure. While these are limited mostly to single player you won't have very many customization options without forking over $220 in DLC for all the costumes and weapons. Story mode creates a huge dissidence from how you're "suppose" to play the game when it's actually a fighting game as it relies on a single "skill" button system. Where as in, say, training mode you're rewarded for NOT using the catch all skill button and using exclusively manual inputs for all abilities and actions. Stuff like having a dedicated block button feels so weird and out of places when you can just hold to block too.Speaking of training modes, worst tutorial and training system I've seen as of late. Yet another Arc Systems game that's going to be a Discord Wiki fighter where the community has to teach people how to actually play; developers, please make it so I don't have to join dozens of fighting game community servers to learn your game I'm begging you. This goes for the jank beat'em up story mode AND the main game too. All tutorials are labeled "missions" which have letter grading attached to them. This could fine if they explained anything in these training missions. Most of your objectives are simple like "Block Attack" then "Punish!" with nothing else but a minor hint on how to perform the action. I had to watch a long video just to learn a basic mechanic of the game.For an Arc Systems game, a high profile AAA fighting game studio, this feels like it's lacking dozens upon dozens of basic features that indie game fighters have added five or even ten years ago. One of my biggest gripes is that in combo training you can't flip starting sides nor does the combo diagram change the input directions as you cross up or change sides. Would be really cool if there was a way to pass around a combo file so I can practice a combo someone else made for me. Even seeing the percentage of where I fail at a combo or having slow mo would be nice. It boggles my mind the brony fighting game has better quality of life features than a current Arc Systems game released three years ago.Hopefully I can update this review with their next big update/upgrade I can firmly recommend this game to people. I did get this game for super cheap so I guess I got my money's worth?

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a fun arcsys title like many others. However this game strays away from its traditional acrsys anime fighting game signature where you have crazy movement like IAD (instant air dashing), jump canceling and so on which usually make the neutral game crazy. But what it does instead is copy the old school "footsie-based" Street Fighter II formula and it's a nice change of pace especially coming from Arcsystem works who are not really known for making these types of fighters. Nonetheless they nailed it, like they always do.I personally am not that big a fan of super slow paced heavy neutral fighting games where you mostly press buttons to poke your opponent out to death without needing much combo conversions, I think Street Fighter 4 is dope as I grew up with it AND Street Fighter 2 since my father had kept his SNES from a while back, but aside from those exceptions I think I prefer it when arcsystem works gives us way more movement options and crazy combo potential in their games. Again, not saying I hate Granblue Versus. I think the game is fantastic but in all honesty, if a player who's new to fighting games were to ask me right this instant; "Should I buy this game or should I wait for Guilty Gear strive?" I'd probably recommend them to wait for strive. I've always thought Guilty Gear was the better game compared to blazblue, dragon ball fighterZ and now granblue versus, but this time around it seems as though it's even MORE worth it than before to wait for the new guilty gear since it has been confirmed that strive will in fact run on roll back netplay for its online which not only is a first for arcsystem works but will also make the possibilities of playing online with people fruther away from you ASTRONOMICALLY better. So to recap; granblue's a solid fighting game with amazing visuals thanks to its godlike devs, has a fun little RPG mode that's an interesting take on story modes, it's more old-school fighting gameish in terms of playstyle so it's definitely super easy to get into, but the online is atrocious so I'd recommend waiting for GG strive if you wish to fight people a lot online later on.

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue Fantasy Versus is an incredible addition to the modern fighting game roster. Whilst it's upsetting that the world seems to have done everything in its power to dampen GBVS' success, the same cannot be said of the community.I'm re-writing my review to address some of the false claims that you'll see fairly commonly addressed in (recent) negative reviews of the game.Both of the major western regions (NA and EU) have active player bases. We run lobby night events where everyone gathers in the public lobbies which frequently (even recently) have completely filled up the lobby.I can still actively queue ranked and find matches, though I do not advise this as like with any other fighting game, its ranked matchmaking systems are pretty piss poor.If you're looking for something more, both sides of the community have active discord servers that facilitate discussion, matchmaking and events for the title at pretty much any moment in the day (or night, thanks Jundo).It's incredible to me how many people seem to actually be viewing this as a negative thing. It's inarguable that the monetisation of GBVS up until this point has been egregious at best. However, what the game needed more than anything was better bundling of content to help incentivise new players to take the leap in purchasing and trying the title. This is ONLY A GOOD THING for existing players, more people playing and talking about the game will only serve to give existing players more opportunities to play and talk about the title. Please stop being so shortsighted with your reviews. This is a step in the right direction and hopefully we'll continue seeing the publishers pushing the monetisation to a more reasonable place.I'll keep this nice and simple, if the lack of Rollback Netcode is a dealbreaker for you, I cannot recommend that you get the game, and I understand if that's the case, it's your prerogative. However, this game does have functional online and the best delay based netcode that you'll be able to experience. The unfortunate reality is that this is often not enough to facilitate the level of online play that some people are looking for, and thats understandable.It's unlikely that the game will get rollback netcode for a plethora of reasons, but given the recent display from the developers and publishers its clear that they plan to support GBVS well into 2022, more so than ever before even, with plans for support for the title and the community going forwards.

_childDocuments_.review: Been told from many people that the battle pass concept has been scrapped. which was my only real issue with the game. Good on them, but its probably poor sales not the goodness of their heart that removed it. Regardless its gone and I can recommend the game again. Whelp this review didn't age well, a game that was already expensive with expensive dlc packs and felt the need to screw over steam players with no codes for GBF now has seasonal battle passes in it. You can now pay $11 for the PRIVILEGE to grind your ass off for small rewards like unique character skins OH BOY!... or you can pay $30 to skip all the grinding and have the rewards... This honestly disgusts me, and not even the fact it exists, more looking ahead cause this wont be the last one, its just the first. They will soon have enough seasons that you've sunk hundreds possibly thousands into this little crappy pass to get things the honestly the game could use as natural padding as something to do. While we have a netcode so bad its actually less laggy to play the game with a friend via steam remote play than to play the game on offical connection."A fighting game for non fighting game players" wait wat.That may sound weird but its honestly true. There's often a stigma for fighting games that discourages non regular fighting game players from wanting to try them cause they are too difficult if you're not used it, also there being nothing to offer for anyone who doesn't enjoy enjoy constantly pvping other human players. GBVS manages to have plenty to offer the more casual player.The first change is simplified inputs. Anyone who has played fighters enough know execution of complicated inputs to do specials and combos has always been a barrier to anyone wanting to get into fighting games. GBVS has very simplifed input systems very akin to a smash brothers game, and not to alienate the more hard core player they still have string input. I actually find myself mixing between doing string input and simplified cause some things are easier to flow together in one vs the other, and the game allows you to do so. You can even use simplifed in online matches so it evens the playing field from a matter of execution to who is the better strategist.Pvp not your fancy? me either, I'd rather explore the game's world and take in its characters, while the fighting story mode is okish for this, there's better. They have the amazing RPG mode to play which lets you experience the game and world of Grand Blue Fantasy and go through the game with your character in a more beat em up action game style, even getting a more condensed version of the mobile games rpg systems. This was a lot of fun for me and the story even continues the moblie game's story somewhat and kind of forging its own story.The game is still adding more characters and story currently, so there's still even stuff to come back to. if I had one complaint, the game with all its dlc gets rather expensive, you are paying for quality made stuff but if its too expensive I completely understand and I suggest waiting for a small discount, I honestly suggest waiting for a discount anyway due to steam version not getting any codes for use in GBF. But otherwise you cannot go wrong with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: GBV is a back to basics fighting game from Cy Games and ArcSys. If you have ever played Street Fighter or Guilty Gear, you will understand almost immediately what the system is trying to teach you. There is a dedicated story mode, which is separate from the arcade mode. The artstyle is heavily detailed, which is what you would expect, especially when ArcSys is coming from all that DBZ money. The game looks great, and does a decent job of introducing you into the Granblue world. (I know literally nothing about Granblue Fantasy at all) Characters are slowly being added with each season and it seems that the roster good enough to most fans.GBV has the 4-button layout that matches Guilty Gear, having a light, medium, heavy, and special. Combo strings usually rely on building up the buttons, but the systems implemented make it easy to get your combos out. There is also a dedicated block button that can be finagled into a dodge mechanic as well. All of this culminates into ground games with spacing being the best advantage. The online gets jittery here and there, but I have thankfully not run into anything too awful. Overall, GBV is a very solid and great for Granblue fans.

This game is an artistical marvel. Arcsystems are just on another level. Gameplay is fun because for a casual fighting game player like myself, it's easier to get into. It sacrifices a lot of depth and complexity in comparison to let's say Guilty Gear. But i don't view it as a negative, cus come on, i can't do half of the GG mechanics and just don't understand the rest. So this streamlining was a positive for me. Simplified inputs are a bonus too. Some of my friends can't do a quarter circle if their life depended on it. With simple inputs i can at least drag them into this game. For a hardcore fighting player, GBFV may become stale rather quickly, but i had fun with it.Lack of rollback is also regrettable. But i played mainly with my friends on local and didn't have latency issues XDMusic was kinda forgetable for me. It's not bad, it's just barely noticeable, a background.Would recommend this game for casual players, newcomers to fighting games, gacha-simps and for weebs of any kind (Cuz all the girls are so cute!)

_childDocuments_.review: One of my absolute favorite fighting games to come out in recent years. From the game play to the artwork in this game its nothing short of beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: These are some of my quick initial impressions... I like this game and I like it quite a bit actually. But there are few reasons why I haven't and why I simply cannot recommend this particular release.And I just have to mention that the online features (store, statistics, seasonal, etc.) at least here where I live cause the game to get stuck in loading / downloading menu screen. It tends to take much much longer than what I deem reasonable. Sometimes it can last for minutes but on average I timed that it takes at least 30 seconds to resolve. It takes time to learn which menus want to take connection and download and it gets quite annoying fast.I also need to mention that the default gameplay keys are just physically impossible to play this game with. And I play almost exclusively with keyboard and mouse. And I'm not a stranger to playing fighting games with a keyboard. Thankfully the gameplay keys can be rebinded and I strongly recommend that people do.On a more personal note I really hate the WSAD keys for movement in fighting games in-particularly. We have perfectly fine arrow keys for movement and that's how it should be controlled. Attempting to emulate gamepad layout on a keyboard is just insane and proponents of such layouts need to be taken behind a sauna and shot with a gun.Furthermore I simply don't like the fact that the cutscenes are clearly done in 3D but the framerate is limited in them to just a few frames. I guess that they've done that in an attempt to emulate look of 2D anime or something to that effect. But it just doesn't look in this game in my opinion. It can look decent and for example in ArcSys's own modern Guilty Gear games it is fairly acceptable although I don't think it looks particularly good there either. But here that effect is just particularly annoying for some reason.So like with Naruto games at Steam, I just cannot recommend this port. Technically it runs fine and I didn't experience any major issues with it.However I should mention that the monetisation model here is quite greedy. It isn't as bad as it is in some other games and I don't think it's particularly anti-consumer. But still paying 35€ for extra characters feels quite steep in a game that normally doesn't go to sale and costs around 80€. And there's that FoMO meter which encourages you to play like this was a job which I always find eating away the fun I might have with playing the game in-order to meet the "next seasonal level".Once I got over those hurdled and into the game I did quite enjoy this and will play more later. In many ways this regular ArcSys game but with a Granblue Fantasy theme. They've done some interesting things with various characters but I haven't played enough to have a solid opinion of them all yet.Some of the gameplay modes are quite fun. I'm also extremely happy that Granblue Fantasy: Versus runs just perfectly in Linux as well through Valve's Proton compatibility layer. I didn't encounter any issues while playing. I tested this in Gentoo GNU/Linux with kernel version 5.13.4-zen using official Proton 6.3 release.Also just like in most ArcSys games the music is pretty good. Sound design however didn't seem on part with their usual releases. Also the voice acting (JPN) seems to have audio quality issues but the voice cast from what I experienced thus far is doing excellent job acting out their roles.I'll come back to this at later time and update this if I have more to say. It's a good game overall. It's just a lazy port but not as lazy as for example the Naruto games are.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: Feels like playing a graphic novel. Backgrounds are lively, character animations are pretty smooth, UI is clean and easy to read. If you're looking for Single Player content this game has more than any other fighter out right now with an entire RPG story mode that turns the game into a beat-em-up like Final Fight or Streets of Rage.Gameplay: This is a grounded footsies, street fighter-style game with an emphasis on accessibility. The Guard button eliminates left/right mixups so there is only high/low unless you catch them not holding. There are also the Roll and Dodge mechanics, which let you gain advantage in certain situations so you're not stuck walking and blocking all the time.There is a 'special' button that allows for very easy special inputs (ex: Forward + Special for fireball, Down + Special for shoryuken, etc.) but you can also use classic quarter circle, half circle, 360, and z motion inputs like other fighters. Using the Special Button causes the cooldowns of your special moves to be longer and they do less damage while the 'technical' inputs reduce the cooldown and increase damage. This helps to ensure mashing the special button is not the optimal solution. Speaking of mashing: this game has an auto-combo system that is both useful and non-optimal so beginners can put strings together easily without dumbing down the combo routing at deeper levels. The cancel windows for moves are a little more strict than SF5 but not as bad as pre-Strive Guilty Gear titles. Community: With the EVO announcement and new mechanics just added (Overdrive, Backdash, and Rush) it has a larger playerbase than it has in a while, ranked is populated with similarly-ranked other players, and the official Discord is very friendly.I like the accessibility, the graphical style, and a few of the characters' personalities but I dislike the netcode (Delay, not rollback. It can get rough, no lie).If they implement rollback it's a 9/10. As of now it's a 7/10 for great graphics, smooth and accessible gameplay, great tutorials, and interesting characters.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this review, I feel obliged to say that - speaking strictly of the core gameplay - Granblue Fantasy Versus is perhaps my favourite fighting game right now. An emphasis on footsies, a generous buffer system, and optional one-button special move inputs makes the game very kind to beginners, while still rewarding intelligent play and mechanical skill with wall-bounce and juggle combos.BUT...does that mean I recommend Granblue Fantasy Versus? No. At least not on PC, and especially not if you're on a budget!Firstly, the price. It's an ArcSys game, so what do you expect? The main game bundled with the base roster of 11 playable characters, delay-based online play, and a singleplayer/two-player co-op story mode is all priced at a whopping 80$ CAD. Purchase it with the character pass set, bumping the roster up to 16 playable characters, and you're paying 100$ CAD. If you want the two DLC stages you're now paying 111$ CAD just about. And that's not counting future dlc character releases, which will all cost you an extra 9.50$ CAD each. Naturally, prices will vary depending on your national currency, but any way you slice it this is one expensive fighting game.Secondly, delay-based online play. The flaws of delay-based netcode and the advantages of rollback-based netcode have been discussed to death, so in short, delay-based netcode means the online play is...not good. It doesn't help that the online lobbies are, for the most part, a wasteland devoid of life. To get the best experience, you'll have to play locally or find an online community.Thirdly, the story mode, or "RPG Mode" If you're dead-set on playing Granblue Fantasy Versus on PC, the only value you'll get out of RPG Mode is weapon skins usable in local and online play, a handful of fully animated cutscenes, and a whole lot of visual novel-esque cutscenes with a textbox taking up a third of the screen while some mostly static 3D models slide around on top of it. The core gameplay of the RPG mode at its best is interesting, at its worst is time-wasting, but it's usually just something to turn your brain off to.If you were playing on PS4, however, reaching certain milestones in the RPG Mode (and Hell, even just owning the game and certain DLC) would earn you substantial rewards in the actual Granblue Fantasy mobile game, for those of you that care. On PC, none of these rewards are present at the time this review was written.So finally, do I recommend Granblue Fantasy Versus? Yes, on PS4. At the time of writing this review, you will get more rewards from the RPG Mode, on top of having better populated online lobbies if you play on PS4 compared to PC.

As mentioned, some of the default keybindings just don't work, you need to reassign them. Player 1 can never use a controller, even if there is no keyboard plugged in. Now the reason why I don't recommend the game at this point in time is being two major reasons.First, with lackluster netcode and no cross play, the online pc player base is dwindling and so it is coming to the point of having to find people through discord to play with, which isn't something I find fun to do. In a competitive game like this, this is inexcusable (out of date)This game is great. It is yet another gorgeous arc system works fighting game, but this time with a very unique footsie-focused flavour. Skill/Specials are cooldown-based instead of using meter, the cooldown depending on if using manual or easy input as well as the strength of it (Light/Medium/EX). The Supers use meter and typically only get enough charge for 1 per round. The game is very grounded as there are no air-dashes and most characters have no air-specials and even then only one of them has an air projectile.Combos are a lot shorter but also more heavy-hitting, giving the game this very tactical and calculated feel as you'll be relying mostly on netrual and footsie plays.The roster is a bit small but every character feels distinctly unique, with only Gran and Katalina being the closest in design as they seem to be the "Introductory" characters like Ryu and Ken.There is also a singleplayer/Co-op RPG mode which is pretty neat and lets you unlock cosmetic weapons to equip on characters when playing online. I think the only disappointing things about this game is the fact that there is no casual match queue, so you have to use the same lobby system of dbfz, which also means there are no private lobbies, and that it .I really love this game and I would recommend it to anyone, with the warning that the netcode is the same as other arcsys games like ggxrd and dbfz so if you have issues playing online with them, don't expect this game to necessarily have better internet play.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game a lotIt's pretty much the game I've wanted for a long time: a very "oldschool" ground-driven fighter with an emphasis on footsies and patient spacing, but with some modern fighting game twists. To give a brief rundown of the mechanics for those that appreciate that sort of thing:-You can't chain cancel normals at all except the throw-range-only version of your standing l,m,h normals.-There are no air mobility moves (double jumps, air dashes, etc.). You can block air to air but not air to ground.-You can tech throws but doing it with less than predictive timing means you still take some damage.-You have EX versions of your specials but instead of costing meter, this puts the whole special itself on a short cooldown, which leads to some interesting situations and trade offs.The hitboxes and priorities in general are also balanced towards being able to punish almost any normal from the very tip of the attack, leading to some very fun but also extremely intuitive SF2-esque footsies and neutral. Also while the game is not combo heavy (hit confirming into a special is about as far as it goes in neutral) a lot of your EX specials will wall bounce or juggle in the corner so there's still a lot of fun but short high damage combos and resets for those willing to dig in.There's also a really cute rpg mode that plays like a Guardian Heroes-esque sidescrolling brawler. If you've played GG Isuka, it's a bit like that but feels a lot more functional and fun to play and with a lot more content. Haven't dug too deep into it though so can't offer much more thoughts.I'd say the only downsides are the delay based netcode and the steep price on both the base game and the DLC (without which the roster is a little on the small side). Personally I don't mind the "seasonal" dlc plans much more compared to "buy a new version of the game in 1.5 years and throw your old one in the bin", but the prices involved are a bit steep atm and I have a hard time recommending to my friends who might not even have the connections necessary to enjoy playing online. Still I think the game is worth it if you're not strapped for cash and like the above ideas, I've certainly enjoyed it more than any of Arcsys latest fighters and plan to put a lot more time into it.Also it's a fantasy themed fighter (a jaw dropping gorgeous one, at that), and we need more of those. Oh and some of the music was done by Nobuo Uematsu. Zooey's theme sounds like a PS1 era Final Fantasy mid-boss track. So yeah, it's pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: So I think this might be my first ever Steam review? But anyways, I play a lot of fighting games, and played the hell out of this on PS4 before it came to PC too so my hours might not reflect my actual gameplay time. But I think this is deserving of a talk about as unlike most fighting games, this game is designed for both longtime fighting game players and new/casual players coming into it. PROS: - Simple to play, hard to master: Granblues specials are not like other fg's where you have to always use things like dragon punch inputs, fireball inputs, charge motions etc to access them, they offer simple inputs as well as manual inputs. This is good for newer players who may struggle with these inputs while still encouraging to learn the manual inputs as the penalty for it is a slightly longer cooldown on the skill for using the easy inputs. Supers can also be done with simple inputs. But yeah, by far this is the biggest reason I love this game, I love the accessibility of it and yet how hard it can be to beat someone better than you in this game. It's very simple to see where you are going wrong, and it's a great game to improve yourself in, that's what I love about this game the most.- The skill system: This is probably my favourite feature of this game, the unique thing about GBVS is the skill system. Instead of a meter system where you use powered up versions of specials in exchange for meter, you can always access these ex moves in GBVS but in exchange your entire skill will go on a cooldown and you will be unable to access that move for a set amount of time. The only thing meter is used for in this game is for supers, one you can access at any time when you reach 100, and a 'desperation' super when you go below 30%. This may discourage some people, as it is a very very simple system, but for me I find it refreshing. The game focuses a lot on basic classic 2D fighter style such as a more balanced version of SF2. - Single player content is fun and good: RPG mode was actually kind of refreshing for me. FG's are not exactly known for having amazing single player content and that's not really the focus for me either. I want to just get on and play people and improve - but I went back and tried out the RPG mode and I was surprised to find it wasn't just beating up mindless AI opponents (though an arcade mode does exist for that with character endings and all that you can unlock), but more a Streets of Rage'esque mode where it's more of a beat 'em up style. It's obviously not as great as an actual beat 'em up game but it was refreshing and a new experience. The side scroller levels get very tedious and repetitive I won't pretend, but the boss fights are legitimately great and have mechanics to avoid and all that, so that is very fun. The customisation is based on the gacha game of Granblue where you collect and upgrade weapons onto a grid with different elements opposing each other, with a skill based system too. It has multiplayer too though I doubt you'll find randoms in the queue for that, so would probably need a friend.  CONS:Activity: This isn't a con on the game itself but more the accessibility of the game. There's obviously no crossplay between this version and the PS4 version and the game can be kind of dead online. Ranked especially, you will mostly find people in the open lobbies of the game. And while the avatars and art are all great in ASW fashion as they are known for, the amount of actual people in the lobbies can be.....very low, you will have to go on in prime hours to get many games. Don't get me wrong, for me at least, I can still find games every single day on the open lobbies, but there are also a lot of times where I'm just sitting on an arcade cabinet with my avatar and just.....waiting....hoping someone will show up (who is also not going to be laggy/a lot worse than me who will leave after one game). However, the discord community for this game is huge and places exist where you can just ask people to play, so if that's for you, you can do that too - and most people in fact prefer the PC version as it has a better netcode, though that's not saying much, which raises me to the next point.Netcode - The netcode for this game is.....to not mince words....not great. It's delay based, and it's not a great delay based netcode either. It's definitely playable and not as bad as other fg's atm such as UNICLR and Samurai Shodown or whatever, but it's still not passable in my opinion. Prices - I have no idea why this game is still so expensive, and the pass you get from steam does not even give you all of the character colour DLC and the two stages, it's just a character pass. PSN made slightly more sense as they came with gacha codes for the gacha games, but the prices are the exact same on the PC version, and they're way too expensive for the content you get.Final thoughts: I highly recommend this game for anyone who might be considering getting into a fighting game but don't know what to learn. This is a great first fighting game. I also recommend this to any fighting game fan who might be looking for a simple game to outfootsie people in but not be too boring, a bit of anime sprinkled in here and there, which this game has plentiful of. Not much else to say sorry if I rambled, reviews are not normally my thing I just kinda felt like leaving one as this game is pretty unique to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, first of all, I just wanna go over the fact that I bought this game for the following reasons:1.) I LOVE fighting games, though not all of them need to catch my desire to play them.2.) Ark System Works have been one of, if not THE most popular 2D Fighting game creator in existence, responsible for the works of the Blazblue series, Dragon Ball Fighter Z, both of which I've played and loved, and many more; Most notably, Guilty Gear. Being made by this company is not the main contributor, but is a BIG factor.3.) I have been a fan of Granblue Fantasy for about 4 years now; the fact that it became a Fighting game was a fantasy-come-true.Having these 3 factors made this game an INSTANT buy for me, popularity be darn.I've played this game for bout 100 hours, and here's what I think; take it with a grain of (gacha) salt.When compared to the other 2D fighting games in the same creator's list, it's pretty simple and nothing fancy like the others. It's a pretty footsies-based tread and combos mid-screen are not common (though still possible given the right situation). Don't let that fool you though; despite it's simplicity compared to other 2D games, it has it's own charm. The fancy stuff is when you (or preferably your opponent) is literally backed to a wall where the REAL damage is. Getting comboed with a wall behind you is the last thing you want, and is where the show starts. You'll see your healthbar drain a LOT more than it would in midscreen. That said, it's also a satisfying thing to A. get the opponent to the wall, B. get a string in, and C. actually pull off the combo. Sure, this is pretty much a given in most, if not ALL fighting games, but with the difference between mid-screen and wall gameplay, the game makes this VERY apparent.Speaking if Combos, the game rewards those who can pull off more advanced techniques. Arc System Works has somehow been adapting to simplifying their games for even newbies to feel good in landing the simplest strings, but hasn't forgotten the more experienced players. In this game, there are easy inputs for each character's special abilities. moves like a "hadoken" which needs a quarter-circle input on the D-pad plus an attack button can be done in this game with just a mere press of a button. However, if you decide to forego the easy input and perform it the old fashioned way, you're rewarded with given practically no cooldown to use that ability again. Yes, using the easy input is offset by being given a cooldown of a few seconds before being allowed to use that move again. Don't worry about that cooldown so much though; given the right circumstances, if you land that hit, you'll likely find yourself in an offensive that you can use the other tools while waiting for that cooldown to finish, so it's not really discouraged even for experienced players.For balance, I'd say it's in the right track, but it's probably because the game has only a handful of characters. it IS still a new IP of Arcsys, so the game needs time to grow.Outside of the main fighting game aspect, there's also an "RPG Mode" that allows you to delve into the lore, though if I was to assume, it's not canon and is made purely for this game. Still, it helps other players who are not into Granblue fantasy get into the lore and understand who is who, what is what, why is why, and why Vyrn keeps claiming he's not a lizard. Unfortunately, I've actually yet delve into the RPG Mode myself since I DID buy this game for the fighting game aspect, so I can't really give much of a review there. what I DO know is that playing the mode also allows for unlocking and choosing the appearance of your character's weapon. It's purely aesthetic, unless you believe the change in weapon will distract the player.Graphics? OK, I may be biased here, but it's just FANTASTIC for a 2D fighting game. The characters are 3D rendered so you can definitely enjoy every nook and cranny of their figure. And as someone who's played the game and seen the "Grancypher" only as a still image, seeing it in it's 3D glory COMING OUT WHILE YOU ARE FIGHTING WITH SOMEONE was a sight to behold; it was a miracle I wasn't completely distracted with the real-time beating I was giving while reveling at it's splendor.Music? The game pretty much remixes the main game's music, and as expected of Arc System Works, they did a FANTASTIC job doing so. Legit looking for the soundtrack of this game and putting it on my phone.Story-wise, I sadly can't review that. As I've said, I've only played the fighting game part, not the story. However though, I CAN say that the main Granblue Fantasy game has fantastic story; heck, it's one of the main reasons why I love that game. If we're getting the same story writers for this game, expect good stuff. again, take it with a grain of salt.TL;DR, this is a great 2D fighting game to add to your collection. Even if you're not a fighting game fan, if you're a fan of the main granblue fantasy, this may tickle your curiosity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun for offline versus with friends. The easy specials make it pretty approachable, and having attacks on cooldown is both thematic twist for MMO genre, and a nice way to balance easy specials. The controls are also universal between characters, so it's easy to pick up and try out for everyone.That said the roster is pretty small - even with all additional characters. The game is also sold in too many pieces. If you buy just base game then special versions don't get discounted by base game cost, the season passes don't have stages, so you have to buy them separately (and with how little stages there are it gets bland pretty quickly). Compared to other games in genre this is pretty painful process - especially since the game gets discounted to dirt anyway. Just give players one-click solution to buy this game...The visuals are really nice, using Arc-sys 2D-like 3D. It's coupled with really good looking aesthetics from the Granblue world, so it's a joy to look at. The game also doesn't have too high requirements, so it looks perfectly smooth even on SD. Specials are flashy, SFX are great. The intro animations for characters are always the same, but they say different things depending on the opponent. _childDocuments_.review: Probably the best footsies style game I have played so far. This game, compared to other traditional fighting games, is very simple to get into and have fun. It's made simple because of a button dedicated to using skills, which changes by using directional inputs. However, there are still technical inputs you can do which rewards more damage and less cooldown and overall better to use. The technical inputs can be simple as a quarter turn, but the others that I have trouble with, like the right down-right command or half turn forward inputs are usually what I use the skill button for, and it helps so much.Besides the gameplay, the RPG mode is decent and you'd want to beat it to unlock Beezelbub. Unlike a game like FighterZ where the single player was just monotonous, RPG mode changes it up from time to time and has some cool bosses to fight.I highly recommend this game for people looking to get into a 2D footsies style (where the gameplay isn't about stringing together a 50+ combos, but more of getting hits in and dealing damage) fighter game. Very fun and pretty much the entire roster has their own charm and personality.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:The game itself is a good fighting game I recommend it to anyone who's versed or new to the genre. There are many built in tools that help explain a range of helpful information. From tutorials about basic mechanics of the fighting game genre to match-up specific training modes that teach you how to punish troublesome moves you'll likely see.It takes a more "old school" approach to gameplay with a more stressed focus on neutral and fighting game fundamentals. This comes as very refreshing at a time where most games attempt to "speed-up" gameplay with more focus on button-pressing and long combos.The presentation is gorgeous. Simply looking at screenshots of this game should be ample proof of that. WIth amazing in-game "cutscenes" reserved for supers that are continuing to be more impressive. (Soriz's SSBA animation is the coolest thing in the game). The music also top-notch with memorable tracks all fitting for a fighting game.THE BAD:The netcode of this game is pretty bad. Released in early 2020 the delayed based netcode is rarely every stable, making it a frustrating experience to play at times. Even compared to other ARCSYS games, such as DBFZ, the delayed based netcode seems to not be at the quality previously seen. The HUD displays the delayed frames above your name in an online match and it's very common to see that number constantly moving up or down. Compared to the aforementioned DBFZ, which will usually at least keep a constant amount of delayed frames, I can't help but feel GBFV's use of a poor netcode solution (delayed-based netcode)  isn't even implemented that well.As of now, the only way to unlock colors and weapon skins for characters is to play through the single-player "RPG" mode. I honestly don't know who they made this mode for. As a fighting-game player it is a horrible, mind-numbing tollgate you must pay with your time in order to pass. As a person who enjoys RPGs as well as mobile Gacha games, this mode fails to satisfy both of those needs as well. It falls in an awkward in-between of all three genres, leaving you with an incredibly mind-numbing experience.You will also need to grind RPG mode after completing it to get the crafting materials/draw tickets necessary to obtain the rarer weapon skins. So even after completing RPG mode for the first time, prepare to pay more time-tax to get the rest of unlocks.It's fair to note that I suspect this will be changed in the future when more DLC characters are added to the roster, since a larger roster means more required materials for all the weapons and colors... which means more time in RPG mode... I just can't imagine they would still expect us to play so  much more RPG mode in this situation... right..?CONCLUSION:Overall, GBFV will most likely remain to be a staple for the foreseeable future of the FGC. It makes a successful effort to lower the entry barrier for new players of the genre, as well as focusing on more "old school" gameplay to keep veteran players coming back for more. If it wasn't for the unsatisfactory netcode and hard-requirement of grinding through the single-player "RPG" mode for skin and color unlocks, I would have no complaints about the game. Even so, recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Versus brings the beloved Granblue universe to life with stunning anime-inspired visuals and smooth, polished gameplay. This fighting game is designed to be accessible for newcomers like myself, with intuitive controls and simplified special moves that make it easy to pick up while still offering depth for veteran fighting game fans to enjoy. The roster may not be huge, but it’s diverse, with each character showcasing unique moves and distinct playstyles that keep gameplay fresh and engaging. Interestingly, despite my experience with many other fighting games, Granblue Fantasy: Versus still feels refreshing and unique.The RPG Mode adds a story-driven experience where players can grind, customize their builds, and dive deeper into the Granblue universe. While the story isn’t particularly deep, it is original and offers a new perspective to those already familiar with the franchise. Online multiplayer is generally stable, although pretty much deserted these days.Whether you’re a dedicated Granblue fan or simply love anime-fighting games, Versus is packed with charm, easy-to-learn mechanics, and captivating design choices. Though there are a few minor drawbacks, it still remains a valuable addition to my fighting game collection today.

_childDocuments_.review: YES, it's good.The lack of rollback is what killed it in the first place.But my baby will live on.I figured i'd make this review since Rising is comin' out this year which LOOKS to be similar to how Rev2 might've worked. I can't confirm it because of the lack of info BUT i can compliment pre-Rising GBVS itself.GBVS is one great entry for fighting games in the ArcSys catalogue. The RPG Mode which plays like a beat-em up fightin' game, which has lots of content to go through with it's challengin' and rewardin' "Hard Mode" and many unlockables, givin' fightin' games a progression system similar to M.O.M from Guilty Gear but expanded upon.It's hell of a lot of fun to go through with a friend, that's where the RPG Mode really shines with it's amazin' boss fights.The traditional bread and butter fightin' game is still here, though! With it's easy to pick up and learn but hard to master controls, i have absolutely loved the gameplay since i got it one or two years ago. To me, as a scrub, it has a lot of DNF vibes to it's way of givin' the toolkit out to the player, although the tutorials could be better.I gotta emphasize though..This game is not combo heavy. While yes, you do chain attacks and do combos, specials, etc. It isn't as technical as a French-Bread title or somethin' like that.A lot of people don't give this game a chance because of the IP not bein' a new one or the infamous rep it got from havin' delay-based netcode. But at it's core, this game is still a lot of fun. I will always be a Guilty Gear player first and foremost but this thing has always brought me back, even if it's just to mess about at a LAN party (because if i play gg it's unfair with my mates #flexin') or to run through some quests in RPG Mode.If my suspicions were right about Rising bein' kind of like Rev2 for the game, then i'll update this review once i've gotten my hand on Rising which brings to whether or not i think you should buy it NOW or later.Well, the most logical answer would be to wait for Rising. You'd basically get more than what Legendary Edition has anyway. Even if it was a new game, pick that up instead (Unless it'll be hot garbage)The rollback and additional content is much welcome. Fall Guys momento.But if you're too hyped and need to sink your teeth in now, you can, just... don't play PvP online?As you can guess, i'm hyped. But also, i've been comin' back to the game a lot recently which is kind of why i wanted to write this "review".
