_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful 2.5D art style, and incredibly smooth game play.This game is a lot more neutral heavy than most anime fighters, in the sense that right off the bat there are no insane combos that last half the round.While most anime fighting games are known for their incredibly technical combos this game is very beginner friendly with the tutorial being very well done and even offering matchup advice. Granblue differs from other anime fighters with a spot dodge and roll forward as a new option to reposition and reset neutral instead of waiting forever for your opponent to drop a hit on block pressure.Having Something as simple as rolling or spot dodging makes this game feel much more Dynamic and adds an extra element to pressure and reading their reactions.There are only two types of supers in the game called the Skybound art which can be used when the meter is full, and the super skybound art when your at or below 30% giving a way for the lower player to instantly turn it around. The meter resets each round and can built up in many ways through the match such as perfect blocking or landing hits.The game focuses on figuring our your opponent and the matchup as well as good spacing and a lot more neutral play than most fighting games, but still rewards combo grinding just as much as a solid punish game is crucial. You can also clash attacks of the same degree and the first player to react out of it gets the advantage.There is a low point of entry with the combo styling but adds much more depth by the mix of more neutral options making it very rewarding when you master both and overall makes the matches feel a lot more like your playing a person than a combo bot, similar to the smash games, I have not fought two players who played the same and finding those  unique styles and countering them is what makes the victory so satisfying.Over all it is a super fun game, the cast maybe smaller than most so far but each character has a very unique style and matchups so far seem very balanced compared to most games on launch.The RPG mode is there, it's interesting and a good change of pace from ranked but its not what you buy this game for.The accessibility, Incredible art style, and rewarding both neutral/matchup knowledge and combo grinding are the selling points for me.I played with one guy in a online room for two hours and seeing each other improve in the matchup, mixup, and have awesome clashes felt so cool and the game as a whole just makes you feel like a badass when you start to improve and get to understand the general tendencies of other players with such a dynamic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: If you're new to the game and struggle to find opponents at a similar skill level online, join the GBVS discord community and there are plenty of awesome people eager to help here.This is the most beautiful anime fighting game I've seen.The characters are very faithfully recreated with incredibly vivid facial expressions and top notch camera works for their cinematic supers. Every single character also has unique lines for the intro/outro with every other character, which really captures the cast's personality well.As for the game itself, this is also the most approachable fighting game I've ever played. Simple shortcut commands for easier input at the expense of longer cooldown timer is imo a great idea to lower the entry barrier for fighting game beginners. At the same time, the game retains a high skill ceiling for users to hone their skills. Very much a case of easy to learn but hard to master.Compare to some other fighting games though, this game's characters have fewer moves in general so this might not be for people who enjoy having a very long list of moves and mastering all of them. There is a much heavier emphasis on the fundamentals in this game from what I can see.Lastly, I really like the idea of RPG mode. Although the story is undeniably sub-par and the difficulty up until beating Beezlebub in RPG mode is braindead easy, the challenge does pick up later in the mode. Most importantly, I appreciate this mode trying something different for its single player content offering, and the inclusion of gigantic bosses is a great way to break up the pacing. The RPG mode also supports local and online coop, making it a great way to chill with a buddy.This game uses delay-based netcode however. This means online play will inevitably run into some very laggy matches. As a result the online community is not very active. That's not to say you can't have a good time online, but the peak of players playing in online lobby is usually around afternoon PST in the New York lobby. Trying to find online matches during other time periods (especially for ranked mode) can be quite difficult.  Overall, I really enjoyed playing it. I bought it at first 'cause I'm a fan of the source material, and I saw my favourite character (Vira) recently got added. I wasn't expecting to be playing for as long as I did given that I don't usually enjoy fighting games all that much, so I'm very pleasantly surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to get into fighting games and improve at playing them because almost all of my friends are very good at them and I wanted to be able to provide them a challenge when we play, however most games I tried to learn were very difficult to grasp the concepts of. Learning frame data, set-ups and conversions off of stray hits is daunting and takes time and you can typically go dozens of hours with hundreds of matches before you ever see a win.GranBlue Fantasy: Versus remedies this not by making it easier to win or simplifying/removing concepts that are innately difficult to understand in fighting games, but by allowing access to a vast wealth of knowledge about how some of these concepts work. It provides a level playing field where the game is easy to understand and conceptualize, but still gratifying to become a master of. Whether you are a pro of fighting games or new to the genre, I truly believe you will enjoy this game.Beyond that, the game is visually stunning as are all Arc System Works fighting games (See DragonBall FighterZ, Guilty Gear Xrd, and the upcoming Guilty Gear Strive.) and has an excellent soundtrack from across a range of songs from the Mobile Game "GranBlue Fantasy." The game offers a couch co-op story mode which is barebones at most, but mostly serves as a way to teach new players the ropes of fighting games through a fun little side-scrolling beat-em-up. The storymode is short, being easily completed in roughly 4-6 hours, but continuing to play after completion allows for unlockable colors and weapons which are completely cosmetic for use online or in local matches. So overall, I'd rate this game as a 8.5/10 as a fighting game. I cannot say I've ever had this much fun playing and improving at a fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super mega simple and fights are all about the neutral game. You won't see gatlings or air combos or aerial battles or cancels that chain lots of attacks and specials. I said this game doesn't have gatlings but you still can chain simple 3 4 hits combos. It's just rather than chaining different button actions a la Guilty Gear (not that crap called Strive), you just mash just a single button and get a 3 hit combo. You can then chain them into a special and then extend the combo with another hit confirm and special or go for a super. The artwork, characters designs and visual effects are to die for. I think I spent most of my time watching character animations and artworks rather than playing the game.Also online is not as dead as people complain about in the reviews (at least not in Europe). And the delay based netcode is not god awful and surprisingly playable. I could play ranked with some people and there were also rooms in the early morning. But you have to play your placement matches before you can fully unlock the online modes (ranking, rooms, lobbies etc.) so depending on where you live you might have a hard time with getting matched with people playing ranked.If you wanna start playing fighting games but think that they are way too complicated and overwhelming, then definitely try this game before trying other faster paced games like Melty Blood, Guilty Gear AC+R, Guilty Gear XRD, Under Night In-Birth.

_childDocuments_.review: The roster is small compared to what consumers ought to expect for a fighting game, but for what it has to offer now, I personally feel it's worth the pickup. The characters are well designed in terms of aesthetic and fighting abilities. Being an Arcsys game, the graphics/artstyle look breath-taking as always with well-animated models, good sound effects, good music, and detailed environments. I especially like how the stages transition each round. Only thing that would make it better is if they were destructable. Though it is an anime-fighter, don't expect any overly flashy 50 hit combos and infinites. As someone who is a big fan of MVC and other tag fighters, I honestly feel its a bit of a fresh air. The game is simple enough that anyone can pick it up, especially with inputs, and blocks being akin to how Super Smash Bros. handles them, but timing on moves is still strict, traditional inputs still exist and offer specific rewards for utilizing them such as no cooldowns on projectile moves  and such,and there is still plenty of room for high-damaging comeback combos. The game puts more emphasis on neutral exchanges, which is something that I have been looking for, and with Samurai Shodown still not available on this platform, I was overjoyed to find that this is offering that type of move and poke gameplay. RPG mode is a solid casual experience and can be fun with friends, taking advantage of the gatcha system of obtaining loot which is a good way to increase replayability. Some may find the mode too barebones and simple. It definitely isn't for the seasoned fighters wanting more, but I wasn't expecting it to be overly detailed anyway, as the main fighting mechanics and online are the selling point for the genre. For what it is, it's a welcome addition, especially for first-time fighters and anyone who can appreciate simple light-hearted fantasy tales. The cast is likeable and the script is decent enough to be entertaining, and well voice-acted well for the most part in either languages. The game also has a working arcade mode. Thank goodness. That's been a scarcity for triple A fighters for quite sometime. It also has probably one of, if not the best training mode I've experienced. Aside from basics, and combos, and all that jazz, the tutorial even covers character specific matchups, and how to deal with certain moves.If there is anything I feel the game needs, well imo, I think the characters could use an extra Super/Skybound Art or two. I've probably been spoiled by MVC, but I do like the idea of having 2 Supers for different properties and combo variations with the Super Skybound/Desperation Super as THE finisher. That's just me I guess. The lobby system is same as other Arcsys games in recent, and while welcome still has the issue of too much waiting. I'm sure a lot of us simply just wanna jump in and play a match instead of having to do so much to set it up with randos. The lobbies imo are best for group tournaments online, and with friends. Also, online needs rollback netcode. Please Arcsys.Of course, the roster is light, and I don't like that we're having to pay such a price with day 1 DLC slapped on, but I can forgive them due to the quality of the project as a whole and the fact that this is new IP that they're working on with brand new models and such. People complained about FighterZ in the same boat for its initially light roster, now look where we are. Solid single player experience, simple and accessible mechanics, but plenty of complexity, and just high production values across the board. This is easily my pick as one of the best 2D fighters in the market. Wait for a price drop if you're hesitant, but I definitely recommend this one when you can get your hands on it. I truly hope that this is the start for GBF as a fighter, as I've had issues trying to get into the mobile game, and have only really been able to enjoy the anime.

_childDocuments_.review: GBVS is both a good fighting game and a decent 2D Side-Scroller Action RPG. It offers a good amount of content and is overall well designed, but held back by its pricing and online netcode. Purchase when on sale.Con:- Expensive. Doesn't come with the mobile gacha promo codes like the PS4 version. Lots of DLC.- Many customizables, characters and stages are DLC only.- Online PvP runs on outdated Arcsys delay netcode. One or two frames of delay are okay, but it often goes up to 4+, which is close to unplayable.- RPG Mode controls are somewhat unintuitive due to left/right directions changing on a whim, takes some time to get used to it.- Has short movelists and no "Gatlings", similar to Guilty Gear Strive in this regard. Both games feel restrictive in what your character can do compared to other anime fighters.- The audio volume tends to be all over the place during rpg mode. For example, the music during boss battles is a lot louder than usual, some characters are very quiet as narrator, etc.- Low player count. Just like with every other anime fighter that isn't GGStrive or DBFZ, you'll have to join a community Discord server and look for online PvP matches there.neutral:- Designed to be played with a controller, doesn't let you navigate the menus via mouse.- I didn't run into any bugs or major performance issues, but I did have to turn on Vsync to fix screen tearing and one of rpg mode bosses caused the game to lag a bit.- The story itself is nothing spectacular, just okay. You might want to read a summmary of Belial's story arc from the mobile game before going into it, since GBVS is effectively a spinoff sequel to it.Pro:- The game's RPG mode is the best out of any traditional fighting game I've played so far. That's not setting the bar particularly high, but it is PvE content that is actually worth playing, which is almost revolutionary for the genre. It mixes "side-scroller beat 'em up" with fighting game gameplay. Especially the endgame bosses were fun.- RPG Mode has local and online coop.- The 50 "episode" main quest offers about 20 hours of content and it is safe to assume that there is more to come due to DLC expansions. As far as I can tell, you also don't need to own the DLCs in order for the main quest to be expanded.- Art and animation are amazing and the soundtrack is great too.- Unique intro&outro interactions for all character matchups.- Full english dub, including narration.- Decent amount of customization (when including DLCs, it is 19 colors and 8 weapon skins per character). The highlight being the weapon skins that you can unlock in rpg mode and then use in PvP.- Has a tutorial mode for both universal mechanics and individual characters (including a few combos). Also features an ingame glossary for fighting game terminology.- Does almost everything right in terms of accessibility, one of the best options for fighting game newcomers, especially because you can "learn by doing" in RPG mode.- Unique gameplay feel due to the mechanics taken from RPG mode, like cooldowns on special moves, the option to do either simple or technical inputs, block button vs holding back, etc. Lots of choices to make mid-combat. Adds a surprising amount of gameplay depth.- Has an active community tournament scene (Hearts are Blazing, MatchStickMelee, etc. see: gbvs.keeponrockin archive)- Ongoing developer supportI bought the "Character Pass Set" (base game + first season pass) on sale at -50% (= $40/€) and am pretty happy with it. The full price is still a bit much to ask, mostly because the online PvP is held back by the delay netcode and the RPG Mode doesn't offer enough content to be worth the full price on its own (yet?), but it is a very good pickup when on sale. It has improved a lot in this aspect since the initial release in 2020 and it might continue to improve going into 2022, depending on what Cygames decides to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, here we go again. Granblue fantasy versus review tiem. I personally have, like many people, discovered the fighting game genre with the SSB series. I then moved onto 2D fighters with Skullgirls (i need to re-review that) and finally found my main game in Strive. It was only natural that i end up playing Granblue Fantasy Versus (which i'll start calling GBFV from now on), and oh boy, what a good discoveryGBFV is a simple fighting game. Characters have limited kits, with very limited options. That sounds boring the first time you try it, but it allows for a fast, easy pick-up of any character, allowing you to have fun within minutes of playing them, and to play them with intent in less than an hour. This makes picking up characters incredibly rewarding, and GBFV is the game where i've found myself to play the most character, as i regularly play 5 different characters on a regular basis. That simplicity, however, hides the true focus of GBFV: Placement, spacing and resource management. Nearly all characters in GBFV have big, disjoint normals, and their movement is usually limited to jump, walk, run, forward roll, and back dash. This essentially leads to a gameplan that revolves around placement, walking to hit your opponent with the tip of your sword, walking away on block, trying to hitconfirm on hit. This sounds a bit boring at first, but it quickly turns into a game of surgical precisions which quickly becomes extremely enjoyable. Navigating neutral has very little to no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and feels very rewarding overall. The cooldown system for specials is a great idea, and i wish id see it in more games. Each specials has 3 versions, A and B, both of which have flaws but gives you pretty much no cooldown, and C, which usually has no major flaw, but disables all 3 versions of the special for a LONG time. This adds a whole aspect of resource management to the game: Your advancing rush special might help you win neutral, but using it means you can't use it to get a good combo if it works. Your C Reversal is stronger, but if you use it, you'll have no access to any reversal for a long time. All of those situations add time pressures and complexity in a way i cannot find in other games. What granblue has that i cannot find in other fighting games is A LOT OF SAUCE. Every character has a stylish intro, a stylish victory screen, and dialogue for those that adapts depending on who your opponent plays. ALL specials look GREAT, much better than the concurrence (Sorry boys, but besides some exceptions, Strives supers are bland as hell). The music follows to give the game a solid, consistent style that i've been finding myself to love way more than i should've. You can feel the love of the devs for the characters they're porting from the gacha. This makes the game more enjoyable for people who aren't full on about FGC competition, which is made better by the solo modes.The solo modes of GBFV are quite simply the best you can find in modern FGCs, if that's why you enjoy. They clearly aren't worth paying the game full price just for them, but unlike other games where you simply get a boring arcade mode, this one has a full playable story with RPG elements, actually engaging boss fights, characters to collect, rewards to obtain, and a whole progression system overall. This isn't important to most players, but it is so important here that i simply cannot ignore it.... Onto the bad now, and everyone already knows what'll be said, so i'll make it short. At the time of this review (August 9th, 2022, 10AM) EVO just ended and GBFV was one of the main games. The game has a competitive, engaged playerbase that wants more of this recipe they love so much. And right now, they are unable to enjoy it without meeting themselves irl. Rollback netcode isn't perfect. I'm the first to absolutely despise it as soon as it shows its flaws, but it NEEDS to be implemented to at least allow people who do their best to have a playable connection to play the game. GBFV still shows a dated delay netcode, forcing you into 10+ frames of input delay even with a decent, short ranged connection to your opponent. This would be understandable usually. But in a world where GGPO exists, where indies like Skullgirls have implemented it, where nearly all other main titles from one of the devs have it, and where online has been the norm for over 10 years, this is unacceptable. ESPECIALLY if Cygames and Arcsys clearly want to keep the game alive and competitive, as they've shown by announcing the Granblue Fantasy: Versus Community league. To conclude, even if that rollback problem is insanely frustrating, and clearly not a tiny issue, just seeing the size of my paragraphs above is enough to let me decide on my final review. GBFV is an excellent fighting game, much better than some recent releases (i'm coming for you DNF, you'll get your thumbs up but you'll also get your bad brick'o text), so consider it if you want a simpler game with great graphics and a lot of sauce. If there's local tournaments close to your home, great!If you plan to buy it to progress in a competitive, online ladder, then move away. There's few players online, and the netcode has the problem we mentioned above

_childDocuments_.review: Game is overpriced as hell, with only 11 characters in the base game [plus 5 (2 actually, the other 3 will be released in April) if you buy the day one dlc like a good boy] and character pack DLCs already in the works, so if that turns you off already, you might as well wait until all the packs are out in a year or two or to just avoid it like the plague. This game also has godawful netcode which is no excuse since smaller games with even smaller devs have better netcode. I'm hoping this gets fixed but I'm not holding my breath. There are also some pretty blatant balancing issues, but that can be patched (hopefully).This game is also really fun. If you want a slower paced (think Street Fighter) anime fighting game then this game is for you. because that's exactly what this game is. Instead of the long combos that shave off half of your opponent's health bar that you see in most anime fighters, this game opts for shorter combos and a more poke focused gameplay. Of course, if you're good enough you can still do long combos that take out half of the opponent's health bar, but that's not really what it's focused on. Movement in this game is far slower compared to usual anime fighters, which is why you need to play in a more subdued manner: Trading glancing blows in the middle like true gentlemen, before finding that one hit that allows you to go in and beat the other guy to death.It's also easy to pick up for people new to fighting games because of the simplified inputs for specials, the lack of meter management (only used for supers, and 100% at that), and of course, autocombo. All in all, it's honestly a surprisingly good game with solid and simple mechanics. Maybe not something for veterans of fighting games, but it's a good entry game for people new to the genre, or casuals like me.Also, honest men play Katalina. Take my word for it.EDIT: The second character pass is far too expensive, the netcode's still awful, and the playerbase is kind of nonexistent now. Get it on sale or not at all at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: A short remark you won't find in other reviews: it's not devs banning people around in Discussions. It's Steam Support. They can ban you for something like that  . At any rate, IT'S NOT DEVS, as some people are speculatting on reddit over increasing number of [banned] users. I have contacted at least two others on that.Now, to the game itself:Personally, I was expecting another round of stylish-only club with auto-combos and homing attacks after BB:Crosstag and DBFZ, but ASW decided to break that pattern, and, dear Lord, they've made it astounishing. "Smart" inputs aren't MUST inputs in this one. At the same time, you don't have to remember the values for initial\in-combo hitstuns for each move - there are more intuitive sources for combos, namely catching opponent mid-air, wallbounce and chaining your specials. Those 3 makes for 90% of combos avialable in the game (characters like Lowain and Beelzebub have other sources, though). On the one hand, that allows people to have fun from get-go with smart skills and stock combos showcased in the training mode itself; on the other, it gives you a load of possibilities to hone your skill, since there are mechanics like "guts" or "hitting assists" that won't be relevant to your playstyle unless you are aware of them. Also, the game is much more frame-sensitive than previous ASW's "technical" titles (buffer times are shorter, no safe frames to cancel your move into defence on Overdrive\D-Drive, etc) and ussing technical input on specials gives you a number of benefits over the easy inputs (including plain damage buff on some moves).Three words about the port:1) They have fixed issues with keyboard. Completely. So, older reviews are no longer relevant on that aspect.2) Good word about Netcode. Personally, for me it's stellar. Synchronization casts literal miracles - I have 3-4F delay in most of the matches over Europe and, holy wholesomeness, those 3-4F is a big difference with 3-4F delay in Xrd (even after they've fixed 30 FPS issue). 70% of matches are completely stable - no spikes at all, no inputs are getting missed. I saw a lot of reviews stating this, but replays, somehow, show a number of "unsprung" moves on opponents side from time to time, mostly, when they are showing you their back with something like "pfff, get yourself some Internet, Wi-Fi pleb" (I'm not on Wi-FI, I'm just not from Europe, but pshhhhh).3) And a Bad One: Sync-phase may take up to 2 minutes depending on the time you've logged in, and there is a real chance between 19:00 and 22:00 GMT that you will wait even more just to get into the game (it's negotiating something with their servers even before you ask for that, so be prepared to wait for 3-4 minutes just to play a singleplayer game within the said timeframe). It can also kick you out of the lobby AFTER the match or durring the sync phase (you can abuse that to kick from the full lobby whoever you want, by the way) or even erase your profile, if you would spam "confirm" button while trying to log-in. Sounds terrifying, but matches themselves are unaffected. Oh, and those connection bars in rooms and ranked queue are traditionally broken: Light Blue could mean over 10F spiking to 16F while a lot of matches on Red are within playable 2-6F margin.4) And something ugly about netcode at last: some people experience crashes while trying to set up a match in a room or lobby. That's completely different from the issues I've listed above. You can confirm that in the pinned thread. Personally, I have no such issues, but this worth mentioning since I've been through it with BB:CF and they have NEVER fixed this (I'm aware that this one is not an ASW's port, but it bears so much resemblance with that case) . As the rule of thumb: hit some lobby right after you've finished with initial matches to check whether you are affected or not while you are within the refund window.5) English VO. It's attrocious. I can't imagine anyone ussing it in their good faith. Don't be such a troll, please, because your opponent would be forced to melt their ears on that cacophony as well.A little bit of advice to wrap it up:1) Most of the people use New York or UK's lobbies to play their games regardless of their actual locations (other non-asian regions died out a week after release).2) Don't try to be smart on Discussions forums. I've only posted a Goat Simulator MMO video to show people that you can't add GGPO in three clicks. Somehow, other users got the joke, but, apparently, not Steam Support. That week-long ban for "spam" (I've only posted this link once ever on Steam) is real. People are getting banned here around another user that is really active on one of the SS member's page. Maybe, it's just a coincedences, of course, and the person who banned me for spam here and the other, that found "no abuse" in that action did it by mistake. Probably, they just don't play videogames (safe for god-sims) and are not absolutely good with all those silly references.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could have been the most accessible AAA fighting game for pros and new players alike. It has beautiful graphics, engaging mechanics, well-done voice acting and interesting characters. The easy input mode was a fantastic idea. However, I dislike that they penalize people for using it (It's not a terrible punishment, but for the sake of accessibility, it should not penalize the player at all, in my opinion).Like many people who played the game, my main criticisms (and the reason for the "would not recommend") comes down to a few key factors:1. Delay-based netcode severely damages the online experience.2. No cross-play with the PS4 version severely limits the number of players you'll be able to find while attempting to play online.3. Months after the initial release of the game, the most significant new feature they added to the game was a battle pass. I did not like that.There are other issues people can reasonably be upset about: It's a costly game for how few people play it, the DLCs are pretty costly as well.This review is essentially a call to the developers to implement rollback netcode and cross-play into the game. For people looking to buy this game, your enjoyment might severely be limited until those two features are implemented.Update (2021-05-20): Two other things this game does well that I want to give it credit for include a very helpful training mode that helps you learn how to use the characters and play against others. This is opposed to Street Fighter training which only gives you complex combos to execute. The other very nice touch is that the command list has nice video clips of the move and information on using the move in different situations.One more lousy thing I forgot to mention is constantly seeing load screens and a "Communicating With Server" dialogue even when just navigating the main menu.Update 2023-01-21: Changing "No" to "Yes." The rollback is real! On its way with cross-play in 2023!Update 2023-02-03: Changing from "Yes" back to "No". I've been playing more since the rollback announcement, but the "Connecting to server" message that was introduced after they added the battle pass pervades across the entire menu experience and adds lots of extra unnecessary load time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great fighting game.  If you liked Street Fighter II/IV it sort of plays like them but with an anime fighter spin. If all the DLC currently available was available on release you'd have an A+ fighting game release, but with 4 of the 16 characters being DLC in addition to colours and 2 stages behind a paywall already I can't recommend you buy it at its current price unless you have no issue with it or really want to play it like I did.  It should drop to around $20 AUD in July for the EVO discount though so if it catches your interest put it on your wishlist for when that time comes around.Regarding smaller playerbase, granted it is true that there's a small playerbase on PC but there are plenty of fighting game discord communities where you can ask people to play matches with you. _childDocuments_.review: One of the easiest fighting games out there (I say that as a positive, for all my interest in the genre I can't play one). Every move except super can be done using [direction]+[button] (or 2 buttons), and the auto-combos are just a-a-a-d/square-square-square-R1 (or other button combinations). Characters movement speeds are fairly moderate. Playing defensive is also easy as dodge and roll have i-frames and dodge can go through the enemy to get you out of a wall. There isn't any combo break or wake up mechanics and the meter is an integer of 0 or 1. The gameplay itself is an extremely competent 2D anime fighter. It's Arcsys, if anyone know how to make a 2D anime fighter, it's these devs.However, this game is so lacking in content that I cannot recommend it for full price. There are 11 playable characters and 2 (AFAIK) AI only characters in the main game, which is a rather low number but each character also has few variety because of the low difficulty mentioned before (compared to other fighting games, not implying they are shallow). Disclaimer: it's not fair to expect this game to have the same roster size as large franchises, since all 11 of the characters are new whereas those games gradually build up their roster over time. Nevertheless the fact remains that this game has a fraction of the roster size of other games.The game also has a questionable online player population. I won't pretend to be an expert at this, but looking at Steam data will show this.The campaign mode is like a beat-em-up with very light RPG elements, frankly any stage aside from bosses are a waste of time as the mob soldiers basically never attack and only spawn in hordes to get killed, and from what I've heard it's only 8-10 hours long. There are also almost no unlockables in this game (only bonus colors and weapon skins), as characters don't even have alternate costumes.The looks of the game was a large part of what drew me to this game, but playing it myself it's disappointingly underwhelming. The resolution maxes out at 1080p which takes a significant hit to its graphical clarity (I know it's because of the drawn art, but still), and the overall details on non-character elements are just not very good. There also seems to be no anti-aliasing whatsoever, the title screen being most blatant example, where Lyria stands at a distance her hair swaying to the wind, and it looks bad.

_childDocuments_.review: + Cool skill system+ Excellent learning curve+ An actually decent singleplayer campaign+ Very nice aesthetic- Inconsistent online multiplayer- Limited rosterGranblue Fantasy has seen a sharp increase in popularity these last few years. It went from this mobile game that was only really known in Japan to becoming this big media franchise just a few years after its release. I personally got into the series when its anime adaptation aired back in 2017 and, although I don't play the mobile game, I am a fan of the characters and the universe. I also happen to be a big fighting game fan, so a combination of the two was definitely something I needed to check out.GBVS is not only an incredibly fun 2D fighter, but probably the best-looking one I have ever played. The combat, while streamlined a bit with the skill system, actually has a good amount of depth to it, making it a great choice for both veterans and newcomers alike. Whatever skill level you may be, the game offers a variety of tools to ease you into it, making for a great overall learning curve. And for those looking for a singleplayer experience, the RPG mode here actually has some effort put into it, unlike what we usually see in the genre.Still, it is disappointing to see the game follow the multiple character pass route, especially with how limited the roster is in its current state. That and the multiplayer issues are likely not going to be fixed, so if you're going to be playing the game online a lot, you'll definitely want to keep that in mind. Regardless, it is a fun a fighting game and one I would recommend, even to those not familiar with the franchise.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

The gameplay follows a more easy aproach like the Dragon Ball Fighterz game, there is auto combo and shortcuts for skills although you can use the proper input and get lower cooldown (yes skills here are based on cooldown and not a metter). For single player content you have plenty, from a extensive training mode with all it could possibly offer for you the learn from basic to advanced gameplay mechanics, a robust RPG story mode with loot, quests missions, cutscenes (most of them simple old style dialogue where characters just talk) and a tower mode where you need to clear floors and go up to get more loot, money, exp and crafting.So this is my opinion, the game itself is worth it if you accept the current state of it's online AND on sale, my biggest problem with this game is not even the current state of the online but it's price tag, I got it on sale for 40 eur character pack version, that has the base game (only having a very small roster) and the first season, sounds ok on sale but then there's Season pass 2 that off sale also feels overpriced and then you still have 3 Stages to buy that I also got on sale but feels that it's a very bad move to make paid stages instead of free updates for all, surprise it's not over, there is also a few VERY overpriced color packs, only 2 of them were cheap on sale (60cents).I hope this review helped you make up your mind on spending or not spending your precious money on this game =)

_childDocuments_.review: The newest fighter from ArcSystemWorks, Granblue Fantasy: Versus is possibly the most unique fighter ASW has currently released, though I use the term 'unique' loosely. ASW has always been known for it's slick, fast-paced, anime fighters in 'Blazblue' and 'Guilty Gear', both game series praised for their unique takes on 2D fighting game action compared to their contemporaries, yet what makes GBVS different from both the prior entries is that whilst it has a system comparable to said contemporaries, it is able to stand on its own as a perfect entry fighter and higher competitive fighter because of its engaging combat and diverse characters.What GBVS brings to the table is a fighting game based upon the world of GBF, a popular mobile and PC game from Japanese developer Cygames. Now, whilst in my opinion, the world is rather dull, and much of the best parts of the world comes from the lore pertaining to characters and creatures from the world of GBF, what really sells GBF to me, is its vast variety of characters and their developed lives and stories from the world. Now, within GBVS, the characters that are represented each feel diverse and unique from another, creating possibly one of my favourite rosters for a franchise fighter yet. Another thing that helps sell this game and its characters is that, this is one of the current most prettiest fighters to look at, with ASW going for a more grounded colour palette compared to their previous work on DBFZ. Just go look it up for yourself and be amazed, especially with its skybound arts.Now when I say it is an entry fighter, I mean that in the sense of, it doesn't have terribly complex combos and inputs aren't needing to be inputted at a mile a minute. It is, without a doubt, one of the slowest fighters ASW has every put out, yet in doing so, I feel allows many who look at the complexity of their faster paced fighters with fear to look at GBVS and learn in a comfortable environment. it features many mechanics and design decisions that, in my opinion, allows for many newcomers to antiquate themselves with fighting games easier than others have before. One of the main ways it simplifies things is with its usage of meter, that whilst some may call brain dead, allows its players to essentially focus solely short combos to the opponent without having to worry about advanced meter usage like in ASW's previous games. Now, what must be said is, that whilst it, in my opinion, is a perfect entry fighter, it also suffers a lack on complexity and engagement to those used to the genre that might put people off. It features a string based system, allowing a person to mash a single button to perform an easy combo, and my main gripes with it, a dedicated block button and a simple special button. My gripes with the block button, isn't that it simplifies blocking, but rather that one of GBVS' most unique mechanics, the spot dodge is tied to it, without access to it with a form of regular blocking, meaning that the block button NEEDS to be used to access this mechanic which I feel neuters my enjoyment whilst playing, though that is possibly because I am, at this point, so used to holding back to block, that a dedicated block outside of smash is very foreign to me, though I have spent long enough in this game to come to grips with it. The other grievance, the special button, I feel is just a rather lacklustre inclusion method, as it simply allows specials and supers to be done with a far more simplified version, which wouldn't be an issue, if the difference between traditional inputs and simplified wasn't such a binary subtraction with simplified inputs making the special do less damage and put on cooldown longer.One thing that must be stressed however, is that GBVS has, imo, some of the worst dlc prices I've seen for fighting games. It essentially had day 1 dlc, which always reeks of scummy business practices, and the worst part, if you are like me and want to get all the characters, feel free to buy one of the most expensive season passes for the least amount of content, with all forms of dlc content being spread out and priced ridiculously. When you buy the season pass, you get 5 - 6 dlc characters and their respective songs. That's it. Stages are seperate purchases as well as colours, with colours being absolutely ridiculous prices, varying from 0.99p to £7 in total. It's baffling when, in comparison to other ASW fighters, purchasing a character gives access to the character, stage, music AND all colours (-minus the weird all dlc ones). In my opinion, this game doesn't warrant spending so much money on, when it has yet to have a sale on any of the dlc. Trust me, the moment they reduce the prices on the colours I am bagging them, I need my blue and black alts, it's like the coolest stuff ever. Overall, I'd consider GBVS definitely worth your time, just don't go overspending on cosmetic dlc.GBVS = 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue Fantasy: Versus is a fighting game, developed by Arc System Works as a collaboration project with Cygames. Unlike other fighting games, devs wanted to implement a proper RPG experience & story mode here, which will be a bit similar to original game.  While the game does a brief introduction for all characters, it does expect you to know about the main story and characters backgrounds. Well, if you never played (and don't plan to do so) GBF mobile game, you can watch Season One of GBF anime, which was done by A-1 Pictures. It will give you a pretty good understanding about a lot of events & characters.There's a Season 2 too, but it's by another (smaller) studio and quality (&budget) kinda dropped /sad.The game itself will tell you an original (spinoff) story. Gran and his friends are going to meet Katalina, but suddenly got attacked by her. Unable to reason and talk it out, they are forced to fight not only her, but a legion of Empire soldiers, which appeared from nowhere. After some time, they noticed that it's definitely a mind controlling technique and thus, they proceed and try to free her from it. Welp, that's pretty much a summary for entire story ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)"The enemy" main goal is to control Primals. So, you will be fighting familiar mind-controlled faces and Primals as bosses most of the time, while watching a lot of well done cutscenes. It's simple, but fun, so it works.p.s. The Final Battle is one of the most epic battles ever done by ArcSys. The game offers traditional Vs., Arcade, Training and Mission modes, that you pretty much saw in every recent Arc System Works game and an entirely new (for ASW and fighting games in general) RPG mode.  with quests to complete, gear and weapons to collect, giant bosses to fight, abilities to equip and cooperative play. This mode also play a role of a tutorial for new players.There's tons of different equipment and skills, ranging from buffs, debuffs, heal or unique damage spells/skills. Actually, the game took RPG-like approach not only for RPG mode, but the general fighting mechanics too. You can also activate a stronger version of the skill, but this will result in a much longer cooldown. You can track cooldown timers under your HP bar.   - A lot of character recolors. You can purchase them at Sierro's Shop.- Weapon skins. Weapons are not affected by recolors and each weapon skin got unique color + 2.5D model.- A new character - Beelzebub. So yeah, you don't need to buy him as DLC, but you should get a Season Pass 1 anyway, support Narmaya onee-chan ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°).- Some minor stuff like portraits for multiplayer profile, etc.Not sure how the game perform without internet connection, but you get a bunch of "Daily Quests" for RPG mode, which will give you various useful stuff, but the most important are Gacha tickets. Yeah, they added a small fanservice gacha here, which will give you SR and (rare chance) SSR weapons. This will be a good source of SSR (aka the strongest) weapons, though it's luck-based and the chance is shet. Don't use or upgrade R(Rare/Bronze) weapons, just sell them. (But keep weapons with skins via "Favorite" button).   is that they DON'T equip weapons in ALL grid slots, as you can see in this screenshot. This was also one of the main mechanics in a mobile game. Basically, you choose your main weapon and then setup a lot of SAME ELEMENT (important!) weapons, which will gives you various passives and ATK boosts. You also can stack identical passives. You need to create a grid for each element in the game and swap it according to the mission elemental weakness. It is kinda annoying, but you need to do it.Note: Weapons are just a "stat sticks" they don't change your character attack pattern or skin.I'd say that that the RPG mode is pretty easy at start, but the endgame bosses will be quite a challenge.Also,, which can't really farm Raid bosses, but pretty much fine with farming normal stages, providing a lot of EXP, upgrade materials and money. While i do play with gamepad, it seems like there's a pretty important bug, known as "sticky keys". You can wait for a patch or try a temporary solution from reddit: It will (most likely) be fixed in April patch.As for Netcode, sadly, even in 2020 Arc System Works still use the Delay-based version. However, Granblue Fantasy: Versus will be the last ASW game and a new Guilty Gear: Strive will use a Rollback netcode. While Rollback netcode is not exactly new, it is a much better multiplayer experience, compared to delay-based. Many popular games use it, like Mortal Kombat 11, for example.To save you from all technical details, rollback netcode can be described as: Granblue Fantasy: Versus is an excellent fighting game, with amazing 2.5D unique graphics, great RPG/Story mode & OST.  Sadly, it's still uses an archaic Delay-based Netcode and there's some critical bugs (like keyboard one), which can hinder player experience.Recommended to both Granblue Fantasy fans (even casual ones) and veterans in the fighting genre. - This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, albeit a tad expensive. It mostly feels like SF2 (strong specials, no great reliance on meter, decent amount of pushback on most moves, and a generous helping of active active frames on all normals) and features a lot of classic archetypes with some fun twists. Running, spot dodging and rolling give the game something SNK-esque, whereas the universal overhead, juggle system and crouching hitstun add a little bit of 3S to the mix; the super jumps recall memories of both. Air blocking is more of an anime feature (bar Alpha), and it is executed well enough in this game (no blocking grounded normals, ex moves or supers).The most prominent modern elements of the game are the lenient buffers, easy inputs, auto combos and slow throws (8f, although it has incorporated an SF2-like system on delayed techs). The buffer system makes frame data more important than it was in any classic fighter, but luckily most moves have a decent amount of pushback, meaning that there aren't  many -1 or -2 scrambles (looking at you, SFV); this is partially due to the aforementioned laggy throws. The easy inputs are also not that much of an annoyance, as they actually allow for some interesting choices to be made by the player: shall I sacrifice my recharge time and some move properties for a more reliable, faster answer to the situation? GBVS contains a lot of great elements from old fighters and as a result the game is both familiar and exciting. The modern elements aren't too much of a nuisance, and don't just detract from the title; they coalesce and make sense in the context of the game. I think this is one of the better fighters that has been released in the last few years, and as such I recommend GBVS.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the game longer than 17 minutes at this point, I have come to greatly revise my review.If you have a high-end custom-built computer or a dedicated gaming PC that can handle the game without lag, it's an absolutely gorgeous game.  The models and effects replicate the art style almost 1:1, down to the anime-styled facial animations.  The Skybound Art animations and effects are beautiful, with my two favorites being Weiss Flugel and Chaos Legion.  The story for RPG Mode is interesting, with writing on par with that of Granblue Fantasy proper, and I'm curious to see where it goes.  The gameplay is pretty simple and controls are easy to pick up, if a little fickle at times, making it accessible to both newcomers and veterans of the fighting game genre.Unfortunately, this is where my praise ends, as this game does have quite a lot of faults.  If you don't have a very high-end computer, you're pretty much required to play GBVS on low settings or suffer extreme performance loss, which means that the game doesn't look nearly as good as one might hope.  In fact it looks very, very chunky on low settings, and even then I still experience lag.  The story, while interesting, does little to catch players up to speed on the plot of the main game; it's apparently set after a point that I haven't reached yet, because I'm confused as to who Ares is, why she's partnered with Katalina, etc.  It also all but requires players to have played through the entirety of the What Makes The Sky Blue trilogy (including Paradise Lost and 000) to understand who Belial and Beelzebub are, and also leaves a huge plot hole that I hope gets explained (how the two are even out and about, given what happened at the end of 000).  Some of the plot of the trilogy does get explained in-game...but only if you have the DLC to use Djeeta.This leads into another complaint of mine: nearly half the playable cast at present is locked behind DLC, which is a very blatant money-grab, with only one of the DLC characters also being available for free (by completing RPG Mode, at which point there's not a lot you can do other than basic battles or replay it on Hard).  The game should not be this expensive if it has so much DLC to get the full experience.  The season passes mitigate this only marginally as, while you get all of the characters, that's literally all you get with them.  You don't get the palettes or anything.  Additionally, the biggest draw of buying this game, special serial codes for a load of rewards in GBF proper, .  For players who were looking forward to that 5k crystals, the Belial costume, and the draw tickets, we all got shafted.  The justification of "people could just take the codes and refund the game" can't even be excused--they could have implemented them as milestone rewards for completing certain chapters of the game, to ensure people actually played it and couldn't refund it.If you're a hardcore Granblue Fantasy fan, the game may be worth at least checking out.  However, I can't in good conscience recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst fighting games I've ever played. The game's visually stunning, but that's about the only thing it's got going for it. Gameplay-wise, it's Arcsys's take on an extremely simplified Streetfighter, no aerial movement at play, and the 4 buttons don't cancel into one another. For a game simplified to this caliber, there's not much variety between characters. Character strengths and weaknesses don't stand out a lot, the moves that makes characters unique usually have niche uses or are very weak in comparison to general movesets, As a result, most the time you'll be running the same pressure strings and mix ups across the cast. Combos also work in the same boring way, mash auto combo then end with an EX move for a hard knockdown then run your safe jump, and when you get to the corner just start spamming EX moves to juggle your opponent. And despite the game being simple and uniform, the game's balancing has been awful.

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue fans and Fighting games fans alike can enjoy this game. The game is lovingly crafted by both cygames and Arcsystemworks but still lacks some essential Quality of life improvements.Gameplay: We go back to basics, Where most Arcsys games are high flying combo plays, Here we have one that's focus on neutral and short combos Similar to the street fighter games. Character playstyle are defined by their normal and specials, but combo routes are not too rigid that it doesn't allow creativity. The game adds a cooldown system for special move  to show its RPG roots. and meter is dedicated to Supers only. Other elements include a spot dodge and forward dodge, auto combos and the familiar ability to high jump from anime games. The game also provides accessability with the skill button for shortcut specials and a block button similar to Mortal Kombat. These options help newbies to have and easier time picking up the game but there are incentives to learn the technical method. Frequent FG players may also use this tools to improve their game as it can compensate for reactions.RPG mode:Different from the a typical fighting game story mode. This one is a beat em up that you can play alone or with a friend. Your progression will depend on how you manage your stats with the weapons you pick up, buy  or draw from the gacha system. Fights are divided into 3 kinds, mob battles. Character Raid, where you fight the main rooster with some new systems. and Lastly, Boss raids, Which are unique boss battles RPG boss elements such as telegraph attacks. know that RPG mode will unlock weapons skins and colors for your character to use in normal gameplay.Art direction: Granblue Fantasy has a very strong art direction with their characters that are design to appeal at first glance. It helps that Arcsys animations for character helps to flesh out them even more than what a gacha game can. Stages are lovingly crafted to show off the world as locations are varied from crowded timesquare to a grand colliseum. (Also avoid Valtz Duchy if youre color-blind). The music set the tone for the RPG mode and character themes are memorable. (Party People is number 1! #LowainBros)Where i think it fails:1. Base Character Rooster is one of the least in a while2. Fighting game Character pass payment model3. RPG mode is not good as an introduction to the series, its starts very deep into the story.4. Tutorial does not explain fighting game concepts properly, but provides a glossary for fighting game terminology5. DELAY BASE NETCODE!! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ARCSYS!!6. No cross-play7. training does not provide proper framedata

_childDocuments_.review: one of the most beautiful pseudo 2D fighters out there. Graphics is powered by the Unreal Engine so you get fantastic 3D backgrounds with 2D battles. Based on the mobile game (and you can watch the anime on Crunchyroll) this fighter is like a combination of 2 games, fighting and an rpg mode where you can build up your character and play out a story. Unfortunately this title didn't get the press as it deserves but hopefully people can discover it during these trying times. Base game has a few characters and there are 2 character passes that you can purchase (which does stunningly raise up the price). I believe when you purchase those passes, you gain extra stages in the rpg mode pertaining to those characters. (correct me if I'm wrong). I'm using a 2080Ti and so far so good. What may look like dropped frames during the intermission parts are very similar to the anime. The other component that's big in this game is online gaming. Seems to be automatic ranked matches every time you log in but I haven't had enough time spent on it.Beautiful game, looks just like the anime with their amazing voice staff. can't wait to dig furthur.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty damn fun fighting game.  Don't go into this expecting a standard ASW game.  Its not an "anime" fighter like Guilty Gear or Blazblue.  Its much slower and methodical, like a Street Fighter or a King of Fighters.  The visuals are amazing, the music is fantastic, and as of thus far there isn't a single character I'd say isn't really fun.  Full recommendations to anyone who enjoys fighting games.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue fantasy versus is a amazing fighting game but it suffers from same problems as other fighting games.1.tutorials in the game don't actually teach new players how to play well.(you have to find the info outside of the game yourself)2.you have to play over hundreds of hours just to be decent at the game.3.almost everyone who you find on the lobbies and ranked mode are experienced fighting game veterans.i am pretty new to the fighting game genre. i  bought GBFV today myself and after going through the character move sets and basic combos. i thought i would have myself some low ranked fun only to get absolutely rekt by more experienced players. Some might say that i should "git gud". yeah i get that, but let me ask you this is it really fun that you have to train over 100 hours in the training mode just to have a chance to have decent experience with the game if you don't have a friend in the same skill level as you?so i would't recommend this game to a fighting game noobie if you don't have a friend to share it with.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most engaging fighting games I've ever played.Kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over Australians with server derping for ranked, and the DLC is kinda overpriced. But if you're a regular ol'money bags it's well worth the price.Great community around the game too, friendly, warm, sometimes unqualified and only slightly childish. Mostly worth interacting with.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: Granblue is a really fun casual fighter with beautiful visuals and will hurt your wallet just like its gacha counterpart. If you play fighting games you know you're gonna pay a bit more out of pocket than just the 60 dollar base price tag and this game is no exception. In fact this game is already shaping up to be one of the more expensive fighters regarding dlc content so keep that in mind before you decide on purchasing. Now for the gameplay it is a footsies based gameplay but its extreamly limited. While this can be fun for new players it is holding itself back and preventing you from really getting any better. Also its obnoxious that inputs are read as held inputs and as a result the game will throw out wrong moves all the time in net play and in general practice. To add to this the game also has auto combos that force you to dance around your button presses so that you don't slide into an auto combo suddenly. Keep in mind that it's incorporated to be new player friendly so this game is marketed towards a more casual and newby audience. I just wish they would make it a setting you can turn off to allow the game to truly be at its peak potential. For people looking to get into fighting games this is an expensive but fun starting point. Realistically this game is only worth it for hardcore Granblue fans, specifically the fans with fat wallets.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line: It isn't the best fighting game but good enough to have a good time with the mates and offers just enough to be interesting at the competitive level.The good:- Pretty graphics, personally, I think it looks nicer than GG strive- Cool character design (but that's legacy from the gacha game where it's the only way for people to spend money on .pngs)- Character intros where they interact with each other and have voice lines and such so it's quite cute (unlike strive)- I like the music. My friend says the main menu music is so soothing that it de-tilts him after a bad game.- Simple gameplay and controls so it's simple to pick up and play. Even if you're bad at fighting games (like me)The bad:- Bad online experience: specifically the netcode is delay based meaning that you can only get good connections to people who live in your region. This requires coordination outside of the game in the discord server which is here for North America: - Simple gameplay and controls leave something to be desired after playing for a while, but because this is a adversarial game it sill is very deep relative to any single player game you're going to touch. Speaking relative to other fighting games, this one is quite simple. Which in of itself isn't a bad thing, it just leaves more to be desired. This is speaking in terms of the TOP LEVEL play which, let's be honest here, you're never gonna reach anyways, so why does it matter to you when you're buying a game to play for fun.- Sometimes the game gives me DP instead of fireball and it pisses me off and I have to keep reminding myself to wait a sec before attempting to throw another fireball- The RPG mode is an afterthought and has possibly one of the worst stories written in all of fiction, like worse than tumblr fanfic badThe Ugly:- Vyrn weapon skins- Belial and A. Belial mains
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great and incredibly pretty. It even has a cooperative Beat 'em up - rpg mode. Unfortunately, she also has flaws that prevented her from achieving the success she deserved. The price is too high and persisted for too long. Expensive dlcs (even the character colors are payable). Poor netcode, which, combined with a small number of players, made it very difficult to find an opponent online. Nevertheless, I really like this game. I even think it's one of the best fighting games I've ever played. I keep my fingers crossed for the creators to improve netcode and for increasing the number of players.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: A great game marred by horrifically expensive prices and sales being rare as hell.  Netcode isn't up to par with stuff like Strive or Skullgirls or even some indie fighters, but it plays fine online with people close to you (2 frames input delay on average with me and a friend I play with).Edit 12/14/2023: Ignore this game now and get Rising instead which is the largely improved version of this game with better netcode.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: In short:+ nice graphics+ fun and fluid gameplay- easy in "very hard" mode- menu buttons can´t be configuredMore info:The game is very easy, since I am playing in Very Hard mode and beating the Arcade mode is a piece of cake (I am not a hardcore player).I don´t play online, so I can´t tell about the complaints that other users mention.Bad or weird things I have seen so far:- Button configuration is complicated. In menus you are forced to use predefined keys (AWSD + Enter + Backspace), but when playing I want to use other keys (cursor) so it´s quite annoying to keep changing. Why AWDS and not cursor by default!? I don´t know why they did this. In Guilty Gear they made it possible to use the same keys in menus and battle, so why not here too?- The game connects to a server every time you start the game or you finish a game and return to the menu, and it takes a while to perform the connection. (Maybe this is fixed already?)
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love what I've seen and played of this game (the PC port, and the PS4 version), I can't recommend it to others in its current state. A friend and I planned to play this online together, but when we tried to enter the online lobby, it forced us to queue up for ranking matches first... I was matched up against another player after about an hour, but my friend was never queued up with anyone, even after two hours of him being online. We can't play together, because the game literally forces you to do ranking matches before you even get to the online lobby, and the game's community is currently dead. No other fighting game I've played has had such an awful online system.Oh yeah, and it apparently doesn't have rollback. Not the worst crime in the world, but if ArcSys ever wants this game to have an actual player base again, maybe they should start with that!
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: Really welcoming fighting game for beginners in style as myself, really fun to play with a friend, and the art and moves is awesome. The problem is that the online part only runs well on console, it's almost impossible to connect online, you'll always get an error and when you finally get into online the queue time is massive, probably cause most ppl gave up on connecting part. If you have a friend to play is really funny, otherwise, try it on console onlyEDIT: Yap, the server is still a problem BUT the community has groups in discord that helps you to find and play games with ppl near you, which is awesome, is not ideal, cause y'know, I want to sit press the search button and play. But with the discord and the community help the game is really enjoyable ;P I'll stick with the bad review cause online should work out of the box

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 2D fighter set in the Granblue Fantasy universe... while the asking price is high if you include the DLC... for fighting game fans this is a balanced fighting game that is sort of Street Fighter like but with its own spin on the concept. I guess one could complain about the small roster.... but the more bloated the roster the more unbalanced the game can potentially be... so I am perfectly fine with the smaller selection of characters. The online can be hit or miss sometimes but at least unlike some other games it actually shows a delay number so you can have a idea of if this is just not a good time to be playing online. I have not tackled the single player content so I have no opinion on that.... that being said I am familiar with the characters from the mobile game and anime series so there is that.

_childDocuments_.review: a YouTuber put it in terms i agree with the most: "this is the game MK11 was trying to be."notes: I play on stick. Game seems suitable for a pad tho with only 4 attack buttons. I played mostly as Percival and later tried some Ladiva.major pros:- the shortest time to hopping into real matches i've experienced with a 2-D fighter so far, it's easy to figure out what is plus or minus and develop a gameplan on the fly.- mechanically, it is easy to figure out when it's your "turn" without too many repeated failures.- spot dodge / roll add a layer of options for "getting in" to every character introducing new options to archetypes that would traditionally struggle more against zoners. Options are good but not braindead get-in-free tools.caveats:-inputs for dashes and z-motions feel very weird, not necessarily strict or loose but seemingly random failures to input on motions i swear i can input cleanly in, say, SFV. Straight up, I cannot wake up DP in this game without simple input dp.-this is somewhat mitigated by the easy inputs, which add a layer of risk/reward to your own inputs. You can actually play the grappler without spending insane amounts of time grinding the 360 input muscle memory because of simple inputs, even if it is suboptimal-- which lets you learn characters at slightly lesser potential, mitigating time spent in training mode "getting ready to enjoy real gameplay." Then simple inputs become choices over technical inputs as they are not always worth the risk of misinput in the clutch.major con is delay-based netcode-- the higher you climb the likelier your matches will have some wild frame delays. limits the usefulness of ranked mode. Skill level in player lobbies is all over the place but connections are more stable.That's all for rn, no character has really "stuck" with me and I am patiently waiting to try out Soriz around April 7th.

_childDocuments_.review: The keyboard issues have finally been fixed so I can recommend this game.It's simple 2D footsies action, most compare it to Street Fighter. Combos do require some timing and there's plenty of room for mastery, making it an ideal mix of "easy to pick up hard to get good at". Characters are easy enough to pick up that counter picking seems to be viable. Balance is decent right now, but it's somewhat precarious with characters like Lowain and Katalina being on opposite ends of the spectrum. RPG mode is a fun time killer and for people who like single player / co-op experiences or miss things like Tekken force. The RPG mode also allows collection of weapon skins giving a nice extra customization option along with color palettes (Ladiva gets different masks). I'm still fairly new to the FGC, but everything I've seen indicates something of a renaissance happening with this game being able to draw in 10+ year veterans and brand new players alike. Arksys may have found their golden cow with this game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: As a new fighting player, the hardcore difficulty of the fighting game has always discouraged me. Until I discovered this beautiful fighting game. GBVS opens the door for me to face fighting games, it has simple moves, and beautiful character drawing. But don't get me wrong, this does not mean that the game is easy. On the contrary, you still need to learn various basic knowledge of fighting games to play it well.Excellent painting style and easy way to get started, let me unconsciously played 100+ hours. I can confidently say that I'm not at the same level as when I started playing. [Although I'm still a fighting noob :)]However, because this game gave me confidence in fighting games, now I can consider trying more games in this genre, I plan to buy GGST by the end of the year and Tekken8 next year
_childDocuments_.name: Granblue Fantasy: Versus

_childDocuments_.review: Great 2d fighting game. It is popular at the moment so it is not that difficult to find an online match. Netcode is not the best but it is better than what we have seen in early days of SF V. No teleports, no rollbacks, but if it lags in lags hard. It is also easy to start playing as well due to noob-friendly special move system. You will be punished for not learning a proper input but you will notice it only as you reach the level of play where it is neccesary. The game teaches you a lot of things and presents enough options to play with to keep the game interesting.You have to be alert though because as any other fighting game it is not something you can not expect to pick it up in an hour and start winning right off the bat. Prepare to read, watch videos and grind some practice mode for at least 20 minutes a day if you are new. Another bright part about the game is that despite having  flashy combos and characters designed for such things most of the process is very fundamental-based. So you would better start with things like special-cancels, dodge, dash, hit-confirm, tech-throw, safejump and other creepy things which are actually easy to pick up in this game. This experience will transfer in other games as well so it is definitely worth to put time into.Overall the great game to start learning fightings and to have some fun if you are already experience enough.

_childDocuments_.review: We making it out the hood with this oneA must-play for puzzle fansI recently picked up this game on Steam and I have to say, I'm thoroughly impressed. The gameplay mechanics are intuitive and challenging without being frustrating, and the graphics and sound design are top-notch.One thing that really stood out to me was the level design. Each puzzle felt unique and well-crafted, with just the right amount of difficulty to keep me engaged without feeling overwhelmed.But what really sets this game apart, in my opinion, is the humor. _childDocuments_.review:
In a world where adventurers roam the skies on airships, and the floating islands of the Skydoms lead their way, the Grandcypheran airship of massive proportionssets out on a magnificent journey, traveling the islands, and picking up a veritable army of sellswords, knights, and mages along the way However, these heroes of the sky will soon embark on a brand-new adventure, where battle and glory await!

An international mobile game hit, Granblue Fantasy has topped the charts, charming players across the globe with a plethora of lovable characters and story-driven mechanics. Now, legendary fighting game studio Arc System Works and Cygames are teaming up to bring the universe to home console in an action-packed head-to-head fighter. Featuring a colorful cast of their most popular "crewmembers," each with a unique fighting style that is easy to learn but hard to master, Granblue Fantasy: Versus is sure to appeal to fans of Granblue lore and fighting games alike.

KEY FEATURES

* An Anime Fighter for Players of All Levels!
Arc System Works, the team behind critically-acclaimed fighting series BlazBlue, Guilty Gear, and Dragon Ball FighterZ, and Cygames, the people behind the international mobile phenomenon Granblue Fantasy, usher in a new era of fighting games with a rich and accessible battle system suitable for beginners and veterans alike.

* Fight as Your Favorite Granblue Characters!
A balanced and varied cast of combatants are ready to duke it out, each with their own individual fighting styles and dazzling skills. Whether it's the well-rounded Katalina, the long-range specialist Ferry, or the dual blade wielder Lancelot, there is a character and style to suit almost anyone's tastes.

* A Gorgeous 2.5D Style World, Accompanied by Memorable Melodies!
High production values recreate the well-known locales of the Granblue Fantasy universe in vivid 2.5D, bringing these environments to life as crewmembers cheer in the background, all accompanied by Stelle Magna's stirring soundtrack.

* Captivating Visuals, Designed by a Fantasy Expert!
Hideo Minaba of Final Fantasy series fame contributes as art director, lending his extraordinary talents and unforgettable character and world designs to the Granblue Fantasy universe!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 80 hours with the game and completing most of the main and side content, im still stuck with very mixed feelings about this game. While its a pretty decent RPG/Action shooter, it still leaves alot to be desired and anyone with a brain can tell that its far from finished.Pro's:-Pretty great story-Very well written and memorable characters- Weighty, responsive combat, most guns feel powerful- Weapon and clothing design is pretty killer and def looks cyberpunk'ish-Great SoundtrackCon's:-This game is extremely buggy, and alot of the bugs wlll break your immersion and pull you from the otherwise awesome game world-The performance leaves much to be desired, Im running an RTX 2080S, Ryzen 7 2700x at 4.2GHz and 32GB DDR4 3200MHz. And got pretty constant drops into the low 40's using DLSS Quality and a combination of High/ medium settings at 1080p- Some of the game mechanics and builds are pretty much worthless, like the crafting and Smart weapons.- No vehicle customization- Police AI is horrendous as they spawn directly behind you and give up chase in a matter of 15 seconds, sometimes less.-Bugged achievements that wont pop after completing the pre-requisitesOverall, I wouldnt recommend this game to really anyone at the moment due to it clearly being unfinished. And it isnt very accessible to people who dont have the best of the best PC parts available on the market. I'll update this review once they get it together, fix the bugs and optimize it to where its more accessible to a wider audience.

_childDocuments_.review: So,after completing 85% of the game as of the time i am writing this. I decided to share my opinion of the game.This game.. Doesn't at all meet the standards that this game company is capable of.Graphics are great, but when you look under the hood you start to see the truth and once you do, no amount of work can bring back the lost innocence.As i said, graphics and sound are okay. But once you look under the hood you realize this game is a stripped out GTA style game with worse A.I. (if you can call that an A.I., games in the early 90's had better AI.). The automobile system is a joke. Even after changing the FoV for my 3440x1440 120hz 21:9 screen i just get the feeling i'm crammed in a box.The item system and how they handle skills is a complete joke. I was on the games hardest difficulty and was decked out and almost a god in just over an hour and a half. There is almost never a reason to use a gun when you can just hack a camera and shut down or kill ever mob in an area without ever being seen. Free loot, no chance of death and its a cake walk. also the game feels like its missing systems that were intended and would have made the game better over all. such as the ability to use the claws to climb walls or wall run. just things like that.Over all I would say the game was lazier put together than my review of it, but that's just it does it really deserve more. this guy doesn't think so. I was hopeful too.

_childDocuments_.review: I will always remember my first walk around Night City as one of the best gaming moments of my life. I was simply humbled by the City grandiosity, overwhelmed by its staggering amount of detail, excited by the awareness that whoever made this, shared with me the same vision of what cyberpunk is.For the first few hours of play, I simply could not get anything done. I wasn't able to walk from A to B for a quest without stopping to take a better look at something that captured my attention.I really felt like being in a cyberpunk, dystopic world, and that was the only thing I could not forgive this game for not delivering. Everything else can be worked on and improved, but not this. That sense of wonder either is there or is not. And by god, it's there.All of this, lucky for me, could not be taken away by the terrible decisions taken by CD Project RED management, that led to an unfinished game being released, because that's pretty much evident and synthom of a too common bad pratice in the gaming industry. A lesson that, I'm afraid, will not be learned.
