_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥ this is a hard game to review.Cyberpunk 2077, what is it? It's a massive sandbox first person RPG set in the Cyberpunk world of Night City (and surroundings). It's got guns; swords; hacking; sex; booze; cars; controversy... and bugs.*Updated* Full disclosure: I have beaten the game once so far and am working on a second play-through. The game is so massive in scope, this is both a cool and bad thing at the same time. It doesn't have the same grind-exhaustion that Ubisoft games make you suffer from, and you always discover new things at least. However you will obviously encounter some missions or events that always play out the same way no matter what you choose which is a little disappointing. The vaunted life-paths seems to do little more than change dialogue options a bit, that's it.How's it look and run? It's fantastic. On the right machine this game looks downright phenomenal and on a lower end machine it still looks good. I have run it on two systems (both gaming laptops) the primary being an Area 51M R1 (9700K w/ RTX 2080) and the secondary being an old (2010) upgraded MSI GT780DXR (i7 2670qm w/ GTX 970M 3GB). The 51M can rock this game at 60FPS with Raytracing on Ultra (using DLSS of course) at 1080p and not even flinch. The MSI? Ehhhh not so much, the 970M is showing it's age as it has to run medium to low settings with shadows pretty much disabled to keep a playable framerate. However this does not stop the visuals from being absolutely outstanding. The art; textures and modelling are top notch and the animations are extremely well done. How's it sound? Well the voice overs are absolutely well done, the music screams professionalism and variety while the sound effects are near perfect. Weaponry is loud and punchy; Night City itself has incredible ambience and sounds alive as a city should. I have some gripes with sounds disappearing when you turn your head (a certain guitar around a campfire for instance) but that's all really. Even NPC voice acting of the random citizens is well done, despite the limited and repeated responses you get, but overall quality is excellent.How's it play? Hmm this is a mixed bag. I enjoy it but I am not blown away by it. The melee combat is well done but no Dark Messiah. The gunplay is satisfying but not particularly engaging, I find myself wading in with a solid Katana way more than I do a gun, as it just seems so much more effective. The skill and attribute systems are well crafted and at least make sense; the perk trees are varied and well rounded, effective and meaningful with excellent descriptions and no fog hiding your next choices *cough looking at you Valhalla cough*. The hacking minigame is cool and a good little diversion but there's no Gwent contemporary, what gives? Cars drive. I guess. They don't feel particularly special or unique and I found myself preferring motorcycles to get around but they are nice to have. I wish there was custom modding for vehicles that would be cool. AI traffic patterns are absolutely trash. Character customizing is one-shot right at the beginning and everything from hair style to penis size is modifiable which is cool. There's a lot of things to change and looks to create which is great I love choice but there's no body type changing. Clothing/armour is a mixed bag of results, you can at least spend resources to upgrade the clothes you like to wear and stick with stuff through most of the game. Crafting is excellent and if you do it right you can become a crafting god and almost invincible.Wait you said bugs earlier? Yeah. There's a couple. I haven't encountered many game breakers but I have encountered lots of unexplained CTDs. I also had a few where my skills stopped leveling, that was fun had to find a way to fix that so I didn't have to restart or lose progress. There's often floating cigarettes and glasses and the like, and sometimes objects in an NPCs hand can become displaced in cutscenes which really ruins immersion. Overall I'd say this should have spent some more time in the oven but hey gotta make some scratch and cater to the masses, right?What about the characters? Okay, I gotta say this is where I absolutely love this game. The characters you meet, the stories you unfold, they are incredible. Everyone has a story and ties into the overarching life of V throughout the game. Everyone that you meet matters in some way, however small, even the fixers have a purpose to you. There are just some super well written people you will meet in this game from a certain Nomad who's story just blew me away to a reformed street thug with a heart of gold to disgraced samurai. This game covers all the bases and I think that is what is keeping my interest in this game right now overall. I mean pandemic and all, connecting with virtual people is all I can do right now anyway.Night City? Oh yeah, the city she is alive. It is a well made environment with a moving population. Not gonna say living as they don't really have lives per se, people just kind of exist and their AI and interactions are extremely limited. But it's a great environment to roam and explore. It's well built and wide open, no barriers, you can climb and jump on any building, reach the rooftops and then slide off the side of the building and land with no issues 'cause.. oh wait that's kind of a bug I guess, anyways Night City is cool.AI? It's not all there. Enemies are dense and charge you. Others can breach your systems without line of sight and do it from a mile away because ♥♥♥♥ you that's why. Melee enemies are chaotic and flit around like little nutcases until you behead them. Snipers are deadly accurate and will tear you to shreds if you don't watch out and get them first. It's a mixed bag of cats really. I just charge around and cut limbs off at this point and pound back health inhalers like an asthmatic.Overall this game is a solid 8-8.5 out of 10 at this point. Give it some time to properly cook and it'll be a 9 to 9.3 by the end of the next six months. Some solid DLC (which will be free, given CDPR's track record) and this will be a worthy title to add to your collection. As it is, it's a solid game with some teething issues and a case of the scatterbrained sometimes.Now I did NOT buy into the hype on this game. I kept myself as isolated as I could from it in fact, and I went into this title with no insane expectations. I did not take time off work to play it. I did not sell my children to buy it. It is not the second coming to me. I bought it because I was intrigued by the setting and the game type which is right up my alley and I don't regret spending $80CDN on this game because I will enjoy it overall and get my money's worth out of it.I will end this review with a phrase I like to use: Your mileage may vary. If you enjoy deep, convoluted plot lines with multi-faceted dialogue that can change the outcome of the game at a moments notice, with a decent if flawed combat system and a well developed RPG mechanic set in a over the top gorgeous setting: then this game is for you. Just beware the bugs as this game is still in development, no matter what the PR folks want to spoon feed you. ♥♥♥♥ that was a long review. I'll TLDR this: Cyberpunk 2077 is a great game with flaws. Just like every other game out there. It is not perfect. Live with it and enjoy what this game offers: Solid gameplay. Solid graphics. Superb story and characters. That's it. I'm done, have fun out there chooms and be safe.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent atmosphere/setting/story (main  side!), supported by preem Kiroshi Optics visuals and on par sound(track). All the while Takemura teaches the virtue of patience, awaiting you to finish making BD-worthy memories for 100+ hours. Playing after patch 1.6, I avoided technical drama. The fixes are a big plus, at some cost to story immersion by CDPR putting less fuel on your real life hate for (mega)corporations. Combat/gameplay is well enough and allows catering to your style. Albeit with a multilayered leveling system that isn't intuitive in giving a good overview of options (you can't max everything). No, it's not the hyped up "second life simulator". Many dialogue choices have limited to no effect. There aren't "random" (scripted) events or activities on every corner. But a preem gift with less fancy wrapping is still a preem gift - worth the €$.

_childDocuments_.review: The reason cyberpunk got hate was because it was a bit too ambitious and people expected far too much from the standpoint of gameplay. When it comes to the negatives people cover of this game, they usually go towards gameplay. Personally I didn't find any issue with any of that, i only really began to get upset once i learned of all the wasted potential the game had, this brings me to the real issue which is the story. Cyberpunk 2077's story is ok, it really shines in its side missions where you truly get engaged into stuff happening in night city. The life-path system which was very heavily advertised was significantly chopped down in order to release the game on time, i feel like this was a huge mistake, as its the most important part of the game if you take the role playing elements seriously. Overall i recommend Cyberpunk 2077. good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 - Early Access!?I think my review is legit after 97 hours of gameplay and my second playthrough at the highest difficulty in which I have done 100% of the content.There is not much to say, currectly the game is in very questionable condition. I would rather call it an Alpha Version.Pros:- Gameplay is solid- Soundtrack is pretty awesome- Storyline is interesting with many possible outcomes- Interesting characters- Pretty decent open world- Graphics are absolutely okayCons:- Bugs (too many to count them)- Glitches (some of them gamebreaking)- Most stupid AI ever (repetetive movement/behavior, no interaction at all)- The world is full, but also very empty- Dialogue choices for the story doen't have any impact- Romances are available, but not mentionable at all- No customization of the character after creation (hairstyle, tattoos)- New implants are just buyable, no actual surgery scene like in the prologeThat was a short list of things that I had to mention, now to my personal opinion and why I don't recommend it buying, although I am a hardcore fanboy (as you would say).First of all: I really like the game and the storytelling, but not because it is CDPR, no for real, the game has much potential and I like the 1980s-NYC-Tokyo looking style of the world. But it has as many problems as there is potential. It's not in a finished state at the moment. Far from being released to the public for a full price title. It hurts to write these words, but it's the truth. And if you reflect about your own experience, you should have the same feeling.It is not what we were looking forward to, but it's what we got. Some people out there raged on social media and pressure on the Devs had risen after the past months. So I think they rushed this piece into the release date, to satisfy all the little crybabies, who cry out loud now too.I just give my honest opinion to this title. It's playable, enjoyable and loveable, but also absolutely hateable.The dialogues are sometimes too "cool" for me. V wants to sound like a badass "chicc", but sometimes it feels just like it's over the top. Yeah I understand, he/she's a badass person, but a more decent dub would have been much more pleasant.It doesn't even make a difference what kind of background you choose in the beginning. I had high hopes that the whole gameplay would be kinda different and the story would be a little diverse, but that hope has been flatlined pretty quickly.The only thing that's different: You got a different Prologue, here and there extra choices in conversations, nothing else.Gameplay is for all 3 backgrounds the same. Doesn't affect your skills and appearance at all, or the way other characters interact with you.All in all I would not recommend paying 60 bucks or more for this title, even tho it was the lightbringer of the year 2020. CDPR deserves a lot of good reputation and I am sure they will fix this ting up in no time, but sadly I have to be honest with my critics and tell you: Wait for a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 - one of the most anticipated game of all time. I completed the game on maximum difficulty and got all 6 endings. And it was... awesome. A stunning emotional and philosophical storyline. But as cool as cyberpunk is as a story work, it technically has an insane amount of problems. Retarded AI... maybe one of the most stupid i've ever seen in games. This completely ruins the stealth gameplay. Dead open world, badly vehicle physics, a lot of bug's and many more issues. This product has required at least one year to optimize and fixing all troubles. You can enjoy this game only on high end pc(from 2077 :D). The pleasure and immersion in this game is completely dependent on the visual. At ultra settings with ray tracing Cyberpunk 2077 look's like really nextgen title. In that sense, Cyberpunk is one of those rare games that fully embraces the latest in PC technology to deliver a true leap in fidelity - a modern day Crysis, if you like. Night City is a dense, multi-tiered, vertical city built using the latest in graphics technology alongside smart visual design. Lighting, materials and volumetrics are key to delivering this next-gen vision, but there's more to it than that - what really sells this world is the sheer volume of detail and life on display. Structures are richly detailed, LOD management is handled seamlessly and the streets of often packed. The best way I can describe it is that it has the level of detail you'd expect from a hub area in Deus Ex at a much larger scale. In conclusion, this is a next generation game but there's no doubt that to get a good experience from it, like i said before, u need a high end pc. I mean all pc parts. CPU, GPU, RAM and SSD. This game will eat all computing resources. But it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start by saying that this is not a review it's just my personal opinion and what i felt playing Cyberpunk 2077. I've tried playing the game before CDPR updates it and release the DLC but i never finished it, and not because the game then was in a bad state or anything.Also this isn't a comeback story about making something bad , good. No, there was always something there. Perhaps one of the most beautiful stories of all time that deserves to be heard that was shrouded by the endless hate online. The thing is that this games most endorsed aspects by the people are the exact same things that were always so impactful since day one. It was never about the police chases, it wasn't about the npc's with unique day cycles , a living breathing world or a sandbox RPG that was devoid of all bugs and glitches, this game was always so much more than that. It has a deeper meaning the likes of which i never seen pulled of this well in an entertainment product even outside of games, at least for me. But now it's proven that it's home to something greater and most of all it's because Cyberpunk 2077 focuses on providing what i think is the biggest lessons that we can all learn in life and maybe the most impressive and awe inspiring fantasy  and sci-fi setting to date.I just want to point out that Cyberpunk 2077 is the first ever open world game where i never fast traveled, the city, the sounds, the music blaring on the radio as you drive hundreds of miles an hour through busy streets. That's what this game is all about. There is an enormous amount of scale and wonder in every location, mega buildings stretch well into the sky , neon lights make every scene at night to burst with colors and the sounds of the city as you move from small back streets into open and strawling highways, sells the experience perfectly. Without a doubt cyberpunk has the best city put to games ever and it's not even close. It feels less like a video game level and more like a real place. There is history to every location along with a key focus on making everything in the world feel realistic and lived in. When an NPC in game calls you choom or chika or refers to their lovers as inputs it all just feels right , it feels natural to the world on offer here and makes every scene and moment that much more convincing. When you first step into Konpeki plaza for the big gig with Jackie for instance, looking at the staff in the hotel covered from head to toe in gold plating shows you everything you need to know. People in this world are nothing more that an asset to big corporations. Humanity and individuality is at at it's lowest point and money, power and influence is what truly matters. And that isn't obvious because it's referenced in dialog lines across the game, it's obvious because the world itself acts as if that's truly the case and every interaction you have within sells every bit of lore just as well. Is it the most alive feeling open world ever that you can make anything you want? No, definitely not, but it does succeed at its main goal of immersing you in this world so deeply. A special mention has to be given to the music in this game too. There are countless times in main inside missions alike where a song starts to pick up in the background and truly pull me into a scene and evoke such strong emotions, whether that be feeling sad or bad ass alike. There is probably a reason that every side and main mission in this game is named after songs. That's because music is an absolutely integral part of the product on offer here. Next time you play put on some headphones and just walk slowly around any of the downtown areas, listen to the hustle and bustle and sounds of gunshots in the distance or the birds chirping by the city square. This open world could certainly be improved in a lot of ways but it does what it needs to do most. And that's the biggest accomplishment of this game in my opinion, is just how believable the characters and world are. There aren't romances like other games where everyone wants to have sex with you the second they see you, these aren't superheroes we see in marvel movies who feel like they are spitting out one one - liner after another. These characters feel like real people and the world they live in feels like its own character all to itself, one that would carry on with or without you. Characters have their own personalities there own motives and most of all journeys that define the people they were and the person they've become. All based on small decisions you can make with how you interact with them. Because of how masterfully all of these immersive elements are intertwined, you wind up getting a game that is so good not because it has the best graphics ever or the coolest world or an a-list celebrity cast acting as some of the characters, but so good because it has such a deeper meaning to it all than most games, whose biggest aim is just being fun and entertaining. What I'm trying to say is that this world and people in it are all imperfect in there own ways just like our real world and because of that the stories and narratives that you undergo here tackle some of the most depressing and depraved things in all of our humanity. But each with such care, and such a masterful writing that puts CDPR into a league of their own. Cyberpunk 2077 isn't GTA in the future, it isn't supposed to be a massive open sandbox where you can do anything you want and that's because i think it's something that's much better than all of that, something much more meaningful, a dive into what it means to be human, to love, to sacrifice and to lose our very souls or fight until our last breath in the service of what really matters in life. A set of character pieces that look at the most evil but also the most beautiful parts of what it means to live a life, the things that make us cry at night and the things that awake us in the morning with a fire in our souls to make things right. It's about giving us a look into a world with no happy endings but rather lessons that will last with us for a lifetime. And the single most impactful moments in this collage of so many, the ones that solidify this game as real art, are the endings. Where we can either choose to forge a path in a blaze of glory and become the living legend we always dreamed of or instead forego all of that for something even more greater, for family, friends and a purpose to something more that ourselves. This is a message that only a game like Cyberpunk can pull off and one that is more powerful than anything else this game was ever hyped to be, and now finally with Phantom Liberty we can see the final confirmation of this.

_childDocuments_.review: After revisiting Cyberpunk 2077, I have to admit, my opinion of the game has changed. Yes, I still have to acknowledge the numerous bugs and horrible AI, but despite these shortcomings, I found myself enjoying the game much more than I initially anticipated.I'm a picky gamer, and it's been years since I've spent more than a few hours playing a game per week, but with Cyberpunk 2077, I clocked in 80 hours of gameplay within the first week. The story is fantastic, the gameplay is exciting, and the dystopian setting is brilliantly executed. Even now, months after playing, I find myself missing the game.However, after 100% completing the game, with all main and side quests, collectibles, and vehicles bought, I found myself with nothing left to do. This highlights the lack of new content since launch. CDPR's few updates have been minor fixes, and the promised DLC is nowhere in sight.Additionally, there are numerous features missing that should have been in the game since launch, such as character appearance customization, relationships, romance, player choices, vehicle customization, and realistic NPCs.Although I came into the game with high expectations, I still found myself loving it. CDPR didn't make the perfect game, but they created a world that caught my attention and kept me engaged. Despite its flaws, Cyberpunk 2077 is a game that I will not forget.In conclusion, my opinion of the game is a mix of emotions, but the positives outweigh the negatives. I have changed my review, even though it meant erasing over a thousand upvotes in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: YOU CAN PET THE CATS--EDIT--What do I do with my life now?On a more serious note, here's a full review. Know first that I did a lot of side content, though not all of it, and only went through one ending so far, and that because bugs are inconsistent between experiences, I will be omitting them as a factor.This is NOT a GTA game, and if you go into it looking for that, you will be disappointed.Cyberpunk 2077 places you into a detailed and immersive world where cybernetic enhancement is commonplace and most of the power is held by a few megacorporations. Going through the world will show you the consequences of this power disparity and the hedonistic, consumerist culture of Night City, from the enormous megastructures towering into the sky to scrapyards of discarded assorted junk straight from Wall-E.The world has plenty of quests to do, many of which of have the same good writing to be expected of CDPR, and almost all of them are more of the same game, no tedious or gimmicky shoehorned in bland missions, they're just more Cyberpunk. The side quests for romanceable characters are especially good, and these characters are exceptionally well-written, to the point that they feel like real people.On the subject of characters, Keanu Reeves' portrayal of Johnny Silverhand, the long-dead rebellious rocker-boy turned terrorist, is simply flawless. His input during both the main story and side missions, as well as some points throughout the game world, really helps bring you into the world, and can make you question some of the decisions you make throughout the game.I will not spoil the main story, but I will say the writing is good and it takes you to encounter all major factions in the game, and the endings will give you feels. However, it does imply a time limit to complete the main story, which I am personally not a fan of, as there's a huge disconnect from "you have 2 weeks" and then doing every single side mission while Takemura waits for you to swing by and advance the main quest. In case it's not clear, there is no time limit for playing the game, even though the main story implies it.Story is all well and good, but if you're like me, you also need fun gameplay to really enjoy the game. Cyberpunk's gameplay puts you in first person and gives you several options to approach combat or avoid it. You can run around and take out enemies at close range with a gun or melee while remaining mobile, you damage enemies with quickhacks or cause things like weapon malfunctions, you can play it as a cover shooter, or you can avoid combat entirely, knocking out enemies one at a time, using quickhacks to distract them or even take them out from a distance hacking them through their own cameras. In many cases where your objective is not to take out all enemies, you can given multiple ways in, either through some climbing or by using skills checks to open new paths. As for the weapon and loot system, it is straight out of Borderlands, and that is all there is to say about it.All in all, this is a great game, if you can run it, and I look forward to going through again when any future expansions come out, at which point I hope to have a better computer.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. Even if it still needs work in August 2021 (patch 1.23).Play it now. Then wait 4-6 months for the DLCs and other patches to come out. Then play it again as the other gender with different attributes. Perfect.1. That story. Holy s h i t. Who are you? What does dying mean? What's a legacy? What does living mean? Delicious.2. Voice acting is the best I've ever heard in a large-scale RPG. Better than many tighter narrative-focused games, too.3. Night City has one hell of a culture. You really feel like you've been some place, by the time you're done.4. You'll max out 2/5 of your attributes in one playthrough if you focus only on them. You won't get anywhere near picking all of the perks in your chosen attributes. 5 possible endings. Countless ways to end character-centric side quests. 2-3 ways to approach and end most gigs (single-location, single-objective missions).5. Keanu Reeves does a shockingly good job rendering Johnny Silverhand as an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tumor you want removed from your head. I don't know how he does it with that near-deadpan style of his. But he nailed that feel.6. Combat feels super good. Guns chunk when you shoot them. Enemies react where you hit them. Frying someone's brain with a certain quickhack makes them convulse while sparks shoot from their eyes, ears and mouth. Get a high jump or a double jump. Strap a missile launcher or big fists or huge blades or a whip to your arm for extra lulz.7. Decision making EXTREMELY subtle in just the right places. You make decisions based on how you feel, not what outcome you want to see (because the outcome of a decision really isn't always clear, beforehand).8. All of the RPG things are very cleverly versatile to make for some interesting building. If you go cool and intelligence, you could build a long distance hacker. Cool and reflexes, you've got James Bond.Game mostly works just fine. Glitches are now fixing their selves so the game can get itself back on track. Example: Car stuck in the ground. Go interact with the door and it pops out of the ground and lands where it should, so you can get in. Or a character accidentally sits in the ground rather than on their bike. Game realizes it happened and teleports them to the bike seat so mission can go as intended.There are a few bugs that are still very annoying. These are the ones I can remember:1. ADS sometimes doesn't work. That is, you can fire from the hip, but not while ADS, sometimes. No clear cause. Just sometimes it happens. Have to save and reload to fix it.2. Some "authorization only" doors won't open, even if you have the authorization card. Never breaks a mission. But these doors guard extra loot and data terminals in gigs and side missions. Very annoying.3. Sometimes, you can't change the radio station in your car. No clear cause. Just holding "r" doesn't do anything. Save and reload fixes it.4. NPCs take derpy paths, sometimes. Like walking over railings and then on air. Or walking over a car that's in the way.5. Quickhacks sometimes don't work on enemies. Game lets you upload the hack, but no effects nor damage happen. I think some enemies might be immune to quickhacks. If that's the case, the behavior is fine, but the game shouldn't allow you to try and upload the hack.And then there are things that would just be super rad if they were added:1. If the quest log detailed your decisions and what happened rather than just showing you the mission's flavor text forever. I forgot about whole characters because 50-60 hours passed between the time I met them and the next time they came up in the story.2. More side quests with the relationship characters. You get an intro quest sequence and then a relationship-building quest sequence. Would be really cool to have one more you do as full buddies or romantic partners.3. Other things that I'm forgetting about, right now.Now's the time for a first playthrough. You are DEFINITELY going to play this game more than once. Multiple playstyles, multiple endings, multiple relationships, multiple main characters (lady V, guy V).After the first, wait 4-6 months for more patches and DLCs. The itch will just be returning to you, and you can play a better version in a different style.

_childDocuments_.review: I must preface beforehand I have a decent spec'd computer which is able to play the game very well and as of writing this review I have ~50 hours played based on steam's playtime. If there is a phrase I could use to summarize the game it would probably be .Cyberpunk 2077 was originally announced 8 years ago and the hype around the game was through the roof. Everyone couldn't wait to see the next big game CDPR was going to create after the overwhelming success of The Witcher 3, and it would be this same success which would ultimately lead to their biggest disappointment.Every bit of news that revealed anything about the game was like bits of crack for the general public to get high on. We had reveals of a large open world rpg set in the futuristic city, Night City, bustling with 1000's of unique AI, a "wanted" system with corrupt police officers that could be bribed, an immersive combat system with multiple methods of taking down your foes, a unique hacking system that gave you access to various intel on the world around you, a litany of quests that had a meaningful impact on your playthrough depending on the choices you made, an extensive character customization unlike anything we've seen before, and at the heart of it all is you, the player character, "V".You are supposed to play as "V", who is an everyday bloke that has dreams of making it big one day and to strive towards their goal, they take on jobs from "fixers" that have them doing all sorts of tasks and activities.  The more jobs you complete the well known you become on the streets and at some point big corporations would take notice. Whether they were beneficial to you or not was dependent on your choices in the game and your unique playstyle. After 8 years of development with multiple delays to the release I can tell you the only thing that is remotely close to what was promised is the fact that the map is called Night City. The game feels like a hollow shell of what was advertised and makes you wonder what was being done during development. The AI feels like something from a game 2 decades ago. The world is depressingly empty to the point its like playing in the same universe as Will Smith's "I am Legend". The AI that inhabit the world are all cookie cutter walking/talking npc's with no interactions whatsoever. The wanted system is essentially non-existent and the police AI literally teleports behind you in droves until you are either dead or managed to run across the block to drop your wanted status. The combat system is generic as shooters go, you shoot/pummel/slice someone to death and you rinse and repeat, the only difference is how the bullets come out of your gun. The hacking system is disappointingly shallow, where all you need to do is point and click to "hack" something for a miniscule advantage. The choices you make in quests have no impact whatsoever to the world around you and you are essentially given the illusion of free will. And the character customization is probably the most pointless thing in the game since the game is played in "first person" and you don't even see yourself in cutscenes. This is just a small snippet of things that were changed or is outright missing from the initial reveal to it's eventual release. I haven't even mentioned the vast amount of bugs in the game and unpolished feel the game has. If you have a beefy PC then you can count yourself "lucky" to be able to "play" the game. If you are playing this on a next gen console then the game is somewhat playable and if you are the unlucky few playing on base current gen consoles, then I am truly sorry for your experience. The huge amount of issues the game has at its current state and the vast of fundamental changes or cut to content makes you feel like what was advertised and what was delivered are two completely different products, and this is what is truly sad. The game's story is actually very nice and makes you want to keep playing just to know what happens next, and the side quests given to you by some of the unique npc's are pretty deep and you can tell that CDPR put time into the development of said quests. Outside of the few positive things about the game, you can't just help it but think about  for Cyberpunk 2077.The success of TW3 gave CDPR huge renown which led to expectations for this game to reach astronomical levels, and just like Icarus, CDPR flew too close to the sun. Hopefully over the course of the next year CDPR fixes the core issues with the game and implements some of the main missing features, but as it stands even though I am enjoying my experience with game, I cannot recommend the game in its current state. If you want to play an immersive open world game, go play Red Dead Redemption 2.If you want to play a futuristic, sci-fi, cyberpunk game, go play Deus Ex Human Revolution/Mankind Divided.If you want to play a game with tons of character customization and sex-capades, go play Saints Row the Third.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels wrong to review this, because to be quite honest this feels like it needed 2-3 years longer in the oven. I have no relationship with this company, I'm indifferent to them. I'm not a hater nor a fan boy. I'm going to be honest, I don't like the combat. I predominantly play RPGs but I enjoy shooter mechanics too, albeit I'm not good at it. But in this game, shooting is very, very unsatisfying. The entire RPG element of leveling up and putting points into skills really do not translate well into a shooter. Actually, it removed the entire enjoyment of shooters. When I headshot someone, I expect them to die, and you are rewarded with that satisfaction of delivering it. I don't want to see DPS numbers like I'm playing a MMO. The entire experience would have been much better without this, guns are guns, customisation is great, but at some point it's like you have to take a step back and think about what works great and what doesn't. You can have a lot of ways to work with guns without trying to force a bizzare rpg skill tree element to it.The controls are really frustrating, the universal button for interactions and such in fps games is E. For some reasons, they decided no, we aren't having that. On top of this, you can't customise this without taking the time to edit your configuration files. Great. Nobody likes over complicating simple things, but in this game, that's a feature. There are so many buttons, for so many things during so many different settings, it's a headache! Of course the optimization is pretty bad. A LOT of settings are hidden, and relies on on people to mod it to reveal them. Why? Honestly? _childDocuments_.review: This game was a game of firsts for me. My first pre order, my first modern rpg, my first 500 hours spent in a game, my first long ass review no one will even read. But I need to talk about this game, because it´s that good.The story touched me in ways I couldn´t have foreseen. Johnny's frustration with the system and the desire to change it, when there's really no clear or clean way to do so was incredibly relatable, and it put a lot of my thoughts into words. The story is good, not too long, which, paired up with some great side-quests, makes for a longer experience if you desire it. One of my favourite aspects of this game is the customization. For your build, and for your character. Being able to play as a woman, made to look like I want her too, with great voice acting and to have me able to choose her clothes, and choose the build, which can be anything from melee to stealth to guns to sniper rifles, was a major deal breaker. Yes the game is first person, and I would't have it any other way, as there's many moments that would only work in first person, but you know how your character looks, you hear her, you see her in the mirror. And as a woman, being able to play as one in game was great for my immersion.The gameplay. Ah, where do I even start? There's a lot, a lot of options, so as you imagine there's some hits and some misses. The melee combat could use some work, and as much as I would love to use the monowire more, the execution of it lacks some nedeed complexity. But the gunplay is amazing, the details in the guns, the animation, the sounds are great, and they're just fun to use. The katanas are very good too. There's also a lot of cyberware, from your cyberdeck to the double jump legs, which opens a lot of doors for different builds. The stealth is fun without being too challenging.The music. THE MUSIC. It feels like a love letter to music and rock sometimes. I can't listen to "Been Good to Know ya" or "Never Fade Away" without crying a little. The quality of the music really makes the world believable, they sound and feel like they were recorded there. I could go on forever, I really could. This game watched me grow. I went from struggling on easy with a very bad build to thriving on very hard. I know I love this game because it's message stays with me and I carry it and think about it on my day to day life. I loved it from the moment I read the description back in september 2020, and I love it now, more than one year later, because it taught me to keep fighting, even if the fight seems already lost. The game is not perfect, and this is not an objective review by any means, because objectivity is overrated when there's so much soul to be seen and felt every second you play it.Thank youThank you for everything.

_childDocuments_.review: What a mess... Where do I even begin... Lets start with pros. Visually game looks really good. City looks really impressive and alive at first glance. Character designs look fresh and colorful. Voice acting is superb, radio stations have some bangers and soundtrack overall is pretty good. Whole lore is interesting aswell. But thats where pros end. Im not gonna tell how many bugs and glitches Ive found because its countess, and it would be a low hanging fruit to pick. Lets start with rpg elements. There are very little of those. From the get go you start with choosing what life path you will go for. And pretty much only first intro missions will be impacted by that. Maybe the end aswell, but Im not going to torture myself anymore to find that out. There will be some dialog options of your life path, but it doesnt seem that it makes any difference on how mission will be played out. Skills and attributes are pretty boring outside a few hacking ones that can be fun. Lets talk about loot you collect. This game is more of a looter shooter than anything else. Loot is everywhere. And most of it is useless and pain in the ass to even sell it in those drop boxes or whatever they are called. I dont know who was the genius to make gear that has stats. If you want to have good stats on your character, you most likely gonna look like a clown most of the time. I thought this is going to be an rpg experience... Why do I have to look like a rejected stripper clown with a bulletproof west and a fedora to have good stats? Combat feels alright I guess... I didint expect some top tier fps shooter or anything. But melee combat is just bare bones at best... Lets talk about A.I... Im not sure what happened there, but A.I. is hands down the most stupid one Ive ever seen on any video game. First you step into the city, youll be impressed in how many different kind of people are out there and they look like they have theyr own jobs and dutiers to do. But once you try to fallow them around to see what they gonna do, its like you break the matrix. If you go aggressive towards them, theyre just going to crouch down and do nothing. Car A.I. is as dubb as normal civilians. If youll leave your car in the middle of the street, they will just stop infront of it and do nothing. Cause they dont know how to go around you. Can you have fun just by killing everyone and go on a police chase? No. Cause police cant even drive cars. And as a matter of fact, once you drive off like a block or two, they will forget you ever did anything bad. Whole city has alot of nudity and ads with sexual references, but only two prostitutes if you wanna have fun like that. For the most part you will be driving around the city. And driving isnt good either. Its not horrible, but still could be better. Player freedom in this game is very very limited. I really really doubt that you could finish this game without killing anyone. There goes your role play. I could go on and on with all the negative stuff this game has. And no matter how many patches and fixes theres gonna be, the game is just broken beyond repair in my opinion. 5/10 at best.

_childDocuments_.review: The best compliment I can pay it is that it in decades of playing all manner of games across all meaner of eras, I don't think I've seen something that was as immersive feeling as this game. It is something else in it's ability to set a mood both is visuals and sound. I said to someone yesterday that at times you can just about taste what is happening and I don't think that is an exaggeration. The world feels real and lived in every way possible though this medium.As for the game itself best way I can describe the game is if Borderlands 2, (new) Deus Ex, The Division and GTA V co-parented a game together. The game sits in a unique spot at the cross-section of action shooter and RPG  that makes it seem both familiar and something new. The gunplay feels very solid and exploring the world is endlessly cool. I have to take a break to do real world stuff today, but I absolutely cant wait to play more. I was pleasantly surprised that the game is essentially a sequel/continuation of the old Cyberpunk 2020 RPG - I had presumed it was going to be more of just a reboot using the franchise elements, but it actually tries to present a 'this is what happened' move forward. My playgroups in HS were more into Shadowrun so I had only read some of the books back then and never got to play it. Despite that, I was still excited to see 'old' netrunning decks and Spider Murphy show up in a flashback sequence, though - the nostalgia isn't as high for me on this as others, but its an attention to detail that warms the heart.Game is not perfect - bugs are real (the NVidia update helped a lot though), the melee combat is kinda ass, and the writing early on did suffer from Coolist F'in Guy syndrome due to some trying-to-hard edgelord tendencies. However, the script has improved as the game has progressed and the story becoming more and more compelling. Also the female V voice is way, way better than the male voice - so much so I kinda want to restart so as not to be chained to Chad McChadinstien for the next billion hours. Word of caution though - I bought a good-ish PC a year ago that had specs beefy enough to run the game on High at a good FPS clip. Evidently it runs like boiled carp on old machines, so buyer beware.

_childDocuments_.review: That is the sole word that comes to mind when I think of Cyberpunk 2077. To be fair, I didn't expect it to be the greatest game of all time, but I did hope for an above average game. After almost a hundred hours, a bunch of side quests, and experiencing all of the endings, I feel like this game wasn't anything progressive, and leaves much to be desired.I won't lie, Night City is the shining point of this game. The overall scope and density of the city is one of the things this game did right. In the opening free sections of the game, I found myself just completely lost in this massive city, just one little person among thousands. Getting to play this game with higher settings is real eye candy due to all of the colorful lights and dark shadows the city has. The real big drawback are the NPCs, they just feel lifeless and half the time cower in fear cause you accidentally bumped into them. I always look for a way to feel like I am in the game that I am playing and Cyberpunk does just that. The gameplay is very solid and works great for me. If you've played games like Borderlands or Far Cry, you should feel right at home here. I played through the game as a Stealthy Netrunner type of character and it was a joy to create new and powerful quick hacks that are fun to play with. The ability to approach the side gigs however you want is addictive and it always keeps the game fun, because the game is in  control. Upgrading cyberware is a real treat too, as you can get some pretty sick upgrades to feel like a beast. However, this game adapts looter shooter mechanics having you loot the same guns and armor constantly just because they do a higher damage, or it has higher armor, and it bugs the ♥♥♥♥ out of me of how lazy this all feels. Also, there is no sort of Transmog system in this game, which is just flat out unacceptable. So what if the game is in first person? There are still various ways to see your character in the game, and I think everyone would prefer not to look like a complete troglodyte!This is where this game let me down the most. I can't believe there are so many people out there who say this is the saving grace of this game, I just think it's flat out rushed and uninteresting. I won't spoil anything, but I will say that I forced myself to finish the main questline. I didn't end up beating the game until my 90 hour mark, because I had no desire to even do it. This story had moments where it could have taken off, but I feel like the devs were rushed and didn't bother giving it more life or fleshing it out. The on-the-rails, overly-scripted shooting segments are just flat out embarrassing, is this a serious RPG, or a Call of Duty campaign?? Nothing memorable or really remarkable, I'll easily forget it in a month or two. This story was way too  for a game this size. There are other things that I will discuss that add to this lackluster story below. To keep this short, 90% of the characters in this game are just plain boring. I felt  emotional connection to them, and only really talked to the side ones just so I can do their quests, get the xp, and move on. There are so many times where the game wants you to care about these people that you meet, but they're just uninteresting, and there's just so minimal relationship building done between V and them. Seriously, it feels like most characters you meet in this game just automatically becomes your close friend. Like Jackie, I literally had a dialogue option to tell him that I could get to Night City on my own(Nomad btw), and the game just says NOPE and forces him to become my best friend through a short ass montage. What a joke! Just like the story, not enough time was put in enough to these characters.This, this is probably the worst part of the game. CD PROJEKT RED advertised this game to be a full-fledged RPG. Yeah. NOPE. This game is one of the most casual/minimalist RPGs I have ever played. I'm sorry if I was expecting a lot more, but this is as casual and basic as they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ come. I hardly feel like I am role-playing the character that I really wanted to be. This isn't your story, this is V's. I felt so out of connection with my V that it just felt like I wasn't playing the character that I created. Now one might say: "oH BuT WhAt aBoUt tHe sKiLl tReEs? ThE SkIlL ChEcKs? ThE DiAlOgUe oPtIoNs?" All of those are just equally a let down as the rest of the game. To add to the "rpg" aspect of the game, Cyberpunk has a bunch of skills that can be earned through leveling. I will say that these trees are fine and I felt they did their job respectfully. Most of them just upgrade how fast you can hack, or how much damage you do with melee, etc. However, now comes the point where those skills get put into skill check sections, and this just straight up pathetic. Pretty much all of the "skill checks" in this game do NOTHING! I've reloaded saves and tried out outcomes with and without the successful skill check and they pretty much lead to the SAME outcome. A successful skill check most of the time results in an extra line or two of dialogue. The most disgraceful skill checks are the ones that you pass, but the game literally tells you to ♥♥♥♥ yourself. For example, there is a quest where you need to purchase this quest item off a dealer. The game presents a skill check for a certain attribute that you need a certain amount of points spec'd into to ask the dealer for a discount. I had enough spec'd points to ask him and the response I got was, "Go ♥♥♥♥ yourself". Pathetic, I feel like that was a message from the devs to players like me hoping for my skills to actually have an effect on my character, sorry for wanting something that's in practically every RPG. Basically, your skills are only tied to how buffed you want your character to be with certain weapons, or hacking, that's it. Then comes speech, which is one of the most important parts of an RPG in my opinion. The speech options in this game are minimal and don't really do anything to the story. You may invoke a different emotion from a character depending on your dialogue option, but they quickly snap back into whatever you were talking about. Yet another half-baked aspect of the game. Your life-path? Practically meaningless, especially for Nomads like myself. I didn't expect the life-paths to be anything crazy like change the entire game, but man the life-paths are really just an illusion in this game. Once you're done with the incredibly short intro mission for your life-path you are pretty much at the same point as everyone else in the game. The Nomad intro was just flat out terrible as you're only in the badlands for such a short amount of time, to the point where I don't feel like I am a Nomad, I'm just a Nomad because the game is telling me that I am. From then on, your life-path is only relevant through meaningless dialogue options with other characters. All I wanted was a much stronger start for the life-path, perhaps with characters that you can interact with that are exclusively met in specific life paths, which isn't asking for too much. Then comes the "choices". I already discussed the disappointing speech choices, but when it comes to choices that shape your character, there really isn't any, once again making this a bare bone RPG. There are times when you can choose to kill or save a certain character, and the outcome isn't anything substantial.

I'm sorry to say this game has been a mismanaged mess on par with EA's Anthem.CDPR should take this as a lesson, substantially downsize your marketing team and focus on making good games. _childDocuments_.review: I had originally started writing a much longer Steam review for Cyberpunk 2077, but due to the 8000 character limit, I didn't get even halfway through, so I will condense it into some finer points. Cyberpunk has a few problems. The biggest to me is the lack of content that was promised by developers but never made it into the final game. It's well documented in the development process just how much didn't make the cut and was removed before release. I hope they will reintroduce some of these features in later updates. The AI is hugely problematic and really breaks immersion. Crowds of NPCs will crouch and cower when you commit a crime near them, all doing identical animations, police spawn in infinitely near you out of nowhere, but don't follow or chase you when you flee the scene, the AI is truly a mess. Much of the games content feels meaningless, life paths have no effect on what actually happens in the story and merely offers you a different prologue or some lines in conversation that, again, have no impact on the actual game. Loot has similar issues where for you find yourself wearing a skirt, power scouter and a bandana because they offer 10 points more armour than the kevlar vest you've been wearing for the last 3 hours. This applies to weapons too and makes the loot system largely redundant, as you're swapping out weapons for a tiny numerical increase. Lastly I wanted to touch on optimisation. Although I personally didn't have many issues with performance, I did experience bugs, but all of them were fixed with Cyberpunk 2077 isn't all bad. I've seen lots of people complain about the RPG elements but I think these claims are baseless. The skill tree offers around 240 nodes for you to spec into, changing abilities or giving increases to different stats. A large number of choices in how you spec and the cybernetics will influence how all combat is handled. There are skill checks in Cyberpunk and whilst mostly they aren't influential to the game itself, your attributes are used in the world and dialogue too. Strength can be used to open doors or intimidate people, intelligence gives you more options in hacking, technical ability will allow you to deactivate cameras or pick locks. The visuals are absolutely stunning in this game, even in lower settings, the city looks amazing and feels amazing. The wonky AI can detract from the immersion as I previously said but judging the game solely on how it looks, it really feels triple A. The art design is right on the mark with a blend of eastern and western themes put on top of a city that really feels like a dystopian mega-city. The world-building feels truly handcrafted as little details are scattered throughout from the edges of the wastelands to the bustle of the inner city skyscrapers. The voice acting is also great throughout with main characters being well handled if not a little cliche in places, but I think it's fitting and just furthers the setting that they are in. The story feels compelling and seeing characters react to your plight, with the excellent voice acting, really cements the experience for me.Side missions feature interesting characters, that feel easy to connect with and have interesting missions and stories. The gigs and scanner missions are more repetitive without as much narrative but as long as you don't leave them all to the very end like I did you won't mind them too much. The game has multiple endings, some of which can be influenced by your actions during the main game and whilst they are mostly somewhat depressing, they do tie off loose ends and feel weighty to the story.This game suffered from people expecting the greatest video game of all time. It tries to do too much of everything and it suffers for it with everything being on a scale from just fine to excellent. What it does well, it does really well, what it doesn't do so well, requires further polish and additional content which CDPR do seem to want to work on and fix. All in all Cyberpunk is still a good game, the hype for this game was far too big for it's own good and between the devs over-promising and the higher ups forcing the game out before it's ready, it never stood a chance in the public eye. That doesn't absolve it of it's shortcomings but it does explain them.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRPros:Decent combat, good main story, good side stories, good visuals, good soundtrack, story replayabilityCons:Still buggy as hell, barely any customization post character creation, dumb AI, lifeless city, almost impossible to get immersed, obviously unfinished, not anything near what was promisedThis game... where do I begin. I wish there was a mixed review option. It had it highlights for sure but it is just so obviously not finished. Even 8 months later there are still glaring technical issues, The game *looks* fantastic and I wasn't even playing on the highest settings. But aside from looks Night City is basically lifeless. The pedestrian AI is straight up idiotic. The driving AI is somehow even worse. I didn't experience a police chase one time in the 91 hours I played. You'll see identical NPCs walking in packs down the street like attack of the clones. Traffic will come to a standstill for literally no reason. The minimap doesn't expand enough while driving for you to have enough time to react to the GPS. Driving feels extremely clunky in the city, the physics of car crashes are laughably bad. Sometimes cars clip into the barriers on the roadside and go flying.There is almost no interaction with the city itself. Want to go to the bar? I mean you can, sorta. If by go to the bar you mean open a menu, buy a drink, open another menu to get to your backpack, select the item, and then get a woozy screen for 30 seconds. NPCs don't actually do anything, they just stand around. There's 2 cops at the entrance to V's building that have the exact same conversation literally every time you walk past them. The city just feels so lifeless. The streets are practically empty most of the time and then randomly they will be crowded and a lot of the time you can see the vehicles spawn in right in front of you. Supposedly the city has 6 million people living in it but it looks like a ghost town more often than not. The game is so poorly optimized even months after release, their code base has to be a gigantic mess slopped on top of itself and held together with prayers alone. Want to customize your character after character creation? You can't aside from clothes. I played female V, the most you could do was use some head items that changed hairstyle. Even the clothes, 95% of the things you see the NPCs wearing you can't wear. See a cool looking NPC with fully gold skin? Can't get that. Want a cool cybernetic limb that tons of NPCs have? Can't get that. Want to get a haircut? Can't get that. New tattoos? Nope. You can't see what clothes look like on you before you buy them either. So if you want to test stuff out you should save before buying anything so you can test stuff out. Not like it really matters anyway since there is exactly one cutscene (in my experience) where you can fully see your character and its at the very end of the game and you're wearing a generic outfit (in the ending I got anyway, not sure about the others.). Can't customize cars, can't change appearance after CC, can't even keep a car you steal off the street, can't see clothes before you buy them. You could do all of this stuff in the original Saints Row and that came out in 2006. The lack of appearance customization is the most egregious to me. It's a CYBERPUNK game, the defining characteristic of the genre is transhumanism, being able to modify your body at will, blurring the lines between genders, between technology and humanity, etc. And you can't even get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ haircut. You don't even get to see your cyberware installed outside of one instance at the beginning of the game. I saw that for the first time and thought that was so cool, couldn't wait to see what it was going to be like when I got mantis blades put in my arms. Nope. It's just a menu, you buy it and its there, no animation or anything. It's just so glaringly obvious that this game is not finished in so many different areas.The combat, when it worked properly, was pretty fun. However the game is pretty clearly designed with a controller in mind. I played on both KBM and an xbox controller and found the controller much easier. It also definitely leans towards guns more than melee in my experience. The melee feels clunky, that said I did enjoy slicing people up with a katana or mantis blades or beating someones face in with gorilla arms. The gunplay isn't really anything to write home about, it's there, it's pretty generic. The novelty of mantis blades and such wore off after a bit. While the combat overall was fun it's not really outstanding. But it also isn't bad so that's good.Onto the story, there will be a minor spoiler in this but I'm going to try my best to omit any names.I actually quite enjoyed the main story of the game. A lot of the side missions were really cool too. I am a big reader so I didn't mind going through all the shards I picked up or reading the codex entries and such. The story does start out slow in my opinion, and the game expects you to care about certain characters early in the game without much reason and because of that certain story moments aren't nearly as impactful as they should be. Maybe that's a result of the lifepath I took (I chose Corpo) It gets better later on though. Again this is my opinion so your mileage may vary but I think decent chunks of Johnny's story/character are pretty edgelord cringe, but others are really good. I will say that I don't think Keanu Reeves is a good voice actor and that may have influenced my opinion of the character. I don't want to spoil so I won't get into specifics but overall I felt the story was good, some parts were ehh but for the most part I was pretty invested, especially towards the end. The later conversations between Johnny and V are really well done. The story carries this game.I started playing this game right after finishing Red Dead Redemption 2, so going from one of the best RPGs if not one of the best video games in general of all time to this... well. Again it's very obvious this game is not finished. I cannot in good conscience recommend you buy this game at full price. I bought it during the summer sale and still feel I paid too much. Don't pay full price for an unfinished game. I really hope that further patches and DLC fix the game. But it is just not what was promised, this was supposed to be the game of the decade. A genre defining art piece that we'd all be talking about for years to come. Well we will be just not in the way they'd hoped.All of that being said in my 91 hours I did have a good time and I will be playing it again at some point to get different endings.

Every single thing to do is "go here, kill them" or "go there, kill them".It feels like a single player version of The Division. _childDocuments_.review: After one year following its release, I feel I can finally review this troubled yet addictive game. It should've been amazing, but it ended up being just alright. As an RPG, it doesn't deliver as everyone hoped. You can still be immersed in the game, but eventually, you'll run into something that reminds you that you're not really in control of who you are. V is a really cool character, but other than subtle things like the look of their genitals (which is funny considering it affects absolutely nothing), V isn't a character that you can truly call your own. I haven't played as female V nor any other class besides streetkid, but it seems like once you choose a class, that's where your ability to really customize your character ends. There are many things I do like about Cyberpunk 2077, which is why I gave it a positive review. Night City itself is gorgeous. Driving around and looking at all the details and colors is really breathtaking (you know). However, besides that, it's dead. The NPCs act dumb, they say the same things, and they'll sometimes replicate to the point where I'll turn a corner and see 10 exact same NPCs just walking together. To distract myself from how immersive-breaking this is, I'll joke around and say it's just a glitch in the matrix (pun intended). Now, for the man of the hour: Johnny Silverhand. In my opinion, his character and the relationship he has with V is the strongest part of the game. His remarks during missions makes for a fun time, and he always helped feed that immersive desire that I so desperately wanted. Other characters, such as Panam, Judy, and River, help the game feel more immersive, but it falls flat once you're done with their missions. It's like they ghost V after a while. In the end, V really only has their cyberware, cars, and apartment. The cyberware gameplay is pretty fun, and getting upgrades is exciting. As for cars, there are 26 cars you can purchase, but there's not really a reason to buy cars when you can just hijack them for free (although you can't keep them). On top of that, you can't store your owned cars in a nice garage or anything. It's very disappointing that you cannot change a single thing about V's apartment or even buy a different one. Ultimately, the narrative is driven by forced events that detract from the RPG element we all hoped for. V has a story to tell, but you'll find that your choices don't affect it as much as they should. If you forget about the letdown regarding the RPG element, I think Cyberpunk 2077 is a solid game. The story is fascinating, the dialogue is entertaining, and the characters are interesting. CDPR included a bunch of lore within this game, and exploring that lore is worth it. It's just sad to think how much better it could've been; it feels like we got a small piece of the final product. However, by now I think most people have come to accept this game for what it is. Now that it goes on sale for $30, I'd recommend picking it up and giving it a try. If you can get past the failed ambitions, I believe there's plenty of enjoyment to be found.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most artistically ambitious projects ever made, Cyberpunk looks & sounds awesome. The sheer level of detail the artists have poured into this is mindblowing, From a visual standpoint alone, it is a masterpiece.It is a shame then that the scope of the game just isn't what CDPR advertised at us for all these years. This is not a deep RPG. I was expecting a narrative I could get lost in, where my choices would seriously effect the path of play. In actuality it is more of an FPS with RPG mechanics tied to the levelling. Whilst it does have a huge variety of quests with a decent amount of story, it all seemed skin deep, and it didn't appear that my unique actions bore many consequences.Also well documented are the many areas in which this game attempts to be GTA but just feels half baked. I've played for almost 100 hours and the police have never once seriously threatened me. This is an element of the game which could make the central loop so much more entertaining if it posed some sort of threat. As it stands the AI can be fairly laughable and utterly none-threatening.So do I recommend this? Like I said at the top, if you just want to cruise around an incredibly pretty artistic wonderland, then you can't really do better than this. The visuals are incredible. Regarding everything else, set your expectations a few steps lower than what the pre-release hype would have you believe. I'm excited that they are going to continue working on the game and to see where it eventually goes. With a bit more work this could be the game we want it to be. Perhaps hold off until they do a no man's sky and turn this ship around.

_childDocuments_.review: This review isn't aimed at the boots on the ground devs who undoubtedly worked so, so hard to make this game. It's aimed at the 'corpos' who pushed for it to be released in its current unfinished state, and pressured workers to break their backs to meet an impossible deadline. It's also subtly aimed at those who kicked up such a fuss because a game they wanted to play was pushed back a little bit. This is what happens when games get rushed and over-hyped by greedy corpos. A broken, half-baked game that had so much potential.Disclaimer: I haven't yet completed the game, so may change my review once completed. UPDATE: completed it, still don't recommend. There are multiple endings, all of which are vaguely disappointing. Pros: the story is somewhat intriguing, thus far, and the cyberpunk aesthetic/design is wonderful. My sole reason for playing the game is the story.Cons: despite my rig being able to run it on the highest settings, there are frequent crashes to desktop, and the Steam overlay simply doesn't work for me. That being said, having a decent computer means I'm not experiencing more serious errors that others seem to.At least one quest is broken; Lt. Mower in the Cyberpsycho quest glitched through the floor, making the quest impossible to finish. I'm really disappointed as this was one of the very few interesting side quests.The AI isn't what I'd expect from a game released in 2020. Traffic and police AI are virtually non-existent, and   fighting enemies isn't really that much fun. The police are so easy to run from that there's little point in them being in the game.Side quests generally involve travelling from A to B, either stealing something quietly, or taking out some bad guys, or escorting someone to a car. The city itself is beautiful, but it's very shallow. There's not really much to do or explore in any real detail. The vast majority of buildings and landmarks can't be interacted with in any meaningful way.You can buy lots of cars, but there's no customisation, and you can't customise your character again once the game starts. I was disappointed by this, being used to games like Saints Row which has some excellent cars and customisation options. Honestly? It's not worth the price. I'd highly recommend Saints Row or Deus Ex. Saints Row allows you to roam a large city, customise your character and cars, and there's simply more fun stuff to do. Deus Ex has an excellent (and superior, IMO) storyline and more interesting perks and gameplay. And neither of them are broken.CDPR knew exactly what they were doing when they released the game in its current state. Their watery apology simply reflects that of other recent releases in the gaming world which turned out to be broken, buggy messes that aren't really all that fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here it is. Years in the making. From being intrigued in 2013, to being beyond excited in recent years. It's finally released. The only game I've been looking forward to for years is finally on my computer, and I'm playing it! So happy to be able to do this. I've officially finished my first playthrough of Cyberpunk 2077. Minutes ago I reached an ending. I thought it was a great conclusion, I enjoyed how it was executed, enjoyed the manner in which I got there, and who was along for my finale. I'm not too often reviewing the games I play, however I felt I should review this one.  As a huge The Witcher 3 fan, I expected something close in quality to that, but it was far from that. There are numerous reasons for this, but it had to be said from the get go.  If you're curious, my starting points was a Male Streetkid. Figured it'd be as middle of an experience I could get. Now, let's start. with the   So well done. CDPR did an excellent job in the past, and I don't feel like they missed a step at all. I've seen some criticisms of a few things, some of which I'll gladly address, but overall I feel the main quest, and fair amount of side quests I went through were super well done. The problem with the story that I do have will be addressed below. They're fantastic, super well crafted.I've got a whole list of characters I loved, and characters I hated (in a good way). I absolutely LOVED Johnny Silverhand. Found him to be a great part of the story with V.  Keanu did good, in my opinion. Felt like his motives and impact were strong. Out of all the main characters you can come across, I can't name one I particularly thought was done poorly. I've not seen the starters for the other lifepaths, but in mine I felt pretty good about it all. Side characters were great too of course, just easier to notice the main. ♥♥♥♥♥♥' love Jackie as well. Stunning game, absolutely incredibly beautiful. I borrowed a friends 2060 Super, paired it alongside my R7 3800x at 1440p and was just loving it. Only wish I could've played with 'Ray Tracing'. Hopefully that 3070 comes in soon! Night City is one of the most visually appealing worlds I've seen in games. Genuinely an incredible sight. This isn't the only refer to the graphical fidelity of some pretty buildings. Cars look incredible, guns exquisite, characters (main at least, many of the side as well) are just so well done. The colours, the design overall, so good.  Incredible selections, fantastic. Insanely good soundtrack on it's own, and an incredible radio selection. So many great tracks throughout your time. Fair selection of genres too. Jamming out while walking around or something would be a great means of just chilling. Pairing that with exploring around is so good. If only it weren't for the driving, I'd say you should just drive around blasting tunes. We'll speak more on that shortly. Excellent for customization.So many options to enjoy it your way! I often go down to just shoot things all the time in games like this, but I really enjoyed many other options. Stealthing felt nice, cyberwear options added really nice alternatives to typical things. Really good systems in place. Can't imagine what it'd be like if I was triple the level and could go at everything immediately. On to the bad now though. Strap in.Okay. This has to be one of the worst launches of a AAA game I've ever been through. I can't ignore so many problems. On a technical side, good god the recommended specs did not do this justice. To get proper FPS in this, there's no way you should be following the recommended. This thing can CHUG. That's  just for us on PC, those poor bastards on console. Cannot believe CDPR would even sell people that. Shockingly horrid. It isn't just the performance though, the bugs, oh god the bugs. People disappearing, cars flying away, AI breaking and resulting in soft locks during quests, general crashes for many, falling through the world, weapons/items despawning or not loading at all, audio overlaps. The list can go on and on. Hopefully all of the above woes can be resolved in some way down the line, but those problems alone should've resulted in so, so much more time on this game. For gameplay stuff, there's some notables. The driving is just awful. It's just bad. There's no excusing it. Who cares how pretty a vehicle is when driving around in it is terrible. Numerous Motorcycles, Sports Cars, Vans/Trucks. They're all bad. Floaty, slippery. Just awful. Combat is questionable. The guns don't feel great, the melee doesn't feel great. They're serviceable, but not perfect. Here's the killer in this one though, AI. I've never played a game with a worse "Wanted" mechanic. Cops popping up behind me because they couldn't design a car chase? What in the world lol. It's laughable. Not just their AI though. Enemy and NPC AI is just off. You can walk past enemies sometimes, and other times you're spotted out of nowhere. It seems random, but I imagine it's down more to poor build. Typical NPC AI stings though. All that marketing material about how "alive" Night City will feel, not true. It's not there at all, there's glimpses, but it's off.Now for the final problem section. This game was SO RUSHED. It hurts so much thinking about stuff that was axed. The entire first part of the game, before you ever meet Johnny, it should've and was likely meant to be, so much longer. You're hit with a montage instead of playing through what seemed like a fantastic part of the story. I can't believe they'd go about it this way. I don't think this is all that was cut up though, I believe braindances were meant to be so much more influential and involved in the story. Seeing them around the world acquirable as , rather than  kind of seals it to me. Text even shows that leads you to believe you're meant to at some point interact with them. You don't though. With that, I'm betting the value of the "life path" stuff went out the same window. Your path doesn't matter. It just doesn't. There's bits and pieces, however it's null really. This was so rushed, not to mention overpromised. I noted a little of that with the small marketing bit above. A closing point in the con section. I pray that with Red Dead Redemption 2, and as with Cyberpunk 2077, we start seeing a drop in the crunch culture. Hearing about this in the mainstream is sickening and depressing. I pray that we start seeing change. With my pros and cons out, I'd like to close with how I came to a "Yes". I really enjoyed this game, but I know it could've been more. CDPR put together a really great story. I'm sure you can come out of Cyberpunk 2077 with good takes. I truly hope it'll some day become a perfect game. I feel we're years off though. I'm excited to play through again sometime soon, and try for other options along the way. I loved Night City, I can't wait to take it in again.I'm guilty of wanting this out faster, hell I wanted it far sooner than we have it. That said, I never wished crunch upon any of those poor developers. On top of that, I also don't wish for crunch to be the means of resolving the problems here. Here's to hoping we can see the perfect Cyberpunk 2077 some day. Not sure when that'll be, but what we have now is still really good.
