_childDocuments_.review: This game just barely missed the mark of being one I can recommend. On one hand, you have 40-50 hours of decent content to mull through. The city is beautiful, the main story is intriguing and the early game is an enjoyable experience. It has some of the most stunning looking set piece visuals you'll see in the past decade. It's an impressive visual experience.On the other hand, a lot of the content is unpolished and repetitive without much unique or re-playable value. The city is limp with placeholder dummy pedestrian AI, the wanted system is atrocious and they have a loot system that follows the same formula of many other games (common, rare, legendary, etc). It makes me appreciate games with half the graphics and double the depth. You'll find most systems implemented in Cyberpunk 2077 have been done better by other developers. I purposely didn't read much pre-release info about this game so as not to overhype expectations, and it still let me down. Some of the biggest issues I had: -Looting quickly becomes a chore to find a higher level of weapon, and they completely botched this part along with the crafting system. They chose the wrong loot system for this game entirely with the same old colors used in Destiny and Fortnite. Even the weapon mods are mostly uninteresting. -Choosing a play style barely makes a difference in story or combat. I was a stealth hackerman with silenced weapons playing on hard mode. There was one section that got frustrating, so I tried blasting everything with a shotgun. Despite having no perks or experience invested in shotguns, it proved the easiest way to complete most levels in the end. On hard mode you will die after taking a few shots, but somehow you will not be hit as easily when charging into battle. Despite having high points in hacking, the turrets would just glitch out and deactivate when attempting to turn them on my enemies.-Your background choice (Corpo, Night Kid or Nomad) makes very little difference outside of the intro and a few speech options. The night city montage early on gives you a taste of what they wanted to do with this game, but could not achieve.-You are more so playing a character in an on-rails type story than role playing someone of your choosing where decisions matter. The relationships you build through side quests wind up mattering more than anything, and even most of those feel forced. There's also a chance some side quest for a faction can glitch out and they wind up hating you because of it. -The wanted system is a complete immersion breaker and should never have been placed in the game with its current state. Police spawn in like agents in the matrix whenever you do something 'against the rules.' There is nothing at all interesting about these fights, and there are no real engagements to be had with the famed Trauma Team either.There was so much potential to be had with this game, and its clear that business decisions triumphed over the will of developers once again. I had read some about how CDPR wasn't one of those companies that would pull an EA and release an underwhelming title, but this is further proof that no company is exempt from greed. Hopefully modders come in to save the day with content that is both deep and engaging. The irony is not lost on me here, where a game that highlights the soul sucking malicious deeds of corporations has its soul sucked away by the board members commanding its creation."Function comes 2nd. Looks are what matter." Here's hoping CDPR changes that slogan next go.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame how such a relatively enjoyable video game is plagued by so many petty and game-breaking bugs/ glitches. I've only clocked 30 hours in and I've had character shadows not work properly, side quest NPCs freeze during scripted events, the ability to draw my guns in free roam revoked until I triggered a cutscene, along with a multitude of other minor annoyances. Some of these bugs were easily "fixed" by restarting the game while others seem to stay on your save file, forcing you to reload to a previous checkpoint. _childDocuments_.review: Played around 25 hours so far, and it feels like I've just barely scratched the surface of what the game has to offer. It could certainly be more optimized, but the game has been consistently smooth for me, with no FPS drops or lag. As far as bugs go I've also not seen any game-breaking ones, visual and/or audio bugs mostly, but this is stuff that can be fixed in future updates.As for the game itself, I love it. Many people probably expected the Second Coming of Jesus Christ to be this game, and that made them feel disappointed - but I don't feel like my expectations were betrayed at all. The story is great, I love the characters, the soundtrack is epic, and the game looks great even on lower graphics options. And the atmosphere and setting are absolutely phenomenal - I've been having issues in focusing on quests since I just feel like walking around and exploring Night City.I love it, and I look forward to many more hours in it - and to any DLC's and content that CDPR will make for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Favorite game ever! I wandered Night City for three nights in a row, only doing gigs and side quests, and there is so much to explore. Night City is huge! I've run into very few bugs (none of them game-breaking and usually funny like running over the man floating over the road on an invisible chair). It's like being in a real, living cyberpunk world. The story, characters, and voice-acting are all fantastic. I love that you have so many options on how to play. In this play-through, I am a Nomad excelling at Tech & Intelligence. Tonight, I finally did some more of the main questline and it is incredible. Now I'm going to explore Night City some more because I want to savor every second. 2077/10.Update: Over 200 hours in. I've finished my first playthrough and immediately started a 2nd as a Corpo. I loved my first build but might try my hand at a Ninja Assassin build this time.

But it's also very scummy move to change CyberPunk 2077 from an RPG to Action Adventure....)How i rate games0 - Literally unplayable | 1 - Barely playable | 2 - Horribly bad game | 3 - Really bad | 4 - Bad | 5 - Average | 6 - Above Average | 7 - Good | 8 - Great | 9 - Amazing | 10 - GodlikeThings i would want/change: More character development needed[Characters with good character development] (Dependent on your choices)- Johnny Silverhand (Can have good character development if you do the side missions, gigs, or go to specific locations throughout night city)- Panam (Has a well fleshed out story with V, except if you choose the ending missions with her tribe it can get a little strange if you think of their decisions in a logical perspective)- Judy (Good character development with V)- River Ward (Good character development)- Jackie (Sort of since our character development was through a timelapse of 6 months with him +5 missions)[Characters that needed more character development]- Rogue (Only got a few scenes with her through mostly flash backs, and 2 side missions with johnny)- Vik (Don't know why Vik likes V since we have no clue about our back story with each other is)- Misty (Jackie's GF and she has her character development while talking about jackie, but besides that 1 scene there isn't anything else)- Mama Welles (Best friends with jackie but barely knows her even though she treats V like family)- Evelyn Parker (Barely know much about her other than a few info tossed about her from time to time)- Saul (Would've been interesting learning about them considering how important family is to the tribe)-Mitch/Scorpio (Would've been interesting learning about them considering how important family is to the tribe)- T-Bug (Barely in V's story apart from 4 or 5 scenes)- Peralez Family (Could've gone on a bit longer since they're important figures in night city)- All the Fixers (Literally none of them have any character development unless you look through and read about them on the Shards you pick up)Needs more RPG aspects to the game even though CDPR changed the game from a RPG to an Action Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam had an option to leave a mixed review, that would be my recommendation. While I think my opinion of this game (at least in its current state) will remain the same when I finish the main quest, it's worth mentioning that I'm not done with it yet, and therefore this won't probably be my final review.The thing is: I like this game. I love the atmosphere, the soundtrack and its general themes; heck, I even like the gunplay and the driving. But this clearly isn't the game we were waiting for. I've seen games in Early Access less buggy and unfinished than this AAA title is right now.The sheer amount of content that was clearly cut from the release version is shocking. The AI is lacking, almost non-existent; the world is beautiful, but not at all dynamic; your actions don't have ANY consequences apart from a few scripted choices; the multiple gangs throughout the city are sadly irrelevant; your cyberwares have little effect to your gameplay apart from a few expensive ones; the roleplaying mechanics (which I thought would be at least impactful, due to the source material of this game) are less refined and interesting than the ones from multiple "light RPGs" that came out over the past two or three years.I sincerely hope they patch the plentiful bugs out there and maybe add back some of the cut content, because you can clearly see the love and dedication put into this game by its devs and designers, but right now Cyberpunk 2077 is simply disappointing. It's just a shell of what it could've been, even if the quests and characters are solid and well-written.TL;DR: For now, I would not recommend this game. It has great moments, a good story and interesting characters, but the bugs and its overall unpolished state kinda breaks the immersion and turns what could be a great experience into a chore. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: It’s no secret that CP2077 is buggy. But while people like to mention that it is better now, "better" still means a range of things, from visual glitches, save corruption, loss of control over aspects of your character, NPC animation errors, quests not properly triggering or updating—and the list goes on and on. This is far and beyond the game's weakest point, and for CDPR to feel confident enough to announce a DLC while their game is in this state is frankly a little bit gross.CP2077 looks fantastic. Even in lower settings, detail oozes from every corner of Night City. This does come at the cost of many buildings being inaccessible, which can occasionally make the overworld feel a little plastic, especially early on when players may just want to roam around and explore. Likewise, models are varied in both characters, weapons, and vehicles, which makes collecting them a joy. Clothing and gear can be a little lackluster, in my opinion, but that is an issue that feels overly nitpicky.The sound is likewise quite good. CP2077 features its own unique radio songs that can be a little hit or miss, but I found them to be quite immersive. Voice acting is also fairly high quality, with some exceptions in V occasionally delivering lines within the same dialogue with distinctly different intonation, which can be a bit jarring, and Johnny’s voice acting being incredibly deadpan. Neither of which, however, is a dealbreaker for how well the game presents itself.Cyberpunk itself is a tabletop setting, and it’s a more formulaic one. Megacorps control most of society. There’s a huge divide between the poor and the wealthy, and that gap is being thoroughly filled with guns and pornography. That’s the most basic rundown of just about every Cyberpunk setting, and it fits like a glove here as well. Worth mentioning is that there is a bit of an inconsistency in tone, as Cyberpunk 2077 flip-flops quite a lot between thoroughly gritty writing, tackling themes of death, abuse, depression, and more—but doesn’t quite manage to marry these with either the more humorous aspects of its world or the power fantasy running underneath it all.For example, you may experience tonal whiplash as extreme as a quest handling severe sexual abuse leading to a suicidal subplot only to stumble across a YouTuber cameo about a character having had his Cox get stuck in a sextoy. Granted, these instances are rare enough to not matter too much, but the ludicrous power level of V versus the rest of the world is much more bothersome. As V, regardless of the Lifepath or Origin story you choose, you are a Mercenary. Edgerunner, or whatever you want to call it: A gun for hire. Through circumstances, you get your hands on a chip that infects your body with Keanu Reeves, which will eventually end up killing you. From that point on, Johnny Silverhand, the character played by him, takes on the role of a deuteragonist, and this is where CP2077 shines most.The dynamic between your character and Johnny is fantastic and plays a lot with player expectations, making you question your own decision-making throughout the story and the nature of someone else being stuck within your mind. However, while most of the main story is good like this, it begins to crumble towards the aforementioned atrocious ending, and even before that, it struggles to make V’s journey coherent in the context of the world around them.Apart from the main story, side stories feel largely well written and have some staying power because they tend to be interlinked with one another. For example, a client might call you for their entirely unique quest, and then you come back to someone whose quest you finished before, only for them to mention that they suggested you to your client. Romances will consistently message you tens of hours after you've already finished their arc, and it all serves well by making characters feel like a persistent presence in V’s development.Gigs are less strong, usually being fairly straightforward quests whose entire story is hidden behind pages of optional log entries that, while rewarding, can be very hard to care for given their repetitiveness and lack of presentation.Gameplay is a little bit of a rough spot for CP2077. In general, it suffers from some questionable balance decisions that you can largely pin down to distinctly overpowered parts of the different skill trees; for example, Quickhacking is laughably broken throughout the game given that you have abilities that bypass any sort of damage and just outright kill enemies for almost no cost whatsoever.  However, these abilities are few and far between, so I felt that the game was still decently challenging on Very Hard and rewarded experimenting around a bit.However, enemy AI and poor vehicle handling can’t just be fixed like that, and both drag the minute-to-minute experience down a ton. Police are an utterly redundant mechanic, and leveling is far too slow for players to reasonably hit the capstone abilities before they’re finished with the game. By the time I went into the final quest at just under 60 hours played, the only content I had left to complete were random fights across the map (NCPD events), and I had yet to hit a single skill capstone.Gunplay and melee combat are quite the same, and even the more out-there setting-specific elements, such as the arm implants like the Mantis Blade or Monowire, play disappointingly straightforward. This is all to say: Gameplay is serviceable. It’s all just 'okay', but overall weaker than its genre competitors.Fallout 4+2073 falls short in just about every metric but its presentation. The main story is fantastic until the lackluster ending mission ruins the incredible build-up; side stories are few and far between and suffer tremendously from the peripheral gameplay elements. Ultimately, the game feels unfinished and a victim of its brutal development cycle.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, and completed all achievements at around 85 hours. I'll keep this mostly spoiler-free, no worries there. Might mention how I vaguely feel about certain moments, but I won't mention what happens in those moments. This review is regarding the current state of the game, though it's expected to receive more and more patches to improve performance, handling, gameplay, AI, all that. Couple of prefaces, as you might expect to get. I had a fairly decent machine, played on Hard, and came in expecting to have a good time. I'll leave as much bias at the door as I can.The three games I had in mind that combined into this was Dying light, then GTA, then Witcher 3.Looting of Dying light / borderlands, open world feel of GTA storyline, and a couple of the main story and big sidequests felt almost as good as Witcher 3, but not quite there. 8/10I played as a Netrunner. Most often how I got through each combat was through hacking. It was fairly satisfying to be able to hack people through walls with spreading plagues and whatnot, but from what I played using melee and guns they feel pretty good. It felt good, but it could feel better. Most of the problems you'd find here is that the AI was not very smart and not made as well as it could be, and even at hard it was simple at times. 9/10Game does pretty good here. General sound design is well done. Impacts from melee are satisfying, hacking dudes had good satisfying noises depending on what you were doing to your opponents, gunshots felt good, and the music was really, really great. Would have gotten a better score here with a couple of the bugs being fixed, noises being swapped and replaced. One instance sticks out of a fire hydrant being ran over, and making the noise of bursting water like a geyser hours later after returning and the hydrant had been repaired but the sound remained. 9/10Lotta cool characters here. I don't really have anything bad to say. Main story and sidequest characters were all very well made with their own unique personalities. Including townspeople and other npcs though, they can be lackluster at times. Police get mad at you if you walk in a few feet of them, those sorts of things. Other than that though, I really liked the different endings and lots of the main and side characters, interacting with them was pretty enjoyable. 8/10You gotta have a really good setup to make this game look good. Not well optimized. Does look good though when you have that setup, really does, I thought the game looked great. The faces were well made, the vehicles and major buildings and environment looked good, the lip sync was decent as they talked. Still, with that setup certain things in the environment were given terrible attention, such as food items.  5/10This is the worst drawback of the game. Lots of the other main topics and stuff did alright, but full honesty here there was not a great job done here. Whether it was rushed because of shareholders or executives or fans or whatever, regardless, there's a number of bugs. Throughout my playthrough, I had to restart my game 3 times, and crashed once, so it wasn't too bad in that regard. But I'd probably reloaded saves a total of 30 times because an npc didn't do something right. I'm not too bothered by bugs, so I still had a great time, but I could understand how this would bother some people.This game is pretty enjoyable as is, but it could have been and it will be better in the future as updates repeatedly come out. If you're wanting to wait for it to improve, it will and that's not a bad idea. Witcher 3 DLC was a fantastic part of an already good game, and they did good work improving that game over time.I'd give this game an overall 8/10. Good baseline, enjoyable, but needs improvement, I think it can easily reach 10/10 after enough time.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like i'm going a bit crazy reading all of these positive and negative reviews so i'm going to leave my own small one.Everyone seems to be only interested in how this game runs on their hardware or how they experienced a bug or about the graphics but not many people are talking about playing the actual game which is a little confusing because i almost feel like i'm on the Nvidia RTX reviews more than i am reading a game review.The combat is a rehashed and reused typical bullet sponge shooter and the mechanics feel extremely dated for this day and age, the enemies move as if i'm playing on an online server with 150 ms and when you do land some shots it can take upwards of 7 shots to the head.The story is all over the place with no real direction and i felt like i had no reason to care about the characters that in most cases weren't even introduced to me and it seems like there is an extremely large portion of "V"s introduction glossed over in the form of a multi scene cut scene skipping from one thing to another that seemed like it should've been a playable part of the game to add some much needed context to the underlying plot.Dialogue was extremely one dimensional without even giving the illusion of choice with more often than not only one dialogue option to say. In moments where you're given  a second option is usually has nothing to do with the trajectory of the conversation so there's no point even selecting the option.Missions or gigs (whatever you want to call them) are given in the form of drive to this area because there's a potential mission here, Given by who and for what purpose and how you would even know of it's existence is somewhat of a mystery, My in game cellphone is constantly ringing with random characters giving me things to do with out any introduction to who this person is. How did you even get my damn phone number?!?!The obligatory genitalia post but am i really able to choose the length of my penis but not how tall i am or even a body type?It seems like it's encouraged to go and explore the world but there's so much non contextual random stuff happening that it's more like a sensory overload with npc's randomly shooting at you as you drive by and nonsense happening all over the place.I feel like a few people would notice my time played and to those people i would say with an expected main story length of about 20 hours (supposedly) do you really think it's acceptable for a player to be almost 5 hours into the main story alone and to still feel like i'm still waiting for the fun to begin or waiting for any real tangible form of context to anything that's going on around me?I'm reading a lot of reviews now and i'm confused because everyone is saying this is a very immersive and fresh game with excellent mechanics and a rich story and i'm wondering have i been playing the same game as everyone else because to me it feels like i'm playing an alpha of Deus Ex - Mankind Divided that is functioning more like a tech demo than a game with a purpose and direction.Overall i would say that this game is an average experience with very run of the mill point and shoot combat mechanics that has the player set down a linear story path even though it feels like you have choices. Characters with no context and a plot that seems like it's fallen short in the delivery of both meaning and immersion.A good game can thrive with an immersive rich story or enthralling and engaging game play,that being said it doesn't need to have both of them but it definitely needs to have at least one...This game feels like eating a meal that is unseasoned, it does the job but it's extremely bland.4/10Buy this game on sale if you want to play the latest instalment of Deus Ex - Over hyped and Disappointing--------After more play time the only thing i would like to add is i stand by this review and if anything i should've been way more scathing then i have been. This game is a polished turd, it looks good but it's just ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: I received Cyberpunk about a month after its release from a mate (though i was going to buy it none the less), the controversy never really swayed me, I knew I would need a decent PC to run it. I truly believe this game is as amazing as it could've been even with all the rush for the Devs, I'm writing this review in a few months of retrospect. I have never been made more emotional by a game and its story and ending than Cyberpunk. The story has an excellent build up and even better crescendo. the writing and world have their ups and downs but i think this game is going to be looked back upon as a classic. the soundtrack is beautiful, all of SAMURAI's music is now in my favourites playlist, i get teary eyed whenever 'never fade away' comes on, even the mish mash of radio sounds like RTJ, Carpenter Brut and Kavinsky.I find it hard to put a games value into a number due to the complexity in them, but in saying that i think this game is a solid 9.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: After a turbulent launch, Cyberpunk 2077 has undergone a stunning transformation, and with the release of the Phantom Liberty DLC, it’s finally achieved the promise that was once so tantalizingly close.Gameplay and Story:Cyberpunk 2077's core gameplay is a masterclass in open-world design. Night City, once a chaotic mess, now brims with life and detail, thanks to numerous updates that have polished the experience to a gleaming sheen. The story, which once felt fragmented, has matured into a compelling narrative that grips from start to finish. V's journey through the neon-lit streets of this dystopian metropolis is more immersive than ever, with every choice feeling impactful and meaningful.The Phantom Liberty DLC adds an exhilarating new chapter to the tale, introducing intriguing new characters and a gripping storyline that expands the universe while staying true to the core experience. Idris Elba’s character, in particular, brings a fresh and engaging dynamic to the narrative, making the expansion a must-play.Graphics and Performance:Visually, Cyberpunk 2077 now stands as a testament to what the game was always meant to be. The graphics are breathtaking, with improved textures and lighting effects that showcase the city's vibrant neon glow and gritty underbelly. Performance has seen a substantial boost, with smoother frame rates and fewer bugs. The world is rich in detail, from the bustling streets to the quiet corners of the city, making exploration a genuine pleasure.Gameplay Mechanics:The gameplay mechanics have been refined, offering a more fluid and engaging experience. Combat feels more responsive and balanced, and the RPG elements are deeply integrated into the gameplay, providing meaningful choices and consequences. The skill tree and character customization options have been expanded, allowing for a more personalized approach to how V interacts with the world.Quests and Activities:The side quests, once criticized for their repetitiveness, now offer a variety of engaging stories and activities. The new content from Phantom Liberty integrates seamlessly with the base game, providing additional depth and context to the world. From high-stakes heists to intimate character moments, there’s always something compelling to dive into.Final Thoughts:Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way since its rocky launch. With the extensive improvements and the addition of the Phantom Liberty DLC, it’s clear that CD Projekt Red has delivered on their original vision. The game now offers an experience that is rich, immersive, and truly worthy of the Cyberpunk legacy. For those who have yet to experience Night City, now is the perfect time to dive in. For those who have been waiting for the game to live up to its promise, the wait has been more than worth it.Cyberpunk 2077 is not just a redemption story; it’s a triumph.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077, arguably the most hyped game of the entire year of 2020 made by a beloved company, CD Projekt Red. After putting many hours into the game, 100% the game on Very Hard, and achieving all 5 endings, I feel more than ready with my opinion on the game, and ready to state all the issues at least myself as a player went through, or as I have witnessed via other players that I know in real life and on the internet, but for the sake of the review, I will try to stay at only my own personal experiences. !![QUICK SUMMARY IF YOU DON'T WANT TO READ THAT MUCH]!!- Yes, I do believe the game is worth the $60 and still even in it's current state, worth playing. However, there are a LOT of issues that I will be stating here so that you can decide if it's for you or not afterwards.!![GAMEPLAY & GUNPLAY]!!- The combat play and movement mechanics in Cyberpunk 2077 are pretty clean and satisfying, however, the game is way too easy to manipulate. After the first 3 hours of in-game playtime, using my own builds was able to create a 1 shot revolver that would literally 1 shot anything, bosses included with just a body shot a lot of the time. Headshots were 20K+ damage, which is ridiculous. Then trying to make the game fun again and use a Katana with a point reset, I was able to create a Katana that 1 shot basically anything yet again. Even during the brawl side quests, it's so easy to manipulate the game and make it child's play, as heavy attacking someone around 3 times runs there stamina to 0 so they are literally stun locked as long as you can keep landing heavy blows and do a mix of light attacks. Overall, game is way to easy to create super overpowered builds.!![GRAPHICS]!!- I run my PC on a 2080 Super [8GB] & a i7-9700K, so I had pretty good specs going into Cyberpunk, which having all the settings maxed out except a few on medium I had around 50-60FPS constantly, so FPS wasn't a real issue except in some areas which weren't well optimized I would go down to about 42~. The game in and of itself however doesn't look that bad. Typical triple A title game graphics of the past few years, so pretty good, but nothing really special.!![STORY]!!- Cyberpunk's 2077 story, in my own personal opinion was kinda meh. I was extremely into the story and getting highly immersed during the first couple hours of gameplay and the starting stories. However, not many missions after Johnny was introduced, at least for myself personally, I gradually began to lose interest in the game as the story became stale at times, typical, or just overall not very interesting. I honestly had a more enjoyable time doing some of the 5~ minute side jobs than I did the entire story. Which to make matters worse, none of the endings were really all that good at all and none were actually satisfying or gratifying.!![BUGS & GLITCHES]!!- The main issue and most talked about thing arguably in Cyberpunk 2077 right now is all the of the bugs and ways you can glitch the game. In my own personal playthroughs, I luckily never had any game-breaking issues. However I did have many bugs, a few even causing me to have to load back or even cause death. From things I have witnessed on other people's playthroughs that I was there in person when they happened, there are many times when gamebreaking issues can occur, as I had 1 friend have to load a save that was hours back to fix his issue, and another couldn't finish a side job no matter what as a person you are meant to talk to was bugged. However, in my own personal experience in my playthroughs, as I said earlier, I never had anything this serious. Just some standard bugs or T poses.!![DRIVING]!!- I have had several people state that they personally do not like the driving, I may be the weird one out but the driving in this game was honestly my favorite part of the entire game. The driving mechanics were nice and pretty responsive, making it really enjoyable. There are also many cars to drive and choose from. HOWEVER, the one thing I personally dislike about the driving & vehicles in Cyberpunk 2077 is that the fastest car in the entire game is completely free and can be achieved and locked to your character as soon as you have access to roam around in the main game. Giving no real reason to drive any of the other cars or enjoyable in earning the car or any of the others you purchase. You can buy another color variant of the car later on, but you can quite literally just get the fastest vehicle before doing even 10% of the story or side jobs, which is a big negative to myself personally. !![NORMAL SUMMARY]!!- So, after reading all of this and me really having a lot of problems with the game and it has a lot of issues, I would still say the game is good and worth you time and money. This is because I still had a good and enjoyable time playing the game, but there were just a lot of times where I can see people getting bored or aggravated at the game. Which is why I feel the game is worth it, but you should only make your decision after knowing all the issues with it, as some of them could either steer you away or closer to buying the game. Hopefully this review has helped you with your decision on if you should buy it or not. Also, something I actually said and a good way to summarize my full blown feelings about Cyberpunk 2077 into two sentences would be this. "After I finish this game, I will likely never play again through another playthrough. Though, I am glad I played this."

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is set in a post war, dystopian future, and man, does it nail the feel the first time you get to drive through the streets in the first district. It has the ability to feel like a huge world, despite there not being very many locations to visit at all.You start off by creating your own interpretation of "V". Which is really a pointless exercise, as you will rarely ever see them again, outside of looking in bathroom mirrors, or playing dress up at the wardrobe, as the game locks you into first person mode immediately. Add to that extended periods of playing as a different character entirely, and I was left wondering why I had the option at all. You then get to choose the background story behind you character, which goes on to have no bearing on the story aside from some rare and minor dialogue options, which V will voice, but you have no say in, or memory of. This probably would have done better with a prologue you could play through in each background before starting the game.The main story of the game starts out at a fairly decent pace, with the main point being dropped on you early enough for it to carry weight as you continue, and the rest of the quests in this line are fine. Most of the characters you cross paths with in the main story will give their own side quests along the way to remain relevant, most of which are fine, as well as a handful of "world event" quests that pop up when you stumble on them, and these are also fine, and occasionally someone you don't know will call you with quests, which tended to be the most interesting quests, all of which come with dialogue paths which also tend to have no real bearing on anything, as with the exception of the final quest, there's as many alternating paths as a nascar track.The score is fantastic, especially when wandering the streets at night, or the wastes outside the city. Unfortunately this suffers like many games from trying to inject "immersive" radio music into an atmospheric game, and like an over-inflated jam donut, it leaks out of every crack. Every doorway, every market has electronic music pumping at an elevated level, shattering any chance to enjoy the work put into the NPCs having their own conversations between each other, as well as the instantial music that ramps up during shootouts and incidental moments. The cybernetic system was a very cool feature, and having the option to choose parts that enhanced your play-style was a nice way to add customizability to the player character. Included is the ability to improve the parts you choose but using the parts found in chests and enemies throughout the world. Unfortunately there was not much need for it, as the rate of generating cash was so high, it quickly became more convenient to just buy upgrades than look for parts. To be honest, I preferred that method, but it made me wonder why the improvement feature was there in the first place. Similar could be said of the crafting, as it is never explained in the game that you can craft weapons, or how to obtain the patterns required to do so. The talent build system was a majorly wasted feature in my opinion. The fact that there are some really cool abilities to reach in the tree, but to have enough points to use them, you had to climb to a reasonably high level, by which point, most of the game was over, and there was nothing left to utilise them on. Unfortunately, as of the time of writing this review, I can spend attribute points without them increasing my attributes, which means it is impossible for me to progress my build, or attain dialogue options that require them, as the most recent patch appears to have broken it somehow.Now for the *bad* stuff.I can give a pass to forcing the player to *walk* during conversation with NPCs, stagger through forced sequences because of "immersion", and even suffer through the worst hand to hand combat, because an entire questline requires it. However, since the DLC was released, the game is once again broken. Terrible render time on NPCs in crowded areas, T-posing shadows, random objects or characters completely unloading, NPC vehicles passing through objects, including the player character and the vehicle they are in during unskippable passenger scenes. The game crashes sometimes during saving, crashes sometimes while quitting, and sometimes hangs.Most of the time you are required to drive to new quest points as they're unlocked across the map, however, suddenly and inexplicably your car will refuse to travel forwards, as you are expected to approach on foot to suit the cutscene, once again being railroaded into playing the game the way the developer intended.Some quests are designed to happen at certain times of day, but rather than allow you to get there when that time rolls around, you instead have to go to the location, and "press X to wait". This ultimately means your character design doesn't matter, your background doesn't matter, your choices don't matter, and you have to play the way the developer wants you to, when they want you to. And by far the most outrageous and egregious issue. You can't even pet the iguana.At the time of review, there are over 130,000 negative reviews, and while this is not enough to change the weight of the majority, that is not a small number.I have tried and tried to enjoy this game, I pushed through a lot as it was a gift from a friend, but I have finally reached the point where I can no longer excuse it as little nit-picky issues that can be overlooked. There are issues here that older games fixed years ago.To put it bluntly, this is a 4 year old game, which is being pushed at 90 bucks, claiming to be fixed. Not good enough. Not for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into the game with low expectations especially with all the things I've heard and seen, and with the game being on sale i said "eh why not".I honestly did not expect the game to be this good and fun, especially as someone who's finished FC5 and other single player action games. It has a lot of issues here and there still, but the gameplay itself is what honestly kept me going.Exploration is a blast, as someone who's always fantasized about living in a neo-futuristic city this really satisfied that itch. Cyberpunk is honestly one of the only games where I'd actually look up whilst just exploring / moving around, the sheer scale of some locations - especially the more urban areas - really is breathtaking (thank you Keanu Chungus).Gunplay and combat were honestly the aspects that i definitely did not expect to like as much as i did. As someone who's more accustomed to less arcadey shooting i didn't think I'd enjoy healthbars and tanky enemies much, but actually playing it proved me wrong. One aspect i genuinely loved was the cover shooting system, as someone who adored the cover shooting from FC5, having it here with improvements (gradual leaning depending on the angle you're looking, seriously this is such a small but really great touch) just made me so happy. The weapons themselves are really great with good variety and usefulness too, shotguns and sniper rifles pack humongous punches, automatic weapons pepper and stagger your enemies, and the melee choices makes you feel like you're playing Hotline Miami.Story wise i won't dwelve or talk too much as I've only basically started going through it, but from the 25 hours I've seen it's honestly really fun to go through. It takes itself seriously and emotionally on some areas whilst keeping it lighthearted and even funny in others, kind of like a slice of life anime.Performance wise it's passable as someone who only has mid tier specs (Legion Y530 with a 4GB GTX1050, i5-8300u, and 16GB DDR4 Ram). The inclusion of AMD's upscaler helped immensely in keeping framerates playable whilst making the game still look pretty decent. I've had to restart the game every 3 hours due to increased lag (most likely a memory leak of sorts), but apart from that performance overall for me is passable. Bugs and glitches wise I've had some issues here and there, but nothing actually troublesome so far (only had a single crash, which is far less than I've expected).Overall, it's a game that you'd enjoy if you're willing to give it a chance, 8/10

However the point of this review is pointing out how it's still not fully fixed even after all this time. My expectation was a witcher 3 with a cyberpunk universe, instead I got a bethesda game. I loved skyrim, however, I am tired of games releasing in alpha/beta without the developer having enough self awarness to maybe ask the community if they want to have it released as "early access" with a vote. _childDocuments_.review: "Wake the ♥♥♥♥ up, Samurai, We have a review incoming.Them rats almost flatline the game, If it wasn't for the love and dedication of the developers of CD PROJEKT RED"Cyberpunk 2077 is not just a game; it’s a neon-drenched odyssey through a futuristic wonderland that will leave you breathless. From the instant you step into the vibrant chaos of Night City, you’re enveloped in an electrifying experience that blends stunning visuals, gripping storytelling, and pulse-pounding action.Let’s dive into Night City, a sprawling metropolis that’s nothing short of a high-tech masterpiece. The cityscape is a sensory overload in the best possible way—towering skyscrapers pierce the sky, their lights reflecting off rain-slicked streets, while neon signs flash with an almost hypnotic rhythm. Every district is a vibrant tapestry of sounds, colors, and activity. Whether you’re cruising through the sleek, upscale high-rises of Corpo Plaza or exploring the gritty, neon-soaked alleys of Watson, the world feels alive and impossibly detailed.The heart of Cyberpunk 2077 lies in its story, and boy, does it deliver. Playing as V, you’re thrust into a whirlwind of corporate intrigue, gang warfare, and personal stakes that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The plot is a rollercoaster of twists and turns, and Johnny Silverhand—voiced with charisma by Keanu Reeves—is a standout character who brings a rebellious spark to the narrative. Watching your relationship with Johnny evolve is a highlight, adding layers of drama and depth to your journey.When it comes to gameplay, Cyberpunk 2077 is an adrenaline-fueled blast. The combat is fierce and exhilarating, with a staggering array of weapons and cybernetic enhancements at your disposal. Whether you’re sneaking through high-tech facilities, unleashing a hail of bullets in a firefight, or hacking into systems to turn the tide, the gameplay is dynamic and engaging. The hacking mechanics let you manipulate the environment and enemies in clever ways, adding a strategic edge to your approach.What truly sets Cyberpunk 2077 apart is how it makes you feel like a part of a living, breathing world. The NPCs aren’t just background decorations; they have their own stories, routines, and quirks that make Night City feel authentically bustling and vibrant. The scale of the game is staggering, with countless activities and encounters that keep the excitement going.Beyond the main storyline, the side content is a treasure trove of variety and fun. From hunting down dangerous bounties to taking part in adrenaline-pumping street races, there’s never a dull moment. The depth of character customization allows you to shape V into the ultimate reflection of your playstyle, adding a personal touch to every encounter.In summary, Cyberpunk 2077 is a high-octane thrill ride through a beautifully realized future. Its stunning visuals, captivating story, and immersive gameplay create an unforgettable experience that’s well worth diving into. Night City is a place where every corner hides a new adventure, and if you’re ready to lose yourself in a world of neon lights and high-tech mayhem, Cyberpunk 2077 is the ultimate ride. Buckle up and get ready for an adventure that will leave you craving more.

_childDocuments_.review: In 2020 they launched CP77, the most anticipated/hyped game in the last 8 years.Main Issues Sky-high rate of bugs, weird AI and graphics, optimization issues, more people enjoying on PC than on consoles.cant deny its all true but everyone still wants to play this game.The CDPR always have a promise for you, that can be a lie or an illusion but its there, just around the corner and its it keeps you going in this game.its a game of cyberpunk genre dreams, and im a big dreamer.(^^ above lines are taken and re-worded from 2018 E3 trailer)Welcome to Night City where the city is full of bugs, items and trash to collect, T-pose players and NPCs, dildos and other sex toys to reflect the horniness of the gamers.TLDR: Its a great game, yes with issues but enjoyable, if you havent bought it wait for 2 big patches promised by CDPR Team or when its on sale.Back to being serious and reviewing the game, spoiler free:+ Night City, its awesome, beautiful, have good amount of dark and grim stuff as per the cyberpunk genre.+ Soundtracks/OST are awesome, be the Radio stations or the Music in background.+ Main Story is great, with multiple endings.+ both V (male and female) voice artists done a top-notch Job.+ Keanu Revees as Johnny Silverhand is Breathtaking, he is the megalomaniac, will make you hate him as well love him(if you play some cards right).+ NPCs are great with story, Jackie <3, Takemura, Evelyn, Claire, Judy, Panam, Rogue, Meredith, Misty, Viktor, Kerry, River - their side quests and interactions with them are fun and give more depth to their characters and backstory.+ Vehicles look awesome, driving might be bit funny.+ Cyberware is awesome and mantis blades with double jump are my fav.+ Choice to play without a single bullet fired, either by sneaking or hacking your way through is commendable.+ Cyberpsychos hunting and other side side quests are great, will keep you interested in game.+ the weapons choices are vast, can up the fun with perks.+ cool references and easter eggs in missions, side missions and certain items.- Buggy, but hilarious ones too - AI is dumb many times- Driving is ♥♥♥♥, especially for AI and the races missions, rest love the bikes.- optimization issues, my PC handled it on medium with around 30-45 fps.- crafting system is bit odd, i have 5 johnny jackets now.- no character customization after the initial build.- Police/wanted system is weird, police will spawn behind you untill you die.- certain dialogs or hud bars will remain stuck in the screen no matter if you load the game again or you start a mission.- There is no headshot kills, but once you upgrade the guns or get better ones you can kill certain enemies with 1 hit headshot.- interactions with romance options after that crucial missions and sex scene, is very less interactive and boring after sometime.I admit they should have delayed the game more to finish it, but you snowflake gamers needed it badly and worse sending death threats to the development team they already crunching enough specially in the pandemic time, thanks to the CDPR bad management and investors. However, they have promised patches and providing regular hotfixes. _childDocuments_.review: To encompass any kind of existing media and make it viable for audiences new and old, including fans of said media, is a gargantuan task. No matter the circumstances of release, with the 2.1 update, fixes, Phantom Liberty and all other extra content, CDPR has proven that this was indeed the birth of the AAAA game. Fidelity achievements aside, they made a believer out of someone who had never bought into the hype, who was glad that people were held to the standard of the product they publish now instead of what they did in the past. I played this game at launch, and kept glancing at it at every major update.But boy, was my mind blown with this game at its final version. There might be more games that fully immerse and engross me in the world, the story, the environment, the characters and the system, but I will never have the same epiphany I received from Cyberpunk. From someone who has been playing video games for more than 2 decades, this is the best gift I have ever given myself.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: if you want the best game in the cyberpunk genre with a wide variety of things to do and ways to do them, alongside incredibly well written storylines and characters, get this game. You won't regret it.Holy crap this game is amazing. I'll be upfront and say I am biased for my love of the cyberpunk genre, but even with that bias I have no issues saying that, if you're looking for a game that embodies the genre of cyberpunk then you will not find anything better. I could write an entire essay on just how well the game uses so many themes and aspects of the genre in a way a lot of games (or even other media) just won't touch. Even themes outside the genre are handled extraodinarily well! There's a reason why I've seen the game get so much praise for its casual portrayal of minority or LGBT characters, especially when other games from really big names (e.g Bioware) tend to fall so incredibly flat. Not to mention the discussions it brings up of consumerism, late-stage pure capitalism, corporatism, the sense of self, death, what it means to live, etc. are all wonderful, and part of what makes Cyberpunk 2077 so, well, *cyberpunk!* While I'm on about story, I can't ignore the characters. Obviously people will like or dislike different characters, but it's hard to deny the amount of love and care that went into each one of them, even the ones you really want to punch in the face (if you've played the game you probably know who I'm talking about). I think the biggest testament to this, for me at least, is that this is the first game that made me actually give a damn about the romance storylines. Not even Mass Effect or The Witcher could do that for me. The quest lines for each character are just so wonderfully written and are often times just beautiful (or in the case of some: horrifying) experiences. Not to mention the seemingly large varieties of ways you can go through any given quest line, even in ways that don't at all seem obvious. The amount of times I've seen someone else complete a specific quest with me going "wait, you can actually *do* that!?" is fairly high. Oh and have I mentioned that this game has some of the best NPC animations I've seen? Characters actually feel *alive,* so much so that it feels like every single conversation is hand animated, even though the realist in me knows that can't be the case.Oh and one final note on story: anyone who says "not a true RPG" is blatantly wrong, either through misinformation or maliciously lying. On to gameplay, I will say upfront that sandbox balancing is... yikes. Obviously since it's just singleplayer you can use whatever, but there's definitely some things that are much stronger than others, and some things that are "why would you ever use this?"If you can get past that though, oh wow the amount of ways you can go through this game are actually kinda dizzying. I've seen this game played with the speed of something like DOOM: Eternal or Titanfall, just blasting through at mach 3, and on the other end of the spectrum I've seen people play it more like Metal Gear: making sure they're never seen and that no one knows they were ever there. Not to mention everything in between. I've also seen people clear entire buildings without ever entering it, or cutting everyone down with a sword before they can even react. Chances are: if there's something you want to do, you can probably do it. Combine that with the amount of different ways to complete any given mission, and the ways you can play this game are crazy.And now for my favourite part: the game doesn't treat you like an idiot. This is probably why so many people go "oh your choices don't matter" simply because each dialogue options aren't accompanied with "X will remember that" or "X approves/disapproves" like so many RPGs love to do now, if they're not just outright telling you the results of your actions before taking them. There are a lot of things that have a much larger impact than you first thought, and you may never notice that until the next playthrough where something plays through wildly different. Not only that, but actions matter just as much as words. There's a number of places you can visit and quests you can do that will affect the outcome of a completely seemingly unrelated quest or place, and you may never realise that until you go through it again in a different way.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game. I put 150 hours into it, trying to really see if it was me or the game.Here are my conclusions.1. The game is bland. You can 'go anywhere' but there ins't always something to do. There is so little content that to buy a car... is a mission. It feels like it's just empty and hollow if you try to play it like Skyrim. Leave the main quest, Panam, or Liz, and you basically don't have anything more than 'there are police here help shoot baddies.'2. Crafting and Item ranking systems in the game are a joke. I think they went for 'guns are made of components' and not 'guns compared to the performance of other similar role guns.' There should be clearly defined levels for weapons, and I really dislike the arbitrary level requirements. Make rare guns rare, and common ones junk.2. a. Iconic weapons are another issue. I should be able to find these weapons outside of storyline quests if I missed it. Additionally, some of them are just broken (Lizzie fires 4 rounds at once at 17/sec....) or garbage (Fenrir, looking at you). Final thought on Iconic weapons - they should be a weight class above the tier they say they are. So a 'common' model would be 'uncommon', etc. That way they perform with the expectation of 'better than same class.'2. b. Crafting is broken. There is so much garbage and weapons just left around by all the dead people you kill that finding parts is easy. The quality of guns is totally random too, and is frustrating to no end. That really tough dude you just fought? Common gun with great dpm for some reason. The random guy that is standing around? He's got a rare quality gun with garbage dpm and not buffs.2. c. Icon items should not be able to disassemble. I've had to reload a number of times because you get so much stuff that you have to regularly melt things down.2. d. The reward items should be iconic. You can't exactly get them again...3. The ending... I hated it. I wanted a 'good' end to be available. Shoot, I could have totally done away with Johnny, the chip, and everything else, make dozens of little side missions, and would have been way happier. The story is extremely immersive, don't get me wrong. But everything else is so tasteless that is sours the game.4. Bugs. So many bugs. When I can't pick up items on the ground, or I get stuck on a surface, it really breaks the game and makes it just not fun.5. Driving. Boy do I hate the driving system. Not only did they fail to make the driving feel smooth, braking is a mile long unless you 'bail' and force the car to halt as you exit. The GPS map is marginally useful but you are going to miss every turn since it doesn't zoom. Finally, for a city some bent on car travel... there are too few bridges, the roads are too narrow and there are too many detours. I can't just drive from A to B, I have to take a loop around the entire city to get to the right bridge first.6.Upgrades and mods are not well implemented. Scopes are not sights, for example. There should be different classes of parts for it.6. a. There is no way to organize by quality (and not rarity, I mean I want to super optimize my gun) for parts. If something alters more than one parameter, it get's too complicated to find good combos. Additionally, the ranking is meaningless, so you can have common items better than rare ones. Unacceptable.7. Sneaking breaks a lot, with a body you are carrying somehow being detected...8. There are no organizations to join. I can't be a cop. I can't be a runner. I'm just a guy following a story that sometimes shoots cyber crazies for cash.9. I would cut all the VA work for V and just go the open world route. Add more content - but more like dungeons or gang wars. Not the generic cop fights . Once you clear a mob, they are gone. Forever.I have more complaints, but I don't care anymore. I just wanted an Open World RPG or MMO. I got a story/movie game (a very good one too!) selling itself as a select your own adventure. But it even fails to make meaningful use of the background differences in V.

_childDocuments_.review: I enojoy this game a lot more than other games lately! The plot starts a bit slow but gets more and more interesting after the prologue. The dialogues, sound and graphics are great (install latest graphic drivers). Love the world building and can immerse myself in it for hours.Game controls well for my preferences (Half Life style control scheme). Graphics are ridiculously gorgeous than they have any right to be. Sound design is excellent with so many bespoke effects littered throughout. Gunplay is solid, satisfying and reminds me a bit of Killzone 2 with the cover mechanics. I won't comment much on the story, others will take a lot of enjoyment from it, as do I.Bugs have happened, some random T-posing, clipping, physics going wonky, cars falling from the sky as they spawn in, some NPC scripts or quest scripts not triggering sometimes to name a few. So far I haven't hit anything that has flat out impeded my progress and enjoyment. I keep a rotating run of x number of manual saves. Having to reload a save in the instance a quest bugs might be the final straw for a lot of players. I can deal.Game has steep system requirements, no need to sugar-coat it. The performance fixes floating out there by modders are a possible avenue to explore. Your mileage may vary. There are promises of fixes for the performance down the road, I'm only counting what I've experienced so far in my rating. I have not had much performance issues with it that I couldn't handle so I don't care much unless it continuously locks up or crashes. I've had one crash so far in my 50 hours of gameplay.The world building is incredible and certainly the star of the show here. I love this stuff, more-so in an RPG of this scale and this is the thing I'm weighing most heavily here. So detailed, even small encounters have a back story to them. Pieces of information the designers left for players to uncover and click together for themselves are scattered all over. Seems like little was left to chance and there was TONS of thought put into what goes where and the implications of it. If you give it a shot, pace yourself and let the game's world pull you in. It has all kinds of interesting stories to tell you.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start, no we should never rely on mods to fix the game, mods should be made to expand on the game.This game makes me sad, because CDPR are focusing on making this game a mediocre movie game instead of an immersive open world game, the art team made an amazing world for us to play and explore, but CDPR are more focused on scripted gameplay rather than functioning gameplay mechanics.Gameplay Mechanics VS Scripted Gameplay:A better minimap VS a scripted car chase.Recoloring of clothes, weapons, vehicles VS a fully voiced protagonist.A better AI and a proper joinable factions gameplay VS a famous actor.I only listed a few comparisons, but as you can see, Gameplay Mechanics only require a small amount of resources compared to Scripted Gameplay. The fact that I can't even sit and drink or eat with animations on chairs, food vendors etc. unless it's scripted gameplay, so much potential but it's wasted on mediocre game design.The saddest part is, CDPR will continue making this a Mediocre Movie Game on the upcoming expansion, I hope that I'm wrong and CDPR will eventually make this a proper RPG Game, but as of this time I can't recommend buying this game unless it's on sale and you don't have anything else to play just like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this for a while, i can safely say that this game is more like Story driven RPG and not really open world/sandbox type.If people jump in the game with an expectation that this gonna be like GTA/RDR, they gonna be dissappointed.At best it's closer to Sleeping dogs or the Mafia i think.The world is big sure but it's more like a props for the story.Most npc just walk back and forth with no activities with an exception of those npc at stores/stall and some minor npc doing random things.Take out the story and you clearly cant do anything which is why you can't compare this to GTA and RDR.In those game, the world have lore,secrets,random activities. You can do other sort of activities ,encounter weird things etc Don't expect immersion much in this game. Immersiveness is out of the picture. Don't get me wrong,I still enjoy it.The story itself is good. Especially the interaction with Johnny. If you care about the story only, then yes the game should be fine. _childDocuments_.review: In 2022 this game is very good. The free roam aspect is very nice. You could do a couple main story missions and do a bunch of gigs and NCPD scanners then go to story. All in all a lot of freedom. The story is pretty gripping. All side missions have their own cool stories in them as well. Wish there was more iconic guns besides handguns but all guns in the game are pretty unique as well as having their own traits. One huge thing i wish i knew before starting the game was the game technically never ends. Once you complete the main story it shoots you out right before entering the "Point of no return". Which then in turn you could see what all the endings are. Which, i think is a very cool way to make the story. Only downside with that is i wish you could make an ending your "true" ending and keep that ending into postgame. Specs: geforce rtx 3070 fe, 5800x ryzen and m.2. Was able to run max settings but pc got a little frame drops here and there depending where i was at. So if you want to run max settings you need a really strong rig. Bugs: I ran into a couple funny bugs with npc's being glitched into cars and other things. But, i did get a couple huge ones that have been here since the drop of the game. With the gigs, one of them called "severance package", all the doors are powered down so i can not get into the building. I was able to get into on my first try doing the gig, but i'm playing on the hardest difficulty and was sneaking around and died. Then it shot me out to my last load and now every door is unpowered making it impossible to finish. Really sucks because its my last gig in the whole game. Gun gameplay: a huge fan of the the gameplay. All the guns feel really smooth and it offers a wide variety of play styles. The melee combat feels pretty smooth but a little repetitive. Story: 9/10Side missions: 8.5/10NSPD: 5/10 (gets really repetitive) Gigs: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly two years and lots of promises later this game is still a mess.Pedestrians spawning on highways, every second npc on the street is the same model despite high graphics settings, holocalls often overlap and cut off quest dialogue or the other way around... Thankfully nothing gamebreaking, but can you really be thankful for that? Is it really ok for a title of this level to barely function the way it is meant to?At it's best I'm having loads of fun. Night city is a solid enviroment with beautiful details. Npcs are just empty husks roaming the streets but who cares about that honestly. Gunplay feels good to me and the system for leveling and perks is perfectly fine once you understand it. And most importantly I find the writing and story gripping and enjoyable, truly a game I could sit playing for hours and hours. But how am I meant to do that when my companion shoots an imaginary anti-air missile?When corpo assault team sweeps into a building you're hiding in and your companion... T-poses in a corner?When you end up negotiating with a decapitated security guard about him to letting you in to a compound?Your immersion breaks at nearly every cutscene, at every scripted event I find myself thinking what is gonna go wrong this time.Update:Phantom Liberty and version 2.0 happened and after nearly 90 hours of playtime I stand corrected. Game is in a much healthier place glitch-wise, I love the new Cybernetics system and all in all the whole game is now very enjoyable.However I am keeping the review negative as I feel it took unforgivably long to get here and business model where an unfinished product gets shipped and  gets fixed in the next few years cannot be allowed to take root.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot give this game a positive review even though i kinda enjoyed it after 3 years of postponing.With the release of 2.1 update and Phantom Liberty expansion it was supposed to be the second coming of polish jesus, but hear my thoughts please. The great expansion only highlights how bland and mediocre the original game was and to extend - still is. Because all they added is some features that you could have added with mods if you wanted to, cringe "dates" with your companion where they re-use voice lines from the main story and what? Finally made the progression system and itemisation somewhat coherent? Wow, something that shoudve been in the game 3 years ago? _childDocuments_.review: A truly open-ended RPG. You can create anyone and  anyone. You, the player, can set your own ambitions and the choices you make in the game would directly reflect who you’re trying to role play. Your life path is more apparent in-game, beyond just the opening and certain dialogue. The game actually branches off into different paths and your choices make a difference in the beginning and middle - not just the end. Your choices have impact that also reflects onto the world itself as you play.You get to purchase homes/apartments, customize them, visit futuristic autoshops to customize your cars with interesting and useful gadgets or cosmetics, enter a coffee shop and watch as NPCs go on with their lives - maybe bump into unique interactions with them, walk into a casino and play your hand in a futuristic version of poker, come across different activities that you wouldn't see in the modern world, different means of transportation like subways or flying cars to get a vantage view of the city, entering a clothes shop and actually visually trying on different clothes.. To have the opportunity to set yourself in this world and truly immerse yourself by having the chance to do what otherwise would seem as mundane tasks, but have it become interesting because of the futuristic setting. This sort of detail would create an environment and a bustling city with substance - and one that’d be worth returning to. I would’ve hoped for a more dynamic level of detail where, for example, you would have a greater chance of stealth during nighttime or you’d get dirty after hours of missions while neglecting showering/resting. I never had a reason to enter my apartment, so why not give the players a reason to? These little realistic details & dynamics would only add to the immersion. It was surprising to me that that level of detail was lacking from developers like CDPR.I’d love to see droids interacting with the world and other NPCs, walking the streets, being vendors and interesting characters/quest-givers, etc. There was only a taste of this with the AI taxi service in-game. It would've been neat to see more innovative uses of tech scattered throughout the world that could demonstrate the difference in everyday life compared to the present. I feel the game didn’t take enough advantage of its setting to better showcase a futuristic city. A smart law enforcement system, where being issued a warrant actually means you have to be wary of running into police officers in certain parts of the city and have to give effort in evading the police. There should’ve also been different means of dealing with the law (bribes, surrender, resisting, getting caught and imprisoned, etc.) and those different means could be dependent on your role-playing builds and attributes. Instead I feel as though I can get away with anything and a short drive around the block will clear my name. Where’s the depth? I could go on about the different features that could've truly enhanced this game... And a lot of what I wished for is actually also what CDPR also promised. A huge chunk of these promises were far from fulfilled though. An interesting and good story, decent enough combat/stealth, but with everything else falling at or well below average. Fix the bugs and this review will likely still stand. I'm more concerned by the fundamental aspects of the game... If this description doesn't change, my opinion will stand. V’s ambition is mostly their own. If you aren’t interested in “becoming a legend of night city” and, for example, you chose Nomad because you’d actually prefer to be an outsider - Well, you don’t have much role-playing say. Remember, you’re not playing your own character. You’re role playing V. That version of V still has the same goal in mind no matter where you come from or what you’re actually interested in. The only time you’ll be able to express the sort of direction you want to head, it’s at the very end when you simply choose between the different endings. “Branching storylines” is nothing more than just choosing between multiple different endings. You unlock more endings simply by doing a few key quest lines... That’s it. There wasn’t any impactful decision up until the very end. This takes any replayability away from the game. Just replay the last mission and you saw everything. There's no reason to replay anything else.You can't pay attention to NPCs too much or it'll break immersion. They don't have their own daily routines, they walk in circles and get scared by you simply jumping onto a railing. Law enforcement AI is especially horrible, instantly spawning on you and not really posing any challenge either. NPCs do a lot to a game's environment and immersive-ness, it would need an entire rework to fix.I know the game is meant to be dystopian, but that doesn’t mean Night City needed to be so distasteful. It’s empty, trashy, and unpleasant. I wouldn’t want to set foot in that city in real life. I personally don’t think it really captures the vibe of “cyberpunk” either. Cyberpunk’s world isn’t much of a sandbox. It’s not really the game you’d start up to just to mess around in, simply because there isn’t really anything to do aside from the missions/gigs... Unlike a game like GTA or RDR2, where the worlds are entertaining enough on their own. TW3 was good in that regard as well, so why are we taking steps backwards? Those aforementioned worlds were filled with detail and unique interactions/encounters. You were bound to run into something you haven’t seen before even after hours of gameplay, which made those worlds worth exploring.  I never felt compelled to do that in Cyberpunk, and when I did decide to explore anyways, it just reminded me of the lack of substance within Night City. That sandbox/exploration aspect to the world was just missing and, to me, that was both surprising and disappointing.Military and intelligent taxi droids are there, but why not drones who could sweep the city, for example? The city could sure use it & surely they would’ve have had that sort of technology in the future. Again, it doesn’t feel like the future setting was fully taken advantage of. There could’ve been so much to see and experience in this setting.. There was definitely more room to see technological advances in play.The game felt void and heavily relied on its short story to keep the interest. If the story is the only thing you value, this should be enough for you. CDPR are good story writers. I just hoped for something more and I don't think it's unfair to say that as CDPR promised a difference experience. Perhaps it's at CDPR's disadvantage that I and many others hold them to a higher standard because of their past work. At the same time, I do believe the developers envisioned the game I described in the first half of this review, but for whatever reason(s), it wasn’t delivered. There were so many promised features lacking that it stripped the depth and detail I was expecting. The game to me is just another average open world game now, but with a story that’s above that average. I couldn’t say the experience was unique or amazing, it was just fun and good enough to finish through.
