_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I *wanted* this game to be the best game I've played in years. I wanted the hype to be real. I wanted this game to be my most played game on steam (tall order for me). I have been waiting for this game for a very long time and wanted to believe that with nearly a decade worth of development that it would have a rich story, deep world building, and provide an experience that let me escape the disaster that was 2020. Early reviews came in and said the game was amazing (I'm looking at you SkillUp) but had minor technical issues. I was let down in nearly every aspect of this game.First, let's cover what I did enjoy before I get into the myriad of problems (in no particular order):* Fashionpunk - I absolutely loved dressing up my V, I enjoyed the weird mix and match style of clothing, the possibilities, and the regular experience of trying on clothes to see how they look on my V. I loved it so much, I often kept suboptimal clothes on because they just looked great. I love that when I put on some clothing, I got to see that clothing on my character in sequences.* Loot - I clearly love shooter looters. I love loot heavy games. I really loved killing an enemy and taking their gun/clothing as a result.* Level appropriate items - You don't have to worry about the order you do things as you will find items that match your level.* No Loading - the city is rather large (maybe a dozen km wide) and I never had to wait for load screens. I may have had textures phase in but that's less jaring than stopping the game entirely while driving down the street (really, Borderlands handled this pretty well).* Volume of quests - There is a huge volume of quests to complete, enough to get you to maximum level without grinding (I believe I hit 50 just as I finished, though I was at 50 street cred by a very low level).* The main story - it was interesting and I enjoyed watching it (more on this later). I was fairly satisfied with the initial ending I chose.* Main side characters - I liked doing things with Panam, Judy, Johnny, etc.Unfortunately, that's about it. Here's the rather long list of problems. Let's start with the number one problem describing this game:Shallow - pretty much nothing you do can impact the story. Choices don't really matter aside from a few dialog options near the end. NPCs reside in precisely 2 states: passive or fleeing/attacking. There isn't any variability with how enemies act or bystanders. None of the NPCs are ever aware of any other thing happening (my car exploded feet from an NPC and he didn't seem to care). Time doesn't matter - no matter how much time you make lapse, it only seems to change the weather (which is mostly just day or night). It doesn't have any effect on NPCs or the story, NPCs could ask you to be somewhere ASAP and they will happily way for an eternity. Most buildings are locked and serve as polys to drive around or jump over. Crafting is broken; there is so much wrong here. There are basically 5 types of vendors: ripperdocs, clothing vendors, gun/melee weapon vendors, medicine shops, vendor drop machines - they're all the same and you can skip time to let them change their inventory. Police are pointless and only pose a threat at 4-star warrant level (blatant GTA ripoff), they literally spawn in around you, and you literally run away from warrants in roughly 20s.Okay, so that was a lengthy way to say that there is no depth to this game at all. Here's some more detail on problems as I've seen it.* Story - About 90% of things you do have no impact on the story. I had 4 endings available to me by the end; for most of the endings, the only thing that separates them is one or 2 things at most and I *heavily* disagree with how you get to the secret ending.* Fashionpunk - While there are a lot of clothes, there's not really that many different types within each category. Maybe a few colors or minor variations, but they're all really similar.* Loot - managing loot in this game is a nightmare. Most things are garbage and only act as a means of selling it to a generic rando vendor machine. Worse, unique items are leveled to you rather than have their own uniquely determined level.* Loading - ugh, placeholder polys and pop-in textures happens way too often.* Quests - they're all the same. You are either killing someone or stealing something. The handful of quests that offer real world building really still half-ass the whole thing. Sinnerman was one of the best ones but in the end, it's usually going to resolve one of 2 ways for everyone. Cyberpsychosis was one of the worst - after trekking all over the city and dealing with a whopping 17 of these guys and somehow not killing them with my shotgun, you're rewarded with a meager 1 sentence resolution from the quest giver.* The Main Story - your actions have little to no effect on the main story.* Driving - Dumpster fire is the only way to describe this. I eventually got used to the controls but there's so many problems with it. From the minimap that makes driving fast impossible to the reaction to random textures (you can safely drive your motorcycle off a cliff but if you hit a lamp going 120 MPH, it will stop your car in its tracks).* Cars - most of them are bad. The cool ones drive like they're on ice. The motorcycles are the only things worth driving. See a cool car on the street, like the one with the translucent hood? Steal it, drive it, and it'll randomly disappear after you walk away from it, but you'll have to steal it to drive it again.* Customizability - doesn't exist. I played a female V and while I could change my cybernetics all over town, I couldn't change my lipstick.* NPCs - They're pointless. If they're unarmed, they can only be casual, fleeing, or dead. If they're armed, they can only be casual, attacking only you, or dead. There is no in between or other states and once they go to fleeing or attacking, they never leave. NPCs are unaware of anything going on around them and just walk in circles down the street. They're never doing anything (I saw exactly 1 NPC carrying a box but he went no where). I got my first warrant when I walked out of my apartment to see the deep dive crime scene only to have the cop attack me (literally just looking at it), in which I promptly killed him and ran for about 30s to drop the warrant.* Crafting - It's the only way to get some of the coolest items. Yup, once you max out your skill tree for crafting, you have a solid chunk of your stats that you will use essentially once, and then never again. If you didn't spend on it, you can never obtain unique guns. That's right, the coolest and most unique items in the game can only be made from a recipe, rather than found. Even if you have the recipe, you can't make it. There are no craftsmen, so there's no chance of you getting those items. The craft quality to resource ratio is stupid - its essentially free to create legendaries all day.* Time - it doesn't matter. Skip enough days and V reacts to the relic, that's about it. It has zero impact on the game. Why sleep at your apartment? NPCs wait forever, everything is scripted and triggered from either player actions or an exact elapsed game time.* Technical - the technical warts with this game are literally everywhere. From every poly completely unaware of every other poly (eg NPCs walking through cars) to crashes requiring restarts, the game is a technical mess. No amount of complaining about the pandemic will cut it; they were working on this game for 8 years and aren't allowed to blame this on working from home.As badly as I wanted this game to be amazeballs, it's simply bad. Even if CDPR fixes every technical glitch, it's a mediocre/generic/futuristic GTA clone and they have to fundamentally rebuild this game from the ground up to come anywhere close to the promises they made. I can't recommend this game to anyone for any reason. You're better off watching the story sections on youtub

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, there are still occasional glitches and weird collision issues. But there is also a really solid game and it is amazing.The gameplay is varied. Has your classic warrior/rouge/wizard type builds or play a hybrid. Stealth is very important for a few parts (especially for bonus rewards) you can face enemies in a number of interesting ways.There are generally multiple ways of reaching your goals, depending on your build, adding to replayability and the temptation to explore and see what else is possible.It feels like being in a real city, with distinct neighborhoods and districts. Give Night City a reskin and it could be a modern city.Characters have believable goals and motivations. Do what they want and they'll help you out. Get in their way and they'll (try to) take you out. There aren't orcs/raiders/etc just looking to chase you down.I care about these people and want good things for them, even when I know it's not always a possibility.The story, in spite of a few flaws, grabs me and has interesting and rational twists and turns. The side stories are interesting and fill out the world nicely.The endings are a gut punch. Try them all out and see the different ways things can go. Heck, the game wants you to.So yes, I really love this game. I started playing at version 1.5, having avoided even buying it until I felt sure it would be properly updated. It's been a heck of a journey but I really like where it's ended up.

Honestly CDPR should have just delayed it again even though crybabies would throw hissyfits again the game could have used another delay because as is it just suffered from a rushed launch with a myriad of bugs and glitches ranging from texture pop-ins to framedrops to physics bugs like items clipping through the world of characters spacing out. The game on High/Ultra simply does not look fantastic as well and the texture pop-in problems exacerbate this feeling that it does not look good. Now a big patch is rumored to be dropping soon but until then these problems are just a huge turnoff for me personally even though I'm running it better than a lot of people are with hardly any framedrops and with a good enough fps where it does not really bother me.First Impressions:Let's start of with the character creation, for an RPG it's really really underwhelming and I severely hope that either mods or a later update will improve this because it was a massive turnoff for me personally. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the controversy surrounding its release, I must say that Cyberpunk 2077 is a fantastic game. Yes, it was grossly misrepresented and overhyped by the developers pre-release, but I'm happy to say that the actual gameplay experience is still incredibly enjoyable.The world of Night City is breathtakingly immersive and well-crafted, with an enormous amount of detail and depth that really allows you to feel like you're living in a futuristic metropolis. The story and characters are also top-notch, with a compelling main plotline and plenty of side quests to keep you engaged for hours on end.Of course, there are some technical issues that still need to be addressed, such as occasional bugs and glitches, but these are minor inconveniences that don't detract from the overall experience.Overall, I would highly recommend Cyberpunk 2077 to any fans of open-world RPGs or science fiction in general. It may not have lived up to the hype that was generated pre-release, but it's still a fun and engaging game that's well worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Janky, If I can describe it with one word.8 years of hype to launch and 4 years in development, to be what looks like an early access game. It's glitchy, it's buggy, it doesn’t run well unless you have a RTX card and DLSS enabled. And that's barely passable.But those can eventually be fixed.The core of the game, the massive open world, is incredibly superficial, with nothing to do in it. CDPR crafted a beautiful, detailed world with braindead AI and overly simplistic gameplay.There's no roleplaying involved like you would find in Deus Ex. there's no extracurricular activities that doesn't involve shooting a bunch of bad guys like you would find in Red Dead Redemption 2. You won't find tight gunplay like you would see in Destiny 2. The AI completely lacks any sort of intelligence. Enemies rush you without the sense of self-preservation. Oftentimes standing there letting you blast them in the face. Cops spawn literally yards behind you without any chase, or any threat. Walk a block down and they completely forget you exist. No bounty on your head, no search and apprehend procedures. But stand next to them for 3 seconds and they'll shoot you on sight.Really, there's not much to do except shoot things. guns feel impactful enough, if you use revolvers or tech weapons, and melee combat is passable. You can go for a stealth or hacking approach, but those don't feel as good as just pulling the trigger on some thugs. Hacking is just pointing your reticle at someone, and then select from the menu. And depending on what you chose, sparks just fly out of their head. That's it. The story is engaging, yet forgettable. This is cyberpunk setting, but it's in appearances only. There's all these talks about mega corporations taking over the world, but only one corporation takes center stage. There's no political intrigue, no conspiracy theory that turns out to be true, no investigation into a greater mystery. Keanu Reeves is literally taking your breath away and you go out to make sure that doesn't happen. Your personal backstory is forgettable. it's literally 20 mins long, and your entire introduction to Night City is a montage. CDPR failed the "show, don't tell" aspect. They could have squeezed in a few good hours of character development and worldbuilding with the opening hours. Instead, you get taken straight into Night City, told to care about certain things, and want to have this lofty ideal of becoming a living legend for some unknown reason. You don't have a story to tell, there's a story being told to you.The characters definitely carry the narrative, from Silverhand's personal vendetta, to Panam's sense of belonging, and Takemura's strong honor code.Regardless, I did enjoy this game. But there's so many glaring flaws that becomes hard to ignore and make me don’t want to pick it up again until its fixed with either patches, DLC or any solutions. So, it pains me to say, I do not recommend this game. The numerous technical issues make this equivalent to an Early Access title. But the gameplay loop, the promise of an immersive experience, a sandbox for you to get lost in are totally nonexistent. It's a beautiful world CDPR has created, but it's just a glorified loading screen going from one mission marker to another.It's all style, but no substance.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game good? Yeah, it's pretty okay. It runs fine on my RTX 3090 and R9 5950x I don't see what everyone's problem is.Jokes aside, I played it fine at 1440p on a 1080 Ti and a R7 2700x CPU. There were some occasional dips below 60 fps in large scenes, and it wasn't all maxed out graphics, but it was certainly playable on release, but a 1080 Ti is still pretty damn high-end, tbh. I enjoyed it. Is it worth $60? Ehhhh, probably not, but I've definitely spent $60 on worse games that I still enjoyed.To be honest, it kinda reminded me of a Bethesda RPG. It was buggy as heck but a lot of the bugs were comical, not just game-breaking. If you got sucked into the game and didn't have your immersion broken by an NPC t-posing with a giraffe neck, and if you got lucky where you didn't randomly crash and corrupt your save, you're probably going to be able to enjoy the game at least. Some of the mechanics feel kinda hollow and not as fun/fleshed out as you would expect in a modern game, but you can still go back and play Skyrim or Fallout 4 today and enjoy it... just not for $60, maybe on sale. Tell them to make a VR version like Skyrim and I'd play that again for sure lolThe gunplay is nothing special, kinda like a Fallout game. There's certain weapons and abilities that are way more satisfying, but that'll vary from person-to-person. I enjoyed being a melee/shotgun dumbass who ran in with Sandevistan (time slow/stop) and decapitated (or, if I was feeling nice, concussed by a vibrator or socket wrench) a bunch of gangsters committing the heinous crime of loitering next to their motorcycles. I also played around with the combat hacking, where you can get some cool cyberware later on like having enemies commit suicide, go berserk, or detonate a flashbang grenade on their belt.I dislike how the skill trees are set up, where you invest points in an Attribute, then into individual Perks, where you're somewhat limited and locked into certain paths since you can reinvest Perk points, but not Attribute points (unless you just cheat, which is what I did when I finished the game and wanted to ♥♥♥♥ around for a while instead of just making a new character and re-leveling them again).The crafting kinda sucks and I didn't want to invest into the Engineering tree, since it didn't let me bulk craft. With how limited Attribute points were, I'd recommend skipping Engineering and spreading them out into 2-3 of the other branches, based on your play style. Is it actually OP? Eh, yeah, you can make some broken weapons and armor when I was playing around, but investing points and salvaging stuff to upgrade/craft gear was boring and tedious, and you'd be missing out on more fun perks.The AI sometimes is braindead and will pepper you with BBs, while other times they're psychic and will one-shot you with a sniper rifle. There's no real level-scaling so it's easy to wander into an area where the random gangsters can instantly kill you (and, again, enemies with shotguns or snipers at your level may get lucky and just headshot you for an insta-kill lmao)The story is alright overall, and there's some various side missions that have good storylines and unlock different ending missions depending on which gangs like you. One beef I have with the side missions is that it is sometimes difficult to find/stumble upon the fun side missions vs the boring copy-paste story-less gigs.Also I couldn't get a lapdance or watch porn braindances, 0/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. The bugs are virtually all gone and the game is fun enough to play. They take the plot in all the ways you'd imagine it to go with the setup and don't really innovate in that space much. There are some problems with tone - on the one hand people are having their organs harvested, on the other hand Keanu Reeves is the unstable frontman of a wildly popular rock band who moonlights as a nuclear terrorist - the game gives it a good go at pulling it off with some success, but tonal whiplash can take you out of the experience occasionally.The mechanics are good and fun, except for the irritating dash-dodge enemies. The weapon crafting/upgrade system is mediocre at best, especially so in the later game when you start running out of the more common components. Driving is pretty fun, although early and fast vehicles perform horribly.Overall it's worth a look. It won't change your life but it's a decent enough experience if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is spoiler-free. Cyberpunk 2077 is not the game we got promised but it is still decent after all- nothing more, nothing less. Keep in mind that most negative reviews address the bugs in the game. Me on the other hand experienced a mostly bug-free gameplay. The only bugs i had were mainly of the graphical sort like textures of characters not loading or pop-ins. Only once or twice they extented to a game-breaking level when i randomly got teleported 100ft away but like i said that just occured very rarily. Is this massively hyped action RPG as bad as the reviews suggest and does it manage to keep up with the expectations? Let's find out..The graphics are simply stunning and pure eye-candy. Night City looks gorgeous (Especially at night) and even the remote areas have their own charm. Speaking of beauty- the main character models look just like you'd imagine people living in a dystopian future look like. Hairstyles, make-up and cyberware are just spot-on and immersive. The carefully selected warm neon color themes distract you from all the corruption going on in Night City and arrouses the feeling of security. Random NPCs however, look bland and neglected- their textures can look painfully bad. Everyone has the same face, animation and reactions and i don't even want to mention how often i saw the same NPCs in the same area. Still i would say the graphics are the strongest feature of Cyberpunk 2077 and reason alone to purchase this game- if you like Cyberpunk themes. It's running pretty solidly on a GTX 1660Super + Ryzen 5 3600 with around 65-70fps on medium-high settings (1080p). In dense areas it occasionaly dropped to ~45fps but that did not break the deal for me. Assuming you want to buy Cyberpunk 2077 you have to be satisfied with a pretty average gameplay-style. Whilst there are cool futuristic looking guns- most of them feel pretty ordinary. There are a few exceptions though like Silverhand's revolver, which has one of the sickest  animations of all time. However, the vast majority (Shotguns, sniper rifles, pistols etc.) just feel clunky. Reloading feels like a pain sometimes because it does not keep up with the gameplay's pace during combat. In addition to that, melee fights do not even manage to feel one tiny bit better than Skyrim's melee system. Even The Elder Scrolls Oblivion had a more in-depth hand-to-hand combat system. The skills do not really add a lot of features and mainly serve the intention to make the game easier by simply improving your stats. Regarding vehicles; Even though the bikes and cars look and sound cool, they just feel unnatural. They make the impression that they're made out of cardboard because of their almost comical driving physics. I would not say that driving around isn't fun but still, better driving physics would have contributed to a more immersive feeling of Night City.Main story and side missions. This point is probably one of the most controversial among the reviews. Numorous amounts of reviews state that the stories in this game are repetitive and monotone. On the other hand some people quite enjoyed them. Why? It's probably because CDPR advertised this game with immense amounts of action trailers for the mainstream.  The reality is that action-packed gameplay scenes make up like 10% of the main story. V, the main character, is mostly occupied with dialogues and  there are tons of them  in this game. I  strongly disliked these parts- the ones where you can't do anything else besides standing in front or next to a person and listening to them talking. You get the expression that the story is finally  gaining up pace just to be interrupted by another scripted dialogue scene, which just messes up the overall flow of progression. I mostly skipped through unimportant conversations because they're mostly insanely slow-paced and keep in mind that the dialogue options you choose have little to no impact on the story. Boring. You can do better, CDPR.Sigh. Back when Cyberpunk 2077 was still in development we all expected the open-world to be filled with life. Unfortunaly that's not the case. As a game set in an alternate universe in the 2070s you'd expect a tremendous quantity of custimization options. The truth is: Night City feels lifeless in terms of activity. No barbers, no garages, no in-depth weapon customization except a few attachment options. During it's marketing campaing, CD Projekt Red fed us hungry fans with (pre-rendered) heart-pounding police pursuits. Turns out you can just get rid of the NCPD, Night City's police department, by just driving to the next block.  Voilà! You're a free citizen again. Apart from that, street races do not even remotely reach the expectations. All participating drivers just follow a scripted route with zero efforts to eliminate you. Compared to other AAA open-worlds like GTA5 or RDR2 it is dissatisfying and feels wrong. However, the soundtrack and overall sound-design are sensational. CDPR did a great job choosing fitting songs. In fact, the combat music is breathtaking. Make's you wanna never ever leave the fight again. In addition to that, Cyberpunk 2077 offers a generous amount of radio music (Mostly futuristic sounding genres like Synthpop.) As a lover of Synthwave/Synthpop i spent hours just driving around, free roaming this beautiful city with the radio volume on 100%.  The unskippable radio broadcasts in between the songs are kinda annoying though but you're able to just mute the car radio completely.One of the weakest aspects  of Cyberpunk 2077 is its stupidly braindead artificial intelligence. Every NPC, no matter if common thug or elite fighter owns the same combat AI and offer little variety. This A.I has a negative influence on stealth gameplay. Hostile NPCs fail to spot you even if you're in plain sight.  Besides that, they prove to be the most idiotic human beings i've ever witnessed in a game. They all play the same behavior patterns. Hold them at gunpoint- they all start doing the same animation. Notice a shooting, explosion etc- they just duck and do nothing else. You probably saw a lot of compilations and comparison to other games and we have to admit- the NPCs are just as stupid as they are in those videos. For the most part the voice acting in this futuristic RPG  is fine. CD Projekt Red did a pretty good job hiring high quality and experienced voice actors/ actresses. I played as female V voiced by Cherami Leigh, who is a talented voice actress mostly known for her participation in Animes. While i think she did a pretty good job i occasionaly  got the impression that she tried too hard to make V sound tough. Maybe it was intentional since V's a try-hard mercenary who is attempting to act unbreakable. Who knows! Same goes with the other characters. Sometimes i thought a child wrote the dialogues- words like “Biz“ sound way to cheesy for an otherwise rather serious storyline.   Cherami Leigh's  work and the voicing in general made a decent impression though.This review is obviously addressing the PC version, played on mostly Medium-High settings. Don't even bother playing it on last-gen consoles- it's horrible. I know from first hand experience. You might have noticed that i criticised lots of aspects but what makes me still recommend this game? I think the graphics and soundtrack really make up for its flaws. Some characters like Jackie really stick out and are fun to be around with. If you love dystopian settings- go ahead and purchase it. If you don't want to support CD Projekt Red for being liars and scrapping out tons of features- just don't buy this game and let people enjoy it. I could write an infinite rant about CDPR's marketing campaign but this review is just for the game itself. 5,5-6/10

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this review: I played Cyberpunk 2077 all the way from release up until update 1.2, so any updates that will change the game after that time I will not be able to say anything about. I did a completionist run of cyberpunk with a mostly stealth playstyle (with some occasional handguns and smart guns) and thoroughly explored every corner of Night City. So this is my experience with this game.GameplayStealth gameplay is pretty barebones (killing or choking someone unconscious makes no difference) but I still enjoyed using the environment to my advantage with my hacking skills. It is pretty satisfying to complete an area or quest without anyone ever seeing you. That being said, enemies do seem to have a spidey sense sometimes and will just spot you when you’re not even in sight (through a wall sometimes even). And once you get caught, it’s pretty much run and gun from there onwards since they don’t reset their aggro unless you walk really far away.The gunplay is pretty solid. Handguns are fun to use (even though extremely overpowered) and smart guns are really satisfying (shooting through walls, head shotting without really aiming). Can’t really say much about melee combat since I barely did anything with it. The gameplay loop comes down to: ‘go here, kill guy, get loot’ but the story mostly makes up for that. The game also has some balancing issues because you can basically one shot everyone at level 20 if you spend your points wisely.QuestsThe main quest(s) and associated side quests are really good in my opinion. The characters are believable in the sense that they could actually exist in such a futuristic world. And CPDR does not shy away from what the ‘taboo’ and mature subjects touch upon and are done really well. At one of the main quest endings I even got a little bit emotional, which I don’t get a lot when playing games. Side quests in cyberpunk are categorized in ‘actual side quests’, ‘gigs’ (with subcategories of killing someone or stealing/hacking something) and the most basic side quests which are ncpd scanner hustles and crime in progress (which are basically go here, kill guys, get loot). With the side quests it’s mostly hit or miss, some are really great and some not at all. Cyberpunk often likes to give you the illusion that your choices matter but it’s usually two doors that lead to the same hallway, metaphorically speaking. On rare occasions it does matter what you choose and it has an impact on the world. But generally don’t go in expecting too much from your actions. There is also literally nothing to do in night city once you've completed all the quests. There are no repeatable side-activities whatsoever. EnvironmentNight City is a pleasure for the eye. I played on a mid-range rig (gtx 1060 6gb/Ryzen 3700x) and played on mid-low graphics. Even with these low settings, night city is graphically really good looking. The environment does cause your fps to dip sometimes but generally I was playing with anywhere between 30-50 fps. Night City is one of the best well handcrafted cities I’ve ever seen in a game in my opinion. Each district has its own distinct architecture and feeling which makes you feel like you actually go somewhere else every time. There were countless times where I just opened photomode and just looked at the beautiful sights for a while. On the other hand, the npc’s in the city are incredibly lifeless and walk everywhere with no purpose. Night city also does not have even the most basic necessities like a barber or tattoo shop. So you’re pretty much locked to the look you gave your character at the start. ExplorationI explored night city and the badlands thoroughly and loot can be found on pretty much every corner, although most of it is ‘junk items’ (which can be turned into crafting components). On occasion you can find legendaries hidden around the world, which is a nice touch. You can also find bits and pieces of stories as you explore. For example: you found a body from someone who jumped off a bridge and he has a ‘lore book’ on him explaining why he jumped. And later in the game you could find the other side of that story. Not everything is worth reading from these stories, but some are funny references or give more depth to the world. MusicThe OST is really good and immerses you into the scenes. The songs on the radio are hit or miss, depending on your music taste. The music is good enough that I’ve added some of the songs to the playlist I listen to often. BugsThis game has a lot of bugs, some of which are now fixed with the 1.2 update. I’ve played from release and I have not really encountered too much game breaking bugs. Mostly low level bugs like t-posing, people walking through solid objects and other weird interactions in gameplay. The only two big bugs I had was one questline being completely locked off (which was then fixed in 1.1) and one quest not starting at all (which fixed itself after a while for some reason). While that did feel incredibly bad at the time, I’m glad they fixed it because if they didn’t this review would have a very different tone. I do realize that not everyone’s playthrough will be like this, so liking this game really depends on your tolerance for bugs. ConclusionCyberpunk 2077 has many flaws but also some aspects that come close to ‘masterpiece’ quality. It’s really sad to see that this game didn’t have enough time to cook and was probably pushed out of the door too quickly. We all wanted and expected the game they promised, but it’s just not there yet. Perhaps with the free dlc’s and patches it will reach that level, but we shall see. That being said, I thoroughly enjoyed my playthrough and will probably do another one in the future. 8/10, would play again.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start with this mess. Cyberpunk 2077 is a very good game and setting that was butchered with wrong decisions at every turn. The story, the setting, the characters and the narrative are all top notch. Problem is, the game does not do it's story and setting justice. It starts insanely good story-wise but as you get near the end you feel that this is a very, very rushed game. Game-play wise it is super fun too, playing around with augmentations and iconic weapons feel incredibly satisfying. The problem starts with everything else. You have this incredible setting with amazing characters but you do so little with them it just does not make any sense. Your role-playing options are pretty limited (although you don't notice it till the middle of the game because of the characters and incredible voice-acting on everyone's part) and the plot is pretty linear  despite all the interesting possibilities laid out by the setting. What good is an incredible, lore filled and amazing looking setting if you can't interact with it meaningfully? Not to mention the bugs and performance issues, I really really wish they were honest with us and delayed this game until it was truly finished without promising all those big lies and not played with customer expectations by promising stuff and delaying all the same. If I judged this game by it's setting, Night City, characters and story alone? This would be one of the best damn games ever made. However as it stands it is only a 7-8 out of 10, which is still fine but nowhere near what it could have been. It truly is sad that the setting Mike Pondsmith has created with love and care was not given the opportunity to reach it's full potential. Shame but what can you do eh? Well, Night City - good night and good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitating to write a positive review for this game. I went into this with every expectation for it to be a mess. I was surprised with a game that asks the right questions. A game that knows to throw the right punches at your emotions. The gameplay is surprisingly well polished for the RPG genre, and doesn't put you into loading screens or flip through multiple  menus very frequently. The game is beautiful, if a little buggy in its current state; it could use optimization patches but even on my 2017 budget rig it runs just fine. The game puts you into the shoes of V, a mercenary with a wish to become a living legend in Night City. This journey has many twists and turns, none of it easy for them, but worth it maybe. Some of this journey is sad as hell. Some of it, V experiences pure joy. Whatever happens, this game makes you truly care for V. When V is happy, you're happy. When V is sad, you're sad. When V is scared, you're scared. Cyberpunk 2077 ranks as one of the very few games that has made me cry tears of sorrow, or of any kind. I can count how many games have that impact on me on one hand. If you're a fan of open world sandboxes, of RPGs, of story driven games, than I can absolutely recommend Cyberpunk 2077 even in it's buggy launch state. It's bugs are much less gamebreaking than even the bugs that STILL exist in Bethesda games to this day. Some of this game's criticisms are absolutely true and worth mentioning. But truthfully, some of them are massively blown out of proportion and some based on untruths. This is a game you have to really play for yourself to get a solid opinion on.

_childDocuments_.review: Vast game with lots to explore, but it has some downfalls. Currently, the game just game out and there was two updates, one of which fixed performance with Ray Tracing and demanding settings. Unnoticeable with Low to High. Going over the cons first, there is no way to rebind keys such as the activation key and keys you actually want to be set aren't allowed, that is the major gripe I have with game. The dodging is jank at times, double tap movement keys to dodge, where a modifier should be implemented. AI can be less stupid. And the driving is just ok, good enough to be bearable on keyboard. I would opt for an "alternative" way of control like in the Witcher for Geralt, but for cars. Last thing I found, the ending, where you get locked out of side missions, poor choice. Maybe we could get a New Game Plus mode?Now on to the pros. THE WORLD IS AMAZING! Key word is "explore" in this game, go down every alley, check out what's going on in Japantown, truly an immersive experience. The story really hooks you and not one character is boring. Even the side missions feel like you're contributing to world and the people you know. Gameplay wise, it checks off all the boxes of a common RPG and great gun play with the FPS elements. Although it's not too complex, it does it right. Perks and stats actually matter in the higher difficulty levels, so I'd recommend playing at Hard to Very Hard to get the full experience. You may flatline a couple times more, but it's worth it.All in all, even after the mixed reviews and gripe with bugs or gameplay, it's a game worth having in your library. Most of the cons will probably be fixed post launch week, and there's nothing truly bad about the game or things that can't be fixed with patches. The game is one BIG movie Choomba.Cyberpunk isn't supposed to be groundbreaking, it's supposed to be breathtaking. And it definitely achieves that.

_childDocuments_.review: After many, many attempts at meddling with the graphics, triple-checking on my system specs and so on, I finally was able to make the game work... which was a letdown in more ways than one, given this is CDPR and we were used to the masterpiece The Witcher 3 was. We WERE lied to, we did NOT get the game we were promised and the game itself had (and still has) so many bugs that, even if they didn't render the game unplayable, they made the experience somewhat bothersome and incredibly annoying at times.However, what they did right they did beautifully. The whole environment FEELS like the old Cyberpunk RPG and many of the dialogue, in-game text and interface were designed with care. Clothing designs are beautiful yet limited... and sometimes you have to dress with horrible outfit combinations just to get the best stats or slots to get certain advantages. I guess that was one reason to keep the game in first person instead of offering a third person perspective.Having Keanu Reeves join the ride was quite marvelous and the story in itself is fantastic, with plenty of side missions and gigs that make you get into the role of hero, merc, edgerunner and even anti-hero. The characters you find and play alongside with are top notch and deliver their own set of interesting stories to add to the fold. What about now? Well, the game is still riddled with bugs even with the 1.2 patch (28.8 gigs long, mind you). They fixed a TON of stuff but broke others that weren't even an issue before. It's like those delays on the release date fixed nothing and even now, the game feels more like a beta than an actual finished game. There are a TON of perks and like 30+ of them don't work or are plain stupid (I'm looking at you, knife perks). Others just don't work with other weapons even though the tooltip never says they shouldn't... and those that supposedly should just don't work properly either. I bought the game to make a point. To make my words about the state of the game have meaning. No, Cyberpunk 2077 is NOT a game I'd yet recommend... but I am hoping and crossing my fingers for the corpos and devs at the top of CDPR to get their heads out of their ass and actually fix this game and make it the experience it should have been since the beginning. 4/10 - A good story does not excuse a broken game.They added a patch on February 2022. I now can't even play the game (crash to Desktop). Once again, disappointed. What the hell is the matter with you, CDPR?

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? There is a lot to like in this game but at the same time a lot to hate. The main story is great, it has a nice spread of characters, and there are some really engaging and fun side quests. But the world feels lifeless, empty, and a lot of the activities in that world feel meaningless and repetitive. There is a lot of potential. A lot of it is wasted because of brainless AI, and a lack of simulation. Police just spawns in around you, at times you can see them pop into the world. No car chases, since there is no AI for that. It happens only in scripted sequences. In the race missions if you are too fast, it will spawn in your opponents behind you.  Your car spawns in very close to you, sometimes your vehicle will spawn under another vehicle and catapult it miles away. The quickhacking/netrunning game play isn't that enjoyable, and it's not clear how to get some of the more fun hacks at all. You definitely do not get them in a natural way, instead the best way to obtain them is to farm a group of NPC's that respawn after walking away 10ft. Your apartment although slowly becoming decorated with reminders of your achievements, which is a big plus, feels hollow and useless. There is no benefit from sleeping, and you can craft anywhere. And unlike the impression many people had, you cannot own any different housing then the one you start with. This game is also very buggy, graphical issues, the pop in is terrible even on high settings on a beefy rig, things pop in right in-front of your face. Missions and gigs that get bugged and won't finish, or won't unless you do something contrived. But it is still an enjoyable experience, just not the experience we wanted, what we wished for, and that was promised. And ultimately there is a lot of filler content in this game, and you have to go looking for the enjoyable content.I wish I could recommend this game, but with the issues that plague it, the optimisation, and the bugs, I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely relate heavily with the game, as I too am wasted potential... Take my advice, pretend the game got delayed for another year and wait.Seriously. I could write down pages and pages of hilarious bugs I've personally seen, not to mention the dozens and dozens of videos I've watched online. These hopefully will be patched over time, but the sad thing is even then the game might just be 'decent'. Some core mechanics and gameplay systems are just so broken/barebones, it will take a miracle to fix in my opinion. Horrendus AI, mediocre stealth, gangs / police interactions exist in the simplest form imaginable, etc. It's just so disappointing when comparing them to much older games like RDR2. Of course, it's not all bad. Night city is master crafted and a beautiful game world, and I personally think the characters are interesting (some may disagree). _childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of people forget that the Witcher 3 had bugs and optimization problems fresh off the checkout line, like pretty much EVERY AAA game and if you're a gamer, you know this and expect this. If you want a 100% flawless run, you 're going to have to wait a few weeks into release to give the devs time to patch things up- this is known (this is the way) and if you're acting surprised, then you're out of touch with reality and your expectations were ridiculously high. That said, I personally LOVE the game so far, excluding the few bugs I've come into contact with (which, again, should be EXPECTED). It is a gorgeous game aesthetic wise- if your hardware is dated, you'll need to turn down shadows and accept the fact you can't see it the way it was meant to be seen- just because you meet minimum specs doesn't mean you should still be able to see every detail- all it means is that it is "playable". I am currently playing the female version of V and love her attitude- the voice acting of all characters is actually really great. The NPCs are at least as dynamic as they were in Witcher 3, if not more-so, they have conversations of thier own off to the side, they all pretty much have different looks (I've not outwardly noticed copy-paste civilian NPCs walking about), and all of them are different shapes- I was stoked for some reason at seeing a large woman NPC- it's not something that gets included in many games and that is a wonderful detail, however small. IMO, the environment is interesting and I'm satisfied on that front.Gameplay wise, it is kinda like RDR2 and Fallout 4 had a baby (I don't think it is like GTA much at all). Most of the combat is typical the "shoot em up". I'm not very impressed with the stealth, mainly because of some bugs that allow enemies and cameras to spot you behind walls of other rooms, so this may improve after those things get  fixed. But honestly, combat mechanics aren't much different from other games of similar genres, aaaand I wasn't expecting they would be? Who would expect anything more? I don't get some of the reviews complaining about the combat when the trailers showed you exactly what it was??? Overall, I'm enjoying myself. I'm excited to play more, especially once the bugs get worked out. I'm excited to replay V with other backstories. I'm excited about any future DLC and updates. I'm satisfied and think CDPR met well on their promises to the fanbase- I think a lot of people are being way too hard on it fresh out the door because they're bitter about how long it took for the game to release. If we exclude the bugs- game so far gets an 8.5/10 from me, at least. Again, if you want a flawless playthrough, obviously wait a bit to invest in the game. If you think you can enjoy yourself and stand the few reloads due to bugs then try the game. Make your own opinion unhindered by emotionally butthurt perfectionists. Or do. I'm not your mom.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is buggy, what do you expect? A completely flawless game? (we all know those exist).  It's a newly released game with a massive open world that has a lot of detail - and potential. In it's current state, it's buggy. And do I feel they kept all their promises? No. But, this game is honestly a lot of fun: the major problem is that people had expectations that were just too high and as such, they were heavily disappointed. And honestly, I've not actually seen as many bugs as I'd expected (not saying there isn't a lot, it's just I've only seen a couple with what I've played so far). Not only that but people complained and complained, whined and cried because CDPR kept delaying it: so they released it. And now people are complaining because it's not finished... boo fricken hoo.  And another thing i heard is that enemies are bullet sponges: if they take half your health in one shot, and you're having to load their head with all your lead, than you ain't a high enough level to fight them so come back later.  Am I saying this game is without it's flaws? Certainly not, it is no where near perfect, but has there even been a perfect game?  So yes, it is a good game. There's so much to do and explore, so many corners to peak at, so many roads to drive on, so many side quests to complete, and so many endings to see. I've heard people talk about its performance... of course you wont be able to play the game on high-ultra with raytracing on a f&*%^&* rtx 280 Sherlock. With that being said, my pc isnt great, but it runs well on mostly medium with 1-2 things on high (nvidia 1060 with fx-8350 processor). The world is a very interesting one, crafted with a lot of detail: I recommend this game, not for the state it's in right now, but for what it will turn to be in the future. Maybe give it a month or two to see how things are going with patches and overall development. If you wanna try it now, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: ⛧TL;DR 10/10 just get it play it don`t forget it⛧Cyberpunk 2077 is a landmark achievement in the realm of open-world RPGs, offering a deeply immersive and visually stunning experience. Set in the sprawling, neon-drenched metropolis of Night City, the game allows players to step into the shoes of V, a mercenary with a customizable skill set and appearance, navigating the gritty underworld of a cyberpunk future.The world-building in Cyberpunk 2077 is exceptional, with every street corner and high-rise brimming with details and life. The vibrant cityscape is populated with diverse NPCs, each contributing to the bustling atmosphere. The game’s visual fidelity, from the shimmering skyscrapers to the shadowy alleyways, is a feast for the eyes, making exploration a constant pleasure.The narrative is gripping, weaving a complex tale of power, corruption, and survival. Players can make meaningful choices that impact the story's direction and outcome, adding a layer of depth and replayability. The voice acting, especially from the protagonist V and other key characters, enhances the emotional weight of the story, drawing players deeper into the experience.Gameplay is highly versatile, offering a range of approaches to combat and problem-solving. Whether through stealth, hacking, or direct confrontation, players can tailor their playstyle to their preferences. The vast array of cybernetic upgrades, weapons, and skills ensures that no two playthroughs are the same, keeping the gameplay dynamic and engaging.Side missions and activities abound in Night City, each with its own unique flavor and rewards. These quests not only enrich the main storyline but also provide insights into the diverse cultures and factions within the city. The attention to detail in these side stories contributes to the overall sense of a living, breathing world.Cyberpunk 2077 excels in creating an atmospheric and engaging experience, pushing the boundaries of what is possible in an open-world RPG. Its combination of breathtaking visuals, intricate storytelling, and versatile gameplay makes it a standout title that offers countless hours of entertainment and immersion. For anyone looking to lose themselves in a richly crafted cyberpunk universe, this game is an absolute must-play.Watching Edgerunners might enhance your experience with the game through the roof.

_childDocuments_.review: If your PC can run it, play it. You'll definitely need a 20 series GPU or higher to enjoy the game, don't bother playing without one (as of launch week). The game is optimized TERRIBLY, and it's a shame because I'd truly love to take in the environment this game has to offer. Speaking of which, the map is by far the best map of any game I've ever played. I've never seen a larger, more detailed city in any other game. The story is just as good, it's like Fight Club (1999) in the future with a revenge story. Currently though the game is a buggy mess, but if you've played bethesda games then it's nothing you wouldn't be used to. I'll resume it, people wanted the game to be released already, they got what they wanted, a glitchy game and that's it.It's a buggy game even if I encounter few bugs, it's still a mess. Romance is meh, when you are done with the person, you are done with them, no bonus to the main story.Where the game disappointed me a lot is the lifepath, I thought I would have a different playthrought for like 15 hours or more but it's the SAME, only the 10min tutorial mission changes  and you gain extra dialogues. I wanted to play as CORPO, doing dirty mission, assassination and all but no... this is where the game trully failed. The story is good but, the problem is, they focused too much on it with Keanu Reeves. This should be like, the main story for kidstreet or other. But definitely not as a CORPO. The AI is also awful and the cops is just a big NO, they should have made the cops better or simply removing them at this point because it's a joke...Where the game did a masterpiece is Night City. Night City is beautiful, amazing, the best open world map you can have and I am being honest. This is where GTAV failed for me, an interesting open world because many parts in Los Santos is closed, and you have mostly only the road and streets to go. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the game at basically the 50 hour mark, did nowhere near all of the sidequests. The storytelling, characters, and etc. are all fantastic. There was not a moment where I wanted to skip dialogue, such as in the Witcher 3. I found the loot to be fine and RPG elements to be fine. I found the open world to be beautiful, and fun to explore. The voice acting was top notch, Keanu Reeves was a great addition and I love his character. The bugs were minimal, and none of them impacted the game severely. I found the gunplay to be great, which was my biggest concern; it feels heavy and full of impact, yet fluid. I do not understand the hate for this game. I think it is a solid 4.5/5 with the only deterring factors being the useless difficulty settings, bugs, and performance issues, and is definitely my game of the year for 2020. (FF7R being close behind)Performance: I have a 1070 and i5 6600K, old hardware, but runs all other AAA titles on low settings FINE. Except this game; when I get into the city and have to drive, I get 30fps (on low) and cannot even spin my camera around quickly without freeze-framing. It is an awesome game, and I will finish it even with the bugs and crap optimization. The fact that those are the only negatives so far for me prove this game is what I was expecting. Wait until patches, but if you can stomach bugs and low FPS, I recommend it now. 4.5/5 - Halo 2 was released with TONS of crunch and an entire half of a game cut, yet it is the greatest videogame ever created, Cyberpunk 2077 is nearly as gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it buggy? Fairly, yes.Is it optimized well? God no.Is it unplayable? Absolutely not.The problems with the technical side of the game are overshadowed by the incredible content that IS the game itself. The setting is gorgeous, gritty and sometimes too real. The things that fill this beautiful setting, the jobs, the story, the characters, all come together to make an incredible work of art that, at least to me, is now unmatched in its genre. It RARELY feels repetitive, and almost definitely requires multiple playthroughs to see the game in its entirety. It'll definitely be worth its value in content alone. However, like I said at the beginning, it isn't perfect. There are in fact game breaking bugs throughout that will require you to restart save points and play differently in order to progress. They are few and far between in my experience, and can be worked around, but in a "play it your way" type of game, that does become an issue. There are also places in Night City that absolutely TANK framerates simply due to the level of detail and the density of the population in those areas (The "Red-Light" area of Japan-Town comes to mind). Overall, though the game currently has problems on its technical side, the content itself is fantastic. Hopefully CDProjekt will come through with patches and fixes. I would have rather waited another 2 or 3 months for this game to have been more thoroughly tested, but what's done is done, and I definitely see this game going from "Great" to "Immaculate" once these glaring issues are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077, a game that sparked both anticipation and controversy, has undergone a transformative journey since its tumultuous launch. CD Projekt Red's commitment to improvement, along with the recent introduction of the new DLC, has elevated this cyberpunk epic into a gaming marvel.Pros:• Immersive Night City: The neon-soaked streets of Night City have never looked more captivating. The attention to detail is staggering, creating an immersive urban landscape that breathes life into the cyberpunk genre. From the bustling markets to the towering skyscrapers, every corner oozes with personality.• Compelling Narrative: The storyline in Cyberpunk 2077 is a cyberpunk enthusiast's dream. The intricate plot, rich character development, and moral ambiguity make for a narrative that keeps you on the edge of your seat. Choices matter, and the consequences ripple through the city, shaping your experience in profound ways.• Anime Aesthetics: The infusion of anime influences in Cyberpunk 2077 is a stroke of genius. The vibrant colors, futuristic fashion, and the overall aesthetic nod to the cyberpunk anime genre, creating a visually stunning experience that feels like stepping into a cyberpunk anime.• Gameplay Evolution: The addition of the new DLC brings a breath of fresh air to the gameplay. The expanded content introduces compelling missions, characters, and gear, enhancing the overall experience. It's a testament to the developers' dedication to not only fixing the issues but also expanding and evolving the game.Cons:• Technical Hurdles (at Launch): The game's initial technical issues were well-documented, impacting the experience for many players. However, the substantial improvements through patches and updates have largely addressed these concerns.• High System Requirements: To fully appreciate the game's beauty, a robust gaming system is required. While this may be a drawback for some, it's understandable given the ambitious nature of the game.In conclusion, Cyberpunk 2077 has emerged from its turbulent launch as a shining example of game development resilience. The infusion of anime aesthetics and the recent DLC showcase CD Projekt Red's commitment to delivering a cyberpunk experience like no other. With these advancements, Cyberpunk 2077 earns a well-deserved 10/10, solidifying its place as a definitive title in the cyberpunk gaming genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The wait has been long, but Cyberpunk 2077 is finally out. Ever since the first gameplay showcase, I’ve been excited for the day I would play this game. There’s no doubt I’m not the only one. With every day that passed, people’s expectations grew. Many expected this game to be unlike no other - some even claimed that it would be the best game ever made. The reality is that Cyberpunk 2077 released in a rough patch. The game is filled with bugs and glitches, but is there more to it than that?  is not a feel-good game. It tells the story of a world obsessed so much with technological advancement that it forgot about everything else. Cyberpsychosis and high crime rates are only a few of the problems this world faces. Our story takes place in , a metropolis famous for its industrial prowess. It’s no utopia, however; the divide between rich and poor is bigger than ever. Everyone has dreams, but in Night City, only a few realize them. The rest are left to the struggle of survival on the streets; some as gang members, others as lone mercenaries. This is where you come in. Playing as , you begin as either a nomad, street kid or corporate employee. Unfortunately, this choice isn’t as pivotal as it may seem. No matter your choice, you’ll eventually end up as a mercenary. But it must have an impact later on, you think. While you unlock certain dialogue choices depending on which life path you chose, their impact ranges from a snippet of additional dialogue to a unique approach, which still doesn’t change the outcome of a quest.Don’t worry, though. There are plenty of choices to make in Night City. However, there are also plenty of illusions of them. Often, you’ll be offered multiple dialogue options, which in no shape or form affect the outcome of a story. That’s not to say that Cyberpunk offers no altering outcomes whatsoever - they’re definitely here. However, they are not as frequent as in many other RPGs. It feels like  had a story they want to tell, and it’s that of a character  not one  created. Luckily, this story is brilliant.If any game has heart, it’s Cyberpunk 2077. Few games present characters as believable as the ones in this game. They act, think and talk like real people - their motivations make sense. There are no comic book villains here. Neither are there any heroes. When pushed far enough, a human being is willing to do just about anything; the writers know this, and they execute the concept damn well.Now that we’ve talked about the story, it’s time to focus on the part which caught me by surprise: the gameplay. It doesn’t do anything new, but offers a refined RPG experience. Innovation is important, but not every game needs to be something completely new. Sometimes, we want more of the same. Cyberpunk 2077 is exactly that, and maybe a bit more. You have many ways of approaching each situation. Cyberpunk employs a series of systems for the player to navigate and sometimes even exploit. Hacking was my favorite aspect of the gameplay. It revolves around , programs which can be uploaded to enemies. These come at the cost of , a limited resource which regenerates over time. There’s a good selection of them, and they offer different tactical usages.  can temporarily blind an enemy, allowing you to pass by unseen. Some also allow you to damage enemies, such as  which poisons them. You can also execute a , which allows you to upload daemons to a local network. For an RPG, Cyberpunk 2077’s gunplay is great and took me by surprise. During the opening hours, I had mixed impressions, as every enemy was a bullet sponge; as such, the gunplay felt unresponsive. However, as V grows stronger, the tides turn. As for the selection, each gun belongs to one of three types: .  allow your bullets to ricochet off walls - quite troublesome for your enemies. The  can be charged to release a magnetically-accelerated shot, and their bullets can penetrate lighter objects. Lastly, the  are Cyberpunk’s way of accounting for less skilled players. They shoot bullets which will track your enemies. Finally, you can also use melee weapons. Slicing off limbs is as bloody and enjoyable as you’d expect, but the actual melee combat is rough around the edges. The style is there, but it lacks substance. Overall though, I had a blast with Cyberpunk’s gameplay. The AI could use some work, though, as it’s quite dumb.Cyberpunk’s best side quests are as three-dimensional as its characters.  The real reward is not the money and street cred you get for finishing jobs - it's the experiences. I didn't pursue jobs because I had to; I did it because I wanted to.  offer combat-focused scenarios where you infiltrate locations. While it’s told mainly through text logs, these include storytelling as well. You can also take on jobs from the police, which are the equivalent of bandit camps. Finally, there are  These are the type of quests that made  so special; they tell rich stories, which rival the plot of the main narrative. Sadly, there are not as many of these as I would’ve liked. There’s a high number of gigs, but while I liked them, they’re not as compelling as the well-written plots of the side jobs. The main story is also short, but it's of excellent quality.Let’s talk about something that’s not short in length, though. With a soundtrack nearly 5 hours long, Cyberpunk’s soundtrack spans many genres and styles, showing the full capacity of Night City’s culture. Speaking of Night City, it’s absolutely gorgeous; Cyberpunk is among one of the most graphically impressive games ever made, with stunning textures and amazing lighting. | 1440p  Despite the myriad of technical issues, I enjoyed my time in Night City. Cyberpunk 2077 has many interesting stories to tell, and it’s not afraid to touch on darker subjects. With its believable characters and well-paced narrative, I was never bored while playing the game. There are more reasons to play it, though; the gameplay is surprisingly good for an RPG, and the visuals are simply breathtaking. It would be smart to wait, but if you’re eager to experience what the dark future has to offer, I can recommend buying the game - if your PC is good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I waited until I'd completed the game to write this.I've heard about the bugs and crashes, and I didn't experience that many. The AI is a bit dumb, the cars aren't great to drive, and controls at times can feel clunky and unrefined.But you know what? It doesn't matter one little bit. The game and story are absolutely outstanding. The dialogue options you receive are brilliant, the characters are great and everything is so well written. The game looks stunning, even though I'm playing on an old 1070 at the moment. The music rivals that of Doom. And I don't say that gingerly. The radio music, the club music. Just great to listen to. And the ending. Oh man, the ending I chose, the music that follows that, with the credits and what happens in the credits just fit so well. Right in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ feels! Actually made me think about my teemage years, sitting playing the Dreamcast with a bunch of friends getting drunk and listening to all kinds of metal.Anyway, that's my view on this game. Some will like, some won't. Just you do you and see how you get on with it. This gets a big tick in the success box for me. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I happen to find the game enjoyable and entertaining. The character creation is fun as hell, the story is interesting, and the characters are well developed. There are some bugs but none that have ruined the game for me. It definitely seems like an early access game in terms of development but with Covid and shut downs I personally think this is understandable but I also understand if others do not. Also, make sure to look both ways before you cross the street!-Good story-Fun character creation-Good character development-Keanu Reeves-Beautiful graphics-Beautiful city design-Some quests/jobs are quite interesting-Minimap is easy to follow-You can summon your car (so convenient)-Lots of easter eggs from Witcher, Portal, Half life, etc.-I FOUND A CAT THAT COULD BE PET-Driving is kind of difficult-High gpu requirements-No ability to change appearance (other than clothing) after the character creator-Third person perspective only available when driving-Some romance options are gender dependent-You may find Keanu Reeves to be scary at times-Some parts of buildings that look like they can be jumped onto can't be (important if you plan on jumping on one to break your fall)-Motorcycles can randomly fly at you (it's as fun as it sounds) (if running over long distances, I think it's them loading in)-Motorcycles can also spawn on you (if running over long distances, I think it's them loading in)-Phone calls are buggy sometimes (getting two calls at once)-Dead bodies do weird things-Sometimes NPCs act dead (ragdoll) but still have a health bar and voice lines-Dead NPCs sometimes still talk-Some enemy NPCs get stuck in doorways or objects like dumpsters/cars (makes them easy to kill tho)-Some gunshot noises when no people are shooting-Some items just can't be picked up when you should be able to-The braindance bug - when you exit a braindance and you may still have the weird visual glitches from the braindance. I have learned to avoid this by going back to playback mode, finding a relatively normal looking portion of the view, and then exiting. You also can fix the visual glitch once you have it through going back to before you did the braindance and doing the above steps.

_childDocuments_.review: Needed another delay for about 3 months maybe but in just 3 days of release they made significant progress in stability, just gotta deal with the ugly graphics and rendering til things are smoothed out, stay strong samurais*Edit*After 3 playthroughs and a datamine of the game I thought I should include some notes to help whoever reads this on their purchaseMost dialogues (98%) have no impact on the story whatsoever. The vast majority of dialogue only changes the next line of dialogue and that’s it.Only a very small subset of dialogues (around 2% of all dialogues) actually have any impact whatsoever.You will always end up on the same linear story path with the same objectives and missions no matter what. Even if you go for the choices in this guide or not won’t change what missions you get. The game is much more linear than it seems.After discovering these I've changed my review to not recommended, not because it's necessarily a bad game (the writing is very good, the bugs may bring it down a little but CDPR has promised 2 major patches to fix the problems) but because what they promised and what they delivered are two majorly different things. Hope this helps in some way.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought RDR2 was a tragic game. But this is possibly an even more bleak and depressing story. You could easily make DLC about most of the characters. The VA and MOCAP are insane - characters actually move around the environment and have complex animations when interacting with them. There are certain dialogue choices that you can only get if you picked a specific "life path" at the beginning or depending on your past interactions. There is also something like 13 different endings.Great RPG, insane amounts of customization in terms of appearance, builds, abilities and even your apartments. There's 6 skill trees which give you different abilities to aid you in hacking or combat etc, then you also have the "Cyberware" and weapon upgrades - there is infinite possibilities. There is a lot of weapon variety, you have everything from blades, blunt weapons, throwing weapons, to every type of firearm. Each category of weapon has different types and each weapon has a level which can be upgraded, crafted or found in the world. There are "iconic" weapons which you get from certain characters or defeating bosses etc.Side missions use unique locations and in some cases are as good or better than main story ones. Some are a bit repetitive in terms of objective but the level design makes you consider different approaches depending on if you can hack your way in, use stealth or go guns blazing. The interiors are never boring, every locations had a completely different vibe.Combat is great. Whether you're using melee or mowing enemies down with a shotgun or using quickhacks to fry their brains and hack ♥♥♥♥, it's awesome; good gore and dismemberment. You also have a good selection of grenades and a variety of health items and upgrades.The music... THEY MADE OVER 150 TRACK SPECIFICALLY FOR THE GAME. AND ITS ACTUALLY GOOD.The game is not without flaws but I think a game or any piece of media is more than the sum of its parts.

_childDocuments_.review: In the future, global warming is real and everyone walks around in their underpants.My hours played is not an accurate reflection of gaming but instead reflect my rational fear of being unable to run the game again if I log off.RPG used to be Ultima or Bards Tale. Wizardry or Might and Magic. Pools of Radiance. Ultima Underworld and Bethesda’s Arena changed all that for me and we began a long, long happy journey leading to first person RPG combining action and some strategy. The Elder Scrolls universe has been the limelight – I loved Daggerfall and Morrowind. Love them all actually. Then somebody thought about guns. We need guns – more guns! Bring me guns.Original Wasteland was pretty good leading to Fallouts including the first person versions.So Cyberpunk is ready to play and when I think of RPG with guns I think about System Shock(s), Prey, Bioshock(s). So what to think?Cyberpunk is a game that you should not play in front of your mum or wife. It’s based on Sci-Fi universe similar to Akira, Blade Runner, and Judge Dread etc. The city is designed so well – those guys should get an award. If you close one eye you might even imagine you are in a real city based in current Asia. The sounds, the colours, the lights. It’s remarkable. But mostly smoke and mirrors I suspect.Your character is a lowly mercenary that is given a chance to hit the big time. We have a good character design system with excellent stats and skills. The flexibility here is pretty good. However, missions will all require combat with rarely if ever the chance to resolve through dialogue. No intimidation here. No meaningful speech checks. The assassin/ sneak build is possible but lacking proper mechanics, although there are bins everywhere and options to take people out without killing them.It does not feel as satisfying as Dishonoured for example.Once I got off the floor and escaped from stunned silence the city is your oyster. You can travel around doing missions as you please dipping into the main mission as you like. It feels a bit like Fallout 4 where you need to rescue your son but end up stealing some chips for some meagre cash.There is a disconnect here with the main story. How to balance urgent story timelines against our need to explore the world. The problem off course is that although our character exists in the world, it’s our first time. The game is open world and it follows many of the rules already set by its predecessors.A million icons on the map. More missions and loot than you can handle. Gameplay mechanics to exploit. Different builds to explore. Places to go. Homes to buy. Cars to drive. Romance to be had…One of the best aspects of the game is much of it is experienced through the engine where you are the boss. Cut scenes are rarely done in frozen sets. You can still walk away or look around. It helps keep the immersion of living in the city alive.After a while I began to suspect the developers bit more than they could chew. Promised more than they could deliver. Spent a lot of time and energy making their homework presentable…One thing they did get right is the path finding. I suppose they had to noting the complexity of the city. In Witcher 1 and 2 it was dire. Here it is almost perfect. Fantastic achievement and thanks.For a RPG, the choices and consequences are there at the end but barely during the game. Although the missions are varied enough – they are mostly combat. Even the key people you meet along the way feel one dimensional. Some interesting people are killed off too early and it makes you wonder if that was lazy or if the story is just forced on you…The star of the open world is the city design but don’t look too closely. The million shops have nothing to sell. The million people have nothing to say. It’s just not real…in the same way Skyrim or Oblivion was. In those games people had routines, missions. Even the invisible people could talk to you going way back to Daggerfall or Morrowind.I get it. Cyberpunk is grand. Impossible to create routines for a million people. It’s a good sign I suppose on what technology could achieve with more processor power.The main story itself is pretty individualistic and in the end the main story might not even about you. I hoped it would link back to your life path chosen at the beginning of the game but it does not. I would have liked to see more interaction with the giant corporations that run this city and world but there is hardly anything there.Although the Cyberpunk universe is pretty interesting, raising issues about humanity, technology and corporations, the main story only takes a peek. In the end you are just another soul in the city. You might get a drink named after you.Another update or DLC might just push this into a very good game. Just some tidying up needed. Stats on the cars available in game. Face to face interactions with key people in every part of the city – such as the fixers. Some tangible storylines linked to your life path rather than the odd irrelevant dialogue choices. An explanation of some of the games systems and mechanics. A reputation system might work wonders…On some level it does feel a lot like the Far Cry or Tomb Raider games. That is a shame.In terms of stability – the game crashes a lot and it makes me mad. I have never sent so many bug reports to developers. Almost every time I play I need to go through a now customary at least two crashes on last saved game loading screen. I hate the game needs to catch up to your movement around the map and sometimes it can’t.In summary, fully recommended. Don’t buy it at full price. The developers might get some credit but they started doing their homework too late and should have got an A grade rather than a B-
