_childDocuments_.review: Damn awesome game :)Enjoy Night City!---Okay, this game deserves a better review:- Good writing and narration of the story. The plot progresses when you want it to progress, if you want to do other things, no problem. Also no constant action, there are times when you just drink beer in a motel and that's immersive. You build friendship, you explore the world - that part was done very nicely.- Combat is satisfactional. There is decent amount of guns to choose from and they all fall from one of categories. There are weapons that ricochet, penetrate though walls, auto-aim enemies... pick your poison. The only problem with combat is that if you want to have action... you need to look for it. Gangs are not hostile from start, so you need to find a group and pick a fight. And because they are neutral towards you, a frag to their feet makes them explode in a second - where is fun with that? I would like to see more gang-wars areas, where the constant action is happening. Now we have random events where some people are fighting police or other gangs, but that's something you have to find and not always is at hand. But that's only a problem when you are really blood-thirsty, usually those random events are enough to satisfy (at least me) and move forward with whatever I'm doing in the game.And I must say that the immersion from picking a new weapon and watching the "prepere to fire-up" animation is just great!- Stealth is okay, I guess. Hacking is a nice tool helping you with it, beucase at first you can hack devices in the area to distract opponents, allowing you to pass. Later on you can make them blind, what kinda feels like invisiblity from deus ex - but hey, those are the tools. The only problem with sneaking is... level design. Most location that encourage you to play stalthy have 70% of enemies turned by their back to you, making the whole experience super easy and not rewarding. Not all locations are like that, but quite a few.- World is not as populated as on first trailers, but that depends on location. There are crowdy areas (in mega-blocks or marketplaces), but some are rather empty (outskirts of the city). That option can be also changed in settings, I play on max and can't really complain much on density of population. - I'm not a dedicated driver, I haven't played in any racing game since childhood, but I must say that I have fun while driving though Night City. Faster cars are obviously much harder to control, not to mention how hard is to stop the car from full speed to zero, but hey, that's part of having the fast car :). At first I was mostly fast-traveling, but I quickly noticed that there is a lot going on in the city - and that content would be missed if travelling that way. - Bugs are there, but bugs can and probaby will be fixed. I was able to beat the game without any major problem, so that's something. Nowadays almost every game on Day 0 is released in less or more buggy state and while I don't defend CD PROJECT here - I think the game is in good enough condition to be playable. On previous release date it was obviously much worse :P- There are TONS of content in terms of world-building. Many articles, textbooks, emails or text-messeges left here and there for you to explore. There is the internet - and websites are changing as you progress though the quests, so that's a nice addition.- Flesh-modification is a nice addition, but I think it could be explore further. In comparison to Deus-Ex I believe Deus-Ex comes on top. Here we have mostly passive-bonuses, apart of legs and arms modification, I don't believe there are many active-actions to be unlocked here. That's a bit dissapointing.There are more aspects of the game I haven't talk about, but I don't have a whole day for it :) Go and expore, you won't regreat it. Singleplayer games are definitely not dead :)For now: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Man where do I begin. Let me start by saying I'm 56 hours in and yet to finish the game. The main story is awesome and engaging, some NPCs are really likable, there are awesome side quests and little easter eggs, fun things to find like skippy the smart gun. smart guns and netrunning are fun and refreshing, almost watchdogs like. Combat is good for an RPG.Now the bad part tho is it's hardly an RPG and not at all what we were promised. You don't really define V, he's a predefined character with a dream of becoming a night city legend and he acts solely in that way, it's not your character. Getting to pick your peepee isn't defining your character.We were promised a next level immersive open world RPG where you get to define who you are and how you approach the game. Literally none of it is true. Let me start with the AI or rather lack of thereof. The civilians just run a few feet and duck in the open till the end times. If you shoot a vehicle they just do nothing, don't even attempt to drive away just freeze in place and that's it. The driving AI though, damn that's a whole nother level of bad. I've parked my car on the sidewalk with only like a feet sticking out on the actual road and there formed a huge traffic jam cause of it. The hostile mobs are not perhaps as dumb as some games out there but not the brightest either, certainly nothing next gen about it. The scripted scenes are all on rails, like Jackie driving you the car is literally not driving. The opponent vehicles are all driving along a predefined path and nothing you can do will change it. Shooting NPCs in car chases stuns them at best, you can't kill them, shoot their tires or anything. But that's not as bad as NPC pathing during scripted scenes, try parking a vehicle in their predefined path and they'll clip straight through it. Character creation isn't really as good either, there are no sliders to make your character fat, muscular or short. Cosmetic cyberware is extremely limited. There's no way to modify your looks outside of character creation, which in a cyberpunk game where body modifications are a prime focus is just lazy. Functional Cyberware is also extremely limited and bland. The live megabuildings we were promised, well there are only a couple you can enter and all of them are 1 or 2 stories only.Unique NPC's with full day/night cycles and reactions to your actions literally spawn/despawn behind your back, the same thing with vehicles. The whole vertical build seems to be a huge scam too. Like there are roof tops and multi level streets but that's about it. You can hardly enter any buildings.The immersive features are severely lacking. - There are only a few vendors with only interaction with them being 'got some eddies to burn'. - NPCs have no inventories. - The loot drops like its some hack'n'slash game with most of it being junk. - There are no factions or karma systems. - There's no item ownership, you can literally wipe everything clean and no one gives the slightest. - There are no police chases, you can move 1 block away and all your crimes against humanity are forgiven. - Most the side content is just go there kill every bad guy get your eddies. - There are no dynamic encounters, once you clear an area it's safe and empty till the end of the game. - You can't sit on mostly anything outside scripted scenes and your apartment. - There are no containers that aren't loot chests. - The consumables are junk, there's no animation for any of that and the effects mean little. - There's only one uncustomizable apartment in the entire game. - There's no garage or car customization, you can own vehicles but they just spawn when you want them to and you can only get them in a predefined color and configuration. - The quick travel isn't a train or public transport, it's just a click this holo map and teleport. - There's very little to do in the game world outside of quests in general. The only thing this game lived up to is the Cyberprank 2077 meme. So overall if you want a fun game with a good story and decent combat, go for it. If you expected a next gen immersive world where you could sink hundreds of hours without even touching the main story, this isn't it.Edit: 1.5 made this game infinitely better. It's now somewhat of a GTA in a cyberpunk setting with more customization/RP in some places and less in others. Hoping the DLCs will eventually make the game awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only that the game was overhyped, but broken from the start.Given the time and resources CD Projekt Red had It's a shame how they ruined the release of the game.It can be improved with bug fixes and optimization but even that won't be enough because disregarding the fancy graphics, the game feels like it's from a decade ago.The main story is good, can be very enjoyable but it's way too short and the side missions with the other gigs are random an generic.Yeah you can trigger several endings but they aren't really that different from each other and your choises doesn't have such a weight and impact on the world as it was promised.Speaking of graphics earlier, you can't even play the game on a stable 60fps with the current top of the line PC build on maxed out settings.And if you are an average user like myself who has a decent enough setup to play most of the games (not everything maxed out),then you'll barely have 30-40 fps (if you are lucky) on lower-medium settings and the game will look almost terrible.I do hope they will fix most of the bugs in the future and optimize the performance because the game it self good and has a lot of potential.I could recommend this game but you should definitely wait for future patches AND a sale. (seriously, the game in today's state isn't worth it's price.)Update:Two years later after I had completed the game, I have decided to give this game another try with a calm, open mindset and a new rig.Threating this game as it is (not an RPG), I dare to say that this is a quite solid game that I had a lot of fun playing.The game is now well optimized and preforms 3 times better than it did at launch, even with the same specs, they added many quality of life updates, better icons and some of the basic things such as customizing your hair / character in game. (wow… almost as if this should have been in the game since its release.)Most of the bugs were fixed and those which were not are far rarer to see.The only reason I’m keeping the review as “negative” is because, in spite of the game is getting better with the updates, this is never going to be the game that we were promised and I refuse to gaslight myself from the fact how terrible the launch of this game was…Otherwise, If you know what to expect, it’s worth to get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a year to finish this game because I kept getting pissed off while playing it (finished it a couple of days ago from writing this review). So you have over 180h in it, why do you still not recommend it? Because this game is the dictionary definition of edging and then leaving you with blue balls. I really, really wanted to like it but I was hit with disappointment after disappointment. The good: - it's a beautiful game design wise- it has some memorable side-quests that I really liked - shooting is ok I guess - nice OST/ sound design- cool that you can call you car/ bike and you access them anytime- I actually liked the variety in endings, and could say the depressing one is my favoriteThe bad:- choices don't matter, this is not an RPG as it's advertised- as beautiful as it is, it's just an empty world and you never get immersed because you are walking on the street and next to you there are 7 NPC clones that look the same- Johnny is the most annoying side character/companion I've had the displeasure to spend the time with. Keanu's work in general is fine, but his VA for this game is probably one of his worst performances (the writing doesn't help either). He always sounds like an edgy teen that's about to fall asleep and bored out of his mind. I wish they hired a proper game VA for this role and spent more time on developing the Johnny character since he's so integral to the story.- the thing that made me rage quit this game is a very tiny detail and that's the car AI. Imagine me standing on the road while other cars are driving and they just run you over all the time no matter what. I remember that even in GTA San Andreas the cars would stop if they were driving at low speed and noticed you, but here no matter what you will get your ass dragged for 10m. I was even run over by a hologram car from a Panam mission that was also programmed as a solid car. - can't customize your character, there's no use for your apartment as a base, you look like a bald starfish when swimming- enemies' bodies would fall through the floor and explode which gave me multiple heart attacks while playing stealth- getting spammed 24/7 with messages from characters to buy their vehiclesYes, I have over 180h in this game because I preordered it and never refunded in hope they would fix it. It's the first time I ever preordered a game, and judging by the way this release was handled it's also the last time I preorder a game. I really, really, reaaaaaaaally wanted to like it so I tried to see all it has to offer. Call me a clown if you will for persisting in playing. Buy it only on sale if you really want to try it and didn't have the expectations set by the team through their marketing from all the years of development. Maybe if I hadn't followed it since its first teaser, I wouldn't have been so salty about it but it is what it is. You might enjoy it a lot if you go in without expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk is grand, ambitious, and bloated. I initially stayed away from it because I heard it rolled off the assembly line straight into a dumpster fire, nowadays it appears much more stable but still has a lot of jank. At best it could be described as a flawed masterpiece, at worst you could say it gets crushed under it's own weight. I need to quickfire a lot of points, so TLDR: Cyberpunk is still messy, but perfectly playable. Visually striking, great audio, generally good but sometimes bloated/incomprehensible story. Combat has many ways to break it, but playing above normal difficulty can sometimes end up breaking YOU. Some annoying bugs decrease enjoyment, but overall worth a recommendation if you can stomach the jank.Visual/Audio:-Visually amazing, I thought this would make for fantastic VR title. So much so that it could consistently trigger my discomfort with dirty urban environments. The cities & story areas definitely got the most attention and are gorgeous, while others didn't. Case in point: Japantown & it's associated festival segment, the digital/cyberspace scenes & Judy's dive are all major highlights in my mind-Audio is generally really good, again much more so in the urban environments with hand-crafted advertisements and the everyday traffic sounds. Lots of really memorable dialogue moments where you just sit/interact with people and talk. The voice acting really carries most of these scenes. Two distinct bugs involved a persistent "shivering" sound long after some missions with ice baths, and a more frequent one involving the hostile hack sound playing long after all enemies are dealt withGameplay:-Trans character options are appreciated, I played a futanari girl because I could. Functionally doesn't do anything but nice for RP-Difficulty is completely janked. Normal had me effortless bullet-sponging while hard had me constantly dying in 2-5 hits,  many times instantly. A lot of lategame basic enemies were more dangerous than bosses-They added outfit presets so you don't have to go around dressed like a clown because your combat stats demanded it. You permanently keep items in your wardrobe even after you've sold them. Though not a ton of variety IMO, I found a lot of variations on dirty street gear, but nothing in the way of swimsuits and sandals-Braindance segments are fun and consistently creative-Driving apparently used to be super slippery, now the opposite seems to be true in that crashes are merely suggestions & not actual rules. I've been run over by a semi truck as a character with paper-thin endurance and lost no health. Cars are clunky but motorcycles are really fun & zippy, I bought the admittedly expensive Akira-inspired bike early on (despite the game giving you two others for free) & never looked back-Surprising amount of optional pacifism: I went into Cyberpunk after a sudden urge to play a pacifist-style Deus Ex game, and weirdly this one delivered. Quickhacks are largely non-lethal & there's a few options to make guns the same-However, with that previous point in mind, there's virtually nothing in the way of persuasion in this game, at best you can temporarily defer a fight from one faction to immediately go start one with another. Despite that, there's also an extremely robust background system that gave me unique Corporate dialogue choices through the entire length of this game's runtime, along with skill checks reminiscent of Fallout NV-Inventory management and crafting are major pains due to excessive amounts of items, not helped by interfaces being unintuitive-Lots of character builds and ways to break combat, with several options per skill tree. Some are distinctly better, the good ones will have both combat & utility options in the same tree. I'm a tank/juggernaut player at heart, this game did the unthinkable and had me play as a semi-stealth hacker-Cyberpunk has the most busted, versatile and useful system hacking system I've ever seen in a game. With full investment you're basically a walk apocalypse, lots of missions can just be deactivated by instantly nuking groups of enemies. God help them if you can infiltrate a camera system-Quickfire on other skills: Body gives you soldier/brawler skills, health and endurance-based augments... I needed to invest more in this Reflexes for snipers, SMGS & pistols, mantis blades, time-slowing Sandevistan augments... I used this for secondary pistol-SMG damage. Silenced revolvers and Malorian Arms 3516's badass reload animations make this tree worthwhileTechnical ability for hacking pre-requisites, crafting/engineering... by far my biggest regret skill-wise. Went in looking for ways to shore up defence, ended up wasting a ton of time & resources for basically no result. Only semi-useful for skill checksIntelligence for all things quickhack related... best tree in the game handsdown, everything here is self-contained and you could go the entire game having only invested in this one tree. Choose this, become a cybernetic godCool gives various buffs for kills... I never bothered with this but maybe should have. Can't decide if going for body or this would have helped my survivability Story:-The trailers pretty much exactly spell out how the prologue of the game's going to play out. I hadn't actually seen any of them beyond clips of Johnny's entrance, but still precisely guessed how the prologue was going to play out-Very lived in world with lots of previous events, players and moving parts. Again referring to the "crushed under it's own weight" point, as a new player I struggled to follow events that the PC clearly knew and constantly reference to, but I didn't. First half of the game was confusing for me as I struggled to figure out what the hell was going on. Prime example; for the life of me I completely forgot the catalyst for Judy's questline, who the players were and why we were tolerating dealing with entirely unlikable mob bosses. Didn't help that, for me, the questline ended so unsatisfyingly-NSFW content surprisingly shows a lot, though weirdly for a universe where sexuality is rampant, your character seems to engage in it... extremely infrequently-Romances seem to be pretty elaborate. I chose Judy because of her aquaphilia and wasn't disappointed-Johnny's relationship is really nice, but this game jumps between trusting him with your life and hating his guts at the drop of a pin, even at the end of the game where you're supposed to be buds. In truth I was a bit concerned that Keanu Reeves was spreading himself too thin in recent media, but he plays Johnny Silverhand quite convincingly in this-Multiple endings that, in fairness, are all fairly elaborate as far as final missions go. Some end sadder than others, some screw your relationships more than others. I'm extremely disappointed that I barely under-qualified for the secret "Don't Fear the Reaper" ending; I was consistently nice to Johnny but wasn't fanatically anti-corporate, thus robbing me of the optionProbably more that I'm missing... this game is massive and probably impossible to cover fully.I'll end by restating that this game is massive and ambitious, flawed, mostly enjoyable, occasionally crushed under it's own weight. Really good worldbuilding and dialogue, just needed a slower introduction to ease players in. Driving is mostly fixed, get a motorcycle though for maximum enjoyment. Combat can be broken in many ways, difficulty needed tweaking though because I really disliked going from bullet-sponging on normal and to being semi-frequently one-tapped on hard... being able to re-spec after game completion would have been appreciated. Story was mostly good, romances nice, endings all variations on sad themes though... one I found poetic but screwed my relationship, the other sloppy but ended slightly better for my character.Overall I'd say worth a recommendation. I don't regret picking up this game, but I'm also in no hurry to replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated after patch 2.0:9/10Patch 2.0 has made CP77 a far better game than it was, even after already having improved the game with patch 1.6. It isn't a perfect game by any means, but it's well worth the recommendation now.This patch has massively reworked the game and brought some much needed improvements:Among others, but I think these are the most important ones.Another change that is brought with his patch is that enemies now scale up to the player's level... Which is something I'm usually not a fan of, but I think that it works well with this patch. Even if enemies are scaling with the character's level, there is still a sense of progression, where at the beginning you feel like you're struggling to survive and take down enemies and at the end you can dispatch them with ease.Overall, it's a much better game now.As mentioned, it is still not a perfect game at all and still has some issues - bugs, for instance. There are some bugs that have been present in the game for a long time and still haven't been fixed and it's weird that these haven't been fixed all this time. NPCs are still lifeless, most of the side content is still very repetitive... And I  would like to see an on-screen indicator while driving of where to go when I'm driving towards a marker, so I don't have to be constantly looking up at the side map.However, all in all, these issues aren't major when compared to the overall package and some of these issues are unlikely to be addressed in this game, like the lifeless NPCs or repetitive side content - these would probably be improved in the next game.The game has come a long way since its messy launch and now has me looking forward to the sequel.**************Updated after patch 1.6:CP2077 is a much better game now, even though it's still not a perfect game.After a lot of patches since launch, the game is a lot more stable and way less buggy now and it's a lot better to play overall, in addition to also including some new content like new rewards for completing all gigs in a region, plus some rebalancing in the game like updates to the Monowire to make it a more viable weapon (and it feels extremely satisfying to use now).That being said, even with all these improvements, there are still some bugs that haven't been fixed yet and it feels weird to see some of these bugs still happening in the game after all this time.Replaying the game after patch 1.6 reminded me that, despite all the bugs that were fixed and all the improvements, there are still some areas in the game that are sorely lacking. The Crafting system is still not ideal, rarity levels for gear (not weapons) feels meaningless other than additional mod slots and I still don't get why the game has no NG+ mode, specially considering how there are unlockables for beating the game... Makes these unlockables feel pointless if you have already beaten everything in the game. There are so many cars to purchase but so little reason to do so considering how there isn't anything in the game that actually feels better when you have a better vehicle besides getting from point A to point B - even the race missions can be perfectly done with a vehicle provided by an NPC during those missions.I could go on, but the point is that the game is much better to play now while still lacking in certain areas, which is something I hope improves in the upcoming DLC or in a possible future sequel.**************7/10The best way to describe CP77 is "it's a great game when it works".I won't address launch issues with the game because this has already been addressed to hell and back previously. This will be strictly about my experience with the game.At its core, Cyberpunk 2077 is a great game, with its strengths being the story, characters and gameplay. The variety of skills and perks allows players to tackle each situation the way they want, either by sneaking by unnoticed, quickhacking enemies, combat or any mix of those, along with other options. Devices can be hacked to create distractions or cause other effects. Quickhacking enemies can be used for stealth, to aid in combar or even to cause direct damage. There is a decent variety in guns, from straight up pistols and revolvers to tech guns that can shoot through walls or shoot projectiles that automatically track enemies, plus the gunplay in the game is great and melee combat is also fun.Story and characters are likewise great, with the characters being the game's strongest suit. Characters are believable, well written, unique and their facial expressions during conversations convey actual feelings. A character rolling their eyes out very clearly shows that they're bored or otherwise bothered by something, as an example.The problems the game has are based on performance, glitches and things that are either not there but should be, or they are but needed to be improved on.Performance-wise, the game was causing my CPU to overheat (only game causing that) and I could only play the game with the AC on since it did cause my PC to crash once - and this is regardless of settings in the game. The framerate constantly drops from around 60 to 30-40 in certain areas of the game, plus I also had an issue with inventory management where the more items are transferred/sold, the slower the inventory screen got when trying to transfer/sell items.The game has bugs coming out the wazoo. Every single time I sat down to play the game, I would experience at least one bug at some point, but usually more than one per play session. For the most part they're harmless and sometimes even funny, but I did have a few glitches that forced me to reload a recent save.Even besides bugs and performance issues, there are many things in the game that should have been improved on or were just not included at all. One good example is the lack of bulk crafting options - you have to craft items one by one, which is a huge issue when you want to create multiples of the same item. The lack of a show/hide hat option is also an issue, if you're trying to make your character look the way you want. And on this note, the game having no transmog options for clothes is likewise an issue: you're either dressing for stats or for looks. The only way to combine both is to use Crafting to create the item you want in the rarity you want and even then, you still need the blueprint for that item. There are many other things that could be mentioned here - these are only some examples.Another issue is with how the game ends. Overall, CP77 is a game with potential to be a lot more than it is. It has its strengths and it's a very fun game, but it was clearly rushed out, which caused many of these drawbacks that hinder the game's potential and it could have been an 8/10 or even a 9/10 if some things in the game were fixed or improved.As of the time of this review (Jan 2021), my recommendation is to either wait for future patches or for a sale, but I still recommend the game despite its issues.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, bugs and optimization:I have encountered bugs such as AI struggling to act as they are supposed to (aka follow the player for quests and such) as well as getting stuck in a few railroaded sequences. This has had me reload a few time but not too many that I find it a huge bother. The frames are extremely unstable (I cannot keep i in stable 60), my gear should allow me to play on ultra graphics. These are all and all my biggest complaints about the game but there are minor things in the following sections as well.Story, characters and the world: I find multiple characters quite interesting, including Keanu Reeves and yourself. What I partly lack is a greater understanding of the game's world, it's background as well as the background of multiple important chracters including the main villain. A lot of background can admittedly be gotten from chips with lore but I rarely have the patience to read a lot of them, especially since there are so many of the and I feel like it really interupts the gameplay if that is to be seen as a necessity to understand the lore of the game. I hope and believe that more of this will be fleshed out before the game is over, I have done little more but finish act 1 (albeit idk how many acts there are but I am guessing 3). The writing is overall good and I feel immeresed in most of them.Gameplay:Not many complaints here, I find the "breeching" and hacking in general to be very enjoyable. I invest the majority of my perks into intelligence and tech for this first character. The gunplay is good although I was confused that aim assist was enabled as I started the game even though I play with mouse and keyboard. Driving is a bit meh due to the first car handling like ♥♥♥♥ but I already feel like it improved as I got a motorbike. Night City:A huge map where no district feels quite the same. The map and the environments would be a wonderful experience, less we forget the framerate problems. The art is tremendous and it feels very much alive, it really makes you feel like you are in a cyberpunk world as the title of the game promises. The style of the buildings and the fashion of the NPCs that fill the lively streets really hits it home. Character creation:I personally prefer sliders in my character creation screens but that is not at all a big problem since most sections had so many different presets. At least it makes things go quicker. A lot of the presets are really funny and wack so overall I think it was thoroughly enjoyable and I am ahppy with my result. Also 10/10 GOTY for the genital customization. Conclusion:A not only good game, but a great game. It has problems that I believe can be fixed, except the biggest of them, the overhype. If you expect a game to be perfect then you will, of course, be disappointed. A lot of the details of the game remain to be discovered for me. It is just a bit sad that a lot of experiences, not just my own, get soured by bugs and not optimal optimization. I would not at this moment call the game a diamond in the rough, that would not be fair since I think it is beyond that at this point. More like, you need to polish that diamond a bit more which I believe CD Project Red logically should be good at. I will thus recommend this game since I spent all of launch day playing the game desptite it's faults, even though I should be studying and the risk is that I will do it again. I am procrastinating these very studies at this very moment of writing this review and that to me say at least something about the quality of a game. I will update this review once I have finished the main story and done the most interesting side stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 has been a good game from the start, but 2.0 has actually managed to improve the overall experience. It still has quirks and some of the changes are a bit frustrating but, overall, it is still a great experience. If you want a good mix between FPS and story, then Cyberpunk 2077 is far better choice than other games like Starfield or other new games. The world is beautiful and the details are impressive. I feel like they adjusted and improved them, but I could be wrong. Either way, the graphics are fantastic. I know some players are saying that the bugs are back, but I haven't seen any so far after 2.0. The game seems to be much more stable with a lot less bugs. It also seems to run just fine on high settings with no stuttering or freezing. I could feel an immediate improvement over the original game version. Cyberpunk 2077 story is well written and exciting, although it is cheesy and boring at times. It still manages to keep me interested for most of the game and players can relate with NPC's. They do a great job blending the "feel good" moments with the sense of tragedy and hardship. As for the early story line, it doesn't matter if you choose Nomad, Street Kid, or Corporate because all three have great introductions into the game and minor (but still noticeable) impacts on dialogue within the game. I will say that Nomad feels the most natural, but that's just my opinion. Overall, the content between the story and exploration is good and there is plenty of material to keep players busy for dozens of hours. Combat has been greatly improved. The AI was already better than most other games but they still managed to improve it. The enemies react better and combat feels fun and challenging. That said, some of the 2.0 changes aren't the best, such as linking stamina to using firearms. I do not know if that was on accident or intentional, but I don't think that part was a good idea. The rest of combat, however, is a lot of fun and I enjoy it more than most of the newer games. I don't understand why they focused so much advertisement on probably the worst part of the game. Male "V" goes from plain ugly without much of a chin to somehow even uglier. If they had some form of slider, that would be helpful, but instead players are left with choosing between options that make me grateful that the game is set to first person perspective. I'm sure this one is going to earn me some hate, but the atmosphere in CP2077 is over-the-top at times, and I don't mean in such a good way. From the very beginning, it felt like they were over-selling this product with shows and other media. The game is good, but not that good, and I think they new that. CDPR did a good job using the hype train to sell a good game that people flocked to and screamed "amazing!" because that is what they felt they should do. In reality, it's like walking down to the gang-ridden section of a large city, blasting rap music, and being surrounded by poverty, drugs, and crime--then coming out and saying that's the best part of town. It took me a while to realize it, but the outskirts of Night City are the most enjoyable to me because they lack Night City. They tried and hit the ball on this one, but it's more of a first base hit rather than a home run. 2.0 introduced changes to how stats impact combat and I feel like they messed up with the stamina. It goes way to quick in combat and it makes no sense having it tied to certain aspects like gun play. They should take the dev team to a shooting range and actually have them fire real weapons, as some of these changes are pointless. Other than the stamina tied to firearms, however, combat is still fun and challenging. It's just this aspect that I find frustrating and an unwelcome change.Overall, I feel even better about Cyberpunk 2077 than before because of the far fewer bugs. 2.0 has greatly improved the performance, stability, and overall experience of the game. The graphics are great, combat is fun, and the side story is enjoyable (though entirely unbelievable). Before the new updates, I would have recommended CP2077 as a 5 or 6/10 but now I would rate it as 7 or 8. I do recommend it, but I still wish Steam had multiple options rather than just "yes" or "no."

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start by saying that if you like this game - you've won the argument by virtue of enjoying something I'm struggling to. If you're having fun, that's great. If you're besotted with the world, that's fair, and you're not wrong. Nothing in this review is intended to piss off the hive. I just have to write about the impressions I honestly feel.Cyberpunk 2077 is a game that is unforgivably marred by one thing and one thing only - overpromotion. A thesis could be written on how audacious Cyberpunk's marketing has been. The hype train is, of course, not all CDPR's fault, but the false promises are. Releasing too early and expecting you to pay £50 for the privilege of being an unofficial beta tester is. Look, I work in marketing, so I know how it goes. But when you promise so much and know you can't deliver on it, and change your marketing material in order to refer to the game as an 'action-adventure' rather than an 'RPG' before release - well, it doesn't sit right with me. If Ubisoft had done this, I would have blown my top. I have to stay consistent.Let me make this clear - I was not on the hype train for this game. Hype makes me feel nervous, and I try to deaden myself to it. I'm also realistic. I understood that it takes more for a game to be developed in the current-gen to offer a truly next-generation experience, and found it a miracle that Red Dead Redemption 2, by contrast, was so incredibly detailed and complex, if less dense than this title. I'm also not a stickler for bugs. I know they'll get patched and fixed, and that performance will improve. What I did expect, however, is what was promised. In this game, there is no advanced vehicle AI, which means police chases simply cannot happen. That's a system that was present in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. NPC's are lifeless, and are barely worth interacting with. The world has strong art direction and can look quite beautiful at times, but it's far from 'breathing,' and routinely feels shallow and tired thanks to how repetitive and basic the NPC and traffic routines are. It reminds me of a Mafia game, where the open world is just set dressing, serving effectively as a long loading screen as you move from place to place. But this isn't how the game was marketed. From the offset, they outright promised a sandbox RPG featuring incredibly dense and novel NPC interactions and narrative paths. I didn't buy into everything they said of course, but when your world is even less impressive than the last Watch Dogs game, I have to wonder what's going on.The gunplay is punchy despite the inconsistent ballistics, the upgrade tree is relatively cool (if deceptively limited), and the moment-to-moment gameplay is all just... serviceable? It's not an RPG I find to be particularly deep. This is a somewhat moot point - but there's little gameplay here you haven't already seen achieved more competently in titles like Sleeping Dogs, Deus Ex and Fallout. Driving feels dated, as if the vehicles have no substantial momentum to them. It's the little details that are truly noticeable, like V not even sleeping correctly in his bed, or QoL considerations, like the lack of a dedicated walk button on keyboard, that culminates in making the game feel average at best. I have no idea what happened with the life paths. I was led to believe they would be as long and impactful as the origin stories in Dragon Age: Origins, but they're just 20-minute starter sequences geared to introduce you to the world at breakneck speed. They feel like cut content.The good stuff here involves both the reliably impressive writing and story sequences. Yet thanks to the limited input you have for role-playing, it regularly feels like you're watching a (very cool) television show. It's nowhere near as reactive and dynamic I had hoped, not even half as much as The Witcher 2. If this game only featured its story front and centre, I would have given this a positive review. However, it doesn't, and I can't give a thumbs up for undercooked ambition or good writing when it's less than 25% of the experience, especially with all this mediocre fluff surrounding it. I say that even as someone who is willing to tolerate much for a good story. The amazing sequences you see are, ironically, those that would make for the best trailer-bait, and oh boy, did they.Cyberpunk's writing is far from perfect though, especially in its presentation and pacing. I'm never provided the means to care about V at all. Thanks to his introductory montage, you're given relationships, professional contacts and a criminal reputation in the space of around two minutes. It's hard to get your bearings. Compare this to Kingdom Come: Deliverance, where the horrific origins of Henry's developing heroism are fully-playable, rooted, grounded in your humble status. It helps you build your own relationship to his ambition - ambition that stays with you throughout the game. There's nothing like that here.A side note - it's very easy to assume that it's the fault of those who are heavily involved in watching the press cycle for getting their own hopes up, buying into every op-ed and/or preview carefully curated to generate clicks and escalating excitement for the game. Unfortunately, you would also have to be blind to the design patterns and trends of the last ten years to not see how derivative the vast majority of Cyberpunk's systems are. It's not a bad thing to be derivative, not always, but if you've marketed your game as being anything but that from day one, well, people are going to notice.I have no doubt this game will improve in the next year, in terms of its optimisation, performance, bug-squashing and maybe even additional content. For now, I would advise on-the-fence newcomers to steer well clear. I would also recommend that you stay sceptical of people who want to lambast absolutely everything in this game, as well as those who somehow think critical impressions are misguided at best or hate at worst. Certain elements of this game have been crafted with noticeable care and heartfelt attention to detail, such as the side quests, which can show real glimpses of brilliance. I imagine a few of the actual developers want to strangle the marketing and management teams right now - and trust me, I get it.I would have likely brushed this off as a fine, sometimes above-average game, ignoring the bugs and lack of innovative features as simply par for the course. I may have given it a positive review if it were honestly janky, but feature-complete, closer to the promises we were given. What I can't do is positively review a product sold under wilfully and repeatedly false pretences. That's weird for me because I don't usually take a principled stand, if you can label a cringe review as that. I didn't much care about Epic strong-arming their way into the market, for instance. I'm not entirely sure how much of this ad campaign was straight deception on CDPR's part, and how much of it was comprised of well-wishing narratives that exploded out of control, magnified by the sacred reputation gamers had anointed them with, all while they found their feet in a new and strange genre. For whatever reason, this time it feels odious. Maybe I'm just getting old.

_childDocuments_.review: After more than 70 hours I can say a few things about this game.Are you going to get a fresh new experience?Yes, I don't think there's a world like this one in any other game.Is it fun?Yes if you dive yourself into its lore, conversations and flavor text scattered around the world.Is it filled with glitches?Yes, minor graphical glitches that won't take the immersion away.(I only found one glitch in a minor quest that didn't let me complete the mission, a load game fixed it. Cybermarketing:(Only PC) Yeah people got caught on a promise fueled by consumer desire and developer excitement. The hype made people angry when they got a game that doesn't have any revolutionary mechanic or graphical improvement. (Consoles) Console release was very poor and deserves all the bad reviews it can get til it gets fixed. In fact I think a lot of the console backlash transmitted to the PC reviewers too.Ok, now to what I think this review should be:I liked the game, I got a lot of hours of fun with just one run. There are a lot of quality of life improvements this game needs (basic stuff tbh):1) Let us click various items and select them before selling or storing! Is super frustrating to click each item and wait for a small loading before is successfully sold/stored.2) Let us have more slots for weapons, why 3? You got melee weapons, guns, shotgun, sniper, different rifles, etc. Let me have at least 6 slots, DOOM DID IT 27 years ago.3) NPCs need to have a day/night cycle, different greeting lines and paths. They are boring but look great.4) There's no "Store all" option when storing items at home.5) The character creation menu is very limited, why can't I be fat or super skinny? If I wan't to create a chin less character I just can't. This HAS to be a FLC soon, I can see and meet fat characters in the world, why can't V be one?6) The DLLS is a lie, if you set in on 1920x1080 with quality it upscales a 720 and it looks very bad, you can see it on the character panel when on the menu, your character will be pixelated.The rest I would say is 9/10 and I totally recommend it but maybe wait for a sale or the first big patch.Just don't get carried away by those reviews that consider the PC and console version as one, I would call it media madness.Is it expensive? Maybe, it should be a 40$ game due to some glitches and rough edges.8/10(Will update when it gets retouched and gets its first DLC)

Esp when out in the open with a lot of people or flashing lights. It's pretty bad.This game had 9 years in development, 9 years. I know games take time to create, especially one that looks this good. But I expected a better experience. Especially with the multiple delays and all the hype behind it.  I came in blind, didn't really watch any gameplay footage, so I didn't really know what to expect. Given the game was insanely over hyped I was expecting to be blown away, but I prepared myself for a potential let down and that's kinda how I'm feeling rn. Overall, it's a fantastic game, and I look forward to when I can play it smoothly but for now I say wait if you're on the fence about getting it. Give it some time. I'll most definitely change this to a positive review when the mentioned bugs are fixed because in the end it is still a pretty amazing game and world. Although, Witcher 3 will always be Number 1 to me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's watered down and just depressing to even look at. Anyone just pinning this on only performance issues has low tolerance and hasn't been that exposed to many games in their life if they think this is a great standard the industry should be setting.While the world looks nice, it is the most lifeless world I've seen in a game yet. Everything just exists as a static asset that fades in and out of existence just to "appear" as if the city is a bustling active place. But it's like that episode of Ed, Edd, & Eddy, where they make that whole city out of cardboard and all it took to knock the illusion away was someone trying to climb the tower. Which is of course not possible in the game, despite the big "verticality" marketing they kept pushing. Everything starts glitching out the moment you start trying to explore the city beyond the surface level. This wouldn't even be an issue if the game wasn't filled with padding and filler content nonstop. The reason flying cars aren't in is because the game cannot stream the assets fast enough on the Lowest performing hardware, and the fact the buildings aren't actually there if you were to fly up there to look at them. It's nothing like Spiderman, more like GTA3. The combat feels like every generic looter shooter but worse. Animations have no impact, AI is non existent as a whole throughout the game, and the weapon options feel useless when compared to other categories. Getting augmented just boils down to opening a menu and slotting some stat changes into a slot, the only augments that change anything at all with your appearance or gameplay are the arms and legs. The arms are just a glorified weapon, while the legs are the only thing in the game that changes the gameplay somewhat. But both only offer 3 and 4 options to pick. Gorilla arms are useless because Body does everything Gorilla arms do. Skills like crafting are also useless and the looting system is what makes crafting useless. It's a watered down system like the rest of the game.Regarding the world again, there is nothing to do outside of gigs, main quest, side quests and the 124124515 disturbances padded around the area nonchalantly. There is no in lore "Gwent" like game, no pool, darts, or even street racing beyond some missions for one character. I'll also bet there is no street racing or any minigames with another NPC, because there is no AI in the game that can properly run events like that. The thing this game needed most was more actual RP aspects instead of this half-done looter shooter with the RPG tag line on it. If this was a Rockstar developed game, every single interaction would've had it's own animation, instead of this menu slotting crap. I'm still laughing at the fact the gigs that involve carrying a body back to a car, always have you putting them inside the trunk, regardless if they are dead, alive, or even a hostage rescue. And your character just phases them into the trunk like magic instead of having an animation for even that. It's little things like that hurt the experience when they start adding up. I'm not gonna talk about the writing or story because I frankly just don't care about it. If someone else wants to review that then by all means go ahead. The only thing I'll say is I don't like Keanu Reeves trying to act all bad ass and crazy, because he is terrible at being that kind of character. He speaks like Butthead without the laugh when talking, and he is monotone throughout the entirety of the game. He's a great actor but I'll assume the casting director was too starstruck or didn't push him because he may have thought Hollywood actors are all some magic prodigies that know exactly how to play everything the first time. Who knows at this point. Now in a more positive light, CDPR has shown great passion in trying to fix the issues around bugs and performance. But that's a given and won't ever solve these blatant design flaws that hurt the game. AI might be fixed, but it won't fix the dead city or the gunplay, the augmentations being lackluster, or the fact the entire city is a cardboard cutout that falls over the minute you try to explore beyond the surface. Either save your money or wait for patches, because this is not what you got shown in previews. And if this is what you wanted, you could've had more to it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not a bad game per se. It will provide some entertainment in at least some form to pretty much anybody. That is one of its stronger sides. Did it live up to all the unbelievable hype and expectation? Certainly didn't. Even not meeting the enormous expectations, it could at least have been it's own unique thing - but it's not even that. GTA meets Deus Ex - literally. And GTA and DE are much better in their respective sub-genres than this, their mix. What mostly made me negative in the end is the quality of the writing - plot, dialogues and characters. At their best they are going to be just mediocre assortment of cliches put together in a more or less neat manner. It's not bad in itself - it has been done before and it can work. It's just the halfhearted way CP2077 does it that rather falls flat. At their worst they are facepalm-worthy plot holes and lack of logic. Sure, there have been worse, by far. But it's one of the things the game strives to shine at and fails in that. So, the world is a bunch of poorly thought-through cliches loosely put together, it's never a coherent whole. The plot is not horrible, but neither is it really good, too. The characters... this is maybe the worst thing about the non-gameplay part. The characters are absolutely empty. Some are slightly better, like Jackie, Judy and Takemura, but they are just a little bit more fleshed out than the rest of them - doesn't make them really good or interesting. The whole thing is supposed to hinge on Johnny Silverhand, played by Keanu Reeves. Jesus, even Keanu couldn't salvage this trainwreck of a writing for his character. Johnny almost never makes any sense. His character is, again, a bunch of cliches loosely put together. They never actually work together. His "ideas" are incomprehensible and they aren't even voiced clearly. His motivation is incomprehensible. Arasaka's decision to keep his engram is incomprehensible. You can go on and on and on with this. It looks like they didn't even care if it all makes any real sense or not. Gameplay... as a sandbox it works. As an fps it is absolutely horrible. AI is excruciatingly dumb, playing on the hardest difficulty is never hard at all. Just to illustrate some things that regularly happen in this game: you're driving a car through the city like a maniac, hitting every other car on way, knocking some occasional pedestrians down. Then you see some thugs (always highlighted) by the side of the road. You get out of the car. Take out your weapon - all of it in plain sight of dozens of people walking by. Maybe even in sight of a cop patrol car parked some 50m away. So, you take out your gun and just click their heads - one click each. They're dead. Civilians are running away. Cops do nothing. You casually walk up to the bodies, loot them, leave. If you were unlucky enough to accidentally(?) graze a non-highlighted citizen - new cops spawn behind your back in 1 second and immediately start shooting at you. You can't give up. You can, however, run away in literally any direction and after some 100m you're safe, they won't chase you and they'll forget about you in a minute. What "realism" or immersion can one talk about here?..

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands the game is littered with visual bugs and occasional quest hiccups that require you to reload a previous save. However, it doesn't take too much away from the fact that it's still a great game with a good story, characters, and a rich world.  Exploring does leave a lot to be desired in terms of things to do, and npcs to interact with, but there is still plenty of content in Side Jobs and Gigs to do.  I finished the game at lvl 28 at about 45 hours in with plenty to do left.  I played on the Hard difficulty and I found it to be mostly fine difficulty. Stealth gameplay makes the game a bit easy and the game kind of shoehorns you into "this is a stealth segment" by literally having all the npcs have their backs turned through most of the mission.  Once combat starts, when the AI is working properly, feels very much like they're working to kill you, and will nade you out of the spot and use hacks to get you out of position.  Sometimes the difficulty is absurd for some portions of the game. One particular mission has you fight hand-to-hand and its honestly the hardest missions you're going to get, so you cheese them. That said, when the gameplay works, it feels great. I played as a cyborg samurai-type character with all-in Blades, reflexes, body, and technical.  It does feel nice that you can tackle missions one way or another but honestly it comes down to stealth or no stealth approach.  Speaking of crafting, I had a reasonably high Technical stat, able to build most items, but the components for crafting were generally high for the purple and higher tiers.  By the time you could craft something good the game was already over. I think the best aspect of this game is its narrative, storyline, and atmosphere that makes you feel as if you're in Night City. I just wish the bugs and the game balancing was better.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've beaten this game beginning to end. I've completed all the gigs and NCPD scanner quests. The only thing I've missed out on was a relationship quest which didn't trigger. (Even after a year, it's not surprising.)After all of that, I can confidently say, this game was and still is one of the most over-promised and under-delivered titles I've ever seen apart from maybe No Man's Sky (but at least they've put in the maximum amount of effort to deliver the promises they originally made, Cyberpunk will NEVER reach the heights and content initially promised).The things they promised us that sold me on the game that turned out to be lies? Choices made outside of the starting prologue literally doesn't affect anything except for some very far and between dialogue options (which don't change the path of the story in any way). There is incredibly limited choices to make in the main story to actually effect the path it puts you on (won't spoil but the promise of multiple playthroughs being unique? An absolute lie. The story/dialogue options are ultimately as linear as the average Telltale game, an illusion of choice, all leading to very limited outcomes AND EVEN THEN, the story in my opinion is absolutely nothing special). The AI is braindead (STILL). Purchasing safehouses? A lie. Character Customisation? Very limited. If you want the full breakdown of promises that weren't delivered, there is an entire Reddit thread you can find with a quick google.If you bought the newest model of a Ferrari and were told by salesperson it was the fastest road car ever, you take it home and it won't move faster than a crawl, you would not be happy being told "It crawls now but we'll patch it over the next few years until it hits its top speed". It would be unacceptable right??? So, why do these big game devs keep getting a pass by players for bullsh***ing us? They were nominated and WON the award for the Steam Outstanding Story-Rich Game Award for their lies, when none us would accept this nonsense in any other industry. Restaurants wouldn't be getting Michelin Stars for serving bad food and Actors wouldn't get awards for bad performances, but as gamers we're sold blatantly unfinished products and are expected to accept it? The game industry will never improve if we keep taking this laying down.Anyway, remember this review when Bioware releases Dragon Age 4, inevitably in an unacceptable state and we gift them with a Game of the Year award for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077... First things first, Major spoiler warning :) I'm gonna break this review down into parts and state the pros and cons of each section to try and keep it readable since this is my first review since I feel like I had to get my opinion out there! GAMEPLAY 7/10The gameplay is sadly not groundbreaking, sneak can be abused and has no purpose other than just to avoid fighting. Examples are if you decide to shoot up the place or not. no massive changes in the story are made. Another really bad thing is hand to hand boxing. the boxing quests are Unplayable and terrible! Driving is OK, motorbikes are fun! The guns sometimes feel empty but in general, the feedback is there and it's satisfying enough. Sniping could also be abused but that's until you start getting rushed or swarmed. Hacking in general is repetitive and is really dead to me as a combat feature. it's not really satisfying and leaves me bored when going that way into boss fights. The gameplay around skills in general is kinda dead when it comes to conversations with people. unlike examples from fallout, you can use skills to gain advantages in conversation like speech. In this game, it's completely a dead mechanic that is only there to basically flex your knowledge in conversations. You almost make yourself feel like a complete dumbass when selecting the skill option in convos. Street kid, nomad, and corpo. the only difference is the start and that's it. nothing major story-wise later like a unique nomad ending or a unique street kid ending. the special dialog option is also dead like the special skill dialogs. they never help and are completely ignored.STORY 9/10Wow. The story is one of the strongest I have seen until the ending... hence it's a 9/10, not a 10/10. Let's recap. They decided to kill Jackie in the most annoying way. but this is what later kinda helped you get this status and what made you meet Johnny silver hand aka Keanu reeves so I guess it was an okay plot to go with. I don't agree with how fast he died and how he died but I guess it was one of those annoying plot twists that you have to suffer now or later. In the trailer it these actions around Jackie's death were shown as an outcome but little did we know this was the ONLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WAY???? HELLO? another "plot twist"? Now you get to meet good ol johnny boi and my Gawd is this gonna change the game. Adding Keanu to this game honestly alone gave the game another 3 points out of the 9. He is there like he is not just there like a typical celebrity cameo to sell the game. Oh, boy was I wrong, he is with you the ENTIRE GAME. not just the main story too. he is there for it ALL. he has really funny, sad, and annoying dialog that adds another layer to situations. He guides you and he can also try to aid you with knowledge when it's hard to figure out what to do sometimes (mostly in main story missions). Learning about his character and learning new characters is amazing. Judy, Panam, VIC, Jackie, Johnny, rogue, V, and misty are some of my favorite characters in the whole game. Let's talk about the ending. Everything built up to what? nothing... and yes i mean nothing. no matter what you pick. how you do it. or what you do. you will NEVER reap the rewards of what you have done. why? well because you are FORCED TO GO BACK TO THE LAST SAVE BEFORE THE MAIN MISSION TO KEEP PLAYING... This is the worst way to end it. Completely unacceptable cd Projekt red. This same method of an ending was used in Witcher 3's base game (ignore the DLC ending) and I didn't like it then and I didn't like it now. Well, I understand there has to be a way to keep the door open for potential DLC but this is just not the way to go about it... Let's break the endings down. You raid a base and fight the same boss, and one of the people you made come with dies to Adam Smasher. Spoiler warning again. no matter what you do, V dies. this is hinted at the afterlife bar where you are told that to become a legend and have a drink named after you. You have to die with legend status or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game has no good endings and you are only stuck picking between the bad and the really bad ones like just killing yourself and watching how you made your friends sad later on in the credits where you get to see their reaction to whatever ending you picked. But it's not that bad because you are gonna go back to your last save anyway :) personally, I played a male and I helped Judy out of the city. had a good relationship with johnny and left with Panam. As a male, this was the best ending for me. I had 6 months to live but I'd be spending it with friends and loved ones away from night city.VISUALS AND MUSIC 10/10From the radio to the general soundtrack it's just blowing you away with good music and intense situations aided by cyberpunk-themed music. The visuals (when they work) are just a solid 10/10. I have not seen a game with this much detail ever before in my life and I have played a lot of games. Sometimes I just stop to look around and suck in the detail and I appreciate every small hint of detail that was added to bring night city into life. Also, Night city in general is a fantastic place to be in for a story. The place is alive and you definitely get sucked into its drama.OPTIMIZATION AND PERFORMANCE 5/10Since this is for PC. get ready because you are gonna be playing on low frames. I played on 1440p ultra, no DLSS, and RTX Off with an average of 40 frames. To be honest it was worth it. The game was playable even in gunfights and I don't regret it. The game in general needs a lot of fixing here. The core mechanics and visuals are so buggy when they act up. This can be fixed if they try and it's the weakest point of cyberpunk 2077SUMMARY AND FINAL RATING 8/10If you have a 1070+ on 1080p sure go ahead give it a shot. other than that you are not gonna have a good experience graphic wise which will ruin the game for you. In my case, I had no issues here so that's why the rating is high. I played very hard which was not really that rewarding because there's not really a bonus for beating the game in the highest difficulty which was kind of a bummer but I expected it.FINAL WORDS AND REFLECTIONSI hope cd fix the game. it has so much potential but it was all wasted because of greed or idk something Corpo related obv. I will continue to try to 100% my first run because this game deserves it. The time put in showed but unfortunately it needed another year of development to patch up the cracks. If you actually read this then thank you and stay safe in these times :)The guns

If you can't wait, I'd say the bugs aren't that bad actually. 8 hours, I've had one crash, seen no doubt plenty of weird visual glitches and had one 'stuck and can't move' glitch which I fixed by reloading a save. But so far nothing game breaking.Most likely, by the time you read this review, chances are the problems will be already fixed.The game world is huge and stunning, very beautiful and detailed. The game is DEEP so it's going to take some time to properly explore it. I'd say the first 6 hours or so is just the introduction. Probably best enjoyed by taking your time and taking it at your own pace. Don't let the game rush you.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk is an interesting view into early announcements and how not to go about doing them.To preface, I love this game. I have a ton of fun with it, and it is much of what I want from GTA, and better.This game, even after finally releasing after many delays and months of patches, is still not entirely what was promised. There are still bugs which need fixing, and the game itself has very few choices which feel as substantial to the world. Even still, there is much to do and I do genuinely enjoy everything I do in the game.Though much of it is a run-and-gun experience, I never seem to tire of raiding gang bases, stopping street climb, and better learning the streets of Night City. Everything is sleek and incredible to look at, though I can admit it takes a long time to find any clothing I don't feel embarrassed while wearing. The game has an adequate moral compass, letting me decide whether or not I am justified in my actions while still penalizing me when understandable. Interactions with the denizens of the city, whether in passing or active, feel real. I can believe I would have them with anyone in any normal city, but with, you know, sci-fi.Definitely a great game worth adding adding to your library, but just know it is not perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, well written story, good acting, visually stunning, intensely detailed, the gameplay is fun, driving was better than I expected. Also I would've appreciated a few more little mini-games or side activities in the world, and maybe a little more dialogue choices for characterizing V how I'd like, but I'm not crying over it cause the world still feels very alive, and the dialogue is mostly pretty damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: After an extremely backlash filled release in late 2020, CDPR has done their best to convert the entire game to what players were expecting to it be released as. In summary, they have done that!Over the years, CDPR have focused immensely on bug and glitch fixes that moved it from a broken buggy mess to something distinctly playable, with that wonderful open world experience we all wanted to immerse ourselves in. I’m very impressed with what they’ve managed to achieve with this revision to the game and I believe it is finally living up to its full potential. With the DLC released, this brought fresh eyes to the game and allowed players of old to come back and experience a new play through of the game without those game breaking bugs they were so used to seeing previously.I believe the game is just a lot more FUN to play. It was great because of its storytelling and design before but now it’s just better in every possible way.Considered one of the biggest changes, is the fact that you can now engage in vehicle combat with things like car chases, shooting out tires, and shooting at each other. It’s something that was strongly needed in the game and makes the massive number of vehicles actually useful now. The various criminals and opponents in Night City are no longer nearly as limited as they used to be. This again, helps with the challenge and makes encounters things that players are going to want to take slowly. You can double-jump, slow time, use quick hacks and use all manner of meaningful abilities to cut your enemies into literal strands of ribbons. Fast travel points are everywhere in the large map, and dialogue can be skipped with the press of a button that visually fast-forwards time. The game has NPCs that are relatable and universally well-written, cut scenes that are engaging, and a host of great soundtrack options to accompany your playthrough. Combat is excellent and offers a wide choices of ways to take down your enemies in Night City, so you can always find a suitable way that you prefer to play.As far as 2024 goes, having completed the main game and the DLC, Cyberpunk is a game I would replay in a heartbeat! Highly recommended to anyone who's looking to lose a bunch of hours in an immersive open world RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Wants to say everything, but isn't allowed to say anything. Cyberpunk 2077 is an embarrassing product, not quite because it's bad, but because of how grand the oversight of those producing it was. It's an uncoordinated mess of unfinished gameplay, features lost due to the ego of those in charge, completely unchecked Orientalism, strange hostility to the exact sort of deviance from societal norms that the marketing promised would be celebrated--it is a vast sea of false promises and all things cast wayside to cough out a product.Unfortunately, however, this is what makes the game good, because when you learn that your player character, no matter the choices you make, will inevitably be denied that which they sacrificed their and others' lives to obtain, when you watch a woman crawl back to the abusive workplace the nearly pushed her to her death despite knowing that it will do the exact same again, and when you look into the eyes of a son exiled from his militaristically corporatist family--and see that though he once held ambitions to realize impactful change and light his blaze of glory, he understands that he is, always was, and will always be powerless to change the fate set by his father--you understand, if for but one moment, what it was like to be an artist who wanted to make Cyberpunk 2077.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 surely didn’t turn out to be „the best game ever made” like some expected, and it really doesn’t have to.  Instead it turned out to be an amazing open world game, with a large game world, lots of variety, an most of all, a great story full of amazing NPC’s you learn to love….or hate.  Especially the world building got me hooked, it feels all so organic and natural and not just like another future Sci-Fi Metropolis. Night City feels alive, something is happening everywhere. May it be the usual traffic/NPC’s on their way around the city (which also changes with the time of day), to little shops on the site of the street or markets between the Skyscraper gorges, NPC’s talking to each other and and and. CDPR did a fantastic job there, Night City gives you a great feeling of being at a real place.  I, of course, don’t want to spoil anything story wise and I’m not done with the Main Story Quest(s) but so far, I really enjoy it, it's well paced, the Character design of the people you meet is great and they are diverse, you feel for them and slowly can understand them and what drives them, how you react to that is obviously on you.  Even the side missions are worth doing besides their rewards, many tell their own little interesting stories or even develop into entire quest chains.  I don’t want to do a deep dive on the skill system but there is enough freedom to play as you like, from not killing anyone and being sneaky. Over solving most issues with hacking to be a full melee Rambo that hacks their enemies into pieces with heavy weapons and Melee weapons. And yes, BUGS there are still a ton of them on the game, from rather annoying to very obnoxious at times. I thankfully only got one where I got stuck, and it forced me to complete a mission in another manner than I wanted to. But then all went fine. But every other one I encountered was easily solved, with saving, going to the main menu and loading back in.  But even with the bugs, on which CDPR is hard working to fix from how it looks. The overall experience is just too good to pass on.

I really feel bad for the quest writers, level designers and motion capture folks who made such a beautiful story with V and Jonny. They dont deserve a world with no driving ai, subpar gunplay, and other open world quality of life features present in the elder scrolls Oblivion. This game deserves another year of develpoment to become the game its meant to be. I fully believe this game will be great with about another year of development, and I will change my release. However, its such a damn shame CDPR didnt wait another year to let this one cook. Wait to buy until its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077, developed by , emerged as one of the most anticipated and talked-about video games in recent history. Released on December 10, 2020, after years of feverish anticipation, this open-world action RPG promised to transport players to a dystopian future where advanced technology clashes with societal decay.Despite its rocky launch, Cyberpunk 2077 has made significant improvements in recent years and months. Not too long ago, it received a huge expansion and a 2.0 overhaul update, including a list of the following changes:The game is currently in the best state it has ever been. It has barely any bugs, it runs butter smooth, and the atmosphere was never better! The story of Cyberpunk 2077 is undeniably the best ever written for a video game. Anyone who claims otherwise is trying to ignore the obvious facts. The voice acting, the choreography, the highly intelligent and complex writing… all of this adds up to the most perfect and breathtaking story you will ever experience. No one else would have been better suited to the role of Johnny Silverhand than Keanu Reeves.Moreover, Cyberpunk 2077 has the most impressive open-world you can imagine. It meticulously captures the intricate details, and faithfully depicts the lore of Night City, a dystopian metropolis formerly named Coronado City, envisioned by the esteemed creator Mike Pondsmith, who holds the rights to the Cyberpunk franchise. Notably,  collaborated closely with Pondsmith on the development of Cyberpunk 2077.The quests are intriguing and fun, the gigs are unique, and the game rewards you for exploring every single dark alley within Night City. The open-world feels alive and crowded. Gangs rule the streets, and drive-by shootings are not uncommon. It's important to be mindful of interactions with gangs during quests; the repercussions may extend beyond the mission's conclusion. Proceed with caution and consider your actions carefully at all times.Cyberpunk 2077 is undoubtedly  open-world story RPG ever made. Anyone who claims otherwise is just delusional. The main story, including the gigs and NCPD missions, will provide you with around 90 hours of pure playtime. And that's not even including . Adding Phantom Liberty would give you around 135 hours of gameplay, and that's just for one playthrough. Considering how often the game is on sale, nobody can argue that it's a bad deal. Nothing can be perfect, but Cyberpunk 2077 comes very close...

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 can be considered an open-world action role-playing game (RPG), which has been developed and published by the company CD Projekt Red. One major contributor to this project has been Mike Pondsmith, who is renowned as a cyberpunk author and RPG creator.++ Night City, what a sight to behold! A beautiful, dystopian habitat filled with an absurd amount of details, crass contrasts, and constantly changing environments; the overstimulation has been pretty hard on me in the beginning.++ The side quests and its characters are the hidden stars of this show. With their personalities and stories they perfect the immersive setting. What I love the most is that around every corner, another opportunity awaits to earn some eddies, go after a gig, or hang out with your chooms.++ As far as the gameplay goes, I am impressed how customizable the protagonist is with regards to cybernetic choices and skill trees. Basically, you raise your skills by using them, and the implants significantly impact your tactics. It boils down to your own niche build. For example, my nomadic brawler runs on cold blood and military-grade cybernetics. His hobbies are bathing in blood and collecting servo-skulls.+ The campaign is well done in regards of narrative style and characterization of your relationships with Jackie Welles and Johnny Silverhand; they have grown dear to my synthetic heart. I also like how the underlying topic of transhumanism is handled, especially the cyborgization of humanity and its effects on social life.- The police system is a disaster. Cops must have teleportation devices, because they spawn out of nowhere directly behind you. And they will do so, repeatedly. -- Bugs, a ton of 'em; clunky collision system, clipping issues, cut dialogues, frozen enemies, inconsistent frame rates, and desktop crashes. A few times I have felt like a beta tester.The aspects mentioned above are also the reason why this game has been delayed several times. I pity the quality assurance team working their fingers to the bone, in order to fix the gravest issues of this colossal project before the final release.-- From a marketing point of view, its unfinished state was deliberately obfuscated and the review process conducted in a very restrictive way. A sobering reminder why I should not pre-order a game, and wait for the hype to die down.Cyberpunk 2077 is a diamond in the rough and I can see its potential, which will likely take months to reach. Unfortunately, the initial state of release combined with the deceptive marketing did irreparable damage to the community's reception of the game and to CD Project Red's reputation.Estimated time for 100% completion: +120 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 44Multiplayer achievements: none
