_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is a cautionary tale of a promising project gone awry due to corporate greed and deceitful practices. It serves as a stark reminder of the importance of transparency, honesty, and delivering on promises in the gaming industry. It's a shame that a game with so much potential was marred by such actions, leaving many of us feeling more betrayed than entertained.Even the much-hyped 2.01 update failed to live up to expectations. Instead of addressing the core issues, it felt like the developers were playing a game of bug whack-a-mole. New problems emerged as old ones were supposedly fixed, leaving players in a never-ending cycle of frustration. Graphical glitches, erratic AI behavior, and severe texture pop-ins persisted and, in some cases, even worsened after the update. It was a grim reminder that the company's promises of swift fixes were more smoke and mirrors than genuine solutions. This only added to the feeling that we were being taken for a ride, and the game's potential was squandered in a sea of deception and technical incompetence.

_childDocuments_.review: While buggy, I feel the PC version is significantly more stable (2 days in) than the console version, so if you're reading this...you're thinking about playing Cyberpunk the right way. I'm over 20 hours in at this point and I feel confident writing a review even without fully beating the game--I've done many major story missions and a plethora of side missions and open-world encounters. I'm loving this game, and I think whether you decide to buy it or not should hinge on your willingness to deal with bugs.The reason I believe this is a masterpiece, beneath all the bugs, is that the game so nicely pulls off countless genres of play within its RPG framework. Shooting isn't Titanfall 2-smooth, but with mouse & keyboard it's responsive, fluid, and fun. Don't expect R6: Siege, expect Fallout/Borderlands. Gamepad/controller shooting is less than stellar, so wait for more patches if you are against M&Kb play. Driving is no Forza, but it's dramatic, cinematic, and not so hard that it takes your attention away from the world and events around the car. Turning with a keyboard is a bit jumpy/spazzy, but it's really not game-breaking. Stealth is no Splinter Cell, but combined with special stealth gear, augments, and the entire quick-hacking and breaching minigames, it feels *great* to be a stealthy, net-running force that overwhelms enemies before they're even aware there's a threat.  Combine all of these features and you'll have moments where you distract a gate guard by hacking a nearby TV, infiltrate a compound, steal some data, and then, if you're me, decide to plant viruses in all the enemies around you. As their eyes catch fire (or reset, blinding them) and their guns deactivate, you rise up, switch to your assault rifle, and become a maddened grenadier, only to slide down the stairs and into your car (which just autopiloted over to you, to pick you up) where you make a quick escape. Cyberpunk doesn't *excel* in any of these core gameplay areas, but it does them all well enough that it truly feels like it's not just the  that's open, but your character and each approach, too.Beyond the core gameplay mechanics, the crafting system is solid (with a fun and interesting pair of related crafting skill trees), even if it's missing some sound effects at the moment. The dialog system is fast, and conversation options never jar back and forth--they feel like they always naturally lead into one another (more on the writing later). Shopping, managing inventory, and other key elements like managing the world map are also very easy and take minimal adjustment. A transmogrification system would be nice, but you aren't a slave to goofy outfits as some people say. Even on Very Hard, the game isn't so insanely punishing that you can't leave your helmet off (if you just have a fedora, or some goofy small hat). The economy isn't perfectly balanced, but neither was The Witcher's, neither was Dragon Age's, neither was Skyrim's. As someone who loves econ IRL, video game economies are rarely good or interesting (and it's usually MMOs like EVE or Star Wars Galaxies that do it right. I couldn't name a singleplayer or loosely-multiplayer game with a legitimately well-run economy). The bugs I've had have been few and far in between. 20 hours in and I've had ONE NPC T-pose. I've had crowds of civilian NPCs de-spawn twice while running around. I've had a quest marker point to the wrong door twice. I've died from falling off low ledges once. I've had one cutscene where an NPC's mouth didn't move.  I've never crashed, had texture-pop, or most of the bugs others complain about (running an i7-7700k and an RTX 2060 super.There are definitely bugs, movement feels a bit jerky when running around, but honestly I'm not having the negative experience others are having. If you're wanting a very smooth experience then maybe wait a bit, and ensure you have a strong PC to run it. Otherwise? Get the hell in on this while it's fresh and the internet hasn't spoiled the ♥♥♥♥ out of the plot. The major plot moments have been freaking amazing so far. This is not just my game of the year, but it's one of the better games I've played in recent times. Absolutely loving it, and I'm going to stop writing this so I can dive back in now.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I'd say it was worth it. Surely the game is not the masterpiece for all times with billion features PR promised and have quite a few problems, but still.Pros:+Storyline and side quests. They all are great, as long as it is not random map activity and it is an actual quest.+Atmosphere and level of detail put in the world is something to die for. Probably beats GTA 5.+Level design. Quite on par with Deus Ex - both very detailed and few ways to get around without getting noticed.Cons:-RPG system in a shooter usually do not work well. If it is crappy system with levels and DPS and random stats on items in an open world - it get messy fast.-Generally bad RPG system, overcomplicated, too spread-out and badly balanced all at once.-AI. Stupid beyond all limits. Incapable of reacting to physics-related noises like you stepping on bottles and breaking them, take ages to notice you walking out there, and usually just contempt to staring down a wall or wandering in 5 meter circle asking "where are you?" if they are alerted. But can instantly pinpoint your location if you shoot them from 200m away.-Side activities on map. They are numerous and insanely repetitive. Same for question marks - few are interesting but the rest is same boring thing. A billion spot with 3-10 enemies and some leveled loot to grab DO NOT improve the open world. Would plainly be better if they removed all of them, in my opinion.-Open world is greatly detailed, but if you poke it - it falls apart like wet cardboard. Starting from citizens walking in circles around the street and reacting... let's say weirdly when you act up, to teleporting police and not having anything to do apart from taking in the views or clearing stupid activities I mentioned above.-Fistfighting and races. They are so raw that they drip. -Bugs. Bugs bugs bugs. Granted, I haven't seen anything critical and not even a single crash in my playtime, but lots of things like stuck parts of interface or physics based stuff like car under the road, but these tend to break immersion.-Lack of choice and replayability. You can't roleplay - V is the same V always, heritage and skills baredy do anything but extract extra few lines of text without even dialogue advancing. Choices rarely matter - remember that mission with drone retrieval with like 12 completely different ways it can unfold, that they showed before game launched? Forget it - it is the only one of a kind in an entire game, even in fact that it can influence another single side quest later. Some choices matter, sure, whether you get next mission in chain or not and some even affect the ending - but it is so easy to just do everything and be able to do anything at the "point of no return". It took me 110 hours to 100% everything, and to reiterate through all possible endings - they are quite different and worth experiencing, sure, but they all took like 10 hours. There is no point to continue playing - I've seen it all and I'm done with this game until couple of addons come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2024: I'm still playing 1.63 because it is objectively better. SMD.Edit post-2.0 update:They MASSIVELY changed the perk system and weapon/mod/crafting systems.Now they no longer follow traditional RPG mechanics, which is what made this game tolerable despite its flaws.They changed core gameplay mechanics, added some gimmicky new ones, and added features nobody was asking for except a vocal few shills on the forums.If I didn't have such a good time pre-2.0 with so many hours, I'd be demanding a refund.Nearly a year later and CDPR continues to make questionable choices regarding the future of this game.Players want content shown in the E3 trailer. We want 3rd person and MP co-op. We don't want new guns. We want the guncrafting system fixed. We want more gun attachments. We want to wear NPC clothing.Literally nobody asked for the content updates they are pushing. While I personally enjoy this game, I can't say the same for others. Just wait till the sequel comes out in 10 years.Edit, day after: the game won't even launch now. I was having issues with this before where I'd have to restart steam, and then eventually my entire PC, but now it won't start no matter what I do.Paid $60 for a game I can't even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ play. Well done, CDPR.10 hours in and here's my honest take.I'm extremely disappointed in CDPR.Gameplay:- I didn't even finish character creation before the game crashed.- During the first 5 minutes I encountered a bug where gun meshes didn't even load, an issue that is still fairly common in my playthrough. Kinda hard to aim a gun you can't see.- I've seen better traffic AI in 3D flash games on Miniclip and AddictingGames (Burning Rubber series, for example).- Combat AI is really, really bad. Get ready for grenade spam.- some NPCs are bugged where even though it's a low level mission, some of the NPCs can one-shot you. Not sure if bug or if I need to git gud.- Vehicle handling is awful. I somehow ended up able to drive a motorcycle underwater.- Sometimes you can drive a motorcycle right underneath other cars.- Sometimes cars will spontaneously explode.- Weapons, especially guns, feel like an afterthought despite being a major part of the game. Guns only get 2 mod slots - optics and muzzle accessories. Feels like the first Mass Effect game. Ranged combat is a joke. You want to breeze through combat? Become a ninja.- Out of 40 hairstyles, not a SINGLE ONE for feminine characters is a normal high ponytail?Story:- In a game where choice should matter, there's a lot you don't get any choice in.- most of the time there's only 2 dialogue options and only one of them actually advances the storyline/scene. Dialogue options that require perk investment or skill investment just offer additional pointless conversation snippets.- The writing is very stale. It's predictable and bland. CDPR should stick to adapting novels.This feels like another Fallout 76/No Man's Sky release...Very unfinished and overhyped.For $60 I can't recommend this game. For anyone considering...save your money or buy Witcher 3, a game that CDPR has actually finished.

_childDocuments_.review: While yes, some of the negative reviews do hold valid points. This game was released prior to being actually finished, and we could've definitely seen a more polished game.This remains to be one of the more aesthetically pleasing, engaging and outright enjoyable games I've touched over the years.Visually, this game is beyond amazing, if you're able to run it. The game is quite demanding, and for someone who doesn't have a great rig (i.e. me), I went to use Nvidia GeoForce NOW, which allows you to stream the game without any delay on great rigs. No delay to speak off, and great latency. Not to mention, you can use it for free with the additional option to play it on much higher settings, have longer queue times and even have much longer gaming sessions for a mere approx. $10 a month, which allows you to play not only Cyberpunk, but most games from Steam, GOG and other supported launchers.The entire world appears to be handcrafted. While yes, there are some clipping issues, and some objects might be out of place if you find yourself in some obscure areas you either aren't supposed to frequent or pass through by normal means, that remains in my eyes a minimal oversight. From the artistic catwalks, to the mood of the various regions you can visit in game, everything is obviously handcrafted by a team with great accuracy to simulate a dystopian but colorful Neo-Tokyo-esque city. It can be an adventure on itself if you were to take the time to simply wander the streets and pay attention to the detail around you. I won't go into too much detail, but I can say with certainty that this remains an unpolished but beautiful gem on itself.Second, but personally the strongest point of the game, the story.The writing in the game is almost next to none when it comes to telling a complex story, which I won't expand on too much to avoid spoilers. The voice actors breathe the additional life right back into the complex and amazing story that is told within the game. One can be left with a wonderful (and maybe an emotional experience) if you were to solely focus on the main story alone, but I highly recommend to leave no stone unturned when it comes to doing any side-gigs and secondary objectives. I won't beat around the bush on this, but the game has been launched prior to it actually being a fully polished game. Sometimes the player can easily obtain hints that there should've been more to a certain story, life-path or choice. Even the environments hint to such whenever you explore out of bounds, realizing there might be one or two extremely detailed but obscure places littered about. However, the worst offender of all, was the promise of certain key features (such as climbing with the mantis blades) and several other things that've either been scrapped or not fully developed on.As for bugs, I've personally encountered only two in the time that I've played this game. Back when I originally pre-ordered it and played it immediately on launch, and another near 100% during this summer, which is still ongoing at the time of writing this. Both bugs I've encountered in the previous version of Cyberpunk 2077, and were caused by running a rig that was way too weak to run it optimally. However, these bugs were far from game-breaking. An NPC that would pop into a T-pose during an animation, and the camera being way off-center for about five seconds. Besides that, I've not encountered a bug myself.If given the chance, Cyberpunk 2077 can perhaps become one of your top ten games too. It is quite easy to sink in hours on end into this game, and immerse yourself in the beautiful world-building of characters previously established in the tabletop RPG, which the game builds up on, and enjoy the game for what it is.Despite that Cyberpunk 2077 was released in an unpolished state to say the least, it's receiving way more negativity than for what it is due. This is by no means discounting the fact that the game was unfinished by launch. It's become more of a meme to roast this game, giving the false impression that the game is still a burning trashbin rolling down a hill.The story is extremely engaging and one of the best written ones out there when it comes videogames in general, so much so, that I felt compelled to share my thoughts about this game to anyone that might be iffy whether they should give it a shot or not.As for right now, the game is worth easily up to around $30, and you should definitely pick it up in the sale or off a key shop. I personally urge everyone to at least try and play the game through the prologue to shape their views on it. If you're still iffy, I urge you to watch a playthrough of the prologue alone, and then shape your opinion. It is maybe the best way to get a taste and feel for the game's story and partially its mechanics without spoiling all too much of what's to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk is a game with a lot of problems, some that have been patched out, some that will be patched out and some that can't be because they are fundamental to the game itself. This game ends up feeling like it's in some no mans land between something like GTA V and Call of Duty. As you play the game two things become very apparent: 1. The developers have a lot of love for this game, and have put a lot of that love into the game; this is very apparent throughout the games massive amount of content that bleeds a style in every facet of the game that is reminiscent of Blade Runner whilst also being entirely it's own. 2. This game has a lot of content and I can't help but wonder what would have been if the developers had focused their efforts more on some things and less on others.To summarize I wouldn't write off this game because of its admittedly shaky launch, even with all its problems. _childDocuments_.review: These are my first impressions after about 3 hours of playing so far. Did the first couple missions or so. Walked around and got overwhelmed with the seemingly massive size of Night City.So graphics up first, the game looks stellar. Nice textures, lighting, character faces and animations, etc. It all looks very very nice. Performance on a  10700K + RTX 3080 easily runs 4K with Ray Tracing disabled, 80-100fps depending on the scene/area. Ray Tracing enabled I'm seeing low 50fps and can maintain right at 60-65fps (RT on Medium, graphics all on high/ultra). DLSS is a must with RT and needs to be on performance mode. I set DLSS to quality mode when I turned RT off. Anyone with lower end hardware will have a crappy experience if they're going right in cranking all the settings to ultra.Combat has been spotty so far. A couple strange animations here and there and kind of stiff movement depending on the action. But overall, not bad imo. They did a good job on the gun animations and reloads. Gun tones/sounds could use a little more "punch" when being fired though.The bad: Audio. It is so unbalanced it's not even funny. It's actually terrible. NPC voices are laughably loud, like to the point I don't even want to talk to them. And then ambient noises in the distance that should be very quiet and in the background  sound like they are right next to me and drowning out any main quest dialog. CDPR needs to patch the audio asap. It's bad. I cannot believe they f**ked this up. I tried all the audio settings too. Unfortunately they do not affect NPC dialog. The main mission with Jackie when you enter into Night City for the 1st time, I literally could not hear what the hell he was saying because the ambient sounds completely over powered him. Luckily, subtitles were on.Character creation is awesome. Probably the best I've seen in a video game ever. You could literally spend an hour alone making a single character.Character development like skills, traits, mods, etc. is overwhelming. I need to read through everything at some point to get a grasp of all the skills and stuff. It's almost endless it seems.Most of the cut scene animations are amazing with the attention to detail. I'm so glad CDPR made it to where you can actually see your legs and feet. I cannot stand first person games when you're basically floating around with no legs. There is a lot of stuff to take in with this game. A lot of little hidden nuances and things everywhere you'll miss if you're not paying attention. A couple small patches from CDPR and this will easily be a 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must play for any RPG fan. The world CDPR has created, and the city itself, is second to none. There has never been an open world city of this size with this much detail crammed into every single alley, room, hallway, street, warehouse, gun, bar, ect. The city is a masterpiece. The gameplay is also a breath of fresh air for any action RPG fan. The gun play soars past the likes of Fallout. The loot, while plentiful like in the Witcher 3, is unique and powerful. Builds are diverse and deep, needing multiple play-throughs to try them all out. The characters in this game are on par with those of the Witcher 3, as is the main quest (so far) and all the side quests I have done (so far). What is a nice surprise though are the "gigs". I have spent hours just doing these small, one off,  20 minute quests that are packed with detail and lore themselves. Gigs are separate category to side quests.As of writing this, 4 days after launch, I run into minimal bugs, have solid 60 FPS on High (1080p, RTX 2060 Super, Ryzan 7 1700x) and have had a few crashes. The scope and density of the city and the game make this fine with me. As a massive fan of The Witcher series (most play time on console though) I can honestly say this game has so far exceeded all of my expectations with little faults. Those faults I think are mostly in the character creator options, clothing styles, and rando NPC AI.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are some straight up pros and cons I found in the first couple hours *no spoiler*The game was obviously meticulously created for a long time now, and the graphics and gameplay is there alright. There was just a lot of quality of life issues (floating cars) as well as the low frames that bothered me. Bugs were expecting though as this is a massive game with so many possibilities. Is it worth full price? We will see, but it is definitely a good game and I think it is worth it so far. If you think your computer can run it, I think you should get it. As updates roll out, bugs will disappear as well, and multiplayer is promised which is something to look forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST AND FOREMOST: If you plan on buying this game and trying it for the 2 hours to refund if it isn't your cup of coffee, the prologue alone took me 2-3 hours. Everything I will talk about will only be from those first hours. Will be a very minor spoiler at the end of this review.This is more of a FIRST IMPRESSION rather than a fleshed out review for someone that, like me, was on the fence about getting this game after all these years but hearing about this 2.0 update sparked their interest. Cyberpunk 2077 is a narrative RPG. Don't buy this expecting an open world sandbox like Starfield, per say (sorry to compare but it's the easiest way to get the idea across, that will be my only comparision).PROS: The world feels alive, extremely alive. There are events happening all around, crime scenes and crimes in motion (that you can often interact with, but not in some main character detective way). People walking the streets and actually interacting with each other (and they aren't all copy and pasted NPCs either, they all look different, they have varying heights, have different walking styles, and there are even children that actually look like children, not shrunken adults). This so far this is my favorite thing about this game, the reactive world.The world building is amazing. The game naturally gives you the opportunity to learn about the lore of this world, whether through dialogue choices (that are usually optional), books (or this world's equivalent), or even quests that simply reveal more to you just through playing. The voice acting / mo-cap are amazing. As this is a narrative RPG, you will spend much time in scripted "sit down" moments where you will talk with another character. Often times in games, NPCs just stand still and do a few idle animations in dialogue, but in Cyberpunk, they feel REAL. The talent behind the characters (including your own player character) is impressive and adds to the immersion and that "alive world" I mentioned earlier.The story characters are extremely well written and ALSO feel very real and alive. The characters I have met so far have been amazing to interact with and 9 times out of 10, I always want to interact with them more. The VA and mo-cap I mentioned earlier help this, but I mean that the characters themselves are genuinely interesting. I have found myself wanting to learn more about certain characters at every chance. This is also true for the player character, who I actually enjoy playing with and enjoy progressing with.The movement feels smooth and real as well. Running, walking, and climbing around the map feels great. Another thing, your character ACTUALLY moves at the same walking speed as NPCs during dialogue, as opposed to being too fast or too slow. I think we can all agree this is great.The AI act smart and threatening in combat, actually using tactics to make your experience more difficult, such as flanking.The graphics aren't groundbreaking but they are beautiful, and sometimes they do *almost* feel groundbreaking.ALL in ALL, the immersion that Cyberpunk 2077 often brings is outstanding, with a few caveats listed further below.THE IN BETWEEN: The combat is a little iffy, at least at low levels. I'm sure it will get better but for the purpose of those 2-3 hours, the combat feels very stiff. I don't mean that the movement is stiff, but rather the actual gun-play and melee combat. Melee combats felt like I was just trading blows with the enemy until they died, there is counters, but they seem less useful than just pummeling your enemy by using heavy attacks to break the guard. Melee weapons lacked impact very often, which broke immersion. Ranged combat was a little bit better but still feels "off" to me, perhaps cheap. Enemies kind of just get shot with little reaction, with the exception of a shotgun I used, which would level them off their feet. Once again, ranged weapons also suffer from impact. Stealth at low levels is also sort of meh. You will use gadgets at your disposal to influence the enemy (distractions, for example) and then sneak up behind them and neutralize them using a handful of the same default animations. It is worth noting, if you are a fan of non-lethal take-downs in games, much like myself, Cyberpunk does have them, which I thoroughly enjoy. It is also worth noting that enemies won't ALWAYS just die from gunshots or other more deadly force means, meaning you can shoot someone and neutralize them as a threat, but they will still be alive on the floor laying in pain. I thought this was amazing and it really adds to the immersion this game brings. NOW, the "cyber combat" I suppose you could call it, is where the fun really begins. Without spoiling too much, the augments you can receive in this game add much variation to the combat, both melee and ranged. An example of one such ability is the option to remotely detonate a gas tank, which can not only outright kill your enemies, but also disorient them and cause confusion. Once again, this is a 2-3 FIRST IMPRESSION, it is very possible that the combat will get better as I progress my skills and unlock better weaponry.The loot system is questionable. I am not sure how the game was before 2.0. but looting is repetitive and feels almost "looter shooter" like. Almost all enemies have one shared item that they will drop (some form of crafting item) and then some will drop their weapons and some will drop "health items". Sometimes the enemy would drop their weapon, but it would be broken and also just give the same generic grafting item. The problem is that I often found myself picking up all the enemies weapons just to sell them anyway, which isn't bad, but it also just feels like a waste of time at the end of the day. Because the player character starts off being able to carry well over 100 lbs, I would just stock up on loot to sell. The reason this isn't a con is because it isn't a big deal and can be remedied by simply not looting, but I'd rather have loot be more meaningful. Example: killing an enemy and being able to take their outfit if you so wanted to, rather than JUST a crafting component.THE CONS: I have heard that Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way since release and that most of the bugs have been ironed out, but remember, as a first time player, what I see now is what matters, and I have seen bugs. Nothing game breaking but enough to be an annoyance. An example of one such bug was all of my enemies floating about 1-2 feet off the ground during combat. It's not a BIG deal but it is noticeable and it is annoying. Graphical errors are abundant as well, and I don't mean that the game runs bad, I play almost max settings across the board with my 3080. I mean that there are many graphical artifacts and glitches that I noticed that I wouldn't expect to see this far into the games release. Some examples are missing textures, player models having invisible parts (I suppose this could go with missing textures), and glitched out structures in the distance. These also haven't been game breaking but they are noticeable and immersion breaking.MINOR SPOILER (no names included)Such a small detail goes a long way, and unless the quality drops, Cyberpunk 2077 gets a recommendation from me. Just remember, if you buy this expecting to refund, it took me over 2 hours to finish the prologue.

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly 240 hours immersed in Night City, I can confidently say that Cyberpunk 2077 didn’t just break the boundaries of open-world RPGs—it broke me. From the neon-soaked streets to the heart-wrenching choices, the game lured me in with its chaotic beauty and then shattered my soul with its relentless weight of consequences. Every quest feels like a punch to the gut, every character leaves a scar, and every corner of the city holds a piece of my fragmented sanity. I’ve walked away, but I know part of me will forever wander those dystopian streets.

_childDocuments_.review: I really struggle with this review.This game was seriously overhyped to the point that only two conclusions would be possible.Either the game would go into history as the new gold standard, the nirvana, the Alpha and Omega, the EVERYTHING for any remotely open world oriented game.Or the game would fail to meet expectations and go down as an overambitious project that failed to deliver its promises and forced to continue as the big "meh".Actually, the game found a third way!Not only was it dismantled as an overambitous project but it also came with a nice bug infestation. The worst part is, that all the bugs just shroud how the game is mediocre at best by mere design!Just to give a few examples:- Police spawning just behind you and giving you a headshot before you even notice what's happening- "wanted system" that makes you loose all wanted status right after turning 3 blocks- nothing in this game has any consequences on anything- NPCs not only don't have any of the day and night cycles promised but just spawn and despawn behind your back (what we were promised was "every npc has a unique day and nightcycle" or something along the lines)These points are just the tip of the iceberg. Even Gothic 1 from 2001 had more believable NPCs - and this game is notorious for its bad controls to the point that people say it wouldn't be the same "gothic experience" if the controls were good.I don't mean to say that you can't have fun with the game. The story has its moments and the first hours are amazing. It's just after that the game drops you off into an open world where nothing really happens. There is no meaning in anything that happens. There is no real point in exploring except clearing off points from your minimap. You can't even have a conversation with any of the npcs. There are not even standard dialogues. They just throw at you random lines that often don't even remotely fit into the situation. The hacking is kinda fun and it can be pretty nice to jump into a group of enemies and slash them to pieces with your katana.The graphics are stunning (if you can afford the hardware).The bugs aside, this isn't even a bad game. It just sucks at the open world part but delivers an interesting story. They wouldn't have had any of the problems if they decided to turn the game into a more linear experience with smaller hubs to explore (like Deus Ex for example).So why am I downvoting?Because CDProject blatantly lied. They lied about features the game would have or about the quality the features would have. Yes, marketing tends to overstate things and we are used to it but CD Project crossed the line in my opinion. This is a problem because PreOrdering is a real thing and they collected on our money that was given at good faith by lying so bad it exploded them in their faces.And of course, this is a PC Review but the Console Situation can't be overlooked. They collected on preorders from players on PS4 and XBOX KNOWING the game would run with like 15 fps on these systems. This is borderline criminal. It was so bad that Sony and Microsoft pulled the trigger and kicked the game out of their stores in an unprecedented event.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, definitely worth the money even if you just play through the main story and don't mess with side missions. Story is one of the best I've every played through, connections to characters is really strong. The only downsides are the performance, and some balancing issues/bugs that will most likely be fixed after content patches. For the hardcore RP'ers out there, there is a lot to be wanting, but hopefully mods and added content will help fill that void. 1. Performance-Even on a decent computer this game is quite a tank, so hopefully in the future it can be optimized better2. NPC's and AI- Police are absolute garbage, they spawn in front of you and have no sense of anything- NPC interactions are very limited even among main characters (Panam, Judy, River, etc.)- While not a necessarily a big problem, the rest of the NPC's are braindead and talking to them feels just like it does in the Witcher series, which is slightly disappointing considering how much CDPR said this game was revolutionary in terms of the RPG aspect3. Difficulty- I'm going to be real honest with you, this game's combat is so easy it's almost not fun at end game- The hardest difficulty should have the enemies scale with your progress, it's not much fun when I can go around one shot body shot killing everyone without having to try- Stealth is honestly not that bad, however when you get into "combat mode" it can seem a little overboard when everyone in the tri-state area focuses you even if they're not in the immediate vicinity4. Buildings/Areas- This isn't a huge issue either, but I'd like to bring it up. There seems to be a lot of places with the OPEN sign lit up and of course you can't enter, which even if you couldn't interact with anything in there, at least let me go in and explore.- *bonk* The amount of sexual related themes in advertisements and just walking through the streets leads me to think that there should be more clubs, or something to "explore" ;)5. Roleplaying- This is my biggest issue, like stated before there are a lot of things that are advertised in game that seem like they would be crucial to life in Night City, but aren't included in the game. Maybe we'll see some of these things added in the future: Strip Clubs or other themed clubs, Braindances (since they seem like such an integral part in the game, why are they limited to specific missions?), followers - so I can go on a date with my romance :') 6. CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION- There is no customizing looks beyond clothes and cyberware, which aren't lacking I like them a lot, but the fact that I can't change hair, hair color, or anything else on V, really annoys me. Are we to believe that in all of NC there is no barber, tattoo artist, etc. so that we can change the character- In a game where the gameplay is supposed to be next level, no customization besides the very limited character menu, which is very disappointing in my book, there should be those things to be able to customize things in V's life to make it feel more immersive, without it I feel like nothing has my personal touch  1. Night City- This is without a doubt the best world I've ever played in an RPG, there are no words to describe how detailed and massive the city is, you just need to see it for yourself- The badlands leave some to be desired for, but overall I like the style a lot and I feel it is leading into a DLC that relates towards this area2. Storyline- 10/10 on the story and the main characters, from my first playthrough alone, I felt a strong connection to all the people I met in my journey as a merc in NC. The romances are very good, they work super well and the emotions really connect me to the game. Hopefully this will be expanded upon with the DLC, because... well I miss Panam and Judy already ;)3. Clothes/Weapons- Some people may not totally agree with this but I really enjoyed all the clothes types and weapon types, the balancing of these isn't the greatest right now, but I'm not completely turned off by that. The weapons in the game are very cool and fun to use, and I really like all the clothing options, but at times it can be difficult to find a certain piece of clothing4. Choices in story and endings- This is by far one of the coolest things about the game, during my first playthrough I didn't watch anyone else play the game until I finished, and when I did and started my second playthrough doing quite a different playstyle, I was amazed at how different entire missions were when I choose a different option way back at the start of the game- Bouncing off the first bullet, watching streams and videos of people doing quests different from the 2 ways I did them was super cool, this many options really lends the game longevity- The endings are superb, there are SEVEN, count em, seven in total! Such a suprise to see so much variety and how each of them feel. The amount of ways you can include main characters in the specific endings is something that really make the game feel whole and that its not just a scripted ending that is followed strictlyHopefully I will be able to change some points on this review in the future, but as it stands now I do recommend the game, maybe not on PC/Console if you dont have the horsepower, but rather on Stadia/GeoForce Now. I'm having a ton of fun in the game still and I hope that modding will make me put hundreds of hours into the game in the future, have a wonderful day gamers <3

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a masterpiece in so many ways. So many reviewers talking about broken promises. I went into this expecting nothing. They were told that there would be features, and things that they claim were never implemented. This is an aspect I care nothing about. Other people are saying that the game is empty, and that there is nothing to do. More quests open up as you earn street credit, so yeah, a level 4 who played 8-10 hours will not have many quests open to them. Another thing, the tutorial of the game is long, and linear; however, once past it the game really opens up. For those complaining that the games has the depth of toilet water. Some quests are pretty basic, and some are mind blowing. The game sort of ran with  "sex sells", and made it a brand... I'm not saying it's good but it's supposed to be a dystopian world where morality is in decline. If you watch the news in the game, you will note that it's a theme on many levels. Crime is significantly higher in Night City than it is in all of the New United States. The bugs... oh my... the bugs. They are aplenty lol. Save often.  I mean, save like your sanity depends on it, because it does :D. A fix for the floating trees was merely updating my graphic card. Albeit, that does not fix the other weird bugs you encounter with the game. Saving helps a lot.The world is expansive, graphics are beautiful, music is a nod to Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines in my opinion. There is even a club you can dance in, that was all the affirmation I needed lol.I'm recommending the game because I thought it was really good. Is it messy, yes. I think it's worth the occasional frustration but I am exponentially more patient than most people I know lol.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; the game is not optimized, the world is empty and quests are bugged to hell which lead to me completing the game in a rush, because I wanted to see how it ends.Before we get into the review of the game: Cyberpunk 2077 was the first game I bought after ordering a new gaming PC, so I was pretty hyped to get into it and be able to finally play it with an RTX 3080 Ti and an AMD 5900x, hoping it to be a fluent gaming experience.However after my first couple of hours I was quite disappointed: Without DLSS the game didn't get higher than 30 FPS on 1080p and not higher than 20 FPS on 1440p, no matter if I selected low settings or the psycho settings, even turning RTX off didn't change it, so I naturally decided to go full psycho move and use DLSS to get up to 80 FPS and more or less good graphics quality. But what's worse: the game didn't really use my hardware to it's fullest potential, CPU and GPU usage always being stuck at ~20%, like come on.So with the technical stuff out of the way, let's get into the gameplay review:Gameplay is, ok-ish. You are thrown into a large, multi-layered world. However it's empty, e.g. cars on the horizon are just sprites which, when getting closer to them, just despawn instead of being materialized into LODs and later real AI cars. The streets of Night City appear to be void of people, too. Yes, you meet people, but not as many as you might expect from a megacity like Night City (or the Cyberpunk genre). To give an example: there are tons of markets scattered across town, but nobody is there, apart from 5-10 NPC, a few vendors and densely cramped shops which, for whatever reason, the player can't interact with.The story and the side quests however are pretty darn good, some are weird, others are pure insanity and I loved the story telling, which leads up to multiple different endings.There's also a ton of gigs and other minor activities scattered throughout the whole map, however at one point I decided to ditch most of them, the reason being that I encountered multiple activities so heavily bugged (after patch 1.5 btw) where V just suddenly started moving around on his own without my doing. Or my own cars randomly spawning at the only exit *after* getting into a car which I needed to steal. So the only thing left to me, was to get out of the car in the heat of battle, dodge bullets and drive my *own* car out of the way, running back to the car I wanted to steal from that garage and drive away with that.Speaking of cars: the keyboard controls are horrible and it is not fun to drive them. Most of them feel like you've just become captain of a cruise ship, the also tend to crash against invisible walls which prevents them from driving down a road (I mean: what the hell CDPR?).I've never been somebody to use fast travel mechanics regularly, but Cyberpunk's cars changed that. Yes, Cyberpunk's cars managed to force me to skip some parts of the world, because they are so utterly useless and horrible to drive.Sometimes I even thought "it's just 1.5 kilometers to walk, let's do it"...

_childDocuments_.review: As many other people have pointed out, there are a lot of bugs at this stage of the game. This is to be expected, the game is really huge in scope and there's bound to be bugs in release. Software is never finished, only released. This is not a huge issue for me as I'm writing this review 2 days after release -- they'll iron out most of the bugs I encountered in my playthrough.I didn't have any major performance issues while playing, with a Ryzen 5 3600 and RTX 2060 super. I had RTX enabled and the game looked drop-dead gorgeous. They definitely nailed the visual aspect of the game. The city, the characters and the overall atmoshpere looks amazing, and it's obvious they wanted the game to look as edgy as possible, which is a good thing for a cyberpunk game. They definitely nailed this part of the game. I was not really able to experience much of the audio of the game because of my setup, but the only concern I had with audio was due to bugs, again, something that will probably be fixed later on.At first, I did not really care about the characters and story, maybe because I wasn't attentive, but I also played the Witcher 3, a game by the same developers, and a game that I think had a much more engaging story than this game. This may be because they wanted this game to be more open ended, as it was (more on this later) supposed to be an RPG. And to be fair, I did start liking the story after a while, although still not really stoked about it. I only managed to get one ending as of writing this, and I'll be playing a bit more to get the other ones as well. I do have a gripe with starting paths though. They don't influence much of anything in the story -- it's just there to say something different depending on your path; it doesn't really add anything.Up to this point, everything I've talked about are minor flaws in my opinion. Bugs are to be expected, and I did not purchase the game for its story, but rather for the replayability and the customizability of the game; I've been dreaming of different character builds and cool outfits and custom cars and random events I'd participate in, and this is the main reason why I don't recommend anyone buy the game at its current stage. None of the things I mentioned are in the game. Sure you can buy clothing, and sure you can spec into skills and make different builds, but it becomes painstakingly obvious that these are lacking a lot -- there are not nearly as much customizability that we were lead to believe there were. You can't even preview clothes when buying to see how they look on you. You can't customize cars, and given enough specs into strength, you don't even need to buy most of the cars, as you can just steal one from the streets. Almost none of the cool, edgy things that were in the Night City Wire trailers actually accessible to you, even though some of it is in the game. I wanted my character to look like those mox guards, and clearly, as they are in the game, the game assets are in the game, but as there is no way to modify your character once you've started the game (in terms of appearance, separate from clothing), you got no choice.This issue would have been kind of passable had there been a good character customization screen, so that you would be satisfied to continue with what you got. But not even that is possible. The character creation screen is lackluster -- it does not have nearly enough of the complexity of a good character screen, for example, something like what the Sims has. No sliders, no body build modification, none of that cool half skin half metal body parts. You only have a couple of piercings and some hairstyles. How can any of these features be missing from an RPG?Well, the thing is, Cyberpunk 2077 is not an RPG. At least, the description box never mentions it is an RPG. Instead, it says that it is an "action-adventure story". They slowly shifted from an RPG to an action adventure, and removed a lot of features in the meantime. But this is most definitely not the fault of the developers, the designers, or people who worked on the game. It's got more to do with the people related to the business side of things. They already delayed the game 3 times already, to rush the game development to fit the deadline. They had their developers crunch for the game for almost (at least counting the delays -- they were probably crunching for a whole lot more) a year. Most of the stuff that they showed in their trailers and gameplay demos are either gone, misleading or downright untrue, because they probably didn't have enough time to add into the game. It's easy to act as if you're a progressive company and pander to audiences, mistreating your employees and pushing out content unfinished just for money is just downright low. Maybe CDPR could learn from their game and not be like the corporations they depict, but by that argument, I'm not sure how to format the review, so I'll add any other miscellaneous problems into this paragraph. Please note that these are not game-breaking by any means, it's just that these are minor inconveniences that bugged me a bit while playing. I'll make sure to get back to add more as I remember them.TL;DR: The game has many bugs and missing features in its current state. It lacks a lot of promised features, most probably because of crunch and trying to fit the release into a deadline. I am a fan of CDPR, and I do like the game -- or at least what they meant it to be, but this sort of actions are not the way to go. Fix your game and treat your devs right.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it for 6 hours so far so I will update this as time goes on. My current set up isn't out of this world. Like I'll place something in there, save my game, do something, reload my old save, and everything saved in terms of my set up except for whatever weapon I had assigned to my third slot. _childDocuments_.review: the story and side stories are stellar. the open world is par, maybe subpar depending on how hyped you were. i realize that cdpr did not deliver on a bunch of promises they made for this game, but i never kept up with those promises, so i went into the game pretty blind, despite being pretty hyped for it since the original announcement of the ip. this game has kept me hooked by the story alone. i don't think i'll replay it for the open world aspects, simply because the open world IS lacking. however, i will want to complete all of the story, side stories, and generally any content that has story or lore attached to it. also, to ppl who are complaining that your choices don't matter -- your choices DO matter. The thing is, the choices you make are kinda self-contained within their respective stories. Basically, there can be several possible ways for a particular questline to end, depending on your decisions and choices. They won't affect the overall world too much, and won't really factor into the potential endings you can get at the end of the main story (update: actually, they WILL factor into the ending. No spoilers, but things you do and the people you meet do end up having a pretty profound effect at the very end of the game). However, each of those self-contained stories, that i experienced at least, have been stellar. A+ writing when considering things in their self-contained aspects.Edit: I've actually gone back and am working on a second playthrough, with almost the same character, besides changing the prologue backstory. After mulling over the ending I got, I REALLY wanted to dive back into the game because it was so melancholic.The story I have experienced so far on my second playthrough has been SURPRISINGLY different from my original playthrough. I've had interactions and quests that I never even saw in my first playthrough, despite almost playing through the same way in the early game. I can't really explain it too well, but when I mentioned that replayability would be pretty low, I now think that the replay value is pretty huge considering how *modified* of a story my second V is experiencing compared to my first.Definite recommend for gamers with good enough rigs, or until CDPR patches the game to a better state on lower-end hardware.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels incomplete, rushed to launch and cut short on content.Finished the game and all gigs on the highest difficulty and still unable to unlock the latest Perks.I really hope the next update will start adding substantial amount of missing content, and not just be another "bugfix" patch. It's been more than a year since the game come out. I refuse to believe your team spent over a year just fixing bugs. That would be embarrassing. We want more interactivity, more customization (hair salons, plastic surgery), better AI, better police (car chases), expanded romances, with options to actually interact with them at our apartment and in the city. Why can't we invite the romance option to our apartment to shag? Or kiss them or hug them or do ANYTHING with them after their quests are completed!? They all just stay in their apartment or camp, and repeat the same few lines of dialogue. Give us a more interactive Night City. Let us actually sit and order food at restaurants with animations... you know, like those that ALREADY exist in the game. Let us go to night clubs and sit and have a drink, let us interact with dancers at strip clubs. Let us have those one night stands you talked about years ago and showed in the E3 gameplay reveal. Let us interact with furniture more. Let us sit on chairs, benches, let us lie on our bed without having to go to sleep. Give us a lot more MEANINGFUL side quests, with branching stories and the ability for us, the player, to influence the direction of those stories, and fewer boring "gigs", the ability to purchase more apartments etc etc etc.Next, do SOMETHING to fix the HORRIBLE pacing and the irritating sense of urgency. After the mission to rescue Sandra, have Jackie just text us the next morning telling us that he returned the car to us, and then just let the player decide when they want to call Jackie. Maybe I don't want to meet him the very next morning. Maybe I want to explore that first part of the city for a few days, and then call Jackie after like a week. This leads me to my next point: LET US REFUSE TO ANSWER PHONE CALLS! What's the point of giving us the 'answer' button, when we MUST answer each time!? Let us refuse phone calls, and then later call the NPC at OUR convenience.Have the NPC/Companion/Fixer etc. call us, and if we refuse, they can just send us a short message saying "Call me back when you have the time." Maybe I want to call them in 2 days. This would fix A LOT of pacing issues, and not make the player feel so stressed out, like they always have to rush and do these jobs quickly.I was barely able to explore the city, without feeling stressed out, because I had these urgent jobs and the YOU KNOW WHAT from the main quest always pressuring me. Like, I never felt right just exploring, knowing what was happening to V. I knew that I should not be prancing around a beach, when I had the URGENT main quest to do. Ignoring it felt stupid.Next, fix the way we interact with Johnny. After that first night when he reveals himself to us all angry, he and the player are in A REALLY bad relationship, right? So, then the very next morning we get a phone call from Goro to meet him at that diner. If we go there, the convo we have with Johnny flows natural and V is angry and mistrustful towards him. However, we also get a call from Delamain that same morning to go get our car. So, if we go do that first, V talks to Johnny like they are already friends, which is super immersion breaking. Fix that somehow. Let Johhny start appearing only after we've done the first few main quest missions or something.Also, I don't know if it's just me, but the journal in this game is terrible. It's close to being useless. Like, most of the time it doesn't even tell you what the mission is, who gave it to you, or why you need to do something. It just has some clever little monologue by Jackie or Johnny. So, if you decided to leave some mission for later, then, when you finally decide to do it, but you've forgotten what it was about, chances are that the journal will tell you nothing useful. Rewrite that, if you can. Man, I could rant for hours. Oh yeah, expand on those few endings that are such obvious cliffhangers. Give us at least ONE good one. Man.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is a game with an intriguing narrative and quite engaging mechanics. The main story isn't too long which in my opinion isn't a bad thing, quite opposite I'm not a fan of games that prolong it, and it becomes bland and boring in the end. Plus, the side quests or encounters that you can find in Night City are well written and fun to do when you just go on an adventure or explore. Missions that give an option for romance or friendship are also enjoyable, and you even get into random text messages with them along the way, which is a nice touch. There is a good variety in terms of builds and how you want to approach fights - slowing time warrior with katana - no problem, stealthy net runner hacking everything and everyone - the game is practically on easy mode then. One of the flaws of the game for me was vehicles... cars are terrible to drive, I just stuck to one of the motorcycles which was a bit better but still not great. The other thing is sometimes driving around, streets felt empty - mainly in outskirts and wastelands. Night City had some amazing views, but the city life and NPCs sadly aren't that immersive - seeing 5 people - same model going down the walkway or just randomly spawning in the middle of the roads... The street performance with guitars or other instruments here and there was a nice addition, but besides that, city life could use a lot more attention to details. Overall I loved the game, I rarely 100% games, but I had fun doing that in this one, but to be fair I played it after major fixes - so there is that. I think it is a fantastic RPG, with fun gameplay mechanics, and the biggest selling point for me was its storytelling and of course the addition of Keanu Reeves.

_childDocuments_.review: So I wasn't hyped for this game at all until the day before release when I pre-ordered it, but I must say it has quickly become one of my favourite games in my library.   First of all, it looks absolutely fantastic, and I don't even play with ray tracing on with my 2060! Sure, my friends who play on there 30 series cards get a much better visual experience than I do, but I have genuinely never seen such a beautiful game before. The indoor and outdoor lighting is absolutely fantastic and it adds so much to the overall quality and immersion of the game.   The map itself, while not being the biggest, is certainly one of my favourite when you contrast the packed high-rise city centre to the sparse badlands. I can see why people are disappointed with their hopes of a vertical city which there admittedly isn't too much of and, even when it is accessible, it isn't made very obvious.   The story line has got to be one of the most engaging I have played through and it took me around 55 hours while focusing on side quest story lines too. The endings depend heavily on your completion of many side quests and can vary pretty heavily based on this. The game manages to create characters that you become somewhat emotionally attached with, especially Panam and River in my play through. It's so well written that everyone is exactly how they should be. Rouge is the character that doesn't seem to care too much, Panam isn't quite sure what to do with herself and River is the honest cop who's willing to take a risk to do right by his family.   But you can't talk about Cyberpunk without mentioning the bugs. Sure, I've came across a few visual and lighting glitches and T-posing characters, with a few friends falling through the map, but nothing really game breaking. Sure this will vary for everyone playing the game, but I just can't justify all the hate this game gets, unless of course you're a PS 4/Xbox One player.   Overall, I'd easily say this is now my favourite game and I can't see that changing for some time. Hopefully we'll get some more optimisation and bug fixes in the near future, but I'm loving it even without them. If I were to rate this from 1-10 I'd happily give it an 8.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just say first, that I didn't expect Cyberpunk to run beautifully with the specs I have. Somehow it runs nice on medium-high settings at 60 fps and in some dense areas with lots of moving things or effects at 30 fps. I also want to bring out that I remember watching the first teaser back in 2013 and saying to myself "ahh scary woman" since I was a little dumb boy then. Now I look at this game and call it a treasure trove of anything you can do. Cyberpunk 2077 Is a MAJOR step up from open world games we are used to like TES V: Skyrim or even the Witcher 3 : Wild Hunt. The amount of detail even on medium to high settings is a truly a sight to see. The Dialogue makes characters feel real, including your character "V". The Character customization is unlike any other, Cyberpunk is the first Commercially successful game with the ability to change the size of your Junk or have a Hoot-nanny as a dude, or even a junk as a girl. You can even customize you pubic hairs into a cute little heart! (A little weird but not unwelcome) Gunplay can sometimes feel a bit stiff, but this is coming from someone who plays a crap ton of tf2 so don't take my opinion without a large grain of salt. Perks and Attribute for your character really affects how you play. Whether you always want to take the stealthy route or go guns blazing really depends on how you spend your perk and attribute points. Enemies pose a tough challenge when they have the right guns and cybernetics. Driving in first person in my opinion feels the best, third person feels like your dunk and crashing into everything. The city's people seems small, as I have already seen the same npc walking the streets 3 times in 3 completely different areas all in the same day. I have encountered some bugs with foliage and lighting effects not rendering properly or glitching about when I look around. And some displaced enemies and npcs. Other than that this game is a Genuine pot of gold that is ripe for taking. I believe personally that this game was really worth the 7 year wait, and will become an example of open world games to come into light in the future. _childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying that I have just alt+F4'ed out of the game in a rage at a quest that I am clearly not ready to do, and despite the spew of negativity that you are about to read, there is something about this game that is fun. There is some intangible aspect to this game that I am having fun with, however, I am beyond comfortable saying that this game was not ready for market, and is NOT worth $60 in its current state.I can honestly say, this is an unfinished game. I'll preface this with a few things, firstly is an admission that I'm terrible at shooters so when I say the shooting is stiff and unrewarding take it with a grain of salt. The next three are all reviews. A number: 54/100, would I recommend anyone buy this game: No, I wouldn't and finally am I enjoying myself: Barely.Okay, so let's begin for anyone actually reading this. Chief complaint and honestly what has sunk the ENTIRE experience for me? The hell nightmare cluster♥♥♥♥ trench foot bastard that is the driving. I can't express the level of unfun and genuine repeller from the game the driving here is. I'm playing on mouse and keyboard, and I've often in my long 6 hours with this game expressed that the driving is akin to piloting an elephant on ice skates. No matter how little of how much I use the A or D key, the rear of my car swings out like a drift and starts my car fishtailing away as I try desperately to maintain control. The driving here is some of the worst I've ever experienced. The cars also won't auto path to objectives if placed on the route to them, ironically making this driving technology a regression from the Witcher's horses in 2015, by the same developer.Next is the bizarre and frustrating fact that your character customization options quite literally end at the creation screen. The second that you press "done" on your creation window you are locked into stone. There are no nail salons, no barbershops, no tattoo parlors and none of the body mods that were promised. The game throws you out into the world as a permanent and unchanging entity. Further, the tattoo options are limited to 5 or 6 presets for the face and body each. If you like *some* of a tattoo set but not all then tough luck, you take it all or none, and can never change it later. Hair color is bizarre as well, as far as I can tell there is no option to have a brown hair color, only amber or black, yet V's beard can be set to a normal brown meaning that the color pallet exists in the game.As said in my opener the shooting feels stiff and the aiming feels wrong. Couple this with the fact that despite me going all in on a body build and attempting to lower difficulty to normal when hitting brick walls, the melee combat seems to be wholly unviable. Enemies at equal or higher level simply maul V if you fight in any way other than a slow, cover-to-cover, peak and shoot style. The perks that V can take on level up are also lame, they don't have any cool or noticeable impact on the way that combat flows or plays, they just make simple and minor number changes and fail to add any fun or diversity to the combat.Spotty voice acting seems to plague missions, even main story ones. On the very first mission, where you're sent to steal a car, you meet the cars owner and the voice acting sounds like a child doing a voice over for a covid era science project. There are numerous other times that I've been jarred out of a cutscene by awful voice acting but that one stuck out to me the most of all.PAST HERE ARE SPOILERS FOR WHAT LIMITED STORY I'VE PLAYED; BE YE WARNED♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ man, could the writing surrounding the death of Jackie have been any worse? Seriously, what a joke that was. Despite CDPR spoiling this moment for themselves in the 1st mission playthrough that they released back in early 2020, let's look at all the MASH level corny self spoiling that happens leading up to this.1) Before you go into the Afterlife to meet Dex, Jackie says that he always feels like he's lying to his mom when he says everything is okay, and that he always feels deeper in ♥♥♥♥ the more you do. 2) Right after entering the Afterlife (yes, the sound you just heard was in fact CDPR hitting you over the head with the analogy and not just the wind) Jackie orders the drink of one of their "legends" and V can ask how you get a drink named after you. The answer? Die in an epic way, and literally right after this Jackie has the bartender write down his drink recipe so they can name a drink after him.3) On the way to the hotel for the heist V can remind Jackie to keep his head in the game to which Jackie will reply that he has worked his whole life to get out of this city and after this (say it with me 70's cop show fans) one last job™, he's never going back to broke.4) When you enter the hotel, Jackie will walk up to the bar entrance, turn to V and say that after this (one more time everyone) one last job™ he'd like to come back to this nice hotel with his money and his retirement and have fun with Misty, his girl back home.This kind of stuff is everywhere, the twists so far have been telegraphed, the writing has been either painfully convoluted or painfully obvious. The entirety of what is happening to me with Johnny feels jarring, unearned and has warped my play through by making me feel entirely disconnected from the story. I am, post chapter two, acutely aware of the fact that I'm playing a video game, and unlike in games like Saints Row and GTA, that is NOT a good thing for Cyberpunk.As said to begin. This game is not done, it should not have been released, and NO, you should NOT buy it for at least 6 months to a year post this review being written, I trust CDPR, I loved the Witcher 3 and place is as my favorite game of all time, it's why I went out on a limb and broke a personal rule to never get games on release. Given time, CDPR will patch this game to a point that it is worth the price tag, and probably release DLC to truly make Night City a place worth being explored. Until that time however, keep the $60.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks absolutely amazing, Night City is probably the most visually stunning environment I have seen in a game. The problem is, that's about all this game has going for it. Yes it looks amazing, but everything else is lacking. Let's start with the character customization. In all the marketing we saw, style and body modification were shown to be a huge part of what this  game would be about. What we got, however, was unremarkable. Aside from customizable genitals (which except for in the inventory menu, you will never see again after you've created your character) this character creator had no more depth than your average character customization in games, and in a lot of areas, it had less. Many of the NPCs in the game have cool looking cybernetic eyes, arms, and legs, but your character has no access to any of that. In terms of cybernetics that affect your appearance, all you really have are the little bits of metal on your face. To make matters even worse, once you've created your V, that's it. You can't change your appearance any more. Despite the fact that the ads implied in Night City, you could change your appearance and and body on a whim, you can't. Not even your hairstyle or tattoos, let alone cybernetics.The next thing I want to talk about is character choice. Aside from the intro mission, and maybe a few bits at the end of the game, you really don't have much control over V's personality or choices. V essentially becomes the same character no matter what you choose. For example, I chose Corpo as my lifepath. After the very first introductory mission, V went from being a cold, calculating Corpo completely devoid of morals, to being a passionate, tough talking mercenary. I had no say in the personality shift, the change just happens, and it happens in literally minutes.The world itself was also a let down. I went into this thinking it would be a sprawling open world with lots of exploring to do and interesting things to discover. But what I found was, while it is clear that tons of effort went into crafting the beautiful city, it really doesn't go deeper than the surface level. Yes there are tons of NPCs walking around, but the city does not live and breathe. It is completely static, and the AI leaves a lot to be desired. As many have already pointed out, the AI seem to be the absolute bare minimum, they walk, talk, and run away if you scare them. That's it. The police AI are a complete joke. If you get in trouble with the law, police just spawn feet away from you, no matter where you are. In the middle of the desert, on a freeway, on top of a building, police just materialize out of nowhere.The story definitely had it's moments, and I did very much like the ending I got. I was very disappointed that you do not get to go back to Night City afterwards, and see how your decisions affect the world. Instead, you are simply given the opportunity to go back to your last save before starting the final mission. I found that story missions, side missions, and gigs all played pretty much the same way. Accept a job, go in either guns blazing or silently, find something, then get out and accept your payment.The cybernetics and gear system was weird, to say the least. Even playing on hard, I never had any reason to get into crafting or cybernetics to be powerful enough to get by. I wanted to get into cybernetics more, but even doing all the side missions and gigs didn't yield enough money to be able to afford the good stuff. By the end of the game. I had only added one or two new cybernetics to my character. I was also disappointed with V's apartment. You get one apartment, you can't get new or nicer ones. On top of that, there is no reason to ever return to the apartment you do have. Yes you can stash stuff there, but that's it, other than that it is pointless and you can forget it even exists. I also found it strange that there was no way to customize or upgrade cars. You spend so much time in your vehicles, but you can't do anything with them besides drive from point A to point B.This is tough, because if it had been advertised as what it is, I might have thought it was a really good game. But aside from visually, this game was not nearly as deep as I got the impression it would be. Part of the blame lies with me, after the Witcher 3 I had faith that CDPR would deliver another masterpiece. That was an unrealistic expectation I realize. But at the same time, I don't think anyone can deny that this game is not what we were told it would be. Yes it  was probably largely the media that made expectations so high, but I do believe that CDPR did, in this case, overpromise and underdeliver. If Steam had a numerical rating system, I'd probably give the game a 7/10. But because I have to choose recommend or don't recommend, I have to choose the negative option. I might reconsider later on after patches and DLC, but I believe many of the problems cannot be fixed in that way.

_childDocuments_.review: Upd: finished the game after two years and completed side gigs and jobs. This game is a horrible waste of resources - all this time, work and money could've been spent to create something which didn't introduce more dirt into the world. The only good thing about the whole game were guided zen meditation sessions - those were the real deal and remarkably well done. But you can grab it off Youtube so there's no need to waste your time on this game since it has nothing else of value to offer.original review below: I appreciate this game exists and at the same time I'm displeased it does. With superb worldbuilding, pleasant enough gameplay, a blend of Tokyo with the fast forward of what America is sliding towards, the game is undermined by poor writing full of plotholes and cheap clichés sewn together in a manner that the supposed canvas looks closer to a wire fence, but I suppose climbing it in the dazzling environment of the Cyberpunk is part of the fun with plenty of room to sink your fingers into. The climbing process is unpleasant, fingers digging into the wire, but at the end of it all you poke your head in and get shot but miraculously survive anyway also nanites son lmao aren't we clever and that is on top of having the discourtesy of reminding civilised people that California exists. At the same time, CDPR has seen a rise of purple haired twitter people into their HR and development team one cannot really be surprised by immersive displays of failures of the human race. Speaking of showcasing a dysfunctional society which is understandably a staple of the genre, it has been a while since a game has commanded a similar degree of revulsion in myself, which prompts an ambiguous feeling. For all the failures of soulless, lazy, uninspired writing and shoehorned celebrity arc, the world and people in it are believable and realistic. The problem, of course, it's that they are profoundly disgusting much like the world they live in and are quite content being that way. Is the ability to produce supremely gross characters so faithfully good or bad writing? You decide, but the fact the world is profoundly disagreeable is undeniable. In a city with a few actual human beings with a sense of decency and self-respect, most likely injected for a tantalising contrast, dwelling in a city populated solely by sub-humans, brutalised by neon entertainment and each other even choice of lovers is disappointing, with "body type" locked options obviously denying healthy human interactions. The CDPR director did specify in one of the early interview how much of a big deal sacrum profanum is going to be (not the quest, profaning the sanctity of things thought - or better left as the case may be - untouchable), creating such an in- (or rather sub)human, filth-encrusted world wearing the face of a formerly human being stapled to it in a morbid attempt of make up illuminated by neon lights is a momentous achievement.  The Emperor's death is highly symbolic too, with the last relic of the old world where manners meant something clocked by a self-indulging hedonist with no self-restraint suggests the writers knew what they were doing, wink and nod shot to you, the player, asking for an understanding thumbs up.  None came from me, unfortunately, and the resources sunk into something to create a monument to filth and ugliness might've been better spent elsewhere. The real dealbreaker is that Cyberpunk 2077 doesn't seem like a work of fiction, but a sober projection of the state of humanity, cybernetics or not, which turns it from an open world Deus Ex HR-like shenaniganry into existential horror, though the game doesn't offer any warning nor judges.  Beauty can't save the world because there's none left in Cyberpunk and neither will love, excised from human interactions by the builders of the brave new world comfortably sitting in their offices and tweeting about asinine nonsense on company time. Impressive, very nice. Hats off, really. I hope you never do it again.

If you want to be real rebels, as we claimed to be, it needs to start from the ground up because the folks that built this incredible Polish studio have become the things they claimed to fight against from the start.FEB-19-2022: The 10gb patch has fixed the performance issues! :)We put years of our lives into this game and this is not the legacy we wanted to leave behind. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Now is gud.- Nice atmosphere and graphics but gameplay is seriously outdated. - Choices do not matter. You do not even have choices to be honest, conversations are just "answer A" and "answer B" and whichever you pick makes no difference. - Interactions feel clunky, looting is an absolute unresponsive nightmare. - Night City is gorgeous and the atmosphere is amazing but fails to feel genuine. It only seems to serve as a background to the main story.- NPCs act strange and their reactions are not realistic. Every NPC you try to interact with somehow seems to be offended for no reason. You may walk by them and they'll great you in a nice way, but as soon as you press "F" to interact, they'll be treating you like you slapped their mother in the back of a dark alley. You park your car and when you come back to the area not only has it moved but also it's levitating 50cm above the ground.
