_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: 01.10.23: The game IS better, the character development system were improved, but 2+ years old bugs STILL persist. If it was launched as of 2.0, the reception would be better - and I COULD perhaps recommend it - that was not the case, through. The DLC provided fresh qualities and is clearly a must-play for anybody who at least "liked" the base game.OLD REVIEW:As much as I enjoyed just cruising the Night City, doing side-quests and helping NCPD with all the bandits around the place, the game just feels incomplete.All the bugs (flickering palm trees, cars spawning within each other and flying up, corpses flying through the map etc.) is one thing. Lacking traffic AI is another. Incredibly stupid enemy AI yet another. Brutal scaling of enemies even on normal is tough to understand. Useless "street cred" which I maxed out in about 28 hours of exploration. That's just what I remember at the moment,What hurt me most was the main plot. When the game finished, i felt like someone forgot to add about 50%+ of the content. The execution of the ending I got was pretty fine, but the story quality and length overall is insufficient for an AAA+ game which Cyberpunk was advertised to be. The plot didn't really refer a lot to the reality of 2077 and didn't elaborate too much on problems you could read about in notes found around the city.I really wish I could recommend the game to you, but I just can't do it in all honesty. If anything, wait for a GOTY edition when it's perfectly playable and simply cheaper to buy. Right now, buying Cyberpunk is a risk - a risk not worth taking.EDIT: Added another 50+ hours to get all the achievements done. My anti-recommendation stands, and at least 3-4 achievements are frustratingly easy to miss - which is IMHO not good game design. Still - hardly any game in history has given me so much pleasure in basically running around for 100h~ clubbing/shooting bandits.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Amazing storytelling. Vivid, expansive world that feels alive and vibrant. Lots of replay-ability, with a unique approach to building your character. Very limited restrictions placed on decisions when creating your own build. Go fast and blow ♥♥♥♥ up, or sneak around like a rat living in the cameras, the choice is yours. But most importantly, sad boy vibes from beginning to end. All time favorite RPG atm.Cons- You do not gain enough experience to reach your max level in the main skills you use. I had to clear a majority of side content, only using quickhacks to get that specific skill to 20. Took me nearly 90 hrs (of very casual gameplay not always focusing on this skill) to hit that cap.Difficulty spikes are odd, you can easily out level most of the content without really filling out your skilltrees, and ultimately the content becomes too easy once you reach that point. A lot of interesting buildings are not accessible internally. Sometimes making things too big can be an issue. Would like to see a lot of the "empty space" used. Japan town would feel so much more alive if everything was more compact and interact-able.

_childDocuments_.review: !!!!!ALL THE COMMENTS BELOW ARE SUBJECTIVE!!!!!First thing first, I do like the game, I am a huge fan of Cyberpunk. They have crafted a great world and city for this genre and I am really enjoying it. It's just there are so many more that needed to be added before it really becomes a great Open World RPG FPS with a Cyberpunk theme. Besides all the performance issues and bugs which luckily I have only encounter a few, Right now I would rate this one only a mediocre game due to the characters and plot hard carrying while other aspects are quite a let down for me. Here is the list that most of the stuff I concerned about : 1. NPC AI issueI think most people spoke/knew about this already so I am not gonna explain this one.2. EquipmentCurrently, feels like the weapons/implants are not enough at all cause I am a Gun-Nut & Tech-Lover but still the number of weapons and implants is not satisfying at all.The weapon, the whole level up/crafting system feels redundant for me. There is no point crafting your own weapon because it's just the same one with better stats (sometimes) than the one you can get from killing the enemy. Also, Infinitely upgrading your weapon to get better stats doesn't make sense to me at all. And only 2 customizations (scope/suppressor) for a gun is not enough at all. Not to mention I was hoping we can craft a gun (literally from scratch) by getting/crafting different weapons parts like stock, barrel etc. (I know it's too much to ask but still, it's just what I hope for) The implants, most of the implants you see in the early stages are basically all you will find. The differences between them are mostly just level(color) and the statistic. I mean come on it's 2077, shouldn't your high-tech eyeball come with Thermal / Night Vision etc? But no, it just comes with more slots for chips when you level them up. Also, the scene where you installed your eyeball for the first time was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool! Though I also didn't expect that was the only scene, after the prologue, you just buy it straightly from the store and boff, it's installed immediately.3. VehicleBuying a car, every buyable car is a side quest which confuses me. This is not how we buy a car in the world right? Also, it feels like there is no purpose to drive a vehicle at all. For traveling you can simply use fast travel (I know some people enjoying driving around the city, that's fine, I enjoy that too.). For combat, enemy can still shoot you but you can't fight back in a vehicle. I even once stole a police car and found out that I cannot turn on the light and siren. With the broken driving AI in-game, there isn't really much point using a vehicle.4. QuestGetting a quest after the prologue is mostly boring. You always get messaged or called by a random that you have never heard of or interact with. It would be so much better if we can get the quest from the Fixer face to face, discussing the mission details. And I thought Netwatcher is spying on the network? Shouldn't we take a safer approach to discuss crimes other than using the radio/email/phone? Getting a quest by just a call or message really kills the immersion for being a merc/gangster for me. It also made some of the side quests feel really dull because lack of the explaining. And no, I don't think reading collected text is a good way to understand quest lore.5. GangsThey put so much time advertising different gangs and such but when I am playing, I feel like they feel just like background lore than actual elements that are ingame. Different gangs use the same weapon, the same tactic. The only differences between them are just the language they speak and the appearance.Also feels like there is missing a reputation system. I killed so many Tyger Claw members but Wakako Okada still treated me like it's nothing. There is rarely any interaction between the gangs. I heard you will have random encounters where Gangs VS Gangs or NCPD VS Gangs but I haven't meet any of them so far. Doesn't really seem to use all the potential from the gangs since you have already invested so much time introducing them before the game release.6. CorpoI love all these powerful Corpo settings but similar to gangs, I don't feel like the Corpo appeared enough in the game other than the story. For example Militech, other than the chip and bot we saw from the prologue, I thought we were going to see some weapon, vehicle and implants from these big ass Corpo but no, there are almost none. 7. PoliceThe police are so broken so I decided to separate it from the NPC AI. The way that they behave is utterly unacceptable in the game. - If you are fighting the gang on the street and someone accidentally hurt an innocent. The NCPD will come for you and you only but not also the illegal gangsters that are also fighting you.- When they put a bounty on you, they immediately spawned around/behind/in front of you which is the stupidest part. You can search for videos online if you are interested to see how broken they are lol.- If you try to fight them, you will get a higher wanted level but only result in spawning more and more cops right next to you.- If you try to run away, get in a vehicle, drive two blocks away and wait for 30 seconds. The bounty will be dropped like it never happen.8. MinigameLike come on, in Witcher 3 you gave us Gwent. I thought you are going to give us something special this time as well.9. Other QOL changes- Able to sit, buy food and drinks from the store but not just through the inventory UI.- Crafting should get a button to decide how you craft at once- Selling stuff should allow you to sell a bunch of stuff at once- Braindance?- Tattoo and changing appearanceEtc.At last, I feel like a looooooooooooot of content have been cut out, like in the prologue you can see they fast-forwarded the 6 months with Jackie. Don't tell me that was planned completely from the start...because when the game actually started, there is so little info about wtf is going on around our life, the characters, the gangs, the neighbourhood, the city,  etc. And I believe those should be in the first 6 months after we met Jackie (I chose Nomad lifepath btw) but was cut out...... for some reason.There are other aspects that I might have missed or misunderstood. Feel free to fill in the gap or correct me.But !!!!!ALL THE COMMENTS ABOVE ARE SUBJECTIVE!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes yes yes, it's buggy, glitched, and unoptimized. But don't let that distract you from the fact that this game is a mediocre RPG at best. Only 2% of your dialogue choices affect the story in any way, and even the ones that might have some impact are minor. The main story is completely linear and you will have the exact same missions regardless of the choices you make, the ending you get is completely dependent on the choices you make in the final mission, everything else is inconsequential. Faction relationships are not even a thing, and the romances are so bare-bones it's funny.  So don't expect a genre-defining, branching-path RPG; expect a looter-shooter FPS with mediocre mechanics. The gear system is the opposite of satisfying, weapon variety is almost non-existant and 95% of the time you're just getting a couple more points to your dps. Of course you have the classic RPG problem where the most efficient clothing end up making you look like a robot trying to learn how humans dress. Progression is meh, the late tier perks can be pretty cool but early on it's worthless ♥♥♥♥ like "gain 3% damage" or "10% less recoil" that doesn't actually affect how you play. Not worth $60, wait until it's on sale (added benefit of the bugs hopefully being gone by then), or just play Fallout 4 instead (it's legit a better RPG).

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this review if and when I feel differently (when CDPR addresses the glaring issues in the game). There are three main ones I take issue with: 1. The treatment of the CDPR employees with regard to the development 'crunch' close to release. This is blatant exploitation and it needs to be addressed by ALL game companies, including CDPR. If that means that Cyberpunk 2077 is a commercial and/or critical failure, then so be it. Let it be a lesson to game companies. People should not have to sacrifice their mental and physical well-being for the sake of entertainment. 2. The inclusion of (mandatory to complete the game) segments in the story that are known to cause epileptic seizures. That is unacceptable and should have been removed way before the game's launch.3. Pardon my French, but the half-assing of trans inclusion within the character creator. I've seen many trans people online be disappointed by the character creator. Either do it to a standard that does justice to gender expression/identity, or don't include the option at all. At the time of writing this review, Cyberpunk 2077 is an unpolished, glitchy mess and in my opinion highlights all the major issues with the gaming industry as a whole. , underneath all this mess of a game lies a  story; I feel it needs to be said that the quest-line, the voice acting, the relationships you build with these characters (especially Johnny Silverhand) are the one saving grace of the game because its phenomenal. _childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those games that's very decisive or at least that is what most people see. The community dumped on the game at launch for poor performance, lack of true life paths, the seemingly small amount of legitimate love interests in the game, and a pretty substantial list of other complaints. I honestly agree with both sides, this game is lukewarm to me. I don't love it, but its not that bad.Pros:-Game looks amazing if you can max it out or run at mostly high.-Voice acting for the main cast is superb and V and Johnny stand out above all.-Gunplay is fantastic and the variety of guns and the way they all handle differently was surprising.-The character customization (the beginning) was in depth, although the hairstyles felt lacking.-A sizable amount of fun side quests and side objectives.-The soundtrack is one of the best in any modern game.-The quickhack system is quite fun and not super difficult to learn.Cons:-Poorly optimized, not only on consoles but PC as well. -The life path start was cool for about 10 min then utterly sucked. (if you don't know why, look it up I want to keep this spoiler free)-The fact I can't change my haircut or haircolor is outrageous. Also, there are clearly tattoo parlors, please why can't we get more.-One of the biggest things are the the visual bugs and bugs in general. It's so bad that I had to restart a save less than an hour into the game because of a bug. There are so many visual bugs, from T-Posing NPCs, textures missing, texture pop in, textures slowly changing even once you are close, cars literally phasing out of existence or just being 2D sprites from just a few hundred meters away. In my 25 hour main story play through I saw enough bugs that I pretty much figured this was just a good looking indie game not a AAA developed near decade long endeavor. As bad as the cons are the game itself is still pretty decent. I'd personally give it somewhere between a 7 and 7.5 out of 10. I don't feel like 100% the game like I did with Sleeping Dogs or GTA4 and 5. This game is good, but not amazing. Simply put, if its $40 or less, thats a good price, $60 is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of players arriving in Night City for the first time this week, I was blown away by just how good Cyberpunk: Edgerunners was.  Half way through the series I checked the price on CP: 2077 which was 50% off.  F*cking nova!!20 hours in and absolutely loving this game.  One thing that has made this such a memorable and unique experience is coming from the show straight to the game.  I have a hard time paying attention and remembering lore, characters, factions, and world building in larger games.  Reading random things I find, listening to audio recordings, and hearing dialog that is stilted and boring just isn't enough to make real connections between everything so I can immerse myself in this world and its characters to the point where I believe its an actual place.Enter: Edgerunners.  This show is so freaking good at everything it is doing.  Night City feels like a real place and the vendors, bars, ripperdocs, corporations and people all feel very connected even when ultra violence can happen anytime.   All the characters seem important and interesting.  The protaganoists, antagonists, rippers, runners, psychos, and even the randomly killed characters with 2 seconds of screen time.I could go on, but this isn't a review for the show  :)So basically I feel more connected with this game going in and I understand more about what is happening in each mission and around the city which makes me feel like my time is more important.  In short, this is one of the few RPGs I've played where I can actually believe this could be a place and these could be real characters worthy of my empathy, sympathy, and time.  If you really love the Netflix Anime, and you haven't given Cyberpunk: 2077 a shot, this is the time to do it.  $29.99 is a great price.  Plus the studio is planning even more updates and FREE DLC in the future.  Buy the damn game!Graphics 10/10Audio 10/10Dialog 10/10Mechanics 10/10Character Development 10/10Fighting 10/10Family Friendly 0/10

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get the big question out of the way first.  Yes, the game is play-ready.  Minor bugs still exist, but they rarely surfaced in my playthrough and were generally brief and undisruptive besides two instances that I could recall.  Grab it on sale if you can, but I would be okay with full price given the experience I had.If you can look past the media storm surrounding the game's launch failure, what you'll find is an earnest and expansive RPG.  Night City and its surrounding areas are a joy to behold.  This game is so often compared unfavorably to the Witcher 3 in terms of story content, but I found it gripping enough.  You will run into enough interesting side quests, from silly to sentimental to downright absurd, to appreciate the lives of other denizens in the city.  V's relationship with Johnny Silverhand feels authentic, particularly since the two of them have plenty of time to converse in missions big and small.  For someone well known to be nice, Keanu Reeves played a grade-A rebel jerk well.Some things can be improved.  Talents and skills feel less interesting than they should be, as they are generally simple stat boosts.  On the other hand, if you settle on one of the many, many overpowered builds, combat becomes trivial.  The game's promo made a big deal of the fashions in this world, but as each gear is tied to defense and mod slots, and new gears pop up so often, you will rarely have the luxury of settling on a particular look.  For such a well-realized world, Night City is curiously devoid of any side activities that show facets of the city besides street crimes and more street crimes.  I would've loved to see some kind of stock trading side game or hacking game,  At the very least, a few brawl matches and races beyond what's found in quests would've made the world feel more well-rounded.  I know the game is not designed to be like GTA, but a more comprehensive approach to in-game activities would make this beautiful world feel more alive.Regardless of these criticisms, Cyberpunk 2077 is worth your time.  I recommend slowing down.  Read the shards.  Minimize fast travel.  Take a walk in the streets of night city and just soak in the atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is an unfortunate thing. I wish I could recommend this game to anyone, because it  the potential to be a ultra-modern gaming experience that would go down in history as one of the best RPGs ever. Is this an unfair expectation? Maybe, but it's nothing the developers didn't build themselves with everything they said this game would be and more. Everyone already knows what happened pre-release, the laughable patches after, the game itself (what it actually is, what it isn't, what could be, what's missing, what's broken, etc:.), then there was the release of Edgerunners and a huge chunk of the playerbase coming back and liking the game this time around...I came back as well, for a fresh new playthrough, and I am surprised I am actually having fun this time, but when I know I added the disclaimer in my head that I absolutely could not expect to have the basic degree of control  in this kind of game and I had to deal with dialogue choices that remind us of telltale syndrome but worse, I can't say this is worth it. Don't get me wrong, I am enjoying this but I am not particularly fond of having to shut my brain off at times to do so. I am happy I am able to finally play this game properly and most of the game-breaking bugs have been dealt with but I can't recommend this at all when I feel you can have a better experience with other titles NO MATTER what you are looking for. Do you want a good dystopian RPG in which you have narrative control? Check out some Fallout games. Do you want specifically something Cyberpunk? Look no further than Deux Ex. Go and play the Mass Effect series if you haven't already, The Outer Worlds, etc:. Maybe you would enjoy Borderlands? I am almost 100% sure there is a game out there for you that is more worth its price than this, and will provide you with a better experience, SPECIALLY if you want a good story, or at least one that fits the game itself.TL;DR: Nightcity is so pretty riding on your motorcycle, but you stop by something you find interesting and you can't interact with it. This is not what an open world RPG should be, Cyberpunk 2077 is not worth its price unless you absolutely want to play this game, and I stress  in particular. Edgerunners is amazing, and if you are considering coming back because of it by all means do it and have some fun!

The story telling is forced down the player's throat. They don't show you much but tell you everything to the point it's grueling. From a world stand-point, the map is excellent. If it weren't for the hand-crafted AI that is brain-dead it'd be immersive. They took a well designed map and ruined it with deaf AI.In a year this game will be on discount and have all/most the bugs fixed.100%'d the game in 80 hours. Not worth.TL;DR the core loop is okay. hacking is fun. the ai sucks. the story needs more. wait a year.

_childDocuments_.review: It has bugs, it has glitches.My experience with cyberpunk so far has been enjoyable, the combat seems a bit basic, stealth is overpowered, hacking is interesting to use, melee seems pretty basic, it's just mainly bashing left click. I like that you are able to customize the weapons, add silencers, scopes, chips that are helpful for stealth.The skill system is like of any other RPG, you get skill points, you put them into skill trees. Some doors in the game require you to have a specific level of body or intelligence to get into, some dialogue options require you to have a specific level in the "cool" category, some require body and so on, this puts depth into dialogues, and kind of forces you to be a jack of all trades.The character creation is pretty interesting, there are only 2 voices you can choose from, a feminine and a masculine, 2 body types that are feminine and masculine as well, lots of choices on your hair, eyes, even fingernails. You can choose your genitalia but it seems like it's more for laughs.The story and the characters you meet is amazing, mostly everything comes together in the ending, the different characters feel alive when they call you with jobs or just information about past jobs, what they did. It is pretty immersive but the glitches like characters stopping talking or broken animations break the immersion barrier.The world is pretty vast, it has interesting areas, different regions, driving seems to be too sensitive at most times. There are a lot of quest areas around but they are pretty much the same. Eliminate target, Eliminate all targets, Steal the item.I guess this game depends on the person who plays it. Some might be let down because the game was hyped to hell and back and they expected more, but it is a new game, in every newly released game there are optimization issues, bugs and glitches. I believe the game developers are going to fix everything in time, so i recommend anyone who is interested in the game to buy it after 2 months of it release so that they would not be so disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Was never as bad upon release as the reddit hivemind tried to convince everyone it was but is also not nearly as good as that same hivemind does now.• Unbearably corny, inappropriately kitschy and just always "off": this bizarre cultural disconnect makes sense considering the almost complete lack of Americans or at least native English speakers on the writing team• Not a single Johnny Silverhand moment lands in any way other than flat on its face thanks to awful writing and truly TRAGIC voice acting• Constant at-the-top-of-your-lungs moralizing and impotent, artificial drama the writers constantly try to squeeze from severely undercooked characters with barely any screen time to properly set them up first• Style over substance in just about everything from the character writing to the weak world building: CDPR's idea of cyberpunk era hyper-sexualization is just a million sex shops, le dildos everywhere and penises featured in ads• Not a SINGLE interesting side-quest SWEET LORD: it's abundantly clear CDPR is unable to create interesting stories and characters from scratch when there isn't a pile of books to get their inspiration from• Txt files sharted out into every damn corner of the game are NOT a proper narrative device and are NOT good content• Total lack of a sense of place: the gangs are all region-based reskins with nothing to deepen or set them apart, vendors peddle the exact same things regardless of whether they're placed somewhere downtown NC or in the middle of a desert, the lack of new or region-based challenges, the general lack of LIFE, interactivity and meaningful detail• Witcher 3's setting and story successfully hid away the lifelessness and the non-interactivity of its open world; Cyberpunk with its bustling metropolis and a lack of a deep main character from a book does neither.• Constant Half-Life 2-esque cutscene-gameplay blend sections that, just like 20 years ago, fail to capitalize on the good sides of its two parts while also inheriting the bad sides of both: most scenes like that are neither particularly well-directed nor offer much (or sometimes ANY) interactivitytl;dr quintessential 'ESL cool'

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 hours, I can say that Cyberpunk 2077 has been one of the WORST gaming experiences I've had in MANY YEARS.The gameplay loop is boring, the movement feels clunky as hell, the combat feels like garbage, and the NPCs, vehicles, and enemies are literally braindead. Also, unlike in any other great RPG, there is zero sense of natural progression in this game.The game fast-forwards through the most meaningful parts of an RPG and let's you have almost anything you want without having to earn it through gameplay and character development.The open world of this game is beautiful but it's very superficial. To me it feels like a glorified loading screen for quests. It lacks a lot of basic features that other great open world games (not necessarily RPGs) have had for 15+ years. It's ridiculous. I can't believe it.Even if they manage to make this game playable by fixing most of the bugs it currently has, for me it will still be a mediocre game at best. It doesn't feel good to play, and the story is not engaging me too much or making me want to play it anyway just to see how it continues.I just can't believe that the NPCs and the vehicles have literally no AI. Police can't even drive cars and they spawn on foot right in front of your face. The wanted system is useless. All the vehicle rides are scripted. In the racing side quests the other cars literally teleport behind you if you leave them too far behind. And they slow down A LOT if you're losing.Every enemy is a bullet sponge and shooting at them feels like ♥♥♥♥. Why do developers keep making enemies like this!? It's not fun at all! Keep weapons powerful so that they feel good to shoot. I understand this is an RPG but they could have just made the weapons hard to use (like for example adding movement to the camera, so it's hard to aim), and then remove those effects via character development and progression.There's tons of more stuff I don't like about this game that I could talk about all day, but I'm tired of it. And sadly I don't think any of that stuff will change in the future. It would be too much work and the game was simply designed this way.A big disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: So every couple of months I find myself wanting to play cyberpunk - and then I go to play, and realize I want to play something *like* cyberpunk 2077 , but not actually cyberpunk 2077. The character creator is boring and under-equipped considering that customizability is meant to be the point of the transhuman future, and frankly is one of the things I find most disappointing. Your options are limited, you can't control your body shape, the tattoo selection is boring, you have no ability to choose cyber limbs, or any of the other cool features that you see on NPCs, like exposed mechanical elbows or glossy skin tones. Also, the fact you can't change your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character design once you get out of the creator ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks. They could have just paid a dozen furries for a couple of months and they would have built something 10 million times better.The majority of the skill tree is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ +x% to stuff; the combat feels (to me personally) as uncanny valley - not as loose and terrible as Fallout, but certainly not smooth and precise (although, to be fair, i just could be not good at it). The item system is grindy and the customizations are fine, i guess, but could be better.Hacking is fun, I did actually enjoy that part.As for the campaign, there's a pretty bug 2-hour long quest with a bunch of cutscenes and stuff you *have* to do to get out of the starting area into the rest of the game. This is the biggest thing hindering my replays - I do not give a ♥♥♥♥ about redoing Konpeki plaza. Once I did it once, every new iteration was boring. Having do redo the braindance ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ again, and then Konpeki is just tedious.The politics are also tedious. Obviously, people have a variety of opinions within the game, but they're just so shallow. All of johnny's impotent rage feels hollow, and since no-one else in the game really expouses any criticism of the world they live in, despite the obvious flaws. Not does the world feel politically well developed - it doesn't do a good job of showing abject poverty, or corporations trying to extract every single credit or dollar or whatever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ currency the game uses, or really communicating the collapsing nature of the planet they live on, or the ways in which technology enables people to oppress people. Dan Olson's breakdown of privacy with crypto is a really good example of what they could have explored, for example. I overheard two cops in game talking about how they're rolling out mind-scanning tech and the other officer saying 'well i have nothing to hide' and it never came up again. Cyberpsychosis is also a poor way to model the impact of cybernetics disconnecting people from everyone else; but that's hardly CD Projekt's fault, so much as an issue with the original setting. I don't know how much the writers researched beyond the source material, but there is so much more depth and complexity that could have been explored within the game. Finally, the world - I feel like this world could really, really benefit from layered environments. Trying to get to the Arasaka float is actually a good example of how this was done right, in specific places. But this game really deserves the level of detail in vertical mobility that dishonoured or assassin's creed have,  especially once you get the double-jump legs. There is a considerable lack of environmental hazards which would really do a good job of selling the posioned nature of this city, and just a lack of crowding - if they had of crowded the city more with buildings then maybe they wouldn't run into issues with rendering NPCs, while really being able to sell the overpopulated nature of the city.Overall, CD Projekt tried - they really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tried. But they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crashed and burned so hard, like a studio-sized icarus. They bit off more than can chew, even for a studio that really has successfully made some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ huge games before. I really hope they manage to fix some of these problems, or, if that's not possible due to the monumental cluster♥♥♥♥ they find themselves in, release a decent suite of mod tools. You know, the old Bethesda route - if you can't make a decent game, rely on the players to fix it for you. Fundamentally, a game like this thrives on customizeabilty, and they just failed to do that.If you have the cash and like triple-A games, try it out; otherwise don't bother. Your time is better spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s start with the world and the visuals. The graphics are generally breathtaking (definitely comparable to the red gummy bears!).  Night City is a sight to behold. Especially the raytraced lighting really shines with all the neon lights everywhere, giving the city a realistic eyegasmic look. The illusion of a breathing, living world falls apart though, if you look too closely. The “inhabitants” of Night City feel like bland robots, walking from A to B no matter what, with no brain. The spawn system randomizes the look certain body parts and then spawns these creatures into the world. Sadly, this system does not check if it spawns an NPC-instance more than once in the same area. Occasionally, the same pink-haired meatbags spawn in hordes in a radius of 25 meters... A quote of  describes that phenomenon really well: .There are some interesting, big buildings, that you would love to explore from the inside, but in nearly all cases you will be greeted with the typical “X – Closed”- UI hint, when you walk towards any door. The Main Story is awesome and is the reason that made me keep playing Cyberpunk until the end. Some characters are just hilariously bad and bland (-> “Adam Smasher”) and some parts of the main storyline were obviously cut out, especially in the first Act of the game (-> Jacky). The main aspects, regarding the impact of technical modification of the human body in the near future, the resulting consequences and the question of what it means to be “alive” and “human” are well handled. First, I did not care about Johnny at all, and thought he was quite annoying shouting his “Anti Corpo”-propaganda into the ears of my V every five minutes. However, progressing through the story more and more, he grew on me. Keanu Reeves was a worthy investment.Some of the side quests also tell unique and interesting stories that add value to the overall experience and tone of the game. Depending on which quests you did and partially, which decisions you made, there are a few different endings, that range from “okay” to “Damn, that was actually quite nice”. Like most Open World games nowadays, Cyberpunk also falls into the category of games, that attempt to artificially blow-up the playtime by adding meaningless, repetitive “content” to the game. The so called “gigs” and “NCPD”-hustles are sprinkled over the map, like too much salt on fries. These activities always follow the same few patterns: “Kill all people and collect a Gucci back, that is laying around there” and “Go into that building, free that guy… oh and by the way, that closed door, never mind it! There is an open window if you look 90 degrees to your left or right”. This type of content adds nothing to the experience of the game and feels like those weird liquorice bats added to the gummy bear boxes (for people who like those ones:  …You kind of do not want to have them, but you bought them with the whole package.The gunplay feels generally solid, there is a lot of variety of ranged weaponry. The Stealth gameplay also works quite well, with its quick-hack mechanics and can be fun at times. The melee combat on the other hand feels bland to jokingly bad and consists of the same two to three, clunky animations chained together repeatedly. The dismemberment looks quite satisfying though!The skill tree consists mostly of entries that provide passive stat-manipulations with no real impact on gameplay. To be honest that part of the game could have been cut out completely and I wouldn’t have noticed it at all! The Cybernetics are fun to use and change the way to play the game. There is a lot of variety offered and trying out new combinations and modifications is adding a lot to the gameplay experience! Especially the “bullet-time-like”-feature and the arm projectile launcher are a joy!Audio-wise this game is a mixed bag and suffers from several issues. Sometimes music or ambient sounds randomly disappear abruptly or are missing their fade out-effects. Certain audio-effects are often playing at a way too high or low volume depending on the distance of the player. Those issues are occurring way too often, sadly. The bugs and issues regarding the mixing and spatial audio were the ones, that broke the immersion for me the most in this game. The soundtrack enhances the atmosphere and fits the game perfectly! There are some so called “bangers” in there, as the eloquent kids of the modern world would say! A few more combat tracks would have been nice. The same few action tracks repeat a bit too often for my taste. But in general, great music and the sound effects are also good, just the mixing is totally messed up.Besides the annoying aforementioned audio issues, there are a handful of other bugs, regarding the pathfinding of the AI and some animation issues that can break immersion. Those can be quite funny at the same time though. Each player will experience a different number of bugs, maybe some are even lucky and do not encounter ones at all, I encountered many. Besides some T-Posing while driving a car, NPCs walking in the air or godlike, flying traffic lights, that could be mostly ignored, there are also some bugs that negatively impacted the experience. An Issue, where UI elements did not turn on/off after entering/leaving a vehicle occurred way more often than I would have liked. At one point a dialogue/interaction option that already got triggered, stayed in the dialogue-options and could be triggered again, teleporting me to a position where I have been a few moments ago and blocking the progression of the quest. Most of these issues could be resolved by loading a recent checkpoint, but those bugs negatively impacted the fun I had with the game. All the bugs are a testament of a game, that needed way time in the oven. More than one additional year for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game that you should play if you like story heavy single player games. But do not get it expecting an amazing open world like GTA. CDPR did a great job with this game when it comes to the main story of the game. The side missions are a mixed bag, some are actually good side missions which complements the story where others felt like filler. Then you have gigs which felt like unimportant side missions. And then the 100s of random things to do that are all pretty much the same and which you have no reason to even do ( except for the minor cash reward for completing them ).The open world is gorgeous on one side, however is feels very empty despite all the npcs walking around on the other. Exploring the city also did not feel very rewarding. It is mostly a backdrop for the story. There was nothing else to do. Even the cop mechanics just come down to; you shoot someone, cops literally spawn next to you out of nowhere, you drive off, they forget about you.  The story and side missions is where it is at. The rest seems just built around that . So besides the graphics and story which I loved, there are some elements I did really really hate. Those would be the UI that is clunky and at times I couldn't even find certain things. The radio and music really were a bore for me and did nothing to add to the atmosphere. A really wasted chance. Even the TV ( that you never use ) did more for atmosphere and world building.

_childDocuments_.review: Late into 2020 we finally get to see the release of one of the most anticipated games of the year and needless to say the bumps in the road have left their mark on  wheels. The story takes place in a vibrant and beautiful futuristic world that regrettably, lacks the substance to take advantage of its setting and leaves something more to be desired. Keep reading to find out why! is one of the games that had me hyped up for its release, I fell in love with  after playing the Witcher 3 in console way back and I was sorely disappointed in the result of this title. The vibrant world it presents and shows us with amazing reflections and lights illuminating the city, giving life to it is brought down by the gameplay and the way the systems are designed.To illustrate this, the perk system is based on bonuses such as "deal 10% more damage with light machine guns" or "reload 5% faster" and those are boring upgrades to attain while playing. We as players want to do crazy stuff, meaningful stuff and to see most upgrades just be bonuses leaves a feeling of desiring something more. I would have preferred being able to soak up the damage by using a steel arm or slowing time in gunfights rather than the skills we got. While there are mechanical upgrades, these tend to be few and are insignificant as well half the time.Gunplay is also sort of clunky, giving a sensation of being dull and slow while integrating numbers into the mix that adds more into an already heavily packed HUD. You aim and shoot while getting to cover and playing  recently has shown me that you can make shooting a gun very fun. There is not enough movement during combat to feed the trigger and make those explosive situations action-packed and memorable! It behaves more like a classic RPG rather than a true shooter in that regard.A lot of the issues that  suffers from have been seen in  years ago and yet  keeps committing the same mistakes. Granted, is an open world so is bound to have glitches and such but the number of issues you can find here can give you such a migraine…like in my case after losing all my progress 10 hours into the game.The story can be interesting at points as they use suspense to make you play more to find out what happens next and during the first few hours, it can pull you in with a fantastic storyline job. Then it ruins it by introducing to you way too many characters for you to be able to bond with any of them, go here and obey A, go here and work with B, go here and listen to C, and up to the letter Z. It must be painful for  to have to remember all those people, right? It convolutes the plot by adding too many subplots and characters into the fold.But Keanu Reeves is in it! How it could be bad?! Sadly, the famous voice actor does not equal a good performance and before you start dragging me to a pyre, do not get me wrong Keanu is fantastic. But you know who isn't fantastic?  The way Keanu portraits the character comes off as stiff when compared to the rest of the cast and it just does not cut in the convincing department. Silverhand is also a problem because it diminishes your character presence in the main story while also adding a deuteragonist that is not very interesting…The strong point of  is how beautiful and vibrant the world is. The neon lights shining on the dark streets while in the daylight everything feels compacted, like a maze that makes you want to explore it. The characters look great and so do a lot of the aesthetics and designs you will find during your playthrough! Also, the music is spectacular during gunfights, featuring a badass-futuristic vibe to it that adds more to the encounters you will have.The weak point is that those elements are downplayed because there is no flavor to them. The perk system is pretty standard and boring. The main story can be interesting at times and then have you yawn at others and the gameplay itself feels inferior to games that have been released years ago (just so you know, is not about Titanfall 2, a lot of shooters do have better gunplay than this). The glitches range from partial nudity to going through walls, to losing save data, to objects disappearing, items descriptions getting stuck in the HUD and that is only the tip of the iceberg that is  messy release.It was tested on an RTX 2070 S, I found it to be very annoying that when quest asks the player to unequip items or equip other items (which happens more than what I would like to) one has to re-equip all of it again. A couple of times it could be ok, but 7 times is bothersome. The more I played this particular title the less interesting it became for me and I truly wanted to love  but I am just, disappointed.The detective bits were cool the first few times but after that they became tedious, they basically sum up as “rewind here, now rewind there, rewind here again and that’s it”. They do not make you feel like a detective or something and rather is just a point click to which you already have all the answers to.If you read this far, you probably must be thinking that I hate  I do not, but I would be lying if I said I think it is a masterpiece or something. The game is not bad but is not amazing either so is more along the OK lines which is why I would give it a positive rating. Except…that in this case, we should not settle for mediocrity, it was supposed to be THE game and ended up being something standard, something that failed to deliver and that ended up being a letdown. Get the game if you want to jump on the bandwagon but otherwise, wait until they patch more stuff and keep in mind, is not that action oriented. If you like this review, give it a thumbs up! If you want to add your own opinion or share something informative, do it below in the comments!

_childDocuments_.review: I am very happy to give the thumbs up on this game on steam. While I feel really bad for everyone on console, the PC version was doing really well for me. I started playing from 1.06 on and I have been ever since mesmerized with the game, dumping over 320 hours in it since 15.01. and thoroughly enjoying the experience, the city, the story, the character builds and the branching choices and opportunities.The Good:1. The Story and quests - the story is beautifully crafted, believable and wonderfully cyberpunk. Be it in the main story, or the side quests, all of the dialogue is polished and thoroughly enjoyable. The game has 3 different starts (nomad, street kid, corpo-rat), 4 different gender-specific romance options and 2 additional ones (each and every single one coming with a beautifully crafted and believable story) and 5 different endings to explore that shouldn't be rushed and explored over multiple playthroughs. I'm going to go out on a limb and say, do the Bill Jablonsky quest. You will not be disappointed.2. The overall city life experience - I felt that the city is believable and it was so much fun stumbling upon all kinds of events all over the districts. Sometimes the janky driving can actually deprive you from finding some real cool art, loot, character lines, etc. that the developers have so lovingly and cleverly put in the game. While I would agree that there are things missing (wasting money in casinos, slots, etc. - there are such locations in the game), I personally never cared about these activities.3. The combat - the first person experience is amazing. It is difficult enough to keep you occupied, but also not too punishing, especially as you start learning how to use your chosen build's strengths properly. As I have tested it myself from start to finish over these 320 hours, every build is viable and works - from full on get in their faces to picking enemies from distance with snipers and hacks - it is all very enjoyable. Admittedly, some Weapon/perk combinations work better than others, but as this is an RPG, it has to cater to multiple playstyles and playthroughs - and I can tell you, it does.4. Weapons  - this deserves a separate point, as there are no useless weapons in the game and cater to every possible option a player might desire - close combat to long distance sniping. Every weapon can be accommodated in a build and a specific playstyle. Get in their face with bats, katanas, mantis blades or guerilla arms; get in close range with shotguns, pistols, the monowire; be a true soldier behind cover utilizing submachine guns or assault rifles; or just go the sneaky long range sniper route and combine them with silenced weapons to take out enemies from stealth. The variety is great, and the additional weapon variations (power for ricochets, tech for wall penetration and charging for more damage, and smart for no brain aiming while negating enemy's armor) work well towards creating the character that you want.5. The Music - damn if it isn't damn near perfect, it thoroughly deserves the double damn in this sentence (which became a triple damn, and in the brackets, a quadruple damn and with this damn... quintuple...). I listen to some of the tracks almost every day because they are so amazing. Some are good for pumping up, some are chill but they will satisfy fans of almost every genre - from techno and pop to throat-bursting metal. And of course, you can choose which radio station to play based on your mood!All those 5 points are more than enough to create a good open world game to explore and feel sufficiently engaged for many, many hours.The BAD:1. Bugs - let's just get this out of the way and be done with it. Even as of v1.12, there are multiple issues that, at least on PC, thankfully don't take that much out of the experience.2. Missed opportunities - the building blocks for multiple random activities are present, but not implemented, pretty much like in a live service game - ergo, we may or may not see it. There is the opportunity for gambling (casinos, pachinko), playing various mini-games, and various others, but they are simply not implemented. It's clear that the devs thought of adding it, but it was pushed back in the development cycle in favor of more important things.3. The driving - janky at best and you may be stuck in traffic way too often. While the devs really tried to add realism by having heavy traffic between 6 and 9 and 16 and 19, sometimes it clogs up the engine and creates way too many roadblocks (including cars stuck in one place for no reason). While you can roleplay and say that that guy's car just broke down, if you are in a quest that requires driving or chasing enemies... that is way too irritating. Most of the time the best vehicle you can use is a motorcycle to avoid said problems.4. The police system - it is clearly rudimentary, pushed back in the development process and not properly implemented, simply teleporting police officers in your vicinity, including in closed rooms. Nope. Bad development work on this one. Just nope!5. The 3 different starts - nomad, street kid and corpo could have had more impact than just 1 measly side quest at a certain point of the game. I really hoped for more quests based on it, and not just random lines in dialogue that sometimes amount to nothing. Based on dialogue alone, corpo is the best starting option, as that life path really allows you to deal with multiple problems.Conclusion:I had and still am having a blast with this game, over 300 hours in. I always want to double or triple my cash investment in game hours, and in Cyberpunk 2077 I can see myself dumping over 600 hours exploring, testing various character builds, and even more with the free DLCs that are coming. I can only hope the game will get better and better from now on. Once again, I am very sorry for my friends on console, but... I have a PC, I bought the game on PC and I need to judge it as I experienced it on PC, which started from a 7/10 on patch 1.06 and is now sitting on a  since patch 1.11. I am positive that with the right additions and DLCs, CDPR will get this game into 10/10 status.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 is an open-world, action-adventure story set in Night City, a megalopolis obsessed with power, glamour and body modification. Assume the role of V, a mercenary outlaw going after a one-of-a-kind implant that is the key to immortality. You can customize your character’s cyberware, skillset and playstyle, and explore a vast city where the choices you make shape the story and the world around you. Become a cyberpunk, an urban mercenary equipped with cybernetic enhancements and build your legend on the streets of Night City. Take the riskiest job of your life and go after a prototype implant that is the key to immortality.

name: Inscryption
detailed_description: From the creator of Pony Island and The Hex comes the latest mind-melting, self-destructing love letter to video games. Inscryption is an inky black card-based odyssey that blends the deckbuilding roguelike, escape-room style puzzles, and psychological horror into a blood-laced smoothie. Darker still are the secrets inscribed upon the cards... In Inscryption you will... Acquire a deck of woodland creature cards by draft, surgery, and self mutilation Unlock the secrets lurking behind the walls of Leshy's cabin Embark on an unexpected and deeply disturbing odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried, failed, and failed again, and I just  Inscryption, as the game is just  on so many different levels (a lot of which I cannot even write about, as that would be encroaching on spoiler-heavy territory). But just so you know, I have beaten the whole story and I have played some runs of a mode, which unlocks after, so I have given the game its fair shake.In my opinion, the main problem with Inscryption is that failure is . The game moves at a snails pace, so whereas in games like Slay the Spire, where after every failure, you pick yourself up relatively quickly, Inscryption punishes you just by being a slog to get through. This becomes a real issue when you just want to sit down and play for a couple rounds.Also, why does the map have to be partially covered the whole time? I understand the intrinsic RNG nature of deckbuilders, but how is it fun when the tool that you use to assess your strategy and pick a path to go forward now provides ? There are also problems like: Do you pick a duplicate card so that you can fuse it later into a stronger one? Well, good luck, because that event might not even spawn for you until the very end, and now your deck is just bloated with useless cards. You want to restart the game a bunch of times so you can solve some of the puzzles outside the main game and give yourself a better chance to win? Tough luck; you are getting a worse starting deck now. Some might say that Inscryption rewards players who look around every nook and cranny; I would say that it just kicks everyone who is not interested in every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the game has to offer squarely in the nuts.I understand a lot of effort has gone into making this, so I do not want to call the game bad, but I think it is a lot more frustrating than it is fun. I'm not saying I will not play it anymore (being a masochist, I need to finish everything through and through), but if things I have mentioned above also frustrate you, just stay clear out of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, good story, good atmosphere, and good artstyle. I only have two minor gripes with the game. One being that the gameplay is in service of the story and not the other way around. The card game itself is really quite fun but its scope is finite as its only purpose is to progress the story. My second gripe is the atmosphere. It fits well, and is well executed, but I find myself getting exhausted by its oppressive nature. It's a little draining if you play for extended periods of time, what with the constant presence of creepiness, darkness, and death. There's definently more to be said, but I think you're better off if you know less about this game.If you want to go on a dark card-based rollercoaster, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Inscryption' is an absolutely fantastic time through and through. If you love card games, adore the many differing mechanics among those that exist, even remotely like some of the ones that exist, or anything in between, I highly recommend you stop reading reviews and give this a play.To accurately review this title, I found the card game itself to be among some of the most fun to play. The mechanics involved work tremendously well together, and as the game opens up over time, the more that are added just keep making it interesting. At times, I did like some aspects or 'genres' of the card game over others, but it never disappointed.The actual story was a delight, and I'm amazed at just how deep it ended up being. If people haven't already discovered all the secrets, I can see this being talked about for years in the future, especially with what additions are intended for this universe and the card game.My rating for 'Inscryption' is a classic childhood hunt for plastic Easter eggs. So much fun already comes from the idea and action of playing the game, but as you progress, secrets are consistently revealed and every step unleashes more of the same tasty treats you've come to know and love, with a plethora of similar flavors that might introduce you to other new and potentially favorite concepts.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s rare that I come across a game that puts me at such unease, makes me so uncomfortable in my own chair, that I simply lose the will to stop playing. Doki Doki Literature Club is one such game that caught me like this, as well as Daniel Mullins’ previous outing, Pony Island. I have a soft spot for horror that follows you out of the game once you turn it off, and on that note Inscryption absolutely delivers. In this psychological horror meets roguelike card game, you’ll wake to find yourself trapped in a pitch black cabin across the table from a demonic figure, shrouded in darkness. It beckons you to draw from a deck of cards. You do so. You have entered the game, and you will play until you die. Eventually, one of your cards moves. The stoat motions to you not to react, and tells the player that there is indeed a way out. There are two other living cards in the cabin, and after you and the stoat find them you can make your grand escape attempt. Or at least, that’s the plan. At the beginning the stoat serves as the player companion, providing commentary and clues about the cabin and the demon that you continue to play cards with. After an hour he will be the only thing tethering you to sanity as you witness unexplainable horrors unfold. What makes the setup so damn interesting is that you are fighting only one opponent, the demon, Leshy, for the entire duration of the game. As you continuously build and improve your deck during each run, it will improve and change its deck as well. Inscryption is a tabletop role playing game taking place in a locked cabin, with Leshy serving as both the game master and the only other player. Every NPC you meet along the way is Leshy, every opponent is leshy, every wicked event to befall your poor player is Leshy. There is something cryptically stressful about watching a real demon lead a tabletop game in which it role-plays as many different demons, obviously working hard to make sure the game is fair for the player. Between every encounter round, depending on how the RNG rolls, you’ll be able to either add a new card, power one up you already have, or pick an item to keep. You can keep three items with you at a time. The items range from helpful to horrifying to both, and you’ll likely need to stock them up for the exceedingly difficult boss battles. Which are, again, just Leshy wearing a different hat and doing a different voice. And it is freaky beyond description.The meta-horror elements of Inscryption are what make it a must-play for me, but the card game itself is extremely innovative and addictive. Each card is a monster with HP, power, a cost, and usually a sigil. Sigils are special effects that add a layer of unpredictability to gameplay, since the same cards don’t always have the same sigils. The wings allow a monster to fly high and attack the opponent directly, the dive allows monsters to hide from attacks underwater, etc. Each turn, you begin by drawing either a card from your deck or a squirrel. The squirrel card is a fascinating mechanic - you always start with one in your hand, and you can draw one every turn if you think it’s the right move. Squirrels have 1 HP and 0 power, so they are quite literally only useful for sacrifices, but it heightens the thrill of the draw. Similar to many games, like Yugioh, a more powerful monster with a blood cost requires a sacrifice of less powerful monsters.  Most turns, especially late game, the real question is whether to draw a squirrel and play it safe or draw from your deck and risk getting a card you can’t afford. The real mind game is more often with yourself than the opponent, as you rack your brain about how to win this battle you can’t afford to lose.Every time a monster dies, no matter how it happened, it leaves behind one bone. Certain monsters require blood sacrifices (other monsters) but others require a certain number of these bones. My first approach as a novice was to attempt an all-bone or all-blood deck, but I found very quickly this was a fool’s errand. You will need to strategically use both bone and blood monsters in tandem in order to win. Each run, the player starts with two lives. Every time you deal damage directly to the opponent, that number of teeth drop onto a balanced scale on the table. Whoever’s side hits the table first is the loser.  This means that the battle is truly not over until it's over - finding creative ways to stall until you get a better card is not only doable, but necessary. In essence, you don’t need to deal x number of damage points to Leshy to beat it, you just need to deal 7 more damage than it has dealt to you.Between rounds, Leshy permits you to stand up and walk around the tiny 10x10 cabin and explore. There are puzzles to solve, codes to input, messages to be found, and friends to rescue hidden around strategically. But Leshy will be watching you the entire time, so don’t try any funny business like leaving. Solving these puzzles unlocks new cards to help you in battle. Make sure to get up and stretch your legs a bit, because you’ll need to unlock these things to progress the narrative. Standing up and walking around with its eyes on your back is viscerally frightening. Now, you may be thinking “well I don’t much like card games or roguelikes. “ I’ve got good news for you. Inscryption is a total deconstruction of both of these genres, finding the most twisted and uncomfortable ways to alter their structures and tropes to make sure you’re constantly on edge. One of my favorite things about Hades was that the deaths were canonical, and every time you failed you made a bit of progress and moved the story along. The same is true of Inscryption, but perhaps in a much more frightening way. When your player character dies (and they will die, a lot) and the run ends, Leshy gives you the last-rights honor of creating a death card out of the deck you gathered along the way. You pull the power and HP from one card, the cost from another, the sigil from another, and give it a name. Leshy then pulls an old-timey camera out to take a picture of your dying face for the card and finishes your run there. The player wakes up at the table again as a new character. Yes, each failed run means death for your character, and Leshy brings in another unlucky person to serve as his plaything. This cycle will repeat until the end of eternity. Luckily, the one glimmer of hope is that your powerful death cards will appear in random selections to your future players. Your dying grasp is sad, yes, but not surrender. A piece of that character will travel forward to aid someone else, and so on and so forth, after your death. There’s a strange, sad power in that mechanic. We all fight not to escape, but so that one day the nightmare will end long after we are gone. My biggest complaint with Inscryption is that I am not at all a fan of the art style. I understand it is meant to make players uneasy, but I believe this can be done without using this ragged 3D-pixel style that just looks flat out bad. The cards look great, though, and I love the style of the monsters. I also would appreciate a mechanic that allows for saving regular cards somehow in between rounds, even if it was a late game thing. Additionally, I didn’t enjoy the actual puzzles around the cabin, and after a long while I brute forced my way through them without figuring out how they were meant to be solved.Inscryption is introspective in all the best ways, asking players to make unspeakable sacrifices and decisions throughout its roughly 10 hour narrative. As you struggle to escape with your card-confined comrades from the cabin and unravel the mystery of who and what Leshy is, you’ll be treated to a wildly addictive card game that has you fighting yourself just as often as the opponent. _childDocuments_.review: I bought and completed this game earlier this year and recently came back to 100% it. Shockingly, when I came back, I didn't get annoyed or frustrated by any backtracking or repetition. In fact, sometimes I'd consider fighting just one more boss, or revisiting a secret room or dialogue option. This game really has a way of pulling you in. As someone who loves strategy and card games, this game was an absolute blast to play over and over again. The story and the characters are intriguing and make me excited to find out what will happen next, regardless of if I've seen it or not. I also love that the community has discovered different deck strategies and shared them (these definitely came in handy whenever I got stuck on a boss or challenge), and how you can make your own random deck using so many different strategies. The functionality of each card is very versatile, sometimes you'll get a new card and discover it's more useful than you thought!Some possible negatives (spoiler free):-RepetitionAt the beginning, the game can be a bit repetitive, which can get frustrating (especially if you repeatedly die or miss something). Nothing sucks more than getting to a boss only to die and restart. However, there's often something that changed or a new secret that will help you have a better start on your next run. And, if it's any consolation, this mechanic is  only present in the first act. (As mentioned previously, you can also look for popular decks online that may make your life easier). - Changes in Scenery Between ActsThis game is separated into three acts, all of which have their own unique charm. However, I will say Act 1 was my favourite, based on the vibes and story telling. Act 2 and Act 3 were also fun, though my enjoyment was more based on the lore rather than the gameplay. The gameplay was not bad, but it was a slight change from Act 1 that I could see deterring people from finishing the game. The change was lore significant, and because of that, I believe it is a positive addition to the game that builds more depth.Honestly, I really adore this game and I strongly recommend it despite the negatives. I watched a full playthrough of this game a couple years ago, and while I wish I entered the game blind, it was still such an enjoyable game to play. If you enjoy card/strategy games, I highly recommend this game. Or, if you don't like card/strategy games, I recommend watching some gameplay of it and consider purchasing it because this game is still wonderful story-wise.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game. This is probably one of the most unique, frustrating (in a good way), and fun horror games I have ever had the chance to play. A quick rundown: Inscryption is an Indi-horror/card game. You first start the game by solving puzzles and playing a sick card game against a creature to escape its wooden cabin. This part is ridiculously hard and took me the longest out of all the parts. I got frustrated many times, but when I finally got past this stage, it felt amazing. This part obviously contains a plot but I will not spoil it. The second part involves playing a 2D adventure style game, still including the card-play. You must fight all the different bosses to progress to the final stage of the game. This part was probably the easiest and didn't take me too long to complete. The final stage is hard to explain without spoiling the plot, so I will try my best to be as vague as possible. You are found are found to be in a similar predicament as in the first stage, but not as punishing. This stage is probably the most plot rich of them all.Pros:This game is very well thought out, plot rich, and unique. I don't believe there are any other games out on the market quite like it. The graphics are appealing and the card battles and puzzles are fun. The game gives the player a constant sense of unease and dread which definitely helps for immersion. Cons: This game is very difficult and strategic. This makes it sometimes hard to enjoy if you are stuck in one stage (usually the first) for long periods of time. This is because you may be getting bored (as I did) or frustrated, (also as I did). The plot, although interesting, can be sometimes hard to understand. The puzzles as well can also be confusing.My opinion:Overall, I believe this is a great game. The pros greatly out way the cons. I had a blast playing this. I couldn't recommend it enough to seasoned horror gamers and/or card gamers. However, if you get easily frustrated and aren't good at strategics or solving puzzles, then maybe this isn't the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just amazing. The start is a bit slow, but once you get past that. it really bumps up in speed. The jarring bit itself also got more interesting the further I made it into it, so yeah. I think it's jarring because you expect a horror game, and for a little while, it seems like it suddenly isn't a horror game. But it is! I've never seen so many mechanics being thrown at me in a way that isn't tedious. It almost felt like I was being spoiled somehow; that any other game developer could've stretched this game well up into the 20h+ category without having the game feel slow or grindy. So yeah, the game mechanics are awesome. Slightly frustrating at times, but overall, totally worth said frustration.The narrative is also pretty great. However, in the 2nd and 3rd acts it almost completely lost me, because of the near complete switch that the gameplay brought in these acts. I had to force myself through it just to replay the 1st act. Now, the 3rd act isn't nearly as guilty of the disorienting and ultimately unneedingly brief switch in style, however I still felt that, aesthetically at least, it was a completely different game than what I signed up for. At the same time though, I can't help but wonder if that was intentional. It feels almost ironic that you want to return so desperately to the horrible situation you endured through. Then again, this is only my personal opinion and some may adore the 2nd and 3rd acts. _childDocuments_.review: It's a Daniel Mullins game, what more needs to be said?  ;)A pared-down spin on the collectable card game (CCG) genre, with a ton of Mullins' "trademark" spooky weirdness, hidden items/teasers/events, what have you.  Exploration and experimentation can be highly rewarding, as well as frustrating, at times.  Do you take that rare card with an ability hoping for something down the road, or play it safe?  Use something to help tip the scales early or try to hold on for when it can win the match for you?Expect the unexpected is all I will say without spoiling anything (assuming you have avoided the many people streaming and posting videos of the game).  Even if one is not a fan of CCG's, give this one a serious look, it's highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I can promise you that this is a game like no other. The overall game is a first person card game that includes the essence of an escape room. There are many puzzles to solve in the main game and more in a hidden aspect of the game. You play as many different people through out the game. Defeat bosses and play card games with your killer. I really like how its a choose your own path type of game. If you don't like horror, creepy noises, themes of sacrifice and or violence this game won't be for you. I hope that this review helps you in any way!

_childDocuments_.review: The set-up: You're locked in a low-fi simulation of some cabin with an ominous figure making you play a card game. The rules become apparent as you play. As well as the stakes. A deck building sim that isn't really a deck building sim. The card game in the game is really addictive, elements of luck/chance but overall it's a test of skilful placement and planning. The story is intertwined to the gameplay. The design of it all is so well done and cohesive. There are multiple layers to what's going on. Don't read anything else about this game if you're at all intrigued, surprises are better left as surprises. This is a big game with a lot lurking under the surface. Don't spoil it. Don't miss it.

_childDocuments_.review: A cameraman locks you in a cabin and forces you to play a card game with him using live animals as cards. Please.

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing so many videos made about this game and my friends recommending me to pick up this game, I caved in and used some of my Christmas money to buy this game. After putting a decent amount of time into this game and beating the main story, I can now see why this game got so much praise. The manner in which the developers put so much love and effort into this game really shows, with the level of detail put into every character, every card, and even the ARG elements of this game. Speaking of the ARG, i barely even touched it and it plays a very important role in  the story of the game, with little hints and clues as to where to start seen throughout the game. You don't need to follow through the ARG to understand the main story of Inscryption, but it significantly helps further your understanding of the game. From the gameplay to the story, I love almost every bit of it. The only gripes I've had with this game were some battles that seemed nigh imposible to win without luck, but that might just be some terrible luck on my part. Either way, this game's fun and it's a must buy for fans of card games and mind-boggling stories.TL;DR - This amazing card game is a must buy and should be played in it's entirety.0100100101101110011100110110001101110010011110010111000001110100011010010110111101101110

_childDocuments_.review: Another deckbuilder game that could have been more and seemed to be more than what it was first appeared as, although I like deckbuilder games and have had played multiples and enjoyed them, I was expecting a genuinely unique experience from the start of it but then was heavily disappointed as the game went through.To start, the game paints itself as a sort of deckbuilding game that appears to be an escape room! I was thinking that this would be great, as you went along you got clues on how to escape the room or something, and it does so! Eventually I thought the game would have different escape rooms with different themes based on which deck you chose after making it through act one; however, was sorely disappointed at the sheer linearity of the second act. It basically made you just play card battle after card battle and had little to no puzzles in it that were at least considerably unique. The third act was more of a disappointment than I thought it'd be, don't misconstrue that it wasn't put together well; however, it was ended early in a way I wish it didn't. You literally couldn't fight one of the people painted as main boss enemies in more than a friendly sparring match due to the story. I would have been ecstatic to fight this boss in his own world with his own puzzles and trials, but they cut it short. Then there's the mod, an addition to the game after clearing it. It allows you to go through the standard, beginning of the game, maps with additional modifiers. I wouldn't have been so disappointed in it if it weren't for the fact that I beat the all modifier challenge on my second try with the basic deck.Overall, the game is definitely a noob friendly deck builder with somewhat difficult elements, but certainly left more to be desired. If you find this game on a heavy sale I'd recommend buying it as it would be worth the purchase then; however, buying this full price does not seem worth it with what they could have done with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cool. For starters, the mystery it sets up by only having a "continue" option from the start is really fun and interesting. Then there is the actual gameplay, which is a lot of fun too. The fact that there is a rulebook to help forgetful players is also nice and useful. I like the inspiration it takes from slay the spire with the way you progress and bosses being at the end of each area, which provides a nice flow and more strategy to the game. On top of all of that I like the puzzle-solving aspect in the cabin which is really fun, and the helpful hints that the talking cards give. But I still haven't mentioned my favorite mechanic yet, deathcards. Whenever you die in Leshy's cabin, you get to make a special card which is the culmination of your run, this card can then appear in future runs. For 3 different aspects you are allowed to choose one from 3 different cards. You can choose the cost of it (sometimes you can even get them for free), the stats (health and damage), and the most OP part, the special abilities, I'm not entirely sure if they have a name or not, but you can essentially put special things on them, like the ability to go back to your hand when the card dies, or the ability to be sacrificed infinitely. This usually results in a very powerful card that makes the game very fun. If you have the money for this game and enjoy strategy and turn-based combat, then you should 100% at least give this game a try.(please note I don't know everything so if I got anything wrong please correct me in the comments!)
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down one of my favorite games. I didn't think I would be this invested in a card game, but it was done in such a unique and creative format. There are layers and layers to this game, and goes so much deeper than that. The characters, the bosses, and the talking cards gave the game so much charm to it. The lore was interesting and I never once got bored. Overall, it was amazing. Please play it, it was so worth the time. There will never be another game like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Inscryption shines a flickering light on a new creative style of horror and deck building games. With each new run giving new ideas and trials to think thru and overcome as you push towards the end goals, you find yourself unable to leave the cabin in the woods. As the game carries on there are the highs and lows as you pass and fail each run but you can build your deck and grow from there. Overall, this game provides hours of game play and thought provoking puzzles. I wish you the best of luck and smile for your photo.
