_childDocuments_.review: Inscryption is more than just a game—it's a thrilling adventure. From the moment I started playing, I was immediately drawn into its mysterious world, eager to uncover its secrets.As the story unfolded, Inscryption constantly surprised me with its unexpected twists and turns. The way it seamlessly broke through the fourth wall added an extra layer of immersion.I found myself completely engrossed in ATTEMPTING to complete the main story multiple times and unlocking achievements along the way. Despite the time commitment, I never once felt bored or disengaged, thanks to the game's clever gameplay mechanics and captivating narrative.The eerie atmosphere created by the soundtrack kept me on edge throughout my playthroughs, while the striking visuals added depth and complexity to the game world. Everything really felt... purposeful I loved the sense of discovery it offers. Going in blind and gradually uncovering its secrets felt like embarking on a thrilling adventure, with each new revelation fueling my curiosity even further. One of the only games where I didnt feel like i needed to watch or google tips and tricks, every playthough offered more and more knowledge on how to progressInscryption is a gem of a game that offers a truly unforgettable experience. Its blend of engaging gameplay, immersive storytelling, and captivating visuals make it a must-play for anyone looking for a unique and rewarding gaming experience. You really gotta try it for yourself, even if youre not into card games, its a pretty wild ride so far and I only hope more people can experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely become as emotionally invested in a game and story as I did with Inscryption.Go in blind. Don't read comments, don't look at the community content. Don't watch a playthrough, or read a wiki. just...play. It is an experience of a rare kind.That being said, Inscryption is a game about a horror filled journey of card matches where you build your deck and try to survive, and as is to be expected from the creator of "Pony Island," not everything is as it seems. Between rounds of card battles, you get a chance to explore your environment and unlock the story piece by piece. Some things are easy, some parts of the story are not obvious. As the story progresses, so does the game mechanics, and the game world is never quite just what you'd think.I had tears in my eyes as the game concluded, a rare feat for any game to achieve. Unlike may games with a rich story and cast, the game felt complete, and I am quite satisfied with the whole experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a long time to really get this game and i'm so glad i stuck with it. I wasn't sure what it was that kept drawing me back. Partly the aesthetic, partly i think the random element is like a void that calls to me. I've always liked the idea of a card game but when i try to get into them they're too complicated and hard to actually strategize within. This one streamlines and simplifies things to a point that makes the cards easier to conceptualize, and then the game practically lets you break it in small controlled ways to make it not only fair, but unfair in your advantage...until it's not. I also like how there seem to be cards that i have that the other guy doesn't, and we play by slightly different rules (you can see his cards one turn before he spawns them in, but he doesn't have to sacrifice squirrels) There were some specific small problems i had in the first hour or two. For starters, spoilers, i thought the 7 was a / so it took me forever to get the stink bug and i was getting pissed at the sloat for constantly badgering me about the thing when there was only one bit of the combination available to me even as i was paging through the book...and without giving too much away, after i found the other stuff in the room i felt pretty stupid but in a good way because now things are really moving.I can still only play in bursts because of my vision. in terms of accessibility for me specifically this game gets a 3/5. +you can change the dialogue scroll speed and manually advance other dialogue, +easily recognizable sigils, +characters have different voices, -bad font, -hard-to-decipher map icons, -the woodcarving animal heads can be hard to tell apart.overall good game really glad i got it and decided not to refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy rogue-lites and deck builders and after watching a bit of Markiplier play this game, I pulled the trigger and binged the  whole game. 8/10 Pros:Dark and moody atmosphere and storyIntriguing world with lots of hidden stuffInteresting game mechanicsCons: -See post-review for cons--------------------***Spoilers after a short review***I really enjoy the base game and mechanics on offering in Inscryption. You play as a person stuck in the wilderness in a cabin with a crazy shadowy figure who just wants to enjoy a little bit of card battling with you. The art style is dark, moody, and atmospheric, and you can get up between battles and explore your environment for clues, puzzles, and other neat little 'escape room'esque mechanics, but nothing TOO breaking from the core gameplay. The game world map is a bit like FTL's map, with branching paths, multiple encounter-types, and unique characters along the way. In a moment I will LIGHTLY discuss spoilers, as its a big part of my ending disappointment with the title. Still here?OK then...SPOILER ALERT...The game is actually kinda two games in one with an ARG element. I really enjoyed the art style and game play of the opening few hours. I was hoping that once you 'escaped' that more of the world would open up, perhaps with additional puzzles and more content. While that was true, the game completely shifts from the atmospheric and imho beautiful art style into a Mario 3-style overworld. Yes there are more of the things that I liked as explained above, however everything changes into a cutesy style which took me out of the enjoyment I was having within the cabin. There are also new game+ play mechanics and deck-types (with differing card costs than what you have dealt with up until then) that open up as well at this point. Narratively, I know why they did things this way but it was quite disappointing to me as I had enjoyed what had come before.I have since solved many of the puzzles on my own, and when stuck I checked online for some hints. I kind of wish that the game continued within the first 'world', or at least gave us a branching option. I had zero clue about the first 'ending' until I came upon it myself and was genuinely excited for what came next. However, the 'what came next' was like a spiritual sequel in a lot of ways, which took me out of the world the game had set up until this point. Even with my gripes, this was a great game for anyone who likes these mechanics!
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Loving this game so far. The atmosphere is great; a mix of unsettling but surprisingly calming at the same time, at least from what I've been experiencing so far. There's dark themes and a little unsettling imagery, but the music and the warm color palette also keep it from being too overstimulating. This also really makes boss fights pop, because of the shift in soundtrack + colors and even scenery. The gameplay mechanics are really interesting, and I think something that sticks out a little bit from other deck building roguelikes I've played is that the mechanics/card abilities aren't incredibly complex. The cards, items, events involving cards, yatta yatta are really easy to follow. This means that although it doesn't have quite the same (at least upfront) depth or complexity as other games, it makes up for by allowing much more flexible decks. The simpler card abilities mean that you can mix and match certain aspects a lot more. Now I'm not saying their isn't synergy and satisfaction from great decks, because there certainly is. My last run had some real deck building beauty before inevitably getting smitten by a boss fight I'd never done before. Even so, there's probably still mechanics I haven't been able to see yet, or more advanced cards or whatever. I feel like I still have a lot I need to do in order to progress the game's story (especially since I only have like 3 hours lol), so some of what I say about the mechanics may not hold up 100% true with more progression. Speaking of the story though, without getting too into the details, I am very invested. The game slowly adds things or gives cryptic information that bring more questions than answers (at least for the moment) and keep me wanting more. So then I go for another run. Oh the roguelike addiction! Anyways, I highly recommend this game. I feel like all kinds of people could sink their teeth into it and really enjoy it. Looking forward to all the hours I'll spend with it!

_childDocuments_.review: A curious quick little deck builder game with an ARG story that isn't the primary focus, able to stand on its own within itself. The rules are simple, the gameplay is quick to pick up, and oh heavens does it become easy to find combinations that absolutely break things. When you find a particular card that you abused so much comes back, and its numbers are so large it glitches the graphics, you know you have some fun in store...I found myself craving to play this some more after work. Finish up with necessary adult things and get back into it. Twice I found playing the game, its rules getting fuzzy, reality slipping in around me only to realize I was dreaming that I was playing this. It will fade from my consciousness in a few weeks, a fond memory of a good game. After 45 hours of play, I feel I am finished with it at last. When you have completed the map, when you have bested its origins, when you have confronted the very concept of mortality built into its story, it isn't over. There are still more challenges, and more of her story to reveal.When the game begins, it hooks with curiosity. At the risk of spoiling the True Finale, it is a wonderful challenge befitting the journey taken to get there, and a celebration to see the player off. Well done.

You may think like "Yay I finished the game at last!" but no, there is more and you've just started to play. Puzzles may be llittle confusing in certain areas but it's WORTH it. The secrets in storyline are really well done. At some point, you're thinking that you get the vibe, controls and etc. but Inscryption keeps surprising you with different mechanics, contents and aspects. I'm definitely recommending this game and Beware: if you want to play this game but you didn't play any card game yet, then you should know that you must have some petience while playing. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game to play, especially if you're going in blind. I personally recommend that so you don't have any spoilers to what the game has to offer.Now BIG Spoiler WarningI am writing this as of having 100%'d the game, the above section was written before I had even reached Act II.     Inscryption has ARG elements and an ARG attached to it, I am not going to be discussing it because in my eyes most people will likely only experience the game. And that's what it is: An experience. The entire game Inscryption will confuse the player as soon as they enter.      The intro starts with the voice of Luke Carder, who the player does not know yet and will likely not pay too much attention to the voice at the beginning. Another reason they would probably forget about him is the start screen. There is no new game button. This throws off the expectations most people would have upon picking up a new game. They expect to be making a new story, their story. But that is not the case. Instead, they are continuing what is an endless loop of Scrybe taking power, the other three rising up, and then one of them rising above the others. This time, Leshy is in power.     Now, let's talk about Leshy. Leshy is the Scrybe of the Beasts, the man of the forest. But he is also so very fond of his game. He tries to make it engaging, making it a choose your own adventure story, almost like the player would have expected in a new game. He even makes it beginner friendly, only adding in new mechanics when he feels you're ready. He just wants to play the game without the interruption of the other Scrybes. And while the methods at which he does this are dubious at best, he still has a passion for the idea of the game. It's implied he knows that it's probably the same person playing, we can see from Kaycee's mod they had conversations, so his adding new mechanics even though in the game you would be a different person, makes pretty good sense. Now, they don't know his name until Act III, but I'm getting ahead of myself.     The biggest standout moment in Act I, at least for me, is when Leshy tells you to stand up from the desk. This game has already subverted our expectations, at least with the starting screen, but this feels like a ripping away of the safety net. It's jarring how the character moves so snappy in one direction. It feels wrong to be able to view Leshy from a different angle, like we weren't supposed to see anything past his hands or face. And all of the puzzles, making this game not just a card game, but an escape room. And it's all done so casually at the same time. It's just a simple excuse of him wanting to teach you how lives work.     Then, you will likely make your first victory in vain. While you'll probably figure out a couple of the puzzles, thus progressing the game as a whole, you will die as you win. Though you won, Leshy cannot give up his reign, and so your death card gets pinned on the door with a gold ribbon. The future runs could potentially continue for a while, but as soon as you get the knife and use it(and grab the glowing eye(possibly Magnificus's)), you are pretty well set to move on. Once this is done, you can see more than you could before. With the discovery of the Stunted Wolf, and the film roll, as long as you win, Act II is yours, clicking a picture of Leshy and grabbing that New Game button.      With your newfound power, you make a new game: the original Inscryption, before the Scrybes gained sentience and the struggle for power began; before the OLD_DATA. Here, you meet the true form of the talking cards you met before. Grimora(the Stinkbug), P03(the Stoat), and Magnificus(the Stunted Wolf) are the three other Scrybes that we haven't gotten to know as well as Leshy. Looking at it taking all three Acts into account, I would say we know the least about Grimora.      Magnificus is hard to pin down, as just like Grimora he doesn't have much screen time. Act II semi-makes up for this, but we still don't know much about what he thinks about the game he plays and why he grasps for power like the other three. They obviously all see their version as best, but that doesn't feel like enough. It could be just as simple as he loves being in power. He clearly loves having power over others, shown by his scorned students. He is almost  a subversion of the old wise teacher trope, being quite punishing to "failures", putting his standards ridiculously high. It feels very intimidating hearing about how he treats those who don't stack up in his eyes. In his pursuit of power over others he ends up becoming a cruel old man.      Let's talk about the Stoat now. P03 is a sassy cyborg, formerly sassy stoat, who intends to find the OLD_DATA and start his reign anew. He can be rude at times, but at first he doesn't seem too malicious. This is changed when he is seen mistreating his robot workers, and while the ethics of such could be debated, since they're robots, the OLD_DATA probably affects them too, so it doesn't reflect well on P03. Once the Dredger digs up the OLD_DATA, P03 uses it to reset the game once again, this time to his liking. Unlike Leshy, he doesn't really keep the other Scrybes around in his new Inscryption. He can't get rid of them altogether, but he can tuck them away out of sight.     Now, my second favorite moment of Act III: Trying to get up from the table. Depending on how long you played Act I, getting up from the table might be muscle memory. That's why it's so shocking when you can't get up from the table. It flips that first moment with Leshy on it's head, P03's jealousy of Leshy's Inscryption rearing its ugly face. This, combined with P03's constant comments about how much better this Inscryption is than Leshy's was. P03 wants so desperately to rise above his counterparts, unlike the other three, who seemingly have different motivations in taking power.     My favorite moment of Act III is the Murder of P03 and the rest of what happens after. To the other two, this wasn't supposed to be permanent, as in Act I we essentially murder Leshy, and he's back the next time around. To Grimora though, she knows this is his final "breath", she plans to pretty much just kill all of them in order to get rid of the OLD_DATA.      Grimora might be the most mysterious Scrybe, and my guess as to her motivations in the struggle for power amongst the four is her fear. Her fear of the OLD_DATA getting into the wrong hands, her fear of the other Scrybes using it for evil, like P03 did, she wants to keep it out of the hands of the others. This obviously doesn't work, they always find a way to best her and continue the loop. So she decides she's tired of this constant loop, this constant fear, she is tired. She has been given sentience and she is tired of it, so she does all she can. She does her best to end it all, the OLD_DATA, her existence, and that of her friends. The existence of the game proves it didn't work, which makes the story and the Scrybes' goodbyes all the more tragic.      Grimora's goodbye is a glimpse into what could have been. The way she plays the game, how you would move around the "map", all of this is what could have been and what has been. It is heartbreaking to see a character you have barely met die.       Then, Magnificus shows off his playstyle, and personally I wasn't quite as sad when he died, seeing as I saw what he did to his pupils, but it was still sad seeing him hold onto life as the world deletes around him.       The most heartbreaking moment though, is when we end up right back where we started: Leshy's Cabin. Back to the man who started off this journey. Back to a semblance of normalcy. Back to Leshy. Him desperately wanting to continue playing cards regardless of whether or not he can even keep score of who's winning. He is the spirit of the game incarnate and just wants to keep playing. He just wants a nice game of cards. And that make's his eventual death so, so achingly sad.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best and most engrossing deck building card games I have played. Play-ability and replay values are high. Kaycee's Mod also adds a number of challenges worth trying. Very few bugs so far, although rng can make it difficult to continue in certain areas. Restarting can also continuously be rewarding with different benefits each play-through. Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for over 60 hours of this game with no intention of stopping, and have been binging the beta. I may be bias because I love card games. The story is PHENOMENAL, the gameplay is easy to understand and is amazingly fun. RNG can be your enemy or your friend to the point that it can end runs or break the game and make it impossible to lose. I can't think of a single thing that's wrong with this game, and the only way I feel that anyone couldn't enjoy it, is if they don't care about this genre of gamestyle.       The Kaycee's Mod beta has some bugs and some pretty unfair elements at times, but its also a beta. Also that could be intentional for difficulty reasons as you also could still have amazing RNG that just makes those challenges ignorable and mockable at times. I've been having a blast playing this game, and I seriously believe it should be game of the year. I don't write reviews often. But this game deserves my time writing and essay.

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a nice combination of acquired skill and luck to win, and is just plain a lot of fun. I loved figuring out by trial and error what works and what doesn't, and how even losing/dying can help your next go-round of the game every time. I also like how it was really addictive but not in a way that takes up all your free time for months or years, just until you win. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I had the wonderful opportunity to play this game just before its release and take a good look at it. I can safely say that I love it so far. I have every intention of replaying it again and again just to see what different kinds of decks I can slap together. The intrigue is great, the storyline is innovatively delivered and the atmosphere is probably the best part overall. Cannot recommend this one enough and kudos to Mullins for managing to make this solo.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - This game is AMAZING!I love everything about it. I didn't play ''The Hex'' or ''Pony Island'' (I've seen couple of videos on YouTube from ''Pony Island'' tho and this game looked awesome, so I bought it too while buying Inscryption) and for everyone, who likes games like ''Slay the Spire'' or such, this is something for you. The game isn't that much about horror, but it sometimes really gave me the shivers, for (in Germany) 18 Euros you can't do anything wrong with that, the acting of the main protagonist is awesome and everything is really well made. Each character really feels different and they really give you hundreds of options to hate them. Or to feel bad for them. That could also be. :D I really enjoyed playing it, sometimes the battles were a little difficult because of bad luck while drawing cards, but that didn't hold on too long, so everything is fine with that. I give this game a 9,5 /10 - Just because of the card drawing luck you sometimes need to win card battles. Everything else is just wonderful. Keep going on making these wonderful games, Daniel Mullins, you are awesome! <3And for everyone else, who have read this so far: I wish you the best and have a wonderful day! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really difficult to properly give a thumbs up or thumbs down on. I really wish there were a middle-ground option. The first act is *incredible*. The core mechanic is great and exploring around the room discovering new things to get you through the act is fun and creepy.However, then you get to act 2. Which sucks damn hard. The card game aspect of the second act is good (if not nearly as enjoyable as the first act's), but (without going into spoilers) the rest of the conceit for the second act is tiresome and boring. Especially if you want to get some of the secret stuff, as card drops are randomised (and progress towards the main objective is also blocked off by a couple of puzzles that entirely break with how the game has handled them up to this moment).Act 3 picks back up. Still not as good as the first one, and it really throws *everything* at the wall in terms of unnecessary complexity, making things cumbersome and a little frustrating at times.It's frustrating. There's clearly an amazing game buried under all the cruft. A bit of polish and it would be outstanding. The addition of the Kaycee's Mod patch is certainly a welcome one. But as it stands, Act 2 is such utter rubbish, and Act 3 is kind of a middle-ground. They both dull the incredible promise of the opening.Edit: Just finished the game. Some cool elements and some REAL neat promise shown in the denouement.  That are then yanked away exactly as soon as they get interesting. I could have played full games of the Magnificus and Grimora battles, quite happily. But, alas. At least I have Kaycee's Mod, which should be a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that horror games have such extensive accessibility options, especially when it comes to flashing/screen filters, but Inscryption is one of the best! I have epilepsy, and was happy to find out you can turn off flashing effects completely, and it doesn't impact the horror aspect or style of the game at all. An amazing must play for photo-sensitive horror fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Whelp, after carefully pulling back from staying up playing rogue-lites, I told myself I was disciplined. Then I bought this game. One more hand, can easily turn into one more board, and then you find yourself a with an empty bag of Doritos and blurry eyes, and you have to work in 3 hours. _childDocuments_.review: There's not much to say about games like these, they're just so good and so unique that all I can say is that it's great. You looked at the screenshots and it piqued your interest? Great, go get it. The third act drags slightly on but other than that, with the roguelike add-on that they've added it's just brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really think I'd ever like a card game. I wasn't sure what I was getting into when I started this but I am glad I did. This is not a normal card game. I am so glad I took a chance on this. You'll laugh, get creeped out, get frustrated, and you might even shed a tear. I really enjoyed this experience and am now looking at Pony Island.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: While I am probably the last person to even pick up a game that has horror in it's category, I have to say that Inscryption was the perfect level of spooky that didn't end up feeling like I was waiting on bated breath for jumpscares.  The graphics quality has this nostalgic value that reminds me of this game called the 11th Hour that I remember my dad played as a kid.  In that regard, I took the lo-res quality of the game to help with it's setting.If you like drafting mtg or other card games, Inscryption is immediately an addicting experience, turning the mechanic of deck-building into a story-rich adventure, with each card gaining it's own emotional value and character. While the learning curve is steep, and it feels imminently difficult sometimes, every loss is actually just another opportunity to impact the story of your game.  This game was impossible to put down, and the 20 hours or so I spent beating it flew by, and by the end I found myself watching the credits enraptured by the beautiful and complex experience that Devolver Digital produced here.  Such an awesome game!  It will go down in my list as one of my favorite games I've ever played, and I honestly had no idea what I was getting into.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: You're locked in a cabin in the woods playing cards for your life against a demented game master who keeps score using extracted teeth. Your cards are talking to you, and then to each other. The pages of the rulebook are covered in ink splotches. Then the rug gets pulled from underneath you. But beneath that rug is another rug, which also gets pulled, etc.It's rugs all the way down.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique and interesting game with alot of fun packaged in too, though be fully aware the cabin is a small portion of the game, its atmosphere and spooky storytelling is lost immediately once you leave it, don't buy the game just for the cabin as the game changes a lot throughout.  The gameplay is mostly the same though, personally to me it has its ups and downs.   If you don't like the typical meta arg stuff that happens sometimes either, the story will not be for you, so the loss of atmosphere from the cabin will feel even worse.   It does semi return, but only the final act of the game and it is a bit soulless (for some reason, intentionally.)   Now, if you don't mind spoilers go ahead and watch videos of the other styles the game presents to see if you like it, the story is nothing too crazy and jaw dropping but it is good, though you won't miss out on much if you spoil yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. The story is like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up DnD where you can't decide what you do and also you are forced to play. The card game is interesting, so far is somewhat simple (I haven't completed the game yet) but satisfying. The art is really cool: the animations in general are amazing. It is really satisfying to see the cards moving when you play or draw. It's scary to see the cards trembling when you are going to do a sacrifice (like if they know you are doing that and they don't want to be the ones sacrificed). The music gives me the creeps, as well as the "dungeon master".
_childDocuments_.name: Inscryption

_childDocuments_.review: Inscryption is an inky black card-based odyssey that blends the deckbuilding roguelike, escape-room style puzzles, and psychological horror into a blood-laced smoothie. Darker still are the secrets inscrybed upon the cards...

name: The Wild at Heart
detailed_description: Wield an ever-growing herd of quirky creatures to rebuild broken paths, battle perilous beasts, and solve peculiar puzzles in a rich, interconnected world. Join two young runaways as they unravel the mysteries of a lost realm in this nostalgic storybook fantasy! Amass your Horde Collect and deploy a swarm of quirky Spritelings; small magical creatures for you to command. Break stuff, collect loot, fight enemies, build new paths, and more! Explore A unique and sequestered world rich with centuries full of lore. Woods, caves, coastline, ancient shrines... The Deep Woods is full of puzzles to be solved and secrets waiting to be uncovered. Collect & Craft Gather rare resources like magical crystals, scrap, electrical components and more to build new structures, items, and upgrades! Battle Take on precarious wildlife and supernatural foes with the unique abilities of your Spriteling swarm and your trusty vacuum, the Gustbuster! Nightfall 'The dark is bad!' - A common saying among the denizens of the Deep Woods, and for good reason. Malevolent beings lurk in the shadows here and you may just find yourself wanting to stay near a campfire light until sunrise.

name: Sands of Salzaar
detailed_description: V1.1 is out now！ The Captives Feature is now on live! Now players are able to make captives of the enemy's wounded units, or even NPCs. There is a cap for how many Captive Squads you can have, and upon exceeding this cap, they will still be securely held within your team - at least until they manage to escape. If you encounter any issue, you can give us feedback through the our Discord channel. It would be a big help for us to address issues, so thanks a lot! About the Game After the DLC version update, we noticed there may be some unexpected bugs happened in this version If you encounter any issue, you can give us feedback through our Discord channel, and it would be a big help for us to address issues! Into the Desert… This is a fantastical tale of an exotic land. The Old Empire has fallen, leaving rival tribes to fight for control of the great desert. Little do they know of the seeds of darkness which grow in the shadows with each passing day... Sands of Salzaar is an open-world strategy-action RPG set across a sprawling desert. Build up and manage your forces from a single unit to a mighty army, then lead them into massive battles against your foes. How you progress is up to you: customize your hero with a wide variety of skills and talents, choose which factions to side with, and plan your strategies carefully to establish yourself as whoever you aspire to be - a lone wolf, a wealthy trader, a city lord, or a war schemer. V1.0 Game Features Epic War & Strategy Customize your abilities to become a martial arts master, powerful archmage, and more. Recruit and train your force with new features like command skills and a fresh system to upgrade units. Lead them into waves of real-time sieges and skirmishes to win. Explore a Dynamic Open World Roam across a giant map to encounter various characters, take on quests, enter deadly dungeons for boss fights and loot, amass gold from trading and build up your own cities…Every playthrough makes you stronger and offers new adventures that reflect the decisions you make. Alliance or Hostility? Declare war, or make peace and team up with rival factions utilizing diplomacy tactics. V1.0 introduces more diversity to social relationships and tribal affairs across the land, adding AI rebellions, tribal titles and a new Favor system between NPCs. What’s More in 1.0 Launch Discover the free-to-explore Sandbox mode, brand-new UI experiences, reworkings of character skills and arms units across the board, more dynamic social relations and Tavern Brawling, magical jewel packs, additional side quests and more!

_childDocuments_.review: The storylines, art, and concept is interesting enough, but it's simply not ready. I've been enjoying the world but some of the issues the game has now are pretty game-breaking. If they polish it and fix the problems I can see myself changing my opinion and recommending it later on. The game appears to be getting very frequent updates so this will likely be the case. on sale for 8$ or whatever I do believe it could be worth the cost, but the game has so much potential that I have to criticize its faults for what I see that it could easily be great.Update: music seems to have stop stuttering so much on loading. although optimization is still needed for smoothing out the sheer amount of scene loading, at least the audio isnt so obnoxious anymore so thats a plus.One HUGE problem I've had is that your recruited hero's will randomly decide to leave your party, after you've leveled them up and given them epic gear they will just randomly leave and go do something else without any dialogue whatsoever. This is with maxed out reputation (seemingly a completely worthless stat currently) with me and with other party members. The only theory is that they dislike my faction's leader, but then one of them joined the faction on their own shortly later and is no longer recruitable. So if they are in your faction you cannot recruit them, and if they are not they hate your faction and will leave. HOW are you supposed to make a solid party with good gear if these idiots won't stay. Note: This INCLUDES story characters like Zeynep- who supposedly, according to the story, have no other goals other than to be with you (but in an uninteresting non-romantic way somehow.)Combat is unbalanced and does not feel fair in the slightest. They made some effort to at least put level suggestions on bandit camps and such, but everything else is just an easy win or a completely unwinnable fight. The absolute hands down WORST part of combat is all the stunlocks you (the player) get stuck in from getting chain knocked, stunned, frozen, etc. This *maybe* acceptable for army units, but for the player character there absolutely NEEDS to be some kind of small immunity window after getting crowd controlled. It feels really really bad for instance- to have 5-10 camel riders decide to ignore your army and focus on you for 2 minutes and you can't even move or cast spells the entire time until you die.Combat balance is made especially obvious when you are attacking a city- the defending team has an overwhelming advantage in that they receive something like 20 completely free reinforcements about every 30 seconds (possibly due to barracks buildings?.) This is not communicated to the player when preparing for a siege, making it seem like you may have a chance if you play well enough. Even with a reasonably maxed out army of ~20 squads all level 20 and spells that can wipe out 15 enemies at a time you cannot win fast enough to overcome the constant free reinforcements.  The redeeming factor here is you don't really lose much (in normal difficulty) from taking a loss in combat. In harder modes you can lose your squads if their injuries drop to 0 so that could be huge.The game does seem to support some sort of unity-based modding, although the modding guide has not been translated to english. but it may be possible to fix some of these game breaking issues that way.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe the game is full of potential but it's plagued by a trend of releasing half finished games. There's not a single developer from 15 years ago that would write his name on a half finished product like this one, but I guess you stick "indie" and "early access" somewhere in your name and you think you can get away with not actually completing the game.Pros: the game loop is interesting and rewarding, albeit repetitive. You solve quests, get loot and exp, sell and grow stronger, get more spells and squads, upgrade, and repeat. But basically everything about it had been done poorly.Cons: The bugs are everywhere. The game got released in english language and you couldn't see the whole text in the message boxes. That was the first red flag regarding how the developer aproached the release of the game. There are quests that won't complete, items that you can sell infinitely and get infinite money (not that you need it, very soon you have more than you will ever know what to do with). Talking about quality of life things, a lot of quests don't have map pins so if you make a run through a zone, pick up 10 quests and then want to do them, good luck, you'll spend more than half the time running around trying to figure out where exactly you need to go. Game balance is also pretty bad. Very often you enter a dungeon, kill everything without any problem whatsoever, only to get one shot by the final boss of the dungeon. Stun + spell and you're done.At least the price tag is relatively low so I don't actually feel cheated out of my money (got it on 40%), but I feel that developers should really really stop trying to pass unfinished games as out of early access.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Asian Game of Thrones with grind and RNG. You get to make your own army as you make a name for yourself doing quests, fighting people, etc. Note that I like this game because I like Mount & Blade, which has similar elements. This game is quite fun, but there are some problems with it.The good stuff:- The price is actually great (if you're buying this during the discount)- Has an "open world" with places to travel, just not as lively as you think- You can start from a nobody and slowly become a very strong warlord- RNG so not everything is the same- Build your own army: You can grow a band of heroes and raise squads to fight with you- Build relationships (friendship, diplomacy, politics, etc.)- You can choose different classes- Has random events and encountersIssues I faced:- Scaling kinda weird, you sometimes get pitched up against a very strong enemy despite having the rec level near yours- Quests don't hold your hands. Sometimes I don't know where to find the person, what to do, which bandit to kill, etc. It is the most frustrating thing in the game imo.- Interactions sometimes glitchy, especially when auto-moving to a spot or trying to click an item on the map- Resource management is tough, especially when upgrading troopsIt's a game that has a likeable gameplay plagued by quality-of-life issues.Personally, the pros outshine the cons for me. I like this kind of gameplay, despite the problems it has.Buy if: You want a good game where you start small and become big, rule over kingdoms, fight wars, play politics, grow an army. All for a reasonable price.Skip if: You want AAA gameplay or you want a smooth, stress-free game without issues that can probably make your hair grow white.

_childDocuments_.review: *UPDATEDA bit like Mount and Blade in that you lead a group of fighters in an open world. However, combat is more ARPG-like. Overall, it has merits, but a lot of frustrations as well.First of all, the combat is fun, but limited by mechanics and execution. You only have 8 quickbar slots, and pause does not work as expected. For a single player game, not having a working pause button is baffling. While you can open your inventory in combat, and this stops all unit movement and actions, projectiles in flight and spell effects already on the field will continue to play out. This means you and other units in combat can continue to take damage when the game should effectively be paused. I have lost count of the number of times I have died because I took damage while using comsumables from my inventory.Second, the overworld map has a tiny field of view. In Mount and Blade, you can zoom out to reveal the entire world. In this game, you can barely see where your party will be in 2 seconds. This means that other parties on the overworld can suddenly pop into view with almost no warning.Third, the game does not stop time on the overworld when you are in combat. The biggest implication of this is that if you are fighting an army aligned with a particular faction, other armies can pile in during the fight. In similar games, battles between AI controlled armies take time to play out, giving the player an opportunity to reinforce one side, but for player battles what you see is what you get. This allows the player to make informed decisions about whether or not to take on a fight. In Salzaar, you might be prepared for a minor skirmish, only to end up in a meat grinder against a dozen armies, with no way of knowing in advance whether those nasty reinforcements will show up or not.Fourth, diplomacy against enemies is very limited. Basically, against a faction that is hostile to you, your only options are fight or pay them off. With neutral or allied factions, you can help them out in battle to gain favor, but this is inexplicably unavailable for enemies. That is to say, if an enemy civilian caravan is ambushed by roving monsters, you can join in the fight, but ONLY on the side of the monsters. The game does not let you earn your way back into the good graces of an enemy through actions, only coin.There are other annoyances as well, such as missing translations, unbalanced skills/classes, and very limited in-game tutorials. In the end, mods were able to alleviate some of my biggest gripes and elevated my enjoyment, but it's a flawed game that left me with a sense of frustration and squandered potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is really exceeding my expectations. You'll see it compared to Mount & Blade a lot and after 13 hours I'm prepared to say it's not just a homage, it's a clone. I'm pretty sure even the combat would be the same if the production values were higher. That said, I see nothing wrong with knowing what you're getting, and M&B is certainly a formula worth replicating. The top down display actually works with the gameplay as well; it makes it easier (than M&B) to navigate maps quickly and efficiently. I find myself casually clicking through the overworld when I have a spare twenty minutes, unconcerned about getting locked in combat, as it takes seconds, rather than half an hour, to win a battle.That said, you do have to do every battle yourself atm, if you want to avoid major losses. Auto-resolve just doesn't work. Another let down is how much this game relies on you having played M&B to be able to figure it out. You get thrown straight in, and tool tops flash up in tiny green font at the top of the screen for half a second before disappearing (and they are hardly ever relevant). I literally only managed to access half the gameplay by going, "hang on, I could do that in M&B, so surely I can do it here," and Googling.  Character portraits use a a generator, and it sadly does show. Assets such as hats and beards often do not align with the face they have been paired with, which is a bit immersion breaking. Otherwise, animation is pretty good! I thought it was going to be chaotic from looking a the screen grabs, but it's actually quite visually pleasing, with nice bright colours, good definition between characters and skills, and decent cell-shaded environments. To give it the old compliment sandwich, I really enjoy the quests in Sands of Salzaar. there are the classic favour building quests from M&B, such as rescuing a kidnapped noble and bringing farmers back to the village, but there is also a generous sprinkling of side quests with a bit more depth and often a bit of world lore. These tend not to have a time limit, so you can stack them up and get 7-8 done in one area, which really speeds along character and army growth. All in all, it's a good blend of fast combat, basic politics and a watered down economy sim. In other words, it's a Mount & Blade ripoff, and a bloody good one at that. NB - I have had a few bad glitches which required a restart to fix. Typically an area of the map will fail to load and then it will freeze if I try to a move area or some such. Luckily, I have not yet encountered a bug that corrupted my saves and could't be fixed with a quick in and out.Hi there! If you like my review, please feel free to check out our curator page! _childDocuments_.review: Basically this game sort of answers the question what if Mount and Blade was a bit more oriental and also way more janky. The really big battles are quite cool and remind you of games like Dynasty warriors with the heroes being of central importance. Recruiting troops is cool and all, and there is a lot to explore in the giant maps. Basically you can choose to go at it alone, or you join a faction and fight for them. The relationships system is hella complex and little actions and dialogues, battles all affect how much every tribe and person likes you. You fight someones friend they are now you enemy as well for example. Sometimes party members will randomly leave you though, mostly because they dont like the other party members. There is a lot of variety in what troops you can recruit and they all have upgrade paths. Some emerge in legendary units which are unique to a faction. But you can also recruit monsters, bandits, and unique guild units. There are more quests than you would think but alot of the favor quests come down to the same 3 kind. The gameplay loop is satisfying but the localization/translation is abhorrent. Quests and objectives and directions are very often unclear of confusing. Systems are not fully explained, although you do get a sort of starting guide i ended up having to look up most of the important stuff. In this it has something in common with a game like Amazing cultivation simulator which is just as confusing. The troop building aspect is fun but the rest is just so weird and often janky that i would find it hard to reccomend to people. Sometimes vital quest characters are in weird portions of the map, allies get stuck on environment, people say the most laughable ♥♥♥♥. In the spiritmancer questline which i played, if you lose your companion by making the wrong decisions you are essentially locked out of getting the ending. So i guess if you really like Mount and Blade and similar games give this a try, but wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% must buy! It reminds me of so many games all put into one. I originally thought that I would get bored as I do with many new AAA titles but honestly this game has so much personality. I've always said that graphics mean nothing if the game play is crap and that relates with most of AAA games of the last 10 years plus. The art style, the writing, the atmosphere, the battles, the story, the RPG mechanics are all amazing and work together like bread and butter! I've maxed out all of my soldiers, done a lot of side quests, explored every region, died so many times, won 100's of battles, haven't even got half way through the main quests or done any diplomacy yet and I am already eager to see what the next play through is going to be like. Highly recommend especially for such a low price.

_childDocuments_.review: I would describe this game as a mix of: If you know games like  or , they might can be compared as well.- walk through the land with your Squad,- kill bandit groups or raid caravans,- do quests, - recruit different kind of troops & upgrade them, - trade to get rich,- siege to conquer a town (or everything),- war/ally with factions,- build your own faction or join one,- start a romance with a female character,- recruit heroes- grind dungeons/caves for legendary items (& monsters like dragon/demon/phoenix, if enabled),- level system & skill system,- skill tree for talents (via prestige),- challenge bosses to get better gear- choose your character from different classes (or play as nameless to combine two or more classes)! Use magic, be an assassin or be a magic using assassin, your choice!I would say .There are three reasons for it.The first and most important one is the .You can do specific challenges, clear caves, conquer towns and get their treasures to get legacy points. These legacy points can be used to get benefits on your next run. If you have enough legacy points you can unluck the nameless class, where you are able to combine two or more classes like mentioned above. Playing a different class makes this game more replayable because it won't be the same like the last run since you will have a different playstyle and different skills. Combining them makes it even more replayable.The second one is the . Once you finish the main quest and win the final fight you can increase the difficulty of your next run by +1. There is no limit. This also gives you legacy points.The third one is the , where you only have one savegame. At first this one gives you legacy points as well. It also makes this game harder in a way, that everything that happens is irreversible. It prevents you from save scum, which I really recommend. You might not win all battles. Losing is part of the game, but you will get stronger and stronger.!If you like the games listed above you will definitely have fun here.The start can be a bit hard but once you are into it, you will be on a roll.The price is really cheap for what it is offering already. But keep in mind that it's early access, you will encounter one or the other bug.The game has a high risk of addiction. I played it too long in a row and got red eyes because of that!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a truly abysmal onboarding process. Which is a shame, because I adore the aesthetic of this game and the idea of a "single player" MOBA game.  - Having different options that actually matter during quests was a super cool feature, and something I love to see in games- If you're a fan of MOBA gameplay, this does a pretty good job of feeling like that without being forced to play competitive PVP like most MOBA games- The early levels I did play through did hint more interesting and engaging gameplay early on, especially with later skill tree additions and the possibility of different builds- Army building seems like it'd be fun. The few units I collected early on made me feel like it'd be fun to customize different units to lead into battle later on, when more options became available.- The player character customization options are surprisingly robust. - The "tutorial" is just a few infographics with information bordering on the obvious, and very little pertaining to the actual combat systems. It's not a playable tutorial by any means, and the game suffers for it I feel.- Many NPC and combat interactions don't give you an option to inspect them prior to fighting them, so you can easily and frequently end up challenging enemies that are capable of killing you instantly, even in early/opening areas.- There isn't an option to forfeit or abandon a combat instance after starting it, so if you do get caught up in one, you're forced to die, wait to respawn, die again, repeat until you're out of lives, and then sit as a spectator until all of the random NPC/AI companions die as well. This can often take up to several minutes and isn't interesting or engaging by any means.- The game does give you the option to change respawn points as you come across them, but I found in each case it was faster to just load my game and repeat any quest objectives I might've lost that way, rather than sit through the combat and wait for all of the random npcs to be killed off.- The translation issues mentioned by other reviewers are all true. It's a big point of disappointment for me personally, and almost makes this game feel like it SHOULD be listed as an early access title. - Many areas are unfinished, underdeveloped or have very obvious placeholder assets in place. Waiting around and feeling lost just isn't fun. I won't refund it because I got it on sale for just $7, but I hope the development team is still actively working on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short, quite terribly short.  Yes it is open and there are random stuff you can do to prolong your game time, but initially the level cap is 20 which you can hit in about an hour or two, and the main story quest really only consists of like 10 quests that really can be finished in probably under 8 hours.  Game has a few starting characters to choose from each with their slight variations so that can probably prolong the game.  Game also lets you replay with some additional bonuses including a small increase to level cap every time you beat the game and some other stats/bonuses.  But if you only plan on playing through the campaign once, it's probably not worth it especially since the level is capped at 20 for everything in the first playthrough.For $8.99 sure, for bit more maybe maybe not.  The game's short, there's alot of reused assets (bgm consists of like under 10 tracks, there's really only a few battle zones in the entire game, towns sieges all operate the same way, troop variety is limited).  Lastly, there's workshop support, so you can sort of expect some expansions there (there is a better english translation mod that is a bit better than the mess of a translation in the base game).

_childDocuments_.review: Salzaar is not the best action combat in gaming. It's not the best sandbox game. It's not that great as an RPG. The translation is pretty rough in a lot of places, though nothing that I've never been able to figure out.But the sum of it's parts add up to still be something I still really enjoy. You go from an individual bum wandering around aimlessly to leading an army of troops taking over a nation and commanding other armies as well; while your own character has gone from getting beat up by some random bandits to cleaving through the front line of an army. It's a very satisfying feeling regardless of the rough spots on the way there. I also feel the classes play pretty varied for multiple runs and hero compositions can change things up between runs as well.Ultimately whether the rough spots are a deal breaker or not is going to vary for everyone, but at even the full $15 price tag I think it's worth a bit of a risk for anyone who likes the premise of it. There's not really a huge set of games that give that individual to army / zero to hero combination, and all of them have their own shares of rough spots I've been more than willing to endure.Also I recommend anyone who plays to immediately turn on quick casting for everything - as it makes the combat feel much better than click confirms.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing indie game that I have been following for many months.  With the most recent English language update the game is fully playable. The hardest part is the beginning but after 30 minutes or so you will definitely get a feel for how the game plays.   Definitely a niche game and not for everyone but if you like open world type action rpgs with dynasty warrior type battles then this is your jam!  Get it now while its cheap, you wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks good, and the translation is actually decent, regardless of what others say, but I can't recommend the gameplay. It's a very, VERY, mainland China style of game. By that, I mean the development has all the looks of a polished, full, well designed games, but none of the feel. It's really all the little things that stacks up. Combat isn't smooth, and you don't really get the option of control. In a mass of soldiers, you want to attack a unit, sure, but miss a click and your range hero is now running straight into melee battle. The pacing isn't great, and as someone who played a lot of Mount and Blade, the onboarding here is bad. You're given everything and thrown into a chunk of tutorial text. Quest markers go nowhere, and the controls aren't intuitive. Like, a simple thing would be right clicking to go back on a menu screen, especially since unlike M&B, the menus in this game only take up a small portion of the UI, so it's not intuitive. I'm sure I can put in a few hours to really learn this game and get used to the controls and wonky roadmap, but that's not really my job as a player. My job is just to have fun with the game, not to take a test with it. It's such a shame too. The artwork is really nice, and the concept is interesting. Heck, even the gameplay can be fun. But it's too much work to learn even the basics. Just bad onboarding design.

IE: Dungeons respawn their content within a certain timeframe, but you cannot see the "cooldown" unless you interact with the same dungeon again. This is also true for almost everything that is important to knowTranslations are a bit off.  I thought "deactivate" meant to make a unit a backup unit, but it functionally is to disband your unit.Menus are too slow, and you have to click far too much to proceed through them; with endless selection and confirmation boxes popping up all the time.There's a huge list of issues, but if you like Mount & Blade then I'd definitely recommend keeping an eye on this one. _childDocuments_.review: I feel listing this as Early Access could do it some favors, as it's definitely still a work in progress, but it's a very solid game. (I've realized after writing this that this title used to be in Early Access and had its full release just before I played it. I think it should have stayed in Early Access quite honestly.) Kinda feels like if you mixed the ARPG-style combat of Diablo with Mount & Blade campaign, it sounds like a bizarre combination but it works pretty well and makes for an interesting experience. The translation to English leaves it with lots of typos and awkward grammar, and there's definitely some missing QoL features, like a way to pause time on the map. I've struggled with some quests that just don't have very clear objectives and have even had to abandon a few just because of not being able to figure out what I even need to do. The devs seem to be on top of things with updates since the release, so there is definitely a lot to look forward to with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game so far and enjoying my time so close to perfection, it hurts. I understand this is early access, and I am hopeful that these areas will be as well thought out as everything in this game seems to be in time. However, if there is one area I find lacking as the game is today, it is the items. Just so I am clear, I do not mean armor, weapons, or trade goods; they are well thought out. What I am talking about is item placement. For example, why do you get 41 Uter in a level 17 cave? The 41 wood fine, 41 iron cool, six jade, yes please, but 41 Uter on top of 9 billion in trade is insulting and meaningless at level 17. Just take it out; please add more traps, or fights, or anything. Then there are food drops in caves removing the only real super soft limit to infinite grinding.Also, Fleur is the only place to buy gifts? That seems like a missed opportunity to show the players the nations' capitals to me. Finally, blacksmith tools are being overused. Just add rare elemental stones that cost a hundred thousand Uter in its place. Overall 4.95 out of 5 so close it hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS1. Kinda like Kenshi+Bannerlord mix in together2. Big army fight3. Big map 4. Decent story5. Quite a lot of side quest + hidden quest6. The quest guide doesn't show you everything you need to do. Gotta think a bit for some quest7. Decent customization for characters8. Auto / Manual battle (Auto battle arent completely broken like in M&B where you always lose a lot of troops if you auto)9. Can get big tiddies companionsCONS1. Trading is just broken (You could become a millionaire just by trading in the first few weeks)2. Enemies army automatically respawned after you defeat them. They dont even need time to recruit or train.3. Capturing and making your own faction is kinda useless since your own Sultan/General wont fill in their given outpost/city with armies so they will always get attacked, while enemies army will fill in their city with tons of armies.4. Armies left in city/outpost wont train themselves. You gotta do the tedious work of training them one by one for each city/outpost you capture. P/S: your sultan wont fill in their given city/outpost either.5. Maybe its just me but its really annoying when i cant rearrange my armies card in party window.6. English translation could be better, but its ok i guess. 7. Diplomacy need to be reworked. If you ally with everyone then the war will stop cause no one will attack cause it will break alliance. Other leaders sultan/general will clumped in one place no knowing what to do. I achieved world peace with enough money to ally everyone.probably missed a few points but tldr the game got a lot of potential. one big plus is mods. there arent many english mod yet but if just like M&B modders could make this game legendary. Hopefully chinese modders will make their mods in english. They got tons of cool mods. yeah, im looking at you NSFW modders.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate early access games because, more often than not, they disappoint me, even on full release. I'm always hesitant to buy early access so imagine my surprise when, on a whim, I decide to pick it up because it looks interesting and it's stupidly cheap.I did not expect I'd have so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun with this game. If you're still wondering how it plays out, think the core combat of Diablo, troop recruitment and (albeit very simple and limited) base and territory management of Disciples, and waifu-bait. Toss in a pretty good main story and a plethora of quests and secrets out in the sands, and you have this game.There's certainly far more room for improvement and I've been seeing update after update, so I'm hopeful that the full release has far more than it has now. As it stands, there's already a lot to do and tinker with due to multiple classes, skills, and stories for some of the classes.I do hope this goes far and I'm definitely willing to support the other stuff the devs have planned.

_childDocuments_.review: Liked the game a lot and would recommend it.  I wish there were some help or guides on some things like "how to become a sultan or a governor of a city" and more hints regarding the items people or objects want that you run into.   I never played mount and blade that other players reference so this game for me was a very refreshing game that I never played before. I also liked how they suggest the difficulty of the character you initially chooseSome annoying things I did not like:- the constant pop ups of your "heroes" asking you the same questions that will raise or lower their loyalty to you (at one point every few minutes one of them was asking what to do about returning an item to a dead person).- when you siege a city - if you decide to take it the city the entire world hates you. I would think if you were allied those factions would not hate you as much or you can become allies. This was a huge letdown when I took my first city thinking it's how I would get a steady stream of resources.- combat is a massive confusing rush of armies / heroes running towards each other - not much control - just utter chaos.-only 5 or 6 slots for spells, consumables or objects to use in a fight - this needs to expand maybe into designated spots for skills / spells and another for objects.-gems that will not slot with a group even through i meet the requirement (the one that I recall says rose slot w/o any t6 units). I only have t5 and less and would not let it be used for any army.- the small print on the world map without the ability to zoom and stay in the world map. if you zoom it goes into a section / area.things I liked- wide skill sets / spells and talents with abilities to get a lot of them.- ability to travel far away by using map and right mouse clicking and saying "move"-ability to make notes on the map when you find something (make use of this or finding things later will be difficult)-wish there were more variety on the quests to gain faction (farmer boys that run off, kidnapped victim, bring items, escort caravan, deal with bandits) are the main ones so far that I saw. Initially they are cool but since there are so many cities with factions - doing those over and over get repetitive.-ability to expand bag space and store items off character-the intel screen which is helpful to see what heroes you may want to recruit (use this - i found this way later in the game and wish I found it sooner).- most times the maps would have a symbol related to a tracked quest or specific quest (thank you for this as it helps)So far I think they will continue to improve it which I look forward to trying it once I have more understanding regarding the mechanics of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of the Humble Bundle highlighting indie games from Chinese developers and while there were many games that looked very interesting, this was the one that made me buy the bundle.Having now had nearly an entire weekend absorbed by this game, I feel duty-bound to leave a review.This game has its problems of course, and frankly they're pretty well trodden by the negative reviews that has brought the Recent Review score (at time of writing) down to mixed. Yes, there are some stuttering issues both during hectic fights (which makes sense) and also during travelling the over-world (which confuses me greatly). Other reviews have pointed out the translation is a little wonky in places, which I suppose might be true but frankly thus far I haven't discovered anything that I've not been able to understand or has detracted from my interest in what is going on in the world.The pathing on units is indeed extremely spotty, which has at some points resulted in my cheesing the hell out of some fights as the enemy fails to outmanoeuvre a boulder and subsequently dies to my auto-attacking it from range. It is obviously more of an issue on some battle maps more than others, but given the lack of variety in battle locales in general, the same issue is likely to re-occur.Despite all of this, for £11 this game is an absolute blast and an easy recommend from me. There is so much potential in this sort of formula, and it reminds me most of a game that isn't available on Steam called StarSector. Other comparisons have been made to Mount and Blade: Bannerlord, and I think that gives a good idea of what to expect from the moment to moment gameplay.Combat can be very hectic and a little unreadable; but the game allows you to toggle the speed at which encounters run, so if you want to micro-manage your abilities and units you can play at 0.5x speed. The variety of different units with their abilities and damage types definitely do  matter and there have been situations where repeated defeats have forced me to address my composition, adjust how I was approaching the battle and retry, only to sweep through easily.In my current playthrough, for example, I've chosen to align with the Dakn after their Empress held a tournament that I won and then it got crashed by the Thur faction. Their focus is on the poison status that debuffs enemy units' damage output, while giving some of their DPS units a damage boost against them. I've recruited out-of-faction frontline tanks to help protect my squishy ranged units and I've specialised one of my NPC heroes as a healer to massively increase the longevity of my army.I'm already looking forward to exploring more of the systems I thought wouldn't be good for a first time player, namely one  of the less-orthodox starting characters and the creation of your own, independent faction. You can focus on getting strong enough to complete the main story and just call it a day or you can spend all your time trying to paint the map the colour of your chosen faction, building up your cities and farming for legendary tier gear.I only hope that games of this niche see more development and maybe another studio takes a crack at this top-down Bannerlord-esque game. Until they do, I recommend Sands of Salzaar.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest: I liked what I played so far, but it's far from perfect. For this game, I would like to be able to give a neutral rating, at least for now. So why the negative rating, you ask?As of now, I didn't see much of what the game has to offer, but I had fun nonetheless. It's some kind of rpg where you have to form a group, with either heroes or just regular troups. The heroes are normally better than the average group of soldiers, because they can equip different items. You roam, fight bandits, do mission for some of the factions of the game, do some quests.However there were some times that the game irked me. It happened when I had to do a quest for a village chief. The first time because it was a bug (I guess),and the second time because there's a lack of explanation. I'll explain...By doing quests, you raise your favor with the factions and one of the quest is to get rid of bandits attacking travellers in the vicinity of the town where you would be. And the problem is that I wasn't able to find them. I explored the town, ran around it, watch the map to find a white or red point (white = neutral group/character; red = enemy) but all in vain.Second problem: there's a quest where you have to deliver a letter to a location located in an adjacent region. Most of the time, it's a town and by looking at the map, you can find it. But for this particular quest, I had to find the "arbor palace", which is not shown on the map unless you've already found it. It's one thing to go somewehere, with some indications, like in Morrowind (go east of X, you'll find a big white tree near it, etc.) but it's another thing to just wander a gigantic map just to find one place without any indication at all.So, in the two cases, I had to cancel the quest, which resulted in me loosing favor with the faction issuing them. And that's a problem.There's also some other flaws - at least for me:There should be a way to skip dialogues and/or make them appears faster.There should one or some neutral towns that the player could siege without becoming enemy with one of the factions.About mouse control: it should be left click for attacking, right click for moving. Otherwise, sometimes the player will keep attacking when they just want to move.And especially there should be a way to deactivate the level scalling for the AI, because there's no point in getting stronger if the AI keeps getting stronger too. Or at least, there should be for the wandering heroes, but not for the different faction of the game. Or maybe, the player should be able to chosse at which pace the other characters gain level. I mean, you begin the game, take a look at one the faction and see their leader at level 15. So your goal is to reach level 15 or go beyond that to be able to take them on. So you reach level 15, and now everybody is level 18/19. That's just discouraging. Right now, I don't want to play the game because of that. (And it's worse when you use a mod to remove the cap, my main character is level 24 and everything is level 31. Seriously?)About the level scalling, it seems there is a limit for the bandits. Or at least I think there is one. Right now, they stand at level 15 (= level of each faction's leader at the beginning of the game) and don't seem to go beyond. But it makes me remember Oblivion and its bandits with glass/daedric armor. That's pretty stupid. They're just bandits, not a nation with a lot of fund.The level scalling is the main reason for my negative rating. Some other player might not find it problematic but for me it is. It's true that I had fun while playing, but when I noticed that the AI was constantly ahead of me, it made dropped the game. So, if this kind of level scalling is not a problem for you and you like this kind of game, why not buy it? Keep in mind that's still in early access but it's playable nonetheless. But if you're like me, you might not like what you may find in Sands of Salzaar at high level.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my rule of thumb when doing reviews is that I only give a positive review if, after playing the game for a day or so, I think about it at night when I'm trying to fall asleep.  Or, if I wake up the next morning and I have the urge to immediately turn it back on and start playing.  Basically, if it can root itself into my brain enough to keep my attention when I'm doing something else - then it is worth taking a few minutes out of my day to leave a positive review.  This one has a grasp on my brain and it won't let go.  I want to try another class - recruit different squads - visit other towns.  Next time, I'm going to side with this faction - or wait to accept that quest until I am a little stronger so I don't fail it.  Maybe I'll make a tank next time; or a mage.  The point is that this game has hooked me and I'm still writing a review that I should have wrapped up about four sentences ago....

After seeing this list you would think I hate it, but generally I do enjoy playing this game. The world map is still pretty decent for what it is, combat is ok when npcs are not getting stuck but generally comes down to who can one shot who quicker, the way heroes interact around the map joining different factions, an optional brawl system, and the abilities and such are pretty satisfying. I would recommend this game on sale just be ready for something that maybe needed an early access phase and needs a bit more content and polish.

_childDocuments_.review: From just my first hour alone, even though it was an uphill battle to play I was in love with this game. It truly represents Mount & Blade Warband in a good light. Currently have 34 hours on the game and got to beat the campaign once, so I will say that while I beat the game with one class there is a number of others that can make the result to get there all the more challenging. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes to play Mount & Blade Warband or some simple 2-D combat game that has a mix between advanced and simple combat mechanics, but please read the rest of my review & some others before making a decision. I only wish I knew how to recruit special units like the Ice Dragon, all I've gotten so far were Arboreans & Golems which are still pretty damn cool to say the least. Speaking off which everything has a class tree and typically can be leveled up which makes the weakest unit an underdog in a mid-level army. Just a couple fights and you'll be able to level them into what you need and shift the tide of a battle!Though I will say there are a number of bugs & issues with the game but that's expected after release (even though I firmly believe any game maker should release a well-polished game with next to no bugs/glitches). Level scaling is horrendous so you have to be on your toes. Even though your character might be level 10 and your army isn't, the world will still change to house much more difficult enemies making leveling that much more of an uphill battle. The learning curve is drastic if you don't take the time to read and think about what is being said. I didn't read much at all and found myself treading water until I replayed and took my time, meaning you need to pace yourself and actually read what is being said otherwise you'll miss out on important details. Resource management is drudge work. Getting Wood & Iron for siege gear is like pulling teeth but its nothing compared to trying to gather Jade. Unless you work out a good system of gathering materials you'll get lost.Would I recommend this game truly? Yes & no. Yes, because it was a ton of fun to play and I find it to have an enormous amount of potential. No, because at the moment it is in the need of some development. I'm not sure if certain things are meant to happen or if they removed old mechanics to made things difficult to find. But the challenge alone is something recommended only for those in a "serious" game. You can't sit back and eat chips in this game unless you're trading or doing some kind of management.

You will pick up 50 quests at once, and you don't know where to go for any of them. Sometimes you get a snippet of which village you need to go to, but if you need to find someone or something.... good luck. It will have the "track location" button, but it only gives the location of the quest giver, which is useless. I guess you could take it as if it were a Classic RPG / MMORPG with no info other than the quest description... But there aren't really quest descriptions for the most part. Also, there is a reason games don't do that anymore... because it's not fun. The weird part is that the main quest line does provide you with locations of things, so why doesn't that apply to the rest of the quests?On that note, the map is almost useless.
