_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-The battle concept is good-The idea the game overall is good, but partly underwhelming-Lots of heroes to recruit-Lots of units to recruit-Legacy systems and character customization is great-Great variety of skills and good animationsCons:-Lags more the longer you play the game.  Needs a lot of optimization.  Big battles are awful.-AI levels up way too fast.  They will always be 5+ level above you no matter what.-AI has an insane number of armies and will always outnumber you.-AI don't require any resources to recover after a battle, so slowly eliminating their army is pointless.-It's more work to defend from an attack on a base than what it's worth.-The level for the dungeons are not accurate.  Sometimes I go into a level 6 and get one-shot when I can run a level 9 no problem. -You need to recruit early and fast, otherwise the AI will steal all of the heroes.  Terrible for newbies.-It's near impossible to battle 2+ unit battles-The final boss has the most idiotic mechanics for a fight.  Just stupid and pointless.-Jade is the most annoying resource-Repairing is terrible at a high level-If you lose a large scale battle, you will LOSE ALOT OF RESOURCES.  You will lose at least 1/3 of your units and if you don't have anything to restore them, you're screwed til you scourge some up.-STUNLOCK.  This is the worst part about combat which is beyond retarded.  It ruins large scale battles and just makes it frustrating and impossible to win.  This game needs a cool down before being able to get stun again.  Just so retarded.Overall, there needs to be A LOT of balancing on the AI side with regards to the RTS and battle portion of the game.  Actually make them rely on resources just like players, otherwise it's just pointless to even have this in the game.   For the most part, I did enjoy my time playing this game to an extent to put in 30+ hrs.  However, the cons are just so bad that I don't recommend this game.  There's just way too many cons in this game currently that I don't recommended it.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this game looks REALLY bad. Translations messed up, graphics glitching, battle soundtrack weird and not fitting at all. However, don't be put off by that, once you put a few hours into the game, you'll realize how deep this game potentially can be and how much replayability it has.The amount of content in this game, especially for a game with this price tag, is amazing. The genre is also hard to describe - the best idea I have is a mix of rimworld and sacred, but extremely simplified. To be short, there are different tribes in the game and you can see the activity on the map. These tribes will wage war against each other, trade and interact in many different ways. You can, if you want, join one of them, or found your own. If you choose to found your own tribe, you'll be put into a tough situation that's very hard to combat as every clan will basically be at war with you, but once you've survived this and expanded a bit, it's very rewarding to see your own units run around the map and interact with the other tribes.The combat system is a bit janky, to be fair - CC is not clearly shown to you and sometimes you'll wonder: "Why the hell can't I move?". CC chains are also not very uncommon (shoutout to dhib frost archers I hate you all), which can be quite frustrating. However, once you got a hang of it, it's quite fun to play, even tho fights in the later game are very easy.There is a total of 7 different characters you can play with from teh start, each with their own skill tree and starting benefits/disadvantages and the option to learn other skill trees from teachers in the open world. The bounty hunter, for example, has a very strong early game with his skills, but has negative standing with all tribes, making them attack you on sight. This gives each new playthrough another dynamic and changes how you play the game and in which region you start. Also, there is another character you can unlock after you finish the game once. Also, it's possible to unlock legacy points, and you can use those legacy points to "power up" your future playthroughs with better gear, more starting resources or strong heroes already in your squad.Story is okay from what I can tell, however, nothing mindblowing. Can't say anything else about it.Now, not everything is great about the game. The UI, for example, is horrendous. In order to control your tribe and members, you have to go through a bunch of textboxes. While this does work, it's really not state of the art an I can imagine that there is a much better way to do that. Also, the dialogue between your heroes (strong NPCs you can have in your squad) is basically always there same. There is a variety of 4 - 5 different dialogues (at least with my heroes, apparently different heroes have different "personalities" and the dialogue may change with other heroes) and in the end, you just pick the option that will make the person that likes you the most happier so they stay with you. There is not really anything to it and it's just a rather boring side product.However, considering that the game only costs 12.50€, I can't fault the devs for these problems, especially because many of them (like the messed up translations) are easiely fixable. Overall, the game we have here is amazing and it's something you can dump a lot of hours into, if you like the genre.For my fellow linux users: The game works perfectly fine on the latest proton experimental. No tweaks necessary.For my fellow steamdeck users: The game won't work. While it starts and runs, the controls are horrendous and you need the mouse for walking and aiming, it simply feels bad on the deck. Maybe we will see a controller-optimized version for the game and then, the game will be great for the deck.

_childDocuments_.review: After more than 25 hours I have to say that is a pity to see all this negative reviews for reasons that, in my opinion, are not justified. I even think that the asian people may see us somewhat slow if they read why we think the game is bad. I almost miss the game for these reviews. I'm very glad that curiosity made my bought it.  I will try to tell the most important things, WITHOUT SPOILERS, just making up a little for the lack of TUTORIAL in the game. If you want to discover everything on your own, just explore the options. If you want a minimum info and tutorial here it goes:1. Language: As they say they could have made a better job, none the less not an issue at all to enjoy it or go thought.2. The map: You have a hotkey where you can open a map of the region and also a worldmap. You can make personal markers with descriptions of your own (second click). Also you can go through areas by clicking in the portals and even set your party to move there once you have revealed the map.3. Quest descriptions: In the top left corner you can click on the quest and read important locations of the missions. If you didn't care to look the map in the moment you start a quest you may have to search later for the minority of the secondary missions. But still, this adds to the exploration and it will never be an issue if you don't accept a quest just to accept it and forget it later.4. Quest Marker: In the top-right corner of the quest menu you can activate a quest marker for the main quests, the lack of this marker have been a mayor issue for the negative review, and there it is... Although it is true that some don't have that option by zooming out the camera you can search easier if you prefer. Even combine this with the speed up hotkey and you will be completing secondary quest in no time.5. Tutorial: is non-existent and this could be the real issue and why many players are complaining about things that the game actually has. But in my case it added to the sense of reality and exploration. However, it is true that it would have been better to make a tutorial and let to the player the choosing part. In my opinion it, it would have changed positively the reviews of the game. A big mistake from the devs.6. Making your own faction: To create your own faction you have the option of "siege" in every village or city. But this will set a totally different mechanics from that moment on. So be sure that wars between clans its what you want before you decide to do this. I would recommend you to go for the main quests until you feel like you want a change. There is another reason why you shouldn't rush this. All factions will get really angry with you, the game warns you and it does so for a reason. You may want to improve your relations with other factions before your first siege.7. Giving orders to your troops: F1 to F3 are essential hotkeys, be sure to try them.8. Recruiting troops: you can get them or pay for them. But when you get them the units in the troop will be somewhat less than the maximum capacity, 9. Talents: Certain events and red rocks will give you talent points that are important for your development. 10. Recovering troops: your troops will recover their health with time and with white rose potions. Use them from the party menu and manage.There are more things but I don't think is worth it to reveal more. The exploration is a big part of the experience of the game. I like mount and blade better, but this game for the price and what it offers its a pretty decent game with lots of fun to offer. The style of gameplay is different than M&B. This is not a realistic war simulator and it clearly didn't pretend it also. Just different kind of fun.To me its a steal. I hope you don't end up missing the game if it is to your liking due to negative reviews. I do agree that more hours of development in this game would have been awesome and there is a lot of potential in the game that could have being developed. But that's also why the game is not 30 dollars either. Being honest, I don't understand seeing this game other way than a bargain. If they put cheep DLC I will buy them too.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Mount & Blade and Greedfall made a game-baby in a cartoon world; that would be Sands of Salzaar. There is a lot to do, and it's really fun becoming O.P.A.F. blowing away Bosses easily, but there are a ton of issues (janky coding) like environment-collision-pathing problems, some skills are missing English translation, and there are a lot of balance issues with enemy scaling. You can charm tavern maidens, you can recruit beasts or soldiers, you can recruit heroes which balance your hero type, and really do anything you want to do. I haven't really explored killing down caravans, besieging cities, and political espionage yet, but you can do all this and more. Lots of heroes to choose and unlock as well (free DLC!) But damn, it's really fun and addicting to ride around on an eagle, stomping bandits and religious fanatics, with a huge army and a bunch of heroes. I have only played the first hero (shadowmancer?). I do look forward to trying the other ones. Basically nothing is explained and you learn as you go - the drawback to this is you can't reset your talents, so making good choices early is somewhat critical. Another shortcoming is lack of controller support (which was promised and revoked). The quests are alright overall, some good lore, and the game-world is pretty enthralling.I would really recommend this to folks who like the art, like open world sandbox-esque games, and who are okay with some jank in their games. If you need a perfectly performing game, this is not it. Overall I am having a blast and probably will end up in the 50-75 hour range, which is a lot for me. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Group:Curator Page:This game comes from Chinese Indie studio: 汉家松鼠 Han-Squirrel Studio. If the Chinese portion is not correct blame steam! This is an early access open world title in which you form your own caravan of armed forces and go on a journey of mostly fighting other groups and running errands for various characters. Sands of Salzaar somewhat throws you into the open world that it has to offer to you very abruptly. Armed with a couple of items and a companion that cannot be dismissed, you make your way around the map trying to figure out what the goal is. The main purpose of the game is as follows. You are the leader of the group. Your responsibility is to hire and take on as many units as possible. Help them grow by levelling up, promote them to the next rank, and progress through the story. There are battle sequences in which you mostly control your character that can get quite easily overwhelmed if too many enemy units focus on attacking you. There is no voice acting, just a lot of text that you have to go through. If you are ok with a lot of it repeating when you are going through options then you might not have an issue. If however you do not like repetition, you might find this annoying. Going through options that will bring you back to the original menu choice of dialogue, will have the characters repeating their welcome message, which can be quite lengthy at times. This might sound like picking on the details, but it is a detail that is related to the majority of the game, and that is text based dialogue.The world is pretty big and you can go anywhere you want that is so far available. Be prepared for long journeys however since there is no fast travel yet. You can have your character auto travel to distant locations, but that literally means sitting back an watching them travel on their own. Inevitable, is their struggle to find the road which they have to follow once they begin auto travelling. If you have emails to go through, now might be a good time to take out your phone. Sadly, you cannot organise your squad or open a menu either to check on your inventory. When you open up another window in the game, whether that be the inventory or talent tree, or anything really, the movement pauses. It would be nice if you could organise your things and strategise on levelling up your squad while you are letting your character travel for a few minutes.The battle sequences are satisfying, at least for a while, with the maximum number of units stretched to 200 for now. You can either issue mass orders to different unit types such as defend, follow and attack, or have them automatically decide, often the bad, choice of action. You also have full control of your character. Do not expect a dynasty of warriors type of battle system, as this has been previously described. This is a MOBA style top down battle system. You point and click to move and attack, and aim skills with the mouse. There is no WSAD movement.I have had most of my fun levelling up my units and promoting them to the next rank. The more you upgrade them, the slower the upgrading capability gets. The game has resources, and among them is one called Jade. It is very seldom to come by and at later ranks, a considerable amount of it is required in order to further promote your units. The talent tree is nothing to write home about at least at the current state that it is in. It is somewhat unbalanced since you can choose the auto XP talents, allowing them to stack and quickly level up your units. Be warned however. If your unit dies, you cannot get it back. I would prefer that the unit gets injured to the point where it needs to recover fully in order to return to battle rather than having the unit completely disappear after putting all the hard work and effort into promoting it to the level that it is at.The skill tree is not impressive either. You can equip yourself with consumables you find throughout the world that add some skills you can use a limited amount of times. You can also unlock a limited amount of skills you can use in battle that are indeed very limited. I am sure these are things that will be improved upon full release, or at least I have faith that they will.In the video I mention things that I would like to see in the game, but here they are:-Improve ranged combat-Add quest markers on the map-Make Jade and healing items more common-Balance and improve Talent tree-Unleash the skill tree for more freedom of choice-Render squads injured instead of disappearing once dead-Remove item durability-Skip text quicker-Fast travelIf you like squad managing open world adventure games but do not want to pay the premium price of M&B, then this is the game for you. It looks simple but there is a lot of depth to it in general, with a lot of things to explore in the world.Publisher: X.D. Network Inc.#sandsofsalzaar#gamereview#gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! Happy to recommendRoam around like Might and Magic style with all kinds of resources to pick up, wandering bandits, places to raid, new troops to take in your army and upgrade through different trees like Mount and Blade style as they gain xp.But then you can also join factions, quest for towns and build your reputation with factions, be a trader or explorer. Or attack the towns and take them over so they give you resources or troops also like M&B.The time progresses through hours and days and days as you travel around. And the dungeon raids and other locations reset as times progresses, so you can make the rounds through lands clearing the buildings, caves, etc again, gaining more loots and levels. You need food too for your party, but fighting seems to provide often.Lots of different builds for your own character too, plenty of different npcs to meet, new party members to find, and seems like a considerable amount of lore for those looking to go deeper.--Only issue I saw so far is that there are flags around the map that you can click to make into rally points (to teleport to), and the text isn't translated into English yet, so you don't know what you're saying 'yes' to at first.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wanted to throw my hat into the ring here. Some points *Updated 12/24/2021*  Pros:-Great soundtrack (Like relaxing when you are traversing the world and decent during combat)-Animations and art style are unique-Combat looks smooth (Once you unlock more skills and troops it shines a lot more than when you first start). You can mix and match with skills and weapons.-Translations are decent. Better than I expected.-The classes/characters to choose from come with their own character quests so far have been interesting.-It's neat that the Ai characters are in motion and doing their own things.-The trait system is clean and not too simple nor complex.-Legacy system is cool (encourages the player to make multiple characters).-Saves on different characters are in their own categories so it's not grouped together. Makes it easy to bounce between different character saves.-Tavern brawls are fun once you unlock a few skills and can be tricky to where you can't just spam one button to win. I like that I have to pay a little more attention to the combat in this mode. Example I can't just spam one heavy hit move to win i have to stagger the enemy then do the heavy hitting move.-Siege mechanic is pretty simple but map is larger then normal combat maps. You start out with at least one base and then you have to break the waves of enemies down then capture their bases. -So far the loot feels decent (since I have a couple heroes with me and a solid squad Before that I was having trouble doing the little dungeons). -The game kind of wants you to not strictly follow the story quest line and that's a good thing. After putting a little more time I noticed that as I was on my way to do story mission quests, side activities that weren't in the spot were the main mission was before, were present now. I did them (weren't too hard) I got some much needed gear which helped push me through what would have been a challenging series of encounters. I tested one of my alt characters to see if those encounters were there when I got to the same mission. They weren't but other small encounters popped up. I don't know if it has to do with the day I'm on or timing or if there is something implanted code wise that offers those extras based on your character level or gear. With that being said I noticed with main story quests from that point on there were always options of other things to do that would in turn almost always give me gear.Cons:-Ever since the recent patch the game freezes for about a second (maybe a little less) when parts of the map (sometimes enemies) load in. It wasn't doing this as often as it does now. It used to be once in a while. Last sessions which was about a hour it happened around 7 times. -Cpu % went from 3-6% (It was before the patch) to spiking to 28-47% since the most recent patch. I monitor cpu usage whenever I'm gaming. My cpu is a ryzen 9 5900x. After asking a few different friends the ones that had AMD processor told me they noticed random spikes in their cpu (never lasts more than 10 seconds). While my friends with intel processors haven't experienced that but they have experienced the random freezes for a couple seconds.-There is a lack of direction from time to time where you will be instructed to go find something or kill someone and marker doesn't work. On top of that some of the information doesn't feel accurate (example one of the stories says someone will invade your camp in a month. I hit day 34 and get a pop up that they will come in 7 days ???)-Sometimes the characters get stuck on rocks. Run in slo motion while it's happening (kinda funny)-There is a general inconsistency when getting information on mobs and encounters. Sometimes you can get their level other times you can't. Some areas there are small groups of enemies that are much higher level then all the other enemies near it.-Explanations on some of the other mechanics aren't the best (I've had to resort to guides to get some of the basics down)-There are some monsters that are supposedly on your level but are way tougher then other monsters on your level. Example did an event where you had to fight grunts (like orcs) they were only level 3 and my units are all 10+ and they almost wiped all my units out lol. They aren't even elites or unique or bosses. Just normal enemies who pound the living crap out of you.- About 11 hours in I finally found some of the quest bugs that other players ran into. Nothing that was game breaking. In most cases I just had to leave the area and come back and then I could finish the quest. I put this under con list because it happens every so often but work around just to leave the area and come back which is a hassle if its a quest thats not near a portal to another map.Final Thoughts:At the end of the day this game is an indie game that is under $15 (currently $8 on sale). It's well worth the price. I'll update the game as I play more. I enjoy it for what it is. Does it have issues? Sure. Is it fun for me I dont mind it in between other games. If you like banner lord and diablo then give this a try. If you don't like it then refund it and move on. Oh and the game starts off a bit tough. It has a somewhat steep learning curve. I highly recommend going to taverns and seeing what each hero wants as a gift and get them at least ONE gift. By the time you are level 5 you'll have 1-3 items you can give to someone as a gift. Once you get your first hero it makes the game a lot easier. I want to say the mod support is pretty outstanding with the overhauls (mind you half of them are in Chinese). Current score: 7/10 *Dropped the score by .5 because of the random cpu spikes.

_childDocuments_.review: Sands of Salzaar isn't a bad game as such; there's been a lot of effort put into certain aspects like character customisation, NPC variety, spells, the art is nice and the story and dialogue is solid if not amazing.Unfortunately the experience is ultimately shallow and after a while it becomes bland.The battles are flashy but tend to have very little in the way of strategy and it all take place so fast most of the time that even aiming your spells is pointless, the brawl battles are slightly better but aiming sucks and the balance is all over the place.Trading is very shallow and after a while money means nothing as the most important resource that I needed I couldn't buy anyway.The faction system is nice in that the world changes around you with the factions taking over towns and fighting amongst themselves but when you join one it's a massive grind to rank up.There are bugs aplenty, mistranslations and occasional places where text is still in the original Chinese.Overall the developers ambition is greater than their current skill level but there's still plenty to like about this game. It's worth a shot if you like games like Mount and Blade or Kenshi but it never quite rises above mediocre.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment I would say this is not a buy. Although it has many features I personally enjoy I grow frustrated with the lack of balancing. I don't know if other people have different experiences however the game for me starts off very easy then all of a sudden ramps up the difficulty with mobs in starter areas all of sudden wiping me and my party out when initially I could take them out with just me and my starting companion. Missions are not balanced to the recommended levels with bosses having area of effect attacks of high damage which basically take up the whole screen so there is next to no chance of dodging. I often don't have time to use a healing potion before I am killed as some of the area attacks seem to over lay each other and stack damage. I start the game off as spiritmancer with realism turned off.

_childDocuments_.review: I feared for this game for quite a while since I had heard that the English translation was not so good. I am pleasantly surprised to see that around 98.5% of the game is translated, and while it might require some polish, there were quite few cases of Chinglish or unlocalised text. Nothing too bad that you can't work out with the Google Translate photo tool.Gameplay itself is a hell of a drug: every single time I launch the game I end up losing my whole day in it. It feels like overland Mount & Blade map meets... Diablo-ish combat? Weird mix, but highly effective, imo.Models for enemies are not exactly pretty, but I actually like them in their simplicity, they're good enough to distinguish what the unit is and its main traits, but vague enough that imagination can cover the details (and performance doesn't tank in massive battles with 300 models in screen at the same time).All in all, definitely a must buy if you find it at half price or so (and even without discounts, if you're feeling adventurous). Mod support is improving, and the devs publicly published basically all of the tools and console commands you would ever need. Give this game a try, really.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love it, but...Here's what the game does right:-Fun Combat-Fun character builds-Mount and blade but with sorcery -Cool character designs-generally fun gameplay (Brawls, tournaments)Here's what the game does wrong:-Poor translation and some completely untranslated descriptions and dialogue-Certain ability mechanics fail to work-Ungodly load times, which wouldn't be a big deal if you didn't have to sit through one every time you ran a dungeon/event-For whatever reason, the Nameless class starts out with every faction hating them, making it impossible to traverse without getting assaulted at every turn. Even worse is the fact they don't auto check the nameless legacy option (Gives you 100 legacy points). I get that it's a challenge class, but it's the only class that can multi spec physical talents (IE: Berserker/Bounty Hunter). Just make the other factions hating you a checkmark that gives legacy points.-You cannot see what talents the different Arcanas have before learning them, which is a hefty investment-You cannot romance the cool NPC's, only the tavern maids-You cannot see NPC abilities before recruiting them (which is big now that you can potentially get one of their skill trees)The game has loads of potential, and I spent way more time then I should have trying to make things work. But the little things really pile up as you keep playing. I'll keep this on my radar for updates and improvements though (The new DLC may have broken some things).

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this is a beautiful mess.My main issue:Combat needs some serious rework. Right now its a mass pile up with exactly zero tactis. Just spam stun and AOE. You wont see what happening anyway... my idea for a fix: slow it down - put in some unit/formation system (maybe with heroes as center) - implement a useful tactic/order system.All units run around like headless chicken - you spend most time hunting down single ranged enemies - not funThe whole capture the flag minigame kinda sucks right now, because of the issues above.All menues and buttons need a serious work over - visual and usability wise. Inconsistencies between different menues. Example: how to move items - sometimes you drag and drop, sometimes you mark and need to press buttons, etcThe text speed in dialogues absolutely needs to be adjustable AND skippable!Dungeon idea is awesome but needs a lot more work - very bare bones atmAfter action reports need MUCH better visual representation - how about a AA report page instead of the fade out text?Why the thumbs up then? _childDocuments_.review: Anybody who enjoyed the classic warband simulator, Mount and Blade, in any of it's iterations is sure to enjoy Sands of Salzaar.Salzaar comes off as a 3rd-person top-down version of M&B, but with a much more interesting overworld map.  There's loads to see and do as the player explores the world, either as a freebooting adventurer, or as a member of one of the world's several factions.After the player has had her fill and explored the map to whichever limit she is comfortable with, she may also found her own faction and try to expand her ambition as a liberating or conquering force.I'm still uncovering new things on the map even after 25 hours of play-time... though even if one play-through may last 20-40 hours, there is also a rogue-like 'legacy' system, where one can roll a new character and enjoy boons bought with a currency accrued by the previous character... in fact, it looks as if some content may only be possible to win on a second (or further) play through.Loads of content, fun, and well worth your time!I recorded a series of videos where I explore the game's mechanisms and essential gameplay loop... all with my review-style thoughts.Check it out, it's available here:With more episodes on my channel, if you want to see more.  Thanks for watching!

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels like a weird jumble of features the devs thought were cool and wanted in their game... Mount & Blade conquest, MOBA battles, visual-novel style interactions, dungeon expeditions, etc. None of these features really coincide with one another well, it feels like someone just mashed together a bunch of different games with little rhyme or reason.Many parts of the game feel unfinished or unpolished like really bad english translations, poor character creation, lack of visual changes from wearing different equipment, confusing or lackluster quests, really bad balance(in every aspect of the game), poor direction, bad path-finding, ugly UI, etc.Game needed another two years to cook in the oven. Developers have a rather vague and unambitious roadmap covering the next two months. I say just play Mount & Blade Bannerlords instead. If you have a weaker PC, get M&B Warband.

_childDocuments_.review: God i really wish i could recommend this game but it has some really annoying problems that can kill the fun and made me deinstall because i was getting bored. There are some mechanics that aren't very well explained and the way you get new units also kinda sucks. Its way to grindy imo. Overall the balancing feels super random way to easy at points and literally impossible at others. There where times i had a stacked party ready to beat ass and all of a sudden the enemy keeps getting reinforcements and you just cant win because your so outnumbered and get stunlocked. I have no idea how to get more units to join you because the game never explains anything and it really isnt obvious if you can even get a bigger party than the one you have (when you max out a skill tree to get more units and party members the enemies still outnumber you to a degree that makes victory impossible sometimes). It also doesnt tell you if u can ask your allies for help which they CAN so you would assume that YOU can do this to right ? no clue if thats a thing but the game doesnt tell you so ur kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥. The thing is this game has some really cool ideas and can be very fun aswell... its not all bad but when it sucks it really sucks. Thats why i hate giving this a negative review because there is some real talent on display here and its such a shame that the game isnt more polished and balanced. So many cool and interesting mechanics that with just a bit more work could be really cool. Such a unique and intriguing game with some nice art and awesome ideas that misses the mark just by a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Chinese Scam ahead!Lies about content: Despite not being Early Access anymore, the game immediately warns you that 3 of the 5 areas have little to no content and should not be chosen to play in.Lies about content-depth: I also won the game with just spamming one troop type - showing that the "strategy" in building an army in this game is just nonsense. Get a melee unit type, upgrade them to max tier and you're done with army building.Lies about world-depth: Yeah it's an open world, but every enemy reaches max level based on time, not on what they do. Before Day 100 (~8-10 hrs of gameplay) almost all enemies are max level because they level when time passes. You yourself can't reach max lvl in that time.Lies about translation: Large parts of the game seem to be translated by Google Autotranslate and you still encounter chinese characters instead of english writing regularily.About Mount & Blade / Diablo comparisons: This game plays very differently from Mount and Blade and the comparisons don't hold up. Unit types don't matter at all. One-unit type spam wins everything. people compare it to diablo but this game is just a bunch of units smushing into each other and you left clicking into a ball of enemies. Unlike diablo, you can only have 4 abilities to use in a fight. The fight system feels very basic, weapons don't have an "oomph" or feedback factor at all. The fighting lacks all the good elements of diablo and all the good elements of Mount & Blade when it comes to execution.

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers fun gameplay at first, complete with large battles. But it quickly devolves into swift annoyances and terrible UI experiences.While the combat can be enjoyable, the trouble lies in the imbalances you'll eventually find, the terrible user experience, the lack of UI elements, the continuous 5 second freezes, and the unresponsive commands.The terrible user experience is simply just that; Hitting a hotkey should cause the menu to pop up immediately, not 2 seconds after. While using items in battle, like healing or arcane potions, there needs to be a visible cooldown timer like on the combat abilities. When you're trying to rally with allied troops, that message sent to you needs to give you the area/mark it on the map like a normal quest marks areas on your map. Otherwise, give us something to look up the coordinates with! 1 in-game day is not long enough to run around the map while eyeballing the coordinates on the minimap wondering if you're getting closer or not due to terrain. When you want to go for certain troop types or see what troop types exist in the game, you have to recruit them yourself- there should have been a visible 'tech tree' available to the player. Mount and Blade came out years ago. Bannerlord 2 Just released. There is no excuse to be lacking key features in a game like this. Especially not one that has DLC available to purchase. The repeating quests are simple and repetitive with the only variety coming in for the unique story quests and world quests. That being said, to earn favor from a city, faction or character you'll need to dress much like a mail courier because that's usually what you'll be doing- delivering letters.The game was fun for 5-10 hours, but it quickly becomes boring. The stunlocking combat of the brawls made it turn from a fun little diversion to an annoying combat alternative. The one-shot defense towers in sieges prove themselves too annoying to deal with and the inability to pause the game so you can click a person you wish to talk to and navigate that pop-up menu makes chasing npcs a hassle. The lack of information the game wants to give you is an oversight as well. Overall, I feel the game is somewhat unfinished with these lacking systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so there isn't a neutral review option and I feel this game has had a lot of reviews that are positive so negative it is. First when going into this game understand that its a mix of different kinds of game. RTS + RPG. If I had to liken it to another game it is like Mount & Blade without the interactive aspects during battles. You control your leader kind of like a League of Legends hero, and they can level up to cap of 20 at the moment. Now NPC interactions are basically non-existent. There is some dialogue outside of a quest line but its very two dimensional. You can win over heroes/leaders from other factions and you can in turn start your own faction. There are sort of 'waifu' characters at main towns which you can woo but even after you woo them it doesn't seem to do anything else other than offer you a unique item. Now unless you cheat big time with mods its very difficult to take on the main leaders of the factions, some of them have such crazy abilities that they can oneshot you and your army if you aren't careful. So its a difficult game in that sense. Not much is explained about how units upgrade or how to recruit. A first time player is likely to end up with a piece meal army without full unit stacks. So you end up with a massive difficulty spike when you start to take towns and you can rapidly find yourself cornered and out of options but to cut and run. Lastly there is this section in the main quest line where you have to get signatures from every faction leader for an agreement and the game forces you to jump through hoops and complete challenges that seem to have nothing to do with the story. It feels like padding and it is. Thus far I have't summoned up the will to even bother trying to finish it.Overall if I was to recommend this game I would say it needs improvements in city management. Make the Sultan class interface for buildings universal for all towns and villages, allow for more in depth upgrades for each city.Make the town waifu's do something more than just brush you off like a passing interest after you get their item. Maybe make them into a character than can then join you on your adventure or let them become an administrator in your main town. I would also introduce more economy aspects. At the moment I can own entire sections of the map have 300+ top tier units in garrison without any economic upkeep of any kind, no wages nothing. To some extent the upgrade system bottle necks your progression but once you have a few jade mines under your belt you can just keep recruiting and training up your units endlessly. So that difficulty spike I mentioned disappears into thin air later on. Overall there seems to be a healthy modding scene but watch out its in mostly chinese so you might need to bust out google translate once in a while if you are looking for a specific mod. So overall its a good game, it just needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 25 hrs in and I have revised my review to recommend. There is a lot of beauty in this game and for an early access game it has phenomenal "bones" and massive potential. The world building framework and party building concepts are some of the best I've seen. There are a lot of things that need to be polished and balanced, but that's expected for an early access game. It is a already a very interesting game and can be incredible once it is all fleshed out.However, it can be quite frustrating to onboard at the start. I gave it a thumbs down through the first 10 hours because of one very frustrating mechanic - quest expiration timers. This game is an open world sandbox. Yet a huge number of quests and events in the game have expiration timers attached. The timers are a problem because many quests do not tell you beforehand that they have an expiration. Quests also mention locations that unless you've explored the whole map, you often have no idea where they actually are. So what ends up happening is that as you meet NPCs and take on quests, you end up with a bunch of quests that have unexpected timers attached, and you have no idea where they actually are, or you find out after studying the world map that they are actually multiple regions away from you on opposite sides of the world. This forces you to either ignore the ticking timer and take reputation penalties when they expire, or run around like a headless chicken trying to beeline from one quest area to another. For me, this killed the open world sandbox aspect of the game until I learned the map.There are a number of ways to solve this, from removing timers, to making every timed quest clear upfront, to showing the player a map of the quest location (and NOT just a name) before you decide to take it or not, to allowing you to abandon quests in the quest menu without penalties, etc. This game has so many interesting and even brilliant mechanics, but it also shows that just one influential and poorly executed mechanic can really dampen the experience.BUT, if you have the patience to learn the game mechanics and learn the world map, the above issue will cease to become an issue. The late game also drags a bit once your character hits his level cap, but I think that's just expected for early access.Bottom line: beautiful game, worth the effort to learn, but be prepared for a rough onboarding.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Mount and Blade in a oriental-arabian night fantasy setting, and what i write is basically the EA feature so far.Gameplay is basically your regular action RPG style battle mixed with Mount and blade-esque squad building and grinding although when you're down in squad vs squad mode you can get respawned if any of your army still alive. the world exploration is also following mount and blade style where you can interact with:- npc's squad (to interact, gift, asked pardon, or even entice them to join your faction (no capturing or executing them though)), - outpost, cities (where you can trade (caravaning is also a thing here to make money much more like Mount and blade but it still need improvement on accessible information of goods supply and demand between settlement), get factional repeatable quest, interact with unique character, recruit local villagers (outpost) or mercenaries (main cities), woo the local tavern maid in some settlement, and lastly to siege them for a faction, for yourself, or for ♥♥♥♥ and giggles where you "liberated" the city and unaffiliated it with anyone). later on when you own your own faction and cities or outposts you can build facilities around the city for regular resources utar (the setting currency), wood, iron and jade (the four resources to upgrade your squad) and also caravans.- dungeons exploration for unique loot (this is important because you can mostly get gifts which you can use to win or recruit special character only from finishing the dungeon.) MIND YOU THAT MOST DUNGEON CAN ONLY BE EXPLORED WITH 1-4 SPECIAL CHARACTER and without some of your squad forces like in Mount and blade (although mod might change that, not sure). dungeons are roguelite in that some event that happened in the dungeon are RNG based and it all culminated in defeating the dungeon boss which is after clearing events in 1-10 or more floors depending on the dungeon and some events (which could add some floor).The main story is not that engaging imo, but some of the side quest is pretty good and i think they would improve on this later on. the main meat is the five main factions of the game: - THE NASIR (arabic medieval force that build around strong cavalry unit with strong ranged and magical support and strong spear infantry. they're the toughest faction in-game), - THE DAKN (Militarized indo-persian-western china Assassin-Cult force, that mainly use quick, status inducing infantry, strong magic support, and decent ranged infantry, they got no cavalry but their army usually has exotic creature like giant scorpion. also important note if its your thing to build waifus army, since this is your main faction to recruit female soldier but you can only develop them into a ranged or magical infantry (while there other source like the peasant, but they were more rare and you can also recruit the church of radiance as well). - The AKHAL (central asian nomadic desert raider (mostly inspired by desert raider that lives around Taklamakan i think) which has Strong Cavalry Force that is supported by a strong-balanced melee sword infantry, a decent ranged infantry and a decent magical support.- The THUR  (southern china barbarian tribes inspired faction) that has the most offensive minded meaty-aggresive infantry of which the local forces you can develop into a hulking barbarian that has shield and axe or a hulking barbarian with two sword. Their settlement in the south region (the Umbra Bluff) (a city called as Fleur...such a flowery barbarian they were) also has THE ONLY MARKET THAT SELLS HEALING POTION INGREDIENT (very important early game).- and lastly THE DHIB (Mountain Barbarian culture that was inspired by tribes that lives in the high mountain range of central asia which is use the same name as the real world in-game, The Zagros Mountain). Their force is build around Heavy Two handed infantry that will punish the enemy with stun debuffs. also of note Their home region has the toughest monsters around so be pretty careful when exploring it on low level.Character Creation and progression:When you start a new game, it will prompt you to create a character (which you can edit again later except for the gender by interacting with an NPC at Red Keep) and its starting condition via a system called as "legacy points" which you can use to buy skills, companions, additional item, character, factional support, and stuff. just like the name implied, legacy system can only gain more points after you have played a playthrough and use the earned legacy points on new game. - Character gained stats when leveled up and by unlocking skills, when you level up you can only gain skill points. the character is based around melee class (warrior, tank, assassin, the stuff) ranged (ranged assasin, archer, for physical damage and Mage for Mage ATK) and Support (which benefit from supporting squad members). of note MAGICL SKILL NEEDS TO BE LEARNED FROM NPC and it is divided around three arcana so far as i know of (FIRE, AIR, and ICE) of each has level of progression I, II, and III. you can learn by paying for resource for the I Class, but for further class you need to clear some side quest for the teacher.- another character progression is using TALENT POINTS which can only be obtained by accumulating prestige points (from winning battles, clearing dungeons, defeating world map bosses, owning cities, interaction with prestige shard pillars in map). Talent points will buff your capability of Trading, Survival (squad and character recovery, squad ration management), Leadership (for squad management), Marching (world map speed mainly), Charisma (for characters interaction) and Politics (interfaction interactions).- You can date some tavern lass (but no tavern lad, idk about a female playthrough yet) (get them to 80-90 relation at minimum i think), but you can't marry them (don't know if they will planned this) dating can only be done on one character (so no polygamy or having side girl) in vanilla and if they accept they will gave you a unique item). also as of now i don't think that you can date a waifu or husbando material squad character yet (again, idk if they would change that later), which is a shame.....MODS:this game is pretty stable with mods, but mind you almost all of the mods description and ui in game is still in CHINESE ( my method to beat this language barrier is to copy paste the mod description on google translate (chinese to eng) and you can still guess what the mods do, while the rest is trial and error).Conclusion: if you want a good fantasy mount and blade this is a game for you. Also another points for using a rarely utilized setting and if you love like the simplistic game art. the Early Access state is pretty decent and stable to play right now and i guess it will play pretty well on potato PC, even on battle map. It justified the price and if you're unsure just get it during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment I saw Sands of Salzaar, I knew I would love it! It’s been sitting in my Steam library since release as I (impatiently) awaited the English localisations. Fortunately, English was introduced in September, and come November I finally got around to playing. As expected, once I began playing, I found it hard to stop! For an early access game, it’s really pretty awesome! That’s not to say it’s without flaws though.Upon starting the game, you choose to play as one of several different characters/classes, each with their own specific skill tree, unique troops, magic/arcana, starting troops and specialties. I played through as a Jackal which had me starting the game with two Bounty Hunters, the ability to recruit other Bounty Hunters, and the Jackal skill tree. I wasn’t able to learn any Arcana with this class though. The Jackal skill tree was pretty basic but the addition of the legacy skill trees made it a little better. Other classes, especially with Arcana and additional Legacy unlocks, can become much more impressive and diverse.The next part of character creation involves the Legacy system. Legacy Points can be used to start with additional bonuses, be it skills, items, more inventory space, specific party characters and more. You initially begin with 60 Legacy Points, which I put into additional passive skills for crit and dexterity boosts. Each completion of the game will increase the total number of legacy points depending on what you’ve achieved during your playthrough. After my first playthrough, I now have 392 Legacy Points ready to use at the start of the next game.Following the class selection and legacy points allocation, you move onto the character creation. You get to select your hairstyle, face type, eyebrows, eyes, nose, mouth, beard, body, and trinket (masks, scars, wrinkles). It’s a pretty simple creation system, but it still took me plenty of time to choose what I wanted!I’ve seen many people saying that Sands of Salzaar is similar to the Mount and Blade games, and they’re not wrong. There are numerous similarities, but there are just as many differences too! The obvious similarities are with the different factions, cities, and characters, and your ability to improve and reduce relations with them depending on your actions. The character and city quests are incredibly familiar with the likes of rounding up runaways, collecting debts, hunting down fugitives, making deliveries, and a few other quests. You can also besiege, take over cities, and appoint your followers as sultan of cities.There are many differences with Sands of Salzaar, the first one I noticed being the focus on exploration. Unlike Mount and Blade, Sands of Salzaar is split into different maps, each of which are unexplored and unknown, other than the city locations. Exploring uncovers a plethora of different explorable locations, combat scenarios, plants, items, and prestige shards throughout the world, as well as other characters with side-quests and other mysterious events.Another big difference was the focus on the main story questline, side quests, and character questlines (depending on the character you choose at the start). The main questline didn’t seem particularly long for me, but that’s likely because I took over the world prior to doing most of the quests. I imagine if I had attempted the quests first, I would have hit a wall and had to stop to level up and recruit more soldiers before being able to progress. The way I played it, the only slight challenge was a the very end.Battles and sieges were the biggest difference between Sands of Salzaar and Mount and Blade. Unfortunately it’s not a good difference. I absolutely love the battles in Mount and Blade! It’s one of the aspects that gives it such awesome replay value! Sands of Salzaar has a rather disappointing battle system though, especially when it comes to sieges. You have basic control over your troops, with the ability to command them all or based on their category of melee, ranged, or mounted. It was of some use, but not as much as I would like. Battles were just pure chaos for the most part, particularly with larger battles. There were many times when I couldn’t even see myself. There was just a mass of bodies smashing together. While I appreciate the reality of chaotic battles, it doesn’t make for a very enjoyable experience in this case. Troops often moved so fast that I struggled to click on them to use my skills. It’s a real shame, because this is the main flaw I’ve found with the game, and I truly hope it gets a revamp during early access. While there are various reasons to replay the game, the battles are the one thing putting me off doing so.Sands of Salzaar is an awesome game overall, albeit not well polished just yet, but then again, Mount and Blade games are far from polished years after release and I love them! I noticed a variety of mistakes with the English translation, but considering the amount of text, it was pretty minimal, and nothing that disrupted my understanding of what was being said too much. The stories, characters, soundtrack, and most of the gameplay were great, but the battles really let it down. If they can improve the battle/siege system then it would likely become one of my favourites! It’s still well worth at least one playthrough as it stands though, and I highly recommend it despite its flaws!

_childDocuments_.review: At first I recommended this game, but now that I'm in the late game I can't anymore (the old review is till there). That's because the balance of 1-1 fights is just terrible. At first, I I though I was just not experienced enough, but now it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.I'm at what seems like the last boss, I've maxed out my level, my gear, bought plenty of hp perks from the legacy system, and even with that I get destroyed in less that 5 sec. You also have a healer in your team in that fight. she heals you for 400 hp once or twice, while the boss hits for 1000 hp ten times per second. Also she goes down even faster than me, probably less than a second. TLDR: endgame is broken, so it's impossible to finish the game. So I can't recommend it anymore until that's fixed.Old review:Still in early-mid game, but the overall execution is pretty good for an early access title, and I have very high hope for this game.I love the character idea, with each of them having a different quest line. The world is great, the skills are neat, the number of unit types and all their upgrades are fantastic,  the story is.. what I would expect for a game of this genre. The radiant quests types could use more variety.Bugfixes:* Some skill just don't work. Ex: The berserker jump skill doesn't do damage* UI shortcut that don't work (F1, F2, ect to control your units in a battle* There are some collisions issues where your party can get stuck on the map and you have to use your teleport scroll to get outGeneral gameplay suggestions* Reduce the number of loading screens, it feels like there is one every minute sometimes.* As many other mentioned, quests where you need to find other people are just terrible. Just give us the same quest marker used for the main quests please* Healing high level troops is too much of a pain in the ass IMO (even with the potion perks). I'd love to get a full heal when the unit level up instead of on promotion.* Leveling wolfs is a pain in the ass because you need 5 units to make an alpha, but they come in pair of two.* For ransom quest, give us the location BEFORE accepting the quest.Battle suggestions:* The ability to pause the game (without bringing up a menu)* The ability to instantly resolve battles against weaker enemies. * More finely grained controls for the units. Ex: Id like to assign melee guards to my caster instead of having all of them zerging the enemy troops* Bigger maps with the ability to zoom out (not sure if Unity can handle this though)* In a 1-1 fight, caster characters seems super weak. My spiritmancer gets his ass whooped by boss half his level, while my berserker can just plough through almost everything.* Some boss can stunlock you and that's very very annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Sands of Salzaar is a diamond in the rough.The game has a lot of really promising features, and fans of games like Mount & Blade will feel right at home, but any newcomers are going to have a hard time understanding what's going on.Pros:Solid soundtrack. Themes are pretty well-arranged, the combat music slaps.Freedom of choice. Recruit basically any major or minor character, join any faction, or just do your own thing.Addicting. It's easy to lose hours in this game just messing about and losing track of what you were doing.Fantastic character creator. For a game based around portraits, they did an amazing job incorporating it.Cons:Hard to learn, easy to master. Once you understand how the game works, the difficulty is non-existent.Clunky combat. The combat's decent, but you can easily cheese lots of encounters with the right set up.Mediocre story. The game would almost be better if it didn't have a story.Let me say two things right off the bat. Firstly, this game should still be in Early Access, and secondly, I still adore it nonetheless. People in other reviews have been exaggerating the amount of bugs in this game, in my 8 hours of play I've not encountered a single game-breaking bug. I've seen a character's name be Chinese where the translation messed up, yes. I've also seen that the translation in parts is decent at best. But people who focus on such trivial things are missing the point of the game.The point, being, this game thrives on its lore and setting, rather than its story. SoS is a game about carving your own path in an existing world, much like the game that inspired it, Mount & Blade. People don't need eloquent dialogue or deep character building, because the main appeal is to build an army and conquer your way through countless battles. And that's something the game does very well. There's a lot of characters to choose from, both for yourself and for your allies, and a lot of abilities to use. And the troups are also wide and varied, having unique upgrade paths.But this is also a point where the game falls a bit flat for some. The game is wide, not tall, meaning that while it's true there's a lot of customization in who you want to play as and with, there's very little customization beyond that. The amount of spells that are given to each class varies from like 4-5 tops, with some passives strewn about. Armies don't have much more depth beyond upgrades and while you can learn new abilities, you'll also find that they're all about equally good at killing things. Oh, and as a side note, the skills you get to start with that are not class-based? Those are abysmally bad compared to class-based skills.So, why should you play this anyway? Because it's a fantastic game, despite its issues. I'll be honest with you, if you've not played any of the M&B games, you're going to have a hard time grasping what's going on, and I can wholeheartedly recommend playing those games first and then coming back to this later. This would also give the devs some time to clean up the game. Which, to their credit, they are doing a great job with. Right now as of writing this, the game enjoys frequent update cycles every few days addressing bugs and balance changes, so I'm confident that in due time the game is going to reach its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Sands of Salzaar is mostly centered around tracking down characters and combat; gameplay features include outposts you can conquer, grow and gain resources from, and character and faction reputation; game progression rewards the player with more army units, level ups, increased reputation and characters joining your party.It’s three main issues are being unpolished, grindy and having a lack of depth: Tracking down characters is often confusing and can be difficult: characters can you tell you the region another character is in, but can’t tell you there current location, where they’re going or if they’re in an outpost; the region map does list the names of characters and units inside of outposts, but the text box display arranges them poorly. Furthermore, if they’re in an unfriendly outpost and you can’t take it over, you have to wait for them to leave.Many combat encounters don’t level scaleBuilding reputation is very grindy: it took more than a dozen hours to max out reputation with a faction and the rewards were mediocre: you can command lower ranking characters to attack outposts and you can take units from outpost garrisons, but that’s it. You don’t get more resources, special loot, abilities or character interactions. Character’s are generally uninteresting, most don’t have storylines and their combat traits feel unimportant. Most enemies, except for distinct NPCs, don't level scale, and even when they do they don't reward higher level loot.The first 8 hours of play is fun, but after that there is a steep decline; by 36 hours of play it wasn’t worth playing anymore: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooo this video game ... Chinese developer, cultural differences bla bla bla, but it's got lots of good reviews so I thought hey give it a shot! Bad choice, I really wanted to like this game but it's a bad game and it's bad because ... well for many reasons, but not for cultural reasons or "lost in translation" reasons. Here is what I disliked about the game and you can decide for yourself:- story - bad- music - terrible- UI - awful: you can't even see where your pointer is in in battle, there is so much going on and your pointer is the colour of the background.When you upgrade your troops aside from gaining or changing an ability sometimes it's not clear how they are better so when you're deciding how to spend your hard won Jade it's super unclear where to invest.- combat - The abilities are cool and worth chasing but there is massive inconsistency if fights. In general I found you needed to be at the recommended level for the dungeon or at least one above it. But some fights you get to fight with your whole party, some fights with a couple of companion hero characters and some fights need to be done solo. I played mage and the solo fights were stupid. I kept getting KO'd as melee fighters would just yeet at you, stun lock you and pummel you into the ground.- companion AI - what are they doing? I'm certainly not sure. You get a damage report post-combat and I routinely caused 3-10x the damage. You might be thinking well your character is a glass cannon being the mage, sure ok, but then give the mage an ability to get out of being KO'd in single combat. There was a story campaign I could not complete because I could not get past a encounter which was single combat and the enemy was so oppressive that it didn't matter how much I leveled, how many potions I bought, what gear I chased.- level gating and character progression - there is some really cool things to unlock for your character and as you roam the world you encounter masters of certain disciplines who you can learn different talents from, sounds pretty cool right? Ok but to learn these skills from the masters you need to prove yourself by clearing a hard dungeon. Ok, NP NP. I go to the dungeon and it's recommended level is 18-20 (depending on the master), I'm lvl 5 so ok lets grind some exp. Finally I get to a reasonable level and clear a dungeon, I learn the new skill tree, sick! Then I reach level 20 shortly after and the game tells me that's the max level. You only get one skill point per level so I was able to unlock one item in the new skill tree .... k. Of note I had only unlocked about half of my starting skill tree. Why would they do this? Who's design decision was that?Anyway I'm sure you get the point, it was a baffling experience and strange to me that it got a mostly positive rating on steam

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has a hundred hours on this game, I have say, right now I do not recommend this game. For several reasons, the first of which is it's combat. Combat gets very boring towards the end of the game as it starts feeling less like gameplay and more of a stat check, both for the individual battles and the army battles. The second reason is that the writing is really bad. Like, really, really bad. Most characters have absolutely zero depth, and the quests are all either shallow or vague, melodramatic, convoluted nonsense that often becomes completely incoherent. Finally, let me go into the setting and look of the game. The game looks bad. Some of the zone, Umbra Cliffs especially look horrendous. And it's not just the setting, I don't mind gloomy looking swamp levels in other games and wouldn't rate the game's art down simply because a setting is gloomy looking. I mean level and art design decisions are bad. For example the main river looks horrendously out of place. Don't get me wrong the river is a bad looking in the other areas but looks even worse in Umbra Cliffs because it's blue screen color looks so out of place and got me looking at the other part the map which looks like the person who made it just took one dark green color and splotched a bunch of lighter green colors on top of it without caring about what the final product would look like. There's no logic in where they colored using their color pallet. For example, in one area, there's a bunch of light green splotches which is suppose indicate that this area is wetter, but by the river itself which is suppose to be the wettest place it goes from the darkest green color straight into the computer screen blue colored river which they should have darkened for Umbra Cliffs but didn't.Finally, there was the setting which I initially excited and was hoping to learn more about the factions. But I eventually found out, that all of the faction lore is completely superficially and suffers from the problems with the plot in that it is always told but not shown. For example Jamal City which the plot and other character repeatedly mentioned is never visited once during the game despite it supposedly being the seat of the Nasir faction and capital of Salzaar: the name of the whole region. None of the factions leaders, in any quest or dialogue take any action regarding it, despite it supposedly being a very important city. Furthermore, all the all regions the feel the same once you get past the intial tile swap. You don't a feeling of cold when you visit the Zargos Mountains, it doesn't feel hot in the North East Desert that I forgot the name of. And I'm not complaining that there isn't a climate system, I'm complaining because it doesn't feel like the people there have a different lifestyle or culture from the people living elsewhere. And there are a ton of design decisions they could have taken to do that. For example having the people residing in those areas wear different clothes since one is snowy and the other is supposedly a really hot desert. Instead they all wear the same clothes, and what's worse none of the people seem to care about the other regions or even mention that there's a major civil war going on after the main government who previously ruled all of Salzaar collapsed. The main quest hammers you over the head with vague platitudes about the "horrors of war" but none of the people in Salzaar seem to care about it in the slightest. In fact, outside of the main quest, I don't think a single other character even mentions there is a war going on. Caravans coming from one faction are fully willing to travel and trade with cities of factions they are at war with. I've been told to deliver supplies from one settlement to a settlement of a faction they at war with the same gravity of being told to milk a cow. And when I became the head of my own factions, I could wander around freely in a region entirely controlled by my enemies, without a care in the world. I could even sneak into their towns, talk with the enemy lords and mayors and do requests for them as if nothing was going on between us. Which is why I say that the characters, setting, and plot are extremely superficial and bad. The very textbook example of tell but don't show. There are other examples I can give of bad writing, but I think you get the gist already. Overall, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "To live is to suffer. Surviving and thriving requires finding meaning in that suffering...." ~An old wise proverbChinese-Cultivation-Micro-Management-Torture-Simulator with an Arabian Nights twist! I mean that endearingly by the way! Personally I find it difficult to get passed the growing pains in this genre. Everything requires specific resources and you can neglect the simplest things to disastrous results. Want to build up a strong army? Okay, but you're going to have to feed them and get enough iron,jade,and wood to upgrade them into better units. Meanwhile important characters around you are constantly flip-flopping between friends and enemies as if you are still dealing with the most unstable of high-school cliques. If you help a certain fraction you will anger at least two others so forget about being a people-pleaser whom is loved by everyone. You can be a good individual but there are difficult decisions in which you'll wrong others even with the best intentions.Your character can amass some sweet wuxia-like powers such as a jumping ground pound that knocks down and stuns enemies,a purple wave of toxic vapor that blinds and poisons anyone unfortunate enough to be in the line of fire,or chain-lightning that jumps from one adversary to the next. That's not even going into more fringe traits such as beast mastery or bewitching your enemies to the point they are either your slavish servants or terrified bewildered quivering lumps of meat-jello!At some point I realized SOS began hitting that sweet spot that lands somewhere in the vicinity of Diablo 2,Fall-Out 1-2,Never-Winter-Nights-Diamond-Edition,and the Baldur's Gate games. Sure, you could say there's a bit of Kenshi,Mount & Blade Bannerlord,and Dynasty Warriors in its' pedigree as well but my point is it's a serendipitous blend of good story telling and mostly no-holds-barred immersion. You can pursue the main quest,flirt with a bar wench until you woo her socks off,buy an exotic menagerie of wild animals,dive into abandoned mine-shafts for some left over goodies,escort caravans across the harsh tundra,fight frost dragons in a giant derelict library,engage in magic duels with ifrit wizards,enlist mercenaries in a rescue attempt to free a kidnapped noble,or help the village elders against encroaching bandits. This is a living world constantly shifting and constantly in turmoil. As such new opportunities are always presenting themselves!Atop all that there are many helpful steam-workshop mods that combine into a magnificent genie that can do everything from increasing your level cap to upping your charisma whilst doubling your incoming resource allowance.Really cannot recommend this desert-gem enough!Pros+ Pervading story-line and lore are truly enthralling.+ Do "everything" from drunken bar brawls to gradually creating your own army of bad dudes,femme-fatales,and exotic mystical beasts.+Politics of the various fractions keep things interesting.+Look at your horse,he's friggin amazing! Stroke his mane and I bet it tastes just like raisins!+Fall in love and even sire a legacy character. (With the right expansion)+Every "class" is also an individual protagonist with unique aspirations,disadvantages,and perks.+Soundtrack is silky and sublime with the audio swagger of a sexy Arabian belly dancer! Whether upbeat or melancholic the compositions are great!+Game and its' expansions are reasonably priced.+Steam-work-shop support!Cons-Rough time starting out. There is a lot to learn! If you've never played a game like SOS before it can seem overwhelming but if you persevere you will be greatly rewarded!- Sometimes I wish the character models in-game had just a bit more detail. However,their simplicity of design allows a lot of chaos to happen on screen with minimal lag!-Quests between settlements eventually break down into the usual types. Encourage wandering teenagers to go home for their own safety. Escort a merchant caravan. Kill some bandits. Find a thing. Return said thing to the one asking for it. Kill some monsters ruckus-ing around in a mining-shaft. You know the drill! (To Sands Of Salzaar's benefit the narrative or character driven quests often come with unexpected twists and turns,even if they seem mundane at first!)-Think you charmed the socks off your newest recruit? Think again! The heroes and heroines can be quite fickle whilst enough botches during multiple choice conversations can quickly lead to defections. Better have a lot of gifts on stand by! _childDocuments_.review: A mixed experience, but entertaining. The game is very flawed but has an entertaining gameplay loop and a lot of potential if some of the flaws are fixed. I'll start off with the bad parts so that I can end with the good. 1) Bad translation. This isn't unusual for a chinese game. But some parts in dialogue are particularly egregious and in general sap all immersion. A lot of scenarios reminiscent of those youtube ads for mobile games that don't exist. A few menus have small portions still in chinese, but most are translated fine. Mainly just the dialogue that is wonky. 2) Memory leak. The game gets slower and slower to save and traverse through map areas the longer you have it running. If you play the game for more than like 8 hours in a sitting it will take like a minute to traverse areas. Clearly a memory leak, needs fixing. 3) Lame story/sidequests. This is partially due to the translation, but in general all the side quests and story quests are very uncompelling. At their best they are just very anime and uninteresting, at their worst they are mistranslated nonsense. But it's a mount and blade type game so you don't play it for story. 4) Combat. A shame really. It tries to go for an Arpg + M&B type thing. You control your character from a top down view whilst your army does its thing. Uses league of legends type controls. Tactics are basically non existent. There is a menu for it but honestly, its a waste of time, the battles are too quick. You can't issue commands as the armies close in like you can in mount and blade or starsector. Combat is also really clunky. Especially tavern fights are REALLY clunky. Overall just not very fun unless you have particular builds (knight errant is fun). Mixed points: 1) World design. The world in general is uninteresting and uninspired. It has some locations I like a lot, like the Umbra cliffs and Twinluna valley. But if you asked me to tell you the difference between West docana desert, crying rock, and redstone valley, I wouldn't have an answer. 2) Factions. I can see what they were going for. Nasir have a balanced military with a bit of everything, makes sense as they were the biggest remnant of the old empire. Dakn have mainly ranged units, all units are light armor, they prefer to use poison and such. Dhib don't have much unique about them besides their cool animal hats. Thur are heavily armored units, with the tankiest units in the game, as well as unique siege weapons. Akhal are the cavalry based faction. The issue is that The factions don't have very good unit cohesion within their own faction, you kinda gotta mix and match in order to have a good army. This is a problem for doing faction based runs that a lot of people (including me) like to do in mount and blade type games. Thur units are so slow that their ranged units tend to run in front of their melee troops, because the melee troops walk at a snails pace. Dakn troops are super squishy and just get ran down, in fact, dakn has such bad unit cohesion that they get eliminated by the AI pretty early in every run. They have cool scorpions though. Nasir is the only faction with a balanced military, so they basically always take over large swathes of the map. The AI doesn't react to snowballing factions well either. So basically only you, the player, can stop them. 3) Music. There are some good tracks. They are just too short and play constantly, unlike games like kenshi that give the music time to breathe but have bangers every once and a while. Good things:1) Customization. This is the main good thing about the game. It has very very very good customization. There are some premade classes availible, but you can pick skills using legacy points that you earn in your runs to slap additional skills onto effectively a second skill tree, to spec skill points into as well. Once you beat the game you unlock a unique class where you essentially just build your own skill tree, making an eldrich horror out of all the skill trees of the other classes, or making your own fresh one. There are gems that you earn throughout the run that you can slot into units that give them bonuses and stuff, and you can customize your units further with this. Party member skill trees are also customizable so you can have your party member play off your strengths or make up for your weaknesses, etc. 2) Unit variety. Even though the factions units don't dont work that well together if only using one factions units, there is still a lot of variety and some cool ones. Especially the secret units, though how you get them is a little wonky. From infantry that summon crows, to ballista, to giant demons, to dragons, to snake people, there are a lot of unique units, with their own upgrade trees. Conclusion: Overall, if you like mount and blade type games, played all the others and want more, then consider it. Especially if it is on sale, don't quite think its worth full price at the moment. I got it for 6 bucks. It's extremely janky and you might walk away dissapointed, but I found it entertaining at least. It has a ton of flaws but overall has a lot of potential and I hope it gets some issues fixed and becomes a great game in the future.
