_childDocuments_.review: edit: This is my first time changing a review on steam. My review is now changed to negative. I Thought of doing it for about a year now, but was sure after I read this update to Sands of Salzaar. In quotes a major detail in this update on June 21st, 2022, in the V.1.0.4 ,"- Adjustment: After the heroes have been defeated, they will return to the nearby cities and enter a 3-day CD, in which the hero will not go out of the city to attack other people within the CD." Sands of Salzaar is...A SANDBOX WAR GAME... that will NOT let you kill enemy heroes as an alternate way of playing the game readily available in the settings. Think about that for a minute.I seriously wonder if this game is being intentionally sabotaged by some of the developers, not all of them, but some. This isn't the only major issue for me, just the one I feel is one of the most immersion breaking and easiest to add, and just common sense.... again a sandbox war game, but you cant kill the main characters, even if at least it was only in rare types of high stakes battles...The disturbing irony here is outrageous. I am considering buying the more popular Tale of Immortal game instead of trying to play this again. Overall this game has been such a huge let down. I regret buying the 5$ music dlc, as small an amount as that is, because of how hyped I was about it, and at the time I just wanted to give more money because it seemed so much better than I thought it would be.I recommend people to try Tale of Immortal as a similar type of game to this, but some major differences. With Tale of Immortal, despite the recent review bombs because of the steam workshop debacle which is now fixed, it has some common sense and fundamental things that Sands of Salzaar lacks, and I would probably like it more overall despite it being a bit too "wuxia" for me. Oh, and you can kill people in Tale of Immortal...you know...a feature that people would expect in a sandbox war game...previous review below:___________________________*****Note to developers please hear me out on this multiplayer idea for Sands of Salzaar, also note to other players reading this, please mention this in your own reviews or spread and share this elsewhere if you would like a multiplayer game similar to the idea I have below*****Before I discuss the idea, I want to emphasize this is a very unique and good game that I would compare to a more rpg and isometric version of the Dynasty Warriors Empires series of games. I played this game for about 30 hours(a lot of that time was offline which is why it only shows 17 hours played). I liked many aspects of this game, but what really stood out for me the most that I enjoyed is the various classes/skills that the main character you are playing can have and the other well designed character companions in the game you can recruit into your army, as well the different types of troops you could get in your army that can be upgraded and ordering them where you want them to go in battle.If this multiplayer idea I am recommending is designed very well I think it has the potential to ideally become as popular as League of Legends. This idea is an adaptation to the moba and rts genre of games in addition with an element of the fighting game aspect of "Dungeon Fighter Online" game in the pvp part of that game, and would be something I thought of called an "mssoba" standing for "multiplayer skirmish strategy online battle arena." Simply put no more of the overdone 5 versus 5 player, with 3 lane type of game like League of Legends. Instead it would be for example at least 7 versus 7 player games, much LARGER maps with more variety of maps and strategic depth to that, each player has their own 6-9 stronger "companion characters" and 30-50 troops that can be given orders, in addition to the players having their own highly customizable rpg character they play as, and the gender freedom to pick a boy or girl rpg character with lots of freedom to pick various different abilities and skills for many types of class/ability combinations, and NOT a specific preset "champion" character you control like in League of Legends that only has the skills it has in that combination. Perhaps also add a Dungeon Fighter Online type of depth with the action "fighting game" depth and mechanics that Dungeon Fighter Online has and would make the combat, especially in 1 vs 1 fights, have more depth and skill ceiling to it, but would also enhance team fights with many warriors from your army in addition to your teammate's "companion character's" and army's. If done well I think this idea could be a good foundation for an in depth multiplayer game that many people might prefer playing instead of League of Legends or any other moba type of game. A bit random, but even though it is somewhat easy to ignore and not a huge part of the game, I think if it's not too difficult that the characters in Sands of Salzaar should have faces even if it's not really well done, but maybe it is something already planned to be added because it is still in early access. This is also slightly off topic, but if there was a game that is an mmorpg that sort of combined the best of the aspects and gameplay of Sands of Salzaar with Dungeon Fighter Online especially with the pvp "fighting game" mechanics and skill ceiling(also making sure to remove gender locked classes), Albion Online, Tree Of Savior, Lost Ark(again remove gender locked classes), I think many people would like it. Each one of those mmorpg games I mentioned has good things about it, but there are too many things I dislike about it that discourages me from bothering to play it; yet I think a really good mmorpg could be made that is inspired from what's good about those games that I just mentioned, if it's done very well.

_childDocuments_.review: Go from nobody to nightmare in Sands of Salzaar. In this game you start off struggling to fight a small group of bandits and you'll finish being able to take down whole armies single handedly. If you like the feeling of growing substantially in power then this game is great and a lot of fun. Character customization is great (at least in the stats and abilities department) and if you want to just lead a massive army that can be fun too. A very enjoyable rpg that is rough around the edges. That is to say it does have some problems. The game can run like ♥♥♥♥ at times which seems to get worse the longer you play, this can be a problem because it's very easy to dump hours of time into this game without realizing it only for the game to start hanging every time you hit a thick crowd of enemies with an AOE. The game also has translation issues, it is fully translated now, though the problem is that the translation can break and leave you with some things in chinese (though this could be caused by installing different mods). I'd give this a strong recommendation, though catch it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute dumpster fire.The game kicks off with character creation, where you pick a bunch of skills and abilities that the game makes absolutely no effort to explain, then or later - there's not even a Help codex or anything. Is having an extra squad good? What does Spirit do? Can you figure out via context what Arcana means? Amazing. Enjoy doing all that to music that loops every 20 seconds or so, which you can't turn down until you're done.It doesn't get better. Combat is auto-battles except your character, with AI that gets confused by complicated concepts like needing to go left 4' to get around a wall, and heavens help you if you summon things. An early dungeon has exploding barrels that my fire elemental killed itself on repeatedly, preferring to attack those over actual enemies - and a boss in a tiny room with exploding barrels, which also inexplicably adds an invisible wall behind you. There's no dodge roll or anything either, so it's basically kite or stand-and-brawl.The "story", other than crit-path, feels heavily randomly-generated, and nothing is explained, so if you can find some reason to get an emotional investment in any of it - well, you're more fortunate than I was. English translations were excellent for everything that I saw.There's some neat ideas here, but oof.

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult to get into.  The introductory plot didn't grab me and I found myself unable to muster much interest in exploring the world.  The game railroaded me to the first settlement.  I could have gone elsewhere, but the areas off said rail seemed to contain only enemies above my level.Although the skill system seemed interesting you don't have much to choose from.  Early game the "recommended" character is a fairly boring ranged attacker.  Combat was, unfortunately, boring and clumsy.  Hold the left mouse button down to run around but also use left mouse to attack.  Holding shift keeps you in place so you can aim.  Diablo-style interface.  Click, click, click, use hotbar power, click, click, click.  Timing, reading the opponent etc. not really a thing.  The enemies, rather than fight, ran all over the battle map and I had to chase them down one at a time.On the plus side, the hand-drawn art is nice and I enjoyed the combination of Arabic and Chinese influences.  Character customization has many cosmetic choices.  The music didn't stand out, but wasn't bad either.This game may develop into something more exciting as it proceeds through Early Access, but for now I say give it a pass.  For Mount & Blade fans enticed by reviews comparing the two, you may find the similarities only superficial.  Stick with M&B for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a surprisingly entertaining game. Some compare it to Mount and Blade, but I'm not so sure. It has similarities, like taking over the map, raising armies, vassalage for companions and so on, but the core, the combat, is quite different. But the game is rough around the edges. It has a lot of translation issues, but nothing you can't handle. As a non-native English speaker, I can easily follow the story, but some quest descriptions could be misleading. The combat suffers from its ponderousness. You might enjoy the battles at the beginning, but the more warriors involved, the harder it becomes to keep track of them. Most fights take place without the player doing much damage, at least if it is not a mage class. As long as you're fighting bandits, it's a lot of fun, but as soon as AI armies are involved, the chaos begins. And at that point the game can be unforgivably difficult. Time passes while the player is in battle, this can lead to a victory on the battlefield while in the same second someone has besieged the player's city.Many things are not explained well and have to be figured out by the player. This may be fun for some players, but for me it led to a lot of confusion. It's not so easy to figure out why someone hates you while you're making friends with everyone. In fact, there is a strong relationship system under the surface. If the player befriends someone, everyone who hates that friend will also hate the player. And this feature is not particularly well explained or clear. One can combine troops of the same type to a full squad, but that also is not explained.The graphics are a bit simple, but I like them. The mod community seems active, but most of the mods are in Chinese, so they barely work in the English version. (Unless you can live with the mods converting parts of the game back to Chinese). The game can get boring with running around, fighting, running around.... But there are a lot of quests that the player can do. Nothing special here, but it adds needed variety to the game. Some characters that the player can choose from have their own backstory and setting in the world. For example, the player can choose to start as the sultan of his own clan. This is nice and adds replay value. The music fits the setting and I personally like it a lot. (So much so that I am considering buying the soundtrack).All in all, you can have fun with this game, even if it is frustrating at times and lacks some Qol-Features.Update:I have to change to negative, beause of the missing translations. Parts of the game are still not propper translated and I had to stop playing the game. Wil change back, if this is fixed. I hope they will.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game that deserves recognition. It's as if a dungeon master for DnD decided to make Mount & Blade. If you've played M&B, you'll find the map and party system familiar. There's companions and your army (which can level up, unlock new skills, etc.), there's towns you can take over, etc. The battling in this game does not go into as depth as M&B. However, M&B definitely lacks the creativity and deep story that Sands of Zalzaar does offer. That's where it reminded me sort of like DnD. It has rich story elements, different character races (which learn different spells and abilities), and it's dialogue is as if it was written by a creative DM (one with great flow and who is easy to understand!)Highly recommend this game, it's one of those games that I think really deserves to be played. It's got that charm and it has that depth.

_childDocuments_.review: surprisingly good. seriously. if mount and blade / kenshi + some diablo + anime waifus + a little bit of heroes of might and magic thrown in sounds good to you, get it. it's addictive as hell. the price is a steal.the translation isn't perfect but it's more than fine. a few of the quests give vague directions and GASP you might have to actually look around a little or pay attention to the map/compass/dialogue, but I have yet to run into any issues i could not solve in less than 5min. if you need guides and wikis to hold your hand or are too dumb/lazy to use more than two brain cells at a time, then maybe take a pass.my ONLY other complaint is that at first the game will feel like a cheap mobile game. the graphics and ui will feel janky. etc etc. but i can only compare it to experiences with games like rimworld, kenshi, mount and blade etc where at first it feels unfinished or cheap but the more you play the more you realize how good it actually is and the jank just gives it a unique character and before long you won't notice it anymore.otherwise game is awesome, belongs right up there with games like rimworld and kenshi. perfect example of "don't judge a book by it's cover."

_childDocuments_.review: RPG wise - I don't particularly care for story that much and I usually try to ignore it but in this game I find myself having to pay attention to a few things and there is so much dialogue that I can't help but feel so much effort went into the RPG element of the game. So many companions and their own in depth side quests. Choices seem to actually matter and some of them are quite hard to make.Gameplay wise - Great potential for this to be a fantastic game with some polish added to it. If they make it Co-Op campaign playable It will be amazing. Combat can be perhaps a bit too fast paced, either you stomp the enemy or they stomp you and the targeting system is a bit iffy when theres lots of enemies on screen. Still I find the big battles incredibly fun if you have AoE skills.Gear system - The gear system is interesting but it feels very lacking. A little too heavy on RNG as I normally find myself selling countless wizard weapons and usually the same lackluster armor pieces. Then randomly ill be given an amazing weapon at lvl 6, and won't be able to replace it till level 20. Perhaps adding a relatively simple crafting system might solve that?Diplomacy - I found this a little annoying honestly. Very few options and a lot of faction leaders can be super hard to track down, then when you speak to them the only way to really neutralise their war declaration is to throw all your money at them or somehow earn their favour without their generals just slaughtering you or you slaughtering them and making it worse.Questing system: It is good that there is a lot to do, I wish there was a bit more of a quest tracking system. I've found myself a bit overwhelmed with the amount of quests I take on and then some of them have very little indication of where to go to complete them. Where as some also do have good dialogue and markers to show this. Just not all of them.Classes - This is what makes the game re-playable really. So many classes to try out and so many different ways to start the game each time do make it somewhat of a completionist's dream to play eventually. I think some of the non magical classes need a bit more substance about them though. Some classes are bonkers in terms of strength compared to others so far.Overview - Play this game and review it yourself, see what you found different.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I originally played the game during the 1.0 release and coming back to it two years later is a disappointment. They've improved nothing of the base game and has instead focused on releasing DLCs. AI and UI are just as bad as ever. Some playable main characters still don't have their own dedicated stories. Just a shame for a game that had so much promise.This is already a good game, however it's clearly unfinished and the current edition of the game is still very barebones. There needs to be more user friendly controls on the world map and on the battlefield. The companions need to be fleshed out, given their own stories and reacting to your actions/the world in a believable way. This well then also create more emergent story telling, which is current lacking the Paradox flair. Balance is also subpar, with siege weapons being crazy OP.Despite all that I'm still giving it a recommendation. You can see the potential and the game is fully playable as is, albeit can be frustrating at time.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me Mount and Blade, with new quirks thrown in.+ My old toaster can run it+ Large world map+ Battle map scales with the amount of troops, so you wouldn't get a battle where you would simply run half of the battle to get to the enemies+ Different classes, each with its own unique quirks.+ Mods!Mods!Mods!+ Bosses and dungeons to clear. When you get sick of trying beat up everything that moves you can go and try clear a dungeon.+ New Game+, each time you start a new game you get fixed amount of legacy points, which you can exchange for nice stuff when you start, like more bag space or skills.- AI can be weird at times, like using AoE spells when no one is around.- Durability on gear, while great mechanic, I would like automated system for it instead of having to manually repair each time.- Rather low max level on heroes/characters.- Gift system. Giving a gift shouldn't get you make people like you more than doing a personal favour/quest for them.Overall it's a great game, I would suggest trying it out if you are a big fan of Mount and Blade and like diablo style games.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished story as Sentinel (focused on swapping auras to buff allies with small bursts of personal damage), haven't tried Sandbox yet. I liked it overall. It plays like Diablo in a Mount & Blade setting, but isn't individually as expansive in gameplay style as either of the two. Your own character can become relatively OP towards the endgame, but not to the point where it can solo an entire army and make the strategic layer irrelevant, as enemy leaders also level up similarly.Pros:+ Gameplay is generally fun if you like building up your character while seeing huge unit blobs fighting it out and spending time convincing powerful characters to join your side+ The aesthetic is cozy, reminds me of classic CRPGs+ Trying to minmax your unit composition is fun+ Devs seem to be actively improving the game+ Mod support is always a good thing; nothing too groundbreaking seems to be out yet, but the game was only recently fully released+ Losing a battle usually doesn't fully wipe your squad, which is a great thing given how expensive it is to reach high level compositionsCons:- I only found out time acceleration exists as a random tip several hours in, that should really show up sooner (Hold ctrl for anyone who also didn't know)- Inventory management is a pain- Limited quest selection between town and character favors, they get repetitive pretty fast- Battle/map load times get progressively slower while playing until a game restart, there's probably a memory leak somewhere- No way to test out how certain squads would work, you commit to units before you know what they do- Map AI needs more work, can't fight grouped battles outside of sieges- Settlement development doesn't really feel meaningful- When you run your own tribe, managing your companions/leaders is kind of poorly optimized from a UX perspective, hard to keep track of who's where and doing what, and they also don't seem to ever go on the offensive on their own. This last point might be since I wasn't playing on max difficulty, though.- Endgame is mainly running to the same jade chests from bandit camps and repeating two dragon fights on a fixed timer to get jade and skill points for the extra oomph on the character level, strategically you try to win one town at a timeSo in short, the pros are that it's a fun idea, executed decently enough, with a suitable aesthetic, and the cons are that the game still has a lot of jank especially surrounding the strategic layer and endgame content. It's not for everyone, but if you can't get enough of personally leading armies in games, it's worth a try. I'm hoping the devs spend more time polishing the game, I think it has a solid core in place.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect much from this game as it only cost around 100k in my currency which is about 7USD, so I thought, nah this game doesn't cost much and probably poorly made but I'm willing to try. Man, how surprised I am, the game is so good, although there are still many bugs and some untranslated word in game, you can use your google translate on your phone to understand with auto translate(the chinese character or hanzi is not much). If you don't mind a few bug, the game is really awesome, the story is very deep, the BGM is spot on, the illustration is beautiful. The cons is the game just put you directly into the game without tutorial or any explanation, but you can use Spiritmancer first to understand the game. Once you understand it, you won't be able to stop playing, at least I do.You can be anything you want in the game, all conquering sultan, a powerful general that will make your sultan the strongest ruler in the game, or even a standalone power figure. No matter how strong your character is, it's impossible to win a war without troops as you will be stunlocked till you die, unable to move. So if you read some people said that the stunlock is game breaking bug, I don't think so. If you don't get stunlocked you will be able to solo almost any war, and that's not supposed to happen. You need troops to take damage for you, and you can create your own team however you like, strong shielded tank, or poisonous assasin that will poison through that thick armor, or so on. A strong troop can even beat a weak hero solo sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: If you know what Mount & Blade is then meet it`s stream-lined mythical counterpart. Honestly before you throw the "cheap knockoff" tag on this game it`s worth giving it a try since it might surprise you as much as it did me.You start by picking a class which also acts as your background and will also give you your class quest. After making contact with your first mythological enemy you may choose the area of the world in which you will start to make a living. The world is separated in 5 factions each with it`s own territory and they often also fight one another, with you acting as an agent for them or a 6th faction if that is what you fancy. Your avatar is the interesting part here. In battle he controls like a hack&slash character while you attack and spam skills, while your army is commanded through a simple yet efficient menu for issuing basic orders. In sieges on the other hand which play more like an RTS where you capture keeps you may order your army more directly.  The gear in the game is also different from what you`d expect since it falls in the RPG type of quality and stats over realism. In the world you have resource nodes, bandit camps, adventurer camps and temples to fight 1 on 1 with heroe of legends. Each granting you resources and gear. And then we have the dungeons, giant visual novel style dwelves that end in an exploration map with some though enemies and a boss that sometimes might wipe the floor with you even at the recommended level. The freedom si great: join a faction, ,make your own, work as a mercenary. recruit a giant army or just settle with a small group full of other heroes. You dive in this world and explore, conquer or work as a grunt as much as you like. The main quest is also pretty long and so is the class quest as I derailed constantly and have yet to finish them.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is terrible and the dialog is INCREDIBLY annoying, you are playing this to try out "builds" and engage in fantasy warfare.It's real-time but you can slow it down to 50% speed which is pretty slow (hit CTRL to speed it up) and hit any menu button to pause. That's true in combat and in the world map.But I put over 300 hours into it, messing around with different ideas, different team comp, etc.People will tell you to start with Spiritmancer, which is fine. Berserker is easier and IMO is quite fun because you can benefit from all different kinds of weapons, armor, and trinkets.Wizards can't.On the other hand, Berserker only uses ONE active skill (basically) so you might find that boring if you want something more dynamic.The devs are constantly updating the game, which is great.I don't think any of the updates are related to player input (other than bug fixes which we report) and they don't test or localize well, if at all. So after an update you'll see parts of the game in a foreign language until they get around to fixing that. And lots of typos and so forth.BUTThe base game was pretty well polished, this is just things from the last few months.There's no tutorial and explanations for most of the game's functionality and features, that's not good because there are many things in the game that are not intuitive or outright do not make sense.But as you can see, I have over 300 hours in the game, so none of that bothered me. This scratched my itch..YOU MUST USE THE WORKSHOP in my opinion.You can play the first game without mods just to figure out how it works but I don't think this game is fun without mods.

_childDocuments_.review: --DO NOT BUY UNTIL THEY PATCH LATE GAME BOSSES--Game is fun, but some builds you do make the game unbeatable. The first class (Spiritmancer), literally has to 1v1 duel a boss monster called Raksha who kills you in 2-3 hits. Even if you equip heavy armor to be tankier at the cost of a less efficient caster, you still get murdered.She also has a dash, a stun, and a ground burning effect that will STILL KILL YOU WHEN YOU PAUSE INTO YOUR INVENTORY TO HEAL YOURSELF (this last one might be a bug). She also summons a fire golem go some ungodly reason, just to help block some of the ranged shots on her or aggro any shadow summons I can muster. One of her sword swings does 3,500 damage. With heavy armor and bonus hp and physical damage reduction, I have 7,700 hp. If you're crit it is a one hit KO boss on you. I've had her literally teleport on me and just insta-die. No animation, no swing, just death. I've played games all my life and I've never seen such a blatant disregard for game balance before.I have an elite level army and 6 max level companions. We've had bosses in this game that my entire army has fought together, and some bosses I've had to fight with up to 3 of my companions. But this one, for some reason, is a 1v1 honor duel that makes this 20+ hour run dead in the water. I don't get more skills or skill points, and even if I did, none of them would nerf the boss. Why can't I bring a party to such a strong boss?Up until late game I did enjoy the game as a charming, small scale version of Mount and Blade but with an Arabian charm, anime aesthetics, and the ability to have animals and monsters in your army high-fantasy style.But the end game balance is SO INSANELY OFF that you just can't waste this many hours of your life just to hit a wall you cannot possibly overcome just because the devs are bad at their job.Add to wishlist. DO NOT BUY IN CURRENT STATE.

_childDocuments_.review: The world building, art, and concept make the game intriguing. The mechanics and story fail it.It has a fun concept and compelling world that will sink its hooks into you, causing you to wish for what it could be, and tricking you into ignoring what it is.Mechanically there is no real challenge you will win most fights without interaction, letting your minions bring victory as you stare out the window. In the few combats you must be involved in it is just a quick sequence of button mashing or kiting. Then there will be a small handful of battles that you practically have no chance, but do not worry there is almost no cost or gravity to any loss.Story wise, the game is very trite and inelegant. In the main story and character story of my primary play through my character was non-nonchalantly declared subdued (in several ways, over eight times) as if it was a mere rag-doll. Further the story seems to center around an NPC and you are treated like a cherished stuffed animal that gives them comfort, an undistinguished mascot, as it were.I feel the game hooks people between the endless paths of micro grinding improvement, giving you ceaseless line of tasks you can work toward, and a vibrant looking world. It is a lovely feeling world.Even though I completed a play through (my usual criteria to recommend a game), I will not be recommending this game. Though I will counter not recommending the game if you just want to twizzle yourself in an unchallenged game and feel all munchkinesque while you grind your character in some kind of power fantasy, than this would be a great game to express that.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Hybrid of Mount & Blade and MOBA.-Nice Concept...Cons:-...which feels like a wasted opportunity.-Combat (Design and Execution).-Bugs and glitches.-English translation is off at some points.-Questionable design choices.-Lack of polish.Summary:The game which some people want, in theory, as it combines the open-world, sandbox and action in a pretty decent way which actually makes the game even worse as it tries to play safe and sometimes, it is too safe I'd say. You don't need to reinvent the wheel to make something appealing to the crowd but here it feels like it is a wasted opportunity by sticking too close to the source material. Also, the general lack of polish or refinement - it goes from small missprints all the way up to game-breaking bugs and hard-locking yourself from the main story if you want to play the game in a way which is different to what the developers wanted. _childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about the game, but also a lot wrong with it. Maybe it should've stayed in early access for a little while longer...The world and lore seems to be well crafted, and the hand painted grafics look really nice, combat is good enough and the skill system seems to be well thought out.Sadly that's where the good things end already.The difficulty is all over the place, it's really unbalanced. The main story sends you into and through areas you're nowhere near to be ready for almost immediately, I guess you're supposed to do side-quests, but several side quests do the same. Even some enemies in the starting area and areas where most enemies are on your or even lower levels are totally overpowered.Bosses in dungeons can often kill you so quickly that you don't even get a chance to heal, while every other enemy in the same dungeon barely causes any trouble.English text is often cut when it doesn't fit the dialogue box, it doesn't continue in the next dialogue window, it's just cut, gone for good. Sometimes you can guess what the cut part probably was, but often you have no idea and miss information.Several quests have no marker. While for some quests it makes sense, I've had several cases where I had no idea where to go.Resources: Why do I have to pay a hefty sum in advance in every single village when I want to buy or sell something, this might make sense in the later stages when you actually have a settlement and trade routes etc., but it doesn't make any sense in the early game when you're basically on your own.It also doesn't help that you barely get any wood, one of the most important resources to upgrade troops in the early stages, so you need to pay a hefty sum to be able to buy wood, then get lucky that the traider even has wood, and then hope that you still have enough money.There's also barely any explanation of how the game works, for example, the first time I noticed my troops are starving it was already to late, I didn't even know such a thing exists in the game and at the time I wasn't able to get any food in time.Conclusion:This is a solid base for a good game in the future, but right now it's not. It's unbalanced and feels unfinshed and needs some (a lot) polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for 6~7$ on sale.  I recommend it at this price, but not at full price.  At full price its a hard thumbs down from me.  The world map you need to click 50-100 times to hit just the right spot for it to give you the 'travel to location' option.  There are items, skills, dialogue, and ui elements that are still in Chinese.  Max level is kind of low, talents are fairly bland and you'll max them all out pretty quickly, skills/spells range from worthless to op.  Some quests are bugged, I've got a few that despite exploring the location multiple times will not advance.  On other hand there are some quests you can start/finish by simply moving your party to a specific spot on the map, you'll end up triggering an event that shouldn't be possible yet.Turrets have like tier 7 hp with tier 6 unit damage.  I have no idea why they are so stupidly op.  By end game you'll have siege damage units and can likely handle them, but they still show up in early game base/bandit camp invades.Encounters are all over the place.  I solo'd level 16 encounter at level 1, but actually wiped on a level 5 encounter at max level lol.  No it isn't common, but the fact it exists just shows this how beta this game feels.Combat rewards are just awful.  A bandit/monster you steam roll might drop better loot than the level 20 tier 6 decked out general you just beat.  That said, I haven't found any point in fighting the enemy faction's armies.  You'll get 50-100 coins which you could just find laying on the ground, and likely you'll risk major casualties.  The enemy faction will respawn at their rally point with full army ready for another round.Enemy reinforcements are bugged too.  You might find a lone caravan of the enemy faction in the middle of no where, so you attack it, and 10 seconds into the battle instantly 100-200+ enemy reinforcements with multiple heroes show up, aka you're very dead. I would sum it up that this feels ALMOST like a great and finished game, but then you see the hallmarks of beta/early-release shining through and it just ruins the experience.  For what I paid I had a great time though.Unit combat also feels very clunky, frequently they get stuck on rocks, enemies just 100-0 you with stun lock, or you get aim botted from two screens away by op turrets+archers with homing arrows.  Spells/skills that cause confusion(enemies can't tell friends from foe) don't work properly.  If I cast such a spell/ability the enemy units will continue to target my hero until i invis.  On invis they finally start treating everyone on the field as an enemy.Lastly encounters scale with your level.  I have very mixed feelings about this.  In these types of systems there isn't really a reward for getting stronger, since enemies will be stronger too.  I would consider allowing the main character and units to surpass enemy level cap or at least not have enemy levels scale 1:1 with the player.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this after hearing it's like mount&blade + diablo. That was definitely a half truth.In short: the game has a lot of problems it needs to work out BUT I've had a ton of fun with it and will continue to do so.On the technical side I've never encountered any crashes or freezes even with mods installed but the game seems to suffer from stutters on each ingame day swap in and out of combat. Combat is isometric but it's plagued with a lot of problems. For starters animations are slow and clunky, characters are unresponsive, unit ai is braindead to the point of every single units doing a hit and run strategy regadless of what they are, sieges are extremely boring again due to the ai on both sides ,there's very little feedback on when you hit someone or get hit yourself and getting stunlocked to death or just outright getting 1 shot is common lategame. Early on these problems aren't all that visible so buyers beware if you're just doing a 2 hour trial.The mount&blade part of kingdom/army management is also kinda bare bones. Most characters can easily be converted by just showering them with gifts and they don't bring much to the table as the vast majority of them don't have any real skills to speak of. Couple that with an infuriatingly simple and tedious gear durability system and they end up being an annoyance more than anything else.There's a huge variety in the unit department, from your standard sword/spear/cav/archer to different kinds of mages. There's also a ton of animals like sneks, foxes, good boys and ox. Mystical creatures such as dragons, demons, dryads and so forth are a bit hard to get due to being mostly rng drops but they're very powerful to compensate.The main story is fun the first time you play trough it but the game is designed around multiple playtroughs. As you achieve different things in game you'll earn legacy points and those can be used to unlock different bonuses at your next character creation. This is fine however there's a lot of pointless text that really slows the pacing down on your second playtrough and onwards.The game explains almost nothing on how it works, there are a lot of secret things to find and sidequests to complete and the process of learning is quite fun.I'd recommend to everyone to get a few mods off the workshop to make the experience a bit more fun such as:Infinite durabilityPandora's boxTeach companions skillsAnd look around the other mods too, they're mostly in chinese but once you get the hand of the game you don't really need to understand the ingame writing all that much and for the mod description you can just use deepl or google translate,

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing this half because I like it and half because there are so many negative reviews of the game that are just laughably incorrect, despite having 50+ hours. I will correct some of them here:- There is a bounty system in the game, and its distinct from the Bounty Hunter class. The Bounty Hunter class is labelled as such because he specializes in assassination and because he has unique abilities that inflict the Bounty debuff.- Diplomacy works and is dependent on more than just doing quests. Anyone claiming otherwise has never clicked on the "Intel" tab in the UI to view character/faction/town disposition.- The game doesn't have much of a tutorial but I don't think it needs one. Its not as complex as similar games like Mount and Blade and even with little experience with those games I was able to pick it up pretty fast. If you're having trouble, watch a video tutorial.- There is a trading economy, and its largely impacted by disposition.Basically, ignore the negative reviews that complain about missing/broken systems. They aren't missing, people are just blind as all hell. This is easily worth $15.

_childDocuments_.review: It may seem like anime Mount and Blade in an East Asian setting. Actually it is a well-thought-out fantasy RPG with a decent story and world, lively characters, dialogue choices, diplomacy, and talent points.Well-thought-out and well-written, but not very well-executed. Every time I come across an idea in this game that would easily put Mount and Blade to shame, I find some annoying flaw that ruins it.For example, characters get stuck in geometric details on the global map and tactical map. During a tavern brawl, the southern wall of the building obscures your character and your opponent, forcing you to guess what they are doing. Once the plot becomes interesting, they begin to deliver it through text.In places, the translation is surprisingly good, in other places, the text is not translated at all. You can minimize the game to tray, but no one guarantees that you will be able to maximize the window back. While exploring a cave, you may be ambushed by the "creatures that dwell in the dark". The dark creatures turn out to be city guards. There is no autoattack. Click the enemy to death (and your mouse too). And so on.Speaking of Mount and Blade, it consists of two main parts: an adventure simulator on a global map and tactical battles. Salzaar is mostly the first and it's done well (except from getting stuck). Tactical battles here are not very tactical, they are chaotic brawls full of ability abuse. So here is Salzaar. Sometimes genius, sometimes shameful. It's grindy. It is definitely playable, but also very facepalmable. For me technical execution of a game is very important, so I can't recomend it. Otherwise, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this?  Hesitantly, yes.  Sands of Salzaar manages to scratch my ARPG within a simulation itch despite its many flaws.  The early game needs some serious work, but once the end game is reached, the combat becomes a lot more fun for me. I've also enjoyed exploring the various stories in the game.Combat is where Sands of Salzaar focuses the most.  There are a variety of characters and play styles, including ones only the AI characters can have (typically the faction leaders).  Army battles in the early and mid game are 10 second affairs which are over before they even begin, and combat only starts to get really good at end game when units actually live long enough to have real fights.  Mods can also drastically extend the lifespan of combat in the game by adding new characters with new skills to play as and by changing aspects of the game to fit personal preferences.Army management is lackluster and counter-intuitive.  You'd think a game which wants you to build an army would encourage it, but the opposite is true.  If you build a large army early in the game, you will quickly fall behind and get crushed because the exp is divided evenly between all heroes and squads.  That large army will quickly become under leveled and start suffering heavy casualties, which becomes harder and harder to keep up with as they are promoted.Army building only really starts mattering at end game to handle large sieges and faction wars.  Sadly, almost all sense of progression is gone at that point because you easily have the resources to immediately promote your recruits and fights at that point almost instantly level your soldiers to max level.  As for the story, it actually has some good stories in it following the update to the English translation.  The main story is decent enough, but the story for each character is where it really shines.  Currently there are ~9 characters, and 5 of them have their own stories in addition to ones made by the modding community.As for the simulation part of Sands of Salzaar, it is bare bones but functional.  Everything most AI's do and have is the result of a dice roll, and I've never seen any of them do anything on the map to earn what they have other than attack towns.  Will an AI hero level today?  Roll a dice.  Will they find some better equipment today?  Roll a dice.  Will they gain a promotion today? Roll a dice.  Will relations improve or worsen today? Roll a dice.  The simulation is incredibly shallow.  Often, they'll just be wandering back and forth between two towns for most of the game while somehow leveling, ranking up in their faction and gaining equipment.Sands of Salzaar is alright for the price.  It's a game with a lot of shallow features, so it's hard to really say what it is.  An action rpg real time simulator?  Sadly, it doesn't explore any of its features enough to feel like a whole game, and instead ends up being a Frankenstein's monster of various ideas.  This is exacerbated by how little documentation there is for the game (in English anyways).  If you choose to play this, be prepared to figure things out as you go and don't be afraid to click all the buttons and dialog options to see what happens (or else you'll miss on a lot of "hidden" features in the game).

_childDocuments_.review: People say it's like Mount & Blade and Kenshi mixed with Diablo, and they're not wrong.  Especially Mount & Blade: you start out on an overland map and wander around, mostly trying (much like early M&B) to not die and make any friends at all.  But eventually you have a solid army made up of whatever you like.  So, you run into armies but now instead of M&B's TPS perspective, it's a Diablo-alike, where your troops charge their troops and you help out.  It's not too much like Diablo on the APRG front; you aren't going to win the war alone.  You get allies and they fight and you all work together as a team.So do I recommend it?  YES I DO, strongly.  For some of us, "Diablo meets M&B" is a no-brainer; if you're not one of us, then maybe you won't like it?  I mean, it's possible.  But I do need to say that none of the cricitisms aimed at this game have really moved me.  Okay, there are some odd translation issues--but they are SUPER minor.  Okay, the early game feels a bit unfocused and hard--so does M&B.  Get in there, stay alive, and eventually the game opens up and you're tackling whoever you like.  I am just pleased as punch to have bought it on sale at $9 USD; I think it's worth double that, easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Picture this: You're wandering through a world that's like the lovechild of Mount and Blade Warband and an over-caffeinated fantasy novelist. Sands of Salzaar takes the best bits of Warband, cranks up the creativity dial, and just lets it rip!You want depth? This game's got more depth than a well-dressed penguin trying to flirt at a polar bear party. We're talking lore that's so intriguing, it makes you question if you're reading a game manual or a Pulitzer Prize-winning novel. Quests? Oh boy, they've got more quests than a squirrel has nuts, and each one is like a surprise treasure hunt for your inner adventurer!Items? Abilities? Characters? Sands of Salzaar serves them up like it's an all-you-can-eat fantasy buffet. It's like a medieval fantasy RPG mixed with a talent show where every contestant is trying to outdo the last one with their epic abilities.In Sands of Salzaar, you'll never run out of things to do. It's like an amusement park for your brain, and the rides are called "quests" while the cotton candy is replaced with epic loot. So, saddle up, sharpen your sword, and dive into this hilariously addictive adventure. Sands of Salzaar: it's Warband on steroids, and it's ready to rock your world!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I just haven't got to the parts that still have Chinese, or I picked a path that was more translated (there is the main story, and then a bunch of side character stories based on who you are playing).  The only Chinese I have seen in the game so far at all has been on a menu where they hadn't translated the "Okay" and "Cancel" buttons when I first started to play, but that was both incredibly easy to figure out, and it was updated to be changed last night so now that's in English.I don't know what it's like without the free updated game DLC, "Champion of Chaos."  This contained some updates to various things (though it looked mostly to gameplay) and was just released this past week, just before I started to play.  You can shut it off and not play with it active in game, but I've only played my game with the free DLC update turned on.The game was a bit more difficult to figure out than average.  What it calls a "Tutorial" is actually a game manual, not a playing tutorial.  I enjoyed getting the hang of most of it through experimentation, but that experience may not be for those who like a more gentle and thorough introduction to how everything works.Be mindful that it's a budget priced title that needs a bit of figuring out.  Some people expect this full priced experience to come with a 1/4th priced game, for some reason.  As others often mention, think of it more along the lines of figuring out that first Mount & Blade game.I'm finding it to be incredibly cool and well worth the money.  If I get near done and I hit any untranslated story, I'll come back to edit this review to say so.I just went to briefly test it in between playing numerous big budget titles, and the enjoyment of this one drew me in.There is story, and I enjoy that story, but it's more about how fun the gameplay is to me really and all the options.  There are so many ways to do things, so many skills, different units, etc.  You can play how you want.  You can kind of ignore a lot of the story and just make your own fun of taking over towns and balancing your relationships with other factions.  There also is a full on sandbox mode where that's what you totally do, but the story does help steer you a tiny bit easier into it.It's nice that the game lets you make your own avatar no matter what the story avatar you're picking is supposed to look like.  Some people may want to take that seriously, but I had some fun with that.  This does include gender as well.While I've only been experiencing a single character line story, it's been interesting.  At this point I am unsure if I'd replay it as a different character once done, maybe, since it does give incentives to do so, but I barely finish any of my games, let alone replay them.  The only reason I might is that I could pick an entirely different way to play next time, different partners, etc.I won't get too deep into describing the gameplay loop.  That's been explained by a whole lot of other reviews here already and I'm typing single handed because a cat is wrapped around my other hand, so I'm a bit ready to finish up here.  Also, being that there are different ways to play, it's a bit strange.  There is one where you play like an RTS with a hero under you control, with towers and buildings and troops etc.  There is another where you're just straight out fighting, sometimes by yourself, sometimes with another hero or three, where it plays more like a MOBA action RPG type game.  It's kind of difficult to get away from the MOBA action RPG type of play at least in the story mode, as there are numerous story quests that you are restricted to just your hero, or you and other heroes, and you can't bring troops and don't have to worry about buildings during them.  The RTS type of play can be a little more complicated, and I'm unsure if the manual is decent enough to cover all of those tactics.  There's a whole line of your hotkeys (F keys) that are devoted to that part of the game.  I haven't really got deep into that part of the game yet to see.  I may skip that entirely, too.  I may join other factions and not worry about my own.  It's cool that the option is there for those who want to go that route, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Mount and Blade. I don't love, but definitely enjoy plenty, ARPGs.The problem is that this game just isn't remotely good at either. Well, it's maybe a *passable* sandbox for 5-10 hours, before your character outgrows it and it just starts to feel like a waste of time. But as an ARPG if someone told me this was an alpha they made in a month, I'd tell them the controls still feel way too stilted, and they should try to make fewer, more in-depth classes so you can actually get some feeling of real choices and gameplay. Movement is so clunky you'll mostly stick to just pressing your 2-5 buttons at the biggest clump of enemies for 30 hours of gameplay.Combat is short, messy, and usually either obnoxiously hard or agonizingly easy. The introduction of a lot of raw level numbers into an open sandbox takes the "this basic monster is randomly 20 levels too high" problem up to 11. I can't even force myself to finish the main story because it's just be fast-forwarding back and forth across the world doing 15 second at a time zero-effort battles where I need two buttons.I tried a number of different characters and mostly they either sucked, or went wildly out of control right away. And I imagine the ones that seemed bad just take an extra hour to go wildly over the top. The max difficulty does nothing to help.Basic combat just isn't fun. It's a very clunky and stilted ARPG with an absolutely tiny variety of options in the moment. The army-building side has potential, but really "just get as many heroes as you can and throw them at the enemy" will beat almost everything you run into. Keeping up with gear durability is a drag, food spends 90% of the time being irrelevant and 10% of the time being annoying, partial squads and combining is just obnoxious.And all the mods are in Chinese so unlike some other games there's no chance in hell of me finding a fan rebalance mod that makes there actually be a video game with compelling combat.Basically, imagine an ARPG you enjoyed. Remember what it was like to fight mobs at level 5? You probably had a couple of abilities with simple interactions, but it probably wouldn't be fun if you had to keep going with no interesting gear drops or anything new, and also wonky pathfinding, right? That's all of the combat in this game forever.The open world sandbox will challenge you for a moment, but once you accrue a bit of power the challenge is gone. Most quests are very simple "go talk to person" or "go clear out location" or maybe the weirdly common "bring me X of X flower" (fortunately I already obsessively stockpile flowers).Those hours I have on this game are partially spent AFK or such, but in large part spent restarting as different characters on max difficulty hoping to just find myself having an interesting challenge. In the game, turning up difficulty beyond just picking the hardest initial option apparently requires you to beat the game repeatedly before you can go further, which I have no interest in doing. Imagine a 15+ hour action game that forced everyone to beat "Very Easy" and then "Easy" and then "Normal" before it would let them actually experience a moment of resistance, not to mention knowing the game inside out by the time it would've had a chance to challenge them and likely cheesing it to death.There's real moments of brightness in there - getting your first couple of heroes and trying to customize them a bit to click together, going after your first bandit camp or two and trying to decide how much to put your soldiers to use (although the actual only threat in any camp is just wildly high HP and high damage towers that you'll spend half the battle mindlessly bashing as it kills people)...Everywhere I look the game is overflowing with charm and potential, and every attempt to look deeper sees a clunky mess that I don't think I should have any reason to expect further development to rectify. I still like the idea of the game. I'd *love* to pit my army against worthy adversaries, using my own character's skills to try to turn the tide. I'd love to roam the world, finding locations, making allies, accruing power, etc - if only I didn't reach max level in a blink and just be stuck in a world where the only chance at resistance would just be bashing my head against a hyper-fortified faction capital or something (faction leaders are chumps who could kill maybe like two individual soldiers before I mass magic aoe their entire army to death).Argh. It's hard to even stop writing a review like this, because every part of the game I think of reminds me of one thing I really like and three things that frustrated me.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what the tag on Steam says, this doesn't have co-op campaign. Not yet anyway.So here goes: this game is an odd mix of Mount & Blade, Diablo-like, Chinese/Korean MMOs, and also bits of roguelite/New Game+ element. I'll discuss the pros and cons in a bit, but I'd like to talk about gameplay briefly.Game has a campaign and a sandbox mode. In the character creation, you can pick 1 from 8 predefined classes or craft your own class. Classes affect both combat and diplomacy. Each classes have skill trees unique to their own and a more general "Talent points" on the non-combat side of things (movement, army building, survivability, diplomacy, etc).You traverse through a map just like you do in Diablo-like games, but with troops and companions in your party like in M&B. The map is separated to 6 areas, each initially controlled by major factions. Just like M&B, each areas have settlements (towns, villages, camps) which each factions vye to control. Settlements are upgradeable and the sultan (governor) assigned to that settlement can decide its development and economy.The settlements are a bit mix of M&B and Diablo-like games: important NPCS (merchants, bartenders, rulers, etc) usually can be found only in the central building. But you can also meet some random NPCs, quest-givers, and some important ones around the settlements. Those NPCs also travel around the map, most of which you can engage in battle. Like M&B, in battle you're transported to a different battle map.Here comes the Chinese/Korean MMO part. Some people describe the combat as ARPG-like/Diablo-like, but honestly it's closer to those MMOs: you click on an enemy and the character will attack them until they die. You can also use skills and it's the same. Imagine Ragnarok Online or Fantasy Westward Journey. Distance matters as well.Like Diablo-like games, grinding is a major part of the gameplay. You can find many "dungeons" with several floors scattered around the map for this purpose. They reward you with EXP, equips/items, and resources for army/settlement building. Some of those dungeons are explorable, but mostly they are just screens of dialogue where you will be taken to the battle map when you encounter enemies. Some dungeons are lore dungeons or sawmills/mines that you can dig for resources.Equips/loots have prefixes and randomly generated, so their attributes can be very different. Ordinary troops (spearmen, archers, etc) can't have custom equips, but you can assign equips to your companions. Equips play major role in combat - so make sure you always grind those stuff or you won't be able to progress further.Last, the roguelite/New Game+ element is the Legacy points. In character creation you're bequeathed Legacy points which you can use for additional skills, items, etc. Those points are the collected from your previous campaigns: story progress, sidequests, and other stuff you do such as conquering settlements, brawling, etc.This game is "the world moves with or without you" type of game and I love it. I'll put it alongside M&B, Drox Operative, Rebel Galaxy, etc. Raiding caravans affect settlements' economy. Factions wage war. Territories change. Individual lords can be friends/enemies with each other. In terms of combat, I enjoy brawling in taverns/tournaments much more than the day-to-day combat. Brawling has a separate skill tree which points you can only acquire by winning brawls or buying scripts from other brawlers. You can't spam those skills to win as you need the right combo to pin the mdown. This, combined with the small arena where tactics became important, feels really rewarding and is a major improvement to M&b boring, mostly "just for the sake of it" tournament.The story is pretty standard, but I appreciate the time put to write down the lore. Lore bits are scattered through the game world and if you're interested you can dig into them. I also really like that there is a Campaign option in this type of game, that gives me some sense of purpose. Each character classes also have their own quests, which is nice.Although it's a bit too trope-y (silent killer ninja, luscious minstrel, loli witch that's actually hundreds years old, etc), I also like the personalized, unique named characters in this game. I also appreciate the fact that there's a console command so if you just want to mess around with your game, you can do that. The modding scene also seems to be huge, however at the moment most mods are still written in Chinese. Hopefully there will be localization as the game gets more updates and more players.Unfortunately, the game seems to copy M&B down to its kinks. There are issues that really bug me such as:Day-to-day combat can be very hectic due to the visuals, and there's no option to auto-target. As such if you're a ranged combatant, you're in disadvantage as you can wrongly click the ground and move into your death instead of attacking enemies.AI pathing during combat could use more wrok as well, as troops sometimes get stuck on rocks or buildings, and sometimes the bosses do that also so you can just cheese them.NPC dialogues is kinda repetitive and template-y, despite the fact that most named characters have unique personalities. It's really jarring to see a silent killer ninja who in one dialogue would elaborate carefully how to effectively eliminate enemies and in another dialogue would say "Friends know no secrets!" with an upbeat tone.Last, English translation is mostly fine. But some can be confusing. Like the dialogue option to dismiss your vassal when they're in your party. It says "Get out of here and don't come back!" I thought that option is to kick them permanently. Pronouns also need more work; for example, regardless of the NPCs gender, NPCs will refer each other as "he" and "him". Really odd to listen to someone talking about your waifu and they refer her as "him".Despite these several cons, I still recommend this game. Sands of Salzaar being M&B-like is 80% reason I recommend this game. I usually finish a game first before writing reviews, but this game is an exception.

_childDocuments_.review: Gradually going through my Steam games and leaving reviews (if I feel like it. This one, I did).I wanted to sink my teeth into this game. But for me, the controls and lack of gamepad support really did a number on my enjoyment. The English translation at the time appeared to be a work in progress for story, UI, and side quests. And if you misplay your run while progressing, you may end up with content that is very difficult or too difficult to overcome - and better off starting over. The action combat, to me, really could have benefited from having move controls separate from your attack. (whether that's WASD / IJKL / arrow keys). And with so much of the combat, I can only hope that I overwhelm the enemy rather than finely outmaneuver them. And also at the time, there didn't appear to be a pause feature in combat to carefully reassign what my units were doing. Trying to emulate the mouse ultimately made this a cumbersome experience for me and I wanted to make this work, but gave up after a couple dozen hours.I realize this is unfair to the game to review it without seeing if the patches addressed these things. Gamepad, the ability to effectively emulate the gamepad, or if it can't be emulated - non-timed input is critical for my enjoyment of a game. An admittedly, wouldn't have bough the game if I didn't see the controller / gamepad support on their roadmap originally.I also realize this review is half-baked, but that's kind of what this game made me feel when I played it back way when.

name: Smelter
detailed_description: Smelter is a strategy, action-platformer combo inspired by classics from the 16-bit era. Lead Smelter and Eve, along with the faithful Zirm forces by expanding Smelter’s territory across the Rumbly Lands in top-down strategy levels included in the Classic Mode , or dive into thrilling side-scrolling platforming mayhem with Action Mode , leaving Smelter’s forces to annex key locations themselves. Build, attack and advance your army -- unlock, upgrade and unleash elemental action skills against vicious enemies, perilous environments and take on dangerous bosses with Boss Rush Mode . Release the power of Smelter ! STORY After the untimely destruction of the Garden, Eve finds herself in an unfamiliar world with her beloved Adam nowhere to be found. In her search for Adam, she encounters Smelter, an unusually over-confident, winged creature with the powerful ability to transform and fuse with others, giving them incredible powers. Offering his apparently “invaluable” assistance, Smelter transforms and fuses with Eve. They depart on a journey to the treacherous Rumbly Lands. There, they expand Smelter’s territory, allowing them to reach further into the various domains to find out what happened to her Adam, hoping to find him in one piece and find a way back home to their peaceful lives... FEATURES Classic Mode : Hybrid gameplay that combines fast-paced platforming with top-down strategy. Expand your empire across a variety of regions, utilizing a variety of building types, upgrades, and units. Meet a cast of characters with personalities ranging from the eccentric to the completely insane. Uncover a multitude of secrets, including powerful hidden upgrades and hard-as-nails trial levels. Action Mode : Take on challenging 2D action levels, enemies, and bosses with their own back stories, while leaving minions to deal with the strategy and base building. Explore incredible, diverse worlds ranging from the hellish to the beautiful. Master three skill sets, complete with over 40 upgrades obtainable through multiple challenges, allowing for varied combat, movement and defense tactics. Fire up the “Smelt” ability, which can be used both in combat and on objects to navigate through difficult terrain. Boss Rush Mode : Battle against the many wild and outlandish bosses in an array of ever increasing challenges and claim your spot as the champion. Rock out to a killer soundtrack combining synth and guitar, featuring music by Evader, and opening and ending theme by Manami Matsumae (Mega Man, Shovel Knight).

short_description: You are Eve, fresh out of Eden and armed with a living suit of armor, Smelter. Explore a dangerous new world, battle its bizarre denizens and expand your empire in a desperate journey to find Adam.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing about Smelter is that it's a really good platformer, but there is a lot of story and tutorial shoved into the experience to support the strategy features, especially the first 2 hours or so it tends to interrupt gameplay a lot - not as much later on. The campaign can take anywhere from 10 to 15 hours to finish, so keep in mind that it takes a few hours to get going. I understand that it's not ideal, and no game should be boring for that long, but it's where we at, and I think the devs are very much aware of it. I didn't like the game at first, I thought the 'RTS' was too much of a chore, that said, the platforming gameplay is very enjoyable once you can switch between 3 different armors. I am not against the narrative in my platformers, but it feels like you get bombarded with text walls, and if I being completely honest, the narrative had very little impact on me, even though I like the design of the characters. The game does not take itself seriously, instead going for a silly take on the world, but on a personal level, I found it a bit uninspired.I would say that Smelter is an overall tribute to retro platformers, not just ActRaiser because it has a similar genre, but also games like Megaman and Castlevania. To give the devs some credit, outside of the Nutoro armor, I don't think the movement and abilities are all that similar. It's a hybrid game, the way it works both games are engaged in a symbiotic relationship. You can collect resources during the stages for builds on the overworld, and by exploring the map, you will unlock power-ups for the platformer. For the most part, I think the system makes sense, if there is one thing the game does well, it's the power-up variety. You can switch between 3 different armors that have individual skill trees, and the cool part is that each armor has a unique way of mobility. The game is not a metroidvania, but when you explore the map you are being funneled by the abilities, so in order to access a new zone you will need a specific power.Personally, I did not have any issues with the controls, and I don't mean the buttons, I am talking about actual platforming and the movement mechanics. I noticed some criticism in regards to those features, and  I can't say that I agree, I think you did a great job with the momentum. I can't say that I ever struggled with how the character behaved.(+)  - not including some of the cave stages (the tutorial and the last one), I think the levels were very fun, both visually and from a gameplay perspective, continuously adding new features and utilizing verticality. Every stage also has some hidden areas in a form of challenges and special resources. I would say the difficulty is very fair, and it gradually gets more challenging toward the end of each zone.(+)  - each armor has a unique set of skills and it's not just some passive trash, they all have some mobility tools and other niche qualities, and depending on what you doing, they excel at doing different things. Some of the bosses are designed in a way where it's beneficial to switch between them. Overall I think the platforming gameplay is executed very well.(+)  - you can debate if it's good content, but I still appreciate just having it. Many stages, lots of challenges, bosses with multiple layers, some hidden trinkets, and lots of achievements. Even if the strategy was not a part of the experience, it's still longer than many regular platformers.(+)  - I see all the hard work with the animation. Overall, I feel the game has some issues with the direction in general, but if we talking just purely aesthetic, Sina did a fantastic job. I like the visuals, it's just that the world did not capture me.(x)  - the way the story in this game works is always a pop-up, you stop what you doing and read the text. Like I enjoyed the cutscenes, that is visual storytelling, use that. Have a conversation between characters without locking the player, have some optional lore, just not text walls everywhere. I hate complaining about pacing in games because I sound like I take it a little too seriously, but it's important, I don't want those moments that put me to sleep. You have a wonderful platformer here, but you drag it down so much, it's so slow for the first few hours. The first feedback I ever gave in the beta was - "will there be an arcade" mode, and I was not the only person. Many of us saw those MegaMan references, and I think many of us bought the game because of them.(x)  - I think what makes a good strategy is an AI that plays a tug of war with you. There is no sense of AI taking over or pushing you back, you just kind of build toward the desired location, and kill a few enemies on the way, kinda hard to lose. Maybe if the AI could build his own buildings and upgrades to fortify positions, maybe if I actually had to think for a moment it would be more fun. I realize that it would delay platforming even longer, but if you going to make me watch the map for hours, might as well make it challenging. I still like what you did with unlocks, just not the actual gameplay getting there.I recognize that devs put so much work into game, I just don't think it was necessary. Honestly, I would enjoy the game more if it had the generic stage select with the boss icons. One of the best platformers I ever played, but then you add other features that are not as enjoyable, and ultimately I think it did more bad than good. I got very bored, then I was very engaged, and then I got bored again, and then it was fun again...

_childDocuments_.review: While there's alot to like like the Platforming and Nostalgia from games like Actraiser and Megaman X but there's just something fundamentally wrong with how the game itself plays and feels.The controls are clunky, even on a controller where levels are designed where it feels like it was "yup I did it once it's fine it doesn't need tuning"Switching between elements is slow and cumbersome, almost to the point where you are better off to stick to only one and ignore the others during any gameplay, thankfully so far I have no seen any required swaps to perform any platforming but if it were to be required it would be extremely difficult with how slow the switching occurs.The hit boxes are inconsistent both on the platforming and hit detection with certain enemies, falling through the edge of a platform is insanely frustrating, player expectation is if I can touch it I shouldn't pass through it or be pushed to the side of it by awkward collision but nonetheless that's where we are here.With enemies, specially the lightning ones you'll get hit by a dash attack at both the start location and the end location and everything inbetween making it hard/impossible to judge how to dodge certain enemies.Which leads to the ultimate frustration: The Trials.These are not fun, but are required for upgrades. Many of them have the condition "don't get hit" but are covered in INCONSISTENT patterns of timings which lead to failure after failure until you get lucky on a pattern. It's not uncommon to have some setups (Specifically in Trial 2 of the 3rd Lightning Dungeon) where you get corned by off-screen attacks and have no where to move, or a projectile that passes through walls was fired by an enemy off-screen.While I thought this looked appealing the amount of enjoyment I was getting has quickly been soured by the negative experiences and I sadly cannot recommend this to anyone in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Smelter alternates between being a joy and a nightmare to play. The music, most of the graphics, most of the physics, the power unlocking, and especially the strategy/sim mode, are extremely well done.The writing is very humorous, and although I found it all appropriate and well timed, other people will get annoyed by the tone. I thought that part was good.But it has a lot of rough edges and plays like an unfinished and unpolished beta. The controls for dashing and dash jumping are just Not Well Done, half the time it doesn't work. Some of the trials are pointlessly brutal, and run into problems with the physics.  I managed to complete all but one trial I ran into before I stopped playing.It has a lot of softlocks, entirely too many for a game outside of early access. People keep running into cutscenes that don't work correctly, and they have to go back to the main map.There are a bunch of shmup sections. And they're not really much fun or well done. They work, but they're not fun. They seem like an afterthought. The action platforming and the strategy sim are fine, but the shmup sections are incredibly weak.There are unmarked hidden unlockables. Although they eventually tell you which 6 stages have them, they never indicate which ones you already found them in. You'd have to write that down, which is bad.There are boss fights where the room scrolls, and the boss attack broadcasts can be offscreen, at which point you're just relying on luck for not being hit.Only get this game after a few more patches, if they fix some of the glaring issues.If you're looking for an action platforming game with strategy sim elements, go back and play Actraiser. Smelter just isn't up to code yet.
