_childDocuments_.review: For those who grew up playing Super Nintendo games, certain elements about Smelter (SM) might seem familiar. That's because it takes inspiration from the ActRaiser games, which combined an overhead civilization builder with an action platformer. In spite of growing up with that console, I never played the ActRaiser games, but am aware of how popular and beloved they are, and was interested in giving this title a try. There are two main components to the gameplay. The first deals with the world on a larger scale, as you take an overhead view of the terrain. With the objective of reclaiming the land, it plays like a mix between a twin stick shooter and a strategy game. You'll build four types of properties on any given tile: houses to increase your army, trees to feed your people, barracks to house soldiers, and towers for archers. Principally, you'll build houses and trees far away from the front lines so you have ample resources to maintain a strong army, which will be built closest to the enemy forces. As you start exploring there will be barriers preventing you from going too far because you have to clear an obstacle and gain more strength first. Usually this requires you to protect a few points on the map as you fight off approaching enemies. Afterwards, you'll be able to enter a platforming stage, which opens up the next section in the overworld area, and so on. It's not a very complicated system, but the learning curve is a bit skewed as you switch back and forth between gameplay types before learning all of the game mechanics for either. Switching to the second emphasis of the game is the platforming areas. Even though the background will change in the overhead areas, the gameplay is pretty flat as it won't change very much throughout the game. There's a lot more flexibility in the stage layout and design in the platforming portions though. For instance, early stages will end without any boss battles, but as you get into later sections in the overhead parts, you'll start fighting bosses consistently. Some stages also become more maze-like or incorporate enemy gauntlets to survive through. Regardless, each stage will have three types of collectibles: apple cores, moxie deposits, and trials with relics to earn. At first I didn't know what the point of beating trials or collecting apple cores was, but these allow you to unlock power-ups. Each trial you overcome will unlock one feature of one of the types of armor, which helps out with the platforming sections. This leads to a catch 22 though, because if you don't have the skill to clear the trials, which tend to be the hardest portions of the game, you don't receive the abilities that'll help beat the stages themselves. I don't know how much play-testing was done, but if I didn't have some of those powers, such as the double jump, I'm not sure I could even beat the game.  One aspect that can be confusing with the controls is the three variants of armor available as you progress in the game. Even though your main move set won't change wildly, there's still enough of a difference that it can throw you off. For instance, your control scheme won't change, but one attack will be a short-range combo while another fires projectiles. The one that messed me up most was being able to double jump with one type, while none of the others have that effect. It takes time to adjust and you may still mix them up now and again, but these options are more of a boon than a hindrance. Aside from this matter, I played with my controller and found the controls worked well in both gameplay areas.  Even though the game's focus seems to be on Adam and Eve getting split up, with you playing as Eve, she's a mute character who barely reacts to anything that happens, let alone expresses any will for herself. Instead, the character that takes much more of the spotlight is the armor that attaches itself to her, as Smelter is quite talkative, wants to restore his army to its former strength, and knows many of the other characters you interact with. With all of the implied history he has with others, it kind of feels like I'm playing a sequel and missed out on prior events. The worldbuilding also feels slapdash because many areas are made up of old ruins and temples, but there's also a few composed of incredibly advanced machinery.  Despite never playing ActRaiser, I was still happy about how the game looks because it reminds me of SNES era games. It has a style that would have been right at home for that time, but looks very clean and polished. Enemies have interesting designs, such that they don't look like unoriginal copies. The backgrounds make use of layering to create an illusion of depth and build up a sense of actual places that harmonize with the foreground. I think most would be pleased with how the game looks.  I couldn't find a soundtrack for the game, but I believe each stage has its own song. There was a decent variety in tempo and composition, and the ones that had faster tempos tended to hold my interest more because they built up more action and energy for the gameplay. Regarding the audio balancing, some of the sound effects could be a touch loud, but it was otherwise alright. None of the sound effects I heard were disruptive or ill-fitting for the game.  🌟 I was initially confused by the design of the bosses because I'd played so much of the game without fighting any. However, they're pretty fun challenges as you figure out the right way to counter them. 🌟 Early on, I think the gameplay styles switched back and forth a bit too quickly. However, the pacing later on was much more satisfying.  ❌ The story was interesting enough, yet it could have used more focus and not used so much innuendo about important events that happened years ago off-screen. ❌ Giving more prominence to what are normally optional, worthless collectibles isn't a bad idea, but I'm not sure if it makes the game unbeatable or not. ❌ Some of the gaps in-between checkpoints were on the long, overly hard side. 🔍 Overworld combat won't initiate until you speak to the NPC with a question mark over their head. Use this prep time to place down roads and all the buildings you'd want. 🔍 You have to manually save, as there's no auto-save. Additionally, you can't save progress partway through a stage. 🔍 You don't have to clear a trial when you find it in the stage. It can be done afterwards from the trial select screen.  Although SM was made with a classic game in mind, it still made mistakes with its design. Some of the trials and obstacles are obnoxious, the world-building is muddled, and it'll be too hard for some people to beat. However, I still enjoyed myself once the game started getting some momentum. The distinct armor styles remind me of different platforming games I've enjoyed, and even though one boss kept beating the Hell out of me, when I was able to vanquish it, I actually completed a no damage run. I recommend SM for those who like a platformer with some old school difficulty to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was debating on whether or not I wanted to write a review for this game. Although I had  frustrations playing through the trials portion of the game (completely optional, but rewarding if you do them all!), I had no qualms about anything else. I had the pleasure of having Insops4 coming towards the end of my 100% playthrough to say "Thank you for playing Smelter!" which drove me to go ahead and write my review. Devs, If you're reading this, you know what I want !!!I had an issue with the wall jumping at first, wondering why it only went straight up, but after playing through for a bit I realize that mechanic was intentional.Now on to the actual review!Check my reviews, I eat graphics like this up. Referencing my tagline, the graphics had satisfied everything I loved about the SNES and GBA era of video games. I'm not a fan of Kill La Kill, which is obvious that they took inspiration for designs from, but they made it work.The character design was A+, it wasn't too extra and it wasn't too barebones. Adam and Eve's depictions were great along with the extra characters that were met along the story. To add to my Mega Man X fanaticism, particularly X3, If you have a game that looks as beautiful as it does with the direction it was trying to go to, you have to have the right type of tracks for it too. A graphic style like this  a  style of music, and they nailed it. Not once did I enter an area or level and think to myself, "I don't really like how this sounds." The nostalgia levels were skyrocketing, and I'm not just writing it based on nostalgia - the tracks are bangers.Unfortunately, I cannot give the game a 10 for its story. Although the gameplay, music, and core mechanics were phenomenal and a 10/10 for me, the story falls sort of short of that. Without providing spoilers, I'll do my best to explain why I chose a 7 and not higher or lower.When you are introduced to new characters (outside of Smelter and Eve), they are introduced with a certain significance that... well it doesn't really go much further than that. They aren't seen all that often except for the key moments that Smelter and Eve require their assistance (if at all) and kind of vanish into thin air after that.Now if you put it in perspective and treat each character separate and unique to each region, it makes perfect sense; outside of the region that you meet the new characters they are almost non-existent.Also reiterating my previous statement that the game provides a sort of "open world" playstyle, it would make sense to make the story the way it is. I don't know, it just felt all over the place. It's not that it was terrible it just wasn't.... great.I understand it's a (mostly) a platformer, story and lore aren't really the key points of games like these - and that's why I give this factor a 7 out of 10; only because I understand why it had to be the way it was, but not without changing the fact that it still falls short here.I really hope there's a sequel though!!The overall experience is a 9/10 for me (9.25 if you wanna get mathematical), the 1 missing is where the story falls short.I recommend anyone who's a fan of platforming, speedrunning,  Mega Man X to PICK THIS GAME UP IMMEDIATELY.I was watching this game like a hawk the second I saw the trailer for it. It was a day 1 buy, and a great buy.$19.99 is the perfect pricetag for this. Good job devs!

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, I want to like this game so much.  There is so freaking much greatness I want to hug whoever did the writing, graphics, overall design, and sound.On the other hand, I wanna PUNCH whoever signed off on the finished product.  This is not okay!  This game is not finished and it plays like you had zero QA.  Whoever you are, you ruined a potentially awesome game and you should feel bad.  The good points:The graphics - retro, cutesy, and perfect really.  I love them so much I'm almost willing to forgive the pile of other things that piss me off.The dialog - edgy and cocky.  It gets the job done.  Might annoy some but I really like it.The sound - satisfying sound effects.  All fit together and well represent the actions they're tied to.The music - catchy, appropriate, and upbeat. Good times.  Not particularly memorable but loads of fun to listen to.  Some really epic tracks, especially early on.  Pause is how I most enjoyed this game.The upgrades - I enjoy the linking of new moves to over world progress and vice versa. All the sweet moves gives your character incredible versatility and there are so many of them, I am even more remiss to dislike this game overall as a result.The elements -  I love that each one has a completely different move set and feels unique but distinctly effective.  I like that some enemies are weak to certain elements, and not just because of the element itself.  Some moves are just better against some enemies.  The concepts - This was one of my favorite parts!  I love act raiser and this feels like a great homage.The story - what I could get was okay, but the game was otherwise too frustrating to find out where they decided to take the story. ::shrug::The not so good:The controls - see above for who I'd like to punch.  You know who you are.  This game plays like a child designed it.  Everything else about the game ranges from okay to AWESOME.  But these controls.  Damn... It's like finding out your otherwise awesome date is a die-hard trumper.  Feels like love till she starts spewing toxicity.  In this game's case, the controls are the toxicity.  You think you can deal but it digs at you.  Even if it's not specifically the point of frustration at any given time, you know it's there in the back of your head. Any semblance of fun is ruined by knowing the game is totally going to make you do things the controls are not designed for.The enemies - They are frustrating to fight unless you can kill them before they have a chance to act which is, dare I say, somewhat rewarding. But because of the controls (see above), there is no way to consistently dispatch them before they have time to piss you off.  The game loves to inflict difficulty and annoyance by strategically placing them just out of your reach as well.  It also enjoys sticking them in a corner where Eve gets stuck on a wall allowing the enemy there to wail on her.  It makes pushover enemies feel completely unfair somehow.  There are so many BS moments I can't even. Even if you somehow managed to address and individually remove the poorly placed enemies, it would still feel like garbage overall.The elements (again) - I think the IDEA is awesome but it was executed poorly.  I don't really know how to fix it. Sorry.  I think it belongs, but the way it is done is just... bad.  I'm not a game designer.  Squandered potential here really.  The designers managed to take something great and make it annoying and I don't even know how they did it.The straight up bad:The controls (again) - different reasons though.  Momentum is all wrong.  The dash mechanics are horrible.  The gravity and acceleration is wrong.  Wall climbing specifically is extra horrible.  Attacking freezes your character in place for the entirety of the animation, but not always, and not always to the same degree. The inconsistency is  unforgivable.  It must have been horrible to write the physics code to feel so obtuse.  It feels floaty but also rigid, the worst parts of both.  It is not perspective or opinion. It is objectively bad.  The challenge trials - oh my... you know, if you took all these out of the game and just left hidden collectables, this game would have been so much better.  Probably not good, but... just so much better.  These are a huge, embarrassing mistake and not one is fun.  They are all crap and some are controller-destroyingly bad.  (The don't get hit electrical element one is truly awful)The cheap deaths - why does this game want to punish me?  It's not challenging.  It's player abuse.The combat - It's like the enemies mentioned above, but in addition to the enemies, Eve also personally wants to die.  There is no way this game plays like they intended.That about sums it up.  One of the most annoying games I've ever played because a part of me is in love with parts of it.  There is so much right here, and not much wrong.  Boy is the wrong wrong though.Update:  I kept playing this game despite how abusive and unfair it is.  I hate this game now.  All of the awful parts just kept getting worse but none of the novelty remained.  I think I can say safely, screw the developers of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Some bozo claimed that if you like Megaman X and get Smelter you'd be disappointed. I wanna lay that BS to rest. I played all Megaman X and Megaman titles, and I can tell you: If you loved Megaman X and Actraiser, you're gonna fall in love. I'd also like to point out, that the genius that claimed this BS played for a grand total of 0.4 hrs... Right now there might be a few bugs, but the studio is really quick about fixing anything that shows its head and it's their first title, so... well, what can I say? I witnessed huge AAA studios not fixing gamebreaking bugs for months and for some reason, that's cool. Here it's always fixed less than 24hrs and it's a huge deal apparently. Yes, bugs can be annoying, but none of them get left in or are so numerous/severe that it really influenced my experience. The game itself is Actraiser1/Megaman X for all those that need to slam a label on it to know if they want it. The rest, well, look at the videos and decide for yourself.I am in love and I don't regret my decision and even bought it twice, once for Switch and once on Steam. There's also the criticism that the game feels "clunky" by somebody who didn't even play for two hours... Seriously?Yes, the beginning IS clunky because you literally have zero movement powers and the first "element" you uncover is quite literally STONE. What exactly do you expect? Seriously... Later you discover a ton more skills which allow you to do a huge number of things and that make the game much more fluent. All in all, the game is a loveletter to many retro hits and really mixes them well without just kitbashing them. It adds a lot of it's own, puts a twist on things and stands on it's own two feet. It is clear to what games inspired the devs to make Smelter, but that's it. They are inspiration and not blatant "what can I take and dress up and sell as our own?". Very much like Axiom Verge, where it's clear which games inspired the dev, you wouldn't go and say "huh, metroid, eh? What a lazy rehash!".Same here. Yes, ofc, I'd say it's very much like Actraiser 1/Megaman X, because it's easier as a description and more helpful than pointing out the differences. So if you are into Platformers/Retrogames/Metroidvanias this game has it. And even a few very funny segments where the game pulls your leg and throws you into a short bullethell segment. Sounds weird, but again, they mixed it well and it just works. So please, try for yourself and don't get dissuaded by less than 2 hrs reviews claiming that the game is or is not something. I can promise you, you'd probably be missing out.
_childDocuments_.name: Smelter

_childDocuments_.review: Good and bad.The gameplay is very similar to Megaman X both visually and in some of the mechanics, not to mention the general level exploration. I like this about the game and it's what kept me playing for the roughly two and a half hours that I did. Unfortunately, the game has a ton of very specific mechanics that all claim to interact with each other, and in the time I spent playing, about 2 hours of it was mind numbing amounts of tutorials and game entry backstory. The controls are also very oddly formatted, and I had trouble re-mapping them to a position that I could handle. Because of this, I'd say the game is not very accessible to newcomers or casual gamers of an average to low skill set. Ironic, considering how in two and a half hours of gameplay, I didn't even officially escape all of the tutorials.The gameplay is further bogged down by that kind of self-awareness that comes when you don't necessarily believe you're making a good game, so you point out all the flaws and plot holes in a sarcastic manner. It's difficult to deal with a narrator/companion that's so very full of themselves while at the same time crapping on the game they're in. Please dev, I just want to enjoy your game, please let me enjoy your game without being told what to do and how to do it every 5 seconds by a companion that I want to like, but feels like if Bowser and Deadpool had a baby without genuine self confidence.

_childDocuments_.review: After our Adam absolutely had to bite into that stupid apple, we, Eve, are teleported from paradise directly into a dark cave. All alone, dressed only in a tiny bikini, we jump over poisonous acid puddles to escape as quickly as possible from the cave. In the process, we meet a supposed angel, whom we help out of his miserable situation and who, in return, wraps himself around our bodies as our armor... thus giving us new abilities. The fact that we look like Megaman in green in the armor is of course purely coincidental. Our new friend is called Smelter, and he was apparently the ruler of a small kingdom, which, however, was completely destroyed during his absence in the cave. Back in the fresh air, the real game begins. On the one hand, as Smelter we expand our empire in a simple real-time strategy game, on the other hand, as Eva with Smelter as armor, we traverse countless platform sections in Megaman style to find our Adam again.This mixture of real-time strategy and platformer works excellently, I haven't seen a similarly successful RTS/platform hybrid since ActRaiser (1990, SNES). In the platforming sequences we collect resources for buildings on the overworld, and as we expand our territory in the strategy sections we also learn new abilities that make Eva more and more powerful. Over 40 such power-ups can be learned in the course of the game, which then also allow different solutions at certain points.  Eva also gets some upgrades in the platform passages through difficult trials, others are rather easier to find. Eva can switch between three different armors after a while, which allows for completely different play styles. However, it takes a bit to get that far - at first we have to make do with a few basic skills, which makes the first hours of the game a bit tougher. The regular humorous conversations to advance the story (and as a tutorial) are certainly not everyone's cup of tea, but I find it good to get a little distraction. Each level includes hidden areas, and the difficulty gradually gets more challenging towards the end of each zone. The real-time strategy part, on the other hand, is designed to be easier, and here you have to work hard to lose. Overall, Smelter offers quite a lot of content - many levels, many challenges, elaborate boss fights, excellent pixel art graphics, animated cutscenes and a great soundtrack. Fans of challenging 2D platformers who don't mind a bit of real-time strategy and who like silly humor will absolutely love it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good Stuff:+ The action-platforming is tight and fun+ The pixel art is fantastic, and I love it+ The game has a sense of humor. Doesn't always land, but the attitude is funThe Bad Stuff:- The first RTS/Base Building part of the game requires you to keep building long after you've learned how- Shortly after the first full level, you're thrown into a constant RTS assault that the defenses you're  to build for the tutorial portion are completely useless against- After defeat, you're given no time to make changes, and no guidance on a decent defense strategy - which would be fine, if they hadn't forced you to build a completely inadequate defense first- The one thing the tutorial doesn't go over - how to remove buildings to replace them with different ones - is  to getting past that first RTS assault.Now, don't get me wrong - I'm dead certain that this is going to be a lot of fun for people who are into it. And there  an "action mode" that skips all the base building and just does the platforming. But I'm not willing to pay for a whole game when I'm enjoying half of it and getting pissed at the other half, and it seems ridiculous to only play half of a game when there are tons of other games out there where I enjoy the whole thing (or at least more than 40-50% of it).SO, if you're into simple RTS/Tower Defense/Base Building and action platforming both, then you might enjoy this more than I did. Me? I'm sad to say that I'm going to have to return this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's gorgeous. It's complex. It's clearly full of effort and care. I want to love it.But it is so smash the controller frustrating.Trials are the obvious example. The controls are too full of float and imprecise for such unforgiving challenges. I also love one that involved constant mid-air movement without pause until my hand started going numb. There is a reason we left some bad platforming design back in the 80's. Brutal difficulty requires dependable controls.One-hit kills miles from a checkpoint. Damage and attack effects that prevent you seeing your character. Unreliable button combos that, you guessed it, can get you one hit killed.It feels like there is a classic game just below the surface here, but right now it's one where the bolts need tightening and the gears need oiling.

_childDocuments_.review: is an enjoyable, well-designed, and challenging action-platformer that plays like a cross between , , and , with a bit of a  visual flair to its character designs. If this sounds like your jam then dive right in; You're sure to find something to like here.Admittedly it is a little bit rough around the edges, and the controls can sometimes feel a bit stiff and clunky. But it was nothing that I wasn't able to adjust to and it didn't detract from my overall enjoyment at all.It's also worth mentioning that the barely-present story doesn't take itself seriously at all. Some people might be put off by this, but it never bothered me as the dialogue was never obnoxious or annoying, and the characters themselves are charming enough.The soundtrack (courtesy of Evader) is absolutely excellent, and it's one of the best I've had the joy of listening to in quite a while. It genuinely feels like it belongs to a classic SNES game, and there are tons of catchy tunes that are guaranteed to get stuck in your head if you're a fan of that genre (and era) of music. All in all, I greatly enjoyed my initial playthrough of  and will definitely be replaying it for 100% completion. There's not much in terms of replayability, but it does offer a lot in terms of collectibles and optional challenges, so it should keep the average action-platformer fan satisfied for quite a while.Also it has copious amounts of underboob, and you can never say no to that.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours later and Smelter is still fantastic! Really glad because I was looking forward to this one. I love platformers and RTS and this game has both to a very satisfying extent! The quality of aesthetics and gameplay really brings me back to the days when these types of games were the bread and butter of companies like Nintendo, just pumping out hit after hit on handhelds. A very nostalgic experience, but it still manages to go beyond that and keeps up with modern quality of life. Titles like this and Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night are the reason why I still strongly believe that these types of games are still in demand and great fun, even with the level of detail and graphics that AAA and some indie titles have made standard today.For technical aspects, the controls are tight and responsive, and the menus and interface are good. The difficulty feels just right so far, though there is a bit of a learning curve; Anyone who is unfamiliar with action games or platformers in general might find it challenging, but that shouldn't come as a surprise for a game that looks and feels kind of like Mega Man X. After playing through some more of the stages, I can say the platforming is definitely tough, but never tear-your-hair-out unfair.Music is great as well! My favorite track is the one that plays during the trials, but a lot of them are just plain bangers!I managed to dodge the bugs, but the devs jumped on them and seems like they fixed the issues very quickly, which is a good sign.It's a 9/10 for me and the price is just right!

_childDocuments_.review: I hidden Gem in Steam.And yes, i read all the other Reviews and i cannot agree. Not at all. I dont know why this game is mixed. It is a lovely crafted world with funny characters and i totally like the idea that the Game is called "Smelter" and you actually play the Character Smelter. You will understand this if you play the Game.Controls:The Controls are awesome and smooth. People say it is not good. I dont know why. She jumps as high as much as i press the button. She moves only when i move the Stick. Awesome Mobility-Skills with obvious References to classic Games like Mega-Man. To be honest, if i die. Its my fault. And i played many many Games like this. The Mega-Man Z series. Ori, Celeste, The Messenger and many more. And this Title can absolutely stand next to them in Terms of Controls and Mobility Options for the Player.Level Design aka Difficulty:Yes, this Game may seem hard for beginners but, in my Opinion, the Stages hit the Sweetspot many times. They are not to long, not to short. Plattforming is Fun, Puzzles are Fun and there are many rooms to discover. This Team makes use of old Classic "Hidden Rooms in a Wall" Thing which may annoy many modern Gamers. Because you have to actually check the walls to be sure. But Even for this the Developer implemented a Sound so you can hear if a Secret is near by. So thank you for that."Enemies are to Strong"Two Questions1. Which Difficulty do they mean?2. Are they making use of the Element System?I literally 2 shot enemies with my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome electro whip. I snipe them with my charged Blaster aka we love Mega-Man Weopon from across the Screen. BUT to do so you have to use the right Element :D You would not attack Pikachu with a electro Attack and than say "Why is this Pokemon so tanky? If you chose the wrong Element, your Units wont kill them. Ah and yeah. This Game has a tiny Base mode which is totally funny and the visuals totally reminds me of the old SNES Times. I love it and it is super fun after you understand the buildings and the upgrades better.so what are the cons?Well there are not many. If you like you could say some levels are to complex but i like this kinda Games. I come back and use my new Ability to find new Areas if wish so. Here and there some wall jump problems or some challenges are really hard and you have to be patient to beat them. but ye....not really a "bad" thing.I dont mean to offend people here or potrait myself as a Pro-Gamer. Accept the fact that this game is, in some ways, like a classic Game. Which is intended to kill the Player at the very first tries. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Finished stage 5 and the game actually slaps you in the face by giving you what appears to be a boss fight and then it disappears before you fight it and the level ends. If I could refund this game, I would because thats actually messed up.I'm only writing this after close to two hours of gameplay, but this game is really rough even after the patches it got after the month it came out. I managed to complete 4 stages (3 and the tutorial), which isn't a lot, but I feel that I need to write this now.The story is fine, honestly. Its kinda cheesy but I think that's ok. I came more for the gameplay itself.The music is fantastic, and would easily put some of the songs on my daily playlist.The gameplay, however, I'm super mixed on. I came here expecting a modern-day indie version of Actraiser, and it checks some of these boxes. Its got the overworld management concept and the powerful warrior sidescroller concept. However, I've found two major issues with them so far:1) There is way too much tutorial and dialog for the overworld segment. In the two hours I got to play, I barely got any free control over the building segment. By the time I was allowed to build my own stuff after the 3rd stage, there were no enemies spawning and all I ended up doing was just building stuff just for the sake of having something to do (besides continuing the plot). The whole point of ActRaiser's overworld system was to build a relationship with the humans and aid them in rebuilding while having them help you reach the next stage, which Smelter only held your hand during the first two hours.2) The combat is interesting, but there's literally nothing to fight. In 4 total stages, I didn't fight a single boss. I've had no reason to use my big Smelter attack. All I'm doing is playing a platformer with somewhat stiff controls and occasionally has a foe in the way. The challenge rooms started off interesting, but nothing to show off the game's customizable combat within the first two hours of the game. And with the lack of bosses in FOUR STAGES, I doubt there is any kind of customization that will cover this.I will probably keep playing it after this review to give it more of a fair shot, but you won't get a refund after 2 hours of constant tutorials and little meat, even if I'm alright with the story/writing and love the music.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY YET!!!!I was initially excited about Smelter when I saw what it was all about, but upon playing it, it is a slogging exercise in frustration.The platforming tries to mimic Mega Man-X and fails in the most miserable ways imaginable.  Aggravating enemies that have way too much health, sluggish player movement, lead-heavy jumping, inputs that cross over mechanics that actually clash with each other (parry bullets with the same button that causes you to dart towards the ground while in midair) all add up to make this game a controller-smasher in the making.The level design seems to want to cross over Mega Man-X and Rayman at times but the developers do not really seem to get why it works in those games and why it can't work with the character they created.  Mockingly-annoying instant-kill spike placement, enemies that knock you around and stun you with their attacks and world traps that are overused to the point of abuse make the long-as-hell levels feel like an eternal torture session.The strategy element (which badly imitates Actraiser) is also bad, with most of the gameplay bogged down by unfunny story dialog written by at least one person who is very, very impressed with their wit.  So much so that even secondary characters never shut up, and so the player has to endure endless, unskippable, insufferable writing and an exceedingly-long, overbearing guided tutorial that actually has bad strategy that would go much smoother if the player were allowed to actually play the game instead of following the paint-by-numbers build-a-long the game wants you to endure to get into the guts of the game.  To make matters worse, at one point I got my character Smelter stuck over one of the towns while I was setting up defenses between waves of enemies, I couldn't move, I couldn't do anything as mob after mob came in, wiped out my fighters and overtook my entire empire.  I was helpless as I watched a tutorial's worth of progress just get wiped away with no feedback as to what happened.  I quit the campaign at that point because if that WAS scripted, then it was hands-down the worst scripted event I have ever seen in a strategy game, and only strengthens my position that this game is made by people who hate the player.  If it was a bug, it's a bug so bad, that it can not only cause a game over, but could potentially erase hours of progress if you either did not save or were confident in your efforts, which means the game is potentially completely broken (I also confirmed other posts on discussions that other players experienced this bug).At least I didn't pay much for this game, but even still, I do not recommend this game unless the make these changes:- Make all dialog and cutscenes entirely skippable (you aren't as funny as you think you are)- Fix the movement issues with dashing and wall jumping- Make ankle-biter enemies take less hits to kill- shorten or make the strategy campaign's tutorial completely skippable (including all the "witty" dialog that comes along with it)- Test your game!  Do not publish your game with a price tag and expect players to do your beta testing then join your Discord.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the premise of this game hooked me immediately. When I started up the game I saw the fun little anime opening, and also heard the game's awesome music. I was getting really good impressions at this point, so I begin a new game. I get through the "tutorial," head into the first mission, and then it hits me...this game plays like megaman X! Hook, line, and sinker. I was having a blast with this game, but the overworld base-building aspects put me off from the game a little bit at first. The more I played, the more it grew on me honestly though. I personally love the inclusion of it because: it gives you something interesting to do between missions, it serves as a change of pace with a unique form of gameplay that is still fun, and it demonstrates the locations and scope of the world you're in nicely. The best part about it though by far, is the fact that the overworld doubles as your ability grid. So the more you "conquer," the more you unlock, the more skills you obtain, and the more passive bonuses you get. There's just one main problem that I have with this game, and that's that it doesn't offer a superboss for you to cut your teeth against when you unlock all of your skills. And I know some could argue that the final boss counts, but it wasn't difficult enough to really fit the role of a superboss. The game could have also used more play time, but there's already plenty to find in terms of secrets and collectibles, so it has a hefty amount of content to it. This feels like one of those great indie games you play for a week or so and never forget, kind of like The Messenger. Overall I'd give this game an 8.5/10, great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Review made after 6 hours:TL;DR: A blend of Act Raiser and Mega Man X. Excellently done, highly recommend.Gameplay: 8/10A hub world where you're expanding en empire, then flying down to 2D platforming segments to sort out business in person is very much in line with Act Raiser and I love it. The strategy part is fairly simple, but you're incentivized to look for bonus goodies on the platforming stages in order to expand into places on the map that give you new abilities, as well as upgrade your buildings. having more soldiers on the map also gives you more hitpoints in the platforming levels. You fuel your empire and your empire fuels you, and this cycle between the 2 gameplay types is very satisfying.There's a clear sense that the platforming levels have been play-tested. You're given 3 distinct 'forms' with their own ability kits that change up how the game plays, I.E. One allows double-jumping, another lets you long-jump, and then you have one that gives you a glide/slowfall.There is no 'lives' system, and the checkpoints were spaced out just enough for me to get frustrated at lost progress, and then feel the subsequent satisfaction of actually reaching the next checkpoint. Good stuff.It takes a while to get to the boss fights but they're also a treat. They're very much exams that test you on everything you've learned up to that point, and if you die against them you automatically retry without having to wait. Seriously, this game oozes good design choices.Flaws: Sometimes controls don't register, or hitboxes feel misleading.Visuals: 9/10Nice-looking 2D sprites and environments. It's easy to tell what is and isn't an obstacle, projectile or enemy. I subtract 1 point because of the MC's armor. I couldn't get it out of my head how impractical it looked, and its raunchiness means I can't introduce my young nephew to this game.Sound: 10/10The music is catchy as hell. And it's got range, from frenetic high-energy tracks in line with Mega Man to the more calm, introspective music that can be found in Act Raiser.Story: 7/10Eve is a silent protagonist with a motive as old as video games themselves, and co-protagonist Smelter is a witty little imp (angel) that does the talking for both of them. The dialogue is very tongue-in-cheek, packed with meta-humor and the NPCs are woven into the gameplay loop. The text is actually super-enjoyable to read and just like the rest of this game it feels like somebody really put in the work.I'm liking the story so far but it's hard to judge since I haven't finished the game. This score and part of the review may change.Edit: Finished the game in 14.6 hours. The story and characters aren't anything profound, but they're entertaining enough and don't wear out their welcome. The ending felt satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Forged In Hell Update:This update includes the ability to exclude the RTS elements of the original release. Which allows you to quickly play through the 2D "Megaman X" like areas. While it's an improvement by removing the RTS mode, it also cuts down the humor too. I would recommend at least giving the default mode a go first. As the game's humor is part of it's charm. Other than that, the game remains the same. It's a challenging but fun platformer with an amusing sense of humor. It might border on too challenging for me, personally, but I liked the time I spent with it. -=-=-Original Review-=-=-What, did you think I just down vote ? Smelter is a fun, but challenging Megaman X like platformer with an Actraiser feel. The game doesn't take itself too seriously and has some entertaining dialogue between Smelter and the various cast of characters you meet along the way. The game is divided into two distinct game-play styles. The first one is the Megaman X style combat levels, where you play as a transformed Eve, traversing various platforming and combat challenges. In my usual method of not spoiling things. You don't acquire new abilities from fighting bosses, but rather acquire new forms that allow you to do different things. These forms are viable for mobility, combat, and defense. Making switching between them a fun experience. The second is a very bare-bones, RTS like system. You build houses, "farms", and then have two forms of defense. Either converting servants, called Zirms, into either melee or ranged fighters. It's not overly complex, but it's serviceable for what it has you do. As you expand your empire across the map, you have various tasks to do both in an RTS form and a Platforming form. All of that is introduced in the first 30 minutes. To unlock new abilities for Smelter's various forms, you have to complete various challenge rooms. These trials. I'll admit I usually hate these kinds of things. Emphasis on usually. They're on par with Escort Quests, if you ask me. Annoying, frustrating, and often not rewarding enough. These trial rooms do get challenging, but they never overstay their welcome. They are short, and occasionally punishing, but not so long or so hard that they made me quit in frustration. Furthermore, if you do find a door in a level that leads to one of these areas, you can always go back to it later. So you don't have to do them all in one run if you don't want to. Also, once you open one of these doors, and try it, you can unlock an upgrade on the world map to try them later. It's not a perfect game by any means, however, my negatives really devolve down to nitpicks. One: I immediately passed this game upon first viewing because Eve's outfit with Smelter is just stupid in design. If it wasn't for a friend streaming it and I got a look at the game play of it, I would've never have given this game a second chance. Two: Three: Smelter's main ability is to "Smelt" enemies (or objects) by grabbing onto them with his green floating hand. Objects (or enemies) that you can interact with in this way develop a green floating outline around them. This can be used to hold objects in place, restore your health, or deal damage to bosses. I wish this mechanic was active more often so it wouldn't fall by the wayside. I constantly kept forgetting it existed because the chance of it is so low at the start that the button doesn't become a part of the regular method of play. So when an object goes glow green, sometimes I just forget that I'm supposed to use his ability to take advantage of it. Sometimes I outright died because I didn't realize what I had to do against a particular boss because of how rare it is as it starts. Beyond that, I'm looking forward to finishing this. It's an entertaining ride, and I hope it maintains it's momentum. I do feel like the game might be on the shorter end, but I've gotten 12 hours out of it thus far, and I don't feel I'm too close to the end.I'll edit this when I get to the end to see if my opinion changes. Thus far though, I'm excited to see how this turns out.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the comments before already pointed out: Smelter is a mixture of ActRaiser and Mega Man (X).The strategy part is fun to play and gets challenging at times. Apart from the top-down-shooting it offers some strategic elements that directly influence the platforming part, so the connection between the two of them regarding the game mechanics is very well done.Speaking of challenging: The platforming part will get quite hard, but the checkpoints are set well and even some of the boss fights have checkpoints at certain points. Getting stronger as you are proceeding through the story really feels that way. The trials are woven into the concept in similar way: You need to collect the coins you get after succeeding at a trial to unlock skills for the platforming part, while the unlocking takes place in the strategy part. The trials can be very hard, but as they are only up to one minute long, you will try to beat them again and again. And if you succeed after half an hour, it's as rewarding as it gets. Of course you do not have to beat every trial to beat the game, but for the completionists out there it is a very nice challenge. Speaking of game mechanics: Apart from the trials you can find collectibles in the platforming levels like apples which can be used to upgrade your central building in the strategy part which will allow you to build houses with more inhabitants which will lead to more health in the platforming part... So again, it is very motivating to search a level once more for missing collectibles not only for the sake of having them collected, but it can really have an impact on your playthrough.The technical perspective: I've experienced no bugs, locks or anything of that kind. The jumping and running worked perfectly fine, the controls were on the spot. My controller was accepted without any problems.Overall Smelter is a brilliant attempt to recreate the feeling of the mentioned old games: Game mechanics that work very well combining both gameplay parts and within that concept an exceptionally well thought and therefore highly motivating integration of collectibles. I definitely got my money's worth out of this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever gotten sidetracked from the main plot with sidequests? Smelter feels like one massive sidequest got made into a game.If you want to see gameplay and my first impressions as they happened, watch my video. Smelter puts you into the role of Eve (yes, as in Adam and Eve) and Smelter, an "angel" (definitely not a demon) who is looking to conquer- I mean, help Eve find Adam. Cue a magical girl transformation sequence and now you're a female Mega Man X, occasionally disrupted by flying over your domain and building your empire.For those who haven't played ActRaiser, it's a beautiful mess that switches between different game styles. Eve's silence and Smelter's ego makes for writing you'll either love or hate. The tutorials drag unnecessarily long, and the writing can drag on as well, but the platforming stages are decent off-brand Mega Man fare. Smelter's weakness comes in a few mechanical oddities. It seems to have been designed for Nintendo controllers, so for those (like me) who are on an X-Box controller, A is cancel, B is confirm, and Right Bumper is dash. You can remap controls for platforming, but you can't swap confirm and cancel for menuing. Dash jumping either isn't intended or outright doesn't work, and I'm never quite sure which it is. And wall jumping doesn't reconnect to the wall if you do a full jump, making the trials unnecessarily brutal.Other reviewers are mentioning bugs, but I personally didn't encounter any.So is Smelter worth it? The highs are high, and the lows are boring. The opening movie is fantastic and an instant hook. I've been enjoying my time, but if you're on the fence then I'd recommend wishlisting Smelter and waiting out a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Game of the Year contender, without question.  Smelter scratches the itch of some the SNES's best titles, giving players a plethora of play styles that harken classics like Megaman X and Actraiser.  The ladder of which has been grossly ignored in modern gaming.  Thankfully, Smelter picks up the slack and then some in this robust 16-bit blockbuster.  As Eve in search of Adam in a biblical beginning of age tale (that could be more true than the original source material, for all we know) you befriend a being known as Smelter who bestows powers upon you that exceed imagination.  There are new abilities to constantly obtain, and each actually feel great with the platforming sections wonderfully crafted maps.  There are even challenge trials that actually add to upgrades in the city/army building segments.  In these moments, you actually control Smelter, who flies around building outposts for soldiers, discovering blessings to boost your chances for victory, and you even have the power to fight off enemy forces with projectiles.  There's too much to cover here, but it's amazing!  Even if, admittedly, understanding the torturous tutorials might leave your head spinning.  Once you wrap your head around it, it's incredibly marvel!This title needs it's audience, as it far exceeded even the high expectations I had going for it.  Developer X Plus certainly showcased their passion for 90's 16-bit with Smelter, and we're all the better for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Take parts of that, and  the god creation and villages in between the Acts. Now take a silly mask, Eve from the Bibble, and very silly writing.This one reminds me of Batbarian with it being an excellent game, with a less-than-serious approach to the story telling. The game breaks things up into two parts: Sidescrolling Action, and Top Down Map Navigation.These are your standard side-scrolling affair, with moves and level design akin to MegaMan X series of games.You start with a limited move set, and gain more and more skills as you progress ( eventually getting to the point where you swap elemental powers on the fly, changing your entire move set ) They ease you into this with 3 distinct areas as a sort of tutorial. Each area only allows the ONE element you'll be learning there to be used, so you can't cheap them out with the double jump from the rock element, for instance. It's a neat way to show the player the elements are more than the flavor of attack, they drastically change your very moves. Each level has some collectibles - 3 apple cores, Moxie ( a currency ) and coins, you get them from challenge areas. These are sort-of challenging areas, where they make you learn a mechanic usually - and say " don't get hit " or something.They really feel like tutorials masked as " challenges " because you can die and fail in them as many times as you like, and you can repeat em on the spot ( they even move them all to a localized spot on the world map for you to re-try if you need)For the most part the varied moves are welcomed, although jumping always feels a bit spongy and unimpactful, The main issue is each of your elements act as your new skill set, it kinda feels like a " jack of all trades, master of none " sort of deal at times. Not a huge deal, but the platforming can feel loose at times ( especially if you're playing 20xx,30xx, or are a Megaman X fan ) There's this extended jump when you dash and jump, and the timing feels bad, I almost always mess it up - so I don't do the jump, and plummet into 1-hit kill spikes, or something. Stuff like that might happen a lot, so bring patience with you. That pretty much wraps up the Side-scrolling part, so what is the other part of the game like? This is where the game wears it's Actraiser influence on it's sleeve.You spend time in between levels building a world map path ( which gives you access to levels, and events ) and in addition to this, you manage your population, and their food supply ( you also construct buildings  to house them, your food, and defenses ) ...defenses? yes. At times on the world map, your entire domain will be attacked by enemies. You will control a character on the world map that can fly, and shoots like a twin-stick shooter ( also, heals buildings ) This happens occasionally, and is a nice mix-up to the pacing. The World map stuff serves as a means to provide you with a unique map for level selection, and give you more to chew on while you do it. It never feels overly complicated, and it never feels liek it's really  either. But it's fine as it is. All in all, this game is a very solid package. The art is top-notch, there's tons of content to dig in ( completionists, enjoy ) and the controls and overall game play loop are satisfyingFirst 30 Minutes of Gameplay ↓

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt the clunkiest platformer I have ever played. The wall jumping is extremely unresponsive. Eve will often get stuck on the upper part of walls near ledges and not jump upwards, which is very annoying in some segments - there's one part with spinning chainsaw pillars and a few of the trials that comes to mind.Dash-jumping and dashing in mid-air with the dark suit upgrade also feel really bad, like there's some sort of input lag that makes it so Eve dashes later than I tell her to.In general, jumping is very finicky. During the fight versus the screen boss, I found I got hit by the electrified water several times, even though I was pressing and trying to jump out of it. Eve would just take way too long to jump, and sometimes even ignore my inputs. It took me an embarrassing amount of time because I kept taking lots of damage because of these refused jumps.Attacking also feels very slow and clunky, with the wind-up animations being super long for how much they lock you in place.And this is just the platforming. The RTS element is just... not very fun. It doesn't feel challenging at all and I find that all I have to do is just spam buildings. It might be because I haven't gotten that far into the game (I've only just now unlocked the third element for Eve), but it's taken me this long to progress this far because of how much the movement in the platforming sections fights against me.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Plattformer, trivial and rudimentary RTS. In the later part the game is restricted to just a few types of buildings which you upgrade in tower defense style, all while you fly across the map and support your troops with Twin-Stick shooting, sounds like Actraiser, but isn't as engaging, especially because there is no actual "building and development" part except from cluttering the maps with your towers.The plattformer on the other hand is really well designed. There are different Movesets to unlock which you can switch between on the fly, all of them kinda resemble traversial mechanic that remind you on different Plattformers and Metroidvanias.There is one moveset where you can shoot and glide, another one where you gain iframes through evasion and cross large distances and one rather "bulky" fashioned who allows you to block and jump higher.These forms can be upgrades by unlocking certain structures on the RTS part, to do that, you have to find collectibles in the levels itself.Noteworthy are the challenge rooms there are up to 3 in each level and they test your understanding on the game on different departments. These challenge rooms are pretty diverse, varied and most of the time simply challenging in a fun way. Since there are plenty of them, there is no problem if you might miss a few rooms that seem to hard at first, there is plenty of ressource to upgrade your favourite moveset.So yeah wouldn't it be for the RTS part which is seriously underdeveloped and dull the gameplay would have a great flow. Well with a new update they released a new game mode where you can let someone else manage the RTS sections so it's just levels, i'm not so particulary fond of cutting out what seemed to be THE selling point of the game (at least to me) but at this point it looks like the whole RTS part was largely compromised by the devs themselfes too, maybe it was just too big so they couldn't make something more complex and stimulating (and would probably shoo even more people away because the overlap between RTS and Plattforming fans isn't that high - unfortunelately)If I would play the game I suppose I would still play the dull RTS parts just because its in the idenity of the game, but yeah I have not too much good to say from that side.Oh and there are very rarely twinstick shooting sections, these are underdeveloped as well and i'm fortunate that there were only (2 I think?) in the game.As for the plattforming part, the leveldesign is well crafted, each level presents its own ideas, you can tackle the storylines of 3 areas parallel in any order you want. The game can be pretty challenging, There are no difficulty options but cultivating your empire will give you health upgrades up to a certain degree. I think it's a elegant way to handle that topic rewarding players for their efforts in other departments, instead of just dull difficulty sliders. I kinda like it when games just have one definitive difficulty where you can compare your experiences with (makes the game stand out from the rest) and taking down the bosses can definitely feel satisfying, so if you value challenge, the game has plenty of it.The writing of this game tries to be funny, while it definitely doesn't suit my taste of humor and it has pretty predictable story developments. I actually don't know why there is an Adam and Eve theme in the game, the game is largely unrelated to the biblical tale of eden.Also I really have a problem to take Smelter serious when he always tries to be funny, he definitely has not really villain vibes, which makes some later story developments pretty unbelievable, Eve on the other side is your typical silent protagonist. there is not really much to say about her. Side character can be more interesting... sometimes, So yeah don't expect a great story here.If you are an extreme player, the new Boss Rush Mode from this game is very very good I can fully recommend it, especially because there is a twist to it, your moveset becomes restricted, so they don't play exactly the same like in story mode and you can make them even harder.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start that this is not an actraiser wannabe and that I  deeply regret buying this game.There are way too many parts that annoy the fk out of me and despite all the effort I put into liking it it's just not going to work.Let's get good things out of the way first:Platforming and combat are good, controls are responsive, movement is smooth, smacking enemies is satisfying. The only part I found weird is the whole element system where you can change between different modes with different skills and control scheme- for instance one of them has double jump and the other one doesn't. It's really confusing at the start but you probably can eventually get used to it I guess.Art and animations are good enough, pleasant to the eye.Music is decent too, banging tracks especially in trials.Now for the bad parts.The writing. Since game is japanese I can not say for sure If it's the issue with the original script or just bad localization,but it's extremely obnoxious,cumbersome,  nonsensical, filled with garbage jokes and a lot of made-up ugly words that don't make sense.There is no story and you're not a heroine of it. You're just a puppet serving the weird mask with the wings. After several hours playing I still couldn't say what this is all about, what is  the endgoal and who are the bad guys.The "strategy" part. It's actually just a very barebones tower defense.There are 4 building - 2 defensive, 1 for food and 1 for "peasants". That's it. Now go fill the tiny map and fight waves of enemies until timer runs out. Extremely boring.The platfroming part, as I mentioned earlier, is great. Those 2D levels are masterfully crafted, they are fun and full of secrets and stuff HOWEVER. You can NOT save in them. So you need to do each one of them in one sitting or you'll lose the progress. With all the exploring and challenges (I know you can access challenges later but that doesn't solve anything) it should take around 40+ minutes, so If you don't have that time - don't even start the level.So do you want some nice 2D action-platformer gameplay? You should play literally any other game, because this one is filled with questionable design decisions and outright bad writing.I warned you

The mechanics for the real time strategy part of the game are not overly complex and are mostly there to have a more interactive level select/ world map. There is also a mode which cuts this part out entierly from the begining, if you only want run and gun action. The game got good tight controls, very megaman X like, nice visuals and good music. The sound mixing is a little odd as all ingame sounds appart from the title theme in the main menu are very quiet even if all settings are set to max. While the story is nothing too special the dialogues are written pretty charming. I didn't encounter any major bugs for me the game ran without issues. Difficulty wise it's challenging but not frustrating, although the game seems to have some balance issues with the abilities, the claws / earth element are pretty much the go to option until very late in the game when you have some more skills unlocked for al abilities, but its not too bad. _childDocuments_.review: Why "no"? Everything except the game not respecting my time is great. There's no save option mid-level, where you're supposed to explore. I routinely rack up 40 minutes on the clear time. It would be way less if I were using a guide, but I haven't so far (though I will after this review). Say I just couldn't find the 3rd hidden item, or trial, or ore deposit. I'd have to finish the level. I couldn't just stop and pick back up later.Anyway, this is a wonderful homage to Actraiser and Mega Man X. The gimmick is neat, and some twists on things exist. One of those twists is what you find while exploring the platforming levels. Unfortunately, as levels get longer and more punishing, that system suffers. If most of the challenge were centered around trials that you have to search out to begin with, this would be a "yes", because it would mostly be skippable. Now, I don't like a lot of the trials. They're supposed to be themed around the power set you get from the area you find that power set and trial in. Got it. You know where else that gets done? Several of the levels. You know what those levels -don't- do? They don't force you to keep doing that. Trials do. You get whichever power set and that's it. Only one of the power sets gets double jump... in a platforming game. Yes, there are other moves. Yes, trials make it excruciatingly and painfully clear that they're adequate. But that's all they are: adequate. If trials let you use other power sets or some of them had checkpoints, it would be better. Yes, I realize most trials can be done in less than a minute if you win. Lots of them have instant lose spots. Some of them aren't properly restarted, so some elements differ entirely from the first run of a trial (versus a 30th consecutive attempt).Speaking of instant lose spots, those questionable choices bleed over from the trials into the platforming level design. Annnnnnnd they eventually invalidate the gimmick, because in later levels just clipping into a certain kind of enemy will time warp you. Previously, you had to use Smelter to grab switch objects. Remarkably bad choice, in my opinion, especially because it's very often used as a "♥♥♥♥ you" on top of other  already difficult platforming elements. An example in the following paragraph.You reach a long stretch before a boss. The long stretch has 5 main obstacles: (1) the level is designed so that you go right-then-left and left-then-right, (2) a giant laser that takes up roughly a third of the vertical area and all of the horizontal area fires on a timed loop, (3) rotating laser turrets aim-lock onto you, (4) the time warp monsters litter the whole area in one timeline, and (5) other monsters exist. Did you run into one of the time warp monsters? Back down the shaft to where a reverse time warp monster is. Now back up. Dodge them better next time. Now bait and dodge the big laser. Now dodge the 3 aim-lock lasers. Why, yes, they DID put a time warp monster right in the way of the exit, but just think how good it will feel when you switch to the other power set to phase through it. No? You died... again? And you want to quit playing until later, but as you mentioned you can't save mid-level (despite there being checkpoints). All those sound like you problems. It's not like other levels put spikes under those time warp monsters so that you time warp into spikes if you make the mistake of hitting them, but it's not a mistake to hit them when the hidden stuff requires you to time warp. That's different.That type of stuff puts me in a bad mood. So, other stuff I'd normally give a pass to stands out instead. For example, I was able to infinite loop one of the world map events with no way to stop it other than reloading (because walls heal and you have to take down 3 separate sections on different timers). Thing is, you have to pick the first of the 3 things to advance. Well, that means the next stuff is limited by when your personnel show up to man the tower. Get in the habit of building a house near wherever you are, because they will literally walk in real time across the whole map if you just call them and the last one you built is far away. I haven't checked, but I doubt they use the altars (which are fast travel points). It isn't great. Other things that aren't great are that using Smelter's attack (which pauses the screen) doesn't bother to pause the projectile launch from the enemies that walk walls. It saw you, it's firing, and Smelter can't do a thing about it. Bam, you got hit in the middle of what amounts to a cutscene. Have fun with that. Oh, and, yes, those little creatures will be warping with you between some time warps. You wouldn't want to have a way to logically avoid them, would you?

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game to anyone who loves platformers such as Megaman or Castlevania, but also loved the old SNES Actraiser. It's basically a very well done Actraiser type game where you have your overworld view doing your tower defense essentially, and then the sidescrolling game play is reminiscent of a megaman/castlevania hybrid. 9/10 game. Only thing I'd like to see is being able to upgrade your soldiers more.
_childDocuments_.name: Smelter

_childDocuments_.review: Yes but with an asterisk. Definitive yes for Megaman X/Zero/ZX fans.The combat is fun, the game looks good and it's not very long which is reflected in the price. You're basically getting Megaman ZX tho that may not be apparent at first but it becomes very obvious once you get the mega blaster suit. You can swap your suits out instantly to get some pretty neat combat sequences and to help you traverse but it's never a requirement.There's a whole secondary mode about building up an empire but it's shallow. You only get 4 (+1) buildings, a very basic resource system and no opponent. You're just stuck on an island with randomly spawning enemies until you do whatever dungeon is stopping your progress. This whole ordeal usually takes about 5 minutes and then you're back to the side scrolling levels.The challenges are mostly fine with a few exceptions which really live up to their name but they are optional upgrades. Some of the later levels are frustrating in design with platforms that change every half second and switches that give you less than a second of error but the process of trying again is usually really fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Smelter

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, had a lot of fun. Gameplay outside of the tower defense bits are more or less Megaman X adjacent. I recommend it if you like moderately tough but not super tough meme difficulty platforming adventures (this isn't Wings of Vi but you will still die, perhaps a lot). The platforming isn't the tightest experience, but it is an acceptable one, and the level design isn't boring. But, BUTI think it was a poor design decision to pack these side bonus stages in the levels, instead of having people do them outside of the levels. They will make the levels in this game feel very long especially since you can't save while you are in a level. Like what would be a 10-15 minute excursion will turn into 30 minutes to an hour trying to get all the collectibles. I will swear up and down that the lightening whip armor is bugged. You can at some point learn to charge your whip and if you try climbing a wall and hitting something with your charge, your charge will up and disappear. Also can't get the wall run jump flying spin sword tech to work consistently for the life of me.This games story doesn't feel very complete. You will end this game wondering who all these people you met are, and the game doesn't actually care to tell you more about them. Thankfully, it doesn't pull a golden sun (find out more in the sequel that is never coming lol) sort of ending.

_childDocuments_.review: if you're looking for a challenging platformer that you can step up to and work your way through, this is the game for you. If you get frustrated needing to retry sections from checkpoints, then this game may not be the best choice for you. There certainly are a few sections of the game that will push your skills. The additional overhead game mode where you build your settlement is a welcome respite from the platforming levels and is somewhat of a respite from the regular game mode. It has a few challenges as well, but they are easier to overcome and rely as much on strategy and building placement as dexterity. It appears to be optional in some game modes anyway.The story of the game isn't particularly cohesive, but it's cute and surreal, and it's just strong enough to add to the sense of progress.I have seen some people remark on the controls, but I found them clean enough - you don't need to be pixel-perfect, and the feel is overall pretty good.

Is a bit clunky at times when wall sliding or element swapping and when there are multiple things happening on screen that you gotta skirt by they wont line up in cycles which might leave you stuck waiting for a good time to go.Good soundtrack, though i feel the title theme is kinda weak compared to the rest of the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fun as hell, but it is easily one of the HARDEST metroidvania's I have ever played and beaten. If you manage beat this hard S.O.B, kudos to you! I also just wanna say I appreciate a game that's not afraid to be both fanservicy, and humorous, gotta give these credit for that!My one big complain is I do think some of the trials are a bit too hard, there's one notorious one where you have to beat an area damageless, while lightning strikes come down every 4 seconds, ontop of some tricky platforming. That one in particular seemed like it took me 150+ attempts because inevitably I was getting furious from the repeat attempts.The tower defense mode is kinda bland as well, the platforming stages are way more fun, but you may feel differently.There's a few bugs here and there, but no deal breakers. It seems like the dev is constantly patching to improve the game, so good on them.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game in the same line as Actraiser. The sidescrolling sections play out like a Megaman style game, while the civilization building is simple but good. The Kill la Kill influences should be obvious to those who are familiar but homages aside, the game does a good, but not great job of using all of its different elements. Dashing feels stiff in the sidescrolling, while the civ parts feel stiff and not being able to fly over water can make it hard to navigate corners. I still highly recommend for people who enjoyed Actraiser or want to play a unique little game.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions video: Smelter caught my attention because I'm a huge fan of the classic SNES title Act Raiser. The unique blend of action platforming and light city building is something that's never really been duplicated since and this looked like it could scratch that itch. It does to a degree but I think it also has some frustrations that will make it not to everyone's taste.The city building component is simple but also much more advanced than Act Raiser. As you push forward into the world, you'll have to build a mix of a small handful of structures to recruit troops, feed them and house them for battle on the front lines to hold off waves of enemies as you complete the varied objectives. You'll have to manage the locations of your troops and ensure they're placed properly to handle the threats and you can also assist them in battle directly.This is complimented by periodic platforming levels that you'll have to go through. They start off easy but will get quite challenging fairly quickly. Some of them have boss battles, some of them don't but they alll have challenge rooms and collectibles that will help you advance your character and you have the option to replay these levels whenever you want to get more collectibles, as well as go through them with a stronger character.Your "living armour" has 3 different states that you can switch between in both the platforming levels and the overworld, all of which have their own abilities and traits. You'll need all of these to overcome the levels and each one has benefits against certain types of enemies as well. You will also obtain a number of different additional skills for each of these states as you go, that will add different moves and abilities. Your character will evolve a lot over the course of the game.My issues with it are that there seems to be a notable input lag that will lead to a lot of situations where you die going "I totally made that jump in time." The difficulty curve is also very uneven, going from challenging to injuriating very quickly. If you like difficult games, I think you'll welcome this but others will find it frustrating.While I do recommend this game and plan to continue poking at it until I get to the end, I strongly suggest trying the demo first and making up your own mind. This is the closest thing I've yet seen to a modern Act Raiser and there's a lot more depth to this than that game but it also has some frustrating elements that I think will turn off some players.

_childDocuments_.review:
You are Eve, fresh out of Eden and armed with a living suit of armor. Explore a dangerous new world, battle its bizarre denizens and expand your empire in a desperate journey to find Adam. Smelter is a strategy, action-platformer combo inspired by classics from the 16-bit era. Lead Smelter and his faithful Zirm forces by expanding Smelter’s territory across the Rumbly Lands in top-down strategy levels, then dive into thrilling side-scrolling action stages after annexing key locations. Build, attack and advance your army -- unlock, upgrade and unleash elemental action skills against vicious enemies, perilous environments and dangerous bosses. Release the power of Smelter!
Story: After the untimely destruction of the Garden, Eve finds herself in an unfamiliar world with her beloved Adam nowhere to be found. In her search for Adam, she encounters Smelter, an unusually over-confident, winged creature with the powerful ability to transform and fuse with others, giving them incredible powers. Offering his apparently “invaluable” assistance, Smelter transforms and fuses with Eve. They depart on a journey to the treacherous Rumbly Lands. There, they expand Smelter’s territory, allowing them to reach further into the various domains to find out what happened to her Adam, hoping to find him in one piece and find a way back home to their peaceful lives...

name: Helvetii
detailed_description: Character-action set in ancient Swiss Gaul Around a hundred years BC, all of Gaul is far from Roman control. In the lands controlled by the Helvetii, a Roman legion was subjugated by young warchief Divico, blessed by an ancient boon brought to him from parts unknown. However, this victory came at a great cost, as soon the result of the war chief's pact would turn into a curse; an ever spreading rot crawling through his land, and slowly corrupting his mind and heart. Monsters and cultists start appearing throughout the land, and a shadowy figure makes his move, taking advantage of the chaos he helped create. With the help of the trusted yet reclusive druid Nammeios and the curious half-beast Renart, Divico sets his journey to undo the source of the rot and restore what was lost inside him. Through his own martial prowess and powers conferred by the old gods, the fight ahead promises to be intense. THREE UNIQUE CHARACTERS A disgruntled war chief, a snarky fox or a wise druid. Three characters with their unique playstyle and special attacks that will help you dominate the legions of monsters. Regardless of whatever items or summons you find, you will never be completely helpless in Helvetii. Regardless of power ups, your core moveset will always feel complete from the get-go. EASY TO LEARN, HARD TO MASTER STYLISH ACTION With a wide variety of abilities and situations, it’s not just about finishing the fight, but doing it in style! Take your time to master each character with acrobatic combos, using the terrain at your advantage and mercilessly juggling your opponent for the highest ranks, and highest rewards. THE GIFTS OF THE GODS AT YOUR COMMAND Lost treasures, ancient burial mounds, curious owl shopkeepers and altars containing the essence of powerful gods await you, scattered across the land. Harness powerful summons and obtain items that will give you even more options in a fight. A PRECISE, VISCERAL EXPERIENCE SET IN A CAREFULLY CRAFTED WORLD With a closed-in camera, carefully detailed 2D environments and an enchanting soundtrack composed by Dale North and sung by Emi Evans, get thrusted into intense combat scenarios that keep you close to the action THE SECRETS OF THE GAUL Discover the ancient Celtic world of the Gauls, mixed in with more unique legends from Swiss and Germanic folklore. Journey from yet untamed forests to abandoned villages overtaken by cultists, merciless snowy caps, underground tunnels and beyond... We have now been working for a while on Helvetii from our humble studio here in Switzerland. Our primary goal is to share our love for precise and intense character action mechanics by making absolutely sure combat is fine-tuned and always enjoyable, mixed with the best art we can provide. This is a project we've been caring a lot for a long time, and we really hope our excitement will reach all the players out there! We wish to thank anyone who shares our passion and decides to support and believe in us. Let's all do our best! - Hoot and Ironbell, from Team KwaKwa
