_childDocuments_.review: Clive 'n' Wrench is a monumental accomplishment and might stand as one of the most ambitious solo-dev projects of all time.While the duo setup might evoke an impression of Banjo-Kazooie or Ratchet & Clank, I'd say that Clive 'n' Wrench's identity is more closely tied to Spyro the Dragon. Levels are in semi-open worlds that have lots of nooks and crannies to explore, but also have an "intended" path that eventually leads to an exit. Big collectables are mostly found hidden in the key points of a level, but some are received as rewards for helping NPCs. Gems (in this case, stopwatches) leave a bouncing 3D number in their place, and Clive has a charging run attack similar to Spyro's that can break vases. I do love me some Spyro, so this is very welcome from my perspective! I only compare them to give a better sense of what to expect for other 3D platformer junkies.Clive and Wrench's moveset is a real highlight and a main reason that I feel the game stands well on its own. Clive is , and he's got big rabbit hops. If you see some tantalising platform off in the distance, odds are you'll be able to reach it by crouch jumping and twirling Wrench around for a bit. I think it's very satisfying to get across the worlds at mach speed by holding run and maintaining that insane momentum into jumps. Wrench's only contribution to the moveset is to be twirled around as a meat copter, which begs the question why he needs to be a monkey instead of anything else at all. Then again, this way, he gets to make silly ooks and screeches as you bash stuff with him, so I approve.It's important for me to point out how solid the game's core is. Browsing negative reviews will point out things like the overuse of tutorial robots beeping, wonky climbing animations, or non-remappable controls as the game's biggest downfalls. Those things are annoying, but easily patchable. What I'm concerned with is the foundation: the character feels great to control, the world has a lot of charm, and there's a wealth of content available. I'm currently only finished 100%-ing four worlds out of an apparent 11. That is way more than I expected! I just finished the platforming gauntlet in the Egyptian level and thought it was a real highlight.Clive 'n' Wrench is a lot of fun in a genre that doesn't get much love any more. If you like 3D collectathons, I'm happy to report that this one is very charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: Clive 'N' Wrench is an incredibly charming dive into the collectathon genre with some of the best and most satisfying platforming I've seen in a while. The game is packed with content and was created in its entirety by one person and plays/performs better than some of the recent titles from massive gaming companies. First off, the movement, which is by far one of the best things this game has to offer. It feels so fluid and there are always multiple ways to tackle various obstacles and you almost always have a way to recover if you miss a jump. It combines Spyro's ability to constantly dash with Banjo/Yooka's ability to glide which can be combined with other moves to create some really satisfying strides. Secondly, the music is ridiculously well made. Collectathons have always been known to be equipped with a stellar soundtrack, especially with all that time you'll spend listening while collecting and this game delivers. It's even got that really cool feature when you enter different areas or go underwater the music shifts in pitch/tone. I've always really enjoyed that and was delighted to experience it here. Thirdly, the charm just pours out of this one. There are comical references almost everywhere and loads of throwbacks to classic collectathons. It makes the game feel like it's adding on to an already incredible legacy left behind by games such as Banjo-Kazooie. The enemies are also well-varied with dynamically different enemies appearing in each world. There is also a ragdoll feature when killing enemies which becomes absolutely hilarious. Some weaker enemies can be hit so hard they go flying across a zone and you'll just see them just ricocheting off objects in the distance. It's amazing. Enemies are also able to interact with each other, such as one enemy's attack damaging another enemy which as you can imagine leads to some comical gameplay. Lastly, there are new additions such as the radar which is actually quite nice and prevents you from spending hours trying to find one last collectible you may not have noticed. The "magnet" feature which pulls collectibles to Clive is incredibly responsive and really helps to keep you rolling and not feel worried about missing things along the way which complements the movement as a whole even further. Throughout the entire game there wasn't a single stopwatch (akin to notes in BK or quills in YL) that wasn't picked up by this feature as I dashed through.As a collectathon veteran (fully beaten every one to date), I thoroughly enjoyed Clive 'N' Wrench and I really hope people aren't swayed by the negative comments I've seen here. This game has so much to offer and has such a great concept behind it I would be more than thrilled to hear of a sequel being developed some day. Thank you Rob for bringing your dream to life and allowing us to experience it firsthand. I had a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: Clive 'N' Wrench is a collectathon platformer in the vein of PSX-era games such as Crash Bandicoot and Spyro the Dragon. The player passes through a series of areas based on time periods, collecting stopwatches and sacred stones to unlock (respectively) regular and boss levels. The controls are reasonable tight and the game is very easy to get into. Graphically, it is a mixed bag - the animations are a little janky but the backgrounds are highly detailed.Overall, Clive 'N' Wrench is a fun game, but I personally would have preferred it if the game had been a little more ambitious.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall just ok. I think with some somewhat minor changes i'd change this to a positive reviewI think the game lacks a lot when it comes to audio obviously we don't want a Banjo kazooie talon trot situation, but a lot of your moves and enemies just lack any audio queues at all orthey are of very poor quality also the majority of the world theme songs are very repetitive and generic.Pole climbing feels really wonky & for some reason physics objects and even just animations sometimes play at around 10 fps while the rest of the world and your character moves at 60+ or on pc 120+ fps.this is obviously better than some of the AAA games released lately that have horrid fps all around but overall this brings the quality of the game down a lot.Also I completely understand this is mostly a solo project but the animations and some of the modeling is just very sub par.like I'm not even sure why. cleo's statues look great but her actually animated model has horrible polygonization.Maybe your models have bad topology so when you apply additional subsurface modifiers or AA it leads to bad clipping when animated or something but overall makes little sense to me. Nancy for instance look pretty bad.An additonal 40-60 polygons on the main character Nancy and maybe the bosses for instance shouldn't effect performance unless the coding is horrible. I enjoyed the egypt platforming based sub sections I would have loved to see some sooner. but it seemed very odd to hide them behind collecting 5 mundane hard to find collectibles. though I will say that in this case there where actually audio queues that helped out finding them.The boss difficulty is also all over the place. the first boss fight is somewhat hard but then a similar boss fight later on is easier.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, with some big caveats.If you're a big fan of 3D platformers from the N64, PS1, GameCube, and PS2, this is up your alley. It definitely feels like one of the lower budget releases from that era, rather than one of the hard hitters. If you have a soft spot for those lesser known platformers, you'll enjoy Clive 'n' Wrench.Flickering lighting, jittery physics and animations on environment objects, crazy pop-in, and framerate stutters regardless of hardware go a long way to hamper the experience, but the level themes are cute and there's plenty of jumping and collecting to do.Here's hoping the developer is able to sort some of these issues out - it'll be an even easier recommendation then.

_childDocuments_.review: I did some of my own time travelling and was able to load my saved game from the beta build! Obviously I'm a huge fan of this soulfully crafted instant gaming classic - inspired by the classics which came before it - it's got everything from the references to the visual artistry, to the joyous mechanics which feel like they combine into something which is greater than the sum of its parts. You don't have to be a classic 3D platformer veteran to get sucked in by the awesome environments, exploration and platforming, yet if you're a hardened collectathon-er you will find refreshing challenges to get that sweet satisfaction of clearing one of its huge, yet expertly paced levels, which make use of every trick in the book to both help you take in their different areas bit by bit, whilst still allowing for open exploration which actually holds surprises and rewarding experiences - much more so than the most popular 'open world' games out now. I'm having fun continuously being engaged by the next bit of gameplay which immerses you in a sort of parallel universe (or collection thereof) of references and inspirations from some of the best in the genre, while being wrapped up in a package that feels wholly original, and more than anything, like the work of a developer who is a fan of games, and poured his artful heart and soul, informed by their own idols, into their own vision. And dammit if it ain't a fun one - just what the industry needed. May this in turn inspire other, original, modern classics of 3D platforming and adventuring! Received for free as per DinosaurBytes' principles, simply because I lended my voice to the hilarious Gator Gangster enemies; I was already a fan of this when it was a work in progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets the most important thing right, it's fun. The level design is great. The controls are tight, and the movements are fun to chain together. There's a lot of charm and character evident throughout with cartoony slapstick cutscenes and expressive characters. Now, there is definitely some jank. The transitions from cutscenes are incredibly abrupt and your character barely reacts to being hit by an enemy. The boss fights are also not the best. There is certainly some polish missing. But the game's design leads you to want to 100% it in the same way the first spyro the dragon does. It's simply fun exploring and collecting everything. I definitely recommend it to any 3d platformer fan
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely ugly. Its visual design is cluttered, and what visual direction it has is bland and generic. What I enjoy about old school 3D platformers like Banjo-Kazooie is their simplicity and clarity, whereas this game is visually cluttered. The cutscenes were also poorly animated, and it was difficult to understand what was happening or who these characters are or what their deal is. The game's first level also had a huge amount of hint boxes, all clustered together in a tiny area, and which made obnoxious beeping noises. And the majority of these hint boxes gave painfully obvious advice like "Don't touch that fire, you'll get hurt!" etc. Poor game design.Controls are also awkward. In Banjo-Kazooie you can just hit A twice and hold it to do a double jump glide, whereas here it's press A twice then hold X, which feels like it's using extra buttons for no reason imo. There was also an issue that occurred several times during the tutorial, where the character's state machine broke, and he slid along the ground without animating for a couple seconds. If this game was really in development for over 10 years, a basic issue like that should have been ironed out. It's embarrassing that a glitch in the character's basic movement made it into the final product.I refunded this game after half an hour. It was giving me a headache. Kinda makes me appreciate Yooka-Laylee more.

_childDocuments_.review: Just over an hour so far. Foundationally it seems solid, however it has many issues.The primary and major issue is that a lot of logic is incorrectly tied to the render loop, or scaled to the render loop when it shouldn't be. For example, your camera rotation speed will vary based on your framerate. In other cases, your physics can go completely insane (you can super jump for example) if your framerate drastically changes during the start of a jump.For more minor issues, the quality control of the game is almost zero, and the polish is all over the place. Some things were very clearly high effort, but others seem almost dire in the laziness.The game has horrible optimization, which seems to mostly be rooted in the developer's misunderstanding or lack of knowledge about rendering.These are all things that can be improved, and I hope that ends up being the case. I would not suggest purchasing this game if these things will bother you. Otherwise, it's an alright platformer. We need more platformers these days, so I am going to go ahead and give it a thumbs up

_childDocuments_.review: - I want to like this game, I am a huge fan of this genre of game and usually don't have a high standards for these types of games, but I can't really recommend this one, maybe if it was on sale for cheap.- The controls are OK, I enjoy that you already have everything unlocked to get around and collect everything right from the beginning of the game.- The levels are too big and don't really have anything in them to explore, just random collectibles scattered throughout. The developer made the smart choice to add a button to point you toward collectibles that are easy to miss though.- There are different frame rates between the items in the world compared to the main character that just look bad.- All the enemies just do a straight line straight to you, your attack isn't long enough to hit some enemies without taking a hit. Also, slight spoiler but I was just able to stand on a pillar and avoid the final boss for the whole timer in the battle as they just kept running into the wall to get to me.- I really enjoyed the first level and then I felt like the rest of the levels went downhill in quality. The final two levels did get interesting and fun again.- Overall, this game isn't that fun, but I will be excited to try more games from the developer. I think its worth a try if you are a big fan of the genre, or if there are future patches that fix a lot of the issues.

_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: It's far from perfect - very janky and unpolished, but I can't deny that the heart is there and it's pure. It does accomplish what it sets out to do for the most part. Very much a callback to N64 Rareware games, both with the good parts (the charm) and the not-so-good parts (the camera). Clive is pretty fun to control except in water, where he inherits Banjo Kazooie's swimming controls. He otherwise feels fast, jumpy and acrobatic with decent feedback to his movements. The level designs are a mixed bag, with some creative ideas but unpolished implementation. The graphics of these levels are likewise mixed, with some good artistic concepts marred by bad texturing or lighting. It could use some debugging but I don't think it's ultimately bad. Still has loads of charm and fun moments. Pick it up on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant 3D Collectathon Platformer with great movement controls, good characters/character designs, and some nice music. Really appreciate having all movement options available from the get go, it really made traversal fun and made it so no backtracking was necessary if I was vigilant when exploring the levels. The amount of detail in many of the levels is also really nice. Combat was usually fine with some exceptions when trying to hit enemies while at a slightly higher elevation to them, as well as some inescapable rapid hit combos from a couple of the bosses (these issues will likely be patched). The game also looks really nice. In-game models and textures look great. Cutscene models. however, did look a little off at times. I think it was likely the fur added for detail on the cutscene models was clipping with itself when characters mouth were opening and closing, causing strange creases to appear. Some aliasing was also present in some shots of the opening cinematic. This probably won't bother most people, but it was something I kept noticing. Spontaneous pop-in was also an occasional occurrence during gameplay.I would say that if you enjoy the genre, Clive N' Wrench is worth a try, assuming your okay with a little jankiness. When the previously mentioned glitches are resolved, I would definitely recommend the game to anyone that enjoys 3D platforms.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m mostly reviewing because I can see there are quite a lot of negative reviews and that doesn’t match my experience. I got it in a Fanatical bundle for about eight bucks, so that probably influences my value for money perception, but I found this to be a slightly rough, but very enjoyable and addictive little collectathon, the sort of thing that you might play when you’re after something like Spyro. I started it for a quick playability check (steam deck playability is listed as unknown) and looked up and nearly an hour had passed. The intro is done in cartoon-style mimes and the tutorial is in pictograms, so I went in with only a vague idea of the goal (although I did get that the world goes boom if we don’t prevail), but there are further information drops as you go about gameplay, and the mechanics themselves are varied and pretty smooth once you settle into it. There’s a vaguely demented humour feel to it, the sort of thing that might be really hysterical to play stoned or drunk. I think this does need a bit of tolerance for being a one-dev indie title, but the rough elements were really just relatively forgivable things like the odd bad camera angle, there was nothing that seriously reduced playing enjoyment for me personally. I couch-played with the Steam Deck, docked, with an XBox controller, and had no issues. It’s probably overpriced at full price just because it’s missing that final polish, but if you can pick it up on sale, it’s worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very hard game to "not recommend". I flip flopped multiple times but there are enough negatives that I could justify my choice. First of all, this game has a lot of charm and detail. The level themes are fantastic and there are a lot of them.  Sadly, the game revolve too much around just collecting items laying around instead of solving puzzles. I'm halfway through the game (and likely done at this point) and I only recall two puzzles. There aren't any challenges that require you to learn new moves. You have them all from the start. I fear I am just too bored to continue.Attacking enemies is kinda janky and its common to both kill your enemy and take damage at the same time. With no  iframes, its common to be hit multiple time by an enemy in a short amount of time. This isn't that big of a deal because the game difficulty is quite easy.The game more closely resembles a Gex or Spyro rather than a Banjo Kazooie. There's a reason I couldn't get through Spyro 1 either when playing the remaster. I'd only recommend this to superfans of the genre or when the price comes down.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: Clive and Wrench is what seems to be a passion project trying to sell itself past it's competitors but failing to give a justifiable reason for its increased pricing point. This game I got on sale for 15 dollars, and that seems like it should have been it's base price. At least. I say "at least" because it might sell even better under 10 dollars. But 30 dollars will turn off a lot of the market, which I think has reflected in the reception as well.I enjoyed playing through this overall, but there is a lot of weird bugs ranging from annoying to almost game breaking. This is coming from someone who considers himself to be very/abnormally good at 3D platformers, and is actually working on one right now. (Not relevant i know lol, but I can see and understand the development process. This is also my personal account, not my dev account)The game is functional so that isn't a problem for me.The opening cutscenes when you start the game are way too long and immediately disengage the player from any immersion. Even if you skip all the cutscenes there is a considerable amount of wait-time between you starting the game, and actually being able to move your character. I would have made it play once, and optionally added it in some "archive" where you can revisit cutscenes (unless that's already done)The character models have some weird design choices, specifically referring to the weird way the low-res-fur is applied to the models, making it look unpolished. I'd much rather have that toon-ish cleaner look that's shown in the cover art.Also I don't like the character design of Dr Daucus. He looks really weird and his head is very deformed especially compared to Clive who is presumably the same species. (I know 3D platformers exaggerate the characters, but I still don't like his design nonetheless) I don't want to hate Dr Daucus solely because the design is bad/weird/ugly, I want to see more of his motivations that turned him into the "power seeking control freak" he is now. Maybe how he was treated contributed to his motivations? Not just "stop/kill the weird-looking person who wants to take over the world for no apparent reason", because there is quite literally 0 backstory behind why this is even happening. The weird imps also look really... weird, and is quite similar to yooka laylees interpretation and integration which is a one hit kill (glad its not more). Still I don't find that very engaging and i'm incentivized to ignore or avoid it because i don't get anything most of the time. In contrast I really like the character design of Vlad The Impala, Arnis Mantis, Cerratopple, and Cybro the Dragon. Everything else I cant find really recognizable (even Clive to some extent feels not too recognizable), and this might have to also be because there's so many worlds and characters that the player breezes through only to fight a boss one time and move on.Talking about Clive specifically. He isn't really recognizable because I don't really understand what he is supposed to be. Even classic Mario ("Jump-Man"), who was meant to be indistinguishable was a plumber and the game features a lot of pipes that he traverses through. Is clive supposed to be a hero, or a "1950 refrigerator time traveler"? or both? I really don't understand any of his motivations, and while I know the games story and clive doesen't exactly take itself seriously, it makes me unable to take it seriously as well, which makes the characters not memorable in my opinion. While Yooka Laylee also suffers a similar problem, at least Yooka and Laylee express their lack of seriousness through dialogue when they interact with the various NPC's around.Also there isn't a lot of cutscenes that develop the story past the beginning and the end, besides "fight boss and save purple goo from destroying world", so I dont know what the games story is trying to tell me. It might have been better off to just prioritize pure platforming gameplay at that point, but it seems to be more about exploration, which involves a lot of exploring the maps, doing the same fetch quests, and moving on. Theres nothing wrong with the first time its being introduced, but when the same characters are present giving the same tasks, it starts to hinder the experience.In terms of animation, the opening cutscene with the girl rabbit, and Clive and Wrench is way too long and not engaging at all. Its a lot of weird panning with the camera that lasts too long before cutting to the next angle. The ingame dialogue is really annoying, specifically because of the vocals that repeat more than three times and it's not amusing either. It's just annoying, and I would recommend to either have a typewriter effect ambiance (like in Undertale), or full voice lines, or at least don't make that random gibberish repeat more than once. It makes my head want to explode, truthfully.I was almost about to quit the game because of how the mouse and camera force you to look in a certain direction (probably for controllers) I have no idea why this functionality cant be disabled and it hindered my experience greatly in the beginning and I would have left a negative review if I ended there, which sucks because I love 3D platformers.The keybinds were also really weird, and I don't think the game tells me what to do with my keyboard, and only tells game controller users what to press for specific move abilities. Which is very weird to be because i know Unity is meant to be developed on a computer, so computer support would be the most easiest to implement....The graphics are good enough for me but i'd appreciate it if the characters were textured better at least. Also theres some weird culling of objects right in front of you, and tons of Unity warnings talking about some physics not being optimized. The character gameplay animation is also pretty good as well. I'm worried about the cutscene animations a lot more, and THAT needs to be worked on.Overall it feels and looks like something one person would have made in unity in a 10 year development cycle started in 2011. (which is what happened lol) I also started making a game around two years ago, and decided to pause that, and work on another project and I was able to do a lot more more efficiently with all the previous skills/knowledge once I was familiar with the game making process. So I'm sure the developer would have learnt a lot from this to take into account on their next project. Also lower your scope please. A big reason why my newer games are turning out a lot better is because I significantly lowered the amount of content i'm making for it rather than some "grand idea" or "dream game".Looking at how much this game has gone through from its original kickstarter to this final release though is a true testament to how determined the developer is to make this game, and I very much support the developer behind this and wish him good luck with his next projects. The fact that this game has both released under a publisher with console support, and improved to the point where I can forgive the jankiness is more than enough for me, though of course there's always room for improvement. There is also a lot of cool content you can experience if again, you let all the jankiness aside. I'm sure the developer has also had to read a lot of hard reviews, so I wish that he takes it all as a great learning experience, and he should be proud of this for persevering so much. Because I very much care about people who put in effort to make games to make people happy, especially since game development is brutal and not financially viable most of the time. A fresh clean project would be the ideal direction truthfully, which I can currently see a new one is being developed which I am very interested in seeing.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: Before we get started I want to make a disclaimer. Just because I am going to be pointing the issues and major problems with Clive ‘n’ Wrench, I do NOT hold any ill-will towards the indie developer who made this game. The reason is that unless someone has done something bad or immoral, I am always willing to give indie devs the benefit of the doubt as I side with indie devs more than AAA nowadays. Also, much like with my Penny’s Big Breakaway review, I will be leaving out the “Story” segment in this review because most games, especially platformers, don’t need an in-depth story unless it’s an RPG. So, with that being said, let’s get started.Presentation	The presentation is a bit of a mixed bag. Aesthetically, I really enjoyed the environments in the game with my three favorites being the swamp, Christmas ice age, and medieval worlds. In my opinion, I really enjoyed the music in the levels as I think they fit greatly into the worlds you will be playing in. The boss fight soundtrack, while a bit cheesy really sets the mood from time-to-time. However, we need to talk about the textures. I know I said I like the environments aesthetically but when looking at the textures closely, they can look a bit muddy depending on your perspective. Now, we have to talk about the character models. I don’t want to sound harsh here, but they look a bit goofy. What I mean by them being goofy I mean the fur textures and the stiff animation. Now I am going to give the animation a pass since I know the dev was working on this by himself. As someone who loves animation and does digital art and graphic design as a hobby, I should tell you it’s tough and really time-consuming, especially with how expensive it can be. I know this is a minor nitpick but when I look at the 2D promotional artwork for Clive ‘n’ Wrench, I would kill for a cartoon cel-shaded art style. But that is just my personal preference, and I don’t want to discourage the work of Dinosaur Bytes Studios. By the way, this game was made in Unity. I know this because when I booted up the Steam version, I was met with a Unity splash screen showing the logo and the logo “Numbskull  Games,” the game’s publisher. I know this is also a minor nitpick but there really should have been a way to get rid of it.Presentation: 6/10Gameplay	Before talking about the negatives, I want to be pogative. Pogative is a word I completely made up, which is a mixture of both positive and negative. I want to discuss my two favorite enemies, the crocodiles/alligators (I don’t know what they are so feel free to tell me what they are), and anglerfish-looking pirates. I like not only their whacky designs, but also the fact their models will glitch and bug out like they are a Looney Tunes character before dropping dead and glitching through the ground. I know this is a bad thing but it’s pretty funny looking back on it. I hope that gets patched though but only time will tell.	Okay, back to reality. So, like Super Mario 64, Banjo-Kazooie, or Battle for Bikini Bottom, Clive ‘n’ Wrench plays like a 3D collect-a-thon platformer. You jump, double jump, do a spin attack Crash Bandicoot style, swim above and underwater, ground pound, sprint, sprint jump, crouch jump, and use Wrench as a propeller to hover in the air like you’re Rayman or Ratchet and Clank. The swimming in this game is pretty bad. The controls while not too bad don’t really do you any favors. It’ll take time to get used to them, but you better do it quick because Clive and Wrench have some pretty weak lungs as their air will run out faster than Mario or Banjo’s. Okay look, I know people have said the combat in this game is lackluster, but this is not a fighting, beat em’ up, or hack ‘n’ slash game; this is a platforming game, first and foremost. You will fight enemies as you explore but they pose little threat whatsoever as you can just smack them around with Wrench. By the way, when they die, the demon imps will poof away but the level-based enemies. So, I was wrong, this is Banjo-Crash’s Bad Fur Day here.Throughout the game you will be collecting Ancient Stones, this game’s version of Power Stars, Jiggies, and Golden Spatulas. There are 110 in total; not 100 or 120, just 110. Now you might think it’s not a big deal but when you actually play the levels, the stones can be hidden in sometimes obscure or cryptic places. It also doesn’t help that these levels are massive. Yes, you could argue that SM64 and Kazooie had big levels too but here’s the thing, those games struck a good balance between having the collectable challenging, but also fun to obtain. Here, I got so confused by what I was doing wrong, I had to look up a walkthrough in order to even 100% this game. In addition to the stones, you will be collecting stop watches. However, unlike SM64 or Banjo which require 100 coins or music notes, the total stop watches for each world will sometimes range 800-1000. Don’t get me wrong, I love collecting items in games, especially platformers, but there is such a thing as too much. I’m not asking for a whole lot here, but I wish that the devs would trim the amount down to just 100 at the very least.The boss fights in this game, they’re pretty bad. They can sometimes range from awkward, to frustrating, to almost non-existent. Most of the time, you won’t even fight the boss but instead be treated to a running segment or just a plain cutscene. Now I know I hate spoiling games/movies, but I need to call this out. If you have not played this game yet, please exit and go the play the game now so that I don’t ruin the experience for you. As you get to the final boss, there are three phases you have to do with two phases being just normal jumping and dodging. In phase two, however, you are treated to an airplane dog fight in the likes of Star Fox or Sly 3: Honor Among Thieves. The problem, however, is that you are never given a tutorial for this airplane section, and you are forced to see and learn what button does what on the screen. By the way, when you get hit by an enemy or hazard, there are no invincibility frames, so you better pray that you don’t get comboed by hordes of enemies.Right off the bat, this game is littered with bugs and glitches. I hope most of these problems have been ironed out, but I still found myself stuck in Clive’s falling and ground pound animations. If you can overcome these obstacles, more power to you but I’d much rather wait for these issues to be taken care of first.Gameplay: 3/10Performance	When playing on the Steam Deck, the performance was fine for the most part but as you get into the later levels, the framerate will start to dip a bit. While not too bad on PC, it is bad on the Switch and PS4/PS5. By the way, there is pop-in everywhere. What I am assuming happened is that the devs must have used some type code to try and load in every piece of geometry at once but the game for some reason will only load in the assets when you are just a few inches away. The pop-in, while not bad, can be distracting at points. The loading times were not too bad though, only a few seconds.Performance: 6/10Love/Tolerate?	Do you want to know what the saddest part in making this review is? I really wanted to like this game as platformers are what I love the most, next to RPGs. However, due to the bugs and other issues the game has, I was more disappointed than anything else. I hold nothing against the developer who made this. Let me make it clear, making games is hard, really hard. It takes time, learning, and resources. I mean I am learning to make games and I am even struggling learning these things. So, while I will support the dev going forward, I think I’ll stick to playing SM64 or Kazooie for now. Dinosaur Bytes, I wish you the best. I hope to see what other projects you have in store for us. Keep up the good work guys.Tolerate: 15/30Fun Fact: Did you know that Clive made a cameo as a hat for Renata in Frogun?

_childDocuments_.review: A game with flaws, and a lack luster staring duo, that redeems itself in its' fun worlds and game play. For fans of collectathons this game, particularly given its' lower than average price, will not be a difficult sell. It will sit on the shelf right along side of Spyro The Dragon, Ratchet and Clank, and Banjo And Kazooie. However, it will sit right next to another forgotten and poorly written duo of Yookah Lele. Buy this for the game play, the collecting, the cheap laughs, but definitely not for the story or characters.

_childDocuments_.review: It's almost there, so very close to being an amazing collectathon.First off, some positives.It immediately caught my attention as a collectathon with a character duo, time travel plot, very retro inspired level design. Since we don't have Banjo Kazooie and Yooka Laylee is kinda "meh" it's nice to have this option.There's a neat easter egg in the tutorial which felt nice discovering, the first level was completable without feeling too easy or childish, and the variety of level themes is pretty cool.As for the cons, the game does not have configurable controls. You basically need to use a controller to have this game work at all, there's also no camera sensitivity control and it moves very slowly making the game feel sluggish, which a platformer should not be.Controlling Clive feels... floaty? He slips and slides while staying in the air a little too long and it doesn't feel as if you have gravity in your movements. Swimming feels way off, and movement is so imprecise.There's some graphical issues, Clive getting stuck and jittering in one spot, the fur looks really weird in cutscenes.I was hoping that the hats/costumes would be unlockable as well. They showcased them which almost lead me to believe it was customizable but they're tied to the worlds you're in, sort of like Gex but without any commentary or charm?I have a few personal gripes regarding interact-ability on level props, though it's more of a nit-pick, having a bunch of interesting things but unable to interact with them in any fun way. Overall, its kind of fun, but doesn't have much pay off. You collect a bunch of stuff but for no reason other than to progress the plot, it doesn't much give me a reason other than to unlock the next level (transmog would have been neat like Mario Odyssey does it)Maybe I expected more, but its just okay. 4/10 Carrot Cakes

_childDocuments_.review: "10 years in the oven, and the Game still seems to have come out half baked." Edit: This was how I opened my original review, however I neglected the fact that half baked food can still taste amazing! If that's the case, then this game is cookie dough. Would have been nice if it was baked long enough to become actual cookies, but the dough still tasted great! This also isn't a big pile of cookie dough, this is a plate of 11 different flavours of cookie, some better than others. The game prioritises quantity over quality. I usually prefer more polished, shorter games, but I admire Rob for not settling on making a short game, he wanted a 8-10 hour experience, and that's super respectable for a mostly solo dev.   I would say the first 2 levels really didn't set a good precedent. The first level is a homage to Andy's house in Toy Story 2, but it's WAY shorter, the level design is nonsense, and the music sucks. The next level wasn't great either, dark, moody, noisy, and dreary, not a great way to open your cartoony 3D Platforming game. Also both levels were filled with a lot of bugs, with poor performance. This really didn't give me a good first impression after playing for an hour, so I gave the game a bad review. However, after completing the Game, I feel bad I ever wrote that review, because there actually was a lot of really fun levels to explore, and finding all the collectables with the super fun movement mechanics was a blast. I'll go in to more depth below, but I would say if you like 3D Platformers, then this is a decent one at the least. Levels: Mixed bag, but most of them were decent. The Game boasts 11 unique Worlds, each with a classic free roaming stage, and a ""Boss"" stage. The main stages varied, but most of them were decent. The stand outs for me were Egypt, Medieval, Pirate, and China. The "Bosses" on the other hand were super under-whelming, janky, barely functioning, and forgettable. However most of these  stages aren't even bosses, just harder platforming sections. The first one felt like a cool build up to a boss, but then there was no boss, which was very disappointing. That being said these more challenging platforming sections were some of the best in the game. The Greek Maze with the Bull, the Egyptian Pyramid ascent, The Wild West Train, and the Pirate Cove were all really fun, and memorable. The best traditional Boss was probably the final boss. Movement: Pretty damn good honestly. Clive n Wrench have an assortment of moves ripped directly from Rob's favourite 3D Platforming games. Spyro's charge, Mario's long jump, Rayman's hover, and more! You have a variety of different moves at your disposable, and which ones you chose are up to you. You could probably get through the whole game with just the double jump, and hover, but it's more fun to use the charge, and long jump. I wish the game had Mario's triple jump, I think it really would have felt right at home here. Not the best move-set ever, but the duo did feel super fun to control.   Combat: Bad. Really bad. An Enemy will run at you, you'll hit the attack button, the enemy will hurt you without you knowing, and you will kill the enemy at the same time, the enemy will then shoot into the air at 50 mph, then come plummeting back down, and the rag-doll will freak out indefinitely, and dance all over the stage. I just summed up basically every combat encounter you will have in the game. In a well polished game like Spyro, enemies will have a nice death animation, then their bodies will disappear. That would have really helped here (also enemies bodies disappearing probably would have helped with poor performance Rob). I like that enemies have those cartoonish rotating stars above their rag-doll heads, to show they're knocked out, but I wish the rag-doll animations weren't so violent, and broken. The worst part is there is no real impact from enemy attacks, no knockdown animation, no invincibility frames, just Clive's brief "Ah!" sound.  The controller will vibrate when you get hit... but it also vibrates when you hit an enemy, so you really won't even know you lost health unless you look at your health bar. Luckily combat features very little in the game, so it's not a huge issue. Sound: Horrible. Music might be some of the worst music I've heard in a 3D Platforming Game. It was all so loud, brash, and obnoxious. Most of it just felt like a cacophony of noise made by somebody that had no real grasp of musical theory, and just learned how to compose music with software that week! Most of it just felt like random notes thrown together with no real purpose, or melody. The best piece of music was Clive n Wrench's theme. It's not brilliant, but it was memorable at the least. I did like how their theme was played in the sound style of each world, that was probably the best the music ever got. At worst, I actually turned the music off, and listened to better platformer music on YouTube while I played. Sound design is also pretty bad. The main collectable, the pocket watch, has a HORRIBLE pickup sound, which makes picking up hundreds of them feel like a chore on the ears, which is not something I've ever said before. Footsteps were inconsistent, and didn't sound like the terrain it was supposed to be, for example, walking on snow sounds more like walking on wood. Not good.Graphics: Game looks mid, and runs bad. I can accept bad graphics if the game runs well, and I can accept poor performance if the game looks nice, but looking bad, and running bad, is... bad. The game can look good in the moment, the lighting is pretty, the art style is nice, the textures are all adequate, but the models really look a bit too inspired by those classic N64 games. They're very low poly, and some are straight up ugly. Clive n Wrench themselves really should have had nicer models. The animations are also terrible. Cutscenes are super stiff, go on way too long, and overall have the same feel as a first year 3D Animation project. I say that as somebody that spent 2 years studying 3D Animation at college, so I've seen amateur 3D Animation, and this game has it. The in-game animations on the other hand, are all smooth, fluent, springy, and full of life, which is very odd. Feels like 2 completely different animators did the in-game, and cutscene animations, although I don't know if this is the case.   Bugs: There were a lot of bugs. I listed a few in my original review, and yes I encountered a lot more in my entire playthrough. The worst was a ledge grab glitch that left me stuck in midair, with no way out, requiring a complete restart of the stage. This happened to me twice, in 2 different stages. It has since however been patched. There has only been one patch since the time of posting this updated review, it fixed a small handful of bugs, that was about it. I would love to see Rob continue to work on this, patching bugs, listening to feedback, and improving where the game is lacking. Conclusion:I had fun. I didn't 100% the Game, but I did 100% 9/11 of the levels, and beat the final boss. You know what? I had a good time for most of it. Sure some of the bosses were jank, the combat was terrible, the music hurt my ears, the sound design sucked, the graphics could have been better, and the performance should have been better... but most of the levels were designed well, and the controlling Clive n Wrench through them all was super fun, and in a 3D Platforming game, fun levels and movement are the most important parts. It's not a solid recommendation, I would say you should only play this if you love the genre, and this isn't the best place to start. But if you've played the old classics, the new classic, and are looking for something else, or you just want to support a single dev that spent 10 years making his dream game, then give Clive n Wrench a shot. Better to support Rob, than any of the big evil AAA Publishers out there...  Hopefully we can get Clive n Wrench 2 one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review Here: Clive 'N' Wrench is a new 3D platformer that feels like a celebration of the N64/PS1 and GC/PS2 eras respectively. It has a very solid moveset with lots of options and several worlds spanning different time periods. Gameplay and combat are pretty standard for the genre and it's a collectathon through and through. The performance though was not as solid as I would've hoped it would be. Rough framerates, glitches and bugs, multiple softlocks, and other visual issues definitely weighed this down for me. The game doesn't innovate on the genre either so if you're looking for that, you won't find it here and the game doesn't take advantage of the duos moveset as much as I'd like. Still, if you're looking for a more old-school collecthon and you can tolerate some jankiness then you'll still have a good time. It was an up and down experience for me that I recommend to superfans of the genre, collectathons specifically. If you're on the fence on the genre or are a newcomer, there are options that I'd recommend over this one. More is in the video review but I could see that as a start of a series though, and if so, that's pretty exciting!
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: Some of these other reviews baffle me.... does the game have issues? Sure, is it the worse platformer I've ever played in my life, absolutely not. I think sometime people forget that there is a strong distinction between this game could be better, and this game is actively bad. Sure the pole climbing animation is janky and the swimming controls feel sub-par ( you have to swim maybe twice in the whole game) but The worlds are colourful, it was clearly made with love for classic 3D platformers from the 90s, it's oozing from references and nods, the sound effect remind me of banjo-kazooie, the platforming is smooth most of the time, there are pop in issues here and there (especially in the wild west level) and I've ran into a glitch where one level didn't spawn all of the collectibles preventing me from unlocking the secret world but ultimately what truly matters is, is the game fun? Yes, yes it is, and if you like any old school platformer I.E. Mario 64, Banjo-Kazzoie, Spyro, Jack and Daxter, you will probably enjoy this too, It's not the best platformer ever, but it's nowhere near the worst platformer as some of those other reviews would have you believe.And seeing as how this was developed by 1 person for over 10 years I believe the end result is pretty good all things considered
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: A hat in time is $30.Clive & Wrench can be quite fun and enjoyable.But when you set yourself with a similar tag as the king of indie 3D platformers, there is a standard of quality that has to be met.This game does not meet it. It definitely needed more time to cook.If the game simply would have been overcooked otherwise, then the game should be significantly lower in price, at most $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Clive 'N' Wrench

_childDocuments_.review: This game is up there with a hat in time as one of the best modern 3D platformers out there IF the countless bugs and optimization got fixed. For a passion project that was worked on for 10 years to come out in THIS STATE is pathetic. right now it has inconsistent framerates, the animations bug out constantly, crashes, the game uses up way more resources than it should for a game that looks like a PS2 game, sound bugs, etc. I overall do recommend this game right now if you love 3D platformers even if you're not a fan of the furry aesthetic because the control feels amazing but if you don't LOVE this type of a game? wait for a sale, wait for the countless bugs to get patched out and wait for better optimization.if the bugs were fixed, top 5 modern 3D platformers (there's not alot these days)

_childDocuments_.review: game is pretty cursed tbh. my issues are mostly with the fact that the monkey kinda looks like a baby and you shake it around an slam it into things the whole game and that makes me super uncomfortable. Not sure what they were thinking with that one, but that's an early design decision that should have been corrected. also a lot of areas and whatnot feel like gex (derogatory) with outdated references and some of it is real close to being racist if not just really mildly so, but that's what you get when base your areas off countries and stereotypes I guess. cutscenes are trying to be cartoony, but aren't executed super well, lot of tweener frames seem to be visible both too long and not long enough so sometimes it looks like characters friggin teleported, other times you see these cursed model warps attempting cartoon stuff cause they lingered a bit long.as far as the gameplay goes, it's not bad, but it's not super great either. would probably have a higher opinion if collectible requirements weren't as tight as they were. _childDocuments_.review: Clive N Wrench is a fine but otherwise unpolished 3D platform. I have two major criticisms and one is that there were several instances that I found myself having to leave a level because of a bug/glitch as well as other bugs throughout the entire game. Some enemies I would take damage from when I attack them but sometimes I don't which didn't make sense. The combat could be very buggy at times. Mostly minor annoyances but things that delayed my process regardless. The second criticism is even for a collectathon the sheer volume of things to collect was unhinged. There were too many stopwatches and they were placed either randomly or simply unnecessarily throughout each level. The worst ones were the ones in the boss levels where instead of bosses I was more focused on trying to collect all the stopwatches on a single play through which I cannot stress enough that is the last thing I want to worry about in a boss fight. Otherwise the game itself was fun and engaging. The inspirations taken by the 3D platforms that came before it were obvious and utilized well. The open world sandbox levels that I got to explore were the highlight of the game. Although i would have liked them to be more elaborate but in the sense of hidden secrets more so than some of the levels that were way too big and tedious to navigate just to simply find stopwatches. The worlds needed more life in them. Many have only four npc's max which made the worlds feels soulless and sad. They were worlds I didn't want to spend time in as much as find all the collectables and leave as soon as possible. The same goes with the bosses which I was disappointed the ones where you don't fight but instead either complete a platforming gauntlet or simply run. The diverse bosses needed diverse boss fights. The actual gameplay is where the game also shines. The fluid platforming and jumping mechanics were the real star of this game and made expiration a breeze and a joy to do. I could tell a lot of work when into playing other games and learning what they did right and how the platforming mechanics could be improved for this game. Honestly a good game all things considered but definitely needs big improvements. If there is a slim chance for a sequel then again I would recommend lowering the number of collectables to a more reasonable amount and really utilize the environment more. The swimming mechanic was practically useless for the entire game which was disappointing.  I would recommend people play this game but it needs work.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of love went into this game, and you can see that. Once you get used to that, you can still have fun with this game, but it's sad that many won't give it a chance because of that. There is a lot of potential, and I hope they release another patch, remaster/remake the game or perfect their good basis in a sequel. I haven't finished the game yet, but from the few hours I've played, I'd definitely recommend it to genre fans.

_childDocuments_.review: While Clive 'N' Wrench is ostensibly a send-up to classic 3D platformers and collectathons, it doesn't entirely stick the landing for the tricks it's trying to perform. The graphics and character designs aren't exactly great, the animation is subpar, the controls are quite clunky, and the game is overall pretty buggy, yet I would still recommend checking this out if you're a fan of games like Jak and Daxter and Yooka-Laylee. Despite its flaws, the ideas are here for a great game. It just seems as though the developers fall short of the technical prowess needed to really knock it out of the park so what you end up with is a clear, albeit amateur, attempt at keeping the collectathon genre alive from people that have an obvious love and appreciation for it.The one standout here is the variety of worlds. Though bordering on cliché, I did find them to be very charming. For me, the environments of a collectathon are one of its most important aspects, so the competency for which they are made here is the game's only real saving grace. They aren't exactly designed well in that the items are haphazardly placed all throughout the levels, but I did enjoy exploring them and often looked forward to seeing what came next.At the end of the day, it's not a great game, but it's not terrible either. If you're a big fan of older collectathons, there's a lot to be charmed by here, but don't go into this expecting it to be on par with its genre peers.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a solid mix of many great platformers from the 90's and 00's. It's not going to blow anybody's mind, but it's good for scratching a run-and-jump/nostalgia itch. It's laid out more like Banjo-Kazooie, Sypro, or Vexx being world based, not as much Super Mario or Hat in Time being episode based. Exploration and collecting feels easy enough with the huge range of motion you can achieve, I 100%'d every level as I encountered them. Turning 180 on the spot and jumping yields a faster, higher jump than crouch jumping, and it plus the glide trivializes almost all the verticality if you can pull it off reliably. Moving on the ground feels very responsive and consistent, except for hitting enemies which seemed I would take damage from imps anyway half the time.There are a few 'quest' like puzzles, but overall not very much interaction with the world. Some levels have a few switches to open doors, but most Ancient Coins (this game's "stars") are just laying around to be picked up. You start with a radar to detect the many stopwatches (Which says there are 10,000 but I maxed every stage and it says I have 9278?), so no need to worry about missing a few if you want to find them later.World 'Bosses' are (usually) an interesting platforming challenge, but none of them really felt very connected to anything. The final boss,The framerate drops in a few places, though the only place it was really bad was in the frog boss fight. Fortunately it's one of the easier boss fights, but it was a shame because I like the theme. The camera turn speed is very slow, though you can snap it behind you with Right Trigger/R2.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say its fairly mediocre. Games like Hat in Time have really spoiled us showing us what modern games in this Genre can be. This feels like an early 2000s game but then that does a disservice to games like psychonauts and battle for bikini bottom both which are vastly superior to this as well.-Graphics are OK but there is occasional pop-in and flickering textures. -There is no character upgrades or skills to unlock etc so no sense of progression. -The game has a level hub but you have to complete the levels in fixed order anyway so while its nice it may as well have been a menu. Bizarrely even though the game is linear in that sense, the boss difficulty is not. -Like other reviews have mentioned swimming is an absolute chore. -Like other reviews have mentioned there is some weird frame rate mismatches going on with certain things. Like if your climbing a pole in the game your character is super blurry. I didn't think the issue would bother me when I read about it but it turned out to be quite distracting. - The movement is something I see the game get a lot of credit for and while it can be fluid there is some annoyances. The edge/ledge grab in particular seems wildly inconsistent, your figuratively always on the edge yourself wondering whether the character will actually grab on or not. Also the jump sometimes behaves a bit erratic, like if you are landing near the edge then it can sometimes bounce you upwards almost like a double jump. Also in certain situations the camera can be complete obstructed so you can't see where your character is or where they are jumping to. The Xbox controller controls are strange in that when your in the air you press X to swing your monkey companion, but when your on the ground you press B to swing him. Why use two different buttons, the X button was not being used for anything else. I'm constantly pressing the wrong button.- Level design is another area given praise and while the areas all look pleasant enough there is not really much going on in terms of mystery, puzzles, unlocking secret areas, shortcuts etc. One mechanic of the level is finding a scroll to give to an NPC and in at least one particular case the scroll was just directly opposite the NPC. Its all fairly basic stuff.With all that said overall I'm still enjoying it enough to give it a thumbs up. I guess it has a certain nostalgic charm and Its quite easy to play so its a nice chill experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start of by saying I've always been a big fan of the platformer/collectathon genre and I had fun playing it.I was very exited for the full release of Clive 'N' Wrench. I had even played a demo beta release a while ago through Patreon and it was pretty fun. Albeit there were some weird visual and also movement issues BUT I still had high hopes because it was a demo after all, and I could see there was still room for improvement and it had a lot of potential.That said, I think I could still say the same for the actual release sadly. The visuals did improve on most things, but the movement/controls are the one thing my mind just kept going back to. I can't get over how badly it feels to move around in this game. To put it short, its just janky.I also experienced an issue where I was going through a world and had 599/600 items collected but it glitched out and it said "World 100% Completed". I was afraid I was going to have to start a new save file to get an actual 100% game completion, but luckily there was another glitch I ended up exploiting where there is a collectible that can be duped.One last thing of note to add, I do like a good few references here and there, but not everywhere as this game has a plethora of them.TLDR; if you like platformer/collectathon games BUT don't mind glitches/bugs, jankiness and a bazillion references, then you should give Clive 'N' Wrench a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Clive n Wrench is a delightful experience, i'm a big fan of 3d platformers (it's my favorite genre of game) and I had a blast with this one. I think overall the controls are nice, the worlds are all fun, and the passion for this game's creation is incredible. It's made by mostly Rob Wass and took a decade to complete and their love of the genre of 3d platformers is very apparent through the game. The game is not without it's faults; the camera clips through walls, the controls and terrain can be a bit wonky at times, and enemies can spawn in odd locations, but! I cannot hate Clive n Wrench for these small things, I have had more fun with this game than other higher budget 3d platformers and I hope that Rob will continue to create fun experiences such as Clive n Wrench in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and I didn't expect to enjoy it as much as I did. I loved my time with the game and was actually a bit sad that it was over. I got a bit worried when I saw the reviews and thought I'd have just an okay time with the game and move on, never been more glad to be wrong.The game has 11 worlds, and which increasingly got me more invested into the game. Each world is extremely unique in both setting and gameplay. Some worlds are smaller/more linear, while some are more open or have more interiors. This variety extends into each of the game's boss fights, where no two boss fights in the game are the same. There's your traditional platformer boss fights, there's some obstacle course stages in place of boss fights, there's some other ways the game handles boss fights that I really like that I won't spoil.The game's a lot more of a Spyro-like than a Banjo-like, with more of an emphasis on exploration and collecting than unlocking new powers throughout the game. The main collectibles are stop watches, which are very similar to the gems in the Spyro games, with different colours representing different denomination. While the gameplay structure is a lot like Spyro, Clive 'N' Wrench move a lot like Banjo or Mario (with a bit of jank), which allows for a lot of verticality, which made the platforming in specific levels extra fun. Combine that with the ability to traverse large distances really quickly, and you've got a pretty great moveset to play with.I did this playthrough on PC on Ultra (surprised my laptop could handle it!), and I thought the game looked great. Each world has its distinct feel and is fully realised. The pirate world is appropriately piratey, the Egyptian level is Egyptiany. I also loved that both Clive and Wrench had unique costumes for each world. The soundtrack for each world is also very theme-appropriate, with some tracks that I'll definitely be listening to even after I've stopped playing the game.One of my favourite things about the game is the attention to detail. The game is just packed with little things that really do add up. There's a lot of references to popular games of yore, but not in an in-your-face way where it drags down the experience. The game also has an entire book's worth of puns in it. A lot of the objects in the environments can be interacted with (e.g. gongs, snowmen, bottles etc.). I had way too much fun knocking around random things within levels, and the fact that I could do the same with enemies after I knocked them out added at least an extra hour of gameplay for me.Now a lot of the reviews mention technical issues and jank, and I did experience my fair share of jank in my playthrough, but nothing near as much as I expected. There is a chance that my brain just got used to the jank in the game, but the more I spent time with the game the fewer issues I had with it. There is the occasional indie game quirk, with things like the camera speed, the way dialogue is handled (either wait for the dialogue to fill out or skip it), the one second loading screen after beating a boss before the cutscene starts, random enemies floating mid-air and falling when they detect you, but other than those, I really didn't run into that many issues. The biggest bug I encountered was half an hour into the game where I was stuck in "ledge grab" state and had to restart the level, but that just happened the one time.Again, I had a lovely time with the game and really hope the reviews don't negatively affect the sales too much. This game deserves to do well, especially with how much time has been put into it. I hope the technical issues get ironed out and that the general consensus isn't as mixed as it feels right now. It's a true homage to the PS2 classics, I just hope it doesn't suffer the same fate as they did. There's a lot of potential with the game, and a sequel that improves on the game's weaknesses would be an instant classic for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is lots of fun and is a must play for any collectathon fans imo. The worlds look great, sound great and are fun to explore. Enemy variety is pretty good, but they don't function well (I'll get into that later). The boss fights / levels are neat and can be fun when things function correctly, but most of the time they don't (again, gonna talk about the issues below). There are 10 main collectables per world, a TON of mini collectables scattered throughout (like notes in banjo-kazooie) and some easter eggs to find. With 11(?) worlds to explore, 100+ main collectable items and 10,000 of the mini collectables, there's a ton to do in this game. Graphically, It looks real good in some areas but in others it just looks bad. Overall though, I feel like if you're into 3D platformers  you should give this a go now or wait for potential future updates if you can.So there are a lot of issues with this game. Hitboxes that make no sense, a ledge grab glitch that can softlock you and ruin your progress for the save 5 animals type quests plus having to reopen every door. Enemies also feel very weird to hit, as they don't get knocked back so you can get hit unless you run away straight after. Not satisfying at all and makes no sense for them to keep walking to you unaffected. Very bad performance issues. I play on an RTX 3080, Ryzen 3800x, 16gb ram and I had fps dips (bad ones) while playing at 1080p. Cutscenes feel unfinished. They'll end abruptly or go on for too long. The mumble voices activate when talking to an npc and can either stop, reset or keep going depending on when you exit the dialogue and it's very buggy. Plus, it doesn't sound very good. The repetitive lines like "CLIVE" or the humming when you exit to the hub get annoying fast. Speaking of the hub, there is no way to view your totals per world, even in the hub. There is also no way to get to the boss of a world without exiting to the hub, re-entering the world's area in the hub and entering the boss fight. I feel like this would be an easy fix if you could "exit area" and spawn right outside of the world you entered. This would make boss re-fights feel less tedious when achievement hunting.I know that's a lot of complaints for a game I recommend, but I feel like if they were fixed this would be a GREAT game. Hopefully they update it.

_childDocuments_.review:
One fateful morning Professor Nancy Merricarp wakes to find that her proudly displayed time travel blueprints have been nabbed by the downright evil Dr Daucus! Luckily Nancy's cousin, Clive and her apprentice Wrench are there to help pursue the wicked doctor and put an end to his horrid plans! But to do this they must travel through time themselves!

Clive 'N' Wrench is a 3D platformer starring Clive, a rabbit, and Wrench, the literal monkey on his back. Your adventure takes you hurtling through time and space in a 1950's refrigerator on a heroic quest to thwart the tyrannical Dr Daucus and stop his evil plans.

name: Black Legend
detailed_description: MORE FROM WARCAVE About the Game Lead a squadron of Mercenaries into the accursed city of Grant to aid a struggling resistance against a deadly cult of fanatics. Explore deep into the city to eradicate a madness inflicting fog that shrouds the streets in this thrilling alternate history Turn-Based Strategy RPG! Main Features: Explore the ruined streets of Grant, a 17th century city based on the architecture of the Low Countries of Northwestern Europe. Search every corner to discover hidden sidequests, treasure troves, and recruitable characters. Fight using an alchemy system based on the old concept of Humorism. Master the four different instabilities and combine them with Catalyst Attacks to deal massive damage to enemies! Be warned, your foes will do the same to you. Unlock 15 playable classes , each with unique abilities and equipment. Master and combine class abilities to become the ultimate liberator of Grant. Approach battles on your own terms using free exploration before diving into tactical turn-based combat . Build and customize your team using cross class abilities and discovered equipment. Aid the resistance in their struggle against the Mephistian Cultists and battle beasts pulled from regional folklore. Uncover the history of Mephisto , a menacing Alchemist who brewed the maddening fog clouding the city. Choose Your Difficulty : For those who wish to see the story, the path can be gentle. For those who wish for difficulty, even the slightest mistake will be greatly punished. We await our liberation at your hands, stranger. Grant us our wish!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED WARNING: Encountered a game-breaking bug after about 6 hours of gameplay that required me to load a MUCH earlier save and redo about an hour and a half to get back to that point without issues.First impressions: Disappointing and sloppy. Not worth $30. Some aspects seem rushed and not fully finished. I really wanted to like this but ultimately, it feels like a chore to play.One thing that is a huge plus: the ai plays by the same rules you do. The ai does NOT cheat! Finally a game where the ai is not given unfair advantages!!!It feels like a modded version of mordheim. Better or worse in some aspects. Much more forgiving though.I've completed the tutorial and the graphics, sounds, and style of the game is very familiar and nice. I was able to (kind of) customize my main character and I have been looting everything in sight to get some items and equipment. Update: I've continued playing and it seems like battle after battle and the quests are mostly fetch quests and just go here and hit a button and repeat.The combat is another story. It feels VERY strange and the AI is pretty odd... I had an enemy move back and forth between 2 tiles several times and then finally use an ability. The movement in combat feels a little clunky as well and it seems strange having absolutely no reaction attacks of opportunity for moving, so constantly, every single turn, it is you and the enemy repositioning for flanking attacks and just feels odd. Battles are not done well in my opinion. You can also not attack with melee diagonally, so it results in being DIRECTLY next to an opponent and being able to do absolutely nothing to them very often.Grenades do like less than 10 damage. Characters have a base stat for health around 100 and you can get up to like 300 after a couple hours of gameplay. Enemies also have very high health... Grenades are completely useless.Another thing regarding combat: you can verify this for yourself by watching the store page videos: the enemies only engage you if within their radius which is like about 10 feet away. So you can run around them and they won't even chase or acknowledge you, despite them having a clear line of sight with you just down the street. That's not stealth, that's just odd.The alchemy system in combat with humours is cool in theory but honestly kind of poorly executed. It seems like combat is just dominated by playing a "match the colors" game and it's repetitive and honestly bland it seems like they were so infatuated with their own idea that the overuse of some wording and abilities became a little unbearable... You cannot move through your own units, so my characters often will have a visible 3-5 foot wide gap between them, yet my character cannot slip through so the turn is completely wasted unless I want them to do acrobatics and jump up on some debris first and then move forward 1 tile.Regular movement is weird and you can run up on top of barrels and boxes randomly and it ruins immersion.Enemies respawn every time you switch zones so you have to fight through the same area many times.Classes are not permanent and you can freely and constantly change classes to any that you've unlocked by finding all of their relevant gear.Characters and enemies have a huge amount of health (even on hard) and take A LOT to die. Even using the humours, alchemy, abilities, etc. To kill one dog, it took a molotov, 1 spear hit, 2 crossbow bolts, a throwing knife, and a sword hit from the back. All of those were guaranteed hits by the way.The interface is a bit hard to understand and not the most user friendly, but I've seen far worse.Some attacks/abilities have NO sounds. Very ruining for immersion.Some of the voice acting is awful, some is good.It took me 20 minutes to figure out how to rotate my characters in combat. It says press "R" but it DIDN"T say to click on them as well.I've encountered a decent amount of bugs in my playtime.Quests are terrible, boring, repetitious, and send you literally running back and forth several times (one quest made me go between 4 areas over 6 times, each time to talk to someone yet again) and it made me totally lose interest.First impressions 4/10 Could have been A LOT better.The developer met my criticisms with passive aggression on the forums when I asked questions about mechanics.No.

_childDocuments_.review: I think when judging this game, it is best to keep expectations in check. This is from an indie developer and not a AAA one so there is a limited amount of time and money that can be put in a project. This naturally means some areas of the game will suffer and I am a bit more lenient regarding it.My thoughts:My first impressions of this game were actually very good. This is because I love the 17th Century period in general and was drawn to the turn based approach of this game. I have also wanted to play some of the classes present here in a game. The atmosphere of this game has been good along with how you can freely run around the city. The animations and designs, although not perfect and could do with some work, are still pretty impressive. I paid full price for the game and do not regret it as I do not find it disappointing or sloppy.I have not experienced any game crashing bugs or issues once during my game play and I believe I am coming up on half way through (insert loads of Cyberpunk flashbacks here).Further, as someone else noted the AI plays the same rules as the player. I have not seen it cheat or appear to have unfair advantages.I think it is unfair to compare this with XCOM. XCOM uses a percentage based hit system (which the developers play with for the lol's) whereas in this game the player will always hit. The amount of damage the player does depends on flanking or backstabbing, the amount of adrenaline built up (crit % chance) and which attribute it uses (Strength, Skill, etc).Combat wise I have been thinking for a few days why others would find it cheap, badly done, sloppy, boring or repetitive. The biggest reasons I can think of are for the first few hours scaling is difficult and neither the player nor the AI has any decent ways to build up humours and may also expect other forms of damage to outdo this system (in real life it may not take much more than a sword swing and pistol at short range). This game is based around building up humours as quickly as possible and then catalysing them to deal massive amounts of damage - note the AI is also trying to do this to the player at the same time. Grenades are based this way as well - not damage but to apply a humour or bleeding/blindness. For example if a tank has to run many squares to hit an opponent then get bleeding on him and let the DOT wear him down, or stop the annoying ranged units from doing so much damage by making them blind, or punishing the AI for grouping up by chucking a fog grenade.It is possible to see enemies (not bosses) before you engage them so I used this as a very simple form of Neverwinter Nights or certain MMO's where Wizards have to prepare their spellbooks before engagement. For example swap some skills out to ensure I can stack a load of certain humours on enemies that go deranged.As you go through the city there are sign posts telling the player where to go so I have never got lost. Repeat enemies or similar scenery makes sense to me and to the lore - it is in a 17th Century town covered with fog not in the middle of Tokyo in 2021 with loads of different districts and changing skyscrapers.Disadvantages:I found a few of the sound effects repetitive yet did not notice the potato chip until I read some posts in the forum and now cannot unhear. Also some of the dogs are silent when hit. Fortunately the latest patch seems to have fixed these.The audio levels of the people the player talks to are quite off putting and have not been tuned to fit in the game. I am not too harsh here because this is an indie game. On the plus side they do give it some emotion so at least it is not the same person monotoning by reading a script into the mic.Scaling is also an issue that I ran into. The first area really is the hardest as the mobs are slightly larger and the player has not levelled enough to cope with it. It really is around 10 hours before more skills can be unlocked and the player starts to get into the swing of it. More work could have been done with the scaling rather than just presenting a cliff and expecting the player to keep up. Then again I am happy with the combat so it must work on some level.Finally:I do not really do scoring or reviews (as is probably apparent). I just felt moved enough to write this. I do not regret playing it and will happily carrying on playing it into New Game +. I am very happy the developers are patching the game rather than leaving it.
