_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, it is one of the funniest puzzle platformers I played in a long time. The platforming part is not too challenging, it is more important to know where and when to jump. Or where to throw your body parts.Bjørn is a Viking boy, but he hates fighting and pillaging. While trying to avoid another brutal fight, he falls to his death and accidently kills a large bear on the way. So he immideately gets the name of Bjørn, the Bear Slayer and goes to Viking Heaven, a place called Valhalla. Valhalla means fighting and killing all day long. For Bjørn this is hell, he would love to go to Viking hell, a calm place called Helheim. Many years after his death, he gets a chance to go to Helheim. Resurrected, he joins a funny guy on his quest to get a sword from Helheim with the promise to stay in Helheim afterwards. Lying around in the forest for a long time, Bjørn's body is decayed and he can throw his limbs (head, arm, leg) around at will, controlling them seperatly and reaching places that are inaccessible to his whole body. He can also reattach his body parts again, as long as he finds them. Or he can combine them in strange ways, like a head with an arm. Most puzzles require you to use your body parts in funny ways. Dying is possible, but you are resurrected a few seconds later. The dialogues come with professionally voice-overs, gamepad is supported, ultrawidescreen as well. The same devs made the game Manual Samuel before, which has the same kind of humor but had some (slightly) difficult action sequences, I never managed to win the final bossfight. Helheim has far more puzzles, but also easier action sequences.Puzzle game with funny conversations, odd characters and some (mostly) easy platforming parts.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ignore the chase sequences and other timed parts of this puzzle game, it's quite alright. If it had not been for the story/humor I would not have kept playing it. The controls make it very annoying at times.You can keep on playing after the game ends to finish up optional puzzles and such but... they're just too frustrating for me.So it's more of a Maybe than a Yes from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I was having a blast with this game. And then the final sequence completely ruined it for me.Why this relaxed, low-impact game suddenly needed to end with a lengthy insta-death abbatoir of absurd timing-window precision platforming is a complete mystery to me, and a wild violation of the contract between developer and player. Pull that nonsense in the first hour if you're going to, so I know to not bother playing your game.Instead they did it at the 98% mark. So I banged my head against it, taking 80-100 tries and watching my affection for the game just wither away and die. By the time I rolled credits I was furiously growling obscenities at my Steam Deck, had completely abandoned the notion of fun, and recognized that the idea of recommending this game to anyone or ever thinking back on it fondly was a laughable farce.Which is a terrible shame. Because up to the final sequence, it was a delight.

_childDocuments_.review: ✿ PROS- funny dialogues and a fun story overall- okay, it's not just the story but the extra things not related to the main game are hilarious too- norse mythology with satan and his gang doing a crossover- odd but unique characters- lots of side quests- you get to be a chill viking who refuses to do what vikings do✿ CONS- puzzles are too easy (not really a con but if you're into a more difficult puzzle, you shouldn't expect that here)✿ RATING: 5/5// wow, this game had me chuckle from start to finish. i don't think i had played a game which made me do that in a while so hats off to the developers of this game. the humor was great and i enjoyed it! this puzzle platformer is quite easy and straightforward (don't pay attention to my no. of hours. i had this game running in the background several times), you might be able to finish it in less than 2 hours if you choose to disregard the side quests. now, the game play isn't bad. you basically have to throw your body parts around and figure out how to solve a puzzle. the game doesn't punish you if you fall, get squished, get caught, or whatever else that can potentially kill you because there's no dying in this game. there are no such thing as "fights" (wink wink) but i enjoyed the mixture of a chase scene while solving puzzles. i wish that there could be more like that out of personal interest but i think the way they did it in this game is quite alright. i was here for the humorous adventure to begin with. so yea, i highly recommend this one if you like a fun story with a chill game mechanic. you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Funny and smart puzzle game where you need to use body parts to solve problems. Too bad the game clearly wasn't tested properly. It's even worse when it happens towards the end of the game; I'm stuck in Huldra's Cave because the devs didn't think of all possibilities and now I can't progress. They didn't even think to include a reset option that would solve most of the broken puzzles! I had a positive experience until I ran into this game-breaking bug. I was even prepared to overlook the fact that you need to move all body parts individually after solving a puzzle in order to join them, or that you need to complete puzzles again if you want to explore for collectibles. Unforgettable!

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle feels like stepping back into a solid 90s puzzle platformer combined with the story, thrill and witty spirit of a LucasArts adventure game!The puzzles are innovative and challenging and can be solved in multiple ways. If you're a demanding puzzle master / completionist, there's also alternative much MUCH harder puzzles to solved as you go!So far the story has been nothing but engaging, constantly introducing hilarious and charming characters that are easy to fall in love with. The pacing of the game is well laid out, and you'll rarely find yourself stuck at one area for too long - making it easy to end one adventure before venturing into the next.Whether you're here looking for a good puzzle platformer, or just came for the story, definitely give this adventure of game a shot, mate

_childDocuments_.review: Before I criticise, I should say I've mostly enjoyed my time playing Helheim Hassle. It's a bit rough in places, the humour doesn't always land, but it's been generally fine. Unfortunately, it's left such an ugly taste in my mouth on reaching the end of the main quest that I can't recommend it. This isn't just because the final boss "battle" is incredibly frustrating (although it is), it's because it's galling to have sunk 15 hours into a game only to discover by looking online that something I did in the first couple of hours was the wrong thing to do (and not just in a "if you do this, the character is a jerk" way) and that I've been locked out of huge parts of the game: Characters I can't meet, places I can't go, and quests that will sit forever in my quest log but cannot be completed. The game's not fun enough to play the entire thing again to get the good experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Wandersong became 75% puzzle-platformer and only 25% action-adventure and adopted the "Who the bleep came up with these annoying puzzles anyway?" style from Trover Saves the Universe. That would be Helheim Hassle.It's a huge step forward from Manual Samuel. The art is very good, the voices are superb. The puzzles revolve around the same main idea, but there is enough variety. The game does puzzles with alternate solutions and different consequences of those solutions better than many of "choices matter" games. Most of the puzzles are fairly easy. It takes about 10 hours to complete the main story and probably as much time to complete all side activities.It has great ambiance and quite a few funny moments and understands how to do a spoof properly. The dialogs are excellent.There are some downsides as well:some puzzles, such as the chase sequences, the snow level and the force fields, become tedious;there's the usual issue where it can be unclear whether you're missing a jump because you're off by a pixel or because the jump is impossible;there is only one key (Down) for the legs. If one leg is attached, Down can't be used to switch to the detached one. If two legs are detached, it's unclear which one Down will switch to;it's not clear in which order Q cycles between limbs;it may be difficult to focus on the correct hotspot when there are several hotspots close together (it's an issue in the snow level in particular). Made worse by the fact that C is used for Look/Talk and also for Unite;selecting a limb and aiming for throwing is rather clumsy.It's all very carefully thought through and the action feedback is great (and a huge amount of work must have gone into implementing all the combinations and making sure none of them break the game logic), but sometimes it's a bit too awkward and cluttered to be a smooth experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls take a while to get used to, but after the initial hassle you'll be good to go. Truly a bizarre title with good puzzles, odd characters and cool ass voice-actors. If you haven't.. you might just have to play that one aswell!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an enjoyable game. My biggest issue is that the controls for throwing weren't thoroughly explained and during the finale become incredibly important. _childDocuments_.review: I was only expecting a decent game, but this is actually a great puzzle platformer with several hours of entertainment and only very minor issues. I loved it. If you enjoy puzzles and/or platformers, this is money well spent.The core game mechanic is original and works really well. It felt the right amount of challenging without being frustrating, and that includes tightly parametrized body parts and combinations that never made me feel like I was fighting the engine instead of the puzzle. There was also plenty of side content, requiring the player to backtrack, but the fast travel mechanic was so snappy and unobtrusive I was never really bored.The humor is great. It took a short while to grow on me at the beginning, because it's so aggressively silly, but once I got into it I really appreciated all the little references. I felt adequately pandered to by the unsubtle mockery of other indie games. Bjorn is an adorable protagonist, and all the other characters were charismatic and/or funny; I was invested in their story. Props to the voice actors; this game has really good, professional voice acting, which is sometimes not the case with the works of smaller studios (and it makes a big difference, at least for me). I like that this game has meaningful choices that affect your progress on a higher level.I don't want to overlook the graphic design. The aesthetic is great, clean and consistent. Bjorn's facial expressions are well synchronized.None of these quibbles should hinder your enjoyment of the game very much (they didn't for me).The in-game menu system could have used some more polish. It annoyed me greatly that whenever I opened it (by pressing 'select'-equivalent on my controller) it never seemed to default to the tab I wanted (which was almost always the map). Quest updates took too long to be marked as 'read' due to an unnecessarily slow fade-in effect. On the other hand, letters didn't have such a system at all, making it confusing to keep track of which ones I had read. They didn't even say which one you'd just picked up!Speaking of the (Balder's) letters, I was very indifferent to these. I appreciate the desire to make your collectibles 'useful', but the letters were a lot of black and white text to read in an otherwise very visual game. The smoothies are a much better idea, even though the descriptions for some of them are vague and I'm not entirely sure what they did for me.Highlighting the body part targetted by merge/pick up but not the currently selected one leads to a lot of confusion when cycling through separated body parts that are next to each other. I wish cycling body parts highlighted them too, in a different way (only until you move).I'm normally not a fan of timed puzzles. I'm *especially* not a fan of timed puzzles in a game that involves complicated disassembling and reassembling of your body requiring the full d-pad, analog stick and three additional buttons. It's hard to do on a deadline, and boy were they tight. Fortunately this mechanic wasn't used often, and was usually optional (Erika). On the other hand, I didn't find the couple of times I was forced to do this nearly as frustrating as other players seem to report.On that subject, I like that the final sequence can be made easier by the choices you made along the game. However, it feels like some of those choices were presented in a dishonest manner--the player doesn't know he has a choice at that moment, and is "tricked" into following the "bad" path (like when you set a certain building on fire, or the importance of petting critters). At first I assumed you could "undo" every accidental bad choice by making amends, and I would have loved if that was the case, but at this time I'm not entirely sure.Which leads to: At the time of writing, I have completed the main story and the vast majority of the side content. But there are a few things for which I just have absolutely no idea where to even begin looking. For example, I still can't see in dark places (I haven't been able to do this other than in the prologue, because Bjorn apparently forgot how to pick up torches when he died). Sure, I could ask in the forum, but I shouldn't have to!Good job. The core of the game is nearly flawless. Any issues with the menus could easily be patched away. I would be happy to buy a sequel or another game made by this studio in the future if the genre and aesthetic are to my liking.

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle is a thumbs-up game for me, but a weak one on that. The game is a quirky puzzle-platformer that is fun and enjoyable to play. Puzzles are well-designed, and most of the time they are challenging without being overbearing, with the exception of any puzzle that requires timing or precision platforming. Plus, the humor is spot-on, injecting laughs into every corner of the game.The progression feels smooth, but the story can get a bit convoluted, leaving you scratching your head for reasons beyond just the puzzles. The main line is already a bit dense, but then the game throws a number of side quests and characters and as soon as they appear, they disappear. It's very confusing. The game is humorous, but too frequently breaks the fourth wall in a way that gets overused quickly. The graphics also lack polish, which might be a turn-off for players expecting a more visually stunning experience.Controls can feel clunky at times, especially during moments requiring precision or timing. This can lead to frustrating deaths or missed opportunities, detracting from the overall enjoyment. You can hardly read the puzzles - sure, I know that a leg+leg combination jumps higher and farther than a full body, but you can't clearly read how much higher or farther, and you never know if you missed jump because you're designed to miss that jump, or if it was because you jumped too soon. For the main story this is hardly an issue, but for optional content this is way too frequent.But despite its flaws, Helheim Hassle delivers where it counts, offering a delightful blend of brain-teasing puzzles and belly laughs. If you can overlook its rough edges, you'll find a charming adventure well worth your time. First playthrough is roughly 7 hours long which is already pretty decent, but if you're going for 100% you can triple that playtime which is not too bad. Not a masterpiece by any stretch of the imagination, but they could have done much worse than this

_childDocuments_.review: Many moons ago the people cried out " Oh woe is me, I wish to experience manual living for a single day, preferably a Tuesday!" They preferred that day for it was after bleak Mondays but before the dreaded Tuesday. "Oh I wish to be responsible for my own breathing but only in a safe, non-reallife threatening way!" They exclaimed, they had managed this in real life but the medical bills were piling up. "We wish for several wacky biblical characters to help flesh out this experience!" they finally added.And so Perf Para presented Manual Samuel , the first part of The Tuesday Trilogy.Oh how the people were enraptured! There were riots in the street and a certain gum chewing horseman had a busy year.But the people cried out once more " Oh how we have enjoyed manually controlling a body, especially on a Tuesday!" They craved more and exclaimed "But we wish more independent control of our limbs, the ability to combine them in different forms that alter how they control and appropriate puzzles to test these abilities!" They also wished to see more " We want to see the rest of the Horseman! We've already seen Hell, how about a new afterlife? How about Helheim!" They finally added.Perf Para once again delivered! This time they presented Helheim Hassle, the second part in The Tuesday Trilogy.

Mostly in an absurd direction, rather than a uncomfortable one. The post-game exploration of the world is also fun with some less obvious usage of your condition as a dismembering viking. But you can have a fun time without worrying much about difficulty for the most part, I did not get stuck on any main quest puzzles.There is some action part though in an otherwise puzzle platformer, but nothing too bad for most people.I recommend and will buy their other games once I'm finished with this one.I do recommend playing with a game controller though, it is more intuitive

_childDocuments_.review: LET ME BE CLEAR I played the entire demo before I got the game, I thought I really would like the game, but to be perfectly honest by the end I was just trying to get to the end because I wanted it to be over and I did not even get to the end, I quit because I just was not having any fun. I was frustrated and tired and just overall unhappy. That being said I want to give a few disclaimers to this statement: 1) I played both the demo and the full game on the keyboard, the game recommends a controller, and maybe that would have changed it for me. 2) I played this while I was laid up sick, I thought a chill little puzzle game would do the trick like it normally does and the folks at Perfectly Paranormal are hilarious! I highly recommend Manual Samuel (with a friend!!! its a rage game on its own.) because it was also a puzzle game that was hilarious and I enjoyed it so much I've beaten it twice! However, this made me feel worse and I don't know if it is because of the aforementioned controller choice or what. The jokes are funny, the characters still have that dry sarcasm I love and it is a well-made game, I would love to see custom controls for the keyboard, I spent half the time playing mixing up my buttons and having to re-do an entire puzzle from the top because I made one tiny mistake or miss click due to the controls feeling clunky. Also, I would love a "summon limbs" button. The fact that at the end of every puzzle, my limbs are everywhere and I have to go through and bring each one back to the main body gets old fast.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent enough game, especially at the price of 1 euro. I didn't actually play 42 hours, perhaps a third of that is more accurate and I experienced everything in the game and collected everything except for getting stuck on the very last quest where you have to "do everything" and not bothering to finish it after trying for a while.Had perhaps one or two laughs and a few smiles. Not sure why people seem to think it's so incredibly funny. Different taste maybe.As a puzzle solving game, it's nothing much to write home about. Kinda fun mechanic where you use your different body parts to reach places but it starts and ends at that, not really fun enough to keep you entertained for the full game. The puzzles aren't that fun and sadly often end up frustrating even if they're not hard, the worst part is that you never know if you CAN actually solve something at any given moment. You often need to unlock more body parts, get the smoothie for night vision and so on. Sometimes you don't even know where the last few items are and they're hidden somewhere on the map that doesn't count as part of the map and might not even show up on the map itself after discovering it, so you might miss some items mysteriously and have to look up guides.The thing that took the most time in this game was trying to figure out how to do stuff, guessing, going back and forth and then realizing that it was simple. Wasted so much time on something that you couldn't do anyway before later in the game. I personally don't enjoy the immense amount of backtracking going on in this game to actually collect things. Simply too much going back and forth.But still, at the price point and decent comedy, it's not too bad. Wouldn't recommend it at more than max 5 euro though.I absolutely hate how some sections suddenly get a spike in difficulty while some are too easy, as if they didn't bother properly balancing things. But the worst thing in the entire game was honestly the feet game with all the damn saws which is more of a side quest or not even a quest at all but like a mini game you can complete for some dialogue and souvenir. The last one is ridiculously difficult. So difficult that I felt like rage quitting, and you can't even get out without finishing it, except maybe exiting the game and reloading, haven't tried that. Minimal marginals where you simply have to die over and over and over again until you learn the patterns by heart and even then it's a matter of some luck if you manage to finish the puzzle as there's little to no room for error. Whoever designed that did it on purpose but honestly it's an extremely bad call even as a side quest/mini game for a gag. It pisses people off that end up stuck trying to complete it, dying 50 times if decently, perhaps 100 or hundreds of times for many if they don't rage quit due to being stuck. I finished it after about 60-70 deaths perhaps. At that point I was so fed up I just walked around a little and gave up on the full completion quest.I would never recommend this at full price. If you can get it for 1-5 euro max, sure, why not, a good time waster and maybe you'll find it more funny that I did.

Graphics- MehSoundtrack- Not too badAudience- Kids or Teenagers Difficulty- Not too difficult overall Story- Okay storyGame time- it's got a decent length to itPrice- Its expensive for what you get6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle is an above average game that has a campaign thats a bit too long and a final boss fight that is brutally difficult due to clumbsy controls not meant for 'fraction of a second' mission critical imputs.The game would have been a low 7/10 (5 being an average game with no bugs but not creative or interesting with mild amusement), as it has an amusing set of stereotypical goofy characters, mostly great voice acting, a fun gimick, and no noticeable bugs or glitches.The problem comes where the game is a little too long and the puzzles get repetitive, even with mid to late game 'new' gimicks it does little to stir up the pot.Problem is, after wanting to wrap up the game, the final 'set' of bosses must be fought without saving.  There are checkpoints but if you quit the game and come back, those checkpoints are erased and you start all over again.  The worst part, the final boss relies less on problem solving, and more on fast twitch reflexes trying to do various puzzles "at speed".  This concept was hinted upon twice previously, and while those two instances gave you a couple extra seconds, the final boss you effectively have to be frame perfect.  Which is annoying when the rest of the game has been very good explaining techniques and mechanics, maybe a bit too much, and now the final boss requires an entirely different set of skills thats got a near vertical learning curve.  There are various bonuses you can get to improve your stats, but they are 100% completion quests for various levels that, until that final point, you never actually need.  And there's nothing suggesting to go back and 'bulk up' to defeat the final boss.With that, I give it a low 4/10 due to a very terrible wet blanket of an impossibly infuriating to beat final boss that sours the mood of what would have been an above average quirky puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and very original game. The puzzles are well constructed, the graphics style is cute, the story is solid, it's a decent length, there's some funny songs... No reason not to recommend it.The one down side for me is that it's often more difficult to *find* the puzzles than to *solve* the puzzles. There's a lot of hidden passages and things and often not much of a clue as to where they are. Sidequests get listed which can be helpful for finding something you haven't done yet, but there's no way to annotate on the map, nor automatic indicators of things you need to revisit, so even if you should know where something is (having been there before) it's often a bit painful to actually get back to the right place.For the main storyline/quest this isn't an issue, so I wouldn't mark it down, but I did want to play more, and eventually got turned off after only about half of the side-quest content due to spending too long revisiting places hoping to notice something I'd missed. I'm sure some people enjoy that sort of experience, but that aspect is not for me.I enjoyed the "puzzle convention" area in which the game makes fun of other popular indie games, but was locked out of half of it by not finding other hidden areas.

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania puzzler from the creators of Manual Samuel (which I knew of but never played). I loved the majority of the game, starting from the opening menu where I was humorously berated for not having a controller plugged in yet. You could probably beat the game in 8 hours or less if you just plow through the main story. However, the side content (which adds a lot to the game) will probably double that. For reference, my 17 hours was done without a guide. This is a strong recommend if you're willing to put up with some optional and rare annoying platforming/action sequences on the road to 100%. Be sure to learn the alphabet.+Pretty unique gameplay mechanic+Great writing and twists on Norse mythology+Laugh-out-loud funny, lots of clever and caustic satire+Great voice acting+Developed characters that I didn't want to leave+Good music+Fast travel+Save anywhere with 3 slots+New mechanics in each area+Lots to do for completionists+Side-content provides immediate and delayed rewards+Can continue playing after beating the game+Some new content after beating game+Items and map to help you find missed secrets+The final bits of unlockable artwork were very nice+Pet all the things, and such a good doggo!+Family-friendly: no cussing, blood, or crude humor. A few references to Satan, but they're certainly not flattering to him.~Switching between body parts can be frustrating~A few spots of tricky platforming, though most are optional~Super Feet People section is intentionally frustrating~Timing on the third race is really tight~One of the cosmetic items is bugged~I think a few achievements are missable?~A number of secrets in the game that no one has solved yet?-Game locked up once when going to main menu-Map navigation is cumbersome and occasionally buggy-The marked point of no return, isn't actually a point of no return. In fact, some activities can only be completed after beating the game. Wish I knew this...wasted a lot of time trying to 100% beforehand.-Chase sequences are terrible, even with the frequent checkpoints. No time to react. You only complete them by dying over and over like a frigging minecart level.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it, its essentially a point an click but a significant amount of the puzzles are based around the premise that you can break-up and reattach body parts in different configurations and move them independently (the trailer basically shows this aspect.)  It reminded me a little bit of that headlander that game from double-fine which had some head-switching mechanics of its own. It also kind of reminded me of stick it to the man/flipping death maybe in the humor department. I will say its easy to get overwhelmed, frustrated and maybe burnt out on the amount of collectibles (letters, chests, berry bushes) and side quests, I was thinking of calling quits after 6-7 hours, but I would suggest just concentrating on progressing the story as much as possible, you can always go back. Obviously grab the ones you can but don't get bogged down. Some of items aren't achievable until you get control of all your body parts and others are locked behind abilities which you get from buying smoothies. Unfortunately it just so happens the currency for the smoothies are the berry bush collectibles themselves so just be aware of that.The only real issue I had with the game is switching control between body parts. It just seemed really finicky for me; sometimes it would highlight the part but not make the switch. Especially problematic when parts were close together or in stages of the qame where quick changes were essential. Consequently Its really difficult then to determine which body part has control and a lot of the time I ended up accidentally moving the wrong part causing me to have to repeat several actions again or start some puzzles over.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome platformer, and this is coming from someone that isn't a fan of platformers.Take on the role of Bjørn, a deceased young viking trying to make his way to Helheim, Viking Hell, because he doesn't want to spend eternity in Valhalla battling other vikings.. or FPS nerds. A thousand years after your death you're resurrected by one of the four horseman for an arbitrary task she can't manage herself, and your adventure begins. But wait, you accidentally have magical powers - disassemble and reassemble your body parts to solve puzzles, find secrets, and make your way through the afterlife.The game feels really solid, there's plenty of playtime and a lot of allusions to Manual Samuel, the first title from this studio, which is also an awesome game. While they're independent, I highly suggest playing both. I never found myself bored - maybe frustrated a handful of times because I couldn't solve a puzzle, but this game is an absolute win. There's also plenty to do after finishing the story if you enjoy platformers and achievements (I watched the stuff I missed on the walkthrough on the because, again, not a huge fan of platformers, but the story and comedy is great).As for replayability, I'll probably revisit this again in a few years. It's going on my favorites list, but there isn't immediate replayability. The game is what it is, you can't pick this up again and expect something fresh, just like a favorite show. First play, though? Refreshing dive back into indie games.Plenty of challenges and a lot of silly writing to enjoy. I can't wait for Perfectly Paranormal's next release. Pick this one up.

Definitely play this.EDIT: I replayed it to get some of the achievements I missed and skipped cutscenes, and in most cases instead of just skipping like most, it adds a small line of dialogue, usually Pesto cutting the scene off and saying they don't have time and Bjorn calling her rude, which was hilarious. _childDocuments_.review: Hello, new hyperfixation! You are just what I needed to get through everything else, my ray of light in this time of darkness!That might sound overdramatic, but in all seriousness this game is excellent. To be honest I was a bit worried that the world of Manual Samuel might have been ditched, so finding out that this takes place in the same universe was a relief! I’d been pretty attached to MS’s characters back when I was into it, and it would seem that Helheim Hassle is continuing Perfectly Paranormal’s trend of introducing characters you can really feel for!The art style is very pleasing to the eye, a smoother and more polished look that still maintains the previous game’s charm. The soundtrack is amazing too, I especially love its usage of leitmotifs that really helps to get more immersed in the characters. This game also has a lot more to do in comparison to MS—while the previous game was short and sweet, the adventure here is quite a bit longer even without the side quests and secrets to find.The gameplay is also a lot of fun, although it does take some getting used to. The puzzles have a fair amount of difficulty that really gets you to use your brain, especially when it comes to uncovering secrets. Although it can be annoying if it takes a while to get through and a character keeps complaining about how much you screw up (looking at you, Mike Cobbles—Bjørn has a name, you know). Some puzzles also require you to be rather quick with your controller to get past the time limit, which of course isn’t for everyone. But the way the game makes you get creative and try out all sorts of unique solutions to get where you want to go can be fun and satisfying.I loved the voice acting too—I can’t think of a single voice that didn’t fit the character it was given to. I know a few people find Pesto’s voice annoying, but I actually found it kind of charming and a good match for the personality she has. I feel like I appreciate the love and care that was put into this game more than anything else, I think that passion is an important thing to put into your work and it’s clear as anything that Helheim Hassle is full of passion!I apologize for the lengthy review, I just love this game so much and I wanted to be able to properly convey that, even though it’s hard for me to find the words I want. Helheim Hassle is wonderful in my opinion, and I’d recommend it to anyone thinking of giving it a go!P.S. Bjørn is my son now

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game, it was an amazing experience with many tongue in cheek moments and interesting puzzles/characters.  With that said that last sequence, both the climb and on rail section, were incredibly rage inducing to the point of almost physical pain.  I had restarted the game to play through again.  I finally did finish the fight, after turning the voices off because it was starting to get on my nerves of hearing the lines yelled at me again and again as I failed the sequence.  Pesto was definetly right when she talked looping dialouge early on. On that note, the game is fun, but quickly spikes from a difficulty of 4 to about 9-10 depending on your choices and reflexes.  I suggest for anyone playing to try and do the "good" actions, berries, and subquests that you can finish first so that you can have as many advantages as possible for the final sequence.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle’s story revolves around BjØrn (who will be referred to as Bjorn for the rest of the review), a Viking with a complete disinterest for battle. After running away from a battle against the giants, Bjorn falls to his death when a bridge collapses. Once he’s done putting his mangled corpse back together, he tries to enter Helheim, a.k.a norse hell, but Is taken to Valhalla on a technicality.Years later Pesto, one of Satan’s underlings, is sent to Helheim to collect her boss’ new sword. Being unable to read norse and thus open the gates of Hel, Pesto stumbles upon Bjorn’s corpse, who she revives as a translator. Being Pesto’s first time resurrecting someone, the spell leaves sequels on Bjorn, whose head pops off and can work without his body. Once the pair manages to open the gate to Helheim, they find that the realm of death is undergoing renovations, meaning everything is littered with puzzles. After some discussion, Bjorn, who hates Valhalla and the constant fighting, manages to convince Pesto to let him help in exchange for staying in Helheim once the ordeal is over.All of the game’s dialogues are filled with quips and jokes, only made better by the fantastic character interactions. Every new introduction to the cast, recurring or not, brings along a new set of dialogues, ready to crack up the players. While the particular set of humor may not be the smartest, it is nonetheless lighthearted and entertaining for anyone but the grumpiest players.That said, it should be mentioned all characters have a shtick, with a few common to all of them. For example, Pesto is unable to pronounce Viking words and makes them up, everyone says belawng instead of belong, etc . These gimmicks are fun for a while, but after the 6 hours the game offers they can get a tad tedious.The game’s graphics have a very nice hand painted style, with pleasant pastel colors that stay constant through the whole adventure. Characters also have very unique designs, even those that belong to a same race or type; it is clear the developers took their time to differentiate every one of them.Sound is also pretty well covered in the game, with a good soundtrack and full voice acting. Said voice acting is really good, with even background characters having their own voice and a great delivery. The soundtrack and SFX, despite overall quality, are pretty quiet though, getting often overshadowed by everything else going on and becoming mostly irrelevant. As one may guess from the introduction, Helheim Hassle is a puzzle game with a core mechanic that could be described as “a very morbid lego”. Due to the reasons mentioned in the Story segment, Bjorn is able to detach all of his limbs and control them at will. These detached limbs can also be combined with each other; a leg and an arm allow for huge jumps while grabbing ledges or stairs, two arms climb faster, a headless body jumps higher, etc. Individual limbs can also be tossed away as long as one arm is still present, allowing for extra long reach.The puzzles themselves start simple enough, accessing a small or high up zone to press a button or pull a lever; but as the game progresses, they start becoming more convoluted. These harder puzzles require specific body parts to activate, be it a head to talk or an arm to tickle. This is even expanded upon with the introduction of specific limb requirements on certain buttons.Sadly the length of the base game doesn’t allow for that much puzzle variety; after the introduction of limb specific triggers the game doesn’t develop, instead it just continues using the existing mechanics. While it is understandable, it still makes the later part of the game become somewhat repetitive. Besides the main mechanics of the game, there are also side quests and hidden collectibles. These collectibles come in various shapes, from berries to letters; there are even cosmetics Bjorn can wear or souvenirs to decorate Bjorn’s house with. The game entices going back to previously visited areas in order to unlock new things and provides the mechanics to make it fun. What’s even more, once the main game is over the player is prompted to go back and finish everything for new rewards.Helheim Hassle is both a fun and funny game with a lot of imaginative puzzles to offer. While these might not be the hardest they are still challenging and require some thought without going too far. Despite currently being unreleased and thus having no price, it wouldn’t be a long stretch to say it’ll be a worthy purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you could go to a place brimming with everything from The goddess of Hip Organic Smoothies, to under-achieving Grim Reapers. Where Odin the Allfather is more interested in his viewer counts on his influencer-channel than anything else. And shallow elves keep body parts and disembodied heads as pets. Where every turn is filled with intricate challenging puzzles. And that this place is loaded with generous amounts of dark and bizzare humor in almost every dialogue.Sounds like fun? Then get this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in my honest opinion, it has been ages since I've played anything so enjoyable and entertaining. The story as far as I've gotten has been silly, funny and it makes you want to progress. The platforming, looking for the (funny) backstory for Helheim in hidden letters and finding berries for power up smoothies makes me want to procrastinate story progression. It's just great, buy it and you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game up until the end. I did not like the last boss section where it was much more about precise controls than the rest of the game. I had to change my method of playing for the last section which was frustrating. It was still a good overall experience the references were great and the puzzles were pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: I will start saying that this is not a kind of game that I usually play, but I was anyway blasted away by the quality of Helheim. The idea is simple but brilliant, in a world twisting in an over-the-top way Vikings myths, and Vikings are blindly running toward their death just to finish in Valhalla, you play as a coward and pacifist Viking. But of course, things will get an unexpected and hilarious turn.The gameplay is quite complex and needs time to master the controls, but it is unique and really rewarding when mastered. Every body-part can be detached and controlled individually, threw away, or combined with other limbs creating abominations that could appear in the Thing. Also, different combinations of limbs have different stats and abilities. A leg-arm hybrid can jump high and grab things, while a two-limbs monstrosity will run fast as hell. This is something not very clear at the beginning but can be learned with practice. The most positive thing about this game is how massive and full of things it is. The first 2 levels are merely a linear introduction but, after that, you will be welcomed in a world full of secrets. Collectables to unlock quest items, to then collect other quest items: the combination of things to do is really insane. The map itself is a very good tool to discover secrets, but the amount of things to do is incredibly huge. Fall in the wrong ground by accident to discover an underground world full of puzzles, while secondary characters and quests are hidden on top of invisible paths. Moreover, every new secret room is also insanely detailed and interesting, so it is also a pleasure to discover. I don't know how long the game is, but judging by the number of secrets it can easily get around 20h.The art-style is really of good quality, same as the voice acting for every single character, with good animation and well-planned cutscenes. The humor is there, and some scenes are genuinely hilarious, while on the other hand, some characters are so annoying that I would strangle them (yes gym singing god I am talking to you!).Anyway if you are looking for a funny and entertaining puzzle adventure with unique mechanics, and an incredible amount of exploration and secrets, this is a game to try.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: i was really vibing with this until a weird cat grim reaper thing showed up and i had to run away and after what felt like 30 attempts it kept catching me. it was not a fun time no matter what i tried or how fast i did it, it would catch up and i'd have to do it again with no option to skip. but previous to that it was plenty of fun . i'm gonna try again later cause i'm a big fan of the story cause I'm really into norse mythology. but if you're smart and good i'd recommend getting this game.so i went back to it and managed to pass that part, and the games still good.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle is a puzzle adventure game dripping with dark humor. Fully voice acted, great visuals, and some unique puzzling come together to make this one a must-play. Using several of your limbs as detachable, mobile entities, this gameplay has never been seen before. Please check out my video for my full feelings on this game.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle is a fun and charming puzzle game where you can detach body limbs to solve puzzles. The artstyle is really nice and the backgrounds are wonderful! It got a interesting cast of characters and the main character Bjørn is really relateable and fun! Soundtrack was done very well and the voice cast is amazing. Clocked in 19 hours without even completing the side quests and unlockables. Absolutely worth the price and I'm happy I got to play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Helheim Hassle

_childDocuments_.review: Helheim Hassle is a narrative adventure game with puzzle platforming elements. Play as Bjørn, a pacifist Viking that can detach and combine limbs at will to solve challenging puzzles and get out of uncomfortable situations involving desperate Norse Gods, Goblins, Dragons, and angry skeletons.

name: Solasta: Crown of the Magister
detailed_description: True to the Tabletop Wizards of the Coast granted Tactical Adventures a license to use the Dungeons and Dragons SRD 5.1 Ruleset , further anchoring our will to make the most faithful video game adaptation with the Tabletop Ruleset and craft the game you are hoping for! Solasta: Crown of the Magister brings back the thrill, tactics, and deep storytelling of tabletop games. As you play, you'll feel yourself reaching for your dice and miniatures. It's time to dive into the world of Solasta. Roll for initiative! About the Game Created and written by lifelong fans of Pen & Paper RPGs, comes Solasta: Crown of the Magister. Bring the authentic Tabletop gaming experience to your PC! Roll for initiative, take attacks of opportunity, manage player location and the verticality of the battle field. Set yourself up for the finishing strike and possibly roll a natural 20 at that key moment of battle.​ In Solasta, you take control of four heroes, each with unique skills that complement one another. Every hero expresses themselves in the adventure, making each action and dialog choice a dynamic part to the story. Players will create their heroes just as they would in a pen-and-paper game by choosing their race, class, personality and rolling for their stats.​ You make the choices, dice decide your destiny. Key Features: An Epic Team Adventure Discover the shattered world of Solasta: explore ruins and dungeons for legendary treasures, learn the truth of an age-old cataclysm - and stop it from happening again. Create your very own party of adventurers with our Character Creation Tool in the classic tabletop RPG tradition. Breathe life into your heroes, and see their personalities reflected in their dialogue. Tailor your squad to your preferred strategy and maximize your party's abilities. The choice is yours. Discover a Mysterious & Dynamic World Delve into long forgotten dungeons to unearth ancient artifacts, but stay watchful of light and darkness: many dangers hide in the dark, but a light can attract monsters. Some enemies have darkvision, some may flee from your torch... Successful adventurers will learn to use it to their advantage. Fight monsters in squad-level, turn-based, tactical combat. Solasta's dynamic environment offers some interesting tactical options. Bridges can collapse, leaving enemies stranded and vulnerable. Walls and columns can be pushed over - on top of your foes, if you do it right. The world is your playground. Prepare to Think in Three Dimensions The dungeons in Solasta are more than flat game-boards. Climb, jump, or fly around obstacles. Evade or surprise foes from above or below. Push them into chasms or drop things on their heads. Position yourself on high grounds to start the fight with an advantage. Size also matters. Escape through narrow passages where bigger enemies won't fit and crawl through tunnels to find secret areas. Take advantage of the environment to find cover suited to your own size. Watch out, though - the monsters are also thinking vertically. Dungeon Maker In Solasta, the adventure does not stop after the campaign is over. Unleash your creativity and craft your own dungeons to play and share with friends with the snap of a finger using the in-game Dungeon Maker! From the room layout, monster composition and treasure the party will find – down to the decoration and lighting of each room or the music track playing – everything is decided by you. Solasta Free Post-Launch Content Updates Level cap increased from level 10 to level 12, unlocking new class features as well as level 6 spells Scars and Facial Paints customization options in character creation Tired of playing through the tutorial? You can now skip it! Rebalanced (harder!) fight at the end of the campaign - prepare for a challenge! Online Multiplayer Co-op is now available: Compatible with both official CotM & Lost Valley campaigns, Primal Calling content as well as Custom Campaigns made with the Dungeon Maker! Spellcasting Chants: Your spellcasters are no longer mute when casting spells, and we’ve added an additional spellcasting animation to boot! (you can turn off chants in the option menu) Crafting Feats: Tired of having to pick specific background in order to craft potions and magic items? We’ve added two feats to solve that problem! Surprise System Overhaul: Now more faithful to the tabletop rules with individual perception checks for each surprised enemy, making fights more even! New Town Exterior & Town Interior Environments for the Dungeon Maker New Campaign Creator Feature, allowing custom dungeons to be bundled together into a campaign with custom monsters, custom NPCs & merchants and custom items! New Quest, Dialog & Custom Loot Table Systems added to the Dungeon Maker, helping creators to make even better and Custom Campaigns!

name: Please, Touch The Artwork
detailed_description: Part of the fun in this game is finding out what the rules of the puzzle are. But there are always hints to help you progress! In essence it's just a calm casual puzzle game where you play with art without shame or punishment. It answers the question: What if you DID touch the artwork? There are 160 paintings to touch (3~4 hours of gameplay) spread over 3 unique games , The 1st game tells the origin story of pure abstract art. It’s a challenging puzzle where you’ll add colors and lines to a canvas to recreate abstract paintings. In the 2nd game you’ll move to a big city, only to be overwhelmed with mixed emotions. You'll be exploring the maze of New York City while collecting words from a poem. In the 3rd game you’ll help Boogie & Woogie, 2 squares who just want to be together, by figuring out how obstacles influence Woogie’s path, in a complex growing society. Three different games in one Simple controls Casual gameplay Fit for ages 13-99 No time-pressure, cozy zen-like Relaxing music Iconic universal art Fun art facts Quotes Lighthearted and bittersweet stories Calm but compelling Hints when stuck Over 160 levels 3~4 hours gameplay
