Help two sweethearts find a path towards each other. Three games in one. Hints when stuck. 160+ paintings, 3~4 hours, set to a chill soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: When an artist is inspired by another artist, beautiful and new things can happen. Please, Touch The Artwork is smart, unique, emotional, and just like it was inspired by Mondrian, I think it will inspire players to develop their own thoughts about paintings, colors, lines and shapes...and art/creation in general.Highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: At some point in your life, you may have seen artwork by Piet Mondrian, or other artwork and designs influenced by his masterpieces, especially from his  series. Developer Thomas Waterzooi used Mondrian’s abstract art repertoire as inspiration and foundation for . What he came up with are three distinct collections of puzzles that are engaging, at times challenging, and wholly enjoyable as a casual game.The puzzles are divided into three galleries, each of which are inspired by Mondrian’s distinct abstract art styles: The Style (named after the Dutch art movement, De Stijl , represented by paintings like ), Boogie Woogie (inspired by  and ), and New York City (named after Mondrian’s 1942 painting). Each gallery also has a narrative theme, which – while completely unnecessary – does provide a bit of incentive for players to complete all the puzzles to see how the stories end.Puzzles in The Style gallery are the main draw, involving filling empty spaces with colours and drawing lines to match the reference patterns. Boogie Woogie gallery puzzles have you sending filled squares (Woogie) along hindered paths to unfilled ones (Boogie). Finally, the New York City gallery features mazes, through which you navigate to collect letters that spell out a poem. The developer had the foresight to include hints for The Style and Boogie Woogie puzzles, of which I took advantage several times near the end.Speaking of foresight, this game also has an accessibility feature to cater to players with colour blindness. It’s also pleasing that there are no time limits to the puzzles, no penalties for taking more turns than the par to find the solutions, and no judgement on your using hints. You can also skip between galleries as you please, should you get stuck, frustrated, or bored with a puzzle.  is truly a casual game that you can start up and drop easily.The creativity of using Mondrian’s artwork as inspiration for the puzzles, and the developer’s full embracement of making a casual, non-penalizing game made  stand out among its peers. Waterzooi did all this without compromising on the difficulty, allowing players to still feel satisfied and proud upon finding the solutions themselves. The ingenuity and accessibility, as well as the fun and challenges the puzzles provide made this game very easy to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Nice soothing/quirky aesthetic, but it started to feel tedious after half an hour. It was too repetitive to provide lots of intrigue and ah-hah moments, but a bit too hard to be shut-your-brain-off relaxing. I think part of it was the lack of a level map; there was no indication whether there was a change coming up, or whether I was going to do 30 more variants on the same puzzle. I can definitely see its value; if nothing else it's similar to sudoku or picross but a heck of a lot more beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, art is touchable! ^^You should definitely give "Please, touch..." a try if you like elegant and chill puzzles. Even when it's brain racking, the game never pressures you. It does an amazing job at making you explore Mondrian's style. Somehow, it manages to make you feel like you're building the paintings, and that's great.It will probably make you want to go to the museum! Be careful, though, cause it's not exactly the same rules there as in the game...
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fun game if you are prone to headaches from flashing lights or lots of movement all at once. I'm chronically ill for the time being and I need something to pass the time, the unnecessary animations in the paintings outside of the pathway you should be controlling are a strain to the eyes. Should be a way to turn off unnecessary animations (rain, black dots). Should also be inclusive to dark mode, I find myself having to take frequent breaks.I wouldn't even call it contemporary nor abstract art, as most of these are spin-offs from Piet Mondrian's pieces and they feel timely to the childish messages that come with them. Writing a story piece-by-piece for characterising shapes is hard, I understand, but the way it was written comes off as silly.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Decent little game, nice style, and fair puzzles. There are three sections to this game, two puzzle games and one which is more a maze with a poem which i did enjoy for the record. If you want to beat everything took me about 5 hours, which a good chunk of that i was distracted texting friends lol. It's a pretty relaxing game too, calming and put me to sleep which was nice actually. 'the style' section is the hardest puzzles and will get your mind working, for me especially one of the mirror puzzles and the ones were the canvas starts blank at the very end, had my head hurting! The other two games are way simpler in comparison but make up for it being just nice little stories and atmosphere. If that all sounds good to you pick it up, if it only sounds mostly good wait for a sale and have fun.I'll give the dev credit, they got me to actually understand and enjoy 'the sytle' and the composition style of painting. before i just thought they where utter nonsense of art and something you had to be fancy enough to understand. So i'll remember the game any time i look at those paintings.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is nice, but the overall game is repetitive & dull. Far too many levels with hardly any change in game play & no change in color options make every level feel the same. This would be best as a mobile game to kill time on a public commute rather than something to actively sit down & focus on.Only buy this if it is on sale for $5 or less (50% off or greater). Not worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I've played it only for a couple of hours, but I can tell that it's a genuine piece of art.I might be a little biased due to actually find the works of Piet Mondrian very interestingUpdate:After finishing the "Boogie Woogie" story and the "New York" one, I am actually a little scared of "The Style", it seems hard after a certain level, but in a good put your brain to work kind of way !
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 3 different kinds of activities (I struggle to call them puzzles) inspired by Mondrian 's paintings.First one is color flipping and it is actually pretty good puzzle.The second one is not much of a puzzle and in the later levels it's more of "guess which one is the right sqare to click".The third one is not a puzzle and it's barely a game. It's... an activity? Basically Snake but with nothing in it.I like how it is made, I like the style of it, I like how it gives life to the paintings life and interprets what we can see. The problem I have is not necessarily that the game is short but that it is somewhat failed to execute on its potential. The latter two activities also seem like an afterthought.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game.Good:3 different kinds of puzzles, so essentially 3 games in one.Interesting plot that makes you think about abstract art as more than splotches of color on canvas.HumorousBad:Very bright colors, might hurt some peoples' eyes.Not a lot of replay value.Meh:Easy to take breaks or complete in one sitting.Simple game play. Two of the games only need the mouse, one requires keyboard.Would definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually 3 games in 1, all in Mondrian style artworks.The Style - The goal in this game is matching the Mondrian artwork on the left.. however the colors fill at the adjacent squares you click and come at a fixed order. You sometimes have to draw the lines too. Every 5 puzzles or so the mechanics slightly change and it’ll get tough in the end. Fortunately you can get free hints.Boogie Woogie - These puzzles are also Mondrian paintings but the goal here is to click the correct sequence of squares to guide them to the correct end point. They follow the yellow tracks but the tracks have all kind of modifiers to steer the square to a different side. Gameplay vaguely similar to chuchu rocket. Fun but sometimes confusing.New York City - The simplest of the 3 games. It’s basically a maze where you have to collect all the letters of the story. It doesn’t change the mechanics quickly enough and therefor it overstayed its welcome a bit. However, it made me get lost in the Mondrian style paintings and probably appreciate them more when I see them in real life again so that’s a win.Overall fun relaxing game which really teases your brain sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the weirdest games I have ever played, but it was fun nonetheless (or because of that). The game is not expensive, so I invite everyone to give it a shot.I know very little about the art style (called 'The Style') which this game is about, but the game seems to suggest that Piet Mondriaan made his famous pieces by applying certain 'rules'. Whether or not these ' rules' are actually idential to the rules (a.k.a. gameplay mechanics) in this game I do not know. For some reason that I do not understand myself, I started to appreciate the finished Mondriaan-style 'paintings' even more when I got a better grasp of the rules by which they were designed.The only frustrating part of the game is that in the second 'game' (which is called 'Boogie Woogie'), there are many puzzle with many 'black blocks' which form pairs of entrances / exits and you have to find out by trial and error which pairs of black blocks are actually connected. And IMHO trial and error that should never be necessary in a good puzzle game. All the other puzzles can be solved by logic alone.Many levels have a helpful hint system in case you get stuck, but unfortunately the final two paintings of the Boogie Woogie game do not have them, and I did not manage to solve them as they are way more difficult than anything you encountered before in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: this piece of entertainment software is a pain in the ass. the puzzles are not rewarding, nor fun, nor challenging and feel like a walking simulator in the worst imaginable way. actually there haven't been any puzzles yet, just clicking four buttons to move through a flat labyrinth. i only played the new york chapter so far but i need to get this off my chest. the visual design literally hurts my eyes and is very hard to look at while playing. it didn't look that bad in the screenshots and i should have tested it earlier in order to request a refund. it is taking me a very long time to progress because the visuals are giving me a migraine. the game is called "please touch the artwork" but there is nothing in it  that resembles an artwork, just ugly patterns and stupid lyrics that try to be poetic and make me cringe. yes, it is trying to emulate the color palette and compositions of piet mondrian, but without any purpose. also, the developer does not give any credit to his source of "inspiration", and i generally despise such behaviour. i will edit this review once i finished the game. i want to give it a chance despite the inconveniences it causes.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda have to say, I really didn't like this one. Please touch the artwork 2 was/is a fabulously relaxing game with no real stress to it with some quirky paintings thrown in for good measure.Please Touch The Artwork 1 fails to deliver on any of this and instead seems to focus on increasingly complex puzzles with no real story line.I do realise that a lot of effort was put into producing this game and thankfully the developer had improved things by the time he got to the second one in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Please, Touch The Artwork is an innovative and creative puzzle game that masterfully combines modern art with engaging gameplay mechanics. The game offers a unique and immersive experience as players interact with famous artworks, solving cleverly designed puzzles while learning about art history.Developer Thomas Waterzooi has successfully crafted an accessible and enjoyable title that caters to both casual players and puzzle enthusiasts. Each of the over 150 puzzles is inspired by a renowned artwork, offering a wide range of challenges that require critical thinking and problem-solving skills.The game's charming visuals and soothing soundtrack create a relaxed atmosphere that complements the engaging puzzles. Please, Touch The Artwork encourages players to appreciate art in a new and interactive way, making it an excellent choice for art lovers and puzzle fans alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I want to recommend but ONLY to support the developer. Please read on and take this review with a HUGE grain of salt. I got it for 5 bucks so there's nothing to complain about. On the other it is heavily flawed in its execution.I wanted to play it for the art aspect and the background information provided about the art movements within. I played the levels in the following order:The StyleNew YorkBoogie WoogieGoing forward there will be spoilers (I guess?)The Style and Boogie Woogie are generally fun puzzle designs, New York is an extremely annoying labyrinth game. The issue is not the gameplay style in general, each leveltype wants to tell a story and they are, for me, hit and miss (but more miss), considering it would likely have been more interesting to just put in information about the artists - but that is subjective and I could see other people liking other things.My main issue comes in the difficulty ramp of the puzzles. For the main part, they are perfectly fine. However, both Boogie Woogie and The Style eventually simply remove control over the puzzle. The Style removes vital HUD parts that you need to figure out the puzzle itself without trial and error, making it impossible to come to a logical conclusion that does not require that.I played The Style first. The last 3 or so levels of it have no more visible lines. You have no way of knowing how to solve the puzzle before figuring out the information you should be provided for it. Slightly annoying, but fine, it's 3 levels.I think my main issue comes with the New York puzzle type. Essentially a labyrinth. Again, the issue is difficulty ramp. Rather than making the labyrinth more complex, it gets harder to navigate as more and more visual distraction is added or the field of view is changed and tremendously lowered. This, to me personally, is not fun, or interesting. Coming off of the New York Gallery I should have taken a break but I figured I'd power through the Boogie Woogie storyline, which was my mistake. I should have taken a step away from the game as I was still annoyed. Overall I think Boogie Woogie is the best designed level group (although The Style is more fun), however it too is not safe of the above issues, but they are much reduced. I think there is only one level that completely depends on trial and error. You have only two tries for a handful of possible solutions before you need to restart and the solution gets reshuffled. Verdict - it's an interesting art experience. But this is not how to make puzzles difficult. As it is not a particularly expensive experience I will still leave it with a recommendation, but know the above factors before going into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Recently there has been a rise in games that are more compilations than single works of creation. Things like the Dread X Collection show that there's a lot of value to be found in a taster menu approach to indie games. It's a trend I've been happy to see, as many genres benefit greatly from brevity (particularly horror) but at the same time need to provide players with enough of a value proposition to justify their purchase.Applying this approach to a puzzle game instead is, on paper, a fantastic idea. There are many concepts and mechanics for puzzlers that are amazing for a little bit but soon become tiresome, so collecting a few of those together and making them an hour each sounds great, but unfortunately, Please, Touch the Artwork fails its premise on a few fronts. Its most grievous sin is making it pretty obvious which puzzle selection (or "gallery", as the game refers to them) was thought of first and making the other two feel like tacked on filler.It's a real shame, because the gallery in question, the De Stijl movement, is great stuff. The levels gradually introduce new mechanics to a simple idea, eventually combining them to produce some surprisingly tricky problems. Your reward for beating a few levels is another factoid about the movement that the game's aesthetic is born of and the artists behind it. Don't get me wrong, it's nothing revolutionary, but in that first hour of gameplay are the seeds for something interesting, a way to make art education truly immersive and involve the player in the creation process that they're studying.Unfortunately, the other two galleries are, not just worse than De Stijl, but actively bad. The Boogie Woogie levels are dull and ugly, the type of puzzles you play on your phone on the toilet paired with a nonsense narrative. The New York gallery is the most insulting though, an overlong selection of mazes that barely qualify as puzzles. While it's better looking than Boogie Woogie, it's a real exercise in wasting your time and I found all goodwill built up by The Style completely burned away before even the halfway point of New York.I'm disappointed, as I think modern art is greatly maligned and something like Please, Touch the Artwork had the potential to recontextualise it in a varied and fun package. While an attempt is made towards this goal, two thirds of the three hour game is dedicated to generic crap. There's definitely something here in this idea, but it's not executed upon half as well as it should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Different types of puzzles lead you through very creative problem solving with a sensible, even poetical touch through the stories and the musical background.Though it is very addictive, it is definitely relaxing, and won't swallow your days entirely, because you want to taste it slowly like good Belgian chocolate.I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: A minimalist package containing 3 small games, wrapped in the presentation of an art exhibition. Two of the games are 2D puzzles, while the third is akin to maze traversal. The games introduce simple mechanics with good pacing to keep things fresh but not overwhelming, and most gameplay elements are introduced simply by playing through the levels, without a need for text explanations or tutorials. A few of the final puzzles of one minigame were challenging, but the rest of the content was approachable and relaxing. The absence of text tutorials frees up the text to tell abstract stories throughout the levels of each respective game. The visual style and sound design are executed upon really well, and with a fairly short runtime of ~3 hours it remains novel throughout. Overall, a fun and relaxing adventure through the presented art gallery, through the lens of small puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: What a nice surprise this "Please Touch the Artwork" is! I was looking for a little puzzle game not too heady and I was spoiledPositive points:- Super chill atmosphere, with minimalist graphics and a very relaxing musical atmosphere. Interacting with the paintings gives the impression of playing small improvised jazz sessions.- The puzzles gradually increase in difficulty, but never become overly frustrating. I was stuck on a puzzle at one point, but after missing it 3 times I had the option to reveal part of the answer.- The presentation and difficulty of the puzzles evolve with the story, which allows for constant variation in moodsNegative points:- I sometimes had trouble understanding the story properly, but that may be because it was meant to be more poetic than plot-driven Conclusion:3 stories of +-1h, each illustrated by a type of puzzle and its variants. Puzzles that are incredibly pleasant to just look at and a music that contributes to an overall relaxing atmosphere. Puzzles without headaches, perfect for a little evening of relaxation.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t give positive reviews just for getting a free game. I also think I should play the full game before giving a review. Full disclosure, I have not played the full game, but lemme tell you bout it, okay?The game surpassed expectation. The story is funny, the graphics are amazing, and the puzzles are clever and fun. I requested this game before a pretty bad night, and was super excited to play it. I spent an hour enjoying but struggling with it on stream before finally giving up and crying and switching games over completely unrelated stuff. I feel I cheated the dev out of a good showcase during the sale, and I’m sorry. I know my community will love it, and several people I saw already wishlisted it. I don’t know when I’m going to be able to get back to it, and I wanted to do whatever I could do boost the game while dealing with some bad IRL stuff. I guess it was too soothing and meditative to distract me from my dramatic issues at the time.I don’t think there’s another game out there like this. They are puzzles, but they also allow us to be artistic. There’s comedy in the narration. The music is incredibly soothing. I’ll update the review when I finish it, but I wanted to encourage everyone to try this game even with an hour of playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: one of those times where I wish steam had a "meh" rating, but here's why I leaned towards negative:honestly felt kinda repetitive. lost its charm quick due to that.if you *really* like artsy-fartsy stuff, you'll probably like this. otherwise I'd pass or grab it on sale, the puzzle half didn't do enough on its own to carry the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. On the one hand, it is a neat little art/puzzle experience and I appreciate the anti-frustration feature added via the hint system. On the other hand, there was one sequence that actually made me motion sick, which is not something that ever really happens to me, and there were some flashing sequences that I know will be trouble for some folks. Also, I spent way more time thinking about horny shapes than I ever expected to with this game...I don't know which hand to put that in, but...  I think if you really enjoy art museums and puzzles, then this game will probably be a big hit for you. It is also not very expensive, is included in bundles, happens to be on sale at the time I'm writing this review for a decent discount, and picking it up does support an indie artist and developer. While I do recommend this game, I will say it probably isn't for everyone. That's ok, though.The folks who do enjoy this sort of quirky experience will really, really enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Please Touch The Artwork offers a refreshing take on interactive entertainment, allowing players to engage with famous artworks in a novel way. While the concept is intriguing and certainly has its merits, there are some areas where the game falls short.Firstly, the visuals are undoubtedly captivating. The artwork comes to life in a vibrant and colorful manner, drawing players into its world with ease. However, there are moments where the graphics feel a bit lacking in polish, detracting from the overall immersion.Similarly, the gameplay mechanics show promise but could use some refinement. While interacting with the artwork is enjoyable, the controls can feel a bit clunky at times, leading to frustration during more intricate tasks. Additionally, the puzzles, while creative, could benefit from clearer instructions to prevent confusion.On the positive side, the soundtrack complements the experience well, adding to the game's atmosphere and providing a sense of immersion. Furthermore, the fact that the game is free is a definite plus, allowing players to experience its unique concept without any financial commitment.In conclusion, Please Touch The Artwork is an ambitious endeavor that showcases the potential of interactive art exploration. While it may have its flaws, particularly in terms of graphics and gameplay mechanics, it offers an enjoyable experience overall. With some tweaks and improvements, it has the potential to truly shine as a standout title in its genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: If you like simple, but clever puzzles that are a bit different than others, you can't really make a mistake with this game (I recommend waiting for sale though because I feel 10€ is a bit much).Making this about real art and weaving a story into the puzzles is a fun approach. I didn't know I'd get so emotionally involved in the love life of a square couple...What I'd criticise about the game is that I feel the balance between the three galleries (the three different puzzle logics with about 40-50 levels each) was a bit off.I'm yet too stupid for the last few levels of The Style (why is the hint button gone?!), while I found New York City was rather tedious than challenging. Boogie Woogie seems to have the best balance for me, and also the most entertaining with fun variations of the puzzle functionalities.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game.I'll play a Triple A game and wonder "Why aren't games fun anymore?" Then a gem like this comes around, and I remember why I fell in love with the medium.On the short side if you calculate dollars-per-hour, but it's a delightful game through every moment. Mind-bending, abstract puzzles; interesting storytelling; atmospheric and soothing. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: It's Magnificent! They used art as a concept for a puzzle game, especially it's about an artist named Piet Mondrian. The game put some of Piet Mondrian's notable art, such as Composition with Red, Blue, and Yellow, Boogie Woogie, The Red Tree etc.But from my experience, the storytelling was fun & lovely (I loved New York City story), the puzzles were challenging but the hints were useful (I can't solve the Boogie Woogie), UI was stunning, and it did give me an education about art.Please, Touch The Artwork 2
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Thomas was a square. Wow. A weird first thought to have. Then it became evening. Then morning. And it was good. Let's take the subway home. GoodbyeWith its three games rolled up into one, "Please, Touch The Artwork" is an odd experience. A joyous one, though, reminiscent of old "Zen" flash games with more polish - in places.Its style of interactive storytelling between short puzzle segments is lovely for a game that doesn't outstay its welcome. And while depending on your puzzling desires and persistence, this one might drag a little; it does let you skip through most, if not all, of the thing you might not enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles in "Please, Touch the Artwork" bring a good diversity from the average puzzle game. You're introduced to 3 different puzzle types- each with its own small story to go along with it. Each story is very immersive without trying to be. While some of the puzzles are a bit challenging (in a good way!), the result from finishing each set is worth the effort. Definitely recommend! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting little puzzler where you explore square ish grids of colors in 3 campaigns. The best campaign in terms of story and gameplay is one where you learn about an artistic style and its evolution through puzzles that get harder or have more elements added as the style shifts. The story melds with the gameplay well and it fits in super well. The two other campaigns are more meh with more abstract stories and less focus on the art. It's hard to get a sense of the story as a whole since each puzzle unlocks a few words or maybe a sentence. The puzzles for these two campaigns weren’t my favorite either. Decent puzzler and decent game. Just temper your expectations a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game divided into 3 parts.The first one is the more interesting and fun, and also the one which teaches you in a fun way about Mondrian.The other parts are stories by the developer, presented in abstract paintings and visuals.It's relaxing and easy as advertised, it has a justifiable amount of content.My only disappointment was about how much we could literally touch the artwork, by the means of some secrets and easter eggs or alternative solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very surprised on how well this game tells the story from just random shapes and lines. All of the puzzles are designed so that the difficulty rises gradually, without any random difficulty spikes. All of the three puzzles types are simple enough that anyone can pick it up and play it, including children. However, the design of the two out of three puzzles can be solved with just brute force.Plus point for the color blind accessibility option!
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like an interactive art gallery, with each set of puzzles serving as art in their own right, on top of the puzzle mechanics and story experience.  The overall experience is relaxing through the use of simple puzzle mechanics (without timers) and enhanced by the simplicity of the visual and sound design.  I have engaged with abstract art for my own art practice, and really appreciated the way this game highlighted this movement, bringing a sense of life and narrative into the geometric paintings of Piet Mondrian.   I found this section to be the highlight of the three puzzle options.  The task here is to recreate paintings inspired by Mondrian’s iconic  paintings using the set moves available to you.  The challenge comes in meeting the par score, but there is no punishment for using more than the required turns.  I found the par number to be helpful as it served as a clue to the order of operations.  The narrative in this section is based on real-world art history, with an entertaining, take on the development of the pure abstract art movement.The second two galleries have a lot of similarity – both seemingly inspired by Mondrian’s   paintings, and narrative being the feature over puzzle elements.  Both these sections utilise complexity in puzzles to reflect the flow of the narratives they portray – low complexity in relaxed moments, and high complexity in tense moments.  These design choices increased my immersion in the story, as I was feeling a similar way to the characters in the moment.  These puzzles have very little challenge, with infinite restarts and backtracking always available to the players within these maze-like art pieces.  The Boogie Woogie gallery has you set squares on a path in the right order to meet their pair, but not block the route for other squares.  The New York Gallery involves traversing increasingly complicated mazes to find letters to write poetry.  These puzzles felt more like exploring and navigational challenges than requiring any heavy logical thinking.This game is short with about an hour of gameplay available from each gallery, depending on how fast you play through them, which allows each experience to be fulfilling, but now overstay its welcome.   I played on launch and ran into a small number of non-game breaking bugs that were updated very quickly in the following days. I enjoyed and appreciated this game as a celebration of abstract art.
_childDocuments_.name: Please, Touch The Artwork

_childDocuments_.review:
What happens when you DO touch the artwork? Part Zen-puzzle, part narrative-adventure, you'll explore the secret world behind iconic abstract paintings through over 160 puzzles spread over 3 unique games. An aesthetic journey to the origins of modern art, set to a soothing jazzy soundtrack. + FUN ART FACTS!

The first game tells the origin story of pure abstract art. It's a challenging puzzle where you'll add colors and lines to a canvas to recreate paintings.

The second game is about Boogie & Woogie, two squares who just want to be together, but a rapidly growing world is making this harder and harder. You'll help Woogie reach Boogie by figuring out how the obstacles influence Woogie's path.

In the third game you'll move to the big city, only to be overwhelmed with mixed emotions. From joy and excitement to feeling homesick and missing your friends and family. You'll be maneuvering through the craziness of the Big Apple while collecting letters to form a poem.

name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town
detailed_description: Willy Morgan is a third-person adventure game , set in a fantasy pirate-themed world with a modern touch. Combining the traditional point-and-click genre gameplay with a unique cartoon 3D graphics, Willy Morgan has the dreamy atmosphere, the humor and the freedom to explore typical of timeless classics such as Monkey Island. The story unfolds through funny dialogues and challenging puzzles. Keen powers of observation, intuition and imagination are going to be needed in order to succeed and ultimately find the truth . Non-linear gameplay – Explore without constraint, collect items and solve brilliant puzzles Unique graphic style – A fanciful deformed world with a magical atmosphere Full HD quality – Cinematographic cutscenes and over 50 locations to see A Pirate world with a modern twist – Pirates and computers...? Well, why not! 15 NPCs to interact with – Learn about the story through several hours of interactive dialogues packed with irony and easter eggs Original soundtrack – More than 2 hours of original music 10 years have passed since the mysterious disappearance of Willy's father, the famous archaeologist Henry Morgan. One day, the postman delivers him a strange letter: “If you receive this letter, it means that something went wrong and it’s up to you to finish what I started. Go as fast as you can to Bone Town, room 09, but don't trust anyone...”

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful game. Willy Morgan is fair to the player; no walk through is needed for experienced players, and it will make a great game for new players due to an optional help feature.This is the devs first game and they really did an excellent job of looking at it from a player’s point of view.  There are no puzzles that you’ve not been given the information to solve.+Art and Animation – Very nice!+Atmosphere – Fun, light, but still engaging+Voice overs – Great!+Story – Pirates, a mysterious disappearance, what else do we need…+Manual saves – ten slots available. Thank you.+Music and soundsMostly Traditional Point and Click.Left click to select something.Right click for information on an object.Spacebar highlights items you can interact with or there is an orange dot in the upper left corner that will highlight items for players.Inventory is located at the bottom, access with the letter “I” or click the mouse wheel.Drop items together in inventory to combineESC Open/close main menuDouble click to zoom to next scene, you can click the speed through the text.it’s a lot more fun to walk around and look at the town and appreciate the art of the game.There are ten manual save slots. Thank you so much. Amazingly, I purchased this the day it was released and had no crashes, no wonky mouse, no stuttering etc; the game ran seamlessly in spite of me alt+tabbing a lot and there was no accumulated memory drag on my machine from doing so.My actual play time, exhausting all dialogues and looking around the town quite a bit was about seven hours.Well done to the team at Imaginarylab!We have a group play with 17 players; nine have completed the game.All had seven to eight hours play time.We have all played Day of the Tentacle, the Monkey Island series, the Lucas and Sierra games this game pays homage to in sneaky ways :-)When you are in a museum do you rush from exhibit to exhibit or leisurely stroll taking it all in?We tend to exhaust all dialogue trees, look at everything, maybe twice Now has controller support! Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It certainly plays in the same league with the best new releases from the genre. It is a classic point and click adventure. Left click to interact, right click to examine. Drag items on hotspots/other items to use. Can't be simpler.You play a boy in his puberty, living alone while his mother is on an expedition in Brasil and his father has disappeared 10 years ago. Suddenly he receives a letter asking for help from his father, telling him to come to a town not very far away. So you search the house for some money and repair your bike to go to Bone Town, where some people seem to be a bit... alarmed when they see you. It is a strange place, like an old Pirate Town. Uncover the secrets of the town, follow the trail left by your father... maybe he is still alive and you can help him.The game is very polished (fully voiced, nice animations, short loading times, no typos, good english...) and has the usual comfort options like double click to exit, SPACE to show all hotspots, save anywhere. No action sequences, no mazes, no dying. There are no built-in hints, but this is only required by cheaters anyway. The difficulty is not too high, since there are only a limited number of items and hotspots. The puzzles aren't too hard either.  Polished and funny point'n click adventure full of references to the old classics.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? My first impression was of Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town was mixed. Whilst the graphics looked appealing to me it, at the same time, seemed slightly childish. Not sure, what to expect of Willy Morgan, I still dived right into the game and decided to give it a try after all. After all, it's a point and click game, so there is not much that could possibly go wrong, right? Anyway, I always loved solving mysteries, although mystery games might be either a hit or a miss. Luckily, my experience with Willy Morgan was rather pleasant, and whilst this game definitely has its flaws, I still managed to enjoy it.Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town opens by introducing the protagonist Willy Morgan. Ten years ago, his father went missing and never returned. However, one day, he receives a letter from his very own father with a task. You see, the letter only briefly mentions that something went wrong, and thus, Willy is supposed to visit Bone Town. However, there are still things at home he has to take care of, although he starts his journey right away. After all, he wants to find out what happened to his father and, more importantly, is looking for him. When arriving at Bone Town, Willy quickly notices that everything seems suspicious and he cannot trust anyone.Admittedly, this is a part I didn't exactly like about Willy Morgan. It's by no means a bad game, however, the playing time is so short that the story feels rushed at some parts and I couldn't relate to the reveal at all. Of course, the development of the plot isn't the main aspect of a point and click game so I could still look over it. Unfortunately, there is no building up to it either but Willy just investigates Bone Town and the game dumps all the reveals at once at the end of the game. On the other hand, I have to admit that I may have expected too much of the story.Regardless, Willy Morgan kept me curious enough so I wanted to find out what happened to Willy's father and implemented one or two aspects I didn't see coming. After all, the game fulfills its purpose and delivered a few entertaining hours to me.Well, admittedly the player has two main locations they can investigate. The first one is the home of Willy whilst the second one is Bone Town. However, while being at home, the player does not get any new insight into the plot but solely prepares their journey. I found that it was a good way to introduce the game, although that means that the development of the plot suffers instead as there is less time available for it.Anyway, gameplay-wise, Willy Morgan works like a typical point and click game where the player investigates various rooms and, along with that, picks up items and combines them to create useful objects or simply use them while advancing with the game.Willy Morgan is a rather linear game where the player has to fulfill a specific task to gain more evidence or create a needed item. Whilst there are multiple tasks available at the same time, the player can only advance with the game when completing them step by step. When reaching a new destination, the player has to go to another location to pick up needed items for the task so this game requires the player to go back and forth quite a lot. Especially as the second location is quite big and contains a lot of areas I spent most of my time there.However, this means that it was easy to get stuck when the player doesn't know what they are supposed to do. While the game is quite straightforward most of the time, it was still a hassle when I didn't know how to advance so I had to try out multiple solutions until one of them worked. However, I didn't have any problems with this aspect most of the time.Unfortunately, I got stuck at one part of the game and couldn't figure out what the solution was. The odd thing here was that I even tried to look up various walkthroughs and guides but the option still didn't pop up for me when I copied their steps, so it was probably a bug. Anyway, this issue appeared close to the end of the game so I just decided to watch the last couple of minutes in a Youtube video instead. Luckily, it seems like this issue didn't happen to everyone, although it still greatly bothered me.This aspect probably isn't very surprising, given that it's a point and click but Willy Morgan implements puzzles. I found that those were very simple and I often read that they were too easy for many players. Anyway, I still think that they're essential as the game adds more interaction to its players this way. However, be warned that they might not necessarily require most players to think outside the box.Something I found utterly useful was the map in Willy Morgan. Especially during investigating the second location, there were way too many areas available. Thus, the map allows the player to fast travel to any previously visited location. On the other hand, this means that I only used the map for traveling and never manually visited any place anymore. Anyway, I easily get lost in games so I am still grateful that this feature got added to the game. After all, no one wants to go through five areas to finally reach the desired one, and then having to walk all the way back.As aforementioned, Willy Morgan implements lovely graphics, considering it's an indie game. The style may seem childish but it's quite charming at the same time. Anyway, I liked the design of each location and, along with that, investigating them. I found that every area was entirely different from each other with some being funky and others being rather dark. In addition to that, the player can experience Bone Town at night, as well as daytime which gave the game a nice touch as well because the town looks rather spooky at night. Unfortunately, only a small part of the town is available during the night, however, investigating might be much more complicated at that time.Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town surely does not appeal to every game lover and doesn't come without its shortcomings, however, it's still a lovely game that offered me a couple of entertaining hours. This game is not a bad game, although it could be better executed if there was more room for the story development. Regardless, the mysteries kept me curious and I wanted to know what happened to his father while I was on guard the whole time as there seems to be more to the mystery as it seems at first. That being said, Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is a charming point and click which will delight any fan of its genre, although the game itself is fairly short.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: The game tries so hard to conform to all the canons of classic adventure games that in some places it even suffers a little from it. A teenager named Willie sets out to find his father, who disappeared many years ago, without even knowing what he will have to face. The plot very skillfully balances between humor and pure adventures, unfolding in a strange town, once the fiefdom of pirates. Of course, this will not do without pirate treasures, ghosts of the past, mysterious messages, maps and an annoying seagull that cannot be scared even by a shot from a ship's cannon. The adventures are developing very vigorously, there is a large number of homages to classic games (and not only), a block of real pirate adventures rises above everything, also mixed with a charming sometimes youth, when a new exciting adventure awaits you around every corner.If we talk about the gameplay component, then everything is fine. Sometimes I even wanted the creators to complicate the gameplay a little, because in some places the game is too straightforward to tell you about your goals. The use of items is very logical and fun, the creators have creatively approached even cleaning the inventory of already unnecessary items. There are a lot of locations in the second act, but it is quite convenient to navigate in them, an understandable mini-map also helps in moving. The dialogues are written wittily, many characters and their actions will definitely make you smile. The design of the locations deserves a separate mention - it is generally made here at a magnificent level, the town has been recreated with surgical precision.«Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town» is an adventure with a bright heart, well-developed in all aspects. Charming main character and supporting characters, lots of humor and adventure, so all aboard!
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little point & click mystery puzzler game.I love the art style- stylized, and very clean- timeless style that ages well.Lots of back and forth, but not too long into the game you will get a map that can be used for fast travel. Some easy and obvious achievements, some missable and very easy to miss. The game isn't long, so playing through a second time to get them isn't bad, or *if* you created saves in the right places you may be able to load older save to go back and pick them up.Some funny easter eggs that give nods to other fairly well known games in a similar genre. Good humor in the game, if you like somewhat dry, sometimes almost cringy teenaged boy humor. (Middle-aged woman here- and I cackled a few times, when the protagonist reminded me of my own son, who was overly serious and a bit nerrdy when he was a teenager. Hell, he's an adult now, and still overly serious and nerdy. Love you Michael! :D )No colorblindness settings, no UI or text scaling- some fonts used on notes and such are not going to play nice with a screen reader, and for colorblindness you will have to rely on machine system settings.No audio needed- no audio clues, though some sounds do give certain scenes a "punch" , but the subtitles for dialogue and labels on items you can interact with that are needed for the puzzles are pretty good- should be playable for Deaf and HoH gamers.Some of the puzzles are a bit vague and can be frustrating because you have to go from place to place and do things in a certain order to solve them or progress to the next step. Could be frustrating for people with certain types of neurodivergencies. No timed puzzles or interactions, so you can take your time and you don't need to worry about button mashing.Can be played with mouse-only.********************************************A hidden gem for point & click lovers and puzzle game enjoyers here on Steam. Full price may be a bit much for people who get stuck on the $$$/hour metric, but a steal at 90% off like it is right now (time of review). Likely to go n sale again i you missed it this time. Personally, I would be fine with full price- I enjoyed it a great deal (and I am not financially strapped). If you have a tighter budget, wish list it and pick it up on sale.Absolutely recommended- like I said, a hidden gem here on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Willy Morgan and the curse of Bone town is an interesting take on the Point and Click/Adventure game genre, based around a fantasy pirate-world theme, with generic point and click gameplay.The story starts at Willy Morgan’s house; it’s been 10 years since Willy’s father, the famous archeologist, Henry Morgan, disappeared. One day the postman drops by to deliver a letter; Willy seems surprised to find a letter mailed to him. It’s from his father, Henry, and the letter was posted the very day he disappeared.The letter states-                                                     ‘’If you receive this letter, it means that means something went wrong                                                             And it’s up to you to finish what I started. Go as fast you can                                                                        to Bone town, room 09, but don’t trust anyone..’’Finding this 10-year-old letter, Willy is eager to know what happened to his father and what he wanted Willy to finish, so he collects all he needs for his journey to Bone town and sets off on his trusty bike.Upon reaching Bone Town, he findings the inn where his father last stayed. Willy goes in and is greeted by a suspicious-behaving character; the manager of Dead Man’s Inn. Although Willy could afford a room at the Inn for one night, he wasn’t allowed to get room number 09. Willy was given room number 10 instead.Throughout the game, Willy has to have a keen eye for clues and hits.  He manages to distract the Inn manager with a spill and gains access to room number 09.Upon inspection, Willy finds some clues about where to look next.The gameplay of Willy Morgan and the curse of the Bone Town is nothing special and provides a familiar experience of traditional point and click style gameplay.What the game really brings to the table is its unique story and voice acting. The unique story brings a great flavor to the game with its interesting plot and timeline in a fantasy pirate-themed world. The voice acting for the main protagonist, Willy Morgan, was for the most part a great touch, until it became repetitive and lost my interest.Dialogues, although limited, were just about enough for interacting with the NPC’s. All the dialogues in-game were short and on point in each respective scenario.The gameplay brings a familiar experience of traditional point and click style. For the most part, the gameplay was smooth sailing, with some minor hiccups. The gameplay puts a lot of unnecessary steps to the puzzle-solving aspect of the game. Puzzles, for the most part, were easy and took a few seconds to solve.  Gathering items to solve the puzzles was generally simple and fast, although in a few cases, it did take some time looking around the world and felt like an unnecessary grind.By far the biggest downside of the game would be its manual save; I didn’t realize there was no checkpoint save and lost 30 minutes of gameplay progress. Positives: + Decent Story + Solid gameplay+ Decent sound effects+ Decent voice acting + Short yet adequate dialogue options+ Beautiful 2.5D art style+ Simple yet fun puzzlesNegatives: - Unnecessary steps added to the puzzles- At times gathering items felt like an unnecessary grind - Dialogues and voice acting started to feel repetitive after a while- No checkpoint save, Manual save onlyA unique story set in a pirate-themed world, Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is an enjoyable point and click adventure.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan is a a delightful narrative-based point and click adventure. The art and music are quite modern but, on a conceptual level, the game returns to the classic roots of the adventure genre. A heroic quest with an unlikely hero, sub-quests galore, conversing with a host of characters, and solving problems by finding inventory and using it in creative ways.The game is played from a 3rd person perspective, controlling the character of Willy Morgan. Ten years after his father disappeared, he receives a note that indicates there are clues to follow in order to learn what really occurred. Willy heads out to Bone Town and begins to investigate. The game played flawlessly and has some nice features - a map of the town that can be used for rapid navigation once locations have been discovered. This saves a lot of traversing, as the game requires quite a bit of travel around town. Also, there is an explicit save with multiple slots. I always appreciate when I can save a game at any time and come back to play later.The voice acting is excellent, the dialog and commentary are clever, and you can't help but cheer Willy on. The 'find and use' puzzles make sense and the game is interesting rather than frustrating.  I played through in about 5 hours and it was time well spent. I seem to have missed quite a few achievements and this is a game I am likely to circle back through to improve my score. If you are a fan of classic adventure games, then this is one that you should not miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing.The first mission in the game is to find all bicycle parts in the house, it's all about hidden objects rather than a click and point game. The few puzzles are mostly about finding the right tools to open boxes, tighten screws, which are typical in hidden object games. There's no fun to search every corner of the house, many parts are poorly hidden, the bicycle seat tube is used as a supporter inside the fridge to hold the upper layer in place - regardless anyone uses it this way, there are milk bottles next to the seat tube with perfect height, and there are hardly anything on each layer. Besides, food is poorly placed inside the fridge and looks like random 3D opponents on the internet, devs even put instant noodles bowls inside the fridge. There is no story, just go from A to B and fetch stuff, be an errand boy. There are no people on the streets in Bone Town in daylight but some work in stores, the dialogues are awkward and can be illogical, like, the librarian doesn't help bringing when asked for a book, instead she tells the player to "go to the upper floor and the book is easy to find", which is not. The book is nowhere to be seen, player is to find a replacement for a pile of books used as a supporter- yes again a supporter,  go around the town and find a jack laying on the ground and come back for the book, same boring trick.I get random stuff in each store with few story going on, and it's ridiculous the town major agreed to give me the stamp on first sight while he states it's still in use and have law effect, and that music shop owner just let people go upstairs to search whatever, especially there's a hidden chamber behind the wall. Some places look interesting on the outside, but usually just 3-4 places to click at when you go inside, with 1-2 lines to state the object has nothing to do with the research. There are some lines that are sarcasm and funny, but 90% of the game feels boring.It might be alright if you play with a young kid, at least it's voiced. But not for the price, and the wrong tags.

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan is a beautiful drawn, traditional point & click adventure game, unfortunately the graphics are also where the good part lays the most (and maybe a large part of their budget went into that). The puzzles are very easy and short, there aren't many locations, and the story is bare.First you start off in your parents' house, and then you enter the last part of the game: Bone Town, which has 12 locations, but with having a map you can quickly transfer back and forth, although even walking doesn't take long either. You can complete the game with 100% achievements in 4-5 hours, the puzzles are so easy and predictable, even for a non seasoned point and click adventure player, especially when you use the hotspots.Normally i would consider the price according to what you get, and 20 euro is definitely not worth it, and even on sale at 14 euro it's questionable if 4-5 hours of entertainment is worth it to you, i think a permanent price drop should be in order.But the enjoyment even though at a high price (and considered a negative review), i gonna say to the devs not to let them discourage that, because actually i would very much love to see a sequel, but longer in size and with more difficult puzzles please!

_childDocuments_.review: ‘Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town’ is an interesting game. On the one hand, it has accessible puzzles, a unique look playing with perspective and deformity in a kid-friendly sense, and a slow pacing ideal for point-and-click adventure game. On the other hand, what keeps it from being great is the writing. It is heavy on the exposition, especially early on. I never felt the emotions of the main characters, but I am happy I played it once the puzzles started, as it was nice and intuitive. The characters. As in the whole cast. Couldn’t connect with anyone, despite it being a fully voiced game.Don’t get me wrong, no one was annoying or tedious, it was all just… meh. The entire plot, story, and characters just all felt lifeless to me. Either being bland or stereotypical to the extreme.As mentioned, very heavy on the telling rather than weaving storypoints into the plot.And some… questionable dialogue around the end. As mentioned, the puzzles are the high point of the game. Which is great for a point and click adventure game. None of the solutions are obtuse, and the pacing of the story lets it make sense that you are slowly figuring stuff out.The gameplay is very intuitive, and if you have any experience with games in the genre, I recommend just skipping the tutorial. You look with right mouse button, interact with left button, and open your inventory with ‘i’, that is basically all you need to know to play the game, because you see the name of important stuff you can interact with when you scroll over it. I hesitate to recommend this as someone’s ‘first’ point-and-click adventure game, because of the problems with exposition and the less than great cast. Someone on the fence about the genre might be scared off by that. BUT if you are someone, who loves the concept of the genre, whether you are experienced or new, then this game is a good addition, because it gives you the relaxing experience with room for trial and error. A title that is both beginner-friendly and friendly for all ages.

_childDocuments_.review: [Received this game as a gift. Thank you, dear friend!]I must say I am impressed. An adventure, a mystery, a child whose father disappeared for 10 years, a legendary pirate and his treasure. What more do we want? This was perfect. A perfect gift from a dear friend. Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town reminded me of all the adventure cartoons and movies that I've seen as a kid. A bit of nostalgia, a bit of adrenaline, a bit of everything. PROS: - Interesting story with twists;- Beautiful scenes/graphics;- Nice environmental music;- Great voice-acting;- Puzzles and logic.CONS:- None that I could think of.To conclude, Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is a gem worth playing. A game to be played on a rainy night or whenever you feel like going on an adventure at sea!

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is what many claimed to be - a well-made, thought-of and fun game inspired by the old Lucas Arts, Monkey Island and what-not, while also bringing something new to the plate. Where many failed, Mr Morgan's son delivered. I cannot even begin to describe how much this game reminded me of the good feels I had when I played Monkey Island for the first time. The story is based on a classic: missing parent sends me on a quest type of plot. However, unlike in Journey Down, we do have a good idea of what has happened - dad went on an adventure to a known town and suddenly disappeared. That was ten years ago; currently, little Willy is a well-mannered, well-behaved teen... Excellent to take on the task to find his dad!I want to applaud the creative use of references in this game. I know a lot of the reviewers said it's too much in-your-face, but I think it's fine to be literal, as long as it fits in with the story and character behaviour. Here, they match up perfectly.The music is one of the things I would have liked to be improved. Unfortunately, although whatever is created fits thew game and is rather cool, the sounds become repetitive and get annoying at times. I don't mind hearing just a couple of songs, but not if one is repeated consecutively during the gameplay.The puzzles in the game, where available are nothing too special, unfortunately, although I did find it nice to have multiple resources at hand. I am a bit mad because that chest just HAD to have a puzzle in the lock. (staying vague not to spoil). It was disappointing that I didn't have to solve anything myself.References to pop culture and not only Monkey Island (although the latter has the upper hand quantity-wise) - can you spot them all? The One Piece moment brought a tear to my Japanophile heart!I am happy the team hinted at a second game. Would definitely purchase it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan is a very charming point & click game with a lot of humor.We play as Willy Morgan the son of an explorer who mysteriously disappeared years ago. Receiving a letter from Dad 10 years later on the anniversary of his disappearance, we go investigate Bone Town, the place where he disappeared.Exploring the town and interacting with its unusual inhabitants was a lot of fun. The dialogues made me laugh so many times. The game also has many games and movies references that were fun to recognize.Progressing in the game was mostly straightforward, I only got stuck once. I also really liked that there were no action or quick-time sequences. I could take all the time I needed to progress in the game.The 3D artwork and animations in the game looked amazingly nice. It was a pleasure for the eyes. The game is fully-voiced, and sound tracks and effects fit perfectly well the different scenes in the game.Controls are very simple: Left-click to interact with/pick up/combine items, Right-click to comment on an item, I key to open/close the inventory, Space key to show hot spots. But there are also secret items to find that are not showed with the hot spots key. So do not hesitate to right click on any item that looks peculiar.The game has manual saves only, so do not forget to save.I did not encounter any bugs, and the game ran smoothly on my Windows 7 laptop.I had a lot of fun playing this game, so if you enjoy games like Monkey Island and Day of the tentacle, I highly recommend this game to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Looks great. Has realistic backgrounds (pre-rendered I'm guessing) with 3D cartoon-ish characters. Perhaps a nod to games like Grim Fandango. Maybe not to everyone's taste but I liked it.- Good voice acting .- Solid point and click puzzle design, very satisfying. Right level of difficultly IMHO. The game flows along nicely.- Great UI, very minimalist.- Great controls, entirely playable with the mouse.- Modern built in convenience features such as fast travel, hot spot reveal tool and removing items from your inventory when they are no longer useful.- Decent story, quite engaging. - Pleasant soundtrack.- Multiple save slots.Cons- Its quite short. I left the game running so my time is overstated.- Although I liked the story over all I thought some parts of the ending were a bit silly. - While the voice acting was good, arguably the English translation could have been better; some of the script was weirdly stilted. - As far as I know there is no auto-save, could be wrong on that.Overall it was very polished and enjoyable. Recommended!

That will break many hearts….“„Ehm…. errrrr…. No! But i have an alternative. Do you know Willy Morgan, Wyvern?“„Willy …… Morgan?“„Yes! A nice little guy, that got a 10 years old letter from his missing father.“„Okay. Continue, Guybrush.“„Ehm, as i said before, Willys Dad is missing. _childDocuments_.review: A delightful point-and-click adventure game made by people that clearly love the classic adventure games. You play as Willy, a teenage kid whose archeologist father disappeared without a trace years earlier. One day you receive a letter from your missing dad dated just before his disappearence. And the game sets off from there. This is the first adventure game by the developers but quaility wise you can't tell it. Good story, good controls, nice setting, pretty graphics, good audio and voice acting. You can explore Bone Town pretty much as you want to and the puzzles make sense. Didn't notice any bugs and nothing game breaking at all.Thought I'd missed something and broken the game a few times, turned out I simply hadn't explored the new areas properly. I would have loved if the game had been a bit longer. I finished it in 5 hours. But the other qualities are more important. The epilogue hints of a sequel and I definitely hope we will see more adventure games from this team.

_childDocuments_.review: is a point & click adventure game that is rather fun. Play as Willy after he received a letter, 10 years after the disappearance of his father. I was left wanting more after finishing in 4 hours. The game plays as a classic point & click adventure with an interesting story. All of the dialogue lines are voice-acted, which gives the game a nice flow and feel. If you want to you can skip the dialogue and just to go to the puzzles, but you would miss out on the story.There is an option to highlight all of the interactive items on the screen, this is good. The game also has a manual save option, which is nice. It's something that a lot of games have removed, and as players, it's nice to be able to use.The game has outstanding graphics, especially for an indie game.It's notable that all of the dialogue lines are voice-acted. There is a lot of content in the soundtrack as well.The game can be fully played with a mouse.The base price is €19,99 or $19.99 US so no regional pricing. This price is a bit too steep for a game so short. If you are used to P&C games, much of the game is rather easy. I finished in 4 hours.Besides the price, I have no complaints about this game. It's a good game for newcomers to the P&C genre. When I was done, I wanted it there to be more. Even though the price is too high, I did enjoy my time thoroughly with the game, and so I will still recommend this game. If the price is too high for you, it's reasonable to wait until a sale price that's more suitable as well. But when you get a chance to, you should try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing this game!Graphic design (the environments, the background animations, etc.), sounds and background music are especially wonderful, I was really carried in Willy's world and lived his adventure.As most of the point&click adventure games nowadays, the puzzles are really simple and accessible to everyone.Personally i'd like to be a little more challenged, maybe with some interactive puzzles or a more extended clue/deduction system, but if you're looking for a very funny and not too much challenging way to spend some hours, this is really a good way.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - this game is a technical marvel. I'm not sure how big the dev team is, but for the most partthis game felt like a AAA outing - gorgeous visuals and animations, quality sound design and slick responsive UI.That alone makes this game a worthwhile purchase.The story, characters and puzzles have a lot to live up to in order to pass the quality gate set by the technical side, and while they do seem to struggle at times, thankfully or the most part they succeed.Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan is a super fun little point-and-click adventure in the classic style. It'd be a great game for kids because the puzzles aren't too demanding and the story is fairly wholesome, but it's a nice short game for the young at heart as well. It's a story about a son of two adventurers who ends up on an adventure of his own. It has all the cartoonish point-and-click tropes, like putting implausibly large stuff into your inventory, but it's all reasonably logical and there are no red herrings or very long item combination chains to trip you up. After playing a tedious, long and much more serious game the rest of the weekend, this was the perfect antidote. Light and charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable and entertaining point and click adventure game. I finished the game in 6 hours and had to repeat several parts of the game to get all the achievement. _childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: The young Willy Morgan travels to the mysterious 'city' of Bone Town to investigate his archaeologist father's disappearance, ten years earlier...Don't let the awkward start put you off of this game! This is an enjoyable point&click adventure game targeting a younger demographic, or at the very least targeting those young at heart. The first section of the game is rather tedious but the pacing improves once you get to Bone Town. After spending the night in the inn you're free to explore that town's many locations. You'll be doing a lot of exploring, talking to NPCs and figuring out what item is used where in typical point&click fashion. There's no 'moon logic' to be found in this game, right up until the finale, but I won't spoil anything about that by discussing it.The game world has quite a few notable unused objects that might just be there to add flavour to the world or might be a relic of a scrapped plot line from earlier in the development process. The  are especially noteworthy, to the point where they felt like a city-wide red herring.All in all I'd recommend this to fans of the genre. Just keep in mind that you might not be the target demographic, age-wise.PS: At no point in the game does the protagonist carry a lantern as depicted in the banner and icon for this game. False advertising! :P
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: A good game. Typical point n click adventure. Major part of the game takes place around a central hub with lots of locations so there's a lot of to and fro backtracking involved, although you get to fast travel after you've been to a place once. There are no in game puzzles and the game progresses by using or combining items in the right place and order. Most of it is easy except for a couple of times in the end that I had to use a walkthrough. The art is good. The voice acting is mostly competent. The dialogues are a little smart alecky in a  juvenile kind of a way so maybe young people may like it. Takes about five hours to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve tried the demo when the game was around 80% off, there were things I disliked about it. Still, I’ve decided to give the game a chance with it being 90% off now. This has been a good decision as the full game gives a better impression than the demo. The demo has the house portion, the save transfers to the full game, allowing me to continue with the town right away. There is also a cave after the town portion and that’s the entire game completed. I’m not complaining about that, I actually like the game not having filler content and the story advancing at a good pace. The graphics look very charming, I enjoyed the voice acting of all the characters, the puzzles in the town and cave were fun and made enough sense even with the point & click adventure logic, the controls are excellent with the mouse, I love fast travel, same for showing most of the objects you can interact with, I love the set-up of the story (not spoiling any) and the achievements are fun!As mentioned though, the house is a bit of a bad start. The way objects are used is a bit more ridiculous and you’re thrown many objects at the same time, making it hard to figure out how to use them when you’re not used to what the game expects of you. There are no other characters nor do you get the main objective until you reach the town, a lot of that appeal doesn’t show until after the house. Although the puzzles were fine for the most part, I didn’t like the 2 instances where you needed to find a hole to put a sign and a spot to put a doll. With the hole, the NPC tells you to put it in front of the church but you can’t see a clear hole you can interact with. And there was no mention of where to place the doll at all in the game. Also, although there is save transfer from the demo, you’re going to have to play that part again if you want to get all the achievements. I did it after completing the game, it’s something I wish developers did better. This has been a pleasant surprise, it’s a better game than I expected. It’s definitely worth the current price of €1,67 on Steam. You will get a decent point and click adventure that should last between 4 and 6 hours for most people. It’s making me look forward to their next game.
