_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played it long, but it has already won me over, easily!It takes all the best lessons from the classics, makes UI simpler, wraps it all up in a very interesting graphics style, smooth animations and unobtrusive, pleasant soundtrack, and serves it with what seems will be a quite interesting story.There are references to 80ies and early 90ies to boot! Just in my first 20 minutes, there was mention of Goonies, Guybrush Threpwood and Twin Peaks! This might've softened me up a bit, but the game _still_ feels like it feel out of that time period, but wrapped in the modern looks and feels.It adds one optional-to-use "cheat" element, which basically lets you just skip the time you hunt for interactible objects - if you hold Space you can see everything interactible in the scene, which is great when you're stuck and wondering if you just missed something.Puzzles I solved so far are logical enough - those that aren't, you'll get more than enough clues by just examining things and reading descriptions.All in all - can't wait to play more. For sure, I will be finishing this one and I just hope the rest will stand up to the standard that the first 30 minutes set.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the film The Goonies will probably fondly recall the classic Lucas Arts point and click games of Monkey Island, and it is in that vein which Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town plays out, with red herrings, puzzles and a dose of humour to top it off ensuring Willy Morgan CBT makes a truly resplendent brew!The Controls are very simple, Pressing the spacebar will highlight interactive elements on the screen then you can right click for information and left click to take an object.The storyline is good, albeit too short, but there is a hint of a second chapter incoming at the end of the game, and hand-on-heart I am truly excited to see more.  I was fully immersed in this game, and I kind of predicted the end story…but having already spent so much time on the BETA I was hoping for even more gameplay than was left of the game…So that really is my only real criticism my own disappointment that the game ended too soon.If you like your puzzlers then look no further, this is absolute quality from start to finish!
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone contemplating giving Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town a go, I *think* I'd recommend it - albeit with a few caveats.Firstly, it's INCREDIBLY short - I finished it in 3 hours - with no walkthrough and no hints - and I didn't even realise there was a hotspot finder (top left of the screen) until I was in the second-to-last location.The script features some rather strange use of English language - most of the dialogue in conversations, or when Willy is reading an item description, feels rather forced and quite unnatural. It takes you out of the moment sadly.  I get the impression they didn't have a native English speaker proof-reading.In my opinion, at full price (it's regularly been circa £15), it's probably not worth the money... BUT if you can pick it up in a sale like I did (£3.87), I think you'll be happy with it.Onto some of the good stuff - the backgrounds are very well drawn and look gorgeous. The storyline, whilst super cliché and not really fully formed, is still relatively interesting. There are many shout-outs to the old adventure games which no doubt inspired the devs, which is a nice touch too - the chicken shop in particular was a nice call-back to CMI 🙂 The music is ok - certainly not terrible – but nothing memorable that you'll be humming to yourself later.The puzzles are very straightforward, nothing too involved and not really any real ‘head-scratchers’. You're immediately given all the clues you need to solve the puzzles and everything is very logical – just a bit too easy. As an example, collecting the map pieces (a pivotal part of the game)should have been much harder, but most of them could be obtained within 5-10 mins.I liked the fast travel map feature - saved a lot of time walking back and forth (because there is a fair bit of that involved), but again this made an already short game even shorter.I felt that the ‘bad guy’ was given away a bit too early on, and so the element of shock/surprise wasn’t really there when the final scene came around. Speaking of which, the end scene is rather rushed and felt anti-climatic as a result.  There's very little to do in the final locations.Overall, despite the criticisms raised above, I thought it was a charming little game, and whilst not without it's flaws, it's certainly worth picking up in a Steam sale 🙂
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: This is a classic point-and-click adventure whose duration is about 4 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is a very well done point-and-click adventure. It has not a lot but very clean animations, very good looking and slightly off-real (i.e. unrealistic) visuals, along with nice music and good voice acting. There are only two subjective imperfections. The game's length is somewhat on the short side (given the price tag) - took me a bit more than 4 hours to complete. And the story is not too deep with two weak twists - one easily foreseeable and one rather unbelievable. The game is also a huge homage to the Monkey Island series of games - appreciated.Hint: Click on interesting things. The game shows action points, i.e. things to interact with, but has secrets that do not show up as such.+ Good-looking and well animated+ Good music+ Good voice acting+ Well-made and short tutorial0 Jump-to-exit functionality slightly hindered by scrolling scenes- Serviceable but simple story- Short lengthThe game offers to jump to exits by double-clicking, but this works only for exits, not for other action points and not for walkable non-action-points. Some exits start as closed doors and need to be opened before they can be jumped to. And some scenes come with scrolling, i.e. the avatar moving to a certain edge of the screen makes the scene's view change. This scrolling can sort of hide exits at first, posing an obstacle to the jump-to-exit functionality. This situation is ameliorated by adding a map - which lets us jump to already visited scenes - shortly after the start of the game.Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is almost an easy recommendation, only marred by its not-super-strong story and shorter playing time. Definitely go for it when the game is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second time I have played through this game and it was still just as fun as the first time! The enviroment is absolutely stunning and the art style is somewhere between photo realistic and claymation animation. It ticked all the boxes for me personally. The diologue is very witty- so make sure you listen to everything that is said. Plus, there are a ton of nerdy easter eggs throughout the game! It is absolutely worth giving a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: The game was really good. Great visuals and voice acting. I do have some complaints though. The price really doesn't match the length. Only 4 hours long for $20 is a bit pricey and not much content. Sometimes the voice acting was quiet when other characters talked even though the voice volume was at max while the others were lowered. One last thing, I got stuck on certain puzzles and had to look up a guide as it wasn't very clear what I needed to do, a hint system would've been nice. Overall, I enjoyed it. The story was great but it's better to get this when it's on sale, I was hoping it'd be longer but oh well. It was a gift from a friend, noting the "received product for free" mark.Edit: One thing I forgot to mention is that I wish there was an alternative text for reading the notes and such as cursive is a pretty dead style nowadays, I cannot read it for the life of me. I can't immerse myself in the story if I can't understand it.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan was a short-lived but enjoyable experience. It's a classic point-and-click adventure where you direct 15-year-old Willy Morgan around his house and Bone Town. The controls are simple and intuitive and just about anyone can jump in and immediately start figuring things out.  Overall, 7/10.PROS- fairly engaging and witty dialogue, good voice acting for the most part- most of the puzzles made sense in some way or another and solutions weren't needlessly complex- fast travel options included, Willy moves at a decent pace- didn't experience any bugsCONS- although the puzzles made sense and worked, I wish there was some more depth to the gameplay- the story was fairly nonexistent; I wish there was more backstory and information about the characters involved in the plot- game looks somewhat dated and the characters look a little out of place when they're walking (the game does have a certain charm to it, however)
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! - It wasn't overly long (which I quite liked) but some may prefer their long winded games.  The puzzles weren't extremely hard, though they all had a little bit of a mystery about them, it took me a while to figure out some little things, but once you do you realise you'd been over thinking it the whole time. haha Really enjoyed the voice acting, and the story was quite gripping.  Would definitely recommend for any point & click fans out there! (lots of little references to other games too!)
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, enjoyable medium-length game to spend some (4-8 hours) with. :)I found+ the graphics a cool mix of whimsical and beautiful, sometimes very beautiful+ the story entertaining, none too extravagant but not boring either - on the "nice job :)"-level+ the music alright, a little repetitive in places but overall tasteful, well-made and fitting+ the mood subtle, engaging but not overwhelming, going back and forth between eye-twinklingly funny and serious+ the gameplay fluid, well thought-out+ the puzzles made logical sense, hardly any moonlogic - big plus! I could actually guess or deduct most of them+ nuanced antagonist(s)+ I liked the way the inventory works - MC just drops items that he doesn't need anymore with a brief remark, it's integrated into the game seemlessly and avoids a cluttered inventory. Also, find it a nice touch how he puts things in his bag he always has with him. Adds realism. Ok sometimes the items are too large to fit in there but still ... it's a start :DSuggestions on what could be better- the gameplay is linear - seems to be normal in this genre. It would be fun though to see an adventure game offer me several ways to solve riddles (just dreaming hahah but who knows ^^...)- while the MC often expresses to not want to take some object because he shouldn't do so without permission, you actually HAVE to make him steal and lie a number of times (and suddenly all his qualms are gone). I think that's normal in the genre, but still, it's something I donnn't feel so comfortable with and so for me it's a "meh" bullet point. At least he made sure to give back one object in a fun way :D- I liked the ending but it was a little too short and rushed for my taste, too much info too quickly, expected more interaction between two characters ... if they ever feel like expanding that a little bit ... :D- the church was odd, no crosses, no religious paintings, no mention of Jesus (or Mary) and I think not even God. Only a lot of pious talk by the priest (which was kinda hilarious though :D)Overall, I can recommend the game. I had a good time with a nice engaging story - just what I'd hoped for.  I'm grateful to the developers for making this endearing game. And if they make a sequel I'd like to check that out too :).
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a lighthearted adventure it's probably worth it. Probably. Depending on your familiarity with this genre and ability to solve relatively basic (but fun) puzzles, you could be done in under 4 hours. For $19.99 that's a little steep but it's a minor complaint.The art style is unique with a cartoony warped perspective, sound design is solid, and writing is I don't know... fine, I guess? "Bone Town" was an interesting choice, but I get that this is an Italian studio so whatever. The dialogue reads (and sounds) a lot like a Saturday morning cartoon for young adolescents. It's not totes adorbs; there are some dark-ish themes but at no point did the game feel mature or age restrictive.Puzzles, as others have said, are intuitive and playful. I'm not going to say I never got a little confused, but overall a walkthrough wasn't a consideration. That doesn't mean you won't get stuck -- like most point and click games you have to kind of settle in to the world and themes before puzzles start to make sense. For example, some games aim for realism and others total nonsense. One game might suggest you pour water in a hole to make a plastic key float to the surface, while the other insists a rude security guard is just going to take and drink a dosed cup of coffee from a random stranger. This game has a little of both. Some of the puzzles are completely obvious while a handful of others dabble in weird and straight up reckless/dangerous.If you like point and clicks that are a little on the cute side with a lower difficulty that lasts a handful of hours, I can confidently recommend it. As mentioned, the only minor issue is the price, but I've spent more having a sandwich delivered during the pandemic so who gives a ♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: I love the 3D graphics because it really makes this point and click game stand out from others! As a novice gamer I really like the "hint" system which is there if you want it. I was able to move around and make progress fairly well, but I did need the help of guides several times. Sometimes you need to combine items in your inventory and then apply to an area in the game; that's when I was thankful for a guide. All in all a very enjoyable game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: I WANT MORE WILLY!This game was mourish, took me back to how I felt playing Monkey Island 2, the game play storyline and graphics were perfect. Gameplay was fun and lots of exciting places to explore. Wish the game was longer, really really enjoyed it! Would deffo purchase a sequel, make it twice as long and ill happy pay double the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Game is advertised as an old-school point and click with in-inventory combinations. Bear in mind there are some modern polishes with resolution, but animations remain to be retro. Do note that the story is sub-par with its only redeeming point is the childish spirit of it.Overall, pleasant experience however a little pricey for what it is worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: With a wobbly art style completely their own, Will Morgan creates a visually interesting and brilliantly new experience.  Complete with pirates, puns, and plunder, this epic adventure replicates the nostalgia of classic point-and-clicks like Monkey Island and Day of the Tentacle while creating its own unique story and cast of characters. For vetrens of the genre, the game also includes numerous easter eggs and nods to adventure games of the past. Five out of five sandwiches.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Great point & Click adventure and a good story. Definately worth a buy, and an absolute must-have for lovers of the  original Point & Click adventure games. I can even say it's almost a little love letter to the good old, late 90's, Monkey Island franchise. When you start playing the first thing you will experience is a smooth and easy working point & click gameplay. Throughout the game there are a few references to Monkey Island indeed (quite funny), but also the general "feel" of this game is a bit like the Monkey Island/BrokenSword. The drawing is beautiful and the texts made me smirk more than once. Offcourse...there could be some improvements here and there, maybe in a few details (like picking up objects). I understand this was made by a studio with only 3 ot 4 devs, so hats off for them. It took me almost 6 hours to beat the game. And I am looking foward to a sequel or prequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan is among the best adventure releases of 2020.Willy is a wonderful protagonist; he is a sensitive, smart kid who never comes off as snarky or know-it-all ish.  He is well mannered and I really liked spending time with him.  Other highlights of this game include the lovely graphics, the polished mechanics, and a very enjoyable soundtrack.The game's tone falls somewhere in between serious and comedic.  You couldn't call it a comedy, but it's very light-hearted.   It includes a number of adventure game in-jokes and references as well, but it's not a send-up, either.I enjoyed myself so much that I wish the game had been longer!  Coming in at about 5 hours from start to finish, it definitely left me wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Full review at: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town is a sufficiently enjoyable point and click made in the style of its predecessors, but it lacks some of the charm and wit of its better written ancestors. While the simple plot and functional characters are neither good nor bad, Bone Town ends up being the star of the show. Interconnected puzzles across the locations of the old pirate haven allow for much greater puzzle depth than you might expect from such a short adventure, and while the game does give you solutions a bit too freely at times, it has some fun ones to puzzle out and helpful tools like the item highlighting with the space bar to avoid pointless pixel hunts. Since most of the game is about unraveling Bone Town’s mysteries through the inventory puzzles, Willy Morgan’s adventure still turns out alright despite having very little personality.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! I've done a play through on my channel,  if anyone would like to see.I have played point and click adventure games ever since I was a little girl, and having recently completed Broken Sword, this was a lovely and modern game to sink my teeth into.The puzzles were of a good difficulty, nothing too hard and not too easy. Easier than Broken Sword, but that's not a bad thing!Wonderful story, graphics and voice acting. A pleasant and enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town heralds back to the classic Lucasarts adventures in the 90's, with many references splashed throughout. However this never tips the scales into parody or clone. Willy has it's own identity. The good: The art is stupendously gorgeous. Willy is a really likeable and relatable chap and the story, although never groundbreaking, is told with wit and style. It's a fairly easy game in terms of puzzles, and the play time is a little short. The bad: The NPC's are a bit dull. Some of the puzzles are questionable.But if you're looking for a new pirate adventure then I'd recommend it. See my full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Willy Morgan does a fantastic job of capturing the look and feel of those classic 90's adventure games, delivering a fantastic presentation of hand painted backgrounds with this whimsical art style that is totally authentic to the classics like Monkey Island and Maniac Mansion. Adventure games live and die by their puzzles whether those are item based or conversational interactions.  This is where Willy Morgan stumbles a bit.  Dialogue trees are linear and more of an exhaustive process of eliminating all the topics rather than trying to go down a certain path.  Some topics don’t even disappear once asked.  Inventory puzzles are also not that challenging with the required item often found very close by its place of use.  Even the practice of combining items to create a new item is rarely used.There are a lot of great ideas and fantastic design aesthetics going on with Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town, but the whole thing just felt like the first chapter in something greater.  Perhaps Telltale has got me used to episodic content, or maybe I am still remembering the 20+ hours it would take to finish those classic 90’s adventures, but Willy Morgan was more of an appetizer than a full meal.Full review at
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Super little game. Puzzles are fairly logical with no weird combinations of items. Quite a few locations to visit where you amass a large collection of items so its just a case of paying attention to what people say to help you decide where items are best used. Graphics are also very good. Only comment is it is very short. Took me around 4 hours to complete so if that bothers you, wait for a sale. Otherwise, if you're a fan of point-and-click games, get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Willy Morgan and the Curse of Bone Town

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little game! Not very challenging for an adult player (I'm in my late 20s), but fun and interesting enough for casual gaming. I found the price was fair for the gaming experience delivered. One note: no cello player would call the hair of their bow "strings" - they would refer to it as hair.

_childDocuments_.review: A letter from 10 years ago, an intricate web of lies to unravel and a mystery to solve. Explore an unconventional town of pirates, dive into the past, collect items and look for clues to help Willy find out what happened to his father...

name: Circuit Superstars
detailed_description: Join Our Discord A motorsport-loving, wholesome and competitive community is waiting for you, join us! About the Game Circuit Superstars is a top-down racer built by racing fans, for racing fans. The game celebrates generations of multi-disciplinary motorsport, focusing on driving that feels great – but with a high skill ceiling, that will have players spending hours honing their perfect lap. Starting out is simple but learning the nuances of each car’s handling and finding the best racing line through each corner of each track will be a challenge for a long time to come. Not only that, but with the option of fuel usage, tire degradation and racing damage, even a good pit stop strategy could make the difference between hero and zero. Feel the rubber bite into the road as you pass the start/finish line and dive, brakes squealing, into the first corner! Feel the tires meet the road Tactile handling model that lets you feel the tires bite into the asphalt. Celebrating Motorsport Race vehicles across multiple motorsport disciplines including Rallycross, Open wheel single seaters, SuperTrucks, GT racing, Eurotrucks and many more. Pit Stop Strategies Featuring tire degradation, fuel consumption, and damage, Circuit Superstars challenges you to dynamically choose your pit stop strategy during the race. Online Multiplayer & Custom Lobbies Dive into specially curated online multiplayer races of up to 12 players from around the globe. Create your own tournaments and play online with friends! A motorsport playground We continue to add features that further expand the possibilities for fun in Circuit Superstars. Weekly Time Trials Every hundredth of a second counts! Challenge your friends and the rest of the world in regularly updated Time Trials events. Grand Prix Master all disciplines by conquering each of the single player tournaments designed for all 12 categories. Always a worthy rival Compete against 5 different AI difficulties to challenge you on your path to mastery on the world of Circuit Superstars. Free Play Mode Create your own race events or tournaments and play vs AI or with your friends in local multiplayer. The Garage Customize your cars and driver with liveries, helmets and victory celebrations you unlock as you level up! Ready Your Engines! 12 vehicles to choose from, each with their own unique handling models. I Ain’t Afraid of No Ghost Global ghosts let you see how players around the world are tackling each track, including the celebrity drivers from Top Gear x Circuit Superstars Star in a Reasonably Fast Car Invitational 2021! Location Location Location Race in 32 tracks across 17 vibrant locations. Race Replays Replays let you re-watch your races to see your epic overtakes or study your racing lines and those of your opponents. Built by Motor racing fans, for Motor Racing Fans A lifetime of racing experience inspired the developers to build the racing world of Circuit Superstars. The developers grew up on the pitlane, the paddock and the racetrack, living and loving the entirety of motorsport.

short_description: Circuit Superstars is a top down racing game with a tactile arcade physics model, pitstops, and a pure motorsport approach. It includes 16 categories that span different styles and eras of motorsport.

_childDocuments_.review: OK let me start off with what you want to know.... This game is Awesome!Its Early Access but there is some good stuff in there and worth the asking price in my opinion. I love top down/isometric racers and pretty much buy them all. If you have played Art Of Rally or  Star Drift Evolution (both amazing games) then you will be right at home here.This is pure circuit racing as per the title, so no drifting here but that's why I like it, its different from the other racing games I have. The online experience works well and people are online which is a good start. The graphics just have a really nice clean feel to them. I also love the fact it saves replays of your races, this is a brilliant feature! I love having replays to go back and watch and re live the race, especially for online races which it also saves.Its early days but if they keep supporting and adding more cars, tracks and features this could be a racer that gets played for a long time to come. It will also support cross play in future, which in this day and age is vital if you want there to be an online community that keeps playing.Fantastic game, go buy it and support the devs and this top down racing community. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: So, I have followed this game from first reveal, to Early Access, to full release, and I will tell you, the game is addictive, fun and an absolute bargain for the price it is. A small team behind it and it has less bugs than most triple A titles. Online can be a bit laggy, but that is being refined with each and every patch.Great game, which I play daily, I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: + Graphics+ Physics engine+ Sim-ish feel+ Skill gap+ Every car (class) feels and behaves differently+ 4 player split screen+ Simple commands- Early Access- Lack of game modes- Only 6 cars (only one per class)- Only 6 tracks- No private lobbies- UI lacking information and customizability (on ultrawide monitors especially)Circuit Superstars is a game that tries to fill a need that we did not know existed. A need for an arcade-looking top down racing game, but with a simulation feel to it. At the time of this review, it is very early in its Early Access, so i expect many things to improve and many things to be added to it.The graphics are fantastic, racing feel is great, skill gap is real. Don't expect this title to be über sim because it has no intention to be that. It does have a full-fledged 3D physics engine, and tires can get worn out, you can run out of fuel, and your pit crew is there to change your tires, refill your tank, repair your car. So, strategize! Be careful how much you push that pedal, because if you're conservative enough, maybe it will save you enough fuel to avoid an additional stop at the pits and give you a chance to win without being the fastest guy out there.The online aspect of the game is (for me) working decently. Of course it depends a lot on the connection quality of both you and your opponents, but it works well most of the time. There are no private lobbies yet, so if you want to race with a friend, you either have to use Steam's own feature (Remote Play Together) or try to join an online lobby at the same time. The offline modes and semi-offline modes (time trials against ghost cars of better drivers) are also fun, but this sort of title will always largely depend on its online capabilities.So far I didn't encounter bugs that would be game breaking, but that doesn't mean they don't exist.I expect this game to improve on its UI, to flesh out more features, to increase the polish level,, but even now I feel like it will be a part of my usual circle of games I frequently play over and over.If you want to support this small studio, and also have a place in your heart for some top down racing but you haven't found the right game yet, take your chance with this game.However, if you are wary of early access, and you don't want to suffer from (currently) not too rich experience, don't buy it. Wait for the full release, or a later part of Early Access.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm posting this on the first day after release, although I've been playing it throughout early access.  Bottom line is that this is a super fun game.  The driving mechanics are superb - creating a game that is easy to pick up but difficult to master.  I haven't played  a top down racer this much fun since Supercars II on the Amiga (I am that old!) and I haven't played a driving game with such a mixture of realism and fun since the early Gran Turismo games.   Each of the cars handles very differently and you have a real sense of the vehicles weight, speed and handling.   The game is realistic without ever sacrificing the fun element. A few early days gripes - there isn't much in the way of progression in single player mode here.  Gamers are used to a progressive mechanic in first person driving games, wherein success in one car type allows the user to buy more cars and access different race types to progress through the game.  There is none of that here, although I am sure we can expect more as the game develops.  But this is a relatively minor gripe.   This game is just super fun.  I see that I had already played the game for 20 hours during Early Access.  In Early Access you could only really race 3 car types on 3 or 4 different tracks.  Now there are lots of tracks, lots of cars and a wide variety of championships to compete in.  At the price this is an absolute bargain and will keep you coming back for more.  I imagine I will still be playing this 5 years from now.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is promising  but at its current state I cannot recommend it for this price (17€) in Spain.I will try to go briefly over the pros and cons.Pros: - Graphics are beautiful- There are different categories and cars- Love the menus music- The handling and physics are quite good.- I like the idea of having tyre degradation and fuel consumption in a game that is "arcadeish".Cons:- Singleplayer is quite forgettable, I do not care about it, but if you are that kind of player, be aware.- At the moment, the online mode has only an automatic match-making, you cannot create a lobby or enter one, or play with friends. You have to pray to be put in the same race when joining.- You´re unable to configure the online event, there are 3 predefined events and that's it, it gets boring really fast.- No manual shift, you cannot configure the car, I am not expecting a complex set up or anything, but at least being able to deactivate the steering help, abs etc... For a more real experience.- The game is promising and I was waiting for a game like this for a long, long time, but at its current status, I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Was a good game, until the most recent update. Despite the lack of updates and the low player count, the foundation was solid and I looked forward to spending many hours playing the campaign, advancing to faster cars and higher and higher difficulties. Until, rubber banding/dynamic AI was added. Rubber Banding is a major reason I moved into Sim Racing and stopped playing Mario kart and Forza. Rubber Banding:1. Makes your driving not matter for most of the race the pack staying bunched up like cycling regardless of your driving until the last lap if you manage to break away. Drive terribly or well for 9/10 laps or really well and it doesn't matter,2. Allows you to quickly pass anyone but the first placer who will then bug you as you are unable to pull a gap and the back of the pack closes in.I enjoyed this game for it's fun physics and how it pushed me to be consistent lap over lap no matter the difficulty and how when I had a bad race I had to fix my driving or fail. That is no longer the case. I have not touched and will not touch this game after trying the new update until an option for entirely disabling dynamic AI/rubber banding is added.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Don't misunderstand me, the game is not bad but I can't recommend at this point in time for 3 reasons:1. The online scoreboard is not working for me, non of my steam friends appear on it anywhere (I bought the game to compete against them).2. The car handling in single player is awesome but in online sesions is clunky, reacts with lag/latency making the car handling too hard to predict and sometimes move in an aleatory way. (I have a decent internet connection).3. No way to create private rooms to play only with friends and AI, that way I would avoid the lag/latency with the main server with one of us hosting the races.Until these 3 points are not fixed someway I will keep my vote and not recommend this game to anyone unless you want to play it single player.EDIT: The game now is way more stable and could finally play with my friends, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a "gamer". Prior to this, I dabbled in F1 and Mortal Kombat, but those were very occasional hours played. When I first got CSup, I played for two frustrating days of trying to sort out the top down view. I was all over the place on track and just could not grasp it. I put it away for several months, then picked it up again. This time, I was introduced to the amazing community the game has built, who embraced me and my noobness, were patient with the track hazard I was, mentored and coached me, and now not only am I 100% addicted to this game, but I have made friends across the world, immersed into the discord and online racing community, and got a lot faster on track. Make no mistake.. this is not an easy game. It looks adorable and simple, and while the racing lines are legit, if you grind enough hours, you will be finding those tenths and hundredths in every turn and straight. What I love about the game: there are a dozen cars and tracks, each having its own features; custom/private lobbies so you can play with your friends; the fact that this is one if not the only racing game that is cross-platform-multi-player so it doesn't matter if my friends have PC, Playstation or Xbox, we can be in the same lobby; the custom liveries; the one-time, low cost to purchase the game without needing any further financial transactions post-purchase; and most importantly, the CSup community... second to none! I have never encountered a game where the developers are SO close to the players and part of the active community. If you download the game (which you absolutely should!) my big tips are:- Don't give up, even if the top down view/steering frustrates you - it WILL click and become second nature- Find the CSup community on discord- Race CLEAN - this is not wreckfest! Learn the racing etiquette right away and don't go by how the AI race- Do the weekly time trials and follow the World Record ghost - no better way to learn those super fast lines- Take the time to grind out hours learning the tracks - this is half the battle, as it will allow you to anticipate the turns and get faster. You can do this with free play and practice mode - then move to the Grand Prix and work your way up against the AI skill levels- Have FUN with the game! With custom lobbies, you can create multi-race tourneys, fun challenges, etc.- Interact with the community to learn about the upcoming update features - the Devs are constantly working on the next patch and most of the features in each update are based on community feedback- Did I mention the community? I cannot say enough about this amazing world I stumbled into... some of the best humans on the planet are in that CSup discord. I can't wait for YOU to be one of them!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this a positive review because it has a really solid, fun, varied racing experience and I love the art/graphic style, but as a game I just cannot bring myself to play it.There is no progression, just unlocking liveries for cars, racing suits and helmets.In solo mode you can play the preset multi race GP mode, or create your own custom GPs but you have to complete them in one sitting as you can't save half way through.Multiplayer is a mixed bag, but with no ranking system you rarely have a good race, after one lap every one has settled into their position and then you're just time trialling unless someone messes up.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Played Early Access for over 60 hours, and loved it. Gameplay is awesome, easy to learn - hard to master, ticking all the boxes for quick but tense racing.Unfortunately development has missed so many opportunities for making this a great game that I can no longer recommend. There are a bunch of little issues to address, but the big ones are:* It is not possible to do a race with friends only. Multiplayer is limited to joining public lobbies without AI. Getting full lobbies is far from guaranteed, and each reach you can vote on a limited number of races/cars. I want to race with friends in a custom AI cup, and I can't even get close to doing anything like it.* It is not possible to save your progress in local play. Astonishing. There is a list of Grand Prix to choose from, which are pretty short but long enough to warrant the need for saving. I can make my own cup, running 99 races with any number of laps each, great! BUT I can't save my progress! Terrible.I can forgive bugs and missing features in Early Access, of course. But this game should not have been released in this state.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into the issues with the game, let me just say I really like the idea behind what the studio tried to create and I appreciate their dedication. At the moment, though, it falls short of my expectations (but I'd be happy to update this review in the future).My biggest disappointment is the handling model, despite it being touted as a central selling point.The cars are way too understeery. You don't feel front end bite when taking a turn, in fact you don't feel anything.Paradoxically, they're  oversteery, in the way they just seem to... rotate, rather than steer. Without properly gripping. Basically, way too skittish, but not in a "realistic" or plausible way. The steering feels a long way off too, especially in the way it recenters itself when you release the stick. No wheel inertia is simulated, or at least not properly. This makes the cars artificially hard to control, without it being down to actual driving mistakes from the player. You don't feel the weight of the car when cornering. At all.To compare with a recent top-down title, art of rally simulates all of that much, much better, with much more flexible options (sensitivity, counter-steering factor, TC/ABS...)As for the racing, surely there's fun to be had even in the game's current state, but it's not without problems either.You hardly feel there's space enough to race (narrow tracks, short straights), and the controls are too squishy to pull off clean moves, properly leave space for other players, etc. It's near impossible to have clean, close racing at the moment.Collisions tend not to punish the guilty party, which could lead to some rather dirty racing. Not to say it can't be fun, but that's really not in line with the game's promise of proper circuit racing.The tracks are also extremely short, with 30s being the average lap time. And sure enough there's no manual gears (or even gears!). Along with everything else, this makes the whole experience feel more like racing toy/RC cars than anything else.And don't get me wrong, I was a fan of Micro Machines and Re-Volt back in the day. If the game evolves towards a proper modern-day take on the top-down arcade racer (with crazier tracks, powerups, faultless netcode, etc.), it could become an awesome multiplayer title. Right now, though, it seems to be sitting in the middle, either looking for a "realistic" feel and not quite finding it, or falling a little short of the pick-up-and-play vibe of arcade games.Bottom line: before you focus on adding content, the core mechanics need (quite) a bit of work still. But that's just my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's been "5 years in the making" its awfully barebones. I just can't recommend the game in it's current state. I really hate saying that, since that in itself will discourage people from buying in, stifling the further development of the game. It's possible though that this game may get fleshed out enough in the near future to recommend (although I doubt it). I enjoyed this game for a couple hours, but once the honeymoon period is over you start to notice some severe flaws. I'll just list the pros and cons here.Pros: +Clean art style.+Runs at high FPS (thanks to Unity).+Car and driver cosmetic customization.+More "realistic feeling" than other titles in the top-down racing genre.+Time Trials with the ability to load the ghosts of your best lap, your friends laps, or even the world record holder.Cons:-Cannot customize controls!!-Multiple features shown in the trailer are not actually in the game (Offroad tracks, WRC and Road Cars).-No private lobbies.-No server browser.-No friend invites.-No control over online race settings (Online races are limited to 3 presets per week where the track, laps, car, fuel, tire, and damage settings are predetermined and the lobby must vote on which one to play).-Huge wait for matches and between races (mandatory 120 second waiting period between races even if the lobby is full)-Although the game feels somewhat realistic at first, using real driving techniques doesn't reward you with faster laps and the devs are overly concerned with making it fair for keyboard players so they implement mechanics to make analogue steering, gas and brake less effective.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, my favourite game of all time is "art of rally". I am in love with its simplistic, yet beautiful graphics and its artistic, yet realistic driving physics. It is the perfect game for me to "pick-up" and play after a busy day. These are the things which I love most about "Circuit Superstars". The graphics are charming. I love the reflections from water features surrounding the racetracks and the trees gently swaying in the breeze. It doesn't look realistic, but like "art of rally", it isn't meant to. The driving physics is really intuitive; if you get your tyres on the grass, your car will probably spin. This is what makes it satisfying - when you finally master a corner or overtake your opponent smoothly around a corner, swooping down the inside. There are currently not too many cars to choose from, however they are all excellent. There are fast 1960s and 1980s F1 cars and the equally terrifying Le Mans prototype cars, and then there are slower hatchback cup cars, trophy trucks, and even European truck racers! It is worth noting that more and more cars (and indeed tracks - see below) are being added. But currently, there is plenty to get your teeth stuck into!There are enough racetracks to keep you entertained for a very long time. As mentioned before, more and more tracks are being added over the coming months. The tracks are excellent - with fast corners and more technical ones. There are also tracks with a variety of surfaces, so you can race on all tarmac tracks, and a mixed gravel/tarmac track. There is something for everyone. The tracks are also not too large, so it is easy to learn the track relatively quickly. Circuit Superstars has plenty to offer the "driver". - It has a "Free Play" option, where you can race against the AI, setting the car, track(s) and AI difficulty level to hone your racing skills. - Grand Prix Mode - a career where you can compete against the AI. A good place to start if you have just bought the game.- It also has online racing (see next point)- Weekly time trials to test yourself against the best (i.e not me).- Garage - where you can pimp your ride and customise driver wear.The online community in this game is excellent. They have a discord server which will offer you support, and has a great community of online racers, who are always happy to help new racers! I have found that the best time to race online (when there are most people online) is at around 20:00 GMT. You can also put forward any suggestions for the future and any bugs you find. You can also see if there are any community events that you can participate in which are happening. Circuit Superstars is an incredible game. Great work developers! If you are someone with a busy schedule, and is looking for a game that they can pick-up and play for 30 minutes, this is the game for you! It is easy to drive in, but difficult to master and compete with the best. I am looking forward to seeing how this game progresses.If you have any questions, please feel free to comment down below, and I will try to respond ASAP. Thank you for reading this review, and have a nice day!

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is a difficult one. It looks very nice, plays smooth, sound and music are ok.The ai is not the best, but i could look past that.The thing that is really annoying is the car handling, as they automatically "counter-steer" when you stop turning.You exit a corner, your car is turned at the perfect angle, so you stop turning and straighten out the steering. But the car then does not drive in a straight line, no it turns to the opposite direction, meaning you always have to turn the car more. And this is not understeering, this is straight up turning. Why would a car ever turn in the opposite direction when you exit a corner? Just horrible to drive as you always have to guess how much more you have to turn the car to get a good corner exit. If this was not an issue i'd highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Auto racing began 5 minutes after the second car was built." is a racing video game developed and published by Original Fire Games!In main Single Player mode of the game called "Grand Prix" you will venture into the diverse, dangerous and always fast world of motorsport. Compete in tournaments and show off your skill in vehicles from all categories of racing to earn victories and prove you got what it takes to be a circuit superstar!Circuit Superstars, which should come as no surprise, has circuit racing as the core gameplay, though an interesting aspect is perspective as game is played from top-down isometric view, standing out from most racing games in that department. Race, improve, win, repeat!Before you drive off onto a track however, you have to select a tournament or race to participate in, vehicle if such option is possible and livery. Those who know a thing or two about motorsports will notice that cars and tracks are "inspired" by real life. In main "Grand Prix" mode there are only tournaments and every driver has same vehicle. Formula of events is similar to actual racing weekends, first you have a Qualifying session where on a single hot lap you fight for best possible time to determine your position on the grid. (And you can get a point for Pole Position!) Afterwards you get ready for a race, reach highest place possible to score as many points as you can, with main goal being victory and glory that comes with it. Have most points after 5 races (that many each Tournament has in Grand Prix mode) to win whole thing and unlock further tournaments!Racing itself is a blend of intense and short lenght arcade style of races where cars will bump one another every once in a while, with realistic driving physics as our vehicle behaves authentically on different surfaces, a penalty system, tyre wear, fuel consumption and vehicle damage simulation! All aspects are tracked by gauges on the screen. So keep an eye on those meters while racing! In longer races pit stop is a must, so the game allows for some strategic maneuvers thanks to unique pitstop system where we have full control over the car in the pit lane, including option of going out earlier because who needs a fuel tank or all tyres swapped?All actions during a race and qualifying earn you experience points, gathering 2000 of them grants you a level up and unlocks new cosmetic items, such as patterns or liveries.Speaking of, customization! In Garage you can change visually how you and your car look, with our driver having option of picking different helmet and suit, plus emotes (how our character looks idle in main menu and how he is celebrating a podium), while vehicles come with different liveries and patterns available.It took me 9 hours to make through every tournament once.Of course you can give them a spin on other difficulties and if game will click with you, additional modes will have you spend solid amount of hours in improving and enjoying the game further!Like a proper racing game should, Circuit Superstars comes with a selection of additional gamemodes!If you need some training, check out Practice mode where you pick a track and car to...well, practice. As name Free Play suggests, here you make races and/or whole tournaments on your own rules, with AI or friends to compete!In Time Trial, you get a designated car and track, do your best and get fastest time to climb up the ranking, with trials changing weekly!And there is Online component where you can drive against up to 11 other drivers, in randomized single races. While game has a Crossplay feature, bear in mind you might have a hard time finding other drivers.While first hour, perhaps two, were...not quite fun, with me fighting tooth and nail against weakest AI to keep my precious podiums as I was adjusting to the game- after few extra hours under the belt Circuit Superstar became what devs wanted, a tough yet enjoyable simcade racer, featuring intense fight for wins where a single wrong move can decide whole race due to their short lenght. Something that I personally really like. The need to be precise, practice, and fight for every tenth of a second cut from a lap until you fully immerse with every lap driven. It's worth mentioning game doesn't have any sort of "rubberbanding", most of the time it pushes hard from start to finish so you better don't blink or run out of breath while fighting on every corner, although AI overall has balancing issues. Unique camera view and manual pistop mechanic is spicing up the game right from the start, with solid selection of tracks and vehicles to drive to keep your interest. Soundtrack while limited to main menu, will put you right in the mood with groovy tracks inspired by different time eras. Customization is simple and gives just enough for every player to spend few minutes on making sure his car looks unique.It doesn't take a genius to point out that additional modes are a massive positive, further letting you enjoy the game, giving you a reason to stick around and making it a very good choice for party/couch title pick, if you seek something to play with (or against) friends every once in a while and have fun!But not all is sunshine and rainbows on Circuit Superstars paddock. Unfortunately AI is the biggest problem. It's "adaptive", meaning awful. After first Grand Prix, where I was fighting hard for best possible position, next up was a "sunday church drive" type of an experience, as I without any problems pulled away from my opponents. But few races later, the teethclenching experience came out again. Calling it unbalanced, is putting it lightly. Plus game has a rather funny issue with pitstops, where AI especially on lower difficulties, can pit twice in a row, giving you a free victory in the process. Why? I don't know!What personally annoyed me is a fact the previously mentioned "tyre wear, fuel consumption and vehicle damage simulation!" is nothing more than a gimmick so you can waste a moment on pitting. Ultimately there is no actual managing it, because AI always gives 100% and so you do have to too, giving zero room to, for example, lift-and-coast in order to save fuel. Sure you can try it, but you will save a mere percent or two that won't change race outcome while AI will gain much, much more charging behind you. There is only one tyre compound so you don't even have any option to toy around with different tyre options. Game also doesn't have night racing nor rain to spice up the races, though I have to say- detail of rubber left on most optimal raceline, making it darker as race goes on, and dirt tracks being cleaner on optimal line thanks to drivers sweeping it is very cool.Ultimately, I still had an intense yet fun time with the game. It's...good, but few tweaks here, small addition there and it could elevate into something great, even fantastic. I hope rumours of devs working on a sequel are true! For now though, I can recommend this, mainly for fans of motorsports or those who seek a racing game to play on a couch with buddies, as previously stated. One has to also remember this is a small game made my only few people, so I also didn't expect something grand. A solid first title with room for improvement.If you, like me, got curious about a game due to Top Gear DLC then jokes on us! Because said DLC is no longer available. You have to dive into the vast ocean of internet to find a key if interested, and if there are any left to snatch.A fun simcade title, Circuit Superstars plays nicely thanks to short, intense racing mixed with realistic driving physics, though overall motorsport aspects need more polish. Recommended nonetheless!Feel free to check out  for more reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all I need to play to leave a glowing review. I was a little on the fence about buying because from the video I wasn't sure this game would be right for me, even though the other reviews are quite stellar... Just watching the video, it seemed to look a little "arcade"-y, like maybe it might be a little more like Mario Kart and a little less like racing. Boy, did this game take me by surprise. Only a few hours in and I know this is one I'll be returning to over and over.I can say without a doubt that the decision to not wait for it to go on sale has not left me dissatisfied. I paid full price and I don't regret it one bit - even being an early access game.So yes, it looks a little arcade-y in the video, but in the actual gameplay it doesn't feel that way at all. The sounds give you that same heart-slamming feeling you might get going to a real race (which is a bit of a thing of mine) - the engines are screaming, you can hear the strain as they fight to crank faster. Although it's zoomed out and top-down, it doesn't look dumb, either - it's actually really nice and graphics you can get into.This game just... feels very natural. Everything about it feels "right." I never get that feeling of "oh, whatever!" you sometimes get when playing racing games (and if you've played a few, you know what I'm talking about - you try to take a section of track at a certain speed or angle, something happens that doesn't feel natural, and you think, "ugh, whatever, this feels like weird coding." Yeah, you don't get that in this game.) The controlling is so natural - even though it's a top-down with a camera fixed from one angle, it's never a "struggle" to get your controlling to translate to the car. (What I mean about that: with some of these fixed-angle camera games, sometimes I'll try to bust a move, and think... no, wait, I should've hit the key for the opposite direction.. darn it, I wish this was first-person!) You always feel in control and know what to do.Another neat thing about this one, despite being fixed-angle: the devs apparently put a LOT of thought into the camera zooming and track layout. First of all, the camera zooming is so subtle you don't even notice it - unlike some games which will pull massive zoom-in/zoom-outs that can be disorienting, this one makes the zoom very natural so it doesn't interrupt your focus. Also, the way they laid everything out and focus the camera in helpful ways, this is also NOT one of those games where you essentially have to memorize the track layout in order to do well on the track (essentially making it more of a memory game than a skill game) - while knowing the track very well may give you an advantage, you can still do very decently on a track even if it's your first time running it, so long as you have the feel of how the vehicle interacts with the road.Speaking of which, the physics are absolutely amazing and contribute fantastically to the gameplay. When they say you can feel the tires bite into the road, they aren't lying - you can almost feel it when you gain traction and start taking off. Start veering off the road, and you'll FEEL the tires slipping on the grass (or whatever) - go too far and you might even spin out.The game has a perfect balance between edge-of-your-seat action and snoozefest - it's definitely not slow enough to be boring, but not so fast-paced that you have to chug seven gallons of coffee to get stimulated enough to participate. You're always excited, but never so pushed that you feel like a single blink will leave you veering into a wall.The wear-and-tear mechanics adds a wonderful element of strategy to the race. You have to keep an eye on overall car health, fuel, and tire wear. In shorter races, so long as you keep your car in good repair, you might not need to pit, but in longer races it's absolutely essential to have a strategy of when to pit, and even how long. (For example in a 12-lap race, you might wait long enough to get repaired, 4 new tires, and a splash of gas to make it to the finish... but for a 20-lap race, it might make sense to wait for full service.) The pit-stop system also "makes sense" and is not intrusive to play. For example in some games that have pit stops, every time you drive down pit road you get the sense that you're about to get screwed, Not so in this one if you're doing well.I VERY much like the fact that this game is entirely player skill based. You don't "upgrade" your cars or driver - those stay the same. It's your skill and how you handle the cars that improves. That makes the online portion VERY fair - when I race against others, no one is winning because they've upgraded their stuff a million times - they're winning because they're just better racers.Each little car has a different way of handling. It's very challenging and TONS of fun to figure each type out and how they should drive. Love it! Same with the tracks - each one has its own set of challenges, none of them "unfair," all of them a challenge of skill.The actual race is a challenge as well. Seems like some games, the one who gets ahead, stays ahead. Not so here. Played plenty of races where I thought it was a sure thing and ended up, say, fifth due to whatever reason.. and plenty of games where I was lagging behind and made a sudden come-back later on. Some racing games, if you have a bad start, you rage-quit and start the race over... with this one, no matter what's going on, you weirdly don't find yourself restarting the race over and over just to get that "perfect start." It's soooo nice to play a racing game in which I begin a race and I'm happily engaged from start to finish.Overall? This is (quite weirdly) quickly becoming one of my favorite racing games of all time. A TRUE gem in the wild. I actually don't usually prefer this type, either - I like the kind with chase cameras or first-person cameras... but somehow this one has captured me and won't let go. I see a LOT more playtime to come... WORTH EVERY PENNY, IF YOU'RE ON THE FENCE ABOUT THIS ONE JUST PULL THE TRIGGER. (I'd like to see more folks in multiplayer lol) They say this was a game created BY race fans FOR race fans, and let me tell you, YOU CAN TELL.

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit Superstars is a fun little game that you can pick up anytime and play. It has a decent selection of tracks and classes of cars, offering an experience somewhere between an arcade and simulation racer. The game offers five levels of difficulty and in that aspect caters to a variety of players with different skill levels and preferences. From Master level onwards, the game does become very challenging. Nevertheless, whichever difficulty you are playing in, the racing is actually engaging and is in my opinion a very good simulation of the basic elements of real-life motor racing. The top down view is very good, with the camera moving alongwith the corners in each track and the controls are simple and straightforward. Circuit Superstars is a good game with the potential to be a great one.However, despite its apparent completeness and wholesomeness, the game is incomplete in surprising ways. Surprising simply because in its current state, it lacks certain basic features and options that are present even in bad racing games. While the game is technically still in early access and while the developers are still rolling out updates and patches, I don't see why they have not responded yet to certain suggestions that the community has been requesting since long.Currently, 1. the game does not have a solo free practice mode and this baffles and frustrates me. In a game like this where the driving is actually fun and challenging at the same time, a free practice mode would be great and I think should be an essential feature. Why can't I just select a car, a track and drive as many laps as I would like to? 2. I don't know why I cannot restart a race after I have begun it. When pausing in between a race, I can only go back to the main menu or the desktop and have to start all over again. This is very strange. Why isn't there an option to simply restart? Also, why isn't there an options/settings menu when pausing in the middle of a race. These are a few examples of the basic features that you expect in any decent racing game or any video game for that matter. 3. Whether in Grand Prix mode or custom tournament, why can I not save my progress and come back later to finish the tournament? Currently, you have to finish any tournament or championship in one sitting and for there to be no option to save the progress confounds me. There are other issues which I have listed separately in the discussion board and don't feel like listing all of them again here. In short, the game is very good but I am concerned as to how the developers have neglected to include some standard features and modes. I hope they prioritise and incorporate these suggestions soon in the coming updates. I was gifted the game so clearly no regrets about the pricing. However, I would suggest that you wait for the developers to finish polishing the game and then buy it maybe at full price or just wait for it go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The AI is pretty bad, every single car follows the same line with absolutely zero variation. Collisions are meaningless, since the cars will make minute adjustments whenever bumped to get back into their lane.There are also zero mistakes from AI drivers on even the lowest difficulty levels, leading to a fairly stagnant experience.I don't know whether the devs expect these issues to be hidden by a reliance on people searching for opponents online, but it's unacceptable in its current iteration. I wouldn't recommend Circuit Superstars until the devs focus on improving their incredibly limited racing AI.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with the game and the driving mechanics are really nice, but after some point I was bored due to the lack of progression/things to do.- There is no tutorial, so you will have to learn everything on your own (or search online): car behaviors, tracks, fuel save, tyre save, etc..- There is no ranking system, so if you are a casual player, you will almost be at the last positions in every online race.- There is no career mode, or some progression mechanism. You will only get some helmets / skins, which adds nothing to the game.- Sadly, there are very few people playing it. So most probably you will end up in a completely random lobby (after some waiting time) when playing it onlineI also found some annoying problems like:- There is no speedometer, which is very weird for a racing game.- No way to save progress during long GP- Some issue with final standings where the opponent's times were not shown.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Easiest recommendation for quite some time.Had this title since early access and the quality simply shines through, i honestly think this is the most fun top down racer i have ever played. It very much reminds me of an old Amiga title Skidmarks but with the graphics taken up several gears.Talking of the graphics they have got them spot on perfectly capturing the balance between realistic and cartoony and it's a joy to watch races unfold on the excellent replay feature.So lots different races to take part in with various types of vehicles (F1 to trucks) and plenty of tracks to race on.There's weekly challenges and online racing which can be a tad frustrating when you are slow like me and you're getting battered at the back of the pack but rather than annoying me it encourages me to get better (work in progress)So in summary great game at a very reasonable price, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: My edited review:This game is GREAT. GREAT I tell you! Graphics:The graphics are bright and cartoon-ish, yet deep and detailed. It's a beautiful mix of realism and simplicity which is downright perfect for this game. Lighting effects, shadows, dust, debris, rubber, oh my! Just fantastic!Gameplay:Do you like racing? Well, here's some racing. Actually, a lot of racing. Like, so much racing you might not be able to handle it. Each car has a unique handling profile, each track has a unique atmosphere, and there are so many of them. After you're finished customizing your cars and driver, you'll find yourself faced with a choice of what to do next. Time trials? Single races? Championships? Online races? All of the above, please. AI present a challenge, but are rather predictable. I haven't gotten too high on the difficulty scale, but I haven't had any glaring issues with them (other than they beat me). Tire wear and fuel usage simulation lead to some interesting pit stop strategies, whether they work out or not.... Besides sliding through the turns, or guessing when you'll hit "E", there are percentages displayed for tire wear, fuel, and damage. It will even tell you when you NEED fuel.The game will also reward your progress with customization options, which I find to be satisfactory.In my previous review, I wrongfully compared this game to another favorite of mine. While they do have a lot in common, they are completely their own games. Circuit Superstars will always be on my desktop. CONGRATULATIONS to the team for this incredible accomplishment! It truly is fantastic, and I can't wait to see what's in store!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is my updated review as of 7/7/23. This game has id good but I feel there is still some much needed improvement. The Pros: The Graphics are nice and are light weight. The physics feel really good with a proper skill gap. They have a sim-ish feel so everything feels grounded in reality. Every car in each class handles much differently than cars in other classes. There is a lot of different car classes, which is nice. 4 Player split screen which is extremely rare nowadays. They added lobbies so you can create one or join one, such as your friends on any platform the game is on. There is slipstream so you are able to pass on straights, tracks with good variety. There is penalties in multiplayer. The Cons: There is only one vehicle per class. Also for some reason the 2 vehicles in the Announcement trailer of the game aren't in the game? There is what looks to be a similar to a C7.R which would go perfectly with the Panther (911 RSR) in game. So there would be 2 GT cars instead of just one. The other vehicle that's in the announcement trailer but not in game is what looks to be similar to a Jaguar E-Type. Which would be a pretty cool addition to the game as well. I dont know why these cars aren't in the game when they are shown to be fully functional in the announcement trailer. Single Player kinda gets old but at least there is some progression now. You can unlock a bunch of other livery styles for your driver and cars. But overall the game is good especially with friends and family, very fun to play. I still think there needs to be some better progression. As well as dynamic weather to help make each race feel completely different. Which would also include rain and possibly even snow on some tracks which will help add a lot of replay ability. As well as multiple cars in even class so everyone is not driving the same car.

_childDocuments_.review: Would love to see in the future:- Time difference between back and front opponent per lap- Pitstop strategy- Play with friends ability- More tracks and cars setup online cause it gets boring fast and people will stop playing i'm afraidThe pro's that are finished to me: - Graphics look awesome- Physics of the car are good to, don't know of they have different handling but would be awesome (Handling is different per car. - You feel the curbs and dirt! awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Immense potential! Many tracks and Car Classes, but only 1 car per class as of writing. Crafted by a small team of 5, the base of the game is great with minimal bugs. Pros: -Easy to jump in and out, laps can be set from 1 - 99 with up to 12 AI racers. -Decent Track selection as of writing, 7 tracks with 1 being mixed dirt and pavement -Variety of Racing Disciplines, 60s and 80s GP, Caterham Featherlights, GT3, Trophy Trucks, Euro Trucks -Car handling is good with each car type feeling differently. Simcade handling/performance (Arcade with a dash of Simulation) -Car damage affects your performance, tire wear affects your grip, and gas usage, all of which can be disabled, or increased/decreased to your preference -Graphics are nice with no stuttering or lag -Music reminds me of Hot Shots Golf, very chill -Track gets wear and rubber is laid on the track from repeated laps -Multiplayer and Remote Play Together is enjoyable -Private lobbies are coming soon, and developers are doing Weekly updates and being open with what they're working on. -Lots of visual vehicular customization and your driver character. Cons:Only 1 car per discipline currently, and only 1 dirt track.AI can be brutal and punt you off the trackNo alternate racing lines the AI take to get around youNo Career mode yetIncreasing difficulty just seems to increase the AI top speed, they don't really drive any differently, too perfect in their lines.No car tuning or performance upgrades, etc.Additions I'd like to see:I hope they add more variety of cars per discipline, even if they have the same handling stats. More disciplines like Rallycross (with Joker lap), F1, DTM, NASCAR, Buggies, LMP, Mixed Class Racing, Drifting could be interesting. Dirt tracks are a must, Jumps, mud/river crossings, different weather conditions(rain, snow, lightning), Night Racing, Career mode, Time based endurance racing could be nifty, even better if you can swap the same car with friends to work together with pits and driving. Otherwise for being in early access for just under 2 months, the game is great! Looking forward to watching and playing the development of this title. Keep up the good work Original Fire Games.

_childDocuments_.review: It is circuit a racing game (well, duh) like others in competitive-racing-sport-whatnot type genre. In it, player will have to do the same things that define the genre: learning tracks, learning vehicles, managing fuel, using draft, overtaking and trying to be consistent to a highest degree. What makes the game to stand out is lap length. Most of tracks can be completed in (less than) 30 seconds. Which means that you can experience main attributes of the genre in 3 minutes races. That is what made me stick with the game - it was not eating my time. In other words, condensed entertainment.This however was what made me quit the game too. 10 - 15 tracks that are in the game at the moment, became boring after 30 hours of play (so fast, oh no!). The game started to turn into more of a chore than fun.That's the main topic that I wanted to cover, anyway, there's a bit more.* The games has custom race mode, where you can set your own tournament (Grand Prix type of race) with custom parameter values for fuel consumption, damage, tire wear.* Online is barely active :-/. I had no luck with it, at least.* Competitive hot lapping still has 500-1000+ players every week.* Pascal Michael Stiefel did great job composing tracks for the game, in my opinion. Every track was produced referencing a different decade (from 70s to 10s). I just love it.* The game does not have FPS limit, so you can run it on your fancy monitor at full speed.* I did not encounter any bugs of crashes.* AI has tiers. In the same tournament, some AI's are better than others most of the time, however even on lower difficulties all AIs rarely do mistakes or use sub-optimal racing lines. This would not be a big deal IF there was a bigger online activity. For someone who is not accustomed to this type of racing even 10 lap races could feel like endurance racing what would lead to not performing as well in later stages of a race. Instead of behaving as rookie or pro or whatnot, AI has its speed controlled by difficulty, which leads to such stupid situations where I was gaining on AI in straights just because their max speed was slower than mine. We still can't get anything better AI wise than Race Driver: GRID (2008)...So that's it. Pretty good for "a very small team of 5".

_childDocuments_.review: The driving is fun, the graphics are nice, the sound is decent.However...The tyre-deg feature seems to be binary. I feel no difference in performance at 100 or 10 tyre wear. If it falls to 0 though the car becomes an undrivable mess.There is no point in underfueling your car, as it has exactly zero impact on performance as well, unless you run out.This means that there is no pitstop strategy. It is an obligation with absolutely nothing behind it.The AI... Oh boy. From my observation they only have 2 possible behaviours:1) Driving like the player isnt there -> came out of a corner side by side, having the racing line and the other car just straight up slammed into side and kept pushing into me to get onto the line2) Actively trying to murder the player -> actually getting of the racing line despite it costing them time, only to shove the player off-track, forcing penalties onto youThey also appear to need fewer pit-stops (very apparent in long distance races where I had to pit every 10 laps and the AI every 13) and ontop of that their pit-stops are straight up faster than yours.I came in just ahead of another car that was pitting (first stop for both). I reach my pit box about 1s sooner and only need refueling and tyre change. The other car somehow is off again already when my mechanics have bearly finished on the tyres.Online appears to be dead. Whenever I tried to find a game it put me into a lobby with only one other player... Rivetting.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun arcade-sim driving game. There is plenty of variety in vehicles and tracks, and there is a lot of subtlety to each, which is fun to slowly improve at and master.I mostly play the game as a time-trial game. The time trial mode resets every week with 3 new combinations of vehicles and tracks. It's a really calming experience to try and chase down your ghost, and lap by lap slowly develop better lines and see where time can be made and lost.The racing against AI doesn't feel tuned too well. One Pro-Am, I am lapping other racers, and on Pro, I struggle to be mid of the pack. The leader of the race always gains a huge lead over the rest of the field, and is often impossible to chase down. But that said, its still kinda fun to make really aggressive overtakes. Always take the inner lane.I have not been able to join any online race. So I can't say how that would be. The youtube videos do seem nice though.
