_childDocuments_.review: A fun game with loads hours of fun especially when playing with friends.Things I like:- Easy to learn hard to master (think TMNF)- Remote play together/ local Multiplayer support- Fun physics/handling- superb soundtrackThinks I do not like:- Sometimes it would be nice to have a car-oriented view (Though i can understand why thats not a thing).Thinks I'd like to see added:- Gap time view to car in front and behind- Toggle switcht for penalties- A mark/symbol for my pit-position on the mini-map (I allways forget where my pit is and only know when i see it, knowing beforehand would be nice.)- Map editor (someday?)- Nintendo Mario kart 8 style chat in the lobby- quick emotes for races (selectable via d-pad)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone remembers Skidmarks from the early 90s on Amiga or Console, this is what Circuit Superstars reminds me of, in look and feel. However something to keep in mind is that the attitude of this game is a semipro race sim - you don't need to tune car parts or have a long campaign of races but the AI Competition is quite tough and drive professionally, so any arcade-style driving will likely fall behind in the pack.Despite my pride, I found that Amateur difficulty (the lowest...) was in my wheelhouse; in some cases I could do the sem-pro difficulty, but any higher and I was just Sunday Driving.The GFX are really nice, in a "cute" kind of way, but I found myself on many occasions distracted by the background and wanting to see what was beyond my reach.The tracks are well made as pro race tracks - there are a couple that are suited to a more bump-n-jump style but those are few and far between and only for a select few cas (e; Rally cars, Monster Trucks, Sprint Cars) however I never got bored of the tracks and fond myself ever-learning the curves of each. Although my pet hate track was Thunder Point... I don't know why but I just always had trouble with that one.I had a lot of fun with this game and my very distant hope would be they add some "bumpy" courses in for that "Skidmarks itch" (ahem..) but after listening to a podcast with a couple of the devs, I believe their intentions for this game is to be a time-shaving type racer, so aimed more to the pro-racing folk.

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent arcade racer that's easy to get into with a very high skill ceiling. I've played for 630 hours according to Steam but I've probably spent a good chunk of that time editing my player avatar and color schemes for my cars.It definitely takes a bit to get used to the top-down orientation but with how small some of the tracks are and how fast some of the cars are it's necessary in order to process how quickly everything happens. Like many other racing games and real life racing in general the way you get better is to practice.There's many cars with their own unique driving characteristics varying from being extremely fast and responsive to slow and cumbersome, and it's a ton of fun for me having to make the adjustments on the fly in online play in order to succeed. There's also just as many tracks that all the cars react differently to and it's great at constantly keeping me on my toes and seeking to improve more.There is also an established playing community that is active and willing to help players improve on Discord. The devs also communicate their future intentions with the game and it is crossplay compatible with Xbox and Playstation, so it is a game that will stick around.I enjoy the variety of cars, tracks, and customization options greatly and have had a blast in online play but like with any games there are some issues. Latency definitely exists the game and depending on your internet connection and what region of the world the server is you're connected to your online races can vary from perfectly fine to barely playable. Other players around the world also have the same issue and it does create some moments where the connection stutters and you're not in full control of the car. The devs had said this is one of the highest priorities to them for the next update so I would hope I can delete this part of the review in the near future.Some other suggestions I have for the improvement of the game are:- Being able to toggle ghosts on and off during practice and time trial- Some more reverse courses of existing tracks that don't already have them- Hexcode for paint colors so that it's easier to copy-paste the color you want- More paint schemes for the cars, along with more designs for the driver's helmet and suit- Some type of career mode for Offline play that offers a set progression and familiarity for players instead of just chucking multiple options at players and overwhelming them- Different cars for the same categories, example would be the Porsche expy in GT being able to be changed to a Ferrari, Mercedes, or some other GT car expy with its own set of paint schemes available
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes you truly feel like a race car driver.All jokes aside, this is a nice game from its menus, presentation, vehicle variety, and physics. Also, its tire wear and fuel consumption makes this more sim like, which definitely sets this 'arcade racer' apart from others.While this game is definitely not for me due its isometric camera, I know you can't really go wrong getting this if you like this style of camera and game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit Superstars is one of those games that feels like it was made just for the Steam Deck. All of my time spent so far has been on the Deck, with no issues at all.Overall a great racing game to grab if you don't have the time for a long gaming session. The handling models for the various cars stand out immediately, and the Grand Prix mode gives you a reason to try out everything. It's just easy enough that it stays enjoyable, but there's still a lot of skill involved in putting good times in. The livery editor is another thing that I enjoyed as well. I've got to make my car as red as possible, I'm pretty sure it adds extra horsepower when you do that! ;-)I've finished the Grand Prix mode on the middle difficulty or higher, and the AI can put up a good challenge. Learning the car you're driving is a must if you want to play in the higher levels. I haven't touched Online mode as I currently have no interest in it. It may be something I try in the future. The Time Trials are a nice option, and I've spent a little while trying to work my way up the leaderboard.There are some things that could be improved, but they're not game breaking. I wouldn't mind seeing some more vehicle variety other than colors. While it's all right for all Formula One, trophy trucks, sprint cars, etc. to look exactly the same, it's a bit funny when every muscle car is exactly the same! The AI on lower difficulty levels can also be a little dumb, they will sometimes stack up on a sharp turn and be stuck there for 15+ seconds. It would also be great to have more options for racing in the Grand Prix mode, but I can understand that the replay value of the game is geared toward the online aspect.Overall it's a very enjoyable game, and definitely worth the money. Especially if you can find it on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr - The game has a fun arcade artstyle, but is deceptively challenging. Id recommend it to those who enjoy shaving time off their laps and conquering corners. This was a hard review to write. I want to call this an arcade racer because of the camera angle and art style, but I dont think it would appeal to those looking for an arcade experience. This is a racing game that is truly won or lost out of the corners. Unlike an arcade racer, I haven't found a cheap gimmick to win races. You either focus and execute in the corners, or you lose. AND I LOVE IT. No vehicle tuning, No upgrades. Just pick a race and drive.There is a timetrial mode where you can compete against the online community weekly, and theres ranks/progression.Cons: I have yet to successfully queue an online race.The tire wear and fuel consumption do seem a bit shallow, but it does allow you to /lightly/ strategize when you will execute your single pitstop.  Each grandprix has its own race length regardless of difficulty (i.e. rally 5 laps, street car 7 laps, etc). The longest grand prix is 15 laps. I would like to see more variety of race lengths or an endurance mode where races are longer and pitstops are more meaningful.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: A nice time killer but not fleshed out enough for its robust vehicle selection.There's times where Circuit Superstars feels empty or unpolished despite its appearances. A solid style and theme goes a long ways in a game like this and the art direction here is top notch. Under the hood all the variety is genuine variety. The cars handle wholly unique while still feeling like they exist in the same universe as each other. It's a fun game to play... Very casually. There's just not enough granular options and details in the game to want to push beyond that. No incentives. Nothing to build towards. No teaching or nurturing of actual racecraft that seemingly works here more than most other attempts at "realistic" top-down racing. No guide or path to improvement. No implied strategy options. Far too streamlined of a "Grand Prix" mode with little to no options. You have to bring everything yourself. The game really suffers from having such a broad foundation but such little built upon it. For a product so focused on quality racecraft, it leaves out so, so much and assumes far too much of the player.All that said, I actually think Circuit Superstars would have benefited most from being more specialized rather than built out. Which is why I'm not surprised to see the team's next entry with Karting Superstars is just that. I look forward to checking that out down the road. But here, I think Circuit Superstars should have picked a style of racing and fleshed out the actual GAME part of the game more. Whether it was just a top-down DiRT or gave us some longer GT races with fuel, tire strategies and teams, it could've been much better. As it stands, it just isn't something worth diving into deep.It's just another top-down racer not worth more than casual time killing entertainment. Which it works for that! It's plenty fun, handles fine, looks great. I've enjoyed it plenty and will play more still. But just can't help but notice the couldas and shouldas.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING!!!   Now let me tell you why.I started doing racing games as a sim racer. I would not settle for anything that wasn't real. I ended up hitting a wall... I would get in the top 100 lap times but why wasn't I getting among-st the best? I spent 8 hours some days practicing. Watched initial D then something special happened. In my frustration and my love of racing I started playing Top down racers because I wanted to be a top racer. This took me back to school so to speak.Although they were arcade and not a sim it started teaching me something Sim racing couldn't. I started seeing new lines on the track. Different approaches and I started compensating for silly physics. Although i was getting all of this it still wasn't totally satisfying my Motorsport itch.  So i went back to sim racing... There I became a hot lap champion. I was truly fast!!! I stated switching between arcade and top-down and sim racers. I added more tools to my box.     This game is truly special..it brings something a top down racer really lacks.  Real racing tactics....If you think your going to hold the pedal down and pick the right approach to a corner in this game your wrong. You have tire wear,body wear and engine wear. It is tough to get a clean pass as it should be. This game is for those who have passion for the perfect lap. If you could just win at this game in a few laps.. its not worth your time.... This game takes practice this is the essence of Motorsport racing. You will wait for you moment... put the pressure on and wait for that sweet pass.          This game is a piece of racing art!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: If you know absolute gem Gene Rally game from late 2000s (you can still get it online) you love Gene Rally already. Loving Gene Rally, you'll love Circuit Superstars.This little arcade racer has on its DNA a very palpable physics. Turn your wheel too much and you'll burn you tires up making you lose time on your stint. You'll count with 100% manual pitstops besides speed limiter.This is a gameplay carbon copied from Gene Rally with AAA treatment around the edges, although the view angle is from up close following your car in contrary to the Gene Rally birds eye view of the whole track always.The online is pretty nice and there is a ranked mode.BEWARE: Being such a silly racer with decent physics, the races will BE VERY DIRTY.1- The tracks are very tight and car control is very.....simple. Not bad but you'll be making contact with another car A LOT.2- It is a arcade racer with NO contact penalty. The only penalty involved on ramming will be damage to your engine (lower power) and the high possibility of facing the wrong way while the races are very tight.If you miss manage your car, you'll face consequences.If you spin, you'll get to the end of the pack.This little game made me go back to Assetto Corsa Competizione in early 2022 by how great it is on portraying real pure racing.PURE racing is key. The devs know what's up.This is the best circuit arcade hilarious racer game there is.You'll count with classes in the like of: Prototypes, GT3, Classic GT, F1, Rally, Stadium Super Trucks, Classic and 80s F1, Minis etc...Is a good fun, and will bring you back to racing sims if you have them on the back of the playlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: First review ever!! :DThis game is amazing! The potential it has for both casual and competitive players is incredible.  If the player base for this game grows the quality of the racing could be better here than any other game out there.  The top down perspective makes close racing incredibly enjoyable and it makes it very easy to see where you are gaining or losing time to the car you are racing against.The fuel, damage, & tire wear additions add a fun strategy component to the game and can provide near endless possibilities for race lengths and strategy.For the price of this game I can promise you it's worth it for potentially more fun races then you will have on many other titles, if this game could become popular enough to house a robust matchmaking/rank system this would be the most addicting thing of all time... also if you enjoy this game but don't usually leave reviews (and you're somehow seeing this, please consider leaving a review just for the potential of truly how amazing this could be with even more people playing and I'm sure every positive review helps! To give this a negative review in early access for some of connectivity issues or worse giving it a bad recommendation because it can be hard to find a match sometimes would be to ignore the awesome potential this game has & is literally helping contribute to it's only current frustrations! Of course if this kind of game is not for you then sure, but i hope everyone can see the absolute golden experience this game could be in the future!  Yes there is a learning curve and yes it is frustrating to get dusted in a 1v1 race with someone who has obviously been playing forever, but with more people and a wider spread of skill levels playing the rewarding and close racing a title like this can provide can be unmatched!Thank you for your time.**EDIT**I wrote my review before looking at any other reviews.  After taking a look my fears have been confirmed. The negative reviews i'm seeing are basically saying "Super fun, but not enough players and my car stutters" if you like the game but not enough people are playing, then down-voting is literally doing the opposite of helping fix your issue!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Forza style barging your way through the field passing then this is fine. The narrow, short tracks and brief races mean that if you qualify below second you need to barge your way through the field if you are going to win a championship. Every time you hit another car or scenery your car takes damage and is slower. Making the experience quite frustrating. I was looking forward to the extra realism this game offered in the top down racing genre but unfortunately that realism needs a different kind of track and longer races. Both things that this game does not have.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, great driving. A wonderful foundation, but sorely lacks content and functionality.There's simply too little content here, and unfortunately, this doesn't feel like a full release - even for a $20 game. I hope the developers continue to add cars, tracks, skins, progression, online lobbies with filters, as well as add to the time trial mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun racer with very few bugs at this early access stage. The handling model is a lot of fun and the graphics look great! The arcade mode offers 5 championships with differing vehicles at this stage, add that to the time trial mode, race now mode and online mode means there is plenty of racing for your money even at this stage. The online mode offers a variety of races or mini tournaments which are a lot of fun. There was some slight glitching in one online race I did but nothing too severe for a game in early access. Some races are broken up with pit stops which add a layer of strategy to some of the races. ProsGood graphicsFun handling modelOnline and arcade races are fun. Excellent starting point for developments as the early access period continuesEasy to find a race online at this stageConsCould do with more information in some races, for example gaps between competitorsStats page that tracks your races, victories, podiums etc for online and offlineOverall this is an excellent racer that will only get better as the developers add more to this game. The handling model is easy to learn and its fun to drive the difference vehicles on offer. For the price I would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: they completely abandoned this game for "karting superstars", which uses all the same assets and tracks, but has karts.It also uses a stupid camera angle, where you are constantly reminded that the physics aren't realistic. The tires aren't connected to the road, and in a top down perspective you don't notice it, but if you are so close to the kart you can't be not reminded of this.There are almost no new features, it feels just like they wanted to get rid of their publisher, and just made a new game from what was planned for the newest update for circuit superstars.It only has a few new tracks, quickly made with the assets from the old game (so it doesn't look unique) and a few old tracks, not even all old tracks, just a few.Some time ago they promised a quarterly update with new cars and tracks, which just stopped when they made their new "top gear" dlc. Which is just a cash grab if you ask me, especially when you don't give any content for free while it was promised. Now they release a new game, which should have been an update or dlc, and give it a new camera angle as it's main feature, for €17!!! WTF.If this was EA, everyone would be madthis is a negative review for the demo, and concept of karting superstars and its developers, (because i cant give a review on the other page if i only played the demo)i'm only giving a positive because this cute little top-down game is worth your money, and i couldn't post a review on the "karting superstar" page
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed reactions with this one... The game is extremely fun and racing itself is fantastic, however there is a missing feature that I personally find unacceptable in 2021, which is basically not having the possibility to create a private lobby to play just with your friends.We are a group of 4 people who purchased the game at the same time and it was a huge dissapoinment to see that we are not able to create our own race and configure it the way we want. The options are there, but you can only create or join a public lobby with a preset race where you can only choose the circuit. Besides, it's a painful and long process to get people joining... Totally obsolete these days.If they implement that standard feature in the future, I will have no complaints because the game is awesome, but at this stage, I simply cannot recommend it to anyone thinking about playing online with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: GOOD: This game fills a great little niche in the racing genre. No other game matches the complexity of pit strategies with accessible yet thrilling driving mechanics. The presentation on show here is phenomenal with stylized graphics and color pallet, simple but effective UI, and great game feel. Win or lose a race, my time is well spent. What a promising little indie title.NOT SO GOOD: Multiplayer lobbies can have poor connectivity when joining and sometimes I experience weird teleporting/rubberbanding throughout an entire race. Private lobby options are missing (for now).Privy to what lay ahead on Circuit Superstars's roadmap, I can say that I highly recommend this game. I am particularly excited for the inclusion of private lobbies as it will provide the endless replayability I enjoy from Wreckfest and similar titles. Thank you devs for remaining active in the forums and listening to community suggestions.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. Each game played has been exiting and challenging and I'm hoping the game grows with new content and features. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Top-down racer. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: While the driving feels fluid, and the mechanics are solid, lack of economy or upgrades makes replayability shallow for me. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game, unfortunately it's not really entertaining :(Simplistic driving, boring AI. Lack of a main mode. The resource mechanics are basically useless, if you hit anything you lost anyway, so what's the point of slowing you down. They just create a frustrating feedback loop, same with the penalty. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of top-view racing games (Micro Machines, Death Rally back in the DOS days), I think this game shows great promise. Each different car types really responds differently; the controls initially feel pretty slippery and "under steering" and thus very unforgiving, but don't let it put you off: as one gets used to each car types specific physics and handling, playing becomes more and more satisfying and fun. I'd definitly recommand playing with a game controller (although remapping isn't in the options, accel is mapped to both right trigger and A, brake is mapped to both left trigger and X, allowing analog input). In most races even small errors can be fatal and it's definetly challenging to overtake AI cars "cleanly". Tires wear pretty fast even in a small amount of laps, so you really feel the difference between the first lap and the later ones; I didn't try very long races to see how the pit stop mechanic would affect the game play, but I expect it to add some interesting dynamics.As expected the game is light right now content-wise (not many circuits, no car customization yet), but at this stage of development how the cars control is what's important and for me the game nearly nails it. The only improvement I'd like to see is the addition of some kind of drafting effect into the physics simulation.The visuals, although not ground breaking capture nicely the nostalgic/legendary mood of the 50's or 70's motorsports.Finally the game even runs on Linux through Proton (YMMV of course).
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games, but when I do, it's to say how absolutely awesome they are!A light-hearted racing game, reminiscent of RC Pro-Am, Super Sprint and Micro Machines, where you can use real racing knowledge to gain a competitive advantage! (Racing lines, coasting, pit strategies etc.)PROS:- A vast array of different vehicles that handle relative to how they should- Attention to detail is nice- Sweet graphics- A fun arcadey style that you can take as serious as you want- Bumpin' tunes- CUSTOMISATION!CONS:- I hope they release more tracks in the future!- Why didn't I buy this sooner?
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Did you grow up playing games like R.C. Pro-Am like me?  Well, this one is for you!Circuit Superstars is well done for being an early access game.  While it's great to play a first person or third person racing game now and again, this one fits perfectly for a casual race session similar to playing Ivan Stewart's Off-road or R.C. Pro-Am.  Controls are solid and the cars feel great.  You have enough variety of cars and tracks to make it feel interesting and not grinding or grueling.  Saving is a nice feature to be able to pick up where you left off after taking out the garbage.  My only knock is that online is very limited.  It's very hard to find a match.  However, for a single player top down racing game, it's top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little disappointed to find the higher end cars handled in much the same way as the rest, very drifty and steering with the back wheels but faster, but I kept playing and got very invested. The sim elements are really quite fun and the AI is shockingly good, I ended up having a very tight title fight with an AI and only just beat them over the finish line on the last lap of the last race. Great fun!Edit: Just to add if you're playing on Steam Deck to go into the settings and remove the FPS limit, you'll get a consistent 90fps.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The top-down, arcade racer you always wished you could play!A true labour of love, Circuit Superstars is a fun, challenging and rewarding experience that feels familiar yet surprises you at every turn. Handling is fluid but with a nice sprinkle of some real-world physics, it requires you to judge your braking points and hit the apex in order to extract the maximum out of the car. With loads of future content planned, this charming game will only get better with time.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad little top-down racer, but I've got several other top-down cartoon racers and to be honest they're all starting to blur together into one. Perhaps we need some new ideas in this genre. However if you're not like me and want a solid arcade top-down racer then you can't go far wrong with this one,

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- fun, cute gameCons: - very weak single player content, no soul.Huge potential wasted, imagine Crazy cars 3 or super cars 2.- No upgrade your car system, nothing. Bare bones.- no one to play multiplayerIn short:They just focused on physics and graphics.No content, no single player progression immersion nothing.Crazy cars 3 or super cars 2 beats this game.Regret buying this project of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, as someone with 8 years of playing GeneRally I never thought that I'd see a game being able to emulate similar arcade-style racing with simpler way of challenging players with fuel/tire wear/damage up until seeing and playing this quite brilliant racing game. To say that I'm impressed is understatement, so I'll try to give a honest look for my initial score to this game (mostly from single-player perspective).(Keep in mind that this review was written on , i.e only 2,5 weeks after the release of the game)+ Very neat appearance overall, using a cartoony proportions and colorization for a solid appeal.+ Decent performance even on a lesser packed computers.+ Solid way of customizing car/driver colors with several patterns.+ Real fun physics when driving that depend on what car type you pick (heavy, light, understeering, oversteering, etc.) offering good deal of task for practicing tracks.+ Well handled pit-stop mechanism for races with modifiers on.+ Quite neat soundtrack.- Occasional minor framerate drops (mostly when cornering).- All cars have a more sliding cornering style (including Formula- and GT-cars) that can create challenge with handling and managing tires on occasion.- AI-drivers can be somewhat derpy and blissfully ignorant of your presence often pushing you into walls (that said, roadmap states that improved AI is on the way)- Relatively small pool of tracks that often stick to more flat surfacing (again, something that roadmap states the devs are gonna address by adding more tracks with time).While there are some rougher edges scattered here and there along with a price being just at the edge of what I'd find okay (then again, 20€'s for a game like this today is a miracle on its own), my expectations for this game was indeed fulfilled extremely well when I saw it and decided to purchase it outright just a day ago which coupled with solid functions for making races enjoyable and exciting in subtle ways and a solid roadmap promising further enchancements for the game I can confidently say that if one likes to have a casual racer balancing in between arcade-racers and sim-racing,  is a solid option to give a go with.As such, I'll leave this game a nice 8.5/10: having already a solid core gameplay, the future is definitely bright for this game with steady, upcoming content and patches. I can highly recommend on this game from a casual perspective!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I've a bone stuck in my craw with this game. There're several problems - grip, understeer, lack of features, monstrous AI, and a joypad handicap.Cars are constantly slowing down so they can regain grip. It can happen in any corner no matter how fast or slow. If you've already committed to a corner, you'll lose more and more speed until the car is stable again - there's no way to correct the mistake, except to not have made it to start with.The AI have the godly reaction times. They drive visibly slower cars but corner perfectly and will make decisions every frame, allowing them to evade crashes a human would career into. I tested this further and couldn't get one to rear-end me from a brake check at 1 car length.Joypad is a poor choice. Triggers and sticks are barely registered as analogue, and continuous inputs will result in more frames of losing speed if the grip threshold is exceeded. The pro choice is the humble mechanical keyboard; the secretary's favourite. To succeed, you'll want to aim for around 60wpm and learn to type in time to the clapper from La-Bamba.50 hours ago I wanted to love this, and 48 hours ago I did, but since I tried Master difficulty I've felt nothing but inadequacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Alright, the boys did it. The Winter Patch added pretty much everything I griped about in my review below, which I'll keep as is just to show how well the devs have answered complaints. Great job guys, happy to recommend this gem.For a game that wants to "an arcade racer for sim racing fans", this game is just lacking an egregious amount of QoL extras. The inability to simply restart a race is absurd, for example. But probably my biggest complaint of the game as it currently stands, is the damage system. It is simply far too punishing with far too little damage. Anything under 90% health, and you're losing entire seconds off your laps.Combine that with the fact that, even with collision damage set at the minimum of 25%, one good shunt can easily do 10%+ damage, and combine THAT with the fact that the very rudimentary AI has zero awareness of space or race etiquette, and combine THAT with the fact that you can't restart a race, and I find myself either in 7th place or quitting to the main menu after turn 1 of most of my races.It's an entire cluster♥♥♥♥ of questionable design choices that combine to make the game almost unplayable with any amount of realistic damage.To compound all these issues, there's also been a sudden and somewhat concerning lack of updates since.*********************************************************************************************This game is incredibly good-looking for something from a 5-person studio that came out 10 days ago. Unfortunately, it feels like those good-looks mostly serve to disguise how incredibly bare-bones this game is. I realize it's Early Access, but there's absolutely no excuse for things like not letting me skip any screens, ever, at all, or not letting me change keybindings, or not letting me ?Time Trials shouldn't be some weird, curated thing. Let me pick any car, pick any track, and drive around it for as long as I want.In terms of gameplay, the most egregious hole is the AI. Please give us some variation within each difficulty. I just did qualifying for a 10 person grid. All 9 of the AI finished within 0.500 of a second of each other, and 3 of them got the exact same time. Why would I want to race 9 of the exact same person? Difficulty is also very... inconsistent. In the 80s GP car, I lapped the Amateur bots in my first race. I've now put about 5 hours into it, and still get lapped by Pro-Am bots. But apparently the AI is better in some cars than others, because I can win races in the 60s GP car against Pro bots lolOverall, the game looks nice, and has potential (I'm very hopeful!) but that's about it - the lack of polish in every area other than visuals is... painful.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Nice top down racing game, fairly good amount of population and events going on. This games 50ms feels like 200ms on other games. Hopefully in the future more customization options will be made (creating own tracks/cars etc.).Overall I'd recommend it, creates a nice variation to other top down racing games like Art of Rally or Turbo Sliders Unlimited.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has both a sim racing background and also huge love for arcade classics such as Slicks ’n’ Slide, Super Cars 2 and Ivan Ironman's Super Off-Road, this game is super fun and it feels just right. The controls are good even with and without analog gamepad.Things I would like to see improvements are some variation and mistakes for AI racing lines and possibility to save championship progress between races.I can highly recommend this game. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Updated as of 21st August 2022.-------------------------------------------As stated by other reviewers, the August summer update has removed our Grand Prix progress! I can also confirm that the grid order seems to be based off championship position during a Grand Prix so if you are leading, you start from the back in the following races. Aside from the new name tags and a new type of car, it feels the same as before. Original review--------------------This review is for single player only. Circuit Superstars is a fun little racer that blends a few of my favourite games into one. It reminds me of Super Skidmarks but has a little bit of a 'sim racer' slant. To explain, there are both race pit strategies as well as different 'feels' for each of the types of car requiring a specific driving style for that car.There is fun to be had and throwing it up the inside of a rival is satisfying. I would like to see a championship option and to equalise the collision response (i.e. I hit the AI and little happens, they hit me and little happens). Also, there is relatively little evidence of errors from the AI which is of course unrealistic.Pros+ Graphics are cute+ Handling style is different for each type of car+ Pit strategies can be fun with some cars+ Good variety of tracksCons- Collision system seems to favour the AI- No championship option- No replays- Few if any errors from the AIOverall, it is great that people still want to make and to play these casual racing games. Simple things can be fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a wicked mix of simple, easy to follow arcade style racing games and the depth and focus command by simulation physics. a system where you can just relax and race, but to be fast requires skill, speed and knowledge. this is one of the best racing games I've ever played  and it comes with a funny, committed community, a committed dev team of  6 (and just recently 7) people who share our passion for all things with four wheels meant for speed and some of the best racing ive seen for a while. despite the fact at this moment features are still being added, and that the online net code is still a work in progress, id still say this game is great valve for money at its current price. 10/10, would always race again
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Here's why me and this game can't be friends:You can turn in and swing your back around corners, together with applying throttle this looks like a drift, but you ONLY EVER turn the steering into the corner to keep it going. There is no real oversteer while on throttle, never any playing with the gas to have the drift like you want it, never any steering into the opposite direction while still drifting into the other. This is independent of what car you use.The throttle never even allows you enough oversteer to keep a small donut going.I also wish the weight of the different cars would make more of a difference, they all feel kinda heavy.Now, to be fair, except for the uneven ai (so far, I haven't played it a it a lot, but on some circuits I barely got second after two tries and in others I finished so far ahead that the game didn't wait long enough to time the other cars, giving them all a -1lap time - this is within the same difficulty setting, same car and same cup), I think this is a beautiful and cute game, with good production values. The handling makes sense and there is absolutely fun to be hand with it, it is just not for me.

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. I've spent hours playing games like Slicks 'n Slide and Race Mania (many years ago) and this game really brings back memories. Racing feels realistic, although there is just enough arcade-feel which makes it very accessable for everyone. If you want rockets and powerups, go play Mario Kart. This game is about mastering your car control and getting these lap times down by 0.1 second.The online community is not huge but very passionate and helpful. Single player mode is nice for practice but the fun comes absolutely in the online racing. Developers are bringing updates and patches on a regular basis. There are some bugs still, especially in the desynchronisation on servers, but I feel this is improving over time and I'm confident that these issues will be fixed eventually. A 100% recommend, especially for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is JOY. It plays super well, it requires precise controls but it isn't hard to get started, like Art of Rally. It also it's surprisingly deep with pit stops and strategy playing a role in races, but the awesomeness comes from achieving it without being a burden or complicated. I love this game, I only wish it had some variety on tracks (night, rain and maybe fog/overcast races). It runs super well on the Steam Deck, 90fps with 11W TDP.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and cosy arcade racer, especially if your aim is to relax for a short period of time. It get's repetitive fairly quickly, especially if playing solo, but if you consider jumping in once in a blue moon it should stay relevant for longer.Minus points for getting rid of the Top Gear DLCs (especially the free one) a mere half year after the game has left early access. Cutting content once added in the past is not cool - no matter if licenced or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Controls feel great, and as you get use to the cars and grip you really can make a difference in time. The tire wear makes the challenge dynamic and interesting, and think about the best pit stop strategy. The AI feels great to race against and the harder difficulties are fair. The game looks great, and is really well done. The best Top Down Racer by far.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Whats here is a very unique almost sim like take on top down racers. From its beautiful presentation to the surprisingly deep physics & handling behaviour it is a great foundation for the game to come in the future. There are balancing issues, UX flow design issues and some bare bones features but the potential is great! This game is going to polarise some people. The handling isn't like many top down racers where you point in the direction you want to go, instead you steer as if they are RC cars where a left turn is always a left turn relative to the current orientation of the car. The Fuel & Tyre use adds a wonderful level of depth where driving the car too hard will result in early pit stops as well as a loss in grip & acceleration.I have found the current Single Player Arcade mode has some balancing problems. It goes from very very easy to impossibly hard pretty quickly. I spent some time competing for Weekly Time Trials and managed a position of 20 on one of the tracks but even after feeling like I was nailing these hot laps I just couldn't keep up with the AI in the later stages. This aspect of the game is where it needs to be scaled back a bit so as not to alienate a larger potential audience for the game or at least offer a difficulty setting in Arcade mode.This level of depth in the skill required at the top is an aspect I personally love. You can race the next person on the Leaderboards ghost lap and it makes for a really addictive challenge whilst also revealing just how good some people are.Overall I love the game and I'm excited to seeing it grow throughout Early Access!Came back and have played through Amateur in Career mode and I still love it, major improvements over the original release version. Its a great game and I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who played GeneRally back in the '00s is in for a very welcome nostalgia rush, and even if you haven't, it's still a fantastic little racing game in its own right. It's a very simple game that anyone can pick up and quickly get into, but has enough going on that even hardcore simracers will enjoy it. This game is an excellent example of "less is more"; it doesn't bury you in a plethora of features & game mechanics that all need to be sorted out & understood. But the few things it does have are very well designed and offer more depth than what you'd expect at first glance from a silly little car game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun, but honestly, I can't see playing it until they add some additional car models (it's not terribly interesting racing a field of even just the same models), but that's a FAR distant second to the need to add a save feature to the championships. People that want to play a quasi-casual racing game don't want to be tied to it in order to progress through a championship.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: AI difficulty spread is trash. Game goes from easy too impossible just by bumping it up once. This makes the game incredibly frustrating and not fun to learn or play. Cannot recommend the game until this is fixed.Also, all of the AI are on the same pit strategy so they all just pit at the same time. This makes the tire deg feature bland and adds nothing but a scripted pointless pitstop to the race. If you try to pit early to undercut you'll lose out. _childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. I normally play out and out sim racing games where my viewpoint would be from the cockpit. So, why would I like this? Well, it's a beautiful looking game for a start and I love the choice of vehicles available - especially the 1960 GP cars. It also has a great racing feel - it matters how you take the corners, sticking close to the apexes to get the best times. It actually feels like a proper racer believe or not, even though I'm using a controller rather than the wheel I would normally use. NOTE TO DEVELOPERS - I only have two criticisms which actually could probably easily be solved. Firstly, the AI cars all seem to go round like a caterpillar (or a train) - all too close to each making it really hard to pass. There is no space to ease past one car and then concentrate on passing the next. Getting more differentiation between the AI cars would make it much more playable. This could be scaled depending on the distances possibly - in other words, in a short 5 lap race, they space out quicker than a 13 lap race. The second thing is linked to the first. In collisions, you as the player will more often than not, will come off worse - or at least they are able to recover much more quickly. Because of the  issue I mentioned above with the cars always being very close together, collisions happen far too regularly. Often, once you crash, you're out of contention too. SO - all in all a brilliant game and I have no regrets purchasing it - in fact, I can't wait to see it develop in the months to come. I would ask the developers though to please look at those two issues. Thanks Original Fire Games.

_childDocuments_.review: Hate leaving reviews, let alone Negative ones. This game, sadly deserves it.If you are expecting any kind of 'legit' racing you will be let down. Game is literally bumper cars. That's it. nothing more, nothing less. You get corner checked or bombed, forced into barriers, rammed so you lose your line, side swiped and forced into pit lane,  and then someone comes along and hits you again while you are already down.  I was expecting SO much more. My fault i guess.If they added power ups or a catch up mechanic like Mario Kart the game would be fine and fun. I'd expect to be wrecked and hit constantly and corner bombed.. That's not what this game is though. It tries to be a 'real' racer and its not. not when all the mayhem and poor sportsmanship is allowed. Once you've been hit and knocked into the grass backwards, you are done. It's over. There is no 'catching up' and the perpetrator goes free with ZERO penalties. Game is just literally aggravating bumper cars. period.Another issue is the blinding white transition screens. You see them constantly before and after the race. I've been in two or so topics in the forums about this for almost a year now. Nothing. no response, no answers, zip. Even after many updates and the EA process... If you value your retinas I would pass on this title as well. Its so bright and jarring and continually is an issue, not just one loading screen and done, there are constant 'loading' screens all blinding white.If you are looking for a legit fun race game look elsewhere, don't let the 'shiny' colors fool you. If you are looking for a Mario kart type game also look elsewhere. If you like to play annoying and aggravating bumper cars with the 'look' of a real racer or you enjoy ruining other people's races by corner bombing and causing mayhem then have a go at this. You'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Circuit Superstars! I'm always a fan of top down racers which isn't a popular genre at all. Everything about this game feels great. The driving mechanics can surprise you as they feel fairly realistic in the sense that you'll actually have to brake going into turns. You can still drift around corners and stuff, but I don't remember many top down racers that actually require braking at all. In fact, they even have pit stops that you'll have to do on any race that has at least 10 laps! It's a nice little change that racers typically don't include.Everything just feels so crisp. The driving mechanics are top notch and I love the aesthetic. My only complaints would be that there's no music, but on the other hand, you can throw on your favorite podcast or just play your own soundtrack in the background. The only change I'd really like to see made is that in qualifying laps and racing against lapped cars, other cars become transparent near you and you just drive right through them. There is collision during races when you're battling for position, it's just qualifying laps and against lapped racers. I do like that design, but there's no indicator for which car is yours. This partircularly can become a challenge in qualifying laps when cars start stacking on top of each other and you lose sight of your car.That being said, this is definitely one of the best top down racers ever made in my opinion. If you like top down racers, you would be doing yourself a disservice by not playing this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The honest truth is that you won't get a lot of mileage out of Circuit Superstars, outside of a few evening play sessions with friends. The content roster is not conducive to extended play, and it's possible to exhaust the selection of cars and tracks within your first hour inside the app.This is because Circuit Superstars is a throwback to games like the PC freeware title "GeneRally", or RC Pro-Am on the SNES, with an isometric camera view and simplistic physics. It is the race car equivalent to Mario Party; a title you dust off in a group for lighthearted fun, without needing to worry about calibrating your steering wheel, memorizing a track, or dialing in your car setup. Basically, if you're part of a sim racing discord group, you'll end up buying this for game night with the boys.What exists, is absolutely fantastic, and you'll have a ton of fun during the first hour. Cars are nimble yet convey a solid sense of weight to them, online racing is practically flawless regarding netcode, and the overall format of races results in a game that takes just seconds to learn. No fancy brake bias, pit speed limit to adhere to, or pit strategy menus to fiddle with - just monitor the HUD to see your fuel/tire level, drive in the pits and stop in the box to service your car when it's obvious you need to. The mechanics are brilliant. It's the ultimate party racing game.The problem is, Original Fire Games unfortunately never provided the other half of the mix that made GeneRally so addictive. GeneRally became an internet phenomenon among sim racers, because of the incredible modding community that spawned from GR releasing first party toolkits - a scene which exists to this day. After a user grew tired of the initial batch of content, there was an entire world to explore of additional cars and tracks; from the hyper-realistic, to the absurd. Circuit Superstars features no such modding scene; and is like asking someone to pay $20 for a vanilla GeneRally that you can't mod.Circuit Superstars is brilliant for those first few hours, but a giant missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit Superstars is a fun, gamified take on F1-styled circuit racing that somehow takes the strategy and sportsmanship of circuit racing and brings it down to a level where it is present and enjoyable on a much smaller, much more casual scale. Circuit Superstars is a racing game where choosing when to pit, when to refuel, and when and how hard to brake is just as important if not more important than slamming on the gas and praying for the W. At its core, the racing in Circuit Superstars is top-notch, comparable most likely to art of rally and BAFL. For a top-down racer, the controls are tight and put great emphasis on racing lines and braking, which is to be expected of a circuit-racing inspired title. The game looks good, run well, and has a pretty solid OST. The racing is easy to learn and difficult to master, perfect for a casual game with friends or a more try-hard game for those who care about beating ghosts and hitting the leaderboards. There is a good variety of tracks and vehicles to race on. The game takes a fairly serious, professional sport and makes it accessible and fun for an audience that might not be very knowledgeable on the source material. The game is outright fun and doesn't ask you to take it too seriously - an easy recommendation for anyone with a passing interest in racing.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely in love with this game!It's the top-down racer I didn't know I needed, and if you loved Art of Rally, you'll love this.On the surface, it looks like an Arcade racer, but it has a lot of sim elements to it. Each car has its own unique handling characteristics, and fuel, tire wear, and pit strategy (for longer races) all play a factor. This isn't an arcade racer where you mash the gas and go. You need to learn the handling of the cars and nail your apexes and braking zones. The AI doesn't give you any breaks either, on the higher difficulties the AI will fight you tooth and nail for any position (there's currently 6 difficulties to choose from). It really makes for some great racing. The attention to detail is great too, from the map artwork to the pit crews. The racing line even collects rubber as the laps add up. You can really tell the developers are passionate motorsport fans.Overall, this is an addicting casual racer that's easy to pick up but a challenge to master! (best played with a gamepad or controller)  Highly recommended to any motorsport fan. For a game in early access, it's incredibly well polished and could pass for a full release. However, it sounds like the devs have alot planned for the future of this game and I can't wait to see the new content that comes.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I thought long and hard before writing this early access review.  I want the game to be a success, and I still think it will be, but I also truly believe that if they aspire to meet their initial vision, then this game will stand out above all the other top-down arcade racers that came before and will stand the test of time.I've been interested in the game from when I first heard about it a couple of years ago.  Since it released on early access, I've enjoyed it, but with specific reservations as I don't feel that they are yet achieving what they set out to do.  My impression from the developers before early access was that they are aiming for an accessible top-down racer with the heart of a racing simulation - tactile steering and realistic driving physics - and not just another arcade racer.  I based it on the gameplay clips they released, what they talked about in interviews and the wording they used in describing what they are going for.  The footage always highlighted cars swinging around a corner, riding on the edge of grip on the curb and shifting weight as the car changed direction and/or steadied heading down the straight. The wording they used included... ”Circuit Superstars offers a unique mix of top-down arcade accessibility with the authenticity of motorsport sims” and "FEEL the rubber bite into the road as you pass the start/finish line and dive, brakes squealing, into the first corner!”I'm not concerned that the game won't have enough content and replayability at release, so my focus is not on that.  I think the game has the potential to be exactly what they set out to do with just a few tweaks and a slight shifts in focus.  That is what I always keep in mind as I play the game and as I write this early access review. I feel it is a wasted opportunity to not e.g. make use of the games excellent physics model that allow cars to tightly ride the curbs and adjusts its suspension, if cutting the curbs ends up being the fastest because the track limits are too lenient.  For me, the developers need to focus on certain aspects for the game to reach its potential and to meet the vision they set out in the beginning.  At the moment for you to drive fast you must abuse the track limits, cut corners, you rarely need to brake (just let go of the throttle) or control your throttle, and you often need to slide through the corner to take it best. Here are some suggestions for what I think they need to focus on...- The game should discourage players from going off track with the car being unsettled, slowed down, and having a lot less traction if you do.- The inside of a corner should be the extent of the curb.  The game should tightly penalise anything over the curb on the inside.- Braking distances should be increased significantly (depending on the type of car).  Just coasting into a corner should not be enough to make it.- Similarly, acceleration must have more of an effect on the car (depending on the type of car).  With a powerful car, if you don’t feather the input and just plant your foot before the car is settled and straightened, the car must spin out/veer of course.- Traction should be increased so that there is less sliding around the corner.  If you slide, it should be less under your control and you shouldn’t be able to make the turn without slowing/bleeding a lot of the excess speed.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally gravitate towards full sim racing games and wasn't sure how I would like a racing title with what appears like a more "arcade" approach. I have to say I am really loving this game. While its graphics are not meant to look photo-realistic, the tracks and cars are very nice to look at and the texture and lighting effects are very well done and add life to the appearance. The tire wear, fuel consumption and damage features add complexity and an extra challenge and pit strategy certainly is a factor in longer races yet it is still simple enough that it shouldn't scare off more casual racers. In terms of the actual vehicle control, the game rewards taking proper racing lines and has a wide variety of race vehicles that handle in a believable and predictable way.  A lot of the tracks based on real-world tracks are done as well as the line up of vehicles. The only drawbacks I see at this point are some connectivity issues in multiplayer that I hope may improve as more people pick this game up and the player base grows and allows for better matchmaking. I am excited to see the upcoming oval cars, track and slip-streaming physics in action. I might be dreaming but I think it would be pretty cool to see in the future a full on moto X style track for the trucks with multiple combinations of jumps that reward proper rhythm and consistency. Keep up the great work Original Fire, loving it so far.

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit superstars is a great game that perfectly marries simracing with a laid back not too serious racing game. The physics is done very well and the game is backed up by a kind, welcoming community! The cars each have their own unique feel, and racing changes depending on what you drive. The fuel/tyre management adds an additional layer of strategy without being needlessly complicated or overwhelming and the fact that this game doesn't let you tweak car setup means that everyone is on the same level! The skill ceiling is also much more manageable than other simracing games, without giving the game too much of an "arcade-y" feel.That isn't to say I have no criticisms though. (As of April 8, 2022) I find oval tracks in this game need some work, defending the inside is way too good and there isn't a viable way to go side by side on the outside because its just objectively slower. Cleanly overtaking on straights can also be challenging because of the way drafting works; not carrying your speed once you're out of the tow of the car in front. But these are two very tiny nitpicks overall, and I definitely think its some of the best money a racing fan can spend atm.

It still suffers from a number of pretty bad bugs.Bugs discovered so far:- The huge gap between AI skills in 'Amateur' and the next 'Pro-Am'. There really could be something in between. - Also, my laptop keeps locking the display update for a second 1-3 times a race. No other games show this behavior so it's definitely a bug in this game.- The career mode called Grand Prix or something is pretty hard right from the start, which makes it unusable.- And last but not least, if you have something less than highest bandwidth network, multiplayer is completely messed up. But with high bandwidth it might work ok.

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult to play when you first try but after a little bit of practice its very fun and great to play. the art style of the game is amazing and when you race around tyre marks appear which is the best small feature I have ever seen in a game. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is great. Awesome car handling, nice graphics and some great racing. New cars and tracks are being added at a good pace right now but even if all that stopped tomorrow, the game would still be excellent. You can have some really good races in this. You can have short sprint races or go long with more laps and bring in pit stops. The game features tire degradation, car damage and fuel usage if you wish to keep them enabled and that adds to the race greatly with the option to save fuel through careful driving absolutely an option, same with the tire saving too, and car damage incurred from scenery collisions and colliding with other cars will slow your car down so this also adds to pit stop considerations. I've mainly played in single player with the Arcade mode which has 5 formulas to race in of ascending difficulty and Free Play in which you can set up any race or championship you like with options of qualifying, amount of cars to race against and of course track selection. The game also features 4 player split screen and online racing too.I'd like to mention the graphics, which aren't very demanding on your pc and really do look excellent and quite charming. Kind of cartoon-ish but not too much, the cars are very clearly recognisable from the cars which they imitate and the tracks look really nice with bright colours and nicely intricate scenery with spectators to cheer you on.    This is just a really great top down racing game and, I feel, somewhat unique because of the focus on more realistic car handling. If you like racing and have any liking whatsoever for top down racing games, you should absolutely pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: My eyes lit up when I saw this on my New Releases queue. It looks absolutely GORGEOUS and plays beautifully.Online is a bit ropey at the moment, lag-wise, but I'm sure that will get addressed.Overall, if you have any interest at all in TDRs, then you NEED to buy this game.  It blows every other top-down racer out of the water!

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the game itself is actually very good. and i will be coming back to this revieuw if and when needed.It's polished, it looks good and the physics are great for a top down view racer (except for the automatic countersteer or "bounceback" when you come out of a turn)What let me to leave a negative revieuw is the absolutely horrific online experience, and by that i don't mean people using the back of your car as their e-brake... thats not the devs fault (altho you could argue a more fleshed out penalty system could help).It takes ages to find match making, chances are you end up in a lobby with one or two other players.When by some miracle you get to start racing online with more then three players on the grid, you have about a 50/50 chance you'll get kicked out of the race with a "server closed" message.It's also not a cheap game, me as a car enthousiast and sim racer find it expensive, so i can imagine average joe simply not buying the game at this price point, and we definitely need average joe, otherwise we're going to keep seeing empty lobbies and the game is going to die before it gets the chance to become great.TLDR;If you're a solo VS AI racer, by al means buy the game, it's great.But if you think about playing it online, i'd suggest to wait and see if the game's popularity rises enough to get full lobbies.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of top down racers since arcade supersprint, I'm really enjoying this one.  It's not what you think it is though, it has nintendo graphics and music, but yet has the heart of a serious racer.  Once they decide which way to go with this it's going to be an amazing game. bit more detail:Races have low numbers of laps (4, up to 10 ive seen) which smells of an arcade racer... the kind where you could come from the back and still win.  Also, the track is quite narrow, and impact between the cars is overly  devastating.  So we have the setup of an arcade racer, but with the conditions of a sim.  On the races without qualifying, it's going to be seriously difficult to fight through the pack in a few laps if not impossible. Tracks are solid, although they all have the same feel, and lack any height changes.  The rally tracks show that the game is capable of exciting crazy tracks, but this is lacking right now. I like to see some arcade style ones just for fun. Car physics are a bit strange, but you do get used to it. certainly room for improvement here. AI is the weakest thing here for me.  cars seem to blindly follow the racing line, never crash and will happily plant you in the wall if you challenge their line. Looks like some improvements are coming though. As it's early access, there's plenty of room for improvement and I look forward to where it goes. Already a solid racer though, I'd recommend playing even at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: And that's why I personally refunded it. Trying to play this with an Xbox controller is an exercise in frustration, because the AI opponents are  consistent in taking perfect lines even on the second-to-easiest difficulty, and after half an hour of retrying the medium difficulty I gave up. On second-to-easiest, their lines were still basically perfect, but their top speed is heavily sandbagged compared to yours which just feels patronizing.I'm no stranger to top-down racers; I've 100%'d quite a few. This game is  unforgiving. Your tires wear down, so they won't corner as well on the fifth lap as they did on the first. The degree to which you turn your wheels needs to be , more precise than you can be with a joystick, and you need to very carefully watch your speed which makes the lack of an obvious visual indicator questionable.Is it a good game? Yes! If you have the right setup for it. I don't.Provided you do - Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun but lacking content. Yes, there are different cars but they handle very same-y. I think it would have been a lot smarter to just focus on GT and Formula 1 and put things like rain, safety car, flags, AI crashes, tire compounds etc. in the game.As it stands it's fun to drive but it's always sunny, you barely need more than 1 pitstop and you can't really select your strategy. This is a fantastic foundation for a much bigger and better game but right now it's only okay.Regarding the save system: Races barely last longer than 10-15 minutes. A championship lasts 4 races, so roughly 45 minutes. The fact that you can't save between races (you also can't restart them or rewind like in Codemasters games) makes these championships great. Every decision, every mistake counts. With a save system between races you'd be able to save scum your way out of every costly mistake which is no fun.

The Good- It looks Nice.- Has some minor cosmetic customization options.The Bad- Car Physics all feel like driving clouds on top of more clouds.- Want to do donuts? _childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game through a Humble Bundle and was a bit more interested in the other titles in that bundle than this game at first.  With its cutesy art style, I went into it thinking it was a simple top-down arcade style racing game. I was pleasantly surprised to find out how much more depth this game has. Each vehicle handles differently with speed and weight distribution. Your vehicle has health, fuel consumption, and tire wear meaning that for longer duration races, you need to take a pit stop to get repairs and refueled. This mechanic brings some interesting depth to it. When do you pit? Can you control your speed so your tires don't wear out as fast? Can you conserve fuel on these curves for one more lap?It turns this cute little arcade racing game into something closer to a racing sim. It's awesome! I think the only downside I can think of for it is there aren't very many tracks, but the tracks they do have are really well designed.8/10 would recommend for anyone looking for a casual racing sim experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Developer, Original Fire Games has created something very simple, straightforward, unique, challenging, and completely addicting with their new racing game, Circuit Superstars.  It’s one of those games that is easy to ignore when browsing the Steam store with screenshots and a trailer that don’t do the game justice.  I was blown away within moments of my first race with all the graphical flourishes, the great car designs, multiple game modes, and a unique arcade physics system that worked seamlessly with responsive gamepad controls.Of course any racing game comes down to physics and handling and Circuit Superstars does take a bit of getting used to with its ice-like tracks that require deft use of the throttle, brake, and analog steering to maintain that perfect drift line while maintaining optimum speeds.  A good example is the 60’s GP Revival where you are driving authentic cars from that era that will spin out if you mash the gas, especially in tight turns.  And the way the disciplines are presented, if you play them in their listed order you then move on to Muscle Cars and then Super Trucks.  By the time you get behind the wheel of a big rig you have likely already driven five other car varieties that in no way prepare you for the shift in momentum or the increase weight of your truck that reduces is stopping distance.  All of these subtle variations across the disciplines do a surprising job of keeping the game fresh and challenging.The one thing I did notice was an overall lack of rumble support outside of driving on the actual rumble strips in the game or actually hitting another car or trackside object.  There was nothing to directly tie the car to the track or hint at tire grip or loss of traction, and 95% of the time I felt I was driving on ice, which made it take twice as long to master the drifting mechanic.  You will figure it out and it feels great when you finally do, but better rumble would have helped.he single-player portion alone is worth the cost of admission and the online modes have a lot to offer if you are good enough to compete with some of the insanely good players already setting impossible laps times.  I really enjoyed my time spent with Circuit Superstars and I plan to spend a lot more earning those final few gold cups.Read full review at: More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little game, sort of like a modern version of GeneRally, but... it's very hard to enjoy it because of the behaviour of the "AI". There's nothing inteligent about it, and that ruins the fun. The AI cars always drive as if you are not there, and they don't do anything differently whether they are alone on track or if you are there. When they are right behind you, you know you are going to get wrecked, and the starts of races are just a nightmare where you just need to restart over and over until you manage not to get hit.Also the physics are different for the AI cars when there's contact, so you always end up losing out. The only real way to have a good race is to be perfect or to race against very slow AI. If it's a close race, you are going to have a bad time. Another great thing the AI does is cut corners, become a ghost and then overtake you as a ghost so you can't do anything. If they add actual AI one day, this game could be great, but in its current state, you need to stick to driving alone or online.It's lacking quite a few things like saving the progress mid-championship, and the cars need to handle way differently than they currently are. They all sort of feel the same, and they all slide too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh.  I thought this could be fun and relaxing little arcade racing game, but the lack of difference in feel on all the vehicles just doesn't give you the incentive to want to try the other cars/trucks.  There's a slight difference in weight and how slippery they are, but realistically, I don't see the point.  Furthermore, the cars you would expect to have traction and responsiveness such as the open wheelers just slip around the track like the rest. For a game with variety in vehicles, I would have liked/expected different handling models. Just for that reason alone, I didn't feel compelled to play more than 20 minutes. After I tried all the vehicles, I figured I would stop wasting my time and move on.  It's not a bad game, but it's not for me. A definite refund.

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, sit down, shut up, and listen to me explain why this game is your gateway drug into racing games:- this game has simple yet rewarding mechanics. You need to learn a total of four things, got it? Move forward, turn left, turn right, and stop/reverse the car. "But that's five!" I hear you cry "Shut the hell up, I'm not here to count." Is my response- You don't need to worry too much about racing sim in this. The controls are simple, and the vehicle management is easy as it gets. If anything gets too low then you can just swing into the pits. Sometimes you go into the pits on accident- There isn't a meta. The meta is don't be a f*cking loser. Think you can do that? Shut up, no you can't. Or can you? Shut up. Everyone has the same cars to pick from, so everyone is getting the same stopping power and acceleration- Square Enix made it- The races are fast. Last night after I mastered the controls in an amazing 10 minutes, I decided to do my own "Mini-GP" where I did five 10 lap races in one sitting. It took like maybe 30 minutes for me to do all these races. I won the GP. You don't care but I do. - You actually have to get kinda good. I play a fair bit of MotoGP and the rewind system is a bit of a crutch imo. You can mess up and just back up like "hahaha, that legendary high-side is a myth." Crashing in this game means you have to face the consequences, and just learn to keep racing. - you serve time penalties by being slowed down. Nothing is deducted from your time and no points are taken away. You serve them instantly as well- The art style is fun and arcade like without being too much. It's a nice balance. - I hate the GT classThis game is simple to play, but it has enough depth that people who enjoy racing games (or who want to get better at this one in particular) have the ability to get better. Each racing class has its own style. Piccino and Superlight are the better classes to start in if you need to get a feel for the controls, and the first two GP maps that come up are super simple. Actually all the tracks are super simple, but some aren't as simple. There's everything for everyone. This game makes you feel like a hobby racer and not someone who has to do it for a living. It's a nice feel knowing that your character isn't one bad performance away from having to eat ramen and can instead show up to their job in something like accounting and be fine the next day. It's an incredibly fun and simple game, with the ability to have races that are shorter than 5 minutes a piece. You can play as long or as not long as you want and it feels very good. I would like them to add a few things though: An endurance style of racing where you race for a set amount of time, not a set amount of laps. Topping it out at a couple hours for the real masochists should be enough, and it could introduce endurance type cars. I'd also like to see some tracks that are replicas of real tracks. Just the more famous ones, like Le Mans or something like that. Overall, I give the game a solid 9/10 - losing points because I can't face the consequences of my actions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a better review but I just can't bring myself to do it. The difficulty is arbitrarily hard at the hardest setting. The AI is in faster cars than you and can push you out of the way while remaining unaffected by your vehicle. To win, you need to set 10-15 back to back world record level lap times and drive almost pixel perfect in a game with all the precision of a drunken elephant. Take it back a level and you'll win by 5-6 seconds, it is highly frustrating to deal with and when you pair that with what amounts to no progression system, it gets old fast. I love the art style and the way the game plays outside of the above though. It is truly unique and has some interesting features. Some of the series have arbitrary pit stops as the AI always does the same thing every race. For all these reasons, I just can't recommend this game until some changes are made. I got it on sale in a bundle or something so I will continue to play it as it is a good time-passer on the steam deck, but that is about it.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play the more I like, this is top down GRID physics racing.  You have to drive the cars like you would in real life to get the fastest times.  Careful braking, throttle control everything, with correct entry into and out of corners mandatory.  Or you can not give a hoot about fastest lap times and drive each car the way you like, either way, this game is fun.  Each genre of car has it's own physics engine, muscle cars feel distinctly different to F1, as they should.  Give this game time, it's a creeper...but know for sure this is more of a serious racing game than it looks.  For wheel users, check out xbox 360 controller emulator and map it to your wheel.  With FF on in emulation and the right sensitivity tweaking, you are hooning on your wheel and feeling the track.  It's super cool.  Hope devs add proper wheel support soon, but until then the emulator works well.
