_childDocuments_.review: Huge improvements since early access, but still some inexplicable omissions.1) No way to save and resume a Grand Prix.  Having to complete all 4 races in one session is unreasonable.  We should be able to save progress between events.2) Auto-start - you complete a race and if you forget to hit pause (there are times between races when you can't pause the game) then it just starts the next event automatically.  Is "Press A to start" too much to ask?3) Predictable AI - the same cars always end up at the front.  At "Master" and above when you try to pass them, they spin you out but rarely lose control themselves4) Qualifying bugs - sometimes you don't get to the finish line and it just ends quali and you end up wherever you were in the queue.  Pretty much every quali one AI car doesn't complete the lap but still gets a time5) Leaderboards - like most racing games it's almost impossible to compare yourself to other drivers.  Can't scroll through the leaderboards for a track.  World, Global Near, Friends.  Needs more visibility of rivals6) Reposition - if you get in a bad crash then just recovering to the track and continuing can result in a "Reposition" prompt.  Problem is the prompt comes so late that you lose any chance of catching the pack back up.7) Multiplayer - no matchmaking.  Why not give us 2-4 player split screen, given that the online multiplayer is so weak?All that said, it's a fun game with good graphics, quite a few different car classes, and performs well at max settings.  But it needs a lot more work.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually i just bought it for my Daughter, so she can learn topdown steering, for later piloting mymini-z racer without destroying it instantly. lolSurprisingly, it hooked me as well - kind of.i like the drive physics for different cars, though i also think there is great room for improvement.The collision physics are not great for example, to not say inexistent.The Cars cant roll over, or just in very few but unrealistic occasions.The damage model of the cars is nothing more than a health bar.The environment is a rock solid world, bumping in a wooden fens-bar is the same as bumping in a concrete wall…Take a look at rat racer on steam which has all of that, but is made by one person and has very slow EA progress.So i strongly missing the funny moments in a racing game, the crashes!This would definitely be a thumbs right, unfortunately steam does not provide such ratings so i have to gofor a thumb down, for missed opportunity's at this price range.Im not regretting the purchase, as my daughter learned fast to steer top down and she had a lot of giggles, so am i.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive, with one major caveat.The good:  Virtually everything.  The best top-down racer I've ever played(*).  The graphics and sounds are all satisfying, the physics feel right, the races are fast, fun, and a joy from start to finish.  If you like top-down racers, this is a no-brainer, buy it immediately(*).(*) Now, the caveat is that multiplayer is currently tagged as "beta", and it feels more like alpha.  For players, generally in the US region in my experience, it is a toss-up whether your race will work.  More times than not, the game does not even recognize you're playing, so you can drive around all you want, but the lap counter will never increase, you'll never use gas, and you'll never finish the race.  When it DOES know you're playing, it has a habit of randomly throwing you across the map, or moving your car back a half a mile, or otherwise make the car uncontrollable.  When it works, it's faaaantastic.  But it usually doesn't at this point.  I think EU region players probably don't run into these problems as often, but I don't have a lot of data.If that's eventually fixed, I will sink infinite hours into it.  If it isn't, then I'm pretty much done.  The single-player modes are fun, but limited, and after a while you've done everything a hundred times.

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit Superstars offers a lot of gaming modes, vehicles and tracks and has visual appeal. In case the perspective is fine for you and you are not averse to speed, then feel free to try this racing game.Circuit Superstars is a quick paced Arcade racing game with simulation elements. Though the perspective makes it hard to drive tracks you barely know, the game offers what many other racing games can not do. Circuit Superstars gives you the ability to fight for track positions the hard way and defend positions successfully, even if you are (little) slower then your opponents, There are many different racing vehicles with their specific feel and different tracks. Fast racing cars with lots of downforce, Fast cars withouth lots of downforce that require a good feel or Trucks and more.In the Grand-Prix-Mode you will find 5-Round Races that are a sprint or 15-Round Endurance Races with Pit-Stops. You can choose multiple levels of Ai-opponents. While the first level is pretty hard when you begin, you get better fast and can choose higher difficulties.Even though my first impression has been good, my second one bad, as i failed to get the right feeling easily, i definetly came to like the game. Even with the keyboard you can have fun driving. Though you may not beat the best computers. Just be satisfied choosing a level you can have good races with. Or try the multiplayer aspects with your friends or drive against the clock and other players ghosts.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Overall fun game-- MORE DETAILED EXPLANATION ---- ART --The artstyle looks stunning and kinda cute. It's a unique stylized art compared to all the modern racing games I've seen so far. It's definitely the trademark of Original Fire Games. You can unlock more different animations for your character when being on the podium and designs for your cars, helmet and race suits as you level up in the gameThe attention to detail of the "track evolution" is insanely good imo. Like I'm blown away and still had to wrap around on how they did it. Basically the tire marks you, and many other racers drive on & off the track are left there for the ENTIRE DURATION of the race. You could see the parts of the track getting darker every lap & you can see parts of the track where racers ran off or where they usually start to turn. But if you find it a bit distracting, you can just turn it off in the settings -- MY THOUGHTS & EXPERIENCE ON THE GAMEPLAY --Disclaimer: I will be talking about the AI on highest difficulty a lot more as this is where I usually play atm & I feel like I also need to talk about this since a lot of people are talking about AI difficulty. I am also using keyboard (even though I know that controller is just the GOAT on racing arcade games especially when being compared to keyboard) XDI had to adapt my style of racing to be able and stay competitive against the AI. I lose lots of times on some corners but the devs are kind enough to give AI a racing line where it's not completely optimal especially on chicanes. That's where I can catch up to them, that's if I don't commit any mistakes. Other places, I had to be cheeky and dive bomb a lot on hairpins & on the entries of the chicanes. Basically, I had to be more "elbows out" when fighting against AI. Hardest difficulty is no joke especially during the recent update regarding the rubber band thing. When they say it's hardest difficulty, it is indeed the hardest difficulty. Same feeling I had when I was playing against bots in Forza Horizon 4 and 5's hardest difficulty.The racing experience is great so far. Its not a totally brain dead type of arcade racing game as I can feel the tire degradation over time resulting me into having to adjust as laps go by. The difference of a fresh set of tires vs like 20% tire lifetime is night and day. Oh and I also have to learn fuel and tire management a bit. Initially I had to release more often if I want my fuel to last longer but then I found out that it wouldn't matter against AIs as long as I pit during their usual pit window. I had a phase where I constantly go for the time trials. I had fun trying to beat other players' times. It's a weekly reset making the hunt to be on top of the leader board refreshing. 1 week to understand the car for the week, how it drives around the track and find the most optimised racing line for that vehicle. They made it 3 cars in 3 different tracks so it didn't burn me out.  I gotta say that AI do have strong tracks. Like this one instance on Nascar Grand Prix series where I had to race on an Outlaw Race track (dirt oval). I could feel my car struggling while the AIs were like "Noice an oval track. ez racing lines". Literally no signs of AIs struggling. So I had to be in full damage control for the points. Aim for P10 was my goal. Glad I wont have to ever do that again.-- PHYSICS  --At first, when I saw the trailer, I thought that the cars might be snappy and would tend to oversteer a lot due to it looking like they all have short wheel bases. That wasn't the case it turns out. It doesn't over steer/lose control except whenever I accidentally touch at least 1 of the wheel off track when driving a road car when turning. Despite me using a keyboard, I could still feel how responsive the car is. Depending on the vehicle, for instance, the trophy truck, I must turn earlier compared to the GT cars on the asphalt for me to be able to successfully enter the corner. Then there are cars like the open wheel ones, its so responsive and I can turn quickly just like irl.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Played on Deck, runs at highest settings beautifully (90fps) with only brief FPS drops before races when panning around the track.Absolutely adore this game. Takes a little time to get a feel for each type of car and how to be fast, but when it clicks you'll be in heaven. It's actually somewhere between sim and arcade, the cars have weight and traction and you can't just drift or throw your car into every corner and still be fast.Great variety of cars, wish there were a few more tracks though. Single player is great fun, love the addition of tyre and fuel wear for certain races, adds a fun tactical layer! Won a few races by being clever with fuel management and when to pit.The AI is surprisingly good, really feels like they are aware of you and not just driving their own line. You'll see them block you off if you go for an inside line early and go for some crazy divebombs themselves, often getting it wrong and going off track. The pack behind you will also get into some really entertaining tussles, sometimes groups of 6 of cars ferociously battling, usually with some funny casualties. My only complaint is that it feels like the AI cars have more weight/impact on you than you do on them, shoving you off track but when you try and do the same, they barely budge.Online is also really fun, just wish the community was bigger! Only had a max of 5 people in a race so far :( Weekly time trials with ranking ladders also adds some longevity.Would definitely recommend if you're into racing games but want something a little quicker, more fun and laid back!

_childDocuments_.review: Circuit Superstars roars onto the scene as a love letter to motorsport, expertly blending arcade thrills with a surprisingly deep well of simulation. Developed by the passionate folks at Original Fire Games, this top-down racer caters to both casual drivers and hardcore gearheads alike.One of Circuit Superstars' biggest strengths is its handling model. The cars feel weighty and responsive, with tire wear, fuel consumption, and damage all playing a role.  Taking that perfect racing line and feathering the throttle around a corner is immensely satisfying, and the high skill ceiling ensures there's always room for improvement.But Circuit Superstars isn't all about hardcore simulation. The top-down perspective and arcade-inspired races make it easy to pick up and play, even for newcomers to the genre. The vibrant visuals and distinct car classes, encompassing everything from 60s-era formula racers to modern GT machines, keep things visually interesting.Beyond the core racing, Circuit Superstars offers a wealth of content.  Compete against challenging AI, vie for glory on global leaderboards, or throw down with friends in local and online multiplayer for up to 12 players. You can even craft your own custom race events and tournaments, adding a layer of replayability that will keep you coming back for more.Circuit Superstars is a delightful surprise, a game brimming with heart and soul. Whether you're a seasoned racing veteran or a casual driver looking for a quick adrenaline rush, Circuit Superstars is a must-play. Don't be fooled by the cartoony visuals – this is a deep and rewarding racing experience that will keep you glued to the screen.

_childDocuments_.review: Was interested in this since launch because of its unique style and arcadey top-down perspective, and thoroughly surprised that it controls exactly unlike how I intended. The "Automobile Sim" tag on here threw me for a loop and I understand it now. Very, very far from the Super Off Road successor I mistakenly assumed it to be, Circuit Superstars took me by surprise by how it incorporates actual GT/Rally techniques and mechanics into a top-down arcade experience; oversteer, understeer, weight transfer, tire snapping and so many additional elements that contribute to its unique handling system. There's a real learning curve, one that I haven't mastered yet as I'm still fumbling on the Pro-AM difficulty, but one that I've been coming back to for how rewarding and satisfying it is to use your car's weight to catapult it around corners. Other than its deep, robust method of car control, Circuit Superstars is simple. There's not much in the way of additional content aside from its cups and time trial methods, and I haven't dared jump into online play just yet. Game modes are customizable enough to experiment and practice with, so as long as you're aware of what's inside the game beforehand, decide for yourself if you're up for it. It's not for everyone, and I see a lot of comments that it's repetitive or controls poorly, and I feel as though those are similar cases of people's expectations not being met. For me, even though Circuit Superstars isn't the return-to-classic isometric rally racer it can look like at first glance, I find it fun to play once you accept what it truly is.Bonus mention to the UI and sound design. Not just counting the dynamic engine sounds, but for the aesthetic design of its menus; it strikes a fine line between minimal and sleek, and the selection blips and starting jingles remind me of Wii Sports. Very uniformed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits a sweet spot in much the same way Super Mega Baseball does - it's fun, but there are enough difficulty levels and strategic elements (tire wear, fuel consumption, learning the cars and tracks) to find an appropriate level of challenge and make racing good, competitive fun. _childDocuments_.review: Brilliant piece of software.... I have played racing games for 35+ years and I can tell you that this is one of the best pure racing games ever. It takes it's origins from the original Super Sprint and Ivan Stewart Off-Road arcade games, but also 2D PC classic's like Slicks'N'Slide and Generally. These all combine to form a fantastic looking, fast-paced, high-intensity racing game which despite it's cutesy looks, has substantial depth. The physics are a bit arcadey, but these are somewhat due to the perspective of the camera and the style of game itself. It's pure motorsport, but miniaturised and concentrated. As a game, it has a reasonable and rewarding learning curve - the cars are all different enough to require individual learning and specialist driving styles; the circuits are varied and deceptively challenging. It shines at the Master and Superstar difficulty levels in the higher classes; these will offer a serious challenge for most casual players. Not only do you have to be able to drive the car extremely quickly and precisely over one lap to obtain a decent grid position in qualifying, but the race is a (at times honestly very frustrating) high-stress juggling act. You have to drive at that super fast qualifying pace, hitting the apexes correctly and driving the car on the limit at all times whilst managing the tyre wear which changes during the race,  formulating a pit strategy on the fly,  managing the fuel usage which may require using the slipstream, lift-and-coast on the throttle, letting the cars behind bump you down the straights or a combination thereof, performing optimal pit entry and exits, finding your pitbox, hitting the marks in the pit stall precisely so your pit crew can change the tyres efficiently, managing the damage to your vehicle all whilst being raced HARD by 11 other cars which don't mind ramming you out of the way and you have your racing neurons firing on all cylinders. The Superstars difficult level is particularly fiendish... some of the sneaky tactics employed to make you lose are well, impressive. From sending out a rabbit car to make you run out of fuel, pitting out of sequence to make you lose time due to excessive tyre wear, AI cars sharing the draft and bump drafting to catch up, dive bombs, cars intentionally crashing in front of you to make you lose time avoiding the accident, AI cars cheating the pit speed limit and pit entry and many, many more ways to screw you out of the championship. I wish there were more tracks, but it's a small dev team from my understanding so I will cut them some slack. Still, it needs a bit more in the competition dept to give it some depth, maybe making a mirrored version of each championship available or different circuits each time or some other feature for variation.Online matches could be outrageously fun, but I'm having trouble finding anyone to play against. Still, it's well worth the purchase... if you like fun and racing and like having the two combined simultaneously.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but I would like to see more people play it to have more fun in multiplayer :))Everything about this game is lovely, and cute and realistic-ish driving with focus on precision and resources is just so fun.EDIT: With PS and Xbox release, multiplayer is very much fun and players are there! <3 Such a good fun to play multiplayer!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say Circuit Superstars is a unique feeling racing game with charming graphics and a good old top-down perspective, which is rare to see these days. The game embraces the more traditional kind of racing experiences with pit stops and more normal tracks which you could imagine to be in a real life racing setting.There are around 12 cups and 13 cars, which means that you will have around 6 hours of content until you start grinding to be a good player. It luckily isn't stretched like most racing games these days. I also wish for the 13th car, which is a stock car, to get a grand prix cup too. Another thing worth to mention is a top gear racing track which is interesting for people who enjoy time trial.When it comes to the tracks itself, I think they're alright. The game has normal races and Rallycross, and I'd say the 5 Rallycross Maps (I think there are around 5, not sure) are way better designed than most of the 14 default racing tracks. For Rallycross, you have a desert with a train and a unique track layout, furthermore there is also a track called Lost Lagoon which has many jumps and feels less flat. The racing tracks themselves feel good, but they sadly blend in as just another grassy plain track.The AI is a mixed bag. Bigger AI cars like the muscle car feel like they excessively bump into you, also on tracks with U turns all AI, no matter the difficulty or car, just take the turn way too early and bump into the wall. The AI needs a massive improvement.There's a lot of customization in terms of car designs and player model designs, which I appreciate. It makes it feel more unique, and I spent tons of times with customization. Note that not everything will be unlocked from the get go, you have to level up by simply driving races. My only complaint is that the victory poses and animations are a bit abrupt when switching.Other than that, 8/10, a great variety in terms of cars.Here a few recommendations for the devs:-Add more environments for all kinds of races. Stuff like deserts, snowy roads, mountains or generally tracks with more elevation is a must. Simple things like driving over a bridge makes the tracks stick out MUCH more.-As mentioned, the stock car grand prix. Either make more maps or make it an endurance test with like 20 or so rounds.-A car recommendation would be a go-kart, or generally something with fast acceleration-More fluent switching between victory and default pose.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: BUY - IT - NOW!Circuit Superstars is one of the best racing games ever. PERIOD. It is Top Down rtacing games that represents motorsports the best possible way including strategy, feul usage, tire wear and damage. Amazing graphics and amazing car physics complete it.The game is amazing, it allows cross play and four local players, wich could go online together from the same computer.Circuit Superstars community is big, active and friendly
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun pick up and play with a controller racing game.Only complaints I have:1) Fix the way that Rallycross cars handle.  Doesn't drive like a rallycross car and was too tail happy.2) Allow to exit in the middle of a tournament and pickup where you left off, instead of having to finish it all in one go.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, what a great game, having been around a while, and remembering some of the top down/isometric classics that have gone before, Circuit Superstars is EVERYTHING I could have wanted from an updated, modern day interpretation of this style.The graphics are great! Track design is superb, cars are great little stylised representations of their real world equivalents, and instantly recognisable to motor-sport fans.Audio is great too, love the little touches with the crowd cheering, the exhausts popping when you release the accelerator, lovely. Also, the lovely understated but effective VFX, little clouds of tyre smoke when you wheels spin, exhaust fumes, little pops of flame, tracks in the gravel/grass when you go off road. (Would love to see some left of the tyres and dragged back onto the track when you return to it!)Animation and physics are great too, with the little driving turning their heads into corners, the cars spinning when they hit gravel at speed while turning, the jumps having real gravitas, especially when landing.Everything combined has led to me really enjoying this game, and its well worth the money! I think I've already spent a few too many hours trying to perfect laps on the weekly time trails! In fact most of my time is spent there! There are some truly fast people already! Great stuff.Can definitely recommend this to old video games/motor-sport fans like myself, but also to just, well, anyone really, its really accessible and great fun to play!*Regarding the 'bumper cars' issues during racing, I think maybe a 'contact' scale rating could be a good addition? Just a bar that increases every time you hit someone, that deducts time or points depending on server preference, and/or possibly slows cars for time when full (Like cutting the track)- bigger the impact, more it fills, once penalty is served, bar starts from fresh again.*Either that, or add a player 'contact' rating to a 'Racing License' that carries with their profile, could be a nice way of dressing it, so people can set up servers that only allow people who have 'clean racer' on their license if its desired?Anyway, I'll definitely be purchasing it again once the PS4 version is released! :) Great work so far and massive Kudos to Original Fire Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of top-down(-ish) racers, ever since the original Death Rally. Recently there seems to have been a little surge with these types of racers. Most notably Art of Rally and this. A few years back I enjoyed Little Racers: Street too. Gotta say this is the best of them and by some margin.Graphically I find it amazing, simplistic but stylish and really beautiful. Runs extremely well even with older hardware (hello 980gtx). The cars have something of a chibi style which I really like.The driving is (almost) perfect. The cars drive well and where you'd expect them too, they have a really nice feel and animation to them. I haven't gotten to trying all of the cars yet but Stadium Supertrucks legit blew my mind. You can feel that soft suspension in every turn. My only complaints for the cars and driving in general are actually pretty miniscule, but something I'll note anyway. Here's some pro's and cons for the cars and drivability.+ Racing line matters more than you'd think for a game like this which was quite a surprise!+ Cool models if you like the style, some are pretty detailed+ Even the trucks are fun to race (name one other game with trucks that are fun to drive)+ The animation for suspension, braking, turning is so smooth and dare I say cute?Cons (really minor)- Engine sounds are pretty weak, it's not something I car massively about but they feel pretty generic like it's from some "engine pack 001 for games".- Some cars seem a bit too slippery? Especially the 1960s formula car.- The AI will never make mistakes, on any difficulty, they just drive slower/fasterI might update this when I've played more, but for me it's a 9/10, 3 hours in.Oh and some feedback to the devs;Please close the pitlane in races where you're not meant to pit. It's definitely a lost race if you accidentally end up there on higher difficulty settings. Also I've multiple times gotten "recovered" to the pitlane even though I crashed outside of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: A game with so much potential and hopefully they can deliver patches to improve the game in the future. Graphics, feeling and atmosphere is first class. Network play need some real improvements. It should be possible to just start some casuel racing with a friend and fill the race with AI drivers. Now you can only play online and you need to wait for 5 minutes at least. Some stuttering as well in the network gameplay. If they continue to improve this game it can be a future classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I was hoping for really. It feels solid as ever and it's chibi art style and music are a delight but the controls. Oh boy, they feel stiff and weirdly overresponsive to the point where a single nudge on the joystick sends the car careening to a wall like if I was driving on ice. But hey, everything else feels great so I do recommend it if you like top down racers
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game, Online lobby could be much better, being able to choose to play tournament would be nice. This came up and got picked once, best racing of my  9 hours raced so far. More tournament ie (grand prix style, 4 races with points system) please  and with options to choose more laps and circuits. Then 10/10 Currently 9/10Really fun but challenging and competitive racing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the garage so far, driving feels pretty good, angle and vision about right. so far only visited single payer as I work in understanding the circuits and the racing. Keyboard play is possibly but prefer controller. Time trials works well. Will update this if I stay hooked and dive into MP. Looking forward to ovals release shortly.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great top down view racing game, which needs way more recognition than it's actually getting. The physics are great and the game is really fun to play, with still alot of new gameplay being added. Overall the creators put a lot of effort in the game and it really shows in this great enjoyable game!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Just Brilliant. Frustrating especially as you can do everything right for three races and get wiped out on lap 1 of the final race and lose a championship but it makes it all the more challenging. More tracks and a way to make additional pit stops a viable strategy would be great but generally its a massive thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's closest you can get to simulation driving but, still more fun then just driving around trying to be a good driver. This has that Mario Kart feel I've always loved but, no one ever wanted to just race in Mario Kart without items. This also brings me back to that classic Off Road arcade game back in the day. But, this game is unique and should be more recognized than it is. It's not just racing, it's enjoyable racing even if you lose.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Fun top-down racer with pleasant handling and just enough realism to have fun. Clearly takes inspiration from GeneRally. My only gripe is that I wish I had the option to zoom out more. As it is right now it's hard to see ahead on the track (a common issue in top-down racers). You pretty much have to memorize each corner. Please let us zoom out!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.I have always thought that those casual kart games featured power-ups, oil stains, etc. just to hide boring drive mechanics/physics.This game does not feature any of those, it is just bare racing, to the point that running alone through a circuit feels satisfying.Also, the art style is very beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I had already seen this game on my facebook timeline earlier this year and this week it was time to actually buy it. No regrets !If you have played the classics like "Death Rally" or "Ignition", you will certainly fall in love with this racing beauty!!- The game looks fantastic. The colours, the cuteness of all the cars, the tracks, the environment, the effects such as smoke, sparks and skid marks are beautifully worked out.- There is a steep learning curve to steer/control the different types of cars around the track for a perfect lap. So you really have to invest time to get to know the cars.- It plays great with a gamepad.- Plenty of tracks and cars to choose from.- The replay value is definitely present.- I would like a practice mode, just for practice different combinations of cars and tracks.- Would like to see the different track layouts in the track select menu. Now you have to regonize the track on some photo's.- Possibility to have night races. Cars with headlights and different lighting arround the track.- Weather like rain. Get your rain tyres and look for the dry line etc- A more extensive Time Trial mode, where you can choose your own car/track combination.- Audio effects are fine, but some car sounds could be polised a little bit further. Would like to hear the GP cars scream with a v10 or v12 for example.- Restart option in the pause menu. Now you have to go to the main menu and start the session again from there.- Some cars are drifting to much. Mayaby a way to make the GP cars more glued to the track, and capable to take the corners with more speed, like in real life? More difference between the top cars, like the GP, GT and the prototype. They feel more the same at the moment.- More tracks..... I would like to see more rallycross venues with jumps etc. But also a track like Le Mans or some tracks with longer length.- More cars...... Mayby Karting, LMP prototype with closed cockpit, Classic DTM 90's, - This will probably remain a dream, but some kind of track editor?
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique and fun-packed thrill of motorsport racing. From its colorful, eye-catching visuals to its bumping sountrack, even the average player who is not familiar with the world of motorsport will get a taste of what it's like to get behind the wheel and burn rubber (literally!) If you are unsure about picking up this game, get it. It is getting updated frequently and will truly grow to become one of the best racing games in the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! This game set a gold standard, easy to pick up, great multiplayer both local and online and at the same time challenging and skill based. It is what gaming used to be, fun and engaging.It is also a very big breath of fresh air in these days that 99% of new games contain zombies that are so "realistic" that you can count the freckles on their face individually. This game is about fun, challenge and gameplay like in the golden age of gaming before everything had to be endless open worlds and rivet counting "realism".  Get it, you wont be sorry!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: the game is really cool, for my part the only fault I could find in it and that it lacks a circuit editor. but I really recommend it, it is entertaining, I play it with my family.le jeu est vraiment cool, pour ma part le seul défaut que j'ai pu lui trouver et qu'il manque un éditeur de circuit. mais je le recommande vraiment, c'est divertissant, j'y joue avec ma famille.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great racing game. I only have 14 hs on record but they are enough to prove wrong my initial doubts about an early access game. The game fisics are pretty good and you will have to be taking care of your racing lines and ettiquete or you'll never win a race. The community is growing and the devs are listening. When I got it, it was almost impossible for me to find someone online to play with, that has been an issue that the community spoke up about, and the devs (with limited resources) have adressed the issue as best they could. Now it is playable and enjoyable online. It went from  1v1 races at best, to races up to 9 cars with no waiting. If this dynamic and loving development continues I think the future for this game is bright.One of those "a minute to learn a life time to master" kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Rock n' Roll Racing meets Forza Motorsport with a charming aesthetic that is hard to beat.  Easy to pick up and play as there's only a handful of controls at your disposal, but truly challenging to master.  If you're looking for an arcade racer that you can sink your teeth into for a while - this is a title with a lot of heart that's probably worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun racing game.Looks and plays very well, surprisingly.The Physics are spot on, the feel and feed back is really good on my Xbox controller, the online racing is tons of fun also very competitive but tons of fun.There are Pit stops the lot.Playing @ 3440 x 1400 on ultra wide Screen looks and plays great.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this since EA and I love it. The devs' story and the love for details, like rubber on the track, tire-wear, fuel-consumption, pit-speed limit and pit-stops in a game like this is just awesome. I can relate really well to the controls. I mostly drive time attack, some Grand Prix and did drive with a friend. So I can't say a lot about how online-racing is. The circuits are well selected and done and the selection of cars has something for everyone, IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Curcuit Superstars is the best fun-racer I have played for a long time. The controls are a bit tricky to grasp at the beginning but once you understand the physical model, the joy of optimizing your driving begins - at least if you have analog sticks on your joypad. Everything looks really cute, but the simulation is pretty serious. It runs really fast even on my not-so-gaming PC and loading times are close to zero which makes it perfect for quick in-between sessions. I should also mention the soundtrack which ranges from Synthwave to typical 90's mainstream house tracks that are very catchy and well produced. Would love to download and listen to them separately.Right now, the game is totally playable and a must-have for fans of Track Mania, Ignition (Bleifuss Fun) and Micro Machines, if you remember them from back in the days. However it lacks many features one would normally expect today, like save game the game during a grand prix or having an overview of all the records. There is surely a lot to improve here, while the core of the game, i.e. the racing engine, is perfect in my opinion and should be left untouched from now.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and all, but it would be much better if my car would sit still in the pit lane. I swear 90% of the time when I go to my pit box, my car keeps creeping forward when it should be at a full stop. My pit crew will run up to the car, pick it up, then drop it because they think I am driving out. They repeat this process extremely quickly and never actually finish the pit stop. I am not even able to complete longer races because I have to go to the pit at some point. If this problem gets fixed, this game will be as close to perfection as I could imagine.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, a perfectionist's wet dream and nightmare at the same time. That being said the top down element is executed REALLY poorly and could be improved, even tilting the camera 45 degrees and fixing it to see in front of you much more clearly would be a drastic improvement to the game. Had a blast playing but I'm going to refund as the camera is just not something I can personally get past.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: this is, while still in early access, a great little racing game. it's got a good mix of physics, sim mechanics, and it looks and feels great to play. A must-pick for any true racing fan - this game brings out the best parts of pure racing and packages them into an experience that is as easy to pick up and play, but even more difficult to put down and further, master.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome hybrid racing game with lots of variety of cars. It's like a Micro Machines and Gran Turismo had game baby! All the fun of small car racing, but the realistic physics for handling, tyre wear and fuel consumption. Can't wait for the full release with hopefully a few more updates to make this a really great game that I'll keep coming back to time and time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: One of my only reviews on Steam and Ive been a Steam member for almost 20 years.. This is hands down one of the most well done Arcade-Style Racers. For it being arcade-ish, dont let that fool you, it can be very competitive and feel nearly like a simulator racer. Very very fun, especially for mindless fun. I highly recommend throwing on some tunes and cruisin the tracks!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally bother to post reviews, this game breaks that trend for me - its so good. The feel of the cars is great, different classes have a real unique feel and personality that gives this game such depth and character.On top of the fantastic handling model adding all the details like tyre wear, pit stops, fuel really offers so much in an overlooked (until now) genre. The game looks fantastic and love the little details of the crowd, the pit crews and the nods to historic tracks and cars.The only slight negative is currently not being able to browse lobby's or set the race settings, but that's just an early access road map tether while they focus on core game play.What they've done so far is bloody brilliant :)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This racing game is one of the BEST I've ever played.  Arcade-style in looks with racing sim physics and strategy.  I've been wanting a game like this for a long time.  It's fun to play but difficult to master.  Racing against others online is a blast.  I'm hoping others pick this game up because there needs to be fuller lobbies.  If your a racing fan AT ALL, pick this game up! you will not regret it.  The devs really have something here, and their constant updating proves it.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is coming along nicely, though I'd like a few things.-Alt cameras (following the car or even on board shots would be great IMO.)-NASCAR  style cars and tracks (With more cars, comes more representation, and a stock car styled racer and a few oval tracks would be a welcome thing IMO)-Street Tracks-More Offroad/Stadium tracksJust things I'd like to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game with an approach to driving physics that remind me of MicroMachines. On one hand, it's very accessible and great fun to drive and learn. On the other hand, it is really challenging to understand the different types of cars and surfaces in order to master the different tracks. It feels close to a simulation physics-wise but is as fun to play as most arcade games. The team is motivated as hell and friendly as heaven. They implemented most of the remarks that were made on Discord and keep on working on new features and improvements even after the release. The AI is too crash-prone for my taste and often times it seems that I am affected by crashes way more than my AI opponents, but the team already announced that this will be fixed within the next updates. If you like racing, invest your money in this game. The only thing you'll regret will be that you burn hour after hour because you want to master the next level of driving, get the next trophy or simply can't stop playing. This game could easily become one of my all-time-favourites, if it not already is.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: [Early Access v0.3.1 at time of writing]A very promising start! Gorgeous visual style with plenty of charm and a really fun driving model. It can take a few laps to shake off the expectation of easy arcade-style handling, but once that happens it all feels pretty natural. The ability to customise the colours used in the liveries is a nice touch!Looking forward to seeing how the content grows moving towards the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, but has a ways to go. The simple, stylized graphics are beautiful, the physics are terrific and the menu music is low-key awesome. The level progression currently feels kinda slow and the arcade mode difficulty escalates very quickly. My biggest gripe has to be the lack of custom game lobbies in multiplayer. It does say it's currently in Beta, but I think prioritizing multiplayer could really help to attract more players.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been looking for a game just like this for the longest time and when I least expected, it was handed to me. Critique sandwich follows- I loved the micro machines racers as a kid and many racers since both arcade and sim. This is a great blend with a fun look to it. Being able to customize my driver and car liveries are a bonus. Currently the arcade mode is....there but is still in development. The online is also being worked on thoroughly but I have seen the progression the team has made so I have faith in its development. Finally, the way each vehicle handles is fantastic, the variety of driving profiles is great. From Baja Trucks to 60s open wheel to a Fiat 500 esque and more each vehicle added brings even more variety. The variety of tracks being added are nice as well. A must play for racing fans both casual and competitive!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I am updating this review now that it is released. I'll start by saying that I absolutely LOVE the hell out of this game. Trust me this is not just another indie top down racing game, this one  is special! You really have to play it to appreciate how satisfying it is drifting and sliding these little cars round corners, the handling really is spot on, sure maybe i'd like to see a few more tracks and cars down the line but even at this stage (just after release) there is a lot of single player content, I just can't say how much I love this game, it is bar none the best game of it's type on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of top down racing games, this hits the spot. I've been waiting for a game like this. Despite it's cute aesthetics, it is really quite involving. It feels like RC cars with Traction Control. On my best form, I'm about a second off the top guys - so there's a lot of scope for improvement in terms of my driving skills. It's still Early Access so I'm excited about what kind of content the finished product will have.Since it's coming to consoles, I'm really hoping for cross-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving this game.  It's not yet perfect, but it's still in such early access that I am hyped about it!  I don't think I've ever purchased an unfinished game (knowingly hint hint BF5) but with this I am HAPPY to play it and help them iron it out and make it a perfect release.  I really hope this game catches on with the masses like rocket league has.  I love this game and I eagerly await every bit of content they drop into it! Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing arcade racer with realistic physics and fun style of graphics great to play at a party or with friends i only have one complaint please please dear developers turn down the music in the main menu in my opinion even the 1 is still to loud i felt i was loosing my hearing as i was setting up my awesome character other than that great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: If you like to hammer the gas down full throttle and steer, then this is not the game for you. If you enjoy a semi-realistic type racing sim where you have to actually brake at the proper time and use the throttle wisely, then you'll enjoy CS. It has a lot going for it even in EA.I was really surprised to see my cars get damaged, leave smoke trails and slow down after smashing into the walls and other cars a bit much on my first few tries when I was getting the hang of how to drive. But once you get it down it's a helluva lot of fun. The only cars I'm having issues with are the muscle cars, but I see they're going to be adding tuning into an upcoming version and hopefully I can adjust some of the looseness they seem to have. As is you have to really take it easy with the gas or you risk losing control.The graphics are great, the gameplay is awesome and it's just straight out fun to play. Once there are more tracks and car options this game will be a huge success I'm sure. One addition that I think would be welcome would be the ability to fine tune the difficulty to the players liking, possible being able to select the # of AI opponents you'd like at each difficulty level or something along those lines.I sure hope they add mod support and custom tracks because I'd like to see this game with an oval track with more cars so you can run a CS 500 type race. Nighttime racing with headlights on an endurance mode with changing weather would be pretty cool too. A motorcycle DLC later on would be nice as well. ;)As is, it's a fun little racing game it just lacks content at this time, but hey, it's EA so that is to be expected. The base game is great though so support the developers early so they can build this baby out to it's full potential! =)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: You can get some really good racing out of this game. The pit stops make for an extra challenge, and the AI can is quite good - both at being fast and slow. Finally, the game looks beautiful and actually runs very nicely (except the sometimes not very smooth camera, hoping that's gonna be fixed soon)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything great about racing but in an arcade like theme. Pick your racing line, curse the driver next to you for not giving you room, late brake to get the overtake done, touch the apex, accelerate, graze the kerb, and rinse and repeat! There are some rough edges that are to be expected with an EA that i am positive will be ironed out shortly. To my surprise there are quite a few tracks to pick from as well as vehicles. Seeing the track rubber in as the race goes on is my favorite feature. There is something nostalgic about playing it. Highly recommend this title as it will only continue to get better! It's also a remote play title!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually incredibly fun, the classic easy to pick up but hard to master kinda thing. The problem is there are only like 15 people online in the entire world at any given time, so you're not going to find a multiplayer race. And I bought this game for the online racing as it looked incredibly fun.Outside of that, the time trial with ghosts is actually a pretty good time sink. I don't understand how this game doesn't have a thriving online community though, it's a good time! Please everyone buy it so multiplayer becomes an actual thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's the type of game I really like.I will write down the shortcomings for a more complete game in the future.1. When the car slides in a corner, I want the tire skid sound to be heard earlier and more. Right now, I'm a little frustrated and lacking in pleasure.2. When the direction change key is released, the straightness of the car is awkward.3. When damage accumulates in the car and the engine smokes, it would be nice if the engine rattled and the broken sound was heard.4. It feels like the steering angle is lacking. Add a steering angle to get through corners faster, or add a side brake function.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: With the polish this game already has, and how freaking fast these meaningful updates keep drop'n this my fellow racing people and  even you wheel owning `Sim die hard ladies and gentlemen will love this instant Top Down Racing Classic, it is most defiantly a "BUY" with two enthusiastic thumbs UP - Baby, Baby- (Said with a hint of The Notorious B.I.G vibe at the end lol)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The racing is top notch. Each of the cars feel different from one another, as well as the track surfaces feel real.  Love how the rubber sticks to the track showing the most taken grooves.Pros:Graphics (Cartoon FTW)Gameplay (Love the classic arcade feel with pit stops and such)Physics (Each car and track surface has its own feel)Cons:Unable to save during arcade progression.  (This is a problem as some of the circuits have 6 races with 25 laps.) Hopefully this will be addressed soon!Unable to skip thru after races complete.  (Meaning you have to listen to the music and wait for the game to progress.)Although its early access I think this is well worth the money if you are a racing fan.Cant wait for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: OK so after a bit more  more time with this game it is clear that it has more content and polish and is a slightly more complete a package. Everything is pretty much as you'd expect for a top-down 3D racer with all the usual modes and things. If anything that's a bit of a problem in that it does nothing new, mostly it's little things that separate it from games of yester-year. So game play features like tyre wear and fuelling are there as is drafting, but it doesn't go into any detail, (no weather or compounds) this is arcade through n through.My issues are that I find it very difficult to improve my pace. I play sim racers as a rule, and I think I get by in a sim. But here, the cars don't behave with the precision I would have liked to see. Braking seems to have a fixed speed and no fine control, steering is sluggish and I don't feel I'm ever turning anywhere near as fast as I should be at full lock. It almost feels very digital, not analogue and maybe that's by design, but I cannot figure how to get faster and more competitive against the CPU. As for real racers it's hit and miss but in time trials some people are great, and online people put in fast laps simply using keyboard. I don't know why but I thought a controller would give my more precision, but it never feels like it does much. I can tell the throttle has some level of precision on controller, but when I driving I'm either going slow, or going fast, little in between and turning always seems sluggish.Also, no matter what PC I use, there seems to be some stuttering. Every 10 20 seconds or so I get a big stutter. It's been like this through early access and there's no logical reason why it should be doing it, but maybe specific to something running on my PC's? I don't have much issue with other games so... who knows?Point is, some people clearly like this game, and there a fun racer in there I guess, only I am not having much fun right now. Maybe that's just me. I would have liked a bit more to the physics of this game and I still think there's a place for a game to do that. Also I get annoyed having to look away from my vehicle to see my indicated fuel and tire wear, this should be indicated close to the car. Useful for people with very wide screens for sure!I will recommend it only because it's fun and worth a go. This is a nice package, but I'd try it first if you like this kind of thing as you might find it just doesn't sit well with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Can´t recommend this any longer.Not because of the tiny community.Not because of the community drama.But simply because it´s a racing game where overtaking without being dirty or waiting for a mistake is outright impossible in pretty much every single car.Especially in the weaker engine cars the only viable line is the shortest distnace travelled so you need to hug the apex in every single corner. There is no way to make the outside line work, so your only option is to lowkey bump the car infront of you in every corner to either annoy them into a mistake or to simply shove them out of the way.If the car infront of you keeps the inside line and you dare to go even remotely side by side on the outside this will onyl result in you being overtaken by the car behind you taking the inside line.One of those games that used to be fun for me when i was playing worse and overall competition was more chill, this game mechanically simply doesn´t work as a proper racing game for me. With equally skilled driver you end up with a DRS train simulatorr..So many better options out there.Oh and also really weirdly optimized, it makes my GPU fan go into overdrive even in the game menus._____________________________________________________________________I'll recommend this now because it is great fun with the right people, make sure to connect with the active community via discord.Open lobbies can be an awful experience with certain drivers, 0 punishments for ramming / crashing on purpose.Cars behave very different to each other so the game stays reasonably fresh.There are some vital QoL features missing (no sector times, no stop watch, no way to change ghost car settings...)Netcode sadly isn't the best but was improved quite a lot compared to launch.Also the DLC was a huge missed oppurtunity as the game doesn't need gimicky stuff you'll try out once or twice and then forget about the rest of your life (caravan cough cough).____________________________________________________________Still no way to disable ghost in Practise.At least 50% of drivers should have to play with 200% damage so its not bumper cars.No sector times.Almost no player base (except right after "big" updates).____________________I almost fully recommend the game... sadly still gonna have to put a thumbs down for now.Main reason for that is that while they patch and improve the game they still give the player little authority over how he/she actually wants to play the game. Which leaves a sour taste for me and turns me off from logging more hours atm.For example they added a practise mode - that's great!Sadly they also forgot to add a single toggle to enable/disable your ghost car - that sucks!Also still heavily missing a timer for laptimes. Precise sector times would be great, but just the option to add a delta clock at the top already would make solo cruising way more enjoyable while still getting pace feedback.So yeah, mechanically great but the presentation and freedom of customization feel cheap.Let's see what the spring patch with custom lobbies can do for the game.__________________________________________________________________________Edit: The better you get at the game the more fun it becomes - at least that was my experience.There is a bit of a learning curve to go somewhat fast and going reeeally fast takes a lot of practise.They finally added a sort of "queue" to find online matches. If you search for a game online and there is a game in progress with open spots it reserves a spot for you and lets you do other things till the next race select starts.I can only account for the EU evening time slot but you tend to get decently fast and big (8-12 player) lobbies and the core group you meet regurarly races very fair. I highly recommend joining the Discord server and checking the live-race paddock, you will reach most of the core group there.There was a patch a while ago that improved the netcode immensely, close racing is now way easier without immediately murdering each other on the slightest mistake.The cars feel refreshingly different and you might notice you're quicker in some compared to others, the driving style needed to be quick in each car varies quite a bit.Solo content is probably the weakest point of the game, online and time trial is where the fun is to be had (for me).__________________________________________________________________________Just came back yesterday after testing the game for a while in early access. Gotta say it improved quite a lot, especially in the presentation and game flow. Online lobbies easily filled up to 5-10 players throughout the night and I managed to get multiple close races.Nice foundation with lots of possibilites for future content, just car collision netcode could be improved on somehow, tends to get a bit laggy for a few moments even on soft contacts.

_childDocuments_.review: A very competent racing game with a unique art style. Every car and track has it's own feel that really sets it apart from the others.The A.I is challenging at points and a pushover at others which is a shame. They go very slowly through the racing line and yet sometimes it's impossible to catch up.As of right now there are only 4(?) tracks in the game which really isn't enough to justify the price point however the developers look very active so I don't doubt there will be many more to come. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's still early access but the core gameplay of this is great. The handling and dynamics of the cars are really crisp and each has it's own feel and distinct characteristics. Practice helps and you can see the improvement in your laptime as you refine your lines and technique. There's a surprising level of nuance for what looks like an arcade racer on the surface, pit stop strategies, tyre wear and fuel usage all count and can affect the result of races.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Almost all of my favorite games have one thing in common - they are easy to pick up and play, but difficult to truly master. This is another one of those games. Everyone knows how to drive a car, but this game takes it to another level. I enjoy it because it's somewhere between a realistic racing game and Mario Kart. No items or anything to throw at your opponents, but the simple controls remind me of Mario Kart. While the need to keep an eye on your vehicle's health, gas and tires the whole race reminds me of true NASCAR/F1 type games; as well as the different handling, braking and turning you get from each different vehicle type.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking at this game, on the fence on whether, or not, to get this game. So I did, and I will be going for a refund...At this point in time, they have a game that needs some added features. It seems to be more made for consoles than PC (and looks like a crappy PC port than a game that would work for the PC). Simple things, like a menu that allows you to change what little settings it has. Also, this game needs a 3rd person camera, or a Iso 3rd person camera, BAD. _childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Classic, top down arcade racer, with sim elements.5 years in development and it shows in the core mechanics. A lot of care and attention has been poured into this. Easy to learn yet difficult to master. You'll be playing this for a long time to come. It's so addictive once you find the groove. It's incredibly challenging.The Damage, Fuel and Tyre Wear add an awesome strategy to a simple yet fun arcade game. It amazes me how well it works, drive conservatively and save fuel for a 1 stop, or go flat out and 2 stop. Get damaged at the beginning (happens a lot with first turn terry's), go pit and try run a long stint. It's all smiles either way.They have limited the online play to random matchmaking, so whilst frustrating you can't play with you're friends, we've found if you join lobbies at the same time, you nearly always end up in a race together. I understand why they've done this, to keep people playing online and what a blast it is. Join the Discord and get involved, they seem quite a nice bunch of folks. Had some great racing, very cool.Currently theirs 3 races per week which are changed every Thursday and 3 time attacks featuring a selection of ghosts from the leaderboard etc. Very cool and addictive. They obviously think about this and not just throw random races out there.Theirs an exp system for you're driver that leans more on race distance than winning, so your always progressing. I like that system.The art style is gorgeous, the music is pumping and addictive, it's on point. Again, a lot of care and attention here.Overall, very limited content wise but what is there is pure gold, all of it. It ticks all the boxes for gameplay, nostalgia, art, music and good racing.An instant classic, just needs more people to take a punt, it's highly recommended. It's a 6 man team, don't expect the earth to be moved and remember it's early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I view Circuit Superstars as the grown up, competitive version of Mario Kart. What you have is a game that is very easy to learn how to play, but very difficult to master. It's the perfect blend of arcade with simulation aspects. You get tyre wear, you get fuel usage, you get damage which can all be used in viable pit strategies. The players that are able to race both consistently and cleanly are the ones who win the race, where as the more aggressive drivers will push their luck too far and crash out.The online multiplayer, while not perfect, is miles and bounds greater than what it was at launch / early-access. You can easily invite your friends into the same lobby as you, the net code is vastly improved although with latency it does still get wonky. The only thing I wish we had was a rating system that goes up and down with your race placements. Aside from that, this game is exactly the kind of casual competitive arcade racer that I didn't know I wanted. I highly recommend this wonderfully imagined, and extremely well executed indie racing game that will only get better as it's online community grows!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game at first and like how it has been adding new tracksBut the game will soon get boring with the limit to having Modding ability and also i cant see why Track Creation and steam workshop cannot be implemented....Overall i think this game is worth buying but im just not in for another car game that i will get bored of eventually as there is editing mechanics that would lift the game overall.Maybe if they do in the future i may re-buy...
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game for any racer who wants a fun challenge. Circuit Superstars is the most fun i have had in a arcade/sim racer. Yes, this game is both an arcade racer and a sim racer. Circuit Superstars is like if Nintendo made Gran Turismo. There is the cute and soft art style that feels at home with Nintendo. Plus the fixed top-down camera angle gives it an arcade style perspective. The fixed perspective also gives the player a new and challenging way to race and read the corners. This is because physics still work in this game similar to more serious racing games. Tire wear, Fuel consumption, engine damage, track grip, realistic driving lines, and competitive AI makes Circuit Superstars a one of a kind.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously with this being in early access you have to expect things to be buggy and there to be improvements but I think the concept is really great and can make the game a hit. Things I would like to see improved/bugs I've found:-Private/Friend only lobbies.-Audio Lag seems to happen a lot even when my frames are fine-AI drivers could use a little work, the only time they seem to know you're there is if you have a corner cutting penalty-Additional cars in each class (Obviously this will come with time but I'm honestly fairly hype to see this area grow)-Adding a practice mode, or the option for a practice session before qualifying. Using qualifying as a time to learn the track can be a little frustrating/confusing. Sometimes I find myself wondering if I should play on a higher difficulty because if I botch qualifying it's gonna be that much harder to work my way through the pack while still learning the map, but for my more preferred tracks I find myself kind of running through the competition.-Interstate has a couple of normal design flaws, the rock walls being jagged make it hard to judge/corner effectively and some of the rocks near apex's can make it feel like you are being punished for driving an optimum route. Plus the pit lane is just not in a good spot, maybe round the final corner a bit more and swap the front stretch and pit lane. As it is, the front stretch is hard to access and can become a clog of AI cars coming out of the final turns, not to mention how technical the gap is to hit in the first place. I really enjoyed the gameplay and it's fairly addicting the tire wear and fuel consumption are awesome as well as the interactive track that wears at time goes on. I don't want the things I've mentioned be things that should scare people away from the game, but just small things that I think can be fine tuned to make this game very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game.  On the surface It appears to be an arcade game; but it drives like a simulator.  Thus, even hard core racing gamers may find it entertaining.  Miss your breaking-point and your in the wall; on the gas to early and you'll swap-ends.  The top-down view seemed a little counter-intuitive at first.  But in time an awakening occurs and you'll be driving like Fangio .  Nailing the perfect corner is even more gratifying then hitting the perfect apex in many other racing games.  I'm not sure what the long-term value is.  Time will tell.  If the game continues to be developed, e.g., more tracks, cars, etc., then it has a bright future.  Congratulations to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: The learning curve is absurd. In career mode the first two levels can beaten on your first go. After that you'll never win a championship again and believe me I tried. One mistake will ruin a race in a game where the precise control required to follow a perfect line can be difficult due to the angled top down view and twitchy controls. In so many ways Circuit Superstars gets it right but I'm afraid to say I'm giving up on it.

_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Still very early and a work-in-progress, but the basics of a great top-down arcade game here are really strong.  The physics are controllable and rewarding.  Driving technique is easy to pick up, hard to master.  The  different vehicle types have distinctive handling.  Contact with other cars is solid and will slow you down, but in a way that you can recover from.  The game gets the basics of cornering right.The graphics are a welcome leap forward for a top-down arcade racer - it's a cheerful little bobblehead world.  Cars and tracks look great.  The implementation of fuel, tire wear, and pit stops (all of which you can turn on or off) is also huge.The cars and environment also feel truly three dimensional.  They aren't flat sprites going over a flat image.  When you go up on curbs, cones or other things, the car's suspension reacts and there is visible body roll.  Harder impacts can lift your wheels off the ground, and the car bounces noticeablyThere are a few negatives.  At this point, the AI is not balanced (some series or tracks it's too easy, others it's too hard).  A fleshed out career/campaign mode would be great.  Could stand more variety in tracks - currently there are a half dozen and mostly seem inspired by F1 circuits.  Online doesn't really work yet - really hope they nail this, as this could be a great game if it could fill multiplayer races quickly and cleanly.   Most concerning is that there is no workshop support and currently no plans for it.  A game like this would gain a lot of value from community-made tracks, cars, or other stuff.Give this one a shot, especially if you like arcade racers.   Even in an early access state, it's among the best top-down racing games, period.

_childDocuments_.review: That perfect balance of simple enough gameplay / art style to enjoy casually yet deep enough to put in the work to master and find time on every lap. In longer races you can actually mix pit strategies.-Driving is very satisfying and rewarding, IMO best you're going to get in top down racing. -Dev team continually provides updates and very apparent they care about the game and community interests. -Wide range of vehicles to choose from and flexible race settings in offline mode for fun A.I. scenarios.-Online is still improving in both gameplay and options but still really fun as is with a good group.
