_childDocuments_.review: Basically a blatant (modern) copy of GeneRally from 2002. Go download that for free and you'll appreciate what this miniature game is all about. I have to say, I don't like the follow camera, I much preferred the static camera in GeneRally because it's not as easy to look into the corners and be perfect every lap. The game is Early Access, does need some work, but has a lot of promise. The only advantage GeneRally has over this is the track editor, and I made a ton of my own tracks back in the day!I am surprised there is no reference to GeneRally or appreciation for the original developer. GeneRally 2 is due to come out soon from a Kickstarter project, so this is a big slap in the face in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Just woow, cant wait for more content. Core of the game, physics etc. is just super enjoyable. 10/10 game for me// After some timeI feel disappointed, production pace of this game is extremely slow, instead of publishing tools (car and truck editor) which would drastically improve the lack of content, designers are forcing us to wait months and years.I was hoping it will be my Gene Rally from my childhood, it will be but when i reach 80 years old. Summarize: the game is good but it's still demo version.Dont buy, waste of money, you will play it once and you will never go back.I wish some bigger company could take this project from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic start!!! Looove the 1 on 1 battles you can get into. Love being able to drive into the pits. Sound FX are great too.I know you made this as an arcade game but you can do so many things to this, listen to all the guys giving you hype on youtube etc... you could totally be the first to make an arcade style sim. Create your own Genre even!!! - Choice of gas / tires / both when entering pits? maybe even soft, med and hard?? lol- some type of boost system possibly? I really like the fact that there's no upgrades but if everyone had a chance at getting a boost here and there somehow or maybe like an ers/drs type of idea would be pretty cool.- more tire wear effect? - Less gas makes you faster?- damage slows you down?- pit strategies before you start the race? (planned pit stops)- this one is a big one for me: why make the cars invisible at all? even if they are a lap car I found it took me out of the immersion when I just drove straight through other cars.Anyway, GREAT GAME guys. Looking forward to seeing what you add.-
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun little game, definitely difficult and worth the money. My recommendation for newer players is to use the break the biggest issue I had was I wasn't using causing me to finish last in most races. However, there are still a few issues, the game's online doesn't seem to work very well I rarely can get an online match.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Very annoying, it was easy on first 3 difficulties - qualifying 3+ seconds in the lead and lapping people and then all of a sudden requires pin-point accuracy on highest 2 difficulties. Like a perfect lap puts you on pole but by like 0.01-0.1 seconds. And even then when you get pole and lead a race the other cars literally smash you into a wall and ruin it. No restart options or anything.Otherwise, looks pretty and runs well. Controls are ok but the cars are a tad floaty to control. It could also do with brake board markers for reference in the faster cars.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: i love my sim racing but when i need a break from it, this game is so much fun, we all need a good top down racer thats more about fun than realism, I highly recommend this game if you just wanna chill and have fun, graphics are pretty cool, again they arent gonna blow your mind but its nice to see different art in certain games,
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this for 45 minutes so far but I'm loving it. This title has only just entered early access co content is somewhat limited at present. That said, the gaming experience so far is great and I'm really looking forward to watching this game evolve.The driving experience is pretty good for this type of game and I love the quality of the graphics. I race twice a week with friends on cross play games (Forza) but cross play games are extremely limited currently. I'm really hoping that cross play and user created lobbies are implemented as I think this would make the game a massive hit in the future.In conclusion, this title is early access so don't expect anything like a feature complete game. If you're not concerned about the current limited content and don't mind taking a gamble on early access titles then give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: If you like top down racers, buy this game. Basically enough said. It's about as good as they come in this genre, and there aren't many good titles. Really cool mechanics - driving feels realistic & requires skill. Recommended.My only suggestion is that they should really add damage from crashing not just into other cars, but also into course barriers etc. It then creates a real disincentive & penalty for going too fast into corners etc. There still is not enough of a penalty from crashing and this does undermine the realism somewhat. Only a minor quibble though.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Love it. The handling of the cars feels really really nice - to be honest it reminds me of those remote-car places i went to when i was young, where we could just try out and drive any of the available cars on the tracks.Kinda nostalgia going on there. Pretty surprised about that.Also the graphics are just so nice!10/10 go for it! Just needs a ranked competitive mode, and open daily live tournaments etc.56 hours later: even better when you sink some of your precious time into it!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a LOT of potential but first that auto-steering correction has GOT TO GO!!It's horrendous! You are constantly fighting with the controls to get your car to go in the direction you want it to instead of the direction that the game thinks you should. At the very least, make it optional so that it can be turned off.I would also like to see a handbrake option so that the cars can be driven like rally cars. Tap the handbrake to throw the back end out for a tighter turn.If those two features were implemented then I couldn't fault this game at all. It is everything I loved from the Amiga era of gaming brought right up to modern times. Perfect!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's early access and it is very rough around the edges, but the soul of a game is here. The way the cars handle is a level above games of this genre with subtle techniques that are hard to master. The cars 'feel' right in way that encourages you to experiment and improve your times. It reminds me of Trackmania, not necessarily in how it plays exactly but the potential scope of it. If this game gets built out properly and adds a track creator, race types, servers, multiplayer championship etc then it could be a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game great potential, been waiting for a game like this for quit some time now. Did take me a few race to get used to it. It would be great if there is a progressive mode in career/arcade so it has a whole new dept to it, I was unable to find any multi player race in my short time (maybe due to region player base?) . since it's still early access it lacks some features but man the graphic and game play are nice for this kind of racing. An option to use mouse to select menu and colour in game would be a better choice rather than using key on the keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The place where this game really shines is in the controls and the feel of the racing. Clearly the devs have spent a lot of time refining the driving model and ensuring that the game can be played in different input devices.This is a blend of arcade and simulation racer, and it definitely delivers on the promise of easy to learn and hard to master.If you crank up the difficulty on the AI you should expect a real challenge where you have to work on finding the optimal lines through corners, the right braking points, and finding the gaps to overtake.The game is in early access but the racing itself is very polished. The game runs well and I didn't encounter any bugs. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Actually quite fun game.  It's like those old 16 and 8-bit overhead racing games.  I feel like I'm racing RC gars in a little diorama!It's in early access.  The devs are adding tracks and cars.  There's some UI and QOL things that I'm sure they'll work on, but fur now, it's an adorable little game.  Definitely one to watch!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: After a quite underwhelming Micro Machines World Series reboot, Circuit Superstars represented the spark of hope we expected for a game of its kind.Don't get fooled by its cutesy lookling visuals, the physics may be easy to take but it offers a real sense of depth and strategy. It simply is the best top down racer of this decade since Generally and Micro Machines V4, and yet it's early access!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: If you had a like for the old-school top down arcade racer this one should be on your list.The AI are hard to win against, control are simple, pits stops are a thing and you have your own pit crew.Single Player mode, Hotlap challenge, multiplayer online, playing with your steam friends isn't really possible at the moment unless you try to queue at the same time and hope for the best, how ever you can plug more than one controller and split screen up to 4 players.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This will sound dumb, because I've only played this for about 20 minutes. But this game is going to be huge.I was playing Rock n Roll Racing in the Blizz thing recently, remembering how much I love that game. This has that vibe.If the devs go nuts experimenting with game modes, weapons (!??), there is so much potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Updated: 6/22/2023I was about to re-play to see what did change / fix but after going through recent reviews and discussions / patch notes and what not. Don't bother... the game after 2 years is in the same spot it was during the beta testing. No content, Pit stops is a badly implemented gimmick, the AI... there's just Artificial because the Intelligent part was not implemented at all - Also read those reviews that praise the game a bunch with a grain of salt, the game had a lot movement before release in their Discord and much of those "10/10 best racing game ever" reviews are people trying to give the game attention to help the devs sell the game. Nothing against helping them, but they lie a lot on those reviews - For the price this one costs there's actually games that you can buy, just ignore this game. Original review in 2021 after the game launched (played the beta testing and the 1.0v)When i discovered Circuit Superstars (CSS for short), I couldn't believe, a top down racer with Motorsport elements, was exactly what i needed! Some fresh air in the racing genre. Finally, I could have some proper racing, with pit stops strategies, qualifying laps without having to spend hours configuring the wheel and setting up a Sim-Racing game. CSS could be my pick up and play.What do you get for your money here? Well, you get a skeleton of what can be a good if not a great racing game in the future.Gameplay options:-Free racing - create you own race/racing series, very customizable, number of races / laps / drivers etc, set up damage / fuel usage / Tire wear. It promises.-Multiplayer - its not good, no matchmaking, no way to join with friends, all you can do is vote for a fixed type of race and...race-Arcade - The closest thing to a "career mode"- you have 5 classes, 3 easy and 2 impossible (more on this later).-Time trials - Time trials with leader-boards, not much to say here.Content:-6 cars -Every car feels different from another, and in general they're all fun to drive. Some cars on the trailers and advertising aren't in the game, go figure;-6 tracks - The tracks are well done, really pretty, regardless, in my opinion they're to short and too narrow, making all look the same after some time, which get boring fast.Physics:Pretty good in my opinion, the cars have mass, and a feel of weight to them which is really nice, unfortunately I would like the brakes to have a more important role...so far is just release the gas and turn. Also tires at 0% needs more of a impact, no need to pit for tires if you have fuel left.and Gameplay:When everything goes to plan the racing in this game is amazing, the overtakes, the pit stops, the immersion, unfortunately those moments are rareThe AI is bad, really really bad - either they don't give a proper challenge to its virtually impossible to win. Racing against the AI is either boring cause you're 20 secs ahead or frustrating cause no matter what you do you'll lose and even get lapped. The AI also drive in a perfect line, like on rails (even with low tire %), have no regards to self-preservation, they will crash into you at full speed if you're in the way.The pit stops need some work, the idea and implementation is amazing, but for now its more of a gimmick than a feature, you cant setup your pits...which makes pit strategies barely a thing. Either you pit in the perfect moment or good bye you lost the race - The crew animation and crew members are adorable, they nailed this I'm not gonna lie, every time i saw the little guys around the car i got a smile on my face.You can't overtake cleanly - well you can if the driver in from of you makes a mistake - lack of slipstream, narrow roads, short circuits and the lack of any pit strategy (you basically have to pit in the same time as the leader or driver in 2º) makes it almost impossible for overtaking without resorting to bumps - the fate of the race usually is dictated in the qualifying lap, the guy in first will be in first the whole race.And there's bugs and a lack of things that a game in 2021 can't be without, nevertheless, i have faith that this team will deliver! all of them are great individuals and are passionate about this project, the game needs more time to develop that's all. (and regional pricing )
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I absolutely love this game. It's fun, the skidding is class, there is a fair selection of cars and custom looks BUT.... the difficulty level is pitched way too high. The difference between amateur and Pro am is 1st place to 12th and I am not a novice. This really spoils an otherwise very polished fun game. Pretty please make it more fairly competitive. I'm on the verge of not playing it anymore and that would be a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: It's really good for what it is! I hope people understand it's more like the old game "Generally" and not a top down racing "sim". Not art of rally etc, it's not trying to be that. There are things basically directly from Generally in this game, and that has been the goal of the devs most likely. It's important that it's understood it's meant for rather casual fun. Seeing a few too many people expecting otherwise.It's probably not quite worth the full price for the average consumer at the moment, so perhaps wait for more content if you're not sure. But what it's trying to do is really good and really well made. It's ea so much work yet to be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Inevitably will draw comparisons to Art of Rally, and rightfully so, in a positive way. It's a top down, arcade, and almost cartoony styled racer. However, it's got a nuanced handling model, and is clearly made with a lot of love for motorsports.The only caveats are related to its early access nature. There isn't a huge amount of content - an acceptable list of cars and tracks, but very limited campaign mode that throws elite level AI at you within an hour. As long as it keeps getting built out, it should end up being an excellent arcade racer, it has all the potential to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes me back to the days of my youth playing Off Road in the arcades with my buds. This game absolutely captures that awesome arcade feel but at the same time has some great Racing Sim qualities, like tire wear. Each car has unique handling. The game runs smooth and just looks beautiful. It has online, currently still in beta. It works but it's not consistent enough and I cannot wait for it to get more. If you like top down arcade racers, or are a racing sim player that wants a little more of a relaxing, yet challenging, racing game, then check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: The game I've been waiting for a long time. As a fan of all the classic top down games mentioned in other reviews and more modern ones like Mini Motor Racing and the Reckless Racing series, this has to be the best one yet. 10/10 pit stop crew and animations. iRacing should be ashamed. The art style and handling are superb. My only request is a Nissan GTR shaped car for the GT class, please. And Fanatec wheel support. I'm just kidding. Or am I?
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes me back to a time when I was younger.The game plays great and has a really good system for damage, fuel and tyre use throughout a race, which works so well and topped off with a really cool pitlane system.Get the game while it is £12.99, worth more, but why wait for more content when the game is so much fun
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: fun game, but get bored so fast, if add manual shift it will be more fun to play with. more custom parts on the cars like body kit or spoiler, only just for looks no effect to the performance. weather change would be nice !!!! like sunny -> rain or rain -> sunny and player need to pit stop to change rain/sticky ties.more cars to each category !!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: 4/2 update - I sadly have to give in and admit... This game sucks. The broken AI and difficulty makes it impossible to play and its simply not fun. How is this not fixed yet? Is everyone having fun racing in last place with no chance at catching up like a normal race when people have to pit (which this AI doesn't need) or something? Just look at the discussion boards. Everyone wants to love this game but clearly have the same shaky feeling that it might actually suck and are struggling to admit it.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I want to love this beautiful game in a neglected genre. It's early access, so there's still time. The game is still well worth the price. Noticeable issues to consider:- AI doesn't take a time penalty when it goes to a pit stop (but you will go from first place to last and stay there)- Seems like the AI lap times are already pre-determined because I lapped the entire group on amateur, but the standings showed the next racer as 1 second behind me- AI doesn't appear to have any vehicle degradation like you do- AI has no flaws on any difficulty - they never crash, oversteer, swipe the barriers, spin out, etc- AI drives on rails while you drive on ice- You can only be a female driver - why?- You can't tune or set up your car and because of that, you can't upgrade parts (because there aren't any)- Missed opportunity to include sports management elements via a franchise & season (car, crew, media)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Each car feels unique in its driving and handling, so you really have to learn both the vehicle and the track if you want to get a decent time.  I find racing offline against bots is a great way to practice, so your ready for online competitions.   I really enjoy the customization of the driver and car liveries, and the fact that the game can be run on a laptop, which is getting exceedingly rare these days.  I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys an accurate racing game that they can pick up any time.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: At its current state it has a solid foundation for an EA game.  The controls are tight and responsive, which really makes nailing a lap feel great.  The variety of car types and maps seems surprising good at the moment.The main downside for me is the online play.  Currently there is only matchmaking games, with no private servers.  Hopefully this improves as time goes on, but I still enjoy learning the handling of different car types and maps in free play/arcade mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a mini/arcade racing simulator, with real pit stop mechanics. The vehicle feels vary from heavier  Supertruck, muscle cars, and Eurotruck to the light snappy and speedy Indy car, Porsche gt, Ford rally car, superlights, and the oh so cute "Paccino" ( Fiat 500 ). These are all looks alikes none officially licensed of course. As they are an indy company I don't expect that. The game looks and plays like a modern Micro machines turned racing sim. The art style is beautiful and vibrant. The single players is great, though the difficulty progression gets steep near the end. The pvp/online racing is the best part of the package. 12 person races with a variety of vehicle/track options to vote on each round. Hope to see you on the track!.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Really good concept and game so far! I adore the style and the mix between top down racer and management of your tires, fuel and hull-status. Controls are on point, easy to learn but hard to master! Different vehicles have all an unique and believable handling. Perfect game to play with your family and friends in local mp as well. Had only minor issues with multiplayer I am looking forward to be fixed soon. Please bring the updates in :) Nice work so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up on a whim based on it's art style and the fact that it seems to be backed by a decent publisher who I hope keeps pushing the development for this game in the right direction. The game is quite fun and feels mostly bug free despite it being early access. What you get for the price is decent and I could especially see myself enjoying this with friends. I can't speak to the local multiplayer quality, but the online was fine for my purposes. The gameplay seems to be shooting for something less arcadey than the top down racers of old, but not so much so that it's a pain in the ass to play. I found myself picking it up pretty quickly and making good times around the track. If you are a sim racer or familiar with standard racing theory, this will be a pretty easy game to pick up, but satisfying to master. Once I got the hang of it, I really started to enjoy the rhythm and zen of the experience. I especially like the addition of pitting in the game and it seems to have been implemented in a fun, yet fair way. My only really glaring complaint is the track limitation tracking. I hopped on the time trials to try and beat the record scores only to see the ghost car flying through the turns well inside the boundaries. I also noticed a few odd clipping issues on some of the qualifying laps where my car couldn't decide whether it was a ghost or solid and I was clipped by a few of the AI whilst trying to set a time. It's also a little squirrely when starting the qualifier as you can sometimes be released by the AI right into a wall on a turn it took too quickly, but these are minor issues and generally the game ran well. All told, I am very excited to see where this game goes and would recommend it if you're looking for a fun zen time waster. To the developers: good stuff so far! I would love to see some additional tracks and maybe even some oddball types of racing (oval, rally, ice track, etc.). I figure the engine might limit you on some of those types, but it would be fun to be a one stop shop for a fun little arcade racer to hop on and complete some laps in between chores and other day to day minutiae.Update: This game became everything I was hoping for. The racing is so much fun and so satisfying and there's just enough complexity to make the races fun whilst having so much diversity in racing styles (caravan Eurotruck is hysterical). There is a little bit of lag and stuttering occasionally when playing with my friends across the pond, particularly during collisions, that can really mess you up when you're racing a very precise track, but it seems to do well otherwise. Overall, A+ effort. This is a must if you have some friends to play with.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome racing game, great style and variety in the cars, challenging game-play that rewards practice but equally fun to pick up and play a short burst.Charming visuals and music mean it's one you can pull out for a couch party and no one will groan about racing, brings to mind the old Micro Machines games but without the nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game already in Early Access, so much potential here to make it an all-time great.The look and feel is truly motorsport, with cars bouncing over curbs, smoking when damaged, and the track even rubbers in after a few laps!There is also tyre wear and fuel consumption so pitstops need to be made in longer races - or not, if you can handle worse handling. This little strategy element makes the racing even more awesome.Great game and will be greater in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: it'd be cool to race on cartoony versions of real tracks (the top gear track knock off could be called "high gear"). and more cars. maybe remakes of popular tracks in other games. maybe a stunt track thing too. cars jump in this game so maybe do some rally stuff? not to step on "the art of rally" turf but could totally do some rally cross stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant top-down racer. This is the most fun I've had with this type of racing game since probably Super Cars I and II. The physics, handling and feel of the cars is basically perfect. It's weighty, drifty and arcadey in all the right ways. Challenging, but you feel like you're in control, so you're aware that there's nobody else to blame for mistakes than yourself.There's still room for improvement though. My wishlist includes more variety in track designs, environment, cars, weather and single player game modes. My biggest gripe with the game though is that it sometimes feels like you're waiting around too much. Loading times seem sluggish, and you sometimes have to wait unnecessarily long after a race or qualifying session is over, before you get to move on to more action.But have no doubt that this game is highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: As an Early Access game this is very nicely done!! I personally haven't had any game breaking bugs or bugs of any kind really aside from one crash which is not unheard of in any new game.Tire and fuel management are pretty well done and the gameplay is just... fun. The AI drivers aren't bad either however they could do with some tweaking here and there. For example they always swerve horribly at the start giving you an instant lead or opportunity to pass several drivers. Having said that, they are still a decent challenge.By far the most fun i've had on a racing game in years (including AAA titles released in the last few years for a significantly higher price). Definitely looking forward to the future of the game...All it needs for now is a better multiplayer...
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I'm only around one and a half hours into this, but that's enough time to tell me that this is something special.The controls are perfectly balanced, meaning the challenge is in the game and not struggling with a poorly implemented game pad calibration. This leads to some thoroughly satisfying and tense game play where if you screw up you know it's your fault.It's early access at moment meaning content is a bit limited, but for the price and the challenge it offers it's still well worth the money, and with the content set to grow it'll offer even more value for money in the future.Highly highly recommended - this is pure fun, and I wouldn't be surprised if this game ends up dominating the Steam charts
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Feels very "WiiSports"ish...  The graphics, the music...  Everything.  Even the big-"wii"headed spectators and everything.  Pretty fun, will keep my eye on it as it progresses.  I think it has the possibility of being great.  REALLY hate having to sit and wait for alot of the screens...  Once I'm done with the race, would like to move on pretty quickly, not sit and watch my car race itself for a lap.  Otherwise, good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate to be involved in some early online play tests and this early access release is just the beginning of something huge - this game is the perfect fun racer whether online with real players or offline against a very good A.I.The graphics and physics are absolutely superb, even with the 6 tracks the possibilities are endless with the different cars and handling, number of laps, fuel, damage and tyre wear affecting pit stop strategy.This game deserves every bit of success - I hope this is HUGE on consoles too.The ONLY thing myself and all my friends are waiting for during early access is a party/lobby system so we can all race and have fun on our own discord/clan groups together, I'm sure this will be coming soon, we need to all have a laugh online with our friends and race each other :)
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Just bought it and absolutely love it, the car sounds could be updated too be a bit more realistic to actual car but rest of bumps and crashes and tyres sounds great! Epic little game which i hope you guys keep updating and bring more cars into the game this will be a awesome racer! Perhaps even get a track creator at some point or bring some legendary tracks to the game and this game will get bigger! Keep up the great work im keen to be part of this and will stream this game on my twitch channel for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Rally fun, feels great! Probably the best racing game of it's type I've played in a very long time. Excited for it to get expanded upon!----Played a bit more after this review and really can't explain how white knuckle it can be. There are some other poor reviews that touch on things that are definitely things to be worked on, but the core of the game is here and very good. I hope lots of people buy it and support the studio so they can continue to expand on whats here!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This is the racing game I have been waiting for! No rockets, huge crashes or crazy stuff going on - only pure driving skill. I love it! The feeling is perfect, the graphics are cartoony, but still detailed. The circuits are really great and fun to drive.Circuit Superstars even have pit stop strategies. You need to change tires, fix the car and do some refueling.Buy this game! Now!
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: Great game when it works. Unfortunately the devs take too long to fix a simple issue that crept in at a previous hotfix.Not saving lap times and ghost data not working correctly which is a huge loss because the little content that the game currently has doesn't take long to get tired.Managed to fix it for myself by deleting the steam download cache after a couple of hours trying all sorts of things.I do recommend the game but it may be better to come back when there's more content and some of the simple issues are ironed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

_childDocuments_.review: FEEL the rubber bite into the road as you pass the start/finish line and dive, brakes squealing, into the first corner! Circuit Superstars is a top-down racer built by racing fans, for racing fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Circuit Superstars

Competitive & Cooperative: Tumble between competitive free-for-alls and cooperative challenges—or take on the Blunderdome with up to 3 friends! Play with Friends: Fall Guys supports cross-play, cross-platform parties and cross-progression via your Epic Games Account. Ever-Evolving Content: Play stays fresh with new collabs and game updates which bring new Costumes, Obstacles, and ways to play. Gloriously Customizable: Choose from a multitude of Colors, Patterns, Costumes and Nameplates. Relish wins with extravagant Celebrations and share your flair with Emotes! Items shown may require separate purchase from the in-game store and are subject to availability. Contains in-game purchases.
about_the_game: You’re invited to dive and dodge your way to victory in the pantheon of clumsy. Rookie or pro? Solo or partied up? Fall Guys delivers ever-evolving, high-concentrated hilarity and fun. Prefer to be the maverick behind the mayhem? Build your very own obstacle course to share with friends or the wider community. Create your own Course: Fall Guys Creative is a level editor that allows you to create fiendish custom Rounds and share them with the wider community. Competitive & Cooperative: Tumble between competitive free-for-alls and cooperative challenges—or take on the Blunderdome with up to 3 friends! Play with Friends: Fall Guys supports cross-play, cross-platform parties and cross-progression via your Epic Games Account. Ever-Evolving Content: Play stays fresh with new collabs and game updates which bring new Costumes, Obstacles, and ways to play. Gloriously Customizable: Choose from a multitude of Colors, Patterns, Costumes and Nameplates. Relish wins with extravagant Celebrations and share your flair with Emotes! Items shown may require separate purchase from the in-game store and are subject to availability. Contains in-game purchases.
short_description: Fall Guys is a free, cross-platform massively multiplayer party royale game. Clumsily compete in absurd obstacle courses with friends or build your very own chaotic course to share with the community.

Surprised me enough that people being more competitive than I expected. Overall I an having fun with these running grabby beans. : PG-3 ish overall, totally family friendly and has a nice render for Unity based game. With colorful graphic to catch your attention and make it more playful. Also Sick level grade of sound tracks. Clearly artists know about their jobs. : Good and easy to learn game-play. Even your girlfriend, mom or little sibling  who have no idea about gaming world, could easily get into. With very simple controls and map design. You can just watch people doing and have an idea about what is happening in the round without knowing English. Some maps really favor the luck and some being favor the skills, which is good combination for any players with different skills and experiences. : You can dress up your Fall Guy aka the bean. Cannot say it's a polished game but rather need more polishing. -Some cosmetic model being clipped, not fully rendered or incorrectly rendered with team game-Fix the OCE server problem, I thought I am S.E.A. server but no, Everyone is playing from North America server after I checked ping and found the truth. _childDocuments_.review: It's a very fun and addictive game.  But be prepared to lose... A LOT.  Sometimes losing can be incredibly frustrating due to the occasional team game with people who aren't as good or cooperative or games that require a little bit of RNG or physics luck.  Overall worth at least the $20.DLC is all cosmetic but I do feel a bit weird about their being an in-game currency shop (which you earn plenty of just by playing).  Again, it is all cosmetic items, so I can't complain too much if that's your thing.  UPDATE: Updating the review to say that the servers have been very stable since a week or two after launch.I'd say half the mini-games are actually enjoyable while the others are stressful and painful slogs, though they are better playing with friends.  It is also worth noting that friends in your lobby will always be on the same team as you in case of a team mini game.

_childDocuments_.review: + Great fun, great soundtrack, and even more fun with friends. Though I play it solo and still find myself screaming like a maniac.+ Controls are simple, and not as sluggish as the likes of Gang Beasts (which I love but.. can be a bit too sluggish for some). + Soundtrack, did I mention the soundtrack? - Naming scheme, I realise that this was taken out early on due to a HTML error where people were making their names MASSIVE with a bit of code.. but c'mon. I want to see my mates.- Deadcam: watching my friends is a bloody task, switch.. nope not them, switch, nope, switch, nope, switch. It's tedious as heck, I'd like to just auto to a team mate, or at least have some filtering where I can view anybody or just my team mates.- Loading times: I'm on a 9900K with a 1080ti, the loading times for games getting set up are near enough half of the gameplay experience. I appreciate from a simple user perspective, I'm not fully appreciating "why" it takes so long to load, but it is a long time. - Quit button on main menu: put a quit button on the main menu, this is an easy fix and all you gotta do is have a "are you sure?" just incase people hit it by mistake some how. Not a big fan of having to navigate to another menu, then to the last button on that screen, just to quit. I alt+f4 most times, that shouldn't have to be my best option.- Getting pulled into another game after falling: I understand now there's a moment of time to get out before I have to sit through another loading screen into a game I'm no longer in. As I mention, the loading times are fairly chunky.. so having to wait to load into a game I won't even be in, just to quit and start a new queue? No a fan, would like a way to get out easier and not suffer through a long loading screen. Appreciate I'm not seeing the "why" to why  this isn't in, but feels like this and a few other simple QoL features would be a great addition in an update.- Grouping with friends: not sure how many others have issues, but myself and 3 other mates who live within walking distance of me, had serious issues getting together in a simple Steam group to play together. Granted this was a couple of weeks ago, but it annoyed them to the point they just couldn't be arsed trying any more. This stuff should be simple to achieve, and not frustrating. We're not here to jump through hurdles to play together, quite the opposite. Would like this to be as straight-forward as possible.All in all I would recommend this game, assuming the above things get fixed. It feels like where some of it is polished, certain things under the bonnet have been rushed. Eager to see more updates as they seem to be quite responsive, but the fact this stuff is still not sorted is a bit disheartening.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this it is 9/10/2020 and I have 5.5 hours on record over the last two daysLet me start by saying that I actually love this game. The bean/potato styled characters combined with the goofy ragdoll physics help make this game fun. The mini-games are all pretty fun and I honestly don't really have anything bad to say about any of them. The soundtrack and color palette fits the game perfectly and for such a simple game it's graphics are still pretty good. The characters handle really well, and you can tell a lot of love was put into the game just by playing a few rounds.Despite all of that, and how much fun I have playing the game alone and with friends I can't reasonably recommend the game as it stands. The core reason behind this is the overwhelming number of cheaters that are currently present in the game is kind of insane. You can play for 3~4 hours like I did yesterday when I bought the game and only get 3 games where there are no cheaters. Tonight's 1-2 hours session averaged the same results, in that time I got 1 game where a player wasn't blatantly cheating. This is about a 1-2 fair game average per hour. When I say players are blatantly cheating I mean they're flying over obstacles from the start of the round, jumping so high they can jump over walls and obstacles, moving so fast that they are completing obstacle courses before the other players in the lobby can even get half way through, teleporting to the crown and winning instantly on crown mountain (the final mini-game to decide the winner), floating above platforms that would otherwise fall or require you to jump something to avoid being eliminated, to as bad as people being able to win in the first round mini-game before any of the 60 player lobby can play and qualify or be eliminated. To cap off the review I gotta be honest in that I will continue to play the game. It's just fun, there is no two ways about it. I can not however recommend the game for the above reasons. If you are willing to ignore all of that and just try to have fun with the game, feel free to pick it up. Until the cheaters are reduced you just can't expect to actually have a fair game.Edit: I would like to officially edit this review to say they have done very well at cleaning up cheaters. Definitely worth full price now.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Rating: ★★★★☆Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout, developed by Mediatonic, is a delightful and whimsical battle royale party game that brings together elements of platforming, obstacle courses, and competitive multiplayer. With its colorful visuals, charming characters, and chaotic gameplay, Fall Guys offers a refreshing and entertaining experience for players of all ages.Graphics: ★★★★☆Fall Guys features vibrant and colorful graphics that are both visually appealing and charming. The game's whimsical art style, cute character designs, and lively animations create a cheerful and inviting atmosphere. The environments, filled with imaginative obstacles and unique challenges, are well-designed and add to the overall fun and playful aesthetic.Gameplay: ★★★★☆The gameplay of Fall Guys revolves around competing in a series of wacky and unpredictable challenges with a large group of players. From racing through obstacle-filled courses to team-based mini-games, each round presents a new and exciting challenge. The controls are simple and intuitive, making it accessible to both casual and experienced gamers. The chaotic nature of the gameplay, combined with the unpredictability of other players' actions, creates a thrilling and often hilarious experience.Sound: ★★★★☆Fall Guys features a lively and upbeat soundtrack that matches the game's energetic and lighthearted tone. The background music enhances the fun and frantic atmosphere, while the sound effects add to the overall immersion. From the joyful cheers of the characters to the comical sounds of bouncing and falling, the audio elements contribute to the game's charm and entertainment value.Multiplayer Experience: ★★★★☆Fall Guys shines in its multiplayer experience, allowing players to compete against others from around the world in both competitive and cooperative challenges. The game supports both local and online multiplayer, fostering a sense of camaraderie and competition among friends. The inclusion of party modes and the ability to form teams adds another layer of enjoyment, making it an excellent choice for social gatherings or online play with friends.Replayability: ★★★★☆Fall Guys offers high replayability, thanks to its ever-changing selection of courses and challenges. Each match presents a different combination of rounds, ensuring that no two games are the same. The addictive nature of trying to secure a victory and the desire to unlock new cosmetic items and outfits provide further incentive for repeated play.Conclusion:Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout is a whimsical and entertaining battle royale party game that is sure to put a smile on your face. With its charming visuals, chaotic gameplay, and multiplayer fun, it offers an enjoyable and lighthearted gaming experience. Whether you're competing for the crown or laughing with friends, Fall Guys is a delightful addition to any gaming library.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game to play, especially with a few other friends. There is definitely some buggy-ness with the servers, but that is just due to an unexpected number of players during the first day or so, and it never prevented me from playing the game and it didn't ruin my experience.I do wish that they would extend the pre-made lobby count from 4 to say 6 or 7, especially since the game has a 60-player-per-lobby requirement anyways. I would be surprised if this caused people to abuse it and team up, since only one person can get the big reward at the end anyways.I think for the game to have serious longevity either the developers need to be very dedicated to releasing new content on the regular, or (better in my opinion) release map and gamemode creation tools to the community so that it can be done for them at a higher pace. I also think that community-run servers should be in the game's future, because they would be a good way of judging the quality of maps and gamemodes, ultimately leading to their inclusion in the base game on official servers.Either way, I think the game is seriously fun. I do think though that the developers need to have a solid plan for the future of this game if they want to continue riding the wave that they've built up so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys is a bit of the tv show Wipeout, Takeshi's Castle, and Mario Party wrapped up into a colorful package.  You control a little dude who competes against 59 other contestants in various skill & luck based levels.  It definitely meets the multiplayer party game criteria.   Levels often go pretty quick, typically within 1-3 minutes.  Some might last a little bit longer, but I haven't really kept track of that.  There's a decent amount of variation with the levels.  It's very possible for you to love a level, and someone else to absolutely despise it.  Most levels are about skill, making it from one part of the level to another while avoiding obstacles and other players.  Some levels are about teamwork, and each time one pops up in a round I can't wait for it to be over.  In a game that's mostly about you vs everyone else, it seems misplaced to have a team based level in the middle of your race to the top.  It doesn't help that the team based games aren't exactly the best.  Jump through rings, push a ball, push multiple balls, or collect eggs(the worst).  Maybe you get lucky and you have players that know the ins and outs of what needs to be done and you win.  Or maybe you've got a bunch of new players that aren't familiar with the best ways to win.  It often doesn't matter how well you do if your team isn't very good on average.  You're most likely going to watch that round end with a drastic message of "Unqualified."Now aside from my displeasure with the team based levels, the rest are pretty fun.  You've got to make it across see-saws, through fake doors, over rising/falling doors, avoid falling fruit, make your way up while avoiding rising slime, and a handful of other levels.  They're difficult enough to keep a veteran player on their toes, and accessible enough for a player that's less experienced.  Here's hoping there are more levels like this throughout the game's life.Each game nets you some kudos(cash), and some experience.  As you increase in level you unlock new rewards, which are cosmetics, crowns, or kudos.  Each day you have the option of buying new skins or costumes from the in-game store, and there have been many costumes thus far.  Kudos gain feels decent enough if you're doing well.  If you're rarely making it past the first round it may seem like you're never going to earn enough to buy anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, poor execution. Despite all its charm, for me Fall Guys ends up being frustrating, boring, and only occasionally exciting. I can only consider about half of the games to be positive experiences, which is unacceptable given they should be the main focus. Tail games, for example, only become genuinely important in the last 20 seconds of the game. Inherently, the inclusion of team mini-games makes many of your losses completely out of your control. Games like Door Dash and Tip Toe typically punish exciting, risk-taking behavior, and only guarantee a win by playing passive and safe. On the other hand, games like Slime Climb are a shining example of what every mini-game should strive to be. It's intense given the ever-rising lethal pink slime, can be initially overwhelming when grouped in a pack (but rarely ever to the point of demise), and finally strikes a perfect balance between casual obstacles and joyfully intense, down-to-the-wire platforming. On a side note, the game lacks certain little things that should be expected in any title to release in 2020. Not being able to change settings mid game, your "ready up" initiation automatically cancelling when looking at the shop or changing your outfit, and a rollback net-code that is often deceiving in games like tail tag are all factors that lead the game to feel like its missing a blatant level of polish. Even if these issues were fixed, however, the fundamental flaw of the game lies in its mini-game design. I'm not just bad, either. I've only played a few days and already have 5 wins. This game just has a lot to go until I can consider it a worthwhile experience. 5.75/10

_childDocuments_.review: It does genuinely make me sad to give it this review, since this game has the potential to be a charming, little experience. It's fun, lighthearted, and colorful. And, it has the potential to be like all the fun bits of Mario Party without the extensively long play sessions and with RNG that doesn't feel nearly as unfair. Which is nice. Sadly...it has a few issues to get over before it can ever fill that slot. First of all, it needs way more game modes. It has a fair number of activities on its own. But, of the activities that I've played, about half of them made me groan in frustration every time they came up. Which wouldn't be that big of an issue except with the small pool of stuff to do, that means you'll be seeing them a LOT if you plan on playing this for any period of time. Second of all, it has a pretty significant cheater problem. Most matches I had in my hour and a half of gameplay, there was someone being dragged around with a mouse cursor all over the place on a plane above where everyone is waddling, walking on air after not making it across obstacles, or what have you. Now, their site claims that those people are having action taken against them, but it doesn't make for a great first impression.Third of all, the player population seems to be really low. Now, admittedly, I do play at off hours due to my work schedule, so that will be a factor, but I was constantly timing out of matchmaking because it couldn't find enough people to form a match with. This game came out about a month ago. This should be a great cause for alarm for a game made to be a multiplayer only experience.And finally, the biggest bug bear. It's a game that charges a fee to get in the door, but everything about it is designed around a free-to-play micropayments economy. All complete with its own special currency to make you not feel like you've spent actual money. Someone might try to argue that usual argument of "it's just cosmetics", but the cosmetics, especially in a multiplayer experience, do matter rather significantly. Plus, this game doesn't really have much else outside of that. And, if they didn't, the game wouldn't have put them in there to sell in the first place. Sure, you can earn stuff through gameplay, but progress is specifically designed to be glacial to bore you into forking over the cash. And, it's not as if the game even displays a big list of stuff that's available to buy. It shows you a handful of things at a time, all with an ominous countdown timer to try to convince you into "buying before its gone". Lads, if you wanted to make a F2P game, then just have it be a F2P game. Or, if you wanted to make a game you charge for up front, don't put a F2P micropayments-based economy into it.

_childDocuments_.review: We’re in the gaming age that communities are looking for the next best Battle Royale game to watch and play with randoms and friends to find out who is the leader of the pack. The developers over at Mediatonic brought us this next best thing with their release of Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout. Fall Guys is a Third-Person Battle Royale game that starts you off in a lobby of 60 players that must race to the end of the course before the others to quality for the next round and not be eliminated from the game. Fall Guys has four stages in their qualifying courses that go from racing, survival, team base, and then the final round to get the crown!Gamers all around have started to try Fall Guys, making it the fourth top played game on Steam to date. So why is Fall Guys so popular? We’ll be checking out different categories of the game, such as the developers’ responses to the massive spike the game has reached, to what is to come for the future of the game to keep it in the top Most Played Games charts.At the end of the day, how many times will you attempt and get the crown in Fall guys? For most, it’s at the end of the Battlepass once you unlock all the tiers. You get to the point that you’ve unlocked all the tiers in the battlepass, and now if you keep going, you won’t gain anything from it. It comes down to the same category as Call of Duty: Modern Warfares Warzone Battlepass system. It’s the same type of tier made system that the developers over at Infinity Ward hope and make the battlepass in a way where it’ll take even an everyday player the whole season to unlock everything, to a point. If you win every match, or most matches, you’re going to finish your battlepass pretty quickly.At this time, Season 1 is still going on, and most everyday players in the community have unlocked most of the battlepass tiers. But with Season 2 on the horizon bringing a whole new look for the game, being most likely medieval theme looking at the latest trailer released a few days ago, this should bring a new face and meaning to play the game for longer knowing what’s to come with each battlepass.So, is Mediatonic game Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout worth USD 20 without a sale? I’d say yes, with the amount of content you get and the fun crying laughing moments you’ll have with others each match, is priceless in my book. We’ll continue following the path that Mediatonic takes with Fall Guys, and we hope to see it in the Esports game one day!You can read by full review here:

_childDocuments_.review: I felt kind of deflated playing Fall Guys. It's entirely possible I expected something completely different than what I got, and I really should have done more research before diving in. But what I wanted out of Fall Guys was a cozy fun experience of mucking about with silly physics and minigames, and what I got was another typical battle royale game only you trip and fall every so often. I don't want to call Fall Guys "sterile", because it's got tons of personality. I love the little beans and how they scream when they fly or mercilessly grab anything around them. But it's definitely missing the "spirit of fun" that I was hoping it would have; it feels kind of like the kid who pretended Sports Day was an olympic event instead of a free day where you can get out of class and hang with your friends. There's seasons, there's currency and microtransactions, there's bonuses for winning a certain number of times in a given period, it's a battle royale. The problem arises when you make the game a silly fun romp where you can fall over and do all sorts of crazy physics based nonsense- it clashes. Suddenly you're getting frustrated over losing when it was only because your character accidentally clipped into the ground and tripped over his own feet, or a minigame where you have a 50% chance of losing because it's team based. It no longer becomes fun, it becomes a chore you feel like you can't accomplish.

_childDocuments_.review: Skill has it's weight but luck dictates what will happen in most matches, personally the bulk of the individual mini-games are good, even though some are quite uninspired and a chore after a while (looking at you memory game and block party, both eliminate very few people and aren't that fun at all). What is a real dealbreaker to me is forcing party games to get rid of the more experienced players, quoting the lead game designer FallGuysJoe on Reddit "As mentioned below, it gives lower skilled players a chance to progress as part of a team.", your skill matters little in those team games and they are designed simply to randomly eliminate people. I don't mind losing because I screwed up, made bad call and so on, but being thrown out because the devs think that being skilled and investing our time to get to learn the game is a bad thing shocks me. Notice that the team game is usually before the final match, that's not random, they really meant it to be that way, quoting dev Joe again "We want Fall Guys to be accessible for lots of players, and we like the way it gives people the chance to qualify who tend to go out in the 3rd/4th round.". There you go, they want you to lose on the team games.TL;DR: The game is luck based by design, skill matters in the solo games but the team games are there to punish you and deny you the chance of winning so others can, regardless of skill.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is made on Sept 12, 2020. The game concept and execution of the actual game play is gold. But, the lack of experience of the development team in making an online multiplayer clearly shows in the final product: 1. The developers decision to have the game reports your location to the server (instead of your button input and replying back your supposed position) makes it very easy for people to cheat and that breaks non-cheaters' gaming experience. 2. Queuing for a game takes several minutes and you can't do anything except watching your Fall Guy falls. They should have let the players go into a spawn lobby while waiting for other players, that way at least we can mess around rather than being bored. 3. After you loss a round, the default next step by the game is to spectate a random opponent. Nobody in the world would like to do this. They should have made returning to lobby the default and spectating opponents optional, unless you play with a friend, then the game should spectate that friend automatically. 4. Why don't they just use Steam ID as the character names instead of random Fall Guy #1234?! That should be the most basic thing to do in a multiplayer game. 5. Many other small but annoying things. This game has BIG potential but in desperate need of an overhaul.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:This game is worst than i thought. Ping is really important in this game. So important, that you have be really lucky to win anything.Examples:•Ping affects distance when you can grab a tail•Ping affects distance when other players can grab your tail•Ping affects ball games VERY much. If not - forget about it, first two hours maybe fun, but later you will get nothing but frustration. _childDocuments_.review: I was very surprised by this game. Unlike so many others, I didn't hear anything about this game until its release day. I saw a bunch of streamers going at it and thought this might be entertaining for my group as well and boy was I right! The game itself is a fast paced, mini-game filled explosion of fun. The graphics remind me a lot of Gang Beasts - very simple and colorful. The concept itself is straight forward: you begin with a group of 30~60 people who have to run through a series of events to see who is crowned the champion. The series range between 3 to 6 events, depending on the type of events and the number of people who end up qualifying at the end of each event. The events themselves seem to fall under these categories: race, team, tail, or survive.Race: Make it from the starting point to the end without either getting eliminated by pink slime or not qualifyingTeam: Work as a team to complete the objective. That might be: collect eggs, score points in soccer/rocket league knockoff, or push your ball down the course quickerTail: Arguably the most intense -- some people start with tails and some do not. Objective is to end with a tail (or if the team event, end with the most tails on your team)Survive: These are the quickest way to "thin the herd". Events like these are instant-elim if you fail. This might be walking on the hexagon tower or running on connecting rotating platformsI'm not sure how many maps there are in total, but I've played for a good few hours and haven't come across too many that I haven't seen at least a few times at this point. Overall though I feel like I already got my money's worth. I am enjoying the game solo or with a group and my viewers seem to be enjoying it as well. - King of the Stream - The KING in Streaming Entertainment

_childDocuments_.review: The game started out fun, but rapidly became grindy and repetitive, as some maps almost never showed up and others I would see every time, and they would almost always play out almost the exact same, with everyone forming disorderly queues leading to the end. One exclusion to this was the matching game, where the tiles would flash a fruit, and then go dark while a fruit would appear on the boards around the arena and a moment later the other fruit platforms would disappear and drop anyone standing on them. After playing it once or twice, you've seen all it had to offer, as it only goes up in complexity once or twice at most then ends. I ended up having five games in a row play host to this, and felt my brain go numb as unless I lost how to count to four or got shoved off by someone (which I almost never saw on this game) I couldn't lose and it was just several minutes of nothing. The equivalent experience to watching tv static while your friend tries to get the box plugged back in so you can watch the actual show.The team based games are not terribly great either, as the three team egg hunt always ended up being one team got targeted by both other teams, and would almost always lose. So roll a dice, and you might end up being disqualified. The "tail tag" games were also random, as the matches were so long and the arenas so compact the only thing that mattered were the last five seconds, where all of a sudden your team could plummet from top to bottom-I saw it happen to both my team and other teams several times, which made the previous minute and 15 seconds feel like a waste of time. The soccer minigame was probably the most balanced of them, and still felt frustrating and unsatisfying to play as the physics and collision was so floaty, I would see players on both sides frequently try to hit the ball by diving at it and watching as they just sailed through the ball instead, and it would collide with their back and roll backwards-or their fingertips caused the ball to rocket into the sky at a weird angle. Kind of funny, until I realized it meant it was a waste of effort on their part-and mine, the odd time it happened to me.The physics in general is very floaty and difficult to work with or predict, meaning several times I'd seen either myself or other players get caught on things they shouldn't get caught on, or get repeatedly knocked around by obstacles that should've already let go of them, forcing them to be eliminated because they spent half the match time being smacked against a wall while everyone else proceeded. Combine this with the fact that slightly bumping into someone meant that there was even odds one or both of you would stumble and fall, and that most games were just conga-lines of people following the exact same paths, meant often times you'd be helplessly stuck on the ground as you get trampled by everyone.The map selection is also very barebones, with only about a dozen or so currently in as of writing this. Oftentimes the same maps would come up again and again and again, while others I would see maybe once or twice. While I understand at some point in the past they added items to some of the maps that would randomly appear to change them up a bit, the few times I would see these additions they did little to change the fact that the maps were all still very samey and there's no room to try other routes or methods-as there is only the one or two paths to take, which all end up leading to the same spot anyways and are often the same path but slightly to the side of one another. While I know they are planning on adding more maps, the current map design is so simplistic and has no room for imagination, so I don't have any faith the newer maps will really shake up the game that much.For the small amount of time I played the game lost connection to the server several times, which meant I was right back to the main menu. The coins and xp I could have earned was lost entirely, wasting the past ten or so minutes. However, this isn't as painful an indictment as it sounds, as the only thing you can purchase with the coins (the "xp" only goes to a progress bar for the "season" and unlocks coins and cosmetics at a very slow rate that slows down very quickly) are cosmetics, most of the time just being colours and patterns that are overridden by most if not all cosmetic pieces. Even the premium currency gained very rarely from the progress bar or from winning games only unlocks other cosmetics/paintjobs, so there is little to actually gain.Overall, it's a very repetitive game with only the one game mode and a very limited pool of maps that almost all end up playing the same, and largely feel like winning or losing is based on luck. Good as a distraction, but honestly if you want to distract someone for a little while I'd say to pick something that'll actually engage them more.Maybe in a year after a few more content updates when there's more than a dozen maps to play, and more game modes available that don't feel entirely random or like you're turning your brain off entirely, I might consider recommending it. But in its current state as of the 3rd of October, I would not recommend it, even as cheap as it is-there's plenty of good indie games out there for about the same price if not cheaper that'd get you more entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys is Mario Party without the board game elements. All mini-games all the time. You play as little jellybean folks in a game show trying to be the one to outlast every other player (out of an initial 60 per game) through a series of obstacles courses, races, team games, and others for a total of 25 different possible maps. Only a certain number of people can qualify per map in order to narrow down the competitor pool. A lot of these maps are not skill based, just luck based. Some are the opposite. There's a lot of opportunity to grief and disrupt other players by grabbing on to them as well.In terms of player base, the ages range from small children to older adults. It's perfectly family friendly because there's no violence, no suggestive content whatsoever, up to four people can play together in a party (and possibly ruin their friendships), and the official discord server allows for partying up with strangers just to pal around and play for a while. Team games (such as Fall Ball and Team Tail Tag) are infinitely frustrating and by far the most hated stages, but this is a rather new game and maybe the devs will reconsider things like that as the season turns. My only complaint: Microstransactions. IF the game is buy-to-play, why have microtransactions on top of that? Especially since the game is marketed towards a younger audience. This seems a bit scummy and I dislike it in any game. You can earn the in-game currency by playing games, but it takes a LONG time to earn enough to purchase anything unless you're winning a LOT. Make the game free to play if you want to go that route or just make the cosmetics easier to obtain via in-game means. MY only real gripe with this.

You will spend half of your time 'playing' this game in loading screens, and this is not an exaggeration by any means.The developers have really dropped the ball in this key area -- when you're playing a game you shouldn't want to check your phone out of boredom due to waiting around time.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing. I haven't played it for that long, but because of the minimal amount of content you need to unlock and the fact that it's pretty simple, I'll review it anyway.:This game is relatively simple. You're an anthropomorphic jellybean in a suit called a "Fall Guy" hence the name of the game trying to win the championship and become famous. Keep in mind that like pretty much every single physics-based game, the physics are absolutely ridiculous. Nearly at the same level as Ragdoll. Maybe make the characters a bit faster and less comical to hit Ragdoll level. It's possible to get yeeted into oblivion by a giant fan 10 times your size. You can grab stuff(including other Fall Guys), a mechanic that a handful of game modes revolve around. Whenever you win a round, you are qualified for the next. If not, your run is cut short. I've never finished a match, but from what I've heard, doing so grants you a Crown, a special piece of currency(a la Clash of Clans gems)which you can accumulate multiple of to buy special stuff. You can also accumulate Crowns by hitting Milestones on your Fame Level(the game's experience system), though this seems alot more tedious and repetitive. About the matchmaking system, it appears as if it's ranked, because across all the matches I've played, I definitely wasn't the only dumbass. You basically end up with 49-59 other players in the lobby and have to conquer a number of different courses. Across these, you can fall off a ledge, get stumped at a wall, get stumped at a slide, not jump over the gap in time, push a ball into a goal, get into a fist-fight over some eggs, get crushed, roleplay as Icarus and get shamed by a TikTok user for being competitive. My personal best in rounds is 4. By that, I mean I beat 3 then failed the fourth one. By the way, the music doesn't really matter at all.It really doesn't matter at all.There is none.Pretty good, though it does feel plastic-y or empty at times. I think it would've been neat if they had one of those Ninja Warrior things where if you fall out of bounds, you fall into some water and get disqualified. Then maybe at the round summary, the disqualified peeps would fall into a jar and get eaten after the match with the winner watching. Bit horrific for a party game, but I'm sure they can find some way. Anyways, summary!Fall Guys is simultaneously absolutely ridiculous, insanely competitive and illegally adorable for a Party Game. And that's what makes it unique. I doubt it would've ever been so successful if it weren't for its emphasis on hilarious physics and momentum-based movement. In fact, it's so successful that the developers put up a notice because of it and it could potentially become a 10-year game! Anyways, time for the final score.Gameplay: 9/10(fits the formula well, though it does feel a bit out-of-control at times especially if your cat just stole your controller and your control key)Soundtrack: Nothing SpecialLore Complexity: An opening sequenceGraphics: 7/10(looks plastic-y at times, needs a bit more detail but overall pretty neat)Verdict: 8/10=Great(the above suggestions explain it all)I hope this review helped. Goodbye!

_childDocuments_.review: Recently, many games have had a focus on trying to make themselves the whole package. Amazing soundtrack, graphics, writing, etc... many focus and succeed in those aspects but forget the core part of the game which is to be enjoyable.Fall Guys isn't trying to have the have the best graphics, doesn't even have a story, and it's OST isn't anything insane. It's incredibly fun though, and I think that's really what counts.Notes: Currently (8/8/20) the game has many connection errors and server downages, but I think these'll get fixed in due time and are just due to an overload of players. Doesn't deter from the experience itself and I'm sure it'll be fixed soon. There are not that many minigames, but they're mostly fun and the developers have said they'll add more later on (still in Season 1).Overall, pretty fun game pick it up, it's a great change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Nope. Too many hackers and their laughable support page I had to get to to attempt to report someone. In my less than 3 hours, I encountered 3 hackers and there is no in-game or out of the game way to report people as far as I'm aware. Their response is something along the lines of : Our system will have caught them so no need to report them! Yeah, like a) has that ever stopped someone in the history of video games and b) highly doubt it, bigger higher stakes games with millions more invested into anti-cheat can't pick up this stuff, no way a first-time indie dev is picking this up. The fact that to even see that response you have to jump through the hoop of going into the menu, clicking support, a separate page coming up, then you have to find the section on cheaters just for them to be like "lol, we gotem" nope nope nope. The game itself is fun, but such a tone-deaf response to such a huge issue. Also, cramming tons of microtransactions into a $20 game, like wtf. Also, the fact you can't even have your own name is mind-boggling in a game that seems to emphasize customizability and creativity, just to be named Fall Guy #169409234502243598 is mind-boggling. I have done some research and can't find a clear reason as to why this is the case, but according to some sources it's to "protect streamers". If that's the case that's absolutely absurd. Why appeal to the .001% instead of the thousands who have bought your game? Conclusion: The game is pretty fun, but the unbelievably tone-deaf company brings it down4/10 in its current state

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually pretty fun. It is quick to get into the action, and there are plenty of rewards to earn without spending extra cash, though I did buy the currently available DLC.The stages can be repetitive but the multiplayer nature makes it a new experience every time. If you are the type of person who gets upset by losing, especially by random circumstance through no fault of your own, this game may not be for you. Otherwise it's a fun and simple party game for which you do not need a party!However, the reason I cannot recommend the game is because of the rampant cheating. While you do earn XP towards seasonal rewards even for a loss, only 1 player may win each match, earning a coveted "crown." Crowns are required for the best and most unique "legendary" cosmetic items.When there is even one cheater in your match (which is a very, VERY frequent occurrence) it will not be possible for you to win. In fact the best thing you can do is quit or try to sabotage the cheaters if they end up on your team during one of the team-based challenges.The developer has already spoken about the cheating, but there does not seem to be much improvement after the first month! They say they are currently waiting to implement a robust anti-cheat solution such as that used in Fortnite, but so far it has been a lot of talk and no action.Well, seeing is believing, and I recommend you do not buy this product until it has become obvious that the cheating is addressed. The developers seem way in over their heads at this point and I would be wary of their ability to support this game going forward.I am also very worried about the type of narcissistic sociopath it takes to cheat in a game like Fall Guys. I imagine they would steal from you in real life, too, if they could get away with it.
