_childDocuments_.review: In this review, I'll first give my honest opinion about the game, how my first experience were and then I'll talk about the thing everyone is talking about.So, the game. One big question: Did I enjoy it so far?Yes. Simple as that.It's basically a collection of fun and quick mini games packed into an enjoyable competitive format.When I first saw this game I had one thought in my head "Is this....is this Takeshi's Castle?".Now after playing I can say, yes it is, and damn it's a ton of fun.If I have to pick a negative thought about the gameplay, it would be that it's just too addictive.Restarting after being eliminated is just a few quick button presses away and you're back in, ready to go, trying to grab yourself that win!The rounds are over super fast, you don't even notice how much time is passing, being eliminated is not frustrating because it feels like you've just lost one small mini game and that's it. It doesn't take half an hour to get back to where you were, just a couple of minutes later you'll be fighting for the win again.Thanks to the quick mechanic it never felt like I've wasted my time when I failed, and that happened often enough.In the short window I had to play the game I even managed to get myself to one victory, ended a few race games in first place, had fun interactions at the finish line with random people, played with friends, made new enemies, had a lot of fun and not for once second was I frustrated for not winning a game.But speaking of short window I had to play, lets talk about the big thing everyone is talking about - server stability.There's a clear warning about server issues on the store page, and some people just ignore it to complain about it 5 minutes later, but, lets look at the issue.I understand why people are upset, their launch has a lot of server problems.But what a lot of people don't seem to understand is one simple thing about server:Fixing server issues is not as simple as flipping a switch and turning on a couple more server or upgrading some hardware.It's a ton of work to get things like that up and running to perform as stable as people would like them to.And here's the next tiny oversight some people might have, we aren't talking about some big AAA game, we are talking about Devolver Digital and Mediatonic.A small 20 people strong publisher team that has brought so many amazing games to life and, compared to other players in the multiplayer market, small dev team of just over 200 people.I'm not saying that the launch was something that should be ignored, because it shouldn't. But it should be discussed in a form that's not just calling Devolver Digital out on how bad the launch was, but to actually try and understand what went wrong.There's always the argument of "look at big AAA game launches, did their server run without problem?" and most of the time, the answer to that is "no".Because preparing a multiplayer game is not a simple task.So in conclusion, would I recommend this game?Yes. It's fun and addictive.If you're a fan of action packed mini games, buy it.Should you wait before you buy the game?Totally. Wait it out, give it a few days, let them work out the server issues and when the warning on the store page is gone, buy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a MMO, 3D platformer, party game in which 60 players compete in mini-games/elimination rounds against each other until 1 man (or 1 team) is left standing. All players are awarded with in-game currency based on their performances. The currency are then used to buy cosmetic items for one's character or name tag from the in-game store, which rotates its merchandise daily. The appearance & vibe of this game is very light-hearted & goofy, but yet the gameplay can become surprisingly frustrating as the little character you control moves as clumsily as a toddler. The game is a fun time killer, but I don't think it would hold a gamer's interest for long term, unless that person has a tendency to be a collector, aka: a loot hoarder. This multi-player game, unfortunately, does not support voice or text chat, which is a MAJOR LET-DOWN for any multi-player game. Without friends to group up with & a 3rd party app such as Discord to provide voice chat, your communications with the other 59 random players are limited to the in-game taunt animations, which people tend to ignore. If you have friends who already own this game, the purchase will definitely be worth it if you guys play regularly with a 3rd party voice chat app to cheer or heckle each other. Otherwise, the replayability of this game will be dependent on how much of a loot hoarder you are.Seriously Fall Guys, Y U NO have chat support?!?!?! UPDATE: Voice chat among group members have just been added. It still would be nice to have voice chat among team members, not just group members, and text chat among everyone else in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential to be the next best multiplayer game. The variety of minigames is tremendous and the core mechanics are so easy to learn that pretty much anyone can pick it up.On PC there are a few issues however:1. Hackers - To be in a game without a hacker is a miracle. You can easily tell which players are cheating, because they zip around the course at impossible speeds. Also, in jumping minigames, they might fall of the platform, but then they spring right back up. Unfortunately, at this time, nothing can be done, because they don't have protection like other multiplayer games such as Team Fortress 2 do. In addition:2. Lack of Unique Names - This is an issue that the developers have claimed they are working on, but currently PC players are unable to use their steam names in game. This means that we are unable to report any hackers.3. Bad Servers - The developers are a very small company and do not have the resources yet to have servers that can hold all of the players. It sometimes takes a while to get into a game that you don't immediately get disconnected from.4. Minigame Variety - I mentioned earlier that the minigame variety is amazing. This is, however, if the randomizer is working properly. Depending on they day, I might play the same game 4 times in a row (upon starting a new episode). 5. The Grab Function is broken - One of the main functions of this game is being able to grab both the other players and anything in your environment. Unfortunately, sometimes the function doesn't work properly. One moment I will fail to grab someone right next to me, but someone else will grab me from a very far distance. This sucks in games that require grabbing. If you don't care about winning a bunch, this game is great. I might even say the best mutiplayer game that isn't an FPS. I think all of these issues will be fixed in due time. The developers are new, but I'm sure they are working hard. This is a great game to play with friends, and honestly even by yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys is a genuinely fun battle royale with a lot of potential, and with seemingly loyal developers at the helm that can support and propel this game forward into the future. Though there are some glaring issues that I do believe the developers desperately need to fix if this game is going to keep holding people's attention, they shouldn't stop people from purchasing the game and having fun with it, especially with friends.--------------------------------------------------Can you guys remember a time where you actually had fun playing a Battle Royale? Where you weren't just constantly stressed out looking behind your back hoping to god that somebody isn't trying to screw you over and end your entire run? I genuinely haven't, as with games like Fortnite, PUBG, you name it, I've probably played it and then stopped playing it shortly after just because of how unfun it turned out to be. Fall Guys is a game with personal enjoyment at the center, though at times this message gets contradicted, at the core you are in control and it doesn't really matter what happens in the game, you're just trying to stay alive.The game can be divided into three types of games: Races, Party Games (similar to what you'd find in Mario Party), and Team-based Games. the most fun, and you can spot them from a mile away. They're the ones with the fun gimmicks like, jump through the holes in the way, grab a tail, or memorize these shapes. These are easily the most enjoyable out of the entire game and I hope that the developers add a lot more of these into the game. I'd say that they are extremely good at weeding out the chaff from the group as at the game starts with 60 people participating, these races should be used to thin that number down. Only problem is that the final round can be a race, and races are completely luck based. You can go from 1st to 10th easily, and during the final round this CANNOT happen when you've done absolutely nothing wrong. It's just feel bad for no reason. there's so many things wrong with them I honestly haven't a clue why they're in the game. Nobody likes them, unless you're with a squad, you dread the team games. Unreliable team members who can just throw the game despite you doing nothing wrong combined with the possibility that the teams can be uneven? Seriously how is this in the game? I played a game where it ended 15 - 0 all because we had one more person on our team than they did.I honestly hope they don't develop any more team games or find some way to balance them, because they're honestly the worst part about the game. Maybe only put them in if majority of the lobby is in stacks?There's also the issue of a lack of games on launch. Honestly, you can play this game for about an hour or so and see majority of the games that are available. This isn't too bad as it seems the developers are being responsive and working on updates, but it's something to keep in mind; there's just not too much to see.If you've played Fortnite, you're very familiar with the cosmetic store, every so often a new set of cosmetics will go for sale and you can buy them with the In Game currencies you earn. There is absolutely no pay to win, and no currencies you can only get by paying either. As such the shop is very very fair and something I'd like to see more of in games.Overall, very enjoyable game that while a little shallow and with some glaring issues, it can be expanded upon and fixed very easily with time. While that might seem like a risk to some, at $20, a huge active playerbase, and responsive devs, it's a very safe risk to take.

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches an itch I've had my entire life, and that itch is: a fun 3D platformer that I can play again and again.The randomness is very much a factor in why this game is so massively replayable for me. Either it's a completely new obstacle in a familiar stage (through updates), an old one sneaking up on me, or the wonky physics of another bean person flying straight into mine. I keep having these amazing moments happen seemingly every time I boot the game up, and I love it so much.Like, I had this round where I was jumping across towers to get over a wall, while a bunch of other beans were doing the same thing, and then ANOTHER bean on the ground started moving the towers, successfully making everyone (but me) fall off! It was such an adrenaline rush, I had to make many decisions on the spot, but it was freaking hilarious to watch unfold.BUT. It's not all fun, as one of my friends got really frustrated and kept blaming the game for a lot of their losses, and there is definitely some stuff that is "unfair". Sometimes you will see an action like grabbing something totally work on your screen, but then what you grabbed is just magically ripped from you afterwards.I tend to not care about those issues (they happen very infrequently and it's only gotten better through updates), but I know it's a deal-breaker for some like the aforementioned friend. Also, keep in mind that the randomness and chaos in general can feel pretty unfair at times.In closing though, I just love playing the game, coming up with on-the-spot strategies to win, and just controlling the beans as it all blends together in hilarious chaos. As far as I know, the money I spent on this game already felt justified after some really fun rounds with my friends so it's a nice surprise that I've gotten over a 100 hours with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys is pretty much what I expected, but not as much of it as I expected.There have been connection issues which don't help, but that isn't a focus of my issues.I was excited for this release since it was first announced and have played Transformice on and off for a decade now, being the closest thing I can compare this to. I would currently say that Transformice is the better game for the following reasons:Round Downtime: In Tranformice you may be eliminated early in a round or complete it well ahead of the rest of the group and have a minute or two of them finishing while you wait. Then you will go immediately to a new round. In Fall Guys if you continue to the next round of a full game you'll need to go through the round elimination screen, the next round selection screen, the loading/game description screen, the stage overview screen, and then the countdown to the start of the round. To start a new game in Fall Guys you need to go through the point accrual screen, back to the home screen, gathering players screen, and then into the screens for every round noted above. In Transformice you immediately load new rounds. If you leave a lobby for a new one you may need to wait the 1-2 minutes for that round to end before joining.Now, notably, Transformice is not actually a battle royale. Fall Guys will take one group and lead them through multiple rounds in a single game until there is one winner of the final round, as you do in BRs. Still, that design choice is responsible for the multiple added delays between rounds.Point 2: There's like 10 stages in Fall Guys. That's a ballpark, but I think it might be generous. To release a game like this where after 2 hours you'll have likely played every single individual type of round, and certainly multiple times each is... well it's a weird choice. Even a casual player will likely get the same games multiple times in one setting, especially if they don't often make it through to the last rounds. Transformice had a lot more variety early on, and has since added a huge number of custom player stages to normal rotation. Fall Guys absolutely needs some kind of player designed stage system to hope to keep people interested long term.tl;dr: if this wasn't a day 1 buy for you, wait until it's on sale and/or there's been some kind of community stage design system implemented. If you love the concept try out Transformice for free. If you love battle royales and this was just a change, I imagine you'll be back to playing what you were before this released inside a week.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY. This is a game for streaming, not for playing.Summary: Good core concept, good primary loop gameplay, terrible secondary/tertiary loop gameplay.There are some amusing concepts in Fall Guys, but these around surrounded by terrible structural choices. If another developer made a game with a similar primary loop (mascot platforming and party games), I would try it. But this game is terrible.Mascot running an obstacle course? Fun.Poor jumping controls? Not fun.Obstacles where outcomes depend on what competing players do, i.e. the see-saw? Not fun.Emphasis on spectating? Not fun.Elimination-based system where losing involves a large amount of luck? Not fun.Hiding the quit button in the settings menu? Punishable by death.This is Mario Party meets PUBG or one of those elimination-based battle royale games. But in Mario Party, if you lose a mini-game, by luck or skill, you keep playing.In Fall Guys, if you make a mistake, you stop playing. If you're unlucky, you stop playing. If you're playing a team game and you're unlucky with the team balance, you stop playing.So if you like Mario Party, but want more frustration, anger, and disappointment in your life, this is the game for you. And you should probably seek help.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has tons of potential. There are major issues I am not seeing mentioned in reviews. 1. The game has blatant and obvious hackers who remain in games even after using what look like developer tools (ex. moving at 100 times normal speed, flying/hovering, being untouchable/immune etc) 2. The mechanics of grabbing (a requirement of roughly 1/3 of the mini-games) seem much too latency dependent. You can often be grabbed from great distances away, or grabs that look solid on your screen don't register (ex. snatching tails) 3. The game will create deliberately unbalance teams. For example, with 14 players remaining, the game will pick a 3 team game, necessitating a 5v5v4. It seems to have no mechanic built in to avoid this problem. It could simply select a 2 or 4 team game when the number of remaining players is even and a 3 team game when divisible by 3. If the remaining number of players is prime, simply don't select a team game. This wouldn't be a big issue with 11v11v12 or something similar, but the game will give 4v5 soccer matches, or 5v5v6 stone pushing contests.  As I stated before, the game has lots of potential, but there are some glaring issues that need addressing. They often ruin what should otherwise be a really excellent concept and much needed fun and social game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Changing my review to not reccomended until the rampant hacker issue is solved. Never have I seen a game so popular have so little control over hackers and exploiters. It's actually ridiculous almost 1 in 2 games I play I have to leave because there is a hacker. Fix your game already and remove these people. Truly unacceptableExcellent game that's a breath of fresh air for the battle royale genre. No shooting people, shrinking circle or lootcrates to open, just your platforming skills, decision making and a lot of luck. With that being said, I'm going to go into the good and bad.The Good:1.Skins can be readily earned simply by playing the game. The currency to purchase skins comes in the form of playtime and crowns, which you can only earn by winning games. Excellent choice and one that limits absurd micro transactions like in other games (Fortnite, PUBG)2.Level Design-Every challenge is very unique with the exception of one or two transitioning to a team setting, but every game you play is different and unique.3.Fun, casual vibe with funny physics that makes this game very anti-competitive and low-key. Something you can kick back on the couch and play and still have fun even if you lose.The Bad1.Hackers-If you look at the other reviews for this game, you would think they're running rampant in the game. I'm nearly level 40 with almost 40 hours in this game and I would say that I only see one in every 10 games, if that. Regardless, this should be the dev's primary focus in banning these people or getting some form of anti-cheat to prevent people from moon-jumping, speed hacking and no-clipping during games.2.-Lack of modes. I realize this game just came out, however it is enormously popular and would hate to see it die off because of lack of innovation. I'm sure the devs are hard at work pumping out new content, but adding the steam workshop/modding tools and curating and selecting community designed levels for this game would be amazing and would add hundreds more hours to the longevity of this game.3-Fall Mountain Tail Tag-The most unfair final mode at the moment without a doubt is Fall Mountain. Unless you spawn in the front row or your opponents in front of decide to have an epileptic seizure and forget how to walk, you are more or less guaranteed to lose if you spawn in the back rows of this mode. Incredibly frustrating because you simply lose the game because of rng. God bless Hex a Gone I wish I could play this every round for the finals. Tail tag latency has been addressed by the devs on Reddit, but it is still a problem when some dude from 5 feet away grabs your tail with one second left. Royal Fumble is definitely being affected by this, so yet another reason why there is only one "truly fair" final round mode with Hex A Gone. Here's hoping Jump Showdown is added back in soon.Hope to see more modes, challenges and features in the coming future. This is a great game all around. Devs please do not make the mistake Epic did with Fortnite and pander to the competitive/Twitch streamer audience. Do not make this a sweaty competitive game with a ranked mode and Win/Loss stat tracking ratios.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to hate Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout upon initially trying it out. I've never really been a fan of the battle royale, one winner takes all multiplayer games, and I'm a bit of a contrarian when it comes to new popular games. I tend to lean away from a game when it gets really popular, so I waited a little while until after the hype subsided before trying this game. I can safely say that waiting was a mistake, I have a ton of fun with Fall Guys.It's fun to play a battle royale without getting shot at, like in Fortnite or PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds. I like that it is a bunch of identical players trying to accomplish the same goal of not falling off of the map, as well as mixing in some team based modes. I find myself getting far less angry, probably due to how much easier this style of game is than shooters. However, it is frustrating when you come so close to winning, and end up choking or getting grabbed by another jokester player. Above all else, it is exhilarating and I still tend to have a good time when I lose.The style is delightfully saturated and silly, and the simplicity of every design choice is so refreshing. It's nice to have a new 3D game that isn't demanding on your hardware, or trying way too hard to look pretty. I could see the sound design being annoying to some people, but it's so basic that I can't muster any reason to complain about it. I have just as much fun playing alone as I do with family and friends.The cosmetics are ridiculous and fun, and I understand the internet absolutely hates paying for additional content on top of a game you already bought, but nobody is forcing you to buy a purely cosmetic change, and you'll unlock free outfits pretty quickly if you get invested in the gameplay.I don't really have any serious critiques or hindrances with Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout. I end up having fun with it every time I play, and the few times I win feel like heaven itself. I think you'll have a good time with it and feel rewarded when you eventually win. I know it isn't as popular as it was currently, but as someone that avoids game hype as much as possible, I had a blast and look forward to any new content in the future. The people that tell you it's a "dead game" are most likely children, or trend hoppers. Don't listen to them, try it out for yourself. If I can enjoy this game, anyone can.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the potential to be a very fun and silly game, but unfortunately, it completely fails at doing so because the developers cant decide what kind of game it is. Is it a silly game for fun where you don't need to care if you win? Or a game where you actually need to try and win for better and cooler skins? They try to do both, but that isn't possible. They contradict each other. Most of the game modes are very luck based, where you don't really have much of a say whether or not you win. That wouldn't be much of a problem, if i didn't NEED to get wins in order to unlock certain skins. If that's the case, and i have very little control over if I win, then technically speaking I could never get these skins. That is pretty stupid and causes way too much frustration which makes it too hard to continue playing the game for after a couple games or so. The games are super unbalanced and there is no actual consistency between the modes. It feels like there almost wasn't any play testing, for instance some levels feel wayyyyy too crowded to the point where you almost have no control of your character because there are too many players on certain levels. Some levels feel like they shouldn't allow so many people, perfect example is tnt run. The gamemode is able to house up to 15 people, which is wayyyy too many people for a mode like tnt run. There are countless examples of this throughout the game, another good example is the slime rising level. This level is actually one of the more fun levels in the game, and can be a lot of fun with friends. However, sometimes there are wayy too many people on the level sometimes and it causes the level to almost feel unplayable, as you literally cant climb the mountain and focus on the actual obstacles your supposed to be dodging, because your too busy trying to get out of the way of other players. I could go on and on about how luck based and random the games feel, but it can be summed up by saying that the game should try to figure out what it wants to be and stick to it. If the game wants me to get wins in order to get stuff, then maybe adjust the levels to be more skilled based and less luck based. Also, the player sizes on some levels definitely should be looked at and adjusted. This game has the potential to be a super fun game that you can sit with your friends and play for hours on end having a blast, but instead it lasts for around twenty to thirty minutes, contains tons of keyboard smashing and then switches to another game because its just too much to bear at that point.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 06/08/2020: I've updated the bottom of the post with some extra info related to comments.I played a bunch of the beta, so now that the full game is released I feel I can write my first review of the game.Fall Guys is SO CLOSE to being really good, but there's just a few things in the game that need to be changed to let me get consistent enjoyment out of it.The positives of the game is that it's goofy fun, and easy to jump into a game. Other people's reviews will cover the fun parts of the game, but I wanted to highlight the things that stop me from giving this game a positive review.1) Team games need to get in the bin. They're the least fun part of Fall Guys, as you can get knocked out from a show even by playing really well. There's very little feedback from the game as to what is happening across the rest of the match. When you lose it wasn't down to your fault, and when you win it doesn't feel satisfying. There needs to be separate playlists for solo play and team play, and the team games need to be adjusted so that you'll be playing with the same team for the whole show and you can actually feel like you're contributing to a team effort. There would need to be ways to communicate with your team similar to rocket league, or by using the otherwise pointless emote system.2) The costume colours need to get in the bin. It feels really scummy that not only do you need to wait for the store to refresh an item you're looking for (the store is ripped directly from fortnite) but you have to buy multiple costumes to have choices of colours. The costumes even change colours for team games, so there should definitely be a way for the player to customise the colour of the costumes they've unlocked. The player colours that you unlock end up feeling a bit worthless when wearing a costume has the possibility of completely obscuring it anyway. Why is it that the design decision was made for a player to either prioritise a player skin/colour or a costume? It's really peculiar and only seems to be used to pad out the amount of content in the store.3) Lack of content. I read somewhere that there are 25 different maps at launch, with some maps sharing the same game mode. The most fun parts of the game are the obstacle courses, and there reaaaaaally needs to be more, preferably with the option of a playlist of only obstacle courses. The maps are all made from the same building blocks, so it shouldn't be too difficult to have a bunch more of them in the game. Considering the game isn't free to play, and this isn't early access, I hope that the roster of maps will be updated very soon and not at the end of season 1 which is going to go on for 60 days...4) Some of the game modes are really not that fun at all. It's usually the team ones, but especially game modes like the Jinxed one. In Jinxed, two teams are pitted against each other and you have to grab players to infect them. Last team with an uninfected player wins. No matter how the game is played it pretty much always comes down to 1 player left on each team, and you'll likely have very little involvement with how the match ends up finishing. I'm sure on paper team games looked like fun, but seeing as this game is "heavily inspired" by Takeshi's Castle, it's worth looking at why they didn't really do team games. I hope that now the game is out, feedback from players will help shape what game modes get further development and which game modes get more maps.5) £50/$60 currency purchase in the store. I mean, what more needs to be said about that. The game isn't free so you can't just carbon copy the store from fortnite, which is a free to play game. I don't like paying for and playing a game that essentially tells me I'm wasting my time earning currency by actually playing it, when I could instead make a purchase of 100K coins that would take me dozens of hours to grind out. I'm honestly okay with paying £4/$5 for 3 exclusive skins as DLC, as is currently on offer, but the in-game store purchases are just really not nice for the players.This game is so close to being really, really good, and I hope that the developer's response to community feedback will shape the game and let me change this review to a positive one in the future.-----------------------------------------------06/08/2020- All maps were available in the beta.- The store is similar to Fortnite's in that content is time exclusive, meaning a player has to spend their currency or feel like they may miss out. There is no way to guarantee you're going to be able to unlock a specific item you may want, unless it is one of the DLC items.- The number of games at launch won't be enough to sustain certain players, and £15 isn't an unsubstantial amount of money. Further, the size of the game at launch makes me worried that additional maps will be added in a conservative way, as the game is already quite large with only the maps at launch. It also seems that the possibility of community-made content would be hampered by large map sizes.- This last point is a personal perspective, so I understand that people may not agree with it, and that's okay. But to me, by definition this isn't an indie game as Devolver Digital is the publisher for it. I know that people have different definitions of what constitutes an indie game, so it's not a point that I'm dead set on defending. It comes down to personal perspective.Overall, I've been enjoying the game, especially with friends (even though playing with friends doesn't get you any benefits and you're guaranteeing not everyone can win!). But this review isn't written for me, it's written for people who have to decide whether they can afford to spend £15 on something that may or may not be worth what money they have.

_childDocuments_.review: While Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout isn't nearly as popular as it was around the time it launched, it still remains a perfect video game for what it sets out to accomplish. Its presentation, gameplay, low skill floor and price tag make it accessible to anyone who'd want to give it a try. If you're looking for something refreshing to play with a group of friends, even those who might not be big on video games, then look no further. Gameplay-wise, it is the best Wipeout or Ninja Warrior game (n?)ever made. You know, those shows where people have to beat an obstacle course in order to win the prize money? Here it’s a bit different, with up to 60 players thrown into a match, consisting of several rounds. At the end of every round, those who fail to complete the objective in time are eliminated. Not every round is an obstacle course however, but can be anything from a vast plethora of minigames spread into six different categories. For example, Race rounds will always task you with reaching the finish line of the course before a certain number of players manage to. Survival rounds will require you to not get eliminated before a certain number of players does, or a timer runs out. These are then further differentiated by themes and obstacles. One Survival round might have you balance atop of an ever-moving platform, dodging projectiles launched at you, while another will place you in an arena with three giant Rhinos attempting to knock you out. Team rounds, which require you to work with random players towards a common goal to prevent your entire team from being eliminated are all about scoring points, but can either be a game of basketball, football (the soccer kind) or collecting as high of a number of eggs as possible. In the main game mode, a match must always start with a Race and end with a Finale – the most suspenseful, final round of the match, usually a Race that only one player can win or a Survival round that keeps going until the last man standing. Other game modes, both fixed and rotating, focus on specific categories or levels themselves. There are also custom matches you can make for you and your friends.Even if all rounds across a category follow a certain pattern, none ultimately feel the same. Additional obstacles will sometimes appear on maps they were previously absent from, so the game can still throw you a curveball even when you think you have them all memorised. Still, some are clearly better designed than others. Door Dash, a Race round, is a course consisting entirely out of doors. Some of these are openable, while the others aren’t – with there being no way of telling between the two until you try going through them. It almost completely eradicates the momentum of the match. If you go for an unlocked door consistently enough, you’ll qualify. If you don’t, tough luck. Other levels that solely consist of multitudes of the same obstacle have a similar effect, though none are as bad as Door Dash.The controls are quite tight due to how limited they are. You can jump, grab (players, ledges, objects and some objectives) and dive, so the game requires a total of three buttons to play – excluding movement. A controller is ideal, but the keyboard and mouse perform almost just as well.Progression feels good, but it could be better. Winning a round will net you a Crown, the game’s ’’premium’’ currency awarded solely through wins or milestones in the current Season’s battle pass-like progression, called Fame levels – limited to 50 per Season and increased by XP, which is awarded for each match you play. Each Crown you acquire also increases your overall player rank, which awards you cosmetics upon leveling up and is separate from your Fame level. Besides Crowns, there are Kudos, a second currency awarded at certain Fame levels, as well as upon completion of a match regardless of whether you won or not. Kudos can also be purchased through microtransactions, in bundles as costly as $50, more than twice the game’s price. While the game isn’t by any means stingy with its rewards, the progression does feel a bit staggered and the inclusion of microtransactions can’t help but make me think of some marketing analyst or currency designer figuring out how to optimize it best to incentivise a purchase. Even when they aren’t intrusive, they’re there for a reason.Your rewards can be spent in the store for cosmetic items. Some cost Kudos, some cost Crowns. There’s a fixed number of items that can be displayed in the store at a time and they reset once a day. Simple as. Customization options for your Fall Guy are quite varied and some visually striking combinations are possible, even without playing much.Visually, the game is a colorful joy to look at, with the audio making it all the more appealing. The Fall Guys make cute ’’oofs“ and other sounds when they collide with each other, and scream of excitement when an obstacle launches them into the air – all of it heightened by a groovy, bass driven soundtrack. It just oozes fun.Performance wise, the game ran great on max settings, at a steady 60 FPS. However, the animation LOD distance wasn’t that great, as players and obstacles further away would be running at a notably lower framerate. I don’t know if this is simply the way the game’s optimised, or something affected by the limitations of my specs. Weirdly enough, the game would sometimes drop down to 30 FPS while waiting in the lobby or the post-match recap. Reviewed on the following system:While the game’s current player numbers are a far cry from what it once had, it still maintains a healthy population, both on Steam and outside of it, thanks to cross-play. I wholeheartedly hope that Mediatonic can keep Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout in such a state, as it’s a fun game that truly anyone can play. Even if you don’t end up winning, the little animation your Fall Guy does during the post-match summary shows that he’s had a lot of fun even participating, just as you will. Here’s to hoping it can keep going strong in the years to come, at least as long until there’s a worthy successor.

_childDocuments_.review: When Fall Guys launched, just a few months after the world shut down, it was right on track to be a perfect game. It brought friends together in a tough time with an engaging and undeniably goofy experience that just felt good to play. But with its refusal to create meaningful variety or adequately reward its playerbase for sticking around, the game just makes me sad imagining what could have been. Despite the promise of its premise, no opportunity for fun goes unignored.Part 1 - The FallThis is a game about falling over. It's simple, it's stupid, and it's brilliant. I love seeing a new course and finding out the new ways it can cause the players, myself included, to land on their face as they contend with an unfamiliar challenge. But a course is only fresh for the first few days of its release, and the moment it's understood, onto the pile it goes. It's just one more line of obstacles to churn through, with no real challenge left to offer you. You've stopped falling over.When variety dies, fun dies with it. I'm not just talking about a lack of new stages. The amount of individual courses is perfectly serviceable as it is (the Vault notwithstanding), and it would be foolish to ask that the developers just keep churning out new and unique maps. What's missing is a way of shaking up the maps we already have. Once upon a time, some effort was made in that regard. Some stages have sections in which the typical obstacles can be randomly swapped out for different ones, or a wildly-swinging hammer may appear in select areas where it can knock a skilled player toward victory. These instances, however fun, are rare, and the developers appear unwilling to add more; this leaves an enormous chunk of levels completely static in their function. What's more, any effort put into these additions does add unfamiliarity to a level, but only for so long. At some point, you've just seen it all. But variety can itself be expressed in a variety of ways, and by their combination, we can multiply the level possibilities for very little additional effort. More possibilities to confuse the player, to get them to fall over.My preferred solution is random stage modifiers. Give any course a chance to inflict a gameplay-altering effect that challenges the player to rethink a familiar course. I could list off modifiers all day, but here's a small taste:Dizzy - Reversed controls!Flightless - Jumping disabled! You can still dive.Slippery - Ice physics!Leaping - Jump is twice as high!Startling - Grabbing another player causes them to jump!Ghostly - Players do not collide! You can still grab.Fishy - Run speed greatly reduced! Use dives to move quickly.Wild - Several Rhinos are placed randomly on the course!Tiring - Jumping has a 3-second cooldown.Xtreme - No respawns, only elimination!By no means is it one-size-fits-all, as not every stage can be completed with every modifier, but it would exponentially increase the total number of unique level combinations and ensure that even an experienced player would need to stop and think about what they're doing instead of always following the same practiced line that gets them to the end the quickest. They will approach with caution, they will be confused, and they will fall over. And falling over is the fun part.Part 2 - The GuysThe bean-shaped playable characters in Fall Guys, are, by their design, nothing. When you boot up the game for the first time, you are given a naked pink Nothing Man to play as, which seems perfectly appropriate for the kind of game you're playing. After all, playing the game is half the fun, the other is how the game plans to reward you! "Great," you say, "I can't wait to unlock some outfits so I can stop being so nothing!". And you're half-right in your assessment: You will find outfits, but you will never stop being nothing.With no intention to spend money on this free-to-play game, and certainly not the 8-or-so dollars the game expects for any of its premium outfit packages, your options may seem limited. By slowly accruing Kudos over days of play, however, you can expect to eventually afford a shiny pair of spiked wristbands and a neat sunhat to keep your Nothing Man looking stylish. If you wear the both of them together, maybe you can put together a pretty swanky new look for yourself. Oh, but what's this? Upper, Lower, Faceplate, Color, Pattern... Where's the Accessory tab? Surely you don't mean to tell me that if I wear these spiked wristbands, I can't wear anything else on my entire top half? And yet, this is exactly the case for every Kudos outfit: You may wear gloves, wristbands, glasses, or a hat. Individually, these costume pieces look great! But "individually" is all you get without Show Bucks, the freemium currency of which the game will toss you a few crumbs each month for dedicated play.Aggressive monetization is to be expected from any free-to-play game, and Fall Guys is no exception. If you want your character to feel less naked, it's either play every day or cough up the dough. However you choose to acquire a nicer outfit for yourself, put it on and experience the freedom of your new polar bear costume! I just hope you don't mind the dead-eyed stare of your Nothing Man's faceplate looking back at you. Regardless of your outfit choice, it will have a gaping hole in the middle, ensuring the bland non-design of your playable character's face will always stab through the fun outfit and into your eyeballs. There's a Nothing Man inside that costume, the game says, don't forget about the Nothing Man. In the great paradox of Fall Guys' art design, it seems no price is high enough to hide the aspirin tablet with limbs they spent so long not designing.If the character's face must be shown, why make it so devoid of identity? The treatment of the character as a strangely-shaped person, rather than a blank slate to be dressed over, is particularly problematic when the likeness of an actual human is hideously stretched over the cylindrical shape of the Nothing Man's body, complete with an artificial tan faceplate to remind you of the dark deed that has taken place. Wouldn't the task be better served by a character with a slight identity rather than none at all? Given the chance to step back to the beginning and present a different design, I would simply replace the slippery clumsy "people" with slippery clumsy penguins. An animal character has instant appeal no matter what outfit it's given to wear or what silly game show stunt it's asked to perform, which cannot be said for the Nothing Man. And if you still insist upon the face being seen, don't worry, at least penguins are cute.Part 3 - The Ultimate KnockoutThe switch from the pay-once model to free-to-play resulted in a change to the players' focus -- it has blurred to the point that it can be hard to see a reason to play at all. Before free-to-play, "premium" outfits were bought with 5 Crowns, one of which was awarded for each win. Crowns are no longer a spendable currency but instead go toward a linear and unchanging list of exclusive unlockable outfits for increasingly sweaty players to wear as status symbols (which, due to the aforementioned character customization, eliminates the ability to wear anything else). If you wish to wear the outfits you've purchased, whether with free or premium currency, winning has been effectively disincentivized.Fall Guys is a game that deserved better than it got, and the window for any kind of real change closed years ago. When I turn back to take a look through that window, I see a better game. With every glacially slow season, it slips ever further into mediocrity, and I wish more and more to return to the first year of playing Fall Guys with friends before we discovered that occasionally being new and shiny was the best this game was going to get.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing way before Season 2, and I've got to say, this game is a lot of fun.Is it the best game I've ever played? Absolutely not. Not even close. I hate so many aspects of this game, from how easy it is to screw over other players, to the faulty grabbing mechanics, to how difficult it is to win even one episode.But you know what? I keep coming back to it.I don't particularly know why, but something about the cuteness of it all and the adrenaline rush you get in the final round, not to mention the one you get when you finally DO win...it makes all the bad times almost worth it in the end.I think what needs to change the most is the hitboxes for other players, particularly for games like Wall Guys or Hit Parade or Slime Climb or Hoopsie Daisies. And there need to be way less luck-based games like Fall Mountain or Tail Tag (team or otherwise) or Door Dash or Tip Toe or the aforementioned Hoopsie Daisies. And, again, the grabbing mechanics MUST be worked on. I'm getting tired of being grabbed by a player who's literally three to four arm lengths away from me.This game DOES have fun aspects, though. I'd say it starts getting really fun the better you get at it, even though it's entirely possible to have a perfect run only to be screwed over by a team game or a faulty grab mechanic. I may have more negative things to say about Fall Guys, but in the end I still see it as a really quality product. It's still in its early stages and has a TON of kinks to work out. But for a battle royale game? Honestly pretty solid. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game design conflicting with itself and marketing in conflict about what you get. Was hoping for more actual silliness in the core gameplay, not "It's silly because you're dodging giant fruit".Already played the same mini-games multiple times in my short playtime.Look, I really  wanted to like this game.After playing heavily competitive games with the crew for quite a while, I was hoping this would be a goofy mario-party type game that was just so darn fun it doesn't matter if you lose. Unfortunately I was disappointed. To be clear I'm not talking about bugs with the game (there are plenty of those too, even in my short playtime), I'm talking about the game design itself. That means two people on your squad can be eliminated but the other guy is unaffected. So...now what? Does he keep playing? Does he quit? I realize this isn't a problem if you 'lol, just don't get eliminated', but my point is that squads are quite literally pointless beyond getting in the same game, and at that point could be downright unfair in some circumstances because members in a party can literally grab someone and hold them in place. Nothing is stopping me or my friends from grabbing people so one of us can win.One person still has to be the victor in the end. In light of the previous point making the game more competitive off the bat than I was hoping, the games(to me) just felt lifeless. It's hard to put my finger on exactly what's missing, but imagine something like 'gang beasts' where the movement itself is goofy. Especially first starting out just trying to do a basic grab is entertaining.Here the movement is basic and yes some funny things can happen, but I wouldn't call the game goofy at all. Just simple. And a lot more serious(in gameplay) than I was expecting.While simplicity is fine(it can even be great), Fall Guys seems so simple that it removes a lot of player agency.Coupled with heavy RNG in some places like race starting position and again I felt like I was expected to compete seriously but without enough control to take it seriously. I had already seen the same games multiple times even in my short playtime. On top of that, many racing games felt the same because they boiled down to the same goal:Run forward, dodge obstacles. I feel it could benefit monumentally from having different mechanics inside a race(example off the top of my head: a balance beam). The more I think about it, the more I realise I just wanted a game made out of Mario-party mini-games.I thought that's what this game would be; but it's not.That could very easily just be put on my expectations and not doing research but I feel like the marketing was a bit misleading in that regard. The 'goofiness' is silly costumes and giant fruit. I was hoping for actual absurdity in the games.And seeing where I think they're trying to take the game, I don't think I could even come up with changes that would interest me without fundamentally changing what the game is.Maybe make the games point-based instead of elimination so partied up players can stay in the game?But again...that would be a completely different game genre.So now it's one of the very few(if not the only) games I've refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys is the perfect “party” game to play with friends or solo. Its vast range of mini games reel players in, and keep them hooked due to the “next time,” mindset. However, its major flaw and ultimate drag-down is the fact that people are able to hack the game for a competitive advantage, and there is no option to report said hackers. This causes major frustration among genuine players, especially in final modes where hackers are able to hover above to the finish line, or to stay above the goo the longest. This is a key point that the developers need to work on for Season 2; an option to report other players is a critical feature for an online game. Overall, I would highly recommend this game for casual and hardcore gamers alike, and due to it being a game you can pick up for a quick round here and there, it’s definitely worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout is a great game with a lot of potential, but has "fallen" short on some issues. These issues are not game breaking, but very important to bring up. One of those issues was launch and the lack of awareness to understand the user demand for the game, which thankfully will go away shortly after launch when the player base will steady out. This lack of awareness is worrisome, but hopefully they will learn from this to gauge user demand in the future.The other issues are small but very annoying, they include the issue of: not being able to leave the game during the after game screen, lack of diversity in mini-games at launch, the ability to purchase kudos (one of the in-game currencies) with real money even though the game costs $19.99 + tax, Issues with getting into a multi-player sessions with a party of two, and some small bugs that can be rather annoying to deal specifically the mini-games, which should have been tested during QA session in development. There are many positives to this game including: the competitive nature of the game which makes you want to play more and more, the progression system seems to rather well thought of, but nothing to stand-outish, the jellybeans are just adorable, the cosmetics are not just color schemes but custom made costumes, the core gameplay is great and the idea of the game is well thought out. All in all, The game is gonna go through some rough times for the next few months as they get some kinks out and hopefully add more content. As of today 8/3/2020 I give the game a 50/50 on purchasing it. IF you really love the look of the game and you know you'll be playing it in the future I suggest it, but if you are a little hesitant I would suggest to wait a bit to purchase.edit: I believe that during the after game scene those who fall are suppose to get some bonus kudos while falling, but it seems to be disabled or not available in this current build.edit 2: There seems to be no way to report people in the game for cheating!edit 3: odd number of people for "Fall Ball" shouldn't be allowed.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since Covid-19 started I have been inside since I am a type 1 diabetic so that makes me Immunocompromised. I have tried to pass the time this year by playing video games to take my mind off of how terrible this year has been and how my own mental health has been. Every game I have played I have enjoyed and put a considerable number of hours into them, but so far none have sparked a great amount of joy and get quite redundant. Then came Fall Guys. I first heard about it the last day of Beta when i was watching some streams of it on Twitch. Even though I didn't watch a whole lot i knew i had to try it out because it looked soo silly and just plain fun. I picked it up on the last day of preorder and waited for release. The first time launching it and jumping into a game i had actually felt extreme happiness and i was actually having fun. The music, the silly noises, the color, everything just made me have a good feeling and it's been a long time since i've had that.This game will put a smile on my face and will have me playing it for hours on end just to take a break and hop right back on it. When the game launched there were immediate issues that all came down to the servers. They just kept breaking after floods of people were trying to get in. I saw their tweet where something like 1.5 million players in the first 24hours. It was frustrating sure , but I knew they were working on it and for how monumental of a task it was, they managed to fix the problems rather quickly. I have since only encountered sporadic such as getting a server error or just getting kicked out to main menu was queuing with friends. This games design, in my opinion is perfect, the games are all . in their own way perfect. They could use a few tweaks just to really nail it down (See Saws im looking at you). The reward system in this game should be an industry standard, the game has you grinding for crowns for those juicy cosmetics.I will continue to support this game for a long time and cannot wait to see what they have in store for the future.  I want to thank the devs for making this awful year just a whole lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. This game looks fun. The premise is great. When you GET to play it IS fun. Unfortunately, you do not spend enough time playing. If you make it to the third round or beyond, it's worth it. If you don't (and most Fall Guys don't), it's not. Matchmaking takes WAY too long. Getting the first 50 players happens right away. The last 10...well, let's just say I spent 3 minutes waiting for it to go from 59 to 60 players (rounds won't start without 60) to play for only ~1 minute. Can you think of any other game where you spend more time waiting for matchmaking than playing the game? It's like when you watch a 30sec YT video but have to sit through 1:30 of adds. Customization options are -extremely- limited until you've obtained enough XP and rewards and there isn't much to keep fresh players going.It's fun to spectate other players troubles' after you've finished, but rounds end immediately once enough players have qualified so there isn't enough of this (yes, there is a spectating option but if you're not involved in the game anymore, why would you do that instead of searching for another match?)These issues could be addressed in a number of ways (a points system/limiting matches to 50-55 players once a time limit has elapsed for matchmaking/customization options upfront). I had fun for an hour, but at the end it's not worth $20. F2P would make more sense. Let people purchase DLC and get more people into the game or fix the current problems. I have friends with this game and now I understand why they didn't want to bother playing and why they only have about 1.1 hours (no doubt half of that was sitting in matchmaking) before they stopped.2.5/5.

_childDocuments_.review: I bounced off this when it first came out.  While I tried to get into it, the rounds were too luck-based and repetitive, and it just seemed impossible to get a crown.  Watching things I would've liked to buy enter and leave the shop repeatedly while I got slapped down due to bad luck got old fast.Fortunately, that's no longer the case.  The maps from the first 2 seasons are notably worse than everything that has come in the next 4, which has created a much more varied experience.  The ability to play as squads helps when you can still be carried through even if you get knocked out due to bad luck.  The game also now gives crown pieces which turn into full crowns, so you can still slowly build up a good collection of them even if you aren't winning.  Along with some very fun crossovers, I can now really recommend the game as a solid multiplayer experience with a lot of ways to play.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay, but it could be better. There's a lot wrong with it right now, and because of that I cannot justify the $20 price tag.Pros:- It's usually fun- The rounds are fast- There are some moments that will make you genuinely laugh- It's a nice casual game to pick up quick for a couple rounds. Would not recommend for long periods of play.Cons: - The game becomes very repetitive very quickly. There's not enough map variety, which eventually leads to losing aggravating you more often than not. Those moments that make you genuinely laugh are scarce. Not a lot of difference happens after you've played over a hundred rounds. Same maps, same stuff happening.- Grabbing is a mechanic frequently used by players to grief other players. This may be a reason for it, but I see this being used a lot more often in maps that don't require it solely for griefing purposes (like the rotating cylinder one, the slime climb, players on your team grabbing you, or any race map at the very end)- Some of the maps are really unbalanced and/or have poor mechanics. There's a lot of RNG/chance in some levels.- There is usually no skill involved with this. It's all random chance with physics, and on race maps it can depend on where you're placed in the starting line-up. This is completely random, even if you've placed first in the race match beforehand.- 60 player matches can only last as long as the hype before it'll be harder to find players for matches. Even now, most matches only get somewhere between 35 - 50 players. I have seldom seen any with 55+- Hackers have been popping up.- Uneven teams is a regular issue in the team maps. Also, more often than not, you will be paired with people who have no idea what they're doing and thus will be inevitably concreted to the losing side. (people getting disconnected or leaving adds to this issue)- There's a lot of server issues. Sometimes exiting too soon will freeze your game, sometimes while loading the server will drop, sometimes when in a queue it'll say the server is full or something along those lines and it'll kick you back to the main menu (forcing you to re-queue).- You can only party with up to 4 people, which is upsetting considering this is an up to 60 player game.My advice is don't buy it until it's on sale for half price (or even $5, if it ever gets that low). It's really not worth the money right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Putting this at the top since I think it will help a lot of people: Mouse/Keyboard: The BIGGEST TIP I have is to bind your left mouse click to DIVE and your right mouse click to GRAB. You do not use your mouse click buttons for anything else so it makes dive and grab SUPER easy to quickly press, which will make a huge difference for you. Left click is easier for me to press repeatedly, so I chose dive for that one and grab for the right click because it's not as often. You'll be diving way more than grabbing. If you are playing on CONTROLLER, it almost feels like cheating cause it is SO much easier. Only thing I hate is you have to micromanage the camera angles a little more for some of the courses that twist and turn, but I got the hang of it. OH and hold down the GRAB button when you are making a jump that you're not sure if you will make it or not- YOU CAN GRAB ONTO LEDGES. Wish I knew that sooner. When you first start out it might seem super hard but it gets super easy and fun once you get the hang of it. --------------------------------------------Review:It's like Wipe Out, the tv show. You gather "fame" to level up. You can dive and also grab onto other players to sabotage them, which is a lot of fun. The courses are a lot of fun and there are a ton of them. The cosmetic items are super cute, and the ones you earn in game are way better than the ones you buy through DLC imo. You get a daily random of selection of items (refreshed every day) to buy through their store using crowns or kuddos(?), both of which you earn by playing the game. They have events once a week I think? Not sure how often they are, but there's been a ton of them where you queue up for a special game that gives you a special currency to buy special items with. I love it because while the game hardly ever gets boring, the special events like that give you extra incentive to want to keep coming back. Ton of achievements through steam too. ----------------------------------------Here are some more random tips:If you're playing on a team for tails, please do not steal your team members tails. Working against your own team members is counter-productive. At first I was thinking, oh okay maybe they feel super confident in being able to keep the tail or something? But almost every time they lose the tail IMMEDIATELY after stealing it lol which is hilarious, embarrassing for them, and frustrating for the whole team. Steal the OPPOSITE TEAMS tails.If you're on a team for JINXED and you have the cooties on you, please spread the cooties onto THE OTHER COLORED TEAM, not your OWN team. XD

A report system: There are already cheaters that can fly and speed through these things.  You'll never win against someone like that and there's currently no way of reporting them.  It's very frustrating and demoralizing when you're trying to play and know you can't win.2. Team games with unfair numbers: I can't tell you how many times I've been put into a team game where other teams had a numbers advantage.  If the number left isn't able to be distributed evenly, then don't allow it to pick that specific type of team game.  (Like you can't split 21 into two teams but you can 3 teams) I feel like this is one of the only things that stacks the odds against you as a player.3. An option to turn off team games or que with only solo players: I don't mind team games, but I do mind them when I'm playing with a bunch of solos and red team has a squad of four on it that can coordinate better.  This makes a huge difference and I see it happen often in my own games and in streamers games.  I think this would also even the odds a bit.These are just a couple changes I've thought about while playing that would improve player experience.  Without those, it's still a really fun game and I still recommend others purchase it.  A lot of fun for the price of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked:A unique battle royaleSimple yet cartoony and cute art style.Good soundtracks.Disliked:Extremely and I mean, EXTREMELY luck based.Skill and depth perception is not enough at all to win.There are not enough tools that you can use to win. The only real useful tech would be lunging, but even that has very limited uses.Conclusion:Fall Guys is a unique battle royale where players compete in mini games and obstacle courses as fast as possible instead of your usual combat battle royale via guns or magic etc. It has a simple yet enjoyable art style as well as catchy music that gets you hyped up for the upcoming challenge. As far as game play goes, that's where things get bad. The game is extremely luck based, meaning that to win in the challenges and obstacle courses you need to be lucky instead of skillful. An example of getting lucky would be your start placement because if you start in the back of the group you may fall behind, if you start at the front you have a good chance of staying in the lead along with a couple of players or if you start in the middle you are more likely to get stuck in the crowd and that is the worst considering how annoying it is to get bumped around by everyone else. There's even more luck involved depending on the obstacle course you have to compete in and where in the crowd you started because in certain courses its better to be in a certain place in the crowd.Another example of luck would be in team battles where you have no choice but to cooperate with a team of random players from a previous challenge and pray that they actually try to win. If the team you got stuck in happens to be really bad, you got unlucky and lose with them. If not, then consider yourself lucky and blessed. One more example of luck would be other players behaviors. When going through tight spaces you need to hope that everyone else does not follow you because if they do you are screwed. There is no way to increase your movement speed in the game and dodging is not a thing so you better hope that people don't start ganging up on you and bumping you, especially mid air.There are basically no tools or techs to help you gain an edge on the competition. There is lunging, grabbing and climbing. Grabbing other players or trying to grab them is not useful in the majority of mini games and courses because it actually slows you down. Grabbing is only useful for a few mini games where holding players and stealing items is necessary. Climbing is also not very useful in many mini games and courses because there are very few ledges that your character can even reach and even fewer ledges that can actually be grabbed. Some ledges seem like you can grab them and are withing reach, but when you try it you will just slide against the wall and lose precious time. Lunging has been the only tech that has some use in a handful of scenarios because it can help you dodge an obstacle in time, reach a far away platform, reach the finish line a second faster and SOMETIMES to help you avoid the crowd. Lunging has a little bit of downside that I can agree with and be happy with. This downsides would be the fact that after lunging you go limp and cannot move for a few moments which gets rid of all momentum and thus slowing you down.Skill and Luck are good things to have in a game if both are used properly. In the case of Fall Guys, luck is the sole thing being used. This creates a game that is fun to play at first, but then can quickly start to feel unfair and make you, the player, feel frustrated and powerless. If you don't believe me but don't want to buy the game like I did, just go watch other people play and count how many times they get frustrated and call everything BS. Luck if used properly can help create a game where everyone has a chance of winning or making it far and if you bring skill into the mix, you create a game where many casual players still have a shot of winning and making it far, but you are also now rewarding those players who are more serious about winning and are willing to put in the extra work. This makes everyone happy. Casual players who are mainly interested in having fun, get what they want and those serious players who are interested in winning, get what they want as well.Adding skill to Fall Guys:The appeal of Fall guys comes from a combination of its art style, music and unique battle royale gameplay. Many players also feel like Fall Guy's heavy reliance on luck is also an appeal of the game which is understandable on the surface, but when you dig deeper into what heavy reliance of luck does to a game, you will see why its not such a good thing after all. But, Fall Guy's has become a game accessible to all, so how do we add skill and not ruin accessibility? How do we add skill without completely crapping all over new or less skilled players? Add new tech. I have some I thought up of while playing the game and writing this review.New tech:Fall Cancel: Many times while playing the game you will be bumped out of nowhere on the ground or in mid air by other players or obstacles. When this happens you character will go limp and fall to the ground unable to move for a few moments. Not only do you lose precious momentum and speed, you can also roll for a bit and fall off the stage! This gets highly annoying because it happens out of nowhere, it happens at the WORST times and there is absolutely NOTHING you can do about it. It does not even take a horde of players to get bumped. All it takes is one. Here is where the element of skill and my "Fall Cancel" tech comes in. When bumped on the ground or mid air, you can press the lunge button the moment your character touches the ground. This will trigger the fall cancel and your character will perform a short roll, keeping (NOT ADDING) most of your momentum and speed. When performing the fall cancel your character will perform the short roll in the direction you are currently pressing. During the short roll you cannot be touched by players and you cannot touch any players and you can jump at any time. You have to time the fall cancel correctly otherwise it wont work. Fall Cancel tech will be beneficial to the game because it gives you a tool you can use to recover from getting bumped and even though it requires some level of skill to perform, it is still fairly easy to do so with time even casual players can learn it.Air Twirl:You do a lot of jumping in this game but its a pretty unsafe when in a crowd. This is where my Air Twirl technique comes in. By pressing the Air Twirl button, your character will perform a twirl mid air that will prevent them from getting bumped. They will only be lightly shoved mid air from other players but will not go limp and fall to the ground. You will also only lightly shove OTHER players when performing an air twirl but will not cause them to go limp. When hit by an obstacle mid air and performing an air twirl, you will still get slammed but will not go limp when you fall on the ground.Speed Up:This one I am not so sure about but I thought I would still throw it out there. If you run without stopping or slowing down for 5 seconds you will gain a small but noticeable increase in speed. This buff will go away the moment you slow down or stop. You must be good at avoiding obstacles and players to use this tech to its full potential. You can also run in circles to try and maintain the buff. This can also be helpful when you have fallen behind from everyone else and need to catch up fast.I am now exhausted from writing this and doing the developer's job so I am just going to say, if you care for skill avoid this game. This game is only worth it if you got it free on playstation or if you are a casual and do not care for skill. Hopefully the devs make the game more enjoyable for all someday.

At best, these can be considered controversial additions to gameplay, and at worst, these are haphazard displays of lack of support and a disconnect from the community to sustain the game properly. I absolutely adore this game, and have grudged through its tenure in my library balancing the good and the bad. I've been through its original fad status, the lack of updates and disappointing Season 2, the savior of Squads mode reincarnating the game, the custom playlist cycles, and have been a day 1 player in each and every new season. After hundreds of hours, I can definitely mark my feelings down in this review. This is a good game with a horrible company, not malicious or evil, but absurdly lazy to the point that the most dedicated players aren't here just cause they're good - it's that these above experiences are so integrated into daily gameplay that at this point we just don't care anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Hilariously Fun, But Developers Dropped the BallRating: ★★★★☆Fall Guys is an absolute riot and has provided me and my friends with 41 hours of pure laughter and chaos. It's the perfect game to play with a group, and its whimsical graphics and absurd challenges make for a genuinely enjoyable experience. It's a party game that never fails to deliver on the promise of fun times and uncontrollable fits of giggles.However, my enthusiasm for Fall Guys is dampened by my strong dislike for the developers' decision to remove the game from sale in Russia. Seriously, what were they thinking? It's like they took a page out of a comedy playbook, aiming for a punchline that nobody found funny. Denying an entire country the chance to join in on the fun is a baffling move that has left me scratching my head in disbelief.While I can't deny the sheer enjoyment I've had with Fall Guys, I can't help but feel frustrated and disappointed by the developers' poor judgment. It's like they've set up the most entertaining party ever and then locked the door on some of the guests for no apparent reason. It's a misstep that casts a shadow over an otherwise fantastic game.So, despite my reservations about the developers' baffling choice, I have to admit that Fall Guys is still a must-play game if you're lucky enough to have access to it. The laughs, the challenges, and the ridiculousness of it all are enough to make it a standout in the party game genre. Just be prepared to shake your head at the developers' puzzling antics while you're at it.

name: Twelve Minutes
detailed_description: TWELVE MINUTES is a real-time top-down interactive thriller with an accessible click and drag interface. Featuring James McAvoy, Daisy Ridley, and Willem Dafoe. What should be a romantic evening with your wife turns into a nightmare when a police detective breaks into your home, accuses your wife of murder and beats you to death... Only for you to find yourself immediately returned to the exact moment you opened the front door, stuck in a TWELVE-MINUTE time loop, doomed to relive the same terror again and again... Unless you can find a way to use the knowledge of what’s coming to change the outcome and break the loop. TWELVE MINUTES blends the dream-like tension of THE SHINING with the claustrophobia of REAR WINDOW and the fragmented structure of MEMENTO.

_childDocuments_.review: There are things to appreciate about the game, like its voice cast, great sound design, good music and overall nice looking artstyle, but the game itself is not something I would recommend to most people. It's fun to figure things out in the first half hour or so, but after a while it starts to really feel slow and repetitive. It requires you to have a ton of patience. It's hard to care about characters when the story is told mostly through exposition, and interactions often feel awkward and robotic, with contradicting dialogue. It has some interesting ideas here, but it ultimately feels unsatisfying and meaningless. I will say that it definitely delivered on what I was expecting from the game: Great voice performance from Hollywood actors, and to hear one of my favorite actors Willem Dafoe. I do  not regret playing this game, even if I felt slightly disappointed after playing.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, whatever you have seen from the NEGATIVE reviews, most of them mention how this game is getting repetitive in late game. From my perspective, it turns out to be the POSITIVE part of the game. Now hear me out:(In order to understand the concept of "death loop", I highly suggest you watch the anime "RE: zero" or the movie "edge of tomorrow")So the whole game is about death loop. The context is you will loop the setting or story whenever you fail or die. In this game, you will FAIL A LOT. Hence, people are saying its super repetitive and the game is bad because of it. However, I think they miss the point of the "death loop " setting, which is the desperation of stucking in the loop. Again, the "death loop" will not allow you to progress unless you do the right thing, and this game is so-called "linear" by many because you have to grab the right thing and do the right action to progress a path of story line that you are looking for. But THIS IS WHAT DEATH LOOP IS. I would call it "by design" than "bad design". In short, the "death loop" setting supposes to make you feel annoyed, repetitive and desperate. Only through walking in the character shoes you then can be in the character and feel what "death loop" really is. About the story, some people say the story is predictable or the ending is not satisfying. On that, I can only agree on the second half. Cliche? maybe. But the story before the ending, I will say, worth our time.Lastly, I have to fully agree that the game is a bit over priced. I would say 5-10 dollars less could be a good balance between the pricing and what the game can offer.After all, how would I rate this? I would say its a solid 8 out of 10 as it did give a brand new feeling among all the puzzle solving, narrative type of games out there. I really like how it gives me the feeling of "pincer movement" from the movie "Tenet" XD
