_childDocuments_.review: Lets start by saying that I love the Dark Crystal movie and have enjoyed the show for the most part.   I am also a huge fan of the original Final Fantasy Tactics game and am always looking for good games that implement that style well.I have played through a hand full of missions and I will likely continue but I am a bit on the fence about the game.  Positive:The gameplay mechanics are close enough to Final Fantasy Tactics combat and job systems to be a positive for me.  It's not perfect but it is good.The Dark Crystal world is one I like and is fairly well done.Neutral: The graphics are okay and I think do a reasonable job of moving the story along but could be better and the models seem to be missing something (If you enjoy Muppets you already know how it looks when they try and CG them but that is one of the issues you should know is going to exists in a digital game) The controls and interface is simple and approachable but skirts the edge of being too simple.  Negative:The story is not anything spectacular so far.  This game takes the show and so far just replays things that happened in it but simplified to the extreme.  If you want interesting or deep story then you will get a ton more out of the show than out of this game.    If you have not seen the show I would recommend you watch it so you at least know there is more to the story.There is no voice acting and while that isn't the end of the world the dialog is so simplified and poor that it really stands out.   I'd like to hear at least the unintelligible murmurs most games use in place of spoken dialog.   Results:If you likes the show well enough and you like Final Fantasy tactics you may find this game to be reasonable.  It's not too expensive though I would have paid more for a more polished story, dialog, and sound.  If you don't like the show or Fantasy Tactics I recommend you pass this one by.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this show with my whole heart, and i really really wanted this game to be good. Its sadly not the case. The gameplay itself is fine, but the game is dull, this genre isnt a good conduit for this story (which is presented terribly and paced even worse), you arent exposed to the world or characters in any meaningful way. The gameplay and the story are two disjointed things, one pauses to give way to the other for a bit and so forth, they never intertwine or work together to form a fullfilling experience. If youre a fan of the show and can get this game at a BIG discount or for free, sure, give it a try, there is some fun to be had here and the Dark Crystal coat of paint can be fun at times. At some points some aspects are so poorly implemented or silly, its genuinely funny (Brea needing to get a book and the game making you brawl the library staff to get it, are you kidding me). But if youre not a fan of the original source material, i dont think youll find much to enjoy here at all. Some more ranting below: There are new characters that come out of nowhere and serve purposes that are dumbfoundingly well suited for already existing characters (a savvy, well traveled Sifa who knows about symbols and decodes messages whose meaning previously eludes the main characters, gee, if only there was someone in the show who met this exact criteria. Oh well, heres some guy). Introducing new characters is great, but when you dont have the time or resources to develop them and give us time to know and care about them, it seems silly not to use already established characters.The story feels unfocused, you spend most (and i mean the great majority) of your time fighting other gelfling and hardly ever see the skeksis (youll only meet 3 of them). This would make sense at the beggining, but not too long after that. As i said earlier, at one point you fight the library staff. Its not even that the game puts emphasis in you having to turn other gelfling into rebelling against the skeksis, because it barely does. I guess that this kind of game just requires a lot of disposible miscellaneous enemies, and there arent that many skeksis, so they opted for gelfling instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly complex and in-depth turn-based tactics game.+ Many classes, each with their abilities+ Mix and match abilities, 3 from your main class and 2 from your secondary+ Comboing abilities from different characters matters+ Positioning matters, there are environmental hazards, height gives bonuses and puts you out of reach of melees+ No bugs or crashes+ Okay graphics, not very beautiful but not ugly and true to the art style of the TV show+/- The storyline is an exact retelling of the TV show, so no surprises for fans- no voice acting, disappointing when the TV show had such great VAWorth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I had watched "The Dark Crystal" movie in the past and was familiar with the characters. They became endearing. I am glad there was a story behind the game and not only tactical fighting. It made the game more interesting. I loved the characters and enjoyed mixing and matching different ones on each mission. It did not get boring. Very enjoyable, not like most strategy, tactical games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I've played a lot of Turb based strategy RPGs. Shining Force, Final Fantasy Tactics, Fire Emblem. If I had to pick one this game reminds me of the most it would be tactics. There's some unique elements that keeps it from being a striaght up clone. The graphics are decent and gameplay is smooth, with decent tutorial levels to get you going. I have a soft spot for 80s fantasy films and while I haven't watched the show I did see the movie. I like the setting and expanding upon the film. It's not as nightmarish being videogame sprites as the puppets were LOL. I'd say it would be worth playing if you like turn based strategy games
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance Tactics is a turned based RPG that I enjoyed. The story is based off of Jim Henson’s The Dark Crystal movie and television show on Netflix, which I am planning to watch after beating the game. The game was pretty simple, but as I made it to the mid-game, I noticed that there was a severe balancing issue in the game with the AI. I started playing on normal difficulty but had to lower it and it was still pretty hard. Basically enemies became damage sponges and they would constantly use stuns or other status moves to make attacking them almost impossible. The story was very shallow, if you were going to understand what was going on you would need to watch the Netflix show. That all being said, I did enjoy the intricate job system and pairing abilities to make the best loadout.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Crystal is a highly addictive and fun game. It lacks a bit tactical abilities, For example, the inability to move after an action, leading to not having the ability of attacking and running esp. when at low health. And with everything riding on staying alive, you are forced to bring along a mender of some kind. Instead of being able to use items. especially for things like MP recharging.It has however brought me to a very fun level of meta play, As I am a puppeteer, who streams on twitch and playing puppets as a puppet felt very meta and an exciting experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game.  I was a bit worried after reading some reviews but I'm pleasantly surprised.  It feels like Final Fantasy Tactics with The Dark Crystal as the story and setting.  I would've paid even more for more polish and a longer game (although I'm only 3 hours in but I hear it's not super long) but for $20 this game is a lot of fun and I feel like I got my money's worth. _childDocuments_.review: Short: Wait for a sale or major content adds (unless you got a $20 burnin' in yer pocket then go for it)HUGE fan of Dark Crystal both the movie and show. Love me some TRUE turn based RPG although I've not played a ton of them, usually because they are too hard and I'm a wimp who likes games beatable the first time. SO really a no-brainer for me to pick this up.It's a tablet game. Very shallow. Basic everything. And yet I keep playing. And yet I can't decide if I'm mad. And yet I don't know whether to hit the recommend or not recommend. Why no Maaaaaybe? button, Steam?I have 11 hours in. I've got all the characters so far (10?) all trained up to around 12 or 13 with equal experience in 2 Jobs each. Which is the first of my complaints - in order to keep skills in Jobs (just call 'em classes, shall we?) you have to swap back and forth between the 2 for each character or they don't gain experience in the skill tree of the secondary job. That makes nooo sense. How are you not getting experience on skills you're using? So grinding, there's grinding, for gear and levels and skill tree stuff. There are very few replayable maps for the grinding so that got boring fast. My next big complaint is the way they've pared down the story and shown it with kinda cheesy cartoon panels. Why not clips from the show or at least animation or better drawn panels even, fully rendered? Without the grinding, given how quickly the story maps are progressing, it would be a very short game.  And I'll add my vote to the lack of voice acting complaint. Yeeees, the real actors would be too expensive, but there's lots of people who can mimic famous voices.But my BIGGEST complaint is total lack of information. There is NO description for what the (lots) of stats mean. How in the heck are you supposed to know how to build a character, how to gear them, how to specialize when you don't know how that affects play? Some description of combat effects but not enough. What does "Down Move" mean? Buuut I keep firing it up for a couple battles. Like I said, tablet game.*sigh* I dunno. It's a world I love and characters I love and a battle system I don't hate, and a not tooo terrible price? Maaaaaybe?

If you haven't seen it you might be in for some spoilers but hopefully it will entice you to check it out.  The jobs, abilities and equipment will be fun to rotate around and try different combinations of heroes.  Looking forward to playing this some more!

_childDocuments_.review:
Netflix's The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance comes to life as a thrilling tactical strategy game!

In The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance Tactics, lead the heroic Gelfling to restore light to the world of Thra! Experience everything the fantasy world has to offer by playing throughand going beyondthe events of the Netflix series. Encounter never-seen-before playable characters, stories, and environments. 

Over the course of 80 unique turn-based campaign battles taking place across the lands of Thra, recruit new allies and customize their forces by assigning them jobs and outfitting them with new equipment.

Continue the Story in an Expanded World of Thra - Delve deeper into the legend of The Dark Crystal to learn more about the Gelfling clans and their histories across more than 5 diverse, modular territories. Choose from over 15 character jobs, play through reimagined and brand-new battles against the malicious Skeksis and help lead the proud Gelfling to victory.

Gelfling Tactics - Devise unique ways for the outmatched Gelfling to fulfill their prophecy in multi-layered, turn-based tactical combat. Units can be customized for specific fights with gear, upgradable abilities and a job system. Use guile, planning and cunning to overcome superior foes!

Highly Replayable - Replay finished battles to earn full marks or replay the entire game! Once completed, challenge New Game+ mode, keeping all progress from the first playthrough while facing more difficult versions of battles.

Rich, Dynamic Environments - The world of Thra is a living, unpredictable environment as dangerous as it is beautiful. Dynamic events on the battlefield may create opportunities or put the Gelflings at a disadvantage, necessitating rapid changes in strategy.

name: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro
detailed_description: “You’re listening to Radio August. Dark nights, with Poe and Munro…” Adventure in the strange town of August with local radio hosts and secret lovers Poe and Munro, as they encounter six unique mysteries on and off the air. Direct the banter and the action as they fend off a nightmare stalker who just won’t let go, a vengeful ghost looking for everlasting closure, a demonic painting that grants wishes - and more - but can you keep Poe and Munro together, and alive…? * Six simultaneously released, fully interactive episodes * Almost 5 hours of full screen HD video * An intuitive point and click timed hot-spot interface * Alternate endings for each episode and hundreds of branches From the developers of the award winning and Guinness World Record breaking “The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker”, “The Shapeshifting Detective” and “Murderous Muses”, Dark Nights with Poe and Munro is a standalone spin-off set before the events of The Shapeshifting Detective, with different gameplay and all new stories! FEATURES + Click disappearing hotspots to choose what happens + Explore the town of August + Talk to the locals + Help Poe and Munro escape tricky situations + Keep them alive… + And together… Starring Klemens Koehring (The Shapeshifting Detective, Sniper Elite 4) and Leah Cunard (The Shapeshifting Detective) as Poe and Munro. With a special guest appearance by Aislinn De’Ath (The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker, The Shapeshifting Detective). Guest voiceovers include Justin McElroy (The Adventure Zone, My Brother, My Brother and Me), Jesse Cox (Monster Prom, The Shapeshifting Detective), Joseph Beacham (My Time at Portia) and David Homb, star of 1995’s Phantasmagoria. short_description: Guide local radio hosts Poe and Munro through six TV-like episodes of supernatural strangeness and sizzling on-screen chemistry. From the creators of The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker and The Shapeshifting Detective.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it! This FMV turned out to be better than I thought. The story is about Poe and Munro, August local radio hosts who made their first appearance in D'Avekki other game  In this game, they took the lead of six different episodes. You'll learn about some mysteries in August town and you'll have the choice of either calling the police or investigate the case yourself. Both Poe and Munro have different opinions, it's up to you who's side you are going to take. The game is really good and each story is not connected to the other except for the first two episodes.  I liked the references to their other games, very smart.Choices really do matter in this game, I played the first episode twice and one choice changed the whole story. The good thing that you can choose to reply to the episode once you've finished it to experience the other endings. Now what I didn't like about the game that once you get to choose something, you need to use logic, there is no written choices, only an indicator that you can choose this thing (if you dislike timers, you can freeze the choices from the main menu)There are some funny moments in the game, as well as suspense, depends on your choices of course. Most of the episodes based on supernatural activities. You can take those strange phone calls or just hung up on them and play some music. I enjoyed every episode thoroughly, the cast did an amazing job, it felt like watching a movie, this also could be something some people will dislike as the interaction and involvement in the game is quite minimum.   Pros:+Good cast and very-well acting.+invistigation detective style.+Episodic game with multiple outcomes. +Good soundtracks.+Previously seen cutscene can be skipped in the second playthrough.+Steam achievements.Cons:-Choices are vague at the beginning since there are no written choices.If you enjoy FMV games you'll love this one, and if you've played The shapeshifting detective, you'll definitely enjoy this one. I'm going to give a big thumb up for Munro's outfit choices!
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro is a story focused game about the hosts of a late night radio show in a small English town, where you’ll watch live action video clips and occasionally make choices which can influence how the story plays out.I usually enjoy games like this (for example Life is Strange or the various Telltale games), but unfortunately I can’t recommend Poe and Munro. The acting is fine, not great, but I’ve seen worse on some of SyFy’s TV shows. I liked the interactions between the main characters. Sadly its not enough to overcome the game’s other flaws.The game contains six short stories which aren’t connected to each other in any meaningful way. As each episode only lasts around 20-30 minutes (combined total of all 6 episodes is around 2.5 hours), they all feel incomplete, ending with unresolved plot threads. Supporting characters appear for a couple of scenes and then are never seen again.And the impact of making choices is undermined by the fact that most of the time I didn’t know what effect my choices were going to have. You just have to click on a picture of an item or a person without having any extra information. For example you’ll often have to choose between Poe or Munro, but you don’t know what each character is going to do or say after you select them.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro

_childDocuments_.review: A brisk and mysterious supernatural romp that echoes the likes of X-Files with its 6 standalone episodes. Dark Nights with Poe and Munro is a very entertaining paranormal(?) adventure that plays similarly to the likes of Until Dawn, Telltale Games or other recent FMV efforts.The production is of high quality, the acting & chemistry are superb, and the drama/comedy is very compelling. Any fans of the games that I've previously mentioned are sure to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro

_childDocuments_.review: Six stories about two radio hosts - Poe and Munro, who can find adventure on their own heads in any situation. We could already meet them in the game “Shapeshifting Detective” from the same creators, and now it's time for them to finally come to the forefront of the story. As a result, we can say for sure that they really deserved their own game. There is an incredible chemistry between Klemens Koehring and Leah Cunard, each of their dialogue, even the shortest, always carries some kind of light inside. Sharp hairpins of jokes are adjacent to incredibly warm care for each other, their very complex relationships are closely intertwined with the strange events taking place around, and all this allows each story to get its own face, which will distinguish it from others. Each episode here deserves separate words of admiration, even if everything starts at a very leisurely pace, but by the second episode, it accelerates so quickly that it is impossible to stop.Describe in detail the surprises that the creators have prepared in each episode, this spoils half the fun. This is some kind of crazy mixture of the B-movie style, supernatural, absolutely charming and appropriate wackiness in some moments, a touching love story and Edgar Allan Poe. Intersections with past games do not look far-fetched, but look just perfect, then I realized once again how much I want to return to Dr. Dekker's green sofa. Do not forget about episodic actors who, with their excellent acting, made these dark nights even more sinister. And as far as I'm always glad to see Aislinn De'Ath (and her scene with Munro made my heart beat so often that I forgot how to breathe), but from the character played by Vincent Gould, I screamed so loudly that because of this I almost fell off the ceiling. Here, literally every minor character is a little (or very much) crazy, I will remember scenes with almost all of them for a very long time.If we talk about things that not everyone may like, then this is perhaps the overall integrity of the story. Nevertheless, we have six separate stories, the decisions in each of which do not affect the subsequent ones, they are all complete and help to reveal the characters fully. The total duration of the game is 7-8 very saturated hours, the replay value of the episodes is extremely high, in each of them many interesting surprises are hidden that radically change the course of events. It is fresh, it is delicious, it is unbelievable. I want more. I WANT MORE!
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "mixed" recommendation on Steam.Although the stories aren't that great or novel, they're still pretty fun and interesting. Poe and Munro's interactions with each other pretty much carried this game. Acting and production quality are superb, just like in previous D'Avekki games.However, if you're looking for a fun game here, then you're bound to be disappointed. 3 chapters into the game, I was completely annoyed at the decision-making mechanics in the game. After I finished the 6th and last chapter, I would've never bothered with it again if it wasn't because they introduced a way to skip scenes from chapters you've already completed. I can't understand why they'd make decisions as circles on front of things that you click on a timer instead of just putting an explanation like almost every other FMV and decision-driven game out there. 2-3 sentences to choose from is far more sensible than trying to figure out in 3 seconds what happens if I click on this purse, on this door and on these digital scissors, then finding out that I was wrong about what I thought 2 of them meant.The game strongly relies on you knowing the main characters with no background given other than "Poe is eccentric and Munro is a tease and they both love each other" in the first 3 minutes. Even after having played The Shapeshifting Detective, I couldn't figure out their thought process at all so when the game tells you to choose between one or the other - meaning choosing to lean over one character's decision-making to influence what they'll do in the end - your choice is just a guess half of the time. You don't truly know them at all until you play this game, yet it still expects you to know them.Funnily enough, the best part of the game is finding and watching all the different scenes, while it's worst part is trying to find meaning in your personal choices. Do have this in mind if you're looking to get this game.I'd strongly recommend that you play The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker and The Shapeshifting Detective, specially the latter if you wish to have some background on Dark Nights' main characters and the town of August.

_childDocuments_.review: My game genre guilty pleasure has to be FMV games. Sure, there’s a high chance that it ends up being really cheesy, but that’s the charm. And when a really good FMV game releases, you just crave more. This is very true for me as my first dive into FMV games was MISSING: An Interactive Thriller. The studio has since closed, and you can’t buy the game anymore, but it was really promising and it’s a shame that only one episode was released. Since then, I have played a handful of other FMVs and I have to say FMV games coming from D’Avekki Studios are definitely at the top of my favorites list. If you have been following D’Avekki Studios, the one thing you can tell is that they’re passionate about what they do and strive to improve however they can. Their two previous games, The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker and The Shapeshifting Detective, was structured to their advantage. While other FMVs focus on action, these were more like interviews and focused more on having the characters drive the story. Even then, you can tell the improvements made between games. Their newest game has made the biggest leap yet by moving past that interview-like style.In Dark Nights with Poe and Munro we return at a familiar setting with some familiar characters. Taking place before the events of The Shapeshifting Detective, we return to the small town of August. This time around, instead of investigating a murder you follow August’s very own favorite radio co-hosts, Poe and Munro in six of their adventures. These six adventures are self contained and don’t link together other than a few references that can be spotted as well as containing supernatural elements. Without spoiling anything, Poe and Munro’s adventures will take you to dealing with a stalker in the first episode; doing a special 24 hour show to raise money for their radio broadcast in the next; investigating why children are going missing in episode three; episode four brings in a hypnotist to put Munro in a trance to relive a past life, as well as giving us a huge The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker reference; episode five starts with a call hinting about a werewolf sighting which Poe and Munro of course have to see if it’s true; and lastly a wish gone wrong. Each episode is short, as they all are short stories, which is great if you’re aiming to see all the possible routes you can take or if an episode isn’t just hitting it for you. Although, I recommend playing through all six episodes first so you can unlock the skip function.There is also another major difference. Considering that you’re making choices for what’s going to happen, rather than what you’ll say, you make choices by clicking a circle hotspot that’s hovering over the video. Each choice gives you time to decide what you want to do before it’ll just pick the default choice. For the most part, this does work well and it’s easy to get used to it in terms of knowing what it’s most likely expecting, but there are situations where it’s vague. Like when you go back to The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker where you’re choosing what you’re saying by clicking symbols rather than worded choices. There are also choices that act like QTEs that pop up, which isn’t that often. They certainly will take you by surprise though. However, these QTEs can be hard to actually click considering how small the circle is and that it follows along with whatever it’s attached to.If you’re someone that has difficulties with games that require you to pick a choice in a short timeframe, rest assured that there is an option to give you unlimited time to decide. It may seem like it didn’t do anything, but it lets the original timer go out before freezing the screen. This also applies to the QTE scenes and will give you the option to purposefully fail or succeed at it.After you finish a chapter, there is also a nice touch of being able to see the stats of how many people picked which choice. You will also get a sneak peek into what the next episode will be, which I didn’t really find necessary. After all, this game isn’t being released episodically, just using its format to tell short stories, and I’m sure most players won’t be able to stop themselves from playing most of the game in one sitting.For the acting and general camera work, I think both were pretty good. The dynamic and chemistry between Klemens Koehring and Leah Cunard (who plays Poe and Munro respectively) was the standout. It’s really believable that these two characters decided to work together, why they’re radio show is popular in August, and why they eventually start falling in love. Though, that doesn’t mean the other actors weren’t just as good. The only scenes that were laughable were most of the action scenes where Poe or Munro was supposed to hurt someone (though they did nail at least one of them where Munro kicks Poe).Despite feeling that I would have preferred if this focused on telling one story or an overarching story, Dark Nights with Poe and Munro was really enjoyable. The scenes are shot well, the dynamic between Poe and Munro is great, and most of the stories told here are interesting. This title was certainly used so the team can be more experimental compared to their previous games and it works. While there are downsides, like some choices being vague, it’s worth picking this one up. Although, I don’t recommend Dark Nights with Poe and Munro being your fist D’Avekki Studios game. While this game is technically a prequel, I recommend at least playing The Shapeshifting Detective first as it introduces you to the town and the dynamic between Poe and Munro. Also, it’s pretty obvious but if you didn’t like Poe and Munro in The Shapeshifting Detective don’t pick this one up.With that said, I can’t wait to see the future projects D’Avekki Studios has in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed The Infectious Madness of Doctor Dekker so when Dark Nights: Poe and Munro was released onto Linux I snatched it up right away. It didn’t disappoint. To my surprise it wasn’t one story but each episode is it’s own self contained story. They do reference each other a bit but could be viewed on their own. The FMV quality was great and had no issues. The stories were engaging and overall good. The acting was above average overall save a couple people. The humour was top notch and my favourite part. One of my only gripes was that the choices you are presented with are often not obvious. Sometimes I had no idea what each of the choices meant or what decision they would render. It took an episode or more to get any kind of handle on things. For instance sometimes when you can pick Poe or Monroe it is because that’s whose perspective you will be following for the next few scenes but I only know that by experience not because the game explained it well. I think adding text to the choices would have made things clearer. I also found the ending to the final episode to be a bit rushed but maybe that was due to my choices.	I played Dark Nights on Linux. It never crashed on me and I didn’t encounter any bugs. There were options for vsync; triple buffering; and a 25 FPS lock. There was only one save slot. There was no save option present but the game may have saved on exit. I played an episode through before exiting just to be safe. Alt-Tab didn’t work. You can pause the game at any time.Game Engine: UnityGraphics API: OpenGLDisk Space Used: 6.17 GBGPU Usage: 2-19 %VRAM Usage: 482-565 MBCPU Usage: 3-12 %RAM Usage: 3.2-4.1 GBFrame Rate: 86-144 FPS	Overall I enjoyed my time with the game. Each episode felt a little quick but was able to tell an interesting story anyway. If you enjoy FMV games or the developer’s previous work you should find some fun here. I finished all six episodes in two hours and thirty minutes. It felt a bit quick but nothing too bad. I paid $13.04 CAD for the game and felt that was fair. _childDocuments_.review: Dark Nights with Poe and Munro could have been a good game, if only it weren't completely random.Between one video and another we will find ourselves having to click on points, this is the "choice" left to the player. But this choice is random. There is no way to know what will happen when clicking on a point nor is there a particular reason to do so.I can't understand why the developers omitted the description forcing the player to click randomly. No sense.Imagine a pic where you have to click/choose a torch or a sofa.If you choose the torch, the door opens, a yellow dragon enters and starts dancing.If you choose the sofa, the scene where you take the newspaper and kill a mosquito begins, the neighbor starts to get angry and you break through the wall.Can you see any correlation in these examples (not from the game)? Well, there is no correlation in the game. No choice.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it. It's a must if you enjoyed their other games (Dr Dekker, Shapeshifting Detective) - you'll also see some of the same characters pop up and it's set in the same universe.It's got quite a few different paths, accessible by making different - albeit ambiguous - choices. It's sometimes a bit hard to figure out what clicking an option will do, but okay.Each episode is somewhat different to the others, and I replayed a couple of them to get alternative endings (3 and 6 in particular). The plot can be a bit confusing, but that's the genre.The actors have done a great job. It's all in that same over-the-top not-actually-scary style as in the other games. I like that. I hate being scared, least of all when I'm trying to relax. This is - in a nutshell - a fun and relaxing game that feels somewhere between a good TV show and a good game. As in, I do feel engaged, but not under pressure. This is a good thing! Stress is bad!There are some funny moments, too. I won't spoil them, but they're pretty good.TIP: I'd activate the pause on choices option, because I just hate making the wrong choice under pressure.

_childDocuments_.review: Find more reviews on my curator page  Dark Nights is an excellent FMV mystery game that follows Poe and Munro, the radio hosts from The Shapeshifting Detective, as they deal with crazed killers, disappearing callers, a demon librarian and more. It's got a whole cast of great characters, the situations they deal with are wild and the amount of actual content is pretty impressive once you realize that the many paths are quite different. This is a standalone game and you don't have to have any prior knowledge going in but if you've played D'Avekki's other titles, you'll be treated with myriad easter eggs and call backs that left me grinning throughout. The game's progression is episodic and presented in a pretty linear fashion with branching story paths and plenty of cause and effect. It takes about 4 hours to beat which makes it perfect to knock out in a single sitting. I've played through it twice fully and just started hunting for story bits and achievements. You can jump to the start of an episode at any time and click through conversations pretty quickly, making it easy to navigate the story in subsequent playthroughs and to hunt those achievements. In short, if you like this type of game I'd say it is certainly worth your time. If you have played D'Avekki's other games, then you really should be playing this already.

name: The Crimson Diamond
detailed_description: The Crimson Diamond is an EGA text parser mystery adventure game where you play as amateur geologist and reluctant detective Nancy Maple. Nancy is born and raised in Toronto, Canada, where she works as a clerk for the Royal Canadian Museum. She dreams of attending university to study geology and mineralogy, and she's prepared to venture into the unknown to achieve her goals! Follow Nancy as she travels north to the ghost town of Crimson, Ontario to investigate the discovery of a massive diamond in the area. Eavesdrop on conversations to learn more about the eccentric cast of characters who find themselves gathered at Crimson Lodge. Explore the lodge and its environs to evaluate the diamond claim, and maybe solve a mystery or two along the way! The Crimson Diamond is a cozy mystery that encourages reading and engaging in the story over devious arcade challenges. -------------------------------------------- If you love the old murder mystery games like the Laura Bow Mystery Series, you will enjoy this game by Julia Minamata – The Crimson Diamond. The art style will give you that sentimental feel of the first Laura Bow Mystery, The Colonel’s Bequest. If you relish the nostalgia of the ‘old games’ -- perhaps taking you back to your childhood – this game will do it for you! It has the requisite feel of an Agatha Christie novel, set in the early 20th century. It even has a parser interface, so that you can question the other characters that you meet, develop your hunches, and write your notes along the way . It’s an observational, detective-type of game, and for those who love mysteries and suspense, you should really give this game a chance. To coin an old phrase: It’s the ‘bee’s knees!’ Roberta Williams – Director & writer of The Colonel’s Bequest, co-founder of Sierra On-Line -------------------------------------------- - Explore Crimson Lodge and the surrounding wilderness - Listen and talk to a cast of characters with different personalities and motivations. - Uncover secrets, discover hidden areas, solve mysteries!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is amazing.The game is fully fleshed out and large scale in ways I simply wasn't expecting. The pixel art is extremely lush, atmospheric and detailed and is initially what grabs your attention, but beyond that the scale and depth of the characters and the story really surprised me, ending in an incredible climax where all previous details pay off in an extremely fleshed out and satisfying manner. The music also is worthy of mention, despite the game being mostly silent there are many, many incredible musical interludes that appear at just the right times in the narrative to create more drama, suspense and atmosphere when it's needed.These three elements, the art, music and story itself being all so incredibly well realised and larger scale in volume compared to what I was expecting along with how they all mesh together to create such a focused artistic vision make this a truly remarkable release.

_childDocuments_.review: One hundred and ten years after this game is set, I sat down on launch day and I played. I played until I finished the game. It was that good.I must admit, I've been following the development for a lonnnng time and eagerly awaiting the release.I was completely wrapped up in the game from start to end, running into new challenges at every turn. There were so many surprises and secrets and I can't wait to return to it and find even more.There's a stunning amount of beautifully crafted 16 colour EGA pixel art, and a gratuitous, enormous amount of dialog to explore and many interesting characters to learn about.If you're a fan of adventure games, this is really one you should check out. Julia has absolutely outdone herself. If you're reading this, wishlist or buy the game now. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone nostalgic about Sierra On-Line's adventure games, particularly titles such as The Colonel's Bequest, Space Quest III, Quest for Glory I & II, etc. - I'd strongly suggest putting this on your wishlist. The beautiful backgrounds and sprites, the masterful use of the extremely limited EGA colour palette, the soundtrack...It's incredible, playing this is like going back in time, but with a refreshing twist. The text parser is massively updated, there's an options menu for adjusting many UI and gameplay features- it's impressive how streamlined this feels whilst sticking to the classic interface of yesteryear.However, as a faithful invocation of the SCI engine of the late 1980's - the quality-of-life improvements this game brings to the table may seem quite bland for those unfamiliar with its limitations. Modernized features such as a tutorial, a (mostly) point-and-click interface, event-based auto-saving, and less pixel hunting- these newfangled additions make the experience feel up to date, but in a way that might be overlooked by newcomers to this style of adventure game. This isn't a bad thing at all, if anything, it’s a much-needed improvement that’s exciting to see implemented. Well, at least in the same sense of finding an undiscovered sequel or spin-off to a beloved franchise can feel; the game very much plays like one that Sierra worked on but ditched for whatever reasons before they switched over to SCI1.Bucking against the trend of Sierra orthodoxy, the game comes with a built-in hintbook! Instead of being nickel and dimed to solve seemingly impossible puzzles like back in the day, we're given a fair chance once we're stumped. The pacing and flow of the story so far seems logical enough that I hopefully won't have to check it that often, but I'm glad it's still there. Codename: ICEMAN could have used that feature, but at that stage I'm ranting about a game made by Jim Walls, the guy who promised an exciting franchise of espionage thrillers after that came out, and gave us Blue Force instead, but I digress.Anyway, so far this title is really interesting both stylistically and narrative-wise. The attention to detail is nothing short of captivating, plus the story is intriguing enough to have me wanting to come back for more.Definitely consider picking this up if you're into DOS games or adventure games in general!
_childDocuments_.name: The Crimson Diamond

_childDocuments_.review: (Full in-depth review below this section)The Crimson Diamond is, without any doubt, paying homage to what I will argue is one of Sierra’s finest works in their contributions to the point-and-click adventure genre, that being the fantastic ‘The Colonel’s Bequest’ originally released in October of 1989 which is coming up for it’s 35th anniversary at that!Evidently the sole developer behind this most intriguing indie, Julia Minamata, decided that it has been too long since we were blessed with a game as charming as The Colonel’s Bequest and made it her goal to set out a vision for what’s essentially carrying the ‘spirit’ of Sierra’s first entry into their Laura Bow duology as there’s a lot go into detail concerning the game’s story, graphics and gameplay alongside other relevant factors to anyone curious about this title.To start off though, The Crimson Diamond has you play the role of Nancy Maple, a novice geologist who has been thrust into the mysterious and meticulous world of detective work, as it takes place in the province of Ontario over in Canada, certainly a rather intriguing part of the world that isn’t covered nearly as much as other regions of the globe such as Japan, the United States and Europe to name a few!Although I won’t go into any particular details (given the game is still brand new as of the publishing of this review) of The Crimson Diamond, I do quite like how it doesn’t take place on just the one night like how The Colonel’s Bequest does, instead taking place over the course of several days alongside having the unique angle from a geologist that plays a central role in the narrative and overall plot of The Crimson Diamond.It could be argued that perhaps some of the dialogue is a little ‘lackluster’, although the same could be said of The Colonel’s Bequest given that the banter and style of conversations often reminded me of Sierra’s own work, which I can only take as a sign of Julia having done her homework with keeping the spirit of the Sierra game’s intriguing commentary seen in the Laura Bow games alive and well here with her own indie game inspired by their works! What originally caught my eye when first hearing about this indie from OneShortEye’s video on The Colonel’s Bequest  (highly recommend his channel by the way!) was the faithful adaption of the 16-colour EGA graphics from the original as The Crimson Diamond beautifully captures the beautiful and illuminating atmosphere that is pleasing to the eyes even when you consider look at it from the lens of a modern ‘hyperrealism’ gamer in today’s era!Given just how gorgeous some of the cutscenes are from what was inspired by The Colonel’s Bequest, it’s a good thing too that Julia took some steps forward with presenting the game with some extra-needed changes as, alongside the cutscenes themselves being more animated, there exists other improvements such as various buildings/doors that become transparent whenever Nancy is moving behind them to help the player with keeping a track of where she is alongside plenty of close examinations revealing detailed item descriptions that only help to aid the player in immersing themselves into the world carefully built here!It should also be noted that, although the graphics themselves can be perceived to be ‘dated’ compared to today’s triple-A games, one should not underestimate the value in a game’s aesthetics as this can easily become timeless when it is executed well, something I am happy to report that this indie easily excels in!Regardless of how one may perceive the story and graphics of The Crimson Diamond, ultimately for some it is the gameplay that truly makes or breaks whether it is worth buying in their eyes.Seeing as this game’s inspiration makes it quite the tall order compared to arguably any other Sierra title, with how The Colonel’s Bequest made great use of a hidden ‘timer’ of sorts that would advance whenever you triggered specific events in one of many rooms of the mansion you inhibited and explored both inside and the grounds outside throughout the course of a from 7PM to 2AM in various acts that would indicate how far you are into the story, however with the beauty of many optional and interesting moments that would easily be lost to first-time players and thus encourage a second, more thorough, playthrough to learn more about the game as well as to perhaps gain a better ending too! (Not to mention that ‘Sleuth-o-meter’, with how devilishly hard it was to get the prestigious 100% ‘Super Sleuth’ rank at the end!)Going ahead with this then, what does The Crimson Diamond do to distinguish itself from it’s inspiration as well as how it perhaps improves upon the formula as well?No doubt the immediate gameplay improvement that stood out to me are the notifications of opportunities to listen into conversations as well as Nancy herself giving subtle hints on certain goals to give the player some form of direction on where to go or giving them an idea on how to accomplish their current task, albeit this isn’t always the case from what I’ve noted.Although it also helps that the ‘Notes’ section does act as a fairly reliable guide on what you are meant to be doing, given that it will note in asterisks what you must accomplish alongside any optional goals and points of interest as far as any evidence-chasing goes, certainly a handy feature that I wish was in The Colonel’s Bequest!Worst-case scenario, should all of the above prove insufficient in helping you out on how to proceed, there's a handy ‘hintbook’ via the game menu that has various hints in increasingly-helpful manners that allows anyone who is legitimately stuck to choose how much help they want, whether it be just a subtle hint to point them in the right direction or to just be outright told in specific instructions on how to get the task done!I will say though that, as odd as it may sound for me to put this forward as a criticism, the reduced amount of deaths compared to most Sierra games is a tad disappointing as these are where some of Sierra’s best humorous and witty moments come from, often creating many a fond (if not funny or perhaps frustrating!) moment for many in the genre here though, to give Julia credit here, there are still some moments of danger where you may not expect it, so it is possibly more of a personal nitpick on my side here than anything else.The Crimson Diamond sets out to create a fascinating adventure of intrigue and mystery for it's players to enjoy, and I would heavily argue that it largely succeeds in doing just that! Seeing as I've always enjoyed the prospect of a good and exciting adventure that has a certain kind of 'atmosphere' that many later adventure games simply lack in today's modern era of gaming, I can respect Julia Minamata for dedicating the time necessary to craft such a memorable adventure and, short as it may be, it is one that I will be remembering quite fondly for years to come!

_childDocuments_.review: The page itself and many other reviews talk plenty about this being a throwback and love letter, and it is, but I think focusing overmuch on that is doing a disservice to how delightful this game is. This is a passion project made over several years using old stylings, certainly, but modern conveniences and evolution in storytelling. As much as I love the old Laura Bow mysteries, there's a real empathy for the characters in The Crimson Diamond that wasn't really as present in them, as well as an insistence on solutions and clues being more sensible. The adventure game puzzle magic is present, but I never found myself rolling my eyes at a solution. The text parser feels a lot more like it listens to you, too, not making things overly simple but if you have an idea, there's enough flexibility in the language it can process that you'll find a way.The graphics and music are downright gorgeous too. This is a game that feels delightful to look at, and the soundtrack in any given area or event flows perfectly for an experience where you're likely to take your time contemplating the scene. For a game with tense investigations, it's simultaneously soothing to be inside.There's plenty to love about old Sierra adventure games. But don't feel like you have to have childhood memories of those to have a great time with The Crimson Diamond. This is a game that stands on its own two feet.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like retro adventure games, beautiful pixel art, relaxing gameplay, and Agatha Christie-esque mysteries, then you'll like  is an amazing game for folks that resonate with the  adventure game niche. If you remember fondly the EGA Text Parser games of Sierra On-Line, especially , then  will feel like walking right back into those days, but with a bunch of modern QoL improvements that make the infamously stubborn and obtuse Text Parser style feel both easy and intuitive. After getting used to the keyboard shortcuts and shorthand commands, as well as a very detailed library of synonyms, you'll forget the old days of "Guess the verb and noun the game wants you to use" of yesteryear.That said, the game  a text parser adventure game that closely follows the conventions of SCI games of the late '80s, so if you don't want to read or type, or if investigation and a slow, methodical pace aren't for you, then this isn't your game.The game itself is beautiful and makes the absolute best of the EGA palette, the story is well-written, fun, a little bit spooky, and the puzzles are challenging but never resort to "moon logic" to require you to find your way through. It definitely feels like you're meant to experience the story, instead of satisfying some designer's Sphynx-like riddles.Julia is a good friend of mine, and I was playing  during its development, contributing feedback and bug reports during beta. Julia is also a co-host on our YouTube Channel, Level 0 NPCs, where we are playing TCD.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. Caution: this game is not for everyone! You better be aware what kind of game this is and not downloading it at random or you might be disappointed.It is a game developed by a single person, who is an artist and not a game developer and she did this game because she is passionnate about old school pixel art. This game is an hommage to very old school games like "The Colonel's Bequest" or "Mortville Manor". If you played and enjoyed these games 20 or 30 years ago, you will probably really enjoy Crimson Diamond as the nostalgia is real. The game is not perfect and has some minor flaws, but is really enjoyable if you like this kind of games. This game is a detective game where you play by using a text parser. At the end of your investigation you must confirm what you discovered by answering some questions. And the game will tell you how well you managed to investigate with a point system. After my first playthrough I got around 60% of the points. I really want to get to 100% by myself, without looking online for a solution. I will keep playing it to discover what I missed.I would also suggest you try not to "cheat" and try to solve the mystery by yourself, not looking at a walkthrough.Basically, play it like if you were in 1989 with no internet connection (and no other games to play as soon as you are stuck).Congratulations to Julia Minamata for this wonderful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really good you guys, it's really good.If you grew up on Sierra games like I did, or are curious what "retro" adventure games were like in the late eighties early nineties, then this game is for you. The Crimson Diamond really captures the spirit of those games.Although I love point and click games, there was something special about the text input of those classic games that was lost when Sierra also adopted the point and click interface. A Je ne sais quoi. I really enjoyed experiencing that feeling again, that maybe anything might happen if only I found the right words.Solid game, fun puzzles, good story, beautiful music and graphics.It's really good you guys, it's really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I won't waste your time explaining that this is a spiritual successor to "The Colonel's Bequest" and stuff and there will be no spoilers. Let me just say that this is good game mostly for two reasons. Julia Minamata understands what made Colonel's Bequest a good game and eleborates on that (that is the first reason) and she also understands what was missing or underwhelming in "The Colonel's Bequest" and corrected these "mistakes" in her game (that is the second reason). I always found interaction with the characters in TCB disappointingly limited. I wanted to talk about stuff! Now I can finally do that. Thank you! I feel way more competent and powerful in "The Crimson Diamond" than I did in TCB. In this regard the game is not just an homage but a wise improvement over the original. If you are a fan of TCB you should play it. Just one tiny thing bothered me so far: The music in the intro is way too upbeat for the scenes. I understand that it references the roaring 20s and its dance halls but I just does not fit the mood.Edit: The game runs on Steam Deck out of the box. No changes needed. SInce the game is centered on a text parser it is more fun to play with a bluetooth keyboard. But (for some reason) the save states are not shared between the Steam Deck installation and the PC installation. But I don't know if that is even supposed to be different.Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: The Crimson Diamond is a phenomenal game!I never played any of the games that inspired this one, so there was very little nostalgia involved when playing it in my case, and I think this is probably as good of a first experience playing a text parser one could have.The game clues you in on what to do without giving anything away, and feels very fair while also being a good challenge. It never felt condescending or harsh.It's hard to get proper stuck with no idea what to do, and if you reach the end having missed something interesting you can get a little hint and go back with a new goal. It's generous with synonyms and I probably had to retype prompts more often due to misspellings than due to not using the right phrasing. And even then most of the words I needed to know were mentioned either in the notebook or elsewhere in the scene.You really get to feel clever a lot in this game. A few puzzles I figured out before I needed to which was fun, and the more challenging ones were incredibly satisfying to finally untangle.The plot and mysteries are very intriguing, and the reveals are satisfying, the writing in general is very good. The art is fantastic and the music is too. Even without nostalgia goggles, the fact that both are very accurate to games of a certain time, genre and hardware makes the whole experience feel very consistent and unified.You should play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Everything you want in an 80s/90s-style adventure game, great spiritual sequel to The Colonel's Bequest. Would not hesitate to believe Sierra actually made it. Thick with detail and a great unexpected storyline focusing on lots of interesting stuff. Filled with things you can miss and lots of variations on the endings. Absolutely spectacular tbh ngl.

_childDocuments_.review: Just look at my image on Steam and you *know* you're hearing from a fan of the Laura Bow series, so that is *very much* the perspective of this review:But this game is freaking awesome. It hits *all* the right notes for those nostalgic for the Colonel's Bequest-era of Sierra gaming, and has something extra for those who know Dagger of Amon Ra too (thank you THANK YOU for letting me ).As per that era of gaming, there are a few irritations (having to both 'look at' and 'examine' as separate interactions always slipped my mind back in the day), but almost all of those have been nicely covered by auto-save and other similar functions.I was waiting for this game for a few years, and it's *exactly* what I'd hoped it would be.
