_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - It'll be obvious if you actually manage to read my full review but I really enjoyed the game.  The characters are engaging, the backstory is interesting, I love the aesthetic and the gameplay is fun.  The gameplay stays interesting thanks to: I haven't played long enough for the story to resolve itself as of yet but so far it's interesting enough for me to be getting into it.  A spoiler-free summary of how it starts to follow:The setting is a bleak Cyberpunk post-apocalyptic world (though not in the traditional sense) where most facets of day to day life are run by a mega corporation and stars a couple vigilante hackers making ends meet through... less than legal tasks.  Things heat up when the main character's father has something the mega-corp wants so they start going after him (and you, by association).  Aside from that, there's lots of world-building by the sheer number of NPCs who litter each town area.  I'm also a fan of the writing in the game.  The way the characters refer to the cataclysmic event that changed the world, the slang they use, it all feels natural somehow.This is where the game really shines.  The battle system is fun and fairly deep, but not overly complicated.  It involves hacking (melee), as well as three types of software (spells) that work like Rock/Paper/Scissors (or Fire/Water/Grass if you prefer).  The cool part about the software is not only do they level up as you use them à la Final Fantasy 2, but you can change them out as you see fit.  New software can be purchased in shops, and if you find yourself ill-equipped during a battle, you can take a turn to defend and swap out your software as-needed.  You also unlock the equivalent of limit breaks, which are also typed and level up the same way.  You have a limited amount of RAM for software, but that can be upgraded as you go along, either with permanent upgrades or with hardware.In addition to the software, you can customize your build with different types of hardware, which can increase the amount of RAM for software, give counter attacks, reveal weaknesses, increase stats, auto-cast software, increase software effectiveness and much more.  Hardware space is also limited, so this is another area where you can try to make your character well-rounded or customize based on the situation.  If you like to see numbers go up, or being able to max out everything possible, you'll like the battle system.There are other minor quality of life things such as frequent auto-saves meaning no backtracking after a death, the ability to tweak the random encounter frequency and (possibly the thing I'd like to see in future games the most out of EVERYTHING here) the   As many NPCs as there are in this game, that is a HUGE quality of life upgrade for me.  Their text tends to change after each major (or sometimes minor) event, but you can tell whether or not they have anything new to say, just by running past them.  No more talking to everyone over and over again just because you want to see if they have anything new to say.  I truly hope this becomes a new standard because I love it.There are side quests scattered about as well but so far they're mostly fetch quests or Link's Awakening style 'Get the thing to give to the guy to get the thing for the other guy' quests, so time will tell on those.OK, so I'm no graphics snob but this feels like pixel art done right.  It's not aiming for any particular retro aesthetic that I can tell, but if I had to slot it somewhere I'd say it's 32-bit'ish?  In my opinion what really makes it look smooth is the animation.  Everything feels alive thanks to the fluid animations, whether you're wandering around town or in combat, characters (and some background/foreground elements) are always moving, keeping things interesting.  Character portraits also do that thing where they convey emotions based on the portrait chosen, which is always a nice touch.Admittedly this is another area I don't care about much unless it's bad but the music and sound are unoffensive.  The victory music is a bop as it should be, the town theme is pretty chill, the battle music is decent enough (but not something I'll be humming to myself later).  Overall the music is good enough and I think fits the game well, but is neither offensive nor outstanding for me.  I do like how the music gets muffled slightly in the menu though.  Those are the little touches that are all over this game.  As for the sound, all the bleeps and bloops are just as you'd expect them to be, from the menu sounds to the attacks and text scrolls. Having taken my time and done everything I could see to do, I spent a comfortable 8 hours on the game.  I definitely would've enjoyed more but at the same time it was very lean and (aside from a couple optional fetch side quests) never felt padded for time.  Decide whether or not it's worth it for you but I absolutely recommend checking it out when time/budget/backlog allows! _childDocuments_.review: As an RPG, Jack Move is "just fine", but it overall suffers a bit under the illusion of choice and the slow gameplay. In a cyberpunk world, you play as Noa who is trying to rescue her dad from an evil research corporation.Let's start with some of the good points: the game's pixel art looks really good overall, the soundtrack fits the mood and the game tries to hammer home the vibe of "gritty data-driven Cyberpunk future" mostly with success.The main problem lies in the game's progression and gameplay. This is an RPG with randomized battles - not my favorite, but luckily you can actually set the rate of encounters yourself or even deactivate them altogether, which I absolutely love. More RPGs should have that option. I don't always want to have to fight random battles if I don't want to.The battles themselves are relatively straightfoward, maybe even too much so. There are a lot of different abilities you can buy and learn, but most of them aren't really that useful - all you need is the strongest ability of whatever your enemy is weak to (there are 4 different types of damage) and then go to town. Inflicting status effects is mostly pointless in random battles and most bosses are immune to them. Also, every ability you equip takes up RAM slots, which is dumb, because it means you can only equip 4 or 5 strong abilities at a time. You can switch them out in battle, which is cool, but it takes up turns and that means you will take damage, which can quickly kill you later in the game. It's an interesting system, but not executed that well. You also have strong JACK MOVE abilities that charge up over time, and while they are animated well, there are only 4 of them and don't really make the battles any more tactical.Similarly, there is a Cache ability that lets you defend and then attack two turns in a row, which is useful against bosses, but later bosses can randomly attack twice when it's on cooldown, and it's very possible to die to a random ability you did not see coming. Your attacks can also randomly miss, which is frustrating. The balance of the game, all things considered, is okay until the last two bosses, which represent a huge difficulty bump which means you need to grind a lot, which isn't fun because the battle system is too slow and animations can't be skipped. The final boss is especially annoying, but you can cheese it and there is also an option that allows you to instantly win a battle, which after a few tries I resorted to as I did not feel like grinding for an hour or two. Aside from the final bosses, though, most battles are just slow, but not really dangerous, and boss battles take way too long for how non-threatening they are (until the end, anyway). They are HP sponges in the worst way.Overall, I think Jack Move suffers a bit from being too simple even for a short RPG. Most of the abilities are pointless, the side quests are mostly pointless as they give you items you can buy very cheaply anyway, there are only three equipment slots and a lot of useless equipment you would never use - there is so much choice in this game, but 90 % of it is absolutely pointless. And even only using the strong abilities, the final bosses are still a pain in the rear, requiring quite a few retries, grinding or cheesing, whereas the previous bosses and enemies are almost too easy. And while I do like the Cyberpunk aesthetic of Jack Move, I really do, it leans way too hard into pointless lingo that doesn't even make sense in-universe as far as language goes, and that translates to the combat too. It's an admirable effort and I don't hate it entirely, but especially the ending is a bit too grindy with how slow the battles are, and the game before was okay, but mostly boring as it just revolves around spamming your strongest abilities that enemies are weak to over and over. For a budget RPG, that may be sufficient, but overall I don't think I can recommend it. On a big sale, it might still be worth checking out, but I do think you can get better RPG's for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move had me very interested since I tried its demo before release. I can't deny that it was mostly because of its pixel art aesthetics, which boasts fluid animations and a very noticeable charisma, but it also picked my interest from the JRPG side, with its turn-based combat, endearing characters and a story fit to the setting. It's a game I had high hopes for, and it didn't betray my expectations, but I must say that while I think it's great, it left me unsatisfied in terms of duration, and I was left with a great desire to continue in its little world.The story puts us in the role of Noa, a hacker who performs various tasks with her partner, Ryder. But between one of her jobs, she receives a call for help from her father, and gets involved in a conspiracy bigger than she would believe. She must then take on the troops of the Mono-Mind mega-corp, rescue her father, and try to stop them from getting his research in the process. While it has it's own approach, the plot is fairly usual and classic, though it fulfills its goal of entertaining of course.Gameplay is split between exploration and combat, nothing out of the ordinary. The former is the weakest part of the game in my opinion, as the maps are quite short and with no nooks and crannies to investigate, with a few chests and side quests scattered around. This makes for a fairly linear experience, especially since there aren't that many areas in the game for anything else. As we travel through the areas, we'll have a danger meter that indicates how likely a random confrontation with enemies is. If the bar fills up, we will enter combat.I want to add that in the options you can change the frequency of encounters, from many to completely null; although the game itself does not recommend it, of course, because then we may not have enough level for some of the mandatory fights, like a boss for example. There are also other options like defeating enemies in one hit, but I didn't really touch this section much, I didn't feel it was necessary, nor did the enemies overwhelm me so much for it. It's clear that it's for those who want to enjoy just the story, plain and simple.The combat, on the other hand, is quite entertaining and with an interesting touch. The game is turn-based, each unit will have its moment to act, and we'll see it reflected on screen with a row of icons, both of enemies and our own. Some actions can affect the order of the turns, such as defending ourselves or using a speed ability, which can get us out of trouble, but enemies can slow us down, too.As for attacks, they can be of three different elements: Wetware, Electroware, and Cyberware; and each one is effective and weak against another, as in any power triangle. What gives it a twist, is that we'll have Hardware modules (passives, like more health or attack) and RAM, which basically runs our Software (the skills). We'll have limited RAM slots, and let me tell you right now that you cannot have all the skills equipped at the same time, at no point in the game.That's why we'll have to change Software on the fly, depending on which enemies we have in front of us and what their weaknesses are, usually hinted by their colors. This generates an interesting dynamic, since in a fight we may change "builds" several times, so to speak, and using defense and turn order strategically is what makes combat more fun.To culminate, we will also have the Jack Moves, special moves that affect all enemies, and that will be unlocked as the plot progresses. When we use them, we are presented with a sequence of commands to press, and hitting the right buttons increases the strength of our attack. Performing the perfect sequence will cause a devastating effect, and they also look very cool.All in all, it's a short game but it has very good fundamentals, and I liked it a lot. The art is exquisite, the animations and character design left me charmed, along with the catchy soundtrack that accompanies a story that, although predictable, is entertaining. The combat was what amused me the most along with the plot, and while the exploration felt a bit lacking, it may be because I was way too invested in the game's setting, and simply wanted more and more. I am left wanting more, but who knows, I'm keeping my fingers crossed for a possible sequel!

through the steam new release page and found this.this game is very pretty and stylized however the main mechanics of the game is lackluster at best.i will be using terms like magic in place of whatever the game says it is because this game is effectively a rpgmaker game with a coat of paint, which there is nothing wrong with but it makes these terms interchangeable to me and makes me compare to all other rpgmaker games.for overworld exploration there is only 1 major hub area and a couple of areas you unlock to spend maybe 15 to 45 minutes in depending if its a sidequest location or mainquest location. a majority of side quests in this game give you an item for another sidequest to complete a chain and at the end of the chain you get a piece of equipment that serves as a _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I recommend it as I would an action movie based on a book. It's fine for what it is and I got what I thought it would be from the trailer, albeit still a tinge of regret and disappointment that there wasn't more depth in the systems, story, and length.As other reviewers have pointed out, this game is short. I managed to achieve all side "objectives" and the main story in around 7 hours due to the relatively easy difficulty. The story is average, the combat is average, and the writing is average. There are no typos, but there are those typical quirky/cringe-worthy sentences here and there.. either through translation or through inexperience. The music and pixel art are quite nice for the setting and it does just leap off the screen with quality animations throughout. The UI is bright and utilitarian. You'll definitely want to play this game with a controller.In terms of the core gameplay; which is what really matters - my advice would be to give the demo a try and if you like it; then expect another few hours of the same. Make sure to buy this on sale because there is no replayability and no randomness. You can't have different builds and there are no choices to be made. It is entirely linear. In terms of target demographic, Jack Move is clearly trying to aim for the folks who remember fondly the SNES rpgs of old. This includes those simple switch 'puzzles' in dungeons and the typical turn based fight/block/item battle system. The addition of being able to buy/swap new skills at first made me think it was going to be more complex than it ended up being. The addition of swapping out skills to target enemy weaknesses really only comes into play during boss fights - and really only the last one.One additional note: Despite the colorful saturated art style; I would not recommend the game for children as there are topics around death and a scene where people are shot in a pixel art graphical style that has blood.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I'm gonna start this off with the main question: Is this worth the asking price? And the answer to that question is: Yes, but only just barely.Pros:Cons:All in all it's a solid game, but the in-game systems were a major pain point for me. There was so much potential with it that just wasn't realized due to the way they limited how many skills could be equipped at once, especially given how many options for skills you acquire.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just baffling. The story is mediocre, doesn't really have a point and just rushes through everything, so let's just disregard that. Talking about the gameplay there isn't anything particularly good either, you have four types of attacks which may or may not be super effective against enemies, you need a special upgrade to know except in some obvious cases and that's it. Now, the main caveat: What the actual ♥♥♥♥ is wrong with the encounter rate, every two steps there's one. Worse, you actually need to keep the encounter rate like this to have a chance to keep up with the recommended level for bosses. Topping everything off, this "recommended level" isn't even real, since once you reach the last two bosses they gain the ability to oneshot you at the recommended level (21) with some attacks. After trudging through the 5/6ish hours the game offers I just turned on insta win mode for the final boss. My only other option was grinding levels so I'd have more health than the oneshot attack and I wasn't down to do that with the incredibly slow XP gain rates. Also worth noting, after a certain point your attacks seem to have a higher chance of missing for whatever reason. It's rather frustrating spending half your turns doing nothing while the boss pummels a third of your health off. Oh well, at least I got this for cheap in a bundle. If you wanna kill 5 hours in a pretty frustrating manner buy this, if you want actual fun maybe get a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me wish there was a neutral option for reviews. There is nothing I would call bad, there just isn't nearly enough content to be worth the asking price. I would say definitely get it bundled or wait for a sale.Gameplay itself is good, I didn't run into any bugs, glitches, or other such issues. The menus are functional and not clunky. It has a decent story, nothing spectacular but it isn't bad by any means, it's just very short and doesn't leave anything to the imagination. The game is very linear, there is nothing to really dig into or expand the story, there is nothing hidden to be discovered, and no secret areas. It is also very short, I 100% completed it in about 8.5 hours. There are sidequests but they usually just reward you with a few healing items, and don't actually add anything to the game, though some of the quests themselves are amusing.The mechanics are actually fun at first and on the surface it looks like there are a lot of options...until you realize it's not actually making good use of them. There's what could be a really good weakness/resistance system set up with a limited number of skills you can equip at one time to make you think about what you want to do. Couple this with a really nice system where you can skip a turn to swap out one equipped skill for another during combat if you discover your current loadout is a bad fit, and a set of super attacks called "jack moves" that work similar to limit breaks from various final fantasy titles.Unfortunately you will almost never need to do any of this because everything has an easily identifiable weakness and areas have a majority of enemies weak to one type of damage. All you will ever need to do is equip an AOE damage skill that hits the most prevalent weakness of that area, a heal skill, and maybe a resistance buffing skill of whatever type of damage the majority of enemies in an area use if you are for some reason underleveled. Jack moves are basically a free trash clear skill when the meter is charged, and an easy way of depleting most of a boss's HP if not outright OHKOing them. That is the entire combat system in a nutshell. Skills (including jack moves) level up by using them, and this only serves to pad playtime. That 8.5 hours it took me to 100% complete the game would have been more like 6.5 if I hadn't also maxed out most of the skills.This pattern continues until the final boss. Mild spoilers ahead. This wouldn't be a bad thing at all if the rest of the game wasn't basically "use one or two AOE skills per fight to clear trash, use jack move to kill boss, repeat in next area". Suddenly having an enemy that is more equal to you is jarring because the rest of the game has been very simple without needing to actually think about anything beyond whether you bought enough MP restore items.Or you could just say "hell with it" and use the built-in kill enemies cheat and not have to worry about it. Yeah, the game has built in cheats. Make of that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the story and the content.  The final boss fight was fun and involved.  Considering I one-shot all normal mobs, and some bosses, it was nice to have to actually execute some strategy for the final fight.The game uses an elemental-esque system, which is ultimately paper-rock-scissors.  That's fine.  I will say the spread of elements could use a bit better balance.  There's really not a lot that's weak to "cyber" out there, for instance.  It seems like I got a lot more use out of Wetware and uh... well shoot, I forgot the other one.  I'm getting old.Where I think the game is weakest is in terms of quantity of content.  Most of the dungeons are very, very short, for example.  Two or three screens, tops.  Some of the later ones had a lot more effort put into them, which was fun.The next weakest point I think is in terms of balancing.  I mentioned above that I was one-shotting trash mobs and some bosses.  This is because leveling up is exceptionally potent, and the max level is fairly low and easy to reach with a bit of grinding.  By the time the final dungeon came around, I had hundreds of consumables for restoring health and data, and hundreds of thousands of credits leftover.  I would've had to try in order to fail.That said, as mentioned at the beginning, I enjoyed the story and the characters.  It was nice having a strong female lead that still managed to have character flaws and tenderness.  A lot of efforts these days create strong "female" leads by making them act like male leads, and this game didn't do that.  They also managed to not inject present day politics into the characters or plots, which was also welcome.  We get enough of that in our day to day lives without it invading our hobbies.The only thing I found actively annoying was not being able to press up in the main battle menu to go more directly to some of the options at the bottom of the list.  It seemed to me it was only that one menu like that, whereas all the other battle menus allowed you to skip to the bottom by pressing "up" on the first option.I didn't experience any bugs, and the game never crashed for me.If the developer is working on a sequel, or a successor, I would just advise increasing the quantity of content, putting a larger enemy variety into the game, and, well, just doing "more" with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has some good elements to it, a very glaring lack of content holds it back in terms of overall quality and value.Characters (2.5/10):The protagonist and deuteragonist of  have reasonable aspirations and reasonably develop over time. Unfortunately, the antagonist feels mostly flat, and the "twist" near the end that reveals their motives feels forced and out of nowhere. The central characters in general just don't have much personality to them; the only one with any form of compelling personality is the protagonist's uncle, who is just a side character.Gameplay (1/10):There is little challenge or creativity in the gameplay of , which just repackages the typical turn-based RPG gameplay into a Cyberpunk-colored paper bag. The boss fights feel boring, with the final boss feeling like it was given inflated stats just to stretch out the play time. Its RAM system, while interesting in concept, is awkward and clunky in practice. It puts a limit on the number of skills that you can take into a fight; then, if you want to change skills during a fight, you must waste a turn doing so. To add salt to the wound, there is essentially zero side content for those who are disappointed with the main game.Art (5.5/10):The art and music in this game is passable. The different game areas are very well designed and look very good, but I could probably count the number of pixels that made up each of the characters on one hand. The skill and attack animations are generic and become boring to look at after a while. The music is typical electronic-cyberpunk game music and adds almost nothing to the overall experience; perhaps the most irritating thing is that during the final fight, it cuts to silence, which made the final fight even more agonizingly slow-feeling.Story (4/10):This is the only element of  that has any measure of quality, and in all honesty the plot is pretty decent for what it is. It follows a young woman who lives in a ghetto area trying to put up resistance the monopoly that rules over her life. Unfortunately, due to the somewhat lacking personality of the antagonist, the story isn't as compelling as it could be. Additionally, despite the many mentions of various other cities that exist in this world, we can never go there, and it just feels like wasted potential.Overall,  is a fairly disappointing game, especially for its price tag. Perhaps in future there will be more updates to flesh out the game, but as of writing this review, it feels more like a rushed sketch rather than anything complete.Final Score: 13/40 (Bad)

_childDocuments_.review: Slick, svelte, and stylish, Jack Move condenses a pulpy cyberpunk story into a fun (if occasionally uneven) adventure. It excels at presentation - vibrant pixel art and head-bobbing tunes in particular - and it creates dynamite atmosphere and setting. The turn-based combat is definitely engaging, but an uneven difficulty curve made it difficult for me to know how much tinkering I needed to do before the challenge of battles suddenly spiked. This is more forgivable thanks to the ability to turn off random encounters and the relatively short length of the game - you can get past your frustration long enough to make it to the next chapter.Still, I would come back for a second game from this publisher. They have a gameplay foundation that they can build on and unimpeachable style, so I look forward to whatever else the team does next!

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fun and easy to follow, but it lacks build-in/suspense to make it more interesting. The characters are okay and personally i like Uncle Quin. However, it suffers from 1-dimensional antagonist while the main characters (Noa and Ryder) could be better with longer backstory and character development.Jack Move has great pixel graphic and satisfying animation during combat, especially skill/special skill animation. Although personally i wish the game also has cinematic video on certain part of the story since the store page has cinematic trailer.Good enough to emphasize game atmosphere/story setting and there are few OST which i like.Mixed bags. While there are feature to change frequency of random encounter and instantly kill all enemy (AKA cheat), decent amount grinding is required if you don't plan to cheat. I got bored quickly grinding through random encounter, so i use cheat halfway (with exception of boss and special enemy). The combat mechanics itself is mediocre, where i feel some of those is just sci-fi/cyberpunk reskin of general RPG game mechanics and you need to grind level of  skill/special seperately by using it on combat.None. In addition, the game works well on Linux with Proton 7.0-6.If i were to make a comparison, Jack Move would be similar to average Sci-fi/Action Hollywood movie. It's fun to  play, but doesn't leave much impression and there's nothing outstanding. If Steam were to offer "Neutral" option, i would choose that option rather than "Yes" or "Recommended". _childDocuments_.review: This is a very small scale RPG, everything about it on the small side really, from the combat to the story and overall length.It plays like most any other turn based game, with an action bar at the top of the screen. enemies have weaknesses to exploit, you can buff yourself and debuff enemies, all very standard stuff. The primary areas where this game excels is in its art and music. The pixel art is excellent, while the areas to move around look fine, both the noa and the enemies you fight in combat and the npcs walking the look and animate great, the only knock on the art would be the extreme reuse/recolour of enemies. And while i don't think every track is an earworm, even the worst music in the game works to set a mood or tone. The primary problems i have with the game are its simplicity in combat and the turn economy. Almost every fight can be won by just spamming whatever attack the enemy is weak to, and while that is the basis to most RPGs it feels more egregious here, you do have buffs, debuffs, etc to use in battle but you dont need to use them 90% of the time, and they only come into play during boss fights. Which is where my other problem, the turn economy is. Your party is only ever one character, Noa, so you only get one turn every batch of enemy turns, unless you guard and get two turns in a row, this leads to a lot of tedium, your first few moves in a boss fight will be to buff up and debuff the boss, then you slowly go onto spamming the boss weakness like regular fight, being slowly interrupted to either heal, or somewhat more inconsistently, re apply buffs and remove debuffs etc. This whole cycle for boss fight causes them to take so much longer than they would be fun to fight, its mostly just tedious, and the only real way they raise difficulty in the game is to just dump tons of HP only later bosses.Also, while I do mostly like the writing and characters, it does come of as trying to be a bit to cute and it does feel somewhat cliche.Ultimately I do recommend this game as I think its mostly cool and interesting and I like to support these types of things, but do go into it expecting a pretty stripped down game, but again its also very short so it doesn't really out stay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Final Fantasy had a cyberpunk baby with none other than Megaman: Battle network... That game turned out to be Jack Move.Take on the role of Noa, as she takes runs to pay the bills in Bright town, a post-apocalyptic cyberpunk city where reality is a weird spectrum. After the Monominds attack your flat looking for something, so begins your adventure... Your father, Abner the scientist, gets kidnapped and then it becomes clearer that Krall, the madwoman that's out to get you, is just a pawn in a bigger scheme.The game is a final-fantasy clone with some of the most memorable battles I've seen yet... This game should've been a cult classic, but I can't help but wonder why this never happened. You get Data, or as all of you RPG kids would say, Mana, that you can use to EXECUTE software... or as all of you RPG kids would call it, Magic! You can also equip Noa with hardware, or as yall would call it, equipment (lol). Thing is, to equip software you'd need RAM, and in late game, you would only be able to equip a bunch of softwares, and then there are Jack Moves, ultimates that cost a meter that charges as you whack the mechanical nutjobs that are after you. The battle system is amazingly done, and this pixel art is incredible, with the most satisfying moments is when you input the correct code to execute your Jack Move. Nothing more telling of a game than a green wormhole that swallows your enemies whole lol. All in all, Jack Move, from the writing, to the graphics to the gameplay, is a  amazing experience... And instead of cussing, Noa just says "PLUG IT"... I can't tell you how much I'm in love with the whole atmosphere of this game. Well done, devs, well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Just the type of turn-based pixel art game I needed! The pixel animation overall was so pleasing to the eyes, and the battles were a lot of fun! I love that we were given an option to turn off or raise the encounters so that we can grind or just concentrate on the puzzles to the game. Story wise was alright, nothing too amazing, but I enjoyed all of the characters as well as the little interactions with the NPCs. This game definitely made me miss turn base RPG style games, and for the price this game is absolutely worth your time! Hoping to see more from this team; thanks for the great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move has an interesting setting and the pixel animations are pretty good. But its a been there, done that kind of story and has characters that you don't fully connect with. The game-play has some interesting ideas with equipment customization and the jack move, but isn't showcased well because of the lack of overall difficulty. The main challenges you'll get from the game is staying under-leveled and most of the time making battles last artificially longer. The game could've also used more side content which would add to the length. Despite being short, this game has some interesting ideas and a sequel has very good potential. However as it is now this feels more like a demo for a sequel and I can only recommend it at a sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This is an *okay* game in the "walk around and get interrupted by final fantasy style numbers-battles" genre.First, a positive thing, I liked the "defend" mechanism, where it acts as a defend *and* defers your turn, so (unlike most games in the genre) the defend action is actually useful because you can prevent some damage without giving anything up except a bit of precedence, whereas most of the genre has defend take up your whole turn which makes it totally pointless.The story is okay, and I appreciate the config option for "just appear the text don't make me wait for it to appear one character at a time."Unfortunately, the game makes up for that positive by having unskippable overlong combat animations, which you'll be forced to sit through a lot of times. Another config option for 4x combat animation speed, or making the animations skippable, or something like that would have been enough to make this review a soft-recommend rather than a medium-unrecommend.The other annoying thing is the final battle is *so* much harder than everything leading up to it, almost enough to require going back and grinding for more levels - which you kind of can't do, once you reach the final battle you can only go back a short distance, you *could* grind there but it would be extremely boring. The final boss one-hit-killed me a bunch of times, and also sometimes takes a double-turn which makes even a not-quite-one-hit-kill still result in you lose if the actions are unfortunately aligned.I eventually figured out that rejecting the debuff before the big attacks was a bigger "defend" action than doing an actual defend through the attack - but again, because of the occasional two actions in a row, there's a possibility you won't get that chance.Also in the negative column, there are a few sidequests but they mostly just get you an item that you could have just bought anyway, and don't even give you any XP - if they gave XP then maybe I'd have been a high enough level at the end that the final battle wouldn't have seemed like it needed some grinding!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Not a very long game (took me almost 14 hours to complete the whole game at max level) yet super nice! Jack Move gave me a lovely RPG experience. Loved the combat system and the story too. The characters are way too intriguing and Noa is a super funny yet tough hacker, nice and very well designed.If you love Cyberpunk style games and pixel art games this one is a deal you must have!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine. I don't think it is worth the money but you may expect different value. The game has about 2 hours of interesting content. I played for 4 hours before I the repetition caused me to lose interest. This game is very deceiving. The game play loop is tight. The story is fine. The graphics are pleasant and the sound is adequate. You start playing and you think; I kind of like this. The problem is there is just not enough here. I don't mean the story is short, though it is. I mean after 90 minutes you have seen everything the game has. After 3-4 hours you have every upgrade and figured everything out. At this point it is just a mediocre story and extremely repetitive game play.I it is a love letter to antiquated jrpg systems that should be left in the past. Endless random encounters. Boss battles with huge HPs.  Nothing is hard. In fact it is really easy to win. It just take a lot of times to kill the "hard" bosses. The game is 90% padding and 10% content. Not worth the ~8$ bucks I spent to get it on sale. Not worth my time to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a special kind of awful. The game has a difficulty problem in that it can't figure out if it wants to be easy or ball-bustingly hard, and then sometimes just takes the cheap route for the harder parts such as just having enemies or attacks that can one-shot you just kind of out of the blue (such as when you guard a hit from the final boss and it does more damage than your max health despite earlier instances of that attack not doing that unguarded and with decreased resistances thanks to the boss). The story is, while short and advertised as such, just really awful in that it feels very 'meandery' and pointless. Dad is kidnapped, go save, needless family drama somewhat involved, and then the final act is go save friend, which that takes up the last like hour or two of gameplay. There's traces of something good here, had the game been longer with better development and fixed difficulty to at least be consistent I could see myself enjoying it a lot more. Despite having like 6 hours of game time I can barely remember anything interesting actually happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: 8h Without accessibility options/ 3h with accessibility options 1/10 1 You don't need a guide No No, they are all story related No No No No No No, you can turn the battles off and still unlock all the achievements as they are all story related NoJack Move is the type of RPG I'm more interested in the older I get. Not only does it respect your time and doesn't add hours and hours of filler content/grinding, but it also tells an interesting story that never gets boring because the game doesn't take that long to finish. The story is different than most RPGs, it takes place in a cyberpunk future where AI stuff has become very big and the difference between the poor and the rich is huge. It reminds me a bit of the Dutch Young Adult book "Slaap Zacht, Johnny Idaho" by Auke Hulst. It seems this book hasn't been translated into English. I haven't read many cyberpunk books, so maybe that is why it just reminds me of this book. A feature Jack Move offers and what we see more and more in RPGs is that you select the option of how many monsters you'll encounter. I'm glad this has become a thing now for games with random encounters because in some areas you link to fight monsters and get experience and at other times you just want to keep moving and don't get bothered by them. The achievements are all story related. None of them is missable and I would not recommend looking them up as they will tell you a lot of spoilers.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good, but it's also really short, as RPGs go. The above time is how long it took for me to clear the game, with all side quests done.The game has the distinct feel of a "Chapter 1". The length is probably somewhat of a good thing, though, as the charm of the battle system really wears off in the final area, where several common enemies are both damage sponges and have reaaally annoying abilities.The main character is, to turn a phrase, a woman-child, who got older without growing up. So, her two forms of response to anything is either Sass, or Angry Outburst. I dunno, I'm sure that'll appeal to some, but I grew tired of it pretty quickly. Sure, she's got her own issues, as does everyone else, and I've certainly met real people like that, but that doesn't mean I enjoy spending time with them.Putting that aside, running around chatting with everyone who has new things to say, after each time the story progresses far enough is pretty fun. Conveniently, the talk icon will also let you know if you've already heard everything that person has to say at the moment. My favorite character is the uncle. It's pretty obvious someone had a lot of fun creating and animating him.Of the several side quests, there's 5 steps of the Straw Millionaire, a few treasure hunts, plus a small smattering of other things. The treasure hunts were kinda fun to find and collect, but the rewards were pretty meh. The side quests are, otherwise, worth doing for their rewards,There were a few things that could have used a more thorough explanation, for example, the attack abilities gain xp as you use them, and they max out at Lv 4, which  makes them stronger, but it's not particularly clear. There's also more advanced versions, which cost more to use, and may be more powerful than the less advanced versions at any level, but, again, it's hard to tell from their descriptions in the menu.One last thing: the achievements are all gained as you progress through the story: complete the game once and you'll have all of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Simple old school RPG, with awesome pixel art and a good storyline. The game is quite short, I've 10/10 it in about 8 hours. I do recommend it a whole lot, even as short as it is. The characters are fun, the moves are awesome and the game environment (although a bit confined) is worth discovering. Great job, dev teams! This game is rock solid!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Finally. An RPG that is actually playable.An RPG that can figure out good systems you can actually make use of without an encyclopedia. And implements the absolute BEST leveling progression I have ever seen in an RPG. This is easily the best RPG I have played this year. HIGHLY recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better RPGs I've played. The art is fantastic and the music is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: JRPG/10.Decided to give this a shot since it came with the October 2024 Humble Choice. With the main campaign (which unlocks all achievements, thank you devs) and all side quests clocking in at just over 6 hours, this is a  difficult sell at $20, and even a sale tag of $8 feels a tad overpriced. While the visuals, lighting, and sheer amount of optional npc dialogue betray decent measures of effort, the music is very conservative and the level design and story are middling at best. However, the main aspects that cause me to not recommend this game are its dialogue, which suffers from the cheap 'nonsensical geekspeak to replace profanity because cyberpunk' syndrome, and its extreme cookie-cutter adherence to its genre. When I had fun, it was due to my enjoyment of JRPGs, not anything this game did. When I felt underwhelmed, it was due to the game's refusal to innovate upon the genre.

_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Visually beautiful and entertaining 7-10 hour game, but the battle system is very lacking.I've been following this game for a while until it released. I liked it for the most part. The characters are likable and the story is entertaining. The cyberpunk setting is really interesting and the pixel art animations are absolutely beautiful. I'd recommend getting it on sale, but the pricing for the 7-10 hours of gameplay is fair i think.That being said, the game is ~really~ easy and the combat gets old real fast. The game's magic and abilities are called software, and there's 4 offensive "elements", most enemies in the game are naturally weak or resistant to one of them. You can only equip a certain amount of software at a time, so if you go into battle and don't have the type of damage the enemy is weak to, you can change your equipped software at the cost of a turn. That's where the battle system shines. Juggling between equipping different abilities to combat different scenarios feels dynamic. Unfortunately, though, the game barely uses this outside of 2 boss battles.On most areas there will be a prevalent enemy type. As long as you equip whatever ability counters them before battle, you probably won't have to change your strategy until the boss fight. This is optimal, but makes most fights really boring. Damage types have no special qualities. There is no offensive attack that can do something no other attack can. It's just different colored damage. Half the bosses can't do anything against debuffing and none can't clear your buffs. And contrary to debuffs, buffs never go away. Unless the enemy can clear their debuffs and has different weaknesses at differen't stages, every fight is pretty much the same. Pick the right colored damage, and maybe buff yourself once.Overall this game is very beautiful and a nice experience. But if the characters don't grow on you, all you're left with is a pretty bare-bones battle system.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: like concentrated JRPG; all taste and no fillers. Can be finished in less than 8 hours; has a good story, great music, fun (if a little simplstic) combat, and jaw-droppingly gorgeous pixel art. Smooth, beautiful, chunky, vibrant, clean pixel art. Does not reinvent the wheel, but is still well-worth enjoying IMO. It's honestly nice to get the JRPG fix without settling in for a 60+ hour game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a relatively short, straightforward turn-based RPG in a cyberpunk setting. Briefly, combat operates with an elemental rock-paper-scissors system and status effects (some virtually useless, and some insanely good). Your skills themselves have levels in addition to your character, but in all honesty, this is really not something you need to worry about, as you can afford upgrades by the time you'd max out a skill's levels anyway. Sidequests are inoffensive, and encounter rates can be tweaked to your preference, so points for quality of life. As far as difficulty goes, this is a pretty easy game, and there's nothing wrong with that, but I would have preferred a little more pressure from bosses to make me sweat on occasion. All in all, I had a good time with the game, and don't feel like it overstayed its welcome. I would give it a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun RPG, with a lot of beautifully expressive animations, intuitive and polished battle design, and computer-based humor. the only issue I had was that the game feels as though it should be much longer - it took me about 8.5 hrs to beat 100% with most of the "dungeons" (major areas in which you have random encounters) only lasting a couple of screens. overall, definitely give this game a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: A short but fun rpg.  Jack Move doesn't really pad out the playtime a lot: things move pretty fast, you can turn off the encounters if you want to move on from an area, and most of the areas are pretty compact, and thats ok.  You get out of the game what you want to put into it: All the townspeople constantly are changing dialogue and theres some unique interactions if you want to constantly chat them all up after each story beat and/or do all the sidequests or you can just move on and try to get thru the main storyline, maybe even as fast as possible with a low level run.  The battle mechanics start easy but get tougher later, but they are more or less always fair.  Its really advantageous to use all of your options at the right times, and your hardware setup can determine what strategy you use.My main complaint about the early experience is the extra Ram slot upgrades seem a bit bad: they start at +1 which is basically useless, and then by the time you can get the large upgrade its not really useful anymore as you have already upgraded your base slots enough and have other powerful hardware.  Later, you have a handful of options you can change out depending on what you are doing, though usually if you play smart you wont have to rely on hardware at all, so thats nice.Overall, I do wish there was more, but I did enjoy my experience just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: If you like classic JRPGs there's not much to not like here. Fun soundtrack, interesting cyberpunk futuristic setting, fun main character. Classic turn-based style combat with a limit break-esque system. The only downside is there is a single party member. You can happily support this developer if you're a fan of JRPGs and not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, like REALLY great.It's well designed; looks brilliant; soundtrack is a complete bop; combat isn't so deep that you need to start filling a note book to keep up with the strategy demands but still deep enough that you're not simply spamming the strongest attack; the story is cohesive and well thought through; the characters are relatable and avoid the usual JRPG and cyberpunk tropes, the writing is done by someone who actually knows how to write well; it's also short enough that it's not a huge time drain but long enough that you don't feel short changed.Tbh there's very little actually dislike about it. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: It was really hard to figure out whether to give Jack Move a thumbs up or down, because for the most part, despite it being a bit derivative I really enjoyed its style, theme and combat.But the further I got in the game, the more its warts began to show. A game breaking bug where you enter a menu during battle then suddenly can't exit it may force you to force quit in the middle of a fight, for example. Additionally, while the story was okay, I wouldn't say any of the characters or plot points were especially interesting.I think combat is where the game really starts to fall flat as it goes on and unfortunately why I would have a hard time recommending it. I LOVE turn based combat systems, and this one seemed solid at first - enemies have weaknesses/strengths sort of like rock paper scissors, and you can slot different hardware and software abilities to give you interesting legs up in fights.The problem is that the difficulty becomes an absolute **** show by the end of the game. A game that had previously been generally on the easy side becomes absolutely sadistic, throwing you into fights where the enemies will do so much damage in a single hit and impart so many nasty status effects that you spend 2/3 of your turns healing/debuffing and can barely attack! There's nothing more frustrating than playing this little game of healing/debuffing and barely attacking for 10-15 minutes, only for a boss to pull out a new move that decimates your health bar in one fell swoop and makes you restart from the beginning.It's a shame because about 80% of this game is a solid 8/10, but by the ending it was more like a 3, and every single moment playing was infuriating. I don't care enough about the story to grind like hell to beat the final boss here - I think I'm just done. If you can handle a lot of grinding and side questing to reach the end, you may have more fun than I did, but if what I described above sounds frustrating to you, give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I love RPGs, I love the grind of combat, I did all the side quests, I collected most of the Software and even got the upgrades to have the three Hardware slots available to use and enough RAM to have enough of the "spells" to use in combat. But at the halfway point boss where no matter how I tried to optimize, I got wiped 3 times before finally winning after doing over 30-40k damage when previous bosses were a fraction of that, at least to memory when I played through this the one time. Honestly, the combat is what lost me at that point. Some things felt bloated and I got wiped by a single mob enemy moments before the last boss, even with the high tier Software and equipped with defensive boosting Hardware. I was just so fed up I turned off the random encounters and pushed the Auto-Win Battle button for the last two bosses (oh yeah there's an Auto-Win Battle button, which I like for the sake of accessibility but it's silly that you can just choose to not do ANY boss fight with it).I enjoyed the story, I liked the characters and their writing, the setting was neat and the ending was good enough for me. But I hated that one of the core gameplay loop staples of RPGs, the combat itself, was just annoying to do and made me so fed up with it that by the end I didn't bother to even engage with it for the final bosses. I can't recommend this if you're looking for an indie RPG that has good combat to keep you engaged, but if you want a game where you can just hit a button to skip bosses and just look at the story then sure get this. But in my opinion there are better RPGs that do this a bit better.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Fun byte-sized RPG with great cyberpunk themes that remind me of some of the best parts of the Shadowrun tabletop, with an air of whimsy. Delightfully animated pixel art that brings naught but awe, and a good soundtrack, to boot. Favorite part is definitely the boss design (esp. the Final Boss). Able to use statuses on the Boss without it feeling unfair on either end, and is still a fight that takes some thought and planning due to the fun elemental system!Only downside is some of the screen transition times, between finishing a fight and returning, it can be a little long, for example, but the animations are so charming, I was never too bothered by it. Save often! Didn't overstay its welcome, and well worth the price for a tight, fun experience that uses what little time it has with you is used well and makes a mark! Great job to the dev team!

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Nothing all that innovative, but nothing really bad either. It feels a little like the vision of the game was lost somewhere in the combat system, with its whole "limited space system" being under utilized. I went through 3/4 of the game without swapping my skills at all and didn't even feel like I was missing out on anything.Story: meh. Nothing that makes me go "That feels shoehorned" but also nothing that made me say "didn't see that coming." The dialogue is quippy and felt very character informed. A shame these characters were fairly bare bones archetypes.I will say however, the world building is fantastic. It takes the perfect approach to it: if you're just here for the story and don't talk to anyone you don't need to, you won't learn much, but talk to the NPCs and you get to see Noa's relationship with her town and how the town perceives her. The game also marks people you've already talked to, and it also updates almost every npc's dialogue after major story beats.Music was good. I found myself jamming along to certain tracks, but nothing extremely memorable. However, there were times when the music got in the way of the story. For example, when Noa is all depressed that her dad died, the music is the regular theme for the area she's in, and it does not fit at all. This happens a few more times throughout the game. Even just straight up cutting the music in those scenes would have been better.The game looks great. It really leans into its cyberpunk-dystopian theme in every aspect of the art from the menus, to the enemy designs, to the world and buildings, to the characters themselves. Minor gripe: taking a character sprite's face and putting it on top of the textbox for a major character as they're typing does not count as a character portrait.The game runs great, and despite being a pixelated game, has support for all resolutions. I only encountered 3 bugs. One was that Noa's attack animations have a pretty good chance to just not go off when poison ticks. The move still resolved, but you don't see the move hit or how much damage it did. The other 2 were during the final boss. When transforming, the animations for "The Construct" transformation didn't load. Its attacks were animated, but it's idle animation never were. I didn't even know what I was fighting until it used an attack, at which point, The Construct would just be stuck on the last frame of whatever the last animation was. The other one was that I got stuck on the flying mech transformation around 75k hp or so of 99k. The boss just would not transform after that. If there was a third phase to that fight, I completely missed it.Overall, Jack Move is good. Not bad, not great just good. If you're looking for a classic NES rpg, this is your game. If not, odds are you've seen about everything in this game somewhere else before. I'd wait for it to go on sale before buying it, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a wonderful game that combines the joy of oldschool RPGs with some beautiful modern elements to create a very enjoyable experience! Carried by a story that is based in a typical cyberpunk setting, but quickly dives deep into the characters and makes you care about them, the game itself keeps you on your toes in a great way! Everything looks and sounds great. The fights are challenging and far superior to most run-of-the-mill RPGs.  While I received the game for free, I would have gladly paid full prize on this because I care much more about this then some AAA games of the same genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really good time. Great pixel art, music is pretty good though I'm not sure it's the kind of music you listen to outside of the game. Not necessarily a bad thing. Combat balancing is a weird thing. Game is a one-track mindset kind of game at the start where you just wail on the enemy with the occasional heal. Then suddenly you get to purchase any skill you want in the shop, I of coursed loved this but at the same time made me kind of sad because everything you see in the shop is everything you can get for the REST of the game. The thing I love about RPGs a lot is discovering new skills and the ways to use them, but if I'm just handed the entire list, it felt like I could just plan out my build right there in the first hour. The combat overall is fun, it's not super complex and I think if this game lasted anywhere around the 20 hour mark the combat would get extremely boring but considering the short length, it's good for what it's trying to do. Characters are fun, and the story is surprisingly engaging after a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it being a short experience, I really enjoyed a lot of aspects to this one: the style, the technical jargon in the whole game from dialogue to abilities, and some of the flexibility with some of the combat options.I was 6 hours in when I realized we might be nearing the end, and it did end, so I hope developers continue to make some cool projects, thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

Definitely worth for the asking price and good for those who want a turn based jrpg styled game and don't have 80 hours to dump into it!  The ONLY issue I have with it is that when you use the install function in battle, if you accidentally go into the tutorial in it, then you're seemingly stuck and have to restart the game, but that's really a minor thing that's from my own habits of trying to press 'start' to exit menus, lol!  BUY IT TODAY

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game at full price since buying it on sale and hearing/seeing how amazing the game's audio & animations are, feels like stealing from the So Romantic devs.The worldbuilding through narrative design and naming things natively is done really well, as well as adding a social & political layer to the gameworld by means of modern-day cult mockery, comedy & hypocracyI highly recommend it, the game's presentation & gameplay are AAA-indie and after just one hour in, I'm totally sold this game is worth going through a full playthrough
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: TL DR: solid (6.5-7)/10 but in laymen's term I say for the price of around 20 bucks CAD and avg 8 hours, worth buying and playing. Though there are issues.ReviewFor the story, nowadays I don't expect RPGs to suddenly break new grounds, this is a story we easily understand and have seen but it's about execution. What is frustrating is that I love the look of the game and the locations because it feels like there is so much to learn but the story never goes all out or fulfils the expectations. Sometimes it seems like its going to do that but then it stops or pulls back preventing a full emotional connection/release. Its fine but that's exactly it, its just fine. Too short as well. They could have done so much more.CharactersThey are..fine =)The Main characters are at least and the final villain.Again feels though we could have really explored all of them but we get surface level characterisation but the game won't go deeper. Which is a shame cause I like the design but the game stays pixelated even for cutscenes so we can't enjoy it fully. Hopefully the sequel does them justice if there is one.MusicThis is where it gets tricky for me to judge. For me story, music and visuals make the game (gameplay too obviously butthese 3 are important to me). Now based on the size of the game in terms of story which determines the different areasand battles, I understand why there aren't too many diverse tracks but the tracks do exist while I understand why they soundthey way they do, it doesn't wow me. They are fine to listen to while playing the game, but I won't be listening to them outside of it. I would say most will get bored of the battle theme and the town theme possibly.Basically don't expect much.GameplayHahaha this is easy and hard to explain. BattlesThere is a rock paper scissor dynamic for both offence and defence. Actually there is technically 4 elements so I don't know what game that signifies.You have 2 sets of skills (may not be the right word): Software and HardwareSoftware are skills that can be switched in the middle of the battle and outside to an extent and Hardware can only be set outside the battle so there is room for strategy but I will be honest, other than the final boss, I very rarely swapped during battle. This is more a nitpick but gameplay is more advanced then required ironically for this game. Its so easy to overpower regular battles that once you have a setup going, I doubt you will do much.You can buy more skills at shops of course and you definitely will.Software skills can level up but don't pay too much attention to it as I could never tell how much more powerful they got.I didn't see a tutorial but some stats are not obviously named. Like a speed buff in this game is called overclock so just figure out that stuff on your own.In any case, like any RPG this will be more subjective. For me, I found it fun and enjoyable but kinda brain dead. I rarely used buffs and debuffs until final boss. But that is kinda what RPGs end up being lol.OverworldSomething really nice this game has is the ability to toggle encounter rates allowing for exploration for any sort of reason. So A+ addition there.There are sidequests but not too many, they are generally worth doing but not much stood out for me. There is also no indicator that certain NPCs will give sidequests so you will have to talk to everyone.While the toggle for encounters exist, I do wish there was fast travel from one location to another.The other npcs of this world are actually fun to talk too, some have relations with the MC so they have fun conversations. And after certain events, the dialogue will change so it keeps that fresh.Final thoughtsSo based on all the above, you may be thinking that my score should be lower but I am used to being devil's advocate. I did genuinely have fun playing this but I will admit I probably won't replay it anytime soon or even later. Especially since there is no new game+. My recommendation, if you still think 20ish $ CAD is too much, wait for a sale, and play once. While there are better RPGs out there, I don't regret buying and playing this.Please let me know if I miss talking about anything or didn't talk enough about something.I hope this review aided you in some way.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game (minus the visuals) is either poor or serviceable. I genuinely have no idea how anyone can recommend this game (hell, even the recent most helpful reviews are pretty negative themselves).Let's talk about the visuals. It's gorgeous and the game knows it. That's why they make you sit through the slow-playing animations with every single action. It makes completing a battle take considerably longer than it should. The battles also take way too long to load for some reason (longer than instantaneous is way too long for a jrpg).Let's talk about the RPG/battle mechanics. They are very very simple. So simple in fact that they don't even bother to give you detailed statistics for the most part. How much damage does this do? More. How much do you heal? A little. What's the hit chance? Bugger do I know. What do these attributes do and how do they scale? I don't know, just don't care about it, the game is incredibly easy (on the hardest difficulty) anyway. There's not enough dynamism in the turn-based combat for it to be interesting either. An example (this is indicative of the majority of my playthrough and what got me to uninstall) is the second boss. After finishing the first phase (which was just punching the right console 3 times in a row), the fight turned into the boss does the same move, which always hits 2x35 damage, I retaliate with my wetware skill (what is wetware? How do I know if an enemy is weak to wetware intuitively? lol, don't ask) and rinse and repeat until I'm low on mana or health. If I'm low on health, I heal myself. If I'm low on mana, I use a mana potion. Continue this for a couple minutes as there are no dynamic elements nor could I have played that fight more optimally. Regular battles play out the same way but instead of doing a specific skill that an enemy is weak to, (also since there's no way to intuit that imo from enemy design/name) you just use a skill you want to use to level that skill up (skills level up by using them in battle). The dialogue is a kinda cute (although gets a little grating as the game goes on) as so much dialogue has turned into "technology references". I think something that sucks actually "vacuums" and something cool is actually "coolant", or at least that's the level of dialogue we're dealing with. At least if you do decide to play the game, the game only lasts ~6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 40 minutes of game play up if you want to get an idea: I got this as part of a turn-based game bundle. First impressions: kinda light action with fun combat abilities. The game runs about 8 hours to beat on average. I liked the characters, they are not just some flimsy cliche NPC, they actually are kind of empathetic and likable.  Environments look great without being too cluttered--love the pixel art graphics. If you're looking for something kind of satisfying without too much tension, Jack Move has some really nice ideas for its genre. Skipping ahead in let's plays and press images, I think the game stays consistent but nails the cyberpunk genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it feels very harsh to throw a not recommended since my feelings are more mixed than anything else. The game is too short for its own good, a vast majority of equips feel pointless by the time you reach the shop, the basic attack is entirely useless and the same goes for all physical moves IMO, battles are a little too slow for how many random encounters you face. Now that the criticisms are out of the way some of the positives are the beautiful pixel art, the environments, enemy design, the music, the story (although a tad cheesy) and the general cohesiveness of the experience. If they make a sequel to this game, I hope it clocks in at about 10 hrs since that feels like a good spot for a shorter RPG. I would also like for them to expand on the world they have already crafted and ditch the random encounters for something more concrete to help immerse the player in the world like how chrono trigger handles them.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: The only bad thing about this game is that it may leave you wanting more. Everything is polished, the music is good, and the combat well done. However, you could beat the game in 6-7 hours. This is good because there isn't any wasted space or padding for playtime, but regrettable because you'll want more content on the characters and in the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a nice blend of classical turn based rpg gameplay with some modern quality of life rpg features which allow the player to adjust the experience to their own preferences. The characters and the world they inhabit are brought to life by the excellent pixel art and animations. They story is enjoyable although it will leave most players wishing that it had been longer. I really enjoyed the game from its beginning to its conclusion and can see myself replaying it from time to time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I got it off Humble Choice. I feel like the current rating in the 70's is just a little low. Is it the most fantastic revolutionary RPG ever? No. But I enjoyed it all the way through. If I'd paid full price for it, I'd be perfectly happy with the purchase. It's obvious that the developers cared a lot about what they were making. There are some complaints about it being grindy, which wasn't exactly my experience. It actually made me want to grind a good bit at certain points just because I was enjoying the combat, figuring out the best hardware/software build, and levelling things up, so I spent a good bit of the early parts of the game on hype mode (more enemies), and then backed it off to the default mode once things started getting too easy. I finished the game reaching max level a few rooms before the end, and the last boss wasn't too threatening, though it was a long fight.If I could change one little thing, I think it'd be cool if the rhythm game mechanic for the jack moves got a little more complex as they levelled up, just adding some more arrows, and making that be where the extra power comes from.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very beautiful, has an interesting story (on paper) and is about the perfect length for a bite size RPG. The problem is that the only meaningful gameplay it has is the combat, which is about as deep as a puddle on the sidewalk. There is an equipment (called hardware) in the game that automatically scans each enemy, telling you their HP and weakness automatically during a fight. This equipment had to be locked to level 15 (in a game where the highest equipment lock is 20, and the recommended level to start the endgame is 21) because getting access to it earlier completely trivializes the rock paper scissors combat mechanic. There are a whole host of stat up and down powers for the different elements and stats avalible in the shop, none of which are more useful than just hitting the weakest enemy with your biggest fireball because the action economy is completely tilted against you if there's more than one opponent. The game also has 3 attacks for each element, and that's it. It's a shame because in the first hour or two Jack Move shows a lot of promise. I don't think there's any replay value at all however, and I think if you've played a single JRPG in your life, you've seen everything Jack Move has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, short JRPG style game. Took me about 5 hours from beginning to final boss, and a little extra to do the small amount of side content. The combat mechanics feel good, and they're explored decently well -- the last leg of the game especially rewards engaging with all that the combat system has to offer. I ended up focusing on a build that was extremely risk-reward heavy, and the experience either involved destroying everything basically instantly or making boss battles more engaging rather than slow and plodding. The script is a little corny (there are toooons of tech-related puns; think Cyberpunk 2077 dialed up to 11, and then add a few more on top), but it got a chuckle out of me, and it made me feel An Emotion a couple of times, so that was good, too. This game has appropriate accessibility options -- there's an "autowin" button for battles, you can modify the frequency of random encounters, and the only kind of attack that requires specific button inputs can be automated. I do wish there was a run button for overworld traversal, but it didn't make my experience measurably worse by not having one.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good cyberpunk-themed indie JRPG/SRPG. It's relatively short—6 to 10 hours—so it's perfect if you don't have a lot of time to play all those giant RPGs these days. You play as Noa Solares, a young hacker who pays her bills by stealing corporate secrets. When her father gets kidnapped, Noa goes on a quest to rescue him and unravel corporate secrets along the way. The story is decent and nicely condensed, with little to no filler.There are a bunch of open-area hubs that are fully explorable, with some side quests sprinkled in each of them. Combat relies on random encounters; it's a turn-based system with the classic HP/SP formula. There's a decent variety of skills to learn and use, split into four damage types. There are also very powerful ultimate skills that you need to charge up called "Jack Moves," hence the title. The game also offers a few accessibility and difficulty settings; if you just want to enjoy the story, you can turn off all enemy encounters and get a "kill everyone in 1 hit" option during combat. If you need more challenge or faster leveling, you can also increase the number of random encounters. Overall, it's definitely worth checking out, and I had a ton of fun in Jack Move!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of problems from the get go.The main problem of this game's on its Story and Duration. I finished the whole game in 5.4 hours without taking into account the 30 minutes I spent taking a massive dump while this game is on. The game is relatively short specially considering its price. It is a literary mess in terms of its plot. we are introduced to a world where a lot is happening and nothing is explained. Main casts are built in stereotypes which is not bad per se, but all of their development and explanation for their characters usually comes in a form of exposition dump between conversations of said character. The stakes of the story are presented in the same manner, making it less of a threat and more of a hollow urgency. The writing struggles to set its tone as it bounces back and forth between dialogues with serious connotation implied by having pretentious sci-fi jargon, and cringy, but bearable jokes.The Battle system is designed like a common JRPG with a pinch of variety when it comes to customizing and the mini-game for the special moves. The difficulty of this game adequate for people who are not accustomed to JRPG battle systems, but it is a breeze for people who play JRPGs regularly. Enemy variety is not an issue for the game and it is surprisingly abundant considering the game's runtime. The battles became repetitive in the latter part of the game, but it could be neglected as the battle system of the game does not overstay its welcome given that the whole game can be finished in 5 hours xdd. Puzzles are non-existent in this game which is a letdown since games like this could use puzzles to make the game interesting and maybe stretch out the playtime of this game xdd.The music in this game however, absolutely SLAPS. it really compliments the retro vibe that the game is set on. and the details in area and character designs are noticeable. This game has encapsulates the oppression and social hierarchy present in the game by using the environment as its leverage. Though the game falls flat on setting its tone in its writing, it succeeded in developing the disparity between the villain and protagonists through its design.Overall it is a short and bitter experience. I know that the development is an indie company composed of few people. The game could be great if they have addressed the said problems, and I think this is a significant milestone for the developers, but I cannot justify its price for the experience that I have considering that you can also buy outstanding games for the same price.5/10 I hope that the devs release a free expansion or an update for this game. It felt like the ending of chapter 1, rather than the ending of the whole game.
