_childDocuments_.review: For a game that boasts of a unique and gritty story, it's bland. It doesn't help that I've seen the same story beats done better elsewhere in different mediums such as films and books. I'm not asking for something completely never seen before but I do want some effort if you're going to brag. And they should hire someone else to write the dialog because I didn't think the relationship between Uncle Guin and Noa was anywhere close to reality. None of my uncles ever called me favorite like that unless it was my favorite blah blah. The only thing that felt believable was the slang and even then some of it was a bit much for my tastes.The gameplay is fun the first few hours but drags on after that. No auto battle but there's an option for a perfect jack move along with an autowin but that's hidden in the option menu at the title screen. It's rather irritating that I had to look for it when it could have been available during the game at any time that I wished. If the game devs make a sequel then they should take notes from Ikenfell which had ease of accessibility options during gameplay. And cut down on the grind to level up abilities and to progress past the next boss. Also, more memorable boss fights and mook battles with less copy and past enemies would be awesome in the sequel when there is one.Graphics are serviceable for what the game's price tag indicates. If you're expecting gorgeous pixel art then look elsewhere. The current sale price of 7.99 USD is asking too much for a game that I beat in five hours.  The curious and the desperate to play it should wait for the price to go down. Otherwise, they're wasting their money on a game that has very little replay value and there's better games out there that give you more for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move captures that cyberpunk aesthetic and delivers it in a fast, punchy and mechanically easy to understand rpg experience that's a joy to play through. One of my concerns going in was that it'd lean too heavily into the trappings of cyberpunk as a genre, but what it gives us is a tight cast of characters that range from easily detestable to immensely enjoyable, like Uncle Guin. Noa encapsulates being the spunky female lead tomboy without being insufferable, and leads with a massive amount of charm and heart, enhanced by how she interacts with characters close to her. If a diligent player talks to NPCs between events, you'll slowly piece together micro-stories that gives us backstories for some NPCs to have the world feel properly inhabited, but without it feeling needlessly bloated or without meaning. Combat is stylish, fast, and punchy - although if I had one complaint, it's easy to overpower and remove all challenge from the game so if you want a fair run, then don't increase the encounter rate too high. Boss fights and mobs have personality, even if some of palette/move swaps in parts. I haven't finished this game as of writing this, but the journey so far has been immersive, entertaining, and definitely a joy to play so I'd highly recommend it to people seeking to scratch a turn-based affair in the trappings of a cyberpunk world. The amount of polish to the environments and detail to sprites, interiors, and combat is slick, and a treat for fans who miss the days of jrpg sprite work.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, it seemed like it was designed for me. A Cyberpunk theme, eye catching pixel art, cool looking main character and an interesting battle mechanic. However, the game is just bad. Pros: ART:Stunning pixel art and a fairly novel battle system. I'm aware that even the pixel art is a little divisive but it really hits the mark for my taste. Cons: Everything else. Cons In Depth: AUDIO: The music is nice but not great and definitely not great on repeat. At this point I've only played about 30 minutes and it's already getting grating. STORY/CHARACTERS: This is the largest barrier for me. The writing is just bad. It feels like the writer had an agenda or point to make and a group of characters in mind and just chose to make a game around them rather than making an interesting game world and wanting to add interesting elements into it. The dialogue is full of edgy ribbing between almost all people you interact with but it feels like it's written by someone who's never actually had friends, or at the very least friends that interact like this so it feels unnatural. If the dialogue doesn't include unnecessary sarcasm then it's probably a really bad pun, usually about hacking. As a Brit, I love sarcasm and puns, just not these. As for the agenda that feels somewhat rammed in, definitely a ham-fisted approach rather than subtle commentary. Keeping in mind I've only played 30 minutes, barely past the tutorial, I already know the writer hates landlords, dislikes the idea of chivalry, traditional masculinity and the "damsel" story trope. The way you discover the latter by the way is when your uncle who seems to own a bar/distillery gives you a free bottle of something nice as a favour to which you of course must be educated that stronk wamen don't need help. God forbid a close family member offers a kind gesture. And your best friend/colleague lost his partner, your ex colleague, who is of course gay. I'm going to try a little more of the game. I truly want to enjoy this as it's so close to being something I'd want to play. If this story was in an action adventure or something I could just skip past it. But in a RPG, all I'd be left with is random encounters.. For those who haven't already written me off as a bigot, I hate the fact I now have to add context to this bit. But I don't hate the idea of inclusion. That's great. As mentioned above, one of the things that grabbed my attention when judging a book by its cover as it were, is the cool looking main character. What I hate is the fact people seem to have lost the art of subtle writing. Some of my favourite games have a diverse cast and interesting story themes around it, but they're good because you often learn these things through context and further exploration. A good example would be Bill from the Last of Us 1 where you go through a bunch of dialogue and side missions for Bill and never need to consider where he likes to insert his member. It's in a funny piece of dialogue later on that perfectly fits the dynamic of the Joel and Ellie's relationship that you learn more about Bill if you're paying attention. Not look it's Bob, Bob's gay! Yay Bob.

_childDocuments_.review: i'll just say now that this game isn't doing anything inherently wrong. visually its very good! particularly in the animation department, very smooth. the overworld has the ambience set well, and there were times where i really got invested in the world. the game isn't long and you can have a good time with it, but..this game's price is significantly higher than other indies i've played lately.This is rarely something i'd harp on about at all, if the product is solid, i'm willing to part with whats asked within reason. i love the art and am happy to support the creators of the game, but it only exasperates some gripes i have with the game itself.this game is a great art piece, but an inoffensive video game at best.Despite what i said about the game being short, it still feels like it wastes your time.Battles are fairly standard turn-based affairs with a turn order mechanic present that works fine. here's my main problem with combat.. it's slow. despite what i said before about the animations being excellent, fluid weighty movements, they take time, to the point where it actually felt like a detriment. Couple this with some really long encounters that have far too much hp for how surface level the combat actually is, and you lose interest pretty quickly..on the topic of losing interest.The story lacks a hook. gameplay is rarely the standout feature for short, top down rpgs. it's always a careful blend of solid storytelling with all the other factors that makes video games (plus a little innovation). Jack Move's story isn't bad per se, its just not interesting. there's some fun characters and great designs, but it failed to hold my interest for very long at all, the setting itself of a cyberpunky pixel art city was doing most of the heavy lifting but that only goes so far.The music is fine. tonally consistent and fits the setting, somewhat unmemorable perhaps but its there to serve the setting mainly.tldr: i can't in good faith recommend the game at full-price for what is offered when i can think of over a dozen titles with similar gameplay formats for roughly half the price. The game never does anything to earn that price point, everything within the game works fine, its just too basic from a mechanical level. the prime selling point are the visuals, theyre solid.overall a 5/10 game from my own perspective. thanks for reading.

There is no greater depth to the mechanics of the game other than having the correct spell to one-shot the enemy until late game where enemies become far too tanky to one-shot. Late-game enemies either have a ridiculous amount of HP or have some status effect that halves your damage so you're stuck being unable to flee from a battle trying to whittle down these enemies you're fighting for the 5th time in the same room as random encounters are overbearingly frequent. The bosses are just as bland typically having 1-3 moves,  playing like a regular enemy but with 20x the HP. The final Boss has a ridiculous amount of HP and took 30 minutes of mind-numbing repetitive attacks to beat but it could easily take up to 1 hour if you didn't get certain buffing skills which you have not needed up until the late game which at the point you realise you need them the game has blocked you off from getting them. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 5th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A pixel-art cyberpunk RPG.Jack Move takes the standard RPG, puts a nice coat of cyberpunk terminology over it and lets the player loose in a short but interesting RPG. Players will go on a job to steal information from a corporation and then get embroiled in a larger story. The art is excellent; the combat has a bit of variety but is well designed, and the story is interesting so far. I even was challenged already and have actually had to continue, but that also comes with learning the battle system, and understanding I should be using those consumables instead of hoarding. The writing walks a line, and for every clever phrase or updated terminology the game has, there are a couple groaners of a line as well. Nothing that would stop you from playing, but it tries way too hard to update lingo. The challenge in the combat is good, but it also feels like once you understand the systems, and enemies’ weaknesses it’ll quickly become rather much easier. I struggled with the first boss, and the second boss I breezed through. Also, I have heard this runs about 6 to 8 hours, so it’s not a normal RPG length experience, even if it uses the typical battle system. Pick this up if you like cyberpunk or RPGs. This is a delightful combination and while it won’t last that long, that does also mean it won’t overstay its welcome. I’m a person who believes RPGs get bloated with grinding and this one doesn’t feel like it’ll fall into that same trap. _childDocuments_.review: The game is solidly ok. I got what I expected out of it. I liked the setting and characters enough. It's kinda somewhere in the middle, but there are definitely better ways to spend your time.I found myself getting bored near the latter third of the game. There just isn't a ton of strategy in the combat system. The loop of attack, attack, heal, attack, attack, heal... got pretty repetitive after a while. The game doesn't properly explain what a lot of its keywords are, and I didn't feel compelled to try them until pretty late into the game. The buffs and debuffs felt underwhelming for the most part. I also have mixed feelings about the NPC dialogue. The game keeps track of if you've exhausted all of the dialogue options for a character. Every time you progress the story, the NPCs often have more dialogue; it's kind of impressive. I felt compelled to walk around the world and look for them. There's a lot of it in this game, but most of it isn't interesting. Ultimately, I feel like exploring the world was tedious and unrewarding, which is a shame. _childDocuments_.review: It's worth $3 or less.Bog standard turn-based RPG with poor pacing, mediocre combat, and a nearly trivial difficulty curve. _childDocuments_.review: I just completed the game and, while there were a good many positives to Jack Move, in the end I can't recommend it.Let's start with the pros: the world is small but immersive, and the dialogue is top-notch. A couple minor typos [missing apostrophe here and there] and minor bugs [a simple boss attack not playing it's sound effect or displaying the damage over your character but otherwise functioning normally], but nothing that blocked my progress or ruined my enjoyment of what I did find enjoyable. The biggest pro, though, is the OST. I purchased the OST to support the dev further, despite not recommending the game.My two biggest complaints are the very short length of the game and the mind-numbing combat. This is a JRPG in it's simplest form - you have one party member, basic stats, it's turn-based, and there are no gimmicks. There are a handful of run-of-the-mill status effects [poison, def up/down, etc] and four "elements" of damage, but for the entire game except the last two bosses I followed the exact same formula and didn't have trouble with a single fight: equip your strongest three moves of each of the three elements, and your strongest healing spell. Heal when you're low on HP, use whatever element the enemy is weak to when you're high on HP, repeat. Very few of the enemies have any gimmick to them other than attacking in a specific pattern. Some buff allies, but enemies generally never lived long enough for me to care. Some debuffed or poisoned me, but...same thing. A couple enemies delayed me sometimes, and...yeah. It didn't matter. It never felt like the stakes were particularly high at any point in the game.You have the ability to switch out what moves you're equipped with in the middle of a fight at the cost of a turn, and the second-to-last boss fight is the only time I ever needed to engage with the feature. The final boss I accidentally cheesed, skipping it's entire second [of two] phases. Poison is super powerful in this game; it lasts until the fight ends or it's dispelled, and hits for a % of the afflicted's HP after they take any action. When the only truly interesting thing about every boss other than the final two is the fact that they're HP sponges, poison is unreasonably strong compared to your normal attacks. Why would you spend turns dealing 800-1200 damage when instead you could just defend and let poison deal them 3000+ damage every turn for free?Combat was further made trivial by a couple of overpowered accessories purchaseable in the shop; I kept waiting to be punished for always using my permanent auto-haste, but the only enemy that ever used the slowing effect I encountered long before I was the minimum level to equip it. That and the accessory that turns all your single-target moves into target-everyone moves [with no penalty!] made the already-easy combat an absolute bore. I turned off random encounters for the last hour of the game to make it more challenging, but it didn't help me feel any more excited about the final boss fights.Other cons are the lackluster and abrupt ending, the LGBTQ+ rep being one couple [and one of them is dead all game] in an otherwise heteronormative world, the MC's design not matching the splash are and being SUPER generic in-game, and the only real sidequests being an item-exchange-chain. This is an easy pass. I'd have refunded the game [but not the soundtrack, it slaps] if I didn't keep playing to see the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move...How do I put it...Originally I got here while looking for games similar to Anno:Mutationem, a great game I loved.Then stumbled upon this.First off.Graphics. Each animation has a lot of character and love in them. The general art style is great. (I love pixel graphics.)Some of the music tracks are pretty sweet as well.Combat is also fine but pretty simple and straightforward. So...meh I guess?But...What makes me so split on recommending it?Length. When buying a game, I usually come with the play time to price ratio of 1 hour = 1€.Jack Move fails spectactulary in that regard.I have 10 hours on record when writing this and this is all you get out of the game. And that is literally all you will get. I explored every nit and cranny of the game. A 100% playthrough. So it really isn't worth when buying it at full price.Story.The story is relatively simple about the villain trying to achieve immortality through the work of the protagonist's father, where we try to save him from the antagonist's hands. (Do note that those played the game might notice some inaccuracies with this summary, I want to keep it vague for those who didn't play it yet.)You sadly don't really get attached to the characters during that story. At least I didn't. Which likely is due to this extremely short play time, allowing for little character buildup, etc.Overworld.The game follows 2 modes.An overworld mode and combat mode.In the overworld mode you basically run around like in any other game world.When you encounter an enemy, you go into combat mode. A turn based fight with a maximum of 3 enemies vs you. The enemies and the amount is always randomly picked out of the enemy pool of this area. (You obviously will have to fight security guards in secret facilities and thugs in slums.)Why do I mention it in a reason on why it makes me not want to recommend it?Areas where you encounter enemies are very dead and empty? Why is that? Let me explain.The game has a "threat" mechanic.Every time you enter an area where enemies can be encountered, a threat meter appears. This threat meter fills up when walking around. (This can be adjusted to be very fast, normal, slow or you can disable it entirely.) Once the threat meter is full, you will encounter an enemy. That's it. You can run on an empty road for a short while and will encounter an enemy out of nowhere. This is how you encounter enemies all the time.You won't find people walking around like in other games. (Heck, even cheap RPG maker games do that better than Jack Move.) This leads to very empty and dead looking areas.Which I dislike a lot.......................To conclude.I originally wanted to recommend the game, but there are just a bunch of issues that prevents me from doing that.So Romantic put some more work into it and expanded the story, then it would be great.But they didn't. Sadly.If you get a key for free or see it being on a 50%+ sale, then I'd recommend getting it if you are into the genre the game aims for. But not at full price.Not at full price.(Do note, this review has been tagged with "Received for free" due to me receiving it as a gift from a fellow friend.)(I will not be liable for any strokes or depressions caused by spelling and gramatical errors on my side.)Have a good one.- Code : Azura

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving a thumbs up because I think the pixel art and game feel is really on point. You can tell the developers has put a lot of passion and care into making it.But on that note unless you get it on a sale I wouldn't necessarily recommend it.The game is very short, easy and mechanically shallow. The story is also much too simplistic and doesn't really do anything we haven't seen before in any other sci-fi world.Characters in the game are inconsistently written, one moment they can be really sad and depressed but seconds later they completely change their mood and vice versa. They have a really hard time making the characters feel like a driving force in the story and not just victims of circumstance.Same with side characters constantly cracking jokes and having their own little "side stories" that don't really go anywhere and are so fragmented I have to wonder why there are so many non generic npc's in the game.The gameplay has a kind of rock paper scissor dynamic aswell but it's so easy to get around that mechanic the game would largely be identical without it to be quite honest, also it only applies to the enemies. You're not weak to anything, you can simply sometimes do more damage to certain enemies.It's not even that if they are weak to something they are strong against something else, you deal natural damage unless you use the right damage type. So you don't even get punished for not engaging with the mechanic.So yeah it's a very typical RPG in the style of older Japanese RPG'S but on a  smaller scale.It might sound like I hated the game from all the negative things I have to say but I enjoyed it while playing on my Deck and I really do think the developers are going to make a lot great things in the future given the chance cause this is brimming with potential. However it's faults makes me have a hard time recommending the game despite liking it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 7/10, quite good IMO.  For the money I spent on it, everything felt clean and well tested.  I did not find any glitches or serious typos.  The techy lingo can be a bit... much.  It's far from the worst dialog I've experienced though.  Hands down I prefer even vomited up crap text dialog to the awful screechy high-pitched Japanese voices you often find in games like this.  They aggravate me to unreasonable levels.  Really, anything that isn't THAT is an improvement.  Graphics are pretty good with lots of animation frames to the sprites.  They are probably the star of the show in Jack Move.  The care that went into designing the characters allows for plenty of amusing gestures and facial expressions.  Super charming and often funny.On the technical side, spec-ing out your character has some nuance to it that goes above and beyond the typical equipment you see in turn-based RPGs.  Once you figure out how the game's system works, it can result in fun min/maxing for major fights.  On the other hand, a poorly-optimized build will generally just result in fights dragging on longer than you feel like they should rather than any of it being a deal breaker in the fight.  The only real challenge was the last battle.  Turns out I did it very wrong and it was still easy so just take that into account.  A challenge this game is not.There are minor complaints with the mechanics.  For example, there are objectively bad but expensive items that probably shouldn't exist (like the RAM SLOT upgrades that use Hardware Slots when there's an item that barely costs more and unlocks all the RAM slots permanently without using any slots) A lack of understanding at first can lead to some poor choices and wasted money/time.  There really isn't a lot to say about this one.  It took me about 6 hours to do all the side quests and main quests. There is a REALLY cool feature I wish more games would add.  If you press start, you can edit the rate of enemy encounters dynamically.  You can opt into fighting enemies every 4 steps or none at all.  What a fantastic idea!  I could hug whoever decided to do that.  If you like turn-based RPG's, Give Jack Move a shot.  It's north-of-mediocre in terms of story, graphics, and gameplay.  Sure there are lots of better games, but there are lots more worse ones so when you run out of the other good ones, Jack Move will still be ready.

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a JRPG made for the Nintendo Switch handheld gaming appliance.  It's fairly well polished and looks a lot better than an RPG Maker asset flip... but that's not saying much and the fact that's the closest comparison is a distinct problem in itself.  There's a wacky sci-fi/cyberpunk (cyberpunk is like, so hot right now) theme as you plod through a rather shallow and uninspired story doing shallow and uninspired, ultra simplistic JRPG turn based combat.  Shallow is the hallmark here.  Baldur's Gate 3, this is not. There's an overwhelming amount of mediocre Visual Novel/E-book style cutscenes in this game.  So you'll spend a huge amount of time not playing the game, but clicking through endless lines of poorly written VN text cutscenes because the developers couldn't work out how to relate their narrative through the game mechanics, and decided instead it would be better to compete with reading a book for your time.  We're here to play games, not watch hours of garbage intersituals.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.  To make matters worse, there's no mouse input, despite this being sold on PC as if it were a PC game.  This is unacceptable and somewhat insulting to PC gamers.  It's a good demonstration of the poor attitude the developer has towards PC gamers, and this attitude has resulted in yet another defect in this game.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Jack Move has the preposterous price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Rise of the Tomb Raider", "Kingdom Come Deliverance" or "Final Fantasy XIV Online" (Yeah, FFXIV or this Nintendo Switch pixelcrap! What a choice!).  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as part of a recent Humble Bundle, and honestly, I still feel a little ripped off. I'm honestly surprised this has so many positive reviews.I'll get the one positive I have about the game out of the way first - it's a nice looking game. Decent pixel art-style which fits the setting, but it soon becomes apparent that even that was skimped out on, with how quickly palette swaps become the standard enemies of the game. Even the final boss is just fighting the same bosses over and over.Now for the rest. It feels like whoever made this game had no idea how to balance it. It's a game which could really benefit from some sort of party mechanic, not a one-vs-many set up as for the majority of the game, it's a cakewalk. You'll hit about three hours in, unlock the ability to wipe out entire groups of enemies in a single move, and progress - until you hit the final dungeon and the flaws really begin to show.Enemies suddenly deal twice the damage they have been. They have no weaknesses, all get the first turn and have enough HP to tank at least two or three attacks. God forbid they use the power down move (9/10 they will), which now means combat takes twice as long.It seems this is likely the reason the ability to skip combat, and even skip entire bosses, was implemented. It really overtunes the last section of the game, where no only are bosses taking multiple turns, but now include new mechanics introduced -just- before the last boss which renders half your items obsolete (Deflekator), as being able to ward off a single subsystem attack just isn't viable. You're now spending multiple turns healing to counter the damage output, while doing small amounts of damage in return.If you want to beat the final boss, you're looking at about 90-100 turns to beat the first form. The second form, assuming like me you didn't grind, but did all content on normal encounter level, you're looking at another 90+ turns of damage dealing -alone- to beat her. It's not hard. It's tedious. Your only other choice is to grind for a couple of hours, which is also hugely slow, as despite the huge spike in enemy difficulty, the rewards they give are tiny by comparison. I've never been so glad for an I Win button, just to get through the slog and finally see the ending.Which may not have been so bad if the plot itself was anything worth fighting her for. It's a very simple, point a to point b plot. Girl has to save her father, has to save the day and evil corpo lady wants to do evil corpo things with supertech as she takes over the world. If it had remained a simple, cozy 8-9hr RPG, it wouldn't have been so bad, but really, the last two hours turn what was a fairly mindless, chill RPG into a relatively frustrating slog just as you're already starting to lose interest.Even on sale, I'd highly recommend avoiding this. Characters which aren't endearing, a plot which doesn't grip you, cringeworthy writing which is so full of quasi-scifi lingo that at points, it's illegible. Hard pass.

Of course, the actual gameplay is great too.I'd say the worst part about it is some of the dialogue wherein the writers have tried to imitate 80s/90s commercials for slang and insults... and it's just not as cute as they think it is. Otherwise the story was simple and enjoyable with some really good human moments.I think the gameplay is where this game hooked me the most. It had a very simple but enjoyable trinity of "elements" that were the core of every fight, while letting you take a turn to change what software (spells) you had installed so that you were never locked in a bad situation of elemental disadvantage. Bosses were also predictable in a good way as to reward the player for paying attention, memorizing patterns and coming up with a strategy.As a last side note: the game lets you specify the frequency of random encounters whenever you want, which goes a long way.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: It was quite a suprising game for me. Its not super long or deep storywise, but it was an overall good time.In terms of gameplay, its a simple classical turn based crpg with a combat system like earthbound and the old FF's. It works well with what it has, and doesnt try to be overcomplicated, which works in its advantage. With my time with this game, i never felt underpowered, nor had a reason to grind random encounters., as you will gain enough levels through the main story. It even has the option to turn encounters off completely.Design of characters is fine. The sprites look well made and although it is pixelart, they look quite detailed.Only real gripe i have it that the music can get grading fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a lot of fun, with an interesting graphics system and an engaging story. The game runs extremely smoothly on the LCD Steamdeck, and a playthrough without much grinding will take you about 5-6 hours if you complete the few side missions. Grinding *will* trivialize the difficulty as levels very quickly boost power and the only difficulty adjustment is encounter rate.My only criticisms, which are minor, is that you never need to use some of the things they teach you in the intro until very late in the game, and the combat system can be very repetitive in places - typical of the genre even with the somewhat innovative combat system.Definitely a worthwhile game!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: 11/10 - Amazing story and beautiful art style, recommend this game to any casual gamers.-Jack Move dazzles with its stunning pixel art style, blending retro charm with modern flair to create a visually captivating world. The detailed, expressive characters and vibrant environments immerse players in its cyberpunk universe. Paired with a gripping storyline that balances emotional depth and action, it keeps you invested from start to finish. The narrative’s themes of family, revenge, and digital warfare are compelling, making Jack Move a must-play for fans of both indie RPGs and cyberpunk adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice pixel art turn based RPG.Story:  Nothing here is going to really surprise you.  The story is decent enough however with some of the characters it feels like it could have taken a little more time to flesh out the relationships and the personalities but overall still isn't too bad.Combat:  Turn based combat that is pretty simple but still fun.  You have a lot of software, hardware and abilities that you can build your character out with through the game.  4 major damage types along with Boss Abilities called Jack Moves that you can pull out to turn the tide in battle.  It did feel a little grindy towards the end but that's really my only complaint.Overall this game isn't going to hit you with anything that's too crazy but its a solid entry a turn based RPG genre and worth the $20 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I DNF'd this game. It's a lovely small little RPG but the combat is meh and sometimes it glitches you into a menu you cannot leave. That causes you to have to restart the game, if you haven't saved in a little bit that can set you back a while. It was too much for me to take after the 5th time it happened. Dialogue was enjoyable but somewhat cringey but that might be because of a teenager character. The best part of this game has to be the music though!Overall if you're fine with a somewhat buggy title this could be great for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: First I don't feel its worth the full $20 price for a short 5-7 hour JRPG.The story is pretty common, the game play can't be compare to the bigger titles.So if you looking for top tier amazing game, this is NOT it.But really i did enjoy playing this, pixel art and cyberpunk theme. - Story cheesy, but bearable. - Game play little incomplete, but simple enough to understand and it grow on you. - Can complete the game and without spend 100+ hours.Overall i recommend for anyone who like JRPG and have few hours of free time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: As some have mentioned, it is a good introductory JRPG game because there are limited options, a linear story and a single character to handle. It is not a very in-depth game, but I’d still recommend it considering the game is pretty short and enjoyable despite its lack of depth. However, I must also mention, rather , that the game is pretty easy until the end-boss who not only shape-shifts into all the other previous bosses, but also becomes pretty much invulnerable to all but one random attack type for a fair bit of the fight, unnecessarily lengthening the encounter so much so that you may even need to reload a few times unless you’ve enough HP to tank repeated double blows from the boss – including ultimate attacks about every four turns – and/or have brought a huge stockpile of health/data boosters.There is a ‘software’ that allows you to see vulnerabilities, but you have limited RAM slots – and must take three ‘elemental’ attacks for a well-rounded deck – and have only space for one extra buff, etc., making it a difficult choice. You are expected to install-uninstall software during the final fight to keep rotating what is useful at the moment, but I read about a game-breaking bug about that and decided not to risk it (not sure if the bug has been fixed).There are many side quests which you discover by talking to NPCs, but the handy icon to distinguish between which NPCs you’ve already talked to resets after every major plot point, forcing you to talk to everyone again and again or put off the side quests until the point of no return, which is clearly mentioned in-game. The side-quest rewards are also largely useless and won't make you stronger. Also, you'd have more money than you can spend in the end, so don't worry about wasting money on an upgrade to test out. You can grind in this game and are expected to do so to some extent, as you are warned about being under-leveled if you turn off random encounters, but they are very annoying when you are trying to explore. I’d advise you to turn it off when you feel uncomfortable and turn it back on when you are ready to grind. You are expected to be around level 25 for the final boss fight and keeping the recommended encounter difficulty on, I had reached level 23-24 before the final fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst not the greatest title, Jack Move is a decently put together, albeit short game. You play as Noa, a hacker geared towards taking down the corporation ruining the city. Things happen to get a bit more personal, involving her family leading her on a quest throughout a futuristic technology focused world. The biggest standout here, surprisingly, is the story. That's not common for me but it's one of the more solid elements as the story deals with a lot of topics and overall handles them well from Familial bonds to loss and corporatism. The story is what kept me most involved and engaged overall. It also helps that the character work is pretty solid and the writing is reasonably good. More-so if you're more tech minded, though some lines can be a little cheesy. Gameplay wise it's a decent RPG but it feels like it has some good ideas with some less great execution overall. In short you take turns battling opponents and levelling up. You can equip up to three items as well as a variety of skills that can  be bought from shops, obtained through progression or as rewards to side quests (Of which there are a handful). Combat doesn't necessarily boil down to the usual turn based affair as the player can increase the frequency of their attacks or opt to take a defensive move to get 2 or more turns back to back. You can also use a turn to switch your moves mid combat. Moves also level up depending on usage. Overall there's not a tonne of variety to the moves meaning you don't need to switch them up much, at least if you get space upgrades. Levelling moves doesn't seem to matter much overall. You also play the game solo meaning you have to fully rely on your one character in fights that can have up to 3 enemies. There's also a simple rock paper scissors mechanics but it doesn't go far beyond that. If you're not a fan of the RPG mechanics, you can disable combat and turn on an autowin mode and focus on the story. I opted to play through on the standard encounter rate and found that was about right overall. Combat was seldom a struggle overall with most bosses being pretty simple to sus out and handle. On the visual and audio side of things, this game definitely succeeds on providing some solid pixel art from characters, enemies and environments. The soundtrack is also pretty good too. It's varied but tracks manage to stick in your head and fit all of the varying zones. I always enjoy when the visuals and audio are nicely polished and Jack Move is no exception to that. it's a decent but short game that delivers a strong story but the gameplay may be slightly disappointing for some as it fails to stick the landing on the mechanics presented. Nonetheless I had a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, corny header aside, this is a great little game. Turn based cyberpunk RPG sees you play as Noa, a sassy (not kidding, one of her stats is Sass) hacker from the slums on a journey to take down a megacorp. It's not the most unique of stories, but it gets the job done, and it's all nicely wrapped up for the most part. A vibrant pixel art style with smooth animations and a lot of charm,  is a short but very entertaining game. To be praised is its approach to difficulty, in which you can choose how much "random battles" you have at any time. Yes, you can even turn them off. This does mean levelling up is sacrificed, but if you just want to run around exploring the levels and collecting items, you can do it without the constant interruptions. It's a neat idea. As are the systems in place, where as you level up and gain money, you can adapt your deck to have more programs or a few more powerful ones. There's even a sort of 'Limit Break' system where as you take damage, you gain a little meter that when full let's you pull off the titular  of which you can get a few that are animated in fantastic, if slightly too long and unskippable, little cutscenes. It's also loaded with references, some dated, some not. But even just having them brought a smile to my face as I cringed at them. YMMV.Give this one a shot if you fancy something simple but charming and interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. For the very fair price they are asking for this game you'll get a straightforward story that works well enough, a simple but effective combat system with rock-paper-scissors like weakness mechanics and charming, lovable characters.The main story is rather short - like 5 to 6 hours and then you have 1-2 hours of side quests. If you like deep systems and things you can git gud at: you will not find that in this game. For me, it was an RPG I can play in-between in bite-sized chunks, relax, take in the world a bit, read through all the dialogue quips and look around for some treasure chests. More comparable to a one-season animated TV show.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a relatively short but charming turn based RPG that graphically shares a style with UNSIGHTED and a combat system that feels strangely like Pokemon. The story is your standard cyberpunk story, nothing groundbreaking but still enjoyable enough. My main critique with the game is that the difficulty is on the easy side even with little to no grinding except for the two last bosses that will take great pride in kicking you in the teeth and draining your recovery items.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This was basically all the things I liked about 16-bit era jrpgs without the stuff that can drag them down.  It's 10hrs, which I think is a great, I don't want to spend all my time grinding.  I liked the different take on a "magic" system.  I loved the writing, where are a lot of little jokes and, critically, it clearly indicates if a character has something new to say or it will be a repeat conversation so you don't waste your time.  You also get to choose your encounter rate at any time; another great way they show that they respect my time.The art is fantastic and I looooooove the soundtrack!  I had a great time start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, but that's all.The pixel art is cool, especially in battles. Speaking of which, the battle mechanics are repetitive, it's pretty much using the same abilities and healing yourself when you're low on health. I didn't really relate to the story even though I liked Noa's personality.The bottom line, it's not a bad game, but I don't have much to say about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for free when a friend gifted it to me some time ago because it meant something to them. I slept on it for awhile because sometimes I'm a dink like that. But I've circled back to play it because I miss that friend. I mention this because the story is in part about broken connections, and the pain which comes from loss, and what people will do to try and overcome the loss of people who matter to them. If you've lost a friend or family member in you life,the story might speak to you more than if you haven't.  The Music's good, the combat is pretty satisfying, and there were some pretty amusing writing beats throughout. I found myself wishing it was a little longer, which I don't consider a bad thing when it comes to little indie RPGs like this. I would happily return to this game's world in a sequel. You can expect a playtime of around 7-9 hours to see all the game has to offer, and it wraps up with an open enough ending that I could easilly see them build upon it. If you've cut your teeth on a lot of RPGs you'll probably have little trouble mastering the combat. The game world is fairly small, and the dungeons are charming but somewhat basic. In my opinion the asking price of $20 is right at the edge of entertainment/value ratio, so if you're strapped for cash, catch it on sale, but catch it, it's worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game, from the story to the characters to the animations. Its was very well thought out for an Indie. There are some cool abilities in the form of software and upgrades in the form of hardware. I suggest saving for the good stuff right from the beginning, but not sure if there is a wrong choice. If anything its poison because the damage is low and the cost of use is decently high. There are lots of great choices for software each with their own use cases and animations. My favorite hardware is prolly the Link letting you hit everything at once. Followed closely by the one that gives you a ton of buffs but lowers your software defense to all 4 types.     This game tugs on nostalgia strings of old rpg's while standing on its own completely. It is rather short because it has no extra baggage. There are a couple side quests you can find by chatting and that's about it outside the main story The characters and even townsfolk are all well written and feel authentic.     I went into thinking cards were gonna be involved somehow as i kept seeing stuff about building decks but its just like a cyber-deck. Highly recomend to any old school rpg fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: **My actual playtime was about 12 hours (I left it running unintentionally)**I really enjoyed the game, it is a well crafted short experience that did most things really well (sound, visuals/animations, and combat) and has some good QoL features. There is a bit of a balancing issue by around the halfway point though as you can get quite overpowered from grinding which makes the second half a bit of a breeze.The dialogue may not be everyone's cup of tea, I found it amusing and I thought the emotional stuff was balanced overall with light-hearted and even comedically dark NPCs dialogue.I feel bad that I took so long to take a chance on this, but I must applaud the developers for producing such a gem and I look forward to a sequel or spin off that is similar in style.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Played it offline on my Steam Deck, so it says I only played it for less than an hour despite the fact that I finished it.Solid little game. Not complicated or difficult, and a fun cyberpunk adventure you can knock out in a couple of days. The explorable world is not too large, but that's okay because the game is not that long anyway. _childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a very mediocre video game with an extremely boring narrative of generic plots, generic settings and generic story-telling. The gameplay itself isn't so bad. And the game is short, but if it was longer, it definitely would be an awful experience. Mostly because the game really has nothing to say. It's just a bunch of... Cookie-cutter 90s continuum. Even the cover art itself was drawn by someone with far more interest in art. Not because the art in the game itself is necessarily ugly. But because the game's cover has far more personality than that... Pixel stuff.No offence to the devs. I'm sure it took a lot of work to animate all of these robots, monsters, abilities, etc. It's definitely really pretty. But also, why was it made? To me... The answer is "just cause" and not in a good way. This game was someone's homework. And they did their homework well. But there is no blood in it. No art. It's just competence.

_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Very cute little game, lots of fun to play, the battle system is unique and original. The world is well thought out and you feel the cyberpunk vibes 100%. Nice character design, amazing animation, and even some groovy songs that get stuck in your head. It's a short game, but for me that's a big PLUS. I don't have time for 200 hour long epics anymore, unless it's something fantastic like Elden Ring or Zelda. So, short cool games are the way to go for me when it comes to new IP. All in all, I enjoyed it a lot.Cons: Usually, with indie games, the dialogue is big miss and it's the same with this game. Most of the story is spewed through giant dumps of exposition instead of letting the narrative develop naturally. The main character is a bunch of anime tropes (the usual bouncy, energetic, kick-ass chick tropes that get used in female lead games), and this leaves no room for a real personality or even character development. Shallow story, and some twists that don't really fit with the direction of the plot. BUT IT'S OK! It's Indie level story telling! I wasn't expecting The Last of Us. I did find an exploit in the battle system that allowed me to level up all of my .Exe's and Jack Moves TO THE MAX within the first section of the game. I won't mention what it is, but it was actually very fun to use it and to get OP quickly.Overall: Super cute fun game. You can run through this game in a few hours and not feel like you have to slog and grind eternally. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: A decent length casual game with some impressive effects given the underlying RPG Maker framework. The story is heavily dipped in cyberpunk dystopia and then flourished with spunky characters. It's a fun, light, and sometimes intriguing little game. It's like a cupcake - you won't get lost in it or call it a meal, but you might appreciate the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: A fun retro game that knows it's goofy and embraces that, never getting too serious or caught up in its lore where simply throwing out computer jargon as a catchphrase will suffice instead. The combat has great flexibility in how you want to approach your builds from the time you reach the first store, and an interesting 'Rock, Paper, Scissors, Wet Noodle' format for combat.The builds are flexible, even letting you (and requiring you to in some battles) change up your loadout mid-fight, and the game offers many different powerful tools, while limiting how many you can equip at a time, making you choose what's most important to you. And did I mention THIS ABSOLUTE BANGER OF A SOUNDTRACK!?The end of the game suffers from some bloating and unbalanced leveling numbers which makes it feel much slower and less prodcutive than the opening 5 hours or so, but overall the experience is well worth the purchase.I've played a lot of RPGs, and this is the first one I've ever played that just let you see every 'spell' option you'll be able to purchase almost right off the bat. In some ways, it's almost overwhelming, but it's also very freeing- it lets you get a sense of what you as a player want to work towards and what to prioritize. There's an interesting system that lets you equip a limited number of passive buffs, and another system that lets you equip a limited number of 'spells' (that you can swap out mid-combat). Throw on top of that a 'Rock, Paper, Scissors (and a predominantly useless except fringe cases melee attack)' combat system, and the ability to level up 'spells' the more you use them, as well as ultimate moves... you've got a solid and engaging system that will keep the combat interesting for 75% of the game.The music is absolutely killer, like a throwback to the Sega era of game music, but with modern production; throughout the beginning of the game, I kept finding myself exclaiming 'Damn!' every time a new song came on, and at one point thinking "I didn't think we were allowed to make games with soundtracks this good anymore."The story is functional- there are no real surprises, and it's about what you would expect from a Saturday morning cartoon. It serves to move the player forward, and although the main character starts off pretty unlikeable, it's part of an arc that leads to her becoming a better person. And it's worth noting that the game has a couple of boss fights that actually make you think and learn their mechanics on the fly, instead of just repeating what you've done to every regular enemy, which is a very welcome addition to the formula.The map design is (mostly) well thought out, with chests and items that reward you for thoughtful exploration, and though there are randomly triggered combat encounters, there's at least a meter that makes it feel less random, even if it's truly not (as well as options to turn off combat entirely if you just want to explore, which is a welcome addition).Unfortunately, the end of the game is not as polished as it starts. Leveling up your abilities or your character's level becomes impossible in the third act without heavy grinding, just because of how large of a disparity there is between how much experience you need to level abilities up, and how much experience you get per fight late game. I had equipped the strongest 'spells' in the game as soon as they were available, and almost none of them made it past level 1 by the end of the game while I was playing at the regular enemy spawn rate. To be fair, they don't really need to be leveled up to finish the game, but it really drove a sledgehammer into that sense of growth and progress that the game did so well at the beginning.The maps in the third act of the game are also not as well designed as the first 3/4. Someone decided that all the late game area maps needed to be huge, and for non-combat areas that just makes for tedious trekking about while you talk to NPCs in the hopes that they have a side quest (the game trains you in this early on), but none of them ever do. For the combat areas, it just makes the random spawn rate of encounters more apparent, as you walk about 4-6 steps and get into another fight. These feelings are accentuated BECAUSE the pacing of the game is so good for like 5-6 hours, and then just falls off a cliff for the last two or so.It was disappointing that the titular ultimate abilities (Jack Moves) ended up limited to only 4 for the whole game. They have cool animations, and they are strong, but they lose their wow factor the longer you play.I ran into one game breaking bug where I went to change my equipped abilities in the middle of the final boss fight, accidentally pressed escape, which I think triggered a tutorial, and then couldn't get out of that menu in any way.The end of the game definitely needs some polish as well, tuning the damage numbers, encounter rates for large map areas, lowering the experience needed to level abilities or increasing the amount of experience late game enemies give... The front half of the game balances all of these systems wonderfully, and then as soon as you hit around level 20, all sense of progress brickwalls. It would also be nice if there were ever situations in which it felt like physical attacks did something- looking back at the game, I can only think of one instance. Overall, a fantastic game with interesting mechanics and fantastic music (I'm headed to buy the soundtrack right now). The third act suffers from some balancing issues, which is only made more jarring because of how well everything that precedes it was paced, but even with that considered this game is well worth your money if you're up for a fun, entertaining and thoughtful ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, short turn-based RPG with fantastic pixel art, attitude, and markers to let you know when you've already talked to NPCs. There's also a button that turns off random encounters - which can come in handy for when you're playing this between game releases  Definitely worth it to scratch a quick RPG itch if you don't want something involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a simple RPG with an interesting software developer/hacker theme. The story is cute sci-fi one, nothing ground breaking. I find it funny how the situation of the world in game could actually be an issue in real life. Gameplay wise there could have been a lot more depth put into this game but it is incredibly easy. There are a lot of software skills in the game you will never utilize. You will essentially steamroll everything at a certain point. The mechanics are really cool but aren't fully realized due to how easy the game is. Would like to see the software/hardware system fleshed out and used fully with more in-depth and strategic battles in a future installment if Jack Move continues. I would recommend it if you are looking for a RPG  to play for a quick story.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals. Serviceable story, but not amazing. The characterization leans on indignation and rage too much. The battle system looks great, but the mechanics are fairly simple.The progression and difficulty is both too easy for most of the game (quickly progressing to the point of easily one-shotting most enemies) and then limited toward the end (permanent upgrades quickly run out and damage caps out at either 4999 or 9999, depending the particular attack, even tho regular enemies have more than that much hp).Overall, a fun, short RPG that will visually please but likely not amaze with storytelling or mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Ngl this game is carried heavily by its aesthetics and soundtrack for me. The characters and story are enjoyable, but they are fairly simple. Combat is similarly enjoyable-but-too-simple. Though the final boss of the game is great and I wish the game was more like that the entire run through.The game looks great, I love the pixel art and animations in this game. Though there are a few rooms where the perspective is ♥♥♥♥♥ due to changes in elevation being hard to tell apart.I also love the soundtrack, though I wish the final boss had a more banging track. It's a very lowkey ambient type of thing.Nonetheless, short and sweet RPG. I enjoyed my time with it. The credits are the most soulful credit sequence I've seen since Dead Rising 2: Off the Record, as it blatantly references classic PS1-era cracktros.My biggest gripes are actually two bugs I encountered. One is that you can softlock yourself in combat by pressing the start button in the Install screen. The second is that the final boss' boss rush phase is completely skipped if you kill the boss via poison damage, which I did because its insane health meant poison was extremely effective. The boss rush looks lame tho!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. It's not too long, making it feasible to beat with a busy schedule, but despite only being 10 hours long it still offers a compelling story with good character development. The pixel art is great and the battle system takes me back to the good old days of the PS1. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Really tight RPG with great characters and gameplay. The combat system is quirky enough to set Jack Move apart from other turn-based systems without getting too bogged down with over complicated mechanics. Not to mention some of the best modern pixel art and animation I've seen. Punchy sound design, fun world building and a satisfying battle system that stays fresh through the whole 9ish hour campaign. Jack Move would make an excellent intro for anyone looking to try (J)RPGs
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move offers a dose of nostalgia with its classic JRPG turn-based combat, though it lacks the complexity of an equipment system and restricts control to the main protagonist, omitting hero/group management. The storyline, while competently presented, falls on the shorter and predictable side. However, the game does earn points for its quality of life features, such as the ability to turn off random enemy encounters. The art-style is a standout, but some side quests may not be the most engaging. Overall, Jack Move delivers a mixed bag of retro charm and missed opportunities.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: It's a "good" game I would say, I was expecting more from this game, all the enemy are technically the same just different color, and the story was fine. Pretty good pixel art that's for sure but I really don't know what to say about this game really, when I played it the first time I was kinda excited for this new game, but the gameplay is meh for me, at some point of the game you will need to adapt your "build" to fights enemies/bosses so that you can't really go through the game with one build.The game itself is quite short finished it in 6 hours, these 6 hours definetly was more in my mind.This game is fine 7/10 ? even 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move's brevity was actually a draw for me. I'm a busy man with two jobs. I played about 8hrs (some offline time), and found it enjoyable.Pros-Artwork is top notch.-Solid music.-Enjoyable, puzzle-like combat (even if it's turn based).-Likeable characters.Cons-A bit rushed with the ending. Seriously, that was quite the narrative load in the last five minutes.-While I like the characters, I don't love them. I'm a little tired of "everyone has a tragic backstory". And while I like sassy Noa a lot, she came off a little jerkish at times. The trailer lead me to believe she would be a bit more grounded and less Marvel Movie sarcastic.-What was the point in the little robot???If you're looking for a good time that fills the hour or two before bed, Jack Move has it covered. A tip: try for a more defensive loadout. It'll payoff at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little indie JRPG with a lot of problems but a lot of heart. The combat balance is pretty janky, the final boss sucks, and overall the game is pretty easy with a lot of extraneous cruft, but if you're in the mood to kill 5-10 hours plunking away with a cyberpunk aesthetic you could do far worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: i was looking for a short and fun game to play. as i like turn based combat games like this - seemed like the perfect choice. the game is a bit repetitive or even tiresome due to lengthy frequent fights type dungeons. that is a minor issue though, the main character is naive and infantile, but also fun and nicely drawn. overal pixelart graphics is fine, music doesn't bother. one thing i hated was the pre-last fight. 25mins of a single fight, come on! solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I had real fun with this game, Dialogue is really nice, gameplay is solid, story is solid.The small nitpick i have is that the game is quite short, and i think the attacks/possible ways to play is quite simple. wish there was a bit more you know. I was left with a taste that wanted more.but overall I had real fun and i think it's a solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "meh" option.The game is very charming as a nice little project but unfortunately have very little substance - I was actually going to recommend it until the ending section, where the tedium finally outweighted the good.The story is very basic. Evil corporation do evil stuff, standard cyberpunk ideas. While it starts decent enough it soon devolves to the comically evil level (because obviously everyone who is rich or have high status job must be either an idiot, absolutely evil or staight up insane, right?), which is neither fun nor interesting. The characters are likeable but not enough to carry the story.Now for the bad part, the combat. It is very simple, extremely repetitive, and feels pointless.  You make 3 steps in the very long corridor, you get attacked. You spam one of the 3 abilities you have depending on the enemy weakness while healing from time to time, you win. Repeat. What is curious the developers seem to understand that because you can turn off random encounters completely and there is a hidden "I win" key which will instantly defeat all enemies. And it is very useful since bosses have some 50k hp while you do 3k ish damage.I feel that it would be much better game if it was just a point and click or even visual novel. In this state - while admittedly very cute and clearly made with passion - I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a small and short turn-based RPG but the amount of polish basically blinds me. It's like reverse of Skyrim - they thought of basically everything. I only saw one typo and one minor visual bug, the rest worked flawlessly.For example options, it goes from having encounters every 5 steps to giving yourself the "win" button if you dont care about gameplay (it's up to the player by settings). Then again, the gameplay is simple yet fun - four types of damage and basic yet important and understandable buffs (maybe except berserk effect you get from Silicone Beast - it's hard to know what the flame icon does...). you also have many customisable option with three hardware slots (the equipment of this game) and software slots for your abilities (which you can change mid-battle at the cost of a turn!)The story is very likeable too (especially many NPC's you met, even minor ones) and the polish really shines too by showing who you talked to before with special icon and also journal with quests (main and side separately). Every enemy is also greatly animated and you see new and interesting variants even in last parts of the game. There are little to no duplicates and even they serve small purpose (different weaknesses of course). Seriously if they added party members (you fight alone basically), some ways to interact with dodge/accuracy (wish i had accuracy boost. so many misses...) and make it longer at the same level of polish and quality it could rival even the mightiest and strongest turn-based RPG/JRPG titles!Just keep in mind the game is rather short - 6 to 8 hours is small for such type of game, but its quality that counts after all.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed bag. Looks nice, has a great soundtrack, and it's short. Unfortunately the combat isn't very interesting, you'll never have a reason to use 80% of the software or hardware, you can grind near a vending machine to trivialize the random encounters, and the final boss has just way too much health. At least all of the achievements are tied to completing the main story, so you're completely done when the final fight is over.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good, but very short RPG. The devs clearly put all on quality over quantity, with a 6-8 hour story full of charming and (for the most part) light-hearted writing. Animation quality is through the roof and the game has a vibrant, detailed art style in general. I'm not entirely sure the game is worth the original 20 bux price, considering the shortness of the game  but marked down even just to 17-16 I would recommend you buy it if you love these types of pixel-art top-down turn-based-tactic (can I get more hyphens?!) games. I hope it gets a sequel one day!
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Screen jitter causes major headache if I play for more than 1 hour.The game itself is very good!  I have been looking for something to play since Octopath Traveller 2 and Star Renegades.  I've tried a few titles and then found Jack Move.  It's a great modern take on the traditional turn based JRPG.  The pixel graphics are strong and the detailed sprites are refreshing.  The soundtrack is also strong.  It's got a bit of techno, some retro 90's synth style, and some dubstep mixed together.But seriously, please FIX THE SCREEN JITTER!  I can't play more than an hour without getting 8 hours of head pain.  This is not an exageration.  The screen jitters and jumps constantly when on the map/overworld and the character is moving.  The problem goes away during fights, when the character is stationery, and when in the menu screen.  The background motion needs to be smoothed out.  I don't know what the cause is, but I've not experienced this issue in any other game.Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Jack Move is a good little Deck game for relaxing and doesn't hit the battery hardly at all.This is no 60 hour epic story. It is about a 10 hour short story with a fun little three-way balance between items, hardware, and software wrapped up in a turn-based action. The story reminds me of the old arcade games and 8bit days on computers and consoles. It was a great deal when I caught it on sale and I've enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Dunno about this one. I kinda liked it but it's slightly small or short or something. I didn't change my hardware nor my software too much, never used Install, barely used Patch in the last two boss fights. I didn't like how hard it was to level up the software, I'd have liked to max it all out. Also didn't like how you couldn't go over 16 ram slots, definitely limited me, especially towards the end when you get all the software.As you can see by my playtime, it only took 6 hours, and I think I did all the sidequests plus I also grinded a bit. I'd give it a mixed review if I could but I can't so positive it is I suppose. I did get the game on a nice sale, though.Back to game elements ... I kinda liked the characters a little bit but I also feel like I got thrown in and had to figure out who everyone and everything was. Felt kinda real because a lifetime of relationships doesn't pop out of thin air, but there was no place for me to catch up on who everyone's relation to MC was until it came up in dialog somewhere.Walk speed was too slow for my taste but at least you can control the encounter rate so it was alright.Money was weird. I'd save up tons, enough to buy anything I wanted, but I also did not buy everything, since there was no point. I barely used 2 types of consumables in the game as well.I did absolutely enjoy being a 1 gal party though, since I didn't have to worry too much about turn order, specializing someone, targeting my heals, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: This game was on my back burner for a while, after trying the tutorial dungeon on a switch version.Mistake......Jack Move is actually a fun game. At first, it seemed confusing with how the "spells" and "gear" work...but understanding comes fast (especially if you have played FF7). Thinking of the ram abilities as materia, and the hardware as armor slots, it makes a lot more sense. And being able to change "spells" mid battle is pretty nice too.I think getting through the terminology is really the biggest factor if you will like this or not. The story is great, and the battles are a lot of fun. It is also a game that likes to have fun with itself and subject matter.If you find this for a good deal...don't pass this gem up.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this exceeded my expectations!The pixel art and animation are vibrant, expressive and delightful. The soundtrack is infectious. The cyberpunk setting is populated by characters with varied motivations and responses to the overall dystopia, similar in vibe to 2064: Read Only Memories. Bright Town and its surrounding locales are a pleasure to see, hear and explore.I'm someone who's easily overwhelmed by a lot of concurrent systems in turn-based RPGs, so I love when games visualize upcoming turns and use straightforward rock-paper-scisssors-esque strengths and weaknesses. Jack Move does both, which made its combat very approachable to me.Finally, the game manages to tell a complete, coherent story with some solid progress and optional side quests inside of seven or eight hours! It's perfect if you feel like a handheld RPG but you aren't ready to surrender several weeks' worth of evenings and weekends.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous sprite work, great music and fun writting. The final boss was a test for everything you've learned during the gameplay, which considering I just brute forced my way through almost the entire game, meant that I had to learn a lot of mechanics REAL fast. Still, I've enjoyed my time with this game immensely and I would love to see a sequel for it, perhaps with a party of 3 for more depth in the fights? Well worth its full price and during the summer sale, it's a must have. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: First the negative parts: up until the last fight it's usually too easy. There is also never more than one and the same character which feels a like wasted potential and make the fights become repetetive at some point. Especially if you want to level up to deal with a boss. To shorten and mitigate that there is the instant-kill option, which is indeed better than brainless grinding (you can still do it, if you want, suit yourself). But it still feels odd and more like a workaround for a deeper problem than an actual solution.However, I still had fun with the game. Both with the gameplay / fighting mechanics (especially against the bosses) and with the (linear) story. So that's a win in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Jack Move

_childDocuments_.review: Sat down not knowing I'd be spending the next 7-8 or so hours playing this game to completion, yet here I am. Thoroughly enjoyed it! So much charm and lore packed into a tight package with satisfying combat that doesn't overly rely on weakness mechanics like other games I've played. There are so many little things in this game that made the experience fun and a joy to play I'd rather not list any and let you find them for yourself!
