_childDocuments_.review: I've played every Dungeon Defenders game hundreds of hours a piece and have over 300hrs in this one (playing sporadically since beta).Dev team constantly talks about how they're making improvements to the player experience, but it only amounts to a UI change literally every patch and constant, unnecessary nerfs to the best builds to facilitate regrinding gear for the new meta. The community dev team for the first game does a significantly better job than these people. Multiple stats have "hard caps" that do either absolutely nothing after you reach it, or roll over into another stat at a reduced rate, so building a character literally just becomes "put all the points in damage/health" because no other stats help. The hardest difficulty is balanced around using only "meta" builds and having the best gear in the game, so breaking into it is tedious and generally unrewarding for your time. Still feels like a beta game, even after the first free DLC update, as there was more enemy and boss variety in all the previous games. If you want a good Dungeon Defenders experience, play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing this game and I'm loving it so far. This combines so many genres that I enjoy. ARPG, Tower defense, and a decent loot and upgrade system. I chose to drop all of my Mage attributes into tower range, tower atk, and tower HP. Same thing with the monk, tower range and atk. On defense I wall and setup mage towers and monk bubbles. Then when its time to fight. I use my warrior or archer with all of the attributes stacked on HP and Damage. If you do get this make sure you are using all of the heroes to help support you on defense! I met a lot of new players only using one hero and had no idea about adding the other heroes and swapping.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare and harder difficulties are locked behind hero level 70. You can beat all insane maps by level 45. This is fine if you're okay with grinding a game for no gear upgrades for 35 levels, but in general is a TERRIBLE idea. Just because you made the game and couldn't beat nightmare before level 70 does not mean that the people who play your game are as bad at it as you. Even if I am unable to beat nightmare at that level DOES NOT give you the right to stop me from trying. I paid money for the game, I should play how I want. I'm sure there is a lot of things I have yet to experience, and I know this game can be grindy (I played the original on ps3 for 2k+ hours), but telling me I have to spend 5 hours with 0 chance of an item upgrade is a dumb idea no matter how you look at it. I want to like this game, and I will likely push past this just to see what the end game is like, but the rule that difficulty should NEVER be locked behind a level applies to every game I've ever played. This is no exception. Blocking someone from moving on for an arbitrary reason is Anthem (on release day) level of poor game design.Update: I have put an additional 30 hours into the game since writing my last review. I beat the final map on NM difficulty (hardcore) with my highest character being 73. I then learned that massacre difficulty is locked behind character level 83 which, like DD1, is a significantly longer grind than levels before 70. I'd say about 24 hours after beating summit I am at level 77 (after learning to keep a single character permanent in my deck simply to level up). There are two main things I have learned in my playtime since my last review: 1. This game puts emphasis on survival only. After beating each map once you will have no reason to ever go back. The armour that drops is useless compared to survival (which makes sense), there is only one pet that drops from campaign missions (which boosts your towers so it's designed to be used in survival), and there are no map-exclusive weapons until late game (which are useless anyway due to point 2). 2. DPS characters are useless. With a dedicated dps character on NM in gear farmed from high wave survival runs you will still only be hitting around 400k dps. Fighting a boss that has 34m health would take you 20 minutes assuming you don't die. The meta strat is to stack DSTs where you will be fighting the boss and watch it get melted without doing anything yourself. This game might as well be pure strategy only. The only difference between you being there and not is that you can be there to boost your DSTs and might get attacked by a ninja and die. If even the boss fights are best fought with towers then why am I there in the first place?

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Defenders, my beloved. This franchise has a special place in my heart because I grew up playing the first Dungeon Defenders game with my dad and brother. I was excited to play DDA because it has a lot of similarities to the original, but with additional maps/characters/game modes, as well as improved graphics. Despite the influence that nostalgia has on my experience, someone without a connection to the franchise would also enjoy playing this game. It can be fun to play solo or work as a team. My main issue with the game is the redundant grinding required to achieve some of the achievements, namely the one requiring several different character builds to be at least level 105. I have completed every achievement except for this one. I currently dread going back into the game to get this last trophy, as it requires countless hours of repetitive actions. The completionist in me wants to grind for this last achievement, but the realist in me does not want to waste hours of my life while not having fun... the second that grinding for a game is no longer fun, I find it is not worth it. I will probably suffer for the last achievement eventually, but as of right now, I need a long break before I play again. A smaller issue I have with this game is the glitches that occur when playing with someone. If you are not the host, the chests at the end of each wave are glitched and say something like "player," when each player's name is supposed to be above the respective chest. Items often are glitched into the ground when you are not the host. My brother also had a large amount of gold disappear from his account one random day when he logged in (I have not personally had this problem). The boss countdown also does not typically appear when I am not the host. While the game has a Discord server, it feels like most suggestions fall on deaf ears, and that the developers have pretty much moved on from this game.TLDR:Fun game, good to play solo or with people, too much grinding in the end game for one trophy, random glitches occur during multiplayer if you are not the host.

_childDocuments_.review: DDA sucks. Please buy this pile of garbage anyway. You could just set fire to your wallet instead but then you wouldn't be able to leave a negative review so you'd kinda miss out.You may be confused about me telling you to buy a game that sucks and can't possibly be recommended, so to clear things up a little; the Dungeon Defenders concept is good but literally everything other than the first DD game and its DLCs has been disastrously flawed one way or another, with DDA being the lastest trainwreck. However unless the DD devs have enough funds there will never again be a GOOD title in the DD universe, so please buy this piece of trash game, downvote it will all your heart and write the scathing review it deserves and cling on to the faint glimmer of hope that one day we'll see something that replaces this disaster of a game.Wondering what sucks about this game and why someone who's played it for hundreds of hours still thinks it's trash? Can't blame you for doubting my sincerity, unfortunately I've been playing it as a way to waste time and it still makes me feel like I want a refund of my time. Let me present a few bullet points of what makes the game so unbearably crappy: ¤ At some point they crippled the game by capping how fast your defenses can attack, for the sole reason of being able to sell it on the 357th platform that nobody wanted; the Switch. The most awful piece of trash console in recent years, one that should never have seen the light of day and one that barely anyone would ever use to play something like DDA in the first place. They crippled the game on ALL PLATFORMS to make it just BARELY run on a platform nobody wanted and that never ended up generating any profit. Now in their defense they did backtrack somewhat from how badly they crippled the game initially, but "too little too late" is far too mild a statement, a big part of the very soul of DD is the chaos and carnage of spraying absurd streams of projectiles in the grinning faces of the minions of evil and DDA threw out a chunk of its very soul in pursuit of a pathetically tiny percent more profit. ¤ The game was sold unfinished. Badly unfinished. There was the promise of more content over time and it was actually mostly kept, but the game is STILL unfinished - just mostly in the form of missing bits and pieces. Some item descriptions even have such horrible spelling and grammar that I've seen elementary schoolers have a better handle on english, not to mention sometimes even entire words are missing and the descriptions are flat out so incomplete one has to guess what they mean. ¤ The game has horrible balance on the highest difficulty, players are forced into extremely narrow playstyles in order to stand the slightest chance when dealing with endgame content. While I applaud the ability to quickswap heroes from a "deck" that levels up regardless of which hero the player actively controls during waves, one ends up having no choice but to use specific ones for specific purposes because no alternative exists that provides a similar function. ¤ "Runes" are special drops that one can obtain and use to greatly alter the behavior of various defenses. While the general idea of runes is good because it offers more variety in how to play, the actual effects are horribly unbalanced and some almost don't scale at all while some get so exponentially much more powerful with level that they utterly wreck the balance of the game.  ¤ There is a gamemode called "rifted" that has some unusual effects on gameplay. Normally the enemies can have various attributes (fire or lightning and so on) and look vastly different from each other, but in rifted mode they all look like a smeary dark mass and have only a single attribute; rifted. Everything about them that visually sets them apart is sacrificed in favor of "smeary dark mass" and everything that makes elementally enhanced enemies a unique challenge is completely thrown out. This feels like a very poorly thought out addition to the game, and unfortunately it's a gamemode that players have to use in order to get the absolute best gear and unlock the ability to switch out one defense per hero into a "fused" version that deals damage to any enemy regardless of all attributes (meaning a fire tower can kill a fire based enemy) and also deals double damage to rifted enemies. The whole thing sacrifices much of the DD personality for pure dull grinding for gear. ¤ Defenses are so irritatingly bad at actually HITTING enemies that it can drive players insane. The projectiles typically travel so slowly that any fast enemy will be absolutely nowhere near the point of impact once the projectile actually covers the distance... and most projectiles have no homing ability. And yes NONE of them actually tries to predict where the enemy WILL be, they aim where the enemy IS and then typically never get there in time to be of use if they're shooting at any enemy that isn't moving in a straight line towards the defense. ¤ The map designs are incredibly frustrating. Not only do they often have spawn points extremely close to the crystals that are supposed to be defended, they also have droves of stupidly tiny obstacles that block shots from defenses. For some reason defenses seem to aim at the feet of enemies, so if there's literally a 10cm tall obstacle in front of an enemy your tower will waste every single shot hitting that obstacle.That about covers my biggest gripes with this stupid game. Of course I haven't even gotten to the point of mentioning all the irritating bugs yet but it's not like listing them will do any good, I have no hope whatsoever that this game will get any actual patch that fixes the issues. Anyway if you're still reading this awful review you might as well give the game a try, you clearly have abundant patience...

_childDocuments_.review: To start off I love this game, and will try to give as much depth to the review as I can as an early game player.Recently I had the urge to play a DD game after years upon years of not playing one, so I decided to redownload DD1 to fulfill that urge, however, DD1 just didn't hit the same as I remember (probably due to the games outdated graphics etc). So I was scrolling through and found out they released a new game a year or so ago in Dungeon Defenders: Awakened, so I decided to get it since it was on sale. And let me tell you, I do not regret it. Pros: - Almost endless replayability - Updated and charming graphics - RNG loot (IMO this is a plus because it adds to the replaybility) - Updated maps (as well as new) - From what I hear, the devs are actively supporting the game - Easy to pick up for solo players (more fun with friends)Cons: - You may feel "stuck" at times, for ex: you may not know what to grind for, where to grind for certain items, etc. (Discord is really helpful for this) - Tutorial is only helpful for the bare minimum (Does not teach you about the auto loot function, or how to mass sell items in your inventory) - Nothing else as of almost 30 hours inDo I recommend this game, absolutely. If you like grinding games with a lot of replay value and loot, this is the game for you. Its not completely mindless as you have to use strategy across multiple characters for the defenses, and boss fights, but it makes it that much more engaging. And the community is pretty tight nit and friendly as far as what Ive seen. I would personally rate the game 8.5/10 but this is a review of an early game player and should be subject to change higher in the future depending on the value of end game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, it's sort of hard to put this into short words, but this game is genuinely great if you're into tower defense. It's also the series' return to form, as DD2 took a different direction with, in my opinion, a much more generic art style and micro transactions heading its ship. There wasn't that warm, glowy aesthetic I had come to love with the first game, and I didn't find DD2 to be all that fun - at least when playing for free; I never spent money on the game.Now we have DDA, which sees a return to the original character designs, an enhanced art style that pops like DD1's did (only perhaps less "glowy" if you know what I mean, but still looks good if not way better), and even many of the original locations/maps - plus some new maps added in.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------A lot of people will tell you that this game is inferior to DD1 because of two main reasons:1) There is less content in DDA compared to DD1 and DD1 is cheaper2) DDA seemingly offers nothing new in its current stateTo those points of concern, I have this to say:1) DD1 may have more content by technicality, but only because of its bloated amount of payed DLC. There is SO MUCH DLC to buy, which when playing only the base game makes you as the player feel like you're missing out on the "True Dungeon Defenders Experience", and I wouldn't have a problem with this if you didn't already have to pay $15 for the base game. If you purchase the DLC package on the DD1 store page, you're probably saving money than by purchasing DLC individually - but you're still spending somewhere around $50 on TOP of the $15 base price of the game, unless you know to get the game along with the DLC first. I personally do not enjoy paying for a game, and then realizing I have to pay more money if I want to improve my experience or increase my play time with the game. You can't even play the hardest difficulty, Nightmare Mode, unless you fork over the funds for the DLC that it comes with!DDA, in its current state, does not hold back anything from you via a pay wall. You get the game and all of its features by paying for the base price once, and that's it. As far as I'm aware, Chromatic Games has plans to add more content into the base game, for which then they may increase the price of the game as its content slowly becomes steeper. If they DO add content in the form of payed DLC, I will edit this review appropriately and I probably won't have good things to say - but who knows?2) I would say I agree with this, although Nightmare mode comes free with this version, along with a brand new difficulty called Massacre mode which by itself seems like it can change up a LOT in terms of longevity with the latter half of this game (not that I have played on that difficulty yet, though if I notice anything notable when I do I will insert my thoughts here later). There are also plenty of brand new enemy types that appear solely in the higher difficulties which really helps to shake up the gameplay. Part of the core experience with Dungeon Defenders imo is testing yourself on higher difficulties to see how well you can survive given your current stats and ability to strategize building placement, and only when you have beaten the campaign on the highest difficulty have you truly "beaten" Dungeon Defenders.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------So, TL;DR: This game is best thought of as the series' reboot, and though I am aware DD1 has been redone several times over, I believe this version is the one that holds the most potential. If you played DD1 and purchased much of its DLC, I can see why you wouldn't want to give this game a shot. But if you played mostly the base version of that game or haven't played it at all but are interested in tower defense, I think DDA is the version to get.P.S.: I am aware the game still has glaring flaws, such as its inability to teach the player basic concepts like which hero abilities do what (for instance, there is a special ability the Monk has that I have no clue how it works yet, and I've been playing for roughly 27 hours using all four heroes). There are still bugs to crush and apparently a lack of a couch-play co-op mode, but none of that stops me from enjoying myself. If you're looking for a much more in-depth review, I advise looking through some of the others posted here. Juuuuust be wary of the angry backers of this game...

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I reviewed this back when it was on the humble bundle. I hated it and recommend against it. Seeking more DD content, I finally put down DD1 for a while and forced myself to try DDA again.Do I recommend it now? Yes and no.If you're a returning DD1 player, this game will throw you. It is missing an insane amount of Quality of life content, stats are simplified, loot is poorly laid out across the difficulties, if it's new mechanics then it won't be explained in any form. The campaign is a joke if you actually played DD1. It's a complete random jumble of levels with no coherent flow, they literally teleport you to a desert theme for 2 levels and then just bring an Act 3 DD1 level into Act 2 after it. The Campaign uses strictly 5 waves on all difficulties and all levels, ultimately feeling like pointless content. They could remove it and the game wouldn't change because it's been done so badly.I still reinforce my stance that a DD1 remaster with fresh quality of life and modernisation would've worked. This game is legitimately incoherent and there's a focus on random new content versus fixing old stuff and polishing.If you're new to Dungeon Defenders, unfortunately this is the best bet. DD1 does suffer from its age, becoming a gem in the rough. DDA is the most approachable to a newbie who has no prior experience, and looks the best. You'll feel more at home with a more modern UI and smoother gameplay, and the list of issues won't hurt you as badly, at least not as soon.The game is already dead unless you have friends, at least DD1 had many years of full community. Changes feel questionable or random, they added two new acts to campaign and they are the most random assortment of crap possible, some of them have pathfinding bugs, and even missing content where levels don't play music properly or have no enemy path previews.As a DD1 veteran, this game is a joke. It does just enough to make it tough to go back to DD1s graphics, but from god-awful map balance, half-baked content, and general lack of QoL, it's a no for me unless you are specifically new.*might* be worth it on a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Effectively what you got here is a remaster of DD1, with 90% of the content still missing. Which in itself wouldnt be so bad. The graphics look modern while keeping the original flare. Well done! They even added some convenience features, like starting in higher Survival Waves after you reached there once. Which is great. And all in all this had potential to be something good, even if it's "just" a remaster.However, reality is different. It's basically unplayable - or rather unenjoyable. : The UI, well.. does not look bad. It is just highly unpractical to the point it feels bugged.If towers are close to each other (not overlapping, just close), it is near-impossible to get the information you want. Inspecting them, upgrading them, it all becomes a pain. What's worst tho is the missing HP bars. Like, some HP bars you cant seem to get rid of, others wont show even  something. So most of the time, and i'm not exaggerating, you fight ogres next to your defenses without the slightest idea of how much HP they got left.Then there is problems with the UI not upgrading properly. Like, for example, when you upgrade a tower from 1* to 2*, the UI, while doing so, does not upgrade. As a software developer myself, i can say these are super basic things and i absolutely fail to understand how these can still be so badly done one year after showing up on steam.: There is just plenty. A lot (like a lot) of small ones that are semi-annoying but not gamebreaking. Then there is things like EV mid-round not registering her weapon anymore, and instead shooting with the default MK1 weapon from the tutorial. Unequipping the weapon and trying to re-equip it then tells you that you cannot equip that. Fun little things like that, which may as well ruin your runs. And there is lots of this.: They have some (..) kind of Anti-Cheat in place. But it simply does not work well. Which is likely the reason for why the "Prevent Hackers from Joining" option is OFF by default. I'm pretty sure they know just how badly it works. So what's the problem here? Expect to be flagged as cheater (and thus be unable to play together with people enabling that option) for no reason whatsoever. A member of my local group, who played every single round together with us, just suddenly got flagged as Hacker after restarting and thus was not able to play with us anymore. So we could either have him restart over, or disable the option (and get flagged as hackers outselves for playing with one), or contact the support (which supposedly can take weeks), or just get fed up with all this BS and try to return the game. Which is what we did. I'm honestly pretty sure 95% of the entire playerbase is flagged as hackers without knowing, simply because false-positives seem to happen pretty requently, and playing with anybody who was flagged flags your account as well.

I don't feel like I have to use a certain character or defense to be effective, even on the highest difficulty, which wasn't always the case.With any game, there will always be optimal choices, but it doesn't feel like they're mandatory and that's the sign of a healthy game, imo! Go have fun, explore builds!Beyond that, updates are a bit slow but still happen frequently enough that this game is something I consistently return to and it's always a delight. _childDocuments_.review: ***Ignore the mixed reviews.******As a seasoned original DD1 player all through to DD:A this review is one you can trust.***If you have ever played dungeon defenders 1, you will likely enjoy this remake which blends dd1 and dd2 story line into dda.As a kickstart backer i have the benefits of the exclusive pets which by the way are a great boost to your character for early levels adding +20 to all stats of the character equipped.The original levels have been revamped with better graphics even in 4K resolution it is amazing.  Trendy Entertainment now known as Chromatic games has heard the original dd1 fanbase and remade our lovely dd1 into dd3/dda.  You can see this game differs from dd2 while keeping the dd1 mechanics alive, we can revisit dd1 in a new age.  Chromatic games has been updating DDA into the DD1 version we all once loved and has been on top of their game listening to the player base and delivering what we have asked for, with no surprise since the original DD1 team is working on DDA, well some of the old Trendy team is still on and had be bought out and relabeled as Chromatic.The stages are like the old days, increased graphics while keeping the old mechanics.  Even though the game is still receiving updates on a regular basis, we can only assume with the progress that Chromatic has made, they will deliver all the original DD1 content.The chat window is a bit buggy at times, sometimes you can talk, sometimes you cannot.  This has been an issue since early access and now at full release is still an issue.  There was a silent nerf on some defenses which you would notice if you played on early access in order to balance the game mechanics out.Characters are actually worth putting points into DPS character builds now.  While useless for the most part before, they are no longer useless as a DPS build.The music and stage graphics are similar to that of DD1 with encore stages for stages such as endless spires, magus quarters and the legendary Glitterhelm Caverns.  The difficulty on medium is fairly decent while easy is well... far too easy.There is an issue which should be corrected;(a) Players who participated in a stage and battles through four waves can be kicked by the host also known as "progress griefing".  This should be removed so that players whom have participated for the majority of the game stage should not be allowed to be removed due to progress griefing.  You are free to reset your character points free of charge at any time unlike DD1 which required currency to do so and could be expensive.The bartender should relate more to the original one from dd1 however he has the appearance but not the personality.The tavern from dd1 is revamped while keeping some of the old tavern from dd1 and now has a blacksmith that doesn't say much at all.Currently there are the four basic classes of monk, mage, squire and alas huntress.  Familiar with DD1 PC and Playstation, we can expect additional classes for the PC version but the console may only be stuck with the four basic classes like in console DD1, unlikely they wouldnt update the PS4 version however as CPU and RAM is no longer an issue compared to the old PS3.If you have played DD2 then you would like to see the upgraded defense towers have a more improved look, this is the down side in my opinion.  Sometimes it is impossible to select defenses that overlap on the same space making upgrading difficult so you are required to move your defenses in a different alignment to ensure you could select them to repair, remove or upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Defenders is a niche game in a small genre, action tower defense.  This is the 4th titled game.  Chromatic games has managed to capture the spirit of the original while bringing improvements from DD2.  While the game is not perfect here in Early Access, the developers have shown their commitment to this game by being active and releasing updates at an impressive rate.  The gameplay has improved over the beta, and continues to.  I feel cautiously optimistic for the future of this game as long as Chromatic continues their hard work.  I have seen many questions about this being a remake of DD1.  Let me be clear, it's not.  Awakened has taken the better template from its 2 main preceding games and it using that to springboard into a new game.  There are already new maps in early access, with a few more remade maps coming in this early access period. Gameplay is solid, though not especially innovative.  Dont fix what isnt broken, right?Graphics have a new feel from either preceding main game, and I personally love them.Sound design is currently the weakest overall, but has seen an improvement so far, and I'm hoping for continued improvement. The 4 primary characters return.  They have slightly changed abilities and towers, and I personally dont agree with a few changes here.  It is bearable though.All in all, a good game with great potential.  The price may be a turn off for some, and I believe it's a little steep, but this game promises much more value to come.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few times where Steam has a middle ground for recommending games.As a fan of the Dungeon Defenders series with about 600 hours spread across DD1, DD:E, and DD2 prior, I am leaning towards recommending this game in it's current state, but with a caveat: this game is not polished and will feel janky at times.TL;DR: I would suggest waiting a year or two before purchasing this game after a few more updates are release to polish a lot of the core features.Pros:• This will satisfy a need for Tower Defense X Action Games (although, you will probably spend a lot of time just tower building and perfecting layouts)• The new engine feels like a great choice for this game: looks cleaner and plays smoothly.• Upgrading system has been simplified from DD2 and DD1 in a way, which gives players ease to control their points.• Infinite-ish storage was a welcomed change.• Gameplay has not lost the soul of the previous three games and is a true DD addition to the series.• Easier to level characters compared to previous iterations.• Stages are a mix of familiar and new that gives old players a chance to try a few new setups.Cons:• Missing that Dungeon Defenders visual polish everyone is used to seeing.• The U.I. needs a rework in general. It feels roughly done and not polished as compared to when DD2 was released• Storage needs a rework as well. Would benefit from a stats section and a lot of polish (which is odd since they had those in previous games on release). At this time, it requires too much effort to look at values.• Loots Power Level seems to revolve more around potential upgrades than actual stats at the lower levels (hopefully that changes). As from what I have initially seen, I had items at Power Level 40 and 50 that were still worse than my Level 1 starting weapon.• Gameplay feels a tad bit slower, like it's running at 0.8x speed compared to previous iterations.• Switching characters to look at available loot and level up points during a match is noticeably tedious. Should find a way to streamline menu options for quicker swaps and point allocations.• Although they should be added back in future updates, a lot of QoL functionality from previous games feel like DD:A regressed back to their early early states.• I definitely do miss the special abilities of towers that DD2 had which is painfully missing from DD:A.Hopeful Changes:• Did the Dummy get buffed? Pls tell me it did. At this time, I want to recommend this game, but to also warn new players that this is not a polished Dungeon Defenders experience and I would highly recommend going to try DD1 or DD2 first. However for all old players who want to play the third reboot in the series or for new players who want to go through the original torment of DD1/2 update cycles, it's not bad in its current state, but I would suggest picking this game up in a year or two to avoid aggravation with this game.

That's my DD :DORIGINAL: I'm not saying that Dungeon Defenders 2 was bad but Dungeon Defenders 1 had a little something that made me play for hundreds of hours. I found back this little something in Dungeon Defenders Awakened. Indeed, some will call it a cheap remaster. It is a kind of remaster but the quality really improved if you compare it to the failed project that was Dungeon Defenders Eternity. Some good improvements that were brought with Dungeon Defenders 2 are back like the hero deck that allows you to quickly swap heroes AND level them up ALL AT THE SAME TIME. No more grinding to max level 4 times in a row. The gear changed a bit but the progression seems more interesting. They removed the endless survival, which required, in DD1, to survive between 12 to 24h to have a chance to get something else than just junk all over the place. Comapred to DD1, there are maps back from the first game but also new ones. The heroes are the 4 ones we had in DD1 but, hopefully, they'll add back the others (or different ones, who knows). The biggest issue with the game right now is that for the price it cost, you barely get 25% of the content of DD1 while you can grab DD1 often at 75% off for a couple of bucks. So be aware of this if you decide to purchase.The only other thing that bother me with the game are the stats and upgraded towers. In the first game, the stats were icons with colors and all. It was super easy to quickly understand the gear you picked up. In DDA, there is too much text and the small white icons always getting me lost. Which is why I would not go as far as to say that DD1 is clearly superior.I'd say, play DD1 first, but stop after you finish the Quest for the Lost Eternia Shards DLC. The content that came afterwards, both from the OG devs and the community devs, sharply drops in quality due to balancing issues. Then, maybe pick this one up on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't mind all the negative reviewers who are mad about their overpowered unbalanced early access loot being inaccessible.I had 400+ hours in Dungeon Defenders 1, both on PC and on Xbox, and I am definitely going to play it again after this one.For new players to the Dungeon Defenders series:If you have never played Dungeon Defenders 1, go buy that instead of this one. It is much better. For everyone else:This review is mostly neutral. I think Dungeon Defenders 1 is an overall better game. However, this game is also fun and a fine game, just not as refined and perfect as the first one.The graphics in this game is definitely overall worse than in Dungeon Defenders 1. The UI is absolutely terrible and very clunky. The character movement is clunky and feels less smooth than in DD1. The first one definitely had better map progression and a refined reward system. I was young when I first played the original and I distinctly remember the grind and thought I had to put into progressing through the maps. This one is just too easy or the map progression is based solely on grinding gear and no actual strategy is involved other than "defend the least amount of intersections where enemies meet", which is a sad way for a tower defense game to end up, in my opinion a tower defense game should involve some form of clever thinking (like a puzzle) to solve the map and each map should be different in strategy. This game does not use the fact that it is fully 3D in any clever way and is frankly boring in respect to a tower defense game. The map selection screen is severely lacking in features, and configurable options for each map offering some kind of score multiplier would be nice, but is missing. The game doesn't have a score system as in DD1 which is disappointing.On the other hand, this game features some quality of life improvements over DD1, such as a loot auto collector with filters, auto sell loot. The level design of the new maps is actually quite good and the hero combat is better than in DD1. The tower defense (probably the most important part) is just as good as in DD1 if not better. The towers feel more powerful in this one with stats that actually matters other than just pooling everything into damage.The game is lacking in content. They didn't have to copy every map from the old game. New content is not bad, just as long as it is of the same standard as in DD1. The game currently only features some extra maps that were not in the original, and those are absolutely up to standard with the original DD1 ones. The actual gameplay is quite fun and is just as good as in the original.TL;DR:with "standard" being DD1;- Overall feel of the game is below standard.- Gameplay is same or better than standard.- UI is clunky and much worse than standard.- Graphics are subjective, but in my opinion much worse than standard.- Severely lacking in new content that is better or same as standard.- The game does not have any new interesting and refined mobs over DD1 or other special features.- There's nothing new about this game other than some small QoL features.Take this review as a neutral review, as the game is actually fun to play, and you should try it if you have already reached Ultimate Gear in Dungeon Defenders 1. In my opinion this game just needs more refinement in almost every way, and it should have been better than DD1 not worse or the same, but it should have been just as or more refined and have the same or more (or equally as much new) content. The game should have been in early access for at least 2 years more, so maybe wait 2 years or more if the developers are still actively improving the game in that time.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/13/21 EDIT =================================This went from a Dungeon Defenders 1 remake with huge potential to a downgraded version of DD1 that's made to be played on the switch. They literally re-hauled the entire game in order to smoothly play on that sorry excuse of a console. Switch couldn't handle so many enemies on the map: reduced the amount of enemies. Too many projectiles on the map for the switch to handle: capped all tower firerate. Too many towers on the map, switch no like: reduced the amount of towers you can put on maps.I did a test run, and sadly there was no longer any of that chaos of dungeon defenders that I loved. No more giant hordes of enemies that can overwhelm your defenses with sheer volume if built incorrectly. No more RNG 5 ogre spawns on one door. No more waterfall-esque cannonball turrets because you maxed your tower speed on your squire for memes.It also all feels just *so much easier*. I breezed through a NMHC survival run while completely botching my build because it's just been so long. (Mind you, I put the game down for a while because I could not, for the life of me, manage to pass wave 20 on this specific map with this specific setup; but now here I am, nothing changed on my characters, and I blew through it without repairing, and only 3* upgrades on anything at most.) I reached wave 25 and there were only 800 enemies spawning on a map that previously would spawn 2000+ by wave 20.And to top it all off, the giraffe is now a *hero stat buff* pet. Yup. No more tower stats on giraffes.If you bought this wanting what it was supposed to be, a DD1 remake with more content, then it's sadly turning away from it.HOWEVER. I feel that it is still playable and a decent game if you instead look at it as "Dungeon Defenders Awakened: the pathetic switch downgrade". It still is a generally fun dungeon defenders game, but is just extremely toned down in order to accommodate the lacking hardware of the switch, and the laziness of the developers to make a separate switch version like the community wanted (instead of downgrading the actual already-released game to work on the switch).I'd recommend the game if you don't care about it being a switch downgrade, but personally do not recommend it because it is clearly steering away from what I signed up (and paid) for.Original Review =========================I'll just say three things to people debating to buy this game:1. It's a remake of DD1. The UI is a bit different, the maps you know and love look nicer, and there's even a few new maps as of right now. It doesn't have as much content as DD1 since there are no DLC maps for Awakened, but it's still a pretty damn good remake of a really damn good game.2. Most of the negative comments are from people who are mad that they didn't buy the game when the Kickstarter first started, so you can ignore that chunk of reviews. (It boils down to price fluctuations)3. The rest of the negative comments are from people who are mad that beta progress got pushed to a legacy branch. Yea, it's frustrating, but in my opinion it's a better move than having the early-game stage nonexistent due to beta players giving their new low-leveled friends all the high-leveled gear they don't need.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was made after beating the campaign and a few challenge modes.When i saw this game out, i was having a wave of nostalgia and was hoping to have fun like i did with regular DD, however after a while playing, it felt very lacking.Quick rundown of the game; Dungeon Defenders: Awakened is a Tower Defence game where you build up defences to prevent the horde of enemies from attacking your core, each character has their own weapon and playstyle making each build different. As you defeat the hordes of foes, you will earn gear which will help power you up, which has some replayability to grind out stronger gear and levels.So why am i down-voting this game, as i said before, its very lacking from the past DD, the story is meant to be a continuation from the first and second DD games, but overall it felt like a re-release of the game, most of the maps, not all of them but most of them, i could remember from the first DD game. There are many features from the past titles that are missing that i will highlight that i wish would return.Character Customisation: The characters had different colour palettes layouts that you could choose on startup and can be changed later on when you felt like it, a few even changing the players model. This game doesn't have that so your stuck with the default colours till you unlock a item later down the line where you can use the Transmog system to change your look.Core Customisation: After earning achievements in the past, you could change the look of your core your defending, even changing the colour of what it looked like, not in this.Home Tavern Shop: Occasionally after a run, with the earned gold you earn, the barkeep would have some weapons or pets for sale, this game doesn't have that "yet" but it is mentioned when speaking with the barkeep, so no idea if that'll be added or not.And some minor things lacking but not important;Character Lineup: You have access to only 5 characters at the start, when playing solo you can swap between four of them, which is unique and i actually like, theres a couple of characters missing from the game for example the Summoner, but that doesn't bother me at all.Gem Gathering Aura: I could swear in the past there was a button you could hold and all the gems on the map would slowly gather towards you, saving you time running laps around the map and more time planning your defences.Steam Workshop: I've never used any Steam Workshop mods etc on the previous games but i know some people would like to showcase their own designed maps or even character designs. Again that doesn't bother me but i know for others they would miss that.With that all and said, does this automatically make this a bad game, the answer to that is NO, it may be lacking, but its the classic Dungeon Defenders feel we all know and love. People will enjoy it and some people may even hate it, its all a matter of opinion, the devs however are working on patches and new maps, so down the line in the future, anything is possible, so all i can do is wish this game the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Defenders Awakened is a tower defence game, heavily influenced and based on Dungeon Defenders 1, which was a classic in the history of tower defence games.DDA (Dungeon Defenders Awakened) is effectively a remake of DD1, based in a different time period in the DD universe. This review will break down the game into several parts. These parts are-•	Graphics•	Gameplay•	BalanceI will explain how these factors influence the game, starting with graphics and concluding with balance.1.	Graphics.The graphics in DDA are excellent. They take heavy inspiration from the DD1 graphics, however, they are much more refined and polished. The colours are much more bold and abrasive, which is a stark contrast to DD1’s dull, flat look. The visual effects from in-game abilities and weapons are outstanding.2.	Gameplay.The gameplay is good.. not great, just good. There is very little bad clipping with enemy interactions on the map. It flows well for the most part, and it is satisfying to play. The flow is disrupted, however, at the end of waves when you have to run around picking up mana. This can sometimes take more than a minute on big maps. Hero damaging is fun and viable, and is a valuable feature to exploit against powerful enemies such as Ogres. The gameplay gets highly repetitive at later-game stages, when you are experienced enough to roll most content first try.3.	BalanceThe balance is one of the biggest flaws in this game. Some defences are flat out overpowered as they are so dominant in their ability to take down troubling enemies, such as Djinns and Ogres, an example being the Deadly Strike Tower. Other defences are monstrously over-tuned, such as gas traps lasting for 1 and a half minutes, the length of an entire wave on quite a number of maps. Hero DPS is balanced for the most part, but there is really no reason to use one over the other… besides Squire. Squires DPS is pointless. Just play a ranged character.The over-reliance on certain defences makes things stale, fast. Late game, a lot of defences lose viability for consistent use, and only work on heavily rehearsed maps.Good game in general, I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: *5/14/2024 EDIT*I picked this game back up after a few years because I got the itch again. I wanted to see how far it had come. I have to say, this game is everything I wanted the original DD1 to be. I am leaving my original comment intact for anyone to review. It was overall positive, but had some criticism. I officially retract all criticism. Here is my edited, review. (This is more aimed at those who played the original or may still play it.):1) You are no longer punished for playing solo!! The original was nearly impossible to play solo in the endgame without mods. Advancement is possible solo and still feels good with other players. Progression is quicker and feels much more rewarding. It feels too easy for the DD veteran, but try to consider those just starting out. The endgame will still kick your butt until you get those late wave drops. Then you scale the difficulty and do it again!2) The classes I loved the most were added. It certainly wasn't because of my request I am sure. I think the devs always had a solid plan for what the game would turn into. At least that's how it feels. As mentioned in the original post, I wanted the Summoner added. It was. The Summoner no longer gets its own tower resource, but I will get over it. It makes considering strategy that much better. The Summoner having its own placement limit in the original was broken.3) Familiars are as powerful as ever. Another criticism in my original comment. Only, the super powerful familiars are way easier to get. It doesn't feel exclusive, but is still super rewarding.4) The new features were a pleasant surprise. Each class has lootable modifications. Amazing add. I can't say enough good things about this. Exp is balanced better. Upgrades are balanced better. The Apprentice is an absolute monster.5) You don't necessarily have to choose between dps and building anymore!! Not at least in the early stages of the endgame. My stats are perfectly balanced to reflect a "jack of all trades build" and it works! You don't have to build two of your favorite class anymore. Keep in mind, I have only started the endgame.While the original will forever hold a special place in my heart, this iteration fills every hole the original had. It feels like it was made for the hardcore fans. If you loved the original, you will love this one. It's more of the same, but sometimes that is what we want. I don't mean to be "that guy" who keeps comparing this game to the original, but it's the best point of reference. This game is worth full price because it reflects everything a game should be in an age where prices are skyrocketing. I have a clear bias, but I don't care. 10/10!!!Feel free to skip the rest. It's just my original comment with critical opinions that I technically have no right to express. Thanks for reading it anyway and I appreciate the dev for taking the time to respond.**********************************************************************************************************This game feels like a half baked version of the original Dungeon Defenders (that is sort of a compliment). This game has just enough of those elements that made the original game so much fun. 4 very familiar characters are available to play. There is some hope that more of the DLC characters from the original game will be added. The Summoner would be a welcome addition.For those that have sunk 1000+ hours into the original like I have: While I do like this game enough to recommend it, it's still just a pseudo remake of the original. Characters, towers and quite a few maps remain unchanged from the original. Not all gameplay translated over...The Apprentice no longer has a directional charge attack to name one feature I miss. Most familiars were either removed or redesigned. The Genie is no longer an endgame, early stage familiar. From what I can tell, game changing familiars like the Apprentice Familiar and Guardian have been removed which is a little disappointing. Tower synergy is pretty on point which was my biggest expectation.For new players: don't listen to the folks complaining about "a lack of content". The original game evolved to have lots of maps, but it was never about expansive content in that regard. It's about designing better strategies on maps cranked up to harder difficulties. Pro tip for newbs: create all 4 heroes at once and maintain them so they level together. If you are a solo player, you will want to practice toon swapping to get the best of all worlds. Build your strategies and share them. It's pretty addicting. The "I beat the game on hard in 3 hours" crowd has no idea how difficult and fun this game can be. My 6 y/o can play this game on hard.... This same crowd needs to comment again after raging because they died on a hardcore survival play and watched as 3 ogres wrecked their barricades and smashed their crystal on wave 24.If you are still playing the original, don't bother with this one unless you want to support the developers with hopes that they will continue to add more of what we loved from the first game. I am all about supporting folks that seem to be listening to the cult fan base that this franchise has amassed over the years. So far, I don't see any indication of super active development though. One can hope. I'm still happy with my purchase as is.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit BelowDungeon Defenders 1 is a janky, outdated, unpolished, mess of a tower defense game. Yet it is still leagues better then Dungeon Defenders Awakened. The original has so much content, so much charm, so much of a history, it is impossible to remake. Yet DDA tried to remake it for a modern audience and it has failed to live up to the task. First off DDA has about 40% of the content Dungeon Defenders has, while yes, DDA content is more polished, less bugs and looks nicer it still is missing dozens of maps. Everything runs smoother but it also has been dumbed down to the point of making everything boring. It doesn't play like a fantasy rpg tower defence game, DDA plays like a cartoon minecraft game. Gear progression has gotten so dumbed down, so easy, and condensed that everyone just power levels to get to the actual levels where you can get meaningful equipment. There is no early game or mid game you just power farm to equip gear to gain the ability to farm for higher level gear, that's about it. Once you beat the main story which is 80% re-used content from DD1 that's it. It just farming for the sake of farming, farming to get better stats to be able to farm places that drop equipment with better stats. The content doesn't get harder by making you play differently, it gets harder by taking things away from the player, like the awful rift mode. Every time they update this game it's half baked, tedious to farm but a joke once you complete it. It tries it's hardest to be DD1 but it doesn't know what made that game good, so instead of getting a brand new game with new ideas we get a half baked remake of which every DD1 player hates but is so niche it doesn't draw brand new players. Only avid Dungeon Defenders players play this game which begs the question, why would you play this game instead of the old ones? The devs haven't given an answer. You can remake all the old content you want, if it's not as good or better then the original whats the point in remaking it. Dungeon Defenders 1 has the exact same story mode with 2x as many maps an entire dlc side story, a dozen bonus maps, more heroes, more customizable options, more game modes, more mods to try out, more fan content to try out. All DDA did was cut Dungeon Defenders 1 in half sprinkled in some aspects from DD2 made it run smoother and look prettier then asked for your money. Not to mention how they completely lied on their kick starter page. The company has gone down hill. They've made 2 great games but not they just copy what those did in hopes to re catch those lighting in a bottle games. If you want DD1 again then update the original game and move on to new projects. The amount of money, time, manpower, and the sheer amount of praise from the community you would've gotten updating the orgnial game instead would be huge. Edit: After coming a good 6 months later to play DDA again, I've changed my mind a bit. I went from disliking this game to being neutral on it. Now that a lot of the content they promised at the beginning is finally out, ( 7 months late ) it is a very solid game. If DDA released with all of it's current content back then it would have been so much better. I like the new summoner, it's a more balanced take on the og one. The remade maps look amazing. The thing about DDA is that going from DD1 to DDA is night and day. DDA runs way smoother, looks way cleaner, better ui, has so much QOL it is really easy to get back into to. I still think the late game content is way too grindy with no incentive but tbh most DD1 late game was just brute forcing everything with over statted towers to so . . . do I like the improvements DDA has made yes I really love them. However DD1 is a decade old at this point, it is very very easy to improve over a 10+ plus year old game. If DDA is alive after a year. If we get at least 2 more heroes, an actual paid dlc story like DD1 shards dlc I would be happy with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, because it's basically just the original game, but worse, with less content. But the original was a great game, so this is too.With so many obvious and annoying glitches and oversights, I don't understand why this is considered a full release, and not early access.Why does selecting "equip" from your items menu only move the item to the top of your list, and not actually equip it? You have to select equip, have the item teleported across your screen, and then actually equip it.You can easily get around that by just equipping items off the floor, like everyone always does, but why is it that ONLY when an item is on the floor, if the game considers the item an upgrade over what you have equipped, it displays ALL of the item's stats in green, signifying an increase, even if that stat is severely lower than what you have equipped? For some items that might not be a big deal, but say you're playing Monk, someone with both ranged and melee attacks, and you see an item with *slightly* higher melee attack, and MUCH lower ranged attack. The game will consider that an upgrade, and display the terrible ranged attack stat in green, prompting you to equip it, despite being a significant downgrade to your current weapon, if you're primarily using ranged attacks.Every few minutes in the game, I come across a very minor but inconvenient glitch, oversight, or just bit of bad design (why doesn't the game tell you what stats do? Especially considering every stat has had its name changed from previous games).Love the game, because I love the genre, but this is the most inconvenient full release I've played in awhile. Just shocking that all the annoying oversights I've seen are the most obvious things that anyone playing the game will find

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT TO MY REVIEW: With the recent development of the game, I can't recommend this game anymore. The game seems to have strayed further and further away from what made DD1 good. With questionable game design direction and the devs' refusal to listen to the community, and also the fact that the game hasn't been update for many months, and also the fact that the game currently averages 37 players daily, and the fact the multiplayer has been down without being patched for a while now, there is no way I can recommend this game anymore. If you're interested, you can still read my review from a year ago right below.JANUARY 2021 REVIEW (doesn't apply anymore):Alright, this is going to be a lengthy review, but I feel like this is needed. As you might have guess from my amount of play time, I'm recommending this game and find it to be a very good game. However, more context is needed. I'm reviewing the game in its current stat (January 2021).Let's start up with the most important thing: my recommendation varies depending on who you are. If you're the kind of gamer that likes playing through the game's story once and then move on to the next game, then you'll probably like this game in its current state. The first campaign playthrough is really enjoyable and, for the most part, well designed and well balanced. Boss might be a bit hard though, but I'm sure the devs will rebalance them. Either way, it's not so terrible.If you're a Dungeon Defenders fan and plan on playing for hundreds or even thousands of hours, then I would ask you what kind of player you are. Do you require a finished products so you can play nonstop for many weeks? Or are you fine with a game that still feels like early access and will get many updates to add more content? If you want to play a finished product, I would say play DD1. If you don't mind playing for a couple of weeks, then waiting for the next update to jump back into the game, then I would say go for DDA.The game is REALLY good, it's just lacking some content. This game recaptures the DD1 atmosphere and feeling while adding some nice Quality of Life stuff, like the hero deck from DD2 (all heroes in your deck gain XP, and you can swap in and out heroes in and out of your deck). There is no doubt in my mind that with time and many updates this game will become as good as DD1. The game currently is basically DD1 at the beginning before the Eternia Shard maps came out, but with more content and lots of quality of life stuff (hero deck, free hero points reset, etc.). So if you're a DD1 fan, I 100% recommend DDA.Like I said above, even though the game is listed as released, it technically is a lot like an early access game and should be viewed as such if you decide to buy the game. There are some bugs, content is limited in the endgame, balancing needs some rework, new maps need to be added (there are only 15 maps currently), new heroes need to be added (there are only 5 heroes currently), etc. Some people seem to think that this is just a DD1 remake, which is not true. It is highly inspired by DD1 though, and understandably. Out of the 15 maps in the game, 9 of them are DD1 maps, 1 of them is a map from CDT in DD1, and 5 of them are completely new maps to the franchise. However, there are some differences, and some major ones at that. Let's start with the smaller changes: 1) we now have a hero deck with 4 slots. All heroes in your deck will gain XP at the same time. Don't worry, it's not like DD2 early days when we were limited by the deck, you can swap in and out heroes from your deck during build phases. 2) There are no more negative stats on gear like in DD1.3) Hero abilities were changed a bit. The huntress now has a hero boost that increases her fire rate, the monk's tower boost is a bit different, etc.4) You can reset your hero points and respend them for free now. Now here are the current major changes/new stuff:1) We have a new game mode called Rift Mode: enemies are stronger and have new skills. Like rifted ogres can throw kobolds at you, rifted djinns can buff enemies and make them immune to crowd control, etc.2) Clearing a map on rift mode will reward you with a fusion gear. Fusion is the new element in the game, and no enemy can resist it. Fusion damage also deals double damage to rift enemies.3) A fusion set of gears will evolve one of your hero's defense into a fusion form. For instance, a fusion ensnare aura now is fusion element (so not poison, so it's can't be resisted), and also enemies inside it will receive 10% more damage. 4) We have a new difficulty called massacre, and there's a new mob in that difficulty called the siren. Sirens can cast an aura around them and give enemies inside it a permanent resistance (fire, lightning, poison, or physical, but never fusion). 5) There are now bosses at the end of a survival run on boss maps. Those bosses will drop a random pet from that act. So the Demon Lord in survival can drop the Deeper Well pet (Griffin), the Ancient Mines pet (rock pet), the Lava Mines pet (Steam Robot), the Alch Labs pet (Cat), or the Magus Quarter pet (Paddle pet). This make a lot of earlier pets a lot more relevant. So to conclude my review, this is a pretty good game if you like action tower defense games, especially if you like DD1. Add to that a lot of new content coming in the future, and DDA has the potential of being as good as the current DD1 and even more.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is currently going through a fairly buggy release; your save file might get deleted, it may crash on launch or be unplayable, etc. For this reason, if you aren't willing to deal with these kinds of bugs, it's probably best to wait a week or so for them to get ironed out; the devs have said on Discord that they're aware of these issues and are working on a fix. Most of all, please remember that this is an EARLY ACCESS GAME. It is obviously going to be missing features, because it is not the full game yet; it's early access for a reason. These features will come in time.However, I wouldn't say that the game is unfun or not in a playable state right now, quite the opposite in fact. A lot of people have complained that it feels much like a copy and paste of DD1; to which I'd say... that's a bad thing how? I thought the entire problem in the sequels was that they moved too far away from the original game? So far, Dungeon Defenders Awakened feels like a remake with some nice quality of life features added, such as being able to reallocate your skill points at will, improved melee animations for squire and monk, and some nice new graphic design (this is a subjective point, even original DD had a very "you like it or you hate it" art style.)In short, I definitely recommend this game; it has plenty of content as is, and if you're willing to tolerate some potentially game-breaking bugs, you'll have a great time. If not, wait a week or so. If you played and enjoyed the original Dungeon Defenders, you will absolutely like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: After watching two streams that addressed the problem this game faced at launch. I've decided to change my product recommendation.  Although I do think the game is self feels a little bland in the itemization department, this game could still provide hundreds if not thousands of hours of enjoyment.   I think players should be wary about product pricing since this game is a good example of how something good (lowering the game cost) upset some of their player base because many bought it with certain expectations based on their early access FAQ and as a result ended up buying it for 25% more than the launch price.  It may be common practice in f2p games that offer early access for a premium cost, but in many b2p games, the increased cost comes with known benefits that a consumer is aware of before the purchase is made. Original review:The game is really niche but if you enjoy tower defense with a small mix of arpg then you might find this game to be a good time killer. As for the reason I'm not giving it a thumbs up  is that I wanted players to be more aware of misinformation. In this case players bought the game under the pretense there would be no wipe and that the cost would no change. Although there technically wasn't a wipe, instead they created a new server for players to start fresh on. My biggest problem is the change in price point. Once they were questioning their price, they should have removed that from the faq and made sure employees of CG were made aware that they shouldn't confirm/deny any possible sale or change in price.  I think the lack of communication or rather allowing misinformation to spread because no one could take 30 seconds to remove 3 lines from their faq shouldn't be an acceptable practice.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you've put hundreds of hours into DD1 and are on the fence about pulling the trigger on DDA. You've come to read some reviews and gauge the public's response to this game in the hopes of reading that one review that either sells you on the game or makes you delete it from your wishlist so you can move on with your life. I've been there, my friend. That was me basically the entire time the game was in early access (EA). It was on my wishlist for a while but I just couldn't bring myself to buy it for two reasons:1. I've been burned on EA games in the past. 2. The reviews I had read all had the "Stay Away" vibe to them.I finally decided to bite the bullet on the day it came out of EA and I must say I'm glad I did. Chromatic Games (CG) has done, in my opinion, a good job putting a more modern spin on the soon-to-be 9 year old classic that we all know and love.Some things that I like:-The Hero Deck: A new (to me) system that lets up to 4 heroes receive XP simultaneously.  -The visuals: Overall, the game looks great. It was nice to see some of the old DD1 maps "remastered" as well.-The Challenge: I thought I would try nightmare after beating the campaign on insane. I proceeded to get my ♥♥♥♥ pushed in by an Ogre with 750k health immediately after starting wave 1. I find the progression is just difficult enough to make you want to grind the gear/levels to get better and keep going, rather than just making you want to /uninstall.-The Nostalgia: It's nice to be back in 2011 when there were just 4 heroes, some towers and a crystal or three. Part of the reason I took such a big break from DD1 was the release of all the DLC heroes. More content is all well and good, but  it was impossible to push late game content without buff beams, reflect beams and summoned archer walls. It basically became pay to win, and pay to win is bad.-You can Double-Jump. Whoever's idea that was should get a raise.Some things I don't like:-Upgrading/repairing aura's that are stacked together can be somewhat challenging. (especially when there are 7 Dark Elf Warriors trying to involve you in a very violent orgy). In DD1, when I press the upgrade or repair button, my cursor defaults to the aura/tower/trap which has the lowest "rank" or which has the lowest health. That was nice. Bring that back please. Edit: It was brought to my attention that if you press "T" while upgrading/repairing, it switches to an aerial view that also snaps the cursor to defenses! :)  -Monk auras slowly lose health even if there are no enemies walking through them. -The indicator for what "rank" your towers are is a little lack-lustre to me. Bring back the Chevrons/stars!-It can sometimes take a while to join games you've been invited to. Sometimes I just get brought back to the title screen and don't actually make it into the game.-The opening cut-scene is "unskipable" for about 15-20 seconds.  There are a lot of negative reviews from EA buyers/kickstarter backers being upset that all of their progress was wiped upon release (despite being told this wouldn't happen) and that the price of the game has come down. I can understand the frustration there but, to me, that's the risk you take when you buy into EA titles. (Part of the reason I waited to buy this game. Also, $40 is a tad steep for an EA game IMO)My point is: Don't let those negative reviews sway your decision. Bottom line: If you enjoyed DD1 and are considering purchasing this game, I say go for it. If you're one of those people that "don't want to support bad devs" or "The devs betrayed me and hurt my feelings, how can I trust anyone ever again?", then I guess don't buy it. This is a review for the game, not CG.Also, it should be noted that CEO of CG released a statement saying that they're going to try to allow people to port over some of their heroes/gear/money from Legacy (the dank void where all your ♥♥♥♥ went if you played EA) to "Play" (Current version). If you made it this far, thank you for your time and happy defending!

_childDocuments_.review: I played hundreds if not thousands of hours of the original Dungeon Defenders on console and then hundreds again through Steam, I did not regret any second of it.I gave this one a shot in the hopes that it would bring back that feeling I had when playing the series for the first time. In a lot of ways I am pretty happy with this version (updated graphics, overhauled enemy/hero model & skins, new heroes, new maps). HOWEVER, like a lot of the other reviewers mentioned already, I absolutely cannot support a developer who downgrades the experience for PC players because of the Switch port. I did not buy this game for a switch version, if I wanted to do that I would have bought the game on the Switch.The biggest problem to keep in mind is that any future updates that will be released, will be optimized for the Switch version, meaning the PC version will take a hit. We already saw this in several patches e.g. Reduction of the number of enemies, Attack Rate Cap on Defenses etc. Besides this, there are also loads of bugs and issues that are yet to be addressed e.g. Enemies getting stuck in certain locations on the maps, some enemies not leaving their spawn doors, LOADS of UI/Menu + UX issues (somehow the latest updates made those worse).Whether this will get Chromatic Games to make changes is doubtful, im simply trying to raise awareness to other players so you do not waste your hard earned money. This is ultimately the only way developers will listen to feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed Dungeon Defenders since the first version years ago and in general they have all been fun.  This one does take me back to DD first wave but with better controls and options.   The number of unique levels are not great but with 6 difficulty levels for multiple modes it has more content than it looks like.   It is unfortunate that the content is spread over 100 character levels.  Even with so many options for unique game experiances the fact that is all takes place on only 15 unique levels is a bit short.  Now like the original DD I expect we will see more levels and story as things progress but for now it may feel a bit more of a grind than many will want.   One thing I did like was when I got to insane on one dungeon and found they added a second crystal and area.  It was unfortunate I could not do the two crystal version on a difficulty that did not have a build time limit.  More twists like this and the challenge levels do break things up but I do really look forward to a bit more content so I can get to level 100 without playing the same maps and difficulties 10+ times each.   One final complaint that I hope they fix is the lack of information.  If you want to know what a skill or ability does you seem to have to go create a new character and read the discriptions there.  If you want to know what effect putting points into skills does you have to look up post from people who have hacked it out of the code or done tests to figure it out.  The data is out there on the net but the game would really benefit from having it in game.   In fact the legacy version had quite a bit more tool tips which I miss already.   Overall if you like Dungeon Defenders it is likely you will find something to like in this version though you may need to wait for a few more patches or at most the first DLC or two before it really pops.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a GREAT update to the Dungeon Defenders franchise. It does everything part 1 did well, and improves it. Hands down.However, it is also suffering from all of part 1's shortcomings, and some.Such as, ridiculous wave durations... There is no way to speed up the game clock when you want to wade through a wave you know you are going to beat, but can't skip because you need the mana...Also, the amount of loot that drops is sometimes hard to pick through using the given means, with any haste, which further increases the DELAY between waves. The small highlight underneath each item is supposed to indicate it's rarity, and would do so reliably if some of the terrain wasn't able to obscure it (or other items do so). Forcing you to pause over each item if you do not want to risk missing an uncommon or rarer item, in some circumstances.Also, once a long (deep level) wave gets going... There really isn't much to do but wait, and wait, and wait, until an ogre (or the boss) walks out so you can DPS it for a minute, and go back to waiting. Sure, you might need to repair (when not playing tactician mode) or upgrade a tower, etc... But honestly, these things become rare after the noob levels get pushed through.(I have started alt-tabing out of the game to do something else while such waves run)Besides a few gimmicks, like Boosting and such, there really is very little your hero can do to influence the outcome of a wave besides DPS DPS DPS... And more DPS. Which can get quite stale after a while.I could get even more nit-picky but I won't.I am not saying any of these downsides is a deal breaker. Even when combined in a really bad wave, they are forgivable. But they are also fixable... A few, easily so. But I get it. Small teams need to focus on things that add the most return on the time and resources invested. I would rather have this game than continue to play an aging part 1, or even touch part 2 again (shudder). For that I am thankful.

_childDocuments_.review: well for the amount of time i decided to put into this game i am surprised it took me so long to realize that each game this development team touches is nothing but a sad excuse for a "work in progress". DD2 was worse imo when it came to progress being made to the game. Every time there was something added it went through multiple reiterations basically just slowing down production for new content. They literally had an entire character involved with upgrading equipment moved to a table in the tavern doing nothing but sit there. Back to DDA though.... There just hasnt been anything meaningful added to the game in a while now and no new characters, maps, or anything worth mentioning. Despite how rushed some development teams can get with publishers i think this team needs one to keep them on track and not shifting ideas more than i can take any more. I was wondering what happened to the content being made for it after a while when i noticed that they started splitting development with DD2 again confusing the hell out of me as to why a small team would do that (mind you i dont keep up with them much to know anything about their decisions etc). Then they throw a curve ball and release another iteration of DD??? why??? there is no focus or solid ideas with this team. I had so much hope with them when they had community driven development for DD2 in terms of what content they would add first based on community votes, unfortunately that too was pulled out from under everyone. It should have been clear from the very beginning what would be happening now when there was a Moba version of DD2 in an alpha phase before the tower defense aspect was even in development. But guess what??? that was scrapped too!!! xD  I cant say i wont ever play a game in the series in the future but i will never ever recommend this series to anyone as long as they continue the way they have been.

_childDocuments_.review: I am barely an hour and a half in, so take that into account. From what I see, this is a worthy successor to the original Dungeon Defenders! And that is saying something: wholesome fun that is great to look at.My main criticism with the first game was its community: while not inherently toxic, there was a lot of boosting and gifting of overpowered (and sometimes hacked) items. What's the big deal you ask? Well the fun in these games is not BEING level 100 with the top gear. The fun is progressively getting there: a small improvement here, a nudge there, and suddenly you can do that map you couldn't before.But getting boosted to level 100 and gifted amazing items is an infinitely short-lived pleasure. And now that you are at the top, what do you do, you know? No, the fun is working your way through the levels, difficulty and bosses, getting better stats and items, and being happy with every little improvement you get.If you agree with this idea that gifting and boosting ruins the fun, join me in my group called "Dungeon Defenders Hardcore". We can play together without any boosting, hacking or anything to ruin the fun of PROGRESSION.If my feeling that this is very much like the first game holds true, this will be the best money you've spent in a LONG time.
