_childDocuments_.review: I edited my review because the game has changed a bit!I really, really love Dungeon Defenders titles. And I mean . Awakened is no exception. I even have a Dungeon Defenders Awakened t-shirt from the crowdfunding and I wear it happily!This game has everything I would really want from a Dungeon Defenders game, it's an action game, and it's a tower defense game, with RPG elements too! Does this game meet my criterias? Yes.There is a high variety of towers in this game, towers that shoot, towers that slow, towers that shoot and slow. There is also a high variety of playable classes in this game, heroes that shoot, heroes that boost, and heroes that shoot and boost. Is the apprentice the best class like every Dungeon Defenders out there? An astouding yes. I will not hear your opinion on this.The game does towers really well, they all very much feel satisfying to use. The apprentice is well captured in essence. Truly a masterful class to play.I have to say though I have a few gripes. Rifted Mode is hilariously easy considering all enemies elemental resistances are put to only one and that's fusion damage. On the same issue with rifted, you have to genuinely make one hero per tower as of current, except for the first tower thanks to the Arcanist Helmet (that is going to be removed for hopefully a better system!) heavily limiting your variety of towers when there are so many good combos you could be doing. Another issue with rifted is that... you can only use rifted sets and that's it. You don't get to use any fun specialized sets in the game except rifted tower 1,2,3,4,5. There is no variety for people who enjoy theorycrafting in this RPG game. Unless you don't play Rifted mode. Unlike Dungeon Defenders 1, the floor loot is bad. If you want good gear, you need to open the wave 25 chest of any survival. Then every 5 waves in endless you will get a good piece of gear. Loot isn't guaranteed to have all 4 builder stats, and very often it won't. Which is interesting considering they do seem intent to remove needless grinding seeing as they removed negative stats. This game has an amazing soundtrack by the same person who made the OST for DD1 (and DD2 I believe!). There is no free2play bs! This is a paid game! There are cosmetics DLCs you can buy but that's only if you want the support the devs! (I recommend you do!) The devs are as far as I am seeing working actively with the community and getting feedback! The engine is a lot less buggy and expandable than DD1's, very promising for the game's future and future titles! The apprentice is in this game. And you can give him the DD1 apprentice's hat if you have the DLC for it, and then give the DD1 apprentice's hat to all your heroes. Everyone is the apprentice now. Everyone. The rune system has crazy potential for unique interaction and truly custom builds, I want to see more out of it, more runes, more uniqueness, more! I love armor sets in this game other than the rifted ones. There should be more armor sets. There just should be. I want to see armor set that give unique perks so I can like above with runes, create more unique custom builds! The enemies ragdoll when they get tower'd or hero'd. Great fun for all the family. The game's aesthetic is gorgeous. The maps are beautiful. What can I say? There is a customization system to make your heroes look how you want them to be. _childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about DDA and I'll explain my thoughts below so that people reading this review can make an informed decision before they buy this game.DDA is essentially a remaster of DD1, which 10 years ago was one of the best games on steam. The sheer amount of content and the innovative take on tower defense made DD1 one of my favorite games in my entire library, and when played with friends was one of the funnest experiences I've ever had. DDA in it's current state (writing this on the week of release of DDA) has the same content and gameplay as the base game of DD1, but with many welcome quality of life changes, and nice updated graphics. However, there's no innovation this time around. DDA is essentially the same game as DD1, and it just doesn't feel as interesting or fun as DD1 did. I wish there were new mechanics to deal with, more enemy diversity, a different kind of skill tree, elemental effects that actually matter, more tower customization, or more character customization, but there isn't. DDA feels uninspired,  and there isn't much to keep me going back to the game. The game difficulty uses an archaic and boring system for difficulty where enemies just become meat shields instead of having mechanics that change how you interact with them. The loot that you get from playing the game pretty much just boils down to stat sticks that buff your numbers. There's no theory crafting, no deep character customization, and no true meaningful impact from the loot. The point I'm trying to make is, DDA is just a reskin for DD1 with QOL changes and that's okay. If you want to play DD1 but hate the UI and the graphics and want to play the same exact gameplay then DDA is for you. However, it's 2020 and modern video games have evolved past what DD1 has to offer, Would that the devs had taken this chance to revitalize the dungeon defenders series with DDA and taken some risks and added some actually innovative changes that would have made the gameplay more interesting, but that's not the case. Perhaps in the future when the game receives more content updates, there will be some more changes to the game that add more depth and replayability, but for now it's pretty much just a nice nostalgic gimmick of a game that could have been much more.Thanks for taking the time to read this review, and I hope that if you end up getting the game that you enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE (7/2023): The developers have officially announced that they are dramatically slowing down development on this game, and that new content is basically no longer planned. Since the original time of this review, not much was added. Anybody looking to play an Action TD game should look elsewhere, whether that's the original DD or DD2, or something else like Sanctum or Orcs Must Die. Do not buy this abandoned game, I guarantee that your time and money will be better spent elsewhere.------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW:As an avid fan of the DD franchise and Action TD genre, it is upsetting to see the state of Awakened after two years of development. Advertised in the kickstarter as a "brand-new" game that "recaptures the soul" of the original game, Awakened misses the mark on many of the things that made the original game great.One of my fondest memories with the franchise was a decade ago when I joined a public game where the towers placed had such low fire rates that they caused my computer to lag. While lag can certainly be avoided, I found the absurdity of what you could do with a max character extremely enticing as a newbie to the genre. The sheer absurdity of the game's towers fueled a power trip and provided tangible feedback to your character's progression throughout the difficulty tiers, and this unfortunately is not fulfilled in Awakened. The towers in Awakened were nerfed substantially in this regard to ensure that the game is able to run on all platforms (such as the Switch with its notably weak hardware potential), and while being multi-platform is great for accessibility, it results in the game's "feel" being significantly diminished compared to the first game.Another key point of criticism I have for the current state of Awakened is the glaring lack of new content when compared to the original. Despite being advertised as an entirely new product, Awakened has only recently started to add brand new content to the game, with all prior updates essentially just adding remastered content from other games (such as old maps and the Warden, which is a re-imagining of the Dryad from DD2). On that note, the new content has not provided the variety and engagement needed to truly feel like new content. In addition to that, no new content has been released in about a full year.Chromatic has not displayed that they have a true "vision" for what they want this game to be, because so far they have essentially just cloned DD1 and diluted its elements down to a depressing degree, and have provided very minuscule new content over the two years since launch. In its current state, there is not much "game" to be played, only a monotonous grind that results in you being allowed to grind more. _childDocuments_.review: It's in active development so take all this with a grain of salt. Did you like the gameplay of DD2 but hate the microtransaction spam, the horrible loot drop rates, and the shard grind? This game takes all of the best parts of DD2 and removes all the garbage. Don't get me wrong, it's still a grind game; but it's a grind game that you can see the progress in beyond waiting for the RNG gods to get you your 10th defense rate so you can gild another one finally. The GoodTowers all feel like they have a place depending on map and spec. Everything feels viable through Insane difficulty so far, as long as you allocate your points around. Oh, and you don't have to pay anything to respec, points are movable whenever you have access to your inventory. Visually the game is stunning, imo, and the sound effects fit well with the aesthetic of the game. Also devs are very communicative about their plans so we know more characters, including the EV2 from DD2 will make it's way over. The BadTooltips. We need more of them. None of the stats actually have a tooltip saying specifically what that stat gives you when points are invested. That information is available online, but when I find a good grind game I don't want to be alt tabbing to read a wiki article before making every decision as I make progress. The MiddleThe difficulty spikes are real, and I think they're fine, but unexplained. For example, in Nightmare difficulty they start dropping spiders around the map that will attack your towers sometimes, and you as well. Mechanically, how they target, and what their abilities are, can't be found in the game.  I think an essential of tower defense games is making the stats available in a logbook of some kind. I don't mind seeing a new enemy that looks like a shark and having an "oh ♥♥♥♥" moment when he suddenly pushes my wall out of place, but I want to then be able to look up how he works so that I can plan for it next time. Currently, finding that information is difficult. THE WORSTBuild timers. Forcing me to build stuff on a timer doesn't make the game fun for me. It should be a toggle for a loot bonus,, or a point bonus, but as it is I genuinely am having a hard time enjoying the campaign at Nightmare difficulty only because of the timer. I can't imagine I'll enjoy it more when I get to Massacre. I want to strategize, not deal with artificial anxiety because the devs want me to go faster? I pray that they remove this or make it a toggle every time I play. _______TLDR: All in all this game is fantastic. The devs are very active in their development and utilizing community feedback and I can't wait to see how it continues to improve. I wish they'd remove timers on the build phase, or make it a toggle.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my "pandemic lockdown" games in 2020, clocked over 300 hours then. Recently came back, this is a good semi-afk game; once you have your setup running, it involves a lot of semi-AFK farming for equipment. You can watch videos, do some light reading while this runs on another device. There are still a lot of hands-on situations, such as when transitioningto higher difficulties or maximising your push into higher and higher waves. Comparing this to 2018 Dungeon Defenders 2, I like this more. The progression rate feels reasonable. You don't need to pay to expand your stash either. Currently, there is a Steam guide that really helps new/returning players to adjust to the game. I have to clarify the multiplayer is mostly dead, you'll have to play solo most of the time. Progression doesn't seem to require other players (tested in endgame Massacre Survival Hard Core Rifted). In terms of bugs, there are some, but far fewer than it was in 2020. I still don't know how to reduce some of the blinding flashes from certain defense towers, turning down the graphics settings doesn't get rid of it completely (do take note if you're photosensitive). It also gets quite annoying to have to make multiple of the same characters to serve different purposes, for example one Guardian for Owl Perch towers, another for Obelisk towers. This is mainly for endgame though.Note this game also involves a lot of loot, so if you're not used to ARPGs or games with loot filters, that part might suck for you. It would be better if it had an option auto-start timer for solo Survival farming. Also, having an option auto casting for boost monks/apprentice would be useful too.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr; A more modern take on their first game. Pros:Similar to the originalSome new characters to playLots of QoL improvementsA new difficulty toggle that is fairly interesting (Rifted)Cons:Simplified gear systemSimplified character rolesFairly easy until much higher difficulties, which are gated behind levelingThere are still several bugs.Review: I have had a lot of fun playing through the game. I personally recommend DD1 over DDA, but both are enjoyable even if you have played the other. Actually, it would be harder to go from DDA to DD1 because some of the QoL that was added in DDA is not in DD1 and will annoy you.The game has several of the same maps from DD1. Some of them look a lot better or have the layout changed to be less annoying or janky. Others look like they were made in MS Paint and they lost the original assets used. This could be due to my graphics settings, but seriously, something is wrong with Royal Gardens.The new classes they added in DDA were probably why I had a lot of fun. They are fairly unique and interesting to play and I was able to level both at the same time using the hero deck system, which I believe was a concept from DD2 (which I have not played much).The other cool thing they added was a Rifted toggle, which gives each enemy a unique ability and causes the 5th wave to drop fusion gear to counter them. Some of the abilities include archer's have homing arrows. Dark elf warriors are stealthed and cannot be attacked by most towers. This has been fairly interesting to play through as it adds a different direction for difficulty and loot. I would gladly take more toggles like this. Especially if they could be all turned on at the same time.However, once I reached nightmare difficulty I realized just how stale the loot system was in DDA. It's fairly linear and doesn't allow for much customization of your character. 3 pieces of gear are related to dps (or active) stats the rest are related to tower stats. Not only that, but most of them eventually get all of the relevant stats in varying amounts. This means that a piece of gear that is higher level is often better in almost every way. There is no choice, you get a higher level piece of gear, you equip it. This in my mind is its biggest downgrade from DD1. The linear gear combined with the fairly samey stats creates very little room to create characters that fill unique roles. You do not have the Jester or Summoner, but even if they did, they wouldn't have a move/upgrade focused Jester because you cannot focus enough on abilities to make it any different from a DPS Jester. Same goes for pretty much every class I have seen. You have a couple of random "bonus" stats on gear, but they only really effect generic stats.There are also a few bugs here and there. For example Ogres and Dark elves will often fail to pathfind properly and will just stand around doing nothing. This is only game breaking on pure strategy where you have to wait out the 5+ minute despawn timer. There are other minor bugs such as UI stats resetting if you press a combination of buttons in a specific order, but nothing truly major that I found.Other than that, the game seems fairly casual until the much higher difficulties. Even nightmare doesn't pose much of a challenge when they force you to reach level 70 to enter it.Overall it was fun though and I recommend picking it up if you have already blasted through everything there is to blast in DD1.

_childDocuments_.review: Is Dungeon Defenders Awakened worth the price?Even for a player that just plays through all of the games content you can very easily get plenty of hours of entertainment per $ spent. If you are a player that likes to chase extremely rare loot and min max in game you can get an astonishing amount of hours of play per dollar spent. So absolutely, the game is well worth the price tag.Is this a failed remake of Dungeon Defenders 1?Contrary to popular belief in many of the reviews, this game is not and was never advertised or promised as a remake. TBF I  can see player's confusion to this topic by the re use of so many of the maps from the original. Although the original game is a legendary product, DDA is trying to capture the "feel" of the original, not the original itself.This game is judged heavily in comparison to the appearance of DD2. DD2 is a beautiful game no doubt. I personally like the art style of DD2 much more than any of the other DD games. Yet this game's graphics are done well. All of the games assets were recreated in UE4 for this game. Although I would agree with many reviews here that the art style in DD2 is more appealing to me. If you take a side by side look at the textures, lighting and volumes you can clearly see there is a huge difference between UE3 and UE4.DDA just got a very large update bringing new systems and content to the game. The rune system allows for a massive amount of diversity on how you build out your strategies.To sum it all up. This is a loot based game about farming for extremely rare items. If the thought of putting in a grind to a game with the chance of getting a super high end game changing item on the very next map appeals to you, then you will likely enjoy this game. If you are wanting this game to be DD1 or DD2 you will likely be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Barely a thumbs up, and *only* if you:1 - Have a coop partner. Many maps basically require 2 people to cover 2 lanes on top of your towers.2 - Are willing to cheat for gold since the game will delete your gold at regular intervals (beyond normal gold loss for losing a map or whatever). Especially true for the person joining the host as they inexplicably get dropped from the group after every map.3 - Are both willing to mainly play as ranged characters during combat phases. Not only is it required to shoot down tough flying enemies later, but it's much safer.Pros:- Rather fun (with a friend, anyway. Solo might be kinda boring.)- Good class variety - You can switch between heroes, giving you access to unique tower combos- Many game modes  - Tower lineup and overall strategy will probably change quite a bit over time. I love to see this kind of thing in these game to prevent boredomCons:- Coop partner is dropped from group almost 100% of the time when ending a level. This results in loss of gold/items, more often gold- *Horribly* low framerate. It's very noticeable and looks trashy. I have read this is because they lowered pc framerate cap to match the Switch, which is complete crap.- Not enough of an upgrade from DD1 in terms of graphics and in terms of reused  classes/towers/etc- Wonky tower balance and wonky tower synergy within classes. Some classes like Apprentice have an incredible tower lineup which can handle every situation and others have strange traps with obvious glaring weaknesses like complete inability to hit flying enemies- Making, gearing, leveling, and maintaining multiple heroes gets really old really fast. Instead, you should only get 1 hero who can learn 1-2 towers from another class- Inconsistent tower design. Some shoot through walls and some don't. Some are wildly overpowered for the price and if you don't use them, you're just gimping yourself- Some nasty bugs like losing all your gold or items- Can't do tutorial in coop- Way, way WAY too many items- Summons can't handle stairs and corners, getting stuck, which can severely cripple the Summoner class to the point of ending an entire map in failure.- Very awkward and tedious to move summons as the Summoner- There's a huge gulf between difficulty levels, leaving you bored out of your mind on the current level but unable to raise it.- Since levels vary wildly in difficulty, it forces you to restart repeatedly to find a good balance, and you'll lose your coop partner/runes every time you do- Enemy path lines stop working often for no reason, making it impossible to know where they're going to be. Especially bad for flying enemies- Enemy sounds stop working on larger maps. Not good since they're a cue as to what tougher enemies are coming out- Enemy pathing can fail sometimesTL;DR: it wasn't ready to come out of EA. It's barely a beta.

This game is tough to review, it isn't quite complete yet, but it'a getting there. I would almost recommend the game.Original reviewThis game should still be in early access (promised features are not available yet)Early access players were promised that there will be no wipe before full release. What the devs did instead is create separate "ranked" and "legacy" modes, and Early access characters are placed in legacy only. So not a "wipe", but this definitely should have been announced ahead of time.I do not recommend the game at its current state.Update: Devs announced they are addressing this issue, will update when they follow throughUpdate: Legacy transfer tool is now available, seems to work.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until I had 1,000 hours of in-game playtime before writing this review.  As a long time player of the Dungeon Defenders games, DD:A was a welcome addition to the family with the nostalgic revival of DD1 that included some much needed quality of life improvements, as well as the promise for some great new content.  I will not criticize the studio for lack of new content, because the game is still within a year from launch.  Unfortunately, the studio has MASSIVELY dropped the ball on support for the game.  They are too focused on their platform releases for Switch, Xbox, and PS4, and are not patching major game bugs on the PC platform.  When I asked a developer on Discord if they had a comprehensive list of known bugs and at least a release schedule to address them (some are game breaking), the response was very concerning.  First, there was no list of bugs, outside of scrolling through Discord or the forums.  Second, they would not announce a bug fix until after it was deployed (i.e. no transparency to the players).  Do I like the game?  Yes, it is a fun game and I will continue playing.  However, the studio is in desperate need of a leadership and support change.  It is nothing new that the success or failure of a game rides on the support and transparent information from the studio to create a loyal player base, than it does on pushing out undeveloped content.  Players should very concerned about the release quality of the game on other platforms when they launch.There is no excuse for how poorly Chromatic Games has handled the release of DD:A and the poor ongoing support.  Players who purchased DD:A on PC are still beta testing an unfinished product.Chromatic Games, If you are reading this, please step up your support efforts and fix these bugs before releasing any new content.  As of 10/4/2020, it's been over a month since a hotfix has been deployed, and while you have acknowledged other major bugs, you have done nothing to give players a timeline or confidence that you care about having a quality or finished product.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels overall unfinished almost as if it was an early access game or an underdeveloped live service release. Regardless, the early game is far too easy, with the only threat being ogres. Would like to see tanky-er enemies, I didn't have to worry about my towers getting hit until the summit on my first play through (Hard mode, hardcore, and rifted) and even then the only unit to hit them was ogres. I do like being able to play hard mode right away, but found the leveling was far too fast and I didn't end up having a challenge ironically. I also ran into a problem with the summoner where I would have to zoom in in order to move units because (I think) the camera was too far up and the cursor was over the ceiling terrain. Finally, I'm personally not a fan of being able to level-up so many heroes at once. I feel it takes away from the experience of getting a character to a higher level, because by the time you do it once you have potentially up to 6(I think) others at the same point, but this might just be a personal problem.Now for some things I do like. Coming from the first game, the ability-mana is a very welcomed change, although it does ever so slightly take away from the strategy. The lack of build-mana cap as well as the mana automatically depositing at the start of rounds is also a very welcomed change. I like that we're now able to see the pathways they will take to the crystal(s), would like some more visual clarity on the pathways that get added partially through the level, as sometimes they caught me by surprise, maybe something like a greyed out pathway. I do like the new levels, but would like to see more clever usage of higher terrain, and insensitive to place towers more strategically throughout the map instead of just choke points. The rifted optional difficulty is very fun, with the only flaw being that the enemies look identical to summoner spawns. I also enjoy the ability to respec without spending currency in this game. I also like how the DLC (so far) have been almost entirely cosmetic, that is a very good change to the series.One of the most disappointing aspects to this game is the summoner lost his strategic options. There's no phase shift anymore, and you can only move the units now to 'hold defensive,' no target seeking, or follow target, no direct targeting either which in my opinion is the worst part of it all. In the first game I used to designate an archer or a group of archers to "play" as since I didn't have pets at the beginning, and since summoner has no weapon slot it was a way to kill the time in the rounds, and I personally found it very fun, and it's a shame I can no longer do that. It also very much so minimizes the impact of the summoner. Essentially, he lost what made him fun, and only kept fragments of the unique play style. One thing that is MUCH much better in this game is the equipment system. The equipment is far easier to understand, and faster to compare than the first game, with each piece of equipment focusing on just one or two stats, at least for the early game. This is a very nice change, and the set bonuses as well are phenomenal. Some things I think the first game did better were the following; The first game is far less buggy and broken than this game (which is saying something), had better and more well defined 'rules' and more iconic special equipment. (eg. challenge rewards etc.), had much more and harder maps than this game, Overall still feels more fleshed out, and the easter eggs (from what I know so far) are much more present in the first game, and the first game felt way better scaling into the higher levels than this game does, where it genuinely feels like none of the stats you get after say level 30 matter because equipment is proving you much much much more anyways. I also miss crystal customization. So, honestly speaking, this game isn't perfect, but it has a lot of merit to it. I think the large amount of comments on the reviews talking about how the first game is better are sadly short-sighted, and very tainted by rose-coloured glasses. I think this game is a massive step in the right direction, especially after DD2 with the whole mmorpg thing going on. I am personally excited to see where this game goes, especially with the guardian hero, and I hope that in some time it will out-shine it's predecessors in such a way as to where everyone is happy. Until then, it's still a solid game, and I would say worth the 30$ asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the DD series and again I like the idea of this one, I just wish it was given as much love as the previous games, it feels as if the developers thought it was just time to release another DD but didn't love it like the third child. This is mainly coming from a mindset of frustration with bugs/lag, if you can get past this, there are MANY positives (read on for details).I've previously played DD2 after being recommended to it by a friend who also enjoyed DD1 & DD2, after some hours on DD2 that's when I heard about DDA being released, which was great because I felt like I'd got to a stage of DD2 where it was just too grindy.So there's just a few things I want to point out1. Online Co-op (We play as 2) is full of bugs, from small stuttering after the joiner dies once, not being able to stand on the crystal in challenge mode without it elastic banding, other plays health showing as 0 when they're alive, wrong character icons, and some others. It always seems whoever is joining has the worst end of the stick. (We're also using the same internet connection, so it's not that)2. As we are playing as 2 people, it'd be nice if there was a working trade system (correct me if I'm wrong), we play different sets of heroes so we both have our own place in the game. It'd be nice if we could share some loot between us rather than hoping for some luck. Not that it's a big deal on the levels we're playing right now, but I think further down the line it could get a bit frustrating3. The waves seem really slow, we killed a wave of about 10 mobs and then waited for what felt like 30 seconds+ for the next wave to come? I know this was on lower levels but it still seems really excessive. I was tempted to go back a cup of tea and come back! 4.  when there are plenty of waves flowing in harder modes/challenge mode it seems the game cannot cope! I was playing on the highest settings and changed to fullscreen from the default borderless, and even as the host, this made my game very laggy. So I dropped down to medium settings still at fullscreen and the lag still seems to kick in at certain points, but not all the time, it's very unpredictable. (& as mentioned above it's worse for the "joiner" on Co-op, and it's not the PC as we run most games on ultra/high settings)5. On my most recent playthrough (I've come back to it for the first time in a couple of years), it feels as if all the levels are super easy as 2 players (on medium difficulty) then you just hit the last boss level that seems to go insanely difficult in comparison.  we're only playing as 2 people, I think if you're playing as a group of 4, you could probably blast through most of this game without even trying. At the moment we've skipped the last boss on medium and just gone directly to hard mode and again are breezing through the first 2 acts. I'm unsure if this is intended and I'd assume not looking at recommended levels for each map. 6. The grind! Now as a long-term player of WoW, I know what the grind is and I don't mind the grind in other games , thankfully what I've encountered so far is very minimal and it's still fun. I think down the line on the most difficult levels this could be a real issue for me as there's not too much variety and I'm not sure if I'll finish this game completely unless I can jazz it up somehow.7. With that being said I would still lean for a  of this game, if you can look past any bugs you may encounter (some can be more frustrating than others), the graphics are really pretty, it's NOT pay to win (thank you!), QoL changes and experience share between heroes, the challenges are really fun, I like that there are different modes and more difficulties/modifiers to keep you entertained, and from what I've seen of the new heroes I like the place they come from and their playstyle's/abilities.Thank you for another DD, I'm sure I will have many more hours of playtime. :)

_childDocuments_.review: While there's some fun to be had here when the game is functional, the amount of bug-free (or bug manageable) time you'll get with the game is going to vary. The Steam discussions can't seem to reach a consensus on whether or not the game's auto-loot function even works. There are a myriad of issues which are able to be repeated at will. For example, loot comparison often shows as if you have nothing equipped. Sometimes, opening and closing your inventory will fix this. Other times, it will not. When you die, sometimes every item will be marked as if it is a higher Item Power than what you have equipped, because the game thinks you have nothing equipped.The nail in the coffin after all of the above, which I could live with, was twofold. First, the cloud/local save feature doesn't always clearly state which save has more progress. Or just straight up doesn't save when you want it to. For me, this meant I lost four level 20 characters and plenty of (albeit bad) items along with them. Second, and the true last straw, since yesterday all multiplayer attempts result in the guest dealing with unplayable lag, jittering across screens worse than the goblin assassins do.I don't know how often they update this game, as features seem to change from day to day. But the issue comes when I can't tell what's a feature and what's a bug, whether it helps or hurts. I'm hoping that I can change my review and recommendation in the future, but from the community discussions I've seen, this isn't likely. There's no way this game is worth full price, and I'm frustrated with the sale price I paid for it.

It is all familiar, and well executed.There are subtle refinements (or the prospect of such). The artwork and rendering style is improved and quite lovely. The UI promises to be quite a bit better, even though character and inventory management are both very much in-progress.Overall, as a stand alone game it is good fun. If only for the chance to replay a pure version of the original game, I give this an enthusiastic thumbs-up.However, I am looking forward to seeing CG take some risks and evolve the game into something properly "new".

_childDocuments_.review: The devs said several times there wouldn't be a wipe on release. Players spent hundreds and thousands of hours grinding end-game and preparing for the hyped-up new hardest difficulty coming out with release. While the devs didn't strictly lie, they did, practically, by omission. All early-access progress was siloed to a separate "mode" called "legacy" which cannot play cooperative with the default/normal mode (where the vast majority of players will be).The devs said there were no plans to offer any sales at or shortly after release. While the devs didn't strictly lie, they did release the game at a reduced cost, effectively causing many players to essentially pay $15 to beta test a game that wasn't ready for release.Then the devs released a statement where they acknowledged that players are upset, but didn't offer any confidence that they understood why players are upset. In that statement they did apologize, but they apologized for the fact that players were upset, not for their actions or for the effect of their actions.The gameplay is fun, and there's no denying that, but it should be committed to with the understanding that the devs lack integrity as well as respect for how their actions affect their players.. so much so that I'm writing my very first game review (I think?) ever.EDIT: I'm changing my review to recommend this game after the developers demonstrated their understanding of the problem and quickly implemented a solution. Even though there are still some problems with the current state of end-game, it's clear the developers have a close ear to the community and take what their players say to heart. I am once again hopeful that this game will be great for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the negative comments are because of some bug, that caused most of the players to lose their savegame after they closed the game, but this problem got patched and fixed after 3 hours. Ever since the game got released (21. February) the devs brought out 3 patches with tons of bugfixes and adjustments. The devs are working hard and released a roadmap of what is planned for this year for the game.Dungeon Defenders Awakend  runs mostly smooth and is alot of fun with friends but also solo play.There are still alot of bugs which I'm sure the devs will take care of over time though. I have to agree that the price tag for the current state of the game is quite heavy but alot of content is on the way. If you never played any Dungeon Defenders title I strongly recommend checking out the first game since it's easily the best one of the series.EDIT::A good while has passed after I wrote this review. The corona pandemic hit GC as hard as everyone else and development is slow, but they are still trying to get things done. I have to criticize their communication towards the community and their transparency. A switch release is long overdue and the development was put on hold (Release was set for Februrary 2020 and got pushed back till atleast April 2021) .  News for the game and or a possible update is posted every like 3-4 months and during that time you are just left hoping for something new to appear and when they actually post some news they barely explain anything or give much insight to what is happening at all. Well, atleast they are giving news at all (looking at you Cube World devs). Features like local co-op are still not implemented and cross play is still not a sure bet. The devs probably are scared to admit that they overwhelmed themself a bit with this project and struggle now to get anywhere close to what they promised. They are all  kind and wholesome people but they need to work on their priorites and decision making alot. The game itself has alot of potential and looks stunning and I'm hopeful it will even outgrow the masterpiece DD 1 was/is but it's a long, long way and the team needs to grow with the task. I'm hopeful and wish the devs all the strength and motivation they need. But please grant us slightly more insight. I still recommend the game. Even at this point new players will definitly hit their 1hr=1$ mark with this one and it's a blast. Just returning players from DD1 and DD2 might be dissappointed with the state the game is currently in. Give it some time, I'll wait patiently as well.EDIT2:Well Episode 2 Part 1 here we are. Runes are fun but they could be way more creative with them and completely go all out in the craziest ways changing towers completely.. so far they are quite tame. This update also added the Summoner and it's a viable fun to play class. I'm quite okay with how the Summoner turned out in the end. The 2 new maps are quite boring sadly and so far there are no new desert themed weapon models. All in all development seems to be a bit quicker now and they are finally getting some stuff done. They are finally on the right path with this game.EDIT 3:Last night they announced that there won't be new content for this game for some time. This hurts. After 4 Years of ups and downs they are giving up on this game. At this point it just doesn't make sense to buy this just get DD1 if anything.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I recommend the game, it is fun, colorful and easy to jump into. Also, if you played DD1 you will get hit with a wave of nostalgia. However this statement from their Kickstarter page “Here at Chromatic Games, we all agree — let's go back to the roots of what made the original Dungeon Defenders so amazing!”. They have not hit this mark, not even close yet. Additional info below. I would recommend Dungeon Defenders: Awakened to anyone looking for a fun, simple (more on this later), highly addicting game. The game has enough for casual experiences and a bit of depth for the hardcore min/maxer in us all. Fighting waves and waves of enemies to get showered in loot is a lot of fun and never gets old. . Getting to the simplicity of the game. Though I recommend this game it is not without faults. The game is nowhere near what DD1 was early or late in it's lifecycle. With the implementation of Rift Mode the gameplay is watered down to an elementary level. There is no longer a need for resistance counterplay, all enemies are damaged by fusion and take more damage. The scaling with this fusion/rift gear and mobs is more health - more damage. Sirens have become completely irrelevant and simply serve to delay the progression of waves if one decides to linger. Build, weapon and armor diversity has been severely limited by this as well. The games current scaling skews hard in the favor of the new toons, now this is not unheard of for a dev to make the new toons more powerful but in this instance they are far and above nearly making the base game toons irrelevant. The interface of the game and technical mechanics of gear and stats is also watered down form DD1. The menus are clunky, unattractive and a pain to manage. There is no way to know or monitor the other players in game. If you are not listening for a hero yell (what they do when they spawn in) or monitoring your mini map you oftentimes won’t know there is anyone with you. Graphically the game is nice to look at but after hours and hours you begin to notice corners cut. Textures and lighting are nice, but limited for a PC title in 2021 in UE4. This may be limited to the fact they are working to directly port the build to other platforms. - This has been a point of contention within the community and seemingly limits respected platforms from being their best. Content is currently very light. In an effort to extend play time the loot tables are large, the floor is low and the ceiling is high even on maps and difficulties where the floor is to be raised to allow for more upgrades to be found. It does add more time for those who wish to keep searching for that next best item. However, due to the lack of content it feels more of an intentional effort to ensure concurrent numbers than to actually reward players. One massive gripe is the tavern, the tavern of old is gone and an overly simplified disappointing excuse for a hub is in its place. You have stacks of trophies which is nice to have an in game visual of achievements. However the layout of these trophies seems lazy and an attempt to limit the size of the zone.

Cons {I can't help but to compare this to DD2}- Can't swap active hero during combat phase, so if you forgot a defense you're screwed. While DD2 allowed you to do this no problem. - Some maps, without any advanced warning, end your build phase before you decide to. - Some maps don't tell you ahead of time there will be a really hard end boss. - Although the gear is easier to manage when compared to DD2, it's still hard to manage on it's own. {Upgrade system isn't clear and costs a lot} - {Some heroes use multiple weapons, looking at you EV, and it took me an age to figure out how to swap.} - Some weapons like the guns and crossbows have an ammo limit meaning you must stop and reload. The ammo limit is small too. Like 12 shots or so before you're out and must reload costing you time. This wasn't a feature in DD2 and I don't like it here. - Weapons sometimes look like a gun but are actually a crossbow. I get having fun with designs but please make weapons look like what they are supposed to be. That's unnecessarily confusing. Overall I'd say it was a good game. It does some things better than DD2 but there are some things it does worse. This game is still developing though, so it has lots of room to grow!

_childDocuments_.review: This would make a REALLY good beta and (for better or worse) reminds me of the old 'Dungeon Defense' tech demo that became Dungeon Defenders 1.Simply put, this is a lot of fun. It just doesn't feel done. It's pretty buggy, but it's generally not that broken, frustrating type of buggy, it's (mostly) that charming 'lol, they're gonna get to that' type of buggy that may or may not be entertaining jank. Sometimes this is funny rag doll reactions (stools shooting away at 100mph in the tavern when you bump into them), sometimes it's enemies zooming across the map despite their slow walking animations, sometimes it's turrets not shooting at flying enemies right in front of it, sometimes it's archers clumping up under a roof top and refusing to budge because there's a turret on it that they can't seem to hit, sometimes it's being relieved to see that there's 'only' -1 monsters left in the wave,  etc. The only frustrating thing I've hit (so far) has been my luck with online play. Sometimes I'll get into a match and.... be immediately logged out. Sometimes I'll get in, be relatively fine, then be kicked from the game when the next wave starts. It's not enough to ruin the game for me, but it's also not enough to peel me away from the single player side.All in all, it feels like it SHOULD be in early access, but early access has sort of moved the goal posts on that. It's certainly past that alpha stage that early access has come to represent, but it still needs more time to bake.TL;DR: If you're super into dungeon defenders and/or have the expendable income to make this purchase, this is a no brainer. If you're strapped and every cent truly counts, you're going to find more value elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game has a ton of content and is easily worth the $30 whether or not you like the end game grind, presuming you didn't play a lot of the original (Dungeon Defenders 1) since a lot of the content is taken directly from it (as it was originally intended as a remake, but expanded to become much more than that). Despite the recent (valid) complaints stemming from a lack of communication, the devs are actually super awesome and will continue to support this game for the next few years if there previous work is anything to go off of. As for the data wipe when launching 1.0 and the price decrease, the devs absolutely should have communicated better with the community, however both of these truly had the best interests of the game at heart so I'm not so upset about it, unlike many others. I really don't see any scenario like this happening in the future since the issues were specific to Early Access and the devs have really been fantastic in the previous entries in the franchise.As for the gameplay itself, I super love the bright, colorful scheme and artstyle the game brings to the table while also always having something else to do in the game (at least for the first few hundred hours it would seem, I'll update again later). Whether its grinding for better gear, collecting various pets, leveling new characters, completing all the maps on every difficulty, collecting achievements or preparing for the next update, the game has an absolute ton of content to sift through, though you are mostly replaying the same relatively small group of maps. This is my biggest complaint that I expect Chromatic will make progress on in the future since it can get a bit annoying to play the same few maps for literally hundreds of hours. Anything that incentivizes the play of all/most previous maps as well as adding new maps ocassionaly is going to be necessary in preserving the longevity of the game (and I do believe the devs will deliver on this front).

_childDocuments_.review: Which part of Dungeon Defenders to play? You don't need to know the history, as it might as well not be there. Now you know which one.It is worth noting that the game was created on the Unreal Engine 4; thanks to this, we are dealing with the support of cross-platform functions.In the case of Dungeon Defenders: Awakened, we are not dealing with anything new, because we are going back in time , and the only story change is the fact that now not only the present is threatened, but also the past and future of our fantastic land. Once again, we return to the four heroes: adept of magic, squire, monk and huntress.When we add the fact that in the case of the newest part everything takes place in a world that looks twenty times better, the fun enters a whole new, much higher level . And it is excellent - still, like in two, we can simultaneously develop each of our four daredevils, and then turn them between waves of enemies. But in the first Dungeon Defenders it was often impossible to perform such procedures. For some reason, the game did not allow you to choose some characters after increasing the difficulty level. In addition, it was becoming too demanding alone.Here, however, the first problem appears: either you are inhumanly determined and enjoy even losing, or you decide to play with friends or random people whose sessions can be found in the search engine. Sure, Awakened is geared towards having fun with others, but you can certainly do much more alone here than in the previous parts.Awakened allows you to search for currently playing sessions. A list is then displayed with details for each item - difficulty level, location, game mode. If you like something, you just click and that's it. You're in the game. You can go into battle. Seems such a simple and efficient solution, what in my opinion is a huge plus of this game. And the problem for some is also that not everyone likes to play with others. It is known that some individuals do not play games focused on cooperation.In addition to the fifteen levels included in the main campaign, Dungeon Defenders: Awakened has also a survival mode, which increases the total number of waves of enemies to a minimum of 25 on all maps, and the same waves are much more difficult. In the survival mode, we can choose any difficulty level - as long as we have previously passed a specific map on a given level. Survival is quite useful - not only for fun, but also for equipping our heroes with much better weapons and other equipment. we also have mixed mode, which is even more difficult, because - as the name mentions - we deal here with both the survival formula and randomly generated types of enemies.Added to this is the pure mode , where the player can do absolutely nothing but totally rely on his strategic skills . In this mode, we cannot wave a sword or cast a few spells - we can only build turrets, barriers and other types of protective objects, which will then have to deal with themselves and defend the Etheria crystals. For players who are enjoying challenges and achievements, the game also offers nine levels in the challenge mode. In short, it is impossible to get bored in DD: Awakened. Unless it's hard to please you or you don't like repetition. You can always, start the game right away on the hard difficulty setting .At times the game seems not fully balanced - the first boards, especially on easy and medium levels, may turn out to be extremely boring and too easy for the vast majority of players problably. The only challenge turns out to be the bosses, which for some reason seem much stronger than even the most difficult of ordinary opponents. The result, in my case, for example, was dying at the very end of the map process, so that I would have to start all over again, because I did not expect that the big green one that the game threw on the map as a boss would be able to kill my character with one blow.But that's basically the only irritating point in DD: Awakened. If I were to summarize all the above, i can confidently say that the work of Chromatic Games studio is undoubtedly a product that needs to be a bit refined and refined. We are dealing with the best graphics in the history of the series and probably the best combat system. I'm just sorry that some parts of the game have not been fully used - for example, the only purpose of collecting gold by selling unnecessary items is to improve your inventory.====Cons.- lone wolves will not necessarily find each other- underdeveloped inventory system- little variety of character classes- the beginning may be a bit boring for some====Pros.+ gameplay mechanics maintain a high level ...+ repeatability is an advantage in this case+ you can see that the series has evolved - a plus+ very nice graphics+ the co-op mode significantly increases the fun+ the ability to join the games of strangersHowever, if you have ever played any of the previous installments in the Dungeon Defenders series , Awakened will most likely be a great adventure for you and a journey to the past at the same time - the past that you know well and probably like . If, on the other hand, you would like to start with the series, Awakened is the part to start with. Dungeon Defenders: Awakened is a good game, a lot of the purest fun, and nothing else needs to be done.8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: With great sadness, I just can't recommend DD:A. The TL;DR: The first game, Dungeon Defenders, is still the best game in this series. It is packed with content, loaded with tons of fun maps and characters to play, and will provide hundreds of hours of enjoyment. You are given tons of meaningful choices and it is the best hybrid Tower Defense game I've played. Tower Defense + 3rd Person Action RPG. It's fantastic.Awakened is an attempt to Reboot the franchise after they lost their way with DD2 and DD:E (which was ANOTHER attempt to remake the first game) and just falls way short. The performance feels worse, there's a lot less content, only about a third of the character choices that exist in the original, and everything just feels... Worse. Itemization is completely boring, and many of the fun aspects of the original (like being able to really supercharge your towers at high levels) are now a shadow of what once was.For anyone with any interest in a Tower Defense / Action RPG mashup - do yourself a favor. Spend less money and buy the first game, simply titled Dungeon Defenders.  I suspect you'll enjoy it more, because most of us did.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Defenders Awakened is a tower-defense game where you use 4 characters: a huntress, a squire, an apprentice and a monk to defend Eternia Crystals from the hordes of orcs and orgres. Each character possesses different abilities to destroy the opponents: the huntress is specialised on the traps whereas the apprentice is focused on the fiery, electric or plasma towers to destroy the enemies. Each of them has own advantages and weaknesses so using them altogether will make your defending the crystals with ease!As an avid fan of DD franchise, you can find something good in this game:PROS:Old maps which look refreshing and beautiful thanks to the new but quite similar to DD1 artstyle.The same old gameplay from DD1 WITHOUT some DD2 innovations which make game look cheap and lazy, really appreciate that.New maps which do no clash with the main game style and really complement it.Also, upgrading 4 heroes at once instead of 1 is a perfect time-saver.DEVs are communicative and active enough to fix all the bugs in a short amount of time and listen to the community, which is a great advantage.UI changes look impressive.CONS:No notable additions comparing with the Early Access, some promised additions like the tavernkeep or massacre survival aren't in game yet.The hero pool is quite small, it could've been bigger.Now you can play 16 maps with 4 characters + challenges, it's not a sizeable number to start with, hope new maps will be added.Sometimes mobs stuck in maps, so the completion of maps becomes longer and it still persists in 1.0 Release.New maps might look quite good yet they weren't convenient enough to place towers to defend the crystals on them, their amount isn't that big to enjoy the new experience for people who have already played previous DD games.UI still needs polishing as tower stats and hero stats can be mixed altogether and it becomes difficult to manage the loot and gear up your character.CONCLUSION:Even though the game has been released, its contents aren't enough to keep you there for a long time, BUT for newcomers it's a great game, tower defense mechanics and massacre difficulty will make you adjust your gameplay to suit the needs of map completing. Especially if you're a new player you may like it with the price decrease, but changing the price three times isn't a good tactic to start with, though the move is understandable beucase it can stimulate new players to play the game.Looking forward to new patches incoming.Still wishing for a Neutral Review as the mixed reviews aren't explanatory enough when people go from one extreme to another.UPD 28/02: New Info Added.UPD 11/04: New Patch ReleasedUPD 10/06: 1.0 Released

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly the most painful review I have ever written, and ever will write. As the main artist of the DD1 Community Development Team, I have poured hundreds, if not thousands of hours of unpaid volunteer time improving the iconic title we all know and love. All those CDT weapons, accessories, and pets were modeled and textured for this community, fueled by my passion for the game. I think it goes without saying that I love this series to bits, and I want nothing more than to see this game wildly succeed. I genuinely hope that it will as it leaves early access.Why don't I recommend this game?Despite Chromatic's avid claims that this title is not a remake of DD1, in its current state this is quite literally a remake of DD1 minus 90% of the content.I played through the campaign on hard, and that was super fun! Chromatic (and Trendy) have an excellent track record of making an enjoyable campaign. DD1's was great, DD2's was also great, and DDA's did not disappoint either, even though it was missing bosses.However, other than the new maps,  The $40 price tag here bought me nearly the exact same defending experience that the $15 price tag did 8 years ago. Sure, DDA is prettier (subjective opinion) and it was neat to see ragdoll enemies (which tanked my machine's performance), but at it's core, I got the DD1 experience with all of its pros and cons. I didn't need to pay $40 for an experience with a new coat of paint that I already got back in 2011. My DD1 experience has 10x the content too.When the community saw DD2 and said "we want Chromatic to go back to their DD1 roots", we did not mean literally recreate DD1 in Unreal Engine 4 with the same defenses, enemies, and maps. What we mean is that we want a tower defense RPG without all that free-to-play crap, which was by far DD2's biggest folly. Chromatic didn't need to copy the DD1 experience in its entirety to achieve that.To give us a genuinely new Dungeon Defenders experience:And honestly? That's about it. Everything else I can think of is either on Chromatic's roadmap or otherwise plans to change.I can forgive the lack of content since the title is in Early Access. Great content will come with time. However, I cannot forgive the fact that we're getting the DD1 experience with a different coat of paint at a $40 price tag. If we get a genuinely new Dungeon Defenders experience in the future, I will not hesitate to update my review and be a strong advocate for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: DUNGEON DEFENDERS: AWKWARDEDAn unfinished beta, despite being out for a LONG TIME. Mistakes that would've taken 5 minutes of playtesting to discover were left in there. Like, on XBox 360 and XBox One controllers, me n my bro were struck by conflicting key-bindings, and intermittent un-responsive or wrong-responsive actions from our inputs.Also, why remake a game if all you do is make it worse instead of improving upon it? The original DID have a few UI flaws, but rather than fixing them here, they just added even more, so the entire process of looking over gear, placing towers, interacting with said towers, etc are now stress-inducing and aggravating. Completely un-intuitive, with tiny numbers mashed between walls of text so it's hard to instantly pinpoint the important stats of towers you're trying to place, especially during combat when you need to be able to rapidly take in the usefulness, cost, health of your traps, and run the numbers quickly.When playing with EV-A, you can't even strategize with your DU. In the original game, when placing beams, a big easy-to-see number would pop up to let you know how many DU the current length of your trap is going to take up. It's VITAL to make the most of your DU, so that's VERY important information. However, in this game, they do NOT tell you! All you have is the base cost (in small numbers that are hard to instantly take in, like everything else pretty much...). So, you have to look at your current DU, haphazardly estimate how long to make your beam/wall, place it, look at current DU again, and try to do friggin' math to figure out how many you subtracted from the total. And if you used 1 too many or too few, you have to sell the trap, and try all over again!If we were to play to late-game, where every point of DU counts in budgeting and making the most out of defenses... that'll be completely un-viable! You can't just guess, sell, guess when there's no more setup time between waves. You can't just sloppily go 1 DU over here and there, then not have enough for a vital defense point elsewhere.Like... HOW could anyone think GETTING RID OF such an IMPORTANT INDICATION is a good idea?! At VERY LEAST, put little dots on the walls/beams so I can count them and make sure I stay under a certain dot if I wanna save 5 DU for my partner or something. Numbers would be best, but ANYTHING would be better than NOTHING! :(Then there's how you have to micro-aim right at each tower to check their status, you can't just see what star rating (upgrade level) they are if you're running around, trying to top off all your beams and stuff. No, you have to aim riiiight at them, and the health number and star are SO TINY!And you can't even properly test out your weapons or traps in the level 1Tavern, where it should be a neutral zone. Your trap detail says it'll do 150 DPS, you set it up at the target dummy, it only does 120 DPS. So, you can't even trust the info you have to squint and search for anyway!And to pick up items, you have to look riiiight at them too, the game won't do you any favor in going "close enough" and sucking up items in your reticle's general vicinity. So in a game that's HEAVILY about loot, it makes it feel like punishing drudgery to pick up said loot! >:(The whole key to a properly functioning action/strategy type of video game, is for useful information to be quick and easy to get, controls to be easily adapted to, and collecting goodies to be rewarding. That's the mere BASELINE of a FUNCTIONING game with judgment, action, and looting emphasis respectively. The mere skeleton required for a game to, from that point, ever hope to become a GOOD game. If you don't have those three elements, then a game like this simply can't be good.When you're balancing strategy and action, where you have to make very quick decisions based on crunching numbers and knowing which defenses are weak/strong and in need of reinforcement... this game does everything in its power to HIDE that information. Sure, it looks more clean and modern... but this isn't a pure 3PS that can be played well like that, it's a hybrid with Tower Defense. And it utterly FAILS half of itself.Also, no new music, just the same old songs, not even remixes or built-upon versions. Not necessary sure, but if this was an all-out polished version of the original, you'd think they'd also put a shiny layer on the music too. But forget it being even a visual upgrade; enemies have extremely low movement framerates, and trying to max my video settings hard-limits Detail to Medium.I really wanted to enjoy this. Wanted a fresh new take on our favorite classic, was hoping that what few flaws existed in the original would be ironed out, and that we'd be in for a much better experience. But nope. Instead, the UI and menus and default controls make this game feel more like 'Dentist Patient Simulator', skipping straight to 'Level 10: Root-Canal', in 'No Numbing' difficulty! :(I'm glad we got to try it for free, due to the "Play for free" weekend Steam offered, because this cements my decision to NOT buy it. Sadly, I can't get a refund on the time and stress I wasted on giving it a chance. Time to eat chocolate cookies until I pass out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've already played the original Dungeon Defenders then don't bother buying this game. Just go start a new character and campaign on the old one and you'll have way more fun. This re-tread of an already great game is poorly optimized, with a UI that blends into the screen in a bad way. The misused budget is also appallingly apparent. 2-D hand drawn logos and icons that were clearly meant to divert money into the flashy, over-saturated neon lights and washy graphics that, I guess are supposed to be an upgrade from the last game? Instead it just makes it look like a high-schoolers homemade unity engine nightmare. The previous games polish and shine are a distant memory, replaced by massive info boxes that cover a quarter of the screen for no reason, hotkeys that will have you accidentally fumbling your way through the build phase, and whats with the need to hold keys to accept things? A small nitpick for sure, but when I'm trying to skip the intro cut scene when it plays for a SECOND time in less then 5 minuets, in case somehow I missed it or I suddenly care more about it then the first time, I shouldn't have to hold the space bar for 5 seconds. I don't need time to stop and change my mind about skipping past it. If there's one thing that surprised me, its the long loading screens for such a shallow game. The same loading screens might I add, where the menu music and the in-game music like to fight for dominance while the game is deciding weather or not it wants to break. I'm so glad they didn't think about charging any more then $33.99 for this, fresh out of early access (and by golly it shows), disappointment.  Overall, unimpressed. The original is cheaper, smoother, and more polished. Do me a favor and buy that one instead, while i sit and wait for my refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write a lot of reviews but I felt this game deserved one. I've played DD since DD1 and was a huge fan of the first one, putting a ridiculous amount of hours into it. The second one was a buggy, clunky disappointment and I barely touched it. When I saw DDA and a lot of people claiming it was essentially a remaster of DD1 I was excited and picked it up.It feels exactly like DD1 and I was overjoyed to be playing it in a new light. The maps, the characters, just the overall feel of the game will give anyone a sense of nostalgic satisfaction. The graphics improvements and character handling are also welcome additions. Now, there are issues. First off there are bugs. So far I've noticed 3 obvious ones.1 - The mouse cursor becomes non-responsive if you tab out and then back into the game sometimes, requiring you to shut the game down from the desktop and reload.2 - When typing in chat the "H" key will open the hero selection screen which then obscures the screen and what you're typing. If you close the hero selection screen it clears what you were typing as well.3 - A lot of loot items have bugged tooltips and incomplete information. I especially noticed this for any of the Squire weapons.I am sure there are others but I know the devs are working on them.The game itself is fun and, again, a fantastic remaster of DD1 but there is a HUGE amount of content lacking. I know this EA and they are working on it but they need to get some stuff out sooner than later.1 - The tavern keepers and shop mechanics.2 - Additional characters (I miss EV).3 - Additional maps.4 - HUD improvements that show your teammates including their level, health, and character selection.5 - Filtering options in the game search menu (the search bar is fine but limited in narrowing down the difficulty, map, and mode I'm looking for)6 - More detailed tooltips for loot and character stats.7 - Essentially everything from DD1 should be put back into this game and then just make it better from there.Ultimately I would recommend this game to anyone that loved DD1. It's a bit bare bones right now but I honestly have faith that the devs care about this game and want to do right by their fans. They will make this game amazing.It should also be noted that a lot of the negative reviews are from people that backed the game on kickstarter and a lot of what was promised by the company was not delivered.I agree with the people that are upset that this was not a good way to launch a game and understand their frustration but the company actually released an open letter accepting responsibility for this, apologizing intently for their mistakes, and promising to do what they can to make things right. This is generally unheard of from most game companies. They just take your money, say "oh well we screwed up" and then disappear. I don't see that happening here.TL;DRThe game is a bit buggy and bare bones in it's current state but shows an immense amount of promise. As long as the devs listen to the fans and work toward implementing a lot of what made DD1 so good this is going to be an amazing game so get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely still in its early/fledgling stages. However, for anyone that has been playing DD since the early early early days before they even released the first extra content pack, this game is an absolute gem. It really does combine the best features of all the versions of this game to date. I have found it to be the most balanced and intuitive of all the games thus far. Progression in this game, if not ruined by joining a much farther ahead multiplayer game, is the smoothest out of all games. It's definitely a grind, but not one that leaves you unrewarded multiple times before finally getting lucky. I play on a 3070 all settings max and even with max towers and rapid animations I never have any lag and the graphics are classic but improved. The hero deck addition to the first game is fantastic! Also keeping DD1 Pets/levling system also much much better than DD2 or eternia. All this game is missing at this point is MORE CONTENT! For 30$ though its a great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal, full game no micro trans or buying bag/bank slots. -Removal of build timer for majority of game modes is a super fantastic improvement on the game. -Games don't auto close super quick!!!!!! This is important for people who have lives. A 25 wave survival or/pure strat can take an awful long time. I am able to leave my pure strat on at wave 14, go to sleep, go to work, come back after work and its still there at wave 14. This is huge. 10/10 best change to the game. -Player trading isn't available yet, however is apparently on its way (a much desired/classic feature of the game as it creates a mana economy for existing/new players to be useful to eachother)-No Summoner yet (hopefully when added it doesn't have its own defense units as that completely breaks the balance of the game and instead just balanced to be on par with other heroes) -What the heck is hardcore pure strategy? still havent figured this out but its an option (pure strategy drops = loot as survival now and is one of the most fun modes if you want to set something awesome up and sit back and watch, this change really makes a big difference for people like me who favor towers over heroes)-Loot filter/acquisition systems after some tweaks/bugs are working fantastic and make managing easier than its ever been. 525 items cut down to 80-100 safely with one click, no fear of selling something you don't mean to as long as you filter properly. -Challenges/challenge rewards feel pointless. I've yet to do them on Massacre but everything under that difficulty doesn't even seem worth doing, least fun thing in the game currently. First challenge is also very unbalanced for single player, even at level 78 with all mobs dying in one hit Easy mode is way to challenging for level 10 rewards lol. The rest of the challenges are balanced fine. Either a re-balancing of rewards for challenges or just focus on them having ONE difficulty with an appropriate "worth-it reward". -There are bugs! However they are infrequent and all that I've found are mostly player beneficial. Pathing and damaging bugs mostly. You can glitch a Siren of Massacre Pure Strat on Deeper well for example to get stuck so that it will die and drop phat loots. Normally in pure strat you can't kill sirens as they take hero damage only. -Spiders, Ogres dropped from Sky Copters and Copters themselves are all unable to damage Crystals. Not sure if this is bug or intentional? But several times I've had a stray spider attacking a crystal not in range of a tower only to have to wait the 5 min for it to die to the games anti-bug mechanic. Or a random sky ogre just hammering the crystal to no effect lol.Overall guys buy this game. Play this game. Support these guys so they pump out more content. This is nothing like the failed DDE project, this one has a lot of potential to keep DD relevant in current mainstream gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:  I'd say give it a few years and an overhaul or two.  It really feels like a soulless game.  (both graphically and mechanics wise)Graphics:  While I don't have automatonophobia all of the humanoid(and a few of the non-humanoid) models just strike me really hard as completely off putting.  If I had to describe the feeling, it's like looking at a husk or an empty shell, zombie like.  The skins/textures also throw me off.  How is it that an ogre is iridescent/glowing while underground?  Neon freakin green, really?  I get it, different artistic direction.  But holy crap, get some continuity and quit breaking the immersion.  Cartoony approach is fine, whatever.  Just keep it consistent.Gameplay:  It's hard to put my finger on any one thing but overall the game is very clunky and rough.  UI is not intuitive.  The controls for building/upgrading/selling feel out of place; not a fan of switching to a top down view and maintaining the action over multiple clicks.  Movement leaves much to be desired; animations are fluid but are noticeably slower than historical movement animations.Mechanics:  Where are they?  The degree to which you could manipulate your gear in DD1 was immense.  And I'm absolutely baffled why we moved away from Mana being the de facto currency for purchasing and upgrading.  That was an intrinsically unique and refreshing mechanic.Overall:  This is not a worthy sequel nor a spiritual successor to DD1.  They've lost all the magic, it's absolutely crushing for me to admit that.Gripes:  Why do we need such extensive physics and ragdoll in this new iteration?  Seems like an absolute waste of computing power for such an insignificant enhancement to the experience.  (While I appreciate how cool it looks for a downed wyvern to fall and crash into a bridge and for it's wings and head to be accurately depicted draped over the railing, it's just completely unnecessary.  I'd rather be able to run massive waves with ease and just live with pre-rendered stationary death models.)

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure whether I could recommend this game for its price tag this far before release.  But here I am, hours and hours later, still having fun, still having lots left to do.You should already know that Chromatic's fusion of tower defense and action RPG makes for a fun as hell genre.  I almost don't feel the need to discuss the pros of this game because they're so plain to see; the game is pretty, its mechanics are streamlined from DD1, and it will keep you hooked for a very long time.The cons of this game, of course, are that it's in early access.  You have enemies getting stuck in places, and many UI elements without their final coat of paint.  On the more serious end, you have memory leaks, crashes, and even reports of multiplayer progress not being saved.But there's a patch nearly every day.  Chromatic is active on their forums and their discord, and they even pop into livestreams of the game and let people know what they're working on and when the next update is coming (Edit: and take a look at this steam page!  How many reviews can you see *without* a developer response?).  They prioritise the most prominent bugs that people are more likely to complain about.  If a new patch introduces a serious problem, you won't have to wait long before it's resolved.I understand not wanting to buy this because its glitches are serious at times, or because it lacks all the content you want.  I'd still implore you to put this on your wishlist.  Chromatic have a roadmap up on their website explaining exactly when each major feature is coming, and due to what I've seen, I trust them to stay on that schedule.  Chromatic is a company doing early access right, and I'm happy with my decision to support them on that.The bottom line is this:  If you liked Dungeon Defenders, you will like Dungeon Defenders Awakened now, and you will love Dungeon Defenders Awakened when it releases fully later this year.

This game has the old four heroes, the old four abilities, the exact same towers, minus the weapon/pet shop.  They spent their entire development time on what, exactly?  A slight graphics overhaul with 80% of the same old levels, plus four new ones to take the bad ones' places?  And just FYI, the graphics are worse on some stages than the first game.  ie. Castle Gardens.So, what does that leave left?Pretty much nothing.  It lacks heroes, it lacks content, it lacks the shop, it lacks pets, it lacks customization, it lacks just about everything. Massacre required the help of friends to play through.Is it possible to review DDA without comparing it to DD1? Not really. While I do like the addition of the auto loot filter system and the Hero Desk, I do miss using emulators to have 4 toons on screen to increase the end loot rewards as well as being able to tower/hero boost with one toon while fighting with another.
