name: Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break
detailed_description: Make your own Levels. Break everyone else's. Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break is competitive tower defense and arcade action rolled up with ACE Team's quirky, Monty Python-esque humor into one giant, creative game for the ages! Jump into the expansive, gut-busting story for an eclectic adventure featuring bizarre and irreverent takes on legendary characters, or for the first time, create and share your own levels to compete with friends and strangers online in a real-time mix of hectic tower defense and epic boulder-racing arcade action. Make & Break Worlds Design and build your own levels in the easy-to-use editor and share your creations with players from all over the world for nearly limitless creative fun! Competitive Tower Defense Build defenses and race to destroy your opponents’ in up to 4-player online multiplayer, or head-to-head in 2-player split-screen action. Boulder-Smashing Arcade Action Crash your way through everything in your path as fast as you can in six distinct and arcadey game modes with over 20 zany boulders! Absurdly Funny Take a ride on the wild side with ACE Team's hilarious story – everyone from Caesar and Moctezuma to Krampus and the Flying Spaghetti Monster make an appearance in an expansive campaign across history and beyond. Game Modes Galore Defend your base in the new Boulder Avalanche, perfect your rolling skills in the fragile Humpty-Dumpty Mode, race the clock in Time Trials, or create your own unique gameplay with the creator for hundreds of hours of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: It's very easy to tell this game was done on the cheap and not by the original devs.The official levels are no where near the quality of RoA2, there's no flavour to them, they all feel like they were made in the level editor and with repeated use of 90 degree bends and jump pads.A lot of the quality of life improvements from 1 to 2 are gone, you can't play the levels in order like you could in RoA2 which makes lobbies a pain to use. Little things like race mode only requiring two stars to win with no way of changing it are very annoying.There's a lot of bug and connection issues and a huge lack of general polish such as the boulder animations are very frame-y. I didn't expect completely new assets for everything but it's all mostly reused so this could have been an expansion to the previous game.I don't expect this game to get fixed or updated anytime soon either and it's a massive shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break

_childDocuments_.review: Stick with 2, they dropped the boulder on this one.Man this is heartbreaking. I thought 2 was a dang masterpiece, and this one is just not. The game FEELS bad. The interface is awful, the camera in Build mode is jacked, the respawn system is bad, the AI is bad, there's just tons of little nuisances. I found one campaign map where it was impossible to make one jump with just a moderately heavy boulder.But the WORST part is that the devs seem to have used the inbuilt level editor to design all the campaign maps and boy does it show. The beautiful meticulously handcrafted clever levels of 2 are GONE. Everything unnaturally juts out of an empty plane, decorated with a small handful of cut and paste assets.For what it's worth Patricio Meneses is, as always, killing it with the OST.

_childDocuments_.review: A review taking place about halfway through the main game.This entry into the Rock of Ages series isn't as polished or well thought out as its second entry, but it is by far and large not nearly as problematic as many popular reviews say it is. I wouldn't even go as far as to say it's disappointing like many have. It's really just more Rock of Ages with a slight shift to quanitity over quality by a mildly noticeable albeit relatively small margin.The attention to detail in each stage is certainly not as good as its predecessor, and the difference in quality can be felt throughout (level designs are simpler, win-screen doesn't show squished opponents, collisions in areas can be funky where they didn't used to be) but it doesn't ruin the fun that Rock of Ages offers. Traps are still fun to place, the game still plays like it usually does, and the new stuff is really fun to mess with.With the inclusion of all previous boulders and traps along with new ones, as well as a fully fledged level creator, it really was a developer choice to focus on including as much as possible. If you want something that feels more fully fleshed out and hand-crafted, go for RoA2. RoA3 may not be as carefully put together, but it's certainly worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Rock of Ages 2, but worse. Most of the absurd humor has been stripped out, leaning entirely on the 'joke' that things are poorly drawn and animated. Level design is now entirely blind hairpin turns, changing the pace of the game from careful acceleration to a constant series of stop and go till you have the final goal in sight. The tower defense levels are mind numbingly stupid, they didn't bother to put any strategy into it, so you just plop down walls and anything else you can afford then spam lightning bolts.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Patch 1.01: Fatal error crashed to desktop first race.Day one review: As it stands this is the buggiest Rock of Ages game I've played. I've been knocked through the floor numerous times, bounced over the enemy in the castle; gone through the wall then got stuck in the castle wall unable to do anything but wait for the ai to win or restart twice, the music cuts out if you retry a level once you've finished it, on the world map when you unlock something the notification animation and sound effect is repeated every time you press confirm so you can spam it, then the fatal error that crashed me to desktop mid race. All these problems without even trying to make a level or play online. In it's current state I can't recommend it.Edit:As for the game itself; it's missing a lot of the charm and personality the first two games had. It's kept the Monty Python art style but dropped the writing and humour. I've made it 5 bosses in and there's hardly any writing at all. At best you get some very mild slapstick and the speech is replaced with comedy mumbling, there's nothing clever or funny about it. Yeah comedy and humour is subjective but even compared to the previous games you can see a clear difference. A lot of the levels seem poorly balanced and not thought through. For example there are levels where you can only use 1 or 2 types of obstacle. The ai will have all of them placed and start rolling before you've even fully looked at the map to work out where's best to place them. So you find yourself just front loading your towers in the hope you can start before the ai, if you do you'll get to the castle first no problem. But then you have to fight one of the obstacles inside the castle from a stand still. Since momentum is how you get through most obstacles it can be infuriating since the ai is still rolling towards you. You also have to wait for the enemy in the castle to despawn before the ai stops moving, so it might be possible to still lose after beating the enemy. On paper it's got everything you'd expect from the previous games but more, in reality the game feels weaker in every category. Though In fairness I never tried the level creator or online. Since user generated content doesn't interest me in the slightest and the online has been historically unstable in this franchise I'd rather not bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the series, but unfortunately I'm quite disappointed in this entry. It feels like the producers of this game tried sticking to the "if it ain't broke don't fix it" strategy without actually realising what makes the previous games so good.The game suffers from generally flat execution of it's core gameplay mechanics. Level progression just became grindy with completing extra game modes necessary to open up new levels. The quirky humour is mostly absent being reduced to some slapstick here and there. Even game music feels like a downgrade compared to the previous game.Honestly, haven't tried the map editor yet, and I'm pretty sure that some user generated levels will eventually raise the quality bar for this game, but so far the game does not justify such an egregious price tag and I doubt it ever will.If you still want to try it out, get it on a considerably reduced price and keep your expectations very low.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, a straight upgrade to rock of ages 2 with more obstacles, boulders and gamemodes but there are so many bugs I just need to give this a negative review. Honestly if you can look past the incredibly infurating bugs (you can get stuck under enemy units and instantly die, UI sometimes doesnt show up in gamemodes such as obstacle course or skee-boulder, your units just do not attack the enemy boulder wich affects mostly the rams where they attack once, turn around, and stop moving for the rest of the game) this game is an expanded rock of ages 2. Also keep in mind the game doesn't save progress on the steam cloud so if you start up a new game on a different computer you'll have to start from the beginning.I haven't used the map maker much so I cannot speak of any bugs or errors you might encounter there.Overall the game is very fun, just like its predecessors, but you need to ignore some absolutely infurating alt+f4 moments to get enjoyment out of the game. Of course the bugs arent so common as to make the game unplayable, you might be able to play at least two to three games without encountering any, if you don't use the ram (wich is also the strongest unit with the heavenly bull when it works).I'm sad to see this game in such a pitiful state, and it seems that work on the game has been discontinued so no more patches or bug fixes. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for April 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 4th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.After an playing an hour to review for the Humble Choice April 2021 Bundle:This is a frustrating game.  I spent about half my playtime on the tutorial because Rock of Ages 3 doesn’t want to explain anything about its gameplay to the user.  But the tutorial was difficult enough, that its lack of explanation made the experience far worse. Rock of Ages 3 is about sending your giant boulder down a course at an enemy, and then the enemy sending boulders back at your base.  You can build up your base with traps on the path to try to divert or stop the enemy, but ultimately the experience becomes one of frustration as players feel like they have limited control and the gameplay here is one of quantity, not quality.  The cutscenes as well are like the vignettes in the middle of Monty Python Episodes along with the characters never saying anything.  It’s an attempt to retell the story of Odysseus, but ultimately it just feels like fluff. If you loved Rock of Ages 2, you might want to check this one out, but after a bad tutorial and several levels that feel like players aren’t even given a fair shake by the developer, I am fine forgetting about this game existing and if I want to play it, I’ll go play the second game in the series.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: All they had to do was take a look and RoA 1 and 2, see what made it great and continue along that path but they ffed up.The first 2 were charming with good level design and sometimes frustrating boulder control especially when you need to break and turn at the same time.Here the poor controls while breaking continues but okay whatever.The animation style is still there although it has lost a bit of its charm this time around.But what really annoys me is the poor level design ( they need fences to stop people from becoming creative and try something fun), some of which has become "maze" like combined this with a camera angle which really should have the option to pan it backwards and upwards just a bit more, so that players can see a bit better what is coming. Now with the zoomed in camera reaction times are late and the game plainly depends on replays and you remembering the course, combine this with poor breaking mechanic and you have lost me.Now it really deserves a neutral thumb but since steam doesn't allow this I need to choose.A thumbs up was going to be my choice but then minor collisions with other balls or objects send you spinning. and I hate that so much when they can knock you but you can't knock them..So a thumbs down it is sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: Did they change the writer or something?  This wasn't that good..I was looking forward to playing this game so much, but it feels like a huge let down.  Is this the dev team trying to phone it in?  Like the devs for the last Shantae game?  First let us talk about the good.  The graphics are decent, although I suspect a bit of it was copied over from 2.  The music is good.  The first few tracks are really well done.   It goes a bit downhill from there.Everything else is just... meh to bad.  With the level design they went for a quantity over quality policy.  While i can fully understand that when it comes to skeeball or obstacle levels, the main story levels needed that extra care and love.  Not the slapdash approach they went for.The game has some bugs and poor design ideas. Although minor, are some very basic coding fixes that I'm surprised they didn't figure out.  For example if you complete the time trial course and restart, the music goes away.The game loves to take the camera away from you.  On one boss you need to deactivate near 10 segments, and it pulls the camera from you for every single one of them...  This is not needed at all.  I got it the first time, I don't need you to stop gameplay and screw up my camera (since it always returns it in a random position) for every single one of these.   On top of that if you are racing the enemy, i don't need to see them breaking through my door when victory or defeat is a few seconds difference.  Especially if you are going to give me the camera back 90 degrees to the side.The worst part is that the cutscenes are not at all funny.  While humor is subjective, the other games went for a more zany monty python feel to them.   Here stuff just happens... They could have easily added the random and silly like we have come to know and love, but settled on a boiler plate.  A single cutscene made me smile (involving a certain wiggling monster)  but everything else was dull.  It is like they completely forgot they were trying to take liberties with history.So no I cannot recommend it for full price.  get RoA2 instead.  Taking a single player game and focusing so much on multiplayer is the death knell to good games.

And I wedged myself stuck in levels way to many times, with no unstuck option.The second game might be one of, if not my favourite game ever, but this one is disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break is very similar to its two predecessors. There is little to differentiate it and the core gameplay is identical. There are a few new units and the graphics are slightly better in some places, but don't let this somewhat faint praise put you off. Everything has been lovingly crafted, especially the boss battles which are awesome. You can justify buying the game for the level design and the new content if you enjoyed the previous two games, or this could be a good entry point for a new player. The game is a mash up of a marble-run game and a tower-defence game. The graphics and sound are really good and emulate Terry Gilliam's art style from the cartoons in the 1960s comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus. The tower defence element of Rock of Ages is a bit hit and miss, but it works. There is a level editor built into the game, which is a nice inclusion, but I haven't used it. Multiplayer is well implemented, but I've yet to be matched with a human opponent. From past experience, the multiplayer is fast, hectic fun. The various game modes keep the game constantly fresh and the frustrating nature of the gameplay drives you to demand 'one more go'.

Also, please ignore my playtime it says 14 hours but is likely closer to 6, I left my game running most of one day and some of another.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh I hate down voting this. I loved the first game and really enjoyed the second game. RoA3 could have been amazing if they'd polished it up, but they didn't. They tried to make it much bigger and better than the first 2 games, but they must have run out of money along the way and didn't get to the polishing part and just gave us a mess of constant frustration.What was once a fun, relaxing and quirky, well thought out game will leave you nothing but frustrated and filled with the desire to constantly rage quit.I hope this doesn't kill the series and I hope that there will be future games that return to a more fundamental RoA game that people can enjoy - or - if they want to go over the top like they tried to do with RoA3, they HAVE to commit to finishing the job!The AI has way more slots than you.The AI has way more gold than you.The AI has way higher limits per trap.The AI has an RNG timer on their boulder builds. You'll destroy an AI boulder and they'll have another one deployed almost immediately.They also added a trap that obscures your vision, which will of course, never affect the AI when you use it.AI always gets a head start during obstacle mode.You'll  touch the jagged edge of something (like a tree stump) and go flying into eternity.A boost ring behind a ramp will fling you into a wall because the ramp simply won't work.I didn't love RoA2 as much as the RoA1 because there's an issue with the jump in RoA2 where it just randomly doesn't work WAAAAYYYYY TOOO OFTEN..... aaaannndd.... they used the same physics from RoA2 in RoA3 and they DIDN'T FIX THIS! :(Clouds are hit and miss - you'll land in EXACTLY the same spot on a cloud as you did before and you'll fall through it.Sometimes your rock slows down when you try to slow it down, other times it just skips along and flies off the map.Because of the ridiculous amount of obstacles on each level and the massive hit boxes for each object, your rock will often get stuck and you'll have to restart the map because you can't rescue it. Hit boxes are WAAAYYYYY too large. Play RoA1 and then play RoA3 and you'll see what I mean.Sometimes you'll get dropped back on the map where you flew off the edge (like you're supposed to) and other times you'll be dropped WWAAAAAYYYYYY back from where you were - even BEFORE checkpoints (for modes that have checkpoints like Humpty Dumpty).Sometimes your rock will get dropped directly onto an enemy trap and you'll get flung off the map again.Sometimes your rock will get dropped into an illegal area and the rock drop animation will get stuck in an infinite loop and you'll have to restart the map.No plain cursor mode for picking gold up - you have to select a trap to build (or the lightning bolt) and hover EXACTLY over the bag of gold.Gold bags drop that can't be picked upNo undo option for a misplaced build because you tried to pick up a bag of gold, but built something instead.The cut scenes are meh. Each one is a bunch of disjointed slap-stick silliness that didn't have the same level of well thought out humour like the cut scenes from the first 2 games.The hour glass timer icon for each rock is no longer available in the rock selection menu, so you have to work out which rocks take less time and which take more time to build through trial and error... or play RoA2 and get the timings for most of the rocks from that and write them down to keep with you while you play RoA3 ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Avalanche mode is waaayyy too easy.There's a locked trap slot that never unlocks.There are random open tiles on every map that can't be built on.The lightning cloud doesn't work.Traps sometimes don't work.The game randomly crashes JUST as you're about to crush an enemy after breaking down their gate.They added massively overpowered traps like the guillotine, which can kill your rock in 1 shot. Highly damaged rocks still do massive damage to your door.Maps have WAAAAYYYYY too many obstacles and visual impairments, and this combined with the wonky physics mentioned above, make the levels a lot less fun to roll through. It's a constant frustration of flying off the edge and never really getting any true speed on any map. It's as if they took the worst map from RoA2 (Dover) and wanted to only make this map or worse in RoA3.Map are also uninspiring because they moved away from a key design principle that made the first 2 games so great. In the first 2 games, each map HAD to be designed to accommodate all game modes and this made for some truly inspiring and fun maps!On top of the AI being overpowered, they increased the amount of gold you and the AI have access to in game to be able to build more traps - probably to make it feel more like a true tower defense. This, on top of the frustrating level design with too many obstacles and wonky physics, make the navigation of your rock to the enemy castle a frustrating chore that sucks ALL of the fun out of the game. You can almost NEVER use rocks like the prehistoric wheel (or other low health rocks) because of this either, which limits you to using specific rocks ALL THE TIME and makes the game boring, while you rage at the same time after falling off the map for the hundredth time.Boss fights could have been A LOT better!I'm not sure why they decided to rock theme the music when rolling because one of the most charming things about the series was the upbeat classical music while playing, which set it apart from most other games and fit the theme so nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game but sadly I just can't, I loved the first two games but this one sadly only made me feel two emotions the entire time playing it: frustrated and dissapointed.The main problems is the level design: Controls in this game are slow and you must start pressing buttons seconds earlier to slow down or move in a specific direction (you are controlling a heavy boulder after all).The issue comes with the fact that the level design is absolutely RIDDLED with blind corners and other many shenanigans which keep making you fail while you cannot do anything about it unless you know the maps out of your head already. This happens so incredibly frequent that the game is nothing but downright frustrating.To make it even worse, the game adds many challenge levels like races and such (which give you better rewards the better your time/score/etc. is), then combine this with the issue above to make things even worse.Furthermore the AI has a massive advantage over the player by having MUCH more money than the player and being able to place down MANY more units than the player.To top it all off the game is inconsistent at times, occasionally hitting small things make you go absolutely flying off the map and other times some traps deal ridiculous amounts more damage than usually if not straight-up instakill you.I also want to note that comedy is a large part of this game and I feel like its much worse than the previous games, maybe my taste in comedy changed or I have rose-tinted glasses for the previous two games but I never really found any of the jokes funny, maybe I was just too frustrated with the game to be able to laugh, that is also a possibility.All in all, a very frustrating and disappointing game compared to the previous two ones, I really wanted to like this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Rock of Ages games and you really enjoyed 2 maybe this games for you. Personally this game feels more like a DLC to the second game with a level editor, trap upgrades, new traps and new boulders. There's also a new story campaign which is a great deal longer because the levels break up into the main level, sometimes there's time trials, skeeball, obstacle courses or the new Avalanche mode. There's a lot of content and each of the modes plays on a different map with the same theme as the main level. Where the second game lacked variety and interesting level designs this game uses a lot more levels designed similarly to that of RoA1 but without the fun boss units that were in said game. Not to mention the levels do feel quite cobbled together. I had a reasonable time with the game overall but the game just feels like some weird add on rather than a sequel and with this game it felt like some of the magic was lost from the first couple of games. Another weird point to note is that the game is really quite buggy which is weird given everything from RoA2 was seemingly ported here minus the levels and general level aesthetics. You usually cant click things and have to use a hotkey, walls don't connect to towers, sometimes your boulder just explodes for no reason from full health, you can fall through the floor, people float sometimes, sometimes traps just decide whether they want to work consistently or not and the list goes on. I was going to give this game a positive but meh review and then I played the Humpty Dumpty levels. Screw these levels of not falling and not getting hit more than twice in a gauntlet with an egg shaped boulder (Which you unlock after completing these levels and is absolutely useless) This may sound fun to some but it made me realise moreso that this game is underhwhelming. Sure there's heaps of content but it lacks soul. The level editor is pretty cool though...

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw Rock of Ages 3 by Modus Games, I honestly had no idea what I was getting myself into. I have heard of the series, but it never caught my attention enough to give it a try. However, after the first cutscene, I knew I was going to enjoy this experience even if just for the animations alone.The game consists of two sections, MAKE and BREAK. In BREAK, the game is simple in premise, you take control of a rock, speed through a track of obstacles, crush the gate of the opposing team’s castle and flatten the enemy.You select a character to represent your empire from a list of leaders and memes, everything from Julius Caesar to the badly painted Jesus restoration painting (Ecce Mono) that was the source of viral news back in 2013. You can also unlock new rocks to use, such as a stone fist, the Earth, and a cluster of cows each with their own stats such as speed and destructive power. Finally, you can customize your empire’s banner with colors and patterns to give it the final touch.In the story mode you start out in 840 B.C. escaping the cyclops Polyphmus and carve a destructive path to 1910. Squaring off against dragons and Gods with pit-stops along the way to fight the Mongols, Romans, and other historical empires. The story reminds me of Bill and Ted’s Excellent Adventure but more destructive! The story is full of funny vignettes that are in an art style that represents the age, complete with a slapstick comedy approach. While these are short, they made me laugh quite a bit.Your encounter with Polyphmus serves as a tutorial to introduce you to a few modes of the game. As the story progresses, you fight different historical figures like Napoleon, Caesar, and Genghis Khan. Each age has a variety of modes to play and you collect stars as a reward for your performance. The stars unlock new ages and different types of offensive and defensive structures. The different stages have a mix of modes such as tower defense, time trials, ball races, and other types of obstacles courses.In the tower defense game mode, both teams start out building structures on the track in order to defend against the other team’s rock. You can build explosive barrels, walls, cows, humans, tigers on a balloon, and many more. These structures can either damage the player’s rock or slow it down. The first few levels are okay in difficulty, but by the 4th age my structures barely made a dent in the enemy rock. The AI would also have fully realized tracks while I was just placing a few walls and other structures. I ended up having to focus on the other modes to unlock new structures to progress through the story, which gave the game a nice balance of difficulty and progression.The time trials are where you try to get your rock to the finish line as fast as possible. This mode seemed linear, but after my first run I saw that the goal times were substantially lower than mine. On my second run, I noticed that by using momentum and perfectly timing jumps I could access alternate paths in the track to shave precious seconds off my time. I spent a lot of time trying to perfect my times because this mode was so challenging and fun.The skee ball mode is very simple, and the AI might be a little broken here as well. Your goal is to make your way down the track crushing targets. The targets provide points that you multiply by directing your rock into specific holes on the skee board at the end of the track. I noticed the AI did not go for the targets, so the score it obtained was low. I focused on hitting as many targets as I could and even if I did not win the race, I was still able to win overall because my score was higher.Every so often, there are also special “boss fights” where you square off against a creature or God to break targets and win races in order to unlock customization options for your rock.The second main section of the game is MAKE. This is where you can build a track for others to play. You can modify the land and design of the track to make some interesting obstacles to get through. I could see myself putting tons of time into playing this mode however, the controls are a bit tough to get use to. It is hard to move the land mass exactly as I want it to move and it seems a bit more complicated than it needs to be.After you finish your level you can post it and go back to the BREAK mode to play other community levels that have been created. Currently, there are quite a few different maps, but I am not sure how long that will last as its entirely based on the game’s community to continue creating new experiences.For the asking price of $29.99, you get a decent amount of content. Single player and multiplayer modes and a quirky story mode that, if you want to collect everything, will last you a decent amount of time to get through. The base game is there, all the parts are functioning and function mostly well.I did run into a few bugs involving music cutting out, rocks not wanting to respawn, and being able to completely go through some environmental pieces. The story, while funny, maybe equates to about 20 minutes of cutscenes. The second half of the game is based on the community and their willingness to provide more content to the game. This may already be problematic to the longevity of the game because the multiplayer’s players base seems lacking when I have tried to connect recently.

_childDocuments_.review: On the main menu screen, you’ll find Make, Break, Customise and Options, on the left side of the screen you’ll see the latest updates for the game. Selecting Break will allow you to choose Tutorial, Story and Community Levels.  Playing the tutorial will have you play as Odysseus who has just made landfall along with his fellow Greeks. You then smell some food cooking so with grumbling bellies you head off in the direction of the food. You enter a cave where the smell of the food is emanating from, you pass a huge bed as you make your way to the food cooking over a fire. Paying no attention to the bed, you start eating, throwing the empty bones outside. It’s here that Polyphemus returns home with his flock of sheep, Polyphemus, is a cyclops and he isn’t happy that you’ve invaded his home and ate his food. You try to escape the cave and one of your crew gets stamped upon and eaten by the cyclops. He now rolls a large boulder into the caves entrance trapping you in the cave with him. Knowing that you have no way out and that he’s eaten, he goes to bed for some beauty sleep. Odysseus has a cunning plan! Tying the sheep together into a giant ball, you’ll then be able to roll the sheep downhill and hit the boulder blocking the exit out of the way. The faster you can roll the harder you’ll hit the boulder; it will take more than one hit to move the boulder and set you free. After your first roll downhill, obstacles will appear on the track, these will slow you down or block your path. In this tutorial if you hit anything you could lose some of your sheep in your ball. If you lose too many of your sheep then you may not be strong enough to move the boulder at the end.  After removing the boulder blocking the exit, Polyphemus awakes with his club dropping into his eye, blinding him. However, he manages to make it to the cave entrance, stopping you from escaping. Although Polyphemus is blind, he could still grab you as you exit the cave, so to escape you and your crew clamber to the underside of the sheep to exit the cave. Once out of the cave Polyphemus closes the cave entrance with the boulder again thinking that you are trapped within. However, you make it back to your ship where you start taunting the cyclops, so he throws the boulder which blocked his cave. The boulder lands on Odysseus squashing him while everyone else gets thrown from the ship. With Odysseus squashed you’ll continue on as Elpenor, Polyphemus is still after you but you’ve managed to hide behind the gates of a castle. Polyphemus is at the top of the hill and has plenty of boulders to keep throwing at you. You’ll be safe as long as those boulders don’t break through the gates of your castle. As it happens your crew are skilled builders so you’ll be able to construct defences to stop the boulders from reaching you. While you are placing defences down the enemy will also be placing them down on your track to stop you from smashing down his gate. The winner will be the one to enter the castle of thier opponent. It can take two or three bashes on a gate before it gives way, if it doesn’t give way at first then you’ll restart at the beginning of the track once a new boulder has been carved out for you to roll down the track. Each time you restart at the start and are waiting on a new boulder you can add new defences. After completing the tutorial, you find yourself on the World Map, there’s a white line with dates marked on it at certain points. Where you start the date is 842 BC, nearby are Padlocks with Stars on the front of them. These indicate how many Stars you must own in order to open that Padlock. Once opened each padlock will reveal a new location. There are various game types at each location, maybe four or five types. The game types which you will come across are War, Obstacle Course, Time Trials. Skee Boulder and Unit Challenge. War is where you’ll place defences against your opponent map and try to reach and break into their castle before they do the same. Unit Challenge is the same although you’ll have limited resources in which to build your defences. Times Trials has you rolling a bomb down towards the enemy’s weapons stash hidden behind the walls of their castle. You must reach the enemy’s stash before your rolling bomb explodes. Skee Boulder is where you’ll need to break as many targets as possible and be the first to land in the giant platform at the end of the track, doing so will multiple your final score.  With each of the games there are objectives which will determine how many stars you’ll collect for completing that level. Also scattered around the world map are small islands with Pillars upon then, these are new Defences which you can unlock. The number of stars on the pillars indicate how many stars it will take to unlock the new defences. You can customise your Army Leader, decorate your Boulder, and choose a banner, you can also choose a colour for your boulder decoration and banner. You will also unlock new boulders to play with and you can choose which to use on any map as you start that level. A light boulder may be better than a heavier one while on time trials but less effective when trying to bash down a door.  You can also play against other players online and you can even make you own maps, I haven’t tried either of these yet so I’m unsure of any outcome. However, if the online games are anything like they were in the second iteration of the game then it was certainly fun, especially after spanking The Cpt Froggy’s botty. In the options you’ll find settings for Camera - Boulder View; Camera Sensitivity, Camera FOV, Camera Adjustment Speed, Invert Y Axis. Strategy View - Rotation Speed, Movement Speed and Border Movement. Video – Resolution, Brightness, Window mode, Vertical Sync and Quality. Advanced Video Settings – Texture Quality, Antialiasing, Effects, Shadow, Postprocess Quality, Resolution Quality, View Distance Quality, Mirror View Distance and Motion Blur Quality. Controls - Global Controls for both Keyboard and Game Pad, Boulder Mode, Construction Mode. Audio - Sound Effects and Music. Game - Language (English, French, German, Italian, Chinese, Korean, Russian and Spanish), Difficulty, Controller Vibration, Destructible Density, Voice Chat, Show Rankings and Delete Progress.  Positives + Fun characters + Looks and sound good + Has achievements + Has cards Negatives - I got stuck on one of the islands on the world map - Can be frustrating  Build defences, race against time, smash down the defences and gates to your enemy’s base with varying boulders in Rock of Ages 3: Make or Break. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me just say that I am horrified by what they've done to the soundtrack. What was memorable & unique about the first two games in the trilogy was the Patricio Meneses soundtrack. Fun, kid-friendly renditions of classical music from different periods that beautifully supplemented the graphics, which also changed with time period! This has been reduced to "medievalist rock n roll kitsch". Imagine Monty Python, but with electric guitars. Yeah........ Did they fail to get Patricio Meneses onboard this time? Presumably his name would've otherwise been plastered all over this title - which it isn't. And I can only guess because there is no information online, and the credits can only be reached by beating the campaign.The credits are not the only thing missing from the menu, though. Minimalistic is an understatement.The game is a bit buggy right now, which is to be expected when playing on release day. This wasn't the case with RoA2, though. And as far as I can tell, RoA3 is just an expansion pack. Same engine, same UI, same graphics, most of the game is made up of one hundred percent recycled assets. They hadn't changed a thing. We get the "meh" mapmaking tool (main selling point of the game, apparently), some prebuilt maps, and some new units (though most of them recycled).What I'm upset about the most, apart from the soundtrack, is that they charge full price for this abortion, as though it were flirting with AAA title status. This being a 33% price increase over RoA2... for an expansion pack which recycles old material, doesn't fix the old problems, introduces new ones, and releases in a messy, buggy state, lacking the various art styles of previous installations, with soulless, unfunny cutscenes, and with a way weaker soundtrack.This is difficult for me since many people will tell you that I have been a very big fan of RoA titles so far. But not this one. I actively regret the purchase. Buy RoA 1 or 2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It needs a HEAVY polish, starting in the "Make" mode. The camera controls need tweaked. This includes limiting the zoom in speed to around a quarter of the current value, also preventing the camera from clipping through objects and track pieces. The max zoom out needs increased to accommodate taller track pieces, or limit the height tracks can be build. Moving the camera across the map by moving the cursor to the edge of the screen needs to be doubled the current value, as I relied on the middle button grab and swipe method a little too much and causes the camera to jerk. Track placement needs to be limited, I found it easy to kink the track in places when adjusting them, which made a niche that caught and broke my boulder multiple times. I feel like track pieces need to "snap" together as opposed to drawing them in place. This is also why the AI doesn't seem to work when making longer tracks. This is an error on my part since I should of drawn the length of track first before adding breaks for jumps and forked paths. I noticed the "air flow" graphics are missing that were in the trailer, they would help to show the flow of the track so the player and the AI would know where to go to finish the track. Placing down units seems bugged too, with the banner model not showing up on the cursor sometimes before placement. After choosing what units the banner would spawn I couldn't exit the selection menu without hitting Esc twice. It was also annoying that I couldn't place normal towers and walls, instead they were the boiling tar variant. I also I had a lot of lag on the map I made, the track is a little long but does not have that many units placed. When validating it to publish it there was no lag, but that doesn't spawn the obstacles so the lag has something to do with it. The UI seems clunky, I have no idea whats selected and it seems like there's 2 options selected at once. This also carries through the title screen and options menu and map selection. There's also a bug in the Vs. screen in story mode, after I skip the intro cut scene. The opponent sometimes will face to the right which makes for a hilarious start to the match! Also there is a bug in the story mode on the map screen. You can spam unlocking power ups for as long as the pop up is on the screen. (lots of confetti!) Everything else is rock (hahaaa) solid. OST is killer. I love classic remixes and reminds me of TSO so much. The story mode is great. The bosses are good even though the Vitruvian Man seemed easy. Just wish there were some more variety in track obstacles and objects. Please keep the patches coming!

The music felt way less involved or researched this time using way more generic classical standards than probing the depths of period music and classic arrangements we got in the first two games. It’s good but not as amazing as the earlier games. The humor and story telling is the weakest and only got like one laugh out me for the whole game and some very faint chuckles. _childDocuments_.review: Do not recommend. The second part of Rock of Ages (ROA2) is so much better.This game is unfinished, buggy, unfair, repetitive, and just straight up boring.Here are the reasons for my conclusion:Unfinished:The cutscenes are short, low quality, and oversaturated. They also lack creativity - compared to ROA2.The game modes are more or less copies of each other, giving the illusion of choice while having the same exact concepts.Overall, this game follows the motto "Quantity over Quality." It is a vastly different experience compared to ROA2.Buggy:There are so many bugs. The most annoying one is probably spawning in a way where you always die instantly again.The other ones are minor but ruin the experience. For example, the enemy looking in the wrong direction or just not being there at all at the beginning of the fight.Also, Humpty Dumpty's death animation being a buggy spectacle.Unfair:The AI in this game has a very different collision than you. As soon as you touch them, you lose all your momentum and come to a complete stop, while the AI continues flawlessly.Sometimes the AI gets stuck.When players die or fall down, they get set back a decent amount. When the AI falls down, it just skips the trap that made it fall, making bigger traps completely obsolete - extremely frustrating.Some objects don't seem to have any mass, making you fly through them.Sometimes the castle does not have collision in the back, making you dive out of bounds.Other times, the game is extremely laggy with no apparent reason.The castle can explode in a stacked explosion, instead of just one, when parts of the map was skipped.Repetitive:The game modes are boring; there are many old weapons or rocks (more than half), and other things just make you think like spending money on this was not worth it.Even the cutscenes seem repetitive - it's always the exact same joke.The music also seems to be worse. There are some good tunes, but most of it is repetitive again and just tiring.Also, nobody plays this game. There is basically no online matchmaking anyway, and getting your friends into this would be a bad financial decision.[...]All in all, my rating will be:Game Design (3/10)Creativity (2/10)Gameplay (5/10)Fun (4/10)Uniqueness (6/10 - only the concept, not this game)+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++TOTAL: 4/10 or ★★☆☆☆+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++Just play ROA2; this is not worth it - even when it was just a $3.00 key.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock of Ages 3: Make and Break is a game developed by ACE Team and Giant Monkey Robot and published by Modus Games and 3goo and is the sequel to Rock of Ages 2: Bigger and BoulderI truly loved the original Rock of Ages with it's quirky characters, funny comedy, Monty Python-esque cutscenes and so on. The sequel took what was great in the original and made it fun and different, somewhat... In this third game, ACE Team and, surprisingly a new developer joining the fray, Giant Monkey Robot literally copied and pasted the sequel; Rock of Ages 2, however, they took a few  steps back in my opinionFirstly, the good thing they did was that they kept the quirky characters, funny comedy and the Monty Python-esque cutscenes, I feel if these were even slightly changed from the original, then it wouldn't be a Rock of Ages game and I'm glad ACE Team and Giant Monkey Robot understood what made Rock of Ages, , and managed to keep those cutscenes inWhat the first game had which was made completely different in the sequel and they kept in the third game is it's linear gameplay. The first game went from one era to another and even though that's still evident in the sequel, the developers made it into a world map. As with the sequel, I hated this change as I was so used to the linear style of gameplay however, as opposed to the sequel which after a while of playing, I got used to it, I absolutely hated it hereAnother change they did was the addition of boss battles... why? These boss battles felt really out of place, although I found them slightly funny, the way they handled them, was way too easy and few and far between. I feel that these boss battles were unnecessaryAnother addition which I felt was unnecessary was the addition of some sort of mini-games which need to be played to gain more stars to unlock more sections of the world map, as otherwise, you won't be able to progress in the game which was really annoying and made me miss the liner gameplay even moreAnother thing I noticed was that the A.I. is ten times cleverer and you will fail once or twice (on normal difficulty), so they definitely kept it much more challenging as they did in the sequelAnother thing I noticed was that the developers kept this game mainly for co-op and multiplayer, which is fine and all, however, I have no friends, so I couldn't really try out the co-op or multiplayer components of the gameRock of Ages 3 does some (sort of) good things and makes some more bad things. This time, it is definitely an okay historical game, remains very funny and very very challenging - if you like that, also it includes co-op and multiplayer - if you also like that, but I feel like the 'Rock of Ages formula' is starting to get repetitive, boring and not fun, it is an okay and challenging game to play alone or with your friends, but this game feels more like an expansion or DLC to the sequel and not a new full original game, it lacks originality and innovation which made the original so greatRock of Ages 3 is definitely not my favourite if I had to choose between Rock of Ages, Rock of Ages 2: Bigger and Boulder and Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break and I feel like the trilogy should be put to rest and leave it be

_childDocuments_.review: I've always LOVED the Rock of Ages games.  I started on the first one on my uncles 360, to the second one on my Xbox One, now to the THIRD one on my computer.  It's amazing how far this cute little game has come, and I hope it continues to grow with the new features and new game modes.  I really like the new boulders and units, and I like the mario maker kind of style with the level creator and community levels and multiplayer.  I don't fully think it's AS superior as Rock of Ages 2, but I think this one is unique with the new game modes and boulders, and I would be interested in seeing a potential fourth one, but that wouldn't be for a good little while.  I could keep going on and on about this, but I still haven't beaten this game, and if any of you are still reading this review, then you should try the game out for yourself, or maybe watch some people play it.  Hope you guys enjoy if you do, and thank you to the ACE company for this amazing game series!

(I can't say much about the final game after all patches, I barely played that.) But for the amount of content you now get more than in the other two parts I really think that a bit of quality loss is acceptable.Of course I would like to see improvements and the biggest change are the maps since they are no longer modeled as an asset but created with the map editor everyone can use. The editor lacks many nice features of older maps and when I tried recreating old maps in the editor I completely failed because of that but the maps are nice nonetheless.TLDR:- Yes, there is a quality loss compared to RoA2- BUT: there is way more content than in any of the previous parts- BUT: we now have community made maps, meaning possible unlimited content- I'd conclude that the devs had a bit of a different focus on this game. More content, a bit less quality. But the quality is not bad. It is just not as good as in RoA2. It is still good.

_childDocuments_.review: Really not as bad as people say it is. A lot of the reviews are calling this 'quantity over quality', but there aren't any more levels than there were in ROA2. The game modes, boulders, and traps all carried over. In fact, so much carried over and stayed the same that you have to wonder why this wasn't DLC for ROA2. I'm positive even the assets are the same ones used in ROA2. 	The 'new' in this package is the 'Make' portion of the game. A level editor. It's pretty basic: you can increase or decrease land height; skew land so it slopes to the left or right; narrow or widen terrain. I'm positive they used this level editor for the campaign itself. To the campaign's detriment.  Rock of Ages levels take place atop bottomless pits or on mountains. But ROA2 had a fair amount of levels that played with the formula. Pompei was atop an active volcano, with the layout having you make your way down and around it. A level based on 'The Scream' (painting) was on flat terrain, with a bridge section atop water. Then there was what I believe was the final level, designed like a downward spiral.	No such creativity here. The level editor is fine for community maps, but I'm positive it's what they used to design the campaign levels. Which is a damn shame, cause it just feels like a lesser experience than ROA2. Not a bad experience like many are saying--it's still ROA. But a bunp from the improving quality each release gave us. 	I also want to touch on the art of each level. ROA2 took it further by giving some levels a unique art style to better match either the time period or painting the map is based off. ROA3 does that, but there's less creativity here. There's only so much you can do with a game engine, but I feel the previous game tried pushing its boundaries further than this one. 		The humor and general game formula is still here, so if you enjoyed everything before it you'll like this one as well. It's tower defense for defense and monkey ball for offense. Kind of hard to screw up, really. Some of the community maps are interesting, and if you can find others to play this with there's further game longetivity there. But I have a feeling most people are in it for the campaign, and this is possibly the weakest of the trilogy. Still good, but weaker than the last. You generally expect follow ups to be bigger and bolder than the last. 	I'd definitely stop short of calling this game bad, though. I definitely still had fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock Of Ages 3 is a fantastic sequel that expands on 1 and 2 in nearly every way. The shame is...the few problems it has are pretty massive ones. In terms of positives, the game looks gorgeous. I've always loved the art-styles of these games, but 3 takes it to another level. Some levels like Russia almost made wanna stop and take in the beautiful surroundings. The soundtrack is incredible too, with both a symphonic and rock variant of each track depending on whether you're attacking or defending, while still being based on classical music. Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Elizabeth of England's attacking track (a rock cover of Vivaldi's Four Seasons) is some of the best music I've heard in a game in the past year.The core gameplay remains largely unchanged from 2, which isn't a huge issue cause its still fun. The extra modes you can play for progress are quite fun though. Skee-Ball Runs and Time Trials in particular are a blast while the new Wonderland levels are really fun precision platforming levels. But by far the biggest improvement overall are the boss fights. There's still only 4, but they're much more interesting. The fight against the Vitruvian Man and the final conflict with Poseidon are the highlights of the game.So far, it all sounds great right? Weeeeelllll...not quite. To start, the difficulty curve is all over the place. One level can have me blast down the opponent in about 3 strikes, but the very next can set up a wall of death within seconds while blasting my door to bits. The opponents ALWAYS have an advantage and it doesn't always feel fair. On top of that, while the physics normally work fine, they're sometimes inconsistent. Sometimes my boulder will come to a complete stop in a reasonable distance, sometime it'll soar off the edge at lightspeed, both in the same scenario. Which brings me nicely to the final point.The game's pretty damn buggy. Not "Cyberpunk at release buggy", but still more than I'm ok with. Boulders can glitch through the sides of terrain, sometimes boulders can jump infinitely, some portraits are flipped from how they should be and sometimes the timer for time trials just isn't there. I kind of need to know my time during TIME TRIALS game!Really though, the game's like my castle's door after a round of War. It's battered alright and there's stuff to fix, but the core remains as strong as ever and the emblem on it representing new ideas keeps its lustre. At full price, it'd be a bit of a tough sell, but if it's on discount, I'd recommend giving it a shot. It's not a stone cold classic, but if what you wanted was 2, but more and with extra stuff? Your wish is granite.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this game seems to have less effort behind it than other installments. It does have some new things that breathe life into it, like the Wonderland levels. But it's unfortunate that the cutscenes (which used to be the best part of the game, don't @ me) have fallen far down from what they used to be. _childDocuments_.review: I always wondered what it would be like to expand a simple minigame into a fully fleshed out title. I need not wonder anymore...Rock of Ages 3 is basically Roll the Ball Overdrive. The atmosphere it creates is clearly its highlight. The music, the Terry Gilliam-esque animation and visuals all form into a cohesive and really funny vision. However that doesn't change the fact, that this is the most simple version of the roll the ball game. After advancing a few levels I felt like the game became stagnant and there was nothing else to add or improve, besides my coordination of the ball. The story was funny, but is it as funny that I would force myself play yet another boring track? Nah... I just don't find the gameplay compelling enough to last 15 something hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this game for the first couple hours; suspiciously the time allowed for a Steam refund, but somewhere in that third hour and beyond I truly began to hate Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break.  It was brutally unforgiving and seems to punish the player with every new game mode and every race and attack round within those modes.  It’s easy to deal with when you have options on the map, but eventually you’ll finish all the stuff you enjoy and have stars for and then you have to ask yourself how much hell you want to put yourself through to unlock more of the same punishing gameplay.  I had lots of laughs and fun memories from the first two games, but the third just seems like a bad dream I want to forget.  There is a solid foundation for some serious fun here, but in its current state Rock of Ages 3: Make & Break is a pile of rubble that needs to be avoided.Read full review at

name: Monster Train
detailed_description: Hell has frozen over. Only you can protect the final burning pyre from the forces of heaven and restore the inferno. Monster Train brings a new strategic layer to roguelike deck building, with three vertical play fields to defend. Visit powerful locations To take back hell, you’ll need to power up. Choose your route carefully, different locations give different benefits; upgrade your champion, recruit powerful units, upgrade cards, gain passive bonuses or duplicate any card in your deck. Strategize to fit your playstyle With five clans to choose from, each has its own unique and surprising gameplay. Pick your primary and supporting clan to gain access to all cards from both. During your run you will be able to improve cards by mixing and matching upgrades to open up new roads to victory. You can even duplicate your favourite card at special map nodes before facing off against the final boss. No playthrough is ever the same You’ll never play the same deck twice! Over 220 cards, build up your deck from 10 different starterdecks 5 monster clans with each very different gameplay Each clan has 10 levels to unlock, bringing new cards to your deck Upgrade your clan specific champion multiple times Mod support through Steam Workshop Upgrade any card twice More than 21 unique random events 25 covenant (difficulty) levels Multiplayer HELL RUSH In the Hell Rush multiplayer mode, eight players compete in a frantic real time contest. Each player has the same resources and opponents to create a level playing field. With the clock ticking it’s a test of who can make the best decisions under pressure. Only a true speed demon can remain undefeated. DAILY CHALLENGE Take on a new challenge every day with a hugely modified run due to gameplay mutators. Compete globally and against friends, and climb the leaderboards with a skill-focused scoring system. CUSTOM CHALLENGE Design your own unique challenge and share it with friends. Each custom challenge has its own leaderboard so you can send your friends straight to hell. Content updates FRIENDS & FOES UPDATE The exiled champions have returned to the fold to battle the forces of heaven. This second major update for Monster Train adds new champions, new bosses, new cards, and new artifacts, which combine together to add a significant amount of new strategic options and replayability. We’ve also added a number of frequently requested player features like a personal run records page in the Logbook, an enemy wave counter in battle, and a preview of the ring 3 and ring 6 bosses at the start of a run. WILD MUTATIONS UPDATE This content updates the train tracks with 35 new mutators, new difficulty settings for experienced players and new simple ways to challenge friends and community. HERZAL'S WORKSHOP UPDATE Mod support!

short_description: Monster Train is a strategic roguelike deck building game with a twist. Set on a train to hell, you’ll use tactical decision making to defend multiple vertical battlegrounds. With real time competitive multiplayer and endless replayability, Monster Train is always on time.

_childDocuments_.review: Best deckbuilder I've ever played and I love the genre.Maybe the artstyle is not your thing, or the trailers seems too... casual? But in reality this is far more complex than Slay the Spire, with a lot of statistics and possible synergies combining all the clans.There are 25 levels of difficulty, 5 clans that you can match with one another, lots of different upgrades for the cards...Look for Northernlion let's play if you have doubts about the game.The only thing that could improve the game is maybe more enemy variety, I guess they will go to that (or another clan) for possible DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Very much like Slay the Spire, but with an emphasis on tactics. It's sort of a blend of StS and tower defense games. If you enjoy rogue-like deck building games, this one will not disappoint. Overall I love the game and the way it plays, but my one complaint is the disparity in clan difficulty. The red/purple clans are much more difficult to win with as primary than the green clan and the yellow clan (Umbra) are frustratingly difficult to make work. I kept on failing run after run until I unlocked the final clan and I'm on a 3 win streak with them as primary and I'm not even that good. I like how different each clan is to play and the emphasis on synergy between them, but some of the cards are just diametrically opposing strategies and it makes it a struggle to even get past the first fight.7.5 or 8 out of 10, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a good step away from Slay the spire. Now I have to deck building games that have different feels but still have the core mechanic I know and love that I have doing since the early days on MTG. Deck building is still my all-time favorite nerd/geek/gamer pass time and I would highly recommend this to anyone else that has ever play STS, Marvel Deck builder, or build their own commander deck in magic. This is 100% a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Great deck building game with its own unique twists! I view it as almost Slay the Spire meets tower defense - easy to enjoy this game if you love either of these genres. Pros:- Pick 2 out of 5 interesting factions. The factions have strong archetypes and unique champions, e.g. tanky, spellcasty, which allows you to create synergies within and between them. - Tower defense twist to it, where you have to stop monsters from reaching your 'heart' while striking a balance between offense and defense. - Fun power spikes. No boring upgrades like '+1 to attack' here, every upgrade can easily boost your deck strength by 20%, 50% or 100%. Yet somehow, the game is still balanced, it doesn't ever becomes too easy. - Fun game play. Just a lot of fun, everything is at the right pace, animations are fun to watch, game play loop is satisfying!Suggestion- Will be great to make it faster to unlock factions. I've won 3 runs with the 3 factions I unlocked, but still only 2/3 way to unlocking the 4th faction, and 1/3 to unlocking the 5th.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I saw Monster Train, I smashed that purchase button enthusiastically. However after 12 hours of play I am a little confused - I was expecting to drive The Ghan, Australia's 2.5KM long train, or perhaps trek the enormous Trans-Siberian railway which is 9,300KM long, going hog wild in the Big Boy 4014 (a guy can dream right!). Sadly it turns out it's a game about monsters on a train, not monster trains or tracks of the world. I was past the refund window, but I guess an on-the-rails monster card game is alright too.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Very deep roguelite deckbuilder.  I've spent 25 hours with it, feel like I've barely scratched the surface.  Steep learning curve to just basic understanding (at least 30+ keywords to learn after first couple games, maybe more???).  I'd imagine an extremely steep learning curve to mastery.  I imagine this is one of those games where you'll see lots of people with 1/2 hour played (immediately intimidated/turned-off), lots of people with 20-30 hours played (tried to learn, failed), and lots of people with 500+ (mastered).That said, if you are willing to put in the time, Monster Train is quite rewarding.  I will probably find myself in the 2nd category, don't see myself really investing the time to get great at the game.But I'm certainly not disappointed with my purchase and if I was missing a game in my life with much depth (right now I'm focusing on my chess game), I could see this taking its place.Casual players beware, too deep to give you a good experience I think if you are trying to go up Covenent levels (basically the games' hard mode).  I also think it's hard to understand why you lost, so the loop isn't particularly forgiving unless you really sit back and analyze what went wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but I do not enjoy anything based on luck. This game is 99.9% luck based. Yes you can make completely dumb decisions and screw yourself... But equally likely is that the game will give you cards that don't work well together.  Nearly everything is random, which means sometimes you'll start the game with artifacts that actually hurt your chances to succeed, or monsters that are all 1 hp, or spells that truly serve no purpose.Developers looked at procedural generation and thought "slot machine the entirety of every game so as to eliminate player skill from the equation".Just updating my review to show that I keep trying to like this game. It's just too luck based for me to enjoy it. If you are the type of person that plays the lottery, you'll likely enjoy this game. It is also a tax on stupid people.

The (so far only) DLC adds a metric F-ton of new builds, mechanics and possibilities and an optional, harder Endgame. If you like Deckbuilding and Roguelikes, absolute Must-Buy, preferrably with the DLC. But everytime it works, it truly works, and you WILL love it. For real, get this Masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like slay the spire, or card games, I can't recommend this enough. The game makes you split focus on improving units, and forging spells in order to create a deck that can withstand some truly harrowing encounters. Creatures are played from the deck, but it seems like if they perish during combat, they stay in the "expended" pool until the next fight. Keep that in mind, or enhance your favorites with holdover charms to keep them coming back for more. You are bound to come close to success a few times, but to truly beat your final boss, you must maximize your deck synergy, and keep your card pool optimized. I hope there's some more boss variety upcoming, as the same bosses can feel a little stale, but there are modifiers to keep it interesting, as well as challenges in the mid-tier to tempt your greed.   A+ would punch ticket again.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, honestly. I've tried a bunch of games of the sort recently, and Monster Train is the one I go back to the most. The gameplay loop is simple, and you might think it'll get repetitive, but actually, the fact that you have 2 clans (out of 6, or 5 without the DLC) to choose cards from makes it more unique every time you do a run, and it's fun to play on random and see what kind of deck you'll end up this time. The music is great (and I had to buy the soundtrack because of it), and the game is challenging, also letting you increase the difficulty mid-run if you feel confident if you have the DLC. And then there's the little things which keep you playing, such as being able to unlock different card frames, the comprehensive system of stat tracking, and features such as mutators or mods. Even though I've beat all the 25 difficulty levels now, I still find myself coming back to do a run occasionally, just because it stays fun.And there's no real progression beyond unlocking all the cards, which is quite nice. You can easily stay at the lower difficulty levels if you wish as long as you have all the cards unlocked, or you can go and truly challenge yourself.If I had to pick areas for improvement, I'd say the story could be expanded on more, it leaves me wanting more, because all we really get is tidbits in events, the logbook, and character bubbles. I wish I could've found out more about why the Monster Train world is the way it is.Additionally, you could say that the map being virtually the same every time is a bit of a downside (even though it is with slight variety in enemies, boon placement and so on). The difficulty levels don't add much variety, more could have been done in that regard, or just providing more procedural generation or alternate map kinds. If you don't want to replay the same gameplay loop over and over again, then this game is not for you. However, it still remains fun, balanced, challenging, and the feeling of gathering the perfect synergy in your deck, with the right artifacts, and completely obliterating the final boss as the music rings in your ears is intoxicating. Be warned, if you buy this game, it'll probably eat up a lot of your time for a few weeks as you are driven in the quest to reach Covenant 25, but in the best possible way.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Train is a Rogue-Like deck building with elements of a tower defense game. Hell has frozen over, can you take it back?Monster Train utilizes RNG to distribute its many cards to the player after encounters/events. The unique take of Monster Train is that you can choose what two clans of units you can see throughout your run. This leaves up to 20 different variations of builds that can be tried out.There are 5 types of clans, which can be described if anyone has played Magic The Gathering (MTG) as such.The Clans Are as Such: 1. Hellhorned The Hellhorned playstyle is based on aggression, cards are heavy hitters with low health. However some card effects may grant armor to combat the low health. This would be compared to playing White or Red decks in Magic. 2. AwokenYou like to build up tank units and make the enemy kill themselves on your units? The Awoken are for you. With Awoken units you can buff yourself with healing items to buff the strength of your units, and build around multi-hitters and sweeper units to keep defense high and attacker protected. This is compared to playing Green decks in Magic, or Defense Ironclad in Slay The Spire.This game is a fine deck builder if you enjoy this genre of game. If you enjoyed Slay The Spire, you will sure as HELL like Monster Train.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I avoided this initially due to the complexity of the multiple floors, but it's everything I like about Slay the Spire, just a bit more fair - you know more about what your run will be like from the beginning - including which final boss you will face - and you can start embracing deck strategies earlier on as a result. This makes the whole game feel more strategic. The addition of clans adds a magic the gathering vibe to the game as well, with some cool metrics associated with it.While I "won" on my second playthrough, it's clear that mastery of this game takes an intense investment, but it's a great and fun journey with each run taking around an hour or so.
