_childDocuments_.review: This game is genre defining, creative, and deep; while no game is perfect, there is no game like Monster Train, and you owe it to yourself to give this a shot.Deck builder roguelikes are easily my favorite genre of game - I'll play and enjoy even mediocre ones. Monster Train's mix of units, spells, and breadth of mechanics easily stand it apart from the competition. There is a huge diversity of viable strategies, and while it's not perfectly balanced (no deckbuilder is), it does an excellent job at ramping up challenge.Customization (5/5): This is the great strength of Monster Train - you pick two factions every run, which give you access to new combos, units, and mechanics. Each faction explores multiple interesting mechanics within deckbuilding, and each has a distinct flavor. Almost every card has a place in a potential strategy, and while most runs are winnable, every choice matters when putting together the right deck. Speaking of which, your deck changes significantly between each battle, possibly adding/removing 2-3 new cards, artifacts, and upgrades along a selected path.Difficulty (3/5): This is no darkest dungeon - if you're familiar with deck builders, this game offers a moderate, but overcomable challenge as you work your way up the covenants.Replayability (5/5): 160+ hours in, I can safely say this is a permanent classic in my Steam collection. As someone who has much less time to play games than I used to, this is the game I find myself picking up most often for 30-60 min of game time. You can save and quit any time, and at most lose 3-4 minutes of progress if you have to quit suddenly (If you quit mid-battle, you start from the beginning of that battle). It respects your time as well (you can speed up the animations with a simple button in the corner).Mechanics (5/5): There are virtually no bugs, cards interact in interesting ways. Some synergies are not particularly subtle (X mechanic is stronger) but the sheer variety of ways to "break the game" and make weak cards into powerhouses is unparalleled. The game is balanced around needing an extremely strong deck to beat the final boss, and it pretty much always gives you the tools to get there, whether by copying upgraded cards, powerful synergies, or a classic tank/dps unit pairing. Many mechanics, like the three floor train with limited unit space, movement between floors, that enemies frontline tanks for their backline, and the shared health pool (your pyre) are completely unique to the game, and give it unique flavor.This game is a gem, and has been worked on tirelessly by some excellent devs - buy it, play it, don't look back.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed this game so far. It scratches that "Magic the Gathering(tm)" itch, without the abject poverty that comes along with playing it. I personally only play single player so I can't comment on the multiplayer aspects of the game.This game strikes a happy medium between "puzzle game", "deck building card game" and "rogue". It also manages to do it all fairly well. Now you're definitely not going to find the sheer depth that is an established TCG here. There are maybe 80 unique cards per faction and 5 factions total, with a small pool of non-faction cards. (See the similarities already?). Each faction has 2 major heroes and each of those have 3 different variations that you get as you level up.There isn't too much left to the RNG either in most of the runs I've done. Your deck being shuffled is the biggest, after that it'll usually be some trinket you've picked up that maybe procs n% of the time. All in all I've not found myself cursing it even nearly as often as I'd curse at the sky playing a TCG. In the end it all comes down to cleverly drafting your deck. You're going to start the run with a small card pool but you'll gain cards as rewards for events, battles and locations. It's this drafting that really becomes the meat and potatoes of the game. Learning how to manage your card pool, what to add and when to cull is the real root of all of this. If you've got experience with TCGs, this'll all be like riding a bike.The graphics are colorful and a little cartoony; they're fun, not schlocky. Sound is adequate though for long play throughs you'll get tired of the same tracks over and over. I honestly turned the music down after the first few games and I don't miss it.I can heartily recommend this game to anyone who loves TCGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like rogue-likes? Do you like deck builders? Do you like tower defense?Then give Monster Train a shot! On a speeding train to restore the flames of hell, you battle Heaven's guardians to do so. With five different tribes to utilize in pairs, lots of strategy is possible, and often times victory comes to those who plan out a few turns in advance.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Slay the Spire but Fun ?This game is potentially better than slay the spire for a few reasons- More player creativity- Better artwork- 5 Heroes that can be combined for many run types- More impactful choices- Game feels more of a 'fair' roguelite- Push your luck with more player choice rather than slay the spires you randomly die despite perfect decisions.Overall this game is decent in current form and you get your hours for the price, that said its lacking in a few ways that I hope they work on within the year if not I would not recommend this game without a deep sale.- 2 of the Heroes feel too similar in their buff focus which makes them feel pointless and undistinc- UI needs work add logbook to the main menu obviously- Make the monster train icon customizeable because its me on it !- Add more heroes because theres certain kinds of hero missing you would expect to be there- Enemies need to be more intresting and have more intresting deaths- Bosses need more personality- Reduce the starting pack duplicates so much of this game feels like card removalI hope for the best because this game is certainly interesting
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and addictive, and GREAT production value!  Beautiful art, UI, sounds and music, all making for a super engaging experience.  This is the game I now compare other roguelike deckbuilders to...and it makes sooo many of them just fall flat!  If I could change anything it's just that I'd like to see MORE!  Good on you, Shiny Shoe (see I'm a poet!) and I'm looking forward to more from you in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this review is for people such as myself that have never played StS or other, i guess, roguelike/roguelite (no clue) games.  Also, not a big card game/deck building type of player, but this game is really fun.  Every single run through is different based on the buffs you might receive through artifacts, cards and power-ups you use on your cards.  I sat down after buying it and almost 4 hours of my life disappeared.  So for those of you whom are uninitiated to this type of game I highly recommend it or if you are looking for a way to cut down on food consumption, I recommend this as well; as you will forget to eat!  Great job devs and the price point is really a deal.  I have not done any online playing but even that looked promising with online dailies, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I've never liked deck-builder games, then I came across Ratropolis (since city builders are my favorite) and that changed my opinions on deck builders completely.  First game I've ever gotten 100% achievements.Then came Slay the Spire, which I hated;  bored me out of my mind all three times I tried to get into it.Then comes Monster Train.  I am thoroughly enjoying this deck-builder and how they juggle all the different abilities, spells, units, etc.  It is very well done and engaging.The only negative thing I have to say is true among all deck-builder games [I've played] - there's always a mobile feel to them.  If you can get passed that though, it's tons of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: If you like strategic card and deck-building games like Slay The Spire and Hearthstone adventures (like the Dalaran heist, which was a personal favorite of mine) Then this game will probably entertain you for a while.It has a fascinating combat system based on floors on a train and spaces available on it. you start with 2 classes, each with a set of specific class cards, and as you play you unlock more classes, and more cards to appear when you play these classes.Between battles you get to upgrade and alter some cards.The only shortcoming in my opinion is that overall, it seems like the amount of cards in the game for each class are too little, and with very similar card texts. For example, One card gets spikes when you heal it, another gets damage and health, but overall they are pretty similar: you should heal this card to buff it up over the course of the battle. Same goes to hero upgrades, which you can only choose one of two, they generally fall into what feels like a more "dps" buff and a more "tank" buff.The combination of little card text variation and few cards (there are not that many unlockable cards, either) make me worry that this game's replayability may suffer.There's also a multiplayer battle which gives me anxiety (good thing), however doesn't seem like it affects your progress towards unlocking cards and classes.Overall, though, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Feels like a cross of Slay the Spire and a Tower Defence. I think it's less deep than STS, with fewer opportunities for creating interesting combos, but it has more starting factions who all play in different ways. I like that you can customise your units on each run. There's definitely plenty of fun to be had.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Do I dislike this game? NoDo I like this game? Yeah sure.Definitely not better than Slay the Spire. Monster train throws a lot of things at a wall at once and most of it sticks. Nothing is particularly bad. Some things are addicting. Nothing really is a home run though and I was finished with the experience way sooner than I was with Slay the Spire's.Do you buy it? Ehh. Maybe?~4.2/5
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I think many people are gonna compare Slay the Spire against this game while deciding whether to pick this game up or not. My take is that they are different enough to be their own thing, and if you're looking for something different but still having that roguelite deckbuilder experience, then pick this game up.I found myself actually enjoying this game more because it wasn't as difficult as Slay the Spire to start off with, but I can definitely feel the difficulty creeping up with the "Covenant" levels (this game's version of Ascension). Somehow, the losses just don't feel as bad as the losses I get in StS, and I'm more inclined to jump back into another run.  This is further incentivized with the way you can combine two different clans/factions as well as having a different champions for each of these factions. It makes for a lot of build variety that makes me want to keep playing to try out more builds to beat the run.All in all, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like card games? What about terminally ill step-demons? Well, if you answered yes to one or both of those questions, you couldn't have picked a better dayto stumble upon Monster Train.I don't think I have had more fun playing a deck building card game. This game is phenomenal in every aspect of the word and has become one of my all time favorite games. If you haven't picked this game up yet, then what the heck is your problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just solid as ♥♥♥♥. It takes the game play that Slay the Spire mastered, and added more to the formula. Monster Train is a great evolution in the genre of deck builders and can compete with the best of them. My first wins came very naturally and easy, but as the difficulty curved up I have been stumped with some runs. The runs are quick, the art and music are great. I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes Spire or even just deck builder games in general. Monster Train goes one way with it, and Griftlands goes to other way with it. Both are top level games released in 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: You see the hours I had when I posted this? Well, that was literally after a day. I spent so many hours just after buying it and had to force myself to sleep, otherwise I´d be really numb for work.10/10. I´d suggest some balance to certain cards but that´s pretty much saying what the game is about: Cards. It has mulyiplayer, btw. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: After Slay the Spire made me love card games, this one made me love the genre even more. I appreciate the quality of life features like the animation speed-ups. It's just a ton of fun and I've gotten farther in this than Slay the Spire, and it didn't make me want to rip my hair out because of how bad I am at playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: While enjoyable at times, victory is entirely too RNG reliant even for this genre, and it ultimately sours the experience. Losing early on and unlocking new tools is a staple of the genre, but there are so many ways even a well-made deck and unit setup can get royally screwed by sheer dumb luck in this. Even after maxing card clans and unlocking their relevant cards and relics, I always feel i'm fighting Lady Luck over any in-game enemy or boss, regardless of strategy employed. Avoid Monster Train if you prefer your own skill to be the determining factor in whether or not a run is successful. If you're just looking for another deckbuilding rogue-lite game to scratch that itch, I'd look at something cheaper before investing in this. It's not a bad game, per se...just VERY poorly balanced.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I found that the more and more i played this game the less I liked it. The base cards of the game sync very well but as you unlock more and more the decks feel clunkier at the higher difficulties and it starts to become more of a routine "I need these specific cards to win" which get less and less common.I really hope it get's some balance changes soon, will change my review to positive when that happens.*edit, tried to refund, too much time played which the game feels good within the first few hours so that's never fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Dude, a Slay The Spire-esque deck building game but with its own unique mechanics. Its not as crunchy as StS but overall it is a faster paced and harder hitting game, but without sacrificing the the strategic elements of both building an effective deck and then playing it in a smart manner to obtain the win. If you want a rogue-like deck building game that provides a different flavor and provides a refreshing new take to the genre, then I suggest trying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Spire-likes are becoming a thing now, and this one feels the most like playing a card game while also tying in the turn-based RPG elements to an impressive degree, thanks to faction pairing, unit and spell card designations, and a focus on unit combat. The basic elements of Slay the Spire are here (health, armor, trinkets, deckbuilding, etc.), but taken a few steps farther. Playing units on each level of the Train, with limited space, adds a degree of planning and decision-making that other Spire-likes simply don't demand from the player.Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys card games, turn-based-RPGs, or deckbuilders like Dominion or Slay the Spire.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun, casual and very great for killing time.if you want to take a break from big content RPG, endless grinding MMORPG, stressful PvP games and you like deckbuilding kinda games, this is for you. Every run is RNG but that is the beauty of it, sometimes you get very lucky and build very powerful deck, but sometimes you struggle, and somehow have a way to deal with it.One run is around 1 hour top, you can always quit and return anytime, no pressure.9/10 for me. It will be 10/10 when we have different final boss later in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Monster train is a fast-paced rougelike deck builder, unlike Slay the spire where  card synergy matters. It's more like a action, bash'em,  beat-em up. The story is laid of in the very beginning so all that's left is level progression and card collection. The fun comes in exactly what champion you'll pick with what selection of hell's helper. You can play it normally or use game an in option called MUTATOR'S that give you Dante, a kick ass hell warrior. And trust me you want him. All in all you'll have plenty of fight styles to choice from and card deck selections that'll keep you occupied for many hour's! So give the hell train a ride and protect MONSTER TRAIN!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I have been shortlisting Monster Train for awhile, seeing as I already have tons of Roguelites and Deck Builders. I finally decided to give it a try. What turned out to be a 'Let's demo this and see if it's any good", turned out to be an extremely exhilarating 2 hour "Demo session" which got me hooked, leaving me with an immediate "WOW" factor.PROS:+Great synergy and replayability as you mix and match your deck between two factions (Reminds me of Smash Up, which I love).+Great production value and quality from the artwork and animations, making it feel very fluid and top notch (Reminiscence of Bayonetta as you fight the forces of Light).+Decision making is exciting and propels you forward with choices rather than negative RNG. +Game is relatively clean cut and simple to understand with cleverly placed UI and icons to aid players comprehension.+Great Soundtrack, creating a hyped up tempo.To sum it up, this game has HEART.<3 Ever wonder what the name of that kickass soundtrack currently playing is? The Music track pops up in this game.<3 Do you like leaderboards when competing? You can receive live notifications on current daily runs from other players competing simultaneously so your run does not feel so barren.<3 Small little touches like traversing the landscape from top to bottom (Very thematic as hell freezes over). <3 Do you like your patch notes being updated with developer commentary? Well, their YouTube page has that in spades and its obvious the developers care deeply about their game.<3 Do you click to test every single options in the menu? Well, there is a particular Option called "Lore Tooltips" which i would normally click, but the game was kind enough to remind me that the Lore Tooltips is already viewable from the Logbook so I would not have to clutter my in-game with additional text, unless i desire to.Final Thoughts: Monster Train is a very solid roguelite and deckbuilder on its own. However, the additional care and thought process that went into the game propels it to another level and is definitely a keeper, even at full price. And hopefully like me, you are left caring for this little gem, and thus, writing a review of this game in the middle of your run.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that's like Slay the Spire, this is your go to. The game invokes a lot of the same you've become accustomed to over the years with deck builders, but the way the present the formula is a lot better in my opinion. With the "double decks" that you pull from two different clans, you have a lot of ways you can build and adapt to a situation. The roguelike element is pretty much the same. You go until you die and you unlock cards for the decks. Each clan has it's own level and each has it's own unlocks and artifacts. So between the main runs and the custom modes you can build and share out, you should have a lot of game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Trains trailer doesn't, and couldn't, do a great job of expressing what kind of game Monster Train is. If you're expecting StS but throwing down many units into the blender, thankfully you're wrong. Monster Train is about finding something that burgeons into broken and then pressing advantage as hard as you can, while maintaining synergies and a slim deck to keep the rest of the machine moving. Maybe that's just a new players perspective, but boy does it feel fun regardless.The freeform upgrade system allows you to make combinations that feel fun and unique and want to share with your friends. Do recommend. This game slaps.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks NL, this is already a serious GOTY contender!The mechanics are crazy cool, the game achieves this super weird (and probably really hard to pull off) split that almost every upgrade you get seems super powerful when it's actually well balanced. Your cards get out of control at the same pace that the difficulty ramps up, super quick, and as a result the next upgrade-and-battle-phase feels like a rush. Real "just one more turn" vibe from this!the great art goes hand-in-hand with the over-the-top mechanics, and details such as the train you're playing on actually being animated to move at what feels like breakneck speed add a sweet sense of urgency to the gameplay, which is then exacerbated by the very pushy, absolutely *banging* soundtrack!Loving this!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: After my first few hours of playing Monster Train, although I enjoyed it, I wasn't sure why it was so popular. It took me a while to understand the basic combat and card rules, so the results seemed to be based too much on RNG. I think the game could do with an intro tutorial or even a few help screens to explain the basic rules and some of the terms that I'm not familiar with.After making a few unsuccessful runs I started to learn more of the strategies and I began to appreciate how good this game is. Although it could be called a Slay the Spire clone, for me it is better than StS. I enjoyed playing StS but felt at times it was too RNG dependent. Developer support is excellent, they are continuing to add significant features months after the game has been released.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable deck building rogue liteit seems all of these games probably need to be compared to Slay the Spire and I really enjoy the 2 factions deck set up compared to the single classes of StSI am finding it slightly easier than StS but its still a very good challenge and just as addictive as StS too
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Train is a card-game cocktail with a sniff of tower defense and a large dose of strategy, resulting in one heck of a smooth drink with a long and intriguing aftertaste.The story is as simple as weird: Hell has frozen over and it is up to you to drive an Sbowpiercer-like train through the Nine Circles of Hell and deliver the spark that can rekindle the infernal fires. During this journey you will battle angels and priests that invade your train and try to reach the top of your train through 3 vertical levels and attack the heart. Should this 'Pyre' be destroyed, it's game over, so better prevent the heavenly hordes from doing this by summoning your own fiends and other monsters to battle them. So better start drawing those cards and flinging those spells because there is an netherworld to save.'Choice' is one of the main keywords for this game, since a lot is offered to the player. Which clans shall I choose to play with, and then which or the unique gameplay mechanics of the chosen clan will I focus on in my run? What difficulty shall I choose, which starting artifacts and powers and which route should the train take to pickup new units and loot? The balance of all this so very well done: when you lose a run you can usually see where you made a strategic error; rarely did I had the feeling I was unjustly punished by the RNG gods. So all this, together with a cartoony art style, some uniquely weird lore and a decent soundtrack means this is one of the better games I had the joy of playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and trailer really threw me off at first as I just assumed it was a mobile port of some sort. But it's actually an insanely fun deckbuilding roguelike. I am currently at covenant 13/25 and I do find the game a lot easier than Slay the Spire but it adds new mechanics and flavor to the genre that it's well worth playing it regardless of the difficulty. Anyway back to doing runs CHOO CHOO
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something that is both fascinating and frustrating in all the best ways. I will say that the way the format for the decks is designed is novel. It is similar to Slay the Spire in the sense of being a card based roguelike but it adds in the faction blending to give an experience somewhat similar to Smash Up. Creating multiple interesting and interconnected combinations and deck designs. The gameplay is fast and fairly intuitive and even if it feels like you were slapped viciously by the RNG the game flows quickly enough to bring you back fairly fast. Overall I would recommend to anyone who is a fan of similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 40 hours at the time of this review, and I give Monster Train a THUMBS UP!Really love this take on a deck-building card game! There is a lot of replay-ability here for me, at the medium sized price tag it is well worth the purchase. Full controller support, the game feels natural with mouse and keyboard, too. I am going to keep coming back to this one for sure
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: After clearing the true final boss with every single class combination, i can safely say this is up there at the top with Slay the Spire in terms of quality roguelite deckbuilding games. Simply an amazing game in every regard. Can't recommend it hard enough! The DLC is a must-have though for the full experience, but it's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addictive. Each run is ~30 minutes which is the perfect amount of time for me. The difference in clans and how they interact with each other makes for different decks almost every time. There are some archetypes that can be easy to get into (signpost arch-types they would be called in another tcg like Magic the gathering) but there is a lot of room to discover different unexpected synergies.Wholeheartedly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A deep and strategically deep roguelike card game with some tower defense elements. Each faction plays extremely differently, and I never felt like it was bad luck's fault when I lost. The ability to alter and improve your important pieces as you progress means the end of a run feels extremely different than the beginning in a way that you have a lot of control over.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: If you like deckbuilding roguelites like Slay the Spire, there is a lot to like about this game. Starting a run by mixing together two of the five classes creates a lot of variety. Just like StS's ascension mode, this game's 25 difficulty covenants really allow you to hone your skills more and more as you play. I would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Figured I'd update this review to say that after nearly 2k hours in the game... yes this is the best game ever created.Way better than Slay the Spire, much less RNG dependent (every game on the highest difficulty CAN be won, but it will take you quite the journey of learning the ins and outs of the game to get there).  Game is so fun and has so much replay-ability.  I especially love that you can run multiplayer games on it, but they aren't PvP like your typical card battlers, instead everyone has the same RnG and it's just a test to see who can beat the same seed more effectively than the other.  Highly highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Its Slay the Spire meets tower defence type game, absolutely loving it so far. Combat is good, you can break the game which is fun, but you can also think you've broken the game only to get absolutely pummeled at the end.There are interesting systems that sets it apart from other deck builders, the use of 2 decks at once is interesting and leads to some crazy synergies. Think if you could get Silent cards as the Ironclad and just laugh at your 999 defence only to face an enemy that deals direct health damage instead of shield damage.If you need some better insight on the game, I'd suggest watching Northerlions YouTube, the egg is hilariously bad which makes you want to get the game just to do better. But in his defence, he is showing youtube every single mistake he makes, whereas we can just forget it and move on..
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for about 70 hours now, I can confidently say that it is one of the best, if not the best deck building rogue-lite game out there. Monster train combines elements of rogue-lites, deck builders and tower defence game and serves it in a intricately woven package of pure strategic fun. This game will pull you in and keep you engaged through its variety of class combos and enemy variations. You will have to learn to adapt to the run every time, since the bosses have unique mechanics that can counter your decks needing you to build your decks around them.The progression in this game feels awesome, from the gold card collecting from beating the game on high difficulty levels to the subtle unlocking of powerful cards which open up whole new deck archetypes with each level up. Having played a significant amount of this game however, I have discovered all the combos it has to offer. But the journey of that discovery was well paced and enjoyable.Overall, I would recommend this game whether you like the genres it embeds or not. It truly is a one of a kind game in this age or one rip-off after another.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't up to you. Unlike other deckbuilders, its up to the dice you roll and the relics you've unlocked. Worse yet, it's a time sink, requiring far more grinding than other deckbuilders. You'll play your first run and likely lose. You'll play your second and do a bit better, and then you'll play a few more times until you win. As you level up you'll unlock new classes, and in that process the game reveals its worst qualities. You'll lose with those new classes when you unlock them, and by the time you unlock the second heroes, it's clear that the issue with your early runs wasn't how you were playing but that you hadn't unlocked enough quality gear yet. This retroactively soured me on all my prior accomplishments. Additionally, the choices you're given are far more binary and far fewer than other deckbuilders. The economy also seems poorly calculated as I never ran out of gold making the bonus challenges for gold pointless. This leads to really simple decision trees and gives you so little agency that this might as well be an idle game. That helped me get 25 hours in the game as I was depressed and needed something to turn my brain off, but that's also why I'm not playing this game again.Lastly the game has the absolute worst sound work I've seen in a long while. I have to play with the game muted. It's better to look at than Slay the Spire but that's little accomplishment.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of games like Slay the Spire, this is basically "The same, but more, but a bit different".Stands on its own as a concept and is massively replayable. Great art and music accompany addictive gameplay.A roguelike, deck-building card with some interesting twists - there's plenty of fun to be found here.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Two annoying issues with this great game. (1) You basically will get thrown into a game and your chances of winning are solely based on randomly obtaining rare combination of cards...hence, be prepared to waste a bunch of time on random garbage the game sends you to wreck your matches. (2) There is one boss in particular toward the end of the map you cannot beat without having random special high damage cards luckily drawn. The boss attacks 5x to each of 1x attacks. You need the correct Spells and Artifacts. GOOD LUCK! Be prepared to spend 30 minutes in a match with your fingers crossed with low probability you'll luckily get the right combination of cards...
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Like most of the other negative reviews, I found this game lacking. It's ridiculously easy to complete and there's very little in the way of effective choices to be made.I clocked the game first try and with relative ease as well. I assume the nerfs you get as you win more and increase the difficulty are supposed to increase the challenge, however I don't see the fun in it.Maybe I'll have another look in a year or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: When I first got this game I thought it was so awesome. The mechanics are fun, the races amusingly different from each other.. However, I think that one of the best indicators of a good game is that it gets more fun as it gets more difficult. This game fails that test in a rather epic fashion. Firstly, the decks seem to get worse the more cards that you get. The increasing number of cards means that you never seem to get the right combination of cards that were already present in the starter deck. It is very frustrating that you cannot curate your deck. I feel I should feel stronger with better cards, not weaker!Secondly, difficulty mechanic is pretty bad. It simply adds more difficult 'facets' as you progress without adding any new mechanics. So as your deck gets worse, the game gets harder until it feels more frustrating than fun. Finally, the wormkin expansion deck just seems worse than almost any other race. It's just disappointing. Certain mechanics can be powerful, but they require such specific cards so that it most often just falls on its face. All in all, I had a great 50 hrs on this game, a frustrating 19 hours trying to relive the glory days, and sadly I can't see myself playing this anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game and Slay the Spire for rogue like deck building games but I've enjoyed both very much.While Slay the Spire does a slightly better job in many aspects from my perspective, the main class + sub class system in this game makes it very fun to just play over and over again to see what kind of unique deck you can make with each combination of classes. I feel like a couple of cards are slightly overtuned and a couple are slightly weak, but maybe that's cuz I'm still on covenant 3 so I shouldn't be judging card balance quite yet.I'd say the only change I really want in this game is for there to be more variety of the big bosses. Sure they have like 3-4 variations of what they do but it's generally the same except maybe Seraph who has a bit more of a defining difference so maybe Seraph can always be the end boss but having a bit more variety on the 2 mid bosses would be really cool for me overall a very good experience and I'd recommend it to anyone who likes rogue like deck builders
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Slay the Spire with a flavor of Magic The Gathering added on.- Deck Building- 5 Different factions ( You choose a primary and secondary for your run )- Amazing Synergies hidden waited to be found - Unlockable cards- A bare bones multiplayer ( but hey its there )- Difficulty settings into impossible if you look for it
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, even if you never before played a card draw game before, I recommend you try this one out. I'm 14 hours in and i'm HOOKED. Awesome animations, cool game design choices, a LOT of variety and replayability with different combinations of factions and within different heroes, challenges and even a progression system to keep you going. TLDR: Buy this, it's a damn fine game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Great deckbuilding rogue-lite that is similar to Slay the Spire with a few noticeable differences.The runs turn around much faster, averaging around 45 minutes depending on how you play. Because of this, you are less "locked-in" each run and there is less emphasis on building an enormous deck. You also have much more control over what you pick, so you have a lot more flexibility and seemingly mediocre run can turn around rather quickly.The card types are split into Minions and Spells, and you can choose to emphasize either one or both; the minions offer a huge variety is probably my favorite difference from Slay the Spire. The minions vary widely in terms of their stats and many of them have some unique mechanics that can really change a run.You have the progression and the deck types, which is probably my favorite part of the game. Each run, you'll choose a Primary faction that gives you one of two heroes to start with as well as the deck you'll draw from. You'll also pick a  Secondary faction from which you will also draw cards. Each faction has two heroes, and each hero has three specializations that will get upgraded along the run. If you've done the math, that's a lot of widely varied playstyles. The faction are also widely different to play at a fundamental level. I won't spoil the fun, but the three unlocked factions are super interesting from a design perspective and dramatically change the way you approach each run.Overall, this game is a fantastic rogue-lite that is most easily compared to Slay the Spire, but manages to improve on that game and also carve out a niche for itself. If you even slightly enjoyed Slay the Spire or other deckbuilding games for even a moment, buy this game - you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge fan of deck-builders this game was a winner for me. It's a cut above most others.Fights feel dynamic and you have a lot of flexibility on how to deal with the enemy.The mix n' match of faction decks can make for some really subtle or powerful builds.With difficulty scaling this game is great for replayability and challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: So long and sweet of it is this is a Slay the Spire clone with much more color and multiple units to choose from. The game has a rather nice soundtrack which is honestly wasted here because most people I imagine just listen to their own music while playing and this OST could have been paired with a game that has an actual story.          The aspect however that isn't getting enough attention I believe is...how there really is very little challenge/variety in bosses. I personally found the boss encounters bland and repetitive. I beat my first run after about 30 minutes into the game and was disappointed there wasn't an 'end boss' grind or something to at least aspire to. Perhaps there is something I'm missing but...if I can beat the game in under 30 minutes what incentive is there to keep playing? Ideally I could unlock all the units and spells but to me, at least, the thrill would be a foe too hard to beat.      Naturally you can increase the difficulty higher and higher but somehow this level of challenge feels artificial. Imagine playing baseball and always beating the minor league teams and you want to one day win a championship in a large arena with a crowd cheering but instead of facing new and complicated challenges you just fight the minor leagues over and over with sandbags on your ankles. Yes it is harder but it is a difficulty that is self-inflicted and therefor robs you of some of your agency.        All this aside I felt the music, animation and user interface to be top notch. If you enjoyed Slay the Spire and want more of the same kind of grind then give this a try. I'm personally finished as I feel like I've seen everything I've wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun mix of mechanics - deckbuilding and tower defense.  I really like that the runs are short so it's easy to play just a little and have a satisfying experience - and the number of decisions to make per run is just right.  As a fan of Slay the Spire, I've been enjoying Monster Train a lot and would recommend it to anyone that enjoys StS who is looking for something similar.I suspect this has less replay value than Slay the Spire, but still plenty for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Best roguelike or card game I've ever played on steam.  The wide variety of cards and vastly different mechanics of each faction plus the different ways to combine factions gives this game far more replayability than you would guess at first glance.  And that's before getting into the modifiers you can apply to each run and the expert challenges.  The sense of progress provided by climbing covenant ranks, earning card masteries, and unlocking card frame combined with the wide variety of each run has made this game last far longer than any other roguelike or card game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game on the day of release without having heard of it before the day it showed up in my Steam queue.Monster Train is a deck building rogue-like. Expect to play through the game many times (this isn't a bad thing). Here's how it works: You'll choose a primary and secondary faction to join you in your quest to protect your demon train as it travels through the tracks on its way to relight the pyres of hell. At each stop you'll face a boss and its minions. You'll play cards to bring out minions of your own. The object of each level is to keep the angelic minions from reaching the top of the train and destroying the last pyre of hell.Okay, it may sound a touch confusing, but it's super easy to learn.If you like deck building games, as I do, you'll probably like Monster Train. Each game can take up to an HOUR to play through, so it's similar to a digital board game in many respects. Maybe you make it to the pyres and relight them, probably you'll get killed by Fel ... or that ass with the bombs. But you WILL have fun along the way.  I've played it ever day since I picked it up and I've been having a blast.  I hope you do too.  #Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Single Player Card Drafting game very much in the Slay the Spire mindset of continues small decisoins that add up to define your progression through the game.  Combat takes more of a Magic the Gathering mindset of summoning creatures to defend yourself and beat back your opponents than StS's more typical RPG combat.  Runs are a good length, about an hour, to fit well in a single session but you'll end up starting a new one to try some new mechanic or get revenge on some boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Slay the Spire:I should play this perfectly and calculate my damage accordingly.Monster Train:Haha minions of hell goess brrrrIt is very fun and explosive. The first impression is really great when you're exploring the demon factions and see the numbers go up. Monster Train doesn't concern itself with OP builds and let's you go ham.But it is not really the thinking man's game like Slay the Spire, or Hearthstone, or, which i thought it was similar in party building sense: Darkest Dungeon. It does not have the same depth, or synergies. Unlike Hearthstone, you hardly have any units you can reliably make use of, as you can't really hold onto your hand. It is also more difficult to build a deck as reliable as Slay the Spire, due to the train overworld where you have to choose between only two different combination of rewards. and also because you have to mix two demon classes. So you really have no idea what build you're going for, and you don't get stores or events to buy yourself the cards for them.It also doesn't make use of movement and positioning like Hearthstone or Darkest Dungeon, even though it has the mechanics for it with an extra layer on it which is ascending and descending between wagons.So as the difficulty goes up, i feel like it will be very difficult to make reliable strategies without the RNG screwing you. But the good part is, this game is still very fun without making 300 IQ plays. Additionally, this game has great ideas and a great foundation and i really hope the devs continue working on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent deckbuilder/tower defense.Very polished for an initial release.  Great artwork, soundtrack, animations.Card balance is good, game has depth; both vertically in climbing the ladder like in Slay the Spire, and horizontally with multiple factions that get unlocked as you accomplish certain goals in the game.one of the best deckbuilders I have ever played.  very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game has built on the foundation laid by Slay The Spire and, in my opinion, improved on it in almost every way. If you enjoyed Slay The Spire, you absolute should buy this without hesitation. If you haven't, but you enjoy good rogue-like games or card games/deckbuilding games - you should not miss this.You should be prepared for a merciless difficulty curve -- however, losses rarely feel unfair and climbing through the Covenant (difficulty) levels feels like an accomplishment. You'll always feel like you're learning the game better and continuing to find satisfying card interactions/combinations.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A rather unique take in card-rougelike games, what I appreciate the most about it is how good the battles flow. It is infinitely entertaining, easy to learn, easy to master, and a pleasure to play thanks in a lot part due to its amazing soundtrack. The only game in the same venue I can put above it is Slay The Spire. My sole problem with it is that the "completing" the game is not that fun, but, hey, a run or two? Hell Yeah!I give it a 9.5/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, love the art and animations. It's very clever. And complicated, steep learning curve and so many synergies and game mechanics to consider with every build and bossfight. Only thing I really dislike are the card and champion unlocks. It's designed in such a way to make unfavourable decisions for your build to unlock cardframes and champion upgrades. Just to make you play more. That's very lame design in my opinion. Game is complicated and hard enough without being forced to make ♥♥♥♥♥♥ build decicions.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Its not a bad game, I think Slay the Spire is much better, but this game certainly isn't worth 25 USD. My main complaint is the enemies are exactly the same every run, sure some of their modifications change, but its hardly noteable. Some may like it as a feature but i think it gives less variety on a per run basis. So my recommendation is to buy it on sale for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. If you enjoyed Slay the Spire, this is an auto-buy. Something I really enjoyed in this game that set it apart: Mastery of cards. Unlocking all the cards and getting gold borders for them is a really fun completionist hobby!I think this game is screaming for a mod that lets you play as the Winged. The art and animations are there. Someone just needs to spend the hundreds of hours making the cards and code... NOT IT!Also, I was a little surprised that there wasn't a Fallen Angel themed faction. Maybe DLC? If they put out DLC for this game, I'd be throwing money at my monitor, because this game is worth every penny. With the added mod support, I can see this game providing hundreds of hours of enjoyment. If you're on the fence, just buy it already.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super addictive and fun! It is such a great excitement to try creating the most compatible deck. The only problem is the lack of game length, I hardly want to see how far my deck can be and it is sad to have the feeling of "losing this deck" after the end of run. I suggest adding an Endless mode after the final boss.Besides, hopefully the develop team can research on the possibility of multiplayer cooperate mode. I bet this game will be more epic if I can play together with friends. Anyway, 9/10 for me already. Nearly a perfect game except the point I mentioned.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This is goooood. Also scratches my deckbuilding rouguelike itch like Slay the Spire did - except that in Monster Train, games are much shorter, so it's easier to pop in for a quick game before bed etc.Also: I bought it 2 days ago. Days in which I worked and had to drive several hundred kms. Somehow I played 11 hours in this time. It's gooood.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: As I stand guard on the Monster Train, I cannot help but marvel at the irony of it all. Hell has frozen over, and the inferno that once raged with unbridled fury has now been reduced to a mere flicker. But as the last line of defense for the final burning pyre, I must stay vigilant and protect it from the forces of heaven.The stakes are high, but the journey is thrilling. With each battle, I collect new cards and artifacts, each one bringing me closer to restoring the inferno to its former glory. The strategy involved in building my deck and choosing which demons to summon is endlessly entertaining.But the challenge is real. The enemies are fierce, and their tactics unpredictable. I must constantly adapt and evolve my strategies if I hope to survive. And the rewards for success are truly satisfying. The sense of accomplishment I feel after a hard-fought victory is unmatched.In Monster Train, the fate of Hell is in my hands. It is up to me to lead the charge against the forces of heaven and restore the inferno. It's a daunting task, but one that I am more than ready to take on. Bring it on, angels. I am ready to defend the final burning pyre and ensure that the inferno burns bright once again.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches the same itch as Slay the Spire, and much better in my opinion! I haven't played STS since downloading, this game is so good!However, completionists will very likely feel frustration. For example, there is an achievement to earn 50,000 points in a daily challenge. As of writing this, today's challenge was attempted by 715 players, with the highest reaching 46,140 points. If you want to 100% this game, expect to put in a lot of time.The game has a lot of tools to customize your run and create the deckbuilding experience that best fits your preferences. If you think this game might be your type, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice Card game / Rogue Lite... Scratches the typical CCG Itch trying to come up with broken combos and interessting builds while being somewhat relaxing since you are playing the computer and not other players. Even multiplayer is about beating the computer better and/or faster than your opponents.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A great deck-builder with RPG and Tower Defense elements. 40 clan/leader combos all with their own unique flavor and playstyle, detailed customization, hundred of relics and special events, 25+ difficulty levels, community challenges, and crazy casual play options give the game a ton of replay value. The devs are actively adding more to it, and support the modding community too! It even has some limited multiplayer interaction beyond leaderboards for the daily challenges and such. A pretty great pickup overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: The main game is a weird stress/zen combination where it's pretty easy to become powerful at the end of a run, but getting there is a challenge. However, where I've spent most of my time actually has been the multiplayer, with a fast timer counting down and limiting your thoughts, competing for the most successful, riskiest runs has me doing run after run. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Simple to understand, but there is lots of depth that opens up to you almost immediately.  Game plays a lot like Slay the Spire, but has a lot more going on mechanically.  Difficulty gets brutally difficult as you unlock higher and higher levels that force negative modifiers on you that you have to work around. Class combinations are numerous, allowing you to mix and match any two of the 5 factions that determine what cards and, by extension , what playstyles are available to you in any given run.  Outside of the RNG of card draw, the game isn't super gimmicky with random events.  They are pretty tame and won't completely decimate your run when you come across them.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have too much time? Too much money? Enjoy agonizing through every little decision? Monster Train can help you with all of those problems! The good:+Wildly entertaining, a deckbuilder that is deep, wide, and more forgiving and transparent than predecessor Slay the Spire+Decisions matter, but often both your options have significant upside potential, so it becomes a process of deciding what's best in short term vs. long-term for your particular run / game state+Tons of variety - each run feels very different, despite fighting same enemies+Progression and pacing are satisfying, take it at your own speed+OP combos not nerfed into the ground by devs but rather encouraged / to be discovered and exploited when you can+Opt into more risk (and more reward) when you're feeling strong on certain fights - build an unstoppable snowball of hellish destruction! +Music, graphics and animation are all a win for me. Some may disagree, but they're wrong. When in doubt turn on googly eyes for a good time. The could-be-better: -Eventually I'll want more variety of fights, enemies, and backgrounds-Music is great, but if you're putting in dozens or even hundreds of hours, it will get stale-Price is a bit high to try it out (but if you decide you love it and pump tons of hours in, it becomes a steal in terms of value). I got it 10% off in Steam summer sale, but can recommend it at full price to anyone who already loves deckbuilders like Slay the Spire.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well polished for a game coming out of nowhere. Music is great. Gameplay is great. Synergy between factions is great. UI and multiplayer elements are great. It not only stands on the shoulders of giants of rogue-likes past (heavy emphasis on Slay the Spire), it vaults off and soars. I genuinely hope this game doesn't get ignored. The only weakness I can foresee would be a lack of proper scaling to keep it interesting after enough runs. I've only progressed through about 1/5 of the levels of difficulty available. I get the feeling the difficulty will ramp up at a reasonable level, and there is still tons of progression left in the way of unlocking new cards. There just needs to be a point that hits that perfect balance of "hard" and "rewarding". I have felt that the limited chances to add combat units to your deck can win or lose you a run depending on their quality. I will probably update this review if it plateaus hard, but for now I don't feel it.Outside the above, I just hope to see more updates released for the game. New factions would be amazing, but there might not be huge amount of design space left. Re-balancing as things go, and new modes would also be great.If you enjoy deck building rogue-likes. Or Darkest Dungeon. Or most other modern turn based strategy games I would highly recommend you pick this up
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply, this is the most fun I've had with a deck builder.  It has a looser design than something like Slay the Spire, but it has a much greater variety of possible builds as a result.  The main single player mode has 20 possible combinations of primary and secondary clans, and there are 25 Covenant ranks to climb, each with higher and higher difficulty.  I am currently at Covenant 10 and I can see that it will take a lot more practice to progress further.The Daily Challenge and Challenge modes have a selection of interesting and entertaining modifiers available, and I have enjoyed the few I have tackled so far.Hell Rush, the multiplayer mode, is also very fun and a surprisingly fresh approach.  You are placed in a lobby with a handful of others and much work against strict time limits to clear each combat encounter with the same initial setup as your competitors.  If you die, you are dropped from the competition.  If you run out of time, the combat will auto-resolve from that point on, meaning you can play no more cards and must hope your units last on their own.  Succeed, and you will be competing for score with the remaining competitors.Simply put, if you enjoy deck builders and roguelites, this is more than worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game in which strategy matters more than luck. Some clans are clearly more powerful than others, so ultimately it's tempting to stick to a particular play style and not take advantage of all the variety available, but being able to mix primary and secondary classes, being able to add modifiers, and the daily challenges all result in a fresh experience after >25 hours of playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult for me to write this review without referencing another game, Slay the Spire, and if you aren't familiar with that game than this review might not be the one you should base your choice to purchase Monster Train on. In short, Monster Train is a Rogue-like Collectible Card Turn Based Tower Defense Game. You pick two factions which represent decks of potential cards, and use those cards to defend against waves of enemies that are attacking your 4 tiered "train". After a few rounds of minor enemies you have a boss fight and, should you defeat that boss, you are able to choose upgrades in the form of passive bonuses and improvements to your cards abilities. The narrative is very thin and, as a rogue-like you are meant to loose often and start again with better knowledge of how to play and different randomized elements for the next run. The fun comes not from the story or twitch skills but from overcoming the challenges through mental skill and preparation. That's the game in a nutshell. Now if you are Familiar with Slay the Spire, it must be said that in concept and general gameplay this game is very similar but there are enough differences to make it worthwhile. First the runs tend to be MUCH shorter. A solid run in StS typically took several hours for me, while most of my runs in MT clock in at an hour or less. Obviously you may take more or less time to make your moves, but I doubt anyone would claim that MT is as much a draw on your time. In my opinion this is a very good thing as it means that I can play an entire run in a single sitting, which allows me to stay familiar with the deck I have been building where as sometimes I would play StS for an hour or so and have to quit only to come back a week or two later and have to re-familiarize myself with the game in progress.Second, possibly as a result of the shorter times, the game is a good bit easier in my opinion. While you can certainly add modifiers (called a "covenant level") which make the game more difficult and interesting, the general flow is a bit more forgiving due to less combat overall and more upgrade opportunities between combat. If you are the type of person who really loved digging into Slay the Spire and overcoming its ever mounting challenges then Monster Train may not hold your interest as long, but that is not to say that MT is without depth and a worthy game in its own right. I could continue to compare and contrast Monster Train with Slay the Spire for several more paragraphs but the bottom line is that Monster Train is a good game and if you like the elements that it brings you should enjoy it well enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: this is a very underrated game! it feels quite intense for a card game and the power gains during each run is usually satisfying, the graphics are nothing to write home about but the artstyle is quite competent and even pleasing sometimes. there's a problem with visual clarity when one too many units are on the same floor, sometimes it is hard to tell where's what.the sound bits are interesting and add some personality to each faction but the music is just... there, it does nothing for me but it is not offensive to listen to.all in all this is definitely a hidden gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: A tower-defense, turn-based, rogue-like game inspired by Slay the Spire where you need to think carefully about unit placement, play-style (Big Magic DPS, stacking stats e.t.c) and overall the choices you make in order to re-kindle the flames of hell.Things I love about this game is that although you move from area to area, gaining strength and adding/upgrading spells and units, is that you don't necessarily feel weak straight from the start (but maybe this will change as I climb the difficulty levels);- Given random cards from the 2 factions you choose initially (making every experience feel somewhat unique)- The variety of playstyles from needing to choose 2 out of 5 factions.- The system that calculates damage taken, dealt and if units will die (numbers get big and rather than trying to calculate everything, you can focus more on decisions you need to make such as sacrificing or losing pyre health).- The pyre being able to attack is a quirky feature.- Thinking my deck is overwhelming and then being overwhelmingly crushed by the Seraph.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: How did I become sooooooo addicted about this game? At first look, the graphics were like a mobile phone game for me, and I want to play on PC, so... I wasn't pretty sure. But then, I begin to play a first run, and Oh my! I was so impressed by the love the devs gave to this game in every aspect of it: a SOLID and original roguelite deckbuilding game, with battle so EPIC, and  a ton of replayability with clans, allies, ennemies, bosses, level ups... I'm impressed. The combos that you're not expecting, the damages that you do in one turn sometimes... I'm speechless how this game makes me want to play more of it! An actual game I want to replay again and again. Cause even if the gameplay looks the same, the feeling when playing won't be.Thank you for such an amazing game, and I hope to see a second game like this, or more clans (but I know I'm dreaming, but maybe it'll come true?)
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Why not just burn your money? Yes, it's such bs. No actions are taken against cheaters in leaderboards rather your posts on discussion forum gets removed when you ask about it, no updates since Ice age, no content what's so ever, just rinse and repeat, I play from time to time while waiting for my mates and to get some achievements done, that's all. There's no strategy, no planning goes on at higher Covenant level, nor you can play all clans to climb up the Covenant table, you're given hands by RNG which are pre-determined, doesn't matter how good you play or how well you strategies, it's all on luck and pre-determined hands given.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I already played a bunch of rogue-like deckbuilders alá Slay the Spire, but none facinated me like this one before. Monster Train is funny (well... at least until you have seen everything), but not laughable. The mechanics are really good, especially if you are like me and aim for deck-optimizing (culling starter cards, aiming to build a "perfect" deck). Also the different clans are really different! Especially the champions which come with each clan, but they also have a specific mechanic which they specialize in (or is even unique to them!).So, even if I only scratched the harder modes on this one, I just can recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely take the time to do a review for a game, but I have to for this one.  Monster Train is just so much fun, even when I get defeated.  At first I got a little frustrated, but it's not long before you're giggling at some combination of cards and mechanics you just discovered, that just changed everything!  It's no joke when people say, no two runs are the same.  Even if you have a certain build in mind, it's not always going to play out as you expect.  This keeps it from getting boring.  I also like how I can play casually.  There is no timer making me rush my turn.  I can take my time to formulate a strategy, or pause to watch a Jenna Marbles video.  Just buy the game, You will enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Train is an innovative rogue-lite which interestingly combines deck-building and tower defense in a coherent and engaging manner.  Deep, and often subtle, interactivity provides a fertile terrain for mastering synergies.  The system of added run difficulty after each win makes the initial games forgiving to new players, but slowly ramps up the challenge as players master the challenges it presents.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I love about Slay the Spire but with so much more!The mix of upgrading units, skills, and finding artifacts with just enough randomness always feels interesting but never frustrating. Each clan is unique and trying to find ways to mix and match them is a lot of fun.Easily a must get if you enjoy deck building games!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 198 glorious hours to beat this game. It was addicting, challenging, rewarding and a lot of fun. I loved the variety of clans/champions and their different skill sets though I ended up building a tried and true strategy using the Wurmkin and Umbra duo. After Slay the Spire I swore nothing could compare - until I tried Monster Train. I really enjoyed the format of having increased challenges as I climbed up the Covenant Ranks instead of feeling like I was just replaying the same scenarios.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: When it's time to actually write something for a game review I get a wave of ennui and tend not to do any reviews. Ill keep it simple. Monster Train is a game I thought I wouldn't like, I was wrong. It's easy to start up a play a round or two if you're pressed for time. Low story and time investment makes this easy. I love deckbuilders such as Slay the Spire and Roguebook and the twist that MT provides is easy to pick up. Give it a go and you'll know if you like it within the 2 hour return window that Steam has for games. Enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: This a great tactical deck builder, the mechanics are straight forward, the art style is fun and inviting. I really like the players ability to augment their cards, this combined with some of the "branching paths" you can take with your champion lead to some really interesting builds. Over all a great game with near endless replay-ability.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I feel this is the best card battler on Steam. The factions are all different and unique. Lots of customization and styles. Covenant ranks also add depth and customization via merging of units and additional ways to modify spells. Covenant (w/o modifiers) is quite difficult to progress through however (esp. to get streaks). RNG can greatly affect the game, just like with most "rogue likes". Slay the Spire is also good, but I think this one edges it out personally speaking. I only wish there were even more factions or another expansion. Even at full price, this game is worth it to me. Highly recommend if you like card battling rogue-likes. If you like depth and customization this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun deckbuilding roguelike.  It's like Slay the Spire, except you're the Spire this time.Could definitely use some balancing checks, but I'm optimistic the devs will support that.  It very quickly goes from "nothing gets to attack me" to "I just got one shot" real quick at the final boss or two.  That or you get a super OP Artifact right away that basically ensures you'll win.  But the gameplay is super fun overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I really like how Monster Train doesn't dangle the carrot so far in front of your face that you can't even see it.  Was able to successfully complete a run on my second go.  Am not sure if that'll bode well for my long term enjoyment, but it certainly feels even more fulfilling in the short term than Slay the Spire has at any point for me.  I just don't have the patience for games that feel knowledge-gated to the point you have to bash your head against it and completely pick things apart in order to succeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend Monster Train to anyone that enjoys digital card games!The main thing that sticks out to me is how much influence you as a player have on your experience.  Although it's a rogue-like, you can decide to have the game automatically up the difficulty for you each win, or you can stick with the rank 1 difficulty and have fun unlocking new cards all the same.  Player choice is a core philosophy of this game's design and it shows.Each run is made of two clans and it's a joy to unlock new cards and experiment with mad scientist brews. There's a constant unlocking of new cards and clans which keeps it fresh. There is some RNG, but there are so many countless winnable strategies that the game is more about tailoring choices to your ongoing strategy rather than hoping you find an OP artifact.Compared to Slay the Spire, Monster Train is more forgiving.  If you're looking for a challenge though, the game can be set to up the difficulty with each win.  The higher levels of Covenant difficult require absolute mastery of card knowledge and a little bit of luck.Overall, I'd say Monster Train is a must-play for any card game fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Train

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing entry in the card battler category. Fantastic strategy elements, A+ art, great musical score with so many bangers, choices that matter and so many strategies you can replay for hundreds of hours. I played this on gamepass and did a full unlock of the game, and when it was on sale on steam i bought it again because its just so great. Also, pssst, come here. Closer. _childDocuments_.review: Monster Train is a fresh take on the card build genre that I found pretty addictive in the way you can keep playing, unlocking more cards as you go along. Given the nature of the game, some card combinations are stronger than others, and while the cards themselves are not hard to understand, this game does somewhat suffer from power creep that eventually makes the game state too difficult to progress. I am no stranger to difficult games, but in an attempt to make your cards stronger, your opponents also become stronger gradually.While in that of itself that isn't an issue, it's the fact that your cards are getting oneshot or close to being useless if you don't have time to set them up, In addition, the use of RNG is tons of fun, I love being able to mix and match cards to make better ones, but it's the fact that it generally takes a few runs of getting specific cards that make certain strategies viable. I would love to see more variety than just finding one shot combinations, since that generally becomes the easiest way to deal with enemies but isn't the most fun. Having more "bridge" reactions with cards as opposed to strictly playing Card A to get Effect A would be more interesting to work through and encourage chaining cards creatively. Overall this is still a solid game with a great soundtrack. The final boss from the DLC is absurdly strong though, to the point where it's not fun to play against if you aren't gunning on doing the most amount of damage in one turn.  Overall an 8/10 of trains

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend this game, but it still feels as though it's struggling to find its way to being a great game like Slay the Spire. While StS is polished and smooth, Monster Train feels a bit bumpy. For example, the Relic system feels largely unbalanced - When offered a choice in game, I tend to get either 1) really great relics paired with quite poor relics, or two poor or mediocre relics. I feel like either more choices need to be offered (eg. 3 or 4 choices) or have these relics offered more frequently throughout the run. Since the game is so short as well, I sometimes only pickup 2 to 3 relics throughout the run - I feel there is room for more of an expansion here.I also feel that some of the energy costs for cards just feels bizarre - some really great cards are 0 or 1 while some other cards cost 3. But maybe I'll figure out how good they really are later. That being said, I didn't feel this way playing Slay the Spire - the card cost was clearly associated with its power or importance.I think the Clan dynamic is great and the mixing of these clans allows the game to be more diverse - there's lots to explore with these combinations.Maybe a nit picking thing here, but the top HUD just seems "mobile game" to me - I think it could look a bit more polished.I haven't encountered any game breaking bugs or glitches yet. Everything is smooth and looks great otherwise.Overall, as I said, I'd recommend it. I think MT is a game that is trying hard to emulate Slay the Spire, but falls short in several ways. I can't shake the feeling that MT is, for lack of a better way of saying it, much more aggressive having the player die / lose runs. In StS, I lost because I didn't have the right cards or relics unlocked or made a bad choice - unlocking better cards and unlocking better relics made the climb not just easier, but smoother - each run felt more about skill and how to use the cards in specific situations. I don't feel that quality is present in MT - it feels more like its trying to brute force its way. That being said, I feel the potential for MT to improve is there. Judging from what I've seen from the developers, I think they can.I hope there are more updates to come to smooth out the many train rides I feel I'm going to be taking in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much a must have if you like card-based games and/or rogue-likes.You will find the familiar "creature combat" concept that is at the core of smost TCGs, but with a unique spin that qualifies as truly original. I will not explain those differences, but just know that while the initial games may feel strange, once you are used to it, it becomes extremely enjoyable and strategic.Being a rogue-like (also called "deckbuilder" for card games), the game has some randomness and it is possible to get the jackpot dream deck sometimes, or to end up in an unwinnable situation other times, but this is par for the course in this genre. In my experience, though, terrible runs in which you have no chance of winning almost never happen. The game offers many options to alleviate the damages of RNG on your deck, and while there are cases in which defeat is unavoidable, it is rare enough to not feel too bad, and that is the mark of a well balanced deckbuilder.I also think that this game has the perfect duration of roughly an hour for a run, which is a good balance between depth and not dragging on : not too long, not too short.One thing you should be aware of, though, is that the game is very hard. But let's be honest : if you do not like the idea of a game where you can not win 100% of the time, you shouldn't care about this genre in the first place. Deckbuilders are all about trying to mitigate RNG as much as possible, but it's also impossible to get rid of it. So sometimes, you just get screwed.That's a common trait of most rogue-likes, and you probably were aware of it. Most of the negative reviews are indirect consequences of "salt" from those times RNG was a b****, as the game is unapologetic about it : it is hard, it knows it, it assumes it. Fully.But on the other hand, this difficulty isn't mandatory : the creators had the nice idea of having 25 (!) difficulty levels, called "covenants". So you can definitely find the difficulty that suits you.  Beginners can stick to covenant 1 for as long as they want, until they feel ready for harder stuff. And one you start to understand the game, covenant 1 isn't that hard at all.Heck, you can even go back to it for a cheap revenge against a loss in an higher difficulty. The option is always there.And when you want that challenge, you definitely are going to get it. Not only will the difficulty get relentless as the covenant increases, but the game also includes a lot of secondary objectives besides just winning standard runs (score, achievements, "mastering" the cards...)Add on top of that that this game is much cheaper than an actual TCG (cards are unlocked through progression. no micro-transactions), and you get an amazing game that I really, really recommend. Hundreds of hours of fun and strategy are waiting for you in this cheap, but brilliantly made package!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version - Slay The Spire + a bit of tower defense. It's fantastic. 10/10.Longer Version - It has the challenge for those looking for it, much like ascension mode from STS.
