_childDocuments_.review: Yet another amazing entry in The Room franchise.......... that is sadly let down by its short run time.To preface this review, I would definitely recommend you to buy the other Room games, as they are fantastic, but mostly for the story, as the story of the game somewhat concludes in this game, which I found very interesting.GRAPHICSGraphics in this game are very well done and the textures are very realistic. Special effects and ambient occlusion are also added for an added bonus to a PC that has extremely good graphics. For me, my settings were set at medium, but the game still looked absolutely fantastic. From location to location, the lighting in each area varied and were very unique.2/2Music/Sound EffectsAs always, the central theme song of the game brings you back, the moment you start the game. However, other than that, there isn't much in terms of music. Though, that theme song really is good. Anyways, sound effects are absolutely brilliant and extremely satisfying. From opening boxes, locks, and hearing voices from the Null Void, everything is done very well.1.5/2Storyline/BugsIn this game, the storyline actually comes to a conclusion for any fans of the series. The series's storyline is very cryptic, which is why I would definitely recommend you to play the other great games, before this one. If not for the short runtime of the game, the storyline would have been great, but it seemed like it reached its conclusion rather quickly. No bugs were found in my playthrough.1.5/2PacingPacing is done well, but the game feels like it speeds up by the last two chapters of the game. To be frank, the last two chapters and somewhat, the first chapter, should not be counted as chapters. The first chapter introduces you to the game, storyline, tutorials, and all which is a standard affair for the room games. The 2nd, 3rd, and 4th chapter are full chapters and where the game fully shines with all of its unique puzzles. Each of those rooms took me about an hour to complete. And finally, the last two chapters seem like cop-out chapters in which its basically a walking simulator with a few "light" and I mean "light" puzzles in the mix. If the game stuck to its pacing, like the first half of the game, it would definitely be worth its price, but sadly the last two chapters fail to impress. Although, the environments are very cool.1/2Gameplay/LengthGameplay is absolutely fantastic and the puzzles truly shine as unique game mechanics. I especially liked how they introduced all the mechanics in the previous games for each level, and even introduce a new one, in the 4th chapter. This game was meant for VR and I mean it. All of the interactions in the game feel absolutely swell and truly make you feel like you are truly solving the Rube-Goldberg of puzzles. Length is my main complaint for the game. For then price, I paid a total of 30 dollars for a game that lasted me just under 3 and a half hours. This game should have been at least 6 hours at the least for a standard game. But because this game is the first "true" VR game for the developers, I will give them a slight pass. I just wish the game was longer, as the other Room games are cheaper, around 4-7 dollars, and last around 5-6 hours. Anyways, sorry for my little rant, but that's my main complaint for the game, along with some of the puzzles being slightly tedious, and that's a rarity.1/2FINAL VERDICTFor any VR owners that love puzzle games. Get this. For any VR owners that love The Room franchise and want to see how the story concludes. GET THIS NOW. I give this game a 7/10 (GOOD) and must say that it's a must have for puzzle fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Caution: Overwhelming VR experience!I am big fan of the The Room series. Having played all the (smart phone) games, I am always craving for more escape room games that have the intensity of this series. After the release of The Room 3, no more follow-up was added to the series and I reckoned the developers quit making the series all together. Then, this new stand-alone games was released, supporting full and only VR.For fans of the series and for escape rooms in general, this VR edition of The Room is a must-play. All puzzles you might've done swiping your smart phone in the past, you can now do in VR. The puzzle interaction is truly superb and for a technique that is relatively new, The Room VR explores the boundaries of possibilities with VR with this epic puzzle game.I sincerely hope more developers will explore the possibilities of VR further. One thing is for certain. Escape rooms are a superb addition to the VR genre.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best VR title I have played. In fact, I would say it is in contention for the best game I've ever played. The graphics are incredible, and the puzzles have just the right amount of challenge. The scenes are intricately detailed (think, you can angle your head to see outside a window, and the world beyond is rendered completely). They create a sense of place and atmosphere, along with the music, that transports you into the world of The Room. The VR is used in creative ways as well, from interesting tools to playing with scale. The game was a good length for the price. I can't wait for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: talking about pricing for games always seems tricky.on one hand, as a consumer, i want prices to be low most of the time, and i usually expect that the higher the price of a game the longer and better it will be.on the other hand, as a creator, creating for VR is usually a task that won't yield much return, as playerbases remain small, and building a game like this in vr is also probably pretty expensive.so the price tag: 30 dollars for about 2-3 hours of gameplay. (i technically got it on sale for 20 dollars) i can't help but feel that this is a little expensive for what you get. and what you get isn't bad. it's the usual cleverness and spooky vibes of the room series, with engaging puzzles that are never too hard or too simple. the graphics and style of the game are pretty great too, and the hint system is always subtle yet helpful. it's a polished game for VR, and while it is short most entries of the room series never were that long anyways.i like what the game is, it's really enjoyable, but I'm not sure it's 20-30 dollars enjoyable. if you have spare cash go for it, especially if you are familiar with the room series already.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like "The Room" and you like VR, you'll like The Room VR. It takes what works from the other games and puts you in the situations. VISUALS: The textures aren't the highest quality that I noticed, but they are good enough to let you escape into the world and feel like you're interacting with objects. LENGTH: The game is a little short for my liking, but all of the ROOM games kind of have their length on the shorter side (aside from 3) Only took me about 3 hours to play through the whole game (less if you consider I started, had some issues with my computer, so I restarted the game when all issues were fixed). There are roughly 3 different levels. I hardly count the "detective" office as a full room, and the ending bit is kind of on rails and doesn't have much to figure out. PUZZLES: Some puzzles are great, some are your typical 'take item A to slot A, insert, get Item B, find where slot B is' while others have you going in and out of multiple areas and using your brainOverall, I had a great time with it even though it was short.

Fireproof Games always delivers smooth highly optimized 3D Room games... and it amazed me how they delivered such high details on the Ipad.i've only learned of the Room VR two weeks ago and was hyped the moment i read it. just like the devs i've always felt that if ONE game was ready for VR it was The Room. And wow...they did it! i'm glad Fireproof dared to take the step, and boy ...how they did it! The Room VR really gets the original Vibes back and More... its little bit more creepy but i like that. The sound is spot on (i like the london 1800's setting!! very much, i hope sequels stay in this Era!)Graphics are detailed, just as on the mobile versions... smooth, lots of details. Tip, dive into the settings menu, if your system can take it enable all high settings like volumetric lighting, ambient occlusion.Controls are alternating from great to ... a bit ackward.... i think in some puzzles the controls could be more precise and intuitive (i have index controls, and would like to you use full finger controls like grabbing with index and thumb). But this is not gonna spoil the fun. The Room VR is another Great Title in the VR realm, i'm happy they switched to VR and hope ther e is more, way more to come from Fireproof on VR. Thank you Fireproof for delivering a great game! i'm having a blast playing it!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows that the concept of the Room games is as a good fit for VR as I imagined it to be. I enjoyed the "sizing" and "stars" puzzles in particular, think they really work well in VR.The environments are interesting enough that I would have loved a more free type of teleportation to look around and be much more immersed  - you are limited to a very few fixed spots. Perhaps just marking these with a slightly different color or circle size when teleporting would have been enough to indicate their importance to the puzzles.Here is to hoping the devs can find a way to efficiently design their games for both flatscreen and a VR edition, and release many more VR editions of their games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: An instant classic. This game surpasses the previous Room games so if you have even a passing interest in the genre it's a must play. The developers have outdone themselves with the multiple levels of detailed environments richly decorated with period artwork. The puzzles are well crafted and range from being fairly easy to solve to moderate head scratchers so you don't need to be a genius. The hints are unnecessary. The ending is very satisfying. The length of the game is just right. Hope the devs keep on making more VR games like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting puzzle game that offers a decent single player escape room experience. However the puzzles were easy and took only 3.2 hrs to complete. VR games tend to be more expensive but I got this on sale which means its £5 per hour, with no replayability. I feel 6 - 10 hours would have been better.The visuals were nice but there are better looking VR games available with more interesting interactions and longer play time. The game only allows for teleportation and not smooth movement. If you are looking for something more puzzling I'd suggest going to a real escape room.Visuals 6/10Puzzles 5/10Entertainment 5/10 Cost per hour 1/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great VR puzzle game. With thought through rooms and a soundtrack to match, it creates a deep immersion experience. It makes great use of mechanics available with today's VR equipment. The puzzles are a good mix ranging from fairly obvious to starting to doubt your own intellect.The problem? It's short. I hope they make more of these.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE MAKE MOOOOAR OF THIS!NERDGASM FTW!On a more professional note:I have been a fan of Room series on my mobile; I've played them twice with some years inbetween. I like the hidden in the details approach to these puzzles and the quality of the work. This game sets the bar to another level, I really liked the perception of actually fiddling a lever in different angles with my hand rather than on-screen touches or mouse movements.It is like picking a lock with an actual tool and hand movements rather than spamming WSAD at needed times if you get my drift :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was actually the first game I played when I got my Index.  I feel like it was a great introduction to VR with its teleport movement system.  The puzzles were varied and challenging.  If you have ever played one of the phone app versions of The Room and liked it, then this will be right up your alley too.  Overall, I would recommend for anyone who is a fan of VR puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: YES!Thanks YOU Fireproof games!I have been a massive fan of The Rooms series for years and ever since I got VR I always dreamt of The Room in VR.Now I finally have it lemme tell you what I think!It runs like a dream at least on my PC with everything enabled/maxed, I do get a little motion sick but that's just VR that always happens to me.The immersion is unreal, it's very atmospheric and it just feels great. Especially when played standing but it's still incredible in seated mode and definitely worth playing.The story is brilliant as always, but it is much much creepier in VR and I thought the previous game was creepy lolThe puzzles (so far) haven't been obvious, they're fun to figure out and even in VR the game still feels familiar.TL:DR  Don't sit and wonder whether or not to get this game. Just get it and think about it later, you won't regret it.Update:Now I have finished the game. It is not a long game but that in no way makes this a bad game. It's incredible. Everything I've said up until now is still true and the story is pretty awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The entire Room series delivers. Every game in the series is fantastic: high quality visuals AND puzzles, with a wonderfully creepy atmosphere. "The Room VR: A Dark Matter" takes The Room series into even an deeper level of immersion, with an intuitive user interface and navigation free of motion discomfort issues. I don't know of a single other game series that I anticipate the next game more than The Room series. I recommend for anyone that enjoys puzzles, escape rooms, and point-and-click adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: In line with the flat screen games that came before - The Room VR is one of the best puzzle games around.  In this case just wrapped up in a super sharp AAA graphic blanket :)  The atmosphere is amazingly rich with great sound work and just the right tone of Lovecraftian horror without going for outright jump scares throughout.  Its a series where you really should play them all but its not essential to get the gyst of the storyline,  Theres no reason not to get it, unless you specifically hate head-scratching puzzle games (but even then there's a very generous hint system).  Buy it and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first 3 games. Held off on this because didn't have a VR set until recently. Played on Quest 2. Loved it. I wish it was longer and more complex as was done with The Room 3, but I'm sure implementing it all into VR took enough work as it is. Would've been fun if the VR aspect was used a bit more like forcing you to bend down and look under a table and such. All in all if you're a Room fan or VR fan, this game will not disappoint. Highly Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed all the puzzles needed to solve the case. I especially enjoyed the journey through multiple locations. As this is my first VR experience I found myself a little scared and shocked during much game-play. Another positive aspect of this game is the notes or hints feature. The hints feature works just well enough to be a good guide while letting you continue solving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned this is a short game. Took me 5 hours to beat without rushing. Smarter people would probably take less. I loved it though and I would buy it again if they came out with another story. The game play is in three major parts with unique puzzles for each part. The controls are not difficult. I did not get dizzy except at one small part where a door opened in front of me. I will say that the ending felt a bit rushed and unexplained but maybe this was intentional if they are to make a fallow up game which I hope they do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Right up my alley and a good way for me to get back into VR. To be honest, VR can be a bit anxiety inducing. I'm not often face to face with things trying to attack me, so it was nice to find a game where I could take a breather from that. A casual puzzle solving romp in some neat environments was just what I needed. Sure, some of the environments are a bit spooky, but it's helped by the fact that I realized nothing was going to get me. I never played the original, but I think it was a good use of VR. It's the closest thing I can think to a very legit VR escape room. A+ I'll play more if/when it's available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric feel to the puzzle / mystery game. Movement within a chapter scene (6 achievement levels)  by point to point (pre-defined) locations adjacent to clues / artefacts / puzzles. Visual graphics / sounds for puzzles are excellent with interesting "hidden" visual transitions using lens / view glasses. Some neat "scale shifting" within certain puzzles using superbly done "crystal portals" which work extremely well in VR. Absorbing & great fun .....
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I got me an old discarded Rift from a colleague. Then I noticed that The Room had a VR installment, so I didn't hesitate and immediately dove into it.Man, is it everything I expected. A baffling experience with EXTREME attention to audiovisual details. The sound design and graphics details are simply out of this world. Amazing.Be sure to look around, and duck and bend around corners etc., because they put LOTS of nice little surprises in many places you may not immediately look. Little notes of paper with fun details, books under desks etc.. So much to explore, if you just take the time.It's an exiting adventure (not horror/jumpscare exciting, just alice in wonderland exciting), full of well-balanced puzzles, amazing twists and turns, a great story and some awesome map design, beautiful sound and music. It's simply hitting all my spots. They really did themselves justice.Is there nothing to complain about? Sure... They could have done more puzzling things with the hand interactions, e.g. object manipulations, gestures, I don't know, something more than just gripping things. And the movement system, with the jarring teleport and swiveling, feels a bit clunky and outdated and takes away some of the otherwise awesome immersion. And puzzles are always a question of taste, but they feel a little bit on the easy side until now. But those are just small things and in no way should dissuade you from diving into this sensory overload of VR puzzle goodness and pure audiovisual bliss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Having played all of the Room games on iOS, I was hoping that I would find this game as polished and fun. It is (was) and then some. Beautiful graphics, challenging yet not impossible puzzles, great story-line. I loved it. A bit short (I milked it for 4 hours), so I am hoping that additional Room games will be coming. A definite must have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the earlier games in the series. Unfortunately, this game had some issues that prevented me from enjoying it.For one, I was disappointed that you can't walk around rooms and you're stuck to pre-set locations. That's more than a little immersion breaking.The other big issue is how turning the camera works. You move the right stick, the screen fades to black, then it fades back in. I know it's supposed to prevent motion sickness, but for me, it actually CAUSED it. I was incredibly annoyed to find there wasn't an option to move it smoothly and I was just stuck with that fade. That was the last straw for me and I got a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. And WOW what a great game and what a journey. The Room VR: A Dark Matter is such an incredibly well made game that I could not stop playing at all. I was gripped by the game right from the start and was only more impressed the further I got into the game. There has really been a sense of detail both in the puzzles while also for the surroundings.I can only highly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I feel as though The Room was not ported to VR very well. However, this is not to say that it doesn't still look quite visually pleasing and definitely have its moments. I disliked how many of the puzzles just kinda felt like a fetch-quest for a specific piece, move it from point A to point B. I get that VR can be limiting, but I had hoped for more. 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the better puzzle room experiences with 4 (main) puzzle rooms of increasing complexity. Each room introduces a new mechanic, increasing complexity and scale. Each of the larger puzzles are generally quite straightforward, but it is interesting to see how all the small pieces fit together. It can sometimes be quite annoying if you fail to notice a small rope, dial or lever that is crucial to solving the next step, but thankfully a hint system is there to help you out if you're really stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a puzzel game this is for you. From the graphics you would think this is a scary game but it isn't. Only once in whole game did I jump and that's when a door flew open I didn't expect. They do provide you with a hint option, which I suggest using. Sometimes things aren't as obvious as you would think.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmospheric puzzle game, with 2 small flaws:1) Too short for it's price, I'd suggest getting it on sale2) A few interactive objects blend in too well, making it quite unclear that they're actually part of a puzzle (game has optional hint system you can access anytime, which helps).But all in all I quite enjoyed my time spent playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since playing the very first "The Room" game when it first came out, I have been a big fan of the series. Fireproof Games keep knocking it out of the park with these games! The "The Room" franchise focus on puzzle mechanics, and have traditionally done these very well, and in interesting ways. The gameplay experience on mobile devices with touch screen have been stellar, and one of the very few high quality, story and puzzle focused games you can play on mobile. I mention the past games as a reference to the challenge of moving a game concept from one interactive medium to another, in this case a display with touch or mouse controls and a curated array of camera angles in game, to giving the player complete control over the camera and two motion controls. It is a different system entirely, yet the Fireproof team have done a great job of translating the concepts and gameplay of the series over to virtual reality. This new virtual reality title "The Room VR: A Dark Matter" has a lot of highlights, and it feels like a genuine "The Room" game. The puzzles are great fun to solve, and when you struggle with that, the clues are helpful without being too revealing. The graphics are very good, a series staple in fact. They have also implemented a few neat physics mechanics. Motion controller implementation is good and modern. Although control of the camera is in the players hand, you are not fully allowed to move everywhere. The game features a teleport system to the different places where the puzzles are. This is not really a bad thing, as this keeps you informed of all the possible places to be, avoids you getting lost, and keeps you focused on solving the puzzles. In that regard it is a valid gameplay decision. The different in game locations are of good detail and variation. In the end the biggest weakness with this game is that I would have liked it to last even longer. The puzzles are great, and I really would have appreciated more of them. I think Fireproof Games first entry in virtual reality is terrific, and I hope they consider making more!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled onto the room series of games a while ago and really like them as a bit of relaxed puzzle solving, this in VR is a fairly immersivive. Coming from Alyx as my last real VR game at first I felt fairly constrained, but after a bit once you get used to it being similar to the other games but in VR you get more used to just being able to jump between specific points. All in all, lovely little game, Some really nice immersive views and scenes and some interesting mechanics. Easy to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First off: I love escape rooms IRL.  This has lead me down the path of The Room series and they've all been excellent entries.  I was recommended this game on Steam (thanks Steam) and I was stoked to find out The Room had a VR game!This game has all the trappings of a game from The Room series but it works so darn well in VR.  Everything feels very tactile and I love the sense of scale of some parts.  I will happily continue to play The Room in VR because Fireproof Games are just so damn good at what they do.  Pick it up for any fans of The Room series, puzzles or if you have a VR headset and are looking for something that'll kill a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The visual fidelity and mechanical detail of the phone games always struck me as out of place. Players squint at a little screen and try to poke the right spot to signal turning a knob or pulling a handle. The games had a low-fidelity interface for a high-fidelity world. Now along comes VR, and it's such a perfect interface for the world Fireproof already built that it's hard to believe development didn't happen the other way around: first the VR game, then the phone games. It's as if the developers designed the game for virtual reality but had to settle for mobile and wait 8 years for the technology to mature. Now that VR is here, this game is an great experience.Fireproof did well utilizing the unique aspects of VR. Interacting with objects requires acting out the desired motion with the controller. Interactive components are not always planted in front of the player, head movement is required to explore the world. Information is sometimes hidden in the 3D space in satisfying ways, although I would have liked to see more of that. Only one or two puzzles utilized the unique depth perception available in VR, I hope the developers build on that in subsequent games. There was one classic parallax/perspective puzzle, and it was actually made worse by VR; stereoscopic depth perception interferes with the illusion.There are a handful of problems with the VR implementation:- The player grips objects to interact with them, but lens toggle is bound to trackpad click by default (Valve Index). When gripping, it is natural to press with the thumb as well; that's what opposable thumbs are for after all. I found myself constantly toggling the lens by mistake when gripping objects. Thumbstick click would be a better binding, I think.- When teleporting, the game moves the player to the destination rather than the play area. As a result, the center of the play area tends to drift away from the spot the game intends the player to stand on. I had to reset my view four or five times over the course of my playthrough.I was surprised to discover that being miniature for certain puzzles was a little nauseating. Not sure why. I rarely have discomfort in VR.Overall great game. Despite being $30 and only taking a few hours, I would buy this again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting and varied puzzles to solve, nice implementation of the hint system which I had to use in a few spots, though I wish the game was longer. The way you can fiddle around with some of the game objects is very satisfying (the bottle lids opening and closing, extremely nice), object giving controller vibration feedback to guide your hand to the correct spot etc.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the rest of The Room series, this is very much in the same vein. All atmosphere and puzzles and creepy occultism, but now in VR. The VR is well implemented, but being released just a couple days after Alyx, well... it suffers in comparison as far as a VR experience goes. You teleport between the stations of different puzzles and can't move anywhere else. The immersion otherwise is great and it really is the ultimate Room game. But, it's about 3 hours and you have to decide if that's worth $30 for you. I love the games and wanted to support the developers so I can see more of these games, so it was worth it to me. If it's not worth $30 to you, well... it'll go on sale eventually and when it gets to the price you think it's worth, I suggest you buy it because it is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: LOVED this. Absolutely loved it. Always loved the games for being what they are but love the developers more for being able to make what they're able to make. Whatever puzzles are in the game, the puzzle of being able to bring them to life is a thousand times the challenge and they seem to do it with such ease. These types of games are perfect for the VR medium and I hope to see more like it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the kind of experience that I purchased a VR headset for. While it's certainly a short experience, the environments, the exploration, and the hands-on puzzle solving made this game stand out as one of the best VR experiences I've had so far. I really appreciated that this game maintains a spooky/creepy vibe throughout, but never delves into being a horror game with any sort of jump scares.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game. Definitely worthy of 'The Room' series. There's a few puzzle points that are a bit obtuse, but part of that could be continuous puzzle solving over the course of a few hours (all in one go for completing the game). But the hint mechanism is pretty solid if you need it.Would recommend others to play it, nothing to put people off.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.user: K n e d l í k
_childDocuments_.review: The Room is undoubtedly one of the best puzzle game series I've ever played. Although the VR version is relatively short for its price—I completed it in under 4 hours without rushing—it still managed to deliver a satisfying experience.The atmosphere of the game is truly captivating, giving me goosebumps at times, particularly during the climactic ending, which was exceptionally well-executed and enjoyable.Things I liked about the game:- Immersive atmosphere- Engaging puzzles that kept me intrigued- Goosebump-inducing moments, especially towards the endThings I didn't like about the game:- Short playtime for the price- Felt like it could have offered more contentStory: 7/10Visuals: 9/10Audio: 9/10Originality: 9/10Difficulty: 8/10Replayability: 7/10Loot: 2/10Overall, The Room VR offers a captivating puzzle experience that, despite its brevity, is still worth the time for fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Good VR controls (including what should be, but amazingly isn't in a lot of games, recentering views and option to sit or stand). The atmosphere and graphics are excellent, VR is perfect for this genre  - the developers have spent a long time creating a very immersive feeling and a great story line. The puzzles are not impossible but hard enough to keep you thinking throughout the game - importantly there are very few puzzles that have you scratching your head thinking that's just stupid. I was impressed by the depth of the game and certainly can't complain about the length of time to complete. The best praise I can give it is that I'd have no hesitation buying any sequel, fingers crossed there will be one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just wow. I didn't know how well the puzzle elements would transfer over to VR, but Fireproof does this brilliantly. They wrap up the story excellently, and the environments are the right amount of expansive. The visual storytelling is top notch. Recommend all of these games, play this one last as it builds on the rest of the games' environments and stories.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. I had zero issues with controls, tracking, or view obstruction. Once again, These guys have raised the bar for their game series! I highly recommend anyone that enjoys puzzle games (and a VR headset) pick this up and play through it. There are a few callouts to previous games (no spoilers though!) that I really enjoyed, and speaking of that go try their mobile games as well!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended – 7/10As a fan of the previous The Room games, I had to pick this one up once I got a VR setup.  Overall, the game has much of the same look and feel as the original games, however, the puzzles are not as intricate.  This might be on purpose as the VR controls were not as precise as I was used to on the prior Room games, and therefore the puzzles had to be limited.  Playing this game in VR definitely gives a different perspective and the game does a good job with the atmosphere.  Puzzles aren’t terribly difficult and the only issue I had was the VR interaction mechanic when pulling ropes.  Overall, I’d recommend this game to any Room or puzzle fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was the first game of the franchise that I've tried, and frankly didn't think that the style of play would suit me but other reviews convinced me to give this a try.  However, I found this game to be absolutely stellar and a pleasant break from the action oriented games I normally enjoy.  Fantastic graphics, intriguing puzzles, and excellent VR mechanics.  Experienced on a Pimax 8KX w/2080TI.   Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What a masterpiece! I loved all the games of the series, but VR is the best way to have the experience! For those who have played at least 1 of the other Room games, you know what to expect. The interactivity though of the VR is making the game so alive. Everything worked flawlessly, The graphics/sound is awesome, the riddles very logical and satisfying and the scenario interesting. I highly reccomend to anyone with a VR set
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've always said that this series would do well as a VR game, and it does.There's a bit less emphasis on individual puzzle boxes in this one, and more on entire rooms containing different things to interact with (though there still are several smaller boxes to solve as well).The story is similar to the other games (what little there is of it); you're a regular person thrust into a wild ride through mad worlds, seeking to ultimately return back home.  Some of the same mystical themes as the previous games return in this one, but it's reasonably self-contained and you don't need to have played the previous ones to understand and enjoy this one.It does feel a little bit shorter than the other games, though, which is the only downside.  But it's a great experience being immersed in the puzzle rooms this time around.The game does have teleport motion only, which might put off some people -- but then the 2D games were also teleport only, so this is just this series' style rather than a VR limitation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the phone games, this is a nice treat in VR. You can finish it in about 3 hours and its got great atmosphere. The puzzles are pretty interesting overall, but nothing too hard that stumps you for too long. The teleportation nodes take a little getting used to, but I'm hoping the next game allows for some more freedom in exploring the environments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice VR escape room game, the price is a bit much for 3 hours, luckily I got it on sale, but the quality is very high. Didn't really have that many issues with puzzles except with some objects not being obvious that you could interact with, ex. (Inside the organ or the rope inside the church box. Still, was a blast to play, hope to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: There are two types of people, those who love The Room series, and those who haven't played it yet. Not much to say besides I will sell my house to keep Fireproof Studios in business because they are masters Craftsmen (get it?) of these games. When The Room 1 came out it masterfully turned the mobile experience into an immersive interactive journey, and with A Dark Matter they have surpassed their former efforts ten fold.Funnily enough I didn't find the play time short at all, may be because I got stuck in one particular part of the game. The puzzles are not as challenging as those in the previous The Room games but it is still one hell of an amazing experience.Buy it, play it, love it. What are you waiting for?
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A lot like doing an escape room, but with a surreal twist. It's in line with the rest of "The Room" series, getting increasingly weird and creepy. Definitely overpriced for the length of the game but considering how cheap we got the previous games I guess it evens out. The VR worked well and felt immersive, not just a gimmick converted from a 2D display.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from an escape room enthusiast, I LOVED this game! Everything you need to figure out the various solutions and puzzles are present for you to find with varying degrees of difficulty, which makes it awesome that you can turn off hints in the options. I only ever used a single hint and it turned out the only thing I was missing was the fact I hadn't paid attention to the shape of an object I had in my inventory. Just a moment of not paying attention. The room(s) themselves are beautifully modeled and crafted to encourage exploration and attention to detail from the player. would definite recommend to any escape room lovers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The ONLY negative thing about this game is the fact that it is so short! Every puzzle is interesting and all interactions are well mapped and leaves you without any type of cybersickness. 10/10 Look forward to more VR The Room adventures in the future- I would even be willing to pay more for a longer one ♥ Highly recommended to anyone that enjoys puzzle games, and especially if you enjoy their previous series of puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What a great example of where VR is heading. It does a great job of interacting with the objects around you and making you actually feel you are in the room. Pulling ropes on a pulley was such a cool experience that can only be understood once played. I really hope the next one comes out sooner rather than later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this has such great reviews. The 'puzzles' are not that difficult at all. Mostly they involve  matching one item up with a tool or piece of equipment and are hardly mentally challenging, which is really disappointing. I also imagine it would help to have played the other games as I had no idea what was actually happening or why I should particularly care beyond needing to complete puzzles. Most of the puzzles don't make sense, especially the Egyptian one. Why so much of the same puzzle was spread out over so many different and unrelated artefacts was never explained, or at least I missed it if it was.The VR is good, very good in fact, and the visuals in VR are impressive. Which is why the actual gameplay being so disappointing is a massive let down for the game overall. It all sort of feels like the designers had a drawing board of ideas and just said yes to everything with no thought as to how it should all go together. I completed the game in about 3 hours, which includes stopping to get a cup of tea and some biscuits. For £10, it was fine but I wouldn't buy at full price. If I had my time again I wouldn't have even bought it at the price I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale. Played it and was hooked. I couldn't put it down for hours. My wife, a friend, and I worked together to finish the game. I ended up completing it a few hours later. I loved the VR puzzle experience and look forward to more! Manipulating the features in the game with VR made the "escape room" style experience so immersive. Keep these coming, Fireproof!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make a VR puzzle game. Having played all the other Room games (I still have not completed 3 - got stuck and put it on the back burner), this was a pretty familiar formula - and that is a good thing! The Room's puzzles have always been well thought out and just complex enough. I did find this one to be a touch easier. Maybe it was actually being in the environment vs just playing on a flat screen. The graphics are top notch, sound is perfect, and overall quality is solid. If I had to come up with one minus, it would be the price. It took me 3 1/2 to complete. At full price, that is nearly $10 an hour. Grab it on sale and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not already a fan, I strongly suggest the mobile games as well (They aren't necessary, there's no narrative connection, but they're just fantastic and the best games of the genre I've ever played). The Room is a series of "escape room puzzles", played in a mix of occult, mind-bending, other-worldly spaces, combining objects that you twist and turn, as you manipulate mechanical and magical items together to progress gradually towards an unknown destination.This game captures all the spooky atmosphere of the mobile games, and brings them to life size, almost tangible presence.The puzzles are what you'd expect - having the opportunity to fiddle and twist the objects in mind-bending virtual space. Everything overall is just a bit more solid, a lot scarier. Form the moment the familiar theme music starts playing you know you're in The Room; when you put on the lenses, you know this is not like any Room game you've played before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: An immersive and atmospheric puzzle game for VR.As VR controls go, it could probably be a desktop game, but the the immersion kept me playing.Most of the puzzles felt good, plenty of clues around to help out otherwise the tips are good at helping out.I would mainly recommend the game for puzzle game fans with access to a VR headset, but I also think it can be a good game to show off VR in a relaxed manner.NOTE: I did have some issues using my left hand on my Oculus Rift (CV1)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the previous installments of The Room very much and the VR sequel did not disappoint me. The graphics is beautiful and very detailed and nicely conveys the creepy atmosphere. The puzzles are logical and not too hard, I was never stuck for long. Definitely recommended.(Played on an Acer WMR set with only a couple of small glitches in the beginning.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully done! The Room VR does a fantastic job making you feel like you're in the game. The environment is nicely crafted with spectacular lighting and crisp, detailed textures. The soundtrack perfectly fits to give the entire ordeal an eerily haunting, spine tingling feel. There are no jumpscares, but the immersion is more than enough to make the hair on the back of your neck stand up. The puzzles are plentiful and solvable, but range from very easy to quite difficult, but doable if you look for the clues. The storyline is intriguing, entertaining, and unfolds very nicely. My only complaint is that it was over too soon. I'm hoping for a sequel as I love The Room games. A MUST HAVE FOR VR!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game!It's got great visuals, intriguing and varied puzzles and a really peculiar atmosphere. There were some times where I got a little stuck because of affordance issues (not for that long though) and the game isn't that long to complete, but I'd rather have 4 hours of well crafted puzzles and environments instead of 15 hours of obscure riddles and copy-pasted environments. As a VR game it's a bit safe-ish (teleport locomotion, no real physics interactions -this is no boneworks- ) but that's totally fine! It makes a great entry point for those new to VR and stays enjoyable for even more seasoned players.Overall, I really loved the experience and definitely hope that we'll see more 'cases' as either DLC or full games!Also, to the devs, play the credits at the end! don't hide them in the menu, be proud of what you made!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of previous The Room titles, I was predisposed to like the VR foray, so I'm glad I did.The puzzles were not as intricate as some previous titles, but still flowed nicely, and in some cases made good use of VR 'space'. The detail and atmosphere of the environments are good, maintaining a slight sense of menace without resorting to jump scares. Some excellent use of sound and light in some areas.I suffered from the same thing I did in previous titles - it was obvious what the puzzle needed but I couldn't see how - usually because I hadn't spotted a movable component. Pixel hunting by waving your hands around is somehow more satisfying than scanning back and forth with a mouse, and the game occasionally gives you rumble feedback where its helpful.3 hours (ish) isn't a bad length for a puzzle game, and the story telling was okay - giving enough plot to hang the puzzles on is all I ask from these sort of titles and it did that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Best puzzle/escape room VR experience by far! It blows every other one out of the water in my opinion, and I have tried them all. Creative, engaging, and challenging puzzles, amazing environments and storyline, and extremely immersive. I was able to beat the game in about 3 hours without hints (although there were 2 moments where I almost took the hint) and I have to say the game was stellar in every aspect. 10/10 If you like to solve puzzles and have a VR setup "The Room VR: A Dark Matter" is a MUST have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's an experience!!Good job Fireproof Games, you have made an outstanding job!!The game is basically The Room VR. Same as the previous versions of the game, it's about solving some cool puzzles with a mysterious story. The differences are that the puzzles are a little bit more challenging, and the VR makes every thing a little complicated. Due to that you must move your head to look into the details. "I've been stuck alot :P"I borrowed my friend's VR for the first time to play this game and I actually think I'm gonna buy the VR for next projects of this amazing game! Looking forward for your next projects <3 !
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: amazing experience and well worth the money!! Played this in a mix with Alyx and it stood next to it nicely. Graphics, pacing, story and PUZZLES are all Top Notch. My playtime is between 2 people, so roughly 6hrs for each of us. I know, we are perhaps not the sharpest and took our time haha I will certainly buy their next VR game without even looking what it is. This dev deserves applause!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Bare-minimum effort to make it immersive and very mediocre puzzles when compared to the previous games, especially the recent ones. As a first VR entry in The Room series, it is ok... ish. Hard to recommend at full price to the average player, even to die-hard fans. If solving puzzles sounds awesome to you and you don't have much experience with such games - I think you will have a blast. But for anyone with experience, especially the previous The Room games and similar, better wait till it drops to 50% off or lower. It's a letdown when compared to previous game in the series (Old Sins), even when compared to the one before.I'm a fan from pretty much the start of the series with The Room (1) for iOS and Android, this is technically The Room 5 as it continues the story from the previous 4 (mobile) games. So far, each next instalment has built on top of the previous. Not only in terms of story progression, but also in how intricate and complex the puzzles are. It felt like a nice progression in difficulty so we don't get bored. Regrettably, to those familiar with the series as a whole, this is more like a The Room (1) experience - it is short even by The Room standards and no complex and memorable puzzles. I finished it in less than 3h and that included breaks where I just paused the game, so probably took less than 2.5h. On top of that, the puzzles are even easier than the first game, but not by much. At no point was I stuck for more than a minute and most often it was because it wasn't clear with what I can interact it and with what not so I was just circling around looking for things to open or pick-up. Most puzzles are pretty obvious as they take ridiculously few actions to resolve, especially when compared to The Room 4 (Old Sins).In terms of gameplay - you again teleport from place to place and turn around in "blinks" as opposed to smoothly. The only gameplay-related configuration available is whether you are sitting or standing. There is almost no button pressing and no interaction with inventory objects like in the mobile games. For those unfamiliar with the previous games - in them, some objects in your inventory have moving parts that you have to adjust to make them useful. None of that here... just pick up, drop it in a place with the same shape/cutout, and once rotation was necessary. You also occasionally turn some wheels / pull some levers or ropes. The game takes no advantage of finger movements - just grabbing stuff, except for one place where you have to press piano keys. What's more annoying is that they don't even take advantage of the available buttons. Turning on/off your lens (an in-game item that has been around since the beginning of the series) is done by opening the inventory (the only button press used) and pulling a lever... why!? There should have been a lens on/off button, considering how often you have to put it on and remove it. Or better yet, should have been an actual eye-piece that you grab and use as a magnifying glass or something like that. Not to mention the lens doesn't stay on when you move around, so the whole open inventory, pull lever, close inventory routine gets really annoying.Storyline - the game does continue the story, but quite poorly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, the only negative aspect is that it only takes three to four hours to beat. Though the puzzles aren't too difficult, they're still fun to figure out.Has nice-looking graphics and some interesting and creepy atmospheres, which make you wish the game didn't strictly let you teleport to a few select spots. The story was nothing too special to me, but that wasn't really an issue.Worth picking up if you want a puzzle experience like nothing else. The game lets you have three profiles, so you can easily let others play through it as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very good VR experience.  Took me about 5.5 hours to finish, so its not the longest game unless you get stuck.  Many small puzzles to figure out and I did get the feeling like I was going back and forth between several places, but it was enjoyable in the end.  Its not a free-roaming experience; you can only teleport to specific places in each environment and are very limited on how far you can navigate from those areas.  That made this game easier because you could not actually explore far from the path.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I completed it in 4.5 hours and found it one of the better VR experiences.  It is a sequel to the rest in the series (including Old Sins) so you get a little more out of it (and have familiarity with some of the mechanics) if you have played those but it is not necessary if you just like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Really enjoyed how this game used full 3D interaction with the clues and items. That being said, it was very short. Beat the game fairly quick. The puzzles were interactive and satisfying, but there weren't any puzzles that really left me stumped. Got the game on sale, but the cost for the short gameplay is not worth it IMO. To wrap things up, DEFINITELY grab this game if you see it at or below $20!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are excellent.  What I cannot understand is why I can only teleport to small spots around the room.  You cannot go to any spot in the room.  There are markers on the floor and you can only go there.  That's not VR at all.  That's the same as playing on a restricted screen.  Free movement is what makes a game VR.  Everything else is great but the main thing that makes VR VR is free movement in the 3D space and it is not.  Therefore this game is not really VR but just a 3D scene.  Also, why can they not add audio of someone talking but instead you have to read words that appear on the wall or objects which immediately makes the whole thing feel like it's not real anymore.  Words don't appear on objects in real life so why would you do that to VR.  Now its less like VR and more fake.  All this good work and because of these small things makes me feel the game is not immersive at all.  I minus well just play it on the computer monitor.  Get the programmers to rework these things please.  From now on I am avoiding games with this type of restricted teleportation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining, but not what I was hoping for.Fireproof paved the way for new puzzle interactions on mobile. Smooth turns and slides made me feel more present in all the mobile versions. Every puzzle opened new dimensions in the same space, new spaces folding out from impossibly small containers.Unfortunately, the VR version does not live up to their UX legacy. The controls feel clunky. Rather than being distinct, the system is clearly pulled from the phones.  I was really looking forward to actually putting lenses to my eyes but it's just a switch in the pop-up inventory system. Even that could have been improved by allowing the player to actually grab items from it, rather than point-and-squeeze.  I was especially looking forward to interacting with items I was holding -- so many of the puzzles in the mobile games involve manipulating the objects on their own after you had picked them up.As for the spaces, they start out large and get smaller. Beautifully decorated rooms turn out to have only a few interaction points. There's really only one mechanism to enter or open smaller containers which was already present in the mobile games.The only thing that sets The Room VR apart from other VR escape games is the visual ambiance. Visually it's fantastic as always, though some of the volumetric effects could use work. I think the sounds, however, were borrowed from previous mobile incarnations. The rumbles weren't rumbly. Even the thunder was underwhelming.I think Fireproof could have had a much stronger showing if they had solved the problems with making a small box contain something bigger given that they can't control the perspective in VR because, as it stands, it's not really worth its nearly 10USD/hr cost.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Both as a VR game and as a adventure/puzzle game, it hits the right spots.Puzzles are logical and sensible and It is pretty clear what in the environment is intractable. The magic lens provides an additional layer to solutions - quick to use and hinted at even in normal view.There are only spots of interest you can jump to - no free movement - but that is a good way to clear up any doubts about what is important in the scene. Handling items works great and so does pulling levers or turning keys. The Environment has good details, I found it pretty immersive.The chapters it's broken up into are good, natural stopping points.It's not the longest game, but with the different puzzles, mechanics and environments I think it is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet puzzling experience. About 3 hours long, the puzzles are interesting enough to make you feel clever when you solve them, but not particularly challenging. The game is filled with clever interactions that can only really be achieved VR, and a number of them genuinely instilled a sense of wonder in me. Maybe not quite $25 worth of wonder, but share that wonder with a friend or two and it'd be *well* worth the price.If I had one criticism, it's that what you can and can't interact with isn't always clearly marked. The hint system helps here, but not after giving you a few clues telling you things you already know and making you wait on a timer before finally helping you spot the interactive object.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this VR experience. The puzzles were fun. If you get stuck on what to do next there are time locked hints in the inventory menu. This helped me get through a couple places where I just didn't know where to go after finishing a puzzle. This game gave me a little over 3 hours of game play before I finished it.  I found the VR controls to be pretty satisfying, and didn't really have issues with the VR environment. There are a couple points where you have to manipulate an item by touch and the game doesn't do a great job of making that clear to the user. Each chapter has a very unique environment/theme. You get 100% of achievements for progressing through and completing the game. Overall, it was like having a really cool escape room experience from the comfort of my home, and at my own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room Dark Matter is the best VR puzzle game at the moment. It has an interesting story and good graphics. On the other hand the puzzler are simple if compared to other games by the same franchise. You have the option of playing standing or sitting and walking by teleport or walking around the room. Score: 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Oculus Rift S. If you have played any of The Room game before you will probably enjoy this one. Loved the experience and puzzles in VR. Most the puzzles are fairly straight forward but the VR view and motion controls make it more enjoyable in my opinion with the exception of rotation items on a platform feeling more awkward compared to just spinning with your finger like in mobile. The only real negative is it will only take 2-3 hours to complete which may or may not be worth the price to you,
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the other Room games and have a VR headset, you will definitely like this game. Not only did the developers recreate the feeling of the previous games, they also implemented several puzzles that utilize what VR gaming is capable of, which brought me a familiar yet unique puzzle solving experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Not very often will I come right out of the gate and say what a great game. But here we are. Just about every game has it flaws. No bugs, game played smooth, great graphics just all around good.  And I believe that the kind of games people could get behind if they were smooth and bug free. This game was enjoyable from beginning to end. Just something about the game grabs you and pulls you in. VR made it a lot better. Felt like I was part of what ever was going on in game. For some it may of been simple, me not so much had to use a few hints to get by and that what I really like about it. It definitely is not a point and click game. Would like to see more game like this. Not to long, maybe a little too short, but fun never the less. 9/10Reason I gave 9 is do to re-playability. Super game but  it's a game you wouldn't play again for about a year or more. No fun if you know what to do all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* It's a Room game.* Good VR interactions and environments.* Callbacks to the previous games.Cons:* Short compared to the other games, there are just 3 major areas.* Only point-to-point movement.* The organ won't play after you solve its puzzle.I'd like to see them patch in an "advanced movement" mode that let's you move freely in the environments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A polished escape room game in VR. If you've done the other The Room games you know exactly what this is like, but with a bit more production value. The sets are very beautiful, was a nice change of pace from my home during a time when I can't go to museums or anything. Definitely interested in more of these.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully detailed graphics see you through essentially what is a series of escape rooms.  The puzzles are cleverly designed and some had me stumped for a while, but everything makes sense in the end.  Persevere and you will be left with a great sense of accomplishment.  I really enjoyed this title and didn't want the experience to end...  If you are into puzzle games then I highly recommend you give this one a go!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A great little VR puzzle experience. Pretty quality throughout and doesn't outlast its welcome. The ingame hint system doles out appropriate clues if and when you want to look at them--there was only one part where I had to look online for on a silly thing where I couldn't figure out what the clue was even talking about.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: While it's definitely on the shorter side (I finished in just over 3 hours) the production values in this game are EXCELLENT, a well-polished AAA-quality VR title. The puzzles are also enjoyable to solve, though a bit on the easy side. You might be put-off by the game's teleport-only locomotion, but it's actually used to great effect here. By only allowing you to teleport to fixed locations, it helps streamline the game, removing a lot of the random wandering around, pixel-hunting for some item that you need to progress that's common in this type of puzzle game. Teleporting puts you in the ideal location to find the thing you need to interact with, and if you can still teleport there, it means there's probably still more to do there. It's a bit like what Myst did, where each scene was framed to draw attention to the stuff related to solving the puzzle.In short, if you're craving a VR that doesn't look like it was made by one guy over a weekend, you can't go wrong with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game overall, puzzles were fun enough.2 complains: - too short, only maybe 4 hours - Lots of things should have been interactable, I don't care if I can't pick it up, if something is hanging from the ceiling and within arms reach I should be able to swing it. Brings you out of VR when that stuff doesn't happen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well done VR game. I'm amazed - from great graphics, to amazing atmosphere, it's hard to complain. If I were to have one, I guess is that I would want it to be much longer (so that I could enjoy it for longer!). But overall, I think the length is fine - mileage will vary depending on the individual playing, as to how long the game takes (puzzle solving speed!).To dig a bit deeper into why I find this game so great - the main thing? Cleverly interesting puzzles. The puzzles are so well constructed, I was amazed throughout my entire playthrough. Not only that, these are the type of intuitive puzzles that give you a ton of "aha!" moments; you won't find obtuse (for the sake of obtuseness) puzzles here, because as long as you are looking around the environment and actually paying attention at the details, you'll be able to figure them out, and that's why this is such a great VR game, it really makes use of the fact that you are "present" in that game world, to serve you the puzzle clues. Love it, and would recommend any VR enthusiast to buy this now - heck, it can even be a great VR demo game to share with the family, since it allows for multiple profiles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks absolutely gorgeous and the sound design is great. It is eery and but not overly so. It truly gives me the feeling of being a mystery detective (a bit Lovecraftian in my honest opinion). Despite the fact you cannot freely move around the entire room, it does help with the puzzle solving. As you are not blindly walking around the entire room for clues. So I think that is a smart design choice. The hints do offer some help if you are stuck and only on tip 3 it flat out tells you the sollution for your current issue. Although I feel the full price is a bit over the top for this title given the playtime and the fact that it has little to no replay value. I would certainly recommend this game if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable puzzle game. Very immersive and atmospheric, decent graphics and audio, and very clever use of VR. It's quite short (3-4 hours), and probably doesn't have a lot of replay value once you've solved all the puzzles, but I enjoyed it very much. I don't know if they have plans to release any more The Room VR games, but I'm definitely interested in playing more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in just over 6 hours. No re-play value to speak of. With that I enjoyed my 6 hours. The puzzles were real brain-teasers and I had to used the hints a few times which is a good thing as they weren't too easy.Good detail in the environments and spooky in a good way.  I would say it would be worth $10-15 to play through once.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: In 7 hours of playtime I completed the game on three profiles. I got 2 hours of enjoyable gameplay out of it, but my immersion was interrupted by loading screens and unnecessary fades to black. This is an enjoyable puzzle game, but understand that it is only around 2 hours long. If you are a longtime fan of the series you may be disappointed by the interactivity and lore. Items you collect cannot be  The fan service seem to just be there to add cheap value without improving the final product.Overall, while I like the game, many of the decisions made makes me think that the game was rushed out, and that the team is very inexperienced with VR as a platform.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all of The Room games and this is by far my favourite. The sense of place is (as ever) fantastic, the objects are wonderful to look at. The puzzles are as satisfying as ever, and the VR movement adds some nice location based variety compared to previous games. Really is a great VR experience but more importantly a great game. Please make more!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was an amazing experience.....EXCEPT...WHY CAN'T THE DEVELOPERS PUT IN A QUIT BUTTON?  When you decided you've had enough you have to take off the VR headset and crash the application via the close button in Windows. Very Frustrating.  Other than that 5 stars out of 5 stars.  Most puzzles were intuitive. I had to use the help less than 3 times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So it's not quite as polished as the other room games, but it was enjoyable waste of time.  The puzzles were super easy and not nearly as complex as the other Room games, but for their first foray into VR, not bad.I liked the magic goggles effect.  I prefer the walking mechanic, but this one only had the jump to circle option. Each "chapter" had it's own room to experiment with and explore, many much larger than others.  Some areas feel like content was left out and seem to be just walk through areas.  Worked very well with Index.  The grip mechanic was a bit picky and sometimes I felt like it wouldn't release my grip quickly enough, but that may be my tight grip play style.  Ending puzzles much easier than the game as a whole and felt like it just rushed to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Just wonderful, totally immersive, intuitive and beautiful to play. Always enjoyed the "flat" games, this is everything I hoped it would be.It's not 7.8hrs as I took, I left the game idling, and regardless other people's opinions about cost and value, this was worth every penny.Desperately wanting more now!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice quality escape room style game with nice puzzles to solve. For 4h quality gameplay, I would however recommend to get the title on sale for around 15 € or $, it's not worth 30€/$ in my world. Too short and no replayability for that. On the other hand, if you go to an escape room IRL you get to spend only 1h but probably pay the same. Your choice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I like that it sort of follows the premise of the other Room games.  The problems/puzzles are simple so it's super easy to solve them and still have a good time looking around.  I don't like that the player doesn't get to explore the world.  You're basically going from one puzzle to the next and back and forth. Still, it's mindless fun that doesn't require you to shoot or run over anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great Puzzle Game that makes great use of VR. It was a tad bit short for the price, some riddles could have been a little more elaborate and harder and the story could have been fleshed out a bit more. Maybe have a voiced cast for the next entry?  Though it is imo without a question still the best VR puzzle Game out there currently.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you are new to the "The Room" series of games, and you like puzzlers, then you are in for a huge treat with The RoomVR.  I have played every version and this year, when we received a VR headset for Christmas, I was very happy to finally play this VR only entry to the series.  I only wish I could go back and play all the others in VR format now!  Fireproof has never disappointed and this title is the best of them all with the addition of VR!  Please continue the excellent work Fireproof!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. It feels very immersive and the graphics on the secret rooms/passages are really great! This game just BLEW ME AWAY! I really hope a sequel will be made for VR!!This game really, REALLY pays attention to detail. Watching the special effects of doing various things in VR really sucks you in and makes you feel part of the ongoing story. This game really brought me in and made me feel part of it for a while. Really what more can you ASK FOR from a game? HIGHLY recommended if you like creepy escape room type games with LOADS and LOADS of details.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most awesome game on VR. I finished all "the room" games before buying VR and regret that I cant play Dark matter...And now I bought VR and first of all I completed just it. What I can say... Wow. For me its a new level of "questroom" game. Recomend for everyone who loves The room and Da Vinchi series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game!  The puzzles are light, but stimulating, the environment is awesome, sounds are integral and I enjoyed the length and progression.  I can not wait for another, so immersive when I took off the headset I had a bit of a shock that I was not in a temple!  the scale puzzles were my favorite portion.  More please!!!BTW folks complain that it is expensive for what it is, they are just wrong, this game is well worth the $30, think of it as 3 nights at a movie, but in reality you are in the movie!!!  The graphics detail alone is worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. I recently got my new rig build with the Reverb G2 and the clarity, details andimmersiveness is off the charts. The game itself is layed out very well and also the mechanics are working perfectly fine. Not all puzzles are the most difficults but this also keeps the flow going in the game. They are well thought trhough. Also the story line is great. If I can make 1 suggestion to the development team....Please include free roaming around in your next title, this will give the player way more immersiveness and probably more challenging. Because now you know with the snapping to certain places you need to do something there.Please keep them coming. I just love these type of games....and happy to pay for them as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of last year, I didn't know much about The Room series when I bought the three games available on Steam.  When I played the first game, I got hooked and played all three games back to back.  When looking for more information on these games, I saw that the next game in the series was in development and would support virtual reality.  Perfect!  I was immediately sold and knew it would be a day one purchase for me.The Room VR was a perfect fit for me as someone who had played three games in the series, and as VR gamer.  But I think The Room VR will also seem strange to people who don't have both of those characteristics.For VR gamers who have never played a The Room game, the lack of free movement will feel limiting and unnecessary.  But, I believe this decision is in keeping with what I noticed in the very first The Room game I played: these games are designed with a focus on the puzzles and objectives.  They have never let the players waste much time wandering around or wasting time on objects that are useless to progression.  Preventing VR players from searching every corner for clues allows the puzzles themselves to remain paramount.  The Room VR maintains this design philosophy, and I understand that very well from playing previous games in the series.For fans of The Room, yet don't play games in VR, they will be disappointed by this game for obvious reasons.  This game was designed in a manner that goes "all-in" on the kind of experience and interactions that are possible in VR with motion controls.  In my opinion, it's still a bad idea to develop games that are VR-only, especially for small, independent studios.  Limiting a game to only the VR audience, for what are often small gains in taking uncompromising advantage of motion controls and an immersive perspective, probably isn't worth it.  I say this even for a AAA VR-only title like Half-Life: Alyx.  I prefer to see developers take the route Cyan Worlds did with Obduction, or White Lotus did with Xing: The Land Beyond.  These games lack physical interactions with motion controllers, but they are playable in VR and on screens.  I don't think motion controls and physical interactions are the end-all/be-all of Virtual Reality, though I'll admit to having met some people who think it is.The Room VR is dazzling to witness, with many of the special effects and mechanics from previous games adapted to work in virtual reality.  The extremely high level of detail for objects and in the game world is maintained here, though my first generation VR headset can't let me appreciate that fully.I completed the game in a little over five hours.  This ties into my biggest criticism of The Room VR: value for money.  $30 is steep for a short game with no replay value.  The extremely high quality of this experience elevates it despite its brevity, but I'm not sure it reaches the $30 level.  I don't know if Fireproof Games considers The Room VR as a platform for DLC, but I'd like to see some additional puzzle rooms or boxes to purchase at a reasonable price.The Room VR goes all-in on virtual reality, which I can appreciate as a VR gamer.  I am happy to pay $30 and support Fireproof Games' second attempt at a VR game.  This game proves that they are experts at creating great virtual reality experiences.  I hope to see many more from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I am I think 80-90% through with this game. The game suffered in that I played it right after Half Life Alyx and no indie game can compete with the textures and production values of Alyx. But coming back to it to finish it this week, it really is an excellent VR puzzler.
