Agreed the puzzles are probably easier than the mobile Room games but the scale and VR-specific nature of the puzzles makes up for that.I do wish there was an explicitly a one-handed mode. I think most puzzles can be done one-handed but not all; accessibility would be greatly enhanced if it was possible to finish one-handed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Good graphics, great sound design and an outstanding level of polish gets me excited for what this studio can provide in the future. This game is great for seated play with no stretching required so far, so if you look for that specifically in your games for whatever reason, know you should be good here. Its also good for VR users yet to build their VR-legs, as all motion is teleport to specific set locations. I've never played The Room on another platform, but it works incredibly well in VR. If you are good at these puzzle games, then you might be able to complete it in under 3 hours, but a more leisurely approach will easily get you 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It was a pretty fun puzzle game but as other reviews have stated definitely wait for it to be on sale as 30$ for a game this short is a bit of a hard sell at least for me. I did like that there's options for standing or sitting depending on your preference and the only real complaint I had is that snap-turning and teleport are on the sticks so it felt really easy to try to teleport somewhere and accidentally turn if you even dared nudge the stick a little left or right.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the other games in the series this is an easy recommendation and if you haven't play the others and then jump into The Room VR. It's shorter than the previous entries and uses similar mechanics, but how it uses the VR element adds a really fun level of interaction.The story continues the lore you've learned from the other games and if you enjoyed them you'll like this one just as much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a bit short and the puzzles are pretty easy. But man is this game ever a wonder for the eyes. There is so much environmental story telling and amazing mechanical mechanisms to see. This is a great game for anyone, even those who do usually like escape room style games (like me) and I think this game would be amazing for kids. You should play this and the Devs should make another game.Notes to devs: -I know this game and the ones before had every thing blocked off so you can focus on the puzzle. But come on guys! Let me explore more! I wanna see everything in your beautiful environment. And being able to do it with smooth locomotion would be awesome.-Smooth turning is essential to modern VR games guys. Id love to see it as an option in this game and future ones.-Even if you dont let us fully explore the environment  can you give us a little movement options? Most of your puzzle were nice and tight to the player but playing my my tiny play spaces was barely doable. Artificial movement helps a lot. And if you implement it in future game you could make much larger and sprawling puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's The Room as you remember, this time in VR. It was a bit confusing the first couple of levels because I wasn't aware of what I could and couldn't interact with - then I realised most loose objects can be picked up. It's unfortunately short, taking me only 3+ hours - while I was hoping for at least twice of that considering The Room 3 took me 6+ hours. I can Recommend this game if you love The Room, but be well aware you're paying $30 (non-discounted release price) for 3 hours with little replay value (since you'd already know all the puzzles' solutions). More value, of course, if you have multiple folks to share the game with to have their own playthroughs.TL;DR: It's The Room as you know and love, but short playtime for the price you're paying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So... I played the game through in just under 3 hours. That makes it over 10€ per hour of gametime. An Escape Room is very similarly priced but is also a better experience (imho). If you like puzzles and it is on sale, buy it! The puzzles were mostly straight forward and lean on the easy side (as long as you paid attention to your sorroundings). A great way of adding gametime would be to just make people search for information. Also give us more freedom to move about and find stuff - having the fixed standpoints allows for quicker playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game, as always then you play a "The Room" game. But VR adds another level. It's great to see things and be much more immersed in the environment. There is so much to see.I would love it if the developer would make more VR games like this. They nailed the puzzles, maybe do some experimenting with VR controls? I would love to walk around free. Maybe some puzzles involving making gestures with your arms. I don't know. I feel like there still is a lot of untapped potential for VR controls.And even if the developer makes another VR game like this, without any special additions, I would still buy it, because this game is solid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What great timing for this to come out! I actually got on here the day it was released and coincidentally found this because I was thinking that The Room would make an excellent VR game. After playing this, buy was I right. The puzzles weren't too difficult. I only got stuck on a bug that I found where the dresser was unlocked, but couldn't be opened. Restarting the game fixed it and it worked the second time.People are only complaining about the game being too short because it was so awesome and we just want more. Perhaps you could add some kind of expansion that makes it fun to play all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved it. While it took a few missteps here and there with one or two puzzles where I did't notice something rather small, I still absolutely loved it. The first four games were wonderfully atmospheric already and this game in VR adds even more to that. I rather enjoy that these games are more based around logic puzzles rather than other point and click games where you just go to a place and use an object. I had no issues technically and I overall had a lot of fun. I definitely cant wait to see where the series goes next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed playing. I have played through the first 3 games and this one holds up very well. VR mechanics handle nicely (HTC Vive). Played completely through in 4 hours. I don't know if it's normally worth full price for that short of a game, but it was definitely worth it while stuck at home during CoVID. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The best VR experience I've had to date. The gameplay is engaging and just challenging enough without being frustrating. It's decently long, and totally worth the price. The game is also gorgeous to look at and had me stopping in my tracks to look around and admire the environments I was in. Left me wanting more, in absolutely the best way.Oh, also in terms of how the VR experince is comfort wise:-Standing or sitting options-Comfortably playable in minimum required room space size-Easy "Reset View" option-Comfortable "teleport" movementAll in all it's an extremely enjoyable and comfortable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little puzzle game that makes great use of the VR setting and controls. The puzzles were challenging enough to make me feel accomplished when finished but not too hard to complete without numerous hints. The hints I did use were helpful without giving too much away. The biggest weakness I found was with the plot. While it gives some hints as to a story, mostly through notes, it goes through all of it without giving much background info on the events happening in game. Putting that aside, it's a solid VR title and worth picking up if you have a headset.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, with nice innovative mechanics that would be impossible or hard to understand outside VR. Took me about 3 hours to beat.There are some slightly creepy moments, but not really any jump scares (or other scares) to speak about, so don't dismiss it for being scary if such games aren't your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the game is good for VR, but this is not going to take you long.  It took about 2.5 hours and is not challenging in any way, it's mostly just following along the story and using the items where they totally make sense.  If you have played any previous Room games you will move through this very quickly.  In the end its a couple hours entertainment and about the same price as a few pints, so it works out the same as going for few drinks with buds :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, especially if you love The Room series of games. If you haven't played the others I would recommend playing those first so the plot makes more sense (though definitely not required).  The puzzles are interesting and fit with the theme style and theme of previous titles. I beat the game in one "standing". The game itself is beautiful and using the motion controls was intuitive. I do admit I kept forgetting I didn't always need to use the trigger to interact with some dials, but there is no negative effect in doing so. Aside from that it was more just doing the right motion (which I admittedly failed on a few times, or didn't do it enough). The only frustrating motion was pulling on rope (which you do several times). You need to do hand over hand but sometimes it didn't quiet grab and I would need to move quickly to catch it (would be nice if this was improved). The only other game play issue I really had This was everything I hoped for a Room themed VR experience. Sadly not open world, but then neither were the previous games and having specific locations to stand can keep you from focusing on the background scenery so it isn't a negative.  And because of fixed locations you can play the game sitting or standing (though after 3 hours standing my feet wish I chose sitting, then again I played this after an entire day on my feet already). The only two negatives:I experienced were:The game would lose the center of my play area and have me on the edge, trying to correct this would put me in an object and the game would complain.  Likely could have fixed this by doing a reset position from the steam menu (though not sure as I never tried, too focused on the game itself). The game crashed on me after finishing the 4th section (placed the object, watched the letter fly down, picked it up, and froze. Kept pulsating between the game scene and the steam loading screen for a few minutes until I just ended up in the Steam loading area with nothing else.  Opening the steam menu showed the game was no longer playing and I was able to start it again.  Due to the recent auto-save I only lost about a 1 minute, and simply needed to place the object down and watch the letter come back. Even with the crash, positioning issues, and sometimes difficult movements (these are not limited to the VR game, some puzzles in the rest of the series require awkward mouse/finger movements but they aren't to bad and just require another attempt to complete the movement) I have zero reservations about recommending this game to anyone who loves puzzles, VR, and/or the rest of the series. I hope they keep the series going, and definitely would like another VR title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Buy. This. Game.Have you played the other Room Games?  Do you have a VR headset? Do you want to  in The Room rather than tapping on a screen, alone and on the outside looking in? Do you want to be surrounded by and washed over with the dark aesthetics, manipulating the puzzles in what feels like meat-space? Why are you still reading this review? He calls you. He is waiting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It may be short (took me 4.5 hours to beat fully) but it's excellent. I can't wait for the next one! It has very accurate manipulation of objects, the difficulty is reasonable, and you can play sitting. My only incremental wish is that it allowed for full motion versus teleportation as that would bring you into the game further.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant addition to the franchise! The series' dark atmosphere translates in to virtual reality remarkably well, creating a great sense of foreboding and the uneasy feeling that you are completely and utterly alone. The art is beautiful and there were numerous occasions where I would pass the headset to my significant other to have a peek (she loved the witch's house!) The difficulty of the puzzles consistently felt like they hit the sweet spot, with the solutions not always being immediately apparent but never so obtuse that you simply give up. The game does a very good job of making you feel smarter than you are! My only complaint is that I wish it was longer. I feel satisfied with the money I spent versus the experience I had but I crave more! Chop chop, Fireproof Studios. You have work to do!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Short if you can figure out what your doing. A visually stunning and enjoyable VR experience. I played it with my family and had fun yelling possible solutions at each other and taking in the scenery. Ran perfectly on my decent PC setup. If you can get it on discount it's a must-buy. Otherwise, it's up to you how much you want to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: For those who played all past "The Room" games (e.g. on tablets), it's not a big challenge. But still, from the moment you enter the game until you finish it, it's just perfect. Amazing details bring your VR experience to the highest possible level. Super easy controls allow to enjoy the whole game while seated.3 hours of gameplay for 30 Euros seems expensive but it's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely awesome. A bit expensive for play time but on sale grab it up ( I did) Absolutely super fun. The puzzles are just hard enough to be challenging but not ridiculous. I only got "stuck" one time and it was over something stupid though I did finally figure it out. Graphics amazing too . Very relaxed, can one hand all but one part of the game. I really never felt dead ended. If you feel "stuck" try grabbing everything in the puzzle areas, sometimes you just havent noticed other objects work too. Even though their other ones are not VR im going to buy the bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to the whole VR games world so this is one of the games which made me want to get a headset given that I've played through all the other games in the series.  So far I've found the transition to a VR game from a game in front of a screen is amazing and very immersive.  Due to how much greater the level of immersion VR games appear to have with you essentially being "in it" I for one would very much like to avoid any kind of horror/jump scare games due to my disposition.  Thankfully, despite the general creepy Lovecraft atmosphere which is commonly associated with the Room series of games I can safely say that this game delivered in this aspect.  Enough atmosphere to raise the tension and put me on edge, but no jump scares/shocks to put me off playing it (there are two bits I recall in 2 and 3 which if done in VR could have).  Despite reviews saying the game is short it still delivers exceptionally well as previous titles in the series do and I found the ending particularly poignant including a nod to previous games in the series.  Well done Fireproof Games, you've hit the mark again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game (The Room VR: A Dark Matter) was such an amazingly, beautiful, mind bending game with ahead of its time graphics. I absolutely 100% recommend this game to my fellow vr players, this stunning game is a true masterpiece in which you start right way with the use of your mind. From the eerie soundtrack to the infectious story line that keeps you wondering what is next even when not in game, it always draws you right back to it. I completed this game in seven hours only because you know LIFE and ADULTING. Otherwise I would have played this game all the way through with as many hours as it took me. Lastly the extraordinary effort that went into the creation of this what I call a masterpiece is deeply appreciated by me. I cannot wait to see if there are more chapters. muahahahahahaha
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It is very well made. If you like mechanical puzzle games don't miss this one. Victorian England, Ancient Egyptian, and Templar themes. A nice balance between challenging and enjoyable. Optional hints available in game that are specific enough to get you unstuck but not ruin the game. I can't say enough good things about this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played their games on mobile and always thought it would be awesome in VR. And I was right! I played with the valve index, and while the controls were OK, it probably could have been better with finger tracking. However, it was still very enjoyable, and still recommend playing if you like these types of games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun. However, you have to make sure that you're physically always facing the same direction, otherwise it will change the way the camera's oriented every time you teleport in the game and you'll have to manually turn yourself around. It's hard to explain, but the game would always turn me around when I teleported, as if I were walking backward into rooms, and every teleport had to be followed by me manually turning back in the right direction, until I figured out that that didn't happen if I kept my chair always pointed in the direction of my starting position.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting story and the gameplay is alright. I would say that other than one problem I have with this game that it is worth picking up. and that major problem is the price. It's not worth 30 dollars for a 2 hour gameplay experience, those of you with different skills when it comes to puzzle games may disagree or have an entirely different experience with the game, however it barely took me over 2 hours and I found that to be slightly lack luster. Otherwise the game was rather enjoyable! So just wait for it to go on sale
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR puzzle games I've played. The $30 price tag was a bit off putting first considering how short the game is, but its worth every penny. The controls for the puzzle are simple and don't require quick reflexes or even a lot of movement. I do wish there was the option to walk around, but it would be confusing for new players.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: ive played all the mobile games of The Room and really enjoyed it so i wanted to try this one and i must say, Its kinda creepy to be in the game and hearing all the sounds around you but at the same time super awesome! also i think its some pretty interesting quests, some a little difficult but still worth it!thank you for making the vr game, hope to see more in the future
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Holy cow. Now, I'm new to VR and I've only seriously played two games so far - Assetto Corsa and The Room VR. Both are AMAZING. I have a laptop I'm playing on right now, and while the game initially said my laptop wasn't optimal for the best experience, once I disabled anti-aliasing, the frame rate was superb. On my gaming rig (12th gen Intel and an RTX2080) I expect no issues at all. VERY pleased with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic entry in The Room series, with a nice nod to a couple of persons from The Room 3 and Old Sins.  I was a little disappointed that the organization holding multiple Null elements at the end of Old Sins wasn't expanded on, but a great entry nonetheless. One critique: as a VR only entry, this entry must be held to a higher standard, as to whether the gameplay is dependent on, or enhanced by, its dependency on VR.  I'm sad to say it does not.  While the visuals in VR are impressive, the gameplay is the same style from Old Sins.  It is even detracted from a bit, as manipulating inventory items in VR, a staple of the previous games, is incredibly frustrating.  I assume this was realized in development, as this only occurs once in the entire game. While a fantastic entry in The Room series, this is, ultimately, a mobile game in VR form, and gains nothing as a VR only title.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: There is this simple correlation that states that the price should be proportional to the game play time. I find that correlation to be a bit off when playing some particular games.There are some games that offer an experience that cannot be reproduced easily (or not at all). The team(s?) behind these  series is completely off the charts. I have found other dev teams that create similar games, .If the price seems a little high, you should try some other VR (VR!!) games out there and see how buggy they can get or how poorly optimized they are. And I'm not even talking about the price tag, the length of the game or the quality of the game!My girlfriend and I went back to play all the  to sharpen our minds before diving in this game. We were amazed by the simplicity of the controls and all those captivating animations.  offers a nice combination of past game mechanisms and continues exploring the same themes with a new perspective.The length was perfect for us. The experience is on point and I can say that I have not seen a better VR puzzle game than this one (and I have tried a lot of them). I prefer to have a shorter game of quality, than a more longer version with visible flaws.It's a magic experience. I recommend it for sure!Nice job guys and girls!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this enough.  I've played all of The Room games on mobile and love how this company does their stories.  Put the flawless story telling into VR with intricate puzzles and fun environments and you get a game that truly holds water.30 dollars for a demonstration in masterpiece is worth every cent.  If you have VR, this is an absolute must own.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, themes of egypt,templars and witches; puzzles scale in difficulty and provide an enjoyable challenge. Play areas are very atmospheric and capturing.  im really glad i bought it and im going to be playing through more than once. Can't wait to see what these folks come up with going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A great continuation to a series of puzzle games.Though be aware that the move to VR doesn't mean you'll now be able to walk around freely - you'll still mostly teleport between predefined points, but you'll be able to look around more freely while there.And because of the move to VR, the visuals aren't as good as in the previous games, though the game's still charming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I am conflicted, this is a very good game, it upholds the standard of the other room games. It's aesthetic is wonderful, the puzzles are fun and I can only think of one that really stumped me due to mediocre design (a rarity in a pure puzzle game).The one and only problem is the price. The experience, however good, is half as long as The Room 3 for five times the price. I have personally experienced professional VR game development and do not consider it to be even close to ten times more difficult than regular game dev making this leave a sour taste in my mouth after this otherwise very pleasant experience.If you can get this on sale, a serious sale, and you have a VR device, do so, otherwise I would recommend you pass up this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fireproof took what was already a rather epic puzzler and moved it a step further. I've played most of the games of this series on mobile, but playing a Room game in VR blew me away. Getting immersed in this world was absolutely wonderful. The control scheme was very well-done (at least in Windows Mixed Reality) and, while I think freedom of movement in this world would generally be a great thing in VR games, that they kept to the notion of having narrow focus points as opposed to an open-world and this was much appreciated. High hopes for another VR title in the not so distant future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. VR fits the genre really well in my opinion. Especially inspecting/rotating items feels so much better with your own hands instead of a mouse. I think, however, that the inclusion of free movement would really bring the experience one step further. With the way it's implemented here you are limited to only a few perspectives, while VR allows for many more ways of exploring the puzzle pieces, like crouching down, moving around a table instead of rotating it and generally feeling less steered towards the points of interest and solution.One small thing that annoyed me while playing was the strong vibration of the controllers in certain spots, I'd have appreciated an option to turn it down or off but maybe I just didn't find it in the menu.I definitely recommend it and really hope there will be another VR entry in the series, that hopefully explores some more possibilities.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of The Room, definitely pick it up, though you may want to wait for a sale. However, if you're new to the series, go try the other entries first. They're each five dollars for three-ish hours of excellent puzzles. If you want more, come back and get this one.Personally, this was an absolute 10/10 experience that I have no regrets paying 30 dollars for, but I don't blame anyone for balking at the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was my final stage of my binge play of The Room series. I have played the first 4 on desktop as a build up to the VR release and I was not disappointed! The atmosphere was just the right amount of spooky and mysterious. The difficulty of the levels as you progressed was  pretty balanced except at the end it felt very easy. I did struggle quite a bit with the church level personally so my brain appreciated the slow cool off. I left the game very very satisfied. Would highly recommend this to any one with a VR headset who is a fan of The Room series or who just enjoy solving puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare for a first VR game to be quality, but this is one of them. The gameplay was really good and its one of the better puzzle/ escape the room games that I have played. Even if you aren't that good at puzzles, it has a really good hint system to help lead you to the answer so you don't have to worry about looking up the answer. Very highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room Series of puzzle adventure games are absolutely the best of their kind, bar none, with incredible environments and game play.  And now, with "A Dark Matter" in VR, it's unbelievably immersive and looks incredible!Keep up the phenomenal work Fireproof Games, we can't wait for many more, with hopefully more in  VR too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So good, The Room games are always amazing. The puzzles translate amazingly into VR. It's not the longest game BUT every second of it is condensed with beautiful visuals, audio and brain teasing puzzles. Amazing that it came from a development team of 12. I really hope the Room makes a full or partial migration to VR as it offered a completely different experience from the other games while still staying "The Room"I'll be waiting patiently for the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very intuitive game with straightforward controls. Graphics (High) are good, but not exceptional. The content and ambiance of the game is awesome. Some puzzles are really easy, some difficult - For the difficult ones, you have the option to reveal a hint but most of the time it's not needed. I was stuck in "Into the organ", I have to admit that for that one I had to use Google, I just couldn't find it and the hint was pretty useless.I have the feeling that the last part of the game was added more for the storyline than for the puzzles. The last "puzzles" were so easy, it felt more like was just moving some boxes, I was hoping for a really hard puzzle to end the game.I had fun for more than 4 hours and there are 3 extra profiles that can be used for the rest of the family / friends (you get a total of 4 profiles)Regardless of the little details, the game is worth every penny. Really enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free review: I had a great time playing this moderately short game, about 10 hours. The puzzles are fun and grow on one another in a nice way. There were no jump scares which my partner was worried about. My only minor complaint is that some of the sprites are obviously 2D used in a 3D environment, but it was never enough to take me out of the moment.If you are a fan of the Victorian Era and occult themed puzzles, this game is a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely gorgeous game. A level of detail every VR game should strive for. Shorter than i was hoping (3-4 hours) but long enough as a VR game. Just not sure the dollars per hour of entertainment was appropriate at full price ($30), given 0 replayability, but I'm not disappointed with my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally proves how much VR can enhance even more traditional game genres like the puzzle adventure game. I have loved The Room series since the start and I always thought they'd be great in VR.The only downside, it is a little short for the asking price, which certainly isn't outside the norm for VR. However, there isn't too much replay value in these games if you already know the solutions.If you can find it on sale, it'd probably help. Overall though, a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics good and the game play was nice and smooth. Puzzles were not hard, (not Myst level hard), but were engaging. I am a great fan of teleportation mode of moving around in VR so this worked well for me.  Took me about 11 hours to complete, but a large part of that time was spent looking around for fun. Will play it again and look for Easter eggs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful V.R. experience.There were many times when my jaw dropped at what I was seeing and experiencing, and the puzzles were, for the most part, satisfying to solve.  There were a couple that were like, really??? That's the solution?!  But for the most part, I would play a sequel, and will recommend this to my puzzle solving friends.This is for the person that likes to explore and solve puzzles.  The price is justified in the quality of game play, the quality of the puzzles, and the quality of the story and graphics.  There's no open moving around, you'll have to get used to moving to only very specific locations the game lets you go to.  But after playing for a level, you'll realize it's a "quality of life" decision.  If you could walk around everywhere, you would spend hours exploring every corner looking for clues, instead it only took me three hours to complete the game.The developers did a great job, there was only one bug I experienced and restarting the game solved it, but I would definitely consider buying another game from them.Not sure if it's possible to have an easy and hard mode, but I would appreciate being able to go through the game a second time with harder challenges and puzzles.  It would also be incredible if you could revisit earlier levels with tools you only receive later in the game in order to solve puzzles you couldn't solve, or didn't have access to before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: By far my favorite Room game in the series. I've beaten the game roughly 3+ times and I loved it each time. I loved how being in vr immersed me in the game. The puzzles were fun and rewarding. My only issue would be a lack of secrets or any hidden ending, which I really enjoyed in The Room 3 so I would love to see an update where they developers add more secrets or another ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: [Review Copy Received]-Overall highly recommend this, if you like puzzle games and escape rooms this is the game for you.-ProsAtmospheric environments.Puzzles scale up as you progress.It has a hint system (lots of VR titles do not have this feature if you get stuck and left wondering around)Note: It's the normal length of most VR titles.If you loved the original services on mobile and PC with VR this adds another element to the game. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I had tried The Room on my iPhone a few years ago and didn't really expect much since I wasn't hooked back then. But this is quite amazing. At first I was irritated because you can't move around freely in the rooms, but after a while I got used and started appreciating the wonderful and detailed environments. Incredibly nice.The immersion and feeling of scale that you get in this game is honestly something that has to be experienced. Very high production standard throughout!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Always wanted to play a The Room game but when I found out they had a VR one I had to buy it. Physically having to interact with the puzzle gives it an extra element of fun. Some of the controls can be a little jank but isn't frustrating, each puzzle seems to be longer than the previous and all the visuals are done well.The game isn't the longest but is very dense in content, even so I really wish it was longer and really hope there will be another The Room VR but longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, the good points: > Graphics were amazing. > Puzzles were fun, and reminded me a lot of MYST.> Gameplay was challenging, but not impossible.> Most interactivity was within a comfortable range above and below my neutral head position. The stuff that needed work:> Fixed playing positions: it was really a pain to not be able to pace around in-game. Jumping from spot to spot was really jarring and unnatural, and it broke the immersion, right along with the angry yellow message to "return to play area" any time I accidentally walked into a wall. > Really clunky position correction method, it required you to basically leave the experience to recenter yourself in your play area, and then click a button to calibrate the game. Due to how you're basically locked into a very tight space, and the game expects you to not walk around, any amount of walking around you do in your playspace means that next time you teleport, the whole world is now reset to your new standing position. I quickly found myself drifting to the edge of my playspace and even hitting physical objects like my desk and walls, and in order to fix it, I had to go through the clunky process. >Mediocre storyline. I know this is a puzzle game and the focus was supposed to be on solving the puzzles, but the story aspects were a little too light. There wasn't really any direct character interaction, and while it did play to my memories of the first version of MYST from way back in the middle-ages of PC gaming, it also hit the parts I didn't like, like the sheer lack of other visible characters to interact with. Overall, I think the game was fairly well made, and if you like this kind of puzzle game, and are okay with the complaints I've made, definitely give it a play. Just remember, Steam won't issue refunds if you play for 4 hours, and decide it wasn't worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles in The Room are incredibly well-crafted and satisfying to solve, with each one feeling like a new challenge that requires careful thought and attention to detail. The game also tells a compelling story that draws players in and keeps them engaged from start to finish. Despite its spooky atmosphere, The Room is a game that can be enjoyed by players of all skill levels. It's a game that is easy to pick up and play, but challenging enough to keep players engaged for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: OK, yes, let's get the elephant in the room. it's £25 here in the UK. That's a LOT of cash for a 'mobile length (yes, I know I've got 8 odd hours in it, had to keep stopping due to life) HOWEVER. with that said? you'd be SO hard pressed to find a more immersive, interactive experience, the likes of which oozes love from every single pixel anywhere else. Almost every interaction and solution comes with a surge of pride as you realise that yes, you have to DO the thing, be it, pull, push, turn.. yes, you're THERE. albeit with no body and a dubious choice in gloves.I want to say, as everyone's short on cash to wait, but honestly? I cant. just, pick it up. yeah, it's short. but the OTHERS that you show, their first 'eureka' moment, the impossible to hide smile of achievement is worth every. single. penny.Just, get it if you can. Thank you Firebox, thank you so so much. Just, not so long for the encore eh? :POverall, four paws out of four.. and a creepy black tentacle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A good VR experience, but too short for the full ticket price, definitely worth picking up on sale.The game offers standing or sitting options, I only tried standing. Each level is a wide, reasonably detailed environment which suits VR well. To ensure you don't spend hours wandering aimlessly, the game hops you between the places you need to be, where you can interact with objects. You can physically move about about, but if you move too far from your spot, the game says you are out of play.The puzzles are similar to other 'Room' games, often using the lens to show hidden puzzles: having an option to toggle the lens without having to load up the inventory would have been nice, maybe touching the side of my head rather than a button?Good points:Some effort has been made for certain puzzles to make the most of the VR which is good where you need to move objects around, pull ropes etc, but more puzzles using perspective shift, two handed problems or dexterity would have been good as these cannot be easily replicated without VR, though am aware these may present some accessibility issues.The levels have the right amount of detail and feel big. Any object that is just cosmetic is nailed down which while it does save you some time and you don't need to tear the rooms apart, I think there is a balance to be made however between ease and the ability to turn a place upside down while looking for something!Meh points:There is a story in as much as an escape room has a story; you're there to solve the puzzles. I wasn't quite sure what happened at the end, but didn't really care.Bad points:The ending level was pretty lacklustre compared to the earlier levels which was a shame. Rather than combining the problems from earlier levels together; there is a whole environment that you just walk through and then you have to find 4 pieces that are carefully hidden on crates around the room and do a jigsaw puzzle. More puzzles where I need to find information around the rooms rather than simple 'find object, put object here' would be good.It is pretty short, I finished in about 3.5 hours. At full price this would be pretty steep for such a short game, on sale it was better value. Compared to an escape room, it is of equivalent value (when on sale).Conclusion:Overall, if you like escape rooms, you would like this game and I would love to see more games like it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I saw people comparing this to an escape room. That's pretty accurate. You're paying for about two hours, maybe three if you get really stuck, but its a good few hours. Most of the replay value is either months later when you've forgotten things, or making other people play through it. If you like puzzle games, and like this series, definitely pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: You like ? You have ? Get This game continues the story from the rest of the  series, but it's not essential to have played those to enjoy it.Each location, just like the rest of the series is beautifully rendered, and if there's any criticism, it's that due to the "teleport to fixed point" movement you don't get to full explore and appreciate them!Is it easier than the previous games? Yes, I'd say so (I completed in just over 3 hours and I wasn't rushing). The previous games weren't all super-long, but  does feel a bit small (certainly compared to 3), but maybe more on par with  1Should you get it? As I said, if you like  and you have VR, then definitely.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: While it is short for the price, it's about the length of what we've always expected from The Room games, and the quality of the content is still stellar as it has always been. Some puzzles felt a little unintuitive, and as their first VR outing, there were some bugs I encountered (hand was caught on a lever at one point and crashed the game), but it didn't hamper the overall experience much. I especially enjoyed the especially creative last area of the game. The Room VR is also a great continuation of the story set up in The Room 3 and The Room: Old Sins (though it is unfortunate this came out on Steam before The Old Sins has). Here's hoping for a The Room VR 2!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR was a fine little jaunt into the VR puzzle room space. At 3-5 hours though, I cant recommend it at full price but, on a decent sale, its not a bad pick up. The environments are pretty cozy and puzzles range from baby mode to head scratcher.I was disappointed that it only has teleport movement and it dose suffer from the point and click, stick your inventory items into every space you think they might go until it works, syndrome. But the story is interesting, graphically its pleasing and I enjoyed it enough to keep me coming back for 4 sessions to finish.If you find it for a good price and like puzzle games, its not at all a bad grab.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all of the 'The Room' games and I gotta say when I heard a VR version was coming out I was super glad I had brought VR. This game is great, I love the puzzles and the graphics for a VR title is one of the best out there, especially from a indie studio. This game almost has 0 flaws, apart from the last level which seemed weak in comparison to the others, I felt it could have been a little more longer and exciting seeing how it was the 'end'. Overall I would highly recommend this game if you like puzzle games, escape rooms or just want something pretty to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fireproof games never fails to deliver on style, atmosphere and intrigue and A dark Matter is no exception.Amazingly crafted visuals and puzzles that are fun to work your way through, ADM would be perfect if it weren't for a couple of minor thing. First and foremost is the length, I'm a seasoned room player and I made it through in under 3 hours, which for a $30 game is tough to justify. I can see someone with less experience with the franchise and maybe VR in general might get a bit more out of the game but not enough for me to get over it.The second story based so if you haven't played ADM or any of the other games I'll conclude here, an amazing experience that I was happy to have paid for to support fireproof to keep making these bloody brilliant games but a pricey one none the less.SPOILERS AHEADMy second gripe is one I've had since Old Sins, it feels like Fireproof don't know how to follow up The Room 3. The teaser hidden ending of TR3 has had me waiting for the next installment in the main story of these games for four and a half years and the conclusion of this game with the seeming defeat of the craftsman worries me that there isn't one coming. The use of the craftsman as the antagonist in this game is excellent as returning player, as you see him trap many souls like he has tried to yours in the past. But hang on, if I'm playing as the detective, a new character, how would I know who the craftsman is, and the jump in platform means a lot of new players to the franchise will be starting here, robbing the defeat of the craftsman and the imagery of the last levels of a lot of their impact. It feels like a confusing choice and it's one that I hope my fears will be completely allayed of in the next installment of the franchise (come on Room 4!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, satisfyingly responsive, puzzle game with a story. The levels get better as you go (I especially loved the 'moon' level) and the puzzles are a good mix of obvious and challenging. There's a hint system that worked for me when I was utterly stumped.I'd definitely buy and play another one like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very very good! Great atmosphere and "be there" feeling.However, I needed quite a few hints during the game. Not because the riddles were too hard (actually they're quite fair and logical) but sometimes a new way of doing something is introduced without any explanation. As soon as you've found out (or opened a hint) it's like yeah...of course. Why didn't I try that in the first place?The only thing suboptimal is that very often it is unclear or not obvious enough which objects can be manipulated or used. Of course you can say "dude, it's part of the riddle" but from time to time it simply is *too* unclear (like flipping the organ pipe. That it is necessary to continue is obvious but HOW to do I didn't find out, had to check Youtube).It is the naturee of such games that as soon as you're finished you're done. Playing again will be exactly the same and not much fun since you know all solutions. Because of that the regular price is a bit too steep IMO.But anyway, great great game and hope there will be more.

_childDocuments_.review: I like The Room series, they're simple but good puzzle games. Check them out if you like puzzle games. As someone who likes those games and loves VR, I was intrigued when they made this game, which is a stand-alone VR game.This game turned out to be a disappointment. Its not bad, but it disappointed me. What disappointed me about it is that despite the fact that its a VR-only game made from the ground up for VR, it doesn't do anything to make use of and take advantage of what VR is capable of. It doesn't feel like a made from the ground up for VR game, it feels like an optional VR-mode for a non-VR game. It feels like a VR game that came out in 2016. The studio that made this is a good studio as they made a series of games that I enjoyed, but sadly they don't understand VR at all. Even when ignoring the lackluster VR elements, the game isn't as good as the other games in The Room series.Also, compare the pricetag of this game to the other games in this series. If this game took advantage of what VR is capable of, then I would have understood the pricetag being much higher than the other games, but like I said it doesn't. Plus the game's length is the same as the other games. So I don't understand it's pricetag.I do not recommend this game. Instead, play this series' main games, along with other VR games.

_childDocuments_.review: There are few genres that are as inherently well suited for VR than first person point-and-click adventure games. While other genres often end up feeling like throwbacks to an earlier time or experiments in need of further polish, titles like this latest chapter of  series feels refreshingly full featured.For those who are unfamiliar with the previous entries in the series, The Room is basically what you'd get if you made an H.P. Lovecraft themed version of MYST.  Environments are dark and foreboding, riddled with tarnished steampunk gadgetry and mechanical puzzles that defy the basic laws of geometry.  Most of the story is delivered indirectly in the form of environmental clues and journal entries rather than direct dialog or exposition, and generally involve a hapless Victorian who's gotten roped into playing errand boy for someone who knows far more about what's actually going on than they're willing to share. doesn't try to do anything to subvert the devs' established formula here, but rather uses the shift in medium to render their familiar unfolding puzzle boxes in a way that's far more tactile than they've ever been able to deliver before. The puzzles aren't likely to be too taxing for anyone who's played the previous entries, particularly with a hint system built in to let you get a gentle nudge in the right direction, but there's just enough challenge there to make you feel like you're having to work for your advancement.  Unfortunately this means the game isn't likely to take more than a few hours to get through and there's little to no replayability, but I didn't really mind that much. The environments you visit are well realized and varied enough to be worth the price of admission.As for VR comfort, I'd give the game high marks.  They're using a teleport system rather than free locomotion, which honestly fits for this game as the previous entries were pretty much all 3D slideshows, and there are options for both standing and seated play.  It's equally playable in both as it doesn't really make a ton of use of vertical space or require broad hand gestures, making it a suitable title for all room sizes and comfort levels.  Controller mappings are also handled more or less perfectly, though admittedly it's not doing anything too fancy with finger tracking or the like.  This is a bit of a shame in my opinion as there was one puzzle in particular where I would have very much appreciated being able to use the Index Finger tracking instead of having to rely on a fixed pointer, but I was also never fighting with the controls to get them to do what I wanted either.So in summary it's not quite a perfect game, but it's still got plenty to recommend it.  I'm hopeful this will be the first of many future VR projects for this development team.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I eas not familiar with any of the other "room" games the other reviews are talking about.This is a blast so far. The game appears to be separated into 4 chapters, and I am starting the 3rd one as of writing this review.So far the puzzle are just the right degree of challenging. You don't need to be smart to solve them, but you do need to pay attention to details a lot. I have used the hint system a few time that I was about to get bored and when I realised what I missed I was disapointed of myself for it was never that hard to find. Usually I was over-complicating things.The geaphic design creates an ambiance that is absolutely outstanding. I visually loved the intro and 3 chapters I have played so far.The story... well I don't care about the story honnestly. It's more about a pretext to do a bunch if puzzles. I have no reason to think it is not good, i just quickly learn that reading the papers was pretty much irrelevant the puzzle to I stop reading them.I am not sure there would be a whole lot of replay so value this very well polished game based on a play time of about 3-4 hours.The performances are also really great. You can fine tune the setting in the menu and instantly see how the changes impact the visual. This allowed me optimize it to play at 120fps consistently. So I'd say it is the only game so far that I have been able to get such good visual AND 120fps as most games I end up cha ging setting blindly and the end result is never as great.If you liked games like Myst or Obduction, this is for you.Speaking if comparable games. What makes this one so great is that you never end up not knowing where to go and what to do. (I must have spend hours wondering all over looking for something to do in obduction; not the case here)I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, 30 dollars for a game you can complete in 3 hours. How can I convince you to make that investment? I can't if you've never played the room before.I feel like this game is a love letter to the fans. Not a farewell, hopefully! Being able to do the classic room puzzles in VR has been amazing. Having these boxes and gadgets right in front of me, LIFE SIZE, was a surreal experience, and made solving them even more fun. I will say however, that's as far as VR lends itself to the game. It otherwise is just another room game and it seems strange to have the steep price increase... were it not for the story.SPOILERS BELOW! If you love this franchise and want to have this play out for yourself, just trust me when I say this game has a short but amazing plot.And there's only more to continue on, with shadowy agencies and corrupted scientists abound. If the next Room game is $30 - VR or otherwise - I'll spend that much in a heartbeat. These games deserve it with all the care that is put into them.So TL;DR - this isn't for you if you haven't played the other Room games yet. How about you pick them up? The first four are pretty cheap, and you can probably buy all of them in total for less than this game when they're on sale! If you love puzzle games with a rich atmosphere, then you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enthralled with games in this series on my iPad for a few years. I almost feel it has been worth the purchase of my entire VR rig just to play this game. The puzzles are fantastic as always, but the sense of immersion you get in their richly detailed environments just takes it over the top. Even having solved the puzzles, I'm inclined to play again just to see the atmosphere again. _childDocuments_.review: The Room VR: A Dark MatterBy Fireproof GamesGenre: Hidden-Object Escape-Room Point-And-Click in VR!Release: March 26, 2020-----So I just finished the latest The Room graphical adventure, only it's in VR! That's right, The Room VR: A Dark Matter is yet another in a long line of great point-and-click escape room games by Fireproof Games. And you do not use the mouse and keyboard for this, nor a tablet; instead you use your VR headset and tracked-motion controllers! And as you might imagine, it is quite immersive with this display and control method.Full disclosure if it is relevant: I used the Oculus Rift S with the Nvidia RTX 2070 Super, and I experienced no frame loss or other anomalies throughout my play. Fireproof most definitely handle the Unity engine's VR implementation like pros!The story line is similar to but also different than the first three in the series, before the fourth one went in a slightly different direction. You are contacted by someone who, if you played the third one especially, will turn out to be quite familiar, and if they are, you will know that they do not exactly have people's best interests at heart…So, looking through a police detective's eyes, on his assignment of investigating disappearances, you are tasked with solving various puzzles in various areas, and again you are granted a special eyepiece which enables you to see beyond – I think that's sufficient for me to say, just "beyond." To say much more would be quite spoileriffic, in my opinion. Suffice to say, if you have played the others, you know that you're going to be entering some somewhat surrealistic places and seeing more than you can see with the naked eye in order to solve the various puzzles you find.A technical note before I close up: there is no free movement, and no smooth turning. Fireproof intentionally designed the game like this, in order to be able to present puzzles, and your access to them, as efficiently as possible. You teleport among up to a dozen nodes throughout the various locations you visit, and certain ones are turned off as their puzzles are solved and it's no longer needed to go there. I think this is good, to avoid too much confusion. Also in the furtherance of that latter, the time hint system makes its return: within the inventory you can pull down a tab to view hints that are relevant to your current puzzle, and more are revealed as time goes on and you get slightly more frustrated.But let me assure you: like with all the other games in the series, it's a good kind of frustration. When the wall breaks through (sometimes literally!) and you solve a puzzle after gathering items and throwing switches, turning knobs and wheels and looking around for something you might've missed – for maybe 5 to 10 minutes on the more challenging ones – you get that endorphin rush, and it's a wonderful feeling. That's why I love these kinds of games, and that's why all keep on playing them as long as they're made.Thank you again, Fireproof! You have again teased my brain and given me those aforementioned endorphin rushes aplenty, and… No, I won't say it! Spoilers. Buy this game. Buy all the independently developed ones (or, heck, those that are released by big companies for that matter!) in this genre, whether on desktop or in VR, to let the developers know that we want more of them!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A great game and a perfect fit for VR as a medium, I'd love to see more of this! The story is great as usual, though the pacing was a bit off (the cathedral part specifically). I also encoutered a few minor gameplay issues like the left controller not working as good as the right one (no hardware issue). But overall this was a great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I love how you can examine the models up close like you were there. If you remember in the flat The Room games, you could look at objects in your inventory. But this one allows you to pull it up to your “eyes” and it zooms and scales effortlessly. The puzzles could be a little more challenging. I think the story is interesting and they even have cameo scenes of the previous games if you played them. The game is really really well done as always as I expect from Fireproof. The price isn’t bad but I was able to catch a good sale on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the other The Room installments you know what to expect -- atmospheric, a little spooky but not scary, puzzles that use a variety of mechanics, not too hard, relaxed pacing. All of that carries over *very* nicely to VR, and the developers put a lot of polish in as well: art, music and audio are impressive, controls and inventory are easy to use, automatic height calibration so that interactables are at the right level, works both standing and sitting, hint system if you get stuck, save slots so it's easy to share with others on the same machine. A solid franchise making a welcome appearance in VR, easy to recommend to anyone with a headset and I hope Fireproof is able to make a second entry at some point. Looking up at and listening to the rain on the second level was my favorite little piece, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: + Excellent hint system (I needed to google once though, when an interaction wasn't quite clear)+ Feels like it is made for VR- Some interactions are a bit weird with the controllers, and some stuff wasn't visible or clear enough (checking a hint I sometimes would say "I've already tried that!", just to go back, try with more effort, and then it snapped correctly)

_childDocuments_.review: Any game that forces you to play with snap turn and teleport locomotion is a no from me. But let me elaborate.  Cons:-snap turn-teleport locomotion-hard to follow story-extremely short ( you can beat it in 3 hours fairly easily, I bet I could do it in 2 but it's not worth playing again)-overpriced for what it is-extremely little replay value-You're a copPros:-The puzzles are fun-graphics are good (not mind blowing)In conclusion:This game is worth 5 dollars. There is very little content and very little going on in this game. This is probably a great game for someone who has never tried VR and you want to show them what VR is capable of without overwhelming them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the best if not the best implementation of VR escape room. I played it together with my gf and we had a great time solving the puzzles. The puzzle design are stunningly beautiful and well executed. If you own a VR headset and love puzzle/ escape room you will love this. To fire proof games please release more of the VR series we will love more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: All The Room games are great, but The Room VR brings a fresh experience to the series that makes for one of the best VR games available. All future The Room games should be at least VR optional. They translate over so well and it really enhances the atmosphere.Technically you don't have to play the other Room games to enjoy this one, but I would recommend working through the series from the first game so the few references to the previous installments aren't lost on you, and so you can enjoy the seeing how the series has progressed for a fuller experience.The Room games never miss

The puzzles are insanely well made and the vr aspect was absolutely incredible. If I could erase my mind to play this game all over again with the same feelings, I would do so, over and over. <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game, like every other The Room game, is just so well made. The story and sound effects are eerie and compelling, the puzzels are amazing (how do they come up with this stuff??) and the graphics are done just so very well. It's my very first game I did and finished in VR and I hope they make more of this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A nice looking "very extended escape room" puzzle game as expected, with puzzles in the spirit of the The Room series. I thought the puzzles were interesting, but not too hard. There were a couple of places where I was stumped for a bit, but the game has a VERY nice hint system, and I never needed more then the first general hint. I absolutely loved the atmosphere in this game. It's easy to scare people in VR, but this game was not scary and manages to just get the right amount of earie. No real jump scares, no enemies, and no dying. I was mostly filled with wonder when I solved a bit of the puzzle, and something new emerged. The atmosphere helps to make it feel more mysterious. It took me 3-3.5 hours to complete. It's a bit on the expensive side for a short game, but don't forget that 1: It is VR! the potential audience for making a profit on a game like this is a FRACTION of what mobile phone/PC market can give you, and 2: A lot of work goes into making these puzzles! In making them look nice, and themed, only for the player to spend 30 seconds with them and moves on. Pros:* Nice visuals* Nice puzzles* Very atmospheric* Good music and sound effects* Impossible to drop items (picking stuff off the floor can be tricky for some VR users ;))* Very suitable for all setups with motion controllers. Sitting/Standing is supported, only very limited play area is required. Cons:* Not too many interactable items lying around. Just the puzzles. This helps with focus on the puzzles, and prevents you from being confused by useless stuff, but limits immersion or presence. * Motion controller integration not great. Fingers don't respond to touch controllers, and some gestures are done automatically in context, rather then you doing them. This makes controls simpler, but again, breaks presence a bit. Being able to stick out a finger to press a button goes a long way. A controller button could be used on controllers that don't support that. * Only teleportation, to predetermined spots. Now this is entirely in the style of the other The Room games, but something to consider for this VR title. Conclusion: I played all of the The Room games on mobile, and enjoyed them a lot, and thisone fits right in. All things considered, I really like the game, and was not disappointed. If you like escape room type puzzles, be sure to pick thisone up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: While a bit short for the price, I would still say it is definitely worth it. I played on a Quest 2 and had no issues at all. Lots of interesting puzzles with a simple hint system if you start to get frustrated. The story in general is a bit confusing, but this is coming from someone who hasn't played the other games, so I assuming it ties in. If you like escape rooms or any of the previous Room games, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved The Room puzzle games since I took a chance on the first one and bought it on Android store. I highly recommend this game, it's a shorter experience (2-3 hours), but you will be excited, surprised and intrigued at how these puzzles intertwine with one another. The puzzles aren't too terribly difficult, they never have been and that's OK. I got stuck a couple times and only had to resort to a hint on the internet once. But the animations, the artwork the creepy factor are out-friggin'-standing. They took it to a whole new level in this one, with it being VR and all. The only downsides for me was: No free-roam explore...I was hoping to be able to walk around a huge pyramid of a puzzle and explore all different sides, but they compensated that with a turn-table. Which is fine, they had to make the game accessible for everyone, especially those who are induced to motion sickness!The other downside was not taking all the advantages of the Index controllers (or even the crescent oculus controllers!). I found myself really wanting ot just use my pointer at times to do stuff, but had to rely on an entire hand grip to find grab points and such. It's fine, once again they had to make compromises for all walks of VR devices. They definitely would've had to have made this game specific for the Index if they really wanted to use Index to its max and that wouldn't be fun for everyone.TL;DR:Seriously, the game is great, I'd buy it at full price for sure and support Fireproof Games. The puzzles aren't too terribly difficult, but you get a huge friggin' treat with the animations, artwork and the brilliant use of VR!!BTW if there is any Fireproof dev that reads this...were those live action captures of people or were those digital animations? The motion was very fluid/human-like! Great job nevertheless!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I have purchased all of The Room games on tablet and while they are short games, I have enjoyed all of them (and bought them as soon as they came out), however, I like the games on the tablet better as the controls for the VR one are a little out of whack when sitting on the lounge. The other thing I didn't like so much is that the developers seemed to get bored by the end and there is more porting from spot to spot and just picking things up rather than puzzles to actually figure out. I liked the game, but I would have liked it more if I had waited for it to go on special...I am not disappointed with spending almost $50, but I guess I expected more from this game since the previous ones had more content. Yes, I will buy the next one that comes out, but probably not at full price.Slightly disappointing, but I still enjoyed it
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room series does it again with this deep-dive immersive joyride of intrigue. As with the first three installments, the Room VR has all of the dark charm and mysterious puzzles you've come to expect from the franchise, but now with a whole new dimension. Although reaching all around for what is and isn't an actionable object is a bit more exhausting in VR than when point-and-click, The user can easily sink into the small worlds that the game has to offer, and so the addition of VR to their resume was a welcomed one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first VR Escape Room I have played - and I was very impressed. The graphics are beautiful and the puzzles are nicely paced and feel rewarding when they slot together. Some of the puzzles were ingenious and were never too frustrating. Some of them felt a little too easy though, especially towards the end, when they just felt like busy-work. The game progresses through several (I think, 4?) separate areas before they are joined together at the end and each has a different feel and puzzle style. It all works very well. It has an engagingly creepy atmosphere and avoids cheap jump-scares. It took me about 5 x 1 hour sessions to complete but to be honest there is almost zero reply value. So, wehil I doubt I will play this again I would certainly buy another similar game from Fireproof Games. Excellent fun. Excellent graphics. Excellent atmosphere. Only moderate value for money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an amazing experience. I absolutely *Love* escape rooms, and puzzles, so this game was right up my alley. There are certain reality bending effects that VR escape rooms achieve over the real life ones, and this game does the perfect job showcasing this. I wish the game was a little longer, but mainly because I enjoyed it a ton! So many cool effects, creative puzzles, and immersive environments that help give this game so much life. I would highly recommend it if you own VR, and love puzzles or escape rooms. Really hoping they make more of these games because I would love to play more stories by them!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, but 30 bucks is quite steep in my opinion. 20 would be more fair considering you can complete the game in 3-4 hours (depending on how fast you solve the puzzles of course). I waited for a hefty sale and it was well worth the sale price. It's a quality game though! Especially if you're familiar with The Room games.Environments and sound are immersive and controls were easy to pick up. The game offers optional hints if you get stuck. Easy to get all achievements in one play through. Looking forward to more The Room VR games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice escape room kinda game. Some puzzles were easy other puzzles you really have to think. I enjoyed playing the game. I took me 4h to beat it. I wish they make more games like these.I think its suitable for children as well. Things i didn't like, is the snap turning, i know why its there but it would be good if there was an option to switch. I played standing up, and sometimes i move too far away from my center, but when moving to each spot you get in the middle as your body not as your starting point so i had to readjust a few times by going back and forward.Sometimes the dialog was too fast to read.9/10! Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I like Escape Rooms in Reallife. The i figured, give it a try in VR. Well i didn't master it in the typical hour, but it where time spend awesomly. This Atmosphere is awesome and you could do riddles, you can do in RL. Graphic wise you can see it on the Screenshots :P But inGame, you get the Details and the Time Spend to create this game. Time very well spend and i had fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not stumped and you take your time looking around, it's just under 4 hours to complete.Note that there's a slider in the second area that stops mid-way and the developer had to add a FAQ on their page to explain it, admitting it could've been more obvious.I feel at this point that VR could've come a little further and that Fireproof Games should've aimed a little higher, not necessarily for more content, but for a little more interaction with things and more atmosphere. The puzzles are mostly just slide and place, which I suppose is the main gist of 'The Room' games, but more effort could definitely have been made. Anyway, if you enjoy the other games, then this is more of the same, if a bit less to do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this. Great game for dipping in and out of or for playing for a longer time. It's really well made, the VR scenery is brilliant. I wish I had stayed in a couple of the places longer just to look around. Very, very immersive.  The puzzles all interesting and help the story along. I hope they make more in VR. I would happily pay the higher price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Well done puzzle game with a touch of a slightly creepy atmosphere.Time: 5 hours- puzzle games- escape rooms- using your brain for some logical problems to solve- to solve a mystery without the pressure of time or a horde of monsters gnawing at yout heels whilst you desperately try to open a lock- expect fighting or shooting- expect to die (then buy 'I expect you to die', also a game I recommend)- hope for an Indiana Jones style game - no traps, sorry!- want interaction with people. you have objects and riddles onlyYou have in a location (e.g. your office you start in) some points of interest (your desk / the pin board / ...) you can switch between. These offer some few items to collect or interact with. The riddles have a fair level. Not too difficult, but not too stupid either (such as three buttons you have to press in the correct order). They can be solved applying logic. There are no traps, no reloads, no time limits, no red herrings. A game like a book: you can relax and enjoy a good atmosphere. If a riddle should be too difficult: after some time you can activate a hint.  I completed and enjoyed several real escape rooms. In VR, though, you have a level of riddles and ambiance not possible in reality. The game hands you that.The difficulty level was right that I never got frustrated.And: if you play it through, you automatically have all achievements and a perfect game. ;-) Sometimes I got stuck because I did not know what I should or could manipulate. It usually helped to have a good look around: some objects have railing-like structures or ropes, if you pull on them the object moves. (But I prefer that to games that automatically highlight everything important.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Quick romp through space, time, and whatever else is at play.  The puzzles are intuitive but not neccessarily push overs.  I kind of hope for more from the dev, as this is like a perfect amount of spooky for me, especially in VR. This was masterfully done, about my only gripe, is that I kind of wish the...parties at play...had voices to them?  I feel that would have added a bunch to it, but otherwise, this was incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you are an adamant puzzle player and have played the other four in the series then this is a must have. The gripping details mixed with the amazing plot and story helps bring this amazing world together. The lens's are much more than amazing while in VR and only does the mobile/former counterparts major justice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR is a great transition from mobile puzzle game to VR. The only downside being the price, which I would assume is due to the audience for this game being substantially smaller. You'll be met with the same quality of game found in the rest of the series, with unique mechanics that can only be achieved in VR.I certainly hope the cauldron puzzle gets a standalone release, reminds me so much of Harry Potter 6 for the Wii.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the series since the first The Room. Like others said, It's relatively short, i got stuck a couple of times here and there, i think it took me about 6 hours to finish it. Really enjoyed the new mechanics in VR and i hope to see this series continuing for VR. Keep it up developers please!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it!  I've played all of The Room games on mobile from the start and have been a big fan.  The attention to detail, story, atmosphere, and music were always top notch.  I was really looking forward to what the move to VR would bring and I wasn't disappointed.  If you are familiar with their previous mobile versions, then you should feel pretty at home with this version.  The environments and puzzles are setup as hot spots that you teleport between, much in the same way you navigated from place to place in the mobile version.
