For those expecting to freely explore full environments with smooth locomotion, might be disappointed in this, but they have kept to their original game design, just expanded into the VR realm instead of flat screen.  That's OK by me for this application.  Maybe the future will bring something different, but for a first time venture into VR from the mobile platform, it's really great.And the game feels really polished too.  All the mechanics, UI, etc. work well.  Very happy with how this turned out.Some might say that the price may be a bit too steep for a game like this.  It's considerably more than the mobile versions in the past.  But, VR is way more niche and it's a first time attempt at it.  I'm happy to support them and hopefully that translates into more content down the road.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The only games I have ever purchased on an app store was the Lego Star Wars game (it's an drm free version of the entire saga, that was a no brainer) and The Room 2 and 3.  I got the first one for free somehow and I played it like I played the 100 other escape room app games I had.  Hints on, casually.  But it only took me half of my first play through to realize that this was not another escape room/puzzle game.  The detail, the story, the simultaneous intuitiveness and complexity of the puzzles... it's on a whole different level.  Games 2 and 3 I payed full price and played with the hints off.  Sometimes there were sections I just couldn't figure out, so I'd put the game down and come back another day.  This game is finite. The solution to the puzzles, once solved, will always be a shadow at the back of your mind making subsequent playthroughs that much easier.  The real magic is in the first playthrough, so I make it an event now.  I turn off the lights, I wear headphones, I immerse myself.  The Room VR does that for you.  By the nature of the platform you are immersed in the world that the devs have created.  The controls and gameplay mechanics are just as intuitive and complex as the tablet and PC versions of the game, but being able to walk around this world... to manipulate puzzles with your hands... to shrink down small enough to walk into a padlock and solve its riddle so seamlessly that you don't even question it... this is how the game was meant to be played.  $30 is a lot for a short, one time play through VR game.  I bought Squadrons on sale for less than $30.  During Steam sales you can pick up like all of the Batman games for $5, you can get the whole series for $30.  What makes this game worth this high price point?  This is art.  There are 100 other fantasy space shooters and flying mammal-themed vigilante RPGs, so they have to price competitively.  There is no other game like The Room VR, so they can charge what they want.  And do you know what? When The Room VR 2 comes out, I'll pay $30 for that too.  I'd pay more, because I know that The Room devs will have worked their butts off to make it worth every penny.  You aren't buying a game, you're paying for an experience, and it's a unique, wonderful experience you can't get anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Steam showed me The Room VR: A Dark Matter because I played Half-Life: Alyx. I wasn't really sure what these two games had in common but nonetheless the game caught my attention. The graphics looked good and it was a puzzle game. I liked the idea but wasn't really sure if paying 30 EUR was something I wanted to do. In the end I bought the game and I'm really glad I did.I was immediately hooked. I loved the visuals, sounds and puzzles. I enjoyed the mystery and the story even it seems there were pieces missing that I was already supposed to know them (it makes sense since this game is a part of a series and this is the fourth or fifth game bearing the name 'The Room'). The Room is a series of puzzle games that were originally developed for Apple's iPad but later ported to iPhones and Android devices. The element making the games more interesting and intriguing is the 'Null' which as I understand it is an element from which things can be created. In order to see the Null the player needs to equip a special lens. Thanks to it you can see the otherworldly creations and solve puzzles from the Null and from our reality.The Room VR is set in 1908, Britain. You are a police detective investigating strange disappearances. You are led through the game by notes left by the Craftsman (who as I understand it is the originator of all the Null things you will encounter and who slowly became insane). In order to advance you need to solve different kind of puzzles and figure out what happened to the disappeared people.I appeared on the balcony of the police station I was totally immersed in the game. The atmosphere was great throughout the whole game - mysterious and sometimes spooky. I could even feel the scorching sun and sand beneath my feet (not really, but my imagination set me in a real Egyptian desert). The puzzles were fun, usually different and relatively clever. I enjoyed them even though some could be lengthy even though not hard. This is exactly what I expected from a puzzle game. It required attention to your environment, little bit of logic and some manual dexterity (since VR is not perfect).The environment was very well researched and well done. I felt like standing in the British museum when I was at the British Institute of Archaeology. The otherworldly places felt great, I felt like I was in a different dimension and I actually wanted to come back to the 'real world'. What I also found cool is that at some points you can enter objects and you need to solve the puzzle both inside and outside of it. I call it 'Detective in the Wonderland' mechanic. At the time I didn't appreciate all the sounds and physics because I took them for granted but after playing several other VR games I have to say that these are way above average. They kept me immersed and I never felt distracted by them (with few exception of sounds that are used by other games as well). I even played the organ or rather tried with two fingers.The game is awesome for sure but there were several things that bugged me. I wasn't fan of the game somehow centering around me whenever I teleported. The game uses teleportation system which allows you just to go to places relevant to the game. This limited movement is actually a good thing since you don't need to run around in frustration trying to figure out with which objects you can actually interact and with which you can't. The centering around myself rather than the center of the play area also made me scratch my head few times because I had to reach for an object which was out of reach suddenly (see in the middle of a real life wall). Walking blindly around and trying to stand somewhere so it centers in a way I could reach it wasn't easy.Next thing I'd probably do if I were the game's creator would be assigning a button for the use of the lens. It is great that you can change it from the inventory by using your hand but when you are doing a puzzle in both real world and null and you need to switch often this gets a bit annoying.I also had problems with reading all the notes and other text. That may be due to my eye defect which is quite rare or Oculus Rift not being the best for reading text. Watching my stream after I finished actually showed a crispy sharp grahics though.The next thing is something I'm not sure if it is a bad thing or not. The game is quite short. I finished it in 3 hours which included all the head scratching since I got stuck. (Often it was because I couldn't interact with an object that was obviously meant for interaction). When the game was over I was hungry for more. When I put the headset down though I realized how terribly exhausted I am. In the end I was glad the game could be finished quickly. It is still longer than other escape room games.The last thing I really longed was walking around and taking a better look at things. Unfortunately I was stopped by 'Attention! Please return to the play area' message. I was sad I couldn't watch animations happen from other place than the one I teleported to. I wish that in the next The Room VR game we will be able to freely walk at least around our real life play area while still being able to teleport to important places.As for the price tag. I found it expensive at first but after I finished the game I felt like they deserved all of the money. There may be a big difference between the Room non-VR games prices and this one but still I'd pay 30 again for a game like this. True, compared to a high price of Half-Life: Alyx and its 13 hours of game play it is indeed expensive. I don't regret paying this much for the game and I'd even tell you to just buy it for the full price (on sale it's a snap buy). For me it was totally worth it.If you like good puzzles and you also enjoy a very well done environment I can highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: They did everything to make this game perfect in regards to avoiding motion sickness. I also liked that the riddles were not too easy. It took me quite some time to figure out everything. The hints were mostly helpful, but sometimes the mechanics were keeping me from solving the riddle even though I already knew the solution. Nontheless I recommend this game to everybody who likes escape rooms and enigmas.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 4 non-VR versions of The Room (and loving each part), playing the VR version as well was kind of mandatory. Even though it's just under 4 hours to get through the whole game it felt longer and all in all very rewarding (I bought this on sale though). I especially loved the cottage setting with the cauldron. The atmosphere there is on point, lighting, colors, everything very enjoyable and immersive. The other parts I played on mobile (tablet) and while using objects is equally intuitive, they didn't use some of the more intricate control movements that I remember from mobile, so its very playable in VR as well. While playing the games in the order they were released in isn't strictly necessary, as the story part is more in the background in my opinion, I do recommend playing the games in that order, because the things you can do kind of evolve which each game and I know that some people enjoy even small references to earlier parts of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the atmosphere and the ambiance of the game. The controls could at times be a little finicky e.g. I couldn't always grip or let go of objects, but nothing out of the ordinary for VR games.The puzzles aren't hard, though I did have to use a hint or two when I had missed an obvious clue here or there.I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys puzzles and HP Lovecraft.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a solid VR experience. The puzzles are interesting and moderately challenging without being frustrating and the environments are well-crafted and highly detailed.My major complaints are certainly the short length of the game as well as a rather unclear plot that is communicated primarily through letters that the player must read. I don't feel those points substantially detracted from my enjoyment of the game though.I would love a sequel with more chapters and a plot that is more clearly communicated so I could be more invested in the story and understand  I was solving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the mobile games. When my wife and I picked up VR we always like puzzle and room escape games. Though we always missed the atmosphere and visual style of the Room.Thanks for making our wish come true and put the Room into VR.We really hope you will continue with the series in general and when you do, please don't forget VR! :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! Played since The Room first came out on phones. Got an Index and couldn't believe my eyes when I randomly found this game here on Steam. I had no idea! It's incredible. The only problem I had with it were that the controls were a little wonky sometimes and that it was over so fast, but I loved it just as much as the other Fireproof games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the other room games, but the puzzles are a little less impressive because they're more human sized. It's also a bit shorter than 3 & 4. I got this game on sale and it's definitely worth it!These are a few problems I ran into that may or may not be user error. Maybe they could be made more obvious or maybe I should just get good. -The organ bridge puzzle in the church had some unobious interactions. I didn't realize I could interact with the giant wheel that could spin so the bridges would actually be facing the correct way.-The clock puzzle at the church also stumped me. I knew the time to put on the clock, but couldn't set the middle gear. It looked like you could only move it left or right so I assumed I needed some other piece to let me access the middle gear. I didn't realize that the middle was an option. I wandered around for a long time trying to figure that out. -Didn't realize where the blood moon key went in the witches hut and wandered around for a long time. I thought the spot under the moonlight was a red button not a key slot. I didn't think they'd give you the key right next to the lock.-In the witch's hut they give you a tarot card. I wandered around for so long trying to figure out where it went because the door did not look like a slot. I don't know if I missed some visual cue but it annoyed me the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was really good. Lots of cool places to be in, with quality atmosphere. The game doesn't feel like a detour from the main series. Instead there are puzzles here that suit VR quite well, helping A Dark Matter stand on it's own. The story all pulls up with the others, so if those are your cup of tea you'll feel at home.I especially liked the intimacy of the fourth chapter. There are several actions that feel quite natural, despite the unnatural setting, and picking up the  was actually slightly unsettling to me. I would really look forward to more of that in future titles.I'll also say that even though the atmosphere can be spooky, the game does  spring any jump scares on you, which is appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A bite sized delight for puzzle lovers! Fireproof Games took full advantage of VR, making actions like opening drawers, turning keys, and examining ancient relics or throwing bugs in soup feel quite satisfying. While  isnt heavy on dialogue, it doesnt need to be. The narrative unfolds through eerie environments and cryptic discoveries, making each puzzle feel like a piece of a larger mystery. Solving one puzzle just pulls you deeper, until youre questioning if youre dealing with reality or something else entirely. Visually, the game is a treat. Every room and object is designed with a high level of detail that adds depth to the dark, mysterious aesthetic. Sound design was great too, the subtle creaks, whispers, and ambient music build a tense, immersive atmosphere that had me looking over my shoulder more than once. I mean seriously, I was being watched, .
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend The Room VR - A Dark Matter.With "A Dark Matter" Fireproof Games took its beloved franchise of puzzle games from mobile to VR, an experiment that has to be considered a resounding success. Previous games of the series did not rely on the clever puzzle design alone, but to a large degree utilized atmosphere to keep the player invested. Both, the atmosphere and the very hands-on approach to puzzle design, translate very well to VR, making "A Dark Matter" a very impressive and memorable experience. The game has about 3 hours of content. I think it is a bit expensive for that and would recommend to wait for a sale. The difficulty is quite a bit lower compared to the previous entries to the series, so veterans might feel disappointed about the challenge. If you are ok with the price and like a more beginner-friendly puzzle game experience or are mainly in it for the atmosphere, you won't regret the purchase. For a more in-depth video review see:
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The game has five levels (five chapters) and requires you to complete all puzzles in order to progress into the succeeding chapter. Each location has both unique puzzles and aesthetics. While the game is relatively short and can be completed in a few hours depending on how snappy you are with solving the puzzles, it will feel worth it to go from one interesting locale to the next, with a brooding, creepy atmosphere and relatively intuitive use of VR space with it's puzzles.The game does not allow you to freely explore each level, rather you must go from one puzzle location to the next within the map, as such the game is without locomotion and uses fixed point teleportation and snap-turn to have you jump from one puzzle location to the next, with an optional smooth turn update branch  An excellent seated or standing VR experience.The only downside to this game is that there is not enough of it, at 3-5 hours you will be done with no additional content or replay value. While I would consider this game a must-have puzzle adventure for VR, it may be prudent for others to wait for a sale below $30 USD.Absolutely add this game to your collection as soon as you can, it carries Fireproof Games' torch into VR flawlessly, from their almost decade long history of "The Room" series in non-VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointingly short and the majority of puzzles were fairly simple compared to others in the series. The  puzzles took me the longest to solve, due to struggling with the controls on valve knuckle controllers, not because they were complex and difficult to figure out. There also did not seem to be any puzzles that really took advantage of the move to VR, I can't think of one that could not have been easily implemented for a regular flatscreen 3D game.Lastly, besides taking less time to finish than the previous two entries in the series, there is no replayability here. There are no alternative endings or hidden puzzles. After playing the old sins, this feels like a step backwards for the series.This is not a bad game, but it lacks depth and has a lackluster VR implementation. I would not recommend this game even for fans of the series unless it was on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I have played and greatly enjoyed every game in the "The Room" series, so it is with great regret that I cannot recommend The Room VR: A Dark matter.  None of The Room games are very long, but A Dark Matter is remarkably ephemeral.  Given that it costs a great deal more than other games in the series, the difference is keenly felt.  What's worse, portions of the game feel somewhat unfinished.  The game's climax has an interesting setting but is notably devoid of clever puzzles.  One gets the impression that there were deadlines to meet and the game may have been rushed out the door.Additionally, likely as a sacrifice to accommodate lower powered VR setups, the games graphical fidelity has taken a pretty big hit.  One of the joys of the series has been marveling at the intricate, beautifully crafted puzzles, and to a certain extent that's lacking here.To sum up, the Room VR: A Dark Matter is game that suffers by comparison to its forebears.  Viewed solely on its own merits, the game is engaging but quite brief.  I would wait for a very large sale before I consider picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on sale and not sure if it was worth the price. 3.3 Hours with only 3 hints needed (because I was too blind to see movable stuff.)Some parts feel overly easy. A good bit of it actually. It really didn't feel like there were any head scratchers. Everything was pretty observation based, which makes sense for a VR game.I'm still going to recommend it on sale though because it was a pretty fun experience. But it is pricey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is very good made Puzzle VR game only i think its not worth 30 bucks sinds my boyfriend finished it in 3 hours.Fireproof Games needs to either, make the game longer or they need to put the price down a large amount.I still give it a thumbs up because its a very immersive game and a very polished game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.user: Me Huele el Pito a Canela
_childDocuments_.review: The whole surroundings, sound design, mechanics, and the slightly not too complicated puzzles makes this an amazing experience that if you have a VR headset, you MUST give you the pleasure to enjoy it. I was hooked right from the start, and I finished it in one go, not being able to put down the headset!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: As with all of "The Room" games, this exceeded the expectations set forth by its predecessor. The visuals alone are positively stunning and left me awestruck. I'm not talking about the graphics per se, but rather the animations and visual styling. I'm neutral when it comes to graphics anyway.More to the point, the developer shows a a substantial level of intelligence and creativity in their puzzle designs and machinations.I was rather saddened that the game was so short, but it can't be helped.My only real gripe is the ability to play the game seated. While it technically does work, there were several points during the game where I had to back out into the quest 2 menu in order to lean forward and recenter the view because your character stood too close to a mechanism and I kept bashing myself in the testicles trying to reach a crank or place an object.My suggestion is allowing the player the ability to pull back on the stick to make the character take a single step back to make room for such actions.10/10 My nuts grew three sizes that day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game I have played so far. I think "escape rooms" work so well with VR and this was just a fantastic experience.  Awesome this was made by a indie studio. You will like this game if you like escape rooms. Not a lot of movement required so you can do this in a tight space if needed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First off, another masterpiece by Fireproof Games. The things I loved about this game were the amazing and well put together visuals (especially  for a VR game), the excellent continuation of the story, the usage of the mechanics of this game, and lastly, the puzzles were clever and well thought out. I did also appreciate the fact that even if you didn't use hints, the designer's choice of only having your character interact with certain objects was a smart decision in my opinion. The only thing I would say negative about this game was that it was shorter than I expected. All I know is I'm excited for whatever else Fireproof Games has in store for the future of this series!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: (Review based on Quest 2 + Virtual Desktop)Been in library for a while and glad I finally gave it a try.  Cool atmosphere, doesn't require much memorization so far after completing the first two levels.  Slightly creepy, but definitely not a horror game by any means.  Puzzle difficulty is just right, and in-game hint mechanic is easy to use and access if you have short patience.  Overall a pleasant and well done immersive VR game that is suitable for pretty much anyone.  Look forward to seeing more from the studio.I originally wasn't fond of not having free movement, but I think the restrictive teleportation mechanic helps aid in solving puzzles limiting your scope of focus.  Game would probably be a bit harder with free movement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: In case the devs are reading this, I want to make one thing clear:I'm a sucker for this stuff.  If you keep making it, I'll keep buying it.  Mystery, Lovecraftian majick, Egyptian blahdyblah, escape-room puzzles, etc.  I love, love LOVE this stuff.  My only complaint is that I played this right after playing Obduction and it's obviously quite simple compared to that (which is quite simple compared to Riven, but whatevs).  I had a blast and I hope that they continue with VR and that they continue to make things bigger and better.Or not.  I'm totally good with shorter, simpler experiences, too.  This was SUPER fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A well polished and expertly put together puzzle adventure game.  For those into puzzle games, buy at full price and support the developers so we can get more of these, and everyone else, even those VR gamers not into puzzles, should still pick it up on sale and you will not regret the ride, and atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I am fairly new to the vr world so have not played many games. Found this game and decided to try it. BEST purchase I have made!! This game is amazing from the graphics to the story to the puzzles. I did not want it to end!!! Played over a period of three days and absolutely loved every minute!! I did not think it scary in away way, nothing jumping out at you or anything scary like that though there are a few creepy moments but nothing to harsh. Now I have to find a games that is going to give me as much  pleasure as this did, dont think I will find it though. Hope they have another game coming out soon!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really good, it was the first one I played with my new VR headset. The pricing could have been better as I finished the game within 3 hours yet it was worth $45AUD, I get it has to be expensive because its a pc VR game, but even the PC ports of The Room 1-4 were only $8 and $13. Visuals were perfect, audio was nice as well, but I feel like compared to the other 4 games the puzzles were remarkably easier. I loved the references from  as those two games were my favourites out of the whole series because of the creativeness. Either way, the game was still fun and creative, it would have been nice to add a bit of scares here and there however.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game.  One of the rooms I did great with only a few clues while another room I needed a lot of clues.  I did find 1 glitch that I wasted a ton of time on.  The final solution should not of worked.  The graphics are fantastic, the puzzles are creative and the game is very addictive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of The Room, I was of course excited to play a Room game in VR! And I have to say they don't disappoint, it's a good length for a Room game, looks great, and they take advantage of the medium. Recommended for The Room fans who have VR, or if you're not familiar with the series, all I need say is that it's a spooky puzzle game with eldritch themes! No jump scares.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this since it's been anounced and Fireproof simply delivered. This game comes with what made the three predecessors great: fascinating riddles in a very athmospheric lovecraftian environment along with a thrilling, mysterious yet conclusive story. All this has successfully been ported to a VR environment that allows for very deep immersion in a Rift room-scale setup, standing. Awesome and worth every bit of time we spent playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to express the atmosphere that this game builds. It feels like the Room but it's such a different game when you are truly inside and immersed. It is a short but fantastic experience worth the price especially for those that are fans of the story and mechanics. I would not call it a full fledged game due to its short nature and limited path, but it is a great experience that can give the player a glimpse of how future Room VR games could feel and function.If you are a fan, buy it so Fireproof can keep making games like this.If you are new to VR and want something different buy it.If you are curious about the game or don't fit on either of those, wait for it to go on sale (but honestly the price is not too steep for what you get).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great escape roomesque game with a slight horror setting (though no real scares or anything). It looks great and has great atmosphere, though puzzles are quite easily done (especially the teleport points instead of linear walking gives away a lot of where to look, and having seen those places it often is easy to figure at what to do). If you like a well crafted vr escape room, pick this one up on sale (30 euros for a 3 hour game is a bit steep IMO)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Although short and a little on the expensive side for the amount of time it will take you to finish, 5.4 hours for me though I spent a lot of time just looking around at the artistry of the game, I would certainly recommend this one for those who own a VR headset.  The story fits in nicely with the rest of the Room Series though you are playing a different character from the previous chapters. Other than a couple fragments of story or locations from the previous chapters, the story arc follows its own path and you don't need to be familiar with the story up to this point. Game Play is taken to a different level now that the puzzles are hands on.  Most of the time, using my Index controllers work great for picking up an object or pulling a rope or lever.  But there are a few spots where it does not quite work perfectly.  Sometimes my inventory window would be too close or too far away resulting in a little difficulty grabbing puzzle pieces out of it.  Or pulling a rope got a little monotonous after you hand over hand a dozen or so times, miss one grab and the thing goes the other direction as you fumble to grab it again.  The only other gripe I have is when you would sometimes turn around using the thumb sticks, your view point would not turn around a center and you would collide with an object resulting in everything disappearing with a "Return to play area!" message.  I was playing seated and had to lean forward a couple of times so that I could see again.  Mostly minor annoyances that don't detract much from the enjoyment of the game.I give this one a very positive thumbs up and I hope that if the developer revisits The Room series again that they will bring us another VR chapter featuring the detective digging deeper into the dark power of The Null.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really did enjoy the game, I have and always will support the move to VR, and even more so after playing this game. The controls worked fairly well and the graphics and sound, as always, never cease to amaze. While I would recommend this game as well as every game in the series, I have a couple qualms about this. That is the price of the game compared to the length of the game. Now, I completely understand that this is a very new environment for the developers and that, naturally, programming a VR game will cost far more than a mobile version. I just felt that I should make it be known that this game felt decently shorter than the previous installments, namely Old Sins, compared to the price point. I am done with my ranting now, just wanted to say great job to Fireproof Games for another awesome game in my favorite puzzle series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone does have VR I'd suggest getting this one. The puzzles seemed moderately difficult without being too hard, you're not going to be cracking the enigma code. Plenty of opportunities to think outside the box, I'm surprised I managed some of the puzzles out to be honest. Average game time is apparently 5-6 hours according to Google but I managed in in 4. Think of a single player escape room, except you're not escaping anything. My only concern on the Oculus Rift, was the button to bring up inventory seemed off. I kept pressing the button for the menu initially repeatedly.. Perhaps the options to change layout or re-keybind may be of use. Oh and my Achievements have not activated for some reason.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the game. As some people already mentioned, I would love if it was longer. (took me about 3 hours with some downtime for pauses.)There is one puzzle I solved which I am not sure what was the logic of it.Two of the puzzles added a new game mechanic 'mid game' and this mad things take longer. The best way to explain it: If you do an escape room IRL, you know your limits and usual physic. In VR, those rules are different and not always obvious.PS: When the key is in, you need to release it before operating the mechanism.Beyond that, it was a pretty great game. Full price is a bit much for the short duration.10/10 would like to forge and just redo it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric, with great visuals. One or two of the challenges are moderately tricky but otherwise not too difficult to keep making progress. I would say that the challenges are fairly well balanced so you do not get hopelessly stuck.On the slightly negative side it is a little on the short side and probably the easiest part of the game is the  last chapterOn the whole I enjoyed it very much especially as a first foray into VR and look forward to the next investigation..
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. Expect an atmospheric puzzle game. Puzzles are pretty straightforward and based on the delight of exploration (as opposed to obtuse or complex systems). At first it might seem like this was made to be a scary experience. Not so. The supernatural elements are there for mood, not frights. If you are nervous about being scared, don't be. Nothing's going to jump out and make you throw your headset off. That being said, if you like a creepy aesthetic it's also probably up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is actually really cool. I usually wait for sales but I wanted to give this a try and support them for doing vr, all I can say is I hope they make more!Edit (potential spoilers): After completing the game, my opinion stands. This is a really great puzzle/exploration/escape room game, and vr makes it even better. There were only a few parts where I was truly stuck, many of the puzzles were very clever. Many places in the game felt very dream-like, specifically when inside the organ. I could swear I've seen some of these places in dreams before, or something similar. Very cool feeling. The way they transform scale is a really cool gameplay element, and Im sure there are more ways they can expand on that idea. The visuals are great and this is for sure one of the most interesting puzzle games I've ever played. Really looking forward to more The Room vr games. Really a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! I lost track of how many times I said *wow, while playing this game. I bought this game because I wanted a VR game that I could play while seated. Room VR did not disappoint. Generally speaking I suck at puzzles and games requiring deductive logic and reasoning, but I managed to solve most of the puzzles on my own. The game will actually give you hints but most of it can be solved by using basic common sense. When I was in the middle of solving a puzzle and it *unlocked, I would jump every time. I was constantly thinking how *cool everything looked and felt. I hope they produce more VR games in this style as I will be first in line to buy them when they're released. 5 Stars!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth buying at a sale price for a few hours entertainment. Some very attractive environments and immersive atmosphere along with some clever and satisfying puzzles. i found in a few places it wasn't obvious how or where to proceed and for this walkthroughs will help to skip any frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another great The Room game and a brilliant example of the wonders of VR; I can't wait for the next game.What I'd like to see more of: more box puzzles like those in the first three gamesMinor gripes: changing the view mode requires entering the menu each time and since you do this very frequently, it ended up becoming a chore.Some of the puzzles require you to change view mode and make multiple movements just to get into them. This is bothersome enough, but when you're having to do this going in and out multiple times on the same puzzle, it becomes frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from the makers of the Room, no surprise that the puzzle aspects of this were fantastic. I do have a few minor complaints, but all in all this was a really fun game. I was very excited to see a VR title of the Room, as I’ve thought for years that this series would be a perfect fit for the medium. By and large this game delivers on that promise, but there’s a few areas which could be improved. I certainly agree with other reviewers that for a 3 hour game $30 is a steep price. I bought it on sale, and am glad that I did. My only other real issue is that the controls were a little finicky, fortunately however the game doesn’t require fine motor control at any part time to proceed (though some actions like pulling a rope do not function well and take some trial and error). The puzzle quality is on par with other Room games, maybe a little easier which is great since due to being so immersed in VR I found that it actually became more difficult to see an obvious hint on an object than on the normal Room titles. All considered this is a 9/10 puzzle game, and a great VR experience. Pick it up on sale for sure, or at full price if you need a VR fix.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Every small detail, every feeling of passing one trail after the other to learn of a dark secret, its THRILLING, no jump scares, no sudden scary monster's and other stuff, just a good VR Puzzle game, this is by far what a GOOD and FUN puzzle game is, its not gonna take hours to complete, its not gonna take minutes to complete. from the complex level designs, to the puzzle mechanics, its all EXCITING, this game is a MUST buy, if your into the detective and puzzle game like myself. I really do insist you get this game, it is really a 10/10 solid game and has been a big refresh on the occasional games that come out these days.amazing puzzles, amazing level design, no plot holes or jump scares, there's moments of "I don't know what that is, but it slightly terrifies me" but other then that, it keeps you on edge, scared to know what comes next but excited at the same time to keep going and figure out the mystery behind the story. 10/10 have played many times, and can't wait to see what else this company makes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really well done VR puzzle game, even though it was a bit short. It plays out similar to a Myst-style game where the puzzles make you think, just without all the excessive back-tracking and nightmarish note taking. Most of what you'll be solving is purely visual relying on symbols, patterns, and common knowledge. The design of the world here has a lot of time put into it, I don't think there was anything visual or audible that ruined the immersion even once. Very well done all around.I did get stuck in a few spots where the puzzles weren't intuitive. Like the mechanism to adjust the clock in the cathedral, it took way too many tries to realize it had a middle setting considering you can just go right past it. Also the moon-phase machine, again no idea you could rotate the moon-shaped ball at the top. I think the problems arise because almost everything you can interact with has some sort of handle or railing, the intuitiveness falls apart when those familiar mechanics simply disappear.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Please dont pay $30 for this. VR adds nothing to the game. Since it has predefined standing spots with locked degrees of view rotation, you're always just looking at a 2D picture of a 3D scene. It's also very easy. The puzzles feel like you're just going through the motions. "Move around a small number of predefined standing spots, each containing keys for the other spots, which you unlock one at a time. Continue cycling around the spots moving 1 item at a time until something ominous happens. Change scene." Oh and I guess there's a story in there somewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: it's a bit short, took me about 4 hours to complete it and I didn't feel like I rushed through it, but those 4 hours were very enjoyable. if you've played any of the previous games then the puzzle logic is quite familiar but for a VR title it ticks all my boxes. I could see anyone playing this as the movement is static teleportation and solving the puzzles with a bit of manual control is good fun. Quite a few clever perspective changes make it a great experience in VR. However the price is a bit steep for such a short game. In my opinion, if you played any other other ones and enjoyed it, you will like this one too. but maybe wait for a discount before getting it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games yet released, whether puzzle-based or otherwise. Some reviews refer this as an "Escape the Room" type of game, but that is really inaccurate. It's really an adventure game of the Myst-variety, where the main interaction is in fiddling with objects and the story is largely told through notes and occasional ghostly video. In fact, if you are a fan of Myst-style games and have VR, this game is definitely for you.Familiarity with the four previous games is not necessary; certain little bits of information may make slightly more sense with respect to overall story, but nothing critical as the game works quite independently from the others.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Off the top I'll say right now it is one of my favorite VR escape style games. If you come from playing the other Room games this one is going to be quite a bit shorter with the puzzles being not quite as complex. I think the animation and graphics more than make up for the short gameplay. This gave me the feel I always felt The Room series needed. I felt like I was actually there doing the puzzles. Now let's address probably the biggest drawback to this game, the price, honestly I think it is more than worth the $30 tag. A big reason why I feel this way is just my love for the other games. I'll most likely hop back on in a couple weeks for another playthrough. I highly recommend it, solid 8/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Having tremendously enjoyed the previous The Room installments this one had my interest the second I learned of its existence. The puzzles in the game and the settings seem to be made for VR, the extra dimension truely bringing the environment to life. And it must be said: puzzlewise the game is up to par with its predecessors, environment-wise it runs laps around them, actually allowing the player to walk around the puzzles. Absolutely loved playing it, and would absolutely love to see a VR conversion of the previous 3 parts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: As a former game master of escape rooms and playing all of the older "The Room" games (4 in total) I would say 23.99 € (usually 29,99 €) is pretty justified. I like to compare these kind of games with their real counterpart. In a real escape room you pay about 20 € (at least in my city) per person for 60 minutes. Usually if your group is pretty experienced you will beat a room under 45 min. So for 20 € you get 45 min of fun. This game gives you (kinda) the same experience as an escape room in the theme of "The Room" and you get about 2,5 hours (even more if you haven't played the older titles) of fun for 23,99 € (or 29,99 € full price).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I finally decided to drop the cash to get this game on sale, expecting an escape room like game in vr.And I have to say, this game does not disappoint! I found myself immersed from start to finish, and the only annoyances I dealt with were from my own fumbling with the buttons.  Overall, great experience, and worth every penny.  I might even play again because I particularly liked the fourth chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only room game I haven't finished since I sold my Occulus, but I plan on returning once I get another VR headset.  If you enjoy puzzle games such as Myst and haven't touched this series then just go buy them all right now.You might think because its a VR title that it is watered down from the other entries into the series, but that is not the case.  It is just as good, and in some cases better.Do yourself a favor and buy this title right now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: "The Room VR: A Dark Matter" sets a very high standard in both graphical fidelity and the types of experiences only VR can convey, exemplifying Fireproof Games mastery over the VR platform just as they have on the mobile platform with their previous games. Whether it's pulling out drawers, turning dials or otherwise interacting with objects, "A Dark Matter" nails the experience with a sequence of spectacular and truly unique puzzles. Where it falls short is in it's length, as the whole game spans just about 3 hours if you know what you are doing. That being said, the content is worth it if you are a fan of the puzzle genre or the previous games in the series, due to it's sheer level of quality.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. I have played all The Room games on my android phone and one on PC and I loved them. I was initially disappointed to learn that their latest game would be VR only (because I didn't have a VR headset and no plans to purchase one). Well, I picked up a VR headset shortly before Christmas and...wow, just wow! This VR effort is just everything! The puzzling was as fantastic as ever but now I am actually inside! The immersion and quality of visuals is simply stunning.More please....Edit: Seriously...more please - this game is too good!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game for £16 on sale, would say that is the perfect price for this game because of how short it is. I found this game absolutely amazing! The graphics and the effects were beautiful and it has a creepy, but really interesting story that keeps you hanging on the edge of your seat. Honestly, I am so glad I got this game and I have enjoyed every minute of playing it!I also love the fact that there's a hint section if you get stuck on a puzzle. Definitely worth the money. Has taken 4 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome games - 4k-ish textures like only Alyx and Boneworks. In fact I only know of 3 games that fully takes advantage of ultramersion textures and the Valve Index - namely Room VR, Alyx and Boneworks. This makes Room VR a must-have - and the very best puzzle game on the planet. Seriously. Really made me feel like Indy.Also performance is awesome, disabling SSAO (which doesn't mean much) I get solid 90 fps using res 200% with my oc'ed GTX 1080 and the Valve Index. My oc'ed GTX 1080 does get similar scores in the OpenVR Benchmark as the non-oc'ed RTX 2070 Super though. You don't have full locomotion in the game, but it doesnot matter and full locomotion would create too many possible locations and increase the likelihood of players getting stuck. Sound is great too - using Index speakers it really sounded like real rain in chapter 2. Also the Index trackpads are supported - really great, even if full finger tracking isn't. In short, this in one of the finest VR games ever made - if you haven't, you simply need to play this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This latest entry in the Room series is a great game in itself and VR done well. VR is such a natural way to play a game where examining complex objects from multiple viewpoints and then manipulating them is the core mechanic. The ability to lean and/or tilt your head to look at the side of an object (or even walk around it to see it from the side) adds to the fun.VR is core to this game and not an add-on. The inventory management works well, the interactions with objects (limited to those objects necessary for puzzle solving) are pretty natural and logical. At one point I had to reach into a hole to pull out a living creature, some of the puzzles were only solvable by crouching, tilting my head to the right angle and pointing in the right direction.You get around by teleporting to specific locations and it's intended to be played mostly in a static standing or sitting position, but I played it with a room play area and walking around things to look at them works fine, although it's a good idea to walk back to your original spot before teleporting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Right now the vast majority of the game reviews are positive and most of the negative reviews simply complain that the game is too short. But I haven't enjoyed the game at all. First the game wasn't immersive. Second, I found its point-and-click gameplay really boring.  Please note that I haven't played point-and-click adventures since early 2000-s when I was around 13. Also, I should note that I have played only up to the middle of chapter 3 (as far as I understand the game has 5 chapters).I'll start with the lack of impressiveness, since I believe that this part of my review will be relevant to more people. Few days before this game I played another VR puzzle adventure Red Matter, which in my opinion far better manages to be immersive. So I will complain about the aspects of Room VR that were in my opinion much better implemented in Red Matter. The movement in the game is restricted to  teleportation between few designated spots; the room-scale movement is of no use either since when you leave a small area (it felt like 0.5 meters in radius) around a teleportation spot the game stops rendering the world and shows you a warning.  The vast majority of puzzles felt completely arbitrary rather than grounded in the game universe. I have mostly played the second chapter, where for the most parts you are opening secret boxes that typically have multiple layers of locks and contain keys from each other. The only thing that was tying this to the story and surrounding were the appearance of boxes; otherwise, the same boxes could have been used in any other setting. Finally, the actions of the detective you are playing for doesn't make any sense (if you are a detective in late 19-th century Britain probably you would freak out when you realize that you are dealing with something clearly supernatural rather than just calmly go along) and the game doesn't offer any explanations for the protagonist behavior. Due to all of this I completely wasn't immersed in the games universe.Giving that lack of impressiveness there were at least two options why the game might still be interesting. Namely the interesting gameplay and interesting story. Since I played through less than a half of the game, I wouldn't be judging the story (I wasn't hooked but it is easy to imagine that it might got interesting latter in the game). Gameplay basically works like this. You clicking on different object trying to find which one are interactable and pickable as well as trying to interact with static objects using pickable ones (the latter I guess is more intuitive and typically it is possible to guess where you should put a pickable object). Also there are some logical puzzles. Puzzles might become more interesting and substantial part latter in the game, but in the part that I played puzzles were really trivial (and I haven't felt satisfaction solving them, unlike more dedicated puzzle games, e.g. The Witness). So for the most of my play I was figuring out what object I haven't yet tried to interact with. Obviously there are people that do enjoy this kind of gameplay, but definitely not me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping the atmosphere of the other The Room games, A Dark Matter proves to be an interesting and intriguing experience. While I don't feel its quite as good as The Room 3, it's still a solid experience. The puzzles require you to really think and pay attention to details. The controls can be a bit finicky at times, but it doesn't hinder the game. I highly recommend to any escape room game enthusiast and fans of the previous The Room games
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A very good but quite short VR puzzle game.  If you like puzzle games then I definitely recommend getting it at a sale, but for full price it's a tougher sell. Depending on how good you are at puzzles, you'll get 2.5-4 hours out of The Room VR for a single playthrough. There's no replay value since once you've solved the puzzles there's no reason to replay the game only to do the puzzles all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What's to say about the Room that hasn't already been said? They have some puzzles that are hard, but actually pretty easy, so you feel smart solving them in rapid fire succession while occasionally encountering the "thinker". Then maybe a couple puzzles that are total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and require a wiki so you feel like maybe those other puzzles weren't so easy after all, which justifies your self-evaluation as a super-genius. (The witch's orb, I’m looking at you). The ending is some sort of Bioshock Infinite shocker of an ending but the actual story is so vague and nonsensical that you really have to wonder what was the point - some other people played this game and also wikied the answers? A million dildos shoved up a million butts and the universe is an illusion? The room will never be mass market "Myst", or wait - maybe it has because you’ve made like a billion dollars on app stores-  but as a discerning PC gamer I say - either give up the storytelling or commit whole-heartedly. I'm pretty sure you guys could pull it off very well if you thought your target audience could handle it. Good VR title. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Longtime fan of "The Room" (Oh, Hai Mark) and I was not disappointed. The atmosphere is creepy without relying on jump scares (I counted MAYBE one, and that was probably less an intended jumpscare than a door opening quicker than a nervous man like me was expecting), the puzzles make great use of the VR platform and are interesting and fair--I would say "moderate" difficulty; neither obvious nor requiring you to take notes to solve. Plus, when you get stuck there's a helpful hint system.  Having just beaten it, too, I can say that those who pay attention to the plot of this series--especially "The Room 3"--will find the ending very satisfying. Keep 'em coming, Fireproof!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've play a few other games: The Rroom of the series before and I think they are okish fun game. This one tho because it's in VR brang me much more fun and excitement. I really had the feeling to do some kind of escape game from my home. It's not hard but it is really enjoyable. I would definitly buy more in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great atmospheric VR puzzle game. Not long, about 4 hours, but the puzzles are unique, mostly fitting its environments. There are some mechanics which work well in VR (playing with scale/size). If you get stuck, it has a hint system. Only issue I encountered was with one rope which had to pulled by both hands (swapping between them few times). VR on Linux has its issues, but I had no problems with this game. Played using Index on Manjaro.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game contains four or five different escape rooms that are all full of interesting puzzles. There are no silly "find the key"-puzzles, but rather unique and well-thought puzzles. The puzzles are therefore quite original. The teleportation system is made in an intelligent way, so you don't need a large space to play this and there won't be any problems with locomotion or motion sickness. Good graphics also, quite detailed. Music is quite calm and atmospheric. No jumpscares, that's also a plus. The total playtime is 3-4 hours (we did use a walkthrough to finish the game in 3 hours), so it has a lot of content (meaning, compared to other VR escape rooms).I'm totally satisfied with this game, it's one of the best VR escape rooms.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the previous Room puzzle games, this is an amazing addition to the series. For those who have not played the Room games before i would recommend them all, including this one.Some may complain due to the low time it takes to complete, but it does offer multiple save files for multiple people to play through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game. I honestly don't know if everything was an actual set with real props or built in a game engine, it was all so realistic. I am absolutely amazed. The puzzles were quite challenging and were really good puzzles once you figured them out. I will be buying this whole series and anything else made by this company. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience, totally in the same vibes as the first 4 games, just perfectly designed for vr. There were also some nods to earlier games (the one with the table thing). Extremely atmospheric, with perfect music to match, and thankfully, no jump scares or anything too scary. I had one minor bug in the 3rd stage (I think) where I was supposed to push a square handle into a mechanism. For some reason, I could only push it in with my left hand - I primarily used my right hand to do stuff so took perhaps 10 minutes running around until I brought my left hand up and ooops it works now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another marble in  the "The Room "series.  I highly enjoyed it .  VR is just the perfect platform for games like this!  On the downside : I do think this VR version of  The Room was too short, compared to the other titles in the series.  Finished it in only 11 hours and I did not hurry (and been  afk for a bit while running the game even) .   I think that is a shame.   After the witch hut, the rest of the game feels rushed. Not many challenges left after that.   Still recommended, but not at full price due to it being too short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: BEAUTIFUL!!! I love all of "The Room" games, but the VR experience was just amazing. To Fireproof Games: Please do NOT stop making these! Please, please, please! :) For everybody else: If you like these kind of puzzles, in my opinion, this game is the best in the genre. Overall the puzzles are not hard, but If you overlook something you might get stuck for a while. At least I did a couple of times. The graphics are just beautiful! The gameplay is as it should be for a VR experience. You pull ropes, turn cranks, etc and it feels great and immersive! I have only one complaint: The movement is the same as in the other "The Room" games. You can "jump" only on the places that helps you solve the puzzles. I expected a bit more freedom to move and look around. Probably that would've made the game a bit harder or at least longer. I would've probably looked around for hours and touch everything  that looks remotely interactable. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A really good vr puzzle game ( if you can pick it up on sale well worth it) - A little on the shorter side, would have appreciated it being longer then 3 hours.- As other reviews have said a little more interact with the set dressing items would have been nice, it kinda drags you out of the experience when you can just wave your hand through a curtain without it moving.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked: * Utilizes VR to its fullest, requiring players to pay close attention to the 3-dimensional nature of objects and their environment in order to progress.* Fun puzzles. * Great to play with friends! * The environments were atmospheric and well-done. I like the creepy ambiance. What I didn't like:* Maybe I'm just not galaxy brain enough, but sometimes it's not obvious how you need to physically interact with an object in order to progress. There's sometimes some guesswork involved in how to interact with objects.* The nature of finicky VR motion tracking and the required motions to move objects (such as rotating, pulling, pushing, etc.) is a little frustrating sometimes, For example, I might want to make a circular motion with my hand, but the motion tracking might determine I want to rotate the opposite way for a second. Not a major deterrent, but occasionally took me out of the otherwise immersive environments.* The game is a bit short for $30. That said, it's still a $30 well spent!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully polished, intriguing plot and puzzles that are tough enough to make adventure game veterans put their thinking caps on, but never relying on moon logic. This game is an awesome experience and definitely one of the best I've played in VR. I only wish there was already a sequel ready to play. Don't miss this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very good. Ever since I played the first The Room game one of my first thoughts was, "damn, I'd love this to be in VR." While I miss the series having more of an intricate puzzle focus with boxes that open up into more boxes with doors that open up to cool little slots and stuff, the puzzles are still pretty neat and have some element of that. Not a fan of the more horror direction the series has gone, which this being in VR cranks the unease and freakiness immersion to 11.Still though I'm glad they made this experience but yes, it is quite pricey for a game that will only last you about 4 hours and that's with me getting stuck and fumbling around multiple times. If you're not invested in the series, better wait for the game to go on larger sales as time goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is fun, but it's a little expensive for what you're getting. The game is short; it took me 3 hours total, and a lot of the puzzles are too simple, involving little more than just turning cranks, but there are some brain teasers. The story is also basically non-existent; everything is explained via letters you read with absolutely no voice acting or NPCs at all. The rooms you explore (four of them) are pretty cool looking at least.VR wise this game is beginner friendly. Snap movement, snap turns (although you can make it smooth if you prefer) and No motion that's out of your control.Buy this on sale only. It's not worth the full cost they are charging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the other games or like puzzle games you will like this game. I have all the room games and i really hope they make more of these. Do i wish it was longer yes but i still really enjoyed it. The game is beautiful. I bought it on sale is it worth the not on sale price I believe it is. I felt like i was in the the locations i was not disappoint. Just didn't want it to end. The only reason i got it on sale was I got my VR  set. I do recommend this game and I'm hoping for more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is why I bought VR in the first place, for experiences like this, being completely immersed in a fantasy world, following an interesting story and solving well thought out, VR friendly puzzles. I needed the hint system only twice and I'm not great at puzzle games, but these puzzles are so well put together and make complete logical sense. Fireproof really came through on this one and I am hoping for many more from them in the future. 10/10 Completely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the previous games in the series I was really looking forward to this. The puzzles are really good without exception. I really enjoyed seeing all of the puzzles in VR. I didn't really get stuck as such, but there were some drawings that distracted me. Presentation really is top notch. The game took me (Experienced in the Room games) 4 hours to complete. I would definitely liked a bit more!  I hope they bring out some additional DLC for the game. A quick note for the devs is to add object manipulation in your hands. In other games you could extend items or join 2 items to make another. That would make it fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fanboy for The Room series. I owned all previous The Room games on Android. I had multiple playthroughs to get all the different endings. I have waited a long time to play this game in its only play mode - in VR. I have bought the Oculus Quest 2 specially for this. The game itself is a little short. I complete my first play through in around 6 hours. I have used around 10 hints to complete. Maybe due to me using physical Oculus Link and was sitting down, some of the turning motion was not registering and I ended up stuck in a particular chapter in the game for quite some time. The game made use of the VR quite well, as if you are immersed in the environment. The movement implementation is OK. I am a little disappointed that I am not allowed to freely walk around in the environment. The item control is fine. It has added another layer of realism when compared to the non-VR The Room games. About mid way through the game I realised you can pull an item out of the inventory and walk around with it, this allows me to get through certain item heavy section a little quicker. I appreciated the nods towards the previous The Room games, however i do feel that those sections were too short. As in a single puzzle for each of the previous The Room games.If I have pay for this game at full price, I would feel I am cheated.Since I bought this during the Halloween sale 2021 with 40% off discount,  I am less upset but still feel something should be added to increase the game's replayability. Since I have acquired all the Steam Achievements for this game already, I am unlikely to keep this game in my HDD.TL/DRConcept *****Gameplay ****Replayability *Price *** (with 40% discount, otherwise it is a ** for me)Overall  ***However I will still recommend people who:1. enjoy The Room series to pick this up;2. enjoy VR puzzle / escape room games to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game I've played, and I highly recommend it to everyone. The value is amazing. For the price of Escape Room ticket IRL, you get the content of 4-ish rooms, and multiple profiles, which means the wife and I got our money's worth 8+ times over. Highly detailed and polished. Not a one-gimmick wonder like a lot of VR games. Don't let "Dark" in the title scare you aware if you're not looking for something spooky. While I definitely would describe the whole thing as eerie, nothing ever jumps out at you. Great fun. Loads of puzzles. Intriguing story. My best VR purchase to date.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game, and is definitely one of the more high-fidelity VR experiences available.  Setting is great, puzzles are interesting, and it just looks good in general.  One thing to keep a note of though is that you can finish this game in a single sitting (under 3 hours), so at its normal price it might be a bit too steep for some people.  Definitely grab it on sale, but even if you buy it for full price you're still getting one of the better VR experiences available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If y'all have access to VR you should get the room vr. The room is my favorite game series cus it's like all of my favorite things, it's a dark academia, eldritch horror puzzle game where you have an eyepiece that lets you see hidden things from another world. It's a super immersive game series as it is, there's a lot of behind the scenes world building but just enough to where it adds to the air of mystery the games have, and the VR game is literally everything about the games accentuated, obviously more immersive, the puzzles are super cool cus you get to interact with them with your actual hands instead of just clicking on stuff, the atmosphere which was already incredible in the other games is off the damn charts, one of the best gaming experiences I've had
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! I kept expecting it to have a jump scare but it never happened. Was just creepy enough to still get a 'dark' vibe. It really had me thinking a lot and I felt accomplished once I figured out each puzzle/clue. Best part about the game was I never felt motion sickness. There were a couple bugs that I recommend the devs fix such as the screen can sometimes look like everything is slightly shaky. Another bug was one of my hands got stuck in the game so I was only able to use one hand. Fortunately, you don't need two hands to play. Overall, really great game and I hope to enjoy more of these types of gameplay using my vr.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the previous games then you already know what this will be like; an enjoyably but not particularly taxing puzzle game, it works particularly well in VR, as you'd expect.I think the full price is a too much for the amount of playtime (4.3 hours for me including 2 short breaks), but a really enjoyable experience overall. Grab it on sale and play it in one shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game was gifted to me by a friend, I was worried at first as I am not great at puzzles but this game was such an exceptional experience in VR, truly enjoyed the atmosphere and pretty much all of the puzzles.  Definitely recommend this to anyone who wants to get swept up in a little puzzle adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I played this together actually, during the pandemic quarantine. She was in VR and I watched through the monitor, I would help out with clues / insights into what I thought we needed to do next, and she did all the in game controlling. All around it was a great time. Definitively helped me justify the Index purchase in her mind....
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed The Room series for its exceptional puzzling for over a decade now, previously just playing on dark evenings in the winter on a tablet.  Let me tell you that being inside the experience while playing in VR just makes an amazing experience SO MUCH better.  I can't recommend this enough and thoroughly enjoyed the adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the past "The Room" games, this one is just as good as the rest! Super immersive in VR and rich environments felt like I was actually in a real life escape game. My only gripe would be that it felt somewhat short, as I finished the game in just under 3 hours, but I still think it is totally worth getting, if just on sale for ~$20.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's the Room... in VR. It has all the detail, charm, and accessibility of the originals wrapped up in a nice VR package. Interaction doesn't feel as good and physical as it could, but that is a side product of facilitating the escape room type gameplay - extraneous detailed interactions detract from the actual objective.It makes up for this with the rest of "The Room" package, with impressive environments, good audio design, and most importantly, engaging puzzles. The story is interesting enough as well, and each area feels unique with a variety of mechanics.I recommend picking this game up on sale, as the playtime is rather short for its full price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to try a puzzler in VR. i'm not a fan of "in-your-face" or scary stuff so I made sure to check the comments. While there are some potentially creepy things, it's mostly the atmosphere. There are no jump scares or anything like that.Puzzles were nice and they generally make sense after a few tries.Audio and graphics were good but not exceptional. I think it's fine for its genre.Price point is a bit tricky. I finished it in a little over 5 hours. 30 euros may look like on the pricey side, but if you compare shooters being full-price for 10 hours of gameplay, it's fair, I guess. I would recommend getting it in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing, took me a while to get the game since I just got a head set, but I have it now. Being new to VR I was absolutely blown away by the experience in every way. The level design was detailed and fun to look at, I got to experience The Room in ways I wasn't able to in the previous games. The puzzles were interesting and well thought out as usual. The sound I wasn't able to fully experience because I was using the Oculus Rift S on board speakers which are trash, but I'm sure the sound was great just like in all of their other games. I found it so fascinating being able to look around the levels at the detain and interesting things in the environment. The only complaints I have with the game is it's length and that I had to buy a VR headset to be able to play my favorite puzzle franchise. The length I feel was this way because they were trying something new and didn't want to get in too deep or something, regardless, the game is great from start to finish even though it's only around 3-4 hours. As far as the VR headset goes... I am super happy that they are going in this direction, they did one hell of a job on this game and I hope to see more just like this in the future as well as more of the standard The Room series. Great job Fireproof Games, you have yet to disappoint me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game even more than I loved the mobile games. I really hope they continue to make more in VR. They're short; I completed it in one sitting and I was sad it was over. The plot is minimalistic but it makes me want more, it has some H.P. Lovecraft vibes that I just absolutely adore. 10/10 amazing job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Classic escape room puzzler.  Great locations, art, and sound effects along with nice puzzles and interaction. A thin story to pull you through, nothing complicated, but enough to hold the various scenes together.  Only two complaints:  I thought the puzzles a little too linear.  It never felt like I had more than one puzzle to work on, or several avenues to explore... you'll run into boxes and levers and things that you know need to be solved, but the solving is pretty much all linear. Solving one gives you a piece to solve the next, etc.  And second, I thought the ending could have been a little more dramatic... there was good lead up to it, but then the enemy is just defeated. Maybe some improved audio at the climax, such as a blood curdling scream, would have helped. In any case, these are minor complaints. I enjoyed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Always loved The Room franchise and being a fan of VR was looking forward to this.  This was so much fun, very atmospheric and the graphics are simply sublime.  Everything in this game was done with so much care and detail, the puzzles were spot on.  Also I did stop to play classic 80's Depeche mode songs on the church organ, but that's just me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Having played all of the prior versions of the app, I was super excited to here they came out with a new game in VR. The quality of the game and puzzles did not disappoint and I enjoyed immersing myself more fully in its familiar world. Experienced puzzlers can get through in 4 hours or less but it was well worth it (and the ending left me with a sense of awe/wonder).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Like all the other The Room games made by Fireproof Games, this is a very good puzzle game made even better by the fact you are in VR and physically (in a way) interacting with the puzzle. The sounds and environment are great to the point I jumped in real life when one of my cats knocked something over and I thought it was in the game. If you love puzzle games and VR, this is the game for you. I am disappointed, and glad, at some missing jump scares that could have happened.
