The game isn't meant to be a horror game, so I am not going to hold the missing jump scares against them. I would love to see more of these games, that includes the VR ones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game.  If you've played any other games from The Room series, this is much the same.  So if you liked those as I did, you will absolutely love this.  If you've never played this game, its basically like a VR version of a puzzle box mixed with an escape room.  There are all these little keyholes and hidden drawers and knobs in every scenario you find yourself in.  The world the developers created is sort of steampunk/1900's era looking and its beautiful.  All these fun little gadgets to play with.  Wow that was fun.  I wish it was longer.  Dev's please keep doing what you are doing! I want to play more of these games!! So fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the price. Buy it. Length: about 5 hours. Node-teleport only. No free roam, but it's ok. It keeps you focused on what's important. If you're on the fence because of price, buy it. It's what held me off for a while, but I can tell you now these guys deserve it (if they promise to make more!). This is 4 high quality environments and bonus area after. Lots of interaction and it's fun to play. Well done, Fireproof Games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes very good use of VR. It makes the interactions with the environment feel natural for the most part. The puzzles and scenes were great. The game is not very long. I played for 4.3 hours before I completed it. I wish there was something extra to go in the game one you complete the story. Like extra challenges. Without that the game has no replay value, unless you want to enjoy the view, which is a bummer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: very much enjoyed this gamethe room series has been one of my favourite puzzle games for years, and this one did not disappointi especially liked the interactions with the ropes and piano/organThis was my first VR game where it required the character to move (beat saber doesn't really count to me) and despite the motion sickness forcing me to pause every few 'steps' I still thoroughly enjoyed the experience  I recommend this game to all my puzzle loving friends who have VRthough if like me this is one of your first games I would recommend keeping a bucket nearby
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I have played every game in The Room series, and this one holds to the same quality as the others. I was very excited to see the email for this game's release in my inbox. A few nitpicks, if any. I take a trial and error approach to this game, as  I get to absorb and understand the world and touch everything. Sometimes I felt a little lost and I felt the piano puzzle but the intricacy of the controls to the test.I understand that this is a VR game and it probably took a lot of work for you guys, but I finished this game in three hours. Due to its nature, I am likely to never reopen the game until years from now or to let one of my friends play it. I do not feel this experience is worth $30. I spent $10/hour to play this. I feel a more reasonable price may be  $15 or $20, but I also understand the company has to make money. Other than that, the game was fun. I await for the next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible.Pretty much all you need to know.Sure 30$ for four hours is a bit steep, but it's an experience, not just a game, and totally worth it.The game has about 5 rooms.First room - really nice, not that complex, great to start off with.Second room - Really ups the scale, with really big puzzles, and a big mysteryThird room - My least favorite out of the bunch, had some fiddly mechanics, and some repeating "puzzle" which got old after the second time, as well as a couple of puzzles with such small details, you miss them easily.Fourth room - The best one, really nice puzzles, everything makes sense, a masterpiece.Fifth room - Don't know if you can call it a room, because it's so short, but it ends the game in a really nice and pleasant way.10/10, worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The previous installments of this game had me hooked, and I was glad to see that there was a VR version of this game. The devs did quite a nice job with it. It is a bit shorter than the last two installments. The levels were isolated like the first two installments, but that may have been better for VR. The puzzles had a good flow, and I rarely got stuck, though there were a few that had me scratching my head for a bit.I think in some ways the VR gimmicks were done quite well, and in other ways I think there is room for improvement. You could not interact with items in your hand/inventory, which is a standard trick in this franchise. They found a good workaround for this, but it would have been nice to pull an item from your inventory and interact with it with your other hand.I wish the lens had been used a bit more, but the new lens types, and all the others make for a nice experience. I appreciated the throw backs to the other games as well. Definitely a great game and worth playing. Asking price is a bit steep, though it is certainly a quality product. I'm sure the price is accurately reflective of the development effort, but it does seem steep for about 3 hours of game play. Overall, I've been very satisfied with the franchise and I'm glad to support the devs in hopes for more of these games! Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing The Room series because of this game. I saw the teaser for this VR game and just had to have the full experience. So, I played the other installments and finally got to reward myself with this visual treat. The puzzles are trickier than the previous games, but the layout of the game is so amazing, I hardly even cared when I was playing. I loved the interactivity of getting to pull on ropes and lift things. Everything's so mystical and awesome, it's like being in an Indiana Jones film. I would love to play more games like this. I would also like to see the genre expand from seek-and-find to something with some NPC interaction. Not complaints, just wishes. This game really is fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow -- this is the best VR game that I have ever played.  It is essentially a series of puzzles, distributed across several settings.  The setting are larger than a room, and have a common theme.  You can play for hours without getting motion sick due to the point and hop movement.  The settings are immersive, and the puzzles can be solved without using hints -- though hints are available in game.  The attention to detail is excellent.  This game occasionally goes on sale at 25% off -- which is a good deal, though even full price is O.K.  I hope the developers release another game like this in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! Just once though I'd love to see them make a room game where I can actually walk around in VR properly without fading in and out every time I jump to another spot.  That fade gets annoying on the eyes fast. I hope they make another one and let people walk around and grab stuff. That would be just the near perfect experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Since I had already played all The Room games (1-4 at the time), I put this on my wishlist as soon as I saw it, - and purchased it as soon as it went on sale.  It's well done with just minor differences between the originals and the VR.  The immersion into the game world is excellent except I kept wanting to walk around and look at everything.  Not a big deal as you can't walk around in the original games either.  Lots of fun - only got really stuck on 1 puzzle (the pipe organ). Thanks for a really fun experience - 6 hours for about the price of a movie ticket is just fine with me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A step backwards from Old Sins but the gameplay was on point. Very much enjoyed the experience on my Quest 2 and would recommend it to anyone intrested in puzzles or escape rooms with a decent push on story. I loved how the last chapter had a ton of pieces/throwbacks from the previous 4 games. My personal head canon is Abigail is the Witch even tho Firepoof said stated "she sleeps with the fishes." during their AMA.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A nice treat to have a new The Room game in VR! Never had the time of my life pushing, pulling, and turning handles. The unique aspect is how it uses the lenses from previous games, so there's a trickery of depth in place. However I wished there was detailed item inspection. I also felt like there could've been more interactivity with objects. Overall despite the flaws, this is a must-buy of a VR puzzle game especially for previous fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So good, one of the best VR games I have played so far. Really nice graphics, really engaging puzzles including one of the coolest and most original/fun puzzles I have ever come across (no spoilers :p). I got it on sale and definitely worth every penny. It is quite short but they packed in quite a lot. Go go go!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've cleared maybe half of the game so far, but I really like how it's implemented. It's not particularly groundbreaking, but solving actual physical puzzles in 3D feels fun and a lot more direct than the adventure games of old where you just click item on thing and watch the hero do the action. I think VR is fertile ground for the further development of games of this nature and hope to see a lot more in this vein.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of the game is really well done, but I completed the game in less than 2 hours. If the game had more difficult puzzles, I would recommend the game. If you want to play a simple puzzle game that doesn't really benefit from being on VR, get this game. Otherwise, you should save the 30 bucks for a game that will certainly be more worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: (Index user) Top 5 of all VR titles I've played, and easily a solid 9/10 for me!An incredible VR experience, it feels perfect for this style of game (Red Matter, I Expect You to Die, etc) and The Room series especially. My only gripe is that it is shorter than the other Room games but since it's a made for VR title, I can give them a pass here. If you've played the previous The Room games, this takes place after 3 but before 4 (I believe) and explores the world even further. It's honestly so incredible, I started asking friends who have never played VR to come try it. Teleport movement to determined locations, so I never got motion sick, and while there are plenty of creepy parts, I don't recall any jump scare gimmicks.Price is a little high for a VR title and, honestly, that held me up on getting it initially. After playing through it, I was fine with the pricing because I would have paid about the same amount for 1 hour in a real escape room, and my friends can come try it as well.Also, please Fireproof, make another VR title like this! This was so good! I've been chasing this high ever since!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: At this point it's pretty clear The Room will not return to the puzzle box formula that made the earlier games so good. The Room 4 and A Dark Matter are both mood piece escape rooms.The horror element is better than ever. The sounds and feeling of eldritch things watching you navigate virtual reality is just excellent. The mysticism is largely lost thanks to very distinct and abstracted puzzles. Many solutions are a matter of finding the right item or doing a line puzzle rather than tinkering with non-Euclidian contraptions from parts unknown. This is a different take on The Room, just as the fourth game was.As the fourth sequel, it revisits elements of previous games in a nod to all the good times exploring the otherworldly. Definitely a game to experience if you've followed the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of escape rooms (real life or otherwise) and The Room games in general, you will love this one! The worlds are beautifully designed and the puzzles are fun. This is, hands down, one of the best VR games I have played and the first VR game that I actually finished! It took me about 6 hours but I really took my time in each world. I only wish it had been longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an instant BUY!  Playing this game reminds me of all the times I played the mobile versions 1, 2, 3.  I wished this could be a VR game and here we have a VR game.  It is just as wonderful as the room series for the mobile and  PC.  Menu design, only teleport option are set in a way that it guides and enhances your experience without the frustration of dealing with glitches introduced by other aspects of VR.  This game is made to be just that!  It is a good experience, graphics, sounds and  gameplay are just excellent.  Don't mind the amount of time, in my profile, i played this game on another pc and am thoroughly enjoying this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games can be a terrible fit for VR unless the developers nail it, and in this one, they nailed it.  No one is surprised by that, at least not anyone that played any of the 2D The Room games but the same complexity is brought into VR in expert fashion.  Using your lens to hook up the serrated saw blade to cut the rope to drop the weight onto the etc etc etc (but in VR) is really great.  The game doesn't overstay its welcome, tells a cool story, and the sound design is incredible.  This one is on my short-list of VR puzzle games that get it right along with A Fisherman's Tale, GNOG, I Expect You To Die, and The Curious Case Stolen Pets (and a couple others).  However, none of those are really on The Room VR's level when it comes to straight up classic puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game follows the same principles as the regular non-VR versions and enhances them in a very good way. The design is as always wonderful and clear. It looks amazing in VR. The puzzles themself are balanced in a way that they are in the perfect spot between too simple and too complicated. They are all solvable by applying logic. It's fun to interact with those puzzles objects in VR as the controls are intuitive.The only bad aspect about this game is the time to complete it as it with most VR games. Nonetheless, I can fully recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences I have had. The game is just as puzzling as the other games in the series, but this time you can do it like you were there irl. I would rate this in my top 5, among Project Cars 2, Phasmophobia, Boneworks and Kingspray Grafitti. Loved the graphics, sound and all. If I could wish for one thing with this game, it must be a little longer gameplay. The Roome VR: A Dark Matter was finished in 5.4 hours (taking my time to look at everything), but it is still worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was surprisingly good. Went in this with mixed feelings, and in the beginning felt like the restrictive hotspot bases locomotion would be a deal breaker to me. But after a few Minutes this game caught me in it's detailed immersive world. This is by far the best seated VR experience I have ever played. I would recommend this game to anybody who enjoys escape room styled puzzles. There is only one downside after only 3 hrs of play you are left with a longing for more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one thing I could fault The Room VR for, it's sticking too close to its roots. The VR implementation suffers a bit, because of this; one would think a game titled 'The Room' would be a perfect fit for a roomscale puzzle adventure, but instead it plays largely the same as its traditional predecessors, making you teleport from one fixed point to another and never letting you stray too far from them (walking at all, in most cases, will lead to the game simply guiding you back into place). Similarly, most everything that isn't important is fixed into place, and without a cursor it can be difficult at times to tell what is or isn't important. But while these may frustrate those who are new to this franchise, and unaware of how it usually works, its close adherence to the established formula also makes it as good of a VR title as you would expect. The environments are just as gorgeously rendered as they've ever been, making it one of the best looking VR games I've played, and the things that are interactive have every bit of the trademark physicality the series and its many strange mechanisms have become known for. Every puzzle is filled with things to get your hands on, rarely settling for a simple point-and-click solution, and it works better than ever in VR. If you've kept up with the series to this point, you can probably already imagine how much fun it could be, and your imagination is likely pretty accurate.The story, in the end, was what surprised me the most. Being a VR-exclusive title, I fully expected it to be something 'safe', a spin-off story that could easily be skipped by those without a headset. Instead, it cements itself fairly clearly as a main entry game; the story is presented in a way that makes it just as easy for newcomers to pick it up and get invested in the world, but there's a lot here for fans who have been interested in its lore for the last four games as well. For $30 I would say there's somewhat of a VR tax, given that the game is shorter than the much cheaper previous games (it lasted me about four hours), but it's certainly worth playing, sale or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasant VR puzzle game. The puzzles are not difficult, but the environments are atmospheric and lovely to look at. The object manipulation feels very natural and adds to the feeling of immersion.Movement is not free so you must teleport to specific spots. My only gripe with this implementation is that the game does not account for the direction you face, so you often teleport and rotate to face a predetermined direction, rather than teleporting and continuing to face the same direction.Completed in 3 hours of play. I haven't played a VR puzzle game before, so this was a lovely introduction. For a second game of similar quality and length I wouldn't spend the full £25, but would eagerly pick up a similar game on sale. (But for what it's worth I got this and HL Alyx at the same time, and this is the game I've played to completion)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of this series for quite a while, and was really excited for a VR sequel. Having just finished the game, I think that Fireproof did a fantastic job of translating the gameplay from the iOS apps to VR. The puzzles are structured similarly to the previous games, but still very creative and engaging. The static teleportation nodes help to make the experience more familiar to returning players of The Room, but I did miss the freedom of movement that I've become used to in VR. However this didn't take away from the experience any, and I appreciated the authenticity. The puzzles were perhaps a little bit too easy, but this is coming from someone who knows the series well. I never got super stuck, and most of the time was able to breeze through a chain of puzzles in one go. I think there's definitely room for more complexity and more interactivity with VR puzzles, which this game seems to just scratch the surface on. I hope if a sequel is planned on this platform, that it makes use of physics interactivity and full body movement.The storyline has always been quite cryptic, and this is no different. However the pacing and story do keep a tangible thread, and wrap up with a satisfying ending. It does feel as though you're digging deep into something ancient and powerful, that's only barely understood. The game is however, a little bit short for $30 in my opinion. The Room series has never been super long, they aren't RPGs after all, but I know I would have definitely enjoyed and been more satisfied with an extra hour or so of gameplay (DLC?). As a returning player, it took me around two or three hours without a guide but using hints. Brand new players might take a bit longer if you aren't familiar with Fireproof's particular flavor of puzzle solving. Something more like a five to seven hour game might be more worth the price tag, but I don't feel like I wasted my money. Just know you can probably finish this in an afternoon.For me, the best part of The Room is always the atmosphere, which I have loved since the first game. I can say the Fireproof are the only studio that has really done Lovecraft right, which is definitely saying something. I had similar high expectations for this title, and was absolutely not disappointed. It's spooky, it's mysterious, it's old as balls. The visuals are top notch as always, and the sound design does a particularly good job of immersing the player. I'd love to have the witch's hut as a SteamVR Home Environment. All in all, I think Fireproof did a great job with this first VR title, and I'm really excited to see where the series goes from here. With only a little let down with the length and puzzle difficulty, this is definitely a must for fans of the series and fans of VR. Definitely give it a try and support Fireproof!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Really good atmosphere which gave me goosbumps a couple of times. Maybe a little bit too easy and short because of that, but to see it positively, solving most riddles in a continues flow was a nice feeling and they didn't feel too easy at the same time.Glad I bought it at 50% for 15€ because I think 30€ is a bit much for a ~3h game with not much replayability because once you were through you know the drill and its not that difficult even on the first run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: So far it is great! The only issue is controls kind of are crap. There should have been two types of grab, one whole hand, and one the index and thumb. It doesn't look feel right when what you see is the thumb and index finger holding something but you are grasping with you middle, ring, and pinky finger.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an experience out of this world! It brings the cool puzzles and interesting mechanics of the previous games in a vr format that allows you to experience even more and see all the small details of this game! One thing I would have loved to see was full finger tracking support! But that's not a game breaker!9.9/10 would play again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable puzzle based strategy.  Keeps you thinking and if stuck offers some good hints to get you going again.  Not super great for a small playspace /sitting arrangement, (even though it does have the option). In a larger space it would be better, as the option to do a bit of "free look" around, aids immersion.Well, finished the game, very enjoyable. It kept my interest throughout the gameplay.  I bought it specifically for VR, but now maybe I'll get some of the PC based "Rooms" and see how they go.Hopefully there will be a followup VR title as I thourght the concept is really well suited to VR. Particularly if the free movement aspect is pushed a bit more. Lots of really good interactions during the puzzles and not so terribly complicated that you lose interest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this is actually my very first proper VR game and I enjoyed it all the way through! I always like the ROOM series but this takes the game to a whole new level with the VR experience. The puzzles are just about the right difficulty, good atmosphere spooky enough but not jumpy scary. Story is a bit predictable but all the rest makes up for it. I would recommend buying this game when it's on sale because it's a bit short and overpriced compare to the rest of the ROOM games. Overall, it's a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all 3 of this games predecessors and all I can say is w0w. The environment is amazing, and I loved how they incorporated the same navigational mechanics and feel to this game as they did from the previous games. I am new to VR and actually got a headset to play this game, the graphics were amazing, the puzzles were alot of fun, although there weren't as intricate as some of the puzzles in the other games, but the developers did a really good job of still making them challenging. I really liked the twist at the end of the story too. This is a beautiful and well executed game and I had a blast playing it. Thank you to all of the teams that worked really hard to put it together, it really showed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I have been willing to play this game as soon as I got my headset last year. I only got to play the game right now and 'ow boy', i should have played this earlier. It is one of the better puzzle / escape room games for VR. And I must say that the graphics and the sound design are really on point. I loved the whole victorian styled game design.As for the story. I did find it a bit confusing and I did not really know what was going on. In my opinion they could have simplified some things. But I am just a simple peasant. The puzzles itself are not too difficult and most things you get to do without asking for any hints. The levels are very diverse and it never felt repetitive! All by all, a great game and a must play VR title if you like puzzle games!Big kiss,Laubox
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you at all like puzzle games, escape rooms, anything like that, this is a solid buy. Great environments to explore, a few good "aha" moments, very solid all around. There is a hint system as well, which is extremely unobtrusive (you have to open your inventory and select for a hint to be given, and it will start vague and go from there), so you can safely put on hints without having to worry about the game leading you by the nose, and also use them if you get stuck somewhere or forget what you need to investigate.That said, it's a rather short experience, as others have pointed out. Up to you whether or not a ~3-hour game is worth 30 bucks. It's a quality 3-hour experience, though. If you enjoyed the puzzlebox of the previous games, you'll probably enjoy this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, i have all of them on android, loved them there, and in VR it just adds a certain something, the feeling that you're actually doing something and not just clicking and dragging on a screen. The story is great, the environments fantastic, all in all, i would recommend you give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Price may be steep but this is probably the best adventure type game for VR that I can think of.  If you wanted to show off VR to a non gamer or someone who was not looking for a fighting experience I think this would be a top tier contender.Good puzzles, probably easy if you are familiar with earlier titles.  No one in my house was familiar but we all picked them up relatively quickly.  Younger children may be a little creeped out at the theme as that definitely... pops at certain moments.  Was a relaxing experience for me personally.I think the pairing of this type of puzzle game with VR was genius.  Normally the beginning of puzzles is a little boring in this type of game because.  It is just figuring out what objects you can interact with vs what is just art or decor.  But picking junk up and looking at strange shapes is 10x better in vr.  Plus the hotspot teleport system they use does a good job communicating "hey there is a puzzle over here dummy, that other stuff is just to look cool."
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've absolutely loved the earlier mobile games versions. When I learned that they were making a VR version, I nearly lost my ♥♥♥♥. I started to gather all kinds of expectations in regards to how cool it would be to be actually looking around a puzzle and interacting with them as if I was there. I hyped myself up and started to fear I had sowed seeds that would blossom into a huge disappointment. I am happy to report that I had not. The game is visually pleasing, and while I'd had loved to see a more free movement around the different areas besides the predefined spots you could teleport to, I do realise that would have complicated the game quite a bit. The puzzles are challenging enough to be engaging, but not at all impossible to figure out reasonably quick. And, if you get stuck on something, there are some hints to guide you along the way if you get impatient.The game is not a long one though, and while the development of the game is guaranteed to have been costly for a rather small studio, the price is a bit steep  for the amount of hours of game play you get, and the game's replayability isn't great. That being said, the hours you do get out of it is really great and engaging. The puzzles are satisfying to solve, and the mystery interesting to watch unfold. The game's general "aura" is rather creepy, and while it never tries to flat out scare you, I myself found myself entering rooms quite cautiously, often feeling as if someone was watching me behind my back. My only complaint is the price, but it isn't a huge deal. If you can afford the price well enough, you won't regret buying this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This. Is. AWESOME!When I first found The Room on Steam, I had no idea I wanted this (cause it didn't exist yet), but now I've played through it and it's a pretty cool escape room game. In VR! Yes there's some on Steam, but of those I've played in VR this is by far the best one I've played. Maybe I'm biased because I like the Lovecraftian atmosphere in The Room games and own several Lovecraft books.If you like escape room games (and own vr), you should seriously consider buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, reminds me of when i was little trying to figure out the puzzles.the graphics are outstanding and the puzzles, although simpler than the original games, are incredible fun and satisfying once you figure them out.The only thing i would say that could of been improved was that its only a 3 hour long game which left me wanting more, but due to the effort Fireproof Games has but into this and the fact a vr game can be very complicated to make, it makes up for that.Would recommend to anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I'm not very much into puzzle games, but this one was quite entertaining - especially if you are a fan of egyptian artifacts, ancient rituals, mysteries etc. The game is mysterious but never scary and probably a good way to start VR gaming since there are no elements which might give you motion sickness. 30 Euros for 4 hours playtime might be a bit much, but there is always a sale around the corner. I got it for 50% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I've come to expect from the "The Room" series. The environments are just amazing, the puzzles are not insanely difficult, but satisfying to manipulate and complete, A little bit spooky, if you find that off-putting, but I'm pretty glad they didn't put any of the super jarring jump-scares that are in some of their phone games in a VR title! I also really like that there are some cool Easter eggs if you've played their other games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR is well... another entry in The Room series. Let me rephrase that. This game is very similar in the way you interact with objects and solve puzzles as the rest of The Room entries. This game assumes you've played the others and wastes little time getting into the meat of the game. The puzzles are fun, but nothing ground-breaking for the series and the shorter length doesn't help it that much.However, where I think this game excels is in it's presentation. The Room series has always prided itself on its atmosphere, but experiencing the various locations and interacting with the puzzles in a VR setting is a game changer. Engaging with many of the series' established mechanics such as shrinking down to climb into machines is so much more immersive and potentially terrifying and it's great! Maybe not worth the full price, but on sale this is a must play for fans of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: No wonder this game is constantly critically acclaimed and at the top of the charts.  It is a really great puzzle game with some cool gameplay and creative mechanics.  My only complaint (if you can call it that) is that I don't like only being able to teleport.  I like some free movement locomotion in VR.Regardless, this game is a lot of fun, it is quite pretty, has a cool mood to it and the puzzles are challenging without being ridiculously difficult and frustrating.  Very much recommend.  Looking fwd to more games from this dev!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Quick: + its The Room VR+ Interesting environments, lots of detail.+ Fun puzzles+ More narrative For the world they have build= It is a shorter game (4 ish hours and I was hella slow) 2-3 average= 34$ Canadian, bit expensive for the length= Stationary locations. (will explain)- Does not play well with indexIf you have a VR headset I would recommend you give this a try. Pros: -The Room series has been a fantastic dive into an interesting curated world, and with the introduction of VR interactions it adds more. - The environments are interesting with great detail- The puzzles are fun to interact with - While the The Room VR has an Interesting story It is not clear if it is a stand alone from the main games story or just a side project, non the less it is interesting. Meh: - It is a shorter game. If you are Good with puzzles expect two to two and a half hours of play. - Price tag. It is 34$ Canadian for myself which it a bit experience for the game length but with it being VR and from a smaller studio I can understand the asking price,  as more work has to be done to accommodate the VR systems.- You are Stationary, besides walking around your physical play space. While it would have been nice to wander around the areas and see different perspectives I can understand why.Some environments are a bit larger and if it didn't lock you in place letting you know that there is an interactions in that location or movement i would have been stuck for a freaking while. Also programming in boundary's would have been a ton more work for the game.Con: -HOLY CRAP DOES THIS GAME  DOES NOT LIKE THE INDEX.Everyone has different hardware and software, and the quirks that come with them.Between the controller mapping, head tracking and UI interactions it was a perfect storm for the first bit.Resetting position did help but it was a struggle on some locations.I Liked this game and it was a blast getting my family to try it for their first dive (that was not horror or combat) into VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR: A Dark Matter uses amazing puzzle mechanics and techniques. The game makes sure you think before you grab a hint. The game uses a scary vibe or theme but this is part of the story and since there aren't any jump scares, that's nothing to be afraid of. It just feels scary. I'd suggest buying this game if you're looking for a puzzle game in VR. there is the main storyline but this isn't that big or polished. It's mostly the puzzles that make the game great. I really enjoyed it.[]I have never seen a puzzle game this good in VR. I liked the puzzles but I hated the scariness of the game. The game also felt a bit short but this fits the type of game, which is a puzzle. I would play this again with some friends or after a while. ----------------------------------------------------------The Room VR: A Dark Matter takes you through an investigation as a detective. Somehow you're involved in some 'dark' magic-like things. I'd find myself closing my eyes for nothing. There aren't any jump scares or things like that. The game just has a creepy vibe. This goes with the story. In my opinion, the scariness of the game was a bit disappointing. I'd rather have an amazing story and less of a scary environment. This didn't break the game though. It fit with the story well enough. I would just be a little extra excited if there was a different, more modern style and vibe with the game, without all those witch and Egyptian dark magic. But this is just how The Room VR is. Therefore, I don't think you should skip this game because it might look scary. This is the best puzzle game I have ever played. Following the above message: I was a bit scared at some levels. This was mostly in the beginning. After a while, I'd find myself being busy with nothing else than the puzzles. The puzzles use some cool mechanics and require you to look and dive (literally) deeper into the puzzle than you might think. I had a lot of moments where I didn't know what went where. Sometimes it even went as far as me reading a hint. Buy this game if you like puzzles. The scariness of the game takes a bit of courage (at least for me it did) but doesn't ruin the game. It is part of the game and story. If you want a puzzle game. This is the one to go with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best VR game I've played.. having played the entire "The Room" series which was also spot on.. I knew what to expect, however that didn't stop my amazement at the level of immersion, detail and creepy atmosphere. I actually stopped at times to look around the environments and almost forgot it wasn't real. I found myself considering civilisations past and becoming enthralled in the occult. I love a puzzle and I wasn't disappointed.I would have liked one or two more levels. I was just getting in to it and it was over.. all good things I guess. The lens mechanics are little intrusive but that didn't stop this from being a thoroughly inventive work of VR magic. The level of imagination and creative ability involved in putting a game out of this calibre was not missed!!Good job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the mobile "The Room" games, and this addition to the series in VR is not a disappointment. The graphics are top notch. The detailed environment and textures is something I've always loved about these games. The puzzles are very unique by not relying on common basic puzzles or by repeating a small handful of puzzles throughout the game. They obviously put a lot of time into devising them. I really enjoy puzzle games, and have a fair amount of experience. That said, I spent a little under 4 hours completing it. That's not just rushing through the puzzles but reading all the papers and sometimes just stopping to take in the scene. I would still gladly make the purchase again (disclaimer: I'm cheap and waited for 20% off)!Teleportation is the only thing that gave me any trouble. When teleporting, it sometimes reorients you in ways I don't understand. Maybe there is a default orientation for each waypoint. It can be disorienting when you're trying to get to a room that's a couple hops in a line from you, but the middle hop reorients you to see something on the wall every time you pass it. There were a couple times when I was doing some back and forth with quite a few teleports that I could start to feel a hint of nausea coming with all the chair spinning (they do offer rotating via controls as well, though I've never preferred that). I think it would be more intuitive if you were facing the same direction you were before you teleported as if walking in a straight line, but this in no way kept me from thoroughly enjoying this amazing game and is going to probably be more subjective.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this for $30 - it's very short at about 3.5 hours and the mechanics are dated by modern VR standards - but it's not a bad little puzzle game, if you can get it on sale.The presentation does set you up for a bit of a disappointment, though. Shortly after you start, you end up in front of a plinth with 4 triangle markers that fit an artefact you just found which unlocks the first chapter so it seems like you will play 4 chapters, one for each artefact, and you kind of do but I don't know if they ran out of time or budget or what but the 4th chapter is basically nothing so you're left with a "That's it?" feeling at the end. Chapters 1 and 3 are about an hour long, Chapter 2 is a little longer, maybe 1.5 hours, and then Chapter 4 is like 10 minutes, no joke.The story also set up this conflict that just sort of vanishes in the 4th chapter and your character doesn't do anything to resolve it so I get the feeling this definitely intended to have a more fleshed out ending but it was cut short for whatever reason.The first 3 chapters are pretty good, though. It's a lot of escape room style puzzles where everything is kind of obvious and you just have to run around trying to sequence everything together in the right order. It's fun, though, and well-polished. Not the best puzzle game in VR but not bad, either. Just get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very well done. Definitely the same gameplay and creepy atmosphere I'm used to from their past games but in VR. Exactly as advertised :) For anyone that hasn't played a The Room game before, expect slightly obscure "puzzle box" style environments and a spooky tone but no jump scares or anything too far into horror territory.As a side thing, the default turning and teleport blink intervals were close to right for me but a tad too short so if I turned quickly (as is common in these games) too much I would eventually get a bit nauseous. Being able to tune those a bit more would be nice but I just took a short break between each level and was fine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game that gave me the same feelings as playing through the original Myst way back when and a great addition to a series I've enjoyed for some time. I personally would have preferred it was longer or cheaper (current asking price is $30 USD), but if you can grab this on a sale, it's a wonderful VR experience. I hope another VR The Room is forthcoming!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Having originally played all of the mobile games and loving them, the bar was kind of high for this one. Fireproof knows how to create a solid puzzle solver, and this is no exception. My first recommendation is this. If you are new to VR, this should be one of the first things you play. While it's a great game, it also is a great introduction to VR with how easy the mechanics are. The puzzles are very well done, and aren't impossible. The only exception to this may be the organ puzzle from the church, because that was incredibly frustrating. My only complaint with this one seems to be how vague the story is. I realize this is done to retain that air of mystery that this series is known for, but at some point along the way I became completely lost. That's kind of how it's been in the majority of these games. You are on the track of a scholar, priest, investigator who is trying to find more information on the Null element, and as they keep going the very fabric of time and space seems to fall apart. But that isn't the end of the world, the game is so good it gets that free pass. 100% recommend, for both gamers and non-gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room is, in my opinion, the single best puzzle game I've ever played, and to have made it in VR goes above and beyond. There are no words I could use to describe how passionate I am about this game and all other Room games before it, but I can say that if you enjoy click escape games and/or puzzle games, The Room franchise is an absolute must have, ESPECIALLY if it's in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun game. I'm a long time fan of The Room series, and the only reason why I didn't play this earlier was that I lacked the hardware to play it. I liked how it slowly introduced mechanics from the previous games, allowing new players to learn them, and old players to get used to them in a new setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a big fan of puzzle games ever since the Myst series.  This franchise is one of my favorites.  The $30 price tag at first deterred me because I heard it was a very short game.  I ended up buying it and I can say that it is worth every penny.  The graphics, environments, quality of the puzzles.  Everything about the game was top notch.  I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a virtual reality story in the The Room universe. The previous The Room games were detailed doll house-like mystery games describing a Lovecraftian world. This version is no less detailed and is able to maintain a consistent tone to previous games, but is arguably better. The developers have translated what makes The Room enjoyable into a solid VR experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: After playing it for a bit: This is an amazing puzzle/escape room game. If you liked the "The Room" games already and have a VR headset: just get it. If you have a VR Headset: This is one of the better VR experiences. It is not close as detailed as some other games and the "freedom" is a bit limited, but overall this shows what the medium of VR can achieve for the next generation of gaming.I even got my aunt to play and enjoy it, without a lot of gaming experience just by how intuitive the VR medium can be. Can't wait to finish it as a "co-op experience".
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzler. Loved the non-linearity of the puzzles (you could be solving multiple puzzles at the same time). The puzzles could have been harder (they were usually straight-forward, once you found all the elements) and I only got stuck 2 times because I didn't see the thing to interact with. But they were nicely made, provided a lot of variety and in a great ambiance with a lot of detail!Very fun! Would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, I don't play VR games very often anymore and I had bought this game A while ago after starting the previous Room games, as I was thoroughly enjoying them. I finally tried this game (as I admittedly forgot I had it) recently and I've not enjoyed a VR game like this one in a long time. The feeling of being in some of these environments were amazing. I highly recommend this even if you haven't played previous Room games, but I also recommend them. Didn't encounter any glitches or problems with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: What a amazing puzzle game. and never feeling like the puzzles are just random crap like myst can at times but never too easy. if you like puzzle games get this The only down side is the controls can be a bit finicky like 40% of the time i try to go forward it just turns me since it needs you to press forward but got to be super precise or it will think you wanted to just turn so thats the only downside i can think of
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game! Fantastic story line and awesome use of the VR technology. Totally immersive for the duration and great puzzles. It gives you optional hints in case you get stuck that help figure out what to do next without saying exactly what to do. Awesome experience, recommended. Only around 4.5 hours to beat for me but worth it. First of the series I played (didn't know the others existed) and I just bought all the rest!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side, it is technically excellent, and the rooms and puzzles are well designed. But what annoyed me, is that you can't really dive into the VR world because you only teleport yourself between fixed points in the room and solve puzzles and find objects there. Also the mystic flavour and the amount of text to read was a bit too much for me and therefore not a good fit for me, so I got it refunded.However, I still think it could be a great fit for other people, which explains why I'm still recommending it. If you are looking for a game which can be perfectly played from the couch (just by looking around and using the controllers) and/or if you liked Myst (the 90's adventure game) then it might still be a good fit for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first VR game so I might not have the perspective of someone who has played a lot of other VR exclusive titles.  That being said this game was really impressive for me.  Some of the effects were insane to see.  There were times when I got so immersed I completely forgot where I actually was in the real world.  I wish the puzzles were a little harder though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room series has always been a great example of the 'escape the room' type of puzzle games. The Room VR is possibly the best one yet. It takes full advantage of the immersion of VR without any sacrifices to the quality of the puzzles.If you have a VR headset and like this type of game, you should absolutely pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: *- YOU ARE PAYING TOP SHELF PRICE FOR 3 HOURS AND NO REPLAY ABILITY-*To be honest this was a spectacular game, the graphics where great, the story was engaging, and the controls were easy.  all and all a really great game...so...whay the bad review simply put, its over in three or four hours, it is not a complicated or deep game with a only a few levels.  there is also no replay value as the story simply repeats.  No increased difficulty, no surprise, wash rinse repeat.  for 5 buck syeas but for $30...no...absolutely not.  Honestly I liked the game but when I hit the ned and relized it was over in a day I was pissed.  and its just long enough to get over the 2 hour return policy.  So bye bye $30 dollars, if it's on sale for under $7 go for it but until then realize         *- YOU ARE PAYING TOP SHELF PRICE FOR 3 HOURS AND NO REPLAY ABILITY-*
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY recommend you play this game. Its by far the best VR experience you will have. The game isnt super hard but it gives little direction and lets you discover how to do things naturally. Its so damn good. The game will take you a few hours to complete, likely 2-3 decent sessions depending on how long you usually VR. But straight up, buy this game. You will not regret it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game! This is proper immersive VR with detailed environments and clever puzzles that have been built for VR. The use of "special lenses" within the game to see another dimension, or inside some of the puzzle boxes, is very well done as are the sections where you shrink down to be inside some of the locks and puzzles. Puzzles are complex but not too hard, most have many steps that must be completed in order but nothing felt repetitive at any point. Sad that it was over so soon - more please!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: My Library has been filled with all of the other Room games for quite some time, however, I recently was able to finally afford getting a quest 2, and using virtual desktop, play this game. Man it's so worth it. The story is connected to the rest of the room games, so it's recommended that you play The Room 1, 2, & 3 (4 is unrelated to this storyline it seems) to really know the characters, some settings, etc. But even if you don't want to do that, still a *fantastic* game. mix of puzzle boxes and rooms, basic escape room stuff, but very dramatic lol. The ambiance manages to be creepy without ever actually scaring you bad, just constantly making you feel like you're being watched or someone's about to jump you or something, so pretty good. Honestly, if you've got a headset, and a decent graphics card (I ran this pretty well on a NVIDIA 1660) you should love this game, if you like puzzle games at allP.S. Really recommend if you do use virtual desktop to play this, make sure that the quest has good signal, and that whatever computer you use is hooked up with ethernet, specifically. Tried to use wireless, and it worked, but was really stuttery, and like to freeze up sometimes, which is uh, not pleasant.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews say the same thing: It's "The Room" but in VR. This is true and for people who love the series, this is a decent recommendation as long as you are OK with the playtime. Personally I'm quite happy with it, but given the obvious detail and production value which has gone into this, I felt kind of short changed by the actual VR side of things.Specifically, it feels like this was developed primarily for mobile VR interactions and anything larger-scale was something of an afterthought. The environments are so lush that I wish I could move freely around them. My controllers have a whole bunch of unused buttons, couldn't one of them be somehow used for the lens? Or better yet, some kind of gesture. And why, in room scale, do you recenter the play area around the player whenever teleporting? If you are turning around then you are moving and it just means that your play space slowly drifts around the room and you have to recenter yourself constantly. There is even a separate calibration at the start of each play session so I don't understand why this was necessary. The only other slight grumble I have comes down to interactions. The Room VR plays like the mobile games in terms of puzzles but in the mobile games you are physically interacting with your device. In VR your hands just phase through things. Looking at HL:Alyx (I know it's an unfair comparison I'm doing it anyway) you can see how they have made things feel significantly more tangible. I'd love to see something like that applied to this game.Having said that, these are not in any way deal breakers. In a less polished game I probably wouldn't even have bothered to mention them. If you like the other The Room games and are OK with the playtime (or get it on sale) then you are going to have a gorgeous and immersive puzzle-solving experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It took me around 3 hours to finish the game, using only one clue. So 30€ is a bid of a steep price for this game but if you like puzzle, it certanly is worth the price.Even outside of the puzzles the visuals and interactions are stunnind ang together with the fact that you don't need to move around much (only teleport from clue to clue) it could be a must have to show Vr to your friends. Everyone has a idea what a escape room is and it is so well adapted to VR that everyone playing it will be blown away (atleast my Mum and friends were^^).So if it is on sale it's a must have, else only if you like puzzle or want to show of VR to your friends/family.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Short VR Experience of about 4 Rooms/ChallengesChapter 5 and 6 Are only about 5 minutes long combined, so don't get fooled by the achievements.The Puzzles are well made and use VR as en element. Puzzles are okay in difficulty, definitifely challenging but solvable.For WMR Users: Start the Game in Oculus Mode, Steam VR Version was Laggy AF for me
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room is a saga that never disappoints, across the five games, it never felt like more of the same, each game has it's own identity, although they all use pretty much the same mechanics.This is one of the games that in VR can explore it's potential to the fullest, if you like puzzles, this will test your brain (I strongly recommend to not use hints), personally I just got stuck once because of a rope, a rope I didn't saw although I got past it so many times, so don't  overlook anything, sometimes the answer is right before your eyes.Even though is a little short on content, it is a well dosed amount of entertainment, well worth the price in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the other games in The Room series, then you'll no doubt enjoy this short VR entry in the series. It takes the basic gameplay mechanics you enjoyed about the previous titles and scales them up nicely. Compared to other titles in the series, the puzzles do seem a little simpler, but that's to be expected with the series' first entry in VR.The game supports Standing or Seated play, with the game offering you those as options every time you start the game so it's easy to jump in. However, be advised that a couple of puzzles require a little bit of reach so do make sure you've got room to stretch your arms around you to avoid colliding with real world objects. At the time of writing, movement is done by teleportation to specific areas of the game's environments, so there's not much in the way of exploration options. On the other hand, at least there's minimal chance of you losing track of where you're supposed to be. Some of the environments are better than others too, with some feeling living and atmospheric, whilst others feel more still and sterile.For the 3-4 hours of content you get in the game, the price tag at launch may be quite steep, but it was a nice experience which I'm sure will be appreciated by fans of the other games in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic game in the series, but this time really enriched by the VR platform. Fireproof Games have always succeeded in making puzzles creative and interesting, and this game is no different - the puzzles make spectacular use of the potential offered by VR gaming, and I can't imagine how they'll push the boundaries even more next time, though I'm confident they will! Every fine detail appears to have been considered, the art is fantastic - it's so immersive and easy to forget that the world of The Room VR is a virtual game world. I highly recommend this game even if you have not played any games in the series before, because it is definitely fit for newcomers, and it's a must-have for the VR platform! Thank you for a brilliant game experience, Fireproof Games, you always exceed expectations!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited 3 years to play this game!  Finally happened upon an Oculus 2 and it was everything I hoped it would be!  Honestly, this could have very easily not have been in VR and I don't necessarily feel that VR enhanced the game in any way.  However, Fireproof Games remains one of my favorites, and I hope they don't abandon this series.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought this the very moment I've noticed it in the Steam store. As a fan of the original games, I always thought a Room game would play terrific in VR. Spoiler: it does. I played it on Pimax headset with Index controllers.Even on a mobile phone The Room series was immersive, here it is much more so. The general esthetics are the same and the game plays small homages to the previous entries in certain chapters. The sets are not the most intricate I've seen in the series, yet developers use depth really well, most of the puzzles have require certain spacial awareness or changing perspective, even though there is no free locomotion in the game, only predetermined teleportation points.  The whole lovecraftian Null presense gets additional creep factor in VR.Perhaps the only thing I didn't like was the interaction with pulleys. The game requires you to grab a rope, pull it down, move your other arm high, release the lower arms hold and grab it with the upper arm. One cannot grab onto the same object in two places. This general limitation is present through the whole game. Whereas before you could interact with objects from your inventory in a more conventional way, in this game most of the inventory object puzzles are about placement and movement. Even though developers were creative about this limitation, I feel it takes a bit from the experience in the whole.The game is not long, I've managed to breeze through it in about 3 hours, but whose were very fun hours for me. If you loved the series mobile entries, you would surely like this one. It is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you like escape rooms,  puzzle games, or any of the other 'Room' games by this developer then do not hesitate, just buy this game. The VR mechanics are comfortable, with either sitting or standing play, a really high level of quality and attention to detail. Movement is teleport only, with snap turn or rotate in real life, I thought this would be limiting but given all the details in the levels it works really well.I finished the game in about 12 hours and enjoyed every moment, so about £2 per hour feels fair for a game this polished.The difficulty of the puzzles is very good, with a subtle hints system if you get really stuck.The story (without spoilers) exists in the same universe as the previous (non-vr) Room games and is suitably curious and creepy at the same time with lots of atmosphere.No negative issues or bugs, with just some very small areas for improvement.Hope to see many more from this developer.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First, Thank you for proper sitting controls! I don't have much room to move around. Controls were fairly intuitive,  puzzles were fun, and the world was just beautiful in VR. I always loved the atmosphere of "The Room" series, and being in these areas, with my Samsung Odyssey+ headset... it was breathtaking to see.Also loved holding up the bottles with the liquid and just swirling them around. A true pleasure to play!Thanks again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game has blown my mind! This game had an exceptional lore, challenging puzzles, and really cool affects. Was hesitant to install it at first, but once I played the intro I was hooked. The game has very simple movement mechanics, Smooth grip feel, and amazing audio ambiance. The levels were packed with detail, and the puzzles and mysteries to uncover were really an interesting trip. Would highly recommend anyone who is starting out in VR to try this game. What a fun experience for hours and hours of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: good graphics - good puzzles (thanks to YouTube Ren Stefanek for his walkthrough to get past the tough spots) - and a lot of fun.Cons: a little too long - 3/4 of the way through I'm saying when will this be over - puzzles became repetitive - story line, as such, started off good but finished poorly Overall: I really liked the game
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this series immensely! I have to say Old Sins is probably my favorite because it felt a lot more challenging and substantial (plus alternate endings was fun). This VR version is a great start; the visuals are realistic and interacting with objects is a lot of fun. Please make a second one, add even more content, and allow us to move more freely about. Ease in turning and even just allowing us to walk instead of hop around would be great!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Shortest than The Room 3 and 4 at a little bit more than 2½ hours with only three "maps" and a very short epilogue. The story is still very poorly told with cryptic, boring and basically useless texts and it ultimately goes nowhere like the other games in the series. The level design is fine and it's still fun to play since this genre doesn't have many games and it's using VR well enough. I'd recommend waiting for a sale as it's extremely short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty awesome game.  The "story" wasn't super-compelling, but the puzzles were great.  There's one place where I got really stuck (middle position of the clock crank) and even the hints didn't help, and maybe like 2-3 others that were pretty obscure to have figured out, but generally well crafted.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It took me probably longer then it should have to realize how to interact within an object and how it pertains to being on the outside of that object.  Once that was figured out everything came together nicely . The inner games are not too difficult and just in case the clues can refresh your memory or help with the most challenging obstacles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations of Fireproofs execution off this title on VR, coming from the mobile series(which i enjoyed plenty) there was much to be desired.  Ofcourse i felt very pleased with this release, controls felt solid and intuitive, story is good, puzzles good(although not as challenging as the mobile implementation) all in all a great experience. My only regret is that i wish there was more and more to play, took about 5 hours to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I played all The Room games so far on Steam and iOS. I love this sort of games, so I was very happy to see that a VR version existed. And I wasn't dissapointed. It's a great installment and would everyone recommend this game who likes the other The Room games. The Room is perfect for VR. The Graphics are great and it runs very well. The atmosphere is definitly there. The puzzles are what you would expect from a The Room game. It's just sad thats so short. Of course, it depends on peoples playstyle. I saw reviews from between 2 and 12 hours of playtime. Well, I took my time and it were still "only" 3,5 hours. As a fan of the series, the full price is definitly worth it.I hope that Fireproof Games continues The Room in VR with a more complex and longer part.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned this game for almost a good month, without ever playing it until now. As a returning fan of "The Room" franchise, I expected story, I expected mind-boggling puzzles, and I expected some sense of uncertainty and fear. By gods, this game delivered every single thing I had hoped for.For those who favor puzzles, escape rooms, and a bewildering story to tie it all up in a wondrous bow, do check this out! (Maybe you'll find an intricate key in here too? >>)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the other The Room games, you'll know generally what to expect here -- it's an escape room-y puzzle game, never gets too crazy so it's fun without getting seriously frustrating. It's about a 3 hour game played blind -- it has a hint system, but I didn't use it so I don't know how beat-you-over-the-head the hint system is.I was a fan of the mobile The Room games, so when I saw they'd released a VR game I was in for it. I'd say buy it on sale, but I'd say buy any VR game on sale since they're typically shortish for the price compared to normal PC games.I'd recommend playing seated - I played standing and all it did was make me wander around my room and slowly get closer to the walls since you are on rails with teleport points and do not have free movement, and every time you turn or teleport it resets your position based on where you are physically. Playing seated will keep you from slowly meandering into your desk if you are more used to roomscale experiences. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I love the mobile games and this VR version although short did not disappoint! Yes it is a bit expensive for 3-4 hours of game play but I will happily support the developers and this series because I love their attention to detail, storytelling and ambience. The games are all magical and engaging but VR takes it to a whole new level. You feel fully immersed in the story. I'll be eagerly awaiting the next one. 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Albeit being short, but very good The Room chapter. I would love to experience a sequel!Couple of quirks:1. No finger tracking on the Index controllers (understandable, yet sad)2. Playspace shifts after teleport. When you teleport, you teleport to the middle of the area in the game, yet remain in one of the corners (for example) of your boundary. Therefore, having to reset occasionally. To solve this, the devs could just implement the teleport mechanic that would be aware of your position regarding SteamVR boundary and therefore position you not in the center, but according yo where you are, so that you won't have to reset in the future.Otherwise, great!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this game because of VR for VIVE and this game is INCREDIBLE the experience is like no other puzzle game in VR.  The creators did an excellent job and I hope they're creating another VR experience because I DID NOT WANT THIS TO END.  I could play this game for days on end the creative puzzles and combinations of clues were so AWESOME.IT'S A MUST BUY!!!! I was lucky to get it on sale but I would pay regular price and when the next one is released I will be.When you play DO NOT USE CLUES it makes the game that much better and last longer making you have to think harder.To all those involved with the creation of this masterpiece, EXCELLENT JOB.PLEASE continue your artistic creativity and give us the privilege to enjoy another journey in the next ROOM.I truly didn't want this to end, Hopefully the next ROOM is twice as long if not longer with more difficult puzzles making the game last even that much longer for those of us that enjoy the trip through the ROOM.Congrats on a job MAGNIFICENTLY DONE.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've always enjoyed The Room series as a fun puzzler that also manages to tell an interesting story. When I found out they did a VR game, I thought it was a marriage made in heaven...and I was right!The game is engaging, fun, intriguing and clever! My only gripe is I felt some of the puzzles were a little easy and the short run-time. The game could have done with more levels - that being said, I hope they make a VR sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A very good The Room experience translated into VR. There are multiple profiles for saves and in-game SS, performance is good on my Pimax 5K+. Graphics is surprisingly impress even played after Alyx. Puzzles/objects are visually more enhanced when you can hold and experiment up close in VR. Good use of 3D tracked controllers for puzzle solving, some require just a finger and some require both hands to operate at the same time, I think they are what make The Room special to be played in VR and I want more. Puzzles are not too hard, clues are well hidden in the environment, some spooky moment here and there and I am enjoying it so far, played 3/4 rooms in one go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not someone who complains about a game just because "it's too short". I don't think a game has to provide X hours of gameplay to be worth a certain amount.But: This is basically another The Room game (which I do like) at 6 times the usual price because it's in VR. There were very few instance when being a VR game actually made a difference, most of the game could just as well be played on a screen with a mouse without missing much and it took me roughly 3 hours to complete.I get that making this as a VR game is more work and I'm willing to pay a premium for VR games, but for 30€ I would have expected something "new" or at least bigger? Perhaps an actually interesting narrative that's not just there to tie completely unrelated puzzle rooms to each other?I had some issues letting go of objects after a while using the Index controllers, but overall, the game worked well enough. Visually, it's okay, nothing breathtaking. Sound and music were really nice.It is a decent puzzle game overall. Just buy it at a decent discount and don't expect much more than the other The Room games, but in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Pretty game. Fun and engaging puzzles that work well for VR. The hint system is well implemented (Pull the ? tab down in the inventory). There is a semblance of a story.The bad: There is a fair amount of reading that is required to follow the story but not required for puzzles. On an Index it's OK, but have a feeling reading on older hmd's like the Vive would be tedious with the screen door effect.The ugly: No voice acting. It's a short-ish experience. On higher graphics settings tracking doesn't work properly causing nausea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences I've had yet. Fireproof has an incredibly reputation on mobile for their The Room games which are some of the most polished, gorgeous, puzzling, thoughtful games I've ever played. They're one of the few game series I buy immediately upon release, at full price, and play through ASAP. So when they announced they were going VR, I was incredibly excited because I trust nobody outside of Valve to pay this much attention to detail.I was not disappointed. The atmosphere and visuals and sound and music are stunning and immersive. Mechanics work well and smoothly and represent nearly everything I always wished for in their games as far as physical interaction. Being able to actually grab objects and manipulate them directly is the dream, and it's achieved here.The only "bad" marks are that it's short, which isn't terribly surprising given the past games and the amount of work that goes into it, but considering the big price jump from mobile, it's still sad to have only 3 hours. That said, an escape room ticket which is a third as long and a tenth of the experience costs at least twice as much as this game, so if you look at it THAT way it's an exceptional value. There were also times I wished they'd allowed me to better use both hands. There are some rope-pulling sections that would have gone SO much faster if I could go hand over hand instead of leaving one hand just hanging out on screen. Those are my only critiques. Seriously.I've not spent a massive amount of time in VR since getting my headset last year, but this game re-sold me on why I bought a headset. It's truly a masterpiece. I can't wait for the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good, polished VR puzzle game. I enjoyed the story even if it's a bit tricky to understand. The puzzles themselves are all really imaginative and enjoyable to work through. I wish you could move freely though and that more objects were interactive. Still this is a fun little game - recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR stands out as one of the most beautiful, well crafted and ambitious VR puzzle games I’ve played since Xing The Land Beyond. What I really love about it is how it leans heavily into VR’s strengths— using scale. It’s something only VR can do and is very well implemented in this game.  For example you can shrink and step into a keyhole to unlock a door from the inside. Or you’ll step inside a church organ to fix the broken pipes- with its inner workings becoming the game level.  Actually standing inside these impossibly small locations is just a surreal experience.  The puzzles themselves are fun as well.  You turn gears and pull knobs which give off satisfying clicky, sounds and haptic feedback, lending them a tactile quality.  The level of detail and interaction throughout is just stunning.  Excellent game worth every penny especially if you like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful VR escape room - or, rooms. The experience threads you along through several different themes of environments with clever (but not difficult - and if you do find yourself stuck, there are hints) puzzles. There were also several visual effects that I have not seen before in VR - with lots of tiny bits of polish added that were definitely not necessary but made the whole world feel tactile and full of life (one example is that papers you pick up have a bit of 'bend' to them, as you move them around with your hands.) Will absolutely be recommending this to others as an example of how to set a mood in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and handling is very good and something you can expect from a 2020 VR game. Most of the puzzles are too easy for me.
