And for just three hours it is not worth the 30 €. However, I enjoyed the three hours.I do recommend it because technically it is a very good game and others probably get more than 3 hours out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "puzzle" VR game, thou I say it's a bit more. Fireproof have a perfect understanding of what they are doing and it shows. I want to also mention fantastic atmosphere and presentation.In case you are wondering - this is not a horror game (there are no jump-scares), but It has a fantastic "spooky" atmosphere.10/10 - would face horrors beyond my comprehension again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Im new to VR and grabbed a few different 'Escape room' style games. This was, by far, the most polished and best looking. Mechanics were great and evolved through out the game, it made good use of teleporting and walking around my room space, and plot was enjoyable. As with all escape room games, it has 0 replayability, but great sharability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen people saying the game is too short. IMO, it is not. If you don't act like a speedrunner and don't look at clues every single chance you have, this game could easily entertain you for 4-5 hours, replayability is pratically 0, but the game is REALLY well made and there are a ton of mechanics, there's never the same thing twice. Also, the price tag isn't abusive. If you like VR, good gameplay, puzzles and incredible visuals, you should buy it NOW!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: While short, this is how The Room was meant to be played from the beginning. Being able to manipulate all of the intricate object with your actual hands is truly a fun and immersive experience. Typically I despise teleport movement in VR, but this game sort of needs it as some of the puzzles are location dependent. If a free-roam locomotion version of this game came out, I'd be all over it though. As far as "challenge" goes, the puzzles aren't really brain melters and you can motor through this game without using hints. The story is told through flashbacks/memories and notes so you are left to decipher the finer details on your own. As with the other games in this series, take your time, enjoy the sights and revel in playing with all the toys they give you. Overall this is a great romp through VR and I hope Fireproof keeps it going with more of these.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: In LOVE! What an amazing experience this game was. Portions were just challenging enough, though it did become a bit tedious on the home stretch. Coming from someone with a Master's in Archaeology, this was pretty dang fun! Naturally, I'm into the mystery, puzzles, and the brief Tomb Raider/Da Vinci vibe. Moving onto similar games like A Fisherman's Tale, I actually appreciate the point-and-click movement The Room has as opposed to free roam. It is nice to be able to get as close and personal in a VR surrounding as possible, but it can also waste time and draw you away from the task at hand. If that makes sense - it works well here! I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a lot of fun so far with the game. The difficulty of the riddles is very well balanced so that you are not likely to get stuck too long looking for an answer. The clues you need to solve something are always nearby (or you can bring them along with you) so you don't need to move around too much (which would cause motion sickness to some).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a short but really good game, a very immersive puzzle experience for VR. Sadly it's quite linear, so you don't actually make any difference in the game, so it kinda feels like an interactive movie. Other than that the game is really fun and very well made, full of small details. If you like puzzle and mystery games, you WILL love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone with a VR headset should own this game. Fireproof exploits the capabilities of VR very well, and it makes for some truly astounding environments and puzzles. Side note - I'm quite sure this is the first time I've thought of a game as "astounding", but no joke. There were parts where I just _could not_ stop exclaiming in wonder at what was happening. Beautiful. Satisfying. My one regret is that it's over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at bottomI have played and reviewed every single game in the The Room series. And I love them all, including this one. Once again, this game was challenging enough to be lots of fun, but not so challenging I got super frustrated. It was also really polished, and it was impressive how well Fireproof was able to integrate some past game mechanics into this one. Overall, it's just a really good puzzle game that anyone who likes puzzle games would enjoy (play the other games first, or you won't understand what's going on!)That being said, I do have one major problem with it: The length. Now, every other game has been pretty short (about 4, 5 hours long) but that was balanced out by the fact that they were super cheap, even for their length. However, this one... it's $30. I was able to complete this in 3 hours on my first playthrough. I don't mind it being 3 hours long, because like I said, all the other games have been short too (though not as short as this one). What I have a problem with is that I payed $30 for a 3 hour game. Honestly, it makes me really sad saying this, because I've never had any problems with the price of the other games, but I would definitely suggest getting this on a sale. All in all, I suggest this game for anyone who enjoys playing puzzle games. However, if you haven't already, make sure to play the other games first, or you will not know what is going on (and if you like this, you'll want to play those anyway).Also, for Oculus users: there is an option to play without SteamVR. All you have to do is have SteamVR closed, then click play on this in your library, then an option box will appear. Click "Launch The Room VR: A Dark Matter in Oculus VR mode" and you're good to go. If you're using an Oculus headset I highly recommend this because it makes the game run much smoother.TL;DRgame is very good puzzle game, buy when on sale, but play other games in series first
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed all of The Room games prior to this one on iOS- they are wonderfully devised, and I share them with friends who enjoy a good puzzle.  A Dark Matter is a standalone game and doesn't require any knowledge of the previous games to be enjoyed.  It was made for VR and it's a wonderful experience, with the puzzle mechanics incorporating actions which are smartly devised for VR navigation.  The environments are enchanting, richly detailed and delightfully creepy, and the puzzles are challenging without being frustrating.  Hours melted away like minutes as I played, and while I wish there was more to be had, I found the conclusion well satisfying.  Like a fancy dessert, it seemed to go quickly, and its memory lingers fondly in my thoughts.  Kudos to everyone at Fireproof Games for absolutely knocking this one out of the park!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the escape room puzzle VR game I have been searching for. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal!!! I would absolutely recommend to fans of the other games in the series. Puzzle heavy gameplay. Atmosphere is adequately creepy but without the unnecessary jump scares. I played on the Oculus Rift. I paid full price ($30) and it was definitely worth the money. I sincerely hope more are coming. My 21 yr old son played it after me and thoroughly enjoyed it as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: a charming VR title that lets you solve puzzles by interacting with various items, levers and a few cool tricks!  it is a bit short, finished it at around 4 hours but it is a recommended experience even for a VR user that is afraid of  purchasing VR titles(such as myself) because they always end up having terrible performance or the gameplay isn't fun at all! this is a must have!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy sleep. I enjoy VR. I had a good time playing through this. I liked it enough to stay up late to get it finished, and not sleep as much as I might normally. For those of us who get awakened in the morning by either a pre-dawn alarm or the noise of family... you may appreciate that is quite a statement. There are some nice settings to explore in VR. Would have been nice to have free roam in them. The locomotion isn't a game stopping issue as there are only key points in each space to interact with. So it helps keep focus on what matters. It's not especially scary, but it does build some tension. The puzzles were suitable for someone like me who routinely fails at puzzles, but also, I had help from people looking over my shoulder. Definitely would not have finished it so quickly if I hadn't received a bit of help along the way. I don't see much immediate replay value, but it's certainly left a positive impression, so might be nice to go through it again when the memory of the details have faded a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the Room games are very good; I have been playing them since 2012.  The issue with this one is that it tries to be a sequel to all the previous ones while exploring a new medium.  The VR aspects are not much of an addition:  no free movement, a poor implementation of the controllers (on the index, anyway), constantly having to go in and out of, ahem, special vision--which requires opening the inventory and flipping a switch and is cancelled while warping between location nodes.  The puzzles are an evolution on the things seen before and that's partly the problem:  we're past the simpler mechanical puzzles which are a blast in VR (since those were done to death in the previous games) so there is a lot of backtracking; as in, flip a switch here, remember a thing, go several locations away, change some stuff (and, rinse and repeat in case of error).  In principle, that could be good, especially if there were some way to take notes that did not require taking off the headset.  However, since only certain things are interractable and these objects are not highlighted or outlined, one finds themselves poking and prodding at the scenery in hopes of finding an interractable object.  Not to mention, the lore and story are forgettable and there is a constant "puzzle for the sake of puzzle" vibe.  This cannot be avoided completely in a point and click puzzle game but it is so elaborate here that it is difficult to suspend disbelief and that breaks immersion.  VR shoud not be point and click; a medium that allows so much freedom should not be restricted to standing in only certain places and being able to interact with only certain things. I would have preferred a VR redux of the first Room game.  That would have been a more manageable task development-wise.  I am sure I will finish this game, but, frankly, I just want it to be over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I really really loved this game. It creates such an amazing atmosphere, the puzzles are challenging yet rewarding and doable. I got creeped out more than once honestly and I just really enjoyed working my way through the chapters and solving the mysteries put before me. The game was so addicting and catchy that i played all the way through it in a single run and it had me craving more. I really hope - and cannot wait - for another game of the Room Series to be released, be it VR or normally. Lots of love to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful addition to the The Room series by Fireproof. The VR adds such an immersive experience and the levels are so incredibly detailed. If you've played the other Room games, the puzzles probably wont hurt your brain too much, but the experience is so wonderful and atmospheric, you won't even mind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game for at 33% off, which was still a little on the pricey side in terms of playtime but worth it nonetheless. After having picked up the other four titles at the very low price of €10 I can't be too bothered about it. A few pints in a pub on a Friday evening will set you back more.The Room series has given me fun late nights and the VR experience was the cherry on top. The gameplay of the series translates really well into VR, and I loved how the game mixed things up by putting you in a different room for each puzzle similar to The Room 2. Each location is full of atmosphere, with stunning visuals, brilliant lighting and excellent sound design. The Room's puzzles have mostly been of the hidden object type but this game does away with that. I never really went for the hint button except for a few instances when I missed something I didn't know I could interact with.As with the other titles, the story is minimal though I'd recommend playing the others first. Not only will it give you a taste of the franchise, you'll appreciate the title a bit better as the game refers to previous entries in the series. I played on Quest 2 and had zero problems using Oculus Link.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First let me just say:  I do not have bad anything to say about the game itself. It combines the puzzle aspect, mystery, atmosphere and eerieness very well. During gameplay i had no problems or glitches, sure some puzzles needed more steady hands than others but nothing that no one can manage.The only minor problem i have with this game is the price. I do not know what goes into making a VR Game but for a one time playthrough of around 2-3 hours, 30€ (at time of purchase) was a little bit steep for me. Nonetheless i had fun stimulating the ol' grey matter in a virtual environment!If i had to rank this game from 0 to 5 i would give it a solid 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I found A Dark Matter to be very enjoyable and engrossing--there's always a crafty new puzzle or mysterious task leading me deeper into the game.  I actually made it through ADM in about 8 hours without taking a single hint, so I can't comment on that part of the game. Note:  It probably helped that I previously played a few editions of The Room series in 2D on my Android tablet. I greatly enjoyed them as well, so go check them out for the dozens of unique puzzles to solve--if you are clever enough.  There's an over-arching story to all of The Room games,  but the puzzles are definitely the dominant feature.  In ADM, the set pieces are terrific, and moving around is simple enough.  The tutorial hints, mostly offered in the first chapter, are well-placed and helpful for getting started and I wouldn't change a thing.  While I ultimately escaped The Room, I didn't yet collect all the playing cards so I will have to go back in and replay it soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of "The Room" series ever since they released the first game I was hooked! This installment, however, of the series is a whole different level! Experiencing the game in virtual reality is INSANE! It's so good! The controls were smooth and the visuals are amazing! Everything was just perfect! I can't wait for them to release another one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, every puzzle is expertly crafted and well designed, everything fits perfectly.I dont exactly how to explain it... but this game is NOT janky at all, ive played a LOT of escape the room games, and this has to be on the top of how good the puzzles "feel" when solving them. You dont get many "am i supposed to be doing this?" moments, because the game doesnt let you use items incorrectly, BUT you have to solve the environmental puzzle on how to use them correctly for you to advance to the next item you need to use cleverly.So, It all fits, it flows perfectly gamewise, puzzles arent hard to handle, but some arent so easy, all have a hidden hint in the environment, i solved all the puzzles the "right" way except one, after i "brute forced" the solution, i looked around what i had missed... and it was super obvious and right under my nose (after the fact :/ ).Every puzzle specially the ones i got stuck on, once i got them i had awesome "gotcha!" feelings or whatever, i got more than a few in this game, and thats pretty cool.Took me ~3.5hrs to complete, i think i could have done it faster, but honestly i took my sweet time, game looks really good, the environments are very well done, audio is spot on, readeable items are clear and easy to read. Some might complain about the "spot teleport" only mobility, but i honestly think it fits perfectly, if you can move to a spot, you can still use something in that location, you cant go back, dont worry you are good, everything you need is ahead. Helps a LOT when trying to find out what you might have missed. But i do understand how escape the room pros could feel this is an extra hint, I would have loved to be able to look behind every corner in the gorgeous environments. The theme while a bit creepy, is not that scary at all, its all about the puzzles, no scarejumps of any kind, that being said. the atmosphere is greatly done, so its kinda spooky at times, like in a dark museum with thunders and what not.For the price / duration ratio, some might say its a bit steep, but i think the overall quality more than makes for it. I got it on sale and i dont regret my purchase!This is one of the best Escape the Room games ive played, fully recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for a relatively hefty price to time ratio. I'd suggest waiting for a sale or general price reduction (I got it for 20€ at the Halloween sale 2020, still expensive but sadly most VR games are). A playthrough takes 2 - 4 hours, depending on whether you use hints or not and how good you are in puzzles in general. The puzzles are relatively simple but interestingly done and thought out. There are progressive hints if you get stuck, although I'd recommend trying for yourself since especially the third and final one outright just spoilers what to do. The graphics are good, albeit not on Alyx's level, and the game runs a pretty much constant 90fps on Index on Medium with a 1060 6GB (some cutscenes on higher settings needed some reproj so I played on medium). Since it's a puzzle game there isn't much going on and the game's requirements reflect that.As a fan of the Room games I enjoyed this game as well. However, I was missing some of the bigger one piece puzzles you take apart more and more. Pretty much all of the puzzles were separated across several boxes and pieces in a room. It fits in some cases but I was missing the magical unfolding present in the other Room games. Other than that, if you played any of the Room games before, it plays exactly like that but in VR. If you haven't played the Room before and are afraid this game might have horror elements - it doesn't. It does have some creepy things but it's never scary. It's more a mixture of mystery and a tiny bit eeriness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Another triumph for The Room team! Their games have always been immersive and beautifully orchestrated. Playing through A Dark Matter in VR upped that sense of immersion even further, and the hours passed like minutes. Strongly recommend to any fans of the puzzling genre, and play standing if possible for an even greater sense of depth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fireproof games knocks it out of the park again with this jam packed and enthralling VR escape the room title. Most puzzles are well designed, varied, and mildly interconnected in engaging and compounding ways. There's a sense of progression from figuring out each next puzzle and the presentation is wonderfully sharp and controls work well.I appreciate that the game takes the effort to focus what you can interact with so you always know what you're missing and what you can interact with, unlike some other free roam escape the room VR titles. It means there's less focus on finding things everywhere and more concentrated puzzle solving familiar to players that have played the other games in this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: When i bought this game i expected a puzzle heavy adventure in the tradition of the Myst series with some "light" lovecraftian horror and investigation elements. Basically that's what i got, minus the investigation. The Room VR: A Dark Matter is overall a good puzzle game, but to be honest: It's not a good adventure game. There is a story, but most of the time it feels like it was constructed just to give all places and puzzles in the game a tiny bit of sense, to connect them. I'm not a huge fan of this design concept, i prefer games where the world design, gameplay and puzzlea are created to support the story, not the other way round.But overall The Room VR: A Dark Matter is still a very good VR puzzle game. The graphics and locations are nice, the puzzles are mostly well thought out and if you're not looking for a story heavy adventure game with lots of lore this might just be the right game for you. Just keep in mind: This isn't a long game and while chapter 2, 3 and 4 are extensive enough the final part of the game was really short and imho not on the same level of quality as for example chapter 3 and 4 (my favorite parts of the game).And there's one more thing: 30 EUR for about 4 to 5 hours of gameplay isn't cheap, but i understand this game needs to cost a bit more than the other games of the "The Room" series because they won't sell as many copies because it's a VR exclusive. So i can partly understand the high price, but it's still expensive. If you're not sure wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Superb VR puzzle experience. Played on HP Reverb G2 and the graphics and overall presentation are top notch. Great puzzles, and good ambiance. Also fun to play with another person by choosing to view VR content through the Steam VR menu. We both swapped in and out of the headset so we each got a good chance at different puzzles and the VR experience. Additionally, there are things that visually you'll just want to share with the person viewing on a computer screen or TV. They just don't translate as well to a flat screen but in VR they are much more compelling to see. Was just part of the way through the game and was inspired to go back and buy the three non-VR versions of The Room (which are different than the VR version). Have been playing the first one and that has also been a lot of fun so far.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're already familiar with the Room series on iOS, you kind of know what you're in for - but the immersion is cranked up to 11.  If you're not familiar with the series, it's kind of in the escape room genre.  Overall; fantastic.  Not at all disappointed.  But it's about 3 hours total to work through it - just be aware of that going in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Really good VR experience. An atmospheric puzzler with a lot of very tactile mechanical puzzles - switches, knobs, pulleys, cranks, etc. Slightly creepy, but doesn't cross over into horror and there is no one else inhabiting the world (outside of some flashbacks), it's just you against the puzzles. If you played any of the pancake mode The Room games, this is the same thing, just in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played The Room games on mobile, this is a wonderful transition to VR.  Definitely keeps the cosmic horror undertones in spades.  It is a little short so if you're bothered by dollars to hours arguments, maybe wait for a sale.However I'm more than satisfied with my purchase at full price.  Quality definitely does meet expectations at that level.  Here's hoping for more adventures in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: It's a The Room game as you know and love, but being able to look around freely (using your head, no less) gives the impressive scenery a whole new kick.You can't walk around, but that's part of the series. Personally, I don't like locomotion in VR, so I'd be teleporting anyway. You're still free to move about the play area, of course.My favorite is honestly the miniature puzzles. Seeing yourself in the context of the whole is just cool.I've noticed that achievements unlock only when closing the game, but they'll be there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle and adventure. I played through in three sessions, 6 hours total. The intriguing story draws you in and keeps you playing. Very original puzzles that fit in with the story and each other, not just a random collection. The difficulty level was just right for me, I did get stuck at one point and had to quit for the night, but with fresh eyes the next day I was able to progress. Great graphics, effects, music, and atmosphere as well.  Really well done on all levels!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game does not have a smooth turning option which completely ruins the atmosphere. As a huge fan of the Room games I was very excited to play this but gave up after about two minutes once I realized the issue above. Since my headset uses a wire I can't really turn around that easily.Will revisit if they ever add smooth turning though given the game is four years old, I doubt it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down best VR escape room out there. As a fan of the series who's played all of the previous games, this game truly amazed me. The original games had an enchanting atmosphere, which this game reenacts perfectly (maybe even better), with you being completely surrounded by it. The mysterious surroundings, the music/sounds and the overall prettiness of the game made me feel that VR magic again. A short, but perfect masterpiece, definitely a 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly well done. I wasn't sure if escape room type of game would be for me, but I liked the trailer so I gave it a go and honestly, I think this is one of the best experiences I had on VR so far. My GF tried as well and couldn't stop playing, so she finished it in slightly more than a day :-).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR is a great mix of good puzzles, ambience, mechanics and graphics. The game was a blind purchase for me as I wanted to try it out because of the fantastic reviews and I wasn't disappointed. Although the playtime was somewhat short, you can see the effort that has gone into making the game playable and enjoyable. I would recommend this to anyone wanting a good few hours playing puzzles and getting invested in the story you're trying to uncover.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but its fun. Like a less complicated version of the other "The Room" games. IMHO, it's by design that the puzzles are (a little) simpler, since there are things harder to do on VR than when you're sitting next to a computer. If you liked the other "The Room" games, you'll probably like this one as well
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game right off of the heels of The Room 4, and this was certainly something different. I did enjoy this game and played it all in one sitting.. or standing I guess- anyway, the fact that I played this in one continuous sitting should tell you how engrossed and fun this game was, however there were some things that I felt were a little lacking, and those are simply down to a few mechanics that were abandoned for this game.Primarily, the manipulation of objects was abandoned. Do you remember how, when you picked up an object, you could spin it around in another screen and possibly change it's shape? well you cant do that anymore in this game. In fact you could probably complete this game with just one controller, which was a missed opportunity in my eyes. As well, I also found it kind of annoying how you had to open your inventory to turn on the eyepiece instead of flicking something to the side of your head- see Ghost of Tabor's Night Vision Goggles to see what I mean.With that said, this game definitely keeps the feel and atmosphere of The Room series, and I believe was a welcome addition. Should they make any more in the series, I'd recommend trying to make it in such a way to allow VR players to play with their headsets, while still allowing Keyboard players to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The only downside of the game I can think of is the relatively short play time. I finished it in a little below 6 hours as a casual puzzler with using the internal help function once (got stuck because I didn't interact with something long enough to progress). But seeing that they are a rather small studio I guess it's not that easy putting in more and more gameplay mechanics in a reasonable amount of time and also not getting repetitive in some ways, which could result in the game just feeling stretched for the sake of a longer play time. The last chapter felt a little rushed to me, it would have been nice to have another hour of puzzles there.Apart from the play time, everything was positive (I played it on an Index with a decent PC, so this might vary for other HMDs and setups, but I don't think it's that much of a hardware hog): The graphic and sound design are mostly really nice, the immersion is great and the interaction with the levels felt good. In another review, someone stated that they give you a nice perception of the scale of everything and I can confirm that.I liked the puzzles and since I didn't play The Room 1 to 4 yet, I'm planning to do so in the future, Fingers crossed for another The Room VR game in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent VR game, worked well with my HP Reverb G2. Graphics, environments, soundtrack and gameplay is very good, very atmospheric, puzzles are well balanced with increasing difficulty although I don't like much the few that have to be done within a timeframe or on a time constraint sequence. I definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Call it attention deficit, but I tend to leave a long trail of unfinished games.  So this one gets high marks just for being engaging enough for me to finish.  Some have said that it gets easy at the end.  They are right; but it is one of the things I actually liked about it since to me it felt more like a reward to my labors than a letdown.  Viewed progressively, I'd say the puzzles started out challenging, got difficult enough by the third act for me to use the hint system once; and then midway through the fourth act got progressively easier until it was basically an almost unfettered dash to the end.  I wish more games had this curve since I hate investing lots of enjoyable time in a game only for it to ramp up so much in difficulty that by the end my enjoyment is stolen and I'm forced to cross the line where the game is making me feel like I'm at work.  Consequently, since this game didn't do that, I can really say it was fun.  I was about to also say that at around 5 hours it was kind of short for a $29.95 game, but in checking my time, it looks like I actually have about 10 hours on it, which surprised me.  So I suppose that's another plus since it was good enough me lose track of that much time.  Graphics and sound were quite nice on my Valve Index, along with some genuinely "spooky" moments.  I do agree that it would have been nice to have some more mobility, but the waypoint system does have the benefit of eliminating pointless wandering.  And as the closest thing to a negative, I felt that the scenes were disjointed enough to not make a whole lot of narrative sense; but really, the game is about the puzzles and environments, and they were cool enough keep my interest going strong.   All in all, I'll give this one a firm recommendation and hope to see another VR title like it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you've not played The Room games before, I'd recommend you play the others first. While the game play and puzzles alone in this are amazing, the plot will be a bit confusing without the backstory. They're all absolutely worth the time and money.The puzzles in this aren't as difficult to do in VR as I was thinking they might be, it played so smoothly and I didn't struggle to find things to interact with. The puzzles themselves start off simpler and become more complex as you go along, introducing new mechanics along the way, it's a great warm up. The variety in mechanics and functions of the puzzles are great. There are a few puzzles that are similar to previous games puzzles but I feel like this helps tie the games together since the puzzles are built by groups of people.I wasn't sure how much this would build on the plot since it's a VR game. The plot in this is so good, and does add more to the lore of The Room, but isn't leaving out fans that don't have VR by being a direct sequel to The Room 4. The atmosphere on this is so creepy as well, the footsteps and creaks and thunder really made me feel on edge. I know these aren't jump scare game but even so the way they build up the anticipation without an actual scare feels like a good thriller.I played The Room when it first came out on the ipod touch so many years ago, and to see that it's progressed on to VR, to see the complexity of the plot now, it's really amazing to look at where it started. I really don't think I have the words to say how good these games are, I can't wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all The Room games since the old, original The Room, followed by The Room two and three, etc. They all mesmerized me because Fireproof Games really know what are they doing. The engaging storylines, the mind-boggling-fun puzzles, and the quality of the gameplay. Not mentioning the Graphical quality of each product.But if you have VR sets JUST GO AND GET THE DARK MATTER!...VR sets bringing this game to another whole new level!Instead of just playing on the regular screen, The immersive experience will blow your mind away!Pros: Enough said, just get the game!Cons: The game is just way too short...
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Played all the other Room games before on Android and therfore this was an instant buy. It is an awesome game. I have to say that in the first three games I sometimes lost orientation where what object/unfinished puzzle was, but in VR this is way easier. Also on the phone the letters were sometimes hardly readable, but in VR no issue, just get it closer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A must-play VR title!If you've never played the previous instalments of the series, I urge you to do so!The Room VR: A Dark Matter is an excellent addition that expands on the lore ever so slightly, and is chock full of the same high quality puzzles as usual. You'd swear the game's unique mechanics were made for VR, because it's an absolutely sublime match!The game, much like the previous ones, isn't awfully long - you can finish it in a good 3 to 4 hours. There's also the fact that this one was perhaps way less difficult than previous entries, most likely because it was the first attempt to stray into VR territory. Despite all that, it's perhaps now my favourite of the series and I just can not wait to see what's next!10/10, amazing game if you have a love for puzzles and stunning, otherworldly, magical mechanisms.Play the first games first, since there is definitely a loosely linear structure, and there's references to previous ones. If you don't have VR yet, I wouldn't go out of my way to get it just for this but definitely consider playing if or once you can!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: From the beginning I liked the art and the type of puzzles. I also enjoyed the story. I was never scared, I don't like horror games and this is not one, it sets the ambient for you to feel some kind of suspense but that is all.  I want to play more of these.  It was very easy to understand the controllers, I used Index without any issues.  I used the hints a couple of times because I took a week off in the middle of the game and I was a little lost when I came back but you should not needed if you pay attention (not like me). You can also play it sitting down. You don't need a lot of space to play it. I got it on sales and it's a fantastic game to own.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. The atmosphere of the environment, the difficulty of the puzzles are so fine-tuned. Also, the optimisation of the game is so well that it runs very smooth on my low-end (GTX 1060) VR-ready computer. However, the ending of the game is just too short. Overall, it is a good game and I don't regret paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Best VR game I've played so far. Precise and easy to understand Controls, incredible graphics and a great addition to the storyline of the series.Almost all of the puzzles are are well thought out and have a well balanced difficulty. There are some exceptions that are pretty frustrating and some that are way too easy but, as I said, the Majority are fine.All in all an incredible VR game and my favorite in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I love the series, I really like this game.  It's a good sequel to the other 4 games.  The game play is exactly as I expected, and the level of detail is top-notch.It may be a bit on the pricey side, but I imagine that's because not everyone has 3D capabilities, so their audience is smaller.  It's a damn good game.  Buy it and feel like you're contributing to some solid game-makers and appreciating what they do.I look forward to many more in this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fun VR game, and one which you can do whilst sat down (just not near anything in arms reach as you will end up punching it and knocking it over). Interesting story with lots of really fun puzzles. There are a few times it got a bit frustrating as you can miss a few items or miss some subtle hints. At times I worried it could get repetitive with some of the puzzles, but I was wrong as it keeps changing them slightly and in new ways that mean you have to keep thinking and keep being observational to the environment.Only real drawback for me is not being allowed to move around the rooms free style, you can only teleport between spots. I see why they do that, so you keep close to the areas that matter, but its just a bit annoying as I like exploring the environments and dislike teleportation. But that is more feedback for the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, Brilliant puzzles which were challenging but not the most difficult I've played. This game is far the best of all the room games and by far the best VR game I've played. The graphics and audio make you feel like you're there and the story is brilliant. Please please please bring more of these out. The future is bright, the future is Room VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy this, given all the reviews stating that it was a three or four hour game. My wife told me the price was the same as an escape room (at least in my area), and those only go for an hour, which convinced me.Sadly, there's *maybe* an hour and a half of gameplay. Steam says I've played for three hours, but a good portion of that is paused time and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around to see what I can interact with.The answer to that question is "very little," unfortunately. I turned off hints before starting, but the fact that your hands react to anything you can interact with, and you can rarely interact with things while being unable to do something that progresses the game with them, so there's very little mystery about what to do and little problem solving required beyond the immediately obvious. Often the clues are in plain sight right where you need them.Maybe I'm just too accustomed to The Room's style of puzzles. I don't feel like I expect too much though. I mean, Riven in 1997 allowed you to at least touch any surface and hear what it sounded like to tap on. This game isn't so large that adding more interaction (and smooth turning please! I hate snap turning) would be a monumental undertaking.All that said, I did have fun. If I hadn't, I wouldn't wish it were longer. It's not a bad length for a game my friends and family can play when they come by. We tend to be a bit unfair about game prices, i think, and I know I'd have spent more taking the wife to a movie or the aforementioned escape room.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun and really uses the medium of Vr to enhance the puzzles. Probably worth 4 hours of gameplay or so (not quite finished myself), but in any case well worth the money if you like puzzle games. The puzzles are not too hard (and you can get some tips in game), and I only encountered 1 or 2 that really aggrevated me (I am looking at you, pipe organ).
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the game I expected from this studio, as a fan of the other games in this series that I have bought and played on mobile. I enjoyed it and found the puzzles interesting and challenging. The hint system is excellent. VR teleport system worked well and while I wished I could move freely to explore the areas, the designated teleport spots kept me only to the areas with the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful. I've loved every single The Room game thus far, the series has yet to let me down.Now don't get me wrong, this game isn't perfect.Snap Turning, Locked teleporting system between certain points? I can excuse it, since the format is important to the gameplay.But there are a few things I  excuse.Like the fact that the Or that the  now has a real world representation, and the mask looks like a Friar Tuck mask, or what Jerma fans know of as B.F. Bugleberry...Okay so maybe its forgiveable, but it does kinda take you out of the immersion.But besides immersion breaking, Only have 3/4/5 levels really feels limiting. Compared to all of the levels in The Room 2, The numerous secrets and endings of The Room 3, and the insane increase in quality and quantity of The Room: Old Sins, the decline in quantity, and slight decrease in quality, may make this game easy to pass up for Fans of the series.HOWEVER (COMMA) If this is your first time playing The Room Series, or you just want a fun puzzle game, especially one in VR, as rare as they are, this one is definitely a (albeit scratched) Diamond in the Rough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: First i thought 30 euros? Is quite a lot nowdays.Then again...Ive played all 3 The Rooms on my phone.So i decided to buy it.I cant really say something bad about the game.Its a really nice game. The mechanics are really well implemented.For me its a 9/10 and i give it a 9 cause i wanted to play more.Thanks for making this kind of beautiful game.Its a really nice game. The mechanics are really well implemented.Well im not really good at writing reviews. BUT THANK YOU GUYS A LOT.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect setting for a VR Room challenge. Having played all previous The Room games, this was a fantastic addition that allows any VR player to jump right in. The puzzles are just challenging enough to where you're not speeding through but not so challenging that you'll get stuck often. If this is your first The Room game, I can almost guarantee you're going to want to download the others straight afterwards. And then you'll be like the rest of us who wish other puzzle games came anywhere close to Fireproof's level and try our best to wait for the next The Room game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I read reviews saying this game was only 4-5 hours of playtime. I bought the game to see if the quality could justify the price.  This is far from a 30$ experience. Well polished and interesting puzzles I admit but lack of free movement displeases me greatly. Doesn't have any flexibility for people who prefer free movement or smooth turning. There isn't any replay value after you complete each puzzle either. I really want to give it a thumbs up but the current asking price is absurd. I would only recommend on sale for 9.99-14.99$
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room brings together in a single game all the aspects that I like the most about video games: puzzles, atmosphere (especially atmosphere!), Graphics and, of course, VR.It has been a pleasure to play it, from start to finish, and it is worth every one euro it costs.For asking, I would like it to be longer ... maybe new DLC with new research ... that would be great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed the Room games ever since the very first one, and I was --still-- blown away by this VR experience.  Rich, lush detail on every surface, a world that felt real and lived in, rather than pristine and texture-less.  Excellent puzzles, and adds to the lore of the intricate, deep universe that they've slowly built for the games.  One of the best VR experiences I've had, and great fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles in this game are amazing and and the game feels very immersive. The transforming elements of this game lend them selves very well to VR. I would highly recommend people play the mobile games as well as these games a a continuous story. Over all I loved the game as I am a big fan of this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room VR is a fascinating take on the puzzle experience with Virtual Reality. The game feels more like an escape room than a traditional puzzle game. The use of ambiance and story telling drives home an unsettling feeling throughout the levels of the game. If you enjoy the darkness of the Lovecraftian genre then I'd highly recommend this game. Pros:- Amazing ambiance- Intriguing puzzles that utilize VR mechanicsMeh:- The puzzles are not especially difficultCons:- The game is short (Less than 4 hours)
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I love The Room series.As usual, the puzzles and environments are beautifully crafted and the world is interesting. However, this time around I found the game too short and the puzzles too easy. In all fairness, I think this game is worth the money you pay, so the length and difficulty issues are more personal preference/skill level thing. I did become frustrated with the lack of interaction between my hands and the other non-puzzle objects. But most of all, I found the ending to be too brief and anti climactic.This is the 5th "The Room" I've played. I very much enjoyed the VR experience and am looking forward to more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most amazing VR experience I've had yet which when compared against the titans I've played like Hellblade, Senua's sacrifice & Azgards Wrath is saying something.  It does not take a beefy system to play which is nice.  I rarely (if ever) finish a game but I finished this one over 3 days fighting through the pain of using glasses in my oculus.  I've ordered prescription lenses now for the oculus, because of this game....Absolutely jaw dropping amazing, if you enjoy puzzles & VR this is a must have game.  I simply can not endorse this game strongly enough, I wouldn't change a thing.Please do make another!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Fireproof Games has a history of producing fantastic puzzle games and while this game is their first venture into VR, it is certainly no exception. Those familiar with the games in the Room series will find themselves right at home as this game is very similar to previous games in the series.Like the previous games, the story continues to be excellent and very intriguing. It does make some heavy references to events in previous games (specifically from ), so I’d highly recommend playing at least the first three games before trying this one, but it isn’t required to understand the basic premise if you really want to play this one first. There were also some fairly heavy references to witchcraft in a portion of the game, which I also wasn't crazy about, but despite this, I still really enjoyed the story and what they did with it.The puzzles were also quite similar to the style you would find in previous games in the series, although they obviously have some different constraints and freedoms given that this is a VR game. The puzzles and mechanics continued to be excellent, for the most part, although I did find the VR controls to be a tad bit finicky with some puzzles. While I had no major issues using the controls in this game, I did occasionally miss the precision of a mouse for some of the smaller items and mechanisms that must be interacted with. Some of the puzzles were the opposite, however, and were vastly improved with VR controls (specifically those the puzzles where you must  to solve them), so all in all this balanced out pretty well.The visuals were fantastic, as always, and it was quite exciting to be immersed into such an interesting world. The game was also very stable, and I had no issues with bugs or crashes.The biggest issue most people will likely have with this game is the price. It is currently $34 CAN, which is $25 CAN more than even , which came out several months ago, and it took me roughly the same length of time to play through both of these games. Thus, if all you’re looking for is a fantastic puzzle game for an outstanding price, I'd highly recommend trying out the other four games in the series first, as you can buy all of them right now for less than the price of this title (and for almost nothing during a sale). However, if you've played through those already or you're looking for one of the best puzzle games you can find in VR, then I'd highly recommend picking this game up, as I'm not aware of any other puzzle games in the VR space who have come close the quality of this title. This is a fantastic VR puzzle game with great mechanics, an intriguing story, phenomenal visuals, and no stability issues to be found. While it is a bit expensive for the length, I'd highly recommend it for anyone who's played through the other games in the series and is looking for more, or anyone who wants to enjoy a fantastic VR puzzle game and can tolerate paying a bit more for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: In have really mixed feelings about this game.The game is both beautiful, atmospheric and spine tinglingly creepy. The game also benefits hugely from the VR visuals. In fact I'd say it’s visually astonishing. The audio is also really well done, with some great spatial sound.The puzzles are well presented, engaging, logical and just the right difficulty level to present a challenge without being impossible. You'll frequently find yourself stumped for a minutes, but never for hours. But the weak implementation of motion controllers, really drags down all the fantastic work. The pressure required to pick things up is way too low meaning that everything is held in a vice like grip making putting object down difficult. Your hands don’t actually seem to interact with anything, happily clipping through all the objects in the game. When you are holding things your hands will inexplicably snap to objects the item can interact with, and if you hold onto something immobile like a door handle you can then walk away leaving your hands behind.However I have hugely enjoyed the time I've put in so I'm giving it a thumbs up. It’s worth buying. It could be so much more though, and I really really hope the developers work on the hand interaction because as it stands it really lets the game down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there were more puzzle room type games in VR. This one is excellent but does have some problems. There were parts where it felt like you had to get everything done in exactly the right sequence or you couldn't move forward. I like puzzle rooms and escape rooms that allow you to shift between multiple approaches and problems when you get stuck instead of forcing you to bash your head against them one at a time until you solve them
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you're itching to play escape room games, but can't because the venues are still closed due to the pandemic, then this game will definitely satisfy that itch! It's a classic The Room game, with its wonderfully crafted and carefully made puzzles, and the entire experience is enhanced by being in VR, letting you closely interact with the puzzles, just like you would in a real life escape room game! I've bought all their previous The Room games, but even though their puzzles are just as good, the feel of this one just can't be compared to those other ones. Fireproof Games have once again outdone themselves!
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The best VR escape room type experience to date. I was stumped in 5 different areas but managed to get past it without hints. A lot of the puzzles make sense when you think about it. The only one that didnt make sense was the tarot cards. This was the only time I used a hint. Other than that my only gripe would be the ending. The final stage felt rushed as there were next to no puzzles to solve
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The Room feels like one of the most obvious franchises to move into VR. All the familiar mechanics translate into VR naturally, and the more exotic environmental tricks feel even more impressive when you're actually in the world. I found it interesting that not being able to interact with all the objects would normally be a negative in a VR game, but in this kind of an environmental puzzle game it feels like a natural way to indicate where to focus your attention. The additional objects and scenery still add to the immersion, and the creepy atmosphere from earlier games is there stronger than ever (it isn't a horror game, though). I'm ready for more VR Rooms.The difficulty level is on par with earlier games - nice and rewarding head-scratchers, but nothing too obtuse. I needed the hint system a few times because I didn't notice a detail that could be manipulated.(edit) One small wish regarding controls - a smooth turning option would be nice, as I find snap-turning more disorienting. Not a big deal in this game, though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Over the last three days I've been playing The Room VR: A Dark Matter after work, so about an hour or so - I've just completed the game and if you're a fan of the previous games or have never played; give this and the back catalogue a go - you will not be disappointed.  Yes it's around 4 hours, but those 4 hours over three nights while yes tired have still been an enjoyable mind bending experience.Given this game is in VR, I was hoping for a tad more two handed interaction, but hey it's their first VR game and I will play through the four titles I have The Room 1-3 + The Room VR again in anticipation of the next title.The puzzles can be...confusing the hints however do help.If fireproof games, want to expand the genre, perhaps branching puzzles for committing errors, although a shorter game for those who get the puzzles right doesn't seem fair and these titles and puzzle games in general take long enough to do any way.I'm not sure if the character models used in the game was mo-cap, as they were brilliantly animated in the near silent cut scenes.Yes buy the back catalogue and enjoy a series of games in a sadly under represented genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through the entire series and enjoyed every part, especially The Room 4: Old Sins.The Room VR: A Dark Matter is the reason why I bought VR in the first place: The immersion in this game is really intense!The puzzles are great, logical and very VR-friendly.The different scenarios look great and are exciting.Get it during sale and you won't regret it.If you want to persuade your friends to buy a VR headset, show them this title.10/10Would play with mummies again
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the room and you have a VR set: GET IT! It's worth it. If you don't know the room, but like puzzle games: this is for you! You might not get the references to the other games, but you will definitely have fun playing it. Can be played in standing or sitting positions, works even if you don't have too much space. As always: it could have been just slightly longer :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, as the previous episodes. However I don't have the feeling that the VR is a real plus compared to other episodes. For me it is the same good experience of solving good puzzles. I am just a bit sad that the game is really REALLY short, something like 2h30-3h to finish it, which is far below the precedent games :/
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

_childDocuments_.review: The British Institute of Archaeology, London, 1908: The disappearance of an esteemed Egyptologist prompts a Police investigation into the unknown. Explore cryptic locations, examine fantastic gadgets and uncover an otherworldly discovery which blurs the line between reality and illusion. Designed from the ground up for the unique capabilities of virtual reality, players can inhabit the spine-tingling world of The Room and interact with its strange contraptions in this compelling new chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Room VR: A Dark Matter

name: Yakuza 4 Remastered
detailed_description: Experience the fourth chapter of the Kazuma Kiryu saga in 1080p and 60fps. 2010, Tokyo. A shooting incident one night in a red-light district sets the city swirling with human desires and clamor. It was supposed to be a ''common incident'' for this town... until the appearance of one woman burdened with sorrow. As if drawn to a flame, men of the city's dark underground are gathered, one after another, at the door of the ''legendary yakuza'' Kazuma Kiryu. As the fates of these four men overlap, the story of a miracle created by the passionate and violent way of life begins to takes shape. Take control of multiple protagonists, a first for the series, allowing for unprecedented story depth and battle action. Three new protagonists, each with a rich personality, will leave their impact before the story concludes. Complete The Dragon of Dojima’s journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 4 feels, in different facets, both like a clear advancement of Yakuza 3 and a hard pivot in another direction. The previous game completed a trilogy of sorts even with its goofy fakeout-cliffhanger ending, feeling as though it left Kiryu settled in a new, satisfying place in his life, ready to move on from all the yakuza nonsense for good. Story-wise, Yakuza 4 follows through on this by featuring three brand-new playable characters before you get to take control of Kiryu again, easily constituting nearly three quarters of the game. Each of the four playable characters starts their story in a different place from the others, but together they constitute a surprisingly well-tied-together collective narrative, each character flowing into the next one (albeit with rather abrupt perspective shifts - the best one was easily Akiyama into Saejima), their actions having a trickle-down effect that cascades through to the final chapter. It's a huge change from simply playing as Kiryu, and a fundamentally different structure from the only other character-switching game in the modern play order in 0, as you don't switch back and forth between any of the four - once you're done with one of them, you're done with them until the finale. It's a bold move for the series, and one that I think ends up being done rather well.Visually and gameplay-wise, Yakuza 3 and 4 feel very closely tied into one another - fitting, since there was just over a year between the releases of 3 and 4. It very much feels like these games were developed back to back, as while there are advancements in the combat (Blockuza this is not), and the chase segments have been improved, Kamurocho feels mostly the same, Kiryu's model is clearly ripped straight from 3, and there's a familiarity to 4 that you'll feel if you play 3 and 4 close together. A welcome change is in the fighting styles of the four protagonists, as each one is distinct from each other - Akiyama is purely kick-based, able to combo and juggle with ease, Saejima is focused on power moves and tanking hits, Tanimura has both flow and aggression in his barrage of punches and kicks, and Kiryu feels very much fully-formed from the moment you take control of him, fully living up to his reputation as a yakuza legend from the get-go, rather than having to re-learn all of the moves that actually have impact. Each one has a learning curve, but you get the hang of them pretty quickly, as the fundamentals underneath them all are the same, and each style is satisfying in its own way.Story-wise, 4 is characteristically both strong and absurd, with several absolutely heart-wrenching segments throughout, though there are a couple of twists that are utterly groan-inducing. 4 is one of the worst offenders in this regard, with major plot elements and individual scenes that test your patience and suspension of disbelief, particularly regarding Saejima's circumstances and actions early in his chapter. Tanimura also starts off supremely unlikeable, and only comes around if you do several of the substories that focus on the area he grew up in and the community he's part of. By contrast, Kiryu's involvement was surprisingly believable and natural given how easily he could have been written out of the series entirely after 3, and it was very satisfying to get to his part of the game, almost like a reward after playing through the stories of three other characters.4 isn't without its faults, of course - the way progression is reset at the start of each new character's part meant a tutorial segment at the start of each part, along with a grind to build up your health and Heat back to respectable levels. Saejima's combat is easily the worst of the four, being slow, plodding, and one-note, and he gets paired with one of the dumbest early-game bosses in the entire series in Saito, an enormous style mismatch for him that does nothing but irritate. As mentioned above, some of the twists that the game's entire story is built upon are either nonsense or infuriating, undermining some of the otherwise well-considered themes and narrative threads of the game. The cabaret club minigame continues to be absolutely worthless, and the segmented nature of the game felt as though it discouraged me from exploring substories, though that may just be my personal distaste for how the early PS3 games handle substory discovery and tracking. Though Kamurocho is expanded with the addition of the underground sections, rooftops, and underground mall, I was a little disappointed that no other cities were featured - the only non-Kamurocho locations are the Okinawa prison, a small section of Morning Glory and its beaches, and the docks accessible from Kamurocho.On the whole, Yakuza 4 continues the series' track record of engaging story, satisfying combat, and generous helping of goofy nonsense, managing to be another vital entry. It takes risks by widening the focus beyond Kiryu, covering subject matter that surprised me, and feels in some ways like it really has something to say. Even with the quick turnaround on development time, it feels like RGG Studio was determined to advance the franchise in just its second main-series PS3 entry, and I think they did a great job on it. Recommended, as always.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Yakuza 3, 4 is a much-needed breath of fresh air gameplay-wise and a lot of the "soul" of the series came back.Splitting from a purely Kiryu-focused storyline is really well done. My opinion is that Akiyama has the most endearing personality and mannerisms out of the three new joiners, but I think Saejima and Tanimura have more compelling story and mechanics. The indisputable fact here is that all three of them are great and they grow on you quickly. The gameplay loop really hasn't changed but RGG got to express a lot of different playstyles between the four characters.Yakuza 4 hasn't dealt with  of the poor quality-of-life issues that 3 was plagued with, but it's dealt with some of them. No more begging your enemies to stop blocking and not attacking you, but some sidequest opponents aren't worth fighting because they're just reading your inputs and it saps any interest out of the fight. The sidestories are improved, in my opinion, regaining more of the "soul" they had in the previous games. The level of "soul" in Revelations also skyrocketed from 3 to 4 which was overall a really enjoyable thing.While Yakuza 3's story went off the rails rather quickly and upped the ante at any possible opportunity (which ended up being the strongest draw of the game), Yakuza 4's was much more interesting and nuanced.  If you're this deep in the series, you already know if a character's , but there were still quite a few curveballs and an ending that absolutely blew me away in its scale.It's not without its problems... ... etc., but Yakuza 4 is definitely a return to form from Yakuza 3 and is well-worth trudging through Yakuza 3's gameplay prior.

_childDocuments_.review: (Possible light spoilers)Yakuza 4 turned out to be one of my top favorites that I've played(so far) in the Yakuza Series. Apparently some people find some of the plot twists in this particular entry into the series to be too over the top, but to be honest? I actually like the plot twists in this entry: This is because while they are abit jarring at first, it adds additional stakes to the story, and honestly, I think this entries plot twists are a jab at previous Yakuza entries' plot twists; and with this in mind, the plot twists works with the over-all tone of the series, because if you have ever play a Yakuza game, you know that this series doesn't have any trouble poking fun at itself from time to time.Plot twists aside. This game is obviously a vast improve of Yakuza 3 Remastered: It looks alot better(still not modern graphics, but they aren't everything), Mechanics are an improvement from Yakuza 3.Story-wise, I would say that this is one of the better stories in the series, even with its flaws(looking at you, creepy-ass orphanage scene). After playing the series this far(In order of the when the story takes place), This entry feels like a breath of fresh air after the relatively somewhat unmemorable story of Yakuza Kiwami 2, and the slow starting Yakuza 3. This is, in my opinion because Yakuza 4 follows 4 different characters(sounds abit fimiliar to those who have played Yakuza 0, I know), and shows the evolution of the stories of each of these characters. People also apparently complain about the somewhat short time you get to play Kiryu as compared to other characters in the game. I like Kiryu as much as any fan from the Yakuza series, but honestly, I feel like the amount of playtime you get as Kiryu is fitting to the game, as it gives these new beautiful characters more time to shine.All in all out of the five Yakuza games i've played in the franchise so far(being: Yakuza 0, Kiwami 1, Kiwami 2, Yakuza 3 Remastered, and Yakuza 4 Remastered in that order), I would honestly place Yakuza 4 Remastered at atleast a solid Third place(atleast, so far), beating Kiwami 2, and Yakuza 3 Remastered. It's a pretty good addition to the Yakuza series, and would recommend it even if you just play Yakuza to play Kiryu.

_childDocuments_.review: This was going to be the "last" game of the series back in the day, same with 3. Glad the series didn't end here, though if it did it would have ended on a high note.In this game you may be disappointing if you expected to play as Kiryu from the start, cause you play it at the Part 4 of the 5 parts. Each part focuses on a new character, with certain styles with similarities from the ones in Kiwami 1.Not gonna spoil any of the parts, but i'll write my opinion on them.Part 1: Akiyama. My favorite character of the new 3 that got introduced in this game. A smug and kind hearted loan shark who wants to make lives better for everyone else. Has a fast and kick-based moveset and a great easy-going attitude.Part 2: Saejima. My most disliked character to play as. We start with a pretty bad segment with no directions where all we have to do is talk to every single NPC. Not that bad or complicated as some people complained in the forums. His gameplay style is really, really slow. Clunky.  All about charging your finishers after each combo. Feels really bad and unintuitive.Part 3: Tanimura. He was alright, until he wasn't. At first I liked Tanimura, his style has a counter, that does absolutely nothing, specially against bosses. His moveset is all about the grapple finisher/heat moves, thing is, in this game those heat moves barely deal any damage against bosses, and is your main source of damage as Tanimura. Also Tanimura has a story chapter that is barely 5 minutes long, what the hell?. Also for the purists who wanna experience the game as intended, Tanimura's appearance and voice got changed and recasted because the japanese actor who played as him is no longer in the industry. Theres a mod that restores his appearance and voice if you're interested however.Part 4: Kiryu. Wow Kiryu sure has step himself up  from 3. Plays great, much better than Yakuza 3's, more smooth. Same moves. As always is a joy to play as Kiryu.The story was pretty good, if a bit overdone. As you'd expect in a game with 4 characters, each story unveils something of bigger thing and then all stories meet eachother for a big finale.And we get to the biggest problem this game shown to me: Its extremely, badly designed, worst Yakuza boss yet. The final boss. No spoilers, but this boss is garbage. In the fight this one has 10 adds and all the boss does is run run and shoot you while the 10 adds get in the way. And you're playing as a character that isn't good against crowds or has any real tools against them. The boss before this one was also not good at all, it was garbage to fight too, but not as bad as that one, this one just blocks most if not all your attacks, has 2 counter moves, can't be staggered and all the problems in Yakuza 3.However, the story was quite enjoyable. I do recommend everyone who enjoyed the previous Yakuza to try this one and finish it. Don't let the small bumps remove you from this otherwise good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza 4 takes what Yakuza 3 did and greatly polished and refined it. Whether it's the more fluid combat, slight changes in the map, and the significantly better side missions, Yakuza 4 is just an improvement over the previous game in nearly every way. Along with this, Yakuza 4 switches things up by making the player play as multiple different characters. Even though it did take a bit to get used to the new characters, once their stories and personalities got fleshed out, they were a joy to play as. Moreover, every character has a unique fighting style and move set; they aren't just a reskin of Kiryu. However, even though Yakuza 4 does a lot right, I did find the story to be a bit worse than Yakuza 3. While the story is not bad by any means, it just lacks the emotion that Yakuza 3 had. Still, outside of some questionable plot points, the story is pretty good. Overall, Yakuza 4 is another great entry in the Yakuza series. For fans of the previous games, I'd highly suggest giving it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Yakuza game to feature multiple playable protagonists. Each one of them represent the Four Eastern Gods (Seiryu the Azure Dragon, Suzaku the Vermillion Bird, Byakko the White Tiger, and Genbu the Black Tortoise)Shun Akiyama represents the Vermillion Bird due to his fast and elegant fighting style. He also has a red coat, which is the color of the Vermillion Bird.Taiga Saejima represents the White Tiger as he has the most brute strength and has a tiger tattoo.Masayoshi Tanimura represents the Black Tortoise as his fighting style is heavily based on parrying. He also has the thickest coat, representing the Tortoise's shell.Kiryu Kazuma is obviously the Azure Dragon, though he doesn't have as much brute strength as Saejima, he has more technique which makes them equal if they were to fight. He also has a Dragon Tattoo.The game's only hated for a stupid plot device (rubber bullets), but other than that it's really good. It's just really refreshing to have new protagonists and fighting styles especially if you start from 0, which means you've played as Kiryu for 4 games straight.

_childDocuments_.review: Major story spoilers up ahead. Was loving this game until *that* plot twist just made me lose all respect for this story and had to change my recommendation immediately. The entire story is just a huge waste of potential. It starts off great but then it's just plot twist on top of plot twist and it just ruined the entire story experience for me. I've played 0-4 so far and this is easily the worst story in the entire Yakuza series so far. Gameplay is also terrible in many other ways too. Yakuza 3 combat gets a lot of hate but at least that game had Mine and Joji, some of the best bosses in the entire franchise, while Y4 has Saito, who is easily one of the worst bosses this series has ever had. He is on the level of Kyohei Jingu from Yakuza Kiwami and the Man in Black from Kiwami 2 with how annoying and difficult he is, and Katsuragi’s 4 goons were also extremely frustrating to deal with, and I hear Munakata is just godawful to fight. As for the master training, they're annoying. Saejima's requires you to play baseball to complete, Kiryu's consists of 3 fights against laughably easy enemies, and Akiyama's was annoying, especially when he had an SMG. Tanimura's however is the absolute worst. Nair is just so godawful to go through and takes forever to exploit the wall bounce so you can actually get a combo off of her. The four protagonists are the best part of this entire game. As characters, every one of them is unique and likable, but some have issues. Akiyama is fast but he severely lacks counter options and most of his heat moves are restricted to specific terrains so fighting a group with him isn't fun. Tanimura's attack combos are boring and his parry just feels so out of place in this series, and it's not even helpful because most of the time the parry pushes enemies too far away so they recover right before you can land an attack, oh and the fight against Sugiuchi sucks because he becomes immune to parry so Tanimura has very little options outside of poking and running. Kiryu is fine, he plays just like in Y3 and once you get Tiger Drop and Tiger Parry you'll destroy most enemies effortlessly (except for the fight where the 4 Ueno lieutenants gang up on you). Saejima is by far my favorite character to use. Once you get enough abilities, he's an absolute beast to use and his heat moves are brutal. No complaints gameplay wise.The main reason I decided to change my recommendations was because Saejima as a character was just done so dirty, because of *that* plot twist. The rubber bullet plot twist is legitimately one of the most pathetic plot twists I have ever seen in any kind of media and it just destroys Saejima's character arc entirely. If it wasn't for that twist Saejima would have been a top 3 character for me easily but now he's just ok. It's still fun watching his interactions with Majima and seeing him get confused about the modern world but wow that scene where he just breaks down in tears at the coliseum because he realizes that everyone there will only ever see him as a monster was so emotional and made me tear up, and now it means nothing because he didn't actually kill anyone, little ♥♥♥♥♥ Katsuragi did. God forbid we play a character who has actually killed in a game centered around a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ criminal empire. Well, at the very least Kiryu is the same as ever, and Shun Akiyama is a great character. Tanimura is pretty good as well but wow the story behind the original model is just so sad. 100% gonna use the mod to restore his original model. TL;DR: A game that started out promising pisses any semblance of good away around Tanimura's chapter. Stupid, cheap plot twists and betrayals you can see coming miles away. Gameplay that is only marginally better than Yakuza 3's except this time it lacks good boss fights. To be frank, I don't understand the positive reviews at all and disagree with almost all of them, and the characters being fun isn't enough to redeem this game for me.
