_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the most ambitious Yakuza game i've played in terms of scope, length, story and characters. There are 5 different playable characters in this, that all live in 5 different cities, so there are 3 new cities you get to explore which haven't been featured in other Yakuza games, taking place in Nagoya, Fuku oka (i had to add a space to it becuase Steam censors this word lol) and Sapporo and of course Tokyo (Kamurocho) and Osaka (sotenbori).It plays out in a similar way to Yakuza 4 where you play each characters individual story first before they all come together in the finale. They also have side story mini games you can play through, a taxi one for Kiryu, where you also compete in street racing. Saejima has a hunting mini game, think Red Dead but rubbish. Haruka has a dancing rhythm based mini game. Lastly new character Shinada has a baseball batting center mini game, Akiyama doesn't get a side story mini game.I enjoyed part 1 with Kiryu and actually finished his taxi mini game, it's interesting they keep giving Kiryu these jobs you wouldn't usually associate him with.Saejima is just an awful character in my opinion, he was bad in Yakuza 4 and he's just as bad here, he's like a dumber less interesting version of Kiryu but with a f*cking terrible tanky slow fighting style, what's worse is they repeat some of the story beats they had you doing in the last game with him, who's idea was that, i don't think anyone was dying to play as him again, if you are a fan of his let me know because... why.Ok so this is where things start to take a weird and for the most part unwelcome turn, you play as Haruka and her whole story is centered around her becoming a pop idol, and you are forced to play dance rhythm mini games, like the karaoke mini games. I'm not a fan of QTE's or button tapping rhythm games in general. It's only really 2 chapters that forces you to play through this with her, but i think the way they did this was a mistake. If this was a separate mode or something you unlocked after completing the game i wouldn't have a problem with it, but halfway through the story it makes a sudden stop from being a brawler to this.It would have been cool if you got to fight Yakuza as Haruka, i mean her dad is Kiryu ffs! you're telling me he didn't teach her how to defend herself all that time they were together? it feels like a missed opportunity. I also don't know who this is meant to appeal to either, were they trying to get more teenage girls to play a Yakuza game? because i don't think they will stick around for 20 hours to get to the Haruka part of the story. I will say if you knew nothing about the jpop industry like me then her story is insightful in that sense and shows you what it's probably like to be an idol in Japan, they even have mini games where you have to shake hands with fans and go to events to promote yourself.The new character Shinada i thought was ok, but his whole arc and story is about baseball and you are just wondering for most of it what this has to do with the larger story, eventually all these character stories do tie into the larger narrative being told, but it feels like they got bored of making nothing but Yakuza games so included a baseball and pop idol game in here.Overall there is a ton to do here, there are so many mini games and sub stories, i have so far mainly focused on completing the main story, so there is a lot of content i haven't played or mentioned in this review, you really get your money's worth with this game, and if you don't feel like playing every Yakuza game then you could do worse than starting with this one as it gives you so much, and the mini games i did play weren't broken like they were in Yakuza 3.I should mention i had issues with the framerate and cutscenes skipping slightly. The remedy for this is to turn off the Steam overlay while playing, so try doing that if you have this issue.

I did complete major things like victory road and hostesses as well as all substories and side stories including all the missions for all the characters. The only training I didn't complete was Shinada's baseball coach because a game of pool is impossible to win.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it as part of the bundle (I have not finished this game pre-review)What can I say so far, ive picked it up and put it down and pretty much lost interest. Why would i want to become  a taxi driver? Why would i want to become a hunter in snowy peaks? _childDocuments_.review: Mixed about this one, I still like it, but DAMN some things could've been done better. This is a long game since it follows 5 protagonists, and unlike Y4 it feels a bit dragged out, mainly in part 3 i felt personally. The story is a bit hard to follow until the finale. Though this game is probably one of the best in terms of combat.This game also features Hatsune Miku, meaning it is automatically the best game in the series despite my criticisms. Play it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like in yakuza 4 you play as multiple protagonists. 5 to be exact. Kiryuu, saejima and akiyama (from yakuza 4), haruka (first playable female char!) and a brand new character called Shinada.To me yakuza 5 was simultaneously the best and worst yakuza game that I've played. Sometimes I was bored out of my mind, and sometimes I was having so much fun!To me the worst part was the main plot. It had some good plot twist and reveals, but it had an extremly bad pacing. It felt like it dragged out for way too long. It was like 80% of the plot was filler.While all the optional/side content and parts not related to the main conflict were really fun. I had a blast It's one of the yakuza games that I want to go back to and get to at least 80% completion. There's so much to do and experiance.

_childDocuments_.review: The legendary dragon returns to the criminal underworld of Yakuza. Kazuma Kiryu, once known as the Dragon of Dojima, was living a quiet life as a taxi driver in Hakata after severing all his ties with the underworld.  However, at the dawn of the bloody war between the Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance, Kazuma is forced to accept his inescapable fate and returns to a life filled with crime and violence to protect his loved ones.

name: The Last Spell
detailed_description: In a desperate move to end all wars that have been rampaging the world for decades, the mages provoked The Cataclysm. Massive balls of pure magic obliterated nearly everything. A strange purple mist propagated everywhere, with hordes of bloodthirsty mutants coming at night. Our only hope is now to banish all magic from this accursed world by casting The Last Spell, requiring several days of uninterrupted incantation whilst a few strained Heroes try to protect those damned mages. The Last Spell is a tactical RPG with roguelite elements in which you have to defend a city against hordes of deadly enemies. During daytime, prepare your Heroes, carefully choose how to rebuild your Haven and position your defenses. Over the night, exterminate all the monsters coming at your walls with a large range of weapons and skills. Then heal, level up, and repeat until the Magic Seal is broken. Turn-Based Tactical RPG: ● The whole RPG package: a flurry of stats, skills, perks, traits… and more. ● Tons of items: armors, weapons, trinkets and potions… with their own stats and skills, as well as optional random modifiers. Each weapon has its own skillset and playstyle! ● Build your own classes : upgrade your heroes with stat bonuses and perks, and equip whatever gear you wish. Want to make a glass cannon rogue/mage fighting with a gun? Do it! ● Manage your squad of heroes: they’re strong, but they are few and have access to limited resources. Healing and mana are scarce, so try to find a good balance. Hordes of Evil: ● Think and adapt: you will face swarms of deadly enemies with only a few hardened heroes. Optimize your positioning and plan your actions: big AOE attacks, crowd control, buffs, poison... Every Action Point counts towards another day of survival. ● Enemies have strengths and weaknesses that will challenge your wits. And because hard is not enough for us, be prepared for the terrifying Elites ! ● Each map will end with epic fights against unique mind-bending bosses . Protect the Haven: ● Rebuild the city to help you in-between fights. Get healed, forge new magical weapons, get new heroes. Spend your resources wisely, commander! ● Build up your defenses : walls, traps, towers, catapults… every tiny bit of help is welcome. ● Protect the Magic Circle at all costs! If you lose it, humanity is doomed. ● 5 Havens to protect, each with their own setup and challenges requiring you to tailor your strategy to beat the Great Evil. Roguelite Elements: ● The game is meant to be hard . You will fail… A lot. But every time you do, you’ll grow harder, better, faster, stronger! ● Procedurally generated enemy waves, characters, weapons and a ton of unlockables will keep you entertained until the real world collapses. ● Tailor each run thanks to the Omens : a limited amount of bonuses that can be picked for the upcoming run. Do you prefer more Action Points, more characters, sturdier defenses, better loot? Experiment to find your preferred tools of destruction. ● Scale the difficulty to your liking, with 6 levels of Apocalypse to entertain even the most hardcore players. Headbanger Soundtrack: ● Over 25 tracks of thunderous synths-driven progressive metal to guide you through this joyous slaughterfest ● Composed by the incredible Rémi - The Algorithm - Gallégo

short_description: Defend the last bastion of humanity with your squad of heroes! Exterminate fiendish monsters with magic and brute force by night and re-build your battered city defenses by day in this tactical RPG with rogue-lite mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't tell you that you can Alt+F4 out of the game to start a night over, and honestly it's not really a good idea to do so while you're still learning the game and unlocking things at a decent pace. However, knowing this is an option later on down the line makes the game possible to recommend. Having to restart an 8+ hour run from scratch on some of the longer maps is a very hard sell, but with a night-restart it's a very easy game to recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Reviews suggested this game was really hard, some even suggesting it was technically impossible to beat on first run. So on my first play (at normal difficulty), I took it very slowly, read tooltips thoroughly and considered my options and strategy carefully. Over the course of 6 hours I made it through 4/12 nights without losing any vital building or character and I'm about to start the 5th. Have to take a break now for a meal and thought I'd drop a review to emphathize that difficulty is actually ok, at this moment of time. Unless, of course, nights 5-12 are much harder than the prior. Anyway, I really enjoyed the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the runs are long, but knowing this going into the game and personally not minding, was not an issue for me. In fact it's a boon; more bang for your buck! This scratches many itches coming from playing the likes of Into the Breach and XCOM to death; tactical, turn-based roguelikes centred around skill-specific units, with pathways for perks and upgrades. Throw in The Algorithm for the soundtrack and I'm sold.Early days as far as release 1.0 is concerned and I'm only halfway through the second map, but haven't experienced any issues or found the difficulty particularly taxing so far on normal difficulty.A couple of gripes: we should be able to refund our 'tainted essence' from favours that are not yet 100% funded (or at least have a 'confirm/cancel' option before leaving the page), and same for constructions; before leaving the production phase we should be able to refund materials from placed defences before they are permanently confirmed, instead of just having a demolish option.All in all however, from my limited 15 hours of gameplay, I'd give it a solid 8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Starts a little slow (single-target weapons and a horde of zombies is a slog) but really picks up once you unlock more weapon types. And boy, are there a lot of weapon types. Seems almost like there are *too many* possible builds between semi-randomized character talent trees (perks) and weapons, but it also goes a long way towards making each run really feel unique.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. Worth the purchase even at this stage. If developers continue to work on it, can easily become a must buy.Needs:   * some QoL changes.   * more than 12 nights (or more than 12 nights in apoc levels)   * a rebalance on the base building of the game        - gold mines are too essential. without them difficulty is very high. with them diffiulty nearly evaporates        - inn also breaks game. can go from 3 characters barely surviving a night to 7 characters breezing            through the next night.   * a rethink on how apoc levels work.  They increase the difficulty of the game for follow up playthroughs,       however unlocks received that make you stronger end up making apoc levels actually easier than the       original playthrough. which makes the replayability more of a grind than actually entertaining. (new       towns with new layouts, new mobs with unique traits, skills etc, more nights, new win conditions or fail       conditions. these are the things that make a new playthrough worth doing. NOT mob hp increased 15%)This game is already so good and has enough polish that I can easily recommend it as is. Most of my minor complaints are already things the developers have already said they are working on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm at lakeburg day 11. I cheated. Still can't beat the game and there's still 2 more cities left to go. The developers have lost their mind. I lost a 3 hour run and now i have to redo it several times just to grind enough exp and unlock enough challenges just to beat the current city...Absolutely ridiculous. no wonder this game is dropping off fast. looks like a fun game but its made by viscious developpers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game stifles your early progression by locking it behind the in-game premium currency or various tasks you have to do such as building a certain number of structures. This on its own is not terrible, except some of these feel like basic quality of life improvements to give you a fighting chance of beating levels, such as the Inn which allows you to have more than the paltry 3 it starts you with.This is made much worse by how it will take you hours to get to the end of any level, with it taking about 5 hours getting to the end of the second stage, Lakeburg, only to be wiped out because I had built my characters in such a way that they could not kill the boss.Which on that note, bosses all rely on some form of gimmick, one that you will not be at all aware of going into the fight the first try, practically guaranteeing a loss and a waste of the past 5 or so hours you spent getting to that point.One boss requires ranged damage, another requires high movement (and to a lesser degree, the ability to ignore line of sight), and all rely on drip-feeding the boss phases to you, usually by adding a turn of waiting after you kill it once before it respawns, to artificially make things more difficult by allowing enemies to get closer in numbers you cannot hope to manage.All this might be fine were it not for the huge time investment, most roguelikes will have you spend at most a couple hours a run, making a loss less impactful but if you spend your entire free time in a day playing a level just to lose at the very end it is frustrating beyond belief.Unlike something like say Darkest Dungeon where a full playthrough will take a great amount of time, having a hero die is only a bump in the road in the gran scheme of things.If a hero dies in the Last Spell, you are all but guaranteed to lose, once again wasting all that time you just spent.If you play the game, play on boundless mode with every omen you think might be fun to help make the experience less frustrating, but I would personally recommend just passing on the game or waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A very deep and engaging game, the game is very well balanced and at first i was a bit overwhelmed by all the mechanism and different weapon but it truly makes you feel awesome when you finally complete a campaign, and let me tell you, the campaigns are hard, you need to grind a lot to unlock the stuff in order to make it, id say invest in poison build with propagation and opportunism , the druid staff is probably the most beginner friendly weapon . id also say to focus on offense and leave defense alone or youll get killed in 2 seconds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun game, but... (it is missing a lot)It desperately needs more towns!  Needs different landscapes, needs different amount of days before boss, needs different bosses.You can say "hey they are only in early access", but if I am looking at the version number 0.91.6, that seems pretty close to 1.0.  Lets hope more things actually make it in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a great game, the amount of content and replay value for early access is a really strong start. The pixel art is masterfully created and very high quality and just the art, the audio is also just a good. I think its worth to note that this game is very hard and it does not help that the game nearly requires you to grind to start having a decent chance of winning. While these factors might discourage some players i do think they have some benefits, there is a very strong feeling of progression with each new mechanic that you unlock and that also allows the games brutal difficulty to be lowered. there is an easy mode for players who are struggling with the default mode but even still easy is pretty much setting the game to (Normal). The character progression is one of the best parts about the game, building these hero's and build their stats is very rewarding. The base building mechanics are also very good, while i do think that is a little slow due to the small amount of resources that are provided with. The rogue mechanics are present but are not the key part of the game, it is a turn based game and then a rogue like. Overall its a really strong start to something very big, if your up for a turn based game that will definitely challenge your skill then this is the right game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: What a masterpiece. This game was made by true gamers for gamers. All of the QoL are so well thought through. Amazing soundtrack, the pacing of combat is very refreshing. I love tactics games, but most of them are so slow to play I get bored very quickly, but this feels super satisfying. It's quite challenging, but once you play through the maps few times you get a good idea on what you should do. Sound design with visuals makes every attack feel powerful. Although I'm not really a fan of pixel graphics, I can't imagine the game now in any other artstyle. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Just put 4 hours straight into it, and I can't wait to get back to it. The unlock system is awesome in this game, and there appears to be quite a few items. Customizing my characters for my first and only run was fun. Some mistakes were made, lessons learned, but it was fine trying to adapt and eventually win. I wound up with a heavy-hitting tank, a character that deals damage when they get hit, and an archer that chained explosive arrows. New weapon unlocks have me itching to see what other characters I can create or have them evolve into. My next run, which I only generated characters for, two of the 3 have poison damage...sounds fun trying to get away with just a poison build. That being said, I hope a mode exists where you can fine tune your characters even further or keep importing them into the next runs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 42 years old, I've been playing games since I was 5 years old (you read that right), and this is one of the best games I have ever played.Very solid tactical game. There are a lot of heroes attributes but they all blend well together.More importantly, there is a lot of room for hours of high quality decisions which can also surprisingly culminate in the craziest / tightest boss battles you have ever fought.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Original review (not recommended):Some amazing design went into this, but there are so many tiny, tedious details and any one of them can cause your run to crash and burn with 10+ hours lost in a moment. It could be a single bad choice, bad RNG, or something visual overlooked on the (visually monotonous and overstuffed with enemies) map. In a word: it's a punitive game, with consequences that are oversized for the many, many small decisions and considerations involved. You can do 99 right things, then lose because of the 100th.New review (recommended): I actually forgot I wrote the above review, and after noticing it I wanted to update to do right by gamers and the devs.The Last Spell is fun. As I mentioned earlier, it's very well designed, the depth is impressive and engaging, there are many meaningful decisions to make. Character progression feels good and the earning/spending cycle is well-tuned. The challenge is real-- sometimes brutally so-- but enjoyable. Although having said that, I stand by my earlier criticisms: You can easily lose a *lot* of hours playing this game, and not in a fun way, if you're not very diligent and adept with strategy RPG games. Ultimately, that is still a problem point for me. It feels really bad to do everything well, make one slip-up (or experience a stroke of bad luck), and basically fail, having to start all over again and risk losing many more hours building up to another obstacle that ends your run in the same unsatisfying way. Overall this did not happen to me so often that I would give the game a thumbs down, but it can be very fatiguing and can occasionally feel like the game doesn't respect your time. Patience is probably the single most important thing you can bring to this title.That said, I recommend the game. Dollars to fun, I got many hours of enjoyment out of The Last spell, and if you're like me and love a good, dense strategy game, then it's probably worth your time to check out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! It’s brutally challenging, with tactical choices that’ll have you on the edge of your seat. I barely scraped through each win, and while it eventually proved too tough for me to finish, the ride was worth it.The pixel art is spot-on, capturing the game’s gritty vibe perfectly. And the music? Absolutely epic. It ramps up the tension and intensity, making every battle feel massive.If you thrive on intense, high-stakes gameplay, prepare to be thoroughly shaken. This game delivers in spades.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Early access title with lots and lots of promise. Unlike many early access games, the core foundations of this game are solidly laid down, very competently from a technical perspective, as well as having a clear and well-established gameplay loop with great aesthetics and soundtrack to boot.The one thing that will make or break this game at this point - and I feel it would be hard for the developers to screw it up - would be ironing out of the little balance and minor gameplay issues. For example: When starting a new run, your 3 heroes might have complete garbage traits and talent trees - but to reroll them, you have to back out of the run, sit through a couple of (short) animations, then go through again. You can't rotate buildings during production phase, a feature people seem to have been asking for for at least a year. Do you only have a 1x2 strip of land available, need a worker house and have the gold for it? Better hope that strip of land is oriented top-left -> bottom right, otherwise you aren't building that house.The game OTHERWISE gives you a huge amount of flexibility that its hard to list here. There are tons of weapons and variants of each, ditto for armour, the omen system is very nice for tweaking a run further yet, the difficulty ramps up satisfyingly, the tension and payoff to *just* making a risky play is a great feeling.I really hope the developers keep up the momentum and make it through to the end with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I'm usually pretty good with tactics games and find most of them easy but this one really makes me think for a few minutes before executing a turn. Your heroes don't really get too powerful like in Disgaea or Fire Emblem. They are easily killed and sometimes don't deal enough damage especially in higher difficulties. So you have to be efficient, from supplies, buildings, skill points, health, mana and energy points, everything must be optimized if you want to survive the later nights and it really fuels my addiction to minmaxing characters. There are times that I spend minutes just planning for the build that I want for the random character that I just got based on their traits and available perks and those times that I just stay quiet and think stuff over is reaaaally fun because it's so satisfying once your build starts materializing in the game. The RNG is also not that punishing, sometimes you'll get a character that doesn't have synergetic perks and traits but I end up discovering powerful builds just by trying to make them work and using perks that seems weak at first glance. Seriously, give this a try, you won't regret it
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - If you're even thinking about buying the game... just buy it, it's worth the cost. I love this game, the world needs more humble developers like these guys. Passionate about the game they made, and having the labor of love shine true with this game. Dark gritty environment, peril looming just around the corner, and turn based tactics that rival some of the best of the best out there, and the rogue-lite portion of unlocking things is on point.... and it's still in early development...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging tactics roguelite with an energizing heavy metal soundtrack, it turned out to be my favorite game I've played this year so far! While I was initially a bit intimidated with the number of stats the heroes have, after maybe 2-3 hours with the game they all felt intuitive. The level up and perk system offers some real choices in terms of how you can build your heroes. I am also grateful for the "planning tool" the game offers, right clicking perks marks them for the future - so when I come back to the game after a few days, I don't have to wonder what kind of build I had planned for this hero.The goal of the game being defending your base from incoming horde, The Last Spell takes a different approach to enemies than most other tactics I've played. In these games, you are outnumbered by enemies in a ratio ranging usually from 1:1 to maybe 3:1. The Last Spell really cranks up these numbers and it is not uncommon to be outnumbered 10-30 to 1! This changes the dynamics of how your heroes feel compared to the average enemy, making them feel powerful and forcing the player to be efficient in mowing down the hordes. The VFX and SFX of heroes' abilities certainly play a role in making them feel powerful, too - they are all top notch and very satisfying to use.I think that the difficulty of the game could be a bit much for someone new to the genre, but if you're a tactical game veteran, you should feel yourself right at home with The Last Spell, making your victories feel earned. And if you fail, there is the metaprogression system to unlock new options and get some stat gains to make things easier - as well as an ascension (Apocalypse) system to crank up the challenge if needed. In short, it had everything I wanted from this kind of a game. A solid recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It is great for early access, its well polished, it has good mechanincs, and has lots of potential. I like how we need to think throughly before each night and to make sure everything will go smoothly.The variety in equipment is great, the level up mechanics are very creative as well, nice and fair reward system and good level of RPG complexity, just the right amount. Even though some people aren't found of the progression system, it's important to understand that yes, it limits the player for the first runs, but at the same time, it serves as a tutorial for the player to get familiar with the mechanics, which will make a lot of sense when the game is rich in content and fully developed. Not to mention that the combination between currency unlock and achievement unlock is really satisfying. Some sugestions for the full game:1- Implement more high risk high reward situations:Right now holding position and playing safe are the best ways to prevent panic from rising. Would be cool if there was rewards for abandoning your position and get an item or resources droped by an enemy, especially for archers.2- More enemies and different variations of the existing ones to give a richer feeling to the horde.3- More cities or, even better a randomly generated map and city, to make each run more unique.4- Expanding the building aspect: the possibility of having buildings outside the city and greater rewards for having buildings in certain areas, like having a gold mine in a gold rich soil. It will make the player consider if is it worth to have a more risky playstile in order to get higher rewards.5- More perk balacing, there are some perks that never seem to be usefull during my playthroughs, whereas I feel some are indispensable. (This will come with time as the game gets more mature).  Overall a very creative base building and defense strategy game. 9/10 (for the great early access)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! I think it would be sweet to have an online coop option! Or maybe in the future develop a PvP type game mode. Perhaps having item drops and different objectives in the future would be cool to. I think its beautifully done and the soundtrack is kick ass. Keep up the good work! You guys rock my socks!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a rogue-light, X-com inspired horde defense game in a fantasy world with two distinct phases of gameplay - tactical turn based combat, and base management.  The base you manage is always the town you are protecting against never-ending, ever-increasing waves of undead horrors while mages in the center of town cast a spell to end the nightmare.  The spell takes multiple nights to complete, and if the casting circle is destroyed by the attackers, you lose.The two phases of this game are excellently designed and fully integrated, and the decisions you make in either phase will affect your outcomes in the other.  To start, you build on the same map that you fight on.  For example, mana-dumping on the first night will force you to build a mana well to survive night 2, which prevents you from building an extra house, making you a worker short, slowing down your gold mines, and possibly resulting in only having 4 heroes by the time you should have 5.  However, conserve too much mana, and the undead could damage town infrastructure, causing panic, reducing rewards, and slowing down your progression.The game is difficult and balanced against you, and forces you to theory craft your units into overpowered machines just to survive.  You have to do this with pseudorandom level-up options, perks, and traits.  Your soldier's abilities are determined by their weapons.  One handed weapons can exist in off-hand variations that let you use one specific ability from a different weapon type with the rest of your main hand abilities.  Other wepaons are two handed.  You can equip up to two weapon sets on any given hero, allowing them to access a wide range of abilities.  All weapons are categorized into ranged, physical, or magical but hypothetically there is nothing to stop you from mixing and matching different weapon types on the same hero.  Off Hand magic orbs are awesome, by the way!At first you will feel overwhelmed by the bosses and power and horde scaling of the enemy, but then you will find out how to use stats like Momentum and Crit Power to build a hero that can run up to bosses and crit them in the face for 6000 damage.  You will learn how to abuse Multi Hit and Propagation to clear 20+ trash mobs in a single turn with one hero.  Once you've gained an understanding of bonus stats like Opportunism, Momentum, and Isolation and how those stats interact with specific abilities from specific weapons, you realize how many powerful builds you can create with this wonderful systemI have yet to beat the second boss and 9 hours of my total 30 were afk (I left the game on by accident), but I literally find my brain drifting back to this title while I'm busy with other things, thinking up new and interesting combinations  of abilities and stats to try to survive just one more night.Extremely addictive, extremely fun, and extremely challenging.  Oh boy, this title is hard, in such a great way.  The meta progression unlocks are tuned in a way that you are likely to lose many runs.  Later levels may be nearly impossible without most of the meta unlocked.  The difficulty is very tunable, as there are options provided to make a run easier in certain ways, and the game is nice enough to not call it "Easy mode"PROS:- Great tactical combat phase requiring thought, resource management, and theory crafting - The game lets you get stupid OP, then smacks you in the face and humbles you.- Designed to be a very difficult title, by default, but difficulty is tunable and meta progression makes it easier naturally as you unlock stat bonuses and upgrades- Excellent RPG progression / mix and match weapons/abilities system creates tons of theorycrafting opportunities.  Not only can you make your heroes stupidly powerful, you *have* to- Awesome integration of combat and management phases of game play and inter-twining of outcomes and decisions, better than x-com's.  - The pixel art is RAD and the animations and sounds are great.  Tons of atmosphere to this title.- Good enemy variety- The music is absolutely killer.  Awesome metal soundtrack, fits the action on screen PERFECTLYCONS:- You will have hard lessons- Your favorite hero with the perfect stats that is a 1-person army and can hold a whole cardinal direction by themselves will get gutted in one turn if you make a wrong move, and you might cry.  You might be able to replace them with someone else, but they won't be as amazing, and you will miss your MVP.- Runs feel a little long, and can start going south well before they are truly lost.  I think my first level 1 victory took me 3 hours.  My failed boss attempt on Lakeburg was around 6 hours.  Losing a run 3-4 hours in because your glass cannon crits themselves to death with a propagation attack on a group they were standing next to is a hell of a way to go.- On default difficulty it feels very very hard to beat Lakeburg without at least half the meta progression unlocked.- When you are getting attacked from all four directions and are maxed on 6 heroes, turns get long and finishing one night can take quite a while.VERDICT:  One of my favorite tactical turn based titles I've ever played and it isn't even finished!  I can't comment on how complete the content is yet, as I'm currently struggling against boss #2, but the core of this title is truly excellent and it's gonna be hard for them to ♥♥♥♥ it up at this point.BUY THIS GAME if you like X-Com, Final Fantasy Tactics, or Turn Based Tactics games in general, and if you like RPG theory crafting!  You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches an itch that I never knew I had. Combining RPG and grid based tactics into a roguelike is an extremely difficult task - something that Ishtar has pulled off spectacularly when so many others have failed. There's a serious amount of detail and complexity here that will keep you constantly coming up with different strategies and builds long after you turn off your monitor. Also, The Algorithm, a djent/electronic LEGEND, is truly in his element here. As the composer, Remi has created an exceptional soundtrack that you'll find yourself headbanging to as you kill wave after wave of enemies.Although the story doesn't feel like a primary focus of this game, I did find myself immersed into the world and rooting on my heroes and mages night after night. You can save and input character codes making it possible for a legendary hero from a previous run to join you in your next. For criticisms, I didn't feel like I had a lot of connection with the "Commander", and definitely feel as though my "dudes fighting for survival" was more compelling than the overarching narrative. I also could've used a bit more variety in the base and more ambient themes. There also is no friendly fire warning, so you only learn about how quickly you can kill off your fellow heroes through doing so. Several of my early runs ended early due to a misclick accidentally killing myself. That all being said, to Remi and the rest of the folks at Ishtar, congratulations on making a true gem for strategy/RPG/roguelite fans! I can't wait to see what comes next and will be following enthusiastically!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy grid-based tactical games like Fire Emblem and Disgaea you will LOVE this game! There is a huge amount of customization for each character with the level up and perk system. There are TONS of weapons, all with unique movesets. And while it is a rogue-like, in each run there is room for a feeling of progression, within the run as well as in the overall game. As you complete the meta-tasks, even the early nights of later runs are contributing progress toward an achievement. This game is incredibly well thought out. The only issues that signify it as an early access game are the controls and performance - BY AND LARGE the controls are fine, playing the game as-is is excellent, but there could be tweaks made with the controls that might make it even better. Performance - the game is small, about 350MB. But consumes around 1.2GB of RAM when running, as well as a high GPU load. However the game is not dropping FPS. I suspect there are optimizations in the engine that can (and hopefully will) be made mitigate this issue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy and incomplete. Good music, cool graphics, and B+ gameplay don't matter when you lose your entire campaign to a bug. You have to invest way too much time for there to be no cloud save, no way to recover. Using a wireless controller also causes the game to bug out, especially if your controller goes dormant for any reason. I would wait another year or two and buy it on sale; hopefully the game will be more stable then.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Stellar gameplay and mechanics, this game has frightened me with the sheer multitudes making up the hordes.Sometimes you feel strong and like you have everything under control. Sometimes just one small thing leads to another and you watch your poor town get flooded with carcasses. Hopefully they're not yours!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Very tactical fun game with increasing difficulty (it starts slow, super easy and gets progresively harder and harder . Great game if you like turn based combat, RPG. It is improved by having also a city that you develop as you progress through the nights. After 160hours and finishing all achievements still highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Fast Remarks:Gameplay: base defense mission in FF tactics in an apocalyptic setting, with roguelite meta progressionSoundtrack: Slaps hard (in a DOOM kinda way)Difficulty: Hard, but the meta progression each run help A LOTStory: Just enough to make sense, not good/developed enough to be a major draw. Not the focus of the game.Is it good? If you like turn based combat with a good variety of Units, Interesting stats and weapons, its great! If you like power fantasies were you **don't** work hard and get to kill a lot of monsters, this is not for you.Is it difficult? Yes, the first runs will make it feel like the idea of completing a run is VERY hard, but after you start unlocking (after each run) some extra production buildings/unit upgrades it gets substantially easier, but making some misplays will still get your units permanently killed.Bang for Buck? The quality is great, I've already broken the hour/$ mark I'm comfortable with (3 hours per dollar) and I still have many unlocks to get (I got 31/81). You can put a lot of time into this even without the devs adding new maps/weapons/unit traits/monsters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game is designed in such a way: It simply forces you to lose because the mission being inherently impossible to beat until you reach specific milestones through unlocks and power up enough. And how do you get the "powerups"? By getting killed over and over and over again, losing the mission without a chance repeatedly, maybe surviving one or two more waves with every attempt. Maybe there are some people out there that enjoy such a game "loop" (quite literally...), but I don't enjoy a game that doesn't take my preparation skill as a player into account and forces me to go into gunfights with just my fists, without even giving me the opportunity to get a gun before and during the fight. Survivals don't have to be fair but they should at least present the illusion of being beatable through skill and strategy. That's not the case here at all. You're totally outclassed and you will only lose, until you unlock the ingame tools to win.This kind of progression system is inherently flawed and feels unrewarding. It's a design decision I respect, but one that I don't appreciate. Hence a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly addictive turn-based tactical defense game with a rockin' soundtrack.I slept on this game for a long time before finally giving it a try, and boy was i pleasantly surprised. It's hard, sometimes very hard, but it's never unfair (even if it seems like it sometimes). There's plenty of different builds you can do, and since hero abilities are semi-randomized each run you rarely use the same tactics every time. The X-Com-esque split of the gameplay between building and combat rubs me in all the right ways, and while it could be more expanded and balanced here to not make the "corpse-strat" less overpowered in the post-endgame i'd be happy, The game isn't that long if you only do the regular standard difficulty levels of each haven, but imho it's well worth trying the higher apocalypse levels to change up the gameplay and test how far you can go. Well recommended for fans of turn-based tactics games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I need to downvote this game.I see big potential here, and I like current mush up of genres, but:1. Progression design is terrible.Light side is ok, but Dark side is pure hell.It is not roguelite progression system, more of an Idle Game progression as @gilldash mentioned in another review.It feels like I am waiting for a buddy to come by and bring me cheat codes. And I hate him for being so SLOW.2. Music.Oh well Menu music is very nice, but not the game/battle one. Too repetative and uninspired. Just bring Rock to battles.3. Perks are not randomized.Why? All characters have a bunch of useless perks and they are the same. Just randomize them too, it would be better.You've implemented Character Looks Customizations. But why? We don't care about any characters, because we need to progress with our grind. I didn't try, but I guess it will be faster just to complete One Wave and abandon the run over and over, rather then just trying to be better.Basically this game is all about waiting for currency. You can't get better. Just need to get overpowered through the course of time/useless runs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably, the game's only significant downside is its performance. I started playing on the Steam Deck , then switched to a laptop, and eventually moved to my main PC with a 4080, where I saw 45 FPS in the storage with a large number of items. The game has a pleasant visual style, but I can't understand what might be causing the GPU to load at 80-90%.Nevertheless, it's a fantastic tactical roguelike. At times, it's very challenging and mind-bending and hold interest for a long time. I'm not sure if I'll manage the final stage since I spent about ten hours clearing the previous one and got significantly worn out, but it was worth it. There's a vast amount of strategies and items for use, many different types of enemies, a wide selection of characteristics and upgrades. They even included customization and a somewhat humorous storyline. On one hand, the game has a complex characteristic system, but on the other, it offers a huge scope for employing various defense methods.After 40 hours, the game shows that I've only uncovered 60% of all the content, so if you're willing, you can certainly continue challenging yourself.Endure, explore new possibilities, use your head, and you'll be rewarded... at least, upon reaching the final stage, I felt satisfaction, although a couple of times I intended to quit the game.I definitely need a break, but I don't rule out coming back here sometime.Special praise should be given to the local soundtrack, it was written by a genius!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game during early access, and I'm happy to say there are surprisingly few bugs! The replay value is very real since this game is intentionally difficult - I've put 37 hours into the game at this point and I'm still coming back for more so I can unlock further upgrades that will eventually help me beat the game finally. I also really enjoyed the fact that I'm staving off literal hordes of enemies each in-game night!TLDR: If for nothing else, the replayability alone is a reason to get this game. Unlocking the upgrades feels truly earned because each round of enemy waves is hard fought!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: As the game mentions, it is quite difficult though there is an easy option. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I sat on this for a long time before I decided to give it a go. Watched people play a bit, but finally now that I'm playing it myself, I'm having a blast.I'm a big fan of the music and art style. I hope to see more of this art style in future ganes. I think the UI is very good. I play this exclusively on the deck and I think it is the perfect game for that system. Overall I can just see a lot of good thought went into this game and I can't wait to see it finished.So far I passed the first area on my second try, and now I'm deep into the second. I'm liking all the new enemy variants I'm seeing. Finding myself making some very difficult choices. I've enjoyed the equipment I've gotten to play with so far, and there is a lot I haven't been able to try yet.A lot of these complaint reviews I'm reading about balance or difficulty don't ring true at all. It is possible the game has merely advanced well beyond where it was when some of them were written.Don't get me wrong the game is difficult, and it is possible that you could make a few bad choices and throw away a game, but I think if you are the sort of person that agonizes a bit every turn you will have no problem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: If you like :- Strategy- Customisation- RPG- Roguelikes- Turn-based ( I usually dont like them )You are in luck, this game is the perfect combination of all of those. And the cherry on top is the really, really insane progression that feels super natural.I have been playing this game for the past 2 weeks and I can t get enough. Even after deaths, I just want to go back in with all my new knowledge.The spells are based upon equipped weapons, so it s easy to change abilities you don t like, and it sort of forces you to play with certain weapons till you find another one, that you like more, but that is statistically better. _childDocuments_.review: A game that makes me wish there was a "Neutral" option in Steam reviews. The game's not bad, necessarily, it's just really difficult for me to recommend it in it's current state. I'll break down my pros and cons below.Pros:For an early access game, this is incredibly polished. The art, music, sound, and UX is pretty damn good. I haven't run into any bugs or crashes. There's a few easily fixable UI issues, and the game occasionally stutters once you finish a level, but it's not generally noticeable. The game's general idea and balance is pretty good. You have to make meaningful choices every level on which buildings you need, how much gold you can invest into the future versus the present, whether you really need to spend mana or health, etc. This is the best simulator of city planning in a phone booth I've played. There's a great variety of weapons, which each have their own individual skills associated, and each hero can have two weapons, allowing you to combo them in interesting ways. For a full release, I'd expect more, but for a day 1 early access, it feels good. Some of the weapons don't feel as balanced as others, but those details can be worked out.Cons:This is not a roguelite game, it's a tactical RPG with roguelite elements. Yes, technically, you restart the game every time you play, and you can buy meta upgrades that let you get more powerful. However, currently, the game has an idle game's level of grind. It's not actually possible to win the game within the first few runs. Or the next few. In fact, I've played about 15 hours, and only now do I feel like it's technically possible for me the win a run. This means that you need to play ~15 hours of losing over and over again before you can even get a chance of winning. This is compounded by...P.S. on this: The Steam description is very misleading about this. It states "You can play the first part of the game, which consists of 12 consecutive ingame days + a boss fight. You should be able to reach the boss battle and maybe succeed after a few tentative runs.". I would not consider ~10 runs to be "a few", and I have not yet reached the boss fight.The game is very luck-based in a number of ways. Heroes, items, dodge, criticals, level-ups, and enemy composition is all up to RNG. This is problematic, because the game runs a very thin balance line between getting obliterated and winning without problems. If you get some bad RNG on getting the items you need (which have distinct levels of power), or monsters spawning on the left of a side rather than the right, or enemies dodging too many attacks, or getting defensive instead of offensive level-ups, you are going to lose, which doesn't feel great. This is compounded by....It's very difficult to comeback from even minor setbacks. If enemies enter the town or attack your buildings, you get less resources at the end of the level. If monsters hit your walls, you lose resources which you don't get back. If monsters destroy a building, that can easily cost you the game. You can normally tell when you've lost too much to effectively continue; you may not lose on the next level or the one after that, but you'll eventually hit a point where you just don't have enough to the win the next wave. This is part of the most fundamental problem with the game....It's not fun to play a game you know with absolute certainty you've already lost, and for your first 10+ games, you are going to do nothing but that. Skill is irrelevant, you simply do not have the tools to win. Each game can easily last for 1-2 hours as well, so you have to just grind through that slowly getting money so you do a little better so you can get money so you can do a little better. The things you are unlocking are, apart from the weapons, massively boring stat increases and armour with slightly different properties. A friend asked me if this game is fun. I think it technically is, it hits the bare minimum level of fun for "having fun", but it's not.... exciting in any way. Every level, every game is a war of attrition. You gain or lose single tiles, watch your mana bar slowly go down, spend your gold so you can make 30% more gold later so you can get items with 20% more power which lets you deal enough damage to kill the next wave's monsters at the same speed as the last waves monsters. You never feel like you're powerful, or like you've beaten the odds, or made a great tactical decision. You never get a cool treasure chest or a reward that makes you wonder how you're going to use that (apart from grinding enough to unlock new weapons ~5 times).  There's no story to keep you invested, or next cool thing you want to get access to or try, or characters, or really anything. I am generally a big fan of very difficult games, but this game really doesn't feel good right now. It's technically difficult, yes, but it's a test of endurance more than anything. In it's current state, playing this game feels exhausting. It feels like a job where I have the barest basic motivation to do the next thing that doesn't matter so I can get my just-good-enough "keeping up with inflation" raise, knowing that I'm never going to be promoted because of factors completely outside my control.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok, but the meta progression system is far too important for strategy. No matter how well you play you're required to fail several six hour campaigns to grind enough tainted essence and progression unlocks to stand a chance in the later missions. You're essentially handicapped without your knowledge. I say this as one of the 1% of players to defeat the level 3 boss after two weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Defend and build up your town.  Slaughter the enemy as fast as possible, acquire money, material and lots of gear, and try to equip your defenders as best you can.  It's very fun and addicting to smash enemies as hard as possible, then prep for the next wave.  There is a speed up button so that you can pick up the pace of the game, which feels great when there are a lot of enemy interactions to resolve.  Unlike other games, you can adjust it and really speed it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bomb take on tactical RPGs. Where in others games characters will either feel underwhelming or have no challenge at max stats, this provides many characters that feel strong while providing hordes of enemies to both reinforce how strong the characters' abilities are while providing a challenge. The production phase also adds another level of game play that provides plenty of decisions for the player to make while the quickly ramping up difficulty makes each of the decisions matter. The only small problem with the formula versus some of the other story based tactical games is the lack of character depth due to the rogue like elements. Early runs past the first will feel like characters are just fodder until the player can unlock more to have a chance at winning, and a death will mean the likely end of a run versus losing someone important. The mechanics in this are very smart, and while the early difficulty and the rogue like elements might not be for everyone, its a must have for fans of tactical RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review with a playtime of 46 hours and having beaten Apocalypse 5. If this game keeps working on some of its major flaws, this could easily become one of my favorite Roguelites of all time, right next to Hades, Slay the Spire and FTL.It only happens very rarely that we get to see a completely new game idea that fuses multiple genres into such an interesting and unique design. In this case I guess this game would be something like a Roguelite – RPG – City Builder – Tower Defense. Now I’m gonna leave the discussion on whether this really is a pure Roguelite up to other guys and concentrate on the game itself.In The Last Spell your goal is to defend a city for a period of 12 consecutive days, so that a group of mages can cast their final magic and save the rest of humanity. During the night you control a group of 3 to 6 heroes to fight back hordes of undead and defend the core of your city. During the daytime you use your newly earned resources to build new buildings and defense, hire new heroes or get them better gear and level up your roster, all with the goal of being able to hold back even stronger and more numerous amounts of undeads.There are numerous positive points about The Last Spell as it currently is:However, in its current state, there are some major flaws to be found:Here are some design-ideas for the devs:All in all this is a very fleshed out game for Early-Access and there are only some very minor performance problems.If the devs continue to work on the problems and fine tune some balancing aspects, as well as release more maps and rework Apocalypse mode, this game will most definitely become one of my favorite games of all time.Good luck out there!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 100% stolen the place of one of my favourite games to relax with. It combines the aspects of roguelites and tactical, turn based gameplay into something that I never knew I was looking for.Having grown up playing final fantasy tactics, and more recently falling in love with roguelites this scratches both itches with a gameplay loop that has me coming back for more.The recent Omen update has added a layer that makes this game that much more enjoyable. I have nearly 150 hours in this game, and will probably double that in the future.TLDR: if you like roguelites and tactical turn based games with similar style to FF tactics, you will love this game hands down. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: So far really liking this. The claim someone else made that you can't make it further than night 2 or 3 on your first go is bogus. I made it to night 5. And I think 6 is possible if you have enough knowledge (none of my heroes died, but in the end my mage building got rekked). That said, I don't see how you'd be able to actually beat the game on your first try. My main complaint is that your first run you don't actually get much from getting far (seems like you get a flat 500 souls no matter what, which is enough for the first soul unlock). So kinda feel like I wasted my time on my first run. Just suicide on night 1 to unlock soul gathering is my tip.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is 10/10. The developers married turn-based strategy and base building extremely well, and the main gameplay loop is addictive. Add to that fantastic music and pretty good meta progression, and you got yourself a great game.My only gripe with this game (as do other players) is that there is no option to turn off or disable unlocks, which makes going for a specific build difficult, though I suppose there are others who enjoy being forced to be flexible (but I'd rather have the option, since giving players the option is never a bad thing.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of replayability to grind for the unlocks/achievements and a solid building challenge.  Would like some QOL improvements like giving the essence even if you fail a night as well as deselecting certain weapons to name a few.  The latter being that some weapon play styles aren't very enjoyable to use but also that some weapons are hot garbage currently and it's easy to notice which are S tier and which will end your run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The best tactics game I've played.This game is brilliant. Simply put, games like the Xcom series have struggled with the dynamic of a meta-base builder, valuable soldiers, random chance, and consequence. This game strikes an incredible balance between your random options and agency for decision making both crafting the heroes and your base. The 'roguelike' nature of the game means that each mission can really ramp up the difficulty, making overwhelmed and losing part of the game and coming at it new with fresh unlocks and knowledge and not feel like you wasted an X hour play through like many of its counterparts, including X Com, pheonix point, and many others.The art style is cute, clear, and just all around good quality. Animation isn't padded to increase playtime. The 'rush' animation for the enemies where the whole wave moves in a surge and the actions shown not one by one, but in distinct pockets acting simultaneously both works thematically, and gets the action back to the player swiftly.I'm simply shocked by the myriad quality of life features in this early access game- or perhaps I'm suffering from stockholm syndrome from not really having decent tactics games available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Something about this game just hits everything perfectly for me, I would HIGHLY recommend it to anyone who likes a challenge. Base planning and deceptively deep character customization combine beautifully with a fun combat system. I wouldn't change anything about The Last Spell, I simply want more of it. The art style is also a favorite of mine, old school pixel graphics with a modern polish that looks simply amazing. The music is boss.  I almost never prepurchase games but if they made a 2nd one or an expansion I would buy it immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game is set up in a way where you're meant to get your ass kicked.Kinda put me off it the first 2 runs, but you progress really fast, and can unlock a lot of things. And they even put in an easy mode for people who think the progression is too slow, I haven't felt the need to use it though.I'm 25,5 hours in now, and i've made it to night 9 of 12 on what I assume is only the first village.It's very challenging but also very in-depth with a lot of customization and decision making. I lose track of time whenever I play!Definitely recommend the game :)- Only advice and complaint: Don't bother try-harding the first run, as you won't get any progression from it, which is a shame!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This is an insanely well polished Early Access release. Im around 8 hours in and have encountered zero bugs or glitches, zero overall issues and everything ive seen so far looks fantastic. Animations are crunchy and death animations for both sides look great, turn speeds feel right, movement has no weird sides to it. Unlocks feel like they come at a decent speed and each time has been a major click moment for ''problems'' i thought the game had. This is a Rogue LITE done well, gradual upgrades giving more options but still needs you to actually use them properly. I feel like i need to say at least something negative.....uh....the portraits for the characters look lower quality? Yea go with that. Boo devs boo.  0/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This is one hell of a ride.Turn-based, rpg-tactics, with base building and tower defense. Whew. A bit of rogue-lite in there for fun, too.It's got a lot of things going on, and it does a lot of them really well. _childDocuments_.review: I haven’t beaten all the maps in The Last Spell but I feel done with the game. The first 50 hours was an absolute thrill ride, only being bogged down by slow meta-progression and tedious gear optimization. Runs are long but maybe not what you would call a campaign, think 10-15 hours. Run strategies don’t feel all that different, building economics and good hero builds always work. 70 hours in and I don’t have a whole lot of motivation to continue. Many of my favorite games: Rimworld, Battle Brothers, FTL, the list goes on, I bounced off of the first time around. I enjoyed them, but was too fatigued to finish them, I saw their greatness but didn’t have close to a complete understanding of their mechanical depth. The Last Spell might fall in this category and only time will tell. The bones of something great is here, the snappy, stylish turn-based combat, the flair in the presentation with a dynamic and genre-spanning soundtrack, the fun and flexible classless hero builds, all highlight some exceptional game design. So, while I might be done for now, I look forward to revisiting The Last Spell with a fresh set of eyes in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting little rougelite where post run progression is a huge focus.Some players might not like that they must die several times in order to beat the game but I actually liked the progression, as it makes dying in a run less of a "damn now I gotta try again" and more of a "that was a good run I can't wait to use all the stuff I unlocked"Think of the core gameplay loop like:play - upgrade -  die - repeat around 20 times- then eventually winProgress is made by two separate methods:1 - Getting kills and fulfilling certain conditions during the night gives you currency that you can spend to unlock whatever upgrades you want.2 - Completing achievements that give you specific upgrades.It can admittedly be a grind to acquire the currency but I never got too annoyed with it until later on when it started to cost upwards of 10 times more to get them.The upgrades gained between runs - and sometimes in the middle of runs - do make a big difference and are pretty interesting for the most part (rather than simple % increases to your stats). They tend to keep the game fresh and made me want to play another run to see how different unlocking it allowed me to play.Still can't believe this is an early access game with the amount of replayability already here. Seriously did not expect the level of quality present and I am exited for future updates.Recommended to anyone who enjoys rougelites with tons of post run progression and turn based games. If you are on the fence thinking about buying just go ahead and get it, you will not regret your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: takes a while to grab youmy relationship with this game started troubledi cannot stand the rogue(light) tag, like at all. and Last Spell is a rogue-light in essenceyou pick your location and start a "run", which means using your up to 6 heroes and building options to secure your spellcircle till your mages can break the seal. all while fending off hordes of enemies (and bosses) in turnbased combat.you will lose, like you would in most rogue-games. what's different is runs taking pretty long, your heroes level up (different progression systems, starting by all sorts of gear, perks and stats), your township grows in size and options. each individual run is pretty engaging and motivating.but there will be walls.perma progression is tied to the plot. you collect a ressource (tainted essence) and unlock "achievments" to get new tools, passive upgrades or perma-perks. the meta progression is pretty good, but takes a while to get going.there's a whole, and i do mean a whole lot of content here. each armor, weapons and trinket can completely alter your heroes:become a 2hander wielding berserker, a plague calling druid, an aoe-machine wizard, paladin, cleric and the list goes on and on. the options grow the longer you play.when starting out i wasn't very happy; the game is kinda slowburner, which means after 1 or 2 complete runs (or cleared locations) it realy gets going, but once it gets going it's absolutly brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is looking to be WAY longer than I originally thought.    It's unfortunately off sale rn.  I got it at 50% off and bought the dlc with it.  Off sale and bundled both cost $30 (without the sound track).  I was unsure at first (which is why I waited for a sale), but now that I've played for a bit and see that it goes WAY deeper than I thought...  I think $30 is actually worth it. The game is challenging.  It's real nice to find something that actually taxes my abilities in a way that is challenging, yet isn't excruciating. Plus they have a way of making things "new" each run (referencing sorta).I genuinely dig this game and like physical games of old, I do not mind paying for a game that is worth it.-following is not spoilers, just game mechanics-About (sorta) The way the game works is, you have one save.  ONE.  Every time you start a map, that run's main progress (perks and things you earn) will be right where you left it.  Including any unspent points.  Here is the catch...  And this is also why the game sorta keeps itself fresh. Each run you get new, what seems to be generated heroes, that start fresh at level 1.  The perks you have earned in previous runs is how you progress in the game. _childDocuments_.review: The Last SpellA well-made, wave-defense tactics RPG with a phenomenal art style, sound design, but slightly grating music.I can't quite compare it to anything. Yes, it's obviously got the grid-based movement of plenty of other tactics games, such as Into The Breach, XCOM, Xenonauts, etc. But unlike those games, this is a wave-defense with a much, much heavier focus on character stat-builds, almost as important as equipment choice. Whereas the listed games, there's less focus on builds (Not to say your stat-build isn't important in XCOM, but it's also deeply simplified there, and also basically linear). You get your group of three-to-six heroes, and must equip and level them up appropriately in order to defend your Haven's ritual circle.The story itself is quite simple; some horrible mage brought hell-magic to the world, which created spooky purple mist, which promptly destroyed basically most everything aside from a few bastions and holdouts. The remainder of the human world is trying to dispel the hell-magic via massive ritual-casting, you are the Commander, sent to guide each Haven's defenders in order to ensure that their ritual is complete. Explaining the story any further is basically spoiling the plot, but that's the basic gist of it. The plot is, though, the game's weak point. It's nothing particularly interesting, and there's really only two "characters", which are the two people who run their respective progression shops. You, as a character, don't really say or do anything. If you absolutely NEED a well-written/compelling story, you won't find it here; but it's also not the focus of the game, and it's basically relegated to post-run cutscenes.Each "run" of whichever map you pick is divided into two phases, the build phase, and the defense phase. During the build phase, you manage your Haven. Spending Gold and Supplies in order to build and upgrade production buildings, purchase gear from the shop, buy new heroes, distribute stat points to any heroes that have levelled up, equip them, place them near whichever direction the horde plans to come from, and build defensive structures such as landmines/traps, walls, turrets, teleporters, etc. Then, when all is said and done, you finalize, and the defense phase begins, which involves you using your 3-6 heroes to kill off the entire enemy horde as it comes in each turn. A successful, winning run is around six-ish hours long, depending on the difficulty you pick, the map you pick, and just how quick you are. Unsuccessful runs, of course, end when your ritual circle is destroyed by enemies.Combat itself is very fun. The sound design is appropriately-meaty, and it's got excellent sprite work, especially for a lot of the magic abilities. Using as many buffs and stats you can manage is necessary. Certain weapons are affected by an "Isolation" stat, meaning if an enemy has no friendly enemies touching it, you get a certain % bonus damage. Some weapons are affected by "Momentum", which means the amount of tiles you move before you attack with it, the more damage you deal. Some have poison, which is pretty self-explanatory. Some let you pick and choose multiple targets within range to hit, while others will let you choose the first target, before bouncing off and hitting any adjacent enemies at random. Others stun, some debuff certain enemy stats such as damage, accuracy, or movement, and so on. It's all very fun. There is an excellent mix of fodder/cheap enemies that take one, maybe two hits to kill, and stronger enemies that take a handful of hits to kill, on top of the occasional elite/miniboss enemy, such as a suicide-bomber, an enemy that heals itself by killing it's own allies, an enemy that is basically the Tank from Left 4 Dead, and each "run" is capped off by a big boss fight.When you win (or lose!) a night, you're awarded Dark Essence, which is a special currency that you can spend in one of the two progression shops that lets you get permanent buffs that apply to every run, including the one you are currently in. This can range from pure stat-boosts, such as every hero getting a bonus +30 hit points, or dealing an extra +3% damage, to getting access to a completely brand-new style of weapon such as a staff, greatsword, or rifle. Some of these buffs can also be new buildings, and some of them can be "Omens", which are modifiers you pick at the start of a run that grant certain boosts, usually far greater than the permanent stat-boosts above; however, each map only lets you pick a small number of those omens, and some cost more slots than others. There is a SECOND progression shop, HOWEVER, unlocking things within it instead is based on completing certain objectives/tasks. For example, to unlock different types of Hand Crossbows, you are required to use the Wooden, and Regular Hand Crossbow, totaling to 200 action points across as many runs as needed. Some of these tasks are simply unlocked by playing the game, such as getting to Night Six of the Lakeburg map, while others require you to purposefully go for them, such as having a single hero that resists a total of 500 damage in a single run through the use of the Block stat. That is to say, progression feels GOOD. Even if you lose, you're usually getting some amount of Dark Essence which can be spent on permanent stat-boosts that help make up for the sometimes-poor character builds you can get from a randomized character system, and of course; you're almost always making progress on SOME task in the second progression shop.My only real complaint is that the music is a little bit grating. Maybe it's because metal/rock isn't my personal taste in music, but it does feel like it loops a bit too often, and honestly? I personally would've much rather preferred some sort of Darkest-Dungeon-esque haunting orchestra, not grinding metal. That being said, this is an issue completely resolved by simply going into the settings, and disabling music and turning my own on. A non-issue, really.Very strong recommendation for anyone interested in tactics RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting of fantasy apocalypse is one I haven't seen much elsewhere, and definitely not this well. The hordes of enemies that swarm in each turn invokes dismay, but if you know what you're doing you can beat the game without losing once. Each of the three weapon types has its own advantages and disadvantages, and each character can have 2 weapon sets equipped at once, encouraging experimentation and further specialisation. And even within the weapon types, each weapon has strengths and weaknesses. The graphics are amazing, the music is great, and the replayability is very strong. One of the best games I've played in a while. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.Xcom. Final Fantasy: Tactics. Kingdom Rush. I have spent many hours with all of these series. They are some of my all time favorites. The Last Spell combines elements from all of these to make a wonderful, unique whole. Build up your town during the day. Level up and equip your heroes. When night falls, the hordes will descend upon your town. The seamless integration of building and battle remind me so much of the original XCOM: Ufo Defense. Building placement matters, because your town becomes the terrain for the battle ground.Your characters level up RPG style. There are many different builds to explore, involving combinations of perks and weapons. Each weapon feels unique, and each weapon has it's place. This combines with a huge variety of armor, potions, and other equipment. Every run is different.The battles are a ton of fun. You will have 3 - 6 heroes defending your town. There are multiple maps, each of which provides their own challenges. However, the real terrain is the horde that attacks your town. Each enemy has its own strength and weakness that will force different responses from you. You may have a hero with a 95% dodge rating, only to be forced to flee from an enemy who detonates with a magical, undodgeable blast. The hero with 300 armor may seem invulnerable, at least until the armor penetrating Lancers attack. The boss battles, in particular, are a  tour de force. There are multiple stages to each boss, forcing you to desperately improvise a response. They push you to the absolute limit. Graphics are excellent pixel art. The UI clearly displays the vast amount of stats and other information. The sound design is also very well. Meta progression allows a satisfying series of unlocks that expands your options for each campaign.I highly recommend this game. Purchase it, and you are in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent mix of tactical Roguelite RPG and...base defense?It sounds like it shouldn't work, but it absolutely does. You have a small band of extremely powerful characters that are trying to defend a town from hordes of monsters. It perfectly encapsulates the RPG power fantasy while also being stressful as hell and feels like a resource management game at times.Also, the soundtrack is full of bangers

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the Year here for me! Really good early access almost flawless in my opinion, it's a rare sight to strike a good balancing and progression like that from the get go.
