_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you a story... I built up what I thought was an impenetrable town, surrounded by thick reinforced stone walls, high-rise ballista covering every possible angle, catapults making up the back ranks as trump cards for when the horde got too thick. My heroes were an archmage, a paladin-esque tank, an archer, a crit-oriented dual-pistol-wielding lady, and finally a chonky sledgehammer fighter. I was pretty certain I'd win this run, I had built up this archer to be a powerhouse that could crit and slay anything, my archmage could double-dip on restoring mana and actions in one turn, all whilst summoning multiple fireballs and chain lightning.. not to mention my fighter and paladin tanks were so hard to kill I would have to put them in the middle of the horde and let them get hit for 4-5 turns just to get them down to 1/3 health. In the end, the lake boss spawned, and since it was my first time running lakeburg, I mistakenly decided to greed my archer outside the walls, where he was promptly slapped into meat paste, and the rest was a slow-burn of watching my mighty town get destroyed by raining waterballs, swarmed by exploding zombies that could destroy the walls in one go, and other such monstrosities turn after turn. Most of my heroes died by the time the spell altar got destroyed, it was a tragic sight watching hundreds of enemies swarming all over the, the boss at half health and too far away from my remaining heroes... In the end the altar was lost and the run was done. I took a couple of minutes to mourn the loss of my band of misfits before running lakeburg again. ♥♥♥♥ this stupid lizard i'll kill it this time.The game looks great, the turn-based combat is to my preference, the game has the league of legends formula - no two runs will ever be the same. You get truly invested in what you're building and the heroes that you are shaping and seeing them perform. The combination of perks, equipment and hero traits mean that you'll have a wide variety of strats in every run. There's poison builds, damage builds (using spells, using melee weapons, using crit on melee or ranged, etc.). I mentioned above a very pleasing build with mages, where you can attack using spells and regenerate the mana you just used back by using a combination of trinkets that give you extra action/mana. There's also a build where you can have a massive-hp tank that has a damage buff based on his maximum mana. Poison builds are a-plenty. Ranged builds as well, with anything from muskets, pistols, to shortbows and longbows. You choose between a pure damage build or a crit build. The game has a sweet spot in terms of balance. And they just added Omens which drastically changes the particular run you will play in. You can control your run to a certain extent using Omens, by forcing additional loot drops of a specific weapon, increasing base health/armor/mana... There's so many possibilities that you would have to play this game a very long time to get bored of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ironically, The Last Spell is my first ever game review. I divided the content in 2 sections:* The review;* Pro tips for new players.I initially wished to make a third section about possible enhancements but Steam decided I wrote enough with 2.This game does many things right, it’s actually harder to make a synthesis of them than to beat the game.The set up of the game is OK, reminds you about how humans are dumbasses just like in real life… It’s a shame there isn’t any story behind the set up.The art style does its job well. The user interface is good, you'll get used to it fast, even if there is a lot to take in.The intro music is cool, a shame that you hardly listen to it. The rest of the music is a bit bland in my opinion, though it matches the theme well. Now, let’s move to the thick of it. The gameplay is where the game shines the most, though “shines” maybe isn’t the greatest word to describe a post-apocalyptic night war with monstrosities… First of all, I’m amazed by how you can keep up with growing challenges with what you have at hand, even though you will often think “Holy hell, how much of those cursed monsters are going to appear on this damned screen?!” or “Again with those insane elite monsters ?!” or “Can this night end now… please?”. The variety in heroes builds is impressive, you can easily find and taylor heroes that will suit your playstyle, though I have a major grip with it because of poorly designed RNG issues but I don't have enough room on Steam to explain it. When you reach the point when your heroes are on par with your ambitions, it’s just thrilling to roam the battlefield, swatting whatever is in your way. And then when you think it’s getting somewhat comfortable, you find out that the next wave is tricky and you’re back to the edge of your seat. This game hooked me in so strongly that I often forgot about the world around me while playing and regularly found myself going to work with bags under the eyes darker than even the plot of this game.The economy adds a nice layer to the gameplay, both as a respite phase and as a cornerstone to the development of your haven, directly related to your opportunities to get the stuff you need to survive the next night. Your choices are of outmost importance before and during battles! Depending on the level of challenge you tackle and the maps, your strategy will change, which means you need to adapt if you want to win. This gets easier as you get to know and understand the game.I read a lot of reviews about how hard the game is. How long a run is.While the latter is absolutely true (a run can range between 1 and around 8h depending on your knowledge of the game, the map and the difficulty you play on), I can hardly say the game is “too difficult” since I managed to get all the successes without suffering a single loss… It is hard though, to the point that you might often feel desperate to survive another night. I guess, written like this, it will only appeal to masochists… You might rather view it like a test of your tactical mettle. You overcome the swarm, beat bosses, meet daylight again and then you feel like you’re accomplished something great. Behind the potential frustration I described lies a well-crafted, rich tactical RPG that might glue you to your computer and what I consider after 100+ hours a “fair” challenge. Up to you to undertake it. And if you do, I strongly advise you to read the pro tips below!1. Don’t unlock all the weapons at the beginning! Unlock only those that might suit your playstyle after several runs, when you’ve gotten a feel for the game. This will greatly increase the chance you get the weapons you actually use during your runs. As for me, I’d recommend avoiding most of the 2 handed weapons.2. Build a strong economy fast. It makes the beginning a little harder but rewards you later to face the stronger challenges (huge waves, elite enemies, bosses), especially when you can get the equipment at max level. If you’re tight for money, always prioritize better weapons or stuff that gives you strategic assets like actions points.3. Plan what you wish to do with each hero and what you need to complement what you have. A hero is the sum of his traits, his perks, his weapon(s) and his equipment besides the weapon. Be sure to take advantage of the different types of damage, to grow your heroes so that everything works together to make them mowing machines. If you don’t, you’ll see a “Game Over” screen sooner or later… Which would be a shame after several hours of deadly combat, wouldn’t it?4. Most of the damage boosts work a in multiplicative fashion. It is then important to understand that, for instance, getting a 40 % increase in damage (140 % total) is less efficient than getting a 20 % increase in damage and a 20 % increase in a specific type of damage (144 % total). You have lots of way to increase those multipliers via isolation, opportunism, critical hits, and so on.5. When you see a boss, kill it. Immediately. I mean it. And if you see it again, beat it to a bloody pulp. And then smash it. Bury it. Bosses are the top priority unless your mages are in direct danger.I enjoyed my time casting The Last Spell, really hope the developpers will adress the "hero-centric" issues I sent them to get me down to save the world from the mist again. As heroes say in the game: "Hasta la mist-a, baby"...

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to avoid early access as I've been burnt on release slips and/or feature prunes.That said, this game shows quite a lot of promise and if you're a turn based tactics weirdo (or roguelite weirdo) it is already difficult enough to get your money's worth.This is a game about popping zombies with bows, mallets, and wands so they don't kill your mages, who are nameless mooks trying to set off a good magical atomic bomb.Do note if you aren't familiar with "feel-bad" turn based mechanics like in XCOM, accuracy capping is going to be near mandatory.  I see a few reviews bemoaning rng without elaborating, I expect they are referring to dodges more than anything else.  You can play to your outs quite well in this game.Note that I have a lot of afk hours, more in the 40 active hours range, but this game is a 9/10 for me, and probably at least a 7/10 for anyone that already enjoys the genre generally.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. Don't listen to the naysayers, there's no grind involved unless you want it to be easier without boundless mode / are hunting for all achievements. If you like to spend time min-maxing in tactical roguelites, just buy it. The great part about this game is that in order to optimization involves both permuting the item builds between characters and the order of actions you do in the prep phase. Doing this right is time consuming, any run will last multiple hours.If you want a challenge, up the difficulty every time you pass a level -  completing glenwald for the first time on apocalypse 2 with less than half the upgrades was definitely fun.The DLC is worth it, Do note however that the new items it provides are somewhat overpowered and lower the overall difficulty - especially the cannon. There aren't many bugs and it's getting constant updates - so I'm sure they'll be ironed out in the end. Looking forward to quickshots on the runes from runenberg not freezeing the game! _childDocuments_.review: My biggest recommendation is to play your first 1 - 2 games on easy. A single run lasts hours, and at the start you have 0 unlocks (even buildings related to your economy are locked behind progress points). Farm points in these easy runs, *then* play the game on normal once you accrue enough points to unlock the basic unlocks, unless you enjoy(?!) watching the slow death of your run over the course of hours as your heroes swing sticks for a measly amount of progress points. The core gameplay loop is very enjoyable and highly addictive. Although, this game seriously didn't need to be a rogue-like (lore-wise, and gameplay-wise). This game is incomplete, but it has the potential to be a classic with more bosses, maps, and balancing. If doing massive AOE in a turn-based setting makes you happy, then this game is worth the investment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game deserves a big thumbs up.Long version: It's hard. You will die. You will curse RNG... You will enjoy it. And that's what counts for me. It's a roguelite (i.e. there is permanent progression) and the unlocks feel great to try out. The game is user-friendly and upfront with everything you need to know. I've had "eureka!" moments when I thought I found a broken combo. It was nowhere near broken enough for higher difficulties but that's why they are optional higher difficulties for when you finish the main game. The story is... serviceable. Sure, it's there, I suppose. It was nice. But the fun is in the mechanics and the fights.And they are magnificently made. The Last Spell FEELS good to play and the sense of achievement when you win a map juuuust in time is amazing. Or at least it was for me. The graphics are pixel art and well made, the soundtrack is simply amazing. What else to say? I've had my fill. More than my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in Early-Access it's already tons of fun.Ok... the first run is pretty pathetic... barely got to night 3 and already gave in to despair and hopelessness because 80% of the town was ravaged. The second run goes more smoothly... for now you know what awaits you and besides - NOW you get to upgrade - and that is where the real fun starts. Now you get the feeling of progression and the "just one more turn"-feeling.The atmosphere is amazing. The story-telling from the start is great and you feel and know why you do what you do. The feeling of building raggedy defenses with the little material you have, and huddling your warriors together for that last stand has something cozy, exciting and dangerous (and hopeless) all at the same time.Like the 13th Warrior: you need to defend against who-knows how many and you're not even sure what you're fighting against - but you know you must and you will give it your all...The equipment needs a bit of tweaking in my opinion. The weapons are interesting and most of the time the skills are kind of like side-grades instead of pure upgrades. For me it oftentimes feels like it is just not enough... not the right equipment for what I need it to do right now. But it makes for some interesting combinations with the stats and perks - so you get to try things out.Overall I'm really... REALLY looking forward to what else is going to happen and can't await the full release of this gem.Needed to edit my review for the following reason: when I posted this I immediately started it up again and then it slapped my right in my face what I forgot to mention... THE MUSIC!The music is AMAZING... nothing else to be said... check it out yourself. Plain goodness... <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a pretty interesting game that has a very "They Are Billions" feel to it, with a few key differences.The big differences of this game compared to They are Billions is twofold: One, its a turn based strategy game, and two its a hero / rpg based combat compared to They are Billions. This means that you can spend time during invasions determining the best way to effectively deal with invasions. The combat feels pretty good with a few exceptions (more on that in a couple) and the game is pretty hard, boasting a sort of prestige system where after every wave, you can unlock things like more buildings as well as buffs for your heros that are permanent and stay with you for future runs. You will lose over and over in these runs; be prepared to deal with that. Losing is a core point of progression in this game, but its a admittedly addicting gameplay loop.Now for the minuses. One of my biggest problems in this game comes from a few various things: Dodge chance and armor being a rather HUGE problem later on in the game. It feels like I have to put all my level ups in accuracy because everything dodges everything you throw on them later in the game. Also, because of armor and mages / archer classes not having a good way to deal with it, Melee is effectively the best option to deal with a lot of waves since your archers and mages have to go through 2 health bars instead of the normal one, while also having to worry about missing. Melees effectively one shot armor, which just makes them better at the job. This isn't saying that Archers and Mages are weak, but they seem a bit lackluster later on in the game. Some perks seem to alleviate this issue, but these perks are available way too late for them to fix the issues when its originally needed.Another slight issue I have comes from losing waves. I understand losing is part of the game, but at the moment it feels better to just "quit" during a wave you think you'll lose because there is literally nothing that you get for trying your hardest to survive it. I think tainted essence should be changed to be given after every enemy kill, rather than calculated at the end of a wave so that you get at least something for trying your hardest to defend.Overall however, I consider this game pretty interesting and fun. If you like TABs, then you'll likely enjoy this game as well. Just know that this game is still early access, so hopefully some of the issues I and other have had with this game will be corrected in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cool game, grabbed it totally on a whim when in popped up in the Steam RPG sale page. Reminds me of something like Into the Breach, except your situation is basically hopeless to start off with, but you unlock improvements to your starting conditions and things you can build as part of the metagame. Yes, you will lose, yes you will be replaying. I don't see that as a problem. I started off the first attempt dying horrible pretty quick. But the unlocks do things like add an extra action to each hero, start them with higher mana pools, add some starting stone walls in pieces around the town, and so on. A few attempts in I was surviving multiple nights. I don't think of it as losing to not make it to the end, I think of it more like a campaign where you're trying to get further each time.Even screwing up can lead to some fun times. I messed up and had a hero die the very first night, and my city was panicking; I didn't give up. My two remaining heroes managed to do the next 2 nights on their own without a scratch to the town; it was a unique challenge that run trying to defend two sides of the town.Not sure what the complaints are about melee, or what people are doing wrong trying to use them. I've had a couple runs where I let my melee guy defend one side of the town all by himself for the first couple rounds, while the other two heroes clean up their side. Enemies are severely hamstrung when damaged, slowing them to a crawl, so delaying the whole front line can leave the rest unable to rush forward.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I just really like this game. I got it several months ago and played it for a couple of weeks; since then, I've thought about it at least once a week. I just got back into it, and its still immensely satisfying.The basic premise is simple; you have a handful of heroes with which to kill a horde of monsters slowly approaching your town. To accomplish this, your characters are an order of magnitude more powerful than in a standard tactics game. Each will have 4+ actions per turn and a loadout of several weapons, each of which imparts several diverse abilities. Carefully puzzling out how each character will carve its way through the oncoming horde is immensely satisfying and is rewarded with both immediate payoffs and metaprogress that carries over between runs.Weirdly, the closest point of comparison might be Into The Breach, which also consists of thoughtfully combining diverse abilities to annihilate an oncoming horde. Into the Breach lacks TLS's progression elements, though...each night your characters' abilities grow, you can invest in the town you are protecting, and you can unlock more metaprogress milestones.There's a lot of other stuff to like. The driving guitar music is immediately engaging, there's a ton of stuff to unlock, and there's an easy mode if you just want to stomp on the AI for a bit (to name a few).There are also a few things I could complain about. The most unavoidable one is the pacing; the sheer size of the oncoming horde and the number of actions and abilities available means that a single night can take 15-30 minutes, and a run can take upwards of 4 hours. There are also several rough edges that should get sanded down by Early Access development: defenses are boring (you build walls that monsters won't reach unless ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan), and equipment is overly complicated (there is level AND material, both of which give random stat increases, and most armor provides minor buffs to unimportant stats).One more thing: The game development is about to hit a "progress wipe" milestone (sometime in October 2022), which features a massive amount of rebalancing and new content. Once that drops, it'll be a great time for new players to check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell - A Deeply Engaging Tactical RPGPros:- Challenging Gameplay: The Last Spell demands strategic thinking and careful planning. Every decision feels impactful, making for a deeply engaging experience where you must consider the long-term effects of your actions.- Progressive Difficulty: The game nails the slow-build RPG elements. Each level you conquer feels like a genuine achievement, rewarding your time and effort with a satisfying sense of progression.- Atmospheric Pixel Art: The 2D pixel art style not only brings a nostalgic feel but also enriches the game's dark, apocalyptic setting, enhancing the overall immersion.Cons:- Pace of Play: This game is not for the impatient. Each session requires a significant time investment, as rushing through can lead to frustration rather than enjoyment. It's best enjoyed in longer play sessions.- Learning Curve: The unforgiving nature might deter newcomers to the genre. However, for those who stick with it, the payoff is substantial.Stream-Friendly: While the game's slow pace might not be for everyone, it shines in a streaming environment where interaction with viewers can make the experience more dynamic and enjoyable. Chatters can engage with the decision-making process, making each session unique.Overall Experience:The Last Spell is not just a game; it's a tactical journey that requires patience, strategy, and time. If you're looking for a quick gaming fix, this might not be for you. But if you're ready to immerse yourself in a world where every choice counts, and you enjoy sharing that experience with others, then The Last Spell offers a rewarding adventure. Set aside a few hours, dive in with the mindset of a strategist, and let this game's depth and challenge captivate you. Highly recommended for fans of tactical RPGs who appreciate a game that respects their intelligence and time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of tactical RPGs like Wildermyth, Into the Breach and Horizon's Gate, and 30 hours in I'd  say The Last Spell is one of the best. I'm hooked on this pretty hard. Ever since I started playing this game my heroes have been awake every night all night fighting hoards of monsters, and so have I. So the game is very immersive.There's a good mix of different skills and equipment. Every weapon feels really different from every other, so there are a lot of different builds you can do. So far my favorite and most deadly is a dagger/handgun/crossbow armed assassin with the ability to blink teleport. Of course I named him Corvo. Second favorite is a poison spellcaster specialist with the druid staff for the creation of BEES, with a magic orb for backup and pondering.The randomness and difficulty both feel like they're well tuned. There's a lot of randomness, but it seems designed so that you need to experiment rather than just getting one build and going for it. You may not get the option to use the weapon or perk you want, so you'll need to improvise sometimes. Monsters have different weaknesses, so you may need a variety of tools and in the right place to deal with them.The music and artwork are a lot of fun too. The music sets a similar style and mood to Doom and also Diablo. There's a lot of character customization options and different equipment, and it's all rendered on the character sprites. You can also customize the portraits of your heroes at any time, although I wish the clothing customization on the portrait would automatically change based on what they're wearing in game. It's great!

_childDocuments_.review: Way too much emphasis on grinding to unlock even basic mechanics to the game. As of this writing I'm probably ~12 hours of real time playing and just on my last run I've finally unlocked what I'd consider the "basics" of the game. While "metagame grinding" could be a clever tactic to get players to learn the core mechanics before introducing the mechanics that require these core mechanics to do anything other than cause you to fail, this game doesn't do anything of the sort. Not only are you locked to the 3 basic weapon types, you are locked to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ possible version of those weapons for more than the first run. You'll get access to another 3 basic weapon type after your first run, but all of these weapons will still be locked to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "wooden" versions of them for several more runs. Same is true, and far worse, for armours. You also have to unlock all the buildings individually, action points for characters, and to make all of these unlocks worse, almost all of it is on the SAME reward track where you get points based on how long you survived the last run, which is completely gated by the content that you have yet to unlock. The process is extremely grueling because there's no way to optimize your gameplay in a way you could in hades to crush the whole game on a fresh save. Instead, you'll die very early in runs due to literally not having basic resources available for several runs in a row, in a turn based strategy game. With all of that said, the game mechanics are pretty fun, once they're available. If you can stand 20 hours of mostly pointless grinding before getting access to a serviceable version of the game, go ahead and pick it up. otherwise, don't botherEdit: Now at ~75 played hours, I've unlocked everything the game has to offer. I want to reiterate that the game is quite fun, but much of the "difficulty" does derive from basic stats being locked behind half a dozen or more runs. I went from dying at night 5 from having my "mages" killed to immediately beating the game after my initial post. The talent tree has a bunch of useless picks, and you actually stop accumulating talents after level 14. If they kept the grind the same length but put interesting choices in there as opposed to "basic weapon set 1, basic weapon set 2" and 4 action points being unlocks I'd change my review to a rec, but as of right now, you need to invest at least a dozen hours before you get to even experience what the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a thumb up, I'd like to give a rating firstGameplay concept  9/10. Love itGameplay experience 2/10.I've been waiting for this kind of game for so long. The game reminds me a version of Final Fantasy Tactics, but it feels better. As a survivor, you need to hold the base from waves of zombies. I have always longed for a tactical-survival game such as this one, and it feels amazing. I can see myself losing my life in replaying this game so many times. However, I wish I could give a full recommendation about this game. Aside from the good experience in playing the game, there are also important things that need to be addressed.Here's my view how this game is lacking:GAME PLAY INFORMATIONI don't know if I'm missing the information or anything, but there are a lot of information that this game does not provide. a. There are traits that could improve my characters, but the trait's information is non-existent. I had to google about opportunistic or isolation buff to understand the mechanics.b. There is no clear explanation of the game objective. I felt a terrible experience about this one. After 7th time trying the game, I finally meet the final boss on the Night 12 (The final night). I have killed the boss and the sprouts, yet the game didn't end yet. After couple of rounds, the boss spawned again. But this time, two bosses spawned. I thought this prank is quite upsetting, but I managed to defeat these two bosses. Yet, the game has not ended, I wonder why? There is no clear explanation what should I do in this final round. While trying to understand of what should I do, infinite (Literally) hordes are spawning continuously. There was NO indication of the night progressed despite defeating three bosses. So, I kept my best to hold the base by defeating hordes of zombies. But guess what? TWO MORE BOSSES SPAWNED AGAIN! It's totally ruined my experience in playing this game. It's like saying to my face that I could not win no matter what, regardless my effort in holding my base. If that so, then why should I defend the freaking base? I would just play aggressively until all my heroes die.There is no clear information how to win the game, should I kill the boss 10 times? should I kill the boss in 2nd round? should I survive until Xth round? Should I kill the boss with bow? Should I put a sacrifice a babyborn so that the boss will leave my base? What should I do to clear the stage??? This totally ruined my experience, and I don't think I want to experience it again. Spent 8 hours of my life just for a terrible prank at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but it's honestly the first turn-based strategy game that has really challenged me and made me excited/nervous for each encounter.I just beat the second difficulty stage for the first time as of this review and cannot imagine how it will get harder. The boss encounters are daunting and at times feel impossible but when you overcome the endless tide of monsters and come out on top it's a pretty great feeling that other turn-based games have never quite achieved for me.Something I feel like the game pulls off really well is the feeling of having bad-ass characters. In games like final fantasy tactics your units level up and get cool moves but you never quite feel like your character has become this unstoppable force of brutality. In The Last Spell, however, one of my characters has leveled up to the point where he has a 95% chance to dodge every attack. 95%! It gets better. Not only does he dodge practically everything thrown his way but every time he does he GETS ANOTHER ACTION POINT. The fact that the game lets you spec into so many different things is one thing I really love about it. Other examples would be my long range crit sniper who can hit the entire map, or my tank who takes pretty much no damage and kills anyone who attacks him.Despite how strong your characters can get the game is by no means easy. Every encounter can be lost just as easily as it can be won if you don't plan properly.This game is seriously something special but it's only for people who are prepared to crack their knuckles and accept the challenge. _childDocuments_.review: Not for the faint of heart, The Last Spell forces you to rethink your tactics and manage your playstyle on a whole new level. Most tactics games balance the player and enemies fairly, but here, the opposition is relentless, aiming to overwhelm you with a tidal wave of mist-bound foes. The limited resources push you to make every decision count, balancing between the dread of the incoming horde and the triumphant relief of scraping through by the skin of your teeth. If you’re looking for a deeply challenging, rewarding tactical experience, The Last Spell will keep you on the edge of your seat. My most memorable run of The Last Spell was:The first three nights were about building up the defenses, with my tank MVP, Rockfoot—a hammer-wielding juggernaut—holding down one side while my other two heroes took the opposite flank. Each night, I fought to keep the walls intact, my mage Shama spreading poison like wildfire to thin the horde. By night six, I had grown my team to six, balancing just enough firepower to survive but never with room for error. The defenses began to strain under the constant onslaught, but Rockfoot and Shama pulled us through every time.Then, on night eleven, disaster struck. Poor positioning at the beginning of the night cost Shama her life, leaving us exposed just as the walls started to crumble. I nearly lost two more heroes that night, scraping through by the narrowest of margins. I was careless, and the game reminds you that if you let your guard down for one moment, all can be taken from you.The city was in ruins, and with just enough resources left, I hired a new recruit with barely functional gear, hoping he’d survive the final night.The last night brought an endless horde and a boss. I stationed a hero on each wall, with 2 teleporting defenders ready to reinforce weak spots. But when the boss emerged on the north side—where my under-equipped recruit was stationed—I realized he’d have to face it nearly alone until the 2 teleporters arrived. Rockfoot held the southern wall, buying us time. The eastern defenses began to falter, forcing me to split forces as the boss entered its second phase.At the city’s heart, Rockfoot regrouped to defend the magical seal. Quick crawlers slipped through, but Rockfoot stood fast, refusing to let the defenses collapse. The final phase of the boss starts.I wanted to ended it quickly, so I rushed towards the it to deal as much damage as I can. In a desperate final push, the northern wall broke. The 2 that went to support the recruit had fallen trying to finish off the boss, leaving my recruit face-to-face with the bloodied and battered boss and a flood of enemies. My heart sank as three foes surrounded and clawed at him... but miraculously, he clung to life with just a sliver of health. He landed the final blow on the boss, dispersing the mist and bringing victory. Conclusion: This heart-pounding, nerve-wracking experience is exactly why The Last Spell is unforgettable. If you enjoy tactical games that demand every ounce of focus, where every loss feels personal and every win hard-earned, then I can’t recommend The Last Spell enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow,I only write reviews when I LOVE a game, and boy did I love this one! I wanted to actually finish it before reviewing. For me, this is the best game of 2023 so far. STORYThe world was almost destroyed by magic. You play as the Commander, a man who tries to save a village that gets attacked every night by ever growing waves of zombie-like enemies, imbued by magic. The story, which I won't spoil in this review, is nice and actually goes well with the gameplay.  You start with 3 heroes that each have randomly generated traits (bonus/malus) and talent trees. After every night, you can level up you heroes, but the characteristics you can upgrade for each hero is also randomised, meaning you can upgrade one characteristic from a selected pool. You can have up to 6 heroes.Depending on how well you did, you will receive gold and materials. Gold is used for constructing/upgrading buildings (which help you passively in many ways), recruiting new heroes, and buying new weapons for your heroes. Material is used for defences, such as walls, catapults/balistas, and traps. Defences help you actively during the waves.You have to survive a certain number of night (between 7 and 15), and you get a boss during the last night. Once the boss beaten, you can advance to the next village. There are 5 villages in total. I will list the pros and cons succinctly first, and I will go a bit deeper afterwards. PROS :+++ Gameplay (who doesn't love turn-based RPG mixed with roguelite element?)+++ Difficulty (rewarding)+++ Music (awesome!)CONS :- Difficulty (sometimes frustrating to spend hours in a run that end badly :( )- Randomness (I know it's expected of roguelike games, but still)Don't think that 2 cons for 3 pros is bad. The pro easily outweigh the cons by a factor of 1'000.+++ GAMEPLAYThe game, although simple at first glance, hides a loooot of complexity. The devs did a formidable job of introducing difficulties one after the other. I would even say that most of the game is a tutorial (from village 1 to 4) and the last village is the actual game in all its splendour and hardship. While I call it tutorial, there is barely any text or explanation. You get dropped in the world and then you survive. Each village brings something new to the game, and you learn how to overcome it by yourself. I absolutely loved it, but I see how it could be a tiny bit overwhelming for a less experienced player. Not that I am a beast, I took hundreds of hours to beat this game. Each weapon has it own moveset, and each hero has its own talent tree. It's important (and fun!) to try every combination.+++ MUSICNothing much to say except it awesome to listen to it while playing. The music, while of course played in a loop, isn't annoying even after hours of it. Kudos to whoever did it!+++/- DIFFICULTY/RANDOMNESSThis game is hard and ask a lot of the player. A run (from the first night up to the last) can and WILL last for many hours. You have to pay attention to every detail, because every hero is veeeeeery precious (even though some more than other), and a single error in placement could lead to an instant death. That is of course expected (and you can alt+F4 and go back to whenever you saved last :D yeah yeah call me a cheated I don't care), but it can be harsh. The random element of this game, although tempered a bit by the omens (bonus you can select at the start of each run), can be a bit frustrating. For exemple, I really wanted a mix of certain talent when starting, because some talent are only worth when paired with another specific one. So it was a bit frustrating to not have any way of choosing talent, even at a cost. You get what you get, and at least for me (call me a cheater I guess AGAIN :s) it meant restarting a run as many times as need so that I could get a "meta" (in my own opinion) character. And the game is so hard that it feels mandatory to do so. I only managed to kill the last boss because of my carry character...I'll take a concrete example : There is a trait that lowers the action point by 1. To be honest, having this trait is a direct reroll for me, as AP are so important in this game. This kind of randomness, to me, goes against the flow of the game. In the end, I loved loved LOVED this game and its difficulty level, especially as it doesn't spike. It goes at a steady pace until the very end where it culminates in hellblazing chaos. But potential buyers need to know this game will NOT go easy on you. **** CONCLUSION ****You should absolutely get this game. Just don't expect an easy, afk-winning game. Currently (as of 08.05.2023), only about 3% of the playerbase managed to kill the last boss.My congratulations to the devs. Awesome game. Can't wait for the DLC/next games.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game base with a cool genre-blend . Already value even in early access. Really promising with solid design and possibly new weapons/building/monsters.Gorgeous art Style and VFX. Good value for the price rn if you like tacticals.Major weak point right now imo : REALLY heavy on the meta progression side.Survive the  magical zombie horde every night by managing your heroes in a tactical turn by turn combat. Build, organize and produce in the village by day. Cool ways to organize your defense. Somewhat of a "simcity defense" aspect (think RTS like SC2) as your building have hp and can blocks foes as last resort. Lot of variety in the hero management with weapons, skills, gear and statistics. On this aspect, gear and stats are really well designed as you can pick from multiples possibilities, giving a random ever changing aspect but with some control.Terrain is for now pretty unexploited except from some obstacles that block line of sight and water that in unpassable. This aspect will most surely by enhanced in the future, with new maps.Loving the graphics of this game, dark fantasy vibes with cool-looking models and gorgeous VFX/animations.The OST is ON POINT. The music quality is at a level rarely seen and fits the game perfectly. Sound effects are good.Can fit anyone as there is both meta progression to make the game easier, ascension mode (scaling difficulty) or even easy mode with extra ressources to get you going.Nukes are bad, magical nukes are worse and you are the last hope of humanity.Game length, replayability and money value are still pretty hard to evaluate for me as the devs still have content coming. If done right, this could be one of this exception rogue-lite with hundreds of hours of replay value.This is currently meta-progression the game. Not being able to win first and second run is questionable design. You lose because your heroes are weak, not because you are bad at the game and lack knowledge about the game. Then we have runs with all meta progression unlocks that are basically easy mode with heroes having more stats, actions per turn, better gears and traits. Its weird because the devs got an ascension mode so they are aware of the importance of scaling difficulty that benefits new as well as experienced players. But you still have to lose the first few runs till the third/fourth, making the whole process grindy. This will be the major challenge for them to balance, more so when the run length will be upgraded to its final state.As for now, the runs are pretty "snowbally". You get more ressources for defending the city perfectly (with a smart design that discourage boring kiting techniques). As you have to split your gold between building an economy and giving enough to your heroes to get through the night. For this reason starting heroes make or break a run and some weapons way better than others (♥♥♥♥ you one hand hammer). Good starting gear/heroes allow you to greed and go full economy before getting hundreds of golds in mid-late game. Why would I build a melee character that require move points, HP, damages, defense, armor, regen, etc when I can have everyone a ranger/mage with only +range and damages giving them the best AOE and versatility ?More content (monster/weapons/skill/building) will be welcomed and the devs assured that they are already working on it.Big thanks to the dev team and good luck,

_childDocuments_.review: The other reviews aren't wrong. This is a dang good SRPG.Like Darkest Dungeon, you're building and maintaining a fortress in a world overrun with monsters, but unlike DD combat is handled in the fortress itself, as a tactical roguelike.The game's tone is bleak and grisly, and the writing doesn't take center stage, but it is strikingly creative. By turning the high fantasy genre into the apocalyptic genre, it ends up playing with some fairly interesting concepts and subversions.The real meat of Last Spell, however, is its gameplay. Like Darkest Dungeon, you lose your way to victory, but unlike Darkest Dungeon the game's feeling isn't one of slow attrition. Last Spell is about being absolutely overwhelmed, right now.Enemy units spawn in massive waves. Players have AoEs and ranged attacks, but they're a pittance against the mass and variety of mobs. RNG is a factor in hit chance, but it isn't too intrusive. For the most part, your attacks connect, and you survive if you've made the right tactical and strategic choices.Apart from Darkest Dungeon, probably my best other comparison for Last Spell is Into The Breach. Combat here is an open-ended puzzle, and you win if you can use your kit and the map creatively.However, Last Spell does lean a fair bit on its roguelite progression. Unlike Breach, you should expect to get mulched every time you play a map for the first time. It *might* be possible to clear all existing content without unlocking anything, but I'm not sure how human-achievable that would be. A lot of unlocks are straight up improvements over your existing capabilities.Overall, I'd strongly recommend this to anyone who likes basebuilding, strategy, and survival. Even in early access, it's a gem of a game, and I'm stoked to see it develop further.Edit: The game has some weird rubber-banding. When you first challenge an area, it's bonkers impossible. But then you get a couple key unlocks and it becomes pretty easy. And then the next area you challenge is bonkers impossible. I guess, as a pre-req for liking this game, you have to be okay with losing periodically. The first time you try an area, the challenge is in seeing how far you can get. Once you've tried it a few times and gotten some important unlocks, then the goal is to win it. Reinforcing this is the fact that you can't really sight-read a boss. The first time you fight one, it's going to do things you don't expect, and it's going to roll you. This is fine for me, I kind of like that the game feels impossible half the time, but if this is something that bothers you, you might not have the same experience.2nd Edit: Game rules. Now that it's out of early access, everything's been tightened up and made more accessible. It's still difficult, but you have a little more control over that difficulty, and the emphasis is slightly more on the waves being hard than on your resources being throttled. Interaction with the game also feels smoother. If you want to try one of the more interesting srpgs out there, and if you like a good mix of Number Go Up and blind panic over how many enemies just spawned, this is a firm recommend.3rd Edit: Good lord. Elderlicht is a mean stage. Any concerns I had about the game being too easy are absolutely invalidated by it. It's not unfair, and you can strategize to beat it, but there's never a moment when the pressure lets off, and it's long. I used every bit of cheese I could and barely scraped by. 10/10, good stage, I do not want to replay it.4th Edit: I will not be beating Glintfein. Every attempt on the map is a huge time investment, and by this point you're no longer really progressing with your unlocks. The individual waves start to require very specific builds, and your economy has to be perfect to go into these builds, and you have to get lucky with drops/misses and playing riskily to maximize your economy. And then in order to beat the boss, you have to have already known what it was going to do and built specifically for that thing. You can't sight read it like the other bosses in the game, so your first encounter with the boss means rerunning all of Glintfein again. I really enjoyed the game, but I'm not going to sink another dozen hours trying to clear one map.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game that does a lot of things very well. This is a fabulous turn-based RPG that allows you to develop a settlement and characters in a very difficult environment. The game is very hard and you are guaranteed to lose your first few runs. This is a bit annoying on one level, but the game makes it work because you still feel like you accomplished something making it as far as you did in your first few play throughs. Overall - Very high hopes for this game as this is an exceptionally good start to its early access journey and the replayability is already very high in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a clean, well-polished game created by developers who clearly understand the genre and good game design.  Everything from the menu, UI, sound, controls and gameplay are elegant and implemented harmoniously. This game will struggle to get Overwhelmingly Positive reviews because it's not an easy game.  This is true of any game that is remotely difficult.  People will write reviews crying (while pretending not to cry because they 'love' other difficult games) about how the difficulty is unfair.  It's not.  It's well-tuned and continues into a scaling difficulty mode after you win your first run.If they aren't crying about the difficulty, they're crying because they don't like rogue-likes when they purchase a rogue-like game.  You start weaker.  You unlock upgrades as you complete runs.  There are many games like this and this design is core to rogue-likes.  If you don't like that, don't buy this game.  If you do like that, this game is an instant classic that you should put into your library right away.I'll be looking forward to every update that this game sees and hope to keep coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh how I absolutely fell in love with this game. Had never heard of it, but the premise seemed cool and it wasn't that expensive so I decided to give it a try. Became completely hooked.It feels like a mix between X-Com/Final Tactics, Darkest Dungeon and all the new rogue lites that are in vogue right now, but it somehow reminded me of the first time I played System Shock 2 many years ago in the sense that, like with Shodan, you end up developing a toxic relationship with the game. It will punish you hard for your mistakes, and you will most likely fail some runs, each of which can take a couple of hours. It can feel pretty brutal.But you learn, you adapt your tactics and you prevail. Without going too much into spoiler territory, I lost my 2 best heroes the night before the last night of the game. I was tempted to quit right there, but decided to carry on, hiring two bozos from the inn to hold the line while my one-armed gunner butchered the battlefield. I was able to beat the last map by the skin of my teeth, and I promise it was glorious.I don't know how Ishtar Games were able to balance the game so that each boss ended up being just difficult enough to feel so frikking epic, but it really worked for me. _childDocuments_.review: A well executed game in many respects but one that suffers from fundamental design issues that hold it back from being a truly good gameimagine a very detailed turn based rpg/tactics game. imagine if one random type of mission in that game you could get, was "defend the base" or whatever. Defend the crystal core, yadda yadda. Which type of mission do you think players of that game would hate - the basic "kill monsters and dont die" gameplay, or the "defend the stupid immobile town and be penalized every time monsters damage it" type gameplay?The last spell is exactly that, which is why the designers have painted themselves into a corner, trying to turn this into a viable and compelling game - it barely works, but it would have worked better without this conceit, if the game was just a traditional dungeon crawler/tactics battler with its otherwise solid mechanicsThe best example of it is all the defensive traits/stats/perks/items in the game which occupy a permanently awkward spot since enemy attention is always gonna be on the base and not your heroes - you cant "tank" in any meaningful sense so the best investment is always killing power, CC and offensive utility - this is true even in games where monsters focus your characters, but in Last Spell the issue is compounded. Every time the RNG offers you defensive options you feel, rightfully so, that they are inferior options, since they compete with the vital offensive/utility stats you need to kill the stupid monsters fast enough that your base doesnt die.I wont claim The Last Spell isnt a deep game, because it is - what I'm saying is that the depth is sort of wasted on a gameplay loop that really isnt all that fun due to the flaws I talk about above. For that reason I wont recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you play an early access game, and the entire time you’re playing it, you’re under the grand delusion that the devs have done everything in their power to tailor this game to suit your expectations. You’re waiting for the doubt to come up, but it never does, which just leaves you enthralled with the experience whenever you revisit it. This was the case for me when it came to . Everything I describe will either light your world on fire or cause you to slam your head against your middle mouse key as you attempt to scroll away from this review in unleashed fury. Please don’t hurt yourself if you’re in the latter camp, by the way.TLS has a very straight forward game-loop: Defend against waves of undead as they assault your base, and then use limited resources to fortify your team and base after each wave has ended. Your main resources are Gold (for recruiting, buildings, and acquiring items), Building Materials (For defensive structures), and Mana (for heroes to unleash their most devastating attacks). The last resource, Essence, is for progression, since the game features Rogue-Lite unlock elements. I prefaced that the game seemed tailor-made to me, and here is where the first of my gaming kinks align. I enjoy resource-management when done correctly (IE starving you early, but rewarding you if you persevere), which is why I was always a sucker for classic Resident Evil-flavored survival horror and XCOM (oldschool and new) base-management. Those games pushed you to consider every tool/resource and never made you feel like you were well-stocked until the end-game. TLS accomplishes this beautifully. Your determination not to needlessly waste gold/materials/mana ends up paying off big time as you approach the end-game by allowing you to enjoy your arsenal, rewarding you for being smart enough to make it this far.But with Essence comes the boiling question from those who might be turned off by the fact that it does have meta-progression: Does this mean you will be ill-equipped without grinding for Essence? I wanted to have this question answered after the year-long anticipation of the dreaded beta-wipe, because it took me a few attempts to win a game when I joined the Early Access early in development. Since then, much-valued balance tweaks transformed the game-flow, entirely. I can safely say now that the answer is a very satisfying NOPE, you don’t need to grind. I have won the majority of my games with what resources I was dealt, even cranking up the apocalypse one tier at a time per run in order to expedite my essence-gains. Ishtar Games have committed a rare occurrence by making TLS one of the few examples of Rogue-Lite experiences where skillful play can override the need for progression-unlocks. Will this apply to all players who are brand new? Absolutely not, but the fact that you  succeed means they have once again struck another chord of joy in my heart.Time to talk mechanics. The meat and potatoes of the experience, where number-crunchers become heroes and “The Meta” rears its ugly head to—Wait, what, there’s no meta? You’re encouraged to be creative and react to the game’s challenges using your own intuition!? Yes.  Number-crunching monkeys will claim that the weapons can be segmented into tiers, but as someone who has completed Apocalypse 6, I can assure you that weapons are diverse in their implementation and utility as you make them out to be; the recent shift in damage-spec’ing, specifically, has transformed every weapon into having their own purpose when applied appropriately to your composition. A pro-tip: I highly advise against restarting whenever you have seemingly inadequate starting characters. I have had games where the negative traits were unbelievably stacked against me and I still won, because I assessed my starting equipment and randomly-generated perk-spreads, pushed for specific boosts during level-ups, and simply made-do, regardless of the seemingly weak circumstance. TLS pushes you to make the best of a bad situation, and while you can never feel truly safe and comfortable until the last few nights, the enjoyment factor of reaching that pinnacle of your run’s performance is deeply satisfying. The more you experiment with perks, weapons, and traits, the faster you learn to stop feeling like you  multi-hit, poison, and crit to dominate your enemies. You will learn to respect momentum, to tank professionally with a healthy dose of dodge & block, and to melt with isolation. All while enjoying my favorite aspect of this game: The aesthetics.Aesthetics can really swing me on how I feel about a game, regardless of the mechanical depth. I see two home-runs from TLS, regardless of its seemingly simplistic pixel-art. The first is the customization of your survivors. Full visual depiction of every item you equip? Check. The ability to hide helm so I can enjoy the look of my lads and lasses? Check. Full portrait + accompanying sprite customization with the added option to save portraits for future use? Super-check. The show-stealer that got me into the XCOM reboots was the ability to name and tailor my characters, to the point that I’d always get attached to them, going so far as to create fun head-canon about the interactions between the squad. In TLS, I refuse to even start a mission until I’ve played with appearances, saving favorites if I’m lazy and want to load a specific look and name back from the dead. That sticking point helps to keep me immersed. As for the second aesthetic factor? The  in TLS. The UI sounds, the combat-sounds, but most importantly? The absolutely orgasmic banger of a soundtrack. Subjectivities-aside, this music has a tone and it is as consistent as it is auditory peak-pleasure every time any of its tracks kicks in when the battle starts. I would even go so far as to say that without this soundtrack, I might not have invested a quarter of the time I have put into this game. Some later-added tracks during development only heightened my hype for its inevitable release.You owe it to yourself to play The Last Spell. It is  and deserves to be played if any of what I have said has perked your interest. To me, this is tactical turn-based gameplay perfected.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game on the 5th run...This is a masterpiece of strategic design. Never in my wildest expectations would I have thought something so simple, could be made so compelling and satisfying to play.Of the few nits I could pick, the most obvious is a lack of casual game modes. Even after setting all the easy options ON, the game is still often unforgiving and frustrating. But for those willing to endure it, the sense of satisfaction on success is unparalleled. The next nit, is the way the game ends on victory... It rings hollow, and is extremely anticlimactic. It is a good thing that this games mechanics stand strong on their own, and more than make up for it.The last, is the total randomness involved in the initial Hero team. At least after the INN is built you can pick and choose your additions. But the initial new game experience, leads to constant resets until you have a party with reasonable traits and weapon sets, that are unlikely to make things even more frustrating than normal.Should these three relatively MINOR issues get addressed, I can't imagine anything holding it back. A few tips for new players:- Unlock the Seer ASAP, to help keep the fog at bay.- Focus on Bows (Long and Short), and Hand X-Bows early on. Then make ample use of Druid Staffs.- Daggers and Hammers are the most efficient melee. Both are one handed, and offer excellent utility.- Don't underestimate the power of propagation effects!! Late game they become KEY.(I could go on, but this is a review... TLDR and all that.)Edit: 21_0829Just figured I'd mention that I have not felt the desire to play this much, since beating it the first time. I've tried a few times, only to be so irritated at the RNG of my party, and knowing I was going to slog for half a dozen rounds just to 'compensate' for it, that I quit before starting the second battle phase.I do not take back the fact that this is one heck of an addictive first run experience... But knowing that nothing but more heinously repetitive RNG is in store for each new *cough* non-victory-victory, just saps me of any sense of pending satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: After 120 hours of pure enjoyment, this is my favorite game of 2021, and possibly one of my favorite games I've ever played. After covid hit in 2020, I got into playing hundreds of different demos with all the new online gaming events, and the demo for The Last Spell was the best one I have ever played. I sat glued to my PC for 6 hours straight until I finally beat it, and was hooked to this game ever since. Now 2 years later, the game is out and in EA, and I couldn't be happier. This game is so good -  the gameplay, the atmosphere, the music, and most importantly, the pure emotions of barely scraping by a night when you thought you were gonna lose, or putting up a epic last stand until the end. The Last Spell puts you into the shoes of a hand few of overpowered but extremely outnumbered heroes defending a city tooth and nail until the last man stands. Everything about the game feels so awesome and epic, and once you get a few upgrades and the right equipment, your heroes become unstoppable. I will probably come back to play this game here and there for the rest of my days. Thank you Ishtar Games, The Arcade Crew, and The Algorithm for making this incredible gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Get in on this. If you like ANY tactics games - Fire Emblem, Advance Wards, Final Fantasy Tactics - you're going to like this. Right now, there are still clearly balance/difficulty issues, but I have full faith that stuff will get figured out, and it's very playable as-is. This game throws a LOT at you all at once, and at least some parts are *immensely* difficult, so this isn't a game to cut your teeth on if you're not an adept turn-based/tactics/rpg sort of person. However, with experience with these sort of games, almost everything is intuitive and doesn't require a Google search. Ranged users don't need to worry about armor...crit damage goes well with crit chance...you want to invest in resource generators early...that sort of stuff. This is ALL about the gameplay, but they nail the lore and setting too. It's bare boned, which is what you want for this kind of thing. The excellent heavy metal soundtrack and dark palettes are all you need. The story is clear, believable, awesome, and contains ZERO monologues or fluff - you seriously get right to it. What's good about the gameplay? Punishing difficulty and limitless ways to customize and optimize. Sound effects and animations are smooth and punchy, but "running the numbers" is quick and your decisions are rewarded each and every turn. The overwhelming variety of weapons & skills make me feel like I'm just starting after 40+ hours, and add replayability...as if this game needed it. This game is NOT perfect yet, but here's the thing: every last thing feels like it's in place already except for the balancing. The weapons make sense, the upgrades make sense, the story makes sense. Some menus & administrative stuff doesn't feel quite done, but this is waaay on the clean end of Early Access. If it looks like you'll like this game...you will. BUY THE LAST SPELL!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Game is alot of fun, easily worth the 20$ asking price. Because the developers are still adding alot of content and quality of life updates, I'd be careful about reading older reviews that had been completed prior to updates. They recently added a tutorial map (2 nights), a beginner map (7 nights), and then there's the "standard map" (12 nights), and a newer "advanced map" (12 nights) that's greater difficulty than the standard map. You unlock things between runs, and runs take variable amounts of time depending on all sorts of things (I think I beat the beginner map in 3-4 hours, but the standard map I think took me 10-12 hours on a run that I actually beat it on, but I take my time).  The variability of heroes, enemy waves, and strategies to succeed are so varied that you'll have fun playing and trying things out. There's a little bit of RNG with dodge stats and stuff, but to me it never felt that bad and there's ways of getting around RNG elements at times (e.g., weapons with non-dodgable attacks).

Wish there was a little more of that.I know they intend to release more DLC for this game. That's good. The only thing this game needs is to be expanded. _childDocuments_.review: If you like rogue-likes with the same gameplay loop, that requires multiple runs to unlock stuff, then this is your jam. I quit not long after getting to the 4th map because I was tired of the gameplay loop.  Starting from 0 just isn't fun for me after I've already done it several times.  Starting with the 4th map some b.s. kicked in too.  Suddenly I was missing way more than previous maps, even though the accuracy/dodge numbers were similar to previous maps.  Also, mobs magically started attacking from areas with the absolute least amount of coverage my ballistas and catapults had each round.  On top of that the 4th map starts a new mechanic that really puts the already weighted odds further in favor of the computer.  This is probably where that gameplay loop of play, fail, unlock, play, fail, unlock, play, fail, unlock really kicks in.  Again, that's not my jam but it's not going to stop me from giving this a thumb up review.  For the type of game it is, it's really good.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable tactics game with great music and good gameplay.  For early access, I've encountered no bugs or game breaking issues personally, so this game is very playable.  It has a decent difficultly curve on standard and feels vaguely similar to Into The Breach in regards to difficulty and some of the tactics elements.  It's much more variable though as there are no set character archtypes, just weapon sets and perks.  Additionally there are planning elements where you determine the pace of your city and that dictates upgrades or city defenses, so you can go about things all sorts of ways.  That said if you wanted to min/max everything I'm sure there are generally strategies that should routinely win if followed consistently.  Unlocks in the game are handled through what are essentially achievements that once met unlock something for the rest of the game and all subsequent games.  This system can be a little frustrating because all the unlocks are not available or visible from the start.  So if you heard about a certain item/tower and wanted to target unlocking that, you wouldn't know what you needed to unlock first to make that option available.  On the whole I highly recommend the game to anyone interested in some tactics with long term planning/city building as well as individual fight mechanics.

The only downside is the grind to get there, but I like grinding so that's not an issue for me.As this game is still in early access, they're adding new enemies, varieties, quality of life updates, etc.. and they listen to community feedback. I look forward to more updates and will definitely keep coming back.Update: I do keep coming back, such a joy to just play the game every now and then.

_childDocuments_.review: hours of playtime writing this review: 23I am pleasantly surprised with how much I have been enjoying this game over this past week. This game's progression system from run-to-run feel really solid to me and make me want to hop right into another game to try out my new unlocks. The game is hard by design and I love that. You need to plan our your heroes' action economy to kill, slow, stun, and wipe out hoards of different creatures before they breach and destroy your city. Even on the wave before you wipe, there is a sense of pride having your heroes slowly falling back to your town center to fend off against enemies pouring in through the gates knowing very well they will not see the next dawn.Pros:-Variety of weapons allows for in depth team customization-Progression allows for introduction of more advanced play-styles once you have started to figure the game out-Great soundtrack-Lovely pixel graphics-Very polished for an early access game-Well worth the price even as an early access titleCons:-It is best to wipe on your first night in the game, as this quickly introduces you to the meta system and allows you to start your progression-Some weapons seem to be more powerful than others and may need some balancing-To some, the grind for progression might be too high, however, there is an easy difficulty setting if you are having a hard time-If you fail a wave you don't get any default fraction of essence for the night once you fail, so sometimes it is more efficient to abandon the run and start anew

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game.And I started off unsure if I'd like it, but it is like a fine french cheese, at first you're afraid, you're petrified...but then you enjoy the intricacies of its generous mechanics.But like any good french cheese, it is not to binge. Take your time to savour it, runs can get lengthy anyway (I cleared the first town in 4h, the second in 8h), but it's okay. You don't have to rush things. And the more you understand the mechanics (stats/perks/buildings/weapons& moves/omens/damage types), the easier it gets to break open this trove of fun.The game itself is not hardcore as you would imagine from the aesthetic, you can do "boundless mode" runs which allows you to use all the run modifiers (omens) at once at no other cost than having a bit of silly overpowered cheaty fun.The music is gorgeous too, it supports your heroic battles perfectly, doom style.In short, this game is a theory crafters heaven. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very neat and cool turn-based wave defense game. Balance your base building/economy while leveling up and equipping your 4 heroes to fend off waves of very bad purple monster guys. Solid and standard turn based combat, your heroes have movement points, a few abilities and some action points to spend each round. All heroes go, then all enemies have their turn. Decent difficulty, with several ways to tweak in game. You have the option for adding on challenges to get increased rewards, and/or using "omens" which are little slots you unlock that give bonuses. Has roguelite elements where each run is slightly different, and you slowly unlock permanent rewards both by standard progression and achieving certain actions. Good graphics/art, sound and music are nice, cool background story and atmosphere.Remember to upgrade your inn, you can have over 4 heroes at the same time. Good luck!

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is still in beta, I think it is absolutely excellent. It is a clash between tactics style games and the tower defence genre, personally I enjoy that. The story, while cool, it just a catalyst for the gameplay and personally it works very well. PROS- Fantastic soundtrack- "classes" or weapon types feel distinct from one another and have their own upsides and downsides, they are also relatively balanced- Level up system is basic but fun, given the roguelite elements- Unbelievably satisfying to wipe on 30+ enemies on your turn- The daily regeneration feature for HP and Mana is very intesresting, and implemented excellently CONS- I can see this game getting a tad repetitive towards the end, although I am still absolutely loving it so far.- The audio for the spell tome and pistol need some serious work, they are very poor quality.- Sometimes the starting traits of your characters can kill a run before the first night is even started. (Personally I would implement something similar to how State of Decay 2 deals with this issue, you can randomize your characters until you get something not awful and start when you are ready)All in all, this is an absolutely excellent game. If you are on the fence I genuinely cannot recommend this game enough. I do not leave reviews EVER but the devs have really captured something special here. This game is difficult, even brutal at times, but I just can't stop playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played.The story, the gameplay, the challenge, the progression, the art, the music... all so masterfully done!Every choice matters, and each action really makes you think before you commit. The separation of the missions into two repeating phases, night combat and development, really makes the game unique and gives some relief between the tense night begins again.If you like tactical games like XCOM, but also wave clearing games like tower defenses or survival genres, and even base building games, this is a great mix between them all, and I couldn't recommend it enough.The combat feels very tactical, with a low skill floor but a high skill ceiling. There is probably always a better way to do what you just did, and you notice yourself getting much better as the game progresses.The hero progression throughout the missions are also very rewarding, and you really feel like each hero is unique. Seeing someone you spent so much love and time on die really hurts, but adds to the dire tone of the game.When your base is literally overrun and you are about to lose once you end your turn, but you get that last hit on the boss to win the mission in the clutchest of victories just feels SO  SATISFYING.With new unlocks coming out of almost every night, and new difficulties to attempt once clearing an easier difficulty, the replayability is also massive.5 stars out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the premise: pixel art meets final fantasy tactics meets tower defense. It's a roguelike, so expect to repeat the same city over and over again wiith the same monsters. Buuut... it could have been made in a more diverse way. Ok, I mightn not be the brightest strategist, but I got bored of playing the second city four times, which was I think 15+ hours, with no changes. Imagine playing the same level with the same environment, music, monsters... for 15 hours. The nights were too long, reaching night 8 over 12 (i think) and lose is way more annoying that losing on night 4 over 8. BUT i know that this could be something that people could enjoy. As I said, it's a time sink. I'm actually still wanting to play this game, it gets kinda addictive, but I uninstalled it because i know that It would be just another 50 hours of repeating the same pattern, which i'm not interested right now. _childDocuments_.review: I like to always check the Developer before purchase, just in case they're Ukrainian. Sorry, I meant Russian.This is from Ishtar Games' website:"Ishtar is the symbol of a strong feminine – free of all masculine guardianship – contrasting with the patriarchal society norms. Using Ishtar’s name – a strong and free woman – is to fully assume our feminist convictions."That's fine, everybody has the right to their beliefs, however ridiculous and/or wrong.However, notice that the "patriarchal society norms" comes from a company where the three directors are all men. Yep, you couldn't make that up. There aren't any women programmers in this company, and there is only one woman Game Designer.Women at Ishtar Games seem to occupy the 'traditional', or even stereotypical roles, ie. artists, HR, marketing.Ok, so much for feminist convictions.The company used to be called 'CCCP', which - for those who are not aware - is the Russian name for the USSR (Союз Советских Социалистических Республик, or Soyuz Sovyetskikh Sotsialisticheskikh Respublik). It could be a general lack in education, or ignorance, or insensitivity, to be unaware your company bears the same name as the acronym for one of the more murderous regimes in history, responsible for tens of millions of deaths via deliberate starvation (Ukraine 1932-33), mass executions (Katyn, 1940), assassinations (Stalin's Purges) etc. Perhaps the three white, male directors of Ishtar Games eventually did realise that, hence why the name has been changed. But then, why mention it on your website?Would you have named your business NSDAP, for example? Good luck with that.As for the game itself - I see why it may appeal to many people, just not my cup of tea, but perhaps I will re-purchase at a 99% sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Zombies. Swords. Guns. Magic. More zombies.Excellent game, very good feeling while playing it.It's basically a strategy - survival game, where you have to protect a small village.It's hard, especially the first games (you cannot really win the 1st time).However the perks you unlock give a long life to the game and make it way easier.The developers are doing a great job with the updates.I played 80h, mostly after launch.Came back recently with Glenwald update (new map).It's very fun and I like it a lot.For the price, it's a good investment if :-You like tactical games with thinking about upcoming turns.-You like difficult strategy games.-You want to kill waves and waves of zombies to chill after a long day.It's not a good investment if :-You don't like hard games (which is fine btw).-You don't like zombies.-You want a game that has a story (there is ~none).As for myself I'm happy with it and I'll play it a little more.But expect to be bored after a few dozen hours played, it start to get repetitive, even with new content.
