_childDocuments_.review: It is quite grindy, and you will 'lose' quite a lot in the beginning. But thats also part of the game. It feels good to come back and progress further than you did the last time as you power up in various ways, and there's actual progression between all of your runs. All in all, its a great game from what I've seen so far and one I don't mind recommending at all. I'm looking forwards to seeing what else the developers can pull out of their hat for this game in the days to come, because if they can continue improving it, then this is going to be one of the better games of 2021 ^^
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Sink into tactical zombie whooping. In a magic-postapo world you're the last bastion. Your objective is to survive for several days.Game is split in days & nights. Build up your village & upgrade your heroes during the day, fight off the hordes at night. Easy to understand, hard to master. It's roguelikish - if you loose you get to unlock more stuff like buildings & equipment for next runs. Loosing is expected. Experimentation is needed. Satisfaction is guaranteed. It's beautiful, and it has awesome music. The attacks & spell effects look really good, the attack feedback is meaty. For an early access game devs really put the effort in and every now and then smaller or bigger update drops.The only thing I hope will be shaped in the future is more things to do. Game offers currently two maps - hard, and harder. After beating them you may replay them in Apocalypse modes (few levels of it), each increasing difficulty in one way or another.I'm not a fan of grinding over and again the same challange, with just upping the difficulty for sake of it - you are not rewarded in any way for beating game on it's harder difficulties. It may take time to unlock all metaupgrades (i.e. buildings & weapons for the new starts after you win/die), but after you get everything there's nothing to look forward to. With that in mind I already spent 114hrs with it. It's worth a buy, devs work hard on it and really listen to user feedback (thanks for adding arrow towers!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Either I suck at this game or the devs have no idea how difficult it is to reach the boss after "a few tentative runs." Try 15. Nearly both shops completed and I can't get past day 8 lol.But the game is wonderful, truly a basebuilding roguelike that scratches a FFTA2 itch (partly, wish you could field more heroes). There are some things that I wish were present, like specific traits to pick for a magic class vs. ranged just to specialize, but I won't complain too much. It is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game has everything you would want in a nice tower defence game and it's not a bad game by any means.Personally, I don't think they got the progress curve right, you need to lose a lot! before you get anywhere, and you don't really have any chance at the lower levels to out skill your pending death.It basically you are "this good" at the game, now get "this far" before you die so then you unlock permanent perks that will let you get a bit further into the game, and the cycle repeats till you eventually have enough "helps" to beat the game.And I don't think that's fun.Sadly I don't recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: It's simultaneously overwhelming and manageable. There's crazy numbers of enemies afoot, and it almost always feels like a game of scarcity when dealing with it. Every turn you ration what you have and prepare the best you can, and then you make do with it. It very often feels like you're losing until you're not, and sometimes you're doing great and winning—until you're not. The challenge feels very nicely balanced; It is neither in your favor nor in the favor of the enemies. Your decisions before, during, and after the night carry an uncommon amount of weight and the strategy game is real.The one negative—and something pretty standard in rougelikes—is you get drip-fed unlocks as you play. You might play for hours and then unlock an essential building for your town that you really would've liked sooner. For as difficult as the game is, I feel like they could stand to introduce some of the essential infrastructure and weapon types sooner. It doesn't feel great trying to put together a puzzle with only half the pieces early on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: So, I picked this game up because I'm a huge fan of turn based tactical games. It is definitely a great concept of the turn based genre. But, as it is in early access, there is a lack of continuity to the game. Where traditionally games like these put you through different maps/layouts this one bogs you down in the same map. There are many different factors that will make each playthrough unique. BUT, the game is designed for you to fail. Many, many times. And each time you restart the map is the same. This is my biggest gripe about the game, as I would like to have a feeling of progression that is more diverse than what it currently offers. Without the constant failing. The premise of the game shines through this lackluster feature, and if you stick with the game it is very fun to, slowly, build up to endgame. If you are a patient person, and enjoy the grind, this game will definitely be for you. The meta in this game definitely is unbalanced in its current state, there are critical builds that outshine all the others. If you don't follow the meta, victory is never going to happen. I have made it as far as the 8th night in the game, and I have definitely enjoyed myself. I do recommend the game, the developers seem to be interested in fixing the issues that the game has, and they have a process for feedback that is fairly simple. With that being said there is definitely room for improvement. If you are looking for a finished product go elsewhere. If you want to take a chance on the studio sticking with the game, like I am, I think you'll enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start with a simple statement. This is an amazing game, you should try it if you have any love for turn based games, difficult challenges, or incremental progress.When I played the prologue when it was available, this game felt like it was made by someone trying to make a game specifically for me. That holds true for the EA version as well. It has a dark setting, atmosphere, good detail, and a banging soundtrack. The game challenges you every night on how well you prepared and invested your resources, and it will happily roll right over you if you made poor choices. You won't win the first, second, or third time you make a run. This is by design though, you just don't have the resources, and that's part of the theme: fighting impossible, hopeless odds. As you learn the game, you'll unlock new and better tools, a better starting position, better gear. It's going to take a while before you'll have the right setup to get to the end, but that's the way it's meant to be, because you probably don't have the experience to get there right from the start either. It could definitely use some tweaking, and speaking of...As much as I love the game, it isn't without its flaws. The dodge mechanic needs to be reworked, and there's an angry horde screaming about it on the forums and suggested features so I'm sure it'll come. Some of the unlocks could be a bit more timely, and honestly I dislike how you don't get any rewards for the night you fail, the game should want you to play to the bitter end, because it's heavily, heavily themed towards fighting to the last moment where everything falls apart. As it is, though, you're better off time-wise just giving up once you're in an unwinnable position and starting over than playing through another 20-30 minute night just to lose.The last night also sealed the game for me as my favorite of the year, and I probably won't be moved from that. It took me completely by surprise and I won by the skin of my teeth, but it was iffy at best and I was not prepared. I want to see more maps, layouts, maybe even some customization options with the towns. Can't wait to see how the game grows from here, but even at the price I paid, I've gotten more than enough time out of it to justify the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: One heck of a game. They are already nailing it and the price is a steal with this Replayability. There is a bit of Rng to your runs but that is the whole fun of it. Would love to see a save game feature added that just removes the save when you load it so it could not be abused to reload when you die however. 11 hours in and I am hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: My where did the time go?! I recently bought this game on a whim when it was on sale after having a couple of beers and it exceeds all expectations. The Last Spell excels in mixing current trending genres in gaming in a way that most other games fail to accomplish on their own. And the soundtrack, my lord, the soundtrack blaring in the background as you mow down hordes of enemies and survive down to the last enemy is an experience in itself. Whether you get this game on sale or not, give The Last Spell an honest try until you reach the first boss battle. Worth the struggle and triumph. Trust.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great but it has its flaws right now. Highly recommend playing on easy mode as currently the roguelite elements make the normal difficulty just too hard. It is possible to beat the game playing normally but you have to have tons of time to play and make every decision in the most optimised way or you will lose. something as simple as misclicking can ruin your 5 hour run. playing on easy gives the game room to shine with tons of growth and replayability. this is early access and a lot of balancing will probably happen to make this a tad bit easier but overall the game is fantastic and has a lot of potential.

I'm only on the second level with all these hours stacked up.  I've lost on this level nine times now I think. It will break you down and you will want to come back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent base defense roguelite. Ton of unlocks, plenty of different ways to kit out your heroes and some different play styles for them. Boss fights are fun and challenging, you can clear some on your first try others the mechanics might surprise you and wipe you fast. It is a time sync though, doing a single zone is 6-8 hours if you play from night one until the end. This is not a 30 minute run type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A very weird and gritty top down tactics RPG roguelike.  I think most of the major system revamps are done, and the game feels good, if a little slow and time consuming at times.  The highs of barely scraping by the last few nights are hard to undersell though, so its worth the grind if you're looking to burn some time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty great. For a roguelike it has pretty great balance between completely resetting your progress and giving you little bits to help you with the next run.My biggest gripe is there are a lot of QOL improvements that could be made. I feel like on a single turn I'm clicking 10+ times per character. The keyboard shortcuts are helpful but not as useful as I'd like. The way the camera recenters over your character in deployment phase is annoying because you have to constantly scroll near where you want to place them, and placing one character doesn't auto increment to the next character to be placed. The dialog and some of the information screens can use a quick button. Like when you clear a night, why do I have to click on each individual reward if there's no choice between them?And in construction phase there doesn't seem to be an undo button. I've misclicked placement a couple of times and had to either eat the cost in destruction or make do with my sub-optimal choice. Can't even reload the game because it saves after each action. This is especially frustrating because the way you can upgrade and fix buildings in the town can also eat a ton of resources if you don't know to fix the structure before upgrading it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, satisfying to improve at with a lot of skill expression in both the combat and building aspects. Notably tough at first but once you get some unlocks and get a hang of the more powerful things you can do like power-leveling an item crafting building or stacking multi-hit it's not hard to win 100% of the time on the base difficulty and map.Devs also seem to be on the right path with updates and patches, not just abandoning it though it's in fair shape now especially with the perks update.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Devs working the kinks and balance out though. At the moment though the game is way too hard. I like the random seed aspect of it but some of the combos shouldn't be seeded together or maybe buff them a bit? Magic is very very lack luster. Debuffs are nice but any type of consistent hoard management would make me feel less like I'm getting cheated on a wand sword xbow seed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely savage tactical defence. Respond each turn to the changing waves of enemies, shrinking battle map, limited resources and evolving demands.This is a slog, and you will pay for every inch with the lives of your heroes. You will not start off with the material you need to win, so expect to play multiple hours long runs without needed equipment, structures and manpower as you fight across repeating runs, slowly gaining the tools you need to hold the line. Mean Spirited, grindy, and demanding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is super addicting. It's a mix of turn based strategy, tower defense, and an incremental progression system that really keeps me hooked. Each run, I unlock new abilities that help me make it just a little farther the next time, which always makes me want to start a new run as soon as the previous one ends. It makes me totally lose track of time in a way that no game except Civ has done before. Open the game up, and seemingly instantly 3 or 4 hours have gone by. Love it and looking forward to updates coming!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing quite scratches the SRPG Itch like the Last Spell. Dynamic and deep difficulty with the mechanical parts to allow for runs that can end in defeat, a slim victory or a crazy overpowered breaking of the game (in a good way!) The one main complaint about each run taking several hours long is a valid one, however I tend to see them like campaigns, meant to be played across several gaming sessions. The Day/Night cycle gives you a breath of fresh air. Doing nothing but the nightly zombie grind or nothing but the day's econ mode would wear out its welcome but flipping between the two and having what happens in one have a huge impact on your performance on the other keeps the stakes high and each day and night interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A solid rogue-lite base defense game that does a dam good job making you feel weak at the start and the gradual rise in power is so noticeable that it feels like a weight is being lifted off your shoulder. Right up to the next map where is slams that weight right back down.It is honestly worth it thus far in my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually stupidly good. A great game for people who like to strategically weigh options, try to "solve" games by min-maxing characters/builds, try to figure out the most overpowered combos. A point of some people's criticism, I really like the RNG nature to the game actually, keeps the player on their toes so they can't literally just copy a cookie cutter build they are comfortable with over and over again, you need to adapt, at least a little... _childDocuments_.review: its a fun game definitely not polished yet. you control heroes in a city and fight huge hordes of demon/undead/minions I don't know what they are but they are dead. start with 3 heroes and maneuver trying to kill hundreds of monsters. I think the first day of survival has like 50 to defeat. rogue like game, turn based strategy, survive as long as you can get some new bonuses gear up as go all heroes reset on restart. the game slowly turns into a tower defense game in addition to your heroes it kind of reminds me of dungeon defenders but with a birds eye view. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Good combat that reminds me of the old Final Fantasy tactics in some ways. Love the fact that characters get random stats rolled on them, hoping there is a way to reroll the starting units you get with an upgrade or a future update. Definitely hard but its rougelite so even if you fail you still make some progress and make your next run better.Solid game as is and very excited to see the progression of this game.EDIT 11-15-22Well, I came back to the game a year later cause I didnt enjoy the progression wipes that kept happening during development. It looks like the game is almost finished so I decided to give it a go again. I still have the same disdain for the roguelite meta progression. This comes down to a personal preference though. Personally I dislike when a game feels like you have to fail a few runs and get upgrades before you can win, and I definitely feel that here. If you are ok with these sort of meta progression systems in other games then you will enjoy it here. There are plenty of unlocks to get and you always feel like you earned something from a failed run.I really enjoy the Daytime planning phase and base building elements.You have plenty of choices on how to use your resources. You can decide if you want to econ hard early and just pump out insane amounts of defensive structures, or maybe get structures built to buff the stats of your heroes each day. The fact that certain building offer buffs/bonuses each day make it much more impactful to get them early on and really makes you think about what to do with your limited resource pool early.Overall I'd definitely say the game is worth the $20. If you like roguelites with a meta progression system and turn based tactics games with just a sprinkle of base building, then you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent entry into the tactical roguelike genre. Tough, tactical decision making that rewards careful thought and planning. Unlocks galore give you a supercharged feeling of progress. The interaction and strengths and weaknesses of the incredible array of weapons/gear/skills is very satisfying. Buy this immediately if you enjoy tactical combat

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a solid turn-based tactics game with between-battle economic development reminiscent of real-time strategy designs, and I do recommend it, but with a significant caveat.  The gameplay here can be succinctly summarized as "what if 'They Are Billions' but more 'X-COM-ish'."During the game, you'll defend a town over a series of nights, each night with an escalating threat, and during the daytime you'll develop the economic base of your town while recruiting, equipping and leveling a small squad of heroes.  There are trade-offs between long-term economic gains and defenses and upgrades which will be immediately useful for the next battle.  Perma-death and significant randomness in the available heroes and upgrades give the game a rogue-lite feel.  This is all delightful.The big caveat here is that many of the interesting and useful options for your town are behind unlocks which can be a significant grind to make available.  This is not my preferred design philosophy for rogue-lite or rogue-like games -- I much prefer having all options available from the start, and any unlocks should be able making a run harder, not making a run easier.  The design here seems exactly backwards to me, as the game will be its most difficult when you are new and still learning the systems, but will become progressively easier not only because you will gain a better understanding of how to play effectively, but also because you have unlocked significant upgrades.Still the battles are fun enough, with a necessity for crowd control which seems unusual for turn based tactics games, and the strategic choices in the daytime phase are pleasingly difficult to make.  Given all of this, I am recommending the game, despite the flawed progression system.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a very interesting take on a turn-based tactics game that takes some cues from town management sims and tower defense games, mixes it with some solid turn-based staples and a few very unique new ideas. The result is fun and refreshing take that is both approachable at first and rewarding for long-time players. Scenarios in TLS involve two phases. During the day phase, you'll use workers to clear out ruins and corpses and work at various buildings you can construct to offer better equipment, healing, or other bonuses to your heroes. At night, you use your team of heroes to fend off seemingly endless waves of night creatures who are dead set on raiding the center of your town and smashing everything on the way.I think where The Last Spell is most unique is in it's approach to combat. Compared to some turn-based games like XCOM, Battle Brothers, or other popular ones, you'll be dealing with hundreds of enemies simultaneously. Of course, a lot of them are zombie-like shamblers that will crumble in a single hit but you'll find quantity has a quality all its own in TLS. Of course, there are also elite monsters, ranged threats, enemy spellcasters, and other unique monsters mixed in too. Thankfully, all the enemies take their turn in one big swoop and you can fast forward as needed. In turn, your heroes in The Last Spell can typically move farther and take many more actions per turn than playable characters in a lot of other turn-based games. You can freely move between heroes and use their actions in any order as you like (move one guy, have another use a ranged spell, have the first guy move more, have someone else buff him, then have the first guy use an attack, etc.) This means you can (and will on harder difficulties) get REALLY creative in combo-ing weapon skills, hero perks, and consumables like potions and scrolls. The name of the game is balancing crowd control with enough flexibility in target selection and damage to still take out major threats.The story in The Last Spell is to me, secondary to the great core gameplay mechanics but still interesting enough. Think fantasy post-apocalypse where the old warring kingdoms' use of catastrophic spells of mass destruction have kickstarted a total end of the world event, and now you control the united survivors as the recalcitrant mages attempt to cast "the Last Spell", sealing away all magic forever.The games' presentation is also rock solid. The pixel art is pleasant and some of the spell effects are really impressive, especially the giant AoEs and the spells that grapevine through enemy crowds, like chain lightning. I will say this game has a banging prog-metal/djent - inspired soundtrack. Day phase music is appropriately chill and atmospheric, but when the night falls, the combat bangers kick in and do a great job keeping you engaged. The music is definitely a plus for me!I think most fans of turn-based games will like what they see here. I very much enjoyed the different take on turn-based combat that The Last Spell provides. The city management side of the game is engaging but not overwhelming; it's definitely more about the combat. Individual scenarios can run long, so expect to either have a 3-4 hour play session for some of the later ones or be prepared to take a break and come back another day for some. I easily got 100+ hours out of this game (for me, this was enough to wet my feet in the post-game content but by no means a full clear of the game) and plan on returning as more content is released.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I had a bit of a rollercoaster of a start with this game. I loved it, then I struggled on the boss nights, got frustrated and quit. Then I picked it back up again, and I'm glad I did. You gradually unlock new buildings that introduce new mechanics, there are several combinations of weapons that you can build with your heroes as well. It's difficulty scales nicely as well. There are difficulty modifiers you can add as well if you feel like there isn't enough challenge. The developers worked hard on this game and it shows. For the price its worth picking up
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A very good strategy experience that is quiet worth your time and effort. I like the concept, and every night you play can be different whether it's which enemies come, how you build your characters, or which buildings you make and what you do with them. It's got tons of replayability, very fun and I've quiet enjoyed my time with it and would recommend it to anyone who likes strategy games, and who wants a challenge cause this game can be quiet hard. Starting out before I knew the mechanics better i could tell what nights were gonna be my last, now I can sometimes correct myself if it's going down hill but sometimes you know you didn't prepare well enough. But i like that it's hard and isn't easy, and i wish more games were like that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game hits the mark for every type of game I enjoy. I won't lie the game itself is really hard. Very basic game play to understand but the amount of strategy that goes into every night is unlike anything I have played. I have seen a lot of reviews complaining about the difficulty and yes it can be frustrating but also extremely rewarding when you get a good run going. The essence reward system is something that I think a lot of people are overreacting about. I think it is completely fair to have perks and buffs locked behind a reward system. It directly reflects your skill and ability to get further into each run to earn more essence. Games like Hades which is EXTREMELY popular has almost the exact same system for buffing your character.My only major complaint about the game is the point I'm at right now I have been able to test every weapon and I just know that their are some weapons that are just never worth grabbing(short sword lol) but even then maybe some weapons are better for different towns and challenges i'm not 100% sure about that yet.If you like Grid style turn based combat, town management, party management, and rougelike elements I highly recommend this game. I am 25 hours into the game and definitely see myself playing this for a long time. But be warned you WILL die a lot but if you stick with it you will get better and enjoy the game more and more.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Game's not even done yet and there's already so much content. A whole bunch of skills per class/archetype, buildings, upgrades and meta-upgrades. The combat is incredibly enjoyable thanks to the many kinds of builds you can try and combine, the satisfying visual and sound design for abilities, the massive hordes you whittle down and the occasional lucky propagation effect. Having 10 enemies explode at once thanks to a chain lightning with a good prop build just puts a smile on my face. Also, void waifu.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I was very interested in the game and it is right up my alley, but I encountered nothing but crashes.  Several flavors of crashes too, bluescreens, unity errors, clean dumps to the desktop, etc. I've updated drivers, updated windows, verified the game files, and even switched out my video card to try and get this thing to run.  No matter what, the game doesn't survive a few nights of battle.  It took me over an hour of troubleshooting and restarts to get through the tutorial.  After the 3rd crash in the first mission I was done.The little I was able to play I enjoyed, but the game just doesn't run for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a little bit of everything I like.  Character customization, a roguelike progression system, an RNG-based leveling system to keep players from building Godlike characters, tactical turn based combat...I'm not sure how much replayability it will have once I have beaten the 12th night, the lack of camera rotation is a bit clunky, and the game doesn't really excel in any area, but I have played it for almost 2 days straight since I bought it.  They've clearly done something well.First impression rating: 9/10 (I can really see myself binging this for awhile)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Just an amazing game, sadly melee just seems the least viable path for your heroes. With movement being such a big deal even for casters/rangers it becomes almost a problem for melee. Perhaps better melee perks are needed to really give them a leg up. Regardless, I had lot's of fun with this one, incredible amounts of depth and replayability, just need to branch out from propogation and crit builds lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game - not perfect, but a refreshing take on base building and defense strategy. I've been playing since EA began and I've seen great improvements. There are only a few games I've retuned to in EA and this is one. In fact, this is the only review I've written for a game. I'm doing so to support a team whose commitment to this product is evident in their constant updates and major reworks. Well done and keep it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game opens a pandoras box of theorycrafting between perks, itemization and weapons. I would say if you ever liked finding your own kombos in games and you are not afraid of at least a 20h investment you should give the last spell a go. keep in mind it is no easy game! and I would add that the update that just shipped could make it even harder for most - me included.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Beaten the game in 8 runs, that was my 2nd time reaching the boss, and being prepared made it feel like a piece of cake.Don't listen to the comments claiming that this game is too hard/grindy. People who say that just suck at it!Yes, you can't clear it from the first attempt, and you accumulate bonuses after every try. But the amount of gear and possibilities is so vast that given it all from start, you would probably lose anyway. Every time you try, you get further, you become stronger, and you also get better. Eventually you collect just enough bonuses for the game to provide just enough challenge for your skill to beat it.My advice: don't focus too much on "farming" bonuses, but instead try to think of how to utilize what you already have in a best way. The most immediately useful things to look for: the number of your heroes (Inn) and the number of action points they have. Everything beyond that - just find what suits you.There are some minor bugs, but the game is quite polished and very enjoyable.Looking forward for the release!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing rogue-lite turn based game. Has a learning curve and provides a great challenge that leaves you feeling satisfied by the time you reach the end of each map. _childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a difficult and sometimes admittedly frustrating game.It is also a good game. There is much to learn, and to master, and there is content for people of varying skill levels, including boudless mode which allows even players who are not confident in their tactical skill to access later areas of the game.A little bit of a spoiler ahead, if you want to experience the game for yourself - skip the last part.The greatest downside of the game to me is its bosses. For all nights except the last one the challenge of the game is to manage a horde of enemies, with some elites sprinkled in. This dynamic is heavily flipped on the last night, which features a unique boss to every area. Each boss has its own identity and a way to fight it, which makes for a variety at the end of the run - however the first time each boss is encountered it is a surprise unless the player decides to spoil the boss for themselves.This makes The Last Spell a game which in my experience does a very good job of teaching you the basics throughout the first nights and making you learn lessons that are applicable towards the rest of the game, EXCEPT for the final night of each run which is a bit of a 'got ya' and often a loss the first time around since you were not prepared for the boss. This results in having to play the run again to face the boss that you now understand better and can defeat.Nevertheless the downsides do not outweight the upsides, the game is still a treat and I can honestly recommend it with just a pinch of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is an early access title that already has a great deal of content available. In The Last Spell you are thrown into a rogue-lite survival RPG where you construct defenses and town upgrades by day and by night you employ a team of 3-6 heroes to fend off increasing numbers of undead pouring out from an oppressive magical fog. Death is assured, as eventually you will be overwhelmed, but with every game you unlock new starting bonuses, a greater ability to find new and powerful equipment, and even permanent character upgrades like an increased number of action points. With these upgrades you can push further and further and eventually enact The Last Spell.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, an excellent game with a lot of really strong points in its favour. The game being in Early Access feels more like a Developer-end decision in terms of "We have concrete plans for some extra features" rather than a "The core game is present, but the gameplay loop is not complete."As far as strategy games go, I find this one to tread the line between complex and accessible in a truly delightful manner. Certainly, there is some tremendous randomness, and so the experience in a run will vary, but I found the game did an excellent job with the progression from each run--I found my progress was equal parts unlocking new features/bonuses for my town/heroes and actual learning about the game, the mechanics, and the specific events/strategies you need to employ in a given level. It also merits mention that the vast majority of unlocks feel genuinely impactful and useful. Sure, a few Omens I'll probably never use, but that's less a comment on their use and power and more on my personal playstyle.The true highlight for me, though, is the various layers and elements the game gives you to work with, and the fun in experimenting with different aspects of them. In no particular order, the game has the heroes, which come with more or less random traits and perks, which are themselves fairly defining of how you can or want to build the character; it has items, with various base types and baseline innate effects, but also special bonus effects, the quantity and power of which scale with item rarity; the weapons, as a subset of the items, each have a unique skillset, and all, in my experience, have their own relatively individual playstyle (I hate the pistol though--that weapon type is the worst, fight me); there's a leveling system with primary and secondary stats, two rerolls per level, and different rarities for level benefits which I find to be excellent--unless you get greedy with rerolls, the vast majority of levels will be useful, and hitting that rare level bonus that's perfect for a build just feels great; there's an Omen system which is essentially passive modifiers for a run which, honestly, merits an individual discussion all on its own; and finally there's the whole town system with gold/supplies management, buffs, effects to prepare for and have advantages in combat, and a bunch of other things. There's just... A lot. And a ton to experiment with, and all sorts of fun to have with different character and omen setups as well as town priorities. Of course, if you're the kind of person to min-max-optimize everything to death and "play to win" instead of have fun--you know who you are--yeah, the replay value/core loop of the game might fall a little flat. Can't help you if you optimize the fun out of a game.The game isn't perfect, though, and so there are a few pain points. First, I can't quite figure out what causes a save state in the game. Sometimes I exit, come back, and get booted back to production phase. Other times, it'll remember where I am mid-turn in nightime combat. Rounds can go for a LONG time in this game--having the saving be more consistent--whether that's just after every action, or simply "anything past production phase is not saved," would be nice. Second, some extra clarity with tooltips/effects would be helpful. For example, it took me ages to figure out that Omen of the Engineer adds a second blue hitbox to ballistas, rather than being the same as the Seasoned Operators upgrade. Clearly a reading comprehension issue on my end, but the effects of each read pretty similarly. Third, pistol still sucks. At least as a starting weapon. Anecdotally, I've found it's the worst effects of all ranged weapons combined--the low range of a hand crossbow, the limited point-and-click targeting of a 2H crossbow, the lower damage scaling of a shortbow, and the low total use count of abilities on a longbow. All it's really missing is a negative stat bonus from the muskets and it's the perfect makes-me-want-to-reset-instantly weapon. I would just like to not die a little inside when I see a character start with a pistol, mostly. But as ever, this might be a personal problem. Finally, my only other real complaint is ballista target priority is a little... Off? I've had plenty of times where a single enemy has gotten into the town, and is going to attack a building and cause panic, and is in range of any number of ballistas, and they just... Don't even attempt to take it down. So it can be quite irritating to have to essentially give up a turn for a hero to deal with one single flying enemy that just yeeted past all defenses and was subsequently ignored for some reason. ...Oh, right, and traps, at least with the trap target omen (haven't tested without) can damage your own structures, which seems an awful lot like friendly fire which the trap states it does not do. So either a fix or clarification on that would be nice....But seriously, those complaints are all incredibly minor; the gameplay is excellent, and does an excellent job blending the highlights of multiple genres of game. It's been a delight both to steamroll and struggle in the game, and I look forward to future updates, as well as fiddling further with different setups in the current iteration. Oh, right, and the soundtrack is just excellent. So do give the game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with a great premise, overall would definitely recommend but as it is right now it has a few  problems which make it a bit frustrating at times. The first and most important is rotation of either buildings or skills; I've had a lot of trouble with the auto-aiming of skills which doesn't make any sense as it sometimes outright targets no-one even if a shot is possible at a few enemies and for buildings it makes absolutely no sense to not be able to rotate them, as it proves to be quite infuriating when you can't put a building in a place just because you can't rotate it. The second is no indicator when you're doing friendly fire; Although it's a pretty minor nitpick, I've had a many games where I just straight up shoot my teammate with an AOE spell just because I was rushing it, a simple "are you sure you wanna hurt your teammate?" pop-up would fix this issue. The same thing could be said with spells aimed at nothing which don't hit anything, every time I misclick while using a spell, it just fires it, which could have disastrous effects, as it's not an exaggeration to say that you have to make every spell count in the game. Balance wise it needs work, as the archer class is much better than the other two and the weapons themselves are unbalanced; For example the longbow is completely inferior to the shorter variation due to it's lack of AOE spells while the shorter one has one very strong spread-out AOE and one tightly spread but weaker.Although the game is great, it really needs to polish it's gameplay, which is why it's in beta so I still definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so difficult, but it's so fun! But it's so incredibly difficult... yet just so fun! But still... so very, very difficult. And yet..!The Last Spell is really something special. The gameplay is fantastic - a highly polished blend of base building, tower defense, and strategy RPG. Mechanics are unique, there's plenty of content, and the game has decent meta progression. I have way too many games I want to play, so it's rare that I come back to a game I already feel I've fully experienced. And here I am, almost 300 hours in and still going. That should speak volumes to the level of quality we're talking here. That being said, the game isn't for everyone. Each run is quite long for a roguelike, so you can lose a ton of progress if you die near the end of a run. And you WILL lose. A lot. Don't let that deter you though. As unforgiving as it can be at times, if you're up to the challenge, you're in for a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the 2nd map decided to drop a review since there were a good amount of negative comments about gameplay aspects on steam which were not quite true. Since other positive reviews, no doubt, talked about the game in a more general sense, this review is dedicated to people who might think this game is unfair, broken, imbalanced and etc.:* Melee weapons/builds are not viable - not only they are viable, but some of them are S-tier builds. Beat the 2nd map with 4 melee heroes. Both the damage and tankiness are very good from melee builds. Had 400 armor 60 block 20% resist gigachads who can facetank just about anything while fully surrounded (including Boomers and Bulkies).* Game is unfair / too hard - Partially true. Game is VERY hard and forces the player to min-max to some extent. This isn't a chill, laid back game, When you think you have enough, you don't. But to consider it unfair is a bit unjust. 2nd maps' boss waves seemed bafling, but anything is possible with an isolator sniper who can crit for 5,5k damage.* You get penalized for failing which can botch your whole run - the penalties for letting enemies run around in your Haven are minor in my opinion and it never impacted any attempt in any significant way for me. You can miss out on an item and around 30% of income if things are bad enough, but that doesn't kill your whole run.* Tanking is pointless - not true. Most enemies will flock to your heroes instead of walls (like a passive taunt), so you can body block a bit of the waves and slow them down.* Defence perks and skill up's are vastly inferior to offensive level ups - not true. From mentioned points above, I exclusively pick armor/block etc. for melee.* There are only a few viable weapons - Not really true. Through RNG the game has forced me to try out some other weapons and builds and they do work. Although, some weapons are "main-line" and can do just fine with the spam of basic attacks. Others require at least 6 action points to be viable enough, others are "support(CC)" weapons or "ability based". I thought poison builds are garbage, but I was wrong. Players who are saying weapons are bad, are probably using support weapons exclusively to deal main damage.* Game is too grindy - Kinda not true (yet). I beat the 1st map on my second run and beat the 2nd map on my fourth run (although here, the first two runs were with a higher difficulty, which I was not supposed to pick for the 2nd map from the start). Meta progression felt fast enough to unlock upgrades, some of which are required to beat maps. So far it feels you do a normal run as far as you can -> then go do a "essence grind" map with nothing but +%essence omens -> then back to progression attempts.HOWEVER, I'm not sure if I will still unlock lots of unique upgrades progressing through 3rd and 4th maps.Just to paint the picture - In the amount of hours played, I've done 1st map on apocalyspe +2 difficulty already and 2nd on normal. There were some reviewers who still struggled with 1st map, having played 60~ish hours. Not to be mean, but I have no idea how that is possible. * End of map can have unique mechanics, if you don't know them, you will lose - WIll have to agree with this one... Bosses do require knowledge about their behavior, if you don't know how to position for them, pretty high chance to lose. Not very fun to lose your run, because you had no idea how many phases the new boss will have, when they will pop-up etc.* Too much RNG can botch your run, even on the 1st wave - not true. I've dealt with waves using garbage starting weapons. There is enough RNG to stabilize your builds and game plan through 2-3 rounds. By that time you will usually have builds and item sets going.So far this game has been fun, albeit being very hard. As I am a metal fan, I really appreciate more devs making metal OST's for games, the soundtrack here is great, almost Djent on some tracks.In summary - it's a good roguelike tactics base defense game with heroes, level-ups and rpg elements. Will hope more content gets added ant 1.0 gets pushed out soon (as some reviews mentioned the BETA has been going on for quite a while)Note: Might adjust this review based on 3rd and 4th maps. Maybe the difficulty will truly get too insane.Feel free to agree or disagree on the points mentioned.UPDATE: Beat the 3rd map on the first try, without googling any mechanics or getting spoiled about the boss. Was one turn away from losing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is lots of fun, at least for the first 3 of 5 towns. Lots of variety, interesting game mechanics and tons of play value.Unfortunately, at least for me, the difficulty curve is far too steep once I reached the fourth of five towns. This wouldn't be a problem if there were still useful permanent upgrades to unlock, but at this point for me, I had unlocked everything that would help me make further progress. I might still be motivated to continue trying but since each attempt takes 8-10 hours and one bad bit of luck starts you in a death spiral, I think I am done with this game. In my last attempt one hero got killed in a single poison attack. From past experience the 200 gold it will cost me to add a similar hero will doom my attempt.I can't "git gud" enough in this game to complete it and I find it frustrating to not be able to complete games that I enjoy but am not good enough at. I noticed that only around 10% have completed the third town - I think developers should pay attention to stats like this and adjust the game appropriately. Instead, developers seem to listen to the vocal minority who don't want the difficulty lowered.There is an easy mode where you can use all the town bonuses you have unlocked. I'm sure this will make the game too easy, even for me. I do appreciate having difficulty levels but I shouldn't have to manually create my easy mode.I'll still recommend this game as it can be great fun but for me it is frustrating that I have no chance of completing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unforgiving, hard AF, and (like every RNG game like this) luck plays too much of a role in having a successful run. Last Spell is also in early access and horribly balanced at the moment. The game gets disproportionately harder the more unlocks you earn.But -Its very good and highly addictive if you like turn based strat/RPG games like these.The only problem I've had is there seems to be a memory leak that causes the game to lag the longer you play which goes away when you close and restart the game.You know those 'which games would you have if you were on a deserted island' lists that people used to make a long time ago? _childDocuments_.review: What if Final Fantasy Tactics was just a super difficult horde mode?This is not a casual game. Fans of X-Com and roguelites can do well here, but it is daunting. The new player experience is very rough as there is so much to take in (which is a credit), but a single run takes a loooong time (many hours) and you will not have anything unlocked because it's a  roguelite.My biggest takeaway up front is that it's incredibly difficult to get into. I play a lot of these types of games, and this is definitely the most unforgiving of the bunch with the biggest hump.. BUT! If you are willing to stick it out, I give two thumbs, definitely worth the price. I'm very impressed with the amount of meat they put on this bone, it goes deep, but is so terribly slow to get anywhere that I feel most players won't get to enjoy the meal.EDIT: The last map is awful. I still enjoyed the game, as the story premise is so cool, the grid-based tactics gameplay is great, etc, but I won't be playing any further now that I've beaten it. It's kind of a shame because there is so much to work with here, but the obscure map mechanics and roguelite unlocking progression gimping are just too much for a game where a single map takes 5+ hours to finish. As I mentioned earlier I think it demands far too much of a casual player (PROTIP: you can alt+F4 and restart the night once you get bodied by mechanic you didn't know existed).If they expanded the game to have different maps and mission types, and frankly just ditched the roguelite elements altogether, I think they could have had a beloved single-player game in the same vein of X-Com. There's so much potential here with the story premise and broad weapon sets (although I abandoned melee weapons entirely by the end of it).A small aside, the onscreen quips from the characters reek of western localization and don't match the overall aesthetic at all. Not a big deal, but did really detract from the atmosphere and take me out of the setting instantly (much like Cobalt Core does).

_childDocuments_.review: I've been pretty blown-away - this game is a desperation simulator in all the right ways.A unique blend of turn-based tactics, horde defense and rogue-like, the Last Spell is is a gem in a sea of forgettable entries. Trying to get the most out of your heroes and level them up, plan builds and manage the sheer chaos is an addicting loop. Sound design, soundtrack and smart use of pixel art all shows a level of TLC that helps make it more captivating. Bonus that all your equipment choices show on your character, too!Only complaint I have is the metaprogression comes on a bit too strong. At the time of this writing, your first game is a wash in terms of rewards, and some of the unlocks are huge power spikes (like +AP). But even this is an annoyance more than a real issue that prevents the game from being great.If you love turn-based games, get The Last Spell. It's worth your time.EDIT: after a lot of updates, and hours, the above problems have been solved over the many updates and patches. While still "early access," this feels like a game in 1.0 to me. One of my favorite aspects is how the game is really hard to "solve" perfectly. The decisions stay interesting long into the loop, and you have to make due with a lot of imperfect builds and scenarios to succeed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game. It has a learning curve but also an on-ramp for difficulty - you get upgrades that persist between runs, and the game's story is taught through your deaths and through your victories. Reaching the end of each map feels like a triumph. You're going to lose the first time you get to the last night of each map - that much is inevitable - unless you've googled the fight beforehand. But it's much more fun to go in blind and learn the mechanics. The last night of each map turns the game on its head - you don't care about anything in the city, you don't care about your heroes. All you care about is killing the boss so you can clear The Mist and move one step closer to enacting The Last Spell. The first 3 maps give a gradual on-ramp for difficulty, the fourth map is a bit of a difficulty spike, and "bends" the previously established rules of the game, but in a fashion that's intuitive to learn. And without spoiling it - the 5th map is a grueling but very rewarding end to your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: A gradual slope from helpless to hopeful where you have to change your strategy to bend around what the game gives you. The core gameplay is engaging enough for me and the price is absolutely right for what's on display here, it's a good beta.Long Version: The game has one core loop so far and if you don't like it, you probably won't like what the game has to offer, I'll say that straight out. You're going to be guarding the same town with the same starting layout over and over- but that's about the only static part of Last Spell. Your starting trio (or foursome, if you go Easy Mode and take that option) are going to be one of each 'class' consisting of Physical (melee), Ranged (self-explanatory), and Magic (variable range) each with a slightly less-random main job that alters stats, then two completely random traits that further mutate the character. From there you set up your heroes- and from the second night onward, build up your doomed hamlet with buildings and defenses as well from directed waves of undead. It's a nice, simple premise with a good amount of variation and its rogue-lite elements allow you to slowly trickle the means to succeed via a clever two-tier progression system. On one hand, you have a constant flow of Dark Sou- Essence- to pay out for a variety of progressions, and on the other you have a more concrete long-term goal that you can try and dedicate a run to, like having a single hero with 50% bonus damage of a certain type, or reaching a certain amount of mana spent. At the time of writing I've unlocked 56% of the left path and 86% of the right, so I feel like I have some grasp on the scope of what's on offer here.It should be noted that I've spent just north of 20 hours so far on this beta and have not run into any bugs or save corruption thankfully, and the game runs smoothly. Looking forward to what's yet to be added on. Currently I'm 'stuck' on Night 9- that being, I can get there pretty confidently and even finish it but there wasn't much left, and that was with 6 heroes on Normal. Even so, there's more to unlock and small buffers left to add, so I get the idea that the game is meant to be completed when near-everything is open to the play to get around, at least in the beta. The game is definitely worth a play and it fits a nice niche of strategic... tower defense-rpg? It's the closest genre I can think of really, to what it is. Last up, my suggestions for the developers:I think it would be better for the counting of Essence at the end of the rounds could be faster, or skipped entirely with a click, it got a little annoying once it gets past 3k+ in a night. It might be nice for some of the 'classes' for characters to have a bias for specific loadout checking what's unlocked, i.e. druids having a druid staff- I've not seen anyone start with one, etc. The game isn't done but doing missions or hero-expeditions to reduce enemy waves outside the town during production might help to mix up the gameplay loop, I assume that there will be different 'town' layouts when enough data is gathered otherwise. The only thing the beta really lacks is variation, which I'm sure is coming eventually- so keep at it, you're doing good work.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that I didn't know that I needed in my life.This is simultaneously an incredible tactics game and a great base defense game, while also being a fun roguelike. I love that characters aren't class locked, allowing me to customize my characters and try new strategies every run. I also appreciate that I feel like I have a sense of meta-progression even in the middle of runs and pretty regularly. It makes even failed runs feel worthwhile, and oh boy there will be failed runs. I'm 23 hours in and still haven't won one, but it doesn't feel as frustrating as failed runs in some other roguelikes since every run yields real progression and helps me formulate a better strategy for the next one. Playing out your "Last stands" intense, and surviving one is such a great feeling.That said, it's not perfect. I've seen some people call it "grindy", and I do get where they're coming from. While the meta progression is enough to satiate me from run to run, it is true that you're defending the same map from the same hordes every time. There is enemy variation, but most often you won't see much of it nor will it matter much for the first few nights. Considering how often you will lose, I can understand some people finding it repetitive, even if I personally didn't.Runs are also brutally long, which is alleviated by the meta-progression mid runs IMO, but sometimes you know a run is going to fall apart and since you don't get much in rewards for failed nights, there's not much motivation to stay in a failing run unless you enjoy playing out the last stands (Which I do).The music is also really good, but I do wish there were more songs for the various nights as the main one does get repetitive when you hear it in every battle, which is a very large portion of the game.All in all, if you like tactics games and/or challenging roguelikes, you owe it to yourself to check out this gem. While there are flaws, the core game play loop is so good that I find myself not noticing them until after I've put the game down, read them online and go "Huh, yeah I guess that's a fair point".
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Started out fairly interesting but became a brutal slog by the end. Beat the game by the way before anyone asks.-Defenses are really bad and 99% of the work is done by your heroes which you have to use some very powerful particular builds to stand a chance. On that note catapults are almost completely worthless for their massive cost.-Worker management is not exactly balanced well and the exorbitant cost of some actions makes things even worse for the player trying to get things done after surviving another few hundred enemies to slaughter their way though.-Bosses are heavily RNG based and can screw you over on a whim based on where they decide to appear or teleport to. Not good mechanically, and doesn't feel good to fight against either.-Halfway through the game your upgrades just kind of, stop. You run out of things to unlock except for one or two things every now and then. Making the game much more boring because you're just grinding through wave after wave of enemies for basically nothing but to get the game over with.The game had quite a lot of potential, but the execution is very lacking and turned out to be tedious to beat. By the end I just wanted to get this game over with. Would not recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: In case it wasn't clear from the tags, this game is: tower defense + roguelike + team/turn-based tactics.Each mission (map) plays in repeating phases (day/night): build up your base, then defend it from the baddies.And it all works together really really well:* the pre-mission modifier selection influences how the mission plays out* the base-building gives meaningful choices which shape your approach* the tactical gameplay is top-notch, with a heavy emphasis on understanding the strengths of your heroes and weaknesses of the monsters* mechanics & stats are pretty intuitive* there is enough RNG to keep the game interesting even when repeating the same map* yet there are enough ways to react to or mitigate RNG that I never felt like a loss was anything but my fault* everything you do rewards some kind of meta-progression, so there's always something new to try* just amazing variety and customization between weapons, perks, gear, etc.I do have one small complaint: it's easy to lose sight of heroes and monsters when they're behind buildings/objects/etc. A highlight would go a long way here.I also want to note that individuals runs can take a while, which means failing a run feels pretty bad since it's such a large time investment. I would have preferred a larger number of shorter maps. On the other hand, winning does feel absolutely amazing.I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of turn-based tactical games, here's the skinnyPros & Features- Excellent art and very responsive juicy sound effects- Each battle is wave defense, so you defend with both units and siege weapons (catapults, ballistae, etc) to ensure the survival of a town that you build up with houses, production buildings, and so forth.- Units are randomized (but customizable after) with different traits they can learn, so it's vaguely roguelite- If you like musical artists like Perturbator, Carpenter Brut, or other synthwave you will love the soundtrack, guaranteed. It absolutely rocks.- Wide variety of weapon types that are generally interesting and balanced- Tension is also very well balanced. When trying out a new map, you should expect to lose and learn from the process. - Controls are very snappy and intuitive in a genre that often has problems in this area.Cons & Criticism- Bosses are probably the least intuitive part of the game, particularly ones that have to be defeated multiple times or are invincible for an unclear amount of time. Most of my time spent with this game was in Early Access, so I hope the tutorials they added for 1.0 make up for this.- The gulf between Boundless Mode and "normal" mode in my opinion is a bit too wide. Boundless Mode is too easy for me, yet the default difficulty with the standard amount of Omens is a tad too unfair. I wish there were some sort of middle ground. - Grinding unlocks might be fun for some people but I consider it a negative. Some of the point requirements for the dark-side unlocks are a bit too high/draconic/punitive for my taste. Overall, this game is a blast if you like turn-based games, tactical games, wave defense / tower defense, with a mild flavor of roguelite thrown in as a spice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic TBS!  Every weapon feels unique and fun to play. The game is very balanced and each run feels a little different from the previous to shake things up. The big key is learning how the weapons work and exploiting the bonuses you get. Longbows and daggers like isolated units, swords like momentum, druid staffs and hammers like debuffed enemies etc. It's all about learning how one weapon pairs with another and being able to adapt that as your heroes grow. It's not a game where you employ the same tactic over and over, seeking the same skills and weapons each run, but taking a good look at your heroes skills and adapting as they level up. To me it's very rare that a strategy game can do this, as I know there are other games were you find something that works for you and always stick to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: this games another one on the long list of making me wish their was a neutral option for steams reviewsthe games got a really unique setting and its mechanics are extremely solid combine that with a banger of a sound track and you got a decent timethe biggest con this games got for it is the progression system really holding it back, this isn't like other rougelites where if you had the skills you could beat the game without the progression system which the system itself is fairly bare bones in concept, the verity could use a bit of work as well, I've already grown tired of runs with the little amount of time I have in itand while not a major gripe the story really doesn't seem to have any reason to have the rougelite elements it have, given as of writing this review I have not completed the story elements so maybe near the end their might be some reveal to the why
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging yet enthralling turn-based combat will keep you on the edge of your seat with The Last Spell. There's a large variety of skills you can make use of in this game, all of which is dictated by your gear. Want to fight in close range? Throw a hammer, sword, or spear into one of your weapon slots and have at it! Want to attack from afar? Equip a magic or ranged weapon in your other slot, giving you the option of both! This game is all about making choices and playing as tactically as you can. Will you make the wrong decision and accidentally obliterate one of your units with friendly fire during a boss wave like I did? Sure hope not, but you'll have to play to find out!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Its a progressive turn based game that makes you feel an incredible sense of dispair as everything is going fine, and then BOOM, lancer you missed hits your tank like a truck out of nowhere, and you suddenly realize 'Yeah... i'm going to fail this run'. Its the same sort of thrill as dark souls. Expect to lose a lot. Expect to lose heros. Overall, I would say the game is a strong 8.5 out of 10. It currently has some issues (Such as graphical stuff, keybinds, camera, and some other stuff) but its in beta so some things are expected.On the otherhand, the music is really damn good, as is the ambience. Graphics are meh, but its a pixilated style, so that doesnt matter really. The progression system is pretty solid. Things you use more get stronger, and things you dont get left behind, but are still usable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Each run is extremely addictive and fun, so much is in place for a great finished game.Unfortunately, this needs serious balancing and updates to improve of game pace.  It starts out impossible (first run) and soon you realize how monumental the unlocks are between games.  Once you get some of the major unlocks and realize how overpowered certain weapons are the challenge almost completely dissolves.  There's only a small window of time between unlocks where you don't feel all powerful, but don't feel overwhelmed and unfortunately it comes pretty early.Having said that, the art and animations are great, the characters are varied, the mid game economy is fun.  If the devs stick to their road map, they could see this as one of the best Indie Turn-Based Tactics games of this or next year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a challenging tactics game, get this game.Every run is a little bit different because you get randomly rolled heroes each time. They have different stats, and on level up, you get a few select stats and perks. Even if you don't win, you still get essence that you can trade in that will give you benefits to nudge you towards a victory, so it's never a total loss.The pixel art is gorgeous.So far I've made it through the first two maps. It is a very punishing game, but very rewarding once you get some wins. It's mostly about figuring out what is the most efficient use of resources to kill the most enemies at once. If you are not efficient, you will not win. Period. Beyond all that, one of the biggest bonuses in my opinion, is that there are no microtransactions, at least as of this writing. I don't believe there are any plans for mtx in the future either. In this day and age, this is becoming increasingly rare. Please support indie developers who aren't monetizing the **** out of their games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: A interesting horde rogue  with some rough issues posting this before the latest boss update so this may be outdated pretty quick.  Struggling tooth and nail is what makes up much of this game you may struggle through multiple waves with starting gear in a mere effort to speed up your mines, sure up your weaker party members so they survive, and most importantly put a wall in front of the enemy.   I will say this I played with the optional easy mode settings for my 40 some hours, and feel that is a more proper start for most people unless they crave a grater challenge. Of course you are expected to fail and improve over time so chances are you will need to replay the current few maps until either your luck carries you through, or say an upgrade pushes your party over the current curve of pain. Some of the foes I felt were a bit too tanky even on easy but then I also didn't min max with a guide on hand but even some of your strongest can die to the elite type enemies offer. The enemy spell casters are very much a threat of that given they can become invulnerable and blast through the walls to slay an unlucky hero as one of mine found out at the face of their charged spell.  The current lone boss is certainly interesting but I'll hold off on what I think of them till later given they are still on the way. But in the end even at this stage I had a fairly fun 40 hours once the ball started rolling without hitting any large hitches with easy mode smoothing things out just enough to make things enjoyable while you grind out your upgrades. Granted eventually some things become locked behind the harder modes but i advise you enjoy easy mode to get used to the game first. Then slowly strip away that net once things become too easy and sink deeper into the despair the setting wishes to invoke.

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: No replayability, and no REAL tactics. You're just faced with an overwhelming horde of enemies who slowly become impossible to drive back until you lose, then start over again with a tiny bit more power now that you did some progression. Unfortunately, the huge masses of enemies and the fact that you are expected to fill the map up with barriers that also block your own heroes means there are no real tactics. The first boss is just "kill all the boss spawns before the endless horde overwhelms you" and I thought that was very boring. There are some great ideas here and a solid gameplay loop with no idea how to make that loop engaging and rewarding

_childDocuments_.review: easy 5/5, very worth the pricegreat artstyle/intense musicThe usual turn based combat with AP and movepoints but instead of i.e. 5v5 its more like 5v200 which is great fun. wave survival with a boss at the end and inbetween waves you heal/restore mana a tiny bit and you can choose what to build i.e. gold mines to get more gold overtime or new gear, more workers(for more building abilities like blessing heroes with more mana) buy consumables pots/scrolls(that refill between waves) or spend it on walls and defensive ballistas etc.what building to get every turn and which workers to employ where is not very obvious cause everything helps alot and so this is fun to try to optimizethe amount of depth in hero customization items/perks/abilities is very deep without being overwhelming as you start with only the basic items and keep unlocking new stuff overtime.Every turn in combat is very tactical, which skills to use on which enemies for max efficiency to keep them at bay, if you get into trouble you can start spending mana on epic aoe abilities. however hp and mana only regen so much between days so you want to limit mana usage until you purchased more mana regen or until you hit the boss stage where you can fully empty the tank feeling super powerful which is alot of fun. There are alot of abilities which are defined by the weapon you wear and you can do 2 sets on each hero so you can i.e. be a tank with a long range magic attack to kill stragglers. hero too weak? give it a support staff with a switch to a multihit weapon to finish of those low hp enemies. Later on waves come from multiple sides, so where do you put your best character where your worsed? I made i.e. a mobility/long range hero focussed purely on being able to have aton of movepoints and range so it can just run around with the most OP items in her bag, so if one side is in trouble she can help alot everywhere.The creativity and depth possible already in the first stage due to the impactful handpicked perks and abilities system is really fun.There is alot of rng which helps with replayability but unlike many other games it is actually balanced such that having bad rng does not set you far behind and strategy and unlockables are alot more impactful than luck.Ive only just completed stage 1 but im sure itll get alot more complex later on, as you can unlock even more heroes, even more buildings and a ton of different buffs and items.Amazing strategy game, with tons of replayability and unlockables! 5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic tactical rogue-like with a fun and refreshing tower-defence concept blended in. Runs can be quite long, around 3-7 hours and meta progression is definitely grindy, but I have found even when I fail a run I am happy with what I learned and what I have unlocked. Difficulty can also be modified to your liking.I had put in ~110 hours during early access pre-progression wipe, and have been thoroughly enjoying working my way back up to where I was before and further. The devs are fairly responsive as well, and have put a lot of TLC into fixing bugs as they appeared through the patches.Heavily recommend picking this game up for those who are fans of rogue-likes and turn based tactical games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has incredible potential. But it's not there yet. It's fun, until it's not. _childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really unique. Amazing soundtrack, art. There are lots of items and stat variation. Most classes play differently which helps to keep it fresh. It's an interesting mesh of tactical RPG with a dash of tower defense. The story, for how spartan it is, is well animated and intriguing.The game has a built in soft progress limiter. You'll probably not be able to beat the game without doing many runs and collecting enough tainted essence to upgrade everything. Even then, there's an element of luck as to what classes you start with, their weapons, etc. Each town takes 6-8 hours to complete, and failing the last night, 8 hours in, is par for the course. That's probably my biggest complaint. It's a "rogue like" except each session takes so much time, and there's a massive difficulty spike on the last night. I got 40 hours out of it and feel that's pretty good for the money. At town 3 it's a little grindy and repetitive, but I might come back to the game later on.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a new Turn Based Tactics Roguelike game, that is all about defending your base for 10 days until your wizards can cast "The Last Spell" to vanquish the evil in the land and bring you to the long coveted victory screen - And I mean "long coveted" literally, as after just over 20 hours with this game I'm finally on my 7th run through of the game that I finally have enough strength to hold back the monstrous armies of the night. TLS's gameplay is all about try, try, trying again, as you kill hordes of monsters to complete feats that will eventually strengthen your heroes and give them new tools to fight with, similarly to Binding of Isaac meets Zombicide. By design, you likely won't last long on your first 3 runs but with every run you complete you will actively feel your heroes getting stronger and such a sense of progression feels very rewarding.For being an Early Access game, there is also a nice variety of items, heroes and monsters, though the higher rarity items seem to only provide stat upgrades rather than unique abilities attached to them (though it's possible that these type of effects are in the item sets that I haven't unlocked yet so please take this small criticism with a grain of salt, it's just a trend I noticed trhoughout my current game time). Another small criticism of the game that I have is that each weapon will always have the same abilities. For a roguelike game, I was hoping that weapons would have some RNG to the actual skills you got to work with, as a way to encourage shopping for an item with just the right stats and abilities when you max out the uses for your gold. Perhaps this could be added in a future update or as a toggle-able setting, and of course I understand why they went with their current design decision so that you know what to expect from each weapon, so this is another critique that comes from a place of personal preference. I think the worst criticism I can give this game is that you can't rename your heroes. What a shame.Over time I hope that the developers decide to take the route of making this a Tactics-Tower Defense version of Binding of Isaac that is filled with secret 1% bosses and items that will require tens to potentially hundreds of playthroughs to unlock everything, but even as an Early Access game I highly recommend checking this title out. Here's to hoping that the developers stick through the development of this game, unlike the developers of They Are Billions who made their money and ran out after a few measly updates.
