_childDocuments_.review: While I could just say that I like this game, that goes without saying with how many hours I've put in so far.However, I figured I'd like to use my review to give any new players reading it some advice, mainly around avoiding friendly fire, as it is actually easier to have happen then most people would think, and can easily sink a run with the loss of one or more heroes due to a mistake in judgement. While The Last Spell does a very good job at warning the player about obvious situations when an aoe power you are using will also hit one of your other heroes, there are a few cases where this warning does not exist. Below are the examples of this that I have personally had happen to me.First up is any ability with the "propagation" property; simply put, these are chain attacks, that move from the initial enemy that you target to any random enemy that is directly next to them, and then repeats this for however many jumps that are indicated in the ability text. The danger with these powers, is that they can just as easily jump to one of your other heroes (excluding the caster) if they happen to also be directly adjacent to a mob that is along this chain, causing them to take a hit from the attack as well. This can take an even worse turn if the other hero has a block build with the "spiky counter" perk, as that will activate if the chain hits them, and the caster of the power will in turn get smited, possibly leaving you with two dead heroes in one single bad RNG roll.Next are three specific perks that also give no warning about possibly damaging your other heroes with your own attacks; "Epidemic", "Contamination", and possibly most dangerous of all, "BOOM!".Epidemic (tier 4 of poison perk tree) and Contamination (tier 2 of debuff tree) both fall in the same bucket, as both perks afflict targets with a "contagion" debuff. This specific debuff causes whatever negative ailments that enemies who have it to spread to two random adjacent targets upon the afflicted creature's death. Very good for spreading high stacks of poison, stun, or whatever else you have debuffed the enemy with when the mobs are blobbed together. However, contagion can just as easily decide to unfortunately be spread to another hero if the mob with that debuff dies next to them, possibly poisoning your own hero to death by accident.Last but not certainly not least, is "BOOM!". This tier 5 perk of the melee tree can turn any close range hero who has it into an unholy aoe machine when combined with stacking damage boosts. The text for it reads "Whenever an enemy is killed within a range of 3: the overkill damage is transferred to all adjacent units (except this Hero).", with the key words here being "all adjacent units". In short, if the hero with this perk kills an enemy that is within 3 squares of where the attacking hero is currently standing, the damage they deal gets the remaining amount of HP the killed mob had subtracted from it, and then the resulting number is how much damage is dealt to all non-structures/terrain features that are standing right next to the killed mob. As you can probably guess, just like with the other cases above, this does not discriminate between friend or foe, and will hit any other hero who is standing next to the mob(s) who were the initial targets of the BOOM! enhanced attack. Which can, you guessed it, lead to a very dead hero if the overkill damage is high enough.Hopefully, these notes about the above abilities/perks will help other players to prevent their heroes from meeting very tragic accidental ends like the few unlucky ones of mine did. And with that, I wish you all the best of luck with smashing the faces of the undead hordes! >:P

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game. It combines Diablo like character building, base building, tower defense, and turn based strategy combat for a unique feeling game. Gets much easier with experience and meta progress, but it fun right out of the gate. If you like guides, Aldenpotamus on Youtube is the guy to look for for the Last Spell.

_childDocuments_.review: This easily became one of my new favorite games. While I don't think the game play loop will be for everyone, those that do enjoy it will find a rewarding, engaging, and satisfying game.As others have said, The Last Spell is a combination of tower defense, meets Final Fantasy Tactics/Vandal Hearts/Rogue Legacy, meets a legacy style board game. You're put into a dire situation to protect your town from a seeming endless hoard of zombie creatures with a handful of heroes that are randomly generated each attempt. The operative being "each attempt" as you are unlikely to succeed on your first tries as the difficulty ramps up with every night. You'll need to unlock different permanent boosts through the meta progression before you'll have a chance at the later days.I really enjoyed the meta progression as you have some freedom in choosing what you want to unlock which can compliment your play style. It also encourages you to experiment as not all unlocks are on the table. I liked that I always felt a little stressed as there are so many options to unlock but only a limited amount of time and resources to choose. Ultimately I had to plan for future attempts and what would help me survive another day.I thought game play felt a lot like a single player board game of sorts. There is a TON of resource management and more often than not you're going to always feel the squeeze of being short handed. You'll have to optimize where to spend your gold and materials in order to minimize damage to your town and heroes. When combat starts you'll need to decide how to focus fire down the hordes to protect your town. There are quite a few enemy types with various strengths and weaknesses so knowing how to deal with each unit becomes increasingly important. Thankfully, everything about combat moves quite quickly so you don't have to wait through lengthy animations and the enemy horde moves as a giant unit keep things moving.I also really enjoyed the escalating difficulty on the initial loop and additional cycles. You'll have a rough idea what to expect from playing the game (what night multiple hordes attack, when you'll want to build certain structures). Additional cycles unlock new types of challenges that will force you to modify your tactics and stress your resources further. Apocalypse difficulties really gave me reason to keep playing the game and I loved them.I loved it and am looking forward to more. Even in its current state I think this was a worthy $20 purchase. After finishing apocalypse 4 I'm ready to give the game a rest, but I'll definitely be watching for the next big patch.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell has a wonderful combat system. It engages and challenges your mind. But that's not my favorite part. If you like stat customization and planning builds, you will have a blast. Every run you'll have one or two characters that come together so perfectly that they'll carry the team.I haven't completed the story, but so far it's fun to unpack. I always prefer game play over story, but it's a nice bonus.

_childDocuments_.review: At the beginning of the game there doesnt appear to be much content, maybe 4 weapon types and you get overwhelmed pretty easily, but as you kill and unlock new stuff the game starts to give you a lot more options to choose from. Battling through a massive horde with only a few heroes has a good balance of feeling powerful yet in a position where overpushing will leave you scrambling to save a hero.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Strategy, strategy, strategy.  This game is a min/max'ers delight.  You control the economy, the equipment, the perks, the gear; every little detail is under your control and has a modest to profound effect on your performance.  In addition, it's single player, so you can create absurd builds which just annihilate the enemy and it's not particularly balanced out.If you hate minutiae, this game is definitely not for you.  But if you want to straight up murder hundreds of undead monsters with your finely tuned, perfectly equipped heroes, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: There have been few tactics RPG games that even come close to as good as The Last Spell. Having played nearly every major one released for the last 20 years I'm really impressed by how much they were able to fit into this game.The game has tons of fun and interesting build options, massive replay value, and a huge amount of enemy and strategy variety. There are potentially hundreds of hours of gameplay. The game is difficult with lots of different levels of difficulty. The game doesn't hold your hand. You will need to figure out the mechanics and systems as you go and when you do you will be rewarded. In all likelihood you will die a lot.It does not have much in the way of story, so if you only play RPGs for the story you will not like this one. The narrative is good, the world they've built is interesting, but you will not be stuck in hours of dialogue or cutscenes. If you want a crunchy system that blends RPG, hero wave defense, tower defense, base management and rogue-lite mechanics into a great system with a lot of depth that will take a long time to master this game is what you've been looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say this game is souls-like in the sense that it's brutally difficult but gives a good sense of accomplishment when you beat a run.I beat Gildenberg in 2 nights (on normal). I'm in the middle of my seventh run on Lakeberg and well...I fought the boss once. I think I'll beat it at the end of this run.The game has 3 phases, though one is just a formality (it gives you a chance to position your heroes, though you can do that during production). On your first night you will immediately start the position phase and then fight before getting to production.There is a lot of strategy to the production phase. You can build a variety of buildings, upgrade buildings, buy items at the shop (all using gold), build defenses (using materials), and use your workers for a variety of tasks. The problem is that you have a very limited number of resources. Do you build a few walls or build a ballistae instead? Or do you just do some traps and a catapult? Do you prioritize gold mines/scavenger camps (increase gold/material production) or do you focus on building your item generation buildings? Or do you get a nice weapon for one of your heroes? There are a lot of choices and you will get punished in a bad way if you choose poorly (Gildenberg is so easy it doesn't really count, the game starts at Lakeberg).As far as the battle phase, well that's pretty self-explanatory. Kill the monsters, and don't let them inside the city to break the seal. There is a panic mechanic, and if you let monsters stay in the city overnight you lose points, reducing your gold/material reward for the night and hurting you for later nights.I've understood the general idea is to get gold mines/scavenger camps built and upgraded as soon as possible, but there is a great danger to that, as it reduces your capacity to focus on defenses/getting other weapons, etc. It's hard to thread the needle with this game.As far as heroes go there are no classes per-se but as you upgrade you will pick from a skill tree that will enhance certain weapon types, which I'll get to in a second. You get to pick a primary attribute (damage/armor/health/mana, etc.) and a secondary attribute (momentum bonus, poison damage, magic damage, etc.) per level up, plus a perk. When you start you will have I believe 5 branches of perks to pick from; magic/physical/range/2 general. You can unlock 4 more perk branches (stun/contagion/isolationist/poison) later on, but only 2 get selected. You can select any sort of perk from any branch and mix and match how you like. I really enjoy the poison branch, though a few of the other perks I also like.Weapons come in 3 basic flavors; melee (hammer, sledgehammer, sword, dagger, etc.), range (shortbow, longbow, rifle, pistol, crossbow, etc.), and magic (death orb, magic wand, tome of secrets, scepter, etc.). Each has it's own skill set. You can have 2 sets per character, so you can switch sets at any time (the longbow can't attack within 3 tiles so you could have pistol as a backup to do CQB).Each weapon has 4 attacks. Typically there are 2 non-mana attacks (your basic and a specialty) and 2 that require mana. Needless to say, you only have so much mana and you only recover so much a night, so you have to think about when is best to use it up. You are also limited by action points (5 to start, though you can get more by leveling up if you get lucky).As far as perma-upgrades, there are 2 types; achievement based from the light angel and tainted essence (perma-money) based from the dark angel. They help to some degree, but a lot of them feel incremental, and I mean heavy on the incremental. For example, your basic weapon is not good, and after 200 action points (AP) spent with it, you unlock 2 better variations. After 1k AP you unlock better variations. The 1k will probably take you at least 4 runs depending on which weapons you get. Getting better chances at a rare level up (you get common/uncommon/rare as choices for level up options) cost me 9.9k tainted essence, and 2k~ is average for a night (with +30% from an omen I'm using). So that's 1 run to get that one upgrade, though they're not all that expensive.Before beginning a run you get to select omens to aid you--these will give you buffs, but you can only pick so many (3 for gildenberg, 5 for Lakeberg, I don't know how many for the last 2 cities). Some cost more than 1 spot. Some of the options are: increase tainted essence by 10% (1 slot) or 30% (3 slots), increase armor/damage/accuracy, etc., increase available houses, start with another hero, etc.If the difficulty is too much you can also do boundless mode, which allows you unlimited omens. I haven't done this yet because I feel like it's cheating, but I'm a stubborn man.Lastly, this game might feel grindy to you. Seems like a lot to get just a few upgrades. Then again, I'm sure if you used boundless for a few runs to get a ton of tainted essence the game would be far less grindy.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good!  I've made over half a dozen runs and have gotten a feel for how the game handles and feels.  In a nutshell The Last Spell hits some of my favorite gaming notes.  * Final Fantasy Tactics* Tower/Wave Defense* Base Building* RPG* Roguelike * ZombiesA better way to say it is it does all of these but not as complex.  It won't have the depth and breadth of FFT's class system, the RPG mechanics are relatively rudimentary, the base building simple.  However it does all of them well, and more importantly they all work together to feel like a complete package rather than bolted together.  -Graphics/SoundThe graphics are reminiscent of FFT, they manage to look detailed without being too busy or too cartoonish which in my opinion is too common in the 8/16 bit style games, particularly in turn based tactics.  It pulls off a dirty, gritty feel with everything looking run-down and ruined, the heroes have enough detail for them to feel like different characters, and the monsters have a nice variety.  The sound effects are perfectly serviceable, but the soundtrack rocks.  Very much gets you into the mood of fighting off swarms of the reanimated dead, I would recommend paying the extra bit to get the soundtrack.-MechanicsI really enjoy the day/night staging.  After each night you stave off the dead, you get a chance to level heroes, buy/sell equipment, erect support buildings, stand up defenses.  Of course there's never enough resources so you have to juggle and decide whether you want buildings to give your heroes health/mana, more resources, extra heroes, or give advantages for when night falls.  I am glad they didn't have gold just do everything, it is a related but separate mechanic, buildings and upgrades cost cash, defenses cost materials which are accumulated separately.  The hero upgrade system is fairly streamlined but flexible, you get a couple different ways to improve your heroes although one is fairly random.  It's enough to give them enough variety through different runs to keep everything from being samey.  Like other rogues you get some abilities that carry over from run to run, I won't delve into particulars but it's nice that you have one 'tree' you pay for with resources and another from essentially accomplishments.  So far I am really digging The Last Spell.  It's a roguelike so it's the Fail To Win model, you die a lot, you screw up a lot, but every run you understand more and get better abilities/equipment.  I like Dark Souls's difficulty and would say in spite of the Dev's warning, this game isn't hard.  A couple runs and you start figuring stuff out and getting further, at no point have I felt like things were unfair or I was "cheated", it's always something I did that was dumb.  Yes you lose all the time but that's the expected experience, you die to grow.  They're not breaking ground on anything here or making revolutionary changes but they do a lot of things very well with no glaring annoyances.  There's a lot of content for an early access game, and so far I have yet to run into a single glitch or bug, no crashing, no freezing.  I usually don't do reviews let alone gush through them, but The Last Spell is a gem and it really has entertained me in a way games haven't for some time.  Really looking forward to new content and expansions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Until this becomes a game where you can potentially win on the 1st run due to skill and a little bit of luck, it'll remain a thumbs down. I highly doubt this'll change as the developers themselves stated in one of their patch notes that they realize this issue, but can't redo it as it's already a deep core of the game and will instead attempt to make balances and changes to this. Regardless, I'll update my review depending on what changes they bring.I'm annoyed that there have been plenty of games where I would beat the 1st day and then abandon it once I've acquired the essence because the heroes I started with were garbage for end game meaning I'll probably end up losing by day 7 or 8 with little to no chance of getting further than that. The few times that I've gotten to the end resulted in me completely destroying the bosses with ease cause I got  with good weapons and heroes, but a majority of the time, it's a loss due to the fact that I wasn't lucky enough to roll some weapon types that are just far superior than other weapon types or good heroes.For example, a short bow combined with long bow are generally incredibly powerful for clearing waves and picking off single targets while the guns and crossbows are inferior for ap used per enemy killed. A single good dual wielding short and long bow hero can easily defend an entire side by themselves. Wield a crossbow, rifle, or pistol and they'll start to struggle.The game's potential is bogged down by this repetitive grind to lose due to circumstances out of our control  just to acquire essences to upgrade stuff to allow progression instead of rewarding players for playing skillfully.If you enjoy grinding and losing due to bad luck then this game is for you. Personally, I don't mind grinding to get stronger, but the difficulty progression needs to properly reward the players accordingly. Also, please try to buff the other weapon types to make them equally viable. As for now, I can't find the motivation or interest to crank the game back on until further updates/changes are made.*EDIT/UPDATE*After over a year, I can finally change my negative view to a positive view. I appreciate and like the new system and updates. It is no longer a game where you have to grind/die repeatedly just to progress slightly.  Looking forward to more content in the future. Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good. There's not much in the way of a story, but the gameplay carries it. It's repetitive in terms of gameplay loop and your goals each run, but offers a ton a variety in how you go about it and the different ways you can achieve your goals. Do you focus a run on using traps? A variety or traps or focus on a specific type? Maybe try and make your characters into superheroes instead? What kind of weapons and builds do you use (there's a bunch)? Perhaps you just want to combine a little bit of this and a little bit of that... Or even just go at it without any planning at all. Everything is doable. Sure, some strategies are a little better than others but it's all very well balanced and I've managed to win runs with just about anything I could come up with. I don't even attempt to 100% very many games, but The Last Spell kept me interested and excited to keep trying new things until there wasn't much left to experiment on, almost 400 hours in. The only criticism I can come up with, is that each run can take quite a bit of time, sometimes 12-15+ hours, which I'd consider unusual for this style of game. BUT, you can save your game at ANY time and return where you left off so it's not really a big issue.Oh, and the music kicks ass!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Spell is a game I enjoyed, but is also difficult to recommend. The sound and sprites are phenomenal, and the game is (unless you use the optional Boundless mode) very challenging. Each map takes around 3 hours to complete however, and losing your run because you had no idea what the boss was going to be and didn't build the right tools feels awful. For example: Map 4 is literally unbeatable unless you build at least one movement-focused hero, but for it to be comfortable you'll need more. Movement is not something you have really needed in previous maps, so getting 4 hours into the map only to be engaged in a boss battle you have no hope of beating is rough.The Apocalypse modes do make for decent replay value and ways to challenge yourself, but even without those modifiers I think this game is best suited for players who enjoy the feeling of throwing themselves at challenging scenarios and failing until they learn how to succeed. It also bears mentioning that the metaprogression system means you'll initially find yourself thrown into maps without many of the tools to succeed. A player will therefore need to be comfortable with failure in order to see the game through to the end.I also feel that the game needs more content. It only has 5 maps, and while Apocalypse modes do increase the difficulty for replay value, there is no survival/endless mode. The monster variety is excellent and the existing maps do provide significant and engaging tactical challenges. The soundtrack for the game is also worth talking about, because while it is great overall I did find the lack of variety in the battle themes to be very grating. The metal music is good, but I was desperate to mute it and put on literally anything else after a while since there are only I think two tracks for the whole game. Fortunately the settings menu does allow you to mute just the music, so you can replace it with whatever you want.I did enjoy my time with The Last Spell, but whether I'd recommend it to someone is down to how well I know them. You wouldn't be wrong to call this game a miserable slog, sorta like Darkest Dungeon - and much like Darkest Dungeon the extent to which the art and difficulty overcome the game's grind is entirely subjective. For me it was worth it, but I completely understand that it won't be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Last Spell is a very intuitive tactical roguelike.  Honestly haven't seen many like this, but it feels fun and easy enough to understand after a brief learning curve.  The flavor is all in mixing and matching what kind of unlocks your heroes spawn with and lining them up with the right equipment and weapons that determine their skill loadout.Even just skimming the surface, it's obvious there's a lot of possibility and depth there, and it's really obvious you can mess with a variety of playstyles like tank, AOE bomber, hit and run, etc.You can DEFINITELY get behind if you don't do great on early waves - everything builds on itself.  Like any roguelike I can see that you might wind up with suboptimal builds or just a combination of stuff that makes it vastly harder.  Once you build out a hero after a few levels to do a particular thing, it's basically impossible to pivot them into another role.  Still the game lets you pick up more, but I can see that it's punishing if you make mistakes early.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Tight and well thought out mechanics, game is fun because of the gameplay so the early access status is not a big drawback, excellent pixel art and visual design with very impactful special effects, brilliant music and sounds effects, generally just great production values all around.There were a few minor issues with the progression system especially early on, but since the game is so fun to play anyway these can usually be discounted, and there's always a strong lure to just start one more run to see what you get.  As of the latest version (October 2022) I think the progression issues have been solved - if you know what you're doing you can now win a run on the default difficulty on the easiest map with nothing unlocked, without it even being that difficult, so while there are effectively things you'll need to buy to be able to survive the higher difficulties, it no longer feels like a totally unwinnable scenario right from the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible delivery of a strat game for turn-based fans.  It doesn't have the scale of an Age of Wonders III, but the devs have created an incredible amount of flexibility and balance in your choices which clearly surpasses most games out there.  They have a clever built-in catch up mechanic so it is really accessible for new players as well as highly enjoyable for pure min-maxers.  The below-the-surface complexity is flat out delicious.  Due to random starts and no 'save-maxxing', very high level of replay value.  Also gotta luv strat games where you actually kill a lot of #$%@!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting roguelike tactical/strategy RPG with city defense elements. Very neat concept with some minor flaws. The world is overrun by the undead and mages in your town are attempting to unbind a spell that destroys all magic from the world which is expected to end the waves of zombies. You have to protect those mages from the waves until they can cast the spell.You start each run with three random heroes with different random classes, usually some kind of split between a warrior, ranger and a mage. They level up and acquire new skills and equipment as you defend waves. Each turn has a production phase where you build resource and defense faculties, purchase items from shops, and customize/level up your heroes and a positioning phase where you place your heroes where you see best to make your defensive stance and a combat phase.You will die, especially early in the game. There is no way to win on your first runs. You gain resources for slaying undead to purchase new faculties and unlock other faculties for completing accomplishments/tasks.Right now it has some minor issues such as not being able to rotate structures or AoE skills. A few other things to work out as well but I'm really enjoying it. I want to wait until full release to play more but its very fun and addictive so I don't think I'll be able to hold off.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite an interesting mixture of roguelike with turn based strategy/tactics game (alla XCom).The main section of the game is about spreading scarce resources into buildings, equipment or work... and then there's turn based combat, with (in the beginning) few of your heroes against hordes of monsters.You survive for 2-3 nights, and then you die. Its inevitable. You just get completely overwhelmed.What happens then, you get permanent upgrades, such as - new classes unlocked, new equipment unlocked, new buildings you can add to the camp, camp starts with few walls, all heroes get +1 action point, etc... you get the gist.And then, you try again. Maybe survive one night further.It is quite addictive, and the cool thing is that most of enemies are bullet sponges, and they fall pretty fast. There's just an insane number of them. Its completely normal to fight about 40-50 enemies (or more) with your 3 heroes (can get more later).The thing which is, at least for me, a negative - is the fact that you just have to lose. I know its a part of the gameloop - but it starts to get slightly annoying that you repeat things over and over, as you keep restarting the loop. Build a mana well, build a quarry, build a mine. Clean this salvage up, put walls there. Level up heroes from scratch, buy new equipment.I find I can spend about 30 minutes in it (one-two nights), and then I'm done for the day. Unlocking perma-upgrades is fun enough because you get to unleash all that power the next loop, and you can _see_ that you're getting more powerful, not just because of upgrades and equipment, but because you get to understand skills and enemy units better.I just have this vague feeling that I won't be playing it for much longer... I think, while its a good game, the expiration date -due to roguelike mechanic in it- is going to be pretty soon.Still, worth your money. Its unique in what it does.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: GOOD for EARLY ACCESSAt the time of this review I have just finished a 10th Run and the 3rd Map. I have MANY things I could say about this game but I will try to keep it comprehensive and brief. In terms of Gameplay I would say its for the most part fleshed out. I will say in terms of balancing there is A LOT of work that needs to be done. Each run I find myself using 3 weapons, Two Handed Hammer, Daggers and Druid Staff. A Spell Book may be thrown in there but for the most part these three weapons seem to be best at crowd control and boss rushing. In addition to this these weapons are the most efficient in terms of mana cost to kill ratio. Once you learn that poison/contagion builds are the most effective at crowd control you have a hard time convincing yourself to use any other primary method of crowd control. Every single one of my heroes has a druid staff if I have anything to say about it. Meanwhile other weapons like the rifle, sword and one handed axe need some serious re-balancing to make them worthwhile to use. Some of these weapons have high mana cost to use their crowd control or debuff abilities. Final Nights come down to a boss rush. I cannot say that I do not like this but once you figure out that the final night changes your runs from going to crowd control to dumping all of your damage onto single targets as quick as you can, it really changes up the pacing and formula. I managed to coast and not have to have as bad whiplash by just giving a majority of my heroes daggers as their second weapon. My recommendation to the developer would be to make the final night also wave based and waves don't stop generating until after a certain turn. Bosses could still be present and defeating them could earn a extra bonus of tainted essence. Speaking of rewards.The leveling and rewards system in this game is strange. I feel like its almost where it needs to be but it needs something to keep players from using meta strategies every run. It would be really cool if on certain runs some weapons got ridiculous buffs and others got nerfed. In addition to this it would be cool if there was say a Bounty Hunter building that gave you rewards for accepting contracts and attracting additional enemies. This could add an extra risk in the early game and the payoff could be you could build your haven and economy much faster. In terms of the leveling system, I don't mind it. I would go so far as to say I like it. My last run I built a Two Handed hammer user with a skill range of 10 and laughed at how absurdly overpowered he was. The RNG leveling system forces players not to min-max every single time. Obviously there are some stats that are almost never worth picking (Health and Health Regen) meanwhile others like, Action Points, Skill Range and Propagation bounces are almost always worth a pick.Overall you should consider getting The Last Spell its very fun with the correct amount of difficulty. My recommendation to the developer would be to add some tweaks to weapon balancing and maybe quests that you can do during runs to net more rewards.

_childDocuments_.review: This may very well have one of the the best soundtracks I've heard in a videogame. On top of how modular the game is, where each run is unique and a new experience, with additional challenge modes after you beat the game the first time.If the developers keep their passion for this project, this could be in one of my top 10 games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been steady progress since it hit EA, and it's in a great spot even now.  This game does a great mix between RTS Wave combat and tower defense.  Even decent resource management and character customization.  It's a fun game that has a lot of different levels of game play to it, and all of it fun in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like, this a primarily tactical turn-based game that pretends to be rogue-lite. The waves feel very the same and the game has a crippingily depressing gameplay loop (early on). The game isn't 'get good', it is 'you will fail, but keep playing.'Now, the game is fairly good if you like games like XCOM. Your people are randomized a bit as well as the equipment you get so you will get plenty of replay value. But, as of writing, the monsters are relatively lackluster and sometimes hard to differentiate. The game tells you information in the tool tips of damage but is it visually obvious that a monster with platmail is weak to physical attacks? You'd think magic since magic is set up to be excessively powerful against manmade structures but instead magic impacts resistance. Also, there is the awful inevitability in this game that you know you cannot get past a certain night. The worse part about this is if you fail a night, at least in the games I have played, achievements and the 'special' currency aren't tracked. Getting no consolation prize when the game has a replay cycle can feasibly support this feels pretty bad. What's the point of putting in effort for even a pyrrhic victory when you can just spam pass turn and get on with the next run?All this said, this is a game worth watching. Maybe in a few updates, it'll iron out the issues and really shine. The aesthetic is great and doing smart maneuvers make you feel like a god.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really captured me. It hit all the checkmarks in what I had been looking for.It just keeps bringing you back for more. You'll realize a new strategy and you're excited to start over to give it a whirl. While it may not be for everyone because of the treadmill style of unlocks but in a way, that's what I enjoy about it. Almost every playthrough you'd unlock things and progressively get more invested in your strategies. Highly recommend to anyone who likes turn-based strategy with a rogue-lite element.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The game is difficult and at the beginning every decision feels like it matters, especially since you need to have an Idea where to skill your heroes to.Also the rounds take a long time at the beginning, planning is a big part of the game. Once you got used to it and you have some Strategies and Tactics thought out, the game has a unique flow that goes a lot faster.Which brings me to the mapping of the buttons.I have played it on switch and it's very unpleasant. On PC though it's almost a different game!I love it!!The only thing Im missing, is beeing able to rearrange my Characters. Combat goes fast, the way the skills are utilized is smooth, the overview is nice and there are a lot of different playstyles.All in All it is a really unique and great Strategie&Tactic Rogue-Like!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun actually. idk why but the grind for the unlocks is a good time albeit a bit repetitive but even then i still dont feel bored at all.Edit: alright after pumping through another couple of hours in this game, the map DOES get SUPER repeptitive to be honest, it would be nice if there could be variation on each reset to alter where the ruined buildings are, the tree, shop, etc. Give me a new layout.I think so far my pet peeve about the map (which is super trivial) is the south west side, the trees and rock placement are hella annoying. I want to clear mobs EARLY to survive the mid-wave onslaught so i can rotate my characters around but to the other side that needs help, the tree and rock obscuring vision is just so annoying to manoeuvre around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I went in to this game expecting very little but was incredibly surprised by the detail in the base building, character creation and my most favorite of all the horde mechanics. Let me first say that this game is very slow and will eat up a lot of your time which may turn people off, since it has a big grind at the beginning, but this grind is also supposed to help you learn the basic mechanics of the game before you start unlocking more complicated features. The hordes in this game feel amazing to  fight against as you go up against hundreds of enemies and thin them out before they are able to get to you base center. the sound track is awesome having a mix of rock and metal when you defend against hordes, and another thing good about this game is that it does not hold your hand and is considerably difficult until you start optimizing a strategy to survive until  the last spell finishes. I can't wait for the full release but even if this was the final product i still feel as though i got my moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is absolutely fantastic as a base defense turned based roguelike RPG. Sadly it's currently held back by its progression system and lack of longevity, which isn't nearly as motivating long term as in games like Slay the Spire.The beginning is very satisfying. It might take a while to get an overview over the stats, but it turns out fairly simple and intuitive after an hour or two. Both the base expansion and fighting are satisfying, the sound design is great. You will likely get your money's worth for 30-40 or so hours of fun as you unlock the key permanent upgrades for your account.However, that's when it gets frustrating and this title currently wastes potential, since the replayability quickly runs out. There are not enough maps (only 3, and their geometry is fixed), the randomisation in enemy variation is miniscule and generally results in the same tactics every round, and there is barely any incentive to use the higher game modes since you can actually farm permanent upgrades faster by only playing the 2nd map on base difficulty over and over again.Since the title is still updating, this part will surely improve as new content gets added. However the progression system will need a more fundamental overhaul.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, 8 hours in I'm barely scratching the surface and only beat the first town. I'll admit, it gets repetitive fast, but only because the waves are big and you suddenly realise that the entire wave took almost an hour and there's like 6 more of them.The building part was a bit underwhelming for me, it's more tower defence than town building, and i'm not too much of a fan of tower defence. The strategy combat though is pretty good and a good amount of the skills feel very satisfying as you squish the enemies into viscera. HOWEVER, some of the weapons/skills feel much weaker than others, especially when the diceroll is involved, and you don't get enough MP to play around with the "fun" stuff for long enough.As a game? Pretty good, if you're the type of person who calculates game hours vs money spent, then this game is basically free for you. What really gets me though is the INSANE BANGER OF A SOUNDTRACK. Imagine listening to doom OST but it's paced for a turn based strategy game.EDIT: As of 7 more hours into the game. Once you get more unlocks and progress (especially in the 2nd town), you finaly feel like the slog is a bit less...sloggy. You see new buildings, new defenses, new mechanics, new enemies, new weapons, and the game then feels much better than the first level, and the waves don't feel as big and slow anymore because you're always on edge. Solid stuff, still feel some weapons are just flat out worse than others, and some builds which abuse health are too punishing.

_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing like knowing you have to grind a game for like 10 hours before you can even really begin to make progress. That is just sooooooooo unfun to me. I can win in Slay the Spire, Rogue Legacy, or Dead Cells in one run with enough skill. That's the allure of games like that. The benefits you earn just give you more handicap to make it easier or they unlock further difficulty levels. It is downright, unquestionably impossible to win this on your first run and everything you need to win is locked behind achievement walls. Most of which you can't see. After my first game, I didn't even see any towers available to start the unlock process on, which feels immensely important. So, you're stuck grinding, knowing full well you will lose and lose and lose before you grow.HARD. PASS.

Added to by the gimmicky bosses which you can really mis-prepare for until you've fought (and probably lost) against them once.

_childDocuments_.review: There is an incredibly steep difficulty curve. The first haven after the tutorial I completed on my 4th attempt, and did it on apocalypse on the first. In twice as many attempts, I have still not beaten the second haven.Outside of this, the game is incredible. It's exactly my kind of game. The turn based strategy, building your haven between waves and the roguelite elements are brilliantly done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I was considering refunding this game after the tutorial and not being super confident I'd like it, and now am glad I didn't. I decided to give at least part of a regular run. I ended up giving my melee character a perk that makes him reflect damage on anything that hits him relative to his block value, and stacked block, making him unkillable and 1shotting everything that had the audacity to hit him. Then, I gave my caster a book that gave him a chain lightning spell. Well, I go to cast the chain lightning on a massive group of enemies, it chained onto the melee character doing negligible damage to him, and instantly killing my caster.I'm convinced this is actually a comedy game disguised as a tactics game, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun turn based strategy game I've played in my life. It can seem tough and unforgiving at the beginning, but trying out different things through failed playthroughs is part of the fun for this piece. And even later when you've got a good thing going, mixing up the way you play keeps it extremely replayable.As others have mentioned you can't beat it on the first run or anything like that, but I really don't see it as a flaw. Get beat down, stand back up, try again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Great tower defense - survival - rpg game. I didn't think I'd get to play something like this.It's like darkest dungeon but tower defense.If you had fun playing that game, then this is a really good game to play.Warning: Not for snowflakes expecting a "chill game"There will be a lot of back tracking. Rethinking of what you did wrong. Think of it as having a multiverse.If you lose the first city (the only city for now, they are planning to add more), you redo everything, except for the buffs you already unlocked. On the same city.Basically every time you "fail", you come back stronger.Some people don't get this because when they play the game, they think that "winning is the only way to end game".Once you play long enough, and you unlock more and more buffs, each start becomes easier and easier (although not that easy mind you - still gotta plan ahead).RNG - It's everywhere. Again, very familiar concept if you played darkest dungeon.CPU Intensive game. When I check my CPU usage, it took 51% to run it. Also, multiple times my CPU fan would run really, really fast for like 5 seconds, and then go back to normal. This only happens when I play this game. I have an i9-9900k.Lastly, since it's early access, there's not a lot of content yet. Although it already gave me hours of gameplay just playing the first city.I wish they'd allow us to upgrade weapon, instead of relying on RNGesus. Maybe they'll add this feature to crafting buildings in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Grind - I mean, the Last Spell is an interesting game crippled by various mechanical flaws.In your sudo-tower defense/tactics game, you lead random generated but dialog limited goofballs to defend a craphole covered in dirt and what I can only assume to be diarrhea until all the monsters or boss is dead. Now, I like tower defense games. I like tactic games. I was thinking "Oh, boy! Finally, my two favorite things together!" and after a few hours felt like perhaps I have a problem. Like, playing, I felt "Hm - You know, despite me loving these genres, this game is... terrible."So, what makes The Last Spell so bad? Let me hit you up, homes:1. The grind - Waves last too long. I am not kidding when the average run for a single town will take anywhere from 20 minutes to two hours.  This is combined with rogue-lite elements where to get passive and active upgrades to handle later maps requires failing/dying over and over and over again after spending two hours. You will never lose a run 90% of the time due to skill, but instead due to not having enough upgrades. Everything in this game feels SO LONG in a bad way. Bosses? Oh, they have 12 life bars and there is like four copies of them. Enemies to clear with your heroes? Only 502390 zombies left! It feels like such a slog. 2. Hero/town management bloat: Do you like clicking the "Add mana" button to a hero every wave? Or having to click another building to add health to a hero? Or telling your peasants to mine gold instead of materials? Instead of these things being streamlined or smoothed out, prepare for each wave for you to go though the same boring clicking/steps over and over and over again taking up time that already is being killed by the next wave which is only going to be an hour long.3. The dialog/story: Basically, magic bad and magic needs to go away so wizards need to cast final spell which removes all magic. Blah blah blah - The thing is the story itself is not bad, but it's the character dialog in battle and the like which are absurdly cringe. Prepare to hear lines similar to "COWABUNGA, IT'S RAINING BLOOD" and "IM HYPED, HOMIE!" as the same 10 or so lines get repeated over and over again by oddly enough looking asset flips from RPGmarker portraits. And if you kill bosses? Oh boy, things like "Man, I can't believe there was a dragon in that lake. That's going to cause a block in tourism!"  - It's all insanely painful.You can ignore point three, but I can't stress enough you should watch a YouTube video of someone just playing the first town and see if you can watch the entire run without falling asleep.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about The Last Spell. At base level, it's a turn based, squad tactical RPG combat game mixed with some light town building. Build up your town during the day, fight off horrid monstrosities trying to destroy it at night, using a crew of up to six heroes as well as walls, traps and other defences built during the day. Roguelite mechanics drive the progression once your town has either fallen, or survived the last night with its associated (intensely difficult) boss fight. There are five non-tutorial maps in the campaign, with their own attendant landscapes and challenges, including a unique boss and a smattering of unique enemies.The mechanics are very crunchy, but easy enough to understand on an intuitive level, so your little band of defenders will quickly establish their individual fighting styles as the nights go on, using a great classless system of skills and attributes that all feed into each other delightfully for those of us that like poking and prodding at intricate systems.Where this game truly shines is its atmosphere. I can't think of a game I've played that conveys a sense of being a complete badass in the face of a hopeless situation as well as The Last Spell does. I usually don't like pixel graphics, but I can't deny they work great here, truly best-in-class, giving your imagination enough to work with to make the creatures you're up against even more horribly distorted and grotesque in your mind's eye. Spell effects and sprite work are all wonderful, combined with excellent sound design to make your spells and abilities feel like you're hitting enemies with the broadside of a skyscraper.And the soundtrack might be the best part of all, a grinding, electronic masterpiece that sets the tone for fighting off unending hordes of terrifying monsters in a glorious last stand. I'll inevitably turn off the soundtrack in most turn based games after a roughly a dozen hours so I can either listen to my own stuff or throw on a podcast. I can't imagine ever wanting to switch it off here, it's perfect.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is grueling. Even when you think you've found really unbalanced, broken combinations of weapons and perks; even when you have perfect level up bonuses, this game will stomp you. If you get addicted to punishing games like Darkest Dungeon, you'll feel right at home in this one.Get ready for hours of slowly getting the hang of the game then beating yourself up when you make the wrong move or slip with your mouse. Thank you for this game, devs. I hate it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Very creative little game, fantastic nuanced turn based strategy with interesting base building mechanics in between waves. Takes a bit to figure out where its best to allocate your gold and building materials. RNG can at times be cruel but overall fairly balanced combat that certainly ins't a pushover, especially as you progress. Highly recommend overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. Every turn of combat feels overwhelming at first with how many enemies are thrown at you. Every enemy deals a good bit of damage, but you can kill upwards of 15 enemies a turn. It is incredibly satisfying when you clear a board before the next wave comes. Progression is also very rewarding. During the day you build/upgrade building in town and buy items from the shop. If managed well to create a good economy, you can make your heroes significantly stronger each day, making them feel like absolute monsters by the final night. The difficulty keeps pace though, so it never becomes easy, you just feel stronger.10/10. Can't wait for the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Get your groupBarter your way to gear to fit your strategyLevel them to best fit your strategyBuild the base to keep your town safeWatch as night comes and the horde arrivesRealize that your strategy was garbage all along Stare as the fast mob you neglected for 2 turns obliterates your defensesHear the shrieking and cries of the town as it crumbles to your neglect and worthless leadershipSee your best hero succumb to their grievous woundsDie while telling yourself "Next time will be better."Hell yes I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Solid and highly addictive. Watch some gameplay videos / streams to understand if it's for you. The game has about 2 downsides for me personally:1. RNG. Some of the random elements you can mitigate by rerolling your starting squad (basically abandoning the run). Other things you can't, and meta progression makes it worse by unlocking a lot of stuff you potentially not interested in (although you can weigh in into your stuff using omens, by that comes at a cost).2. Longer runs. Especially when you are learning the game, a run can easily take you a couple of days (or more). This makes it very hard to pick up the run on the next day and try to remember everything you planned. One stupid mistake can easily ruin days of efforts.Otherwise the game is beautifully designed and fun.Absolutely worth its price (if it's your kind of jam)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Very good strategic roguelike, with very long runs (~4 to 5 hours for a full run of a long map)VERY heavy on the meta-progression, to the point where I'm fairly certain its almost impossible to win your first run, as some meta upgrades increase the number of actions each hero can perform in a turn. Which, as people familiar with xcom-ish games are familiar with, is always the most important stat.There are definitely some weapons or strategies that I feel are just simply better than others (hand crossbow crit build can absolutely wipe out any boss faster than almost any other weapon, blood magic + vampirism is incredibly strong on any melee weapon, etc.) but the game itself is fairly well balanced. I cant speak for higher "apocalypse" levels, which is this games system of ramping difficulty, as each level adds a TON more difficulty.All in all, a good game. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack, great art, great game. Definitely worth the price.It's really hard though. If you aren't good at turn based games with action economies, then you're going to get absolutely destroyed and you will have to grind.Hand crossbow, druidic staff and daggers are so much stronger than the other weapons that you should basically always look for them. Sure, there are a few more viable options, but you absolutely need multihit and propagation builds to stand a chance.There are just way too many enemies on screen to spend two action points on a crappy five-square fireball spell for example. You need things that can wipe out entire clumps in one attack. Things like the hand crossbow, which can clear entire screens even with a mediocre build.The game is unfortunately too hard to experiment with off-meta builds. Even if you kill one guy with a 1k damage momentum meme attack, you still need a way to kill his 15 angry friends or you turbo lose.But the game is stylish as hell. It feels great to play, sound design and art is on point, and the soundtrack is super good. Unlocking stuff is fun, building your characters is fun. The appearance editor is surprisingly robust and it's fun to name your heroes after your IRL friends. All in all, I had a blast playing this game. Bear in mind that it's slow and very hard, but give it a try if you think it sounds cool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Runs can last for a long time but if you manage to beat a stage on your first try (or on stressful subsequent runs) it goes from hoping you set everything up correctly, despairing when certain enemies appear or unknown boss mechanics, praying to kill the boss before it slaughters your team, to relief and joy when you land the final blow. Great game, my favorite part is taking a 30 minute break after a freaky night and spending another 30 minutes thinking about what items to pick before the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty good so far.a last stand tower defence game, your gonna die, but it doesnt matter. it doesnt even feel like game over when you die but more of a reincarnation and has good continuation, each go and death through is like a attempt to unlock more stuff so that your future play throughs can be easier. so its kinda designed so that you kinda need to go through and lose to unlock stuff anyway. not that its really losing but instead feels more like continuation.good replayability. havent cleared the first 10 stages yet which is all they have at the moment. will require a lot of playthroughs to unlock stuff to do that. then hopefully they will add more map areas or stages or whatever.pretty decent game though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good, fun game at the minute and seems like its got some initial meat on the bones. It's not a must buy, but I feel like with a few changes this is going to be a top game.A few things that I'd change and for potential purchasers to be wary of include...- You can not rotate buildings/aoe attacks, seems like a really odd design choice and the "auto rotate" the game tries to implement doesn't work. This is actually pretty game breaking for me, it leads to less tactical options and poor building placement.- Achievements, the dev says they're coming, I'll probably hold off playing until they're in the game as I know a lot of you will too.- Sometimes its not abundantly clear when enemies are close to your buildings, especially when they are behind them. Be nicer to have a "enemies close to your buildings" warning.- A way to select your initial 3 heroes from a pool would be nice, I don't like the RNG of my team select. Maybe this is an unlockable further in the game but no one has mentioned it and I haven't seen it in streams.- The ability to place buildings over the ruins of old buildings. It's clear thats what I'd like to do, I shouldn't have to come out of the building menu, go into the ruins menu, click salvage the ruin, go back into the building menu and build the building. If I have the units to clear, I should be able to do all this in one action with a popup warning for "are you sure you want to use X units to clear the building.a- The sound needs more work, the loops are pretty short. Its good music but not enough.The game does a lot of good things which deserve a mention,- It has a plethora of unit types and abilities. - There seems to be a lot of "persistent" unlockables which change game play between runs.- A run seems to last around an hour which is a decent amount of time, unsure how long a full clear would take as I haven't managed it.- There are multiple difficulty tweeks which make it accessible for every, the starting difficulty is pretty hard.- The art is great.- It has a surprising amount of "base building" within it which I was not expecting.- Unique genre type, like Final Fantasy Tactics mixed with They Are Billions.Overall at the minute there are things which stop me proper deep diving into the game so take this with a pinch of salt, this is obviously meant to be a game you sink multiple hours into. However from scratching the surface I'd recommend jumping into the game in its current state, its a 7/10 with solid 10/10 potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: [June 13, 2021]This game has the mechanic where you must lose to unlock things in order to win.I hope when it comes out of EA, you can play the game on any difficulty without any unlocks and beat the game.--------------[October 24th, 2022]It has been over a year and updates are aplenty.I have come back to re-review the game and... it has shown to be fundamentally flawed both in developer and game.The game has become a meta-progression grind. And it's a boring unrewarding treadmill.Frustrating actually.Here is my experience:You do your best with the knowledge you had a year past. You fail within a few hours of the game losing to what the games throws at you an overwhelming amount of enemies. Your loss is not in vain however as you are given more power and unlocks with the progression.You come back for another round and now you are able to win. Finally.The next stage shouldn't be too difficult right?Wrong. It's actually three times harder.The boss on this stage must be killed THREE times and the health pool of this meat bag is at least 10 time larger than those regular mob.I have optimized my units with the best of my ability. I have built my base with defense efficiently. But in the end, the boss sieges through and overwhelms the base with numbers.What the ♥♥♥♥?And I lose, and now I have to start from the town over but a little stronger.What kind of gameplay loop is this? This is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ experience.Present it this way: We WIN then we can choose to make it harder to win.Not: We lose and now it just a little easier not to lose.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like doing a lot of planning and prep work for gambling and then investing a lot of time to see if that gamble is going to do anything more than fall apart you might like this.Some aspects of the game feel like they need to be re-balanced. The problem is if everything you get is RNG then every enemy needs to be solvable by multiple approaches.The music is pretty great.The full review (the wall of text that is).It's fine if you're big into gambling on whether you'll have anything good half way through. RNG is god and if you don't have a good one then kiss your run goodbye once you get past the first few levels of difficulty. The re-roll mechanic seems to be either broken or intentionally bad. When re-rolling the stats for leveling up I get the same thing as before the re-roll but in a different order and less of them far more often than not.To highlight how RNG dependent this is I present the following.1. You receive characters who have three traits that boost or hurt stats. Until you unlock better traits through gameplay you just have terrible traits and it sucks to be you. But even after that is isn't uncommon to get traits that contradict each other and cancel out each others benefits. So you need some luck with traits but not too much.2. These characters have a perk tree. After a certain point your characters get two extra perk columns. Do you have perks that compliment the traits the character had? Maybe, but you can work around them not aligning perfectly they just end up slightly worse. Did you get perks that compliment each other? No? Then that character is going to be pretty bad. Perks are huge part of how good a character ends up and a perk tree without perks that compliment one another is a character who is dead on arrival at higher difficulties.3. every level your characters gain a primary and secondary stat boost. These are a choice between a number of stats to bump that come in varied levels of rarity. Are you building an evasive melee character who runs around picking off high durability targets because they got increased movement and dodge and they have perks that are really good for it? Well you rolled HP, Mana, Critical, resistance, and resistance reduction... None of those help a scepter user continue to kill things on the field so you re-roll the stats and loss two options and you got... Mana, Critical, and resistance. Didn't you just roll those? There are five other stats  it could have rolled: damage, accuracy, block, armor, and dodge. Any of those other than block are better than anything from the previous list except possibly for critical. Get two or three levels like that and your character goes from a potentially really good character into a corpse waiting to happen. Meanwhile the enemies stats all grow every with every wave.4. You get random weapons as rewards. You can build buildings that will give you a weapon from a certain category after each night like physical, ranged, or magic. Unfortunately what weapon you get from that category, the level, random stats, and sub-type of the weapon are all up for grabs and the game isn't opposed to throwing you three options of the lowest quality of a single weapon type with no modifiers even after you've bought all the chance of better quality gear upgrades and re-roll isn't opposed to showing you another three slightly different versions of the same weapon again despite the number of weapon types available in each category.5. Remember what was just said about weapon rewards? Armor is the same except you have more armor slots than weapon slots. At least with armor producing buildings you are likely to have characters who want different armor types to use the random different things but there are so many more chances to roll bad secondary stats on armor like dodge up on an armor that penalizes dodge or plus physical damage on an armor that otherwise boost poison damage and propagation.I found the defensive stat bonuses and stun resistance the enemies get to be particularly egregious. They do threatening levels of damage while having enough dodge that anyone with a less than great accuracy to miss or have well over a thousand hp but halve the damage of my attacks or just remove a flat hundred and change damage while after reducing it by a percentage and have a couple thousand hp. Some people who have played the game will now chime in saying that I need to use the correct type of attack against the right enemy type but whether I have a correct type or not is entirely up to RNG and killing anything with over a thousand HP requires that you have had some luck with RNG on three different aspects of a character. The stun resistance problem is that enemies start showing up with stun resistance higher than the stun chance of stun on most weapons. You can increase you stun chance using level up and some pieces of gear but any opponent worth stunning has enough stun resistance that unless you built a character to do stun(which means they probably don't do much damage) then you don't stun. See the common 80% sun resistance versus a very high stun value on a weapon attack being 75%. You can't stun them unless you boosted your stun chance and unless you boosted it by 55% or more then you don't even have a 50/50 shot of stunning them on the highest stun chance move available to you.The fact that some enemies have 100% stun chance ranged attacks on a several thousand HP enemy makes it feel worse.The final straw for my realizing the game is kind of bad was the unblockable, undodgeable, and halves my resistance attack that does more damage than most of my characters have health and armor on a random normal(not boss or elite) enemy. The guy who does it has over a thousand hp and resist half on all damage dealt to him and removes debuffs from enemies in an aoe and makes them immune for two turns. The other big enemies have multiple solutions to them. You can stay away from the melee threats, slow them using debuffs, use big momentum hits or unblockable to overcome their block to do enough damage to kill, debuff to lower dodge so they can't avoid them, target armor with melee characters to remove it with half the damage required, or a number of other techniques. This guy you just have to hit him over and over again with high damage moves in one turn so he doesn't kill one of your characters at range. Hopefully in all that RNG earlier you rolled the exact type of character needed to kill this one thing before the first one shows up and that character is on the right side of the map.Also Why do the outer defenses being attacked cause a lot of panic? They exist to take hits they shouldn't cause any panic at all. "But the people hear it being attacked at night and it worries them" but they don't hear the explosive crossbow bolts, catapults, fireballs, and lightning strikes and panic about how close those are?Going to go finish doing higher apocalypse values since inevitably someone will try to say that I didn't like it because I was bad at it instead of acknowledging the issues in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: New and fresh way of rogue like tower defense game. Each round is really long compared to other roguelike games but if you are fine with turn base battles which take around 20 minutes and for one run you need around 10 battles....then you will love this game like I do.PRO:- manage your city / defenses- level your heroes- collect and equip items - defense turn based battles- really cool progression mechanicsCon:- after a long run to be defeated feels sometimes bad- you need at least fight once each boss in order to beat him (need to know the mechanics)For all base and tower defense fans ....Get this game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game, dont think this turn based, rogue like rpg is something that was done before that often. I think the game is pretty intuitive, but can be tough once you reach the later days or higher Apocalypse Ranks, for me its just the right balance between difficulty and reward. The graphic is retro style which ofc is not everyone cup of tea, but it feels fitting for this game. Think it would be a nice touch that the heros you get at random all come with a bit of personality, so you grow attached to them for that run and dont feel like shrugging when one of them bites the dust. What the game needs to make it really good is maybe a bunch of maps that maybe provide different levels of terrain and gimmicks like a set up catapult, or a "nuke" that gets rid of all undead but its only usable once. Also the perkz should enable a more versatile game style, sure there will always be cookie cutter builds, but some talents are just so useless that i cant see a situation where anyone would pick it (Potion throw?? Or punching poison damage). Generally the scrolls or potions are pretty much useless at the moment and not worth the scarce money you have.   Overall a pretty enjoyable game with a load of potential of the devolopers dont drop the ball.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: I will keep coming to this game, despite it kicking my ass everytime I play, one little mistake is enough to ruin your 5 hour playthrough. I love the design of this game and the defense aspect but damn is it difficult, never played a game that took so much concentration and prudent actions. Much of the game is also luck based but you can improve your chances through essence, increasing your chances of success over time. However, it is still very hard and my pride won't allow me to use boundless mode, so I'll update this review once I have beaten it (whenever that days comes). Overall, 9/10 game, I don't usually enjoy strategy turn based games like this, but this one has definitely gripped my attention.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: Original review: ♥♥♥♥ this game, but like, y'know, in a good way. It feels pretty complete from what I've played of it. Roguelike feel if you know what to expect you're gonna get what you expected. It's pretty hard, and some of the choices feel like they don't matter, but it's satisfying chunking down like 15-20 enemies in a single turn when there's 70 of them and you're sure you're about to get overwhelmed.Update:I've now played about 70 hours of the last spell, and have beaten two of the endings and am working on the third. With a lot more experience I can see that a lot of the choices that didn't seem like they mattered do and the game has a pretty healthy metagame. There's not one spam solution that works, and in fact it takes the approach that several work. By the late game, you can basically build any class in almost any way and have it work. It's a great feeling. While some weapons have very weak use cases (like the scepter, which seems great at first glance, but I've never been able to make it work), they all work and you can win with them. figuring out how to best combo your guys together is pretty fun and actually designing your build order is super important for getting this game to be easier. At any rate, I'd say this is 100% worth a look. Even in early access, it feels very complete and it feels like anything we get out of early access will most likely be QOL and longevity. At about 70 hours I'm pretty near completing the game at its current state, and I'm super excited to see what's in store for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: This has all the potential to be a real classic. I love the music, settings, and challenge of the game. You and your ragtag group of warriors give it your all to defend a village from hordes of hungry ruthless enemies that come every night. Combat is turn-based and action point based in a tactical style similar to Final Fantasy Tactics in some ways. You collect resources to upgrade your warriors, town, and defences. Death isn't the end - you can always start over and keep the stuff you have earned. Truly give this game a look you will not be disappointed if you love tactics style games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Spell

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game. I was not expecting that! To put it simply, go get it. It's one of those games you start playing and before you know the sun is coming up.It's roguelike, but not to worry, it's actually not annoying to lose because you're always unlocking new buildings, weapons and mechanics. It's a simplified Final Fantasy Tactics game. Every hero has like 4 skills and two weapons. (Totally customisable heroes).You fight hordes of undead every night. Lowering their HP slows them down, so you have to plan which undead to target so that they're all just one square away from you while slowing them down as much as possible. _childDocuments_.review: I feel ready to finally review this game. Note that I played the beta years ago on another Steam account, but the 115 hours on this account have been played since patch 1.0 a month ago.Pros:- The game mechanics are original. Instead of making something related to elements (fire, water, etc.) like most RPGs, this game uses momentum, isolation, opportunity, propagation, and multi-hit. I also don't think there's any other game that adds Base Building and Rogue-lite to the TRPG genre. This game is unique.- Every character can equip two weapons, making the build variety interesting. Even after 100 hours, I'm still learning new builds on the forums I didn't think of myself.- The enemy variety is also pretty large. This is the reason you have to use two different weapons on each character. For example, using a rifle to kill enemies with high dodge is not efficient.- The music and sound design are really good. Many players praised the developers for the BGM that plays during the night phase.- The art and design are correct. The UI is confusing at first but very detailed.Opinion: These are my personal opinions that are not in Pros or Cons- The game difficulty is weird. I found the game pretty easy; I played every map and finished the game in a single run with no repeats, but some other players are stuck on the first map for over 15 hours. I think this game needs a difficulty slider in addition to the Apocalypse system. The base difficulty is too easy for players who are experienced in the genre but too difficult for the average Joe.- The character generation has too much RNG. When recruiting a character, you can see its traits but not its perks. But you almost never build your characters around their traits. The most important information is what perks they have. There's also no reason to buy characters who are lower levels, so half the character shop is useless.- The game shows you how many tiles enemies can move but not their attack range. I'm so used to that in other TRPGs; it's weird to always select enemies to look up their attack range instead of getting the information from pressing ALT.Cons:- The game is missing a tactical view. Many times, enemies can be hidden behind some tree or decoration.- The omens that give you more chances to get a certain type of weapon are boring. Boring to unlock in the early game because the player will prefer using the +8% damage instead, boring to use in the late game because you know which weapons are stronger than others, and it locks you into a certain build type for the entire run.- The corpse system doesn't work. Basically, every enemy you defeat can leave behind a corpse. If many enemies died on the same cell, it can become a pile of corpses that gives more rewards. The enemy who died has a greater chance to become a corpse if it was near the walls of your city. So, here's the thing. It doesn't work for three reasons: First, piles of corpses are too strong compared to gold mines. The rewards they give make your characters stronger, and the excess items can be sold for extra gold. There's no reason not to use your workers on corpses instead of gold mines. But they are also generated randomly, so if you decide to make gold mines and get 10 piles of corpses, you feel like you wasted your resources building the gold mines. The other scenario feels bad too. If you didn't make gold mines but only two piles of corpses spawned, your workers have nothing good to work on.Second, there's no control skill in the game. You can stun/slow an enemy, but you can't push it, pull it, or make it move to a certain square. An experienced player can certainly wait a few turns and kill enemies near the city walls, but he can't stack the enemies on the same cell to make a pile of corpses intentionally.Lastly, it's designed as a catch-up mechanic so players who had trouble surviving a night can get more rewards, but it has the opposite effect. Now you WANT to play badly, let the enemies into your city, and ignore the panic level. They say "good players can use the corpse mechanic efficiently to get more rewards," I say "the corpse mechanic is counterintuitive and forces the player to play in a way that doesn't fit the theme of the game."- The developers like to balance the game by nerfing instead of buffing. The issue with this way of balancing is that it punishes the average player while the experienced player will just find the next broken build. It's more interesting to buff weaker weapons so everyone has more options.Overall, I'd say it's a pretty good game. I would recommend it to anyone who likes TRPGs. I'd love to come back for more updates and DLC (I would love to see more mechanics like summons...etc), the developers made a good game that can be improved in many ways.
