_childDocuments_.review: I was willing to give this a recommendation if it wasn't for the inaccurate "choices matter" tag. Almost none of your choices matter. A singular somewhat arbitrary choice near the end completely dictates your ending between two primary endings, everything else being small variations on those endings. There's maybe one of those variations that could be called a seperate ending, so that's three endings. And only one of the characters matter for some of the variation in ONE of the primary endings. If you want a okay FMV story, then this is for you, but if you want your choices to matter, look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to play The Complex, expecting a tense interactive thriller, but the storytelling was unfortunately very weak and it does little to create enthusiasm to see the alternate paths after your first playthrough. The sequence of events, which doesn't change all that much except near the final minutes, takes rather cheap shortcuts and paints characters in such broad strokes that it feels as though it was made from a thin, bullet-point outline rather than a properly fleshed out screenplay. I don't want to get into spoilers, but the security of this supposedly very new, "spared no expense" superlab somewhere near London is laughably bad and the nature of the bio threat, while gross and painful in its visible symptoms, doesn't make much (if any) sense.Things are somewhat better on the technical side. The video quality is decent, I would guess 1080p, and looked fine on my 4K screen. Not a blu-ray level bitrate, but good enough. The decision prompts also have a nice, clean design. However, one glaring issue is the music, which seems to be hard-embedded into the videos themselves, and this creates situations of both abrupt fade outs of the score and moments that last longer than they should where I've made a plot decision but the lead character (supposedly an expert research scientist) stands in place looking indecisive, often spoiling the drama of the moment.There was a great deal of potential here, I love smart science fiction stories like The Andromeda Strain, and Wales Interactive really impressed me with their earlier FMV game Late Shift, where your decisions can lead to wildly different outcomes, but the designers here made major errors not giving the story and fluidity of the experience the attention they deserved.Story: 2/5Gameplay: 2/5Graphics: 3/5Sound: 2/5

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is another FMV title from Wales Interactive, featuring a compelling sci-fi story with decent acting and a multitude of choices throughout the game. With 9 endings and an emphasis on the weight of players’ choices, I had expected playtime to last longer and to have vastly different cutscenes when choosing opposing options. Unfortunately, this is not the case and although some of the endings are surprising, almost all scenes leading up to the final chapter are exactly the same. Proving that most of the minor decisions made throughout the game had almost no effect on the story. The Complex should be treated like a good movie, something to try a few times, but nothing to be over-enthused about and is not worth the full price.+ Decent acting, script and story that had me intrigued from start to finish.+ Easy to skip scenes that have already been seen before by simply pressing TAB.+ Clearly displays the number of scenes/endings unlocked and personality traits at the end of each playthrough.+ Manages to steer away from the awkward silence / transitions that commonly plagues the FMV genre.+ Steam achievements.- Choices rarely matter, only towards the conclusion of the game do they become apparent. Making most minor decisions pointless or leading exactly to the same cutscene no matter what option was selected. - The first playthrough only lasts approx. 85 minutes and subsequent replays are much less than that, due to copious repeated scenes.After treating the victims of a bio-weapon attack in the oppressive state of Kindar, the head scientist in Nanocell technology, Dr Amy Tenant is confronted with a possible new outbreak in London. Reports of a Kindarian citizen vomiting blood on a local subway lead to terrorism suspicions and Amy, along with other colleagues quickly find themselves under lockdown in their laboratory. Racing against time, they try and uncover the identity of their assailants as well as the truth about their organisation and what really happened on Kindar.The Complex is similar to an interactive movie, like Netflix's 'Bandersnatch'. It mostly involves watching the scenes unfold on screen and occasionally making a decision. These choices are supposed to be the backbone of the game and encourage players that all decisions matter and influence character traits, endings and other relationships. Regrettably, I found this was not entirely correct and most choices, leading up to the final chapters were completely null, and had little to no effect on the story.Sometimes, after making a decision, another character would step up and say that's the wrong choice and the game will automatically proceed with the latter selection, making the entire 'choice' process completely null. The menu screen does easily display how many scenes have been unlocked, acting as motivation to encourage players to replay and complete to 100%. Yet, even after picking other options, the exact same cutscenes would play time after time and I found myself continuously pressing tab until I finally got to a new screen. This process also becomes more apparent after each replay and soon becomes tiresome. Although I was fascinated with my first playthrough and found the story quite compelling, I was also under the impression that the gameplay was tailored to my own decisions, which I later subsequently found out, that this wasn’t completely true.Nonetheless, some of the endings are different and took me by surprise, but instead of being influenced by a multitude of selections throughout the game, I found it was only really impacted by a few key options towards the end. To give a better understanding of the game length, I achieved 5/9 endings in only 2.5 hours, with the first full playthrough only averaging around 85 minutes. Before purchasing, it is important to note that this is not a long game, like many others in the genre and can be completed to 100% in one sitting quite easily.  Being an FMV game, the graphics and sound are of course, decent with high quality filming and it does not appear restricted through low-budgets or other restraints. The acting is excellent and manages to avoid the cringe factor from dramatized expressions and responses, which I have seen plague many other FMV titles.The Complex is a great, interactive cinematic experience for sci-fi fans as well as FMV enthusiasts. Its compelling story and well directed script make for an enjoyable first playthrough. However, choices in subsequent re-runs feature majority of the cutscenes that players have already seen, highlighting the low importance our choices actually have over the story. Some of the endings do make replaying a tad more encouraging, but to know that they are only swayed by key decisions, making earlier choices seemingly null, frankly is just disappointing and I advise on waiting for a sale before purchasing.This review copy was provided to the OCG-Curations curator.

_childDocuments_.review: An interactive movie by Wales Interactive who brought us amazing cast in this sci-fi thriller.  Everyone did a phenomenal job in this short but multiple-ending game. The story starts with Dr. Amy Tenent, a scientist who presented a Nanocell project which helps injuries by regrowing bones and generate extra blood to help with the healing process. They later discovered that one of the interns developed weird symptoms and after some investigation, some secrets started to unfold before the scientist's eyes. I've enjoyed this interactive movie so much, the story is well-written and the acting is amazing. All of the actors did a good job capturing the emotions of the characters and expressions.  it didn't feel like any of them just a side character to fill a space. I also loved the filming, this movie doesn't feel cheap at all. The soundtracks are great as well, I was also pleased to find an option in the menu where you can pause the choices, no need to stress out by choosing quickly or worry about missing a choice. Also after finishing the first playthrough, you'll be able to skip scenes, however, if you skip quickly you'll even skip the choices, it'll automatically pick the first choice as a default one.  This game has multiple endings, eight in total and a ninth one you can get in the middle. Your choices really matter here, everything you say and do will shape Amy's personalities and the direction she'll take into solving the matter. Your relationship with the characters is also important, you can either gain their trust, getting them close to you or the other way around. Pros:+FMV game.+Very-well written story.+Well done acting+Choices and consequences.+Choices are timed by default but there is an option to pause them. +Building relationships with characters will give different outcomes. +Multiple endings.+High replayability value.+Good soundtracks.+Steam achievements.Cons:- No manual save.Each playthrough can last for more than an hour, I found myself replaying the game multiple times enjoying the different choices. This is really a very well made game, I enjoyed it so much and highly recommend it to FMV lovers or people who enjoy watching movies.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summed up as "Do you want to have important and meaningful choices that affect the course of the game? lol Why don't you tell me instead if you'd like to use a pan or toaster to make your bread."I couldn't not recommend this game enough. The choices are absolutely lackluster and you can never tell which way they will go. Vast majority of choices is like "Do you want to use a crowbar or hammer?" and then they take you in exactly the same direction with absolutely no difference beyond one scene where you hold the said item OR they lead you through a completely different route that WASN'T affected by your item at all. This game laughs at you attempting to use logic and reason and throws the most ridiculous and out of nowhere plot twists at the weirdest moments.The story is very subpar and you have very little control in what your character is actually going through. It felt like watching a film where I could choose what the character will have for breakfast and that was about it. The only slightly significant plot changes that you can make basically wary between "be a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for absolutely no reason" and "be a normal human being just trying to get out". There's absolutely no reason to go for the bad guy option unless you want to test out where it will take you. I really wish the game provided more ambiguity and make the options worthy of actually choosing.Another gripe I had is that for how the bad guy tries to convince you they're right, and they actually use solid arguments, and for the heavily relationship based the game is, you actually can't choose anything other than being a strongly moral person. It feels like Mass Effect series all over again where the only "evil" choices you can make are basically being a petty douchebag without even a reason.Total rating I would give this is 4/10. I wish I could refund this game, it definitely wasn't worth what I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is by developer's Wales Interactive, Good Gate Media, Little Jade Productions and filmed in the UK. Also featuring guest acting performance by Twitch streamer and former Xbox UK presenter, Leah Viathan.This is a story rich adventure FMV game where choices matter. Most playthroughs for each game are roughly about an hour long with one much shorter. Be forewarned: U do have to make quick, tough decisions/judgement calls that matter and alter the progression of the game depending on your choices. The Pause Choices (timer) can be turned off in the Streaming Options. This was mainly for Streamers with audience participation during live streams. I left my timers on.Starts out with our 2 main scientists, Dr Amy Tenant & Dr Rees Wakefield in Kindar testing  Nanocell technology unaware that the Kindar government had released a major biochemical attack on the villages recently. 5 years later Amy is working in London and giving a presentation to continue getting funding for their research when  Clare, (later we find out is one of her techs) gets sick on a train. Someone releases the video online which has rumors flying wondering if it's some kind of attack.  Rees rejoins her and the staff to help figure out how to treat Clare and keep things contained within The Complex while in "locked down" mode. All the while someone is trying to break through the high tech security. I will stop here so I won't  spoil the game. Features:Real-time Relationship Status Tracking: Depending on your choices u will either strengthen or weaken your relationship with those u come in contact with and are scored at the end of each game. Real-time Personality Status Tracting: Your decisions and interactions, your character's personality is tracted. U have 5 basic personality types; Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism.Pros:+20 Steam Achievements (some secret)+10 Trading Cards+Tab to skip previously watched scenes+All achievements are doable+Amazing story+Fantastic voice actors+Multiple endings (9)Cons:+NoneFinal Thoughts:Price is reasonable and interesting enough to replay and get all the endings. I really enjoyed playing this fantastic Sci-Fi Thriller and have gotten ALL 9 endings. One of them is a "Secret" ending. Yes I enjoyed it that much and didn't encounter any issues playing!Also Wales Interactive has more FMV games for your enjoyment. I'm gonna play all of them.Rating: 9.5This review was submitted for , where every game deserves a review.Follow our .

_childDocuments_.review: ***NO SPOILERS***For any prospective buyers – I was on the fence about purchasing this. I wasn’t really sure if the price warranted what ultimately is a movie with an occasional moment of awkward silence until I click the mouse. I already owned Late Shift from a bundle I purchased long ago, but had not played it. I figured since I already had it, I may as well play it and see if I would even enjoy this company’s work. Without getting into detail on Late Shift, I will say that I ended up enjoying it. After I finished the second playthrough I went looking for some detail about the Complex. One question I found on the forum was “how long will the story be?” The answer of 80-90 minutes was satisfactory. Then I did the math, and figured for the price I would be paying less than a ticket to a movie theater (that we can’t go to these days…) So I went ahead and pulled the trigger.I am glad that I did. I will give away nothing of the story, but will leave a few high level thoughts here for any prospective buyers.1.	Don’t be afraid that the quality will be subpar. It clearly doesn’t have the budget of the Avengers/Mission Impossible/Star Wars, but it also was clearly not done on a tight budget. Sound is good, video is good, special effects (what there are) get the job done well enough. There was even a familiar face for me which you will know if you have seen, for example, Prometheus. A quick look on IMDB tells me that there will be other familiar faces to people as well.2.	The writing is well done. This is subjective, but I did not find more than a couple of lines spoken where I thought the writers dropped the ball. And that truly did not take away from the experience3.	The awkward silences aren’t that awkward. It is a necessary evil in this kind of game, but it is handled well here. When the characters have to stand around waiting for the player to make a choice it doesn’t just loop the same video over and over again. A lot of times, there is still dialogue during those times. And, if this really bothers you, it appears there is a setting to pause the game for these decisions. I did not use that, but I did see it was available.For players that are coming here from Late Shift – a lot of what I thought could have been done better has been improved on here. Less odd transitions (for example, where there isn’t a choice that was made, but the dialogue ends up getting cut off for some reason,) more choices, and easier to hear voices. If you are like me, on subsequent playthroughs I turned on the subtitles because the background was so loud I couldn’t hear what people were saying. The Complex improves on all of these issues.Also, I will mention what may be to some the most compelling reason to give this a shot. Sometimes the allure of seeing that there are multiple branching paths and endings can be outweighed by the realization that in order to see them you have to slog your way through scenes and choices you have already been through. 9 endings? That means 8 more times of seeing the same thing over again. I am extremely happy with the way The Complex handles this. Once you complete the playthrough you have the option to press ‘Tab’ to skip ahead. The way this is implemented is fantastic. It will skip scenes you have already seen, and get you to the next choice. But it won’t let you skip new scenes. This was confusing for me at first because I was frustrated with why I couldn’t skip a scene. Turns out, a choice I made earlier in the game had this scene play out just a tiny bit differently. This is such a nice feature that even though I have less than 5 hours currently, I have seen almost 80% of the endings.  Last, I will put a couple of stats that may help someone who is on the fence. My first playthrough:1.	Took roughly 90 minutes2.	I discovered 82 out of 196 scenes3.	I made 81 decisions I hope this was helpful to someone. A fantastic job to all that were involved in making this!

_childDocuments_.review: I hate giving this a poor review. I love this genre and want to see more content like this. For that reason I don't regret buying it. The production design and filming is excellent. I also think the acting is good as well. The problem lies deeper.There are really no meaningful choices in this "game." What is the point of making an interactive movie if it isn't interactive? I know it is hard to produce a movie that has many different twists and turns. But if the production company didn't want to do it right- why make a movie in this format? A money grab? Without meaningful choices it just becomes a weak story that has been told many times before. Even the biggest decisions like who opens the box don't matter at all. Why bother offering the choice other than a vein attempt at pretending this is actually a "choices matter" game?I didn't hate the experience but "The Complex" feels like it is exploiting the people who like movie/games like this rather than celebrating and embracing the format to tell a unique story.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a testament to what you can do with a refitted basement, a couple of jumpsuits, and an iPhone--it's not a good game, though. Not by a long way.I normally love choice-type games, but here it's often only the illusion of choice. There seemed to be a few times where, regardless of what I picked, I was railroaded into one of the other decisions anyway. Most of the choices also lacked any real tension--there was either a fairly obvious option, or I didn't care. If the story and script were good, this wouldn't matter so much, but it's just sci-fi schlock (unapologetically so, in fairness) with many plot contrivances sure to elicit a groan, and with little interest in player agency.The other big problem is that most of the "action" takes place in one location. You could make this work (Reservoir Dogs comes to mind, or many great stage plays), but they don't.Finally, I could say some nice-ish things about it. I could tag weak compliments with the phrase "for what it is", as in: it's got some passable acting, ; the script isn't  bad, ; the characters are fairly likeable... (etc). But I'll spare you. Now, please: spare yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is more an interactive movie than a game. However, it is more interesting to play it like a game by trying to get all different endings (including a secret one), and see how the story changes with different choices. The interesting subtleties lay in how good you maintain relationships with various characters. I found all 9 endings and 191 of the 196 scenes, and there was a lot of fun in trying different avenues in the story. The main weakness is that many early choices do not make a major forking of the story, and therefore the movie seems linear at times. Nevertheless, the various endings are satisfying. While the scenario is not as impressive in its complexity and richness as "Bandersnatch" from Black Mirror, the cinematography, the direction and the cast does a very good job. It is a genre that should be widely encouraged; it turns average movies into engaging adventures.  I hope this team makes more of it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an alright story, nothing impressive. It started somewhat well and then became a dull for an hour of being stuck underground with absolutely no progression. Other than that - don't have high hopes and you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointed after all the rave reviews. The Late Shift, by the same company, is MUCH better. (obsessively replayed that one and it inspired me to buy this one)But this is just your standard choice game, if you get people to like you they are more likely to help you. There's really nothing more complicated about this than any other narrative choice game, yet the reviews made it seem like there was some new innovative system.Biggest complaint: Your choices barely matter. The story is basically the same no matter what you do, you just discover slightly different clues but get to the same ending. Or fall in a story trap door and die early. The endings feel so similar I lost interest in replaying the game. And I'm normally meticulous about finding every single ending. The first time through it felt like I made mistakes that eliminated possibilities/killed characters. But on subsequent play throughs, you discover that no matter what the same result (more or less) still occurs. That's okay in an RPG where there's actual game play but this is literally all about the choices, why are the choices so inconsequential? The different endings are mainly different points where your character can die early.2nd biggest complaint: The lead actress is the worst actor in the entire cast. Flat, bland, forgetable... why bother casting an American lead if its set in the UK? There's no story significance to her being American, it's as if she was just unable to do a British accent so they said "screw it, she's american!" I say this as an American, she is clearly the weakest actor in the show, the possible love interest male is MUCH more charismatic and interesting, he should've been the focus. The other women in the cast give very good performances but lead is bizarrely terrible in an otherwise strong cast.I'm amazed one of the reviews explicitly said none of the characters were one dimensional. There are literally numerous "bad guys" who don't have any lines, let alone a backstory! There are some characters with complexity but there are many that are pretty simple cardboard caricatures and archetypes. Overall, aside from the bad lead, the story just needs way more variety and consequence.

_childDocuments_.review: Ya know what ?  It doesn't suck.  That's more of a compliment than it initially seems.  Typically my reaction to most FMV game is a bit of a cringe:  horrible acting, suspect story, choices that aren't choices at all, etc.   But this raised the bar on all of those elements.  Acting was actually solid.  The story was at least interesting.  Your choices carry weight.  The only real negative is that the price ratio of content to length isn't great.   I was just getting warmed up and then it suddenly ended in spectacular fashion.   Not unlike most of my relationships.  I got about an hour and 30 minutes out of it.  And I was definitely not speed running.  There are 9 endings for replay value, so.. if you multiply it out that's roughly a dollar per ending.   Or in other terms, about 4 rolls of toilet paper. _childDocuments_.review: It's....acceptable. The acting is decent. The storyline and poor narrative kill it. There's no character development. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up in the golden era of cheesy 90s full-motion video (FMV) games, I do recommend this but with two caveats: That you don't mind that a run of this is very short and that it's designed to be played multiple times and also that you're into schlocky B-grade cinena.Wales Interactive is filling a very specific niche with their FMV titles and indeed, one I'm into. They call these interactive movies and they're not wrong. They have about as many game play mechanics as a Telltale game. You make choices, usually on a timer and those choices determine how events progress. Unlike some of their prior titles where despite your choices, the games often ended in a "similar but different" kind of way, the choices in this can wildly change the ending you get. I've seen two of the nine possible endings and they couldn't be more different, which is a good thing.The writing and the acting (more the direction to be honest) are not going to win any awards. FAR from it. Be prepared for a lot of super cheesy dialogue that's poorly delivered and plot holes and logical inconsistencies you could fly a jet through. The thing is, that's the way these games are and I enjoy them for that. If you don't, then this probably won't click with you. Half the fun of these is playing them on stream while my chat and I laugh at the absurdity of them. I was playing FMV games in the 90s during the dawning age of the CD-ROM and I have a soft spot for that kind of cheese. Like I said, they're filling a small niche here.A single run of The Complex will take you about 90 minutes but if you want to do multiple runs and get multiple endings and scenes (which as I said, are worth it), it will take you a fair bit longer. I really appreciate that unlike some of their previous games, you can skip scenes you've already watched, making subsequent playthroughs much faster. However, you can't skip back and forth through scenes to make different choices so you will be starting over multiple times.A major touted addition in The Complex over previous Wales titles is the relationship system. This is supposed to show you the impact of your choices on various attributes of your character's personality, as well as showing how your choices impact your standing with other people. This is supposed to be impacted by every choice you make. Personally, I found it pointless. It has almost no bearing on the story and at least in the two runs I did, the relationship status didn't lock me out of any choices. Characters that supposedly hated my guts still talked to me calmly and rationally and some characters (one of which is so tertiary, I don't even know why he's tracked) literally sat at the same relationship status for the entirety of both runs, except for the very end of my second run.Overall, I still enjoyed this and even if I hadn't received a press code, would have been happy with my purchase if I bought it. It's definitely not my favourite Wales FMV game. With what is out from them at time of writing, here's my order of preference:1. The Bunker (if you only play one Wales game, play this one)2. Late Shift3. The Complex4. The Shapeshifting DetectiveIf you're a fan of 90s FMV games, I do recommend all these but if you're not, I would start with The Bunker and see how you feel after that. I hope Wales can take things like the relationship system from this game and flesh it out more in future titles. Right now, this is still decent FMV cheese but I've played better, even in the modern era.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically an interactive B-movie. While an entertaining way to pass some time, I did have some problems with the storytelling and acting. Namely, the actor who plays the lead (Dr. Tenant) was so unbelievable as a doctor/scientist, it was laughable--I mean, she looks and talks like a 20-something model, so there's, um, no way she is some sort of leading expert in her field (do you KNOW how long it takes to get a Ph.D. or M.D.?). She's also been through a combat zone, and the actor looks like the worst thing that's happened to her is getting the wrong order at Starbucks. She's supposed to be a tough cookie, the grizzled scientist dedicated to her work above all else--they needed to get an older, more nuanced actor for that role (someone more like Sigourney Weaver in the Aliens series).  TBH, Tenant came across as quite unlikeable and ignorant--a naive scientist who has no clue that the technology she's creating could destroy the world. The way the plot is set up, we're supposed to empathize with her and be on her side (not so much). The actor who plays Rees gave a better performance--he was a more interesting character, as was Claire, the tough-talking "Kundaran." It would have been a stronger effort had the entire story been told from the perspective of Claire, if they wanted to subvert the whole "white savior" narrative. It also wasn't greeeeaaaat that the native peoples mostly served as victims or bad guys, secondary characters to the white heroes. Yeah, that could have been done better. My other issue  was simply on the level of galaxy-sized plot holes and lack of realism. Spoilery/plot thoughts:   Despite the laughable, B-movie elements, however, I enjoy the occasional interactive movie (check out Bandersnatch on Netflix, if you want another good example of this genre). It reminds me of the "choose your own adventure" books I used to read as a kid, and I like to have a break from my usual type of game, from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: Wales Interactive has been a boon for FMV games, though many are hits or misses. The Complex is an interesting game of espionage, romance, backstabbing and betrayal with quite a cast of interesting characters with an okay sort of storyline. In terms of it all, this is better than some of their other attempts but in hindsight of their latest fare, shows some of the early issues with the series, which has helped them improve over time.Good+ Interesting storyline with gripping moments.+ The main casts are quite good especially Reese and Amy with a middling effort by the other actors/actresses and some downright bad ones.+ Thankfully they put in a fast forward and skip feature for scenes which have been seen before, really helpful for completion runs.+ Dialogue is passable with the most interesting one being the two protagonists flirting.Cons- The choices given are not all that different and generally don't affect the outcome much with exception to the tie in with the relationship meter which determines the major outcomes, generally its quite linear.- Storyline is generally linear with not much repeatability after a few rounds. - There are some janky transition problems between some scenes and not as fluid as their newer games and quite apparent.- Some suspension of disbelief in terms of science, e.g. how come a heat flash powerful enough to turn bodies to ash doesn't affect a gun's condition and still allows it to fire afterwards.Overall its worth it on a discount and I'm generally give it a moderate score if i wasn't constrained with yes or no recommendations imposed by steam.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty decent FMV game. The story is pretty good and it's well shot. Impressively high production value for an indie game like this.I really enjoyed it on the first playthrough. My evaluation sank a bit after subsequent playthroughs because there are really only two endings, each with a few minor variations, plus one extra "hidden" ending. Most of your choices don't matter that much, and which of the two main endings you get comes down to a single choice near the end. I know it wouldn't be cheap to shoot a movie like this, so I can't fault the devs too much, but it still feels kind of disappointing.Anyway, even if most of your choices don't matter that much, it's still an enjoyable experience. The choices are smooth and give the player enough time to decide while keeping the movie naturally flowing. Choices do usually lead to small variations in scenes, and the interactivity makes for a more immersive experience than a regular movie. Also, you can turn off the timer for decisions in the settings if you want, but I think it adds to the experience because the time pressure provides a sense of urgency and forces you to think quickly.Overall, good game. Although I must say that I don't particularly like Amy, the protagonist. She just seems bland and lacking in personality. The other characters are fine.

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is a new FMV “game“ in the likes of Late Shift, that puts us in the position of a young scientist trapped in a lab fighting a new virus and finding out if there is something more to it all. You are Amy Tenant a scientist researching on dangerous nanocells in a modern lab facility and find yourself locked in the lab with dangerous intruders and the even more dangerous nanocells with hints of spies, terrorists, an old romance and betrayal in the air. I personally liked the story and found it to be very entertaining. The actors were doing a good job and were in no way campy like in the older FMV games. The settings seemed realistic to me. There is an office like setting, outdoor setting and of course the lab complex. I can really judge the lab as I am not a professional scientist, but to me it looked good and did not break the immersion or looked obviously like a movie set. Even though it is an all-around good game, I somehow did not manage to get emotionally involved as I did in games like “The Last of us”. Maybe it was due to the playtime being extremely short (I played around 2.5 hours and I did idle a bit)? A really good movie like game. I don’t know how to rate this. It was goodHonestly, there is not a lot gameplay. It is really a movie where at various points in the game (around 10 or less) you have to make important or not so important decision that may change the ending, not the course of the game, mind you.Music:None whatsoever. Only normal sound and the voice of the voice actorsIf you can enjoy a game that is like a movie with not much gameplay going on, for a price of around 12 USD, but a well told story and a playtime of around 2 hours for one playthrough, then this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I will avoid specifically mentioning any big spoilers, but as some of the problems I had were in regards to the games logic, I will vaguely address some plot points.Overall it was well acted, (shout out to Katie Kat from Letterkenny) and it was polished and well produced, (however, I immediately refused to accept the obvious "love interest", nothing against the actor but it was a poorly written stock character who me and my girlfriend who watched along with me had zero motivation or curiosity about) my issue is truly with the writing.  For a video "choose your own adventure" I found that, at least during my play through, my choices had very little effect.  While I understand that writers have to introduce contrivances to manage exponentially branching story lines from expanding exponentially and "trim the tree" so to speak, with the exception of one end game decision, it felt like nearly every decision I made was immediately undone.  Perhaps I'm just a bad decision maker, but it didn't inspire me to replay the experience. An example of this concept well-done would be "Bandersnatch" on Netflix, where you could die, kill off prominent characters early, fail early and start over, etc.Even worse, there were times I wish the story gave me choices but didn't, the choices it gave me didn't seem to be motivated by human logic, and some of the main friction points of the story just didn't make sense (this massive biotech company doesn't have an internal security force that can handle three armed men?  Also, when it comes to a potentially deadly pathogen, I'm sure the British government or the London police would be happy to help.)

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure, I'm reviewing this game after one playthrough so I can't comment too much on how much your dialogue choices impact the game, though I do have some insight on that that I'll comment on at the end.  One complete run through took me a little over an hour so if you're thinking of picking this up I'd position it in your mind as buying a movie.  Maybe a movie that you'll want to watch 2 or 3 times, but you're probably not going to get Skyrim level playtime out of something like this.As a choose-your-own-adventure type movie I was happy with it.  The production values are right up there with what you might see in a movie on the sci-fi channel... I'd definitely put it at "Sharknado" level, at least, with better acting.  I really thought the actors in this were very good and I liked the leading lady a lot.  The writing has plenty of eye roll moments, of course.  First there's the obvious one.  Like... sure.  One of the most brilliant pioneers in medical nano-technology looks to be about 20 years old and oh... she first spent many years helping victims in a war zone.   Lord knows when she actually found time to attend medical school and do a residency.  Toss in a "oh, this other young, brilliant but mercurial doctor who we tolerate because he's The Best took a few years off from doctoring and in his spare time became a brilliant computer hacker while also learning to skydive."  Hacking into computer systems, as usual, involves Typing Extremely Fast while Random Nonsense Computer Code scrolls down the screen at breakneck speed.  But this is hardly the first time we've been asked to swallow stuff like this, I see it every night on network TV.  And this story, at least, is as good a story as any of that.  And you get to personalize this one.As I was going through it I really wondered how much of an impact my choices were actually making, I was under no illusion that I was going to fundamentally change the story arc.  I figured my picks would lead to minor cosmetic changes to the story at best.  So I was surprised at the end when the game evaluated my performance, gave me a rating, and while not giving anything away showed me how much I didn't get to see.  And it's intrigued me enough that I'm sure I will play through this again at some point.  So for what this is and what it claims to be, I think it does it very well.  Definitely better than I expected going in.

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I encounter another choose your own adventure game, be it The Walking Dead, She Sees Red, Late Shift, etc, I always look out for a potential readable message in the totality of the choices. The Walking Dead season one, for instance, almost justified its false choices as a commentary about how the player isn't the centre of the universe and can be overruled and otherwise ineffectual. That was until it started cosmically shifting pieces on the board for dramatisation purposes - cause and effect be damned. The Complex, to it's credit, remains consistent. A big plus in my FMV enthusiast book. That you can see logical cause and effect is largely what makes replaying interactive films so interesting. You can enjoy the intertextual narratives told over multiple playthroughs and the totality of the choices. The player is god - often a restricted to branching, binary choice-selecting god, but a god nonetheless.The Complex's timeline divergences hinge almost entirely on how you treat characters in the sum of its binary choices. A summary screen neatly digests your character's personality in a nutshell. It's neat, if unambitious in its scope. Most endings are swung by final choices alone. The rest of the choices are mostly relegated to mere narrative colour. Given some largely copy-and-paste endings, you could also safely say it has half the number it boasts. Character relationships fundamentally aren't the most interesting of story splits.  Its writing and acting credits speak for themselves. VFX elements betray its budget, but it's undeniably striking in its look, and set/wardrobe design. The plot doesn't sparkle, but with many a revelation up its sleeve it entertains. It's a very confident show. It's also fully featured with all the essential FMV settings you could want - skipping scenes is here. One of unfurling motives, various gun-toting sides, and sci-fi underground labs rather than full-on virus-that-shall-not-be-named. It's entertaining, if not massively affecting outside a few moments. If one thing truly works, it's the relationship of the two main characters. Adversity forcing them to consider their relationship hits all the right emotional chords. It also highlights the issue with any interactive film. Certain moments, like one that arises for the two towards the end, that arise from specific strings of decisions just feel dramatically right for a film. To not see a dramatically optimal route isn't to gain, but lose something for using an interactive medium. Equally, engineering an alternative moment that's equally impactful to avoid an optimal route is nigh on impossible. Such moments are impactful because of the natural set-up they're given. An alternative leveraging the same set-up would either be too similar or not land. FMV games have to perforce play a balancing act between their system complexity and having a budget-friendly, logistically possible shoot. You can always see the flowchart of the branching narrative in your mind's eye because it had to be simple enough that this 200 scene behemoth could be seen through. It robs scenes, endings and branching of significant differences. It's largely not it's fault, but it's undeniable that multiple playthroughs outside of a few standout moments were a letdown for this reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: THIS REVIEW DOES NOT CONTAIN ANY SPOILERSThe Complex is a game where you control a scientist, Amy, dealing with a deadly nanovirus, which has infected one of your interns. At multiple points, you make choices which can eitherA) Affect the next 1-3 scenes of the story, before taking you back to a central point you'd always end up atB) Increase/decrease your relationship with a certain character, which doesn't make a massive differenceC) Get you a shiny achievementThe Complex seems a bit interesting at first. Until you start exploring the game after your first playthrough to explore more endings.The game boasts 8 endings and a secret ending. The normal 8 endings can be easily split into 2 groups of 4, with very little differences between each other in each group. Just slight variations of your final choice with barely any effect on the ending (Despite each one of these endings having a different name).As for the secret ending, it's not really that secret. You find it a good 3 minutes into the game after your first playthrough and it's not as interesting as it might sound (It's not like this hidden easter egg that's entertaining. In fact, the ending itself doesn't even make that much sense.)As for the endings themselves, they don't particularly go into a lot of detail as a result of your actions. Just a 5-10 second boring scene with at most 1 or 2 lines of dialogue before ending.So, this game is not satisfactory in its conclusions. What about the journey?Well, I won't lie to you. I have played this game for 4 hours in total and I have 100%'d the achievements and seen 99% of the game's content. And a good part of that 4 hours was grinding to see the last remaining scenes, the last 5 which I gave up on, on account of these scenes will have made barely any difference. Like the endings, a lot of the 191 scenes this game boasts can be grouped into clunks of scenes with barely any difference.For example, there's a scene where you grab a girl's arm to extract some blood.There are 2 scenes for this. One - which she willingly gives it to you. The other - which she holds back for a bit because of her distrust for you, before giving it to you anyways. These are not 2 separate, distinct scenes, yet the game treats it as such. This is all before the game brings you back to a point in the story where the distinction between those 2 scenes didn't, at all, matter.I understand parts of games are re-used and for any other game, this would be fine but for a game that tells you choices absolutely do matter, the story is very linear.There's about one point in the story 85% of the way in where you make a choice that massively changes the remaining 15% but that's about the only point your choice truly matters. All other choices either don't matter or will take you on a short meaningless variation before leaving you right back to the main story that you'd get to, no matter what you picked.What about the character relationships? If this is a game about choices, surely how you treat people and those you make friends/enemies should matter, right?Not really.There are 2 characters out of the 9 who actually have some sort of effect, depending on your relationship with them. And, that's only really a thing because you're basically stuck with them for most of the story.There's another 2 characters out of the 9 who you will only see at the beginning of the game. That's it. Yet, they are somehow important enough to be considered a character on your relationship list?There's 1 other character who may give you a bit of extra info in 1 scene depending on your relationship with her. But, not only does your relationship not matter for the rest of the game, but the info she does give you doesn't even change the story. Like, at all.As for the other 4 characters? Don't bother. It doesn't matter how positive or negative your relationship status is with them, it literally changes nothing in the story. Not how they act toward you, and certainly not how things play out.Tack on the other 2 characters that you only interact with at the beginning of the game and that's , no matter what terms you are on with them. A majority of your relationship slots taken up for no reason, other than to pad out the game? Make your choices seem more important than they are? I don't know.Speaking of numbers, the game does provide stats on how intelligent/brave/whatever your choices were. But, honestly, I have paid this no mind whatsoever. It doesn't affect the game or the story. If you're into that sort of thing, fair play but honestly, you'd probably get more enjoyment from an online personality quiz (without spending a penny).As for the story itself, it's kind of okay but not particularly exciting. You'd get more excitement out of a movie. The plot has you hooked for maybe 20 minutes? But, beyond that, suspense is shoddy, certain parts become a bit predictable and characters that should be important (Such as, y'know, the board of CEOs you're securing funding from or the owner of the whole building) may as well be removed from the game entirely. They basically matter very little to not at all.The game's acting is atrocious and the characters are not at all interesting. I'd say the 2 characters you stick around with for most of the game do a pretty decent job at acting and have some fairly witty and/or interesting interactions but beyond that, my 10-year old cousin could do a better job at acting. The main character you play, even at the most crucial and hard-hitting moments, just carries this bland aura that I just can't get on board with. Like, at all.All in all, this game is absolutely not worth your money. Stay away from this game, . If it were free, I'd suggest maybe grab it if you had a few hours to kill. But, even that's a big if. There are far more entertaining games, movies and fusions of the two out there which are a better use of your time. and  (on Netflix) play with the idea this game is trying for extremely better, have a lot more interesting content (even beyond your first playthrough), perform brilliantly in the meta-realm (Bandersnatch, for example, having your choices on your first playthrough affecting future playthroughs and DBH mapping out every choice you've ever made on a clear map) and as it currently stands, a month's subscription to Netflix is already cheaper than this game (Alongside the fact you get a lot of other movies + TV shows to watch alongside it).The only positive thing I can commend the game for is the ability to auto-skip scenes you have already seen after your first playthrough. This was pretty important to allow me to explore other 'endings'.But, honestly, as you probably already realise - This should be expected in a game like this so the bar's just below the floor, at this point.I usually like playing Devil's Advocate so with other games I don't recommend, I can see the appeal to others, even if I hate the game with all my heart. But, with this game's price, replayability, empty mechanics and lack of content, there is .This game is basically a movie but it even fails at that. Like, if this were in the cinema, I would not go and spend money to watch it. If it were on TV, it would be torn to shreds by reviewers and fans alike.Positive reviews are currently ranging between 77-81%: In an ideal and honest world, this value would be majorly low. I'm talking < 30-40%. Which makes me think either the reviews have been artificially pumped or people just don't expect much from video games anymore.I repeat, for the final time:

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing wrong with the UI, or even the choices that you're offered in this science-fiction thriller. The flaw is more fundamental than that. It just has terrible characters.First of all there is a fundamental difference between a sci-fi story and a horror story. In horror, morally corrupt characters are punished for doing "sinful" things while the final character, who is somehow morally superior, survives by overcoming their fear. In sci-fi, people overcome a problem because they are competent and intelligent, and if people die, it is usually because they didn't listen to the scientists. Sci-fi horror is usually a blend of these two concepts, where the sin is not listening to the science. A thriller is just a story that starts with a dead body and has lots of twists.While The Complex manages to nail the thriller aspect, it fails at both horror and sci-fi. The scientists make stupid emotional choices and hardly use their decades of knowledge to solve problems. One character has magically gone from being an epidemiologist to being a hacker. And the plot is entirely lacking in moral nuance. The "bad" guys face no negative consequences for either amorality or bad science. I was kind of kept in it by the possibility of making a choice that would stop the train from derailing, but I never felt like there was actually a choice that truly used either cleverness or morality to assert some sort of complex outcome that would have changed the character's perspective.Consider the first choice you make in the game. Do you:A. Save a dude who was playing soccerB. Save a pregnant woman who might also be a freedom fighterThis is not a choice. There is no moral quandary. There is not even an intellect vs. emotional choice here. A better one would have been saving the leader of the opposition of a tyrannical country, or saving a CHILD who had been playing soccer, with his family waiting for good news outside the tent. The Complex has a good setup for storytelling, but somehow passes right by it without blinking.If you like a Patterson story, though--a pure thriller, and many people do like that enormously for good reason--then this is a good story. It's up there with The Zoo, where people in labcoats make decisions any one of us could make without even getting a degree or building a global business. It's not my thing, but if that is something you enjoy then don't be intimidated by the sci-fi/outbreak presentation, this is comfortably mainstream and not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: London is under siege. A major bio-weapon attack casts a heavy shadow. Two experts in the Nanocell Technology find themselves trapped into a laboratory where assassins have just infiltrated and with time and air running out. Their only option is to take some hard decisions. But soon, those decisions will come back to haunt them. An interactive sci-fi thriller movie where you must ponder each and every decisions. A nice piece to kill some time, it is worth buying if on sale (half the price-tag would be decent). - This review is a personal opinion. Try the game for yourself.- Game was played on max graphics setting and ultrawide resolution.- Do not expect an epic story, it is a rather short and simple novel and the FX are not top CGI.- At the end of each playthrough, you get a Personality Score based on five markers of personality.- Choices are timed but you have the Pause Choices option so you get to think enough what to do, an option that was also designed to help improve audience participation during live streams for content creators.- The game is starring Kate Dickie (Game of Thrones, The Witch, Prometheus), Michelle Mylett (Letterkenny, Bad Blood,  El Camino Christmas) and Al Weaver (Grantchester, Colette).- Yes, there also is a 2020 full movie version based on this game, named "The Complex: Lockdown".- A cinematic interactive dark narrative with 8 different endings that provide some degree of replayability.- A decent quality of movie production and atmospheric sound effects.- All relationship status and personality traits evolve real-time, based on your interactions and decisions.- For a sci-fi movie, it is nice depiction of a near-future sci-fi setting, with attention to visual detail and interesting color composition.- Making different decisions may lead to some interesting plot twists.- An unlockable hidden event.- No ultrawide support at all. Given that the game is completely cinematic, it is a disappointment to see it all filmed in 16:9 and pillarboxed.- At some points, the story felt like a cheap James Bond novel, less satisfying and intriguing.- The product is rather short. You can play all 8 endings in a few hours.- No manual save, but you can let the game paused on choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Wales Interactive games are becoming a staple in my library.  They're unique and fun, and sort of like playable B-movies, and one thing do especially well is choose locations.  Wherever they film is always perfect for the story.  Great settings really set the stage for the narrative.The characters were likeable and relatable, and I really felt the environments.  Also the danger factor. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's a B movie about nanocells, terrorists, and human experiments in poor countries, as staple as they come. But the interactive aspect does help a lot! I would get very bored watching this movie, but I was quite engaged throughout the game. So engaged, actually, that after the first blind playthrough I used a guide and got all achievements, i.e., watched all endings. _childDocuments_.review: I usually enjoy games like this, but I had a lot of gripes with this one.  It seems like almost no research was done into any of the subject matter before they started filming.  I understand that this is sci-fi, but realism is the basis for any believable story.  The general incompetence of the characters and the general disregard for lab/IT/medical practices was very distracting.  Whenever creating a story like this, it is essential to have someone who works in a lab, the medical field, plumbing, computers, or anything relevant to advise you.  So many little details could have easily been changed to make this a very engaging story.  The game mechanics, camera work, lighting, acting, and other technical aspects were well done, and this game had the potential to be very good.  That being said, I can't really recommend this game as much more than a "so bad it's funny" experience.  It could have been so much more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: I would call The Complex an interactive B-movie.The technical aspects of filming is done well and the setting is good and well set up for success, but the acting is pretty cringe at times and the emotion that the actors should express doesn't always fully come through the screen. The main character was also not very believable as a doctor/scientist and neither as someone who has worked on a battlefield. It felt like she was a deer caught in headlights at most times and her personality was quite weak.The actor who plays Rees gave a somewhat better performance, he was a more interesting character and was also great comical relief. Claire, the tough-talking "Kindaran" was also a very interesting character and she was probably my favorite. It would have been a stronger effort had the entire story been told from the perspective of Claire.Honestly speaking, I think this was a decent FMV game and an attempt was made for an interesting story, BUT I don't think I will recommend this game, since there are other way better FMV games out there. Still, if you do decide to play the game, definitely don't get it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually all for these choice based games and the premise of this game was up my ally. Unfortunately, I have to say that it was a dud! The story line was intriguing but the characters were never fully developed. Worse of all, the main character was the worst actor I have seen in a while, it's like they picked her for her looks Not for her acting skills. With a game like this, Acting is what counts NOT looks! This could have been a great game, but it seems like the developers hurried this along hoping to make a quick buck!
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Really professionally produced, the sets, props, prosthetics and effects were really high budget. Loved Al Weaver as Rees, his acting was great. Really enjoyed his characters witty humour too. The story was interesting and there were a couple of twists that caught me by surprise. There are 9 different endings and several different versions of scenes that are affected by how high your relationship is with certain characters which is really cool. And once you've finished the game once you can skip through scenes you've already seen to make trying out the other endings quicker which I appreciated.Cons: Writing was slightly cheesy/cliche at times. Some of the actors, a few of the minor characters, were not very good/believable. As with most choice based games there were a couple of choices where the prompts didn't fully convey what the character would do if you chose them. For example one of the choices I clicked said "F*** you (characters name here)" so I clicked it thinking I was just gonna swear at them, and then I shot them. Choice based games are my absolute favourite genre and all in all, I enjoyed myself a lot with this one - 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: We are talking about a modern pandemic topic here. _childDocuments_.review: The Complex is not a game in its usual sense, it's an interactive movie with lots of decisions to make - unfortunately a bad one. If you like the story baseline in games from Quantic Games like Detroit: Become Human, Heavy Rain or Beyond Two Souls, or if you enjoyed intreactive movies like Late Shift, you might like The Complex, too. But I doubt it, because the aforementioned tend to be classy stories - this one doesn't even qualify as a B movie, imho.+Nice score+Your choices do matter in that sense, that you will see scenes and different developments according to your decisions-it's debatable, whether this is a movie or a game; and if it's not the latter, is it worth the money? I would argue: No, no matter the category!-the actors and actresses are mediocre at best, except for Clare, who does a good job and is believable-the dialgue is abysmal! And I mean ABYSMAL!!-you can tell the cut between different scenes due to a small portion, where the sound is muted for a short period of time; it's nothing too bad, but takes away from the immersiveness heavily-there are several plot holes, that show how bad the writing is (you'll see, when you "play")Rating for gamers: Rating for everybody else: The Complex tries to be an interactive sci-fi-y thriller movie, that lets you build your own story. But due to its many, many flaws it is nothing but a disgrace for the gaming and movie industry, that is not worth a penny of anybody's money; so stay away!

_childDocuments_.review: I have only watched a couple of these interactive movies and I really enjoyed this interactive movie. None of the other movies I have watched have appealed to me to watch it again and again. You do have to play through at least 9 times in order to get all the endings. I ended up having to play through it a couple of more times to get my chooses correct, but it does have a tab feature that allows you to skip through the scenes you have already watched. It did take about 1 1/2 hours to get through the first play through but that is an average movie length. The thing is though, it didn't feel like an hour and a half, I was that engaged in the movie. I have over 5 hours of play time on this movie and when I am not sitting here going "that was 5 hours I will never get back" than it was engaging and worth the time I spent discovering the different scenes and endings. It was a nice change of pace compared to the other games I play. It was a movie that your decisions drive the different scenes. Even though I have completed all the achievements and found all the endings, it does appeal to me to watch it again and to see what other decision combinations I can use to see additional scenes. _childDocuments_.review: More cinematic than their other fare, but fewer variances except for the endings.Wow, this team has upped its game.  I've played most of the games from Wales Interactive, and I can say that this one is up there in terms of the production value and ambition.  There are huge set pieces, wide panning shots, many intricate costumes, and a complex, winding story line.  I was amazed the entire time at how truly huge their sets either were or appeared to be, from a wide shot of tents near the ocean at the beginning to large offices, a huge lab, and a gigantic vacuumed security tunnel.  Even the acting was cinematic in nature, making for a movie-like experience in a choice-based game.I can't say enough about the sets and the costumes.  Whoever designed those went all out.  I've never seen anything like it in an FMV game.  Heck, it likely outperforms many TV shows and some low-budget movies.  There are multiple hazmat suits and lab uniforms used.  Other than a small glow for the actors standing in front of the comm screen in the lab, I didn't see where the CGI began and the real environments ended (and there had to be some CGI because at least one of those sets was impossibly large).  Even the unsung effects like the laser beam, the smoke, the virtual keyboard, and the video screens were very nice.  Well done overall in that regard--everything felt very, very real (hard to do in high-def).The acting was fine.  I know people are often critical because they can't afford Meryl Streep, but I always think they do a good job.  There are some actors from other games, like the bartender from Mia and the Dragon Princess, who make appearances.  As usual, they get an attractive female lead who really drives the show forward with screen presence as well as a male comedy relief who can turn to drama on a dime.  They gave the male lead a lot of depth, from having panic attacks from the stress of his field to having a fondness for TV and movie references (he referenced The Office, Jurassic Park, and Speed that I noticed).  The initial antagonist has a lot of depth as well, as you learn about her backstory and motivation throughout.  The other antagonists don't get a ton of development, but it's because they're not in most of the scenes and so they can't do much with them.As for the plot, I really enjoyed it.  Effectively, there's a lot of drama involving nanotechnology's double-edged sword of being either life-saving or life-ending.  Of course, there's the typical inclusion of monetary vs. societal motivation, though I love how most characters had mixed motivations so there weren't too many mustache-twirling evil-for-the-sake-of-being-evil characters.  They really did a fantastic job with the multiple endings--it wasn't like many of these where you either win or lose.  Instead, there are many things happening, from various people living or dying to various consequences from how the nanotech is handled via your actions.  In fact, the "best" ending from my perspective was one of the seemingly "bad" endings...what a bold choice on the part of the creators.  No obvious perfect-mediocre-bad/evil endings here.The thing I think is most noteworthy about the gameplay is how they tweaked their typical formula.  Unlike the I Saw Black Clouds approach where they had hundreds of decisions with hundreds of variations of scenes, they had fewer than 200 in this one.  I think this improved a lot, from having almost no unskippable scenes that were near-identical to previously viewed ones upon replay to having scenes connect more seamlessly without cop-out moments where people just mysteriously leave to keep continuity.  However, it did make many of the choices have minimal impact on the story, which is the trade-off of that decision.  I think just a few additional weightier options throughout would've been fantastic, but otherwise I felt that it was an improvement over the more options with lesser quality of others.  The weighty decisions are all at the end, which means that to get all 9 endings, I basically just tabbed through the whole game until the last 5 or so decisions to complete the achievements--again, positive because it's a time-saver, but it does mean that more decisions don't affect much than other games by Wales.Overall, I enjoyed playing it and probably put it in my top 5 of the games by these folks.  I'm impressed with what they did here scene-wise.  Amazing.  The variety of endings were also strong, with very, very different things happening to all of the characters based on your choices.  I enjoy the kind of actors they get for these and thing the story was beefier than similar games.  If you like the other games of this type, I think this is one of the better ones.  And, as per usual, I have to applaud them for just delivering a story that engages you and makes you think without filling it with sex/drugs/sociopolitical commentary that most TV shows and movies seem to do these days.  The risk/reward of bioengineering that they explore here is much more interesting and, while not analyzed heavily per se, they show instead of tell by having the various endings play out for you to consider.  Very well done.

_childDocuments_.review: Waste of even the 4.4 hours it took to 100%.  Entertaining to play with with family/friends because they feel like they're part of the process; however, as a game, most options lead to very slightly different cut sequences that don't matter and aren't worth revisiting. Decisions are so mundane they shouldn't matter as much as they do and I felt ripped off after making the seemingly most intelligent decisions. Aside from alternate endings based on very mundane (not just seemingly mundane) decisions, there's no real substance to your decisions.  It's profoundly unrealistic and there are no real options to actually "play the game." You can't choose to lie, stay silent, use items, explore alternate plans, or formulate your own escape plan by tricking other characters.  All in all, it could've been a lot better and you can actually see where certain parts were probably cut (where decisions should have been and just weren't).   I would've liked the option to kill off Rees early and investigate who the mole was really myself aside from it being handed to me within the first minute of arriving at the lab.  ...or at the least have some kind of impact on the escape options based on exploration or choosing to explore rather than having conversations, formulate a real escape plan by either staying silent or lying to other characters, etc. It just seems like most decisions lack intelligence.  Deception and real negotiation tactics would've been the way out.  Why isn't there an option to side with Natalie?  Why isn't there an option to pretend to side with Natalie then stab her in the back a week later? Why isn't there an option to cut a deal with Parker or Emily to stab Natalie in back?   It looks like those options could've/should've been there but just weren't.  Yes the release would've taken considerably longer and cost more; however, that's the difference between another "meh" game and a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is an interactive cinematic thriller that immerses players in a gripping story filled with suspense and moral dilemmas. Set in a high-tech laboratory, players take on the role of Dr. Amy Tennant, who finds herself trapped in a crisis that forces her to make difficult decisions affecting both her fate and those around her.What I Liked:Engaging Storytelling: The narrative is well-crafted, with twists and turns that keep you on the edge of your seat. The blend of science fiction and psychological thriller elements creates a captivating atmosphere.High-Quality Production: The game features impressive production values, including excellent cinematography, strong voice acting, and realistic character animations. This cinematic approach enhances immersion and draws players into the story.Meaningful Choices: The choices you make throughout the game significantly impact the story's outcome, leading to multiple endings. This encourages replayability, as players can explore different paths and outcomes based on their decisions.Atmospheric Setting: The setting is intriguing and well-designed, creating a tense and claustrophobic environment that enhances the game's suspense. The use of technology and ethical dilemmas adds depth to the story.What I Disliked:Pacing Issues: At times, the pacing can feel uneven, with some sections dragging on while others rush through critical moments. This can disrupt the flow of the story and affect immersion.Limited Gameplay Mechanics: The gameplay is primarily focused on making choices and watching the story unfold, which may not appeal to those looking for more traditional gameplay mechanics or action sequences.Character Depth: While the characters are interesting, some could benefit from deeper development. A few side characters feel underexplored, which may leave players wanting more from their backstories.Recommendation:Overall, I recommend The Complex to fans of interactive storytelling and cinematic experiences. Its engaging narrative, high production quality, and meaningful choices create a compelling experience that keeps you invested. While it has some pacing issues and limited gameplay mechanics, the emotional weight of your decisions and the atmosphere of suspense make it a worthwhile play. If you enjoy narrative-driven games that challenge your moral compass, The Complex is definitely worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: Decent sci-fi story in this FMV with likable characters. Fairly short at around 1.5 hours for your first playthrough. Thankfully you can skip previously viewed choices if you want to see all endings.My total playtime for 100% was 3.1 hours.The only other FMVs I have played are the Tex Murphy series 25 years ago. The Complex cannot compare to the ‘more complex’ Tex Murphy series which mixes live action and adventure gameplay, but if you fancy a quick and thrilling interactive movie experience it’s worth picking The Complex when discounted.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: 'The Complex' is an impressive interactive sci-fi thriller from the publishers of 'Late Shift' and 'The Bunker.' Set in the aftermath of a major bio-weapon attack on London, you take on the role of one of two scientists trapped in a locked-down laboratory, racing against time and a dwindling air supply. The game's standout feature is its branching narrative, where your choices and interactions with other characters lead to one of eight suspenseful endings. The immersive storyline and the high-stakes decisions make 'The Complex' a shining example of the potential of interactive gaming. This game is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the mediocre ratings I didn't have high expectations, but I quite enjoyed my first play-through. The acting is mostly good and you have a few interesting decisions to make. The ending I got (the promise) was a little weird, but given my choices, the way it was resolved was probably acceptable.Play time was ~90 minutes, so pretty much in line with your average movie.Given that I've seen less than 50% of the scenes and there are nine different endings, I'm quite happy with my purchase and will likely revisit it from time to time.

_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: Like many reviews before this state, it's more a movie than a game. Both parts are nicely done. As you progress through the movie, you get to make choices. Although there is not a hugh amount of choices to be made, they all have a effect on how the story continues. This means that if you'd go for a second, third or fourth playthrough, you get to see new scenes with sometimes other choices. That are up to nine different outcomes! Don't be affraid that a replay might get boring, as you see some scenes over and over. After the first playthrough, you can skip any unlocked scenes while you go through it again.All with all i would recommend this, if it is your genre.

_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: The Complex is an interactive sci-fi thriller which I enjoyed playing through. _childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: Very short, but enjoyable interactive movie. _childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: I like FMV games and this is one of the better ones. The acting is good, the video is clean, the props are realistic. The stats you get showing your friendships and personality are also interesting but it's really unclear what they effect. If you're okay with being a bit at the whims of the story telling and not understanding what's going on under the hood then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: The whole game takes about 2 hours to complete, and it was a shore.I got this because I liked Contradiction, and The Complex seems to promise something on the same lines, but it doesn't deliver.Contradiction is a grounded, relatable and compelling story, that gets you in the shoes of the protagonist, while this is a very cheap and simplistic SciFi full of plot wholes, bad writing and such bad acting that some characters make me cringe.Mind you that all this "positivity" is looking at the whole thing as a movie, as a game it's just terrible. All relevant aspects are out of control, scenes between interactions are huge and the choices don't carry much weight.I'm a fan of SciFi, even some of the worst I still find entertaining. I love Aventure/Point and Click games, even when they are not great. Still, this is really, really bad. No idea why people recommend, but maybe there are better scenes in options I didn't take? Metacritic says 62, which still feels too high to me.I hope the two leads get better projects in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: My first FMV and gosh it's a good one!Well acted, great settings and environment. Takes itself seriously. Good story with some interesting moral choices. _childDocuments_.name: The Complex

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: This is not a game. It is an interactive film that is based on relatively few player A/B choices. Relatively few choices doesn't mean that there are really very few choices. According to the game, I made 83 choices in my playthrough. However it felt more like 15. Choices are usually far apart, which in for a film is fine.The issue I have is mainly with the vast amount of plotholes, illogical behaviour of the characters and the generally unrealistic setting.I realise that the budget for this kind of thing isn't a that of a Hollywood movie, but one could work around that.*spoilers ahead*The basic assumption is a nanobot cure for everything - not a new idea but okay, it works.But why is there only one sample and why can't this sample be replicated? Why are people trying to steal a very clearly unfinished product anyway? Multi-million funding round at the beginning but the 4 year(?) old Complex looks decades old from the outside.Also, why is there water in the basement of a brand new lab?Other issues I have are too numerous to list comprehensively, but include:A biolab with a vaccum chamber outside, but no biuosecurity measures inside.A lab without even a first aid kit. Hello, health & safety?A doctor who's not immediately helping a wounded colleague.A scientist who doesn't know what chemicals are in the lab that she's worked in for 4 years.A multi-million dollar operation with 7 employees and a few interns?A top secret lab but no security and no response team? (Until the bad guys are all the way in).An "Oxygen Tank" in the air vent of the size that would last for about 10 seconds for a whole room.Rees suddenly has a lethal pathogen?A toilet with a deep tunnel to the subway?A toilet explosion with just a chunk of potassium hydroxide? What would that explode with a boom anyway?An "architect" that behaves like a dandy.Why does security not shoot her immediately when they face her in the basement?At the end, MI6 probably does not arrest people openly, they'd send the police.
