_childDocuments_.review: Though it wears its overly obvious influences on its sleeve, Eldest Souls is an incredibly satisfying boss rush that still manages to set itself apart. Its brilliant combat is complimented by a smart skill system and some incredible pixel art. Designed with replayability in mind, it’s a little bit of a bummer that its impressive customization doesn’t really blossom until partway into your first playthrough. But one thing that’s there from the start is that feeling of immense glory after every hard-earned victory: Ceremoniously slumping onto the living room floor, clutching the carpet for dear life with one hand while exhaustedly flipping off the television with the other.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: There are casual, fun games that leave you feeling relaxed after playing them. Eldest souls is not amongst them. It’s been a long time since I have raged at a game, swearing at the screen and wanting to throw my controller through it, but Eldest Souls invokes that. Having finished it, I now have that stress free feeling, as I know I don’t have to endure that again. If you are into punishing pixel art or boss rush games that are totally unforgiving, then Eldest Souls is for you. The story starts out really well, and describes a world where gods and humans lived aside each other in harmony. The old gods are corrupted by one of their kind, and start a war and enslave humanity. On the brink after 100’s of years of servitude humanity fights back and imprisons the gods in the sacred walls of the Citadel, a fortress to house the gods where they can be contained not only from humanity, but each other, watched over by a standing army. The peace doesn’t last, and you are sent to reinforce the standing army and slay the gods, who have unleased another wave of ruin upon the land. The story briefly expands during the game as you meet a few surviving NPC’s or read logbooks, notes and piece the scrapes of information together that you find, but it’s fairly sparse. I did like that some choices that you make change the ending (all rewards come at a cost), and even then it’s not clear who exactly you are serving. This is a game for those who want to be punished for misdeeds in their previous lives. It’s all about timing, and is totally unforgiving as there are no invulnerability frames when you get hit by an attack, mistiming means you can have multiple attacks hit you in rapid succession, all dealing damage (which is usually fatal). Some boss attacks can hit for 70% of your life in one hit, life steal is really low (which is the only way to recover health during a fight), and there aren’t any options to increase your health pool or increase the amount of dashes you have to escape attacks.Each boss attacks differently and I feel some are really there to teach you have to play the game. You only have a very basic tutorial, and while you can somewhat flounder against the first 2 bosses, Eos the likely third boss (the game lets you wander the keep and pick who you want to fight at this point) is the boss that actually makes you learn the game mechanics and experiment, if you don’t just rage quit. The game actually feels harder to play at the beginning, as you have less mechanisms and upgrades to help you through certain boss fights. Each defeated boss drops a shard that can be slotted into either an active ability, enhance a dash or charge attack with an effect, or add an effect to your skill tree.  Each shard is unique and does a different effects depending on where you place it, giving you a large amount of wriggle room in how you setup your character. Some of the gained abilities actively damage you when used, so again care needs to be taken when using them.The games 3 skills trees are really well designed, with Windslide being focused on mobility and passive DPS, Berserker Slash being straight up high DPS, and Counter focusing on defending and technical play. They all play really differently, and what you have selected can drastically change how a fight plays out. I finished 4 bosses with Windslide, before switching over berserker slash and found my enjoyment increased substantially. You won’t receive enough skill point in one run, so the game encourages multiple play throughs if you feel like enduring the suffering a bit more.The Pixel art really works for the game. While the keep is ruined the artwork does a great job of invoking the idea that it must have been majestic, before it was corrupted from within. The game is fair in that nothing is hidden in the environment, items of importance shine to grab your attention, though its up to you to try and investigate what they might be used for. You somewhat channel the essence of Guts from Berserk (but with a red cloak), wielding a weapon that’s like giant hunk of steel in a nod to the series.Each boss is fairly unique not only in its attack sequence(s), but in appearance. Each of the attacks are telegraphed, so if you are quick (and I mean really quick), and can remember each of the bosses attacks you have a good chance of preparing to either rush in to attack or get ready to dodge. While the game is totally unforgiving and absolutely punishes mistakes, there aren’t any cheap invisible attacks that other games love so much. After beating a boss, the environment changes and some other areas can open up for exploration. The game doesn’t support many options for graphics, but what it does works well. you aren’t going to be playing this on anything higher than 1080pThe music fixes the game perfectly. There’s a solid mix of percussion heavy tracks with chanting vocals, to somewhat more low-key, relaxing string based numbers for when you are exploring the keep and the ruin that the gods have wrought. During fights you don’t have time to focus on the music as you can’t pause. Other than the introduction, there aren’t any vocals in the game. There is a free DLC that adds some extra bosses, and expands the story. Its free (which is great) and totally optional (you have to defeat the optional bosses before the last boss other start a new run.You would have to live for pain to want to 100% Eldest souls. I’m convinced anyone who has finished the game without dying, or using any shards or abilities is cheating.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would love  at first, especially after watching its intro, which intriguingly presented the premise of its universe. There, various deities tried to conquer humankind yet have failed and been imprisoned inside of a gigantic, pompous citadel; however, the peace and prosperity did not last long, as one day, these vicious gods started gaining back their strength, using it to perform dark, twisted experiments. While they could not break free just yet, they managed to unleash calamities upon the human race, mainly destroying food and water resources. That is when you come to save the day, perhaps being the very last chance for your kind.Even though all of that beautifully fits the boss rush nature of the game, it is the only positive aspect I can think of about the narrative, as otherwise, it is almost non-existent. Sure, there are a few lore entries lying around here and there, but they tend to elaborate on each god’s background rather than trying to form a compelling plot. One could argue that it partially makes sense because these deities are the prime focus of this title, after all. That goes against the intro’s premise, though. As they do not have a visible nor emotional impact on my character or the world during the playthrough, I could not bring myself to care about them, as it seemed pointless. I was hoping that it would get better with other people you meet along your journey, but that is even worse; in fact, I would not be afraid to claim that their presence is useless. Those NPCs just sit there, repeat a few bland, vague sentences, and perhaps give you a primitive quest revolving around finding an item and bringing it back to receive a pitiful reward… as in several generic, subpar fantasy games.All of that ties to another problem—the said citadel is not that interesting to explore in the first place. While  portrays its locations beautifully with its pixel-art visuals, the world itself, with the abovementioned so-called content, feels like unnecessary bloat. I often found myself thinking that I would prefer to fight every boss by choosing them from the main menu instead of meaninglessly galavanting around.Nevertheless, there are some redeemable qualities, for sure, such as the combat system. It might sound like a cliché, but you truly must time your moves precisely – especially dashing – as well as have a bit of skill, or you will perish. Simple as that. The introduction boss is pretty easy to handle, but the following ones will not give you much time to think, as their continuous, diverse attacks will keep you busy all the time. Thus, you must get into the fast-paced rhythm and make your decisions within milliseconds. Just mindlessly dashing around will not save you, though. Sure, you can easily rush through a basic thrust, but doing so with a fireball is not be the best idea, as it leaves flames behind it. Getting used to it may take you some time, so healing yourself will become a routine. Yet, there is a twist, as to fill up your bar with that lovely, red colour, you must boost your weapon power, rush to a god and keep hitting them as long as you can. This was a sweet change of pace for me, as in many titles, you usually need to get into a safe position to heal; here, it forces you to take the risk and be aggressive, and I applaud that.Moreover, there are three distinctive ability trees that change the way you play. There is Windslide, focusing on faster movement and manoeuvrability. If running around is not your thing, you can pick Counter, which specializes in deflecting incoming attacks. However, my personal favourite was Berserker Slash, which boosts your weapon damage even further, sometimes at the cost of being more vulnerable. It is the high-risk but high-reward style, which suited me. Apart from that, there are several shards you can use to boost those powers; though, some of them might even have negative perks.What about those bosses, though? I already talked about what you can expect from them combat-wise, but prepare to face beings that excels at both melee and ranged combat. Their design, both gameplay and visual-wise, is mostly great, and most of them feel unique. I said most because that is my gripe with this title, as there are only nine gods, but two of them use very similar attack patterns, making the second encounter way too easy. Moreover, several deities use the same spell, such as a wave you need to dash through, which only has a different colour each time. Given the fact that boss fights are the one and only focus of this game, I would not expect to see that. Plus, I have encountered a weird situation at times, which made dashing away unavailable, making me lose my health or even worse at times. That occurred when deities decided to go in a certain direction, and as I was in their way, he just dragged me along; however, I could not get away, so I always got hit afterwards no matter what. Yes, I have tried to avoid this from happening afterwards, but it is still a design or an error that should not be in this subgenre.In the end, I cannot recommend  despite its good qualities, as I was not really satisfied after finishing it. Maybe I would be inclined to give it a thumb up if there would be more gods to fight. There is a New Game +, which gives them some new attacks, yet that is not enough for me to replay it. I would say that this is a good foundation on which a possible sequel or a similar title could be built, but only the future will tell.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: visually very beautiful game, but the tags are very misleading. this is not a souls-like, nor would I say it's an action RPG. this is a boss rush with no exploration beyond traveling from one door to another, not a hint of exploration. you can just keep bashing your head into the wall until you beat a boss dying over and over again with no repercussions, you don't lose anything other than time you spent on that attempt. every boss gives you one upgrade point that you can invest to one of the 3 skill trees, out of which 2 are just different versions of deal more damage and the third is: get a shield sometimes if you are lucky enough cause it doesn't really trigger when it should. but it's ok cause you can relocate your points at any time for no price. game seems a bit too short (I didn't finish it myself) for the price-tag, and the only replay-ability it offers is for achievements. so if you are interested in it, I definitely recommend waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like here—the combat is REALLY fun, the skill point talents are cool, and the boss shard concept is interesting (think of a Transistor-style upgrade that has a core theme but changes functionality depending on which specific slot you put it in). The art and music are fine—passable, but nothing you haven't encountered before.The problem is that "challenge" in this game quickly turns to tedium. I'm not averse to hard games, but I think the core issue here is that the boss-rush style of game design just doesn't fit this level of difficulty. It almost feels like a waste of a great combat system to not give a wider variety of non-boss encounters and enemies to utilize it against. Instead, it feels like there's this great fighting system that's bottlenecked by only having a small number of combat counters to explore it in. It feels like holding in a sneeze; there's so many cool things you can do whilst fighting, but not enough actual fights to engage in.The result is that grinding the same boss over and over again just gets sort of... boring. Not the worst thing in the world, nor the most frustrating, but just sort of boring. The appeal of the cool attacks and talent synergies begin to lose their lustre when you've been fighting a single enemy for the past hour, dodging the same attacks you've dodged a hundred times and listening to the same repetitive soundtrack you've heard a dozen times. This is reinforced by the fact that there's almost NOTHING to do besides fight bosses. The story elements and side-quests are completely forgettable and largely unrewarding.I regret playing this over two hours, as I would've refunded if given the chance. As it stands, I just don't think the game is interesting or complete enough to be worth your time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game concept, with horrid execution.Game devs: Huge HP bars/bullet sponge enemies DO NOT EQUAL ACTUAL CHALANGE. Only tedium and the feeling of wasted time.I swear to god, I spent about 45 mins to an hour mastering the 3rd bosses moveset, and even after all that spent time, despite pretty much only getting hit every so often, it took me 10-15 minutes to take about 3 quarters of his HP down. That is NOT a challenge, at that point it becomes a CHORE. Couple that with the fact that most boss attacks will nearly one-shot you, it makes the margin for error almost non-existent, which might lead to death, if you make just one too many mistakes, which lead to restarting the whole fight, which in a Souls-like game is not necessarily a bad thing, but since it can easily take 15 minutes to down a boss, die a few time and you are looking at about an hour wasted, not due to actual challenge, but rather artificial difficulty which leads to tedium.Stay away from this game if you value your time, and look for a game which, if you are like me, will offer you a challenge you will want to overcome while still feeling like you are playing a game, not vacuuming or doing laundry.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah.This is not a souls-like. It's a boss-rush game, with 9 bosses in the main-game and 3 in the free dlc. You'll either be fighting bosses or nothing at all. Having a little npc chat in-between, maybe, but there's precious little square feet to explore and even less in terms of setpieces to see.In the main game, there is no equipment to choose from either - only a vague fighting style, which feels like it won't heavily come into play for the early bosses (looks like a long upgrade path)The tutorial boss does a good job of being an introductory challenge for what looks like a souls-like.The second boss can already hit you for 80% HP while taking a huge amount of hits.Third/forth (which can be accessed parallel) are another significant step up in terms of rapid fire heavy damage AoE attacks.I'm no stranger to difficult games - wether it be FromSoft or games like Furi.But this just doesn't have the same draw to offset the frustration.It's just not fun or rewarding to have to learn attacks, when it only takes one miss-step to be reset to the start of phase 1. Also, yet another purely singleplayer 'souls-like' with  online functionality, but no menu-pause function. Is it really that difficult to have?I might smash my head against this some more in due time, but for now I'm not having fun.Especially not when looking at the 20€ price-tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game. The art is awesome, the bosses look cool, and it looked like a great 2D take on what I assumed to be a "souls-like."Boy was I disappointed. This game should not be $20, and whoever put "souls" in the title was just baiting fan boys. Well played dev. You won, I lost.The problem is really that the combat doesn't feel good and that it isn't balanced. This is the type of game where you achive success by memorizing every possible move of the boss, never making a mistake, and also getting lucky. Sure, you can slog through the battles over and over again until you memorize enough to beat it that battle, but is that fun? Is it fun to have to hit the boss 100+ times when they can two shot you?The thing is that the game really isn't about skill. You don't "git gud", you just memorize. There's also no variety of weapons, builds, etc at your disposal, so you cant be smart and try different approaches for different bosses. You're stuck with what you have been given, so get slogging.In the end, it plays much more like a precision platformer than a souls game. Might be worth $5-6, but since there is only one playstyle and only one thing you can do in the game and that thing is mostly just super tedious, I think it is way overpriced.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A Boss rush with Souls-like combat. I don’t think Eldest Souls deserves a Souls-like comparison but the word is in the name of the game.  Eldest Souls appears to be focused on exploring an interesting world and constantly running into bosses.  I ended up getting stuck on the second boss but also enjoyed throwing myself at the extreme challenge that it provided.   The music here is a bit loud but man, it gets you pumped as well. The downside here is it’s not a Souls-like experience in that the only real gameplay is the bosses, so it’s more like a hard version of Shadows of The Colossus without the implied morality.   The fast-paced combat is all about reading attack patterns and trying to survive long enough to see and learn the move sets of enemies. Pick this up if you like challenging games.  I enjoyed this quite a bit but the focus here reminds me of Furi, where players will have to play challenging battles over and over to beat each boss even as those bosses made me feel foolish after every loss. I spent almost fifty minutes on a single battle and still want to come back to get that win. _childDocuments_.review: + Skill trees and boss gems add a lot of variety to how you tackle a fight in lieu of rpg stats and gear.+ The souls method of storytelling is implemented well, and there is more to enjoy in the writing than I anticipated.~ Bosses are fun to meet and fight the first time around, and the way NG+ evolves them makes for nicely refreshed encounters. However, they're often cramped into a tiny arena or area of fighting space, and they don't always feel like they explain themselves well enough– either telegraphically or otherwise. A lot of fights and moments can feel more frustrating than they should.~ Lovely art– for the most part. Some animations and cinematics can feel janky and out of place. The music isn't bad, but the tracks blend together and aren't as different as they should be to distinguish the bosses more.~ There's a bit of a disconnect between what seems like the game wants to feel like in a fight and what the mechanics actually lean your playstyle toward. My initial assumption was that it was going to lean more into an evade-everything and strike style, but it's more of a knife's edge fight to keep yourself alive.- So incredibly many design and aesthetic elements are either copied 1-1 or masked from Dark Souls. Some fit nicely or are morphed into a more suitable form, while others are limited and don't fit right with the short scope of the game.- Very brief, and it invites and relies on replayability like ds, but the shorter length and focus on bosses means much of what makes ds replayable is either absent or replaced with frustration.- Annoying achievements built to pad many more hours than the game is worth.Eldest Souls shows exactly the error in the assumption that Dark Souls is a game about fighting bosses. Though it is a soulslike, and though it tries its best to appear as one, it really is nothing like Dark Souls (for better and for worse). It's fun, but occassionally quite frustrating. Worse, it's condensed down to what a fraction of what it should be, and lacks too many of the elements Dark Souls relies on to invite replayability. Consider it if you really enjoy boss rushes, but wait for a sale.( full review at  )

_childDocuments_.review: Brutally difficult to the point of being unfun. I'm no God Gamer but I've beaten every  game, , , and , without using summons or other cheese tactics. Soulsborne games always have some bosses that feel frustrating and unfair, but on the whole I find them very well-balanced. They also have a lot of exploration and tense combat scenarios outside of the bosses.  is a boss rush game, so there's not much to it outside of the boss fights, and they're just too punishing to be enjoyable.I'll reiterate a few aspects of the combat that another reviewer pointed out: your stamina bar is divided into three pips, and you can't dodge at all unless you have at least one full pip. It regenerates slowly, too, unless you time your dodge perfectly such that you actually dodge through an attack animation rather than just away from it. This often leaves you without the ability to dodge when you need it. Bosses can corner you against a wall and body-block you so you can't escape even by dodging. A couple of the bosses I've fought so far have abilities that can two- or three-shot you. The  has the same health regeneration mechanic as  from , so if you get hit, not only do you lose a third of your life but the boss heals a substantial amount as well.It's a shame, because the game seems very well-made from what I've seen so far. The artwork is beautiful and highly detailed, the music and sound effects are great, and the boss designs are ability sets are varied and interesting. But for me,  is squarely on the wrong side of the fun challenge vs. frustrating grind divide. Maybe I'll try it again if they add a noob mode.

_childDocuments_.review: (Overall score at bottom)I wanna preface this review by saying; don't listen to the bad reviews this game has. If you look at them you will notice a VAST MAJORITY of them are people complaining that the game is too hard. Does that garner a negative review? No, if its too hard, get better. It's either not for you or you just got to get better.I didn't know what to expect heading into this game, I hadn't looked at any reviews, didn't look at any game play, never even played a souls like before. Had this game in my library and decided I was gonna sit down and play it. The start is fairly simple, teaching you the basic mechanics of the game, I thought "meh this game seems alright. I'll give it a go."It then gets very difficult very fast, and this is where most of the player base probably gives up. First 2-3 bosses are cake walks, then suddenly you're dying over and over and over again to the same boss making no progress getting filled with rage not knowing what to do better. Than after many and I mean many attempts later something clicks and you finally get it. You beat your first difficult boss. You get that dopamine hit and suddenly all that anger and hate you felt toward that boss has turned into euphoria.Then you go to the next boss, attempt after attempt, building up that same rage, eventually overcoming the challenge and getting paid off with that massive hit of dopamine again. Suddenly you start to really enjoy the struggle and reward of all of it. Every boss hits you with a different challenge, different attacks and different ways you must approach the battle. And they truly are intense and right down to the wire. When I first started the game, after my first 2 hours I did not think I was going to finish this game. I thought I was gonna give up and let the game be forgotten in my library but I kept playing and kept pushing on boss by boss. The feeling I got when I finally beat the game is unmatched, or at least it has been a really long time since I had such a euphoric feeling after completing a game. The hundreds of deaths, all those boss fights, the grind. It was all over and I had come out on top without giving up like I had initially thought I would. The art style is beautiful, and the boss design is top notch along with the boss fights. The story is alright, nothing spectacular but it definitely does add to the game making it a masterpiece in my opinion.Overall I would rate the game a 9.5/10Really a game that can be truly appreciated once you have conquered it.

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically, it gets better after the first 8 or so hours where you got enough upgrades and shards to customise your gameplay. At my current save where I just finished he game once, got all he modifications and started ng+ it feels so much better. although I will say most people might not want to bother with the annoyingly sluggish early state of the character, so I cant blame anyone for not making through.Edit: I just found out about the no-hit and no-death achievements. This game does not have the tight/responsive enough controls and animations to support that kind of gameplay. The fact that devs think it's reasonable to add those kinds of achievements tells me they don't even know what game they made. Also only being able to pick up one upgrade item per run AND you lose them at the start of the next one? perfect way to make the player feel like their character is stagnating whereas every enemy is getting more powerful each run. Just arbitrary difficulty increase for the sake of it. A lot of design decisions in this game does not make anything you achieve feel rewarding or satisfying.Overall, a 6/10. Quite mid. I had my and fun rage but there are games (eg FURI) out there that do the exact same thing(boss rush action) but better. so go play that if you havent already.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge souls-like fan, I have been excited for this game since it was announced. However, it wasn't until recently that I discovered it was a boss-rush type of game. I must admit, I was initially a bit deflated. From the early impressions and screenshots, I saw a world I wanted to explore, (the lore in these games is a huge draw for me), and I was worried there wouldn't be much more to this game than boss-killing. After playing for about 10 minutes, I felt my worries leaving. I don't know if it was the creeping audio that seemed just right, or the general atmosphere, but safe to say I started liking this game almost immediately. Wandering around for a bit, I found myself exploring every spot I could reach, and the sense of deliberate lay-out and lore placement (yay lore!) already had me looking forward to see what else I could find. One thing that really leaps out to me is how well the initial lore-bits and environment ques (something you can examine) really tie things together. I have played other games like this in the past that are so vague you really have to reach to piece together a narrative; not so here. Granted I have only just defeated two bosses, but so far the game yells quality. I'm about two hours in, but I am impressed with how it has shattered my expectations so far.-Great sound design. Sparse, but fires up when needed. The boss tunes are great so far.-Great layout and generally interesting world-Lore is well-written and already seems easy to connect some initial dots. Figuring out why the initial landing looks the way it does, etc-Characters are interesting, and sound is used sporadically to bring some color to the conversations. Really liked this. (Reminds me of Hollow Knight, one of my favorite titles recently)-Sprites are well-done-Action is pretty spot-on. Input seems good, attacks register well, etc-And the big one. Bosses! So far they are interesting, and the patterns are decent. I admit I've only really played Cuphead for a boss-rush type game, but was happy to see the bosses here vary up attacks, have multiple stages, etc. -Game seems decently challenging. The second boss got me three times or so before I nailed him, but seems more like a teaching boss than anything. -My one concern is that I have no idea how long this game is. I'm not used to boss-rush games so no idea what to expect there. But the world seems interesting enough that I won't just bull-rush through. (even if I could, which is doubtful lol). All in all, this is a very solid title so far. Considering there are a lot of indie titles in this genre along with some triple AAA efforts, this one is quality. Highly recommend for those who like these kind of games.Edit: Defeated a third boss, and delighted to find the difficulty really went up. A great, multi-layered fight that bested me enough to re-evaluate my tactics. I whooped when I won. :D Cannot wait to play more

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of this game's difficulty comes in the form of frustration. Games like Dark Souls have fun difficulty where when you die it feels fair. This game deals more in frustration than difficulty.I wanted to like this game I really did. It did have its fun points, when it was fun, it was really fun. The combat feels satisfying and the hits feel meaty. The lifesteal mechanic is fun and unique. The skill trees are well designed, and I like how you can just switch your skill points to try any playstyle at any time. I liked the berserker class and the resets with the fury fragments and the bloodlust. It felt very fun when I could get a combo off.Now onto the negatives:I do not understand why there are so many slows and stuns in the game, And a lot of them are really hard to dodge. If you get slowed or stunned it is NOT FUN and causes frustration. The main enticing point of this game is the combat and the movement. When you get slowed it feels very frustrating. And takes away from the fun of the movement.The animations and hitboxes are not clear. Some attacks hit you even when they shouldn't, and this also causes a lot of frustration.There is so much going on on the screen, it gets very overwhelming. Some of the gimmicks are extremely frustrating and RNG based. For example the Rotted crown, the corpses are very annoying. The bell gimmick is frustrating, you can hit it by accident and waste the bell. The corpses always spawn away from the bell you can use. And the boss goes into a phase where it locks out the bells. So if there are 3 or more corpses you are screwed. Because in this phase he spams the lightning balls and the green stuff on the floor and the invincible corpses make it way worse. I was mainly using the Berseker class, the fury fragments need to be coded so they don't spawn in places you cannot pick them up. Sometimes they can spawn out of the arena and you can't pick them up. Sometimes they spawn inside the boss and you can't pick them up. Again that is frustrating.Honestly, the world and art was very cool to look out and the art is amazing. But it gets boring running around when there are no common enemies. If you were going for a boss rush, the map should be smaller.

_childDocuments_.review: buyer beware and a TLDR for you: this game is a boss-rush with a souls-like aesthetic and telegraphed enemy attacks. think cuphead. therefore, there's not really a level-up system or mobs to fight, areas to explore like a traditional soulslike game, no traditional quests. You get stronger through skill trees (skill points) by beating bosses as you  go. Game is only bosses. Awesome art, awesome music, awesome sound design. Cool things. Ball-crushingly difficult game. Also get it on sale preferably. I don't think it's really worth the entire 20 dollars (19.99USD)PROS AND SOME INFO:with that out of the way i want to start by saying i honestly never thought i'd beat this game. i started the game a few years(?) ago and i received it for free i believe from a friend in a bundle they had. I beat the game earlier last night (few hours ago of writing this review). the game is h a r d. think cuphead, but cool pixel art and aesthetics of a souls game or similar. Once you beat a boss, expect to fight another hard boss not long after that when you traverse to the next boss arena. now, you CAN get stronger in the game, but it's not in the traditional way of what a souls-like does. basically, you beat a boss and you get 1 skill point that you can use to allocate into three fighting styles of your choosing. at any time you can actually reallocate points to better suit a certain fight if you feel it, or to try new things and different strategies. you can also get stronger by looking around the areas before bosses. there might be lore to read or items to pick up. some of these items may not have a use right away but will have a use later on. some of these items is how you'll get stronger later. there is a blacksmith and there are weapons you can use. but these things won't really be able to be unlocked fully or used until late-game. the pixel art and aesthetics, the boss graphical designs, the NPC designs, everything from music and sound design is awesome in this game.CONS AND SOME INFO:now, i know i have been singing the game's praises for a while but im actually kind of mixed on this game. I beat the elden ring DLC recently and that had the hardest final boss i've encountered in souls. going through that DLC taught me to persevere and never give up. so I decided to reinstall this game and just give it another chance because I don't really like dropping games. upon giving it a try, I found myself once again getting frustrated at the second and third boss of this game. but i kept going. I kept trying. this was about where I originally quit the game. I beat that boss and was surprised. now I knew I had to keep going. the bosses got harder as time progressed and I was more uncertain of whether I'll actually beat this game. next thing I know I beat all the bosses except the final boss. I got to the final boss and beat it. I can't say it was easy. It was far from easythe reason I talk about my experience in this review is to elaborate how the gameplay loop may be like for most. it's a very punishing experience and there's not a lot of room for error in some fights as there is with the souls games. the stakes are always usually high. You only heal by dealing charged hits and hitting using that blood meter thing. Some "shards" you can get later might help you regain HP in ways but that requires beating certain bosses to get them. the time to beat this game ultimately varies on the player.there were quite a lot of times I was unhappy with the game that got me close to quitting it altogether, I won't lie. There were a lot of questionable design choices with certain fights and the way things operate. for instance, the character moves extremely sluggishly, but this is mitigated through certain shards and fighting styles; even weapon(s) although the one weapon that gives you a speed increase you don't get until you beat the game. even with these speed increases, I always find it annoying to dodge certain attacks. Attacks hit like a semi-truck carrying a nuclear ICBM. And when you do use your blood charge attack thingy to heal on hits you don't heal for that much; meaning you need to keep on top of the boss. The scenes are often very chaotic to tell what's happening a lot of the time but not so much where it's unplayable. your mileage may vary though. I felt like a lot of times the game was just ball-crushingly difficult just to be ball-crushingly difficult. the game has cool animated pixel cutscenes here and there, cool pixel art, cool everything but i can't say i really enjoyed the gameplay and difficulty. I'm just glad it's finally over and proud that I conquered it. Some people will beat it quicker than me and have no difficulty, some will have an even harder time than I did. everyone's mileage may vary in these kinds of games. But nonetheless the pros of the game is kind of what kept me coming back I guess. I won't be doing NG+ though but the game has that if it's your thingOVERALL:overall if i could give the review a mixed recommendation i would put that instead of positive, but I put positive because it's not a bad game. you can tell love and passion went into it but also I sometimes wonder who hurt the dev lol

The balance is rather ♥♥♥♥♥♥. As I’m not going to write a 6 paragraph review for a 4 hour long game, I’ll just say that it’s lacking in content, and is rather inconsistent in general game design with things like annoyingly slow overworld travel, a unique but insanely annoying stamina system, improperly explained boss mechanics, and highly variable boss difficulty, with a general downward trend in required skill and “fun had’ by late game encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cool boss-only game at first. I loved the demo last year, I thought it'd turn out excellently, but there are some big issues. For starters, it's not really a souls-like at all except in the overused superficial sense (there are bosses, you can dodge, there's stamina, it's "hard", some menu elements and sound effects resemble Dark Souls'). The exploration is unrewarding. The fact that there are open areas with no enemies and really bad infodump lore actively harms the game, it makes it less fun to play. You don't build an interesting world by leaving a bunch of boring notes about King Kinglyman The 73rd and his Cool Throne upon which he did bad things. Or by letting the player read a 3-line poem about how it’s cold in the ice area.Though the empty world detracts from the game, the gameplay is what you get the game for. And the gameplay turned out messy. The demo was very light on abilities (you could spend just 1 skill point in one of 3 skill trees), and this was good. The second boss (first non-tutorial boss) was fun and well-balanced, rewarding you for dodging into its attacks (longer time to attack the boss before its next attack) and playing carefully.The problem is that there are a lot more skills (mostly passives, which is good—it avoids unnecessary additions to a combat system that's fundamentally solid) in the full version. And they're too powerful. I only tried the red "offensive" skill tree, but another negative reviewer wrote that  the trees are too powerful, so I wouldn’t be surprised if they all break the game on the first playthrough. The red skill tree allows you to do so much damage and healing that, as the other reviewer wrote, you stop caring about what the bosses are doing. You can tank attacks and heal back to full HP. The only threat is getting hit by several attacks in quick succession, or getting hit by the same attack (eg. a travelling projectile) several times. It stops feeling like a game where you’re interacting intimately with the boss’s attacks, and it starts feeling like an ARPG like Path of Exile.But remember, this game really wants to be known as “difficult”. As a result of the player becoming so powerful, the boss attacks get sillier, too. Past the first few bosses, the telegraphs for boss attacks start becoming really bad. It’s not an issue on your first run, you can still roll over the bosses. The problem arises because of what another reviewer said: their first run was so easy that they tried another run without using the skill tree (there’s a Steam achievement for this). As I expected, this magnifies the problem of the garbage telegraphs. Once you’re not doing abusive stuff to the boss, their poor design makes the fights a slog where there are very few safe windows to attack, and even then your fate is up to chance sometimes.It’s a shame, because the foundation for this game is great, but those two grave errors do a lot of bad for the game. If I were the developers, I would make the world more interesting or not bother with it at all/make it much smaller, and I would severely rein in the player’s power level so that later bosses can have interesting attacks instead of stupid ones.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a reason I wish for Steam reviews to have something between "I recommend" and "I do not recommend". I mean, it's nice, I had my fun, but its VERY short, it has only 10 bosses, which in my opinion is not enough for a proper Boss Rush game - while it can give you some enjoyment for 5-6 hours, Furi this is not. I finished this game and I will forget about it in a month.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played through this game now 4 times on normal difficulty and once on NG+. I got through the normal game in about 4 hours and if 4 hours of gameplay is worth 20 bucks to you, I'd say get it, definitely a fun first playthrough imo. The main issues really only become apparent in NG+ where it all falls apart unfortunately, thus not giving a whole lot of replay value despite the fact that only then do bosses get all their moves (which WOULD be kinda cool as a difficulty ramp if it only actually worked gameplay-wise).So what are the problems then you might ask. It has mostly to do with enemy attack overload and poor telegraphing/visibility. Like enemies will start having overlapping moves, so one move is still going while another attack already starts or is also going. This in and of itself isn't a bad thing, however the main issues are, you can't see the second move sometimes because the first move's graphic blocks it entirely. So you don't see it coming and can't dodge it. Sometimes moves are not well or at all telegraphed and it just comes out of nowhere which sucks even more. Weirdly enough this seems to be a problem for animations which have multiple angles as sometimes depending on which direction they attack you from the same attack can be clearly visible or not at all noticeable. Then we have some hitbox issues where enemies hit you when it seems they shouldn't or just miss completely. The later seems like it wouldn't be that big of a deal, however the game has a mechanic where you only have 3 dodges and stamina recovers very slowly UNLESS you dodge THROUGH an enemy move, so missing those is really painful, also every "class" has some move that requires you to dodge through an attack and again missing those sucks.Then there's the thing of enemies shoving you around. You can't dash through enemies and whenever they move into you they just shove you along. This wouldn't be that big a deal if you could dash through them, but it becomes a huge problem since they can sometimes just shove you into a wall you can't escape from anymore or block the dash path you need to have to dodge another ability, this effectively making it impossible to dodge that attack because they're in the way.There are also attacks that can be impossible to dodge, since you always dodge a fixed distance, sometimes depending on rng the attack pattern will be such that dodging through one will have you end up in another attack.For some bosses there's also camera issues (hey, it does call itself souls-like, so I guess you gotta have that, right? :P) where the camera will zoom out or zoom in to a certain part while the boss will keep attacking you from offscreen and you can't see it.There's also some problems with the classes imo. Some abilities don't make sense (collecting powerups that randomly spawn as a mechanic doesn't work in an action game about deliberate movement and positioning) or are very bad (like getting a tiny bit more damage (1-3 points when you usually chunk for 20-100) by executing a very hard to do maneuver that goes against the normal game flow.Anyway, I don't know what the plans are for the game and what the devs try and do now. The normal game and the design is generally really good, just when you really want to sink your teeth into it it becomes a mess and loses it's appeal through all the stuff mentioned, so I hope they work a bit more on that, cause it's otherwise a really good game. Just really NOT worth the price for a 4 hour experience that you can't really continue due to all the problems it has afterwards.

_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game but it goes too far with the difficulty, keep reading. You must play ES for the sake of the challenge and anything less won't cut it as the combat is not that fun or deep and you assume the role of an underpowered turd who must die to several bosses until he memorizes their attack patterns. You get to pick from a few minor enhancements to compliment your strategy but learning the boss attacks is still the only way to progress. You'll need to try again and again each fight, getting closer and closer to winning until your execution is good enough. In the mean time you get nothing in return, no exploration, no leveling up, no rewards.I really hate games like this, they demand that you sink so much time for the sake of it. The worst part is most of the time it feels like it would be enjoyable if only they relaxed the difficulty very slightly. Avoid ES unless you really are looking exactly for its kind of experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging and rewarding experience! Good variety of bosses and 3 different fighting styles to mix up the gameplay. Some bosses I beat fairly quickly and others gave me some trouble. It took more than a few attempts to learn what it took to take them down and the good thing is that once you die, you get back into the fight immediately. Highly recommend for souls-like fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled on my 1st playthrough, it is not an easy game, you get 12 bosses, all different, you have 3 skill trees and each has 2 specializations, the game is great, I don't understand why the mixed reviews, this is a hidden jewel.It is a boss rush game with some narrative and story along the way, if you like hard games this is for your, you may spend 10+ hours on your 1st playthrough then beat the game again in 4~6 hours, just like Furi game for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Not much content in the game if you only complete it once. Continuing into the NG+, I started encountering bugs with the last tiers in the skill tree either not activating properly or just not showing visually. Some skills started bugging out which a restart of the game did fix, but some bugs seemed to just persist such as the ones that I mentioned before. The bugs themselves are not that big, hence why I still have 20 hours of this game played, but they really make the experience unfairly frustrating when you wonder if you could have completed the boss with the skills activating/displaying properly. As it is currently, the overall quality of the game doesn't reflect the 20 € price tag and I would only recommend you try this game if you can get it on sale for less.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The game is advertised to be "brutally challenging" but the game fails to deliver just that.The game at first glance is nice, though one thing you notice immediately is the lack of good animations for attacks. You just have to learn when bosses position themselves or stay in certain positions and X seconds later the boss attacks and remember that for most attacks, which is fine but I can see how some people might have a problem with that.The game promotes you to dodge and actually play the game for the first few bosses, but then when you get more powerful, you have so much health regeneration and damage that you can get hit by 80% of a boss's attacks and still out-heal/dps him.The game just then becomes about doing as much damage as possible to the bosses instead of dodging and once you do that the game just becomes so stupid.I completed the main game and ng+ in 3.5 hours. The only boss that gave me trouble was the last boss on ng+ because he did so much damage you can't out heal it, so you actually had to learn his patterns which was nice. If only all the bosses were like that.I got 100% of the achievements in 13 hours with the hardest achievements being the no hit. Every single boss usually has one cancer attack that does 1 dmg but can be annoying/hard to dodge and without good RNG or mastery of dodging, you can't get 0 dmg taken. But still since it required actually actively dodging and attacking instead of face tanking it actually gave a decent experience.Overall I can't really recommend because the game specifically advertises as brutally difficult when the game design for most players allow them to face tank and max dps heal...I also don't know why everything is called souls-like when there is just a dodge. Not even really a stamina bar for attacking, just for dodging. Just because there is a roll/dash/dodge and the game intends for you to learn boss attacks doesn't automatically make something souls-like. By that definition...you could call so many platformers souls-like because of iframe dodge and needing to learn boss patterns...The closest game I can think of that this tries to create is Furi. Also a walking simulator / boss rush except from my memory in that game you couldn't just face tank max dps bosses. You had to dodge attacks to win. And Furi is certainly more difficult than this fiesta.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun boss gauntlet with interesting character progression. Skill points can be refunded for free at any time. This encourages trying out different build paths, and the different skill trees are distinct enough to warrant trying different builds. The base game is pretty short (~4hours), but it does have a ng+ mode that continues the progression and adds new attacks to the bosses. The bosses were really enjoyable with a decent variety of mechanics. The graphics are quite nice, if you like the style, and the music was enjoyable if a bit forgettable. Get it on sale for a fun afternoon diversion.Edit: Had to come back and say the DLC bosses (and weapons) really step it up a notch. They were some of my favorite souls-like bosses ever at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Boss rush game where bosses just don't feel very fun to fight, and that's made worse by clunky controls that can easily misfire (the direction you charge in, attack etc.) and confusing pixel art that makes it difficult to determine where you need to be standing at times. The bosses being bullet sponges and you using the equivalent of a toothpick against them doesn't help either, what that does is push you down the skill path that does the most damage and pretty much just spamming the charge attack. I tried to push through for a bit and got a few bosses down but I wasn't having fun so I'm dropping it.I wouldn't call this a "Souls-like" btw.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Boss rush game - no mobs and limited activity outside of that. The non-battle portion of the game is very limited and the fast travel/map mechanics are pretty bad and not user friendly at all. The actual combat is decent, and it does offer some flexibility in how you can play. Unfortunately, the skill tree for each is somewhat uninspired and relies heavily on defeating bosses to unlock shards for further customization. The bosses themselves are generally well designed and the battles are challenging, so defeating them is satisfying. Unfortunately, I am not having enough fun with this game to want to finish it. If you can pick it up on sale and like what you see, it might be worth checking out but at full price I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, bad execution with a surface level of souls-like. Normally, I have no problem with unable to dodge pass the boss since it push you to better your positioning. But most arenas are small and every boss uses zoning attack that it's outright annoying to play. But if I look at this game as a kind of bullet hell, the aforementioned are still in the level of challenging that I could enjoy. The greatest blemish in this game is the infuriating invisible hit box of most bosses that extend above their sprite. Combine with the small arena and the boss can just walk up and body block you in the corner then literally wait for the area attack to cook you up.I actually enjoys the game, the boss, and the flexibility and variability of the builds, but the flaws just whittle away the fun so quickly that I cant even finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game. -Short game with good replay value. -Cool combat system and skill trees.  This meant I was trying out different builds depending on what I thought fit for the boss.  Made the experience that much better and ReSpecing is a breeze. -NO TRASH! You move from boss to boss that's it!-Your play-style is what matters most and they made it work for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Good isometric boss fighting game. There are no ordinary mobs in the game. There are small locations with secrets that end with doors with bosses (like in Cupheads, for example). There is only one weapon - a large sword, but it has 4 variations, 3 of which are unlocked after beating the game (one playthrough per skin). Each sword provides a number of buffs and one debuff. There are three different skills, each with its own leveling tree. Bosses drop shards that can be stuffed into different slots and which further change the gameplay (dodge, strong hit, active skill, etc.)The bosses themselves are difficult, they have a lot of movesets and they are quite fat. The main disadvantage is that there are only 8 main ones (this is with the last one). Also there is also an underground elevator, where are new bosses on each floor (I have opened three so far, who knows how many more).But what’s cool is that after death you can simply click on Retry and you will immediately fight the boss. There is no need to run anywhere.In conclusion: a cool game about fights with bosses, I RECOMMEND it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: after beating all bosses normal, on abyssal and without any upgrades at all I feel comfortable leaving this review. The game is very short and only worth full price if you're going for the abyssal kills (NG+) as well, if you know already that you're not going to replay the game for the challenge and different endings then wait for a sale.tl;dr: short but fun game, "fun" if you like to learn some pattern and then kill some bosses with pretty smooth combat! if you want to braindead hack & slay badass bosses without getting punished for it, stay away from this game, you'll just get oneshot. A bit of patience is required~ also great OST!I did start going for the 0-dmg taken achievements but quickly stopped after many frustrating hits like this one here (). The biggest problem in many fights is that projectiles still exist for some reason even after visually despawning. what hit me in the video was the red light you can still see at 0:12 but after the laser it fades away, the hitbox doesn't. This is just a single example but by FAR not the only one i could make. Also, for casual playthroughs, you'll notice that you are not multihit protected at all. Most noteably in the Nightmare fight in which the boss can start spawning 3-5 projectiles in one place and hit you with all of them, instantly killing you, also making one of the items that gives you a oneshot protection once per fight useless because it just blocks one of the projectiles, the other ones kill you anyway. That wouldn't be a problem if the boss would not be able to spawn clones directly in you (very fun for 0-dmg attempts, they can spawn anywhere on the screen). There is so much more just badly programmed stuff going on that I midway through concidered not recommending the game but I did end up with 20h+ playtime in the end and overall had fun.Also I hate comparing different games, in this case a 2D souls-like with dark souls etc. If you like to do such comparisons then don't bother with this game. It is nothing like dark souls and thus will leave you in a bad mood. However, if you like challenging games, then give this a fair shot! and by fair, I mean play at least past the first 4 bosses and then check the next ones out. The 2nd boss is definetly a dif. spike compared to the first one but once you realize that , you shouldn't have much of a problem with him. If you decide to go for the NG+ abyssal bosses then don't quit after attemting the 2nd boss as well! he is much harder than any of the other bosses on abyssal tbh. once you get past him you most likely finish the rest in less than 5 attempts.Finally, I wanna give a shoutout to the music in this game. really great orchestral songs that I never got bored of, I absolutely likes every single boss OST!that's it, I'll give the game a 8/10, fix the projectile issue and maybe the multihit "issue" and I'd give it a 9.5/10 and continue the other 0-dmg taken attempts.also great free DLC btw, I killes the 3 bosses in my first playthrough and did not even notice that they were not part of the main game until further investigation after the final boss. I was confused at first why they did not have achievements haha.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game it was alright. there was some annoying boss fights that I just didn't like and beating them didn't make me feel any satisfactory and the final boss was a bit underwhelming compared to previous boss fights. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Yeah, yeah, so I came back to this one because I really did want to like it, and got through almost all of it this time, so I'm back with a bit more perspective on why I don't recommend this game. Frankly, I can't be bothered to beat The Rejected Daughter and whoever else comes after her, or Eksyll. Either of which I'm sure at this point I could have beaten and have frankly just stopped caring about beating. And despite playing an additional 12 hours (Steam tells me), I still don't recommend this game unless you get it on sale, and I still stand by my previous statements. You can't just tell someone to "get good" when the mechanics of your game **aren't clean.** Implementing ideas where you're only able to dodge through things if you follow a specific skill tree, but then allowing bosses to be able to push you around and pin you against the walls of the arena with no way to escape (re: The Rejected Daughter who has some major glitchy issues like poor timing on her audio cues and getting literally stuck in the wall of her arena, but others like Drakmur do this too) is just dumb. The isometric(?) view style is also a nice idea in theory, but then you have to actually make your arenas take into account the fact it's super helpful for your player to be able to tell what is actually an obstacle and what are the edges of the walls if you're not going to let them dash through things (Azikel had a bit of this problem with things sticking out from the sides somewhat irregularly) because the perspective is different. And you sure as hecc want to make sure the arena is properly closed (again, it's possible to get stuck on the edge of the entrance with TRJ because the webbing doesn't block it properly). You've also got to take into consideration the fact that if your arena is so big that your player can't see all of it at once, they might get irritated if something is flung at them from off screen without an amply mastered audio queue (Zylad is guilty of this with his floating weapons, which surprised me because The Deer God did a great job of handling a larger arena; zooming out when the vines are going everywhere was very clever, if absolutely necessary). Also, trying to pretend you're a platformer of sorts (the road to get to Drakmur) when the player's "jump" (dodge) doesn't allow them the ability to "change the height" of the "jump" accompanied by an insta-death if your pinky-toe goes over the edge has just gotta stop. That stuff is annoying af.So, yeah. Still enjoyed the lore. Thought the out of combat movement speed or dash regen could have been a touch higher when trying to explore the pretty sweet setting, but all-in-all, wouldn't tell people to pick this one up. Beating a boss just doesn't feel satisfying when half the time it seems like I have to depend on the luck of the draw instead of building up a set of skills that you learn by relying on the math of the game because there are too many inconsistent variables to make the process enjoyable.Original Review: I really want to like it. I really do. (Edit: The story seems great, the artwork isn't bad, and the sound design is pretty neato) I enjoy games that are challenging. And for the first couple of this singularly boss rush game, I could tell it was just a learning curve and that *I* could improve to the point of beating them. On the reverse of that, I stop enjoying games where it feels like the mechanics are consistently working against me, hindering my progress because they aren't clean, snappy, and/or responsive, and thus making me feel as if it's no longer MY fault I'm not getting any farther, but the game's itself.Is it just me or is being unable to dodge *through* enemies something that's the norm in most games (and absolutely is missing from this one)?Anyway. I got this for $10 and I'm not gonna say it wasn't worth the $10, but I sure as hell wouldn't pay $20 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, and at first glance everything appears to really well polished.tl;dr: punishing, but not fair, and buggy where it counts. Play Furi instead if you haven't already.Pixel art is great, sound design is great, music is pretty good, boss designs are cool. For the first hour or so, it really feels like it could end up as one of the greats.Unfortunately the area that this game fails the hardest is the only thing it's actually designed to do. Bosses only, and as far as I can tell there's only 10 or so of them. Even so, not a big deal if the game is perfectly polished.Unfortunately, the game doesn't play like a souls game, even though it explicitly references it. It is hard, but not really fair. In a lot of the boss fights, the bosses attack very randomly, and don't really have a pattern. You generally don't react and punish, you dodge.Unfortunately, you only have 3 dodges that in the heat of a fight take a _really_ long time to recharge. A boss might use an attack 10 times in a row that requires you to dodge; it's random. If you get unlucky, you die, period.The game really wants you to feel like you do in super meat boy, where you give it another go over and over and over, until you eventually master it. But due to the sheer amount of random attacks from the bosses, and the sheer bullet hell it throws at you, sometimes you literally can't win, even after you've made it past a boss' first phase or two.The game also has bugs. Hits don't register, attacks don't activate even though they take time to use, sometimes you'll use up two dodges at once in the middle of a single animation, etc. Pretty much all of the bugs I've encountered are exclusively in combat, which is 90% of the game.Even with a build where I killed a boss in 5 seconds and sustain through it all, I go to the next boss and no matter what I do I can't win. Maybe I could play absolutely out of my mind to beat this boss, but I've fought him roughly 100 times and have still yet to see any consistent patterns, with way too much going on. If a boss completely beefs an attack, sometimes they'll do nothing, sometimes they'll use their strongest, fastest attack 10 times in a row and completely destroy you, with no chance to fight back.Good when it's good, but some of the most frustrating moments I've ever had in gaming when it's not. Inconsistent, and unpolished in the only place that actually matters.For what it's worth, I'm pretty sure I beat all the bosses but the last one. Regardless of whether or not I was able to nearly beat the game, it really didn't feel like I earned it; it felt like I happened to get lucky every time after the 3rd boss or so.Feels like a frustrating game of chance, not a game of skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is very difficult and it is definitely not the kinda mashing attack & dash game that will be enough to progress. For that reason it is very rewarding if you master it. Those who complain that this is too hard, should become better or just let it be. I have read some "steam-reviews" where they say the dash is not invincible or feels clunky, which I don't think so. You can dodge attacks with your dash fully, but you can not dash through your opponents body, so you need to be aware of the obstacles. Always dash away or sideways from your opponent, never towards your opponent. If you now how to time your attacks, you definitely know when you can dash and when not. So in my opinion the fighting mechanic is really good and fun. This mechanic feels rewarding, because by observing your own and your opponents moves, you will be able to plan your approach and react accordingly. There is a skill-tree system which you can change at any time between the fights and will make it possible for you to adjust the character according to your favorable playstyle. The move-set by your character is quite simple overall, yet you need to use it wisely. Those who like very difficult challenges I can definitely recommend it. Others should better stay away from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of souls games and souls likes.  Thousands of hours in the sub genre, done all the stupid challenges and everything on the planet.This game suffers from being hard for the sake of being hard.  There is no learning to get better, it is simply built around making zero mistakes.  This wouldn't be as bad if healing was balanced, but it isn't.  When the game punishes aggression that's fine, many souls games do, but when healing is tied to that aggression and the game hates aggression then it becomes a game built to make zero mistakes.  If a boss is going to take 90% of your health bar on one hit I don't care, but if the way to heal that requires timed aggressive melee then it becomes unbalanced, especially because you can't heal very much during each window.  So I can't enjoy this game because it's not about fun, it's about perfect gameplay which is tedious, not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The part from Game's Description i think is misleading "Eldest Souls is a unique Soulslike experience". It is .There is no "Souls" mechanism/ farming souls to upgrade your character or something. You upgrade your character by killing bosses and once you kill a boss that you were fighting for an hour + you get straight to another boss whose difficulty is 100% advanced.Graphics are beautiful but the game experience after a while gets too repetitive in a way that will drive players to leave the game way too early.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, I once made a polemic post on Reddit around Dark Souls' design, on which I commented how disappointed I am with the fact that they won't allow you to try again with the boss without having to go all the way through the enemies and back to its chamber; the way some routes are so hidden to the player and you have to spend HOURS to be able to progress in your game (or watch a guide if you have no honor); and lastly the leveling system which can easily result in a gap between the player and the enemies, making the game either turn into super easy mode or impossible mode. But this game, fixes all of these issues, there's no levels (you get to choose if you want an upgrade), you get to respawn in the boss chamber when it defeats you and the map is really easy to navigate. There are bugs, but none of them make the game unplayable. This game goes straight to you and says "ok look, you wanna kill bosses? how about a game that is fully about bosses and no fill in the middle?" and hell they executed it just perfect. My only complain is with the secondary quests, I barely finished any and it's really hard to figure what to do, at least that was my experience. Regardless, not like I care a lot.  There's not much left to say, if you have the minimum interest, absolutely give it a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying, Eldest souls is a brutal game, so much so, the challenge me be too much for some. In fact, it might well be the hardest indie I’ve played this year. And I love it! Inspired by the Dark Souls series, it's primarily a boss-rush game where you definitely have to ‘git good’ to overcome the enemies that lie in your path. Enveloped in gorgeous pixel art, the horrors that await are plentiful – and without mercy. The dozen or so bosses have a vast set of attacks at their disposal, meaning you’ll be spending some time getting use to each’s move set. Like Dark Souls, patience and perseverance are required. Button mashing will get you nowhere.  You need to wait for the opportune moment to strike; a mistimed swipe of your sword will leave you vulnerable – and on the ropes and reeling. Expect to attempt each boss many times as you learn their patterns, and work out the best way to bring them down. Eldest Souls has a far deeper combat system than I expected. Defeating bosses gives rich rewards, including skill points and new powers. There are three very different skill trees you can choose, from one that focuses on improving your speed, to one that allows you to defend and counter attacks. And, thankfully, you can remove skill points and shards and  apply to other options, at no cost. Playing around with the different styles is great fun, as you test which works best for each boss. There’s a multitude of possible combinations. You really can play the game the way you want to.All in all, Eldest Souls is a beautiful brute of a game. If you’re a glutton for punishment, there’s plenty to feast on here!

_childDocuments_.review: Full Disclosure: I won this game in a giveaway/raffle.Despite being called one multiple times in the description and the quotes from various reviewers, this game is NOT A SOULS-LIKE. This is simply one boss fight after another with no other encounters in between. There is no real exploration that I've seen. You just walk for a minute or two through the empty landscape until you encounter the next boss.Maybe Eldest Souls does have boss fights that are as good as Dark Souls games. But boss fights are my least favorite part of those games. In Dark Souls, the bosses are just gates, and the reward for defeating them is opening up a new area to explore, sights to see, treasure to find, etc. In Eldest Souls, the reward for a boss fight is a measly skill upgrade and more boss fights.In other words, I found the game to be the worst parts of souls-likes--exhausting and frustrating--without any of the better parts to make it worth it. If there was more to the game, I probably would have stuck it out and finished it. But there's not enough here to motivate me enough to persevere through the challenging boss fights.While I'm sure a big part of my frustration is that I didn't "git gud" yet, there's more to it than that. For example, one of the early boss fights, Azikel the god of light, has an attack that does damage to the entire screen on the left or right side of himself, wherever he happens to be when he uses the attack. And sometimes he positions himself farther to the side of the screen than you are able to move (i.e. outside the bounds of the arena) and then activates that attack, leading to inescapable damage anywhere within the boss arena.No thanks."Boss Rush: The Game" is not for me. For people who like that kind of gameplay, there's a good chance they'll enjoy this game because it seems competently made, and it seems there are plenty of good things going for it as a boss rush game. But I feel the game was misrepresented as being more than it is, and different to what it is. If they had honestly marketed the game as a boss rush instead of misleadingly calling it a souls-like, I never would have entered the raffle to win this game, and I never would have left a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: This is not a souls game. This is a boss-rush game in vein of FURI, Titan Souls, Death's Door, etc. Second, the presentation can be a little lacking at times. There is a lot of small quality of life stuff that would have gone a long way, such as a nicer looking title screen, some minor animations in the world, etc. The world feels very... cold and stiff, but less in an atmospheric way and more of a "man I feel like I'm looking at a png" way.But my god the bosses in this game are great, and the gameplay is amazing too. The dodge and bloodthirst systems are deeply rewarding to master, there are lots of unique builds to add replayability, and dear lord the way some of these boss fights evolve throughout the fight is just S-tier boss design. I'll update this review when I finish off the last couple bosses xDUpdate: Finished all the bosses.New Game + is amazing. It's more than just "make them have more health", it actually changes the bosses movesets and really puts yourself to the test. Yes, a first playthrough is short, but the whole appeal of these boss-rush style games is mastering the bosses that do exist, which this game does excellently. By far some of the best boss designs in gaming. ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone calling this a soulslike fundamentally doesn't understand what a soulslike is. This is a boss rush game, where you travel through an empty world from one boss fight to the next, with NPC to talk between fights to fill in some minor lore. There are no small mobs to fight, no real lore comparatively, no way to upgrade your character if you feel like you hit a wall on a boss, no, it's fight bosses, and grind the boss until you win. I get any "hard game" is compared to the Souls game, but there's being hard and then there's being extra tedious to play while lacking all the things that makes Souls game fun, e.g. beautiful and interesting landscapes, tons of items to get the lore, tight controls, and ways to make other progression if you hit a wall with a boss.In this game, the combat is slow and clunky as you hit bosses with a wet noodle that does no damage and they can essentially one shot you with attacks where dodging felt more on RNG to not get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over vs skill. I'm sure there are people that love grinding out a boss fight for an hour, plinking away 1/50 of an HP bar per attack a couple of times a minute, but it just comes off tedious when there are much better boss rush games out there. Like coming off Cuphead into this, and it just makes everything feel more egregious given how good Cuphead is to play, and that it feels better to learn to play and feeling like I was always making some meaningful progress on a boss vs here where, oh, another fight lost where I only plinked off a few bits of HP.

There's just no middleground with this game, it's either depressingly easy or outrageously hard. Hitless achievements are here to point out the massive flaws of some of the boss fights. Like Eos for instance, that has an attack that disables 90% of the arena for a while and make the fight a massive chore where you have to wait for a long, long time before having a window of attack. Or Drakmur, the lord of bullcrap, that can throw 2 patterns at you at the same time... which is not fun when one of it requires you to stay still to dodge it and the other one requires you to move constantly.NG+ adds even more patterns that make the fights even stupider then their base versionAll in all, Eldest Souls was a horrible, horrible experience for me and I blame my inability to drop a game until I feel like I did everything I wanted in it. The game has wasted potential and could profit from an overhaul of his boss fights, too few of them are properly designed to make the game an interesting experience. Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan. A combination of poorly telegraphed attacks, cluttered visual effects, janky hitboxes and a lack of clarity regarding what can and can't be dashed through means that every boss needs several attempts just to figure out what rules the game is playing with this time. I suppose replayability and playing with the multiple combinations of skills and shards (one of the better points of the game) is meant to be the rest of the content, but after plowing through the bosses in about a single sitting I don't feel like I'd get anything other than irritation from going after NG+.Get it if it's on a steep discout.
