_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 got blisters on my thumb from playing the gameEldest Souls is a challenging boss rush game. NOT a "soulslike". The marketing is a bit misleading here unfortunately. I did honestly enjoy the game, but some positive comments are a bit suspicious. "Amazing quests, beautiful lore"? ... no, not really. You can find items and hand them to certain NPCs, that's about it for "quests". Lore is dull and sparely found via flashing items (etc) in the world and the little bit of dialogue from NPCs. Don't mind for a boss rush, just wondering how anyone could describe it as amazing...I do like the pixel art style, the music is superb and I've enjoyed almost all of the boss fights. Regarding difficulty, the beginning is tough, but patience, focus and learning patterns is the key.  You do NOT have to play perfectly in order to kill bosses, not even in Abyss Mode (NG+). You will unlock more and more skills which make it easier along the way and alter your playstile. You can change your build any time, which I really like. The third/fourth boss was the hardest for me personally, took me around three hours to beat. Everyone else died much, much faster.What I did not like were some awful large hit boxes (you can't dodge through bosses) and you sometimes get squeezed into a corner with no chance of getting out. There is a lot of animation lock going on, meaning you might tank consecutively  hits. If you get hit/pushed back, you can't dodge because of the animation lock. Or use a skill. Same goes for attacking and dodging. It's not awful, but it did annoy me sometimes. (skill issue tbh)When restarting a fight, it would sometimes start immediately (instead of being able to change your build). All in all, if you do like a challenge and don't get too frustrated by dying, give it a go, maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: With each year the thought that Indie Games are more enthralling and engaging than mainstream games has become the norm in my mind, as it has become a struggle to find any interest in anything that is made from a big developer since a long time. I'm happy seeing Nier Replicant on PC, and dedicating my time to the hidden intricacies of Lobotomy Corporation. rather than 'forcing' myself to play Resident Evil 8 and Control to see how the story would go without desire to continue. Growing up I came to appreciate stories more than gameplay, so I often would forgive clunky mechanics and ignore them altogether when a game let me want to know and have more.I saw that another title with "Souls" in its name came out: the game itself is actually short, objectively some people are facing difficulties and mentioning it's the hardest game they tried so far, but most will be able to finish it in a couple of hours even if struggling initially for some time. Beware that the below might contain spoilers for the game, in case you'd like to go fully blind. I will try to keep it as vague as possible, but read from this point onward at your own risk.It begins with a motif typical of the soulslike games: a lone person with a weapon, moving slowly, through what appear to be a battlefield or a location containing a certain history. We are not aware of what has come to pass in the places we visits, until we find information through the items we collect and the things we read. The game itself appears to mix the real-life crusaders-like knights with knowledge of 'gods' that have come to dominate and influence lands.I think the nicest thing it has to offer is the progressive involvement the player gets to have: you begin from a menu that welcomes you with a chant, begin by facing a sort of 'guard' which is more or less a literal watchdog, are about to venture inside a fortified city but are stopped by another guardian, clearly inspired to abyssal corruption from Dark Souls 3, and from there the game keeps going up with the challenges: no mobs are introduced, but traps begin to appear. You are frail, but you are pushed to dive into peril and drain energy from your enemies, as to replenish your own, just like in Bloodborne. You continue to fight what is brought to you, but you start to want to look for more items, talk more to the available, few entitites present in the game, wondering whether you can trust them and who you should listen to, while understanding more and more how doomed this world was, and how this travel will not end peacefully, regardless of the approach you will take.The fights are the main attraction of the game: bosses are what made Souls games famous beyond the ridiculous, punishing and sometimes funny deaths that players endure while trying to get further in the story, toward the next enemy, and the motif of having to fight and harness power, or liberate the way on your path, was the main driving factor in them. It figures then that the developers would focus on a sort of boss-rush game and put the main care on them: they all have a sort of recognizable motif or element, but while this is true, they are not uninspired: unique elements and mechanics are added to all of them that fit very well the top-down perspective and gameplay action, with clear phases where they realize you are bringing them down: the arena is being used sometimes subtly, sometimes evidently, to trap and kill you, the music adapts swiftly and in one boss that I particularly loved it changes altogether from instrumental to vocalized. Each boss clearly wears the inspiration from past souls games, as the rest of Eldest Souls does, but it does so proudly and adding their unique touch.All of the above is condensed into subtle hints, small dialogues, gorgeous art and beautiful music, enough things are given to us on screen to allow the player to add their own imagination and thoughts in the game: was this citadel being subjugated by a false god? Were they prisoners of the guardian that was supposed to help them? How has the forest god been corrupted? What was the entity behind it? Hints at other organizations (alliances, churches) are given scantily but fit all too well, sometimes however it kind of seems like there was a desire to insert a relatively recent fantasy trope just to fill in more variety to the game. Although sometimes it seems gratuitous, especially considering that the game doesn't last that long, it adds to the lore repository and makes the player wants to have more.You can personalize your playstyle with a classic agile fighting technique, a purely damage / berserky build, or a defensive approach that allows you to withstand brutal hits as long as you time parrying them correctly. While I could get through the game with one single style until the very end, where I then switched to another and cheesed the last boss, it's clear that the game wants you to experiment and personalize your crusader not just with the choice of whom to talk to and help, but also in the approach you take to the game itself. The choices are small but able to make the difference, and different bosses might benefit from different attacks rather than focusing on a rinse and repeat attempt. All of this is condensed, which is the essence of the game (even 'upgrades' to your character are bestowed only after fulfilling a small quest, and work in their simplicity, like with the blacksmith's choice of upgrade for more damage or more defense), a condensation of successful elements characterized by a unique touch that differentiates it from other games attempting to follow into the success of the Souls series.Last but not least: the developer studio is made of 4 people, and it makes me very happy to see that the game was created by Italians, as an Italian myself, knowing all too well how difficult it is to be able to fulfill oneself into our country marred with poor job prospects and obstacles in realizing projects. The understanding of what works and what makes the grim dark fantasy series likeable, together with familiar yet different art and music that turns boss fights into a meditative session with an enemy that you come to respect and 'dance' with between life and death, shows how passionate they are for the genre themselves. This isn't just a derivative of a souls game, it is a game that immediately engages players that want more of the thing that has introduced them to the genre in the first place.Unfortunately, while the way the game end is nostalgic of old games and let's players add some replayability, to know what other choices bring to the ending, the game is overall really too short. It functions quite well as it is, and clearly there could've been a risk of becoming repetitive or having less attention and detail put into what we have now, were more content put there just as filler for time. If you do like souls games, you will throw yourself into this, want to finish it, and want to know what you might've missed by exploring further. If you're thrilled by boss fights, new game+ will let you fight bosses that will change their mechanics and make the fight more difficult through learning to get through those, rather than merely receive less damage and inflict more onto you (although that does happen too). In the end however, there is the wish for more, and hopefully we will get more content in another game, or more addition to the current one, as in a sea of clones this one is able to satisfy one's craving for challenge and discovery, but just like many good things it ends all too soon.I recommend, in spite of the length, to experience what the game has to offer, as it is a small Indie gem showing yet again how much potential and quality there are in games coming from small developers, and putting yourself in the shoes of the small crusader that will be facing divine entities, overcoming yet again impossible odds and surviving a bleak, damaged world, is absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review I have completed more than half of this game.  As a big fan of souls-like games and Dark Souls, there is a lot this game does right, and a few things that could be fix.  Lets start with the good.Positives:+ Very detailed sprites and looks polished well.  All the areas are unique and exciting to explore.+ The controls are pretty tight, and allow the combat to succeed.+ The combat mechanics are at their best when everything is used, leading to tons of action.+ Three different upgrade paths for three different play-through's, allowing enough changes to be worth repeats.+ Interesting lore, though it could have been shown a bit differently to add more mystery.+ Though some bosses are a bit questionable, most are very enjoyable with different attacks and patterns.  Its awesome to overcome such a great challenge since some of these bosses are ferocious.The Not So Good:- Some of the NPC's seem kinda pointless.  Some are good like Edd with the Harp and some apply new lore.  But some have no reason to be in the game.  One example is the Crusader you find before the Last Guardian fight.  He has no reason to be there, and it does not make sense how he is alive.- Only about 6 hours of playtime, though repeat runs are recommended.Should you buy this?Yes, it is well priced at $20 and is well worth your money.  Though a bit short, repeat play-through's with different combat styles allow 3 unique play-through's to be fun.  Its also the type of game that is really fun to come back to after a long time, like Dark Souls. (;Final Score: 8/10Eldest Souls is a well polished, beautiful, and entertaining game.  Its easy to overlook some small problems and enjoy the tough fights ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: To my disappointment, unlike the tags and the description would suggest, this is not a souls-like, in fact, it has almost nothing to do with souls-likes. This is a boss rush game and the only souls-like thing about it is the combat. Sorta. However putting this aside it really is a fun game, I just finished my first playthrough and damn, the bossfights really are engaging and the lack of boss runbacks really encourages retrying until victory is achieved, they all seem unique while also following a common scheme, it's really hard to name a fight I didn't enjoy. Except Drakmur, hate that guy. The combat itself feels pretty smooth, having only tried one weapon I can't say much about it, but there is a NG+, so gonna be trying more of them pretty soon. The game does also fill the world with some NPCs to try and get the lore going, but not gonna lie I didn't pay attention to them like at all lmao. Would highly suggest trying the game out, maybe on a sale tho, 3 hours for one playthrough is not a lot of value for one playthrough players and non-speedrunners.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky, unsatisfying, uninspired. The UI and controls feel pretty clunky and there were several times when I healed and saw my HP fill but I still died because the game hadn't registered my new HP pool.Even when you do defeat a boss the game lacks the sense of accomplishment and gratification that souls games give. Since the bosses take forever to bring down and there is no direct weapon/hp/stamina upgrades it gets stale after reaching "Concord Sanctuary" (about 4 bosses in). The backdrop for the world is more or less a copy of Gwyn rising against the dragons, but with a reskin and minor tweaks. The map looks intriguing until you realize that you can't go anywhere outside the small paths you walk.All in all, not a soulslike and not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a boss rush game, not a souls-like. I've played dark souls, bloodborne, elden ring, and other souls-like series and compared to Eldest Souls, the difficulty curve into this game is absolutely insane. The 1st boss is not bad and the 2nd boss is pretty challenging. Getting through the third and fourth boss is where I stopped. They are absolute damage sponges and the only way to heal is by a damage ability which gives you low amounts of health back slowly. You lose a signfiicant amount of health when hit once to where all the health you recovered is lost and more in an instant. If you have a lot of time and patience with learning the fights and mechanics perfectly, you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is an isometic Hack 'n' Slash game, which is a cross between the two games/franchises that may come to mind when one hears the word "Souls", namely FromSoftware's "Dark Souls" and Acid Nerve's 2013 indie darling "Titan Souls". The Dark Souls influence is self-explanatory, and the game's almost excessive revelling in long walking sections, with breathtaking, yet somehow uncanny and melancholy visuals, evoking a sort of "ancient liminality", as well as its boss rush structure, are where the Titan Souls influence is unmistakable. It was developed by Fallen Flag Studio (,  and ) and published by United Label and CI Games on PC, on 29.07.2021.+ Gorgeous Graphics and Animation, paired with somewhat clever environmental storytelling+ Creative Boss Design+ Wonderful Orchestral Soundtrack by Sergio Ronchetti+ Interesting, Stylized Cutscenes+ Pretty fun, Weighty Combat (though the skill tree for a 6-7 hour game is maybe a bit much)+ You can redistribute skill points at will+ Some very surprising moments during the fights, that genuinely caught me off guard- Typos, extra spaces, weird sentence structures in the notes strewn about the world- No Pause feature (A thing I despise in Dark Souls’ offline mode as well, and this game doesn’t even have any online functionality that could half-explain this glaring oversight)- Got stuck in a wall mutliple times during one of the bosses ()- Dodge seems a little inconsistent (sometimes you dodge into an enemy, and your character genuinely dodges, other times he just stands there, even though you have stamina – the timing in general seems a little off somehow)- Active Shard attacks (R2) kept getting stuck on nothing in some boss fights, thus consuming the charge, but not properly activating- Characters don’t feel too fleshed out- Odd, last second attempt at didactic storytelling- Obtuse quest design (also just feels unnecessary in a boss rush game in general)- Skill point unassignment should have a confirmation screen, I ended up having to painfully respec, one-by-one like four times during my playthrough.- Slightly finnicky hitboxes (especially during the one platforming section)Eldest Souls sets out to do many things, and it is definitely a valiant and commendable effort, in spite of what I am about to say. For all that Fallen Flag Studio set out to do here, however, it falls a bit short on most fronts, sans visuals and music. The game has an identity crisis: It wants to be Dark Souls, and thus, an RPG, but it only has about nine bosses (and 3 bosses from the free DLC), with each one granting one skill point. There are three skill trees: one that is all about aggression, one that is all about counterattacks and one that is all about defense. I chose the aggression one, and it was a solid way to play, but it still leaves me wondering if a whole, semi-elaborate skill tree system isn’t quite past the scope of this 5-6 hour experience. It also wants to tell its story through elaborate notes, but a lot of them are not written the best, and I even found one duplicate note. They provide little to no context: The story ultimately falls flat to me and its message seems last-second and deflated.The bosses are a joy to fight, and are all immensely interesting mechanically. It is clearly visible that this is where all of the time and money went. So I wonder: why couldn’t  of the effort have been spent here and on creating a satisfying world? The environmental storytelling is there, but it never quite leads anywhere. Some characters seem like they come from wildly different games. The notes that you felt might provide context, actually just reveal more cryptic writings: Mostly field reports describing the thing that is right before your eyes at that very moment.While the combat is fun, for the most part, it can feel a little weird: from the hitboxes, to the timings, to the damage received – often things end up feeling off in one place or another. Not enough to frustrate me, but enough to leave me confounded. Abilities (active shards) sometimes refuse to work properly, too. There is one platforming section, which is just okay. The game has some fantastic ideas and even some refreshing attempts at execution (for example, one boss has two phases, and after you beat the first phase once, it takes significantly more damage on subsequent tries, to advance to the second phase faster), but it needed some more direction, practice on the side of the designers and time in the oven to molt from a jack of all trades, master of none, to a truly memorable experience. If you, like me, still enjoy seeing developer's efforts at creating the art they are so passionate about, then be sure to pick this game up, it might still surprise you (like it did me a few times) if you can look past its flaws and shortcomings.P.S. I look forward to seeing more from these developers. A link to their website can be found

_childDocuments_.review: is a difficult souls-like boss rush game, the bad thing about it being that the difficulty feels way too forced. First off I finished the game once and it was enough for me, there's a new game+ option that sends you to the beginning of the game to start over while keeping your skills and shards but the game becomes even more difficult/ tedious (the player heals less and takes more damage, bosses have more health and new attack moves).In true souls-like fashion we wake up alone and wondering where has everyone gone in the desolate lands around us. Any drop of lore that exists we either read through notes or find out about it from the few NPCs that exist in the game. That's definitely not the main focus of this game. Now the bosses themselves.......... they gave me mixed feelings with them feeling more like an uphill battle at times. There's a few good ideas in the combat, you got limited dodges so you can't abuse those, got normal/charged attacks and different skill paths which translate to different playstyles. The player can change their point allocations from one boss to another if they so wish which brings versatility. Boss design is nice for the most part, they had potential. The patterns are respectable and learning them feels fair enough. However what's not nice is that some bosses either attack way too fast or their AOE covers way too much distance. The ice boss ? Frigid Waste ? Good luck dodging falling ice + boss attacks + DoT effects that are already on the gound from before. Bad thing is if you don't die then you'll get permafrosted and die anyways through all that flurry. Nightmare and the last boss had the same vibe. They seem to still be updating the game from time to time but I can't specifically recommend it knowing there are better games in the genre. Try it if you have it from some bundle otherwise get it at a sale if you really want to. Just that you'll need a lot of patience and praying to RNJesus for boss patterns which I don't think it's a fun way to spend a couple of evenings even if you wanted a challenging game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is extremely clunky, because of the dodge mechanic. The combat build is actually good, with free respec on 3 different build, and plenty of buff and shards at your disposal, but the dodge mechanic is absolutely horrendous. Sometimes when you get too close to the boss, you can't dodge through it. You need to space yourself away from the boss to be able to phase through the boss, which is stupid. You also cannot cancel your charge attack with a dodge, so any attack coming your way when you're charging, you have to tank it, which loses your bloodlust meter, and you're back to charging another charged attack anyway, because the whole combat revolves around charge attacks to do any damage.This is definitely something that you can enjoy, because the art style is pretty good, but you really need to get used to the clunky combat system to be able to enjoy the game.Also the game is a boss rush with almost zero story, no a single mob, which is a minus in my book as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a short and slightly challenging boss battler. The whole game consists of 10 boss fights, no grind, no trash enemies, no crafting, just you vs the bosses.Each boss is unique and requires a proper strategy to beat. Because it is not possible to over-level or farm better equipment each player will have to depend on their skills alone to overcome the challenges. Attacks are well telegraphed ahead of time so it is possible to do hit-less runs without having to depend on good RNG. Combat while simple is good enough. The only way to heal is to keep attacking which encourages an aggressive play-style. Eldest Souls is yet another game which tries to tell you it's a "souls-like". It is not. There are no bonfires, no souls, no equipment load mechanic, no estus, no stamina based combat and no animation locks. The only similarities are rolling and cryptic quests which honestly 90% of RPGs have so it's just not enough to classify as a souls-like.Overall, Eldest Souls is pretty good and gives a nice dopamine rush when you finally kill a boss. The length of the game varies a lot depending on skill level. It took me 4.5h to finish the game, but that's mainly due to my boomer-level reaction time. If you don't suck as much as me at video games Eldest Souls can be finished in a couple hours.Eldest Souls works great on the deck out of the box. It's very lightweight so battery will last longer than the game and fans will be quiet. One thing I would recommend changing is rebinding the dash to B. For some reason it is on A by default which is very confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Not super far into the game so far, but the fights are fun.I do think that the game does need to improve on a few things;- Sound queues could be a few frame sooner than they are.- hitboxes could be a fraction smaller (specifically for very wide floor projectiles you have to dash over)- the dash feels clunky, in the sense that in doesn't interrupt what you've inputted and sometimes doesn't dash at all, especially when right up against a boss or wall.so far, i haven't seen any enemies other than bosses and they are all very close to each other. so the game lacks any sort of pacing. It feels like a boss fight gauntlet.While i wish the game had basic enemies to fight, and certain mechanics could be polished, it's still fun so far, so i'll keep playing it. I just won't be able to play for long sessions at once, because i feel exhausted with the amount of bosses that appear one after another.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to review. Is there potential? Absolute, art direction feels great, controls often feel good, and the overall narrative is headed in the right direction. However, this game is just not for me. The game hardly rewards you for exploration, most of the times defeating bosses doesn't feel rewarding (because there is another one waiting for you right around the corner), NPCs feel rushed and they don't really contribute much to the story. Finally, we get to my biggest critic: The game is just... empty. The path between bosses is just completely empty, and all the items you can acquire are just there, it doesn't feel rewarding at all.Overall, I do not recommend. If you like a good old boss rush, go for it, but at least wait buy at a discount. It is just not worth the 20 dollar price point...
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a souls-like game; all you do is fight boss right after boss. I enjoyed the first fight, but anything after that, it just becomes tedious and annoying to fight the bosses. I was hoping that this game was almost a copy of the Bloodborn mod, but more well done since this is an actual company. Why is there no other enemies that i can farm and fight for fun? Why is there skill upgrades when this is only a boss game? This just feels rush, the movement and controls are easy and responsive; however, when fighting a boss, your character becomes small and hard to see because you need to dash into them to hit them and heal. I do not see how this is a good mechanic, it just makes the game more difficult. I do not mind the challenge, and that's why I enjoy the Souls series and games close to it. This seems very rogue-like compares to souls-like. Just because it has a dodge mechanic does not make it a souls like game. I would enjoy this game if there was more to work with and fighting was not so tedious. I enjoy making a little bit of progress each time, then dying, then trying again. I just felt like I was making no progress each boss I fought. Maybe I am just bad, but I feel like this game could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a horrible game but it's underwhelming. The game just does not feel fair often. The hit boxes don't feel right on many of the attacks, where you will think you are on the edge but nope its gonna hit you. A lot of the time the stages of the bosses are just the exact same attack but double. The tells of the attack are hard to spot and not always for good reasons. At times the animation is just mixed with the background too much and that's why it gets difficulty the actual dodging is not at all. The traits and runes don't feel like they actually contribute that much and you still basically can play the same way no matter what fighting style you choose. You can probably find a story in there but it's told almost completely just through text. Although I personally wasn't playing this game for a good story. The fact that you can't pause the game is straight dumb and needs to be fixed. The bosses just feel uninspired and there was not one that i was actually interested in. Or through was a fun use of mechanics. If you want a good boss rush there are far better. Furi, Titan souls do the genre better than this. I just didn't have fun or feel rewarded when i beat a boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy with a discount.I was able to beat this game in 6 hours while exploring areas for hidden items.But there's new game+ mode that adds new moves for the enemies, so I'd treat the first playthrough as a tutorial and new game+ as a real game.The good:- Well telegraphed boss attacks- Visuals- Combat feels impactful and satisfing.- Short, doesn't overstay it's welcome.That being said, I have some issues with this game:- It's a test of patience, like many games of this genre. You need to attack your enemy 100+ times, only to die and start over if you happen to get hit 2-3 times in a row. Of course, the lifesteal mechanic here makes it more forgiving, but it's still tedious in cases where first 50-80% of the enemy health bar are boring and the final 20% of the health bar, enemy suddenly goes all-out and spams you with new moves. And the parts where there are two bosses in a row without a checkpoint are the worst.- You could in theory respec at any moment, but I found anything but the right branch of the counter attack tree useless in comparison.- Counter seems OP. With counter attack + bulwark build, you can just hold attack (X) and counter when it's ready (LT) that seems to be most effective. There's not much sense in using bloodburst attack (B), active shard (RT) or light attack (mashing X). I cheesed through most bosses, taking most of the damage and not bothering to dodge much, because it's just more effective to spam charge attacks and counter.Overall, I liked the idea of this game, but I wish the combat balance was diffferent.I still enjoyed cheezing through it by holding X, abusing counter and occasional dashing around. I'm actually glad I found this curlpit and didn't have to try that hard. Some days you just want to relax and be a filthy casual :)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually a fan of souls-like games like Dark Souls series and I do enjoy a good challenge, but not with this game. Of course, Dark Souls games are also difficult but the difficulty is mostly caused by our own mistakes and we gradually learn from those mistakes in order to progress, which is what I like, but for Eldest Souls it's totally different.For me, this game is trying so hard to force the impossibility of beating levels, with things like the arena being too narrow while the boss skills takes up space more than half of its area, some boss skills are almost non-interactive, meaning they give very little reaction time, making them almost impossible to dodge and there're also some skills that seem to affect a larger area than the casting area, some bosses that we rarely have a chance to attack because they spam their skills way too often. Sure, all you have to do is just dodge and wait for the opportunity to attack, but I'd say character movement seems to be problematic as well, like dashing in this game sometimes have a delay or no dash at all, especially the diagonal dash where you have to press multiple buttons at the same time.As for the progression, I feel like there're too few early game bosses for us to fight, which isn't enough to strengthen your build before encountering more tougher bosses. This makes the game less fun since your game play will get dull and extremely repetitive early on.My favorite thing about this game is its unique art style and character design, but that's still not enough for me to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: So this is a boss-rush. And literally nothing else. The game tries to pretend to have NPCS and items, but no,it's just bosses. The visual Style is beautiful, but hard to read at times and the perspective chosen makes certain attacks have very different or little tells from certain angles. The 3 (not counting the tutorial one) bosses I have beat so far, were decent. The first one is ripped straight out of darksouls and creatively barren, but mechanically mostly fun. The other two were more interesting, however both suffer from visual clutter.Both your abilities and the boss attacks tend to be flashy.  Combined with the worst dodge I have seen in a while, this makes it hard to avoid hits. Then again, it's not like that really matters. Your good attacks have lifesteal. From the start. This makes fights significantly less tactical and you can easily out-lifesteal some weaker attacks.The combat is otherwise fun and slow enough to feel challenching, but for this to be a "souls-like" it severly lacks core mechanics normally associated with those games. Considering the low price it's not a bad deal, but I was still somewhat disappointed that such a promising concept was executed on such a limited scale.Honestly my biggest critique is less of the game, but more of the store page, which is severely misleading.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a "no" from me chief. This isn't a bossrush, it's a memory game. The boss's are long and generally pretty damn boring. They use poorly telegraphed attacks that will remove half of your health bar every single time. You basically just memorize what the attacks are going to be and how to avoid them. Now that wouldn't be so bad if the boss fights didn't last eighty years (unless you get good rng). So you end up spending WAY to long on a boss and by the time you finish you don't even feel satisfied. It feels more like "Yay, I slammed my head into the wall until the wall finally gave out!"which really isn't the feeling you want when playing these types of games. This game tried to mimic Dark Souls, but fails to understand how to properly balance difficulty and fun, leaving the game just feeling more like a rage game than Dark Souls.

_childDocuments_.review: TRYHARD SOULSThe game presents itself reasonably well and while not exactly a looker has a charming art style and decent core mechanics.What ruins any attempt to enjoy it for me is that it's mostly the way is balanced. The title will give a hint.Imagine any sort of exaggerated stereotype you heard over the years about the alleged unfairness FROM Software games and realize that this is a game where they actually come true.Every boss battle demands to keep your attention for a disproportionate amount of time while being incredibly punishing on every mistake, as from the beginning they come with almost-one-kill hits, on top of multiple phases and extremely BEEFY health bars.Even in case you'll master the moveset of said boss, be assured you'll have to hit these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Now, to be clear, I realize that challenging games have their own niche, difficulty is somewhat subjective and there's probably somewhere a bunch of neurodivergents who can finish this one blindfolded with the Guitar Hero control.Me? I don't give a flying ♥♥♥♥. I'm not enjoying this one.The realization came in the middle of the fourth boss in the game, Eos God of Something. where on Nth attempt I found myself progressing enough to get CLOSE (well,less than a third of his health bar) only to mess up and realize that in the very same fight I had gone between its two phases three times already, hitting the bastard a million times already.But to be fair I realized this already when I tried to play it years ago and I didn't give it a bad review then, so why now? Well, as I was trying the game again today the proverbial straw that broke the camel's back has been trying to pick up my ringing phone only to realize that this game doesn't have a freaking PAUSE.This is not even an online co-op. so that excuse is out of the window. The only reason it's there it's because the devs think way too highly of themselves and the importance of their little game and how much "you should commit to master it", so they probably think the feature  (or more properly the lack of it) should give their game some street cred as "super hardcore".Textbook tryhard.

_childDocuments_.review: I was kind of on the fence of whether i would refund this game when i was 1.5 hours into it since i found myself three bosses away from the final boss. I stuck through with it and i finished NG+ at i think roughly 3.5 hours. At first the game seemed a bit short for the price, but at second glance i think you can easily get your moneys worth out of it. There are 6 main builds for NG which you can switch through freely at anytime. I think most people will stick with 1 build so that means that you can replay through the game at least 5 other times and get a different experience in each of them.The bosses are fun and the world looks pretty, you can see that a lot of love and care went into designing the world and the bosses.As for the game-play, the game feels smooth and responsive and the mechanics such as the dash attack and the life-steal you get from it are fun and make for a fast paced combat.There are achievements for finishing the game without dying and killing bosses without damage which i think is important for a game of this genre. Wish there was one for filling up a whole skill page since it is quite the task.My only gripe with the game was a certain platforming section where i think i died a total of 40 times out of my 80 deaths in NG, please add some borders to the floating rocks in the nightmare world.TLDR; Furi and Darksouls 2d lovechild with a skill system that's fun to tinker around with. For me it is an 8/10, 9/10 if they fix the platforming section.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't feel I can recommend this in good faith.As with most games that have tried to be difficult after the release of Dark Souls, I feel this game tried a little too hard to make a challenging game rather than a fun one. If I could give this a mixed score I would, but I spent more time not having fun than having fun. The bosses all have what feels like way too much health and it makes the losses all the more crushing when a wonky hitbox takes out most of your health. This game has a lot I like going on, but at the end of the day I think you'd best spend your time on a game that wants you to enjoy playing it.Also, no pause feature - why? If you're going to just copy Dark Souls, at least do so in a meaningful way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an absolutely gorgeous combat system. Your attacks have a lot of power, but there is a lot of build-up involved, forcing you to wait for opportune moments (or create your own). There is a ♥♥♥♥ ton of build variety, and the boss designs are different from each other. I liked how most bosses did not have a second phase, (outside of small behaviour shifts), instead boasting a diverse & unique moveset and challenging you right from the get go.There is some small issues with some bosses, such as  Most of the time the bosses are great though and I felt like I was going against a fair, albeit difficult challenge. It took me about 9-10 hrs of actual play time to beat the game, and I beat around the bush a lot. The story and lore is sort of fragmented and cryptic like the souls games. I did like the general vibe and storyline, but I couldn't figure out what was going on all the time with all the NPCs, which can be charming / interesting or annoying depending on what you are looking for.---I've now been just trying to do hitless runs of the bosses in the Arena. More games need features like this! Trying out different builds with the ability points you are expected to have at the start of a boss has been a ton of fun! I finally beat that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Eos without getting hit after hundreds of tries lol. This kind of stuff really adds longevity to the game. I just wish there was a restart button, since I have to wait to die after getting hit to do my hitless run.The achievements in this game really are no nonsense. It adds a lot of replayability, especially since the game has no filler & is very fair. The expansion bosses don't seem to have achievements though :/Oh also I should mention the lifesteal mechanics. Attacking in this game is a form of defense; you don't have an estus or something but instead must attack to regain HP, with a "bloodburst" attack regaining the most HP. This reinforces the whole mechanic of waiting for opportune moments to attack (or doding like crazy, but watch your stamina!), and generally being graceful in how you execute your bursty af moveset. God, I love this game!! Even defense class has a ♥♥♥♥ ton of burst centered around parrying.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very qualified "yes" from me.  There is a lot about this game that I just love, but there are a few substantial negatives.  I got this on sale, which felt worth it at $10.  I don't think I would recommend it at $20 for reasons I'll get into below.First the positives: Trying to keep this to ground the other reviews haven't already stamped smooth, I *love* the RPG/build system built onto the boss-rush formula.  It is well-designed, exciting, and kept me motivated through each new conquest.  And I *love* the boss fights themselves (the designs [if not the execution--see the negatives] for the DLC bosses stand out in particular).  The game bills itself as a souls-like, here meant in the sense of "has a materially important dodge button" and "has epic/gnarly/gross boss fights", with a side of "is an RPG", but what really made the boss designs stand out to me was the way in which they did things that were atypical of souls bosses, like extended dodge puzzles and environment/debuff mechanics, reminiscent almost of an MMORPG-style boss fight (except, of course, being fought as a souls protagonist with a dodge button).  It was very cool, and in playing the game, the vision mostly comes through.The trouble starts coming in with polish.  Throughout my playthrough, I encountered numerous instances (read: this would happen on average once every 10 seconds in combat) where I would attempt to do something, and it just...wouldn't work.  This seemed to be a good mix of both intentional and unintentional.  On the unintentional side, there was at least one extremely frustrating bug, where the corrupted grappling hook ability would just plant itself in the ground in front of me when I pressed the button (this seemed to be contextual, but I could not for the life of me, determine what the context was; and it happened about 30% of the times I attempted to use the ability, which was a lot, because the ability is otherwise extremely good).Beyond bugs, though, there were a number of game elements that felt poorly thought out.  Key among them was the fact that you can't dash through enemies, which, sure, okay, except all the enemies are really sticky in the collision sense (so when your dodge connects with them you just stop).  On the one hand, this is unpleasant and adds a spike of difficulty to the game in the skillset of "precisely aiming my dodge", which, to be blunt, is not the sort of fun I came here to have.  If I press dodge, I expect to dodge.  The normal logic for a top-down game is that I'll dodge through a guy if he's in the way (since I can dodge through [most] attacks), but if that isn't the case, I at least expect that the collision logic will default to moving me *around* the enemy.  The fact that this blanks your highly limited and highly important dodge uses is frustrating, but an especially problematic consequence is that a boss that doesn't move around a lot (e.g. Rotten Crown) can actually pin you in a corner and leave you no way to get out.  I would urge the developers to consider whether this is really a key feature to the game experience.Beyond the goofiness with dodge collisions, animation interrupts were another dynamic that felt out of place and inappropriately frustrating.  It's a thing you wouldn't think would be a big deal, except you basically only have one animation that can be interrupted: your Bloodthirst.  Given that hitstun from enemies' attacks don't affect you in any other way (except sometimes move you around), it is jarring and obnoxious that you can burn your meter to use a (relatively quick) attack and it won't go off because they swiped at you as you pressed the button.  Even Dark Souls (which has a much greater role for hitstun/stagger) doesn't dock you mana if your spell gets interrupted during the casting animation.  Third, as some other reviewers have pointed out, the boss mechanics could use some explication.  Some of them speak for themselves (e.g. Eos), but others (all the DLC bosses in particular) could use a description, in words, of what the things on the screen are supposed to mean.  Where does Rejected Daughter's DoT debuff come from?  What do the bells in the Rotten Crown fight do (hitting them seems to reduce the number of zombies, but, like, not always?)?  Why are there certain hitboxes that I'm not allowed to dash through (mirrors in the Nightmare fight, but there definitely seemed to be others) and how can I identify those?  The developers should (or should have) explore ways of visually (or at least verbally) explaining these mechanics to the player, because many of them are illegible right now.Finally, and this isn't an issue with polish, the game is *short*.  I cleared it in five hours (DLC included), and it's not like that was a smooth run--I died a lot and had plenty of trouble.  There's lots of replay value given that you can continue your build in NG+, but given the quality-of-life issues above, I have to admit I probably won't be replaying it much.  The experience was solidly worth $10, but $20 is asking a bit much for the amount of content and level of quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relatively mixed review - it's a fun, fast paced, difficult boss rush that looks and sounds the part as well. It's very much on the short side, despite exploring the NPC quests, my first playthrough was over within 3 hours, and definitely doesn't live up to the 'brutally challenging' aspect, especially if you utilise your skills well (that red tree just melts bosses).
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Majority of the game mechanics are simply un-fun and poorly designed. Some bosses have awful design and can either lock you in a corner, stun lock you and then kill you with 3 other attacks in about a second, or just have bad hitboxes. Many dodge windows also feel off and decide whether to hit you or not on some occasions.You are unable to cancel charge attacks, meaning you either hit the boss and get hit, or get stun-locked and die.I felt only relief rather than satisfaction after beating all 12 bosses.The game is fine, but the poor mechanics involved are just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls, despite its name, is not a souls-like, but a boss rush. A very good one.+ doesn't waste your time, it's simply good boss fights with no downtime+ a lot of customization on skill tree - you choose one of three skills and upgrade how it works after every boss. Plus you get a boss-core object to modify any of character mechanics (6 slots, 8 cores total) - each configuration is unique, and some slots depend on the tree, so that's in total 13*8=104 unique effects they put in? Many of them are similar and just activate at different times, but it's still impressive for a small game like this+ all of the above can be adjusted at any time+/- difficulty is strange - there are bosses in the middle that I beat on first and second try, far harder than previous ones. Third and fourth boss provided best balance (Unity especially, great fight). Second boss was too tanky and later bosses were alright, since your character gets too powerful, but so do they- there are 12 boss fights and out of these one is a simple tutorial boss, one had far too much visual clutter during second phase to avoid everything properly (Steel) and half of a boss was pretty bad imho (Purity)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Not a souls like, not fun.Tedious boss rush game that is just frustrating by design.Bosses are spongy and can kill you in a few hits.If you like dying by trial and error just to restart a tedious frist phase again, than go for it.If not just avoid it. I played a ton of different souls clones. I cannot recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game succeeds with its design goal of making a game with a guy with a sword who kills his enemies by dodging through their attacks, but they clearly thought it was a lot harder than it is. 8 bosses in a boss-rush game and it only took 2 1/2 hours, because they're really not as difficult as they are made out to be. Extremely disappointing on length, but decent otherwise.If you're not particularly good at this kind of game, it would take a lot longer, and probably be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: bad boss design, underwhelming last boss, no interaction between player and boss at allFeel shallow in different aspects.For example developer choose to implement unit collision in this 2D boss rush game which most of the bosses are huge compare to your character. They always body block you to dead and people feeling super unfair about it. It would be much better if players have choice to utilize the unit collision physics to deal with bosses in certain mechanics or skill sets. Not to mention though the art design of the bosses are quite cool, many of their attack and skills feel so similar. Just with different skins.Sadly not a single boss i found interesting in terms of combat mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend the game. I love boss battles and learning attack patterns, so this game was enjoyable at first.However - with rising difficulty the flaws of the controls or design decisions became clear:- Too much RNG in enemy abilities: for example the god of light light beams - where... - your only dodge / dash ability keeps jumping into the beams because of its fixed range.- permanently getting blocked by enemy bosses trying to dash past them- too hard to properly aim with the sticks with the 3sec attack charge- combat completely focussed around the charge, making "normal" attacks basically useless- healing is too punishing: you get hit after 5min of perfect dodging  - then you can't heal up - you need 5min perfect dodging and hitting again to slowly life leech your health back up - which in most cases forces you to be aggressive instead of careful - others stated that already - it's basically a "No mistake" game - because after doing mistakes you basically can't heal up anywayI enjoyed the attack patterns and beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of the bosses. But the clunky controls combined with the poorly designed moveset and attack skills never made me feel like being full in control of my character. Most of the times I died because of unresponsive movement, dashing into enemy dmg areas because of the dash distance that is just too far or not being able to move past bosses - which is a pity in a melee centered game. You can basically only dash away from the enemy instead of rolling past it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Having heard nothing but praise for Eldest Soul, I decided to jump into the fray, and after defeating just 3 bosses, I can confidently say that the hype is well-deserved. Each boss encounter feels like a tense, high-stakes battle of wits, demanding precise timing and quick thinking, and boss designs are nothing short of awe-inspiring.It's hardcore, so not for who want to win a fight at first try. A bit of trial and error is needed but it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game took me longer to finish because I had to restart every boss to complete the no-hit achievements. Pretty solid indie game though perhaps a little bit more exploration and some fodder enemies would have made it more enjoyable. Right now, it's just running to a boss then another then another. Buy it on sale; it's not worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: There seems to be some discourse on the game's difficulty, so take your skill and familiarity of souls-like into consideration.I found the 3rd and 4th bosses to be pretty brutal and unfair. If I was still in the time range, I'd return it. If you do get it give it a good effort, but return if you're not having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, boss design is exceptional and the fights themselves flow incredibly.  I don't know if this is a common issue with the game, but I have no idea what causes it, so be aware that at least one person has had to deal with this annoyance. Otherwise, the upgrade tree is a bit shallow but functional. The boss cores are more exciting, and can change the function of some of your basic skills/attacks. The game is a boss rush like Titan Souls, in case you haven't looked at every other review, which makes this a point of contention or praise. You'll probably get 5 or so hours out of it, judging by my playtime and progress through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I'm not the greatest gamer so feel free to write my review off as a "Get Gud". I finished Elden Ring and Dark Souls and I play a lot of games but I'm not the best gamer or even that good. I can say that as far as difficulty goes, this falls into the category of being too challenging. Unless you're one of those no-hit speed runners, pass on this game.Lack of customization - you're stuck with what you have. If you can't beat the bosses, you're screwed. The bosses deal way too much damage and tank way too much. This is just poor balancing. Healing mechanic is scuffed. Areas are lifeless and boring. Sometimes, there are obstacles but they're just nuisances and don't really contribute anything.The payoff of beating the bosses just isn't worth it. It feels like a chore and I honestly didn't want to keep playing after some of the bosses. Also, this isn't really souls-like, despite the name, unless your definition of souls-like is to have a dodge mechanic. Feels like the tag was just slapped on just to say "This game is hard".It does some things well. The boss design is great and the art is captivating. Some fights are really well designed. I like the 2D graphics. I appreciate where the developer was going with this but I can't recommend getting this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, yet I couldn't.Say about Pixel art what you will, some love it, some hate it. I think there is gorgeous pixel art, and butt-ugly pixel art. This is a mixture.The game only consists of the 9 main bosses (+3 DLC ones) and New Game + where everything gets harder (and the bosses also act quicker, use more and a bit different moves, etc.). There's also an arena mode that allows you to face all defeated bosses again after you beat the game.For 20 bucks that is already a very steep asking price. But the execution it where it, sadly, falls apart.The general combat loop is okay-ish, but not really suited to this game, imho.For starters, you do not get any active health regen, only passive really. Your character has a rage bar. If that rage bar is full, every swing heals a small amount of your HP. You can also choose more skills and upgrades later on to increase overall healing. And your skill tree determines that as well, of course (there are 3, but I only played the game with the Berserker one, the other ones focus on dodging and shielding, respectively).The problem is that in order to fill your rage bar, you generally have to land a charge attack (which is also necessary to pump out any meaningful damage ... normal attacks are pointless if not powered up), then you get a few swings to heal a bit of life. The charge though takes forever. At least it also is a dash move, but still. You'll be standing around a lot, charging up your attack.The 2nd problem is that it is the propagates the opposite of what the game wants you to do: learn the patterns and make every attack deliberate. What happens instead is that you either tank half the hits, because you know you can deal more DPS and healing just staying still or that you end up in a situation with almost no health, desperately trying to get some back, which often ends in you dying. The risk-reward factor is off, imho.On the plus side, this gives you potentially and with the right build almost permanent, high healing towards the end. The downside is that learning a boss "the right way" is almost futile, because as soon as you take the inevitable 1st hit, you're instinctively trying to heal up, instead of learning the patterns.That being said, this isn't the mechanic that breaks the game for me. That dubious honour is awarded to the "dodge" move. Never in my life have I seen such a bad implementation of a mechanic. Or maybe it's deliberate. In any case: it sucks.You get 3 dash bars that very slowly refill. In a game that requires constant dodging that would be a severe issue. However, you will not deplete a bar IF you manage to "perfect dodge" an attack. And that's the problem... the game has no idea what hit boxes, hit detection and collision are. Most bosses are quite huge, they push you around and into corners. Instead of automatically dodging around or through them like in most 2D or top down games, Eldest Souls simply either ignores your input or has you spending all 3 dodge moves in rapid succession without moving an inch. You have to deliberately dodge to the side or away from bosses, then charge back in, instead of dodging into a boss. That is IF the game even registers that you've just dodged. I've had so many occurrences where I watched the screen, and dodged in the right moment, only for the game to say "naaaah, you didn't dodge". And even more occurrences where I DID dodge through an attack, but apparently the game didn't see that as a perfect dodge. And thus a dash bar was gone. When a boss attacks you multiple times in a row though, that one "missed" dodge can mean you take a big hit, maybe you die, but you're definitely going down the healing-spiral...And that's a shame, because the bosses themselves are well designed in general. Funnily enough though, after the first 6 bosses the game just stops trying to present a challenge. The final boss, as well as the 2 bosses before that one I could basically brute force with occasional dodges. All in all though I liked every one, well minus the Watchdog, perhaps... Just, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dodging or rather not-dodging was infuriating. And thus it's a "no recommend".
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for me a hard pass. The visual style of the game is really nice to look at, the bosses themselves are not that bad either(stopped playing at Hyem and do not intent to continue any further), but the movement/combat is just....naaah dude keep it i don't want it. The attacks are well telegraphed, everytime boss is about to attack i know what is coming, but the dodge window is jsut weird. I dodge right at the start of the attack, but still get hit-you always have to dodge a bit earlier before the boss attacks and not as he attacks, which to me is very irritating. Also lingering hitboxes and the dodge itself being kinda ify at times...just nope
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's a boss rush, except combat mechanics are terrible.Your only viable attack is a charged one, and horribly unpleasant to use on top of that.Add to this that the patterns are really difficult to read and the animations are on par with a low-tier mobile game.The result is that fighting feels incredibly messy.Also:Some attacks are close to impossible to avoid.Arenas are either way too big or way too small.NPCs are absolutely useless, they literally have no purpose but a short dialogue.Seeing 6 bosses was enough for me. Hell na.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to buy this game, prepare yourself for a nice dose of adrenaline because you're going to need it.The world of the game and the overall lore is great, a bit empty and sometimes confusing at the end of the road, but well done.The ost is really well done as well, with a specific theme for each boss.You have this dark theme and the "end of the world" aspect that remind you a bit of the souls game. However, this game is not a souls clone at all. It can go to the "try and die" category and with each death you learn what you did wrong and you do better the next time.The difficulty of the game is well dosed overall, except maybe for the second boss.You are a little soldier and you attack with your big sword the enemy in front of you with light attack or charged attack. Charged attacks fill a gauge that make you recover your life a makes your character better in every aspect. You can consume the rest of your gauge to unleash a powerful blow, and start the cycle again.The basics of the game are easy to understand and there is enough dept into it so you can search for what fits the best in your fightning style. You can maybe win without doing the optimal build but if you wish to complete the game in a superior difficulty you will struggle, a lot.There are 3 different style : Windslide, Berserker and Counter. Each style is a way you have to choose and you can change it anytime and anyway you want to without any cost, witch is really cool and open for testing new things. You will not get "locked" in a style you don't like for the rest of the game.It is a really fun game if you give it a bit of time, and it feels fulfilling to kill all the bosses, especially on the abyssal difficulty. I was surprise to see people stopping to play after beatting the game only once. The game really start on your second run !Note for the devs if they read it : I test a lot of new builds during my progression and find that Windslide is really underperforming compare to the other two. It would be nice to balance things either for your next game or this one. Also the character is really slow if bloodlust is not active. You cannot dodge immediadly after a light and heavy attack. I don't know if it is intended but it annoyed me quit a lot.The second boss (the guardian) has ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit box and is actually harder than most of the rest of the cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Put this game on the shelf after the 3rd boss (its tough) then picked it back up 1 day and toughed it out the rest of the way, took about 8 hours after already having 12 or so clocked into the game. After beating 2 bosses (after many failed attempts) I found myself wanting more story, more content, hell even more bosses that would make me rage after doing 20+ times to the same one.Game is good, fights are hard don't let the people who say "it's easy I beat it in 2 hours" deter you, in fact i dont think you can beat the first 3 bosses in 2 hours to an average souls like player who understands stamina bars, attack patterns, etc. VERDICT:I WANT MORE
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game in 2.5 hours. There's seems to be secret stuff and NG+ content but I'm not really the type to replay over and over. Each boss is pretty original and has a unique fighting style that you have to learn before you can really take it to them. Some are more fun than others, but none feel unfair. On the higher NG+ difficulties I can imagine the bosses being health-spongey as other reviews mentioned, but at least for a vanilla playthrough they were fine. I kind of wish this game was less boss rush and more like a traditional Dark Souls game with mob enemies and the like, because the combat is fairly fun. If you enjoy boss-rush/dark souls style games, you'll probably enjoy this, but I suggest waiting for a sale, as the game is quite short.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: For those who like challenging their reaction time and memory-This is the game. You have to remember the mechanics of each bosses attacks- sounds daunting but after a few hundred deaths, youl start to get it. I loved the simplicity of the skill tree system, it made it very satisfying to activate skills at the right time. The boss shards were kinda disappointing- like for how much effort it took to take them down, I got this? That was the kind of feeling I got. But then again, the game got easier as I progressed and got more shards-so I guess if they were any better itd make the game too easy.Overall- a challenging and satisfying game- not for the weak of will though. Squeeze those buttcheeks and pull through buddy:)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the name deceive you. Eldest Souls is not another low effort soulslike. While there are similarities, Eldest Souls differentiates itself in many ways.Combat:Combat is the main focus of Eldest Souls, and it is done very well. I was initially dubious about mechanics like lifesteal being the only way to regain health, but I think it works to promote an aggressive and fast-paced style, along with the ability trees. While initially simple, essentially starting out as dodge, hit, hit, bloodburst with little strategy, the abilities and infusions quickly develop into something that requires just the right amount of thought put into it. This all adds up to a very satisfying system that rewards aggressive play.Enemy Design:Being a boss rush, there are less enemies that had to be designed, which means less things got overlooked. I don't think I've had a single moment where I felt a move was unfair. There are some things that were a little hard to see at first, or a little difficult to get used to, but for the most part I had no issues. Each boss is very unique, and has it's own moveset with almost no overlap, making for a fresh experience every time you walk into a new boss room.Visuals:I have no gripes with any of the designs in the game. The UI looks good, not cluttered and not oversimplified. Some of the areas look downright gorgeous. The animations are clean and smooth. There is nothing that can be considered to look bad anywhere in this game.Story:Story definitely takes a backseat, you can play the entire game without experiencing any other than the intro cutscene. But the various notes scattered around, descriptions, and quests, do a decent job of establishing a loose idea of what is going. You can definitely see the dark souls influence in this.Bugs:There are numerous bugs in the game, most relatively minor, some having a large impact on gameplay. That being said, this point is effectively nullified by the fact that the developers are actively communicating with the players and continuing to fix any bugs found. I highly recommend joining the Eldest Souls discord server if you want to chat with the devs about the game, get more insights into the development or report a bug.Content:This is potentially one of the most important points I have. There isn't all that much in this game. Gameplay-wise, there's 10 bosses, and an expanded moveset for each at NG+. There's more to do in terms of story, but not much else. (Note: this doesn't mean the game is all that sort given how many times you will probably die). This is to be expected for a first project of 2 developers. If you're the type of person to finish a game once and never touch it again, this may not be for you. However, I do think there is a significant replayability factor, no matter how many times I face these bosses, they never seem to get old. There are also active speedrun leaderboards, so if you're interested in that, definitely check it out.If you like a challenge, and aren't going to abandon it after 1 playthrough, this is a very good game. Definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Know what you're getting into with this one. 9 very difficult bosses, Minimal story with a choose-your-flavor-of-Ice-Cream ending, some basic inventory puzzles, and that's it. Its a good game, but don't get your hopes up for anything other than gameplay, music, or graphicsThe gameplay is fluid, the combat is weighty, and the customization is varied enough that each playthrough is different. My only real problem is with a few of the bosses. Specifically the Deer god feels unfair due to the speed of the blood flowers mechanic, and the 2nd phase has a tendency to overlap attacks to force damage. The other one is the final boss. Its a competent boss, but its just too gimmicky to work thematically, instead of building on the rest of the game it instead just adds a mechanic that was absent from the rest of the game. Other than those 2 the bosses all hit the markThe visuals and music are 11/10. Not much more I could say, it looks gorgeous, it sounds grandiose and epic.The game is a bit lacking in content. There are only 3 different Item quests, and most of them are simple. The only really complex one is the one that unlocks most of the flavors of Ice cream for the ending. While the 9 bosses all get as much as they can out of their respective concepts, its just over too quickly. There is a NG+, which is brutally difficult, even bordering on unfair, it similarly is over rather quickly. Now, this is subjective, as some players take 8-10 hours to get through the game, but for me my first playthrough only took 3. There just isn't enough meat on its bones to keep me engaged for long periods of time, despite my multiple playthroughsAs I've said, the story isn't that good. Even putting aside the Flavor of Ice cream ending, it just doesn't go anywhere. You arrive, kill 7 gods, and then get your flavor of Ice cream. Nothing really happens. Don't go in expecting a deep story, because that's not what the game is trying to do.Overall, go in with the right expectations. Great gameplay, Great soundtrack, great art. That's what the game is offering, so don't look for anything else
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: As a boss rush game it is great. But if you are wanting something like Dark Souls you will find this feels a bit empty. There is a world but it is mostly void of anything. The story progresses by moving from one boss to another. The areas in between kind of feel like a waiting room. This creates a huge problem in the game which is that the bosses have no lead up to them. You can try the same boss over and over again with no consequences. Meaning beating a boss can sometimes come down to just one of those attempts being a lucky one, instead of mastering the boss.Despite this flaw I still found myself coming back to it and enjoying the boss fights.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I played it as a demo before and never managed to beat the second boss. After getting the full version yesterday and struggling a bit, I finally did it!The game is hard, but it's hard because that's how it is meant to be. It is not hard because you don't know what to do - you are always in control of your characters and the abilities are well explained in the tutorials.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, visuals are cool, combat is tight and the talent tree is great (you can swap talents/skills at any time).I really enjoyed the game so far, (Beaten 7 bosses). It's a hard game, but since it's a bossrush game it wouldn't be great if the game was too easy. So far the bosses have been great (some less great, boring mechanics).The only negative thing I have for now is the "charge attack" aspect of the game. You _NEED_ to use your charge attack very often to get lifesteal/dmg etc. (im not a fan of charged attacks in any games, i never use them). I would be fine with it if it didnt come with a dash aswell, or maybe another attack button or something like that.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses 1 or 2 shot you, but require a few hundred hits to kill. Basically you have to avoid almost every single attack without fail or you'll be setting yourself up to get hit by the next attack and killed. You have 3 dashes which can be used, and in the 2nd phases of each fight you'll need to use 2 at a time, meaning again, any mistake generally equals death.I like challenging games but this one just feels like bashing my head into a wall over and over, so no, i can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a trainwreck of unfair design decisions. Tons of bugs and inaccurate hitboxes, all against the player's favor of course. Constant input dropping with the dodge move (and I'm not exaggerating when I say this was the cause of 90% of my deaths.) Enemy attacks are unreadable half the time and they often attack while covered in particle effects from transitions. They also attack really fast depending on RNG and the controls in this game are sluggish and unresponsive, incapable of keeping up.There's never a safe time to do a charge attack (which is 100% required, not only to heal but to do any decent damage) because depending on RNG the enemy could begin an animation and complete an attack all while you're recovering and unable to perform a dodge.I finally gave up when, after struggling with the pile of nonsense that was Eos, the next boss (deer god) was a complete cluster♥♥♥♥ of unintuitive mechanics that I never actually figured out. And in the 1 in 10 attempts I killed the deer god, it had a phase 2 which was a completely different boss and made the first phase seem straight-forward in comparison. Putting one of the most opaque, trial-and-error bosses I've ever seen in any game in a second phase following a pure RNG boss with unreadable animations that you can't really get better at killing is unforgivable. These kinds of poor decisions were found in all bosses up to this point, but this was really the nadir of my experience with the game and a sign that I really shouldn't be pushing forward in hopes of getting something more fun.In summation, if you want to make a game like Dark Souls, you have to earn the difficulty with polish, fairness, tight controls and readability. This game fails in all fronts.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: plenty of noticeable bugs/poor coding.bosses can pin you against walls and trap youthe stupid spider boss creates pools of poison on the floor that you're supposed to be able to clear by activating some fountains on the outer edge of the room, but sometimes they don't clear the poison at all, and you will eventually get stuck in a room full of constant damaging poison AND super slowed down because of the webs that come in later, eventually leaving you in an unwinable situation because while you CAN get rid of the spider webs by attacking a thing at the center of them, you have to stand in the poison anyway to get rid of them. Meanwhile same spider boss has a spinning attack that launches it towards you, and while that is well and dodgeable, that attack can BOUNCE off the walls of the room in a random direction, and guess where they land fairly often? Correct, the spot your dodge animaton is finishing its i-frames.I'm getting tired of people trying to ride the 'souls' bandwagon to get their game more attention and use it as a means to try to pass off a badly made game as "oh yeah, this is a souls style game, it's going to be difficult and challenging but can be beaten with skill"absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SMH.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here I am, 30 more hours spent on this game. I said git gud in my original review (below) but this game it takes on a new meaning. I now own this game on Switch as well as Steam, and I've got about 1400 deaths between the two saves. I only just defeated Azikel, God of Light. My god, how many times I've died to that boss, it defies logic. I don't know how I kept going but I'm glad I did so I could gaze upon his empty throne and laugh.It feels good to overcome adversity. And this game has adversity in spades. If you like hard, punishing games, this game is for you.-----Original Review Below-------Music and ambiance is fantastic, 10/10.Graphics are passable, 6/10.Mood is 12/10. I love a little Lovecraft in my souls-like.Gameplay is 10/10, astoundingly good.Story is ?/?, I will update this later.Like many others, I'm writing this review after defeating the first "real" boss: The Guardian. He is the first real test of your mettle and patience provided, and let me tell you, the test is steeply graded. Like many souls-like games (from soft or otherwise), it is unforgiving, but it is also fair and sets your expectations early. You know going in that one mistake can cost you all the effort you've put in since you started this fight, and you do surprisingly little damage. This is going to be tough. Git gud. There is something glorious about that perfect dodge, the just-in-the-nick-of-time counter activation, the well-timed combo that drops a healthy chunk of a boss' health bar. The dread of being cut down one more time just to start again is palpable, but overcoming a combo just as it is executed upon you and allowing a few precious seconds to punish your prey is magical.

_childDocuments_.review: I have less than 2 hours on this game, but so far I have defeated the bosses up until Eos, and holy hell is this game great. The bosses feel challenging (albeit unfair at times due to the isometric camera), but the reward for being able to recognize their patterns is so massive. Each boss seems to have a gimmick that makes it stand out from the rest, which is nice, because the game keeps you wondering what you are going to encounter next in between zones. The overworld at the beginning is very boring, and there are very clear RPG elements that will come into play, the desolation at least adds to the tension of having to fight the imposing bosses.I am not a huge fan of souls-like games, but I am a fan of difficult titles, and this definitely is definitely one of them. The builds definitely look like they can get insane too, and the game promises to deliver even after clearing the game once. Playing with a controller feels like a must, which is the only downside, but that's a minor complaint as the game was very clearly designed for a game pad. If you want to get your ass kicked over and over again, but think you have the mental fortitude to persevere, this game is a must.Edit: Completed the game, and I can definitely attest to the difficulty of this game. I struggled a few more times than I should have on certain bosses, but at the same time, the game gets immensely easier as you get more buffs and skills. Overall, still a solid buy and I'll be giving NG+ a shot.
