_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing boss rush with a world that doesn't feel like filler. It's a beautiful yet haunted and destroyed land, almost entirely uninhabbited, but the art and sound is just so good you won't mind exploring. Every boss is a lot of fun.If you're pretty good at games like this and feel it's getting easy, just beat it really quick like I did and start NG+. Holy crap, NG+1 is no joke and I missed a weapon upgrade on my blind first play too, yet I found a really powerful build that allowed me to just feel like a bloody god.  Emphasis on the blood.Which brings me to my next point, the build system is AMAZING. Every boss down means new upgrades for your skills and you get a shard from the boss that can either be an active ability, or augment the abilities of your kit.  For example the very first boss you beat gives you a shadowy tendril. It can work like a hookshot from zelda as an active. OR, it can add a purple explosion to your main meter dump attack that does extra damage and steals life from the enemy.  OR it can make your dash leave behind shadowy tendrils that damage your enemy. Every single boss drops a shard that does something like this, and every shard and skill point can be FREELY reassined from the character menu, it doesn't pause the game though so you're not going to be able to realistically do this in combat even if it allows it, but the QoL is so immensely high here I absolutely love it.This might be an indie that hits as hard as Dead Cells, and that's NOT something I say lightly.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: game good, kinda buggy, great bosses and combat. Very challenging but very rewarding. Lots of replayability. Short (took me 6 hours), get on sale.Long review:Ever since I first played Bloodborne (my first Souls game), I loved the feeling of struggling against bosses but then overcoming them by learning their attack patterns and weaknesses.I've never been able to recapture any of those moments since then, even with games such as Dark Souls, Sekiro, and other soulslikes. Not until I played this game.Firstly, the combat. The combat is excellent. You only have one weapon, but you are given a lot of customization through the skill trees and boss gems. The only way to heal in this game is by attacking bosses. In this game, you have to constantly be aggressive if you want to succeed. This playstyle is not for everyone, but it really is satisfying to get a hang of the mechanics.Next, the bosses. All the bosses in this game are incredible. There are only ten bosses, but this only shows that the devs were more worried about quality over quantity, which I personally appreciate. The bosses all ask a lot from you, but they never feel unfair or cheap. There is one boss which I felt was asking too much of me, as the first and second phase were basically separate boss battles with completely different attacks and patterns (and you always have to go through the first phase everytime you die.) But other than that, excellent bosses!With those factors together, this game created a very challenging but rewarding experience for me. I always felt relieved whenever I defeated the next baddy with a smirk on my face. Some of the bosses later in the game were kinda easy, but they were still enjoyable.Now for some of the cons:This game is kinda buggy. When I went to the discussions section on Steam, all I saw were threads about bugs. This is to be expected from a game that just launched, but some of these bugs can soft-lock or you. This biggest most reoccurring bug I got came from the boss gems in the skill tree menu. Basically, you can assign a boss gem onto your skill tree's ability. Whenever I did that, I couldn't change the gem anymore, because whenever I clicked on it, the game would just select another gem slot and I would be able to interact with my skill tree while having the gem menu opened. I fixed it by refunding and re-spending my skill points, but it happened a lot.The bright side is that I never encountered any bugs relating to the combat system itself or any of the boss fights.Game is short. It took me 6.6 hours to complete, but most other people got an average of 4-5 hours out of this game (because I suck c';). But this game is clearly designed with replayability in mind. You're encouraged to continue fighting these bosses just to see how much better you can get. New game+ is a thing, so you can constantly replay through the game as it gets harder and harder.Overall, game is sick. I only recommend it to people who are looking for a short, but very challenging adventure. I recommend picking it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid little boss rush game. It's definitely on the shorter side, but if you're bad at combat, you might not make it through the game ever. It's not as hard (and not as janky) as Dark Souls. The combat system is incredibly well done, and very satisfying. It's a slower type of combat than some other games of the genre, but it feels deliberate and weighty. There is a really flexible combat customization system in place which makes for some fun experimentation.The lore and story is immersive, although there are a couple of things that took me out of it just slightly; the text is sharp while the world is pixelated. It also doesn't have any kind of noise or irregularities in it. It feels a bit pasted on top of the pixel world. And the way some of the lines are phrased seem very modern, especially when it involves pure numbers like "Unit 03" or "250m".Otherwise a very good and polished game! I hope Fallen Flag's next project is a little longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Looked good based on the premise, but it fell short really quickly.The whole game is about boss fights (not really a souls-like) and combat mechanics:-All skills require the player (who wants to optimize a fight) to spend way more time managing counters, bars, stacks and timers. Once you memorize your optimized rotation, that's it.Not refined enough to be worth it, unless you happen to really love this system, not clunky enough to be considered bad.-No matter which of the 3 skill trees you pick, everything is about charge-attacking, filling up the power bar and consuming it with one skill (just one for each skill tree). It feels like there could have been just 1 skill tree with more defining choices.Again, not terrible but also not that interesting.That said, being difficult isn't really a flaw, but since fights (and repeating them) is what constitutes all the content of the game,  I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest fan of games just being boss simulators, like at all. Games that grate down it's inspirations to the bare minimum can work, like Mortal Shell, because it keeps the lesser enemies you fight along the way in mind. Sub enemies aren't just there as a necessity to practice the mechanics of the game you're playing before you fight the belly of the beast, but they contribute to the world around it, and paint the nature of the setting you're exploring. Without that, you're left fighting a boss where you're "practicing" on the spot, which really doesn't work considering you didn't get a chance to learn on much more simple enemies before then and you're just fighting a colossal titan with much more attacks than you,  and this makes a game feel empty and shallow. While i'm not looking for an open world that's needlessly bloated or so huge that the enemies between it make it feel empty, I am looking for there to be at least some variety. Play "there is no light"  it has a similar iso view to this and mechanics, and while it is a different setting and story overall, it's what I was hoping eldest souls would be.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes its hard, good booses, souls like bla bla bla, its nothing new, it does things good BUT... Lets talk about the stuff that make it so great and outstanding. -Bloodthirst mode: by charging your attack you enter the Bloodthirst Mode which doubles the Damage you and lets you Lifesteal. Its similiar to Bloodborne. This makes for an aggresive, high risk high reward gameplay and I love it.-Skilltree: By far the best part of the game and one of the best executed I've ever seen. Ingame its called Fighting style and yes, it really does change the way you approach a boss COMPLETLY. And you can respec anytime too. You got you Agility, Berserk and Counter Tree and in the Tree itself there are two different paths you can take.I think its great to see a new Boss figure him out, change your fighting style accordingly and try again. Its really changes how you approach a boss and again its one of the best Skill Tree I have seen.- The Boss... Trinkeds?: If you beat a boss they drop a kind of Trinked which you can equip in one of 5 slots. They alk have a Theme, one goes about corruption, light etc. You can equip them to empower them either your Bloodburst (special attack) your charged attack or your dash. You can also gain a special ability by equiping theem in the... Ability slot.. Like one will give you a hook shoot and fill your bloodthirst bar etc. And the last one will alter your Fighting style tree. Look these Trinkets change alot and combine them with the Skill Tree you got a vast amount of combinations.Look dont go in a fight being like "Hurr Durr I played Dark souls. Git gud, *spams roll*" No. You will fail be angry and just say its a "bad souls like cuz you played all dark souls"You learn the patters, you get better ingame and you optimize your fighting style and loadout.I love it, it got me hooked

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Having more than 600 collective hours in the Soulsborne series, I can confidently say this game is hands down one of the best Souls-Like games I've ever played, 10/10 well worth the money!Only recently did I find out about this game being a thing and was excited to see that it was coming out within a week after I discovered this project while watching a video by MythyMoo on Youtube.  I'm always fascinated with studios adaptation's to "Souls'-Likes" and if they really do the genre justice by understanding what a Souls-Like really is;  an RPG with a fun yet fitting combat system, unique and challenging bosses, great sound design (boss music included), a well designed world to create an immersive fantasy setting, and a story that the player themselves has to piece together to make their own assumptions about the events that took place.  My favorite souls-like to come out recently that I believe did a great job achieving the above points was Mortal Shell.I believe Eldest Souls is one of the best Souls-Likes to come out, and I can honestly say I'm enjoying it as much as when I went through and played Dark Souls for the first time.  Getting my ass blasted by the second boss in this game for a solid 15 minutes was hilarious and extremely fun,  I haven't beaten the game yet, but I've gone through 7 bosses so far, and I just want to lay out some things that I love about this game:-Every boss has been a 10/10 in terms of design, visually and mechanically.-The artist(s) for the map should be extremely proud of their work, as every area has been a beautiful visual experience,-The audio design in this game is amazing and always hits when it needs to.-So far every piece of dialogue, including the paper logs around the map, have been engaging and fun to read to piece together the story of what happened.-The NPC's in this game are great, I love the dialogue they have and the quest-lines they have with giving them items.-The combat is extremely fluid and really enjoyable to use.-The skill trees are fantastic and I love how different all 3 of them are,The only "downside" that people keep bringing up about this game is how short it is, but from my experience thus far, some of the difficulty for these bosses should keep you well enough occupied to even care about that and want to go into NG+ to beat their ass again (NG+ apparently gives the bosses new mechanics).  I would love to see this game somehow get an expansion for more bosses, not because of it being too short, but because of my eagerness to see what other bosses the developers could come up with.Kudos to the team that made this game, very well done, I can tell there was a lot of passion put into the makings of this.  10/10, would sit there mashing the dash button as Hyem drains all of my stamina with their ice attacks again.

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Furi except bad. I find myself angry at the game a sizable chunk of the time. Somtimes its ok but then it just completely ruins any momentum it had with bad mechanics. My brother would call this type of game a "controller breaker" because he throws the controller across the room.The camera has a mind of its own. Sometimes it follows me, sometimes the boss, sometimes it just does its own thing. No idea why sometimes. I have no control over it. This happens in the middle of combat by the way, not cut scenes.The dodge mechanic is enraging. The dodge button only sometimes works. You need stamina to use it, and it takes 10 entire seconds to recharge to full. So you have to stop having fun and go hide in the corner for 10 seconds. Why is this a thing? I think the dodge also doesn't work on some attacks. Where I come from I-frames mean invincibility, not sometimes avoid one attack. You also cannot cancel out of  your own attack by dodging. Once you hit the attack button you are locked in until it finishes no matter what happens. Its very frustrating. I wish they did the dodge more like how it was in Wizard of Legend or Dark Souls.On top of this there is a mechanic where if your body passes through an attack while dodging you get bonuses. This doesn't work if you dodge an attack and your body doesnt pass through the attack. It forces you to play like a moron and intentionally put yourself in harms way.The bosses in this game have a habit of using lots of area denial weapons. AKA anti-fun. You have to go hide in the corner until the terrain goes back to normal. Oftentimes you cannot even approach a boss because so much stuff is in the way.The charge up attack is a dash, but not a dodge. Even though they look and act very similar, this one wont avoid damage. Thats also a missed opportunity in my opinion. The dodge and charge attack are so similar I sometimes get the buttons confused and im 6 hours in at this point. The bloodburst attack also has a slight forward dash, but that IS a dodge (I think). Or maybe it just teleports you forward. Its a strange way of doing combat and I dont like it.The terrain in some arenas is NOT flat and you can get stuck on it. Not sure why they did this but ok. The second boss in particular has some stuff on the left side of the room but not the right. It was enraging until I figured out I had to only fight him on the right side of the room. The Eos fight has the arena being wider than it is tall, which is not obvious at first till you get blown up by his explosions even though you are pressed against the wall.

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, just overpriced.If you're familiar with another indie game called Titan Souls, this game is a little like that but more complicated. This is a short, top-down boss rush game ("boss rush" meaning there are no other enemies to fight, only bosses). You take your little chibi guy and swing his giant sword at things until they stop moving. The fights are actually pretty well done and the environments are as well. A couple of things of note, however:- The length of the game is entirely dependent on how good you are at it. If you've already played other difficult action games like Bloodborne or Blasphemous (and have good peripheral vision), you're going to have a relatively easier time here than most of the reviews make it sound. Not counting the DLC or NG+, which do add a respectable amount of extra content to the game, you can probably clear the main game in about 5 hours.- Bosses are the only combat, but the areas between them are just slightly too expansive, making the game feel empty. There's a few things to pick up and/or read, but trekking through these areas can feel a little boring with nothing to do.It's a well-crafted game tailored to a higher skill level, and unlike most games that are described that way, this one is actually pretty fair (if you have good peripheral vision and pattern recognition). I just don't quite recommend it at $20. The bosses are good, but the empty overworld, short duration, and lethargic music make it ultimately forgettable, so I would only pick this up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but for the most part I just mashed my way through the boss fights. The different types of builds are negligible, because the same combo and game flow is used for each of them, charge attack, light attack until your meter is almost at half, then hit B. The movement feels clunky, with the dash being at the core of the problem. Not being able to dash through enemies feels like a huge oversight, as perfect dodging melee attacks feels unintuitive when you get stopped on the bosses body. On top of this, if you run out of stamina, the base movement speed is far too slow to dodge most attacks. This is primarily an issue with melee heavy bosses, as most of the ranged bosses have plenty of perfect dodge opportunities.Admittedly, I did not do all of the optional item fetching, but I always talked to new NPCs I found. Most of them were fun to look at, but the dialogue was nothing special and I didn't feel an obligation to help them with anything they wanted.All in all I had a very "ok" time with the game. I liked it enough to beat it, but it is forgettable when compared to other games in it's genre such as Hotline Miami, Hyperlight Drifter, Titan Souls, or Enter the Gungeon. Based on "Game Feel" alone I would rate this game 4/10, given how bad the movement feels to use, but the boss designs were fun and unique so I think a 5 is fair.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Difficulty Padding: The Game. 8 Bosses/~90 minutes of content stretched to infinity.The bosses are unfair by design but doable. While you have to hit them like 100 times, they can kill you in 2 hits (or less in some cases). Dodging their attacks is key, but almost unavoidable chip damage forces you to take risks to heal and stay alive. There are no partial hits; everything seems to apply full damage, even if you stand far from the center of the attack, walk into the aftereffect, or multiple things hit you at the same time. This is a legitimate game loop, but I wouldn't call it exactly hard but fair. I have gripes with the imprecise controls. I get stuck all the time on some ledge or the boss itself, and the character seems to move at an inconsistent speed. Maybe this is due to the tendency to overheat my system. Nonetheless, this points towards a lack of polish and optimization. The story is thin, and there is nothing else to do in the (non souls-like) game if you get stuck on a boss (other than "git gud" or uninstall). Apart from that, there is a cleverly crafted boss rush for those who seek a challenge (or two in NG+). I can see why some people love this game, but I didn't get fully hooked. The price point for this game is largely irrelevant. Sale or not, I would rather recommend trying it for 90 minutes and then walking away or buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Two main problems:1. Just not enough content. Eight boss battles, and that's it.2. The combat system is all right, except for the dodge mechanics. Basically dodging/dashing consumes one of three stamina bars. If the game determines you did a "perfect" dodge, then you will keep your stamina. Otherwise, you have to wait a long time for the stamina to recover. Getting perfect dodges is key to staying alive, but what the game considers to be a "perfect" dodge is completely arbitrary. If you see the enemy prepare an attack, and you dash behind the enemy so the attack wiffs you, then well sorry that's not perfect! On the other hand, if you stand still and the enemy's attack misses you, but you dash through the attack's hitbox, then congratulations your dodge was "perfect"!! Basically the devs are punishing you for not dodging in the exact manner they intend, even if it looks and feels wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a boss rush game heavily inspired by Dark Souls (if you couldn't tell by the title). While the game tries to differentiate itself in multiple ways from Dark Souls, a few of those changes end up making the game a bit too forgiving.In Eldest Souls, you have stamina but it's only used for dodging. There's no blocking or parrying in this game. Furthermore, stamina recovers really slowly BUT if you dodge an enemy's attack (i.e. their hitbox connects with you while you're in your dodging animation), then your stamina recovers almost instantaneously. This is very good as it encourages players to try and master the bosses they're fighting and their attacks. I would say this is an improvement over Dark Souls because in that game, it can be far too easy to simply block all enemies' attack (e.g. with a strength build using great shields) or to spam dodge roll. In regards to your offensive capabilities, you can light attack and charge attack. If you charge attack, you gain the "Bloodthirst" effect. While you have the "Bloodthirst" effect, you can do a "Bloodburst" attack, which is basically a heavy attack, that does a lot of damage but removes the Bloodthirst effect. Furthermore, while under the Bloodthirst effect, you do increased damage, attack faster, and gain life steal on the damage you deal. That last part about "gaining life steal on the damage you deal" is what causes the game to be a bit too forgiving. This isn't Bloodborne where you can regain SOME of your recently lost HP by attacking. In Eldest Souls, you can go from like 10/100 HP to full HP with one big attack. What this means is that you don't have to respect all of the bosses' attacks. If the attack only does like 10-25% of your HP as damage, then it's not a big deal because you know you'll heal up that damage by the time the boss does their next attack. Only attacks that do more than 25% of your HP as damage do you have to worry about and try to dodge.Having said the above, it's not like the bosses are a complete cake walk. Every boss has some hard-hitting attacks, and so I did have to master them to some degree in order to beat them. I even died multiple times to a lot of the bosses, so the game still provides a decent challenge. Furthermore, while the game is relatively short (can be finished in like 5 hours), there's new game plus which causes all the bosses to get enhanced attacks, get more hp, deal more damage, etc… Not only that, but you as the player can try out different ways of fighting the bosses in subsequent playthroughs. As you beat bosses, you gain skill points (which carry over to new game plus) that can be used in 1 of 3 skill trees. There's a Berserker style, Windslide Style, and Counter style. All of the styles play pretty differently from each other, which keeps the game from getting stale so you're looking at around 15 hours of content assuming you try a different style in each playthrough. In my 1st playthrough, I played the Counter style, and it was a decent amount of fun since while I was ignoring the smaller attacks of the bosses, I was waiting for the bosses' hard hitting moves so that I could counter them for big damage. I decided to play 2 more playthroughs, as I was hoping that the increased damage and new moves that the bosses gained would make me respect them more and provide a decent challenge. While that was true to some degree…..once I started using the Berserker style, the bosses became WAY too easy (even on new game plus++!!!). Berserker style is all about doing big hits constantly, and these hits basically always restore you to full health with the right build. So if the boss couldn't basically one hit kill me, I didn't care about their attack. I am sure that at some point, subsequent playthroughs will cause the damage of the bosses' attacks to be so high that I will have to care about every single one of their attacks. I could even see this near the end of the 2nd playthrough where the last DLC boss and main boss suddenly had a lot of attacks that could one hit kill me, so I had to actually master them in order to beat them…..but 3 playthroughs is enough for me.Overall, Eldest Souls is a pretty decent boss rush, if a bit too forgiving.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah, this game's controls is crap. There is no input queuing, so if you want to dash after you attack, you better dash after the animation ends of you won't dash. There is also no animation cancel, once you are charging and you see the enemy attacking, you cannot cancel your charge. And since enemies don't stagger, and will hit you when you hit them, this guarantees a loss on your side since you can't cancel and dash away even if you see the attack coming, an utter garbage system. Attack direction just changes for no reason, making you miss consecutive attacks. Oh right, you talk and press the "triangle" button to skip to next dialogue, but somehow to end the dialogue, you have to press a "circle"... who even design such a stupid feature?? Hit boxes aren't accurate, many times it's bigger than the enemy's animation. Stupid stamina system, you are limited to 3 dash and it charges pretty slowly, but because dash is integral to the battle, having no stamina is a guaranteed death, enemies just attack you 3 times while you walk slowly. Played Hades, Curse of Dead Gods, Devil Slayer Raksasi, Warm Snow, and a number of isometric action games, this is the worst garbage control. I've never wrote a review so fast, usually I end a game before writing one.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, I'll review a game after I've completed it, but I think I've played enough already to get a general idea of what it is. First, though, I'd like to address the idea of a "Souls-like", because I think the people that actually describe a game that way are smooth-brains, and it physically and psychologically hurts me to see and hear the term thrown around. There is no such thing as a Souls-like game. If you're describing a game that way because it's difficult, Super Meat Boy is a Souls-like. If you're using the term because you leave something behind when you die, then Sonic games are Souls-like. If you're using that term to describe games in which you can dodge-roll, Megaman X7 is a Souls-like. If you use the term to describe games in which you can't jump, Phasmophobia is a Souls-like. The term describes nothing, and it's just thrown around to call games with no resemblance to Dark Souls a Dark Souls game, so that people will try it for sheer difficulty and then compare the two despite there being no reason to do so. That said, basically every game that's been referred to as a Souls-like still has more polish and more depth of gameplay than Dark Souls. It says more about Dark Souls than it does those games.Regardless, Eldest Souls has decent combat, I like the charge attack mechanic since it allows you to quickly close distance and throw a few attacks without using your dodge roll to engage, and it feels very nice. I also appreciate that it triggers a type of hyper mode that allows your attacks to life-steal instead of needing to use items or a limited power to heal yourself. The art direction is great, all of the bosses look fantastic, and it's really neat that all of the bosses can change forms when entering their second phase, and bosses transforming like this, in my mind, makes up for the lack of mooks in the game. The style system that you use the talent points to upgrade is really interesting and I look forward to testing it out some, especially since you can switch talents without losing your talent points, you just move them from one place to another.Now, with the positives out of the way, onto the negatives; The fights feel like banging your head against a wall until you manage to kill the damn things. Their attacks are like playing a bullet hell with a dodge roll. some of them move around CONSTANTLY, and feel like you're fighting multiple enemies at once. One in particular, the one that made me decide to write this review, has two healthbars, and the first recharges every time it finishes its second phase, and is two enemies at once that launch attacks that cover nearly the entire battle area. Another fires rotating, map-covering lasers, and has an attack that covers half the battle arena. All attacks will kill you in 2-3 hits, and will tick multiple times. Multiple times, I've successfully finished the first phase of a boss without getting hit, only for it to start an attack that covers nearly the entire map, tick damage 2-3 times and kill me near-instantly. I consider this type of difficulty artificial, and I despise it. I fully intend to finish this game, and I'll probably enjoy it at least a little, however I do not recommend anyone paying full price for it, as there are more difficult games that are far more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: My personal opinion:"Eldest Souls" is one of the best Souls-like 2D pixel art games I have ever played in my entire life. The game is basically about fighting a couple of bosses and kind of exploring the world and lore if you are willing to. The sound design is as good as the visual design. They are not perfect, but definitely good as hell. The boss fights are so damn hard, and I love it. At first, you may think that the game forces you to play in one way, but later you can choose which boss you would like to beat before the others so you can power up. About leveling up, whoever made this system, he/she/it balanced it well, and basically every build is good. _childDocuments_.review: "Eldest Souls" wants so badly to be spoken of in the same breath as its purported inspiration, but it makes so many divergences that I can't even consider it a 'Souls-like,' for reasons both good and bad.  I very much welcomed how there are no eponymous "Souls" and no grinding, as well as no corpse/bloodstain-retrieval runs—you can just press "Retry" to start a boss battle over, which is wonderful.  The settings starts as boring but gets more interesting as it goes, but I found the story dull.  It feels like a bog-standard edgy (not even "dark" or scary, just edgy and depressing) fantasy setting with few standout elements until toward the very end of the game.  I never particularly loved Dark Souls' jigsaw-puzzle method of story presentation, but I got the feeling something potentially interesting was waiting beneath the service for people who were willing to cobble all of the item descriptions and random documents into some sort of bigger meaning.  Eldest Souls' story feels like every other "this world is doomed" fantasy, complete with religious references that feel like ominous or mournful Bible passages with a few words changed.The game is an isometric boss run cut up into exploratory segments.  I like the way stamina works (instead of using fractions of a bar, you have dedicated dodge segments that tell you how many dodges you have left before you need to recharge), but as many other people have mentioned, movement is very slow.  I get how this works in-universe, since you're carrying around an enormous greatsword, but the final product looks like a much slower Supergiant game but feels slow enough to make Dark Souls 1 look like a good number of its successors.  This isn't an insurmountable problem—the plodding pacing didn't stop me from getting all of the achievements in Dark Souls 1, which for all my issues with it felt like more of an accomplishment than just beating Eldest Souls once did—and certain playstyles can render a large part of your own speed issue moot, even against environmental hazards, but it still tends to look silly when certain bosses can unleash devastating attacks that, even with your very slow movement speed, you don't even need to dodge to be able to avoid.  A lot of combat revolves around charge-up attacks that can be in turn detonated for additional effects.Blah blah, skill trees.  Dodging, raw damage, and defense.  I got little use out of the third and (understandably) widely see most of the recommendation go toward the first, but I finished most of the boss fights in my completed playthrough using the raw-damage section.  Each section has two branches, and even though you can only invest skill points into one of the three playstyles at a time, you can still invest in either or both of a given playstyle's respective branches, and you can change your choices outside of battle without cost or penalty.  I do agree with others that enemies have too much health for my taste, and I'll absolutely say that even your most devastating attacks will only do a tiny amount of damage to an enemy's health.  While again this wasn't enough to keep me from finishing the game, I feel like it's just not as fun as it should be to memorize an enemy's entire attack pattern, wail on it with all of your most powerful attacks, and see an enemy's health bar drop by twenty percent, if even that.Some parts of the game allow you to engage a number of boss fights in a chosen order, but the game definitely feels like it has an optimal order that it doesn't communicate to you.  In one section where there are several separate branches (one of which itself has a set of three bosses you face and heal from one after the other), there's another boss I didn't discover until I'd defeated most of the others.  It was pitifully easy in a way that I don't know if the game intended.  One of the game's menu tips tells you that you can reselect your skills at any time, but this is misleading since you can't do this in the middle of a boss battle, and oftentimes clicking "Retry" will instantly aggro the boss to you again, making you stuck with your current build.  This game doesn't have multiplayer, but   There is an Arena Mode that unlocks after the game is complete, where you can pull up the various bosses from a menu, which is a nice touch.  Non-combat exploration gets tedious, since while having no non-boss enemies is a refreshing touch, it also gets boring since only a few areas have deadly environmental obstacles, so even with side quests to account for (of course there's no quest log), usually you're just looking for the next fast-travel point or sparkling item.I feel like the advantages you get from various playstyle upgrades are too often minuscule, which is a shame because there are a lot of good ideas here.  Most defeated bosses drop magical items that can be reversibly slotted into various aspects of your character sheet and provide upgrades that have different effects depending on where they are placed but that also feel unified according to a common aesthetic.  One boss's effects damage you if you're above a certain amount of health while healing you if you're below that; another boss's effects mimic the moon's phases, and so on.  This would be a lot easier to appreciate if enemies didn't feel like they have 50% more health than they need to make the player feel like they've earned a victory.I do think this game went to a strong effort of looking like one of those games that was made by one person, but aspects of it feel very much divided against one another, especially the boss designs, which range from "very cool if unoriginal" to "blatant ripoff" (in the foremost un-fun encounter, one of the mid-game bosses could easily be ).  It's a shame, since the boss music itself is consistently superb, and a lot of the boss aesthetics are graphically impressive relative to the art style.  But I wouldn't recommend paying more than my $5 sale price, not even because the game is short (it only took me about 10 hours to finish, a fraction of which went unreported because my Internet went out) but because the accomplishment of finishing the game felt only as mild as the recommendation I'm giving.  As far as games that were made by a company of people, however, if you don't mind paying more money and you'd rather have something with a more interesting aesthetic, also-difficult boss fights, and much more engrossing writing, I'd just recommend you buy "Hades" instead, and I never even finished it.

_childDocuments_.review: No trash mobs, no backtracking, no repetition. Just straight up boss battles with a little bit of exploration thrown in. _childDocuments_.review: A masterclass of boss rush game design. The bosses are so well made and the dance between the games mechanics and the bosses are incredibly well done. If they were incorporated into a legit Fromsoft game people would be singing their praises.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a fair shot, but it quickly became clear that the lack of visual clarity is persistent with almost all bosses. _childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is worth every cent. For the first two or three bosses Eldest Souls seems like a decent 2D adaptation of the Dark Souls formula, and then, then you meet Eos. You better start learning those Eldest Souls mechanics properly, otherwise those flying balls will curb stomp you into questioning if all that Souls experience has just been a dream and in reality you've never even left the Undead Asylum. Holy sh*t. If ever there was a 'skill check' boss, Eos is it.  After initally being in disbelieve at the perceived bullshiterry with his HP pool, once I got the hang of things, he might be one of my favourite boss designs, period. He really forces you to git gut.Overall the game has damn great boss designs, both in terms of gameplay and flavour.  If I had anything to criticise it is that the difficulty pacing feels a bit off. The mid-game encounters felt much harder than the late game bosses - though none of them is a pushover. However, if you try the three DLC bosses difficulty does spike back up again, with Rotten Crown being one of the hardest bosses I've ever faced in a Soulslike. Dude makes Midir and Malenia look like absolute whimps.I can definitely recommended Eldest Souls for fans of the genre. Replayability is definitely there two, with NG+, Arena Mode, and Iron Challenges (no hit) giving you plenty of wall to bash your head against. A caveat would be that I wouldn't recommend Eldest Souls for people new to the Soulslike genre, there are definitely more beginne friendly games out there. edit: If they ever decide to add more bosses via payed DLCs - I'm up for it. give me 2-4 bosses a pop for a reasonable price, and I'm in.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm no stranger to difficult games and 'soulslike' series, but the biggest issue I'm running into playing this is the fact that the game is bizarrely isometric but only operates on two dimensions.Presenting a game with a pseudo-isometric appearance but being strictly top-down (Binding of Issac style) is incredibly frustrating when trying to dodge or move around the world. You can walk into enemies and get stuck on walls even though the sprites are not on the same plane, but because the 'hitbox' of the enemy is pushing against you, you can be stuck.For example, the second boss fight is my current hurdle due to the bad design of the 2D world having a need for 3D mobility. Several times I've become stuck when dodging away from the boss. Additionally, the boss can summon 3 spears that instantly hit you if you're anywhere near them, and because this game has a 2D plane, at any point you can take damage by them crossing the path. The hitbox is also active for the entire model, not just the tip as it should be. Dodging directly through a spear will cause you to take damage.Another issue: Dodge. Dodge is not Dark Souls iFrame dodge like you might think. It's more akin to the Sekiro dodge where it's a positional avoidance tool. The timing on the iFrames have got to be some absurdly tight window, because allegedly dodging 'correctly' will give you a Stamina boost, but so far I've not been able to hit those windows if they do exist.I'm only giving this a thumbs down because Soulslike Zelda needs more testing and better hitboxes. Having a boss's head pin you to a wall while their body is out of reach is not conducive to a quality game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: All right. Where to begin with. Ah, yes! It was 2018 and I met the developers at the Milan Games Week, in the indie games stand that I usually haunt, looking for new, non major, stuff that is gonna come out because you find diamonds among small indies.Besides the fact that I was flirting with their PR (can't help, she was too cute), I played the demo of the game and it was just few scenes and a boss fight. And what a boss fight. Almost harder to get than the PR. Which I didn't get, in case you're wondering.Anyway, I knew this game was good at the time and I have been waiting for the release since then. I had to wait THREE FREAKING YEARS to play this thing and I am ABSOLUTELY DELIGHTED.It is a soulslike indeed, not as much for the background but those damn boss fights in pure style DKS, that try to wear your patience down and make you yell insanely and punch your desk or your brother that just randomly entered your room without knocking and DON'T YOU SEE I'M BUSY TRYING TO NOT DIE YOU IDIOT?This is the soul of this game. Exhausting and then rewarding. ANd when you have finished your stock of blasphemies, you get to the next boss and you fill up your bucket of swear words or invent new ones.A very simple soulslike with lore to be explored and the perfect outlet for your yells.Totally worth the price.- Don't play if you're already frustrated and you broke more than 5 controllers.

If you didn't already get it I would and if you have check out the DLC it's pretty dope plus the new weapons based on your playstyle are sick cosmetic and playwise you also get a new relic after completing the new bosses which is sick.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has nothing but boss fights, clunky controls, and confusing pixel art (try to figure out where the floor ends and the wall begins until you bump into it).It could be good if it had responsive controls (like Hades or Children of Morta, even though those games have more than only boss fights), but in its current state it's not fun at all. Moreover, bosses kill you in 1-2 hits, but you deal miniscule damage to them, so this game is even more punishing to mistakes than any of the Souls games. You might argue "git gud", but with clunky controls and horrible pixel art trying to master this game is no fun at all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard just for the sake of being hard. As someone with hundreds of hours of the Dark Souls games, I love a good challenge, but, it shouldn't take ~30 deaths to kill a boss. Also, the way you heal in this game is to do a heavy attack, and you have ~5 seconds to attack an enemy, and you gain a small percentage of the deal you damage. Problem is, the heavy attack wind up can cost you a life, and you need to get up close to the boss to get this chance to heal. A lot of the time, however, the game punishes you for getting close to the boss. It's a good idea, but it's terrible executed. There are three different combat types you can choose, a fast but somewhat weak type, a slow but powerful type, and a defensive type. To be honest, I can't even imagine how long it would have taken me to beat the first few bosses without using the defensive one, because at least with that one, if you time your block correctly, you perform a counter. Not only that, but the defensive play style seems to have more ways to heal.Will I keep playing it? Yeah, probably, because I already dumped an afternoon into it, and would kinda feel "defeated" if I didn't finish it. If you're a fan of playing against the same boss many, many, MANY times over, then this game is for you. Otherwise, unless it's on a heavy discount, or you get it for free, I would recommend you skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I, a big soulslike fan, like the idea and the flavour of game, it is just very raw and borderline playable because of wacky controls.Soulslike games are great because they are tough, but fair, and every time you make a mistake, you know - that is on you.In this game - it is almost always the controls. I tried both controller and mouse/keyboard.The core attack system of the game is charged jump, which should always hit the boss, or you will surely end up dying.It is very easy to do with the mouse, becuse you jump right to the cursor.But, as you can imagine, it is very hard to do with gamepad, because stick is not good for aiming at all.For the reference, imagine Hades, but you are forced to play with the bow and you can't ignore it, because it's crucial. So, no gamepad, though they specificly say, that game is meant to play with the controller.But if you play with K&M, you'll fimd out, that the movement is very limited and requires of you to very quickly change the direction of moving in 360' angle, and keyboard can't do that.Bosses always block you, and, because of the specific visual design, you can't really see anything and react accordingly.Dash has only 3 charges and insanely slow recharge, without any means to make it better. So you can't even cheese you way out with stamina management. On top of all that, game is very punishable and you will die from 2-3 strikes usually, which are badly telegraped.As summary, you are not fighting bosses as much as poor controls and design. This is not fun.Not to mention that the game is about 5 hours long, and they charge for is as it's 50 hours long.So at this point, I can't recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Want to like it..but no. It's not fun to me. There is 0 exploration in game, which seems to be odd, you literally just go boss after boss. It's my fault that I didn't realize it's a boss rush game, so this shouldn't be the main reason to not recommend it. The main problem I have with even the boss fight is, it's not fun. At least at the early stage of the game, the only mean to recover health also happens to be attack. Basically what's going on is you attack to recover your heath. Attack is risky, in order to recover health you also have to attack, wait but attack is risky? Yep, it's that loop. Basically you HAVE to attack not matter what, there is no "safe time" during the boss fight like DS where you can run to the corner, take a breath, drink, then fight. And if that's it, aside from some repetitiveness it's really fine (since you are literally just using 2 buttons ALL THE TIME), another problem comes with this mechanism is how ridiculous the damage the boss does and how little damage you do. Boss usually 1 or 2 shots you, and the amount of damage you do is pathetic, bosses obviously have more than 1 phase. So after spending quite some time you get to second phase for the first time, it takes 5s for the boss to kill you if you are not familiar with the movements, now start again to the first phase with your pathetic damage to get to second phase. It's just not fun at this point due to the damage you can do. Honestly I don't mind multiple phases as long as I can get through it rather fast, like nameless king's in DS3 first phase is fast once you know what to do, but for this game, even if you know what to do, it simply just has to take time because you can't upgrade until AFTER you beat the boss. After couple tries this becomes very very repetitive.I know there are ppl think it's fun and is 100x better than me, I am not saying it's a bad game, it's just not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a hard action game with a dreary, messed up environment from some cataclysm that happened before the game starts. It  doesn't have multiple weapons, level ups, non-boss enemies, a customizable character, and it's lore is presented in a much more bog-standard method. This game has Souls in the title but it has few of the aspects that people who like Soulslike enjoy outside of the combat is slow and the game is difficulty.The good: The art and music is fine but it feels pretty generic for the genre, the world and boss design feel very standard and I don't think a lot of the designs really stand out all that much.  The game also runs well with it running at high frame-rates which is good for games like this. Getting back into fights is really quick and easy along with saving the game.  The idea of using boss souls to be abilities like a Metroidvania is a great concept instead of what the souls games do with them as well.The bad: Remember what I said about alright designs earlier, the game doesn't do itself any favors by having the first boss be a very blatant attempt at Iudex Gundyr that doesn't really hold a candle to the OG parasite armor man.  It also feels needless to have a overworld and then barely have any of it be usable because there are very few items that effect the game which sucks because I think if this game just had some healing or buff items it would be a more worthwhile experience.  The focus on story is weird, the intro to the game is fine and interesting but finding notes describing the catastrophe feels so weird and very un-Soulslike.  The games method of healing feels weird and clunky makes you play the way the devs want you to play it with little flexibility.  I think the games is clunky overall, the targeting mechanics don't work sometimes, the dodge looks awkward as it's hard to tell you're actually doing it, the games has some bad hitboxes which is weird for a pixel based game, the camera can be your worst enemy as it moves out of the way of attacks that are going to hit you, and the game is dark overall to the point I had to brighten my monitor because the game doesn't have any sliders for this.I think if the game had more variety in what you could use (more weapons and less emphasis on styles) and addressed some of the major complaints I had, the a sequel for the game could be a very fun time.  Though ultimately I think having Souls in the title does bring in people with the wrong expectations because this game is much better framed with the hard, slow, boss rush aspects rather than the overall Soulslike framing because the game lacks so many elements of the framework while it desperately tries to advertise itself as one.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a console ported 2D retro pixel top down brawler with lightweight RPG elements.  The RPG elements (nice skill tree etc) are welcome but overall, the game is horribly deficient in terms of both concept and technical implementation.  And not just because 2D top down brawling is an incredible archaic, obsolete and generally un-fun consolesque kind of game mode that amateur developers love because it's easy and they don't need to know much about game development to churn one out. The game is notably designed to be specifically very difficult, in a "Soulslike" vein.  In fact the developers unabashedly tried to associated themselves with the developers of Dark Souls by copying their trademarked name (not ok... and in this case, a bit cringey).This is a generally poor and unpleasant design choice, and while at face value it should make the game seem "Challenging", more often than not this is done deliberately by developers to make it harder for gamers to access the full content of the game, reducing the amount of overall effort the developer needs to add before they can push the game to Steam.  Whether that's the case here, I'll leave to the gamers to decide, but for sure, it makes the game frustrating and un-fun to play, a surefire deterrent.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The controls and game handling are notably very clunky and unsmooth here.  It's janky and unsatisfying to play... and any experienced gamer will tell you, the handling, responsiveness and general gameplay feel of the control scheme must be well polished for this kind of game to succeed.  Unfortunately, this is something the developer seems to have phoned in, with little to no apparent gameplay testing.  They dropped the ball on this one.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Eldest Souls has the laughable price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Grand Theft Auto V", "Dark Souls III" or "Mass Effect Trilogy Pack".  That's right, this pixelcrap garbage costs MORE than Dark Souls 3, and the developers here didn't even know how to do video game graphics properly.  What a joke!  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I often don't recommend a game unless it is trully terrible but I can only recommend this game to a very few people who enjoy sitting down and trying to conquer a boss or two in a play session and trying to overcome the extreme challenges this game throws at you. This game is hard, yes some of the mechanics are extremely hard to master especially the dodge mechanic since you only have three stamina bars (which is why using the perfect dodge = no stamina lost upgrade is vital for any real play through for this game, I don't know why this is not default). I want to go through the things I like and than go into the aspects I didn't like.Level Design: I do think the art style is very nice, its convenient that all the important npc are near the teleportation crystals. I do think that most of the boss arenas are appropriately size. The environmental puzzles are nice and not annoying unlike Unsouled where I thought they did this super poorly (unsouled is the closest game to this one which I will be referring to in this review). But why are there no mobs anywhere in the world? This game desperately needs a break between boss fights because thats all it is. Walking from boss fight to boss fight. Which btw sidenote why don't we have infinite dash when not in environmental hazard zones since there are no enemies?? I feel like devs ran out of time and it really hurts the game. They designed a whole ass skill tree and all these special abilities that you can swap in and out but there are no small mobs to practice on between bossfight so you don't know which ability you're going to like. Mobs also help the player visually understand the theme of the next boss, helping to build a visual story to add into the game's lore/story. The only times we learn anything from the bosses you are fighting is from a few npcs which don't appear for every boss, Why not use the notes that you sometimes find around the map tell you more about the boss instead of having to create a whole new npc character since the devs definitely had trouble with making more characters in this game. Unsouled did this quite well where for each boss they had 5 notes that you can find throughout the level tell you about their backstory (they weren't very good but at least they tried and it did make the bossfight more interesting) accompanied with mobs that fit the theme of the level. Its such a huge misstep and very unfortunate because many bosses in this game has extremely cool designs but they have no minions to support them or substantial backstory especially how this game is about man vs god. Are the bosses demi-gods? Man's creation to counter the gods used against them? corrupted beings? nothing. If you want to feel something (like stakes) for your boss fights or understand the world go play bloodborne or elden ring because it ain't here chief.Progression: I really like the awards you get from defeating a boss in this game. In eldest souls defeating boss grants you their soul and you can use the soul to modify and change your core abilities, some can inflict burn on the enemy others can lifesteal and so on and the best part you can change them in and out with other boss souls allowing pretty cool combos and builds. This is by far the best part of the gameplay and definitely very well polished and thought. It isn't very cool you can't test your build on mobs before heading into a bossfight and in order to change anything out during a boss fight once you realise you don't like something is kinda a forfeit on the run since there is no pause in the game is kinda annoying but a really good feature. Now there also a skill tree. I think its pretty simple and easy to understand. You have three different skill trees in the game that affects what I like to think of as your ultimate ability. Its shame however that you can't change your ultimate ability throughout the whole game unless you want to reset your whole skill tree which its not very viable to do so since the only way to earn skill points to upgrade in the skill tree is by defeating bosses and each boss defeated = 1 skill point and the more you upgrade eventually it goes up in cost but thankfully very little and slowly. Once again if this game had mobs and exp system this wouldn't be a problem but it is. The boss fight to boss fight is very draining and there is no way anyone whose casually playing this game will ever be willing to sit down and do multiple bossfights in a single play session since each bossfight is pretty hard and some are frustrating but I'll get to that. Gameplay: Ok this should really be called bossfights because thats all there really is. I think I've already said why I don't like bossfight to bossfight a lot in this review but for this section it is shows a pretty poor gameplay loop. Take Unsouled for an example. The gameplay loop is, cutscene with a npc or mob character at the start of the chapter than you go on and kill a bunch of mobs and do level puzzles, midway through you may encounter the minor bosses or encounter a triggered event than you level and upgrade to finally go fight the big boss, Verses Eldest scrolls loop, walk around until you stumble at big giant door maybe encounter a puzzle or eviromental hazard but most likely not. fight the boss, upgrade your tree and checkout new ability than go again. That me being generous. Lets talk about the bossfights. I think a lot people talked about how the first three bosses are a cake walk and they are. and then you meet fire ball and water ball of AOE poophousery (I actually ecounter this boss third and the other easy boss fourth). Now there are a lot of AOE attacks in this game, way too many in fact but most of them even the late game bosses are not as egregious as this fourth fire ball and water ball boss. There definitely harder bosses in this game but fourth boss is by far biggest hurdle for the player to overcome and I think it will turn away most players once they realised the dodge stamina mechanic is very poor and only gets better once you've found the perfect dodge = no stamina lost ability which only appears after defeating the boss after this one. Why is it not default? I think the bossfight will be 100% better if players were rewarded for perfect dodging without have to get an upgrade for it. Needs to be there from the start its like the same criticism I had for lies of P (Btw love that game a lot) where you couldn't roll strait away after being hit until bought that upgrade and you know what the devs for lies of P changed it that the ability to do that was there at the very start. it would've erased 80% of my wipes it would also free up more chances to modify my dash to do different things because you must have the perfect dodge ability or else I don't see any way of beating this game. 100% everyone that hated this game hates how the stamina works in this game and I can't blame them because it is garbage until you get that ability. All the other boss fights, the bosses with backstory/ has a unique npc such as the forest elder has an engaging first and second phase so well done. Also quite nice that some have environmental changes during second phase as well. I do like there are obstacles that you must destroy to progress in the bossfight I think it does need a little bit of hp tuning however the spider boss is particularly annoying because eggs have a little too much health were you can't quite combo them they are left with the fraction health which is really bad because its one of the few bossfights where your heal by doing damage gets turned against you because of the insta poison ability in the boss's second phase and the only way to get rid of poison was to drink from the fountain but you had to destroy the eggs before you could do that and man its just annoying bossfight. apart from the fire and water ball, the spider boss is also a very annoying bossfight because some of the mechanics didn't work.Overall a really challenging game, 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: picked this up super cheap after playing titan souls and i enjoyed this game even more. i loved the skills, the boss designs, roaming around despite the world being small and enjoying the art and music. the gameplay is intense. the bosses hit hard, especially the later ones. i mainly play third person or 3D souls games so this was an interesting learning curve. i like the character design, the NPC's are chill and nice and you can find a good amount of lore scattered around the world as well...and it's pretty hidden. i'd say this game is well worth the money, especially under $3 and if you are someone who replays these types of games often, you will definitely get your money's worth. check this one out if you're into 2D games but don't want a heap of exploration and getting lost. awesome asf, recommended!!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is another boss-rush game that throws in some exploration and questing that takes away from its challenging boss fights with combat that focuses on aggressive healing. Its amazing build variety is truly great and left me wanting happy and craving more.  You carry a big sword that has a light, heavy, and specially charged attack that is used to heal because you don’t have any potions. This takes Bloodborne healing to the next level. This can be both a blessing and a curse, hence it's mostly positive rating. Because if you suck you can’t heal without being risky, but for people that can handle this risk, it's a really creative and super engaging way to heal. Alot of people complain it's too hard. I would recommend Elden Ring if want an easier game. You have these shards that you get from each boss that you can stick in your different attacks:They modify similarly to Diablo.Take your dash:Each of these seven total runes dropped by bosses can be and mix-and-match to build a crazy number of styles. Really engaging system.The bosses are great and thankfully so because it’s all it’s got. Usually, lesser games will make bosses take 15-20 minutes to kill  to pad a boss-rush game. These fights are over in minutes after 20 attempts and an hour of trying.I always say the length of the fight is equally important to the variety of movesets and the readability of them. This game does everything you would want for a boss fight. Each boss is distinct and not just a dude with sword. I mean you fight two balls that I died over 30 times to. They all have 3 phases that increase the speed, add more complexity, or new movesets to prevent any fight from getting stale. The start and end of a fight can at times feel like 2 separate boss fights. Basically saying the fights are readable and varied.The game is really short and people who love their games padded will hate this. The game is linear with sometimes a quest to get some items to boost your stats. I didn't care for this backtracking. I am fine with just a breathing section of walking for a minute or two as Furi did, then move on to the next boss. These quests and characters felt tacked on and "required" as boss-rush always games sell less than a souls-like. Name a boss rush-only game with more than 10,000 reviews on Steam. I hope their next is only bosses and it will have no major issues from me. The Bosses and how many times I died to each:

_childDocuments_.review: A simply marvelous experience, from beginning to end.A soulslike with a wonderful 2d graphic style, with a beautiful BGM that accompanies you through this adventure - you feel all the frustration of dying over and over again against the same boss, and the insane amount of satisfaction when you defeat one... just to feel the same way at the next boss, until you master the game.The story of the game is great, narrated through few optional dialogues and many interactibles scattered all over the broken world in which this game takes place.Characters, bosses, everything feels unique in this wonderful world. You have options as per your build, and also per which quests you want to follow - which will reward you in different ways, and also slightly different endings.Die, learn, repeat. Die, learn, repeat. Every single fight learning a new pattern, increasing your timing. It's a fast paced game which still adapts to all different playstiles - whether you want to go for mobility and dodging, whether you're willing to tank in a defensive playstile and "parry" your opponent or you just want to go full DPS and trade blows, you got the options.The DLC is also very enjoyable. New bosses, new detail for the story, and also a new, powerful item that can greatly enhance your playstile.

_childDocuments_.review: 80 minutes stuck on first actual boss (guardian) gotten to second phase thrice its one of those games that when you die your not even punching the screen you just stare at it and think deeply why your doing this to yourself at the end of the day my autism and retardness has gotten to a new level Pretty good so far, 10/10 would recommend really easy and relaxing

_childDocuments_.review: A nice polished tiny game with an amazing art style, music, and bosses design. Well executed, but very short. I spend max 10-20 tries on a single boss, it's not that hard.To me this is a 9.5/10 game, I recommend it to everybody!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to leave a bad review, but that's precisely how the game was meant to be played.Prepare to die a lot. This is a bossfight-oriented game, the bosses are unfair and that's part of the experience.Most attacks are very hard to anticipate until you know them. You can hardly know if the boss will dash at you, cast a huge slash or summon annoying stuff. Then you'll have to learn the timing to dodge these.The sword is very clunky. It's backed up by strong movement options, but while you wanna spam the heck out of it for most damage, I got caught so many times by the boss starting up an attack while I focused on spamming and couldn't react in time.Despite the difficulty, the hero has access to very powerful lifesteal. While it really helps, it also feels cheap to get hit and replenish health in a burst of swings like it never happened.I'd feel more satisfaction being able to tank 10 hits and have barely any heal than having enough hp for 2 but full-healing in 5 seconds while beating up the enemy.The gameplay is very charged. I feel like the heavy pixelated graphics + movement + attack direction + tight timing to spam the sword + abilities to manage eats quite a lot of brain power, but it only adds to the challenge if anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Hades but every fight is Hades himself. If you enjoyed Hades get this, you won't regret it. The developers don't waste your time either, you die, you restart the fight within seconds and keep going. Non-stop fun. My only complaint is that I didn't find this game earlier.Pros:- Amazing art and character designs- An intriguing world- Satisfying gameplay and controls (Usually these types of games have really bad mouse and keyboard controls)- Does not waste your time with petty BS (ex. walking back to the boss fight after every attempt)Cons:- I have a feeling the game isn't very long, but I'm not sure yet. - I'll want more if the above is true, and I won't find it.One of those games that makes you feel like the developer made something that they wanted to play. 10/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty fun game! It's not terribly long, if you aren't concerned with additional post-game content. I wasn't compelled to play the new game+, but I think I've still come away satisfied for the price I paid. (Mind you, I bought it on a 75% sale, I'm not sure if I would maintain this opinion at full price.) This is a boss rush through and through, there are no common enemies at any point. It focuses on those boss fights, and it delivers a unique theme and relatively unique fighting experience for each boss. I have completed the game in just under 6 hours at a leisurely pace, but I believe you could easily get several tens of hours out of this title going for the achievements and extra challenges if you end up really loving the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a game that could be good with a little more polish. The upgrades also feel kind of pointless, and the game tips really grate on me considering how much you will die playing this game.It's a shame because it's a very pretty game, each of the bosses feels unique and I really like the bloodthirst mechanic where you can regain health when you've charged up your attack. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Was frustrated, pushed through, got a grappling hook, enjoyed the game more.Disclaimer: I've only played this a couple hours and beat about 5 bosses.The game is unforgiving and you will die a lot, however the quick respawn makes it less tedious than other Souls game where a long walk back awaits you with every death. I was frustrated at first, feeling like my character didn't handle properly or that attacks from bosses were too quick and I was only getting through because the early bosses didn't have a lot of health and I just got lucky. Soon enough, I reached a harder boss which didn't let me half-ass it and after retrying many times, I started recognizing the attack patterns better and being able to plan ahead. Your attacks are very slow and you cannot dash through entities, so it is a constant choice between evading the attack or repositioning so you can avoid it while charging a counter attack. After an early boss, you unlock a grappling hook-like ability on a very short cooldown that also propels you and powers you up the same way landing a charge attack does if it hooks an enemy. This adds more mobility and makes it a lot easier to move around during tricky fights with lots of simultaneous attacks to avoid and it made the game a lot better to play for me, even though I have the feeling it is more of a crutch I am going to have to learn to do without at some point, since there seem to be more and more powerful abilities to use instead.In general, I think the game looks very good, plays decently, has a lot of different playstyle options, and I personally enjoy the watered down Souls formula where you only fight bosses. It removes the urge I usually get to farm trash mobs and power up (you power up once for every boss you defeat), it makes you get to the action faster and still offers a formidable challenge. It also means there is little to no exploration, but also no spending time exploring places for useless consumables or items of little to no significance. There is some text/lore sprinkled here and there, but so far it hasn't been very original or caught my attention particularly so I think it's for the best that there isn't much more.All in all, a decent game to try out if you have the mental fortitude and the time to get invested in it. Persevere through the difficulty like you would any other Souls game and you should have some good moments like I did. :-)

Game is quite short, so you are probably ment to go trough NG+ cycles, which introduse new mechanics to bosses and probably develop the plot.PLOT is by far the weakest part of the game. In first cycle you get so little info about the lore and overall plot. I know that it is probably in NG+ but you have no insentive to play it. Unlike in HADES where the plot is engine moving you forward and not just premise of harder game.Lore is trying to by misteriously told as in Dark souls(in items descritions), but it is just a shalow clone.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm probably playing this game wrong, but the game does nothing to teach you about how to play or change your play style based on certain bosses.  I'm familiar with tough boss battle games, and this one needs a disclaimer that it is extremely difficult.What doesn't work for me is that you have to charge up to attack effectively, and the bosses are so quick, and they use their abilities so often, that it seems like I do more dodging than attacking.  Ultimately it isn't fun for me to hold a button for a couple of seconds every time I want to engage the boss.  There may be a better way to play the game, but I'm not able to figure it out.I also think the bosses are poorly designed, very little telegraphing for what abilities they're going to use, and it seems like some times there is one too many abilities, or they happen a bit too quickly, or you can't dodge quickly enough (you have three dodges that need to recharge).
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has beaten Elden Ring twice and is almost done beating Sekiro... this game is kind of difficult. The first boss took me 1 try and the second took me 3 but the fourth base I fought were the ice and fire gods and DANG that was hard. It took me like 30 tries to beat it, but It felt amazing to finally do so.Positives: 1. Unique boss fights. The boss fights are all great and unique in their own way. 2. Music. The music for this game slaps! it's still good listening to it for like the 40th time dying to the same boss.3. The moves/mechanics. The fighting system is nice and simple with a light attack, charged attack, a dash, and two specials moves. you can earn more skills and better moves by defeating bosses. I also love how you get health back by attacking the boss.Negatives:1.unfair? Some boss fights you sometimes feel like you have to get lucky with and some attacks will hit you more than once basically killing you one hit, and getting hit can completely mess your rhythm up and you'll end up getting pushed back and walking into a few more projectiles instantly killing you.2. difficulty curve. The game does not hold your hand or hold back. The difficulty curve can get a little ridiculous3. The Rotting Crown and the Spider boss are incredibly infuriating, but at least they are very far in. I don't know who made the Rejected Daughter boss, but they deserve o stub their tow every single morning forever. seriously it can leap anywhere in the room, lay poison everywhere, curse you so you are almost always one shot, cover the entire room in spiderwebs slowing you down, make the spiderwebs really hard to destroy and cover the only thing that can release you of your curseThe only boss fight that I legitimately HATE is The Rotting Crown. The arena is too small, its attacks cover the entire arena, The electric balls that stun lock you are absolutely terrible, the boss is a complete bullet sponge and takes way too long to kill, and when the bells are locked it just fells like you have to run away from everything but there's nowhere to go.All in all would recommend if looking for a good and very challenging game, but you better be a masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice Isometric souls game.  BUT!!!.....The story is confusing and I accidentally got the bad ending by siding with the wrong team.
