_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with flaws. Moving around the map is unnecessarily slow (teleporting doesn't help), combat can be wonky along with hitboxes, but the game itself is fine. It has good writing and amazing environments, however ultimately what holds this game down from being renowned as a good souls-like is just the lack of polish. Oh, and this is not even considering the DLC. The DLC has interesting environments at the start, and then for some reason they just drop the ball and decide to repeat the same room over and over for all 3 bosses. I know pixel art is hard, but it's a bit disappointing that there wasn't more to do in the new are. The first boss was janky, especially the spinning attack that had a LOT of knockback, but it was fun. The second boss was janky, unpolished and just poorly designed. I don't get how the spring/poison system works (Does it refresh? Are there only 3 uses? Who knows), and those web eggs just make the gameplay annoying by significantly reducing the area in which you fight in (As trying to go into the webs without KNOWING you can take them out in 1 second is just suicidal, because you just kill your movement.) It's just a poorly designed boss. The third boss was just unpolished to a degree where I wondered if they even tested the DLC. Some attacks have bigger hitboxes than they should be, there's little time to react to the green/stun attack on the ground, the boss itself has a gigantic hitbox that protrudes from his actual sprite, it's easy to just land on a spot where the boss is going to spawn those stun balls and to instantly die, etc. It's incredibly unpolished and it's disappointing, because the design is actually quite awesome. Overall this game is a solid 7/10. Or something. Buy it at a discount, though, it's not worth 20eur. I cannot, in good concience, reccomend it at the price it is set, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls, but only bosses and pixels. Pretty fun game with some cool bosses. Three different build paths enhanced by boss shards make for some interesting builds, but only really slightly enhance the builds. You are still locked into three skill trees essentially. Can be completed relatively quickly and once you learn the mechanics of the boss they are pretty easy to fell. I'd recommend if you like souls like and its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a fun game with a unique play style that feels clunky at first but really picks up once you spec into the skill tree. Challenging boss fights with unique mechanics (and sometimes pretty cheesy mechanics). Overall a solid game if you're looking for a challenge, HOWEVER, for a game that boasts challenges such as "beating every boss without taking ANY damage" (ending and DLC bosses not included), the programmers really needed to take more time on making sure hit boxes aren't buggy. My only gripe with this game is that the hit boxes on many of the bosses are honestly a mess. I went through the pain of 100%-ing the game, but after countless attempts it was clear that certain attacks just shouldn't connect, many things that SHOULD be a perfect dodge were NOT a perfect dodge, and often times when you click "try again" mechanics from the previous fight will carry over onto the new fight (including if you took damage). In that regard there is a lack of attention that really should be addressed in a small hot fix, but I doubt it would. What I mentioned is not crippling, but a nuisance more than anything. In my case it was the difference between getting a difficult achievement and not getting it in a number of scenarios. It is what it is.Wrote this in a hurry, overall solid game 7/10. Pick it up if you like a challenge and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I just got this game and made it through all the bosses for the first time. It was one of the funnest games I've played in recent memory and the only major criticism that I can give it is that I want more of it!Don't listen any of the reviews putting a thumbs down on this game. Most, if not all, of the bosses are fair. Some are more challenging than others, and some can be pretty damn frustrating, but ultimately it's almost always fair. Just pay attention and get the reps in and you'll be able to beat any boss. The people giving this a thumbs down got smoked by some early bosses because they wanted to steam roll the game in 5 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: When you start playing, the game looks very simple, but as you progress you get more and more tools to customize your builds.This has been one of the most challenging souls like games I have every played, at first I thought I was doing it wrong, but it turns out this game won't hold your hand on the way to the end, you will have to die, die and die in order to learn bosses patterns and your gear if you want to kill any of the bosses in this game.Unlike your regular Souls Like games, you cannot get good by farming, instead, you get good because your efforts, its a very rough but satisfactory path from the start to the end of the game, it really makes you think about your build and your strategy.I leaved this game for like a year, because I thought I was not good enough to defeat the bosses, and few days ago, I decided to return, to my surprise, the change on mindset opened the gates for a different fight approach, and allowed me to finish the game, I ended up loving this game, it might not have an enticing lore, but the game-play and character design is fantastic and absolutely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a different take of Dark Souls II, but before you buy it lets keep this in mind:Pros:* Art is good. Might not be your stuff, but it delivers enough eye candy effects.* Story is ok. It has some.* Its hard and punitive with border line soul sucking gameplay, Its a trial and error experience.* Controls are smooth.* Its a boss rush game.* Has enough builds to keep you entertained.* There is no silver bullet build. You will need to switch between bosses.Cons:* Bosses are quick, punitive and AoE centered. Fail twice and you're pretty much dead kind of game.* It can be frustrating.* Its a trial and error experience.* Some builds are just more powerful and rewarding than others.It is worth the money if you like being bent over and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. You're looking for 10ish hours of extremely punitive game where you need to perform every single action with precision and perfection (at least when I played it). My only gripe with this game is that every single boss is AoE oriented in small arenas. And they're quick and unpredictable. If you dash you will often dash into another AoE. Knowing the pattern helps, but there are some string attack that will hit you regardless of how good you are.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up on sale and it was worth it.- There are only bosses, no low-level enemies.- It's not a long game (I beat it in six hours, and I'm doing this review afterwards), but it has a NG+ type mode, which I'll keep on playing with.- This is Soulslike in the way you have to learn the boss move-set to be able to beat them. Learn, get your timing right, and you'll get there. - This game rewards aggressive play. You get more buffs as the game goes on, which stack to deal a lot of damage.I enjoyed the first half of the game more than the second half, as I felt I was overpowered by then. Next time I'll use a less stacky build.Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, but highly replayable. The boss battles are well designed and it has a cool art style. There is an arena mode but it could've used some QOL features, such as build loadouts. If you enjoy this type of game, get it on sale, it's definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Fun souls-like boss rush with pixel graphics, a dark world to explore, and good replay value.I enjoyed Eldest Souls more than expected. I'm a 'play on story mode' person at this point in my life. A challenging boss rush game doesn't have much appeal to me. The dark fantasy vibe, those pixel graphics, knowing it could be finished in less than six hours, and learning after years of avoiding souls-likes that 'souls-like' just means old school gameplay drew me in. I gave it a shot and I'm glad I did.The gameplay is an enjoyable rewarding challenge! Certainly frustrating at times. The first boss feels like a tutorial boss, the second feels like the first real boss, and then when you take on your third (you have two options as to whom your third boss is--this applies to both), that's when it gets difficult. I spent most of my playtime and 200ish deaths on the third boss options--initially taking on Azikel as my third boss, dying several times, then moving on to trying Eos instead. This is not the point in the game to give up. These two bosses force you to really learn how the game works. Some of it works kind of crappy. I swear the dodge is a bit sticky at times and getting pinned against the wall by bosses without being able to dodge is lame. But, the majority of it, you can and will learn. You learn to distance, use your charge attack, work your lifesteal power up, and manage your dodges that cap at a stock of three and recharge. Each boss you take on, you spend time learning their attack patterns, as is to be expected in any old school/souls-like game. By the time you graduate the school of hard knocks and take out one of the third bosses, frustration decreases while respect and your power increase. Right after I finally defeated Eos, I went back to Azikel and took them out in my first fresh attempt. It feels good to develop that skill! Of course there are still difficult moments moving forward, but you navigate them with a different confidence that keeps the fun there.There's also some great exploration and world building. I didn't know what to expect from a boss rush on that side of things and I was pleasantly surprised with the feel of exploration between boss fights. There are no minions to fight. There are world dangers that will kill you and will require some movement and dodge skills to advance. I really like the different settings you explore as you go from one boss to a next. It is a beautifully, dark, pixel graphics game. There are a few NPCs, story entries to read, and quests to complete to earn some additional power that also add to the adventure between bosses.Being more of a 'story mode' gamer these days, I probably won't try to get past the second boss in new game plus (That's as far as I am at this time), but it is great that NG+ adds extra difficulty and opportunity to complete additional quests for power ups over multiple play throughs. And you don't need to load up a NG+ to enjoy the free DLC that includes three additional bosses, which effectively makes the game 33% bigger. Awesome value as a free DLC. I wasn't able to beat the first DLC boss, but I have to say the design of their attack patterns is fun.Edit: For laughs, I have to add that I didn't earn the logged achievement until playing New Game plus. I don't think the logs get buffed in NG+, but that's when they got me, haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game needs a very long review. I also recommend it.Right from the get-go, Eldest Souls really feels like what a souls-like should be played. The bosses have clear indicators of what is happening (most of the time), and they're all beatable/cheesable like in a souls game. Although lore is not one of its strong points.You have a dodge, basic attack, charge attack, special weapon, and some RPG mechanics here and there. Some are better than others, and there's some room for build exploration, even if not much. And obviously some combinations/weapons are just better than others, but you can beat the game with anything, thanks to the healing given from filling your meter.20€ might seem much from what the game offers, but I feel like they're worth it. There's enough content and replay value for you to spend that much, maybe not more.The only complain I have is about the pixel art. Everything is animated and drawn manually, except.. The friggin' playable character. Which has this weird kind of rubbery animation.Some bosses can make it work as you will see in the game, but I don't dig it on the character I'm playing as. It doesn't affect gameplay, just the feel you get while playing it.Everything else about the art is incredibly well done. The lights and details are marvelous, and they help building the setting you're playing in. The game can be very atmospheric at times, which needs to be praised towards such a small studio as Fallen Flag Studio.The game also gets balance updates every now and then. A couple of days after I stopped playing they made some bosses more fair, and made some easier ones actually challenging. Meaning it's also great to check back every once in a while.I can easily recommend the game to anyone who'd like a challenge. The customization of your build is limited, but it's also very influential of your gameplay, meaning the game can be enjoyed by anyone: from the casual player, to the speedrunner, up to ymfah fans trying to beat the game without walking. Which I think is possible.

_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A lot of effort went into this intense and challenging game. It will teach you patience and the value of persistence in exchange for some of your sanity, while demonstrating the appeal of games with high difficulty. The story and setting is whatever, but the skill tree and feeling of progression was great. I'd leave boss encounters feeling like I went super saiyan. Worth your time if you love a good challenge.----- Full Review -----Eldest Souls is a high quality experience, carefully crafted with tons of effort and care. The title and 'box art' had me thinking this was going to be a poor quality, knockoff cash-grab. I went in quite skeptical, knowing that this game was going to have to prove itself to me, and it truly delivered.It took me until boss 5 of 12 to find my footing with the experience, and I almost didn't hang around that long. Every new boss you fight feels like complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, leaving you wondering how the ♥♥♥♥ you are supposed to beat the current encounter, let alone subsequent ones. For me, it wasn't until beating boss 5 that I was able to overcome this feeling, and this game unexpectedly delivered an experience of self-growth that helped me understand the appeal of painfully difficult games such as this.After I had come so far, I knew the upcoming bosses would seem ridiculous and imbalanced... but I was no longer tempted to give up. I knew that by studying their attack patterns, and modifying my build, I'd learn more every time and would eventually get the boss to 50%, 25% and 0 health. I honestly felt like an anime protagonist the remainder of the game.The art direction (music and animation) really impressed me. The boss fights were frustrating in the moment, but I look back on them with admiration. I didn't get the sense that any encounter was 'thrown together', rather that each of them were repeatedly revised until the intended vision was achieved. I didn't pay any attention at all to the story or setting. Maybe it was great? I just didn't feel drawn into it by the game - it's not why I was there. I super enjoyed the skill tree and optimizing my character builds to outsmart each boss encounter.The game isn't a 10/10 by any means, and MANY of my ~250 deaths were rage inducing. I can't tell you the number of times I had a boss at 1% health but died to an attack that seemed like it should have missed me. The attacks are telegraphed well enough, but your movement speed and stamina regeneration are so, so slow.  Despite hating this, I can't help but think that changing it would have spoiled my aforementioned anime protagonist character arc.I'll note that the steam page description uses the term 'souls-like' pretty loosely here. The game is sorely challenging, and it employs a generic, apocalyptic medieval fantasy setting. That's all it has in common with the sub-genre. While inaccurate, this description is still useful; I can see souls-like fans in particular getting a lot of enjoyment out of this game. That's definitely the target audience here. If you enjoy a tediously difficult experience that can teach you a valuable lesson about patience and persistence, I recommend Eldest Souls. But just know it will take some time to warm up to the idea of finishing the game. You can do it :)

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love the art and music of this game quite a bit. But that's where my enjoyment stops. I know I'm not the best souls-like gamer out there, but I couldn't even get past the first non-tutorial boss. This game is hard.... and the combat is extremely lacking and not enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The art, sound design and music score for this game are top notch and the idea behind the gameplay mechanics are fantastic! However, some executions of those mechanics and the hitboxes of the game are... not so great...The bosses, generally, are good at telegraphing their moves but some of the "randomized" AoE's will end up covering 80% of the viable surface to safely move on (which *doesn't* include the threat area of the boss itself) so forced hits can be frustrating. Another issue I have is the punishment *upon* punishment. For example: you only get 3 dodges in the game and each has a pretty slow recharge time so you have to use them strategically and precisely. Totally cool and understandable. Getting hit by a mistimed dodge? The punishment is not only a loss of a dodge chance *and* a chunk of your life taken out. Also cool and a valid "punishment". What isn't valid is some boss moves will then lock out TWO of your dodges for a long duration *adding* on top of the punishment. So not only were you punished (properly) by a mistimed dodge by using us a dodge chance *and* having your face smacked in buy you also have *two* less chances to dodge now... Completely uncool and overpunishing. If you mistimed that original dodge and it did the move to lock up your other two you are pretty much guaranteed dead in the next 5 seconds because you will be unable to avoid whatever comes next.I ended up throwing in the towel when I got to a certain zone  because it legit felt like the designers wanted you to *not* play their game. Why, in a boss rush game, am I being forced to traverse an area, full of "wait" cycles with 1hit, instant, undodgable kills that not only resets your progress but resets you to a random location in the area?! No thanks.I really wanted to like this game and it had SO much promise but there are a few key decisions that really just make this game frustrating and unfun :(You can watch my livestream gameplay of the game over on my !
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid boss rush. The bosses all have different mechanics and gimmicks and there's a surprising amount of build variety. The different skill trees feel really meaningfully different, and you can respec at any time so you can try out different fighting styles as you please.The game feels a tiny bit clunky at times. The high-commitment attacks, low player movespeed, and the low iframes on the dodge can sometimes cause the gameplay to feel like you're walking through quicksand. That said, if you like boss rushes this is a must.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really understand a lot of the reviews of this game claiming that the game is unfair. This game is extremely forgiving to mistakes and even allows you to be quite sloppy with your execution at times. Perfection is not demanded from you. Your character is extremely mobile for a souls-like game. you have three dash charges that give you plenty of invincible frames at the beginning of the dash and it gives you quite a lot of distance. Your character starts with a life-steal effect that is easily triggered, and the charge attack allows you to easily close the distance to your enemy when you've dashed away to dodge. That being said, the game is quite difficult. Bosses will require trial and error and generally provide an enjoyable souls-like experience of learning enemy attack patterns and throwing yourself at the boss, improving each time. If you don't like souls-likes, don't buy this game. If you do, you'll probably enjoy it. Don't buy this game expecting to have an easy experience because this isn't that type of game. definitely worth picking up during the pretty generous sales

_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I enjoy high difficulty in games, Eldest Souls provides obstacles you cannot use logic to beat. Bosses have interesting and creative attack patterns, but quickly overwhelm you with sheer speed and spam, as your slow movement speed and restrictive dashes make it difficult to work on anything other than instinct. Different tactics, skill trees, or even mentality do absolutely nothing until you spend an absurd amount of time on an enemy you know you can't beat yet.And that "yet" is incredibly infuriating. It's not fun going to an encounter and thinking "Hmm, let me sit here for 10 minutes observing the enemies' behavior before even trying to land a single hit." When a game wants you to repeatedly bash your head against a wall to move to another stage, it becomes a rage gaming session filled with a mindless time of trial and error, which I'm not a fan of. The skill trees are simple and easily interchangeable, but despite their clear coding of “Agility, Damage, and Resistance” they barely offer any gameplay experience, besides simple number changes and a new ability with a cooldown. I’d prefer to see more variety like ranged alternatives, or complete move style revamps, other than just another ability added to the repeating combo.But there are certain parts of the game I enjoyed greatly. The scenery is great at its dark and grim storytelling, combined with notes and NPCs telling you more and more about the Citadel you explore. I genuinely had more fun surveying the corridors and halls finding little tidbits of lore, than the actual fights themselves. Boss designs are creative and fun, and as I said before, their attack patterns match their fantasy and aesthetic. Having a portion of their power moved to your abilities makes the fights memorable, and genuinely feels like you wield a part of your fallen foes. And the fact you can use that fragment in any part of your skillset? Amazing!I can understand people finding the game genuinely fun. But as a person with very low reaction times and a preference for a more methodical and adaptive mindset, the game isn’t for me. If you enjoy “souls-likes” and other games that push you through trial and error, this game is definitely for you. But in other cases, it might be a rough start to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend the game, but only while on heavy discount. The game is very short, I finished in around 8 hours including DLC content.The game is a souls-like boss rush game, and all the bosses are incredibly interesting, although not without their flaws.Pros- Very interesting boss design- In general, you are forced to learn boss behavior and adapt to them, throughout the whole game I only found a single boss I could mow through with very few attempts (that being the questionable deer boss, but I had already beaten the DLC by that time so that might be the cause of it)- Boss fights are very short, max of like 1-3 minutes. I read another review stating that they have too much health but their expectations must be really really fast fights or they were playing crazy slow. I've had DLC boss fights where I chunk them to half health in around 30 seconds, altho I have to slow down eventually- Smooth and responsive controls, i-frame dodging is satisfying and rewarded, controls are responsive*Cons- Short game, I didn't think NG+ was worth doing since I saw... +140% enemy hp * - You can't walk through bosses and this sometimes causes you to be pinned against a wall- There's only 1 primary moveset, the skill trees are cool but truly only minor augmentations to your playstyle, at least in my experience- The spider boss is a total ♥♥♥♥♥- Some of the later bosses' movesets are a bit... spammy / bullet helly. They are of course still very well telegraphed individually, but when there's like 3 or 4 different things going on at one time it feels a bit unfair. On the other side of the coin here, it's really rather easy to iframe dodge most individual boss moves, so it's possible this was necessary to ramp up the difficulty.Neutrals - Only bosses, no normal enemies- Story is very vague, probably due to game length
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The game has a beautiful style and amazing art. I had a blast playing this game and recommend it to anyone who seeks a challenge.TLDR: If you are looking for a fun challenging game that'll ruffle yer jimmies this is your game. 10/10

I mean really precise.I'm liking it so far for my experience in souls games. Art is gorgeousThis may be your game, and it may be not, and it's okay. _childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game on a whim because I loved the artstyle without knowing anything else about it really. Went in, beat the first 3 bosses, who I found reasonably challenging and rewarding to kill, took a little longer for the 3rd one and I was pumped to finaly best it and move on. So far I found movement to be a little bit clunky but otherwise had fun.After the 3rd boss you reach an area that leaves you the choice between 2 fights. Both are in extremely small arenas and both features AoEs that take up pretty much the entirety of said arena. So in both cases you have to constantly thread the needle, which would be fine if it weren't for the fact that as I mentionned movement feels a bit clunky, to be more precise the character feels very heavy. That in itself makes things a bit hard but really what makes it feel terrible is the dash. They ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the dash in a souls like... The dash has 3 charges, pretty standard, that recharge very slowly, pretty standard, and if you do a perfect dodge you don't spend a dash charge to reward good timing, pretty standard, that part is okay. What's not okay is the dash is extremely short ranged, just barely shorter that the bosses reach in fact which means you can't realiably dash out of an attack. The dash does not allow you to move through enemies, which means you can very easily get stuck against a boss or a wall or whatever. And worst of all the dash animation cancels if you collide with anything, meaning that for example if you're stuck in a corner because you're threading the needle toa void a ginormous AoE, and then the boss makes a targeted ranged attack, and you want to dodge out of the way, and you happen to rub a little too close to the wall : GET ♥♥♥♥♥♥ LMAO. The dash cancels and you lose half your HP.Another thing that bothered me although minor complaint in comparison to the above, is that there's no way to tell how long an action takes. The game relies on making charged attacks rather often, light attacks animation already takes a fair amount of time, charged attack feels like it takes over a second to fully charge. In either cases it's hard to gauge when to attack once more or when to retreat because the only way to know is to pay very close attention and learn how long the animations take. Which I suppose is part of the skills expected of the player in these kinda games, so as I said minor complaint.It's a shame because the story seemed interesting and the artists did a wonderful job, musics were pretty cool too. I didn't play around with the 3 different fighting styles but that seemed cool as well especially the fact that you can rearrange all your skill points into any tree at any time out of combat. Won't bother tryharding against those two AoE bosses I described to figure out the other fighting styles though.TLDR: clunky movement + skill issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: pretty short game (i finished all the bosses minus one from the expansion in about 3 hours) although its got ng+ and some extra stuff. gameplay is very good id definitely get it on sale, or full price if you are into getting 100% on games.Favorite boss so far: ZyladHardest boss: THAT DAMN SPIDER THINGEasiest boss: that moon fortress person-thing
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: A very strange game. At first I really liked it, but the bosses in the game are weird. It's not that I die often, it's normal and I don't get angry about it. On the contrary, I was specifically looking for a difficult game. That's just in this game due to the fact that it is 2D, but the space is three-dimensional, which is why the bosses move and attack very strangely. You often die for no reason
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The base game feels challenging but fair. There's plenty of build options especially once you've beaten the first few bosses. Along with the three different skill tree's each with two paths. Allowing for a myriad of effective play styles. Each boss felt unique both visually and mechanically and I never felt that any individual boss had any unfair attacks or mechanics.However the opposite of everything I've said applies to NG+ the "tank" skill tree does no damage so each fight lasts 10-15 minutes. The tutorial boss has a screen covering attack that does 70% of your HP unless you perfectly dodge it. The game throws so many particle effects on the screen that fights will eventually just lag out and kill you. There's no way to opt out of NG+ once you beat the final boss so if you didn't get 100% progression you're just forfeiting buffs you should have by that point in the game. Fun game, I bought it on sale. Definitely wouldn't recommend paying full price for it if you want to beat the game more than once.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Bosses with unique mechanics kept every fight fresh- Attacks are generally clearly telegraphed and readable- Variety of viable builds that grow throughout the game, with the ability to swap between them freelyDisliked:- Writing felt a bit dense and cryptic for the length of the game- Non-boss sections were a bit tedious
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Game is about dodging and developers made the worst possible dodge in the history .... It feels random every single time. Some bosses are buggy - rejected sister is broken, because sometimes you can clear poison pools with fountains and sometimes it just doesnt get removed. If you can buy it for less than 3 euro, then go for it, otherwise it is not worth time and money. It is a pity, because I like the idea of talent trees and boss shards.

_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a good design, feels fun to play, and puts a unique spin on the usual souls-like formula. _childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe that I've beaten the game. When I encountered the 3rd boss/es I found it/them so difficult that I wanted to refund it  (actually I'm a dark souls veteran, what ever that may mean :-); but I thought the bosses would give me less trouble), but it was too late, the first 2 bosses took way(!!!) longer than 20mins. Eos for example splits in two, with both parts doing different attacks at mostly random times, where some of the projectile sprites can be hidden by others and some combined attack patterns are seemingly impossible to dodge depending on your position, especially in his last phase. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. But man the input lag + ghosting or just straight up unresponsiveness is just not worth it anymore.Wanting to play this as a lazy couch game with a controller is just not gonna happen. The randomness in input-preping your next move is RNG. You go do a 'Charge Attack' and before your animation is done you 'prep/press and perhaps hold' your next move and it goes off like it should. Sounds great right? Works 6/10 times.  Just felt like everything was 'off' like a delay in a rhythm game.So for enjoyment of the game over comfort + testing; I switched to Keyboard and mouse + Binding dodge to my side mouse button due to Left Shift not being available to use as Dodge and my brain for some reason doesn't like hitting space to dodge. [My thumbs reaction time is not all that great]Like my 'rhythm game' statement earlier. I was right. Everything was amazing in terms of input. Now I was passing stuff way easier on a new save file. [Re-re-tested out on controller just to tripple check I wasn't just 'getting gud']Only problem now is the fact I dislike the keyboard and mouse control scheme. I prefer the movement and button scheme of the controller. Though I love the precision of the mouse with dash attacking. If you're not a picky little @$%#! like me. Love that gud 2D souls combatWilling to adapt to the controllers jankOr just likes Mouse and KeyboardGameplay first lore second.I'd pick it up.If we ever get a hybrid Joystick controller movement with mouse aiming. _childDocuments_.review: Short but well-crafted, with fun, intense boss fights and tight, satisfying controls. Note to devs, if reading this: I know the point of the game is to be hard, but just going by the stats there's a giant drop-off right early game - it's worth having a micro-starting boss that introduces the basic controls and gives a skill point, and that would help both with the huge difficulty cliff at the start and also give players a bit more change to play around with their builds if they're having a hard time with the Eos / God of Light initial bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if someone came up with such idea (to put only bosses) before this game, but its brilliant. As a person who is a fan of Dark Souls series and always wanted to repeat boss encounters multiple times its a perfect alternative. I love that simplicity in the design - 3 talent trees and boss shards with unique effects in every single slot. Also admire that creative, rich encounters along the path. All these fights looks cool, have plenty of mechanics, are rather readable and are quite challening. Everything is on spot. I also really respect the little things, like the freedom of changing talents in every situation or instant respawns inside the boss chamber.The only thing that annoyed me was the fact that the game forced NG+ automatically after the ending cutscene and I lost all the statistics that I wanted to check (unless I pressed something by accident and agreed to go into NG+)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: ** PART OF HUMBLE CHOICE FOR NOV 2022 **I really don't get why people are hating on the game for being a boss rush, it's along the line of Jotun and Titan souls, and that is a compliment.Tough as nails fights, the lore is there if you look for it, all the people saying there's nothing to interact with have obviously not played the game nearly enough, (Just like in Dark souls which seems to pollute everyone's opinions) there are hidden letters, the boss items give you even more lore and the few npcs that there are add to the world.However my experience with the game has not been all positive, the grappling hook enchant seems to only work properly on some levels, in others it has ended up making me restart the boss, some Boss attacks move the player against their will to unfortunate positions and end up chain stunning you resetting a 10 minute long boss fight.There are some kinks that I wish they cleaned up before releasing the game completely, but with the product as it is I've had a great time and I'm looking forward to hating myself with hard mode

_childDocuments_.review: A nice fun, little game. I am recommending this game, but I'm going to list a few negatives about it.- Game-breaking bugs, an item for one of the side quests completely disappeared from the game when I restarted the game with the item on me. Nowhere in my inventory and it's no longer the spawn point. I googled the item and found out that it's crucial to progress in one of the sidequests.So no 100% for me, at least not in the first run. I haven't started Ng+ and checked if I can pick it up there.- The game is way too short, like, incredibly short. There is NG+ ofc but it's baffling how little content there is in the game. - the 'platforming' section in one of the boss areas is pure hell. I do not understand how someone thought putting that junk in the game was a good idea. - The game gets way too easy after a certain point. The upgrades and special items beefs the character up to Saiyan level. Sure, it's fun to be strong... but I feel like it was a mistake to make the player that strong.- Like I mentioned before, lack of content really drags this game down. This could have been an incredible indie title, but instead it gets stuck on just 'OK'. If the game wasn't so linear, if it rewarded players for exploring, had more side quests and just things to do... This game could have been amazing.--------------------------------------Either way,  I recommend the game. The game play is pretty smooth and feels good. Visuals are gorgeous, animations are great. Bosses are fun for the most part (except the Ice boss, f him) If you can get this game for 11€ or less, I'd say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game will likely frustrate you or piss you off multiple times...that being said...Eldest Souls is amazing and worth a buy. There are a variety of builds to play with and quests to complete to power up your char on a run. People who say the game is short probably only played the base game, but honestly new game plus is really a must play. You continue on with all your skill points and shards (which get buffed on each subsequent run i think), bosses have double health, you take more damage, but most importantly the bosses have new attack patterns.NG+ is no joke, but it is doable. The game requires constant focus to beat NG+ bosses. If you want to play a casual game, this is not the game for you. But if you like a challenge that seems insurmountable but in all honestly is absolutely doable then this is a must play. Dodging mechanic is  honestly amazing. Yes you can only dodge three times and have to wait for a recharge. that's intentional. You MUST perfect dodge attacks in NG+ to beat any of the bosses. If you do the dodge essentially costs no stamina. So you are rewarded for playing well.Combat itself feels very satisfying. Only thing that is buggy is the grapple...sometimes it just doesnt connect and that has cost me a battle numerous times. Other than that, if you like roguelikes/roguelites like Slay the Spire, Trials of Fire, Wizard of Legend, Sekiro, etc. this is a must buy. Can easily get 15 hours out of this game by doing the base game + NG+ + DLC bosses. Have to say though...0 damage achievements. WHAT!? lol
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10This is a great game. it is challenging and presents multiple build options depending on the play style that you would like to go for. I've also noticed a few bugs where boss attacks don't work properly. it's way more noticeable on the second play-through where every move counts. I would give it full marks if these bugs got fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game if you enjoy challenging boss fights. There are a variety of different builds available but Berserker feels a lot stronger than the other 2 trees. Perhaps it just caters to my play style better.I think the Guardian on Abyss mode (NG+) was the hardest fight out of all of them for me although I didn't try the DLC bosses in Abyss mode. The 2nd and 3rd boss have a tendency to box you in, and the skeleton summons on the 3rd boss have a larger hit box than their sprites which makes them hard to navigate.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent soulslike and boss rush game but imo the fights would've been much more enjoyable if the bosses had 2/3rds of their current health pools. The battles felt like they went on for too long and dying at the end was too devestating.The flow of combat is very nice, with a responsive dodge rolls, charge attack and fun life steal mechanics. The skilltree is very confusing but there's a lot of variety and if you're really good at this game and love the challenge i think you can find a lot of replayability here.All bosses are highly unique and different and there's a few true gems in there (eos, azikel and drakmur) sadly there are also quite a few mediocre or bad ones. I even resorted to cheese tactics for one of them. The final boss is also a bit anticlimatic because it's quite a pushover compared to the other ones.Lastly the (free!) DLC adds a few interesting fights but they don't feel as polished as the others. They are however INCREDIBLY difficult but after a while you'll get the mechanics down and it's just a matter of trying until you finally slay them. I'd give this game a neutral rating but steam doesn't allow that so i'll give it a thumbs up. With the DLC included and on sale i'd say this is worth it if you want a real challenge. Beware however, as this is one of the harder titles (that i've played thus far, much harder than titan souls and even dark devotion)

_childDocuments_.review: A fun boss rush title in which each boss has its own unique gimmick in how it fights you. There are 3 main classes with 2 subclasses for each class, and every boss drops an crystal you can use to give a new ability to any of your existing attacks. What makes the game stand out is that you can swap boss crystals and classes at any point, leading to a lot of experimentation and optimization. The fights are well thought out and while the story is minimal, it isn't something that's necessary for enjoying this style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a boss rush that focuses on quality over quantity. I played the game entirely on my Steam Deck and found the experience perfect for mobile, albeit a short one with some minor deck exclusive bugs. First and foremost, the game is VERY short with such a price tag. I bought the game at a fair $10 and enjoyed my 4 hour playthrough considerably, but have no desire for the new game plus + that might double my playtime or the DLC that might add a few more hours of new content. The content here however is very refined, combat feels great with some unique ideas, and bosses are very enjoyable to fight.The game also has some exploration with a story, but felt no desire to explore every inch and complete additional side stuff or find lore. The biggest upgrades you get are from bosses, each boss drops a power that can be used on one of your abilities. Weapons can be unlocked by completing the quest for each weapon, usually using one of the 3 trees to deal damage or kill bosses. Each tree has several upgrades to tailor your own playstyle, but unless you plan on playing through the game several times, you'll probably role with one of the trees and not really experiment too much on builds.Eldest Souls is a great game at the wrong price point, but considering the quality of the overall game, i understand the price. If they added an additional 4-5 hours of content, 100% worth $20, but right now its worth it only on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls
