_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I played this I didn't enjoy it and left a negative review. After a year I decided return to the game and try it again, and this time around I enjoyed myself very much, but this is still a very flawed game.First off, I can say that the music is pretty solid. It isn't something I would listen to in my free time, but it does fit the game very well and adds more to the world than it takes away from it. Sound for your weapons and the environment fit quite well and sound good. The pixel art has grown on me overtime. The environments and bosses look wonderful and are beautifully animated, but there are two fatal flaw in the visuals. One being the player character. Compared to the rest of the game it seems that the player character's visuals and animations were glossed over. The lower detail put on his body makes him seem out of place in this world. It's the same for the cutscenes in the game. The cutscenes look terrible compared to the rest of the game as they go for an even lower detail look for them.Gameplay involves fighting a boss and then walking to the next boss, like most boss rush games. The bosses here are pretty well done and each feel unique from one another. In combat, you have the ability to charged up your sword to perform a flurry off charge slashes. These charge slashes also give you back heath and deal a lots of damage. This helps encourage aggressive and fast play. This is well and good, but there is a huge flaw here which will be a huge turn off for most people. The movement system in this game seems off. It's really hard to explain and the only real way to understand is to play this for yourself. Your character seems really heavy, almost like he's not comfortable walking. This takes quite a while to get used to and despite the aggressiveness of the combat, this movement system can sometimes make it feel sluggish. I can say I do enjoy how the skilltree and shard system works in this game. My build will most likely look and play very different from yours will, which is definitely a plus for the game. Another positive for this game is that you can new game+ it multiple times. Currently I'm on new game+4 and it gets more difficult every time. This game does have side quest as well, which can make your character way stronger, but the side quests sometimes are not very clear on how to complete, and the lack of guides and information online on how to complete them can lead you to being very confused and frustrated. Finally, we get to story and lore. In conclusion, there almost is no story. Simply put, there is the intro and ending. There is an attempt to set up lore for this universe, but it's implemented very poorly, because there is almost barely anything to read or figure out. It's a real shame, because there is potential here. Funnily enough, there are different endings to the game, but these are terribly done. The only thing that changes is the background of the ending cutscene, and the final dialogue sequence of the game.In conclusion, I did really enjoy this game, but I'm hesitant to recommend it because of its flaws. If you really wish to play this game, I would recommend you buy it on sale for a low price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and challenging game where you only fight bosses and do a little bit of exploration. For players who seek a challenge, after the 1st clear, you can complete the new game+. During new game+, every boss will be in Abyss Mode, they will not only have buffed stats, but they also have some new patterns. You will also be able to keep your skill points from your previous playthrough for the new game+.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: As a sucker for boss design i love this game. all of the bosses have both interesting visual and fight designs. i do however how a few complaints, first off the berserk slash skill tree is just far better than the other 2. second i found the final boss quite disappointing, which sad because the art for the boss is really cool and some of the ideas have a lot of potential but the fight ends up being basically a reskin of a previous boss. and finally i find it quite disappointing that you cant 100 percent the game in a single run, however to make ng+ better is that the bosses have some upgraded moves and some entirely new moves. despite my complaints its still incredibly fun! 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who can only play games that give me migraines, this is definitely worth your time. The game cuts out a ton of filler from other games, getting you right to the good stuff.As far as challenges go, Eldest Souls provides a very high level of difficulty. The best decision the devs made was allowing the player to start the fight right away, rather than traversing the world to get back. It could have just been me, but the balance between the bosses felt a bit jarring. The ones that were difficult were incredibly difficult. The ones that were easy were very easy; never felt like there was a great middle ground. My only big gripe, surprisingly enough, is the time it takes to walk around the map. I think the developers should patch in a horse or something that allows the player to constantly sprint- there's no reason to worry about stamina drainage when you are just exploring without fear of combat.As an adult with limited time, Eldest Souls scratched me right where I itch. I don't have a ton of available time to play games like I used to, and logging about 5-6 hours felt perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: With an isometric view precision is not the word to describe this game.  for Dark souls fans better turn away it is not as thrilling as dark souls far from it. the bosses are difficult yes, but more annoying than challenging. even cuphead is even better than  this game. the controller are sluggish at time and the graphics are to pixelated for it to be a game of precision. i really wish i could have my money back but now its too late. this game disappoints me and i m not touching it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Very good boss rush game, but unfortunately very short. Combat system is excellent but rewards mindless attacking too much on lower NG+. Somewhat interesting character customization with different builds and active abilities. Lore/Exploration is almost non-existent. Boss battles vary in quality, but the good ones are very fun to fight. Recommend playing through it on at least NG+, the bosses movesets get massively expanded.Overall I would recommend it, but its pretty expensive for how little content there is. Grab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This a boss rush game, just like Titan Souls was. And it's surprisingly deep, mainly because of the "fighting style" system. This allows you to spec into on of the three styles, each with one main ability that you build around. Skill points can be re-spec'd at any time, promoting experimentation with different styles. First half of the game feels unfairly difficult, but the other half feels the opposite. Unlocking enough skillpoints makes you a monster, so much so that the last boss of the game is actually the easiest. I tried one of the early game bosses at least 30 times, and last boss was finished on third try. Perfect difficulty exists somewhere in the midgame bosses.Still, I would recommend this, it's overall enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun if you're a fan of the challenging bosses found in souls games. However one thing to note is that due to the isometric 2d art reading boss attacks can be unclear due to the wonky movement of animations and the camera being locked in place that doesn't happen with the 3d souls games. The second boss has a tentacle attack and he can turn to face you while also casting the attack in a way where it will show the animation for the boss turning, but not the boss casting the animation for the tentacle attack. It's a small but noticeable annoyance that makes fights more annoying rather than challenging but fair.Also besides bosses, there's no mobs or normal enemies to speak of. The game is a straight boss rush. It's a shame because combat is fun and they could have added groups of enemies to spice things up between bosses.Overall if steam had a neutral score I would give this game that. Buy it when it's like 10$ during a sale as there's not much otherwise except for bosses that justify its full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great Boss Rush!*not* multiple bosses in a row, but rather only bosses to face in the game with no trash mobs in-between. You can change talents however much you want, whenever you want besides in combat with bosses. The customization is surprisingly large for a two handed blade! + You get 3 skill trees+ Each tree has 2 "routes"+ Each boss gives unique passive items that you can equip on skills to buff them in a unique manner= Quite a lot of alternatives. Boss music is better than expected! Bosses are as good as I hoped! Which is very good! Game has surprised me again and again.But I probably won't play much more of it than I have. New game plus is cool and brings new options to builds (since you still gain talent points and items get upgraded for each boss killed). And yet, I don't find THAT much enjoyment from fighting epic bosses to the point that I'm willing to have 60+ deaths on some of them in ng+ just to have to wait one more boss before I get a noticeable upgrade. Can recommend on sale, good few hours of enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: To me, the gauge that shows how much I truly enjoy a game is when I spend hours in the game without realizing it.  That is true for this game.  I look at my hours and I just cant believe it.  Mind you, its only about 10 hours. But I havent progressed very far.  I have games Ive nearly beaten and quit sitting at 6 hours.  Ive got at least 10 hours in this game and have not truly gotten bored.  That how I want to preface this review.Now....This game is unnecessarily hard.   Like it truly is.  Its hard for the sake of being hard.  That usually turns me off.But theres something about this game that makes me continue to fight.  Every death is truly my fault and each death is a learning experience.  Each fight is a dance that you must master.  Even when you master the dance, it can be exceedingly hard.  I know the devs are still trying to balance it.Anyways, this game is basically a boss rush game.  Imagine Cuphead but even less filler between bosses.  I must say this... each battle is fun and fair.  And I think that is what keeps me coming back.  Once you learn the dance, its a cakewalk.  But most cakewalks dont have grenades thrown into them constantly.  Thats why I must say in the end...Great game.  Hard for the sake of being hard.  But rewarding once you learn the dance.Get it on sale.  Not worth 20 bucks unless the devs fix the unnecessarily hard part
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice game. Getting the lacking element out of the way, if you're looking for a title that will capture you with an impressive story that moves along beautifully, this probably isn't the game you're looking for. While the bits of lore tossed in the game are nice and help build the depressing, yet elegant and beautiful setting of the world, it's not enough to merit an award for storytelling. That being said, if you're looking for a souls-like that's going to punish you over and over, but you still keep going back for more because you're a masochist, this is your game. The controls in this are intuitive and easy to get down. The combat is excellent, giving you three different skill trees to go down depending on how you want to fight and, therefore, experience the game. One thing to note about the combat as well is that there are different runes of sorts that you are able to throw on your character that will enhance different aspects of your abilities (like your dash, charged attacks, etc.). This variety of runes that you get from beating bosses also helps to keep the game fresh and unique to how you want to play, and I love that. The bosses have great designs and really test the player's ability to persevere and beat it after dying a multitude of times. There isn't much bad I can say about this game, the only bad thing really being that it's really short. Because of its design of that of a boss rush rather than a fully fledged out story-driven game, you can complete it fairly quickly, its length deriving from how much you will die. That being said, they do increase the replay value by adding a new game + (aka the abyss mode) where you'll get to continue to level up and test your abilities further against harder versions of the bosses you've faced. I haven't had the chance to go through the full ng+, but I'm very excited to. Anyways, this game deserves some attention and I recommend that you give it a try if you're interested in actually good souls-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many bad "Soulslike" games on Steam that as soon as I see the Soulslike tag I roll my eyes.  Among a pile of garbage Soulslikes, Eldest Souls is truly a treat.  This boss-rush game has some truly challenging bosses that took a LONG time to understand and defeat.  I'd recommend this to anyone as long as you don't mind a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept....but The difficulty of the game is based on luck and persistence. Once you find the attack patterns of the bosses it all comes down  to time. The time you need to actually beat each boss before it beats you because of the insane amount of damage they need to suffer before going down.I would have loved if this game was a 2d "rip off" of dark souls while keeping its own levelling system. I found the art, story and gameplay really nice otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Pocket-sized Souls-like -- it's simple marathon of different bosses that will make you teary eyed from staring intently at the screen trying to memorize all the boss' tells. Fighting styles was a simple but decent attempt at customizing. The additional upgrades received from bosses are no big deal in the first run of the game. I think you have to run the game multiple times to master a fighting style and see how the boss upgrades really improve the play style. NG+ and beyond is not something I will do anytime soon. It's a quick fix for filthy casuals who are looking for some pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet gem for those who enjoy the souls-like genre and are looking for something unique.  The game isn't long, and it is made in a boss-rush style, so for those who are looking for an expansive, interconnecting world filled with strange enemy mobs to fight, this game may feel like it is lacking a bit.At its core, however, Eldest Souls does an excellent job distilling the Dark Souls experience of triumphing over some truly hard-as-nails enemies, but without the repeated trudging back to the boss arena after each failed attempt.This game also gives players a branching skill tree that is easily respecced, giving players the flexibility to try their hand at slightly differing combat styles, or even tailor their skills to a particular fight at will.  After the game is complete, a newgame + with upgraded boss fights becomes available, giving the game some replay value to have you coming back.For those who enjoy this genre of game, I think it is definitely worth checking out.  A short but sweet 2D souls experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: On new game plus 5 now. The first play-through was a bit rough and very enjoyable, but once you finish about the 4th or 5th boss, the game becomes cake walk. The right side of the counter skill tree becomes very broken when shards are specked correctly. you can just hold the attack button and counter powerful attacks to ignore the damage and deal massive chunks of health. STORY: 4/10The Story of the game is very vague, and none of the bosses really tie into one another.The fragments of lore scattered over the world makes almost no sense. Would not recommend if you are looking for a story game.  GAME-PLAY: 8/10       The mechanics of the game feel very smooth. Essentially you have a basic attack, a charge attack (which fills up your meter under your health, this grants life steal when above 50%), an attack called blood burst(Which empties the bar under your health for heavy chunks of damage), 3 charges of dash that refresh over time (refresh is faster if you dodge through and attack), an active ability (interchangeable by boss shards, which are granted after defeating them), and a skill tree that grants active and passive buffs dependent on play-style.(Dodging, Attacking, and Blocking). The only issue i have with the skill tree is the fact that the blocking(Counter) skill tree in absolutely broken when specking to the right side. Just give your charge attacks an healing effect of some kind and you will never die.  DIFFICULTY: 6/10        On the first and second play-through, the first three non-tutorial bosses were by far the hardest. This is due to learning the mechanics, along with their hard hitting abilities. Every boss telegraphs their attacks pretty obviously making it rather easy to dodge.  REPLAY-ABILITY: 7/10       While the story and lore itself doesn't change, your ending can (There are 5 endings that I'm aware of). There are 4 NPC's you can choose from to give a unique item to that will alter the ending of the game as well as give you a buff for the remainder of the play-through, or you can remain neutral and receive a separate ending. Along with the multiple endings, each NG+ difficulty adds or modify the attacks of bosses along with buffing their damage, aggression, health, and self healing reduction.OVERALL: 6.5/10      Would recommend to people who like souls like games without all the trash mobs. Don't expect to sink endless hours into the game, but still worth the money for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Combat and skill customization are excellent. Art style is gorgeous and the music captures the tone and atmosphere. Bosses are not too hard the first time around, but New Game+ is where the fun really begins.Excellent game for those wanting a challenge and like having variety to your playstyle and build. Would have loved to see more lore and secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging boss rush game with good environmental lore and good art. I paid $16 on sale for the game and it took me 3.2 hours to beat on the first play-through, so I would probably suggest waiting for a bigger sale... but it's definitely worth a look. None of the bosses felt unfair to me. For me, the 3rd/4th bosses were easily the hardest, but I think it's because I wasn't using my shards properly at the time. I will definitely consider NG+1 after taking a short break from the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I start with this game, first off its worth the buy.This game is no joke, it can be quite hard and take some time to fight these bosses. The skill tree is deep and complex which is really nice. This makes for a lot of different ways to tackle each fight. Its okay to die this allows you to learn each boss more and more with each try. Is this game only bosses? Yes but this game has a lot of game to still offer. Boss rush, speed runs and new game plus. I'm pretty bad at these games and it took me 9 hours to beat the base game. Overall I think its worth the buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game. This is a soul like game where you have to die multiple times in order to figure how to beat the boss. The pixel art is one of the best. The soundtrack, the scene and the characters are top notch! You can see how much effort the developers put on this game.Highly recommend this game if your into boss battle scene right away. The only way to earn upgrades is to beat the boss. just remember dying is okay, you have to fail multiple times in order to beat this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest souls is a blast to play. It's also more bloodborne  and sekiro than dark souls in that the only way for you to heal is to keep attacking. The game looks fantastic with an amazing art style and the bosses and the sound track are all 10/10. The game might not be the longest game out there but with what you get, you'll surely have a fun and frustrating time. None of the combat ever felt unfair as every boss clearly telegraphs their attacks and it's up to you to figure it out and find a way to kill them. Another great feature is that you have 3 different main skill trees each with 2 sub sets of skills that would completely change the way you play. You have 1 skill tree for movement and dodging, another for damage and buffs, and another for defensive counter/parrying. You can change and respec the skills at any time to drastically change how you would take on a boss. Overall, I cant recommend eldest souls enough, especially if you love the boss battles of games like sekiro and bloodborne.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is a boss battler game, which means that the only enemies you get to fight are bosses, there are no regular enemies. This causes the world between boss fights to feel empty, but to be fair the space between bosses is very small. Once you beat the boss you will find yourself fighting another fairly quickly. Boss fights are very well done, each of them feels unique and I had a blast fighting them and learning their move-set. You can also customize your combat abilities - there are 3 skill trees to choose from. Additionally bosses drop unique shards which you can place in your skill tree to gain new abilities. Depending on which boss shard you place in which slot you get different bonuses. You can respec your skill tree any time allowing you to try out everything and find what fits your playstyle best.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think boss rush only game counts as an RPG. The game looks good but it's just a tough game. I see no particular resemblance to the souls-like genre and literally no exploration just heading in to a boss fight. Maybe I personally don't prefer this type of game but even so, it's not a game I would enjoy playing or give a second try.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Got jump scared by a crow....An awesome and addicting Boss Rush game with some amazing pixel art! Had some really awesome boss designs and was fun learning their attacks and how to destroy them! It felt like the game got so much easier the further in you got because some of the skills you get are insane! On first run, killed the last like 4 bosses in an hour and a half vs the first 5 bosses in 3 hours. NG+ was a pain in the neck and left me a little salty about the game though. Often it felt like it came down to having good RNG runs for a lot of the bosses because some of the boss's attack combos were near impossible to escape. You could be having a really good run but then the boss does one cheap combo and you're dead because there's nothing you could do, not to mention the amount of health they have is absurd (+220%!!!).Would recommend to those who enjoy repeatedly getting wrecked! Maybe just pass on NG+ unless you feel like getting PO'ed lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, but it’s still just a boss rush, which I’m not really a fan of. The bosses are pretty fun, but can be a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ as they have a lot of hp and can easily kill you in 3 hits, but eventually you'll get the hang of it and triumph.A few points to give more info about the game:- There are 9 bosses total.- There are different endings, but they are just a different end screen art you see for 3 seconds before it fades to black with a different closing text, though you get a different item that can help you with the remaining bosses after you complete the quest.- Speaking of quests, they are basically about finding items in the areas between bosses and bringing them to the right places. Which also means there’s some light exploration, but the areas are short and small.- There are some segments between bosses with environmental hazards that can kill you. One of them felt pretty cheap as you have to dash between moving platforms and avoid bullet hell style projectiles while destroying some objects, which wouldn’t be that bad, but you can easily overshoot with your dash and die instantly, or your attacks move you forward, which can result in you charging into a pit and die instantly.- You heal by charging a full heavy attack and hitting something with it, which gives you a short life steal buff. There aren’t any consumables or anything.- There are 3 different skill trees that define your style and each have 2 branches that specialize in something different. I tried 2 and one was way more powerful than the other, had better synergies and once you started your rotation, you could just keep rolling. The other one felt like it didn't know what it wants to specialize in, your main ability benefits from fast attacks, but the passives give you bonuses to heavy attacks or made you reliant on perfect dodging attacks to boost your dps.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE THIS GAME 10/10Honestly when i saw a preview i could not wait to get my hands on it. The graphics are amazing, the controls are ultra responsive, just everything about this game is super polished. It has earned a place in my favorite games of all time.its a boss rush souls like, dont play this game for the story, because there is barely one, and it can be a short game if youre a good gamer. however it took me several hours for a couple of the bosses.my ONLY complaint about this game is the difficulty of the last two bosses. they were far easier than 2 of the previous bosses. Once you have beaten the harder pre endgame bosses you are pretty much up to snuff to steamroll the rest of the game.with that being said, NG+ is the real game. Bosses have new or modified abilities, are sponges, and extremely dangerous. after beating a couple of the bosses on NG+ it kinda makes the base game seem like a joke difficulty wise, and the base game is pretty hard. So thats a huge plus for the game in my opinion. If youre looking for a cool game and you like a challenge, this is the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: 4 bosses in so far, My gripes so far are:Love the combat overall, especially the fact you heal for dealing damage and the many build options.No sound when you try to dodge but have no stamina,No red flashing Screen effect when hit or when at low hp(some games go overboard with this, but a little bit of it is nice) which can make it hard to notice when you're about to die sometimes.I seem to randomly attack faster and so far I have been unable to tell why, it happens after I do a full attack charge, but only sometimes.Can't dodge through bosses, even small ones and they can push you around, which takes some getting use to. Would be nice if the controller vibrated slightly while you're being pushed by bosses/got hit.There is a very slight delay on movement, which has gotten me killed sometimes as you can't instantly change direction and dodge. Need to change momentum to that direction first.Ohh and so far Mouse and keyboard seems better than controller to me, soley for the fact I can aim the charge attack more preceisly, though obviously you can then only dodge in 8 directions instead of 360 degrees.Overall great game, solid 7.5/10 from me,
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Just an hour into the game done the first 3 boss fights and just had to write a positive review at that point. There are only few games that have a combination of great combat flow and fair boss fights in combination highly difficult gameplay. Well this game is one of the few which seems to tick the boxes.So if you like the adrenaline rush you can get from highly difficult but fair games then this game might be for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing, the boss designs are all unique and when you do a first play through it leaves you amazed at what each fight has to bring. The game does have a New Game+ mode which if you thought the game was hard the first run in just wait till New Game+. Its quite nice to have multiple endings that aren't to obvious but not too hard to figure out. I would most definitely recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Has some issues with hitboxes, but overall pretty good. Interesting atmosphere/universe, fun bosses, and lots of depth with fighting styles. You can respec at any time so it's easy to try different strategies. I found some bosses were much harder than others, though this was before a couple of updates
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: To give you an idea of the difficulty here, the third boss already only has a 48% completion rate. Let that sink in, of the thousands (or however many sold) of copies sold less than half of those copies beat the third boss, and for very good reason. This ♥♥♥♥ is legitimately hard, but still fun. You gain power after every boss you kill and innate skill in top down action RPG's will bring you far even without the skills.Coming from someone who has beaten Dark Souls 1-3, Sekiro, and Cup Head, this game is mechanically simple with a very high skill ceiling and bosses (minus the first two) that feel almost impossible on first encounter. If you still wanna play it then good luck I hope you enjoy your time! 10/10 am gonna try to beat it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been kicking my ass, but it's still fun. Well worth the $20. Here are a few things I like and dislike from the game.Pros- The pixel art world is BEAUTIFUL!          The combat is fast paced.          Bosses (have not beat all yet) are interesting.          The game mechanics are brutal but fair.          OST is great.          The story telling threw the environment and the letters you find.Cons- No dash cancel.            No healing aside from Bloodlust that I am aware of yet. That is my opinion so far. Will probably add more to the review later.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Quite good, way too short even for a boss rush. Will give NG+ a shot sometime.Some bosses have issue of same wind-up animations for different attacks, some very questionable hitboxes too.Only tried Berserker so far, which was kinda silly build, loads of damage and ability to face tank attacks oftentimes.Edited to not recommended, as it's too short + what's mentioned above.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Very difficult but satisfying when you finally beat the boss.  The combat has a very satisfying rhythm and there's several different tech trees of styles to explore.I *REALLY* love the art and design of the game as well!  The pixel art is so beautifully done, the characters are really cool, and the lore is fascinating as I'm exploring it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Great Souls like game that is arguably harder but also lets you retry right after dying which saves it from being frustrating though the story isnt nearly as thought out as the fromsoft games but its still a great gameedit : today i was informed that the devs the didnt have the resources for a proper story and there were about 6 devs in total that made this game
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a positive review if they'd stop having so many bugs. The grappling hook one being one of the most frustrating things to play with. The hook stops mid air for no reason. The hook doesn't deal damage or restore bloodthirst even when thrown in the boss's face. It's literally the first mechanic they have and it doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for an hour and i already love it to bits.I waited months for the games release and it was not a let down what so ever, and more or less better than what i expected.The art style is amazing, it feels like a 2D dark souls but yet still 3D.The sound design is done so well in this game, it really sets the mood and you can feel when you are in a safe relaxing area or approaching a boss fight. Some sounds in the game even fade out when you go to different areas and really add to the realism of the game.The boss fights are so unique between each other and I love how quick you are to come by a new boss. Even the first few boss fights are really good at giving new comers information on how the mechanics of the game work.Their are also many different builds and unique game styles, and some if you find the right build can help with the difficulty of some bosses to an extent.Overall i would seriously recommend this game, especially to anyone who loves Dark Soul's or Boss rush games in general
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, not a good game. The skill tree system is initially interesting and empowering, it gives you the possibility of choosing your playstyle since the beginning of the game, but after upgrading a branch you'll have to change your playstyle to adapt to the use of the other one (or it will be useless to upgrade it).Most of the boss fights are good, made to let the player improve with logic timings and patterns, however there are some bs boss moves which just destroy the rythm of the boss fight.There are bugs, some of them are visual and some of them concern the use of shards (for example the guardian's active shard, the grappling hook, will not always max the bloodthirst bar).The exploration is very interesting, but it's a pity that there aren't many ways of obtaining upgrades from items and npcs (excluding the feather, the vessel's upgrade and the blacksmith's one), it's also a bit disappointing to see the absence of side quests and secondary bosses with such an incredible environmental setup.Not worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely addicting and rewarding boss rush game.Fluid movement and ambient world effects make the game feel alive as you walk around picking up items and extra information on the game's world.Fresh boss mechanics that give you sweet injections of dopamine every time you perform well3 skill trees to choose from that honestly felt like a little turbo boost to the tempo of the fightingNew Game+ Feelsgood man. More to dodge :3Easy 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game in less than 10 hours and it's been about a week since, and I'm left with that bitter-sweet sadness.The game is incredibly fun and easy to pick up. The bosses are hard, but within reason - you can pick up fairly quickly on their moves and figure out an optimal strategy for yourself. The levelling and upgrade system in this is a huge bonus compared to Titan Souls and it feels so damn good trying out the different boss souls for different features. Makes you feel like you could play the game a million different ways and have fun every time.The adventure aspect is really good and expands upon an interesting and very hidden lore embedded within it. This however, like the rest of the game, is not fleshed out enough though. It gives me a taste and takes it away too quickly. My ONLY qualm - and it's a big one - is this game is too damn short. Even for the price, I still think it's too short. You only finally get your groove with a good feel for all the upgrades and secrets you find, just to have it cut short. I really hope there's a fat expansion for this cause I'm craving more!!!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough of the game. Amazing gameplay and combat systems. I was not expecting the skill trees and perks to be this fleshed out.I can't help but wonder what this game would be like if it had a big 30h+ campaign with normal enemies, items, a more developed story and so on. The foundation is there and i can't wait to see what the devs will do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I only just beat the game once through at 4 hours, and even though I enjoyed it there are a few points I didn't quite enjoy. The first one is the total lack of direction or tracking of any kind. There's no quest markers for any of the side objectives nor is there a map outside of the fast travel points (and even then it never marks anything important). I always feel like trackers and maps are very important to games like these to save players time and frustration when the entire game is a frustratingly difficult boss rush, no need to add to the woes.The second is the imbalance of the skill trees, at least in my opinion. I did appreciate that for some bosses I had to change up my play style and use different skill trees, but I felt like every time I changed skill trees it was all about getting as much healing as possible. This game has a cool mechanic of being able to heal when you use a charge attack, but unfortunately because of how many of the later bosses play out it becomes the core mechanic in beating them. Because of this I found myself using the berserk tree and brute forcing my way through all of the final bosses. This mostly came down to the arenas being too small to play with dodging and the enemies simply covering too much area in damaging attacks. One boss even has a stage where they deal constant damage to you and pull you into AOE damage if you don't have enough dodge charges, forcing you to heal blast through it all.The third is specific to the second to last boss (at least the way it went for me). There's an area where you don't have to fight anything, but you get constantly assaulted with attacks and if you misstep by even a tiny pixel you instantly die. I found this incredibly frustrating and it nearly made me not recommend this game, along with other confusing points and annoying confusions in the lack of information I mentioned earlier. Honestly in all this was a fun experience, plenty to enjoy if you like to conquer challenging enemies in unique ways. And for all the bad I mention here there's still plenty of good, but it just felt outweighed by the issues I kept encountering. I'll still recommend this game because I managed to see it to the end, but I hope some of my issues are addressed by the developer at some point because I'd love to go back and try to find all of the things I may have missed while trying out new builds.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love the game. I'm excited to try the two trees I didn't try on my first save file. The ng+ is 90% amazing with the exception of Corrupted Guardian. Every other boss seemed like a good step up from the first playthrough except this guy. On ng++ now and once again this guy is destroying me. Maybe it's just my playstyle but I feel he could use some tuning.Bosses are great. Playstyle variety is great. Replayability is great. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Found that I wanted to review after finishing the game. Although it is kinda a short game I loved every minute of it. Bosses are hard enough that you might rage at being one shot, and the difficulty increases with each boss. Although that is the case, deaths have no penalty and you can always keep on going at it until you get it. While I might say it is a short game there is definitely replay-ability with new game+ and changing up the skill trees you go down to add more difficulty and challenge. Overall it is a fun game and buy it for a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, it's pretty short, and very much a boss rush, so make of that what you will. The combat is fun, neat, fast paced, and pretty intense. I feel like it's really meant to be played into NG+ with the way the progression system works, but that's not really for me, so I just played it through once and was satisfied with it. That said, the price point is up to you. I felt like it was worth it at 20$ CAD, because it gave me a fun, unique, shotgun blast of a game, and if every game is 20+ hours long I'll have to retire from this hobby ;-;I do feel like I have to make note that I found the world very neat and I would be interested in a larger, longer game where some of that world building and lore got a chance to breathe.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a refreshing addition to the souls-like genre. Its gorgeous art style and sense of stillness invites exploration of its quiet world. The subtle story unfolds slowly as pieces of dialogue, logbooks, and item description come together to draw up the big pictures. That sense of peaceful wandering, in a citadel devoid of life, is only disrupted when a boss appears and destroys the player. Once. Twice. And probably a lot more times. The boss battles are dynamic, brutal, and unforgiving. They complement the gameplay so well by challenging the player, but still giving them the ability to overcome and improve. When the player can only heal through charge attacks, they are left with no choice but to live up to the challenge and adapt.It's a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a fantastic game that really tried my reflexes. Beautiful pixel art and intense music adds to the action of the game, which is fast, frenetic and deadly. I came in looking for a challenge and it's exact what I got. I think some accessibility features would be a good patch, like a way to slow down bosses to practice them (like in guitar hero). I would recommend you buy Eldest Souls if you want sweaty palms. For anyone who wants to try but it scared of the difficulty then I would suggest you try it for an hour and if you feel yourself getting more frustrated then engaged then get a refund! This game feels like a complex puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but note that this game is almost entirely bosses with some very lite exploration and some obscure lore. Definitely worth your money if souls-like bosses is your jam.I found it challenging all the way through to the end. On NG+ I stopped playing after beating the Watchdog, and I can see that it definitely offers a substantial increase in difficulty with slightly changed move sets and much harder hits.This is a game where pattern recognition will take you a long way. Take your time, you have more than you think, and really learn how these bosses move and attack. There are three skill trees which you can respec at anytime to change up your abilities, but I didnt find these changes would result in a change to my playstyle (charge attack, couple of hits, dodge away). Arena design is solid, from the sprawling deer god arena right down to the confined EOS area, and plenty of environmental variations in between.Great job
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: -Decently hard game-Quite shortIm kinda ♥♥♥♥ and finished the game in a couple days without going through new game plus. I would say that the difficulty certainly varies wildly between bosses. You unlock multiple at the same time and they are not made equal. If I had one thing i wished the game would improve upon is level design. While the bosses move sets are interesting the arena in which you fight each one is almost always unchanging, and considering how you learn to dash through gaps and obstacles so early on it feels like a huge missed opportunity. Another thing i would like to add is that the berserk skill tree is very much overpowered. Throughout the whole game not once did i feel compelled to change my skill tree to better fight a boss, life steal is too high making the defensive blue skill tree never feel useful. All in all still a very good and specially POLISHED game. This is a lesson to game devs that small is not inherently bad, rather get a small complete experience then a large mess. Good Job :)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short, but can be played a few times through on regular difficulty or NG+. The combat system has 3 branches to try, and the upgrade points can be taken out and tried elsewhere, though you can just pick one at the beginning and stick with it if you so choose. I think it's well put-together and will interest those looking for a shorter Dark Souls experience with a different art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: finished the game in just under 3 hrs, did the first 2 bosses in NG+ just to see how much harder the game would feel, sadly... not much. In the same sense as Dark Souls (and all FromSoft games) once you understand the mechanics of the game better (and attack patterns/Mechanics of each boss) the difficulty comes way down. Still had and enjoyable time and though few, has unique boss fights.6.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced, fun gameplay and excellent music combine in this fun little boss rush game.  Be ready to die often but it almost never feels unfair.  For some hardcore souls-like fans it MIGHT be a bit too easy but for most players there should be plenty of challenge here.  If you like beautiful pixel art, this is a treat.  After a few hours of play I give it a solid recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very responsive and consistent you can actually learn it, and get rewarded with being better and better. NG+ is actually crazy as I just got to it and it is way more difficult, so if you are fine with multiple playthroughs this should be a great value for the price. If you are just looking for one run then beware that it will probably take you around 3-4 hours which might not be enough for some people when it comes to the price
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews for games, but I will make an exception just this once to say this:pretty cool game, but I got my crow friend stolen away from me as fast as I got him. How could you take away my crow friend developer's?other than that, yeah, it's a cool game, pretty short if your just looking for a single playthrough, but it does have ng+ which adds new stuff to the bosses and an arena mode to really challenge yourself. good game, I definetely reccomendbut I still really want my crow friend back.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good, but short, game. 4 hours of play and I just cleared it the first time (I suspect much of the playability will come from the NG+)Don't think it should have the 'souls-like' tag, as it's really more of a boss arena game. No trash mobs or anything, the only enemies in the game are the bosses. Sort of like Titan souls, but less puzzle and more combat based. The combat is hard, but hardly impossible. You can retry bosses right from where they are (no running back to the boss each time), and the difficulty is... well some of the bosses seem downright impossible after one or two attempts, but repetitive tries and learning their combat patterns has you gradually learning how to take them out. Regardless, that combat is good. Assuming NG+ adds some solid continued replayability, I'd say it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is fantastic, I've been waiting for it to release for a while and I was not dissapointed. The artstyle, music, and feel of the game come together to create this great atmosphere that so fun to traverse. But where this game excells the most is its combat each boss feels unique and the difficulty is just high enough where I would need at least a couple tries on each boss and for some would take around 20. By the last run on a boss you feel dialed in, your attacking pattern is perfect and you perfectly evade every attack. Dodging in this game is rewarding and feels very fluid. The attacks combined with the skill trees make each fight feel explosive. As you continue to upgrade your character the things that you can do expand and the skill cap increases. You can build your character a pretty much infinite amount of ways with the skill tree and items that you get from bosses giving this game lots of replaybility. Overall if you have any interest in souls or rouge like games you should give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is good! If you are up to a challenge and don't have a problem with dying and retrying, I would say try it. It took me 4 hours for the first playthrough, but I want to still No-Hit-kill all the bosses and maybe try a faster run. If you want to get everything out of the game besides a simple playthrough, it is worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Really really like this game! Combat is smooth and feels really great after beating a boss. I REALLY love the different combinations for builds and am personally a fan of fighting hard bosses/dying multiple times to try and beat one. Highly recommended, definitely would buy a second installment/DLC if the developer ends up adding something in the future, well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game. At first I was skeptical of how difficult an Indie Pixel game could be. Boy was I delighted to find out how wrong I was. The 1st boss was standard introductory difficulty. The 2nd boss was challenging and probably culled the herd of players that needed to refund the game. But the 3rd and 4th bosses (Azikel or Eos) made me put down the controller and contemplate if completion was even possible. 10/10. Can't wait for DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is an amazing Souls-like/Boss Rush game. Just like many games similar to it, it involves learning boss patterns through trial and error. While reading people's negative reviews why this game is bad, I found to disagree with most of their reasoning. I have beaten the game normally and on NG+, with as of writing this review, I am now working on the iron man achievements, so I think I could add some input to this game."Attacks are unfair and not telegraphed at all."This statement is mostly false. 99% of every attack I was hit by felt like it was completely my fault. I either was too greedy and swung an extra time, miss timed my dodge, or flat out just stood in something. Working on the Iron Man challenge as of now, you have to pay attention to every single detail and pattern a boss has in order to not get hit. Every ability I have encountered has had an animation that gave away what they were about to do. Sure, some attacks are annoying, but I felt as if there was always something I could of done better, and not just, "Garbage attacks." "Can some attacks be improved on?" Of course they can! I'm not saying all attacks are perfectly telegraphed, but if they were, that would reduce a lot of skill required to react on the fly rather than predicting everything."This game is too difficult."I think besides a few bosses on NG+ and all of Iron Man, the rest is quite easy. The problem I believe being from how strong some of the talents are. Before hand, you would have to deal so much damage in order to down a boss in the early game. Once about half-way through, some of the builds are so insanely strong that I you can down a boss less than 20 seconds. Even while playing NG+ and with the bosses extra mechanics, I beat  some of them first try do to how strong my build was. I do hope the developers continue adding hard content to the game, such as maybe a Hellish version of all bosses with even more improved attacks/you aren't allowed any talents or gem powers. I do love the boss design in this game and how it works, it just leave me wanting even more. "Game lacks content."In a way, I agree that the base game is quite short. I believe over-time with updates, this game has the ability to be loaded up with things to do. Currently all you have to do is, First play-through, NG+ play-through, and some of the hard achievements. (Also increasing ng+ if you are into that.) I believe the main content of this game right now is pursuing all of those tough achievements, cause that really adds on to the play-time. If you expect this to be a huge adventure like Dark Souls or Hollow Knight with places to explore, this is not that kind of game. You fight a boss, walk through some cool scenes with lore hidden around, then fight another boss. Which don't get me wrong, is a game I enjoy, cause I am a sucker for boss focused games. I highly suggest if you already beat the base game, try Iron Man out, that is the real challenge. Overall:I am highly enjoying this game and trying to compete with friends. I believe this game has the potential to be even better as time goes on with updates, there is so much more that can be done with this game and I hope the devs pursue that. I do agree there a few bugs but I rarely ever encountered them, as well as a few tweaks with some attacks and hitboxes. Talents could use a few changes due to being too powerful. But besides that, its left a taste in my mouth wanting even more from this game, with even crazier bosses that feel on the verge of impossible. I want to fight two bosses at once, I want secret bosses/phases, I want challenges that make me go insane. Highly recommended to anyone who pursues challenging fights that are seen in games similar to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: If you think you are tough and got mad skills, this game will humble you at the second boss.Pros:You don't have to worry about drinks, tears of frustration and rage will keep you hydrated during extended sessions.Visual style is ravishing (shame the resolution options are all for CRT monitors).Cons:No 4K resolution? I know the difficulty is old school but you don't have to go all in with the 1995 game design.Dash really should go through enemies, being stuck in a corner feels like getting Ground & Pounded by Fedor Emelianenko.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just starting with this game and I like it already.It's a boss rush game like Furi (fantastic game). You just fight bosses. No mobs. Minimum exploration.The few bosses I have fought were well designed. It's Brutally hard. You can't grind you're way out of it. Skills only.I was wondering at first if it was fair, and I didn't see anything broken.It's just tight. You have to be accurate and manage your dash bar like a miser.Edit: Now that I've finished a 1st playthrough I can add that:- The bosses and the cambat/build system are very well design and fun to play with- NG+ is much more than just an ordinary NG+. It's like Furi's Furier mode of difficulty. Bosses do get buffs in term of damage and HP but they also behave differently. They have upgraded attacks and patterns. It's pretty much like playing a new version of the game. The true game. A lot of fun if you like challenging games.- The game is short but what you get is really well crafted.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly tight designed boss gauntlet in a charming and forlorn setting.The area interconnecting the boss arenas are a nice stroll through quite a variance of locations, with some charmingly strange NPCs and small "puzzle quests" throughout it. While the base game can be finished in somewhat under 4 hours if your experienced with these kinds of games ALL bosses gain new moves in NG+ and you can keep gaining skill points during. And there is a nice and simple arena mode.) So if you want there is quite a lot of worthwhile content to be enjoyed^^ But you can also walk away after one play-trough without it feeling hollow, which I appreciate.One last note:Core game is quite polished, but some rough spots remain around the edges. But that's nothing a few post launch patches cant fix.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: For 18 hours+ i have reached New Game +2.Mostly time spent is to read the lore and do the "quests"The game is really fun and has a lot of quirks into it.Sadly it lacks content. I know one of the core mechanics of the game is ascension,  that further drives you into a new game+Ill summarize some of the pros and cons of this game.Pros: *Challenging aspect where each boss is really uniqueness*The skill system drives you into try different talents to best suit of the fight*The unique items you get as you progress gives you a nice boost but not powerful enough to break the game*Items has own uniqueness for depending what slot you use them in*The pixel art is really good. From icy world to forest/jungle to watery area and so onCons:*There are basically no lore*The "quests" is lacking in sense of a lot of subtle hints but no progression further*Some of the items you pickup is useless*When you find your build and you playstyle you can basically faceroll some  of the bosses*After learning the new game+ changes it just gets harder because less healing and more hp to bosses as you ascend*Not enough bosses to satisfy it as a many hours game. Can easily complete the game within couple of hoursOverall if you like this type of game killing same bosses over and over again. Than this game is for you.If you want lore and more exploration/questing type of game than this is not the game for you.I hope the devs will add more bosses in the future and some more lore. Right now i love the game but the number of bosses makes it to short.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant masterpiece.Ive never really played a Boss-Rush-Game before and expected more like another Dark-Souls in 2D. But its so much more. It maybe only contains bosses but each and everyone of them is perfect and with special abilities on their own. The combatsystem is absolutly satisfying, the pixelart ist lovely detailed, the music and the overall atmosphere is fantasic. The bossfights are hard, but always fair. Each mistake will be punished and they will mop the floor with you, as long as you wont learn and show them, whos the BOSS (get it?)Yes, the game is very frustating but when you finally achieved victory, you feel so alive and happy, that its over. Its more than just another souls-like. In itself its an masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I beat this game in 4.7 hours having played the demo in the past. Actual hours to beat maybe around 5-6 hours.Customization: 9.5/10What this game does well is it's customization. After each boss you earn a shard and skill point. You can change what shard goes to what ability and change your skill points into 1 of 3 fighting styles. Each fighting style have 2 branches you can put points into. You can have a speed build where you can run away from danger fast or a healing build that allows you to heal most of the damage dealt by the boss or a parry build where you master the timing for the boss and can quickly destroy the boss. However with two very straight forward branches for each fighting style it is almost like you only really get to choose 1 of 6 skills and 3 of the skills being very similar.Visual: 9/10I really enjoy the pixel art but sometimes with a lot of different effects happening at the same time, it can be overwhelming. Gameplay: 9/10Fighting each boss and finally beating them after countless tries really feel great. Apart of some reported weird hit-box issues and a few visual/functional bug the game is phenomenal. Most boss attacks can be dodge and punished.audio/ music: 8/10Music fits the bosses well but it's not super memorable afterwards. after a boss, the sound effect of the remains is kind of annoying, especially when you beat the game, the sound is rather annoying.Menu settings/ others: 6/10One of the gripes of the game is it does not allow aspect ratio/dimension change. It forces you to play on the window size your monitor has. The devs said they will change this which is great. Another thing is you are not to explore the area once you beat the game once but goes straight to NG+. I think it would be best to allow creation of another save to start at NG+ than to just go straight to NG+.This is a great game that has good new game + mechanics where you can fully enjoy the customization. I tried the green wind build which was probably not as good as blue or red. Wish there were more bosses but the devs stated that they were going for quality than quantity. Hopefully a DLC comes through.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I like this but, keep in mind, it's really short. I beat the game in just under 3 hours. I doubt I did everything I was able to in my first play through but I also didn't completely rush through the story either. In fact, I was a little disappointed when I realized that my game had already ended before I could find out how to unlock all the secret areas or give all the NPCs what they wanted. Like other souls-games the player is immediately thrown into a New Game + save after beating the final boss. This means I will have to do another play through to reach those areas I didn't see the first time I played.        That being said, the game's complex skill tree makes the idea of playing through Eldest Souls again seem not so unpalatable. Taking into consideration the three distinct skill branches and boss infusions, there's a lot to experiment with in regards to kit-building. I wish I could speak on the use of "Special Items" but I very unfortunately did not find any on this single play through. This is another reason why I'm motivated to start another play through.        Eldest Souls has a lot of depth hidden beneath its surface which makes it all the more frustrating when you realize how short the experience is. My advice is to make sure you have found all the items and discovered all the secrets before you face the boss at the top of the map. Overall though, this is a very challenging game. The combat system is relatively easy to figure out but difficult to master. The boss attacks are brutal, at first, yet they feel fair and telegraphed most of the time. If you are looking for a laid back and casual experience, this may not be the game for you.         In conclusion, Eldest Souls is a fun experience with a lot of complexity hiding beneath its initial impression. The game's biggest flaw is its short run-time. The seemingly large amount of replay value this game has, however, makes that flaw weigh less in comparison to the rest of the game's shining accolades.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Atmosphere is very much like Hollow Knight/Hyper Light Drifter. Bosses are very "Souls"My only negative point would be that I would have preferred it to not be a boss rush and have had regular enemies to flesh out the amazing areas they devs have designed. Worth buying at full price if you enjoy Souls Likes. (NG+ Feature adds to replayability)
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Eldest Souls is a top down, souls-like, boss rush game. It boasts a crisp pixel artstyle that is utilized to create visually striking bosses and environments. The boss fights were fair, gratifying to complete, and had cool, surprising moments in them, which should satisfy you if you are after that feeling of nailing a hard boss fight. I was also surprised by how in-depth the build diversity was: it may not be the deepest, but for a short, indie game it felt more than sufficient and should give you opportunities to test different and unique playstyles.That being said, the game is quite short if you are not going for any of the hardcore challenges: it took me about 4 hours to complete my first playthrough and I'd say my skill is average at best. Moreover, in the later fights once I got a lifesteal build going, I could ignore several boss mechanics and the gameplay became spammy and the victories felt a bit cheesy. The final two bosses took me less tries than earlier bosses, just because of how much damage I was outputting while lifestealing simultaneously.Overall, I think it's worth it at the 20$ price point if you are looking for an afternoon of fun, and more than worth it if you are interested in diving into the hardcore challenges, like New Game+, no-hit/death, or speedruns.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a challenging but rewarding boss rush that I recommend to anyone wanting to test their skills a bit. The combat is fun and satisfying, and the different customization options allow for a lot of flexibility in builds and strategies. The game does feel buggy at times, notably with the grapple ability not always working as I expected it to, grabbing onto what seems to  be nothing. The mechanics seem cheesy at times, where you can just abuse life steal abilities to hit the boss and replenish your health with minimal dodging. Some boss mechanics are frustrating as well, but it does help prevent the player from abusing life steal to brute force the bosses and requiring some movement and strategy. I did find myself getting caught on the bosses when trying to dodge around them very often. I would try to get behind them and instead dodge directly into them, wasting stamina and getting hit. Just dodging away instead of trying to go through them solves that issue though. Overall a very difficult but rewarding game, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: So far I like this game a lot. 80 minutes in with 5 bosses down. I think they crafted some really fun bossfights, it's satisfying to learn their attacks and really beat them up. There's also an interesting upgrade system that changes how you play. There's a little bit of exploration in between bosses as well, which I'm liking as a change of pace.Edit after beating the game: Had fun til the end. It feels like the real meat of the game comes at the end because You can tackle bosses again going for zero-damage runs, and you can re-play on NG+ for harder bosses.Cons: Overall the 'obstacle avoiding' exploration segments are more annoying than challenging. It's not too hard, you can die and restart your way through but it's just not very engaging.The 'purple void' area was especially a bit rough because you need to break obstacles to progress and your attacks can make you land into the insta-kill area. So I ended up just dying and restarting until I could make it to the end. Also, the boss arena here is small so the fight starts right away after retrying, I think it's good to start in a 'safe spot' that lets you change some of your skills/equipment up if need be, and most of the other boss arenas seem to work that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but first of all, it is NOT a dark-souls.It's boss rush, like titan souls, furi, shadow of colossus, etcSecond, gameplay has a problem imho. It feels too much like a loopWait boss action, Charge attack, get blood mode, attack x2 or x3, release blood mode, rince and repeat.Normal attack deals nothing so must charge attack first, that's little bad
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the first run. Combat system is fun even though sometimes relying on charged attacks to deal good DPS can be quite annoying. Considering the fact that the game is only made of boss fights, i would have liked some nice exploration or platform segment (there are just a couple, and really really easy). The art direction is nice and everything is pleasant to watch.The game is a bit too short (i've finished it in 7 hours) and yes, there is a NG+ mode, but it's poorly made: ofc NG+ is supposed to be harder (bosses have new animations and deals more damage), but give more than triple HP to the bosses is honestly a kinda unfair way to make the game harder.
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Its an OKAY game.There are alot of flaws for example the big empty world filled with texts and dialogs that serve no purpose.It could have just been 10 rooms and each room you fight the next boss...That being said the shard system is cool and makes for unique and interesting builds.The balance of the game is kinda off, but i think this game is meant to favor the player at first and things get harder in NG+.Overall i recommend buying this game for 10€ max (1€ for each boss i guess).20 bucks is definitely too much IMO!
_childDocuments_.name: Eldest Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I have not completed this game, and I do not think I will, I recommend the game, because if it is what you want, it is there. But if you want to know why I won't complete it, continue to read on.The game does a fantastic job of encapsulating the soulslike experience in terms of.. bosses, with a few.. egregious  exceptions. There is always a boss that does something that isn't particular, or great. The first bosses are challenging, they're difficult enough to maintain the desire to die, and retry, and keep on going.Which in my experience is great. Now as the further you get into the game, some of the bosses will have a sin, actually all bosses have a sin, some worst than others, you could say I'm just complaining. You'd be right, I am complaining, but in the same vein, there is still enjoyment to be had.Some of the arenas are very confining, this is okay some of the times, it can be dealt with, some of the arenas are just to large. I am avoiding spoilers by mentioning anything to specific here.  Among the sins, is overwhelming projectiles, and the inability of seeing visual clarity with some attacks. Especially if those attacks share the palate of the environment, which further frustrates seeing them. I don't have any form of color-blindness, but I do suffer from an inability to different some shades of colors from each other in high-tension situations where everything is moving very fast.Some attacks are hard to see, and very difficult to see coming. Some bosses are very well illustrated and telegraphed, while some feel sloppy, and aren't always so telegraphed. There is a boss  I quit upon, after taking care of 4-7 bosses. That has a bunch of attacks, and multiple phases, making the fight tedious.  Honestly, I do not want to relive an experience like Sister Frieda from Dark Souls 3. I'm good, I'm done.I have enough trauma from stuff like that, but again, the game is good, it has some rockiness to it, it's beautiful to look at, sound design, and music is clean. Controls are fluid, and responsive. I have no super big complaint from the mechanical nature of the game.Most of it comes down to visual clarity, and sloppy telegraphs in certain aspects. I normally wouldn't compare a game to Dark Souls, or the soulslike genre, but seeing as how it's written in the description, and its drawing a clear inspiration from it, I have to make that connection. I finish this game in the future,  but it serves a point of contention that the idea that difficulty is fun, isn't always the same. Horizantal difficult is not the same as vertical difficulty.  Horizantal is preferred since its ultimately more mechanical, tho. That is subjective, and ultimately everyone has personal preferences. If you want to suffer, this game is for you. If you're looking for picture perfect- or better Dark Souls like boss design, try to go in with a grain of salt, and lower your expectation. It is a 2d game, and translating 2d and 3d, effectively, may not come as naturally. But some of its hiccups, turned me off from the game, and for others it might make it thrive, and continue to push for enjoyment.But this game has made me rage harder than any Souls game I ever played, even bloodborne.  Like, I don't know, I feel like less of my deaths are my fault, and usually I feel that is the case in most of those games. I had moments where I healed up and still had HP, but it still decided I died. Many, many times. And its a bug. But it still left me with a lot of frustration.I'll prob just wait for Elden Ring, not that I'm super excited for that yet, since I want gameplay. :P But, All in all, I'll just say Eldest Souls, tries really hard to do exactly what it wanted to do best. And it hits the mark, but in someways the game could use some TLC, for visual clarity, and situations that overwhelm the player through visual, or cognitive overstimulation. (to many projectiles/things going on at once. Thus making it hard to play through blind information, as well discerning information cleanly in the midst of a fight.)Still, A lot of bosses Ir eally liked. Bot Multiple boss fights sequentially, I'm just scarred thanks to From Software and Sister Frieda, my mental health takes critical hits. >.>

name: Evan's Remains
detailed_description: Evan's Remains is a mystery-thriller puzzle adventure about finding a missing boy: Evan. The game combines logic-based platform puzzles with narrative inspired by Japanese graphic adventure games. Gameplay: Every time the player solves from two to three puzzles, the story goes forward and new mechanics are introduced. The challenge of the puzzles lies in the player’s ability to figure out what do rather than solve challenges based on skill. As the difficulty curve increases, the puzzles become more complex by combining two or more previously introduced mechanics. Story: Evan, the genius boy, has been missing for years. One day, a letter signed by him is received, claiming he’s on an uninhabited island somewhere in the Pacific Ocean. Nobody knows why, but he asked specifically for a girl named “Dysis” to go and look for him. The player will take control of this girl, who we don’t know much about. As we follow Dysis’s adventure, questions will start to be answered little by little. All of the little puzzle pieces which seemed unrelated in the beginning will now begin to slowly fit together as the truth is slowly revealed.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a beautiful puzzle platformer with a touching story.The main attraction is the story. It's a mystery that you unravel with plot twists, how people positively impact others they meet, facing fears, search for immortality, all with a positive message about how life is beautiful.The gameplay is simple and satisfying. Jumping off platforms makes them disappear and that's the core of the puzzles. Switches, teleports, jump platform that uses momentum add variety but ultimately the puzzles didn't feel too challenging. And should you want to progress the story, you can skip any puzzle.The animations feel smooth and are cute. Beautiful graphics and relaxing music make this an enjoyable experience from start to finish.I'd recommend the game's story even if you aren't interested in playing the game and only skipping the puzzles.For achievement hunters:There are missables for spending 15 minutes on a puzzle, skipping a puzzle, playing part of the game in Spanish and replaying a puzzle with a sequence break to see a meta error message.
