_childDocuments_.review: I had been putting off this game for far too long, but now that I have had the chance to play through it, I will wholeheartedly recommend giving this a go.You can see with the trailers and screenshots that the art is incredibly well-done and super smooth. Huge props from me for that.That leads to the gameplay itself.Essentially, as most others have already summarized, this is a mixture of a puzzle platformer and a short visual novel. It is a visual novel in the sense that you're along for the ride, however. There are no choices and you are only here to experience the storyline.One cool thing about this, though is that since the two genres are so different, they actually included skips for either the puzzles or the story, so you can experience the elements that you appreciate in case you're not inclined for one piece or the other.The puzzles themselves range from fairly simply to a decent challenge, though don't expect the difficulty to slowly ramp up. It goes all over from simple to a challenge, to a normal one on a whim. The story covers the reason why, but this is certainly something to be aware of if you are a pure puzzler.The story is short and sweet, and well-worth the time invested in it even if it isn't as "interactive" as traditional visual novels.Although fairly short (around 3 hours for me), the price point fits really well whether on sale (which happens frequently) or at the original full asking price.Well done on such a beautiful game!

_childDocuments_.review: What drew me in here, and what probably will for a lot of others, is the style and presentation of Evan's Remains. It's clearly a triumph creatively and artistically - especially as the work of primarily a single developer, with quite a scant credits list of collaborators. The pixel art of the game in motion is among some of the best I've seen from an indie game, achieving both incredible aesthetics while remaining clean and readable for gameplay. The lighting, effects and animation on top of it all round out the visual delight.However, I wasn't expecting this to be SUCH a narrative-heavy experience. And being a 2D indie game, that takes form as somewhat of a visual novel, as you might expect. I genuinely think you probably spend in excess of two-thirds your total playtime reading sentences of dialogue here. That would be fine, if the story itself wasn't convoluted and contrived, consisting of a cast of characters who are generally unlikable and subject to wholly unbelievable & unconvincing circumstances.You can skip some dialogue segments, but I opted to sit through them all because I was hoping there was going to be some kind of development with these characters or revelation that was going to tie it all together in a satisfying manner (sunk cost fallacy, innit). There wasn't, really. And I don't really consider the ability to skip any of that content in the game's favour, because that just shreds the total playtime down to the meagre actual puzzling, which frankly, seems to take a backseat in this whole experience, acting more as a vehicle for story delivery.I have to give the game its dues for its artistic and technical achievement, obviously. And the puzzles themselves are well-executed and honestly pretty enjoyable and satisfying. I also feel like there are probably people out there who would get more out of the narrative experience than I did. I just don't think I'd be recommending Evan's Remains to anyone any time soon.★★★✰✰

_childDocuments_.review: My impression could be affected by the fact that I don't like thriller movie. And this game's story feel very much like a typical thriller story to me.Story conjure up a bizarre world, with alien technology, mysterious man in hiding and some evil scheme waiting to be unfolded. But in the end none of that ever get resolved, and you realize all of them are just "icing" created to add atmosphere to an otherwise meh story.It's like watching a water park ads on TV with giant castle and huge water tunnel, and coming to the park just to realize the castle is a cardboard plate for taking pictures, and the water tunnel is still under construction. You can swim in the pool, though.---Another complain I have is that the game and the story doesn't really have any connection. Basically if you replace the platformer puzzle and just leave hieroglyph in its place, you will have a <described above> story. And vice versa if you remove the story you will have an okay-ish platformer puzzle.It'd greatly help if I had to spend half a neuron deciphering the words myself, or if Dysis' questionable addiction to platform jumping resulted in some kind of revelation (like that's how "special" she is, as the game hinted at).But nope, she's just especially crazy.At the end of the game you realize that she should've just walked around them and save us 3 hours of jumping.Also, what kind of visual novel doesn't have auto-advance? My wrist is sore from pressing Space zzz

_childDocuments_.review: Really short, neat story game. Coming across this game for the first time what really caught my eye was the art style. It is beautiful and every location just looks amazing. All the animations and little details really added to the atmosphere. The music was very good as well. What really surprised me though was how engaging the story was. At first I was a little worried with how long some of the dialogue sequences were, but after a couple of them I got super invested into the story. The one complaint I have, aside from no settings menu or at least a volume slider, is I just wish there were more puzzles since they were so much fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Cute pixel artwork- Beautiful landscapes- Clean puzzle designThe bad:- Story/Gameplay dissonance-- Puzzles design is isolated from the rest of the world. In the lava level? Don't expect the puzzles to incorporate lava. The background is just that, only a background.-- There's a person you follow through most of the game, presumably they complete each puzzle before you, but you still need to solve them afterwards. This makes 0 sense as you are both travelling through the world as a group.- The dialogue is far too long, but as the gameplay doesn't add anything to the story is required.- A game, (spy master?), is mentioned in the game... it would be neat to play it, but it's only a plot device.- And a weird thing I found lacking in this game, the jump height is binary. _childDocuments_.review: The game started out great and I really liked it at first. Sadly, the story really took a bad turn towards the end.You play as a girl who has been sent to an uninhabited island - or so they thought - by an organisation to find a boy called "Evan". What seems like an easy mission is everything but that. The idea for the story is great and at first i was really invented in it. The puzzles are quite nice and I enjoyed trying to solve them. There even is an option to skip them if you get stuck or just don't want to complete them.Throughout the story and the more is revealed you start making theories of what could happen etc. The twists(s) are nothing I could have thought of (which is good) but they changed the story in a way that I didn't like. The whole message is that things and money are not important but your connection to people/ the ones you love. This morphs into a "As long as you like your life everything is great, even if you've been living a lie". While the ending wants to be emotional and deep it just made me sad to see such a good story shattered into bits.The second half of the game was also mostly dialogue and cutscenes, of 3 hours gamplay, 1 1/2 hours was "game" at most, the rest was clicking though text.

Firstly, the story, which is supposed to be one of the main selling point of this game, is really rough around the edges if you ask me. It's also fairly shallow. The post-credit scene introduces two completely new characters that literally add nothing to the experience. The post-credit section is also buggy. I watched the credits once, and then when I tried to play the section, the character I was controlling wasn't showing up, I could only see their shadow. The second time I played, the game crashed after I was done the first puzzle. I really don't recommend you get it, it's not worth the money it's asking.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a  subjective review......you know how some people love pineapple and ham pizza and others hate it?  Neither side is "right" or "wrong", it's just different subjective tastes.Well, this game had enough elements that raked their fingernails across my metaphorical mental blackboard, that I ended up disliking it quite a bit.....to the extent that it became a chore to finish it.Let's look at the good stuff first:**-Gameplay-  When you're actually solving levels in this puzzle platformer, the game is quite enjoyable; none of the puzzles is so head-scratchingly difficult that you feel frustrated, and even if you do reach that point there is a "skip puzzle" function in the menu, which doesn't impact your achievements in the slightest.  Problem being that out of three hours of play-time, I suspect only around an hour was actually puzzles....the rest was "cut-scenes".....**-Music and puzzle graphics....the music is harmless, if a bit overwrought from time to time, and the pixel graphics are serviceable; nothing special, but nothing bad either.  **-Cut-scene graphics-  While the colourful pixel art is used for the side-scrolling puzzle solving, every cut scene features some of the worst anime style head-art for the dialogue that you have seen in a long time.....like Sailor-Moon would be ashamed at how bad it is.  Here is where some of that subjectivity comes into play.....I personally cannot stand bad anime where the female character's eyes are literally 1/3 of her face, and all the lads have hairstyles that defy not just gravity but common sense and human dignity.  Just plain woeful.  And the scenes are static with blinking character heads to the left and right of the dialogue boxes that you scroll through, labouriously, so you're stuck looking at these ugly portraits for more than half the game....-Dialogue/plotting-  You won't believe how wretched some of the "plot" and inter-personal dialogue is.  Kids in high-school creative writing classes have crafted less banal/trite, more realistic dialogue than this.  Nobody talks like this.  Ever.  Unless they're trapped in a bad anime......wait, I'm detecting a pattern.....-Cut-scenes-  While one can chalk up my loathing for the cut-scene art and the dialogue therein (not to mention the entire plot of the game) as highly subjective complaints, I think I'm standing on pretty solid, objective ground when I kvetch that after the first three or four levels (out of thirteen or fourteen, depending on how loose your definition of "level" is) there are so, SO many cut-scenes interspersed between the levels, each with so, SO much dialogue, so many that by the end you won't even be solving puzzles anymore, just trying to scroll through the rancid dialogue in the hopes that you'll make the pain end.The game loses all forward momentum and just becomes a wince-inducing cringefest as you slap away at the space-bar, trying to get through the interminable scenes to maybe get to another puzzle (which are increasingly few in number).So, what started out as fun and entertaining quickly devolves into a dull, protracted exercise in bad art and inane story-writing, which leaves behind the enjoyable puzzles in favour of more of the stuff that (YMMV) you probably won't enjoy.Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some good unique puzzles and starts out well with an intriguing and cute character and strong puzzle mechanics which are introduced well. However I found the dialogue to be a bit annoying with lots of "Um", "Er.." etc. throughout and less focus on interesting plot. The game plays very linear and is too repetitive for my liking. Near the start of the game you even literally solve the same puzzle twice as part of the story, but isn't explained why. Even the graphics are quite repetitive with all the monoliths. After getting through a few "zones" (the achievements) I found myself just kinda losing interest in the game and I stopped playing it. I found myself wondering if I could skip the puzzles to just get some satisfying progress on the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, I cannot recommend this game. The puzzles were okay, but only two of them really got me thinking. The fun was essentially interrupted over and over again by endless dialogues that kept me mashing skip and continue buttons on the controller, until I learned by accident that there's an entire menu option just for fast-forwarding all of it. This, however, felt equally wrong, so that I eventually decided to endure the short yet never-ending walls of text ... I ended being horribly disappointed by what can only be explained as an irritating and contrived plot with pointless twists and stereotypical exposition, just to throw in some more when you already had enough of it.I will give the game credit for its style and the overall game play, especially given that it's an indie game, but the story really didn't do it any good. A solid meh.

_childDocuments_.review: (review code provided by Whitethorn Digital)I first saw Evan's Remains during its Kickstarter campaign and followed it as it was picked up by its publisher (Whitethorn Digital). looked great the whole way, so I applied for a review code. here are my honest first impressions after ~2 hours and 20 minutes of gameplay:+ gorgeous pixel art, with stunning environments and character designs.+ majestic chiptunes soundtrack that's worth picking up, methinks.+ cerebral yet fair puzzles, which allow those that have troubles with them the option of skipping them by going to the menu. so it's very accessible, though I personally haven't yearned to skip any of the puzzles yet (I don't think I will skip any of them until after I've beaten the game once; I do want to review this comprehensively rather than phoning it in, since I WAS given a free code and it'd be feel slimy to not bleed a bit of ink talking about how I feel about it) and none of them have taken me 15 minutes yet (since the game gives an achievement for taking 15 minutes on a single puzzle and I haven't gotten that yet, lol). and I'm not super into puzzle games aside from Baba Is You and some other light puzzle/platformers besides ER, like GRIS and Mekabolt. so that should give an idea of how difficult they are. as far as I've gotten, it doesn't take long to survey the puzzles and figure out what you need to do, and once you solve the puzzles it is very satisfying.+ intriguing story that's mysterious, but generally keeps to its zenlike atmosphere. you have so many questions when you're at the point in the plot that I'm currently in, and it has me eager to the code for all of these mysteries just as I've been solving puzzles.+ controls are pretty solid, and I dig the animations for Dysis, the main character. very smooth and lively.~ generally strong, charming dialogue although there are some lines which come across as first draft. a lil stodgy, like they could've been hewed down into something more natural. but overall, I am leaning more towards enjoying the dialogue than not.+ the facial expressions of the characters in their portraits are pretty fun.and no, that other commenter's review is a lie, this is not "Sonic where you don't go fast and you're a waifu," lmao. I hope they find the attention they so crave.

_childDocuments_.review: The Moon in this game is completely wrong.I can ignore the size. Dramatic effect to show the passage of time, fine, whatever.But it was a crescent moon, and stars were seen in the middle of it. That is not how the Moon works! It's not invisible in the middle, it's just not being hit by enough light to be reflected back at us! Or is the game implying that the stars are in front of the Moon? Because that's even worse! The only stars that could be small enough to be a dot between the Earth and the Moon are neutron stars. Maybe you might think a 10-mile wide neutron star can't be that bad, and that would be wrong, at that distance the Earth and Moon and you and me would be ripped apart. Don't worry about suffering though, it would be fast. Especially for a magnetar. We wouldn't even so much "die" as much as "instantly stop being biology and start being physics".Next is that the angle of the crescent moon is wrong for the Pacific Ocean. Do your research! Don't specify that this game takes place in the Pacific islands and then get basic facts about the night sky wrong! You don't have to go there and take a picture, just google it, there are pictures of the night sky from the Pacific, and it's a different night sky from what is seen in this game.The crescent size is problematic too. It is somehow more than 50% of the circumference of the Moon as seen from the player's perspective. That is not a normal crescent, that is a lunar eclipse. A lunar eclipse where the Moon is either much farther away from the Earth than it should be, which seems unlikely given the size... or the Moon is bigger than the Earth, and we need to stop calling that thing the Moon and start calling it the Planet because clearly Earth is the Moon.Also the story the pretentious. It's like they're trying to be deep, and seem to genuinely think that they were, but they failed badly. Not a good thing when the game is around 2% simple puzzles and 98% bad story. That would normally bother me more but I'm more upset that they got the Moon wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: You've probably heard of this game at some point. It got a pretty strong marketing push leading up to it's release and sustained it for a bit after. It was also looked at by a fair amount of folks. Now that I've gotten around to trying it out for myself, this $7 puzzle platformer lives up to all the hype and then some.The music is good, the pixel art is gorgeous, and the main mechanics are interesting and cool. It's kind of hard to describe, and I'm still very much at the beginning of the game and giving an initial impression. But so far, there are regular platforms that disappear when you stand on them. Some instantly, some take a minuet. There are other blocks that don't disappear, but they make "there" platforms go away, and "not there" platforms come back. There are some specially marked blocks that will teleport you to other such marked blocks. The goal is to mess around with the arrangement of the platforms until you can figure out how to get past the obstacle in your path.These seem like they will be broke up with dialogue and story segments, and from everything I've seen about this game, the story promises to be an emotional rollercoaster. I'm probably going to be diving into this one for a while. Paladin says check it out, you've missed out, maybe look into fixing that.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as a cash grab.  It's one of literally thousands of 2D retro pixel platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  This is a particularly puzzle heavy precision platformer as you're presented with a number of switches and toggle puzzles to ensure platforms are just right for you to negotiate them, and other similar logic puzzles intertwined with the platformer gameplay.  In this case some degree of polish went into the game, the lipstick has been applied to the pig.  This does not change the fact that, like all 2D retro pixel trash, it's fundamentally defective.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality graphics. In a sheer insult to PC gamers, the developer has locked out keyboard and mouse controls on this game.  The developer demands, without compromise, that you must use a console peasant children's toy gamepad to play this garbage game.  This is simply unacceptable, developers must never dictate to gamers how a game is to be consumed.There's no audio controls so you can't turn off the exceedingly annoying BGM track.  Another unacceptable defect. Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is often used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthough for the Android developers who are to blame for this.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  They might even complain that they dumped this on mobile phones after it got a console peasant appliance launch, but that doesn't matter... it's not about the  that a mobile app is launched on different platforms, it's the fact that the developer specifically ensured the game would be inferior enough that it can run on mobile phones.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $7 USD, on Google's app store, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a SEVEN DOLLAR premium for a free mobile game just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is an adorable little indie game that completely caught me by surprise. What starts as a simple puzzle platformer quickly unfolds into a story-rich adventure with a depth I honestly didn’t expect. The narrative is emotional and filled with twists, keeping me engaged from beginning to end.The pixel art is beautifully done and clean – you can see the love and care that went into the details. The puzzles are creative and genuinely fun, challenging without ever feeling unfair. The balance between storytelling and gameplay is spot-on and makes the experience feel well-rounded.As a bonus, I found it incredibly cute that the backers were honored in such a sweet way at the end of the game. It’s a nice touch that shows just how much heart went into this project.If you enjoy short but impactful indie experiences, I highly recommend Evan's Remains. I definitely don’t regret my purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: This had been a game I'd played during one of Steam's many Next Fests, and it was a pretty fun puzzle game!  During the demo, there was a hint of the storyline, but nothing too crazy.  Playing the game though, I found out just how amazing the game itself is.  It is fairly short, something that can be completed within about 2.5 - 4 hours, so it's the perfect game to play during an afternoon!While the game does start off slow with the story, it very quickly captured my interest.  You start off by playing as a woman named Dysis, someone who is chasing a mysterious man named Evan.  As you explore this mysterious island, you first come into contact with the mysterious monoliths that litter the island, then soon meet a man named Clover.  Together, you both are trying to solve the mystery of the island, and try to complete both of your objectives.  However, there is so much more to this story than meets the eye.  The conversations between Dysis and Clover uncovers new information, some good and others bad.  The longer I played, the harder it was for me to stop because I needed to know what happened next.  While the story does give a ton of detail and goes over a lot of the questions I had while playing the game, I wish there was a way to figure out the rest of the information.  Evan's background, the company that sent Dysis on this adventure, and a few others were left unanswered.  However, these questions were fairly minor in the grand scheme of the game itself.The monoliths start off easy to solve, but eventually get harder to.  For the most part, they were fairly easy for me to solve, but there were a few that I struggled with that I had to pause on and come back to later to figure out.  Every chapter had a new monolith function to learn, but also continued building on and using previously learned ones.  My favorite part of completing the puzzles were the little flowers that grew on the pillar you land on at the end.  It's hard for me to find an art style I don't like, and it's rare to find a game that doesn't have a decent soundtrack to it.  Pixelated games are something that always have a special place in my heart, and this game was animated so gorgeously.  Everything is so fluid, the scenery is so vibrate and detailed, and the character movements always felt well-placed.  The amount of detail put into the game to show the difference between the foreground, middleground, and background is incredible and I have a lot of respect for people that can pull this off.  The music was beautiful too, and there was always something new based on the chapter.  This is definitely a soundtrack that I would add to my list.Overall, this is a game that I would definitely recommend playing!  It's short, it's beautiful, and the storyline will keep you hooked from the first moment you play it.  There are mentions of terminal illness and death, so please take care when playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the visual style of this game. It's pretty.That's about all the praise I can give this "puzzle platformer," which is a term I'm using very loosely. The gameplay, what little there is of it, is just way too braindead and simple. I think there winds up being, maybe, close to two dozen single-screen platforming sections where you jump on platforms that, for the most part, just disappear and reappear. Otherwise, the game insists entirely of your running to the right of the screen until you trigger dialogue boxes. What's absolutely baffling to me is that every single "puzzle" section of this game is skippable via an option in the pause menu, meaning actually playing the game is entirely optional. This can be done without limit and without penalty, so the game description of how you "need to solve an intricate series of puzzles" borders on a complete lie. What you're left with then is a convoluted story with often cringe-inducing dialogue. The plot barely makes sense, and the resolution given is plain bizarre and counter-intuitive. There's an attempt at a big twist here, but it just doesn't work for me.Like the puzzles, feel free to skip this one entirely. I promise you aren't missing much.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game a few years ago on the Nintendo Switch under the new releases and always wanted to try it because it looked pretty and the name sounded really interesting. I didn't really look much at the description, but eventually now grabbed it off Steam during some sale and got around to finally playing it.I wish I played it sooner.This is a really short game, around 2-4 hours depending on how fast you read or how fast you solve some puzzles in it (my computer crashed so my hours should really be around 2 and a half for the game even though Steam says 1.6 hours), but it's focused mainly on its narrative and the ending has a surprising punch with what it leaves you to think about and determine for yourself. I think it's a really nice blend of plot and puzzles because the puzzles did help keep it from being just a visual novel (not meaning they're bad; it just helps break it up a little) and the atmosphere, music, visuals, everything is great and the puzzles were not too challenging.It's hard to really say much more about this game because it was really fun and interesting and I'm still left digesting what happened in it, but I don't really want to spoil much. But man.If the price is a concern for the amount of time you get out of it, it's relatively cheap on sale, but it's still just a beautiful little thing and I only know it exists because of checking my Switch one singular day and then adding it to my wishlist there. It's a really nice little niche game and I recommend checking it out! I'm not one to usually write actually detailed reviews (all of mine so far except for one other one are jokes), but I immediately wanted to once I finished this game and it's really something beautiful. Time is a valuable thing; there's never enough of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews super often for games mostly because I really don't care enough about most games to write reviews unless it's super negative. In this case, I genuinely enjoyed this game so much I want to publish a review for it. Overall, I would give this game a pretty solid 8.75 score. It could have honestly been almost a solid 10 if it weren't for just a few reasons. The biggest of which is the short playtime. Don't get me wrong, this game was almost perfect in length for what it offered (more on that later). But an extra 1-2 hours of game play would have made this game that much better. That being said, though, I think for what this game is and what this game offers, it is nearly the perfect length. Any longer and the story wouldn't have been intriguing, the puzzles might have been less enjoyable to play, and the entire game likely would have been filled with a lot of fluff and filler content. I personally feel like this game had a perfect balance of puzzle and story. While some of the puzzles did repeat,  and I feel like it was justified. The puzzles got a little boring towards the end being that they just repeated the same mechanics for almost all of the puzzles and didn't add anything new. But I personally feel like the puzzles were good enough for the length of the game to keep my interest. Again, had this game have been even an hour longer, I feel like the puzzles would have been too boring and I would have lost interest but the extra hour would have been appreciated if done right. Based on the puzzle aspect alone, this game would get a 6.5 from me. The puzzles had a good balance of challenging and easy, but with the repeating of mechanics and repeating of puzzles, it definitely had me starting to lose interest in the puzzles towards the end and was just skipping them after just two or three minutes of trying. Again, the puzzles were good enough for the length of time this game takes to beat; that's why it gets a 6.5. Moving forward to the story, in my opinion, this is where this game really shines and gets a 9.5 from me. The story kept me engaged throughout. It had a lot of character development, was written so well, and even made me get very emotional at the end. The story contained quite a few twists and turns that were completely unexpected. This was absolutely one of the best written story games I've ever played. The only reason this doesn't get a solid 10 from me is just because some of the story scenes dragged on just a little bit longer than necessary and sometimes didn't add much to the story. To wrap up, this game would get a pretty solid 8.75 from me due to the story being slightly longer than necessary in some places but mostly because the puzzles were polished but overly repeated. Given the chance, I would play this game again but would probably skip the puzzles as I felt that some of the puzzles were unnecessary.

_childDocuments_.review: + Beautiful pixel art+ Likeable characters+ All puzzles and dialogue scenes are individually skippable+ Good OST- Ending doesn't quite pull together its ideas and themesA pleasant puzzle game balanced with a good story that ask for too much of your time. The mysteries presented aren't cliché ones you're likely to instantly predict the solutions to, which is rare enough in and of itself. Some scenes drag on a little more than they need to, and one or two lines don't land like they should, but the characters, their relationships and their interactions are enjoyable. Their personalities hold little of the forced zaniness so often present in video game writing, especially ones borrowing an anime aesthetic. Overall, the story's been given far more attention than the average puzzle game where the plot is more of an excuse to progress than an actual story.The presentation's generally on point as well, as you can tell from the trailer. I especially loved the fluid animation and sleek designs of the characters. There's only one thing I'd bring up to the devs to do better: The puzzles themselves are also great! I don't tend to have the patience for puzzlers that require you to meticulously plan out every move before interacting with them. Evan's Remains is the perfect balance of intuitive fiddling and "ah-ha!" moments. Another nice twist is that the puzzles don't have a difficulty curve—an easy puzzle might be followed by a much harder one, or vice versa, which keeps things relaxing with lots of breaks. It might be on the easy side if you are the type to want 50-step puzzles with mind-melting solutions, though.TL;DR: a brief puzzler with fun, relatively easy puzzles and a likeable cast and some entertaining mysteries to unravel, as long as you don't mind an ending that leaves a few plotholes lying around.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains provides a mixed experience, prioritizing its engaging story over its puzzle platforming elements. The platforming sections offer simple yet enjoyable gameplay, enhanced by attractive visuals and suitable music. However, the plot starts off strong but gradually becomes complex, leading to a confusing and unsatisfying ending. Despite these drawbacks, the game deserves a cautious recommendation, especially given its affordable price point. The game is generally easy, and most of the achievements can be unlocked intuitively. There are only four missable achievements, two of which are particularly challenging and require some prior knowledge. The "Boquita papá!" achievement involves playing a specific part of the game in Spanish, while the "Aurelio" achievement requires backtracking after a specific scene. Missing these achievements is not a major issue since the game is relatively short, but it can be frustrating regardless.Evan's Remains is a tricky game to review. While it's marketed as a mix of puzzle platformer and graphic adventure, it leans more towards the latter.The game's main focus is on the story and how it's presented. Although there are over 30 logic-based platform puzzles, you only get to solve a couple of them before the next part of the story unfolds.The issue is that I actually find the platforming parts more enjoyable than the overall story. Evan's Remains has lovely pixel graphics, smooth animations, and easy-to-use controls, especially during the puzzle sections. The puzzles themselves aren't too difficult. You jump from platform to platform, making them disappear. Later on, you encounter switches, platforms that boost your character's momentum, and teleporters. The goal remains the same throughout the game: use the platforms to climb and reach the top of a wall that blocks your path. It's simple, basic, and fun. Most puzzles can be solved after a few tries, with a couple requiring more trial and error. Overall, the puzzle platforming part delivers what you'd expect from a good game in that genre.On the other hand, the story of Evan's Remains, which ties everything together, is where the game disappoints me.The story starts off decently. You play as Dysis, the character with the sunhat on the game's cover. Dysis is hired by a corporation to find Evan, a highly gifted person, on a remote tropical island. The island is where Evan was last seen, and he even sent a letter asking Dysis to come find him.As you play, you control Dysis and explore the mysterious island. You discover strange monoliths scattered around, which serve as stages for the puzzles and are powered by ancient technology.Eventually, Dysis meets Clover, another person exploring the island. Clover believes that the island holds the secret to immortality. He thinks the monoliths form a message, with each one representing a word. Conveniently, Clover has a notebook to decipher the message. He doesn't explain how he ended up on the island; he just vaguely mentions a boat journey and waking up on the shore. Dysis and Clover team up and continue exploring together.So far, Evan's Remains is mostly enjoyable. The puzzles are simple yet engaging, and the story builds up with mysteries and questions. Will Dysis find Evan? Can Clover decipher the monoliths and uncover the truth about immortality?The most frustrating part is how the story is told. As I mentioned earlier, you can only solve a few puzzles before the game interrupts with more of the story. Unfortunately, the storytelling relies heavily on flashbacks and lore dumps. It feels more like a visual novel than a puzzle platformer at times. There are many of these segments, suggesting that the focus during development was more on the story rather than the platforming elements.The main problem with Evan's Remains, in my opinion, is that the story quality declines as you progress through the game. Especially after about two-thirds of the game, it takes a rapid downhill turn. I won't go into too much detail to avoid spoiling, so if you don't want spoilers, you should skip the next part where I discuss the story in more depth.This is mainly because the story becomes overcrowded with too many elements, possibly more suitable for a longer game of 8 or 12 hours, rather than the shorter length of Evan's Remains. The game simply can't support such a multitude of plot twists.While some of the twists add intrigue to the story, there is such a thing as too many plot twists, and Evan's Remains unfortunately exceeds that limit. The last part of the game is particularly guilty of this. Suddenly, a strange and creepy character is introduced, giving off a typical anime villain vibe. The game's tone noticeably shifts after this point.In short, by the end of the game, it is revealed that almost everyone was deceived, and many things were not what they seemed. It turns out that most of the events were part of an elaborate scheme. Predictably, the strange character turns out to be the villain. The game concludes with Evan and the antagonist contemplating the question of whether the end justifies the means and if ethically questionable actions can be justified by seemingly altruistic motives.The game attempts to present this as a deep, thought-provoking and original question, but in reality, many other pieces of media have explored this theme more effectively than Evan's Remains.

_childDocuments_.review: Gripping. Amazing. Incredible.I really didn't know what I was signing myself up for when I started playing.The puzzle gameplay is fun and enjoyable in a very relaxing way, which is completely at odds with the exceptional characterization and deeply-emotional narrative. Considering the game allows you to skip puzzles if you want to, it's obvious that the focus here is placed on the narrative. A good decision, I would add. The narrative is incredible and very worth experiencing. As my play time indicates, the game is very short if you don't get stuck on any of the puzzles, but I would gladly have paid more than four times the asking price. Games are art, and there is no length requirement a game should need to aspire to. Evan's Remains is exactly as long as it should be.This is a crushing, uplifting, hearbreaking, incredible experience. If you are looking for that kind of experience in games, then let this serve as a way marker on the journey traveled. I hope your experience is as wondrous as my own.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty straightforward platforming puzzle/visual novel game that takes about 3 hours to beat. The art is cute and the story flows pretty naturally. After it seems that the main game has ended, there were 2 more shorter runs with some exposition (1 before the credits and 1 after the credits). Avoiding spoilers as much as I can, the overall story was satisfying and eventually all the questions that come up during the game are answered at the end. Might make you sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: simple but extremely beautiful and fascinating game, i don't understand the complains from people that the story tries to put too many things together, everything is explained enough and the things tie with eachother, sure there are things that are given granted, but it's a very heartbreaking story which is leaving an important moral, it's not overly complex but also not dumb simple, which is a good balance for the playtime, it'll probably leave you feels.The gameplay is simple and sweet, the puzzles will be relatively easy, some will be slightly harder but all managable, there's a nice feature of skipping puzzles if you really can't solve themThe visuals are really beautiful and relaxing, the pixel art is a great artistic choicegood job on the dev(s), this game is a sweet gem, for the price i'd say it's completely worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The game is simply beautiful, with smooth animation, gorgeous colors and just quality pixel art! The puzzles were challenging but not too much for someone like me who is, unfortunately, often struggling in platform puzzles like these. I wll say however that an ending has never made me so angry before. I've had depressing endings in game before and can handle it, but this took the cake I think? It's probably a good thing that a game can trigger such emotions in someone, and I suppose everyone will have their own opinion on this, but personally if I am ever terminally ill and someone ever pulls a Evan's Remains on me, I hope ghosts are real so I can come back and beat their ass with my two ghost hands. SCREW that ending tbh!! My boy deserved better >:(
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a stunning game that puts story before gameplay itself. I personally found the idea of so much dialogue to be a bit of a downside until towards the end where the story truly unraveled. The pixel art/ animation is gorgeous as is the story and music that plays in the background.I would recommend this to anyone who wants a casual gaming experience with a good story. Ending had me sad. Good game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Beautifully polished art style and soundtrack, well written plot (barring a few plotholes), simplistic yet challenging puzzles.I liked the "big reveal" at the end quite a lot and I'm a huge sucker for very-well designed puzzles. Every piece in each puzzle in the game felt intentional with no extra pieces and all of them were enjoyable to solve
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Game isn't bad, but it's one of the most 'fine' games I've ever played. I liked the puzzles, story was fine to meh, but honestly, it's a puzzle platformer that I wouldn't recommend to anyone really. If there was a middle option, I'd pick that, but due to the clear talent on display, it's at least worth the 2-3 hours and $7.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10SPOILER FREE REVIEWPROS___________Soundtrack: The music is great. Some of these tracks will be stuck in my head for days. Very chill, mainly acoustic track. Theirs one track that has this electric guitar riff that goes so hard.Art: The game is stunning. Beautiful pixel art, every single level is gorgeous to look at. The characters are all very well done and have a great art style.Gameplay: The puzzles are super challenging but in a really good way. They really require you to think outside of the box and slow down and carefully consider every jump you make. I cannot stress enough how fun some of these puzzles were, especially if you like to take your time on harder puzzles.Story: I liked a lot of the characters. The ending was beautiful. Lots of cool plot twists I didn't see coming. How they completely change the narrative just by changing perspective is super super cool, and I don't think I have ever seen it done quite like this. CONS___________Difficulty pacing: Some of the puzzles feel way too difficult early on, and then some puzzles are just super easy and I could beat first try. I get that they kind of explain this in the story as to why this is, but it makes the game suffer. I was legitimately stumped on some of the earlier puzzles, that felt like they deserved to be in the middle or towards the end.Story/Dialogue: This games story has a lot going on, sometimes to its detriment. The gameplay is broken up by some pretty lengthy dialogue scenes. Sometimes they drag on too long, and the last 15 or 20 minutes of the game is almost entirely dialogue. A lot of whats going on will be very very confusing, until the big reveals at the end, and even then I felt like I had some unanswered questions. I think trimming some of the excess characters and scenes would help with the pacing a lot and make it more digestible.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very nice and cozy style. Looks very promising when you just start playing. Then there is a very slow build up, keeping you in anticipation of some kind of interesting plot twist or the gameplay change. The further you go, the more of the gameplay is just storytelling, there is just a bare minimum of puzzle solving and the puzzles don't get harder and otherwise nothing else changes, so 90% of it is just a visual novel. I guess I expected more action and interesting puzzles or some kind of active participation in the story (choices, interactions, etc.). The story ends with the strangest plot twist (read Reiyu's review explaining why). I get that it's a casual indie game and I got it with a discount. I don't regret playing it, but I would appreciate it more if it was either shorter or more engaging or have a better story, so I can't really recommend buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains was... a unique experience for me, to say the least. I came in expecting a puzzle platformer with a dash of story, and got almost the exact opposite.You spend more time in Evan's Remains following the story than you do solving puzzles, which is usually not the kind of games I enjoy, as visual novels usually bore me. But you know what? Evan's Remains made it work, for some reason I can't pinpoint. I really enjoyed the story, and it helped that I didn't feel like it tried to waste my time.The puzzles are short and simple, but fun to solve.In summary, Evan's Remains is a short and sweet story based game with some nice amount of puzzles between story beats. It's a great way to spend ~3 hours!
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This was an inspiring story and a moderately challenging platformer. The story is actually quite engaging and reminded me of Celeste's method of previewing its story (Bit of gameplay, rewarded with story after). I am pleasantly appeased by this game and I recommend you at least beat the game, cuz even if you don't like story, its still fun to challenge your brain.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Not a long game by any means, more visual novel then game but there are some nice light puzzle platforming between dialogues. Music is nice enough and the story tho not groundbreaking was engaging enough with perhaps a message if you really want to take one away from it. Fun little game for a couple hours worth the 5 euro
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

Some of them did take me a few tries before figuring it out. So a good balance in that aspect. What I was more intrigued about was the story, which... wow! And some of the discussions among Dysis and Clover had a lot of deep thoughts.And also the art is so pretty; I personally like the pixel artstyle. So Evan's Remains is overall an indie I can recommend! Here's my first impressions:

_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game a while ago on a giveaway, found it interesting, asked for it, and was lucky enough to get it. Jump forward an entire year, I think? And I played this from back to back and 100% it. Is it good? Yeah, beautiful graphics, exciting and sometimes hard puzzles, just the perfect small game to play during an afternoon with nothing to do, since I took approximately 4 hours to 100% it. However, I will say I do not like the story at all, I like the characters but the story is clunky, nonsensical, and didn't really answer what I wanted, with so many plot twists I got really lost during one point in the game.TLDR: excellent graphics and puzzles, bad story, 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get it tbh. The platforming and puzzles are alright, The graphics are lovely, the soundtrack is nice, but the story side of things is weird. It starts up interesting but by the end starts throwing plot twist after plot twist at you with most of them crammed into the last twenty minutes or so. I don't want to get into spoilers but the story just rapidly spirals out of control and there isn't enough time in a three hour game for any of the twists to be set up or sink in before it moves on to the next.Do I recommend it? Eh, the game part was nice and if you can get it on sale its alright but I wouldn't buy it for the story. I would put it as neutral recommended but steam doesn't let you do that, so negative I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little puzzle game with an interesting story.Puzzles are relatively simple; what surprised me was that difficulty of them stayed roughly the same throughout the whole game despite the additions of new mechanics.Gameplay as a whole could be a bit smoother: during one puzzle my would refuse to move after jumping as if hitting a wall for some reason (but that was just one specific place); you can skip puzzles but the dialogue can only be fast-forwarded and only from the pause menu - I didn't find a specific button for that; and the lack of options menu was really annoying (I couldn't change out of fullscreen and had to deal with the game minimizing whenever I clicked on the second monitor and the initial volume was too loud with no way to change in-game).Again though, these are just minor complaints that didn't detract much from my enjoyment of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The story was... outstanding, touching, a million words couldn't describe how great it was. I haven't thought the story could turn out this way. On one hand, I'm sad it ended like that. But on the other hand, I can't decide if it's a happy or a sad ending. And that's one more thing that makes it special.With the lovely music accompanying it alongside. The art, that was wonderful, full of colours, and feelings. And the animations and fun puzzles gave it a real charm.It is a masterpiece of a game, and I enjoyed every second playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan´s Remains is an easy puzzle platformer. With a story that left me disgusted with what I spent my time doing in this game. I get the message this game is trying to push but it lands flat in so many ways.I genuinly don't know how to say this without spoiling anything. But basically, in this game you play the villain except it really tries to play itself off as you are the good guy/girl. In the end, this game left a really bad taste in my mouth. I don't wanna be to mean to this game couse before the ending I was hooked on the story, it was a good mystery until the end. Which makes me feel like the story writer here really has alot of potential, as the ending does work it only sucks. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out so nicely, you get some backstory on why do you even jump around and solve puzzles and who are you even looking for. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: It's games like Evan's Remains that make me wish Steam Reviews offered a Star ranking system than a simple Up/Down one, because I didn't HATE this game... I just also think it was pretty mediocre.Evan's Remains is a narrative-driven, 2D puzzle platformer where you play as a girl named Dysis, who goes to a strange, uninhabited island to look for a missing boy named Evan. As the game goes on, you learn more and more about who Evan is, the company that sent Dysis to the island to search for him, and the nature of the island itself. That's the spoiler-free version. Despite my gripes with this game, if you wish to play it for yourself, you deserve to go in knowing as little as possible, because your mileage may vary from mine.My biggest problem with the story is the same problem I have with the game - it's way too short. I beat this game in one sitting in two hours, and while that means the story moves at a solid clip the whole time, almost constantly giving you more and more revelations, it also means nothing gets the chance to really settle down or develop. Characters speak in somewhat vague terms, and by the end, the story only ever felt like a peek into the bigger picture, but never like a full package. It left me wanting more, and not in a good way. I'm also not sure how I feel about the ending, since it seemed to be left intentionally emotionally ambiguous, but that made playing through the game feel somewhat unsatisfying. I don't mind ambiguous, but I don't like incomplete.Now, I did not get all the achievements in this game, so it's likely there are elements to the story that I missed, which I accept. But I didn't feel compelled enough to go search it out after my first playthrough.Which is a shame, because the actual gameplay isn't terrible. The puzzles aren't exactly challenging, and that almost works to its benefit. It means there aren't long stretches of frustrating tedium or moments where you feel like bashing your head against the wall. The makes playing the game almost like a comforting experience, since the mixture of the presentation and simple gameplay make it very appealing. But, due to the short length, the puzzles feel like they're over before you know it, and aren't particularly clever on their own.Easily the best part of this game is its presentation. The pixel art and animation is downright gorgeous, and the music is soothing and somewhat atmospheric. Character portraits are very well-drawn, and the colot choice is incredibly vibrant and full of life. There's no doubt in my mind the people working on this game are talented, but given my problems, Evan's Remains almost feels like a waste of said talent. I can only hope the developer's next project will really knock it out of the park.Despite my negative opinions of this game, it's length means that it's at least worth a shot. If you still want to play it, I recommend letting it go on sale first. Otherwise, you're better off spending that time watching a good movie instead.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute hidden gem or a game.To be completely honest I was not to big on the puzzles at all and if it took me more than like 5 minutes to figure it out I just skipped it. That is because the story of this game is what shines the most. I didn't even care about the gameplay as much as I wanted to see what came next in the story.The story was so profoundly interesting and made me feel all kinds of emotions. off sale this game is $6.99 and I say it is 100% worth the price of admission and if it is on sale at all just buy it. Took me 3 hours start to finish and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game! A great challenge as far as puzzle solving goes, and what a plot twist! (No I'm NOT going to reveal any spoilers! _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The visual style is great, and the music is pretty good.The story is certainly not what I expected, and although it is certainly a sad story, it is also pretty good, and that twist at the end, I did not see that coming at all. Throughout the game you have to piece together the story, but by the end you'll have everything revealed and explained, with I think not many things left to be confused about, well perhaps except one or two things, but very minor things..Clover is quite a deep character, which makes sense given his situation. Some of the stuff he says is quite interesting, and I would certainly agree with him. That whole story is quite interesting. Which would you choose in such a specific situation, the lie or the truth? Well, I'm getting off topic.The puzzle platforming is fairly nice. It was interesting and fun. I didn't find it too difficult, but for those that do or simply want to focus on the story, you have the skip puzzle option, which is nice.The only bug I've seen is a sound bug if you fast forward dialog while the dialog has already started it will play the speaking tone of whoever was speaking at the time you press the option and it will stay there until the screen switches.Overall, a pretty great story and game, although a very sad one.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story-first sort of game. There are 24 puzzles centered around creating and destroying platforms, none of them super difficult. The music is nice, the pixel art is gorgeous.The story will be polarizing because, although the mystery is interesting, the way the reveal works and the subsequent moral of the story will frankly be repellant to some. There are other flaws, like pacing issues, an info-dump heavy last act, and a player character who needs but never receives a proper character arc.The game IS worth playing, the whole package is beautiful, and it's by no means incompetently told. But your enjoyment will totally rely on how you react to the game's messaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to have to give this a thumbs down, unfortunately. I really enjoyed the pixel art, and the puzzles were relatively easy and relaxing, but that's about it. The only character I genuinely enjoyed was Clover, which I think you're meant to. But if I was supposed to like the rest of them, or that ending? No can do.The overarching purpose for the ending wasn't explained in depth enough, and was vaguely explained in the most confusing way. The characters (other than Clover) didn't seem to have any purpose, really,  nor were they interesting to me. I won't even get started on the "plot twist." Apologies to the creator in advance, but it was a failed attempt at seeming way smarter than the average person and ended up being corny and completely destroying the depth of anything attempting to be created. I wished it was better.3/10
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a Review for this one is really hard. I got it as part of the humble bundle and just now got to play it and it has me split.This Puzzle-Platformer is rather simple. Of the 28 mini-puzzles in the game only about 5 are really challenging which is fine if you take this one as a relaxing platformer. After every few puzzles you learn about the story, which sometimes works perfectly, sometime however you have huge story dumps which leads to disproportionate playtime vs. exposition time. Exposition is another keayword here, due to this being a small project it relies a lot on "don't show, tell" which is a rather bad approach to storytelling, especially with videogames. While the locations are well designed, some places just don't make any sense or are not explained well, which hurts the world building (I can't elaborate on this without spoilers). The story itself is a little convoluted and I am actually repulsed by the plot itself which is a stark contrast to the lovely pixel art used. I feel happy looking at the game but disgusted thinking about it's contents from a moral view.Overall the 2.5 hours i spent on this game were ok but nothing more.  Looking at the price of 5.69€ I cannot reccomend this game to others as it has too many issues both in gameplay and complexity. I appreciate the dev's effort but sadly I have to provide a thumbs down here.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend gave this game to me, and I gotta say I really am glad they did.This game is pretty good at telling the story. It has an interesting twist to the end that when you play a second time you view it from a whole new angle entirely.  (that sorry I will not spoil) It's a game that makes you realize your own mortality with the theme of immortality.The puzzles are not overtly hard. Some will be head scratchers, but nothing that makes you look up a guide.Before you say anything about the platforming and needing "par-core skills" it's as difficult as a 1st level of Mario. Just remember sometimes you gotta run agenst a wall before you jump.8/10 Would definitely recommend for a day killer.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game with nice art and some light platform puzzles. You can skip the puzzles from the pause menu and treat it like a sidescrolling dialogue driven mystery if you want, although i never skipped any.My only gripes with the game would be the uneven spacing of dialogue in some parts. I think it would have flowed better if some puzzles were moved between some sections of dialogue. Also the ending. If they took the very last major reveal of the game out, the story would have landed for me much better, as it would have ended on a more upbringing note.If you feel like spending a few hours with some interesting characters doing some platforming puzzles, I recommend.Won't recommend if you're impatient with dialogue boxes.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay / puzzles are... fine; not too difficult and I didn't have to look up a walkthrough or skip any (though it's nice to have that option). They get kinda samey near the end, but they're broken up by story segments and the game is short enough that they don't overstay their welcome. The art is pretty; no complaints here. The story keeps you guessing right up until the big twist is revealed, at which point you will either find it very fun (like I did) or hate it. I think it's an interesting plot, and one we don't see enough of in games.A perfectly adequate game, though definitely not all that complex. Also, the post-credit scene makes absolutely no sense and I have to assume it's just mentioning backers. Would be nice to signpost that a little more clearly; I was hoping for one more bit of clarification about our protagonist. Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan’s Remains is a sort of story, puzzle, platformer, and the real draw to it is the story and the art. The main purpose of this game is to tell the story. If you are interested in the idea of this story, it is worth picking up, but if you want a good puzzle game I would give it a pass, there are a lot of cutscenes and they are definitely just a supplement to the experience. The puzzles and platforming is fine, but not necessarily anything exceptional. In fact, the puzzles can be skipped entirely.The pixelart for this game is gorgeous, it creates this tone and world that feels surreal and amazing. Mixing nature and artificial with the sky and world around it, makes for some of my favorite background art in any game, and why I was initially drawn to it.I don’t want to go into too much detail about the story because it is the entire game, but it is short and is worth the effort to play through to unravel it all. I do not think that this will resonate with everyone, but the people that it will resonate with I think will really connect to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to describe. Basically, you play a series of jumping puzzles, and then read some dialogue. At first, the puzzles seem to have nothing to do with the story, but then they slowly merge together. The story itself is...well it's unique. It doesn't entirely make sense, but it has a good message and is well written.  It's actually the kind of thing I'd play again at some point, as the puzzles are fun, and it would be interesting to see the story unfold while knowing (mostly) what's going on. I'd actually love to see more of this world, with its towering monoliths and strange mix of tropical locations and straight-up science fiction.It's short, but sweet, and I very much enjoyed my time with Evan's Remains. Er, with playing the game, I mean.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend Evan's Remains?Sure.Yes, even, if you want to do some 90-ish minutes of above average puzzle platforming with some really great pixel art, very nice music, and overall pretty pleasant game-feel.My caveat is this: if you make it through the first couple story moments and aren't crazy about the writing... it doesn't get better. There gets to be more of it... and it gets...well.. "soap-opera-y" might be generous.Before I make it sound like I'm not impressed, this game was developed by just one guy, Matias Schmeid, and it's clearly built with incredible love and care, and what it does well, it does REALLY well. This game is lovely, and it's nothing to sneeze at. That said... The writing is not the strong-suit of this game, although, credit where credit is due, it's VERY unique. The plot is the sort of convoluted mess that, once pieced together chronologically (it's told out of order) makes less sense than if it just hadn't been explained at all. The ending reads like one of the joke Silent Hill 2 endings. It's really bizarre, in a contrarian, "every expectation must be subverted" type of way, not in a shocking or satisfying way. It's a twist on a twist and it seems like the sort of thing that just got away from the creator. The world-building in the cut scenes is alternatively much too specific, or needlessly vague. The story doesn't particularly connect to gameplay, and the couple of times the core puzzle-solving mechanic is brought up, it's handwaved away in a fashion that is both unsatisfying in the moment, and, in retrospect even more nonsensical. The dialog boxes, the character portraits, the little "mumbles" that accompany dialog, they're all pretty good. The dialog itself is in a bloated, overwritten, visual novel style that takes you out of the gameplay really significantly. It's unskippable, with input required after every line, which is wild, because the puzzles are skippable for some reason... if you're not enjoying the story, or you're waiting for it to become something comprehensible, the cutscenes quickly become a chore between otherwise fun puzzles.The puzzles themselves are, as I said, above-average. Not genre-re-defining or anything, but extremely solid, with great feel to them, and exceptional art! The character sprites, the level backgrounds and foregrounds, the particles, the animations... they're really top-notch with so much polish as to make this game seem like it's coming out of a big studio. The music and sound design is also incredible. The sound of gently rolling surf mixes with the mostly chill soundtrack beautifully. The higher energy tracks are also surprisingly suitable and catchy (although, they don't quite accent any particular ramp up in tension in the plot).Here's the thing: I love puzzle games. And I love a good story game. But forcing a story onto a puzzle game like this, without having any gameplay implications for the plot.... it's unsatisfying at best, detrimental at worst.So here's my suggestion: Give players the choice, puzzle mode or story mode. I think the couple dozen puzzles in this game are very good, and the art and sound is outstanding. there doesn't have to be much, if any connective tissue between puzzles. Just string them together and give the players the option of getting that dopamine hit of solving puzzle after puzzle in succession. And leave the story mode in there. There's plenty of appeal there... it's not my cup of tea, but the character portraits might be worth the price of admission.AnyhowDo you like Puzzle games and can put up with a bonkers story that kinda pads the game out so long as the puzzles are good and the art is great? This game gets my recommendation for that case.Alternatively, do you like oddball contrarian visual novels with great art and weird writing, and won't mind a few puzzles between the cloudcuckooland logic, then this is also a recommendation for you folks.Bottom line:+Amazing Art Design+Great Music+Fun Puzzle/Platforming+Completionist Friendly (only a few hours to play through the entire game)-Overwrought Plot  -Mediocre Dialog-Plot Slows Pacing

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend Evan's Remains with a massive asterisk. The pixel art is beautiful, the puzzles are shallow with the exception of a 1-2 that are more annoying than fun, and lastly the story is great but a bit long winded. If this sounds like your cup of tea go for it. I think the current price tag of $6.99 is about right although I did get it as part of my Humble Monthly. The game will take you about 3 hours to finish and a bit longer if you choose to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a mix of a 2D-platformer, a side-scrolling puzzler, and a visual novel.Yes, you will do so much reading (around 50% of the playing time) because it is heavily focused on the narrative. No voice-overs, only texts. The story telling is quite brilliant, and the dialogues are well crafted. However, for some, the story itself may feel hit-or-miss. For me, it is serviceable. Some of the questions remained unanswered.I really like the music and sound design. I'll definitely purchase the OST DLC.Also, it is a decent-looking game.The gameplay is good. I played with a controller. The movement felt smooth. For the most part, puzzles are on the easier side. One can skip the puzzles and dialogues if they want. The platforming may feel janky at times, but I quickly got used to it. Since this game is quite short, that didn't become a major issue. The achievements are easy to get. (You may need to refer to a guide for a couple of achievements.)For me, a character named Clover has carried the game throughout. Kudos to the developers.He delivered so many great dialogues that I really liked.I choked up a little at the end.The post-credit sequence felt unnecessary. They could have avoided that.But overall, I enjoyed my playtime. It kept me engaged till the end.It is worth getting during a sale or when available in a bundle.My verdict: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The first time a videogame managed to make me cry, the story isn't as bad as everyone says on the internet. The music is amazing, the sound are really well composed too, and it was really cheap, there is no reason why anyone shouldnt have this game. You can say that the playtime is really low, i managed to "beat" it in 3.6 hours, but to that I can only answer that this game is not a puzzle game, there are some puzzles that make you think real intense, but there are no impossible ones.This game is mainly a linear story based visual novel, and that can be a drawback that outside of speedrunning there is no replayability, but I still love this game with full of my heart, I think everyone who can should give it a shot :).Edit: I just remembered a minute after I posted this, this is actually the second time a game made me cry, the first was in Honkai 3rd.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Why is it so hard for makers of 95% of these dialog-intensive games to make sitting through the dialogs less of an annoying chore? You (any one of these kinds of games) could:- make the text speed variable (from instant to slow)- make the font variable- have a checkbox to enable/disable the screechy bleeping- make the amount of text variable that pops in with each balloon- include an option for "stop type-in effect and immediately drop all text when pressing <key1>", while having a different <key2> to enter through to the next balloon, so I don't accidentally skip very short text balloons while frustratingly tapping <key1> because the text is entering too slowlyWhy do I have to click through DOZENS of balloons with just three words in them, that appear haltingly slow, when they could just allow me to decrease the font size by 50%, increase the amount of text in the screen by 100%, and deliver the story in a much more readable way (to me), and to anyone else who wants different variations?This kind of annoying thing happens ALL THE TIME in these asian dialog-intensive games. I really, really don't get it. Please allow players more freedom in how they consume all that beautiful dialog. At this point I'm like 15 minutes in, played about 5 pretty fun platforming puzzles, and finally simply RQ'ed when the umpteenth annoying dialog sequence popped up.If you make the text story delivery devices annoying, uncustomizable, screechy, unskippable and altogether unnecessarily retro, then you distract the player from the actual story.Why. I don't get it.Also, the platforming is awkward in this game, somehow the detection boxes are unintuitive  to me. But I could easily get used to that.The music is great. The graphics are OK, although the protagonist girl for some reason has one brown arm and leg while running, probably as a shadow effect but that just looks weird. Again, small nuisance.The big thing is the text delivery. I'd rather go back and play Leisure Suit Larry 1 and 2, released in 1987/1988. Now those were terrible games by today's standards, but at least it had good text delivery.I'm so sorry that there are so few dialog balloon games to like because of this, but at the same time, I fault the developers for simply not getting this. That said - it's probably me, because typically I'm the only one I see complaining about this. Whatever. Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is really interesting.
