_childDocuments_.review: A hidden island, an undiscovered secret, a shady megacorp and a collection of child prodigies. This isn’t an adaptation of 2004’s TV giant Lost, but Evan’s Remains, a Gameboy Advance-evoking title; solely developed by Matías Schmeid and published by Whitethorn Digital. On the surface Evan’s Remains is a straightforward puzzle platformer title that could easily be overlooked if it wasn’t for a compelling narrative woven around its problem solving offerings. The set up is simple, our titular character Evan, a world renowned child prodigy, has gone missing. But a letter sent to megacorp UpBring details his whereabouts on a mysterious island in the Pacific Ocean. Unbeknown to anyone, Evan has requested a girl named Dysis be the one to journey and find him with the player assuming the role of her as she arrives at the island alongside her UpBring handler. The art design throughout is decent, with a calming and almost pastel-esque colour scheme. Different stages, seven in total,  provide variety in backdrops and foregrounds with well drawn art that fits the location well. The layered backgrounds help lift the perspective beyond its two dimensional restraints, but at times can be a little empty; there is often not a great deal for you to look at whilst your eyes wander between puzzles. The puzzle sections, or Monoliths, themselves do not vary as much if at all, and whilst that fits with their purpose, it can become a bit repetitive and dull. The character sprites are animated well, and little touches such as crunching sand beneath feet and a spectacularly satisfying thud as you land a jump, really helps to ground the characters within the stages. The sound design overall is functional, sfx are minimal but work as intended whilst the score, seemingly taken from a free archive for the most part (fair enough for a solo dev.) fits well but is often forgettable. Having said that, how the pieces of music are used is well thought out. It helps transform sunny beaches and sleepy coves into more melancholy explorations and at times creates a truly surreal atmosphere that plays well with the narrative. We’ll touch more on the narrative in a moment, but the other side of this game beyond its visual novel approach to storytelling, is its puzzle platforming screens. You start at one side and must navigate various surfaces to eventually leap over an imposing pillar that marks the end of a puzzle. Platforms can be revealed or hidden via different ledges, marked with a symbol, that act as switches. The puzzles gradually evolve to incorporate teleportation and spring platforms, but never grow too far beyond the initial format. In general they are fine and can be satisfying to solve, but the lack of variety becomes a bit strained. The difficulty curve is also all over the place, with levels varying wildly. This is addressed by the characters, but it doesn’t help the fact you can sometimes feel like you’re not really learning organically as you go. You can also skip almost every puzzle in the game without penalty, which could either be generous to the player or perhaps a concession that they can be too frustrating at times for the player to be motivated to see them through. It might also be considered that the ability to skip these puzzles is for players more interested in experiencing the story of Evan’s Remains and this is fair enough, as it is a good tale told well. The majority of the relatively diverse cast are likeable characters with interesting and relatable motivations. Their relationships develop well, especially that of the Dysis and her eventual partner in mystery solving ‘Clover’. The latter, in general, is well fleshed out with flashback sequences filling out his history. The downside of these narrative heavy expository scenes between characters is that they are guilty of perhaps going on slightly too long at times. The story drip feeds information well and subverts itself a few times which keeps your mind running wild with theories. As it pans out, red herrings will become more apparent and ultimately after embracing themes of honesty and openness, how the story evolves may end up being divisive. It eventually leans heavily on morality and your opinions on that, will likely come down to your own perception of morals. How the story blends with the puzzles that break up the story is telegraphed but ultimately frustrating. You learn that the monoliths scattered throughout the island paradise represent a language and solving them is helping Clover with his translation, an aim he reveals early on to the player character. This feels under-explored and it may have been more interesting to work out what they say yourself, rather than simply being told their definition by Clover. Ultimately the narrative is well written and structured, a science fiction mystery crossed with existential philosophy that goes to show the talent that exists in the indie space. Evan’s Remains is a title that offers puzzles that may or may not be of interest, depending on your preference, but never allows them to hinder a surprisingly complex and layered narrative. The roughly three or four hours you spend with Dysis and co. is a rewarding experience that leaves a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it a thumbs up, but do note: it's a "it's a bit complicated++" rather than a straight-up endorsement.The short of it is, Evan's Remains is a truly excellent example of what a tiny studio run-of-the-mill indie game should be in an ideal world. In that world we have a studio whose capacity for handling the workload isn't very big, but instead of that leading to the project getting away from it with all the things they'd like to do until it either ends falling apart, turns crap or just gets stuck in the early access hell, they scale it back and polish it according to their strengths. And so it's a small game from a small studio, but one that's lovingly crafted. The art is pretty, the story is interesting (even its plot holes) without dwelling on needless detail, and the gameplay is serviceable - it's a "puzzle platformer" but the puzzles aren't really the point so they're kept rather easy. The result has its limitations, but it's overall a worthwhile experience that doesn't overstay its welcome. I don't know how big the studio who made it is in actual reality, but this picture of what that perfect world tiny indie studio would do should give you the idea of what to expect of this game.For the long of it just play the game and see. It's basically a movie length affair.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. The story will take you less than 3 hours to complete. It's got some good noggin fuel to think about after the game is done. The post-credit scene isn't story related, just a thing for backers so try not to let it take you out of it since it kills the mood a bit from the ending. Good puzzles, some clever ones, not too hard and not the worst writing in an indie game I've seen. Overall pretty solid and easy to 100% complete the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting story, lovely pixel graphics and nice atmospheric music to top it off. There's also puzzles based around a nice concept, but they are pretty simple so as to not distract from the story, while still breaking up the monotony of constant dialogues, but in essence the game is here for the story, which definitely manages to tuck at the heartstrings while also bringing some twists that managed to catch me off guard.If you're looking for a short game to get immersed in for an afternoon, pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. The Puzzles are pretty simple, not too challenging, but I doubt that was the direction the Developers were going for, for the main reason I love the game is the story. It kept me engaged, kept me thinking, and kept me going to know more.It's honestly given me a new perspective on life, and how I've been wasting mine this whole time. 10/10 I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: the art is beautiful, the music and sound are great.for a casual game (as it's classified on this page), it's chill and great as a package. for me personally, the (plentiful) dialogue wasn't engaging enough to draw me to the story, and the platforming and puzzling weren't deep enough to draw me into playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely have so big an urge to write an review.Great, great game!!I started playing for the puzzles. But i stayed for the story. The atmosphere, life perspective and wisdom, in this chill enviroment does something good to me.The puzzles are not hardcore, but can still be challeging, as they shouldIn the start of the game, i was eager to play more puzzle and hurry the story, since i did not yet know the game concept. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: My gameplay time is probably about an hour too long, as I did leave the game running without being on it once or twice. So consider that this is about a 90 minute game, which isn't bad. It's pretty. It's got really fun gameplay. But there's about 20 minutes of good gameplay in a 90 minute game.I kept being met with overly long dialogue/cut scene sections when I really wanted to play more of the game. Seriously, there was one time where I spent a minute or less solving a puzzle, then there was an at least five-minute long scene of just text dialogue. And then another under-a-minute puzzle followed by another long cut scene.I wanted to be interested in the story. I tried to be in the start. It did interest me. But it got annoying. I would like to know the story, but at this point I have to watch it like a movie. Because the pacing in this game kills it as a game. It's a movie where every few minutes you do a puzzle. It's not a puzzle game. There's a good puzzle game in there, if only you had a chance to play it. And if only there were more of that. I think if there were more puzzles, it could have been paced better, I wouldn't have felt annoyed if there'd been the same amount of story but four times as much gameplay time. But as it is, I ended up using the "skip dialogue" option every time I had the chance after I got sick of not being able to play the game.As it is, if you want to watch a little movie where instead of commercial breaks you play an interesting 2D platformer puzzle, this is great! But if you want to play a 2D platformer puzzle game, you're going to be annoyed because you'll get one simple one done and then get hit with a wall of text. And you'll be wondering, "When do I get to play the game?" And then it ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great considering its size and price.Beautiful artworks + music creates a calm atmosphere and I appreciate that.Even though the plot is kind of weird and unusual, it's still pretty effective and I like it.The ending is great and it makes me feel a bit better about life. Thanks for making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I see some review complaining that the game is not a fast paced platformer or that it has a lot of story. Well, go play Celeste or something then, since this game is not for you.This is the problem with putting games into genres. Some might like the puzze aspect of it, or the platforming, or the story (which is the main focus).All in all, the art and visual design is really nice in my opinion. The world and the movements are fluid. The way the dialogue is presented could be different, but for me it didn't matter all that much as the story itself made me feel things. The puzzles are not very hard in my opinion, although I don't have much experience with such games.Overal, 8/10, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start off by saying this is way more about a story than a puzzle platformer. If you're coming just for a puzzle/platformer, look elsewhere. There's about 30 puzzles in the game and each one will only take a few minutes. The other 2 hours of the game is reading dialogue. You'll spend more time reading than playing, that's for sure.That being said, the story is rather interesting. I think it's worth a playthrough for a story if you want something more casual and relaxed. It took me about 4 hours to complete the game and unlock all the achievements. If you blow through the dialogues, you can probably perfect this game in an hour to an hour and a half if that's all your looking for. The story's interesting enough to keep going though. If you're looking just for a good puzzle/platformer, look elsewhere, but if you want an interesting story, you can give this short game a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: For $7? It's basically the price of a movie, so if you treat it like one then you can get your money's worth. The puzzles are fine - some may need a guide, but the rest are fairly easy. The story is a bit meh, especially since a big crux of the story is that  It's like the creator wanted to add a twist but just wasn't sure how to do it properly. The post-credits scene which was just to highlight Kickstarter backers was also a bit tonally offputting given the ending. Summary: good if you get it for free or on a sale. At full price, that ultimately depends on you.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer in which you play a woman who was summoned to an island by a mysterious genius and has to unravel the mystery of its monoliths. The puzzles are all right and the game lets you skip them if you like. My feelings about the story are mixed, but it was interesting enough that it kept me playing all the way through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't sure if I should play it, but after playing for a while it really won me over. The story is a bit confusing at the beginning, but it gets better in the middle to the end. It's a very good and emotional game. The puzzles are really good and challenging the further you get. I really enjoyed playing this game and I appreciate the hard work of the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This game was nothing what I was expecting when I first saw it nor when I started playing it. Usually when I decide I want to play a game I do watch a bit of gameplay to get the idea what the game is all about, but this time I went completely blind and I cannot express how glad I am. This game blew my mind 3 times over the course of it's story and really the story plays a bigger part in this game that the puzzles. Puzzles were short and interesting, giving us a break between dialogs and story progressions and I thought that was a great touch.I recommend this game to anyone who likes beautiful pixel art, a touching story, a mystery drama and a bit of puzzling on the side.i will definitely be replaying this, my new favorite indie game!(The soundtrack is awesome btw)
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this is an enjoyable game with lovely art and puzzles that are just challenging enough. The gameplay is very straightforward, but I do not at all mean that as a criticism. You run, you jump, you press switches. The puzzles offer challenge without being frustrating. According to Steam, it took me about 2.6 hours to complete my first playthrough of this game (including the post-credits section), and I will certainly spend some more time at some point to get the remaining achievements.Visually, the game is just lovely. Whilst not a style I usually enjoy, I couldn't but appreciate the visuals. The music is good too, but I will admit that the 'speech' can grate after a while.I was drawn in by the story. Whilst not delivered in the most elegant way, I found it charming, and I enjoyed trying to work out what was going on... to a point. For me, there is a turning point in this game where it feels forced, and nonsensical, but I can see what the developer was trying to do. However, this wasn't such a problem to stop me playing the game.Overall, this is definitely a game worth picking up and spending an afternoon playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Dear God this game is incredible. The art is stunning, the music is calming, and the puzzles are a great level of difficulty. None so hard that you feel desperate, but hard enough so you don't fly through them. But, if at any time you can't figure one out, you can skip it immediately. The focus of this game is on the story though, which absolutely blows everything else out of the water. It kept me hooked the entire time I was playing, building up to a scrambled plot twist that resolves everything in the game (though it is a tad exposition dumpy). PLEASE do yourself a favor and play this game, and drift through this masterfully told story.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great puzzle game with a clear and captivating story line. The art, sound design, game play and story really create a relaxing and inviting game that helps you unwind. The puzzles were not too tricky but felt like enough of a challenge at times... highly recommend as a relaxing cozy puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, story rich experience with breath-taking atmosphere & visuals. Whenever I wasn't gushing over the visuals and reflections, it was spent relating to the characters & trying to crack the secret at hand. The puzzles, the character design, the writing - I well recommend giving it a play through if you enjoy story-rich games.Also, big 10/10, can pet the dog.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I was impressed!  The platforming elements do NOT take skill to complete.  If you are worried about not being fast or precise enough...don't worry.  The puzzles are forgiving enough and just require some thought or trial and error, depending on how you prefer to handle puzzles. The music is amazing!  I don't often notice music in games, but the serene melodies here fit the game well.  I also enjoyed the smooth controls and animations.The storyline has a bit of twists and turns.  Initially, I felt that it was dumping too much story at once, and I just wanted to enjoy the actual gameplay.  But the game turns out to be rather "story-heavy" for a platformer.  Some people may hate taking breaks from gameplay for the story and some people may enjoy it.  The ending hurt my soul, but it was still a good ending.  There are some minor plot holes here and there, but nothing that I felt ruined the story or game overall.The game is a bit short, but the price reflects a game of this length and the polished nature.  This game seems to be a decent buy at regular price, and an even better deal if on sale.I wouldn't be surprised if a sequel appeared eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a very linear puzzle platformer game that has a decent story and some fun puzzles. Graphics are quite pretty and music is great. The best part of the game was the story which was like unwrapping multiple layers. The only grime I have about this game is that there is an achievement that requires changing the game language which although is a decent easter egg, it caused some confusion and made me restart my first run on accident because I cant read spanish. Overall: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most heart breaking game that I've played...But well done, perfect plot, perfect character, a very deep theme and an excellent moral dilemma!"Is it better to let the man die alone with the truth, or to die with fabricated lie to blind him from the truth?" It is the same question asked in the Matrix (by Morpheus) with a twist on "the man is dying and there is nothing you can do about it."And who is the hypocrite in that dilemma? I hate the ending, but I love the game.Wish to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzle game. Not very hard, only really got stuck on one of them but overall this plays more like a visual novel than anything, the puzzles feel like they're kinda there just to break up the dialogue. I've seen some people say this game has a convoluted story and while i don't disagree I don't think that it's poorly told. Everything wraps up nicely and it gives you a lot to think about in the end. I loved how the characters involved had a surprising level of depth and that the "mystery" behind the island was the way it was
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT A TWIST! _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game in an ad on YouTube, and I am really glad I did not skip it. The style captivated me and I looked it up to see what it was about. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little game. The puzzles remind me of Fez to be honest. And the story is an intriguing little one too, though it loathes me to admit I do not fully understand it even now. Laugh if you will at me. Overall I had fun with this! _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I like a good story time where I can find it. I happen to like puzzles and platforming too. Lo and behold, this game did not disappoint! Short and sweet. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: I really quite enjoy this style of game. _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: bough this game for like 3 euro and while browsing the reviews i saw many people complaining about the story (probably because the ending is not rly happy) or puzzle being to ez and short. I give it a shot being on sale for 3 euro and was totally worth the money puzzle being not ez or hard but and fun enough and the story was cool af despite being sad
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's remains is a ride full of surprises.The gameplay is good, it has a nice pair of puzzles, but it is not the main attraction of the game. The reason why you should play this game is the story that presents elements full of mysteries with a few twists that are very well thought, all accompanied with a really beautiful pixel art and an amazing soundtrack! If you have some free hours in your weekend, don't think too much about it, buy and play the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Very short game that still manages to have a pretty good story and characters. The artstyle and music are both great as well. _childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Fun gameplay gimmick.✔️ Enticing story with original characters, and a somewhat deep thought behind it.✔️ Really nice ambience created by cute pixel art graphics and enjoyable music.✔️ The puzzles generally aren't too easy or too hard, and can be skipped if you're just playing for the story.I loved this game and recommend it to pretty much anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains has gorgeous pixel art, nice music and unique and fun puzzles.The only bad thing about the game is the story and it is seriously bad. There is a ton of tedious dialogue and the plot twists only make sense in the writer's head.If there had been a simpler story, and less of it, and more puzzles, it would have been easy to recommend Evan's Remains. But if there is a sale, it is probably worth the money, because the puzzles are quite good. 3/5
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: A short game with interesting ideas and plot that's not too well executed.The story hooks, surprises and has more depth than you would expect in a 3 hour game, but sometimes the dialogue situations becomes too long and boring,The puzzle are easy and shoehorned into the plot, they could be in a diferent game where they could be exploited better and deeper.Despite everything, it leaves a good taste in your mouth and has a correct price.6.5 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: There's 2 sides to this game: first is the casual puzzle platformer, that's perfectly fine, but the majority of the game is a Visual Novel that is just not worth the time:+ Great pixel art+ Decent soundtrack+ Puzzles are engaging without being challenging- Limited facial expressions and no voice acting. This wouldn't be too bad but the story tries to be emotionally impactful, but with no other way to convey emotion they've gone with the tell, don't show approach- Convoluted plot leads to a solid half of the dialog being exposition dumps- All the characters have about as much depth as a scoobie doo episode. Why do you talk up your title character do be this brilliant, rich and famous paragon of your story's society, then leave him bumbling around clueless for the whole plot, serving only to be the target of relentless exposition?
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a fairly simple puzzle platformer with good music and beautiful pixel art. The gameplay is good for someone who likes puzzles casually; they were easy enough for me to never feel frustrated, and often only took a handful of tries tops to beat. As for the story, a big part of it moved me enough to make me cry, but other parts seemed like they came and went too quickly, specifically towards the end. The writing brings up a couple of ideas that are worth thinking about after the game ends. Overall, I'd say Evan's Remains has its flaws but is well worth the time and money. I found myself wishing that it kept going after it ended, to further explore the world and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful narrative-driven puzzle game. The puzzles themselves are short and simple and not the reason to play the game, the main attraction is the story, without it and the presentation the puzzles could be not bad but a bit boring.I'm not sure how I feel about how some moments in the story were executed, especially later in the game, but overall I found the experience enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is a short, sweet, and beautiful platformer. You play a girl named Dysis who has been tasked by Evan, a genius boy, to go to an uninhabited island, find him, and bring him home. As you venture into the island, you find puzzles to complete which increase in difficulty. As you complete each puzzle, you will slowly come to understand what is really going on, and what is the significance of you and the island you're on. With beautiful pixel art, a relaxing soundtrack, and an intriguing story, this game is quite the hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most polarizing games I've ever played. On one hand, the art style, the soundtrack, and the characters were all amazing. It looks so beautiful, sounds relaxing and i loved all the little interactions people had with each other throughout the game. But then we get to the less fortunate part, the story. In the beginning I was intrigued and I couldn't stop playing so I could know what happens next but by the end the story began to crumble. There is one or two major loopholes that just blew it for me in a time that I should've been moved. If this game was able to tie itself together I would have said It was my favorite game this year but it didn't! I feel it barely gets by with a positive for the beauty it has and the relatively low price tag. Considering everything it was a cute little romp that could've been improved with a more concrete narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I've played some games with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark themes this year, but this one might take the cake. I can't really say more about it without spoiling the story and the story pretty much is the entire game. The puzzle platforming segments really only seem to be there to break the pace, and I'm not actually sure what the purpose of them is within the narrative. Not only that, but you can skip them if you so desire.Suffice to say, I did enjoy the game, though I think the enjoyment of anyone else who plays it will largely depend on their tolerance for the narrative which is not a sure thing. In that sense, I can't really recommend this game to anyone but must also recommend it to everyone at the same time. I'll put it like this: If you feel that you were ripped off by the end, the game is only two hours at max. You'll most likely be able to return it if you don't like it, not that it's all that expensive in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Short Decent Game, Finished around 2.5-3 hours, A few missable Achievements that you should look at the guide for to save yourself a couple hours of going back. Story has an interesting almost predictable twist. you can fastforward dialog in the pause menu and skip puzzles as well. overall would recommend for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid little indie puzzle game.  The game is very kind in that if you ever get too frustrated you can always skip a puzzle and then still enjoy the story.  The ending was a little too long on the exposition but the game has a great twist and a lot of heart.  Overall this game is worth it at full price for a really solid puzzle platformer.  Can't get any simpler than just moving and jumping.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet, Evan's Remains is less of a puzzle game and more a story-based experience in tight package of easy and chill platforming riddles and excellent presentation.When I say story-based experience, I definitely mean it. There are  of text boxes to go through.. While writing is not perfect in many places and game tends to test your patience a little bit with the cutscenes' length, but thankfully everything lands nicely at the end. Characters have tons of secrets to reveal. Plot twists and turns quite a lot despite game's length. Everything end on a quite emotional, ambiguous note that I could consider a perfect little bow where it need to be.The puzzle part of the game is based on platforming using several gimmicks. You always need to get to the other side of the monolith while navigating through platforms that disappear, teleport or change position. Challenges are very elegant, reasonably balanced difficulty-wise and definitely not distracting from the core experience.Top-tier pixel art and calm music definitely seals the deal. Story is intriguing, puzzles are chill and game's art is excellent. For a relatively small price, Evan's Remains is certainly a soothing experience that will not leave you unsatisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Very intricate level designs along with tricky platforming with an enjoyable story tinged in mystery. Really liked the lush environments, music and animation as well. I'll admit: though I actually really liked the story, I can safely say it's not for everyone. Some people may like the game's structure more, and that's understandable. It warrants a try of course. I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy pixel art and puzzle platformers and want a relaxing game with a bit of a story added in I would recommend this game. It's very well done in many aspects. HOWEVER: I would not recommend this game to anyone looking for a long gaming experience or a strong story that pays off and makes you think. The art throughout the game is absolutely amazing and very much one of the main standouts from my playthrough. The reflections in the water, the backgrounds for each of the main locations that you are in throughout the game, and the character drawings that pop in and out during the story are incredible. The platforming is quite solid and was fun throughout the game. It didn't take away from the puzzles and controlled well. The puzzles themselves were the main draw to the game for me. I did feel that there could have been more of these and that the mechanics could have been further explored and build off of. Other than one puzzle that really stumped me (and got me and achievement for taking over 15 min since I just couldn't wrap my head around it) all of the puzzles felt straightforward and I had no issues with the game introducing new mechanics without giving the player any instructions for using them. Overall the puzzles were fun and for the price I didn't really feel like there was too much of an issue with the price of the game and the amount of content (a few more puzzles would have been nice though and really could have rounded out the game a bit more and added some extra difficulty).And then there's the story. This was really one of the roughest points and I wouldn't recommend this game based on it. I was initially pulled in to the mystery and really enjoyed it up until the ending. It felt like there were a couple ways that the game could go to make a compelling story and those were ignored in an attempt to do something different. While that isn't necessarily a bad thing I feel that this game just didn't stick the landing and the story really suffered for it. So taken all together it's a very nice looking game with a few dozen fun platforming puzzles with a bit of a rough story throughout it. It's not a long game (3.3 hours to 100% for me, although I did look up a couple of the more obscure achievements) but it isn't expensive either. I enjoyed the game but I'm very glad I was interested in it for the puzzles and the art and not majorly invested in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from the fact that the music is super relaxing and comforting to listen to and that the graphics are incredibly beautiful and captivating, the puzzles have been a lot of fun! This was my first time playing a puzzle adventure game and I never thought it'd be the type of game I'd enjoy, but I genuinely couldn't stop once I started - it was addicting getting to solve the puzzles and coming closer and closer to the revelation of the game and all the secrets the island held. A tragic, and beautiful and captivating and thrilling game! Definitely worth every single penny and I can only whole-heartedly recommend this! _childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains is solid as far as functionality is concerned and it was fairly entertaining. I wouldn't say that the 3 hours or so that I spent on the main game (and the extra half hour or so spent on completion) was a waste of time, but I am left with the feeling that I could've spent that time better doing something else.I found the puzzles somewhat lacking. I don't think I spent more than 5 minutes on any single puzzle (yet there is an achievement that expects you to take 15 minutes to solve a single puzzle). I was worried about this, having played the demo a few months before the official release, but I convinced myself that the puzzles would get more challenging the further you get in the game, so I wishlisted the game and eventually purchased it. New gimmicks were gradually introduced, and it looked like the challenge was starting to build up, but then the game just ended before it could go anywhere with its puzzles. Although the solutions weren't always obvious, it was often easy to see the solution after messing around with the platforms a little bit.I spent more time reading dialogue than actually playing the game. The story was somewhat interesting, but it also made the game feel slow. It felt less like a game with a story in it, and more like a story with a game in it. That really must have been what they were going for, because when going after the last few achievements (after having finished the game once), I discovered that I could skip the puzzles and that there was an achievement for doing so. Apparently you can do this even on a puzzle you've never completed before. At the time of this review, 50.2% of players have the achievement for beating the game. Only 27.5% have the achievement for skipping a puzzle at least once, and I would assume that a sizable portion of that group only skipped puzzles for the sake of the achievement, leaving little room to deny that only a very small fraction of people (who weren't interested in playing the game at all) ended up skipping every single puzzle. This tells me that people actually wanted to play a game and not just read a story.Even though it leaves a lot of questions unanswered (specifically when it comes to the ruins and the ancient technology found on the island) Evan's Remains has an interesting story. If that's what you came for, you might be satisfied with this title. If, however, you came looking for a tough puzzler to challenge your mind, then Evan's Remains might not have enough to scratch that itch. It could benefit from having about 50% more puzzles along with enough increase in difficulty to ensure you don't stumble upon solutions by trial and error.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some fun puzzles, although they shouldn't be too hard for people who are into this type of game. The story starts out intriguing, but ends up very, very convoluted, taking some of the fun away. If you can get this on sale, give it a go, but I feel there's more that could have been done with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr This is a decent visual novel that has a bad game tied to it which hindered the development of the visual novel.This story of this game honestly isn't that bad. I am giving this game a bad review because I believe the game play is holding it back an enormous amount. I may be harsh on the game because I was primarily expecting a puzzle platformer with visual novel elements. But I ended up getting the opposite with neither side of the game feeling polished.To be frank, the way the game itself is designed is not good at all. Even the reason for the game isn't great. "Why are you jumping on those monoliths? Just walk around  them." "But I feel like it's important to solve them." The only good thing about the game is the semi-original concept that is introduced in the first puzzle, platforms that disappear when you leave them and platforms to swap the state of the aforementioned platforms.For the bad things, there is a ton. Even jumping is bad. The jump in this game is set to one, predetermined height. The devs may have a reason for this, however this is extremely frustrating in the game. When one of the main things you do is jump on the same platform to "undo" the action that jumping on the platform took (e.g. re-swapping the blocks, teleporting back, etc.) it is annoying to have a jump that puts you in the air for a few seconds. You just have to sit there and wait, over and over and over again since you will be doing the move so often. Hell, this is even something you have to do in the first puzzle. The second block is set to "on" so when you jump on the first block it switches the second block to "off" making you jump on the first block again. The level design isn't good either. This may as well have been called a platformer because the small sections aren't even puzzles. There is a reason there is an achievement for spending over 15 minutes in a level and for skipping a level, and that's because almost no one is going to do either of those things without an achievement to get for doing so. Not one level took me more than a few minutes to complete. If I did ever have a minor problem solving a puzzle it was always because I was overcomplicating the solution, not because I had to think of the puzzle from a different direction.A third issue is the lack of backtracking. This game has a plot that can be convoluted if you aren't paying attention. There are also a few obscure achievements hidden in the game which you will almost certainly miss on your first play through. If you end up wanting to backtrack through the game for whatever reason, there is only one option; play the whole thing again. This is made more reasonable by the fact that you can skip puzzles, but it makes me question why there is a lack of such a basic feature as a level menu. There is also another issue with backtracking which I will bring up later.The other major design option holding back the game is how the dialog system is made. It is extremely bare-bones. It only has three things, a key to advance the text, a menu option to speed up the text, and a menu option to change languages. This is a big issue because most of the time is spent in this menu.I read mildly fast and don't like to wait for text-scroll so I generally immediately advance the text box when I can. This means that I am generally pressing space two times for one or two sentences of dialog. Having to repeatedly spam the space bar for relatively long periods of time in order to advance is extremely annoying. An auto-option or an option to have text boxes auto-fill instead of scroll would be great, but there are no such options.Another issue is one that I already mentioned, which is backtracking. The game does allow you to "fast-forward" text, but this only solves part of the problem of backtracking. If you are in a scene with text you will likely see character animations in the same scene. This is annoying due to the fact that nothing happens to the animations when you are skipping the text.  When you choose to skip the text, all that happens is that you sit in front of flashing text boxes and then watch a character animation for a few seconds. I again don't  understand why they would implement this feature instead of a "skip cutscene" button, which would likely be almost as easy and a lot less annoying to deal with.The third thing is the lack of saves. Most visual novels have saves. This one does not.For the last thing, I just want to add a minor gripe that didn't fit in the other two categories, that gripe being the achievements. I basically already passively mentioned the ones I have issues with but I just wanted to go into a bit more detail here. They are overly annoying to get for what they are.  My first play through only took just over 2 hrs, but my total time is almost three because of the achievements.For the two story based achievements, they aren't reasonable. For one you literally just have to play a certain part of the game in a certain language. Who would ever think of that except for people who speak the native language? The other achievement doesn't make sense either. Backtrack after a cutscene, quit and reload the game, solve the puzzle again, and then get a fake error message with dumb backwards text. I just don't understand why they would add such a thing. For the two puzzle based achievements, I again don't understand their purpose. Was the skip one added to to make sure that the player knew of that function? And was the spend 15 minutes one added for the sole reason of adding play time to make the game look harder than it is?For the good part of the game, I won't go into much detail because I am much better at giving detailed criticism than praising something. But I did like the story. I really liked to increasing number of twists that got revealed as the story progressed. If this game was released as a normal visual novel with the settings and saves that almost all visual novels have then it would be great.The other thing I liked was the pixel art and animation. I believe that both of these aspects are beautifully done. Again, I don't really know how to praise it other than saying that it looks great and I really like it.For my conclusion, I don't recommend buying this game if you are looking for a puzzle platformer. This game falls completely flat in that aspect. However, if you are looking for a good visual novel that you can knock out in an hour-hour and a half (as long as you skip the puzzles) then go right ahead. My review will stay as a negative because of the issues in both sides of the game and because this (at least in my eyes) is primarily marketed as a platformer with story nailed on, which it is certainly not.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan’s Remains ReviewPlatforms: Steam, PS4, Switch, XBOPrice: $6.99Players: 1Genre: Puzzle PlatformerDeveloper: Maitan69Publisher: Whitethorn DigitalIntroHello everyone, in this review we’re going to be covering an incredibly good puzzle platformer that wound up just blowing me out of the water with its insane plot-twist ending. We’ll get into that shortly though.I’ve actually had my eye on this game for some time now, though in truth I didn’t actually know much about it other than the fact that it was a puzzle platformer and I really liked the art style. Which is why this game’s story took me by complete surprise. I was not expecting such a dark turn of events from a puzzle platformer, especially not one with such a colorful and rather cute art style.That said, this game was quite superb and without any further ado, let’s get this review started!Story and SettingEvan’s Remains’ story puts you in the shoes of a young woman named Dysis who had been sent to a seemingly uninhabited island after receiving a letter from a boy genius named Evan, who had been missing for many years. Upon arrival Dysis discovers that she isn’t alone on the island, and she meets a man named Clover who has been researching the monoliths that are scattered around the island.This game’s story starts off quite innocently with Dysis and Clover working together to solve the mystery behind an artifact that’s said to grant immortality to those who find it. It subtly becomes much darker as more of the story is revealed until the game goes into straight “WTF” land with a plot-twist so evil that my jaw dropped to the floor.As I was watching all this play out, my brain was like “WHAT?!?” and “That is some straight up evil S**t”. I felt so many mixed emotions leading up to the ending of this game that I wasn’t sure how to feel. First I felt sad, then angry, then sad again, then happy, then angry etc. It messes with you hardcore and it was not expected in the least because the game is incredibly subtle about revealing anything behind the mystery that’s going on then the plot-twist is revealed and it’s like getting punched in the face.A++ for storytelling ability from the developer on this one, that ending will stick with me for a while.GameplayMuch of the gameplay in Evan’s Remains is solving platforming based puzzles that revolve around activating platforms. This is another area that was really well done in this game.I tend to think my puzzle solving ability is quite good but there were some puzzles in this game that wound up stumping me hardcore. The solutions to them were so obscure that there seemingly wasn’t a solution to them. There obviously was one but the solutions wound up being beyond my ability to figure out. The vast majority of the puzzles that I encountered varied in difficulty, but they were solvable, these few that I couldn’t solve were on a whole other level.One really nice thing about this game that I wish more puzzle platformers incorporated was the ability to skip a puzzle you’re stuck on. If this wasn’t an option I likely would have given up on one of the more difficult puzzles, so I was very glad that it was included.Graphics and AudioFirstly I want to say that the pixel art in this game is absolutely gorgeous. The foreground reflections on the water, the beautiful backgrounds that highlighted the time of day and all the ancient machinery and buildings in the middle ground all coalesced into an absolutely amazing scene that really draws you into the experience.Audio wise, the game didn’t have any voice acting but it did have some very good ambience and music. I’ve always been a firm believer that good audio enhances your overall experience and this game is no different because the music and ambience really set the scenes and added to the overall experience a great deal. If they weren’t there, I doubt the story would have had such a big impact on my emotions over the course of the game.ProsGorgeous ArtworkAmazing Story With One Heck of a Plot Twist EndingExcellent Music and AmbienceInteresting and Well-Written CharactersExcellent Puzzle DesignConsI honestly can’t think of anything bad about this game, everything was superb.Final ThoughtsNot gonna lie, Evan’s Remains is easily the finest puzzle platformer I’ve played this year, and I 100% mean that. Everything about this game is superb. From its story all the way down to its puzzle elements, every piece of this game is just amazing and for only $6.99 it’s an absolute steal what you get for such a small price. If you’re a fan of the genre you really don’t want to miss out on this one.I give this one our first 5/5 stars. It’s absolutely amazing and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains starts out pretty slow, which can be discouraging to players starting the game, but if you stick with the game you will truly see what you would've missed out on. At first when I was playing the game, I enjoyed just the puzzles and found the excessive amount of text boxes annoying, but after a while the story began to grow on my and I was actually interested in getting the next piece of dialogue. Although, at first the game play kept me going, as the puzzle platforming style was drawing me in, and I enjoyed solving the puzzles, which were fairly easy/simple, except getting caught up on one or two of the puzzles. This is a very character driven story, so you will start to appreciate the story when the characters open up and you begin to become more and more attached to them. The story does have a lot of twists and turns, but they always made the story more unique and interested which I enjoyed. As I mentioned above this game took me a while to appreciate it/ get used to it, as the story and massive amount of text boxes annoyed me, and I was not found of the visual novel style of delivering the story at first, but then I grew to like it. I didn't like the sprites of the characters in the visual novel portions of the game, but then I started to grow fond of them, and believed they were the best ways to fully represent the characters. Besides the visual novel sprites, I always enjoyed the art style outside of the visual novel portions from start to finish.Overall, I would give Evan's Remains a 3/5 due to the time it took me to get used to the style of the game, and the lack of variation that there was from puzzle to puzzle, but overall I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys puzzle platformers and an interesting story, and if you don't want to do the puzzles and just want to experience a visual novel like story then you are able to skip puzzles in the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not much of a puzzle person so I was tentative about going into this game at first. Thankfully, I find the puzzles manageable and often even enjoyable. Even if you're not into puzzle platformers, it's worth a shot to solve the puzzles by yourself and be rewarded with snippets of plot progression.That said, I have mixed feelings about the final plot twist. By adding this extra twist it pushes the storyline a bit further, but I feel like it complicates what was supposedly established and undermines the impact of the touching plot twist that came before it. Endings don't always have to be perfectly happy, but the story feels like it might leave a better aftertaste if it didn't have yet a twist on top of the cake.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully spectacular game.The puzzles are engaging, the pixel art is maticulously crafted making beautiful scenery, and the sound track provides great ambiance.Story wise, this is one game that had twists that you can't see coming. It's broken up between what's happening and memories giving you bread crumbs, but never enough to grasp the true picture until the very end where you find yourself finding that you are thinking the same calls the game puts on the main character when things are explained.It may be a short title lasting 6 or less hours depending on your pace, but it's definitely worth checking out. Contrary to people saying that nothing or not everything gets explained, everything in the story does get explained. Without spoilers, you'll see the story from 2 sides; one from the main character throughout the whole game, and the other at the very end. There's a lot going well for this game, and a lot of heart built-in.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet puzzle game with an ok story. The story relies a bit heavily on developing a mystery that isn't resolved until the end through lengthy exposition and slightly convoluted twists but characters are likeable and the dialogue is mostly fun to read. There are some interesting themes posed here and there but aren't developed as much as I would've liked.The puzzles never get too hard or deep, but the mix of satisfying controls and their simplicity make them fun to solve. It would've been cool to see them develop more with additional mechanics and larger sizes as the game progressed. If anything, the nice pixel art gives you a sense of progression as you visit different areas.All in all, if it's your kind of game, it's worth a play due to its low price and duration that doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nothing to write home about, but the controls work well. The puzzles are incredibly easy, so even if you're not into puzzle games, you'll do fine. You can even skip puzzles if you get stuck.I am recommending this game because the STORY is absolutely amazing. I was happy, sad, crushed, happy, and then amazed. This is one of the few games that ends and you're really not sure which side to be on. Both are plausible. There is no right or wrong answer. Simply amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I'm feeling very mixed about this game. The platforming puzzles were easy, but fun. For the most part, this game was short and sweet. Although there is one problem in the game which I'll get to. Let's start off with what I like about this game.I love the music that plays on the title screen (which was used in the trailer). Just that soundtrack alone helps me calm down after going through a day of hardships and whatnot. I'd open this game up any day just to listen to it.As stated earlier, the puzzles were fun. I enjoyed the gameplay. This game is designed for the casual audience and it helps take our minds off of everything else when playing it.For the story, it was great... except for the fact that the dialogue just goes on...and on...and on...and on...and on...and on...and on...AND ON!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!Once you walk into a cutscene, it's going to fill the next dozen minutes of your life to the BRIM with dialogue that never ends! You can skip them once you already know the story when replaying the game, but for first time blind players, they have to go through all of them in order to know everything about the game's plot. And whatever you do, DO NOT select Continue after clearing the game. Otherwise, you will be forced to sit through the credits that you cannot skip!Overall, I'm pretty neutral with this one. It's not a bad game, but half the "play time" is literally just reading the dialogue. In my book, this game barely gets a passing score with a grade of 65/100. This is a game to pick up whenever you need to help yourself calm down and get out of a bad mood. Once you do, it's time to continue living through your daily routine.By the way, I disagree with some people who call this a "visual novel in disguise" because a visual novel gives you choices to make and whatever you choose affects later events. This game does not do that.

There are some flashback scenes scattered throughout that can be hard to keep track of, but if you stick through it and pay attention, they will fall neatly into place by the end.The dialogue between characters is a definite strong-point of the game. Little details like every character having different "blips" as they speak really make the game stand out. The sound design fits well with the game's overall aesthetic and feel. Completing monolith puzzles throughout the island with soft colors and music behind them is very soothing and lots of fun.If you're struggling with the puzzles but still interested in the story, there's an option to skip them, which the game includes as a tongue-in-cheek reference to the longstanding critique of 2D platformers: "Why don't you just go around?" Personally, I appreciate their design and challenge, so I decided complete them all, but it's nice to have that option all the same.Overall, I'd say this game is well worth the $7. _childDocuments_.review: So, I liked this game. It’s a little short and it does have shortcomings I noticed, but in general, it was a decent experience and it made me feel emotions. The story is quite good (decent) with enough twists to make me feel invested in it and the interactions between characters, especially our main character, is just nice to read. There are some quotable lines of dialogue in there and some did make me think some things, although not fully philosophical., with emphasis on . I’d still say it’s pretty casual and accessible everyone though, not too hard, either on the thinking department or the action-platforming department.. I think I personally took exactly 180 minutes, if not 170, since I checked the steam overlay near the ending, but steam likes to round up numbers to hours instead of telling specifics. I didn’t use a guide and solved all puzzles on my own, and there are some miss-able achievements I could still get.. I once quit the game in the middle of a dialogue to try to get back to the beginning of the scene, but upon continuing, the game remembers the exact dialogue box I was on. Which is good, but can be considered bad, considering I wanted to catch a typo/re-read the dialogue from the beginning without having to replay the entire game. This could be solved with manual saves or better yet, let us have a scene/part select after we finish the game. But it’s not so bad, because…. You could skip any puzzle you want and any dialogue you want. Which makes getting miss-able achievements, (or confirming typos) so much easier. One Achievement in particular kind of requires you to do this. I don’t think doing this even prevents you from getting any achievement. There’s no achievement for “beating all puzzles without skipping”.. I liked most of it, it felt cohesive. Although I only fully understood 90% of it and still had questions in the end, the story is quite nice and it kind of.. taught me something? An interesting viewpoint about what matters, I guess. It didn’t make me feel tears coming, but it’s still pretty nice. Twisty? I’d say there are twists for sure.. They complement each other and the artstyle is nice. Beautiful backgrounds even if it’s “pixel”, not to mention the characters. The music is not particularly memorable but it just fits, nothing felt out of place with whatever is happening.. I feel like the sounds are satisfying. From disappearing platforms and platforms ing around to teleporting sounds, they’re pretty cool. When I first tried out the demo a few months ago, I kept jumping around in the sand for a minute because of the sound effect. Based on credits, the sounds might be just freesounds from some random site, but it’s still nice.. Quite clever but not frustrating. There’s an achievement for solving a puzzle in 15 minutes or more and I never involuntarily got it. Meaning, without a guide, no puzzle made me stuck for 15 minutes. I think there’s around 28/30 puzzles in total? But I still had to do some thinking (some trial-and-error-too when I don’t want to think, which sometimes work). Some puzzles do make me feel clever.. I know, since it’s more about the puzzles and not a platformer, this is not game breaking, but there’s no jump buffer like in celeste as explained  (from 10:26 to 11:12, if it didn’t redirect already). Basically, if you are mid-air and press the jump button “a little too early” before actually landing (like, only missing by half a second or a single frame), the game doesn’t let you jump. This just doesn’t feel good, because it makes you feel like the game malfunctioned and didn’t get your input, or you feel like your spacebar is broken. If you try to mitigate it by  your spacebar (hoping that, since you’re HOLDING it, you can jump ASAP when you land), it also doesn’t work. The game just won’t listen to any jump inputs if it’s made mid-air. It just makes the movement not feel good, not as good as you’d expect. Which is different with what Celeste did. I feel like this is an important thing to put in every single platformer. But, what do I know? I’m not the dev here.. Nothing gamebreaking but I found 2.1. When , I stepped on the reset state block on one of the puzzles but the puzzle' state didn’t return to a good default, it just made everything blank and softlocked the game. I managed to fix it by simply quitting and continuing. I forgot the puzzle’s name because, again, there’s no manual saves, so I didn’t try to “go back a bit earlier” once I finished that particular puzzle.2. During the final sequence when .. Again, not many, just 3, not sure about one of them1. When 2. When 3. I think when  he also was missing an “L” in the middle of “talking” or some other word. Not remembering it clearly, or maybe my eyes were playing tricks on me. is not entirely accurate. The one that says "Find Aurelio". I felt like I FOUND the secret man (before even looking at the achievement list) , and when I opened up the achievement list, I wondered why I didn't unlock it.  It turns out that (minor spoiler not story related) . That, my friend, is called "meet" if it requires interaction. If I only need to "find" him, then "seeing" him on my screen should suffice. But apparently it was not enough. oh well. Either fix the wording or make the unlock condition easier. But again, I'm not the dev.. Sure, thank all the patrons/people who contributed but being able to speed it up would be nice. . I finished the game and clicked "continue" out of curiosity, and I was taken directly to the credits, where I can't skip, fast forward, or quit to main menu. That was the most annoying 5-10 minutes I experienced in this game EVER.All these issues are mere inconveniences and I'm willing to give them a pass, but a fix would be nice. I still could enjoy the game for what it is. It's still a decent game, and I think it's worth getting. Nothing particularly spectacular but it did make me think about the search for meaning. Clover in particular says some interesting insights. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Below is an almost entirely spoiler free guide for Evan's Remains. I've included a few names, as well as discussion on some of the blocks relating to puzzles. Talking around the story for Evan's Remains is tricky. As a narrative focused game, I'd rather not spoil the ending, or some of the more important story beats. The first forty-five minutes or so act as set-up. You play as Dysis, a girl on an isolated island looking for a man named Evan. It seems Evan called for Dysis in particular, and it's a company called Up-Bring that assists in guiding her to him. A companion also accompanies you through a holographic screen. His name is Nikola, and he works to provide additional context and information. Of course, this is all only at first. It quickly becomes clear that there is more to the entire situation than anyone is letting Dysis know. In fact, perhaps none of what she was told was ever true at all. That's our job to figure out, and to run through a series of puzzles to decipher. What's truly going on? Is anyone being honest? Does Dysis remember anything prior to being on this island? Does anyone really know Evan? It really only takes about an hour before all of the answers start to set themselves up. Again, I can't spoil them here, but the pacing is handled decently enough. There are a few aspects of character development that get delivered a bit clunkily through dialogue, but it didn't trouble me too much. Additionally, a few of the later plot points can be a bit difficult to follow, but most of the characters do their best to describe things as concisely as possible. The pixellated art style of Evan's Remains is beautiful. The animation is rather small in places- specifically sprites- but is still fluid and wonderful. Dialogue is accompanied by talking heads, and each character receives a variety of different states and emotions that change depending on the message they're delivering. The game is gorgeous, with multiple scenes and landscapes as you progress through the plot and puzzles. The primary method of interacting with the world in Evan's Remains is via puzzles. There is no combat in the game. Instead, your character moves left and right in a side-scrolling format, and can jump onto different platforms available above her. In-game, the platforms are a part of cryptic ancient puzzles, and you must solve them in order to progress. No block is too tremendously complex. When you jump on a regular brown block, it will disappear when you jump off of it again. There are blocks that swap active and deactive blocks, ones that teleport you, some are green and stationary no matter how much you jump, blocks get introduced that help you jump higher, and some can convert between many different types. Still, if puzzles aren't really your cup of tea and you came only for the emotional narrative, there's also an option to skip puzzles entirely. You can do this immediately upon stepping into the puzzle area, or if you get stumped mid-way through. It's as easy as pressing escape-- or pause-- and selecting to 'skip puzzle' in the menu. You'll find yourself on the other side of the tall, dividing pillar, and you can move on as normal. There's no detriment to the narrative, or to your experience overall, and the game doesn't shame you. The puzzles seem to sort of vary in difficulty. At first, they ramp up in a way that makes sense, and then they same to go back and forth. Personally, I didn't find any of them too unmanageable. More than anything else, the puzzles are trial and error, and I never hit one that really stumped me. If anything, I only wish there were a few more puzzles or blocks available.Of course, you can also fast-forward through the dialogue if you only pick the game up for the puzzles. There's only an achievement for skipping a puzzle though, for all you completionists out there. This does require its own category. The music in the game is fantastic. Often, I'm a person that has background noise or extra sounds going on in my headphones or around me. I'll play a playlist while I game, have a conversation, hop in a Discord call-- but for this game, I found myself wanting to listen to the sounds. The intro music on the homescreen alone had me hooked. It starts as a wonderful series of acoustic guitar chords, and morphs into less organic sounds, adding synth and twinkling melodies. It sets a curious atmosphere, one that I paused to take in before ever beginning. Should you buy Evan's Remains? I would say, in the event that you're looking for something narrative and, admittedly, more than a little bittersweet, then yes. The game isn't expensive at only $6.99 full price, and it gives about 3-4 hours of content. Still, I think the story will stick with me for a little bit. For all of the occasionally clunky dialogue and divisive reveal, I found myself considering what the ending meant for the characters, and what it would mean for me. I didn't mind it, and was glad that there was any sort of closure to be had at all. Sometimes, closure is all we can hope for.

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid indie game and one my favourites I have played in 2020. The game starts off as a girl on a beach of a mysterious ancient island where no one lives, her one goal, to find a missing boy genius named Evan. You get no more details than that, which adds to the mystery and quality of the story.The game is filled with puzzles, make no mistake about it this a story game with puzzles, not a puzzle game with a story. Normally I would love to complete puzzles and take my time but I was desperate to complete each one to continue the story and work out the mystery. Where is Evan? Why am I looking for him on this island? These simple questions turn into complex ones as the story continues; more questions and mysteries are added without real answers keeping you intrigued and wanting to play more.The artwork is beautiful and adds to the relaxing and enjoyment nature of this game. I am also a sucker for a good soundtrack and Evans Remains soundtrack is now one of my favourites because of the calming nature but also how each musical elements fits with the story and level. Most games repeat the soundtrack over and over again but the depth of the Evans remains Soundtrack is fantastic.Without spoiling the story all I am going to say is the ending may leave you with a tear in your eye. It left me smiling at how clever the ending and story really is . The story also attempts to teach us, the player, life lessons and gets us to really think and evaluate ourselves without actually asking you to. Why do we do the things we do? What motivates us? Is it money? Love? Family? The ending will divide people with the question of whats right and what is wrong, it should also open up a dialogue with yourself and other players of how far would you for the people you care about?  Just to quickly add that I love the fact that those who backed this with a considerable sum of money on kickstarter got to have their names in the game and some got to add some lovely quotes with the seagull one really making me smile. If Matias Schmied ever decided to make another game, it would 100% have my backing. 10/10 Go buy this game, its good value for money.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Video Review: Full Playthrough: After completing the entirety of this game, there are a few things I’d like to say.  Out of all the video games I’ve played in recent memory, Evan’s Remains is by far one of the best I’ve played in a long time.  With its cute pixel art and beautiful music, Evan’s Remains is a wonderful addition to the Indie game genre.You start off as a girl named Dysis looking for a genius boy named Evan.  On your quest to find him, you explore an ancient island in the Pacific Ocean.   To get through each stage, you must pass through various puzzles to do so.  The puzzles are rather interesting though.  But some can be very, very annoying…  Ahhh!!!!While difficult at times, in the end, it feels very rewarding when progressing through the story.  There is no set difficulty of the puzzles as some feel much harder than others.  When you touch the plain platforms, they will generally disappear.  Touching the colored platforms will do the opposite.  Some platforms allow you transport from one location to another while other platforms will let you high jump.  Overall, the puzzles were really well thought out and some really are good brain teasers.Dysis eventually meets a guy named Clover and they explore the island over the course of the game.  I won’t spoil the story, but I have to say that it has a very heartfelt narrative I’m sure will resonate with its player base.And unlike other indie developers, the story is presented in a visual novel style.  Combining the elements of mystery, puzzles, and visual novel components, you get the very beautiful “Evan’s Remains.”Evan’s Remains is a wonderful game with very beautiful story telling and graphics.  As one of the best games I’ve played in a long time, I highly recommend it to any who likes puzzles or visual novels.  My one nitpick of the game is that I wish it were a longer game.  Therefore, I am giving the game a 9/10 for its breathtaking art style, game mechanics, and overall story.

For example the sound of waves when near the ocean, and the sound of scribbling when getting near Clover.In conclusion I'd highly recommend this game because it has a bit of something for everyone and would be highly enjoyable to anyone who would like a game to play even if they don't usually play games. _childDocuments_.review: Evan's remains is a puzzle platformer in the truest sense of the word. With a beautiful pizel art style, and contained puzzles that slowly introduce new mechanics and an intriguing plot that's drip-fed to you throughout, I'd recommend to anyone who enjoys the genre.Evan's Remains is a platformer that isn't focused on skilled jumps, but rather the patience to learn the game's language as it introduces it to you in digestible pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan's Remains wasn't exactly what I was expecting, but I think it was even better for it. Instead of a traditional platformer it plays like a visual novel puzzle rpg in that the only "platforming" you will do are the puzzles and it's very much a story driven through dialogue. The puzzles vary in difficulty without becoming too impossible, but even if you do feel stuck they offer a skip puzzle feature so you can continue on and enjoy the story without feeling too overwhelmed or annoyed. Now the story - all I can say without spoiling is that even when I though I knew I had it all figured out, multiple times I might add, I ended up being wrong. It's a beautiful game and you should definitely give it a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Check out my full gameplay review video for Evan’s Remains. I go into great depth about the Story, Graphics, Audio, Gameplay, and other noteworthy things I feel needs to be mentioned: Disclaimer: I received this game for free. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!(This is a transcript taken straight from my video review of Evan’s Remains)This game is a puzzle platformer with very heavy sections of story dialogue. So is it worth playing, is it worth buying? Let’s get into it.This will be a spoiler free review. There are a lot of mysterious elements to the story that are worth experiencing yourself if you decide to play this yourself so I’ll give you the quick gist of the plot.You play as a girl named Dysis. You are tasked by your employers with exploring an uninhabited island in search of a boy genius who goes by the name Evan. He’s been missing for years but after a letter specifically asking for Dysis to search for him she sets off and the long and winding mystery begins.Just a quick heads up. Although this game has a lot of puzzle platforming levels there are even more dialogue sections you’ll be sitting through. I’m not exaggerating that this really felt like a visual novel at times with the length of conversations characters were having.If you really want to, however, they have an option to speed through all of the text but I don’t recommend you play this game if you were going to that in the first place. The mix of tranquil puzzle solving alongside this engrossing story really works well as a whole package.So let’s talk about the gameplay portion. You will be primarily finishing levels by getting over these giant monoliths.It starts off pretty simple with you jumping on triggers that makes platforms disappear and reappear. Each monolith gets progressively harder and introduces new mechanics. For example, there’s a mechanic later on that teleports you between two platforms and another that moves platforms along tracks. It definitely becomes a head scratcher but as a word of advice, take each step slow. At any point during the jumping puzzle figure out which options are available to you. If you fail, reset, get back to that point, and it’s trial and error from there.If you’d rather focus on just the story and are getting frustrated with any of the puzzles you can press start and simply skip it. It’s definitely more gratifying persevering through the challenge but it’s not worth sacrificing the flow of the game in my opinion.So after a puzzle or two you’ll progress the story via long dialogue sections and pretty much repeat that for the most part. It’s simple but alongside the presentation it works.The graphics are very well done and the animation is smooth, The environments do a great job at conveying how chill and simple the situation you’re in is while at the same time not feeling like you have to rush.It’s a little hard to explain but it all just flows together and makes you want to keep getting to the next section in order to uncover the mystery of all these characters. It goes without saying, the story is very intriguing. Evan’s Remains is a fun little title that you can complete at your own pace and skip sections whenever you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Evan's Remains

_childDocuments_.review: Evan’s Remains is a mystery-thriller puzzle adventure about finding a missing boy: Evan. The game combines logic-based platform puzzles with narrative inspired by Japanese graphic adventure games. Every time the player solves from two to three puzzles, the story goes forward and new mechanics are introduced. The challenge of the puzzles lies in the player’s ability to figure out what do rather than solve challenges based on skill. As the difficulty curve increases, the puzzles become more complex by combining two or more previously introduced mechanics.

name: Mortal Shell
detailed_description: Mortal Shell is a deep action-RPG that tests your sanity and resilience in a shattered world. As the remains of humanity wither and rot, zealous foes fester in the ruins. They spare no mercy, with survival demanding superior awareness, precision and instincts. Track down hidden sanctums of devout followers and discover your true purpose. The dead litter this tattered landscape, but not all are without hope. The lost remains of defeated warriors are yours to discover. Awaken these Mortal Shells, occupy their bodies and significantly open your understanding to diverse masteries of combat. Your path is guarded by desperate adversaries, devoted to inscrutable gods. Behold creatures both pitiable and grotesque, but do not let fear halt your journey. Muster your courage and face them down. Combat is strategic and deliberate. You must commit your sword only when an opportunity opens. Calculate your parries to unleash devastating counterblows. Temporarily entomb your Mortal Shell in stone to block attacks, or play aggressive and use your stone-form to add brutal weight to your own sword swings.
