_childDocuments_.review: I got the end of my first playthrough with 54% achievement at 14hours with small farming (2-3hours), good game mechanism but some achievement just feels stupid and make this game tiring and unenjoyable, decent fight variation (only 5 weapons and some combo set) and upgrade & customization, overall this is a short souls-like game but really entertaining. 1Hour into the DLC and i think the DLC is pretty good that make you stay and want to play the game even more to see your limit and what's beyond "the walls" and i would say it really worth the bundle. 10/10 to buy in sale, and 10/10 would play mortal shell 2 if it available in future.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: This game blew my mind! From game play, sound, character, world design and music all top notch imo. I was NOT disappointed. I have NEVER used the word "metal" to describe anything... Until now. Gives you a direction at the very start of the game and just says, go. This game whooped my tail at the beginning and pretty much forced me to understand their hardening mechanic! But that is ok. This is their world, I'm just playing in it. And I'm very pleased to be. For a smaller package its got content. I can easily see someone putting in multiple runs. To be honest, it does kind of come off confusing at first but you'll get the hang of it. There IS healing items by the way. Actually there are a few ways to heal (saw a review saying there wasn't). Search if you need to, but I went in blind and I enjoyed it all the more. Also, seems ppl have a gripe with the central hub area. Can you get lost? Yup! However if you're like me and adventure while learning the game or have pleasure in finding the secrets, you'll get used to it pretty quick. Although it is a swamp, they put giant landmarks to give you a sense of direction. Like a giant tree with bats hanging from it, or a creature the game calls a Grisha (if spelled right) hanging on fire from a pike. Only one location is kind of tucked away, but coming over the path leading up to it trust me, you cannot miss it. Nothing is that far away from the starting tower. If you like SoulsBourne, here you go! Hope to see more from this series.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry to say, but this is simply not a particularly good or enjoyable game. I will give it points for its original mechanic, graphics, interesting visual design for the characters, animations and audio design, but that's kind of where it stops.I tried really hard to like it. I did. But it's exhausting because every fight in this game is an ambush. Here is the layout of the first temple as an example:First room has two two visible enemies, two more hidden behind pillars, one at the end of the room that patrols, usually coming in when you're fighting the group. The next corridor there are two guys hidden left and right, just behind the corners as you enter. The next room as one enemy in it and two others become visible as you get into aggro range, after that you have another two enemies hiding left and right, behind the corners as the corridor widens, then the next room has 1 visible enemy and 4 hidden behind pillars.Every fight is a slow, monotonous  dance of go close, bait out the attack, attack the enemy, harden, dodge back, wait for the harden cooldown and restart. You typically don't have a lot of stamina to dodge very often, the harden cooldown is long, the attack animations are slow and everything is a drag. Yes, there's that one shell that is fast and some weapons you get later, but for the most part it's too slow of a game.You have no potions that refill, you can only buy healing items for your common exp/gold currency or farm them from the world or get them as drops. It's not a particularly big issue, but it adds to the sluggish pace of the game. Imagine going through the gauntlet I just described only to lose most of your health halfway.I almost never skip enemies in games, but this one made me do it.Later in the game I saw one of the most mind-boggling game decisions ever Congratulations, you made me skip the rest of the game with that stupid decision.

Go back and play FROM games in the 90s, maybe you'll find satisfaction there.This is a fun game (purchased at 70% off) and I'm happy with the difficulty. It's annoying but I'm going to figure it out. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty bad take on Soulslike. Graphics is decent save for animation which is just not able to be smooth nor convey proper sense of weight - it has that cheap feel of a budget game.And overall game design is lacking - levels are modelled well enough, but overall placement of things is just annoying, and infuriatingly glitchy at times physics is not helping. Neither anything catchy about enemies design, nor (lack of) difficulty balance, esp. in relation to weird rule system which is used (I appreciate attempt to invent something original, but it didn't quite seem to mesh with me).If it would be a standard game, I would say its worth a price, but you don't want to take "hard" kind of Souls-like game punishment for whatever cheap it can come - its just a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface by saying that I'm clinically bad with souls-likes. BUT I love the nightmarish dream-like worlds that seem to be portrayed in them so here we are.I have played DS 1/3 and completed Elden Ring so I am exactly 0.001% qualified to speak on anything.I enjoyed this game....especially once I started to understand and groove w/ the combat.The slower pace and clunky swinging really lends to the satisfaction from connecting while avoidingor mitigating damage.I beat the game in a little over 14 hours including idling while snacking, drinking, forgetting what I was doing, etc. I almost don't want to do pros and cons because I feel like its gonna just look too negative when I didreally enjoy this game especially at its run time and with what I feel was a reasonable challenge for non-soulsvets but here goes.I like the idea of different 'shells' and their looks, but honestly besides health/ stamina and resolve I didn't feel there was enough variety between them. I would have loved to see different fighting styles with the weapons depending what meat suit you were wearing. There are only four weapons, and honestly there are only 3 because 2 of the weapons on big bonks. Would love to have seen more visual differences when you upgrade the weapons. Limited monster variety, but the game world isn't like massive or anything and even if they were reused, they had different skins and themed attacks.I got lost.... a few times... too much of certain areas kinda looks samey or I don't know where to go. There's no map and early on I kept finding myself scream running around an area trying to get out (and that was before I got my first gland).Last....being vague. Good lord, I know it's a "SOULS-LIKE" but why does every souls game have to be so vague and devoid of storytelling and even BASIC GAME INFO.... Upgrade your weapon? "Performs an attack". Pick up a new item that you might only find 5 of in the whole game? "Consume to learn more". Also with parrying requiring resolve to use, I rarely bothered and saved it for weapon attacks. I would recommend this game on sale even if you're not a no-hit ultra-parry ng+420 god on dark souls. Enjoy the game. Have a nice day. Watch for bear traps.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a "Pocket-Souls" game, but with interesting new mechanics.  While I definitely missed the ability to block with weapons/shields, the game still maintains a familiar parrying mechanic (provided you pick up the appropriate item near the beginning hub), along with an innovative "hardening" mechanic (basically you turn to stone and negate an attack completely, in addition to staggering most smaller enemies), with the main caveat being it takes a few seconds to recharge between uses (managing this cooldown is important especially in boss fights).  The dark universe and environmental visuals are a major selling point for this game as well, and it was a very enjoyable experience playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game for fans of Souls games. Mortal Shell incorporates unique mechanics to create a fascinating and fun experience that creates many ways to defeat your enemies. Shells and weapons have their unique abilities that adds to a wide range of adaptability. Although, the game does experience some glitches that can make the gameplay either quite easy or unnecessarily hard, and is quite short in terms of game time. Despite this, i will clearly recommend this game for any Dark Souls fan.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful experience that's very similar to a souls like game but different enough to feel like something fresh and new, interesting game mechanics and beautiful dark and gloomy locations and enemies.It took me 26 hours to beat it but only because i was often distracted reading item description, inscriptions or i simply spent some time admiring the environment while playing the lute.Could use a few quality of life improvements, this is obviously not a perfect game but even then it is still a great game, i am a big fan of the dark souls universe and this game did well enough to look like a souls like game but still managed to have enough unique features that made it its own thing unlike other souls like on steam.I wholeheartedly recommend whoever reads this to buy this game, while it may seem harsh at first with enough perseverance you will grow to like it. At the time that i'm writing this i have barely finished the game and i have entered new game plus and i can't wait to see what that brings to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend Mortal Shell... I was pretty hyped to, at last, play the Dark Souls clone that was Epic exclusive for its first year.The game captures the dark and moody atmosphere of the Souls series insanely good. The ambient music is amazing, and it introduces a bunch of new mechanics that are pretty interesting to experiment with.The biggest plus of the game are its new mechanics, that range from changing builds on the fly, to becoming untouchable for the next attack. All these in addition to the normal parrying and attacking mechanics known from Souls.The world design tries to mimic the DS1 map which was very complex and interconnected. Ultimately it feels more like a maze with shortcuts and less like a cool location.The biggest flaw of the game though is enemy placement. Oh my god, how badly the devs misinterpret the enemy placement on Souls with hiding-all-enemies-behind-corners. This "surprise" did not work 95% of the times, since the player was either accustomed to such enemy placement or everything was a pretty obvious trap. Apart from that, most of the enemy fights and "camps" required frustratingly mechanical "kiting" and agro-ing. It felt like playing an MMO from 2005.Bosses were pretty boring too, with maybe the exception of one (of the four). The final boss was ridiculously boring that required the same tactic/pattern of attacks for about 20 minutes....Overall a good first game from a new developer but I can't recommend it since 80% of the game felt like a chore. I will definitely give a spin on any new games from Cold Symmetry though.On a side note though, the DLC is pretty interesting and the new roguelike elements are awesome (along with the new shell (build) and weapon)5/10If you are interested grab under a heavy discount since it's mostly boring.

_childDocuments_.review: right - i'm done...giving up with it....this game is just a repetitive grind fest with a boring world to explore with bland enemies and the most boring loot/items to find. I have never played an action rogue like and been so uninterested in the loot. I never spent any currency at a shop as I didn't require anything,,,,EVER! The items I did have I never used...other than the healing mushroom.if it isn't the badly designed maps (mazes?!?) or the reskinned enemies that ALL attack the same...then it's the boring boss fights that can be beaten first time that will always result in the boss having two health bars like it's some kind of surprise!! The map is laid out to purposely waste your time. It does not respect the player and it is either overly complex or stupidly linear. No middle ground...just annoying.The need to backtrack through the areas in the dark...I mean, if the game was good this would be cool...but it's a grindfest so having grind back out of a boring area that was a grind to get through in the first place is well...just boring and not fun.This is for the absolute bored...the lonely and those Dark Souls fans who need to exercise their ego so they can tell everyone that "yeah, I've beaten Mortal Shell..."A waste of time....copied ideas, copied assets, copied loading screen....blah blah blah.The graphics and sound are nice...but these things do not make a great game. Great gameplay and world design make a great game and Mortal Shell lacks both...I'd say this game is on the same level as Lords of the Fallen and The Surge. Fine if you really need it but nothing new and nothing interesting.bored out of 10 - Bought it to try out the DLC but I've already experienced enough for now. Maybe I'll come back to it in a few years. To be truly successful this game needed to be it's own thing...if you copy Dark Souls you need it to be as good as, if not better than what's inspiring you. To be such a clone and to fail real is sad...I tried my hardest to like this game...but I just spent too much time swearing and shouting at my PC through frustration at just how boring it all is!!

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review after completing the first cycle of the game; looking forward to the Repayable Content and getting the related trophies.Quite a satisfying run for such a short game. Doesn't offer a lot of ground-breaking mechanics for the base content but pretty excited to try out the rougelike mode it offers. The game isn't a build crafter's playground but the Shells and Weapons do provide some healthy dose of variety throughout the game. Mastering the Shells is a minimal time investment as I've completed one run while maximizing each one.  (including the additional Shell from the DLC) As far as I understand, the weapons progressively improve for every new run you start (NG+) as the materials required for it is limited in each run. From a mechanical standpoint, the system has pretty good variety to fit different melee fighting styles. Conceptually the weapons are uber interesting to say the least, its not a wide range but you can definitely feel the ideation that brought them to life. Combat was pretty engaging despite the low variety of enemies. I love it that Parrying is a core mechanic. The design in this game makes it necessary as the most concrete way of healing and improvement to it through progress allows for more offensive flexibility.Harden is another sweet mechanic that offers additional dynamism to combat. Much like the Umbral Lamp of Lords of the Fallen, I hope I get to encounter more unique mechanics in souls-like such as these. Setting and visuals are stunning. I'm a big sucker for Dark Fantasy types with really nice armor aesthetics. Not much to be had for fashion except for some goofy color variants. Solid 7.5 for me overall. I would imagine this goes out at a steal on Sale Days -- it's a solid recommendation for Souls fans looking outside of From Soft genius.

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous genre entry with especially weighty and visceral combat compared to the average. The biggest complaint against Mortal Shell is that it's too small - too few areas, too few bosses, too few weapons - and with an character / item system that was appreciably simplified (perhaps a little too much so). All a sequel needs is just 'more of everything' to be one of the greats.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really hard to recommend a game like 'Mortal Shell' to other people. The abridged version would be something along the lines of:"Hey, do you wanna play Dark Souls but more obtuse, more clunky, with worse level and art design and even more incomprehensible story and minimal production value? But it has a nice blocking mechanic where you make your body hard!"Like seriously, I'm trying to come up with a scenario where somebody would play this over any other FromSoftware game, and to my mind the only answer is: When you've played all other games to 100% and want something new, for catalogue purposes. Lets start with  Whoever came up with a brilliant idea to have the main diverging area with the firelink shrine be the incomprehensible maze of a forest needs to never get hired as a visual artist ever. i mean they've TRIED at least with some subtle clues indicating which way is the 1 of the 3 main dungeons where this relatively-short game takes place, but the emphasis is on 'subtle'. This game could use giant freaking neon signs with arrows and descriptions, or better yet, some sort of a teleport system, although that would probably reduce the playing time by about 3/5th. The stand-out of bad level design for me is fthe tar-cube zone, which feels like it has the length of 2 dark souls 2 and has the samey-looking tar metal texture throughout, making it particularly unpleasant to look at. Also the non-interactive manholes you crawl thru were just awful, as well as being all samey and confusing the player sense of direction, it's just boring pressing forward.People writing the story (I assume there were some people tasked with this) kinda forgot that you need a point of reference to anything in order to give a crap about anything thats going on. The world is boring and ugly, all the characters are cryptic and boring, (except the funny brigand, that was good actually) and there's no intro or anything pretty or interesting thats going on. Like wow some fish ate me in a dream I guess that means something to someone.Okay, here's a tough one: The main gimmick of the game whereupon you switch the titular shells with diff stats and power ups is boring.  First of all, the game flat out doesnt explain to you how to switch out weapons and shells, otherwise I found the game pretty straight forward, but once you find a shell with the stats that best suit your playstyle and skills - you're NEVER switching off of it. At least I didnt see a need to? Just picked up the shell with the most insane amount of HP and you're good, as health is something thats hard to come by in this game, speaking of which...This is flat-out the worst health system in any of the Souls-Like I ever played, not only do you not have an equivalent of the Estus Flask, but you eat stupid mushrooms that you cant farm reliably since enemies dont drop them and they appear with a cooldown in specific areas, which makes it SUPER hard to stay alive at the start. Thats when you find out the Merchant sells rats at stupid cheap price so you can just buy 99 heal items and pretty much stay alive till the rest of the game at that point. Maybe restock once or twice. This health system is stupid because you pretty much have infinite heal and its not balanced at all.The  Honestly this is the only redeeming feature of the game as far as I'm concerned - being able to turn rock-solid during an enemy swing or during your attack to correct bad timing is such a rewarding experience, and makes you wish it was in an actual From Software title because it changes drastically the flow of the combat, it's really fun. The virtuous cycle or w/e its called is a neat idea, basically a randomized version of the game world with various perks and increased difficulty with rogue lite elements, which in theory is a fun distraction for about 30 minutes until you realise the clunky combat just doesnt support this level of difficulty to make it greatly enjoyable. Once again - I wish it was in a better game, and I think its paid DLC anyway....So yeah, as you can see, even though the game wasnt terrible, it just has insanely low production value, feels cheap and poorly balanced at times, even though I initially wanted to give it a thumbs up, honestly I just feel like there's no reason to play this unless you've beaten all of the Soulsbourne games, but even then there's better stuff out there. Maybe the devs could improve drastically in a sequel, cuz there's a few interesting ideas in here.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really hard to express my feelings about this game. Everything is fine, but the game is mediocre at best. It's frustrating and not by it's difficulty level but with weird game design issues that were either overlooked or implemetend deliberately with the intention to make game unique and not like "that other dark souls games".Combat is fine, but you'll be excited to fight each enemy type only once and then you will be just running past all of the enemies because fighting with them is extremely boring. Graphics and effects are ok, but camera is just a piece of garbage and it is much worse than in any DS game you've ever met. Voice actors are wonderful, but their voices do not fit on some character. Difficulty is challenging, but it's more like dark souls 2 level of difficulty, just don't waste too much stamina and you are good to go.This is just an endless stream of "yes, but" and the game is actually ok for it's price, but expect a huge portion of frustration syrup on your dark souls ice-cream.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a dark and atmospheric action RPG that successfully carves out its own identity in the challenging Soulslike genre. From the moment you step into its haunting world, the game envelops you in a sense of mystery and dread, with beautifully desolate environments and a hauntingly evocative soundtrack.The combat in Mortal Shell is both brutal and rewarding, demanding precision, timing, and strategy. Each encounter feels significant, and the unique mechanic of inhabiting different Shells adds a fresh layer of depth to the gameplay. Each Shell offers distinct playstyles and abilities, allowing for a variety of combat approaches and encouraging experimentation.The game's lore is rich and intriguing, gradually unfolding through exploration and cryptic dialogues. It’s a narrative that respects the player’s intelligence, inviting them to piece together the story and uncover the secrets hidden within the world. The sense of discovery is palpable, making every exploration a rewarding experience.Visually, Mortal Shell is stunning. The detailed environments, eerie lighting, and meticulously designed enemies create an immersive and unsettling atmosphere that keeps you on edge. The graphics are complemented by fluid animations and impactful sound design, enhancing the overall immersion.While the game is challenging, it never feels unfair. The learning curve is steep but manageable, and each defeat serves as a lesson, pushing you to refine your skills and strategies. The satisfaction of overcoming a tough boss or navigating a treacherous area is immense, making the journey incredibly fulfilling.Mortal Shell is a standout title that offers a fresh and engaging take on the Soulslike formula. With its innovative mechanics, captivating world, and satisfying combat, it’s a must-play for fans of the genre and anyone looking for a challenging and atmospheric adventure.

The combat is fine, but the enemy density is not. Instead of having the freedom of pacing you are forced into a complete stand still in many bottlenecks waiting for the enemies to react first.The closest Souls-like experience I could compare this to combat wise is Lords of the Fallen.I've personally not experienced map design this frustrating in any memorable sense. It is frustrating to the point of turning the game off after 2 deaths because those deaths are not productive ones.I'll update my review if this changes, but as it stands I genuinely cannot think of a single person I know that I think would enjoy this game and so I cannot recommend it. I will still continue to play it to see if there's something past this ridiculously steep barrier to entry, but so far this is simply too hard - it is not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Half an hour in and for the first time in ever, I can honestly say I am hating a souls-like game. After having played what must be 20+ at this point this is the first one that feels terrible to play. Super slow, clunky start. Enemies have super basic  patterns, but they are a lot faster than the player is. They hit you with a melee attack standing above you on a ledge, which they can't get down from. They phase in occasionally. There is knockback/ragdolling which is just horrible because you randomly die before getting up without any counter play. Items have a set respawn so you can just afk and farm them if needed. The harden mechanic would be nice, if it wouldn't not block damage half of the time you activate it. Enemy targeting is nice, but if your character swings/stabs next to enemies standing in front of you  while you have them targeted it doesn't exactly do a whole lot. Terrain clipping, terrain clipping everywhere.... already fell through the world once and was able to reproduce a second time. Also forced crawl tunnels on every corner, which in most cases don't help the loading at all. The menus take 10 seconds to open and are obnoxious with the fade and sound. Shadows only look good on high or ultra, else it is literally smoke and your entire screen is gray. As a software tester myself this just feels largely untested given the sheer amount of issues I've found already and it's such an utter shame. I will likely power through for a while longer just because... I've finished dark souls with a ladle and have at least one deathless run for all of the main souls games so I'm not one to throw the towel in easily... But this game? I'm already tempted after 30 minutes of gameplay and that probably speaks volumes.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I truly love the aesthetic of the game, I cannot recommend it. Or, unlike me, if you love punishing combat, with "bonfires" far and between, you'll love this. _childDocuments_.review: So I went into this game having heard good things about it. It started off great, good setting, nice environment and meaty swings with the weapon but then I started noticing a lot of technical issues.It took me a while to realise but I was not getting any tutorial pop ups when I pick something important up, for example, I got my parry tool early on but did not realise it was the tool cause the pop up that is supposed to explain it did not show up. After roaming around for while, I finally looked up how it works on youtube. The lack of tutorials stayed though out the playthrough.Another issue is the enemy pop ins, why do enemies who I just went past 2 mins ago suddenly disappear and come back to whack me when I am 2 feet away ? It is not a draw distance issue, all other objects are there, the enemies just phase in.Lastly, what really put me off, I got to the final boss, beat him on the second try but then the game bugs out and doesn't let me click on the prompt to take me to credits and NG+. Had to quit out, which put me back in the boss arena with a full health boss while I don't have any more items and am at half health. It is a good thing the enemies in this game are not too hard.I understand it is a small dev team but I think the above issues should have been caught and fixed. Coming to mechanics, the game does have some neat stuff, the whole mechanic of having different class like loadouts which can be freely switched into are really nice and the weapons are good. I would say it would have been nice to have enough upgrade mats to level up and use more than 2 though.The level design is good and is manageable once you get to know the layout of the maps though I have to say enemies in the game taper off the difficulty as you level up. The bosses are pretty good and the combat with them feels meaty and satisfying which is really the best part of the game. The DLC seems interesting but rogue like elements are not that appealing to me and this looked too grindy.All in all, there is good stuff in the game and some nice unique ideas but they were held back by the technical and balancing issues in my playthrough. If someone has an unbearable itch for a souls like, give it a shot, else it can be skipped.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like Dark Souls but it's not as good. Even Demon Souls was a better game, now that I think about it. The first in the series, Demon Souls had multiple character archetypes to use, different weapon types, different magic paths, upgradeable gear, and so on. Mortal Shell really doesn't. As far as I can tell, you can't upgrade gear beyond giving a weapon a 'special move', there aren't very many weapons to begin with, there are no character builds for different playstyles, and what they did give you (the two-hander heavy hitter sword) kinda sucks. Instead of letting you block, they have this stupid "harden" mechanic that has a cooldown, and spoiler, it doesn't cool down enough to actually keep you safe. They make you play a slow, lumbering armor guy who is constantly out of stamina (because why would they let you actually have fun and hit things), they give you a slow-ass weapon to use that you can't upgrade in a meaningful way, there's no armor to find, and then the one thing they DO give you to keep your slow ass alive is on a cooldown. Also, you know that whole "level up a couple times and upgrade your gear, then come back stronger" thing dark souls has? As far as I can tell, this game doesn't have that.I really should have known better buying an action game with a 70% rating. I dunno if the game gets better the farther you get in, but so far, I'm not impressed and I do not recommend it.Oh, by the way, no ranged weapons or magic, at least not that I've found. So if that's your bag this game doesn't want you playing it.

I have actually gone out of my way to avoid purchasing any games that did, including sequels to games I love. (Metro and Borderlands come to mind.) I was going to avoid this game for the same reason, but something just kept calling me back to it. I am a huge Souls fan, and really wanted something I could play to scratch the same itch. But that's not what really turned me around on this title. _childDocuments_.review: First let me adress the many reviews that says this game is too short. Yes if you run straight from boss to boss you can finish your first run in no time ( 3-6 hours) but to the many reviews that says "i completed the game in 7 hours", no you didnt you just whent from boss to boss in your first run:) This is not a game you just wanna rush through. Theres alot of secret lore, items, shades, etc to discover, and if you really wanna experience the full game you should explore and go for all achievements. Just like dark souls, you can run through the game pretty fast, but if you are going for all trophys, its a very differet matter. Try "No lifer" run or "Life is suffering" run, upgrade your shells/caracter to max, learn to master the mechanics, weapons and caracters and you have a wonderful game with many hours of great gaming! Im very impressed by a team of 16 devs and a small budget making something this great!And yes It can feel a tiny bit clunky at times but in general the mechanics are great and feels fresh and original the fact that you can change caracter/shell and weapons fast during boss fight (come in as a stamina based warrior, switch to tank, and back to stamina style) did that it never felled boring fighting the same bosses and enemies, learning their moves and so on. (The bosses in this game are pretty easy, the enemies and the way to the boss is a bigger challenge) And speaking of mechanics, I loved how the way you progress and play the game completely changed in the DLC, this gave me so many fun runs on such a relative small map. I also love the sound of the weapons, footsteps and dying enemies, the atmosphere and also the visual style of each area, but mostly I love how music plays a part in this game, you can clearly feel how the devs has a passion for music/metal, and the fact that there are hidden references to "Black Metal" and "dark ambient" is a big plus in my book:)I liked this game so much that i 100% it, and during that, I woke up every morning looking forward to continue my journey in it.. _childDocuments_.review: Good ideas, bad execution.It's obvious what Mortal Shell is "inspired" by to the point that it seems like a rip-off. However it brings enough unique ideas to the table, to make itself stand out. The combat is focused a lot on parries and blocking, instead of dodge rolling past everything. This takes some getting used to for people familiar with similar games. Attacks are slow and deliberate while enemy tracking is off the charts. It's very much intended for more reserved defensive and offensive play. Otherwise it's your standard Souls-like afair.What makes it unique is how this different focus plays out:"Blocking" is named "Hardening" and bascially works in such a way, that you can freeze in place and make yourself invincible against attacks at any given point. Even while performing other actions like attacks. You can hold this status for quite some time or just quickly use it in a pinch. This is on a cooldown however and needs to be timed well.The parry move can be equipped with different effects for the follow-up ripostes. You may leech some health or do different types of special attacks, adding some much needed reward for the higher risk of parrying. Attacks you cannot parry have a warning sound and effect (more on that later).Besides healing from parries the only other way to regain HP is consumable items. No auto-refilling flasks here. You may farm for the most basic ones or buy some at a store later on. The rest of the consubales are either additional XP or add effects to your parry and block moves such as more damage on the next attack after a successful parry or getting hit while hardened converting the damage to HP.So much for the games good ideas on how to mix up the souls formula. Now why a negative review?Because what would be the one thing you don't want in a game like this with such a focus? - for it to feel inconsistent. That's the first thing that comes to mind, when describing the combat of Mortal Shell. It just feels off in many ways. For example:- The timing for the "cannot parry" warning seems different for every such attack. Sometimes it's way ahead, other times it's a split-second before the attack lands.- Everything is animation-based so how quickly you can string another action onto your last one can have a jarringly big difference. All the more noticable, because in harsh contrast to that the "harden" move is available immediately on demand when not on cooldown.- This extends to enemies. When they stagger from your attack or recoil from your block doesn't follow consistently comprehensible rules. I've seen enemies miss me entirely while hardened in place, not recoil because of it and hit me with the follow-up attack. Something that never happens when not blocking.- The damage output of combos follows no real logic. With the first sword you get for example you can string together a light and a heavy attack which is super fast and still does more damage than 3 light attacks in a row. String together 2 light attacks and a heavy as the 3rd however and it's barely more damage than the 3 lights plus is slower.It doesn't help that on top of that, there are instances where you can get stuck on level geometry during fights, since there is no jumping and the overall level design is pretty bare bones. Which is especially bad, because it has the usual souls-like problem of allowing the player to just run past everything to the boss. Something you become very tempted to do, when the experience can turn out to be frustrating and there isn't all that much to see.Overall Mortal Shell is a game, that can be worth checking out when on sale just to experience its own spin on the souls-like combat forumla. But all of it is held back by a lack of polish, that can make these unique features turn into a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I do not write reviews with such little gametime done, but Mortal Shell is one of the few examples of too little sometimes actually is too little. Mortal Shell shrouds itself in mystery and doesn´t reveal much - or more like anything. There is no save, no quicksave, no maps, no progression by experience - and that in a game where you are supposed to slay tons of enemies to get anywhere. Where? No clue. I had to watch walkthroughs - which were more like run-throughs - to find out what is what. I don´t expect to be taken by the hand and lead, but some clue what to do or where to go would be nice and I expect a game to do at least that. I can absolutely play without a map - but if you build a long-winded, mace-like landscape full of enemies I do expect one. If you add to that faulty combat animations that hit you although the enemy is out of range for you but he can hit you because he is going downhill, crossbow bolts flying through tree trunks and in impossible ballistic arcs - yeah, that is really fun. Worst of all are, again, the controls. The combat system relies on extremely precise controls, that the game had, when it came out on console. The mouse and keyboard translation for PC is clunky and slow. Add to that tons of enemies and you losing all progress (parts you already cleared) and all currency you need to improve your armor upon death and you got a really great game (sarcasm warning). This could be fun - but it isn´t. The combination of intended game mechanics and abyssmally bad controls where perfect precision is required just doesn´t work. 5/10 - do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing Games as Though They’re My ExesMortal ShellGraphicsI met MS twice, in two different marketplaces. The initial meetup was a rush! I came away from that much taken by his unreal, black metal, dark fantasy aesthetic. In our second meeting, and throughout our relationship, one of the highlights was just how beautiful he was. Even when he wasn’t feeling like delivering the most effort and had to dial it down a bit, not much of his beauty was lost. GameplayMS was a difficult fellow, but he wasn’t the first to give me a challenge throughout the run of a relationship. In fact, of the four difficult men I’ve dated before MS, I could say he wasn’t even the most difficult among them. However, I could probably attribute my experience with my previous relationships in helping me navigate my relationship with MS. That is, without ER, CV, N and N II, my time with MS may have been a bit more of a pain than a fun challenge.DifficultyFor the most part, when we hit a rough patch during our time together, we could work with each other on the best compromise. You go this way, I go that way. I say this, you say that. You do this, I do that. Easy, like a dance. And I was not the best dancer by any measure, but when the steps clicked, it clicked! Sometimes, it took longer to figure it out with him. Sometimes, not so much. It took the longest and became the most frustrating whenever he would sabotage the argument or the problem, and it sends us back to square one.That isn’t to say I didn’t have my own failings. Now, as I said, I wasn’t the best dancer and I know when I messed up, and I would readily admit that. I would say maybe half the time, the argument/difficult situation crumbled because of my own ineptitude, and other times, it was because he was fundamentally broken inside and just could not cope.AudioAs I alluded to before, MS was very much into black metal music, particularly the band Rotting Christ. Personally, I enjoy most music genres, and black metal was certainly one of those that I could listen to regardless of my mood.GrindThe first few dates with MS were great, literally one of my favorite moments in dating. But that feels like a long time ago now, as we quickly fell into a routine where a small voice in the back of my head would go, “Do I really want to deal with him now?” The voice never became too loud as to not be ignored, but it was always there. Even when I was sure I was having fun with him in the moment, I would catch that tinny tiny voice gnawing inside my ears.StoryMS’s life story was dark and grungy, but throughout my time with him, I feel like I’ve only ever pieced together some of it. He can get caught up in his fancy way of speaking when detailing his past and describing his present, and despite being deeply interested in him, I would realize that my eyes had glazed over, and I would be too embarrassed to ask him to repeat himself.CompletionMS and I stayed for as long as we could until our relationship reached its intended end. At 115 days, we went through everything together, turned over every rock that we could and learned about each other in every which way. I don’t know how he feels at the end of it all, but for me, I remember more his quirks and self-sabotaging more vividly than what made me attracted to him in the first place. I can say I had a good time, initially, but the more we stayed together, the more it was tempting to just end it earlier than it should have. BugsMS suffered from so much self-destructive behavior that it was a struggle at times to really enjoy my time with him. At first, it was easy to ignore or even flat out not notice his… “quirks”. But the more we spent with each other, the more apparent and problematic they became. At times, not in public, I must say, I would just walk away from him and not speak with him for an extended time.Final ThoughtsMS was a beautiful, dark, excitingly challenging fellow, but upon closer inspection, his self-destructive behavior comes through and it can be a bit of a relationship killer if you can’t navigate that sort of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Its simply not fun.I had my eyes on this game for a while because the animations and characters looked cool, the game looked like a unique souls-like game that I decided I wanted to try especially since it was on a huge sale.The game just simply isn't fun for me, having played other souls-like games this one just feels very very clunky and very very grey-toned. Everything is relatively the same, there are tons of enemies absolutely everywhere with no bonfires/checkpoints, no reusable heal, no fast travel and a massive twisting map that I got lost in several times.The combat feels very clunky, animations are relatively slow and your attacks all chew through stamina like it didn't exist in the first place, if you want to play aggressive it simply doesn't feel like you are able to at all and even get punished for simply trying. The hardening mechanic is interesting, being able to harden even between attack animations is unique and useful but it doesn't feel useful enough, parrying in this game is the main way you'll be able to heal yet the timing is extremely awkward, for me at least.The bosses I fought had far too much health compared to the damage I was dealing, there were far too many mobs just about everywhere and the combat simply isn't fun. I have no problem with the game, it just simply is not fun and I do not want to continue playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Me: "Mom, can we have Dark Souls?"Mom: "No, we have Dark Souls at home."Dark Souls at home:Jokes aside, what I do respect about Dark Soul clones is that they are accessible to all gamers.While Dark Souls only now finally have been brought to PC, games like Bloodborne are still gated as exclusives!!The pricing is outrageous as well, even at discount!That's where games like "The Surge" and "Mortal Shell" come into play.Mortal Shell is a much smaller indie game that has only 7 bosses compared to 26 from Dark Souls.It is considered one of the easiest soulslike gmaes. The gameplay feels clunky and primitive.(I probably got spoiled by the polish of the much acclaimed "The Surge" game.)The bugs killed it for me: when attacking or using items became impossible, especially during boss fights..The story is very convoluted and told in disjointed pieces (common in this genre) but has the same atmosphere as Dark Souls and the VERMIS books.Lack of maps is annoying (also common in this genre), but can be found on the internet. nice.The Virtuous Cycle DLC is a great addition,beside the new playable modular character/shell and the ultra-cool Axe-katana,the new mode adds a roguelike aspect and a far greater challenge. (exactly what this game needed.)Overall a fun little romp for such a cheap price at discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it fun? Yeah. Very reactive combat with lots of ways to go into something. Parry, harden, dodge, strike. Feels really good.So why can't I recommend it? Enemies pop in at distances of less than five paces. In a game where enemies can and will chunk you for half or more of your health, enemies not pre-loading at a good distance makes some areas feel entirely unplayable. It breaks up the flow of exploration in the worst way possible. It ruins the immersion.Unfortunately, unless the enemy pop in issue is fixed I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The start of this game is very frustrating, directionless, and difficult until you get the hang of its mechanics. If you want to enjoy this game then give it a lot of patience, and I mean a LOT of patience. If you're frustrated easily then just pick up and put down this game whenever it becomes too frustrating. I think I alt-f4'd this game about 2 times out of frustration of not knowing where to go and maybe 5 times out of getting my ass beat. However, with that out of the way, the game has a really great combat system that is fun and lets you be aggressive. The harden mechanic is a fantastic idea and you can use it literally at any time, mid attack, mid roll, literally at any time. That combined with the ability to animation cancel a majority of attacks makes the combat very dynamic and allows you to be aggressive; you're not sitting there dodging attack after attack waiting for a window to retaliate, you make the window yourself. If you can get past the frustrating learning curve then I think you will enjoy this game. Once you get a good grasp on the combat system in the game you shouldn't have too big of an issue with beating the main game, especially when you upgrade the tank character. Additionally, the Virtuous Cycle DLC is a challenge mode that is like a rogue-like, it can be fun but some of the challenges in that are extremely difficult, I enjoy this game a lot but some of those challenges are far too difficult for me. I recommend this game greatly, especially since there is a sale going on right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best, most interesting settings I've ever seen in a game. The world that was set up by the recollections and the visuals is surprisingly spectacular. It is admittedly disappointing that be only really see Fallgrim and that you could probably count the number of named characters on your hands, but the game's still interesting. _childDocuments_.review: First played through this game on PS4 and finally got my hands on it for PC. It may be hard to get in to, but after a few hours you can cruise through no problem. For someone who has over a combined 1000 hours in Fromsoftware titles, this game is actually pretty easy. The hardening adds a safety net that is like an "oops" button if you get caught whiffing an attack. The shells are all super cool, both in their designs and playstyles. They are all relatively accessible and let the player experiment early. The dodging and movement feels a little floaty and unpolished both on the players side and enemy side. The weapons are incredibly cool and the movesets animations are beautiful. A lot rides on parrying; its a way to do massive damage to enemies or heal and you can use items that further affect the parry. However, parrying is not super crucial and attacks can be dodged or blocked with hardening. My personal favorite thing about this game is the shell and weapon designs. Cold Symmetry really outdid themselves with the characters. I definitely recommend this game to people who like third person fantasy RPG games like Dark Souls, Nioh or Bloodborne.

_childDocuments_.review: I have owned Mortal Shell since day 1 on steam. I played it in 2021 and left it a negative review. Here I am, 3 years later giving the game another chance. Giving it a PROPER play after all the bug fix's, patch's and optimisation has came in.I have just completed the game without using ANY "shell" at all. I went for a no shell run - Obsidian dark form. To give myself a challenge. To really test my skills and I have to say, I am rather impressed. Below I will state why but first a small disclaimer!  ⚫They fixed the crashing, stuttering, freezing. What I am saying is - they finally optimised it. This was one of the main reasons why I left it a NEGATIVE review.⚫The NPCS are perfect for this world. They mutter creepy little lines.⚫The world was very atmospheric from start to end. From the moody, creepy landscapes and the extremely vague story... it felt like a souls-like game, finally. Here is a screenshot that I recently took: ⚫The many, many unique shells can be swapped out whenever you want to tailor a build for yourself. You are not forced to play as one the entire game. There is a "shell" for everyone and I thought this was cool.⚫I finally got the hang of the "HARDEN" mechanic. It took me a while to properly use it but when it clicked... oh boy was it fun. How unique this "method" is, is astonishing to me!⚫When I got "Solomon" I fell in love instantly with the game. Having more resolve, being able to unleash that SPECIAL skill... man... why did I not respect this sooner?⚫If you manage to pull off a "pefect parry" you get to riposte which plays an absolutely fantastic animation.⚫You can now summon all the weapon types on the go!!! This was one of the most annoying aspects back then, not being able to do this.⚫I thought the different areas of the game were gorgeous. I fell in love with the frozen area. Here is a quick screenshot:  ⚫The only BUG/GLITCH or issue I encountered was a "LOCK ON" problem when no eneies where around me. I know this has been around for a while.⚫I abused the "Dodge, dodge roll" aspect of the game from start to finish as the "obsidian dark form" (One hit death mode - no shell) to beat the entire game. Nothing was able to kill me due to an invincibility frame basically. I thought this was WAY to lenient.⚫The "parry timing" felt really off to me. I do not know if I am just struggling with it or not but this definitely is the weakest part of Mortal Shell, in my opinion. ⚫It's pretty easy to get lost, if you have not seen any gameplay before. The swamp, you start in, is connected to all 3 areas which all kind of look the same. If you have an eye for detail, they you will be fine as you will notice the differences but a casual player might get lost real fast. The DLC is a scam. It is the exact same game but made roguelike. All it adds in is ONE new weapon and ONE new shell. They don't make a new map. All they have done is used the entire map we have already explored, changed up enemy positions and added in "RNG" debuffs/buffs.Whoever made this DLC, you should be ashamed. I hope you got fired. I wrote a pretty DAMNING negative review in 2021. More or less stating how bad Mortal Shell was in terms of optimisation. Now, 3 (almost 4) years later, I have to say - Mortal Shell is definitely worth the "Souls-Like" tag. I consider Mortal Shell "bite-sized souls". I just bet the game in obsidian dark form in - 2.8 hours. This was the one hit death mode where you could not use a shell. Now, I am going to go and actually collect EVERYTHING. EXPLORE EVERYTHING. The reason why I challenged myself to that mode was because I felt like I wanted a challenge and boy, did It kill me over and over. One mistake is all it took and I felt a sense of accomplishment with each victory without a shell.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a genuinely gorgeous game, and it wants you to believe it's a souls-like, it doesn't understand what makes those games appealing. They kept the clunky controls that the originator of this style fixed by the 2nd in the series. Leveling up doesn't feel rewarding as you simply unlock abilities that are worse than just dodging and attacking. I would rather have improved my stamina instead while I waited to see what kind of build I wanted to go for. The reviews kept saying it's a faithful Dark Souls clone, but I just beat Dark Souls recently and I think they don't remember Dark Souls very well.Someone is going to absolutely love this game, it just isn't me.Edit: While my review is negative, I do want to say that I hope they make a Mortal Shell 2 and that they take the criticisms and improve upon them.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, what seemed a very promising soulslike with some interesting mechanics turned out to be an unfinished, at best unpolished and janky product. Pros and cons below:Pros: - I'd lie if I said the attack animations look bad, far from it - it's the first thing that caught my attention- The hardening mechanic, while flawed in implementation, is an interesting concept- Unlocking new weapons and their progression system kind of works- Some locations can be quite visually appealing (Seat of Infinity)- Atrium Carceri- BallistazookaCons:- The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jank, it's everywhere, both in level geometry, attack tracking, hitboxes, and input reading. I can't even count the number of times my character was stuck in some weird geometry, ganked by several mobs and unable to get up- The ridiculous level design - in the starting location everything looks the same and there are very few environmental cues to guide the player, and on the other hand it's unnecessarily confusing. Once again, Seat of Inifty, and specifically Eternal Narthex needs to be mentioned - I spent an absurd amount of time looking for the third torch to access the final area. Without a guide I'd probably still be stuck there.- It seems the devs' idea of a soulslike is the typical 'make the enemies spongy and put gank squads everywhere'. Yes, it's easy enough to just run past them, but that's not the point - they should be balanced so that they can be beaten without relying on cheese tactics- Speaking of balance, there's hardly any difference between an unupgraded weapon and a fully upgraded one. Tested on the final boss. It feels that in general the game maths is off, as there's marginal difference between a standard, heavy and jumping attack. Special attacks and ballistazooka pack a punch at least.- No rechargeable healing items and no warps between this game's equivalent of bonfires make certain sections tedious, artificially stretched and just not fun to play- Boring, heartless and overly dramatic dialogues and lore. Not a single bit of the story was gripping enough for me to even care about it, not to mention the idiotic premise of the main 'questline'I wish I could recommend this game, but I really can't. It feels more like a POC or a vertical slice to demonstrate the core game concepts and gameplay loop. There are some interesting ideas there, but their implementation is flawed, broken and rushed. Shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Make no mistake, mortal shell is a good game. The mixed reviews seem to be some controversy about they price of the game staying fixed regardless of region. I don’t know much about it one way or the other, so I’m going to provide my inputs on the actual game. It’s pretty obvious that it’s inspired by the Demon souls/Dark Souls series. I had initial thought so, but 18 seconds into the game when I see the loading screen in between areas… well all doubt left my mind at that point. At one point, right after I died and NPC told me to “get good.” Inspirations aside, there are some major differences between the combat of Dark Souls and Mortal shell. The harden mechanic is pretty neat, as it can function as a way of adding invincibility frames to any attack, delay a dodge that was mistimed, or rapidly recharge your stamina after a flurry of attacks. There is a lot going on with just this one mechanic… And I don’t feel like the game does a good job explaining weapon abilities, parrying to heal, or the resolve system/second chance system. The graphics are pretty good and I’m impressed how well the game runs. I guess I’m just use to every modern game running like *** so it’s impressive to see a 15 man indie team make a game that runs well. (maybe that was the year it spent in the epic store). Regardless, as a souls fan it seems like a nod to one of my favorites but it does enough to differentiate itself.  For those having trouble, I would highly recommend checking out a video explaining the combat before you get started. You will have a lot more fun that way, rather then  suffering through. I would die every 30-60 seconds until I got fed up and just looked up some videos. Now it’s only every 5 minutes. Also look up a video on how to find Eredrim at the start. He has a massive health pool, paired with the highest defense. This game (like most souls like games) is all about understanding enemy attack patterns. Being able to survive a number of attacks will help you to that end. ****One thing I will say... the drawing distance for enemies and traps is really unacceptable. If traps just hindered you in combat, i could forgive it. But the traps can suddenly appear 10 feet in front of you, right after you checked and didn't see anything, only to suddenly be stuck in a bear trap. Luckily they don't deal that much damage, but DEVs come on... That needs to be patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! I went into this expecting another mediocre Dark Souls clone, and while the game does have a very Souls-like feel and aesthetic, there are a number of interesting and really fun twists that let the game stand on its own merit. The combat is fluid and well designed and the upgrade/progression mechanics are interesting, especially Hadern (if you get the DLC, and I recommend you do). The different shells let you really have fun switching up combat styles throughout a playthrough and let you tackle each challenge in new ways. If you've been looking for something new to sink your teeth into since playing DS3 half to death, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Rare that I will not like a souls-like game, I want to give it thumbs down but for the price, it is an okay game. -Enemy attack intervals are faster than your stamina regen. So instead of dodging, staying away is more viable. -No "bonfire" mechanic (you spawn at certain locations but they are considerably far apart), this makes sense at first since I like a good challenge, but then you realize that just running away from every enemy is a better strategy than fighting them. "Why don't I run away from everyone in the game, until I reach the bosses" yes, you can and will do that, then it will be a run-through until you finish the game without actually playing, because there is no need. -Parry, you need to earn a parry by not parrying. Yes, it is as dumb as it sounds. -Heal -> you need to parry to heal -> to parry, you need to not parry to earn a parry -> better just run away until you reach a bossFinal thoughst; if it is on discount get it. It is still good enough and you may enjoy the things that I criticize in this review. It has some interesting mechanics as well (weapon arts, different shells, hardening etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixed bag for me. The harden mechanic makes combat trivial & I feel that the rolling i-frames are too generous. The fog phase is annoying because of the lack of visibility and the enemies that jump on you out of no where. Some bosses have long AoE phases that make combat less engaging by making the player stand back and wait for bosses to finish their AoE attack. The bosses should've had more unique melee & range attacks to make them less boring. When I play games I tend to hoard finite items and never use them until I hit a wall in my progress. I didn't want to waste healing items by healing damage from regular mobs, and since they give small amount of XP, I started running through areas to reach the bosses and ignore all optional mobs. I had plenty of healing items for the final boss and never felt threatened. This hoarding problem could've been solved by having an "estus flask" like system where all healing items get refilled at check points or, at least, have a smaller carry quantity limit. The positives are graphics, the unique shell system, interface and items' art.Overall, a good effort by a small development team that missed the mark of being a good Souls-like game.

_childDocuments_.review: A shining ode to souls without replicating the genre entirely. I do recommend going into it somewhat blindIf you love souls, I recommend this for sure, it's confusing but the ease of the gameplay makes up for that (it is easier than souls that's for sure, and smaller, it's made by a smaller team, and it's reflected in the price - people complaining about the game size aren't remembering that the games release price is £25)You will get lost at the start, I ended up missing the entire starting area and ended up at in the  area, I had no skills or levels, pushed through until I got to Crucix - he was my first boss, he was tough and the area was tough but I figured that's what the game should be. After I defeated him, the game got a lot easier, not even the last boss (I will admit I did find him disappointing/also there was an attack I'm not even sure was a bug? Some weird black whirlwind thing, as long as I avoided it I was fine, but it looked like the texture had bugged out..), gave me even not nearly as much of a hard time, but it's not too easy. A really good entry game for people threatened by the Souls genre's difficulty, teaches you git gud subtly and you genuinely start to feel powerful pretty quickly, as opposed to not so much in Souls where everything is always a threat to you. That is, if you pick the right shell.. Tiel and Eredim op.I really enjoyed the enemy design, as much as there's a lot of enemies and a lot of back and forth, they are fun to fight and the sword guys  is very cool lol. There is somewhat an issue with enemies popping in, I've ran past enemies spawn points before and then they spawn behind me, but it's not a big deal really, if you remember where they are, or just take your time it's not a major issue.Combat is definitely different, as I said above, it's like entry level souls. Much faster paced though and arguably sometimes smoother (but still got that clunk that we all love), Harden allows you to play so much differently and adds another layer to aggressive/defensive play. Sometimes I'd use it to go crazy with hits, harden to tank and let stamina come back, and hit again and roll away with my last sliver of stamina - or the best cheese in the world, run, harden and jump attack, wait for them to hit you, get an easy hit in, and roll away lol. The only complaint I'd have is that it can be a little janky if you're locked on and near a ledge and hardened in the air.. But it's a small gripe, and it's a whole entire mechanic added in, so it's not a big deal imo. Also, it will save your butt a lot.There is a lack of weapons, but then again this isn't made to the same scale of souls but they are vast enough to give you variety and upgrading makes them hit with quite a punch.. The addition of shells to replace creating a build really works as it's not supposed to be a Souls replica, just an ode, I really enjoyed the differences between them and ended up watching a lore video on each characters back stories etc. Having to defeat Haedern for weapons was a cool way to expand the game a little further, although I would argue he's easy as hell to cheese once you get the pattern, but that's the point of any souls-like really, it's mostly pattern learning or finding ways to cheese things.The maps are confusing.. There is no fast travel, you will be travelling back and forth, the main 'hub' area, is a bit of a mess.. But once you make your way to the areas, it's pretty worth it, the atmosphere really hits the mark at times, with big vast areas and rooms, I do wish they had added a bit more to fill the vastness.. It does sometimes feel a bit rinse and repeat, but it's a good looking game imo.There's probably more I could say but I scrolled up and that's a lotta paragraphs lol, I really enjoyed the game as a whole, will probably do more playthroughs of it and ng+ etc, it isnt the longest game in the world, but for a small team it's definitely a feat and I highly recommend : D.

_childDocuments_.review: First & foremost, screw EPIC! ( Yet another tragic decision by a new developer )If you've experienced souls like games and enjoyed them or if you wish to start the souls like journey, Mortal Shell is the perfect option to begin with. Compared to Souls it is far less challenging, though addictive,  fun and can get you hooked into the genre.Is it any special? No! The game introduces its own feature to stand out from its inspirations, but it does not muster up to be anything new, memorable or special. The story as with souls like games offers minimalist storytelling and is up to the player to uncover. However, at the end of it, I feel the story is underwhelming and lacking any compelling qualities. Level designs are far from good, lack of diverse enemies which contributes to the low level of challenge and due to this easy mastery eliminates replay value.But at the brunt of it, Mortal Shell is a good  game to pass the time with and have a lot of fun. The combat is smooth and visceral, its a joy to parry, use harden and the shells offer versatility. Furthermore, the game has a very gentle learning curve making it extremely easy to master. This  does not mean the game lacks challenge, just less challenging than souls and most souls like games I have played. This is not a bad thing either as it opens up to many players but not the right calling for the usual challenge seeker.For the usual souls to Sekiro player, do not go into this with high expectations, just enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I really, REALLY want to like this game. The artstyle, the graphics, the enemies, look and sound amazing. But the sad truth is, there's not much to the game. You have a tiny arsenal, with little to no variability. There's no real way to rest or "reset" the world or your character, other than dying. In addition, the combat is slow, clunky, and feels like a slightly different version of Dark Souls II's movement system (not good, FYI. It's like playing GTA V, you have no clue where your character is really going to stop or land.), the combat is pretty dry and simple. You "harden", which is basically stationary blocking/dodging, then you riposte, dodge, attack, repeat. There's pretty much zero variability with enemies (and they're pretty dang stupid too lol), and the ones that are different only change things by having grab attacks. Weapons are weak and slow, but you can(?) upgrade them with material(s). The dodging feels horrid (although they give you a ludicrous amount of invincibility frames), it's as if they pulled it right from Jedi Fallen order and it just sucks. On top of all of this, your stamina is always low (unless you have certain shells equipped), and drains incredibly fast. It takes ~70-80% of your stamina to complete one singular combo with the 2 starting shells. On top of all of this, there is zero fast/quick switch with shells, which is plain stupid IMO (however you can fast travel at 'some' point.) . This is really disappointing, because the graphics and artstyle is amazing, the animations look cool (however clunky), the sound effects are nice, and the overall aesthetic of this game is great. It's an okay game if you are not too big into soulslikes, because this honestly really isn't one. It's too easy, too slow, and too different to be considered one. While it's hard to really score this game with a #/10, I'd probably give it a 4 to a 5/10.It's got some neat ideas, and great looks, but that's pretty much it. I suggest you get it on sale (anything below $20).

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a really strong souls-like game, and you should check it out if you like the genre. Some things about this game practically go without mention; the graphical fidelity is top-notch, along with the atmosphere the game puts you in. The combat is fun, with lots of depth, and lots of good hit detection. However, there ARE issues with this game.For criticism, I'll first bring up the various technical issues I had playing this game. My sound would stop and go periodically, and my frames would also drop, sometimes at random, even on the LOWEST settings I could possibly do. My specs are a 1070 and an i5, so I have nothing too top-of-the-line or anything, but my performance issues were surprising to say the least.As for technical issues within the game, the biggest 'bug' I encountered would be mobs spawning into the world only within a certain distance. This wasn't easily replicated, since it also seemed to happen at random, but sometimes there would be no mobs in a space until you walk directly up to it, already getting hit by an attack you couldn't see coming. I haven't really seen many other people talk about the performance much, so maybe these are issues only I've experienced.For the actual gameplay, it was fun, challenging, and expressive. A lot of the real 'meat' to the game here are your boss fights, in typical souls-like fashion. Giving the player the Harden mechanic gives you a lot of freedom for when to pick your moments, since you can let enemies attacks bounce off of you. With mastery, you could really fly through some bosses; rewarding player skill, as any good souls-like should. Hit detection was very good across the whole game, for both player and enemy, making bobbing just out of attack range a viable strategy.Variety between weapons is pretty low, with only 4 equippable weapons in the game (+1 with DLC). These are no Bloodborne weapons either, featuring incredibly fleshed-out movesets, or double movesets in that game's case, save for the extra DLC weapon that is. While there's certainly some complexity to the weapons, it's nothing remarkable.When it comes to your character, you have 4 'shells' you can use (Also +1 with DLC). The shells are your characters, with a different skill tree for each. For the most part, aside from the passives tree, each one mostly just features different stat arrangements. It seems a little dumbed-down, but I liked the shell system overall, it removed the whole stat arrangement headache and gear setup nonsense (which let's be fair... You were either meta or doing it wrong with gear/stats, especially in games like Dark Souls 1), and being able to change between them when I felt like switching it up. The biggest problem I had with the game itself would be the content between the actual boss fights. For the most part, you will fight countless copy-pasted humanoid enemies to waste your time and give you barely any tar. While it's not unexpected to have your time padded out like this in a souls-like, it's not even that difficult to run past everybody. And, without spoiling a whole lot, you won't really find much of anything if you stray off the beaten, story path, save for some items to upgrade your weapons and such, but that's pretty much it. You will find various consumable items that are pretty easily forgotten about, so mindlessly dashing past everybody to find the next respawn point isn't going to really penalize you or halt your progress in any meaningful way.Overall, this game was very fun, even if it was a little short and narrow. The combat more than made up for the game's shortcomings for me, offering something truly satisfying to sink your teeth into. If you don't think the combat alone will keep you interested, definitely purchase with a grain of salt. Myself, I'm eager to see what the developers will put out next!
