_childDocuments_.review: To my own surprise this game has grown on me. The game does not hide its love of Dark Souls and stays very true to some of the core ideas from that franchise (particularly managing a limited stamina pool, high commitment attacks and the risk of losing your souls, or tar as they're called in this game).But what has won me over is that the devs have not been afraid to introduce their own ideas. Enemies can be difficult to cut off between attacks in this game and so you have Harden. This ability with a cool down turns you into a statue until you get hit, then your invulnerability stays for a very short period and you stop being immobile.You can be very aggressive using this ability and can turn into a statue mid attack, so you could Harden during the windup of a heavy and when an enemy hits you, that attack will come out. You will often have to play more defensively when Harden is on cool down depending on which character you're playing as.Instead of building a character with stats Mortal Shell lets you find characters to inhabit. Some of them dodge better than others and one enhances the Hardening ability in various ways. But no matter which you play you can't ignore the Harden ability and expect not to struggle somewhat, since you will need it to approach a lot of enemies and most if not all bosses without having to be constantly on the defense.Parrying is powerful but can be really hard to use and you can't always rely on it. If a particular enemy is making it hard for you to parry reliably you'll have to fall back on using harden.I'm also really fond of the hub map in this game, it's a wonderful web of connections that's easy to get lost in. The game is not long compared to other souls games but I don't mind that personally as I often find souls games can overstay their welcome and I like to replay and try to master certain things. The DLC also offers a randomizer mode crossed with roguelite elements which I've started toying with after beating the game.Gameplay aside the game also looks really nice and I was pleasantly surprised by how well optimised it seems to be. It's not usual for an Unreal engine game to run so well on my computer at high settings and maintain a really good frame rate. Every so often enemies do pop in, which might be part of what the devs have done to maintain good performance, so it isn't perfect, but still impressive.Story wise the game is a bit hit and miss. Without spoiling anything I like the way they've approached it but parts feel like they were rushed or time ran out (some of which feels plugged in by the DLC).Selfishly, I would like more people to give this game a chance because although its rough around the edges I am excited by the ways the game has differentiated itself from other souls games and would love to see the devs make another game so I can see if they build on what they've learned from their debut.

_childDocuments_.review: it's a very fun and pretty game. when you start playing it, the camera, character movement and controls feel quite clunky and difficult to manage but you do get used to that overtime. personally i learned to love it. the game feels unfinished. more like an extended demo. however, you do have to understand that it is a smaller game made by a smaller group of developers with a small budget. the animations (especially for some of the bosses) and some cutscenes just feel... like a highschooler made them. but again, factoring the previous points about the development, you can't exactly blame anyone for that. the concepts for this game are incredible. the idea for the game is definitely there and it really makes it easy to forgive everything else (again, for me personally).my last point is, it feels they put most of their effort into the aesthetics for this game. the graphics are beautiful, the look of the areas, the menu's, items, etc. and not the actual gameplay. but there is still a lot of really great areas of gameplay.i believe this game is a hit or miss. you hate it or you love it. but i recommend at least giving it a try until you get a feel for the controls. that is when your true opinion will show for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game very much appears to be a love letter to probably the Dark Souls series. The weapons are few but all unique. The combat is fairly tight. 'Shells' or characters are pretty easily found when you find your bearings and feet which all have different health/stamina/abilities. My first run I went with high HP. The story is as compelling as it is mysterious. Voice acting was done extremely well. Bosses and 'dungeons' are done well and all unique as well. The world is like any Dark Souls except its not huge but plenty of gameplay to explore and 'shortcuts' to find. Some games are too long, some are too short - this one pretty much fits the bill especially if you get it on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Be prepared for a steep learning curve. The story and art direction are creepy in the good way.  The combat is fun and offers its own uniqueness by throwing some really cool special abilities and weapons your way. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, the only souls like games I have ever played are the following : Jedi Fallen Order... list is done. I have seen a lot of negative reviews on this game from Dark Souls players, but I have found it a very nice experience actually. The Game is Short, you can finish if you speed run like in 6 hours or do it at normal pace and get like 15-20 hours. At the start you are weak, but you will get stronger with weapon upgrades and new Shells that offer different play styles : 4 shells, 4 weapons. The game needs a map I think, so I just used the map on the mortal shell wiki thats showed where to go to get parts and items. Maps arent Elder Ring size, they are Small,    4 different zones tho. The Game looks fantastic, but you might get performance issues sometimes (one boss spawns a lot of particles), enemies are unique, but lacks variety for replayability. Hardening mechanic is pretty cool and it also has parry mechanic that I miss 1/3 times. Also, the familiarity thing backfired cause I lost 14 glimpses with the mask, lol. The progressing feels good, you actually feel like you are getting stronger and I thought I would die a lot without checkpoints (there are but like 1-3 per area, atleast you have a checkpoint before a boss, you can fast travel as well later when you unlock it, but by that point you will use if for new game plus). You can also avoid enemies if you dont want to fight them to regain your lost tar (last place you died), which is cool. And the lore is also interesting, I wish it was bit clearer. The main cons are : Lack of mini map; Enemies can sometimes just spawn in front of you; Enemies can sometimes turn too fast; I find difficulty to keep resolve up sometimes when I play defensive (ability that gives a special attack and you get it by hitting people), so it feels like over time that agressive playstyle actually is better which I started doing later. Feels like Parrying is difficult on bosses, like super hard to tell when they wind up or even when it looks like it should have parried, it didnt. On other enemies its good. Performance issues from time to time like fps drops on some areas. Also, you gotta collect consumables like health, resolves drinks, etc if you want boosts for bosses all over the map which is a bit annoying (but you can beat the bosses without them). Farming glimpses later in the game is harder.TLDR : 7.5/10 , pretty good.Also, people suggest to not buy the DLC cause it has almost nothing new to offer, basically a rogelike mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Had this on epic, bought it again on steam so I could put a review here. Its a souls like so I'll compare it with dark souls so you can get an idea of what it is if you're on the fence about buying it.Pros:* Movement and combat feels a lot smoother and dynamic than DS, its still very slow paced combat with dodge and rolls but without the mechanical sluggishness. * There's a backstep/dodge, and a dodge roll like souls, but the regular dodge feels actually useful and having 2 different options for dodging opens up more possibilities in a fight.* There's less weapons/armor but with the abilities etc. they all get it still feels like it has depth in terms of making a build.* Graphics are better than ds as well as elden ring, it's made in unreal 4.* Harden mechanic is pretty interesting overall, its like a parry, a feint, and a block combined.* Kind of like bloodborne, shields aren't really present here (there's one, I think), so you have to be dodging and rolling a lot, which in my opinion makes fights more dynamic and fun.Cons:* It feels like 2/3rds of the game was rushed, level design is never great but the further you go the worse maps get.* Game is overall very short, I finished it in about 4.5 hours or so, though did not complete it 100%.* Walking animations feel a bit floaty and janky, I think there may be an issue with animation speed vs character movement speed. Also there's no turn in place animations so it looks odd at times.* No multiplayer features* Not much replayability* Whatever lore/world building there is, it feels like they tried too hard to make it obscure, odd, and basically souls-like. Doesn't feel coherent, and didn't really catch my interest in any point.Overall I liked it, I'd love to see if they make a sequel or something with more polish and more content, and will definitely keep these devs on my radar.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept having issues with both screen going black and audio cutting out so refunding this.It wasn't satisfying enough to try and fix the above or truly immerse myself into what the game had to offer.I might buy it again and give it more time if it sees some improvements as that is not the reason for me to thumb this game down. Supporting a game on all PC hardware in existence is impossible, and also what you expect Unreal to solve for you so I can't blame the developers, or judge the game, for that!Pros:The visuals are nice, insane really if you consider the team size.Animations and FX are both very satisfying, and while it wasn't super clear when your attacks would stagger an opponent and when it wouldn't, it overall felt like your actions had weight and impact.Adding the hardening mechanic to your fighting routine is fun to explore.Discovering what items do by using them is neat, I can enjoy eating a poisonous mushroom to figure out what it does, throws me back to alchemy in skyrim, only with actual consequences.Cons (besides crash above):Healing items are too few and too weak, I either don't understand, or didn't find, any checkpoints which made me not want to re-engage the same enemies again because I wanted to save health and see if I could advance, seems to seriously undermine a game about fighting things.Arbitrarily lost the ability to walk or dodge (is it collision, am I stuck in the floor?) at times.Combat feels somewhat off:- Constantly locking onto enemies that are further away or even off-screen.- Jump attacks missing resulting in exposing your back instead of properly colliding with the opponent.Mousing in menus feels bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Brutally difficult from the get go, Once you learn you're weapon and abuse the hardening mechanic its a cakewalk. Gameplay is kinda linear and meh, there is NO build diversity or options, its all very limited. But graphic/sound wise the game does deliver, its nice playing through in like 2-3 sessions. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but i cannot reccomend it for these reasons;1. Bugs and clunk, I get random freezes while fighting enemies.2. Parrying anything takes 10s of hours to master.3. Some bosses are really repetitive and visually uninteresting.4. It took me 4 hours to find my first dungeon5. Any items you use are gone forever, even after you respawn.6. It is really easy to be left with no items, heals nor buffs for bosses which makes fighting them unfun7. Lack of equipment variety and differences. There are 5 shells and 5 weapons. The weapons aren't different to eachother in a major way other than them being ''heavy'' and ''light''.8. It can get unfun really quickly and sometimes extremely difficult to progress if you have no more items (like i said earlier)Other than that it's a fine game with interesting voice lines (although few). If you like a very difficult game that isn't forgiving in any way then I'd buy this game *ON SALE*. It isn't worth paying over 20 Euros/ USD

_childDocuments_.review: The worldbuilding in this game is great, the environments are cool and the level design is interesting.The enemy variations are quite fun to fight as well, the combat itself ranges from interesting to sometimes downright unfair which gives me a lot of mixed feelings.Especially some of the combat encounters required to obtain specific weapons.The DLC is incredibly fun though, I can see myself playing quite a few 'cycles' of it for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: First off, i did enjoy the game - tho more in the later parts of the game then early on. For people that have played a bunch of Soulslikes outside of the Dark Souls series, this could be quiet interesting.The mechannics added by this game are unique and fun to play around with but they take their time to get used to and make the game rather slow. This especially counts for the early game and the first few bosses. The enemy placement can be incredibly frustating at times (even more so after certain points in the game) and often enemies jump at you without you getting time to react. On top of that some meachnics like the parry are not given to you and have to be found instead which can mean you found and fought the first 2 or 3 bosses before you actually pick it up, even tho it can be aquired without killing any boss. On top of that, the game only provides you with a vague sense of direction and the bosses are not ordered in any way so i found the hardest bosses first and that lead to a great ammount of frustation.The Weapons and Shells you find are good and give you enough room to play around with so you can find your own playstyle with it and adapt accordingly if needed.

_childDocuments_.review: It has exactly the same issue as "Kena: Bridge of Spirits" - the parry(here hardening) is the only viable way to play. _childDocuments_.review: This is a REALLY good souls-like game, albeit a bit short.I've played around 9-10 hours and I'm already at the final boss who is the most difficult/annoying of them all. The rest are pretty easy and you can kill them all first try without dying or loosing your shell.But overall if you like souls-like games (which I don't. _childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: A very competent souls-like. I find it had enough mechanics to distance itself, and I was sucked into the mystery of the world, the characters, and even the items which gain meaning with use. I could not put the game down.     Though it gets a little easy once you invest heavily into one character and weapon, most of the power in the game feels earned through the trials of the early learning period.------My major negative is being knocked out of my shell off an edge to my death, despite that causing me to laugh out loud to an empty house numerous times.++++++The best part of the game for me was the soundtrack and environment design which instilled an oppressively haunting vibe. Guttural  echoes and clangs pervade the areas.+You can find your favorite playstyle among the melee weapons and shells and have at it. Eredrim with Martyr's Blade was my favorite once you can get stacks of damage from kills. It maxed at 100 stacks, and I felt indestructible being the tankiest character with only 3 swings worth of stamina bar. It was enough to smite most enemies in one or two swings.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Completely missed what actually makes the Souls game fun.1. No initial customization. Shells have to be found.2. Combat is very repetitive and boring. Attack, harden, back up and repeat until dead.3. Hardening is a unique twist on a shield but isn't used as it should be since enemies aren't aggressive enough.4. Every encounter is a gank squad.5. Horrible level design. The central area is a samey looking maze.6. Why do I have to use an item to know what it does?7. Should have just used some form of a Estus systemBut the game sure is pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: With a title like that you would think this game is some kind of blasphemy or really bad, when it's biggest sin is having nothing new to offer.The areas (and bosses) are all based on elements like fire, ice, and stone because.. you turn.. into stone. The hub is way too big and hard to navigate with lots of paths meanwhile the actual areas being incredibly linear, short and dissapointing.4 weapons, 4 shells, all change your playstyle to the most default boring things possible to the point the actual abilities are things all shells share, making choosing between them a stat related choice rather than a playstyle which is highly dissapointing since each shell has different personalities and story, yet the only thing that differentiates them in actual gameplay is how much HP or Stamina they have.For such a low variety in weapons they sure all act and work the same and those that don't go out of their way to be annoying to use. If you have the dlc you have access to a weapon that literally gives you I-Frames while attacking (at the cost of being quite buggy) so, if you want to have a breeze just buy that dlc I guess.The story is just your characters and discovering who they were before they died. How? by getting upgrades in the xp tree and reading lore. NPC questlines are few and often related to the character you're using, but the only way of changing characters is by walking to the hub so you quite literally have to walk from one corner of the map to the other with a character you either have unleveled or just dont like using and the enemies never lose aggro so you're forced to kill all of them too. Cool on paper; obnoxious in action.Mortal Shell is one of those games that the more I played, the more I disliked it. It's a game so lacking in content and originality that the DLC adds a mode where you replay the entirety of the game but receive loot (passive abilities) that modify your stats in a sort of roguelike fashion. Your reward? recolors of the characters as "skins" and yes, there is an achievement to get them all. To get them all, you need to do a minimum of 50 runs, each run being 1h+ if you're speedrunning it.If you're hungry for a souls game, skip this one.There's nothing great here.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Clocking in 10 hours, I have finished mortal shell and have moved on to new game plus. This is accounting for exploring all the nooks and crannies and trying to find all the secrets. You should be looking to spend about this much time excluding the DLC. ===============================================================================================I personally thought this game would be reviewed much better and found some of the criticisms to be out of place. I saw a lot of the typical criticisms in souls like games where some people just need to git gud (kinda like Sekiro on initial release)I will address some of these faulty complaints. (Keep in mind only 15 people worked on this game)-Enemies turn on a dime: This is the most common complaint i see being harped on about in the reviews. While the enemies turn quickly they most certainly aren't so quick to where you can't get behind them and strike. Some also claim that you can't run past them due to this. I tested this and I was able to run through the games longest stretch of enemies without taking a single point of damage by simply rolling past the enemies when they'd try to attack (on my first attempt). -It's Clunky: While this can be mostly seen as a subjective feature. I think the game does a good job of making combat feel fluid, your attacks come out right when you tap and can be chained from light to heavy to light to do interesting combos. You can also harden mid attack and the game encourages this system to be used in such a way. If you don't harden while using attacks you're going to have a bad time, but hardening comes out smoothly and can be done in any animation. -Parrying is inconsistent: I personally didn't have much a problem with this, you can parry an enemy pretty easily they just have tricky wind ups that are hard to read (I like that because then it would be too easy). And some attacks can't be parried and will flash red.-Hardening requires precise execution: I think this is a ridiculous thing to complain about, especially because hardening can be done in a split second and can be held as long as you want. You can actually just harden and wait for the enemy to strike you before dealing a good beating if that's what you want. -Enemies disappear: This is a valid complaint and enemies that are in the distance do tend to disappear and pop in when they're already swinging at you. Needs to be fixed. -Healing is weird: I did not have much of an issue with it, I think parrying to gain back health is a good system as it encourages risk-reward gameplay. And to be completely forward if you play as Eredim and you die often it's really just your fault. ================================================================================================NOW MY ACTUAL REVIEW:1. Sounds: This game sounds phenomenal, you can hear the minute details of the background, lutes being played by brigands, frogs croaking, your armor clacking and your boots stepping on the mud as your weapons ruck around. It's all really well made and has great positional audio and real quality sounds along with some deep humming sounds with some real depth to it. I'm all about the sounds, while the music really isn't there I can definitely stand by some mostly silent fights with just some very high quality audio. Although there is the option to enable Rotting Christ in the audio menu and it sounds awesome but I almost preferred listening to the silent background and the shuffling of armor and clashing of blades. You really can't beat that satisfying clunk and chunk of blade hitting flesh. ===============================================================================================2. Visuals: Astonishing visuals, for what such a small team this genuinely looks better than many modern triple A titles, both in art style and in the graphics themselves. Especially the shells, all of them are real good looking and have tons of details put into them with my favorite being Eredim who looks like a walking cathedral. I was running this game on an RTX 3070 and boy did I have a blast looking at the visuals. ===============================================================================================3. Level design: I think the level design was overall pretty good in this game, yet Fallgrim needed a bit more land marks. I appreciate confusing layouts that allow one to get lost and feel like you're truly exploring but Fallgrim sometimes felt a bit too much, they could have toned it down a bit. Especially because the first time you explore Fallgrim which is the games main area, you find yourself completely lost almost not even knowing which way is up. ================================================================================================4. Enemies: Enemy design besides the basic brigand guys in Fallgrim is pretty badass. I just wish there was a greater variety of these badass enemies. It often felt repetitive when you had these large open areas where it's just a couple of enemy types. Fallgrim is the worst for this as it has 3. The already boring brigands, brigands with crossbows, and then you have the Sturdymans which are larger brigands that actually have really interesting move-sets and can be quite tough. There's also a mode that enshrouds Fallgrim in a mist that turns all the enemies into either Nocteserpers which are these weird monkey imp creatures that bite your head off or Grisha (could be considered a mini-boss) which are large gorrila monsters with wolverine claws that also bite your head off. But obviously it's going to get boring fighting the same enemy over and over, to the point where I was using the same tactics to kill them. ================================================================================================5.Bosses: The game has 5 Bosses which are all different weapon wielding versions of Hadern. 4 Bosses which are all unique to their corresponding mcguffin zone as I'll call it. And 3 mini-bosses. While seeing Hadern over and over sounds boring it's actually quite fun. I loved the Hadern fights, it's basically some big knight guy that can use your weapons and you have to fight him to unlock that weapon. He relies on the same trick as you which is hardening hence the name. As such around the third time you fight him you're already accustomed to his bait and switch antics. But I will say each weapon he uses makes him vastly different from the last as each weapon has its own unique move-set that can be chained in unique ways. The other 4 Bosses are awesome and all have really unique fighting styles that are both visually appealing and interesting to fight. The 3 mini-bosses are a mixed bag, one is literally just Noctespecter monkey thing but with more health and one or two more moves. One is Grisha that is awesome but it re-used 3 times. And one is Grisha but with two more moves and more health (and a change of appearance). ================================================================================================6.Story: I don't know what any of it means but I'll probably watch a video on it type of story. Yet I will say it has enough deep voiced characters and puzzling sounding people that satisfied my grimy dark souls character love. Everyone sounds like a deep philosophical piece that actually doesn't mean squat, it's great. ================================================================================================7. Characters/Shells/Progression: There are 5 shells in this game each with their own abilities. One that you'll get at the end and probably won't use. One that's utter garbage, one that's too balanced to be any good, one that's the one you're probably going to play, and one that's broken if you play it a certain way. So there's 2 shells in this game and each has their own skill tree that you can invest points into by killing enemies and finding insight/tar. The skills are all meaningful and do help/change the way you play.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried many times over the years to play mortal shell. From PS4 to PC, i have given it much more of my time than i would like to admit. The fact is, the gameplay is incredibly bad. Everything is delayed, from rolling and dodging to parrying and moving. The only thing that isnt delayed is the enemy attacks, half of them are Dark Souls 2 levels of tracking while attempting to master these god awful controls. Once you get the ability to parry (which is VERY easy to miss btw) the game gets slightly better, problem is the parry is inconsistent and has a cooldown, adding a new layer of frustration.It sucks because i think the game has alot of decent ideas going on. Weapons feel good to use, the sound design is great, the style is beautiful at times, its just the card-nil sin of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gameplay ruining an otherwise decent attempt at a soulslike. I got the game for $2, im not going to refund it or never give it another go, but its ability to frustrate is really quite remarkable. On sale, sure why not. $30? HELL NO.

_childDocuments_.review: I have the same problem with this game as I did with The Surge (1). The enemies have a crap ton of health, and can kill you very quickly, and there are a lot of them. The only thing that really puts this below The Surge for me is the lack of healing items. A one time use mushroom that heals a small part of your health bar over 10 seconds scattered all over the map is just not enough, and encouraged me to simply run past enemies rather than fight them and waste my precious healing mushrooms. The heal on riposte is a cool mechanic, but when it requires you to charge a resolve bar that inevitably takes more attacks than your full stamina bar allows to fully charge, it's of limited use, especially against new enemies and bosses. I've played DS1, 2, 3, Bloodborne, Sekiro, The Surge 1, 2, and Ashen, and this is my worst experience with a "Souls-like" with less time played than The Surge (1).
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up for this one but with a lot of compromises. In the end it's a souls-like game which makes it awesome in my book. The graphics are quite polished and I've had no performance issues aside from a few skills glitching in weird ways but nothing game-breaking. Overall the game is rather short. Initially until you get the hang of the combat you might struggle but in a few hours you should be familiar with how your character moves, the movesets of the enemies (which is honestly a little bland) and your combos. Word of caution, the movement is rather floaty, there is a bit of camera shenanigans and once you're used to the combat your biggest nemesis will become sliding off a ledge, of which there are many. Why sliding off? Because most attacks include steps or jumps and while locked on to an enemy, if they step towards you, you will slide/circle around them as you execute the move. If that happens on a narrow bridge it often spells the fall to your death. The skills and items are rather bland an uninspired. instead of chaging character aspects to influence damage, roll speed/distance, poise, defence etc they are single-use attack or parry-based single effect buffs. In the end you will probably end up using none of them as the advantage they provide isnt really worth breaking your combat rythm to consume the item. The biggest issue is that there are 4 basic weapons which you are locked into so the aspect of finding a better weapon somewhere in the world is removed, which I feel makes exploraton empty. The items you find are never equipment, but buffs/currency. The game's basic mechanic of inhabiting a "shell" with a specific set of skills sounds cool but there are only 4 of those with a very limited set of skills, a lot of which are the same across the different shells. This means there are no "builds". If you want to make a tank you cannot experiment with different equipment, you can just inhabit the tank shell and that's it. From a story perspective, the mythos is rather cryptic, but it's a bit insufficient giving you a few glimpses into what it all means but even if you scour the entire game for lore it remains rather limited. I enjoyed it, but I onesty expected more. I understand budget and time restrictions for the developet but this is a great start to a product with potential, not a finished game. It feels like an extended demo.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a satisfactory soulslike experience, also the new DLC it's good, the roguelike mode adds a few more hours of fun. Shells look good, as well the art style, I think the new gameplay mechanics are interesting and some npcs are cool as well.The first three hours, I didn't really understand what I should do or where to go, which is always good for me, it was funny and a really challenging experience I always appreciate. I also admit it's a bit short experience and I would have liked more variety of enemies, story and there were two final or area bosses, I definitely didn't like. The price it's also good, so for all these reasons, more positive than negative, I could say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A classic souls-like game, that is definitely worth the investment (time and money). The harden mechanism makes for satisfying combat and a nice change from the typical block and roll combat of these sorts of games.A couple down sides... This game is not nearly as challenging as a lot of similar games (Dark souls, Nioh ect), with the enemies and bosses being fairly predictable meaning not as many deaths and opportunities to learn from your mistakes (as these games often force!). The only other is that it is a little short - I finished in under 20 hours (although perhaps I missed optional content not discovered!).

_childDocuments_.review: decent "souls-like" some interesting spins and mechanics. certain features of combat were for sure leaning in a very good and positive way. but thats about all the game has going for it. it feels clunky and stiff. many times in getting all the achivements i thought "wow, this is horrible game design". Like being in the 1hp mode and the fact you dont have invincibility in locked animations is horrendous. As well as the lizard dudes dropping out of no where with nearly impossible to dodge attacks. I can see the vision they had and it couldve been amazing if implemented perfectly but I hope they take what they learned with this game and go on to make a much more polished and refined game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: The game has interesting ideas, but it just feels like a very budget Souls-like, that's just minimally done. When playing, there's no real way to "level up" and get stronger, so the difficulty curve is just a cliff into a plateau where once you get a hang of the mechanics, that's it, you've mastered the game. When navigating the game, there's 4 maps, each with their own handful of unique enemies, but all the enemies are very similar, where they all will walk slowly toward you and have some basic light or heavy attack. There's very little overall variation, and every fight ends up feeling very samey.The foundations are there for a really cool game and I did like the overall art direction, just needs more variety, more polish, etc. Given how saturated the souls-like market is at this point, it's hard to really recommend this game, unless you get it for super cheap and have nothing else in the genre to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Many years ago I attempted my first Souls game, Dark Souls 3. After many hours of rage inducing game play, not getting past the first boss and a burst Xbox controller, I rage quitted Dark Souls 3 vowing to never return to the souls genre.Skip ahead a few years and while browsing the steam page Mortal Shell appears in my recommended, intrigued by the cover image I had a better look into Mortal Shell before deciding to purchase the game despite the Souls-Like tag. Like any other Souls game the start was rough, very rough. Died more times than I can count to pretty much everything that could kill me, basic enemies, heights, poison frogs, side bosses and my own stupidity. Normally I would have given up in anger but I found myself drawn to Mortal Shell because of the game itself, the world design, enemy design, the atmosphere all of which are fantastically done and kept me hooked. 16 hours later I have finished 2 of the 3 towers and have maxed out my main shell and weapon and I'm yet to give up, despite numerous moments that caused me to either rage quit or brought me to the edge of rage quitting.Mortal Shell may very well be the game that gets me into the souls-like genre, I cannot recommend this game enough. Also the lute music is amazing, love banging out a few tunes with the brigands, I aim to get a few tunes in with every lute Brigand before I complete the game.In all 10/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: Another decent soulslike game. I only recommend it on sale, and overall I think the negatives outweigh the positives. I bought the DLC, but do not recommend it: I have no intention of playing NG+ or the "virtuous cycle" mode, and the extra shell and weapon are not worth the cost if you don't plan to replay anyway.Positives up front: The harden mechanic adds an interesting twist to combat that I think is interesting and fun, especially once you start levelling your shell(s) of choice to add features to it. The NPC and boss designs are really cool, and the voice acting is mostly on point. The music in boss areas and that you can play on the lute is fantastic, and I like that during a certain game phase, you can tell how close you are to the hub by sound. I think this game had a lot of potential. The world and level design fall flat. Of the ~16 hours it took me to beat the game, roughly 10 of them were just running around in circles in the bland, repetitive hub zone with its four enemy types (or one, depending on game phase). Aside from a few cool moments (Crucix was the one "oh hell yes" from the entire experience), the experience was really dull. Although they could be completed in any order, each of the three dungeons was very linear (little fun to be had from learning the layout or solving puzzles) and only took about 1-2 hours tops to complete. The final boss was ridiculously easy, to the point that I expected it to be a fake-out. Nope, that's really the end of the game.What lore exists is decently interesting. As it stands, I'll probably go read the lore on a wiki, as I know I didn't find everything and I'm not replaying to find it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell : By Triple F"Mortal Shell", the debut title from Cold Symmetry, is a hauntingly beautiful and punishing action RPG that wears its inspiration from the Soulsborne genre proudly. While comparisons are inevitable, "Mortal Shell" establishes itself with a unique identity through its innovative "shell" system, strategic hardening mechanic, and cryptic narrative world.Instead of traditional character classes, "Mortal Shell" offers a variety of "shells" – fallen warriors each with their own distinct playstyle and abilities. The hulking Harros, the Shell found at the outset, boasts high health and slow, heavy attacks. In contrast, the nimble Solomon offers a focus on dodging and quick strikes. Mastering each shell requires adapting your combat approach. This system injects a layer of strategic experimentation, allowing players to tackle challenges with the shell that best suits their playstyle or the situation at hand.One of "Mortal Shell's" defining features is the "harden" mechanic. By instantly turning their shell to stone, players can become temporarily invulnerable. Mastering harden is crucial for survival. It allows for deflecting enemy attacks, creating opportunities for counter-attacks, and even interrupting enemy combos. However, harden comes with a cooldown, forcing players to carefully manage its use and remain aware of their vulnerabilities when the effect wears off. This mechanic injects a strategic dance into combat encounters, rewarding precise timing and calculated aggression."Mortal Shell's" world is shrouded in obscurity. Gone are the grand narratives and overt exposition found in other titles. The story unfolds through environmental details, cryptic item descriptions, and melancholic whispers from ethereal entities. Players piece together the history of the shattered lands and the enigmatic beings that inhabit them. This approach fosters a sense of mystery and compels exploration, encouraging players to delve deeper into the world to satiate their curiosity.The world of "Mortal Shell" is also a masterclass in atmosphere. Lush, decaying environments bathed in an oppressive gloom create a sense of unease and isolation. Enemy designs are grotesque and unsettling, perfectly complementing the game's oppressive tone. The soundtrack is sparse but impactful, with haunting melodies and environmental sounds that heighten the tension during exploration and combat.Combat in "Mortal Shell" is deliberate and unforgiving. Enemies hit hard, and mistakes are punished swiftly. Mastering the timing of hardens, dodges, and parries is essential for success. The game's focus on strategic positioning and well-timed attacks creates a thrilling back-and-forth between player and enemy, rewarding patience and calculated aggression. However, some players might find the lack of character customization and upgrade paths limiting in terms of creating a personalized playstyle."Mortal Shell" is a challenging game, but not an unfair one. Unlike its inspirations, the lack of experience points and traditional RPG elements creates a more streamlined experience. Checkpoints are plentiful, and death doesn't punish players too harshly. While challenging, the game offers a sense of accomplishment when overcoming difficult encounters. However, players seeking a deep character progression system or an easier difficulty might find themselves frustrated."Mortal Shell's" world is compact compared to other Soulsborne titles. While some might find this limiting, the concise design keeps the pacing brisk and avoids the sprawling open-world fatigue found in other games. The focus is on quality over quantity, with meticulously crafted environments and boss encounters that provide a constant sense of challenge and reward.Ultimately, "Mortal Shell" doesn't simply imitate the Soulsborne formula; it builds upon it. The innovative shell system, strategic harden mechanic, and cryptic narrative offer a fresh take on the genre. While the lack of character customization and a shorter playtime might deter some, the game excels in its atmosphere, challenging combat, and unique world-building. "Mortal Shell" is a must-play for fans of demanding action RPGs and a strong debut title from a promising new developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Just not a fun game.The flow of the gameplay is kind of weird. The combat is passive and slow which is super boring. Being fast or aggressive is punished by the game.You can't block in a conventional way. You can 'harden' yourself. This is an ability with a cooldown and it breaks upon being hit. But since enemies are placed in groups of up to 5 or 6 this is pretty much useless against them. One attack breaks your hardening and the next few will definitely hit you right afterwards.As a result fighting them all at once is pretty much impossible. So you have to seperate them. You do this by pulling one out, fighting him 1v1, going back to the group and then repeating that until they are all dead. On the way from Point A to B there are 4 or 5 groups of enemies. Have fun wasting your time.And don't you even think about just 'tanking a hit or two'. You have no proper healing on you. You can find consumables in the world which heal you, like mushrooms that you can pick, but those are limited and they respawn on a timer. Something like an Estus Flakon doesn't seem to exist. So either you go around without healing or you stand in front of that stupid mushroom for an hour to farm those things.And for some obscure reason you don't even get to know what an item does when you find it. You have to use it first to discover that. Found some old mask? I wonder what it does. Teleports you back to your hub, respawns all enemies and thus wipes the progress you just made. Have fun wasting more time to regain all that.Bosses are made difficult by just having a lot of HP. So you fight them by blocking an attack with harden (if it works properly), dodging the follow up, striking back one or two times and then backing up to recharge your ability. Because the boss has a lot of HP it takes long. If you don't have healing items (because you were unwilling to farm them for way too long) then better pray that you don't get hit at all.The controls are too unprecise. Even in the menus it seems to lag behind the inputs. It all feels kinda mushy. For a game that wants to be hardcore and difficult this can not be a thing. Dying because the controls didn't do what you told them to do is completely unacceptable. Combines this with your blocking ability having a cooldown and you're in for a disaster. Enemy attacks, you hit the button, character does nothing, enemy hits you, then you do something. Thanks for nothing. This is infinitely worse when you want to parry enemy attacks. Afterwards you try the same thing again but this time you hit the button sooner to account for the delay. Well now it happens immediately and thus you fail because you hit it too early. Better bring a bunch of luck and frustration resistance. Cause you'll die from this ♥♥♥♥ over and over again.No it's not my hardware. Two controllers do this and mouse and keyboard do it too. It's the game. And it sucks ass.There is no character customization. Apparently you have to find new shells in order to unlock the means to have properly different playstyles. Don't like the starting character? Well screw you because you don't get anything else.The only positive thing is that this game looks pretty. But when the gameplay sucks the graphics won't save it either.Overall just stay away from it. Not even on sale it's worth the money it costs. Thus I'm refunding it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of potential here and there are some parts that are definitely very fun (combat, specifically) but... first of all the game is rather short - the starting area can be confusing at first but it's easy to remember after you run through it once or twice, two out of the three temples are linear, straightforward, and Crypt of the Martyr just felt... disappointing. I'll be honest, if the other two areas were as long and complex as Seat of Infinity I'd probably give this game Recommended instead, because Seat of Infinity was the pretty much the only area I was looking forward to...Lore feels very scattered, the only NPC you can really talk to is Sester Genessa who half the time rambles about something seemingly completely random, and by the end of the game you're just left with a lot of question and a vague feeling that you've completed... something. Weirdly enough most of the coherent lore comes from the DLC, from Twin-Sister. Again, if I got that in the main game, not a DLC, I probably would also give this game Recommended instead.Combat feels very fun and enjoyable... however, the harden ability can get you through the game without getting hit (very important for a no-shell run) and is pretty easy to master whereas parry feels OP... *if* you can get it, because it is sooooo hit and miss sometimes. I'll admit I was never good with parries but there were attacks I knew I should've been able to parry that just went straight through.Finally enemies and difficulty. Each area has a handful of types of enemies but you'll figure them out pretty easily, the bosses are manageable and shouldn't take long to understand the mechanics, it's the final boss (also, it's immediately apparent that the guy giving you the main quest will be the final boss...) that will give you the most trouble and the only enemy where the difficulty is actually high.In conclusion, it's not a bad game, it's a great idea and it's genuinely fun (at times), it's just... not enough, there's too many pieces missing. Get it if it's on sale, I guess (got the DLC for $1.74...)

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if it is on a sale like it is at the time of this post. For full price I probably wouldn't recommend this for some of its issues, but buying it for $12 was worth it, primarily due to how short the base game story is (finished in 12.3 hours, I imagine someone better would finish it much faster). I'd honestly compare the map layout and story-telling style to be similar to absolver, with my understanding being that most of the story is up to interpretation behind "unknowable secrets of the world" type lore. Its combat systems is much more limited compared to elden ring with it primarily being limited to what shell (basically a type of class that determines your base stats and perks) you choose and which weapons you invest in. combat is fun if a bit clunky at times, with a definite learning curve to figuring out hardening and parrying as well as weapons spacing. _childDocuments_.review: [Review at 50 hours in]Great game. It's not a 50 hour game; some people say 10 hours, others 20. If you play like me, it's more like 30 hours. Worth every penny.[Is it Open world?] Yes, it is. Not a gigantic one, but still, it is open world, indeed.[Graphics] Absolutely beautiful, and yet, it is so well optimized that it's not too demanding on my GTX 1070. Meaning: easy on the graphics card whilst amazingly beautiful.[The mood] Very well done. Dark and mysterious. Basically Dark Souls' little cousin.[The difficulty] Hard, but NOT so hard that you'll pull your hair out. You'll be fine. I suspect it's actually easier than Elden Ring.[The story] It doesn't bombard you with lore details that you wouldn't care about. This is the sort of game that whispers in your ear without tarnishing your gaming experience. In other words, not too much lore, nor so little that you'd be confused. Just the right dose. Perfect.I might even be tempted to call this game the 'male' counterpart to Senua's Sacrifice - but maybe I'm just not making sense anymore and that very remark proves it... Maybe I have spent too much time in the swamps of Fallgrim.[So, verdict?] Great game, as I said. It very much feels like all the challenges you'll face are meaningful. You also have a lot of freedom to choose 'how' to go about it. So yes, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't play any games that try to imitate that "Souls" game feel, they always looked rather soulless to me. Maybe I'm wrong, but that's the impression I always get looking at their gameplay.This game, however, was the first game of this kind that caught my attention with its aesthetics and in reality it indeed gripped me in its atmosphere, a combination of its aesthetics, sounds and perhaps context of all things around you.Although the gameplay looked questionable, just as other games of its kind to me, and mostly indeed felt only okay, I did find a style of play with a specific character that ended up feeling quite satisfying, actually making me want to come back for more when initially I thought I would not be finishing the game. The character in question was one of the weaker characters in health, but had perhaps the highest stamina and definitely the coolest evasive moves. It allowed me to be all over my enemies from one spot to the next constantly and effectively being in complete control of all fights due to the high stamina and the strong dodging ability which looks and feels very nice as you phase from one place to another like a ghost... But that's just one of the characters, the one I liked the most.I've seen others complaing about a lack of progression or lack of incentive for it, but I don't think it's lacking. Around the world you have to find characters and weapon with which you can then play with. After getting them, you can upgrade both and need to fight to have enough resources to make upgrades for your characters and weapons. Arguably, the characters are all quite unique in their strengths and upgrading them might not be necessary, but I wanted to get the upgrades to make them stronger and be more likely to dominate all encounters. Even if you choose not to upgrade them, I think it's fine that you don't have to, maybe even great, because as soon as you get a character of certain skills that you like, you don't have to go through mad grind to start enjoying the most important fruits of that specific character, though doing so can definitely be worthwhile. To me an additional incentive for upgrading were also the voiced thoughts / lore fragments about the characters that you receive once you get an upgrade for them – the voice acting here and in other parts is superb and fit this dark, gloomy world very well. As a sucker for good atmosphere, this game sure held my attention.Perhaps you too are not a fan of "souls" games but something about this game caught your eye? In that case, I do recommend trying it, especially now as it goes down to very cheap prices in most stores you can get it in. I don't know how it compares to other games similar to it, but I found that this game was not frustrating to get the hang of things and as such I think most people can enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: One thing to remember is that this is not a Souls game, it is similar in concept but lower budget so it won't act the exact same way. If you have not played a Souls-like game before then don't worry about being bad at the start of this, the combat system takes time to get used to but once you git gud then it'll be really fun to go around. - I enjoy having to figure out the story because this is something entirely new and it is very interesting to learn- I like the "block" system and how it's not like in other games, it's literally your body that hardens as the shield- The center map is somewhat small and it can be confusing so it can be helpful to start out by farming around Fallgrim and just learning the pathways that take you certain places- If you are new to this game I would suggest staying away from the obsidian/floating temple area because it is the biggest and hardest area for the first play-through (in my opinion), it would be better to start with the fire place or the ice place (I can't remember what the names are) as those are much easier and will help you get used to combat.- The weapon you wield should reflect your play style and as you go from area to area, search the living crap out of it for anything you can collect for yourself or to upgrade your weapon- It should also be noted that if you want to land running/jumping attacks, you must attack at the correct distance as to hit your target. Some running/jumping attacks, if activated within a certain range, will miss the target because you will run into them or the target will have moved/dodged out of the way- The system of items is also VERY important for those starting or early game. The more you use an item the more familiar you are with it and eventually you will get a bonus for using items that you are completely familiar with. - Health is another important issue to keep track of, the main source of regenerating health for me is Parrying, if I don't have enough focus to parry then I use Weltcaps, followed by roasted rats. Parrying can be very difficult to learn. What helps me parry is pressing the parry button when the weapon is at the apex of its draw and ready to swing. With that being said some enemies have a VERY quick draw into a swing so I still trip up sometimes there. In my experience playing this game I have had a few bugs when spawning in or the camera bugging out but it has only been like one or two times. I give this game an 8/10.Also Gorf is your friend and DO NOT FEED HIM RATS OR FROGS, I learned that the hard way.

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving this game a thumbs down, not because I found it hard, but because I found it not fun. I love Souls and Souls-likes and many of the best bring something interesting while having a familiar time-tested foundation.I want to like this game, but it fails at those basic foundational mechanics and aspects.1) The parry is satisfying but needs charges to use2) The lighting and colour makes things too difficult to just see - Souls games are dark and have some muted colours, but here it is tuned up too much. The low and medium graphics settings also have this fog layer on screen while high doesn't. Not sure why this is. But this makes it objectively harder to see on low or medium settings.3) The enemy render distance is TOO SHORT - I literally saw enemies get rendered in a few meters from me and that is not acceptable in a game like this. This isn't some special enemy that can go invisible. This is many of the normal enemies.4) There is a reason why all great Souls-likes have a replenish-on-death healing item like Estus flasks. It significantly reduces the frustration for death. And in cases where there is no such thing, the healing item is usually very easy to get. Here neither are the case which increases frustration. In addition to this, the "level-up maiden" has a voice line each time you die which very quickly gets annoying.5) The "Shells" skills and abilities are not shared. So you are incentivized to stick to only one even though they have vastly different stats, and one of the main selling points seems to be the fact that you can change shells/classes on demand.6) It has good graphics but poor art direction. Having high graphics mean nothing when it is not used well. The maps and levels get annoying to traverse, and in some cases, just looks like an amateur level designer made it.Overall, this game could be so much better and fun. It is definitely a decent game. But if you are someone who doesn't have a lot of free time each day, then there are other better Souls-likes or just other better games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I genuinely had a fun time playing this game and I am just writing my personal and purely subjective opinion.The graphics are fine and once you get into it, it can be quite atmospheric.And although i experienced some bugs, they rather made me laugh and gave me a good time....-the game is too short. (In a negative way)I beat the endboss and litteraly looked online if there was anything I've missed.It took me about 14.5 hours actual playtime to beat and i got lost alot during the first 3 hours.I also took my sweet time finding out what I had to do due to me perfectly maneuvering around most of the given clues.Someone with a better sense of orientation and a little more attention to the information found should be able to clear his/her first run in about 10-12 hours.Considering the price, thats too short.-combat feels repetative.Due to the lack in enemy-variety, there is almost nothing new to learn after you've gotten through the first half of the game.Finding and using different weapons (ain't that many) helps but in the end every fight feels the same as you just go infor a few hits, walk backwards a little bit to evade entire enemy combos, then hit again. There are enemies with unique move-patterns but unless its at least a mini-boss you will meet them about 20 times per area  so they get old very quick.Additionaly there is not a single non-boss enemy (mini-bosses included) that doesn't have an easy-to-abuse move, which you can bait out and punish relentlessly.Also half of the mini-bosses are variants of the same enemy which pretty much share exactly the same move pattern.-the traveling of big distances is tiresome. (Some light Spoilers below)The fast-travel options in the game are limited and can not be directly accessed at the start of the game.I won't describe every area I would've liked to fast-travel into or out from, its sufficive to say there are big and winding areas that take a lot of time to get through even with all enemies cleared out.-the game does'nt reach its climax.------------For the reasons above, i would not recommend the game at its current price.I would recommend buying this game IF its either for sale (10€ or less), or if you like playing rogue-likes but hate having to start from scratch each time.The "The Virtuous Cycle" content makes the game more rogue-like. As I said, if you like rogue-likes you might even like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review sits between neutral and mildly recommended, as it was fun to play, albeit short.Ultimately,  is a good effort at adding something new to the Souls-like genre, but the various homages to the  series tend to overshadow the original elements of the game, which can be a double-edged sword when trying to make a mark in an established field as there will be constant comparisons.Being Souls-like, you can expect a decaying world, kooky NPCs, overzealous boss fights and being thrown into a very dangerous environment when you enter the game. The concept of taking on various 'shells' is a novel mechanic to try and mix up playstyles. The hub area also signposts you to explore the world as shells and weapons must be unlocked through discovery (and boss fights), which is a nice touch. The 'hardening' mechanic for blocking hits is unique, as well as the various effects on parrying hits (although timing can be a bit questionable).Healing is limited. Although some items do respawn, the onus is on the player to manage resources through careful and patient gameplay. This isn't gamebreaking and adds additional challenge (mileage varies on whether this is enjoyable from other reviews; I personally didn't mind as it's a common mechanic in other games). Items require usage before knowledge is conferred on what they do - again, an intriguing touch that isn't gamebreaking.I do feel that  could have separated itself a bit more from the  shell (no pun intended) as there are many original design ideas here that could've been expanded on. Clearly a lot of thought has gone into the lore of the shells, weapons, items and currency, and the 'shadow version' of areas ramped up the difficulty. However, the weapon art loading screens are  similar to , as well as the concept of gathering Sacred Glands (read: Boss Souls). Sester Genessa (the bonfire/Firekeeper equivalent), although amusingly sassy at times, does feel like an Emerald Herald applicant who didn't get her first choice of Majula (or second or third choice of Firelink Shrine) and got sent to Fallgrim instead. It's possible to do a homage without reskinning design concepts - I feel this was a missed opportunity given the strength of the unique elements.The DLC adds a more roguelike experience, but otherwise nothing gamechanging. Wait for a further drop in price.  is fun, but with caveats. Best part is repeatedly running over a lute and ruining its tuning. Also, there is a cute cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Just not very good.The production value seems pretty good in terms of art & animation, but  the controls suck.From Ashen to Immortal Planet, I've played some janky & budget souls-likes, but none that felt as straight up bad as this to control. You get stuck on the environment all the time, there is no jump, everything - including the combat - is slow, clunky & awkward. The last hit in any weapon combo might as well not exist, because enemies  punish you for it and the dodge comes out way too late. Even the basic enemies have oddly lurching jump attacks with janky & early hitboxes and all enemies have near infinite tracking. I hate seeing enemies doing a 180° U-turn during a jump attack in FromSoft games, I  hate it in a game as unresponsive & slow as this.On top the game has weird glitches. Enemies sometimes manifest 3-4 meters ahead of you, as if the game has trouble keeping them loaded in or depending on which side you approach an area from. A 2v1 suddenly turning into a 4v1 at a moments notice & out of thin air is not appropriate - especially in a game with survivability this low.Oh, and this is another of those souls-likes that - despite  online functionality - thought it'd be a great idea to have no pause function. I'm a damn adult, make it possible to pause this game so I can answer the phone or door & not have to risk loosing 30 minutes of drudgy, painstaking progress.If your thought-process for making a souls-like is "no pause function", "trudgy combat" & "HARD!!1!" then congratulations & f#ck you.So no. This game is not for me.I would've liked to have seen more, but the visual & audio production value is not worth the pain of slogging through these muddy mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I've made a full playthrough with both Eredrim - with the Martyr's Blade - and Tiel - with the Hammer & Chisel. This game takes inspiration from Demon's and Dark Souls and really cranks it up to eleven on the aesthetical department. Mortal Shell is a really gritty, grimdark game with a booming, somber musical theme accompanying it. Entering Fallgrim for the first time gave me that same sense of dread, curiosity and impending doom as Demon's Souls gave me eleven years ago when I was a noob at these types of games.The combat is fluent, with different shells and weapons catering to various playstyles or builds. However, I do miss the ability to backstab. This game offers you a variety of ripostes, but no backstab. The settings and environments are hauntingly beautiful, and varied outside of the Fallgrim mire. The NPCs are engaging and display a sense of depth and mystery rivaling those from Dark Souls.Although being too short for my liking, this game neatly wraps what I loved the most from the Souls games in a modern package. Although one playthrough took me roughly 12 hours, I decided to play it through again immediately after I was done, with another shell and weapon.Out of the two shells and weapons I tried, as stated above, I did enjoy the fluent, dodge-based combat of Tiel with the Hammer & Chisel. I am also a fan of auxiliary effects, so the poison theme around Tiel and the Hammer & Chisel fits me perfectly!In conclusion: I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the Dark Souls games or just enjoy a well designed, grimdark action RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I "binge-played" Dark Souls 1 - 3.Now I tried it and what shall I say - I ♥♥♥♥♥ like it. It copys many of the great system of dark souls, but it is doing this pretty well. And it is refreshing with its combat and the "shell-system". You can do much less compared to Dark Souls, cuz u just have 4 swords and 4 shells. The shells do just vary in stats: More life, less stamina and vice-versa. And then there is "resolve" as a 3rd stat. You need it for special attacks or parry. You collect it by attacking enemies. This is something FromSoft should copy in the future cuz it is very nice and makes me using special attacks more often - contrawise to Dark souls... And well, you even need 1 Resolve for kicking which is kind of a joke - but ok. And one thing i liked after all these hard from software stuff: It is much easier. There is only one bossfight that i did not kill on first try cuz he was too agile for me. And that is something i adored: An AI-Boss being aware of dodging and and "sneaky-sliding" attacks. That fight was super fun!And it is much shorter. If you get to know the Fighting System fast (Which you will, if u finished a souls game) you can easily finish this game in 10 hours (NG+ NOT included).TL; DR: Buy it on sale if u like Dark Souls and wanna have a more chill game as a change.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a soulsborne veteran and a fan of the genre, so when this game came out I got instantly interested in. It's hard to not compare this game with its "father", since Mortal Shell is reportedly inspired by Dark Souls. Still, it manages to build its own personality. I kinda missed the character customization but the whole individuality of the game revolves around the shell mechanic, and it is awesome. The graphics, scenery and atmosphere are beatiful(as you expect a souls-like to be) and gives a reaaaally creepy vibe, which fits good to the game and genre. The armor and weapons are badass and really well designed. And we are talking about an indie game developed by around 15 people, so it's just incredible what they've managed to pull out with the amount of budget and labor they had. The dark atmosphere has as protagonist the soundtrack that does a great job building an atmosphere of tension, especially in the post boss fight moments, when the fog appears and you must return to the Fallgrim Tower. Still, it has its cons. Aside from a few upgrade items, exploration isn't very rewarding, as there isn't much loot to collect, and this takes away some of the soul-like exploration essence. There are only 6 boss fights in the game, and none of them are very memorable, I'm hardly sure there are 6 at all, I may be missing some. The overall gameplay feels a little bit clunky, specially talking about the camera, which has always been an issue in souls-like games, but in this game it's a bit worse than general. For example, when you have the camera locked on an enemy and you try to roll you just don't have the slightest idea of where are you going to, and it sucks since the most part of the game combat happens in close range. The graphic settings are really bad, if you do not have the shadows settings on High or Ultra you have to strugle a lot changing the brightness everytime you enter an area that has a different lightning because the lightning itself doesn't have the slightest consistency so you'll have to keep adjusting the brightness according to if you're either seeing something in the area you are or not. And it sucks A LOT, since in a lot of boss fights you'll get teleported to a different area, and if the lightning in the area is bad you can't change middle game since it doesn't have pause, so you have to go to a safe area JUST TO CHANGE THE F***ING BRIGHTNESS.Despite those technical issues, I do recommend this game to any souls-like fan, since this game has a lot to offers and it's a great experience after all.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming little soulslike that does enough interesting things to the basic Souls formula. Your parries are your heals, but you have to earn your parries by being aggressive. You also have hyperarmor on demand, even mid-attack, which also rewards aggression. Instead of linear character levels there are shells that are basically builds you can swap at will - you are never stuck with one archetype and minmaxing is impossible.The art direction is gorgeous, courtesy of Vitaly Bulgarov, one of the most renowned 3d artists alive (he did Alita and Ghost in the Shell, among other things). It's consistently sleek, variating between moody minimalist and over-the-top Giger-esque dark fantasy.   Oh, and do turn on the optional black metal soundtrack for the boss fights, it makes all the difference.  Takes off a bit slowly, but if you endure the first hour, it all clicks and becomes enoromous fun.

_childDocuments_.review: i'll refrain from using the term "souls" to describe this one but it's a genuinely great experience that feels like a D&D campaign or some other homebrewed project that someone made for you. generally best played alone and when you're undistracted to really feel it and get into it.the environments are pretty fantastic, every character instills a sense in me of "i should be playing them more, i feel bad that i'm not" which most games can't really do to the metamancer within me. every weapon feels fantastic and generally "like it should", if you'd like a piece of inspiration for how a big as hell weapon with a complex and varied, yet not entirely without weaknesses (as opposed to the " do x task" found in some other games, like the eponymous souls) moveset & string of animations should look, Mortal Shell nails it better than pretty much anything else ever. writing also hits just right for me. it isn't a flawless god masterpiece of a game that fulfills buzzword reviewer criteria and it certainly isn't "triple A" in terms of raw budgeting and everything else that entails, but it's a genuinely good experience and i'll always attest to it just being a great thing that someone spent their time on earth making.

_childDocuments_.review: I started this game hoping for a great souls-like with a unique twist.  For starters the harden mechanic is genius and is one of the best parts of the game.  There are 4 weapon types and only one of them actually makes you feel powerful.  There are 4 shells but only one has the stamina to allow more that one combo before backing off for 30 seconds.  The game does have the brutal difficulty you might expect, however it isn't done in an engaging way.  Every enemy of the game is beaten in the exact same way.  Hold back until your stamina is full, do 1-3 attacks, harden to avoid the counterattack, hold back for 30 seconds, and repeat.  Out of the three temples one of them is invalidated by a single ability from the best shell and another one is a massive, empty, poorly thought out mess that punishes you for exploring by ambushing you the moment you pick up the item.  (This is a repeated thing not just a once off.)  After beating the boss in each temple the game goes into "Fog Mode" and rearranges the temples to make it difficult to leave.  Essentially punishing you for completing your objective.  Your objective being completely obscured and barely even existing outside of: "Beat the Game".  Despite all of this harsh criticism, I have more that twenty hours and two playthroughs down and am considering a third.  I genuinely don't understand what kept me going through this game for multiple runs but it keeps me coming back.  The visuals are absurdly good, the alternate soundtrack absolutely rips (please use the Blood Christ soundtrack it's the best), and it kept me going for multiple playthroughs.  However, the difficulty is poorly constructed, the freedom to choose the way you play is punished often, and the game is strangely buggy for being months out from release, and it spends far too much time punishing you for playing the game.  Despite all that I still find it captivating.  My rating is a 4/10.  Just below average enough that I really can't recommend it strongly but not so bad I don't think it shouldn't be played if you find it interesting.  Given it's around 10 hours of playtime and I couldn't see paying more than $20 for it in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing an offline mmorpg with terrible combat and repetitive combat loops along with buggy enemy attacks, movement and animation. this is your game. Otherwise, just get a fromsoft game.The combat is clunky at best and most enemies you fight are just minion from dota with some frame 1 buggy attacks. The weirdest decision they made was to make the weak enemies that hit you with a wooden club on your hardened steel armour, do more damage than a big boss with a flaming steel hammer. That's right, if you get hit with a wooden stick you'll be running away faster than getting hit with an ancient hammer of hardened steel forged in the volcano of demons or something. Yeah. good job guys.The voice acting is mostly good, but sometimes it can feel like a middle schooler writing a narrative essay while using a thesaurus. Characters randomly giggling or just emo. None of the characters feel like they actually live in this world, they feel like they're all short stories from people who want to sound deep.Combat could be summed up with either left click, right click, left click, or something close to that. The only ability worth using is the kick. The kick looks like a toddler punting the shin of an adult, and yet it's the bane of any enemy who's shin you kick. Letting you wail on them for hundreds of damage. The parry system is absolute trash. Not only does it not work for 90% of enemy attacks either based on what they attack with or the angle your character is based on their position (yes literally, it's clunky and useless). When you finally land a parry, you can choose from a few things, the healing is probably the best as if you're trying to parry, you're going to be taking more damage than if you just dodged. So better heal back the damage from all the clunky missed parries.The Art style is amazing, the world is extremely alluring, if only there was a game built around it. I feel whoever designed the game created the world and the art first and then had a sudden realisation that they had to add enemies and a story, then rushed out a sloppy mess.Consumable items are a huge mess. The inventory feels like a junk drawer that you sift through. Not only this but there's no reliable way to heal other than grinding enemies at the starting area and buying rats to eat, or foraging around for mushrooms which goes without saying is a horrible way to balance a healing system. I'd imagine they wanted the parry to act as the primary healing mechanism, but it's actually a worse than useless tool for that. given the frame 1 animation skips of enemies, timing parries is unreliable, and enemy attack patterns and attack range do not lend itself to learning timings if even possible as certain enemies seems to have no problem attacking right through the parry even if the talisman doesn't glow. Not to mention the talisman sometimes only glows hot red when the attack lands which is comically bad.4/10. Has potential and I hope if a sequel gets made they really learn from the downfalls of this game. Animations are skipped, clunky and unresponsive. The main combat revolves around hitting light heavy light, repeat. and the most interesting parts of the game like combat are held down by poor game design. The world locks you out of changing your playstyle unless you want to drop everything and walk back to the starting areas just to access the anvil, shells, etc.I'm trying my best to give this game a good review because I did have fun with it, but I can't imagine recommending this game to anyone else as the combat which is a focus in these games; is dreadfully unresponsive and boring. Thank you for reading, have wonderful day.
