_childDocuments_.review: An OK soulslike. Nothing to get excited about, just OK.Authors should have done more to distinguish their games from Dark Souls in terms of style, themes and atmosphere. I understand, if it is not broken - don't fix it, but this is way too derivative, imo. Combat however is pretty solid, and fairly distinct. I like how punishing levels of damage enemies deal work together with reliable defensive options, like rolls with tons of iframes and harden. I like that parry mechanics seem to be really well fleshed out. Despite being optional parries can be an important part of every boss and regular mob fight, which is certainly a fine improvement over From Softs souls games.I also like how exploration in this games seems to be as much of a challenge as bosses, and I don't only mean learning the map and how to get around. Relative scarcity of risk free healing options makes long stretches without save points or shortcuts quite tense, and gently nudge you towards being careful with health management.I wish play style options were more balanced. Some people(including devs of this game) say or imply that 4 shells(charactes) are all viable choices that suit different playstyles. That is a blatant lie. Two of them are just inferior to the other two. If I said "hey, there is a character with a really safe roll and a lifebar that can take a beating and another one that dies and two hits, but gets a huge progressively stacking damage buff until you die. Is that balanced?" - most people would say - "Sure. Risk - reward, that is what it is all about".But some poor designer in the developers office got hit on a head one too many times and said - "Wait, I know. I have a great idea! Let's do the opposite - now beefy boi also gets to do ungodly amount of damage and risk less due to how beefy he is, ans squishy boi has a really safe roll to save him from all the dangers."Well, it was not a good idea. It was terrible, actually. Beefy boi is INSANE. It was my second playthrough, and I literally did not die once since getting him. Squishy boi, on the other hand is garbage. Other classes rolls are safe enough, you don't need them to be safer, since you mostly take damage not due to mistiming a roll, but due to being caught out by an attack in the middle of the animation without get-out-of-jail-free card that is harden. Squishy boi is just as good as anyone else in that regard, which overall turns into a big fat suck for him, and a gold star for beefy boi.Idea of having perks and lore all organized together in a neat ring also is pretty bad. Hell, now we need like 10 perks for each character. I know, just throw a ton of useless filler in there. Like half of the all perks either synergize really poorly with the shells concept (like a squishy boi having an extra damage chance on parry, which is the highest risk option, and can often lead to his untimely death, or beefy boi gettin a beefy attack after death which he will probably never usesince he is OP AF) or are just useless (like a chance to be immune to knockdown that didn't proc once during a whole playthrough). Less is more.Speaking of less is more. Half of all shells are underwhelming when compared two others, sure, but wait till you hear about weapons. You know those pictures with swords and stats made in paint, a sword with attack speed of 50 and a damage of one and another one with 50 damage and an attack speed of one? Well, when devs are answering that pic they say that 50 damage one is op, and need to be nerfed. To 2 damage. Sigh. Seriously, slower weapons are hot garbage in this game. For some reason they are not only riskier to use, but also deal less DPS, cause that makes sense.In conclusion - a nice soulslike with potential, but with not much content and a lot of silly decisions. Buy it on a sale or smth.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made by a small studio, and whilst I appreciated some of its ideas and obvious inspirations, it was weighed down by too many factors for me to be able to confidently recommend it.The graphics were good, and the level design was mostly fine, with a central area and hub connected to the main dungeons. I appreciated the freedom to approach any area of the game you wanted, and I enjoyed the dreary atmosphere. The enemy variety is decent, but notably lacking in the main central zone.The combat is very slow, with the core feature being the harden mechanic, which is essentially a shield that can be used during attack strings. This is an interesting concept, but leads to the combat being incredibly monotonous, where you enter a combat loop of attack - harden – wait, until an enemy is dead.Most of the bosses in the game were underwhelming with very little attack strings, and the mini-bosses were simply basic enemies with increased health pools.The shells are essentially pre-set stat builds for your character with unique skill trees. Outside of some outliers, most of these skills are uninteresting. There are also 5 unique weapons if you include the one from the DLC, and they were all pretty fun to use, and felt very distinct from one another.The DLC content is a roguelike version of the game, and was probably the most fun I had with the game, although I think it could have been more ambitious with the buffs you can acquire.6 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the game is a little bit clunky.Yes the game is a bit short.It's not as polished as Dark Souls 1 was when it was released.And I don't care.The game has a lot of details and love put into it.You get different "characters" to play as, different parts of the world to explore and actually quite a lot of different enemy designs.Playing the Lute actually makes you more proficient with it over time and some characters may even react to you playing the Lute, which, yeah it's not important for the game, but it helps make the world feel more real. The movement of some NPC's looks VERY REAL, almost to a point where I have to say I don't think I know any other game where random NPC's move naturally - on this small aspect - to me at least - it can rival GTA V (I know it's a super weird comparison but I can't think of a better example because people in GTA V CAN move very realistically). And while not always the case, certain NPC's should be watched from a distance to admire their movement.Again, the game isn't perfect, but it's fun to play.You also gotta take into consideration that the studio was (I think) around 20 people when the game was made. Like, how did you guys manage that?? Graphics are also quite good. My hopes are that this company can make more games like this. Maybe a bit longer, but with the same amount of detail.Tl;dr - if you have the money to buy the game, please give it a try. I think this company deserves the money for what they have made and I hope to see more of them in the future. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Played it quite a bit when it first came out a year ago. Back for the DLC.If you're interested in playing this game, don't pay attention to a lot of these negative reviewers who've barely played. I can tell you as someone who has played this, a lot of these reviewers just haven't taken the time to learn the game mechanics. They have been ignoring tutorials that pop up on their screens. They are literally spouting misinformation about the game.SOME of the complaints are a little more understandable. Auto tracking is a thing, but its no worse than soulsborne games. The level design is pretty open and can be confusing early on, but the game does have noticeable landmarks and will point you in the right direction. You pay attention and you'll find your way. Just takes a little bit of time.Some people might not like the healing items. Legit complaint. Can't really argue that. I don't think it's bad, but I understand that people have different opinions. To explain a little further, you pick up mushrooms off the ground that spawn in specific places. They are on a 10 minute or 15? minute timer. Can't remember. These are your main healing item and they are not instant heals like flasks. They are a heal over time. You can consume multiple of them to heal faster. But they are not instant, so if you are about to die, they will not save you if you're gonna take another hit in the next couple seconds. Once I got the hang of kiting, hardening, parrying, ripostes, and dodges, I found I was barely using healing items anyway. You have a lot of tools at your disposal to not have to use that many heals.Parrying is not that hard. Game warns you when you can't parry. Different enemies have different attacks with different speeds. Learn your enemies attacks and you find your parry windows. Some enemies have very fast attacks, and are more difficult to parry, but you can just dodge, kite, harden and wait for them to do a slower attack you are more comfortable in trying to parry. Takes practice. Probably won't be that good at it if you've only been playing 2 hours.Stamina is another complaint. Didn't find this to be an issue. Again, you play, you learn how many attacks and dodges you can do with the various shell and weapon types. Easy to mess up and expend too much stamina, leaving yourself open to attacks because obviously, you can't doge without stamina. Well, you can harden. Your stamina recharges while hardened. You can also parry, which will do damage, give you health, and replenish stamina during the animation. Only issue is if you've expended all your stamina and the enemy is about to do an attack you can't block or parry(which is rare). But you learn to be careful around those enemies and not expend all your stamina.The game is definitely not too hard. If anything, between dodging, parrying, and hardening, it's much easier than soulsborne games IMO. You just have to take the time to learn how the combat works and you're good to go. Game only gets easier as you level up your various shells and weapons.So again, most the complaints I've seen about this game are from people that only have a couple hours under their belts and haven't actually given the time to learn the games systems. Most the streamers I've watched play this game recently are having a blast with it because they're actually playing long enough to learn how to play it.My 2 cents. o/

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a soulslike game with a few twists. You are a soul inhabiting empty shells and every shell is a somewhat of a class, like knight, assassin, support and tank. Instead of regular block, you “harden” aka turn to stone and you can combine that with various attacks.Pros:- strong gameplay foundation- beautifully dark and twisted environmental and enemy designs- cool twists on standard mechanics- lore- fun- polishedCons:- pretty short (around 12 hours to complete)- finding/farming healing items is time consuming and boring- no magic (if you like that playstyle)Neutral:- hard and confusing at first, but that's to be expected and it becomes easier as you progress- no explanation for almost anythingThe game has a DLC The Virtous Cycle which gives you a roguelike mode, a new shell and a new weapon. If you like the base game, I would definitely recommend getting it.Made by a small studio, you can feel the passion and work put in. It's only 25 euros and even cheaper on sale. If you like soulslike games, this is a strong recommendation. Support indie gaming and we'll get more gems like this one.Score: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a big Dark Souls fan I really enjoyed this game. I was a little hesitant before I started but the game is solid. It is souls like but not overly difficult having said that enemies can present a challenge at times. Again the bosses aren't too difficult and can be slightly repetitive as they all follow the same formula (whittle down their health bar, then they have a phase 2 but its the exact same fight). However the designs and concepts behind them is really interesting. I'd love to see this universe that has been created by the devs expanded on as this game is really really good platform for them to build upon. You can explore the world at your own leisure, use different weapons, upgrade those weapons and play as different shells. There are secrets to find, lore to gather and the world feels pretty polished, it doesn't just feel like a landscape to run around trying to find the next boss. Again combat is souls like and feels pretty good and fluid as well as introducing a couple features which makes the game the unique. Worth the purchase. 3/5!

_childDocuments_.review: Had high hopes, but turned out disappointing.This is a spoiler free review (to the best of my ability)Mortal Shell was fun to play, although it didn’t offer much. The hardening ability was original and creative. And the skill tree was limited but satisfying. The different “shells” one could inhabit, added a hint of customization and strategy, but it felt very restrictive.Unfortunately, the drawbacks outweigh the benefits. For starters, the map was confusing and difficult to memorize. The parry, to me at least, was difficult to time. A small variety of items and weapons to add to the game’s experience. The variety of enemies available were small too. Some voice acting was poor and the general dialogue was cheesy. The overall story was predictable and generic. I would suggest other soul-like games.3/10 - Not unplayable, but I suggest spending your time elsewhere.-BigBlaBlue

_childDocuments_.review: (MSH) is a third-person Souls-like set in a grim-dark fantasy world. Players impersonate a mysterious being capable of manipulating bodies, called Shells, and use their abilities to its own advantage. Thrown in this obscure land without any other clue, the Foundling starts a journey as a stranger in a strange land.Solid animations, impact behind hits and a general slow pacing make MSH's combat realistic and meaty. Forget button-mashing or spam of any kind: here every swing or action generally takes a lot longer than in most other Souls games, but still feels fluid and well done at all times instead of clunky.Despite level linearity, exploring has good rewards in the form of consumables, weapon upgrade materials, hidden NPCs and lore fragments. Those who spend extra time looking for secrets and remotely-located items will have significant advantages, as it should be.Each weapon and character feels very distinct, with markedly different movesets, speeds, statistics and abilities. The combinations of various Shells and weapons can lead to interesting synergies, experimenting with them is recommended to grasp each nuance.Sadly enough, one specific Shell and one particular weapon dwarf all others as far as combat effectiveness goes. The game remains perfectly viable with all characters or arms, but many of them are just worse than what is, evidently, the best choice overall. Some Shells' abilities combined with specific weapons also may result in pretty "broken" outcomes, going as far as stun-locking bosses with certain combinations of skills. Balance needs a lot of work.No weapon, character or stats of any kind on anything, except a few consumables. How much damage does this weapon do exactly? How much Poise does this Shell have? How much chance does this ability have to trigger? All these and more questions simply can't be answered as the game doesn't provide statistics most of the time.The early game simply throws players into a frustrating setting without (yet) the ability to parry, no consumables, no fast travel and most importantly no idea about what to do whatsoever. In this part, weak Shells will find a multitude of enemies in a labyrinthine location that will be quite frustrating to traverse for the first 2-3 hours. After that things improve, luckily.Except for Fallgrim, the first zone, most other ones except one in particular will be corridors with very few deviations, no verticality and limited shortcuts. There is a stark contrast between the almost confusing layout seen earlier, and the linearity of other areas. Those seeking complex layouts will be disappointed with hallways filled with enemies and little else in the way of interaction.Is performed on foot, with the ability to fast-travel only being unlocked with a specific item one may or may not ever find. Save for the central area, most other zones will have linear layouts with some small side zones containing additional items or upgrades, however less intricate than most other souls-games out there. As customary in the genre, there is no map nor pause. Sester NPCs act as "bonfires" and allow saving progress, other than respawning players upon death, which ensues in losing all Tar (souls) which can then be recovered, as usual for souls games.Only offers melee options in the form of four distinct weapons, found in each zone and awarded after defeating a hostile Shell wielding them - a special, limited-use ranged weapon can also be unlocked eventually. Each murder tool can be upgraded at a Forge with Acid (better damage) and two unique items each (found in the world), that unlock special active abilities that are different for each weapon and cost Resolve (mana) to activate - in turn gained from dealing damage to foes. MSH has no blocking, instead once unlocked Parrying becomes the only way to deflect enemy attacks, again using Resolve (and good timing!) to produce different effects such as healing the player or inflicting status effects to the foe.Other than weapons, Shells (characters) have distinct playstyles, each with diverse amounts of Resolve, defense, stamina and health. Every interchangeable shell has a dedicated skill tree composed of both active, passive abilities that further emphasize a definite style, and each can use every weapon without penalties. The Hardening ability is a highlight in combat, as it allows players to stop any animation to Harden their Shell, voiding incoming damage from the next blow and at the same time resume movement - timed correctly, this can be used to deliver a hit right after enemy attacks. Other than that, combat has the same core rules as any Souls-like so learning patterns, nailing the timings, managing stamina and using i-frames correctly are the keys for success. Notably, upon "death" players have a chance to return to their broken Shell and gain an extra life with full HP - or die trying.Can be performed on-the-go in a limited way, such as swapping consumables present in the quick slots, examining their descriptions, or viewing effects. The bilk of this is however done at Sesters, living bonfires that allow investing Tar and Glimpses (skill points) to upgrade a character's ability tree, the only form of progression. Some NPCs offer trader services and usually have unique, limited arrays of wares not present anywhere else or hard to gather. Some of them also offer other utility services or have requests that if fulfilled often unlock unique rewards. Shells and weapons can be switched either at the central hub, or by using specific items found in the world or from merchants. Also, MSH has no Estus equivalent: healing is gained only from consumables or successful Healing Parries once available, a choice not everyone will like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically trying to be dark souls but the devs did everything wrong with it and doesnt understand the essence of dark soul and what makes it great, they just threw in everything that is considered "difficult" in a souls game and make it 50 times worse, such as no checkpoint even after exploring what seem like ages.I dont need to explain much as other negative reviews basically said it all but I'm gonna add one more point.At the very beginning of the game, on the first map called pilgrim, you are in a swampy forest, its the first level and already the map is very confusing, too many detours and you get lost easily not knowing where you are or where you're suppose to go. I played all the soulsborne games and sekiro and also other souls-like game like nioh 2, the map of those games are huge but not confusing cause you know where to go next, this game however, just the first map alone is already over complicated. Not to mention, there are no other checkpoints(i.e bonfire) other than the starting area even after exploring for 1.3 hours without dying.I think the devs took the idea of BlightTown from the first dark soul where that map is a really long map and only 1 checkpoint but here is the thing, BlightTown may be long but its a linear map with obvious route while this game has a humongous map with no obvious route whatsoever and no checkpoint. _childDocuments_.review: Very "Meh" game, but I appreciate the effort for a team of around 10 people.On one hand this is a very unique souls-like with it's primary focus on blocking which makes some fights very satisfying and fun, the boss of the Ice Dungeon in particular. Building charges for special attacks, knowing when to attack and when to dodge, parrying to get health back, knowing when to harden either to keep on attacking or manage stamina, It can be a lot of fun. The enemy variety is great and so is the visual variety between the overworld and it's 3 dungeons, and some of the Bosses are quite great with all of the mini bosses being at least decent. I really like the shell system I think it provides great variety for repeat playthroughs with essentially different characters. although Eredrim is significantly more powerful than the rest.On the other hand Mortal Shell feels awkward to play with it's inconsistant parry timings that not only wary on enemies but also on different attacks, luckily this is my only gripe with the combat but I found myself not parrying at all later. This game also only has 4 main bosses, quite a low amount, and while there are mini-bosses I wish each dungeon had it's own mid-way mini boss but only the ice dungeon has one. There are also only 3 main dungeons connected by an overworld, I wouldn't really complain about the lenght of the game but If I had to choose I'd rather they make another 4th dungeon since the 3rd dungeon overstays it's welcome by way too much, it's at least triple the size of the other 2 dungeons.All of these were so far personal nitpicks, but there are a few things worthy of critique in this game. First of all the overworld start out fine but once you beat 1 or 2 dungeons every single enemy on the map turns into an Imp, these enemies ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck, they are fast so you must chase after them, they also come in groups and fighting them in groups pretty much guarantees damage done to you, but the worst part is even if you run past them the game has several gotcha' moments when you are shown a tell for around half a second, before they jump on you and take at least 20% of your health away, in an animation that lasts for around 5 seconds, massive waste of time and It encourages running past the overworld even more so than if it just had the regular enemies that had nothing wrong with them. The second point I'd like to talk about is actually the bosses, the Fire boss, and the Ice boss are great, but the Final boss and the 3rd boss are quite bad.Spoiler alert: the Final boss in this game is pretty much just a worse version of the Elden Beast, constantly running away from you in a game where your movement speed is already slow, at least he closes the distance afterwards so you don't have to but overall a disappointment.The 3rd boss just feels unfinished, just take a look at that phase 2 cutscene I was laughing my ass off and I still don't know what is supposed to be going on but it's animated about just as well as that one horrible Czech movie from 2018. His moveset is uninspired, but most importantly after one of the longest dungeons in the genre you would expect some epic boss fight but all you are left with is the most generic and unfinished boss in the game. This is a game I'm very split about, on one hand the first 2 dungeons and their respective bosses are very good, the combat is very solid, and the sound design and graphics are impressive. On the other hand this game is filled with unfinished or unrefined ideas, the entire 3rd dungeon which is quite a long portion of the game feels extremely unfinished and barron along with it's boss and unfortunately this applies to the game's finale as well, on top of the change to the overworld which I still don't understand why.

_childDocuments_.review: No minimap, no directions, no story, no interesting NPCs, no level progression, no point in farming Tar (currency). No fast travel, no QoL improvements. No atmosphere, no innovative game play, no new mechanics. 4 bosses, 4 weapons, 4 armors that plays just about the same. Each map is played "twice" because you have to go in reverse, the 2nd time is in the dark. The map designs are linear but also as confusing as a poorly designed, dimly lit maze.This game tries to capture the feeling of soulsborne games but neither the aesthetics or gameplay is inspiring. Every single character is forgettable, especially the bosses. The visual design is bland, border-lining on annoying with how difficult it was to see.Examples: What's the point of poison damage if you can only access it via a specific shell and a specific upgrade but also you lose it after getting hit once? Poison damage appeared twice on the first map and never came up again. What's the point of bear traps if there's no counter play? It's there to be annoying in three areas of the first map and never came up again. There's an ice level but the ice did nothing, a fire level but the fire did nothing, and a black tower level where the blackness did nothing and the tower did nothing. Are we in purgatory? Are we in the afterlife? Is this a messed up, decayed world? Who knows! The bosses in Elden Ring/Dark Souls were compelling because there's some motivation behind them. In mortal shell, they might as well have been chilling in their own home until the player comes kicking down the door and attacking them for no reason. The final boss is an eldritch legless chicken and their entire AI consists of 'Spam AoE loop'  and 'When within player attack range, move away and repeat AoE loop.'If the devs or the publishing company sees this review, I'm going to need you to do me a solid and donate 3 buckeroos to sick kid's hospital because you don't deserve my money.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10  (Average:7.9999999~)My comments in short: Good game, loved the animations, game length is pretty long. Map is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Combat is so satisfying, there are some bugs or errors in making the game (I think) it's playable but just sometimes the powerups don't really work (I think :) ...)Review:I got this on a pretty high discount. The reason why I bought this is because after playing god of war on my playstation I wanted some more RPG games like dark souls and assasin creed. I played dark sould before and it's pretty good, but it didn't have a discount so I was afraid to regret and I saw this. Mortal Shell, I looked through the gameplay on youtube and it did look really well made and the reviews were mostly positive but some of the bad reviews did give me a second thought. After I bought this game I realized that after so many hours of playing god of war I really messed up my concept between adventure games and souls like games. I know that comparing God of war to this game seems pretty unfair because my pc isn't a gaming pc so I could only run it in mid quality on 50 fps, with motion blur on it's worse. I did watch people playing full ultra quality and motion blur on youtube and it looked pretty much the same. I like how it has smooth combat, the animations were pretty overwhelming, it's really fun using my swords.  One bad thing that I've noticed that if you get the hang of the rhythm you can get through the game pretty quickily and the boss is just easier to kill than the little ugly monsters, it goes something like this: shift W, right click, and space+S, and then repeat and repeat, if the boss look like it's about to hit you you can always harden by pressing ctrl which is a cool feature. Another bad thing about this is that the mushrooms (im talking about both of them) is just so rare, they do spawn after each time sipping the divine (going to the witch which literally scams me everytime, half the time I don't think the powerups work lmao) but there is probably just 50 or so in the who entire game where mushrooms spawn, and the names for weapons, consumables and other stuff is just too confusing, to be honest until now I still don't even know the name for the green stamina bar at the bottom (if you know pls tell me). Last bad thing is that the map is such a maze, I wanted to swear at it everytime I get lost, and I had to use half of my glimpses to teleport me back to the uglyass witch. The good things tho, is that this game is a new experience to me, first time that I've dug into a souls like game. If you follow the guide it'll be very easy to get through and finish the game, but I just loved how the combat is, so smooth so satisfying and I even wanted to copy some of them myself. Another good thing is that this game has one of the coolest animations I've ever soon, probably better than God of War even tho I have mid quality on, I loved how the guy puts his hand on the shell's head and the yea (can't remember what he did lol). It's on a bargain right now go buy it, you won't regret, just a couple of more hours of your life grinding and having fun. Ratings:10/10 Animation8.5/10 Combat5/10 Map7/10 Story line (there wasn't a fixed story)8/10 Mechanics (loved it)9/10 Playable (it's playable even on a crappy pc just motion blur and v sync makes my pc kinda struggle)

_childDocuments_.review: This is like the colder more methodical step brother to Dark Souls. Before I get too much into it, YES, I do recommend this game... How could I not?It has the graphics, the sounds, and the game play befitting of a true-blue souls like.I said it is colder than Dark Souls because of the lore as well as the stylistic choices the developers made in Mortal Shell's creation.I said it is more methodical than Dark Souls because of the "harden" ability each "shell" has. It is also simply different than Dark Souls due to the character (or "shell") leveling system being skill or perk based instead of stats based. The IS a stats based leveling system for each weapon in the upgrade item called "quenching acid" but, beyond that, each weapon has two abilities unique to said weapon. I think there are a total of 5 (4 base game + 1 DLC) different weapons each with two upgrade materials to be found out in the world and five slots for damage upgrades. After the intro you, within your shell, will find an item that allows you to parry given you have the "resolve" to do so. Each shell has a different, finite but refillable amount of resolve that can be gained (and stored up) through combat or by other means.The NPCs are interesting. The soundtrack is fitting. The gameplay is rich with heart pounding battles.I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys action RPGs or is craving a unique challenge.Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: First - please don't look at my registered playtime. I actually have 30 hours in base game on EGS and have just imported saves to Steam for next pass with DLC.Mortal Shell is pure classic soulslike game but it’s definitely not a Souls clone. This game has it’s own turf and for the good sake. Many aspects here are the same as in other classic soulslikes – it’s a 3D action-RPG in 3rd person perspective in dark fantasy setting. It has high difficulty, challenging fights with bosses, respawn on checkpoints, loosing all earned currency at death but with possibility to reclaim it after respawn, etc. The world itself isn’t linear, it has main hub and few dungeons with bosses, It’s pretty compact but without any map and requires some time for familiarization.But Mortal Shell also has some unique mechanics. First it’s the Shells itself. Instead selecting class at game start you have possibility to change classes any time in game, even mid-combat. It gives lots of variability. The second interesting unique mechanic is Hardening. In a very simple way the hardening is a block which completely absorbs next attack but it’s only tip of iceberg. You can hardening yourself at any moment, even mid-attack animation or midair and after getting struck you’ll finish that move. It gives many interesting tactics but you can’t spam it because of cooldown. You also able to hot-swap your weapon even mid-combo. Parrying is also viable strategy though it requires some skills due to tiny parrying window. It very risky but gives huge reward if succeed. There is also such mechanic as familiarization – you need to use an item one or few times for knowing it’s properties and maximize it’s effective. And at this point I want to tell about exploration aspect of the game. There is an interesting and twisted lore but you’ll need to learn about it on your own by reading inscriptions, by short dialog with NPCs, by reading items descriptions etc. At starting point you’ll know nothing about world, yourself, you purpose (if you even have one). It’s like Scorn’s vibe at some point. “Who I am? What I do here? And where I am? And why?” Later that vibe changes to Zelda-style. Your main motive is curiosity. “Hmm… What the hell this amulet does? And what may be in that cave?” You accepted quest from Dark Father but not because you feel obligated. You just curious to know consequences.But even if you don’t cares about lore and story and only interested in combat, you will not be disappointed in any way because combat there is very solid. And the game have good replayability thanks to different available playstyles. I recommend to buy full game because DLC offers very interesting new shell and a new transforming weapon, both of them gives unique experience. It’s not an AAA game and have some flaws but in general it’s a very good game which already gave me many happy hours. Must have for all soulslike’s funs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game advertises 100s of deep upgrades, but in reality there are 7 unique upgrades for all 4 characters and 2 unique upgrades for all 4 weapons. So, maybe if you count non-unique upgrades (generic damage upgrade on each weapon) you might get near 100 upgrades. Aside from that, the game is just boring. There is 1 enemy that you fight repeatedly to unlock weapons, and each area just has a couple of enemy types in different arrangements. Most of the damage that you'll be taking comes from attacks with no windup at all, the most annoying of which being the archers. These guys can shoot over walls and at any range, and their patterns are completely unpredictable. Sometimes they can fire shot after shot without stopping, which doesn't cause too much damage but it can effectively stun lock you while other enemies do whatever they want. This game does have very solid ideas going on, such as the ability to harden your body instead of traditional blocking, but the execution takes away from being able to appreciate them. The graphics are incredible, I didn't see a single visual bug in my time playing. If you're mostly interested in visuals then you might enjoy this game, but if you only care about how something looks then maybe go to an art gallery instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a fantastic souls-like game, easily one of the best. However, the player movesets are somewhat janky,  the performance isn't great, and a few enemies have poorly telegraphed or hard to dodge attacks. Aside from these few flaws, Mortal Shell is outstanding in its genre. The 4 weapons (5 if you count the ballistazooka, and 6 if you have the dlc) are all interesting and unique. The 4 shells (5 if you have the dlc) are all balanced and useful in different scenarios due to their well-crafted abilities; additionally, they each have interesting lore behind them that unlocks as you upgrade them. Mortal Shell is slower than the Dark Souls games, and debatably more difficult, giving it a unique feel of weightiness that adds to the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting take on the dark souls formula that misses the mark in some aspects. Overall it's worth picking up on sale for those looking for a short souls-like game. On the positive side: The combat is weighty and pretty satisfying. The shell system is interesting although could be expanded on. It allows you to switch play-styles and weapons without ever being locked in to anything at the cost of not being able to really maximize a single one. Aesthetically it is a very nice looking game and nails that grim-dark feel. The lore seems interesting enough if you want to dig into it. I did like the consumable item familiarity mechanic where you have to use something to learn what it does and the effect improves as you use it, although, it would have been better if there were more varied items. Also, the new rogue-lite mode adds some replayability for those looking for it.On the negative side:My biggest complaint is the level design. There is one sprawling main area and 3 temples with a boss at the end of each. the main area, Fallgrim, is a dark swamp that is very challenging to navigate. I knew where I needed to go but would end up wandering in circles trying to get there. The temples are relatively short and linear. The difficulty level of the game is a bit lower than I would expect. I only died once on one of the main bosses, and several times to the minibosses you encounter early. I beat the main game in about 10-11 hours. I ended up sticking with one tanky shell and the starting weapon since i really didn't have any incentive to switch since switching shells on the fly requires limited availability items. Also, since there isn't a leveling system, there isn't much to spend your money (tar) on after you fully upgrade a shell and weapon. This can be done before or right after your first temple.I played the rogue-lite mode for a few hours. It's a single life run through the whole game with randomized buffs. It is very punishing but ultimately the enemies don't change much and the layout stays the same. It was fun for a bit but the grind and very careful playstyle required was not something I wanted to spend a lot of time on. I think some people will really enjoy the challenge, however. The Virtuous cycle was free at launch so definitely worth it. I would recommend seeing if you enjoy the main game before buying the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another Dark Souls clone that completely misses the mark.You have a central hub and then 3 separate areas, each with a boss. After you beat the 3 bosses, you return to the hub area and fight the final boss. If you know the maps, you can probably get it done in under 4 hours.The central hub area is a swampy forest, but it's very convoluted, like a maze; also, everything looks the same, so you will get lost a lot.The 3 separate areas are for the most part linear, so they don't suffer from the same issue. Although, in one area, you have to traverse it by using some teleporters, and you have to remember the order in which to use them, because they send you to different parts of the area, and these parts are, again, quite maze-like.It has a ton of health, it spawns aggressive adds during the fight and, once per battle, it consumes said adds to regain health.- They misspelled one of the achievements, ffs (after you beat a boss called The First Martyr, you get an achievement "Martyr'd the ".- Also, it's like the game tries to be obnoxious. After you die, you respawn in front of a Sester (the level-up NPC, kind of like a firekeeper), and she always has a dialog line. This gets really annoying after dying to the boss a few times, like "there's no need to remind me that I'm bad at this game". I turned the dialog volume slider to 0 because of this. I'm sure the voice acting in this game is amazing, but I'm never going to find out.- The DLC is the exact same game, but now in roguelite form. I haven't bought it, because it sounds terrible.Also, as with other games, the DLC achievements appear in the achievement list even if you don't own the DLC (not sure if this is a Steam limitation, though), which I hate.- There's plenty more of these little quirks, but this review is getting quite long already.You are a Foundling, some sort of alien creature, and you can inhabit Shells, armors of fallen warriors. However, nothing is really explained.- Each Shell has its own unique skill tree, and each unlocked skill also unlocks a bit of lore about the warrior that inhabited it previously. It's an interesting concept, but the problem is that some skills are quite uninteresting/bad or too expensive, so you won't probably get the whole story.- You do find some monoliths with notes around the world. In addition, there are some hidden notes that only appear when you hit certain walls and that reveals the true history of the world, but, without a guide, good luck finding those.+ The hardening mechanic is interesting. Basically, you can harden your shell, which makes you invulnerable to all damage. You can remain hardened indefinitely, until you let go of the button or are hit by an attack. This ability has a relatively short cooldown. The fun thing is that you can do this at almost any time: while attacking, while healing, while dodging etc. While you are hardened, any effect you are under continues, e.g. your stamina replenishes, you continue to regen health if you used a healing item etc.There are also consumables that give boosts if you are hit while hardened.So, there are quite a lot of gameplay elements and combinations possible.+ If you take lethal damage, you are instead ejected from your shell and have to get back to it. Thus you kind of have an extra life. If you are hit even once in your shell-less form, you die.There is a (rare) consumable that gives the extra life; there is also a skill that gives the extra life after you kill a certain amount of enemies, though it's quite expensive.+ Visually, the game doesn't look bad, it's quite gritty and has this depressing vibe to it.The separate areas are all different to each other and visually distinct: one is fire/lava, one is ice and the last one is obsidian/rocks. The bosses are also related to these elements, both visually and with their attacks.All in all, I recommend avoiding this game, or at least getting it on a deep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you are a strong fan of dark-souls like games.THE GAME- GENERALWhere this game does things right, it is a pleasure to play. The weapons feel properly powerful and "weighty." The variety, though not staggering, is enough to fit various play styles. Moreover, the mechanic for obtaining the weapons feels rewarding. The combat feels fast-paced and (mostly) fair. There is not a large variety of enemies, but if you can look past that, the general game play loop of - explore a direction, kill enemies in said direction, find a checkpoint, levelup - is quite enjoyable.ENEMIES AND BOSSESAs said above, the enemies are not horribly varied. Moreover, in some areas of the game the enemies feel less naturally part of the world and more so seem to be pawns dropped onto a board in convenient locations. With that said, the general humanoid style of enemies do have different combat styles that provides some differing challenges. As for the bosses, they  were fine. Outside of one boss (the twiceborn), the boss fights felt fair if a little bit simple. The Twiceborn boss, however, was not enjoyable for me whatsoever. The issue being that the boss has no cooldown timer between attacks; causing the player to have to employ a game of bait the easy attack, strike once, back away, rinse and repeat until death. LORE AND WORLDI will admit, I did not look into the lore of the game that much, but there is a codex style of log for the player to examine at their pleasure. Beyond that, each of the "shells" has somewhat of a backstory that is teased out through leveling; an interesting idea! The world itself is relatively simple dark fantasy with some fantastical elements thrown in occasionally. As an example, there were certain sections of the game that I stopped and simply appreciated the very visually appealing scene before me, and there were others where I just walked through not caring of the surroundings. FINAL THOUGHTSOnce more, if you enjoy dark souls like games then you likely will enjoy Mortal Shells. With a playtime, for me, of about 11.5 hours to complete the initial campaign, the game was well worth the $20.00 I purchased it for while on sale. The full price is a bit more questionable, but I think still is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you've played the Dark Souls games or not, Mortal Shell is worth the buy, but adjust your expectations if you absolutely must compare it to them. Both the Harden mechanic and different shells you pick up throughout the game essentially simplify the combat and character building, which is something you may or may not like if you prefer managing every inch of your stamina gauge and min-maxing your stats. Let's talk about the core mechanics of this wonderful action RPG: there are no shields in Mortal Shell, just dodges, rolls, parries and the new Harden mechanic. It forces you to be the aggressor, but in practice, I found that it removed a lot of the challenge and nuances of managing stamina. For anyone familiar with these kind of games, Poise is a mechanic that punishes you for spamming the attack button -- something you don't want to do as the enemy will eventually counter with their own attacks right at the end of your flurry. In Mortal Shell, you can effectively negate this danger by holding your Harden during your combinations for when the enemy decides to retort. AND it slightly staggers them if you get hit while Hardened, allowing you to continue mashing away if you have enough stamina to do so. Depending on how fast you pick up on this, you'll come to realize that stamina is the best resource. Which brings me to my second point, the different Shells, or armours, you come across will give you varying stat distributions across your HP/Stamina/Fervor. In general, I found myself using the Shell that trades HP/Fervor in favour of Stamina. It's a glass cannon style that really just focuses on dodge-rolling your way through everything, and the passives you unlock for that skin are all damage-focused. All the other Shells just didn't seem to bring the same overall consistency. Fervor is your "mana bar" that takes on the form of individual blocks/nodes, and each one allows you perform enhanced parries or fuel weapon skills, but the game being so focused on aggression made me skip this playstyle and Fervor-focused Shell. The game is literally balanced around spamming attacks and managing your ~5 second cooldown Harden ability. That's it. Although  Harden makes for some clutch moments where you're launching attacks mid-air that are about to get countered, I felt the ability was just too strong, but perhaps this was a deliberate choice to make players experience and finish the game sooner than Dark Souls, which can easily take three times the ammount of hours to complete.Mortal Shell is a beautiful game that runs really well, has what seems to be a good story behind it, but the combat might turn off purists of the genre. The AI can get wonky in some areas too, and there's not many which further shortens the experience. Overall, I'm glad I bought and played Mortal Shell, but I don't think there's enough depth for me to NG+ it. The final portions of the game were a bit of a slog.

Players can choose from a range of shells, or bodies, each with their own unique abilities and stats, and must use their skills and weapons to defeat enemies and bosses throughout the game's world. The game's combat system is precise and punishing, with a focus on timing and strategy rather than button mashing. The game's world is large and atmospheric, with plenty of secrets and hidden areas to discover.Graphics and Sound:The game's graphics are impressive, with detailed environments and character models that showcase the game's dark and moody setting. The game's use of lighting and visual effects also adds to the overall atmosphere of the game. The sound design is also well-done, with great sound effects and a haunting soundtrack that complements the game's tone.Storyline:The game's storyline is minimal, with the game's focus being on exploration and survival rather than a pre-written narrative. The game's world is rich in lore, with plenty of hidden secrets and mysteries to discover. The game's writing is generally strong, with interesting characters and dialogue that help to bring the game's world to life.Technical Issues:One of the most notable aspects of "Mortal Shell" is the technical issues that can impact the game's performance. Players have reported bugs, glitches, and other issues that can impact the game's stability and playability. These issues can be frustrating for players and may detract from the overall experience.Overall:"Mortal Shell" is a challenging and atmospheric game that is not for everyone. The game's combat system, RPG mechanics, and world design are all impressive, but the game's technical issues can impact the overall experience. Despite its flaws, "Mortal Shell" is still worth playing for fans of the action role-playing genre and those looking for a dark and challenging game world to explore and conquer.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so this is NOT the next Dark Souls. It is kind of a different take with some nice ideas.That does not say it is a bad game and concept. So basically you get thrown into this confusing swamp like area, where you will fight enemies and farm mushrooms to heal yourself ( regular items respawn after like 5 minutes). There is no block, but a pretty intresting harden feature. Also you can parry, but the timing seems off and I rarely got it to work. I have found no way to fast travel yet, I have found a few shells(there is no character creation, just shells you find and improve). Also there are only like 4 weapons in the game. So forget about builds, pick a suitable shell and upgrade your abilities. Do the same for your favorite weapon.I think with a guide this game will not last long,  Since you rarely get awarded for exploration(very sad), so if you know where to go it will probably be an easy game. But since I play blind for first time, I do struggle a bit navigating the game.For me it's good enough , and I must say the graphics on ULTRA look amazing. They really did a great job on graphics and sound. For a smaller indie team that's a job well done.It's gonna be a recommended, certainly after all those hours in Dark Souls.... Even those games can get boring after a long period of playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a distillation of a Souls experience: the world is a lot smaller; there are three dungeons you can approach in any order; there aren't builds, but there are "shells" you can find that are effectively pre-built characters (each having their own level-up set of talents); there are 4 weapons you can unlock that provide different playstyles and upgrade options.  The combat is tight, and the shell-harden mechanic brings an entirely new strategy to fights.  I loved the art-style, I loved the combat, I loved trying to piece together the lore, and I loved the build I created.  For a small developer, this is an impressive feat, and hands-down one of the best soulslikes I've ever played.  A small, condensed, great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I got the game and DLC for a little over 3 bucks. I definitely recommend buying on sale, as the game is pretty short and heavy with the bugs. As far as bugs go, you'll be dealing with invisible enemies that appear when you're right next to them, freezing in combat and unfreezing a few seconds later (often resulting in you taking damage) loss of controls at random times, and crashes at random times as well. Length-wise, anyone who's familiar with souls-like games can probably get through it in 8 or so hours, those who are bad at games might take a little longer like me. You start in the hub/forest area, and you're instructed to beat 3 dungeons. then you fight the final boss... yep that's it. In spite of all the flaws it looks pretty cool and combat is probably it's best aspect, balancing your attacks with hardening and dodging can be challenging especially with certain enemies. Worth for 3 bucks but not full price. Wait until it's at least 50% off.  And there's a rougelite mode as well. Haven't really tried it tho

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal shell is unique take on a souls like. definitely worth playing with a certain mind set. I've seen mixed reviews online and would like to put my personal input as a fan of the souls the genre. first off, the main gimmick : Hardening. Mortal shell doesn't have shields, but instead, defense is centered around hardening into a shell that can block any and all attacks once per a short cool down (roughly 5 seconds). you can harden at any point in time during a jump and or attack. Making the mechanic not only a basic defense, but a strategic and unique offence as well. Once you get the hang of it. It is by far one of the best most creative mechanics I've seen in a souls like. also, because you cant spam hardening, It teaches you to keep moving, and plan your attacks. I have nothing but good to say about this mechanic, despite some online criticizing it. I feel they don't understand how to use it to its full potential. secondary gimmick: parrying. I will say parrying in this game is sadly the only thing holding it back from being one of my favorite games. The parry window itself is pretty big. Its just very, very inconsistent and unreliable. And i'm not sure why. One thing I do like about it, is when you have resolve, parrying and counter attacking can heal you. But I generally avoided parring unless I was CERTAIN it was going to work. third gimmick: shells. instead of leveling up and dumping stat points into one character. You unlock different shells, each with there own strengths and weaknesses. I found this mechanic to be great. Because you don't have to worry about respecing your character if a fight isn't working out. You can just switch shells for whatever situation you're in. Nothing is more stressful to me in a souls like then that dreaded question "Am I doing my build right?" also note: Mortal shell is short and sweet. I beat the main story in about 11 hours. You may think that's far too short. But I actually think its a benefit. If you are interested in souls like but cant invest the time in going on the longest, darkest, hardest quest of your life... this game is for you. Its the first souls like I genuinely excited to start new game+. Not only cause its short but because  Also, its not THAT hard of a game. If you find other souls likes too annoyingly hard, and are tired of crying and smashing your controller against the wall. This game is a good test of skill, but its not so overwhelming that your sweating bullets by the end of every boss fight. What I didn't like: Rest zones are sometimes FAR between. Like stupidly far. Nothing hurts more then dying and realizing your body is miles away. The map is very confusing at first. Navigation can be a nightmare. Adding to the pain of dying. More then once upon death I said out loud "I have no clue where my body is, dammit." too much padding. Because there is no fast travel. After defeating a boss, you have to travel ALLLL they way back to the center tower on foot, fighting recycled enemies the whole way. Obviously if the devs put in fast travel, you could beat the game in half the time. But, by the time I was heading back from the last boss, I was just sprinting back home avoiding everything on the way back. overall this game could have been one of the best. With a bit more effort in making the map bigger, adding 1 or 2 more bosses with unique zones, and adding more enemy types... I would have no complaints. But as far as an indie dev souls like. Its worth playing. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: there are quite a lot of flaws here. its very short maybe 8 hours on a second play through. on a first play through once you get a mastery on the combat its final boss time. you have 4 different characters to choose form and other than having different stamina/health/mana ratios there kinda the same,  i really dont understand why skill trees in games like this are always full of useless abilities like if you kill two guys really quickly your instant block ability will come back faster which wont help you if your block takes 4 secs to regen and your never going to kill that many guys in a row.you also have 4 weapons which another problem with these games is nothing is better than your starting weapon. you start with a basic sword, you get a slow heavy weapon, a really slow heavier weapon and a quick dual hand weapon but the problem is they all basically do the same damage despite being 2 or 3 times slower. the dual hand weapon isnt bad but its essentially end game.new game plus is also pointless since when you do that you usually want to try to use some of the other weapons or characters but the weapon damage upgrades are finite and the enemies are stronger so to keep up you have to upgrade the weapon you maxed out on the previous play through again.Overall its decent its just hard to call it decent compared to  any of the souls games and its fallen far from that which is why is always on a high discount sale which is the only way i would recommend buying it.It feels like if they made a sequel off of this platform and addressed all of these issues it would make for an awesome game

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a good time if you like some Souls-like with a taste of some bugs and nice combat. The game mostly shines with its control of combat mechanics and shells that go deep to provide more variety. You can even use a character that burrows abilites from others and customize to your liking. Combat is mostly good but enemy variety is lacking. You'll see way too many of the same enemies and this basically makes the game's bad sides surface more, otherwise some good level design in last sections of the game.There are some bugs that disable your ability to attack or open menus, disabling your ability to speak to certain npcs etc which can be fixed by reloading. Other than those two I don't remember anything serious. The game has roguelike mode coming from its DLC which is a great addition for more replayability other than the already present New Game+ mode. It was short overall with 5-6 weapon types and 5 different locations but still an enjoyable experience. I recommend if you are willing to push thru some jank(as much as in Dark Souls) and enjoy its unforgiving but fun side.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played every Dark Souls game to date. I like the genre and I like souls-like games. Mortal Shell has a very clunky system that punishes you far harder than other games. The button mapping on the keyboard is not good. I like the idea of the harden ability, but it's too slow and leaves no room for error. I like the idea of try the items to find out what they are, but there's no explanation of resources or how to spend them. What's the point of tar? What's the point of experience? Also, the time limit on gathering mushrooms or healing is infuriating. There are so many things about this game that could be good, but the devs decided to not be friendly to the players. I get that some games are hard, but there's a difference between challenge and difficulty for difficulty's sake. Sadly, I don't find this game fun.

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who finished all of the Dark Souls game 1/2/3 , Bloodborne , Sekiro , Nioh 1/2 , The Surge 1/2 , Code Vein and most of the known games in this genre , i feel qualified to say that Mortal Shell is one of the worst souls-like i have ever played.the devs clearly were heavily inspired by the original DS , they nailed the atmosphere and the general feeling of the game with some beautiful visuals and thats basically it , everything else in this game is a mess.1- the combat is an absolute jank , feels unresponsive and slow for you - fast for your enemies , both parry and dodge feels inconstant , sometimes it works and sometimes it won't and you have a very small window for them , same goes for hitboxes.2-game is hugely unbalanced , enemies numbers and distribution around the maps are insanely high , the lack of checkpoints and healing system is very limited to an item you pick around the map or to the inconstant parry mechanic , all of this discourage progress greatly.3- game is very boring , very slow and very grindy , the game wants you to die alot but instead of learning new things you usually die from its bad design , purchasing upgrades is very slow , unlocking weapons require beating the same boss 4 times , the areas looks fresh at first then they turn bland real fast , also the story is non-existent.4-exploring is unrewarding , most of the items are useless in this game except some upgrading items.Mortal Shell is the perfect example of bad design , they wanted to make their own Dark Souls but they forget what made it great , sadly i don't recommend this mess at all even to a hardcore souls-like fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Not every game have to be DS and Mortal Shell chisels its own path with what they refer to as shells.Just recently discovered that there are no weapon upgrades and no armor upgrades. The shells and the accompanying gear are all you get! They can't be mixed and matched and they can't be upgraded. I definitely didn't know that. That makes the game slightly tangy, with very little character customization. If there was a neutral recommendation mark I'd put this there.You're controlling a Westworld android type of muscle guy that can acquire other classes known as shells. While wearing these your stats and abilities change according to what shell you're wearing. A unique feature here is the option to harden, basically hold down a button to turn to stone. You can use these in battles to make opponents stunned (since they're basically hitting a rock), and is empathised to use throughout the game. Natural to any aspiring hero trying to beat the living hell out of anything that moves, you're going to take damage. Healing is mitigated through items, like mushrooms and fruit, that you pick up from the environment. They're on respawn timers, but weirder still is that they don't reset if you die. So you may have to relax around the vegetation for some time to loot new ones. Level designs in the first areas seem sprawling and interesting enough to wander around. From the little I've seen so far it's a different take on the Souls formula and that's okay. For the price (current game and dlc sale discount) you're getting quite the deal. The DLC also adds roguelike dungeons like in Bloodborne, adding to replayability and new things to see and overcome.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the weirdest Souls like i have played so far, very confusing in terms of story and mechanics, it reminds me alot of The Surge/2 with its annoying enemies and stamina problems, and im no stranger to Souls like games.Bugs:Aside from the game not closing down completely, i havent run into anyThe enjoyable:Runs well.I Like the theme.I like the Atmosphere.Combat feels nice.Good animations.Visuals are nice and gloomy whenever you can actually see anything, there isnt much ligh in this game.The "Shells" for the most part look nice but since its dark background on dark atmosphere on top of dark lightning and the "shells" are all dark, there isnt much to look at.World items seem to regenerate, so this is nice if you know an area where healing shrooms spawn, just takes a few min for it to regrow.The Less enjoyable:You are pathetically weak for a long time and you run into either some really chonky dudes right away (Like Black Knights from Dark Souls) or you get swarmed by 3 dudes, a big dude and a archer that you can´t see because they are on a ledge.Not alot of weapons.All we do is Melee essentially, we do have a single ranged weapon, but that thing is so slow you are not going to use it all that much.. _childDocuments_.review: Whew... I hadn't expected that. First of all, the design and the look caught my eye, everything looks incredibly chic. The visual impressions were captivating right from the start. I just thought .... wow, that's how I wanted Dark Souls 4 to look. Right at the beginning I wanted to play it like the original, but that didn't work, I had to get involved with something new. But after the first hour you have internalised it well. What picked me up next was the incredibly good acoustic background to the whole thing. I'm a big fan of dark ambient and soundscapes and immediately thought... wow, finally someone has made a game with such acoustic treats. It's dark, ominous, melancholic and yet beautiful.From now on, Mortal Shell had me under its spell. The swamp (Falgrim) is really very confusing at the beginning. Where do I have to go? What are these items (I still don't know what they all mean, even though I've just played through it)? Is that an enemy there or... bang, bear trap. I really died a lot at the beginning, every enemy was a challenge for me, before I understood how to handle enemies and how to use hardening, it was really tedious.Then the first dungeon (a kind of fire temple), wow... great, it looks fantastic, the enemies, the music, the atmosphere... Damn it, I have no life, where is the checkpoint? But enough of the praise, what's negative to say? The biggest drawback - it's really very short, after a good 10-15 hours you see the end sequence. It took me a little over 15 hours, but I was also totally on a discovery tour and looked at everything carefully... oh what the heck, I was immersed.The second negative point of criticism is that the bosses are too easy. I would rate myself as an average player and I had most of the bosses down on the first try. The first boss fight excited me at first, it wasn't too short, you could work with the opponent, however, with bosses two and three I quickly learned that the tactics are always the same except for the ice boss and the final boss. Too bad...What I find difficult are the trash mobs, which often appear out of nowhere and sometimes come in packs when you are barely alive and have no mushrooms.There are four so-called shells in the basic game. You can't personalise anything here, the hulls have predefined attribute slots into which you can put the appropriate attributes if you have enough resources.In any case, all my praise goes to the designers, the atmosphere is outstanding for me and even after Dark Souls it still fascinated me. Unfortunately it's really short and you get the feeling you've only played a demo. However, I can recommend it for little money, it is often on sale on Steam.If you like Dark Souls, you will also appreciate this one. You have to understand it as a bow to Dark Souls - great game.Update: After playing through the game several times, I have noticed many design and programming errors. Also, the game is really short, just when I get along well with a weapon and a character, the game is suddenly over. It feels like you've just left the beginner area and the Unchained is the first real boss and the game starts. But then it's suddenly over and there's a bad aftertaste. The game is really good, and you can overlook some of the mistakes, but why so short? You've just got hungry and then you're left unsated. I would also have liked a bit more background on the different shells, some of seem really interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, as a long time Soulsborne fan. It's not quite the same as others, but it has charm. _childDocuments_.review: In the 70 minutes I spent playing this title, I admittedly didn't get anywhere. So if you feel like that discredits my review entirely, then read no further. However, I think this is one of the worst soulslikes I've ever played. The combat feels like you are walking through a swamp, light attacks feel like you're performing heavy attacks in terms of animation speed, the dodge ranges from unresponsive to launching you way too far away to do a follow-up attack on the target. Hardening is this game's own unique combat mechanic; I think it feels terrible, and the visual indicator that it's recharged is too subtle and draws your eyes away from the action. The "second life" element of the game feels mostly pointless because half the time I get knocked out of my shell I've been ping-ponged a good distance away, so getting back into it before being killed is an often unlikely turnout. Healing is extremely limited from I saw, maybe even practically nonexistent. Waypoints are limited. The starting area is a confusing maze and a horrible introduction to the game's systems. You can't see an enemy's health bar unless you're locked on. Opening the inventory is a visual flashbang of bright white for a brief moment before fading to black... why? Who the fu­ck designed this? If you consider tabbing out while playing to look up something, be warned that there is a very high chance it will simply crash the game. This happened to me five times during my short time playing and is the primary reason I have given up entirely on pushing forward. I'm sure at some point the shi­tty combat could've clicked with me on some level, but I'm not willing to waste my time progressing only to lose it because the game abruptly crashed to desktop. I don't recommend playing this game, not even for free. It is fraught with bullsh­it that has no respect for your time or patience, just for the sake of creating artificial difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Another souls-like that hits most of the marks of what makes a souls game difficult and frustrating, while forgetting to actually make it any fun. The combat is clunky and unresponsive, can't tell you how many times I died when I absolutely hit dodge or harden. The way the i-frames and animation work, if you make a timing mistake, you'll die 3 seconds later when you feel you definitely hit the button that would have saved you. Every swing of your sword is a marriage-level commitment. This leads to beating enemies in the exact same ways every time, there is no dynamic flow of combat. It's "oh it's another one of these, time to pull him away from the crowd and R2+R2+R2+L2+R1." Rinse and repeat until the group of mobs are gone. Then die to some hidden mob around a corner and do it all again. Game is a huge fan of ambushes, it's basically a mechanic. Every single doorway or corner, walk through, double back, dodge attacks from 2 ambushing enemies. It's annoying as hell.Parrying actually feels great once you have the timing down... but if you have no Resolve, there is no combat benefit to doing it. You don't get a reposte or an advantage, you basically just waste your turn. This is obnoxious in a game sorely lacking depth in combat. Even with upgrades, enemies will kill you in 2 hits (unless you pick the shell with no stamina), and frankly, I don't have the patience for this game's bulls***. I've beaten DS2 twice, and would rather play that again than finish this game. I don't regret getting it, because I like supporting new / small devs, and I think these guys can make something great. The pieces are here. The sound design is fantastic and the game looks beautiful and runs smooth. But the gameplay loop is just frustrating, with no payoff.

_childDocuments_.review: MS is one of those games with very divisive opinions. You have people who absolutely hate it and some who love it to death. Then there is my personal worry of playing a Souls like game. I’ve completed two 2D ones (I’m not sure if they count) and tried a bunch of 3D demos. I haven’t really gotten into a proper (3D) one. The difficulty of Souls games along with the demo of Lies of P always intimidated me. 35 hours later, I’ve 100% completed the main game including the achievements. I’ve come to the conclusion that MS is a very misunderstood game for various reasons. One of them is the game itself giving a very bad first impression.I felt it myself and I was doubting my purchase initially. The game just kind of throws you in its world with very little handholding or any basic info with how things work or which direction to head towards. The main hub world has many branching paths to the point that you can easily get lost. The game has no map whatsoever, so this is made worse. It’s scary to explore for a bit since, at first, it seemed like there weren’t enough means to heal yourself. And one of the means is coupled with a parry that appears to be very tricky. Then there is the confusing save system where you’re not sure how it works exactly and where you can save at all. After you figure that part out, you start to get worried about respawning enemies just for saving every single time.So those were the early impressions. I’ve noticed that you can pick up mushrooms to heal and they respawn in the same spots you found them. So you can farm them and collect plenty. The parry system is actually easier than it appears and an important element of that is not explained in the game. The normal parry has a very short parry window without riposte. But with riposte, parrying becomes far more forgiving. I read about it randomly on the internet and it made a difference to my play style. The game appears to auto-save often and it saves when you exit the game too. The game just doesn’t mention this anywhere. The enemies don’t respawn as long as you don’t take a sip from a Sester or don’t go to one of the 3 dungeons (the transition from the hub to the dungeons). As for the hub world, it will feel like second home after a while. The lack of maps seems to be intentional and it works with this game if you try to remember your steps and focus on exploration instead of trying to find your next target at the beginning. But if you still don’t want that, the community comes through with sharing maps online and giving other helpful advice.  This is one of the game’s biggest faults or strengths depending on where you land. Some people love to figure things out for themselves but for others it feels like work. I fall a bit in the middle and I’m willing to put the effort. Even with all of this in mind, the game could have been clearer about a couple of things. The order of dungeons does matter in terms of challenge even if you’re free to play them in any order you wish. The story seems a bit gibberish to me. While the little voice acting we have is good, I don’t like the style of story delivery here. But luckily it’s not important for this game imo. I’ve also encountered a couple of minor bugs, mainly visual bugs and the enemies (from the third dungeon) like to throw themselves in a death pit on the way back (when you have the gland). Oh, and I didn’t like the 2 achievements where you basically have to finish the game without getting hit. You can save but there is a lot of trial and error involved.What you get in return is a very addictive game after you figure it out. The sense of exploration and going through the unknown in every facet is just great. You can even see this with the items where you are encouraged to try them out before you know what they do and you will get better effects once you become familiar with them. Using harden is genuinely fresh and fun. The parry system has a rewarding feeling to it in terms of assessing the risk involved and what you get out of it. The game doesn’t have a lot of content, it’s one of the negatives by the community but it’s a positive to me. It makes the game very approachable and easier to complete for ones with a backlog. Also, I’m never a fan of games giving you too much of everything but not using even half of it. The amount of weapons, riposte effects, items, shells and dungeons is perfect for me. The game looks gorgeous and atmospheric. I like the UI and the game’s style in general. I’ve also read that Souls fans are harsher on MS because it’s not exactly like Souls games but this doesn’t apply to me obviously. I bought the game with the DLC* on sale with 90% off. This is a great price and 1000% worth it if you like what the game is going for. It’s better to give the game a try (with refund policy) instead of blindly accepting the popular opinion online. *I’ve started the DLC today and a proper review will follow once I’m done with it.
