_childDocuments_.review: SO, lots of people are complaining about the game, and a big chunk (not all) seem to have been misinformed about the game. It is not "dark souls", it has similarities, sure, but the idea behind the gameplay is different. I'm even more surprised people didn't know what to expect, given that the game has been out for over a year, so plenty of time to do a little research on the game.Normally you'd play DS starting up as a bit of a turtle maybe, learning to dodge slowly along the way, each encounter is ridiculously deadly, but once you beat it, you can heal up and continue onwards. In Mortal Shell your damage avoid abilities are all timed, if you don't adapt early on, you will be pounded in the rear, you will be poisoned, combod for 70% of hp, and then you're just kinda sitting here with no healing mushrooms.It sounds infuriating, I know, but what if I told you that you have the Majula merchant from DS2 with infinite lifegems in here as well? The problem I think many people might have is not finding those barely visible stairs to the merchant and his cat, that part I think could've 100% been done better, though it's well known that these games reward exploration.So, once you get the items, you will find it much easier to adapt, but the game can be pretty reliably mastered, you can see the iframes on your dodges, harden is also a nice mix of dodge and stun available pretty often. It makes sense that there is an achievement for completing the game with 1 hit death character. With the tools the game provides, it's very much doable.And here is another little messup that the devs did, try running with Shift and hold Space - your character will do this weird spasm and nothing will happen, for some god knows what reason, there is like a leftover of old keybind for holding spacebar, while only tapping has any effect at this point. So in order to dodge reliably and have it feel good, you need to be sure you're quickly tapping it. It's workable, but understandably annoying.Another thing is that the game is rather short, several hours, and you're neatly through with the game. There is a big hub area with basic enemies, then 3 branches to completely new landscapes. They do have completely different vibes despite proximity, so it has that little disconnect like DS2, but at least everything looks gorgeous here. It's not a super high priced game, and it's not from a big studio either, I'm not super pissed that they decided to focus on everything except the length.As it's an RPG still, there are still some build potentials, each shell you get has different stamina, HP and skills, and all of them can use all 5 weapons in the game. Each weapon has completely different animations and special attacks, the variety once again is not extremely expansive, but very distinct and carefully crafted.To be perfectly honest, after completing the game, the only thing I'm really let down by is the DLC mode. The runs require you to complete the entire game, which can take completely different amount of time, depending on if perks you get are OP as all hell, and if you get tokens to unlock boss areas, And even then playing through the whole game to complete literally 1 run, is way too much for my taste, especially since the very decent enemy placement from OG game is messed up with more annoying and/or difficult enemies, especially infuriating if you have no decent perks.The new shell and weapon from the DLC are really good though, however I would tell everyone to not pay full price for it, it's not worth THAT much.So, here is where the Awful Game Store money went to - audio and graphics. Normally I'd separate the sections, but I have very similarly huge levels of praise for them. The combination of silky smooth mocap animations, with "more sensible than usual" movesets for the weapons; the amazing models and textures on enemies and armor; the moody lighting working perfectly with each of the distinct landscapes featured; the really impactful and clear high quality audio - both mixing and sound bytes, like ambient noises, someone playing lute in the distance, or gurgles and cries after a series of meaty slashes.In short, the presentation is phenomenal, to the point that it feels like a tech demo at times, all the more of a blessing that it's actally a playable and decent game.Beware though, the film grain is on by default, and something like chromatic abberation (aka my glasses are ♥♥♥♥) seems to be part of the vfx setting, these two are a foul curse of UE4 games.Last comes story, which is cryptic and a little bizarre. It's hard to give a short description, since all characters are equally important and intertwined in the plot. The best I can do is say that you're playing an offspring of a godly being, one that can inhabit corpses of powerful people, the world is gone to sheet as everyone got really crazy about chasing immortality, turns out that you're destined to walk among the gods, unlike any greedy powerful creatures who crave it beyond anything else. I'm pretty surprised they crammed something this complicated into such a short game, though as a consequence, the amount of lore is much less than big rpg games focusing on it.So to sum it up, it's a very good, short, insanely well presented atmospheric game. If you don't go in expecting a DS clone, and you have some patience for unusual mechanics, you should have a good time.If length is a big concern, wait a few years and pick it up for much cheaper. If you're still hesitant, watch a bit of gameplay from someone who knows what they're doing, maybe that will convey what the game is about, better than my words.

_childDocuments_.review: is a challenging and atmospheric soulslike that captures the essence of its genre with a unique twist. The game's core mechanic—inhabiting different shells, each with its own playstyle—adds depth and variety to combat, making every encounter feel fresh and strategic. The world is dark, mysterious, and beautifully crafted, inviting exploration and rewarding curiosity.However, some areas of the game feel empty, leaving the player wandering aimlessly at times. While the combat is satisfying and punishing, it may feel slow-paced compared to other soulslike titles, and the game’s relatively short length might leave some players wanting more. Despite these flaws, for fans of the genre, Mortal Shell offers a compact yet deeply engaging experience that’s well worth the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, the mechanics seem solid i've had a good time with it. The only thing about it is that once you get good with the mechanics, the game feels stupidly easy when going against the bosses but at the same time the normal enemies can feel overwhelming. My one criticism is that there is obviously meta gear and a specific way to play to cheese your way through the game but if you choose to buckle down and play the game the fast paste, hyper armor, trading blows way that it was meant to be. Its a gem and i just wish it was on a larger scaleEdit: So I've put about 30 more hours into the game and managed to 100% the game and here is what i have to say after all this. It's wonderful. The base game is fairly lacking and after a few play-throughs i found that i wouldn't even be spending much more than an hour running through the entire game start to finish so don't be expecting much from there. The bulk of the gameplay time that i spent was in the DLC. It adds so much rogue like elements to a souls like game and i don't think they could've done a better job. The gameplay is harder imo because to get all the achievements you have to both limit yourself and then try to push your own boundaries. Trying to beat the entire game without getting hit once? that was at least 70% of my gameplay time and i both loved and hated every second of it. The struggle of not even getting 2 minutes into a run and the defeat of dying at the hands of shells that you create is a masterful way to end off a DLC just to replay it again a few minutes later to try and unlock a new shade, or complete a challenge. I felt like a god once i completed both of my obsidian shell runs but i also felt so exhausted about throwing my head at a wall for 12 hours straight. The challenge that this game presents is one of overcoming an obstacle that is tangible. The no bonfire and no estus run from dark souls 2 is something that nobody really attempts because it's not something they can see themselves completing all the way through (It took me 2 months) But the challenges in this game are within reach, the small scale of the game attributes to the replay. You come closer and closer to that goal and you begin to scrape it until you finally reach that apex of the challenge and your heart begins to beat. The pure adrenaline i got in my first obsidian shell run and i made it to the unchained first try, only to die and then spend the next 8 hours just trying to get back there, and when i finally did, i was determined not to make the same mistakes. Even though i fought him once in the past 8 hours, I remembered every single attack and move that he did because my mind was set on one thing, and i wasn't going to give up until i reached that goal. I proceeded to beat him and i let out a huge sigh of relief before promptly starting my Virtuous cycle obsidian shell run. But that's exactly what im talking about is the beautiful challenge, the relief and then the drive to do it again, to prove that you can do it, not just for the achievement on steam, but the personal achievement, of being able to say that you did this crazy thing that normal people dont even think of doing. You've proven to yourself that you know these mechanics and you know that you can overcome these obstacles, now you just have to prove it to the game. Yes the game is hard. Yes the challenges are stupid. Yes the enemies can feel overwhelming. But mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥, you are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ warrior of stone who doesn't break when he's knocked down. Get up, throw yourself at it until you break down that wall and then throw yourself at another. This game made me feel like i was on top of the world, but not before i had to claw my way up there. Mortal Shell is a souls like masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review off by saying that I find it very hard to believe that some of the people who left a negative review on this game have ever played or finished a Dark Souls game. There are generally good criticisms of the game and I understand why some people have issues with it, such as performance issues, enemies turning around fast, or some of the enemies randomly appearing out of no where, but there are people who put .4 hours into the game and call a quits and refund because the enemies and the game mechanics are not exactly like Dark souls, or is too hard and unforgiving.Also there seems to be a significant amount of negative reviews on Steam because the game released first on Epic, so much so that when I opened steam to buy it I was surprised by it being "mixed", I had to actually read the reviews because I thought there was something dangerously wrong with the steam version of this game. No, just a bunch of negative reviews because the game was on epic first. I think that a lot of people should actually play the game and review it based on that, rather than wasting $30 to make a point that it shouldn't be on Epic. Either way, this game does have some flaws and they should be addressed.There are a lot of complaints about this game not being "enough like Dark Souls", going as far as to compare this games mechanics to Dark Souls. The first thing that should be addressed is that this is not a Dark Souls game, it is a souls like game created by a team of around 15 people. It is easy to tell that this game was inspired by Dark souls, however, the overall mechanics and the way it plays out is not going to be exactly like Dark Souls, and people need to keep their expectations in check for that.The first major complaint I am seeing a lot of is the fact the game is unforgiving and difficult, or the enemies are hard and do not have consistent attack movement. This is where my statement at the beginning comes from, where I do not think the people who compare this game to Dark Souls have actually played Dark Souls. You cannot walk into a Souls game or a Souls like game and expect to be able to pick up things and kick ass immediately, that is basically the whole point of the souls experience. Getting your ass kicked then ultimately kicking ass as time progresses. You cannot put less than an hour or 2 hours into this and expect to be the god of the world you just entered, people need to take time and learn this game, it is a completely new and unique experience. I dropped into this game and had a tough time at the start because it was hard getting used to the enemies. But that should be expected considering your character just started and is at the lowest they will ever be. Once you get the hang of things and the new hardening mechanic the game becomes much more manageable with its difficulty.Another complaint I am seeing is that enemies turn much faster than people are used to. I have seen about 3 reviews saying that people are used to being able to go behind an enemy and get a back stab like in Dark Souls. Unfortunately, back stabbing is not in this game, however, the criticism for enemies turning faster is warranted. I have encountered a few enemies that turn around unnaturally fast as if their character model pivoted 180 degrees without an animation for it, and if this is what everyone is experiencing all the time, then so be it the developers should slow it down. I am surprised by the amount of reviews that have this as an issue for as little as I am seeing it happen when I am playing. This is not to dismiss any of the criticism, I just find it odd as to why it has only happened to me a few times. I think most people are noticing this issue on a specific mini boss fight towards the beginning of the game since that's where I have seen a few of these reviews talk about it. In my experience I didn't bother with that mini boss till I got a new weapon and had already beaten a few bosses. I went back and was able to take him out after a couple tries.Sticking with complaints about enemies, there is an issue that I and many other players have experienced where you can be running around the map and suddenly an enemy will spawn right in front of you. Majority of the time the enemy is sitting down in my path so I can run right past it but there have been other times where they spawn in standing in your path and you have to fight them to progress. This is another issue the developers should take a look at and fix, because it can create issues when you are fighting in an area and suddenly another enemy just pops out of no where killing you.Either way, considering all of this I think Mortal Shell is a damn good game so far. I am able to overlook some of these issues I noted considering Dark souls has multiple issues of its own. 15 people were able to create this and I find that very impressive. I have had fun with my experience so far and I am excited to fully finish the game. If anything changes I will definitely update my review.Edit: After finishing the game I stand by my belief that I think this is a damn good game. I still think those issues previously mentioned can turn people off, and I do not blame them. However, in terms of the enemies rotating 180 I only experienced it a few more times after the review, but it was nothing game breaking by any means.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this game a thumbs down, because it’s clear a lot of work and passion went into it. However, this game makes two key changes to the Souls formula that I think completely ruin the gameplay and strongly encourage a degenerate, unfun playstyle.First is the healing system. Mortal Shell uses the same healing system as Demon’s Souls, where healing comes primarily from consumables and consumables stack infinitely in the player’s inventory. There’s a reason From Soft moved away from this system after Demon’s Souls. Dedicated players can farm or buy a massive amount of healing items, making them effectively unkillable. Mortal Shell attempts to fix this problem by making almost all healing items heal over time. Presumably the intent was to discourage their use in combat. All it really does is encourage a degenerate play style where you chow down on a bunch of mushrooms and then run away from the enemy while you wait for your health to tick back up.(Mortal Shell also lets you heal by parrying, but, like in most Souls-likes, parrying is an advanced technique with finicky timing. Genre vets will be comfortable with the mechanic, but it’s not reasonable to expect new players to rely on parrying for their primary source of healing.)Second is the hardening mechanic. Mortal Shell commits the same sin as Dark Souls 3: poise exists for enemies but not for players. This ends up encouraging a very passive, defensive playstyle. Mortal Shell attempts to solve this problem by introducing the hardening system. In the middle of any animation you can turn your character to stone, and enemies that strike you in this stone form will be knocked off balance. This ability has a cooldown so that you cannot tank every attack in the game by hardening. Like the healing system, the hardening mechanic encourages a degenerate playstyle, where you’re encouraged to harden, knock an enemy off balance, get a few hits in, and then run away until your ability to harden comes off cooldown. The hardening system also means you don’t really need to learn enemy attack patterns, since you can just run up to them, immediately harden, and stagger them off their first attack.You’ve probably noticed that both mechanics I’ve highlighted encourage the same kind of degenerate playstyle, where you’re encouraged to frequently run away from the enemy and wait (either for your mushrooms to finish healing you or for your harden ability to come off cooldown). This is the optimal way to play the game, and the only reason not to play this way is your own impatience. I played the game more aggressively for the most part, but any time things got dire (e.g. coming to the end of a hard boss fight and I’m low on health) I reverted to this degenerate playstyle because it was the surest way to win.It’s a shame these two changes ruin the gameplay, because there’s a lot of other things to like in Mortal Shell. Visually it’s very impressive; I’d argue it’s the second best-looking Souls-like on the market, behind only the Demon’s Souls remake. It has great level design; the hub is incredibly interconnected and the three dungeons showcase great linear level design. And the Shells, with their hand-crafted perks, provide much more variety and replayability than Dark Souls’ stat system; no two Shells feel the same to play, even when using the same weapon. It’s just a shame that these positives are shackled to game systems that, when played optimally, aren’t fun. I hate to give this game a thumbs down, but I just can’t recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRGraphics/art design: 10/10Story:2/10Gameplay:9/10Sound Design/Music: 3/10World Design: 6/10Main Mechanic(Harden):10/10Time: 13.5 HoursTotal Score: 41/60Completion Time: 13.5 hoursPlatform Completed on: PC	While Sekiro was a game that was born from the ideas that formed Dark Souls and Bloodborne but very much maintained its own identity, Mortal Shell is about as close to Dark Souls as you can get without being Dark Souls.  Sure, there are a few minor differences such as the main system of defense being your body instead of a shield, but other than these small things, this game is basically Dark Souls on a budget.  But let’s get into the main aspects of the game, shall we?  I will still be scoring based on story, gameplay, sound design, world design, graphics and art, and the game’s main mechanic on a scale of ten.	Let’s begin with the story.  Mortal Shell, as you will soon find, follows many of the tropes found in Dark Souls.  This will be the first example of many.  Cold Symmetry, the developers, went for a nearly entirely lore-based story.  We get some miniscule snippets from the small number of NPCs around the world such as Sester Genessa, Corrupted Sester, The Old Prisoner, and scant few others if any.  The rest of the “lore” can be found, in similar fashion to Dark Souls, within the item descriptions.  These are brilliantly written with such magnificent descriptions as “Hallowed Sword: A Heavy Sword with a hollow at its center.”  The item descriptions, if you didn’t pick up on it, are a little lacking if the developers wanted to give much information to the player.  The story, as far as I was able to tell, followed the exploits of “The Foundling” and their quest to feed organs to a prisoner so that he, the prisoner, may ascend.  That’s basically it.  This game leaves the player a little wanting for story.  In the category of story, Mortal Shell scores a 3/10.	Second is gameplay, possibly the shining facet of the game.  The movement feels weighty and solid to a comfortable degree.  One way in which the game does separate itself from the Dark Souls franchise is to add an additional step to the rolling process.  When the dodge button is pressed, the character does a quick sidestep, reminiscent of that from Bloodborne.  If the button is pressed again in quick succession, the character then initiates a roll.  Rolling consumes quite a bit more stamina, but also has a wildly increased number of Invincibility frames compared to the sidestep which already has a massive number.  The game is extremely generous with the I-frames to say the least.  Unfortunately, I think it may be necessary strictly because of the developers designed their hitboxes.  In most games, the active area of a hitbox, on a sword for example, is the blade, the part which is being swung to deal damage.  In Mortal Shell I was given plentiful reasons to believe that the devs made the entirety of every weapon being swung the active part of the hitbox for the entire duration of the swing.  This means that when the player takes their opportunity to strike directly before or after a strike, a stray part of the weapon such as the hilt, can still hit the player.  This on top of being able to be hit multiple times by a few attacks, is maybe my biggest problem with the game and part of the reason that I still think that one of the most difficult bosses is a variant of the tutorial boss that has a weapon with a particularly long hilt.  Other than this very minor flaw, the combat feels good.  It flows nicely, especially with this game’s specific mechanic (which will be covered later) in play.  The game also revolves around a system in which the player collects “shells” from around the game world which are, presumably, the corpses of once great men.  Each shell has its own stats and upgrade tree which can be expanded via the use of the game’s currency.  As one quickly finds when watching speedruns, the best shell is no shell.	I suppose I should put bosses in their own section in games like this which have a boss centric difficulty system, if you understand what I mean.  There are five bosses in the game, one of which has five variants.  There are also three mini-bosses in the game.  In total, this makes twelve bosses.  There is one which is far and away the best (Tarsus, The First Martyr), but they all share similar difficulty and design (Except mace Hadern.  Screw that guy in particular.)  Beating the three main bosses (and a few mini-bosses) grants you access to the final boss.  This game, while it certainly does it’s best to mimic the Dark Souls franchise, falls a little short in difficulty, at least to the experienced SoulsBorne player such as myself.  I almost failed to mention a cool little mechanic built into the parry system.  While the parry timing is really strange in comparison to the games this one mimics, your parrying tool, the Tarnished Seal, alerts you to incoming attacks from outside your vision, such as a jumping grab from above, as well as to attacks that cannot be parried.  The parry even has a couple different affects, such as healing the player, planting a bomb on the enemy, or freezing the enemy in place.  A fairly novel and welcome mechanic.  In the category of gameplay, Mortal Shell scores a 9/10.Review Continued In Comments.

_childDocuments_.review: I platinumed the game, so you could figure out I got a bit of experience with it. Hear me out though.The game satiates the souls lust in a good manner. That it does well. Really really fun. And challenging. This is why I kept playing the game, and finished eventually platinuming it, for the challenge. If you're into Hades for example, the VC might be for you.Now onto the bad part. I will just lay down a list of bugs, improvements and experience breakers I encountered so far:1. In my 1st playthrough, after successfully defeating Crucix (just after landing the final hit), the game crashed and I had to do the whole fight once again. I reported this with F10.2. I got stuck into a wall while trying the Axatana weapon ability3. Some hitboxes are not well synced with the animation (special mentioning to Tarsus)4. At some point, while fighting the last boss in VC, I lost my ability to harden. Been spamming LT with no effect.5. While at a pillar, I got the option to update a Legendary boon to... a Legendary status. So basically no effect at all, waste of potential boon slot.6. Rolling while locked onto an enemy feels a little bit out of place, and can be extremely dangerous (the camera rolls unnaturally and really fast), especially when you're next to some cliffs7. Faceless Clerics are sometimes knee deep into the floor, being unable to move from that exact spot8. While in VC, after buying a lute, the price will still be visible, leading to confusion (it can be safely equipped though, just a visual bug I guess)9. Sometimes projectiles go through walls, trees, etc.10. You might get hit while finishing crawling (during the animation) and there's nothing you can do to prevent it11. You might get hit during a recovery of a stomp attack (during the animation) and there's nothing you can do to prevent it12. We should be able to skip cutscenes during VC runs13. Loading times could be quite a nuisance sometimes14. Lock-on should lock onto the enemy in front of you rather than the one closest to you; major inconvenience when fighting multiple enemies at once15. Sometimes when you die, you can still move the character. I think the trigger to this is dodging almost instantly after dying.16. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of the bad reviews I've read are from people who haven't taken more than 30 minutes to figure out the combat in this game. You don't have unlimited rolls and parries in this game. You need stamina for those things. Souls-like games are hard. Also, the fact that a few of you obviously rage quit because combat was harder than you thought makes this game more souls-like than any before it. Now for my own thoughts..this game continuously impresses beautiful new locations and punishing new enemies as you get further and further in. It's a sleeper gem, almost a masterpiece in it's own right, It is truly unfair that it's recent reviews are "mixed" because people don't understand that souls-like games are hard.EDIT: Okay, now my thumbs up is going to a thumbs down. I've realized why so many people were saying the combat is trash. It's because on PC, the dodge and parry mechanics intermittently do not work. Like pressing dodge during a fight rolls some dice on the backend that decides whether you'll dodge or just slowly walk in the direction you meant to dodge while getting one shot by a boss you've fought 50 times. Dodge is the main defensive mechanic I use, but parry is also so unreliable that I've completely stopped trying to use it. To the devs.. If you're going to make a souls-like, where the combat is meant to be super punishing, you can not allow the game to be released when the two main defensive mechanics bug out 1 out of every 4 times you hit the button.

_childDocuments_.review: "Mortal Shell" presents itself as a promising soulslike, but it disappoints on various fronts. The combat system is slow and unresponsive, and the hardening mechanic quickly becomes repetitive. The levels are confusing and poorly designed, making exploration frustrating without clear direction. The variety of enemies is limited, and boss fights are uninspired. The difficulty seems artificially increased through the use of unfair moves rather than well-thought-out design. I love the genre, but "Mortal Shell" is a disappointing and frustrating experience. The roguelike DLC makes things even worse and extinguished what little desire I had to play the game. I appreciate that it was made with a small budget and a small team, but the experience still needs to be enjoyable and, above all, fun. It is not.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this review by saying that this game is weird.This game has a lot of good and fresh ideas. One of them being the shell (5 total in the game) mechanic.That system along the limited number of weapon (5 melee, 1 range) acts as the class system.Mix and match those to find your playstyle. However, you start with a greatsword (second fastest weapon). After the tutorial, you're thrust in a long tunnel to crawl through. At that point, you properly enter the game.You can now easily find your first shell.If you stay without one... You die in one hit, of course, one of the requirements is to finish the game this way. That was not fun because of some awkward enemy placements. Combat and movement is sluggish. Once you return from a dungeon you'll come back to the hub engulfed in mist, give an item to an NPC, find another dungeon... Rinse and repeat. While there's fog you'll encounter ghouls that'll instantly jump on you. With your only defense is a dodge (never managed to get it) or a parry.The parry time is off by a lot (same as most of your attacks, does not apply to enemies though). Those two mechanics are your only defense. The previously mentioned range weapon is useless in combat as it's so slow you might never have a hit unless an enemy is walking towards you like the nameless king.To run the game with RTX, you need to hop in a beta that severely impacts performance (i went from ultra up to 120 fps to an average under 30 fps). With or without that, the game crashes very often (averaged to one crash every 20 minutes) leading me to lose my save multiple times, there are a ton of graphical glitches, one enemy type in particular made me go down to 2-16 FPS no matter the settings.Feel free to check my specs on my profile, if it's too much trouble : I have an RTX3060 with 12go vram in there...By the way, if you use the RTX beta, you'll have no control over the settings, due to that, you'll be locked in a worst looking version due to intense filters.The main game has a hub :Kinda like firelink shrine slapped in the middle of darkroot (far more confusing) that will change in shaded woods (the part where you find Vengarl).3 dungeons (Basically Iron Cove, Frozen Eleum Loyce and a maze made of what feels like chiralium and obsidian)...That's all.I finished the game under 20 hours (counting the lost saves in acccount). Feels like a demo and a re-release on the new gen makes no sense. I went offline and turned my phone off for the last playthrough due to how stressed i was through it. I got a massive headhache out of it. If what you want is pain and a weird trip but can't afford DMT, this is for you. Wait, maybe you've just gone hollow... that could explain you reading that.THAT'S IT! What are you still doing here ? Do with that what you will. I'm out.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best Souls-like game i ever played, enjoyed every aspect out of it, Optimisation was topnotch and didn't face any clunkiness either. _childDocuments_.review: Had a bit of a rough start, but by the end I did enjoy this game.There's a strong lack of tutorials, a reasonably difficult-to-navigate central area which drove me insane, and some jankiness with certain mobs which makes parrying challenging. There's a great sense of weightiness to everything you do - which is great in combat, but in the UI - menu transitions etc felt slower than they needed to be. Every path feels a bit too challenging early on, but quite easy by the end. The ranged weapon covering your visual indicator for parries also isn't fantastic. Enemies will spawn in right in front of you - which can give a nasty surprise. There's also some iframe quirks you can abuse - like how with the DLC weapon, you can transform it between 2 forms on a whim but are invincible through the transition - which unfortunately feels a bit cheap.With that out the way - When you do get the hang of parrying + hardening, it feels extremely satisfying tearing through enemies. A lot of design mistakes are made up for by the fact that you can harden at any point to avoid damage. The weapons all feel pretty good to use (especially since you can harden to offset the drawback of a slower weapon), and the shells each offer a unique feel to your playthrough. Once you've found your footing and vaguely know the areas/items/etc and find the right weapon for you - the sense of empowerment carries you right through to the end. The game looks fantastic, and I enjoyed looking at the details up close. A HUGE plus is also that they made use of regional pricing, which for me was a massive win.If you typically do enjoy Soulslikes, I'd say give Mortal Shell a chance - but maybe do some research early on to mitigate the rough start. It won't be better than Souls, but it experiments with a few cool things which sets it apart. I wouldn't hate seeing a more polished sequel which learns from these mistakes.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be deterred by the (currently) mixed rating!Mortal Shell almost-perfectly captures the "what the ♥♥♥♥ am I supposed to do now?" vibe that the original Dark Souls had. The combat is punishing, the character designs are creepy, and the weapons hit hard. Yes, it has a few frustrating flaws (e.g. enemies occasionally spawning a few metres away, awkward AI tracking, and the very disorienting first zone), but Mortal Shell is a great game nonetheless. It's a crying shame the reviews are so average.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started playing this game, I was very confused why it had "mixed" reviews on Steam. I enjoyed the combat very much. Blocking by hardening your entire body was a very unique aspect I've not seen in any Souls game. And the fact that you can do it in between ANY action in the game just won me over. The controls in this game, overall, are very responsive and fluid. Any time I got hit by any enemy I had no one else but myself to blame for not timing it right. It wasn't until I finally completed the base game and started playing the DLC (Virtuous Cycle) that I realized where the negative reviews were coming from. It's SO bare bones and lackluster in content that it really shouldn't be called a DLC so much as a wonky patch update. No new bosses. No new areas. No new skills. Just rinse/repeat by rushing through the same base game while acquiring random power-ups (which CAN be cool; like freezing nearby enemies whenever you dodge, or poisoning them, but that's basically it...) and being given no healing items in between. And to get all the achievements (according to a YouTube source) it'll require about 6 - 7 FULL runs?? Yeah, no thanks. I usually 100% my games; especially the Souls titles, but this is one I'm going to have to put down and walk away from until I really have nothing better to do with my time.So, despite what I mentioned above, I'll be giving this review a thumbs up because I still believe the base game IS good and worth playing, but just be warned once you get to the DLC. IT IS GARBAGE.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has completed the entirety of this game on a no-hit run, I can safely say this is a great beginner souls-like. You get the ability to harden (negate a single, or any/all arrow attacks) without getting staggered or getting hurt. The only catch is that it takes 5 seconds to harden again. Alongside the harden ability, are VERY generous i-frames when you dodge or roll. As you play the game, you unlock "shells" which are forms that you take over and get bonuses to them. Some have more health than stamina, some have more generous rolls, others have way more stamina than health. You have the ability to mix and match which one you want to play the most without having to farm for 15-25k souls to BEGIN a build. The only thing you need to do, is play the game and follow the paths the game gives you to find them.The majority of enemies only have 3-4 attack patterns so you don't have to do a lot of memorizing per enemy. The game is designed like a branching path, and to find your way around you have what are called "instincts" that you find around. When you gaze into them, it gives you tips about the way to go for the next enemy/weapon/shell. If you've never played a souls-like before, or you want an easier one, this is a great pick.

_childDocuments_.review: What to say? I played for a couple minutes, found the combat with mobs dull, did a little speedrunning, drank some tall goblet, died to a boss, and got to writing. I feel instinctively like this is some attempt at playing with some existential theme using environmental storytelling (the tabula rasa protagonist who steps into the skins of others, being put into the world after being devoured by a fish, and the opening crawl) which is all very nice, but I'd like to enjoy the games I play. Far too many mobs too, imho; I saw the sheer number of them as I ran through. No way am I wasting my time fighting that many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - the combat is nowhere near enjoyable enough for that.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Not necessarily a bad game, but not a great one either. Decent ideas, but poorly executed. I'd save up for better options, scarce as they are.As someone who's constantly on the hunt for more action-adventure games focused on combat and exploration (recently commonly branded as 'souls-like'), I picked up Mortal Shell+DLC for 4 bucks thinking it might be a good fit, but I'm pretty disappointed.First off, this is not like Dark Souls, despite the grim, dark fantasy vibe. It's combat is more akin to Sekiro, focused on a few key weapons and mechanics over offering a large build variety. This is where the first problem arises, since the controls feel pretty off. Both with controller and keyboard, it's really hard to get used to the flow of combat when the response to your actions is either too slow or too fast. Dodging in particular feels awful and it's especially aggravating when you notice how poorly managed the tracking feels. I've seen enemies do a jump attack and turn around to chase me when I try to pass by while still floating in the air.Plus, stamina management is absolutely awful. Two or three attacks and you're immediately out of options until it regenerates. I've seen people argue that it's just how the game is meant to be played, but that just doesn't mean it's less of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ creative decision. The hardening mechanic is the only interesting thing, but I wish it had more interesting applications rather than just an extra block/parry.Combat is the core of the game and it's mostly lackluster. The ambience would be nice if it weren't the most generic dark fantasy universe ever conceived. Plus, it's difficult to feel engrossed or immersed when all I'm thinking is how annoying it is to navigate a map that's just a collection of hallways that go through a forest. It's so frustrating to try and find your way through a maze when every damn intersection is exactly the same as the last and the following. As for the plot, I don't even know if there is one. That's how engaging it is.I'll possibly keep playing because I'm a masochist and have nothing better to do, and because, in the end, it's not as horrible as other examples of the genre (i.e.: Bleak Faith or Sinner), but I don't think most people have the same degree of patience I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A very nice lil' Soulslike game true to the originsWot I liked- Combat is definitely it's best point. Comboing attacks, hardens, parries, dodges and weapon abilities create a lovely action packed action;- All weapons have their own niches, some slow but have more stagger (could use more damage too), some are faster - basic stuff but well implemented;- The linchpin Harden ability gives the combat its distinct flavour to transcend the game beyond another Dark Souls clone;- Ambience is very Soulslike, actually it looks like the Dar Souls idea ran through a thesaurus (not entirely sure if it's a good thing though);- Virtuous cycle is a great DLC - the roguelike runs are an awesome way to utilise the otherwise small areas. The combat mechanic is honest enough so you mosltly have yourself to blame for dying;- You can fall down and push enemies off cliffs;- Enemies get stuck in their own traps;- Lutes!- Lute solos!!Wot I disliked- Very few weapons (5(6(7))), no other gear, few consumables, classes-shells are hardly different;- It's a small game. I've sunk 10+ hours running around the first swamp map, but many people run through the whole game in a couple of hours. And you can complete an NG+ run in 30-60 mins no sweat;- Bugs & glitches - quite a surprising number for such a short game - I've had character paralysys (can't attack or use abilities), crashes, ragdoll glitches, getting stuck in textures, falling through the world, enemies pop up, mobs walking off ramps to their death, weapon skins disappearing, SF artifacts, noninteractive object (items/souls/shells), immunities/skills not working properly;- Kbm control scheme is not as good as the controller;- Mobs love to track you too much making dodge less effective;- It's a pity that the virtuos cycle does not implement fully randomized maps;- Unhelpful item descriptions: this shroom will heal you for 30 HP. Great! How many HPs does my character have?- It's a pity the game does not have PVP. There're few classes and weapons so dishing it out with fellow players in some arena could be cool. Also, killing Axatana Hadern was the most challenging and most fun experience (I didn't really grasp harden before axatana boss);- Can't say I'm happy about the late Steam release. We got a free DLC with my favorite shell so I guess it's ok.To sum it all up, the game is basically a charming one-legged cripple who quite proficiently carries itself on one strong leg. Combat is responsive, hefty and brutal enough to keep you entertained. Your characters won't become strong enough to ignore damage even from weak brigands. Games like Mortal Shell help me appreciate Dark Souls even more. Mortal Shell has 1-2 Dark Souls size maps, about dozen enemy types, 5(6(7)) weapons and "classes", and it's an enjoyable standalone game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: First off this game is absolutely STUNNING. It's a solid, dark fantasy RPG. It's definitely distinguished itself from Souls like games. Some better players have done this game in half the time I have, but I really wanted to just run around and enjoy myself, and I'm average to below average skill wise. Still, that's not stopping me from enjoying this dark story(still playing it). While there are some minor inconsistencies with the parry mechanic, this has not stopped me from enjoying this game created by fifteen people. By far my favorite game of the year. And for the price? WORTH IT. Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: The only soulslike games I've played are Sekiro and Elden RingYou might wonder why I gave up after a singular hour. Well, to summarize, it was the lack of direction. You have zero clue where to go or what to do. In Elden Ring, there was a map system, and the sites of grace would give you a general direction of where to go next, not to mention that the open world of ER had clear distinction between areas. In Sekiro, you had a barely legible map, but you could at least go to higher ground and inspect the area before continuing.In this game however, you are thrusted in a swamp, with no map, and no way to get to higher ground to see where you could go next. You start in an area with multiple exit points, that lead to areas with even more exit points, that some of them circle back to the original area. This for me is incredibly confusing, and after beating the first boss I randomly found, I still had no clue where to go, wandering around aimlessly until I gave up. The player should not have to commit the world to memory.Great atmosphere and novel system (where you inhabit dead knights and get their abilities), but the total lack of direction is not it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: -GIFTED FROM A FRIEND-I would say Mortal Shell stands out as a good Souls-like, while having it's own identity.  The starting area can be tedious, but with proper exploring and usage of items it becomes more fun. The lore is fragmented and sometimes difficult to understand, but interesting. Bosses are challenging but defeatable or else I wouldn't have defeated the game. Cons I can think of is the short amount of zones, enemy diversity and bosses.. but then again it's a small company with few employees; another thing is that you need to be certain of which build you're going for, if not you need to farm for a specific currency and there's also limited amount of weapon upgrades; the game also gets a lot easier when your shell and weapon is fully upgraded. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art design, sounds, and game mechanics. The combat was challenging, and the sounds and weight of each attack, both player and enemy, made each encounter feel meaty. The game was a bit on the short side, but I actually appreciated that it didn't overstay it's welcome.The one issue I had with this game was with the leveling. I liked the separation of playstyles into different shells, but it felt like the power curve had the player way too weak to begin with and way too strong to end with. Perhaps a greater variety of enemy difficulty near the end of the game could have helped.Definitely would recommend and I am looking forward to a sequel! (hopefully)
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: I regrettably played it to completion. One of the worst games I have ever played. Just a few highlights- The equivalent of souls in this game are almost entirely useless, since your stats cannot be changed and you cannot level up. They are instead used to unlock passive and active skills, which don't help much at all, and are completely useless against most bosses.- Because of that, there is no motivation to actually fight the enemies. Just run past them to the next boss.- There are so many enemies placed around the map that it makes Scholar of the First Sin blush. To top it off, there are no checkpoints in levels, apart from one halfway through an area. It can legitimately take up to 10 minutes to run through one of the areas from the checkpoint to the boss, with hundreds of repeat enemies placed along the way that can kill you in 2-3 hits, and there's nothing you can do about that because no levelling up.- One of the bosses makes you take fall damage before the fight, which takes away 80% of your health.- The final boss is one of the worst I've ever experienced. It just spawns a bunch of enemies while teleporting to the other side of the map and spamming AOEs, and it has a massive health pool. It's a 6-10 minute battle of attrition against a boss that has 3 attacks in total.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this review is coming from a Dark Souls fan (especially 2 and 3).I picked up this game yesterday and I'm having a blast playing it. Now don't go into this game expecting a Dark Souls level of polish or as much content as Dark Souls has to offer. But you can expect to be entertained with 4 different classes (the 5th in the DLC) and a combat which I enjoy alot.This might be a Dark Souls clone but its the best one yet and its doing its own thing with the Harden ability and the dieing mechanics.I have yet to discover alot more aspects about this game and I will seeing as how I can't stop playing it lol.Do yourself a favour, if you are a DS fan, pick this game up and you will not be dissapointed. You will only be dissapointed if you expect this to be the equal of DS3.I just hope we will see more classes (shells) added in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent Souls-like game. Short and sweet doesn't overstay and has pretty straightforward mechanics.The good:Great Atmosphere.Unique mechanics, the hardening plays a interesting take on being offensive/defensive.Animations are great, the skills and parries feel awesome.For the price there is enough content, I know some complain the game is short but even full price it's pretty reasonable.Run's great. No lag or stutters. The Meh:I'd have liked more monster type enemies? Majority are all humanoids even bosses, perhaps it was due to the parry system but a little more variety would have been nice.Story is a little vague, doesn't seem to have concrete direction but had mystery to it or maybe I didn't get all of it.The bad:I understand that they were trying to use the parry system as a way to heal but depending on which Shell you use it was sometimes more punishing to try and learn parries if you play a Low HP Shell and if you get clipped there is no way to get HP back besides using consumables. I'd have liked a type of Flask or HP pot so it doesn't feel punishing when you use a bunch of consumables on a boss fight and die and the next attempt having nothing. Maybe just a personal preference.Sometimes got stuck in the map moving around.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review off by saying that I find it very hard to believe that some of the people who left a negative review on this game have ever played or finished a Dark Souls game. There are generally good criticisms of the game and I understand why some people have issues with it, such as performance issues, enemies turning around fast, or some of the enemies randomly appearing out of no where, but there are people who put .4 hours into the game and call a quits and refund because the enemies and the game mechanics are not exactly like Dark souls, or is too hard and unforgiving. Also there seems to be a significant amount of negative reviews on Steam because the game released first on Epic, so much so that when I opened steam to buy it I was surprised by it being "mixed", I had to actually read the reviews because I thought there was something dangerously wrong with the steam version of this game. No, just a bunch of negative reviews because the game was on epic first. I think that a lot of people should actually play the game and review it based on that, rather than wasting $30 to make a point that it shouldn't be on Epic. Either way, this game does have some flaws and they should be addressed.   There are a lot of complaints about this game not being "enough like Dark Souls", going as far as to compare this games mechanics to Dark Souls. The first thing that should be addressed is that this is not a Dark Souls game, it is a souls like game created by a team of around 15 people. It is easy to tell that this game was inspired by Dark souls, however, the overall mechanics and the way it plays out is not going to be exactly like Dark Souls, and people need to keep their expectations in check for that.   The first major complaint I am seeing a lot of is the fact the game is unforgiving and difficult, or the enemies are hard and do not have consistent attack movement. This is where my statement at the beginning comes from, where I do not think the people who compare this game to Dark Souls have actually played Dark Souls. You cannot walk into a Souls game or a Souls like game and expect to be able to pick up things and kick ass immediately, that is basically the whole point of the souls experience. Getting your ass kicked then ultimately kicking ass as time progresses. You cannot put less than an hour or 2 hours into this and expect to be the god of the world you just entered, people need to take time and learn this game, it is a completely new and unique experience. I dropped into this game and had a tough time at the start because it was hard getting used to the enemies. But that should be expected considering your character just started and is at the lowest they will ever be. Once you get the hang of things and the new hardening mechanic the game becomes much more manageable with its difficulty.Another complaint I am seeing is that enemies turn much faster than people are used to. I have seen about 3 reviews saying that people are used to being able to go behind an enemy and get a back stab like in Dark Souls. Unfortunately, back stabbing is not in this game, however, the criticism for enemies turning faster is warranted. I have encountered a few enemies that turn around unnaturally fast as if their character model pivoted 180 degrees without an animation for it, and if this is what everyone is experiencing all the time, then so be it the developers should slow it down. I am surprised by the amount of reviews that have this as an issue for as little as I am seeing it happen when I am playing. This is not to dismiss any of the criticism, I just find it odd as to why it has only happened to me a few times. I think most people are noticing this issue on a specific mini boss fight towards the beginning of the game since that's where I have seen a few of these reviews talk about it. In my experience I didn't bother with that mini boss till I got a new weapon and had already beaten a few bosses. I went back and was able to take him out after a couple tries. Sticking with complaints about enemies, there is an issue that I and many other players have experienced where you can be running around the map and suddenly an enemy will spawn right in front of you. Majority of the time the enemy is sitting down in my path so I can run right past it but there have been other times where they spawn in standing in your path and you have to fight them to progress. This is another issue the developers should take a look at and fix, because it can create issues when you are fighting in an area and suddenly another enemy just pops out of no where killing you. Either way, considering all of this I think Mortal Shell is a damn good game so far. I am able to overlook some of these issues I noted considering Dark souls has multiple issues of its own. 15 people were able to create this and I find that very impressive. I have had fun with my experience so far and I am excited to fully finish the game. If anything changes I will definitely update my review.Edit: After finishing the game I stand by my belief that I think this is a damn good game. I still think those issues previously mentioned can turn people off, and I do not blame them. However, in terms of the enemies rotating 180 I only experienced it a few more times after the review, but it was nothing game breaking by any means.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels similar as any Dark Souls game regarding playability and dark fantasy setting.The combat can be challenging if you act too impatient or careless but it's balanced and enjoyable, the bosses could have been harder though.Besides the known dodge mechanic, you got the harden mechanic instead of block and shields, where you become a stone while holding the button or until you get hit absorbing the damage and it feels forgiving as you don't lose stamina when getting hit while using it.The game doesn't feel very RPG like, there is no character creation, customizations, armors or jewelry. Instead of wearing armors you wear a shell. There are five shells in game and they must be unlocked by finding them laying around. Each one offers unique stats and unlockable passive skills.The skills are limited, 2 per weapon, but you must find the weapon's item upgrade first to use the skills and requires resolve which you fill by hitting enemies. Also you have 3 different parrying effects if you got resolve and one of them can heal you but you need timing.There's no magic or archery ways to play, just melee combat.The game is kinda short but easy to get lost if you get distracted meaning you might spend time walking around the places trying to find where you should be, making it feel lengthier than it actually is. Also there are no side or major quests just the main story and the enemy variety is small but since the game is also short it's not an issue. The game looks good visually speaking and I only had a few minor problems like getting stuck sometimes due to not having jump mechanic, but rarely happens and you can just return to the main menu.It's a good and challenging action game that can be sometimes frustrating like any game under souls like tag but it's worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: It's not without its merits, there were certainly some "hahaaaa, nice" moments, and some cool ideas, but, mostly dull bosses, (I don't think one has ran away from me that much since Elden Beast), repetitive enemies, some pretty unfair feeling hitboxes, some glitches (now you can't roll! time to die), there were a couple of times I was like "I dunno if I can be bothered going back to it". Basically, it was okay. If you've played all the fromsoft titles in the genre, and this is on a big big sale, it's maybe worth visiting. It's skippable though.

Definitely recommend it, especially for the price when i bought it ($27 for the game and DLC was free).I see a lot of people complaining that its not as "refined" as Dark Souls, yet trying to be Dark Souls.Fromsoft has so much more experience here and is a much larger developer than Cold Symmetry. And even with that, Cold Symmetry did a really solid job here.Are the controls clunky? a little. But i got used to them quick, using KB+M. alot of people are just quitting before the 2 hr refund window and not giving it a long enough chance. First hour was rough. Now, game is really enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Dark Souls 1-3 and Bloodborne, even though it's still had it's bad moments especially one of the areas was just annoying AF. However overall I still think this is a good warm up to the Souls-like genre if you never played one before because it's a shorter game and the mechanics are more forgiving thanks to hardening.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it, not matter how cheap it is.The one thing they don't copy from souls games is an healing flask. You have to pickup up mushrooms with an healing over time effect, which are spread across the world and on a timer. Oh did you spend all 5 of your mushrooms before you died? Enjoy having no heals because the mushrooms across the space you just played through are on a cooldown. Oh you picked up a different mushroom? It actually poisons you with no other effect.Also get used to attack a max of 2 times if you wanna have stamina for a dodge. Gameplay is basically attack 2 or 3 times, use the block that is on a timer, wait for the cooldown and repeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: It grabbed me at first but after about 3 hours it feels like a slow slog to get anywhere.  There is no direction which is what I like however the level design is horrible.  There are these little areas you need to crawl through so getting back is a chore if you push too far in the wrong direction.  Things can be going great, in fact, too easy, and then all of a sudden your mobbed and dead. Crawling through little holes to get back to your body...hopefully.   Graphically it looks nice, and the atmosphere is pretty cool, but the combat is slow and boring after a few hours of play.  DS and alike keeps things interesting by giving the player a sense of discovery, while this felt like I was picking up a bunch of useless items.  The familiarity levels were cool, but again, most of the items are kind of useless.  I'll keep playing through, maybe, from time to time, but it just doesnt feel engaging enough to pull me in right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: There's a part of me that liked this title and a large part of me that didn't. It's a slow and methodical souls-like that can be fun once you understand its combat, but the title is so short that when everything culminates as an experience you just feel whelmed. Honestly I have such a hard time sorting my feelings on this title. It's just a very middle of the road souls-like. It's not bad, it's not great. It's a title that if you think you'd like it you should get on sale if money is tight or full price if you just wanna support the devs.In closing Mortal Shell is the generic brand souls title if ever there was one.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Playing a back log of souls like games.This is like a souls game, and it has a lot of interesting elements to it- however it looks too much like they saw the difficulty and flair of the souls games and were like "Okay we'll do that" but they forgot that "Difficult" doesn't have to mean taking options away.Healing is scarce and limited and barely does anything, no map, no real sense of direction or ability to properly figure out what you should even be doing.This turns what could be a real cool experience, into just meandering around aimlessly.Many things look the same as well, so without a map or any navigation tools it quickly becomes a boring experience, and constant flood of enemies that pop in like 10 feet in front of you like it's nightmare creatures on ps1 while you have no healing -EVER-, just turns it into an awful game.The best way I cam sum it up, is that it's like they copied what folks love about souls games- but forgot to copy the necessities of them that make them work.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the worst examples of artificial difficulty i have ever playedIt is either hiding additional enemies just barely outside your field of view or straight up dropping them in once you get close (specifically looking at the enemies that latch onto you and keep biting you.) The geometry of the map is poorly optimized. i should not die to enemies for the literally being unable to move because i am stuck to a tree stump or (my personal favorite) the remnant of my past life. yes. it can literally stuck you in a way where you are unable to move.dont get me wrong, the graphics of this game are good, the gameplay? not so much. dying because you get stunlocked or literally oneshot by regular enemies are one thing, but the gameplay loop remains the same: start combat with an enemy, deal damage, harden and wait to get hit (which you can do infinitely apparently), dodge out, wait for harden to recharge, repeat.also one quick thing on the Martyr boss. when he sticks his sword in the ground for the ice storm attack, dont be fooled, the visual effect for the ice storm may have ended, but the hitbox lingers. Dont rush in there thinking you actually get a window to punish him for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: It defo needs a few more bosses! Good fun if you're into souls like genre. Playing this game after beating Elden Ring is refreshing. Was looking for something to sate my palette. It is stylish in its own way. Visuals are very high fidelity and story is decent. Sound is very crunchy and the haptic feedback of the vibration is very satisfying.Quite an underrated game seeing how it has mixed reviews, still better than other open worlds out there.9/10-1 no map-1 discovered cat too late (that's on me)+1 you can pet cat
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: As a non-souls player, I very much enjoyed this. I could tell where some bosses where lacking significantly in design and mechanics but from a smaller studio it's to be expected. Wasn't TOO difficult and kept me going. For a first run this isn't bad at all, it's quite good. I really don't understand the recent negative reviews. Yes it's lacking content but it's also not $59.99. I will 100% be buying any future Mortal Shell games from this developer and other future similar projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Mortal Shell

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Shell is a deep action-RPG that tests your sanity and resilience in a shattered world. Your adversaries spare no mercy, with survival demanding superior awareness and precision. Possess lost warriors, discover hidden sanctums, and face formidable foes.

name: Calico
detailed_description: Calico is a day-in-the-life community sim game where you are given an important and adorable task: rebuild the town’s cat café and fill it with cute and cuddly creatures! Build up your café by filling it with cute furniture, fun decorations, yummy pastries, and get it bustling with animals again! Calico is meant to make you feel all warm and fuzzy inside. The gameplay reflects that with a laid back, low stress creative environment to explore and play in. Character Creator The Calico character creator will allow players to create their own magical person to experience the world through. There will also be plenty of clothing to choose from and collect throughout the game! All Animals are Interactive! The player will encounter many animals in the world of Calico. Once befriended, you can name them, add them to your party, or send them to their new home at the café. Animals in your party will follow you everywhere you go and listen to your commands. The animals in your café will relax and play with any customers that pop in for a visit. Café Decoration Your task in Calico is to bring the town's café back to life again. This isn’t just achieved by bringing in cats and animals alone, however – you can also decorate your café with furniture of different styles to create the perfect cozy home for you and your animals! Cooking Minigame Create a wonderful café by making yummy baked goods and drinks for the townspeople! Learn about your follow villagers to pick and choose their favorite foods to sell! Magic of Calico We wanted there to be no limits to how you could find happiness in Calico. Magic potions are a system that allow us to break the rules of what is possible and to find what would be most fun. Example: the More-to-pet Potion allows the player to magically turn a single animal giant-sized! You can hang out with a giant animal, or even ride a giant cat!

Magic potions are a system that allow us to break the rules of what is possible and to find what would be most fun. Example: the More-to-pet Potion allows the player to magically turn a single animal giant-sized! You can hang out with a giant animal, or even ride a giant cat!
short_description: Calico is a day-in-the-life community sim game where you are given an important and adorable task: rebuild the town’s cat café and fill it with cute and cuddly creatures! Build up your café by filling it with cute furniture, fun decorations, yummy pastries, and get it bustling with animals again!

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game in its current state. I was and am still really excited for the potential this game has, but it seems to be very buggy right now and I personally found it to be unplayable (animals randomly disappearing, reappearing, clipping through things, townsfolk congregating in a solid wall by the cafe gates and getting stuck, etc.) Very cute and I may come back to it in the future once there has (hopefully) been more work done? :(
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Peaceful and fun little cat game. It'll take you around 5 hours, 6 if you achievement hunt (I left the game running a bit on the title screen by accident). Also more animals than just cats, though I still had pudgems on my head most of the time. I wound up muting the music and listening to my own, but great for a chill afternoon or two to unwind.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is chill, cheerful, beautiful. The soundtrack is amazing, the story is sweet. I'm enjoying it. The game itself is about six hours long, but there's a lot to do still, and I will enjoy playing it some more, and potentially making a new cafe owner and doing it all over again. :) The only critique I have is that it's not very mouse and keyboard friendly, but that's okay - they tell you in the intro screen that it's more suited for a controller, but I don't have one, so I made it work. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable game. However, I still encounter the bug with the Owl Club but a quick exit and relaunch fixed it for me to continue. I would recommend this game, its lots of fun and I spent hours exploring and questing the first half of the island. I did find that once you unlocked Costal Cove the game progressed a lot faster then the first half and suddenly I was done the quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: The game is adorable, the stories are entertaining, and the characters are captivating. Running around and collecting animals has never been more fun. The game menu is a live-saver, letting me instantly switch animals from my party to the cafe to "free-roam", all I have to do is pick up the animal one time to collect it, which removes so much stress. Flying at the end of the game is extremely fun, and the quests are not annoying in any way. Also, decorating my cafe is pretty awesome. Overall it is just such a chill game, I feel like I am in my own little slice of paradise.If you look past the occasional visual glitches, this game is perfect. I recommend it to anyone who wants to escape reality into a magical and cute little world of their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME. Seriously, it's charming, cute, sweet, soothing, and most of all, it's just FUN. At one point, I was a cat, holding a cat while riding a cat, who had a cat on its head. I got my money's worth in the first half hour. Yes, the UI is rough and there are a lot of glitches and bugs, but honestly? Most of them are really funny and don't effect gameplay at all. Frankly, I feel the animals glitching out and contorting into weird shapes or spinning in circles is a feature. This game knows exactly what it is, and it goes as extra as it possibly can. God bless u, cat game.I desperately hope there's future content and expansions, possibly including more furniture and maybe some more character creation options like face shapes, but especially one that adds romance options, because being able to kiss a cute witch is just about the only thing that could possibly make this a better game for me. Really though, just let me pet more cats. Please?Well, that, and add a possum.In conclusion: i love u, cat gaem

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews for games, but i HAVE to for this one. IT'S ADORABLE! If you like cute things and cats, this is the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: very very cute fun game :D the art style and environment brings me so much joy. i just wished there was more to do after the mainline quests, maybe some more furniture and clothing too. id be super excited for an update if there were ever to be one in the future, but it is an indie game so i can understand that not happening at least very soon ^^

I wish the customization for colors was a bit easier to manage on keyboard and mouse, and there are a few glitches here and there, but nothing game breaking and nothing that can't be fixed with a quick reboot of the game.If you love animals, adorable characters, inclusiveness and enjoy magic, this game is for you, hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

It's like a cute, sparkly, playground filled with cats and other cute animals!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a big fan of cutesy girly games and you also love animal focused games this is a game for u! This is definitely one of my favourite games despite its simplicity and cuteness. It is a relaxing but entertaining game where you get to run around and bring home any animal you meet along the way, dream come true! The entire game has a very magical cute and witchy vibe to it that made it really enjoyable for me. Plot- the plot is the most simple I would say, it isn't very deep or you know amazingly written...you basically: complete tasks, built a cat cafe and unlock different parts of the island that are all extremely cute and magical in their own way. Once you have unlocked all areas of the map it just all feels very worth it and I love seeing the design for the last part of the island it was really beautiful.Art- personally parts of the art really fit what I like as a person, you know cute little rainbow mushrooms, magical cats and lots of pastel colors. The video game graphics are so and so, the game can be a bit buggy and the overall art just looks like its in its early stages of development sometimes. There's not much detail which is definitely something that could be worked on. Overall I still really love this game even though the art is lacking a bit and there is not much of a plot but the cuteness is definitely overwhelming. The game is still pretty new so I hope to see more progress from it!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely hilariously brilliant! I am really sad that the game is so short, I completed it in about eight hours, and after completion there's nothing else to do than run around and jiggle kitties. _childDocuments_.review: It's cute!! Really cute! I love the adorable animals, the relaxing soundtrack and the general aesthetic. The magical setting, giant loving animals, goofy stuff like picking creatures up and twisting them around has been what I've been looking for in a cozy game for a while. I like the little cats in their construction hats, and the giant cat stuck in the log. Stuff like that warms my heart.But booooy, do I wish there was more. I really thought this game was in early access.It's very fetch-questy. It's a pacifist island so, of course, there's no combat. But there's also no puzzles, or rhythm-mechanics, nothing to rebuild to progress or... anything. Which really only leaves you with "hey, go here, get this, bring this, do it again but somewhere else, bla bla." The quests you do solve, like the poison plants, are ultimately solved by someone else and you don't even see it happen. Just, "yep, thanks for bringing me this thing, guess I'll get rid of the plants."There is no farming, no gardening, no caring for pets... There is a baking minigame, which is very sweet, but also optional. It doesn't matter if your baked goods go stale either, because characters will buy them with zero consequence anyway.The characters are all identical in personality. They all adore you from the get-go. It would be nice to have some friendship building or possibly even romance? Maybe one could move in to your cafe with you?Apart from the clothing shop, all the shops have the same items in day after day. There's no crafting, so forget making your own stuff.It's also quite buggy... Stuff clips through the floors, dialogue doesn't always show up, animal followers randomly disappear forever, animals that live in the cafe fall from the sky whenever you return. Like others said, cute concept! Needs more. It has the potential to go from a good game to a great game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very adorable to play, there are a lot of customizable features to make the character you want, I love that and wish more games had such a unique feature. The UI utilizing furniture around the cafe is nice as well.  I find the general environment very relaxing to go through; but I have a few problems that make the game unsatisfactory for me. I think the game's way too short for the type of simulation experience you'd want. In the 6 hours I've played I befriended nearly everyone on the island, filled up my entire cafe with items, and reached the credits.  By the end of the game it feels extremely rushed to go through, and besides the achievements it wasn't rewarding whatsoever. I LOVE the variety of animals, all very cute and active.  But the humanoid characters were very bland in personality.  All of their designs are great, but there isn't any dialogue to discuss with them once you finish their tasks.  It's like if you take villagers from animal crossing and they just don't have anything to say after you do 3 things for them, they're just wandering NPC's. The environment, while diverse and pretty at first glance, begins to look very dull after the first couple hours of playing, you'll get through the side quests relatively quickly and there's just these wide open dead spaces with nothing to do but collect animals for the cafe.Speaking of the cafe, I filled almost all of it within the first few hours of playing as well, there really needs to be an expansion to utilize all the furniture options, because it fills up so quickly. Overall the game feels pretty unfinished, there needs to be a bit more content, more characters, more dialogue, and more spaces to fill in between all the empty environments, before I think it's really a game worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t really mind the shortness some people mention, as I figured most of its value lay into its customization options and collections, which I am thrilled about ! I thought the cooking mechanic  was very fun as well I’m very biased but I love all the relationships, I really thought dynamics between characters were very sweet, and of course, cute cats everywhere. while the clipping through surfaces can get annoying at times, my main problem is that for a game that’s best played with a controller , it seemed fairly unintuitive, And a lot of actions did not have a key/ button tied to it ( maybe this is an individual issue ) when playing with a controller. putting that aside i really do think it’s a very sweet game, with very endearing characters 🥰

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... well, if you asked me to describe my ideal game for relaxing after several weeks of sleep deprivation, this is pretty much what I'd describe in my sleep-deprived state. It's both sweet and the most delightful kind of ridiculous: there are business cats running punnily-named businesses, construction cats napping at work... oh, and you can ride a giant cat. While wearing another cat on your head. And optionally being a cat. I definitely recommend playing this with headphones, too - hearing aforementioned giant cat purring is incredibly soothing.I also really hope more games will adopt this style of character creation!There are, unfortunately, a few downsides: physics is slightly... different (but then, you might argue it just adds to the charm... except when you try to bake and throw an egg across the kitchen), and it does feel sadly short - it took me five hours to open all paths on the island - but I've heard the devs will be adding more quests with time, and I certainly hope I'll have more excuses to return to this wonderfully weird world.
