_childDocuments_.review: okay so, the game just feels incomplete and almost impossible to control, even with a controller. dont get me wrong, i LOVE the concept, and the art styles very charming, but it feels kinda lacking. the character isnt satisying to move around, and is slow to move which is kinda inconvient with such a big map.  i'd love to give this game another chance in the future after its given some time for updates but for now its a no from me

_childDocuments_.review: A very heartwarming and soothing game! There is no violence or bad language in this game, it is just doing nice things for nice people on a beautiful island full of wonderful animals and mystery. The music is sweet like a lullaby. The potions to customize the game time, weather, animal size, etc. were a really fun addition. Cuteness++ Affirming on many levels - Different body types, genders, faiths, cultures, orientations, etc. are represented. Different, but not all. I understand there have been some issues with people wanting to play a male character, and not all faiths/cultures are presented equally. I hope this game is a launching point to something larger in scope. I've finished the game in 12 hrs and there are 3 achievements left. However, I see it as a game I will keep coming back to just to visit people, pet and ride animals, and customize the cafe.I had minor issues with some mechanics and bugs. I wasn't a fan of the cooking mini games, especially when the developers changed them, the mechanics were iffy on a bunch of the recipes. I had a few animals glitch out on me, especially with the flying. In general the game ran fairly well, nothing really frustrating about it. I hope they do more with this game while keeping it simple and chill. Being able to build a larger cafe would be nice :)Finally, I've seen some rather scathing reviews of this game. If this were a AAA $60 game, then yes my expectations would be different and this review not so glowing. However, as a $12 indie game, it is quite satisfying as it is, with updates and additions welcome :)    I highly recommend it and it is one of my favorite games :D Perfect for cozy game time or after a rough day.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It was adorable! <3 I would definitely suggest this if you like cute, relaxing, & fun games that make you smile. It is short and sweet. It can be a bit glitchy at times, but I don't regret playing it at all. I giggled a lot. Very enjoyable!You run a cafe. You get to do a sort of fun mini cooking game within the cafe. _childDocuments_.review: TDLR at the bottom. It's... okay. It's fun at first, but I got bored so fast. I expected a lot more from the game based off of what I've seen and heard. There's a lot of potential, though. This is somehow my longest review.CONS - The characters are a little weird looking. It's really hard to get a masculine looking character. When I tried, it looked like an adult sized toddler. When I was creating a character and chose the clothes, I couldn't get out of the selection menu without pressing escape twice, once to get out, and another to cancel completing the character. The running animation is... interesting, to say the least. It also made my character look like an adult sized toddler.  The map can be buggy, especially on the path leading up to Autumn. The map is also huge, which takes ages to run around to find a mount. The black birds glitch when you pet them. Annd a lot of things don't appear until you're super close to them, even with the settings maxed out.The NPCs are also pretty boring in my opinion. Sometimes the dialogue options are two sets of the same answer to a question, which made me think that it didn't matter what I said.PROS - That being said, the animals are cute. I like the animal-human hybrids. The giant cat blocking the tree tube is adorable. The cooking minigame is fun, and I like going around collecting animals. The artstyle is adorable, and I really like the loading screen art. Jiggling the animals when you pick them up is my favorite part of the game.TLDR; OK. Boring, animations are wonky, map can be wonky, but adorable. It can be definitely relaxing if you're stressed, but maybe that's the game boring you enough to forget the stress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked cute, and the thought of managing a cat cafe sounded fun. Seemed like a casual, fun game.However, it is very lacking and a disappointment. Cuteness is all it has going for it, and then nothing else. There is not any substance to the game. Really, all this game is a animal collector pretending to have a story and cafe management.You're not even managing the cafe all that much. The mayor mentions that you'd have to build it up but there's not really anything to build, if anything it's in weirdly fantastic shape with the way it's implied it's been shut down for a few years. Sure, you have to run around and purchase or otherwise be given different recipes, and sometimes you have to remake them when they go stale, but otherwise nothing really matters.  As others have said, the baking minigame is really just annoying and kind of grating after the first few times, and I had a controller so it was an easier time, but truly, there is like no way to get a gold star on any of these given the platforming mechanics and the elevator are just too slow. Once you meet someone, they just show up to your cafe whether you're there or not, purchasing something and then leaving after a set amount of time. No budgeting to purchase ingredients, you're not able to upgrade anything about the cafe, you're stuck with 6 display items no matter how many cases you purchase. You're not even doing much of anything with the furniture or animals because there's only two quests where someone even adopts an animal and I've honestly just grabbed both from outside and handed it to them. Really, all money does is allows you to purchase cosmetics and the few recipes you don't get doing any of the fetch quests. Honestly, if this wasn't advertised as a cafe management type game it would probably be less disappointing.I was surprised to finish the main "story" under 5 hours, and I wasn't even really rushing at all to do it. The story is really just "oh no, all these areas are blocked off, go clear them by doing endless fetch quests and talking to people" which, like. ok. This isn't really all that fun, all things considered. Lots of wasted opportunity for little minigames for quests, especially for the magic ones, but the characters just talk at you. The characters are cute. There sure is a faint whiff of worldbuilding here, and it's... eh?, the best way I can describe it. "Teehee, everything is magic" like i guess so. Kinda wish there was a bit more. Or even much actual choices besides starting furniture, dance moves, and whether or not to invest in different cat businesses, which honestly seems pointless not to since you just are drowning in money the entire time. Like, what was up with those city cats anyway? We'll never know, just city cats are bipedal and only like 6 of them speak human, but only once.The extra time on my playthrough was me attempting to get all the achievements and then immediately realized the tedium of trying to find and pick up all the animals in the game, so I settled for recipes and quests and then quitting. It is truly a very empty game. This is also just a general annoyance and nitpicky, but while it is nice to have the character be fat (oh sorry, "fluffy" - calling it this makes it slightly more annoying imo, but sure, whatever, it's there at least) there is no way to just not have an hourglass figure. Like if you wanted to have a girl main character just do that. The facial hair options are kinda nice but you're out of luck if you wanted to not have visible curves, and also they just look bizarre at certain max slider ranges.  Customizing colors is also a pain on the controller, and there's not really a way to save any colors (or if there is it's hidden or so obtuse my brain forgot it on purpose).  The gradients just don't look very good after lots of fiddling, tho that's probably on me for trying to do gradients so much. They only really work on the long tails and your shirts. I got this on sale for very cheap, but honestly I don't think it was really worth it for me personally. If you want to kill five-ish hours or are more motivated than me to 100% the animal collection, then go for it, but I wouldn't pay full price for this. I would listen to the people complaining about the cooking minigames in this animal showcase being an utter nightmare on keyboard and mouse, because controller was only marginally better. Really what killed this was the advertisement as a cafe management sim for me. I'm a fan of restaurant sims and this was really a collect animals and do fetch quests simulator, which is not anywhere close to being the same. The customization was merely ok to a little annoying to navigate on the controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game! The main things that drew me to this game were the character creator and how non-gendered it is, and the aesthetic of the game is just so cute. It ended up being better than I expected when I met all the wonderful characters, including some rare non-binary representation! Nearly all the characters were super cute and easy to become attached to, which made finishing all their quests a little sad because they had nothing else to say. :(Pros:- LGBT+ representation that feels so normal and natural to the world, including lesbian couples and trans/non-binary characters.- Non-gendered character creator that lets you individually change the shape of your body and not force you into picking male or female character models - including clothes, hairstyles, and facial hair that aren't restricted by gender!- Overall cute aesthetic from the environments to the character designs.- The animals are pretty fun to pet?- Fun and varied environments and great NPCs that make for a great world to explore and interact with.Cons:- The game is short and once the quests are over, there isn't a lot much else to do.- The character models are pretty janky (mainly your player character and especially the animals) which results in a lot of limbs clipping through the model, and tons of ragdolling. Though if you like Goat Simulator, you might enjoy the wacky physics.- Not as much customization of the face as I'd like, and the textures for many clothes are pretty flat.You're supposed to be the new owner of a cat cafe and on one hand it's fun customizing it and you don't have to work very hard to keep it running, but it was also pretty easy to forget that running the cafe was supposed to be the main goal of the game. Watching the NPCs come to the cafe and buy stuff from you was pretty great though, like they do more than just standing around and actually seem as if they have a life of their own.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a simple she-man. It has gay, I buy. It has thicc, I buy.This is one of the most wholesome games I have ever played. While there are glitches and bugs, it’s still very charming and adorable. It’s definitely a favorite of mine as I just love this concept of befriending animals and being able to interact with them like that. It’s such a cute little game, and I love how inclusive it is with some of the characters! Not to mention the awesome customization! I feel every RPG should have this level of customization. I also started playing it during a very hard moment in my life.You see 3 days before I started playing this game my cat died suddenly, painfully and quickly on the way to the vet. We were 2 minutes away when he took his last breath laying on top of me. He was on his death throes for a few minutes before I realized what just happened. We don’t know why he died. He was okay, and then he wasn’t. I’ve never experienced anything so painful in my life, and I’ve had rectal hemorrhoids before.I started playing a couple of days after this tragedy and quickly found a cat that looked like my boy. I carried him around on my head everywhere because honestly, I didn’t know what to do then or how to cope with what had happened. My cat was my family. He was only 5 and a rescue. So besides writing a review I’m here to say thank you as well, but from a deeper place in my heart. At first I was on the fence about getting this game, and feeling so lost, alone and so, so deeply sad, but with just a smidge of a smile because thanks to this game, I can still run with my baby on my head. I don’t know if the creators of this game had any idea of what sort of joy it would bring to a deeply sad artist like myself. But I’m so glad they took the time to make this precious gem of a game. And so glad to share it with you. I now play it often with my daughter who absolutely loves it as it reminds us both to our baby. This game has made me laugh and smile more than any game before. I love this game so much. Its actually helped my body positivity a lot. The music is beautiful as well. The cat is a cat song has become our lullaby song we sing to each other. My only complaint is that it was too short!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ahhhhh I absolutely loved this game. Literally my only complaint is that it's way too short! Once you go through all the quests, the game doesn't really have anything else to offer other than maybe trying to buy all the clothes/items? One of my favorite aspects of this game is the cooking mechanics. Despite being a game about running a cat cafe, the maintenance of the cafe is pretty minimal. I wish the items in your display case would slowly sell out as customers come and eat, so it'd add a necessity to continue cooking. It has no impact on the game at that point.Overall, I thought the quests were fun and the game had a lot of charm. The aesthetics were totally on point too. I also loved the inclusivity! _childDocuments_.review: I actually saw this game while it was still on Kickstarter, and I was massively excited for it. I stayed excited for it the entire time I was waiting, and when it came out...I was satisfied.Now, let me clarify one thing here. The game -- at present -- is fairly buggy. There's odd animations, animals get stuck on tables and chairs, and things like that. However, I never once encountered a bug that was more than just odd (or hilarious). there's no game breaking glitches here, no falling through the world, no getting trapped, nothing. It does need some more polish, absolutely, but the stuff that isn't polished is more amusing or ignorable than anything else.The game is honestly ridiculously fun. You start off by building your character from scratch and you can modify every aspect of your body, to make any gender or body type of character you want (mostly). NPCs also have varying body types as well, which makes the world feel a lot more real and colorful. There's TONS of animals, and you can befriend every single one of them, from cats to dogs to ravens to POLAR BEARS. You can make animals big or small at will once past a certain point, meaning you could happily ride around on a giant cat, or have a mini polar bear in your cafe. (This sadly doesn't work on birds, but alas) There are also tons of clothes you can buy, and even some potions that modify your character, like one that makes your hair into an animated galaxy.You can also modify your character at will, straight from its own menu command, right on the fly. Cooking is fun, though stocking is... a little awkward, but it's not a big deal at all.The idea of this game isn't some epic story or major mechanics, or even management like Harvest Moon or Story of Seasons do. It's a game meant for you to play on your own time, at your own pace, in your own way, and to relax while doing it. There's no pressure, barely any time limits at all (and the one I found was EXTREMELY lenient), because the game just wants you to be able to slow down, relax, and just... enjoy it.And it massively succeeds at this. If you want a game that wants you to take a more active role or have to manage supplies, this isn't the game for you, but if you just want a game you can play while relaxing, zoning out, or simply to have a calm and chill time, this is 100% what you're looking for and I would absolutely encourage you to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute, but it does need work. Not realistic looking but there are so many games that don't need to be realistic to look good. I liked the design a lot, and the concept for the game is great. I think it could be really fun, it just needs work on the animations and overall game play. More dialogue options and more realistic conversations between characters would be good too. I should also mention they added visible self-harm scars to one of the more alternative looking AIs in the game. While I do not judge and never would for that sort of thing, I don't think it belongs in video games like this, definitely not how it was done, and at least not without some sort of warning to potential players. _childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny! This is my favorite Indie purchase by far. Any animal you locate (and hold) can be summoned back to you at any time, meaning that if you find more than 10 animals that you love you don't have to tell them all to go back to your cafe. You can summon them from the wild instantly whenever you like. You can ride giant cats with various coats (including one with rotating galaxy patterns that is just beautiful), a white fox, a white husky, a beautiful red fox (I may or may not have relived some David the Gnome nostalgia there), a palomino horse and so many others. I also gave an enlarging potion to a snow owl to use as a flying mount. There are so many different animals you can interact with and ride, including rabbits, dogs, llamas and deer.Your cafe is highly customizable as well with hundreds of different pieces of furniture available with their own unique looks. The cooking sections are probably my least favorite but even some of the pastry preparations are enjoyable. (I cooked every dish once but the NPCs mainly just come in and clean out my coffee. I've had to replenish the coffee multiple times but it's the easiest item to make so I'm not complaining.) There is quite a bit of content in this game and the side quests are mostly enjoyable. I would definitely recommend this game if you're an animal lover. Completion is relatively quick and easy, as well, if you are an achievement hunter.

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is very aesthetically pleasing and has plenty of customization options without being so overwhelming. If you enjoy Animal Crossing, the two are fairly similar in terms of gameplay and how you interact with the island. The game is pretty straight forward: help villagers do tasks, customize your look and vibe with various outfits and furniture for your café, and meet cute cats and other animals that you can either have in a "party" or keep in your café. I love how this game initially comes across as a typical slice of life style game but then introduces a magic mechanic that definitely adds a charming touch. This is a very cute, wholesome game.Overall I loved Calico and it kept me wanting to explore island and collect as many things as I could. However, once you get all of the achievements there isn't really anything else to do that would make you want to continue playing aside from decorating, baking, and swapping animals in your café. I would love to see some multiplayer mechanic as new game plus, or even some additional quests/tasks. Maybe even minigames with your animal pals.I would recommend this game for anybody who is looking for some chill and casual single player Magical Girl meets Animal Crossing goodness.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Light-hearted and very relaxed.  Movement controls are a little clunky, but once you find a mount (relatively quickly) it's not a problem. Character creator OK - the real fun is using items on the animals & decorating the cafe. Bugs present (collision detection between animals, party-members getting suck / removing themselves from the party) but trivial.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- This game is super adorable and comfy. The setting is beautiful, the music is soothing, and all the NPCs are super kind and likable people.- You can RIDE THE CAPYBARAS.- Character customization is great! I kinda wish outfits were more expansive, but as for colors and physical body details as well as the unlockable patterns and designs, it’s spectacular.- I love the variety of animals. Like, I went in expecting mostly cats, and there are indeed a lot of cats on the island — but there’s a wide variety of cats, and beyond that, there’s also possums, capybaras, an alpaca, a red panda, pigeons with hats, dogs of all shapes and sizes, magical animals, sheep, goats, deer, cows, polar bears — I love it. I never get bored of running around the map and then suddenly sprinting up to an animal to pet it, because I never know what to expect.- The cooking mini games are fun! Even when they’re a little tedious (tart filling pool my beloathed), it’s fun to launch myself around the kitchen and carry around eggs as big as you are.- The representation!! There’s so many characters of color, and WLW, and nonbinary people, etc.!Wishes:- I really, really wish this game had PlayStation controls. Like, it’s possible with the XBox controls, but it took some serious trial and error, as someone unfamiliar with the XBox buttons.- I wish the animal accessories (ears and tails) had a few more options. Specifically, I wanna be an owl like Maia and Freya, or a MOTH!! Fuzzy antennae and a cape/shawl would be all it took for both. Cons:- The cooking minigame times can be frustrating. Even as I’ve come to understand the controls and actions better, I haven’t been able to rank above silver on the simplest recipes.- Some people say the controls are janky — they can be in a few places? Honestly, the game is MASSES better when played with a controller rather than a mouse/keyboard. Literally one of the biggest reasons I bought a controller was to play this game easier, and it definitely paid off.- It is really short. I’m almost done 100%ing it and I haven’t even hit 8 hours yet. I wish there was some kind of major endgame / postgame content. Overall, I really recommend this game! I think it’s super fun, super comfy, and a definite addition to my list of comfort games. It’s soothing and sweet and the perfect game to destress with.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute game with a great calming vibe to it. In fact, I’m tempted to buy the soundtrack so I can listen to it while I work. The game is relatively short. You could get 100% completion in 4 hours if you tried hard enough. That said, you will probably spend a lot more time running around petting animals, or holding them while you run around and watch the physics engine bounce them around.A couple of tips, always check your map before going to visit someone for a quest. Several times I travelled all the way to their home only to discover they weren’t there. Once all three people I needed to talk to were at my Cat Cafe. Also, the control are a little finicky, so skipping the cooking mini-game is probably a good idea. You get more money than you need and I ended up with $10,000 by the end, so you don’t need to get the bonuses to charge people more money for food. On the positive side, you can wear a Capybara as a hat. 10 out of 10, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: **EXTREMELY HONEST FEEDBACK**This game isn't worth 10 dollars at all, I'd say 3 at most or less. Like honestly just don't buy it it's literally not worth it unless it's on sale.Character design is extremely pool and at a very surface-level. The game is focused more on being the most inclusive as they possibly can while isolating the most important things that make a good game. Being a game this inclusive makes it easy to farm good feedbacks coming mainly from a group of people that society not always accepts (Lgbt-religion-BLM-overweight) etc. So if you want to play a poorly made game because it makes you feel accepted, sure go for it.Back to explaining: NPC's are extremely bland as they do not have any deep stories aside, once again, very surface level things/facts. Quests are repetitive, the graphic is terrible enough to make you believe this game is still in beta.There's nothing hard to do here whatsoever or any game direction: things would be already challenging or better if you had to gain the wild animal's trust first before letting it into your café but no, you just walk up to this pet and you're like 'go to cafè' and the pet does it. Simply no challenges nor anything to grind, just casually speaking to an NPC with one line dialog that gives 'pattern designs' (which are mad awful). Not many interactions with the animals either aside just picking them up or petting (that isn't as interactive as it could be, like using your mouse to pet the animals, see them react, etc.)This game does not deserve its feedbacks at all, but as mentioned before its purpose was to target a specific group of people which worked well in its intent.The most frustrating part about this game is surely the controls that you have if you play from pc, just extremely uncomfortable and there isn't any settings to change the hotkeys either. The controls aren't intuitive and the HUD is beyond terrible.You can get stuck in certain actions and have to restart the game, glitchy graphics, not being able to navigate with the map open so having to open and close every time... Not to mention this game is special enough to put the map on button 4 unlike almost every normal game which puts it on M. No ability to move the face pattern, or change the eye shine color, or have more color setting options for hair, clothes, etc...Nothing about this game impressed me aside just, well, animals being animals and finding them cute.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, but it's a glitchy mess. I was hoping for a super low effort farm-sim/animal crossing adjacent game. I got a poorly finished disaster. Items despawn, animals float in the air, despawn, melt into the ground, and get stuck inside of fence railings and buildings. The abysmal collision detection means you phase through solid objects you shouldn't and get stuck in weird places on the map. Physics are odd, too. You seem to move in slow-motion, with an odd strafing run that that wobbles the camera as it tries to track your awkward movements. The overly bright cell-shaded graphics make the game feel unfinished, like you're playing in an early access testing ground. The same overly repetitive song plays everywhere on the map until you just shut off the music altogether. Quest objectives sometimes don't update or count as completed even after you've done what's asked of you. Controls feel unpolished because of the jank physics. Just...no. I'm sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend briefly showed this game to me a few years ago, and I thought it would be a cool Stardew Valley-like game, but running a cat cafe. Seems great! You get to decorate the cafe, collect different animals (not just cats) and even make the food for the cafe yourself!Until you get jumpscared by 1: poor performance caused by insanely bad optimisation, and 2: the worst 3D player controls I've ever used.The poor performance seems to be down to the entire game using a single core for pretty much everything. Graphics Card barely gets touched. So even with an R9 3900X and RTX 2080S, i averaged around 110fps, which wouldn't be bad if it was a *smooth* 110fps. I was surprised a game with such simple geometry and textures could run so poorly on an at least decent pc.And then we have the controls...The control scheme itself too bad. Maybe a little unintuitive at worst, but they can be rebound. Some menus may have a delay on pressing the same key twice, but that's nothing in comparison to the player movement. I am genuinely impressed someone managed to make a movement system this clunky. Even I had smoother, more fluid movement when I first started learning game dev through Unity. To make a character controller this clunky (only made worse when inside a building) takes genuine skill, effort, and dedication, and so I think the dev(s) should at least be congratulated on that.Apparently there was a recent patch that fixed some performance issues, so i am terrified to imagine what the game was like before I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Calico is LGBT friendly and family friendly 10/10 recommendWow. Calico is a game like no other. A friend bought this for me off of Steam and its the first game in awhile I sat down to play and found nothing but endless enjoyment. The color scheme is bright and cheerful, the NPC's you meet are all unique, and it does have a short and calm story line. You have a wild range of character customization for such a small game and I found the ability to be a neko in a cat cafe game a cute addition. You make food in one of the most adorable ways I think I've ever seen in a game by becoming pint sized. The game also has extra little things that make it all the more enjoyable, such as potions that do fun effects like allow you to fly, or the ability to get onto the working Ferris Wheel! I will be honest, it has some issues with clipping, and if you ride the horse it will get stuck in Autumns house bowl or the rivers. But these are relatively small issues overall. If you're looking for a cute casual game with lots of furry friends and a spark of magic, Calico is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly cute and cozy, and I do recommend it because of this and the fact that it feels super wholesome and uniquely inclusive. However, my issue with it is I just started playing it yesterday and I'm already a bit bored. It's  TOO easy, even compared to other cute/cozy games. In my opinion it has so much potential but falls short. I read year old reddit posts regarding the issues with the game, and its unfortunate that a full year later the same issues haven't been addressed. Issues such as NPCs not acknowledging animals you've already collected (so you do double the work by freeing and recatching them), they'll also ask you to deliver items to characters right next to them. The game has so many small glitches such as the animals disappearing through the floor of the Cafe, the animals getting stuck in the same spot continually (even after you move them), and a glitch where they all stop using the furniture if you play long enough in one session. Not only do these glitches ruin immersion, but they make me not want to play. The game needs an option for full cafe editing, I'm talking walls, floors, and cafe expansion options. I think a large part of the problem is having so many animals in such a tight space. They literally fall through and render on top of one another. Npcs dont acknowledge being in your cafe when visiting and will proceed to sell you things or give you a quests. Another glitch I'm coming across is customers walking through walls rather than the door when leaving my cafe (This also ruins immersion). The map is unpleasant to navigate, even though you can mount animals to travel- this is bc Its a huge predominantly empty abyss. The city area is sad and the town lacks signs of life besides the shop owners/mayor. All in all, the  game just feels incomplete. It's like they ran out of money and resources and decided to release it unfinished. I am genuinely sad at the wasted potential here. I would honestly love if this title got a rework with lots of added features. It deserves it.

I love the control and UI updates, it's made it so much easier to control.Anyway, Calico is such a sweet, wholesome game- I literally can't say a bad thing about it. I love every single part of it. It's so creative and it will take your mind off the world. Calico is one of my favourite games, and a concept that I actually adore. I would die at the chance to work with this team on anything related!Thank you for all the joy and laughs this has brought me!

_childDocuments_.review: I experienced zero game-breaking bugs. I think they finished patching those on pc recently. There are a few graphical bugs, such as a cat occasionally lounging in midair, but it adds to the charm rather than harming it. The gameplay is more quest/plot-driven, but it really scratched that animal crossing itch for me. Dialog with the NPCs feels very genuine and often made me laugh and learning about the relationships between the characters really carried the plot. They suggested playing through with a controller, but I powered through with my keyboard/mouse and got used to it. _childDocuments_.review: I am so disappointed that this game was such a mess for me, I loved the idea of it!While some of the aesthetic was rough around the edges there were cute moments.  Picking up a cat and swinging it is cute, having a cat ride on your head is all kinds of adorable.The big deal breaker though was keyboard and mouse support.  As in, it's almost impossible to play without a controller.  For a game releasing on Steam for computers, that's pretty inexcusable.  When they say a controller is recommended for "best experience" they mean "playable."  The mouse can't select menu items.  Trying to back out of menus is bizarrely wonky on keyboard.  Trying to use the character creator, which should be a joy, was just a chore.The final nail on the head.. and this is just a personal thing for me.. was the sound they use to generically represent people talking.  The "Charlie Brown teacher" sounds were just at a pitch that was grating to me, and the thought that I'd barely be able to control my character, struggle with the interface, deal with a wonky camera, and have to listen to this sound that was to my ear grating for EVERY CONVERSATION in a game that should be about being social... I am so sorry, I had to back out and ask for one of the things I almost never do: A Refund.For a game to be released on a computer platform, the UI and form factor should support computer inputs.  I had hoped for a somewhat rougher My Time at Portia or Stardew Valley Experience.  Instead, I found myself the kitten abandoned on the roadside.  I hope one day this game could be polished enough that it was playable -- again, I loved the inspired concept and the female-centric narrative, and also have to give props for allowing your protagonist to have what are often thought of as generically masculine features as a woman in case you wanted your story to have reflections of more complex gender or trans* identity (though perhaps being allowed to offer pronoun choices such as "they" might be cool too, considering the protagonist is female but you can even have a beard, for example.)

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad because this game has a very cute aesthetic and seems to have been made with passion. However, the game feels lifeless and static, with stiff, cookie-cutter NPCs and an empty-feeling world. On day 2, I already felt like I had run out of things to do. The NPC quest system seems to largely be the only thing to do in the game, so when you get no quests or when a quest requires waiting, there's just... nothing to do. It's really sad to say, but it gets so boring. I feel like the game would be better improved if it had something outside of NPC quests, like maybe a fishing or bug-hunting system. Heck, it would be good to even let the player interact with the world through something like resource-gathering, but there's just nothing. The world, while cute on the surface, is dead- you can't interact with anything except for the NPCs who might give you a quest so you can continue gameplay. The core gameplay seems to be that you get a quest, do it if you can, and then wait and wait for another with nothing else to do in the mean time. I wanted to like this game, but this is so bare-bones that it hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: I, like just about everyone else, really wanted to like Calico. Don't get me wrong, it *is* cute. It's just not great. I'm always willing to pay up for an indie game, but I think this one is just a little too expensive for what it is. For every good thing it had, there was also some weird game breaking problem, or something that didn't look very good visually. I liked all the cat variety (and animal variety) in general, especially some really fun guys towards the end. Dialogue is repetitive, drawn out, and boring. I really wasn't into it. The characters all looked visually interesting, but were flat in terms of personality. I do like the level of customization you can achieve with your character and your cafe, but getting everything exactly how you want it takes a while, and I didn't find the game fun enough to warrant waiting for everything I like to come into existence. Controls are awkward and clunky at times. Getting anywhere takes a looong time unless you have a horse, but you don't get that until quite a while into the game. Having to slowly make my way up and down multiple, seemingly endless mountains got old after a while. Any large animal outside my house would stand by the window, break every limb, and spasm by the cafe. If I touched a fish in my pond, they would float high into the air and keep wiggling. I love the music, their vocalist is talented, and Meyoco did a great job on the album art. I hope this game updates. I think it is such a good base, but as it is now, it doesn't feel like a very complete game. I think if the developers take the feedback they are getting in this game, they can create a new game (or tidy up this game) into something truly fantastic. I can't recommend in its current state though.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing my first ever Steam review, for this game. Wish I could post a "mixed" because it is really mixed.General thoughts about the game:- It takes a lot of inspiration from animal crossing, cooking mama, farming games and other cute life sim style games.- Many of the mechanics that are present in other games similar to it, have the more "stressful" elements removed, such as no time limits to the game clock, no resource scarcity, quests can't be failed, you can't fall to your death, get lost or get hurt, etc. This was welcome for me.- The physics are not very realistic. You can pick up horses and hold them up above your head, ride dogs up cliffsides, etc. I don't mind this and think it's just goofy and a stylistic choice almost but it may bother some people.Good:- It's really, really cute. If you love animals you will love this game- The writing is funny and quirky and familiar to gen Z/millennials who are very online. I laughed out loud multiple times while playing this game, whether from character dialogue, animal behavior, or from some of the story quests- Fun model designs. I like most of the NPCs, the furniture, some of the NPC houses and the animals themselves of course- Good variety of different animals to meet and befriend including some that were unexpected to me- Pretty good animations for the animals, like the horse running and jumping animation is quite smooth- There is a collection aspect to the game such as collecting all the food recipes, meeting all the animals and NPCs- Some of the potion effects are fun, like - Lots of clothing design and character customization options, and you can mix and match them as you see fit (styles are not locked to two genders)- Unique and inventive ideas with the cooking minigames. All of them are unique and I appreciate that they put in the effort to program these- Some effort was given to representation of marginalized identities in the NPCs which was niceNot so good:- It feels very unfinished in terms of content.  If as much dedication to the main area was given to the other areas, this would feel like a fully fleshed out game, and I would wholeheartedly recommend it even if it still had the remaining "not so good" bullet points.- Some of the controls are frustrating especially during the cooking minigame and playing with toys with animals while using a gamepad. It feels like they get in the way, even though this game is supposedly best played with a gamepad. I used an xbox controller on a regular pc as well as the Steam Deck. I didn't try very hard to achieve gold stars on the cooking recipes but I would be surprised if anyone was able to achieve gold on all of them, the controls are just so frustrating. The controls are also somewhat poorly explained in game and sometimes conflict with each other if models are too close to each other with different context specific controls.- Missing polish/QA that is sorely needed. Some of the animal models especially feel pretty janky when they try to follow you or you pick them up and they ragdoll pretty hard. Some mountable animals such as Horsey the horse will just start running back to the cafe as soon as you dismount, whereas some others will stick around like they should.  I can't imagine either of these mount behaviors are intentional. There is what I assume must be a cutscene toward the end of the game that started kinda randomly in the middle of doing something, where my character was pushed through the bottom of the map and the camera zoomed all over the place while playing credits. My character was stuck under the map until the cutscene was over and it was just panning the camera around through all of the terrain while I was stuck underneath and I couldn't see whatever the cutscene was supposed to be showing me at all. There is also at least one area where your character can get stuck via jumping, near the log with the giant cat in it your character can get stuck by jumping next to the log between the log and the cliff. I had to quit and reload to get out of it within the first few minutes of the game.- Some minor text bugs such as referring to a character (Gabby) sometimes as "he" and sometimes as "she". Gabby looks like a girl and wears a dress but is listed as He/Him in the character list, some characters referred to Gabby as "he" and others said "she". I don't give the developers enough credit that this would be an intentional choice. There are also some cases of missing punctuation or misspelling in character dialogue or quest text.- Bit of a nitpick but the walking and running speed is variable with no discernible reason why- The character creator is definitely designed for a more cute aesthetic and there are far more feminine options than there are masculine or neutral. There are also only maybe 2 or 3 characters who are not female (based on pronouns and presentation, and one of them seems to be a text mishap rather than an intentional use of He/Him pronouns)Overall I would rate this game at a 3 out of 5. I don't regret spending time playing it but it really left me wanting more and wishing that there would be a patreon campaign for finishing the game as it feels quite unfinished where it is now.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to collect cats, document other animals, make tons of friends and help save a small town just by making yummy food, then you might want to give Calico a shot!Calico is a sim game where you get to help rebuild the towns cat cafe, as well as building friendships with the townspeople. Collect different kinds of animals in your journal, as well as toys, many different furniture styles, and silly potions! Even if you just want to run around on an arctic fox (or dog) for hours on end, you can! It's a completely adorable take on a sim game that keeps you entertained and smiling. This game was really fun! I didn't quite expect a full "cat sim" game, so it definitely felt more fun to me. I loved just running around completing quests, finding animal friends and exploring such a beautifully crafted game! Although sometimes it just stopped playing music randomly, but that's okay. The music was quiet, nice and overall a relaxing feel to the adorableness of this game.The graphics in this are just downright ADORABLE. I could not stop smiling while playing this game.I loved every single animal, the furniture designs were on-par and the entertainment was high.There wasn't really a 'story' per say, but it was still really fun to progress through the quest 'story' mode and build friendships, a cafe and an animal collection.If you want to grin from ear-to-ear for a few hours as you play a feel-good game, then this is it. The bugs are minor (and mostly entertaining - hello flying cats?!) and it just brings a whole lot of joy into your life for such a small price. I recommend this game to anyone. No seriously, anyone. We all need a good smile-fest.You can read my review with game stats here:

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest about what this game is, and isn't. This game isn't a deep exploration of moral grey areas, or trauma with deeply flourished character drama. If you are expecting a story rich rpg with creative solutions to complicated problems, and characters making flexible ethical decisions on which rail the trolley car goes down this is not it. And it's not meant to be. It's a game where you can ride a giant red panda. It's a water color and pastel world where you open up  a cafe. It's not complicated, or difficult. It's designed as a pretty soothing experience, that is both joyful and wonderfully unchaotic. And that's how you should judge it.Roger Ebert, the great film critic despised when people, specifically other critics, would compare films to the greats without context. He hated the star system he was forced to use and would rather people have context for his opinions in his sometimes lengthy reviews of films. You should not judge Calico, which succeeds at it's intentions and goals quite favorably for its intended audience, the same way you'd judge Pathfinder, or Mass Effect. You should see the positive qualities in their intentions, just as Roger Ebert saw with 2001's Evolution when he deliberately did not judge it to the same bar as Citizen Kane. And then you should play Calico, and ride a giant red panda through a beautiful forest.

_childDocuments_.review: From the beginning, it took a bit for me to really get a feel for what I was playing here. I received it as a gift from a friend, and honestly thought about dropping the game after the first 30 minutes as it wasn't what I was expecting. This is marketed as a cat cafe management type game when in reality its truely a cozy life-sim where the majority of gameplay is fetch quests and chatting with the NPCs in and around town. Many quests involve traveling from one NPC to the next, either delivering or picking up an item to deliver to someone. The main enjoyment I got from this game was exploring the map and collecting the cute animals. It really felt like a love letter to my younger self, little me would have adored this game. Adult me was skeptical, but I did enjoy my 5 hours with this cozy game. Diversity is a major plus in this game, as there are a few Lesbian couples, a non-binary character, and many different types of bodies represented. None of this was "forced" and I found it to be a breath of fresh air compared to many games with all male casts. There were many cute animals to chose from, and the recipe mini-games were really fun the first time around. The map was large without being too big, and the late game travel options made cleaning up achievements a breeze. Not a lot of masculine or gay rep, which I see some complaints about in discussion posts. Sadly it seems like the devs aren't making any more updates, so it seems like that is just something this game doesn't include. Its for sure got a more feminine vibe even for your own character customization, so keep that in mind. There are also quite a few bugs in the game, but through my playthough they ended up adding to the humor and charm of the game instead of being game-breaking. The recipe games were fun the first time, but eventually became a chore and I only found myself cooking the items that I needed to for quest. If you love cooking mini-games, then thats another plus but it was not a part of my expectations going into this game. For a $12 game I expected a bit more polish and content, but on a sale price it is worth the playthough. Just be aware that even though it is marketed as a cat-cafe game, that is mainly a background aspect so maybe pass on this if thats what you're looking for.TLDR: An ACTUAL Cozy game where your primary gameplay is meeting the townsfolk and completing their fetch quests. A few bugs, but overall a cute game to pickup on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a charming quest/collection game. You do various tasks for the towns people, unlocking new areas of the island map and finding unique animals along the way to add to your collection. You also must find recipes for your cafe!Character customization is robust within the genre: you are a magical person in the vein of Madoka or Card Capture Sakura. I could wish for some better detailing on your costumes, but I understand what needs to be prioritized for launch. You can also change your look at literally anytime; there is no need for a potion or a ticket/coupon to be purchased in game if you want to change your hair, your eyes, your skin color, or your outfit. It's simply an option toggle. LGBTQ+ is well represented with non-binary pronouned characters and multiple gay couples. You get to put cats on your head to 'store' them, and ride other giant cats. It's pretty great.It isn't very long, maybe a week of evenings. Replay will be for patch updates and any new content added later on. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of this game for quite a while and I'm so happy to finally play it! It's a charming and peaceful little world, perfect for when you need a breather from anything hectic going on in your life. Very Important features include the ability to pick up and rotate animals in your arms (they all have names!), putting animals on your head as storage (the birds T-pose majestically), and shrinking down to the size of a hamster to assemble ingredients and follow recipes, with comically over-the-top physics as the cherry on top of many components (cat jiggle physics!!). Currently has a bit of weirdness as to be expected at initial release for an indie game (I encountered a bunny with a glitchy character model...poor Stanford), but I trust the wrinkles will get ironed out in due time!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes!! You Can Pet the Animals: Calico Reviewed by @Palkuka﻿I want to reiterate to you that in Calico, you can pet every animal in the game!!! It’s every gamer’s dream! I could end the review there because it’s reason enough to buy Calico, but let’s dive into this sweet, magnificent, and colorful game. Calico is an adorable addition to the sandbox genre of gaming. It has bright and happy environments, cheerful music, and the best part is that you can shelter animals you find in-game. The premise is that you had just opened a magical café in a fantastic world of friendly neighbors and free-roaming animals. As you venture around, you can tame animals to follow you in a party, or send them to hang out and be the main attraction of your café. You also collect furniture to spruce up your café and also use magical world items. Those items slightly change the experience you have in the game, but most of it is cosmetic for the fun of it. It’s a cute game for all ages, but definitely a game to relieve stress and unwind.The first thing you get to do in Calico is customize your character, so have fun doing that for an hour… or two, lol. It’s really inclusive of how much customization they’ve programmed for character creation. It opens up a wide range of body types and allows you to represent your own body type or any body type you would like. Later on, you can find outfits and clothing that are mostly colorful and cute. Once you’re in the game, there’s a short explanation on how to name and collect animals, and then it’s time to have fun. There’s no hurry to do anything and it’s all about making your café as cute as it can be. There’s a really cute cooking feature too, but I’ll leave that as a surprise because it’s imaginative and fun. I ran towards every animal and started filling up my café with cats, birds, a red panda, and I really wanted to find a snake, but I haven’t found one… yet. There are short and easy quest lines that are simple but involve quite a bit of travel around the map. Later on, you’ll be able to tame bigger animals and mount them to roam around. I would try to remember names of the NPC’s because some of the quests ask you to visit those neighbors.Calico is such a stress-free game. You should definitely add it to your collection. It’s peaceful and whimsical. I highly suggest buying Calico for PC on Steam because there have been technical bugs on the Nintendo Switch version that still might need a few more patches to work out. Calico was developed by game developers who represent the LGBTQIA+ community, which is even more of a reason to support this game. I really want to see more queer game devs in the future, so please support Calico and get your copy today.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a cat café themed management type game. I can hardly say I was expecting ‘Recettear’ style gameplay but understand there is nothing remotely management about this game like you might expect. You can buy and create recipes but that’s about it, each recipe only needs to be made once to be able to sell many and you don’t even control the price. I still love ‘Calico’ though, filled with flaws and extremely shallow but so very sweet and wholesome. Noticeably - one bug I encountered had a cat stuck orbiting around me for the rest of the game but I honestly didn’t mind.‘Calico’ offers brilliant customisation options for your avatar and is very inclusive of many body types and representation. The same goes for furniture in your café/house and you can adopt animals other than cats. At times the game can feel very ‘Ghibli-esque’ in presentation and story, it’s a magical slice-of-life. The quests are very positive and the way to bake is hilarious. Unsurprisingly, there is no combat (not that there needs to be); quests focus primarily on adding themed items and animals to your café, finding lost items/animals and exploring; forming a very relaxing and chill experience. I hope if a sequel is ever made (or future updates added) the café side of the game is greatly expanded on - the potential is there.

You're limited too many how many animals you can have in your cafe and on you Along with how many you can wear.Finishing the "story" is super easy. But it's not meant to be for the story. This is obviously for someone else. And for them, this probably will be their favorite game of all time. Just not me.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: 6.2h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (7 achievements). No. is a quest-based game intended for casual players where you explore the island and finish the quests given by the residents. In doing so, you'll be able to interact with many types of animals and ride them to your liking.- A lot of side quests to do- A lot of animals to ride- Walking speed is slow without the right animal- You can't aim properly in the baking minigameIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 looks unique from other games with its pastel colors and simplistic design. I like the choice to give a gradient to the buildings and characters' colors. The gradient color is also done perfectly to match the pastel color palette. That being said, I found the visuals sometimes distracting, especially due to the animals following you and blocking your sight when you are baking something.There isn't much story in . Most of them either revolve around the quest you are in or how to unlock the next area. To be honest, I didn't pay much attention to it either since they didn't catch my interest.The game is divided into two sections: the first one is where you have to explore the island and finish the side quests given by the residents, and the second one is where you are baking pastries to be sold in your "cat cafe". Well, it's not exactly a cat cafe since you can place any animal in your cafe, though. The animals can be found in the wild, where you can choose to either follow you, go to the cafe, or roam free in their natural habitat. encourages you to use the animals found in the wild as mounts to travel. Different animals have different walking speeds, and you can only ride animals that are bigger than you. At first, this might sound problematic, but it will give you no issue later on since you'll be able to convert smaller animals into bigger ones. That being said, it can take a while to explore the area at first due to slow walking speed until you can ride the animals.There are a lot of side quests that you can take. These side quests can be done alongside your main quests, although some of them will be locked until you progress the main quest. They are usually simple, ranging from talking to someone, selling a certain pastry in your cafe, to catching some animals. However, clearing them can take a lot of walking, which again, can be problematic if you don't have a fast-walking mount.The baking section pretty much acts like a minigame. It's optional unless you want to do it to finish a side quest, and simple. You just need to follow the given instructions to finish it. However, the instructions can be vague for first-timers, forcing you to look around to figure out what the game means. Different recipes will have different instructions, and you need to either finish a quest or buy a recipe to unlock it. Baking all recipes might feel repetitive, but doing so is not mandatory - the quest that requires you to bake recipes will only cover some of them.There will be some sort of grading after you finish baking the pastries, and those who want to seek some challenges can attempt to ace them all. I found it to be challenging, especially since it gives almost no room for error to do. Moreover, it can be hard to throw objects to the right location in this minigame since you can't control where you are throwing at except by moving your position.The game doesn't seem to do much about the cat cafe part, though. You are not mending your cafe at all; you just bake it and put it on the display, and people who want to enjoy it will just come to your cafe and purchase it themselves, even when you are not inside the cafe. Moreover, customers come randomly, and you won't get any profits if you keep on sleeping to pass the next day. The pastries can get stale, though, and you need to do the baking minigame again if you want to replace it. There was a button to skip it, but I didn't find it to be working on stale goods.The game has a lot of customization. You can customize your character and your cafe. It will be limited at first; you need to spend money to unlock some of them. However, I found the character customization to be focused on females. There are only 2 male hairstyles as opposed to 5+ female hairstyles. That being said, you get most of your money through finishing the side quests, meaning that it is almost impossible to buy everything. You don't have to worry, though. You'll get a lot of money to cover most of them as long as you are not blowing your money on furniture.I finished everything at 6.2h. The game is very easy to complete; you just need to check the quest log to find what you are supposed to do, and if you don't know who you are supposed to talk to, there is a character list that you can check, along with a map that shows where the said character is currently located at. The only problematic thing that you will find is to figure out where all animals are located, but there are a lot of guides online that you can consult for that. is such a cute, relaxing game. You need to finish side quests while riding the animal that you like to explore the area. Moreover, the music is also nice to listen to. It can be a bit boring to some people, though, especially those who don't like slow-paced games. If you are a casual player in need of a relaxing game, buy it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Cute but too short!While it has some RPG elements and  Management Sim elements, ultimate this is more of a Walking Sim-Exploration game. This isn't a criticism, but if you were hoping for more of the Management Sim stuff, this may not be for you.Pros: Extremely cute style, wide customization options, can play with a ton of animals, devs leaned into the wacky physics engine for very entertaining results, lighthearted.Cons: Short (finished the main game content in maybe 5 hours), little to do post-clear, limited interactions with characters after finishing quests, fairly linear.I do recommend Calico and enjoyed it a lot, but be aware that a lot of the enjoyment comes from you the player deciding what to do. There's quests to get every NPC up to three hearts, at which point they won't have new dialogue for you outside of rare other quests (usually another NPC's).  Ultimately this feels more like proof of concept than a full-blown game. There's QoL options that are pretty solid (like starting the game with a potion that instantly warps you home, great if you get lost or stuck) and what bugs I remember running into tended to be more entertaining than anything.The BGM is chill and pleasant, there's a wide variety of cats and non-cats to play with, the NPCs are interesting, the humor is fairly solid and fits with the overall light and wacky tone. I found out that if you 'store' a carried animal while wearing headgear, the animal will then get that headgear... forever, so my town is full of jackalope cats. Also there's a cat the size of like a double-decker bus blocking locations at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, relaxing game but also very basic. It is perfectly suited to young children who enjoy the aesthetic, but not great for someone who wants a game with a long term goal or to actually be a cafe manager. I recommend this game if you just want something simple to do with no stress, or if you like decorating and exploring a non-aggressive environment (this game has no combat or enemies).The 'cat cafe' aspect is very simple - Animals you find in the wild or in the street can be picked up or spoken to, then requested to go back to the cafe, and that's it! They will go by themselves and be hanging around when you get back. You can pet them or apply stuff like magic potions to make them big, small, or have sparkly colours, etc. There is no requirement to provide care to the animals - you never need to do anything to keep them happy like feed or play with them, or even give them any friends. The cafe is more like a house for you to play around with, and for the animals to inhabit. When the animals are made to be big (or if they are big already) you can ride around on them for exploring, and you can ask some of them to follow you. If an animal is small, you can pick it up and wear it on your head to carry it around.For decorating, you can buy furniture, wall hangings, floor mats, plants, and recipes from people in town (or earn through quests), place them wherever you want inside or outside the cafe area (recipes are stored in a cook book, and cooked items are placed for sale in a display case). You never need to buy ingredients for cooking, and if you cook something once it never sells out - From memory I think you need to cook it again if you take it out of your display case. The cake decorating shown in the trailer is not in the final game! Instead you become very small on the kitchen bench, pick up each ingredient with two hands and carry them into the mixing bowl.Different customers from town will arrive depending on the types of items on display - sweet, savoury, etc, and will buy the things they want. If you don't have something a person wants then they will never visit. They immediately buy what they want when they walk in the door, and you don't need to be there to interact with them, you receive the money no matter where you are. They only arrive during 'business hours' (6am-6pm in game).
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: OK I am 3 hours in and I can honestly say I am in love with this game.. love the avatar creation, love the village and the characters, love the animals and all the little touches, i went in pretty blind so there was alot of little things i didnt expect! My only gripe and its a teeny one.. is the cutaway walls , id like to be able to control that but hey thats a minor gripe! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a very adorable game! You can interact with every animal by picking them up and wiggling them around - placing them on your head and petting them until your heart was content. The animal interaction seemed to be the main focus of this game, finding your favorites and hoarding them. You can also customize the Calico cafe with a few different styles of furniture and it did not take me long to fill up my cafe.  The most charm came from the Cafe itself.  Once you got to the village and city it felt very hollow and there needed to be more shops and homes to bring the world to life. The character designs were very unique but dialog was lackluster and quests just came down to "please go ask/find" which did not feel rewarding.  I still enjoyed my time overall and hope to see more in the future:3
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a game that I had high hopes for, but unfortunately, it didn't live up to my expectations. Despite its cutesy aesthetic and animal collecting aspect, the game failed to draw me in. The lack of depth and challenge is a major issue, with quests feeling like a tedious chore rather than an engaging activity. It's disappointing that after less than two hours of playtime, I was already bored with the game. Furthermore, it's evident that the game is geared towards a younger audience, which may explain the lack of complexity. Overall, while Calico has some positive qualities, it's ultimately a lackluster experience that falls short in several crucial areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is buggy, the graphics are kinda funky (tiling textures and the like), and the controls are a nightmare.It was the most fun I have had in the last month. Frustration with the aforementioned problems instantly disappears when you put Pudgems, the chonky cat, on your head and run around like a lunatic. 100% worth your time and money.I was choosing between this and Cyberpunk 2077 and I am completely happy with my decision.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very cute and I love that you can collect so many cute animals for the cafe. But I can't recommend this title. It's very lacking in content and has many quest breaking bugs. For the price and even on sale I wouldn't recommend it, there's just not enough content to justify buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I really like it. A magical game about witches, cats, cute villagers and a cat café! I couldn't wish for more. Just buy it, you won't be disappointed. As you may expect, it still has some bugs (but they're quite small, you won't even notice them). Congrats to the game devs! Keep updating the game please <3
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Never in my life have I felt so spiritually fulfilled by a game. It's witchy, it's queer and it's fabulously low stakes to the point where if you want to spend an entire day (whether it's an in-game day or a full 24 hour period) flying about on your broom and patting ALL THE CATS...you can do it! I love the fact that I can run a cafe without actually having to put in any work (beyond decorating). I love that I can "cook" by basketball throwing ingredients into a bowl. I love riding my ghost dog around a magical forest while wearing a capybara as a hat.  I love that this can all be achieved without the use of hallucinogenic substances!I love Calico so much.Yes there are bugs, but none were so gamebreaking that they stopped me from playing. Eagerly awaiting more content (and would really appreciate fancier outfit choices).  Buy this game if you've always wanted to live in a fluffy utopia where your biggest problem is not having enough room in your cafe for *another* polar bear.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rather adorable but this does come with quite a few issues.  I was able to finish the story and complete all achievements in under 7 hours of game-play, this could be shorter due to my time exploring and collecting furniture.The controls feel very clunky when playing with a keyboard and mouse, I also felt like my character was floating and not interacting with the terrain properly.The whole cafe aspect of the game feels purely cosmetic as I was able to complete the game and finish all achievements without bothering about it at all. Cooking is so clunky as I spent so much time having to take ingredients out of the bowl and play a mini game of Tetris to fit everything in to complete the recipe,  putting finished products on to the tray was the same deal. Playing with the animals also offers no benefit, maybe a friendship meter could enhance this feature.  Buying furniture felt obsolete outside of gathering pieces and placing them to finish a quest as they gave no achievement or benefit to the cafe, saving money for the recipes from vendors is the way to go if you are collecting achievements.  This also goes for buying clothes in the game.The game is receiving regular updates so a lot of these issues may be resolved in the near future with new content added.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: i really wanted to like this game but unfortunately, the mechanics really ruined it for me. there's a lot of glitches, it's hard to navigate, and the controls are unworkable if you're on a pc. the character design page had a lot of body inclusivity which i loved, but the character art itself has an uncomfortable uncanny valley feel to it and the graphics feel incomplete. it's in deep need of a visual rework and other adjustments.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and wholesome game. I did almost everything in 5 hours. The dialogue is fun, the pets are cute and character customization is great. I liked the characters, they're sweet. You can ride a giant cat, snow dog or fox. Also, tiny horses. The game doesn't take itself very seriously, and there's absolutely no problem with that. Pets can ragdoll hilariously so they don't block your path. The devs are patching the game pretty frequently though, I only had to deal with one or two visual glitches and oddities, no problems gameplay-wise. Yeah. Cute, fun, hilarious at times. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, feels like a sandbox game! The only thing to note is that the controls on keyboard are a bit unconventional but that didn't retract from the game at all! Every silly idea i had to put into this game was already in it! Really recommend this game for people who are searching for a short cozy game.

_childDocuments_.review: around 5h 1/10 1 No I made one for finding the animals, you can find it  1 on Astats No No No No No No No difficulty option NoCalico will introduce you to a wonderful world. Where all different kinds of people and animals live together in harmony. I expected a little bit more from the cafe part and had to switch my mindset when I kept getting fetch quests after fetch quest, especially early on in the game when you don't have the option to mount animals because the walking speed is very slow at the beginning. After I was able to mount on animals the game was a lot more enjoyable.To get all the bad things out of the way.. at launch the game had quite a few bugs, even game-breaking ones. The developers are working hard to solve those and I'm pretty sure that in 1 a 2 weeks after release everything will be sorted out, but it still made me wonder if this game was tested enough before the release. As I see how fast they are able to fix the bugs.. it would have been nice if that process was started before the official release, but the most important part is that they are fixing those bugs very quickly.Now onto the good parts, this game is lovely. It has a very peaceful and colorful world in which you'll help out members of the community with their daily struggles. While exploring and helping community members which quests, you'll also see a lot of animals. 56 of those are listed in the "animals" menu and you'll have to find them all for an achievement. This might be the most challenging achievement in the game.About the achievements, most of them you'll unlock by just playing the game, for a very few you need to do a bit extra, but none of them are grindy. I would highly suggest first complete all the quests that unlock a new area, because at the end of that questline you can unlock a new and very fast transportation item, which makes the other quests so much easier and faster.I had a lovely time in this game and I hope you'll be able to enjoy this game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game with lots of cute animals, friendly NPCs and little quests to do.You can decorate your cafe, change the looks of your character, so quests you get from NPCs, explore the words, unlock new parts of the map, collect animals, etc. I spent almost 6 hours completing everything the game offers (doing all the quests, meeting all the animals, opening all parts of the map), it is surely possible to be faster I just took my time.The game looks very nice, I love the graphic style of the world, characters and animals. The music was a bit annoying after a while but you can turn that off.There are a few bugs in the game, no question, nothing game breaking for me, everything fixed itself after a while.I really enjoyed the game a lot and guess that you can spend a lot more time on it if you want. If you are not the type of player who enjoys a world after the story is done, maybe get the game on sale though :)A controller is recommended for playing the game. It is possible with mouse and keyboard  but some bits are very akward without controller (I especially struggled in the character creation and inventory).
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: its a really cute game, and I love being able to just wander around on the back of a giant cat, and the game is fun and I enjoyed it, but it just glitches out so, so, so much that it feels almost impossible to get anything done because some form of annoying glitch will disrupt the gameplay meaning you have to leave the game and then re-enter and pray the glitch won't still be there. _childDocuments_.review: While the game does warn players that mouse and keyboard are not as good as using a controller, there's a significant difference between "not as good" and literally unusable.
