_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: LGBTQ+ right here and I don't love this game. I love sim games. I love time management. I love collecting animals and recipes, but this game felt like it had too many things going on at once with no real idea other than "let's make it cute". I'm all for kawaii culture and my room looks like Hello Kitty threw up glitter in there, but the game is just far too disjointed otherwise.So there's a cafe system. You make food items and add them to your menu. You get recipes for your food (and drink) if you complete quests. This makes up the bulk of the game. Eventually you will run out of quests (and achievements) fairly quickly. As of writing, I'm right about to finish the last part of the game other than buying a few cosmetic options I don't really like. So that's about five hours of game time.You're supposed to collect animals for your cafe. You can steal your neighbors' pets... which seems like something should be done to stop that. This can impede some of the quests you do and they'll just generate another animal for you to have instead... but this isn't the easiest thing to figure out if you can plop down the named animal in your cafe, so I'm not sure why we can do that...Interacting with the NPCs feels hollow. They have text, but it's repetitive and it doesn't even feel like you have a relationship with a customer, let alone someone you're doing fetch quests for. Nobody feels very unique and their quests just feel like busy work rather than something meaningful where you learn something special. Learning that a character can speak cat? Pretty awesome. Encouraging someone to enter a dance contest? Pretty great. And then every other quest just feels empty and just handing me an award so I can get to the next part of the game.Don't get me wrong, I love the ability to do a lot with how my character looks and I appreciate that... but it's not perfect. Even the controls on customizing your character are a little difficult so I ended up with a character who had great hips(not me!). Trying to get a character that looked pale and sickly like myself (hey I exist) without selecting plain white wasn't really cutting it. I was honestly better off turning myself into a green-skinned witch and pretending I was sewing chaos instead. It's hard to keep yourself as a human here so why even say it's LGBTQ+ friendly if the way to look appealing for yourself is to just opt for a non humanoid option all together? So let's say I'm not completely sold on this. Maybe if the tools were a little more intuitive and it wasn't so difficult to figure out on a keyboard (I suspect a controller isn't too different) I might feel different.Maps in some sections are huge and you can ride forever without hitting anything. It feels like there should have been something there, but it's just a huge vast plot of nothing in areas. I'm not sure if this was to pad out playing time, but considering the set up of the town or the woods, this seems odd and as if the game was very unfinished.I feel like this game needs an early access warning on it. This doesn't feel finished or worth the price I paid and knowing how close I am to the end of my playtime, I'm not satisfied. I'm not satisfied on the selling points this game boasted as well. It's cute, but I need more.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: The not recommend is purely because the game doesn't truly support mouse and keyboard, nor does the screen show all mouse/keyboard controls, especially for character customization.  It makes the entire experience very frustrating.The game is fun, you travel around a magical island and make friends with locals.  Those locals share recipes you can bring back to your little cafe.  The characters, animals, and environments are so well designed and animated, and have the cutest art style.  Such a fun little game, but lacks a good UI/UX.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! There are many cute animals to pet and interact with. The customization options are great as well. You can customize your avatar and your café. What's not to like. The story is not too long but still very much enjoyable along the way. When you get stuck, there is a discord community ready to help you. There are some bugs too but the game receives updates regularly so no need to worry about those.Overall, a SUPER cute and bright game. : )
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It's short and sweet. I finished in about 5 1/2 hours without rushing and I can only wish it was longer. The mechanics are a bit clunky and the animals have a weird jiggle when you run into/through them but it didn't take away from the game at all, just made it a bit funny. After all the other types of games I've played it's nice to not die when you jump off a high cliff. There isn't too much depth to the game nor does it seem like it will have a big replayability to it either however I think I would enjoy coming back to it in a year to simply relax. I recommend this game if you're looking for something chill and comfy. The music is great and the colours and designs are really cute. Overall it was enjoyable to play but I would say to buy it on sale. 3.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: the game is really cute and has a great concept, but unfortunately, i can't recommend it. it's INCREDIBLY buggy. like, you'll encounter bugs every couple of seconds. animals would clip into each other and glitch out, i managed to get the upsized owl to go at an even faster speed than it was supposed to, sometimes the animal's pathfinding would break when you send them from the cafe to free roam, there's some objects that clip and float off the ground, the music at the cafe is really weird with bad, nearly incomprehensible vocals inconsistently fading in and out, and don't even get me STARTED on the cooking mini game. i don't know if it wasn't tested or what but it's virtually impossible to get anything but bronze on most of the recipes (except for coffee). if the game wasn't riddled with so many bugs and errors i'd recommend it, because it's cute and fun, but it's way too janky to recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game coming into it, it was really sweet and cute. Love the diversity of the characters and their designs. This was a super easy and relaxing game to pick up. Though after a while once you complete all there is to do the replayability of the game goes down by a lot. _childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of cute animals which is nice but the game is buggy and barebones with some not very good menus. Worst of all it just feels so empty and still comes off as unfinished product. It's okay if you really just want some soft adorable time but if you actually care about the quality you'll find there isn't much there. Cooking was especially broken for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: My 6 years old daughters love it so much I had to buy them their own copy on Switch so they'll let me work on my laptop in peace. They can't get enough of wiggling cats, baking sweets and flying on the back of giant pigeons.I'm glad this game exists, with its chill gameplay and organically diverse cast... Though if I'm being completely honest Calico just doesn't feel complete. Although the different locations are beautiful and unique they often feel empty (you can't enter almost any of the buildings and besides chairs you can't interact with any of the furniture), the dialogue options aren't polished and there are glitches abound. The cooking mini-game is fun but I wish there were more recipes, the quests are nice but there aren't nearly enough of them for a game that's supposedly open-ended, the NPCs are wonderful but with only 3 friendship levels there aren't enough bonding opportunities with them. All in all, it should be a good sign when my main (and only?) critique of this game is that I want MORE of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable and cozy game! The story quests are fun and I loved meeting all the animals! I wish it didn't end! One of my favorite things about this game is how inclusive it is. The characters all have different pronouns, are different weight/shapes, and some have little details like cellulite. It is a small thing, but it makes me feel normal and seen.The character customization is amazing, with so many options for hair, skin, and accessories, which are also easy to obtain!10/10 would play this over and over again! I wish I could play it for the first time again!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: So, I wouldn't give this a  recommend, I'd give it a neutral choice if I could, but when pushed I would say yes this game is worth the money.: 5/5 is strongest in this department. The music is soothing and catchy, the character designs are interesting and friendly, and the beautiful watercolour textures are a lovely change.: 2.5/5The actual gameplay of  is very basic. Quests often boil down to talk to Person A, then talk to Person B, then go all the way back to Person A to finish the quest. Some of the more interesting quests involve bringing the correct animal to a townsperson, but these are rare and most quests are as previously described. Tedious and feels like filler to be honest.Now I wouldn't care about this if the world was fun to explore, and even though it is a very beautiful island, there isn't really much to discover. Once you've unlocked all the areas you realise how small and barren the island is. Even the most busy area, the city, feels bland and very barebones. It's a shame because the island is fun to travel around, it just doesn't offer much reason for you to go out and explore. Sure you can collect all the animals, but they aren't very hard to find. I found all but two without actively searching for them.The most fun part of this game is probably the Café itself, which does have its fair share of issues...: 3/5The Café isn't where I spent most of my time, however it feels the most fleshed out and depending on your play style you may spend more time there.Throughout the game you collect recipes, furniture and animals for your Cat Café. You don't have to have cats, I filled mine with raccoons and birds.With recipes you play a little mini-game where you throw ingredients into a bowl. To be honest, the mini game feels kind of tedious and pointless. You can't make the recipe incorrectly as far as I could tell, you don't mix the ingredients together, you don't have to put a certain amount in, you literally just throw stuff into a bowl and it spawns in a cake. The actual models for the food you make are very nice, and really fun to have on display, but overall the whole café part of the cat café is pretty lacklustre. You don't run out of food for customers, and it doesn't matter if they're on display or not, as long as you have made the item once before people can buy it for all eternity. I don't know if this is inherently a bad thing, cause I'd find it annoying to have to constantly play the minigame to make more, but it's just overall a shallow experience from a gameplay perspective.The furniture is much better. There is a variety of furniture you can collect and you can arrange them any way you like. I made a café with a wild plant theme, I used some spooky furniture, succulent furniture and others to make the theme come together. It's very fun to mix and match, kinda like Animal Crossing. The biggest problems are these two things: the size of the café, and the lack of wallpaper/carpet. Your café is not upgradeable, and as far as I know you can't make the upstairs bedroom (which is the bigger space) into another café space. This makes the café feel a little bit cramped sometimes. I get that it's supposed to feel cosy, but it would have been nice to edit the kitchen and stairway layout and/or just have it a tiny bit bigger. You also can't decorate outside, you can't even remove the furniture that's already out there! And finally, you cannot change the wall and floor colours. This makes the rooms look kind of bland.The animals are the main draw, and they are pretty good. They semi-interact with their environment, climbing on furniture objects and going up and down the stairs. They feel alive at least. It would be nice if the customers pet them though. Petting them is pretty fun but the animations are often very buggy and weird looking.Overall, the café is nice but feels a bit undercooked.: 3.5/5You can customise your character to some extent. The body can be made most sizes, you can't change the height but I don't personally care about that. There is a nice amount of hair styles, although a few more shorter haircuts might be nice, and personally I'd like some more pony-tail styles too. You can add patterns to your face but only ones that are in the game, such as stars, hearts, freckles, stubble, etc. It'd be nice to be able to add my own face patterns! The game sort of feels like the kind that would be easy to modify, so I'd love to see some mod support for these sorts of things. I also wish that I could add images/textures/patterns to fabric on the clothing, they all look so bland and it sort of makes you feel like your character isn't really part of the world since the NPCs have such nice, colourful clothes. I would love to be able to change the fabric using my own patterns, it'd also be nice to have effects for the clothing like Kiva does (like moving stars, animated textures and things.)You can customise the animals too. Mostly you can do this by giving them head accessories, such as hats. There are a couple of potions that change the way an animal looks but it feels like there's supposed to be way more. Towards the end of the game you find a lot of animals with special animated textures and weird looking effects, I thought they were going to give me potions that made this happen to my animals, but no. I would love to give my animals something like a ghost effect or a galaxy effect.The customisation covers the basics, but I feel like the game would benefit greatly from more advanced options such as these discussed.While playing  I encountered numerous bugs. Most of them were actually pretty entertaining, but it gets old fast in some cases. The most common glitches I encountered were animation bugs. When you bigify an animal, they often bug out when they go near buildings (especially birds!). I also found a weird glitch which squashed my character into paper (I have put a video of this on the Calico community tab). There's also the aforementioned petting animation bug, the characters are goes really weird when petting animals most of the time. It's even worse when you "wiggle" an animal by picking it up, you can twist your arms in unnatural ways.The most annoying bug I found (which may not be a bug, but I couldn't find any information about it either way) is that the flower shop doesn't restock their shop. This was annoying to me cause their furniture was my favourite and now I can't finish my café :(There are other minor bugs usually to do with the character creator. Using certain potions and then changing back will often remove clothing colours or hair colours. Putting an animal on your head if you're wearing a hat makes them wear it, even when you put it down again. It's hard to use the character creator at night cause the lighting of the sky affects your character model in it. There are a lot of oversights and bugs is what I'm getting at.When experiencing the game as a whole,  has obvious problems, and it feels like there is a lot of missed or not fully realised opportunities here. However, the game isn't exactly expensive, and for the price it's a cute little game. The devs do seem to be updating the game with fixes and content additions, and if these are substantial the game will probably be worth more than what it is right now! The game's atmosphere is genuinely very soothing, it feels safe and nice to just be playing it, there is a familiar feeling here too for me personally, and I don't get that feeling from very many games. It feels rather homely, I've heard people call it "cosy", I'd say that's a good way of putting it. If you like animals, decorating, cute stuff, or chill games, then I'd pick this up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a cute, casual, wholesome game where you decorate and fill up your cat cafe with animals, explore, and help your neighbors with their problems. It is extremely LGBTQ+ friendly: there's lesbians, there's people that use they/them pronouns, and you don't pick a gender when you make your character. I finished the game in just over 6 hours, and I bought the game on sale. I would recommend it at full price, just know that it is a short game. But what is there is fun and worthwhile.Pros:Light and danger-free: no consequences, can't fail.Lots of animals for your cafe! You can pick up almost all of the animals and wiggle them around, pet them, and make them big and ride around on them.Diversity of characters, including: gender, orientation, body type, race, and species.Decoration of the cafe is in-depth. Lots of furniture to use, and lots of space (to a degree, see cons) to decorate.The cooking mini-game is fun! Without spoiling much, you get shrunk down and cook while small.Cons:The run animation is not good. It was the first thing I looked up and I was really disappointed I couldn't turn it off. When your character runs, they stretch their arms out and waddle like a toddler. Really just, weird. You get used to it after a while and it's less distracting, but very distracting and offputting in the beginning.The cafe doesn't feel very important. Yes, you unlock recipes and progress quests by putting animals and furniture in it, but you really aren't interacting with it very much during gameplay. Once you use a recipe, the food remains available in your cafe forever. People come and buy food while you're out, so you don't have to be at your cafe. I think that would be fine if there were maybe also a mini-game where you mind the cafe and people come in and ask for things, but as it is your cafe is just a money-maker you decorate while exploring and questing. I just wish there were more to do at the cafe.Similarly, the cafe does not grow as you progress. I would have really liked to have seen upgrades to your cafe, as in, making the interior bigger. The outside of the cafe has plenty of space to decorate to your liking, but you have to be very choosy about what you put inside. It would have been nice to be able to expand the interior to make more room for decorations.The pros definitely outweigh the cons on this game. It is a really wholesome, short, casual adventure through a pastel world full of diverse characters. Just don't go into it thinking it will be long, or that you will be spending a lot of time tending your cafe, because the focus is definitely on aesthetics, characters, petting animals, and exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR at the bottomCalico is an interesting game.  It's fairly short and simple (me having completed it in 7 hours), and holds a fun simple concept.  Cottage core vibes that is VERY LGBTQ+ positive.  It is absolutely wholesome playing through the game and the characters are fun to enjoy and befriend.  The landscapes are simple yet pleasing to the eyes, all together it is a pleasing game.  However my only complaints are the fact, while you can chose the overall furniture style for your cafe, you are unable to change the exterior theme to match.  A long with the fact the human models are kind of strange to look at in the beginning, however this you adjust to as you play through the game.  Some of the textures (mainly the galaxy ones for the cats) are very strenuous on the eyes having a continuous motion effect as the character moves around on the screen.  They also include this fun inclusion of magic that is rather disappointing that we don't get to learn more about or how to do in the game.  On top of that the game glitches are abundant, you never know what exactly will set your character or cats off that will cause a strange glitch to occur, to which the only fix is to save and quit the game.  In conclusion while this game has a great start, it has a lot it needs to improve upon.TLDRPros:Cute conceptCute catsCute character personalityLGBTQ+ friendlyCute game in generalCons:Lots of bugs and in game glitchesTexturing problems with character models and effectsCharacter designs are off putting at first.

_childDocuments_.review: I do definitely recommend Calico but with some big caveats regarding what experience you are going to get with this game (not a bad thing, I just think some people might be misled about what this game is or is not).Let's start off with -THE GOOD STUFF -- This game is CUTE.  I mean, if you like a cutesy, feminine, whimsical aesthetic - you'll be into the look of this game for sure.  It has cute coming out the wazoo.  Every aspect of this game has a very cohesive aesthetic.  It's definitely simple, but it's so immersive, that never comes off as a negative.  The color palette, the art, the decor, the clothing options, the animals themselves - everything nails this look.- The music!  Lovely, soothing, charming music!  You can hear one of the vocal tracks on the trailer - I think they did such an awesome job with the music and how well it suits the game itself.  There is another song at the end of the game that is equally great.  - This is a calm, cozy game.  There's no pressure here, there's no punishing game play.  You can take your time and do things as slowly as you'd like, or you can make a bee-line for the objectives in order to wrap it up as quickly as possible and then just focus on things like decorating.  This is a game for all ages truly.-  Have I said this game is cute?  Oh yes, I have.  But here it is again.  Everything in this game is cute.  The baked goods, the furniture, the clothing, the animals (there's several very magical looking animals that are super cool in this game), the music.  The atmosphere is fantastic - they have multiple areas on the map, each with a distinctive feel.  And yet they all still fit together.  - They have a very cool system in this game with potions.  Potions are like character effects that you can turn off and on.  One gave my character an adorable cupcake themed outfit, another one gave her glowing hair.- The animal variety is very good - lots of cats if you're just here for the kitties, but there are also dogs, bears, foxes and many more you can discover.  You can also use the animals as a mount!  I loved that part, getting to traipse around the place on a giant calico cat in my cupcake outfit was pretty great and definitely made me smile.THE NOT SO GOOD STUFF -This isn't a cat cafe simulator.  Not really.  If you're looking to actually regularly tend a cafe you'll be disappointed I think.  You do get to decorate it, decide what baked good will be available and pick what animals will be present.  That's about the extent of it.  So if you're looking for something that emulates the experience of running the cafe (such as serving characters, doing a lot more baking, etc) you'll want to look elsewhere.- There is no cake decorating in this game.  It's shown in the trailer, I know many of us were excited about that aspect, and it's not in the game.  -  There are broken achievements.  It looks like just two of them but it is disappointing that this game should be a "perfect game" for me but isn't because of broken achieves.  Other people have complained of the same thing but it hasn't been fixed.-  This game is very short.  I completed this is about 5 hours.  And by complete, I mean I got every achievement (well, a few were broken as mentioned above but I did do them) and got the end credits.  Now, you could get more time out of this game by going further and spending more time decorating or unlocking more decor.  I didn't personally feel motivated to do that though.- Questing is very simple in this game.  I'm actually going to say right now that this isn't necessarily a bad thing, in fact to some people it may be a good thing.  For me personally, it's more of a neutral thing so please understand this isn't listed as a negative necessarily.  It's more of a Roblox style questing system.  Townsperson asks you to do something, it usually involves running to another person, then running back to the quest giver.  They are very simple quests, typically of the fetch or deliver nature.  - Pricepoint - the full price for this game is 11.99.  Is this worth it?  For me, I think at full price no.  Certainly at a discount, I think this experience would be better priced out in the $5-8 range.  To be clear, I still recommend this game but I would just wait for a discount and understand that it's a short experience.TLDR - This bite-sized cozy casual game has cute in spades. A fun way to spend an afternoon in a no-pressure, fun for all ages, whimsical experience.If you enjoyed my review and want to see my curator picks follow me at
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: My boyfriend gifted me this game today and I beat the main story (with some side stuff here and there) within 4 hours-- granted, I rushed through the last 2 areas without doing sidequests in between because I wanted to open the whole map and see all of the animals before I figured out what I wanted to do with my cafe, thematically.I was initially only planning to play an hour or two and then play a different game, but I got sucked in fast. The cast of characters are adorable, the animals moreso-- the addition of being able to pet an animal is always a plus in games and this one goes a step beyond with being able to actively play with them, pick them up, put them on your head, WIGGLE them (best feature), accessorize them, etc.Even though the two games aren't comparable past "collect cute things", I got drawn in the same way Slime Rancher hooked me, to be honest. You passively make income in the same general way as well, unlock more means of making money and cute animals by unlocking new areas, and meet a fun, quirky group of characters in both games, but that's about where the similarities end.Calico's jiggle physics are delightful and never cease to amuse, and even though some parts of the game feel a bit "rough" at times (animals and npcs clipping through walls/into the floor, some missing punctuation or abrupt dialog) you very quickly accept it as part of the overall charm.Very cozy and cute game, perfect for anyone who just wants to sink into something relaxing. Also an absolute riot to either watch a friend play or experience alongside friends for the first time-- there are so many moments in the game that made us laugh out loud.

I had issues where control prompts wouldn't appear, stopping me from proceeding in the tutorial. Placing furniture takes you through 3 menus, and takes so long I didn't bother to put anything other then a couple chairs down to advance. *The sounds are... not for me. It seems like there's only one song per area, which means that if you spend any extended time in a spot you should just mute the game. This could change as the game proceeds, but I didn't make it that far. *The tutorial alone is already pretty buggy, I can't imagine it gets any better.I really want to like this game and play more, but it was all just too much.

This game does a great job with representation as well, there are pronouns listed for each person on the villager list and there are conversations where they talk about their relationships! Seeing a character in a game using They/Them pronouns like me made me really happy honestly!! Overall, the game is very silly and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Cute, but there's very little to do. You set up your cafe with some tables and seating, cook the first few foods that you manage to get, gather the animals you want in your cafe, and then basically never interact with it again aside for quests that require it. Most areas are sprawling areas with very little in them. A few NPCs, a few animals and nothing else. You interact with every area the same as you did with the last one. Interacting with NPCs is basically meaningless, the main story is only a couple hours long, and every quest is just a fetch quest. Either go talk to a couple different NPCs, go cook this specific food for this one person, or go grab this specific animal for your cafe.Overall, I wanted to enjoy the game, but I just didn't really find myself having fun. Also if your entire game is essentially walking around your map, the movement should be a bit more interesting or fast-paced. I dreaded every time I had to go up the mountain.

_childDocuments_.review: Calico helped me get back into gaming. I think I just needed a relaxing and cute game to play for a change and I had a lot of fun. I loved carrying all the animals with me and riding them. The cafe is cute and I loved putting all my animals to bed before going to sleep in game. The characters are all cute. I'm happy that the girls are diverse and some are gay. It's nice to have a they/them in the game as well. I like customizing my character and putting hats on the animals. (Oh and I love the mouse girl) The music also is very relaxing and I added 2 songs to my playlist on Spotify.I really did enjoy the game but it is buggy and has some glitches. The characters were cool but forgettable. The quests are pretty simple nothing too exciting. I'm not sure if the devs are going to update it or not but being able to upgrade the cafe for starters would be nice. In conclusion, I did enjoy the game I just wish there was more to it
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a really cute game for everyone. The artwork for this game is beautiful, from the saving screen to the game play. It has a very cutesy aesthetic and matches perfectly. Unfortunately there are quite a lot of bugs. There are many parts of this game where characters would get stuck on chairs and animals would get stuck together. Overall, Calico is a casual and relaxing game to play anytime. The bugs can be very annoying at times but it almost makes the game more silly.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a short, 100% stress-free adventure full of cute animals and characters.There's no deadlines to meet, nor is there any health that could result in a failstate.The animals are cute and wonky in a delightfully charming way. The only cons I'd have for this would be the animation on the player character. The run animation isn't anything spectacular, and the sprint(?) animation frankly looks weird.And it's fairly short, in my 7 hours of playtime I managed to 100% it.Animation gripes aside, for the length and price it's a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A cute and enjoyable game with charming character designs and a lovable atmosphere! I did enjoy playing the game, however it had a few small flaws. The game itself mostly focuses on quests for characters and less about the cafe aspect. Also, the map feels incredibly large and unique, but often pesky to travel sometimes due to the character's speed. It is fun to play through but once you have completed all the game has to offer there isn't much to do anymore. Still had fun despite that :)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is janky as hell, cheesy as macaroni-... and I love it. You can just FEEL the love oozing from the devs in this game. There is next to no management; this game is about being goofy with cute animals and accessorizing your character and cafe. I had an owl riding on my head for probably seven or eight hours of my playthrough and my mount of choice, always kept in my party, was a man-sized rabbit that was (by my tests at least) the fastest creature in the game. He got to wear a crown for his contribution to my journey. My cafe itself was entirely populated by cats, save for a single possum with a flower crown trying to blend in for easy food. The makeup of your cafe, however, is up to you. There's enough animal variety in this game that you could choose to have a dog cafe or even have the local population of bears roaming around outside.Totally silly fun for a relaxing weekend. Grab your cocoa and a cookie to nibble and settle in.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty chill and adorable game. I adore the concept as well how the game allows the freedom for you to be whoever you wish without restricting to gender norms. Also, did I mention that you can ride cats, or fly over the skies? No? Well guess what you can! Plus the soundtrack of the game really helps immerse into the universe of Calico.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game, and it is worth of waiting for its release. I love the music, the characters, and the charming style of the game. It's cute and simple, and I love it. It's a kind of casual game I can enjoy whenever I feel down.I want to continue playing this game, but there are glitches/bugs I have experienced that needs to be patched up:(1) Using my controller, when I press "A" to resume the game, my character jumps. (2) Poppy is in a sky where I can't reach him until thankfully he floats back to his farm area. (3) For some strange reason, when I'm interacting to one of the NPC characters, they suddenly stopped talking and just walking away. I don't know what's causing it, but I think skipping their speech causes the NPC to stop talking to me unless I can talk to them again and take my sweet time letting them finish. (4) When I load my save file, everything's reset even though the progress I've worked on (the money, the animals, the display, clothing on my characters, quests, etc) remains the same. Because of this issue, I cannot able to progress this one quest where I need to find all five pigeons (especially the last one which I cannot find).There's also jiggly physic in the game that also needs to consider to be fixed. Like, every characters in the game, especially mines, is all wobbly like ragdoll-y.I would love to keep playing this game in my free time, and I do hope that it'll get fixed later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a very cute and very chill game. If you fancy running around and picking up cute animals the definitely give it a go. If you rush through it it will take you a long afternoon, if you go slow and enjoy the adorable world then a day maybe more. For anybody who only cares about achievements this is an easy chill game with nothing too difficult to get.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: So far, absolutely love this game. The visuals are beautiful, the interactions with all the animals are great, and the music is so relaxing. The character creation is a nice plus too. I'm excited to see the devs add more and more to this game. in the future, I could see this becoming the next Slime Rancher. Things I'm looking forward to:-yes, the graphics are insanely pretty, some of the character models are awkward looking. -some of the terrain when you walk across them, the character jitters. -a lil' nitpic but, maybe some penalty to falling from high places. Not dying or anything, but maybe like a falling over animation. and when you get up, you're slower for a short time.Overall; 7.5/10 on a first impression. Please keep it up Peachy Keen!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly shocked this game has anything other than mixed reviews. I understand that the keyboard and mouse controls are an afterthought and the game was intended to be played with a controller but I've never seen such a ridiculous setup for keyboard UI. The bottom of your UI has 4 tabs, labeled 1-4 and you need to hit 1-4 to open the desired tab. It may seem like a tantrum to expect M to open map but I feel like that's a very general keybinding for it and having to fight the instinct to hit M every time instead of 4 is a very annoying. There are other keyboard input bindings that I don't care for but I've said enough.Moving past my keyboard and mouse master race attitude, the overall game is really short, which luckily is reflected in the price but I personally wouldn't have paid more than $5 knowing what I know now. I could have taken my time with it but honestly I couldn't wait for it to be over so I sped through. From the screenshots and trailer it seemed like a charming game but to play it makes it seriously feel early access at BEST. It really just feels hollow. You setup your cafe and then move on. After cooking a few recipes you really don't even have to do anything with it again because once you set the food you want to sell, it will stay filled and ready for purchase until you swap that item for something else. The map is big but mostly empty. Every character is cutsie wootsie little thing that barely leaves a lasting impression.If you want 6-8hours of gameplay where you don't actually need to be in the cafe or tend to it with love and care and instead are just running around doing tasks, then have at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rather strange game. While framed somewhat as a management game set in a cat café, there is very little of this - at least as part of the core gameplay. You can choose to adopt animals, decorate the café and prepare various food items, but there’s no real depth to it and no gameplay purpose (aside from specific quests, which are few and straightforward). It is perhaps more of a sandbox, given the array of customisation involved. The core gameplay instead is largely a bunch of fetch quests. This could easily become grating, but the small world, cute presentation, occasionally amusing writing and short playtime combine to make it relatively painless.That still doesn't necessarily make it a particularly good game. The graphics are glitchy, there is little depth and it's all rather repetitive. And yet...it has such a good spirit to it, a real sense of joy, that it's nice to just kick back and play through it. Sometimes it's nice to play a game which just leaves you feeling good, and this one did.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute game; the aesthetic is nice, the cats are fun and adorable. _childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely cute and has a good vibe/aesthetic, but the physics and mobility on this made it frustrating to play. _childDocuments_.review: People complaining about the mouse and keyboard keys being awful like the beginning of the game it doesn't say "works better with a controller" get over it.This game is super cute and i really enjoyed playing it. Didn't really take long for me to finish the game but it was still overall super nice to play ~ my cafe is riddled with snow animals it's not even funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so incredibly cute and simple and that's pretty much all it goes for. Controls were easy and smooth. Art was adorable. Game play was fun and easygoing. Nothing clunky. I did fall under the ground once as I glitched out trying to land my giant bird I was riding, but they have a teleportation potion always available and that fixed it immediately. The magic is fun. I LOVED the music. The characters are fun and simple. Some of the quests and walking from one place to the next got was a little mundane, but  overall it was super fun and cute. I enjoyed decorating my cafe, cooking some baked goods, and collecting all the adorable pets. I loved using the potions (especially making critters giant or small). I LOVE CATS. haha. It's a short game but worth the price and experience. I'd love to see more of this game -- romancing characters, more depth to the characters, more magic to learn, crafting, fishing, more interaction / taming / content with the animals, farming, maybe help building up other locations / businesses / cities would be cool. More engaging quests, etc. But, if you are just looking for some relaxation, cute cats and other critters, and no stressful time limits, this game is for you! This isn't the game for you if you are looking for a true farming sim like Stardew Valley/Harvest Moon/Littlewood/etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little janky, but that doesn't take away from the game's overall charm. My only lament is that I couldn't make my cafe any bigger or allow for more animals to live there, because being me, I wanted ALL the animals. So I just chose the coolest for my cafe. Otherwise, it was a delightful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: If you love animals, magic and carefree quests that you do in your own time with no consequences no matter what you do, this game is exactly that. Everything is at your pace.It is a short and sweet game, very open world on a small map and it's not hard at all to unlock each little area.The customisation is brilliant, you can literally be anyone/anything you want. The further you progress, the more items you unlock/can buy from the clothes/furniture/potion shop.Very LBGTQ+ friendly and the characters are adorable.The music is beautiful and fits the game very well.The graphics are somewhat basic yet very smooth and in my opinion add to the carefree feel of the game. There can be little glitches here and there with the movement/animals, but they're mostly funny, don't happen often at all and don't cause you any grief.Definitely use a controller to play. It's recommended to use one when you begin and when I first played I understood why straight away.When it comes to the cafe itself, there are three things you can do:-Decorate the interior and exterior-Make food which is stored in a display case (the way you make the food is adorable)-Store cute animals that walk all over the cafeSo there isn't any interacting with actual customers. It would be nice to be able to do so, but that's just a little con.Overall, if you're looking for a fun, adorable and magical little adventure where you can ride around on cute animals, this game delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute. There are a few things that could be done better, but overall it was a decent, cute game.  I was expecting there to be more management about the cat cafe, and that wasn't there, but I enjoyed it while I was playing it. It's a lot more about running errands for the townsfolk. I was very fond of the progression of transportation - walking to riding animals to riding larger/faster animals, etc. It is a little short, but yeah, if you like cute games then this is one you might wanna look into.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very sweet, cute, and easy game that I think is worth the price it's at. It can play a little janky and I've accidentally clipped through the map and into the ocean beneath the world more than once, but the baking minigames are simple and fun while providing a challenge needing near perfection to get gold scores on some of the recipes, as well as locating some of the animals hidden across the world. I blazed through the main quests and side quests relatively quickly before relaxing with decorating the cafe, collecting animals, and buying out all of the available items on the island.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game! I don't know why it says I have 0.1 hrs on it, steam can be faulty like that, but I have like 10+ hours in the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a joy to play, but maybe only buy it when it's on sale, like I did. _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable.  I had fun playing it.  The music is relaxing.  There's a lot of character customization to start with, as well as a lot of decoration for your cat cafe.  There are a few quests in game for each character you meet; all are non-combat (collecting, delivering, talking to another character, etc.).  Some of the food mini games are more fun than others.  I would say all aside from the pool table one were fun.  There's a lot of fun potions for your character and toys to play with the animals you encounter.  You can choose up to 10 animals to be in your cafe and up to 5 animals to have in your party at any given time.  You're also able to get larger animals to use as mounts (or any smaller animal with the use of a large potion).  Money is easy enough to earn; you make recipes at the cafe and with time people purchase the items.I did encounter a few bugs while playing, mostly while flying.  Occasionally my character would get stuck in a tree, in the ground, or on the side of something.  It was easy enough to fix by closing the game completely, selecting continue, then using the teleport to the cafe ability.

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: **EDIT**I have revisted this game a few times, with hopes for positive changes. The character customization has improved immensely! My only unique complaint from my previous review? This game is probably the worst-running game I have EVER played on my pc. I can play games like Elden Ring or COD on fairly high settings with little to no issues, but Calico??? Lowest settings and I can barely walk in a straight line. Buyer beware, it's cute and goofy, but - in my opinion - most of these reviews just don't shed light onto the issues the game has, and there are a lot.initially i had a review posted as a joke. after forcing myself to play this game long enough to have gone around the town, experienced using a bird for flight, trying the terrifying mini game for cooking, and trying to set up furniture somewhat decently in the cat cafe, i can honestly say...this game is not worth the $13.49CAD price it is at - at this point in time! Calico has a lot of potential, but for a game coming out on the Switch console, it doesn't seem like many things could be changed much without consistent updates on console as well. the character creation is a nightmare to work through, from accidentally making your character green, to the misleading hair choices. holding animals - from birds, to dogs, and of course cats - can be pure terror when the animals begin clipping through your character, not to mention the petting feature, in which your character pretty much just shoves the animal around until you give up with petting them. this isnt to say everything is awful, of course, just that it feels like more of a sandbox game at this time...i love the 'store' feature for storing animals, where your character puts an animal onto their head, so you have free hands to pick up another animal. i also love that when you place a bird onto your head to 'store' it, if you jump off of a cliff, you can glide down with ease thanks to a comedically large bird on your head. the graphics in the game are cute - looking too closely at some of the grass might cause a headache, but overall they suit the games style without a doubt. while this game would need some improvements to make me happier with it personally, it's still a funny little game, that i enjoy streaming to friends in discord, so we can laugh at how wrong some of the things go. i'm sure the game will be improved upon greatly, unless it's intended to be more of a silly game.(though, the description says it's meant to make you feel 'warm and fuzzy' so i'm not too sure about that one)unfortunately, i just cant recommend purchasing this at this time, but i'm sure one of the tons of other reviews saying how much they enjoyed it for what i disliked it for could convince you otherwise
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A game like this has a lot of promise. Many people love custom sims where you can build, shape and decorate your own property/farm/business. It gives you a sense of freedom and accomplishment when you create something that is truly beautiful in your own eyes. Calico, however, falls completely flat in almost every area.PRO:You get to customise your very own cat cafe. Amazing! Right?CON: You are instantly limited by a hard lock that cannot be broken that does not allow you to collect all the cats in the game, let alone all the other cute/diverse animals.PRO: Open world.CON: Very small, empty zones with no personality or ambient decoration.PRO: Storyline.CON: Just kidding. There is zero story and the few NPCs are hollow and devoid of character, outside of their names.PRO: Character customisation.CON: The devs specifically said you CAN make a male avatar: (Pikachaos  [developer] 25 Jun, 2020 @ 11:13pm  Hello! Yes! The full game will have a character creator.)During creation the game tells you flat out you are only allowed to play as a FEMALE or TRANS character.The vast majority of the NPCs in this game are female and of a very unhealthy body type. It only encourages same sex relationships.Before all the "You hate LGBQT etc.".. No, as a matter of fact I have many gay friends whom I treasure. I have an issue with anyone producing a seemingly "anti-X" product. This game - feels - very much so like it is intended to be "anti-man".That's a shame because I really wanted to love the potential of this game as it has been a dream of mine to one day open a real-life cat cafe.Overall, the game is just a poor product that thoroughly missed the mark. It has clunky controls, has an absolutely abysmal painting/decorating system and you can't even build a bigger cafe. You can fit maybe 4 tables and a couch in the entire building. Which cannot contain the games cats. Which is the sole purpose of the title. The game looks unfinished and could have used another year or so in development.For all these reasons, I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Calico in a bundle of indie games for donating money. I finished the game and then kind of fell off of playing it. When it went on sale on steam, I bought it again and was very happy to find out that all of my progress from the non-steam version I own carried over, so I didn't have to restart.! So it may say I only have 40-so minutes of playing, but that's only playing on the steam version. I absolutely adore this game, the characters are amazing and the music is beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and relaxing game! It's basically similar to Animal Crossing, except that there's a story and quests. The game takes about 8 hours to fully complete, but there is replayability by customising your home and buying more parts to make it more lively. I got lost in this world. It was well worth the pricetag. I hope to see more updates for the game since I would love to play some more! The music is also excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so wholesome, fun and relaxing.The animals are super cute and I wish there was space for more animals in the cafe, 10 is not enough and it's so hard to decide which ones I should keep it and which ones I should let go. I JUST WANT ALL OF THEEEEM!I had lots of fun with the potions and cooking. I was making a dessert and one of my cats decided to jump at the counter and laid down on top of the food. LOLDespite being short and very glitchy (the glitches are funny though, especially when you use a cat toy on a bird and the bird starts to roll on the floor like a cat), I recommend it. ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is an adorable cat cafe sim with plenty of magical girls and different animals to adopt. I really love this game because of how adorable it is, but as someone who easily gets lost, it was a little tricky navigating the map as there is no pointer/direction, just a circle for where you are. The vocals in the music are a little annoying, and totally unexpected - they had me looking around to see where the music was coming from mid-stream, and confused my viewers, too. Other than that, and a few physics issues, it's a REALLY adorable game with lots of animals to befriend and lots of different things to do. I haven't played all that much of it yet, but I can't wait to play some more!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredibly cute and you can tell a lot of love went into making it. However, if you're expecting some RPG-type depth, that's just not what it is. It's a combination of numerous little wholesome experiences that are unfortunately connected by a lot of very slow and tedious backtracking. It feels like the game is still in Alpha and you can tell that more features were intended to be there, but they're not. It is a wholesome little experience that can be completed in about 5 hours (with all achievements), so I wouldn't recommend buying it for its full price if you don't intend to support the artists - who honestly did a great job. It's just the gameplay that is lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: omg, okay, calico is like stepping into a warm hug wrapped in a fuzzy blanket! 🐱💖✨ first off, can we talk about how insanely adorable everything is? the cats, the pastries, the cosy little cafes – it's like a dream come true for anyone who loves cute stuff!but beyond just being cute, calico is seriously so cosy. like, imagine your favourite sweater but in game form. you get to run your own café, decorate it with all sorts of cute furniture and decorations, and, of course, cuddle with all the adorable animals. it's like the ultimate chill-out game after a long day of, well, life.and can i just say, we need more games like this! don't get me wrong, i love a good farming sim as much as the next person, but there's something extra special about the whole café vibe. it's like a slice of heaven fr.overall, calico gets a solid 5 stars from me. it's super cute, mega cosy, and just all-around delightful. seriously, everyone needs to play this game asap. it's like a warm cup of hot cocoa for your soul. 🌟💕🍰

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing look at a gaming environment. Cute cats and bunnies everywhere, friendly NPCs and a warm color pallet make this game inviting for children and causal gamers. My kids loved it, and it served well as something that could run on my Surface Pro 6 while watching TV with the wife.The graphics and frame rate are not going to push anyone's GPUs but it was enough to run around in the colorful/comic world and collect furniture for my cat cafe, learning new recipes, and baking them in the kitchen.  Recommended for anyone looking for a light-hearted, fuzzy, cutie-pie adventure.  Puzzles were not too difficult to figure out with a little running around.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about Calico is just cute, in the best possible way. _childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: In Calico you play as a newcomer to magical island full of animals! Your main task is to restart the cat cafe your aunt has given you when she moved from the island. The cafe itself is not very hands on once you get started, you only need to appear to make recipes for the first time and switch out the display case. Villagers go to the cafe once you meet them with no prompting and products sell themselves!Calico is very inclusive, with mostly female villagers, very little males, and some people that appear to be non-binary. There is a canon lesbian relationship and many POC. Character creation(in my experience) is mostly impossible without a controller, and you will have feminine proportions no matter what(the degree of these proportions can be customized), although you can give yourself a beard and/or stubble. There is complete(possibly even excessive) color-customization with skin tone, hair and clothes.The self-sufficiency of the cafe is a plus for me, I've never been very into diner games. I also like the variety of animals, including cats, dogs, red pandas, polar bears, and more! The most reoccurring(and, by extension, annoying) visual glitches I've encountered is your body clipping through clothes and spots of void in the landscape(which fix themselves as you get closer). However, this is a small negative that I don't think takes away from the game at all! What bothers me more is the dialogue, which includes multiple or sometimes all options repeating the others, a lack of ability to show your own personality, and characters repeating themselves(not in the way where you talk to them over and over and they repeat, but they'll say something and immediately after repeat that something). The running animation is very unusual to the point of irritating me and I wish it would be changed.Some other tweaks I would appreciate are better graphics all around and for more furniture to change once you choose your style, such as bedroom and kitchen appliances. Display cases should be individualized, so you can display different foods with each one(if this is added display cases should also be more expensive). In the map, it would be great if you could scroll over the villager's icons to see their name. A big want of mine is an in-game overarching goal(besides improving the cafe). I've always enjoyed games with no big goals or ones you don't have to do, like Stardew and Minecraft, but the constant meaningless quests can get boring. I still love the game, my interest always comes back, and I plan to play it more, but I just want more to do and/or something to revert to. The following suggestion doesn't affect my review in the slightest, and I don't believe the mechanic is necessary, but I think it would be neat if you could date some of the villagers.With all these critiques, you may be wondering why I recommend this game. It's simple, the pros outweigh the cons! Calico is one of the cutest games I've ever encountered, if not the cutest. The villagers are all so kind and it really reminds me of Stardew Valley! I like that you can change your character whenever, even if you need potions to change some details, which I think makes sense. Cutie City very much lives up to it's name, I partly wish you could buy a house just so I could live there! All the animals are absolutely adorable, I'm in love with Pudgems. Walking around with an animal on your head and watching them jiggle around makes me surprisingly happy. The pronoun situation is great(no one ever refers to you by any), in fact the inclusivity of the whole game is a major plus for me! I've seen some people complaining about the controls, and while I can't comment on the keyboard version, I think it's fine with a controller. The magic aspect is one of my favorite parts, I immensely appreciate the teleport home potion and I like that potions never run out.Overall, I agree with the people that say Calico feels more like a demo than a finished game, but updates are still rolling out and I'm very optimistic. Calico has a lot of potential and is already pretty great! If you want a cute, calming experience, something to unwind with, Calico's the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and super cute! It's really relaxing and overall just a good time. All the animal friends are so cute and it's so entertaining to explore the island! I completed just about everything there is in the game, and I wish there was more, but of course, it's an indie game, so you can't really expect so many hours of play time like you might have in a game produced by a large corporation. The physics are a little wonky as well and animals keep ending up in weird spots at my cafe, but it's not a massive issue. Anyways, this game was so fun and I'll definitely play through it again!

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with this game when I first played it, it's simple, cozy, very cute, immersive, and has a subtle  underlying melancholic/somber feeling, the different environments are the biggest draw for me. I would absolutely recommend this game, it's great fun. The new update has made the cooking aspect of the game quite challenging and frustrating. What used to be a rather quick and simple minigame is now time-consuming and iffy on some of the controls/mechanics. The biggest drawback being the scoring system, as it's near impossible to achieve the highest mark, or it requires too many attempts for the time it takes. Although the new cooking minigames seem fun and more engaging, as it currently is, the cooking doesn't seem to match the relaxed/casual difficulty of the rest of the game.The game is still lovely nonetheless and the care put into it clearly shows!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend gifted it to me, in other words:(hint hint fellas ;) ) (your welcome ladies <3)So it was a literal gem of a game. Adored the gorgeous graphics and safe concept, loved how chill and not too difficult to play while anxious or stressed the game play made it! The creators literally outdid themselves with this one, there's a ending too the game itself but the free roam after and even before the so said ending is so fun and just cosy in general. You never really get bored either because there is just always something new, the concept of the cafe is cute and all but the best part of it is that it doesn't take over the whole game or your time. Most of the game is what you want and there are no time limits or any problems you may face! Would a million percent recommend this game to anyone who suffers from anxiety or ETC. Either way your really gonna enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is short, simple, adorable game about running a cat café in a small town. The gameplay is mostly running around (most of the time riding a giant cat), talking to your neighbours, running errands for them, and trying to find all the wild animals around the island. There is also an aspect of decorating your café and deciding which items will be on the menu, but I haven't really played around with that part of the game. If exploring an island filled with wild animals while running around doing quest sounds like fun to you, then try this game. I found it extremely cute and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Such an adorable game! The premise of a magical island with everything from potion-making witches to talking cats that do construction work is just so precious. Of course, with how new the game is, there are still some bugs (like accidentally throwing my butter outside my cafe while baking and not being able to get it back, or the bigified red panda i'd been holding in front of my cafe appearing a solid 5 meters away) but none of them are game-breaking, so I don't mind them. The townsfolk are all so cute, each with distinct personalities and, get this, the handbook even contains their preferred pronouns! I was so overjoyed seeing that when I went to check for Lumi's name after I'd forgotten it. Not to mention Blossom and Sunny, the adorable flower-loving lesbian couple with a shared garden between their two houses... makes my heart so warm. All in all I find this game absolutely adorable. I can't wait to see what more comes from it.

I picked up the big pig and lifted it over my head while it was still wearing the little pig as a hat. I put a red panda on an Australian Shepherd's head, then rode it while carrying the pig stack. 10/10This game is adorable and fun, and I was constantly laughing as I found new, charming things to do.

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing and calming.Nice music but it gets a bit overwhelming after a while so I´ve turned to playing Lo-Fi and the two mesh perfectly. The design of this game is simply stunning and so are the characters - not to mention the characters that identify as They/Them and the absolute freedom you have in choosing a skin colour and body size. _childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute, and I had a great time playing it!The main story itself isn't quite long, but there's a bunch of side quests to do, so you won't get bored with the game too soon. It's great that you can choose which animal to have in you café, decide if you want to change their name or not. I also loved walking around with a cat on my head and seeing it wiggle while we're walking around!I do wish that there would be more clothing options available. I thought that we would unlock dresses or something like this later in the game, but no. I also thought that there would be more accessories (like hair accessories for example), other than just animal related things and funky hats.Anyway, I still loved this game and had hours of fun with it. If you're looking for something cute and cozy, I'd absolutely recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Super unfinished, runs like a $2 meme game and shouldn't be priced for more than that if this is the finished product. It's like a less interesting but more cute Goat Simulator. The recipe minigames are legitimately impossible and the camera angles make everything more frustrating than it should be. The artstyle feels like it should be cute but everything looks so boring in practice with hardly any world details. Most of the gameplay time will be spent going from point A to B because travel is extremely tedious and mounts hardly speed that up. Don't recommend, for this price point you could get a cute game that actually manages to be engaging and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I helped Kickstart this game, so I'm a bit biased, but I think the finished product is exactly what was advertised! It's a super chill game about starting a cat cafe and that's exactly what I need right now, at the end of 2020. I can definitely see how it's best to play it with a controller (I'm still eagerly awaiting the PS4 release) but I've managed to play it on PC with only a mousepad, so a controller is not a must. If you're looking for a game where the point is to find cute animals, hugging said cute animals and also decorating a cafe, this is the game for you!The game has got some bugs, yes, but I've not encountered anything game-breaking yet. Seeing as there are patches coming in swiftly and that the game is made my a small team, I don't find the bugs to be an issue. If you're worried about bugs, maybe wait another patch or two before buying this, but I definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is an aesthetically appealing little game with lots of animals to choose to run around with, ride, and house at your cafe. It's a little sparse right now as far as content goes, but I really enjoyed what there is so far. It would be nice to see more little favors to run for townsfolk and if decorating your cafe is not rewarding in and of itself to you, then the cat cafe itself doesn't really contribute heavily to the game. I think that Calico is starting off in a great place and has the potential to be a very rich, relaxing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Heart-warming, nostalgic, wholesome game. The 3D rendering style, somewhat reminiscent of Okami when it comes to the environment and animals, instantly pulled me in at first glance and made me purchase the game.The variety of animals you can get, and the fact that the game doesn't take itself too seriously at all, is what I love about this game the most. Some hilarious and random things you just won't normally find in games unless you encounter a bug, are features in this game, which I enjoy a lot. Such as having your cat float in the air in a ragdoll state while your bird is T-posing comfortably on your head. The food-making is another thing I really enjoy. You're a tiny person, throwing huge ingredients into a bowl to make your food or drink of choice. Very wholesome and creative way of going about it. Sometimes, the cats come and see what you're doing on the counter. Bonus points.The quests are simple and fun to do, as far as I've played there is no pressure to perform them in a specific time-frame or by a specific day, which makes playing the game a relaxing and uplifting experience. You can just run around having fun if that's what you want to do.I have encountered a few bugs (trouble with picking animals up or mounting them, etc.), which is totally okay as I expect them to be fixed down the line with player feedback. Saving and relaunching has solved my problems every time, which is very quick and easy to do, so my experience was still great despite the bugs. Quite honestly, the bugs that I've encountered only made the experience funnier and jankier, I love how funny it can be to interact with your animals, shake them around while holding them, play with them and make them flop around hilariously. I'm having a blast playing through it. I had some trouble getting used to the controls in the beginning, especially during my character creation phase. I switched between controller and keyboard/mouse inputs several time until I got used to playing on keyboard and mouse, as I couldn't get used to the camera controls despite having the option to invert them. It would be great to have separate options for horizontal and vertical sensitivity inversion. Playing on keyboard and mouse, I'm sometimes unsure which button to use to perform a certain action when it comes to things like using items or removing furniture, so I have to try a few times to get it right. Otherwise, the game has the base controls right on the screen at all times, in case you forget, which is very useful! If you don't want them showing, you can easily hide them with one button.If the controls get slightly polished or refined in future updates, that would make the experience perfect!But other than that and encountering a few bugs, I absolutely recommend the game. It's a very unique, silly, wholesome experience and something I've recommended and showed to many of my friends already, and they adore it. Major props to the developers, I'm very happy to support the project as it's exactly what I didn't know I needed in my life. I wish this game all the success in the world!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game non-stop since I've bought it. I was so worried that this would be a game that I would play for an hour or two until there was nothing else to do, but I'm about 5 hours in and it feels like there's tons more!TLDR: I really like this game! It feels really good to play and the gameplay is fun and a little goofy. Pretty sure I've found my next hyperfixation, although there's a couple things that I wish were tweaked to make it a little better. Definitely worth it!Good Stuff:-This is the best stress-free game I've played. There's no deadlines, no meters that you have to keep full, you can choose when to do quests. You don't even really have to maintain the cafe that much either if you don't want to. This is great for zoning out and doing fun little tasks-The game is SO CUTE! The animations feel floaty and a little floppy, but it just adds to the goofiness of the game. The animations while riding the different animal mounts feel really good too!-I really like how once you've met an animal, you have access to it wherever you are, whenever you want. And you can access the character creation menu whenever too!Now, it's not without it's faults:-This isn't super streamlined and has places that need to be fine tuned. Honestly, there's nothing game breaking or anything, but for instance when I was talking someone, every time I would get the next line of dialogue, I'd also jump. It doesn't happen all the time, but it happens while in menus and that can be annoying when it happens.-At first I was really wishing for a mini-map, but after a while I just kinda learned where everything was so I wasn't constantly pulling out the map anymore. Same thing with the characters on the map; I thought it would make it a lot easier if the sprites for the characters also had their names. But again, after I played for a while I learned who everyone was and where they usually hang out. It's not really problems with me anymore, but it was something I noticed.  after a while, quest markers stopped showing up, and I do want those.-I really wish there was a reason to cook more! I don't know if it's different in the endgame, but it's kind of a bummer that once you make it once, there doesn't seem to be a reason to make it again? I like not having to worry about making them  morning, but, it would be cool if they'd start to "get stale" or something so we'd have to make fresh ones every once in a while. Like I said, this could happen later in the game and I'm just not there yetI didn't mean to ramble this much, but I had so much I wanted to say about it! I love this game!

_childDocuments_.review: okay so here is the thing. i do recommend buying this game. But i have some complaints that are kind of good reasons why you wouldnt buy it.Lets start with the positive thing:- the art stye is amazing and really cute. it is kind of wonky but that makes it different and way cuter. also the colours are amazing!- i really like the idea of the game, where you have a cat cafe, befriend animals and help town folk. - the story is also fun and really peacefull. I am at a bad place mentally right now and the littlest thing gives me stress. but this game was really relaxing and made me feel a little better and gave me the feeling like i finally had some time to just breath and clear my mind.- it is very LGBTQ+ friendly. The npc's are not all cinsgender heterosexuals. they all have their own pronouns and there are a few gay relastionships. also there is no toxic masculinaty, for example, there is this dude poppy, with he/him pronouns, who has a beautiful strapless croptop, and glitters in his beard. I think this game gives a good example for other games- i loved the minigame where you made your food for the cafe. it was really fun and i really wanted more of that. negatives:- it is really glitchy. like not just a little, like big time glitchy. at first I kinda liked it and thought it was pretty funny and i made some funny screenshots. It gives the game its own kind of character. but the longer you play the more annoying it gets. i really thought they let it be a little glitchy on purpose, for its character, but it would be weird if the developers didnt realize it was going to be annoying. i really hope they are going to change it in the near future.- i havent finished the game yet, but i am almost at the last place you can unlock. but the story line and gameplay is getting a little more dull and boring. the first few hours you had a lot of quests and it took longer before you could unlock the next place. now i have like 2 or 3 quests, where is just run around from one place to the other. i have my fingers crossed that this gets better in the end of the game. other stuff:- if you have a controller, you should really play with a controller! for the first few hours i played this game, i hadnt have my controller with me so played it with mouse and keyboard. it isnt that bad and really do-able with mouse and key board. but the gameplay feels so much smoother with a controller.-i think the game would have been even more fun when you would have a little bit more to do in your cafe, because it is now just making the cafe look fun and bake every recipe once, i think if there were more things to do in the cafe, for example like really serving people or somthing, the game would be funner to play. in summary:i really recommend this game if you are into cute, peacefull indiegames that are really LGTBQ+ friendly. The game is really glitchy but that is kind of funny but also annoying. and i think in  the end, the game had the potential to be even more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: super cute game, however there are some issues with it at this moment:- the color customize system is very off, pink shades are always purple and yellow shades are always green- even though the game is about owning a cat cafe, i feel like the game has little to do with it. you don't spend your time running a cafe (ex. making food and serving customers) but instead doing tasks for the npcs- the tasks have low importance since there is no on going story line and the get very repetitive since they are all three step tasks that are not connected to each other- the controls for keyboard are very annoying, it is recommended to play with a controller but better keyboard controls would be a big improvement- the map feels empty. the npc homes are non enter-able, small, and spread out.- the cat rescue system needs improvement. you are supposed to be rescuing stray cats, yet they all come named and some are even found in gated areas. a recommendation would be having one of every cat breed and allowing the player to name them once they are rescued. this would also allow the player to work towards getting every breed of cat.- when you send a pet to the cafe it would be nice to see them start walking away from you and to the cafe, instead they usually stand still or lay down which leaves you confused on whether they received the command or not.overall i still recommend this game because the concept is great and it is so new. the developers have already been putting out updates which is amazing! if the game doesn't appeal to you now, i would recommend checking back on it in a few months!

_childDocuments_.review: Casual calm game where you inherit your aunts cafe and can go around gathering up to ten animals (not all animals - there is no cafe animal storage expansion). You also run around meeting & doing quests for the locals. You can also make food for your cafe, it is an interesting cooking sequence where you shrink down onto the bench top and run around springing off of spoons gathering ingredients that you need (like eggs from the open fridge or sugar from in the pantry above - accessed by a funny tiny elevator I didn't see at first). Not too bad, pretty neat if you like chill short-ish games and animals. As you help the locals and do quests for them, you open up new areas. There is also a giant cat blocking the way to some areas with it's big but. You also get to ride many of the regular animals around the place (near the beginning of the game one of the npc's gives you a shrink/enlarge animals (except birds) potion- you can mount them when they are larger size generally :) Funny little feature but I enjoyed it. To me, the game has it's charms. Not a high learning barrier, which I like. It's nice to just jump into and play.
