_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I love Calico. I get some peoples frustrations with the bugs etc but Calico hasn't even been released for a week! As with any new game, there will be bugs. But, the Calico team have already released a patch! Give them time, if you want seamless gameplay maybe check back in a month or so - I guarantee by then many of the problems will be fixed!Anyway, onto the reasons I love Calico:. The character design for a new game is great. There's so many options in the shops and in the character design menu - cannot fault it!. The furniture options are amazing.. Great variety of villagers compared to other games!. Quests are fun and engaging with rewards and special items; unlike most games.. Great price tag for the current 6-7 hours of game play (casual pace no tutorials).. You can see how much effort went into Calico.. You're helping a small company get more money to potentially upgrade Calico and maybe even start work on more projects!I few things I'd love to see added/improved/fixed:. Easier to remove pieces of furniture that go on the wall.. More areas?. Bigger main story/more quests.. Small bugs patched when possible.That's all. I hope you found this review helpful and balanced. Maybe you'd even consider purchasing Calico or writing a review of your own to support the game!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Overall a cute, fun, relaxing game, but only if you get it free. I can only recommend this game because I got it as a gift from a friend. With how short the gameplay is (I literally completed the entire thing twice in a few hours each time) and how buggy the graphics are, I would have been pissed if I'd spent money on this. Tbh I feel like they cut corners to keep the price low, and honestly I'd rather they have charged more and polished the game. There is an unnecessary amount of empty space and buildings that you can't enter that just take up room and impede your travel, the items and animals glitch into each other like crazy, the animations are...interesting (looking at you running animations), and a ton of the cute clothes you see aren't available for your own character. I also hate how there's a TON of recipes but you can only have 6 food items available no matter what. You also can't change your walls or floors to match your furniture style, or expand the cafe in any way. Maybe they'll add all these in a future update and I really hope they do because I'd be willing to pay for it because the idea is beautiful. I will say though, that the names they give to a lot of the animals is hilarious and they deserve props for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is an absolute gem for anyone seeking a relaxing, cutesy gaming experience. The characters and animals are unbelievably cute, and the game’s beautiful pastel-painted world instantly makes me feel at home. I love how the quests are both delightful and stress-free, and the soothing music enhances the game’s calming atmosphere. Whether I'm decorating my café or chatting with the town's charming residents, Calico always feels like a comforting retreat.For me, Calico is a perfect cozy game. It offers everything it proposes. A nice balance of creativity and calm, making it an ideal escape from everyday life. If you’re looking for a game that combines adorable characters, cute quests, and a soothing atmosphere, Calico is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: There are plenty of bugs and glitches, the game is short (approx 8 hours to complete everything), there's lots of back and fourth, some minor flaws to certain game play (like only 6 food items in the food case regardless of quantity) and short relationship needs between characters.. But in all honestly, the game is cute and hilarious at the same time. Yeah sure, all animals react the same way as the cats do but so what? They still included different animals in a game all about cats!?! What more did you want from them. It's still cute to see the birds, wolfs, or any animal go after the toys or play fetch with you.The game has so many glitches and bugs that sometimes I'm convinced they are intentional. Things like where animals get stuck in weird places, or you merge through things.. but I didn't find myself mad at the game for it. I actually laughed every time and showed my boyfriend because it was genuinely a mood booster. The only downside I had was the fact that you're limited to 6 items in the display case. I came to realize this helps you keep playing, because really if you had all items in your display cases wheres the fun in it? You're only profiting and not bringing in specific customers for those food types.Sure relationship quests are short, sure 8 hours total game play isn't a lot but did you not think about decorating your cafe? Did you consider redesigning your layout or changing colour schemes? There's more to the game than people think, you just have to give it a shot. Plus for me, I don't like when I have to do a million tasks for people, I just want to be cozy and relax and this game is exactly that.All in all, I loved the game. I had a super stressful week at work and when I came home to play this I was super happy and relaxed doing it. Certainly recommend this game if you like decorating, cute things and don't mind bugs and glitches.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 7 hours in the game (using mouse and keyboard, which tbh is fine) and am greatly enjoying it. I will come back and do a lengthier review once I've experienced more of it, but I don't really understand all of the negativity of some reviews. The game has been out for two days and I don't get how people are this mad about a few bugs in such a chill game. Most things are fixed by a quick reload and it's not like there's a massive amount of progression that you can lose. The worst thing that has happened to me thus far was jumping into water and getting stuck in the swimming animation, which eventually got me stuck under the terrain. I saved and reloaded and everything was fine.  Most of the bugs add to the joy and silliness of the game, which has a very surreal Katamari vibe to it. On Day 2 they immediately patched some of the inconveniences, but really that's all the bugs are - minor inconveniences (although maybe my tolerance of bugs has been tempered by trying to play Cyberpunk this week). I find that the pros far outweigh the cons of this game, as the dreamy atmosphere and surreal scenarios have brought me much delight. I rode a capybara while wearing a capybara as a hat who was wearing a flower crown. I found a cat that was an orb. I wandered around with a gang of giant raccoons in a town populated by bipedal cat-sized cats and witnessed them breakdance. I can't be angry while playing this game if I tried.Again, I will come back to this review to discuss more positive aspects and see how patching progresses over the course of the first week.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd probably rate this game like 5.5/10. If it's really better to play with controller I'd probably rate it higher.I played with MNK and yeah the game feels really clunky and the mechanics are really wonky. But the bugs also make the game sort of funny, I seen some of the animals just randomly spring up to the air for no reason or my horse launched into the air and get stuck. _childDocuments_.review: A cute game, but it's very similar to The Sims in the fact the more you play it the less playable it is. Having gotten several hours into the game and story, some features just outright don't work anymore, with some of my ingredients disappearing and making it impossible to bake anything, to animals refusing to follow me, not being able to store or pet certain animals, the moment you reach the last game area is the moment the game starts to break terribly. It's a real shame because, at first, this game was very fun/relaxing to play. Although you're mostly doing fetch quests, its just really enjoyable to be able to ride on a big cat or dog as you explore the admittedly beautiful environments and discover new animals to take/send to your cafe. It's also nice to receive visitors and I found all the characters very charming and interesting in their own ways. I enjoyed the amount of shops they offered and checking in on them every in game day. I also enjoy that the game doesn't force you to sleep and instead lets you pass through the days in whichever way you like, either by continuing to explore or setting it to day again by using the bed. The customization for your own character is pretty good, if not a bit odd to go through, and I do agree some more variety with the body shape would be appreciated. But all in all the variety is great and really fun to mess around with. The music is gorgeous and really sets the overall cute and chill mood of the game, and I'll definitely be listening to some of the songs outside of the game. The variety of animals is really impressive and I love that your cafe can in cooperate both big, small, wild, and domestic creatures. The addition of magic is a nice little touch with plenty of cool potions to use on both your pets and yourself. Not to mention being able to pick up big and small creatures, wiggle them around, and put them on your head? Excellent. Aesthetically this game is very pleasing and I absolutely adore the art style. Warm and fuzzy feelings all around at the start of the playthrough....until you start realizing this game about an animal cafe actually has very little to do with said cafe. If you follow the main quests, you will rarely be at the cafe to actually spend time with the cute little critters you sent home.The best and cutest part of this game, in my opinion, the animals and cafe, are very underutilized. There's no system to care for the animals, the only thing you can really do is carry or pet them, both which are adorable but I wished there was more to do rather than just sending them off to your cafe and forgetting about them shortly after. For an animal cafe all you really do is include the animals people want you to, let them walk around and that's it. You can pet and play with the animals, but it doesn't reward you in anyway and is mostly just an aesthetic choice. Aka wanna watch animals be cute and play with something? Sure go ahead. Cute idea and I appreciate it, but when a player is rarely encouraged to be around their cafe there's no reason for it. The only animal I grew an emotional attachment to in this game was the one I ended up riding, and yeah being able to make animals bigger to ride is an amazing concept and I wish more games had it, but for a game about running a cafe you're certainly given a lot of excuses not to be at your cafe. I wish more of the story actually involved what the game was set to be about.Needing to add certain animals and furniture to your cafe also really stunts creativity and customization, making me include animals and furniture I didn't really care for, and I lost my interest in it. My cafe ended up a clash of styles that just didn't look good because that's what the NPCs wanted, and only a few of the animals are ones I actually cared for while others were just quest fillers. I wished your style choice at the start would have been something you'd be allowed to stay consistent with throughout or even change. Maybe even have animals that fit that style, and let the player cater to a certain audience, I think that would have been fun to balance. As is the styles feel like a half baked idea that doesn't effect much, and, ironically, the game feels more fun when you've delved into less of the content. If I'd just ignored the quest and focused on baking at the cafe and remaining there, I would have had much more fun. That is to say, if I stopped playing the actual game at the beginning and just sat there and pet the animals, I would have had a better time, which really shows how warped the actual focus of the game is.The baking in the game is fun in my opinion, but besides bringing in more customers and receiving money there's really no reason to do it. As long as you find a good combo to keep customers coming in, the cafe really just doesn't need any maintenance and you suffer more when trying to switch it around. Not to mention the limited shelf space that just means the more recipes you learn the less of them you can include in your cafe. You can't interact with food outside of the cafe, can't pick it up and give it to NPCs directly or make anything for your pets, compared to everything else in the game it's just a painfully linear process of making it, adding it to your display, and seeing who it brings in. It is also seemingly prone to breaking after a certain part of the game or if you're carrying an animal while you enter the mini game. In general, the game is very easy to break if you're not careful, which is extremely unfortunate considering how cool some of the features are. To my knowledge, you are unable to buy ingredients if they disappear, and while I appreciate that the ingredients don't run out, this is a very easy soft lock to accidentally encounter. The game doesn't do much in ways of letting you fix problems and often backs you completely into a corner when they occur. Most of the systems, while good in concept, are outright broken and do not have a "reset" feature. To think allowing players to reset their ingredients or animals would have fixed so many problems is sad. So, if you have a quest that involves whatever you were soft locked from, well you're never going to complete that quest anytime soon. Have an animal you like but something about them glitches out? Well too bad, guess you'll just have to deal with that or move on to another one. I think the game became too focused on unlocking locations and features to the point a lot of said features ended up either not being well tested or put on the back burner for most of the game. I think this game really would have benefited from just allowing it to be a small, open world were you could collect creatures and focusing on the cafe aspect over a very bare bones story and fetch quests (that still could have worked if they had more to do with your business or animals). A lot of the quests and the main story isn't needed, unlocking locations isn't rewarding, its just tedious. If they didn't want players to have access to everything all at once, they should have just made it time based so it would take a while for the area to be clear. Only the first area needs to be cleared by the players to introduce mounts really.This game could have used some more time in the oven before being released because, as is its extremely janky and bug prone.  A little bit of jank is fine, and earlier on in the game it mostly just makes for a couple of laughs and doesn't effect one's gameplay as much, but later on it turns into outright soft lock territory and can break the save you spent hours on. I really want to recommend this game because some parts of it are really good and it is absolutely adorable and fun in its concept. I will continue playing seeing as I bought it and it's nice to play in the background or talk over, but it's just too broken for me to recommend to most audiences. If you're careful and okay with a little jank, sure, if not, wait for the developers to make something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved playing this game, if you're into cute quest based games you're going to enjoy this one! You play as an owner of a cat cafe helping locals while exploring the island and finding different animals for your cafe! You can also bake treats for your cafe that you can later sell to town folks and learn new recipes. The game isn't too long or hard, completing it plus getting all achievements took me about 14 hours of gameplay, but considering it's a chill and easy game to relax to I'd say it's a good length. I really like the simple but cute design of places and characters as well as customisation although the process could be made easier. Very inclusive characters with different names and pronouns which also gets a plus from me as it's quite rare to find in the media. In overall, if you like simple and cute games to relax to I'd 100% recommend getting this.

_childDocuments_.review: Calico spoke to me the moment I saw it pop up on my recommended games and I've finished it within a few days, the only disappointing thing being that I've done all I can do in the game. I adore wholesome, casual, stress free games and I previously thought Animal Crossing was the best game to fit those tags... But Calico surpassed Animal Crossing within the first minute and actually made me excited to start gaming more. I loved the characters (especially how open and accepting this whole theme is) and I will obviously be recommending this to anyone and everyone as I think this is the best way to showcase how fun and cute games can be, and how you don't need too much challenge or complications to have a wonderful experience. _childDocuments_.review: calico allows you the fantasy of finding an adorable animal in a forest, picking them up, and taking them home with you. using magic, and you can grow a cat really big and ride it like a horse. it absolutely rules.it's short and sweet. my first playthrough was about four hours long, and i've been speedrunning the game, and have gotten sub 30 minutes. i can't stand long video games, so it's a massive plus that the game is so "short". even then, that's only mainquest. there are so many sidequests and other objectives aside from achieving the endgame credits. (even after the credits, the game just keeps going)the game is a bit buggy, but not moreso than any AAA game nowadays. for an indie game (let alone a kickstarter game), it's extremely impressive.one of the biggest things i have to say is that the character builder is one of the worst i've ever seen. no color presets, extremely limited body part customization, and ultimately there's no way to make your character not look like a lesbian. listen, i'm a gay dude, i'm all for representation. but can i.....not play as a girl? please?for $11 it's very difficult to not recommend. it was exactly what i wanted from looking at it, and it's polished enough that it makes me feel like i got my money's worth.i'm certainly looking forward to what peachy keen comes out with in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love cats, pastel colors, magic potions, and lots of puns, this game is for you. It isn't as fleshed out as I hoped it would be and you're very limited in the amount of areas you can unlock (being on a starshaped island comes with this con). For what it was, however, I thoroughly enjoyed it. Loved the music, the character designs, the cuteness of it all, and all the cute animals I got to house in my cafe. Before buying it I assumed it would mostly be about making the food in the cafe, but the majority of the time you're venturing from one side of the island to the other, to the beach all the way to the mountains, and only spend a bit of time in the kitchen. However, I really liked the way they did the baking in this game. You turn into a miniature version of yourself on your kitchen counter and get to yeet ingredients into the bowl to make super cute recipes. Would love to come back to more storylines/updates. :D

_childDocuments_.review: A good, cheerful game that is providing me with emotional support as I job hunt.Some of the animations could stand to be fine-tuned, specifically the jumping–>landing transition and "petting bird" animation. The dialogue has a few grammatical errors, but nothing that obscures the messages being delivered. My biggest complaint is the camera/"disappearing walls" system w/ the café; it's kind of difficult to put up wall decorations when the wall keeps vanishing until you back away.Aside from all that, though, this is a thoroughly delightful game with fantastic aesthetics. All 2D assets are lovely, the character customization options are good, the music is nearly hypnotic, and the overall pacing feels natural and relaxed. I especially appreciate the fish pond and the ability to put hats on creatures. (I'd like to think Poe and Unfamiliar have accepted their fates as a cowpokes.)

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After taking an additional 7 hours to 100% the game, I've got some time to really put my thoughts together about Calico. If the devs are reading this, I don't want this to come off as an attack; they clearly have a vision that can be realized, and good criticism is the only way to get there.If there was one word I had to pick to describe Calico, it would be "unpolished", with the prime example of this being Xin's second quest, Saving Mister Snuggles. Unfortunately, it follows the standard Calico quest formula; Xin requests you go talk to someone in the woods, which is a several minute walk away. When you reach them, they tell you that Mister Snuggles has been under Xin's hat the whole time, and you have to walk all the way back to tell her that. When you return, you don't see him pop out from under her hat, the screen simply fades out, spawns him, and fades back in again. It's little moments like this that gives the game opportunity to show off its personality, and unfortunately it's squandered by what was clearly a time or budget constraint to finish the game. A game that does this well is Deltarune, I feel, particularly the gags in Chapter 2, such as flat ralsei.The game's main selling point, being interaction with townsfolk and running the cafe, are either underdeveloped or entirely unnecessary. The game's main plotline revolves around doing errands for other NPCs that all end up being "Talk to this NPC, talk to that NPC, maybe have something made in your kitchen, come back and talk with me again". Two moments in the game's plot end up standing out to me: breaking through a landslide with a big cat, and using a giant lighthouse laser pointer to get a GIANT cat to stop blocking your path. These are incredibly fun ways to mark progression, and actually tie the player to it beyond asking NPCs to make things available for you. It's a shame the game doesn't do it more.I'm probably going to stop my review here, because I'd probably end up repeating the same few points ad infinitum. To summarize, Calico is something I'd expect to see at a game jam as a concept for a game, not a totally finished one. Although I would recommend against purchasing it, I won't give it a thumbs-down, because I know how much that can hurt indie devs and I really would like to see Calico become better than it currently is.- Kazzi(Original Review: Cute, charming, but doesn't feel "finished". Picking up animals can be janky, swishing them around even more so. Character creation is cute, but something feels... off? I don't know how else to describe it other than "uncanny". Still have more content to play, however, so I'll get deeper into it.)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has lots of problems -- from small bugs that make characters go through walls or get stuck in weirdly funny positions, to the shallow content (almost all quests are fetch quests thinly disguised -- some of them up and down mountains).That said, the game is so light and fluffy, you cannot help but forgive most flaws. All characters are nice to each other all the time; and you can customize your character quite a bit, dress it up in many colorful ways, or turn yourself into a walking Sundae. How can you be mad at this game?At the end, there is a bit of a feeling of "why?", and a sense that this should have been more polished (the management aspect, for example, is nearly irrelevant) -- but I had a relaxing time while it lasted.Score: 61/100.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: A cute, short game I'd recommend if you're looking for a peaceful time, not anything serious. Inclusive, diverse, and funny. Ending and final areas feel unfinished.Pros:- It's a very sweet and pretty game!- The music is lovely and the design of the characters is beautiful- I love the inclusion of character pronouns, inclusion of multiple LGBTQ+ relationships, and diverse characters- The game is graphically really glitchy but I like it? You jiggle an animal and it goes full wonky. Very fun game physics if you're down for that- The decorating is fun with some adorable options- Character customization is pretty darn cute- I wasn't expecting the cooking game to be what it was - shrinking down to miniature size and running around a kitchen playing minigames with your food! I had a lot of fun with that part- Good variety of animals with hilarious names, and you can ride them!- Lovely environment designCons:- Game has graphical glitches like previously stated. If you hate this, this game will irritate you- The story is very basic, though cute- Typos in dialogue- The last few areas have very few characters to do missions for / interact with (last three zones have only five residents combined, which is less total than the starting area)- Ending and lack of quests towards the end felt very abrupt - there could have been more to the game, feels a little unfinished- Once you complete the quests all that's left to do is play with your animals, make food, buy stuff, and decorate the cafe; None of those are means to any ends - you get no achievement or reward for the cooking or decorating other than to complete quests and raise money, which you then filter back into recipes to cook and items to buy to decorate- Once you're out of quests, there's no more dialogue with the NPCs
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: For all cute animal lovers looking for a de-stressing game, you must give these guys your money and buy Calico! Worth it. I have never been so de-stressed playing a game. I love the graphics and the color tones are so cute. The animals are super adorable and you can really customize your character pretty nicely. There's magic, and there's making cute pastries in the most adorable way possible. You get to buy furniture and decorate your cat cafe and house with all sorts of combinations. It's got adventuring in a changing map, RPG character customization, fun potions, collecting things, making money, quests, amazing scenery, interior decorating, baking, you can ride on almost every animal in the game (not just the cats), and you get to interact with nearly everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really sweet and laid back game. Many times while I was playing it I thought, "Wow, how did they make this?" I could tell a lot of hard work was put into it. It's simple and relaxing and is honestly such a nice break from life. I also appreciated how inclusive it was too :) It was fun looking for and collecting all the animals and recipes (although it took me forever to find Patches!). I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a short try and I dropped it because it probably isn't right up my alley. I KNOW for a fact that some people will enjoy this, but I just can't bear with it.I dropped this because of the baking mechanic. I admit that I had fun during the whole baking/platforming segment, but afterwards I realized that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I will have to do this every time I bake and that stressed me out. I expect that you'll be doing this quite a bit, since you ARE running a cafe. Controls feel really floaty too and it's just frustrating, which makes the platforming segments worse.There were also a couple of bugs. I got stuck on a wall for a bit during the baking segment and I got a bit worried that I would have to restart the game to unstuck myself, but it did resolve itself on its own, but do expect some minor bugs like that while playing this game.Overall, it's not quite the simulation game I was expecting it to and that's a bit of a shame. I liked the aesthetic too and I was really looking forward to playing this on my bed.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much, its so cute. The aesthetic are amazing and the characters are so endearing.It's calming to ride giant cats instead of walking haha.I, however, wish there was more to do after the main story line is done. It's boring when you can't do anything else.I also had troubles with the game breaking and crashing frequently.The controls are also super wonky.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: ! ! ! EDIT: I'll leave my original review below (for the two of you that see it). They have changed the cooking since this review, but otherwise the game hasn't received an update or even a post in over 2 years and I'm gonna consider it thoroughly abandoned. I don't recommend buying it unless you want to mod it (which there isn't a huge community for last time I checked) or you want the cafe decorating portion. If you're on the fence, whatever gist you get in 2 hours of playing is about what you're gonna get.I wish there was a "neutral option" but I don't want to leave a bad review. I'm not normally the kind of person to leave reviews however I wanted to put this out there to anyone indecisive on buying this.The aesthetics of this game are on point. It's delightful, the characters are visually interesting and well-designed, the decorating and furniture portion is extremely fun, and the character customization is extremely detailed nice, especially with general inclusivity (thought it definitely could use a bit more work.)I do, however, have a few gripes.The quests are interesting conceptually with what the characters say and the context, however it ends up being "Talk to X character, Talk to Y character" and definitely gets repetitive two hours in when there's a huge map to cross (there are faster ways to travel later on, though). Some quests are reliant on random-spawn/look-for animals which gets extremely annoying (I still have one of the very first side quests because I haven't been able to find an arctic fox, no matter how many half-hour sessions I've spent looking). There are a few bugs however they aren't impactful enough to warrant criticism, at least in my experience. The cooking...I genuinely hope gets changed or edited in the final version since it just isn't very good: I avoid making food just so I don't have to do it. The lack of content is also notable, having finished the mainline quest in around 5 hours and having spent around 3 more doing side quests and buying potions and such. If decorating a cafe and interacting with cute characters and animals (which, there are a lot more than I even fathomed) is what you're mainly interested in then definitely buy this game. If you're looking for a little more, DEFINITELY keep it on your wishlist, they said they were working on a big update and I'm confident it'll improve the game immensely. Overall, I'd suggest keeping an eye out and buying the game if it ever goes on sale.Incredible aesthetics and potential, but it just needs a bit longer in the oven.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, straight up, if you're into relaxing and super adorable aesthetics then you'd probably like this game. However I strongly suggest you wait for it to be on sale or wait until future patches improve things otherwise I don't think it's worth the money.KB/M controls are awkward and while there is controller support, it's not 100% reliable, and I don't know if the devs are working on the controller problems at all because I've seen quite a few discussions for this game asking about controller failures and there are no responses. Graphics wise the world looks very unfinished and the dialogue (at least in English) doesn't seem to have been proofread. The game has potential but in its current state it's underwhelming and unpolished.The only reason I'm debating not returning this is because I'm praaaaying that patches fix things as I know the devs are actively working on it. If you just need a cute world to run through and relax with cute animals then you'd probably like this game but be warned it's not the cleanest experience. :(
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: There have been several updates since I left my first review and it has only led to me feeling more confident about buying this product. 2 updates have come out, one with outdoor decorating and one with expanded clothing customization. Both of these updates really expand upon two of my biggest gripes - not enough to decorate, and too few ways of customizing your character. The game has come to feel more complete. My only warning would be to make sure you have a gamepad laying around, as keyboard controls are still very bad. You can still enjoy the game without one, the experience is simply enhanced tenfold when using a controller.Outside of that this game is an easy yes if you want a low-cost wholesome experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? This game is super creative and beautiful! I absolutely love the art style and music. Not to mention, I'm an animal lover, so this had me hooked from the beginning. If you're looking for a relaxing game filled with cute fuzzies and adorable characters, this is for you! From silly potions and ragdoll effects to mini cooking! If I could compare the experience you'd receive from playing this game, I'd say it's somewhat similar to Harvest Moon and Animal Crossing. But that's just a comparison, this game is completely unique! Just buy it already and show this developer some love! Well done hun. ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. Love the player customization, shop customization, the vivid scenery, and the animals you can kidnap and bring with you. Playing the quests felt like an estrogen-filled midnight run to the store with your lady friends all dressed in cute Lolita-looking dresses, and I didn't know how badly I needed that particular experience until this game came out (I work with all men, am surrounded by men constantly. I miss women. The pandemic has turned me gay.)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This entire game is a delight. I haven't gotten very far yet, but my 4yo was watching me play and we both went "aww" at all the critters and laughed at both the cooking minigame and the giant cat blocking the log, and she advised me on my fashion and decor.I rode my first giant rabbit this evening. My husband asked if I'd placed our grocery order yet, and I turned my laptop to show him that I was on a giant bunny, and he said, "Oh. You were too busy experiencing pure joy. Gotcha."
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: a gameplay sister to animal crossing and a style that somehow reminds me of early spyro games, if you love cute outfits and cats with a beautiful soundtrack and Npcs that feel genuinely kind and sweet, get this game, its the most fun ive had playing a game without tons of mods and it's the probably the cheapest game i own. buy it you will not regret it (also the character creation is so freaking awesome like, thats my magical thembo persona right there! thank you <3)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is everything a cat/cute animal lover wants in a video game. If you like Animal Crossing, you'll love this game. It is reminiscent of Chibi Robo mixed with AC. It's adorable, fun, and relaxing. That said, the controls are not intuitive. Play it using a controller. Furniture arrangement is a bit clumsy, but it gets the job done. Sometimes the animals get stuck clipping through tables or chairs too close to walls, but they easily right themselves if you pick them up. Delightful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I have fallen absolutely in love with this game, the atmosphere and characters are so cute and charming! I love the fact that you can change the way your character looks at any time, perfect for those of us who want to change up our look everyday. :) I haven't even gotten to the fact that you can interact with EVERY animal, some you can even pick up and wear as a fancy hat! Without spoiling the rest of the magic of this game, I'll just say that if you like adorable simulation games with lots of animals, this game is for you!!#Calico
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: In my short time playing so far, I've been enjoying running around and exploring the watercolor world and taking on quests from various people as well as having a little bit of fun messing with the potions.  However, I'm a little disappointed that I'm not ACTUALLY running the cafe like I hoped.  I was wanting people to come in and buy the food I make and physically stop by and enjoy what I set up instead of just saying that they did.And then I turn my cat into a sparkling, majestic, starry steed and I forget about the shop for a moment as I'm filled with pure, unbridled joy.All said, I think it's worth the $12 price for a cute, pastel romp about the world, doing quests and the like with the occasional bit of jankiness.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I was a kickstarter backer of this game and I'm super pleased with the direction it took. The game is short and sweet, with cute characters and a character creation engine that allows someone to make fat characters with ease, which I find lacking in most games. If you want a relaxing experience on an island full of lovable characters, this is the best way to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable game. The soundtrack is beautiful and honestly i'm blown away with how good the game is. Very prompt response time from the developers when it comes to a patch fix for bugs.Would recommend this game to anyone who wants a sweet little game to take their mind off what's happening in the world right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I would give a middle thumb if I could, definitely enjoyed my time and will continue to play the game, because I genuinely do enjoy it. But it definitely feels clunky and unpolished, there's no real story and I don't feel like I really progressed. The most fun is unlocking stuff, but that's about it. The "story" ended really abruptly. This game has such potential to be the best comfy cafe game to exist but it falls a bit flat. It's fun for like 5 bucks but not the full price, I don't think. Despite my grievances with it I can't bare to give it a negative review because I do like the game, I think it's fun and if you enjoy these types of games, this is an ok game for the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: this is such a cute game. i will say if you don't like over the top cute things involving all things animals, not for you. You run a cute cat cafe (you can bring other animals to the cafe like polar bears/owls/dogs/foxes etc) to the cafe. you can grow animals to be bigger so you can ride them everywhere. You unlock cute cafe recipes (cupcakes/bagels/croissants/donuts etc) & get cute patterns/designs to put in your hair/clothes/walls/floor/even toppings on your recipes a lot like in animal crossing) its a well done indie game. I want more content to be added into the game please! i am obsessed!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the harmless bugs (I simply save and restart since the game loads so easily, and I'd say 95% of the time that fixes whatever bug I had) I think this game is beautiful not only in creativity but its art style as well. Very easy going and the music is relaxing to listen to. I'd love to see this game go further even- I am still enjoying running about even after doing all the little quests, I'd love even to just keep doing those cause while it seems menial the tasks were quite adorable and fun in their own ways
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I love Calico! It's super cute, having your own cafe to customise and furry friends to find is absolutely fantastic! Though most of the quests are fetch quests, it *should* be dull but I find myself enjoying running around and doing errands for everyone!My only complaint: ITS TOO SMALL! I need this game to be on a much bigger scale, I need MORE!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Calico but with caution - don't expect much from this game.The main reason why I recommend it is because I had a good time playing it - not because I achieved anything in the game, given that progress is minimal except for the new gadgets that you unlock (that at the end of the day are primarily cosmetic and make no difference), or because the story moved me (it's almost non-existent). The good vibes I got from this game are from the generally relaxed atmosphere and from the absolutely fantastic soundtrack. This is not a game per se, it's more of a relaxing pastime in a somewhat interactive beautiful land.In a landscape of games that stress you, this is quite a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stunning. There's so many things to discover in this game, it makes the world feel big and immersive. Calico isn't a super long game, but you could always draw the tasks out a bit longer and focus on other activities in the game. Every character in Calico is beautifully designed, and I loved getting to know each of them and their unique stories. It's an amazing blend of witchy, cottagecore, adorable aesthetics and themes, it really felt like I was playing the perfect game for me. My boyfriend even enjoyed just sitting and watching me play! He's excited to play it himself at some point, but made the comment that it would be a nice game to play together, multiplayer-style.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I love the diversity when designing your character, the artstyle is adorable, and the story is really enjoyable so far. HUGE animal crossing vibes, and very cozy feel. My only criticism is that some mechanics could be explained a bit more clearly in the beginning, but figuring things out has also been quite fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: My bf bought me this game so I got it for free!Really cute and fun game!! Even if I didn't get it as a gift I think it was worth the price (~$8 on sale at the time). It is a short game (I completed it, got all achievements) but I feel like $8 for 5 hours of entertainment is fairly reasonable!! but i don't think there's really any replayability in the game to be fair. I'd love to see more quests (like  or maybe adding something like being able to upgrade the cafe for more space!! i feel like i have way too much furniture and it feels weird to put beds outside and also rugs do not work outside (they either float high above the grass or are below the grass ...)Everything in the game is super cute!! Although the characters can be a little bit... unsettling at times. Mainly the male characters just do not work with the art style LOL and i think the characters' faces are just a tiny bit uncanny? might just be the eyes though i think. But i liked the options for the character creator and once i unlocked clothes it was fun to make my character really cute! though i think the way you pick colors is a bit overwhelming and honestly it would be better to just have ONLY preset colors (but more of them) instead of the gigantic grid...there are probably some things in the game that need to be adjusted and while i noticed these things at first after a while i kind of forgot about them so... clearly they didn't bother my gameplay very much? lol but i think it would be good to get a better keyboard control. I used a controller but i know a lot of people prefer keyboard and it would be really beneficial to get that working!!overall i know i had a good time with it !! thank u for the fun <3
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill and relaxing. My only issue is that I have a max on the animals I can put in my cafe and I want to put them all in...the game is very relaxing and short n sweet. you can collect/ride different types of animals, cook/bake, complete quests, and more! the game doesnt offer a whole lot to do (at least, not since i last played in early 2022), but its very cute and relaxing. if youre looking for a cute game to kick back and relax to, you should definitely give calico a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a simple cozy collectathon about finding an assortment of animals to fill your cafe with. The game was alright but doesn't exactly leave me wowed; a lot of cool ideas exist like designing your cafe or the bizarre cooking minigame, but I didn't find them interesting enough to distract me from just looking for all the animals across the several biomes of the cafe's home island. Additionally, there were also some technical glitches, like the player character freezing and some animals floating off. Still, I though Calico was a pretty charming game, and a decent way to spend a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an incredible and precious game! There hasn't been a single second where I haven't enjoyed every little drop out of this game; so much so, I really hope more content is introduced! The characters are so sweet, and I really appreciate seeing their pronouns in their descriptions- it's such a small detail, but it means so much to see and I'm sure the creators are aware of that. Something that really stuck out to me was the style of the game- it feels very inspired by Okami, which I LOVE to bits! Overall, playing Calico has been such a sweet treat. It's inspired me to pick up my own projects again! Another note: if you're reading through the reviews, don't be discouraged from playing due to glitches. Genuinely, the minor glitches that happen fit in with the game and are funny to experience rather than game breaking. I recommend playing for the story, characters, and overall sense of ease this game brings!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one-of-a-kind, if only in the sense that it's entirely and completely sure of itself. The devs knew exactly what kind of game they wanted to make - and by god they succeeded. You can feel it in every part of the game, from the really unique cooking minigames to the way the characters speak. This game will not be for everyone; it's as wonderfully, sickly sweet catgirl as it could possibly be - but unashamedly so. And that's what makes it, the sheer pride coming off of it and knowing that the sole, single purpose of this game is FUN. Unabashedly this is a game about cute kawaii witches and a population of domesticated magic wildlife. There's also a cat cafe. Cute characters with fun personalities, adorable animals, absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abilities (sure, let's cook a muffin by pinging oneself across the kitchen on wooden spoons), hilarious animations, and so much more. If you were coming into Calico expecting a serious cafe management game, go elsewhere. Your best bet with this game is to abandon all expectation. Go in with no impression at all and simply embrace the magic of what's put in front of you. There is simply no better way to play the game. Every function that is put in is purely for lighthearted entertainment. My personal favourite with the 'Wiggle Animal' button. Truly top-tier, high-quality gameplay. I couldn't be happier with the hours put into this game. I enjoyed every second of it, goofy and wholesome as it was.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: - A nice, relaxing open-world game (I haven finished the game, but I think the basic idea is that you have a cat cafe and you go around meeting other people on an island).For example, I think it kind of feels like Legend of Zelda, except I don't think you have any weapons or fight any enemies.- You get to pet random animals, pick them up, and (usually) store them on your head.  That is a sense of the kind of quirky fun in the game.- I think there might be some sort of bug that is preventing me from bringing an artic fox to the cafe.  Eventually, I solved the problem by setting the fox back to "Roam," waiting until I  payed the  game another  day, and then I was able to successfully "find" it again to complete the task.- The camera can be wonky sometimes.  Not to serious, but it can be a bit distracting.- I think the game was designed with a mostly female audience in mind.  There were some male options, such as being able to give my character a beard.  However, I think you start the game without the ability to select male or gender neutral shoes (and you earn money to buy outerwear later on).To be fair, the opposite is probably usually true for most females that play games.  So, I don't think I should complain too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, this game is extremely glitchy. Your character and the NPCs (human and animal alike) are often clipping in and out of the scenery and sometimes interacting very strangely with objects around them. It is definitely better with a controller but I still had to use my mouse to select furniture for some reason. However, I'm still recommending Calico because this is exactly the game I wanted and couldn't find. The pastels, witchy vibes, various cute animals, furniture, clothes and cooking all won me over pretty quickly. You play as someone who comes to town to run a cat cafe and you do quests for likeable NPCs while also decorating your cafe and collecting cute clothes. There are multiple witches in town and potions and magic play a large role in the story. The cute aesthetics and endless customization options (for your character, furniture, animals), allow for an extremely satisfying experience. There's no grid, so you can place objects anywhere within the cat cafe property, this is both very helpful and extremely frustrating. The game itself is gorgeous, full of pastels and nature, and there are a lot more types of animals than just cats. If you love cute animals, pastels, and witchy vibes I'd say this is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably the most bizarre entertainment I've gotten from a game in several years. This bills itself as a wholesome, cutesy cat cafe simulator of sorts, but it comes off super weird yet really fun. Honestly I haven't laughed this awkwardly in ages, where else after all can you ride a giant psychedelic-coloured cat through town and nobody minds, not even the owl girls?The cat cafe part is pretty cool, you can set up themed tables on the main floor along with display cases for food and the odd pet bed, then do the same for the second floor living quarters. Every animal in the game can be made a cafe pet, barring a couple story-centric ones. Animals can be carried, played with, worn like hats, and if sprayed with giant potion, ridden upon. Cooking food is...trippy - you get shrunk down in size and toss whole bags, jars, and raw ingredients inside a giant dish to cook items while running to and fro across the stove top and kitchen counters.The developers are still quite active on Discord which is good as it has a few small bugs like stuck animals and people not appearing in the game world despite the map insisting they're right in front of you. New content is still coming out which is good as once you complete the story quests there's not much of anything left to do beyond serving up different dishes and raking in cash you'll never spend.I'd definitely buy it again at full price, but those of you concerned about limited replayability may wish to hold off for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super pretty and it's a pretty relaxing time! It definitely has room to improve, such as better support with the keyboard and mouse as well as other bugs, but I'll still play it whenever I'm craving a cute game to sit down and relax with. I sincerely hope the developer(s) plan on updating the game with new features cause it's something that could have a lot of replay ability so long as it's done right.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could give this game a better review. It's got some very interesting concepts. Unfortunately, aside from being really light on content, it's pretty badly unpolished, especially where things like animation are concerned. People and animals (the main part of the game) constantly bug out. I find NPCs standing with their faces in walls. They don't turn to look at me when I speak to them. They gather in overlapping groups outside the door of my cafe. The animals try to sit on the furniture but end up mostly hovering in midair. They wiggle and flop weirdly when you pick them up.Just now, I had gotten off of one of my horses, only to turn around and find it gone. It neither returned to the cafe or to where I'd originally found it. So I took the other horse which I'm fairly sure moves even faster, and only stops if you completely let go of the stick. It will continue to shoot forward if you just dismount. However, this time I stopped before dismounting and the horse...proceeded to skate backwards up a hill, heading for a mountain. And so as my horse gently ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off into the distance, I decided to partake of that same wisdom and close the game.It's not actually a cafe sim. It doesn't have much story and has extremely little content. And it's just a bit too broken on top of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't live up to the hype at all.Sure, it's cute from the outside and the concept is great but it's been executed so terribly. I'm normally into very stylised graphics but the game does a disservice to the cel-shaded style which is what I *think* they were going for. The customisation is pretty limited and trying to make my character was the most frustrating thing I've done in any game. THE CONTROLS! OH, GOD, THE CONTROLS!!The controls are not in the slightest bit intuitive. I was hoping the controls were only janky and horrible during character creation but no, it extends to gameplay too. Decorating my cafe was annoying and felt gross.I didn't get far into the gameplay but the animations I experienced were weird and off putting. I was trying to play with a cat for a while, wondering why it wasn't working. When I looked closer I realised the cat was trying to grab the toy (I think?) but it's legs were twisting in and out of its body.Look, I know there's very few games out there in terms of representation, but that doesn't mean we can't have standards. Just because a game is inclusive, it doesn't make it good. I'd LOVE a game where my plus-sized, non-binary arse could run a cute cat cafe living the full fantasy, but this isn't it.Save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like Calico was made for me. It's an extremely relaxing and fun game with hilarious touches that would have me smiling and giggling.There are a couple of bugs, particularly when it comes to the dialogue, but overall, I love it and would highly recommend it to anyone who loves cats and games like Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Calico was an amazing experience! I love cute and relaxing games, so it was a perfect match. The story is interesting, the characters are amazing (and I loved that we could see their pronouns), the animals are super cute and the new customization options add a lot to the game. Although I have finished the story and decorated my cafe, I'd like to keep playing, so maybe in the future it would be a good idea to either create a DLC with new worlds to explore or add a few end-game mechanics such as repetitive delivery quests to earn more money so we can buy more decorations (right now the only way to get more money is to wait for customers to show up and buy something), add more decor sets and clothes (hats in particular because I love making my animals look sily in them). Something else I'd like to point out is that the game can be a little buggy when it comes to colliding with animals, objects, terrain and other characters where sometimes I'd go through them or they would clip (my poor arctic fox got seriously stuck >in< the cafe wall). I don't know if that was a deliberate choice made by the devs, but I, personally, would prefer to not be able to go through things, I think it'd make the game look a little bit more polished. Nonetheless, Calico is amazing and I'm really looking forward to future updates and/or DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: What to even say about this game except what an amazing creation it is. There is so much love and care that went into this game and you can absolutely tell. All the cute little details right down to the artwork that went into the world clock, are so beautiful and captivating. This game had me hooked from the first second and I've been playing 5 hours now nonstop. I just now took a break to review the game. Whoever made this gem thank you, I've never played anything so fun yet relaxing. The world, the characters, the fashion, the animals, all of it, has been an absolute pleasure to play and experience and I already can't wait to play some more!Edit: So, I "finished" the game and my above review still stands. This game is magical and adorable in every way. But here's my beef-It's no where near long enough. I bought this game on sale for about $10. My rule of thumb is I want about a dollar an hour, so if I spent $10 that means I want about 10 hours of decent game play. This game could be SO MUCH MORE THAN IT IS. I've never played a game quite like this one, it's so relaxing and fun and magical. The atmosphere and character designs are so on point. But the game feels so empty underneath it all. There isn't much there at the end of the day, and I would love this game to get big so they can maybe expand upon it. I. Want. More. of this game so bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It has a great start but there are bugs and quest issues. However they already released a patch so it's cool that the devs are on top of it. I hope more quality of life and performance features will be added!Overall it is a cute game... although I wish more animals could be stationed at the Cafe! It's a fun. feel good experience with lots of customization for your character. I do feel like it needs more content though.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Calico since the BETA came out and I really enjoy it for its aesthetic and its coziness! I always love to unwind and complete quests for the townspeople whom I also love because they are each unique and cute in their own way. The only 'negative' is that its a bit buggy but the bugs personally don't bother me. They actually give me a laugh from time to time like when a horse is running backwards or when an animal is stuck mid air lol. Just silly little bugs like that. All in all I definitely recommend you try this game if you're looking for something to help u relax or something cute to play. I find it very underrated!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very cute. Exactly what I expected from screenshots and videos. In the few hours I've played so far, I haven't had any game-breaking bugs (did get stuck in a wall once, but issue was fixed with the teleportation option). I like the customization options and find the wackiness charming. Spent the majority of my time sending silly clips to friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I actually played this game before the major update. I found it super cute, and was honestly not too disturbed with the few bugs. It reminded me of early video games, and added a strange feeling of nostalgia. The simple whimsical feel of the game is great, and the cats are super cute. I wasted so much time playing this game, just looking for cats! I had a blast. That being said, its probably not for everyone, but if you like cute whimsical games and dont mind a few tiny bugs, you should try out this slightly absurd little catgame :D
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A very laid back game, full of fun & adventure! You inherit a cat cafe and it is just magic from then on, you can collect animals, furniture and cute clothing. Help the local people in the area, go on quests and discover fun new places! I highly recommend this game if you're wanting a visually cute game that has a fun story and is easy to follow.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It took about 10 hours to beat the main story and almost 13 hours to collect all the achievements. This is a delightfully calm game with a wide range of animals for the player to befriend. There is a plot, but it's low-drama which I adore. You can also continue managing your café after beating the main story, meaning there's a theoretically infinite amount of content in the form of just doing your job.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: LGBTQ+ friendly! Every character has pronouns and it has a beautiful art style. My only complaint is its too short!This game contains a beautifully styled world of running a cat cafe. Complete character customization and yes you can pet EVERYTHING.**Updated**Following the December 22, 2022 update all I can say is WOW. In this update, we were given (for completely free) New cooking mini-games which add so much more replayability, and have better scores to increase money! Which also added new animals to collect and send to our cafe. More customization for your cafe with Wallpaper and Floors! Mouse and keyboard controls are way more tolerable and I can actually play without a controller! While mounted on an animal you are considerably faster. The graphics look much smoother.What I wish for the future:MORE CAFE CUSTOMIZATION. Ability to customize the whole cafe exterior and kitchen. I am a goth baddie and would love to make a spooky kitchen! Stairs are also not customizable but these are all small wishes. Maybe the ability to change your cafe’s logo would be neat! One animal I would love to see included is bats! I have a soft spot for those Lil guys. FAST TRAVEL. Esp for the mountains can be a heck of a journey. Maybe add a swimsuit option for the hot springs? In general, I love this game more than anything and this update has given me more reasons to play beyond 100% completion! Thank you Peachy Keen Games. Keep on creating!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty short, but it is so worth it! The art work is absolutely adorable! I loved it so much I even had to buy it on the switch as well! <3The pc version and the switch version are a little different. This pc version has a lot more customization to it. I absolutely adore how much different stuff is in this game. There's cats, dogs, etc. It is much needed if you adore simple kawaii games.A must buy tbh.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an adorable and sweet (no pun intended) game meant to bring happiness and relaxation to all who play it. The art style is really adorable, the human and animal NPCs are really nice, and some of the cooking mini games are fun although it needs practice to get the hang of it. Good thing the cooking mini games are overhauled from chucking items into a pot to creatively cooking the food when I played the game.OST is really relaxing, the vocals are provided by Emily Evans who also worked on vocals for the music of Nier: Automata, one of my favourite video game OSTs of all time.Some criticism I have with Calico is it is recommended to play on a controller, but an update for mouse and keyboard users would be appreciated, and fix a few graphical glitches so it would look nicer.I got Calico as a steam key from a charity event and eventually played it after going through some painful and busy events in my life, after I finished playing the game, I felt more optimistic, relaxed, and forgiving afterwards.I look forward to more games by the creators at Peachy Keen Games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game awhile ago, and had it on my wishlist ever since, but after watching Jacob and Julia play it on their SecretSleepoverSociety stream, I knew I needed it, and boy was I right! I have to say, what really sold me was the crazy amount of customization options for an Indie game, the inclusivity, and of course, the fact that you can make cats BIG! I'll also say, my thoughts on the game were very similar to Jacob and Julia's, yes, there were some glitchy bits, but that's to be expected with not only how new the game is, but the fact that it's an indie game, and because the glitches haven't been game breaking, they honestly kind of add to the humor and fun of the game! The game is so good, so charming, and has so many cool game mechanics I never even knew I wanted that any glitch is more than worth it! Now, I will say, there were a couple things I'm sure are being worked on at the moment that did affect my playing slightly, but the were fixable by futzing around a bit, and again, I'm sure they're being worked on. The only advice I can give is that you should try to slow down and enjoy it day by day rather than speed through all the objectives like I did, because while there are still a lot of things to do after the game's "ending," there's a bit less incentive, and that could cause some people to want to play less, which isn't the case for me, but still, just something to consider. All in all though, for the price, and the amount of unique and charming content in this game, it is definitely a must have! Ps: I would die for Pudgems! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game was given to me by a friend and this is one of those games that you just enjoy on a Sunday. It's very sweet and you can tell there is a lot of love put into this game. Some of the mini games for cooking (like the one for bagels specifically) were a little difficult but that kind of thing can be easily adjusted. I loved having a little spooky but cute cafe full of cats and becoming a witch that helps the town <3 Definitely would recommend if you wanna have a game that is easy to finish but will a smile to your face C:
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: While I would recommend this game, I feel there are a few things Calico needs to make it really shine.- The food mini games range from funny to horrible (tart pool, never again), but are not great for accessibility, having an option to play the mini game (for the bonus) and making the food without the mini games (for no bonus) would be a happy medium.- Clutter. This game needs clutter to make the cafe really come alive. - I would like to be able to put toys down without having to interact with the animals myself, so the animals would independently play. - Better AI and routines. Having the NPCs live their own little lives while not at the cafe would make the areas feel more alive. Secondly, the animals have a tendency to walk into the house, stairs or fence.  - Wider range of clothing and accessories would be great. Animal feet like some NPCs have as well allowing to identify as animal/human hybrid.This is a great game to sink a few hours into with cute animals and bipedal cats, the silly physics are hilarious at times!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on a whim. Downloaded it god knows how much later on a whim. Instantly fell in love with it, and 100%'d it in one sitting (a little under 8 hours). Time flew by as I went around discovering all the adorable animals that were begging to be petted, baked recipe after recipe as a tiny little creature in a big kitchen, decorated my cafe with bits and bobs and animals alike, and met and fell in love with every npc in sight as I grew to know them a little bit and fulfil their adorable requests.10/10, would fly around on a giant owl again
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: CALICO 7.8/10 Calico is a game where you move to a new island and you are running a cat cafe.Its about 7 hours of gameplay to complete it. More if you keep returning to decorate and hangout with animals.Overall in my opinion this game is that it is worth the 12$ price tag. Here are some pros & cons.PROS:♡ Tiny game, easy to run, easy to 100% complete.♡ The art style of this game is what sold me.♡ The soundtrack.♡ You get to decorate an adorable cat cafe♡ You get to collect jiggly silly animals. They can sit on your head, hold them or even mount them!♡ Character customization♡ LGBT+ friendly♡ Simple story line to follow. Not too drawn out or boring.♡ Controls are extremely simple as they're on your screen by default. (Can be turned off with H on keyboard)CONS:* I know this game just came out but here are some of my ideas on how to make this game better and able to come back to*- There are some bugs for sure. This is an indie game and some physics end up breaking. Normally it isn't too bad and easy to fix.- I wish you could easily buy the furniture and decor you want, or at least could see everything you could buy but have them in rotations. Its hard to know what to look out for or if it just doesn't even exist. -Be able to bring up mouse for the map so you can hover over each character to know who's who.-Have multiple display cases for baked goods.-Expansions for cafe/ room upstairs.-Place items outside the cafe + outside cafe animal list._______________________________________________As I'm sure the devs have more up their sleeves in things they could add, these are just my simple thoughts. I put off buying this game for a bit and I'm honestly glad I finally gave in. I hope with all the support this game gets some epic updates because I think its at an amazing beginning!

_childDocuments_.review: Too much running around for my taste and I didn't care much about the cafe element of the game but:1) there are tiny, normal-sized, and GIGANTIC cats2) you can hold a cat, pet a cat, have it hang around in your cafe, ride a cat and last but not least - put a cat on your head3) there is a city run by cats, including corpo-cats wearing tiesSome of the above is also true for other animals. _childDocuments_.review: Bought this game after I played the demo and thought it was cute! I am probably biased in that I like cats/animals/cute games like this.It's a lil game in which you are the new owner of a town cafe. You do quests for the people of the town and that opens up new areas of the island to discover. The quests aren't complex which was nice and you can't ♥♥♥♥ them up (or I did not manage to), and I generally found that I'd likely already done the thing they were asking if it was something like make this food or find this animal. I felt like some of the characters needed a bit more to them or I completed their ENTIRE bunch of quests too fast, and in the later sections there DEFINITELY needed to be more NPCs. I understand that the town you start in is the central hub but there shouldn't be more NPCs in the town than there is in the city!!!For the animals, there's LOADS of animals, some of which you can only find once you've done certain quests/unlocked certain items. Any animal you find on the island you can have follow you around or have stay at your cafe and you just gotta pick them up to add them to your log of animals. From that log of animals you can change where they are and it's all very nice and simple, you can also see how many you've missed as well. This is super helpful for certain quests because sometimes the animal can be quite far away! ALSO, you unlock a potion to make the animals bigger so you can ride them round the island which was great fun tbh (I had Aussie with me the whole way through the game!).The character creation is really cute, there's a whole bunch of body type options that I rarely see in games! You can change what you look like whenever you like too so you're not locked in to anything. Also there's a bunch of clothes you can buy and you can make them whatever colour you want rather than buying different colour variations. With a magic potion you can make your hair sparkly and that was great. The clothes tend to be more feminine but maybe that was just the combos I was making!The actual cafe section itself is alright but this was the part of the game where I thought it was a bit basic. I'd love to have it a bit more expanded. I liked the cooking part, finding the ingredients and throwing them into the bowl was fun, but once you'd made something you never had to make it again. Also, missing the bowl with the butter and having the butter fly to the other end of the counter was hilarious, thankfully it doesn't fly onto the floor! Wish I could display more things in the cafe too! Also, it was nice decorating it however I wanted though I'd love more wall space to hang the plants/wall decorations!Only other gripes I had about the game was the bug that I know the devs are already aware of and are trying to fix: characters getting stuck at the main gate to your cafe. There's no way to get them to move because they just get stuck on the gate rather than anything you have placed or one of the animals thats running around. The floating potion I used once and only once because I had a very unfun time trying to get the animal to stop floating afterwards. Trying to get close to them to reverse the potion just caused them to rubberband around my character. Also, occasionally the music stops for no reason but I think thats when I'm on the edges of an area but its still really weird.All in all though this was a really cute game that I'm glad I got! Very much recommend it if you want a short cute game that's not difficult and just very chill and wholesome. And has lots of cats. One of which is called Myspace.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Super freakin cute game, peaceful, full of surprises that made me laugh out loud! Good for a stress-free day of playing full of ragdoll physics and Lisa Frank Nightmare Cats- the cutest fever dream you will ever have. My only complaint that there isn't a lot of post-game content and gaining money after quests are done is hard with no reason to farm the money except to 100% the recipes. But still, absolutely delightful. I'll be waiting here to see if more quests or content is added.

Low key, lots of exploration, cosmetic rewards, no pressure from constant combat (no combat at all, so far as I've seen), just very chill in general. As of this writing it DOES have some "earl;y release" flaws but the devs seem on top of things and I expect the worst of the bugs to be ironed out ASAP.
