_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much ♥♥♥♥. I’m not one to give bad reviews but I gotta be honest here. Besides the fact it’s an un-optimized hunk of junk that runs every computer I play it on harder than high graphics triple A games run on a computer from the 90’s, It’s also just plain unfinished. From the textures to the empty vast space. The ugly character models with terrible clipping. The glitches. The fact there are only 4 songs in the entire game.I’ve only spent 12$ on this and I still feel cheated! For starters the start screen auto spawns in 1000 cats that float around the screen. This is not a GIF or video. This is a fully rendered scene and you can imagine suddenly spawning in so many moving objects makes your computer freak out. Or even freeze. Which often happens. For a game that advertises customization it’s customization is plain basic. From your character to your shop you hardly have a choice. Plus for both trying on clothes and decorating your house the controls are complete garbage. The characters are flat. The story empty. The gameplay dull and mostly consists of running from one place to the other.Each character is suppose to have a schedule they follow. A time when they will go to your cafe. However this schedule is more or less random with no way to find out when each person does things at what time. Or keep track of it. And most of the time what they do it just stand in the same place. This wouldn't exactly be a problem if not for the shop mechanic.You make money to buy new things by selling food to people. You can make more money by having a food in stock that certain people like when they come in. Which you can’t tell when that’s gonna be. Also your involvement with managing the place is so small it’s basically a place you set up and ditch. You need money for any customization (what small amount there is) so it makes turns money making into an annoying grasp at creating more playtime.Most missions consist of running across a mostly empty map to one NPC to deliver something and then running back only for them to tell you to go to another NPC across the map. Again. Grasping for playtime. This review has sorta fallen apart but honestly I’m just so very disappointed in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Controls for keyboard and mouse were absolutely awful. Had to completely restart making my character at one point because of the jumbled mess in the creation menu. After switching to controller I gave it another chance, but I can't say that anything really convinced me to keep playing. The controls were clunky and had physics for some reason when there really was no reason. It just made movement annoying. Had the control scheme and feel of basics like walking were better, I would have given more of the gameplay a chance, but it just became far too annoying to play for a game that's supposed to just be a little shop sim.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I had alot of fun with the decorating and spending all my in game money on potions I honestly only used once or twice (not a joke i had fun seeing how they worked), but im pretty sure most my money came from quests? that and specifically the tart mini game are the only problems I had. The only irritating issue was the tart minigame. The physics were.... odd. and my animals I had in my party kept spawning on the pool table so my vision was really bad on top of it? but I had no problems with any of the other mini games! loved decorating the cake especially!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 10 hours to finish Calico, and I enjoyed every minute. Don't get me wrong, Calico does not feel polished like a high-budget game would be, and there were some truly hysterical bugs, but there was nothing game breaking, and nothing super irritating either. The game play is simple, and everything is so cute I wanted to roll around and squeal embarrassingly. There's a heavy focus on player and cafe customization, and not gonna lie, I spent so. much. time. making my little character absolutely perfect. If you're looking for a very sweet, laid-back game, I think Calico is worth a try. The game looks like a water color painting and there's a potion that turns pigeons into lion-headed, bird-bodied, wingless monstrosities. What more could you want?
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game! Everything is very cute and wholesome, the quests are easy to follow, the characters are diverse, the soundtrack is relaxing and the way you cook things for the cafe is super fun. The only downside is I've completed all the quests and gotten the achievements for everything in the 3 days I've played it.. so there isn't really anything more to do now other than start over and do the same things again. I really hope there's plans for anything along the lines of DLCs or updates that put in new characters/quests/animals/islands because I'm not ready to say goodbye to this wonderful universe!!

_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks super cute, but I basically gave up on it because the controls on PC are dreadful. As far as I can tell, they don't mention that a controller is recommended until you actually open the game. For people who don't own or prefer to play with controllers, this can be a deal breaker. There's no cursor support, everything seems to be done with the keyboard and it's very un-intuitive. I can't speak to how good the game is beyond the tutorial or PC controls, but I would currently not recommend it if you are planning on playing with a mouse and keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game with a lot of different animals, though the focus is on cats and dogs. LGBTQ+ friendly, though no romance options. The story is a bit basic, but it's a relaxing game. Potions were interesting to try out the first time, but rarely used more then once (except the obvious helping ones) Music is okay if you aren't spending too much time in one area, otherwise it can and will get repetitive. It took about 5 hours to complete, one achievement was broken and was fixed very quickly. Worth the price for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely, relaxing little game. It's very short and in need of some fine-tuning, doesn't have quite enough content to justify its price at the moment, but I see potential here for sure, and the current content is highly enjoyable. Riding around on a huge cat is so fun! My biggest wish is for the option to assign different animals to stay inside the cafe and for others to remain outside in the yard. Currently, an animal has to be big for it to automatically stay outside. Aside from that, more animals in general (I'm pretty sure an NPC mentioned a dragon off-hand, but nothing ever came of it. What a tease!), and more quests! Looking forward to future updates for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: it's very janky from a physics perspective, some examples being:- ability to bhop, gaining even more speed if you wait until your character starts sprinting- jumping up slopes launches you if your speed is high enough, otherwise you're stuck sliding up the slope until you pass the peak of your jump- animals ragdoll kinda funny when you play with them, some animation transitions are kinda funky (like when you go to pet an animal)but it's still really cute and a nice relaxing time, and i think the janky physics are just fun to mess around with!so if you want a cute game and don't mind/love a bit of jank, then give this a shot :) the cooking minigame is cute and fun too!(love pudgems, absolutely perfect lil kitty)
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: A chill break from hectiness. Somehow the cuteness kept exceeding expectations and the things you can do continued to surprise me throughout (even after 8hrs). I super recommend this game especially for chill streams. You and your community will fall in love. I even found myself indulging off stream :) Minor bugs or glitches. I preferred playing with a controller; mouse and keyboard was less smooth and had some minor control issues. Only real bug i found that required me to teleport out to fix was when I tried to sit in the desk chair in my room and it would not allow me to get up again. This game is in beta right now so I expect more bug fixes as time passes. Nothing was game breaking for me and I have had a truly magical experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:--Very cute, simple, wholesome--Very well-balanced in terms of variety of mechanics and story progression--Creative interactions with the animals of the islandCons:--Glitchy at times--Cooking minigames seem unnecessarily precise for the type of game this is--Having a fully functioning cafe doesn't really add much to the game.--No replay valueI've played this game for 6.5 hours and have reached 100% completion. There's not really any replay value and nothing to motivate me to continue building up my cat cafe and making goodies, so I will basically never play this game again after this. That being said, it is a good wholesome experience that I quite enjoyed playing.It isn't an amazingly polished game, but I like it for that; it adds to a level of nostalgic charm that I have been craving lately. I find just running around riding a giant rabbit very pleasant and running errands for the villagers satisfying. They have enough variety in errands to have you interact with different mechanics in the game that they don't feel tedious, assuming you enjoy errand-based games. The characters are cute and sweet, and the rate at which you unlock new areas and characters to interact with feels very well-paced. I only wish there were more non-quest based dialogue options with the characters.There are a few graphical glitches, nothing terrible, and a few mechanical glitches that only slowed me down a bit, never broke the game. They recently updated the character designer which is, imo, a vast improvement from what it used to be. They added in more minigames for cooking so each item you cook has a unique minigame which could be quite fun, but I feel they don't really explain a few of the mechanics in the minigames enough (such as trying to cook items in the oven; I have no idea how I'm supposed to get it fully cooked and non-burnt), and I've never been able to get a gold star for speed on any item except the coffee despite going as fast as I possibly could. It seems unnecessarily precise for being such a casual game and could be better balanced, imo, but it also didn't slow me down in terms of progression of gameplay.This is definitely a game made for a very casual player who just wants a short, sweet, wholesome experience carrying cats around on your head and using potions to get a giant bunny.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute and relaxing game. It is a bit short. Depending on how you play you could finish it in a few days or even quicker. Still I've replayed the game several times because I love it so much. The character customization is pretty good in my book. I can spend hours tweaking my characters looks and outfit.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight of a game. The graphics are adorable; the game play is simple but engaging. My favorite parts of the game: character customization throughout the game, the baking system, changing animals' names, "storing" the animals on my head and running around with them. I wouldn't call this game challenging by any means, but I'm playing this to have a good time, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does it deliver. This might be my favorite game of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this for women who want a cute cat game, but because i'm a trans man, i cant get myself to hit that thumbs up. the fact that you can only play as a round woman with large breasts (even when you turn the body fat dial all the way down, mind you) makes me intensely dysphoric, and ♥♥♥♥♥ with my body image, two things that i struggle enough with already. i would reinstall and play again if the devs added more inclusive body shapes, and/or added the ability to play as a man. yes, women with more robust body types, and women of all different sexualities should get the spotlight sometimes. but when thats literally the only thing present in a fictional universe, that's not inclusivity. inclusivity *includes* everyone. i'm just not the target demographic for this game.edit: punctuation mistake.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Calico is a cute little game. It can be completed in a few hours, but "completion" isn't really the goal. Chilling, petting cute animals, decorating your cafe, and dressing up are the real goals.Pros:- super duper cute- pet ALL the animals- extensive character customization- lots of dress-up/clothing options- really, really, really cute- chill atmosphere- all gender representationCons:- limited content. "Endgame" consists of dress-up and decoration. Each NPC has three 'tasks' and then they're done and only say "hi". - actual gameplay consists mostly of running from place to place doing pickup/dropoff errands for NPCs. You can ride a large animal instead of run, but most of them aren't any faster than running.If you're a cute/cottagecore fan, this would definitely fit the bill. If you like house decoration or dress-up, you could get many more hours out of it than me. (I'm pretty much done at 7 hours, but extensive dollhouse stuff isn't my main interest.)I'll probably revisit the world when stressed and just pet my cats and bears and zoom around on my giant raven or broomstick.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Nice calm game. Calico's objective is to explore the entire island and make friends along the way. Calico has an ending unlike most games like these, and there are a bunch of side quests too! You also can manage your cafe and do fun cooking minigames for your cafe food. You can assign TEN animals to your cafe so that they become your pets. Final hint: Pick every animal you see UP to get achievement: Animal Expert.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a niche game. it isnt for everyone but i love cats and cute things so i like this game. i like thats its very quest forward and has lots of customization options. yes the controls are wonky and there are glitches but honestly it doesnt bother me that much especially for the low price of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: it's a really cute game, exactly what I was looking for! music, design, story are beautiful - a couple flaws in the graphics and i'm currently stuck... was getting the giant cat with the magic toy mouse and it glitched out, played credits and now i am stuck under the island and can't get out D: - i do really love the game though!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game when I am looking to decompress after a long/hard day. It is chill, the quests don't have a time deadline, the quests don't need to be done in particular order, and I enjoy the music (particularly the soundtrack in witching woods). I have a few critiques but nothing massive. I don't see a way to do multiple saves so I am unable to start a new game without losing my current game. I haven't chanced it yet to find out though either since I don't want to risk losing my progress at the moment. There are some game play features that the advertisement alluded to that aren't present such as cake decorating. There are also some minor glitches such as, I haven't tried it with a controller yet but, with the keyboard the key to wiggle the animals when you pick them up doesn't work (the game does say it does best with a controller though so that is on me for that choice). That being said the occasional glitch is usually more amusing that anything, there is a potion to get you back home if you ever get stuck, if your like me and worried the potion will leave your animal companion ride behind no worries it will transport your buddy with you thankfully, and in general I haven't experienced any detriment to my game play over any glitches.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I played the game on Switch because after installing on PC I couldn't get it to work with my controller, have put about 40 hours into it and cleared just about everything. This is a perfect relaxation game if you like lighthearted, low-stakes stories with sweet and cozy happy resolutions + repetitive and easy gameplay. The cast is full of really cute LGBTQ+ characters and tons of cute jiggly critters, the music is cozy, and overall it feels like the video game equivalent of eating a big bag of my favorite candy (which is to say, fun, comforting, sickeningly sweet, and not necessarily the best choice out there but certainly one I will make again).Pros:-Character customization is super fun and accessible at any time. Lots of cute outfit combinations, flexibility in body shape, and no gender restrictions -There is not a single thing that felt pressing or stressful in this game which is exactly what I wanted out of a hyper-cutesy casual RPG-You can rotate the animals and they jiggle. It is the best feature I have ever seen in a game, followed shortly by "can fly around on a giant cat"-This game oozes LGBTQA+ warmthCons:-Hard to make masculine characters. When I last played there was I think one beard? I think it's lacking in shorter hairstyles and less feminine clothing, too, personally. (Not that clothes and hair are equivalent to gender, but being a trans man I would have liked to be able to make a character that looks like I present IRL)-Nothing really happens, start to finish. There is a plot but every interaction is really shallow, and it feels more like you are watching characters who have rich lives off screen at times than you being part of the community.-It is like 100% fetch quests, which is fine but I had no idea what to expect when going into the game personally and it got boring pretty quick. The cooking aspect is minimal (you only need to make a recipe once to sell it in the cafe for quests). -Customizing the cafe was more of a pain than it was worth for me, too, since there is no grid and items clip through each other and the walls. If you are patient enough to fiddle with it to make it look good this is another case of your mileage may vary!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the loveliest games I've ever played. It has a serene, Studio-ghibli feel to it aesthetically, with sweet characters and lovely interactions. While it's a bit less open-world than I'd like (Nothing to do once the quests are complete but run around), I do feel like I got more than my money's worth. It's a very calm, low-stakes game that really helped me get through the new year. My biggest complaints are bugs and some awkwardness in the animations that are no doubt going to be fixed in time, and even if they don't, I feel as though this game has a replay value for another one or two passes at least.I'd love for the ability to socialize with characters more than just to purchase or get quests, even if it's rotating dialogue of 5-10 lines here and there, too.An Extra few bonuses: *Lack of pronouns for the player character, and no gender-locked design options, and a wide variety of skin tones and body shapes. I was thrilled to make a cotton-candy pink character with a green beard and yellow skirt. It's really comforting to someone like me who has to present as cis/het while at work, being able to just go wild with my presentation in the game and not have anyone comment on it. *Late-stage Game rewards. Getting a Giant CROW???? THAT CAN FLY??? Yes, please, thank you. And the fact that you were able to find new secrets on the tops of buildings and mountains.*The clouds are shaped like cats. It took me about 5-6 hours to stop and go "hey wait a minute" and put it together.*Animal names! Pony and Pony 2: The sequel. Friendo. Vibes. It's so silly and sweet.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to leave a negative review for this game, it looks adorable, but it's basically unplayable with keyboard and mouse, no matter what they claim.Are you reading reviews complaining about the controls and thinking "it's okay I have a high tolerance for weird controls"? No. Not these you don't. It really, really is that bad, and this is coming from someone who has regularly used some three different foreign keyboard layouts because that was the computer I could get my hands on. You have a mouse cursor and yet can't click interface buttons with it. Navigating via keyboard was awful. It was bad enough that I killed the process on task manager to exit, easier and less stressful than try to figure out how to do it normally.I can't say much about the gameplay because I didn't even leave the character creation screen, that's how bad the controls got. After searching to see if my installation was bugged, because a mouse cursor that does nothing sure sounds like a bug, I saw that the issues with controls have been raised a couple of times already - and years ago at that - but the issue remains. It saddens me because I really would have loved to play this game, it looks adorable and quirky and whimsical in all the right ways, but not like this I can't. I have a relatively high tolerance for weird controls and even I can't do this.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really, really hard to enjoy Calico.  The mechanics are very clunky if you're using a keyboard, the dialogue is uninteresting and way too long, and the graphics make the game seem like it's still in pre-alpha stages of development.  I love the game concept, the inclusive characters, and options for character creation but not enough to save the game from a "don't recommend" status. Animals spawn in the exact same spot every single time which is a bit of a let down, I was hoping for random spawning of animals across the map. _childDocuments_.review: I just have to write something for this rough little gem.Calico is one of the most inclusive, whimsical titles I've played. The level of diversity and representation for most, if not all identity groups is something I hope to see become normalized in media. Add managing a cat cafe as a magical being in an adorable little world of witches and animals and you have the beginnings of a lovely game.With that said, at the time of writing this, Calico is definitely in a late Alpha or early Beta state. This game is not finished being developed and will not be for another few months if not longer. There are bugs and glitches in most games, but the nature and severity of them in Calico are inappropriate for a game that is being presented fully released. There's also the issue of the world being underdeveloped, feeling mostly empty and a little lonely.While there are some animals to interact with and bring to your cafe (not just cats, all kinds!) and a few NPCs to do sweet quests for, the world is too big for just them. This feeling only gets worse as you unlock more areas. The city, for example, is spacious but only adds about 4 or 5 NPCs. Many of the buildings are the same texture as the ground and feel like cardboard (not being able to go inside most buildings doesn't help with this "cardboard" feeling) while numerous copies of one upright-walking cat mull around aimlessly. The beach area, as with many leisure spots such as the forest and hot springs, are deserted. I was especially disheartened to see the Arcade, a spot that a couple of NPCs talk about as being a fun place to hang out, look and feel completely abandoned. The machines weren't on, the prize counter was completely empty with absolutely no one there. This is common for the other areas of the game world and it's just so sad to see for a game that clearly emphasizes community within the game world. There's just no life here and when the NPCs do gather, specifically at your cafe, it is a buggy, confusing mess of stutters and stuck-ness.The NPCs that are there, although brimming with potential (like much of the game) feel stiff at best. They have their schedules and do their best to give the impression of autonomy and personality, but there just isn't enough there to make them feel like people you can care about and identify with outside of their sexual orientation and pronouns. Because the world is so empty, the few NPCs that are present carry even more of the burden of bringing life into the world. Outside of their quests, they don't have any dialog for you to engage with. You can only ask them if they need anything and hope that they'll speak more with you through a quest. If they have nothing for you to do, they have nothing to say to you. This is a shame because from what you can gather during their quests, there are hints of interesting personalities that would be wonderful to explore. But like the rest of the game, they too feel unfinished, as if there's just enough to give the player content to do for a while and test for bugs to report as the developers continue to work on the game.While I can see the developers are working towards patches, fixes and content, I just must emphasize that this game is not what a full release should ever look like for a game. I would have been more than happy to support this title in Early Access in this state and that's how I'm choosing to accept and support this game as development continues for it (hence not refunding). It has so much potential to be something that goes beyond mainstream slice-of-life titles like Animal Crossing (a game that I love), but only if it's given much more TLC (time, love and care).I recommend purchasing Calico ONLY IF you can accept that it is unfinished and you'd like to support the continued development of this game monetarily. The price is perfect for an Early Access title still under development and what little it does offer is absolutely delightful. Again, it's a rough little gem that feels like a labor of love and wants everyone to feel magical, no matter who they are or what they look like.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I totally adored the game and enjoyed it very much personally, but it definitely needs some polish and extra love. I'm leaving my review here so y'all can make an informed decision when deciding to purchase Calico. The Good- Very cute graphics style. It has an extremely pleasant water colour look that is reminiscent of Okami.- Character customization is extensive and LGBTQ+ friendly and body positive. Plenty of custom colour swatches to choose from! - Lots of clothing available and everything can be custom coloured. - Interesting NPCs. A lot of love clearly went into designing them and giving them cute backstories. They're a diverse bunch too!- Decorating your cafe is easy and the furniture catalog is well organized. Animal Crossing TAKE NOTES!- Cooking is done in a fun an interesting way! I enjoyed the gimmick of being shrunken down and having to chase my butter across the table, honestly.- My character has superhuman strength and can lift a giant dog above their head without breaking a sweat. The Bad- GLITCHES. Some customization doesn't stick after save/exiting the game. NPCs love to body block the doors. Sometimes sleeping won't advance quests that require you to come back the next day.- The game is TOO SHORT. I don't mind having paid $11 for it, but it feels more like an early access title than a full release. I played through the whole thing in about 6 hours. Bummer. - No tutorial or help interface. There's nothing to teach you how to do anything and while I personally didn't have issues, I saw others struggling to get animals to stay in their cafe.- I have no idea how the cafe works? I wish you interacted with it more than just putting animals in it and playing a cooking mini game that you only have to do once. I was hoping it was more like the shops in Garden Paws/Moonlighter/that one weird Pokemon cafe puzzle game/etc. The Ugly- Lots and LOTS of clipping. Especially in the credit sequence where you literally phase through entire trees. - Parts seem... unfinished? Rushed? You can't enter anyone's houses. Some look way more detailed than others (Is Estelle keeping everyone in poverty??). There are textures left in that look like placeholders. Again, it made it feel way more like an early access game than a full release. - Keyboard and mouse DO NOT WORK with this game. Not even badly. I tried, but in the end had to grab my controller because I couldn't even access the sound settings without it. Overall, I've enjoyed the game a great deal in the short time we had together. Even though I have quite a few gripes about it, my review will remain positive because for me, the good outweighed the bad. Plus, I've put like 50 hours into Craftopia and that game is literally Google translated. However, your mileage may vary as I probably have a higher tolerance for goofy, buggy games than most. Either way, I thought it was cute, fun, and totally worth my $11.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely has some glaring issues including bugs/glitches. The game seems to be fairly unpolished. Its UI is awkward and can the gameplay in general can be clunky at times. Calico is also not feature rich like many other games, and the graphics and animations are OK but not great.If this game was almost literally anything else, I would not be giving it a recommend.But it IS what it is. It is a cat game, with cute characters and plus size girls with pastel colors and GIANT BUNNIES and CATS among other animals. You can pet them and pick them up and put them on your head and ride them and put them in your cafe. They can follow you around and sometimes when you come back, your bunny has decided to sleep on your cafe table or one of the cats is asleep on your bed.So if that is what you really really want in a game, to the point where you can forgive all of the glaring issues that make this game a "bad game," then get it. Because even though I know by all means this game is not as polished as it should be, I don't care, and I love Calico anyway, and I'm so so so happy that it exists.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no denying it's a very charming little game- but it is very little, and a lot more simplistic than I thought it would be. I really thought there would be more emphasis on managing the cat cafe, but beyond decorating and picking what animals you want to have around, you really don't DO much with the running of the cafe. So far I've spent most of my time running errands for people in order to unlock areas that...allow me to run errands for other people. This unlocks patterns and cosmetics and progresses the (thin) storyline of the characters. The characters are very sweet and have cute designs, but they don't seem that deep, and you really can't talk to them about anything except for what errands they need you to do.I see a lot of comments about how LGBT friendly this game is, and as a trans man, I kind of have to disagree. If you are of a certain presenting gender, and body type, then there is definitely a lot of representation. I tried making a character based off myself, and was really uncomfortable with how curvy and feminine the character still looked despite my best efforts. You aren't given a chance to give your characters pronouns, and many of the spell icons show a clearly female presenting silhouette as a stand-in for a player character- as if the game really, REALLY wants your character to be female. I have zero issues with games that have a female protagonist, but if that's what the developers had in mind, they should have just went for it.Bottom line: as cute as it is and as much as I love the idea, there just doesn't seem to be enough gameplay here to reccomend it. And that's a real shame.

All the different animals are really cute, the potions are a lot of fun, and the cooking minigame is probably the best part. The story is a lot of fun, I just wish there were more quests, because there isn't much else to do after you complete them all.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so much fun and it's super low key. I love a game you can't suck at. the music is sweet and relaxing, the animals are precious. the first cat you see in the game looks almost exactly like mine! the design and atmosphere are adorable, you can't swing a cat without hitting a queer character, and there's even a nonbinary witch!I did encounter plenty of glitches and bugs, which ranged from charming (accidentally twisted a deer up while carrying it around) to mildly inconvenient (yukiko was invisible for a day while I was carrying her around to give to Gabby), with one standout issue that was mildly annoying, but still pretty funny imo. (while the credits rolled, giant cat got stuck, and I spent several in game hours swimming beneath/inside the island before I made it to a beach where I could get back on land.) in my experience, none of them were game breaking, and most of them were minor physics glitches that were honestly just silly. one caveat: if you don't have a controller, you are going to have a hard time. I tried playing with KBM and couldn't get through the character creation, but I turned on my steam controller and it was a whole different ballgame. the controls aren't very intuitive, but ymmv on that.with a little more polish, this game will be absolutely perfect. for now, don't let the bugs scare you off: it is still a totally dreamy experience. well worth the money, and I can't wait to see how things progress!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2022.   If you are interested in the game and it's before March 1st, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.It’s not just about cats.Calico is pretty out there for a life simulator.  Players design their characters and then arrive on a magic island to run a cat cafe or at least an animal cafe.  From there, players can meet neighbors, do small quests, cook food, collect animals, and more.  This is just an outlandish game, where one second I was riding a giant rabbit, and then next I was shrunken down to make a delicious Bagel.Much of the game is open-ended.  While there’s the main story, the focus seems to be on making your own fun and Calico is quite enjoyable.  It’s just a game where you can’t wait to see what it might throw at you next, whether it be placing an animal on your head, or finding a giant cat sleeping in a log.Pick this up if you’re ready for anything.  I was expecting this to be a laid-back and chill game, but I found myself getting hooked by the game and wanting to see more of it.  I’ll probably even end up picking this game up again if I get the chance just to play through it as it will take about four hours to beat.  But I’m already having a great time. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game with similar vibes to Animal Crossing, this is the one. Personally, I love Animal Crossing, but I need a little more structure/ things to do and complete. This game is exactly that, but there's no stress about task completion and it's super cute. I'm a cheapskate, but this game was 100% worth my money. It can seem a little glitchy at times when it comes to potion use and animal interactions, but tbh I was actively trying to mess things up at one point because it was so much fun and hilarious, and it's nothing that will crash the game or requires a restart. 11/10 because this game deserves 10/10, but Pudgems exists so this gets an extra point.

_childDocuments_.review: ADORABLE. This game makes you feel so happy and peaceful playing it. From the music to the visuals to the game play. Perfect game for relaxing or for younger kids just getting into video games, as there's nearly zero way for them to be upset at anything in this game. You can invite animals to come and go from your cafe, you can change your character at any time, they don't have to worry about making permanent choices that will ruin the game for them. One small thing to note is that it can be a teeny bit 'buggy' in that sometimes the animals will get stuck on a ledge or in a corner and the models in general are a little wacky with their physics, but it's really nothing that detracts from the game at all for me or my little sister at the very least. _childDocuments_.review: It's alright. For a game that's about being an owner of a cat cafe, you barely spend any actual time in the cafe unless it's for quests. Essentially, it's a quest game. The only way to beat it is to do quests. Your character speed before you find a good mount is pretty slow. The game is kinda buggy with some of the quests, leading you to have to reload the game to fix it. The character editor is trashy, wish that was optimized more for PC controls. The animals are cute, but some of the "more hidden ones" weren't really a pleasure to find if I'm being honest. The cafe decoration bit is also really janky.Honestly overall the game isn't too bad, but it wasn't enjoyable either.Graphics were disappointing too, but I guess it goes along with the games aesthetic.It's a good 7 out of 10 at best 4 out of 10 at worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:* Super cute* I found it rewarding and fun to collect all the animals and interact with them. I was super stoked about the capybaras. The potions were also fun.* Inclusive / LGBT+ friendly* Relaxing / stress freeCons:* Glitchy and buggy, but the devs have already released multiple patches and have indicated that they're working on fixing the further bugs. IMO this is not game breaking, as you can't die anyway and don't have to do anything that requires great dexterity.* The controls are not always clearly indicated, so it took pressing every button and searching the forums for me to know for instance how to remove furniture, or how to get the bird to fly instead of just hop.* Some areas of the game feel unfinished or a bit empty. For instance, there's a cave somewhere that's just empty. I would definitely expect something to be hidden there.Overall:I enjoyed this very much and had a great time. The kinks are still being worked out, but the devs are listening to user feedback and I'm sure they'll patch what needs work. I would love to see more content (especially more potions, more collectables) and I'd definitely pay again for a DLC / sequal.
_childDocuments_.name: Calico

_childDocuments_.review: Edit now that I've finished the story:I absolutely, 100% am in love with this game. I'm honestly pretty sad to be out of quests to do, I'd love more of this game to play! I could sit in this game for hours just going around doing tasks and collecting animals.It took about 7-8 hours total at a /very/ casual pace for me to finish the game, for $13CAD that's a pretty good bang for my buck, especially because I really enjoy these types of games and there aren't many of them that fit my tastes so perfectly. I would love to see the world expanded upon and added to, this game really is just one of my favourites that I've played and I really am so sad to be almost out of things to do.All the games areas are so pretty and come with new animals to discover, it was so hard at times to choose which ones I wanted to put in my cafe - I wanted all of them, but there isn't enough room for them all! I did break the game once or twice - I ended up in the ocean under the map at one point, and somehow broke things so that I was doing the swimming animation in some invisible water instead of walking at another - but these were easily remedied by using the 'return to cafe' potion in the inventory, doing a quick save/quit to title and then continuing the game. Slightly inconvenient to do, but not a huge deal by any means since it was easily dealt with. I do, however, have a weird tendency to break games I play without trying - so my experience may not be yours.I do still stand by my wish for a bigger cafe - simply because it would mean more room to decorate and have animals. I redesigned my cafe on a few different occasions after acquiring new furniture pieces and it was always fun to do. The furniture selection while placing/picking up can be a bit of a pain when it refuses to pick up what you want it to, but other than that very minor issue the decorating of the cafe was pretty fun. I very much enjoyed trying to figure out how to best make a cool-looking cafe while also making sure it was functional and had lots of seats and trees for the cats.I'll still be playing a bit more despite being done with the story - I still have 2 steam achievements left and several animals left to find in the world. The music is nice enough that I can see myself opening up the game on a stressful day and just riding around on a giant cat for a while to relax. I really do love this game, I would love to see more like it! <3//end edit//Played for just under an hour and am pretty pleased with the game so far - it's cute, not laggy, and the only real issue I've had so far is that sometimes my character gets a little wonky while going up inclines - all in all, not much to complain about performance-wise as of right now, which is more than a lot of games can say these days.I haven't explored a whole lot of the map yet, but it looks to be pretty decently sized with quite a few things to do and areas to unlock - there's lots of cute animals roaming about to collect, and the cooking minigame is pretty neat in how it's implemented.My only real issues with the game so far are pretty minimal, and honestly pretty inconsequential tbh, but they are as follows:The colour selection is a bit unintuitive and difficult - instead of having sliders or a colour wheel, it's multiple squares of colours that you then have to select within. It'd be nice to have it be a bit more user-friendly in selecting, but it's not the biggest problem to ever exist.The cafe is pretty small, it would be nice to have a bit more room to put furniture inside, especially because the furniture all seems to take up a pretty decent amount of space. Again, not the biggest issue, but a bigger cafe would have been nice.Ultimately the issues are pretty minimal, the game overall is very cute and the graphics style sort of makes me think of a watercolour painting with how everything looks - it has a cute charm to it. It's a bit difficult to navigate with mouse and keyboard initially, but a few minutes seems to be enough to get used to it, the game says it's optimal with controller - once I can get a USB adapter for my old PS2 controller and (if I can) get it to work I'll probably give it a spin and see the difference for myself. Mouse and keyboard is definitely doable however, even if not optimal.Overall, a very nice game so far - good for just sitting back and relaxing.

_childDocuments_.review: MIXED REVIEW------------------The game itself was great overall, I loved the story and characters and the gameplay.  I recommend it as a game for sure.  However, be warned that there seem to be some stability issues.  For the first 20 hours I had no crashes except for when I opened steam overlay to look at achievements, once I disabled that I was fine for a while. But after 20 hours, I started getting crashes at random intervals.  There was no commonality between when they'd happen.  Sometimes I could play a whole 5 hour session and be fine, sometimes I'd crash before the title screen.  Often it seemed during loading screens, but other times it happened while running around or in a menu.   Saving frequently was definitely key, but sometimes, especially after a dungeon, the game forces you into days of plot exposition with no opportunity to save so my paranoia of "please get me to a save point before I crash" kind of impacted my ability to fully enjoy the plot.   The last time it crashed was during the ending credits before I could make a save for NG+ and I don't feel like going back to the last save.  So as a whole, the story and gameplay are worth it, but I hope atlus works out stability issues with the port soon.  Your mileage may vary on stability though.  It ran fine aside from the random crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever experience with a Persona game.  I decided to try this after having a great time with Trails of the Sky and Cold Steel.  I felt like this might offer a similar experience to those games and gave it a shot. Persona 4 starts off great.  I enjoy the opening premise, the characters and the world building.  I've read that some people feel the opening hours were slow but to me they were great. Where this game fails for me is basically the game play.  I see what's happening...you do the social link stuff and you gradually learn more about characters over the course of the game.  This process is just tedius...and in many of the sequences they don't feel worth the time.  Most individual days in this game aren't that compelling after it opens up freedom to the player.  The dungeons are awful and I think most people would agree with that.  Its the weakness of this entry and that's no joke.  Uninspired to say the least.  That's even by PS2 era standards when this game originally came out.  I have a ton of nitpicks with this games inability to explain systems, direct the player and a slew of other things.  For every point in the games favour it feels like there' something else pulling me away.  I completed the second dungeon and played a bit after that.  Got into a solid flow of things...but I'm not feeling the desire to play through the remaining 60% or so of the game.  To the games credit I see the appeal...this game has a lot going for it but the stuff that interests me is too few and far between.  5/10.   It's possible I revisit this game if I'm bored with other things.  I don't actively hate it.  I'm just not nearly invested enough to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my first experience in the Persona series, and it has been one of the most wonderful experiences I have had so far in gaming. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not one of the people who played this on the Vita before. In fact, I'm a fairly new Persona fan, getting into it because of P5 and then going on to play P3FES. _childDocuments_.review: This is my first review on steam after several years of using it, but I had to leave a positive review for this amazing game. I will start by saying that this game is not for everybody. The mix of life-sim and RPG may sound odd for people not used to the persona franchise, but in my opinion this game pulls it off perfectly. If you like RPGs and animes this game might be right up your alley.The RPG turn based battle system is interesting with the concept of playing multiple turns in a row if you can abuse the enemies weaknesses. That system apply also to your party so it's fair and it keeps even mundane small battles interesting, because if not careful, even weaker enemies could wipe your party.The highlight of the game to me are the characters which are just amazing. Living their daily life in Inaba with them made me feel like they are real people by the end of the game. The game explores the interactions between its cast in a way that is rarely seen in video games. Even after over 90h of gameplay and finishing the game, it made me sad that my time in Inaba was over.At currently 24$ CAD, this game is an easy recommendation in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Persona 5 you'll like this. If you want to play Persona 5 but are sad that it isn't on anything aside from Playstation, still get this. There. That's the short review. Continue reading if you want to know why.Persona 4 is perhaps the best game of the entire persona series. Yes I am even including the one where you fight a time travelling Hitler that secretly turns out to be a lovecraftian monster (no really he's Nyarlethotep, look it up). In order to best explain why this game is so damn good allow me to break it down into three categories: Gameplay, themes, and writing.Let's take a look at gameplay first. Persona 4 is the middle child of the "modern" Persona games and it definitely shows. Persona 5 has all the benefits of being a much newer game with more interesting models as well as stylizations that make it heavily stand out. In addition Persona 5 gets to benefits from all the advances from Shin Megami Tensei 4: Apocalypse. (Yes they are connected, that was the game that made Hama and Mudo skills actually deal damage). Though, the lack of different damage types can come off as more of a benefit to the new player who doesn't want to worry much about having to do anything aside from having a well-balanced team. It's your standard turn-based combat with weaknesses mattering a whole lot by giving you extra turns. Oh yeah and you know those typically useless buff skills that no one uses in RPGS? Well strap in because those are actually the best skills in the game. No I'm not kidding. Imagine there's a skill in a jrp that says "Increase your level by 30%" and suddenly it makes sense. Next up we have something a step up from the gameplay: Themes. Persona, at its heart, is a game series about a central theme per game and Persona 4 I think is one of the best in the series, either tied or right behind Persona 3. If anyone is wondering where on earth Persona 5 ranks, it's dead last. Sorry about that. Turns out having an entire game centered around "Being a bad person is bad" isn't really gripping. Persona 4 on the other hand is a game that wishes to explore the central narrative that others make our time on this planet truly memorable and meaningful. If you are new to this game or if you never realized this, keep this in mind for your entire playthrough and you will see what I mean by it handles its themes so extremely well. The best part is it's never heavy-handed like Persona 5 is, it's a case of showing rather than telling and I have to commend Persona 4 for that.Now the writing. Dear God the writing is phenomenal. Each social link feels very drastically unique and doesn't follow any necessary structure. Due to this, people feel very much alive and you can tell all the nuances within everyone's personalities rather than just giving a blank caricature. In addition, the story is much better written in general. Rather than there being a cartoonishly evil villain of the week scenario, instead you have a central ambiguous villain with a very clear motive each section: Make sure your friends don't f***ing die. It is this and the idea that there is a killer trying to, well, kill people makes for an extremely solid foundation that the game can build upon. Whenever it pulls out any sort of plot twist or reveal it feels extremely earned as you could have easily seen all of them coming if you pay attention. Other than these three it's typical persona fair: Great music. Personas based on religions so you get your fill of education and culture. Social link system that makes each day feel like it matters. All good stuff here.Now the cons.. there's one major one I can think of and it drives me absolutely bananas: party setup. In most other persona games and jrpgs in general you maybe had one or two actual party members that were overpowered and they were typically introduced pretty late. The issue with Persona 4 is see those three original party members you get? Chie, Yosuke, and Yukiko? You want to perhaps use one of the later party members in the game? You can go ahead but fair warning no one is better than those 3. Literally no one. It's extremely difficult to justify levelling other party members on higher difficulties when your main three are just so absolutely overpowered. Want proof? AlrightYukiko has the highest magical attack in the game and gets access to the only severe-type elemental attack for party members. Meaning she just will out dps every other magically-inclined party member. Also she gets the best healing in the game. (Best dps and healing in one party member)Chie... Dear lord Chie... Remember how earlier in the review I said how buffs are the single most important thing in Persona games? Chie has the best buff out of ANY Persona game. Yes, really. She buffs up all party members stats at the same time. Her stats are pretty balanced for a physical attacker but what really makes her so overpowered is that there is no other skill in the game that can increase all stats at once to every party member. Finally Yosuke. He's the most tame out of the three, but he is more than the sum of his parts. To begin with: you can max out his social link during the second dungeon. Yes, really. Plus the magician arcana is always fantastic throughout any game. Plus his signature move is a heal and a buff. Plus he gets access to Diarama first. It's the fact that everything keeps piling up for him to be supremely useful. Overall, fantastic game. Wish they had balanced party members more.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. One of my new RPG favorites. Crippled by one problem. Vagueness. During a first run of the game it is only a minor irritant. you waste a few extra hours looking in every nook and cranny because the game doesn't give you any direction or clues for where to go. Its's fine. The first run is just learning about the game anyways. But when you are on your second run of this sixty hour game and you can't get the ending you wanted because you were supposed to talk to a certain person on a certain day that they didn't clue you in on in the slightest, that's beyond unfair.You shouldn't be forced to take a third lap around the game because of a mistake you didn't even know you made. Now I am inclined to take an online walkthrough with me starting any new persona game because I can't trust them to make it possible the first time around without a cheat sheet. And when you already know what to do it takes all the fun out of a game. But I see no other option due to the rotten hand the game has dealt me. I won't be playing again for at least a few months. I am way past disappointed that my last note on this otherwise spectacular game has to be so damn bitter.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Golden….hmhmhm is it weird that I like this one better compared to P5? A-anyway P4G is a must try JRPG whether you’re an old time JRPG player or just starting out. The game got it all, great character development, wonderful OST, and not to mention a great story. It had a minor bump with the cutscene and several stuff during launch but no need to worry about that anymore since it was patched. Props to Atlus for fixing it. Now here are the breakdown for the game:(+) As expected of persona series they never dissappoint in the story writing. The way the story is told is very immersive and not rushed at all. Even though the troupe is basically JRPG 101 but i still love it. Point is, how the story is told is how a game stands out from the rest. This is definitely one of those game that stands out. Do give it a try and do every social link if you can. They got some pretty interesting story as well.(+) This…this is the core of the game in my opinion. I liked how each character face their own struggles and become a better person. My personal favorite is Dojima and Hisako.(+) ANYTHING GOES! AND I MEAN ANYTHING! The only limit is your imagination.(+) I loved the interaction between character in this game while during some scene it might be a bit over the top but there are some that actually made me laugh. This is a huge plus from me.(+) The game allows you to tweak around with the difficulty of the game with no risk of being locked from any difficulty specific achievements or endings. So, if you feel like you’re struggling against a boss, you might want to change the exp earned and start farming or you can just drop the damage taken (I don’t recommend doing this one though but, that’s for me personally) or if you’re in dire need of gold to make that ultimate persona you want just change gold earned and bam! In a few hours your loaded with gold.(+) (+) (+) (+) As for the cons for Pesona 4 Golden, nothing game breaking to be honest it’s just that leveling persona can be a bit tedious since you’re most likely going to rely on the shuffle to get level up card and golden hand farming. There’s the opt to make exp drop much but it’s still alot of work if you have alot of persona you want to max.The next thing is, the places you can visit and activity you can do (during free time) is quite limited which is too bad. Last one is.....boi if you think leveling pesona is tedious then come the next best thing maximizing persona stat....this.....this solely rely on RNG...ha ha ha ha. Those are pretty much the only things that I personaly do not quite like. I experience no game breaking bugs during my playthrough thank god for that.So, did I enjoy the game? Hell yea i did!. The game ran a okay. Too bad i couldn’t finish ultimate izanagi before completing the game but atleast i managed to make some pretty broken persona haha. Loving the persona fusion in this game. Get creative boys! Anything is possible! Assuming you got tons of gold and skill cards (which you should always pick if it appear during shuffle). Totally recommended. Its a solid game that check all my boxes. Do give it a try.

(Minor) Social Links with non-team members don't give special perks.4. It's a detective story, but not a detective game. The investigation is extremely linear and barely depends on your input.5. The Mystery isn't very good. I think that 5 did a better job and it wasn't even a mystery focused game. Overall, I didn't like the story.6. Soundtrack isn't bad but nowhere as good as 5.7. _childDocuments_.review: Ignore the hours played, already beat the original multiple times, and know how Golden is compared to it. This game's damn great to put it simply. Are what I would say is the highlight of the game. They are all wonderful and fleshed out, and there's bound to be a character that everyone can relate to in some way. Certain characters have what is called a , which you can increase. While spending more time with the your Social Links, you'll get to know more about the characters and their struggles, while trying to help them overcoming them. There are also  which is a special event where you get to spent tim with friends during a special event like a festival or Christmas Eve. Each character has their own quirk to them, and you'll most likely find one that you'll love. Having said all of this praise however, IMO, not all of the characters are as good and/or interesting as others, but that's of course subjective (Rise best girl)It's great if you're into Turn-Based RPG's, visuel novels or in this case, a mix of the two. The game uses an in-game calender, where you have one year at the start of the game, and you're able to do whatever you want during freetime. Half of the game is spent building relationships with other characters, which both makes you, your Personas and your party members (if they're the ones you're bonding with) stronger. You can also level up your , like Courage, Knowlagde, Expression and others. These can all be leveled up by choosing certain dialogue options, doing tasks in your free time ect. All these stats contribute to giving you more options during certain dialogue with characters, while also serving as a requirement if you wanna increase your bond with other characters. The other half is spent of the game is spent in dungeons, where you have to fight monsters called "Shadows". You choose your party members, explore the dungeon in other to find a set of stairs in order to advance further into the dungeon until you eventually find a boss at the end. During your exploration, you'll be fighting Shadows using weapons and Personas in a turn-based format, which is done incredibly well. Golden adds a ton of new stuff to combat as well, with new attacks and animations, making everything better. It also adds new stuff to freetime, like en extra in-game month, new animated cutscenes, more Persona, two new Social Links, new social event and much, much more.Not gonna say much about the story since I don't wanna spoil anything, but IMO, it's great. To this day, it still holds up as a sweet, touching, funny and tension-filled drama/mystery story about a rural little town, and the incidents and the people that the town consists of.  Like I said, this game is great. It's one of my favourite games and left a big impact on me after I finished it for the first time. If you've ever been interested in getting into Persona, or maybe you've had your eyes on Persona 4 Golden but didn't wanna buy a damn new handheld just for it, this is literally the perfect chance to try it. Even if you're just looking for a new Turn-Based RPG, visuel novel or both, it's definitely worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well done port that I've heard was done in-house at ATLUS, which is a great sign. The only issues I've had with it were some stuttering cutscenes. If you're having these issues, I'd suggest doing the following:1. Turn on in-game V-Sync2. Play in Borderless Windowed or Fullscreen mode (Borderless Windowed works best for me)3. Ensure your graphics card drivers are up to date4. Ensure your computer is running on high performance battery settings5. If all else falls, open the game's settings and turn the rendering scale up to 125% or 150%. That seems like a strange fix, but it's what ultimately did it for me.I hope that the success this game has received sets a new precedent for ATLUS, and enables them to port some of their other games over to the PC. I'd be especially excited to see Persona 5 Royal, the Golden equivalent to my favorite Persona game.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew about Persona back then in 2000 when I played Persona 2 Eternal Punishment. The story was so good to the point that I was quite obsessed to hunt for Japanese copy of Persona 2 Innocent Sin and reading the fan translations from internet before any patch was available. I was so happy when Persona 3 popularized the franchise even further by incorporating social simulator and dungeon exploration, however it was truly Persona 4 that catapulted Persona into the mainstream JRPG market. Persona 4 was an outstanding game back then even when it was originally released. It vastly improved Persona 3's battle mechanics (google "Mitsuru marin karin" to know how bad the AIs are), with a very lovable cast.  The game has a very unique storytelling that balances between mystery, comedy, drama, and tragedy. Technically it has 11 bad endings, one good ending ending and one true ending. It's quite interesting how much dedications the developers invested to revitalize Persona 4 into Persona 4 Golden. I used to think Persona 4 was perfect as it was, but they took it further and rebalanced the game, made it more enjoyable.My favorite addition from this PC release is probably the fact you could adjust your difficulty setting anytime. I have played enough Persona games to know the game's difficulty is a joke. I played Persona 4 using a very hard mode from start (with more EXP and money to reduce my grinding time), it made the struggles during the earlier dungeons even more challenging and enjoyable. By the end game though, the game is too easy when you overleveled your enemies already.Story wise, it takes an unique twist which had some similar patterns with the previous Persona games where human's collective consciousness takes into shape and influence the world.Persona 2 is discussing about the power of rumor and the battle between good and wicked side of mankind, Persona 3 deals with the theme of death, and Persona 5 deals with society's obsession of social media. Persona 4 deals with story about truth and lies, and human's contradictions to choose between a peaceful truth or a comfortable lie. The themes and the social critiques in Persona 4 remain relevant to this date.The only thing that I don't like from Persona 4 is probably the writing of the main villain (YMMV), which was weak in Persona 4 (as if the villain was chosen as they had no other options), even in Persona 4 Golden, the additional writings didn't really add any substantial depth. The addition of Marie is controversial to the fandom. Her social link is important to unlock the true Golden ending, however her role remains minor and not really integrated well into the main storyline, and she remains side character which was added for... what purpose just to add another tsundere?Persona 4 is dubbed as "the happiest entry in Persona game or any SMT spinoffs". Which is kinda true. Persona 3's ending sent me a two weeks of disbelief, while Persona 4's ending is simply heartwarming. The extra Golden ending feels like a love letter to the gamers who have played the vanilla version, "welcome back to Inaba, congratulations to finish the game!".With a killer soundtrack, an addictive gameplay, a very strong cast and a compelling narrative, the only thing aged from Persona 4 is it's cartoony PS2-age graphic, and it's still a classic that everyone needs to experience.Having said that, please Atlus, can we have Persona 3 FES Definitive Edition (P3 FES + P3P contents), Persona 5 Royal, Digital Devil Saga 1 & 2, and Shin Megami Tensei Nocturne ported for PC please?

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I'm not even really into these turn-based JRPGs, couldn't even finish FFXIII. But Persona is so much more than that. It's got JRPG passages, which are actually extremely fun, but that's only one side of the game. The other side is more of a social sim, where you meet friends or further your own stats like Knowledge and Courage. You go to school or work, strengthen your bonds with the people around you or just have fun.The plot has you arriving in the countryside city of Inaba, where you will be spending the next year of your life. Coincidentally that year will determine the rest of your future so you better be spending it wisely. Shortly after you arrive a serial murder there's an apparent serial murder in this usually so very peaceful city. Seeing how the police is incapable of handling it, partly due to the fact that otherworldly phenomena are involved, you and your friends take it upon yourselves to bring the culprit to justice. In this quest, first of all you will have to face your own Shadows and reach for the truth, no matter how grim it may be.It's rare that games can suck me in as much as this one does and it's even rarer for JRPGs to do it. Still, such is the truth I have to accept: Persona 4 Golden is an S-tier, five-star game from the relatively generic-sounding but surprisingly engaging plot to the incredible art design and aesthetics. I love how the game feels, I love the time management mechanics. And don't even get me started on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ music. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful that my throat is hoarse bc I can't stop singing/humming along. Oh, also: "Everyday young life Junesu!"Just buy it. You most probably won't regret it. It basically costs nothing for the amount of time you will put into it (your first playthrough will supposedly take 80 hrs minimum). Even if it didn't, trust me: You won't wanna miss out on this emotional rollercoaster.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first persona game I've ever played, never even looked at gameplay before. In my opinion, this the best turn based JRPG currently available on PC. The strength/weakness system is executed well, and the game has a ton of content. I am 90 hours into my first playthrough and I believe I am finally at the final dungeon. I am still having a blast and constantly think about how I will do things differently in my next playthrough (and I rarely play a single player game more than once.)P4G does well at introducing its many mechanics to the player over time, and keeps all those mechanics interesting by weaving them into various stories, which you can choose to ignore or follow. Managing your time, friends, the mystery you are trying to solve and your character as a fighter starts out a bit hectic, but soon you become a master juggler and I think that is the charm of the game, making everything work the way you see fit.I started the game on Very Hard, and at first thought I should lower the difficulty when the first few bosses kicked my ass. I stuck with it, cause mama ain't raise no b**** and did some leveling/preparation and the game started feeling just right. Later in the game there is still some difficulty, but it feels much easier. Early on I lost quite a few hours of leveling due to not being able to save inside dungeons in that difficulty, but I'm glad I stuck with it.This game is amazing, in many ways, and its greatness overshadows any small shortcoming it may have. I highly recommend this game to everyone.

I really like how the way to achieve true ending fits with the central theme of the game - always searching for the truth.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very mixed about this game. After playing through the modern iterations of the Persona series (3,4,5) I have really gotten absolutely sick of the turn based combat and overall gameplay loop. The entire game is truthfully just glorified filler, and the gameplay loop really doesn't play into the themes of the game. I never want to touch a Persona game ever again because I find the social sim aspect to be boring and uninteresting and the combat and dungeon crawling tedious. I still enjoy the Persona fusing, but that isn't enough for me to want to ever play a Persona game again. I say all of this, but I absolutely cannot deny the fact that I hugely enjoyed playing the game for the first time through. When the mystery was fresh and everything was new and I didn't know what to expect I was having a blast for the 90 hours of the game where I soaked everything in. I distinctly remember smiling for the vast majority of my first playthrough. Nowadays, though, I groan at the concept of touching these games. The game has some strengths, but I don't believe it leans into them hard enough. The characters have really great synergy together, but some of them are handled poorly. Yosuke makes a ton of out-of-the-blue homophobic comments which have aged terribly and nobody in the game reacts discouragingly toward him for it, Yukiko has little personality 90% of the time, Dojima is a terrible dad, and the main character is pretty bland and uninteresting (typical silent protagonist crap. They gotta stop doing those soon).I struggle to give this game a 7/10, but I can still just barely recommend this game just in case someone else finds themselves enjoying the game like I did my first time through.

_childDocuments_.review: Since a majority of these reviews are made by already long term fans who simply came to express their love from their experiences of the original Vita version, I thought I would go ahead and give my two cents as someone who has just finished a Persona game for the first time in their life.Short (tl:dr) review: Persona 4 Golden has easily become one of my favorite games and I could easily see why this game managed to become one of the greatest RPGs to many people. There is a lot to love about this game, from the music, to the characters, to the unique mechanics. This game is capable of combining aspects of a dramatic mystery story and the light heartedness of hanging out with your own group of friends. There are many different mechanics and choices that are given to allow many unique ways that the road map of a playthrough can pan out. Everything comes together to create this wonderful experience that will keep you going for hours. Although it does have quite a slow start, it will absolutely make up for it as you begin to break free from the tutorials and be able to do anything you would like in this game. And Atlus, you would be doing a beautiful service if you plan to PC port other games in the franchise.In-depth pros list:In-depth cons and/or new player concerns list:If you have read the entire list, you probably have noticed that most of the cons I have listed are actually very minor and are extremely subjective. This really goes to show how amazing of a game that Persona 4 Golden is. The incredible time you spend in this game will be well worth the minor annoyances you may encounter throughout your journey. There is a very good reason why this game is overwhelmingly positive, and will be a perfect place to start and decide if you are wanting to become a Persona fan or not afterwards.
