_childDocuments_.review: I have very little experience with the (Shin) Megami Tensei series of (mostly) jRPG titles by ATLUS. I first learned of the series after the huge success of Persona 3 about 11 years ago, which is in itself part of the sub-series of games with a different story and gameplay focus. I did play Persona 3 FES around the same time. I loved the unique blend of social simulation and turn based jRPG dungeon crawling and the overall dark horror mood of the story got me through a huge chunk of the game, but in the end I’ve never finished it. Same happened with the original Persona 4, which I’ve tried a few years later – I liked the premise and the gameplay, but playing on PS2 with its loading speeds get to me in the end and I dropped it, hoping that later the game will be ported to other platforms where its problems will be alleviated somewhat.Persona 4 Golden was such a port… which I did miss because I never owned a PS Vita. Yet, moving the title to a portable console seemed like a smart move – these are long games and the social/life sim aspect takes a lot of time, while also being very easy on the pick up and play routine and that’s where a lot of people enjoyed the game even more. Fast forward eight more years and Persona 4 Golden made a surprise showing as a PC port with a few more improvements over the enhanced PS Vita port. And now I’ve finally played the game to the end.Since Persona series (ever since 3) are so unique in their gameplay, I should start with explaining how they work. As the main character in this game is a student (and unlike P3 PSP port you can only play as a boy here), you’re going to live through an entire year of his life. Going to school, hanging out with friends, helping his uncle and little cousin and… solving unexplained bizarre murder case which has a supernatural explanation. An important aspect of the games, and thankfully the game introduces all of these elements at a good and easy to comprehend pace, are “Social Links” – your connections to all these people around you. Which you “level up” by hanging out with them and helping them during the specific times of day when they are available. You also can and should level up your social skills by performing tasks, reading books or sometimes just as part of game events. All of these things have influence over the story, but the most important gameplay part of them all is in how they influence the jRPG mechanics.Every “party member” that you get in the game unlocks their “Persona”, an avatar representation of their inner power with special powers. While the main character has an ability to “equip” a huge number of these personas, each of which have their own unique skills, stats, strengths and weaknesses (which is also somewhat similar to how Guardian Force worked in FF8, I suppose). Also these Personas can also be fused together to form new Personas, inheriting skills from the ones that are being fused. All of these elements of the game are directly influenced by the social sim elements, hence the constant balance between the typical dungeon crawling and “normal life”.It’s a pretty cool idea that most of the time works really well, as the gameplay needs and the story needs complement each other. It wouldn’t work, of course, if the gameplay basics weren’t fun and here’s where Persona 4 is especially good – the combat in the game is genuinely engaging and fun. While the exploration of dungeons, getting treasure chests and entering the fights with the “shadows” is somewhat bland, only helped by cool visual design and awesome soundtrack, the fights themselves are great. They’re almost always about smart use of the strengths and weaknesses of enemies against them. Check out the enemies, figure out what they’re weak to, hit the weakness, get extra hit, knock everyone out, get a special whole team attack in for big damage numbers, adapt to the new situation. It’s so often that jRPGs are either really tedious, because the fights never pose a challenge and feel like time wasters, or are way too complicated with a huge amount of interesting systems and mechanics, where those, who don’t care about the pace of a turn-based combat (like me) just get overwhelmed and tired of each fight. But Persona 4, for the most part, keeps the fights brief enough, while also keeping every one of them engaging.There are annoying exceptions, of course, and some design decisions are more frustrating than anything, like the fact that if your main character dies the game just ends there. Which can randomly happen quite often at the start of the game, yet by the end it stops being a problem at all. Though, at least the retry options are good (how they work depends on the difficulty setting). The extra dungeon originally added in the Golden version for Vita is more annoying than challenging too. And there are some moments and fights were the difficulty simply spikes really hard. Grinding is part of the game, even if it’s not that severe to get through it and at least, with the fights being fun, it’s not annoying to go through. It just takes up more time than you’d hope it would.Which is another thing that I didn’t enjoy much – the game is really really long. And while it has enough stories and moments to fill all this time, and quite a lot of them are great and emotional, the story is, overall, a bit too trite. The journey through Persona 4 does make you feel like you’re hanging out with weird friends and when it ends it is sad to see it all end, but… At the same time, there are so many predictable and tired tropes everywhere and quite a few of these characters are just stereotypes that aren’t interesting to explore. Even the main story, that has a potential to be something amazing if only it would take itself seriously enough and avoid the tropes, ends up giving in to the typical save the world ancient beings blah blah elements that are fine in a heroic epic jRPG where Hero Person saves The World from The Evil, but feel out of place in a tale which focuses so much on interacting with people, on personalities and characters. Also the key choices that affect the ending are really badly phrased and don’t fit the “dialogue” system of the game at all. Oh and also some of the jokes and situations are just so eye-rollingly bad – your typical “teenagers do teenager things anime joke #5” stuff that wasn’t funny in 2008 and in 2020 some of it feels tone deaf. I’ve not seen so many “gay panic” jokes since the last time I’ve watched a Michael Bay movie however long ago that has been. And some characters, no matter the situation, are always pervy because haha pervy.Despite all of that, the great moments, the great gameplay, the great soundtrack and style constantly shine through. Despite being longer than I’d want it to be, I still went back every day to play some more of this game and I won’t be surprised if I do a new game plus playthrough of it some time later. Because Persona 4 Golden is a really fun and unique game. And, I suppose, I did like the mood and the tone of Persona 3 more, at least from what I’ve played of it. Yet, actually playing through 4 was so much more enjoyable. But hey, I wish they’d make an even more updated version of 3 someday on PC anyway. Either way, Persona 4 Golden is a really good game that you should definitely check out, now that it’s out on PC and more people may have access to it. It takes a lot of your time. Not everything about it is great. And you might get tired of the tropes and comic relief that was dated even for 2008 when it first came out. But there’s a really high chance that you will like it and it will, if nothing else, be a memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved persona 5 and persona 5 royal so i decided to pick up persona 4 golden as well. Perfect timing too since its announcement on PC was around the time i had just finished royal. Now im not a MASSIVE SMT fan, like i know every nook and cranny and every butthole opening about SMT ive literally only played 5/5 royal and 4. So alot of things id say would probably irk or make a bunch of veteran SMT fans facepalm. So since ive played only 2 SMT/Persona games (i literally dont even know how different they are, all ik is persona is a spinoff of SMT) im gonna compare 4 to 5.This by far is much weaker than 5, there are so many improvements that 5 implemented that i abhore in 4, the biggest issue i feel is the over reliance on physical skills, now ofc magical skills are still needed for those that resist physical skills. But i personally felt as long as the enemy didnt null, repel, drain or is strong against physical then just during a rush attack or using a couple of physical skills will always guarantee a instant win. Along with that there are a couple of very apparent difficulty spikes. I wont say when but the game imo jumps in difficulty randomly between 2 dungeons and it gets much harder for some reason, maybe its just because im ♥♥♥♥ at persona. But thats what i experienced. Alongside that dungeons r pretty boring... In 5 they had alot more life and story behind them, telling the story of the villains and allowing a seed of hatred and anger towards them to be planted in our hearts growing as we progress through. In 4 the only real sense of life we get is during bossfights and opening sentences when entering new floors, they just dont have alot of life behind them. AND one more thing that really irked me is how there are no "checkpoints", unlike persona 5 saferooms persona 4 just lets you travel to either the first floor or the highest floor you got to last time. Whats worse is if your returning after beating a dungeon and reentering (which yo u should, theres usually 1 more bossfight which gives good rewards) it just automatically resets you to the first floor without allowing you to continue from the top and get straight into the boss fight... why?? Theirs also weird ambush mechanics (at least imo) and a pretty wonky camera/movement system and finally a massive oversaturation of personas, its so easy to get personas (and it probably is better like that). I do have to say tho that the card system at the end of battles did make me raise an eyebrow at first but ive grown accustomed to it and actually end up liking it. All of this just makes it feel unintuitive. This is all in comparison to persona 5 tho, so... take it with a grain of saltThis by far is the strongest point of the game, the main story itself is persoanlly nothing impressive, its good but not extravagant. However what really stands out is the SL stories, these are realllllly good and can get depressing at times (yumi's) but alot of them have alot of life behind them and makes the characters feel reaaallly fleshed out, it also does a great job at bringing all the main characters together, showing their bond and deep woven friendship. It really makes them feel like a group of close friends thrown into unfortunate circumstances trying to live out fufilling lives in the country die, and i love that. Another amazing aspect i love is the whole theme of "facing ones true self" it really humanizes the mc's and shows how everyone has a dark twisted side, even those we trust dearly. And i love that, in P5 it always felt like the main characters were mostly pure hearted, sometimes there were signs that showed their hubris and how pride got into their heads but it doesnt really show their weakness or dark side as much as in persona 4  . Its very hard personally to choose which game had better music, i absolutely loved all the songs in P5 and its jazzy theme it had going on. it fit so well with the whole character of being "phantom thieves" and stylish vigilantes. The music really did a great job at putting the player in the position of all the phantom thieves and fitting their role, persona 4 had some amazing music however. "Shadow world" "Your affection" "Heartbeat Heartbreak" "ill face my true self" the battle music, it just absolutely stomps many of persona 5 songs. Theyre just incredibly god like, but it didnt do as great of a job as putting us into the roles/shoes of our main characters (although they were always just highschool students, they never were anything over the top like "phantom thieves" so it makes sense). As for voice acting, i literally cant decide one over the other, both games have some amazing voice actors thet really invoke emotion into the characters and both are just outsanding.So its kinda unfair to compare visuals since by far persona 5 has visual designs LEAGUES above persona 4, but thats mainly because the game had a better system to work on (PS3 and PS4 for P5, while PSVITA graphics for P4G was just ported over onto pc with it being polished in the HD remake for PC) but i do have to say i like the whole countryside vibe and feel for persona 4 over the very clutered city of persona 5. But without a doubt art design is much much better for 5. Which is unfair... but i thought id still get it out thereOverall i love this game, the storytelling and music is just out of this world, while the art design is still good and enjoyable. And although i did ♥♥♥♥ on the gameplay quite a bit, i still absolutely love the turn based persona style combat. Im a sucker for it and ill probably never stop loving it7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Being fairly new to the Persona franchise, I didn't really know what I was getting into when I played this game. After nearly completing the game, I can say that it is absolutely fantastic. It actually turned out to be more of a Life-Simulator (which in this case is a good thing), where you choose what you do from day to day, with a few events and holidays here and there to break up the pacing. There is also a big emphasis on social interactions with your fellow characters, which feel (imo) very personalized, albeit a little linear.    The RPG aspect actually takes more of a backseat to the story yet still going hand in hand. This, however, does not mean that it isn't that in-depth. The combat mechanics are pretty interesting, as there are specific character synergies that allow them to perform special moves, knock-downs that when done to every enemy allows for an "All-Out-Attack" which deals massive damage, as well as follow up attacks, which have a chance of occurring after knocking an enemy down. It isn't perfect though, as it felt certain bosses would spike in difficulty, or be too easy. In addition, it felt as though grinding was the only way to progress, as I would constantly be severely under-leveled for the next. Do take it as a grain of salt, as I didn't indulge myself to in-depth with its deeper intricacies. Speaking of these intricacies, they are the core of how well you do in battle, besides just picking up gear and equipping it. This being the Persona, which if you are familiar with other RPG's, basically replaces magic attacks, as well as determining what the characters weaknesses, strengths, and all around stats are. The main character is capable of creating Persona "builds" by combining multiple and "passing down" certain abilities, while the other characters get one set Persona. This system of Personas is serviceable, but can be annoying at times, especially if you are like myself who plays more casually.    This isn't too much of a problem though because as long as you aren't a purist, you are able to fine tune the difficulty settings to your like if you are in for a more casual experience, without jeopardizing the ending. The overall game feel isn't too bad as well (at least from personal experience). The graphics can be a little rough, but it comes as a given being a direct port rather than a remaster, while at the same time still having some polish. The sound design and voice acting, while not too memorable, was still very good(Although, I've only played using English Dub, so sue me). The plot and characters didn't seem too bad either.  Im not really that critical of the games I play though, so its up to you to take my word for it. After finally completing this game? Buy it, do yourself a favor.or idk, just watch Zero Punctuation's take, it seems to be a pretty honest one.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into the positive, here’s what you don’t hear about Persona 4 Golden: The game has some of the most boring dungeons that I have completed, to classify it as “absolutely soporific dungeon design” would be an understatement. Enemy repetition is also a problem, by the time you are on the last third of the game you will be tired of seeing the same enemies over and over again. The battle music, while great and catchy at first, also gets tiring due to hay many times you are going to hear the same few loud vocal themes over and over again throughout the game.And finally, there are some problems when it comes to balancing, with some weird difficulty spikes in the middle of the game that force you to grind and an ending stretch that is way too easy with how overpowered you can get in those last few months of the game with minimal effort.But while those are big problems for a lengthy jrpg, Persona 4 Golden not only has good qualities to balance this out but also has something that a lot of games lack: SOUL.When it comes to its good qualities, the design of the UI is stylish, the music is fantastic (even though, as I said earlier they could have used more variety for the battle themes), the art direction and backgrounds are strong, and the combat system is solid.But as I mentioned above, SOUL is what makes this game shine, and that soul is found in its story.The plot is a well-written and satisfying mystery that constantly keeps you on edge with its many turns and revelations (especially in the last third of the game). The theme of truth is thoroughly explored, first delving deep into how the nature of society transforms reality, the media, repression, and identity and then masterfully tying all of those topics up by the end by reflecting on the desire and need for lies at the core of the human heart. And yet despite how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pretentious all of this sounds the messages delivered after exploring these topics feel honest and are presented in such a humble way that they come off as something beautiful.And finally, its main characters are beyond excellent. The dynamics between characters as well as the group dynamic are fantastic, you could put these characters in any situation and it would be entertaining. Furthermore, all of them have lively personalities, are well fleshed out, feel rounded, and go through interesting and meaningful character arcs.By the way congratulations to the English voice actors since they delivered some of the best performances that I have heard in a dub of a Japanese property.The story as a whole has some incredible moments with all its elements working together to create heart-touching, powerful, memorable, cute, and meaningful scenes. Honestly, to see a story in any medium where you can feel that the writers are trying to convey and present something special is rare, but this is one of those stories.To conclude, while its flaws aren’t easy to overlook, the positives way outnumber the negatives. In fact, the game story in particular has a unique charm of its own that makes it feel special, and while playing it you can see why so many have fallen in love with this entry in the franchise in particular and why it's a favorite game for so many. I definitely recommend it.I completed the game on normal difficulty and I got the Golden ending (completing the optional dungeon as well). I maxed out a lot of the social links. And I played a total of 110 hours as of the time of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Persona 4 holds up in 2021 even though it came out during the PS2 era. I lament that I can not beat it for a first time again. The characters and the social interaction mechanic with them in the real world has consequences for the combat and dungeon exploration in the TV/shadow world so the two halves of the story and game-play compliment each other very well. This is especially true for the titular personas, which you have to "craft" in order to improve your combat capabilities and become more powerful the stronger your social link is with a character in the real world. My only real complaint relates to this crafting of personas and the apparent struggle the developers had to build the combat difficulty around something with so many variables. It can make you incredibly powerful by mid-game to the point where most non-boss encounters can easily be exploited by one of the 12 personas you can have on hand at any one time. In contrast, the early game is very difficult until you figure out the nuances of the persona system and have the resources to exploit it. This difficulty balancing issue shows up very prominently during mid-game boss fights, which can be an absolute headache if you do not have the correct personas with the optimal abilities for that boss fight, which you have no way to know about ahead of time.  I recommend cheating and looking up how to deal with said bosses and make sure to bring the right abilities (One boss becomes near trivial with magic reflect abilities/items.) The good news is that even when the difficulty occasionally spikes I was still engaged and enthralled to reach out to the truth of the murder mystery around which the entire game plot revolves around, so I can still wholeheartedly recommend Persona 4.

_childDocuments_.review: After several years stuck on the Vita, Persona 4 Golden has finally made its way to Steam.On the surface, it's a turn-based JRPG that does just enough to keep you on your toes. Hitting enemy weaknesses and using buff and debuff spells matter more than in most JRPGs.Through battle, you collect Personas - of which there are well over 100 - that determine the skills and attributes of the main character in the battle (the other party members have them too, but theirs are fixed, minus two possible upgrades). This is where the real meat of the battle system is, as Personas are naturally important in the games of the same name. You can fuse Personas together - and you'll be doing this a lot throughout the game - into a new Persona, inheriting some skills from the parents. There are many possibilities, and it's fun to experiment with them.Outside of battle, it differs greatly from your typical JRPG as you essentially live the life of a Japanese teenager, going to school, hanging out with friends, and so on. The days progress according to the calendar, so you have to use your time wisely to fit as much in as possible. Along the way, you develop Social Links by hanging out with various characters when you have time. As well as the story and characterisation, these affect the strength of the Personas you fuse and unlock certain special Personas.The story concerns a series of grizzly murders in the fictional Japanese town of Inaba. The school-age cast take it upon themselves to investigate, and at the same time, they discover the TV World, where they awaken to their Persona power.  They find that all of these are connected, and the mystery deepens. Through the likeable cast and the twists and turns, the game will draw you in and keep you hooked.The soundtrack is fantastic with its mixture of cheery, upbeat tracks, epic battle themes and slower numbers that tug on your heartstrings, and the graphics have a certain charm to them, made all the better with the increased sharpness in this version, albeit still based on the Vita version of a PS2 game.All in all, it's a great package that will keep you entertained for upwards of 100 hours in a single playthrough.

The writing is a bit darker than P5 if you're into that, and its still good. The english VA is very good like in P5. The combat isn't as fluid in my opinion and the general monster designs are left to be desired. P5/Royal had a lot of quality of life changes to it apparently. The music is good but again, not as good as P5. I will say though, the game tends to crash often unfortunatly and only during loading screens. Since this was from the time before autosaves, it can result in some frustrating times of replaying sections you already played but didn't get to a save point yet. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game! At the beginning it is very slow, which bothered me, but I pushed through and it is one of the best decisions I have made in my life (that is to say that the game is very, very good, not that I have not made a lot of good decisions in my life). The "formula" of the game is very good; you have an objective, you get some time to do it (days that count down (almost like Majora's Mask, just not as brutal)), you get some free time, new objective. It might sound simple, but it creates this atmosphere of importance, making you really wonder what you should spend your time doing; should I spend time working on the objective? or should I spend important quality time with my friends and family. Though it might sound like an easy choice on paper, when you actually play the game and have to make those choices, it is a lot more difficult than you might think. The combat is great, the characters are great, but most of all, the story is great and very investing, to the point where I would not be able to think about anything else for several days, my mind was set on the story and I couldn't get it off my mind. Over all a great game and it is worth your time and attention.10/10 will play again after I play Persona 5

_childDocuments_.review: With Persona 3 and 5 announced for PC and other platforms a few days ago, I figured it was finally time to review Persona 4. I first played this game at the start of 2021, after a playthrough of P5 and P5R, both of which I loved. But not only did Persona 4 capture my heart, not only do I think it is better than Persona 5, but it ended up being one of, if not my favorite games of all time.There's many things about this game to love. The main cast is written so well and they are all lovable characters in their own ways.  The sense of friendship and closeness with the rest of the cast is stronger than probably any other modern Persona game. The themes of being true to yourself and accepting your weaknesses lead to many strong, emotional moments. The combat system is compelling and interesting once you get into it (playing a previous Persona game helps a lot with this too). The minor side characters have compelling stories in their own right, and even background characters all undergo some sort of development throughout the course of the game. The music is fantastic, with many iconic tracks that you just can't get out of your head. The contrast between the lighthearted/happy moments and the serious moments in the game is handled so well; it's not all doom and gloom, but there's also tension and stakes. The list goes on and on.In terms of performance, the PC port is pretty good; you don't need a particularly strong computer, but it also may not run too well on a toaster. Persona 4 Golden does also have an active modding community, and although I think the game is perfectly fine as it is, I would highly recommend looking into that after a first playthrough as there are a lot of really cool/fun mods out there.Overall, this game may seem small and more simple in scale, and that is not inaccurate, but so much care was put into it that it feels anything but. There's just so many good things to say about it and so few bad things to say in comparison. It's not perfect obviously, but it is an amazing game, and even at its full price of $20, it's an absolute steal. Highly recommend as a first Persona game, especially while we wait for P5R to be released in October.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Golden is a delight to have on the PC platform. From the characters to the music, this game truly displays not only what it means to be a form of entertainment but also an art piece. Every decision you make matters as you are thrust into this dilemma of managing your time, whether with friends or battling it out in dungeons.Persona 3 FES shows this in no time at all as you are shoved into its rich, delightful story. You arrive first handedly at a coffee shop named, “Le-Blanc,” as a wonderful, jazz inducing track plays in the background. Soft vocals penetrate the ears as the player experiences Persona 5 Royal’s rich story for the first time. The player begins to notice subtle things everywhere all over Inaba, from how the people within the city mutter anxiously about their day, to the unique character interactions as the player traverses through its rich world. As the story picks up, however, the player is introduced to “confidants,” otherwise known as the people the player will indulge with daily as they level up their social link. It is important to note that this game has different dialogue options and can quickly impact how fast the social link levels up depending on their choices. The characters are all unique in the aspect that they all seem as though they are genuine real world people. The immersion with how Persona 2 Dancing Star Night, integrates its story is just delightful and so seamless that sometimes the player might actually genuinely care for the characters. From Ryuji’s brash, arrogant personality to Yusuke’s cool calming demeanor are all so charming in some aspects within the game to the point where the player might play more for Persona’s story than its delightful game mechanics. The player also has the fun option to actually date female characters within the story, if they so please. This creates a dynamic of players most likely not just hanging out with their friends just for the sake of maxing out their social links, but just because they wish to be around them more. However, that introduces the main question, “what exactly are social links?”Social links are essential for the dungeon crawling aspect that Persona and SMT are both known for. As the player traverses through these palaces in order to steal a certain target’s (usually an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥’s) treasure, they will often find and gain beings known as “Personas,” which are given to the player quite early into the game. Personas are kind of like Pokemon in a way as the player collect them to deal different variants and types of damage to otherworldly foes. However, it is also important to note that while these dungeon crawling elements are essential to the overall game, the player could tune the difficulty by altering it in the options page. The level of choice that the Persona series has given throughout all its entries is truly something to behold, the game is an overall masterpiece and I would most likely play through it just for the sake of its characters alone. 10/10 Persona 3 Arena Ultimax is the greatest ♥♥♥♥ I have ever taken.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 is one of, if not the, best game I have ever played. I don't even like anime, and I don't usually like JRPGs. Story:Persona 4 has an incredible story, with plenty of lighthearted moments of teenagers having fun, but also plenty of darker, heartbreaking arts such as the entirety of Dojima and Nanako's social links. I won't spoil too much, but the basic plot is that you are a transfer student who moved into the small town of Inaba. When you arrive, a series of murders kicks off, and Yu and your friends are the only ones who can stop it. Around every month are so, someone is kidnapped and you need to go through a dungeon to save them. The characters are phenomenal, and if you enjoy a good story in games, then buy this immediately. The game is constantly trying to throw you off the path of the true ending, and will even end and require you to play the game again if you believe the many false truths. Here is a tip for the true ending: (WARNING: Some out of context spoilers.) Trust nothing. Don’t be blinded by lies, and always stay persistent to uncover the truth. There is always one more layer to the mystery. Also, pay very close attention to everything that happens on the first day, November, and December. In December, think about everything that doesn’t make sense, and use the process of elimination. To avoid spoilers, never look up a character’s name, any date in December, or anything about the starting Persona, as that plays a major role in the final boss. Combat/Dungeons:While turn based battles aren't really my thing, it is a very well made battle system. I would describe it as a 4vX Pokemon, with more complicated mechanics and more of an emphasis on the trainers than the Pokemon. Getting a critical hit or exploiting an enemies weakness will cause them to get a down aliment. Once all enemies are knocked down, you can do an All Out Attack, which hits all enemies. As you level up your Personas, they will learn stronger versions of their skills. They start out as base skills. (Zio, Bufu, Garu, and Agi) The next level is -La/Ga skills. (Zionga, Bufula, Garula, and Agilao) after this is -Dyne skills. (Ziodyne, Bufudyne, Garudyne, and Agidyne) Each version of these magic skills has a Ma- version that hits all opponents. (Mazio, Magurula, Mabufudyne, Maragi, ect.) The downside to these Ma- skills is that they take up more SP. SP is depleted every time you use an attack, and when you run out of SP, you can't use magic skills any more. There are also physical moves, which take up your HP, similar to moves with recoil in Pokemon. As SP restoring items are rare, you need to conserve your SP and use weaker skills when you can, as the stronger the skill, the more SP/HP it uses. There are more mechanics, but these are the basic ones. This is a fun battle system, though it does get repetitive once you reach late game dungeons such as Magatsu Inaba and especially the optional dungeon Hollow Forest. (Speaking of Hollow Forest, max out Marie's social link before December 22nd. You'll thank me later.)Social Life:Speaking of social links, when you aren't investigating murders, you go through the life of an average high schooler, making friends, having part time jobs, and studying for exams. While this may sound boring, it is probably the best part of the entire game. What makes this so fun is that you have to use every day to the fullest, planning it out to do everything you need to do before an event that brings you to nighttime. Events you can do include social links, where you can hang out with a friend. These not only have great story purposes and character development, but also allow you to fuse stronger Personas and get advantages during battle. You can also spend time at restaurants or jobs to increase your social stats, which allow you to make dialogue choices, access new areas, and are also required to get social links to some of the later levels, and can even be required to start some late game social links. You only have until December (Or February if you get the true ending) to max out all social links, so be sure to manage your time wisely.If you have for whatever reason read through this whole review, stop reading reviews and buy this game immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: While longtime Persona fans might deem Golden is too easy due to changes to boss weaknesses compared to the original P4, the quality of life improvements are very nice.The Steam port has been solid up until near the end of the story. Unfortunately, ever since the second-to-last story dungeon, I've had infrequent crashes during cutscenes and at random loading screens. This includes crashes that have occurred right after defeating bosses, causing me to lose significant progress and having to replay a combined total of at least 6 hours of gameplay. Attempting various fixes has still not located and resolved the issues, unfortunately.That being said, as a game, Persona 4 has more than earned its reputation as a cult classic. For hardcore Persona fans, P4 Golden is a must-play. However, it's also a great entry point into the series. P4 gives a great sense of what to expect from Persona combat, and the social links feel meaningful without being over-the-top dramatic. Compared to Persona 3 and 5, it's a great "all-rounder." While P3 has the best overall story and P5 has the most polished combat system, P4 has a memorable cast (Chie is best girl) that are more lighthearted than the dour P3 cast but more complex than P5's characters. Even the NPC's you talk to on the street all have some sort of ongoing story arc throughout the game, rewarding any curious players. Persona 4 also boasts a mystery-based story that keeps you playing.Of course it's not a perfect game; the dungeons feel lacking to the modern gamer. Still, I have to give older games credit where it's due; P4 dungeons are a vast improvement over P3, and the actual combat more than makes up for this flaw. Persona is one of the few JRPG franchises where status ailments and buffs/debuffs actually matter, which adds to the complexity of its turn-based combat system. Golden in particular enhances the combat by adding fun, flashy team-up moves that will clear the battlefield faster while showing off a fun interaction between certain party members.If you're interested in Persona, whether old fan or new, give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything, if you have never played any games in the Persona series, I would recommend playing Persona 5 before choosing any of the earlier games. It has the most streamlined mechanics, the best UI and music, and a good story. If you really enjoyed 5 but still want more, I would then recommend going back and playing the earlier games like Persona 4.Now that that is over...Persona 4 Golden is a very good game, I wouldn't say it is objectively better than Persona 5, but I personally really liked the characters more in this one than compared to 5. I would also mention that I prefer this story compared to 5's, it feels much lower in stake and not as focused on "changing the world" like 5's story, it begins simply with a growing group of friends trying to investigate a strange slew of murders in their small town of Japan, which grows to be something even bigger then they could imagine.I don't have much else to say other than I really enjoyed this game, maybe even have enjoyed it better than 5 and would absolutely recommend playing it if you enjoy turn-based RPGs, I have never enjoyed this genre of game until I played Persona 5, so I would say that is a huge deal.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been hoping for a Persona game to come to Steam, and one finally arrived! And P4G has turned out to be as incredible as I've long heard it is. There's not much I can say specifically without giving spoilers, but the storyline and characters are amazing - my favourite part of the game. It's a great adventure to be a part of, the graphics hold up well considering how old P4G is, and the music is also nice. It's a long game too, which I personally like. The gameplay is pretty fun - albeit I say that with a slight caveat that occasionally it can get slightly repetitive, but the rewards in terms of story and character progression make it worth it. Things also get shaken up regularly enough and there's a good enough difficulty curve this gets offset nearly always. As for the quality of the port, it's good but not perfect. I tended to encounter a split second of lag whenever engaging a particular move, and rarely I'd experience a little lag at random. But neither rendered it unplayable and only lasted a few seconds at most.Most people seem to not have any issues, like me, but a few seem to have a lot so take my word with a pinch of salt.I enjoyed Persona 4 Golden immensely and definitely recommend it, especially at the unexpectedly (for me, at least) great price point of £16. I was both sad and happy when I finished as I didn't want the journey to end. Nominated it for the Steam Game Of The Year Awards 2020 because I loved it so much.P.S. Rise best girl!P.P.S. Give us Persona 5 pls Atlus

(There are a few quests which you should absolutely do though.)-Very long intro until you get to do anything yourself.--Junes.Neutral:=The story is dark, and while I enjoy dark stories, some people don't.=Graphics. While the artstyle is great, the game was originally a PS2 game, and it shows. Even though I personally don't care that much about graphics, I know a lot of people do. Though the game looks a lot better than the original PS2 version, the graphics still look dated.=The game is long. I personally love long games, but some people prefer shorter games.While it lacks the polish of Persona 5 and Persona 5 Royal, Persona 4 golden is still a great game that holds up on it's own. _childDocuments_.review: You know when people ask "What is one game you wish you could forget and play for the first time again?" - This is that game.Preface: I've just finished Persona 4 - My first ever persona game. I've always been a casual fan of JRPGs, and never gotten too invested in them... This game changed that. This is being written to convince any player sitting on the fence that this is absolutely the game for them.This game is a masterpiece of interactive storytelling. Pros:- The vast majority of the game and it's art style are very much anime; beautifully drawn anime at that. - The color scheme is very bright and uplifting which accurately reflects the positive vibes and messaging for this game.- Personal favorite visuals occur when using an "all out" attack in battle, which really makes the player feel as if they were in a manga.Cons:- Interactive segments of the game, particularly the dungeons, can be lacking visually. Even the more fascinating designs for dungeons like  become tiresome after so many refreshed floors.Pros:- Chie and Kanji- Seriously though, the characters are the main appeal of this game to me. Breaking traditional JRPG tropes, Persona 4 prioritzes establishing friendships and fighting the enemy as a team over throwing a ragtag band of misfits together and forcing them to be friends.-  The social link system in this game strongly incentivizes the player to explore the depths of the plethora of characters handed to them.- Certain character arcs are utterly moving and tackle mature topics and themes. Cons:- I personally feel that Marie could have been more fleshed out. All the other lead characters were given some context and backstory upon their introduction, but with Marie you are thrown straight into boosting her social link. pros:- Persona 4 is set in the small town of Inaba. This feels like the perfect setting for the game: Everybody knows everybody, and nothing ever changes - The main story pulls you through many twists and turns, enough to keep you engrossed throughout the whole game's very long playtime.Cons:- Sometimes periods between major events can seem quite long. I particularly felt this in January, by which point most of the social links I was deeply invested in were maxed out.Pros:- Most of Persona 4 I personally felt as if it was a visual novel. There are large amounts of dialogue, some voiced, some not. There is an ocean of possible dialogue choices out there, so the possibilities for outcomes are essentially endless.- The game is reasonably slow paced. I consider this a pro. You have plenty of time to socialize to your heart's desire and play around with your skills, without ever being too pushed for time. In order to maximize your time though, I advise you complete dungeons in one sweep on the first day they are available.- The turn based combat is well paced and visually impressive, with the option to control all four of your playable characters.Cons:- Dungeons. I like grinding in video games, and the combat and levelling systems on persona are enthralling. Sadly the dungeons in which these take place in Persona 4 are procedurally generated slogs. In my opinion they all felt the same, each 9/12 floors, some of which make you backtrack if you try and rush through them. If you want a relaxing grind experience then this may be fine for you, but if, like me, you are in a rush to get on with the story, these dungeons may become more of a hindrance than an enhancement of the game experience.This game is beyond incredible if you are looking for a positive, slow paced, character and story-driven experience. Savor every moment of it. The few flaws in the gameplay are EASILY outweighed by sitting in Junes catching up with all your friends.

I think the game has a great story that is relaxing at times and pageturning at other times. The pace is good and the social links add in for a well suited level of depth to each character while also allowing us to realize that everyone has their own struggles. All the characters are teenagers after all, so this is a coming of age/identity formation type of story. But even if you're an older person, I think the game and the characters have a charm to them that you can enjoy as well. It's simply a good story. And it takes time to explore all of it. The fights are okay too, most dungeon battles are fairly easy and not too taxing in Normal settings. The bosses do require effort, so it's not all easy breezy. Ngl, I switched to high dmg output and high experience gain after the Void Quest dungeon so I wouldn't have to grind as hard, but it's still a rewarding battle experience. Plus, late game is more about the story than the fights anyways imo. And to top it all off, the comedy is pretty good. The music is a banger, thank you Shoji Meguro. And I definitely recommend playing this game, especially if you haven't played Persona 5 yet. Btw, story isn't as dark as Persona 3 but it has its moments and I think they made this story less dark on purpose since P3 was so on your nose about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it a bit ago for the first time and it was amazing. The whole 80h I spent playing it in under a week was an absolute blast. It had a few things I disliked that I will point out below.- The day-to-day life and fighting were a bit disconnected, what I mean is you either spend several hours in a row on in-game day to day tasks or you spend hours fighting monsters instead of alternating nicely between the two, but persona 5 is the same so I get thats just the way the game really is and this is more of a personal complaint.- The other thing I disliked was all the girls treated the MC as a potential love interest and it gives off a bit of a cringy vibe to some of their dialogues.- The cast is amazing imo, each character has their own peculiarities and the group really feels like a group of friends, especially when you see just two or three of them hanging around out of nowhere, just like people would.- I liked the setting, the rural village transfer student was well done and how stuff eventually fell in place was well done as well imo.- I liked the soundtrack a lot, especially closer to the end of the game when It gives this feel that everything is coming to an end and it really makes you feel everything the group as been through.- The story was good, nothing extraordinary but good enough to keep you wanting to know more, all the mystery was pretty fun.- The JRPG gameplay is similar to P5 and is intuitive, I'd say it was fun.- For a 2008 ps2 game the graphics are not ugly and the character models are actually interesting.- It is an amazing port, good variety of settings, can choose spoken language (♥♥♥/ENG)Overall I'd give it a 9/10, if you enjoy good stories, good characters, good soundtracks and don't mind reading or the dated visuals you will definitely enjoy it. This game was ahead of its time. Also, if you enjoyed P5 you will enjoy this one as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this game is so beloved, if I played it on the PS2 when it was released I think it would be a 5/5 game for me. The vibes are impeccable hanging out in a small town in the countryside of Japan. Trying to solve a murder mystery with your friends is a blast and all of the characters are really great. The game tries to tackle deep subjects like depression, loneliness, finding yourself, and not being embarrassed for who you are. It succeeds in saying something about these topics MOST of the time but does falter in certain places.The soundtrack is wall to wall bangers and I cannot wait for the vinyl of the soundtrack I ordered as I will be listening to this music for years to come.For me the major drawback of the game is the dungeon portion. It truly feels like a game from the early 2000's. The randomly generated generic floors did not do enough to break up the more simplistic turn based fights. It got to the point where I dreaded that part of the game so I just turned the difficulty all the way down and blasted through any combat areas. _childDocuments_.review: Played the original? Newcomer? It doesn't matter. This JRPG is full of dungeon crawling, inter and intrapersonal relationship sims, a gripping story, and some really loveable characters with distinct personalities. In Persona 4 Golden, you play as a silent protagonist that moves to a small town in the sticks and the game happens over the course of the one year you are staying. You'll experience excitement, sadness, love, and joy all in one well constructed package. This is the first time this title (or any Persona game) has been officially released on PC, and Atlus really did a great job handling its transition to PC. This game is absolutely LOADED with things to do and because this is a port of the, once, Vita exclusive, it has a ton of additional things like new Social Links, new dungeons, new items, music and more.TLDR: if you love JRPG mechanics infused new takes on old genre definers, you'll adore this game. It has a little bit of everything for anyone. -- And those looking to min-max or even 100% will definitely need to consider the plethora of guides on the internet, because there is so much to do it can be a bit overwhelming at times! but totally worth it!Also, I realize I have a low amount of hours in this game at the time of the review, but I've beaten the original and plan to beat the crap out of this version too.

_childDocuments_.review: Literally writing this just after finishing my first playthrough, which took just over 100 hours. I love this game and will seriously consider doing the NG+ just for (more) fun.Pros:- Superb characters throughout. They all have a depth to them that you must work to uncover. And it is worth it.- Great story. Cliched at times, but what JRPG isn't? Kept me interested right up until the credits (I genuinely mean that)- Great game-play loop. You go to school, hang out with friends, family, etc, improve your stats, go into the dungeons for exp, persona (persons? personi?), gold and materials, sell materials, unlock new weapons and armour, repeat.- Plenty of content which is hidden from a casual playthrough (unless you're lucky). It feels like you've earned the extra social links, dungeons, etc.- Above average voice acting. Not everything is voice acted, but a surprising amount of the text is.- Animated cut-scenes! - To unlock certain endings you will have to use some actual brain power. - Everything else I've forgotten!Cons:- Nanako's voice actress is doing that weird voice that an adult woman does when pretending to be a child. It is an audio-uncanny-valley thing (for me).- Monsters in every dungeon are a reskin of those in the first (mostly). A small and understandable con.- Animated cut-scenes have a weird quality to them. It's subtle, but I noticed it and my eye-sight is garbage. It may be that they run at a reduced frame rate(?)- Sidequests, more often than not, require to reenter a dungeon you have completed and kill certain enemies that will now drop the item the quest-giver wants. The enemy does not carry the item until the quest is accepted. - Other than fishing there are no mini-games. - The trend of these game creators (Persona devs) mocking gay and cross-dressing characters continues. They did the same in Persona 5.TL;DR - buy the game, play the game, love the game.P.S. I unlocked the Rissette comment achievement on the last move of the last battle. The PC dodged the Thousand Curses move and it popped. Lucky!!

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend P4G as an entry point into the Persona series, as t's incredibly fun and engaging. and makes you feel incredibly invested in the relationships you form. While there are some areas where its age is showing, namely its graphics and the way one character in particular is written, the only issue i have with the actual gameplay is that combat can feel very grindy and repetitive at times, which I feel is in part due both to the relatively small number of elements in the game, as well as the fact that dungeons are procedurally generated, which makes the channels feel very indistinct and repetetive.Overall, though, this is a fantastic game that sets the bar quite high, with down-to-earth characters and a story that engages you. If you're a fan of story-driven JRPGs, this is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Golden is a very very good game, whose soundtrack was amazing and memorable and the greater gameplay gripped me for weeks, urging me to play the game without putting it down to play much else. Although I highly enjoyed the time playing this game, there are some very noticeable flaws that me and others I know have noticed.First, I would like to dedicate a section comparing it to Persona 5, it's sequel, and what that game got right or wrong compared to this game. If you want a completely blind experience on either of these two games, Persona 4 and 5, then please stop reading now. To start, the "palaces" of Persona 4 are randomly generated hallways, in which monsters, or shadows, are placed in the center of. You can either initiate a fight by swinging a sword awkwardly at them or try to get around them, which is hard to do because of how much of the hallway they take up. In Persona 5, there is a stealth mechanic that allows you to avoid shadows whenever possible. If your party is already leveled enough, you can easily avoid them. Another big difference is palace design. Persona 5 palaces are large, elaborate places that reflect the nature of the palace. Each palace feels unique and contain vastly different environments from one to the next. These could include a robotic, metallic, and edged bank vaults or humongous, rich velvet staircases. Persona 4 palaces are, more or less, differently shaded hallways. Some hallways are bathhouse looking while others look like an imagined heaven. They all are, in essence, a grid of hallways that get very same-y after the second one, or even halfway through the first one. Palaces are a hallway made as a method of grinding in order to fight the boss. They aren't special, nor are they very interesting. Luckily, palace exploration may be only around a tenth of the game, definitely less than a quarter of it. While palaces aren't interesting or too fun, they are easily bearable and worth it to play the rest of the game. On the topic of palaces, but more on the topic of music, palace music, not to be confused with battle music, isn't particularly interesting. Almost every palace in Persona 5 had amazing music. Persona 4 palace music captured the environment of the place, but it failed to capture my interest. The rest of the Persona 4 Golden soundtrack did not reflect this. Overall, it was outstanding, probably one of the best I've heard. It perfectly contributed to the aura that the entire game was trying to portray. A large issue this game suffers from is the fact that it is a remastered ps2 game for a handheld console. The game does not look graphically good and aged pretty poorly in a visual sense. What redeems this are the anime style character artworks that are seen when you interact with people. These brings so much charm to the game and make it look much better by modern day standards.In the end, Persona 4 Golden is worth a playthrough. They energy of the game is immaculate. The story is great, the characters are better, and the music is somehow even better than that. While some parts of the game seem to drag on and the graphics definitely don't hold up today, it is worth a play.TL:DR - 7/10Cons:- Bad palaces- Bad 3D visualsPros:- Great soundtrack- Good characters, story, and world

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent JRPG that held my attention for over 100 hours. I enjoyed the game, and plan on doing NG+ and going for most of the achievements. And while I might recommend this game to some people (with caveats) as an interesting historical and cultural lens, I can't recommend it to most.This review is super long, so real quick: there are some problematic gameplay elements that could be chalked up to "it's an old game and doesn't care about your free time". Seriously, this is an 80+ hour game where small mistakes with vague or unsaid requirements can lock you out of the last 1/4 of the game, potentially requiring you do a full playthrough again. It also heavily rewards grinding while actively punishing "playing with skill", so... either give in and do the grinding and enjoy being showered in meaningful rewards, or be ready for 20-30 minute boss battles that could end with a single bad RNG. I learned after the fact that this is common for Shin Megami Tensei games, so... IDK, make of that what you will.My true gripes with Persona 4 though are the messages it conveys through its story and characters. Without any spoilers, I found myself dealing with hours and hours of anti-gay and anti-trans story arcs. This is well beyond the simple (but still offensive) jokes you often find like this in other JRPGs, where it's some 10 minute gag. These are whole stories, and pivotal to the overarching narrative. I understand that this is an older game from a country with differing values to my own, but I still think these points should be brought up for those who care. One narrative is, "being gay is an extreme reaction to enjoying non-manly things, you should choose not to be gay so you'll fit in and be happier". The other is "wanting to be a man is an extreme reaction to being a woman in a male dominated workforce, you're a beautiful woman and you definitely don't want to be a man, also you just physically can't be". With the way the story eventually plays out, the message seems to be "happiness is found by being accepted by others", which is problematic because the friends DON'T accept the gay or trans aspects of these characters, so they're forced to "drop the traits" and conform. All the friends are disgusted at the gayness of that character, with one constantly berating him for it throughout the entire story. And, these same friends gaslight the trans character, saying things like "you don't really want to be a man, right?" and not giving him a chance to get a word in before they all start to call him "she". If these things don't bother you, that's fine, you can just focus on the gameplay problems I brought up in the previous paragraph. But let me put it this way: this is precisely the kind of media and mindset that was prevalent when I was a kid, and probably the reason why it took so long for me to accept I was gay. These messages are damaging; you have these confusing thoughts in middle/high school, because you don't like girls, and you don't really know how to feel about it. But then you play games like this with characters just like you, and the resolution for them is that it might just be your girly hobbies and you can choose not to be gay? And then you connect with the gay character's pain and frustration as you see the friends all gang up on and make fun of him repeatedly throughout most of the story. And you see that at the end, the character is happy not being gay, and nobody makes fun of him anymore, all with the narrative that this is "the truth", this is reality, and you're better off accepting it and being happy than "submitting" to your gay thoughts. After seeing all that, what else are you supposed to think other than "oh, maybe I shouldn't be gay...". And same for the trans character, they're miserable and cold at the start as a man, but once everyone knows "they're a girl", they become happier and warm up, and at the very end they're shown as a beautiful girl all on display, no men's clothes. You too can be a beautiful girl, you don't want to be a miserable man!I don't want these kinds of messages being spread, especially in a game so greatly loved. And again, if you either don't care or agree that you can choose to be gay or choose to be trans, then you can happily enjoy this game carefree. But please, recognize that messages like this actively hurt those who are miserable their whole lives because they can't express themselves, who live with games and media like this that gaslight them into believing that there's something wrong with them. And to have the game be so universally loved... it just makes it harder to resist accepting these messages as fact. I'm not saying everyone should hate this game or feel guilty if they like it, I just want to add my voice and say I don't recommend it because I find the messages harmful.Thanks for reading all that, if you did. Tl;dr: I didn't like the homophobic and transphobic story arcs, each of which lasted several hours. There are gameplay aspects I didn't like either, but they're common in JRPGs. If you are sensitive to those kinds of things, you may find a large section of this game distasteful, as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I first found P4G when I was in my first year of undergrad, so this would have been probably about 2013, and I was on winter break and exceptionally bored with most of the games I had been playing at the time. I got a Vita and P4G and started into it entirely without experience in Persona up to that time and became beyond hooked by it. I probably put well over 100 or 150 hours into it on the Vita and beat it basically as much as I could, and was extremely happy to do so. I've also played P5 and would be very happy and excited if Atlus brought P5 to Steam so I could play it on my PC because that one is also good and has arguably the better soundtrack in my opinion. The game as a whole is a weird amalgamation of a JRPG, a high school social simulator, and some form of commentary about society deeply meshed together in a way that is actually quite compelling and backed by an amazing soundtrack. You spend much of your time in the game playing as a high school student in a small town in Japan, making friends, working, studying for tests (which you actually take), joining clubs, much of which will build these social relationships that have tangible effects when you will fuse your personas at other points in the game. The cast of characters you build social links with is quite diverse and includes a fox, a nice old lady, a... bear?, and other people very important to the course of the story as a whole and obviously the ending of the game.The JRPG that is built into this is quite interesting that clearly builds off other JRPGs and combines elements of games like Pokemon and others like Final Fantasy. You as the main character are the "wild card," and so you get to have multiple personas, use up to 8 eventually in combat, capture them from enemies, and fuse them together to make better ones. You will have teammates who are your classmates that will also join you in combat, up to 4 with I believe a total of 8 or so options, and each teammate will focus on different elements that there are in the combat system. One teammate also heals fairly well so that is helpful, but you can just as easily make one of the MC's personas heal and have him handle that and have all your teammates focus on damage. Generally though you will have to find personas for the MC to cover the weaknesses in elemental types for your team because hitting an enemy's "weak" element will grant you more damage and I believe an extra attack in combat and is a massive part of winning fights.The system to fuse personas is actually quite deep and allows you to basically fuse 2 or at times more personas into another higher level persona and then bring some of the abilities from either of the two fused personas into the new one, which will allow you to get abilities onto a persona that they otherwise couldn't possibly use. Personas can have up to 8 total abilities on them and some use a form of "MP" which can be a limiting factor in how long you can remain in the spirit world at times, and then many of the physical abilities will drain your HP to use them instead of the MP. To give one story from the very end of my time playing P4G about the depth and absurdity of the fusion system, I was fusing a persona that was like a level 98 persona and one of the last ones you could get. I went all the way back to the beginning of the fusion system and actually had to go catch level 20 or so personas from early dungeons to fuse up so that I could fuse in this very specific way to get this level 98 persona to a point where when I fused him I was able to make him immune to or reflect every single form of damage in the game except for 1 very specific damage type that only bosses and a few enemies used. So 99% of fights the enemies actually couldn't damage him. He had 1 damage ability but it was a physical one and used his life so most of the time I would just auto attack over and over, which dealt little damage but it didn't matter because he couldn't take damage anyways, and luckily the game has a "fast-forward" option in battle that allows you to perform the same actions repeatedly and skip dialogue prompts and go quickly. So I would start a fight and turn on that option then set my Vita down and do something else for 3 to 5 minutes before returning to find the battle complete. All of my teammates would be dead because I was just ignoring them entirely but the MC would have full HP and all the enemies would be dead, so my teammates would resurrect after the fight and I could heal them if needed. It made the final trash fights comically easy and it's really cool that the fusion system allows for things like that.Definitely a worthwhile purchase, and I will say the same if Atlus brings P5 to Steam as well. Both of those games are wonderful, really just some of the best games of their platforms without a doubt and worthwhile additions to anyone's Steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: So not long after The emotional roller-coaster that was persona 5, I just had to get more of this magic. Persona 4 golden was just the natural choice.I admit, at first I was a little disappointed. Aside from the dated graphics and the lack of the p5 "vibe",the game starts rather slow. No casino heist, no underdog situation. I thought "well, they probably just ramped it up in 5, while this one is rather average."Well, I'm happy to say that I was wrong.See, persona 4 may not have p5's insane palaces or the phantom thief swag, HOWEVER, it does have loads and loads of heart. With a spectacular OST, a cast of adorkable friends, the loveliness of the small town Inaba, and the absolute cinnamon roll that is Nanako.Furthermore, the slice of life events and the whole group dynamic here is even better than 5. The phantom thieves are great as a fighting team, and I mostly prefer them as individuals. But as a group of friends that hang out together, joke around and make you smile with them? The group here takes the cake. If p5's focused on being rebellious and cool, this one is about happiness and friendship, and it shows.The story is complex, intriguing, and the theme of truth really resonates with the twist and turns of the plot.You want to go in blind, and you want to have multiple save files. Believe me, getting the true, full, best ending is an amazing experience. When I was finally done, I felt like someone put a sun in my heart. "Wholesome" is an understatement.So do yourself a favor, and give this game a try.There's a good chance it will make you happier.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 4 Golden

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I would ever play a game that mixes JRPG and visual novel aspects, but 90 hours later and I am done with this game and it was a truly unique experience that I highly enjoyed. The former genre is very well designed. You basically collect Personas (basically Pokémon cards) and you can fuse them into new ones, with different skills, abilities, strenghts and weaknesses while also being able to pass on skills from your previous Personas. It's pretty fun.The visual novel part of the game is well written and often relatable, so it's basically like reading a book, but a little less in depth.Both systems are bound to calendar days so you have to carefully decide if you want to crawl through dungeons or instead meet NPC's and whatnot. That can be challenging to manage since once certain days are reached your options will change or even fade away and lead to different endings of the game.Ao all in all, that is if you can look past some stereotypical anime cringe, this is definitely worth trying out. I would say play this before Persona 5 Royal first, because the latter is more polished, but also quite different story-wise. Both games are very well worth it (and I also can't wait for Persona 3 to release so I can play that too).

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously a lot of this is related to the games age. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there isn't much to say about this game that most people don't know, but this is such a great game! I played 6 hours straight on the day of release!Before the PC release, I had never played the game but watched a YouTube movie on it along with Persona 3 FES and had only played Persona 5 (both the original and Royal version). This Persona game is by far my favorite out of the three for so many different reasons, ranging from the amazing soundtrack, the HD graphics, and every day life of balancing high school life and battling monsters. Despite having prior knowledge of the general basis of Persona games, there is a great learning curve for beginners to the series to try out, but that doesn't mean the game is a cakewalk - it'll still challenge you to solve unique puzzles and put on your thinking cap to unravel the big mysteries. Furthermore, the game still truly does feel like the original Persona 4 Golden for the PS Vita, even if the graphics aren't the most modern. The story is truly one of the best narratives I've ever seen and the experience is even more enhanced if you go out of your way to AVOID SPOILERS! I am so glad ATLUS finally made a PC port so that now you don't have to buy a whole separate (not to mention expensive) device just to play this game! ATLUS did a great job with this port and I hope this game is a catalyst for other Persona games to come to platforms beyond Playstation. If you're still questioning whether to buy it: don't. Just. Do. It. You're really missing out if you don't, and I promise you won't regret that decision!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Golden is a shining gem in the world of video games, a timeless classic that continues to captivate players with its brilliant storytelling, meticulously crafted characters, and the exceptional ability to evoke real and hard-hitting emotions. Originally released on the PlayStation 2 and later enhanced for the PlayStation Vita, then released to Steam and other platforms, this game remains a testament to the power of storytelling in the medium of video games.Storytelling: 10/10The narrative of Persona 4 Golden is a work of art. It begins with your character, the silent protagonist, moving to the rural town of Inaba and quickly immerses you in a suspenseful murder mystery. This story is meticulously crafted, masterfully weaving elements of mystery, suspense, and supernatural intrigue. The pacing is impeccable, with each in-game day offering a new layer of the story, allowing players to slowly unravel the mystery behind the Midnight Channel and the strange occurrences in Inaba. The twists and turns keep you engaged, and the revelations are both surprising and thought-provoking.One of the game's strengths is its exploration of the human psyche and the inner struggles of its characters. As you forge bonds with your friends and delve into the dungeons of their inner selves, you witness their deepest fears and insecurities. The way the game addresses these issues with empathy and depth is a testament to the craftsmanship behind the storytelling. By the time you reach the climax, you're deeply invested in the lives and fates of the characters, making each emotional beat all the more impactful.Character Development: 10/10The characters of Persona 4 Golden are a testament to how well-written and fleshed out video game characters can be. Each character has their own distinct personality, struggles, and growth arcs, making them feel like real people you genuinely care about. As you spend time with them, you get to know their quirks, vulnerabilities, and strengths. The "Social Link" system allows you to deepen your relationships, offering insight into their backgrounds and helping them overcome their personal issues. This not only enhances the game-play but also creates a profound emotional connection with the characters.The central cast, including Yosuke, Chie, Yukiko, Kanji, Rise, Naoto, and Teddie, are multifaceted and undergo significant development throughout the story. Their personal stories are both heartwarming and heart-wrenching, and you can't help but root for them. The antagonist, too, is brilliantly crafted, adding a layer of complexity to the narrative that's rarely seen in video games.Emotional Impact: 10/10The emotional impact of Persona 4 Golden is where it truly shines. This game masterfully tugs at your heartstrings. It's impossible not to feel a strong connection to the characters as you watch them grapple with their inner demons and grow through adversity. The game doesn't shy away from addressing sensitive themes like identity, sexuality, acceptance, and the masks people wear to hide their true selves.The final act of Persona 4 Golden is a roller-coaster of emotions, as you confront the true nature of the villain and help your friends confront their innermost fears. The climax is gut-wrenching and awe-inspiring in equal measure, and it leaves a lasting impact on players.In conclusion, Persona 4 Golden is a game that excels in storytelling, character development, and evoking genuine, hard-hitting emotions. Its unforgettable cast, thought-provoking narrative, and profound exploration of human psychology make it a timeless classic in the world of video games. If you haven't experienced this emotional roller-coaster, you're missing out on one of the greatest storytelling achievements in gaming history.

The theme of introspection got me at just the right time in my life, so I cannot guarantee that it will have the same profound effect on everyone. Pros:-charming characters-stylized visuals that still look nice for a game that was originally released in 2008-lots of Personas to collect and lore to look at if that's your thing-turn based battle system is fun, but kinda easy once you have the hang of it -great musicCons:-if challenge is what you're looking for, this game likely won't cut it for you once you have the hang of it-if you're coming from Persona 5, the visuals will feel a lot more dated-dungeons can feel repetitive due to procedural generation, turn based battles can get tedious for someI would love everyone to love this game, but I'm not going to tell you it's the second coming of Christ.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game. I do enjoy it, but out of the persona games and SMT in general, it doesn't really hold up. The combat and dungeon crawling is unbalanced as all hell, shuffle time makes the game so unbelievably easy. Physical moves are so much better than anything else, there's not too much point to running other things other than to take advantage of weaknesses or kill golden hands with almighty spells. Other than that though, it's pretty fun. Some bosses really did challenge me, and the beginning of the game is much tighter on your resource management which I enjoyed a lot.The story in the game is definitely the weakest part to me. Having a more lighthearted story is fine, and a welcome break from the constant loneliness and dark themes other SMT games bring, but I felt underwhelmed by the social links and main story. The middle part is especially boring, with every arc boiling down to "Who do I have to save from the TV world this time?" Social links can have confusing nonsensical conclusions, the worst being Fusing personas is addictive as ever, but I don't have much to add. Standard SMT stuff.The music is great, it's super cheery and fun, which makes it hard for me to go into different areas because I know it'll stop the track that's playing at the moment. Easily my favourite part of the game. Same goes for the art style and UI design.Overall, it's a pretty decent game, but I feel like it's the weakest out of the modern trilogy of persona games. It's a fun lighthearted time if you can endure the dated jokes about gay and fat people, and the transphobic arc in the middle of it. Definitely a product of the time and place it was produced in. If you want an easily moddable, cheap, chill time without too many hurdles, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't believe all the hate. Prior to the release of Persona 5 this was the best Shin Megami Tensei game ever made. You use your cell phone to summon demons to fight for you. How cool is that? The gameplay is an awesome blend of strategy and turn-based combat. Think Fire Emblem but then when you attack it zooms in to a regular turn-based battle. You travel around Tokyo doing different jobs, discovering your true self, and eventually killing God. But you can also kill Satan. You play as a demon boy brought back to life at a hospital. The cast of characters is great, full of unique personalities pulled straight out of your favorite anime. Be careful though, make the wrong decisions and your favorite character can die permanently. Still not convinced this is the best Shin Megami Tensei game of all time before the release of Persona 5? Dante from Devil May Cry is in this game as a guest character. How cool is that? First-person dungeon crawlers admittedly aren't for everyone, but you'll become nocturnal as you embark on this overclocked strange journey breaking records and summoning devils.
