_childDocuments_.review: I have a confession to make: Persona 4 Golden is my favourite of the "new" Persona games (3-5). That may be controversial to say given that this is the one that makes SMT fans cringe and basically launched the gateway to Atlus' milk money (where Persona is concerned). Nevertheless, this is still my favourite one for a variety of reasons.The group that you spend time with, aka the Investigation Team is probably the most closest knit group that really feels like a bunch of friends trying to solve a murder mystery. Does that basically make it like anime Scooby Doo? Yes, and you can take with that what you will. There is depth to these anime stereotypes if you are willing to look past it, however.Peppy, cheery J-pop music permeates daily life around Inaba, and that's an experience I don't usually get. Soundtrack is great as usual.P4G is also very blatant in that it knows what it is, and knows its audience well. While it doesn't have a story or themes that will resonate as in Persona 3, or the flashy artstyle of Persona 5, it is noticeably better than P3 because of its gameplay rectifications (You can control your teammates, it was AI controlled in P3). The gameplay is about as difficult as P5 is on normal, meaning it's not hard once you get the hang of it. The social sim aspects are good, and you will spend a majority of time either upgrading your stats or hanging out with your friends to grow stronger. Friendship is literally power as the higher your rank is with certain people, the arcana they are tied with will result in higher EXP boosts to strengthen your Persona when fusing them. The dungeon floors (barring story specific ones) are randomly generated but have themes associated with each different one, breaking up the monotony a little but it's still not perfect. The battle system is easy to grasp but you may need to be acquainted with the spell names to get more mileage, though you can always check what they do at any point.The port seems fine from what I've played, but there are occasional slowdowns (this may be due to me having models at 200% or a side effect of having it be unshackled at 120 FPS).P4G is the best middle ground out of all the new Persona games, improving on P3's formula and making lots of quality of life changes to the original P4, adding 2 new Social Links and new story content as its most notable features. You can also search the possible results of fusing Personas in the Velvet Room, similar to how it is in P5. There is also added network functions that can help in dungeons, and other things as well. The story can have pacing issues due to the nature of the game, but it's not slow to start as in P3, and isn't overly bloated near the end in P5. While it's not deep as P3's story, it's at least not as shallow as P5 is, and tries at least to keep some mystery involved. Overall this is a great starting point if you don't have a PS4 to play P5R, or just want to understand why so many others like me love this game and series so much.

_childDocuments_.review: So I finally finished this game after like 6 or 7 months and as a guy who loved Persona 3 and Persona 5 I thought I should share my opinion about this game. First things first this was the third Persona game I had played. I started with Persona 3 then played Persona 5 and finally today I finished this game. Pros:+The mystery was interesting and not the most obvious to figure out+At least in the Golden edition of the game graphics took a huge leap from Persona 3+Music was better than in Persona 3+Castles were more unique and overall better compared to Persona 3+The difficulty was well made it wasn't too hard and it wasn't too easy at least for me (Played with the normal difficulty and tried not to over level my characters)+More Social Qualities compared to Persona 3+The possibility to work in part-time jobsCons:-The characters were not bad but they were easily worst in the series-Worst social links in the series-I liked the story but in my opinion it's still the worst in the series.-Persona 3 did a good job dealing with the theme of death. Persona 5 did a good job dealing with the theme of pursuing your own goals and not letting other control what you should do with your life. But in my opinion Persona 4 and it's message about accepting yourself as you are falls a bit short. I like the message but I just think it could have been handled better than the game did.-The boss fights were pretty boring and the game pretty much made it obvious when you need to guard and when not. Especially the final boss seemed rushed and it was not even remotely close to the final bosses of Persona 5 and Persona 3.-Music was too repetitiveOverall I still very much liked this game but compared to Persona 3 and Persona 5 I think this wasn't as good as they were. I would still recommend you to play this game but I suggest you try Persona 3 and Persona 5 even if this game wasn't your cup of tea. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: For those curious about how the PC Port runs:It runs at up to 1080p natively, but supports scaling up to 200% so it runs at a downscaled 4K, so it's extra crispy. It also seems to run at an uncapped framerate, and supports 144hz. It has very basic but satisfactory visual options. It supports on the fly language switching between English and Japanese, and has full KB+M support.As for the game itself, it's really fantastic. Great characters, fun fights(most of the time), BANGIN' music, good story, and lots and lots of social links. This game is one of the shorter Persona titles, but you can still easily put in over 100 hours if you put effort into completing your social links. I recommend you do take this game(and other Persona titles) slowly, don't rush things, just enjoy the world, take in the atmosphere and characters, and have fun. My favourite title in the series by far.Overall it's a really solid port, and for this price, you're getting a VERY good deal. Pick it up if you can. You're paying $20 for an experience that you can't get with many other franchises.

_childDocuments_.review: While not my favorite of the Persona series, this game still was really damn good. The soundtrack is great (as is the case with all Persona games), the combat is easy to pick up and fun to play, the social interactions are pretty damn great, and the entire cast of characters is pretty good as well. This game is a great entryway into the series, as while it isn't as flashy as 5, or as serious as 3, the lighthearted tone of the game makes it easy to get into and the fairly simple mechanics make it great for new fans or veterans of the series who didn't get to play this game. 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original on ps2 and being my first Persona game, I look back with much love and nostalgia for this game. However, with steps forward in dungeon design and ability to control your party members from its predecessor, Persona 3, it became a step backwards in the series in many ways.Gameplay: Firstly, QOL changes such as being able to split up your party members to explore the dungeon and bring you items was a removed feature that made no sense. Combined with a terrible physical/magic split (P3 had this flaw as well but it became much worse in P4) and the removal of many status ailments such as the infamous marin karin charm. Also, the removal of the variety of physical attacks such as slash, strike, and pierce. The overall gameplay felt a lot like they took a step forward but two steps back type of approach.Design: In my opinion, P3's world design is a lot better than the lifeless world design of P4. Despite being the intention of the devs to incorporate an inaka small world setting in P4, this came across to me as a world with less content and less aesthetically pleasing designs. One thing P4 improves upon is its dungeon designs. While they haven't aged very well, it is nice to see dungeons that fit the theme of each individual character.Characters: P4's characters can be summed up in anime tropes. These cliched tropes create a cast that is largely unmemorable despite a handful of characters. Naoto and Kanji are the few exceptions that carry this cast by being characters that have depth but also fit the games themes of self truth and identity.Themes and tone: P4 captures its themes of pursuing the truth brilliantly. With the fog representing the covering of the truth, and its final boss representing that. The usage of Japanese mythology/Shinto was a perfect decision for the inaka setting of P4. Despite its great themes, P4 struggles heavily with tone. In one scene we have someone get murdered, in the next scene we have Teddie making bear jokes. It is hard to take the game seriously as a murder mystery that deals with interpersonal conflict when the characters themselves act like they come straight out of a shounen anime meant for middle schoolers. Compared to P3's masterful approach to tone, it is saddening to see P4 dumb itself down in this regard. Fortunately, Atlus would later find the right balance of seriousness and lightheartedness in P5.Final Thoughts: I will recommend P4 but not before P5 and P3F first. P4 is a below average entry in the series but an overall brilliant game, which is indicative of how great this series is. Sadly, P4's success became somewhat of a curse in the series, having made fans wait for P5 for almost a decade while all we got were cash grabs in the dancing and fighting games that Atlus has continued milking for P5.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and gameplay of this game is great. If you are new to the Persona series of games the game is a JRPG with turn-based combat. As in every or most of the games from this genre you level up through combat but another important aspect here is leveling up Confidants, which are both your party members and other people you get to know during the game. Both leveling up your team's level and Confidant ranks are equally important in order to obtain stronger Personas and better skills for battles.I will not speak about the story since this is one of the most important aspects of this game. The only negative aspects I found in this game were the laggy animated cutscenes and that somatimes images wouldn't disappear during all out attacks until I clicked outside the game's window and then clicked inside it. Fotunately for me that wasn't a big deal and those problems could be caused because of my computer since many people do not have this problem, but some other do.This is really worth it and fortunately the game isn't expensive. It is also important to mention that this is a standalone game, it may be Persona 4 but you don't need to have played any of the previous games in order to understand this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. When this was leaked a week ago I was expecting it to be fake. Instead here we are with one of the Vita's best titles on PC. Overall, words can't describe how good this game is and how well done this port is done. The mainline Persona games have always been a Playstation exclusive. Today marks the day that a mainline Persona game has made it to PC and they killed it. The game is so high up on the Vita list because it takes one of (in my opinion) best Persona games and gives it the sweet enhancements that has started since Persona 3 with FES. Golden surpasses it give new life to the game that I thought I was well done with.The port of the game is from a Handheld, it may seem like a challenge to bring to a keyboard and mouse system but instead they made this game feel like it was ready for PC since Day 1 of release. The game is visually stunning, the graphics and models are so high res from the shadows to the textures. They also included the ability where you can downscale this and still have it play normally on a potato rig. The voice actors and the cutscenes have been updated for the full 60fps and god do I love it. My only problems are two things overall. I played the crap out of the original and the Vita but even today I can't get over Chie's new voice actor. It doesn't fit her character and really doesn't make moments in the original like her awakening that powerful in Golden. The port also has a couple issues right now. For the anime cutscenes it was have problems keeping up with the game. For example when you first loading the game it can feel a bit choppy with the visuals and the audio. However during cutscenes where a character is talking its smooth and doesn't skip. I trust Atlus to fix it very soon. The pros however is everything. With this being a port on PC we could have some very good mods on our hands as well. I would absolutly love someone to mod Golden with Chie's original voice. I would be fine with some moments of her being quiet if theres nothing avialable. This port is something I never thought would happen and they made the game feel like it was planned all along. The controls on keyboard feel really nice as well. If your reading this review and haven't picked up the game, please do so now. This JRPG is on level with the best and deserves every ounce of respect. One last thing, please get the soundtrack as well. Persona is known for having some of the best Game Soundtracks out there.

_childDocuments_.review: SMT fans already know whether they want this or not. For those who have never played a Persona or SMT game before, Persona 4 Golden is a classic turn-based JRPG with Pokemon-esque mechanics, a lot of style, attitude, and awesome music. If you have the patience for turn-based battles and long conversations with your in-game friends, I definitely recommend it.PROS-Mechanically deep system of collecting, fusing, and building Personas that rewards any effort you are willing to put into it-Tactical combat-Game's design and length leads to you forming emotional bonds with the characters by the end-Awesome music (as usual for Persona)CONS-The game gives you a lot of illusory choices where the same thing happens regardless of what you choose-Some scenes can feel overly drawn out as the characters repeat the same ideas while discussing story beats-PC port crashes rarely but it does happen

_childDocuments_.review: A great game in it's own right.I have never played Personas prior to P5 so this was my first venture into P4G.After putting in over 20 hours I don't know how close I am to the end yet but it has been a fun ride so far.Still, as someone who doesn't have the nostalgia for this game I must mention a few things I dislike in comparison to P5:- Dungeons are boring! They all consist of the same corridors and same rooms with treasure chests/shadows; only the layout of these corridors and floors differs between floors. In P5 every dungeon feels like an actual place with a unique and interesting vibe to it. This may be due to hardware limitations but I consider these RNG dungeons to be lackluster.- Lack of certain Quality-of-Life things such as the ability to see where available Social Link confidants are hanging.  - Combat is more or less the same but P4 lacks the Psi-, Nucler-, and Ranged- types from P5, making it a tad simpler.- The way you engage shadows is awkward.- Visual outlook is a little bit outdated, though that's not that big of deal in Persona as it might be in other RPGs.-/+ The difficulty can be easily tinkered with during an active game. I am not a fan of this system; you should dedicate yourself to the difficulty you choose in the beginning. -/+ The story, characters and OST are all subjective but I personally prefer metropolitan Tokyo over this rustic town.+ The card system you can trigger at the end of combat is in my opinion a more fun way of getting personas and other stuffs as opposed to the persuasion hassle from P5.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play many JRPGs. Well, not specifically Traditional Turn Based combat titles. I mean I have played some like Paper Mario TTYD and Earthbound prior, but usually, my experience with JRPGs is very limited. But that said, Persona 4 Golden is a great game. It's not my first Persona title as I did finish vanilla Persona 5 on my PS4 3 years ago and love that game too, but P4G is definitely worth it especially for it's price. For anybody who doesn't know, Persona is a JRPG spin off from the Shin Megami Tensai line created by Atlus where you play a group of teenagers that have Personas. The Personas themselves represent each of the characters overcoming their weaknesses. Like Yosuke's with fear of rejection and being an outcast. And the gameplay is represented in two forms. The social sim aspects, and the turn based combat. Both of these have a part because socializing with certain people will help you in certain Arcana classes. I'm not the most knowledgeable on the Arcana/Tarot Card systems of Persona, but I like that the socializing both gives you a reason to do it gameplay wise, but also a reason to do it for individual character storylines. They give you greater insight into what the characters are thinking and why they are doing and reacting to certain things in a certain way. And you can also fuse Personas into stronger ones with Egor and Margarette's help. The dungeons each are created by a character's subconscious. Fears,anxieties,flaws that they push away so that their peers don't see their flaws and issues,and when helped,are gifted Personas unique to them. You also fight a lot of shadow beings which help you level up yourself and your Personas for your party team and yourself. And also, from what I understand the dungeons represent a psychology theory between the id,ego,and super ego. The Id wants desires no matter at what cost,the ego keeps to keep the id in check,and the super ego is the moral compass of yourself keeping the regular ego in check. I'm not a psychology expert, but you can see this in a thematic sense for Persona titles. When a character sees the worst parts of themselves being amplified to an over the top degree, they reject it out of fear. And thus, you must beat a Boss Shadow representing that character in order to overcome the worst aspects of the person. It's a really cool aspect of the series. And it gives it something over other titles that don't usually tackle certain stuff that Persona doesn't. Even SMT from what I understand goes for entirely different story stuff than Persona which I think is fine. And Persona 4G is pretty great about the plot and characters. Great arcs all around if you ask me.I recommend also personally, trying to finish the dungeons as possible,use your free time for socializing,books to read for other stats like intelligence and courage,buying armor and weapons to help give your party an edge in the battle. But also going back to dungeons to defeat optional bosses for more helpful armor and weapons. It's also helpful for giving you an edge with level ups. Overall, great system of mechanics and gameplay loops to make you and your party stronger. I think if anything else, if you are gonna play Persona 4 Golden, the character writing,plot,mystery element to the story,and atmosphere are strengths I think Persona 4 has over the more refined and polished Persona 5. Not that Persona 5 is a lesser game,(of course not. I think it's gameplay loop is excellent) but Persona 4 does have that lively community of Inaba and characters that connect back into eachother. Like one big happy family. Persona 5 by contrast is a bigger game, (which is fine) but does sacrifice the livelier community for a bigger Shibuya.This is the thing that did sell me a lot on Persona 4 on it's own merits. Not that the gameplay was bad or underwhelming (far from it), but Persona 4 does generally tend to have certain strengths that Persona 5 doesn't. And that's fine because I think if anything else, that's what makes me recommend Persona 4 in general. Not to mention an adjustable difficulty option if you are having a hard time. It's for me, a 9/10. My only real issue with Persona 4 (and to be fair, I expect this with sequels) is that dungeon layouts don't generally tend to emphasize a lot of puzzle solving. I mean sure, they have great aesthetic changes which are great, but mechanically speaking,they don't do too much to change it up. Not that it never does, but it isn't a focus with P4's design. I say because I think Persona 5's dungeon design is superior in general between the two. (My only other game for reference is Persona 1 which is more dungeon crawling like older SMT titles and not really like the more modern Personas. (P3,P4,P5)Overall though, I absolutely recommend playing Persona 4 Golden. It's a really great and solid game experience. Again, i'm not a JRPG expert. But just giving my general opinion, I absolutely would say it is a must have in your Steam library if you do love Turn Based Combat games with Social Sim Aspects. It's a lot of fun, and Atlus in general I find is one of the most trustworthy developers for me behind SpikeChunsoft and Nintendo EAD. Oh, also. RGG Studios.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but this game is one of the best JRPGs I've played in a hot minute.Pros:+ Fantastic story that tastefully tackles difficult subjects with great characters that are very likeable (for the most part).+ The battle system is solid, having to balance the strengths and weaknesses of each party member.+ The writing is excellent. Characters have nice arcs and the game can be quite funny and charming at times.+ Lots of stuff to do, mostly separated in two parts: A dungeon crawler and a life sim.+ The game looks pretty good for the most part and the anime cutscenes look great.+ The music is fantastic, one of my favourites soundtracks of all time. Voice acting is 95% on the dot as well.+ THERE IS SO MUCH TO DO!!+ If you have a good grasp of the story or you just want to play, the fast forward feature is your best friend.+ Fusing Personas is surprisingly fun.+ The difficulty range is nice. You can cruise through or you can get whacked behind the head with a sledgehammer.Cons:- The dungeons do get monotonous after a while, some can get a little gimmicky as well.- The pacing can be a little all over place, but that does somewhat depend on the player.- Holy crap, the intro is long... 2 to 3 hours long.- The sidequests are my biggest gripe with the game... Essentially, they consist of backtracking and grinding for small rewards.- The game does not do an ideal job explaining all the possible avenues you can take (bit of a nitpick, it's fairly easy to figure stuff out).- I'll put this as a negative; the deluxe edition might not be worth the extra bucks. The artbook is very small and the soundtrack contains 9 tracks.General comments:* This game can be very "tropy" at times, and that can be off putting for those who are not familiar with anime and JRPGs, but it is fairly mild in the grand scheme of things.* In this game, time management is key. It's one of those games where I don't blame you if you look at a guide, and that's without taking into account the grind necessary at higher difficulties (unless you're an RPG wizard, which I am not).* There is a metric butt ton of activities to do out of dungeons and extra bosses (I know I said it 3 times now, but jeez there is a lot of content). You will need at least 2 playthroughs to get everything in the Persona compendium alone.This game is great! 9/10 If you like RPGs, I highly recommend it. I'm hoping more games in the franchise are brought to PC (looking at you P3).

_childDocuments_.review: P4G was my first foray into the Persona series, and honestly, what an incredible showing! I think it's super easy for JRPGs to fall into a traditional slump, where you're doing turn-based combat, journeying across a mythical land, creating a party of knights, wizards, rogues, and fighting the same archetypes of enemies that dozens of other games have provided you with. Persona 4 goes, "Boink everything you know about that; we're gonna do it, but we're gonna do it better, and we're gonna do it weird." The dungeons are all weird and are based on a different theme; they represent a corrupted version of someone's heart, so you face their deepest fears and insecurities as you traverse. They're also divided by checkpoints, only needing to be conquered by a specific in-game date, so you can come and go as you please, leaving the dungeoneering to another day if your party is spent. This, of course, is the coward's option, as everyone knows you should always complete the dungeon in its entirety on day one so as to leave the most time available to nurturing your Social Links.The Social Links were an awesome addition to the experience, as the game wasn't entirely focused around exploring/fighting/grinding, and it was a cool feature to explore the characters you spend the game with. It was set up in a way that you were never forced to advance any character's link if you didn't want to, so you could just max out the characters that you liked and spend your free time doing other activities. This was actually one of my favorite parts of the game though, so I tried to complete as many characters' links as possible. This also led to them getting new Personas, and you gained the ability to craft an ultimate Persona of their given tarot card, so there is incentive.The music in this game trumps every other game I've played by a good amount. None of the repeating music, such as the town or combat themes, get repetitive, and each dungeon has its own theme that also goes hard; really I would just struggle to find a bad song in the soundtrack. When it released on Spotify, I was listening to it pretty non-stop, as there is enough music in the line-up that it wouldn't get old. Even if it did, I could listen to "Affection, Affection" on cooldown.Honestly, unless you hate turn-based combat or anime-styled games, I think this is worth the pickup.Cinematic playthrough:

_childDocuments_.review: Was very excited to see this game pop up on Steam. P5 was my exposure to the series and was immediately taken aback with how vibrant the characters world was. P4 Golden is no exception to that rule, it combines elements from monster tamers, traditional JRPGs, dungeon crawling, and visual novels to seamlessly combine them all into this fantastic game. None of the major characters came across as one dimensional - they all had their personal struggles and dilemmas (that you can choose to explore further). The world feels real and lived in. The sound design and music are spectacular. The only drawbacks I can identify are the dungeon design and character models. The dungeons can be very boring as it is randomly generated using generic set pieces so it feels like you're just running down one hallway after another. The character models are a reflection of it's vita origins and unfortunately did not age well into the modern era.My personal breakdown of gameplay can be roughly split into 65% talking - 35% fighting. If you're not a big fan of dialogue and only want the dungeon crawling side of things, this might not be the right game for you.TLDR; 9/10 - Kanji is best bro

_childDocuments_.review: This may be one of the greatest RPGs I've played in my life. It sucks you in and it just doesn't want to let you go. It's also a proper mince even on normal difficulty, you can be 10 levels above things and still feel heavily threatened if you don't take them out very quickly and utilize some fairly heavy strategy. I'm told it's an 80ish hour game, I'll reserve a full, proper review for when I've completed it. For now, would I recommend someone buy this game? Without question or an awful lot of reservation, but be aware that at the time of this review the blur effect employed in this game is poorly implemented and may not play nice with some hardware (certainly doesn't with my GTX 1080). Unfortunately about the only thing for it if you encounter this until the devs see fit to fix it (and just in general to make the game run better regardless of hardware) is to go download Special K (a very useful code injection tool that allows you to deal with problems that were never patched in games such as NieR: Automata among others), install that, and then navigate the steam forums to find the wrapper that was made specifically for this game. If that doesn't work for you... I don't know what to tell you. Regardless provided you have relatively recent hardware it should otherwise be considered a pretty solid port, and I hope the devs that ported this from the Vita version outdate this matter in a rather timely fashion!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best JRPGs ever made, really, and the best entry in the Persona series to boot (in my opinion), Persona 4 Golden is required playing if you're even slightly interested in the genre. It manages to make turn-based combat addicting and satisfying thanks to stellar sound and visual design and a phenomenal soundtrack (if you like the music in The World Ends With You, you'll like this), and the day-to-day events are always kept fresh and interesting, even as the game spans an entire year. The 20 dollar price tag is unbeatable, too. All in all, if you choose to pass up Persona 4, that's your call, but you're missing out on one of the highest points of the sixth generation of console gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 is one of my favourite games, despite it's being both a Japanese RPG and a Visual Novel, or perhaps because of both those things.  I used to be a big fan of the JRPG genre until the good ship Final Fantasy ran aground, and I'll confess, I haven't really given any time to the Visual Novel Genre, as I do like some mechanics beyond a decision tree in my games and, well, they're mostly porn.Persona 4 manages to take elements of both genres however, and craft something truly special - a Golden Year of life through the eyes of a 14-year-old in early 2010's Japan that's also a friendship-building monster-training tower-climbing murder mystery.  It's a period piece, it's a love letter to vanishing Japanese villages in the face of modernization, it's a coming of age story for a generation with expanded horizons, it's a commentary on Mass Media and how much "truth" can truly be gleaned from it, it's a REALLY addictive catch 'em and fuse 'em Pokemonster game, it's a deep dive into Jungian Psychology and Shinto spirituality, it's a slice of life and a fantasy story, it's a work of art, and you should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write a godlessly long and detailed review about this game, but decided its better to just keep it simple.This is a PS2 game. With that come a bunch of limitations that start to annoy you in the course if this games intended playing time.The presentation values are quite good for a game like this. Nice art, voice overs, even some anime level cutscenes.The concept for the story and setting is pretty good. The characters by themselves are alright as well. The follow the "trope" school of character design, but are made well enough as to not seem cliche. For the most part ....But the implementation feels shallow and lazy. Most of the characters have one or two points about them that are explored in any reasonable matter. And you dont have the ability to learn more. No collectibles, no trivia. The main story also drags on with characters often stating the obvious or rehashing old talking points. How can I best describe this? You have a lot of points of so called interest (characters, events), but these points are often very meek.I stopped playing at November, so I cant say how it all ended or developed. It wasnt bad, but nothing is impressive.The gameplay here is a complete failure from my point of view. Almost everything is designed to waste time. Many things arent shown or explained. During the LifeSim part you dont really get to do anything. You activate prompts for events like studying, eating, movie watching. You either have conversations, do event prompts. There is a mini game with fishing, but I dont think its that great, an incredibly rudimentary bug catching mini game and answering trivia questions in regards to school subjects and cooking recipes. Downside is they have a heavy Japanese focus, so many of these you wont be able to answer properly.The action gameplay is very boring and flawed. Quality of life problems, lack of information, grinding, lack of strategic depth, repetitiveness, thematic inconsistency, pointlessness of planning, filler content. I apologize, but writing down exactly why I think the above mentioned is the case is too time consuming. Ill just boil it down to this. The enemies you fight and they way you fight them has been done in many games of the Persona and Shin Megami Tensei series. These are old and reused systems and assets that by now are horribly outdated and thematically inconsistent. What shocked me even more is when I found out these were still being used in Persona 5, which came out 7 years later.The game shamelessly wastes your time and expects you to sink more on extra playthroughs. Even the skip function in this game is not good. The game would have been slightly above mediocre due to the effort in the presentation department and the interesting concept, but it has been so egregiously dragged out that only no lifers will truly find it appealing. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, as many have already said. This is the first persona and shin megami tensei related game I have fully finished. I quite enjoyed my entire playthrough and by the end I was very satisfied. I was left with the bittersweet feeling of loss and sadness as I reached the end of the game, so I absolutely recommend this game, especially at its low price.That said, as a personal minor gripe, the combat curve as you progress through the game didn't feel great to me. The first few dungeons are okay, but you generally are quite low on key resources and it felt like always scraping by. The middle dungeons felt the worst to me, where combat really took on a weird lull and felt uninteresting, especially with quite long dungeons. At that point, you are okay on resources but I suspect a lack of interesting skill variety combined with lengthy dungeons just really made it drag on to me. It was during this period I dropped the game for a long time and I dreaded the combat, instead powering through it to reach the story sim parts again. However, after this lull, the combat in the game started picking up for me again as it felt like you had more options alongside all party members joining and some nice perks. At that point, the combat became somewhat fun and interesting again and I quite enjoyed the endgame fully.For the most part that is my only real gripe with this game. Though admittedly it did nearly cause me to drop the game for good. This is, of course, also only my opinion on how the general combat progression curve felt as I played through the game and may not be what many others felt.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there's any point to talk about P4G at this point beyond that it's a totally worthwhile addition to the base game and definitely the best version of the game and i would highly recommend anyone even slightly interested to buy this game to support Atlus bringing more games to pc.Now that that's out of the way i'm going to discuss the port because that's probably more informative than saying that persona is a classic that every rpg fan should experience. PERFORMANCE:The port is very bare bones , performance doesn't seem to be an issue and i've played this on my 1070/6700k desktop along with an acer notebook with nvidia mobile graphics from 4 years ago and got basically the same smooth gameplay. OPTIONS:The options menu is incredibly basic with almost no graphical tweaking but that's not really a problem considering this is a 12 year old ps2 game. _childDocuments_.review: If there's any series with a fanbase who hasn't actually played the games, none would be as iconic as Persona. The spin-off series that ended up dwarfing the original in terms of popularity is a classic for a dang good reason, but it's always been one people have watched instead of played. If you know someone who says they've played Persona, they're probably lying.Until now. Persona 4. ATLUS' beloved cash cow of a subseries in a spin-off series of another series. The game that spawned a fighting game sequel (that was also a sequel to P3), a portable enhanced remake, a sequel to the fighting game sequel, a crossover with P3, a rhythm game dancing sequel, and a crossover with P3 and P5 - all of which are entirely canonical. And now we have another to add to the list - a PC port of the portable enhanced remake, which means one thing: people can actually play the dang game. So the question is - does it still hold up?Yes. Yes, it absolutely does.The main reason it holds up is because it's still a dang good JRPG. Sure, P5 might have been an insanely fantastic JRPG, but P4 is still pretty dang good in comparison, in large part to having the same core: Pokemon, but more in-depth, and instead of fun creatures, it's ungodly figures borne from the collective unconscious. Having already played Persona 5, it did take a bit to unlearn the QOL changes, but if this is your first Persona game,you won’t notice a thing. The best compliment I can give P4 is that it's a JRPG where I actually gave a damn about using buff and debuff skills, which should be enough to let you know how much I was engaged in the gameplay.But where P4 absolutely shines compared to its successor is the story. Don’t get me wrong, P5’s story and characters were absolutely stellar; but I have to admit, sometimes it felt rushed, underdeveloped and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥ you Mona, you stupid piece of ♥♥♥♥. On the contrary, I cherished almost every moment in P4G. I loved every character that I met. Even those who I’d gotten a bad first impression of would slowly work their way into my heart. The Phantom Thieves felt like they were merely friends by obligation and circumstance, but the Investigation Team felt like they actually were friends who had reason to care for each other. I mean, ♥♥♥♥, I nearly cried at the end of P4 which is something I can’t say for P5.And the soundtrack, it's just - AH! So many good vibes on that soundtrack, it’s so bright and cheery and small rural town vibes but also with elements of hip hop and it works so well and als- look, it's a really good soundtrack.Persona 4 Golden might not be nearly as polished, as well designed, and certainly not as stylish as Persona 5, but it makes up for its PS2 era shortcomings with more than enough substance in its story and characters to reach out and surprise P5, as it knocks it off its podium so it can reclaim its spot as the king.

_childDocuments_.review: Prior to picking this up, I had never played a Persona game. I didn't really know what they were about other than it had something to do with being in high school and fighting monsters. I knew from reputation that Persona 5 was a great game and as such I wanted to try it out, but that would have required buying a Play Station which wasn't really an option. Then, this was released on Steam and suddenly I started to see it being recommended practically everywhere I went. I was curious to see if it was as good as everyone was saying and decided to give it a go.Well, what can I say except that it lives up to and exceeds all of my expectations. I was hooked immediately, right from the cinematic that plays when you start up the game. I was sucked into the story and couldn't wait to see what would happen the next time I played. The game is an interesting mix of a murder-mystery visual novel/high school live simulator, and a turn based JRPG dungeon crawling adventure. The majority of the game takes place in an idyllic rural community where a run of bizarre murders are occurring. During the the visual novel and life sim portions of the game you go to school, work at various jobs, and spend time with you friends. While this might seem boring and tedious, it is actually pretty entertaining and it was fun to decide which activities to do each day in order to gain the most amount of benefits.The other half of the game is spent traveling through various procedurally generated dungeons, fighting monsters in a turn based combat system. Each of the monsters you encounter have elemental attacks and weakness, and you fight them with your own creatures (or Personas) that have their own elemental strengths and weaknesses. As you play through the game you unlock and craft new Personas to use in battle in a system that reminds me a bit like filling up a Pokedex. (Completing an encyclopedia of monsters? Battling creatures with elemental weaknesses? Yeah, it's a lot like Pokemon.)Both of these game play styles complement one another and help elevate the game above being just a visual novel or just a JRPG. When one game style seems to be overstaying its welcome in that particular instance, it's not too long before the game switches back to the other style and reinvigorates itself. Where the game truly shines however, is in its characters. Each one of the main cast members starts off seemingly being a one-note stereotypical example of a particular character archetype, but as the game progresses and you get to know all of them, they open up to you and you get to experience their arcs as they grow and change over the course of the story. Each one of them is incredibly well written, and it's disappointing that, at least in my play-through, there wasn't enough time to get to know them all. If I had any complaints, they would mainly revolve around the game's handling of sensitive topics. For example, one character who is implied to be a closet homosexual is occasionally the subject jokes or occasionally, subject to outright hostility from other characters that comes across as mean and homophobic. I know the base game originally came out in the late 2000's so this is most likely an example of it being a product of its time, but it is still kind of difficult to sit through playing it today. Luckily these instances are pretty rare and towards the end of the game they go away entirely. These moments could have worked if they were depicted as character flaws that are grown out of as a result of characters maturing as the game progresses but they aren't, which makes you wonder what their point was in the first place. Also, in an attempt at humor, at times the game is weirdly sexual and it comes off a little cringey but maybe that's due to differences in culture as this game is about as Japanese as you can possibly get.In the end, I can't recommend this game enough. It was certainly worth the money and all of the time I put in to it, and I can imagine myself playing it again and again, trying to unlock all of the things I missed before. If you're reading this and you do decided to get it, without spoiling yourself, try and make it to the true ending of the game. Not only will that give you additional playtime, but it will also give you the most satisfying conclusion. Here's hoping Sega and Atlas port Persona 5 Royal to Steam!

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game. If you didn't have a life in high school like me this is the perfect cope. Jokes aside the game has a clear message, value your time. Time is the currency of life, if you squander it you will fail at life, you wont make the connections you could, you wont find the truth.  The concept is executed as a Dating simulator crossed with a JRPG. You play as the protagonist, a new boy in town with determination and the personality of potato. That is the truth. He is a canvas for the player to express their choices on how to manage time, what characters to meet, and if they want to snu snu with the hot nurse at the hospital.  This choices shape up the character like no dialogue could ever do. Are you a exemplar student? a sports man? Maybe you are looking to have a part time job to buy crap from a Tv infomercial, or to be close to your family and friends. On the first run of a player, a blind run, it would be almost impossible  to optimize your choices to be everything that the game has to offer. Mostly thanks to the Stat system which locks certain avenues from ever happening in the game. In this first experience is where the game shines and reveals a shard of truth to the player, your choices are how your present yourself to the world. And beyond that there is the shadow, the true self built on by desires and the wounds of life. The RPG mechanics are lit, your companions play by one or a couple of the core mechanics of the turn based combat, while the protagonist can rotate his spells and  abilities  by changing personas or basicaly demons from Shin megami Tensei. There is much to say but there is little time.Yukino is best girl, give this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: if you're weeb enough this is outright one of the most absorbingly-written and masterfully-paced RPGs available on steam. P4 presents a wide variety of deep characters and themes that invite the player to reflect on their own worldview. it is honestly some existential ♥♥♥♥ in a very good way.overall, i think its strongest point is the fact that, barring a few timeskips, Persona 4 has you live every single day of the protagonist's life from when they arrive at Inaba until the day they leave. that's a lot of days where "nothing" story-related will happen. instead of focusing on the main story constantly, Persona builds the encounters you have with various events and characters on the choices you make in spending your time. although i can definitely see where it would be boring to some people, having a large portion of the game be essentially normal life with character-building subplots for the main cast really immerses you in a way that I think few RPGs today accomplish. if you're someone who enjoys a story that's often light-hearted and very slow-burn, this game has a plot that shouldn't be missed.this isn't an action game, though. the actual combat parts in the game very few in number relative to how much time you'll need to put into it for a single clear. they're spaced far out between segments of just trying to live a normal life while you work to solve a spree of serial murders. during that time, you slowly and steadily work to improve yourself and improve your relations with various NPCs to unlock better abilities and stronger combat options. if you're after something that's constantly about action, this game is not ideal.i have a few nitpicks about the game, but they tend to relate to things that either are too deeply ingrained into the game at this point to ever be fixed, or are likely going to go unfixed as this is a port of a somewhat older game. 1. the english voice acting ranges from passable to pretty awful. this is my subjective opinion, but i really recommend this game be played with the Japanese voice acting and anime subtitles for cutscenes enabled. the last part is important specifically, because turning on japanese VA does not enable subs for the anime cutscenes. if you're weeb trash like me and don't actually speak japanese, you can miss content this way.2. keyboard controls are weird and buggy in spots. the game recommends you play with gamepad and i definitely agree, but prepare for a little bit of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you don't have the option.3. weirdly crashy sometimes. i'm honestly not sure what caused it because i could never really repeat any of the crashes, but for some reason (specifically when reading in the evening, it seemed like) the game will crash during loading screens. given that save spots are fixed points, you should be mindful to save as often as you reasonably can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to do so.overall an exemplary story-driven rpg that excels as both an immersive experience and at selling an effective story with emotive, well-written characters. barring the relatively minor bugs, this is a masterfully-executed _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I've never played any of the previous Persona games, and only bought this one simply because 1) It's on PC and 2) People are head over heels in love with these games. So seeing yet another positive review probably doesn't surprise anyone but most of them are just "yay game good get it" and don't tell you ANYTHING about the damn game. Let's get my gripes out of the way first, since they're not game killers.1) A game that's ported to PC that doesn't have PC reflected controls is a terrible time. Tutorials for game controls are given in a form like: "Fast travel around town with the sub menu button!" BUT DON'T TELL YOU WHAT THAT IS! Even the name entry in the beginning is an exercise in frustration. Luckily you can just click through most stuff in the game, and often on screen prompts help you out, but seriously, just tell me that the sub menu button for fast travel is F. It's not tough to detect my input device is a keyboard, since that's the one absolute default every PC gamer would have access to. If I plugged in a controller it'd make sense since you have options for those!2) This game is a jrpg. One that can get a little rough. But why is it that when you die it's immediate game over? I HATE THIS. I have revival items and 3 other party members, if I can revive them why can't they revive me? It just means I have to hoard any and all armor for myself first since I matter the most and instantly fail if I happen to die but I would much rather spread valuable items around the group for balance.3) The trial and error for some bosses is a bit cruel. It's one thing to hint at me 1 turn early to make sure to Guard against a powerful aoe attack that could mean instant death but to do it with no indication at all just wastes my actual, real life time. And when you die you have to watch the death rp, reload onto whatever floor you're on as a checkpoint, (thank God for that though) and rewatch any and all pre-battle rp. Irritating.Now the pros: 1) The soundtrack is atmospheric, catchy, and hasn't gotten old after 10 hours so far. More jrpgs should be like this in the music department.2) You're a high school transfer student in a small town and something terrible starts to happen once you get there and you and your friends have to take care of it. Almost by the books anime story line. I'd tell you more, but honestly the story is so quirky and interesting otherwise that you should just experience it yourself. I'm enjoying it immensely and am actually paying attention to what's going on. And there's all sorts of neat side stuff going on as well.3) Not every minute of this game is about the turn based battles. You'll go multiple in game days doing other things instead of battling and I actually quite like it. Maybe there's a test and you should study. Maybe you joined a club and have practice. Maybe you have a job. Maybe you just want to socialize. Doing all this provides benefits to stats so even if you did somehow end up disliking it it's not totally pointless. It's a major aspect of the game though, if all you want is turn based battles stop reading this review now because you aren't going to like this game.4) You have 1 in game year to beat the game. It sounds annoying on paper, but the time is very generous and helps keep the pace going; unlike other jrpgs that drastically extend playtime by hoping you get lost and make you trek around a huge map aimlessly in search of where to go next. Then you look it up online and it's some cave on another continent that is a solid 20 minute hike back to. This game will make sure you know where to go, what to do, and nudges you towards your goal.5) It's 20 bucks at full price. What do you have to lose? Just take the risk, you'll definitely know if you're going to like the game or not before the refund time is up.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the games 'True Ending' on my first run (using the internet to avoid any bad endings). This is an incredible JRPG and has both excellent turn based combat, and incredible slice of life sim gameplay (my personal favourite parts). The cast of characters that build up throughout the game are so well created that all of them have a personal tale behind them that you can help them with, meaning at the end of the game you are surrounded by well rounded individuals. This is my introduction to the series, which has blown me away and has landed the follow ups (arena/ultimax/dancing) as well as persona 3 and 5 on my to buy list. The soundtrack to the game is also probably up there in my favourite game soundtracks. The opening theme is a banger to start, the general theme for explorations (Heartbeat, Heartbreak) is catchy and upbeat enough that even after 60+ hours of game you aren't sick of it. The battle theme is blood-pumping and gets you excited to fight even after you hear it's opening for the thousandth time. 'Corridor' is what I have on while writing this review, and is honestly a beautiful piece of piano that I'll probably relax to for years to come. It is not without issues, as it shows its age at times, both in textures and in the way it handles some characters. It also has some minor port issues, most obvious being the fully animated cutscenes being stuttery and oftentimes I would rewatch them on YouTube to get the proper experience. There are occasional frame drops, but in a game paced like this it really doesn't affect much at all.I cannot attest for the Keyboard controls as I used a PS4 controller for my playthrough (which is fully supported, down to the button prompts). It took me about 65 hours to beat, meaning I got plenty of game for my money, and that doesn't include my future NG+ plans. I have come out of it feeling like I have made a new group of friends that I can (and will) revisit in future playthroughs.In conclusion, it's £16, and for that price I cannot recommend this enough. This is looking hopeful to be my game of the year, and will no doubt be a defining memory of my experience in quarantine and possibly my young adulthood as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: IMO this one is easily the worst Persona game and it's not close. I do not understand the love the main cast gets, the designs are all very flat and their personalities are bog standard. Most of the characters are either actively annoying or underdeveloped. The only strong points are that Adachi is pretty funny and Dojima and Nanako are cool but that's honestly it. In the wake of P3 getting a remake this game also feels very clunky in 2024. The camera and dungeon controls are jank which makes the dungeon crawling just feel much worse than any other game, plus it is just as repetitive as P3, if not more because it is way harder to avoid fights.The game is also severely outdated with its humor. Many of the "comedy" scenes feel like they were written by Steven Crowder or Ben Shaprio. The worst one in particular is during the beauty pageant in which the game acts very weird about high school girls, and wherein the punchline is that a fat woman or an older woman daring to have the audacity to even think that they could be viewed as attractive is so hilarious and offensive that they need to be humiliated immediately. To be honest this is a running theme because it is literally the most conservative video game I have ever played. The game has opportunities to develop queer or otherwise socially deviant characters but the second the potential for it pops up it has to instantly shout it down. "Kanji's not really secretly gay, it's just that other people perceiving him as gay made his shadow like that." "Rise is actually not capable of being sexual in a way that might offend conservative Japanese sensibilities, she's exclusively and monogamously horny towards the self-insert MC for some reason." "Naoto is not potentially trans or GNC in any way, it's her responsibility to accept that she's actually a woman and make an effort present like one regardless of any potential discomfort from her." It's not that I even find any of these storylines particularly offensive, it's perfectly fine with me if, say, Naoto decides of her own accord that she actually wants to be more of a woman, but it just seems to clash with the supposed themes of the game. P4G pretends that it's about gaining the strength to confront dark truths about your inner self, but in reality none of the characters ever have to contend with anything that might truly upset their sense of self.But really, for me it just comes down to the designs and personalities of the characters. I think the designs all look ugly, and the characters are annoying. The eventual remake of this game may change my mind but for now I give thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I only kinda recommend this game.Personal 4 Golden walked so Persona 5 Royal could run.More accurately:PERSONA 4 GOLDEN DRAGGED ITSELF WEAK AND DYING ALONG A BED OF JAGGED, SCALDING HOT COALS, SO THAT PERSONA 5 ROYAL COULD ZOOM AROUND THE GLOBE IN A SUPERSONIC JET FIGHTER AT MACH 3 SPEEDS.Such is the chasm in quality I experienced between these two games.P4G does very few things better than P5R, and what it does do better, it doesn't do much better. If you find yourself 10 hours into the P4G and wondering, "Does it ever pick up the pace?" The answer is no, it does not--at least, not in the way you're hoping. It has its own pace, which is fine for a game from 2008, but if you play this game after playing P5R, do not expect it to be the mind-blowing experience that P5R is. It's not even close. I understand that this game is part life simulator and as such you can only expect it to go by so fast, but I found that the things you actually do to pass the time in P4G can also be quite, well, uninteresting.I put 100 hours into this game and beat it. And while I understand why some people like it, the randomly generated dungeon levels will turn it into a tedious slog for many. That's certainly how it was for me. This is just how JRPGs were, way back when. It was more acceptable in 2008. But by today's standards, my god is it hard to stomach sometimes.Some people LOVE the music to this game. I thought some of it was alright, but felt P5R's soundtrack was vastly superior. I tolerated most of the music much of the time. But if by any chance you find yourself NOT liking the music, well, prepare to have the same themes drilled into your head for literally dozens of hours. Some of the themes I liked initially, but they ended up being played so often that they got really old and tiresome.Bottom line: don't expect this to be P5R but with worse graphics; it's not. P5R is a quantum leap beyond P4G in almost every conceivable way. I totally understand why some people like or even love P4G. But I'm convinced some people are also just looking back at it with rose colored glasses.That being said, Nanako Dojima is an incredibly well-realized depiction of a little girl who is struggling to deal with trauma that stems from the loss of her mother (this is not a spoiler). I am genuinely amazed by what they did with this character in this game. It's nothing crazy, but she is incredibly deep. It's really impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly phenomenal experience from start to finish and one of the greatest games I have ever played. P4G has it all; great characters, an enthralling story, satisfying gameplay and a legendary soundtrack to boot. But a lot of games boast such impressive characteristics. What sets this game apart from its brethren? For one, the seamless and consistent transition between life simulation and otherworldly dungeon crawler almost feels like you are playing two separate games. Separate, yet connected - by the intriguing plot and the lovable cast that drives it, packed full of twists and turns like any good murder-mystery. You will get attached to the characters in this game, so much so that the ending had me tearing up, not to mention the numerous genuine laugh inducing moments generated by natural character banter. Typically, such a wonderful story is sadly offset by mediocre gameplay perhaps demonstrating to naysayers that video games are simply not the medium for storytelling. Fear not however, the mechanics, the premise and the execution at the heart of Persona 4's battle system are top notch. This game perfected the SMT formula and it subsequently dwarfs series like Pokemon both in terms of complexity and entertainment value. Outside of combat, the game is rather dialogue heavy and largely consists of player choice and interaction which effortlessly feeds back into the traditional party based RPG elements of the game, providing enhancements and upgrades as you master 'Social Links'. This is how P4G marries two game concepts together so perfectly, engaging with the characters is not only rewarding in itself but it enhances your gameplay experience. In turn clearing dungeons and slaying bosses is all the more rewarding as the deeply interconnected story unfolds. I honestly cannot think of any other RPG that is able to so masterfully balance story and gameplay - usually one of the two stands out. Yet ATLUS was able to conceive a genuine masterpiece in this game, one which will likely always hold a special place in my heart. My only gripe is that this game should have come to PC sooner, because everyone should experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic addition to the Persona series! This is a great PC port of an already stellar game. I played on a laptop and had minimal issues with it. Sometimes the framerate dropped, but it's nothing that an adjustment of the graphics can't solve. The game is visually better than the original. Plus, you can switch between controller and keyboard/mouse with ease. It took me about 61 hours to beat. Absolutely worth it for the price!If this is your first Persona game, prepare for time management: the simulator. The gameplay is easy to understand and relatively straightforward. You conquer various dungeons, beat the boss, and progress with the story. Typical turn-based RPG. Most of the social links are easily obtainable, but make sure you are leveling up your stats when you can, as that is required for some. However, social links are easy to max out except for potentially two characters, who have abnormal requirements. Golden adds new features as well as a bonus dungeon at the end for a new loveable character. However, unlike 3 and 5, deadlines can be unclear at times. You have until "the day after several days of rain" to beat a dungeon. Most of the time that's easy to figure out. To make things easier, try to beat the dungeon as early as you can to leave plenty of room for free time. The story is great, but the ending is pretty underwhelming in my opinion. The last section of the story feels underdeveloped and could have been stretched in another dungeon or two. Many parts of the main story are predictable, but they do pull some interesting stunts. Persona 4 is a murder mystery, something that makes it stand out. It is an enjoyable ride for sure.Overall, 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The maximum word count for reviews does no justice for my thoughts, but here they are:If you haven't played this game, or any Persona game, or are even remotely interested, you absolutely, 100%,  to play this game. It is a beautiful, indescribable-with-words masterpiece that I proudly proclaim as my favorite game of all time, period. Turn-based JRPG dungeon-crawling combined w/ daily life-simulation The game is broken up into calendar days over the course of 1 year. Most days are broken up into different timed sections: . During each of those sections, you can choose to partake in different activities that are available on that day of the week. For the life-sim side, aside from attending school, the gameplay opens up in your choice of what you after school/ when school is closed:Who do you want to hang out with? (Hanging out with others further develops your bonds (Social Links) with them as you learn about their backstories/struggles)Which personal stat do you want to grow? (Personal stats (e.g. Knowledge, courage, etc.) are attributes that help you perform other tasks easier, whether it is unlocking new dialogue choices, increasing your performance in the upcoming exam, or allowing you to get past a threshold needed to get further into a social link)So, what are ? Personas are manifestations of a person's heart; different personalities that one "puts on" in order to face the harsh environment that is life. Personas are you and your party members' tools used for the dungeon-crawling part of the game.You use Personas to defeat Shadows; Shadows are, as you will hear throughout the game, a person's . There's much more to be said about Shadows but I think it's best if you play the game and find out.Social Links: The more you interact with different characters and build your Social Links, the more experience Personas will receive upon creation and the stronger the Personas you will be able to fuse upon maxing out respective Social Links. Dungeons play a key role in gameplay in that as part of the story, you need to enter these unique labyrinths in order to , or else the  and force you back a number of weeks to try again. Once the goal has been met, you can return to these dungeons as your choice of activity for a day and grind for experience/money/quest items/material drops etc.Overall you can expect a lot, and I mean A LOT, of content out of P4G.The original Persona 4 was released on PlayStation 2, and Persona 4 Golden is a remake/remaster of P4 with new content. So yes, this game does look like a late PS2 game. That doesn't mean it looks bad, as actually it looks really good and most things just lack "big" animation. Character/Persona models look great and although they appear kind of stiff in the animation department, they are still able to convey their emotions well like joy, sadness, laughter, anger, etc. The real world settings and dungeons are bright and colorful, and the game's menus and UI are similarly as bright and yellow (P4's main color theme). *: If you have never played the game and do decide to play it, this is a friendly reminder to NOT visit any comment section, forum, or wiki page about the game. The core story element of the game is that it is a  why a series of events is occurring. Since this is an 8 (or 12) year old game, some people out there will obviously spoil the mystery. Consider yourself warned.*You are a city boy who has been transferred to live a year in the countryside town of Inaba. As soon as you start school, a body appears in town and the police begin investigating why something like this has happened in such a peaceful town. Along the way, you somehow discover that you have been given some kind of supernatural power. By using that power, you discover a world never-before-seen where there are hints to the deceased individual's final moments. You soon find out that the individual was not the only victim, as more and more bodies begin to appear in town, all laid out and displayed in bizarre fashions. It turns out that your power, the power of Persona, is a key to the solving of this murder mystery, and that as you pursue the case, you have the potential to save people from becoming the next victims. Will you reach out to the truth and figure out the cause of all this?•Persona 4 Golden has the strongest cast of characters out of any Persona game, let alone any game that I know of. Each member that will eventually become part of your main party, or otherwise referred to as the "", has such a unique and fun personality, has such realistic background stories/struggles in life, and has such a believable relationship with each other. The side characters are equally as well, if not better, written.•Phenomenal soundtrack. The music is so catchy, so ear-wormy, so amazing that if you do not end up humming the tracks in your sleep unconsciously, you are lying to yourself.•There is always something to do and thus, it is hard to get bored. The time management portion of the game is great in that most of the time, you are doing something different every day of the week. •Many different Personas to collect and use at your disposal•If you've played Persona 5 first and not P4G yet, you will be disappointed by dungeons. The dungeons in P4G are randomly generated as opposed to fixed and detailed like in P5. Thus, the dungeon-crawling experience isn't as strategic and objective-based. Even for those who haven't experienced the P5 dungeons yet, you might feel that the dungeons are just boring hallways with occasional rooms with treasure. Overall, the dungeon-crawling experience in P4G isn't the most exhilarating part of the game.:*Disclaimer: I will not talk about Denuvo, , but because it did not affect my enjoyment of the game. If you choose to avoid the game based on the introduction of Denuvo, that is entirely your choice and I will not dispute your decision.•The upscaling resolution and unlocked framerate felt absolutely great. 99% of the game I did not experience a single frame drop, although I have to address the small 1% that is rather noticeable. . All throughout my playthrough I was never able to get rid of said delay, but it did not ruin my enjoyment of the game.•: Play with either English or Japanese voices (wasn't present in Vita version); a welcome additionYes, I'm biased and this is my favorite game of all time. Yes, I think more people should definitely play and experience the beauty that is this game. And yes, I hope ATLUS continues to port future Persona games, and even mainline Shin Megami Tensei games, onto the PC platform. Thank you ATLUS for allowing me to play my favorite title again on my PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 is a JRPG. However, the main crux of the gameplay is not in your traditional turn-based battles, although those are here, but rather spending time enhancing your stats outside of battle. Around 80% of the game will be leveling up your social links or Skills, which you need to level up for some of your social links. Leveling up these links is very enjoyable since most of the characters are very fun to be around and you want to see how their particular problem gets solved. Granted, not every social link is a winner, but a majority of them are very good. On the dungeon crawling side of things, there is an experience system which directly levels you up. Leveling up allows you to learn new moves for your personas and fuse even stronger personas. I played on easy, so I never had to spend too much time grinding levels in the TV world, but it seems that one would have to do that on higher difficulties.Pros:-Amazing story, it's been a long time since a story actually made me feel something-Amazing characters, the main cast are almost all excellent imo, and the supporting side characters are amazing as well, especially Dojima and Nanako-Awesome soundtrack, these tunes will get stuck in your head eventually-Satisfying combat, to me at least, again I played on easy difficulty, so I didn't have to grind-High Replayability, New game + lets you start over with all your skills, money, and persona compendium meaning you can start stronger, and access social links faster than the first run opening up some scenarios you most likely didn't see the first time (I can guarantee at least one, since there is something locked behind new game +) You can even skip through dialogue.Cons:- The story does take some time to get fully going, but I was too engrossed with the character shenanigans to really care, but I feel it still worth a mention- Not all characters are winners, in fact some are downright annoying. I'm looking at you Teddie. You could get replaced with a glasses rack and have the same impact on the story for me.- There will be entire days, or even weeks, where you simply press the A button a couple times while pretty much nothing of importance happens and this will happen throughout the game. I myself am a "gameplay first" kind of guy, so this was a bit annoying, but It's worth going through in my opinion.Overall, a 9/10 from me. It was my first Persona and I loved it. A few nagging issues, but I was more than willing to overlook them for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona as a whole can best be explained being the best interactive anime experience on the market.  This is a game series that is not for everyone but, can be the best thing you've ever played if your a fan of anime and the style the game has to offer. If you have played P5, you can expect much of the same and you'll love it. The reason the game is not for everyone is that a majority of the game is dialog driven. The game can be split in three parts; Visual Novel/Life sim/Turn-based RPG monster collector. Story and characters is the focus here! A majority (and I mean a HUGE majority) of your time spent in the game will be planning your day, spending time with friends, studying and going to school and making choices to help build bonds with the characters. This is the games way of progressing your character to get more powerful in the "Mystery Channel" and the real world to gain access to story goals. What's amazing is how well written and voice acted the game is, all the characters are extremely interesting and likable (even if not at first) as the game touches on their lives often dealing with fairly heavy subject matter and situations. Pair that with the amazing soundtrack the game has throughout that you'll be listening to even when your not playing and the amazing art style and presentation you have a real winner just based on that.Outside of the daily life, there is the randomly generated dungeons that the turn-based combat of the game kicks in. The "TV world" which is an extremely deep rabbit hole to jump into. The "midnight channel" shows people on powered off TV's during raining nights of people who are murdered in the real world all happening in the small town you go to school in. You go into this world with your friends to figure out whats going on and try to save those sent to die by someone/something(?). The combat is very simple and easy to get a hold of fairly quickly, most of this is like Pokemon or Final Fantasy. You will collect a huge amount Persona's you can merge together, power up and teach new skills to help you in battle. Every enemy you fight has a weakness that you need to discover and once you do, capitalize on it to give an opening for an all out attack. To help you do this, you have dozens status effects/buffs and debuffs to help you get through battles. Balancing when to attack and when to guard and knowing yours and your enemies weakness is the key to winning fights. If any of this at all sounds interesting to you, you are missing out on not playing Persona 4, it's one of the best.Some of the problems that do creep up is that the game does tend to get a little monotonous at times mainly where the combat and grinding is concerned. Where the story and the characters always found a way to keep me engaged, the combat often would get really boring to the point where it starts feeling like a chore. The game tends to have a little bit of an issue spacing out its features in a way where there isn't a balance between it all. The dialog and story arcs will sometimes go on for an extremely long time making you just want to fight and do something else to change it up, but once the game allows you to fight, it goes on for way too long that the interest starts to deteriorate. Rarely are you in a situation where you're in a chapter where both are given in good doses, making everything sometimes overstay its welcome. Along with that, they game is long, so expect to hear characters repeating and going over the same talking points to refresh you on whats happening and trying their best to "over explain" situations making them have sort of a circular rambling conversations from time to time along with and extremely long (but interesting) introduction. _childDocuments_.review: This game should be a litmus test for someones media literacy skills. I have been told by a good number of people on how "progressive" Persona 4 is, and frankly that's a load of bs. Persona 4 thematically hates anything that challenges the status quo of specifically being hetero-normative or anything that doesn't sticks to rigid gender norms. Any character who has real criticisms of the world around them is presented as extremely immature or a complete jackass who needs a lesson. Quite literally the overarching theme is wondering if the conditions that they're predetermined to go through are unfair and if they should challenge or change the world around them. And what Persona 4 gives us as an answer is a resounding "Nope, you just need to grow up". Which i find so hysterical as this game really wants to tell everyone that it's really saying something and everyone else is just a mindless drone sticking to the TV world, while at the same time literally having characters that transgress that status quo that are just either the butt of every joke. Or literally have a character double back on himself and his real feelings just to be like "oh it was just a phase" Characters are mostly all cookie cutter anime tropes with no other unique qualities and the ones that do (Kanji, Nanako, Naoto) are either written out for the most part or are chastised throughout the run time. The gameplay is also a massive simplification and step down from Persona 3 and makes this one of the most boring and easy persona games out there besides 2 Innocent Sin. In short this is the second worst megaten game but with the lowest bar being Catherine/Full Body, that's not the best position to be in.
