_childDocuments_.review: tldr; cool enough game, derivative of/iterating on frostpunk in a generally positive way but unfortunately bug ridden and plagued with quality of life issues. game breaking bugs will make you replay scenarios constantly until you give upThe good:- looks amazing and well written story- interesting gameplay mechanics that drive the story- good sound designIf you got everything you could get out of Frostpunk and wanted more, you'd probably enjoy this gameThat being said, the game is plagued with a lot of issues and where it has a lot of visual polish, there's a lot of lacking backend polish:- game breaking/save breaking bugs. certain actions brick your game, enjoy replaying it for hours to reach the same place, and a lot of these bug triggers are normal game actions you may perform but completely destroy your save with no fix. You don't know if your sace is bricked, but once you perform a save-breaking action every subsequent save and autosave is unloadable- simulation ai is really poor - a lot of the things in frostpunk that "just work" don't here, you will be bashing your head in trying to figure out why the ai isn't performing an assigned action- sometimes, it is actually your fault (you deconstruct a building and didn't notice it's not on a road anymore) but the game has very little UX to point this out to you, so you need to hunt for the issue- decision making process doesn't actually change very much - a lot of story decisions seem important but I suspect weren't finished/polished out so are pretty arbitrary

_childDocuments_.review: Top tier game to make me feel like I'm playing an epic space opera shepherding humanity. I love the music, the aesthetic, the story, and the gameplay. It left me with a game hangover that I tried filling with 4x games but I realized this is much more focused on story, city management, and resource management, rather than grand strategy. I think if you like games like Factorio or DSP and are interested in City Builders but felt they were aimless, you'll enjoy this game like I did.Most of the things that other players complained about like hull damage and stability penalties I think added a welcome pressure to the game to keep the player from relaxing too much. They were annoying at first but looking back I can see their usefulness. My biggest complaint would be (1) the lack of ability to navigate your ships around obstacles rather than through them, and (2) the ambiguity of whether a choice for a science team is exclusionary or not.

_childDocuments_.review: The game start out fun. You have one sector that you have to manage and the tutorial is very comprehensive. The issue starts when you open up more sectors, then the game turns into extreme micro management mode and sucks all the fun out of the game. The fact that the game makes you transfer everything, population and resources from one sector to another in just stupid. Your on the same ship, i shouldn't have to say sector 1 need food when it has none and sector 2 has a ton, it should just get the food from the stock-houses. The game would be better if you could set up one sector to be one thing, I.E. housing for population and then they travel to work even if that is another sector, that's how it would be in "real life". You would have to set up each sector to have it own micro economy. It just gets annoying after playing awhile because your always fighting your needs.The next thing is your hull! It has to constantly be feed resources because after your first jump it is always dropping. You lose max hull points every jump which I'm ok with but the fact that you can never repair your hull to a point where it doesn't need metal just adds to the whole fighting with the distribution of resources thing mentioned earlier.My last complaint would be the request your people make to you, some of them are thing that you literally would never be able to control if you want to progress. Example: Your people ask that you guarantee none of your science crew members die while exploring or else they lose trust in you but you have to have them explore and gather info and random events happen that you in no way can control. So you lose a crew member and lose your peoples trust or you don't agree to the request and lose your peoples trust.This game needs fixing and re-balancing for sure and if/once that happens I will give it a thumbs up because the story is interesting and the concept is really pretty cool too, its just more frustrating than fun right now honestly. I am still playing just because I am intrigued about whats going to happen and want to finish it but again right now its more of a chore than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: At launch the game had serious difficulty issues, and unrewarding game mechanics, and my review would've been negative. Things like receiving a punishment for staying in the system too long. And then receiving a punishment for leaving the system right after. But now you can modify about 20 different difficulty settings even during game to tailor it to yourself. The original absurdly difficult experience is still there by default for those that want it.The art, soundtrack and game play are very good, the story is engaging. The only critique that I have now that the difficulty has been sorted is you are almost always discouraged from taking any other path but what the developers set for you. Every choice but the right one is punished, and the only way to know the right one is to pick the wrong one and fail, reloading an entire chapter. It's almost as strict as following an exact build order, every other choice is death.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line: Only buy IXION if you like HARD games. I suspect this game will remain very polarized in its reviews. Most (if not all) of the negative reviews are saying the game is not "balanced". Yeah, it's not "balanced", and it's not meant to be you whiny snowflake. It's meant to feel like the entire universe is trying to kill you. It's meant to punish every single error you make with potentially fatal consequences. It's meant to be so difficult that it'll make your eyes bleed, and I LOVE IT.  For those of us that love challenging games, IXION is simply amazing. The feel is very "Battlestar Galactica", except the apocalypse wasn't caused by robots. You manage a gigantic space ark where the last remnants of humanity seem intent on killing themselves through workplace accidents, terrorism, and a slow descent into Earth-sick madness. It's spectacular(ly hard) and I gave a cheer when I finally managed to beat it. It took several restarts to do so, but I think that's part of the appeal: it's a return to the days when consoles had a reset button for a reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Comparison to Frostpunk:First, I love the hell of out Frostpunk, and have played a lot of games looking for another one like it. This comes closer than most, but it's not there.Second, this game, as of March 2023, feels incomplete, so it may get better.The bones are good. It feels like the people who made this played Frostpunk, and liked it, but it's just doesn't compare. Morality:The "moral" choices don't matter. Taking a bad choice will at worst result in the deaths of a few people or some lost science opportunities, but with thousands of people at your disposal, and no distinction between them other than workers or useless people, losing a handful just doesn't matter, and I ended the game with a spare 999 science, so that doesn't matter either.Any other moral choices, like whether or not to let the dog onboard have an obvious right answer and an obvious wrong answer, and you get a ridiculously huge reward for the obvious right answer (Think a permanent +20% Hope and -20% Discontent)Resources:Resource management is just too easy. Pretty quickly your biggest problem with resources is where to put them all. I had half of my ship devoted to storage, and that wasn't enough. There was just no difficulty to come by anything you needed.Difficulty:Honestly, it's hard to lose. There's only one campaign, though it is long, spanning 5 chapters, each of those chapters is effectively about 1/4 as long/dense as a Frostpunk scenario, and while Frostpunk has great replay-ability just due to how difficult it is (at least on extreme settings) This game doesn't have variable difficulty settings at all, there's one setting, and it's easy as hell. Worst case scenario, is that you didn't know that that one nonesensical requirement would be heaped upon you, with too little time to have any possibility of doing it, so you just reload an older save, and get ahead of it.         The equivalent of that would be something like "The Refugees" scenario, where you might learn, after the lords start showing up, that you need Infirmaries. But just because you know that in advance, doesn't mean that doing it will be realistic in any way, even if you reload, so you end up having to take a different path which has a meaningful difference to both the outcome and moral concerns.Anyway, I still hit recommend, because it's got potential. It's probably the closest I've seen to Frostpunk, at least in terms of opportunity, I'm just hoping that my instinct is right, and this isn't a truly finished product. A DLC, for instance, with new scenarios and increased/variable difficulty could put this up on par with Frostpunk, but until them I'll just go back to eagerly anticipating Frostpunk 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to first explain that I have absolutely no idea what other people are talking about in their reviews about this game being overly punishing or hard.This is one of the best city builder games I've ever played, and I've played quite a lot. If you're into games like Anno or Frostpunk you'll love this game and probably not find it nearly as punishing as some of these reviewers.Even if you're new to the genre, the difficulty options are good and there are easier ways to play, but I will also say that I recommended this game to someone who'd never even played a city builder before and is on track to finishing it first try like me, so I really don't understand the negative reviews around difficulty.This game is, at its core, not a calming or relaxing city builder where you'll have a satisfying end result that you'll admire. The buildings fit awkwardly, the crew are getting tired of being on the station, everything seems to be going wrong constantly. That's the point. Your crappy little space station was never designed to undertake the journey you're about to take. That's why it's hard. You're trying to save the entirety of humanity where the odds are stacked against you in almost every way. If that doesn't sound like fun to you, then don't bother wasting your time becoming another player with 9 hours leaving a negative review about how "hard" it is to demolish a building. Like seriously, I finished the game while barely even using 2 sectors, with over 5800 population. The game is actually too easy towards the end if you play it right.A lot of the things people complain about in other reviews are really easily fixable. I saw a guy complain that inter-sector transport is too slow. You can just build more stockpiles of the same resource, you get more carts. I had over 4000 people with only one sector producing food and it only took 3 small stockpiles to supply every sector in enough time.Others complain that the alloy cost of maintaining the station is too much or that the steel mills can't supply enough. I don't even know what to say to this one other than.. have you tried building more than one steel mill? I only had 3 throughout the game and I usually had 1 turned off and sometimes even 2 turned off once recycling became a thing.Then there's people complaining about stability loss for staying in a system or for various other things that happen in the game. Guys. There's literally a building (without upgrades) that gives you +2 stability (DLS center), a building that gives +1 stability and you're going to encounter a lot more stability upgrades over the course of the game. It's a natural thing to combat, just like the station maintenance. If these stability debuffs didn't exist you'd literally have no reason to continue improving the station to continuously combat the problem. What's the point of playing a city builder if there's no reason to build a city??My point is, the debuff isn't the end of your game lmao. These reviewers seem to think that you HAVE to move on from the system or else your station will blow up. If you lose a game from a -1 stability loss then you're already playing the game badly and it shouldn't come to that. You build a single building or enact a policy and you're fine. It's honestly more lenient than you think.People complaining that a lot of the people you wake up are unable to work and are "useless" - most of what I'm about to say overlaps with the paragraph above, but again guys, just build more houses. It's not hard. There's plenty of space if you know what you're doing, and moving things around really isn't hard either. I really can't imagine much of a game if one of the major problems wasn't that I had to build housing for the last remaining bastion in all of humanity's survival in the entire universe, like, can you imagine if the game didn't have non-workers? Would be too easy imo. Anyway, that's a thing you can change in the difficulty settings now, so that's not really a problem anymore.There's a lot of other complaints mainly about resource management between sectors, but that isn't even hard either. You just move a freaking slider from the left to the right, and bam, you have transfer between sectors. I mean it really isn't rocket science.I love the game, but holy hell the developers do need to learn a thing or two about how city builders are supposed to work and also implement some quality of life stuff. Here's the main problems I'll admit to so far that aren't just a result of people being too bad to play the game:- Cargo ships are stupid. They choose a destination and then go there and back even if the resource depletes during that time. They could be made to change their destination if a resource is going to deplete which would allow for much less micromanagement, but whatever, it's not really a problem once you have enough cargo ships.- There's no GUI showing how many workers there are available in a sector, you have to manually calculate that in your head by taking the workers working and the total workers you have, which is really annoying when trying to remain in optimal conditions.- A lot of the buildings are entirely useless and are terrible to use. The water treatment plant for example, 25 waste per cycle?? My finished Tiqqun had 5850 people and only produced a little more than 5 waste per cycle.. That ♥♥♥♥ is just ridiculous, one fusion station is enough to supply two algae farms (which is enough to supply 5850 people somehow). The game has terrible balancing in my opinion but for the complete opposite of what people are saying. It gets too easy once you research the relevant techs.- Medium and Large stockpiles are stupid. They grant more space sure, but they DON'T INCREASE THE NUMBER OF THE CARTS TO TRANSFER RESOURCES. What?? The speed of constructing and deconstructing things is relevant to the amount of little carts you have transporting resources, but these stockpiles keep the same amount of carts but for more stuff, which just leads to more player frustration, it literally encourages you to not have as many carts. You're better off just sticking to small stockpiles, they're way better.- Game has some pretty bad optimisation and FPS problems when it comes to certain solar systems and places your ship can go. On my system, changing the graphics settings didn't seem to affect this at all. I just had to play on 30fps for some entire sections of the game until it was suddenly 60fps again. Not a major problem, but I see some people literally quit the game just because of that, so.. L I guess.In my opinion, the story is really good, I felt quite entranced by it and super immersed in the mission and why I was doing what I was doing. That being said, the last two chapters were pretty underwhelming. I don't want to spoil any of the story for anyone who's actually read this far who hasn't already played the game, but I was really expecting something harder or more engaging tbh, not just a reason to constantly move around the system.I love the look and animations of everything. The game has a sweet atmosphere that the music helps set in too.It's good in my opinion, but I really like hard games that challenge me. Definitely not for everyone I guess. Frostpunk is a very similar game without all the problems I mentioned above if you'd like to give that a go, but do understand that it is quite hard just as this is, but without any of the annoying problems of the developers not knowing how to make a good city builder I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Frost Punk before, this game is similar to it, but it takes place in space.As an administrator, you must construct facilities, assist your people in improving their living conditions, explore planets, and decide what to do with them because your actions have many consequences. Accept that bugs will exist on the first day of release don't let it ruin your mood.There is no problem with the performance. The game runs perfectly on my PC.The game is not hard. I'm not sure why people are complaining about the game's difficulty.For new players:- Please read the tutorial thoroughly. The majority of complaints come from people who did not read the tutorial.- Turn on the option to pause the game while reading the dialog.- Because roads are free to construct, simply construct them and collect all of the resources on the floor. - Leave plenty of room for large and important facilities and factories.- You are not required to unlock Sector 2 early in the game. Just make sure that everything on Sector 1 is running smoothly. Trust me. - Pause often. Don't overwork your workers. Watch the food. Don't mess up. Pause often. Make sure there are enough or more than enough people for each Sector's work, and everything will be fine.- When things are about to get out of hand, it is a good idea to slow down.

_childDocuments_.review: Great story driven city-builder game with questionable mechanicsSo here is the recipe for IXION:- Take 1 pack of Frostpunk, simplify policy, choice and building mechanics- Add a ton more story/adventure content - 1.5 spoons of nice graphics- Bake for 3-4 years- QA is optional Jokes aside, if you liked games like Frostpunk, you will likely find IXION very enjoyable, similar concept with more focus on story elements. It looks gorgeous, the story is gripping and the soundtrack is truly exceptional. However the game is a lot less refined than Frostpunk and plagued with questionable design choices in its core gameplay loop:- A tetris-like city building is certainly unique, but with every building being a square and lack of certain sizes, like 2x2, end up making the entire mid game an awful chore with hours spent redesigning the station each time you get a new research tier and buildings no longer fitting your grid.- Logistics is annoying at best. There is little to no automation and half of late game is filled with endless manual movement of people and resources across 6 districts and 40 storage facilities. It gets so bad that some of the quests start to bug because game fails to assign resources due to a full storage somewhere in the ship.- UI is anything but useful. It does the basics, but you wont find any real “quality of life” features. Want to calculate your production? Have fun do it yourself. Want to prevent your ship from suicide charges into the storm? Enjoy manually banning every single asteroid in half of the system.- Lack of proper tutorial. The game is difficult, however what often left out is that the biggest challenge is total lack of explanation of its core mechanics. Wanna know what's gonna happen if you fly your cargo ships into a storm? Or why half of them didn’t die? Welcome to google. By the end of your 20 hour run you may fail only because you wasted too many resources in act 2 and 3 while you figured out how the game even works. - Some story points make no sense. No spoilers here, but some of the key story choices and characters receive little to no explanation, leaving you in the dark about half of the key plot mysteries. It gets especially bad in the late game where some of the ingame events/quests don’t get any resolution at all. In addition stability system is just weird. People unhappy that you stuck in dead solar system? Now they will be pissed that you left. Workers unhappy that they work extra hours? Now they are on strike and the ship is about to explode cause you don't have any materials to fix it. Your human sized lemmings would rather die than go to work for a few extra hours.Ultimately, I would recommend this game, as the journey still worth the troubles. It’s just a shame that it could have been so much better, but instead it leaves you with a pile of tedious mechanics that sour otherwise great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewers say is like Frostpunk, not really, Frostpunk was funnier, from what I remember.This game has bugs and seems unfinished (or plain stupid), I almost finished chapter 2 (on Challenge, not as bad as they say) when I got pissed (over stupid parts No. 3), deleted saves and uninstalled the game.I tried the Default and Journey first, too many resources so little time.Bugs:- When you open a new sector sometimes you are missing 30 workers even you did not transfer any crew from source sector (you must load a save before requesting the opening or cancel, pass some time and request again);- After loading several times, the game runs slow and restart is required.Stupid parts:1. Lets say we have 2 ships (30+ cargo space) tasked with gathering Carbon and there is a cluster of 3-4 rocks of it found by the same probe, first ship is near the cluster when the second just leaves Tiqqun. - both target same destination;- first picks the 10 Carbon found and returns to Tiqqun (with 20+ empty cargo), when clearly could visit the nearby rocks to fill its cargo;- second ship does not change destination after first ship empties that destination, it goes there and returns to Tiqqun with empty cargo, a really big waste of time (you are on the clock);- this brings micro-management to a new level.2. Even if I have a lot of unemployed workers in Sector 1 (Space specialization, tier 2), I can't transfer fast enough the resources from space docks (have 3, with no more than 2 cargo ships assigned) to local storage or to adjacent sectors.3. Losing 7% Trust when you overload the powergrid with the game paused. I didn't test if switching on & off a building with game paused, will get you to 0% Trust, probably it does.4. There are building with different sizes: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15 and access to road on one side. Noticed the 5 and 7?! The developers thought is funny to torture people with OCD, trying to maximize the use of space on a 56 x 30 grid. There are no buildings with 3 x 4, 3 x N.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Fun and unique. I haven't heard this story / plot line before and it was refreshing. Gameplay: is a combination of a few game types, specifically elements of Factorio and Escape Velocity Nova (very old game, or for others - Stellaris), without the Civilisation Esque bullsh#t but there are political elements which are fun. There is also a bit of the old school Fallout dialogue choices / consequences.   Overall: very enjoyable 9/10. I do admit I tap on the ol' wemod trainer on rare occasions.

_childDocuments_.review: I love city builders and survival games. If my civilization isn't on the brink of constant destruction, where's the fun? That's why I love Frostpunk. But I rage quit this game so hard. The daily penalties to restore the hull ensure that all I can ever do is focus on that, so I don't move on to the next sector in time. Then I'm struck with a penalty for that, and my people become more unhappy and I'm struck with another penalty.

_childDocuments_.review:
IXION combines city building, survival elements and exploration, into a thrilling space opera as you explore the stars. Propelled onwards through a perilous journey, you are the Administrator of the Tiqqun space station, charged with finding a new home for humanity.

Keeping the station sound and flying will require a deft hand and strategic thinking, as you are constantly pulled between maintaining hull integrity, bringing in new resources and managing power consumption.

What choices will you make when confronted with impending disaster? What will you discover out there in the dark?
